shloka_text: प्रहर्षोत्फुल्लनयनां पाण्डुरक्षौमवासिनीम्। अविदूरे स्थितां दृष्ट्वा धात्रीं पप्रच्छ मन्थरा।।2.7.7।।
explanation: Seeing a royal  maid clad in white silk garment and standing not very far with her eyes expanded in delight Manthara enquired:

shloka_text: उत्तमेनाभिसंयुक्ता हर्षेणार्थपरा सती। राममाता धनं किन्नु जनेभ्यस्सम्प्रयच्छति।।2.7.8।।
explanation: Why is Rama's mother, forever interested in the accumulation of money gifting away her wealth to men with great joy?

shloka_text: अतिमात्रप्रहर्षोऽयं किं जनस्य च शंस मे। कारयिष्यति किं वापि सम्प्रहृष्टो महीपतिः।।2.7.9।।
explanation: Why do the people look exceedingly happy? Tell me, what the king with great delight is proposing to do?

shloka_text: विदीर्यमाणा हर्षेण धात्री तु परया मुदा। आचचक्षेऽथ कुब्जायै भूयसीं राघव श्रियम्।।2.7.10।।
explanation: Bursting with great joy, the royal maid related to the hunchback the great fortune awaiting the son of the Raghus (Rama).

shloka_text: श्वः पुष्येण जितक्रोधं यौवराज्येन राघवम्। राजा दशरथो राममभिषेचयिताऽनघम्।।2.7.11।।
explanation: Tomorrow under the spell of the Pushya star, king Dasaratha will consecrate blameless Rama born in the race of Raghu as heirapparent (the maid said).

shloka_text: धात्र्यास्तु वचनं शृत्वा कुब्जा क्षिप्रममर्षिता। कैलासशिखराकारा त्प्रासादादवरोहत।।2.7.12।।
explanation: Having heard these words of the royal maid, the hunchback became furious and speedily descended from that palace resembling the peak of mount Kailasa.

shloka_text: सा दह्यमाना कोपेन मन्थरा पापदर्शिनी। शयानामेत्य कैकेयीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.7.13।।
explanation: The malevolent Manthara on fire with fury reached Kaikeyi lying upon her couch  and said:

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठ मूढे किं शेषे भयं त्वामभिवर्तते। उपप्लुतामौघेन किमात्मानं न बुध्यसे।।2.7.14।।
explanation: O senseless one, why are you lying down? Get up A great fear is gripping you. Why don't you realise that you are floating in a sea of perils.

shloka_text: अनिष्टे सुभगाकारे सौभाग्येन विकत्थसे। चलं हि तव सौभाग्यं नद्यास्स्रोत इवोष्णगे।।2.7.15।।
explanation: Though you appear to be your husband's darling, in reality he dislikes you. The good fortune you boast of indeed is unstable like the stream of a river in summer.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी रुष्टया परुषं वचः। कुब्जया पापदर्शिन्या विषादमगमत्परम्।।2.7.16।।
explanation: At these harsh words of the furious, evileyed hunchback Kaikeyi   fell into great despondency.

shloka_text: कैकेयी त्वब्रवीत्कुब्जां कच्चित्क्षेमं नु मन्थरे। विषण्णवदनां हि त्वां लक्षये भृशदुःखिताम्।।2.7.17।।
explanation: Kaikeyi said to the hunchback, O Manthara isn't all well with you? I can mark it from your dejected face how greatly distressed you feel, indeed.

shloka_text: मन्थरा तु वच श्श्रुत्वा कैकेय्या मधुराक्षरम्। उवाच क्रोधसंयुक्ता वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदा।।2.7.18।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Kaikeyi uttered in a gentle voice, wrathful Manthara skilled in speech, said:

shloka_text: सा विषण्णतरा भूत्वा कुब्जा तस्या हितैषिणी। विषादयन्ती प्रोवाच भेदयन्ती च राघवम्।।2.7.19।।
explanation: That hunchback feeling still more depressed in her (Kaikeyi's) interest and intending to cause in her despondency and distance Rama from her spoke out:

shloka_text: अक्षय्यं सुमहद्देवि प्रवृत्तं त्वद्विनाशनम्। रामं दशरथो राजा यौवराज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति।।2.7.20।।
explanation: O queen, your end is approaching, and it has no end and it is overwhelming. King Dasaratha is crowning Rama as heirapparent.

shloka_text: साऽस्म्यगाधे भये मग्ना दुःखशोकसमन्विता। दह्यमानाऽनलेनेव त्वद्धितार्थमिहागता।।2.7.21।।
explanation: Plunged in unfathomable fear and stricken with grief and tears I am here seeking your wellbeing and yet consumed as though by fire.

shloka_text: तव दुःखेन कैकेयि मम दुःखं महद्भवेत्। त्वद्वृद्धौ मम वृद्धिश्च भवेदत्र न संशयः।।2.7.22।।
explanation: O Kaikeyi, your sorrow will augment my sorrow. Your prosperity would mean my prosperity. There is no doubt about this.

shloka_text: नराधिपकुले जाता महिषी त्वं महीपतेः। उग्रत्वं राजधर्माणां कथं देवि न बुध्यसे।।2.7.23।।
explanation: O queen, born in the royal family and being a king's consort why don't you realise the ruthless ways of statecraft?

shloka_text: धर्मावादी शठो भर्ता श्लक्ष्णवादी च दारुणः। शुद्धभावे न जानीषे तेनैव मतिसन्धिता।।2.7.24।।
explanation: Your husband speaks morals publicly but in private he is deceitful. He speaks gently  but acts cruelly. Because of your innocent nature you are  beguiled by him. You do not understand this.

shloka_text: उपस्थितः प्रयुञ्जानस्त्वयि सान्त्वमनर्थकम्। अर्थेनैवाद्य ते भर्ता कौसल्यां योजयिष्यति।।2.7.25।।
explanation: When your husband approaches you he swears in meaningless, appeasing words. But today he is going to bestow benefit on Kausalya only.

shloka_text: उपवाह्य स दुष्टात्मा भरतं तव बन्धुषु। काल्ये स्थापयिता रामं राज्ये निहतकण्टके।।2.7.26।।
explanation: That evilminded one, having sent Bharata away to your relations house, is going to install Rama unhindered in the kingdom at dawn tomorrow.

shloka_text: शत्रुः पतिप्रवादेन मात्रेव हितकाम्यया। आशीविष इवाङ्केन बाले परिधृतस्त्वया।।2.7.27।।
explanation: O innocent lady with the intention of doing good like a mother to your husband who is your enemy, you are holding on your lap a venomous serpent.

shloka_text: यथा हि कुर्यात्सर्पो वा शत्रुर्वा प्रत्युपेक्षितः। राज्ञा दशरथेनाद्य सपुत्रा त्वं तथा कृता।।2.7.28।।
explanation: King Dasaratha has done to you and to your son the same thing as a  snake or an enemy would do when ignored.

shloka_text: पापेनानृतसान्त्वेन बाले नित्यसुखोचिते। रामं स्थापयता राज्ये सानुबन्धा हता ह्यसि।।2.7.29।।
explanation: O senseless lady, you are always accustomed to comfort. With deceitful words of appeasement that vicious one (King Dasaratha) is going to install Rama in the kingdom. You along with your son have been surely ruined.

shloka_text: सा प्राप्तकालं कैकेयि क्षिप्रं कुरु हितं तव। त्रायस्व पुत्रमात्मानं मां च विस्मयदर्शने।।2.7.30।।
explanation: O enchantingeyed Kaikeyi, that appropriate time has come. Act quickly for your own wellbeing. Save yourself, your son and me too.

shloka_text: मन्थाराया वचश्श्रुत्वा शयाना सा शुभानना। उत्तस्थौ हर्षसम्पूर्णा चन्द्रलेखेव शारदी।।2.7.31।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Manthara, Kaikeyi of charming countenance lying in her couch rose, full of joy, like the autumnal streak of the Moon's crescent.

shloka_text: अतीव सा तु संहृष्टा कैकेयी विस्मयान्विता। एकमाभरणं तस्यै कुब्जायै प्रददौ शुभम्।।2.7.32।।
explanation: Filled with immense joy and wonder (at the news), Kaikeyi gifted a beauthful ornament to that hunchback.

shloka_text: दत्वा त्वाभरणं तस्यै कुब्जायै प्रमदोत्तमा। कैकेयी मन्थरां दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाब्रवीदिदम्।।2.7.33।।
explanation: Kaikeyi, the best among the beauties, having given the ornament to Manthara, the hunchback, looked at her and said these words again:

shloka_text: इदं तु मन्थरे मह्यमाख्यासि परमं प्रियम्। एतन्मे प्रियमाख्यातुः किं वा भूयः करोमि ते।।2.7.34।।
explanation: O Manthara, the news you have brought me is exceedingly pleasant. What more can I do for you? Here is the gift for one who brings good tidings.

shloka_text: रामे वा भरते वाऽहं विशेषं नोपलक्षये। तस्मात्तुष्टाऽस्मि यद्राजा रामं राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति।।2.7.35।।
explanation: I do not see any distinction between Rama and Bharata as such. I am contented with Rama's consecration in the kingdom.

shloka_text: न मे परं किञ्चिदितस्त्वया पुनः प्रियं प्रियार्हे सुवचं वचःपरम्। तथा ह्यवोचस्त्वमतः प्रियोत्तरं वरं परं ते प्रददामि तं वृणु।।2.7.36।।
explanation: O woman worthy of affection for me there is nothing greater and dearer than this news. I will grant you another reward better than this. Just ask for it. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the  holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: मन्थरा त्वभ्यसूयैनामुत्सृज्याभरणं च तत्। उवाचेदं ततो वाक्यं कोपदुःखसमन्विता।।2.8.1।।
explanation: Annoyed with Kaikeyi and filled with rage and sorrow, Manthara discarded the ornament (gifted to her) and said these words:

shloka_text: हर्षं किमिदमस्थाने कृतवत्यसि बालिशे। शोकसागरमध्यस्थमात्मानं नावबुध्यसे।।2.8.2।।
explanation: O foolish woman why do you display this misplaced happiness, little realising that you are in the midst of an ocean of sorrow?

shloka_text: मनसा प्रहसामि त्वां देवि दुःखार्दिता सती। यच्छोचितव्ये हृष्टाऽसि प्राप्येदं व्यसनं महत्।।2.8.3।।
explanation: O queen at a time when this great misfortune has befallen you, you are rejoicing instead of feeling miserable. I am indeed laughing at you at heart.

shloka_text: शोचामि दुर्मतित्वं ते का हि प्राज्ञा प्रहर्षयेत्। अरेस्सपत्नीपुत्रस्य वृद्धिं मृत्योरिवागताम्।।2.8.4।।
explanation: I pity your false notion. Will any wise woman rejoice at the prosperity of the son of a cowife who is like an enemy? This is like (courting) death.

shloka_text: भरतादेव रामस्य राज्यसाधारणाद्भयम्। तद्विचिन्त्य विषण्णाऽस्मि भयं भीताऽद्धि जायते।।2.8.5।।
explanation: Since Bharata and Rama have equal claim to the kingdom, Bharata is a  source of fear for Rama. Having thought over this matter, I am dejected. Danger springs from one who is in fear.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणो हि महेष्वासो रामं सर्वात्मना गतः। शत्रुघ्नश्चापि भरतं काकुत्स्थं लक्ष्मणो यथा।।2.8.6।।
explanation: Lakshmana who wields a great bow has taken refuge with all his heart in Rama a descendant of Kakutstha dynasty. So does Satrughna in Bharata.

shloka_text: प्रत्यासन्नक्रमेणापि भरतस्यैव भामिनि। राज्यक्रमो विप्रकृष्टस्तयोस्तावत्कनीयसोः।।2.8.7।।
explanation: O beautiful lady in order of birth, too, Bharata's right to the throne is just next (to  Rama's). While being younger, the chances of the other two (Lakshmana and Satrughna) are remote.

shloka_text: विदुषः क्षत्रचारित्रे प्राज्ञस्य प्राप्तकारिणः। भयात्प्रवेपे रामस्य चिन्तयन्ती तवात्मजम्।।2.8.8।।
explanation: Rama is learned in the duties of a kshatriya. He is wise enough to do what he should at the appropriate time. While reflecting the fate of your son, I am trembling with fear.

shloka_text: सुभगा खलु कौशल्या यस्याः पुत्रोऽभिषेक्ष्यते। यौवराज्येन महता श्वः पुष्येण द्विजोत्तमैः।।2.8.9।।
explanation: Kausalya whose son is going to be coronated as heirapparent by eminent brahmins under Pushya  star tomorrow is fortunate, indeed.

shloka_text: प्राप्तां सुमहतीं प्रीतिं प्रतीतां तां हतद्विषम्। उपस्थास्यसि कौसल्यां दासीव त्त्वं कृताञ्जलिः।।2.8.10।।
explanation: With folded palms like an attendant, you will have to serve that renowned Kausalya who is greatlly delighted by getting rid of her enemies.

shloka_text: एवं चेत्त्वं सहास्माभिस्तस्याः प्रेष्या भविष्यसि। पुत्रश्च तव रामस्य प्रेष्यभावं गमिष्यति।।2.8.11।।
explanation: If you thus become her attendant along with us, your son will also develop slavishness towards Rama.

shloka_text: हृष्टाः खलु भविष्यन्ति रामस्य परमास्स्त्रियः। अप्रहृष्टा भविष्यन्ति स्नुषास्ते भरतक्षये।।2.8.12।।
explanation: All the women of Rama's (palace) will be delighted indeed. With the decline of Bharata, your daughtersinlaw will be deprived of all happiness.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतां ब्रुवन्तीं मन्थरां ततः। रामस्यैव गुणान्देवी कैकेयी प्रशशंस ह।।2.8.13।।
explanation: Having seen that morose Manthara speaking thus, Kaikeyi commended the virtues of Rama.

shloka_text: धर्मज्ञो गुरुभिर्दान्तः कृतज्ञस्सत्यवाक्छुचिः। रामो राज्ञ स्सुतो ज्येष्ठो यौवराज्यमतोऽर्हति।।2.8.14।।
explanation: Rama knows righteouness. He has been taught selfrestraint by elders. He is grateful and truthful. He is undefiled. He is the eldest son of the king. Therefore, he deserves to be the heirapparent (of the kingdom).

shloka_text: भ्रातृ़न्भृत्यांश्च दीर्घायुः पितृवत्पालयिष्यति। सन्तप्स्यसे कथं कुब्जे श्रुत्वा रामाभिषेचनम्।।2.8.15।।
explanation: Blessed with a long life, Rama will protect his brothers and the servants like a father. O hunchback, hearing Rama's coronation why are you aggrieved?

shloka_text: भरतश्चापि रामस्य ध्रुवं वर्षशतात्परम्। पितृपैतामहं राज्यमवाप्ता पुरुषर्षभः।।2.8.16।।
explanation: After a hundred years of Rama's rule, Bharata, the best of men, will get the kingdom of his ancestors.

shloka_text: सा त्वमभ्युदये प्राप्ते वर्तमाने च मन्थरे। भविष्यति च कल्याणे किमर्थं परितप्यसे।।2.8.17।।
explanation: Manthara, we have enjoyed prosperity in the past, we are enjoying it now and we will enjoy it in future. Then why are you aggrieved?

shloka_text: यथा मे भरतो मान्यस्तथा भूयोऽपि राघवः। कौशल्यातोऽतिरिक्तं च सोऽनुशुश्रूषते हि माम्।।2.8.18।।
explanation: For me, if Bharata is worthy of consideration Rama is worthier. He serves me even more (scrupulously) than he does Kausalya.

shloka_text: राज्यं यदि हि रामस्य भरतस्यापि तत्तदा। मन्यते हि यथात्मानं तथा भ्रातृ़ंश्च राघवः।।2.8.19।।
explanation: If the kingdom is Rama's, it is also Bharata's, since Rama regards his brothers as his own self

shloka_text: कैकेयीवचनं श्रुत्वा मन्थरा भृशदुःखिता। दीर्घमुष्णं च विनिश्वस्य कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.8.20।।
explanation: Having heard Kaikeyi's words Manthara was extremely unhappy. Heaving deep, hot sighs she said to Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: अनर्थदर्शिनी मौर्ख्यान्नात्मानमवबुध्यसे। शोकव्यसनविस्तीर्णे मज्जन्ती दुःखसागरे।।2.8.21।।
explanation: You are sinking in the sea of sorrow widened with tears and troubles. But you are stupid enough not to perceive your own wellbeing.

shloka_text: भविता राघवो राजा राघवस्यानु यस्सुतः। राजवंशात्तु कैकेयि भरतःपरिहास्यते।।2.8.22।।
explanation: Rama, the scion of the Raghus, will become king. After Rama, his son will suceed him. O Kaikeyi, as for  Bharata, he will be debarred from royal succession (altogether).

shloka_text: न हि राज्ञस्सुता स्सर्वे राज्ये तिष्ठन्ति भामिनि। स्थाप्यमानेषु सर्वेषु सुमहाननयो भवेत्।।2.8.23।।
explanation: O lovely lady, not all the sons of the king will inherit the kingdom. If all of them are installed as kings, there will be great disorder.

shloka_text: तस्माज्ज्येष्ठे हि कैकेयि राज्यतन्त्राणि पार्थिवाः। स्थापयन्त्यनवद्याङ्गि गुणवत्स्वितरेष्वपि।।2.8.24।।
explanation: O Kaikeyi of beautiful limbs, for that reason kings bestow the governance of the kingdom either on the eldest or on other virtuous sons.

shloka_text: असावत्यन्तनिर्भग्नस्तव पुत्रो भविष्यति। अनाथवत्सुखेभ्यश्च राजवंशाच्च वत्सले।।2.8.25।।
explanation: O (Kaikeyi) dear cut off from royal succession as well as from its comforts, your son will become totally forlorn and brokenhearted.

shloka_text: साऽहं त्वदर्थे सम्प्राप्ता त्वं तु मां नावबुद्ध्यसे। सपत्नि वृद्धौ या मे त्वं प्रदेयं दातुमिच्छसि।।2.8.26।।
explanation: I am here to serve your interest. Nevertheless you do not understand me and you wish to confer gifts on me on the occasion of the prosperity of your cowife.

shloka_text: ध्रुवं तु भरतं रामः प्राप्य राज्यमकण्टकम्। देशान्तरं वा नयिता लोकान्तरमथाऽपि वा।।2.8.27।।
explanation: Rama, having secured the thornless kingdom, will banish Bharata from the country or else send him to the other world. This is certain.

shloka_text: बाल एव हि मातुल्यं भरतो नायितस्त्वया। सन्निकर्षाच्च सौहार्दं जायते स्थावरेष्वपि।।2.8.28।।
explanation: Bharata has been sent by you right from his childhood to his maternal uncle's house.  Proximity creates friendship even amongst the inanimate objects.

shloka_text: भरतस्याप्यनुवशश्शत्रुघ्नोऽपि समं गतः। लक्ष्मणो हि यथा रामं तथाऽसौ भरतं गतः।।2.8.29।।
explanation: Satrughna who is obedient to Bharata has followed him. Like Lakshmana who has taken refuge in Rama, he has also resorted to Bharata.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि द्रुमः कश्चिच्छेत्तव्यो वनजीविभिः। सन्निकर्षादिषीकाभिर्मोचितः परमाद्भयात्।।2.8.30।।
explanation: It is said that a tree intended to be cut down by those living on the forest is let off   due to entanglement of a kind of grass known as Ishika (thorny bushes) growing in its vicinity. (If Bharata had been at Ayodhya now, Dasaratha himself would have helped him.

shloka_text: गोप्ता हि रामं सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणं चापि राघवः। अश्विनोरिव सौभ्रात्रं तयोर्लोकेषु विश्रुतम्।।2.8.31।।
explanation: Just as Lakshmana protects Rama, Rama protects Lakshmana. Their brotherhood is renowned in the world like that of the Ashwins.

shloka_text: तस्मान्न लक्ष्मणे रामः पापं किञ्चित्करिष्यति। रामस्तु भरते पापं कुर्यादिति न संशयः।।2.8.32।।
explanation: Rama will do no harm to Lakshmana. As for Bharata, Rama will doubtless do him harm.

shloka_text: तस्माद्राजगृहादेव वनं गच्छतु ते सुतः। एतद्धि रोचते मह्यं भृशं चापि हितं तव।।2.8.33।।
explanation: Therefore let your son go to the forest straight from his uncle's palace only. That alone will please me. For you also this is highly beneficial.

shloka_text: एवं ते ज्ञातिपक्षस्य श्रेयश्चैव भविष्यति। यदि चेद्भरतो धर्मात्पित्र्यं राज्यमवाप्स्यसि।।2.8.34।।
explanation: If Bharata secures the ancestral kingdom righteously, it will bring welfare to you and to your relations also.

shloka_text: स ते सुखोचितो बालो रामस्य सहजो रिपुः। समृद्धार्थस्य नष्टार्थो जीविष्यति कथं वशे।।2.8.35।।
explanation: Your son, that young Bharata, is accustomed to comforts. He is a born enemy of Rama. How will he, deprived of all wealth, live under the control of Rama?

shloka_text: अभिद्रुतमिवारण्ये सिंहेन गजयूथपम्। प्रच्छाद्यमानं रामेण भरतं त्रातुमर्हसि।।2.8.36।।
explanation: Like the leader of an elephantherd attacked by a lion in the forest, Bharata is going to be oppressed by Rama. You should save him.

shloka_text: दर्पान्निराकृता पूर्वं त्वया सौभाग्यवत्तया। राममाता सपत्नी ते कथं वैरं न शातयेत्।।2.8.37।।
explanation: Being fortunate (being the favourite wife of your husband) you slighted your cowife earlier with pride. How will she, Rama's mother (Kausalya) remain without retaliating?

shloka_text: यदा हि रामः पृथिवीमवाप्स्यति प्रभूतरत्नाकरशैलपत्तनाम्। तदा गमिष्यस्यशुभं पराभवं सहैव दीना भरतेन भामिनि।।2.8.38।।
explanation: O lovely lady when Rama becomes the lord of this earth with its oceans, mountains and cities, then along with Bharata you will become miserable and fall into disgrace.

shloka_text: यदा हि रामः पृथिवीमवाप्स्यति ध्रुवं प्रणष्टो भरतो भविष्यति। अतो हि सञ्चिन्तय राज्यमात्मजे परस्य चैवाद्य विवासकारणम्।।2.8.39।।
explanation: When Rama obtains this earth, Bharata will be certainly ruined. Therefore, right now think of the kingdom for your son and the means of banishment for your enemy, Rama. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु कैकेयी क्रोधेन ज्वलितानना। दीर्घमुष्णं विनिश्वस्य मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.1।।
explanation: Thus spoken to, Kaikeyi, her face burning with anger, breathed a deep, hot sigh and said these words to Manthara:

shloka_text: अद्य राममितः क्षिप्रं वनं प्रस्थापयाम्यहम्। यौवराज्ये च भरतं क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचये।।2.9.2।।
explanation: Today I shall at once banish Rama from here into the forest and get Bharata coronated as heirapparent without delay.

shloka_text: इदं त्विदानीं सम्पश्य केनोपायेन मन्थरे। भरतः प्राप्नुयाद्राज्यं न तु रामः कथञ्चन।।2.9.3।।
explanation: O Manthara now see, for sure, Bharata and not Rama will get the kingdom by any means.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तया देव्या मन्थरा पापदर्शिनी। रामार्थमुपहिंसन्ती कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.4।।
explanation: Thus addressed by queen Kaikeyi, that evil minded Manthara said this to Kaikeyi  in order to spoil the interest of Rama:

shloka_text: हन्तेदानीं प्रवक्ष्यामि कैकेयि श्रूयतां च मे। यथा ते भरतो राज्यं पुत्रः प्राप्स्यति केवलम्।।2.9.5।।
explanation: O Kaikeyi, what a joy I shall now tell you how your son Bharata alone will secure the kingdom. Listen to me:

shloka_text: किं न स्मरसि कैकेयि स्मरन्ती वा निगूहसे। यदुच्यमानमात्मार्थं मत्तस्त्वं श्रोतुमिच्छसि।।2.9.6।।
explanation: O Kaikeyi, don't you remember in your own interest what I'm going to tell you or are you hiding it, wishing to hear from me?

shloka_text: मयोच्यमानं यदि ते श्रोतुं छन्दो विलासिनि। श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि श्रुत्वा चापि विमृश्यताम्।।2.9.7।।
explanation: O lovely Kaikeyi if it pleases you to hear from me, I shall tell you. Listen and think over it, too.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैवं वचनं तस्या मन्थरायास्तु कैकेयी। किञ्चिदुत्थाय शयनात्स्वास्तीर्णादिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.8।।
explanation: After hearing Manthara's words, Kaikeyi got up a little from her wellspread bed and said this:

shloka_text: कथय त्वं ममोपायं केनोपायेन मन्थरे। भरतः प्राप्नुयाद्राज्यं न तु रामः कथञ्चन।।2.9.9।।
explanation: O Manthara, tell me the means by which Bharata and not Rama will secure the kingdom in any circumstances.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तया देव्या मन्थरा पापदर्शिनी। रामार्थमुपहिंसन्ती कुब्जा वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.9.10।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the queen (Kaikeyi), the evileyed hunchback, Manthara, said with the intention to damage Rama's interest.

shloka_text: तव दैवासुरे युद्धे सह राजर्षिभिः पतिः। अगच्छत्त्वामुपादाय देवराजस्य साह्यकृत्।।2.9.11।। दिशमास्थाय वै देवि दक्षिणां दण्डकान्प्रति। वैजयन्तमिति ख्यातं पुरं यत्र तिमिध्वजः।।2.9.12।।
explanation: O queen during the war between gods and asuras, your husband went with royal saints intending to render assistance to Indra, king of the gods, taking you along with him. He set off in the southern direction of Dandaka forest to a renowned city called Vaijayanta where asura Timidhvaja lived.

shloka_text: तव दैवासुरे युद्धे सह राजर्षिभिः पतिः। अगच्छत्त्वामुपादाय देवराजस्य साह्यकृत्।।2.9.11।। दिशमास्थाय वै देवि दक्षिणां दण्डकान्प्रति। वैजयन्तमिति ख्यातं पुरं यत्र तिमिध्वजः।।2.9.12।।
explanation: O queen during the war between gods and asuras, your husband went with royal saints intending to render assistance to Indra, king of the gods, taking you along with him. He set off in the southern direction of Dandaka forest to a renowned city called Vaijayanta where asura Timidhvaja lived.

shloka_text: स शम्बर इति ख्यातश्शतमायो महासुरः। ददौ शक्रस्य सङ्ग्रामं देवसङ्घैरनिर्जितः।।2.9.13।।
explanation: That mighty asura wellknown as Sambara, capable of a hundred deceitful forms, challenged Indra to a battle which could not be conquered by hosts of gods.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्महति सङ्ग्रामे पुरुषान्क्षतविक्षतान्। रात्रौ प्रसुप्तान्घ्नन्ति स्म तरसाऽऽसाद्य राक्षसाः।।2.9.14।।
explanation: In that great battle, the rakshasas used to kill by force the warriors wounded by the weapons and those fast asleep during the night.

shloka_text: तत्राकरोन्महद्युद्धं राजा दशरथस्तदा। असुरैश्च महाबाहुश्शस्त्रैश्च शकलीकृतः।।2.9.15।।
explanation: There in that great battle the mightyarmed king Dasaratha lay wounded with weapons (used) by the asuras.

shloka_text: अपवाह्य त्वया देवि सङ्ग्रामान्नष्टचेतनः। तत्रापि विक्षतश्शस्त्रैः पतिस्ते रक्षितस्त्वया।।2.9.16।।
explanation: O queen you had protected your husband by carrying him away from the battlefield when he lost his consciousness. He was saved by you. Once again you saved him when he lay wounded with weapons (hurled) by the asuras.

shloka_text: तुष्टेन तेन दत्तौ ते द्वौ वरौ शुभदर्शने। स त्वयोक्तः पतिर्देवि  यदेच्छेयं तदा वरौ।।2.9.17।। गृह्णीयामिति तत्तेन तथेत्युक्तं महात्मना।
explanation: O auspiciouslooking one out of gratitude he had granted two boons to you (for saving him on two occasions). O queen then you told your husband that whenever you desire, you will ask for those boons. The magnanimous king said, 'So be it'.

shloka_text: अनभिज्ञाम्ह्यहं देवि त्वयैव कथिता पुरा।।2.9.18।। कथैषा तव तु स्नेहान्मनसा धार्यते मया। रामाभिषेकसम्भारान्निगृह्य विनिवर्तय।।2.9.19।।
explanation: O queen I did not know this indeed. Only you had related it to me earlier. Because of my affection towards you, I have retained it in my memory. (Now) prevent preparations for Rama's consecration by force.

shloka_text: अनभिज्ञाम्ह्यहं देवि त्वयैव कथिता पुरा।।2.9.18।। कथैषा तव तु स्नेहान्मनसा धार्यते मया। रामाभिषेकसम्भारान्निगृह्य विनिवर्तय।।2.9.19।।
explanation: O queen I did not know this indeed. Only you had related it to me earlier. Because of my affection towards you, I have retained it in my memory. (Now) prevent preparations for Rama's consecration by force.

shloka_text: तौ वरौ याच भर्तारं भरतस्याभिषेचनम्। प्रव्राजनं च रामस्य त्वं वर्षाणि चतुर्दश।।2.9.20।।
explanation: Ask your husband for those two boons namely consecration of Bharata and banishment  of Rama for fourteen years.

shloka_text: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि रामे प्रव्राजिते वनम्। प्रजाभावगतस्नेहस्स्थिरः पुत्रो भविष्यति।।2.9.21।।
explanation: If Rama is banished into the forest for fourteen years your son will be firmly established in the kingdom by  affectionately winning the hearts of  the people.

shloka_text: क्रोधागारं प्रविश्याऽद्य क्रुद्धेवाश्वपतेस्सुते। शेष्वाऽनन्तर्हितायां त्वं भूमौ मलिनवासिनी।।2.9.22।।
explanation: O Kaikeyi ,daughter of Ashwapati enter now the chamber of wrath like one in angry mood, wearing soiled garments and lie down on the bare ground.

shloka_text: मास्मैनं प्रत्युदीक्षेथा मा चैनमभिभाषथाः। रुदन्ती चापि तं दृष्ट्वा जगत्यां शोकलालसा।।2.9.23।।
explanation: Immersed in grief and in tears, neither look at him (Dasaratha) nor even talk to him when you see him.

shloka_text: दयिता त्वं सदा भर्तुरत्र मे नास्ति संशयः। त्वत्कृते स महाराजो विशेदपि हुताशनम्।।2.9.24।।
explanation: No doubt, you have always been a beloved wife to your husband. For your sake the great king will even enter into the burning fire.

shloka_text: न त्वां क्रोधयितुं शक्तो न क्रृद्धां प्रत्युदीक्षितुम्। तव प्रियार्थं राजा हि प्राणानपि परित्यजेत्।।2.9.25।।
explanation: The king is afraid of inciting your ire. When you are angry, he dare not look at your indignant countenance. Indeed he will forsake even his life for your pleasure.

shloka_text: न ह्यतिक्रमितुं शक्तस्तव वाक्यं महीपतिः। मन्दस्वभावे बुध्यस्व सौभाग्यबलमात्मनः।।2.9.26।।
explanation: The king would not dare transgress your words. O wicked woman, recognise the power of your beauty.

shloka_text: मणिमुक्तं सुवर्णानि रत्नानि विविधानि च। दद्याद्दशरथो राजा मास्म तेषु मनः कृथाः।।2.9.27।।
explanation: King Dasaratha may give you gems, pearls, gold and different kinds of precious stones. Do not pay them any attention.

shloka_text: यौ तौ दैवासुरे युद्धे वरौ दशरथोऽददात्। तौ स्मारय महाभागे सोऽर्थो न त्वामतिक्रमेत्।।2.9.28।।
explanation: O fortunate Kaikeyi, make him recollect the two boons he had granted you in the war between gods and demons. You should not ignore your objective.

shloka_text: यदातु ते वरं दद्यात्स्वयमुत्थाप्य राघवः। व्यवस्थाप्य महाराजं त्वमिमं वृणुया वरम्।।2.9.29।।
explanation: When Dasaratha personally lifts you from the floor and  asks  you what you want  you may make him settle down and ask him for these boons:

shloka_text: रामं प्रव्राजयारण्ये नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च। भरतः क्रियतां राजा पृथिव्याः पार्थिवर्षभः।।2.9.30।।
explanation: 'O best of kings exile Rama into the forest for fourteen years and make Bharata king of the land'.

shloka_text: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि रामे प्रव्राजिते वनम्। रूढश्च कृतमूलश्च शेषं स्थास्यति ते सुतः।।2.9.31।।
explanation: After Rama has been exiled into the forest for fourteen years your son grown strong and deeprooted will remain (king) for the rest of his life.

shloka_text: रामप्रव्राजनं चैव देवि याचस्व तं वरम्। एवं सिद्ध्यन्ति पुत्रस्य सर्वार्थास्तव भामिनि।।2.9.32।।
explanation: O Devi demand Rama's exile as a boon. O lovely queen this way all the interests of your son will be fulfilled (protected).

shloka_text: एवं प्रव्राजितश्चैव रामोऽरामो भविष्यति। भरतश्च हतामित्रस्तव राजा भविष्यति।।2.9.33।।
explanation: Thus, if Rama is exiled he will no longer be Rama (be able to cause delight to the people). Bharata will become king  with his enemy subdued.

shloka_text: येन कालेन रामश्च वनात्प्रत्यागमिष्यति। तेन कालेन पुत्रस्ते कृतमूलो भविष्यति।।2.9.34।। सुगृहीतमनुष्यश्च सुहृद्भिस्सार्धमात्मवान्।
explanation: By the time Rama returns from the forest, your son (now) confident, would have become deep rooted by gaining the company of friends and the acceptability of the people.

shloka_text: प्राप्तकालं नु मन्येऽहं राजानं वीतसाध्वसा।।2.9.35।। रामाभिषेकसङ्कल्पान्निगृह्य विनिवर्तय।
explanation: I think the proper time has come (to ask for the boons). Without fear refrain the king forcibly from his intention of installing Rama.

shloka_text: अनर्थमर्थरूपेण ग्राहिता सा ततस्तया।।2.9.36।। हृष्टा प्रतीता कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Thus, having been made to accept the evil design as a beneficial objective, Kaikeyi  understood (the entire matter) and in delight spoke to Manthara.

shloka_text: सा हि वाक्येन कुब्जायाः किशोरीवोत्पथं गता।।2.9.37।। कैकेयी विस्मयं प्राप्ता परं परमदर्शना।
explanation: That Kaikeyi, even though endowed with sound foresight, expressed her sense of wonder at the words of the hunchback and chose a wrong path like a young (immature) girl.

shloka_text: कुब्जे त्वां नाभिजानामि श्रेष्ठां श्रेष्ठाभिथायिनीम्।।2.9.38।। पृथिव्यामसि कुब्जानामुत्तमा बुद्धिनिश्चये।
explanation: (She said) O hunchback, I never knew that you can speak such excellent words or decide  things intelligently. You are the best among the hunchbacks of this world.

shloka_text: त्वमेव तु ममाऽर्थेषु नित्ययुक्ता हितैषिणी।।2.9.39।। नाहं समवबुध्येयं कुब्जे राज्ञश्चिकीर्षितम्।
explanation: O hunchback you alone always show interest in my affairs and seek my welfare. I might not have known the intended (deceptive) action of the king (without you).

shloka_text: सन्ति दुस्संस्थिताः कुब्जा वक्राः परमदारुणाः।।2.9.40।। त्वं पद्ममिव वातेन सन्नता प्रियदर्शना। त्वं पद्ममिव वातेन सन्नता प्रियदर्शना।
explanation: There are many hunchbacks in this world, terribly ugly with their bodies misshaped and crooked. But you look beautiful like a lotus bent by the breeze.

shloka_text: उरस्तेऽभिनिविष्टं वै यावत्स्कन्धात् समुन्नतं।।2.9.41।। अधस्ताच्चोदरं शातं सुनाभमिव लज्जितम्।
explanation: Your breasts are thick and are as high as your shoulders. Beneath them lies your belly with its beautiful navel (waist) looking slender as if out of bashfulness.

shloka_text: परिपूर्णं तु जघनं सुपीनौ च पयोधरौ।।2.9.42।। विमलेन्दुसमं वक्त्रमहोराजसि मन्थरे।
explanation: You have full hips, round and plump breasts. Your countenance equals the bright moon. How passionate you look, Manthara

shloka_text: जघनं तव निर्घुष्टं रशनादामशोभितम्।।2.9.43।। जङ्घे भृशमुपन्यस्ते पादौ चाप्यायतावुभौ।
explanation: Your hips, glitter with the jingling girdle. Strong are the  calfs of your legs and long are your feet.

shloka_text: त्वमायताभ्यां सक्थिभ्यां मन्थरे क्षौमवासिनी।।2.9.44।। अग्रतो मम गच्छन्ती राजहंसीव राजसे।
explanation: O Manthara when clad in silk garment you walk in front of me with your heavy thighs, you look like a female royal swan.

shloka_text: आसन्याश्शम्बरे मायास्सहस्रमसुराधिपे।।2.9.45।। सर्वास्त्वयि निविष्टास्ता भूयश्चान्यास्सहस्रशः।
explanation: In you reside a thousand deceitful means more than all the thousand mayas (tricks) of Sambara, king of the asuras, was capable of.

shloka_text: तवेदं स्थगु यद्दीर्घं रथघोणमिवायतम्।।2.9.46।। मतयः क्षत्रविद्याश्च मायाश्चात्र वसन्ति ते।
explanation: Your clever thoughts, magic powers and also the skills of kshatriyas are stored in your huge hump which is as wide as the hub of a chariot wheel.

shloka_text: अत्र ते प्रतिमोक्ष्यामि मालां कुब्जे हिरण्मयीम्।।2.9.47।। अभिषिक्ते च भरते राघवे च वनं गते।
explanation: O hunchback, with Rama gone to the forest and Bharata consecrated, I shall drape this hump with a golden garland.

shloka_text: जात्येन च सुवर्णेन सुनिष्टप्तेन मन्थरे।।2.9.48।। लब्धार्था च प्रतीता च लेपयिष्यामि ते स्थगु।
explanation: O Manthara, when my objective is accomplished and I am fully satisfied, I will smear your hump with the best of refined liquid gold.

shloka_text: मुखे च तिलकं चित्रं जातरूपमयं शुभम्।।2.9.49।। कारयिष्यामि ते कुब्जे शुभान्याभरणानि च।
explanation: O Manthara, I shall get a tilaka made of gold for your auspicious, lovely face and shall also order exquisite ornaments (for you).

shloka_text: परिधाय शुभे वस्त्रे देवतेव चरिष्यसि।।2.9.50।। चन्द्रमाह्वयमानेन मुखेनाप्रतिमानना। गमिष्यसि गतिं मुख्यां गर्वयन्ती द्विषज्जनम्।।2.9.51।।
explanation: You shall move about wearing lovely garments like a goddess. With a peerless countenance, as if challenging the Moon and feeling proud, you will attain a state of eminence amidst your enemies.

shloka_text: परिधाय शुभे वस्त्रे देवतेव चरिष्यसि।।2.9.50।। चन्द्रमाह्वयमानेन मुखेनाप्रतिमानना। गमिष्यसि गतिं मुख्यां गर्वयन्ती द्विषज्जनम्।।2.9.51।।
explanation: You shall move about wearing lovely garments like a goddess. With a peerless countenance, as if challenging the Moon and feeling proud, you will attain a state of eminence amidst your enemies.

shloka_text: तवापि कुब्जाः कुब्जायास्सर्वाभरणभूषिताः। पादौ परिचरिष्यन्ति यथैव त्वं सदा मम।।2.9.52।।
explanation: Other hunchbacks adorned with all sorts of ornament shall also serve you in the same manner as you are serving me.

shloka_text: इति प्रशस्यमाना सा कैकेयीमिदमब्रवीत्। शयानां शयने शुभ्रे वेद्यामग्निशिखामिव।।2.9.53।।
explanation: Flattered in this manner, Manthara addressed Kaikeyi who was lying on a white couch and looking like a flaming fire on the sacrificial altar:

shloka_text: गतोदके सेतुबन्धो न कल्याणि विधीयते। उत्तिष्ठ कुरु कल्याणि राजानमनुदर्शय।।2.9.54।।
explanation: O fortunate one construction of a dike is not undertaken after the water has flowed down. Act before the king to the best of your interest.

shloka_text: तथा प्रोत्साहिता देवी गत्वा मन्थरया सह। क्रोधागारं विशालाक्षी सौभाग्यमदगर्विता।।2.9.55।। अनेकशतसाहस्रं मुक्ताहारं वराङ्गना। अवमुच्य वरार्हाणि शुभान्याभरणानि च।।2.9.56।। ततो हेमोपमा तत्र कुब्जावाक्यवशं गता। संविश्य भूमौ कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.57।।
explanation: That beautiful, largeeyed Kaikeyi, puffed with the pride of her intoxicating beauty, encourged and influenced by the words of that hunchback, entered the chamber of wrath. She cast off her highly precious pearl necklace worth many hundreds of thousands (of rupees) and other costly, beautiful ornaments. Thereafter that goldenhued Kaikeyi lay down on the floor and said to Manthara:

shloka_text: तथा प्रोत्साहिता देवी गत्वा मन्थरया सह। क्रोधागारं विशालाक्षी सौभाग्यमदगर्विता।।2.9.55।। अनेकशतसाहस्रं मुक्ताहारं वराङ्गना। अवमुच्य वरार्हाणि शुभान्याभरणानि च।।2.9.56।। ततो हेमोपमा तत्र कुब्जावाक्यवशं गता। संविश्य भूमौ कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.57।।
explanation: That beautiful, largeeyed Kaikeyi, puffed with the pride of her intoxicating beauty, encourged and influenced by the words of that hunchback, entered the chamber of wrath. She cast off her highly precious pearl necklace worth many hundreds of thousands (of rupees) and other costly, beautiful ornaments. Thereafter that goldenhued Kaikeyi lay down on the floor and said to Manthara:

shloka_text: तथा प्रोत्साहिता देवी गत्वा मन्थरया सह। क्रोधागारं विशालाक्षी सौभाग्यमदगर्विता।।2.9.55।। अनेकशतसाहस्रं मुक्ताहारं वराङ्गना। अवमुच्य वरार्हाणि शुभान्याभरणानि च।।2.9.56।। ततो हेमोपमा तत्र कुब्जावाक्यवशं गता। संविश्य भूमौ कैकेयी मन्थरामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.9.57।।
explanation: That beautiful, largeeyed Kaikeyi, puffed with the pride of her intoxicating beauty, encourged and influenced by the words of that hunchback, entered the chamber of wrath. She cast off her highly precious pearl necklace worth many hundreds of thousands (of rupees) and other costly, beautiful ornaments. Thereafter that goldenhued Kaikeyi lay down on the floor and said to Manthara:

shloka_text: इह वा मां मृतां कुब्जे नृपायावेदयिष्यसि। वनं तु राघवे प्राप्ते भरतः प्राप्स्यति क्षितिम्।।2.9.58।।
explanation: O hunchback, tell the king, either Bharata shall secure the kingdom on Rama's departure to the forest or else I will die here.

shloka_text: न सुवर्णेन मे ह्यर्थो न रत्नैर्न च भूषणैः। एष मे जीवितस्यान्तो रामो यद्यभिषिच्यते।।2.9.59।।
explanation: I do not aspire for gold, nor gems nor ornaments. If Rama is installed, that will be the end of my life.

shloka_text: अथो पुनस्तां महिषीं महीक्षितो वचोभिरत्यर्थमहापराक्रमैः। उवाच कुब्जा भरतस्य मातरं हितं वचो राममुपेत्य चाहितम्।।2.9.60।।
explanation: Addressing queen Kaikeyi, the mother of Bharata, with extremely powerful words, that hunchback again made these utterances beneficial to Bharata and detrimental to Rama:

shloka_text: प्रपत्स्यते राज्यमिदं हि राघवो यदि ध्रुवं त्वं ससुता च तप्स्यसे। अतो हि कल्याणि यतस्व तत्तथा यथा सुतस्ते भरतोऽभिषेक्ष्यते।।2.9.61।।
explanation: It is true that if Rama secures this kingdom, you along with your son are bound to suffer. O auspicious one, hence act in a way your son Bharata will be installed.

shloka_text: तथाऽतिविद्धा महिषी तु कुब्जया समाहता वागिषुभिर्मुहुर्मुहुः। निधायहस्तौ हृदयेऽतिविस्मिता शशंस कुब्जां कुपिता पुनः पुनः।।2.9.62।।
explanation: Repeatedly struck down by that hunchback's arrowsharp words greatly grieved queen Kaikeyi was inflamed against the king. Laying her hands on the chest again and again and expressing her amazement, she praised that hunchback.

shloka_text: यमस्य वा मां विषयं गतामितो निशाम्य कुब्जे प्रतिवेदयिष्यसि। वनं गते वा सुचिराय राघवे समृद्धकामो भरतो भविष्यति।।2.9.63।।
explanation: Tell the king that he will see either the fulfilment of Bharata's desire after Rama is banished into the forest for a long period or me gone to Yama's abode.

shloka_text: अहं हि नैवास्तरणानि न स्रजो न चन्दनं नाञ्जनपानभोजनम्। न किञ्चिदिच्छामि न चेह जीवितं न चेदितो गच्छति राघवो वनम्।।2.9.64।।
explanation: If Rama does not go from here to the forest, I want neither a bed nor garlands nor sandalpaste nor unguents nor food nor water nor even life.

shloka_text: अथैतदुक्त्वा वचनं सुदारुणं निधाय सर्वाभरणानि भामिनी। असंवृतामास्तरणेन मेदिनीं तदाऽधिशिश्ये पतितेव किन्नरी।।2.9.65।।
explanation: Saying these ruthless words, that lovely Kaikeyi cast off all her ornaments like a fallen  'kinnara' woman, and lay down on the floor with the carpet removed.

shloka_text: उदीर्णसंरम्भतमोवृतानना तथाऽवमुक्तोत्तममाल्यभूषणा। नरेन्द्रपत्नी विमना बभूव सा तमोवृता द्यौरिव मग्नतारका।।2.9.66।।
explanation: Thus queen Kaikeyi's face enveloped by the darkness of violent anger and her body stripped of all valuable ornaments, she lay restless, looking like the dark sky without stars. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे नवमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends of the ninth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विदर्शिता यदा देवी कुब्जया पापया भृशम्। तदा शेते स्म सा भूमौ दिग्धविद्धेव किन्नरी।।2.10.1।।
explanation: Perversely advised by the extremely sinful hunchback the queen (Kaikeyi) lay down on the ground like a kinnari struck as though by a poisonous arrow.

shloka_text: निश्चित्य मनसा कृत्यं सा सम्यगिति भामिनी। मन्थरायै शनैस्सर्वमाचचक्षे विचक्षणा।।2.10.2।।
explanation: The intelligent, beautiful lady (Kaikeyi), having correctly decided the strategy in her mind, slowly unfolded everything to Manthara.

shloka_text: सा दीना निश्चयं कृत्वा मन्थरावाक्यमोहिता। नागकन्येव निश्वस्य दीर्घमुष्णं च भामिनी।।2.10.3।। मुहूर्तं चिन्तयामास मार्गमात्मसुखावहम्।
explanation: That beautiful wretch (Kaikeyi) impressed by the words of Manthara heaved deep, hot sighs like a female serpent and  thought for a while about the means of bringing happiness to herself.

shloka_text: सा सुहृच्चार्थकामा च तं निशम्य सुनिश्चयम्।।2.10.4।। बभूव परमप्रीता सिध्दिं प्राप्येव मन्थरा।
explanation: Manthara, Kaikeyi's friend, too, driven by a strong desire to fulfil her resolve was highly pleased and on hearing the firm determination of Kaikeyi, felt as if the accomplishment of the objective was at hand.

shloka_text: अथ सा रुषिता देवी सम्यक्कृत्वा विनिश्चयम्।।2.10.5।। संविवेशाबला भूमौ निवेश्य भृकुटीं मुखे।
explanation: Then Kaikeyi finally took a firm decision. With a soiled body and a frowning face she lay down on the floor.

shloka_text: ततश्चित्राणि माल्यानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च।।2.10.6।। अपविद्धानि कैकेय्या तानि भूमिं प्रपेदिरे।
explanation: Thereafter Kaikeyi flung away her multicoloured garlands along with her costly ornaments on to the ground.

shloka_text: तया तान्यपविद्धानि माल्यान्याभरणानि च।।2.10.7।। अशोभयन्त वसुधां नक्षत्राणि यथा नभः।
explanation: All the garlands and ornaments she scattered adorned the floor like the stars (illumining) the sky.

shloka_text: क्रोधागारे निपतिता सा बभौ मलिनाम्बरा।।2.10.8।। एकवेणीं दृढं बद्वा गतसत्त्वेव किन्नरी।
explanation: Tightly fastening her hair into a single braid and wearing soiled clothes, she lay down in the chamber of wrath in a lifeless state like a kinnari.

shloka_text: आज्ञाप्य च महाराजो राघवस्याभिषेचनम्।।2.10.9।। उपस्थानमनुज्ञाप्य प्रविवेश निवेशनम्।
explanation: The king issued orders for Rama's installation ceremony, and taking leave of his close associates entered the palace.                        .

shloka_text: अद्य रामाभिषेको वै प्रसिद्ध इति जज्ञिवान्।।2.10.10।। प्रियार्हां प्रियमाख्यातुं विवेशान्तःपुरं वशी।
explanation: Aware of the fact that Rama's installation ceremony was known to everybody by then he who had subdued his senses entered the inner apartment to convey it to one worthy of such pleasant news.

shloka_text: स कैकेय्या गृहं श्रेष्ठं प्रविवेश महायशाः।।2.10.11।। पाण्डुराभ्रमिवाकाशं राहुयुक्तं निशाकरः।
explanation: The illustrious king entered the excellent abode of Kaikeyi like the Moon entering the mouth of Rahu in a sky overcast with pale clouds.

shloka_text: शुकबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टं क्रौञ्चहंसरुतायुतम्।।2.10.12।। वादित्ररवसङ्घुष्टं कुब्जा वामनिकायुतम्। लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्चम्पकाशोकशोभितैः।।2.10.13।। दान्तराजतसौवर्णवेदिकाभि स्समायुतम्। नित्यपुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैर्वापीभिश्चोपशोभितम्।।2.10.14।। दान्तरजतसौवर्णैस्संवृतं परमासनैः। विविधैरन्नपानैश्च भक्ष्यैश्च विविधैरपि।।2.10.15।। उपपन्नं महार्हैश्च भूषितैस्त्रिदिवोपमम्। तत्प्रविश्य महाराजस्स्वमन्तः पुरमृद्धिमत्।।2.10.16।। न ददर्श प्रियां राजा कैकेयीं शयनोत्तमे।
explanation: The maharaja entered the inner apartment of Kaikeyi's prosperous abode filled with parrots and peacocks, reverberating with cries of kraunchas and swans and sounds of musical instruments attended with hunchbacks and dwarfs decorated with champak and ashoka trees, bowers surrounded with creepers, picturegalleries, altars and sofas embellished with ivory, gold and silver. It was shining with pools and trees bearing flowers and fruits in all seasons. Various kinds of food, drinks and eatables were kept ready. With excellent decorations that abode of Kaikeyi resembled heaven. (But) the king did not see his beloved Kaikeyi in her best bed.

shloka_text: शुकबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टं क्रौञ्चहंसरुतायुतम्।।2.10.12।। वादित्ररवसङ्घुष्टं कुब्जा वामनिकायुतम्। लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्चम्पकाशोकशोभितैः।।2.10.13।। दान्तराजतसौवर्णवेदिकाभि स्समायुतम्। नित्यपुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैर्वापीभिश्चोपशोभितम्।।2.10.14।। दान्तरजतसौवर्णैस्संवृतं परमासनैः। विविधैरन्नपानैश्च भक्ष्यैश्च विविधैरपि।।2.10.15।। उपपन्नं महार्हैश्च भूषितैस्त्रिदिवोपमम्। तत्प्रविश्य महाराजस्स्वमन्तः पुरमृद्धिमत्।।2.10.16।। न ददर्श प्रियां राजा कैकेयीं शयनोत्तमे।

shloka_text: कामबलसंयुक्तो रत्यर्थं मनुजाधिपः।।2.10.17।। अपश्यन्दयितां भार्यां पप्रच्छ विषसाद च।
explanation: Charged with passion and seeking carnal pleasure, the king became dejected when he did not see his beloved wife. He enquired about her.

shloka_text: न हि तस्य पुरा देवी तां वेलामत्यवर्तत।।2.10.18।। न च राजा गृहं शून्यं प्रविवेश कदाचन।
explanation: Never before had queen Kaikeyi missed his time of arrival. Nor had the king ever entered her empty apartment.

shloka_text: ततो गृहगतो राजा कैकेयीं पर्यपृच्छत।।2.10.19।। यथा पूर्वमविज्ञाय स्वार्थलिप्सुमपण्डिताम्।
explanation: Having entered her apartment, the king, unaware of that foolish Kaikeyi's selfish design enquired her whereabouts as usual.

shloka_text: प्रतीहारी त्वथोवाच सन्त्रस्ता सुकृताञ्जलिः।।2.10.20।। देव देवी भृशं कृद्धा क्रोधागारमभिदृता।
explanation: Thereafter, the frightened doorkeeper with folded palms said O monarch the queen in a hot mood has rushed into the chamber of wrath.

shloka_text: प्रतीहार्या वचश्शृत्वा राजा परमदुर्मनाः।।2.10.21।। विषसाद पुनर्भूयो लुलितव्याकुलेन्द्रियः।।
explanation: Hearing the words of the doorkeeper, the melancholic king grieved all the more with his senses agitated and unstable.

shloka_text: तत्र तां पतितां भूमौ शयानामतथोचिताम्।।2.10.22।। प्रतप्त इव दुःखेन सोऽपश्यज्जगतीपतिः।
explanation: The lord of the earth (Dasaratha) saw her (Kaikeyi) lying down on the floor of the chamber of wrath in an unbecoming manner and felt as if consumed by grief.

shloka_text: स वृद्धस्तरुणीं भार्यां प्राणेभ्योपि गरीयसीम्।।2.10.23।। अपापः पापसङ्कल्पां ददर्श धरणीतले। लतामिव विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां देवतामिव।।2.10.24।। किन्नरीमिव निर्धूतां च्युतामप्सरसं यथा। मायामिव परिभ्रष्टां हरिणीमिव संयताम्।।2.10.25।।
explanation: The guileless, old king beheld his youthful wife who was dearer to him than his own life, filled with deceitful  intentions. She looked like a severed creeper, like a goddess fallen down, like a 'Kinnari' thrown down on earth, like an 'apsarasa' slipped from heaven, like an illusion torn, like a female deer tied down.

shloka_text: स वृद्धस्तरुणीं भार्यां प्राणेभ्योपि गरीयसीम्।।2.10.23।। अपापः पापसङ्कल्पां ददर्श धरणीतले। लतामिव विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां देवतामिव।।2.10.24।। किन्नरीमिव निर्धूतां च्युतामप्सरसं यथा। मायामिव परिभ्रष्टां हरिणीमिव संयताम्।।2.10.25।।
explanation: The guileless, old king beheld his youthful wife who was dearer to him than his own life, filled with deceitful  intentions. She looked like a severed creeper, like a goddess fallen down, like a 'Kinnari' thrown down on earth, like an 'apsarasa' slipped from heaven, like an illusion torn, like a female deer tied down.
