explanation: When will the city of Ayodhya attain that glory when having heard that both the brave brothers have come back the people will rejoice and fill it with uplifted banners?

shloka_text: कदा प्रेक्ष्य नरव्याघ्रावरण्यात्पुनरागतौ। नन्दिष्यति पुरी हृष्टा समुद्र इव पर्वणि।।2.43.11।।
explanation: When will, like the swelling sea on a full Moon day, the city hail the return of Rama and Lakshmana, the best among men?

shloka_text: कदाऽयोध्यां महाबाहुः पुरीं वीरः प्रवेक्ष्यति। पुरस्कृत्य रथे सीतां वृषभो गोवधूमिव।।2.43.12।।
explanation: When will the mightyarmed hero (Rama) enter the city of Ayodhya with Sita in front in the chariot, like a bull following the cow?

shloka_text: कदा प्राणिसहस्राणि राजमार्गे ममात्मजौ। लाजैरवकिरिष्यन्ति प्रविशन्तावरिन्दमौ।।2.43.13।।
explanation: When will the people in their thousands shower the parched grain on the highway when my sons (Rama and Lakshmana), subduers of enemies, enter the city?

shloka_text: प्रविशन्तौ कदाऽयोध्यां द्रक्ष्यामि शुभकुण्डलौ। उदग्रायुधनिस्त्रिंशौ सश्रृङ्गाविव पर्वतौ।।2.43.14।।
explanation: When shall I see both of them wearing auspicious earrings and holding poweful weapons (bows) and swords high, like two mountain peaks?

shloka_text: कदासुमनसः कन्याद्विजातीनां फलानि च। प्रदिशन्तः पुरीं हृष्टाः करिष्यन्ति प्रदक्षिणम्।।2.43.15।।
explanation: When will I see them delightfully moving round the city with young brahmin girls offering them flowers and fruits.

shloka_text: कदा परिणतो बुद्ध्या वयसा चामरप्रभः। अभ्युपैष्यति धर्मज्ञस्त्रिवर्ष इव मां ललन्।।2.43.16।।
explanation: When will Rama, the knower of righteousness, possessing the lustre of gods, and fully mature in age and wisdom come back to me playfully like a threeyearold boy?

shloka_text: निस्संशयं मया मन्ये पुरा वीर कदर्यया। पातुकामेषु वत्सेषु मातृ़णां शातितास्स्तनाः।।2.43.17।।
explanation: O valiant one, in my previous birth I must have undoubtedly hacked off the udders of cows when the calves were thirsting for milk from their mothers.

shloka_text: साहं गौरिव सिंहेन विवत्सा वत्सला कृता। कैकेय्या पुरुषव्याघ्र बालवत्सेव गौर्बलात्।।2.43.18।।
explanation: O best of men I have been forcibly separated from my affectionate son by Kaikeyi just like a cow from its calf by a lion.

shloka_text: न हि तावद्गुणैर्जुष्टं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम्। एकपुत्रा विना पुत्रमहं जीवितुमुत्सहे।।2.43.19।।
explanation: I cannot live without my only son who is adept in all scriptures and endowed with all virtues.

shloka_text: न हि मे जीविते किञ्चित्सामर्थ्यमिह कल्प्यते। अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियं पुत्रं महाबाहुं महाबलम्।।2.43.20।।
explanation: Without seeing my beloved son, longarmed and mighty, I have but little strength to live in this world.

shloka_text: अयं हि मां दीपयते समुत्थितः तनूजशोकप्रभवो हुताशनः। महीमिमां रश्मिभिरुद्धतप्रभः यथा निदाघे भगवान् दिवाकरः।।2.43.21।।
explanation: I am consumed by this blazing fire of grief caused by separation from my son like the earth scorched in summer by the Sungod with his oppressive rays इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortythird sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विलपन्ती तथा तां तु कौसल्यां प्रमदोत्तमाम्। इदं धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यं सुमित्रा वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.44.1।।
explanation: While Kausalya, the best of women was thus lamenting, virtuous Sumitra spoke to her these righteous words:

shloka_text: तवार्ये सद्गुणैर्युक्तः पुत्र स्स पुरुषोत्तमः। किं ते विलपितेनैवं कृपणं रुदितेन वा।।2.44.2।।
explanation: My venerable lady, your son Rama is the greatest among men and is endowed with every virtue. Why do you lament in this way? Why do you weep bitterly?

shloka_text: यस्तवार्ये गतः पुत्रस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं महाबलः। साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानं पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।।2.44.3।। शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्छश्वत्प्रेत्यफलोदये। रामो धर्मे स्थित श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन।।2.44.4।।
explanation: In order to vindicate the words of his great and truthful father, O noble lady,your mighty son has renounced the kingdom and has gone (to the forest). He has stuck to the path so scrupulously followed by the wise, the everlasting results of which can be fully realised in the world to come. Such a peerless son is never to be grieved over.

shloka_text: यस्तवार्ये गतः पुत्रस्त्यक्त्वा राज्यं महाबलः। साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानं पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।।2.44.3।। शिष्टैराचरिते सम्यक्छश्वत्प्रेत्यफलोदये। रामो धर्मे स्थित श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन।।2.44.4।।
explanation: In order to vindicate the words of his great and truthful father, O noble lady,your mighty son has renounced the kingdom and has gone (to the forest). He has stuck to the path so scrupulously followed by the wise, the everlasting results of which can be fully realised in the world to come. Such a peerless son is never to be grieved over.

shloka_text: वर्तते चोत्तमां वृत्तिं लक्ष्मणोऽस्मिन् सदानघः। दयावान् सर्वभूतेषु लाभस्तस्य महात्मनः।।2.44.5।।
explanation: Blameless Lakshmana, compassionate to all beings, has acted most nobly in this matter for the benefit of his great soul.

shloka_text: अरण्यवासे यद्दुःखं जानती वै सुखोचिता। अनुगच्छति वैदेही धर्मात्मानं तवात्मजम्।।2.44.6।।
explanation: The daughter of Videha (Sita) who was used to comforts has knowingly followed your virtuous son into the hardships of forest life.

shloka_text: कीर्तिभूतां पताकां यो लोके भ्रमयति प्रभुः। धर्मसत्यव्रतधनः किं न प्राप्तस्तवात्मजः।।2.44.7।।
explanation: Your allcompetent son who considers righteousness and truth as wealth, is waving  the flag of fame in this world. What is that which your son did not gain ?

shloka_text: व्यक्तं रामस्य विज्ञाय शौचं माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्। न गात्रमंशुभि स्सूर्य स्सन्तापयितुमर्हति।।2.44.8।।
explanation: Knowing Rama's sterling purity and greatness the Sun evidently dare not scorch his body with its rays.

shloka_text: शिवस्सर्वेषु कालेषु काननेभ्यो विनिस्सृतः। राघवं युक्तशीतोष्णस्सेविष्यति सुखोऽनिलः।।2.44.9।।
explanation: A pleasant yet moderately hot and cold breeze blowing through the woodlands will serve Rama at all seasons.

shloka_text: शयानमनघं रात्रौ पितेवाभिपरिष्वजन्। रश्मिभि स्संस्पृशन् शीतैश्चन्द्रमाह्लादयिष्यति।।2.44.10।।
explanation: While that sinless Rama sleeps at night, the Moon will comfort him by touching him with cool beams like a father embracing his son.

shloka_text: ददौ चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि यस्मै ब्रह्मा महौजसे। दानवेन्द्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा तिमिध्वजसुतं रणे।।2.44.11।। स शूरः पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः। असन्त्रस्तोऽप्यरणस्थो वेश्मनीव निवत्स्यति।।2.44.12।।
explanation: To the mighty, heroic Rama, that best of men, Brahmalike Viswamitra has bequeathed many divine weapons, seeing him slay Timidhwaja's son (Subahu), lord of demons, in the battle. He will stay fearless in the forest, relying on the strength of his own arms as though he were living in the palace.

shloka_text: ददौ चास्त्राणि दिव्यानि यस्मै ब्रह्मा महौजसे। दानवेन्द्रं हतं दृष्ट्वा तिमिध्वजसुतं रणे।।2.44.11।। स शूरः पुरुषव्याघ्रः स्वबाहुबलमाश्रितः। असन्त्रस्तोऽप्यरणस्थो वेश्मनीव निवत्स्यति।।2.44.12।।
explanation: To the mighty, heroic Rama, that best of men, Brahmalike Viswamitra has bequeathed many divine weapons, seeing him slay Timidhwaja's son (Subahu), lord of demons, in the battle. He will stay fearless in the forest, relying on the strength of his own arms as though he were living in the palace.

shloka_text: यस्येषुपथमासाद्य विनाशं यान्ति शत्रवः। कथं न पृथिवी तस्य शासने स्थातुमर्हति।।2.44.13।।
explanation: When enemies who are targets of his arrows are destoyed, how can this earth, not stay under the command of Rama?

shloka_text: या श्री श्शौर्यं च रामस्य या च कल्याणसत्वता। निवृत्तारण्यवास स्स क्षिप्रं राज्यमवाप्स्यति।।2.44.14।।
explanation: On return from his sojourn in the forest, Rama, endowed with splendour, valour and a strength that brings wellbeing will quickly regain his kingdom.

shloka_text: सूर्यस्यापि भवेत्सूर्यो ह्यग्नेरग्नि प्रभोः प्रभुः। श्रियः श्रीश्च भवेदग्र्या कीर्तिः कीर्त्याः क्षमाक्षमा।।2.44.15।। दैवतं दैवतानां च भूतानां भूतसत्तमः। तस्य के ह्यगुणा देवि वने वाप्यथवा पुरे।।2.44.16।।
explanation: O Devi Rama is the Sun (light) of the Sun, fire (splendour) of the fire, master (command) of masters, prosperity of the prosperous, the fame of the famous, forbearance of the forbearing, god of the gods and supreme among all beings. Whether he dwells in the forest or in the city, he has no demerit whatsoever.

shloka_text: सूर्यस्यापि भवेत्सूर्यो ह्यग्नेरग्नि प्रभोः प्रभुः। श्रियः श्रीश्च भवेदग्र्या कीर्तिः कीर्त्याः क्षमाक्षमा।।2.44.15।। दैवतं दैवतानां च भूतानां भूतसत्तमः। तस्य के ह्यगुणा देवि वने वाप्यथवा पुरे।।2.44.16।।
explanation: O Devi Rama is the Sun (light) of the Sun, fire (splendour) of the fire, master (command) of masters, prosperity of the prosperous, the fame of the famous, forbearance of the forbearing, god of the gods and supreme among all beings. Whether he dwells in the forest or in the city, he has no demerit whatsoever.

shloka_text: पृथिव्या सह वैदेह्या श्रिया च पुरुषर्षभः। क्षिप्रं तिसृभिरेताभि स्सह रामोऽभिषेक्ष्यते।।2.44.17।।
explanation: Rama, the best among men, will soon be coronated with these three namely the earth, the goddess of fortune and Sita.

shloka_text: दुःखजं विसृजन्त्यस्रं निष्क्रामन्तमुदीक्ष्य यम्। अयोध्यायां जनास्सर्वे शोकवेगसमाहताः।2.44.18।। कुशचीरधरं देवं गच्छन्तमपराजितम्। सीतेवानुगता लक्ष्मी स्तस्य किं नाम दुर्लभम्।।2.44.19।।
explanation: When the people of Ayodhya saw the godlike Rama departing, clad in robes of kusha and bark, they were moved to tears of grief. What is impossible for him who is unconquerable and whom Sita, like the goddess of fortune, follows.

shloka_text: दुःखजं विसृजन्त्यस्रं निष्क्रामन्तमुदीक्ष्य यम्। अयोध्यायां जनास्सर्वे शोकवेगसमाहताः।2.44.18।। कुशचीरधरं देवं गच्छन्तमपराजितम्। सीतेवानुगता लक्ष्मी स्तस्य किं नाम दुर्लभम्।।2.44.19।।
explanation: When the people of Ayodhya saw the godlike Rama departing, clad in robes of kusha and bark, they were moved to tears of grief. What is impossible for him who is unconquerable and whom Sita, like the goddess of fortune, follows.

shloka_text: धनुर्ग्रहवरो यस्य बाणखड्गास्त्रभृत्स्वयम्। लक्ष्मणो व्रजति ह्यग्रे तस्य किं नाम दुर्लभम्।।2.44.20।।
explanation: What is impossible for Rama ahead of whom moves Lakshmana, the best of archers, weilding swords, arrows and other weapons?

shloka_text: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहिशोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते।।2.44.21।।
explanation: I tell you the truth, Kausalya, that you will see Rama's return when the period of exile is complete. Hence give up your sorrow and delusion.

shloka_text: शिरसा चरणावेतौ वन्दमानमनिन्दिते पुनर्द्रक्ष्यसि कल्याणि पुत्रं चन्द्रमिवोदितम्।।2.44.22।।
explanation: O irreproachable and auspicious one you will see your son, like the rising Moon, touching your feet with his head.

shloka_text: पुनः प्रविष्टं दृष्ट्वा तमभिषिक्तं महाश्रियम्। समुत्स्रक्ष्यसि नेत्राभ्यां क्षिप्रमानन्दजं पयः।।2.44.23।।
explanation: Soon you will see him enthrouned shining in full glory on his return from exile while tears of joy will flow from your eyes.

shloka_text: मा शोको देवि दुःखं वा न रामे दृश्यतेऽशिवम्। क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि पुत्रं त्वं ससीतं सहलक्ष्मणम्।।2.44.24।।
explanation: Desist from grief or tear for Rama, O Devi nothing inauspicious will happen to him you will soon see your son along with Sita and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: त्वया शेषो जनश्चैव समाश्वास्यो यदाऽनघे। किमिदानीमिदं देवि करोषि हृदि विक्लबम्।।2.44.25।।
explanation: O sinless lady, O queen when you are overcome by fear, how can you console others?

shloka_text: नार्हा त्वं शोचितुं देवि यस्यास्ते राघवस्सुतः। न हि रामात्परो लोके विद्यते सत्पथे स्थितः।।2.44.26।।
explanation: O Kausalya,  with a son like Rama, you should not grieve. There is none in this world superior to Rama who stands steady in the path of virtue.

shloka_text: अभिवादयमानं तं दृष्ट्वा ससुहृदं सुतम्। मुदाऽश्रृ मोक्ष्यसे क्षिप्रं मेघलेखेव वार्षिकी।।2.44.27।।
explanation: Like a flake of cloud in monsoon, you are going to shed tears of joy soon seeing your son along with his friends bowing to you in reverence.

shloka_text: पुत्रस्ते वरदः क्षिप्रमयोध्यां पुनरागतः। पाणिभ्यां मृदुपीनाभ्यां चरणौ पीडयिष्यति।।2.44.28।।
explanation: Your son, bestower of boons, will soon return to Ayodhya and press your feet with his soft, tender hands.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य नमस्यन्तं शूरं ससुहृदं सुतम्। मुदाऽस्रैः प्रोक्ष्यसि पुनर्मेघराजिरिवाचलम्।।2.44.29।।
explanation: While paying obeisance to you, you will drench your brave son, surrounded by friends, with tears of joy like a mass of clouds drenching the mountain.

shloka_text: आश्वासयन्ती विविधैश्च वाक्यै र्वाक्योपचारे कुशलाऽनवद्या। रामस्य तां मातरमेवमुक्त्वा देवी सुमित्रा विरराम रामा।।2.44.30।।
explanation: Irreproachable and skilful in the use of words, queen Sumitra of cheerful disposition fell silent after thus consoling Rama's mother in various ways.

shloka_text: निशम्य तल्लक्ष्मणमातृवाक्यं रामस्य मातुर्नरदेवपत्न्या:। सद्यश्शरीरे विननाश शोकः शरद्गतो मेघ इवाल्पतोयः।।2.44.31।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Lakshmana's mother the grief in the heart of the queen (Kausalya), mother of Rama, instantly disappeared like the autumnal cloud that holds but little rain. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfourth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अनुरक्ता महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम्। अनुजग्मुः प्रयान्तं तं वनवासाय मानवाः।।2.45.1।।
explanation: When the highsouled Rama whose strength was his sense of truth set out for the forest, the faithful people followed him.

shloka_text: निवर्तितेऽपि च बलात्सुहृद्वर्गे च राजनि। नैव ते संन्यवर्तन्त रामस्यानुगता रथम्।।2.45.2।।
explanation: The king and the hosts of friends were forcibly sent back but they did not return. They continued to follow the chariot of Rama.

shloka_text: अयोध्यानिलयानां हि पुरुषाणां महायशाः। बभूव गुणसम्पन्नः पूर्णचन्द्र इव प्रियः।।2.45.3।।
explanation: The illustrious and virtuous Rama was as dear to the inhabitants of Ayodhya as the full Moon.

shloka_text: स याच्यमानः काकुत्स्थः स्वाभिः प्रकृतिभिस्तदा। कुर्वाणः पितरं सत्यं वनमेवान्वपद्यत।।2.45.4।।
explanation: Although entreated by his subjects (not to go) Rama proceeded to the forest  to make his father's vow come true.

shloka_text: अवेक्षमाणः सस्नेहं चक्षुषा प्रपिबन्निव। उवाच रामः स्नेहेन ताः प्रजाः स्वाः प्रजा इव।।2.45.5।।
explanation: Looking at the people with love as if they were his own children and as though drinking them with his glances, Rama appealed to them:

shloka_text: या प्रीतिर्बहुमानश्च मय्ययोध्यानिवासिनाम्। मत्प्रियार्थं विशेषेण भरते सा निवेश्यताम्।।2.45.6।।
explanation: O citizens of Ayodhya may the love and respect you have shown to please me be bestowed specially on Bharata

shloka_text: स हि कल्याणचारित्रः कैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनः। करिष्यति यथावद्वः प्रियाणि च हितानि च।।2.45.7।।
explanation: Bharata, enhancer of the delight of Kaikeyi, possesses an auspicious character. He will do for you everything appropriate, agreeable and beneficial.

shloka_text: ज्ञानवृद्धो वयोबालो मृदुर्वीर्यगुणान्वितः। अनुरूपः स वो भर्ता भविष्यति भयापहः।।2.45.8।।
explanation: Though tender in age Bharata is mature in intellect. Gentle, valiant and virtuous, he will dispel all your fears and act as a true protector.

shloka_text: स हि राजगुणैर्युक्तो युवराजः समीक्षितः। अपि चापि मया शिष्टैः कार्यं वो भर्तृशासनम्।।2.45.9।।
explanation: Endowed with kingly qualities, he is recognised as heirapparent. Therefore, as I did, all of  you should obey the order of the king.

shloka_text: न च सन्तप्येद्यथा चासौ वनवासं गते मयि। महाराजस्तथा कार्यो मम प्रियचिकीर्षया।।2.45.10।।
explanation: If you desire to please me, act in such a way that the king does not grieve after I have gone to the forest.

shloka_text: यथा यथा दाशरथि र्धर्म एवास्थितोऽभवत्। तथा तथा प्रकृतयो रामं पतिमकामयन्।।2.45.11।।
explanation: The more the son of Dasaratha (Rama) committed to righteousness, the more the subjects desired that he should be their king.

shloka_text: बाष्पेण पिहितं दीनं रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। चकर्षेव गुणैर्बद्ध्वा जनं पुरनिवासिनम्।।2.45.12।।
explanation: Rama along with Lakshmana attracted the citydwellers who, choked with tears, were looking miserable. It appeared they were bound with his virtues.

shloka_text: ते द्विजास्त्रिविधं वृद्धा ज्ञानेन वयसौजसा। वयः प्रकम्पशिरसो दूरादूचुरिदं वचः।।2.45.13।।
explanation: Those brahmins who were senior (to him) on three counts like age, wisdom and spirtuality spoke to him from a distance with their heads shaking with age:

shloka_text: वहन्तो जवना रामं भो भो जात्यास्तुरङ्गमाः। निवर्तध्वं न गन्तव्यं हिता भवत भर्तरि।।2.45.14।।
explanation: O horses of noble breed, turn back Do not carry your master swiftyly any farther. Do good to him.

shloka_text: कर्णवन्ति हि भूतानि विशेषेण तुरङ्गमाः। यूयं तस्मान्निवर्तध्वं याचनां प्रतिवेदिताः।।2.45.15।।
explanation: All animals, especially horses have a keen sense of hearing. Therefore, having listened to our entreaty, turn back.

shloka_text: धर्मतः स विशुद्धात्मा वीरः शुभदृढव्रतः। उपवाह्यस्तु वो भर्ता नापवाह्यः पुराद्वनम्।।2.45.16।।
explanation: Your master has a purity of heart. He is righteous, virtuous, brave and firm in resolve, carry him backward and not forward from the city into the forest.

shloka_text: एवमार्तप्रलापांस्तान् वृद्धान् प्रलपतो द्विजान्। अवेक्ष्य सहसा रामो रथादवततार ह।।2.45.17।।
explanation: Having seen the aged brahmins muttering pitiful lamentations in this manner, Rama immediately alighted from the chariot.

shloka_text: पद्भ्यामेव जगामाथ ससीत स्सहलक्ष्मणः। सन्निकृष्टपदन्यासो रामो वनपरायणः।।2.45.18।।
explanation: Then Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana began walking on foot with slow steps towards the forest.

shloka_text: द्विजातींस्तु पदातींस्तान् रामश्चारित्रवत्सलः। न शशाक घृणाचक्षुः परिमोक्तुं रथेन सः।।2.45.19।।
explanation: Rama a man of probity and compassion could not ride off in his chariot while those brahmins were trudging far behind.

shloka_text: गच्छन्तमेव तं दृष्ट्वा रामं सम्भ्रान्तचेतसः। ऊचुः परमसन्तप्ता रामं वाक्यमिदं द्विजाः।।2.45.20।।
explanation: Having seen Rama thus going towards the forest, those brahmins, highly agitated and distressed, said to him:

shloka_text: ब्राह्मण्यं सर्वमेतत्त्वां ब्रह्मण्यमनुगच्छति। द्विजस्कन्धाधिरूढास्त्वामग्नयोऽप्यनुयान्त्यमी।।2.45.21।।
explanation: This entire order of brahmins with the sacrificial fires on their hsoulders is following you, their wellwisher.

shloka_text: वाजपेयसमुत्थानि छत्राण्येतानि पश्य नः। पृष्ठतोऽनुप्रयातानि मेघानिव जलात्यये।।2.45.22।।
explanation: See these umbrellas acquired by us while performing Vajapeya sacrifice are following you like the clouds at the end of the rainy season.

shloka_text: अनवाप्तातपत्रस्य रश्मिसन्तापितस्य ते। एभिश्छायां करिष्यामः स्वैश्छत्रैर्वाजपेयिकैः।।2.45.23।।
explanation: You do not have a royal umbrella and you are scorched by the rays of the Sun. We will offer you shade with the umbrellas acquired during Vajapeya sacrifice.

shloka_text: या हि नः सततं बुद्धिर्वेदमन्त्रानुसारिणी। त्वत्कृते सा कृता वत्स वनवासानुसारिणी।।2.45.24।।
explanation: O dear child, our minds always pursue the study of vedic hymns. For your sake now they are made to follow the life in the forest.

shloka_text: हृदयेष्वेव तिष्ठन्ति वेदा ये नः परं धनम्। वत्स्यन्त्यपि गृहेष्वेव दाराश्चारित्ररक्षिताः।।2.45.25।।
explanation: The Vedas are our greatest wealth and they reside in our hearts. Our wives, protected by their fidelity, shall stay at home.

shloka_text: न पुनर्निश्चयः कार्यस्त्वद्गतौ सुकृता मतिः। त्वयि धर्मव्यपेक्षे तु किं स्याद्धर्मपथे स्थितम्।।2.45.26।।
explanation: We are not going to revoke our decision. We have made up our minds to follow you (into the forest). If you have no regard for this decision, then who will adhere to the path of righteousness?

shloka_text: याचितो नो निवर्तस्व हंसशुक्लशिरोरुहैः। शिरोभिर्निभृताचार महीपतनपांसुलैः।।2.45.27।।
explanation: O Rama, you are firm in your duty.We beseech you, our heads bowed with swanwhite hair and soiled with dust, to return to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: बहूनां वितता यज्ञा द्विजानां य इहागताः। तेषां समाप्तिरायत्ता तव वत्स निवर्तने।।2.45.28।।
explanation: Many of those brahmins who arrived here have commenced their sacrifices. O dear child, their consummation depends on your return.

shloka_text: भक्तिमन्ति हि भूतानि जङ्गमाजङ्गमानि च। याचमानेषु राम त्वं भक्तिं भक्तेषु दर्शय।।2.45.29।।
explanation: O Rama, all these living beings, movable and immovable, are devoted to you and are entreating you with devotion to return. Show consideration to those supplicants.

shloka_text: अनुगन्तुमशक्ता स्त्वां मूलैरुद्धतवेगिनः। उन्नता वायुवेगेन विक्रोशन्तीव पादपाः।।2.45.30।।
explanation: Although the trees uplifted by the speed of the wind, intend to follow you, their movement is stalled by their roots. Unable, they appear to be weeping.

shloka_text: निश्चेष्टाहारसञ्चारा वृक्षैकस्थानविष्ठिताः। पक्षिणोऽपि प्रयाचन्ते सर्वभूतानुकम्पिनम्।।2.45.31।।
explanation: Even the birds instead of foraging for food are sitting motionless on the trees at one place. They are imploring you, you who are compassionate to all creatures, to return to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: एवं विक्रोशतां तेषां द्विजातीनां निवर्तने। ददृशे तमसा तत्र वारयन्तीव राघवम्।।2.45.32।।
explanation: While those brahmins were thus crying out, river Tamasa came into view as if seeking  Rama to turn back to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: ततः सुमन्त्रोऽपि रथाद्विमुच्य श्रान्तान्हयान्सम्परिवर्त्य शीघ्रम्। पीतोदकांस्तोयपरिप्लुताङ्गा नचारयद्वै तमसाविदूरे।।2.45.33।।
explanation: Then Sumantra also unyoked the fatigued horses from the chariot and quickly allowed  them to roll and relax on the ground. Having made the horses drink and dip in water, he released them for grazing not far from Tamasa river. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyfifth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्तु तमसातीरं रम्यमाश्रित्य राघवः। सीतामुद्वीक्ष्य सौमित्रिमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.46.1।।
explanation: The scion of the Raghus (Rama), having taken shelter on the lovely bank of Tamasa, glanced at Sita and said to Lakshmana thus:

shloka_text: इयमद्य निशा पूर्वा सौमित्रे प्रहिता वनम्। वनवासस्य भद्रं ते स नोत्कण्ठितुमर्हसि।।2.46.2।।
explanation: O Lakshmana, this happens to be the first night of our exile. You should not have any longing in your mind. Wish you well

shloka_text: पश्य शून्यान्यरण्यानि रुदन्तीव समन्ततः। यथानिलयमायद्भिर्निलीनानि मृगद्विजैः।।2.46.3।।
explanation: Look at the deserted forest. The wild animals and birds have returned to their hideouts. They fill the air with their cries.

shloka_text: अद्यायोध्या तु नगरी राजधानी पितुर्मम। सस्त्रीपुंसा गतानस्माञ्शोचिष्यति न संशयः।।2.46.4।।
explanation: There is no doubt that now the men and women of Ayodhya, father's capital city must be bewailing our departure.

shloka_text: अनुरक्ता हि मनुजा राजानं बहुभिर्गुणैः। त्वां च मां च नरव्याघ्र शत्रुघ्न भरतौ तथा।।2.46.5।।
explanation: O best of men because of our many virtues, the people (of Ayodhya) are indeed loyal to the king, to you, to me and to Satrughna and Bharata, too.

shloka_text: पितरं चानुशोचामि मातरं च यशस्विनीम्। अपि वान्धौ भवेतां तु रुदन्तौ तावभीक्ष्णशः।।2.46.6।।
explanation: What distresses me is the thought that both father and illustrious mother may become blind by repeated weeping (over us).

shloka_text: भरतः खलु धर्मात्मा पितरं मातरं च मे। धर्मार्थकामसहितैर्वाक्यैर्वाश्वासयिष्यति।।2.46.7।।
explanation: Righteous Bharata will indeed console parents with words in conformity with  dharma, artha and kama.

shloka_text: भरतस्यानृशंसत्वं विचिन्त्याहं पुनः पुनः। नानुशोचामि पितरं मातरं चापि लक्ष्मण।।2.46.8।।
explanation: As I reflect again and again on the benevolent nature of Bharata, there is no concern in me about my parents, O Lakshmana

shloka_text: त्वया कार्यं नरव्याघ्र मामनुव्रजता कृतम्। अन्वेष्टव्या हि वैदेह्या रक्षणार्थे सहायता।।2.46.9।।
explanation: You, O Lakshmana, the best among men, have done a good job by accompanying me. Otherwise assistance for Sita's protection would have been sought (necessary).

shloka_text: अद्भिरेव तु सौमित्रे वत्स्याम्यद्य निशामिमाम्। एतध्दि रोचते मह्यं वन्येऽपि विविधे सति।।2.46.10।।
explanation: O Lakshmana, I shall live this night on water alone. I prefer it, though various kinds of forest products are available.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु सौमित्रिं सुमन्त्रमपि राघवः। अप्रमत्तस्त्वमश्वेषु भव सौम्येत्युवाच ह।।2.46.11।।
explanation: Having said so to Lakshmana, he turned to Sumantra to say O gentle friend, tend the horses with care.

shloka_text: सोऽश्वान्सुमन्त्रः संयम्य सूर्येऽस्तं समुपागते। प्रभूतयवसान् कृत्वा बभूव प्रत्यनन्तरः।।2.46.12।।
explanation: As the Sun was setting, Sumantra tethered the horses, fed them with abundant fodder and sat close to them.

shloka_text: उपास्य तु शिवां सन्ध्यां दृष्ट्वा रात्रिमुपस्थिताम्। रामस्य शयनं चक्रे सूतः सौमित्रिणा सह।।2.46.13।।
explanation: Then the charioteer worshipping the auspicious Sandhya (twilight), and seeing the night approach made  bed for Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तां शय्यां तमसातीरे वीक्ष्य वृक्षदलैः कृताम्। रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सभार्यस्संविवेश ह।।2.46.14।।
explanation: Having seen the bed of leaves made ready on the bank of Tamasa, Rama lay down there along with Sita and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सभार्यं सम्प्रसुप्तं तं भ्रातरं वीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः। कथयामास सूताय रामस्य विविधान् गुणान्।।2.46.15।।
explanation: Having seen that his brother along with his wife had fallen asleep, Lakshmana narrated the many virtues of Rama to Sumantra.

shloka_text: जाग्रतो ह्येव तां रात्रिं सौमित्रेरुदितो रविः। सूतस्य तमसातीरे रामस्य ब्रुवतो गुणान्।।2.46.16।।
explanation: Lakshmana continued to describe Rama's virtues to the charioteer, keeping awake that entire night on the bank of Tamasa until the Sun rose.

shloka_text: गोकुलाकुलतीरायास्तमसाया विदूरतः। अवसत्तत्र तां रात्रिं रामः प्रकृतिभिस्सह।।2.46.17।।
explanation: Rama spent the night with his subjects not very far from the bank of Tamasa which was crowded with herds of cattle.

shloka_text: उत्थाय स महातेजाः प्रकृतीस्ता निशाम्य च। अब्रवीद्भ्रातरं रामो लक्ष्मणं पुण्यलक्षणम्।।2.46.18।।
explanation: On getting up, the brilliant Rama looked at his subjects and said to his brother Lakshmana full of noble qualities:

shloka_text: अस्मद्व्यपेक्षान् सौमित्रे निरपेक्षान् गृहेष्वपि। वृक्षमूलेषु संसुप्तान् पश्य लक्ष्मण साम्प्रतम्।।2.46.19।।
explanation: O Lakshmana, son of Sumitra look at these people, fast alseep under the trees. Out of affection for us, they are even indifferent to their home.

shloka_text: यथैते नियमं पौराः कुर्वन्त्यस्मन्निवर्तने। अपि प्राणान्न्यसिष्यन्ति न तु त्यक्ष्यन्ति निश्चयम्।।2.46.20।।
explanation: On seeing the people's resolve to take us back, it appears they are prepared to give up their lives rather than abandon their determination.

shloka_text: यावदेव तु संसुप्ता स्तावदेव वयं लघु। रथमारुह्य गच्छामः पन्थानमकुतोभयम्।।2.46.21।।
explanation: While they are asleep, we shall quickly mount the chariot and fearlessly proceed on the way.

shloka_text: अतो भूयोऽपि नेदानीमिक्ष्वाकुपुरवासिनः। स्वपेयुरनुरक्ता मां वृक्षमूलानि संश्रिताः।।2.46.22।।
explanation: These loyal inhabitants of Ayodhya, the city of the Ikshvakus will no more sleep again shelterd under the trees.

shloka_text: पौरा ह्यात्मकृताद्दुःखाद्विप्रमोच्या नृपात्मजैः। न तु खल्वात्मना योज्या दुःखेन पुरवासिनः।।2.46.23।।
explanation: The prince should deliver the citizens from the sufferings caused by themselves but should not make them suffer on their account.

shloka_text: अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणो रामं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवस्थितम्। रोचते मे तथा प्राज्ञ क्षिप्र मारुह्यतामिति।।2.46.24।।
explanation: Lakshmana said to Rama who was the very image of like righteousness O wise one, I like this (proposal). Let us quickly mount the chariot.

shloka_text: अथ रामोऽब्रवीच्छ्रीमान्सुमन्त्रं युज्यतां रथः। गमिष्यामि ततोऽरण्यं गच्छ शीघ्रमितः प्रभो।।2.46.25।।
explanation: Then glorious Rama addressing Sumantra said O master charioteer, harness the chariot. I shall (let us) quickly leave for the forest.

shloka_text: सूतस्तत स्सत्त्वरितः स्यन्दनं तैर्हयोत्तमैः। योजयित्व्राऽथ रामाय प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्यवेदयत्।।2.46.26।।
explanation: Thereupon the charioteer hurriedly harnessed the splendid horses to the chariot and informed Rama with folded hands:

shloka_text: अयं युक्तो महाबाहो रथस्ते रथिनां वर। त्वमारोहस्व भद्रं ते ससीत स्सहलक्ष्मणः।।2.46.27।।
explanation: O best among riders the chariot has been harnessed. O mightyarmed one, board it along with Sita and Lakshmana. All the best

shloka_text: तं स्यन्दनमधिष्ठाय राघव स्सपरिच्छदः। शीघ्रगामाकुलावर्तां तमसामतरन्नदीम्।।2.46.28।।
explanation: Rama (along with others) mounted the chariot with his belongings, crossed the rapidly flowing Tamasa agitated with whirlpools.

shloka_text: स सन्तीर्य महाबाहुः श्रीमान् शिवमकण्टकम्। प्रापद्यत महामार्गमभयं भयदर्शिनाम्।।2.46.29।।
explanation: Having crossed the river, the mightyarmed and gracious Rama proceeded on the auspicious and thornless highway arousing confidence even in the timid.

shloka_text: मोहनार्थं तु पौराणां सूतं रामोऽब्रवीद्वचः। उदङ्मुखः प्रयाहि त्वं रथमास्थाय सारथे।।2.46.30।। मुहूर्तं त्वरितं गत्वा निवर्तय रथं पुनः। यथा न विद्युः पौरा मां तथा कुरु समाहितः।।2.46.31।।
explanation: With the intention of confusing the citizens, Rama said to the charioteer, O Sumantra, having seated in the chariot proceed speedly for a while in northerly direction and again turn back the chariot. Accomplish this feat in such a manner that the citizens will not know (where we have gone).

shloka_text: मोहनार्थं तु पौराणां सूतं रामोऽब्रवीद्वचः। उदङ्मुखः प्रयाहि त्वं रथमास्थाय सारथे।।2.46.30।। मुहूर्तं त्वरितं गत्वा निवर्तय रथं पुनः। यथा न विद्युः पौरा मां तथा कुरु समाहितः।।2.46.31।।
explanation: With the intention of confusing the citizens, Rama said to the charioteer, O Sumantra, having seated in the chariot proceed speedly for a while in northerly direction and again turn back the chariot. Accomplish this feat in such a manner that the citizens will not know (where we have gone).

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे स सारथिः। प्रत्यागम्य च रामस्य स्यन्दनं प्रत्यवेदयत्।।2.46.32।।
explanation: The charioteer did as instructed by Rama, returned to him with the chariot and informed (of its readiness).

shloka_text: तौ सम्प्रयुक्तं तु रथं समास्थितौ तदा ससीतौ रघुवंशवर्धनौ। प्रचोदयामास ततस्तुरङ्गमान् स सारथिर्येन पथा तपोवनम्।।2.46.33।।
explanation: When Rama and Lakshmana, perpetuaters of the Raghu race along with Sita were seated on the wellyoked chariot, Sumantra urged the horses to move.

shloka_text: तत स्समास्थाय रथं महारथः ससारथिर्दाशरथिर्वनं ययौ। उदङ्मुखं तं तु रथं चकार स प्रयाणमाङ्गल्य निमित्तदर्शनात्।।2.46.34।।
explanation: As it augurs well to travel north Sumantra placed the chariot in that direction. Thereafter that great charioteer, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana boarded the chariot and departed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortysixth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पौरास्ते राघवं विना। शोकोपहतनिश्चेष्टा बभूवुर्हतचेतसः।।2.47.1।।
explanation: When the night advanced towards dawn the citizens were stunned not to see the scion of the Raghus (Rama). Overwhelmed with sorrow they lost their senses.

shloka_text: शोकजाश्रुपरिद्यूना वीक्षमाणास्ततस्ततः। आलोकमपि रामस्य न पश्यन्ति स्म दुःखिताः।।2.47.2।।
explanation: Anguished and drenched with tears of grief they looked hither and thither but could not find even a trace of Rama.

shloka_text: ते विषादार्तवदना रहितास्तेन धीमता। कृपणाः करुणा वाचो वदन्ति स्म मनस्विनः।।2.47.3।।
explanation: Those highminded people with sorrowful faces due to separation from sagacious Rama expressed themselves in piteous words:

shloka_text: धिगस्तु खलु निद्रां तां ययाऽपहृतचेतसः। नाद्य पश्यामहे रामं पृथूरस्कं महाभुजम्।।2.47.4।।
explanation: Fie on this sleep which robbed us of our senses. We are unable to see (now) that broadchested and mightyarmed Rama.

shloka_text: कथं नाम महाबाहु स्स तथावितथक्रियः। भक्तं जनं परित्यज्य प्रवासं राघवो गतः।।2.47.5।।
explanation: How is it that the mightyarmed Rama who never renders services done to him fruitless has deserted his devoted people and gone into exile?

shloka_text: यो नः सदा पालयति पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्। कथं रघूणां स श्रेष्ठस्त्यक्त्वा नो विपिनं गतः।।2.47.6।।
explanation: How could he, the best among the kings of Raghu dynasty, who used to protect us as a father protects his own children, go to the forest, abandoning us?

shloka_text: इहैव निधनं यामो महाप्रस्थानमेव वा। रामेण रहितानां हि किमर्थं जीवितं हि नः।।2.47.7।।
explanation: We all will die here. We will go on the everlasting journey to death. Of what use is this life to us without Rama?

shloka_text: सन्ति शुष्काणि काष्ठानि प्रभूतानि महान्ति च। तैः प्रज्वाल्य चितां सर्वे प्रविशामोऽथ पावकम्।।2.47.8।।
explanation: There are plenty of dry logs of wood. We will prepare a pyre with them, set fire to it and we all will enter it.

shloka_text: किं वक्ष्यामो महाबाहुरनसूयः प्रियंवदः। नीत स्स राघवोऽस्माभिरिति वक्तुं कथं क्षमम्।।2.47.9।।
explanation: What shall we say (to the people)? How can we say, 'We have conducted him (to the forest), that scion of the Raghus, that mightyarmed Rama, who is of gentle speech and free from malice?

shloka_text: सा नूनं नगरी दीना दृष्ट्वाऽस्मान् राघवं विना। भविष्यति निरानन्दा सस्त्रीबालवयोधिका।।2.47.10।।
explanation: Seeing us return without Rama, the women, children and  the aged of the city (Ayodhya) will certainly feel miserable and cheerless.

shloka_text: निर्यातास्तेन वीरेण सह नित्यं जितात्मना। विहीनास्तेन च पुनः कथं पश्याम तां पुरीम्।।2.47.11।।
explanation: Having left (that city) with the valiant and selfrestrained Rama, how can we now return without him ?

shloka_text: इतीव बहुधा वाचो बाहुमुद्यम्य ते जनाः। विलपन्ति स्म दुःखार्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः।।2.47.12।।
explanation: All of them with grief distressed, and with their arms thrown up lamented like cows deprived of their calves.

shloka_text: ततो मार्गानुसारेण गत्वा किञ्चित् क्षणं पुनः। मार्गनाशाद्विषादेन महता समभिप्लुताः।।2.47.13।।
explanation: For a short while they followed the tracks (of the chariot) and after having gone a little distance, they missed the way. They were again submerged in deep sorrow.

shloka_text: रथस्य मार्गनाशेन न्यवर्तन्त मनस्विनः। किमिदं किं करिष्यामो दैवेनोपहता इति।।2.47.14।।
explanation: When they could not find the tracks of the chariot, those highminded people turned back and said to themselves 'What is this? We have been deceived by fate. What are we to do now?'

shloka_text: ततो यथागतेनैव मार्गेण क्लान्तचेतसः। अयोध्यामागमन्सर्वे पुरीं व्यथितसज्जनाम्।।2.47.15।।
explanation: Thereafter, all of them, the virtuous people grieving, their minds fatigued, returned to Ayodhya the same way they had come.

shloka_text: आलोक्य नगरीं तां च क्षयव्याकुलमानसाः। आवर्तयन्त तेऽश्रूणि नयनैः शोकपीडितैः।।2.47.16।।
explanation: On seeing  the city the minds of the people were agitated due to the loss (of their prince). Tears streamed down their eyes, oppressed with sorrow.

shloka_text: एषा रामेण नगरी रहिता नातिशोभते। आपगा गरुडेनेव ह्रदादुद्धृतपन्नगा।।2.47.17।।
explanation: This city without Rama just as a river with serpents lifted away by Garuda from its depths looks no longer beautiful.

shloka_text: चन्द्रहीनमिवाकाशं तोयहीनमिवार्णवम्। अपश्यन्निहतानन्दं नगरं ते विचेतसः।।2.47.18।।
explanation: Plunged in grief, they saw the city deprived of all joy, looking like a sky without the Moon and an ocean without water.

shloka_text: ते तानि वेश्मानि महाधनानि दुःखेन दुःखोपहता विशन्तः। नैव प्रजज्ञुः स्वजनं जनं वा निरीक्षमाणाः प्रविनष्टहर्षाः।।2.47.19।।
explanation: Those people devoid of delight entered their rich mansions with great difficulty. Even though they, stricken with sorrow, looked at men and their own kinsmen they could not recognise them. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyseventh sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेषामेवं विषण्णानां पीडितानामतीव च। बाष्पविप्लुतनेत्राणां सशोकानां मुमूर्षया।।2.48.1।। अनुगम्य निवृत्तानां रामं नगरवासिनाम्। उद्गतानीव सत्वानि बभूवुरमनस्विनाम्।।2.48.2।।
explanation: The people afflicted with sorrow followed Rama and returned to the city deeply distressed. Eyes overflowing with tears, they longed for death. Smitten with grief, they lost their highmindedness and looked as if their life had been drained out.

shloka_text: तेषामेवं विषण्णानां पीडितानामतीव च। बाष्पविप्लुतनेत्राणां सशोकानां मुमूर्षया।।2.48.1।। अनुगम्य निवृत्तानां रामं नगरवासिनाम्। उद्गतानीव सत्वानि बभूवुरमनस्विनाम्।।2.48.2।।
explanation: The people afflicted with sorrow followed Rama and returned to the city deeply distressed. Eyes overflowing with tears, they longed for death. Smitten with grief, they lost their highmindedness and looked as if their life had been drained out.

shloka_text: स्वं स्वं निलयमागम्य पुत्रदारैस्समावृता। अश्रूणि मुमुचुस्सर्वे बाष्पेण पिहिताननाः।।2.48.3।।
explanation: The subjects reached their respective homes  and surrounded by their sons and wives  broke down their faces flooded with tears.

shloka_text: न चाहृष्यन् नचामोदन् वणिजो न प्रसारयन्। न चाशोभन्त पण्यानि नापचन् गृहमेधिनः।।2.48.4।।
explanation: The people had no joy in life nor did they find cheer in anything. The merchants did not offer their wares for sale. The marketplace looked graceless (lifeless). (The stocks were empty). The householders did not cook their food.

shloka_text: नष्टं दृष्ट्वा नाभ्यनन्दन् विपुलं वा धनागमम्। पुत्रं प्रथमजं लब्ध्वा जननी नाभ्यनन्दत।।2.48.5।।
explanation: Neither loss nor acquisition of wealth mattered (to the people). No mother rejoiced over getting her firstborn son.

shloka_text: गृहे गृहे रुदन्त्यश्च भर्तारं गृहमागतम्। व्यगर्हयन्त दुःखार्ता वाग्भिस्तोत्रैरिव द्विपान्।।2.48.6।।
explanation: In every house, women wept and in anguish heaped abuses on their husbands on their arrival at home with words (sharp) like goads on elephants:

shloka_text: किं नु तेषां गृहैः कार्यं किं दारै: किं धनेन वा। पुत्रैर्वा किं सुखैर्वापि ये न पश्यन्ति राघवम्।।2.48.7।।
explanation: For those who do not see Rama, of what use are the houses or spouses or sons or fortunes or delight?

shloka_text: एकः सत्पुरुषो लोके लक्ष्मण स्सह सीतया। योऽनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थं रामं परिचरन् वने।।2.48.8।।
explanation: Lakshmana is the only fortunate person in the world who has followed Rama of the Kakutstha race along with Sita to serve them.

shloka_text: आपगाः कृतपुण्यास्ता पद्मिन्यश्च सरांसि च। येषु स्नास्यति काकुत्स्थो विगाह्य सलिलं शुचि।।2.48.9।।
explanation: The rivers and the lotuspools have done some meritorious acts in the past as a result of which Rama having plunged into their holy waters will make his ablution.

shloka_text: शोभयिष्यन्ति काकुत्स्थमटव्यो रम्यकाननाः। आपगाश्च महानूपाः सानुमन्तश्च पर्वताः।।2.48.10।।
explanation: Forests with beautiful groves rivers with vast expanse of waters, mountains with their slopes will enhance the lustre of the scion of the Kakutsthas (Rama).

shloka_text: काननं वापि शैलं वा यं रामोऽधिगमिष्यति। प्रियातिथिमिव प्राप्तं नैनं शक्ष्यन्त्यनर्चितुम्।।2.48.11।।
explanation: Whichever hill or forest Rama visits, people will receive him there like a welcome  guest and will not fail to render hospitality to him.

shloka_text: विचित्रकुसुमापीडा बहुमञ्जरि धारिणः। राघवं दर्शयिष्यन्ति नगा भ्रमरशालिनः।।2.48.12।।
explanation: Trees with bunches of cololurful flowers and clusters of blossoms hovering over with black bees will present themselves to the son of the Raghus (Rama).

shloka_text: अकाले चापि मुख्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च। दर्शयिष्यन्त्यनुक्रोशाद्गिरयो राममागतम्।।2.48.13।।
explanation: The hills will exhibit their excellent flowers and fruits off season out of compassion in order to welcome Rama.

shloka_text: प्रस्रविष्यन्ति तोयानि विमलानि महीधराः। विदर्शयन्तो विविधान् भूयश्चित्रांश्च निर्झरान्।।2.48.14।।
explanation: The mountains, displaying various wonderful streams here and there, will flow with pellucid waters (for Rama).

shloka_text: पादपाः पर्वताग्रेषु रमयिष्यन्ति राघवम्। यत्र रामो भयं नात्र नास्ति तत्र पराभवः।।2.48.15।।
explanation: The trees on the mountain summits will enchant Rama. Where Rama goes, there will be no room for fear or dishonour.

shloka_text: स हि शूरो महाबाहुः पुत्रो दशरथस्य च। पुरा भवति नोदूरादनुगच्छाम राघवम्।।2.48.16।।
explanation: Before that valiant, strongarmed son of Dasaratha goes too far away (from us), we should follow him.

shloka_text: पादच्छाया सुखा भर्तुस्तादृशस्य महात्मनः। स हि नाथो जनस्यास्य स गति स्सपरायणम्।।2.48.17।।
explanation: The shadow of the feet of this magnanimous lord will give us happiness. He alone is the goal and protector of all these people. He is the supreme refuge.

shloka_text: वयं परिचरिष्यामः सीतां यूयं तु राघवम्। इति पौरस्त्रियो भर्तृ़न् दुखार्तास्तत्तदब्रुवन्।।2.48.18।।
explanation: We will serve Sita. You will serve Rama. Such were the words of the distressed women of the city to their husbands. (They continued).

shloka_text: युष्माकं राघवोऽरण्ये योगक्षेमं विधास्यति। सीता नारीजनस्यास्य योगक्षेमं करिष्यति।।2.48.19।।
explanation: In the forest, Rama will look after your wellbeing and Sita will ensure our, women folk's security.

shloka_text: को न्वनेनाऽप्रतीतेन सोत्कण्ठितजनेन च। सम्प्रियेतामनोज्ञेन वासेन हृतचेतसा।।2.48.20।।
explanation: The people here are choked with grief. Who will like to stay here where life is disagreeable, cheerless, full of despondency and distress?

shloka_text: कैकेय्या यदि चे द्राज्यं स्यादधर्म्यमनाथवत्। न हि नो जीवितेनार्थः कुतः पुत्रैः कुतो धनैः।।2.48.21।।
explanation: If Kaikeyi rules this kingdom unethically, we do not want to live here like orphans. What is the use of our progeny or property (in such a place)?

shloka_text: यया पुत्रश्च भर्ता च त्यक्तावैश्वर्यकारणात्। कं सा परिहरेदन्यं कैकेयी कुलपांसनी।।2.48.22।।
explanation: Can Kaikeyi, who has brought disgrace to the race by abandoning her husband and son for the sake of wealth, spare others?

shloka_text: कैकेय्या न वयं राज्ये भृतका निवसेमहि। जीवन्त्या जातु जीवन्त्यः पुत्रैरपि शपामहे।।2.48.23।।
explanation: We swear on our sons that as long as Kaikeyi lives, or we live, we will never stay in her kingdom as servants.

shloka_text: या पुत्रं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य प्रवासयति निर्घृणा। कस्तां प्राप्य सुखं जीवेदधर्म्यां दुष्टचारिणीम्।।2.48.24।।
explanation: Who can live with pleasure under the rule of Kaikeyi of  unrighteous character and wicked behaviour, one who without compassion banished Rama, son of Dasaratha, king of kings?

shloka_text: उपद्रुतमिदं सर्वमनालम्बमनायकम्। कैकेय्या हि कृते सर्वं विनाशमुपयास्यति।।2.48.25।।
explanation: The entire kingdom, for the sake of Kaikeyi, is under a great calamity. With no support or leader it will definitely go to ruin.

shloka_text: न हि प्रव्रजिते रामे जीविष्यति महीपतिः। मृते दशरथे व्यक्तं विलापस्तदनन्तरम्।।2.48.26।।
explanation: Now that Rama has been banished, the king will not live (long). After his death there will be evidently only lamentations.

shloka_text: ते विषं पिबतालोड्य क्षीणपुण्या स्सुदुर्गताः। राघवं वानुगच्छध्वमश्रुतिं वापि गच्छत।।2.48.27।।
explanation: Where you are in deep trouble with merits exhausted, it is better to take poison, or follow Rama or walk into the unknown.

shloka_text: मिथ्याप्रव्राजितो राम स्ससीत स्सहलक्ष्मणः। भरते सन्निसृष्टास्स्म स्सौनिके पशवो यथा।।2.48.28।।
explanation: Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana has been deceitfully exiled and all of us delivered to Bharata like beasts to a butcher (for protection).

shloka_text: पूर्णचन्द्रानन श्श्यामो गूढजत्रुररिन्दमः। आजानुबाहुः पद्माक्षो रामो लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।।2.48.29।। पूर्वाभिभाषी मधुर स्सत्यवादी महाबलः। सौम्यस्सर्वस्य लोकस्य चन्द्रवत्प्रियदर्शनः।।2.48.30।। नूनं पुरुषशार्दूलो मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः। शोभयिष्यत्यरण्यानि विचरन् स महारथः।।2.48.31।।
explanation: Rama, elder brother to Lakshmana is a tiger among men, a subduer of enemies, powerful like an intoxicated elephant, and a great charioteer. Blue in complexion, he has a face like the full Moon. He has lotuslike eyes, kneelong arms and fleshy clavicles. Endowed with a sweet nature, he always speaks the truth and the first to speak to others. When he roams the forest, charming like the Moon and pleasing to the whole world, he will surely make it look graceful.

shloka_text: पूर्णचन्द्रानन श्श्यामो गूढजत्रुररिन्दमः। आजानुबाहुः पद्माक्षो रामो लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।।2.48.29।। पूर्वाभिभाषी मधुर स्सत्यवादी महाबलः। सौम्यस्सर्वस्य लोकस्य चन्द्रवत्प्रियदर्शनः।।2.48.30।। नूनं पुरुषशार्दूलो मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः। शोभयिष्यत्यरण्यानि विचरन् स महारथः।।2.48.31।।
explanation: Rama, elder brother to Lakshmana is a tiger among men, a subduer of enemies, powerful like an intoxicated elephant, and a great charioteer. Blue in complexion, he has a face like the full Moon. He has lotuslike eyes, kneelong arms and fleshy clavicles. Endowed with a sweet nature, he always speaks the truth and the first to speak to others. When he roams the forest, charming like the Moon and pleasing to the whole world, he will surely make it look graceful.

shloka_text: पूर्णचन्द्रानन श्श्यामो गूढजत्रुररिन्दमः। आजानुबाहुः पद्माक्षो रामो लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः।।2.48.29।। पूर्वाभिभाषी मधुर स्सत्यवादी महाबलः। सौम्यस्सर्वस्य लोकस्य चन्द्रवत्प्रियदर्शनः।।2.48.30।। नूनं पुरुषशार्दूलो मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमः। शोभयिष्यत्यरण्यानि विचरन् स महारथः।।2.48.31।।
explanation: Rama, elder brother to Lakshmana is a tiger among men, a subduer of enemies, powerful like an intoxicated elephant, and a great charioteer. Blue in complexion, he has a face like the full Moon. He has lotuslike eyes, kneelong arms and fleshy clavicles. Endowed with a sweet nature, he always speaks the truth and the first to speak to others. When he roams the forest, charming like the Moon and pleasing to the whole world, he will surely make it look graceful.

shloka_text: तास्तथा विलपन्त्यस्तु नगरे नागरस्त्रियः। चुक्रुशु र्दुःखसन्तप्ता मृत्योरिव भयागमे।।2.48.32।।
explanation: Such was the lamentation of the women of the city. Overcome with grief as if frightened at the approach of death, they wept bitterly.

shloka_text: इत्येवं विलपन्तीनां स्त्रीणां वेश्मसु राघवम्। जगामास्तं दिनकरो रजनी चाभ्यवर्तत।।2.48.33।।
explanation: As the women of the city were thus lamenting over the scion of the Raghus (Rama) (sitting) at home, the sun set. Night fell.

shloka_text: नष्टज्वलनसन्तापा प्रशान्ताध्यायसत्कथा। तिमिरेणाभिलिप्तेव सा तदा नगरी बभौ।।2.48.34।।
explanation: With sacrificial fires extinguished and the reading of holy scriptures and sacred recitations stopped, Ayodhya looked as if besmeared with darkness.

shloka_text: उपशान्तवणिक्पण्या नष्टहर्षा निराश्रया। अयोध्या नगरी चासीन्नष्टतारमिवाम्बरम्।।2.48.35।।
explanation: With markets closed, the city of Ayodhya cheerless and shelterless looked like the sky without stars.

shloka_text: तथा स्त्रियो रामनिमित्तमातुरा यथा सुते भ्रातरि वा विवासिते। विलप्य दीना रुरुदुर्विचेतस स्सूतैर्हि तासामधिको हि सोऽभवत्।।2.48.36।।
explanation: The women grieved over Rama as if a son or a brother had been exiled. Depressed and distressed, they wept and sobbed. For them, Rama was indeed more than their sons.

shloka_text: प्रशान्तगीतोत्सवनृत्तवादना व्यपास्तहर्षा पिहितापणोदया। तदा ह्ययोध्या नगरी बभूव सा महार्णव स्सङ्क्षपितोदको यथा।।2.48.37।।
explanation: With the cessation of singing, celebrations, dance and music, there was no rejoicing in the city. The markets displaying merchandise were shut down. The city of Ayodhya looked like the ocean with its waters diminished. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyeighth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामोऽपि रात्रिशेषेण तेनैव महदन्तरम्। जगाम पुरुषव्याघ्रः पितुराज्ञामनुस्मरन्।।2.49.1।।
explanation: Recollecting his father's command, Rama, the foremost among men, covered a long distance during the remaining part of the night.

shloka_text: तथैव गच्छतस्तस्य व्यपायाद्रजनी शिवा। उपास्य शिवां सन्ध्यां विषयान्तं व्यगाहत।।2.49.2।।
explanation: While Rama was thus travelling, the auspicious night ended. With the sandhya (morning twilight), worship over, he reached the frontiers of the country.

shloka_text: ग्रामान् विकृष्टसीमान्तान् पुष्पितानि वनानि च। पश्यन्नतिययौ शीघ्रं शनैरिव हयोत्तमैः।।2.49.3।। शृण्वन् वचो मनुष्याणां ग्रामसंवासवासिनाम्।
explanation: Watching the villages furrowed at the outskirts, forests in blossom, hearing the gossips of the people living in the midst of villages, Rama felt he was moving very slowly whereas he had actually covered a long distance with those excellent (swift) horses.

shloka_text: राजानं धिग्दशरथं कामस्य वशमागतम्।।2.49.4।। हा नृशंसाद्य कैकेयी पापा पापानुबन्धिनी। तीक्ष्णा सम्भिन्नमर्यादा तीक्ष्णकर्मणि वर्तते।।2.49.5।। या पुत्रमीदृशं राज्ञः प्रवासयति धार्मिकम्। वनवासे महाप्राज्ञं सानुक्रोशं जितेन्द्रियम्।।2.49.6।।
explanation: (The villagers were speaking among themselves) Fie on the king who is overtaken by passion Alas, the heartless, sinful Kaikeyi, indulging in evil has banished into the forest this prince who is righteous and sagacious, compassionate and selfrestrained. How could this cruel Kaikeyi, by breaking all limits of decorum resort to such atrocious action?

shloka_text: राजानं धिग्दशरथं कामस्य वशमागतम्।।2.49.4।। हा नृशंसाद्य कैकेयी पापा पापानुबन्धिनी। तीक्ष्णा सम्भिन्नमर्यादा तीक्ष्णकर्मणि वर्तते।।2.49.5।। या पुत्रमीदृशं राज्ञः प्रवासयति धार्मिकम्। वनवासे महाप्राज्ञं सानुक्रोशं जितेन्द्रियम्।।2.49.6।।
explanation: (The villagers were speaking among themselves) Fie on the king who is overtaken by passion Alas, the heartless, sinful Kaikeyi, indulging in evil has banished into the forest this prince who is righteous and sagacious, compassionate and selfrestrained. How could this cruel Kaikeyi, by breaking all limits of decorum resort to such atrocious action?

shloka_text: राजानं धिग्दशरथं कामस्य वशमागतम्।।2.49.4।। हा नृशंसाद्य कैकेयी पापा पापानुबन्धिनी। तीक्ष्णा सम्भिन्नमर्यादा तीक्ष्णकर्मणि वर्तते।।2.49.5।। या पुत्रमीदृशं राज्ञः प्रवासयति धार्मिकम्। वनवासे महाप्राज्ञं सानुक्रोशं जितेन्द्रियम्।।2.49.6।।
explanation: (The villagers were speaking among themselves) Fie on the king who is overtaken by passion Alas, the heartless, sinful Kaikeyi, indulging in evil has banished into the forest this prince who is righteous and sagacious, compassionate and selfrestrained. How could this cruel Kaikeyi, by breaking all limits of decorum resort to such atrocious action?

shloka_text: कथं नाम महाभागा सीता जनकनन्दिनी। सदा सुखेष्वभिरता दुःखान्यनुभविष्यति।।2.49.7।।
explanation: How will Sita, highly fortunate daughter of Janaka and used to comforts endure these sufferings?

shloka_text: अहो दशरथो राजा निस्नेहः स्वसुतं प्रियम्। प्रजानामनघं रामं परित्यक्तुमिहेच्छति।।2.49.8।।
explanation: Alas, the loveless king Dasaratha now intends to abandon his own sinless son Rama who is dear to the subjects.

shloka_text: एता वाचो मनुष्याणां ग्रामसंवासवासिनाम्। शृण्वन्नतिययौ वीरः कोसलान् कोसलेश्वरः।।2.49.9।।
explanation: Such were the words of people living in villages and hamlets that Rama the valiant lord of Kosala happened to hear as he was crossing the boundaries of Kosala.

shloka_text: ततो वेदश्रुतिं नाम शिववारिवहां नदीम्। उत्तीर्याभिमुखः प्रायादगस्त्याध्युषितां दिशम्।।2.49.10।।
explanation: He then crossed the river Vedasruti flowing with sacred waters and went in the southern direction where sage Agastya resided.

shloka_text: गत्वा तु सुचिरं कालं ततः शीतजलां नदीम्। गोमतीं गोयुतानूपामतरत्सागरङ्गमाम्।।2.49.11।।
explanation: Travelling for a long time along the river Gomati full of cool waters on whose marshy bank cows grazed, Rama crossed it at the point where it flows into the sea.

shloka_text: गोमतीं चाप्यतिक्रम्य राघवः शीघ्रगैर्हयैः। मयूरहंसाभिरुतां ततार स्यन्दिकां नदीम्।।2.49.12।।
explanation: Gomati gone, Rama with the swiftmoving horses crossed the river Syandika echoing with the cries of peacocks and swans.

shloka_text: स महीं मनुना राज्ञा दत्तामिक्ष्वाकवे पुरा। स्फीतां राष्ट्रावृतां रामो वैदेहीमन्वदर्शयत्।।2.49.13।।
explanation: Rama showed Sita vast tracts of land encircled by kingdoms which were formerly bestowed upon Ikshvaku by emperor Manu.

shloka_text: सूत इत्येव चाभाष्य सारथिं तमभीक्ष्णशः। हंसमत्तस्वरश्श्रीमानुवाच पुरुषर्षभः।।2.19.14।।
explanation: Graceful Rama, best among men with a voice resembling that of an intoxicated swan, called the charioteer again and again and said:

shloka_text: कदाऽहं पुनरागम्य सरय्वा पुष्पिते वने। मृगयां पर्यटिष्यामि मात्रा पित्रा च सङ्गतः।।2.49.15।।
explanation: When shall I return and reunite with my father and mother and go hunting in the blooming forest on the bank of the river Sarayu?

shloka_text: नात्यर्थमभिकाङ्क्षामि मृगयां सरयूवने। रतिर्ह्येषातुला लोके राजर्षिगणसम्मता।।2.49.16।।
explanation: In this world, hunting is a unique pleasure. It is regarded as a delightful sport for royal sages. But I do not have a great longing for hunting in the forest on the bank of river Sarayu.

shloka_text: राजर्षीणां हि लोकेऽस्मिन् रत्यर्थं मृगया वने। काले कृतां तां मनुजैर्घन्विनामभिकाङ्क्षिताम्।।2.49.17।।
explanation: In this world, hunting in the woods is a pleasure for royal sages and is greatly sought after by bowmen. This was later resorted to by others.

shloka_text: स तमध्वानमैक्ष्वाकस्सूतं मधुरया गिरा। तं तमर्थमभिप्रेत्य ययौ वाक्यमुदीरयन्।।2.49.18।।
explanation: The descendant of Ikshvaku related to the charioteer in a sweet voice the thoughts that came to him and went on the way (continued his journey). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fortyninth sarga of Ayodhyakanda of  the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विशालान् कोसलान् रम्यान् यात्वा लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः। अयोध्याभिमुखो धीमान् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.50.1।।
explanation: Having crossed the vast, beautiful kingdom of Kosala, the sagacious elder brother of Lakshmana stood facing Ayodhya with folded palms and said:

shloka_text: आपृच्छे त्वां पुरीश्रेष्ठे काकुत्स्थपरिपालिते। दैवतानि च यानि त्वां पालयन्ति वसन्ति च।।2.50.2।।
explanation: O Ayodhya, the best of cities ruled by those born in the Kakutstha race I take leave of you and of all those gods inhabiting and guarding you.

shloka_text: निवृत्तवनवासस्त्वामनृणो जगतीपतेः। पुनर्द्रक्ष्यामि मात्रा च पित्रा च सह सङ्गतः।।2.50.3।।
explanation: On completion of exile and my filial obligations to king Dasaratha, lord of the world, discharged, I shall, reunited with my parents, see you again.

shloka_text: ततो रुधिरताम्राक्षो भुजमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम्। अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनोऽब्रवीज्जानपदं जनम्।।2.50.4।।
explanation: He looked miserable, his copperred eyes filled with tears. He raised his right hand and said to the villagers who had come to see him:

shloka_text: अनुक्रोशो दया चैव यथार्हं मयि वः कृतः। चिरं दुःखस्य पापीयो गम्यतामर्थसिद्धये।।2.50.5।।
explanation: You have aptly shown your kindness and compassion to me. It is not proper to prolong one's grief. So do go and altend to your duties.

shloka_text: तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्। विलपन्तो नरा घोरं व्यतिष्ठन्त क्वचित् क्वचित्।।2.50.6।।
explanation: All of them paid their homage by circumambulating the highsouled Rama. Crying bitterly, they stood here and there.

shloka_text: तथा विलपतां तेषामतृप्तानां च राघवः। अचक्षुर्विषयं प्रायाद्यथार्कः क्षणदामुखे।।2.50.7।।
explanation: Not yet satisfied (they wanted to linger longer), they stood weeping, while Rama went out of sight just as the Sun disappears at nightfall.

shloka_text: ततो धान्यधनोपेतान् दानशीलजनान् शिवान्। अकुतश्चिद्भयान् रम्यांश्चैत्ययूपसमावृतान्।।2.50.8।। उद्यानाम्रवनोपेतान् सम्पन्नसलिलाशयान्। तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णान् गोकुलाकुलसेवितान्।।2.50.9।। लक्षणीयान्नरेन्द्राणां ब्रह्मघोषाभिनादितान्। रथेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः कोसलानत्यवर्तत।।2.50.10।।
explanation: Rama, the best  of men, crossed the auspicious land of Kosala which was worth seeing by kings. It looked charming with sacrificial posts and altars, pleasure gardens and mango groves and tanks filled with water. It was rich with herds of cattle, wealth and foodgrains. It was inhabited by charitable, contented and wellnourished people free from fear from any quarter. And it reverberated with the sounds of Vedic recitations.

shloka_text: ततो धान्यधनोपेतान् दानशीलजनान् शिवान्। अकुतश्चिद्भयान् रम्यांश्चैत्ययूपसमावृतान्।।2.50.8।। उद्यानाम्रवनोपेतान् सम्पन्नसलिलाशयान्। तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णान् गोकुलाकुलसेवितान्।।2.50.9।। लक्षणीयान्नरेन्द्राणां ब्रह्मघोषाभिनादितान्। रथेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः कोसलानत्यवर्तत।।2.50.10।।
explanation: Rama, the best  of men, crossed the auspicious land of Kosala which was worth seeing by kings. It looked charming with sacrificial posts and altars, pleasure gardens and mango groves and tanks filled with water. It was rich with herds of cattle, wealth and foodgrains. It was inhabited by charitable, contented and wellnourished people free from fear from any quarter. And it reverberated with the sounds of Vedic recitations.

shloka_text: ततो धान्यधनोपेतान् दानशीलजनान् शिवान्। अकुतश्चिद्भयान् रम्यांश्चैत्ययूपसमावृतान्।।2.50.8।। उद्यानाम्रवनोपेतान् सम्पन्नसलिलाशयान्। तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णान् गोकुलाकुलसेवितान्।।2.50.9।। लक्षणीयान्नरेन्द्राणां ब्रह्मघोषाभिनादितान्। रथेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः कोसलानत्यवर्तत।।2.50.10।।
explanation: Rama, the best  of men, crossed the auspicious land of Kosala which was worth seeing by kings. It looked charming with sacrificial posts and altars, pleasure gardens and mango groves and tanks filled with water. It was rich with herds of cattle, wealth and foodgrains. It was inhabited by charitable, contented and wellnourished people free from fear from any quarter. And it reverberated with the sounds of Vedic recitations.

shloka_text: मध्येनमुदितं स्फीतं रम्योद्यानसमाकुलम्। राज्यं भोग्यं नरेन्द्राणां ययौ धृतिमतां वरः।।2.50.11।।
explanation: Rama, the greatest among those endowed with fortitude, travelled through the middle of the kingdom which was pleasing, prosperous and full of ravishing gardens fit to be enjoyed by kings.

shloka_text: तत स्त्रिपथगां दिव्यां शिवतोयामशैवलाम्। ददर्श राघवो गङ्गां पुण्यामृषिनिषेविताम्।।2.50.12।।
explanation: There Rama saw the holy Ganga flowing in three (worlds) with her sacred waters, free from moss, and worshipped by sages.

shloka_text: आश्रमैरविदूरस्थैः श्रीमद्भिस्समलङ्कृताम्। कालेऽप्सरोभिर्हृष्टाभि स्सेविताम्भोह्रदां शिवाम्।।2.50.13।।
explanation: The holy Ganga, adorned with graceful hermitages situated not far away is visited at times by delightful nymphs who sport in her lakes.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वैः किन्नरैरुपशोभिताम्। नानागन्धर्वपत्नीभि स्सेवितां सततं शिवाम्।।2.50.14।।
explanation: The Ganga is graced by devatas, danavas, gandharvas and kinneras. Wives of several gandharvas always visit this auspicious river.

shloka_text: देवाऽऽक्रीडशताकीर्णां देवोद्यानशतायुताम्। देवार्थमाकाशगमां विख्यातां देवपद्मिनीम्।।2.50.15।।
explanation: Since this river flows through heavens for the gods, it is wellknown as 'Devapadmini' where celestial lotuses grow. The river embraces hundreds of hills serving as sporting places and pleasuregardens for gods.

shloka_text: जलाघाताट्टहासोग्रां फेननिर्मलहासिनीम्। क्वचिद्वेणीकृतजलां क्वचिदावर्तशोभिताम्।।2.50.16।।
explanation: The sound of dashing waters of the Ganga is like her laughter and the foam like her sparkling smile. Here she flows straight like the braid of a maiden and there in whirlpools.

shloka_text: क्वचित् स्तिमितगम्भीरां क्वचिद्वेगजलाकुलाम्। क्वचिद्गम्भीरनिर्घोषां क्वचिद्भैरवनिस्वनाम्।।2.50.17।।
explanation: Here the Ganga runs deep but quiet, there she looks perturbed due to fastflowing waters, here she flows with a deep groan and there with a dreadful roar.

shloka_text: देवसङ्घाप्लुतजलां निर्मलोत्पलशोभिताम्। क्वचिदाभोगपुलिनां क्वचिन्निर्मलवालुकाम्।।2.50.18।।
explanation: Here hosts of celestials take their ablutions and there she shines with lilies of pure blue. Here her banks are curved and there her bed is dotted with patches of white sand.

shloka_text: हंससारससङ्घुष्टां चक्रवाकोपकूजिताम्। सदा मदैश्च विहगैरभिसन्नादितान्तराम्।।2.50.19।।
explanation: The river reverberates with the cries of swans, cranes and chakravakas (ruddy goose). It rings intermittently with the chirpings of birds charged with endless pasison.

shloka_text: क्वचित्तीररुहैर्वृक्षैर्मालाभिरिवशोभिताम्। क्वचित्फुल्लोत्पलच्छन्नां क्वचित्पद्मवनाकुलाम्।।2.50.20।।
explanation: Here on her banks stand trees adorned as though with garlands, and there in her waters abound fullblown lilies and a forest of lotuses.

shloka_text: क्वचित्कुमुदषण्डैश्च कुड्मलैरुपशोभिताम्। नानापुष्परजोध्वस्तां समदामिव च क्वचित्।।2.50.21।।
explanation: Here she is decked with hosts of waterlilies and halfblown flowers while elsewhere she looks intoxicated with the pollen fallen from various flowers.

shloka_text: व्यपेतमलसङ्घातां मणिनिर्मलदर्शनाम्। दिशागजैर्वनगजै र्मत्तैश्च वरवारणैः।।2.50.22।। देवोपवाह्यैश्च मुहुस्सन्नादितवनान्तराम्।
explanation: The river, cleansed of heaps of impurities, appears like a transparent gem. The interiors of forests on her banks always resounds with the trumpeting of mighty, intoxicated, wild elephants guarding the quarters, fit to be the vehicles of gods.

shloka_text: प्रमदामिव यत्नेन भूषितां भूषणोत्तमैः।।2.50.23।। फलैः पुष्पैः किसलयैर्वृतां गुल्मैर्द्विजैस्तथा। शिंशुमारैश्च नक्रैश्च भुजङ्गैश्च निषेविताम्।।2.50.24।।
explanation: Just like a lady, Ganga is decorated with the best of ornaments her banks are filled with fruits, flowers, tender leaves or shoots and (flowering) shrubs. It is inhabited by birds and brahmins and infested with sisumaras (small whales), crocodiles and serpents.

shloka_text: प्रमदामिव यत्नेन भूषितां भूषणोत्तमैः।।2.50.23।। फलैः पुष्पैः किसलयैर्वृतां गुल्मैर्द्विजैस्तथा। शिंशुमारैश्च नक्रैश्च भुजङ्गैश्च निषेविताम्।।2.50.24।।
explanation: Just like a lady, Ganga is decorated with the best of ornaments her banks are filled with fruits, flowers, tender leaves or shoots and (flowering) shrubs. It is inhabited by birds and brahmins and infested with sisumaras (small whales), crocodiles and serpents.

shloka_text: विष्णुपादच्युतां दिव्यामपापां पापनाशिनीम्। तां शङ्करजटाजूटाद्भ्रष्टां सागरतेजसा।।2.50.25।। समुद्रमहिषीं गङ्गां सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम्। आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरं प्रति।।2.50.26।।
explanation: Mightyarmed Rama reached Srngaberapura on the bank of this consort of the ocean, this Ganga loud with the cries of kraunchas and herons. This sinless, divine Ganga, destroyer of sins who flows from the feet of lord Visnu and by the effulgence (penance) of Sagara's son (Bhagiratha) emerged from the matted locks of lord Siva.

shloka_text: विष्णुपादच्युतां दिव्यामपापां पापनाशिनीम्। तां शङ्करजटाजूटाद्भ्रष्टां सागरतेजसा।।2.50.25।। समुद्रमहिषीं गङ्गां सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम्। आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरं प्रति।।2.50.26।।
explanation: Mightyarmed Rama reached Srngaberapura on the bank of this consort of the ocean, this Ganga loud with the cries of kraunchas and herons. This sinless, divine Ganga, destroyer of sins who flows from the feet of lord Visnu and by the effulgence (penance) of Sagara's son (Bhagiratha) emerged from the matted locks of lord Siva.

shloka_text: तामूर्मिकलिलावर्तामन्ववेक्ष्य महारथः। सुमन्त्रमब्रवीत्सूतमिहैवाद्य वसामहे।।2.50.27।।
explanation: Beholding river Ganga full of waves and whirlpools, the great chariotwarrior (Rama) said to Sumantra: We shall spend the night here.

shloka_text: तं जाग्रतमदम्भेन भ्रातुरर्थाय लक्ष्मणम्। गुहः सन्तापसन्तप्तो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.51.1।।
explanation: Deeply moved to see Lakshmana, scion of the Raghus, keeping awake all night without any pretence for his brother's sake, Guha spoke.

shloka_text: इयं तात सुखा शय्या त्वदर्थमुपकल्पिता। प्रत्याश्वसिहि साध्वस्यां राजपुत्र यथासुखम्।।2.51.2।।
explanation: O dear prince this comfortable bed has been arranged for you. Rest happily on this bed.

shloka_text: उचितोऽयं जनस्सर्वः क्लेशानां त्वं सुखोचितः। गुप्त्यर्थं जागरिष्यामः काकुत्स्थस्य वयं निशाम्।।2.51.3।।
explanation: We are used to all kinds of suffering and you, to comfort. We will keep vigil during the night for the protection of Rama, descendant of the Kakutsthas.

shloka_text: न हि रामात्प्रियतमो ममास्ति भुवि कश्चन। ब्रवीम्येतदहं सत्यं सत्येनैव च ते शपे।।2.51.4।।
explanation: For me, there is none dearer than Rama in this world. I speak the truth. I swear by truth.

shloka_text: अस्य प्रसादादाशंसे लोकेस्मिन् सुमुहद्यशः। धर्मावाप्तिं च विपुलामर्थावाप्तिं च केवलम्।।2.51.5।।
explanation: I am seeking supreme fame in this world through the attainment of dharma and acquisition of abundant artha by the grace of Rama alone.

shloka_text: सोऽहं प्रियसखं रामं शयानं सह सीतया। रक्षिष्यामि धनुष्पाणि स्सर्वतो ज्ञातिभि स्सह।।2.51.6।।
explanation: I along with my kinsmen, bow in hand, will protect my dear friend, Rama with Sita from every side.

shloka_text: न हि मेऽविदितं किञ्चिद्वनेऽस्मिंश्चरतस्सदा। चतुरङ्गं ह्यपिबलं सुमहत्प्रसहेमहि।।2.51.7।।
explanation: Wandering about in this forest all the time there is nothing unknown to me (here). We can withstand even  a vast army of four divisions.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्तं तदोवाच रक्ष्यमाणास्त्वयानघ। नात्र भीता वयं सर्वे धर्ममेवानुपश्यता।।2.51.8।।
explanation: Lakshmana said to Guha, O sinless one when all of us are under your righteous protection we have nothing to fear.

shloka_text: कथं दशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया। शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुं जीवितं वा सुखानि वा।।2.51.9।।
explanation: When Rama, son of Dasaratha, sleeps on the ground with Sita how can I sleep or live or enjoy pleasures?

shloka_text: यो न देवासुरैः सर्वैः शक्यः प्रसहितुं युधि। तं पश्य सुखसंविष्टं तृणेषु सह सीतया।।2.51.10।।
explanation: Look at that Rama whom all the gods and demons cannot face in war sleeps so comfortably on the grass with Sita.

shloka_text: यो मन्त्रतपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च पराश्रमैः। एको दशरथस्येष्टः पुत्रः सदृशलक्षणः।।2.51.11।। अस्मिन् प्रव्राजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति। विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति।।2.51.12।।
explanation: This favourite son of Dasaratha who has similar traits like his father was born after he rigorously practised austerities accompanied by (Vedic) mantras. When he is banished, the king will not live long. Surely this land will soon be widowed.

shloka_text: यो मन्त्रतपसा लब्धो विविधैश्च पराश्रमैः। एको दशरथस्येष्टः पुत्रः सदृशलक्षणः।।2.51.11।। अस्मिन् प्रव्राजिते राजा न चिरं वर्तयिष्यति। विधवा मेदिनी नूनं क्षिप्रमेव भविष्यति।।2.51.12।।
explanation: This favourite son of Dasaratha who has similar traits like his father was born after he rigorously practised austerities accompanied by (Vedic) mantras. When he is banished, the king will not live long. Surely this land will soon be widowed.

shloka_text: विनद्य सुमहानादं श्रमेणोपरताः स्त्रियः। निर्घोषोपरतं चातो मन्ये राजनिवेशनम्।।2.51.13।।
explanation: All the women having cried so much must have quietened down out of sheer exhaustion. That is why perhaps the sounds from the royal palace have ceased.

shloka_text: कौशल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम। नाशंसे यदि जीवन्ति सर्वे ते शर्वरीमिमाम्।।2.51.14।।
explanation: I doubt whether all of them -- the king, Kausalya and my mother -- can survive this night.

shloka_text: जीवेदपि हि मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्यान्ववेक्षया। तद्दुःखं यत्तु कौशल्या वीरसूर्विनशिष्यति।।2.51.15।।
explanation: My mother may live looking forward to Satrughna. But, alas Kausalya may die, separated from her valiant son.

shloka_text: अनुरक्तजनाकीर्णा सुखालोकप्रियावहा। राजव्यसनसंसृष्टा सा पुरी विनशिष्यति।।2.51.16।।
explanation: That city (of Ayodhya) is full of loyal people. It brings them happiness. It is dear to them. It will perish due to the sad demise of the king.

shloka_text: कथं पुत्रं महात्मानं ज्येष्ठं प्रियमपश्यतः। शरीरं धारयिष्यन्ति प्राणा राज्ञो महात्मनः।।2.51.17।।
explanation: How can the noble king survive unable to see his highsouled, beloved, eldest son?

shloka_text: विनष्टे नृपतौ पश्चात्कौसल्या विनशिष्यति। अनन्तरं च माताऽपि मम नाशमुपैष्यति।।2.51.18।।
explanation: Subsequent to the death of the king, Kausalya will die and my mother will follow her.

shloka_text: अतिक्रान्तमतिक्रान्तमनवाप्य मनोरथम्। राज्ये राममनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति।।2.51.19।।
explanation: Past is past (irreversible). My father, brooding over his desire of installing Rama as king unfulfilled, will perish.

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थाः पितरं वृत्तं तस्मिन्कालेऽप्युपस्थिते। प्रेतकार्येषु सर्वेषु संस्करिष्यन्ति भूमिपम्।।2.51.20।।
explanation: Those who will remain present around the king, my father, at the time of his death and perform the funeral rites have their desires fulfilled (for they could attend the king's obsequies).

shloka_text: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्पन्नाम् गणिकावरशोभिताम्।।2.51.21।। रथाश्वगजसम्बाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.51.22।। आरामोद्यानसम्पन्नां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.51.23।।
explanation: They will roam about happily in the capital city of my father with its lovely squares, wellaligned broad highways, its mansions and palaces, full of chariots, elephants, horses. It will be echoing with the sound of trumpets. It will be full of the welfare of all. It will be graced by the fairest of courtesans. Filled with wellnourished and contented people, the city dotted with several pleasuregardens and parks, will look splendid with community festivals and fairs.

shloka_text: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्पन्नाम् गणिकावरशोभिताम्।।2.51.21।। रथाश्वगजसम्बाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.51.22।। आरामोद्यानसम्पन्नां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.51.23।।
explanation: They will roam about happily in the capital city of my father with its lovely squares, wellaligned broad highways, its mansions and palaces, full of chariots, elephants, horses. It will be echoing with the sound of trumpets. It will be full of the welfare of all. It will be graced by the fairest of courtesans. Filled with wellnourished and contented people, the city dotted with several pleasuregardens and parks, will look splendid with community festivals and fairs.

shloka_text: रम्यचत्वरसंस्थानां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्पन्नाम् गणिकावरशोभिताम्।।2.51.21।। रथाश्वगजसम्बाधां तूर्यनादविनादिताम्। सर्वकल्याणसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम्।।2.51.22।। आरामोद्यानसम्पन्नां समाजोत्सवशालिनीम्। सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राजधानीं पितुर्मम।।2.51.23।।
explanation: They will roam about happily in the capital city of my father with its lovely squares, wellaligned broad highways, its mansions and palaces, full of chariots, elephants, horses. It will be echoing with the sound of trumpets. It will be full of the welfare of all. It will be graced by the fairest of courtesans. Filled with wellnourished and contented people, the city dotted with several pleasuregardens and parks, will look splendid with community festivals and fairs.

shloka_text: अपि जीवेद्दशरथो वनवासात्पुनर्वयम्। प्रत्यागम्य महात्मानमपि पश्येम सुव्रतम्।।2.51.24।।
explanation: Will the king be still alive? Will we see the noble king again on our return from exile after the fulfilment of his vows?

shloka_text: अपि सत्यप्रतिज्ञेन सार्धं कुशलिना वयम्। निवृत्ते वनवासेऽस्मिन्नयोध्यां प्रविशेमहि।।2.51.25।।
explanation: Will we ever be able, after completion of the exile, to enter the city of Ayodhya along with Rama who is true to his promise?

shloka_text: परिदेवयमानस्य दुखार्तस्य महात्मनः। तिष्ठतो राजपुत्रस्य शर्वरी साऽत्यवर्तत।।2.51.26।।
explanation: While that noble prince (Lakshmana), tormented with grief, stood thus wailing, the night passed off.

shloka_text: तथा हि सत्यं ब्रुवति प्रजाहिते नरेन्द्रपुत्रे गुरुसौहृदाद्गुहः। मुमोच बाष्पं व्यसनाभिपीडितो ज्वरातुरो नाग इव व्यथातुरः।।2.51.27।।
explanation: Out of great friendship with Guha, Lakshmana thus told the true story of prince (Rama) in the interest of his subject (Guha). (On hearing it) Guha was deeply afflicted with grief and pain and began shedding tears like an elephant suffering from fever. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्यकाण्डे एकपञ्चाश स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfirst sarga of Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पृथुवक्षा महायशाः। उवाच रामः सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्।।2.52.1।।
explanation: As the night advanced towards dawn, broadchested Rama of great renown said to Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, who had auspicious marks on his body:

shloka_text: भास्करोदयकालोऽयं गता भगवती निशा। असौ सुकृष्णो विहगः कोकिलस्तात कूजति।।2.52.2।।
explanation: O dear Lakshmana the holy night is over and it is time for sunrise. The deep dark bird, the cuckoo is singing.

shloka_text: बर्हिणानां च निर्घोषः श्रूयते नदतां वने। तराम जाह्नवीं सौम्य शीघ्रगां सागरङ्गमाम्।।2.52.3।।
explanation: Listen to the screams of the peacocks in the forest. The Ganga is flowing fast to merge in the sea. We need to cross it.

shloka_text: विज्ञाय रामस्य वचः सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः। गुहमामन्त्र्य सूतं च सोऽतिष्ठद्भ्रातुरग्रतः।।2.52.4।।
explanation: In response to Rama's desire, Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, one who brings joy to his friends, called Guha and the charioteer (Sumantra) and stood before his brother.

shloka_text: स तु रामस्य वचनं निशम्य प्रतिगृह्य च। स्थपतिस्तूर्णमाहूय सचिवानिदमब्रवीत्।।2.52.5।।
explanation: Having heard and accepted Rama's proposal, the king of the nisadas called his ministers at once and said:

shloka_text: अस्य वाहनसंयुक्तां कर्णग्राहवतीं शुभाम्। सुप्रतारां दृढां तीर्थे शीघ्रं नावमुपाहर।।2.52.6।।
explanation: Get quickly to the sacred bank (of  Ganga) a strong, auspicious boat equipped with rowing rods and helmsmen who can help cross the river with ease

shloka_text: तं निशम्य समादेशं गुहामात्यगणो महान्। उपोह्य रुचिरां नावं गुहाय प्रत्यवेदयत्।।2.52.7।।
explanation: The ministers heard the orders, soon brought  a beautiful boat and informed Guha (that his orders have been carried out).

shloka_text: ततः स प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा गुहो राघवमब्रवीत्। उपस्थितेयं नौर्देव भूयः किं करवाणि ते।।2.52.8।।
explanation: Then Guha with folded palms said to Rama: O king, the boat ready. Tell me what else can I do for you.

shloka_text: तवामरसुतप्रख्य तर्तुं सागरगां नदीम्। नौरियं पुरुषव्याघ्र तां त्वमारोह सुव्रत।।2.52.9।।
explanation: O best among men, renowned like a god's son and constantly engaged in vows, here is the boat for you to cross the Ganga flowing into the sea. Do board it.

shloka_text: अथोवाच महातेजा रामो गुहमिदं वचः। कृतकामोऽस्मि भवता शीघ्रमारोप्यतामिति।।2.52.10।।
explanation: Thereafter the radiant Rama said to Guha, You have fulfilled my desire. Keep all our belongings in the boat.

shloka_text: ततः कलापान् सन्नह्य खड्गौ बध्वा च धन्विनौ। जग्मतुर्येन तौ गङ्गां सीतया सह राघवौ।।2.52.11।।
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana then put on their quivers, fastened their swords and holding their bows went towards Ganga along with Sita.

shloka_text: राममेव तु धर्मज्ञमुपगम्य विनीतवत्। किमहं करवाणीति सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्।।2.52.12।।
explanation: The charioteer (Sumantra) approached the righteous Rama and asked him with folded hands: What can I do?

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीद्दाशरथिः सुमन्त्रं स्पृशन् करेणोत्तमदक्षिणेन। सुमन्त्र शीघ्रं पुनरेव याहि राज्ञः सकाशे भव चाप्रमत्तः।।2.52.13।।
explanation: Rama then caressed  Sumantra with his right hand and said, Sumantra, go back immediately and never be inattentive in serving the king.

shloka_text: निवर्तस्वेत्युवाचैव ह्येतावद्धि कृतं मम। रथं विहाय पद्भ्यां तु गमिष्यामि महावनम्।।2.52.14।।
explanation: You have done enough. I shall now leave the chariot and walk into the great forest.

shloka_text: आत्मानं त्वभ्यनुज्ञातमवेक्ष्यार्तः स सारथिः। सुमन्त्रः पुरुषव्याघ्रमैक्ष्वाकमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.52.15।।
explanation: Having been permitted to go, Sumantra, the distressed charioteer, said to Rama, the best among men, and a descendant of the Ikshvaku race:

shloka_text: नातिक्रान्तमिदं लोके पुरुषेणेह केनचित्। तव सभ्रातृभार्यस्य वासः प्राकृतवद्वने।।2.52.16।।
explanation: None else in this world would be able to live in the forest as you have resolved to, like a common man, along with your brother and spouse.

shloka_text: न मन्ये ब्रह्मचर्येऽस्ति स्वधीते वा फलोदयः। मार्दवार्जवयोर्वापि त्वां चेद्व्यसनमागतम्।।2.52.17।।
explanation: If your celibacy and your grief are the consequences of your study of the Vedic lore, your compassionate nature and simplicity of character, I think there is no use of all these (virtues).

shloka_text: सह राघव वैदेह्या भ्रात्रा चैव वने वसन्। त्वं गतिं प्राप्स्यसे वीर त्रीन् लोकांस्तु जयन्निव।।2.52.18।।
explanation: Valiant scion of the Raghus dwelling in the forest along with Vaidehi (Sita) and brother Lakshmana you will attain the status as if you have won the three worlds.

shloka_text: वयं खलु हता राम ये त्वयाप्युपवञ्चिताः। कैकेय्या वशमेष्यामः पापाया दुःखभागिनः।।2.52.19।।
explanation: Deprived of you, O Rama we will come under the control of that sinful Kaikeyi. We will suffer and die.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवन्नात्मसमं सुमन्त्रः सारथिस्तदा। दृष्ट्वा दूरगतं रामं दुःखार्तो रुरुदे चिरम्।।2.52.20।।
explanation: Rama was like his (Sumantra's) own self. When Sumantra, the charioteer, saw that  Rama was preparing to go afar for a long time, he started weeping aloud in deep distress.

shloka_text: ततस्तु विगते बाष्पे सूतं स्पृष्टोदकं शुचिम्। रामस्तु मधुरं वाक्यं पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्।।2.52.21।।
explanation: After the flow of tears ceased Sumantra took a sip of water and became sanctified. Then Rama addressed him with sweet words over and over again:

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां त्वया तुल्यं सुहृदं नोपलक्षये। यथा दशरथो राजा मां न शोचेत्तथा कुरु।।2.52.22।।
explanation: I find none else like you as friendly as you are to the Ikshvaku race. So do whatever you like  to see that king Dasaratha does not brood over me.

shloka_text: शोकोपहतचेताश्च वृद्धश्च जगतीपतिः। कामभावावसन्नश्च तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते।।2.52.23।।
explanation: I tell you this because the lord of the earth (Dasaratha), is in deep distress. He is old. And he is under the control of his passion.

shloka_text: यद्यदाज्ञापयेत्किञ्चित्स महात्मा महीपतिः। कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं कार्यं तदविकाङ्क्षया।।2.52.24।।
explanation: To make Kaikeyi  happy, do whatever little the great king Dasaratha orders you to do.

shloka_text: एतदर्थं हि राज्यानि प्रशासति नरेश्वराः। यदेषां सर्वकृत्येषु मनो न प्रतिहन्यते।।2.52.25।।
explanation: The minds of kings create no hurdles in all that they want to do. That is why they rule kingdoms.

shloka_text: यद्यथा स महाराजो नालीकमधिगच्छति। न च ताम्यति दुःखेन सुमन्त्र कुरु तत्तथा।।2.52.26।।
explanation: Sumantra do things exactly in the manner the great king desires so that he does not feel sad or disappointed.

shloka_text: अदृष्टदुःखं राजानं वृद्धमार्यं जितेन्द्रियम्। ब्रूयास्त्वमभिवाद्यैव मम हेतोरिदं वचः।।2.52.27।।
explanation: After offering your salutations, tell these words, on my behalf, to the king who is respectable, bent with age and who has conquered his senses and never experienced any sorrow before.

shloka_text: नैवाहमनुशोचामि लक्ष्मणो न च मैथिली। अयोध्यायाश्च्युताश्चेति वने वत्स्यामहेति च।।2.52.28।।
explanation: I do not regret my banishment from Ayodhya to live in the forest. Neither Lakshmana nor Sita does.

shloka_text: चतुर्दशसु वर्षेषु निवृत्तेषु पुनः पुनः। लक्ष्मणं मां च सीतां च द्रक्ष्यसे क्षिप्रमागतान्।।2.52.29।।
explanation: Very quickly these fourteen years will come to an end and we will return (to Ayodhya). Then you will see me, Lakshmana and Sita off and on.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं मातरं च सुमन्त्र मे। अन्याश्च देवीस्सहिताः कैकेयीं च पुनः पुनः।।2.52.30।। आरोग्यं ब्रूहि कौशल्यामथ पादाभिवन्दनम्। सीताया मम चाऽऽर्यस्य वचनाल्लक्ष्मणस्य च।।2.52.31।।
explanation: Having said this to the king, O Sumantra tell my mother, the other queens including Kaikeyi again and again about my wellbeing and the wellbeing of Lakshmana and Sita. Convey our respectful salutations at the feet of mother Kausalya.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु राजानं मातरं च सुमन्त्र मे। अन्याश्च देवीस्सहिताः कैकेयीं च पुनः पुनः।।2.52.30।। आरोग्यं ब्रूहि कौशल्यामथ पादाभिवन्दनम्। सीताया मम चाऽऽर्यस्य वचनाल्लक्ष्मणस्य च।।2.52.31।।
