shloka_text: यत्प्रधानाऽसि तत्पापं मयि पित्रा विनाकृते। भ्रातृभ्यां च परित्यक्ते सर्वलोकस्य चाप्रिये।।2.74.11।।
explanation: The sin you have committed with a particular objective has affected me and (as a result) I am left without my father. I am abandoned by my brothers. I am hated by every one in this entire world.

shloka_text: कौसल्यां धर्मसंयुक्तां वियुक्तां पापनिश्चये। कृत्वा कं प्राप्स्यसे त्वद्य लोकं निरयगामिनि।।2.74.12।।
explanation: O woman of sinful convictions you will go to hell. You have separated righteous Kausalya from her son. For having committed such a sin, what afterworld awaits you  (is not known)?

shloka_text: किं नावबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतं बन्धुसंश्रयम्। ज्येष्ठं पितृसमं रामं कौसल्यायाऽत्मसम्भवम्।।2.74.13।।
explanation: O cruel one why do you not realise that Rama, born of Kausalya, is the eldest son and equal to my father? He is selfrestrained and a refuge to his kith and kin.

shloka_text: अङगप्रत्यङगजः पुत्रो हृदयाच्चापि जायते। तस्मात्प्रियतमो मातुः प्रिया एव तु बान्धवाः।।2.74.14।।
explanation: A son born from every limb, big or small, and from the heart is the most beloved of all for his mother while the other relatives are only loving ones.

shloka_text: अन्यदा किल धर्मज्ञा सुरभि स्सुरसम्मता। वहमानौ ददर्शोर्व्यां पुत्रौ विगतचेतसौ।।2.74.15।।
explanation: It is said that once upon a time Surabhi, the divine cow, highly respected by the gods and conversant with righteous ways, beheld her two sons who fainted due to fatigue while carrying the burden of the ploughs.

shloka_text: तावर्धदिवसे श्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रौ महीतले। रुरोद पुत्रशोकेन बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा।।2.74.16।।
explanation: On seeing her two sons lying on earth exhausted, she wailed in distress for them with her eyes filled with tears.

shloka_text: अधस्ताद्व्रजतस्तस्याः सुरराज्ञो महात्मनः। बिन्दवः पतिता गात्रे सूक्ष्मा स्सुरभिगन्धिनः।।2.74.17।।
explanation: The fine drops of her fragnant tears trickled down the body of the great king of the gods (Indra).

shloka_text: ﻿इन्द्रोऽप्यश्रुनिपातं तं स्वगात्रे पुण्यगन्धिनम्। सुरभिं मन्यते दृष्ट्वा भूयसीं तां सुरेश्वरः।।2.74.18।।
explanation: ﻿ When Indra, lord of the gods, saw those tears of holy fragrance fallen on his body he understood that the tears were shed by the venerated Kamadhenu.

shloka_text: निरीक्षमाण श्शक्रस्तां ददर्श सुरभिं स्थिताम्। आकाशे विष्ठितां दीनां रुदन्तीं भृशदुःखिताम्।।2.74.19।।
explanation: While looking around Indra beheld Kamadhenu in intense pain stationed in the sky,   looking distressed and miserable, and wailing.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा शोकसन्तप्तां वज्रपाणिर्यशस्विनीम्। इन्द्रः प्राञ्जलिरुद्विग्न स्सुरराजोऽब्रवीद्वचः।।2.74.20।।
explanation: The king of the gods, Indra, wielder of thunderbolt, saw the renowned Kamadhenu consumed with grief. Alarmed, he said to her with palms joined in reverence:

shloka_text: भयं कच्छिन्न चास्मासु कुतश्चिद्विद्यते महत्। कुतोनिमत्तश्शोकस्ते ब्रूहि सर्वहितैषिणि।।2.74.21।।
explanation: 'O holy cow fear not. You wish the welfare of all, Has any great calamity befallen us from any quarter? I hope not. What is the reason for your sorrow? Tell me'.

shloka_text: ﻿एवमुक्ता तु सुरभि स्सुरराजेन धीमता। प्रत्युवाच ततो धीरा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदा।।2.74.22।।
explanation: ﻿ On hearing the sagacious Indra, king of the gods, Kamadhenu, proficient in speech, calmly replied:

shloka_text: शान्तं पापं न वः किञ्चित्कुतश्चिदमराधिपः। अहं मग्नौ तु शोचामि स्वपुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ।।2.74.23।। एतौ दृष्ट्वा कृशौ दीनौ सूर्यरश्मिप्रतापितौ। बाध्यमानौ बलीवर्धौ कर्षकेण सुराधिप।।2.74.24।।
explanation: 'God forbid, O Indra, lord of the Immortals no calamity has befallen you from any quarter. Only I am in trouble. I am weeping for these pair of bulls, my own sons who are in difficulty. When I see them scorched by the rays of the Sun, miserable, emaciated and weeping, beaten by a ploughman, I am immersed in grief'.

shloka_text: शान्तं पापं न वः किञ्चित्कुतश्चिदमराधिपः। अहं मग्नौ तु शोचामि स्वपुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ।।2.74.23।। एतौ दृष्ट्वा कृशौ दीनौ सूर्यरश्मिप्रतापितौ। बाध्यमानौ बलीवर्धौ कर्षकेण सुराधिप।।2.74.24।।
explanation: 'God forbid, O Indra, lord of the Immortals no calamity has befallen you from any quarter. Only I am in trouble. I am weeping for these pair of bulls, my own sons who are in difficulty. When I see them scorched by the rays of the Sun, miserable, emaciated and weeping, beaten by a ploughman, I am immersed in grief'.

shloka_text: ममकायात्प्रसूतौ हि दुःखितौ भारपीडितौ। यौ दृष्ट्वा परितप्येऽहं नास्ति पुत्रसमः प्रियः।।2.74.25।।
explanation: 'These bulls were born from my body and they are oppressed by the burden. Having seen their anguish, I am extremely grieved. There is none so dear as a son'.

shloka_text: यस्याः पुत्रसहस्रैस्तु कृत्स्नं व्याप्तमिदं जगत्। तां दृष्ट्वा रुदतीं शक्रो न सुतान्मन्यते परम्।।2.74.26।।
explanation: The wishfulfilling cow (Kamadhenu) had innumerable sons spread all over the world. When Indra saw that Kamadhenu too was weeping for her sons, he concluded 'there is no one greater than a son'.

shloka_text: ﻿सदाऽप्रतिमवृत्तायाः लोकधारणकाम्यया। श्रीमत्या गुणनित्याया स्स्वभावपरिचेष्टया।।2.74.27।। यस्याः पुत्रसहस्राणि साऽपि शोचति कामधुक्। किं पुनर्या विना रामं कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति।।2.74.28।।
explanation: ﻿ Wishing always to nourish the worlds Kamadhenu conducts herself with an unequalled character. In accordance with her nature, she has imbibed in herself eminent virtues. She is endowed with all prosperity. In spite of her thousand sons, she is weeping thus for her two bulls, what can one say of Kausalya separated from her only son Will she be her normal self again?'

shloka_text: ﻿सदाऽप्रतिमवृत्तायाः लोकधारणकाम्यया। श्रीमत्या गुणनित्याया स्स्वभावपरिचेष्टया।।2.74.27।। यस्याः पुत्रसहस्राणि साऽपि शोचति कामधुक्। किं पुनर्या विना रामं कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति।।2.74.28।।
explanation: ﻿ Wishing always to nourish the worlds Kamadhenu conducts herself with an unequalled character. In accordance with her nature, she has imbibed in herself eminent virtues. She is endowed with all prosperity. In spite of her thousand sons, she is weeping thus for her two bulls, what can one say of Kausalya separated from her only son Will she be her normal self again?'

shloka_text: एकपुत्रा च साध्वी च विवत्सेयं त्वया कृता। तस्मात्त्वं सततं दुःखं प्रेत्य चेह च लप्स्यसे।।2.74.29।।
explanation: This pious lady is blessed with only one son and (now) has been rendered childless by you. Therefore, you shall experience grief in this world and hereafter.

shloka_text: अहं ह्यपचितिं भ्रातुः पितुश्च सकलामिमाम्। वर्धनं यशसश्चापि करिष्यामि न संशयः।।2.74.30।।
explanation: As for me, I shall do whatever is necessary for the atonement of the improper conduct shown towards my father and brother and for enhancement of my fame. There is no doubt  about it.

shloka_text: ﻿अनाययित्वा तनयं कौसल्याया महाबलम्। स्वयमेव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनं मुनिनिषेवितम्।।2.74.31।।
explanation: ﻿ If I fail to bring back the mighty son of Kausalya, I shall enter the forest frequented by ascetics.

shloka_text: न ह्यहं पापसङ्कल्पे पापे पापं त्वया कृतम्। शक्तो धारयितुं पौरैरश्रुकण्ठै र्निरीक्षितः।।2.74.32।।
explanation: O vicious one, O evilintentioned one being watched by the citizens with their throats choked with tears of grief, I cannot endure the burden of the sin committed by you.

shloka_text: सा त्वमग्निं प्रविश वा स्वयं वा दण्डकान्विश। रज्जुं बधान वा कण्ठे न हि तेऽन्यत्परायणम्।।2.74.33।।
explanation: Jump into the fire or go to Dandaka forest or hang yourself. There is no other recourse for you.

shloka_text: अहमप्यवनीं प्राप्ते रामे सत्यपराक्रमे। कृतकृत्यो भविष्यामि विप्रवासितकल्मषः।।2.74.34।।
explanation: When Rama who has truth as his prowess accepts the kingdom, I shall have accomplished my purpose at last and I shall be free from all blemishes.

shloka_text: इति नाग इवारण्ये तोमराङ्कुशचोदितः। पपात भुवि सङ्कृद्धो निश्श्वसन्निव पन्नगः।।2.74.35।।
explanation: In this way like an elephant driven by prods and goads in the forest, highly enraged Bharata hissing like a serpent dropped down on the ground.

shloka_text: संरक्तनेत्र श्शिथिलाम्भरस्तदा विधूतसर्वाभरणः परन्तपः। बभूव भूमौ पतितो नृपात्मजश्शचीपतेः केतुरिवोत्सवक्षये।।2.74.36।।
explanation: Prince Bharata, the scorcher of enemies, with bloodshot eyes, raiment in disarray, ornaments tossed about lay fallen on the ground like the banner of Indra (husband of Sachi) at the close of the festival of flaghoisting. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुस्सप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyfourth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: दीर्घकालात्समुत्थाय संज्ञां लब्ध्वा च वीर्यवान्। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां दीनामुद्वीक्ष्य मातरम्।।2.75.1।। सोऽमात्यमध्ये भरतो जननीमभ्यकुत्सयत्।
explanation: On regaining his senses after a long time, the valiant Bharata looked at his unfortunate mother whose eyes were filled with tears, and condemned her amidst the counsellors.

shloka_text: राज्यं न कामये जातु मन्त्रये नापि मातरम्।।2.75.2।। अभिषेकं न जानामि योऽभूद्राज्ञा समीक्षितः। विप्रकृष्टेह्यहं देशे शत्रुघ्नसहितोऽवसम्।।2.75.3।।
explanation: Neither did I ever desire the kingdom nor did I ever consult my mother in this regard and I am not even aware of the consecration that was planned by the king for I was away in a distant country with Satrughna.

shloka_text: राज्यं न कामये जातु मन्त्रये नापि मातरम्।।2.75.2।। अभिषेकं न जानामि योऽभूद्राज्ञा समीक्षितः। विप्रकृष्टेह्यहं देशे शत्रुघ्नसहितोऽवसम्।।2.75.3।।
explanation: Neither did I ever desire the kingdom nor did I ever consult my mother in this regard and I am not even aware of the consecration that was planned by the king for I was away in a distant country with Satrughna.

shloka_text: वनवासं न जानामि रामस्याहं महात्मनः। विवासनं वा सौमित्रे स्सीतायाश्च यथाऽभवत्।।2.75.4।।
explanation: I knew nothing of the banishment of great Rama nor did I know how Lakshmana or Sita had gone on exile.

shloka_text: तथैव क्रोशतस्तस्य भरतस्य महात्मनः। कौसल्या शब्दमाज्ञाय सुमित्रामिदमब्रवीत्।।2.75.5।।
explanation: As magnanimous Bharata was wailing, Kausalya recognised his voice and said to Sumitra:

shloka_text: आगतः क्रूरकार्यायाः कैकेय्या भरतस्सुतः। तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भरतं दीर्घदर्शिनम्।।2.75.6।।
explanation: Bharata, the farsighted son of Kaikeyi of cruel deeds has come and I wish to see him.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा सुमित्रां सा विवर्णा मलिना कृशा। प्रतस्थे भरतो यत्र वेपमाना विचेतना।।2.75.7।।
explanation: Having said so to Sumitra, Kausalya trembling and almost lifeless, emaciated, sullied and turned pallid set out for the place where Bharat was.

shloka_text: स तु रामानुजश्चापि शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा। प्रतस्थे भरतो यत्र कौसल्याया निवेशनम्।।2.75.8।।
explanation: But at the same time Bharata, the younger brother of Rama accompanied by Satrughna  proceeded to the place where Kausalya resided.

shloka_text: तत श्शत्रुघ्नभरतौ कौसल्यां प्रेक्ष्य दुःखितौ। पर्यष्वजेतां दुःखार्तां पतितां नष्टचेतसाम्।।2.75.9।। रुदन्तौ रुदतीं दुःखात्समेत्यार्यां मनस्स्विनीम्।
explanation: Then agonised Bharata and Satrughna, beholding that venerable, noblehearted, griefstricken, weeping Kausalya who was  almost semiconscious overcome with grief, approached her with great sorrow and hugged her.

shloka_text: भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं कौसल्या भृशदुःखिता।।2.75.10।। इदं ते राज्यकामस्य राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्। संप्राप्तं बत कैकेय्या शशीघ्रं क्रूरेण कर्मणा।।2.75.11।।
explanation: Looking at Bharata, the deeply afflicted Kausalya said, The kingdom which you had desired has been acquired without any obstacle. Alas Kaikeyi had quickly secured it for you  through her crooked act.

shloka_text: भरतं प्रत्युवाचेदं कौसल्या भृशदुःखिता।।2.75.10।। इदं ते राज्यकामस्य राज्यं प्राप्तमकण्टकम्। संप्राप्तं बत कैकेय्या शशीघ्रं क्रूरेण कर्मणा।।2.75.11।।
explanation: Looking at Bharata, the deeply afflicted Kausalya said, The kingdom which you had desired has been acquired without any obstacle. Alas Kaikeyi had quickly secured it for you  through her crooked act.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य चीरवसनं पुत्रं मे वनवासिनम्। कैकेयी कं गुणं तत्र पश्यति क्रूरदर्शिनी।।2.75.12।।
explanation: What advantage did cruel Kaikeyi visualize in sending away my son to dwell in the forest  wearing robes of bark?

shloka_text: क्षिप्रं मामपि कैकेयी प्रस्थापयितुमर्हति। हिरण्यनाभो यत्रास्ते सुतो मे सुमहायशाः।।2.75.13।।
explanation: Kaikeyi should send me also without any delay to that place where my illustrious Rama with golden navel dwells.

shloka_text: अथवा स्वयमेवाहं सुमित्रानुचरा सुखम्। अग्निहोत्रं पुरस्कृत्य प्रस्थास्ये यत्र राघवः।।2.75.14।।
explanation: Or else I, accompanied by Sumitra, shall go happily on my own holding the sacred fire in front to that place where Rama dwells.

shloka_text: कामं वा स्वयमेवाद्य तत्र मां नेतुमर्हसि। यत्रासौ पुरुषव्याघ्रः पुत्रो मे तप्यते तपः।।2.75.15।।
explanation: Or, you should now take me personally to that place where, my son Rama, the best among men, is performing austerities.

shloka_text: इदं हि तव विस्तीर्णं धनधान्यसमाचितम्। हस्त्वश्वरथसम्पूर्णं राज्यं निर्यातितं तया।।2.75.16।।
explanation: This vast kingdom, with all its abundance of wealth and grain, elephants, horses and chariots has been delivered to you by her.

shloka_text: इत्यादिबहुभिर्वाक्यैः क्रूरैः सम्भर्त्सितोऽनघः। विव्यथे भरतस्तीव्रं व्रणे तुद्येव सूचिना।।2.75.17।।
explanation: Thus reproached by many a harsh word, like needle pricking a wound, the sinless Bharata was intensely pained.

shloka_text: पपात चरणौ तस्यास्तदा सम्भ्रान्तचेतनः। विलप्य बहुधाऽसंज्ञो लब्धसंज्ञस्ततः स्थितः।।2.75.18।।
explanation: (Having heard these words), his senses reeling, he became unconscious, lamented profusaly and fell at her feet. And on regaining his senses, he stood motionless.

shloka_text: एवं विलपमानां तां भरतः प्राञ्जलिस्तदा। कौसल्यां प्रत्युवाचेदं शोकैर्बहुभिरावृताम्।।2.75.19।।
explanation: As Kausalya was lamenting in this manner, overwhelmed with deep grief, Bharata, his palms joined in reverence, replied her in these words:

shloka_text: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकिल्बिषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थिरां जानासि राघवे।।2.75.20।।
explanation: O noble lady unaware (of what had happened), I am guiltless. Why do you upbraid me? You know well my profound, steadfast affection for Raghava (Rama).

shloka_text: कृता शास्त्रानुगा बुद्धिर्माभूत्तस्य कदाचन। सत्यसन्ध स्सतां श्रेष्ठो यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.21।।
explanation: Did not the one who counselled the banishment of my noble brother who is steadfast and bound by truth and virtue, ever adhered to scriptures? (or) My noble brother (Rama), the best among the virtuous, bound to truth, is banished. Let not such thought occur at any time to one who steadfastly adheres to scriptures

shloka_text: प्रेष्यं पापीयसां यातु सूर्यञ्च प्रतिमेहतु। हन्तु पादेन गां सुप्तां यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.22।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother, Rama be cursed with the sin of undergoing servitude in the hands of most sinful of men, the sin of passing urine facing the Sun and of kicking a sleeping cow.

shloka_text: कारयित्वा महत्कर्म भर्ता भृत्यमनर्थकम्। अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्याऽर्योऽनुमतेगतः।।2.75.23।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the demerit of unrighteousness in the same way as a master who gets a difficult work done by a servant without remuneration.

shloka_text: परिपालयमानस्य राज्ञो भूतानि पुयत्रवत्। ततस्नु दुह्यतां पापं यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.24।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way as a man  acting treacherously against a king who rules like a father and protects his subjects like his own children, acquires.

shloka_text: बलिषड्भागमुद्धृत्य नृपस्यारक्षतः प्रजाः। अधर्मो योऽस्य सोऽस्यास्तु यस्यार्थोऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.25।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire unrighteousness in the same way as a king who, having received one sixth of the income as tax from people does not protect them

shloka_text: संश्रुत्य च तपस्विभ्यस्सत्रे वै यज्ञदक्षिणाम्। तां विप्रलपतां पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.26।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way as a person acquires for having promised the ascetics the required offering at a sacrifice and later denies them

shloka_text: हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधे युद्धे शस्त्रसमाकुले। मा स्म कार्षीत्सतां धर्मं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.27।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the demerit in the same way as a person, who having gone to the battleground abundantly provided with elephants, horses, chariots and weapons fails to discharge the duty (of a fighter)

shloka_text: उपदिष्टं सुसूक्ष्मार्थं शास्त्रं यत्नेन धीमता। स नाशयतु दुष्टात्मा यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.28।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire demerit in the same way as an evilhearted person who forever destroys the subtle meaning of the scriptures imparted carefully by a sagacious preceptor

shloka_text: मा च तं व्यूढबाह्वंसं चन्द्रार्कसमतेजसम्। द्राक्षीद्राज्यस्थमासीनं यस्यार्योऽनुमतेगतः।।2.75.29।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother be highly unfortunate like me in not being able to behold that longarmed and broadshoulderd one seated on the throne and resembling both the Sun and the Moon in radiance

shloka_text: पायसं कृसरं छागं वृथा सोऽश्नातु निर्घृणः। गुरूंश्चाप्यवजानातु यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.30।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the demerit in the same way as a person, who partakes the sweet milkrice, sesamerice and goat's flesh without purpose (without invoking and offering it to the gods) and disrespects the teachers

shloka_text: गाश्च स्पृशतु पादेन गुरून्परिवदेत्स्वयम्। मित्रे द्रुह्येत सोऽत्यन्तं यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.31।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a person who kicks the cows abuses elders and causes great offence to his friends

shloka_text: विश्वासात्कथितं किञ्चित्परिवादं मिथः क्वचित्। विवृणोतु स दुष्टात्मा यस्याऽर्योऽमते गतः।।2.75.32।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother, acquire the sin in the same way as a wickedminded person, who divulges the words of abuse secretly confided in him by his friends.

shloka_text: अकर्ता ह्यकृतज्ञश्च त्यक्ताचाऽत्मा निरपत्रपः। लोके भवतु विद्विष्टो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.33।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother be hated universally as one who never helps any one, who is ungrateful, shameless and as one who has committed the sin of suicide

shloka_text: पुत्रैर्दारैश्च भृत्यैश्च स्वगृहे परिवारितः। स एको मृष्टमश्नातु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.34।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother  acquire the sin in the same way as one who, although surrounded by wife, children and servants, eats the delicacies all alone without sharing acquires.

shloka_text: अप्राप्य सदृशान् दाराननपत्यः प्रमीयताम्। अनवाप्य क्रियां धर्म्यां यस्याऽर्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.35।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother die without winning a worthy wife and without begetting offspring and without performing religious deeds

shloka_text: माऽत्मनस्सन्ततिं द्राक्षीत्स्वेषु दारेषु दुःखितः। आयुस्समग्रमप्राप्य यऽस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.36।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother live an entire life of anguish without begetting children through his wife or without seeing his own children

shloka_text: राजस्त्रीबालवृद्धानां वधे यत्पापमुच्यते। भृत्यत्यागे च यत्पापं तत्पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्।।2.75.37।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the same sin as one acquires for murdering a king, a woman, children and the aged and deserting dependents

shloka_text: लाक्षया मधुमांसेन लोहेन च विषेण च। सदैव बिभृयाद्भृत्यान्यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.38।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the same sin as one who supports his wife and children by trafficking in lac, wine, meat and metal and poison acquires

shloka_text: सङ्ग्रमे समुपोढे स्म शत्रुपक्षभयङ्करे। पलायामानो वध्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.39।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the same sin like a warrior, dreadful to the enemy side who will be slain while fleeing from the war at its peak

shloka_text: कपालपाणिः पृथिवीमटतां चीरसंवृतः। भिक्षमाणो यथोन्मत्तो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.40।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother, wander this earth, begging alms, holding a human skull like an insane man dressed in rags

shloka_text: मद्ये प्रसक्तो भवतु स्त्रीष्वक्षेषु च नित्यशः। कामक्रोधाभिभूतस्तु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.41।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother be always addicted to wine, women and gambling and be swayed by desire and anger

shloka_text: मास्म धर्मे मनो भूयादधर्मं स निषेवताम्। अपात्रवर्षी भवतु यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.42।।
explanation: May the mind of that man who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother not be established in virtue May he practise unrighteousness and confer charity on the unworthy

shloka_text: सञ्चितान्यस्य वित्तनि विविधानि सहस्रशः। दस्युभिर्विप्रलुप्यन्तां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.43।।
explanation: May that man's accumulated extensive posssessions of various kinds of wealth be  snatched away by thieves in thousands of ways if he had counselled the exile of my esteemed brother

shloka_text: उभे सन्ध्ये शयानस्य यत्पापं परिकल्प्यते। तच्चपापं भवेत्तस्य यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.44।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the extent of demerit fixed for a person, who sleeps at the hour of twilight of dawn and dusk

shloka_text: यदग्निदायके पापं यत्पापं गुरतल्पगे। मित्रद्रोहे च यत्पापं तत्पापं प्रतिपद्यताम्।।2.75.45।।
explanation: May that one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way as a person who sets fire to human settlements, violates the preceptors's bed and betrays his friend

shloka_text: देवतानां पित्रूणां च मातापित्रोस्तथैव च। मा स्म कार्षीत्स शुश्रूषां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.46।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother, acquire the sin in the same way as a person who fails to show obedience to the gods and the ancestors and to serve his parents

shloka_text: सतां लोकात्सतां कीर्त्या स्सञ्जुष्टात्कर्मणस्तथा। भ्रश्यतु क्षिप्रमद्यैव यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.47।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother be expelled  this very moment from the world approved by virtuous men, from their renown and from their (noble) actions

shloka_text: अपास्य मातृशुश्रूषामनर्थे सोऽवतिष्ठताम्। दीर्घबाहुर्महावक्षा: यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.48।।
explanation: The one who counselled the exile of my noble, longarmed and broadchested brother be banished like the one who commited the sin of leaving the ministration to his mother and engaging himself in purposeless acts

shloka_text: बहुपुत्रो दरिद्रश्च ज्वररोगसमन्वितः। स भूयात्सतत क्लेशी यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.49।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother be always miserable with many sons, poverty and fever and disease

shloka_text: आशामाशंसमानानां दीनानामूर्ध्वचक्षुषाम्। अर्थिनां वितथां कुर्याद्यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.50।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a person disappoints who miserable mendicants seeking alms and looking up to him for help

shloka_text: मायया रमतां नित्यं परुषः पिशुनोऽशुचिः। राज्ञो भीतस्त्वधर्मात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.51।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way as a person, who is abusive, niggardly, impure, unrighteous and always afraid of being caught by the king, and lives by cheating others, acquires

shloka_text: ऋतुस्नातां सतीं भार्यामृतुकालानुरोधिनीम्। अतिवर्तेत दुष्टात्मा यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.52।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way as a wickedminded person who neglects his chaste wife observing the menstrual period unfavourable for conception and had bathed after menstruation  acquires

shloka_text: सधर्मदारान्परित्यज्य परदारान्निषेवताम्। त्यक्तधर्मरतिर्मूढो यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.53।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a foolish person who abandons righteous conduct and  forsakes his rightfully married wife and resorts to other man's wife acquires

shloka_text: विप्रलुप्तप्रजातस्य दुष्कृतं ब्राह्मणस्य यत्। तदेव प्रतिपद्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.54।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the same sin like that of a lowbred brahmin who commits an irreversible sin acquires

shloka_text: पानीयदूषके पापं तथैव विषदायके। यत्तदेकस्स लभतां यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.55।।
explanation: May the sin of polluting drinking water and administering poison to others be put together and be incurred by the man who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणायोद्यतां पूजां विहन्तु कलुषेन्द्रियः। बालवत्सां च गां दोग्धु यस्यार्यो ऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.56।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a person with befouled senses disturbs the offerings of worship kept ready for a brahmin and milks the cow having a young calf acquires.

shloka_text: तुर्ष्णार्तं सति पानीये विप्रलम्भेन योजयेत्। लभेत तस्य यत्पापं यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.57।।
explanation: May the one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a person who in possession of water does not give it to one suffering from thirst acquires it

shloka_text: भक्त्या विवदमानेषु मार्गमाश्रित्य पश्यतः। तस्य पापेन युज्येत यस्यार्योऽनुमते गतः।।2.75.58।।
explanation: May that one who counselled the exile of my esteemed brother acquire the sin in the same way a person acquires while giving onesided judgement between divided religious disputants

shloka_text: विहीनां पतिपुत्राभ्यां कौसल्यां पार्थिवात्मजः। एवमाश्वासयन्नेव दुःखार्तो निपपात ह।।2.75.59।।
explanation: While thus appeasing Kausalya deprived of her husband and son, Bharata, filled with grief, fell down at her feet.

shloka_text: तथा तु शपथैः कष्टै श्शपमानमचेतनम्। भरतं शोकसन्तप्तं कौसल्या वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।2.75.60।।
explanation: Kausalya said these words to Bharata who fell unconscious, consumed with grief, while swearing on painful oaths.

shloka_text: मम दुःखमिदं पुत्र भूयस्समुपजायते। शपथै श्शपमानो हि प्राणानुपरुणत्सि मे।।2.75.61।।
explanation: O son by swearing on oaths, you are choking the very breath of my life and my suffering has grown still more.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या न चलितो धर्मादात्मा ते सहलक्ष्मणः। वत्स सत्यप्रतिज्ञो ते सतां लोकमवाप्स्यसि।।2.75.62।।
explanation: O dear child, fortunately your mind is unswerved from righteousness. You being truthful to your promise shall attain the world of virtuous men along with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा चाङ्कमानीय भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्। परिष्वज्य महाबाहुं रुरोद भृशदुःखिता।।2.75.63।।
explanation: After having addressed Bharata, who was affectionate towards his brother that way, Kausalya  drew the mightyarmed one onto her lap and hugged him and cried out with extreme grief.

shloka_text: एवं विलपमानस्य दुःखार्तस्य महात्मनः। मोहाच्च शोकसम्रोधाद्बभूव लुलितं मनः।।2.75.64।।
explanation: Afflicted by sorrow and lamenting thus, great Bharata's mind became unsteady owing to swooning and  besieged by grief.

shloka_text: तमेवं शोकसन्तप्तं भरतं कैकयी सुतम्। उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठ श्श्रेष्ठवागृषिः।।2.76.1।।
explanation: Vasistha, the most eloquent and the best of ascetics said to Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi who was tormented with grief:

shloka_text: अलं शोकेन भद्रं ते राजपुत्र महायशः। प्राप्तकालं नरपतेः कुरु संयानमुत्तमम्।।2.76.2।।
explanation: O prince of great renown, may God bless you It is not proper on your part to grieve. It is time to perform the funeral rites of the king in the best way possible.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठस्य वच श्शृत्वा भरतो धारणां गतः। प्रेतकार्याणि सर्वाणि कारयामास धर्मवित्।।2.76.3।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Vasistha, dutiful Bharata regained his steadiness and engaged in the performance of the funeral rites.

shloka_text: उद्धृतं तैलसंरोधात्सतु भूमौ निवेशितम्। आपीतवर्णवदनं प्रसुप्तमिव भूमिपम्।।2.76.4।। संवेश्य शयने चाग्य्रे नानारत्नपरिष्कृते। ततो दशरथं पुत्रो विललाप सुदुःखितः।।2.76.5।।
explanation: The mortal remains of king Dasaratha, protector of the earth, was taken out of the oil container and placed on the floor. His pale, yellow face appeared as if he was asleep. Thereafter it was laid upon a magnificent couch adorned with every kind of gem. On seeing Dasaratha in that state  Bharata lamented in extreme distress.

shloka_text: उद्धृतं तैलसंरोधात्सतु भूमौ निवेशितम्। आपीतवर्णवदनं प्रसुप्तमिव भूमिपम्।।2.76.4।। संवेश्य शयने चाग्य्रे नानारत्नपरिष्कृते। ततो दशरथं पुत्रो विललाप सुदुःखितः।।2.76.5।।
explanation: The mortal remains of king Dasaratha, protector of the earth, was taken out of the oil container and placed on the floor. His pale, yellow face appeared as if he was asleep. Thereafter it was laid upon a magnificent couch adorned with every kind of gem. On seeing Dasaratha in that state  Bharata lamented in extreme distress.

shloka_text: किं ते व्यवसितं राजन् प्रोषिते मय्यनागते। विवास्य रामं धर्मज्ञं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।।2.76.6।।
explanation: What have you done, O king, between my absence and my arrival? You have banished the righteous Rama and the valiant Lakshmana.

shloka_text: क्व यास्यसि महाराज हित्वेमं दुःखितं जनम्। हीनं पुरुषसिंहेन रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।।2.76.7।।
explanation: O great king Where will you go leaving me who is bewailing for having been left by Rama, the lion among men and a man of pious deeds?

shloka_text: योगक्षेमं तु ते राजन् कोऽस्मिन्कल्पयिता पुरे त्वयि प्रयाते स्वस्तात रामे च वनमाश्रिते।।2.76.8।।
explanation: O king O father you have gone to heaven and Rama has taken shelter in the forest now. Who will take care of the welfare and security of your city?

shloka_text: विधवा पृथिवी राजन् स्त्वया हीना न राजते। हीनचन्द्रेव रजनी नगरी प्रतिभाति मा।।2.76.9।।
explanation: O king bereft of you, the earth (kingdom) is widowed and has lost its radiance. The city appears to me like a moonless night.

shloka_text: एवं विलपमानं तं भरतं दीनमानसम्। अब्रवीद्वचनं भूयो वसिष्ठस्तु महामुनिः।।2.76.10।।
explanation: To Bharata who was thus lamenting with a dejected mind, the great ascetic Vasistha once again said:

shloka_text: प्रेतकार्याणि यान्यस्य कर्तव्यानि विशां पतेः। तान्यव्यग्रं महाबाहो क्रियान्तामविचारितम्।।2.76.11।।
explanation: O mightyarmed prince, the funeral rites that are required to be performed for the departed king ought to be done carefully without any shortcomings.

shloka_text: तथेति भरतो वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्याभिपूज्य तत्। ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यान् स्त्वरयामास सर्वशः।।2.76.12।।
explanation: Bharata said, 'Be it so' in obedience to Vasistha, who hastened up the learned Vedic scholars, family priests and preceptors to perform various rites.

shloka_text: ये त्वग्नयो नरेन्द्रेस्य चाग्न्यगाराद्बहिष्कृताः। ऋत्विग्भिर्याजकैश्चैव ते आह्रियन्त यथाविधि।।2.76.13।।
explanation: The sacrificial fire of the king has been put outside the firesanctuary in accordance with the ritual precepts and were withdrawn by the attendants and priests wellversed in Vedic lore.

shloka_text: शिबिकायामथा़ऽरोप्य राजानं गतचेतसम्। बाष्पकण्ठा विमनसस्तमूहुः परिचारकाः।।2.76.14।।
explanation: Thereafter the attendants raised the mortal remains of the deceased king onto a litter, with dejected minds, throats choked with tears and carried him away.

shloka_text: हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च वासांसि विविधानि च। प्रकिरन्तो जना मार्गं नृपतेरग्रतो ययुः।।2.76.15।।
explanation: The people went ahead of the king's body strewing on the way gold of brilliant colour and different kinds of garments.

shloka_text: चन्दनागरुनिर्यासान् सरलं पद्मकं तथा। देवदारूणि चाहृत्य क्षेपयन्ति तथापरे।।2.76.16।। गन्धानुच्चावचांश्चान्यां स्तत्र गत्वाथ भूमिपम्। तत्र संवेशयामासुश्चितामध्ये तमृत्विजः।।2.76.17।।
explanation: In this way others brought sandal, agaru and fragrant gum gugul, the resin of balsa tree and woods of sarala, padmaka and devadaru and built a pyre and strew many kinds of fragrant substances on it. Thereafter the priests laid the mortal remains of the king in the centre of the pyre.

shloka_text: चन्दनागरुनिर्यासान् सरलं पद्मकं तथा। देवदारूणि चाहृत्य क्षेपयन्ति तथापरे।।2.76.16।। गन्धानुच्चावचांश्चान्यां स्तत्र गत्वाथ भूमिपम्। तत्र संवेशयामासुश्चितामध्ये तमृत्विजः।।2.76.17।।
explanation: In this way others brought sandal, agaru and fragrant gum gugul, the resin of balsa tree and woods of sarala, padmaka and devadaru and built a pyre and strew many kinds of fragrant substances on it. Thereafter the priests laid the mortal remains of the king in the centre of the pyre.

shloka_text: तदा हुताशनं हुत्वा जेपुस्तस्य तदृत्विजः। जगुश्च ते यथाशास्त्र तत्र सामानि सामगाः।।2.76.18।।
explanation: Then the priests offering oblations to the king's fire, intoned prayers. The reciters of Sama Veda sang the hymns in accordance with the sacred scriptures.

shloka_text: शिबिकाभिश्च यानैश्च यथार्हं तस्य योषितः। नगरा न्निर्ययुस्तत्र वृद्धैः परिवृता स्तदा।।2.76.19।।
explanation: Then in accordance with their rank and surrounded by aged guards, the wives of  king Dasaratha departed for that place from the city in palanquins and other carriages.

shloka_text: प्रसव्यं चापि तं चकुः ऋत्विजोऽग्निचितं नृपम्। स्त्रियश्च शोकसन्तप्ताः कौसल्याप्रमुखास्तदा।।2.76.20।।
explanation: Then the priests and other women led by Kausalya who was consumed with grief circumambulated the pyre in the reverse direction as the king's body was engulfed by flames.

shloka_text: क्रौञ्चीनामिव नारीणां निनादस्तत्र शुश्रुवे। आर्तानां करुणं काले क्रोशन्तीनां सहस्रशः।।2.76.21।।
explanation: At that time, piteous cries of distressed women in their thousands like the piercing cries of female kraunchas (birds) were heard.

shloka_text: ततो रुदन्त्यो विवशाविलप्य च पुनः पुनः। यानेभ्यस्सरयूतीरमवतेरुर्वराङ्गनाः।।2.76.22।।
explanation: Thereafter, the courtesans weeping uncontrollably and, lamenting again and again, alighted from carriages on the bank of the river Sarayu.

shloka_text: कृत्वोदकं ते भरतेन सार्धं नृपाङ्गना मन्त्रिपुरोहिता श्च। पुरंप्रविश्याश्रुपरीतनेत्राः भूमौ दशाहं व्यनयन्त दुःखम्।।2.76.23।।
explanation: The wives of the king, counsellors and priests along with Bharata offered waterlibation and entered the city with tearful eyes. They spent the tenday  mourning period sleeping on the ground (floor) in great grief. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे षटसप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventysixth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो दशाहेऽतिगते कृतशौचो नृपात्मजः। द्वादशेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते श्राद्धकर्माण्यकारयत्।।2.77.1।।
explanation: Having observed the tenday mourning period, Bharata purified himself on the twelfth day and got the shraddha rites (obsequies) performed.

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ रत्नं धनमन्नं च पुष्कलम्। वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च।।2.77.2।।
explanation: During the shraddha ceremony (obsequies) Bharata bestowed on brahmins precious stones, wealth, large quantities of rice, highly valuable garments and various gems.

shloka_text: बास्तिकं बहु शुक्लं च गाश्चापि शतशस्तथा। दासीदासं च यानं च वेश्मानि सुमहान्ति च।।2.77.3।। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ पुत्रो राज्ञस्तस्यौर्ध्वदैहिकम्।
explanation: At the time of performing the rites pertaining to the other world, Bharata bestowed on brahmins herds of white goats, cows in hundreds, male and female servants and spacious houses and carriages.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ त्रयोदशे।।2.77.4।। विललाप महाबाहुर्भरत श्शोकमूर्छितः। शब्दापिहितकण्ठस्तु शोधनार्थमुपागतः।।2.77.5।। चितामूले पितुर्वाक्यमिदमाह सुदुःखितः।
explanation: Thereafter at the hour of dawn on the thirteenth day mightyarmed Bharata visited the cemetery to perform the purificatory ceremony. Approaching the place of the funeral pyre of his father, he lamented in the intensity of grief:

shloka_text: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ त्रयोदशे।।2.77.4।। विललाप महाबाहुर्भरत श्शोकमूर्छितः। शब्दापिहितकण्ठस्तु शोधनार्थमुपागतः।।2.77.5।। चितामूले पितुर्वाक्यमिदमाह सुदुःखितः।
explanation: Thereafter at the hour of dawn on the thirteenth day mightyarmed Bharata visited the cemetery to perform the purificatory ceremony. Approaching the place of the funeral pyre of his father, he lamented in the intensity of grief:

shloka_text: तात यस्मिन्निसृष्टोऽहं त्वया भ्रातरि राघवे।।2.77.6।। तस्मिन्वनं प्रव्रजिते शून्ये त्यक्तोऽस्म्यहं त्वया।
explanation: O dear father, my brother Rama to whom you have entrusted me has been sent to the forest now and I am  left in a vacuum.

shloka_text: यस्या गतिरनाथायाः पुत्रः प्रवाजितो वनम्। तामम्बां तात कौसल्यां त्यक्त्वा त्वं क्व गतो नृप।।2.77.7।।
explanation: Where have you gone, my king my father, forsaking mother Kausalya who is without a protector and whose only support Rama, her son has been sent away to the forest?

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा भस्मारुणं तच्च दग्धास्थि स्थानमण्डलम्।।2.77.8।। पितु श्शरीरनिर्वाणं निष्टनन्विषसाद सः।
explanation: Having seen the circular place, looking reddishbrown with burnt bones and ashes, where his father's body was consumed by fire, Bharata started crying aloud in deep despondency.

shloka_text: स तु दृष्ट्वा रुदन् दीनः पपात धरणीतले।।2.77.9।। उत्थाप्यमानश्शक्रस्य यन्त्रध्वज इव च्युतः।
explanation: On seeing the cremation ground desolate Bharata collapsed sobbing on the ground like a fastened flag staff of Indra, which fell as it was being raised.

shloka_text: अभिपेतुस्ततस्सर्वे तस्यामात्याश्शुचिव्रतम्।।2.77.10।। अन्तकाले निपतितं ययातिमृषयो यथा।
explanation: Immediately all his counsellors ran towards him like the ascetics who raised Yayati, a man of pious vows, when he fell down at the final hour.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्न श्चापि भरतं दृष्ट्वा शोकम् परिप्लुतः।।2.77.11।। विसंज्ञो न्यपतद्भूमौ भूमिपालमनुस्मरन्।
explanation: Beholding Bharata, Satrughna also plunged in grief remembering the king, and fell unconscious on the ground.

shloka_text: उन्मत्त इव निश्चेता विललाप सुदुःखितः।।2.77.12।। स्मृत्वा पितुर्गुणाङ्गानि तानि तानि तथा तथा।
explanation: Recollecting the many virtues of his father again and again, like a madman, Satrughna, mentally unsteady, lamented in profound sorrow.

shloka_text: मन्थराप्रभवस्तीव्रः कैकेयीग्राहसङ्कुलः।।2.77.13।। वरदानमयोऽक्षोभ्योऽमञ्जयच्छोकसागरः।
explanation: With Manthara as the source, Kaikeyi as a crocodile, this terrible sea of sorrow which has submerged all of us lies unruffled.

shloka_text: सुकुमारं च बालं च सततं लालितं त्वया।।2.77.14।। क्व तात भरतं हित्वा विलपन्तं गतो भवान्।
explanation: Where have you gone dear father, leaving the lamenting Bharata, so young and tender, who was always your darling?

shloka_text: ननु भोज्येषु पानेषु वस्त्रेष्वाभरणेषु च।।2.77.15।। प्रवारयसि नस्सर्वान् तन्नः कोऽन्यः करिष्यति।
explanation: You used to make all of us choose delicious food, drinks, garments and ornaments. Who else will do that now?

shloka_text: अवदारणकाले तु पृथिवी नावदीर्यते।।2.77.16।। या विहीना त्वया राज्ञा धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना।
explanation: You are a righteous and mighty king and without you, this earth would have been broken into pieces. But it does not.

shloka_text: पितरि स्वर्गमापन्ने रामे चारण्यमाश्रिते।।2.77.17।। किं मे जीवितसामर्थ्यं प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्।
explanation: With my father ascended to heaven and Rama gone to the forest, where is the strength in me to live? I shall enter the blazing fire.

shloka_text: हीनो भ्रात्रा च पित्रा च शून्यामिक्ष्वाकुपालिताम्।।2.77.18।। अयोध्यां न प्रवेक्ष्यामि प्रवेक्ष्यामि तपोवनम्।
explanation: Devoid of my father and brother, I will not return to empty Ayodhya that was once ruled by the Ikshvakus. I will enter the grove of asceticism .

shloka_text: तयोर्विलपितं श्रुत्वा व्यसनं चान्ववेक्ष्य तत्।।2.77.19।। भृशमार्ततरा भूयस्सर्वएवानुगामिनः।
explanation: Having heard the lamentataions of both the brothers and reflecting the calamity befallen on them, the attendants felt extremely afflicted once again.

shloka_text: ततो विषण्णौ श्रान्तौ च शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ।।2.77.20।। धरण्यां संव्यवेष्टेतां भग्नशृङ्गाविवर्षभौ।
explanation: Thereafter, both Satrughna and Bharata, dejected and exhausted, lay writhing on the  floor like two bulls with their horns broken.

shloka_text: ततः प्रकृतिमान्वैद्यः पितुरेषां पुरोहितः।।2.77.21।। वसिष्ठो भरतं वाक्यमुत्थाप्य तमुवाच ह।
explanation: Then his father's family priest Vasistha of composed mind and versed in the Vedas  raised Bharata and said to him:

shloka_text: त्रयोदशोऽयं दिवसः पितुर्वृत्तस्य ते विभो।।2.77.22।। सावशेषास्थिनिचये किमिह त्वं विलम्भसे।
explanation: O lord, this is the thirteenth day since the death of your father. The heap of bones and ashes still remain on the pyre. Why this delay on your part?

shloka_text: त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः।।2.77.23।। तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हसि।
explanation: There are three dualities  (hunger and thirst, pain and pleasure, birth and death), which are applicable to all living beings without any exception and cannot be eschewed. Therefore, it does not behove you to act in this way.

shloka_text: सुमन्त्रश्चापि शत्रुघ्नमुत्थाप्याभिप्रसाद्य च।।2.77.24।। श्रावयामास तत्त्वज्ञ स्सर्वभूतभवाभवम्।
explanation: The knower of reality Sumantra helped Satrughna to rise, after having consoled him, imparted him the truth about the inevitability of birth and death.

shloka_text: उत्थितौ च नरव्याघ्रौ प्रकाशेते यशस्विनौ।।2.77.25।। वर्षातपपरिक्लिनौ पृथगिन्द्रध्वजाविव।
explanation: Having risen from the earth both the illustrious tigers among men, Bharata and Satrughna looked  faded and weather beaten like the banners of Indra that had faded under the Sun and rain.

shloka_text: अश्रूणि परिमृद्नन्तौ रक्ताक्षौ दीनभाषिणौ। अमात्यास्त्वरयन्ति स्म तनयौ चापराः क्रियाः।।2.77.26।।
explanation: The counsellors hastened up both the sons, who were wiping away the tears and speaking with blodshot eyes, to complete the remaining part of  the funeral rites. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तसप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ यात्रां समीहन्तं शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः। भरतं शोकसन्तप्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.78.1।।
explanation: As the griefstricken Bharata was intending to proceed to Rama, Lakshmana's younger brother Satrughna said to him:

shloka_text: गतिर्य स्सर्वभूतानां दुःखे किं पुनरात्मनः। स राम स्सत्त्वसम्पन्नः स्त्रिया प्रव्राजितो वनम्।।2.78.2।।
explanation: Couldn't the mighty Rama who is the ultimate refuge of all beings protect himself in his own distress? That Rama has been exiled to the forest by a woman.

shloka_text: बलवान्वीर्यसम्पन्नो लक्ष्मणो नाम योऽप्यसौ। किं न मोचयते रामं कृत्वा स्म पितृनिग्रहम्।।2.78.3।।
explanation: And why did not Lakshmana who is strong and powerful release Rama from exile by restraining our father?

shloka_text: पूर्वमेव तु निग्राह्य स्समवेक्ष्य नयानयौ। उत्पथं यस्समारूढो राजा नार्या वशं गतः।।2.78.4।।
explanation: In the first place, the king could have restrained himself by reflecting on whether the course of action adopted by him under the influence of a woman was just or unjust.

shloka_text: इति सम्भाषमाणे तु शत्रुघ्ने लक्ष्मणानुजे। प्राग्द्वारेऽभूत्तदा कुब्जा सर्वाभरणभूषिता।।2.78.5।।
explanation: While Satrughna, brother of Lakshmana was conversing thus, the hunchback Manthara decorated with all kinds of ornaments arrived at the entrance.

shloka_text: लिप्ता चन्दनसारेण राजवस्त्राणि बिभ्रती। विविधं विविधै स्तैस्तैर्भूषणैश्च विभूषिता।।2.78.6।।
explanation: She had besmeared herself with the essence of sandal, had put on royal garments and adorned herself in many ways with every kind of ornament.

shloka_text: मेखलादामभिश्चित्रैरन्यैश्च शुभभूषणैः। बभासे बहुभिर्बद्धा रज्जुबद्धेव वानरी।।2.78.7।।
explanation: Tied with colourful girdle strings and wearing many other auspicious ornaments, she looked like a female monkey tied with a rope.

shloka_text: तां समीक्ष्य तदा द्वास्स्थास्सुभृशं पापकारिणीम्। गृहीत्वाऽकरुणां कुब्जां शत्रुघ्नाय न्यवेदयन्।।2.78.8।।
explanation: Seeing the hunchback, doer of many sinful deeds, the gatekeepers caught hold of her and informed Satrughna.

shloka_text: यस्याः कृते वने रामो न्यस्तदेहश्च वः पिता। सेयं पापा नृशंसा च तस्याः कुरु यथामति।।2.78.9।।
explanation: Here is that sinful, cruel woman on whose account Rama is in the forest and your father has forsaken his body. Do with her as it pleases you.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्च तदाज्ञाय वचनं भृशदुःखितः। अन्तःपुरचरान्सर्वानित्युवाच धृत व्रतः।।2.78.10।।
explanation: Intensely grieved to hear those words, Satrughna who was steadfast in his vows said to the inmates of the inner apartment:

shloka_text: तीव्रमुत्पादितं दुःखं भ्रात्रूणां मे तथा पितुः। यया सेयं नृशंसस्य कर्मणः फलमश्नुताम्।।2.78.11।।
explanation: Let this woman, who caused deep sorrow to our brothers and father, reap the fruit of her malicious actions.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तेनाशु सखीजनसमावृता। गृहीता बलवत्कुब्जा सा तद्गृहमनादयत्।।2.78.12।।
explanation: Saying thus, he forcibly caught hold of the hunchback amidst her companions when she filled the house with her cries.

shloka_text: तत स्सुभृशसन्तप्तस्तस्या स्सर्व स्सखीजनः। क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय शत्रुघ्नं विपलायत सर्वशः।।2.78.13।।
explanation: Perceiving the enraged Satrughna all her companions shook in terror and fled in different directions.

shloka_text: आमन्त्रयत कृत्स्न श्च तस्या स्सर्व स्सखीजनः। यथाऽयं समुपक्रान्तो निश्शेषां नः करिष्यति।।2.78.14।।
explanation: All her companions conversed among themselves. The way he began, it looks he will finish all of us.

shloka_text: सानुक्रोशां वदान्यां च धर्मज्ञां च यशस्विनीम्। कौसल्यां शरणं याम सा हि नोऽस्तु ध्रुवा गतिः।।2.78.15।।
explanation: Let us seek refuge under the illustrious Kausalya, who is compassionate, generous,  and knower of righteousness. She is our sure saviour.

shloka_text: स च रोषेण ताम्राक्ष श्शत्रुघ्न श्शत्रुतापनः। विचकर्ष तदा कुब्जां क्रोशन्तीं धरणीतले।।2.78.16।।
explanation: With bloodshot eyes Satrughna, the scorcher of enemies, dragged the shrieking hunchback down the ground in fury.

shloka_text: तस्या ह्याकृष्यमाणाया मन्थराया स्ततस्ततः। चित्रं बहुविधं भाण्डं पृथिव्यां तद्व्यशीर्यत।।2.78.17।।
explanation: While Manthara was being dragged by Satrughna, the collection of ornaments of many colours and of various kinds worn by her were broken and  scattered here and there all over the ground.

shloka_text: तेन भाण्डेन संस्तीर्णं श्रीमद्राजनिवेशनम्। अशोभत तदा भूयः शारदं गगनं यथा।।2.78.18।।
explanation: The resplendent royal palace, strewn all over with several ornaments on the ground  shone like the autumnal sky (studded with innumerable stars).

shloka_text: स बली बलवत्क्रोधाद्गृहीत्वा पुरुषर्षभः। कैकेयीमभिनिर्भर्त्स्य बभाषे परुषं वचः।।2.78.19।।
explanation: The mighty and the best of men Satrughna seized with fury, forcibly caught hold of that hunchback and censured Kaikeyi with harsh words.

shloka_text: तैर्वाक्यैः परुषैर्दुःखैः कैकेयी भृशदुःखिता। शत्रुघ्नभयसन्त्रस्ता पुत्रं शरणमागता।।2.78.20।।
explanation: Kaikeyi, deeply distressed at those harsh and grievous words was afraid of Satrughna and sought the protection of her son Bharata.

shloka_text: तं प्रेक्ष्य भरतः क्रुद्धं शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्। अवध्या स्सर्वभूतानां प्रमदाः क्षम्यतामिति।।2.78.21।।
explanation: Bharata, addressing the enraged Satrughna said Of all beings a lady is not to be killed.  Pardon her.

shloka_text: हन्यामहमिमां पापां कैकेयीं दुष्टचारिणीम्। यदि मां धार्मिको रामो नासूयेन्मातृघातकम्।।2.78.22।।
explanation: If righteous Rama were not to accuse me of slaying a mother, I would have killed the sinful Kaikeyi of wicked deeds myself.

shloka_text: इमामपि हतां कुब्जां यदि जानाति राघवः। त्वां च मां च हि धर्मात्मा नाभिभाषिष्यते ध्रुवम्।।2.78.23।।
explanation: If righteous Rama comes to know that this hunchback has been slain by us, he will certainly never talk to you or me.

shloka_text: भरतस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः। न्यवर्तत ततो रोषात्तां मुमोच च मन्थराम्।।2.78.24।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Bharata, Satrughna, the younger brother of Lakshmana restrained his fury and also released Manthara.

shloka_text: सा पादमूले कैकेय्या मन्थरा निपपात ह। निश्श्वसन्ती सुदुःखार्ता कृपणं विललाप च।।2.78.25।।
explanation: Manthara, tormented with grief, fell at the feet of Kaikeyi and began heaving deep sighs.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नविक्षेपविमूढसंज्ञां समीक्ष्य कुब्जां भरतस्य माता। शनैस्समाश्वासयदार्तरूपां क्रौञ्चीं विलग्नामिव वीक्षमाणाम्।।2.78.26।।
explanation: . Seeing the hunchback thrown down by Satrughna and lying senseless and anguished like a female krauncha bird caught in a net looking in different directions, Kaikeyi gently soothed her. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टसप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyeighth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ चतुर्दशे। समेत्य राजकर्तारो भरतं वाक्यमब्रुवन्।।2.79.1।।
explanation: Then, at the hour of dawn on the fourteenth day, all those who were empowered to proclaim the king,  assembled and addressed Bharata:

shloka_text: गतो दशरथस्स्वर्गं यो नो गुरुतरो गुरुः। रामं प्रव्राज्य वै ज्येष्ठं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।।2.79.2।।
explanation: Dasaratha, who was our most revered master and preceptor, having exiled his eldest son Rama and mighty Lakshmana, ascended heaven.

shloka_text: त्वमद्य भव नो राजा राजपुत्र महायशः। सङ्गत्या नापराध्नोति राज्यमेतदनायकम्।।2.79.3।।
explanation: O illutrious prince do assume kingship now. Incidentally, there has been yet no attack on this leaderless kingdom.

shloka_text: अभिषेचनिकं सर्वमिदमादाय राघव। प्रतीक्षते त्वां स्वजनश्श्रेणयश्च नृपात्मज।।2.79.4।।
explanation: O prince of the Raghu race (Bharata), your subjects and guilds of traders, artisans, etc, have procured necessary materials for your consecration, and  await you.

shloka_text: राज्यं गृहाण भरत पितृपैतामहं ध्रुवम्। अभिषेचय चात्मानं पाहि चास्मान्नरर्षभ।।2.79.5।।
explanation: O best among men, inherit this stable kingdom of your ancestors, get yourself consecrated and save us.

shloka_text: अभिषेचनिकं भाण्डं कृत्वा सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम्। भरतस्तं जनं सर्वं प्रत्युवाच धृतव्रतः।।2.79.6।।
explanation: Bharata, firm in vows, circumambulated all the articles procured in connection with consecration, and replied them as follows:

shloka_text: ज्येष्ठस्य राजता नित्यमुचिता हि कुलस्य नः। नैवं भवन्तो मां वक्तुमर्हन्ति कुशला जनाः।।2.79.7।।
explanation: It has been the tradition in our race that the eldest son alone should always inherit the kingdom. It does not behove intelligent people like you to tell me like this.

shloka_text: रामः पूर्वो हि नो भ्राता भविष्यति महीपतिः। अहं त्वरण्ये वत्स्यामि वर्षाणि नव पञ्च च।।2.79.8।।
explanation: Our eldest brother, Rama shall become king. As for me, I shall dwell in the forest for fourteen years.

shloka_text: युज्यतां महती सेना चतुरङ्गमहाबला। आनयिष्याम्यहं ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरं राघवं वनात्।।2.79.9।।
explanation: Let the great and powerful army of four divisions be marshalled. I will bring back my eldest brother Rama from the forest.

shloka_text: अभिषेचनिकं चैव सर्वमेतदुपस्कृतम्। पुरस्कृत्य गमिष्यामि रामहेतोर्वनं प्रति।।2.79.10।।
explanation: I shall go to the forest to (bring back) Rama, with all these articles, procured for coronation kept in front.

shloka_text: तत्रैवं तं नरव्याघ्रमभिषिच्य पुरस्कृतम्। आनेष्यामि तु वै रामं हव्यवाहमिवाध्वरात्।।2.79.11।
explanation: After coronating Rama, the best of men, there itself, I will definitely bring him back, letting him go ahead of me, like the sacred fire carried from the place of sacrifice.

shloka_text: न सकामां करिष्यामि स्वामिमां मातृगन्धिनीम्। वने वत्स्याम्यहं दुर्गे रामो राजा भविष्यति।।2.79.12।।
explanation: I shall never fulfil the wishes of that woman called my mother. I shall dwell in the inaccessible forest and Rama shall become king.

shloka_text: क्रियतां शिल्पिभिः पन्था स्समानि विषमाणि च। रक्षिणश्चानुसम्यान्तु पथि दुर्गविचारकाः।।2.79.13।।
explanation: Let the road be aligned by artisans and uneven ground be levelled. The guards who judge the inaccessible terrains should follow them on their way.

shloka_text: एवं सम्भाषमाणं तं रामहेतोर्नृपात्मजम्। प्रत्युवाच जनस्सर्व श्श्रीमद्वाक्यमनुत्तमम्।।2.79.14।।
explanation: When prince Bharata was thus speaking in favour of Rama, all the people responded with these excellent, propitious words:

shloka_text: एवं ते भाषमाणस्य पद्मा श्रीरुपतिष्ठतात्। यस्त्वं ज्येष्ठे नृपसुते पृथिवीं दातुमिच्छसि।।2.79.15।।
explanation: May Lakshmi, goddess of prosperity, abide in you for having expressed your desire to bestow the kingdom upon the king's eldest son.

shloka_text: अनुत्तमं तद्वचनं नृपात्मजप्रभाषितं संश्रवणे निशम्य च। प्रहर्षजास्तं प्रति बाष्पबिन्दवो निपेतुरार्यानननेत्रसम्भवाः।।2.79.16।।
explanation: With such graceful words spoken by the prince within their hearing, tears of joy filled the eyes of the noble people and fell drop by drop down their faces.

shloka_text: ऊचुस्ते वचनमिदं निशम्य हृष्टा स्सामात्या स्सपरिषदो वियातशोकाः। पन्थानं नरवर भक्तिमान् जनश्च व्यादिष्टस्तव वचनाच्च शिल्पिवर्गः।।2.79.17।
explanation: All the ministers and members of the council, relieved of their distress, were delighted to hear these words and said O best among men, on your orders devoted people and groups of artisans have been instructed to lay the road. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ भूमिप्रदेशज्ञास्सूत्रकर्मविशारदाः। स्वकर्माभिरताश्शूराः खनका यन्त्रकास्तथा।।2.80.1।। कर्मान्तिकाः स्थपतयः पुरुष यन्त्रकोविदाः। तथा वार्धकयश्चैव मार्गिणो वृक्षतक्षकाः।।2.80.2।। कूपकारास्सुधाकारार्वंशकर्मकृतस्तथा। समर्था ये च द्रष्टारः पुरतस्ते प्रतस्थिरे।।2.80.3।।
explanation: Then surveyors, experts in measurment, energetic and zealous labourers, excavators, engineers, skilled workers, architects, craftsmen, carpenters, roadlevellers, woodcutters, welldiggers, whitewashers, basketmakers, competent supervisors were sent in advance.

shloka_text: अथ भूमिप्रदेशज्ञास्सूत्रकर्मविशारदाः। स्वकर्माभिरताश्शूराः खनका यन्त्रकास्तथा।।2.80.1।। कर्मान्तिकाः स्थपतयः पुरुष यन्त्रकोविदाः। तथा वार्धकयश्चैव मार्गिणो वृक्षतक्षकाः।।2.80.2।। कूपकारास्सुधाकारार्वंशकर्मकृतस्तथा। समर्था ये च द्रष्टारः पुरतस्ते प्रतस्थिरे।।2.80.3।।
explanation: Then surveyors, experts in measurment, energetic and zealous labourers, excavators, engineers, skilled workers, architects, craftsmen, carpenters, roadlevellers, woodcutters, welldiggers, whitewashers, basketmakers, competent supervisors were sent in advance.

shloka_text: अथ भूमिप्रदेशज्ञास्सूत्रकर्मविशारदाः। स्वकर्माभिरताश्शूराः खनका यन्त्रकास्तथा।।2.80.1।। कर्मान्तिकाः स्थपतयः पुरुष यन्त्रकोविदाः। तथा वार्धकयश्चैव मार्गिणो वृक्षतक्षकाः।।2.80.2।। कूपकारास्सुधाकारार्वंशकर्मकृतस्तथा। समर्था ये च द्रष्टारः पुरतस्ते प्रतस्थिरे।।2.80.3।।
explanation: Then surveyors, experts in measurment, energetic and zealous labourers, excavators, engineers, skilled workers, architects, craftsmen, carpenters, roadlevellers, woodcutters, welldiggers, whitewashers, basketmakers, competent supervisors were sent in advance.

shloka_text: स तु हर्षात्तमुद्देशं जनौघो विपुलः प्रयान्। अशोभत महावेगस्समुद्र इव पर्वणि।।2.80.4।।
explanation: Like a swollen ocean on a fullmoon day the multitude of people proceeded joyfully with great speed to the appointed place.

shloka_text: ते स्ववारं समास्थाय वर्त्मकर्मणि कोविदाः। करणैर्विविधोपेतैः पुरस्तात्सम्प्रतस्थिरे।।2.80.5।।
explanation: Those groups who were skilled in the construction of roads took up their places with every kind of tool and departed ahead of others.

shloka_text: लतावल्ली श्च गुल्मांश्च स्थाणूनश्मन एव च। जनायांचक्रिरे मार्गं छिन्दन्तो विविधान्द्रुमान्।।2.80.6।।
explanation: Clearing and cutting branches of various trees and creepers, shrubs, plants branchless trees and hewing boulders, the road was paved by the king's men.

shloka_text: अवृक्षेषु च देशेषु केचिद्वृक्षानरोपयन्। केचित्कुठारैष्टङ्कैश्च दात्रैश्चिन्दन्क्वचित्क्वचित्।।2.80.7।।
explanation: Some of them, planted saplings in places where there were none, while some others severed trees here and there with axes, hatchets and sickles.

shloka_text: अपरे वीरणस्तम्भान्बलिनो बलवत्तराः। विधमन्ति स्म दुर्गाणि स्थलानि च ततस्ततः।।2.80.8।।
explanation: Some other stronger men, plucked the strongrooted tufts of fragrant grass. Here and there they made impassable terrains even.

shloka_text: अपरेऽपूरयन्कूपान्पांसुभि श्श्वभ्रमायतम्। निम्नभागान्स्ततः केचित्समान्श्चक्रु स्समन्ततः।।2.80.9।।
explanation: Some filled wells and chasms with loose soil, while others made low level grounds plain and wide on all sides.

shloka_text: बबन्धुर्बन्धनीयांश्च क्षोद्यान्सञ्चुक्षुदुस्तदा। बिभिदुर्भेदनीयांश्च तांस्तान्देशान्नरा स्तदा।।2.80.10।।
explanation: People threw bridges at places that needed to be bridged. They pulverised stones that obstructed the path and split open big stones to drain out water.

shloka_text: अचिरेणैव कालेन परिवाहान्बहूदकान्। चक्रुर्बहुविधाकारान् सागरप्रतिमान्बहून्।।2.80.11।।
explanation: In a short time they constructed many water reservoirs of different shapes capable of holding large volumes of water like the sea.

shloka_text: निर्जलेषु च देशेषु खानयामासुरुत्तमान्। उदपानान्बहुविधान्वेदिकापरिमण्डितान्।।2.80.12।।
explanation: In arid places, various good drinkingwaterwells surrounded by dykes were dug.

shloka_text: ससुधाकुट्टिमतलः प्रपुष्पितमहीरुहः। मत्तोद्घुष्ट द्विजगणः पताकाभिरलङ्कृतः।।2.80.13।। चन्दनोदकसंसिक्तो नानाकुसुमभूषितः। बह्वशोभत सेनायाः पन्था स्सुरपथोपमः।।2.80.14।।
explanation: The highway for the army was paved smooth, with its surface decorated with mosaic.  It was lined with blossoming trees with flocks of birds intoxicated with singing. It was decked with banners and sprinkled with sandal water and a strewn with flowers of every kind. Like the path of gods, the highway shone with brilliance.

shloka_text: ससुधाकुट्टिमतलः प्रपुष्पितमहीरुहः। मत्तोद्घुष्ट द्विजगणः पताकाभिरलङ्कृतः।।2.80.13।। चन्दनोदकसंसिक्तो नानाकुसुमभूषितः। बह्वशोभत सेनायाः पन्था स्सुरपथोपमः।।2.80.14।।
explanation: The highway for the army was paved smooth, with its surface decorated with mosaic.  It was lined with blossoming trees with flocks of birds intoxicated with singing. It was decked with banners and sprinkled with sandal water and a strewn with flowers of every kind. Like the path of gods, the highway shone with brilliance.

shloka_text: आज्ञाप्याथ यथाऽज्ञप्ति युक्तास्तेऽधिकृता नराः। रमणीयेषु देशेषु बहुस्वादुफलेषु च।।2.80.15।। यो निवेशस्त्वभिप्रेतो भरतस्य महात्मनः। भूयस्तं शोभयामासुर्भूषाभिर्भूषणोपमम्।।2.80.16।।
explanation: Those authorised ordered the artisans to perform their respective tasks. Thereafter, they selected lovely tracts of land filled with trees bearing varieties of sweet fruits as restingplace for great Bharata and decorated them so splendidly, that they looked like ornaments themseleves.

shloka_text: आज्ञाप्याथ यथाऽज्ञप्ति युक्तास्तेऽधिकृता नराः। रमणीयेषु देशेषु बहुस्वादुफलेषु च।।2.80.15।। यो निवेशस्त्वभिप्रेतो भरतस्य महात्मनः। भूयस्तं शोभयामासुर्भूषाभिर्भूषणोपमम्।।2.80.16।।
explanation: Those authorised ordered the artisans to perform their respective tasks. Thereafter, they selected lovely tracts of land filled with trees bearing varieties of sweet fruits as restingplace for great Bharata and decorated them so splendidly, that they looked like ornaments themseleves.

shloka_text: नक्षत्रेषु प्रशस्तेषु मुहूर्तेषु च तद्विदः। निवेशान् स्थापयामासुर्भरतस्य महात्मनः।।2.80.17।।
explanation: Men wellversed in the study of planetary positions relating to auspicious constellations and auspicious times arranged different restingplaces at different times during the sojourn of great Bharata.

shloka_text: बहुपांसुचयाश्चापि परिखापरिवारिताः। तत्रेन्द्रकीलप्रतिमाः प्रतोलीवरशोभिताः।।2.80.18।। प्रासादमालावितता स्सौधप्राकारसंवृताः। पताकाशोभिता स्सर्वे सुनिर्मितमहापथाः।।2.80.19।। विसर्पद्भिरिवाऽकाशे विटङ्काग्रविमानकैः। समुच्छ्रितैर्निवेशास्ते बभुश्शक्रपुरोपमाः।।2.80.20।।
explanation: They heaped sand and dug moats around the restingplace. It was adorned with wellbuilt highways and broad thoroughfares, lined with mansions surrounded by walls as high as mount Indrakeela. The peaks of those tall residences decorated with flags which looked as if spreading into the sky. (Thus the restingplace) shone like the abode of Indra.

shloka_text: बहुपांसुचयाश्चापि परिखापरिवारिताः। तत्रेन्द्रकीलप्रतिमाः प्रतोलीवरशोभिताः।।2.80.18।। प्रासादमालावितता स्सौधप्राकारसंवृताः। पताकाशोभिता स्सर्वे सुनिर्मितमहापथाः।।2.80.19।। विसर्पद्भिरिवाऽकाशे विटङ्काग्रविमानकैः। समुच्छ्रितैर्निवेशास्ते बभुश्शक्रपुरोपमाः।।2.80.20।।
explanation: They heaped sand and dug moats around the restingplace. It was adorned with wellbuilt highways and broad thoroughfares, lined with mansions surrounded by walls as high as mount Indrakeela. The peaks of those tall residences decorated with flags which looked as if spreading into the sky. (Thus the restingplace) shone like the abode of Indra.

shloka_text: बहुपांसुचयाश्चापि परिखापरिवारिताः। तत्रेन्द्रकीलप्रतिमाः प्रतोलीवरशोभिताः।।2.80.18।। प्रासादमालावितता स्सौधप्राकारसंवृताः। पताकाशोभिता स्सर्वे सुनिर्मितमहापथाः।।2.80.19।। विसर्पद्भिरिवाऽकाशे विटङ्काग्रविमानकैः। समुच्छ्रितैर्निवेशास्ते बभुश्शक्रपुरोपमाः।।2.80.20।।
explanation: They heaped sand and dug moats around the restingplace. It was adorned with wellbuilt highways and broad thoroughfares, lined with mansions surrounded by walls as high as mount Indrakeela. The peaks of those tall residences decorated with flags which looked as if spreading into the sky. (Thus the restingplace) shone like the abode of Indra.

shloka_text: जाह्नवीं तु समासाद्य विविधद्रुमकाननाम्। शीतलामलपानीयां महामीनसमाकुलाम्।।2.80.21।।
explanation: The reached Ganga with its cool and limpid waters abounding in large fishes, its bank lined with groves of various trees.

shloka_text: सचन्द्रतारागणमण्डितं यथा नभः क्षपायाममलं विराजते। नरेन्द्रमार्गस्स तथा व्यराजत क्रमेण रम्यः शुभशिल्पिनिर्मितः।।2.80.22।।
explanation: The lovely royal road constructed in an orderly fashion by eminent craftsmen looked splendid like the clear sky decorated with by the Moon and clusters of stars. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightieth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो नान्दीमुखीं रात्रिं भरतं सूतमागधाः। तुष्टुवुर्वाग्विशेषज्ञास्स्तवैर्मङ्गलसंहितैः।।2.81.1।।
explanation: Thereafter bards and panegyrists adept in conversation with an auspicious start pleased Bharata with eulogy in the last part of the night.

shloka_text: सुवर्णकोणाभिहतः प्राणदद्यामदुन्दुभिः। दध्मुश्शङ्खांश्च शतशो नादांश्चोच्चावचस्वरान्।।2.81.2।।
explanation: The drums of the night watch were beaten by golden sticks. Conches in hundreds were blown and sounds of various modulations were created.

shloka_text: स तूर्यघोष स्सुमहान्दिवमापूरयन्निव। भरतं शोकसन्तप्तं भूयश्शोकैररन्ध्रयत्।।2.81.3।।
explanation: The shrill trempets which seemed to fill the heavens caused much more distress to the already griefstricken Bharata.

shloka_text: ततः प्रबुद्धो भरतस्तं घोषं सन्निवर्त्य च। नाहं राजेति चाप्युक्त्वा शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.81.4।।
explanation: Then Bharata waking up, exclaimed, I am not the king, ordered the pipers to stop and said to Satrughna:

shloka_text: पश्य शत्रुघ्न कैकेय्या लोकस्यापकृतं महत्। विसृज्य मयि दुःखानि राजा दशरथो गतः।।2.81.5।।
explanation: O Satrughna see what great harm has been done to these people at the instance of Kaikeyi. King Dasaratha has gone, leaving me to suffer.

shloka_text: तस्यैषा धर्मराजस्य धर्ममूला महात्मनः। परिभ्रमति राज्य श्रीर्नौरिवाकर्णिका जले।।2.81.6।।
explanation: This kingdom, rooted in the righteousness of that noble king, is now whirling like a boat in a whirlpool without a helmsman.

shloka_text: यो हि न स्सुमहान्नाथस्सोऽपि प्रव्राजितो वनम्। अनया धर्ममुत्सृज्य मात्रा मे राघवस्स्वयम्।।2.81.7।।
explanation: Even Rama, a great protector for all of us, has been banished to the forest by my mother bereft of virtuous conduct.

shloka_text: इत्येवं भरतं प्रेक्ष्य विलपन्तं विचेतनम्। कृपणं रुरुदुस्सर्वास्सस्वरं योषित स्तदा।। 2.81.8।।
explanation: Thus lamenting, Bharata fainted. Seeing him (in this state) all the women (of the inner apartment) at once cried aloud piteously.

shloka_text: तथा तस्मिन्विलपति वसिष्ठो राजधर्मवित्। सभामिक्ष्वाकुनाथस्य प्रविवेश महायशाः।।2.81.9।।
explanation: While Bharata was weeping, illustrious Vasistha, conversant with royal traditions, entered the assembly hall of the lord of the Iksvakus (king Dasaratha).

shloka_text: शातकुम्भमयीं रम्यां मणिरत्नसमाकुलाम्। सुधर्मामिव धर्मात्मा सगणः प्रत्यपद्यत।।2.81.10।।
explanation: Righteous Vasistha along with his disciples reached the lovely golden assembly hall  inlaid with gems and precious stones, which resembled Sudharma, (the assembly hall of Indra).

shloka_text: स काञ्चनमयं पीठं सुखास्तरणसंवृतम्। अध्यास्त सर्ववेदज्ञो दूताननुशशास च।।2.81.11।।
explanation: Vasistha, wellversed in all the Vedas, sat on a golden seat with a comfortable cover and ordered the messengers:

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान्वैश्यनमात्यान्गणवल्लभान्। क्षिप्रमानयताऽव्यग्राः कृत्यमात्ययिकं हि नः।।2.81.12।।
explanation: Fetch quietly brahmins, kshatriyas, vaisyas, ministers and army commanders at once. A matter of great urgency awaits us.

shloka_text: सराजभृत्यं शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्। युधाजितं सुमन्त्रं च ये च तत्र हिता जनाः।।2.81.13।।
explanation: Bring all the royal attendants, Satrughna, the illustrious Bharata, Yudhajit, Sumantra and all those wellwishers of the king.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दस्सुमहान्समपद्यत। रथैरश्वैर्गजैश्चापि जनानामुपगच्छताम्।।2.81.14।।
explanation: As they (invitees) began arriving on chariots, horses and elephants, there arose a great tumult.

shloka_text: ततो भरतमायान्तं शतक्रतुमिवामराः। प्रत्यनन्दन्प्रकृतयो यथा दशरथं तथा।।2.81.15।।
explanation: Then as Bharata apprroached,  ministers and subjects greeted him as they used to greet Dasaratha, just as gods greet Indra, the performer of a hundred sacrifices.

shloka_text: ह्रद इव तिमिनागसंवृतः स्तिमितजलो मणिशङ्खशर्करः। दशरथसुतशोभिता सभा सदशरथेव बभौ यथा पुरा।।2.81.16।।
explanation: The assembly hall looked splendid like a lake of tranquil waters with gems, shells  pebbles, grains of sand and teeming with whales and serpents in the presence of the son of king Dasaratha. It appeared as though Dasaratha himself was present. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकाशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightyfirst sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तामार्यगणसम्पूर्णां भरतः प्रग्रहां सभाम्। ददर्श बुद्धिसम्पन्नः पूर्णचन्द्रो निशामिव।।2.82.1।।
explanation: Sagacious Bharata beheld that assembly hall filled with honourable members, like the fullmoon beholds the night stretching forth (with stars).

shloka_text: आसनानि यथान्यायमार्याणां विशतां तदा। वस्त्राङ्गरागप्रभया द्योतिता सा सभोत्तमा।।2.82.2।।
explanation: When the seats were occupied by the honourable members according to their rank, that august assembly looked splendid with the brilliance of their apparels and fragrance of unguents.

shloka_text: सा विद्वज्जनसम्पूर्णा सभा सुरुचिरा तदा। अदृश्यत घनापाये पूर्णचन्द्रेव शर्वरी।।2.82.3।।
explanation: The most splendid assembly filled with learned people looked brilliant like the night with the autumnal fullmoon.

shloka_text: राज्ञस्तु प्रकृती स्सर्वा स्समग्राः प्रेक्ष्य धर्मवित्। इदं पुरोहितो वाक्यं भरतं मृदु चाब्रवीत्।।2.82.4।।
explanation: The chief priest Vasistha, knower of righteousness, looked at all the ministers present and addressed Bharata in a gentle voice.

shloka_text: तात राजा दशरथ स्स्वर्गतो धर्ममाचरन्। धनधान्यवतीं स्फीतां प्रदाय पृथिवीं तव।।2.82.5।।
explanation: O dear child following the righteous path king Dasaratha conferred on you this vast kingdom abounding in wealth and grains before attaining heaven.

shloka_text: रामस्तथा सत्यधृतिस्सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्। नाजहात्पितुरादेशं शशी ज्योत्स्नामिवोदितः।।2.82.6।।
explanation: Abiding in truth, remembering the righteous ways of virtuous men just as the rising Moon does not leave its beams, Rama too did not move away from his father's command.

shloka_text: पित्रा भ्रात्रा च ते दत्तं राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्। तद्भुङ्क्ष्व मुदितामात्यः क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचय।।2.82.7।।
explanation: The kingdom free from obstacles has been passed on to you by your father and brother. Get yourself coronated quickly and enjoy it along with your cheerful ministers.

shloka_text: उदीच्या श्च प्रतीच्या श्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च केवलाः। कोट्यापरान्तास्सामुद्रारत्नान्यभिहरन्तुते।।2.82.8।।
explanation: Let kings from the north, the west, the south, the bordering kingdoms, and the seatraders offer you crores of gems as gifts.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतो वाक्यं शोकेनाभिपरिप्लुतः। जगाम मनसा रामं धर्मज्ञो धर्मकाङ्क्षया।।2.82.9।।
explanation: On hearing those words, Bharata who knew his duty was overwhelmed with distress and, resolved to abide by righteousness, reached Rama through his mind (thought of Rama).

shloka_text: सबाष्पकलया वाचा कलहंसस्वरो युवा। विललाप सभामध्ये जगर्हे च पुरोहितम्।।2.82.10।।
explanation: Young Bharata with the melodious voice of a swan, choked with tears, lamenting in the assembly, reproached the family priest Vasistha, saying:

shloka_text: चरितब्रह्मचर्यस्य विद्यास्नातस्य धीमतः। धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य को राज्यं मद्विधो हरेत्।।2.82.11।।
explanation: Would any man seize this kingdom which rightfully belongs to sagacious Rama, who practises brahmacharya, who is wellversed in all branches of learning and who endeavours to protect righteousness?

shloka_text: कथं दशरथाज्जातो भवेद्राज्यापहारकः। राज्यं चाहं च रामस्य धर्मं वक्तुमिहार्हसि।।2.82.12।।
explanation: How can any usurper of the kingdom be born of Dasaratha? Or, how would any progeny of Dasaratha become the usurper of the kingdom? I and the kingdom, both belong to Rama. You should tell the truth about this.

shloka_text: ज्येष्ठ श्श्रेष्ठश्च धर्मात्मा दिलीपनहुषोपमः। लब्धुमर्हति काकुत्स्थो राज्यं दशरथो यथा।।2.82.13।।
explanation: The eldest, eminent and righteous Rama, the scion of the Kakutstha dynasty, who is comparable to Dilipa and Nahusha deserves to inherit this kingdom just as Dasaratha did.

shloka_text: अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यं कुर्यां पापमहं यदि। इक्ष्वाकूणामहं लोके भवेयं कुलपांसनः।।2.82.14।।
explanation: If I commit this evil act followed by wretched people which would not lead any one to  heaven, I shall only be bringing disgrace to the kings of the Ikshvaku dynasty.

shloka_text: यद्धि मात्रा कृतं पापं नाहं तदपि रोचये। इहस्थो वनदुर्गस्थं नमस्यामि कृताञ्जलिः।।2.82.15।।
explanation: I will never accept the evil deed committed by my mother. From here itself I shall pay obeisance with folded palms to my brother who dwells in the impenetrable forest.

shloka_text: राममेवानुगच्छामि राजा स द्विपदां वरः। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां राज्यमर्हति राघवः।।2.82.16।।
explanation: I shall follow Rama the best among men. He alone and no one else deserves to rule over the kingdom of the three worlds.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं धर्मसंयुक्तं श्रुत्वा सर्वे सभासदः। हर्षान्मुमुचुरश्रूणि रामे निहितचेतसः।।2.82.17।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Bharata full of righteousness, all the men assembled there   shed tears of joy, thinking of Rama.

shloka_text: यदि त्वार्यं न शक्ष्यामि विनिवर्तयितुं वनात्। वने तत्रैव वत्स्यामि यथाऽर्यो लक्ष्मणस्तथा।।2.82.18।।
explanation: If I am not able to bring back my noble brother (Rama) from the forest, I shall also dwell there like my noble brother Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सर्वोपायं तु वर्तिष्ये विनिवर्तयितुं बलात्। समक्षमार्यमिश्राणां साधूनां गुणवर्तिनाम्।।2.82.19।।
explanation: I shall employ all possible means to bring him back and join you who are respectable, virtuous and pious.

shloka_text: विष्टिकर्मान्तिका स्सर्वे मार्गशोधकरक्षकाः। प्रस्थापिता मया पूर्वं यत्रापि मम रोचते।।2.82.20।।
explanation: I have already despatched the explorers and protectors of roads who work for wages and without wages as well. It also pleases me to undertake this journey.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सलः। समीपस्थमुवाचेदं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रकोविदम्।।2.82.21।।
explanation: Righteous Bharata who was full of devotion towards his brother having uttered thus, addressed  the skilful counsellor Sumantra standing nearby:

shloka_text: तूर्णमुत्थाय गच्छ त्वं सुमन्त्र मम शासनात्। यात्रामाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं बलं चैव समानय।।2.82.22।।
explanation: O Sumantra quickly rise and go. On my authority, order the expedition and let the army be marshalled at once.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त स्सुमन्त्रस्तु भरतेन महात्मना। हृष्टस्तदाऽदिशत्सर्वं यथासन्दिष्टमिष्टवत्।।2.82.23।।
explanation: On hearing the words of the magnanimous Bharata, Sumantra was delighted and as  instructed, ordered everything as if he was anxious to do it himself.

shloka_text: ताः प्रहृष्टाः प्रकृतयो बलाध्यक्षा बलस्य च। श्रुत्वा यात्रां समाज्ञप्तां राघवस्य निवर्तने।।2.82.24।।
explanation: Having come to know that orders were issued to send the army on an expedition to bring back Rama, the subjects and the army chiefs were delighted.

shloka_text: ततो योधाङ्गना स्सर्वा भर्त्रून्सर्वान्गृहेगृहे। यात्रागमनमाज्ञाय त्वरयन्ति स्म हर्षिताः।।2.82.25।।
explanation: Then, the wives of the soldiers having come to know of the expedition were all delighted and in every household hastened up their husbands.

shloka_text: ते हयैर्गोरथैश्शीघ्रैस्स्यन्दनैश्च महाजवैः सह योधैर्बलाध्यक्षा बलं सर्वमचोदयन्।।2.82.26।।
explanation: Those chiefs of the army urged the soldiers, horses, fastmoving bullockcarts and swift chariots (to move on).

shloka_text: सज्जं तु तद्बलं दृष्ट्वा भरतो गुरुसन्निधौ। रथं मे त्वरयस्वेति सुमन्त्रं पार्श्वतोऽब्रवीत्।।2.82.27।।
explanation: When Bharata saw that the army was ready, he instructed Sumantra who was standing by the side of the preceptor to quickly prepare his chariot.

shloka_text: भरतस्य तु तस्याज्ञां प्रतिगृह्य च हर्षितः। रथं गृहीत्वा प्रययौ युक्तं परमवाजिभिः।।2.82.28।।
explanation: He (Sumantra) received the command of Bharata in great delight and set out with a chariot harnessed with excellent horses.

shloka_text: स राघव स्सत्यधृतिः प्रतापवान् ब्रुवन् सुयुक्तं दृढसत्यविक्रमः। गुरुं महारण्यगतं यशस्विनं प्रसादयिष्यन्भरतोऽब्रवीत्तदा।।2.82.29।।
explanation: Bharata, a descendant of the Raghu race, firm in truth, one whose valour comes out of unswerving truth, speaking judiciously said this to propitiate his esteemed brother who was in the dense forest:

shloka_text: तूर्णं समुत्थाय सुमन्त्र गच्छ बलस्य योगाय बलप्रधानान्। आनेतुमिच्छामि हि तं वनस्थं प्रसाद्य रामं जगतो हिताय।।2.82.30।।
explanation: O Sumantra, arise, go at once to the leaders of the army and ask them to assemble the troops. I shall propifiate Rama who is in the deep forest and bring him back for the welfare of the world.

shloka_text: ससूतपुत्रो भरतेन सम्यगाज्ञापितस्सम्परिपूर्णकामः। शशास सर्वान्प्रकृतिप्रधानान्बलस्य मुख्यांश्च सुहृज्जनं च।।2.82.31।।
explanation: The charioteer categorically commanded by Bharata, his desire fulfilled, communicated the royal mandate to all important subjects, chiefs of army and friends.

shloka_text: तत स्समुत्थाय कुले कुले ते राजन्यवैश्या वृषलाश्च विप्राः। अयूयुजन्नुष्ट्रखरान्रथांश्च नागान्हयांश्चैव कुलप्रसूतान्।।2.82.32।।
explanation: Thereafter, men from every household, kshatriyas, vaisyas, sudras and brahmins came out and harnessed their chariots to the camels and asses, elephants and horses of high pedigree. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्व्यशीतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eightysecond sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तत स्समुत्थितः काल्यमास्थाय स्यन्दनोत्तमम्। प्रययौ भरतश्शीघ्रं रामदर्शनकाङ्क्षया।।2.83.1।।
explanation: Getting up at dawn, Bharata boarded his excellent chariot and set forth swiftly, longing to see Rama.

shloka_text: अग्रतः प्रययुस्तस्य सर्वे मन्त्रिपुरोधसः। अधिरुह्य हयैर्युक्तान्रथान्सूर्यरथोपमान्।।2.83.2।।
explanation: All the ministers and priests went ahead of Bharata mounting their chariots,  harnessed with horses and resembling the chariot of the Sun god.

shloka_text: नवनागसहस्राणि कल्पितानि यथाविधि। अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्।।2.83.3।।
explanation: As per tradition, nine thousand elephants were arranged to follow Bharata, delight of the race of the Ikshvakus as he set out.

shloka_text: षष्टी रथसहस्राणि धन्विनो विविधायुधाः। अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तं राजपुत्रं यशस्विनम्।।2.83.4।।
explanation: Sixty thousands chariots and many archers holding weapons of every kind followed the illustrious prince Bharata as he went.

shloka_text: शतं सहस्राण्यश्वानां समारूढानि राघवम्। अन्वयुर्भरतं यान्तं सत्यसन्धं जितेन्द्रियम्।।2.83.5।।
explanation: One hundred thousand horses each mounted by a rider followed Bharata, one who had conquered  his passion and adhered to truth.

shloka_text: कैकेयी च सुमित्रा च कौसल्या च यशस्विनी। रामानयनसंहृष्टा ययुर्यानेन भास्वता।।2.83.6।।
explanation: Kaikeyi, Sumitra as well as the illustrious Kausalya travelled by a resplendent chariot, delighted with the thought of bringing Rama back.

shloka_text: प्रयाताश्चार्यसङ्घाता रामं द्रष्टुं सलक्ष्मणम्। तस्यैव च कथाश्चित्राः कुर्वाणा हृष्टमानसाः।।2.83.7।।
explanation: Venerable people in groups, narrating various accomplishments of Rama and eager to see him with Lakshmana, proceeded in a delightful mood.

shloka_text: मेघश्यामं महाबाहुं स्थिरसत्त्वं दृढव्रतम्। कदा द्रक्ष्यामहे रामं जगत श्शोकनाशनम्।।2.83.8।।
explanation: When shall we see that mightyarmed Rama of darkblue complexion like the raincloud, firm in strength and steadfast in vows and the destroyer of the sorrows of  this world?

shloka_text: दृष्ट एव हि न श्शोकमपनेष्यति राघवः। तम स्सर्वस्य लोकस्य समुद्यन्निव भास्करः।।2.83.9।।
explanation: At his sight alone our sorrows will be dispelled, the way the darkness of the entire world is dispelled by the rising Sun.

shloka_text: इत्येवं कथयन्तस्ते सम्प्रहृष्टाः कथा श्शुभाः। परिष्वजानाश्चान्योन्यं ययुर्नागरिका जनाः।।2.83.10।।
explanation: The inhabitants of the town proceeded joyfully, narrating Rama's delightful achievements on their way by embracing one another.

shloka_text: ये च तत्रापरे सर्वे सम्मता ये च नैगमाः। रामं प्रति ययुर्हृष्टा स्सर्वाः प्रकृतयस्तथा।।2.83.11।।
explanation: Respectable city folks, like traders and other subjects went along in great delight towards Rama.

shloka_text: मणिकाराश्च ये केचित्कुम्भकाराश्च शोभनाः। सूत्रकर्मकृतश्चैव ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः।2.83.12।। मयूरकाः क्राकचिका रोचका वेधकास्तथा। दन्तकारा स्सुधाकारा स्तथा गन्धोपजीविनः।।2.83.13।। सुवर्णकाराः प्रख्यातास्तथा कम्बलधावकाः। स्नापकोष्णोदका वैद्याधूपकाश्शौण्डिकास्तथा।।2.83.14।। रजकास्तुन्नवायाश्च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः। शैलूषाश्च सह स्त्रीभिर्ययुः कैवर्तकास्तथा।।2.83.15।।
explanation: Gempolishers, potters, weaponsmiths, weavers, makers of adornments with peacock feathers, sawyers, makers of artificial ornaments, perforators of shells and ornaments, ivoryworkers, whitewashers, purveyors of fragrant essences, renowned goldsmiths, blanketcleaners, hotbath attendants, physicians, vintners, incense merchants, washermen, tailors, headmen of villages and hamlets, actors along with their wives, fishermen -- all followed Bharata.

shloka_text: मणिकाराश्च ये केचित्कुम्भकाराश्च शोभनाः। सूत्रकर्मकृतश्चैव ये च शस्त्रोपजीविनः।2.83.12।। मयूरकाः क्राकचिका रोचका वेधकास्तथा। दन्तकारा स्सुधाकारा स्तथा गन्धोपजीविनः।।2.83.13।। सुवर्णकाराः प्रख्यातास्तथा कम्बलधावकाः। स्नापकोष्णोदका वैद्याधूपकाश्शौण्डिकास्तथा।।2.83.14।। रजकास्तुन्नवायाश्च ग्रामघोषमहत्तराः। शैलूषाश्च सह स्त्रीभिर्ययुः कैवर्तकास्तथा।।2.83.15।।
