shloka_text: अहमेवाहरिष्यामि सर्वान् लोकान्महामुने। आवासं त्वहमिच्छामि प्रदिष्टमिह कानने।।3.7.14।।
explanation: O great sage I will win all the worlds myself. I (only) want to live in this forest. Allow me.

shloka_text: भवान्सर्वत्र कुशलस्सर्वभूतहिते रतः। आख्यातश्शरभङ्गेण गौतमेन महात्मना।।3.7.15।।
explanation: You are ever engaged in the welfare of all beings. I have heard this from the great sage Sarabhanga of Gautama's clan.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण महर्षिर्लोकविश्रुतः। अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं हर्षेण महताऽप्लुतः।।3.7.16।।
explanation: Thus addressed by  Rama, Sutikshna, the great sage, wellknown to the world was highly delighted. He (then) said these sweet words:

shloka_text: अयमेवाश्रमो राम गुणवान्रम्यतामिह। ऋषिसङ्घानुचरितस्सदा मूलफलैर्युतः।।3.7.17।।
explanation: O Rama this is a salubrious hermitage where hosts of sages live and which is full of roots and fruits, you may enjoy yourself here.

shloka_text: इममाश्रममागम्य मृगसङ्घा महायशः। अहत्वा प्रतिगच्छन्ति लोभयित्वाऽकुतोभयाः।।3.7.18।।
explanation: O illustrious Rama, herds of animals visit this place fearlessly, enticing the inmates and (then) go back without harming any one.

shloka_text: नान्यद्धोषं भवेदत्र मृगेभ्योऽन्यत्र विद्धि वै। तच्छृत्वा वचनं तस्य महर्षेर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।।3.7.19।। उवाच वचनं धीरो विकृष्य  सशरं धनुः।
explanation: When heroic Rama heard that there was no other problem from the wild animals except their frequent incursions, he lifted his bow with an arrow and said these words:

shloka_text: तानहं सुमहाभाग मृगसङ्घान्समागतान्।।3.7.20।। हन्यां निशितधारेण शरेणाशनिवर्चसा।
explanation: O reverend one, I will kill with a sharpedged arrow, glowing like a thunderbolt, all those herds of animals who keep coming here.

shloka_text: भवांस्तत्राभिषज्येत किंस्यात्कृच्छ्रतरं ततः।।3.7.21।। एतस्मिन्नाश्रमे वासं चिरं तु न समर्थये।
explanation: What can be more agonizing for you (than my killing animals). I (therefore) do not foresee our long stay in this hermitage.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वोपरमं रामस्सन्ध्यामुपागमत्।।3.7.22।। अन्वास्य पश्चिमां स्नध्यां तत्र वासमकल्पयत्। सुतीक्ष्णस्याऽश्रमे रम्ये सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।3.7.23।।
explanation: Rama stopped with this. And then the evening drew to a close. Offering his evening oblation, he arranged for his stay along with Sita and Lakshmana in the delightful hermitage of Sutikshna.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वोपरमं रामस्सन्ध्यामुपागमत्।।3.7.22।। अन्वास्य पश्चिमां संंध्यां तत्र वासमकल्पयत्। सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमे रम्ये सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च।।3.7.23।।
explanation: Rama stopped with this. And then the evening drew to a close. Offering his evening oblation, he arranged for his stay along with Sita and Lakshmana in the delightful hermitage of Sutikshna.

shloka_text: ततश्शुभं तापसभोज्यमन्नं स्वयं सुतीक्ष्णः पुरुषर्षभाभ्याम्। ताभ्यां सुसत्कृत्य ददौ महात्मा सन्ध्यानिवृत्तौ  रजनीं मवेक्ष्य।।3.7.24।।
explanation: Seeing that the evening had passed and night had set in, the great sage Sutikshna with due hospitality, served those best of men, food fit for ascetics. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे सप्तमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventh sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्तु सहसौमित्रिस्सुतीक्ष्णेनाभिपूजितः। परिणाम्य निशां तत्र प्रभाते प्रत्यबुध्यत।।3.8.1।।
explanation: Rama, worshipped by Sutikshna and accompanied by Lakshmana, spent the night at the hermitage, and got up early in the morning.

shloka_text: उत्थाय तु यथाकालं राघवस्सहसीतया। उपस्पृश्यसुशितेन जलेनोत्पलगन्धिना।।3.8.2।।
explanation: In the morning Rama and Sita got up in time and took bath in cool, lilyfragrant water.

shloka_text: अथ तेऽग्निं सुरांश्चैव वैदेही रामलक्ष्मणौ। काल्यं विधिवदभ्यर्च्य तपस्विशरणे वने।।3.8.3।। उदयन्तं दिनकरं दृष्ट्वा विगतकल्मषाः। सुतीक्ष्णभिगम्येदं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन्।।3.8.4।।
explanation: And as per routine, sinless Sita, Rama and Lakshmana offered prayers to the fire and other gods of the forest which was the refuge of the ascetics. Seeing the rising Sun, they worshipped him, and approaching Sutikshna,  said these soothing words:

shloka_text: अथ तेऽग्निं सुरांश्चैव वैदेही रामलक्ष्मणौ। काल्यं विधिवदभ्यर्च्य तपस्विशरणे वने।।3.8.3।। उदयन्तं दिनकरं दृष्ट्वा विगतकल्मषाः। सुतीक्ष्णभिगम्येदं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन्।।3.8.4।।
explanation: And as per routine, sinless Sita, Rama and Lakshmana offered prayers to the fire and other gods of the forest which was the refuge of the ascetics. Seeing the rising Sun, they worshipped him, and approaching Sutikshna,  said these soothing words:

shloka_text: सुखोषितास्स्मभगवंस्त्वया पूज्येन पूजिताः। आपृच्छामः प्रयास्यामो मुनयस्त्वरयन्ति नः।।3.8.5।।
explanation: O revered Sutikshna received by one so worshipworthy like you, we spent the night well. We (now)take leave of you. The sages  are hastening us.

shloka_text: त्वरामहे वयं द्रष्टुं कृत्स्नमाश्रममण्डलम्। ऋषीणां पुण्यशीलानां दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।।3.8.6।।
explanation: We wish to see the entire circle of hermitages of the sages, residing in Dandaka forest. So we are in a hurry.

shloka_text: अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामस्सहैभिर्मुनिपुङ्गवैः। धर्मनित्यैस्तपोदान्तैर्विशिखैरिव पावकैः।।3.8.7।।
explanation: We seek your permission to go with the great sages, who are ever engaged in righteousness, selfcontrolled by virtue of their penance, and are like flameless fire.

shloka_text: अविषह्यातपो यावत्सूर्यो नातिविराजते। अमार्गेणागतां लक्ष्मीं प्राप्येवान्वयवर्जितः।।3.8.8।। तावदिच्छामहे गन्तुमित्युक्त्वा चरणौ मुनेः। ववन्दे सहसौमित्रिस्सीतया सह राघवः।। 3.8.9।।
explanation: We wish to depart before the Sun grows unbearably hot like the man devoid of good lineage who acquires wealth through unlawful means (becomes arrogant). Thereafter Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana offered worship at the feet of the venerable sage.

shloka_text: अविषह्यातपो यावत्सूर्यो नातिविराजते। अमार्गेणागतां लक्ष्मीं प्राप्येवान्वयवर्जितः।।3.8.8।। तावदिच्छामहे गन्तुमित्युक्त्वा चरणौ मुनेः। ववन्दे सहसौमित्रिस्सीतया सह राघवः।। 3.8.9।।
explanation: We wish to depart before the Sun grows unbearably hot like the man devoid of good lineage who acquires wealth through unlawful means (becomes arrogant). Thereafter Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana offered worship at the feet of the venerable sage.

shloka_text: तौ संस्पृशन्तौ चरणावुत्थाप्य मुनिपुङ्गवः। गाढमालिङ्ग्य सस्नेहमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।3.8.10।।
explanation: When both Rama and Lakshmana touched the feet of Sutikshna, the best of the sages, he lifted them up, hugged them tightly, and said affectionately:

shloka_text: अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं राम सौमित्रिणा सह। सीतया चानया सार्धं छाययेवानुवृत्तया।।3.8.11।।
explanation: You may safely tread, O Rama, this path along with Lakshmana and Sita who is following you like a shadow.

shloka_text: पश्याश्रमपदं रम्यं दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्। एषां तपस्विनां वीर तपसा भावितात्मनाम्।।3.8.12।।
explanation: O valient Rama the sages, living in  the Dandaka forest, are self realised souls. See how delightful is the location of their hermitages.

shloka_text: सप्राज्यफलमूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च। प्रशस्तमृगयूथानि शान्तपक्षिगणानि च।। 3.8.13।। फुल्लपङ्कजषण्डानि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च। कारण्डवविकीर्णानि तटाकानि सरांसि च।।3.8.14।। द्रक्ष्यसे दृष्टिरम्याणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च। रमणीयान्यरण्यानि मयूराभिरुतानि च।।3.8.15।।
explanation: You will see the beautiful forestareas with abundant fruits and roots, flowers in full bloom, herds of animals, flocks of quiet birds tanks and lakes filled  with clean waters and shining with fully blossomed lotuses, resounding with waterducks and peacocks  and waterfalls coming down the hills. Thus you will enjoy a delightful sylvan sight.

shloka_text: सप्राज्यफलमूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च। प्रशस्तमृगयूथानि शान्तपक्षिगणानि च।। 3.8.13।। फुल्लपङ्कजषण्डानि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च। कारण्डवविकीर्णानि तटाकानि सरांसि च।।3.8.14।। द्रक्ष्यसे दृष्टिरम्याणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च। रमणीयान्यरण्यानि मयूराभिरुतानि च।।3.8.15।।
explanation: You will see the beautiful forestareas with abundant fruits and roots, flowers in full bloom, herds of animals, flocks of quiet birds tanks and lakes filled  with clean waters and shining with fully blossomed lotuses, resounding with waterducks and peacocks  and waterfalls coming down the hills. Thus you will enjoy a delightful sylvan sight.

shloka_text: सप्राज्यफलमूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च। प्रशस्तमृगयूथानि शान्तपक्षिगणानि च।। 3.8.13।। फुल्लपङ्कजषण्डानि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च। कारण्डवविकीर्णानि तटाकानि सरांसि च।।3.8.14।। द्रक्ष्यसे दृष्टिरम्याणि गिरिप्रस्रवणानि च। रमणीयान्यरण्यानि मयूराभिरुतानि च।।3.8.15।।
explanation: You will see the beautiful forestareas with abundant fruits and roots, flowers in full bloom, herds of animals, flocks of quiet birds tanks and lakes filled  with clean waters and shining with fully blossomed lotuses, resounding with waterducks and peacocks  and waterfalls coming down the hills. Thus you will enjoy a delightful sylvan sight.

shloka_text: गम्यतां वत्स सौमित्रे भवानपि च गच्छतु। आगन्तव्यं च ते दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाश्रमं मम।।3.8.16।।
explanation: O dear Rama, O Lakshmana you may leave (now), you may have to come back to this hermitage after seeing those places.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा काकुत्स्थस्सहलक्ष्मणः। प्रदक्षिणं मुनिं कृत्वा प्रस्थातुमुपचक्रमे।।3.8.17।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Rama, scion of the Kakutsthas along with Lakshmana circumambulated the sage (in reverence) and set forth.

shloka_text: ततश्शुभतरे तूणी धनुषी चायतेक्षणा। ददौ सीता तयोर्भ्रात्रोः खङ्गौ च विमलौ ततः।।3.8.18।।
explanation: Thereafter largeeyed Sita handed the brothers two quivers, two bows as well as two excellent swords.

shloka_text: आबध्य च शुभे तूणी चापे चादाय सुस्वनौ। निष्क्रान्तावाश्रमाद्गन्तुमुभौ तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.8.19।।
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana  tied their auspicious quivers, took the two twanging bows and departed from the hermitage.

shloka_text: श्रीमन्तौ रूपसम्पन्नौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा। प्रस्थितौ धृतचापौ तौ सीतया सह राघवौ।।3.8.20।।
explanation: Handsome Rama and Lakshmana, glowing in their radiance held the bows and exited  with Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे अष्टमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सुतीक्ष्णेनाभ्यनुज्ञातं प्रस्थितं रघुनन्दनम्। हृद्यया स्निग्धया वाचा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।3.9.1।।
explanation: While Rama was leaving with the permission of Sutikshna, Sita spoke these warm, affectionate words to her husband:

shloka_text: अयं धर्मस्सुसूक्ष्मेण विधिना प्राप्यते महान्। निवृत्तेन तु शक्योऽयं व्यसनात्कामजादिह।।3.9.2।।
explanation: This great path of dharma you are following now can be attained only through subtle means by one free from addiction born of passion.

shloka_text: त्रीण्येव व्यसनान्यत्र कामजानि भवन्त्युत। मिथ्यावाक्यं परमकं तस्माद्गुरुतरावुभौ।।3.9.3।। परदाराभिगमनं विना वैरं च रौद्रता।
explanation: There are three kinds of vices born out of lust. First, speaking untruth, second, having sexual relation with others' wives and third, resorting to violence with no enmity. The later two vices are of serious nature.

shloka_text: मिथ्यावाक्यं न ते भूतं न भविष्यति राघव।।3.9.4।। कुतोऽभिलाषणं स्त्रीणां परेषां धर्मनाशनम्।
explanation: O Rama you never spoke untruth in the past nor will you speak in future. How can there be any desire in you to destroy the virtue of others' wives ?

shloka_text: तव नास्ति मनुष्येन्द्र न चाभूत्ते कदाचन।।3.9.5।। मनस्यपि तथा राम न चैतद्विद्यते क्वचित्।
explanation: O Rama, lord among men, you hadn't it (lust for other women) in the past. You havn't it now. Never does it exist even in your mind.

shloka_text: स्वदारनिरतस्त्वं च नित्यमेव नृपात्मज।।3.9.6।। धर्मिष्ठस्सत्यसन्धश्च पितुर्निर्देशकारकः।
explanation: O prince, you are always faithful to your wife. You are righteous, truthful and obedient to your father's orders.

shloka_text: सत्यसन्ध महाभाग श्रीमल्लक्ष्मणपूर्वज।।3.9.7।। त्वयि धर्मश्च सत्यं च त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
explanation: O Rama, you are truthful, honourable, powerful. O elder brother of Lakshmana, in you is established truth and righteousness.

shloka_text: तच्च सर्वं महाबाहो शक्यं धर्तुं जितेन्द्रियैः।।3.9.8।। तव वश्येन्द्रियत्वं च जानामि शुभदर्शन।
explanation: O longarmed one, to contain all this is only possible for those who have conquered the senses. O handsome one, I know your ability to control the senses.

shloka_text: तृतीयं यदिदं रौद्रं परप्राणाभिहिंसनम्।।3.9.9।। निर्वैरं क्रियते मोहात्तच्च ते समुपस्थितम्।
explanation: (But) you are a victim to the third (vice born of lust) i.e. showing violence without cause for enmity

shloka_text: प्रतिज्ञातस्त्वया वीर दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।।3.9.10।। ऋषीणां रक्षणार्थाय वधस्संयति रक्षसाम्।
explanation: O valiant one, you have promised to kill the demons in the battle, in order to protect the sages residing in the Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: एतन्निमित्तं च वनं दण्डका इति विश्रुतम्।।3.9.11।। प्रस्थितस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा धृतबाणशरासनः।
explanation: It is only on account of this that you entered the wellknown Dandaka forest with your brother wielding bow and arrows.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वां प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा मम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।।3.9.12।। त्वद्वृत्तं चिन्तयन्त्या वै भवेन्निश्श्रेयसं हितम्।
explanation: I am, therefore, worried in my mind when I see you here and think of your wellbeing. I wish your ultimate good. [The next two lines appear, more or less, a repetition. So omitted : Editor]

shloka_text: त्वां चैव प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा राम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।।3.9.13।। सर्वतचशिन्तय्नत्या मे तव निश्श्रेयसं नृप। न हि मे रोचते वीर गमनं दण्डकान्प्रति।।3.9.14।। कारणं तत्र वक्ष्यामि वदन्त्याश्श्रूयतां मम।
explanation: O brave Rama, I do not like your going to Dandaka forest. I shall tell you the reason. Do listen.

shloka_text: त्वां चैव प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा राम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।।3.9.13।। सर्वतचशिन्तय्नत्या मे तव निश्श्रेयसं नृप। न हि मे रोचते वीर गमनं दण्डकान्प्रति।।3.9.14।। कारणं तत्र वक्ष्यामि वदन्त्याश्श्रूयतां मम।
explanation: O brave Rama, I do not like your going to Dandaka forest. I shall tell you the reason. Do listen.

shloka_text: त्वं हि बाणधनुष्पाणिर्भ्रात्रा सह वनं गतः।।3.9.15।। दृष्ट्वा वनचरान्सर्वान्कच्चित्कुर्याश्शरव्ययम्।
explanation: Of course, you will go to the forest with your brother, holding the bow and arrows. Release the arrows when you see the forestrangers.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियाणामपि धनुर्हुताशस्येन्धनानि च।।3.9.16।। समीपतस्स्थितं तेजो बलमुच्छ्रयते भृशम्।
explanation: A bow in the hand of a kshatriya is like fuel to fire. It surely swells his strength and his brilliance.

shloka_text: पुरा किल महाबाहो तपस्स्वी सत्यवाक्छुचिः।।3.9.17।। कस्मिंश्चिदभवत्पुण्ये वने रतमृगद्विजे।
explanation: O mightyarmed one, there dwelt in the past an ascetic, noble and truthful in a sacred forest where animals and birds lived merrily together.

shloka_text: तस्यैव तपसो विघ्नं कर्तुमिन्द्रश्शचीपतिः।।3.9.18।। खङ्गपाणिरथागच्छदाश्रमं भटरूपधृत्।
explanation: Once Indra, husband of Sachi, came to his hermitage in the guise of an attendant, sword in hand, in order to hinder his penance.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तदाश्रमपदे निशितः खङ्ग उत्तमः।।3.9.19।। स न्यासविधिना दत्तः पुण्ये तपसि तिष्ठतः।
explanation: Then while the sage was practising penance at the hermitage, he gave him that excellent sword to be kept in trust.

shloka_text: स तच्छस्त्रमनुप्राप्य न्यासरक्षणतत्परः।।3.9.20।। वने तु विचरत्येव रक्षन्प्रत्ययमात्मनः।
explanation: Having received the weapon as a trust, the sage went wandering in the forest, always attentive in safeguarding the weapon.

shloka_text: यत्र गच्छत्युपादातुं मूलानि च फलानि च।।3.9.21।। न विना याति तं खङ्गं न्यासरक्षणतत्परः।
explanation: Vigilant about protecting the sword deposited with him, the sage never moved without it even when he went gathering roots and fruits.

shloka_text: नित्यं शस्त्रं परिवहन्क्रमेण स तपोधनः।।3.9.22।। चकार रौद्रीं स्वां बुद्धिं त्यक्त्वा तपसि निश्चयम्।
explanation: While the sage moved about holding the weapon, he gave up the practice of penance gradually and developed a violent mindset.

shloka_text: ततस्सरौद्रेऽभिरतः प्रमत्तोऽधर्मकर्शितः।।3.9.23।। तस्य शस्त्रस्य संवासाज्जगाम नरकं मुनिः।
explanation: By association with the sword, he developed a violent attitude. And in that habitual state of excitement he was dragged into unrighteous ways which (ultimately) took him to hell.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरा वृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्।।3.9.24।। अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुश्शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते। स्नेहाच्च बहुमानाच्च स्मारये त्वां न शिक्षये।।3.9.25।।
explanation: Contact with the weapon has led to this in the past. Like contact with fire, it leads man to destruction. I say this out of my love and reverence for you as a reminder and not as an instruction.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरा वृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्।।3.9.24।। अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुश्शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते। स्नेहाच्च बहुमानाच्च स्मारये त्वां न शिक्षये।।3.9.25।।
explanation: Contact with the weapon has led to this in the past. Like contact with fire, it leads man to destruction. I say this out of my love and reverence for you as a reminder and not as an instruction.

shloka_text: न कथञ्चन सा कार्या गृहीतधनुषा त्वया। बुद्धिर्वैरं  विना हन्तुं राक्षसान्दण्डकाश्रितान्।।3.9.26।। अपराधं विना हन्तुं लोकान्वीर न कामये।
explanation: While holding a bow, you should not have the intention to kill demons residing in Dandaka with no animosity against you. O valiant one  I do not desire that any one should be killed without incurring any offence.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियाणां तु वीराणां वनेषु निरतात्मनाम्।।3.9.27।। धनुषा कार्यमेतावदार्तानां त्वभिरक्षणम्।
explanation: It is the duty of a kshatriya, a warrior to protect with his bow those who practise selfcontrol (penance) in the forest in a state of panic.

shloka_text: क्वच शस्त्रं क्व च वनं क्व च क्षात्रं तपः क्वच।।3.9.28।। व्याविद्धमिदमस्माभिर्द्देशधर्मस्तु पूज्यताम्।
explanation: Where is the question of wielding a weapon and living in the forest, where is the life of a kshatriya and the life of penance? For us, this is an encroachment. Let the law of the land be honoured.

shloka_text: तदार्य कलुषा बुद्धिर्जायते शस्त्रसेवनात्।।3.9.29।। पुनर्गत्वा त्वयोध्यायां क्षत्रधर्मं चरिष्यसि।
explanation: Lord, when we handle the weapon, the mind gets vitiated. (Only) after returning to Ayodhya can you perform the duty of a kshatriya.

shloka_text: अक्षया तु भवेत्प्रीतिश्श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोर्मम।।3.9.30।। यदि राज्यं परित्यज्य भवेस्त्वं निरतो मुनिः।
explanation: You would have been on unlimited source of joy to my fatherinlaw and motherinlaw had you permanently renounced the kingdom for the life of an ascetic.

shloka_text: धर्मादर्थः प्रभवति धर्मात्प्रभवते सुखम्।।3.9.31।। धर्मेण लभते सर्वं धर्मसारमिदं जगत्।
explanation: Righteousness brings wealth. Wealth brings happiness. Righteousness brings everything. In fact, the essence of the world is righteousness.

shloka_text: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तै कर्शयित्वा प्रयत्नतः।।3.9.32।। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभ्यते सुखम्।
explanation: The wise earn dharma through getting their bodies emaciated by carefully adopting different means of discipline (selftorture). Happiness does not beget happiness.

shloka_text: नित्यं शुचिमतिस्सौम्य चर धर्मं तपोवने।।3.9.33।। सर्वं हि विदितं तुभ्यं त्रैलोक्यमपि तत्त्वतः।
explanation: O gentle one you may move in this forest of ascetics with a pure mind. The true meaning behind everything in these three worlds is known to you, indeed.

shloka_text: वाक्यमेतत्तु वैदेह्या व्याहृतं भर्तृभक्तया। श्रुत्वा धर्मे स्थितो रामः प्रत्युवाचाथ मैथिलीम्।।3.10.1।।
explanation: Having heard these words spoken by Sita who was devoted to her husband, replied Rama who was firm in righteousness.

shloka_text: हितमुक्तं त्वया देवि स्निग्धया सदृशं वचः। कुलं व्यपदिशन्त्या च धर्मज्ञे जनकात्मजे।।3.10.2।।
explanation: O daughter of Janaka, you are conversant with dharma. Whatever you have admonished out of affection for me is befitting your race.

shloka_text: किन्तु वक्ष्याम्यहं देवि त्वयैवोक्तमिदं वचः। क्षत्रियैर्धार्यते चापो नार्तशब्दो भवेदिति।।3.10.3।।
explanation: But permit me, Devi, you have already stated, when a kshatriya holds a bow there will be no cry of distress. (it means you approve of my holding a bow)

shloka_text: ते चार्ता दण्डकारण्ये मुनयस्संशितव्रताः। मां सीते स्वयमागम्य शरण्याश्शरणं गताः।।3.10.4।।
explanation: O Sita, the sages who perform rigorous penance in Dandaka forest came to me personally, seeking shelter although they can be their own protection.

shloka_text: वसन्तो धर्मनिरता वने मूलफलाशनाः। न लभन्ते सुखं भीता राक्षसैः क्रूरकर्मभिः।।3.10.5।।
explanation: The sages living in the forest, eating roots and fruits and ever engaged in righteous activities are afraid of the depredations of the demons, with their happiness gone.

shloka_text: काले काले च निरता नियमैर्विविधैर्वने। भक्ष्यन्ते राक्षसैर्भीमैर्नरमांसोपजीविभिः।।3.10.6।।
explanation: The sages engrossed in various austerities in the forest have been victims to the dreadful demons living on human flesh.

shloka_text: ते भक्ष्यमाणा मुनयो दण्डकारण्यवासिनः। अस्मानभ्यवपद्येति मामूचुर्द्विजसत्तमा।।3.10.7।।
explanation: The ascetics, the best of brahmins living in Dandaka forest being eaten up like that besought me to come to their rescue.

shloka_text: मया तु वचनं श्रुत्वा तेषामेवं मुखाच्च्युतम्। कृत्वा चरणशुश्रूषां वाक्यमेतदुदाहृतम्।।3.10.8।।
explanation: On hearing the words that came from their mouth, I bowed at their feet and said:

shloka_text: प्रसीदन्तु भवन्तो मे ह्रीरेषा हि ममातुला। यदीदृशैरहं विप्रैरुपस्थेयैरुपस्थितः।।3.10.9।।
explanation: Be pleased  That brahmins like you have approached me while I should have come to you has put me to shame immeasurable .

shloka_text: किं करोमीति च मया व्याहृतं द्विजसन्निधौ। सर्वैरेतैस्समागम्य वागियं समुदाहृता।।3.10.10।।
explanation: I enquired about what I could do for them. And all the brahmins in one voice said:.

shloka_text: राक्षसैर्दण्डकारण्ये बहुभिः कामरूपिभिः। अर्दितास्स्म दृढं राम भवान्नस्तत्र रक्षतु।।3.10.11।।
explanation: 'O Rama, the demons who can assume any form at their will are mercilessly tormenting us in Dandaka forest. Do protect us from them'.

shloka_text: होमकालेषु सम्प्राप्ताः पर्वकालेषु चानघ। धर्षयन्ति सुदुर्धर्षा राक्षसाः पिशिताशनाः।।3.10.12।।
explanation: 'O sinless one, these cannibals are invincible. They arrive at the time of our sacrificial rituals, on the days of festivities or at the time of lunar conjunctions like no moon or full moon days and attack us.

shloka_text: राक्षसैर्धर्षितानां च तापसानां तपस्विनाम्। गतिं मृगयमाणानां भवान्नः परमा गतिः।।3.10.13।।
explanation: 'You are the supreme refuge for us ascetics, tormented by demons, helpless men in search of shelter.

shloka_text: कामं तपःप्रभावेन शक्ता हन्तुं निशाचरान्। चिरार्जितं तु नेच्छामस्तपः खण्डयितुं वयम्।।3.10.14।।
explanation: Indeed, by the power of our penance, we are capable of killing the night-roamers. But we do not wish to destroy the penance we have acquired over a long time.

shloka_text: बहुविघ्नं तपो नित्यं दुश्चरं चैव राघव। तेन शापं न मुञ्चामो भक्ष्यमाणाश्च राक्षसैः।।3.10.15।।
explanation: 'O Rama it is difficult to perform penance which is ever full of obstacles. Therefore, we do not pronounce curses even if eaten up by demons'.

shloka_text: तदर्ध्यमानान्रक्षोभिर्दण्डकारण्यवासिभिः। रक्ष नस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा त्वन्नाथा हि वयं वने।।3.10.16।।
explanation: 'The demons, dwelling in the Dandaka forest are tormenting us. You alone are our lord in the forest. Do protect us with your brother.'

shloka_text: मया चैतद्वचश्श्रुत्वा कार्त्स्न्येन परिपालनम्। ऋषीणां दण्डकारण्ये संश्रुतं जनकात्मजे।।3.10.17।।
explanation: O daughter of Janaka, on hearing the words of the sages I promised to undertake the entire protection of sages of the Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: संश्रुत्य च न शक्ष्यामि जीवमानः प्रतिश्रवम्। मुनीनामन्यथा कर्तुं सत्यमिष्टं हि मे सदा।।3.10.18।।
explanation: Having promised the sages, I cannot do otherwise as long as I have life in me. To me truth is always dear.

shloka_text: अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां त्वां वा सीते सलक्ष्मणाम्। न तु प्रतिज्ञां संश्रुत्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशेषतः।।3.10.19।।
explanation: O Sita I may forfeit my life forsake, even Lakshmana and you but will not break the promise made specially to the brahmins৷৷

shloka_text: तदवश्यं मया कार्यमृषीणां परिपालनम्। अनुक्तेनापि वैदेहि प्रतिज्ञाय तु किं पुनः।।3.10.20।।
explanation: Even before the sages requested me I should have protected them. What to speak of the promise I have already made ?

shloka_text: मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तंत्वयाऽनघे। परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशिष्यते।।3.10.21।।
explanation: O sinless one all that has been said by you is out of your love and affection for me. I am pleased. What is harmful is never advised.

shloka_text: सदृशं चानुरूपं च कुलस्य तव चात्मनः। सधर्मचारिणी मे त्वं प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी।।3.10.22।।
explanation: Your auspicious words are quite befitting your lineage. You are the follower of my dharma and so dearer to me than my life.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा सीतां प्रियां मैथिलराजपुत्रीम्। रामो धनुष्मान्सह लक्ष्मणेन जगाम रम्याणि तपोवनानि।।3.10.23।।
explanation: Having said this to Sita, the princess of Mithila, Rama along with Lakshmana, bow in hand, moved about the delightful penancegrove. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे दशमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the tenth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by the sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अग्रतः प्रययौ रामस्सीता मध्ये सुमध्यमा। पृष्ठतस्तु धनुष्पाणिर्लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह।।3.11.1।।
explanation: Rama walked in front, Sita with a beautiful waist, in the middle and Lakshmana holding the bow, behind them৷৷

shloka_text: तौ पश्यमानौ विविधान् शैलप्रस्थान्वनानि च। नदीश्च विविधा रम्या जग्मतुस्सीतया सह।।3.11.2।।
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana walked on, accompanied by Sita, watching several beautiful mountain ranges, forests  and rivers.

shloka_text: सारसांश्चक्रवाकांश्च नदीपुलिनचारिणः। सरांसि च सपद्मानि युक्तानि जलजैः खगैः।।3.11.3।।
explanation: (Watching) the swans and ruddy geese on river banks and lakes full of lotuses, and birds on water and in the sky.

shloka_text: यूथबद्धांश्च पृषतान्मदोन्मत्तान् विषाणिनः। महिषांश्च वराहांश्च नागांश्च द्रुमवैरिणः।।3.11.4।।
explanation: (Watching) herds of deer, intoxicated horned buffaloes, wild boars and elephants who are enemies of trees (elephants uproof trees).

shloka_text: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं लम्बमाने दिवाकरे। ददृशुस्सहिता रम्यं तटाकं योजनायतम्।।3.11.5।। पद्मपुष्करसम्बाधं गजयूथैरलङ्कृतम्। सारसैर्हंसकादम्बैस्सङ्कुलं जलचारिभिः।।3.11.6।।
explanation: As the Sun was setting, they had covered a long distance, watching a yojanalong tank adorned with lotuses, and crowded with herds of elephants and flocks of cranes, swans and aquatic animals.

shloka_text: ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं लम्बमाने दिवाकरे। ददृशुस्सहिता रम्यं तटाकं योजनायतम्।।3.11.5।। पद्मपुष्करसम्बाधं गजयूथैरलङ्कृतम्। सारसैर्हंसकादम्बैस्सङ्कुलं जलचारिभिः।।3.11.6।।
explanation: As the Sun was setting, they had covered a long distance, watching a yojanalong tank adorned with lotuses, and crowded with herds of elephants and flocks of cranes, swans and aquatic animals.

shloka_text: प्रसन्नसलिले रम्ये तस्मिन्सरसि शुश्रुवे। गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषो न तु कश्चन दृश्यते।।3.11.7।।
explanation: In that lake of clear waters they heard the sounds of songs and musical instruments, while there were none around.

shloka_text: ततः कौतूहलाद्रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः। मुनिं धर्मभृतं नाम प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।3.11.8।।
explanation: Out of curiosity, mighty Rama, and Lakshmana started enquiring about the matter from sage Dharmabrata by name:

shloka_text: इदमत्यद्भुतं श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां नो महामुने। कौतूहलं महज्जातं किमिदं साधु कथ्यताम्।।3.11.9।। वक्तव्यं यदि चेदविप्र नातिगुह्यमपि प्रभो।
explanation: O great sage, this very wonderful sound, has whetted our great curiosity. If there is no top secret about this, do disclose it.

shloka_text: तेनैवमुक्तो धर्मात्मा राघवेण मुनिस्तदा।।3.11.10।। प्रभवं सरसः कृत्स्नमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे।
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, the righteous sage narrated the entire origin of the lake.

shloka_text: इदं पञ्चाप्सरो नाम तटाकं सार्वकालिकम्।।3.11.11।। निर्मितं तपसा राम मुनिना माण्डकर्णिना।
explanation: O Rama this lake called Panchapsara  filled with water at all times has been created through penance by a sage called Mandakarni.

shloka_text: स हि तेपे तपस्तीव्रं माण्डकर्णिर्महामुनिः।।3.11.12।। दशवर्षसहस्राणि वायुभक्षो जलाश्रयः।
explanation: Great sage Mandakarni standing in water and living on air performed  rigorous penance for ten thousand years.

shloka_text: ततः प्रव्यथितास्सर्वे देवास्साग्निपुरोगमाः।।3.11.13।। अब्रुवन् वचनं सर्वे परस्परसमागताः।
explanation: Thereafter very much perturbed, all the gods led by Agni gathered together at one place and started deliberating among themselves.

shloka_text: अस्माकं कस्यचित् स्थानमेष प्रार्थयते मुनिः।।3.11.14।। इति संविग्नमनसस्सर्वे ते त्रिदिवौकसः।
explanation: 'The gods of heaven became agitated in their minds thinking the sage might usurp one of their places.

shloka_text: तत्र कर्तुं तपोविघ्नं देवैस्सर्वैर्नियोजिताः।।3.11.15।। प्रधानाप्सरसः पञ्च विद्युच्चलितवर्चसः।
explanation: All the gods then engaged five of the important nymphs, glittering like lightning, to disturb the penance of the sage.

shloka_text: अप्सरोभिस्ततस्ताभिर्मुनिर्दृष्टपरावरः।।3.11.16।। नीतो मदनवश्यत्वं सुराणां कार्यसिद्धये।
explanation: The sage, a knower of the inner self and the world of plurality, was gripped by passion for the apsaras, who had come to achieve the target of the gods.

shloka_text: ताश्चैवाप्सरसः पञ्च मुनेः पत्नीत्वमागताः।।3.11.17।। तटाके निर्मितं तासामस्मिन्नन्तर्हितं गृहम्।
explanation: The five apsaras, got the status of wives to the sage who built them an invisible home inside the lake.

shloka_text: तथैवाप्सरसः पञ्च निवसन्त्यो यथासुखम्।।3.11.18।। रमयन्ति तपोयोगान्मुनिं यौवनमास्थितम्।
explanation: The apsaras lived happily with the sage who remained youthful by virtue of his penance.

shloka_text: तासां सङ्क्रीडमानानामेष वादित्रनिस्स्वनः।।3.11.19।। श्रूयते भूषणोन्मिश्रो गीतशब्दो मनोहरः।
explanation: While the apsaras played their musical instruments, their melodious songs mingled with the sounds of ornaments are heard.

shloka_text: आश्चर्यमिति तस्यैतद्वचनं भावितात्मनः।।3.11.20।। राघवः प्रतिजग्राह सह भ्रात्रा महायशाः।
explanation: Glorious Rama and his brother heard the wonderful words of the selfrealised sage and exclaimed, 'How strange '

shloka_text: एवं कथयमानस्य ददर्शाश्रममण्डलम्।।3.11.21।। कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तं ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्।
explanation: When the sage Dharmabrata was telling the story, Rama saw a hermitage strewn all over with kusa grass and bark garments, and endowed with pure brahminic grace.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च राघवः।।3.11.22।। उवास मुनिभिस्सर्वैः पूज्यमानो महायशाः।
explanation: Illustrious Rama accompanied by Vaidehi and Lakshmana entered the hermitage and, honoured by all the sages, stayed there.

shloka_text: तदा तस्मिन्सकाकुत्थ्सः श्रीमत्याश्रममण्डले।।3.11.23।। उषित्वा तु सुखं तत्र पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः। जगाम चाश्रमांस्तेषां पर्यायेण तपस्विनाम्।।3.11.24।। येषामुषितवान् पूर्वं सकाशे स महास्त्रवित्।
explanation: Rama, the scion of the Kakutstha race, wielder of great weapons, stayed in that beautiful hermitage, accepting the hospitality of the sages extended with due honour, He visited in turn their penancegroves where he repeated his stay.

shloka_text: तदा तस्मिन्सकाकुत्थ्सः श्रीमत्याश्रममण्डले।।3.11.23।। उषित्वा तु सुखं तत्र पूज्यमानो महर्षिभिः। जगाम चाश्रमांस्तेषां पर्यायेण तपस्विनाम्।।3.11.24।। येषामुषितवान् पूर्वं सकाशे स महास्त्रवित्।
explanation: Rama, the scion of the Kakutstha race, wielder of great weapons, stayed in that beautiful hermitage, accepting the hospitality of the sages extended with due honour, He visited in turn their penancegroves where he repeated his stay.

shloka_text: क्वचित्परिदशान्मासानेकं संवत्सरं क्वचित्।।3.11.25।। क्वचिच्छ चतुरो मासान् पञ्च षट्चापरान्क्वचित्। अपरत्राधिकं मासादप्यर्धमधिकं क्वचित्।।3.11.26।। त्रीन्मासानष्टमासांश्च राघवो न्यवसत्सुखम्।
explanation: Rama lived happily here for about ten months, there one year, here four or five or six months and there over one or half a month or three or eight months in another.

shloka_text: क्वचित्परिदशान्मासानेकं संवत्सरं क्वचित्।।3.11.25।। क्वचिच्छ चतुरो मासान् पञ्च षट्चापरान्क्वचित्। अपरत्राधिकं मासादप्यर्धमधिकं क्वचित्।।3.11.26।। त्रीन्मासानष्टमासांश्च राघवो न्यवसत्सुखम्।
explanation: Rama lived happily here for about ten months, there one year, here four or five or six months and there over one or half a month or three or eight months in another.

shloka_text: तथा संवसतस्तस्य मुनीनामाश्रमेषु वै।।3.11.27।। रमतश्चानुकूल्येन ययुस्संवत्सरा दश।
explanation: Thus enjoying their stay in the hermitages, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana spent ten favourable years.

shloka_text: परिवृत्य च धर्मज्ञो राघवस्सह सीतया।।3.11.28।। सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमं श्रीमान्पुनरेवाजगाम ह।
explanation: Rama went round who was full of grace and full of knowledge on dharma went round with Sita and came back to Suthikshna's hermitage.

shloka_text: स तमाश्रममासाद्य मुनिभिः प्रतिपूजितः।।3.11.29।। तत्रापि न्यवसद्रामः कञ्चित्कालमरिन्दमः।
explanation: On his arrival, Rama, the subduer of enemies, was honoured by the sages at the hermitage where he stayed for a short time.

shloka_text: तदाश्रमस्थो विनयात्कदाचित्तं महामुनिम्।।3.11.30।। उपासीनस्सकाकुत्स्थस्सुतीक्ष्णमिदमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Once while sitting beside sage Sutikshna at the hermitage Rama humbly addressed him:

shloka_text: अस्मिन्नरण्ये भगवानगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः।।3.11.31।। वसतीति मया नित्यं कथाः कथयतां श्रुतम्।
explanation: I have heard others saying that lord Agastya, the great sage, lives in this forest.

shloka_text: न तु जानामि तं देशं वनस्यास्य महत्तया।।3.11.32।। कुत्राश्रमपदं रम्यं महर्षेस्तस्य धीमतः।
explanation: I am unable to locate the sacred hermitage of that sagacious sage due to the vastness of this forest.

shloka_text: प्रसादात्तत्र भवतस्सानुजस्सह सीतया।।3.11.33।। अगस्त्यमभिगच्छेयमभिवादयितुं मुनिम्।
explanation: By your grace, I wish to go there with Sita and my brother Lakshmana to offer our respectful salutations.

shloka_text: मनोरथो महानेष हृदि मे परिवर्तते।।3.11.34।। यद्यहं तं मुनिवरं शुश्रूषेयमपि स्वयम्।
explanation: There is a great desire  in my heart to serve in person the best of sages, Agastya.

shloka_text: इति रामस्य स मुनिश्श्रुत्वा धर्मात्मनो वचः।।3.11.35।। सुतीक्ष्णः प्रत्युवाचेदं प्रीतो दशरथात्मजम्।
explanation: Hearing the words of Rama, the righteous son of Dasaratha, sage Sutikshna was pleased to reply:

shloka_text: अहमप्येतदेव त्वां वक्तुकामस्सलक्ष्मणम्।।3.11.36।। अगस्त्यमभिगच्छेति सीतया सह राघव।
explanation: I also wished you, O Raghava, to visit Agastya along with Sita and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या त्विदानीमर्थेऽस्मिन् स्वयमेव ब्रवीषि माम्।।3.11.37।। अहमाख्यामि ते वत्स यत्रागस्त्यो महामुनिः।
explanation: Luckily you have asked me on your own. I will tell you where the great sage Agastya lives.

shloka_text: योजनान्याश्रमात्तात याहि चत्वारि वै ततः।।3.11.38।। दक्षिणेन महान् श्रीमानगस्त्यभ्रातुराश्रमः।
explanation: Dear Rama, walk from here a distance of four yojanas. There in the southerly direction  stands the great, beautiful hermitage of Agastya's brother.

shloka_text: स्थलप्राये वनोद्देशे पिप्पलीवनशोभिते।।3.11.39।। बहुपुष्पफले रम्ये नानाशकुनिनादिते।
explanation: This plain land in the beautiful forest tract is adorned with fig trees,filled with  flowers, fruits, and delightful sounds of different birds.

shloka_text: पद्मिन्यो विविधास्तत्र प्रसन्नसलिलाश्शिवाः।।3.11.40।। हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः। तत्रैकां रजनीं व्युष्य प्रभाते राम गम्यताम्।।3.11.41।।
explanation: O Rama, there are lotusponds filled with clear, sacred waters, with different kinds of swans, ducks and ruddy geese. Spend one night there and proceed early in the morning.

shloka_text: पद्मिन्यो विविधास्तत्र प्रसन्नसलिलाश्शिवाः।।3.11.40।। हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः। तत्रैकां रजनीं व्युष्य प्रभाते राम गम्यताम्।।3.11.41।।
explanation: O Rama, there are lotusponds filled with clear, sacred waters, with different kinds of swans, ducks and ruddy geese. Spend one night there and proceed early in the morning.

shloka_text: दक्षिणां दिशमास्थाय वनषण्डस्य पार्श्वतः। तत्रागस्त्याश्रमपदं गत्वा योजनमन्तरा।।3.11.42।।
explanation: If you go in the southern direction for a yojana you will find Agasthya's hermitage by the side of a cluster of trees.

shloka_text: रमणीये वनोद्धेशे बहुपादपसंवृते। रंस्यते तत्र वैदेही लक्ष्मणश्च सह त्वया।।3.11.43।। स हि रम्यो वनोद्देशो बहुपादपसङ्कुलः।
explanation: Vaidehi will feel happy in your company in that delightful forest region full of many trees.So too will Lakshmana.

shloka_text: यदि बुद्धिः कृता द्रष्टुमगस्त्यं तं महामुनिम्।।3.11.44।। अद्यैव गमने बुद्धिं रोचयस्व महायशः।
explanation: O glorious one, if you have made up your mind to visit that great sage Agastya, think of starting today itself.

shloka_text: इति रामो मुनेश्श्रुत्वा सह भ्रात्राभिवाद्य च।।3.11.45।। प्रतस्थेऽमुद्दिश्य सानुजस्सीतया सह।
explanation: Rama heard the words of the sage, offered him reverential salutations and set out along with his brother and Sita.

shloka_text: पश्यन्वनानि रम्याणि पर्वतांश्चाभ्रसन्निभान्।।3.11.46।। सरांसि सरितश्चैव पथि मार्गवशानुगाः। सुतीक्ष्णेनोपदिष्टेन गत्वा तेन पथा सुखम्।।3.11.47।। इदं परमसंहृष्टो वाक्यं लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Enjoying the sight of delightful forests, cloudlike mountains, lakes and rivers on the  way, and following the directions given by  Sutikshna, Rama was happy. He said  to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: पश्यन्वनानि रम्याणि पर्वतांश्चाभ्रसन्निभान्।।3.11.46।। सरांसि सरितश्चैव पथि मार्गवशानुगाः। सुतीक्ष्णेनोपदिष्टेन गत्वा तेन पथा सुखम्।।3.11.47।। इदं परमसंहृष्टो वाक्यं लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Enjoying the sight of delightful forests, cloudlike mountains, lakes and rivers on the  way, and following the directions given by  Sutikshna, Rama was happy. He said  to Lakshmana:

shloka_text: एतदेवाश्रमपदं नूनं तस्य महात्मनः।।3.11.48।। अगस्त्यस्य मुनेर्भ्रातुर्दृश्यते पुण्यकर्मणः।
explanation: Surely this is the hermitage of great Agastya's brother, a man of holy deeds.

shloka_text: यथा हि मे वनस्यास्य ज्ञाताः पथि सहस्रशः।।3.11.49।। सन्नताः फलभारेण पुष्पभारेण च द्रुमाः।
explanation: This is the glade we were told about with thousands of trees drooping down with abundant fruits and flowers.

shloka_text: पिप्पलीनां च पक्वानां वनादस्मादुपागतः।।3.11.50।। गन्धोऽयं पवनोक्षिप्तस्सहसा कटुकोदयः।
explanation: Feel this sudden astringent smell of ripe figs wafted by the breeze from the forest.

shloka_text: तत्र तत्र च दृश्यन्ते सङ्क्षिप्ताः काष्ठसञ्चयाः।।3.11.51।। लूनाश्च पथि दृश्यन्ते दर्भा वैडूर्यवर्चसः।
explanation: Heaps of firewood are seen here and there on the path. There are blades of grass (used for sacrificial ceremonies) shining like vaidurya (gems).

shloka_text: एतच्च वनमध्यस्थं कृष्णाभ्रशिखरोपमम्।।3.11.52।। पावकस्याश्रमस्थस्य धूमाग्रं सम्प्रदृश्यते।
explanation: In the middle of the forest can be seen like the tip of the dark clouds columns of smoke coming out of the top of hermitages.

shloka_text: विविक्तेषु च तीर्थेषु कृतस्नाना द्विजातयः।।3.11.53।। पुष्पोपहारं कुर्वन्ति कुसुमैस्स्वयमर्जितै।
explanation: Priests are coming out of the solitary sacred spots after their bath and making offerings of flowers they had themselves plucked.

shloka_text: तत्सुतीक्ष्णस्य वचनं यथा सौम्य मया श्रुतम्।।3.11.54।। अगस्त्यस्याश्रमो भ्रातुर्नूनमेष भविष्यति।
explanation: O handsome one, surely this is the hermitage of Agastya's brother about which I heard from Sutikshna.

shloka_text: निगृह्य तपसा मृत्युं लोकानां हितकाम्यया।।3.11.55।। यस्य भ्रात्रा कृतेयं दिक्छरण्या पुण्यकर्मणा।
explanation: Having subdued death by penance, with the desire for the welfare of the worlds, by whose brother, of meritorious deeds, this direction was made protective.

shloka_text: धारयन् ब्राह्मणं रूपमिल्वलस्संस्कृतं वदन्।।3.11.56।। आमन्त्रयति विप्रान्स्मश्राद्धमुद्दिश्य निर्घृणः।
explanation: Assuming the form of a brahmin and using Sanskrit language, Ilvala would invite brahmins for offering shraddha to the dead

shloka_text: भ्रातरं संस्कृतं कृत्वा ततस्तं मेषरूपिणम्।।3.11.57।। तान् द्विजान्भोजयामास श्राद्धदृष्टेन कर्मणा।
explanation: Ilvala would keep his brother sanctified, so that he is fit for offering, Then he would feed the brahmins with mutton according to the rituals.

shloka_text: भ्रातरं संस्कृतं कृत्वा ततस्तं मेषरूपिणम्।।3.11.57।। तान् द्विजान्भोजयामास श्राद्धदृष्टेन कर्मणा।
explanation: Ilvala would keep his brother sanctified, so that he is fit for offering, Then he would feed the brahmins with mutton according to the rituals.

shloka_text: ततो भुक्तवतां तेषां विप्राणामिल्वलोऽब्रवीत्।।3.11.59।। वातापे निष्क्रमन्वेति स्वरेण महता वदन्।
explanation: Then when the brahmins finished eating, Ilvala would call aloud, 'O Vatapi come out'.

shloka_text: ततो भ्रातुर्वचश्श्रुत्वा वातापिर्मेषवन्नदन्।।3.11.60।। भित्त्वा भित्त्वा शरीराणि ब्राह्मणानां विनिष्पतत्।
explanation: Then hearing his brother's voice, Vatapi would bleat like a sheep and jump out, tearing open the bodies of those brahmins.

shloka_text: ब्राह्माणानां सहस्राणि तैरेवं कामरूपिभिः।।3.11.61।। विनाशितानि संहत्य नित्यशः पिशिताशनैः।
explanation: In this manner, thousands of brahmins used to be killed daily by those carnivorous demons who assumed any form at their free will.

shloka_text: अगस्त्येन तदा देवैः प्रार्थितेन महर्षिणा।।3.11.62।। अनुभूय किल श्राद्धे भक्षितस्समहासुरः।
explanation: Urged by the gods, Agastya  came  for the shradda . The mighty demon played the same routine trick and Vatapi, for sure, was eaten by the great sage.

shloka_text: ततस्सम्पन्नमित्युक्त्वा दत्त्वा हस्तोदकं ततः।।3.11.63।। भ्रातरं निष्क्रमस्वेति चेल्वलस्सोऽभ्यभाषत।
explanation: Saying, the ritual is complete Ilvala offered water in the palm of Agastya and called his brother to come out.

shloka_text: स तं तथा भाषमाणं भ्रातरं विप्रघातिनम्।।3.11.64।। अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्धीमानगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः।
explanation: Wise Agastya,  the best among the ascetics, laughing aloud, said to Ilvala, the destroyer of brahmins:

shloka_text: कुतो निष्क्रमितुं शक्तिर्मया जीर्णस्य रक्षसः।।3.11.65।। भ्रातुस्ते मेषरूपस्य गतस्य यमसादनम्।
explanation: I have digested the demon Vatapi your brother, who assumed the form of a sheep. He has reached the abode of Yama, Lord of death. Where does he have the power to come out?

shloka_text: अथ तस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्निधनसंश्रयम्।।3.11.66।। प्रधर्षयितुमारेभे मुनिं क्रोधान्निशाचरः।
explanation: On hearing the news of the death of his brother, the demon Ilvala, out of anger, started attacking the sage.

shloka_text: सोऽभिद्रवन्मुनिश्रेष्ठं मुनिना दीप्ततेजसा।।3.11.67।। चक्षुषानलकल्पेन निर्दग्धो निधनं गतः।
explanation: Ilvala who pounced upon Agastya, the best among the sages whose lustre lay consumed by the fire of his eyes which were in flames.

shloka_text: तस्यायमाश्रमो भ्रातुस्तटाकवनशोभितः।।3.11.68।। विप्रानुकम्पया येन कर्मेदं दुष्करं कृतम्।
explanation: This hermitage surrounded by beautiful lakes and forests belongs to his brother (Sudarsana). Out of sympathy for Agastya, he has accomplished this difficult task.

shloka_text: एवं कथयमानस्य तस्य सौमित्रिणा सह। रामस्यास्तं गतस्सूर्यस्सन्ध्याकालोऽभ्यवर्ततः।।3.11.69।।
explanation: While Rama was thus narrating to Lakshmana (the story of Agastya), the Sun set and evening closed in.

shloka_text: उपास्य पश्चिमां सन्ध्यां सह भ्रात्रा यथाविधि। प्रविवेशाऽश्रमपदं तमृषिं सोऽभ्यवादयत्।।3.11.70।।
explanation: Rama with his brother Lakshmana duly offered oblations at twilight, entered the hermitage and greeted the sage (Sudarsana) with folded palms.

shloka_text: सम्यक् प्रतिगृहीतश्च मुनिना तेन राघवः। न्यवसत्तां निशामेकां प्राश्य मूलफलानि च।।3.11.71।।
explanation: Warmly received by the sage, Rama shared the roots and fruits and slept the night there.

shloka_text: तस्यां रात्य्रां व्यतीतायां विमले सूर्यमण्डले। भ्रातरं तमगस्त्यस्य ह्यामन्त्रयत राघवः।।3.11.72।।
explanation: When the night passed and the Sun became bright, Rama took leave of the brother of Agastya.

shloka_text: अभिवादये त्वां भगवन् सुखमध्युषितो निशाम्। आमन्त्रये त्वां गच्छामि गुरुं ते द्रष्टुमग्रजम्।।3.11.73।।
explanation: O Lord, the night has been wellspent. Now we humbly seek leave of you to see your respectable elder brother.

shloka_text: गम्यतामिति तेनोक्तो जगाम रघुनन्दनः। यथोद्दिष्टेन मार्गेण वनं तच्चावलोकयन्।।3.11.74।।
explanation: With his permission, Rama, the delight of the Raghu race, proceeded along the path indicated, watching (the beauty of) the forest.

shloka_text: नीवारान्पनसांस्तालांस्तिमिशान्वञ्चुलान्धवान्। चिरिबिल्वान्मधूकांश्च बिल्वानपि च तिन्दुकान्।।3.11.75।।
explanation: They passed by wild rice fields, jackfruit trees, palmyra and various other trees like Ashoka, trees with white flowers, old trees that existed for a long time, mahva trees, bilva trees and tindukas.

shloka_text: पुष्पितान्पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिरनुवेष्टितान्। ददर्श रामश्शतशस्तत्र कान्तारपादपान्।।3.11.76।। हस्तिहस्तैर्विमृदितान्वानरैरुपशोभितान्। मत्तैश्शकुनिसङ्घैश्च शतशश्च प्रणादितान्।।3.11.77।।
explanation: Rama saw hundreds of trees crushed by the trunks of elephants and by monkeys. He saw some trees echoing with notes of hundreds of intoxicated birds. He saw tree tops coiled with creepers in full bloom.

shloka_text: पुष्पितान्पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिरनुवेष्टितान्। ददर्श रामश्शतशस्तत्र कान्तारपादपान्।।3.11.76।। हस्तिहस्तैर्विमृदितान्वानरैरुपशोभितान्। मत्तैश्शकुनिसङ्घैश्च शतशश्च प्रणादितान्।।3.11.77।।
explanation: Rama saw hundreds of trees crushed by the trunks of elephants and by monkeys. He saw some trees echoing with notes of hundreds of intoxicated birds. He saw tree tops coiled with creepers in full bloom.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीत्समीपस्थं रामो राजीवलोचनः। पृष्ठतोऽनुगतं वीरं लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्।।3.11.78।।
explanation: Then the lotuseyed Rama said to the chivalrous, graceful Lakshmana who stood behind him:

shloka_text: स्निग्धपत्रा यथा वृक्षा यथा क्षान्ता मृगद्विजाः। आश्रमो नातिदूरस्थो महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः।।3.11.79।।
explanation: The leaves of the trees here are glossy, the animals and birds are peaceful. It appears the hermitage of the selfrealized great sage Agastya is not very far from here.

shloka_text: अगस्त्य इति विख्यातो लोके स्वेनैव कर्मणा। आश्रमो दृश्यते तस्य परिश्रान्तश्रमापहः।।3.11.80।।
explanation: Here is the hermitage of Agastya, wellknown in the world for his deeds a place of rest for those tired with hard work.

shloka_text: प्राज्यधूमाकुलवनश्चीरमालापरिष्कृतः। प्रशान्तमृगयूथश्च नानाशकुनिनादितः।।3.11.81।।
explanation: This forest is enveloped with the smoke rising from the sacrificial altar. There are rows of bark robes hanging. Herds of quiet animals lying and different kind of birds chirping around.

shloka_text: तस्येदमाश्रमपदं प्रभावाद्यस्य राक्षसैः। दिगियं दक्षिणा त्रासाद्दृश्यते नोपभुज्यते।।3.11.82।।
explanation: This is his hermitage. On account of his (Agastya's) impact the demons look south but cannot eat the hermits out of fear (for the sage).

shloka_text: यदा प्रभृति चाक्रान्ता दिगियं पुण्यकर्मणा। तदा प्रभृति निर्वैराः प्रशान्ता रजनीचराः।।3.11.83।।
explanation: Since the time Agastya of sacred deeds occupied this direction the demons are quiet, leaving all enmity.

shloka_text: नाम्ना चेयं भगवतो दक्षिणा दिक्प्रदक्षिणा। प्रथिता त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्धर्षा क्रूरकर्मभिः।।3.11.84।।
explanation: The southern side favourable to the people was famous by the name Agastya in the three worlds and stood unassailable to the demons.

shloka_text: मार्गं निरोद्धुं निरतो भास्करस्याचलोत्तमः। निदेशं पालयन्यस्य विन्ध्यशैला न वर्धते।।3.11.85।। अयं दीर्घायुषस्तस्य लोके विश्रुतकर्मणः। अगस्त्यस्याश्रम श्रीमान्विनीतजनसेवितः।।3.11.86।।
explanation: This is the hermitage of the longlived Agastya who is renowned for his deeds and is served by humble people. The great mountain Vindhya that was growing incessantly and obstructing the path of the Sun stopped growing any more in obedience to Agastya's words.

shloka_text: मार्गं निरोद्धुं निरतो भास्करस्याचलोत्तमः। निदेशं पालयन्यस्य विन्ध्यशैला न वर्धते।।3.11.85।। अयं दीर्घायुषस्तस्य लोके विश्रुतकर्मणः। अगस्त्यस्याश्रम श्रीमान्विनीतजनसेवितः।।3.11.86।।
explanation: This is the hermitage of the longlived Agastya who is renowned for his deeds and is served by humble people. The great mountain Vindhya that was growing incessantly and obstructing the path of the Sun stopped growing any more in obedience to Agastya's words.

shloka_text: एष लोकार्चितस्साधुर्हिते नित्यरतस्सताम्। अस्मानभिगतानेष श्रेयसा योजयिष्यति।।3.11.87।।
explanation: We are going to join this sage honoured by the people of the world and ever engaged in the welfare of the virtuous. This augurs well for us.

shloka_text: आराधयिष्याम्यत्राहमगस्त्यं तं महामुनिम्। शेषं च वनवासस्य सौम्य वत्स्याम्यहं प्रभो।।3.11.88।।
explanation: O noble, handsome Lakshmana, I will spend the rest of the exile in this forest in the worship of the great sage Agastya.

shloka_text: अत्र देवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः। अगस्त्यं नियताहारं सततं पर्युपासते।।3.11.89।।
explanation: The gods along with gandharvas, siddhas and great sages always serve Agastya, observing discipine in their food habits.

shloka_text: नात्र जीवेन्मृषावादी क्रूरो वा यदि वा शठः। नृशंसः कामवृत्तो वा मुनिरेष तथाविधः।।3.11.90।।
explanation: This sage is such type that he (his spiritual power) will not allow a liar or a cruel man or a deceitful or lustful  or wicked person to thrive here.

shloka_text: अत्र देवाश्च यक्षाश्च नागाश्च पतगैस्सह। वसन्ति नियताहारा धर्ममाराधयिष्णवः।।3.11.91।।
explanation: Here gods, yakshas, nagas and birds live, following the righteous path and observing discipline in food habits.

shloka_text: अत्र सिद्धा महात्मानो विमानैजस्सूर्यसन्निभैः। त्यक्तदेहा नवैर्देहैः स्वर्याताः परमर्षयः।।3.11.92।।
explanation: Here great souls like sages and siddhas gave up the ghost and with renewed bodies left for heaven on aerochariot resembling the Sun (in brightness).

shloka_text: यक्षत्वममरत्वं च राज्यानि विविधानि च। अत्र देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति भूतैराराधिताश्शुभैः।।3.11.93।।
explanation: Worshipped by benevolent beings, the gods here bestow on them the status of demigods or of the immortals or several kinds of kingdoms.

shloka_text: सप्रविश्याऽश्रमपदं लक्ष्मणो राघवानुजः। अगस्त्यशिष्यमासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।।3.12.1।।
explanation: Lakshmana, the younger brother of Rama,  entered the hermitage of Agastya and met one of his disciples and said to him these words :

shloka_text: राजा दशरथो नाम ज्येष्ठस्तस्य सुतो बली। रामः प्राप्तो मुनिं द्रष्टुं भार्यया सह सीतया।।3.12.2।।
explanation: The valiant eldest son of  king Dasaratha has come along with his wife Sita to see the sage.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणो नाम तस्याहं भ्राता त्ववरजो हितः। अनुकूलश्च भक्तश्च यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः।।3.12.3।।
explanation: I am his younger brother Lakshmana, his wellwisher and faithful devotee if you have at all heard about me.

shloka_text: ते वयं वनमत्युग्रं प्रविष्टाः पितृशासनात्। द्रष्टुमिच्छामहे सर्वे भगवन्तं निवेद्यताम्।।3.12.4।।
explanation: By the command of our father, we have entered this dense forest and desire to see the   divine sire. Please report.

shloka_text: तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य तपोधनः। तथेत्युक्त्वाऽग्निशरणं प्रविवेश निवेदितुम्।।3.12.5।।
explanation: The ascetic heard Lakshmana, and saying, 'let it be so', entered the firesanctuary to report.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं तपसा दुष्प्रधर्षणम्। कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेदं रामागमनमञ्जसा।।3.12.6।। यथोक्तं लक्ष्मणेनैव शिष्योऽगस्त्यस्य सम्मतः।
explanation: Having promptly entered, Agastya's favourite disciple with folded hands reported as he was told by Lakshmana about Rama's arrival to the great sage who was armed with the inviolable powers of penance :

shloka_text: पुत्रौ दशरथस्येमौ रामो लक्ष्मण एव च।।3.12.7।। प्रविष्टावाश्रमपदं सीतया सह भार्यया।
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana, the two sons of Dasaratha along with Sita, wife of Rama, have arrived at the hermitage.

shloka_text: द्रष्टुं भवन्तमायातौ शुश्रूषार्थमरिन्दमौ।।3.12.8।। यदत्रानन्तरं तत्त्वमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।
explanation: Both the subduers of enemies  have come here now to see and serve your Holiness. You may order what is to be done next.

shloka_text: ततश्शिष्यादुपश्रुत्य प्राप्तं रामं सलक्ष्मणम्।।3.12.9।। वैदेहीं च महाभागामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Having heard from the disciple about the arrival of Rama, Lakshmana and great daughter of the king of Videha the sage said :

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या रामश्चिरस्याद्य द्रष्टुं मां समुपागतः।।3.12.10।। मनसा काङ्क्षितं ह्यस्य मयाप्यागमनं प्रति।
explanation: It is good fortune that Rama has come here after a long time to see me. I was longing for his arrival.

shloka_text: गम्यतां सत्कृतो रामस्सभार्यस्सहलक्ष्मणः।।3.12.11।। प्रवेश्यतां समीपं मे किं चासौ न प्रवेशितः।
explanation: Go quickly and with due hospitality conduct Rama, his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana into my presence. Why was he not ushered in so long?

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना।। 3.12.12।। अभिवाद्याब्रवीच्छिष्यस्तथेति नियताञ्जलिः।
explanation: 'So be it ' said the disciple respectfully with folded palms in response to what the great sage, knower of dharma, commanded.

shloka_text: ततो निष्क्रम्य सम्भ्रान्तश्शिष्यो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।।3.12.13।। क्वासौ रामो मुनिं द्रष्टुमेतु प्रविशतु स्वयम्।
explanation: Then the disciple in a state of excitement came out of the hermitage and said to Lakshmana, 'Where is Rama? Let him come himself to see the sage'.

shloka_text: ततो गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं शिष्येण सह लक्ष्मणः।। 3.12.14।। दर्शयामास काकुत्स्थं सीतां च जनकात्मजाम्।
explanation: Then Lakshmana reached the entrance of the hermitage with the disciple  and showed  Rama of the Kakutstha race and Sita, daughter of Janaka .

shloka_text: तं शिष्यः प्रश्रितो वाक्यमगस्त्यवचनं ब्रुवन्।।3.12.15।। प्रावेशयद्यथान्यायं सत्कारार्हं सुसत्कृतम्।
explanation: The disciple humbly reported Agastya's words and ushered him in with befitting hospitality.

shloka_text: प्रविवेश ततो रामस्सीतया सहलक्ष्मणः।।3.12.16।। प्रशान्तहरिणाकीर्णमाश्रमं ह्यवलोकयन्।
explanation: Then Rama, Sita and Lakshmana entered the hermitage, watching herds of quietly moving deer (undisturbed by their entry).

shloka_text: स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमग्नेः स्थानं तथैव च।।3.12.17।। विष्णोः स्थानं महेन्द्रस्य स्थानं चैव विवस्वतः। सोमस्थानं भगस्थानं स्थानं कौबेरमेव च।।3.12.18।। दातुर्विधातुः स्थानेच वायोः स्थानं तथैव च। नागराजस्य च स्थानमनन्तस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.19।। स्थानं तथैव गायत्र्या वसूनां स्थानमेव च। स्थानं च पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.20।। कार्तिकेयस्य च स्थानं धर्मस्थानं च पश्यति।
explanation: Rama saw at the hermitage, the places (altars) of Brahma, Visnu, Agni (firegod), Indra, Sun, Moon, Bhaga, Kubera, Dhata (supreme spirit), Vidhata (creator Brahman), Vayu (Windgod), Ananta (great serpentking),  Gayatri, Vasu Pasahasta, Varuna, Kartikeya and Dharma .

shloka_text: स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमग्नेः स्थानं तथैव च।।3.12.17।। विष्णोः स्थानं महेन्द्रस्य स्थानं चैव विवस्वतः। सोमस्थानं भगस्थानं स्थानं कौबेरमेव च।।3.12.18।। धातुर्विधातुः स्थानं च वायोः स्थानं तथैव च। नागराजस्य च स्थानमनन्तस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.19।। स्थानं तथैव गायत्र्या वसूनां स्थानमेव च। स्थानं च पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.20।। कार्तिकेयस्य च स्थानं धर्मस्थानं च पश्यति।
explanation: Rama saw at the hermitage, the places (altars) of Brahma, Visnu, Agni (firegod), Indra, Sun, Moon, Bhaga, Kubera, Dhata (supreme spirit), Vidhata (creator Brahman), Vayu (Windgod), Ananta (great serpentking), Gayatri, Vasu Pasahasta, Varuna, Kartikeya and Dharma .

shloka_text: स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमग्नेः स्थानं तथैव च।।3.12.17।। विष्णोः स्थानं महेन्द्रस्य स्थानं चैव विवस्वतः। सोमस्थानं भगस्थानं स्थानं कौबेरमेव च।।3.12.18।। दातुर्विधातुः स्थानेच वायोः स्थानं तथैव च। नागराजस्य च स्थानमनन्तस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.19।। स्थानं तथैव गायत्र्या वसूनां स्थानमेव च। स्थानं च पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.20।। कार्तिकेयस्य च स्थानं धर्मस्थानं च पश्यति।
explanation: Rama saw at the hermitage, the places (altars) of Brahma, Visnu, Agni (firegod), Indra, Sun, Moon, Bhaga, Kubera, Dhata (supreme spirit), Vidhata (creator Brahman), Vayu (Windgod), Ananta (great serpentking),  Gayatri, Vasu Pasahasta, Varuna, Kartikeya and Dharma .

shloka_text: स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानमग्नेः स्थानं तथैव च।।3.12.17।। विष्णोः स्थानं महेन्द्रस्य स्थानं चैव विवस्वतः। सोमस्थानं भगस्थानं स्थानं कौबेरमेव च।।3.12.18।। दातुर्विधातुः स्थानेच वायोः स्थानं तथैव च। नागराजस्य च स्थानमनन्तस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.19।। स्थानं तथैव गायत्र्या वसूनां स्थानमेव च। स्थानं च पाशहस्तस्य वरुणस्य महात्मनः।।3.12.20।। कार्तिकेयस्य च स्थानं धर्मस्थानं च पश्यति।
explanation: Rama saw at the hermitage, the places (altars) of Brahma, Visnu, Agni (firegod), Indra, Sun, Moon, Bhaga, Kubera, Dhata (supreme spirit), Vidhata (creator Brahman), Vayu (Windgod), Ananta (great serpentking),  Gayatri, Vasu Pasahasta, Varuna, Kartikeya and Dharma .

shloka_text: ततश्शिष्यैः परिवृतो मुनिरप्यभिनिष्पतत्।।3.12.21।। तं ददर्शाग्रतो रामो मुनीनां दीप्ततेजसाम्।
explanation: Thereafter surrounded by the disciples the sage came out. Rama saw him coming in front of the effulgent sages.

shloka_text: अब्रवीद्वचनं वीरो लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्। 3.12.22।। एष लक्ष्मण निष्क्रामत्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः। औदार्येणावगच्छामि निधानं तपसामिमम्।। 3.12.23।।
explanation: The valiant Rama said to Lakshmana, the enhancer of prosperity, O Lakshmana, sage Agastya is coming out. By virtue of his noble appearance, I know this sage to be a great treasuretrove of penances.

shloka_text: अब्रवीद्वचनं वीरो लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्। 3.12.22।। एष लक्ष्मण निष्क्रामत्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः। औदार्येणावगच्छामि निधानं तपसामिमम्।। 3.12.23।।
explanation: The valiant Rama said to Lakshmana, the enhancer of prosperity, O Lakshmana, sage Agastya is coming out. By virtue of his noble appearance, I know this sage to be a great treasuretrove of penances.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुरगस्त्यं सूर्यवर्चसम्। जग्राह परमप्रीतस्तस्य पादौ परन्तपः।।3.12.24।।
explanation: Having said so, the mightyarmed Rama, the scorcher of enemies, grasped the feet of Agastya who was shining like the Sun.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य तु धर्मात्मा तस्थौ रामः कृताञ्जलिः। सीतया सह वैदेह्या तदा रामः सलक्ष्मणः।।3.12.25।।
explanation: Then righteous Rama with Sita, the princess of Videha, and Lakshmana offered respects with folded palmsstanding.

shloka_text: प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थमर्चयित्वासनोदकैः। कुशलप्रश्नमुक्त्वा च आस्यतामिति चाब्रवीत्।। 3.12.26।।
explanation: Agastya received Rama by offering him seat and water, enquired about his wellbeing  and said: Please be seated,

shloka_text: अग्निं हुत्वा प्रदायार्घ्यमतिथीन् प्रतिपूज्य च। वानप्रस्थ्येन धर्मेण स तेषां भोजनं ददौ।। 3.12.27।।
explanation: After giving oblations to the fire, and  providing respectful offerings, the sage worshipped the guests according to the tradition of hermits and served them food.

shloka_text: प्रथमं चोपविश्याथ धर्मज्ञो मुनिपुङ्गवः। उवाच राममासीनं प्राञ्जलिं धर्मकोविदम्।।3.12.28।।
explanation: And then the great sage Agastya, knower of dharma  first took his seat and addressed Rama, an export in the knowledge of dharma, seated with folded palms.

shloka_text: अग्निं हुत्वा प्रदायार्घ्यमतिथिं प्रतिपूजयेत्। अन्यथा खलु काकुत्स्थ तपस्वी समुदाचरन्।।3.12.29।। दुःसाक्षीव परे लोके स्वानि मांसानि भक्षयेत्।
explanation: O scion of the Kakutstha dynasty, only  after offering oblations to the Firegod, a guest should be worshipped with water etc. Otherwise the host will have to eat his own flesh in the other world like a false witness.

shloka_text: राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य धर्मचारी महारथः।।3.12.30।। पूजनीयश्च मान्यश्च भवान् प्राप्तः प्रियातिथिः।
explanation: You are king of all the worlds, a follower of dharma, a great warrior worthy of worship and an esteemed self. O Rama you are such a dear guest come to me.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मूलैः पुष्पैरन्यैश्च राघवम्।। 3.12.31।। पूजयित्वा यथाकामं पुनरेव ततोऽब्रवीत्।
explanation: Having said this to Rama, (the sage) honoured him by offering fruits, roots, flowers and other things as desired. He then said to Rama once again:

shloka_text: इदं दिव्यं महच्चापं हेमरत्नविभूषितम्।।3.12.32।। वैष्णवं पुरुषव्याघ्र निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा। अमोघस्सूर्यसङ्काशो ब्रह्मदत्तश्शरोत्तमः।।3.12.33।।
explanation: O best among men  this divine bow studded with gold and gems  belongs to Visnu and designed by Visvakarma. This excellent, unfailing arrow, bright like the Sun, was given to me by Brahma.

shloka_text: इदं दिव्यं महच्चापं हेमरत्नविभूषितम्।।3.12.32।। वैष्णवं पुरुषव्याघ्र निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा। अमोघस्सूर्यसङ्काशो ब्रह्मदत्तश्शरोत्तमः।।3.12.33।।
explanation: O best among men  this divine bow studded with gold and gems  belongs to Visnu and designed by Visvakarma. This excellent, unfailing arrow, bright like the Sun, was given to me by Brahma.

shloka_text: दत्तौ मम महेन्द्रेण तूणी चाक्षयसायकौ। सम्पूर्णौ निशितैर्बाणैर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पावकैः।।3.12.34।। महारजतकोशोऽयमसिर्हेमविभूषितः।
explanation: These two quivers filled fully with sharp inexhaustible arrows, shining like flames of fire and this sword adorned with gold and this big silver sheath were given to me by Indra.

shloka_text: अनेन धनुषा राम हत्वा संख्ये महासुरान्।।3.12.35।। आजहार श्रियं दीप्तां पुरा विष्णुर्दिवौकसाम्।
explanation: In ancient times Visnu killed the demons in a battle with this bow and brought back the glittering prosperity for the gods.

shloka_text: तद्धनुस्तौ च तूणीरौ शरं खङ्गं च मानद।। 3.12.36।। जयाय प्रतिगृह्णीष्व वज्रं वज्रधरो यथा।
explanation: O bestower of honour, receive this bow, the two quivers, the sword and the arrow for your victory just like Indra accepts the thunderbolt.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः समस्तं तद्वरायुधम्। दत्वा रामाय भगवानगस्त्यः पुनरब्रवीत्।।3.12.37।।
explanation: The luminous lord Agastya, having said this, gave all the excellent weapons to Rama. And continued : इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे द्वादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twelfth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: राम प्रीतोऽस्मि भद्रं ते परितुष्टोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण। अभिवादयितुं यन्मां प्राप्तौ स्थ स्सह सीतया।।3.13.1।।
explanation: O Rama ,I am pleased. I wish you well. I am glad that both of you have come here with Sita to pay respect to me.

shloka_text: अध्वश्रमेण वां खेदो बाधते प्रचुरश्रमः। व्यक्तमुत्कण्ठते वापि मैथिली जनकात्मजा।।3.13.2।।
explanation: Both of you are tired due to the journey. It is evident that Sita, daughter of Janaka, is anxious (to rest).

shloka_text: एषा हि सुकुमारी च दुःखैश्च न विमानिता। प्राज्यदोषं वनं प्राप्ता भर्तृस्नेहप्रचोदिता।।3.13.3।।
explanation: Even though delicate, Sita never feels discouraged by difficulties. She has come to the forest full of obstacles, since she is motivated by her love for her husband.

shloka_text: यथैषा रमते राम इह सीता तथा कुरु। दुष्करं कृतवत्येषा वने त्वामनुगच्छती।।3.13.4।।
explanation: O Rama, help Sita enjoy herself in whatever manner she likes. By following you into the forest, she has accomplished the most difficult task৷৷

shloka_text: एषा हि प्रकृतिः स्त्रीणामासृष्टे रघुनन्दन। समस्थमनुरज्यान्ति विषमस्थं त्यजन्ति च।।3.13.5।।
explanation: O Rama, the delight of the Raghu dynasty from the beginning of the creation women, by nature,  keep the husband company when all goes well and give them up when hard times come.

shloka_text: शतह्रदानां लोलत्वं शस्त्राणां तीक्ष्णतां तथा। गरूडानिलयोश्शैघ्र्यमनुगच्छन्ति योषितः।।3.13.6।।
explanation: Women are fickle like lightning, sharp like weapons and fast like Garuda or the windgod.

shloka_text: इयं तु भवतो भार्या दोषैरेतैर्विवर्जिता। श्लाघ्या च व्यपदेश्या च यथा देवी ह्यरुन्धती।।3.13.7।।
explanation: Your wife is free from such blemishes. She is praiseworthy and worthy of mention as an example just like the revered Arundhati.

shloka_text: अलङ्कृतोऽयं देशश्च यत्र सौमित्रिणा सह। वैदेह्या चानया राम वत्स्यसि त्वमरिन्दम।।3.13.8।।
explanation: O Rama, subduer of enemies the place where you reside along with Lakshmana and Vaidehi will look adorned, indeed.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्समुनिना राघवस्संयताञ्जलिः। उवाच प्रश्रितं वाक्यमृषिं दीप्तमिवानलम्।।3.13.9।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Rama held his palms together and said politely to the sage shining like fire:

shloka_text: धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे मुनिपुङ्गवः। गुणैस्सभ्रातृभार्यस्य वरदः परितुष्यति।।3.13.10।।
explanation: I consider myself blessed and favoured by a great sage like you, bestower of boons as you have been pleased with me, my brother and my life.

shloka_text: किन्तु व्यादिश मे देशं सोदकं बहुकाननम्। यत्राश्रमपदं कृत्वा वसेयं निरतस्सुखम्।।3.13.11।।
explanation: Direct me to a place with water and dense forest where we can build an ashram and live happily.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्मुनिश्रेष्ठश्श्रुत्वा रामस्य तद्वचः। ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं धर्मात्मा धीरो धीरतरं वचः।।3.13.12।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Rama, Agastya, the best among the sages, coolheaded and righteous, thought a while and uttered these words coolly :

shloka_text: इतो द्वियोजने तात बहुमूलफलोदकः। देशो बहुमृगश्श्रीमान्पञ्चवट्यभिविश्रुतः।।3.13.13।।
explanation: O dear two yojanas away is a place wellknown as Panchavati, a beautiful resort with many roots, fruits, plenty of water and many animals.

shloka_text: तत्र गत्वाऽऽश्रमपदं कृत्वा सौमित्रिणा सह। रमस्व त्वं पितुर्वाक्यं तथोक्तमनुपालयन्।।3.13.14।।
explanation: Reaching there, you wikk build a hermitage with Lakshmana and enjoy your life given to the fulfilment of the pledge to the father.

shloka_text: कालोऽयं गतभूयिष्ठो यः काल स्तव राघव। समयो यो नरेन्द्रेण कृतो दशरथेन ते।।3.13.15।। तीर्णप्रतिज्ञः काकुत्स्थ सुखं राज्ये निवत्स्यसि।
explanation: O Rama, scion of the Kakutsthas  much of the period of exile king Dasaratha had assigned has passed. You will fulfil your promise and live happily in the kingdom.

shloka_text: धन्यस्ते जनको राम स राजा रघुनन्दन।।3.13.16।। यस्त्वया ज्येष्ठपुत्रेण ययातिरिव तारितः।
explanation: O Rama, joy of the Raghu family with the eldest son like you, your father is blessed and liberated like king Yayati.

shloka_text: विदितो ह्येष वृत्तान्तो मम सर्वस्तवानघ।।3.13.17।। तपसश्च प्रभावेण स्नेहाद्दशरथस्य च।
explanation: O sinless one, I have kown all these facts about you by the power of penance and love for Dasaratha.

shloka_text: हृदयस्थश्च ते छन्दो विज्ञातस्तपसा मया।।3.13.18।। इहावासं प्रतिज्ञाय मया सह तपोवने। अतश्च त्वामहं ब्रूमि गच्छ पञ्चवटीमिति।।3.13.19।।
explanation: I know your heart by virtue of my penance. I, therefore, ask you to proceed to Panchavati, after ensuring your stay here with me in this penancegrove for the time being.

shloka_text: हृदयस्थश्च ते छन्दो विज्ञातस्तपसा मया।।3.13.18।। इहावासं प्रतिज्ञाय मया सह तपोवने। अतश्च त्वामहं ब्रूमि गच्छ पञ्चवटीमिति।।3.13.19।।
explanation: I know your heart by virtue of my penance. I, therefore, ask you to proceed to Panchavati, after ensuring your stay here with me in this penancegrove for the time being.

shloka_text: स हि रम्यो वनोद्देशो मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते। स देशश्श्लाघनीयश्च नातिदूरे च राघव।।3.13.20।।
explanation: O Raghava, that forest tract is delightful and beautiful. It is not far away(from here). Maithili (Sita) will enjoy her stay there.

shloka_text: गोदावर्यास्समीपे च मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते। प्राज्यमूलफलश्चैव नानाद्विजगणायुतः।।3.13.21।। विविक्तश्च महाबाहो पुण्योरम्यस्तथैव च।
explanation: O longarmed Rama,that place has plenty of roots and fruits. It is a solitary, holy and beautiful place teeming with various kinds of birds. Sita will enjoy her stay in the vicinity of river Godavari.

shloka_text: भवानपि सदारश्च शक्तश्च परिरक्षणे। अपि चात्र वसन्राम तापसान्पालयिष्यसि।।3.13.22।।
explanation: O Rama, while staying with your wife, you will look after the ascetics living there since you are capable of giving protection.

shloka_text: एतदालक्ष्यते वीर मधूकानां महद्वनम्। उत्तरेणास्य गन्तव्यं न्यग्रोधमभिगच्छता।।3.13.23।।
explanation: O valiant Rama look at the great forest of madhuka trees. Walk north to the forest till you see a great banyan tree.

shloka_text: ततः स्थलमुपारुह्य पर्वतस्याविदूरतः। ख्यातः पञ्चवटीत्येव नित्यपुष्पितकाननः।।3.13.24।।
explanation: Then climb the elevated ground not very far from the mountain. There is the wellknown Panchavati with forests, ever in full bloom.

shloka_text: अगस्त्येनैवमुक्तस्तु रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह। सत्कृत्यामन्त्रयामास तमृषिं सत्यवादिनम्।।3.13.25।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Agastya,  Rama with Lakshmana paid respects to the sage wedded to truth and took leave of him.

shloka_text: तौ तु तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातौ कृतपादाभिवन्दनौ। तदाश्रमात्पञ्चवटीं जग्मतुस्सीतया सह।।3.13.26।।
explanation: Both of them worshipped the feet of sage Agastya, and proceeded to Panchavati with his permission.

shloka_text: गृहीतचापौ तु नराधिपात्मजौ विषक्ततूणौ समरेष्वकातरौ। यथोपदिष्टेन पथा महर्षिणा प्रजग्मतुः पञ्चवटीं समाहितौ।।3.13.27।।
explanation: Both the princes, unafraid of battles, held their bows, tied the quivers and carefully proceeded towards Panchavati along the path suggested by the sage. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे त्रयोदशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirteenth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ पञ्चवटीं गच्छन्नन्तरा रघुनन्दनः। आससाद महाकायं गृध्रं भीमपराक्रमम्।।3.14.1।।
explanation: On the way to Panchavati, Rama, the delight of the Raghu race, met a vulture with a huge body and fearful strength.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा तौ महाभागौ वटस्थं रामलक्ष्मणौ। मेनाते राक्षसं पक्षिं ब्रुवाणौ को भवानिति।।3.14.2।।
explanation: Seeing the bird on the banyan tree, venerable Rama and Lakshmana mistook him for a demon and enquired who he was.

shloka_text: स तौ मधुरया वाचा सौम्यया प्रीणयन्निव। उवाच वत्स मां विद्धि वयस्यं पितुरात्मनः।।3.14.3।।
explanation: With a sweet, pleasing, and gentle voice he said to both of them, O dear know me to be a friend of your father.

shloka_text: स तं पितृसखं बुद्ध्वा पूजयामास राघवः। स तस्य कुलमव्यग्रमथ पप्रच्छ नाम च।।3.14.4।।
explanation: Rama knew he was a friend of his father. So he enquired in a cool, composed voice his name and his lineage.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वभूतसमुद्भवम्। आचचक्षे द्विजस्तस्मै कुलमात्मानमेव च।।3.14.5।।
explanation: On hearing Rama's words, the bird started narrating the origin of all beings including his own family:

shloka_text: पूर्वकाले महाबाहो ये प्रजापतयोऽभवन्। तान्मे निगदतस्सर्वानादितश्शृणु राघव।।3.14.6।।
explanation: O mightyarmed Rama hear from me while I am telling you about the lords of creation from the very beginning.

shloka_text: कर्दमः प्रथमस्तेषां विक्रीतस्तदनन्तरः। शेषश्च संश्रयश्चैव बहुपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्।।3.14.7।। स्थाणुर्मरीचिरत्रिश्च क्रतुश्चैव महाबलः। पुलस्त्यश्चाङ्गिराश्चैव प्रचेताः पूलहस्तथा।।3.14.8।। दक्षो विवस्वानपरोऽरिष्टनेमिश्च राघव। काश्यपश्च महातेजास्तेषामासीच्च पश्चिमः।।3.14.9।।
explanation: O Rama among the lords of all beings the first was Kardama, the next was Vikritha, followed by Sesha, Samsrya Bahuputra, Sthanu, Mareechi, Atri and mighty Kratu, Pulastya, Angirasa, Pracheta, similarly Pulaha and Daksha.Following them were Vivasvan, Arishtanemi and the very glorious Kasyapa who was the last ruler.

shloka_text: कर्दमः प्रथमस्तेषां विक्रीतस्तदनन्तरः। शेषश्च संश्रयश्चैव बहुपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्।।3.14.7।। स्थाणुर्मरीचिरत्रिश्च क्रतुश्चैव महाबलः। पुलस्त्यश्चाङ्गिराश्चैव प्रचेताः पूलहस्तथा।।3.14.8।। दक्षो विवस्वानपरोऽरिष्टनेमिश्च राघव। काश्यपश्च महातेजास्तेषामासीच्च पश्चिमः।।3.14.9।।
explanation: O Rama among the lords of all beings the first was Kardama, the next was Vikritha, followed by Sesha, Samsrya Bahuputra, Sthanu, Mareechi, Atri and mighty Kratu, Pulastya, Angirasa, Pracheta, similarly Pulaha and Daksha.Following them were Vivasvan, Arishtanemi and the very glorious Kasyapa who was the last ruler.

shloka_text: कर्दमः प्रथमस्तेषां विक्रीतस्तदनन्तरः। शेषश्च संश्रयश्चैव बहुपुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्।।3.14.7।। स्थाणुर्मरीचिरत्रिश्च क्रतुश्चैव महाबलः। पुलस्त्यश्चाङ्गिराश्चैव प्रचेताः पूलहस्तथा।।3.14.8।। दक्षो विवस्वानपरोऽरिष्टनेमिश्च राघव। काश्यपश्च महातेजास्तेषामासीच्च पश्चिमः।।3.14.9।।
explanation: O Rama among the lords of all beings the first was Kardama, the next was Vikritha, followed by Sesha, Samsrya Bahuputra, Sthanu, Mareechi, Atri and mighty Kratu, Pulastya, Angirasa, Pracheta, similarly Pulaha and Daksha.Following them were Vivasvan, Arishtanemi and the very glorious Kasyapa who was the last ruler.

shloka_text: प्रजापतेस्तु दक्षस्य बभूवुरिति विश्रुतम्। षष्टिर्दुहितरो राम यशस्विन्यो महायशः।।3.14.10।।
explanation: O glorious Rama it is wellknown that Daksha, the creator had sixty daughters of great fame.

shloka_text: काश्यपः प्रतिजग्राह तासामष्टौ सुमध्यमाः। अदितिं च दितिं चैव दनुमप्यथ कालिकाम्।।3.14.11।। ताम्रां क्रोधवशां चैव मनुं चाप्यनलामपि।
explanation: Out of them(daughters of Daksha) Kasyapa married eight women of beautiful waist called Aditi, Diti, Danu also Kalika,Tamra, Krodhavasa, Anala and Manu.

shloka_text: तास्तु कन्यास्ततः प्रीतः काश्यपः पुनरब्रवीत्।।3.14.12।। पुत्रां स्स्रैलोक्यभर्तृ़न्वै जनयिष्यथ मत्समान्।
explanation: Kasyapa, pleased with them said to his young wives, Beget sons of my stature who can rule over the three worlds.

shloka_text: अदितिस्तन्मना राम दितिश्च मनुजर्षभ।।3.14.13।। कालिका च महाबाहो शेषास्त्वमनसोऽभवन्।
explanation: O best of men, O longarmed Rama while Aditi, Diti and Kalika seriously considered his advice, the rest of the wives did not.

shloka_text: अदित्यां जज्ञिरे देवात्रयस्त्रिंशदरिंदम।।3.14.14।। आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा ह्यश्विनौ च परन्तप।
explanation: O Rama, subduer and scorcher of enemies to Aditi were born twelve Adityas, eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, and two Asvins, thirtythree deities in all.

shloka_text: दितिस्त्वजनयत्पुत्रान् दैत्यांस्तात यशस्विनः।।3.14.15।। तेषामियं वसुमती पुराऽसीत्सवनार्णवा।
explanation: O dear Rama, Diti bore glorious sons called Daityas and this earth with all the forests and seas belonged to them.

shloka_text: दनुस्त्वजनयत्पुत्रमश्वग्रीवमरिन्दम।।3.14.16।। नरकं कालकंचैव कालिकापि व्यजायत।
explanation: O subduer of enemies, to Danu was born Hayagriva and to Kalika, Naraka and Kalaka.

shloka_text: क्रौञ्चीं भासीं तथा श्येनीं धृतराष्ट्रीं तथा शुकीम्।।3.14.17।। ताम्रापि सुषुवे कन्याः पञ्चैता लोकविश्रुताः।
explanation: To Tamra were born, Krounchi, Bhasi, Syeni, Dhrutharashtri and Suki. Altogether they were five beautiful young maids famous in the world.

shloka_text: उलूकाञ्जनयत्क्रौञ्ची भासी भासान्व्यजायत।।3.14.18।। श्येनी श्येनांश्च गृध्रांश्च व्यजायत सुतेजसः। धृतराष्ट्रीतु हंसांश्च कलहंसांश्च सर्वशः।।3.14.19।।
explanation: Krounchi gave birth to owls, Bhasi to Bhasa birds, Synei to bright hawks and vultures, Dhrutharashtri to swans and chakravakas with sweet notes.

shloka_text: उलूकाञ्जनयत्क्रौञ्ची भासी भासान्व्यजायत।।3.14.18।। श्येनी श्येनांश्च गृध्रांश्च व्यजायत सुतेजसः। धृतराष्ट्रीतु हंसांश्च कलहंसांश्च सर्वशः।।3.14.19।।
explanation: Krounchi gave birth to owls, Bhasi to Bhasa birds, Synei to bright hawks and vultures, Dhrutharashtri to swans and chakravakas with sweet notes.

shloka_text: चक्रवाकांश्च भद्रं ते विजज्ञे सापि भामिनी। शुकी नतां विजज्ञे तु नताया विनता सुता।।3.14.20।।
explanation: Dhrutharashtri, a female bird of great lustre gave birth to chakravakas too. Suki gave birth to Nata and from Nata, Vinata was born. Be blessed, O Rama

shloka_text: दश क्रोधवशा राम विजज्ञे ह्यात्मसम्भवाः। मृगीं च मृगमन्दां च हरीं भद्रमदामपि।।3.14.21।। मातङ्गीमपि शार्दूलीं श्वेतां च सुरभिं तथा। सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नां सुरसां कद्रुकामपि।।3.14.22।।
explanation: O Ramato Krodhavasa were born Mrugi, Mrugamanda, Hari, Bhadramada, Mathangi, Sardooli, Sweta, Surabhi and Surasa, Kadruva and endowed with all virtues.

shloka_text: दश क्रोधवशा राम विजज्ञे ह्यात्मसम्भवाः। मृगीं च मृगमन्दां च हरीं भद्रमदामपि।।3.14.21।। मातङ्गीमपि शार्दूलीं श्वेतां च सुरभिं तथा। सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नां सुरसां कद्रुकामपि।।3.14.22।।
explanation: O Ramato Krodhavasa were born Mrugi, Mrugamanda, Hari, Bhadramada, Mathangi, Sardooli, Sweta, Surabhi and Surasa, Kadruva and endowed with all virtues.

shloka_text: अपत्यं तु मृगास्सर्वे मृग्या नरवरोत्तम। ऋक्षाश्च मृगमन्दायास्सृमराश्चमरा स्तथा।।3.14.23।।
explanation: O best of men, all kinds of animals were born of Mrugi.To Mrugamanda were born bears and chamara (a different kind of deer).

shloka_text: हर्याश्च हरयोऽपत्यं वानराश्च तरस्स्विनः। ततस्त्विरावतीं नाम जज्ञे भद्रमदा सुताम्।।3.14.24।।
explanation: To Hari were born lions, and swiftmoving monkeys and to Bhadramada, a daughter by name Iravati.

shloka_text: तस्यास्त्वैरावतः पुत्रो लोकनाथो महागजः। मातङ्ग्या स्त्वथ मातङ्गा अपत्यं मनुजर्षभ।।3.14.25।।
explanation: O bull among men Matangi gave birth to elephants.The mighty elephant Airavata who became the lord of the world was born to Iravati.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलांश्च शार्दूली व्याघ्रांश्चाजनयत्सुतान्। दिशागजांश्च काकुत्स्थ श्वेताप्यजनयत्सुतान्।।3.14.26।।
explanation: O Rama, Sarduli gave birth to tigers and playful, roundbodied monkeys called Golangula and Sweta delivered elephants as sons for guarding the eight quarters.

shloka_text: ततो दुहितरौ राम सुरभिर्द्वेव्यजायत। रोहिणीं नाम भद्रं ते गन्धर्वीं च यशस्स्विनीम्।।3.14.27।।
explanation: Surabhi gave birth to Rohini and Gandharvi,the two famous daughters. May you be happy, Rama

shloka_text: रोहिण्यजनयद् गावो गन्धर्वी वाजिनः सुतान्। सुरसाऽजनयन्नागान्राम कद्रूस्तु पन्नगान्।।3.14.28।।
explanation: O Rama Rohini procreated cows, and Gandharvi, horses as offsprings. Surasa delivered cobras and Kadru, ordinary serpents.

shloka_text: मनुर्मनुष्यान् जनयद्राम पुत्रान् यशस्विनः। ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् वैश्यान् शूद्रांश्च मनुजर्षभ।।3.14.29।।
explanation: O Rama, bull among men Manu procreated brahmins, kshatriyas, vaisyas and sudras all famed human beings.

shloka_text: सर्वान् पुण्यफलान्वृक्षाननलापि व्यजायत। विनता च शुकीपौत्री कद्रूश्च सुरसास्वसा।।3.14.30।।
explanation: Anala (wife of Kasyapa) procreated trees with sacred fruits. Vinata was the granddaughter of Suki, and Kahdruva and Surasa were her sisters.

shloka_text: कद्रूर्नागं सहस्रास्यं विजज्ञे धरणीधरम्। द्वौ पुत्रौ विनतायास्तु गरुडोऽरुण एव च।।3.14.31।।
explanation: Kadhru produced a thousandhooded serpent(Adisesha) who held the whole earth on his head and Vinata, two sons, Garuda and Aruna.

shloka_text: तस्माज्जातोऽहमरुणात्सम्पातिस्तु ममाग्रजः। जटायुरिति मां विद्धि श्येनीपुत्रमरिन्दम।।3.14.32।।
explanation: I am born to Aruna and my elder brother is Sampati. O subduer of enemies, know me as Jatayu, son of Syeni.

shloka_text: सोऽहं वाससहायस्ते भविष्यामि यदीच्छसि। इदं दुर्गं हि कान्तारं मृगराक्षस सेवितम्।।3.14.33।। सीतां च तात रक्षिष्ये त्वयि याते सलक्ष्मणे।
explanation: If you so desire I will be helpful to you in guarding your hut. O dear, it is a difficult forest full of wild animals and demons. When you and Lakshmana are away I will protect Sita.

shloka_text: जटायुषं तं प्रतिपूज्य राघवो मुदा परिष्वज्य च सन्नतोऽभवत्। पितुर्हि शुश्राव सखित्वमात्मवान् जटायुषा सङ्कथितं पुनः पुनः।।3.14.34।।
explanation: Rama worshipped  Jatayu and bending down, embraced him. He heard from him again and again several events relating to Jatayu's  friendship with his father.

shloka_text: स तत्र सीतां परिदाय मैथिलीं सहैव तेनातिबलेन पक्षिणा। जगाम तां पञ्चवटीं सलक्ष्मणो रिपून्दिधक्षञ्छलभानि वानलः।।3.14.35।।
explanation: Entresting the protection of Sita, the princess of Mithila, to that strong vulture,  Jatayu, and accompanied by Lakshmana Rama went to Panchavati wishing to destroy the enemies like fire burning the moths. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामयणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे चतुर्दशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fourteenth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः पञ्चवटीं गत्वा नानाव्यालमृगायुताम्। उवाच भ्रातरं रामस्सौमित्रिं दीप्ततेजसम्।।3.15.1।।
explanation: On reaching Panchavati, which was full of various vicious animals, Rama said to Lakshmana, his brother who was glowing like  fire:

shloka_text: आगताः स्म यथोद्दिष्टममुं देशं महर्षिणा। अयं पञ्चवटीदेशस्सौम्य पुष्पितपादपः।।3.15.2।।
explanation: O handsome one, following the directions of the great sage, we have arrived at Panchavati, a place full of blossoming trees.

shloka_text: सर्वतश्चार्यतां दृष्टिः कानने निपुणोह्यसि। आश्रमः कतरस्मिन्नो देशे भवति सम्मतः।।3.15.3।।
explanation: O Lakshmana cast your eyes all around the forest for a suitable place (for building a hermitage).  Indeed, you are good at judging things.

shloka_text: रमते यत्र वैदेही त्वमहं चैव लक्ष्मण। तादृशो दृश्यतां देशस्सन्निकृष्टजलाशयः।।3.15.4।। वनरामण्यकं यत्र स्थलरामण्यकं तथा। सन्निकृष्टं च यत्र स्यात्समित्पुष्पकुशोदकम्।।3.15.5।।
