shloka_text: न चाहं हरिराजस्य प्रभवाम्यङ्गदस्य वा। पितृव्यस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्सर्वकार्येष्वनन्तरः4.21.14।।
explanation: I am not the master of the king of monkeys, nor of Angada. His paternal uncle, Sugriva, is the immediate authority in all matters.

shloka_text: न ह्येषाबुद्धिरास्थेया हनूमन्नङ्गदं प्रति। पिता हि बन्धुः पुत्रस्य न माता हरिसत्तम4.21.15।।
explanation: 'O Hanuman the best of monkeys, you need not think about (the future of) Angada. A father plans for a son and not (even) the mother.

shloka_text: न हि मम हरिराजसंश्रयात् क्षमतरमस्ति परत्र चेह वा। अभिमुखहतवीरसेवितं शयनमिदं मम सेवितुं क्षमम्4.21.16।।
explanation: There is nothing more befitting for me than joining the king of monkeys either here or in the next world. It is proper for me to resort to this resting place (pyre) used by this slain hero in front of me. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकविंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyfirst sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: वीक्षमाणस्तु मन्दासुस्सर्वतो मन्दमुच्छ्वसन्। आदावेव तु सुग्रीवं ददर्शत्वात्मजाग्रतः4.22.1।।
explanation: Vali, gazing all around, breathing slowly and sighing feably beheld Sugriva at first instance, Sugriva who was standing in front of his own son.

shloka_text: तं प्राप्तविजयं वाली सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरः। आभाष्य व्यक्तया वाचा सस्नेहमिदमब्रवीत्4.22.2।।
explanation: Vali, the lord of monkeys, lovingly said to Sugriva, who had won a victory:

shloka_text: सुग्रीव दोषेण न मां गन्तुमर्हसि किल्बिषात्। कृष्यमाणं भविष्येण बुद्धिमोहेन मां बलात्4.22.3।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva you ought not to accuse me of exiling you, and wresting your wife. My mind was deluded by the force of fate that controls one's future.

shloka_text: युगपद्विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्द भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं तात नान्यथा4.22.4।।
explanation: 'O dear I believe that both of us are not destined to enjoy the love and happiness that come together to brothers.

shloka_text: प्रतिपद्य त्वमद्यैव राज्यमेषां वनौकसाम्। मामप्यद्यैव गच्छन्तं विद्धि वैवस्वतक्षयम्4.22.5।।
explanation: You, having obtained the kingdom of these forest-dwellers today itself, know that I too am departing to the abode of Yama today itself.

shloka_text: जीवितं च हि राज्यं च श्रियं च विपुलामिमाम्। प्रजहाम्येष वै तूर्णं महच्चागर्हितं यशः4.22.6।।
explanation: 'I am leaving this world soon, along with this vast kingdom, prosperity and untarnished fame.

shloka_text: अस्यां त्वहमवस्थायां वीर वक्ष्यामि यद्वचः। यद्यप्यसुकरं राजन्कर्तुमेव तदर्हसि4.22.7
explanation: 'O warrior king you should do whatever I request you at this hour even though it may not be easy.

shloka_text: सुखार्हं सुखसंवृद्धं बालमेनमबालिशम्। बाष्पपूर्णमुखं पश्य भूमौ पतितमङ्गदम्4.22.8।।
explanation: 'Look at this young Angada fallen on the ground, face flooded with tears. Raised with comfort, he deserves to be kept happy.

shloka_text: मम प्राणैः प्रियतरं पुत्रं पुत्रमिवौरसम्। मया हीनमहीनार्थं पर्वतः परिपालय4.22.9।।
explanation: 'He is dearer to me than my life. Take care of him like your own son. He is separated from me. Take care of him in all respects, so that he is not deprived of anything.

shloka_text: त्वमेवास्य हि दाता च परित्राता च सर्वशः। भयेष्वभयदश्चैव यथाऽहं प्लवगेश्वर।।4.22.10।।
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys from now on, you alone will be his father, provider of everything, saviour and protector in danger.

shloka_text: एष तारात्मज श्रीमांस्त्वया तुल्यपराक्रमः। रक्षसां च वधे तेषामग्रतस्ते भविष्यति4.22.11।।
explanation: 'This prosperous son of Tara, your equal in valour, will remain with you in the forefront to crush demons.

shloka_text: अनुरूपाणि कर्माणि विक्रम्य बलवान्रणे। करिष्यत्येष तारेयस्तरस्वी तरुणोऽङ्गदः4.22.12।।
explanation: 'This mighty hero Angada, son of Tara, is young and dynamic. He will strike (the enemy) in a fitting manner in war.

shloka_text: सुषेणदुहिता चेयमर्थसूक्ष्मविमनिश्चये। औत्पातिके च विविधे सर्वतः परिनिष्ठिता4.22.13।।
explanation: 'Tara, daughter of Sushena, is wise and efficient in discerning subtle matters and in foreseeing unexpected events.

shloka_text: यदेषा साध्विति ब्रूयात्कार्यं तन्मुक्तसंशयम्। न हि तारामतं किञ्चिदन्यथा परिवर्तते4.22.14।।
explanation: 'Tara's opinion is never wrong. It does not change. Whatever she speaks is right and should be carried out without any doubt.

shloka_text: राघवस्य च ते कार्यं कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया। स्यादधर्मो ह्यकरणे त्वां च हिंस्याद्विमानितः4.22.15।।
explanation: 'You ought to carry out Rama's work without hesitation. If you do not, it will be unrighteous and harmful.

shloka_text: इमां च मालामाधत्स्व दिव्यां सुग्रीव काञ्चनीम्। उदारा श्रीस्थिता ह्यास्यां सम्प्रजह्यान्मृते मयि4.22.16।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva put on this divine golden necklace. It has great brilliance. Its present lustre may be gone when I am dead.'

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तस्सुग्रीवो वालिना भ्रातृसौहृदात्। हर्षं त्यक्त्वा पुनर्दीनो ग्रहग्रस्त इवोडुराट्4.22.17।।
explanation: Thus spoken to by Vali with brotherly affection, Sugriva gave up joy (of victory) and appeared dull like the Moon eclipsed by planet Rahu.

shloka_text: तद्वालिवचनाच्छान्तः कुर्वन्युक्तमतन्द्रितः। जग्राह सोऽभ्यनुज्ञातो मालां तां चैव काञ्चनीम्4.22.18।।
explanation: On hearing Vali's words, Sugriva became composed with no illfeeling. Considering it to be proper, he received with his permission the golden necklace.

shloka_text: तां मालां काञ्चनीम् दत्त्वा दृष्ट्वाचैवात्मजं स्थितम्। संसिद्धः प्रेत्यभावाय स्नेहादङ्गदमब्रवीत्4.22.19।।
explanation: Having given the golden necklace to Sugriva,Vali, feeling ready to depart, looked at his son Angada who stood by and spoke affectionately:

shloka_text: देशकालौ भजस्वाद्य क्षममाणः प्रियाप्रिये। सुखदुःख सह: काले सुग्रीववशगो भव4.22.20।।
explanation: 'Enduring pleasure or pain equally  with due regard to time and place favourable to you or otherwise, you should submit to the will of Sugriva.

shloka_text: यथा हि त्वं महाबाहो लालितस्सततं मया। न तथा वर्तमानं त्वां सुग्रीवो बहुमंस्यते।।4.22.21।।
explanation: 'O longarmed one you have always been affectionately brought up by me. Sugriva may not rear you that way.

shloka_text: माऽस्यामित्रैर्गतं गच्छेर्मा शत्रुभिररिन्दम। भर्तुरर्थपरो दान्तः सुग्रीववशगो भव4.22.22।।
explanation: 'O conqueror of foes do not align with his enemies or with the friends of his enemies. Remain selfrestrained and loyal to Sugriva. Be subordinate to his will.

shloka_text: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महान्दोष स्तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव4.22.23।।
explanation: 'You are not to be excessively friendly or otherise as both are serious mistakes. Therefore, be insightful.'

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वाऽथ विवृत्ताक्षः शरसम्पीडितो भृशम्। विवृतैर्दशनै र्भीमैर्बभूवोत्क्रान्तजीवितः4.22.24।।
explanation: Having spoken this, tormented by the arrow, eyes popping out and his dreadful teeth ejected, Vali remained drained of life.

shloka_text: ततो विचुक्रुशुस्तत्र वानरा हरियूथपाः। परिदेवयमानास्ते सर्वे प्लवगपुङ्गवा:4.22.25।।
explanation: Then the best of the monkeys and their troop leaders bewailed the death of Vali, crying bitterly.

shloka_text: किष्किन्धा ह्यद्य शून्याऽसीत्स्वर्गते वानराधिपे। उद्यानानि च शून्यानि पर्वताः काननानि च4.22.26।। हते प्लवगशार्दूले निष्प्रभा वानराः कृताः।
explanation: Lord of monkeys having gone to heaven, Kishkinda looked desolate including the pleasure gardens, the mountains and forests. The monkeys also became dull.

shloka_text: यस्य वेगेन महता काननानि वनानि च। पुष्पौघेणानुबध्यन्ते करिष्यति तदद्य कः4.22.27।।
explanation: (The vanaras wailed aloud saying) 'The forests and gardens looked connected together with the flowers that swayed by his speed .Who can do that now?

shloka_text: येन दत्तं महद्युद्धं गन्धर्वस्य महात्मनः4.22.28।। गोलभस्य महाबाहोर्दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च। नैव रात्रौ न दिवसे तद्युद्धमुपशाम्यति4.22.29।।
explanation: 'Great soul, Vali endowed with stout shoulders joined a duel with a gandharva called Golabha for fifteen years nonstop night and day.

shloka_text: येन दत्तं महद्युद्धं गन्धर्वस्य महात्मनः4.22.28।। गोलभस्य महाबाहोर्दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च। नैव रात्रौ न दिवसे तद्युद्धमुपशाम्यति4.22.29।।
explanation: 'Great soul, Vali endowed with stout shoulders joined a duel with a gandharva called Golabha for fifteen years nonstop night and day.

shloka_text: ततस्तु षोडशे वर्षे गोलभो विनिपातितः। हत्वा तं दुर्विनीतं तु वाली दंष्ट्राकरालवान्4.22.30।। सर्वाऽभयङ्करोऽस्माकं कथमेष निपातितः।
explanation: 'In the sixteenth year Golabha, the uncontrollable enemy was killed by Vali with his dreadful fangs and rendered protection to everybody. How did he get killed?'

shloka_text: हते तु वीरे प्लवगाधिपे तदा प्लवङ्गमास्तत्र न शर्म लेभिरे। वनेचराः सिंहयुते महावने यथा हि गावो निहते गवां पतौ4.22.31।।
explanation: Just as the cattle get frightened when the leader of the herd gets killed in a huge forest full of lions, the young monkey became puzzled when the chief of monkeys got killed.

shloka_text: ततस्समुपजिघ्रन्ती कपिराजस्य तन्मुखम्। पतिं लोकाच्च्युतं तारा मृतं वचनमब्रवीत्4.23.1।।
explanation: Tara kissed (smelt) the forehead of the king of monkeys who had departed and said:

shloka_text: शेषे त्वं विषमे दुःखमकृत्वा वचनं मम। उपलोपचिते वीर सुदुःखे वसुधातले4.23.2।।
explanation: 'O hero, not caring for my words (of caution), you are now lying with great pain on hard stones on the ground.

shloka_text: मत्तः प्रियतरा नूनं वानरेन्द्र मही तव। शेषे हि तां परिष्वज्य मां च न प्रतिभाषसे4.23.3।।
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys you lie in the end, embracing the earth and not replying to me. Surely you deem this earth dearer than me.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्य वशं प्राप्तो विधिरेषभवत्यहो। सुग्रीव एव विक्रान्तो वीर साहसिकप्रिय4.23.4।।
explanation: 'O lover of brave deeds, fate has brought you under the sway of Sugriva, although he had lost to you.

shloka_text: ऋक्षवानरमुख्यास्त्वां बलिनः पर्युपासते। एषां विलपितं कृच्छ्रमङ्गदस्य च शोचतः4.23.5।। मम चेमा गिरः श्रुत्वा किं त्वं न प्रतिबुध्यसे।
explanation: 'Oh powerful Vali leaders of the bears and monkeys, the entire lot are standing near you, wailing. Angada has been  crying in grief. How is it that you are not rising up even after hearing their wailing voices and  my call? .

shloka_text: इदं तच्छूरशयनं यत्र शेषे हतो युधि। शायिता निहता यत्र त्वयैव रिपवः पुरा4.23.6।।
explanation: 'Earlier you have killed enemies in combats and made them lie down where now you lie.

shloka_text: विशुद्धसत्त्वाभिजन प्रिययुद्ध मम प्रिय। मामनाथां विहायैकां गतस्त्वमसि मानद4.23.7।।
explanation: 'O venerable hero, born in a pure and noble family, you are a lover of battles. Now you have left me an orphan.

shloka_text: शूराय न प्रदातव्या कन्या खलु विपश्चिता। शूरभार्यां हतां पश्य सद्यो मां विधवां कृताम्4.23.8।।
explanation: 'It is said by wise men that a girl should not be given in marriage to a warrior. See me,  the wife of a warrior, now rendered a widow.

shloka_text: अवभग्नश्च मे मानो भग्ना मे शाश्वती गतिः4.23.9।। अगाधे च निमग्नाऽस्मि विपुले शोकसागरे।
explanation: 'My pride is crushed. My husband, the ultimate resort for me is shattered.I am plunged in a vast, bottomless ocean of grief.

shloka_text: अश्मसारमयं नूनमिदं मे हृदयं दृढम्4.23.10।। भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा यन्नाद्य शतधा कृतम्।
explanation: 'My heart is surely made of hard stone yet it has not split into a hundred pieces even on seeing my husband slain৷৷

shloka_text: सुहृच्चैव हि भर्ता च प्रकृत्या मम च प्रियः। आहवे च पराक्रान्तश्शूरः पञ्चत्वमागतः4.23.11।।
explanation: 'He was my husband, my friend and naturally my loving king. He was powerful in battle.Alas the hero has died.

shloka_text: पतिहीना तु या नारी कामं भवतु पुत्रिणी। धनधान्यैस्सुपूर्णाऽपि विधवेत्युच्यते बुधैः4.23.12।।
explanation: 'Even if a woman without husband, is blessed with sons and abundant wealth and grain, still learned people call her a widow.

shloka_text: स्वगात्रप्रभवे वीर शेषे रुधिरमण्डले। क्रिमिरागपरिस्तोमे त्वमात्मशयने यथा4.23.13।।
explanation: 'O hero how is it that you are lying in a crimson bed of the pool of blood flowing from your body?

shloka_text: रेणुशोणितसंवीतं गात्रं तव समन्ततः। परिरब्धुं न शक्नोमि भुजाभ्यां प्लवगर्षभ 4.23.14।।
explanation: 'O bull among monkeys how can I embrace you with my arms as your body is covered with dust particles and blood?.

shloka_text: कृतकृत्योऽद्य सुग्रीवो वैरेऽस्मिन्नतिदारुणे। यस्य रामविमुक्तेन हृतमेकेषुणा भयम्4.23.15।।
explanation: 'Sugriva has achieved his goal in his dreadful enmity (with you). His fear is dispelled by a single arrow released by Rama.

shloka_text: शरेण हृदि लग्नेन गात्रसंस्पर्शने तव। वार्यामि त्वां निरीक्षन्ती त्वयि पञ्चत्वमागते4.23.16।।
explanation: 'The arrow which has pierced your body prevents me from embracing you. I am only looking at you lying (not removing the arrow lest you die).'

shloka_text: उद्ववर्ह शरं नीलस्तस्य गात्रगतं तदा। गिरिगह्वरसंलीनं दीप्तमाशीविषं यथा4.23.17।।
explanation: Then Nila took out the arrow from Vali's heart with due effort as one would pull out a glowing serpent hidden in the mountain cave.

shloka_text: तस्य निष्कृष्यमाणस्य बाणस्य च बभौ द्युतिः। अस्तमस्तकसंरुद्धो रश्मिर्दिनकरादिव4.23.18।।
explanation: As the arrrow(drenched in blood) was being pulled out, its glow looked like the Sun's rays obstructed by the peak of the western mountain.

shloka_text: पेतुः क्षतजधारास्तु व्रणेभ्यस्तस्य सर्वशः। ताम्रगैरिकसम्पृक्ता धारा इव धराधरात्4.23.19।।
explanation: The streams of blood that flowed all over from the wounds of his body appeared like streams of water mixed with red and copper colour.

shloka_text: अवकीर्णं विमार्जन्ती भर्तारं रणरेणुना। अस्रैर्नयनजैश्शूरं सिषेचास्त्रसमाहतम्4.23.20।।
explanation: She (Tara) wiped the body wounded with the weapon and covered with wardust,  sprinkling her tear drops from her eyes.

shloka_text: रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गं दृष्ट्वा विनिहतं पतिम्। उवाच तारा पिङ्गाक्षं पुत्रमङ्गदमङ्गना4.23.21।।
explanation: Turning to the body of her husband fully drenched in blood, thus spoke Tara to her tawnyeyed  son Angada:

shloka_text: अवस्थां पश्चिमां पश्य पितुः पुत्र सुदारुणाम्। सम्प्रसक्तस्य वैरस्य गतोऽन्तः पापकर्मणा4.23.22।।
explanation: 'O son you see the most terrific end of your father on whom enmity forced sinful deeds.

shloka_text: बालसूर्योदयतनुं प्रयान्तं यमसदनम्। अभिवादय राजानं पितरं पुत्र मानदम्4.23.23।।
explanation: 'O son offer salutations to your venerable father, the king, departing for the abode of Yama (lord of death) looking (red with blood) like the rising Sun.'

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्समुत्थाय जग्राह चरणौ पितुः। भुजाभ्यां पीनवृत्ताभ्यामङ्गदोऽहमिति ब्रुवन्4.23.24।।
explanation: Thus advised by Tara, Angada got up, clasped his father's feet with his stout arms, and saluted, saying, 'I am Angada.'

shloka_text: अभिवादयमानं त्वामङ्गदं त्वं यथा पुरा। दीर्घायुर्भव पुत्रेति किमर्थं नाभिभाषसे4.23.25।।
explanation: 'Why do you not, with the words 'May you live long'', bless, as before, your son Angada who is greeting you? (said Tara).

shloka_text: अहं पुत्रसहाया त्वामुपासे गतचेतसम्। सिंहेन निहतं सद्यो गौस्सवत्सेव गोवृषम्4.23.26।।
explanation: 'Just like a cow followed by its calf would attend upon a mighty bull struck by a lion I will wait with my son upon you who have lost consciousness (died).

shloka_text: इष्ट्वा सङ्ग्रामयज्ञेन रामप्रहरणाम्भसि। अस्मिन्नवभृथे स्नातः कथं पत्न्या मया विना4.23.27।।
explanation: 'You have performed a warsacrifice. You have bathed in the waters of Rama's weapon signifying the end of the sacrifice. How did you take this customary bath without me, your wife?

shloka_text: या दत्ता देवराजेन तव तुष्टेन संयुगे। शातकुम्भमयीं मालां तां ते पश्यामि नेह किम्4.23.28।।
explanation: 'Why do I not see on your chest the golden necklace gifted by the king of the gods (Indra), pleased with you in the battle?

shloka_text: राज्यश्रीर्न जहाति त्वां गतासुमपि मानद। सूर्यस्यावर्तमानस्य शैलराजमिव प्रभा4.23.29।।
explanation: 'O venerable one, even though life has departed from you, kingly glory does not leave you any more than the light of the setting son leaves the king of mountains. (western mountain)

shloka_text: न मे वचः पथ्यमिदं त्वया कृतं न चास्मि शक्ता हि निवारणे तव। हता सपुत्राऽस्मि हतेन संयुगे सह त्वया श्रीर्विजहाति मामिह4.23.30।।
explanation: 'You have not followed my advice. I did not have the capacity to prevent you from going to war. The result is, you are killed and I am ruined along with my son. The goddess of fortune also is deserting me as well as your son.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रयोविंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentythird sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तां चाश्रुवेगेन दुरासदेन त्वभिप्लुतां शोकमहार्णवेन। पश्यंस्तदा वाल्यनुजस्तरस्वी भ्रातुर्वधेनाप्रतिमेन तेपे4.24.1।।
explanation: Sugriva, the unassailable younger brother of Vali, perceiving Tara overwhelmed in the ocean of grief felt agonized for the killing of his brother of incomparable power.

shloka_text: स बाष्पपूर्णेन मुखेन वीक्ष्य क्षणेन निर्विण्णमना मनस्वी। जगाम रामस्य शनैस्समीपं भृत्यैर्वृतसम्परिदूयमानः4.24.2।।
explanation: Face drenched with tears, highly sensitive Sugriva glanced at Tara for a moment. Pained and depressed at heart, and surrounded by attendants, he slowly approached Rama.

shloka_text: स तं समासाद्य गृहीतचाप मुदात्तमाशीविषतुल्यबाणम्। यशस्विनं लक्षणलक्षिताङ्ग मवस्थितं राघव मित्युवाच4.24.3।।
explanation: Duly approaching the illustrious Rama, endowed with auspicious signs, who stood with his bow and serpentlike arrows, Sugriva thus submitted:

shloka_text: यथा प्रतिज्ञातमिदं नरेन्द्र कृतं त्वया दृष्टफलं च कर्म। ममाद्य भोगेषु नरेन्द्रपुत्र मनो निवृत्तं सहजीवितेन4.24.4।।
explanation: 'Your majesty you have struck down Vali as promised and the consequences of your action are seen now. O prince, however, my mind is not interested in the enjoyment of pleasures. I have no interest in life.

shloka_text: अस्यां महिष्यां तु भृशं रुदन्त्या पुरे च विक्रोशति दुःखतप्ते। हतेऽग्रजे संशयितेऽङ्गदे च न राम राज्ये रमते मनो मे4.24.5।।
explanation: 'O Rama when the queen (Tara) is weeping, plunged in deep sorrow, the entire city is lamenting in agony, my elder brother is dead and the survival of Angada is uncertain, my mind no longer longs for the enjoyment of the kingdom.

shloka_text: क्रोधादमर्षादतिविप्रधर्षा द्भ्रातुर्वधो मेऽनुमतः पुरस्तात्। हते त्विदानीं हरियूथपेऽस्मिन् सुतीव्रमिक्ष्वाकुकुमार तप्स्ये।।4.24.6।।
explanation: 'O prince of the Ikshvaku family, the anger due to my exilement and my intolerance of his harsh words, had made the killing of my brother agreeable to me earlier. Now that the leader of the monkey clan is killed I am  intensely hurt.

shloka_text: श्रेयोऽद्य मन्ये मम शैलमुख्ये तस्मिन्निवासश्चिरमृश्यमूके। यथा तथा वर्तयतस्स्ववृत्त्या नेमं निहत्य त्रिदिवस्य लाभः4.24.7।।
explanation: 'I now feel dwelling long on the great mountain Rishyamuka  as usual and somehow  eking out a livelihood is preferable to attaining heaven as a sequel to the death of my brother.

shloka_text: न त्वां जिघांसामि चरेति यन्मा मयं महात्मा मतिमानुवाच। तस्यैव तद्राम वचोऽनुरूप मिदं पुनः कर्म च मेऽनुरूपम्4.24.8।।
explanation: 'O Rama when the wise, highsouled Vali said to me, 'I do not like to kill you in this place be gone from here', his words reflected his nobility. This action of mine (killing of Vali) is, on the other hand, in consonance with my nature.

shloka_text: भ्राता कथं नाम महागुणस्य भ्रातुर्वधं राघव रोचयेत। राज्यस्य दुःखस्य च वीर सारं विचिन्तयन्कामपुरस्कृतऽस्सन्4.24.9।।
explanation: 'O Rama prompted by passion, without thinking of the difference between obtaining the kingdom to satisfy one's desire and the consequent grief, which brother would  be willing to kill his virtuous elder brother?

shloka_text: वधो हि मे मतो नासीत्स्वमाहात्म्याव्यतिक्रमात्। ममाऽसीद्बुद्धिदौरात्म्यात्प्राणहारी व्यतिक्रमः4.24.10।।
explanation: 'The idea of killing me was not acceptable to his noble nature, while my wicked thought caused his death.

shloka_text: द्रुमशाखावभग्नोऽहं मुहुर्तं परिनिष्टनन्। सान्त्वयित्वा त्वनेनोक्तो न पुनः कर्तुमर्हसि4.24.11।।
explanation: 'When my brother hit me with the branch of a tree I screamed for a while. But he pacified me and said it was improper and he would not repeat it.

shloka_text: भ्रातृत्वमार्यभावश्च धर्मश्चानेन रक्षितः। मया क्रोधश्च कामश्च कपित्वं च प्रदर्शितम्4.24.12।।
explanation: 'Thus while nobility, a feeling of respect,brotherliness and duty was shown to me by my brother, I exhibited wrath, passion and  frivolity, the nature of the monkey.

shloka_text: अचिन्तनीयं परिवर्जनीय मनीप्सनीयं स्वनवेक्षणीयम्। प्राप्तोऽस्मि पाप्मानमिमं नरेन्द्र भ्रातुर्वधात्त्वाष्ट्रवधादिवेन्द्र:4.24.13।।
explanation: 'O king  just as Indra committed sin by killing Tvashta, I have reaped the sin by  killing my brorther which is unthinkable, avoidable, undesirable and ignoble.

shloka_text: पाप्मानमिन्द्रस्य मही जलं च वृक्षाश्च कामं जगृहुः स्त्रियश्च। को नाम पाप्मानमिमं क्षमेत शाखामृगस्य प्रतिपत्तुमिच्छेत्।।4.24.14।।
explanation: 'Trees owned the sin of Indra and it was shared by the earth, water and women voluntarily.But who is there to pardon a monkey and own the sin?

shloka_text: नार्हामि सम्मानमिमं प्रजानां न यौवराज्यं कुत एव राज्यम्। अधर्मयुक्तं कुलनाशयुक्त मेवंविधं राघव कर्म कृत्वा4.24.15।।
explanation: 'O Rama having acted in an unrighteous manner, which destroys the clan, I am not fit to accept the respect of people nor the status of a prince regent, what to speak of kingship?

shloka_text: पापस्य कर्ताऽस्मि विगर्हितस्य क्षुद्रस्य लोकापकृतस्य चैव। शोको महान्मामभिवर्ततेऽयं वृष्टेर्यथा निम्नमिवाम्बुवेगः4.24.16।।
explanation: 'I have committed a sin which is condemned by the world. This intense grief has engulfed me just as the flow of rain water inundates the lowlying area when it rains.

shloka_text: सोदर्यघातापरगात्रवालः सन्तापहस्ताक्षिशिरोविषाणः। एनोमयो मामभिहन्ति हस्ती दृप्तो नदीकूलमिव प्रवृद्धः।।4.24.17।।
explanation: 'The elephant of sin (hanging heavily on me) has a tail of treacherous killing of one's own brother, which has resulted in deep sorrow in the form of a trunk, eyes, head and tusks.This elephant is striking at me as he would strike the bank of a river when he grows strong and gets puffed up with the pride of energy. (The idea of a proud elephant striking at the target is superimposed on the sin committed by Sugriva.The animal's tail is  the killing of a brother. Sugriva's remorse spreads all over the body trunk, eyes, head and tusks of the animal. As a proud elephant strikes at the river bank the sin is striking at Sugriva to destroy him. The Rupaka here is perfect and total).

shloka_text: अंहो बतेदं नृवराविषह्यं निवर्तते मे हृदि साधुवृत्तम्। विवर्णमग्नौ परितप्यमानं किट्टं यथा राघव जातरूपम्4.24.18।।
explanation: 'O distinguished Rama this anxiety is unbearable for me. My good behaviour is relegated to the back of my heart unable to bear the sin, just like the dirt surfaces pushing the bright colour of gold when burnt in fire.

shloka_text: महाबलानां हरियूथपाना मिदं कुलं राघव मन्निमित्तम्। अस्याङ्गदप्यापि च शोकतापा दर्धस्थितप्राणमितीव मन्ये।।4.24.19।।
explanation: 'O Rama this race of mighty monkey chiefs is as though reduced to a halfdead state because of my action and the grief of Angada.

shloka_text: सुतस्सुलभ्यस्सुजनस्सुवश्यः कुतस्तु पुत्रस्सदृशोऽङ्गदेन। न चापि विद्येत स वीर देशो यस्मिन्भवेत्सोदरसन्निकर्षः4.24.20।।
explanation: 'One can find easily a son who is controllable and accessible in need but it is difficult to find a good son like Angada, who is virtuous and mighty and who is respectful to parents. O warrior (Rama), there is no place where I can get a brother like Vali. (A brother cannot be made. His relationship is natural. Rama stresses the same subhashita in Yuddhakanda when Lakshmana swooned).

shloka_text: यद्यङ्गदो वीरवरार्ह जीवेत् जीवेच्छ माता परिपालनार्थम्। विना तु पुत्रं परितापदीना तारा न जीवेदिति निश्चितं मे4.24.21।।
explanation: If Angada, worthy of the best heroes, lives, then his mother will also live to care for him. But without her son, Tara, distressed by sorrow, will certainly not live; this is my firm conviction.

shloka_text: सोऽहं प्रवेक्ष्याम्यतिदीप्तमग्निं भ्रात्रा च पुत्रेण च सख्यमिच्छन्। इमे विचेष्यन्ति हरिप्रवीरा स्सीतां निदेशे तव वर्तमानाः4.24.22।।
explanation: 'I am a sinner. I desire to enter the blazing fire (for atonement) in order to maintain friendship with my brother and son. At your command these vanara leaders will go round and search for Sita.

shloka_text: कृत्स्नं तु ते सेत्स्यति कार्यमेत न्मय्यप्रतीते मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र कुलस्य हन्तारमजीवनार्हं रामानुजानीहि कृतागसं माम्4.24.23।।
explanation: 'O prince Rama even if I am dead the entire task of yours, will be accomplished by the  vanara race. I have ruined the whole race. I am sinful and not fit to live. Permit me (to enter fire).

shloka_text: इत्येवमार्तस्य रघुप्रवीरः श्रुत्वा वचो वाल्यनुजस्य तस्य। सञ्जातबाष्पः परवीरहन्ता रामो मुहूर्तं विमना बभूव4.24.24।।
explanation: Rama, the hero of the Raghu dynasty, a destroyer of the enemy heroes, was moved to tears. He lost composure for a moment when he heard Sugriva's lament.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् क्षणेऽभीक्ष्णमवेक्ष्यमाणः क्षितिक्षमावान्भुवनस्य गोप्ता। रामो रुदन्तीं व्यसने निमग्नां समुत्सुकः सोऽथ ददर्श ताराम्4.24.25।।
explanation: In that moment, Rama,the protector of the world, tolerant like the earth, beheld Tara plunged in grief, looking at him again and again and weeping.

shloka_text: तां चारुनेत्रां कपिसिंहनाथां पतिं समाश्लिष्य तदा शयानाम्। उत्थापयामासुरदीनसत्त्वां मन्त्रिप्रधानाः कपिवीरपत्नीम्4.24.26।।
explanation: The foremost ministers of Vali lifted up the beautifuleyed, noble Tara, wife of the monkey hero clinging to the body of her husband, a lion among monkeys.

shloka_text: सा विस्फुरन्ती परिरभ्यमाणा भर्तुस्सकाशादपनीयमाना। ददर्श रामं शरचापपाणिं स्वतेजसा सूर्यमिव ज्वलन्तम्4.24.27।।
explanation: While Tara was clinging to her husband and struggling, and was being removed from there, she saw effulgent Rama holding bow and arrows glittering like the Sun.

shloka_text: सुसंवृतं पार्थिपलक्षणैश्च तं चारुनेत्रं मृगशाबनेत्रा। अदृष्टपूर्वं पुरुषप्रधान मयं स काकुत्स्थ इति प्रजज्ञे4.24.28।।
explanation: The fawneyed Tara saw the magnificent man of Kakutstha family endowed with all royal marks and beautiful eyes, whom she had never seen before and knew he was Rama.

shloka_text: तस्येन्द्रकल्पस्य दुरासदस्य महानुभावस्य समीपमार्या। आर्ताऽतितूर्णं व्यसनाभिपन्ना जगाम तारा परिविह्वलन्ती4.24.29।।
explanation: The noble Tara, desperate, agonised, totally shaken up quickly went near the magnanimous Rama,  who was like Indraunapproachable.

shloka_text: सा तं समासाद्य विशुद्धसत्त्वा शोकेन सम्भ्रान्तशरीरभावा। मनस्विनी वाक्यमुवाच तारा रामं रणोत्कर्षणलब्धलक्षम्4.24.30।।
explanation: Wise Tara, baffled out of grief and agitated, with pure consciousness, approached Rama,  eminent in warfare who could hit the target. And spoke:

shloka_text: त्वमप्रमेयश्च दुरासदश्च जितेन्द्रियश्चोत्तमधार्मिकश्च। अक्षय्यकीर्तिश्च विचक्षणश्च क्षितिक्षमावान्क्षतजोपमाक्षः4.24.31।।
explanation: 'You are immeasurable, unassailable, self controlled, and best among the righteous. Your fame never diminishes. You have great sense of discrimination. You are known to possess forbearance like the mother earth. Your eyes are redcornered (which is a sign of valour).

shloka_text: त्वमात्तबाणासनबाणपाणि र्महाबलस्संहननोपपन्नः। मनुष्यदेहाभ्युदयं विहाय दिव्येन देहाभ्युदयेन युक्तः।।4.24.32।।
explanation: 'You are wielding bow and arrows. You possess mighty human limbs that have the power to destroy the enemy .You  have assumed a divine human body.

shloka_text: येनैक बाणेन हतः प्रियो मे तेनैव मां त्वं जहि सायकेन। हता गमिष्यामि समीपमस्य न मामृते राम रमेत वाली4.24.33।।
explanation: 'O warrior kill me by the same single arrow with which you killed my beloved lord,Vali. I will join him after death as he will not be happy without me.

shloka_text: स्वर्गेऽपि पद्मामलपत्रनेत्र स्समेत्य सम्प्रेक्ष्य च मामपश्यन्। न ह्येष उच्चावचताम्रचूडा विचित्रवेषाप्सरसोऽभजिष्यत्।।4.24.34।।
explanation: 'If Vali with eyes of clear petals of a lotus does not see me in heaven, he may not join the wonderfully dressed apsarasas adorned with different kinds of red flowers in their hair.

shloka_text: स्वर्गेऽपि शोकं च विवर्णतां च मया विना प्राप्प्यति वीर वाली। रम्ये नगेन्द्रस्य तटावकाशे विदेहकन्यारहितो यथा त्वम्4.24.35।।
explanation: 'O Rama Vali will experience sorrow and become pale bereft of me even in heaven just as you are filled with sorrow even on a delightful mountain slope bereft of princess of Videha.

shloka_text: त्वं वेत्थ यावद्वनिताविहीनः प्राप्नोति दुःखं पुरुषः कुमारः। तत्त्वं प्रजानन् जहि मां न वाली दुःखं ममादर्शनजं भजेत4.24.36।।
explanation: 'You are aware of the grief of a young man separated from his wife. Kill me so that I can go to Vali. Let not Vali experience the sorrow of not seeing me.

shloka_text: यच्चापि मन्येत भवान्महात्मा स्त्रीघातदोषो न भवेत्तु मह्यम्। आत्मेयमस्येति च मां जहि त्वं न स्त्रीवधस्स्यान्मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र।।4.24.37।।
explanation: 'O prince as you are great, you might think of the blemish of killing a woman. Since Tara is Vali's soul, you may kill me. It will not amount to killing a woman.(You will only be killing the soul of Vali by killing Tara).

shloka_text: शास्त्रप्रयोगाद्विविधाच्च वेदा दात्माह्यनन्यः पुरुषस्य दाराः। दाराप्रदानान्नहि दानमन्य त्प्रदृश्यते ज्ञानवतां हि लोके4.24.38।।
explanation: 'The  sacred texts as well as Vedic statements declare that wife is an inseparable part of the  husband's soul. To the learned, there is no greater offering in the world than restoring the wife to her husband. You will not beget any sin by killing me.

shloka_text: त्वं चापि मां तस्य मम प्रियस्य प्रदास्य से धर्ममवेक्ष्य वीर अनेन दानेन न लप्स्यसे त्व मधर्मयोगं मम वीर घातात्4.24.39।।
explanation: 'O gallant prince  if you give me away to my dear lord, carefully considering dharma, you will not be committing any adharma by killing me since it will be an offering.

shloka_text: आर्तामनाथामपनीयमाना मेवं विधामर्हसि मां निहन्तुम्। अहं हि मातङ्गविलासगामिना प्लवङ्गमानामृषभेण धीमता4.24.40।। विना वरार्होत्तमहेममालिना चिरं न शक्ष्यामि नरेन्द्र जीवितुम्। इत्येवमुक्तस्तु विभुर्महात्मा तारां समाश्वास्य हितं बभाषे4.24.41।।
explanation: 'O king it is proper on your part to kill me as I am in great distress. I am a helpless orphan torn away from her husband.O king I will not live long without the wise leader of monkeys who walked majestically like an elephant and wore the choicest golden necklace'. Implored by Tara this way, the great soul, Rama, lord of the earth said to Tara these words of consolation:

shloka_text: आर्तामनाथामपनीयमाना मेवं विधामर्हसि मां निहन्तुम्। अहं हि मातङ्गविलासगामिना प्लवङ्गमानामृषभेण धीमता4.24.40।। विना वरार्होत्तमहेममालिना चिरं न शक्ष्यामि नरेन्द्र जीवितुम्। इत्येवमुक्तस्तु विभुर्महात्मा तारां समाश्वास्य हितं बभाषे4.24.41।।
explanation: 'O king it is proper on your part to kill me as I am in great distress. I am a helpless orphan torn away from her husband.O king I will not live long without the wise leader of monkeys who walked majestically like an elephant and wore the choicest golden necklace'. Implored by Tara this way, the great soul, Rama, lord of the earth said to Tara these words of consolation:

shloka_text: मा वीरभार्ये विमतिं कुरुष्व लोको हि सर्वो विहितो विधात्रा। तं चैव सर्वं सुखदुःखयोगं लोकोऽब्रवीत्तेन कृतं विधात्रा।।4.24.42।।
explanation: 'O wife of a valiant warrior Do not lose heart. The entire world is controlled by the creator. People maintain that joy and sorrow are foreordained.

shloka_text: त्रयोऽहि लोका विहितं विधानं नातिक्रमन्ते वशगा हि तस्य। प्रीतिं परां प्राप्स्यसि तां तथैव पुत्रस्तु ते प्राप्स्यति यौवराज्यम्। धात्रा विधानं विहितं तथैव न शूरपत्नयः परिदेवयन्ति4.24.43।।
explanation: Indeed, the three worlds do not transgress the ordained law, for they are subject to it. You will similarly attain supreme joy, and your son will obtain the crown-princedom. The law has been ordained by the Creator in this manner; wives of heroes do not lament.

shloka_text: आश्वासिता तेन तु राघवेण प्रभावयुक्तेन परन्तपेन। सा वीरपत्नी ध्वनता मुखेन सुवेषरूपा विरराम तारा4.24.44।।
explanation: Consoled by the influential Rama, scorcher of enemies, Tara the charming wife of a warrior, stopped wailing aloud. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुर्विंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyfourth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवं चैव तारां च साङ्गदं सहलक्ष्मणः। समानशोकः काकुत्स्थ स्सान्त्वयन्निदमब्रवीत्।।4.25.1।।
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana were equally sad. Rama, scion of the Kakutstha race, consoled Sugriva, Tara as well as Angada in the following words:

shloka_text: न शोकपरितापेन श्रेयसा युज्यते मृतः। यदत्रानन्तरं कार्यं तत्समाधातुमर्हथ4.25.2।।
explanation: 'No lamentation revives the dead. So you should take up whatever is required now.

shloka_text: लोकवृत्तमनुष्ठेयं कृतं वो बाष्पमोक्षणम्। न कालादुत्तरं किञ्चित्कर्म शक्यमुपासितुम्4.25.3।।
explanation: 'You have to go the worldly way. You have shed tears enough. Time is passing. You cannot perform the funeral after the lapse of appropriate time.

shloka_text: नियतिः कारणं लोके नियतिः कर्मसाधनम्। नियतिस्सर्वभूतानां नियोगेष्विह कारणम्4.25.4।।
explanation: 'Fate is the cause of the world. Fate is the means of accomplishment. Fate assigns duties to all beings.

shloka_text: न कर्ता कस्यचित्कश्चिन्नियोगे चापिनेश्वरः। स्वभावे वर्तते लोकस्तस्य कालः परायणम्4.25.5।।
explanation: 'No one can control another's action. No one including God can be the agent of action. No one has the power to entrust duty to others. This entire world is governed by one's own nature. Nature in turn is governed by Time (fate).

shloka_text: न कालः कालमत्येति न कालः परिहीयते। स्वभावं च समासाद्य न कश्चिदतिवर्तते4.25.6।।
explanation: 'God (though independent) does not deviate from Time. Time cannot be escaped or trangressed. It cannot be condoned or avoided. No one can transgress their own nature.

shloka_text: न कालस्यास्ति बन्धुत्वं न हेतुर्न पराक्रमः। न मित्रज्ञातिसम्बन्धः कारणं नात्मनो वशः4.25.7।।
explanation: 'Time has no consideration for relationship, friendship, or kinship or valour. Time itself is the cause. It is never under one's control.

shloka_text: किं तु कालपरीणामो द्रष्टव्यस्साधु पश्यता। धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च कालक्रमसमाहिताः4.25.8।।
explanation: 'However a wise man should visualise the turn of events in course of time with the right vision. Dharma, artha and kama are controlled by an order laid down by Time.

shloka_text: इतस्स्वां प्रकृतिं वाली गतःप्राप्तः क्रियाफलम्। धर्मार्थकाम संयोगैः पवित्रं प्लवगेश्वरः4.25.9।।
explanation: 'Vali, king of monkeys is dead and gone. He acted according to his own nature and attained the sacred fruit of his action comensurate with dharma, wealth and pleasures in this world.

shloka_text: स्वधर्मस्य च संयोगाज्जितस्तेन महात्मना। स्वर्गः परिगृहीतश्च प्राणानपरिरक्षता4.25.10।।
explanation: 'Great Vali has earned a place in heaven by virtue of his own dharma and not caring for his own life .He has got the heavenly position he earned.

shloka_text: एषा वै नियतिश्शेष्ठा यां गतो हरियूथपः। तदलं परितापेन प्राप्तकालमुपास्यताम्4.25.11।।
explanation: 'The state attained by the chief of monkeys is an excellent one.Therefore there is no need to regret. Attend to your duties (relating to rites)'

shloka_text: वचनान्ते तु रामस्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा। अवदत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सुग्रीवं गतचेतसम्4.25.12।।
explanation: Seeing Sugriva had lost his senses, Lakshmana, the slayer of enemy warriors humbly said at the end of Rama's address:

shloka_text: कुरु त्वमस्य सुग्रीव प्रेतकार्यमनन्तरम्। ताराङ्गदाभ्यां सहितो वालिनो दहनं प्रति।।4.25.13।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva perform with Tara and Angada the funeral obsequies relating to the cremation of Vali.

shloka_text: समाज्ञापय काष्ठानि शुष्कानि च बहूनि च। चन्दनादीनि दिव्यानि वालिसंस्कारकारणात्4.25.14।।
explanation: 'Let the best of dry logs and sandalwood be ordered for the funeral rites of Vali.

shloka_text: समाश्वासय चैनं त्वमङ्गदं दीनचेतसम्। मा भूर्बालिशबुद्धिस्त्वं त्वदधीनमिदं पुरम्4.25.15।।
explanation: 'Pacify the despondent Angada so that he does not entertain childish thoughts any more. This city is under your control (now).

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्त्वानयेन्माल्यं वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। घृतं तैलमथो गन्धान्यच्चात्र समनन्तरम्4.25.16।।
explanation: 'Let Angada for his part collect garlands of many kinds, clothes, clarified butter, oil, fragrants and all that is required to be procured.

shloka_text: त्वं तार शिबिकां शीघ्रमादायागच्छ सम्भ्रमात्। त्वरा गुणवती युक्ता ह्यस्मिन्काले विशेषतः4.25.17।।
explanation: 'O Tara quickly get a swiftmoving litter fastened with ropes specially  suitable for this occasion.

shloka_text: सज्जीभवन्तु प्लवगाश्शिबिकावाहनोचिताः। समर्था बलिनश्चैव निर्हरिष्यन्ति वालिनम्।।4.25.18।।
explanation: 'Let those who are strong and capable among the monkeys be ready to carry  the dead body of Vali on a litter'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवं सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः। तसौ भ्रातृसमीपस्थो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा4.25.19।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Sugriva, Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, slayer of enemies, stood by his brother

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा तारस्सम्भ्रान्तमानसः। प्रविवेश गुहां शीघ्रं शिबिकासक्तमानसः4.25.20।।
explanation: On hearing Lakshmana, Tara in an excited state quickly entered the cave city to get the litter.

shloka_text: आदाय शिबिकां तारस्स तु पर्यापतत्पुनः। वानरैरुह्यमानां तां शूरैरुद्वहनोचितैः4.25.21।।
explanation: Tara jumped in on to the litter carried by strong monkeys.

shloka_text: दिव्यां भद्रासनयुतां शिबिकां स्यन्दनोपमाम्। पक्षिकर्मभिराचित्रां द्रुमकर्मविभूषिताम्4.25.22।। आचितां चित्रपत्तीभि स्सुनिविष्टां समन्ततः। विमानमिव सिद्धानां जालवातायनान्विताम्4.25.23।। सुनियुक्तां विशालां च सुकृतां विश्वकर्मणा। दारुपर्वतकोपेतां चारुकर्मपरिष्कृताम्4.25.24।। वराभरणहारैश्च चित्रमाल्योपशोभिताम्। गुहागहनसञ्छन्नां रक्तचन्दनभूषिताम्4.25.25।। पुष्पौघैस्समभिच्छन्नां पद्ममालाभिरेव च। तरुणादित्यवर्णाभिर्भ्राजमानाभिरावृताम्4.25.26।।
explanation: A swiftmoving, marvellous palanquin designed by Viswakarma was brought. Covered with colourful pictures of birds and trees on every side it looking like an aerial chariot fit for saints. Fitted with a splendid seat grilled windows, artificially made small caverns and grottos of wood was embellished with carvings of mountains, choice ornaments and garlands. With red sandal paste, red scented flowers and red lotus garlands, it resembled the rising Sun.

shloka_text: दिव्यां भद्रासनयुतां शिबिकां स्यन्दनोपमाम्। पक्षिकर्मभिराचित्रां द्रुमकर्मविभूषिताम्4.25.22।। आचितां चित्रपत्तीभि स्सुनिविष्टां समन्ततः। विमानमिव सिद्धानां जालवातायनान्विताम्4.25.23।। सुनियुक्तां विशालां च सुकृतां विश्वकर्मणा। दारुपर्वतकोपेतां चारुकर्मपरिष्कृताम्4.25.24।। वराभरणहारैश्च चित्रमाल्योपशोभिताम्। गुहागहनसञ्छन्नां रक्तचन्दनभूषिताम्4.25.25।। पुष्पौघैस्समभिच्छन्नां पद्ममालाभिरेव च। तरुणादित्यवर्णाभिर्भ्राजमानाभिरावृताम्4.25.26।।

Fitted with a splendid seat grilled windows, artificially made small caverns and grottos of wood was embellished with carvings of mountains, choice ornaments and garlands. Fitted with a splendid seat grilled windows, artificially made small caverns and grottos of wood was embellished with carvings of mountains, choice ornaments and garlands. With red sandal paste, red scented flowers and red lotus garlands, it resembled the rising Sun.

shloka_text: ईदृशीं शिबिकां दृष्ट्वा रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्। क्षिप्रं विनीयतां वाली प्रेतकार्यं विधीयताम्4.25.26।।
explanation: Seeing the palanquin, Rama said to Lakshmana 'Let the body of Vali be placed in the palanquin quickly and last rites duly performed'.

shloka_text: ततो वालिनमुद्यम्य सुग्रीवश्शिबिकां तदा। आरोपयत विक्रोशन्नङ्गदेन सहैव तु4.25.27।।
explanation: Then Sugriva along with Angada, crying aloud bitterly, lifted the body (of Vali) and placed it on the palanquin.

shloka_text: आरोप्य शिबिकां चैव वालिनं गतजीवितम्। अलङ्कारैश्च विविधैर्माल्यैर्वस्त्रैश्च भूषितम्4.25.28।।
explanation: Vali's deadbody was placed on the palanquin, decorated with many ornaments, garlands and clothes

shloka_text: आज्ञापयत्तदा राजा सुग्रीव प्लवगेश्वरः। और्ध्वदैहिकमार्यस्य क्रियतामनुरूपतः।।4.25.29।।
explanation: King Sugriva, lord of the monkeys, said, 'Let the funeral rites of my noble sire be performed in a fitting manner'.

shloka_text: विश्राणयन्तो रत्नानि विविधानि बहून्यपि। अग्रतः प्लवगा यान्तु शिबिका समनन्तरम्4.25.30।।
explanation: 'Let the monkeys march in front, showering many different gems in large quantities and let the palanquin follow.

shloka_text: राज्ञामृद्दिविशेषा हि दृश्यन्ते भुवि यादृशाः। तादृशैरिह कुर्वन्तु वानरा भर्तृसत्क्रियाम्4.25.31।।
explanation: 'Let the monkeys perform the funeral rites of our lord in an honourable way as expensively as has been done with regard to the obsequies of kings who ruled over this land.

shloka_text: तादृशं वालिनः क्षिप्रं प्राकुर्वन्नौर्ध्वदैहिकम्। अङ्गदं परिगृह्याऽशु तारप्रभृतयस्तदा4.25.32।। क्रोशन्तः प्रययुस्सर्वे वानरा हतबान्धवाः।
explanation: Tara, Angada and the other bereaved monkeys hastened to perform the funeral ceremony of Valiweeping.

shloka_text: ततः प्रणिहिताः सर्वा वानर्योस्य वशानुगाः4.25.33।। चुक्रुशु र्वीर वीरेति भूयः क्रोशन्ति ताः स्त्रीयः।
explanation: Then all the female monkeys who were in his (Vali's) harem walked past the deadbody of Vali, crying again and again 'Alas, Oh hero'

shloka_text: ताराप्रभृतयस्सर्वा वानर्यो हरियूथपाः। अनुजग्मुर्हि भर्तारं क्रोशन्त्यः करुणस्वनाः4.25.34।।
explanation: Tara along with other female monkeys followed their lord, crying pathetically.

shloka_text: तासां रुदितशब्देन वानरीणां वनान्तरे। वनानि गिरयश्चैव विक्रोशन्तीव सर्वतः4.25.35।।
explanation: When the female monkeys were weeping in the midst of the forest, it looked as if the forest and the hills were also mourning.

shloka_text: पुलिने गिरिनद्यास्तु विविक्ते जलसंवृते4.25.36।। चितां चक्रुस्सुबहवो वानराश्शोककर्शिता:।
explanation: Tormented with tears, the monkeys prepared in a solitary place surrounded by waters a pyre on the sandbank of a mountain stream.

shloka_text: अवरोप्य ततस्स्कन्धाच्छिबिकां वाहनोचिताः। तस्थुरेकान्तमाश्रित्य सर्वे शोकसमन्विता:4.25.37।।
explanation: Putting down the palanquin from their shoulders on the lonely spot, the bearers stood in tearswaiting.

shloka_text: ततस्तारा पतिं दृष्ट्वा शिबिकातलशायिनम्4.25.38।। आरोप्याङ्के शिरस्तस्य विललाप सुदुःखिता।
explanation: Seeing her husband lying in the palanquin, Tara, full of grief placed Vali's head on her lap and cried.

shloka_text: हा वानर महाराज हा नाथ मम वत्सल4.25.39।। हा महार्ह महाबाहो हा मम प्रिय पश्य माम्। जनं न पश्यसीमं त्वं कस्माच्छोकाभिपीडितम्।4.25.40।।
explanation: 'Why don't you look at me, oppressed with tears, O monkey king, O my venerable lord, O longarmed one, O my dear?

shloka_text: हा वानर महाराज हा नाथ मम वत्सल4.25.39।। हा महार्ह महाबाहो हा मम प्रिय पश्य माम्। जनं न पश्यसीमं त्वं कस्माच्छोकाभिपीडितम्।4.25.40।।
explanation: 'Why don't you look at me, oppressed with tears, O monkey king, O my venerable lord, O longarmed one, O my dear?

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टमिव ते वक्त्रं गतासोरपि मानद आस्तार्कसमवर्णं च लक्ष्यते जीवतो यथा4.25.41।।
explanation: 'O revered self even though you are bereft of life, your face looks cheerful. It carries the colour of the setting Sun, and looks the same when you were alive.

shloka_text: एष त्वां रामरूपेण कालः कर्षति वानर। येन स्म विधवास्सर्वाः कृता एकेषुणा वने4.25.42।।
explanation: 'O monkey a single arrow from Rama who appeared in the forest in the form of death dragged you away from us and turned us all into widows.

shloka_text: इमास्तास्तव राजेन्द्र वानर्योवल्लभास्सदा। पादैर्विकृष्ट मध्वानमागताः किं न बुध्यसे4.25.43।।
explanation: 'O king of kings why don't you understand that these female monkeys, your wives who were dear to you have come on foot this long distance with great difficulty?

shloka_text: तवेष्टा ननु नामैता भार्याश्चन्द्रनिभाननाः। इदानीं नेक्षसे कस्तात्सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्4.25.44।।
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys these moonfaced wives were indeed once your favourites. Why don't you look  at them? Why don't you look Sugriva?

shloka_text: एते हि सचिवा राजं स्तारप्रभृतयस्तव। पुरवासी जनश्चायं परिवार्यासतेऽनघ4.25.45।।
explanation: 'O king O sinless hero Tara and others, your ministers as well as the inhabitants of the capital are here sitting around you.

shloka_text: विसर्जयैतान् प्लवगान्यथोचितमरिन्दम। ततः क्रीडामहे सर्वा वनेषु मदनोत्कटाः4.25.46।।
explanation: 'O conqueror of enemies give these monkeys their due in accordance with their status and send them back as you used to do when they were passionately sporting in your company here in this forest.

shloka_text: एवं विलपतीं तारां पतिशोकपरिप्लुताम्। उत्थापयन्ति स्म तदा वानर्यश्शोककर्शिताः4.25.47।।
explanation: The griefstricken female monkeys helped Tara, overwhelmed with sorrow due to her husband's death, rise from the ground.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेण ततस्सार्धंमङ्गदः पितरं रुदन्। चितामारोपयामास शोकेनाभिहतेन्द्रियः4.25.48।।
explanation: Then Angada, helped by Sugriva, placed his father's body on the pyre, with his senses numbed in deep sorrow.

shloka_text: ततोऽग्निं विधिवद्दत्त्वा सोऽपसव्यं चकार ह। पितरं दीर्घमध्वानं प्रस्थितं व्याकुलेन्द्रियः4.25.49।।
explanation: Overwhelmed with sorrow, he offered fire to the father who had set out on a long journey (to heaven). As per tradition he went round the pyre anteclock wise.

shloka_text: संस्कृत्य वालिनं ते तु विधिपूर्वं प्लवङ्गमाः। आजग्मुरुदकं कर्तुं नदीं शुभजलां शिवाम्4.25.50।।
explanation: The monkeys set Vali's body to be consumed by fire as per tradition and proceeded to an auspicious river of pure water in order to offer oblation (to the departed soul).

shloka_text: ततस्ते सहितास्तत्र ह्यङ्गदं स्थाप्य चाग्रतः। सुग्रीवतारासहितास्सिषिचुर्वालिने जलम्4.25.51।।
explanation: Then the monkeys along with Sugriva and Tara positioning Angada in the forefront made waterofferings (to Vali) collectively.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेणेव दीनेन दीनो भूत्वा महाबलः। समानशोकः काकुत्स्थ: प्रेतकार्याण्यकारयत्4.25.52।।
explanation: Mighty Rama, who was equally sorrowful and pitiable as Sugriva, directed the performance of funeral rites.

shloka_text: ततश्शोकाभिसन्तप्तं सुग्रीवं क्लिन्नवाससम्। शाखामृगमहामात्राः परिवार्योपतस्थिरे4.26.1।।
explanation: Then the chiefs of the army of the monkeys surrounded  Sugriva, who was overcome with grief and was still in wet clothes (since he had taken bath at the conclusion of the funeral rites) and waited.

shloka_text: अभिगम्य महाबाहुं राममक्लिष्टकारिणम्। स्थिताः प्राञ्जलयस्सर्वे पितामहमिवर्षयः4.26.2।।
explanation: Just like sages stand before the creator Brahma, all the monkeys stood with folded hands before the longarmed Rama, the remover of sorrow.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभ स्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः4.26.3।।
explanation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod, glowing like a golden mountain, whose face resembled the rising Sun addressed Rama with folded hands:

shloka_text: भवत्प्रसादात्सुग्रीवः पितृपैतामहं महत्। वानराणां सुदुष्प्रापं प्राप्तो राज्यमिदं प्रभो4.26.4।।
explanation: 'O Lord by your grace Sugriva inherited the ancestral kingdom which would have been otherwise difficult.

shloka_text: भवता समनुज्ञातः प्रविश्य नगरं शुभम्4.26.5।। संविधास्यति कार्याणि सर्वाणि ससुहृज्जनः। स्नातोऽयं विविधैर्गन्धैरौषधैश्च यथाविधि4.26.6।।
explanation: 'Permitted by your gracious self, he will enter the auspicious city along with his friends and perform his duties. He had his auspicious bath in fragrant waters with medicinal herbs as per tradition.

shloka_text: भवता समनुज्ञातः प्रविश्य नगरं शुभम्4.26.5।। संविधास्यति कार्याणि सर्वाणि ससुहृज्जनः। स्नातोऽयं विविधैर्गन्धैरौषधैश्च यथाविधि4.26.6।।
explanation: 'Permitted by your gracious self, he will enter the auspicious city along with his friends and perform his duties. He had his auspicious bath in fragrant waters with medicinal herbs as per tradition.

shloka_text: अर्चयिष्यति रत्नैश्च माल्यैश्च त्वां विशेषतः। इमां गिरिगुहां रम्यामभिगन्तुमितोऽर्हसि4.26.7।। कुरुष्व स्वामिसम्बन्धं वानरान्सम्प्रहर्षय।
explanation: 'He wants to propitiate you first specially with garlands and  gems. Pray enter this beautiful mountain cave for the pleasure of the monkeys and establish relationship with king Sugriva.'

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो हनुमता राघवः परवीरहा4.26.8।। प्रत्युवाच हनूमन्तं बुद्धिमान्वाक्यकोविदः।
explanation: Requested by Hanuman who was skilful in conversation, wise Rama, slayer of enemies, replied:

shloka_text: चतुर्दश समास्सौम्य ग्रामं वा यदि वा पुरम्4.26.9।। न प्रवेक्ष्यामि हनुमन्पितुर्निर्देशपालकः।
explanation: 'Dear Hanuman In obedience to my father's command I should not enter any village or city for fourteen years.

shloka_text: सुसमृद्धां गुहां रम्यां सुग्रीवो वानरर्षभः4.26.10।। प्रविष्टो विधिवद्वीरः क्षिप्रं राज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्।
explanation: 'Let Sugriva enter the beautiful prosperous cavern (Kishkinda) and be installed by you as king with due rituals.'

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा हनूमन्तं रामस्सुग्रीवमब्रवीत्4.26.11।। वृत्तज्ञो वृत्तसम्पन्नमुदारबलविक्रमम्।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Hanuman, Rama who knew etiquette addressed mighty  Sugriva, endowed with wisdom:

shloka_text: इममप्यङ्गदं वीर यौवराज्येऽभिषेचय4.26.12।। ज्येष्ठस्य स सुतो ज्येष्ठस्सदृशो विक्रमेण ते। अङ्गदोऽयमदीनात्मा यौवराज्यस्य भाजनम्4.26.13।।
explanation: 'O hero consecrate Angada as heirapparent since he deserves it as the eldest son of your brother, a noble soul and equal to you in prowess.

shloka_text: इममप्यङ्गदं वीर यौवराज्येऽभिषेचय4.26.12।। ज्येष्ठस्य स सुतो ज्येष्ठस्सदृशो विक्रमेण ते। अङ्गदोऽयमदीनात्मा यौवराज्यस्य भाजनम्4.26.13।।
explanation: 'O hero consecrate Angada as heirapparent since he deserves it as the eldest son of your brother, a noble soul and equal to you in prowess.

shloka_text: पूर्वोऽयं वार्षिको मासः श्रावणस्सलिलागमः। प्रवृत्तास्सौम्य चत्वारो मासा वार्षिकसज्ञिकाः4.26.14।।
explanation: 'O noble Sugriva the four months from now will be rainy season. This is Sravana, the first month of the season in which rain is expected to start pouring.

shloka_text: नायमुद्योगसमयः प्रविश त्वं पुरीं शुभाम्। अस्मिन्वत्स्याम्यहं सौम्य पर्वते सह लक्ष्मणः4.26.15।।
explanation: 'O goodnatured Sugriva this is not a suitable time for any endeavour. Go to the auspicious capital city of Kishkinda and I will reside on the mountain with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: इयं गिरिगुहा रम्या विशाला युक्तमारुता। प्रभूतसलिला सौम्य प्रभूतकमलोत्पला4.26.16।।
explanation: 'Dear Sugriva this cavern of the mountain is large and airy. It has abundant water resources with lotuses and lilies.

shloka_text: कार्तिके समनुप्राप्ते त्वं रावणवधे यत। एष नस्समयस्सौम्य प्रविश त्वं स्वमालयम्4.26.17।। अभिषिक्तस्व राज्ये च सुहृदस्सम्प्रहर्षय।
explanation: 'Enter the city and get yourself installed and cheer your friends. Make all arrangement for killing Ravana when the month of Kartika begins as it is the proper time (for the purpose).

shloka_text: इति रामाभ्यनुज्ञातस्सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः4.26.18।। प्रविवेश पुरीं रम्यां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम्।
explanation: Thus permitted by Rama , Sugriva, lord of the monkeys entered the beautiful city of Kishkinda (once) ruled by Vali.

shloka_text: तं वानरसहस्राणि प्रविष्टं वानरेश्वरम्4.26.19।। अभिवाद्य प्रविष्टानि सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्।
explanation: Thousands of monkeys entered the city of Kishkinda along with their king, and stood  in attendance everywhere.

shloka_text: ततः प्रकृतयस्सर्वा दृष्ट्वा हरिगणेश्वरम्4.26.20।। प्रणम्य मूर्ध्ना पतिता वसुधायां समाहिताः।
explanation: Then all the subjects of the city collected together, prostrated to the chief of the monkey clan with their forehead touching the ground (as a mark of respect) and sat down.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवः प्रकृतीस्सर्वास्सम्भाष्योत्थाप्य वीर्यवान्4.26.21।। भ्रातुरन्तःपुरं सौम्यं प्रविवेश महाबलः।
explanation: Asking the monkeys to rise to their feet, the mighty and powerful Sugriva entered the inner chambers of his brother.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य त्वभिनिष्क्रान्तं सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्4.26.22।। अभ्यषिञ्चन्त सुहृदस्सहस्राक्षमिवामराः।
explanation: With Sugriva,the lord of the monkeys, returned to Kishkinda, his kith and kin  coronated him just as the gods consecrated the thousandeyed Indra.

shloka_text: तस्य पाण्डुरमाजह्रुश्छत्रं हेमपरिष्कृतम्4.26.23।। शुक्ले च वालव्यजने हेमदण्डे यशस्करे। तथा सर्वाणि रत्नानि सर्वबीजौषधीरपि4.26.24 सक्षीराणां च वृक्षाणां प्ररोहान्कुसुमानि च। शुक्लानि चैव वस्त्राणि श्वेतं चैवानुलेपनम्4.26.25।। सुगन्धीनि च माल्यानि स्थलजान्यम्बुजानि च। चन्दनानि च दिव्यानि गन्धांश्च विविधान्बहून्4.26.26।। अक्षतं जातरूपं च प्रियङ्गुमधुसर्पिषी। दधि चर्म च वैयाघ्रं वाराही चाप्युपानहौ4.26.27।। समालम्भनमादाय रोचनां समनश्शिलाम्। आग्मुस्तत्र मुदिता वराः कन्यास्तु षोडश4.26.28।।
explanation: The monkeys brought a white canopy decorated with gold and two chamaras with glorious golden staff. They also brought jewels, all kinds of medicinal herbs, sprouts, sap from trees, white flowers and white clothes, unguents, garlands of fragrant lotuses that grow on land and water, heavently sandal, fragrants of different kinds, goldcoloured paddy, honey of priyanga, curds, tiger skin and sandals made of boar skin. Then sixteen beautiful, cheerful females appeared with unguent, gorochana mixed with red arsenic (used for putting tilaka on the forehead).

shloka_text: ततस्ते वानरश्रेष्ठं यथाकालं यथाविधि। रत्नैर्वस्त्रैश्च भक्ष्यैश्च तोषयित्वा द्विजर्षभान्4.26.29।।
explanation: Then they duly propitiated the brahmins, offering them gifts of gems, clothes and eatables.

shloka_text: ततः कुशपरिस्तीर्णं समिद्धं जातवेदसम्। मन्त्रपूतेन हविषा हुत्वा मन्त्रविदो जनाः4.26.30।।
explanation: Then the priests (people who recite Vedic hymns) strew around kusa grass, kindled sacred fire with recitation of mantras and made offerings of havis into the fire.

shloka_text: ततो हेमप्रतिष्ठाने वरास्तरणसंवृते। प्रासादशिखरे रम्ये चित्रमाल्योपशोभिते4.26.31।। प्राङ्मुखं विविधैर्मन्त्रै: स्थापयित्वा वरासने। नदीनदेभ्यस्संहृत्य तीर्थेभ्यश्च समन्ततः4.26.32।। आहृत्य च समुद्रेभ्यस्सर्वेभ्यो वानरर्षभाः। अपः कनककुम्भेषु निधाय विमलाश्शुभाः4.26.33।। शुभैर्वृषभशृङ्गैश्च कलशैश्चापि काञ्चनैः। शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना महर्षिविहितेन च4.26.34।। गजो गवाक्षो गवयश्शरभो गन्धमादनः। मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव हनुमान्जाम्बवान्नलः4.26.35।। अभ्यषिञ्चन्त सुग्रीवं प्रसन्नेन सुगन्धिना। सलिलेन सहस्राक्षं वसवो वासवं यथा4.26.36।।
explanation: Then Sugriva was seated facing the east on a golden throne with fine coverings on top of the mansion decorated with multicoloured garlands. As per tradition, sacred waters  collected from rivers and rivulets and stored in golden pots was aportioned in accordance with the procedure ordained by the sages in sastras. At the appropriate time the pure and fragrant water was poured by Gaja, Gavaya, Sarabha, Mainda, Dvivida, Hanumanta, Jambavan and Nala on Sugriva, the bull among monkeys through horns of bulls and jars of gold, like the eight Vasus bathed the thousandeyed Indra. Thus they performed the consecration.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु सुग्रीवे सर्वे वानरपुङ्गवाः। प्रचुक्रुशुर्महात्मानो हृष्टा स्तत्र सहस्रशः 4.26.37।।
explanation: As Sugriva was ceremoniously consecrated, thousands of monkeys rejoiced and shrieked out of joy.

shloka_text: रामस्य तु वचः कुर्वन्सुग्रीवो हरिपुङ्गवः। अङ्गदं सम्परिष्वज्य यौवराज्येऽभ्यषेचयत्4.26.38।।
explanation: In obedience to Rama's instruction, Sugriva, lord of the monkeys installed Angada as prince regent and embraced him.

shloka_text: अङ्गदे चाभिषिक्ते तु सानुक्रोशाः प्लवङ्गमाः। साधु साध्विति सुग्रीवं महात्मानोऽभ्यपूजयन्4.26.39।।
explanation: The great monkeys concerned hailed Sugriva's action  saying, 'well done, well done' on the installation of Angada.

shloka_text: रामं चैव महात्मानं लक्ष्मणं च पुनः पुनः। प्रीताश्च तुष्टुवुस्सर्वे तादृशे तत्र वर्तिते4.26.40।।
explanation: As Sugriva and Angada were installed, all the monkeys were highly pleased and praised the noblehearted Rama and Lakshmana again and again.

shloka_text: हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा पताकाध्वजशोभिता। बभूव नगरी रम्या किष्किन्धा गिरिगह्वरे4.26.41।।
explanation: The beautiful city of Kishkinda situated in a mountaincave, decorated with banners and flags was filled with happy, wellfed citizens.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु सुग्रीवे प्रविष्टे वानरे गुहाम्। आजगाम सह भ्रात्रा रामः प्रस्रवणं गिरिम्4.27.1।।
explanation: After the consecration, Sugriva entered the cavecity (of Kishkinda) and Rama accompanied by his brother reached mountain Prasravana.

shloka_text: शार्दूलमृगसङ्घुष्टं सिंहैर्भीमरवैर्वृतम्। नानागुल्मलतागूढं बहुपादपसङ्कुलम्4.27.2।। ऋक्षवानरगोपुच्छैर्मार्जारैश्च निषेवितम्। मेघराशिनिभं शैलं नित्यं शुचिजलाशयम्।।4.27.3।।
explanation: The (Prasravana) mountain reverberated with the terrific roars of tigers and deer and lions. There were several kinds of shrubs, creepers and trees.It was inhabited by bears, apes, monkeys and wild cats in large number. The mountain was like a huge cluster of clouds. The waters in the ponds were pure.

shloka_text: शार्दूलमृगसङ्घुष्टं सिंहैर्भीमरवैर्वृतम्। नानागुल्मलतागूढं बहुपादपसङ्कुलम्4.27.2।। ऋक्षवानरगोपुच्छैर्मार्जारैश्च निषेवितम्। मेघराशिनिभं शैलं नित्यं शुचिजलाशयम्।।4.27.3।।

shloka_text: तस्य शैलस्य शिखरे महतीमायतां गुहाम्। प्रत्यगृह्णत वासार्थं रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह4.27.4।।
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana decided to reside in the long, wide cave on top of the great mountain.

shloka_text: कृत्वा च समयं रामस्सुग्रीवेण सहानघः। कालयुक्तं महद्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः4.27.5।। विनीतं भ्रातरं भ्राता लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्।
explanation: Sinless Rama, the delight of the Raghus made an agreement with Sugriva and then spoke appropriately to Lakshmana, his obedient brother and enhancer of glory:

shloka_text: इयं गिरिगुहा रम्या विशाला युक्तमारुता। अस्यां वत्स्याम सौमित्रे वर्षरात्रमरिन्दम4.27.6।।
explanation: 'O Saumitri, subduer of enemies this beautiful mountain cave is spacious and  adequately ventilated. We will reside here in the rainy season.

shloka_text: गिरिशृङ्गमिदं रम्यमुन्नतं पार्थिवात्मज4.27.7।। श्वेताभिः कृष्णताम्राभिश्शिलाभिरुपशोभितम्। नानाधातुसमाकीर्णं दरीनिर्झरशोभितम्4.27.8।। विविधैर्वृक्षषण्डैश्च चारुचित्रलतायुतम्। नानाविहगसङ्घुष्टं मयूररवनादितम्4.27.9।। मालतीकुन्दगुल्मैश्च सिन्धुवारैश्शिरीषकैः। कदम्बार्जुनसर्जैश्च पुष्पितैरुपशोभितम्4.27.10।।
explanation: 'O prince this lovely mountain peak is lofty. It has white, black and red stones with many kinds of minerals scattered all over. It is delightful with caves and streams, and various clusters of trees and variegated vines. The chirps of several kinds of birds as well as the sounds of excellent peacocks are heard here. This place is delightful with bushes of jasmine, kunda and sindhuvara, sireeshaka, kadamba, arjuna and sarja in bloom.
