The trees were huge like dark clouds, cool and shady with wonderful flowers in full bloom, the riches gifted by Indra, were delightful. The entrance was guarded by mighty monkeys holding weapons in hand. It had a golden archway at the entrance decorated with wonderful garlands and strings of golden flowers. Saumitri of great prowess entered the rich abode of Sugriva just as the Sun enters huge clouds unobstructed.

shloka_text: स सप्त कक्ष्या धर्मात्मा नानाजनसमाकुलाः। प्रविश्य सुमहद्गगुप्तं ददर्शान्तःपुरं महत्।।4.33.19।। हैमराजतपर्यङ्कैर्बहुभिश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैस्तत्र तत्रोपशोभितम्।।4.33.20।।
explanation: Righteous Lakshmana crossed the seven enclosures filled with different kinds of people and saw a great harem full of several bright gold and silver cots, excellent  seats here and there with best of cushions spread.

shloka_text: स सप्त कक्ष्या धर्मात्मा नानाजनसमाकुलाः। प्रविश्य सुमहद्गगुप्तं ददर्शान्तःपुरं महत्।।4.33.19।। हैमराजतपर्यङ्कैर्बहुभिश्च वरासनैः। महार्हास्तरणोपेतैस्तत्र तत्रोपशोभितम्।।4.33.20।।
explanation: Righteous Lakshmana crossed the seven enclosures filled with different kinds of people and saw a great harem full of several bright gold and silver cots, excellent  seats here and there with best of cushions spread.

shloka_text: प्रविशन्नेव सततं शुश्राव मधुरस्वरम्। तन्त्रीगीतसमाकीर्णं समगीतपदाक्षरम्।।4.33.21।।
explanation: As he entered, he heard melodious sounds of string instruments and music worded to metre with different kinds of tunes.

shloka_text: बह्वीश्च विविधाकारा रूपयौवनगर्विताः। स्त्रियस्सुग्रीवभवने ददर्श सुमहाबलः।।4.33.22।।
explanation: Powerful Lakshmana saw many females of different forms proud of their youth and charm at the palace of Sugriva.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वाऽभिजनसम्पन्नाश्चित्रमाल्यकृतस्रजः। फलमाल्यकृतव्यग्रा भूषणोत्तमभूषिताः।।4.33.23।। नातृप्तान्नापि चाव्यग्रान्नानुदात्तपरिच्छदान्। सुग्रीवानुचरांश्चापि लक्षयामास लक्ष्मणः।।4.33.24।।
explanation: Lakshmana saw women with a good lineage adorned with colourful flower garlands and choicest ornaments engaged in making garlands and arranging fruits. He also saw at Sugriva's palace attendants, gentle, welldressed, contented and not too busy.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वाऽभिजनसम्पन्नाश्चित्रमाल्यकृतस्रजः। फलमाल्यकृतव्यग्रा भूषणोत्तमभूषिताः।।4.33.23।। नातृप्तान्नापि चाव्यग्रान्नानुदात्तपरिच्छदान्। सुग्रीवानुचरांश्चापि लक्षयामास लक्ष्मणः।।4.33.24।।
explanation: Lakshmana saw women with a good lineage adorned with colourful flower garlands and choicest ornaments engaged in making garlands and arranging fruits. He also saw at Sugriva's palace attendants, gentle, welldressed, contented and not too busy.

shloka_text: कूजितं नूपुराणां च काञ्चीनां निनदं तथा। सन्निशम्य तत श्रीमान्सौमित्रिर्लज्जितोऽभवत्।।4.33.25।।
explanation: Illustrious Lakshmana felt abashed on hearing the jingling of girdle bells and tinkling of the women's anklets.

shloka_text: रोषवेगप्रकुपितशश्रुत्वा चाभरणस्वनम्। चकार ज्यास्वनं वीरो दिशश्शब्देन पूरयन्।।4.33.26।।
explanation: On hearing the sounds of ornaments (of females), heroic Lakshmana lost his temper quickly. He pulled his bowstring forcefully in wrath producing frightening sound filling all quarters.

shloka_text: चारित्रेण महाबाहुरपकृष्ट स्सलक्ष्मणः। तस्थावेकान्तमाश्रित्य रामकोपसमन्वितः।।4.33.27।।
explanation: Aware of the anger of Rama (who likes it not), the longarmed Lakshmana moved away from the spot (abstained from entering private apartments) as per tradition, receded to a lonely place and stood.

shloka_text: तेन चापस्वनेनाथ सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। विज्ञायाऽगमनं त्रस्त स्सञ्चचाल वरासनात्।।4.33.28।।
explanation: Then, sensing the arrival of Lakshmana, by the sound of his bow string, Sugriva the lord of vanaras, alighted at once from the throne.

shloka_text: अङ्गदेन यथा मह्यं पुरस्तात्प्रतिवेदितम्। सुव्यक्तमेष सम्प्राप्त स्सौमित्रिर्भ्रातृवत्सलः।।4.33.29।।
explanation: 'Truly Saumitri, the loving brother of Rama has arrived as announced by Angada earlier'.

shloka_text: अङ्गदेन समाख्यातं ज्यास्वनेन च वानरः। बुबुधे लक्ष्मणं प्राप्तं मुखं चास्यव्यशुष्यत।।4.33.30।।
explanation: As proclaimed by Angada and also from the sound of the twang, Sugriva knew about the arrival of Lakshmana. His mouth parched (with fear).

shloka_text: ततस्तारां हरिश्रेष्ठस्सुग्रीवः प्रियदर्शनाम्। उवाच हितमव्यग्रस्त्रास सम्भ्रान्तमानसः।।4.33.31।।
explanation: Then Sugriva, the best of monkeys got agitated at heart out of fear. He saw the pleasing Tara and said to her these good words clearly:

shloka_text: किन्नु तत्कारणं सुभ्रु प्रकृत्या मृदुमानसः। सरोष इव सम्प्राप्तो येनायं राघवानुजः।।4.33.32।।
explanation: 'O Tara with beautiful eyebrows this younger brother of Rama is normally softhearted. But today he arrived here angry. What could be the reason?

shloka_text: किं पश्यसि कुमारस्य रोषस्थानमनिन्दिते। न खल्वकारणे कोपमाहरेन्नरसत्तमः।।4.33.33।।
explanation: 'O blemishless Tara  What is the cause of young Lakshmana's anger? Great men do not display anger without reason.

shloka_text: यदस्य कृतमस्माभिर्बुध्यसे किञ्चिदप्रियम्। तदबुद्ध्या सम्प्रधार्याशु क्षिप्रमर्हसि भाषितुम्।।4.33.34।।
explanation: 'If anything displeasing has been done by us, you should know and tell me quickly. You ought to speak to him at once.

shloka_text: अथवा स्वयमेवैनं द्रष्टुमर्हसि भामिनि। वचनै स्सान्त्वयुक्तैश्च प्रसादयितुमर्हसि।।4.33.35।।
explanation: 'O lovely lady or else, you should see him personally and propitiate him with your soothing words.

shloka_text: त्वद्दर्शन विशुद्धात्मा न स कोपं करिष्यति। न हि स्त्रीषु महात्मानः क्वचित्कुर्वन्ति दारुणम्।।4.33.36।।
explanation: 'Lakshmana will be clear of all doubts on seeing you and will not be angry. Great men are not harsh to women.

shloka_text: त्वया सान्त्वैरुपक्रान्तं प्रसन्नेन्द्रियमानसम्। ततः कमलपत्राक्षं द्रक्ष्याम्यहमरिन्दमम्।।4.33.37।।
explanation: 'Start talking to him with pleasing words and make him happy. Then I shall see Lakshmana with eyes like lotuspetals, a subduer of enemies'.

shloka_text: सा प्रस्खलन्ती मदविह्वलाक्षी प्रलम्बकाञ्चीगुण हेमसूत्रा। सलक्षणा लक्ष्मणसन्निधानं जगाम तारा नमिताङ्गयष्टिः।।4.33.38।।
explanation: Tara, whose eyes were drowsy with drink, whose long gold string of the girdle was hanging loose appeared before Lakshmana with faltering steps and bent low, bashful of her appearance. (It suggests a state of exhaustion after sexual pleasures).

shloka_text: स तां समीक्ष्यैव हरीशपन्तीं तस्थावुदासीनतया महात्मा। अवाङ्मुखोऽभून्मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रः स्त्रीसन्निकर्षाद्विनिवृत्तकोपः।।4.33.39।।
explanation: Since prince Lakshmana is a great man, he stood with his face down and showing no reaction, controlled his anger due to the presence of a female standing close by.

shloka_text: सा पानयोगाद्विनिवृत्तलज्जा दृष्टिप्रसादाच्च नरेन्द्रसूनोः। उवाच तारा प्रणयप्रगल्भं वाक्यं महार्थं परिसान्त्वपूर्वम्।।4.33.40।।
explanation: Setting aside her shyness for being in a drunken state, and observing Lakshmana's favourable disposition, she spoke meaningful words in a pleasing manner with friendly eloquence:

shloka_text: किं कोपमूलं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्र कस्ते न सन्तिष्ठति वाङ्निदेशे। क श्शुष्कवृक्षं वनमापतन्तं दवाग्निमासीदति निर्विशङ्कः।।4.33.41।।
explanation: 'O noble prince what is the cause of your anger? Who has disrespected your command? Who can approach without fear forest fire rushing towards a thicket of dried pieces of wood?'

shloka_text: स तस्या वचनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वपूर्वमशङ्कितम्। भूयः प्रणयदृष्टार्थं लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।4.33.42।।
explanation: Having heard Tara's unhesitant submission spoken in a pleasant and friendly manner, Lakshmana replied:

shloka_text: किमयं कामवृत्तस्ते लुप्तधर्मार्थसङ्ग्रहः। भर्ता भर्तृहिते युक्ते न चैनमवबुद्ध्यसे।।4.33.43।।
explanation: 'O lady, your husband engrossed in sensual pleasures, has lost sight of dharma and artha. Why don't you understand it in the interest of your husband whose wellwisher you are?

shloka_text: न चिन्तयति राज्यार्थं नास्मान् शोकपरायणान्। सामात्यपरिषत्तारे पानमेवोपसेवते।।4.33.44।।
explanation: 'O Tara that we are in grief Sugriva does not realize. He is not attending to state affairs. He is only enjoying drinking in the company of ministers.

shloka_text: स मासांश्चतुरः कृत्वा प्रमाणं प्लवगेश्वरः। व्यतीतां स्तान्मदव्यग्रो विहरन्नावबुध्यते।।4.33.45।।
explanation: 'The king of monkeys has already spent four months, enjoying drinks. He does not realize that he has flouted his promise.

shloka_text: न हि धर्मार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं पानमेवं प्रशस्यते। पानादर्थश्च धर्मश्च कामश्च परिहीयते।।4.33.46।।
explanation: 'Drinking this way does not help accomplishment of dharma and artha. It destroys wealth, ambition and righteousness.

shloka_text: धर्मलोपो महांस्तावत्कृते ह्यप्रतिकुर्वतः। अर्थलोपश्च मित्रस्य नाशे गुणवतो महान्।।4.33.47।।
explanation: 'Dharma is violated when we help not one who has helped. Loss of a virtuous friend leads to great loss of wealth. It results in destruction.

shloka_text: मित्रं ह्यर्थगुणश्रेष्ठं सत्यधर्मपरायणम्। तद्द्वयं तु परित्यक्तं न तु धर्मे व्यवस्थितम्।।4.33.48।।
explanation: A friend is indeed foremost in virtues and benefits, devoted to truth and righteousness. But if these two are abandoned, one is not established in righteousness.

shloka_text: तदेवं प्रस्तुते कार्ये कार्यमस्माभिरुत्तरम्। यत्कार्यं कार्यतत्त्वज्ञे तदुदाहर्तुमर्हसि।।4.33.49।।
explanation: 'You have a strong sense of duty. You ought to tell him his duty and what we should do in this situation.

shloka_text: सा तस्य धर्मार्थसमाधियुक्तं निशम्य वाक्यं मधुरस्वभावम्। तारा गतार्थे मनुजेन्द्रकार्ये विश्वासयुक्तं तमुवाच भूयः।।4.33.50।।
explanation: Tara heard the sweet words of Lakshmana which showed his good understanding of dharma and artha. What she said to him in reply reflects her faith in Sugriva's effort to help Rama's cause:

shloka_text: न कोपकालः क्षितिपालपुत्र न चाति कोप स्स्वजने विधेयः। त्वदर्थकामस्य जनस्य तस्य प्रमादमप्यर्हसि वीर सोढुम्।।4.33.51।।
explanation: 'O prince this is not the time to get angry with your own people. He (Sugriva) is your friend and wishes to do your work. You should bear with him even if he makes a mistake.

shloka_text: कोपं कथं नाम गुणप्रकृष्टः कुमार कुर्यादपकृष्टसत्त्वे। कस्त्वद्विधः कोपवशं हि गच्छे त्सत्त्वावरुद्धस्तपसः प्रसूतिः।।4.33.52।।
explanation: 'O prince how can you, richly endowed with virtues be angry with an inferior person? How can a person like you, preeminent in virtues,and a source of great penance fall a victim to anger?

shloka_text: जानामि रोषं हरिवीरबन्धो र्जानामि कार्यस्य च कालसङ्गम्। जानामि कार्यं त्वयि यत्कृतं न स्तच्चापि जानामि यदत्र कार्यम्।।4.33.53।।
explanation: 'I know about the anger of (Rama), the friend of Sugriva. I am aware of the time limit set for his work. I am aware of our omissions in this regard. I also know about the mission.

shloka_text: तच्चापि जानामि यथविषह्यं बलं नरश्रेष्ठ शरीरजस्य। जानामि यस्मिंश्च जनेऽवबद्धं कामेन सुग्रीवमसक्तमद्य।।4.33.54।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana I am aware of the irresistible strength of lust born out of the body. I am aware of Sugriva's indifference to his duty due to his  passion with whomsoever it be.

shloka_text: न कामतन्त्रे तव बुद्धिरस्ति त्वं वै यथा मन्युवशं प्रपन्नः। न देशकालौ हि न चार्थधर्मा ववेक्षते कामरतिर्मनुष्यः।।4.33.55।।
explanation: 'You are under the grip of anger and your mind is not involved in carnal desire. One who is engaged in sensual pleasures does not reckon time and place, nor does he consider artha and dharma.

shloka_text: तं कामवृत्तं मम सन्निकृष्टं कामाभियोगाच्च निवृत्तलज्जम्। क्षमस्व तावत्परवीरहन्त स्त्वद्भ्रातरं वानरवंशनाथम्।।4.33.56।।
explanation: 'O slayer of enemy heroes pardon Sugriva, the lord of vanara clan, who is to you a brother. He is here indulging in sports of love with me. He has no sense of shame about his passion.

shloka_text: महर्षयो धर्मतपोऽभिकामाः कामानुकामाः प्रतिबद्धमोहाः। अयं प्रकृत्या चपलः कपिस्तु कथं न सज्जेत सुखेषु राजा।।4.33.57।।
explanation: 'Even sages committed to piety and austerity are sometimes deluded by sensual gratification. He is a king and a monkey who is fickle by nature. How can he be not tempted by sensual pleasures'?

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महार्थं सा वानरी लक्ष्मणमप्रमेयम्। पुन स्सखेदं मदविह्वलञ्च भर्तुर्हितं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे।।4.33.58।।
explanation: Overcome by drunkenness, Tara once again spoke to Lakshmana of unfathomable prowess, in a meaningful way keeping in view the welfare of her playful and drunken lord:

shloka_text: उद्योगस्तु चिराज्ञप्त स्सुग्रीवेण नरोत्तम। कामस्यापि विधेयेन तवार्थप्रतिसाधने।।4.33.59।।
explanation: 'O best of men although overpowered by sense pleasures, Sugriva has already initiated efforts for the accomplishment of your work.

shloka_text: आगता हि महावीर्या हरयः कामरूपिणः। कोटीशतसहस्राणि नानानगनिवासिनः।।4.33.60।।
explanation: 'O great warrior monkeys residing at different mountains who can assume any form they like have arrived in hundreds and thousands of crores.

shloka_text: तदागच्छ महाबाहो चारित्रं रक्षितं त्वया। अच्छलं मित्रभावेन सतां दारावलोकनम्।।4.33.61।।
explanation: 'O longarmed one  come in. You have been standing out guarding your character. It is not a mistake to see the wife of a pious person with a friendly feeling.

shloka_text: तारया चाभ्यनुज्ञातस्त्वरया चापि चोदितः। प्रविवेश महाबाहुरभ्यन्तरमरिन्दमः।।4.33.62।।
explanation: Strongarmed Lakshmana, a subduer of enemies, permitted by Tara entered the harem immediately (thinking of the urgency of the task).

shloka_text: तत स्सुग्रीवमासीनं काञ्चने परमासने। महार्हास्तरणोपेते ददर्शादित्यसन्निभम्।।4.33.63।। दिव्याभणचित्राङ्गं दिव्यरूपं यशस्विनम्। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं महेन्द्रमिव दुर्जयम्।।4.33.64।। दिव्याभरणमालाभिः प्रमदाभि स्समावृतम्। संरब्धतररक्ताक्षो बभूवान्तकसन्निभः।।4.33.65।।
explanation: Lakshmana saw famous Sugriva, difficult to be conquered, seated on a golden throne strewn around with cushions, decorated with ornaments of different colours, endearing in appearance, decked with beautiful garlands and clothes. He was surrounded by women adorned with most fascinating ornaments and garlands. Bewildered at the sight, Lakshmana's eyes turned red in anger. He appeared like Yama, lord of death.

shloka_text: तत स्सुग्रीवमासीनं काञ्चने परमासने। महार्हास्तरणोपेते ददर्शादित्यसन्निभम्।।4.33.63।। दिव्याभणचित्राङ्गं दिव्यरूपं यशस्विनम्। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं महेन्द्रमिव दुर्जयम्।।4.33.64।। दिव्याभरणमालाभिः प्रमदाभि स्समावृतम्। संरब्धतररक्ताक्षो बभूवान्तकसन्निभः।।4.33.65।।
explanation: Lakshmana saw famous Sugriva, difficult to be conquered, seated on a golden throne strewn around with cushions, decorated with ornaments of different colours, endearing in appearance, decked with beautiful garlands and clothes. He was surrounded by women adorned with most fascinating ornaments and garlands. Bewildered at the sight, Lakshmana's eyes turned red in anger. He appeared like Yama, lord of death.

shloka_text: तत स्सुग्रीवमासीनं काञ्चने परमासने। महार्हास्तरणोपेते ददर्शादित्यसन्निभम्।।4.33.63।। दिव्याभणचित्राङ्गं दिव्यरूपं यशस्विनम्। दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं महेन्द्रमिव दुर्जयम्।।4.33.64।। दिव्याभरणमालाभिः प्रमदाभि स्समावृतम्। संरब्धतररक्ताक्षो बभूवान्तकसन्निभः।।4.33.65।।
explanation: Lakshmana saw famous Sugriva, difficult to be conquered, seated on a golden throne strewn around with cushions, decorated with ornaments of different colours, endearing in appearance, decked with beautiful garlands and clothes. He was surrounded by women adorned with most fascinating ornaments and garlands. Bewildered at the sight, Lakshmana's eyes turned red in anger. He appeared like Yama, lord of death.

shloka_text: तमप्रतिहतं क्रुद्धं प्रविष्टं पुरुषर्षभम्। सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रियः।।4.34.1।।
explanation: On seeing the angry Lakshmana, a bull among men, who could not be obstructed,  enter in,  Sugriva was disturbed.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धं निश्श्वसमानं तं प्रदीप्तमिव तेजसा। भ्रातुर्व्यसनसन्तप्तं दृष्ट्वा दशरथात्मजम्।।4.34.2।। उत्पपात हरिश्रेष्ठो हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम्। महान्महेन्द्रस्य यथा स्वलङ्कृत इव ध्वजः।।4.34.3।।
explanation: Seeing enraged Lakshmana, son of Dasaratha, sighing heavily, glowing like bright fire burning with the sorrow of Rama, Sugriva jumped out of his seat quitting the decorated golden throne just as Indra's decorated banner is raised up suddenly.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धं निश्श्वसमानं तं प्रदीप्तमिव तेजसा। भ्रातुर्व्यसनसन्तप्तं दृष्ट्वा दशरथात्मजम्।।4.34.2।। उत्पपात हरिश्रेष्ठो हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम्। महान्महेन्द्रस्य यथा स्वलङ्कृत इव ध्वजः।।4.34.3।।
explanation: Seeing enraged Lakshmana, son of Dasaratha, sighing heavily, glowing like bright fire burning with the sorrow of Rama, Sugriva jumped out of his seat quitting the decorated golden throne just as Indra's decorated banner is raised up suddenly.

shloka_text: उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतू रुमाप्रभृतयः स्त्रियः। सुग्रीवं गगने पूर्णचन्द्रं तारागणा इव।।4.34.4।।
explanation: As soon as Sugriva jumped up ,Ruma and other womenfolk rose to their feet like the clusters of stars around the fullMoon in the sky.

shloka_text: संरक्तनयनः श्रीमान्विचचाल कृताञ्जलिः। बभूवावस्थितस्तत्र कल्पवृक्षो महानिव।।4.34.5।।
explanation: With eyes red as blood through drunkenness,prosperous Sugriva was shaken like the Kalpa tree.He stood there and offered salutations(to Lakshmana) with folded hands.

shloka_text: रुमाद्वितीयं सुग्रीवं नारीमध्यगतं स्थितम्। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धस्सतारं शशिनं यथा।।4.34.6।।
explanation: Looking at Sugriva surrounded by Ruma and other women like the Moon among stars, infuriated Lakshmana said

shloka_text: सत्त्वाभिजनसम्पन्नस्सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रियः। कृतज्ञस्सत्यवादी च राजा लोके महीयते।।4.34.7।।
explanation: 'Only a king who is an heir to a noble family, compassionate, and selfcontrolled, grateful and truthful excels in the world.

shloka_text: यस्तु राजा स्थितोऽधर्मे मित्राणामुपकारिणाम्। मिथ्या प्रतिज्ञां कुरुते को नृशंसतरस्ततः।।4.34.8।।
explanation: 'Which king can be more malicious than the one who makes false promises and adopts an unrighteous path towards those who helped him?

shloka_text: शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं तु गवानृते। आत्मानं स्वजनं हन्ति पुरुषः पुरुषानृते।।4.34.9।।
explanation: 'If a man tells a lie about a horse, he commits the sin of killing a hundred horses. If one tells a lie about a cow, he shares the sin of killing a thousand cows. If one tells a lie about a man, it is equal to the sin of killing oneself and his own people.

shloka_text: पूर्वं कृतार्थो मित्राणां न तत्प्रतिकरोति यः। कृतघ्नस्सर्वभूतानां स वध्यः प्लवगेश्वर।।4.34.10।।
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys he who, having accomplished his task first with the help of his friend, does not return the help is ungrateful. Such a person deserves to be killed.It applies to all beings.

shloka_text: गीतोऽयं ब्रह्मणा श्लोक स्सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः। दृष्ट्वा कृतघ्नं क्रुद्धेन तन्निबोध प्लवङ्गम।।4.34.11।।
explanation: 'O lord of the monkeys here is a verse worthy of appreciation by all the worlds, sung by a brahmin, when he saw an ungrateful person. Listen:

shloka_text: ब्रह्मघ्ने च सुरापे च चोरे भग्नव्रते तथा। निष्कृतिर्विहिता सद्भि: कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः।।4.34.12।।
explanation: 'There is expiation for one who kills a brahmin, a drunkard, a thief and a violator of sacred vows. But there is no atonement for an ungrateful man.'

shloka_text: अनार्यस्त्वं कृतघ्नश्च मिथ्यावादी च वानर। पूर्वं कृतार्थो रामस्य न तत्प्रतिकरोषि यत्।।4.34.13।।
explanation: 'O monkey you have already achieved your objective (with the help of Rama) but have not helped Rama in return. You are surely an ignoble and ungrateful liar.

shloka_text: ननु नाम कृतार्थेन त्वया रामस्य वानर। सीताया मार्गणे यत्नः कर्तव्यः कृतमिच्छता।।4.34.14।।
explanation: 'O monkey, if you are grateful to Rama you should wish to search for Sita. Indeed, you should make efforts to take it up.

shloka_text: स त्वं ग्राम्येषु भोगेषु सक्तो मिथ्याप्रतिश्रवः। न त्वां रामो विजानीते सर्पं मण्डूकराविणम्।।4.34.15।।
explanation: 'You have failed to keep your word. You are engaged in worldly pleasures. Rama did not know that you are a serpent croaking like a frog.

shloka_text: महाभागेन रामेण पापः करुणवेदिना। हरीणां प्रापितो राज्यं त्वं दुरात्मा महात्मना।।4.34.16।।
explanation: 'Rama is illustrious, compassionate and great. He has granted the kingdom to you, to one who is a sinner and an evilminded person.

shloka_text: कृतं चेन्नाभिजानीषे रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। सद्यस्त्वं निशितैर्भावार्हतो द्रक्ष्यसि वालिनम्।।4.34.17।।
explanation: 'If you do not recognise  the help of Rama who can accomplish any deed with ease, you will be killed with my sharp arrows and meet Vali (in heaven).

shloka_text: न च सङ्कुचितः पन्था येन वाली हतो गतः। समये तिष्ठ सुग्रीव मा वालिपथमन्वगाः।।4.34.18।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva the path by which Vali went is not closed.I wish you do not follow him. You stand by the promise made.

shloka_text: न नूनमिक्ष्वाकुवरस्य कार्मुक च्युतान् शरान्पश्यसि वज्र सन्निभान्। तत स्सुखं नाम निषेवसे सुखी। न रामकार्यं मनसाऽप्यवेक्षसे।।4.34.19।।
explanation: 'You have not seen the thunderboltlike arrows released from the bow of Rama, the renowned prince of the Ikshvaku race. Therefore you are resorting to enjoyment without any fear and have not given thought to Rama's work.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfourth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवाणं सौमित्रिं प्रदीप्तमिव तेजसा। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं तारा ताराधिपनिभानना।।4.35.1।।
explanation: While Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, was glowing like fire with his brilliance, thus spoke the moonfaced Tara:

shloka_text: नैवं लक्ष्मण वक्तव्यो नायं परुषमर्हति। हरीणामीश्वरश्श्रोतुं तव वक्त्राद्विशेषतः।।4.35.2।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana you, in particular, should not speak to the king of vanaras in that manner. He does not deserve to hear from your mouth words which are harsh.

shloka_text: नैवाकृतज्ञस्सुग्रीवो न शठो नापि दारुणः। नैवानृतकथो वीर न जिह्मश्च कपीश्वरः।।4.35.3।।
explanation: 'O hero Sugriva, king of monkeys, is not ungrateful or deceitful, He is neither crooked nor false.

shloka_text: उपकारं कृतं वीरो नाप्ययं विस्मृतः कपिः। रामेण वीर सुग्रीवो यदन्यैर्दुष्करं रणे।।4.35.4।।
explanation: 'O hero this warrior Sugriva has not forgotten the help rendered by Rama in combat which was difficult (to win).

shloka_text: रामप्रसादात्कीर्तिञ्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। प्राप्तवानिह सुग्रीवो रुमां मां च परन्तप ।।4.35.5।।
explanation: 'O scorcher of enemies it is by Rama's grace that Sugriva has attained fame, the kingdom of monkeys and Ruma and me.

shloka_text: सुदुःखं शयितः पूर्वं प्राप्येदं सुखमुत्तमम्। प्राप्तकालं न जानीते विश्वामित्रो यथा मुनिः।।4.35.6।।
explanation: 'Sleep did not come to him in deep distress in the past, and now that great happiness has come, he does not realize that it is time to act (search for Sita). He behaves like sage Viswamitra.

shloka_text: घृताच्यां किल संसक्तो दशवर्षाणि लक्ष्मण। अहोऽमन्यत धर्मात्मा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः।।4.35.7।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana great sage Visvamitra was in union with an apsara Gritachi for ten years and felt it was just one day indeed

shloka_text: स हि प्राप्तं न जानीते कालं कालविदां वरः। विश्वामित्रो महातेजाः किं पुनर्यः पृथग्जनः।।4.35.8।।
explanation: 'If the brilliant and the most distinguished of those who knew the value of time did not realise the passing of time, what can be said of an ordinary person?

shloka_text: देहधर्मं गतस्यास्य परिश्रान्तस्य लक्ष्मण। अवितृप्तस्य कामेषु कामं क्षन्तुमिहार्हसि।।4.35.9।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana you should pardon him since he is not yet satisfied, though tired, with the struggle for the fulfilment of his sensual pleasures.

shloka_text: न च रोषवशं तात गन्तुमर्हसि लक्ष्मण। निश्चयार्थमविज्ञाय सहसा प्राकृतो यथा।।4.35.10।।
explanation: 'O dear Lakshmana not knowing the true intention of Sugriva, it is not proper for you to be rashly angry like an ordinary man.

shloka_text: सत्त्वयुक्ता हि पुरुषास्त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभ। अविमृश्य न रोषस्य सहसा यान्ति वश्यताम्।।4.35.11।।
explanation: 'O bull among men men with right vision like you do not become angry instantly without right thinking.

shloka_text: प्रसादये त्वां धर्मज्ञ सुग्रीवार्थे समाहिता। महान्रोषसमुत्पन्न स्संरम्भस्त्यज्यतामयम्।।4.35.12।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana, knower of dharma, give up your agitation arising out of great anger. Be composed for the sake of Sugriva.

shloka_text: रुमां मां कपि राज्यं च धनधान्यवसूनि च। रामप्रियार्थं सुग्रीवस्त्यजेदिति मतिर्मम।।4.35.13।।
explanation: 'I feel Sugriva should (is prepared to) renounce the monkeykingdom, wealth, grains and other treasures and even Ruma and me for the pleasure of Rama.

shloka_text: समानेष्यति सुग्रीव स्सीतया सह राघवम्। शशाङ्कमिव रोहिण्या निहत्वा रावणं रणे।।4.35.14।।
explanation: 'Killing Ravana in war, Sugriva will restore Sita soon to Rama.Rama will join Sita like Moon joins Rohini.

shloka_text: शतकोटिसहस्राणि लङ्कायां किल राक्षसाः। आयुतानि च षट्त्रिंशत्सहस्राणि शतानि च।।4.35.15।।
explanation: 'The number of demons in Lanka is reported to be a hundred thousand crore, three lakh, ninetynine thousand and six hundred. (Note: Indian tradition has numbers up to eighteen digits. One hundred thousand crores is equal to a 'mahapadma' which has thirteen digits. The number described here is 1000000399600.)

shloka_text: अहत्वा तांश्च दुर्धर्षान्राक्षसान्कामरूपिणः। न शक्यो रावणो हन्तुं येन सा मैथिली हृता।।4.35.16।।
explanation: 'It is not possible to kill Ravana who has stolen Sita without killing those unassailable demons who can assume any form at their will.

shloka_text: ते न शक्या रणे हन्तुमसहायेन लक्ष्मण। रावणः क्रूरकर्मा च सुग्रीवेण विशेषतः।।4.35.17।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana moreover it is not possible for Sugriva alone to kill the wicked Ravana without the help of the monkeys.

shloka_text: एवमाख्यातवान्वाली स ह्यभिज्ञो हरीश्वरः। आगमस्तु न मे व्यक्तश्श्रवात्तस्माद्ब्रवीम्यहम्।।4.35.18।।
explanation: Vali, the wellinformed lord of the monkeys, has given an account of the demons. The source of the account is not known to me.Therefore I am speaking from what I have heard.

shloka_text: त्वत्सहायनिमित्तं वै प्रेषिता हरिपुङ्गवाः। आनेतुं वानरान्युद्धे सुबहून्हरियूधपान्।।4.35.19।।
explanation: 'Monkey chiefs have been sent to bring multitudes of monkey leaders to help you in the battle.

shloka_text: तांश्च प्रतीक्षमाणोऽयं विक्रान्तात्सुमहाबलान्। राघवस्यार्थसिध्यर्थं न निर्याति हरीश्वरः।।4.35.20।।
explanation: 'Sugriva is awaiting the arrival of the powerful and strong vanaras without whose help he cannot accomplish Rama's task.Therefore he has not yet started (the search).

shloka_text: कृता तु संस्था सौमित्रे सुग्रीवेण पुरा यथा। अद्य तैर्वानरैस्सर्वैरागन्तव्यं महाबलैः।।4.35.21।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana since Sugriva has already promulgated an ordinance to all the mighty vanaras, they should be all arriving by now.

shloka_text: ऋक्षकोटिसहस्राणि गोलाङ्गूलशतानि च। अद्य त्वामुपयास्यन्ति जहि कोपमरिन्दम। कोट्योऽनेकास्तु काकुत्स्थ कपीनां दीप्ततेजसाम्।।4.35.22।।
explanation: Thousands of crores of bears and hundreds of langurs will come to you today. Abandon your anger, O vanquisher of foes. O Kakutstha, there are also many crores of monkeys of blazing might.

shloka_text: तव हि मुखमिदं निरीक्ष्य कोपात् क्षतजनिभे नयने निरीक्षमाणाः। हरिवरवनिता न यान्ति शान्तिं प्रथमभयस्य हि शङ्कितास्तु सर्वाः।।4.35.23।।
explanation: 'Looking at your angry countenance with bloodred eyes, the wives of  the foremost of monkeys are frightened by the possibility of similar danger of the past (of Vali's death) and do not find peace of mind.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyfifth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तस्तारया वाक्यं प्रश्रितं धर्मसंहितम्। मृदुस्वभावस्सौमित्रिः प्रतिजग्राह तद्वचः।।4.36.1।।
explanation: Thus the gentlenatured Saumitri accepted Tara's courteous words sanctioned by dharma.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रतिगृहीते तु वाक्ये हरिगणेश्वरः। लक्ष्मणात्सुमहत्त्रासं वस्त्रं क्लिन्नमिवात्यजत्।।4.36.2।।
explanation: Sugriva, king of the vanara clan, cast aside his great fear when Lakshmana accepted the words of Tara just as one discards a wet garment from the body.

shloka_text: ततः कण्ठगतं माल्यं चित्रं बहुगुणं महत्। चिच्छेद विमदश्चासीत्सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः।।4.36.3।।
explanation: Thereupon Sugriva, relieved from his drunken state tore off the great, colourful valuable garland worn on his neck.

shloka_text: स लक्ष्मणं भीमबलं सर्ववानरसत्तमः। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सुग्रीव स्सम्प्रहर्षयन्।।4.36.4।।
explanation: Sugriva, the noblest of all monkeys, spoke these polite words in a pleasing manner to Lakshmana of terrific strength:

shloka_text: प्रणष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। रामप्रसादात्सौमित्रे पुन: प्राप्तमिदं मया।।4.36.5।।
explanation: 'O Saumitri my prosperity, fame and the permanent sovereignty of vanaras had been lost. It was  regained by the grace of Rama.

shloka_text: कश्शक्तस्तस्य देवस्य ख्यातस्य स्वेन कर्मणा। तादृशं विक्रमं वीर प्रतिकर्तुमरिन्दम।।4.36.6।।
explanation: 'O crusher of enemies  how is it possible to repay the famous lord Rama's valour (in killing Vali)?

shloka_text: सीतां प्राप्स्यति धर्मात्मा वधिष्यति च रावणम्। सहायमात्रेण मया राघव स्स्वेन तेजसा।।4.36.7।।
explanation: 'Righteous Rama can merely restore Sita with my assistance. By his own fiery energy he will kill Ravana.

shloka_text: सहायकृत्यं किं तस्य येन सप्त महाद्रुमाः। शैलश्च वसुधा चैव बाणेनैकेन दारिताः।।4.36.8।।
explanation: 'Rama shattered seven huge trees, a mountain and earth with a single arrow. What assistance does he need?

shloka_text: धनुर्विष्फारयानस्य यस्य शब्देन लक्ष्मण। सशैला कम्पिता भूमिस्सहायै: किन्नु तस्य वै।।4.36.9।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana the twang of his bow shook even the mountains and the earth. What assistance does he need?

shloka_text: अनुयात्रां नरेन्द्रस्य करिष्येऽहं नरर्षभ। गच्छतो रावणं हन्तुं वैरिणं सपुरस्सरम्।।4.36.10।।
explanation: 'O Lakshmana, bull among men I shall only join him along with others when he leads the army to kill Ravana.

shloka_text: यदि किञ्चिदतिक्रान्तं विश्वासात्प्रणयेन वा। प्रेष्यस्य क्षमितव्यं मे न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति।।4.36.11।।
explanation: 'If I have committed even a little transgression in my faith in Rama or affection for him and exceeded the time limit, my mistakes are to be excused as one would pardons a servant. No one is flawless in the world.'

shloka_text: ति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः। अभवल्लक्ष्मणः प्रीतः प्रेम्णा चैवमुवाच ह।।4.36.12।।
explanation: Lakshmana who was happy to hear great Sugriva replied affectionately:

shloka_text: सर्वथा हि मम भ्राता सनाथो वानरेश्वर। त्वया नाथेन सुग्रीव प्रश्रितेन विशेषतः।।4.36.13।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva, king of monkeys when you are extending due courtesy to my brother,he has a guardian in you by all means.

shloka_text: यस्ते प्रभाव स्सुग्रीव यच्च ते शौचमार्जवम्। अर्हस्त्वं कपिराज्यस्य श्रियं भोक्तुमनुत्तमाम्।।4.36.14।।
explanation: 'You are powerful and straightforward by nature.You are humble and noble. Therefore, you deserve the high prosperity of the kingdom of the monkeys.

shloka_text: सहायेन तु सुग्रीव त्वया रामः प्रतापवान्। वधिष्यति रणे शत्रूनचिरान्नात्र संशयः।।4.36.15।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva with you as associate, valiant hero Rama will kill his enemies in war very soon. There is no doubt about it.

shloka_text: धर्मज्ञस्य कृतज्ञस्य सङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः। उपपन्नं च युक्तं च सुग्रीव तव भाषितम्।।4.36.16।।
explanation: 'O Sugriva you know dharma.You are grateful and will not turn back from the battle. So your words are true and befitting.

shloka_text: दोषज्ञस्सति सामर्थ्ये कोऽन्यो भाषितुमर्हति। वर्जयित्वा मम ज्येष्ठं त्वां च वानरसत्तम।।4.36.17।।
explanation: 'O best of monkeys barring you and my elder brother, who else would be capable of speaking this way about themselves even when you are aware of other's faults?

shloka_text: सदृशश्चासि रामस्य विक्रमेण बलेन च। सहायो दैवतैर्दत्तश्चिराय हरिपुङ्गव।।4.36.18।।
explanation: 'You who are equal to Rama in valour and strength, will continue to be the gift of gods to us for long.

shloka_text: किं तु शीघ्रमितो वीर निष्क्रम त्वं मया सह। सान्त्वयस्व वयस्यं च त्वं भार्याहरणकर्शितम्।।4.36.19।।
explanation: 'Nevertheless I want you to proceed from here with me at once and reassure your friend who is agrieved due to the abduction of his wife.

shloka_text: यच्च शोकाभिभूतस्य श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्। मया त्वं परुषाण्युक्तस्तच्चत्वं क्षन्तु मर्हसि।।4.36.20।।
explanation: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामयणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtysix sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। हनूमन्तं स्थितं पार्श्वे सचिवन्त्विदमब्रवीत्।।4.37.1।।
explanation: Having heard the great Lakshmana Sugriva said to Hanuman, the minister who stood by his side:

shloka_text: महेन्द्रहिमवद्विन्ध्यकैलासशिखरेषु च। मन्दरे पाण्डुशिखरे पञ्चशैलेषु ये स्थिताः।।4.37.2।। तरुणादित्यवर्णेषु भ्राजमानेषु सर्वतः। पर्वतेषु समुद्रान्ते पश्चिमायां च ये दिशि।।4.37.3।। आदित्यभवने चैव गिरौ सन्ध्याभ्रसन्निभे। पद्मातालवनं भीमं संश्रिता हरिपुङ्गवाः।।4.37.4।। अञ्जनाम्बुदसङ्काशाः कुञ्जरप्रतिमौजसः। अञ्जने पर्वते चैव ये वसन्ति प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.37.5।। मनश्शिला गुहावासा वानराः कनकप्रभाः। मेरुपार्श्वगताश्चैव ये धूम्रगिरिं संश्रिताः।।4.37.6।। तरुणादित्यवर्णाश्च पर्वते ये महारुणे। पिबन्तो मधुमैरेयं भीमवेगाः प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.37.7।। वनेषु च सुरम्येषु सुगन्धिषु महत्सु च। तापसानां च रम्येषु वनान्तेषु समन्ततः।।4.37.8।। तांस्तां स्त्वमानय क्षिप्रं पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्। सामदानादिभि: स्सर्वैराशु प्रेषय वानरान्।।4.37.9।।
explanation: 'Send for the monkeys residing at the five mountains of Mahendra, Himavan, Vindhya, Kailasa and the whitepeaked mount Mandara those monkeys residing on the western mountains, on the sea shore and on mount Udaya shining like the rising Sun monkeys like dark clouds shining in the twilight Sun those at the fierce Padmatala garden and those at the Anjana mountain who  resemble dark clouds like collyrium and are as strong as elephants those monkeys of golden complexion residing at the red arsenic mountain caves beside mount Meru those on mount Meru and Dhumra who are of bright red colour like the rising Sun drinking liquor Maireya the monkeys of terrific speed at mount Maharuna those staying at the delightful hermitages in the forests, and those living on the ground all must be cajoled and persuaded to report at once.

explanation: 'Send for the monkeys residing at the five mountains of Mahendra, Himavan, Vindhya, Kailasa and the whitepeaked mount Mandara those monkeys residing on the western mountains, on the sea shore and on mount Udaya shining like the rising Sun monkeys like dark clouds shining in the twilight Sun those at the fierce Padmatala garden and those at the Anjana mountain who  resemble dark clouds like collyrium and are as strong as elephants those monkeys of golden complexion residing at the red arsenic mountain caves beside mount Meru those on mount Meru and Dhumra who are of bright red colour like the rising Sun drinking liquor Maireya the monkeys of terrific speed at mount Maharuna those staying at the delightful hermitages in the forests, and those living on the ground all must be cajoled and persuaded to report at once.

shloka_text: प्रेषिताः प्रथमं ये च मयादूता महाजवाः। त्वरणार्थं तु भूयस्त्वं हरीन् सम्प्रेषयापरान्।।4.37.10।।
explanation: 'This is in addition to the monkeys for whom swiftfooted messengers have already been sent.

shloka_text: ये प्रसक्ताश्च कामेषु दीर्घसूत्राश्च वानराः। इहाऽनयस्व तान् सर्वान् शीघ्रं तु मम शासनात्।।4.37.11।।
explanation: 'Get all the monkeys including those engaged in carnal pleasures and those slow in movement all at once on my command.

shloka_text: अहोभिर्दशभिर्ये च नागच्छन्ति ममाज्ञया। हन्तव्यास्ते दुरात्मानो राजशासनदूषकाः।।4.37.12।।
explanation: 'Kill those evilminded ones within ten days for disobeying the royal orders.

shloka_text: शतान्यथ सहस्राणां कोट्यश्च मम शासनात्। प्रयान्तु कपिसिंहानां दिशो मम मते स्थिताः।।4.37.13।।
explanation: 'The hundreds of thousands of crores of obedient lionlike monkeys should proceed in all directions at my command.

shloka_text: मेघपर्वतसङ्काशाश्छादयन्त इवाम्बरम्। घोररूपाः कपिश्रेष्ठा यान्तु मच्छासनादितः।।4.37.14।।
explanation: 'Fierce monkeys, comparable to clouds and mountains in appearance shall go as though covering the sky from here at my command.

shloka_text: ते गतिज्ञा गतिं ज्ञात्वा पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः। आनयन्तु हरीन् सर्वांस्त्वरिता शसनान्मम।।4.37.15।।
explanation: Let all those monkeys, who are experts in movement, having ascertained the way on earth, quickly bring all the monkeys at my command.

shloka_text: तस्य वानर राजस्य श्रुत्वा वायुसुतो वचः। दिक्षु सर्वासु विक्रान्तान्प्रेषयामास वानरान्।।4.37.16।।
explanation: Having heard Sugriva's command, Hanuman, son of the Windgod, sent powerful monkeys in all directions.

shloka_text: ते पदं विष्णुविक्रान्तं पतत्रिज्योतिरध्वगाः। प्रयाताः प्रहिता राज्ञा हरयस्तत्क्षणेन वै।।4.37.17।।
explanation: The monkeys ordered by the king, traversed the pathway of birds and heavenly bodies, the path Lord Visnu had trod. [Note: the sky is called Vishnupada since Lord Visnu set his foot on the sky in his incarnation as Vamana.]

shloka_text: ते समुद्रेषु गिरिषु वनेषु च सरस्सु च। वानरा वानरान्सर्वान्रामहेतोरचोदयन्।।4.37.18।।
explanation: The messenger monkeys drove in all those living on the sea shore, mountains, forests as well as banks of lakes in order to serve the cause of Rama.

shloka_text: मृत्युकालोपमस्याऽज्ञां राजराजस्य वानराः। सुग्रीवस्याययु श्श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवभयदर्शिनः।।4.37.19।।
explanation: In response to the command of the king, who was like death to them, the monkeys came at once, driven by fear from Sugriva.

shloka_text: ततस्तेऽञ्जनसङ्काशा गिरेस्तस्मान्महाजवाः। तिस्रः कोट्यः प्लवङ्गानां निर्ययुर्यत्र राघवः।।4.37.20।।
explanation: Then three crores of swiftfooted monkeys, dark like collyrium, rushed forth to the mountain to meet Rama.

shloka_text: अस्तं गच्छति यत्रार्कस्तस्मिन्गिरिवरे स्थिताः। सन्तप्त हेममहाभासस्तस्मात्कोट्यो दश च्युताः।।4.37.21।।
explanation: Ten crores of monkeys shining like pure molten gold, staying on the best of mountains where the Sun sets moved towards Kishkinda.

shloka_text: कैलासशिखरेभ्यश्च सिंहकेसरवर्चसाम्। ततः कोटिसहस्राणि वानराणामुपागमन्।।4.37.22।।
explanation: From the peaks of Kailasa mountain moved out one thousand crores of monkeys who were of bright colour like the lion's mane.

shloka_text: फलमूलेन जीवन्तो हिमवन्तमुपाश्रिताः। तेषां कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रं समवर्तत।।4.37.23।।
explanation: Then monkeys residing at mount Himavan feeding on fruits and roots came in thousands of crores. (This number is called Shankha 1000,000,000,000,0, it is one digit higher than Mahapadma.)

shloka_text: अङ्गारकसमानानां भीमानां भीमकर्मणाम्। विन्ध्याद्वानरकोटीनां सहस्राण्यपतन्द्रुतम्।।4.37.24।।
explanation: From the Vindhya mountain came down thousands of crores of swiftfooted monkeys of terrific deeds. They were fierce like fire (Angaraka).

shloka_text: क्षीरोदवेलानिलयास्तमालवनवासिनः। नारिकेलाशनाश्चैव तेषां सङ्ख्या न विद्यते।।4.37.25।।
explanation: The monkeys residents of Tamala forest on the shores of the ocean of milk feeding on coconuts arrived from the groves in countless number.

shloka_text: वनेभ्यो गह्वरेभ्यश्च सरिद्भ्यश्च महाजवा। आगच्छद्वानरी सेना पिबन्तीव दिवाकरम्।।4.37.26।।
explanation: An army of swiftmoving monkeys came from the caves, from the banks of rivers and forests as though it was swallowing up the Sungod.

shloka_text: ये तु त्वरयितुं याता वानरास्सर्ववानरान्। ते वीरा हिमवच्छैलं ददृशुस्तं महाद्रुमम्।।4.37.27।।
explanation: The monkeys sent earlier to hasten all their counterparts saw mount Himavat from the great tree.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्गिरिवरे रम्ये यज्ञो माहेश्वरः पुरा। सर्वदेवमनस्तोषो बभौ दिव्यो मनोहरः।।4.37.28।।
explanation: A divine, wonderful, delightful Yagna dedicated to Lord Siva used to be performed on the beautiful (Himalayan) mountain in the past so that the minds of all deities were satisfied.

shloka_text: अन्ननिष्यन्दजातानि मूलानि च फलानि च। अमृतास्वादकल्पानि ददृशुस्तत्र वानराः।।4.37.29।।
explanation: There the monkeys saw the Yajna, and partook the fruits and roots produced out of the havis which tasted sweet like nectar.

shloka_text: तदन्नसम्भवं दिव्यं फलमूलं मनोहरम्। यः कश्चित्सकृदश्नाति मासं भवति तर्पितः।।4.37.30।।
explanation: Any one who shares even a little of the divine, delicious fruits and roots grown out of that havis will have no hunger or thirst for a month.

shloka_text: तानि मूलानि दिव्यानि फलानि च फलाशनाः। औषधानि च दिव्यानि जगृहुर्हरियूथपाः।।4.37.31।।
explanation: The monkey leaders who lived on fruits collected the divine fruits, roots as well as  medicinal herbs.

shloka_text: तस्माच्च यज्ञायतनात्पुष्पाणि सुरभीणि च। आनिन्युर्वानरा गत्वा सुग्रीवप्रियकारणात्।।4.37.32।।
explanation: The monkeys also collected finesmelling flowers from the sacrificial altar to please Sugriva with.

shloka_text: ते तु सर्वे हरिवराः पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्। सञ्चोदयित्वा त्वरिता यूथानां जग्मुरग्रतः।।4.37.33।।
explanation: The monkey leaders from all over the earth arrived quickly, leading the hordes of them.

shloka_text: ते तु तेन मुहूर्तेन यूथपाश्शीघ्रगामिनः। किष्किन्धां त्वरया प्राप्ता स्सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः।।4.37.34।।
explanation: In a short while the swiftmoving leaders of the monkeys groups reached Kishkinda quickly.

shloka_text: ते गृहीत्वौषधीस्सर्वाः फलमूलं च वानराः। तं प्रतिग्राहयामासुर्वचनं चेदमब्रुवन्।।4.37.35।।
explanation: Offering all kinds of medicinal herbs, fruits and roots collected, to Sugriva the monkeys said:

shloka_text: सर्वे परिगताश्शैलास्समुद्राश्च वनानि च। पृथिव्यां वानरास्सर्वे शासनादुपयान्ति ते।।4.37.36।।
explanation: All mountains, oceans, and forests have been traversed. All monkeys on earth come by command.

shloka_text: एवं श्रुत्वा ततो हृष्ट स्सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः। प्रतिजग्राह तत्प्रतीतस्तेषां सर्वमुपायनम्।।4.37.37।।
explanation: On hearing the report from the monkeys, Sugriva the king of vanaras, accepted all the gifts they had brought him, with great pleasure. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyseventh sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, of the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सर्वमुपायनमुपाहृतम्। वानरान्सान्त्वयित्वा च सर्वानेव व्यसर्जयत्।।4.38.1।।
explanation: On receiving all the gifts presented by the monkeys, Sugriva permitted them to go happy.

shloka_text: विसर्जयित्वा स हरीन् शूरांस्तान्कृतकर्मणः। मेने कृतार्थमात्मानं राघवं च महाबलम्।।4.38.2।।
explanation: The monkey heroes sent by Sugriva performed the task assigned to them and felt powerful Rama's task has been achieved (a successful beginning has been made).

shloka_text: स लक्ष्मणो भीमबलं सर्ववानरसत्तमम्। अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं सुग्रीवं सम्प्रहर्षयन्।।4.38.3।। किष्किन्धाया विनिष्क्राम यदि ते सौम्य रोचते।
explanation: Cheering Sugriva, the foremost among the monkeys, the mighty Lakshmana said in a humble way: 'O goodnatured Sugriva if you would like to come to Rama let us depart  from Kishkinda.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य सुभाषितम्।।4.38.4।। सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह। एवं भवतु गच्छाव: स्थेयं त्वच्छासने मया।।4.38.5।।
explanation: Hearing the gentle words of Lakshmana, spoken lovingly in that manner and asking him to come along with him, Sugriva was highly pleased.He agreed to go with him and said, 'As you please. I abide by your command'.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य सुभाषितम्।।4.38.4।। सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह। एवं भवतु गच्छाव: स्थेयं त्वच्छासने मया।।4.38.5।।
explanation: Hearing the gentle words of Lakshmana, spoken lovingly in that manner and asking him to come along with him, Sugriva was highly pleased.He agreed to go with him and said, 'As you please. I abide by your command'.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वा सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्। विसर्जयामास तदा तारामन्याश्च योषितः।।4.38.6।।
explanation: Sugriva spoke to Lakshmana endowed with auspicious signs, and thereupon permitted Tara and other women to leave the place.

shloka_text: एतेत्युच्चैर्हरिवरान्सुग्रीवस्समुदाहरत्। तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयश्शीघ्रमाययुः।।4.38.7।। बद्धाञ्जलिपुटास्सर्वे ये स्युः स्त्रीदर्शनक्षमाः।
explanation: Sugriva called in the monkeys who deserved audience of the female folk of the royal family. They came forward quickly with folded hands welcoming the heroes.

shloka_text: तानुवाच ततः प्राप्तान्राजाऽर्कसदृशप्रभः।।4.38.8।। उपस्थापयत क्षिप्रं शिबिकां मम वानराः।
explanation: Then seeing the monkeys who had come there, king Sugriva who was shining like the Sungod asked them to get a palanquin ready at once.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य हरयश्शीघ्रविक्रमाः।।4.38.9।। समुपस्थापयामासुश्शिबिकां प्रियदर्शनाम्।
explanation: On hearing the king, the monkeys who were quick to act placed a beautiful palanquin in front of him.

shloka_text: तामुपस्थापितां दृष्ट्वा शिबिकां वानराधिपः।।4.38.10।। लक्ष्मणाऽरुह्यतां शीघ्रमिति सौमित्रिमब्रवीत्।
explanation: Seeing the palanquin placed in front of Sugriva, the chief of the monkeys requested Lakshmana to get in quickly.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा काञ्चनं यानं सुग्रीवस्सूर्यसन्निभम्।।4.38.11।। बृहद्भिर्हरिभिर्युक्तमारुरोह सलक्ष्मणः।
explanation: With this Sugriva, shining like the Sungod, entered along with Lakshmana the golden palanquin carried by ablebodied monkeys.

shloka_text: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण म्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि।।4.38.12।। शुक्लैश्च वालव्यजनैर्धूयमानैस्समन्ततः। शङ्खभेरीनिनादैश्च हरिभिश्चाभिवन्दितः।।4.38.13।। निर्ययौ प्राप्य सुग्रीवो राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम्।
explanation: With a pale white umbrella over his head, white yaktail fans and sounds of conches and drums, Sugriva set out receiving greetings from monkeys, rejoicing in his royal glory.

shloka_text: पाण्डुरेणातपत्रेण म्रियमाणेन मूर्धनि।।4.38.12।। शुक्लैश्च वालव्यजनैर्धूयमानैस्समन्ततः। शङ्खभेरीनिनादैश्च हरिभिश्चाभिवन्दितः।।4.38.13।। निर्ययौ प्राप्य सुग्रीवो राज्यश्रियमनुत्तमाम्।
explanation: With a pale white umbrella over his head, white yaktail fans and sounds of conches and drums, Sugriva set out receiving greetings from monkeys, rejoicing in his royal glory.

shloka_text: स वानरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बहुभि श्शस्त्रपाणिभिः।।4.38.14।। परिकीर्णो ययौ तत्र यत्र रामो व्यवस्थितः।
explanation: Surrounded by hundreds of monkeys wielding various sharp weapons, Sugriva went forth to the region where Rama resided৷৷

shloka_text: स तं देशमनुप्राप्य श्रेष्ठं रामनिषेवितम्।।4.38.15।। अवातरन्महातेजा श्शिबिकायास्सलक्ष्मणः।
explanation: Having reached the place where Rama lived, brilliant Sugriva along with Lakshmana descended from the palanquin.

shloka_text: आसाद्य च ततो रामं कृताञ्जलिपुटोऽभवत्।।4.38.16।। कृताञ्जलौ स्थिते तस्मिन्वानराश्चाभवंस्तथा।
explanation: Thereafter Sugriva followed by the monkeys approached Rama, and stood with folded hands.

shloka_text: तटाकमिव तं दृष्ट्वा रामः कुड्मलपङ्कजम्।।4.38.17।। वानराणां महत्सैन्यं सुग्रीवे प्रीतिमानभूत्।
explanation: Rama was pleased on beholding the great army of monkeys standing, resembling a pond full of lotus buds.

shloka_text: पादयोः पतितं मूर्ध्ना तमुत्थाप्य हरीश्वरम्।।4.38.18।। प्रेम्णा च बहुमानाच्च राघवः परिषस्वजे।
explanation: Sugriva touched Rama's feet, bending his head down, and Rama lifted him up and embraced him with love and great regard.

shloka_text: परिष्वज्य च धर्मात्मा निषीदेति ततोऽब्रवीत्।।4.38.19।। निषण्णं तं ततो दृष्ट्वा क्षितौ रामोऽब्रवीद्वचः।
explanation: Embracing him, Rama offered him a seat on the ground and said:

shloka_text: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च यस्तु काले निषेवते।।4.38.20।। विभज्य सततं वीर स्स राजा हरिसत्तम।
explanation: 'O best among the heroic monkeys, a king who apportions his time properly towards pursuit of dharma, artha and kama is a hero and deserves to be a king.

shloka_text: हित्वा धर्मं तथाऽर्थं च कामं यस्तु निषेवते।।4.38.21।। स वृक्षाग्रे यथा सुप्तः पतितः प्रतिबुध्यते।
explanation: 'One who neglects dharma and artha and pursues only kama (sensuous enjoyment) is like a man asleep on top of the tree, waking up only to realize that he has fallen down.

shloka_text: अमित्राणां वधे युक्तो मित्राणां सङ्ग्रहे रतः।।4.38.22।। त्रिवर्गफलभोक्ता तु राजा धर्मेण युज्यते।
explanation: A king who is engaged in the destruction of enemies and devoted to the protection of friends, indeed enjoys the fruits of the three aims of life and is endowed with righteousness.

shloka_text: उद्योगसमयस्त्वेषप्राप्तश्शत्रुविनाशन।।4.38.23।। सञ्चिन्त्यतां हि पिङ्गेश हरिभिस्सह मन्त्रिभिः।
explanation: 'O king of monkeys, slayer of enemies the time to act has arrived. Think of the strategies with your ministers and other monkeys.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.38.24।। प्रणष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो पुनःप्राप्तमिदं मया।।4.38.25।।
explanation: On hearing this, Sugriva said to Rama,'O longarmed one the fortune, fame and soverignty of vanaras which was lost has been regained only by your grace.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो रामं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.38.24।। प्रणष्टा श्रीश्च कीर्तिश्च कपिराज्यं च शाश्वतम्। त्वत्प्रसादान्महाबाहो पुनःप्राप्तमिदं मया।।4.38.25।।
explanation: On hearing this, Sugriva said to Rama,'O longarmed one the fortune, fame and soverignty of vanaras which was lost has been regained only by your grace.

shloka_text: तव देव प्रसादाच्च भ्रातुश्च जयतां वर। कृतं न प्रतिकुर्याद्यः पुरुषाणां स दूषकः।।4.38.26।।
explanation: 'O victorious lord he who does not repay the help got through your grace and your brother's is despicable among men.

shloka_text: एते वानरमूख्याश्च शतशश्शत्रुसूदन। प्राप्ताश्चादाय बलिनः पृथिव्यां सर्ववानरान्।।4.38.27।।
explanation: 'O destroyer of enemies hundreds of strong vanara chiefs gathered from all over the earth have reached here.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाश्चावहिताश्शूरा गोलाङ्गूलाश्च राघव। कान्तारवनदुर्गाणामभिज्ञा घोरदर्शनाः।।4.38.28।। देवगन्धर्वपुत्राश्च वानराः कामरूपिणः। स्वैस्स्वै: परिवृतास्सैन्यैर्वर्तन्ते पथि राघव।।4.38.29।।
explanation: 'O Rama valiant bears of fierce appearance, also golangulas (a variety of monkeys with tails like cows') familiar with the inaccessible fortresses of forest have come. These monkeys are sons of divine beings and gandharvas who can assume any form at will. They are on their way along with their armies.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाश्चावहिताश्शूरा गोलाङ्गूलाश्च राघव। कान्तारवनदुर्गाणामभिज्ञा घोरदर्शनाः।।4.38.28।। देवगन्धर्वपुत्राश्च वानराः कामरूपिणः। स्वैस्स्वै: परिवृतास्सैन्यैर्वर्तन्ते पथि राघव।।4.38.29।।
explanation: 'O Rama valiant bears of fierce appearance, also golangulas (a variety of monkeys with tails like cows') familiar with the inaccessible fortresses of forest have come. These monkeys are sons of divine beings and gandharvas who can assume any form at will. They are on their way along with their armies.

shloka_text: शतैश्शतसहस्रैश्च वर्तन्ते कोटिभिश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अयुतैश्चावृता वीराश्शङ्कुभिश्च परन्तप ।।4.38.30।। अर्बुदैरर्बुदशतैर्मध्यैश्चान्त्यैश्च वानराः। समुद्रैश्च परार्धैश्च हरयो हरियूथपाः।।4.38.31।। आगमिष्यन्ति ते राजन्महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा विन्ध्य मेरुकृतालयाः।।4.38.32।।
explanation: O scorcher of enemies the vanara troops in hundred thousand crores, ayutas, sanku, arbuda, hundreds of arbudas, madhyas, antyas, samudras and parardhas (100000000000000000), are expected. O king  they are residents of Vindhya and Meru mountains, comparable to lord Indra in courage and appear like mountains Meru and Mandara.

shloka_text: शतैश्शतसहस्रैश्च वर्तन्ते कोटिभिश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अयुतैश्चावृता वीराश्शङ्कुभिश्च परन्तप ।।4.38.30।। अर्बुदैरर्बुदशतैर्मध्यैश्चान्त्यैश्च वानराः। समुद्रैश्च परार्धैश्च हरयो हरियूथपाः।।4.38.31।। आगमिष्यन्ति ते राजन्महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा विन्ध्य मेरुकृतालयाः।।4.38.32।।
explanation: O scorcher of enemies the vanara troops in hundred thousand crores, ayutas, sanku, arbuda, hundreds of arbudas, madhyas, antyas, samudras and parardhas (100000000000000000), are expected. O king  they are residents of Vindhya and Meru mountains, comparable to lord Indra in courage and appear like mountains Meru and Mandara.

shloka_text: शतैश्शतसहस्रैश्च वर्तन्ते कोटिभिश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अयुतैश्चावृता वीराश्शङ्कुभिश्च परन्तप ।।4.38.30।। अर्बुदैरर्बुदशतैर्मध्यैश्चान्त्यैश्च वानराः। समुद्रैश्च परार्धैश्च हरयो हरियूथपाः।।4.38.31।। आगमिष्यन्ति ते राजन्महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः। मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशा विन्ध्य मेरुकृतालयाः।।4.38.32।।
explanation: O scorcher of enemies the vanara troops in hundred thousand crores, ayutas, sanku, arbuda, hundreds of arbudas, madhyas, antyas, samudras and parardhas (100000000000000000), are expected. O king  they are residents of Vindhya and Meru mountains, comparable to lord Indra in courage and appear like mountains Meru and Mandara.

shloka_text: ते त्वामभिगमिष्यन्ति राक्षसं ये सबान्धवम्। निहत्य रावणं सख्ये ह्यानयिष्यन्ति मैथिलीम्।।4.38.33।।
explanation: 'The monkeys who can kill ogre Ravana and his relatives in battle and bring back Maithili will be arriving shortly.

shloka_text: ततस्तमुद्योगमवेक्ष्य बुद्धिमा न्हरिप्रवीरस्य निदेशवर्तिनः। बभूव हर्षाद्वसुधाधिपात्मजः प्रबुद्धनीलोत्पलतुल्यदर्शनः।।4.38.34।।
explanation: The wise statesman, Rama observing the efforts of Sugriva and his attendants looked like a blooming blue lotus through delight. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends of thirtyeighth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana, composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो धर्मभृतां वरः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिम्।।4.39.1।।
explanation: On hearing Sugriva who stood with folded hands, Rama, the foremost among the upholders of righteousness, hugged him and said:

shloka_text: यदिन्द्रो वर्षते वर्षं न तच्चित्रं भवेत्क्वचित्। आदित्यो वा सहस्रांशुः कुर्याद्वितिमिरं नभः।।4.39.2।। चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिः कुर्यात्पृथिवीं सौम्य निर्मलाम्। त्वद्विधो वाऽपि मित्राणां प्रतिकुर्यात्परन्तप ।।4.39.3।।
explanation: 'O scorcher of enemies, gentle Sugriva it will not be strange if Indra showers rain, if the Sun in the sky dispels darkness with his thousand rays, and if the  Moon cools down the earth with his light, and a person like you helps his friend.

shloka_text: यदिन्द्रो वर्षते वर्षं न तच्चित्रं भवेत्क्वचित्। आदित्यो वा सहस्रांशुः कुर्याद्वितिमिरं नभः।।4.39.2।। चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिः कुर्यात्पृथिवीं सौम्य निर्मलाम्। त्वद्विधो वाऽपि मित्राणां प्रतिकुर्यात्परन्तप ।।4.39.3।।
explanation: 'O scorcher of enemies, gentle Sugriva it will not be strange if Indra showers rain, if the Sun in the sky dispels darkness with his thousand rays, and if the  Moon cools down the earth with his light, and a person like you helps his friend.

shloka_text: एवं त्वयि न तच्चित्रं भवेद्यत्सौम्य शोभनम्। जानाम्यहं त्वां सुग्रीव सततं प्रियवादिनम्।।4.39.4।।
explanation: 'O gentle Sugriva this your help to me is not surprising. You always help your friends and speak in a pleasing manner.

shloka_text: त्वत्सनाथ: सखे सङ्ख्ये जेताऽस्मि सकलानरीन्। त्वमेव मे सुहृतन्मित्रं साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि।।4.39.5।।
explanation: 'O friend I will win over all enemies in war supported by you.You are a goodhearted friend and you alone should help me.

shloka_text: जहारात्मविनाशाय वैदेहीं राक्षसाधमः। वञ्चयित्वा तु पौलोमीमनुह्लादो यथा शचीम्।।4.39.6।।
explanation: Just as Anuhlada (son of Hiranyakasipu and brother of Prahlada) took away, Poulomi  (Sachi, daughter of Puloma) deceiving Indra, this lowly demon took away Sita, daughter of the king of Videha.

shloka_text: न चिरात्तं हनिष्यामि रावणं निशितैश्शरैः। पौलोम्याः पितरं दृप्तं शतक्रतुरिवाऽहवे।।4.39.7।।
explanation: 'I will kill Ravana with my sharp arrows just as Indra, (who had done a hundred sacrifices) killed the proud father of Poulomi.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैव रजस्समभिवर्तत। उष्णां तीव्रां सहस्रांशोश्छादयद्गगने प्रभाम्।।4.39.8।।
explanation: In the mean while the dust raised (by army of monkeys) all over obscured the intense heat from the sky and the radiance of the thousandrayed Sun.

shloka_text: दिशः पर्याकुलाश्चासन्रजसा तेन मूर्छता। चचाल च मही सर्वा सशैलवनकानना।।4.39.9।।
explanation: By the spreading of dust, the quarters were not visible.The earth including the mountains gardens and forests was shaken up.

shloka_text: ततो नगेन्द्रसङ्काशैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। कृत्स्ना सञ्छादिता भूमिरसङ्ख्येयैः प्लवङ्गमैः।।4.39.10।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ततस्तैर्हरियूथपैः। कोटीशतपरीवारैः कामरूपिभिरावृता।।4.39.11।। नादेयैः पार्वतीयैश्च सामुद्रैश्च महाबलैः। हरिभिर्मेघनिर्ह्रादैरन्यैश्च वनचारिभिः।।4.39.12।। तरुणादित्यवर्णैश्च शशिगौरैश्च वानरैः। पद्मकेसरवर्णैश्च श्वेतैर्मेरुकृतालयैः।।4.39.13।।
explanation: In a minute, the entire land was crowded with innumerable powerful monkeys of the size of mountains having sharp fangs.The monkey leaders with a hundred crore monkey followers, who could assume any form at their will mighty monkeys from the mountains, rivers and seas vanaras thundering like clouds and other free vanaras who were wanderers vanaras red in colour like the rising Sun, tawny coloured ones like the Moon some who were of the hue of white lotus filaments and some vanaras residing in mount Meru came there.

shloka_text: ततो नगेन्द्रसङ्काशैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। कृत्स्ना सञ्छादिता भूमिरसङ्ख्येयैः प्लवङ्गमैः।।4.39.10।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ततस्तैर्हरियूथपैः। कोटीशतपरीवारैः कामरूपिभिरावृता।।4.39.11।। नादेयैः पार्वतीयैश्च सामुद्रैश्च महाबलैः। हरिभिर्मेघनिर्ह्रादैरन्यैश्च वनचारिभिः।।4.39.12।। तरुणादित्यवर्णैश्च शशिगौरैश्च वानरैः। पद्मकेसरवर्णैश्च श्वेतैर्मेरुकृतालयैः।।4.39.13।।
explanation: In a minute, the entire land was crowded with innumerable powerful monkeys of the size of mountains having sharp fangs.The monkey leaders with a hundred crore monkey followers, who could assume any form at their will mighty monkeys from the mountains, rivers and seas vanaras thundering like clouds and other free vanaras who were wanderers vanaras red in colour like the rising Sun, tawny coloured ones like the Moon some who were of the hue of white lotus filaments and some vanaras residing in mount Meru came there.

shloka_text: ततो नगेन्द्रसङ्काशैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। कृत्स्ना सञ्छादिता भूमिरसङ्ख्येयैः प्लवङ्गमैः।।4.39.10।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ततस्तैर्हरियूथपैः। कोटीशतपरीवारैः कामरूपिभिरावृता।।4.39.11।। नादेयैः पार्वतीयैश्च सामुद्रैश्च महाबलैः। हरिभिर्मेघनिर्ह्रादैरन्यैश्च वनचारिभिः।।4.39.12।। तरुणादित्यवर्णैश्च शशिगौरैश्च वानरैः। पद्मकेसरवर्णैश्च श्वेतैर्मेरुकृतालयैः।।4.39.13।।

shloka_text: ततो नगेन्द्रसङ्काशैस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रैर्महाबलैः। कृत्स्ना सञ्छादिता भूमिरसङ्ख्येयैः प्लवङ्गमैः।।4.39.10।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेण ततस्तैर्हरियूथपैः। कोटीशतपरीवारैः कामरूपिभिरावृता।।4.39.11।। नादेयैः पार्वतीयैश्च सामुद्रैश्च महाबलैः। हरिभिर्मेघनिर्ह्रादैरन्यैश्च वनचारिभिः।।4.39.12।। तरुणादित्यवर्णैश्च शशिगौरैश्च वानरैः। पद्मकेसरवर्णैश्च श्वेतैर्मेरुकृतालयैः।।4.39.13।।
explanation: In a minute, the entire land was crowded with innumerable powerful monkeys of the size of mountains having sharp fangs.The monkey leaders with a hundred crore monkey followers, who could assume any form at their will mighty monkeys from the mountains, rivers and seas vanaras thundering like clouds and other free vanaras who were wanderers vanaras red in colour like the rising Sun, tawny coloured ones like the Moon some who were of the hue of white lotus filaments and some vanaras residing in mount Meru came there.

shloka_text: कोटीसहस्रैर्दशभिः श्रीमान्परिवृतस्तदा। वीरश्शतवलिर्नाम वानरः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.14।।
explanation: Then appeared the glorious warrior named Satavali, followed by ten thousand crore of monkeys.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभस्ताराया वीर्यवान्पिता। अनेकैर्दशसाहस्रैः कोटिभिः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.15।।
explanation: (Next came) the valiant father of Tara of golden complexion like mount Meru followed by ten thousand crore of vanaras.

shloka_text: तथाऽपरेण कोटीनां सहस्रेण समन्वितः। पिता रुमाया सम्प्राप्तस्सुग्रीवश्वशुरो विभुः।।4.39.16।।
explanation: Likewise mighty father of Ruma, fatherinlaw of Sugriva, reached there accompanied by a thousand crore monkeys.

shloka_text: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशस्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। बुद्धिमान्वानरश्रेष्ठस्सर्ववानरसत्तमः।।4.39.17।। अनेकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः। पिता हनुमतश्रशीमान्केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.18।।
explanation: Then arrived Kesari, the wise and illustrious monkey, foremost and the best among vanaras, father of Hanuman. He was of the colour of lotus filaments and his countenance was red like the early morning Sun. He was accompanied by many thousands of monkeys.

shloka_text: पद्मकेसरसङ्काशस्तरुणार्कनिभाननः। बुद्धिमान्वानरश्रेष्ठस्सर्ववानरसत्तमः।।4.39.17।। अनेकैर्बहुसाहस्रैर्वानराणां समन्वितः। पिता हनुमतश्रशीमान्केसरी प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.18।।
explanation: Then arrived Kesari, the wise and illustrious monkey, foremost and the best among vanaras, father of Hanuman. He was of the colour of lotus filaments and his countenance was red like the early morning Sun. He was accompanied by many thousands of monkeys.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलमहाराजो गवाक्षो भीमविक्रमः। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यत।।4.39.19।।
explanation: Next arrived Gavaksha, king of Langurs (whose tail resembled the cow's), of fierceful courage surrounded by a thousand crore of vanaras.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाणां भीमवेगानां धूम्रश्शत्रुनिबर्हणः। वृतः कोटिसहस्राभ्यां द्वाभ्यां समभिवर्तत।।4.39.20।।
explanation: Dhumra, destroyer of enemies, came next followed by two thousand crore of bears of terrible speed.

shloka_text: महाचलनिभैर्घोरै: पनसो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यस्तिसृभिः कोटिभिर्वृतः।।4.39.21।।
explanation: Similarly, the great warrior named Panasa, leader of the troop, reported with three crore dreadful vanaras of the size of huge mountains.

shloka_text: नीलाञ्जनचयाकारो नीलो नामाऽथ यूथपः। अदृश्यत महाकायः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः।।4.39.22।।
explanation: Then appeared Nila of huge body, dark like a mountain of collyrium accompanied by ten crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनशैलाभो गवयो नाम यूथपः। आजगाम महावीर्यः पञ्चभि: कोटिभिर्वृतः।।4.39.23।।
explanation: Then arrived the leader of five crore vanaras, the great warrior Gavaya who resembled a golden mountain.

shloka_text: दरीमुखश्च बलवान्यूथपोऽभ्याययौ तदा। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण सुग्रीवं समुपस्थितः।।4.39.24।।
explanation: Then the strong Darimukha, leader of a thousand crore monkeys approached Sugriva.

shloka_text: मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभावश्विपुत्रौ महाबलौ। कोटिकोटिसहस्रेण वानराणामदृश्यताम्।।4.39.25।।
explanation: Two very powerful sons of Asvini, Mainda and Dvivida, appeared with a thousand crore vanaras.

shloka_text: गजश्च बलवान् वीर: कोटिभिस्तिसृभिर्वृतः। आजगाम महातेजा सुग्रीवस्य समीपतः।।4.39.26।।
explanation: Strong and powerful Gaja also reached Sugriva with three crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ऋक्षराजो महातेजा जाम्बवान्नाम नामतः। कोटिभिर्दशभिः प्राप्तः सुग्रीवस्य वशे स्थितः।।4.39.27।।
explanation: Glorious Jambavan, king of bears, stood before Sugriva with ten thousand crore vanaras.

shloka_text: रुमण्वान्नाम विक्रान्तो वानरो वानरेश्वरम्। आययौ बलवांस्तूर्णं कोटीशतसमावृतः।।4.39.28।।
explanation: Sturdy and victorious vanara called Rumanvan came swiftly followed by a hundred crore vanaras.

shloka_text: ततः कोटिसहस्राणां सहस्रेण शतेन च। पृष्ठतोऽनुगतः प्राप्तो हरिभिर्गन्धमादनः।।4.39.29।।
explanation: Then came Gandhamadana with a hundred thousand crore of vanaras following him.

shloka_text: ततः पद्मसहस्रेण वृतश्शङ्कुशतेन च। युवराजोऽङ्गदः प्राप्तः पितृतुल्यपराक्रमः।।4.39.30।।
explanation: Then arrived the heir apparent, Angada, whose prowess is comparable to that of his father with him came a thousand padmas and a hundred sankus of followers.

shloka_text: ततस्ताराद्युतिस्तारो हरिर्भीमपराक्रमः। पञ्चभिर्हरिकोटीभिर्दूरतः प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.31।।
explanation: And Tara (brother of Ruma's father) of terrific valour shining like a star showed up at a distance with five crore vanaras.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजानुः कपिर्वीरो यूथपः प्रत्यदृश्यत। एकादशानां कोटीनामीश्वरस्तैस्समावृतः।।4.39.32।।
explanation: Then Indrajanu the troop leader and chief of vanaras appeared along with eleven crore monkeys.

shloka_text: ततो रम्भस्त्वनुप्राप्तस्तरुणादित्यसन्निभः। अयुतेनावृतश्चैव सहस्रेण शतेन च।।4.39.33।।
explanation: Thereafter Rambha of the colour of the rising Sun brought together an army of one thousand and one hundred ayuta troops.

shloka_text: ततो यूथपतिर्वीरो दुर्मुखो नाम वानरः। प्रत्यदृश्यत कोटीभ्यां द्वाभ्यां परिवृतो बली।।4.39.34।।
explanation: Thereafter the mighty hero, leader of the troop, by name Durmukha appeared with  two crore vanaras.

shloka_text: कैलासशिखराकारैर्वानरैर्भीमविक्रमैः। वृतः कोटिसहस्रेण हनुमान्प्रत्यदृश्यत।।4.39.35।।
explanation: And Hanuman showed up surrounded by a thousand crore vanaras of frightful valour. They looked like the peaks of Kailasa mountain.

shloka_text: नलश्चापि महावीर्यस्संवृतो द्रुमवासिभिः। कोटीशतेन सम्प्राप्तस्सहस्रेण शतेन च।।4.39.36।।
explanation: Valiant Nala also arrived surrounded by a hundred crore and a hundred thousand treedwellers (monkeys).

shloka_text: ततो दधिमुखश्रीमान्कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः। सम्प्राप्तोऽभिमतस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।।4.39.37।।
explanation: Then the illustrious Dadhimukha, great Sugriva's favourite leader reached with ten crore vanaras.

shloka_text: शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रंह एव च। एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः।।4.39.38।। आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च। यूथपा स्समनुप्राप्ता स्तेषां संख्या न विद्यते।।4.39.39।। आगताश्च विशिष्टाश्च पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः।
explanation: Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni and Ramhi and many other vanara troops who can assume any form at their will and others from all over the land, mountains and forest advanced towards Sugriva. All the outstanding vanaras of the earth came and covered the land.

shloka_text: शरभः कुमुदो वह्निर्वानरो रंह एव च। एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः कामरूपिणः।।4.39.38।। आवृत्य पृथिवीं सर्वां पर्वतांश्च वनानि च। यूथपा स्समनुप्राप्ता स्तेषां संख्या न विद्यते।।4.39.39।। आगताश्च विशिष्टाश्च पृथिव्यां सर्ववानराः।
explanation: Sarabha, Kumuda, Vahni and Ramhi and many other vanara troops who can assume any form at their will and others from all over the land, mountains and forest advanced towards Sugriva. All the outstanding vanaras of the earth came and covered the land.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः। अभ्यवर्तन्त सुग्रीवं सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव।।4.39.40।।
explanation: The monkeys came leaping, jumping and roaring in enthusiasm and surrounded Sugriva just as clouds surround the Sun.

shloka_text: कुर्वाणा बहुशब्दांश्च प्रहृष्टा बाहुशालिनः। शिरोभिर्वानरेन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयन्।।4.39.41।।
explanation: The leaders of monkeys possesing sturdy shoulders made many kinds of noises and reported to Sugriva, bending their heads in reverence.

shloka_text: अपरे वानरश्रेष्ठास्सङ्गम्य च यथोचितम्। सुग्रीवेण समागम्य स्थिताः प्राञ्जलय स्तदा।।4.39.42।।
explanation: Thereafter the vanaras came close to Sugriva freely and on reaching him stood, offering salutations with folded hands.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्त्वरितो रामे सर्वांस्तां वानररर्षभान्। निवेदयित्वा धर्मज्ञः स्थितः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत्।।4.39.43।।
explanation: Sugriva, knower of dharma, at once presented all the prominent vanaras to Rama, and standing with folded hands said.

shloka_text: यथासुखं पर्वतनिझरेषु वनेषु सर्वेषु च वानरेन्द्राः। निवेशयित्वा विधिवद्बलानि बलं बलज्ञः प्रतिपत्तुमीष्टे।।4.39.44।।
explanation: Sugriva told the chiefs to station the forces by the side  of swift mountain streams, in forests, and hills and ascertain their exact number. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the thirtyninth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ राजा समृद्धार्थस्सुग्रीवः प्लवगेश्वरः। उवाच नरशार्दूलं रामं परबलार्दनम्।।4.40.1।।
explanation: Sugriva, lord of monkeys, who was supported by a massive army informed Rama, the tiger among men and a crusher of the enemy army

shloka_text: आगता विनिविष्टाश्च बलिनः कामरूपिणः। वानरा वारणेन्द्रभा: ये मद्विषयवासिनः।।4.40.2।।
explanation: 'The vanaras living in my kingdom have come and have settled down. They are strong and huge like elephants and they can assume any form at will.

shloka_text: त इमे बहुविक्रान्तैर्हरिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसन्निभाः।।4.40.3।।
explanation: 'Dreadful monkeys, powerful monkeys of fierce valour who resemble demons in form, have arrived.

shloka_text: ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः। पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः।।4.40.4।। पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः। कोट्यग्रश इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किङ्कराः।।4.40.5।।
explanation: Powerful vanaras who have earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, those who are indefatigable and wellknown for their valour having gained preeminence through their efforts and living on several mountains, those who can move on the earth as well as water, crores of them have arrived.

shloka_text: ख्यातकर्मापदानाश्च बलवन्तो जितक्लमाः। पराक्रमेषु विख्याता व्यवसायेषु चोत्तमाः।।4.40.4।। पृथिव्यम्बुचरा राम नानानगनिवासिनः। कोट्यग्रश इमे प्राप्ता वानरास्तव किङ्कराः।।4.40.5।।
explanation: Powerful vanaras who have earned fame for their valiant deeds in the past, those who are indefatigable and wellknown for their valour having gained preeminence through their efforts and living on several mountains, those who can move on the earth as well as water, crores of them have arrived.

shloka_text: निदेशवर्तिनस्सर्वे सर्वे गुरुहिते रताः। अभिप्रेतमनुष्ठातुं तव शक्ष्यन्त्यरिन्दम।।4.40.6।।
explanation: 'O Rama,the subduer of foes all of them will follow your command.They are engaged in seeking the wellbeing of elders and can fulfil your wish.

shloka_text: त इमे बहुसाहस्रैरनीकै भीमविक्रमैः। आगता वानरा घोरा दैत्यदानवसन्निभा:।।4.40.7।।
explanation: 'Dreadful monkeys who resemble demons have arrived along with thousands of fierce fighters.

shloka_text: यन्मन्यसे नरव्याघ्र प्राप्तकालं तदुच्यताम्। तत्सैन्यं त्वद्वशे युक्तमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।।4.40.8।।
explanation: 'O tiger among men announce the proper time for action. This army is at your command. Command them.

shloka_text: काममेषामिदं कार्यं विदितं मम तत्त्वतः। तथापि तु यथातत्त्वमाज्ञापयितुमर्हसि।।4.40.9।।
explanation: Indeed, this task of theirs is truly known to me. Nevertheless, you should instruct me as it truly is.

shloka_text: इति ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं रामो दशरथात्मजः। बाहुभ्यां सम्परिष्वज्य इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.40.10।।
explanation: On hearing him, Rama, Dasaratha's son, hugged Sugriva with his arms and said:

shloka_text: ज्ञायतां मम वैदेही यदि जीवति वा न वा। स च देशो महाप्राज्ञ यस्मिन्वसति रावणः।।4.40.11।।
explanation: 'O wise warrior I wish to know whether Vaidehi is alive or not. Let the kingdom of Ravana be found out.

shloka_text: अधिगम्य तु वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च। प्राप्तकालं विधास्यामि तस्मिन्काले सह त्वया।।4.40.12।।
explanation: 'On locating Vaidehi in the kingdom of Ravana I shall take up proper course of action  in conjunction with you.

shloka_text: नाहमस्मिन् प्रभुः कार्ये वानरेश न लक्ष्मणः। त्वमस्य हेतुः कार्यस्य प्रभुश्च प्लवगेश्वर।।4.40.13।।
explanation: 'O lord of monkeys neither I nor my brother Lakshmana should command the monkeys. You are the right person to do it.

shloka_text: त्वमेवाऽज्ञापय विभो मम कार्यविनिश्चयम्। त्वं हि जानासि यत्कार्यं मम वीर न संशयः।।4.40.14।।
explanation: 'O king you have understood the task to be performed and, therefore, issue orders without the least hesitation.

shloka_text: सुहृद्वितीयो विक्रान्तः प्राज्ञः कालविशेषवित्। भवानस्मध्दिते युक्त स्सुकृतार्थोऽर्थवित्तमः।।4.40.15।।
explanation: 'You are my second friend (Lakshmana being the first). You are valiant as well as wise. You are aware of timely action. You are interested in my wellbeing. You are capable. You know my purpose. You are a startegic planner'. (The present purpose is to plan the course of action. That is artha. Sugriva knows this artha very well).

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो विनतं नाम यूथपम्। अब्रवीद्रामसान्निध्ये लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः।।4.40.16।। शैलाभं मेघनिर्घोषमूर्जितं प्लवगेश्वरः।
explanation: 'In response to Rama's desire, Sugriva beckoned a troopleader called Vinata who was wellbuilt and lofty like a mountain. And thundering like a cloud, said to him in the presence of Rama and wise Lakshmana:

shloka_text: सोमसूर्यात्मजै स्सार्धं वानरैर्वानरोत्तम।।4.40.17।। देशकालनयैर्युक्तः कार्या कार्यविनिश्चये। वृतश्शतसहश्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।।4.40.18।। अधिगच्छ दिशं पूर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम्।
explanation: 'O foremost of the vanaras march forward with the sons of Moon and Sun, followed by one lakh swift monkeys towards the eastern direction full of mountains, gardens, and forests. Endowed with political wisdom, you are capable of taking right decision in accordance with time and place.

shloka_text: सोमसूर्यात्मजै स्सार्धं वानरैर्वानरोत्तम।।4.40.17।। देशकालनयैर्युक्तः कार्या कार्यविनिश्चये। वृतश्शतसहश्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।।4.40.18।। अधिगच्छ दिशं पूर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम्।
explanation: 'O foremost of the vanaras march forward with the sons of Moon and Sun, followed by one lakh swift monkeys towards the eastern direction full of mountains, gardens, and forests. Endowed with political wisdom, you are capable of taking right decision in accordance with time and place.

shloka_text: तत्र सीतां च वैदेहीं निलयं रावणस्य च।।4.40.19।। मार्गध्वं गिरिशृङ्गेषु वनेषु च नदीषु च।
explanation: 'Search for Sita in the abode of Ravana, on mountain peaks and river banks and in forests.

shloka_text: नदीं भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकीं तथा।।4.40.20।। कालिन्दीं यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वतीं च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्।।4.40.21।। महीं कालमहीं चैव शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान्विदेहांश्च मालवान्कालिकोसलान्।।4.40.22।। मागधांश्च महाग्रामान्पुण्ड्रांन्वङ्गां स्तथैव च। पत्तनं कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्।।4.40.23।।
explanation: 'Look for Sita in the beautiful places on rivers Bhagirathi, Sarayu, Kausiki and Kalindi, on the great mountains adjacent to river Yamuna, banks of rivers Saraswati, Sindhu, Sona with crystalclear waters, the country of Mahim and Kalamahi adorned with mountains and forests. Proceed to Brahmamala, Videha, Malava, Kasi, Kosala and Maghada with great villages, the country of Pundram, Vanga, the country famous for silk worms and the land with silver caves. (It is the eastern direction of river Saravati between Himavat and Vindhya and not east of Kiskinda)

shloka_text: नदीं भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकीं तथा।।4.40.20।। कालिन्दीं यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वतीं च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्।।4.40.21।। महीं कालमहीं चैव शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान्विदेहांश्च मालवान्कालिकोसलान्।।4.40.22।। मागधांश्च महाग्रामान्पुण्ड्रांन्वङ्गां स्तथैव च। पत्तनं कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्।।4.40.23।।
explanation: 'Look for Sita in the beautiful places on rivers Bhagirathi, Sarayu, Kausiki and Kalindi, on the great mountains adjacent to river Yamuna, banks of rivers Saraswati, Sindhu, Sona with crystalclear waters, the country of Mahim and Kalamahi adorned with mountains and forests. Proceed to Brahmamala, Videha, Malava, Kasi, Kosala and Maghada with great villages, the country of Pundram, Vanga, the country famous for silk worms and the land with silver caves. (It is the eastern direction of river Saravati between Himavat and Vindhya and not east of Kiskinda)

shloka_text: नदीं भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकीं तथा।।4.40.20।। कालिन्दीं यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वतीं च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्।।4.40.21।। महीं कालमहीं चैव शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान्विदेहांश्च मालवान्कालिकोसलान्।।4.40.22।। मागधांश्च महाग्रामान्पुण्ड्रांन्वङ्गां स्तथैव च। पत्तनं कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्।।4.40.23।।
explanation: 'Look for Sita in the beautiful places on rivers Bhagirathi, Sarayu, Kausiki and Kalindi, on the great mountains adjacent to river Yamuna, banks of rivers Saraswati, Sindhu, Sona with crystalclear waters, the country of Mahim and Kalamahi adorned with mountains and forests. Proceed to Brahmamala, Videha, Malava, Kasi, Kosala and Maghada with great villages, the country of Pundram, Vanga, the country famous for silk worms and the land with silver caves. (It is the eastern direction of river Saravati between Himavat and Vindhya and not east of Kiskinda)

shloka_text: नदीं भागीरथीं रम्यां सरयूं कौशिकीं तथा।।4.40.20।। कालिन्दीं यमुनां रम्यां यामुनं च महागिरिम्। सरस्वतीं च सिन्धुं च शोणं मणिनिभोदकम्।।4.40.21।। महीं कालमहीं चैव शैलकाननशोभिताम्। ब्रह्ममालान्विदेहांश्च मालवान्कालिकोसलान्।।4.40.22।। मागधांश्च महाग्रामान्पुण्ड्रांन्वङ्गां स्तथैव च। पत्तनं कोशकाराणां भूमिं च रजताकराम्।।4.40.23।।
explanation: 'Look for Sita in the beautiful places on rivers Bhagirathi, Sarayu, Kausiki and Kalindi, on the great mountains adjacent to river Yamuna, banks of rivers Saraswati, Sindhu, Sona with crystalclear waters, the country of Mahim and Kalamahi adorned with mountains and forests. Proceed to Brahmamala, Videha, Malava, Kasi, Kosala and Maghada with great villages, the country of Pundram, Vanga, the country famous for silk worms and the land with silver caves. (It is the eastern direction of river Saravati between Himavat and Vindhya and not east of Kiskinda)

shloka_text: सर्वमेतद्विचेतव्यं मृगयद्भिस्ततस्ततः। रामस्य दयितां भार्यां सीतां दशरथस्नुषाम्।।4.40.24।।
explanation: 'Search all over the place looking carefully here and there for Sita the beloved consort of Rama, daughterinlaw of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: समुद्रमवगाढांश्च पर्वतान्पत्तनानि च। मन्दरस्य च ये कोटिं संश्रिताः केचिदायताम्।।4.40.25।। कर्णप्रावरणाश्चैव तथा चाप्योष्ठकर्णकाः। घोरलोहमुखाश्चैव जवनाश्चैकपादकाः।।4.40.26।। अक्षया बलवन्तश्च पुरुषाः पुरुषादकाः। किराताः कर्ण चूडाश्च हेमाङ्गा: प्रियदर्शनाः।।4.40.27।। आममीनाशनास्तत्र किराता द्वीपवासिनः। अन्तर्जलचरा घोरा नरव्याघ्रा इति शृताः।।4.40.28।। एतेषामाश्रयास्सर्वे विचेयाः कावनौकसः। गिरिभिर्ये च गम्यन्ते प्लवनेन प्लवेन च।।4.40.29।।
explanation: 'There are people who have taken shelter in the deep pits in the midst of the sea, in deep valleys, mountains, cities and broad peaks of Mandara mountain and forests.All those regions should be thoroughly searched. There are innumerable inhabitants,such as strong cannibals, some who cover their ears, some who have ears extended up to the lips, some with dreadful metallic faces, some swiftmoving, onefooted indestructible beings. There are Kirata tribes of golden complexion and handsome looks whose tuft of hair is set to the sides so that it touches their ears. These Kiratas are Islanddwellers and they eat uncooked fish.They move in waters and are fierce, known as tigerlike men (Naravyagras because half of their body is human and other half is tiger in form). All the shelters of these forestdwellers should be searched well.Those who can be sent by crossing mountains, those who can leap (in air) and those who can swim through waters may be also dispatched.

shloka_text: रत्नवन्तं यवद्वीपं सप्तराज्योपशोभितम्। सुवर्णरूप्यकं चैव सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम्।।4.40.30।। यवद्वीपमतिक्रम्य शिशिरो नाम पर्वतः। दिवं स्पृशति शृङ्गेण देवदानवसेवितः।।4.40.31।। एतेषां गिरिदुर्गेषु प्रपातेषु वनेषु च। मार्गध्वं सहितास्सर्वे रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्।।4.40.32।।
explanation: 'Go beyond Java island filled with precious gems. It has seven kingdoms. It is adorned with gold and silver mines in abundance. There is a mountain Sisira (abode of Garuda) beyond Java Island. It touches the sky with its lofty cliffs. Gods and demons visit this mountain. You may look for illustrious Rama's consort in these inaccessible mountains, waterfalls and forests.

shloka_text: रत्नवन्तं यवद्वीपं सप्तराज्योपशोभितम्। सुवर्णरूप्यकं चैव सुवर्णाकरमण्डितम्।।4.40.30।। यवद्वीपमतिक्रम्य शिशिरो नाम पर्वतः। दिवं स्पृशति शृङ्गेण देवदानवसेवितः।।4.40.31।। एतेषां गिरिदुर्गेषु प्रपातेषु वनेषु च। मार्गध्वं सहितास्सर्वे रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्।।4.40.32।।
