shloka_text: रावणं विरथं कृत्वा स्थापयित्वा च मैथिलीम्। परिश्रान्तश्च वृद्धश्च रावणेन हतो रणे।।4.57.17।।
explanation: 'Jatayu destroyed Ravana's aerial chariot and put Maithili in a (safe) place. But being old and exhausted, he was killed in a combat by Ravana.

shloka_text: एवं गृध्रो हतस्तेन रावणेन बलीयसा। संस्कृतश्चापि रामेण गतश्च गतिमुत्तमाम्।।4.57.18।।
explanation: 'Thus the vulture was slain by Ravana who was stronger. Cremated by Rama and his last rites performed, he reached the supreme heavenly abode. (It was the luck of Jatayu, unlike Dasaratha, to be cremated by Rama.)

shloka_text: ततो मम पितृव्येण सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। चकार राघवस्सख्यं सोऽवधीत्पितरं मम।।4.57.19।।
explanation: 'Then Rama made friendship with my father's brother, great self Sugriva and killed my father.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तः करुणं वाक्यं वानरैस्त्यक्तजीवितैः। सबाष्पो वानरान्गृध्रः प्रत्युवाच महास्वनः।।4.58.1।।
explanation: On hearing the pathetic words from the monkeys who had given up hope of life, the loudvoiced vulture wailing replied:

shloka_text: यवीयान्मम भ्राता जटायुर्नाम वानराः। यमाख्यात हतं युद्धे रावणेन बलीयसा।।4.58.2।।
explanation: 'O monkeys, the one you said to have been killed by mighty Ravana in a combat was  my younger brother, Jatayu.

shloka_text: वृद्धभावादपक्षत्वाच्छृण्वंस्तदपि मर्षये। न हि मे शक्तिरस्त्यद्य भ्रातुर्वैरविमोक्षणे।।4.58.3।।
explanation: 'Even after I have heard this, I cannot avenge my brother's death as I am old, I have no wings, and I have no energy enough (to fight).

shloka_text: पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते परस्परजयैषिणौ। आदित्यमुपयातौ स्वो ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्।।4.58.4।।
explanation: 'In olden days, when Indra killed Vrutra we (Jatayu and I) seeking to challenge him reached the Sun blazing with a garland of beams.

shloka_text: आवृत्त्याऽकाशमार्गे तु जवेन स्म गतौ भृशम्। मध्यं प्राप्ते दिनकरे जटायुरवसीदति।।4.58.5।।
explanation: 'Flying in the sky at a violently high speed, we reached the meridian of the Sun when, unable to bear the heat, Jatayu became weak.

shloka_text: तमहं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सूर्यरश्मिभिरर्दितम्। पक्षाभ्यां छादयामास स्नेहात्परमविह्वलः।।4.58.6।।
explanation: 'Seeing my brother tormented due to the Sun's radiance I was overwhelmed with grief. Out of love I covered him with both my wings.

shloka_text: निर्दग्धपक्षः पतितो विन्ध्येऽहं वानरर्षभाः। अहमस्मिन्वसन्भ्रातुः प्रवृत्तिं नोपलक्षये।।4.58.7।।
explanation: 'O bulls among monkeys, consequently my wings were burnt and I dropped down on Vindhya. Here I have been living, knowing not my brother's whereabouts.'

shloka_text: जटायुषस्त्वेवमुक्तो भ्रात्रा सम्पातिना तदा। युवराजो महाप्राज्ञः प्रत्युवाचाङ्गदस्ततः।।4.58.8।।
explanation: To these words of Jatayu's brother, Sampati, Angada, the learned heir apparent replied:

shloka_text: जटायुषो यदि भ्राता श्रुतं ते गदितं मया। आख्या हि यदि जानासि निलयं तस्य रक्षसः।।4.58.9।।
explanation: 'I have heard you. If you are the brother of Jatayu, tell us about the abode of that demon if you know.

shloka_text: अदीर्घदर्शिनं तं वै रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्। अन्तिके यदि वा दूरे यदि जानासि शंस नः।।4.58.10।।
explanation: 'Tell us about Ravana, king of the demons who is unaware of the consequences. If you know his residence, tell us if it is near or far.'

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा ज्येष्ठो भ्राता जटायुषः। आत्मानुरूपं वचनं वानरान्सम्प्रहर्षयन्।।4.58.11।।
explanation: Then Jatayu's elder brother, the glorious Sampati, said these pleasing, befitting words:

shloka_text: निर्दग्धपक्षो गृध्रोऽहं हीनवीर्य: प्लवङ्गमाः। वाङ्मात्रेण तु रामस्य करिष्ये साह्यमुत्तमम्।।4.58.12।।
explanation: 'O monkeys I am a vulture. My wings are burnt and my strength is depleted. The only substantial help I can render Rama is through my words.

shloka_text: जानामि वारुणान्लोकान्विष्णोस्त्रै विक्रमानपि। महासुरविमर्दन्वा श्च ह्यमृतस्य च मन्थनम्।।4.58.13।।
explanation: 'I know Varuna's worlds(seas and oceans) and all the three worlds measured by three  strides  by Vamana. Indeed I also know about the friction between the great gods and demons and the churning of the ocean for nectar.

shloka_text: रामस्य यदिदं कार्यं कर्तव्यं प्रथमं मया। जरया च हृतं तेजः प्राणाश्च शिथिला मम।।4.58.14।।
explanation: 'Rama's work is my primary duty. (But) my strength is drained by age and I have lost my vitality.

shloka_text: तरुणी रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता। ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना।।4.58.15।। क्रोशन्ती राम रामेति लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी। भूषणान्यपविध्यन्ती गात्राणि च विधुन्वती।।4.58.16।।
explanation: 'I saw a young lady of beautiful appearance, adorned with all kinds of ornaments  borne away by the evilminded Ravana. That dainty lady was calling out, 'O Rama,  O Lakshmana' and was crying aloud. She was throwing away her ornaments and was wriggling to get out of Ravana's grip.

shloka_text: तरुणी रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता। ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना।।4.58.15।। क्रोशन्ती राम रामेति लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी। भूषणान्यपविध्यन्ती गात्राणि च विधुन्वती।।4.58.16।।
explanation: 'I saw a young lady of beautiful appearance, adorned with all kinds of ornaments  borne away by the evilminded Ravana. That dainty lady was calling out, 'O Rama,  O Lakshmana' and was crying aloud. She was throwing away her ornaments and was wriggling to get out of Ravana's grip.

shloka_text: सूर्यप्रभेव शैलाग्रे तस्याः कौशेयमुत्तमम्। असिते राक्षसे भाति यथा वा तटिदम्बुदे।।4.58.17।।
explanation: 'Her fine silk garment was shining like the radiance of the Sun on the mountain peak, like lightning against the dark cloud. (That was Ravana).

shloka_text: तां तु सीतामहं मन्ये रामस्य परिकीर्तनात्। श्रूयतां मे कथयतो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः।।4.58.18।।
explanation: 'Since she was uttering Rama's name I think she is Sita. (Now) I will tell you about the demon's abode. Listen

shloka_text: पुत्रो विश्रवस स्साक्षाद्भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च। अध्यास्ते नगरीं लङ्कां रावणो नाम राक्षसः।।4.58.19।।
explanation: 'He is Vishrava's son and halfbrother of Vaishravana. His name is Ravana and he resides in the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: इतो द्वीपस्समुद्रस्य सम्पूर्णे शतयोजने। तस्मिन्लङ्कापुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा।।4.58.20।।
explanation: 'The beautiful city of Lanka is an island, a hundred yojanas away from here.It was built by Visvakarma.

shloka_text: जाम्बूनदमयैर्द्वारैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनवेदिकैः। प्रासादैर्हेमवर्णैश्च महद्भिः सुसमा कृता।।4.58.21।। प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन महता च समान्विता।
explanation: 'The city has golden gates, golden platforms, huge, goldencoloured, uniformly built mansions surrounded by a tall boundary wall of the colour of sunlight.

shloka_text: तस्यां वसति वैदेही दीना कौशेयवासिनी।।4.58.22।। रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिस्सुरक्षिता। जनकस्यात्मजां राज्ञस्तत्र द्रक्ष्यथ मैथिलीम्।।4.58.23।।
explanation: 'You will see in the city of Lanka, the princess from Videha, daughter of Janaka, a picture of dejection, robed in silk, confined in the harem of Ravana, wellprotected by demonesses.

shloka_text: तस्यां वसति वैदेही दीना कौशेयवासिनी।।4.58.22।। रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिस्सुरक्षिता। जनकस्यात्मजां राज्ञस्तत्र द्रक्ष्यथ मैथिलीम्।।4.58.23।।
explanation: 'You will see in the city of Lanka, the princess from Videha, daughter of Janaka, a picture of dejection, robed in silk, confined in the harem of Ravana, wellprotected by demonesses.

shloka_text: लङ्कायामथ गुप्तायां सागरेण समन्ततः। सम्प्राप्य सागरस्यान्तं सम्पूर्णं शतयोजनम्।।4.58.24।। आसाद्य दक्षिणं तीरं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ रावणम्। तत्रैव त्वरिताः क्षिप्रं विक्रमध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.58.25।।
explanation: 'O monkeys traverse a hundred yojanas across the sea. On reaching the southern coast you will be able to see Ravana's Lanka defended and surrounded by the sea. Now proceed swiftly and prove your strength.

shloka_text: लङ्कायामथ गुप्तायां सागरेण समन्ततः। सम्प्राप्य सागरस्यान्तं सम्पूर्णं शतयोजनम्।।4.58.24।। आसाद्य दक्षिणं तीरं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ रावणम्। तत्रैव त्वरिताः क्षिप्रं विक्रमध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.58.25।।
explanation: 'O monkeys traverse a hundred yojanas across the sea. On reaching the southern coast you will be able to see Ravana's Lanka defended and surrounded by the sea. Now proceed swiftly and prove your strength.

shloka_text: ज्ञानेन खलु पश्यामि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागमिष्यथ। आद्यः पन्थाः कुलिङ्गानां ये चान्ये धान्यजीविनः।।4.58.26।। द्वितीयो बलिभोजानां ये च वृक्षफलाशिनः। भासास्तृतीयं गच्छन्ति क्रौञ्चाश्च कुररैस्सह।।4.58.27।। श्येनाश्चतुर्थं गच्छन्ति गृध्रा गच्छन्ति पञ्चमम्।
explanation: 'By intuition I know you would see Sita and return. On the first plane you will see sparrows and birds which live on grain. On the second, you will see crows living on the food offered to the dead and birds living on the fruits of trees, and then cocks, cranes and kraunchas moving on the third plane, on the fourth, hawks and falcons and on the fifth, vultures.

shloka_text: ज्ञानेन खलु पश्यामि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागमिष्यथ। आद्यः पन्थाः कुलिङ्गानां ये चान्ये धान्यजीविनः।।4.58.26।। द्वितीयो बलिभोजानां ये च वृक्षफलाशिनः। भासास्तृतीयं गच्छन्ति क्रौञ्चाश्च कुररैस्सह।।4.58.27।। श्येनाश्चतुर्थं गच्छन्ति गृध्रा गच्छन्ति पञ्चमम्।
explanation: 'By intuition I know you would see Sita and return. On the first plane you will see sparrows and birds which live on grain. On the second, you will see crows living on the food offered to the dead and birds living on the fruits of trees, and then cocks, cranes and kraunchas moving on the third plane, on the fourth, hawks and falcons and on the fifth, vultures.

shloka_text: बलवीर्योपपन्नानां रूपयौवनशालिनाम्।।4.58.28।। षष्ठस्तु पन्था हंसानां वैनतेयगतिः परा। वैनतेयाच्च नो जन्म सर्वेषां वानरर्षभाः।।4.58.29।।
explanation: 'O bulls among monkeys swans blessed with strength, vigour,  beauty and youth move in the sixth region. Beyond, on the seventh plane, you will see the descendants of Garuda.

shloka_text: बलवीर्योपपन्नानां रूपयौवनशालिनाम्।।4.58.28।। षष्ठस्तु पन्था हंसानां वैनतेयगतिः परा। वैनतेयाच्च नो जन्म सर्वेषां वानरर्षभाः।।4.58.29।।
explanation: 'O bulls among monkeys swans blessed with strength, vigour,  beauty and youth move in the sixth region. Beyond, on the seventh plane, you will see the descendants of Garuda.

shloka_text: इहस्थोऽहं प्रपश्यामि रावणं जानकीं तथा। अस्माकमपि सौवर्णं दिव्यं चक्षुर्बलं तथा।।4.58.30।।
explanation: 'From here I see Ravana and Janaki. We (vultures) have a divine golden vision and great power.

shloka_text: तस्मादाहारवीर्येण निसर्गेण च वानराः। आयोजनशतात्साग्राद्वयं पश्याम नित्यशः।।4.58.31।।
explanation: 'O monkeys therefore, by the strength of food and by nature we can always see beyond a hundred yojanas from this edge.

shloka_text: अस्माकं विहिता वृत्तिर्निसर्गेण च दूरतः। विहिता पादमूले तु वृत्तिश्चरणयोधिनाम्।।4.58.32।।
explanation: 'Our movement and vision naturally extends to distant places. For those fighting on foot, the movement is restricted to the extent of foot movement.

shloka_text: गर्हितं तु कृतं कर्म येन स्म पशिताशिना। प्रतीकार्यं च मे तस्य वैरं भ्रातृकृतं भवेत्।।4.58.33।।
explanation: Indeed, the reprehensible deed was done by him, the flesh-eater. And that enmity of his, done for my brother, must be avenged by me.

shloka_text: उपायो दृश्यतां कश्चिल्लङ्घने लवणाम्भसः। अभिगम्य तु वैदेहीं समृद्धार्था गमिष्यथ।।4.58.34।।
explanation: 'Look out for some means to cross the salty ocean. You will see Vaidehi, and return, your mission accomplished.

shloka_text: समुद्रं नेतुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वरुणालयम्। प्रदास्याम्युदकं भ्रातुस्स्वर्गतस्य महात्मनः।।4.58.35।।
explanation: 'Take me to the ocean, the abode of Varuna. I intend to offer oblation to my brother, a great soul who is in heaven.'

shloka_text: ततो नीत्वा तु तं देशं तीरं नदनदीपतेः। निर्दग्धपक्षं सम्पातिं वानरास्सुमहौजसः।।4.58.36।। पुनः प्रत्यानयित्वा च तं देशं पतगेश्वरम्। बभूवुर्वानरा हृष्टाः प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य ते।।4.58.37।।
explanation: Th mightiest of monkeys carried Sampati, whose wings were totally burnt, to the sea shore and after he had offered oblations took him back to the same place. Having obtained all information from the king of vultures the monkeys were very happy. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyeighth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्तदमृतास्वादं गृध्रराजेन भाषितम्। निशम्य मुदिता हृष्टास्ते वचः प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.59.1।।
explanation: The mighty monkeys were delighted to hear the nectarlike words of the king of vultures.

shloka_text: जाम्बवान् वानरश्रेष्ठस्सह सर्वैः प्लवङ्गमैः। भूतलात्सहसोत्थाय गृध्रराजानमब्रवीत्।।4.59.2।।
explanation: Jambavan the king of bears got up at once from the ground along with the monkeys and spoke to the king of vultures:

shloka_text: क्व सीता केन वा दृष्टा को वा हरति मैथिलीम्। तदाख्यातु भवात्सर्वं गतिर्भव वनौकसाम्।।4.59.3।।
explanation: 'Where is Sita now? By whom else was she seen while being carried? Pray, tell us everything. You are the ultimate saviour of monkeys.

shloka_text: को दाशरथि बाणानां वज्रवेगनिपातिनाम्। स्वयं लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां न चिन्तयति विक्रमम्।।4.59.4।।
explanation: 'Who is not aware of Rama's swift arrows which are like thunderbolt? Who is not able to assess the speed and power of arrows of Lakshmana released directly?'

shloka_text: स हरीन्प्रीतिसंयुक्तान्सीताश्रुतिसमाहितान्। पुनराश्वसयन्प्रीत: इदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.59.5।।
explanation: Pleased to see the happiness and eagernes of the monkeys assembled to hear about Sita, Sampati continued in order to reassure them:

shloka_text: श्रूयतामिह वैदेह्या यथा मे हरणं श्रुतम्। येन चापि ममाऽख्यातं यत्र वायतलोचना।।4.59.6।।
explanation: 'Now hear by whom I was informed about the abduction of the largeeyed princess from Videha and where she is at present.

shloka_text: अहमस्मिन्गिरौ दुर्गे बहुयोजनमायते। चिरान्निपतितो वृद्धः क्षीणप्राणपराक्रमः।।4.59.7।।
explanation: 'With my vitality and prowess depleted, I have been staying for a long time on this mountain, extended by several yojanas and inaccessible.

shloka_text: तं मामेवं गतं पुत्रस्सुपार्श्वोनाम नामतः। आहारेण यथाकालं बिभर्ति पततां वरः।।4.59.8।।
explanation: 'Reduced to this state, I have been maintained by food given in time by my son named Suparshva, best among birds.

shloka_text: तीक्ष्णकामास्तु गन्धर्वास्तीक्ष्णकोपा भुजङ्गमाः। मृगाणां तु भयं तीक्ष्णं ततस्तीक्ष्णक्षुधा वयम्।।4.59.9।।
explanation: 'Gandharvas have intense passion. Serpents show violent anger. Deer have great fear. And we vultures have great hunger.

shloka_text: स कदाचित्क्षुधार्तस्य ममाहाराभिकाङ्क्षिणः। गतसूर्येऽहनि प्राप्तो मम पुत्रो ह्यनामिषः।।4.59.10।।
explanation: 'Once my son came to me without meat after sunset while I was feeling hungry for food.

shloka_text: स मामाहारसंरोधात्पीडितं प्रीतिवर्धनः। अनुमान्य यथातत्त्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।4.59.11।।
explanation: 'I was thinking, tormented with hunger, my son who always keeps me happy told me exactly what had happened:

shloka_text: अहं तात यथाकालमामिषार्थी खमाप्लुतः। महेन्द्रस्य गिरेर्द्वारमावृत्य सुसमास्थितः।।4.59.12।।
explanation: 'O dear father I went to get food at the right time and stood blocking the entrance of mount Mahendra.

shloka_text: तत्र सत्त्वसहस्राणां सागरान्तरचारिणाम्। पन्थानमेकोऽध्यवसं सन्निरोद्धुमवाङ्मुखः।।4.59.13।।
explanation: 'There I stood alone  looking down, obstructing the path of thousands of creatures inhabiting the ocean.

shloka_text: तत्र कश्चिन्मया दृष्ट स्सूर्योदयसमप्रभाम्। स्त्रियमादाय गच्छन्वै भिन्नाञ्जनचयप्रभः।।4.59.14।।
explanation: 'I saw a person who was dark and huge like a mass of collyrium carrying a lady whose radiance was like the rising Sun.

shloka_text: सोऽहमभ्यवहारार्थी तौ दृष्ट्वा कृतनिश्चयः। तेन साम्ना विनीतेन पन्थानमभियाचितः।।4.59.15।।
explanation: 'Since I was looking for food I resolved to seize both of them. (But) he asked me in a gentle and courteous manner to make way (since I was blocking the aerial path).

shloka_text: न हि सामोपपन्नानां प्रहर्ता विद्यते क्वचित्। नीचेष्वपि जनः कश्चित्किमङ्ग बत मद्विधः।।4.59.16।।
explanation: 'Who will strike polite people? Even the mean do not do it anywhere. And what to speak of me.

shloka_text: स यातस्तेजसा व्योम सङ्क्षिपन्निव वेगतः। अथाऽहं खेचरैर्भूतैरभिगम्य सभाजितः।।4.59.17।।
explanation: 'He flew hurriedly with splendour as though he was enveloping the sky (making it small). All the flying creatures in the sky came and greeted me with respect.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या जीवसि तातेति ह्यब्रुवन्मां महर्षयः। कथञ्चित्सकळत्रोऽसौ गतस्ते स्वस्त्यसंशयम्।।4.59.18।।
explanation: 'I heard the great sages saying, 'O dear you are lucky to be saved. He has somehow gone from here with that lady (without hurting you). Undoubtedly you are lucky.'

shloka_text: एव मुक्तस्ततोऽहं तैस्सिद्धै: परमशोभनैः। स च मे रावणो राजा रक्षसां प्रतिवेदितः।।4.59.19।। हरन्दाशरथेर्भार्यां रामस्य जनकात्मजाम्। भ्रष्टाभरणकौशेयां शोकवेगपराजिताम्।।4.59.20।। रामलक्ष्मणयोर्नाम क्रोशन्तीं मुक्तमूर्धजाम्।
explanation: 'I was greeted by the most illustrious siddhas. I came to know from them that he was Ravana, the king of demons. I was looking at him while he was abducting Janaka's daughter, who was the wife of Dasaratha's Rama. Her ornaments had dropped and silken robes had slipped since she lost hold on herself. She was crying, loudly calling out the names of Rama and Lakshmana, her hair dishevelled.

shloka_text: एव मुक्तस्ततोऽहं तैस्सिद्धै: परमशोभनैः। स च मे रावणो राजा रक्षसां प्रतिवेदितः।।4.59.19।। हरन्दाशरथेर्भार्यां रामस्य जनकात्मजाम्। भ्रष्टाभरणकौशेयां शोकवेगपराजिताम्।।4.59.20।। रामलक्ष्मणयोर्नाम क्रोशन्तीं मुक्तमूर्धजाम्।
explanation: 'I was greeted by the most illustrious siddhas. I came to know from them that he was Ravana, the king of demons. I was looking at him while he was abducting Janaka's daughter, who was the wife of Dasaratha's Rama. Her ornaments had dropped and silken robes had slipped since she lost hold on herself. She was crying, loudly calling out the names of Rama and Lakshmana, her hair dishevelled.

shloka_text: एष कालात्ययस्तावदिति कालविदां वरः।।4.59.21।। एतमर्थं समग्रं मे सुपार्श्वः प्रत्यवेदयत्।
explanation: 'O father this is the cause of my delay', said Suparshva, who knew the value of time.                 Thus he gave the entire account to me.

shloka_text: तच्छृत्वाऽपि हि मे बुद्धिर्नासीत्काचित्पराक्रमे।।4.59.22।। अपक्षो हि कथं पक्षी कर्म किञ्चिदुपक्रमे।
explanation: 'Even after hearing this I could not advance (against Ravana). How could I, a vulture without wings, leap even a little?

shloka_text: यत्तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं वाग्बुद्धिगुणवर्तिना।।4.59.23।। श्रूयतां तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि भवतां पौरुषाश्रयम्।
explanation: 'Being endowed with the faculty of thinking and speech I shall tell you what is possible for you to execute with your prowess. Listen.

shloka_text: वाङ्मतिभ्यां तु सर्वेषां करिष्यामि प्रियं हि वः।।4.59.24।। यद्धि दाशरथेः कार्यं मम तन्नात्र संशयः।
explanation: 'I will please you with my word and thought and do not doubt that Rama's task is dear to me as well.

shloka_text: ते भवन्तो मतिश्रेष्ठा बलवन्तो मनस्विनः।।4.59.25।। प्रेषिताः कपिराजेन देवैरपि दुरासदाः।
explanation: 'Indeed, you monkeys are very wise, strong and sensitive. The king of monkeys has sent you on this mission. You cannot be conquered even by gods.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणबाणाश्च निशिताः कङ्कपत्रिणः।।4.59.26।। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पर्याप्तास्त्राणनिग्रहे।
explanation: 'The heronfeathered arrows of Rama and Lakshmana are sharp and strong enough to protect or subdue all the three worlds.

shloka_text: कामं खलु दशग्रीव स्तेजोबलसमन्वितः।।4.59.27।। भवतां तु समर्थानां न किञ्चिदपि दुष्करम्।
explanation: 'The tenheaded Ravana is mighty, powerful and strong, indeed. But you are efficient and it will not be difficult for you to achieve this task.

shloka_text: तदलं कालसङ्गेन क्रियतां बुद्धिनिश्चयः।।4.59.28।। न हि कर्मसु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः।
explanation: 'Do not bother about the time limit. Resolve to achieve the objective, for wise people  like you should not lag behind in accepting challenges.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyninth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः कृतोदकं स्नातं तं गृध्रं हरियूथपाः। उपविष्टा गिरौ रम्ये परिवार्य समन्ततः।।4.60.1।।
explanation: Sampati bathed and offered libations to Jatayu. Then all the monkeys sat round him on the beautiful mountain.

shloka_text: तमङ्गदमुपासीनं तैस्सर्वैर्हरिभिर्वृतम्। जनितप्रत्ययो हर्षात्सम्पातिः पुनरब्रवीत्।।4.60.2।।
explanation: Angada sat near Sampati surrounded by all monkeys. Sampati who had gained confidence spoke to Angada  once again joyously.

shloka_text: कृत्वा निश्शब्दमेकाग्रा श्श्रुण्वन्तु हरयो मम। तत्वं सङ्कीर्तयिष्यामि यथा जानामि मैथिलीम्।।4.60.3।।
explanation: 'O monkeys I shall tell you in detail how I came to know the princess from Mithila. Listen quietly with rapt attention:

shloka_text: अस्य विन्ध्यस्य शिखरे पतितोऽस्मि पुरावने। सूर्यतपपरीताङ्गो निर्दग्धस्सूर्यरश्मिभिः।।4.60.4।।
explanation: Scorched by the rays of the Sun, I was burnt totally and fell on the peak of this mount Vindhya years ago.

shloka_text: लब्धसंज्ञस्तु षड्रात्राद्विवशो विह्वलन्निव। वीक्षमाणो दिशस्सर्वा नाभिजानामि किञ्चन।।4.60.5।।
explanation: After six nights, having regained consciousness, I was helpless and as if bewildered. Looking in all directions, I could not recognize anything.

shloka_text: ततस्तु सागरान् शैलान्नदीस्सर्वास्सरांसि च। वनानि च प्रदेशांश्च नीरीक्ष्य मतिरागता।।4.60.6।।
explanation: 'Then I looked at the oceans, the mountains, rivers, lakes, forests and all locations and  my memory returned gradually.

shloka_text: हृष्टपक्षिगणाकीर्णः कन्दरान्तरकूटवान्। दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे विन्ध्योऽयमिति निश्चितः।।4.60.7।।
explanation: 'I came to know then that this place is inhabited by flocks of happy birds and full of many caves and mountain peaks. This is mount Vindhya on the shore of the southern ocean.

shloka_text: आसीच्चात्राश्रमं पुण्यं सुरैरपि सुपूजितम्। ऋषिर्निशाकरो नाम यस्मिन्नुग्रतपाभवत्।।4.60.8।।
explanation: 'There was a hermitage nearby, where a revered sage, who was even worshpped by gods  lived. His name was Nishakara. He did rigorous penance here.

shloka_text: अष्टौ वर्षसहस्राणि तेनास्मिन्नृषिणा विना। वसतो मम धर्मज्ञा स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे।।4.60.9।।
explanation: 'O righteous monkeys after the death of sage Nishakara eight thousand years have passed. And I have been living here.

shloka_text: अवतीर्य तु विन्ध्याग्रात्कृच्छ्रेण विषमाच्छनैः। तीक्ष्णदर्भां वसुमतीं दुःखेन पुनरागतः।।4.60.10।।
explanation: 'I descended down slowly from the high rugged peak of the Vindhya mountain with great difficulty to the plain land bristling with sharp, harsh darbha grass.

shloka_text: तमृषिं द्रष्टुकामोऽस्मि दुःखेनाभ्यागतो भृशम्। जटायुषा मया चैव बहुशोऽभिगतो हि सः।।4.60.11।।
explanation: 'Eager to see the great sage I reached the place with much difficulty. I and my brother Jatayu had  approached him many a time earlier.

shloka_text: तस्याश्रमपदाभ्याशे ववुर्वातास्सुगन्धिनः। वृक्षो वापुष्पितः कश्चिदफलो वा न विद्यते।।4.60.12।।
explanation: 'In the vicinity of that hermitage there was no tree without flowers or fruits and fragrant was the breeze that blew around.

shloka_text: उपेत्य चाश्रमं पुण्यं वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः। द्रष्टुकामः प्रतीक्षेऽहं भगवन्तं निशाकरम्।।4.60.13।।
explanation: 'On reaching the sacred hermitage, I stood and waited under a tree for the audience of the divine sage Nishakara.

shloka_text: अथापश्यमदूरस्थमृषिं ज्वलिततेजसम्। कृताभिषेकं दुर्धर्षमुपावृत्तमुदङ्मुखम्।।4.60.14।।
explanation: Then I saw a formidable sage nearby, of blazing splendor, who had performed his ablutions and returned, facing north.

shloka_text: तमृक्षास्सृमरा व्याघ्रास्सिंहा नागास्सरीसृपाः। परिवार्योपगच्छन्ति धातारं प्राणिनो यथा।।4.60.15।।
explanation: 'He was followed by bears, deer, tigers, lions, elephants and snakes just as living beings follow their creator.

shloka_text: ततः प्राप्तमृषिं ज्ञात्वा तानि सत्त्वानि वै ययुः। प्रविष्टे राजनि यथा सर्वं सामात्यकं बलम्।।4.60.16।।
explanation: 'Just as the army including feudatories recede, when the king comes, all those creatures repaired to their dens when they knew the arrival of the sage at the hermitage.

shloka_text: ऋषिस्तु दृष्ट्वा मां प्रीतः प्रविष्टश्चाश्रमं पुनः। मुहूर्तमात्रान्निष्क्रम्य ततः कार्यमपृच्छत।।4.60.17।।
explanation: The sage who entered the hermitage came out again within a moment on seeing me and enquired about me affectionately:

shloka_text: सौम्य वैकल्यतां दृष्ट्वा रोम्णां ते नावगम्यते। अग्निदग्धाविमौ पक्षौ व्रणाश्चापि शरीरके।।4.60.18।।
explanation: 'O gentle one seeing your body devoid of hair I can understood that your wings have been burnt and your body bruised.

shloka_text: गृध्रौ द्वौ दृष्टपूर्वौ मे मातरिश्वसमौ जवे। गृध्राणां चैव राजानौ भ्रातरौ कामरूपिणौ।।4.60.19।।
explanation: 'You are the king among vultures equal to wind in speed.I had seen both the brothers earlier and both of you could change your form at will.

shloka_text: ज्येष्ठो हि त्वं तु सम्पाते जटायुरनुजस्तव। मानुषं रूपमास्थाय गृह्णीतां चरणौ मम।।4.60.20।।
explanation: O Sampati, you are indeed the elder, and Jatayu is your younger brother. Let him assume a human form and grasp my feet.

shloka_text: किं ते व्याधिसमुत्थानं पक्षयोः पतनं कथम्। दण्डोऽयंच कृतः केन सर्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः।।4.60.21।।
explanation: 'What disease has affected you? Why are your wings dropped down? Who punished you in this way? Tell me.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्तद्दारुणं कर्म दुष्करं सहसात्कृतम्। आचचक्षे मुनेस्सर्वं सूर्यानुगमनं तथा।।4.61.1।।
explanation: 'Then I revealed everything to the sage,including the arrogant, impetuous action of rashly following the Sun (for challenging Indra).

shloka_text: भगवन्व्रणयुक्तत्वाल्लज्जया व्याकुलेन्द्रियः। परिश्रान्तो न शक्नोमि वचनं परिभाषितुम्।।4.61.2।।
explanation: 'O revered sage I am exhausted and my senses are depressed. I am ashamed of myself. My body is wounded. Therefore I am not able to reply.

shloka_text: अहं चैव जटायुश्च सङ्घर्षाद्धर्पमोहितौ। आकाशं पतितौ वीरौ जिज्ञासन्तौ पराक्रमम्।।4.61.3।।
explanation: 'Deluded by pride, I and my brother Jatayu challenging each other to test our relative strength flew  far into the sky.

shloka_text: कैलासशिखरे बद्ध्वा मुनीनामग्रतः पणम्। रविस्स्यादनुयातव्यो यावदस्तं महागिरिम्।।4.61.4।।
explanation: 'Both of us made a bet on the peak of mount Kailasa in the presence of sages to follow the Sungod until he sets on the western mountain.

shloka_text: अथाऽवां युगपत्प्राप्तावपश्याव महीतले। रथचक्रप्रमाणानि नगराणि पृथक्पृथक्।।4.61.5।।
explanation: 'And from there both of us looked at all the cities on the land which seemed like the size of chariot wheels one after the other.

shloka_text: क्वचिद्वादित्रघोषांश्च ब्रह्मघोषांश्च शुश्रुवः। गायन्तीश्चाङ्गना बह्वीः पश्यावो रक्तवाससः।।4.61.6।।
explanation: 'We heard at some places sounds of musical instruments, sounds of Vedic chanting, and many lovely young women dressed in redsinging.

shloka_text: तूर्णमुत्पत्य चाकाशमादित्यपथमाश्रितौ। आवामालोकयावस्तद्वनं शाद्वलसन्निभम्।।4.61.7।।
explanation: 'We flew quickly into the sky and reached the path of the Sun and looked down at the forest which looked like a green lawn.

shloka_text: उपलैरिव सञ्छन्ना दृश्यते भूश्शिलोच्चयैः। आपगाभिश्च संवीता सूत्रैरिव वसुन्धरा।।4.61.8।।
explanation: 'The earth filled with lofty mountains appeared as if it is covered with pebbles. Surrounded by rivers meandering, it looked as though it was entwined with threads.

shloka_text: हिमवांश्चैव विन्ध्यश्च मेरुश्च सुमहान्नगः। भूतले सम्प्रकाशन्ते नागा इव जलाशये।।4.61.9।।
explanation: 'The mountains of the earth, Himavan and Vindhya and the great Meru looked like huge elephants in a huge pond.

shloka_text: तीव्रस्स्वेदश्च खेदश्च भयं चासीत्तदाऽऽवयोः। समाविशति मोहश्च तमो मूर्छा च दारुणा।।4.61.10।।
explanation: 'Much sweat, pain and fear generated in us while we went on and up. This led to terrific confusion and stupor.

shloka_text: न दिग्विज्ञायते याम्या नाग्नेयी न च वारुणी। युगान्ते नियतो लोको हतो दग्ध इवाग्निना।।4.61.11।।
explanation: 'I did not know which the southern direction was or the southeast or the west. It looked as if the world had been consumed by fire and dissolved, as if it was the end of the yuga.

shloka_text: मनश्च मे हतं भूयस्सन्निवर्त्यतु संश्रयम्। यत्नेन महता ह्यस्मिन्पुनस्सन्धाय चक्षुषी।।4.61.12।। यत्नेन महता भूयो भास्करः प्रतिलोकितः। तुल्यः पृथ्वीप्रमाणेन भास्करः प्रतिभाति नौ।।4.61.13।।
explanation: 'My mind was disturbed and I turned my attention from the object. Once again I focused my attention (on the Sun) and could see the Sungod with great effort. The Sun appeared to us equal in size to earth.

shloka_text: मनश्च मे हतं भूयस्सन्निवर्त्यतु संश्रयम्। यत्नेन महता ह्यस्मिन्पुनस्सन्धाय चक्षुषी।।4.61.12।। यत्नेन महता भूयो भास्करः प्रतिलोकितः। तुल्यः पृथ्वीप्रमाणेन भास्करः प्रतिभाति नौ।।4.61.13।।
explanation: 'My mind was disturbed and I turned my attention from the object. Once again I focused my attention (on the Sun) and could see the Sungod with great effort. The Sun appeared to us equal in size to earth.

shloka_text: जटायुर्मामनापृच्छ्य निपपात महीं ततः। तं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमाकाशादात्मानं मुक्तवानहम्।।4.61.14।।
explanation: 'Without taking leave of me Jatayu descended down to the earth. Seeing that, I also followed him down quickly from the sky.

shloka_text: पक्षाभ्यां च मया गुप्तो जटायुर्न प्रदह्यते। प्रमादात्तत्र निर्दग्धः पतन्वायुपथादहम्।।4.61.15।।
explanation: 'I protected Jatayu with my wings so that he was not burnt. I, however, got burnt miserably and fell down from the aerial region.

shloka_text: आशङ्के तं निपतितं जनस्थाने जटायुषम्। अहं तु पतितो विन्ध्ये दग्धपक्षो जडीकृतः।।4.61.16।।
explanation: 'I thought Jatayu had fallen down somewhere at Janasthana, but I fell on Vindhya, wings burnt, in an unconscious state.

shloka_text: राज्येन हीनो भ्रात्रा च पक्षाभ्यां विक्रमेण च। सर्वथा मर्तुमेवेच्छन्पतिष्ये शिखराद्गीरेः।।4.61.17।।
explanation: 'Bereft of my kingdom, my brother and my wings, and having lost my strength I desire to fall down from the mountain top and die.' इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfirst sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता मुनिश्रेष्ठ मरुदं दुःखितो भृशं। अथ ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तु भगवानिदमब्रवीत्।।4.62.1।।
explanation: 'When thus I spoke to the venerable sage in that manner roaring very painfully the divine sage replied after reflecting silently for a moment:

shloka_text: पक्षौ तु ते प्रपक्षौ च पुनरन्यौभविष्यतः। प्राणाश्च चक्षुषी चैव विक्रमश्च बलं च ते।।4.62.2।।
explanation: 'You will get new wings and feathers and also other parts.You will attain vision, life, prowess and strength.

shloka_text: पुराणे सुमहत्कार्यं भविष्यति मया श्रुतं। दृष्टं मे तपसा चैव श्रुत्वा च विदितं मम4.62.3।।
explanation: 'I have foreseen with the power of my penance that a great task will be done by you. I have also heard about it in the Puranas and came to know of it.

shloka_text: राजा दशरथो नाम कश्चिदिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः। तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा रमोनाम भविष्यति।।4.62.4।।
explanation: 'Indeed in the Ikshvaku family there will be a king named Dasaratha. He will beget a brilliant son named Rama.

shloka_text: अरण्यं च सह र्भात्रा लक्ष्मणेनगमिष्यति। अस्मिन्नर्थे नियुक्त स्सन्पित्रा सत्यपराक्रमः।।4.62.5।।
explanation: 'On account of the command of his father, Rama armed with the strength of truth will proceed to the forest with his brother Lakshmana.

shloka_text: नैऋतो रावणो नाम तस्य भार्यां हरिष्यति। राक्षसेन्द्रो जनस्थनादवध्य स्सुरदानवैः4.62.6।।
explanation: 'The king of demons, Ravana who is indestructible even by gods and demons will be abducting his wife from Janastahana.

shloka_text: सा च कामैः प्रलोभ्यन्ती भक्ष्यै:भोज्यैश्च मैथिली। नभोक्ष्यति महाभागा दुःखे मग्ना यशस्विनी।।4.62.7।।
explanation: 'Immersed in grief, chaste and famed Sita, will not take any food or enjoy pleasures however much she is tempted.

shloka_text: परमान्नंतु वैदेह्या ज्ञात्वा दास्यति वा सः। यदन्नममृतप्रख्यं सुराणामपिदुर्लभम्4.62.8।।
explanation: 'Knowing that Vaidehi is not eating food(given by Ravana) Indra,the ruler of gods, will offer nectarlike food rare even for gods.

shloka_text: तदन्नं मैथिलीप्राप्य विज्ञायेन्द्रादिदंत्विति। अग्रमुदृत्य रामाय भूतले निर्वपिष्यति।।4.62.9।।
explanation: 'Having understood that it has been provided by Indra, Sita will take out a large portion of it and pour it on the ground (as an offering to Rama) and say 'I offer it to Rama wherever he is on earth'.

shloka_text: यदि जीवति मे भर्ता लक्ष्मणेन सह प्रभुः। देवत्वं गच्छ्तो र्वापि तयो रन्नमिदंत्विति4.62.10।।
explanation: 'If my husband and Lakshmana are living or else even if they have attained heaven let this food be enjoyed by them', Sita will say.

shloka_text: एष्यन्त्यन्वेषका स्तस्या रामदूताः प्लवांगमाः। आख़्येया राम महीषी त्वया तेभ्यो विहंगम4.62.11।।
explanation: 'Rama's messenger and other monkeys will be coming to search for the his queen. O Sampati you should narrate this to them.

shloka_text: सर्वथा हि नगन्तव्यमीदृशः क्व गमिष्यसि। देशकालौ प्रतीक्षस्व पक्षौ त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे4.62.12।।
explanation: 'It is good for you in all respects to remain here. Where can you go (without wings)? Wait for appropriate time and place. You will recover your wings'.

shloka_text: नोत्सहेयमहंकर्तुमध्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थ स्त्वं तु लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि।।4.62.13।।
explanation: 'I am not enthusiastic about giving you the wings now. Remain here and carry on the work for the welfare of the world.

shloka_text: त्वयापि खलु तत्कार्यं तयोश्चनृपपुत्रयोः। ब्राह्मणानां सुराणां च मुनीनां वासवस्य च।।4.62.14।।
explanation: '(Carry on) the work not only for the princes (Rama and Lakshmana) but also for the brahmins, sages, gods and others who live here.

shloka_text: इच्छाम्यहमपिद्रष्टुं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। नेच्छेचिरं धारयुतुं प्राणां स्त्यक्ष्ये कलेबरं। महर्षि स्त्वब्रवीदेवं दृष्टतत्वार्थदर्शनः।।4.62.15।।
explanation: 'I also want to see Rama and Lakshmana. But I do not like to hold on to my life for long. Hence I will give up my body'. The knower of self, the sage (Nishakara) said this to Sampati. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे  द्विषष्टितम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysecond sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्वाक्यविशारदः। मां प्रशस्याभ्यनुज्ञाप्य प्रविष्टस्स स्वमालयम्।।4.63.1।।
explanation: 'The sage who was skilful in speech, having  praised me thus and in many other ways,  permitted me to leave and entered his dwelling.

shloka_text: कन्दरात्तु विसर्पित्वा पर्वतस्य शनैश्शनैः। अहं विन्ध्यं समारुह्य भवतः प्रतिपालये।।4.63.2।।
explanation: 'Having crawled slowly and slowly from the cave and climbed the Vindhya, I have been awaiting your arrival.

shloka_text: अद्य त्वेतस्य कालस्य साग्रं वर्षशतं गतम्। देशकालप्रतीक्षोऽस्मि हृदि कृत्वा मुनेर्वचः।।4.63.3।।
explanation: 'More than a hundred years have passed and all this time I have borne the sage's words in my heart and have waited for the right time and place.

shloka_text: महाप्रस्थानमासाद्य स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे। मां निर्दहति सन्तापो वितर्कैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्।।4.63.4।।
explanation: 'Nishakara went on his last journey and attained heaven. Since then many sad thoughts have crisscrossed my mind and I am consumed with those thoughts.

shloka_text: उत्थितां मरणे बुद्धिं मुनिवाक्यैर्निवर्तये। बुद्धिर्या तेन मे दत्ता प्राणानां रक्षणाय तु।।4.63.5।। सा मेऽपनयते दुःखं दीप्तेवाग्निशिखा तमः।
explanation: 'Whenever I intended to die, the words of the sage rang in my mind. The inspiration he gave me to preserve my life removed my agony like the glowing flames of fire that take away darkness.

shloka_text: बुद्ध्यता च मया वीर्यं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।।4.63.6।। पुत्रस्सन्तर्जितो वाग्भिर्न त्राता मैथिली कथम्।
explanation: 'I goaded my son with harsh words saying, 'Knowing the valour of the evilminded Ravana, why did you not protect her (Sita)'

shloka_text: तस्या विलपितं श्रुत्वा तौ च सीताविनाकृतौ।।4.63.7।। न मे दशरथस्नेहात्पुत्रेणोत्पादितं प्रियम्।
explanation: 'Even after hearing the wailing of Sita, knowing that both (Rama and Lakshmana) are separated from her and considering my friendship with Dasaratha, I felt displeased with my son (as he did not make an attempt to rescue her)'.

shloka_text: तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य सम्पातेर्वानरैस्सह।।4.63.8।। उत्पेततुस्तदा पक्षौ समक्षं वनचारिणाम्।
explanation: Even as he was telling this to the monkeys his wings started appearing in their presence.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा स्वां तनुं पक्षैरुद्गतैररुणच्छदैः।।4.63.9।। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे वानरांश्चेदमब्रवीत्।
explanation: He experienced an unparalleled delight seeing wings with red feathers growing on his body, and said to the monkeys:

shloka_text: ऋषेर्निशाकरस्यैव प्रभावादमितात्मन:।।4.63.10।। आदित्यरश्मिनिर्दग्धौ पक्षौ मे पुनरुपस्थितौ।
explanation: 'By the grace of the most revered soul,sage Nishakara, both my wings that were burnt by the Sun's radiance have grown again.

shloka_text: यौवने वर्तमानस्य ममासीद्यः पराक्रमः।।4.63.11।। तमेवाद्यावगच्छामि बलं पौरुषमेव च।
explanation: 'The valour, strength and even courage that I had in my youth,I am experiencing now.

shloka_text: सर्वथा क्रियतां यत्न स्सीतामधिगमिष्यथ।।4.63.12।। पक्षलाभो ममायं वस्सिद्धिप्रत्ययकारकः।
explanation: Make every effort; you will find Sita. This support of mine will be the cause of your conviction in success.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा स तान्हरीन् सर्वान्सम्पातिः पतगोत्तमः।।4.63.13।। उत्पपात गिरेश्शृङ्गाज्जिज्ञासुः खगमो गतिम्।
explanation: Sampati, the foremost of the birds thus spoke to the monkeys and flew up from the mountain's peak keen on finding the aerial path.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रतिसंहृष्टमानसाः।।4.63.14।। बभूवुर्हरिशार्दूला विक्रमाभ्युदयोन्मुखाः।
explanation: The tigers among monkeys felt very happy on hearing the words of Sampati and became sure of their success with their valour.

shloka_text: अथ पवनसमानविक्रमाः प्लवगवराः प्रतिलब्धपौरुषाः। अभिजिदभिमुखा दिशं ययु र्जनकसुतापरिमार्गणोन्मुखाः।।4.63.15।।
explanation: The monkeys as strong as the wind regained courage and went in search of the daughter of Janaka in the direction of Abhijit (constellation known as Abhijit is associated with success). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtythird sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: आख्याता गृध्रराजेन समुत्प्लुत्य प्लवङ्गमाः। सङ्गताः प्रीतिसंयुक्ता विनेदुर्भीमविक्रमाः।।4.64.1।।
explanation: Hearing the words spoken by the king of vultures, the highly courageous monkeys assembled together and leaped with joyscreaming.

shloka_text: सम्पातेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयो रावणक्षयम्। हृष्टास्सागरमाजग्मुस्सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः।।4.64.2।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Sampati, the monkeys felt glad and, eager to see Sita, reached the ocean, the passage to the abode of Ravana.

shloka_text: अभिक्रम्य तु तं देशं ददृशुर्भीमविक्रमाः। कृत्स्नं लोकस्य महतः प्रतिबिम्बमिव स्थितम्।।4.64.3।।
explanation: Having reached the ocean, the monkeys, endowed with frightening courage, stood looking at the vast ocean which appeared like an image of the whole world.

shloka_text: दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य समासाद्योत्तरां दिशम्। सन्निवेशं ततश्चक्रुर्हरिवीरा महाबलाः।।4.64.4।।
explanation: Powerful and heroic monkeys assembled at the northern end of the southern ocean.

shloka_text: सत्त्वैर्महद्भिर्विकृतैः क्रीडद्भिर्विविधैर्जले। व्यात्तास्यैस्सुमहाकायैरूर्मिभिश्च समाकुलम्।।4.64.5।। प्रसुप्तमिव चान्यत्र क्रीडन्तमिव चान्यतः। क्वचित्पर्वतमात्रैश्च जलराशिभिरावृतम्।।4.64.6।। सङ्कुलं दानवेन्द्रैश्च पातालतलवासिभिः। रोमहर्षकरं दृष्ट्वा विषेदु: कपिकुञ्जराः।।4.64.7।।
explanation: The ocean was of terrifying form filled with various violent species of grotesque creatures of huge bodies playing in the water. Full of violent tides, it appeared asleep at one place and apparently sporting in another. In some places it was rising as high as a mountain with huge volumes of water. It was as if roaring with the demon chiefs residing in the underworld. The great monkeys were worried seeing the huge ocean which created horripilation in them.

shloka_text: आकाशमिव दुष्पारं सागरं प्रेक्षय वानराः। विषेदु स्सहसासर्वे कथं कार्यमिति ब्रुवन्।।4.64.8।।
explanation: All the monkeys were worried when they suddenly saw the ocean which looked impassable like the sky. They wondered if they can at all accomplish the task (of finding Sita)

shloka_text: विषण्णां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा सागरस्य निरीक्षणात्। आश्वासयामास हरीन्भयार्तान् हरिसत्तमः।।4.64.9।।
explanation: Angada, the best among the monkeys saw the worried army despondent gazing at the ocean, and comforted the frightened troops.

shloka_text: तान्विषादेन महता विषण्णान्वानरर्षभान्। उवाच मतिमान्काले वालिसूनुर्महाबलः।।4.64.10।।
explanation: Angada,the strong and wise  son of Vali, spoke thus to the tensed vanaras in the right time:

shloka_text: न विषादे मनः कार्यं विषादो दोषवत्तमः। विषादो हन्ति पुरुषं बालं क्रुद्ध इवोरगः।।4.64.11।।
explanation: 'Do not be despondent. It is the biggest flaw. It destroys a person like an angry serpent killing a young child.

shloka_text: यो विषादं प्रसहते विक्रमे पर्युपस्थिते। तेजसा तस्य हीनस्य पुरुषार्थो न सिध्यति।।4.64.12।।
explanation: 'If one succumbs to despondency while he has to exhibit his valour, his brilliance gets diminished and he does not succeed in his manly pursuits'.

shloka_text: तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामङ्गदो वानरैस्सह। हरिवृद्धैस्समागम्य पुनर्मन्त्रममन्त्रयत्।।4.64.13।।
explanation: With the night over, Angada joined the older monkeys again and sought their counsel.

shloka_text: सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी परिवार्याङ्गदं बभौ। वासवं परिवार्येव मरुतां वाहिनी स्थिता।।4.64.14।।
explanation: The army of monkeys encircled Angada like the army of Maruts surrounding Indra.

shloka_text: कोऽन्यस्तां वानरीं सेनां शक्त:स्तम्भयितुं भवेत्। अन्यत्र वालितनयादन्यत्र च हनूमतः।।4.64.15।।
explanation: Who else other than the son of Vali and Hanuman can resist and pacify the monkeyarmy?

shloka_text: ततस्तान्हरिवृद्धांश्च तच्च सैन्यमरिन्दमः। अनुमान्याङ्गदश्श्रीमान्वाक्यमर्थवदब्रवीत्।।4.64.16।।
explanation: Then the illustrious Angada, subduer of foes took the counsel of elderly monkeys and  the army into confidence and thus addressed them all in meaningful words:

shloka_text: क इदानीं महातेजा लङ्घयिष्यति सागरम्। कः करिष्यति सुग्रीवं सत्यसन्धमरिन्दमम्।।4.64.17।।
explanation: 'Now which mighty monkey will cross the ocean? Who will prove Sugriva, subduer of enemies, true to his promise?

shloka_text: को वीरो योजनशतं लङ्घयेत प्लवङ्गमाः। इमांश्च यूथपान् सर्वान्मोक्षयेत्को महाभयात्।।4.64.18।।
explanation: 'O monkeys which one can leap a hundred yojanas and liberate the monkey leaders from the great fear of Sugriva?

shloka_text: कस्य प्रभावाद्धारांश्च पुत्रांश्चैव गृहाणि च। इतो निवृत्ताः पश्येम सिद्धार्थास्सुखिनो वयम्।।4.64.19।।
explanation: 'By whose effort can we be successful and return home happily from here to meet wives and sons?

shloka_text: कस्य प्रसादाद्रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्। अभिगच्छेम संहृष्टास्सुग्रीवं च वनौकसम्।।4.64.20।।
explanation: 'By whose grace shall we approach Rama and Lakshmana and even the monkey king Sugriva happily?

shloka_text: यदि कश्चित्समर्थो वस्सागरप्लवने हरिः। स ददा त्विह न शशीघ्रं पुण्यामभयदक्षिणाम्।।4.64.21।।
explanation: 'If there is any one among you who is capable of leaping  across the ocean he will be giving all of us the sacred gift of life quickly?'

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्य वच श्शृत्वा न कश्चित् किञ्चिदब्रवीत्। स्तिमिते वा भवत्सर्वा सा तत्र हरिवाहिनी।।4.64.22।।
explanation: After hearing Angada, no one spoke a word. The entire army of monkeys became still and motionless.

shloka_text: पुनरेवाङ्गदः प्राह तान्हरीन्हरिसत्तमः। सर्वे बलवतां श्रेष्ठा भवन्तो दृढविक्रमाः।।4.64.23।। व्यपदेश्य कुले जाताः पूजिताश्चाप्यभीक्ष्णशः।
explanation: Angada, the best of the monkeys again addressed them saying, 'you are all mighty, eminent and courageous, born in renowned families and have been honoured again and again(for your actions).

shloka_text: न हि वो गमने सङ्गः कदाचित्कस्यचित्क्वचित्। ब्रुवध्वं यस्य या शक्तिः प्लवने प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.64.24।।
explanation: 'None of you at any time have faced any obstruction in doing your deeds. You are efficient  in leaping. O bulls among monkeys now speak out, who among you can fly and how far? इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfourth sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथाङ्गदवचश्श्रुत्वा ते सर्वे वानरर्षभाः। स्वं स्वं गतौ समुत्साहमूचुस्तत्र यथाक्रमम्।।4.65.1।। गजो गवाक्षो गवयश्शरभो गन्धमादनः। मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव सुषेणो जाम्बवां स्तथा।।4.65.2।।
explanation: Thereafter, on hearing Angada, all the leaders among the monkeys, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Mainda, Dvivida, Sushena and Jambavan as well expressed one after  the other their capability for leaping.

shloka_text: अथाङ्गदवचश्श्रुत्वा ते सर्वे वानरर्षभाः। स्वं स्वं गतौ समुत्साहमूचुस्तत्र यथाक्रमम्।।4.65.1।। गजो गवाक्षो गवयश्शरभो गन्धमादनः। मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव सुषेणो जाम्बवां स्तथा।।4.65.2।।

shloka_text: आबभाषे गजस्तत्र प्लवेयं दशयोजनम्। गवाक्षो योजननान्याह गमिष्यामीति विंशतिम्।।4.65.3।।
explanation: Gaja said he can leap ten yojanas and Gavaksha said he can go upto twenty yojanas.

shloka_text: गवयो वानरस्तत्र वानरां स्तानुवाच ह। त्रिंशतं तु गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.65.4।। शरभस्तानुवाचाथ वानरान् वानरर्षभः। चत्वारिंशद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.65.5।। वानरस्तु महातेजा अब्रवीद्गन्धमादनः। योजनानां गमिष्यामि पञ्चाशत्तु न संशयः।।4.65.6।। मैन्दस्तु वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह। योजनानां परं षष्टिमहं प्लवितुमुत्सहे।।4.65.7।। ततस्तत्र महातेजा द्विविदः प्रत्यभाषत। गमिष्यामि न सन्देहस्सप्ततिं योजनान्यहम्।।4.65.8।। सुषेणस्तु महातेजा:प्रोक्तवान्हरिसत्तमान्। अशीतिं योजनानां तु प्लवेयं प्लवगेश्वराः।।4.65.9।।
explanation: Then Gavaya said to the monkeys 'I can leap thirty yojanas Sarabha said 'I can leap forty yojanas' bright Ghandhamadana said 'I can leap as far as fifty yojanas without any doubt' Mainda said 'I can leap more than sixty yojanas' highly brilliant Dvivida said in turn, 'I can no doubt leap seventy yojanas ' brilliant and best of the monkeys Sushena declared 'I can leap across eighty yojanas'.

shloka_text: गवयो वानरस्तत्र वानरां स्तानुवाच ह। त्रिंशतं तु गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.65.4।। शरभस्तानुवाचाथ वानरान् वानरर्षभः। चत्वारिंशद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.65.5।। वानरस्तु महातेजा अब्रवीद्गन्धमादनः। योजनानां गमिष्यामि पञ्चाशत्तु न संशयः।।4.65.6।। मैन्दस्तु वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह। योजनानां परं षष्टिमहं प्लवितुमुत्सहे।।4.65.7।। ततस्तत्र महातेजा द्विविदः प्रत्यभाषत। गमिष्यामि न सन्देहस्सप्ततिं योजनान्यहम्।।4.65.8।। सुषेणस्तु महातेजा:प्रोक्तवान्हरिसत्तमान्। अशीतिं योजनानां तु प्लवेयं प्लवगेश्वराः।।4.65.9।।
explanation: Then Gavaya said to the monkeys 'I can leap thirty yojanas Sarabha said 'I can leap forty yojanas' bright Ghandhamadana said 'I can leap as far as fifty yojanas without any doubt' Mainda said 'I can leap more than sixty yojanas' highly brilliant Dvivida said in turn, 'I can no doubt leap seventy yojanas ' brilliant and best of the monkeys Sushena declared 'I can leap across eighty yojanas'.

shloka_text: तेषां कथयतां तत्र सर्वांस्ताननुमान्य च। ततो वृद्धतमस्तेषां जाम्बवान्प्रत्यभाषत।।4.65.10।।
explanation: When the monkeys were talking (of their individual capacity) in that manner about their speed, Jambavan the oldest of the monkeys inferred (their capacity) and said:

shloka_text: पूर्वमस्माकमप्यासीत्कश्चिद्गतिपराक्रमः। ते वयं वयसः पारमनुप्राप्तास्स्म साम्प्रतम्।।4.65.11।।
explanation: 'Earlier I was also very courageous, but now I have become old and reached the fag end of life.

shloka_text: किन्तु नैवं गते शक्यमिदं कार्यमुपेक्षितुम्। यदर्थं कपिराजश्च रामश्च कृतनिश्चयौ।।4.65.12।।
explanation: 'However  in this situation, it is not possible for us to neglect (our task) as it is the order of the monkeyking and Rama who are determined to achieve the objective.

shloka_text: साम्प्रतं कालभेदेन या गतिस्तां निबोधत। नवतिं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामि न संशयः।।4.65.13।।
explanation: Now, understand the speed that varies with time. I will certainly travel ninety yojanas, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: तांश्च सर्वान्हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवान्पुनरब्रवीत्। न खल्वेतावदेवासीद्गमने मे पराक्रमः।।4.65.14।।
explanation: Jambavan, the distinguished among the monkeys again said, 'My strength to leap into the sky was not only that much (I was stronger in my youth and could cover longer distances)'

shloka_text: मया महाबलेश्चैव यज्ञे विष्णुस्सनातनः। प्रदक्षिणीकृतः पूर्वं क्रममाणस्त्रिविक्रमम्।।4.65.15।।
explanation: 'In the past, at the time of the wellknown yagna (of king Bali) I was very strong. I circumambulated the eternal Vishnu while he was taking three strides (in his incarnation of Trivikrama Vamana.)

shloka_text: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः प्लवने मन्दविक्रमः। यौवने च तदाऽसीन्मे बलमप्रतिमं परैः।।4.65.16।।
explanation: 'Having grown old I do not have the same courage. In my youth my prowess was incomparable and none could excel me.

shloka_text: सम्प्रत्येतावतीं शक्तिं गमने तर्कयाम्यहम्। नैतावता हि संसिद्धिः कार्यस्यास्य भविष्यति।।4.65.17।।
explanation: 'I guess that at this time I do not have the capacity to fly to that extent. Achieving the objective is out of question with this much of energy.

shloka_text: अथोत्तरमुदारार्थमब्रवीदङ्गदस्तदा। अनुमान्य तथा प्राज्ञो जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिम्।।4.65.18।।
explanation: 'Then the wise Angada said to great Jambavan, in a gentle manner about his  own strength.

shloka_text: अहमेतद्गमिष्यामि योजनानां शतं महत्। निवर्तने तु मे शक्तिस्स्यान्न वेति न निश्चितम्।।4.65.19।।
explanation: 'I can  certainly go to a distance of a hundred yojanas. However, I cannot say whether I will have enough capacity to return?

shloka_text: तमुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठं जाम्बवान्वाक्यकोविदः। ज्ञायते गमने शक्तिस्तव हर्यृक्षसत्तम।।4.65.20।।
explanation: Jambavan who was skilful in speech spoke to that great Angada, 'O leader among monkeys and bears your energy to cover this distance is wellknown to us'.

shloka_text: कामं शतं सहस्रं वा न ह्येष विधिरुच्यते। योजनानां भवान् शक्तो गन्तुं प्रतिनिवर्तितुम्।।4.65.21।।
explanation: 'You can go upto even a hundred thousand yojanas and have the required energy to return also. But it is not proper to send you (because you are the heir apparent).

shloka_text: न हि प्रेषयिता तात स्वामी प्रेष्यः कथञ्चन। भवताऽयं जनस्सर्वः प्रेष्यः प्लवगसत्तम।।4.65.22।।
explanation: Indeed, O dear one, the sender, the master, is never a messenger in any way. All these people are to be commanded by you, O best among monkeys.

shloka_text: भवान्कळत्रमस्माकं स्वामिभावे व्यवस्थितः। स्वामी कळत्रं सैन्यस्य गतिरेषा परन्तप।।4.65.23।।
explanation: 'O scorcher of enemies, you are established as the commander of the army and it is proper for us to protect you as we protect our wives.

shloka_text: अपि चैतस्य कार्यस्य भवान्मूलमरिन्दम। तस्मात्कळत्रवत्तात प्रतिपाल्यस्सदा भवान्।।4.65.24।।
explanation: 'O subduer of enemies in acomplishing this task you are the root. O dear therefore you should always be taken care of by us just like the wife looked after.

shloka_text: मूलमर्थस्य संरक्ष्यमेष कार्यविदां नयः। मूले सति हि सिद्ध्यन्ति गुणा फलो पुष्पोदयाः।।4.65.25।।
explanation: 'The root of any objective should be protected well. This is the basis of an accomplisher. Only when the roots are intact, the trees have the ability to yield flowers and fruits.

shloka_text: तद्भवानस्य कार्यस्य साधने सत्यविक्रम। बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नो हेतुरत्र परन्तप।।4.65.26।।
explanation: 'O warrior of proven valour O subduer of enemies in achieving this objective you are the source, being endowed with valour and wisdom.

shloka_text: गुरुश्च गुरुपुत्रश्च त्वं हि नः कपिसत्तम। भवन्तमाश्रित्य वयं समर्था ह्यर्थसाधने।।4.65.27।।
explanation: 'O best of monkeys you are the son of my guide (Vali) and respectable. We will be capable of accomplishing the goal only under your protection and guidance.

shloka_text: उक्तवाक्यं महाप्राज्ञं जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः। प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वाक्यं वालिसूनुरथाङ्गदः।।4.65.28।।
explanation: Jambavan, the wise monkey having said that, Angada, the great son of Vali, replied:

shloka_text: यदि नाहं गमिष्यामि नान्यो वानरपुङ्गवः। पुनः खल्विदमस्माभिः कार्यं प्रायोपवेशनम्।।4.65.29।।
explanation: 'If I do not go and no other monkey leader goes, then we have to resort to fasting unto death once again.

shloka_text: न ह्यकृत्वा हरिपतेस्सन्देशं तस्य धीमतः। तत्रापि गत्वा प्राणानां पश्यामि परिरक्षणम्।।4.65.30।।
explanation: 'If I do not fulfil the objective of the wise king of monkeys I cannot save my life even after returning there (Kishkinda).

shloka_text: स हि प्रसादे चात्यर्थं कोपे च हरिरीश्वरः। अतीत्य तस्य सन्देशं विनाशो गमने भवेत्।।4.65.31।।
explanation: 'The monkey king has the authority to shower grace or give vent to his anger. If we go without fulfilling the task we will face destruction.

shloka_text: तद्यथा ह्यस्य कार्यस्य न भवत्यन्यथा गतिः। तद्भवानेव दृष्टार्थस्सञ्चिन्तयितु मर्हति।।4.65.32।।
explanation: 'Therefore, think over well so that we do not fail ultimately. You have a vision.You should suggest means by which this mission does not misfire.'

shloka_text: सोऽङ्गदेन तदा वीरः प्रत्युक्तः प्लवगर्षभः। जाम्बवानुत्तरं वाक्यं प्रोवाचेदं ततोऽङ्गदम्।।4.65.33।।
explanation: On listening to Angada's words, Jambavan, the  bull among monkeys, replied this way:

shloka_text: अस्य ते वीर कार्यस्य न किञ्चित्परिहीयते। एष सञ्चोदयाम्येनं यः कार्यं साधयिष्यति।।4.65.34।।
explanation: 'O hero this work will not be balked. I will now inspire one who can achieve this task.'

shloka_text: अनेकशतसाहस्रीं विषण्णां हरिवाहिनीम्। जाम्बवान्समुदीक्ष्यैवं हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्।।4.66.1।।
explanation: Then Jambavan observed the worries of several hundred thousands of the monkey army and said to Hanuman:

shloka_text: वीर वानरलोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविदां वर। तूष्णीमेकान्तमाश्रित्य हनूमन्किं न जल्पसि।।4.66.2।।
explanation: 'O Hanuman you are the choicest one among many scholars wellversed in all sastras. Why do you sit alone? Why do you not speak?

shloka_text: हनूमन्हरिराजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो ह्यसि। रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि तेजसा च बलेन च।।4.66.3।।
explanation: 'Hanuman you are equal to the king of monkeys and also Rama and Lakshmana in brilliance and strength.

shloka_text: अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रो वैनतेयो महाबलः। गरुत्मानिति विख्यात उत्तमस्सर्वपक्षिणाम्।।4.66.4।।
explanation: 'You are the son of Arishtanemi (sage Kasyapa) and Vinata, and your gurulike (elder brother) is Garuda, the greatest among birds. He is powerful and and famous.

shloka_text: बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः। भुजङ्गानुद्धरन्पक्षी महावेगो महायशाः।।4.66.5।।
explanation: 'Garuda is very powerful, swift, and famous. I have seen him snatching serpents from the ocean many times.

shloka_text: पक्षयोर्यद्बलं तस्य तावद्भुजबलं तव। विक्रमश्चापि वेगश्च न ते तेनावहीयते।।4.66.6।।
explanation: 'The strength of your shoulders is equal to that of his (Garuda's) wings. Your speed and valour are no less.

shloka_text: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न बुध्यसे।।4.66.7।।
explanation: 'O leader of the monkeys you are superior in strength, wisdom, brilliance and valour to all beings. Why do you not realise your own strength?

shloka_text: अप्सराप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा विख्याता पुञ्जिकस्थला। अञ्जनेति परिख्याता पत्नी केसरिणो हरेः।।4.66.8।।
explanation: The celestial nymph, best among the Apsaras, famous as Puñjikasthalā, was also known as Añjanā, the wife of Kesari, the monkey.

shloka_text: विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि। अभिशापादभूत्तात वानरी कामरूपिणी।।4.66.9।।
explanation: 'O dear she was famous in the three worlds, peerless in beauty and could change form at her free will. She was born of a monkey on this land by dint of a curse.

shloka_text: दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी।।4.66.10।। विचित्रमाल्याभरणा महार्हक्षौमवासिनी। अचरत्पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसन्निभे।।4.66.11।।
explanation: 'She was the daughter of a great king of monkeys called Kunjara. That young and beautiful lady had assumed a lustrous human form decked with wonderful garlands, ornaments and silk clothes and was roving on top of the mountain which appeared like a proud raincloud.

shloka_text: दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः। मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी।।4.66.10।। विचित्रमाल्याभरणा महार्हक्षौमवासिनी। अचरत्पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसन्निभे।।4.66.11।।
explanation: 'She was the daughter of a great king of monkeys called Kunjara. That young and beautiful lady had assumed a lustrous human form decked with wonderful garlands, ornaments and silk clothes and was roving on top of the mountain which appeared like a proud raincloud.

shloka_text: तस्या वस्त्रं विशालाक्ष्याः पीतं रक्तदशं शुभम्। स्थितायाः पर्वतस्याग्रे मारुतोऽपहरच्छनैः।।4.66.12।।
explanation: 'While the largeeyed lady was stationed on the mountain top, the Windgod gently let her auspicious yellow garment with red border fly away.

shloka_text: स ददर्श ततस्तस्या वृत्तावूरू सुसंहतौ। स्तनौ च पीनौ सहितौ सुजातं चारु चाननम्।।4.66.13।।
explanation: 'Then he (Windgod) saw her curved, wellset thighs, her beautiful plump breasts and her lovely pleasing face.

shloka_text: तां विशालायतश्रोणीं तनुमध्यां यशस्विनीम्। दृष्टवैव शुभसर्वाङ्गीं पवनः काममोहितः।।4.66.14।।
explanation: 'On seeing the broad hips, slender waist and beautiful limbs of that famous lady the Windgod was infatuated.

shloka_text: स तां भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः। मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्।।4.66.15।।
explanation: 'The Windgod lost his control over himself. His whole being was overpowered by love for her beautiful, flawless body. He embraced her with his long arms.

shloka_text: सा तु तत्रैव सम्भ्रान्ता सुव्रता वाक्यमब्रवीत्। एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति।।4.66.16।।
explanation: 'She was bewildered by this and being chaste and strict observer of chastiny she said, 'Who is it that has destroyed my monoandry?

shloka_text: अञ्जनाया वच्शुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत। न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत्ते सुभगे भयम्।।4.66.17।।
explanation: 'On hearing Anjana's words, the Windgod replied, ' O auspicious lady, I do you no harm, O lady of beautiful hips. I reached (enjoyed) you in mind, not body. You need not fear.'

shloka_text: मनसाऽस्मि गतो यत्त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनीम्। वीर्यवान्बुद्धिसम्पन्न: पुत्रस्तव भविष्यति।।4.66.18।।
explanation: 'O renowned lady I have embraced you and united with you mentally (enjoyed you without physical contact).You will bring forth a son endowed with great wisdom and courage.

shloka_text: महासत्त्वो महातेजा महाबलपराक्रमः। लङ्घने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति हि मत्समः।।4.66.19।।
explanation: 'He will be very powerful, illustrious and will be of great valour and strength. He will be my equal in leaping and flying'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता ततस्तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपे। गुहायां त्वां महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभम्।।4.66.20।।
explanation: 'O great monkey O strongshouldered one having been assured that way, your mother was pleased and delivered you, a bull among monkeys, in a cave.

shloka_text: अभ्युत्थितं ततस्सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने। फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्युद्गतो दिवम्।।4.66.21।।
explanation: 'On seeing the rising Sun in the deep forest, mistaking him to be a fruit, you wanted to seize it, when you were young.You suddenly flew into the sky and went flying towards the Sun.

shloka_text: शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाऽथ योजनानां महाकपे। तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं ततोगतः।।4.66.22।।
explanation: 'O great monkey you went three hundred yojanas and were pushed back by the  Sun's radiance. Yet it did not leave you depressed.

shloka_text: तावदापपत स्तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे। क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं कोपाविष्टेन धीमता।।4.66.23।।
explanation: 'O great monkey while falling fast in space, wise Indra hurled his thunderbolt quickly at you, in anger.

shloka_text: तदा शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत। ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्त्यते।।4.66.24।।
explanation: 'You fell on the edge of the mountain peak and your left chin  got broken. Since then you are widely known as Hanuman (one who has a wounded chin).

shloka_text: तस्त्वावि निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहस्स्वयम्। त्रैलोक्ये भृशसङ्कृद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः।।4.66.25।।
explanation: The Windgod who is a carrier of fragrance and breaker of trees became very angry on seeing (the injury on) you and stopped blowing in the three worlds.

shloka_text: सम्भ्रान्ताश्च सूरास्सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति। प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः।।4.66.26।।
explanation: And all the bewildered gods, when the three worlds were agitated, the lords of the worlds appeased the greatly enraged Maruta.

shloka_text: प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ। अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम।।4.66.27।।
explanation: 'O dear when the Windgod was pleased, Brahma gave a boon to you, to appease his anger. The boon made you truly valiant so that you cannot be struck by any weapon and killed.

shloka_text: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च। सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्।।4.66.28।। स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तेभूयादिति वै प्रभो।
explanation: 'O lord observing that you are not hurt even when struck by the thunderbolt, Indra offered, one of the best boons to you, to choose to die only when you wish.

shloka_text: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
explanation: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

shloka_text: स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः।।4.66.29।। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः। त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः।।4.66.30।।
explanation: 'You are a son of Kesari endowed with terrific strength and a lawful son of Maruta also. You are, therefore, equal to the very Windgod in flying and in brilliance.

shloka_text: वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवान्नस्त्रातु साम्प्रतम्। दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः कपिराज इवापरः।।4.66.31।।
explanation: 'Now we have almost lost our life.You are our saviour like another monkeyking (like Garuda, king of birds).You are fully endowed with valour and courage.

shloka_text: त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना। त्रिस्सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्।।4.66.32।।
explanation: 'O dear when Visnu (Vamana incarnate) took three strides I circumambulated the whole earth including its mountains and trees twentyone times.

shloka_text: तथा चौषधयोऽस्माभिस्सञ्चिता देवशासनात्। निष्पन्नममृतं याभिस्तदासीन्नो महद्बलम्।।4.66.33।।
explanation: 'Then on receiving orders from the gods, we collected medicinal herbs and nectar which gave us great strength.

shloka_text: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान्सर्वगुणान्वितः।।4.66.34।।
explanation: 'I have become old and my valour is depleted. At this time you are the sole resort for us. You have all the necessary qualities.

shloka_text: तद्विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्त: प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि। त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामा हि सर्वा वानरवाहिनी।।4.66.35।।
explanation: 'Cheer up and advance.You are the best among the creatures that can leap.The entire army of monkeys want to see your valour.

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्। परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन्या गतिस्तव।।4.66.36।।
explanation: 'O Hanuman, tiger among monkeys, rise up and cross this great ocean.You have that supreme capacity among all beings.

shloka_text: विषण्णा हरयस्सर्वे हनुमन्किमुपेक्षसे। विक्रमस्व महावेगो विष्णुस्त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.66.37।।
explanation: 'O Hanuman All the monkeys look dejected. Why do you delay? O warrior, act quick with your rapid speed like Trivikrama who took three strides that covered the entire universe'.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
explanation: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्। वीर्येणापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्।।4.67.1।। सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः। विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्।।4.67.2।।
explanation: 'In order to cross a hundred yojanas, Hanuman, the best of monkeys expanded his  might and strength. Seeing him, a warrior of great strength, all the monkeys, filled with enthusiasm at once gave up grief and collected together.They rejoiced and propitiated him screaming aloud.

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताश्चैव वीक्षन्ते स्म समन्ततः। त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहं नारायणमिव प्रजाः।।4.67.3।।
explanation: The monkeys collected together happily, gazing at Hanuman.They were wonderstruck to see Hanuman in that huge form, just as all beings were when they saw Lord Narayana in his incarnation of Vamana.

shloka_text: संस्तूयमानो हनुमान्व्यवर्धत महाबलः। समाविध्य च लाङ्गूलं हर्षाद्बलमुपेयिवान्।।4.67.4।।
explanation: The monkeys praised the mighty Hanuman as he grew in size whirling his tail around joyfully.

shloka_text: तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य सर्वैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः। तेजसापूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्।।4.67.5।।
explanation: As Hanuman was being praised by the monkey leaders, his body filled with lustre. It looked excellent.

shloka_text: यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृद्धो गिरिगह्वरे। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तथा सम्प्रति जृम्भते।।4.67.6।।
explanation: Just as a lion grown in a mountain cave stretches its body, the Windgod's son stretched  (his limbs) at that time.

shloka_text: अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः। अम्बरीषमिवाऽदीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः।।4.67.7।।
explanation: On expansion, wise Hanuman's face was bright, glowing like a burning oven and  shining like smokeless fire.

shloka_text: हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात्सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः। अभिवाद्य हरीन्वृद्धान्हनुमानिदमब्रवीत्।।4.67.8।।
explanation: Hanuman risen from the midst of the monkeys with his hair bristling on the body (due to expansion of body), saluted reverentially to the elderly monkey Jambavan and said :

shloka_text: अरुजत्सर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः। बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः।।4.67.9।।
explanation: 'The Windgod is a friend of fire who is a powerful consumer of oblations. His strength is immeasurable. He wanders in the sky and shatters the mountain tops.

shloka_text: तस्याहं शीघ्रवेगस्य शीघ्रगस्य महात्मनः। मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रः प्लवनेनास्मि तत्समः।।4.67.10।।
explanation: 'I am the lawfulson of the swiftmoving Windgod, Maruta, comparable to him in leaping.

shloka_text: उत्सहेयं हि विस्तीर्णमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्। मेरुं गिरिमसङ्गेन परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.11।।
explanation: 'I can with all enthusiasm go round the vast mount Meru a thousand times without resting on it which is as though scratching the sky.

shloka_text: बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे। समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्।।4.67.12।।
explanation: 'I can submerge this world including its mountains rivers and lakes. I can push back the sea waters quickly with my arms.

shloka_text: ममोरुजङ्घावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः। सम्मूर्च्छितमहाग्राहस्समुद्रो वरुणालयः।।4.67.13।।
explanation: 'Thrust by my thighs,the ocean will rise up, carrying with it the shanks and  mighty crocodiles stunned by the force.

shloka_text: पन्नगाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेविते। वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः।।4.67.14।।
explanation: 'I am capable of circumambulating a thousand times the great Garuda who consumes snakes and flies in the sky, the abode of birds.

shloka_text: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
explanation: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

shloka_text: उदयात्प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्। अनस्तमितमादित्यमभिगन्तुं समुत्सहे।।4.67.15।। ततो भूमिमसंस्पृश्य पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे। प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः।।4.67.16।।
explanation: 'O bull among monkeys when the Sun rises from behind the eastern mountain it is possible for me to start with him and go to the western horizon and return before the blazing Sun with its beams of light sets. It is also possible for me to descend to  the earth with the same speed and return to the Sun without touching the earth.

shloka_text: उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्। सागरं क्षोभयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्।।4.67.17।।
explanation: 'If I rise up, I can overtake all those creatures flying in the sky and from there I can stir up the ocean and tear up the earth easily.

shloka_text: पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि प्लवमानः प्लवङ्गमाः। हरिष्याम्यूरुवेगेन प्लवमानो महार्णवम्।।4.67.18।।
explanation: 'O monkeys when I leap, I can crush the mountains into powder and pull the vast ocean with me with the force of my thighs.

shloka_text: लतानां विविधं पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः। अनुयास्यन्ति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा।।4.67.19।।
explanation: And then as I leap through the sky flowers of many kinds of creepers and trees will follow me.

shloka_text: भविष्यति हि मे पन्थास्स्वातेः पन्था इवाम्बरे। चरन्तं घोरमाकाशमुत्पतिष्यन्तमेव वा।।4.67.20।। द्रक्ष्यन्ति निपतिष्यन्तं च सर्वभूतानि वानराः।
explanation: 'O monkey when I fly upward in the dreadful sky or descend down, all creatures will see me, for my path will be the path of the constellation of Swati (a group of stars).

shloka_text: महामेरुप्रतीकाशं मां द्रक्ष्यथ वानराः।।4.67.21।। दिवमावृत्य गच्छन्तं ग्रसमानमिवाम्बरम्।
explanation: 'O monkeys when I fly in the sky like the great mount Meru, you will see me as if I am swallowing the sky because I will be enveloping it with my strides.

shloka_text: विधमिष्यामि जीमूतान्कम्पयिष्यामि पर्वतान्।।4.67.22।। सागरं शोषयिष्यामि प्लवमानस्समाहितः।
explanation: I will scatter the clouds, I will make the mountains tremble. I will dry up the ocean, flying with concentration.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
explanation: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्य या शक्तिर्मम सा मारुतस्य वा।।4.67.23।। ऋते सुपर्णराजानं मारुतं वा महाजवम्। न तद्भूतं प्रपश्यामि यन्मां प्लुतमनुव्रजेत्।।4.67.24।।
explanation: 'Only Garuda and Maruta have the capacity to fly like me. No one other than the king of vultures and the Windgod have the speed to fly like me.

shloka_text: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण निरालम्बनमम्बरम्। सहसा निपतिष्यामि घनाद्विद्युदिवोत्थिता।।4.67.25।।
explanation: 'Just as the lightning generated by the clouds lands at once flying in the sky without any support I can also land in less than a moment.

shloka_text: भविष्यति हि मे रूपं प्लवमानस्य सागरे। विष्णोर्विक्रममाणस्य पुरा त्रीन्विक्रमानिव।।4.67.26।।
explanation: My form will indeed be floating in the ocean, just as Vishnu in ancient times took his three strides.

shloka_text: बुद्ध्या चाहं प्रपश्यामि मनश्चेष्टा च मे तथा। अहं द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं प्रमोदध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः।।4.67.27।।
explanation: 'O monkeys I have a feeling in my mind that I will see Vaidehi. Be happy.

shloka_text: मारुतस्य समो वेगे गरुडस्य समो जवे। अयुतं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामीति मे मतिः।।4.67.28।।
explanation: 'I am equal to Maruta and Garuda in speed. I feel I can cover ten thousand yojanas (at a stretch).

shloka_text: वासवस्य सवज्रस्य ब्रह्मणो वा स्वयम्भुवः। विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तादमृतं तदिहानये।।4.67.29।। लङ्कां वापि समुत्क्षिप्य गच्छेयमिति मे मतिः।
explanation: 'I think I can encounter Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and obtain nectar from his hands. I can even confront Brahma, the selfborn creator courageously. I can even uproot Lanka and carry it.'

shloka_text: तमेवं वानरश्रेष्ठं गर्जन्तममितौजसम्।।4.67.30।। प्रहृष्टा हरयस्तत्र समुदैक्षन्त विस्मिताः।
explanation: The monkeys looked at him and were amazed, happy to see him roaring and shining in brilliance.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ज्ञातीनां शोकनाशनम्।।4.67.31।। उवाच परिसंहृष्टो जाम्बवान्हरिसत्तमः।
explanation: Jambavan, the finest of the monkeys, felt very glad on hearing his words which put an end to the sorrow of the kith and kin and said:

shloka_text: वीर केसरिणः पुत्र हनुमान्मारुतात्मज।।4.67.32।। ज्ञातीनां विपुलश्शोकस्त्वया तात प्रणाशितः।
explanation: 'O son of Kesari O son of Maruta O hero you have removed the great grief of your race, dear

shloka_text: तव कल्याणरुचयः कपिमुख्यास्समागताः।।4.67.33।। मङ्गलं कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं करिष्यन्ति समाहिताः।
explanation: Your chief monkeys, whose inclinations are towards welfare, have arrived. They will, with concentration, perform auspicious acts for the accomplishment of the task.

shloka_text: ऋषीणां च प्रसादेन कपिवृद्धमतेन च।।4.67.34।। गुरूणां च प्रसादेन प्लवस्व त्वं महार्णवम्।
explanation: 'By the blessings of the sages and by the grace of the elderly monkeys may you cross over the vast ocean.

shloka_text: स्थास्यामश्चैकपादेन यावदागमनं तव।।4.67.35।। त्वद्गतानि च सर्वेषां जीवनानि वनौकसाम्।
explanation: We shall stand on one foot until your arrival, and the lives of all the forest-dwellers are dependent on you.

shloka_text: ततस्तु हरिशार्दूलस्तानुवाच वनौकसः।।4.67.36।। नेयं मम मही वेगं लङ्घने धारयिष्यति।
explanation: Then the tiger among monkeys, Hanuman said to those forestdwellers (monkeys), 'The earth cannot bear the thrust of my leaping.

shloka_text: एतानीह नगस्यास्य शिलासङ्कटशालिनः।।4.67.37।। शिखराणि महेन्द्रस्य स्थिराणि सुमहान्ति च।
explanation: 'The rocks on the peaks of the ranges of mount Mahendra cannot with stand it, although they are huge and firm.

shloka_text: एषु वेगं करिष्यामि महेन्द्रशिखरेष्वहम्।।4.67.38।। नानाद्रुमविकीर्णेषु धातुनिष्यन्दशोभिषु।
explanation: 'I will pick up speed on the peaks of mount Mahendra filled with different kinds of trees and minerals.

shloka_text: एतानि मम निष्पेषं पादयोः प्लवतां वराः।।4.67.39।। प्लवतो धारयिष्यन्ति योजनानामितश्शतम्।
explanation: 'O great monkeys these mountain peaks can withstand the crushing force of my feet as I leap over a hundred yojanas.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: ततस्तं मारुतप्रख्यस्सहरिर्मारुतात्मजः।।4.67.40।। आरुरोह नगश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रमरिमर्दनः। वृतं नानाविधैः वृक्षैर्मृगसेवितशाद्वलम्।।4.67.41।। लताकुसुमसम्बाधं नित्यपुष्पफलद्रुमम्। सिंहशार्दूलचरितं मत्तमातङ्गसेवितम्।।4.67.42।। मत्तद्विजगणोद्घुष्टं सलिलोत्पीडसङ्कुलम्।
explanation: The son of Maruta, who was as eminent as the Windgod, the crusher of enemies ascended the great mountain Mahendra, full of grassland inhabited by deer, thickly grown with various trees and creepers full of fragrant flowers and fruits, where roam lions and tigers and proud elephants, a place that echoes with sounds of intoxicated birds and waterfalls.

shloka_text: महद्भिरुच्छ्रितं शृङ्गैर्महेन्द्रं स महाबलः।।4.67.43।। विचचार हरिश्रेष्ठो महेन्द्रसमविक्रमः।
explanation: The mighty, preeminent monkey who was equal to Indra in valour took a leap from the high peaks of the tall mountain, Mahendra৷৷

shloka_text: पादाभ्यां पीडितस्तेन महाशैलो महात्मना।।4.67.44।। रराज सिंहाभिहतो महान्मत्त इव द्विपः।
explanation: Crushed by the feet of the great self, Hanuman, the huge mountain looked like a proud elephant struck by a lion.

shloka_text: मुमोच सलिलोत्पीडान्विप्रकीर्णशिलोच्चयः।।4.67.45।। वित्रस्तमृगमातङ्गः प्रकम्पितमहाद्रुमः।
explanation: The rocks of the mountain got scattered by the force. The deer and elephants were terrified. The trees were shaken up violently and streams of water gushed forth.

shloka_text: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
explanation: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

shloka_text: नानागन्धर्वमिथुनैः पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः।।4.67.46।। उत्पतद्भिश्च विहगैर्विद्याधरगणैरपि। त्यज्यमानमहासानुस्सन्निलीनमहोरगः।।4.67.47।। चलशृङ्गशिलोद्घातस्तदाऽभूत्स महागिरिः।
explanation: Shaken by the rude shock, couples of intoxicated gandharvas left in a huff the vast slopes of the great mountain. Flocks of birds and groups of vidyadharas flew away. The serpents went into hiding. Rocks fell off the shaken mountain.

shloka_text: निश्श्वसद्भिस्तदाऽर्तैस्तु भुजङ्गैरर्धनि:सृतैः।।4.67.48।। सपताक इवाभाति स तदा धरणीधरः।
explanation: The serpents with their bodies half protruded out of the rocks and hissing looked like flags planted on the mountain.

shloka_text: ऋषिभिस्त्राससम्भ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानः शिलोच्चयः।।4.67.49।। सीदन्महति कान्तारे सार्थहीन इवाध्वगः।
explanation: The alarmed and agitated sages abandonned the mountain peaks.The mountain appeared like a lone traveller separated from the caravan in the great forest.

shloka_text: सवेगवान् वेगसमाहितात्मा हरिप्रवीरः परवीरहन्ता। मनस्समाधाय महानुभावो जगाम लङ्कां मनसा मनस्वी।।4.67.50।।
explanation: Magnanimous, wise and heroic Hanuman, destroyer of enemy warriors, fixed his attention on speed, betook himself mentally to Lanka (ere he reached it physically). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामाणये वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyseventh sarga in Kishkindakanda of the first epic, the Holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः। इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि।।5.1.1।।
explanation: Hanuman, crusher of enemies resolved to find the whereabouts of Sita, carried away by Ravana. He followed the path of the Charanas, celestial bards.

shloka_text: दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः। समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवांपतिरिवाबभौ।।5.1.2।।
explanation: Hanuman who raised his head and neck, intending to cross the formidable ocean which none else could accomplish, looked like a leading bull.

shloka_text: अथ वैडूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः। धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विचचार यथासुखम्।।5.1.3।।
explanation: Tawnyhued Hanuman, gifted with extraordinary strength and patience happily strolled on the marshy tracts of grassy land which had the colour of vaidurya.

shloka_text: द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन्। मृगांश्च सुबहून्निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी।।5.1.4।।
explanation: Wise Hanuman went about like a lion scaring away birds, uprooting trees with his chest, and trampling many animals.

shloka_text: नीललोहितमांजिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः। स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलङ्कृतम्।।5.1.5।। कामरूपिभिराविष्टमभीक्ष्णं सपरिच्छदैः। यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्देवकल्पैश्च पन्नगैः।।5.1.6।।
