The arms bore the marks of wounds caused by Airavata, (Indra's elephant), torn by the thunderbolt of Indra in war, and wounded by the discus of Lord Visnu. His strong, fleshy, wellbuilt arms, having auspicious thumbnails, shapely fingers and palms, pressed together, resembled the iron crowbars or beam used for main doors. The arms resembled elephant's trunks, tossed on a clean bed, resembling two fivehooded snakes (fingers like hoods), besmeared with cool, fragrant, red sandalpaste of excellent quality which looked red like the hare's blood. They were well massaged  by the best of women with fine, fragrant sandal paste. They were the arms which could make yakshas, pannagas, gods and demons roar in fear at their sight.

shloka_text: ददर्श स कपिस्तत्र बाहू शयनसंस्थितौ। मन्दरस्यांतरे सुप्तौ महाही रुषिताविव।।5.10.21।।
explanation: The vanara, gazed at the arms of Ravana placed on the couch that appeared like two angry snakes asleep in a cave on (the lap) of mount Mandara.

shloka_text: ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः। शुशुभेऽचलसङ्काशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः।।5.10.22।।
explanation: The lord of demons looked splendid like a mountain with his long, fully developed arms. He appeared like Mandara mountain with two lofty peaks.

shloka_text: चूतपुन्नागसुरभिर्वकुलोत्तमसंयुतः। मृष्टान्नरससंयुक्तः पानगन्धपुरस्कृतः।।5.10.23।। तस्य राक्षससिंहस्य निश्चक्राम महामुखात्। शयानस्य विनिःश्वासः पूरयन्निव तद् गृहम्।।5.10.24।।
explanation: The breath released from the huge mouth of that lion of demons carried the fragrance of mango and punnaga as well as excellent Bakula flowers. It exuded the aroma of rich and delicious food and different drink. It was as though pervading the whole chamber.

shloka_text: मुक्तामणिविचित्रेण काञ्चनेन विराजितम्। मकुटेनापवृत्तेन कुण्डलोज्वलिताननम्।।5.10.25।। रक्तचन्दनदिग्धेन तथा हारेण शोभिना। पीनायतविशालेन वक्षसाऽभिविराजितम्।।5.10.26।। पाण्डरेणापविद्धेन क्षौमेण क्षतजेक्षणम्। महार्हेण सुसंवीतं पीतेनोत्तमवाससा।।5.10.27।। माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।5.10.28।। चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैर्दीपैद्धीप्यमानचतुर्दिशम्। प्रकाशीकृतसर्वाङ्गं मेघं विद्युद्गणैरिव।।5.10.29।। पादमूलगताश्चापि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः। पत्नी: स प्रियभार्यस्य तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे।।5.10.30।।
explanation: Hanuman saw Ravana, whose face was lit up by his earrings. His shining headgear studded with gold and pearls was set aside. His fleshy, broad chest on which the pearl necklace had slightly receded from its position(as he was asleep)  was shining along with the red sandal paste. He had put on a splendid white silken cloth which had also slipped a little and was covered with exquisitely  rich yellow upper garment. His eyes were bloodred. His body was comparable to a heap of blackbeans. He was sighing heavily like a hissing snake. He appeared like an elephant sleeping on the banks of the great river Ganges. With four golden lamps glowing on four sides of the bed,the four directions were illuminated. All his limbs lit up bright (with the glow of lamps), he looked like a cloud with streaks of lightning. His dear wives were seen resting at his feet in the palace of the lord of demons.

shloka_text: मुक्तामणिविचित्रेण काञ्चनेन विराजितम्। मकुटेनापवृत्तेन कुण्डलोज्वलिताननम्।।5.10.25।। रक्तचन्दनदिग्धेन तथा हारेण शोभिना। पीनायतविशालेन वक्षसाऽभिविराजितम्।।5.10.26।। पाण्डरेणापविद्धेन क्षौमेण क्षतजेक्षणम्। महार्हेण सुसंवीतं पीतेनोत्तमवाससा।।5.10.27।। माषराशिप्रतीकाशं निश्श्वसन्तं भुजङ्गवत्। गाङ्गे महति तोयान्ते प्रसुप्तमिव कुञ्जरम्।।5.10.28।। चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैर्दीपैद्धीप्यमानचतुर्दिशम्। प्रकाशीकृतसर्वाङ्गं मेघं विद्युद्गणैरिव।।5.10.29।। पादमूलगताश्चापि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः। पत्नी: स प्रियभार्यस्य तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे।।5.10.30।।
explanation: Hanuman saw Ravana, whose face was lit up by his earrings. His shining headgear studded with gold and pearls was set aside. His fleshy, broad chest on which the pearl necklace had slightly receded from its position(as he was asleep)  was shining along with the red sandal paste. He had put on a splendid white silken cloth which had also slipped a little and was covered with exquisitely  rich yellow upper garment. His eyes were bloodred. His body was comparable to a heap of blackbeans. He was sighing heavily like a hissing snake. He appeared like an elephant sleeping on the banks of the great river Ganges. With four golden lamps glowing on four sides of the bed,the four directions were illuminated. All his limbs lit up bright (with the glow of lamps), he looked like a cloud with streaks of lightning. His dear wives were seen resting at his feet in the palace of the lord of demons.

shloka_text: शशिप्रकाशवदनाश्चारुकुण्डलभूषिताः। अम्लानमाल्याभरणा ददर्श हरियूथपः।।5.10.31।।
explanation: Hanuman, the leader of vanaras found the wives of Ravana,  whose  faces were bright as the Moon, adorned with beautiful earrings and fresh floral garlands.

shloka_text: नृत्तवादित्रकुशला राक्षसेन्द्रभुजाङ्कगाः। वराभरणधारिण्यो निषण्णा ददृशे हरिः।।5.10.32।।
explanation: Hanuman saw  the women there wearing fine jewellery, performing dances, playing musical instruments, and resting on the lap or leaning on the arms of the demon king.

shloka_text: वज्रवैडूर्यगर्भाणि श्रवणान्तेषु योषिताम्। ददर्श तापनीयानि कुण्डलान्यङ्गदानि च।।5.10.33।।
explanation: He noticed on the earlobes of the the women gold earrings decked with diamonds and vaidurya. They were wearing shining armlets of gold.

shloka_text: तासां चन्द्रोपमैर्वक्त्रैश्शुभैर्ललितकुण्डलैः। विरराज विमानं तन्नभस्तारागणैरिव।।5.10.34।।
explanation: There the beautiful moonlike faces of women Illumined by the lovely earrings lay on the cot which looked resplendent like the sky lit up with hosts of stars.

shloka_text: मदव्यायामखिन्नास्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य योषितः। तेषु तेष्ववकाशेषु प्रसुप्तास्तनुमध्यमाः।।5.10.35।।
explanation: Exhausted by drinking and indulging in amorous sport, the consorts of Ravana slept here and there with their visible slender waists.

shloka_text: अङ्गहारैस्तथैवान्या कोमलैर्नृत्तशालिनी। विन्यस्तशुभसर्वाङ्गी प्रसुप्ता वरवर्णिनी।।5.10.36।।
explanation: Another woman exceedingly beautiful and a delicate danseuse of beautiful complexion and rhythmic movements held her limbs in a dancing posture (though asleep) due to her habit .

shloka_text: काचिद्वीणां परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता सम्प्रकाशते। महानदीप्रकीर्णेव नलिनी पोतमाश्रिता।।5.10.37।।
explanation: Another woman slept hugging her veena. She shone like a lotus plant flung in a large river, clinging on to a boat. (Veena is compared to a boat and the woman to a lotusplant in the ambience of flowing waters of the river. The entire hall had put up such a dynamic view showing hectic life of the inmates).

shloka_text: अन्या कक्षगतेनैव मड्डुकेनासितेक्षणा। प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बालपुत्रेव वत्सला।।5.10.38।।
explanation: A woman with dark eyes asleep with a drum placed in her armpit looked like a beautiful mother holding her loving baby (the drum was hung to her arm with a rope).

shloka_text: पटहं चारुसर्वाङ्गी पीड्य शेते शुभस्तनी। चिरस्य रमणं लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्येव भामिनी।।5.10.39।।
explanation: Another charming beauty endowed with beautiful breasts lay hugging a tambourine as though a passionate woman lay embracing her lover whom she secured after a long time.

shloka_text: काचिद्वंशं परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमललोचना। रहः प्रियतमं गृह्य सकामेव च कामिनी।।5.10.40।।
explanation: Yet another lotuseyed lady slept embracing a lute as if a lovelorn woman lay clasping her lover.

shloka_text: विपञ्चीं परिगृह्यान्या नियता नृत्तशालिनी। निद्रावशमनुप्राप्ता सह कान्तेव भामिनी।।5.10.41।।
explanation: Another selfpossessed lady, graceful in dance, holding a sevenstringed lute  was as though lying asleep with her beloved.

shloka_text: अन्या कनकसङ्काशैर्मृदुपीनैर्मनोरमैः। मृदङ्गं परिपीड्याङ्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्तलोचना।।5.10.42।।
explanation: Another lady with drunken eyes lay fast asleep holding a drum close to her beautiful bosom with her soft limbs. (These images show that these women were singing and dancing till late night and slept exhausted).

shloka_text: भुजपार्श्वान्तरस्थेन कक्षगेन कृशोदरी। पणवेव सहानिन्द्या सुप्ता मदकृतश्रमा।।5.10.43।।
explanation: Another lady of slender belly, who had been exhausted by drunkeness was lying with a tabor pressed to her bosom and inserted in her armpit.

shloka_text: डिण्डिमं परिगृह्यान्या तथैवासक्तडिण्डिमा। प्रसुप्ता तरुणं वत्समुपगूह्येव भामिनी।।5.10.44।।
explanation: One lovely woman and another held a drum and slept as if they were hugging their young child.

shloka_text: काचिदाडम्बरं नारी भुजसंयोगपीडितम्। कृत्वा कमलपत्राक्षी प्रसुप्ता मदमोहिता।।5.10.45।।
explanation: Yet another with her eyes like lotus petals deluded with passion tightly held in her arms a musical instrument known as Adambaram and slept.

shloka_text: कलशीमपविध्यान्या प्रसुप्ता भाति भामिनी। वसन्ते पुष्पशबला मालेव परिमार्जिता।।5.10.46।।
explanation: Another lovely lady was fast asleep, having turned a goblet of water  aside, yet another lay like a garland of variegated flowers in spring season.

shloka_text: पाणिभ्यां च कुचौ काचित्सुवर्णकलशोपमौ। उपगूह्याबला सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिता।।5.10.47।।
explanation: Overcome with sleep another woman lay pressing with her own hands her golden gobletlike breasts.

shloka_text: अन्या कमलपत्राक्षी पूर्णेन्दुसदृशानना। अन्यामालिङ्ग्य सुश्रोणीं प्रसुप्ता मदविह्वला।।5.10.48।।
explanation: One woman with eyes like lotus petals and face like the fullmoon embraced another young woman of beautiful hips  and slept tipsy with drink.

shloka_text: आतोद्यानि विचित्राणि परिष्वज्य वरस्त्रियः। निपीड्य च कुचैस्सुप्ता कामिन्यः कामुकानिव।।5.10.49।।
explanation: Some charming maidens held wonderful musical instruments pressing against their bosom and slept like passionate women embracing their loved ones.

shloka_text: तासामेकान्तविन्यस्ते शयानां शयने शुभे। ददर्श रूपसम्पन्नामपरां स कपिः स्त्रियम्।।5.10.50।।
explanation: Hanuman saw some maidens lying on separate excellent beds, women richly  endowed with beautysleeping.

shloka_text: मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम्। विभूषयन्तीमिव तत्स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम्।।5.10.51।। गौरीं कनकवर्णाभामिष्टामन्तः पुरेश्वरीम्। कपिर्मन्दोदरीं तत्र शयानां चारुरूपिणीम्।।5.10.52।।
explanation: Then the vanara saw  a very beautiful woman of golden complexion decked with pearls and gems and with ornaments as if illuminating the excellent mansion with her splendour She was the king's favourite and the chief queen, Mandodari.

shloka_text: मुक्तामणिसमायुक्तैर्भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम्। विभूषयन्तीमिव तत्स्वश्रिया भवनोत्तमम्।।5.10.51।। गौरीं कनकवर्णाभामिष्टामन्तः पुरेश्वरीम्। कपिर्मन्दोदरीं तत्र शयानां चारुरूपिणीम्।।5.10.52।।
explanation: Then the vanara saw  a very beautiful woman of golden complexion decked with pearls and gems and with ornaments as if illuminating the excellent mansion with her splendour She was the king's favourite and the chief queen, Mandodari.

shloka_text: स तां दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्भूषितां मारुतात्मजः। तर्कयामास सीतेति रूपयौवनसम्पदा।।5.10.53। हर्षेण महता युक्तो ननन्द हरियूथपः।
explanation: On seeing her embellished with ornaments, beauty and charm, the long armed son of the Windgod, the chief of the vanaras thought her to be Sita and rejoiced.

shloka_text: आस्फोटयामास चुचुम्ब पुच्छं ननन्द चिक्रीड जगौ जगाम। स्तम्भानरोहन्निपपात भूमौ निदर्शयन् स्वां प्रकृतिं कपीनाम्।।5.10.54।।
explanation: He rejoiced clapping his palms, kissing his tail and jumping up, climbing up the pillars and jumping down on the ground in joy. Thus he exhibited his monkey nature. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे दशमस्सर्गः। Thus ends the tenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अवधूय च तां बुद्धिं बभूवावस्थितस्तदा। जगाम चापरां चिन्तां सीतां प्रति महाकपिः।।5.11.1।।
explanation: The great vanara, having rejected his judgement, started thinking again.

shloka_text: न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुमर्हति भामिनी। न भोक्तुं वाप्यलङ्कर्तुं न पानमुपसेवितुम्।।5.11.2।। नान्यं नरमुपस्थातुं सुराणामपि चेश्वरम्। न हि रामसमः कश्चिद्विद्यते त्रिदशेष्वपि।।5.11.3।। अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य पानभूमौ चचार सः।
explanation: 'Lovely Sita, being away from Rama, will not sleep, will not eat or drink or adorn herself. How can she approach any other man even if he is the king of gods for there is none equal to Rama even among gods'. Having thus decided, Hanuman strolled about the banquet hall.

shloka_text: न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुमर्हति भामिनी। न भोक्तुं वाप्यलङ्कर्तुं न पानमुपसेवितुम्।।5.11.2।। नान्यं नरमुपस्थातुं सुराणामपि चेश्वरम्। न हि रामसमः कश्चिद्विद्यते त्रिदशेष्वपि।।5.11.3।। अन्येयमिति निश्चित्य पानभूमौ चचार सः।
explanation: 'Lovely Sita, being away from Rama, will not sleep, will not eat or drink or adorn herself. How can she approach any other man even if he is the king of gods for there is none equal to Rama even among gods'. Having thus decided, Hanuman strolled about the banquet hall.

shloka_text: क्रीडितेनापराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथाऽपराः।।5.11.4।। नृत्तेन चापराः क्लान्ताः पानविप्रहतास्तथा।
explanation: Some women were fatigued after sporting, similarly some were exhausted after singing. Others were tired through dancing and some were worn out by continuous drinking.

shloka_text: मुरजेषु मृदङ्गेषु पीठिकासु च संस्थिताः।।5.11.5।। तथाऽऽस्तरणमुख्येषु संविष्टाश्चापराः स्त्रियः।
explanation: Some women reclined on tabors, some on murajas, and some on drums and hassocks while some slept on excellent couches.

shloka_text: अङ्गनानां सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः।।5.11.6।। रूपसल्लापशीलेन युक्तगीतार्थभाषिणा। देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना।।5.11.7।। रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः।
explanation: The monkey leader saw thousands of  beautiful women asleep after long dalliance. Some of them were adorned with ornaments, some were good at arguments and versed in the appreciation of songs, some were aware of the appropriate time and place and some were adept in right expressions.

shloka_text: अङ्गनानां सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः।।5.11.6।। रूपसल्लापशीलेन युक्तगीतार्थभाषिणा। देशकालाभियुक्तेन युक्तवाक्याभिधायिना।।5.11.7।। रताभिरतसंसुप्तं ददर्श हरियूथपः।
explanation: The monkey leader saw thousands of  beautiful women asleep after long dalliance. Some of them were adorned with ornaments, some were good at arguments and versed in the appreciation of songs, some were aware of the appropriate time and place and some were adept in right expressions.

shloka_text: तासां मध्ये महाबाहुः शुशुभे राक्षसेश्वरः।।5.11.8।। गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानां गवां मध्ये यथा वृषः।
explanation: In the midst of these women the longarmed lord of demons shone like a (majestic) bull in a big cowshed.

shloka_text: स राक्षसेन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतस्स्वयम्।।5.11.9।। करेणुभिर्यथाऽरण्ये परिकीर्णो महाद्विपः।
explanation: Surrounded by the women, the demon king shone like a proud elephant attended by many female elephants scattered in a dense forest.

shloka_text: सर्वकामैरुपेतां च पानभूमिं महात्मनः।।5.11.10।। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलस्तस्य रक्षःपतेर्गृहे।
explanation: The tiger among vanaras saw at the great Ravana's palace a drinking place where everything one desires was provided.

shloka_text: मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च भागशः।।5.11.11।। तत्र न्यस्तानि मांसानि पानभूमौ ददर्श सः।
explanation: There at the drinking hall the meat of deer, buffaloes and boars portioned and placed.

shloka_text: रौक्मेषु च विशालेषु भाजनेष्वर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.12।। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो मयूरान् कुक्कुटांस्तथा।
explanation: The tiger among vanaras also saw there meat of peacocks and chicken placed in large golden vessels, some half eaten.

shloka_text: वराहवार्ध्राणसकान् दधिसौवर्चलायुतान्।।5.11.13।। शल्यान् मृगमयूरांश्च हनुमानन्ववैक्षत।
explanation: Hanuman saw the meat of pigs and jungle fowls, deer, peacocks and bones marinated with yoghurt and special kinds of salt.

shloka_text: क्रकरान्विविधान् सिद्धांश्चकोरानर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.14।। महिषानेकशल्यांश्च छागांश्च कृतनिष्ठितान्। लेह्यानुच्चावचान्पेयान् भोज्यानि विविधानि च।।5.11.15।।
explanation: He saw several kinds of (nonvegetarian) food like cooked meat of fowls, ruddy geese, buffaloes, goats, fishes as well as food for licking. (Food is of four kinds  1) भक्ष्य which can be chewed 2) भोज्य ordinary solid, semisolid food which can be consumed  3) लेह्य food for licking  4) चोष्य liquid food (which can be sipped)).

shloka_text: क्रकरान्विविधान् सिद्धांश्चकोरानर्धभक्षितान्।।5.11.14।। महिषानेकशल्यांश्च छागांश्च कृतनिष्ठितान्। लेह्यानुच्चावचान्पेयान् भोज्यानि विविधानि च।।5.11.15।।
explanation: He saw several kinds of (nonvegetarian) food like cooked meat of fowls, ruddy geese, buffaloes, goats, fishes as well as food for licking. (Food is of four kinds  1) भक्ष्य which can be chewed 2) भोज्य ordinary solid, semisolid food which can be consumed  3) लेह्य food for licking  4) चोष्य liquid food (which can be sipped)).

shloka_text: तथाऽऽम्ललवणोत्तंसैर्विविधैरागषाडबैः। हारनूपुरकेयूरैरपविद्धैर्महाधनैः।।5.11.16।। पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि। कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्।।5.11.17।।
explanation: The banquet hall looked splendid with food seasoned with salt and sour ingredients. There was ragashadavas (syrup made with grapes, pomegranates, different juices like half ripe mangoes and seasoned with ginger cardomom, butter etc). Heavy chains, anklets and shouldersstraps were thrown aside. (The people relaxed while eating and drinking and discarded heavy ornaments). Many glasses were found scattered or drinks spilt on the floor after use.Many fruits and flowers were kept.

shloka_text: तथाऽऽम्ललवणोत्तंसैर्विविधैरागषाडबैः। हारनूपुरकेयूरैरपविद्धैर्महाधनैः।।5.11.16।। पानभाजनविक्षिप्तैः फलैश्च विविधैरपि। कृतपुष्पोपहारा भूरधिकं पुष्यति श्रियम्।।5.11.17।।
explanation: The banquet hall looked splendid with food seasoned with salt and sour ingredients. There was ragashadavas (syrup made with grapes, pomegranates, different juices like half ripe mangoes and seasoned with ginger cardomom, butter etc). Heavy chains, anklets and shouldersstraps were thrown aside. (The people relaxed while eating and drinking and discarded heavy ornaments). Many glasses were found scattered or drinks spilt on the floor after use.Many fruits and flowers were kept.

shloka_text: तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तै: सुश्लिष्टैश्शयनासनैः। पानभूमिर्विना वह्निं प्रदीप्तेवोपलक्ष्यते।।5.11.18।।
explanation: Good couches and different kinds of seats were wellarranged in the banquet hall. The place appeared as if it was glowing witout fire.

shloka_text: बहुप्रकारैर्विविधैर्वरसंस्कारसंस्कृतैः। मांसैः कुशलसम्पृक्तैः पानभूमिगतैः पृथक्।।5.11.19।।
explanation: In the banquet hall there were many types of meat arranged in a number of ways. They were cooked by experts by seasoning them with choicest ingredients.

shloka_text: दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृतसुरा अपि। शर्कराऽसवमाध्वीकपुष्पासवफलासवाः।।5.11.20।। वासचूर्णैश्च विविधैर्मृष्टास्तैस्तैः पृथक् पृथक्।
explanation: There were many types of wonderful and pleasing wine extracted from sugarcane, honey , fruits and flowers. They were good even though fermented and made delicious by seasoning with aromatic spices.

shloka_text: सन्तता शुशुभे भूमिर्माल्यैश्च बहुसंस्थितैः।।5.11.21।। हिरण्मयैश्च विविधैर्भाजनैः स्फाटिकैरपि। जाम्बूनदमयैश्चान्यैः करकैरभिसंवृता।।5.11.22।।
explanation: (The banquet hall) appeared beautiful with many kinds of garlands arranged in different locations. Also there were vessels made of pure gold, crystalware and jars spread all over.

shloka_text: सन्तता शुशुभे भूमिर्माल्यैश्च बहुसंस्थितैः।।5.11.21।। हिरण्मयैश्च विविधैर्भाजनैः स्फाटिकैरपि। जाम्बूनदमयैश्चान्यैः करकैरभिसंवृता।।5.11.22।।
explanation: (The banquet hall) appeared beautiful with many kinds of garlands arranged in different locations. Also there were vessels made of pure gold, crystalware and jars spread all over.

shloka_text: राजतेषु च कुम्भेषु जाम्बूनदमयेषु च। पानश्रेष्ठं तदा भूरि कपिस्तत्र ददर्श ह।।5.11.23।।
explanation: Hanuman saw the best of wines in large quantities kept in silver and pure gold pots.

shloka_text: ﻿सोऽपश्यच्छातकुम्भानि सीधोर्मणिमयानि च। राजतानि च पूर्णानि भाजनानि महाकपिः।।5.11.24।।
explanation: ﻿ The great monkey saw the wine jars made of gold and silver studded with crystals and gems.

shloka_text: क्वचिदल्पावशेषाणि क्वचित्पीतानि सर्वशः। क्वचिन्नैव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह।।5.11.25।।
explanation: He saw wine jars at one place, some fully drained, and at another place not touched at all.

shloka_text: क्वचिद् भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् क्वचित्पानानि भागशः। क्वचिदन्नावशेषाणि पश्यन्वै विचचार ह।।5.11.26।।
explanation: He moved about looking at different types of eatables and drinks arranged separately along with the left over food.

shloka_text: क्वचित्प्रभिन्नैः करकैः क्वचिदालोलितैर्घटैः। क्वचित्संपृक्तमाल्यानि जलानि च फलानि च।।5.11.27।।
explanation: At some places he saw broken pots, at other places rolling pots and elsewhere flower garlands strewn and mixed up with water and fruits.

shloka_text: शयनान्यत्र नारीणां शुभ्राणि बहुधा पुनः। परस्परं समाश्लिष्य काश्चित्सुप्ता वराङ्गनाः।।5.11.28।।
explanation: Hanuman saw many beds some unused and some occupied by lovely women sleeping, embracing one another.

shloka_text: काश्चिच्च वस्त्रमन्यस्यास्स्वपन्त्याः परिधाय च। आहृत्य चाबलाः सुप्ता निद्राबलपराजिताः।।5.11.29।।
explanation: Overcome with sleep some women pulled clothes of other women and covered their bodies with them.

shloka_text: तासामुच्छवासवातेन वस्त्रं माल्यं च गात्रजम्। नात्यर्थं स्पन्दते चित्रं प्राप्य मन्दमिवानिलम्।।5.11.30।।
explanation: The lovely clothes and garlands on the bodies of women were moving mildly by their exhalations as if shaken by the gentle breeze.

shloka_text: चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर्मधुरसस्य च। विविधस्य च माल्यस्य धूपस्य विविधस्य च।।5.11.31।। बहुधा मारुतस्तत्र गन्धं विविधमुद्वहन्।
explanation: With the many scents of cool sandal, of sweetsmelling wines of diverse kinds, as well as flower garlands of several types and of incense burning in that hall, the cool wind blew spreading several fragrances all over.

shloka_text: स्नानानां चन्दनानां च धूपानां चैव मूर्छितः।।5.11.32।। प्रववौ सुरभिर्गन्धो विमाने पुष्पके तदा।
explanation: The wind wafting through the Pushpaka chariot carried the fragrance of the cool sandalpaste used in bath and the sweet smell of wines and thick smoke of fragrance spread further.

shloka_text: श्यामावदातास्तत्रान्याः काश्चित्कृष्णा वराङ्गनाः।।5.11.33।। काश्चित् काञ्चनवर्णाङ्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षसालये।
explanation: There in the demons abode were women who were fair, some lovely with dark and others with golden complexion.

shloka_text: तासां निद्रावशत्वाच्च मदनेन विमूर्छितम्।।5.11.34।। पद्मिनीनां प्रसुप्तानां रूपमासीद्यथैव हि।
explanation: Withered due to indulgence in sex they were overcome with sleep. The charm of the women was like the lotus creepers with closed lotuses .

shloka_text: एवं सर्वमशेषेण रावणान्तः पुरं कपिः।।5.11.35।। ददर्श सुमहातेजाः न ददर्श च जानकीम्।
explanation: Brilliant Hanuman ransacked the harem of Ravana but found no Janaki.

shloka_text: निरीक्षमाणश्च तदा ताः स्त्रियः स महाकपिः।।5.11.36।। जगाम महतीं चिन्तां धर्मसाध्वसशङ्कितः।
explanation: The great monkey was very much worried as he thought he had transgressed the moral code by watching the women.

shloka_text: परदारावरोधस्य प्रसुप्तस्य निरीक्षणम्।।5.11.37।। इदं खलु ममात्यर्थं धर्मलोपं करिष्यति।
explanation: 'Observing the wives of others in this manner in their inner chambers very much amounts to transgression of moral code  by me'. ( thought he)

shloka_text: न हि मे परदाराणां दृष्टिर्विषयवर्तिनी।।5.11.38।। अयं चात्र मया दृष्टः परदारापरिग्रहः।
explanation: 'I did see these wives of another, but not with a sensual mind. I have only seen them but not with foul intention'.

shloka_text: तस्य प्रादुरभूच्चिन्ता पुनरन्या मनस्विनः।।5.11.39।। निश्चितैकान्तचित्तस्य कार्यनिश्चयदर्शिनी।
explanation: Another  bright idea struck the highly sensible Hanuman, who had a clear vision of the task ahead-- 'I was firm and singleminded in my direction regarding the task ahead' (thought he).

shloka_text: कामं दृष्टा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावणस्त्रियः।।5.11.40।। न हि मे मनसः किञ्चिद्वैकृत्यमुपजायते।
explanation: 'It is true I saw all the loyal wives of Ravana but without any foul desire. Indeed in my mind no passionate feeling was ever aroused'.

shloka_text: मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषामिन्द्रियाणां प्रवर्तने।।5.11.41।। शुभाशुभास्ववस्थासु तच्च मे सुव्यवस्थितम्।
explanation: 'Mind propels the sense organs to do good or bad deeds. (But) my mind is firmly esatablished in righteousness'.

shloka_text: नान्यत्र हि मया शक्या वैदेही परिमार्गितुम्।।5.11.42।। स्त्रियो हि स्त्रीषु दृश्यन्ते सदा सम्परिमार्गणे।
explanation: 'It is not possible for me to look for Vaidehi elsewhere. During such search operations one always looks for women among women.'

shloka_text: यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिस्तस्यां तत्परिमार्ग्यते। न शक्या प्रमदा नष्टा मृगीषु परिमार्गितुम्।।5.11.43।।
explanation: 'One has to search a creature among its own species. It is not possible to find a lost woman in the herd of female deer'.

shloka_text: तदिदं मार्गितं तावच्छुद्धेन मनसा मया।।5.11.44।। रावणान्तःपुरं सर्वं दृश्यते न तु जानकी।
explanation: 'I searched all over Ravana's harem with a pure mind but I have not seen Janaki'.

shloka_text: देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च वीर्यवान्।।5.11.45।। अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान्नैवापश्यत जानकीम्।
explanation: Even while valiant Hanuman was looking among the daughters of gods, gandharvas and nagas he could not find Janaki.

shloka_text: तामपश्यन्कपिस्तत्र पश्यञ्श्चान्या परस्त्रियः।।5.11.46।। अपक्रम्य तदा वीरः प्रध्यातुमुपचक्रमे।
explanation: Heroic Hanuman, unable to find Sita among the women, moved aside and started thinking.

shloka_text: स भूयस्तु परं श्रीमान् मारुतिर्यत्नमास्थितः।।5.11.47।। आपानभूमिमुत्सृज्य तद्विचेतुं प्रचक्रमे।
explanation: Illustrious Hanuman left the banquet hall to renew his effort in search of Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकादशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eleventh sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य मारुति र्लतागृहांश्चित्रगृहान्निशागृहान्। जगाम सीतां प्रति दर्शनोत्सुको न चैव तां पश्यति चारुदर्शनाम्।।5.12.1।।
explanation: Anxious to find Sita, Hanuman revisited the bowers of creepers, picture galleries and domitories located in the midst of the mansion, but  did not find that beautiful Sita.

shloka_text: स चिन्तयामास ततो महाकपिः प्रियामपश्यन्रघुनन्दनस्य ताम्। ध्रुवं हि सीता म्रियते यथा न मे विचिन्वतो दर्शनमेति मैथिली।।5.12.2।।
explanation: The great monkey, unable to find the beloved of Rama thought Sita might not be surviving. So he started thinking, ' I could not see her even though I have searched all over'.

shloka_text: सा राक्षसानां प्रवरेण जानकी स्वशीलसंरक्ष्णतत्परा सती। अनेन नूनं प्रति दुष्टकर्मणा हता भवेदार्यपथे परे स्थिता।।5.12.3।।
explanation: 'Janaki, follower of noble path, anxious to protect her chastity must have been killed by the wicked demon king.

shloka_text: विरूपरूपा विकृता विवर्चसो महानना दीर्घविरूपदर्शनाः। समीक्ष्य सा राक्षसराजयोषितो भयाद्विनष्टा जनकेश्वरात्मजा।।5.12.4।।
explanation: 'The daughter of Janaka might have collapsed out of fear, looking at the distorted faces of ugly, tall and monstrous demon maids of Ravana.

shloka_text: सीतामदृष्ट्वा ह्यनवाप्य पौरुषं विहृत्य कालं सह वानरैश्चिरम्। न मेऽस्ति सुग्रीवसमीपगा गतिः सुतीक्ष्णदण्डो बलवांश्च वानरः।।5.12.5।।
explanation: 'I have spent a long time with vanaras. I have not  succeded in my efforts to find Sita. I dare not see Sugriva now without finding Sita and without fulfilling my task. Sugriva will punish me severely. There is no way out.'

shloka_text: दृष्टमन्तःपुरं सर्वं दृष्टा रावणयोषितः। न सीता दृश्यते साध्वीवृथा जातो मम श्रमः।।5.12.6।।
explanation: 'I have searched all over the harem. Ravana's women have been seen. (Yet) I have not been able to see noble Sita. My efforts have been wasted'.

shloka_text: किं नु मां वानराः सर्वे गतं वक्ष्यन्ति सङ्गताः। गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किं कृतं तद्वदस्व नः।।5.12.7।।
explanation: 'What will the vanaras say when I return? What should I speak when they ask me: O hero, what did you accomplish there?'

shloka_text: अदृष्ट्वा किं प्रवक्ष्यामि तामहं जनकात्मजाम्। ध्रुवं प्रायमुपैष्यन्ति कालस्य व्यतिवर्तने।।5.12.8।।
explanation: 'Since the time limit has exceeded and Janaki is not spotted, surely the vanaras would sit and wait unto death. What am I going to say'?

shloka_text: किं वा वक्ष्यति वृद्धश्च जाम्बवानाङ्गदश्च सः। गतं पारं समुद्रस्य वानराश्च समागताः।।5.12.9।।
explanation: 'What will the elderly Jambavan say? What will young prince Angada and other vanaras collected there say when I reach the seashore to meet them'.

shloka_text: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। अनिर्वेदो हि सततं सर्वार्थेषु प्रवर्तकः।।5.12.10।।
explanation: Wise Hanuman once again declared, 'being free from despair is the root cause of prosperity. Freedom from despondency gives supreme happiness and leads to success'.

shloka_text: करोति सफलं जन्तोः कर्म यत्तत्करोति सः। तस्मादनिर्वेदकृतं यत्नं चेष्टेऽहमुत्तमम्।।5.12.11।। भूयस्तावद्विचेष्यामि देशान्रावणपालितान्।
explanation: 'The action of a living being certainly bears fruit. Therefore, I shall put forth my best effort without feeling despondent. I will once again search everywhere in Lanka ruled  by Ravana'.

shloka_text: आपानशाला विचितास्तथा पुष्पगृहाणि च।।5.12.12।। चित्रशालाश्च विचिता भूयः क्रीडागृहाणि च। निष्कुटान्तररथ्याश्च विमानानि च सर्वशः।।5.12.13।।
explanation: 'I have searched the banquet halls, bowers of creepers, picture galleries and gymnasiums. I have searched everywhere through the paths of gardens and mansions, harems and the Pushpaka chariot also.

shloka_text: आपानशाला विचितास्तथा पुष्पगृहाणि च।।5.12.12।। चित्रशालाश्च विचिता भूयः क्रीडागृहाणि च। निष्कुटान्तररथ्याश्च विमानानि च सर्वशः।।5.12.13।।
explanation: 'I have searched the banquet halls, bowers of creepers, picture galleries and gymnasiums. I have searched everywhere through the paths of gardens and mansions, harems and the Pushpaka chariot also.

shloka_text: इति सञ्चिन्त्य भूयोऽपि विचेतुमुपचक्रमे। भूमीगृहांश्चैत्यगृहान् गृहातिगृहकानपि।।5.12.14।।
explanation: Thinking thus, he started searching once again the basement cells, temples, homes within homes.

shloka_text: उत्पतन्निष्पतंश्चापि तिष्ठन्गच्छन् पुनः पुनः। अपावृण्वंश्च द्वाराणि कवाटान्यवघाटयन्।।5.12.15।। प्रविशन्निष्पतंश्चापि प्रपतन्नुत्पतन्नपि। सर्वमप्यवकाशं स विचचार महाकपिः।।5.12.16।।
explanation: The great vanara searched all over again and again jumping up and down, stopping for a while and moving, opening and closing doors, by crossing, entering and exiting, jumping up and down. Thus he moved about and searched whereever there was scope to search

shloka_text: उत्पतन्निष्पतंश्चापि तिष्ठन्गच्छन् पुनः पुनः। अपावृण्वंश्च द्वाराणि कवाटान्यवघाटयन्।।5.12.15।। प्रविशन्निष्पतंश्चापि प्रपतन्नुत्पतन्नपि। सर्वमप्यवकाशं स विचचार महाकपिः।।5.12.16।।
explanation: The great vanara searched all over again and again jumping up and down, stopping for a while and moving, opening and closing doors, by crossing, entering and exiting, jumping up and down. Thus he moved about and searched whereever there was scope to search

shloka_text: चतुरङ्गुलमात्रोऽपि नावकाशः स विद्यते। रावणान्तःपुरे तस्मिन् यं कपिर्न जगाम सः।।5.12.17।।
explanation: Even a space of four fingers in the inner chambers of Ravana was not left out in his search for Sita.

shloka_text: प्राकारान्तररथ्याश्च वेदिकाश्चैत्यसंश्रयाः। दीर्घिकाः पुष्करिण्यश्च सर्वं तेनावलोकितम्।।5.12.18।।
explanation: He moved in the lanes inside the boundary walls, around the shrines, altars, wells and tanks whereever it was possible to look for.

shloka_text: राक्षस्यो विविधाकारा विरूपा विकृतास्तथा। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सा जनकात्मजा।।5.12.19।।
explanation: Hanuman could see only ogresses of different typesugly, deformed but could not find the daughter of Janaka.

shloka_text: रूपेणाप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्याधरस्त्रियः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु राघवनन्दिनी।।5.12.20।।
explanation: Hanuman could see even the women of vidyadharas who were matchless in beauty among women in the world but not Janaki the beloved of Raghava.

shloka_text: नागकन्या वरारोहाः पूर्णचन्र्दनिभाननाः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा।।5.12.21।।
explanation: Hanuman could see there moonfaced daughters of nagas with charming limbs but not the slimwaisted Sita.

shloka_text: प्रमथ्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण नागकन्या बलाद्धृताः। दृष्टा हनुमता तत्र न सा जनकनन्दिनी।।5.12.22।।
explanation: Hanuman saw the daghters of nagas kidnapped by Ravana forcibly after victory in war but not Sita, the delight of Janaka.

shloka_text: सोऽपश्यंस्तां महाबाहुः पश्यंश्चान्या वरस्त्रियः। विषसाद मुहुर्धीमान् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।।5.12.23।।
explanation: The longarmed Hanuman, son of the Windgod was able to see other great women but not Sita. So he became despondent.

shloka_text: उद्योगं वानरेन्द्राणां प्लवनं सागरस्य च। व्यर्थं वीक्ष्यानिलसुतश्चिन्तां पुनरुपागमत्।।5.12.24।।
explanation: The son of the Wind god, the great monkey realised the futility of his efforts in crossing the sea. He brooded again.

shloka_text: अवतीर्य विमानाच्च हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। चिन्तामुपजगामाथ शोकोपहतचेतनः।।5.12.25।।
explanation: Hanuman, son of the Windgod, came out of the aerial chariot, mind stricken with grief and started thinking again. इत्यार्षे  श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वादशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the twelfth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: विमानात्तु सुसम्क्रम्य प्राकारं हरियूथपः। हनुमान्वेगवानासीद्यथा विद्युद्घनान्तरे।।5.13.1।।
explanation: Hanuman, the vanara leader, jumped from the aerial chariot to the boundary wall like a flash of lightning in the clouds.

shloka_text: सम्परिक्रम्य हनुमान्रावणस्य निवेशनात्। अदृष्ट्वा जानकीं सीतामब्रवीद्वचनं कपिः।।5.13.2।।
explanation: Going round the palace of Ravana, unable to see Janaka's daughter Sita, Hanuman spoke thus to himself:

shloka_text: भूयिष्ठं लोलिता लङ्का रामस्य चरता प्रियम्। न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीं सीतां सर्वाङ्गशोभनाम्।।5.13.3।।
explanation: "I have thoroughly surveyed the entire city of Lanka to please Rama, but I am unable to find Sita of flawless beauty.

shloka_text: पल्वलानि तटाकानि सरांसि सरितस्तथा। नद्योऽनूपवनान्ताश्च दुर्गाश्च धरणीधराः।।5.13.4।। लोलिता वसुधा सर्वा न तु पश्यामि जानकीम्।
explanation: "I have searched for Sita thoroughly in waterlogs, lakes, tanks, streams and rivers and all over the woods and among mountains that are difficult to reach. I have searched all over the land but have not been able to find Janaki.

shloka_text: इह सम्पातिना सीता रावणस्य निवेशने।।5.13.5।। आख्याता गृध्रराजेन न च पश्यामि तामहम्।
explanation: "Sampati, king of vultures had said that Sita is at Ravana's palace. But I have not been able to see her.

shloka_text: किं नु सीताऽथ वैदेही मैथिली जनकात्मजा।।5.13.6।। उपतिष्ठेत विवशा रावणं दुष्टचारिणम्।
explanation: "Can it be that Mythili, daughter of Janaka, dejected and helpless succumbed to the evil intentions of Ravana.

shloka_text: क्षिप्रमुत्पततो मन्ये सीतामादाय रक्षसः।।5.13.7।। बिभ्यतो रामबाणानामन्तरा पतिता भवेत्।
explanation: "Or, perhaps she might have been dropped midway from the hold of Ravana while he was flying at great speed, afraid of the deadly arrows of Rama?

shloka_text: अथवा ह्रियमाणायाः पथि सिद्धनिषेविते।।5.13.8।। मन्ये पतितमार्याया हृदयं प्रेक्ष्य सागरम्।
explanation: "Or, perhaps while being borne away on the path frequented by siddhas, the beloved of Rama might have fallen down (dead), heart broken, on seeing the (vast) sea.

shloka_text: रावणस्योरुवेगेन भुजाभ्यां पीडितेन च।।5.13.9।। तया मन्ये विशालाक्ष्या त्यक्तं जीवितमार्यया।
explanation: "He thinks, on account of the high speed during the flight of Ravana under the pressure of his arms, the noble, largeeyed lady might have given up her life.

shloka_text: उपर्युपरि वा नूनं सागरं क्रमतस्तदा।।5.13.10।। विवेष्टमाना पतिता सागरे जनकात्मजा।
explanation: "Surely, she might have fallen into the sea while wriggling in her effort to extricate herself from the hold of Ravana as he was flying over the sea.

shloka_text: अहो क्षुद्रेण वाऽनेन रक्षन्ती शीलमात्मनः।।5.13.11।। अबन्धुर्भक्षिता सीता रावणेन तपस्विनी।
explanation: "Oh poor Sita, distanced from relations, while protecting her chastity helplessly she might have been devoured by cruel Ravana.

shloka_text: अथवा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पत्नीभिरसितेक्षणा।।5.13.12।। अदुष्टा दुष्टभावाभिर्भक्षिता सा भविष्यति।
explanation: "Or else, the pious, blackeyed Sita might have been eaten by the the cruelnatured wives of the lord of demons.

shloka_text: सम्पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम्।।5.13.13।। रामस्य ध्यायती वक्त्रं पञ्चत्वं कृपणा गता।
explanation: "Or, she might have attained death, meditating on Rama, whose face resembles the fullmoon and eyes the lotus petals.

shloka_text: हा राम लक्ष्मणेत्येवं हाऽयोध्ये चेति मैथिली।।5.13.14।। विलप्य बहु वैदेही न्यस्तदेहा भविष्यति।
explanation: "Or, Vaidehi, the princess of Mithila might have cast off her life grieving intensely and crying, 'Alas, Rama, alas, Lakshmana, alas, Ayodhya'. (Mithila is the name of the  capital city and Videha is the country which was ruled by Janaka. Sita, the princess is known as Vaidehi, Mythili and Janaki).

shloka_text: अथवा निहिता मन्ये रावणस्य निवेशने।।5.13.15।। नूनं लालप्यते सीता पञ्जरस्थेव शारिका।
explanation: "Or, I think Sita might have been imprisoned in a cage like a myna in Ravana's palace. She will be surely crying.

shloka_text: जनकस्य सुता सीता रामपत्नी सुमध्यमा।।5.13.16।। कथमुत्पलपत्राक्षी रावणस्य वशं व्रजेत्।
explanation: "How could Janaki, the daughter of Janaka, Rama's wife, the lady with a beautiful waist and eyes like lotus petals, come under the fold of Ravana?

shloka_text: विनष्टा वा प्रणष्टा वा मृता वा जनकात्मजा।।5.13.17।। रामस्य प्रियभार्यस्य न निवेदयितुं क्षमम्।
explanation: "Whether Janaki is lost or irretrievable or dead is not known The news should not be  reported to Rama, who is very fond of his wife.

shloka_text: निवेद्यमाने दोषस्स्याद्दोषस्स्यादनिवेदने।।5.13.18।। कथं नु खलु कर्तव्यं विषमं प्रतिभाति मे।
explanation: "To carry or not to carry this news to Rama would be a mistake. What shall I do? I am facing a tough situation.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये प्राप्तकालं क्षमं च किम्।।5.13.19।। भवेदिति मतं भूयो हनुमान्प्रविचारयत्।
explanation: "I wonder what the right course of action is when things have taken such a turn? What is proper for me to do? Hanuman once again deliberated.

shloka_text: यदि सीतामदृष्ट्वाऽहं वानरेन्द्रपुरीमितः।।5.13.20।। गमिष्यामि ततः को मे पुरुषार्थो भविष्यति।
explanation: "If I return to Kishkinda without seeing Sita of what use is my effort? What have I accomplished? What will happen? (Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha are the four Purusharthas or accomplishments in life)

shloka_text: ममेदं लङ्घनं व्यर्थं सागरस्य भविष्यति।।5.13.21।। प्रवेशश्चैव लङ्कायाः राक्षसानां च दर्शनम्।
explanation: "My crossing the ocean, my entry into Lanka and my survey of the demons are all futile.

shloka_text: किं मां वक्ष्यति सुग्रीवो हरयो वा समागताः।।5.13.22।। किष्किन्धां समनुप्राप्तं तौ वा दशरथात्मजौ।
explanation: "What will Sugriva or even the vanaras and the two sons of Dasaratha say when I reach Kishkinda?

shloka_text: गत्वा तु यदि काकुत्स्थं वक्ष्यामि परमप्रियम्।।5.13.23।। न दृष्टेति मया सीता ततस्तक्ष्यति जीवितम्।
explanation: "If I report the most unpleasant news that Sita was not found, Rama will give up his life.

shloka_text: परुषं दारुणं क्रूरं तीक्ष्णमिन्द्रियतापनम्।।5.13.24।। सीतानिमित्तं दुर्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा स न भविष्यति।
explanation: Upon hearing such harsh, terrible, cruel, sharp, and sense-tormenting evil words concerning Sita, he will not survive.

shloka_text: तं तु कृच्छ्रगतं दृष्ट्वा पञ्चत्वगतमानसम्।।5.13.25।। भृशानुरक्तो मेधावी न भविष्यति लक्ष्मणः।
explanation: "Seeing Rama in such a painful state, wise Lakshmana who has given his life to Rama, to whom he is deeply devoted will also not survive.

shloka_text: विनष्टौ भ्रातरौ श्रुत्वा भरतोऽपि मरिष्यति।।5.13.26।। भरतं च मृतं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुघ्नो न भविष्यति।
explanation: "On hearing the death of both the brothers Bharata will also die. On seeing this Satrughna will also not live.

shloka_text: पुत्रान्मृतान्समीक्ष्याथ न भविष्यन्ति मातरः।।5.13.27।। कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च न संशयः।
explanation: Having seen their sons dead, the mothers will not survive, Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi, without a doubt.

shloka_text: कृतज्ञस्सत्यसन्धश्च सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः।।5.13.28।। रामं तथा गतं दृष्ट्वा ततस्त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्।
explanation: "On seeing that Rama has ended his life, the grateful and truthful monkey leader, Sugriva will give up his life.

shloka_text: दुर्मना व्यथिता दीना निरानन्दा तपस्विनी।।5.13.29।। पीडिता भर्तृशोकेन रुमा त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्।
explanation: "Distressed, disheartened, pained and grieved on account of her husband's death, the virtuous lady Ruma (wife of Sugriva) will be unhappy and die.

shloka_text: वालिजेन तु दुःखेन पीडिता शोककर्शिता।।5.13.30।। पञ्चत्वं च गते राज्ञि ताराऽपि न भविष्यति।
explanation: "Tara who is troubled by Vali's death and tortured with grief will not live when king Sugriva dies.

shloka_text: मातापित्रोर्विनाशेन सुग्रीवव्यसनेन च।।5.13.31।। कुमारोऽप्यङ्गदः कस्माद्धारयिष्यति जीवितम्।
explanation: "On account of his parents death and also because of Sugriva's calamity, Angada will give up his life.

shloka_text: भर्तृजेन तु दुःखेन ह्यभिभूता वनौकसः।।5.13.32।। शिरांस्यभिहनिष्यन्ति तलैर्मुष्टिभिरेव च।
explanation: "The grief due to the death of their king will make the vanaras hit their heads with their palms and fists.

shloka_text: सान्त्वेनानुप्रदानेन मानेन च यशस्विना।।5.13.33।। लालिताः कपिराजेन प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति वानराः।
explanation: "The vanaras who were reared by the king's kind words, gifts and care will give up their life.

shloka_text: न वनेषु न शैलेषु न निरोधेषु वा पुनः।।5.13.34।। क्रीडामनुभविष्यन्ति समेत्य कपिकुञ्जराः।
explanation: "The chiefs among vanaras together will not enjoy their life in the forest or mountains or caves.

shloka_text: सपुत्रदारास्सामात्या भर्तृव्यसनपीडिताः।।5.13.35।। शैलाग्रेभ्यः पतिष्यन्ति समेषु विषमेषु च।
explanation: "Tormented by their king's death the vanaras with their wives, sons and ministers will drop down from the mountain peaks on the rough ground and die.

shloka_text: विषमुद्बन्धनं वापि प्रवेशं ज्वलनस्य वा।।5.13.36।। उपवासमथो शस्त्रं प्रचरिष्यन्ति वानराः।
explanation: "The vanaras will put an end to their lives by poisoning or by hanging or by selfimmolation or by killing themselves with weapons or by fasting unto death.

shloka_text: घोरमारोदनं मन्ये गते मयि भविष्यति।।5.13.37।। इक्ष्वाकुकुलनाशश्च नाशश्चैव वनौकसाम्।
explanation: "If I go there (without finding Sita), it will cause destruction of the Ikshvakus and vanaras would weep. It would be dreadful.

shloka_text: सोऽहं नैव गमिष्यामि किष्किन्धां नगरीमितः।।5.13.38।। न च शक्ष्याम्यहं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं मैथिलीं विना।
explanation: "I will not go to the city of Kishkinda from here or to Sugriva without finding Mythili. It will not be possible for me to face him.

shloka_text: मय्यगच्छति चेहस्थे धर्मात्मानौ महारथौ।।5.13.39।। आशया तौ धरिष्येते वानराश्च मनस्विनः।
explanation: Both the highsouled warrior princes treading a righteous path as well as the vanaras will survive with a hope of my return if I stay back.

shloka_text: हस्तादानो मुखादानो नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः।।5.13.40।। वानप्रस्थो भविष्यामि ह्यदृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम्। सागरानूपजे देशे बहुमूलफलोदके।।5.13.41।।
explanation: "If Janaki is not found I will stay here and live like a hermit subsisting on whatever is available on this sea shore, which has abundance of roots, fruits and water.

shloka_text: हस्तादानो मुखादानो नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः।।5.13.40।। वानप्रस्थो भविष्यामि ह्यदृष्ट्वा जनकात्मजाम्। सागरानूपजे देशे बहुमूलफलोदके।।5.13.41।।
explanation: "If Janaki is not found I will stay here and live like a hermit subsisting on whatever is available on this sea shore, which has abundance of roots, fruits and water.

shloka_text: चितां कृत्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि समिद्धमरणीसुतम्। उपविष्टस्य वा सम्यग्लिङ्गिनीं साधयिष्यतः।।5.13.42।। शरीरं भक्षयिष्यन्ति वायसाः श्वापदानि च।
explanation: "I will prepare a pyre  and enter the fire  so that sea waves wash off the ashes or crows and beasts will eat up my body while i sit fasting unto death.

shloka_text: इदं महर्षिभिर्दृष्टं निर्याणमिति मे मतिः।।5.13.43।। सम्यगापः प्रवेक्ष्यामि न चेत्पश्यामि जानकीम्।
explanation: "I shall enter water and drown myself to death if I am not able to find Janaki. I think this way of ending life has been suggested by great ascetics.

shloka_text: सुजातमूला सुभगा कीर्तिमाला यशस्विनी।।5.13.44।। प्रभग्ना चिररात्रीयं मम सीतामपश्यतः।
explanation: My glory which had a good start (in the form of bringing Rama to Sugriva) and brought fortune to Sugriva and fame to me has been snapped as I could not find Sita.

shloka_text: तापसो वा भविष्यामि नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः।।5.13.45।। नेतः प्रतिगमिष्यामि तामदृष्ट्वासितेक्षणाम्।
explanation: "I will remain an ascetic and do penance under the tree practising selfcontrol and not go back without seeing the blackeyed Sita.

shloka_text: यदीतः प्रतिगच्छामि सीतामनधिगम्य ताम्।।5.13.46।। अङ्गदस्सह तैस्सर्वैर्वानरैर्न भविष्यति।
explanation: "Besides, if I go back without finding Sita all the vanaras including Angada will die.

shloka_text: विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन् भद्राणि पश्यति।।5.13.47।। तस्मात्प्राणान् धरिष्यामि ध्रुवो जीवितसङ्गमः।
explanation: "If I commit suicide, I will earn numerous sins. By being alive, I can witness auspicious events. Therefore, I will live, for, happiness can come only to the living.

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधं दुःखं मनसा धरायन्मुहुः।।5.13.48।। नाध्यगच्छत्तदा पारं शोकस्य कपिकुञ्चरः।
explanation: The elephant among monkeys (Hanuman) worrying over and over again, holding his head for long could not reach the end of his grief.

shloka_text: रावणं वा वधिष्यामि दशग्रीवं महाबलम्।।5.13.49।। काममस्तु हृता सीता प्रत्याचीर्णं भविष्यति।
explanation: "I will kill Ravana, this mighty, tenheaded demon. Sita was indeed carried away by him. This (killing him) can be a fitting reply to his evil action. My desire would be fulfilled.

shloka_text: अथवैनं समुत्क्षिप्य उपर्युपरि सागरम्।।5.13.50।। रामायोपहरिष्यामि पशुं पशुपतेरिव।
explanation: "Or else, I shall carry him across the sea and put him before Rama like a bull as if he is a sacrificial prey to lord Siva."

shloka_text: इति चिन्तां समापन्नः सीतामनधिगम्य ताम्।।5.13.51।। ध्यानशोकपरीतात्मा चिन्तयामास वानरः।
explanation: Distressed over his inability to find Sita, Hanuman's mind was overcome with anxiety and he started thinking further.

shloka_text: यावत्सीतां हि पश्यामि रामपत्नीं यशस्विनीम्।।5.13.52।। तावदेतां पुरीं लङ्कां विचिनोमि पुनः पुनः।
explanation: "Till I find the virtuous Sita, wife of Rama in this Lanka, I shall keep searching everywhere again and again.

shloka_text: सम्पातिवचनाच्चापि रामं यद्यानयाम्यहम्।।5.13.53।। अपश्यन् राघवो भार्यां निर्धहेत्सर्ववानरान्।
explanation: "Had I brought Raghava following  the words of Sampati, Rama would have burnt all vanaras unable to find his wife.

shloka_text: इहैव नियताहारो वत्स्यामि नियतेन्द्रियः।।5.13.54।। न मत्कृते विनश्येयुः सर्वे ते नरवानराः।
explanation: "I will stay here itself, restricting my food and controlling my senses. Let not men and monkeys perish for my fault.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिका चेयं दृश्यते या महाद्रुमा।।5.13.55।। इमामधिगमिष्यामि न हीयं विचिता मया।
explanation: "Here is the Ashoka grove with huge trees. I will go there. I have not looked for her in this place.

shloka_text: वसून्रुद्रांस्तथाऽदित्यानश्विनौ मरुतोऽपि च।।5.13.56।। नमस्कृत्वा गमिष्यामि रक्षसां शोकवर्धनः।
explanation: "I shall offer salutations to Vasus, Rudras Adityas and Aswinis and proceed to  increase (cause) the sorrow of the demons. (There are eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Adityas, two Ashwins and fortynine Windgods).

shloka_text: जित्वा तु राक्षसान् सर्वानिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दिनीम्।।5.13.57।। सम्प्रदास्यामि रामाय यथा सिद्धिं तपस्विने।
explanation: "I will conquer all the ogres and pass them to Sita, the delight of the Ikshvaku family  as an offering and give Rama to her as the fruit of her austerities."

shloka_text: सः मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा चिन्तावग्रथितेन्द्रियः।।5.13.58।। उदतिष्ठन्महातेजा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
explanation: The brilliant son of the Windgod, Hanuman, whose senses were overwhelmed with worries, regained his senses in a short while and got up.

shloka_text: नमोऽस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय देव्यै च तस्यै जनकात्मजायै। नमोऽस्तु रुद्रेंद्रयमानिलेभ्यो नमोऽस्तु चन्द्रार्कमरुद्गणेभ्यः।।5.13.59।।
explanation: "My salutations to Lakshmana, Rama and divine daughter of Janaka. Salutations to Rudra, Indra, Yama and Vayu. Salutations to Sun, Moon and Maruts"

shloka_text: स तेभ्यस्तु नमस्कृत्य सुग्रीवाय च मारुतिः। दिशस्सर्वास्समालोक्य ह्यशोकवनिकां प्रति।।5.13.60।।
explanation: Having offered salutations to all gods as well as to Sugriva, he looked at all quarters and left for the Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: स गत्वा मनसा पूर्वमशोकवनिकां शुभाम्। उत्तरं चिन्तयामास वानरो मारुतात्मजः।।5.13.61।।
explanation: Hanuman started thinking again about his task after reaching the auspicious Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: ध्रुवं तु रक्षोबहुला भविष्यति वनाकुला। अशोकवनिका पुण्या सर्वसंस्कारसंस्कृता।।5.13.62।।
explanation: 'This Ashoka grove filled with many trees, guarded by many demons is carefully tended. It must be sacred.

shloka_text: रक्षिणश्चात्र विहिता नूनं रक्षन्ति पादपान्। भगवानपि सर्वात्मा नातिक्षोभं प्रवाति वै।।5.13.63।। संक्षिप्तोऽयं मयाऽत्मा च रामार्थे रावणस्य च।
explanation: "The guards posted there are surely protecting the grove. The divinity  pervading all over me (the wind) must also have been controlled as it is also not blowing violently. I have turned my body small for Rama's cause and also to save myself from Ravana.

shloka_text: सिद्धिं मे संविधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षिगणास्त्विह।।5.13.64।। ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्भगवान् देवाश्चैव दिशन्तु मे। सिद्धिमग्निश्च वायुश्च पुरुहूतश्च वज्रभृत्।।5.13.65।। वरुणः पाशहस्तश्च सोमादित्यौ तथैव च। अश्विनौ च महात्मानौ मरुतः शर्व एव च।।5.13.66।। सिद्धिं सर्वाणि भूतानि भूतानां चैव यः प्रभुः। दास्यन्ति मम ये चान्ये ह्यदृष्टाः पथि गोचराः।।5.13.67।।
explanation: May all sages, gods, the selfborn Brahma, Windgod, Indra, the wielder of thunderbolt whose name is invoked in sacrifices, Yama, who carries a rope, Varuna give success and Lord Siva help me. May the Sun, Moon, Aswinis  Marutas assist me. May the gods of the quarters and the lord of all beings help me to succeed. May those whom I could not see also bring success to me.

shloka_text: सिद्धिं मे संविधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षिगणास्त्विह।।5.13.64।। ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्भगवान् देवाश्चैव दिशन्तु मे। सिद्धिमग्निश्च वायुश्च पुरुहूतश्च वज्रभृत्।।5.13.65।। वरुणः पाशहस्तश्च सोमादित्यौ तथैव च। अश्विनौ च महात्मानौ मरुतः शर्व एव च।।5.13.66।। सिद्धिं सर्वाणि भूतानि भूतानां चैव यः प्रभुः। दास्यन्ति मम ये चान्ये ह्यदृष्टाः पथि गोचराः।।5.13.67।।

May the Sun, Moon, Aswinis  Marutas assist me. May the gods of the quarters and the lord of all beings help me to succeed. May those whom I could not see also bring success to me.

shloka_text: तदुन्नसं पाण्डुरदन्तमव्रणं शुचिस्मितं पद्मपलाशलोचनम्। द्रक्ष्ये तदार्यावदनं कदान्वहं प्रसन्नताराधिपतुल्यदर्शनम्।।5.13.68।।
explanation: 'Oh when and how would I behold that beautiful noble lady of stainless character, with a Moonlike face, prominent nose, white teeth, pleasant smile and with eyes like lotus petals?

shloka_text: क्षुद्रेण पापेन नृशंसकर्मणा सुदारुणालङ्कृतवेषधारिणा। बलाभिभूता ह्यबला तपस्विनी कथं नु मे दृष्टिपथेऽद्य सा भवेत्।।5.13.69।।
explanation: "How will I set my eyes on that gentle, frail and suffering thing now, who has been abducted by that mean, cruel sinner of dreadful look?" इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रयोदशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the thirteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा मनसा चाधिगम्य ताम्। अवप्लुतो महातेजाः प्राकारं तस्य वेश्मनः।।5.14.1।।
explanation: Mighty Hanuman lost in thought for a moment, jumped down (the harem) to the boundary wall of the palace.

shloka_text: स तु संहृष्टसर्वाङ्गः प्राकारस्थो महाकपिः। पुष्पिताग्रान्वसन्तादौ ददर्श विविधान् द्रुमान्।।5.14.2।। सालानशोकान् भव्यांश्च चंपकांश्च सुपुष्पितान्। उद्दालकान्नागवृक्षांश्चूतान्कपिमुखानपि।।5.14.3।।
explanation: Standing on the boundary wall, the great vanara contracted his body and observed the blossoms on several tree tops---- Salas, lovely Ashoka trees and blossoms of champak, uddalaka, naga, mangoes with their fruits crimson as the snout of a monkey, it being the beginning of Spring.

shloka_text: स तु संहृष्टसर्वाङ्गः प्राकारस्थो महाकपिः। पुष्पिताग्रान्वसन्तादौ ददर्श विविधान् द्रुमान्।।5.14.2।। सालानशोकान् भव्यांश्च चंपकांश्च सुपुष्पितान्। उद्दालकान्नागवृक्षांश्चूतान्कपिमुखानपि।।5.14.3।।
explanation: Standing on the boundary wall, the great vanara contracted his body and observed the blossoms on several tree tops---- Salas, lovely Ashoka trees and blossoms of champak, uddalaka, naga, mangoes with their fruits crimson as the snout of a monkey, it being the beginning of Spring.

shloka_text: अथाम्रवणसञ्छन्नां लताशतसमावृताम्। ज्यामुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्षवाटिकाम्।।5.14.4।।
explanation: He penetrated like an arrow released from a bow the cluster of trees covering mango grove and overgrown with hundreds of creepers.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य विचित्रां तां विहगैरभिनादिताम्। राजतैः कांचनैश्चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम्।।5.14.5।। विहगैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्। उदितादित्यसङ्काशां ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः।।5.14.6।। वृतां नानाविधैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पोपगफलोपगैः। कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च मत्तैर्नित्यनिषेविताम्।।5.14.7।। प्रहृष्टमनुजे काले मृगपक्षिसमाकुले। मत्तबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टां नानाद्विजगणायुताम्।।5.14.8।।
explanation: Entering deep into the grove, Hanuman saw clusters of trees pleasing to look at, herds of animals and flocks of colourful birds singing melodious notes.The grove was surrounded on all sides by silvery and golden trees which looked colourful with flocks of birds and herds of deer. It was full of lovely thickets looking like the rising sun. It was fringed with various trees bearing abundance of fruits and flowers. It was inhabited by intoxicated cuckoos, bees,  proud peacocks and numerous lovely birds.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य विचित्रां तां विहगैरभिनादिताम्। राजतैः कांचनैश्चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम्।।5.14.5।। विहगैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्। उदितादित्यसङ्काशां ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः।।5.14.6।। वृतां नानाविधैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पोपगफलोपगैः। कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च मत्तैर्नित्यनिषेविताम्।।5.14.7।। प्रहृष्टमनुजे काले मृगपक्षिसमाकुले। मत्तबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टां नानाद्विजगणायुताम्।।5.14.8।।

It was full of lovely thickets looking like the rising sun. It was fringed with various trees bearing abundance of fruits and flowers. It was inhabited by intoxicated cuckoos, bees,  proud peacocks and numerous lovely birds.

shloka_text: स प्रविश्य विचित्रां तां विहगैरभिनादिताम्। राजतैः कांचनैश्चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम्।।5.14.5।। विहगैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्। उदितादित्यसङ्काशां ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः।।5.14.6।। वृतां नानाविधैर्वृक्षैः पुष्पोपगफलोपगैः। कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च मत्तैर्नित्यनिषेविताम्।।5.14.7।। प्रहृष्टमनुजे काले मृगपक्षिसमाकुले। मत्तबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टां नानाद्विजगणायुताम्।।5.14.8।।
explanation: Entering deep into the grove, Hanuman saw clusters of trees pleasing to look at, herds of animals and flocks of colourful birds singing melodious notes.The grove was surrounded on all sides by silvery and golden trees which looked colourful with flocks of birds and herds of deer. It was full of lovely thickets looking like the rising sun. It was fringed with various trees bearing abundance of fruits and flowers. It was inhabited by intoxicated cuckoos, bees,  proud peacocks and numerous lovely birds.

shloka_text: मार्गमाणो वरारोहां राजपुत्रीमनिन्दिताम्। सुखप्रसुप्तान्विहगान् बोधयामास वानरः।।5.14.9।।
explanation: The vanara who went searching for the paragon of virtue born of a noble family, awakened the birds who were happily asleep in their nests.

shloka_text: उत्पतद्भिर्द्विजगणैः पक्षैः सालास्समाहताः। अनेकवर्णा विविधा मुमुचुः पुष्पवृष्टयः।।5.14.10।।
explanation: As the birds flew away, the trees hit by the wings of birds showered flowers of different colours.

shloka_text: पुष्पावकीर्णश्शुशुभे हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः। अशोकवनिकामध्ये यथा पुष्पमयो गिरिः।।5.14.11।।
explanation: Covered with flowers, Hanuman shone like a mountain of flowers in the midst of Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: ﻿दिशस्सर्वाः प्रधावन्तं वृक्षषण्डगतं कपिम्। दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि वसन्त इति मेनिरे।।5.14.12।।
explanation: ﻿ Beholding that sprightly monkey running in all directions, its body covered with variegated blossoms fallen from the trees, all living beings there thought that it was Spring personified

shloka_text: ﻿वृक्षेभ्यः पतितैः पुष्पैरवकीर्णा पृथग्विदैः। रराज वृक्षेभ्यः तत्र प्रमदेव विभूषिता।।5.14.13।।
explanation: ﻿ Strewn with flowers of various colours fallen from the trees of various kinds, the goddess of earth looked charming like a young woman profusely bedecked.

shloka_text: तरस्विना ते तरवस्तरसाभिप्रकम्पिताः। कुसुमानि विचित्राणि ससृजुः कपिना तदा।।5.14.14।।
explanation: ﻿ Shaken vigorously by Hanuman of great speed, the trees shed their blooms of variegated colours.

shloka_text: निर्धूतपत्रशिखराः शीर्णपुष्पफला द्रुमाः। निक्षिप्तवस्त्राभरणा धूर्ता इव पराजिताः।।5.14.15।।
explanation: The tree tops, shorn of their leaves and flowers and fruits fallen, appeared like gamblers who had lost their stakes and had to lay down their clothes and ornaments.

shloka_text: हनूमता वेगवता कम्पितास्ते नगोत्तमाः। पुष्पपर्णफलान्याशु मुमुचुः पुष्पशालिनः।।5.14.16।।
explanation: Shaken by the swift Hanuman, even the big trees dropped flowers, fruits and leaves.

shloka_text: विहङ्गसङ्घैर्हीनास्ते स्कन्धमात्राश्रया द्रुमाः। बभूवुरगमाः सर्वे मारुतेव निर्धुताः।5.14.17।।
explanation: Deserted by the flocks of birds resting on them (flowers and leaves also dropped from branches), the trees were left bare with trunks unable to move.

shloka_text: निर्धूतकेशी युवतिर्यथा मृदितवर्णका। निष्पीतशुभदन्तोष्ठी नखैर्दन्तैश्च विक्षता।।5.14.18।। तथा लाङ्गूलहस्तैश्च चरणाभ्यां च मर्दिता। बभूवाशोकवनिका प्रभग्नवरपादपा।।5.14.19।।
explanation: The garden of Ashoka with trees shattered and crushed by Hanuman's tail,  hands and feet, appeared like a woman with dishevelled hair, with her vermilion mark effaced, her bright teeth and lips faded for being kissed and wounded with nails and bitten with teeth (by her lover).

shloka_text: निर्धूतकेशी युवतिर्यथा मृदितवर्णका। निष्पीतशुभदन्तोष्ठी नखैर्दन्तैश्च विक्षता।।5.14.18।। तथा लाङ्गूलहस्तैश्च चरणाभ्यां च मर्दिता। बभूवाशोकवनिका प्रभग्नवरपादपा।।5.14.19।।
explanation: The garden of Ashoka with trees shattered and crushed by Hanuman's tail,  hands and feet, appeared like a woman with dishevelled hair, with her vermilion mark effaced, her bright teeth and lips faded for being kissed and wounded with nails and bitten with teeth (by her lover).

shloka_text: महालतानां दामानि व्यथमत्तरसा कपिः। यथा प्रावृषि विन्ध्यस्य मेघजालानि मारुतः।।5.14.20।।
explanation: Hanuman shook with tremendous speed the huge clusters of creepers hanging there just like stormy wind in rainy season scatters masses of clouds on the Vindhya mountain.

shloka_text: स तत्र मणिभूमीश्च राजतीश्च मनोरमाः। तथा काञ्चनभूमीश्च ददर्श विचरन्कपिः।।5.14.21।।
explanation: Roaming there the monkey noticed the beautiful floors paved with gems, gold and silver৷৷

shloka_text: ﻿वापीश्च विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा। महार्हैर्मणिसोपानैरुपपन्नास्ततस्ततः।।5.14.22।। मुक्ताप्रवालसिकताः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः। काञ्चनैस्तरुभिश्चित्रैस्तीरजैरुपशोभिताः।।5.14.23।। फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपकूजिताः। नत्यूहरुतसंघुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः।।5.14.24।। दीर्घाभिर्द्रुमयुक्ताभिः सरद्भिश्च समन्ततः। अमृतोपमतोयाभिश्शिवाभिरुपसंस्कृताः।।5.14.25।। लताशतैरवततास्सन्तानकुसुमावृताः। नानागुल्मावृतघनाः करवीरकृतान्तराः।।5.14.26।।
explanation: ﻿ He observed ponds of different shapes filled with clear water with steps paved with rich gems, with sands of pearls and corals and bottoms of crystal, which contained beds of lotuses in bloom, adorned with chakravaka birds and resonant with cacklings of swans and sarasas and vatyuhas rubbing their beaks. There were golden platforms built on banks and platforms built of crystals. There were trees on the bank of streams, and nectarlike sacred waters flowing in them surrounded by hundreds of creepers, and Ashoka blossoms scattered everywhere, with thickly grown bushes of different kinds, with lilies in bloom in tanks.

shloka_text: ततोऽम्बुधरसङ्काशं प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्। विचित्रकूटं कूटैश्च सर्वतः परिवारितम्।।5.14.27।। शिलागृहैरवततं नानावृक्षैः समावृतम्। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो रम्यं जगति पर्वतम्।।5.14.28।।
explanation: The tiger among monkeys beheld a delightingful mountain, resembling the raincloud with tall, pleasing peaks, wonderful peaks spread all over the mountain. There were caves built of stone, with a variety of trees.

shloka_text: ततोऽम्बुधरसङ्काशं प्रवृद्धशिखरं गिरिम्। विचित्रकूटं कूटैश्च सर्वतः परिवारितम्।।5.14.27।। शिलागृहैरवततं नानावृक्षैः समावृतम्। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो रम्यं जगति पर्वतम्।।5.14.28।।
explanation: The tiger among monkeys beheld a delightingful mountain, resembling the raincloud with tall, pleasing peaks, wonderful peaks spread all over the mountain. There were caves built of stone, with a variety of trees.

shloka_text: ददर्श च नगात्तस्मान्नदीं निपतितां कपिः। अङ्कादिव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतितां प्रियाम्।।5.14.29।। जले निपतिताग्रैश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम्। वार्यमाणामिव क्रुद्धां प्रमदां प्रियबन्धुभिः।।5.14.30।। पुनरावृत्ततोयां च ददर्श स महाकपिः। प्रसन्नामिव कान्तस्य कान्तां पुनरुपस्थिताम्।।5.14.31।।
explanation: Hanuman, the great monkey saw a stream descending from the hill which looked like a beloved jumping down from the thighs of her lover. It was adorned with trees whose boughs touched the water and thus looking like an angry woman leaving her dear lover but detained by her relatives. With the water running backward in circles it appeared as if the beloved has returned to her lover pleased.

shloka_text: तस्या दूरात्सपद्मिन्यो नानाद्विजगणायुताः। ददर्श हरिशार्दूलो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।।5.14.32।।
explanation: Not far from there, Hanuman, son of the Windgod sighted lotus ponds filled with different kinds of water birds.

shloka_text: कृत्रिमां दीर्घिकां चापि पूर्णां शीतेन वारिणा। मणिप्रवरसोपानां मुक्तासिकतशोभिताम्।।5.14.33।। विविधैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्। प्रासादैस्सुमहद्भिश्च निर्मितैर्विश्वकर्मणा।।5.14.34।। काननैः कृत्रिमैश्चापि सर्वतः समलङ्कृताम्।
explanation: Hanuman saw an oblong pond, full of cool water provided with steps, embellished with gems and beautified with pearl dust as sand on its bank.  Thronged with many kinds of animals, it looked colourful with large mansions constructed by Visvakarma in the artificial woodlands decorated all over.

shloka_text: कृत्रिमां दीर्घिकां चापि पूर्णां शीतेन वारिणा। मणिप्रवरसोपानां मुक्तासिकतशोभिताम्।।5.14.33।। विविधैर्मृगसङ्घैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्। प्रासादैस्सुमहद्भिश्च निर्मितैर्विश्वकर्मणा।।5.14.34।। काननैः कृत्रिमैश्चापि सर्वतः समलङ्कृताम्।
explanation: Hanuman saw an oblong pond, full of cool water provided with steps, embellished with gems and beautified with pearl dust as sand on its bank.  Thronged with many kinds of animals, it looked colourful with large mansions constructed by Visvakarma in the artificial woodlands decorated all over.

shloka_text: ये केचित्पादपास्तत्र पुष्पोपगफलोपगाः।।5.14.35।। सच्छत्रास्सवितर्दीकास्सर्वे सौवर्णवैदिकाः।
explanation: There the trees had abundance of flowers and fruits. A few trees were full of leaves and branches spread like parasols. There were raised golden platforms.

shloka_text: लताप्रतानैर्बहुभिःपर्णैश्च बहुभिर्वृताम्।।5.14.36।। काञ्चनीं शिंशुपामेकां ददर्श हरियूथपः। वृतां हेममयीभिस्तु वेदिकाभिस्समन्ततः।।5.14.37।।
explanation: The monkey leader saw one simsupa tree covered all over with canopies of many climbers and leaves. The tree was surrounded by golden platforms.

shloka_text: लताप्रतानैर्बहुभिःपर्णैश्च बहुभिर्वृताम्।।5.14.36।। काञ्चनीं शिंशुपामेकां ददर्श हरियूथपः। वृतां हेममयीभिस्तु वेदिकाभिस्समन्ततः।।5.14.37।।
explanation: The monkey leader saw one simsupa tree covered all over with canopies of many climbers and leaves. The tree was surrounded by golden platforms.

shloka_text: सोऽपश्यद्भूमिभागांश्च गर्तप्रस्रवणानि च। सुवर्णवृक्षानपरान् ददर्श शिखिसन्निभान्।।5.14.38।।
explanation: He beheld several pieces of land and streams flowing out of the springs. He also noticed golden trees asresplendent as fire.

shloka_text: तेषां द्रुमाणां प्रभया मेरोरिव दिवाकरः। अमन्यत तदा वीरः काञ्चनोऽस्मीति वानरः।।5.14.39।।
explanation: He saw trees resplendent with golden radiance and thought that he was in the midst of gold like the Sungod getting golden hue by the radiance of Meru, the golden mountain.

shloka_text: तां काञ्चनैस्तरुगणैर्मारुतेन च वीजिताम्। किङ्किणीशतनिर्घोषां दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमागमत्।।5.14.40।।
explanation: Hanuman was wonderstruck to hear the sound produced by rows of golden trees which stood round the simsupa tree. This sound resembled the tinkling of a hundred anklets when the wind passed through (their leaves).

shloka_text: स पुष्पिताग्रां रुचिरां तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवाम्। तामारुह्य महाबाहुश्शिंशुपां पर्णसंवृताम्।।5.14.41।।
explanation: Strongarmed Hanuman climbed up the simsupa tree shining with flowers on its top and surrounded by tender sprouts and leaves. (He said to himself):

shloka_text: इतो द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं रामदर्शनलालसाम्। इतश्चेतश्च दुःखार्तां सम्पतन्तीं यदृच्छया।।5.14.42।।
explanation: "I may see by chance( from this point) Vaidehi tormented with grief anxiously waiting to see Rama while moving about here and there casually.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिका चेयं दृढं रम्या दुरात्मनः। चम्पकैश्चन्दनैश्चापि वकुलैश्च विभूषिता।।5.14.43।।
explanation: "Surely this beautiful Ashoka grove with delightful champak, chandan and bakula trees belongs to the wicked Ravana."

shloka_text: इयं च नलिनी रम्या द्विजसङ्घनिषेविता। इमां सा राममहिषी नूनमेष्यति जानकी।।5.14.44।।
explanation: "This lovely lotuspond is frequented by flocks of aquatic birds. Surely Rama's queen Janaki will come to this place.

shloka_text: सा रामा राममहिषी राघवस्य प्रिया सती। वनसञ्चारकुशला नूनमेष्यति जानकी।।5.14.45।।
explanation: "Beautiful Janaki, beloved queen of Rama loves to wander in forests. She will surely visit this grove.

shloka_text: अथवा मृगशाबाक्षी वनस्यास्य विचक्षणा। वनमेष्यति साऽर्येह रामचिन्तानुकर्शिता।।5.14.46।।
explanation: "Or may be that doeeyed noble lady brooding over Rama will come to this garden she   is familiar with.

shloka_text: रामशोकाभिसन्तप्ता सा देवी वामलोचना। वनवासे रता नित्यमेष्यते वनचारिणी।।5.14.47।।
explanation: "That lovelyeyed queen tormented with grief over separation from Rama will be coming here to stay as she always loves strolling in the forest.

shloka_text: वनेचराणां सततं नूनं स्पृहयते पुरा। रामस्य दयिता भार्या जनकस्यसुता सती।।5.14.48।।
explanation: "The daughter of Janaka, the  chaste wife of Rama,  used to for the company of those creatures wandering in the forest.

shloka_text: सन्ध्याकालमनाः श्यामा ध्रुवमेष्यति जानकी। नदीं चेमां शुभजलां सन्ध्यार्थे वरवर्णिनी।।5.14.49।।
explanation: Surely that lady of lovely complexion, the beautiful Janaki will come to this river flowing with sacred waters for performing the evening rituals.

shloka_text: तस्याश्चाप्यनुरूपेयमशोकवनिका शुभा। शुभा या पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य पत्नी रामस्य सम्मता।।5.14.50।।
explanation: To the auspicious Sita,the beloved of Rama, the lord of the world, this Ashoka grove is a befitting place.

shloka_text: यदि जीवति सा देवी ताराधिपनिभानना। आगमिष्यति साऽवश्यमिमां शिवजलां नदीम्।।5.14.51।।
explanation: "The moonfaced queen will certainly come to this stream of  auspicious water if she is surviving."

shloka_text: एवं तु मत्वा हनुमान्महात्मा प्रतीक्षमाणो मनुजेन्द्रपत्नीम्। अवेक्षमाणश्च ददर्श सर्वं सुपुष्पिते पर्णघने निलीनः।।5.14.52।।
explanation: Pondering thus, the highsouled Hanuman remained concealed on the tree loaded with flowers and leaves and waited, looking eagerly for the wife of the lord of the people. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्दशस्सर्गः। Thus ends the fourteenth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स वीक्षमाणस्तत्रस्थो मार्गमाणश्च मैथिलीम्। अवेक्षमाणश्च महीं सर्वां तामन्ववैक्षत।।5.15.1।।
explanation: Hanuman looked out from the simsupa tree all around for Mythili scanning the ground below.

shloka_text: सन्तानकलताभिश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम्। दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतां सर्वतस्समलङ्कृताम्।।5.15.2।। तां स नन्दनसङ्काशां मृगपक्षिभिरावृताम्। हर्म्यप्रासादसम्बाधां कोकिलाकुलनिस्स्वनाम्।।5.15.3।। काञ्चनोत्पलपद्माभिर्वापीभिरुपशोभिताम्। बह्वासनकुथोपेतां बहुभूमिगृहायुताम्।।5.15.4।। सर्वर्तुकुसुमै रम्यां फलवद्भिश्च पादपैः। पुष्पितानामशोकानां श्रिया सूर्योदयप्रभाम्।।5.15.5।। प्रदीप्तामिव तत्रस्थो मारुतिस्समुदैक्षत। निष्पत्रशाखां विहगैः क्रियमाणामिवासकृत्।।5.15.6।। विनिष्पतद्भिः शतशश्चित्रैः पुष्पावतंसकैः। आमूलपुष्पनिचितैरशोकैश्शोकनाशनैः।।5.15.7।। पुष्पभारातिभारैश्च स्पृशद्भिरिव मेदिनीम्। कर्णिकारैः कुसुमितैः किंशुकैश्च सुपुष्पितैः।।5.15.8।।
explanation: Hanuman surveyed from the Simsupa tree the Ashoka grove of trees full of fine fragrance. It looked welldecorated  like the Nandana garden of Indra. It teemed with animals and birds. It was filled with the voices of the cuckoos. It had tall mansions and underground chamber. There were golden lilies and lotuses in the lakes, enchanting couches with rich coverings and trees full of blossoms of all seasons and fruits in abundance With the  Ashoka tree shedding showers of flowers from time to time the place shone with the splendour of Sunrise. It glittered like inflamed fire. The Ashoka tree had  hundreds of colourful birds on the branches. It appeared as if it had branches without leaves which made them look like earornaments (of the grove). Ashoka flowers in bloom hung down to the base of the tree as if to take away the grief of the onlookers. The blossoms of the Karnikara and kimsuka brightened the whole grove.

explanation: The grove shone bright as if it were inflamed fire with beautiful trees like purnaga, saptaparna, champak and uddalaka in full bloom.

shloka_text: शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः।।5.15.10।। नीलाञ्जननिभाः केचित्तत्राशोकास्सहस्रशः।
explanation: There were thousands of ashoka trees some of which shone like gold, others like the flames of fire and some dark as collyrium.

shloka_text: नन्दनं विविधोद्यानं चित्रं चैत्ररथं यथा।।5.15.11।। अतिवृत्तमिवाचिन्त्यं दिव्यं रम्यं श्रिया वृतम्। वितीयमिव चाकाशं पुष्पज्योतिर्गणायुतम्।।5.15.12।। पुष्परत्नशतैश्चित्रं द्वितीयं सागरं यथा। सर्वर्तुपुष्पैर्निचितं पादपैर्मधुगन्धिभिः।।5.15.13।। नानानिनादैरुद्यानं रम्यं मृगगणैर्द्विजैः। अनेकगन्धप्रवहं पुण्यगन्धं मनोरमम्।।5.15.14।।
explanation: The grove with different types of gardens spread over looked like the Nandana garden of Indra and Chaitraratha garden of Kubera. It surpassed every other garden. It was unimaginable in splendour. It was divine and delightful filled with the radiance of countless varieties of blossoms shining like stars, like a second firmament. It was like another ocean filled with precious gems of flowers. It had trees with flowers of honeyscented fragrance. Sounds of animals and birds filled the air. It was pleasing to the heart with various divine fragrances wafted (by the breeze)৷৷

shloka_text: शैलेन्द्रमिव गन्धाढ्यं द्वितीयं गन्धमादनम्। अशोकवनिकायां तु तस्यां वानरपुङ्गवः।।5.15.15।। स ददर्शाविदूरस्थं चैत्यप्रासादमुच्छ्रितम्। मथ्ये स्तम्भसहस्रेण स्थितं कैलासपाण्डुरम्।।5.15.16।। प्रवालकृतसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम्। मुष्णन्तमिव चक्षूंषि द्योतमानमिव श्रिया।।5.15.17।। विमलं प्रांशुभावत्वादुल्लिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्।
explanation: The monkey leader saw a lofty templelike structure in the midst of the Ashoka grove which was highly fragrant and appeared like another indescribable structure that stood on a thousand pillars like another Gandhamadana mountain. It gleamed white like mount Kailasa. Its stairs were paved with corals. The altars were made of brightly polished gold. This structure glowing with brilliance was as if stealing the eyes. It looked white with light and lofty as though scratching the sky.
