explanation: The army of monkeys had lost control over their bodies due to drinking of honeywine. Not even one was quietly seated there. Not even one was not intoxicated. Not only that, none were satisfied.

shloka_text: ततो वनं तत्परिभक्ष्यमाणं द्रुमांश्च विध्वंसितपत्रपुष्पान्। समीक्ष्य कोपाद्धधिवक्रनामा निवारयामास कपिः कपींस्तान्।।5.61.19।।
explanation: Beholding the destruction wrought by the vanaras to the garden, trees, leaves and flowers, and having drunk all the honey, Dadhimukha angrily asked them to stop and get out.

shloka_text: स तैः प्रवृद्धैः परिभर्त्स्यमानो वनस्य गोप्ता हरिवीरवृद्धः। चकार भूयो मतिमुग्रतेजा वनस्य रक्षां प्रति वानरेभ्यः।।5.61.20।।
explanation: The elderly Dadhimukha who was the powerful protector of the garden reprimanded them and devised yet again a plan to protect it.

shloka_text: उवाच कांश्चित्परुषाणि धृष्टमसक्तमन्यांश्च तलैर्जघान। समेत्य कैश्चित्कलहं चकार तथैव साम्नोपजगाम कांश्चित्।।5.61.21।।
explanation: He spoke harshly to some, to others he asked not to talk, some he slapped on the hind part with the palm of his hand. To some he spoke pleasantly and with some he quarrelled. And to others he spoke in a conciliatory manner.

shloka_text: स तैर्मदात्संपरिवार्य वाक्यैर्भलाच्छ तेन प्रतिवार्यमाणैः। प्रधर्षितस्त्यक्तभयै स्समेत्य प्रकृष्यते चाप्यनवेक्ष्य दोषम्।।5.61.22।।
explanation: In their drunkenness they were using abusive language and with their strength they retaliated without fear. They invaded without considering their mistakes. They caught hold of Dadhimukha and pulled him.

shloka_text: नखैस्तुदन्तो दशनैर्दशन्त स्तलैश्च पादैश्च समापयन्तः। मदात्कपिं तं कपय स्समग्रा महावनं निर्विषयं च चक्रुः।।5.61.23।।
explanation: In their drunkenness some monkeys scratched Dadhimukha violently with their nails, some bit him with their teeth and others slapped and kicked him with their palms and legs.Getting together they looted the garden completely. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे एकषष्टितम स्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfirst sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तानुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठो हनुमान्वानरर्षभः। अव्यग्रमनसो यूयं मधु सेवत वानराः।।5.62.1।। अहमावारयिष्यामि युष्माकं परिपन्थिनः।
explanation: Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, bull among vanaras said, 'Enjoy the honey devoid of any fear. I shall prevent those who object to your action'.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं हरीणां प्रवरोऽङ्गदः।।5.62.2।। प्रत्युवाच प्रसन्नात्मा पिबन्तु हरयो मधु।
explanation: Pleased with Hanuman's words, the distinguished Angada permitted the monkeys to drink.

shloka_text: अवश्यं कृतकार्यस्य वाक्यं हनुमतो मया।।5.62.3।। अकार्यमपि कर्तव्यं किमङ्ग पुनरीदृशम्।
explanation: Even if Hanuman, the achiever, forbids me to do something, I will do it. And now when he has permitted you, why hesitate ?

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्य मुखाच्छ्रुत्वावचनं वानरर्षभाः।।5.62.4।। साधुसाध्विति संहृष्टा वानराः प्रत्यपूजयन्।
explanation: Having heard the words that came from Angada's mouth, the bulls among vanaras praised him for his generous approval.

shloka_text: पूजयित्वाङ्गदं सर्वे वानरा वानरर्षभम्।।5.62.5।। जग्मुर्मधुवनं यत्र नदीवेग इव द्रुमम्।
explanation: The vanaras praised Angada, the bull among vanaras and went to Madhuvanam swiftly like a fastflowing river going to uproot a tree.

shloka_text: ते प्रविष्टा मधुवनं पालानाक्रम्य वीर्यतः।।5.62.6।। अतिसर्गाच्च पटवो दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम्। पपुस्सर्वे मधु तदा रसवत्फलमाददुः।।5.62.7।।
explanation: Overjoyed at the news of Mythili, being seen, the vanaras entered Madhuvanam and attacked the guards violently, drank the honey and ate the tasty fruits.

shloka_text: ते प्रविष्टा मधुवनं पालानाक्रम्य वीर्यतः।।5.62.6।। अतिसर्गाच्च पटवो दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम्। पपुस्सर्वे मधु तदा रसवत्फलमाददुः।।5.62.7।।
explanation: Overjoyed at the news of Mythili, being seen, the vanaras entered Madhuvanam and attacked the guards violently, drank the honey and ate the tasty fruits.

shloka_text: उत्पत्य च ततस्सर्वे वनपालान् समागतान्। ताडयन्ति स्म शतश स्सक्तान्मधुवने तदा।।5.62.8।।
explanation: All the vanaras collected together, entered the Madhuvanam and attacked in many ways the guards protecting  the  garden.

shloka_text: मधूनि द्रोणमात्राणि बाहुभिः परिगृह्य ते। पिबन्ति सहिता स्सर्वे निघ्नन्ति स्म तथापरे।।5.62.9।।
explanation: All of them now gathered at one place and drank honey from large containers. Others were busy preventing the guards.

shloka_text: केचित्पीत्वा प्रविध्यन्ति मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः। मधूच्छिष्टेन केचिच्च जग्मुरन्योन्यमुत्कटाः।।5.62.10।।
explanation: The honeycoloured monkeys drank honey. Some threw large chunks of honey combs after drinking and some went about intoxicated.

shloka_text: अपरे वृक्षमूले तु शाखां गृह्य व्यवस्थिताः। अत्यर्थं च मदग्लानाः पर्णान्यास्तीर्य शेरते।।5.62.11।।
explanation: Some took branches of trees and rested at the root of trees. Some totally languid lay down spreading leaves due to drinking of sweet drinks.

shloka_text: उन्मत्तभूताः प्लवगा मधुमत्ताश्च हृष्टवत्। क्षिपन्ति च तथान्योन्यं स्खलन्ति च तथाऽपरे।।5.62.12।।
explanation: Intoxicated with drink, some behaved like mad people, some pushed others senselessly and some were unsteady and shaky.

shloka_text: केचित् क्ष्वेलां प्रकुर्वन्ति केचित् कूजन्ति हृष्टवत्। हरयोमधुना मत्ताः केचित्सुप्ता महीतले।।5.62.13।।
explanation: Some roared, some warbled happily, some felt drowsy, drinking honey and some dropped off to sleep on the ground.

shloka_text: कृत्वा केचिद्धसन्त्यन्ये केचित्कुर्वन्ति चेतरत्। कृत्वा केचिद्वदन्त्यन्ये केचिद्बुध्यन्ति चेतरत्।।5.62.14।।
explanation: Some made others laugh, some provoked others and some thought of doing something else having got over the intoxication.

shloka_text: येऽप्यत्र मधुपाला स्स्युः प्रेष्या दधिमुखस्य तु। तेऽपि तैर्वानरैर्भीमैः प्रतिषिद्धा दिशो गताः।।5.62.15।।
explanation: All the guards engaged in protecting the garden were driven away in all directions by the fierce vanaras.

shloka_text: जानुभिस्तु प्रकृष्टाश्च देवमार्गं प्रदर्शिताः। अब्रुवन् परमोद्विग्ना गत्वा दधिमुखं वचः।।5.62.16।।
explanation: Some were dragged on their knees and tossed up. Some monkeys exhibited their private parts, showing indecent behaviour. Dadhimukha, highly disturbed at this, said:

shloka_text: हनूमता दत्तवरैर्हतं मधुवनं बलात्। वयं च जानुभिः कृष्टा देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः।।5.62.17।।
explanation: Permitted by Hanuman (to enter Madhuvanam and drink), they dragged one another forcefully tossed up  on their knees showing their private parts.

shloka_text: ततो दधिमुख: क्रुद्धो वनपस्तत्र वानरः। हतं मधुवनं श्रुत्वा सान्त्वयामास तान् हरीन्।।5.62.18।।
explanation: Then Dadhimukha, the guardian of the garden became furious on the vanaras. Having heard from the guards that the garden was destroyed, he said soothing words to them.

shloka_text: इहागच्छत गच्छामो वानरान् बलदर्पितान्। बलेन वारयिष्यामो मधु भक्षयतो वयम्।।5.62.19।।
explanation: "Come, we will all go there to Madhuvanam and prevent forcibly the vanaras who have consumed honey proud of their power.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं वानरर्षभाः। पुनर्वीरा मधुवनं तेनैव सहसा ययुः।।5.62.20।।
explanation: "The heroes, bulls among vanaras, heard Dadhimukha and quickly entered Madhuvanam along with him.

shloka_text: मध्ये चैषां दधिमुखः प्रगृह्य तरसा तरुम्। समभ्यधावद्वेगेन ते च सर्वे प्लवङ्गमाः।।5.62.21।।
explanation: On the way, the energetic Dadhimukha took up a tree and ran to the leaping vanaras swiftly with guards following him.

shloka_text: ते शिलाः पादपांश्चापि पर्वतांश्चापि वानराः। गृहीत्वाऽऽभ्यगमन् क्रुद्धा यत्र ते कपिकुञ्जराः।।5.62.22।।
explanation: The furious vanara guards lifted rocks, trees and even mountains and went behind Dadhimukha the elephant among the vanaras.

shloka_text: ते स्वामिवचनं वीरा हृदयेष्ववसज्य तत्। त्वरया ह्यभ्यधावन्त सालतालशिलायुधाः।।5.62.23।।
explanation: The heroic vanaras held Sala and Tala trees and rushed at once keeping their leader's words in mind.

shloka_text: वृक्षस्थांश्च तलस्थांश्च वानरान् बलदर्पितान्। अभ्यक्रामंस्ततो वीराः पालास्तत्र सहस्रशः।।5.62.24।।
explanation: Then the heroic guards in their thousands fell on the vanaras proud of their power on and under the tala trees.

shloka_text: अथ दृष्ट्वा दधिमुखं क्रुद्धं वानरपुङ्गवाः। अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन हनुमत्प्रमुखास्तदा।।5.62.25।।
explanation: Having seen the fury of Dadhimukha, Hanuman the leader of the vanaras went to him swiftly.

shloka_text: तं सवृक्षं महाबाहुमापतन्तं महाबलम्। आर्यकं प्राहरत्तत्र बाहुभ्यां कुपितोऽङ्गदः।।5.62.26।।
explanation: Seeing the revered, powerful and strongarmed Dadhimukha rushing to him, the angry Angada caught him with both hands tightly.

shloka_text: मदान्धश्च न वेदैनमार्यकोऽयं ममेति सः। अथैनं निष्पिपेषाशु वेगवद्वसुधातले।।5.62.27।।
explanation: "Blinded by arrogance, the prince pushed him (Dadhimukha) on the floor forcibly,  forgetting that he was his revered granduncle.

shloka_text: स भग्नबाहूरुभुजो विह्वलश्शोणितोक्षितः। मुमोह सहसा वीरो मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः।।5.62.28।।
explanation: The heroic Dadhimukha, an elephant among monkeys, with his shoulders and arms broken, and body drenched in blood lost his consciousness instantly.

shloka_text: स समाश्वस्य सहसा सङ्कृद्धो राजमातुलः। वानरान्वारयामास दण्डेन मधुमोहितान्।।5.62.29।।
explanation: At once Dadhimukha, the maternal uncle of the king became conscious and chased with a stick the intoxicated vanaras.

shloka_text: स कथञ्चिद्विमुक्तस्स्तैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभः। उवाचैकान्तमाश्रित्य भृत्यान् स्वान् समुपागतान्।।5.62.30।।
explanation: Escaping from the vanaras with great difficulty, Dadhimukha,  a bull among monkeys, repaired to a secluded place and said to his servants:

shloka_text: एते तिष्ठन्तु गच्छामो भर्ता नो यत्र वानरः। सुग्रीवो विपुलग्रीवः सह रामेण तिष्ठति।।5.62.31।।
explanation: "Let them stay here. Our broadnecked king Sugriva will be there with Rama. Let us go to him.

shloka_text: सर्वं चैवाङ्गदे दोषं श्रावयिष्यामि पार्थिवे। अमर्षी वचनं श्रुत्वा घातयिष्यति वानरान्।।5.62.32।।
explanation: I will report all the faults in Angada to the king. Having heard the words, the wrathful one will cause the monkeys to be killed.

shloka_text: इष्टं मधुवनं ह्येतत्पार्थिवस्य महात्मनः। पितृपैतामहं दिव्यं देवैरपि दुरासदम्।।5.62.33।।
explanation: 'Madhuvan has come down to us from our forefather's time. Dear to the king, its entry is prohibited even to the gods.

shloka_text: स वानरानिमान् सर्वान् मधुलुब्धान् गतायुषः। घातयिष्यति दण्डेन सुग्रीवस्ससुहृज्जनान्।।5.62.34।।
explanation: 'Sugriva will chase all the vanaras and their friends greedy for honey. They will be punished with a stick. They are doomed'.

shloka_text: वध्या ह्येते दुरात्मानो नृपाज्ञापरिभाविनः। अमर्षप्रभवो रोषस्सफलो नो भविष्यति।।5.62.35।।
explanation: 'Indeed those evilminded ones who have disobeyed the king's order deserve to be killed.That way our fury and forbearance will result in success'.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दधिमुखो वनपालान्महाबलः। जगाम सहसोत्पत्य वनपालैस्समन्वितः।।5.62.36।।
explanation: Powerful Dadhimukha having said that to the guardians of the garden rose up to the sky and went off with them.

shloka_text: निमेषान्तरमात्रेण स हि प्राप्तो वनालयः। सहस्रांशुसुतो धीमान् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः।।5.62.37।।
explanation: In a moment, Dadhimukha reached the place where wise Sugriva, the son of Sungod was there

shloka_text: रामं च लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवमेव च। समप्रतिष्ठां जगतीमाकाशान्निपपात ह।।5.62.38।।
explanation: Seeing Rama, Lakshmana and also Sugriva from the sky he landed on an even ground.

shloka_text: सन्निपत्य महावीर्यस्सर्वैस्तै: परिवारितः। हरिर्दधिमुखः पालैः पालानां परमेश्वरः।।5.62.39।। स दीनवदनो भूत्वा कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम्। सुग्रीवस्य शुभौ मूर्ध्ना चरणौ पत्यपीडयत्।।5.62.40।।
explanation: Dadhimukha, a great hero and king of the guards protecting Madhuvanam surrounded by his servants, with a sad expression on his face offered painful obeisance with folded hands bowing down his forehead at the feet of Sugriva. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysecond sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततो मूर्ध्ना निपतितं वानरं वानरर्षभः। दृष्ट्वैवोद्विग्नहृदयो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।।5.63.1।।
explanation: Feeling anxious on seeing Dadhimukha touching his feet with his forehead, Sugriva, the bull among vanaras said:

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कस्मात्त्वं पादयोः पतितो मम। अभयं ते भवेद्वीर सर्वमेवाभिधीयताम्।।5.63.2।।
explanation: "O heroic Dadhimukha, get up. Tell me why you have fallen at my feet. I give you protection from all.

shloka_text: स तु विश्वासितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना। उत्थाय सुमहाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं दधिमुखोऽब्रवीत्।।5.63.3।।
explanation: When great Sugriva gave assurance to wise Dadhimukha, he got up and said:

shloka_text: नैवर्क्षरजसा राजन्न त्वया नापि वालिना। वनं निसृष्टपूर्वं हि भक्षितं तच्च वानरैः।।5.63.4।।
explanation: "O king in your time or even before, during the time of Vali, that (Madhuvanam) was forbidden for entry. Now it has been laid waste by the trespassing vanaras.

shloka_text: एभिः प्रधर्षिताश्चैव वानरा वनरक्षिभिः। मधून्यचिन्तयित्वेमान् भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च।।5.63.5।।
explanation: "Even though the garden guards forcibly tried to prevent them they did not care and have devoured all the honey.

shloka_text: शिष्टमत्रापविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथापरे। निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भ्रुवो वै दर्शयन्ति हि।।5.63.6।।
explanation: "Some have thrown off the leftovers, when others were prevented from drinking off the honey, they raised their eyebrows (to show their grouch).

shloka_text: इमे हि संरब्धतरास्तथा तैस्सम्प्रधर्षिताः। वारयन्तो वनात्तस्मात्क्रुद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः।।5.63.7।।
explanation: "When the guards asked the vanaras to leave the garden the enraged vanaras misbehaved with them.

shloka_text: ततस्तैर्बहुभिर्वीरैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभ। संरक्तनयनैः क्रोधाद्धरयः प्रविचालिताः।।5.63.8।।
explanation: "O Sugriva the vanara guards were chased away by the many heroic monkeys, angry and redeyed.

shloka_text: पाणिभिर्निहताः केचित्केचिज्जानुभिराहताः। प्रकृष्टाश्च यथाकामं देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः।।5.63.9।।
explanation: "Some were struck with hands, some beaten on their knees and were dragged as they liked and showed up their private parts.

shloka_text: एवमेते हताश्शूरास्त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि। कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैः प्रभक्ष्यते।।5.63.10।।
explanation: These heroes struck that way devoured the Madhuvanam on the earth at their will and devoured the honey even when you are there as king.

shloka_text: एवं विज्ञाप्यमानं तं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्। अपृच्छत्तं महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।।5.63.11।।
explanation: While Dadhimukha appealed thus to wise Sugriva, Lakshmana the killer of enemies happened to see them and enquired:

shloka_text: किमयं वानरो राजन् वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः। कं चार्थमभिनिर्दिश्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।5.63.12।।
explanation: "O king why has this protector of the garden come here? Why is he sad? What is he narrating, asked Lakshmana.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना। लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाचेदं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।।5.63.13।।
explanation: Great prince Lakshmana thus said, Sugriva the proficient speaker replied:

shloka_text: आर्य लक्ष्मण सम्प्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः। अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्भक्षितं मधु वानरैः।।5.63.14।। विचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः।
explanation: 'O venerable Lakshmana Dadhimukha as complaining that the fruits and honey have been consumed by the vanara heroes, Angada and others who have come after their search for Sita in the southern direction.

shloka_text: नैषामकृत्यानामीदृशस्स्यादुपक्रमः।।5.63.15।। आगतैश्च प्रमथितं यथा मधुवनं हि तैः। धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं च वानरैः।।5.63.16।।
explanation: "Those vanaras having entered Madhuvanam and broken the trees are quite right. Had they not accomplished their purpose they would not have indulged themselves that way.

shloka_text: नैषामकृत्यानामीदृशस्स्यादुपक्रमः।।5.63.15।। आगतैश्च प्रमथितं यथा मधुवनं हि तैः। धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं च वानरैः।।5.63.16।।
explanation: "Those vanaras having entered Madhuvanam and broken the trees are quite right. Had they not accomplished their purpose they would not have indulged themselves that way.

shloka_text: वनं यदाऽभिपन्नास्ते साधितं कर्म वानरैः। दृष्टा देवी न सन्देहो न चान्येन हनूमता।।5.63.17।।
explanation: "If they have trespassed into the garden that way, they might have done their duty. No doubt, Hanuman alone among them might have seen Sita.

shloka_text: न ह्यन्यस्साधने हेतुः कर्मणोऽस्य हनूमतः। कार्यसिद्धिर्मतिश्चैव तस्मिन्वानरपुङ्गवे।।5.63.18।। व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्।
explanation: "Hanuman alone has the ability to do it, the reason being he has the capacity the wisdom, streneous effort, virility and enthusiasm to accomplish it. These attributes are wellestablished in him.

shloka_text: जाम्बवान्यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च महाबलः।।5.63.19।। हनुमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तस्य गतिरन्यथा।
explanation: Where Jambavan, Angada and Hanuman are leaders directing the task of the army it must have been accomplished.

shloka_text: अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्हतं मधुवनं किल।।5.63.20।। वारयन्तश्च सहितास्तदा जानुभिराहताः।
explanation: Madhuvana was indeed destroyed by heroes led by Angada. And those who tried to stop them were then struck down together with knees.

shloka_text: एतदर्थमयं प्राप्तो वक्तुं मधुरवागिह।।5.63.21।। नाम्ना दधिमुखो नाम हरिः प्रख्यातविक्रमः।
explanation: "Here is Dadhimukha, a vanara, known for his valour and sweet tongue. He came here this incident to tell.

shloka_text: दृष्टा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतः।।5.63.22।। अभिगम्य तथा सर्वे पिबन्ति मधु वानराः।
explanation: "O strongarmed Saumitri the Vanaras must have seen Sita. Or else, they would not have arrived to drink honey.

shloka_text: न चाप्यदृष्ट्वा वैदेहीं विश्रुताः पुरुषर्षभ।।5.63.23।। वनं दत्तवरं दिव्यं धर्षयेयुर्वनौकसः।
explanation: "If the renowned vanaras had not seen Vaidehi, they would not have entered the wonderful garden granted as boon (by Brahma).

shloka_text: ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणस्सह राघवः।।5.63.24।। श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम्। प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।।5.63.25।।
explanation: "Then righteous Rama and Lakshmana rejoiced to hear the words of Sugriva, which were pleasing to the ears.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणस्सह राघवः।।5.63.24।। श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम्। प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।।5.63.25।।
explanation: "Then righteous Rama and Lakshmana rejoiced to hear the words of Sugriva, which were pleasing to the ears.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं सुग्रीवस्सम्प्रहृष्य च। वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत।।5.63.26।।
explanation: Beautifulnecked Sugriva heard Dadhimukha, the protector of the garden, felt very glad and replied:

shloka_text: प्रीतोऽस्मि सोऽहं यद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः। मर्षितं मर्षणीयं च चेष्टितं कृतकर्मणाम्।।5.63.27।।
explanation: "They went to the garden to drink only after having performed their duty. I am glad about it. Since they have accomplished the purpose, they are to be excused for their behaviour. I have pardoned them.

shloka_text: इच्छामि शीघ्रं हनुमत्प्रधानान् शाखामृगांस्तान् मृगराजदर्पान्। द्रष्टुं कृतार्थान् सह राघवाभ्यां श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम्।।5.63.28।।
explanation: I quickly desire to see those monkeys, led by Hanuman, who possess the pride of lions, having accomplished their purpose, along with the two Raghus, and to hear of their efforts in finding Sita.

shloka_text: प्रीतिस्फीताक्षौ सम्प्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थौ वानराणां च राजा। अङ्गैः संहृष्टैः कर्मसिद्धिं विदित्वा बाह्वोरासन्नां सोऽतिमात्रं ननन्द।।5.63.29।।
explanation: "Beholding young Rama and Lakshmana extremely delighted, their eyes filled with joy out of fulfilment of the purpose, Sugriva who was also highly delighted felt an auspicious thrill on his limbs and knew that good time had come. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtythird sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु हृष्टो दधिमुखः कपिः। राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं चाभ्यवादयत्।।5.64.1।।
explanation: Pleased with Sugriva's command (to send forth Angada and Hanuman) Dadhimukha offered salutations to Sugriva, Rama  and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ। वानरैः सहितः शूरैर्दिवमेवोत्पपात ह।।5.64.2।।
explanation: Dadhimukha offered his obeisance to Sugriva and the mighty Rama and Lakshmana  and rose up to the sky followed by the vanaras.

shloka_text: स यथैवाऽगतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः। निपत्य गगनाद्भूमौतद्वनं प्रविवेश ह।।5.64.3।। स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान्। विमदानुत्थितान्सर्वान् मेहमानान्मधूदकम्।।5.64.4।।
explanation: Descending into Madhuvanam, Dadhimukha saw all the monkey troops free from intoxication (of honeywine).

shloka_text: स यथैवाऽगतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः। निपत्य गगनाद्भूमौतद्वनं प्रविवेश ह।।5.64.3।। स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान्। विमदानुत्थितान्सर्वान् मेहमानान्मधूदकम्।।5.64.4।।
explanation: Descending into Madhuvanam, Dadhimukha saw all the monkey troops free from intoxication (of honeywine).

shloka_text: स तानुपागमद्वीरो बद्ध्वा करपुटाञ्जलिम्। उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमिदं हृष्टवदङ्गदम्।।5.64.5।।
explanation: Heroic Dadhimukha went to Angada, holding his cupped palms reverentially and spoke these conciliatory words with joy:

shloka_text: सौम्य रोषो न कर्तव्यो यदेतत्परिवारितम्। अज्ञानाद्रक्षिभिः क्रोधाद्भवन्तः प्रतिषेधिताः।।5.64.6।।
explanation: "O handsome one, do not react harshly at these guards who have obstructed your companions out of ignorance and fury.

shloka_text: युवराजस्त्वमीशश्च वनस्यास्य महाबल। मौर्ख्यात्पूर्वं कृतो दोषस्तं भवान् क्षन्तुमर्हति।।5.64.7।।
explanation: "O mighty Angada you are heir apparent and also king. Out of foolishness I obstructed you. You ought to pardon me this mistake.

shloka_text: आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ। इहोपयातं सर्वेषामेतेषां वनचारिणाम्।।5.64.8।।
explanation: "O blameless prince I have already told your father's elder brother and all the forestdwellers about your arrival here.

shloka_text: स त्वदागमनं श्रुत्वा सहैभिर्हरियूथपैः। प्रहृष्टो न तु रुष्टोऽसौ वनं श्रुत्वा प्रधर्षितम्।।5.64.9।।
explanation: "He was not angry at your destruction of the garden. On the other hand, he was very glad to hear about your arrival.

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टो मां पितृव्यस्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः। शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वांस्तानिति होवाच पार्थिवः।।5.64.10।।
explanation: "Your father's brother, Sugriva, the lord of vanaras felt very glad and indeed asked me to send you quickly."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं वचनं श्लक्ष्णमङ्गदः। अब्रवीत्तान् हरिश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।।5.64.11।।
explanation: At these good words from Dadhimukha, Angada, the monkey leader, an eloquent speaker said this:.

shloka_text: शङ्के श्रुतोऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः। तत्क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परन्तपाः।।5.64.12।।
explanation: "O scorcher of enemies I presume Rama has already heard the news of our arrival on accomplishment of the task. Hence it is not proper for us to tarry here.

shloka_text: पीत्वा मधु यथाकामं विश्रान्ता वनचारिणः। किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र मे गुरुः।।5.64.13।।
explanation: "The vanaras of the forest have taken rest after drinking as much honey as they desired. What is left here to do? We have to go wherever Sugriva is."

shloka_text: सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरियूथपाः। तथास्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम्।।5.64.14।।
explanation: Angada said to the vanara troops assembled, "Tell me what we have to do. I shall act as you wish.

shloka_text: नाज्ञापयितुमीशोऽहं युवराजोऽस्मि यद्यपि। अयुक्तं कृतकर्माणो यूयं धर्षयितुं मया।।5.64.15।।
explanation: "Even though I am heir apparent, it is not proper for me to order you.You have accomplished the purpose and to command you is not befitting on my part."

shloka_text: ब्रुवतश्चाङ्गदस्यैवं श्रुत्वा वचनमव्ययम्। प्रहृष्टमनसो वाक्यमिदमूचुर्वनौकसः।।5.64.16।।
explanation: On hearing Angada's valuable words said in that way, the vanaras repled:

shloka_text: एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन् प्रभुस्सन्वानरर्षभ। ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि सर्वोऽहमिति मन्यते।।5.64.17।।
explanation: "O king O bull among monkeys we think you are an exception to those to whom prosperity brings arrogance.

shloka_text: तव चेदं सुसदृशं वाक्यं नान्यस्य कस्यचित्। सन्नतिर्हि तवाख्याति भविष्यच्छुभयोग्यताम्।।5.64.18।।
explanation: "You alone could speak such words. Your humility speaks of your fitness for a  bright future.

shloka_text: सर्वे वयमपि प्राप्तास्तत्र गन्तुं कृतक्षणाः। स यत्र हरिवीराणां सुग्रीवः पतिरव्ययः।।5.64.19।।
explanation: All of us also arrived, prepared to go there, where Sugriva, the imperishable lord of the monkey heroes, resides.

shloka_text: त्वया ह्यनुक्तैर्हरिभिर्नैव शक्यं पदात्पदम्। क्वचिद्गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठ ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते।।5.64.20।।
explanation: "O Angada the best of vanaras without your command none will find it possible to put forward even a single step."

shloka_text: एवं तु वदतां तेषामङ्गदः प्रत्युवाच ह। बाढं गच्छाम इत्युक्त्वा खमुत्पेतुर्महाबलाः।।5.64.21।।
explanation: Thus addressed by all the vanaras, Angada said 'Well, let us go'. Then the powerful vanaras rose up the sky.

shloka_text: उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतु स्सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः। कृत्वाकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ता इवाचलाः।।5.64.22।।
explanation: All the vanara troops sprang up into the air as though there was no sky, like stones shattered by machines from the  mountains rise up.

shloka_text: तेऽम्बरं सहसोत्पत्य वेगवन्तः प्लवङ्गमाः। विनदन्तो महानादं घना वातेरिता यथा।।5.64.23।।
explanation: The swift monkeys roared aloud as though they went up the sky like thundering clouds driven by  the wind.

shloka_text: अङ्गदे ह्यननुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः। उवाच शोकोपहतं रामं कमललोचनम्।।5.64.24।।
explanation: Seeing the griefstricken, lotuseyed Rama, the lord of the vanaras Sugriva said this before the arrival of Angada:

shloka_text: समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते दृष्टा देवी न संशयः। नागन्तुमिह शक्यं तैरतीते समये हि नः।।5.64.25।।
explanation: "Trust me, Rama. Be blessed. The vanaras have seen the divine lady. There is no doubt. It is not possible for them to come here after exceeding the time limit  (in their search for Sita).

shloka_text: न मत्सकाशमागच्छेत्कृत्ये हि विनिपातिते। युवराजो महाबाहुः प्लवतां प्रवरोऽङ्गदः।।5.64.26।।
explanation: "My heir apparent, the strongarmed Angada, and the best of the monkeys is endowed with virtues. He would not come near me if his mission had failed.

shloka_text: यद्यप्यकृतकृत्यानामीदृश स्स्यादुपक्रमः। भवेत्स दीनवदनो भ्रान्तविप्लुतमानसः।।5.64.27।।
explanation: "In case the vanaras have returned without accomplishing the task, Angada would have assumed a pathetic face, perplexed and unsteady in mind.

shloka_text: पितृपैतामहं चैतत्पूर्वकैरभिरक्षितम्। न मे मधुवनं हन्यादहृष्टः प्लवगेश्वरः।।5.64.28।। कौसल्यासुप्रजा राम समाश्वसिहि सुव्रत।
explanation: "If Angada, lord of the vanaras had not been happy, he would not have destroyed the Madhuvanam of my father's and my grandfather's time. O Rama, follower of righteous practices, Kausalya has an excellent son in you. Trust me.

shloka_text: दृष्टा देवी न सन्देहो न चान्येन हनूमता।।5.64.29।। न ह्यन्यः कर्मणो हेतुस्साधनेऽस्य हनूमतः।
explanation: "Hanuman is the one who has accomplished this task. Who else can? No doubt, he has seen Sita.

shloka_text: हनूमति हि सिद्धिश्च मतिश्च मतिसत्तमः।।5.64.30।। व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च सूर्ये तेज इव ध्रुवम्।
explanation: "O Rama, the best among the wise just like the luminosity that abides in the Sun, capacity to succeed, energy, intelligence, even courage and steadfastness reside in Hanuman.

shloka_text: जाम्बवान्यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च बलेश्वरः। हनुमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तस्य गतिरन्यथा।।5.64.31।।
explanation: "Where Jambavan is the leader, Angada the commander of the army and Hanuman the guiding force, the end result will not be otherwise.

shloka_text: मा भूश्चिन्तासमायुक्तस्सम्प्रत्यमितविक्रमः।।5.64.32।। ततः किलकिलाशब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे। हनुमत्कर्मदृप्तानां नार्धतां काननौकसाम्।।5.64.33।। किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव।
explanation: "You are extremely valiant and it is unbecoming of you to be anxious at this time Rama. Just then chatterings of the monkeys were heard from the sky as they roared in pride talking of Hanuman's achievement. Having successfully completed the errand, they have arrived at Kishkinda.

shloka_text: मा भूश्चिन्तासमायुक्तस्सम्प्रत्यमितविक्रमः।।5.64.32।। ततः किलकिलाशब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे। हनुमत्कर्मदृप्तानां नार्धतां काननौकसाम्।।5.64.33।। किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव।
explanation: "You are extremely valiant and it is unbecoming of you to be anxious at this time Rama. Just then chatterings of the monkeys were heard from the sky as they roared in pride talking of Hanuman's achievement. Having successfully completed the errand, they have arrived at Kishkinda.

shloka_text: ततश्श्रुत्वा निनादं तं कपीनां कपिसत्तमः।।5.64.34।। आयताञ्चितलाङ्गूलस्सोऽभवद्धृष्टमानसः।
explanation: The great Sugriva heard the roar of the monkeys and was extremely happy. He kept raising and shaking his long tail in joy.

shloka_text: आजग्मुस्तेऽपि हरयो रामदर्शनकांक्षिणः।।5.64.35।। अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्।
explanation: The joyful monkeys with Angada and Hanuman leading them descended with eagerness to have a close look at Rama.

shloka_text: तेऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्ठाश्च मुदान्विताः।।5.64.36।। निपेतुर्हरिराजस्य समीपे राघवस्य च।
explanation: Angada the chief along with the heroic monkeys very joyfully and exuberantly descended close to Sugriva, the king of monkeys and Rama.

shloka_text: हनुमांश्च महाबाहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा ततः।।5.64.37।। नियतामक्षतां देवीं राघवाय न्यवेदयत्।
explanation: Then the strongarmed Hanuman with his head bowed down offered salutations and reported, 'Divine lady Sita with her constant devotion to Sri Rama is sound in body'.

shloka_text: दृष्टा देवीति हनुमद्वदनादमृतोपमम्।।5.64.38।। आकर्ण्य वचनं रामो हर्षमाप सलक्ष्मणः।
explanation: On hearing the nectarlike words from Hanuman that Sita was found, Rama and Lakshmana were delighted.

shloka_text: निश्चितार्थं ततस्तस्मिन् सुग्रीवं पवनात्मजे।।5.64.39।। लक्ष्मणः प्रीतिमान् प्रीतं बहुमानादवैक्षत।
explanation: Sugriva and Lakshmana glanced at Hanuman respectfully with affection thinking surely Hanuman alone has succeeded.

shloka_text: ततः प्रस्रवणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम्। प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।।5.65.1।। युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च। प्रवृत्तिमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः।।5.65.2।।
explanation: Thereafter the vanaras arrived at the Prasrvana mount, with wonderful forests and bowed down to Sri Rama and mighty Lakshaman and Sugriva placing their leader, heir apparent in front. Then they began telling the story of Sita and her state.

shloka_text: ततः प्रस्रवणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम्। प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।।5.65.1।। युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च। प्रवृत्तिमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः।।5.65.2।।
explanation: Thereafter the vanaras arrived at the Prasrvana mount, with wonderful forests and bowed down to Sri Rama and mighty Lakshaman and Sugriva placing their leader, heir apparent in front. Then they began telling the story of Sita and her state.

shloka_text: रावणान्तः पुरे रोधं राक्षसीभिश्च तर्जनम्। रामे समनुरागं च यश्चायं समयः कृतः।।5.65.3।। एतदाख्यान्ति ते सर्वे हरयो रामसन्निधौ।
explanation: The monkeys in Rama's presence narrated all about Sita's detention in Ravana's Ashoka garden, the ogresses threatening her and the time limit fixed by Ravana (for her survival).

shloka_text: वैदेहीमक्षतां श्रुत्वा रामस्तूत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.65.4।। क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते। एतन्मे सर्वमाख्यात वैदेहीं प्रति वानराः।।5.65.5।।
explanation: Hearing of Sita alive and not harmed, Rama asked the vanaras, 'How is Sita? How is she disposed to me? Tell me everything'.

shloka_text: वैदेहीमक्षतां श्रुत्वा रामस्तूत्तरमब्रवीत्।।5.65.4।। क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते। एतन्मे सर्वमाख्यात वैदेहीं प्रति वानराः।।5.65.5।।
explanation: Hearing of Sita alive and not harmed, Rama asked the vanaras, 'How is Sita? How is she disposed to me? Tell me everything'.

shloka_text: रामस्य गदितं श्रुत्वा हरयो रामसन्निधौ। चोदयन्ति हनूमन्तं सीतावृत्तान्तकोविदम्।।5.65.6।।
explanation: On hearing the words from Rama, the vanaras requested Hanuman who was aware of  Sita's position to tell Rama all about her.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः। प्रणम्य शिरसा देव्यै सीतायै तां दिशं प्रति।।5.65.7।। उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञस्सीताया दर्शनं यथा।
explanation: The son of the Wind god, Hanuman who was wise in speech heard the words of Rama, offered salutations to Sita in the direction in which she was located and narrated the story about her discovery.

shloka_text: समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वाहं शतयोजनमायतम्।।5.65.8।। अगच्छं जानकीं सीतां मार्गमाणो दिदृक्षया।
explanation: "Having crossed the sea consisting of a hundred yojanas in quest of Vaidehi, I found her.

shloka_text: तत्र लङ्केति नगरी रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।।5.65.9।। दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य तीरे वसति दक्षिणे।
explanation: "On the southern shore of the ocean is situated the city of Lanka , ruled by the evilminded Ravana.

shloka_text: तत्र दृष्टा मया सीता रावणान्तः पुरे सती।।5.65.10।। सन्न्यस्य त्वयि जीवन्ती रामा राम मनोरथम्।
explanation: "There in the inner palace of Ravana, I saw your lovely wife Sita, with all her hopes pinned on you, giving up all other desires.

shloka_text: दृष्टा मे राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः।।5.65.11।। राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभी रक्षिता प्रमदावने।
explanation: "I found her in the beautiful garden guarded by hideous ogresses threatening her again and again৷৷

shloka_text: दुःख मासाद्यते देवी तथाऽदुःखोचिता सती।।5.65.12।। रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभि स्सुरक्षिता। एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा।।5.65.13।। अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे। रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया।।5.65.14।। देवी कथञ्चित्काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया।
explanation: "Sita, who did not deserve and yet was full of grief was detained by Ravana in his inner palace, guarded by ogresses. She had single braid (a sign of desolation), was pathetic,  and totally absorbed in your thought. She was lying on bare ground with her limbs turned pale, like lotus in winter. She was averse to Ravana and was determined to commit suicide. She has only Rama in her mind. Somehow I found her.

shloka_text: दुःख मासाद्यते देवी तथाऽदुःखोचिता सती।।5.65.12।। रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभि स्सुरक्षिता। एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा।।5.65.13।। अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे। रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया।।5.65.14।। देवी कथञ्चित्काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया।
explanation: "Sita, who did not deserve and yet was full of grief was detained by Ravana in his inner palace, guarded by ogresses. She had single braid (a sign of desolation), was pathetic,  and totally absorbed in your thought. She was lying on bare ground with her limbs turned pale, like lotus in winter. She was averse to Ravana and was determined to commit suicide. She has only Rama in her mind. Somehow I found her.

shloka_text: दुःख मासाद्यते देवी तथाऽदुःखोचिता सती।।5.65.12।। रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभि स्सुरक्षिता। एकवेणीधरा दीना त्वयि चिन्तापरायणा।।5.65.13।। अधःशय्या विवर्णाङ्गी पद्मिनीव हिमागमे। रावणाद्विनिवृत्तार्था मर्तव्यकृतनिश्चया।।5.65.14।। देवी कथञ्चित्काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया।
explanation: "Sita, who did not deserve and yet was full of grief was detained by Ravana in his inner palace, guarded by ogresses. She had single braid (a sign of desolation), was pathetic,  and totally absorbed in your thought. She was lying on bare ground with her limbs turned pale, like lotus in winter. She was averse to Ravana and was determined to commit suicide. She has only Rama in her mind. Somehow I found her.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकुवंशविख्यातिं शनैः कीर्तयतानघ।।5.65.15।। सा मया नरशार्दूल विश्वासमुपपादिता।
explanation: "O sinless one O tiger among men To inspire confidence in her I praised the glory of your Ikshvaku dynasty.

shloka_text: तत स्सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वमर्थं च दर्शिता।।5.65.16।। रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च श्रुत्वा प्रीतिमुपागता। नियत स्समुदाचारो भक्तिश्चास्यास्तथा त्वयि।।5.65.17।।
explanation: "When the divine lady talked to me, I presented all the facts about the alliance of Rama and Sugriva. On hearing me, virtuous Sita, whose devotion is fixed on you became delighted.

shloka_text: तत स्सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वमर्थं च दर्शिता।।5.65.16।। रामसुग्रीवसख्यं च श्रुत्वा प्रीतिमुपागता। नियत स्समुदाचारो भक्तिश्चास्यास्तथा त्वयि।।5.65.17।।
explanation: "When the divine lady talked to me, I presented all the facts about the alliance of Rama and Sugriva. On hearing me, virtuous Sita, whose devotion is fixed on you became delighted.

shloka_text: एवं मया महाभागा दृष्टा जनकनन्दिनी। उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वद्भक्त्या पुरुषर्षभ।।5.65.18।।
explanation: "O bull among men I saw Janaki,the delight of Janaka, a formidable lady filled with devotion to you and richly endowed with austerity.

shloka_text: अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथा वृत्तं तवान्तिके। चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव।।5.65.19।।
explanation: "O wise one, with your ring given her, she told me an anecdote of a crow that took place at Chitrakuta.

shloka_text: विज्ञाप्यश्च नरव्याघ्रो रामो वायुसुत त्वया। अखिलेनेह यद्धृष्टमिति मामाह जानकी।।5.65.20।।
explanation: (She said)'O son of the Windgod you should let Rama, the tiger among men know all that you have seen here.

shloka_text: अयं चास्मै प्रदातव्यो यत्नात्सुपरिरक्षितः। ब्रुवता वचनान्येवं सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः।।5.65.21।।
explanation: 'Within hearing of Sugriva, tell him about your efforts. Present this(signet) to Rama carefully preserved by me.

shloka_text: एष चूडामणिश्श्रीमान् मया सुपरिरक्षितः। मनश्शिलायास्तिलको गण्डपार्श्वे निवेशितः।।5.65.22।। त्वया प्रणष्ठे तिलके तं किल स्मर्तुमर्हसि।
explanation: 'This auspicious (jewel) Chudamani has been preserved by me very carefully. Remind him of the decorative red mark he painted with a stone pigment on my forehead, indeed, it is proper to remind him of this.

shloka_text: एष निर्यातितश्श्रीमान्मया ते वारि सम्भवः। एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रहृष्यामि व्यसने त्वामिवानघ।।5.65.23।।
explanation: 'O sinless one tell Rama that this auspicious Chudamani born in the ocean is sent to him and I was gazing at it as if it was him (Rama) and feeling happy.

shloka_text: जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज।।5.65.24।। ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं रक्षसां वशमागता।
explanation: 'O Son of Dasaratha I will hold on to life for a month. Captured by the demons, I will not live for more than a month'.

shloka_text: इति मामब्रवीत्सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्मचारिणी।।5.65.25।। रावणान्तः पुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना।
explanation: "With her limbs emaciated through austerities detained in Ravana's inner palace, eyes wide open in fear, Sita said this to me:

shloka_text: एतदेव मयाख्यातं सर्वं राघव यद्यथा।।5.65.26।। सर्वथा सागरजले संतारः प्रविधीयताम्।
explanation: "O Rama I have spoken everything that has happened. We have to pay attention to the means of crossing the ocean."

shloka_text: तौ जाताश्वासौ राजपुत्रौ विदित्वा तच्चाभिज्ञानं राघवाय प्रदाय। देव्या चाख्यातं सर्वमेवानुपूर्व्याद्वाचा सम्पूर्णं वायुपुत्त्र श्शशंस।।5.65.27।।
explanation: Coming to know that the two princes were sighing in relief, Hanuman presented the token of identification given by Sita to Rama, after having communicated in full the messsage of Sita in an orderly manner. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyfifth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो हनुमता रामो दशरथात्मज:। तं मणिं हृदये कृत्वा प्ररुरोद सलक्ष्मणः।।5.66.1।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Hanuman, Rama held the token (Chudamani) against his bosom and wept with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तं तु दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं राघव श्शोककर्शितः। नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्।।5.66.2।।
explanation: Seeing the precious jewel, Rama's eyes were filled with tears. Overwhelmed with grief, he spoke to Sugriva.

shloka_text: यथैव धेनु स्स्रवति स्नेहाद्वत्सस्य वत्सला। तथा ममापि हृदयं मणिरत्नस्य दर्शनात्।।5.66.3।।
explanation: "Just as a cow fond of its calf begins to distil milk from its teats at the sight of the calf, so does my heart melt at the sight of this excellent jewel.

shloka_text: मणिरत्नमिदं दत्तं वैदेह्याश्श्वशुरेण मे। वधूकाले यथाबद्धमधिकं मूर्ध्नि शोभते।।5.66.4।।
explanation: "At the time of marriage, this jewel was presented by my father-in-law. Vaidehi wore it on her forehead and it looked charming.

shloka_text: अयं हि जलसम्भूतो मणिस्सज्जनपूजितः। यज्ञे परमतुष्टेन दत्तश्शक्रेण धीमता।।5.66.5।।
explanation: "This was found in water and was bestowed by Indra out of great joy on Janaka who had performed a grand sacrificial ceremony. So it was worshipped by elders of the family.

shloka_text: इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं यथा तातस्य दर्शनम्। अद्यास्म्यवगतस्सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः।।5.66.6।।
explanation: "O noble Sugriva now when I see this excellent jewel, I get direct sight of my father and king of Videha (in the same way as I obtained the sight of Sita).

shloka_text: अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः। अस्याद्य दर्शने नाहं प्राप्तां तामिव चिन्तये।।5.66.7।।
explanation: "This jewel was shining on the head of my beloved. Now its mere look makes me feel that I am seeing her.

shloka_text: किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः। पिपासुमिव तोयेन सिञ्चन्ती वाक्यवारिणा।।5.66.8।।
explanation: "O handsome Hanuman Sita is like water for a thirsty person. Tell me again and again what Sita said to you. Sprinkle on me (lifegiving) water of her words in the form of message.

shloka_text: इतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदिमं वारिसम्भवम्। मणिं पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीमागतां विना।।5.66.9।।
explanation: "O Saumitri I see this jewel born (formed) under water but not her. What can be more sorrowful to me?

shloka_text: चिरं जीवति वैदेही यदि मासं धरिष्यति। क्षणं सौम्य न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणाम्।।5.66.10।।
explanation: (Addressing Hanuman again) "O dear, if she can live for a month it is living for long. I would not live for a moment without the black-eyed Vaidehi.

shloka_text: नय मामपि तं देशं यत्र दृष्टा मम प्रिया। न तिष्ठेयं क्षणमपि प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च।।5.66.11।।
explanation: "Take me to the place you saw my beloved. Knowing where she is I cannot stay here even for a moment.

shloka_text: कथं सा मम सुश्रोणी भीरुभीरु स्सती सदा। भयावहानां घोराणां मध्ये तिष्ठति रक्षसाम्।।5.66.12।।
explanation: "She is always very timid. How can my fairhipped beloved remain in the midst of dreadful and fearsome demons?

shloka_text: शारद स्तिमिरोन्मुक्तो नूनं चन्द्रं इवांबुधैः। आवृतं वदनं तस्या न विराजति राक्षसैः।।5.66.13।।
explanation: "Her face resembling the autumnal Moon bereft of its stain, though covered with rainclouds does not shine so bright.

shloka_text: किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयाद्य मे। एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा।।5.66.14।।
explanation: "O Hanuman Tell me now truly what has been told by her. I am eager to know. Indeed, it will keep me alive just as medicne does. (I shall survive on the strength of her message)

shloka_text: मधुरा मधुरालापा किमाह मम भामिनी। मद्विहीना वरारोहा हनुमन् कथयस्व मे।।5.66.15।।
explanation: That lovely Sita who speaks sweetly, that fairhipped beautiful one who has been separated from me, my beloved, what did she say? Please narrate. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtysixth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान् राघवेण महात्मना। सीताया भाषितं सर्वं न्यवेदयत राघवे।।5.67.1।।
explanation: Thus asked by Sri Rama, Hanuman repeated everything spoken by Sita to Rama.

shloka_text: इदमुक्तवती देवी जानकी पुरुषर्षभ। पूर्व वृत्तमभिज्ञानं चित्रकूटे यथातथम्।।5.67.2।।
explanation: "O bull among men queen Janaki related to me as a token of identification an incident  that had taken place at Chitrakuta in the past.

shloka_text: सुखसुप्ता त्वया सार्धं जानकी पूर्वमुत्थिता। वायस स्सहसोत्पत्य विददार स्तनान्तरे।।5.67.3।।
explanation: "When she was lying on your lap happily she awoke early and a crow came swiftly and scratched on her breast.

shloka_text: पर्यायेण च सुप्तस्त्वं देव्यङ्के भरताग्रज। पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथाम्।।5.67.4।।
explanation: "O Bharata's brother, when Sita awoke from sleep you slept on her lap. The same crow again hurt her.

shloka_text: पुनः पुनरुपागम्य विददार भृशं किल। ततस्त्वं बोधितस्तस्याश्शोणितेन समुक्षितः।।5.67.5।।
explanation: Again and again the crow came to her and scratched her. She woke you up as you were getting wet with blood shed from her body.

shloka_text: वायसेन च तेनैव सततं बाध्यमानया। बोधितः किल देव्या त्वं सुखसुप्तः परन्तप।।5.67.6।।
explanation: "O scorcher of enemies pained by the crow hurting her repeatedly, while you were sleeping happily, she woke you up and informed you about it.

shloka_text: तां तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो दारितां च स्तनान्तरे। आशीविष इव क्रुद्धो निश्वसन्नभ्यभाषथाः।।5.67.7।।
explanation: "Seeing the blood flowing from her breasts you became furious like a hissing serpent and said:

shloka_text: नखाग्रैः केन ते भीरु दारितं तु स्तनान्तरम्। कः क्रीडति सरोषेण पञ्चवक्त्रेण भोगिना।।5.67.8।।
explanation: "You are of timid nature. Who has scratched your breasts with the tip of the nail? Who is sporting with an enraged fivehooded serpent"?

shloka_text: निरीक्षमाणस्सहसा वायसं समवैक्षथाः। नखै स्सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम्।।5.67.9।।
explanation: 'Seeing all over, at once I glanced at the crow that stood in front of her with sharp bloodstained nails'.

shloka_text: सुतः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः। धरान्तरचरश्शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः।।5.67.10।।
explanation: 'That crow, the foremost of the birds was the son of Indra moving about all over the earth swiftly. His speed matched the Windgod's.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्मिन्महाबाहो कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः। वायसे त्वं कृथाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वर।।5.67.11।।
explanation: 'O longarmed, wise and revered Rama, then in anguish you took a cruel decision'.

shloka_text: स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण ह्ययोजयः। स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखः खगम्।।5.67.12।।
explanation: 'You took out a blade of grass from your mat and chanted the mantra to invoke the weapon of Brahma (Brahmastra) and hurled it on the crow. It blazed like the fire of the doom's day.

shloka_text: क्षिप्तवांस्त्वं प्रदीप्तं हि दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति। ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तस्स दर्भोऽनुजगाम ह।।5.67.13।।
explanation: 'You hurled the blazing blade of grass on to the crow. That burning blade of grass chased the crow.

shloka_text: स पित्रा च परित्यक्तस्सुरैश्च समहर्षिभिः। त्रीन् लोकान् सम्परिक्रम्य त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति।।5.67.14।।
explanation: 'He was abandoned by his father, even by great sages and gods. Then he went round the three worlds but could not find a saviour.

shloka_text: पुनरेवागतस्त्रस्तस्त्वत्सकाशमरिंदम। स तं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यश्शरणागतम्।।5.67.15।। वधार्हमपि काकुत्स्थ कृपया पर्यपालयः।
explanation: 'O destroyer of enemies the crow came back again to you trembling seeking protection from you and fell on the ground. Even though it deserved to be slayed, you saved him out of compassion.

shloka_text: मोघमस्त्रं न शक्यं तु कर्तुमित्येव राघव।।5.67.16।। भवांस्तस्याक्षि काकस्य हिनस्ति स्म स दक्षिणम्।
explanation: 'O Rama since a divine weapon cannot be withdrawn, it did strike his right eye'.

shloka_text: अथाहमुत्तरं देव्या पुनरुक्त स्ससम्भ्रमम्। तव स्नेहान्नरव्याघ्र सौहार्दादनुमान्य वै।।5.68.1।।
explanation: "O tiger among men In view of her regards for me and and her love for you she was confident and once again addressed me:

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधं वाच्यो रामो दाशरथिस्त्वया। यथा मामाप्नुयाच्छीघ्रं हत्वा रावणमाहवे।।5.68.2।।
explanation: 'You may appeal to Rama, the son of Dasaratha in many ways, that he should come quickly and slay Ravana in the battle and get me back.

shloka_text: यदि वा मन्यसे वीर वसैकाहमरिन्दम। कस्मिंश्चित्संवृते देशे विक्रान्तश्श्वो गमिष्यसि।।5.68.3।।
explanation: 'O crusher of enemies O brave Hanuman I wish you rest for a while in a secluded place around here and leave tomorrow .

shloka_text: मम चाप्यल्पभाग्यायास्सान्निध्यात्तव वीर्यवन्। अस्य शोकविपाकस्य मुहूर्तं स्याद्विमोक्षणम्।।5.68.4।।
explanation: 'O valiant (Hanuman) by your presence here, the less fortunate me, will be relieved of sorrow for a while.

shloka_text: गते हि त्वयि विक्रान्ते पुनरागमनाय वै। प्राणानामपि सन्देहो मम स्यान्नात्र संशयः।।5.68.5।।
explanation: 'O courageous tiger among monkeys when you depart (abruptly) I doubt if I would be alive by your return.

shloka_text: तवादर्शनजश्शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत्। दुःखाद्दुःखपराभूतां दुर्गतां दुःखभागिनीम्।।5.68.6।।
explanation: I am an unfortunate one, afflicted by sorrow and tormented (by demons). If I am not able to see you I will be lamenting in grief.

shloka_text: अयं च वीर सन्देहस्तिष्ठतीव ममाग्रतः। सुमहांस्त्वत्सहायेषु हर्यृक्षेषु हरीश्वर।।5.68.7।।
explanation: 'O brave vanaras I have great doubts about your assistants the vanaras and bears, crossing the ocean.

shloka_text: कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम्। तानि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानि तौ वा नरवरात्मजौ।।5.68.8।।
explanation: 'How will the vanaras and bears cross this great, impassable ocean? How will the princes Rama and Lakshmna be able to cross it?

shloka_text: त्रयाणामेव भूतानां सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने। शक्तिस्स्याद्वैनतेयस्य तव वा मारुतस्य वा।।5.68.9।।
explanation: 'Only three among all beings, Garuda, the Windgod and you have the capacity to cross the ocean.

shloka_text: तदस्मिन् कार्यनिर्योगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे। किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वरः।।5.68.10।।
explanation: 'O heroic Hanuman you know how to succeed. But I wish to know what expedient you have to accomplish which is difficult by all means. O foremost vanara, please tell me .

shloka_text: काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने। पर्याप्तः परवीरघ्न यशस्यस्ते बलोदयः।।5.68.11।।
explanation: 'O Slayer of enemy heroes you have the ability to accomplsh this task singlehanded. By succeeding in accomplishing the objective you will become renowned (and not Rama).

shloka_text: बलै स्समग्रैर्यदि मां हत्वा रावणमाहवे। विजयी स्वां पुरीं रामो नयेत्तत्स्याद्यशस्करम्।।5.68.12।।
explanation: 'When Rama slays Ravana and his entire army and takes me to his city after becoming victorious it will add glory to him.

shloka_text: यथाऽहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हृता। रक्षसा तद्भयादेव तथा नार्हति राघवः।।5.68.13।।
explanation: 'Tell valiant Rama not to take me back the way Ravana, the demon abducted me out of fear. Which is not right.

shloka_text: बलैस्तु सङ्कुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः। मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्।।5.68.14।।
explanation: 'If Rama, the slayer of the enemy army, could fill Lanka with his arrows and take me that will be a good sight for him to see.

shloka_text: तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः। भवेदाहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय।।5.68.15।।
explanation: 'You may make arrangement in such a way that the exalted hero Rama exhibits his might according to his stature'.

shloka_text: तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्। निशम्याहं तत श्शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रुवम्।।5.68.16।।
explanation: "Hearing the meaningful, courteous and reasonable words of Sita, I replied :

shloka_text: देवि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानामीश्वरः प्लवतां वरः। सुग्रीवस्सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्तवार्थे कृतनिश्चयः।।5.68.17।।
explanation: 'O queen The lord of the army of bears and vanaras who is the foremost among the monkeys is endowed with enough strength and has resolved to rescue you.

shloka_text: तस्य विक्रमसम्पन्नास्सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः। मन स्सङ्कल्पसम्पाता निदेशे हरयः स्थिताः।।5.68.18।।
explanation: 'Mighty, powerful and tough monkeys who have the speed of thought are under the command of Sugriva.

shloka_text: येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक्सज्जते गतिः। न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्स्वमिततेजसः।।5.68.19।।
explanation: 'All of them can go upward in the sky, downward into the underworld or obliquely in any direction without obstruction. They are brilliant enough to do any great task without any difficulty.

shloka_text: असकृत्तैर्महाभागैर्वानरैर्बलदर्पितैः। प्रदक्षिणीकृता भूमिर्वायुमार्गानुसारिभिः।।5.68.20।।
explanation: 'O great lady the mighty vanaras of extraordinary strength can fly with the wind and have  even circumambulated the earth.

shloka_text: मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्च सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः। मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसन्निधौ।।5.68.21।।
explanation: 'There are monkeys who are more powerful than me or equal to me. None are less strong than me or Sugriva.

shloka_text: अहं तावदिह प्राप्तः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः। न हि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेत्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः।।5.68.22।।
explanation: 'When I could come here, what to speak of the mightier monkeys?, People do not send the superior ones on errand, but send only the juniors.

shloka_text: तदलं परितापेन देवि मन्युर्व्यपैतु ते। एकोत्पातेन ते लङ्कामेष्यन्ति हरियूथपाः।।5.68.23।।
explanation: 'O noble lady give up your lamentation. Enough of sorrowing. The vanara army will fly and reach this place at one leap and fill it.

shloka_text: मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ। त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः।।5.68.24।।
explanation: 'O noble lady the lions among men, Rama and Lakshmana who resemble Sun and Moon will ascend on my back and reach here.

shloka_text: अरिघ्नं सिंहसङ्काशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्। लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्काद्वारमुपस्थितम्।।5.68.25।।
explanation: 'You will see the lionlike Rama, a slayer of enemies and Lakshmana wielding bow in hand standing at the entrance of Lanka very soon.

shloka_text: नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् वीरान् सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान्। वानरान्वारणोन्द्राभान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्षसि सङ्गतान्।।5.68.26।। शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु। नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामचिराच्छ्रोष्यसि स्वनम्।।5.68.27।।
explanation: 'You will hear before long the shouts of generals of the vanaras who resemble rainclouds on the mountain roaring like lions from the Malaya mountain of Lanka.

shloka_text: नखदंष्ट्रायुधान् वीरान् सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान्। वानरान्वारणोन्द्राभान् क्षिप्रं द्रक्षसि सङ्गतान्।।5.68.26।। शैलाम्बुदनिकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु। नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामचिराच्छ्रोष्यसि स्वनम्।।5.68.27।।
explanation: 'You will hear before long the shouts of generals of the vanaras who resemble rainclouds on the mountain roaring like lions from the Malaya mountain of Lanka.

shloka_text: निवृत्तवनवासं च त्वया सार्धमरिन्दमम्। अभिषिक्तमयोध्यायां क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्।।5.68.28।।
explanation: 'You will soon see Rama, the slayer of enemies crowned as king of Ayodhya with you, having duly completed the term of  exile in the forest'.

shloka_text: ततो मया वाग्भिरदीनभाषिणा शिवाभिरिष्टाभिरभिप्रसादिता। जगाम शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा तवापि शोकेन तदाभिपीडिता।।5.68.29।।
explanation: Sita though afflicted heard from me that you were also in excessive grief on account of separation from her and from my soothing, auspicious and welcome words, she derived comfort and remained quiet. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the sixtyeighth sarga of Sundarakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं यथावदभिभाषितम् । रामः प्रीतिसमायुक्तो वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत् ।।6.1.1।।
explanation: Having heard Hanuman's words, full of love, Rama replied.

shloka_text: कृतं हनुमता कार्यं सुमहद्भुवि दुर्लभम् । मनसापि यदन्येन न शक्यं धरणीतले ।।6.1.2।।
explanation: "Hanuman You have performed a mighty task indeed, which is difficult even to think of in this world and not possible for any one else on this earth."

shloka_text: न हि तं परिपश्यामि यस्तरेत महार्णवम् । अन्यत्र गरुडाद्वायोरन्यत्र च हनूमतः ।।6.1.3।।
explanation: "None else than Garuda or Vayu have I seen to have crossed this great ocean crossed by you, Hanuman."

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षाणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् । अप्रधृष्यां पुरीं लङ्कां रावणेन सुरक्षिताम् । प्रवष्ट स्सत्त्वमाश्रित्यश्वसन्को नाम निष्क्रमेत् ।।6.1.4।।
explanation: "Indeed, who has the strength to return alive after entering that city highly protected by Ravana. It is unimaginable even for devas, danavas, yakshas, gandharvas, uragas and rakshasas to cross."

shloka_text: को विशेत्सुदुराधर्षां राक्षसैश्च सुरक्षिताम् । यो वीर्यबलसम्पन्नो न समस्याद्धनूमतः ।।6.1.5।।
explanation: "Except for Hanuman, who is abounding in valour and strength, it is not possible for others to enter the inaccessible Lanka highly protected by rakshasas."

shloka_text: भृत्यकार्यं हनुमता सुग्रीवस्य कृतंमहत् । स्वयं विधाय स्वबलं सदृशं विक्रमस्य च ।।6.1.6।।
explanation: "Hanuman, with his mighty form and valour not only carried out a great task assigned by Sugriva but also what had to be done as duty."

shloka_text: यो हि भृत्यो नियुक्तस्सन्भर्त्रा कर्मणि दुष्करे । कुर्यात्तदनुरागेण तमाहुः पुरुषोत्तमम् ।।6.1.7।।
explanation: "He, who carries out  a formidable task entrusted to him by the master, with love is  said to be the best among men."

shloka_text: नियुक्तोय: परं कार्यं न कुर्यान्नृपतेः प्रियम् । भृत्योऽभृत्यस्समर्थोऽपि तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम् ।।6.1.8।।
explanation: An efficient servant does not only do what is asked but also does the work dear to the king. One who does not do so is said to be mediocre.

shloka_text: नियुक्तो नृपतेः  कार्यं न कुर्याद्यस्समाहितः । भृत्यो युक्तस्समर्थश्च तमाहुः पुरुषाधमम् ।।6.1.9।।
explanation: "If one who is capable and efficient has been entrusted with a task by a king and fails to do the work agreed to, is said to be a lowly person."

shloka_text: तन्नियोगे नियुक्तेन कृतं कृत्यं हनूमता । न चात्मा लघुतां नीतस्सुग्रीवश्चापि तोषितः ।।6.1.10।।
explanation: "Having done the task assigned to him, Hanuman carried out what had to be done and accomplished without difficulty. This made Sugriva also happy."

shloka_text: अहं च रघुवंशश्च लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः । वैदेह्या दर्शनेनाद्य धर्मतः परिरक्षिताः ।।6.1.11।।
explanation: "On Hanuman finding Vaidehi, I and, mighty Lakshmana and the whole of Raghu dynasty are now rightfully protected."

shloka_text: इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति । यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम् ।।6.1.12।।
explanation: "On the other hand, it is a pity that I am not able to please such a person who has spoken pleasing words. Further this causes grief to me."

shloka_text: एष सर्वस्वभूते परिष्वङ्गो हनूमतः । मया कालमिमं प्राप्य दत्तस्तस्य महात्मनः ।।6.1.13।।
explanation: "To such a great one who attained success at this time, everything can be given. I give my embrace."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा प्रीतिहृष्टाङ्गो रामस्तं परिषस्वजे । हनूमन्तं कृतात्मानं कृतकार्यमुपागतम् ।।6.1.14।।
explanation: Having said so, Rama experienced the joy of love all over his body and embraced Hanuman who returned successful.

shloka_text: ध्यात्वा पुनरुवाचेदं वचनं रघुनन्दनः । हरीणामीश्वरस्यापि सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः ।।6.1.15।।
explanation: Rama, the delight of Raghu dynasty thought over and said while Sugriva, the lord of monkeys was still listening.

shloka_text: सर्वथा सुकृतं तावत्सीतायाः परिमार्गणम् । सागरं तु समासाद्य पुनर्नष्टं मनो मम ।।6.1.16।।
explanation: "By all means good work was done in searching for Sita. On the contrary, having succeeded, my mind is once again agitated when I think of (crossing) the ocean."

shloka_text: कथं नाम समुद्रस्य दुष्पारस्य महाम्भसः । हरयो दक्षिणं पारं गमिष्यन्ति समागताः ।।6.1.17।।
explanation: "How will all the monkeys together be able to cross to the southern shore of the vast ocean? It is difficult to cross."

shloka_text: यद्यप्येष तु वृत्तान्तो वैदेह्या गदितो मम । समुद्रपारगमने हरीणां किमिहोत्तरम् ।।6.1.18।।
explanation: "This has been told to me by Vaidehi. How will the monkeys cross the ocean(enquired Vaidehi)."

shloka_text: इत्युक्तवा शोकसम्भ्रान्तो राम श्शत्रुनिबर्हणः । हनूमन्तं महाबाहुस्ततो ध्यानमुपागमत् ।।6.1.19।।
explanation: Agitated with sorrow, mighty armed Rama, the destroyer of enemies approached Hanuman and reflected (about the crossing of the ocean). इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे प्रथमस्सर्गः This is the end of the first Sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तंतुशोकपरिद्यूनंरामंदशरथात्मजम् । उवाचवचनंश्रीमान् सुग्रीवश्शोकनाशनम् ।।6.2.1।।
explanation: Glorious Sugriva spoke such words of advice to remove the agony of Rama,son of Dasaratha, who was filled with sorrow.

shloka_text: किंत्वंसन्तप्यसेवीर  यथान्यःप्राकृतस्तथा । मैवंभूस्त्यजसन्तापंकृतघ्नइवसौहृदम् ।।6.2.2।।
explanation: "Heroic Rama Why are you grieving like a common man? Give up your grief just like an ungrateful one gives up friendship."

shloka_text: सन्तापस्यचतेस्थानंनहिपश्यामिराघव । प्रवृत्तावुपलब्धायांज्ञातेचनिलयेरिपोः ।।6.2.3।।
explanation: "Raghava Having secured the information (of Sita) and known the location of the enemy's residence, I do not see the reason for your mourning."

shloka_text: मतिमान्शास्त्रवित्प्राज्ञःपण्डितश्चासिराघव । त्यजेमांपापिकांबुद्धिंकृतात्मेवार्थदूषणीम् ।।6.2.4।।
explanation: "Raghava You are an intellectual, well versed in Sastras, wise and learned. Give up this sinful thought just as the one who is efficient gives up the one who violates subtle truth."

shloka_text: समुद्रंलङ्घयित्वातुमहानक्रसमाकुलम् । लङ्कामारोहयिष्यामोहनिष्यामश्चतेरिपुम् ।।6.2.5।।
explanation: "If we cross over that ocean infested with huge crocodiles and ascend the fortress of Lanka, know that the enemy is killed."

shloka_text: निरुत्साहस्यदीनस्यशोकपर्याकुलात्मनः । सर्वार्थाव्यवसीदन्तिव्यसनंचाधिगच्छति ।।6.2.6।।
explanation: "One who is despondent, dejected and overwhelmed with grief, will be dispirited in all matters. Not only that with worry he will meet with disaster."

shloka_text: इमेशूरास्समर्थाश्चसर्वनोहरियूथपाः । त्वत्प्रियार्थंकृतोत्साहाःप्रवेष्टुमपिपावकम् । एषांहर्षेणजानामितर्कश्चास्मिन् दृढोमम ।।6.2.7।।
explanation: All these vanara leaders and heroes are highly capable and for your happiness they are even ready to enter fire. I know this from their joy and I even infer that it is certain (to happen).

shloka_text: विक्रमेणसमानेष्येसीतांहत्वायथारिपुम् । रावणंपापकर्माणंतथात्वंकर्तुमर्हसि ।।6.2.8।।
explanation: "You ought to work such that we would kill that enemy Ravana of sinful deeds with our prowess and get back  Sita. I hope you are capable of doing that."

shloka_text: सेतुरत्रयथाबध्येद्यथापश्येमतांपुरीम् । तस्यराक्षसराजस्यतथात्वंकुरुराघव ।।6.2.9।।
explanation: "Raghava You think that we will be building a bridge and then seeing that city of the king of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: दृष्टवातांतुपुरींलङ्कांत्रिकूटशिखरेस्थिताम् । हतंचरावणंयुद्धेदर्शनावधारय ।।6.2.10।।
explanation: "If the city of Lanka situated on top of Trikuta mountain is seen, you can be sure that Ravana is killed."

shloka_text: अबध्वासागरेसेतुंघोरेचतुवरुणालये । लङ्कांनमर्दितुंशक्यासेन्द्रैरपिसुरासुरैः ।।6.2.11।।
explanation: "Without building a bridge on that dreadful ocean, the abode of Varuna, it is not possible for suras or asuras accompanied by Indra also to crush Lanka."

shloka_text: सेतुर्बद्धस्समुद्रेचयावल्लङ्कास्समीपतः ।।6.2.12।। सर्वंतीर्णंचमेसैन्यंजितमित्युपधारय । इमेहिसमरेवीराहरयःकामरूपिण ।।6.2.13।।
explanation: "On building a bridge over the large ocean up to Lanka, when all my army of vanaras can cross over, you may consider that you have won. These vanaras are heroic in war and can assume any form at will."

shloka_text: सेतुर्बद्धस्समुद्रेचयावल्लङ्कास्समीपतः ।।6.2.12।। सर्वंतीर्णंचमेसैन्यंजितमित्युपधारय । इमेहिसमरेवीराहरयःकामरूपिण ।।6.2.13।।
explanation: "On building a bridge over the large ocean up to Lanka, when all my army of vanaras can cross over, you may consider that you have won. These vanaras are heroic in war and can assume any form at will."

shloka_text: तदलंविक्लबांबुद्धिम् राजन  सर्वार्थनाशनीम् । पुरुषस्यहिलोकेऽस्मिन् शोकश्शौर्यापकर्षणः ।।6.2.14।।
explanation: "O king, therefore enough of this agitated feeling which destroys everything. In this world the valiance of man is lost if he is sorrowful."

shloka_text: यत्तुकार्यंमनुष्येणशौण्डीर्यमवलम्बता । अस्मिन् कालेमहाप्राज्ञसत्त्वमातिष्ठतेजसा ।।6.2.15।।
explanation: "Just as heroism follows a human being in this world on accomplishing a task, you who are very wise, should resort to courage and valour and rise up."

shloka_text: शूराणांहिमनुष्याणांत्वद्विधानांमहात्मनाम् । विनष्टेवाप्रणष्टेवाशोकस्सर्वार्थनाशनः ।।6.2.16।।
explanation: "If you who are great among the valiant ones worry for that which is destroyed or lost, it would lead to disaster of everything."

shloka_text: तत्त्वंबुद्धिमतांश्रेष्ठस्सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदः । मद्विधैस्सचिवैस्सार्थमरिंजेतुमिहार्हसि ।।6.2.17।।
explanation: "You are highly intelligent, foremost among those who are wellversed in the meaning of all shastras. You will conquer your enemy along with friends like me."

shloka_text: नहिपश्याम्यहंकंचित् त्रिषुलोकेषुराघव । गृहीतधनुषेयस्तेतिष्ठेदभिमुखोरणे ।।6.2.18।।
explanation: "O Raghava When you hold the bow in war, Indeed  who can stand in front of you in the three worlds. I have not seen."

shloka_text: वानरेषुसमासक्तंनतेकार्यंविपत्स्यते । अचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसेसीतांतीर्त्वासागरमक्ष्यम् ।।6.2.19।।
explanation: "The task of yours entrusted to vanaras will never be spoiled. Very soon you will see Sita crossing over the ocean that cannot be subdued."

shloka_text: तदलंशोकमालम्ब्यक्रोधमालम्बभूपते । निश्चेष्टाःक्षत्रियामन्दास्सर्वेचण्डस्यबिभ्यति ।।6.2.20।।
explanation: "O Lord of earth Enough of that pain you have experienced. Give up sorrow and take on to anger. When kshatriyas are lethargic, they become dull but all are scared at a fearful one."

shloka_text: लङ्घनार्थंचघोरस्यसमुद्रस्यनदींपतेः । सहास्माभिरिहोपेतस्सूक्ष्मबुद्धिर्विचारय ।।6.2.21।।
explanation: "You are endowed with subtle intellect and now think of the means to cross over this dreadful looking ocean the lord of rivers."

shloka_text: लङ्घितेतस्यतैस्सैन्यंजितमित्युपधारय । सर्वंतीर्णंचमेसैन्यंजितमित्यवधार्यताम् ।।6.2.22।।
explanation: "If the vanara army can cross (the ocean) you are certain that we will conquer. Presume that the army has succeeded."

shloka_text: इमेहिहरयश्शूरास्समरेकामरूपिणः । तानरीन्विधमिष्यन्तिशिलापादपवृष्टिभिः ।।6.2.23।।
explanation: "Being heroic in combat, these vanaras can take any form at their will.They would rain boulders and trees on enemies and cut them to size."

shloka_text: कथञ्चित्सन्तरिष्यामस्तेवयंवरुणालयम् । हतमित्येवतंमन्येयुद्धेशत्रुनिबर्हण ।।6.2.24।।
explanation: "O Exterminator of foes By whatever means the ocean is crossed by us, think that the enemy has been killed in combat."

shloka_text: किमुक्त्वाबहुधाचापिसर्वथाविजयीभवान् । निमित्तानिचपश्यामिमनोमेसम्प्रहृष्यति ।।6.2.25।।
explanation: "Of what use is speaking many words. By all means you will be victorious. I see signs of it and feel highly delighted in my mind." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेद्वितीयस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the second Sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic,the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाहेतुमत्परमार्थवत् । प्रतिजग्राहकाकुत्स्थोहनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत् ।।6.3.1।।
explanation: Rama the scion of Kakuthsa dynasty having accepted the wellmeaning words of Sugriva, who spoke the truth with deep understanding, turned to Hanuman and said.

shloka_text: तपसासेतुबन्धेनसागरोच्छोषणेनच । सर्वथासुसमर्थोऽस्मिसागरस्यास्यलङ्घने ।।6.3.2।।
explanation: "By austerity or by drying up the ocean or by any other means, I am capable of crossing the ocean."

shloka_text: कतिदुर्गाणिदुर्गायालङ्कायाब्रूहितानिमे । ज्ञातुमिच्छामितत्सर्वंदर्शनादिववानर ।।6.3.3।।
explanation: "O Vanara How many forts are in Lanka? You may tell me whatever you have seen. I wish to know all that."

shloka_text: बलस्यपरिमाणंचद्वारदुर्गक्रियामपि । गुप्तिकर्मचलङ्कायारक्षसांसदनानिच ।।6.3.4।। यथासुखंयथावच्छलङ्कायामसिदृष्टवान् । सर्वमाचक्ष्वतत्त्वेनसर्वथाकुशलोह्यसि ।।6.3.5।।
explanation: "Tell me in detail about the strength and size of the army, the number of gateways that are difficult to enter, the way in which the entrances have been protected by the rakshasas, and their dwellings in Lanka. Indeed you are aware of all aspects and are also capable."

shloka_text: बलस्यपरिमाणंचद्वारदुर्गक्रियामपि । गुप्तिकर्मचलङ्कायारक्षसांसदनानिच ।।6.3.4।। यथासुखंयथावच्छलङ्कायामसिदृष्टवान् । सर्वमाचक्ष्वतत्त्वेनसर्वथाकुशलोह्यसि ।।6.3.5।।
explanation: "Tell me in detail about the strength and size of the army, the number of gateways that are difficult to enter, the way in which the entrances have been protected by the rakshasas, and their dwellings in Lanka. Indeed you are aware of all aspects and are also capable."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वारामस्यवचनंहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । वाक्यंवाक्यविदांश्रेष्ठोरामंपुनरथाब्रवीत् ।।6.3.6।।
explanation: Hanuman the son of Maruti, the foremost among those who are good at speech, having heard Rama's words again said to Rama.

shloka_text: श्रूयतांसर्वमाख्यास्येदुर्गकर्मविधानतः । गुप्तापुरीयथालङ्कारक्षिताचयथाबलैः ।।6.3.7।।
explanation: "I will relate the way in which the city of Lanka is fortified, the way in which it is protected by secret forces, everything you wish to hear."

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्चयथास्निग्धारावणस्यचतेजसा । परांसमृद्धिंलङ्कायास्सागरस्यचभीमताम् ।।6.3.8।। विभागंचबलौघस्यनिर्देशंवाहनस्यच । एवमुक्त्वाकपिश्रेष्ठःकथयामासतत्त्ववित: ।।6.3.9।।
explanation: Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras said that he will truly point out everything in Lanka:"Ravana's power, the affection of rakshasas to Ravana, his prosperity, the terrifying ocean, the divisions of the army such as chariots, elephants, horses and soldiers."

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्चयथास्निग्धारावणस्यचतेजसा । परांसमृद्धिंलङ्कायास्सागरस्यचभीमताम् ।।6.3.8।। विभागंचबलौघस्यनिर्देशंवाहनस्यच । एवमुक्त्वाकपिश्रेष्ठःकथयामासतत्त्ववित: ।।6.3.9।।
explanation: Hanuman, the foremost of the vanaras said that he will truly point out everything in Lanka:"Ravana's power, the affection of rakshasas to Ravana, his prosperity, the terrifying ocean, the divisions of the army such as chariots, elephants, horses and soldiers."

shloka_text: हृष्टप्रमुदितालङ्कामत्तद्विपसमाकुला । महतीरथसंपूर्णारक्षोगणसमाकुला ।।6.3.10।।
explanation: "The people in the vast island of Lanka are very delighted. Lanka is filled with chariots and innumerable rakshasas."

shloka_text: दृढबद्धकवाटानिमहापरिघवन्तिच । द्वाराणिविपुलान्यस्याश्चत्वारिसुमहान्तिच ।।6.3.11।।
explanation: "Lanka is endowed with lofty wide courtyards, entrances with doors that are fixed with metal fixtures and large iron bars."

shloka_text: तत्रेषूपलयन्त्राणिबलवन्तिमहान्तिच । आगतंपरसैन्यंतैस्तत्रप्रतिनिवार्यते ।।6.3.12।।
explanation: "The doors are fitted with powerful machines which retaliate by discharging darts and stones on the enemy's army and kill them."

shloka_text: द्वारेषुसंस्कृताभीमाःकालायसमयाश्शिताः । शतशोरचितावीरैश्शतघ्नयोरक्षसांगणै ।।6.3.13।।
explanation: At the entrances are troops of terrific looking guards kept ready with a hundred sharpened stones studded with iron spikes.

shloka_text: सौवर्णस्तुमहांस्तस्याःप्राकारोदुष्प्रधर्षणः । मणीविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्ताविरचितान्तरः ।।6.3.14।।
explanation: "Its lofty golden boundary wall encrusted here and there with gems, corals, Vaiduryas and pearls is difficult to assail."

shloka_text: सर्वतश्चमहाभीमाश्शीततोयवहाश्शुभाः । अगाधाग्राहवत्यश्चपरिखामीनसेविता ।।6.3.15।।
explanation: All round it (boundary wall) are very splendid moats filled with frighteningcold water inhabited by fish and crocodiles.

shloka_text: द्वारेषुतासांचत्वारस्सङ्क्रमाःपरमायताः । यन्त्रैरुपेताबहुभिर्महद्भिर्गृहपङ्क्तिभिः ।।6.3.16।।
explanation: At the entrance of the gateways around the moats are four road ways. Huge engines are fixed to move the bridges when people approach. There are rows of houses (for the guards) at the gateways.

shloka_text: त्रायन्तेसङ्क्रमास्तत्रपरसैन्यागतेसति । यन्त्रैस्तैरवकीर्यन्तेपरिखासुसमन्ततः ।।6.3.17।।
explanation: "When the enemy arrives, the engines all over the moats lift the bridges making entry impossible for enemy armies."

shloka_text: एकस्त्वकम्प्योबलवान्सङ्क्रमस्सुमहादृढः । काञ्चनै र्बहुभिस्स्तम्भैर्वेदिकाभिश्चशोभितः ।।6.3.18।।
explanation: "One of the road ways is very strong and steady, shining with unshakeable golden pillars and altars."

shloka_text: स्वयंप्रकृतिमापन्नोयुयुत्सूराम  रावण: । उत्थितश्चाप्रमत्तश्चबलानामनुदर्शने ।।6.3.19।।
explanation: "O Rama Ravana, who is hostile in his intentions, assuming his natural tendency which is eagerness to combat, is always very alert and looks after the army."

shloka_text: लङ्कापुनर्निरालम्बादेवदुर्गाभयावहा । नादेयंपार्वतंवान्यंकृत्रिमंचचतुर्विधम् ।।6.3.20।।
explanation: "Lanka is difficult to access even for devatas located on high peaks of the mountain. It is fierce to onlookers, surrounded by four kinds of forts, like rivers, mountains, forests and artificial fortresses."

shloka_text: स्थितापारेसमुद्रस्यदूरपारस्यराघव  । नौपथोपिश्चनास्त्यत्रनिरादेशश्चसर्वशः ।।6.3.21।।
explanation: "O Raghava Lanka is located on the other shore of the ocean. Passage through the sea is not possible. It is away from all and there is nothing around."

shloka_text: शैलाग्रेरचितादुर्गासापुरैर्देवपुरोपमा । वाजिवारणासम्पूर्णालङ्कापरमदुर्जया ।।6.3.22।।
explanation: "It is inaccessible like the abode of devatas as it is on the peak of the mountain. It is difficult to conquer for any one as it is full of horses and elephants."

shloka_text: परिखाश्चशतघ्नयश्चयन्त्राणिविविधानिच । शोभयन्तिपुरींलङ्कांरावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।।6.3.23।।
explanation: "Evil minded Ravana's city of Lanka is shining with moats and missiles of many kinds and machinery."

shloka_text: अयुतंरक्षसामत्रपूर्वद्वारंसमाश्रितम् । शूलहस्तादुराधर्षास्सर्वेखङ्गाग्रयोधिनः ।।6.3.24।।
explanation: "There(in Lanka) ten thousand warriors are garrisoned at the eastern gate way holding tridents, and those who are unassailable in war stand in front with swords."

shloka_text: नियुतंरक्षसामत्रदक्षिणद्वारमाश्रितम् । चतुरङ्गेणसैन्येनयोधास्तत्राप्यनुत्तमाः ।।6.3.25।।
explanation: At the southern gate also one lakh of rakshasas are garrisoned with four divisions of army. They are also the best warriors.

shloka_text: प्रयुतंरक्षसामत्रपश्चिमद्वारमाश्रितम् । चर्मखङ्गधरास्सर्वेतथासर्वास्त्रकोविदाः ।।6.3.26।।
explanation: At the western gate are garrisoned ten lakhs of rakshasas wearing shields of skin and holding swords. They are knowledgeable in several weapons.

shloka_text: न्यर्बुदंरक्षसामत्राप्युत्तरद्वारमाश्रितम् । रथिनश्चाश्ववाहाश्चकुलपुत्त्रास्सुपूजिताः ।।6.3.27।।
explanation: At the northern gate(of Lanka) are garrisoned one hundred crores of rakshasas constituting, charioteers, horse riding and elephant riding ogres born of noble families, respected and trustworthy (for Ravana).

shloka_text: शतशोऽथसहस्राणिमध्यमंस्कन्धमाश्रिताः । यातुधानादुराधर्षास्साग्रकोटिश्चरक्षसाम् ।।6.3.28।।
explanation: "Hundreds and thousands of warriors who are unassailable are collected in the center(of Lanka) in multitudes of crores."

shloka_text: तेमयासङ्क्रमाभग्नाःपरिखाश्चावपूरिताः । दग्धाचनगरीलङ्काप्राकाराश्चावसादिताः ।।6.3.29।। बलैकदेशःक्षपितोराक्षसानांमहात्मनाम् ।
explanation: "I have destroyed some of those roadways, even filled up the moats, burnt parts of the city of Lanka, smashed the boundary walls and killed part of the powerful army."

shloka_text: येनकेनतुमार्गेणतरामवरुणालयम् । हतेतिनगरीलङ्कावानरैरवधार्यताम् ।।6.3.30 ।।
explanation: "If by whatever means the passage of ocean can be crossed by vanaras it can be taken for granted that the city of Lanka is destroyed."

shloka_text: अङ्गदोद्विविदोमैन्दोजाम्बवान्पनसोऽनलः । नीलस्सेनापतिश्चेवबलशेषेणकिंतव ।।6.3.31।। प्लवमानाहिगत्वातांरावणस्यमहापुरीम् ।।6.3.32।। सपर्वतवनांभित्त्वासखातांचसप्रतोरणाम् । सप्राकारांसभवनामानयिष्यन्तिराघव ।।6.3.33।।
explanation: "Raghava What do we have to do with the rest of the army when Angada, Dwivida, Mainda, Jambavan, Panasa, Nala and the chief of the army Nila are there? Reaching Ravana's city by leaping over the mountains and demolishing the outer gates, other boundaries, archways and other buildings they will get into Lanka city."

shloka_text: अङ्गदोद्विविदोमैन्दोजाम्बवान्पनसोऽनलः । नीलस्सेनापतिश्चेवबलशेषेणकिंतव ।।6.3.31।। प्लवमानाहिगत्वातांरावणस्यमहापुरीम् ।।6.3.32।। सपर्वतवनांभित्त्वासखातांचसप्रतोरणाम् । सप्राकारांसभवनामानयिष्यन्तिराघव ।।6.3.33।।
explanation: "Raghava What do we have to do with the rest of the army when Angada, Dwivida, Mainda, Jambavan, Panasa, Nala and the chief of the army Nila are there? Reaching Ravana's city by leaping over the mountains and demolishing the outer gates, other boundaries, archways and other buildings they will get into Lanka city."

shloka_text: अङ्गदोद्विविदोमैन्दोजाम्बवान्पनसोऽनलः । नीलस्सेनापतिश्चेवबलशेषेणकिंतव ।।6.3.31।। प्लवमानाहिगत्वातांरावणस्यमहापुरीम् ।।6.3.32।। सपर्वतवनांभित्त्वासखातांचसप्रतोरणाम् । सप्राकारांसभवनामानयिष्यन्तिराघव ।।6.3.33।।
explanation: "Raghava What do we have to do with the rest of the army when Angada, Dwivida, Mainda, Jambavan, Panasa, Nala and the chief of the army Nila are there? Reaching Ravana's city by leaping over the mountains and demolishing the outer gates, other boundaries, archways and other buildings they will get into Lanka city."

shloka_text: एवमाज्ञापयक्षिप्रंबलानांसर्वसङ्ग्रहम् । मुहूर्तेनतुयुक्तेनप्रस्थानमभिरोचय ।।6.3.34।।
explanation: "You may command the total army this way."Quickly start at an opportune time towards Lanka (said Hanuman to Rama)" commanded Hanuman." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेतृतीयस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the third Sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यं यथावदनुपूर्वशः । ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामस्सत्यपराक्रमः ।।6.4.1।।
explanation: Glorious Rama, of truthful valour, having heard Hanuman in the aforesaid manner, there after spoke (to Hanuman).

shloka_text: यां निवेदयसे लङ्कां पुरीं भीमस्य रक्षसः । क्षिप्रमेनां मथिष्यामि सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ।।6.4.2।।
explanation: I will destroy immediately that Lanka of fierce rakshasa, you are telling. I am telling you, this is the truth.

shloka_text: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव  प्रयाणमभिरोचये । युक्तो मुहूर्तो विजयः प्राप्तो मध्यं दिवाकर ।।6.4.3।।
explanation: I desire to journey at this opportune time. The Sun has reached the mid position and so a good time for victory.

shloka_text: सीतां हृत्वा तु मे जातु क्वासौ यास्यति यास्यत: । सीता श्रुत्वाभियानं मे अशामेष्यति जीविते । जीवितान्तेऽ मृतं स्पृष्टवा पीत्वा विषमिवातुरः ।।6.4.4।।
explanation: Where can the one who has abducted Sita go from here? Just as one who has drunk the poison gets some life sometimes on tasting the nectar of immortality, Sita will attain the desire to live on hearing about my approaching.

shloka_text: उत्तरा फल्गुनी ह्यद्य श्वस्तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यते । अभिप्रायाम सुग्रीव  सर्वानीकसमावृताः ।।6.4.5।।
explanation: Today Uttaraphalguni constellation is on the ascent and for me born in Punarvasu star, Hasta, will be in conjunction with the moon. Sugriva You may assemble all the army as I desire to start the journey (as it is auspicious for me).

shloka_text: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति च । निहत्य रावणं सीतामानयिष्यामि जानकीम् ।।6.4.6।।
explanation: I also see manifestations of good omens to start (the journey). I shall get Janaka's daughter Sita on killing Ravana.

shloka_text: उपरिष्टाद्धि नयनं स्फुरमाणमिदं मम । विजयं समनुप्राप्तं शंसतीव मनोरथम् ।।6.4.7।।
explanation: My upper eyelids are twitching thus indicating victory and it strikes me that my desire will be fulfilled.

shloka_text: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः । उवाच रामो धर्मात्मा पुनरप्यर्धकोविदः ।।6.4.8।।
explanation: There after righteous Rama who is well respected by the king of vanaras and also by Lakshmana, who is wellversed in polity once again spoke.

shloka_text: अग्रे यातु बलस्यास्य नीलो मार्गमवेक्षितुम् । वृतश्शतसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम् ।।6.4.9।।
explanation: "Let Nila go leading in front with his courageous and hundred thousand army looking at the way (said Rama)".

shloka_text: फलमूलवता नील  शीतकाननवारिणा । पथा मधुमता चाशु सेनां सेनापते  नय ।।6.4.10।।
explanation: "O Nila, the chief of the army Go fast with the army along the way which has plenty of fruits and roots, shady forests and cool water and sweet smelling honey".

shloka_text: दूषयेयुर्दुरात्मनः पथि मूलफलोदकम् । राक्षसाः परिरक्षेथास्तेभ्यस्त्वं नित्यमुद्यतः ।।6.4.11।।
explanation: "Evilminded one, the lord of rakshasas will spoil the roots, fruits and water (on the way). Be ever alert and protect them".

shloka_text: निम्नेषु वनदुर्गेषु वनेषु च वनौकसः । अभिप्लुत्याभिपश्येयुः परेषां निहितं बलम् ।।6.4.12।।
