explanation: "O Vanaras You should even look for (the rakshasas) in the low lying lands, in inaccessible water sources, in forests and also beyond sight leaping up to the sky".

shloka_text: यच्च फल्गु बलं किञ्चित्त दत्रैवोपपद्यताम् । एतद्धि कृत्यं घोरं नो विक्रमेण प्रयुज्यताम् ।।6.4.13।।
explanation: "If there are any weak ones in the army, they may be used here for this purpose (of looking for fruits etc.). Our task (ahead) is a terrific one and be prepared to overcome your power".

shloka_text: सागरौघनिभं भीममग्रानीकं महाबलाः । कपिसिंहाः प्रकर्षस्तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ।।6.4.14।।
explanation: "These hundreds and thousands of lionlike vanaras would walk in groups leading the army like the fierce tides of the ocean".

shloka_text: गजश्च गिरिसङ्काशो गवयश्च महाबलः । गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यातु गवां दृप्तइवर्षभ: ।।6.4.15।।
explanation: "Gaja who is like a mountain in form, Gavaya, the mighty strong and Gavaksha would go like proud bulls that lead the cows".

shloka_text: यातु वानरवाहिन्या वानरः प्लवतां वरः । पालयन्दक्षिणं पार्श्वमृषभो वानरर्षभः ।।6.4.16।।
explanation: "Let the vanara called Rshaba the foremost among the leaping vanaras, take charge of the right side of the army".

shloka_text: गन्धहस्तीव दुर्धर्षस्तरस्वी गन्धमादनः । यातु वानरवाहिन्या स्सव्यं पार्श्वमधिष्ठितः ।।6.4.17।।
explanation: "Let Gandhamadana, the unassailable and powerful vanara resembling the elephant in rut take charge of the left portion of the army".

shloka_text: यास्यामि बलमध्येऽहं बलौघमभिहर्षयन् । अधिरुह्य हनूमन्त मैरावत मिवेश्वरः ।।6.4.18।।
explanation: "Like the lord of gods riding on Iravatam I would mount on Hanuman and reach the centre of the army encouraging the army."

shloka_text: अङ्गदेनैष संयातु लक्ष्मणश्चान्त कोपमः । सार्वभौमेन भूतेशो द्रविणाधिपतिर्यथा ।।6.4.19।।
explanation: "Let Lakshmana who is like Anthaka (one who excels death) ride on Angada, like the lord of wealth (Kubera) rides on the elephant Saarvabhauma (the elephant that guards the four quarters)".

shloka_text: जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः । ऋक्षराजो महासत्त्वः कुक्षिं रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः ।।6.4.20।।
explanation: "Let Rksharaja the mighty strong Jambavan and Sushena even Vegadarsi protect the rear side (of the army)".

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः । व्यादिदेश महावीर्यो वानरान्वानरर्षभ ः ।।6.4.21।।
explanation: Sugriva the bull among vanaras having heard the words of Raghava ordered the heroic vanaras (to start).

shloka_text: ते वानरगणास्सर्वे समुत्पत्य युयुत्सवः । गुहाभ्यश्शिखरेभ्यश्च अशु पुप्लुविरे तदा ।।6.4.22।।
explanation: Then all the heroic monkeys who were eager for combat jumped down from the caves, mountain peaks and trees.

shloka_text: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन च पूजितः । जगाम रामोधर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम् ।।6.4.23 ।।
explanation: Thereafter righteous Rama who was worshipped by the king of vanaras and Lakshmana went towards the southern direction.

shloka_text: शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्चायुतैरपि । वारणाभैश्च हरिभिर्ययौ परिवृतस्तदा ।।6.4.24।।
explanation: Protected by hundreds and thousands, even crores of vanaras and surrounded by a myriad of vanaras Rama went.

shloka_text: तं यान्तमनुयान्ती सा महती हरिवाहिनी । दृप्ता: प्रमुदितास्सर्वे सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः ।।6.4.25।।
explanation: While Rama was walking the great army of vanaras controlled by Sugriva followed him with great delight.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवङ्गमाः । क्षेवळन्तो निनदन्तस्ते जग्मुर्वै दक्षिणां दिशम् ।।6.4.26।।
explanation: The monkeys went towards southern direction playing, leaping, running and roaring like lions.

shloka_text: भक्ष्यन्त स्सुगन्धीनि मधूनि च फलानि च । उद्वहन्तो महावृक्षान् मञ्जरीपुञ्जधारिणः ।।6.4.27।।
explanation: The monkeys went eating sweet smelling honey and fruits and carrying branches of huge trees having bunches of blossoms.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं सहसा दृप्ता निर्वहान्ति क्षिपन्ति च । पतन्तश्पोत्पत्नत्यन्ये पातयन्त्यपरे परान् ।।6.4.28।।
explanation: Some wild monkeys carried one another, while some fell, knocked down others, some lifted up and some turned their back and pushed down others.

shloka_text: रावणो नो निहन्तव्यस्सर्वे च रजनीचराः । इति गर्जन्ति हरयो राघवस्य समीपतः ।।6.4.29।।
explanation: 'We should kill all the rakshasas and Ravana', saying so the vanaras close by Rama were roaring.

shloka_text: पुरस्तादृषभो वीरो नील: कुमुद एव च । पन्थानं शोधयन्तिस्म वानरैर्बहुभि स्सह ।।6.4.30।।
explanation: Heroic Rshaba, Nila and even Kumuda together with many vanaras were searching on the way.

shloka_text: मध्ये तु राजा सुग्रीवो रामो लक्ष्मण एव च । बलभिर्बहुभि र्भीमैर्वृताश्शत्रुनिबर्हणाः ।।6.4.31।।
explanation: Sugriva, Rama and Lakshmana marched in the middle surrounded by powerful and fierce vanaras who can destroy the enemy.

shloka_text: हरिश्शतवलिर्वीरः कोटीभिर्दशभिर्वृतः । सर्वामेको ह्यावष्टभ्य ररक्ष हरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.4.32।।
explanation: Sathavali alone encircled by hundred crore vanara heroes was protecting the army of vanaras.

shloka_text: कोटीशतपरीवारः केसरी पनसो गजः । अर्कश्चातिबल: पार्श्वमेकं तस्याभिरक्षति ।।6.4.33।।
explanation: Kesari, Panasa, Gaja, Atibala, Arka and their army of one hundred crores were protecting the army on one side.

shloka_text: सुषेणो जाम्बवांश्चैव ऋक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतौ । सुग्रीवं पुरतः कृत्वा जघनं सम्ररक्षतुः ।।6.4.34।।
explanation: Sushena, and Jambavan surrounded by the army of Rshaba were guarding by placing on the western side.

shloka_text: तेषां सेनापतिर्वीरो नीलो वानरपुङ्गवः । सम्पतन्पततां श्रेष्ठस्तद्बलं पर्यपालयात् ।।6.4.35।।
explanation: Nila, the heroic chief of the army who was foremost in the act of flying and descending was going around and controlling.

shloka_text: दरीमुखः प्रजङ्घश्च रम्भोऽथ रभसः कपिः । सर्वतश्च ययुर्वीरास्त्वरयन्तः प्लवङ्गमान् ।।6.4.36।।
explanation: Valiant Darimukha, Prajhanga, Rambha and Rabhasa went about jumping cheering all vanaras.

shloka_text: एवं ते हरिशार्दूला गच्छन्तो बलदर्पिताः । अपश्यंस्ते गिरिश्रेष्ठं सह्यं द्रुमालतायुतम् ।।6.4.37।। सरांसि च सुपुल्लानि तटाकानि वनानि च ।।6.4.38।।
explanation: Those vanaras who were tigers among vanaras, proud of their might went to see (on their way) the Sahya Mountains, the foremost of the mountains with trees and creepers, lakes and ponds with fully blossomed lotuses.

shloka_text: एवं ते हरिशार्दूला गच्छन्तो बलदर्पिताः । अपश्यंस्ते गिरिश्रेष्ठं सह्यं द्रुमालतायुतम् ।।6.4.37।। सरांसि च सुपुल्लानि तटाकानि वनानि च ।।6.4.38।।
explanation: Those vanaras who were tigers among vanaras, proud of their might went to see (on their way) the Sahya Mountains, the foremost of the mountains with trees and creepers, lakes and ponds with fully blossomed lotuses.

shloka_text: रामस्य शासनं ज्ञात्वा भीमकोपस्य भीतवत् । वर्जयन्नगराभ्याशां स्तथा जनपदानपि ।।6.4.39।। सागरौघनिभं भीमं तद्वानरबलं महत् । उत्ससर्प महाघोषं भीमघोषमिवार्णव: ।।6.4.40।।
explanation: The dreadful vanara army expansive as the ocean went knowing about the fear of Rama's wrath. They went avoiding parts of cities and villages making frightening sounds like the great sound of the waves of the ocean.

shloka_text: रामस्य शासनं ज्ञात्वा भीमकोपस्य भीतवत् । वर्जयन्नगराभ्याशां स्तथा जनपदानपि ।।6.4.39।। सागरौघनिभं भीमं तद्वानरबलं महत् । उत्ससर्प महाघोषं भीमघोषमिवार्णव: ।।6.4.40।।
explanation: The dreadful vanara army expansive as the ocean went knowing about the fear of Rama's wrath. They went avoiding parts of cities and villages making frightening sounds like the great sound of the waves of the ocean.

shloka_text: तस्यदाशरथे: पार्श्वे शूरास्ते कपिकुङजराः । तोर्णमापुप्लुवु स्सर्वे सदश्वा इव चोदिताः ।।6.4.41।।
explanation: The heroic and best of the monkeys galloped swiftly on the command of Dasaratha's son like horses that are driven like the steeds.

shloka_text: कपिभ्यामुह्यमानौ तौ शुशुभाते नरर्षभौ । महाद्भ्यामिव सम्स्पृष्टौ ग्रहाभ्यां चन्द्रभास्करौ ।।6.4.42।।
explanation: When Rama and Lakshmana, the best among men were borne by Hanuman and Angada they were shining like the planets Jupiter and Venus conjoined with Sun and Moon.

shloka_text: ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः । जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम् ।।6.4.43।।
explanation: Then righteous Rama who is worshipped by the king of vanaras and by Lakshmana went with the army towards the southern direction.

shloka_text: तमङ्गदगतो रामं लक्ष्मणश्शुभया गिरा । उवाच परिपूर्णार्थ: स्मृतिमान् प्रतिभानवान् ।।6.4.44।।
explanation: Lakshmana, who was borne by Angada, has a good memory and sense of intuition. Set to accomplish his desire fully, he spoke to Rama these auspicious words.

shloka_text: हृतामवाप्य वैदेहीं क्षिप्रं हत्वा च रावणम् । समृद्धार्थस्समृद्धार्थमयोध्यां प्रतियास्यसि ।।6.4.45।।
explanation: Rama After killing Ravana and attaining the desired object of recovering Vaidehi you would go to Ayodhya having accomplished your objective.

shloka_text: महान्ति च निमित्तानि दिवि भूमौ च राघव  । शुभानि तव पश्यामि सर्वाण्येनार्थसिद्धये । अनुवाति शिवो वायु स्सेवां मृदुहित स्सुखः ।।6.4.46।।
explanation: Raghava I am seeing good signs in the sky and also on land indicating auspicious signs of the accomplishment of your desire. The wind is also favourable and agreeable to the moving army.

shloka_text: पूर्णवल्गुस्वराश्चेमे प्रवदन्ति मृगद्विजाः । प्रसन्नाश्च दिश स्सर्वा विमलश्च दिवाकरः ।।6.4.47।।
explanation: The sounds of these animals and birds are very sweet. The directions are pleasing, and the Sun is shining brightly.

shloka_text: उशना च प्रसन्नार्चिरनु त्वां भार्गवो गतः ।।6.4.48।। ब्रह्मराशिर्विशुद्धश्च शुद्दाश्च परमर्षयः । अर्चिष्मन्तः प्रकाशन्ते ध्रुवं सर्वे प्रदक्षिणम् ।।6.4.49।।
explanation: Bhargava who is the master of all knowledge and Sukra, the regent of planet Venus shines brightly behind you. The seven sages who are pure and glowing like fire in brilliance are going round Dhruva.

shloka_text: उशना च प्रसन्नार्चिरनु त्वां भार्गवो गतः ।।6.4.48।। ब्रह्मराशिर्विशुद्धश्च शुद्दाश्च परमर्षयः । अर्चिष्मन्तः प्रकाशन्ते ध्रुवं सर्वे प्रदक्षिणम् ।।6.4.49।।
explanation: Bhargava who is the master of all knowledge and Sukra, the regent of planet Venus shines brightly behind you. The seven sages who are pure and glowing like fire in brilliance are going round Dhruva.

shloka_text: त्रिशङ्कुर्विमलो भाति राजर्षिस्सपुरोहितः । पितामहाः पुरोऽस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् ।।6.4.50।।
explanation: Among the great kings of the Ikshvaku dynasty, the grandfather Trisanku who is a royal sage shines clearly along with Vasishta the foremost priest.

shloka_text: विमले च प्रकाशेते विशाखे निरुपप्लुवे । नक्षत्र वरमस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् ।।6.4.51।।
explanation: The best of stars, Visakha of the highsouled Ikshvakus which is unconnected shines brightly.

shloka_text: नैरृतं नैरृतानां च नक्षत्रमभिपीड्यते । मूलो मूलवता स्पृष्टो धूप्यते धूमकेतुना ।।6.4.52।।
explanation: The star called Niruta (of rakshasas) in the southwest is highly tormented by the touch of the Mula star (close to it) and is oppressed.

shloka_text: सर्वं चैतद्विनाशाय राक्षसानामुप स्थितम् । काले कालगृहीतानां नक्षत्र ग्रहपीडितम् ।।6.4.53।।
explanation: Everything has sprung up for the destruction of rakshasas. Those that are caught up by death will be oppressed at the time of death.

shloka_text: प्रसन्ना स्सुरसाश्चापो वनानि फलवन्ति च । प्रवान्त्यभ्य नाधिकं गन्धान्यथर्तुकुसुमा द्रुमाः ।।6.4.54।।
explanation: The water is pure and of good taste. The forests are filled with fruits. The wind with fragrance is not blowing excessively or violently. The trees are in bloom beyond season.

shloka_text: व्यूढानि कपिसैन्यानि प्रकाशन्तेऽधिकं प्रभो  ।।6.4.55।। देवानामिव सैन्यानि सङ्ग्रामे तारकामये। एवमार्य  । समीक्ष्यैतान्प्रीतो भवितुमर्हसि ।।6.4.56।।
explanation: O King This army of vanaras placed in order is like the forces of gods in their battle with Taraka (a rakshasa who was killed in a battle by Karthikeya) and shines very much. O king, reviewing these (arrangements of army) you ought to be pleased (said Lakshmana to Rama).

shloka_text: व्यूढानि कपिसैन्यानि प्रकाशन्तेऽधिकं प्रभो  ।।6.4.55।। देवानामिव सैन्यानि सङ्ग्रामे तारकामये। एवमार्य  । समीक्ष्यैतान्प्रीतो भवितुमर्हसि ।।6.4.56।।
explanation: O King This army of vanaras placed in order is like the forces of gods in their battle with Taraka (a rakshasa who was killed in a battle by Karthikeya) and shines very much. O king, reviewing these (arrangements of army) you ought to be pleased (said Lakshmana to Rama).

shloka_text: इति भ्रातरमाश्वास्य हृष्ट स्सौमित्रिरब्रवीत् । अथावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम महती चमू: ।।6.4.57।। ऋक्षवानरशर्दूलैर्न खदंष्ट्रायुधैर्वुता ।
explanation: Saumithri reassured his brother who was surrounded by the vanara force saying that those vanaras who use their nails and teeth as weapons and tigerlike bears spread all over the expansive land are proceeding.

shloka_text: काराग्रैश्चरणाग्रैश्च वानरै रुत्थितं रजः । भीममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम् ।।6.4.58।। पर्वतवनाकाशां दक्षिणां हरिवाहिनी । छादयन्ती ययौ भीमा द्यामिवाम्बुदसन्ततिः ।।6.4.59।।
explanation: The terrible dust risen up by the (stamping) legs and hands of the vanara troops spread all over is keeping off Sun's radiance as if creating fear.Alas, the frightening army of vanaras went spreading all over the mountains and forests like the spread of clouds over the sky.

shloka_text: काराग्रैश्चरणाग्रैश्च वानरै रुत्थितं रजः । भीममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम् ।।6.4.58।। पर्वतवनाकाशां दक्षिणां हरिवाहिनी । छादयन्ती ययौ भीमा द्यामिवाम्बुदसन्ततिः ।।6.4.59।।
explanation: The terrible dust risen up by the (stamping) legs and hands of the vanara troops spread all over is keeping off Sun's radiance as if creating fear.Alas, the frightening army of vanaras went spreading all over the mountains and forests like the spread of clouds over the sky.

shloka_text: उत्तरन्त्यां च सेनायां स्सततं बहुयोजनम् । नदीस्रोतांसि सर्वाणि सस्यन्दुर्विपरीतवत् ।।6.4.60।।
explanation: When the army was continuously crossing the river, later (after they crossed) the water flowed excessively like flood.

shloka_text: सरांसि विमलाम्भांसि द्रुमाकीर्णांश्च पर्वता । समान् भूमिप्रदेशांश्च वनानि फलवन्ति च । मध्येन च समन्ताच्च तिर्यक्चाथश्च समाऽविशत् ।।6.4.61।।
explanation: The vanaras went through the pellucid waters of the centre of the lakes. They went obliquely at the mountains, walked on plain lands and underneath trees filled with fruits, plucking them and eating.

shloka_text: समावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम महती चमूः । तेहृष्टवदना स्सर्वे जग्मुर्मारुतरंहसः ।।6.4.62।।
explanation: The great vanara army spread all over the land went with the swiftness of wind with cheerful faces.

shloka_text: हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः ।।6.4.63।। हर्षंवीर्य बलोद्रेकान्दर्शयन्तः परस्परम् । यौवनोत्सेकजान्दर्पाद्विविधांश्चक्रुरध्वनि ।।6.4.64।।
explanation: For the purpose of Rama, the vanaras went showing their valour, happiness and prowess charged with emotion towards one another on the way. They showed their joy and spirit to one another exhibiting their natural youthful enthusiasm, arrogance and several other gestures.

shloka_text: हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः ।।6.4.63।। हर्षंवीर्य बलोद्रेकान्दर्शयन्तः परस्परम् । यौवनोत्सेकजान्दर्पाद्विविधांश्चक्रुरध्वनि ।।6.4.64।।
explanation: For the purpose of Rama, the vanaras went showing their valour, happiness and prowess charged with emotion towards one another on the way. They showed their joy and spirit to one another exhibiting their natural youthful enthusiasm, arrogance and several other gestures.

shloka_text: तत्र केचिद्द्रुतं जग्मुरुत्पेतुश्च तथापरे । केचित्किलकिलां चक्रुर्वानरा वनगोचराः ।।6.4.65।।
explanation: Being vanaras some went swiftly, some jumped, and some others made sound 'kila kila'(the usual sounds of monkeys) while they went.

shloka_text: प्रास्पोटयंश्च पुच्छानि सन्निजग्मु: पदान्यपि । भुजावनिक्षिप्य शैलांश्च द्रुमानन्ये बभञ्जिरे ।।6.4.66।।
explanation: Some hit their tails on the ground, some stamped their feet on the ground, some crushed the mountains with their arms and some broke the trees.

shloka_text: आरोहन्तश्च शृङ्गाणि गिरीणां गिरिगोचराः । महानादान्प्रमुञ्चन्ति क्ष्वेळ्वामन्ये प्रचक्रिरे ।।6.4.67।।
explanation: Vanaras, being the inhabitants of mountains, climbed on peaks of mountains and made loud noises like snapping and roaring like lions. Some went round and round.

shloka_text: ऊरुवेगैश्च ममृदुर्लताजालान्यनेकशः । जृम्भमाणाश्च विक्रान्ता विचिक्रीडुश्शिलाद्रुमै ः ।।6.4.68।।
explanation: With the speed of their shaking thighs, the vanaras broke several meshes of creepers. While yawning also some showed their courage by whirling round and throwing stones and trees.

shloka_text: शतश्शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्च सहस्रशः । वानराणां सुघोराणां श्रीमत्परिवृता मही ।।6.4.69।।
explanation: Formidable vanaras in hundreds, thousands, lakhs and crores spread in a splendid manner around the land.

shloka_text: सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी । प्रहृष्टमुदितास्सेना सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः ।।6.4.70।। वानरास्त्वरितं यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः । प्रमोक्षयिषव स्सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नावसन् ।।6.4.71।।
explanation: The mighty vanara force protected by Sugriva from all sides cheerful at heart, walked day and night speedily. Being eager to somehow liberate Sita they were happy about war and stood nowhere for a while.

shloka_text: सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी । प्रहृष्टमुदितास्सेना सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः ।।6.4.70।। वानरास्त्वरितं यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः । प्रमोक्षयिषव स्सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नावसन् ।।6.4.71।।
explanation: The mighty vanara force protected by Sugriva from all sides cheerful at heart, walked day and night speedily. Being eager to somehow liberate Sita they were happy about war and stood nowhere for a while.

shloka_text: ततः पादपसम्भाधं नानामृगसमायुताम । सह्यपर्वतमासेदुर्मलयञ्च महीधरम् ।।6.4.72।।
explanation: Thereafter having reached the dense forest filled with trees surrounded by the Malaya and Sahaya Mountain inhabited by different kinds of animals, the vanaras assembled.

shloka_text: काननानि विचित्राणि नदी: प्रस्रवणानि च । पश्यन्ननि ययौ रामस्सह्यस्य मलयस्य च ।।6.4.73।।
explanation: Rama too went to see the wonderful woods and streams of rivers of Sahaya mountain.

shloka_text: वकुळान्स्तिलकांश्चूतानसोकान् सिन्धुवारकान् । करवीरांश्च तिनिशान् भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गगमाः ।।6.4.74।।
explanation: The vanaras went adoring the Vakula, Tilaka, Mango, Asoka, Tinisa, Sinduvara and Karaveera trees.

shloka_text: अङ्कोलांश्च करञ्चांश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधतिन्दुकान् । जम्बुकामलकान्नापान्भजन्ति स्म प्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.4.75।।
explanation: Vanaras went adoring the Ankola, Karanja, Plaksa, Nyagrodha, Jambu,Amla and neepa trees.

shloka_text: प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः । वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति तान् ।।6.4.76।।
explanation: Many kinds of trees standing on beautiful rocks and of the forest shaken by the fury of the wind showered their flowers on the vanaras.

shloka_text: मारुतस्सुखसंस्पर्शो वाति चन्दनशीतलः । षटपदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु ।।6.4.77।।
explanation: As the bees humming in delight were spreading the sweet fragrance of honey accompanied the breeze that blew, it was cool like the cool touch of sandal (to the vanaras).

shloka_text: अधिकं शैलराजस्तु धातुभिस्सुविभूषितः । धातुभ्यःप्रसृतो रेणुर्वायुवेग विघट्टितः । सुमहद्वानरानीकं छादयामास सर्वतः ।।6.4.78।।
explanation: That lord of mountains richly adorned with minerals shone very brightly. The mineral particles raised by the stamping of the vanara troops covered the huge vanaras all over.

shloka_text: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वत सम्प्र पुष्पिताः । केतकस्सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः ।।6.4.79।। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः । चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला प्रियकास्तथा ।।6.4.80।। सुफूर्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः । चूताः पाटलयकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः ।।6.4.81।। मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशुपाः कुटजास्तथा । धवा श्शाल्मलयश्चैव रक्ता: कुरवकास्तथा ।।6.4.82।। हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा । नीलाशोकाश्च वरणा अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा ।।6.4.83।। प्लवमानै: प्लवंगैस्तु सर्वे पर्याकुलीकृतां ।।6.4.84।।
explanation: In the mountain ranges were well blossomed trees  such as Kethaka, Sinduvaara and Mango trees Manorama, Madhavi, Kunda, Gulma creepers filled with blossoms of fragrance Chiribilva, Madhuka like wild trees,Vajula,Vakula ,Ranjaka, Tilaka,Kuruvaka, Naga trees Patalaya trees trees with red flowers Arjuna, Simsupa trees with white flowers Kutaja, Dhava and Salmala, Red Kurana, Hinthala,Tinisa,and Churanaka trees, so also dark flowered Asoka trees, Pine trees, Ankola and Padmaka trees were convenient for the monkeys to shake and jump.

shloka_text: गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वत सम्प्र पुष्पिताः । केतकस्सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः ।।6.4.79।। माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः । चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला प्रियकास्तथा ।।6.4.80।। सुफूर्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः । चूताः पाटलयकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः ।।6.4.81।। मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशुपाः कुटजास्तथा । धवा श्शाल्मलयश्चैव रक्ता: कुरवकास्तथा ।।6.4.82।। हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा । नीलाशोकाश्च वरणा अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा ।।6.4.83।। प्लवमानै: प्लवंगैस्तु सर्वे पर्याकुलीकृतां ।।6.4.84।।
explanation: In the mountain ranges were well blossomed trees  such as Kethaka, Sinduvaara and Mango trees Manorama, Madhavi, Kunda, Gulma creepers filled with blossoms of fragrance Chiribilva, Madhuka like wild trees,Vajula,Vakula ,Ranjaka, Tilaka,Kuruvaka, Naga trees Patalaya trees trees with red flowers Arjuna, Simsupa trees with white flowers Kutaja, Dhava and Salmala, Red Kurana, Hinthala,Tinisa,and Churanaka trees, so also dark flowered Asoka trees, Pine trees, Ankola and Padmaka trees were convenient for the monkeys to shake and jump.

shloka_text: वाप्यस्तस्मिन् गिरौ शिता: पल्वलानि तथैव च । चक्रवाकानुचरिताः कारण्डवनिषेविताः ।।6.4.85।। प्लवैः क्रौञ्चेश्च सङ्कीर्णा वराहमृग सेविताः । ऋक्षैस्तरक्षुभिस्सिम्हैश्शार्दूलैश्च भयावहैः ।।6.4.86।। व्यालैश्च बहुभिर्भीमै स्सेव्यमाना स्समन्ततः । पद्मैस्सौगन्दिकैः पुल्लैः कुमुदैश्चोत्पलैस्तथा ।।6.4.87।। वारिजैर्विविधैः पुष्पै रम्यास्तत्र जलाशयाः ।
explanation: In the mountains were reservoirs of water and ponds with cool water inhabited by flocks of Chakravaka birds, water birds like ravens and Krauncha birds. The woodlands were terrific, frequented by boars, bears, hyenas, lions and frightening tigers and many kinds of wild elephants. With flowers in full bloom, the white, blue and red lotuses in the lakes were delightful.

shloka_text: तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा ।।6.4.88।। स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जले क्रीडन्ति वानराः । अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः ।।6.4.89।।
explanation: At that time different kinds of flocks of birds were singing in the mountain ranges. The vanaras after having taken their bath were drinking and sporting with water with each other (pouring water over another) climbing up the mountain.

shloka_text: तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा ।।6.4.88।। स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जले क्रीडन्ति वानराः । अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः ।।6.4.89।।
explanation: At that time different kinds of flocks of birds were singing in the mountain ranges. The vanaras after having taken their bath were drinking and sporting with water with each other (pouring water over another) climbing up the mountain.

shloka_text: फलान्य मृतगन्धीनि मूलानि कुसुमानि च । बभञ्जुर्वास्तत्र पादपानं मदोत्कटाः ।।6.4.90।।
explanation: Then the vanaras who were deluded with pride climbed the trees and ate the fruits with nectar like aroma, roots and flowers.

shloka_text: द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि वानराः । ययुः पिबन्त हृष्टास्ते मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः ।।6.4.91।।
explanation: The tawnyeyed monkeys went joyfully drinking the honey from the large honeycombs hanging there.

shloka_text: पादपानवभञ्जन्तो विकर्षन्त स्तथा लताः । विधमन्तो गिरिवरान्प्रययुः प्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.4.92।।
explanation: The vanaras (who are best among leaping animals) went smashing the trees, pulling out the creepers and purposefully destroying the mountains (on their way).

shloka_text: वृक्षेभ्योऽन्ये तु कपयो नदन्तो मधुदर्पिताः । अन्ये वृक्षान्प्रपद्यन्ते प्रपिबन्त्यपि चापरे ।।6.4.93।।
explanation: While some monkeys that were intoxicated by drinking excessive honey walked where there were no trees, others climbed the tree tops and jumped.

shloka_text: बभूव वसुधा तैस्तु सम्पूर्णा हरियूथपै: । यथा कलमकेदारैः पक्वैरिव वसुन्दरा ।।6.4.94।।
explanation: That land filled completely with the vanara heroes seemed like a fully ripe paddy field.

shloka_text: महेन्द्रमथ सम्प्राप्य रामो राजीवलोचनः । अध्यारोहन्महाबाहुश्शिखरं द्रुमभूषितम् ।।6.4.95।।
explanation: At that time Lotuseyed Rama of mighty shoulders climbed up the the top of mountain Mahendra adorned with beautiful trees.

shloka_text: ततश्शिखरमारुह्य रामो दशरथात्मजः । कूर्ममीनसमाकीर्णमपश्यत्सलिलाकुलम् ।।6.4.96।।
explanation: Then Rama the son of Dasaratha on climbing to the top (of Mahendra mountain) observed the ocean inhabited by tortoises and fish.

shloka_text: ते सह्यं समतिक्रम्य मलयं च महागिरिम् । आसेदुरानुपूर्व्येण समुद्रं भमनिस्स्वनम् ।।6.4.97।।
explanation: The vanaras crossing over the great Sahya and Malaya mountains one after another reached near the frightening ocean.

shloka_text: अवरुह्य जगामाशु वेलावनमनुत्तमम् । रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ट स्ससुग्रीव स्सलक्ष्मणः ।।6.4.98।।
explanation: Rama, who causes delight to others, got down (the mountain) along with Lakshmana and Sugriva and soon reached the wood on the sea coast.

shloka_text: अथ धौतोपलतलां तोयौघै स्सहसोत्थितैः । वेलामासाद्य विपुलान्रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.4.99।।
explanation: Atonce Rama sprung from there (top of mountain) on to an extensive surface of the earth polished by the waves of the ocean spoke these words on reaching there.

shloka_text: एते वयमनुप्राप्ता स्सुग्रीव वरुणालयम् । इहेदानीं विचिन्ता साया नः पूर्वसमुत्थिता ।।6.4.100।।
explanation: Sugriva We have reached the ocean and now we have to think of that idea now, which we thought of earlier.

shloka_text: अतः परमतीरोऽयं सागर स्सरितां पतिः । न चायमनुपायेन शक्यस्तरितुमर्णवः ।।6.4.101।।
explanation: There is only the ocean, the lord of rivers, and the shore is beyond this. We cannot cross the ocean without any mode.

shloka_text: तदिहैव निवेशोऽस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयतामिह । यथेदं वानरबलं परं पारमवाप्नुयात् ।।6.4.102।।
explanation: We will have to leave the army of vanaras here itself. We have to deliberate how to get the vanaras to the other shore.

shloka_text: इतीव स महाबाहुस्सीताहरणकर्शितः । रामस्सागरमासाद्य वासमाज्ञापयत्तदा ।।6.4.103।।
explanation: On seeing the ocean, the mightyarmed Rama, tormented by the abduction of Sita in that way, ordered about the quartering of the vanaras.

shloka_text: सर्वा स्सेना निवेश्यन्तां वेलायां हरिपुङ्गव । सम्प्राप्तो मन्त्रकालो नस्सागरस्येह लङ्घने ।।6.4.104।।
explanation: "O Best of monkeys Now make preparation for all the army to reside at the sea coast. The time to deliberate about crossing the ocean has set in."

shloka_text: स्वां स्वां सेनां समुत्सृज्य मा च कश्चित्कुतो व्रजेत् । गच्छन्तु वानराश्शूराज्ञेयं छन्नं भयं च नः ।।6.4.105।।
explanation: "None of the army should go wherever leaving the parasol. The vanara warriors should keep guarding and you may know that it is dangerous".

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीव स्सहलक्ष्मणः । सेनां निवेशयततीरे सागरस्य द्रुमायुते ।।6.4.106।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Sugriva and Lakshmana made the army to reside on the sea shore filled with trees.

shloka_text: विरराज समीपस्थं सागरस्य तु तद्बलम् । मधुपाण्डुजल श्रशीमान् द्वितीय इव सागरः ।।6.4.107।।
explanation: That vast (sea of) army of monkeys in tawny colour (settled) at the proximity of the sea (that was white) seemed like a prosperous second sea in bright colour.

shloka_text: वेलावनमुपागम्य ततस्ते हरिपुङ्गवाः । निविष्टाश्च परं पारं काङ्क्षमाणा महोदधेः ।।6.4.108।।
explanation: Then the heroic monkeys having arrived at the forest close to the ocean stood there desiring to reach the other shore.

shloka_text: तेषां निविशमानानां सैन्यसन्नाहनिस्स्वनः । अन्तर्धाय महानादमर्णवस्य प्रशुश्रुवे ।।6.4.109।।
explanation: The noise of the ocean was drowned by the great sound produced by the assembly of the army quartered there.

shloka_text: सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिता । त्रिधा निविष्टा महती रामस्यार्थपराऽभवत् ।।6.4.110।।
explanation: The three army groups of vanaras protected by Sugriva encamped for the purpose of Rama appeared enthusiastic.

shloka_text: सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी । वायुवेगसमाधूतं पश्यमाना महार्णवम् ।।6.4.111।।
explanation: Having arrived at the great ocean and seeing the ocean lashed by the fury of the wind the vanaras felt rejoiced.

shloka_text: दूरपारमसम्बाधं रक्षोगणनिषेवितम् । पश्यन्तो वरुणावासं निषेदुर्हरियूथपाः ।।6.4.112।।
explanation: On seeing the expansive ocean, the vanara army thought 'how to cross the abode of rain god whose shores are far away and not connected and is protected by rakshasas'?

shloka_text: चण्डनक्रग्राहं घोरं क्षपादौ दिवसक्ष्ये । हसन्तमिव फेनौघैर्नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.113।।
explanation: As the day was ending and night was setting in, the ocean filled with crocodiles which could catch any animal looked terrific and its waves seemed as if it were laughing and dancing.

shloka_text: चन्द्रोदये समुद्भूतं प्रतिचन्द्रसमाकुलम् । चण्डानिलमहाग्राहैः कीर्णं तिमितिमिङ्गिलैः ।।6.4.114।।
explanation: At the time of the moon rise, the lofty ocean inhabited by dark swift crocodiles, huge Timingala fish scattered in it was rising up with several images of moon reflected in its water.

shloka_text: दीप्तभोगैरिवाकीर्णं भुजङ्गैर्वरुणालयम् । अवगाढं महासत्त्वैर्नानाशैलसमाकुलम् । सुदुर्गं दुर्गमार्गं तमगाध मसुरालयम् ।।6.4.115।।
explanation: Filled with serpents glowing with flaming gems on hoods, the abode of Varuna (was like underworld) with huge snakes and different mountains under water is a difficult path inaccessible and a fathomless abode of rakshasas (vanaras thought).

shloka_text: मकरैर्नागभोगैश्च विगाढा वातलोलिताः । उत्पेतुश्च निपेतुश्च प्रवृद्धा जलराशयः ।।6.4.116।।
explanation: Swarmed with sea animals like sharks and crocodiles and serpents were jumping with huge volumes of water rising and down with force by the stormy wind.

shloka_text: अग्निचूर्णमिवाविद्धं भास्वराम्बुमहोरगम् । सुरारिविषयं घोरं पाताळविषमं सदा ।।6.4.117।।
explanation: The sea that was the domain of snakes was shining as though sparks of fire from the sky penetrated the drops of sea water.

shloka_text: सागरं चाम्बरप्रख्यमम्बरं सागरोपमम् । सागरं चाम्बरं चेति निर्विशेष मदृश्यत ।।6.4.118।।
explanation: The ocean resembled the sky and the sky like the ocean were identical as no difference appeared.

shloka_text: सम्पृक्तं नभसाप्यम्भस्सम्पृक्तं च नभोऽम्भसा । तादृग्रूपेच दृश्यते तारारत्नसमाकुले ।।6.4.119।।
explanation: The ocean and the sky filled with gems and stars respectively appeared alike.

shloka_text: समुत्पतितमेघस्य वीचिमालाकुलस्य च । विशेषो न द्वयोरासीत्सागरस्याम्बरस्य च ।।6.4.120।।
explanation: There was no distinction between the sky with rising clouds and the ocean with moving waves.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यैराहता स्सक्ता स्सस्वनुर्भीमनिस्स्वनाः । ऊर्मयस्सिन्धुराजस्य महाभेर्य इवाहवे ।।6.4.121।।
explanation: The waves of the ocean striking each other making frightening sounds like the blowing of war horns seemed as if challenging each other.

shloka_text: रत्नौघ जलसन्नादं विषक्तमिव वायुना । उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम् ।।6.4.122।। ददृशुस्ते महोत्साह वाताहतजलाशयम् । अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवल्गन्त ममिवोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.123।।
explanation: The enthusiastic vanaras saw the sea inhabited by animals filled with gems and water concentrated in one place rising to the sky, as though infuriated. The rising of the waves (the noise) of the ocean by the cause of wind seemed as if they were talking about.

shloka_text: रत्नौघ जलसन्नादं विषक्तमिव वायुना । उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम् ।।6.4.122।। ददृशुस्ते महोत्साह वाताहतजलाशयम् । अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवल्गन्त ममिवोर्मिभिः ।।6.4.123।।
explanation: The enthusiastic vanaras saw the sea inhabited by animals filled with gems and water concentrated in one place rising to the sky, as though infuriated. The rising of the waves (the noise) of the ocean by the cause of wind seemed as if they were talking about.

shloka_text: ततो विस्मयमापन्ना हरयो ददृशुर्हरयस्तदा । भ्रान्तोर्मिजालसन्नादं प्रलोलमिव सागरम् ।।6.4.124।।
explanation: The vanaras were wonder struck when they saw the ocean that was noisy with rolling waves as if it was highly agitated and distressed. ।।इत्यार्षे वाल्मीकीये श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्थस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the fourth Sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सातुनीलेनविधिवत्स्वारक्षासुसमाहिता । सागरस्योत्तरेतीरेसाधुसेनानिवेशिता ।।6.5.1।।
explanation: Nila settled the army successfully by making them reside on the northern shore of the sea, as per tradition.

shloka_text: मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौतत्रवानरपुङ्गवौ । विचेरतुश्चतांसेनांरक्षार्थंसर्वतोदिशम् ।।6.5.2।।
explanation: Dwivida and Mainda, the best of the vanaras, went about in all directions for safeguarding the army.

shloka_text: निविष्टायांतुसेनायांतीरेनदनदीपतेः । पार्श्वस्थंलक्ष्मणंदृष्टवारामोवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.5.3।।
explanation: After the army had settled down on the shores of the lord of rivers (sea), Rama spoke to Lakshmana who stood beside him.

shloka_text: शोकश्चकिलकालेनगच्छताह्यपगच्छति । ममचापश्यतःकान्तामहन्यहनिवर्धते ।।6.5.4।।
explanation: As time passes, grief passes away. However my sorrow is progressing day by day being unable to see my beloved.

shloka_text: ﻿नमेदुःखंप्रियादूरेनमेदुःखंहृतेतिवा । एतदेवानुशोचामिवयोस्याह्यतिवर्तते ।।6.5.5।।
explanation: ﻿ There is no grief in me that my beloved is at a distance, nor that she is taken away. Indeed her age is advancing. On this account I am feeling for her.

shloka_text: वाहिवातयतःकान्तातांस्पृष्टवामामपिस्पृश । त्वयिमेगात्रसंस्पर्शश्चन्द्रेदृष्टिसमागमः ।।6.5.6।।
explanation: O Wind Touch that place where my beloved is and touch me as it will give me the same feeling as my beloved's touch. Through the moon I will get her eye contact too.

shloka_text: तन्मेदहतिगात्राणिविषंपीतमिवाशये । हानाथेतिप्रियासामांह्रियमाणायदब्रवीत् ।।6.5.7।।
explanation: While being carried away that beloved of mine would have cried aloud saying 'oh my lord'. This thought is burning my body as though I have consumed poison in my stomach.

shloka_text: तद्वियोगेन्धनवतातच्चिन्ताविपुलार्चिषा । रात्रिंदिवंशरीरंमेदह्यतेमदनाग्निना ।।6.5.8।।
explanation: The pain of separation from her is working as fuel and the thought about hers is engulfing me as extensive flame and burning my body day and night.

shloka_text: अवगाह्यर्णवंस्वप्स्येसौमित्रेभवताविना । कथञ्चित्प्रज्वलन्कामस्समांसुप्तंजलेदहेत् ।।6.5.9।।
explanation: O Saumitri Plunging into water alone I will lie down. Probably then the god of love will not be able to consume me while sleeping.

shloka_text: बह्वेतत्कामयानस्यशक्यमेतेनजीवितुम् । यदहंसाचवामोरूरेकांधरणिमाश्रितौ ।।6.5.10।।
explanation: Me and Sita are seeking refuge on the same land indeed. Because of that only survival is possible for me, who is desiring for her very much.

shloka_text: केदारस्येवकेदारस्सोदकस्यनिरूदकः । उपस्नेहेनजीवामिजीवन्तींयच्छृणोमिताम् ।।6.5.11।।
explanation: I am living only because of hearing about her survival, just as a paddy field without water gets wet by the proximity of a neighboring paddy field with water.

shloka_text: कदानुखलुसुश्रोणींशतपत्त्रायतेक्षणाम् । विजित्यशत्रून्द्रक्ष्यामिसीतास्फीतामिवश्रियम् ।।6.5.12।।
explanation: When will I be able to win the enemies and see that Sita of charming limbs, with large and beautiful eyes like lotus petals, who is like an abundance of fortune?

shloka_text: कदानुचारुबिम्बोष्ठंतस्याःपद्ममिवाननम् । ईषदुन्नम्यपास्यामिरसायनमिवातुरः ।।6.5.13।।
explanation: I do not know when I will lift her lotuslike face slightly and drink her beautiful lips like an afflicted man drinks sweet juice.

shloka_text: ﻿तस्यात्तुसंहितौपीनौस्तनौतालफलोपमौ । कदानुखलुसोत्कम्पौश्लिष्यन्त्यामांभजिष्यत: ।।6.5.14।।
explanation: ﻿ Indeed I am eager to embrace my chest with hers like the palmyra -fruit trees hold the fruits.When will it happen?

shloka_text: सानूनमसितापाङ्गीरक्षोमध्यगतासती । मन्नाथानाथहीनेवत्रातारंनाधिगच्छति ।।6.5.15।।
explanation: That darkeyed lady (Sita), even though she has me (husband), is in the midst of rakshasas. Surely she is sad and emaciated being away from her husband, without a protector.

shloka_text: कथंजनकरजस्यदुहिताममचप्रिया । राक्षसीमध्यगाशेतेस्नुषादशरथस्यच ।।6.5.16।।
explanation: My beloved is king Janaka's daughter and daughterinlaw of Dasaratha. Yet she is sleeping amid Rakshasas. How is it?

shloka_text: कदाऽविक्षोभ्यरक्षांसिसाविधूयोत्पतिष्यति । विधूयजलदान्नीलान् शशिरेखाशरत्स्विव ।।6.5.17।।
explanation: When will she come out pushing the Rakshasas like the crescent moon comes out pushing the dark clouds in autumn?

shloka_text: स्वभावतनुकानूनंशोकेनानशनेनच । भूयस्तनुतरासीतादेशकालविपर्ययात् ।।6.5.18।।
explanation: Sita who is by nature slim would surely be slender due to abstaining from eating, unfavorable time and location.

shloka_text: कदानुराक्षसेन्द्रस्यनिधायोरसिसायकान् । सीतांप्रत्याहरिष्यामिशोकमुत्सृज्यमानसम् ।।6.5.19।।
explanation: Indeed by shooting arrows into the chest of rakshasa king, when will I get back Sita and cast off grief from my mind.

shloka_text: कदानुखलुमांसाध्वीसीतासुरसुतोपमा । सोत्कण्ठाकण्ठमालम्ब्यमोक्ष्यत्यानन्दजंजलम् ।।6.5.20।।
explanation: When will Sita, the chaste woman, who is like the daughter of Gods, cling to my neck, and indeed shed tears of joy?

shloka_text: कदाशोकमिमंघोरंमैथिलीविप्रयोगजम् । सहसाविप्रमोक्ष्यामिवासश्शुक्लेतरंयथा ।।6.5.21।।
explanation: When will I get rid of this terrible grief of separation from Mythili for good, just like discarding a soiled garment?

shloka_text: एवंविलपतस्तस्यतत्ररामस्यधीमतः । दिनक्षयान्मन्दवपुर्भास्करोऽस्तमुपागतः ।।6.5.22।।
explanation: While sagacious Rama was wailing in that way the day came to an end with the sun descending to the west.

shloka_text: आश्वासितोलक्ष्मणेनरामस्सन्ध्यामुपासत । स्मरन्कमलपत्राक्षींसीतांशोकाकुलीकृतः ।।6.5.23।।
explanation: Remembering the lotus petal eyed Sita, Rama who was distracted with grief, comforted by Lakshmana offered evening prayers. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्दकाण्डेपञ्चमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the fifth Sarga of Yuddhakanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: लङ्कायांतुकृतंकर्मघोरंदृष्टवाभयावहम् । राक्षसेन्द्रोहनुमताशक्रेणेवमहात्मना ।।6.6.1।। अब्रवीद्राक्षसान्  सर्वान्ह्रियाकिञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः ।
explanation: Considering the terrifying, dreadful action that was carried by the great soul Hanuman who was like Indra in might, the Lord of Rakshasas felt a bit shy and bending down his head addressed all Rakshasas.

shloka_text: धर्षिताचप्रविष्टाचलङ्कादुष्प्रसहापुरी ।।6.6.2।। तेनवानरमात्रेणदृष्टासीताचजानकी ।
explanation: "(Hanuman) After all a monkey in size, entered the inaccessible city of Lanka, destroyed it and saw Sita, daughter of king of Janaka."

shloka_text: प्रासादोधर्षितश्चैत्यःप्रवराराक्षसाहताः ।।6.6.3।। आविलाचपुरीलङ्कासर्वाहनुमताकृता ।
explanation: "Hanuman destroyed huge mansions, killed topmost Rakshasas and shattered all the city of Lanka."

shloka_text: किंकरिष्यामिभद्रंवोकिंवायुक्तमनन्तरम् ।।6.6.4।। उच्यतांनस्समर्थंयत्कृतंचसुकृतंभवेत् ।
explanation: "What is the best thing to do now? What should we do ultimately? What is advisable to do? What strategy is effective? You may suggest that which is good for us."

shloka_text: मन्त्रमूलंचविजयंप्रवदन्तिमनस्विनः ।।6.6.5।। तस्मद्वैरोचयेमन्त्रंरामंप्रतिमहाबलाः ।
explanation: "O mighty Rakshasas Wise elders say that through wise counsel victory is possible. Therefore, in the case of Rama I am thinking of seeking your advice."

shloka_text: त्रिविधाःपुरुषालोकेउत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।।6.6.6।। तेषांतुसमवेतानांगुणदोषौवदाम्यहम् ।
explanation: "In the world, men are of three kinds  good, mediocre and lowly. It is difficult to know their differences. I will tell you about the flaws in their characteristics."

shloka_text: मन्त्रिभिर्हितसंयुक्तैस्समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये ।।6.6.7।। मित्रैर्वापिसमानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपिवाधिकैः । सहितोमन्त्रियित्वायःकर्मारम्भान्प्रवर्तयेत् ।।6.6.8।। दैवेचकुरुतेयत्नंतमाहुःपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
explanation: "He who decides, after deliberating with his wellwishers, with capable ministers of good counsel, relatives of common interest or friends before undertaking his task and tries with faith in god is said to be best among men."

shloka_text: मन्त्रिभिर्हितसंयुक्तैस्समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये ।।6.6.7।। मित्रैर्वापिसमानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपिवाधिकैः । सहितोमन्त्रियित्वायःकर्मारम्भान्प्रवर्तयेत् ।।6.6.8।। दैवेचकुरुतेयत्नंतमाहुःपुरुषोत्तमम् ।
explanation: "He who decides, after deliberating with his wellwishers, with capable ministers of good counsel, relatives of common interest or friends before undertaking his task and tries with faith in god is said to be best among men."

shloka_text: कोऽर्थंविमृशेदेकोधर्मेप्रकुरुतेमनः ।।6.6.9।। कःकार्याणिकुरुतेतमाहुर्मध्यमंनरम् ।
explanation: "He who thinks solitarily (not with others), deliberates with in his mind on his duty and executes his tasks, is said to be a (mediocre) a mediocre one."

shloka_text: गुणदोषौवनिशिचत्य त्यक्त्यादैवव्यपाश्रयम् ।।6.6.10।। करिष्यामीतियःकार्यमुपेक्षेत्सनराधमः ।
explanation: "He who fails to consider the merits and de merits, decides to do on his own and begins without faith in god saying, 'I' will do it, is a lowly one among men."

shloka_text: यथेमेपुरुषानित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।।6.6.11।। वंमन्त्राऽहिविज्ञेयाउत्तमाधममध्यमः ।
explanation: "Just as among men there are good, intermediate and lowly people invariably their counsel is also of three kinds  good, mediocre and lowly."

shloka_text: ऐकमत्यमुपागम्यशास्त्रदृष्टेनचक्षुषा ।।6.6.12।। मन्त्रिणोयत्रनिरतास्तमाहुर्मन्त्रमुत्तमम् ।
explanation: "When all ministers are unanimous and come to one conclusion based on sastras, and having come together remain firm, such counsel is said to be the best."

shloka_text: बह्व्योऽपिमतीर्गत्वामन्त्रिणामर्थनिर्णये ।।6.6.13।। पुनर्यत्रैकतांप्राप्तस्समन्त्रोमध्यमस्स्मृतः ।
explanation: "The conclusion in which many ministers have different points of view and attain unanimity in decision after meeting different points of view is a mediocre vision."

shloka_text: अन्योन्यमतिमास्थाययत्रसम्प्रतिभाष्यते ।।6.6.14।। नचैकमत्येश्रेयोऽस्तिमन्त्रस्सोऽधमउच्यत ।
explanation: "Where counsellors with different opinions hold on to their individual opinions that pleases them and are not for the outcome of a unanimous decision, such a counsel is said to be bad."

shloka_text: तस्मात्सुमन्त्रितंसाधुभवन्तोमतिसत्तमा: ।।6.6.15।। कार्यंसम्प्रतिपद्यन्तामेतत्कृत्यंमतंमम ।
explanation: "On account of that, O wise ones Think over very well, rightly of the task to be done and determine the action required by me now."

shloka_text: वानराणांहिधीराणांसहस्रैःपरिवारितः ।।6.6.16।। रामोऽभ्येतिपुरीलङ्कामस्माकमुपरोधकः ।
explanation: Accompanied by thousands of Vanaras, Rama is approaching to besiege us and reaching the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: तरिष्यतिचसुव्यक्तंराघवस्सागरंसुखम् ।।6.6.17।। तरसायुक्तरूपेणसानुजस्सबलानुगः ।
explanation: "Rama who is worthy of his might, accompanied by his brother and army will be able to cross the ocean speedily and easily."

shloka_text: समुद्रमुच्छोषयतिवीर्येणान्यत्करोतिवा ।।6.6.18।। अस्मिन्नेवंगतेकार्येविरुद्धेवानरैस्सह । हितंपुरेचसैन्येचसर्वसम्मन्त्रयतांमम ।।6.6.19।।
explanation: Rama may dry up the ocean or do something else out of his power. If Vanaras come and encounter us, we will clash with him. When his army has set out that way, you may advise me of a plan that benefits the army and city of Lanka." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्ठमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: इत्युक्ताराक्षसेन्द्रेणराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः । ऊचुःप्रान्जलयःसर्वेरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.7.1।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas of mighty strength, having heard the Lord of Rakshasas, thus spoke to their leader, greeting with folded hands.

shloka_text: द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञायनीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः । राजन्परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम् ।।6.7.2।।
explanation: "O King The ogres are not having political intelligence. They have submitted themselves, even though they are mighty and are having iron bars, javelins, sharp edged spears, and doubleedged swords."

shloka_text: इत्युक्ताराक्षसेन्द्रेणराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः । ऊचुःप्रान्जलयःसर्वेरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.7.3।। द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञायनीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः ।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas having spoken like that, to the Rakshasas, who were very strong, but ignorant about the enemy's strength and who were not endowed with political wisdom, spoke to Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, the following words with folded hands.

shloka_text: राजन्परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम् ।।6.7.4।।
explanation: "Oh king, (our army is equipped with) iron bars, javelins, double edged swords, spears, three pointed weapons, ploughs etc."

shloka_text: सुमहन्नोबलंकस्माद्विषादंभजतेभवान् । त्वयाभोगवतींगत्वानिर्जिताःपन्नगायुधि ।।6.7.5।।
explanation: "Why are you despondent? You have huge and mighty army strength. When you went to Bhogavathi, the Nagas were subdued in war by your mighty army."

shloka_text: कैलासशिखरावासीयक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः । सुमहत्कदनंकृत्वावश्यस्तेधनदःकृतः ।।6.7.6।।
explanation: Surrounded by many Yakshas dwelling on the peaks of Kailasa, having caused a very great slaughter, Dhanada was certainly made subservient to you.

shloka_text: समहेश्वरसख्येनश्लाघमानस्त्वयाविभो । निर्जितःसमरेरोषाल्लोकपालोमहाबलः ।।6.7.7।।
explanation: "O King Proud of his friendship with Lord Maheshwara (Siva), that mighty ruler of the world Kubera was subdued by you in the conflict."

shloka_text: विनिहत्यचयक्षौघान्विक्षोभ्यचविनिगृह्यच । त्वयाकैलासशिखराद्विमानमिदमाहृतम् ।।6.7.8।।
explanation: "Causing terrific disturbance to the hordes of Yakshas and taking them as prisoners, you have brought the great aerial chariot from mount Kailas."

shloka_text: मयेनदानवेन्द्रेणत्वद्भयात्सख्यमिच्छता । दुहितातवभार्यार्थेदत्ताराक्षसपुङ्गव ।।6.7.9।।
explanation: "Maya, the ruler of Danavas has given his daughter (Mandodari) to you as a wife out of fear of you, O leader of Rakshasas"

shloka_text: दानवेन्द्रोमधुर्नामवीर्योत्सिक्तोदुरासदः । विगृह्यवशमानीतःकुम्भीनस्याःसुखावहः ।।6.7.10।।
explanation: "Madhu, another ruler of Danavas who was proud of his valour and difficult to approach, the husband of Kumbhinasi was subjugated by you by your offering to fight with him."

shloka_text: निर्जितास्तेमहाबाहोनागागत्वारसातलम् । वासुकिस्तक्षकःशङखोजटीचवशमाहृताः ।।6.7.11।।
explanation: "O mighty armed king Going to the subterranean world, you won over the serpent demons Vasuki, Takshaka, Shanka and Jati and made them submit to you."

shloka_text: अक्षयाबलवन्तश्चशूरालब्धवराःपुनः । त्वयासंवत्सरंयुद्ध्वासमरेदानवाविभो ।।6.7.12।।
explanation: "The mighty and strong Danava warriors who had obtained boon were made to fight a war by you for one year."

shloka_text: स्वबलंसमुपाश्रित्यनीतावशमरिन्दम । मायाश्चाधिगतास्तत्रबह्व्योवैराक्षसाधिप ।।6.7.13।।
explanation: "O king of Rakshasas (Those Danavas) were reduced to sub mission by resorting to your own strength. Oh subduer of enemies, many deceitful tricks were learned from them."

shloka_text: शूराश्चबलवन्तश्चवरुणस्यसुतारणे । निर्जितास्तेमहाभागचतुर्विधबलानुगाः ।।6.7.14।।
explanation: "O blessed king Mighty strong sons of Varuna, heroes capable of war and of all the four kinds of army have been won by you."

shloka_text: मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहंशाल्मलिद्रुममण्डितम् । कालपाशमहावीचिंयमकिंकरपन्नगम् ।।6.7.15।। महाज्वरेणदुर्धर्षंयमलोकमहार्णवम् । अवगाह्यत्वयाराजन्यमस्यबलसागरम् ।।6.7.16।। जयश्चविपुलःप्राप्तोमृत्युश्चप्रतिषेधितः । सुयुद्धेनचतेसर्वेलोकास्तत्रसुतोषिताः ।।6.7.17।।
explanation: "Oh King Plunging into the ocean, which was in the shape of Yama's realm, with an enormous alligator in the form of rod of death, adorned with Salmali trees, turbulent with a huge wave in the form of Death 's noose, infested with Lord of  Death's attendants as serpents, unassailable on account of the mighty Jwara (spirit of fever), you have obtained a great victory over the Lord of Death 's great army and the army was warded off. By your good battle all the people (of the world) were delighted.

shloka_text: मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहंशाल्मलिद्रुममण्डितम् । कालपाशमहावीचिंयमकिंकरपन्नगम् ।।6.7.15।। महाज्वरेणदुर्धर्षंयमलोकमहार्णवम् । अवगाह्यत्वयाराजन्यमस्यबलसागरम् ।।6.7.16।। जयश्चविपुलःप्राप्तोमृत्युश्चप्रतिषेधितः । सुयुद्धेनचतेसर्वेलोकास्तत्रसुतोषिताः ।।6.7.17।।
explanation: "Oh King Plunging into the ocean, which was in the shape of Yama's realm, with an enormous alligator in the form of rod of death, adorned with Salmali trees, turbulent with a huge wave in the form of Death 's noose, infested with Lord of  Death's attendants as serpents, unassailable on account of the mighty Jwara (spirit of fever), you have obtained a great victory over the Lord of Death 's great army and the army was warded off. By your good battle all the people (of the world) were delighted.

shloka_text: मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहंशाल्मलिद्रुममण्डितम् । कालपाशमहावीचिंयमकिंकरपन्नगम् ।।6.7.15।। महाज्वरेणदुर्धर्षंयमलोकमहार्णवम् । अवगाह्यत्वयाराजन्यमस्यबलसागरम् ।।6.7.16।। जयश्चविपुलःप्राप्तोमृत्युश्चप्रतिषेधितः । सुयुद्धेनचतेसर्वेलोकास्तत्रसुतोषिताः ।।6.7.17।।
explanation: "Oh King Plunging into the ocean, which was in the shape of Yama's realm, with an enormous alligator in the form of rod of death, adorned with Salmali trees, turbulent with a huge wave in the form of Death 's noose, infested with Lord of  Death's attendants as serpents, unassailable on account of the mighty Jwara (spirit of fever), you have obtained a great victory over the Lord of Death 's great army and the army was warded off. By your good battle all the people (of the world) were delighted.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियैर्बहुभिर्वीरैःशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः । आसीद्वसुमतीपूर्णामहद्भिरिवपादपैः ।।6.7.18।।
explanation: "The earth was fully filled with Kshatriya heroes of great prowess, equal to Indra in war who stood like trees on earth."

shloka_text: तेषांवीर्यगुणोत्साहैर्नसमोराघवोरणे । प्रसह्यतेत्वयाराजन्हताःसमरदुर्जयाः ।।6.7.19।।
explanation: "Raghava is not equal to them in valour, excellence and energy. Those warriors who were difficult to overcome by battle were overpowered and killed by you."

shloka_text: तिष्ठवाकिंमहाराजश्रमे णतववानरान् । अयमेकोमहाबाहुरिन्द्रजित्क्षपयिष्यति ।।6.7.20।।
explanation: "Oh great king, you stay here calmly. Why exert yourself? This strong armed Indrajith alone can destroy those Vanaras."

shloka_text: अनेनहिमहाराजमहेश्वरमनुत्तमम् । इष्ट्वायज्ञंवरोलब्धोलोकेपरमदुर्लभः ।।6.7.21।।
explanation: "Oh Great King By performing supreme sacrifices, Indrajith obtained boons from Lord Maheswara, which are very difficult to get."

shloka_text: शक्तितोमरमीनंचविनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलम् । गजकछपसम्बाधमश्वमण्डूकसंकुलम् ।।6.7.22।। रुद्रादित्यमहाग्राहंमरुद्वसुमहोरगम् । रथश्वगजतोयौघंपदातिपुलिनंमहत् ।।6.7.23।। अनेनहिसमासाद्यदेवानांबलसागरम् । गृहीतोदैवतपतिर्लङ्कांचापिप्रवेशितः ।।6.7.24।।
explanation: With spears and javelins as fish, and scattered entrails as moss; crowded with elephants as tortoises, and full of horses as frogs. It had Rudras and Adityas as great crocodiles, and Maruts and Vasus as great serpents;

shloka_text: शक्तितोमरमीनंचविनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलम् । गजकछपसम्बाधमश्वमण्डूकसंकुलम् ।।6.7.22।। रुद्रादित्यमहाग्राहंमरुद्वसुमहोरगम् । रथश्वगजतोयौघंपदातिपुलिनंमहत् ।।6.7.23।। अनेनहिसमासाद्यदेवानांबलसागरम् । गृहीतोदैवतपतिर्लङ्कांचापिप्रवेशितः ।।6.7.24।।
explanation: An ocean with spears and javelins as fish, with scattered entrails as moss, crowded with elephants as tortoises and horses as frogs; with Rudras and Adityas as great crocodiles, with Maruts and Vasus as great serpents, with chariots, horses, and elephants as a flood of water, and a great multitude of foot-soldiers as a vast sandbank. Indeed, having approached this ocean of the gods' army, the lord of the gods was captured by him and also brought into Lanka.

shloka_text: शक्तितोमरमीनंचविनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलम् । गजकछपसम्बाधमश्वमण्डूकसंकुलम् ।।6.7.22।। रुद्रादित्यमहाग्राहंमरुद्वसुमहोरगम् । रथश्वगजतोयौघंपदातिपुलिनंमहत् ।।6.7.23।। अनेनहिसमासाद्यदेवानांबलसागरम् । गृहीतोदैवतपतिर्लङ्कांचापिप्रवेशितः ।।6.7.24।।
explanation: (An ocean) with spears and javelins as fish, with scattered entrails as moss, crowded with elephants as tortoises and horses as frogs, with Rudras and Adityas as great crocodiles, with Maruts and Vasus as great serpents, with chariots, horses, and elephants as torrents of water, and infantry as a great sandbank. Indeed, having reached this ocean of the gods' strength, the lord of the gods was captured and also made to enter Lanka.

shloka_text: पितामहनियोगाच्चमुक्तःशम्बरवृत्रहा । गतस्त्रिविष्टपम्राजन्सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ।।6.7.25।।
explanation: "Liberated by the command of creator Brahma, Indra the destroyer of Sambara and Vrtra entered heaven was adorned and greeted by all Devas."

shloka_text: ततोनीलाम्बुदनिभ: प्रहस्तोनामराक्षसः । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंशूरस्सेनापतिस्तदा ।।6.8.1।।
explanation: Then a Rakshasa whose body was like a dark cloud, called Prahastha, the heroic chief of the army, spoke these words with folded palms.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वाःपिशाचपतगोरगाः । नत्वांधर्षयितुंशक्याःकिंपुनर्वानरारणे ।।6.8.2।।
explanation: "Even Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Devils, birds, and serpents, cannot face you in war. What to say of Vanaras?"

shloka_text: सर्वेप्रमत्ताविश्वस्तावञ्चितास्स्महनूमता । नहिमेजीवतोगच्छेज्जीवन् सवनगोचरः ।।6.8.3।।
explanation: All of us were inattentive and confident (of our ability) while Hanuman cheated us. When I am alive how will the wanderer of woods (Hanuman) go with life?

shloka_text: सर्वांसागरपर्यन्तांसशैलवनकाननाम् । करोम्यवानरांभूमिमाज्ञापयतुमांभवान् ।।6.8.4।।
explanation: "I will make all the oceans, mountains, forests or even the entire earth rid of Vanaras if you order me."

shloka_text: रक्षांचैवविधास्यामिवानराद्रजनीचर । नागमिष्यतितेदुःखंकिञ्चिदात्मापराधजम् ।।6.8.5।।
explanation: "O night ranger (Ravana) I will arrange the protection (of this Lanka) from these Vanaras. For your own wrong action (of abducting Sita) you cannot undergo suffering."

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्चसुसङ्कृद्धोदुर्मुखोनामराक्षसः । इदंनक्षमणीयंहिसर्वेषांनःप्रधर्षणम् ।।6.8.6।।
explanation: Feeling very angry, a Rakshasa called Durmukha said, "He who has caused shame for all of us does not deserve to be excused."

shloka_text: अयंपरिभवोभूयःपुरस्यान्तःपुरस्यच । श्रीमतोराक्षसेन्द्रस्यवानरेणप्रधर्षणम् ।।6.8.7।।
explanation: "Furthermore, this assault by a Vanara on Lanka, to the royal residence, and to the prosperous Lord of Rakshasas is despising."

shloka_text: अस्मिन् मुहूर्तेगत्वैकोनिवर्तिष्यामिवानरान् । प्रविष्टान् सागरंभीममम्बरंवारसातलम् ।।6.8.8।।
explanation: At this very minute I will go alone into the terrific ocean, to the underworld or the upper world and on entering put an end to the monkey.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीत्सुसङ्कृद्धोवज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाबलः । प्रगृह्यपरिघंघोरंमांसशोणितरूषितम् ।।6.8.9।।
explanation: Then a mighty strong one who was endowed with diamond like teeth highly enraged, clasping a dreadful iron bludgeon stained with flesh and blood spoke.

shloka_text: किंवोहनुमताकार्यंकृपणेनतपस्विना । रामेतिष्ठतिदुर्धर्षेससुग्रीवेऽपिसलक्ष्मणे ।।6.8.10।।
explanation: "While unassailable Rama is there, along with Lakshmana and Sugriva, what have we to do with miserable, pitiable and helpless Hanuman?"

shloka_text: अद्यरामंससुग्रीवंपरिघेणसलक्ष्मणम् । आगमिष्यामिहत्वैकोविक्षोभ्यहरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.8.11।।
explanation: "Now I would go alone and with the iron crowbar, kill Sugriva Lakshmana and Rama and return after shattering the Vanara troops."

shloka_text: इदंममापरंवाक्यंशृणुराजन् यदीच्छसि । उपायकुशलोह्येवजयेच्छत्रूनतन्द्रितः ।।6.8.12।।
explanation: "O King If you like, listen to my other statement: One who is cunning and is vigilant would win over an enemy."

shloka_text: कामरूपधराश्शूरास्सुभीमाभीमदर्शनाः । राक्षसावैसहस्राणिराक्षसाधिपनिश्चिताः ।।6.8.13।। काकुत्स्थमुपसङ्गम्यबिभ्रतोमानुषंवपुः । सर्वेह्यसम्भ्रमाभूत्वाब्रुवन्तुरघुसत्तमम् ।।6.8.14।।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas Thousands of fearful Rakshasas capable of assuming any form at free will, heroic ones of frightful appearance should tell Rama the foremost of Raghus, quietly going near him in human form."

shloka_text: कामरूपधराश्शूरास्सुभीमाभीमदर्शनाः । राक्षसावैसहस्राणिराक्षसाधिपनिश्चिताः ।।6.8.13।। काकुत्स्थमुपसङ्गम्यबिभ्रतोमानुषंवपुः । सर्वेह्यसम्भ्रमाभूत्वाब्रुवन्तुरघुसत्तमम् ।।6.8.14।।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas Thousands of fearful Rakshasas capable of assuming any form at free will, heroic ones of frightful appearance should tell Rama the foremost of Raghus, quietly going near him in human form."

shloka_text: प्रेषिताभरतेनैवभ्रात्रातवयवीयसा । सहिसेनांसमुत्थाप्यक्षिप्रमेवोपयास्यति ।।6.8.15।।
explanation: "'We have been sent by your younger brother Bharata and he is coming here very soon with the army."

shloka_text: ततोवयमितस्तूर्णंशूलशक्तिगदाधराः । चापबाणासिहस्ताश्चत्वरितास्तत्रयामहे ।।6.8.16।।
explanation: "Then from here we will go there wielding tridents, javelins, maces, swords and arrows."

shloka_text: आकाशेगणशस्थ्सित्वाहत्वातांहरिवाहिनीम् । अश्मशस्त्रमहावृष्ट्याप्रापयामयमक्षयम् ।।6.8.17।।
explanation: Staying in the sky in groups, we will rain astras, sastras and boulders on the Vanara troops and on killing them, we shall send them to the abode of God of death.

shloka_text: एवंचेदुपसर्पेतामनयंरामलक्ष्मणौ । अवश्यमपनीतेनजहतामेवजीवितम् ।।6.8.18।।
explanation: "When Rama and Lakshmana are distressed that way, they would certainly succumb to our cunning ways and give up life."

shloka_text: कौम्भकर्णिस्ततोवीरोनिकुम्भोनामवीर्यवान् । अब्रवीत्परमक्रुद्धोरावणंलोकरावणम् ।।6.8.19।।
explanation: Thereafter the enraged heroic and valiant son of Kumbhakarna called Nikumbha said to Ravana, who made the world cry.

shloka_text: सर्वेभवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तुमहाराजेनसङ्गताः । अहमेकोहनिष्यामिराघवंसहलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.8.20।। सुग्रीवञ्चहनूमन्तंसर्वांनेवचवानरान् ।
explanation: "Let all of you stay here along with the king. Going alone I will kill Rama along with Lakshmana, and Hanuman also Sugriva and all of the Vanaras."

shloka_text: ततोवज्रहनुर्नामराक्षसःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.8.21।। क्रुद्ध: परिलिहन्सृक्कांजिह्वयावाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Then a Rakshasa called Vajrahanu, mountain like in form, enraged, licking lips with his tongue said these words.

shloka_text: स्वैरंकुर्वन्तुकर्माणिभवन्तोविगतज्वराः ।।6.8.22।। एकोऽहंभक्षयिष्यामितांसर्वांहरियूथपान् । स्वस्थाःक्रीडन्तुनिश्चिन्ताःपिबन्तुमधुवारुणीम् ।।6.8.23।।
explanation: All of you giving up fear, do your duties freely move happily sporting and drinking sweet wine. Single handed, I will consume all the Vanara army.

shloka_text: स्वैरंकुर्वन्तुकर्माणिभवन्तोविगतज्वराः ।।6.8.22।। एकोऽहंभक्षयिष्यामितांसर्वांहरियूथपान् । स्वस्थाःक्रीडन्तुनिश्चिन्ताःपिबन्तुमधुवारुणीम् ।।6.8.23।।
explanation: All of you giving up fear, do your duties freely move happily sporting and drinking sweet wine. Single handed, I will consume all the Vanara army.

shloka_text: अहमेकोवधिष्यामिसुग्रीवंसहलक्ष्मणम् । साङ्गदंचहनूमन्तंरामंचरणकुञ्जरम् ।।6.8.24।।
explanation: "I alone will kill that Rama with Lakshmana, Sugriva, that Angada, Hanuman and the Vanara army." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेअष्टमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the eighth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोनिकुम्भोरभसस्सूर्यशत्रुर्महाबलः । सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञहारक्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.9.1।। अग्निकेतुश्चदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चराक्षस: । इन्द्रजिच्चमहातेजाबलवान्रावणात्मजः ।।6.9.2।। प्रहस्तोऽथविरूपाक्षोवज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाबलः । धूम्राक्षश्चातिकायश्चदुर्मुखश्चैवराक्षसः ।।6.9.3।। परिघान्पट्टिशान्प्रासान्शक्तिशूलपरश्वधान् । चापानिचसबाणानिखङ्गांश्चविपुलान्शितान् ।।6.9.4।। प्रगृह्यपरमक्रुद्धास्समुत्पत्यचराक्षसाः । अब्रुवन्रावणंसर्वेप्रदीप्ताइवतेजसा ।।6.9.5।।
explanation: Then Nikumbha, Rshabha, mighty Suryasatru, Supthagna, Yagnaha raksha, Mahaparva, Mahodaro, Durdarsha, Agnikethu, Rasmikethu Rakshasas, Further Ravana's own son powerful Indrajith, Virupaksha and Prahasta, and mighty Rakshasas Vajradamshtra, Dumraaksha and also Durmukha of huge body holding iron bars, tridents, battle axes, bows and sharp arrows, very sharp swords, got up, highly enraged and all Rakshasas glowing like fire addressed Ravana.

shloka_text: अद्यरामंवधिष्यामस्सुग्रीवंसचलक्ष्मणम् । कृपणंचहनूमन्तंलङ्कायेनप्रधर्षिता ।।6.9.6।।
explanation: "Right now, we will kill Rama along with Lakshmana, Sugriva and vile Hanuman, on whose account Lanka was attacked."

shloka_text: तान्गृहीतायुधान् सर्वान्वारयित्वाविभीषणः । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंपुनःप्रत्युपवेश्यतान् ।।6.9.7।।
explanation: With folded hands, Vibheeshana made all the (Rakshasas) wielding arms to stop and sit and addressed these words to Ravana.

shloka_text: अप्युपायैस्त्रिभिस्तातयोऽर्थःप्राप्तुंनशक्यते । तस्यविक्रमकालांस्तान्युक्तानाहुर्मनीषिणः ।।6.9.8।।
explanation: "Dear father, intelligent people say that an act which cannot be accomplished by the three means (Sama  Conciliation, Dana  Gift, Bheda  Sowing dissension), should only be accomplished diligently by one's heroic deed. Therefore, we should think of war only after the above three means are employed."

shloka_text: प्रमत्तेष्यभियुक्तेषुदैवेनप्रहतेषुच । विक्रमास्तातसिध्यन्तिपरीक्ष्यविधिनाकृताः ।।6.9.9।।
explanation: "O Dear at those who are not alert, who are attacked by the enemy, and who are struck by fate, if you examine diligently according to prescribed method and perform deeds of heroic valour you will succeed."

shloka_text: अप्रमत्तंकथंतंतुविजिगीषुंबलेस्थितम् । जितरोषंदुराधर्षतंप्रधर्षयितुमिच्छथ ।।6.9.10।।
explanation: "How do you wish to overpower, him who is very attentive, bent on victory, mighty, steadfast, has subdued anger and unassailable?"

shloka_text: समुद्रंलङ्घयित्वातुघोरंनदनदीपतिम् । गतिंहनूमतोलोकेकोविद्यात्तर्कयेतवा ।।6.9.11।।
explanation: "Hanuman has crossed over the ocean, a Lord of streams and rivers and arrived. Who can ever know or think of such a task in this world?"

shloka_text: बलान्यपरिमेयानिवीर्याणिचनिशाचराः । परेषांसहसाऽवज्ञानकर्तव्याकथञ्चन ।।6.9.12।।
explanation: "Enemy's strength and valour is inestimable to relate. Do not disregard rashly, O Night ranger"

shloka_text: किंचराक्षसराजस्यरामेणापकृतंपुरा । आजहारजनस्थानाद्यस्यभार्यांयशस्विनः ।।6.9.13।।
explanation: "What offence did Rama do earlier to the Rakshasa king that he abducted the glorious wife of Rama from Janasthana?"

shloka_text: खरोयद्यतिवृत्तस्तुरामेणनिहतोरणे । अवश्यंप्राणिनांप्राणारक्षितव्यायथाबलम् ।।6.9.14।।
explanation: "(It is true) Khara was killed by Rama in war as he acted beyond his limit. Certainly, living beings will have to protect their life with their own strength."

shloka_text: एतन्निमित्तंवैदेहीभयंनस्सुमहद्भवेत् । आहृतासापरित्याज्याकलहार्थेकृतेनकिम् ।।6.9.15।।
explanation: "On account of this, we have a great fear of Vaidehi. She, who was brought here, is to be given away. What is the use of doing anything, which may be the cause of strife?"

shloka_text: नतुक्षमंवीर्यवतातेनधर्मानुवर्तिना । वैरंनिरर्थकंकर्तुंदीयतामस्यमैथिली ।।6.9.16।।
explanation: "To have enmity with a valorous one, a follower of dharma, is useless and not good for us. Give away Mythili to him (Rama)."

shloka_text: यावन्नसगजांसाश्वांबहुरत्नसमाकुलाम् । पुरींदारयतेबाणैर्दीयतामस्यमैथिली ।।6.9.17।।
explanation: "Before Rama comes with elephants and horses and tears with his arrows, this Lanka filled with abundance of gems, give away Mythili."

shloka_text: यावत्सुघोरामहतीदुर्धर्षाहरिवाहिनी । नावस्कन्दतिनोलङ्कांतावत्सीताप्रदीयताम् ।।6.9.18।।
explanation: "Lest the highly dreadful, formidable and huge Vanara troops surround all over Lanka. Give away Sita."

shloka_text: विनश्येद्धिपुरीलङ्काशूरास्सर्वेचराक्षसाः । रामस्यदयितापत्नीनस्वयंनयदिदीयते ।।6.9.19।।
explanation: "If Rama's dear wife is not given, this Lanka will be destroyed and also all Rakshasas."

shloka_text: प्रसादयेत्वांबन्धुत्वात्कुरुष्यवचनंमम । हितंतथ्यमहंब्रूमिदीयतामस्यमैथिली ।।6.9.20।।
explanation: "I am requesting you because you are my relation (brother). Do as I said, as I am telling you for your welfare. Give away Sita."

shloka_text: पुराशरत्सूर्यमरीचिसन्निभान्नवाग्रपुङ्खान् सुदृढान्नृपात्मजः । सृजत्यमोघान्विशिखान्वधायतेप्रदीयतांदशरधायमैथिली ।।6.9.21।।
explanation: "You may restore Rama's Mythili, before the emperor Dasaratha's son sends forth solid unfailing arrows shining like autumnal Sun provided with fresh heads and shafts for killing you."

shloka_text: त्वजस्वकोपंसुखधर्मनाशनंभजस्वधर्मंरतिकीर्तिवर्धनम् । प्रसीदजीवेमसपुत्रबान्धवाःप्रदीयतांदाशरथायमैथिली ।।6.9.22।।
explanation: "Give up that happiness and anger which destroys virtues. Seek pleasures that enhance fame. Be pacified. Live happily with sons and relatives restoring Mythili to Rama, the son of Dasaratha."

shloka_text: विभीषणवच्शुत्वारावणोराक्षसेश्वराः । विसर्जयित्वातान्सर्वान्प्रविवेशस्वकंगृहम् ।।6.9.23।।
explanation: Having heard everything that was told by Vibheeshana, the Lord of Rakshasas sent away all and entered his palace. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेनवमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the ninth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततःप्रत्युषसिप्राप्तेप्राप्तधर्मार्थनिश्चयः । राक्षसाधिपतेर्वेश्मभीमकर्माविभीषणः ।।6.10.1।।
explanation: Thereafter, determined to relate about righteous and material gains, Vibheeshana of fierce tasks got up early in the morning when the Sun rose and set himself to go to the residence of Lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: शैलाग्रचयसङ्काशंशैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् । सुविभक्तमहाकक्षंमहाजनपरिग्रहम् ।।6.10.2।।
explanation: Like a lofty mountain top, and like a summit of a mountain, Ravana's palace was a supreme one, divided into many spacious sections and surrounded by many people.

shloka_text: मतिमद्भिर्महामात्रैरनुरक्तैरधिष्ठितम् । राक्षसैराप्तपर्याप्तैस्सर्वतःपरिरक्षितम् ।।6.10.3।।
explanation: The palace was inhabited by wise ones, and devoted to their Lord and ministers,commanded by trustworthy and competent Rakshasas spread everywhere and well protected.

shloka_text: मत्तमातङ्गनिश्श्वासैर्व्याकुलीकृतमारुतम् । शङ्खघोषमहाघोषंतूर्यनादानुनादितम् ।।6.10.4।।
explanation: It was filled with elephants in rut breathing heavily, which was like a tempestuous wind around, that echoed by the blowing of conchs of the early morning and filled with the sounds of drums and trumpets.

shloka_text: प्रमदाजनसम्बाधंप्रजल्पितमहापथम् । तप्तकाञ्चननिर्यूहंभूषणोत्तमभूषितम् ।।6.10.5।।
explanation: (It was) The royal path was filled with women, with prattling sounds of gossiping. It had shining golden passages and decorated with the best of ornaments.

shloka_text: गन्धर्वाणामिवाऽवासमालयंमरुतामिव । रत्नसञ्चयसम्बाधंभवनंभोगिनामिव ।।6.10.6।।
explanation: (It was) like the abode of Gandharvas (the celestial musicians), like an abode of wind god, abounding in collection of precious gems, like the mansion of Nagas indulging  in enjoyment.

shloka_text: तंमहाभ्रमिवाऽदित्यस्तेजोविस्तृतरश्मिमान् । अग्रजस्यालयंवीरःप्रविवेशमहाद्युतिः ।।6.10.7।।
explanation: Heroic (Vibheeshana) of exceptional splendour, whose brilliance spread widely like the radiance of the highly lustrous Sun entered his brother's abode.

shloka_text: पुण्यान्पुण्याहघोषांश्चवेदविद्भिरुदाहृतान् । शुश्रावसुमहातेजाभ्रातुर्विजयसंश्रितान् ।।6.10.8।।
explanation: Highly effulgent (Vibheeshana) heard sounds of recitation of sacred mantras from Vedas uttered by learned ones desiring a propitious day for his brother.

shloka_text: पूजितान् दधिपात्रैश्चसर्पिर्भिस्सुमनोक्षतैः । मन्त्रवेदविदोविप्रान्ददर्शसमहाबलः ।।6.10.9।।
explanation: Mighty Vibheeshana saw there, brahmins learned in vedas and mantras, who worshipped with yellow rice, curd, clarified butter and flowers.

shloka_text: सपूज्यमानोरक्षोभिद्दीप्यमानस्स्वतेजसा । आसनस्थंमहाबाहुर्ववन्देधनदानुजम् ।।6.10.10।।
explanation: Vibheeshana, of broad shoulders, who is revered by Rakshasas was shining in his own splendour. He greeted with folded palms, the brother of Kubera (Ravana) seated on his chair.

shloka_text: सराजदृष्टिसम्पन्नमासनंहेमभूषितम् । जगामसमुदाचारंप्रयुज्याचारकोविदः ।।6.10.11।।
explanation: Vibheeshana who was learned in traditions and wellversed with code of conduct reached a seat decorated with gold blessed by the glance of the king Ravana.

shloka_text: सरावणंमहात्मानंविजनेमन्त्रिसन्निधौ । उवाचहितमत्यर्थंवचनंहेतुनिश्चितम् ।।6.10.12।।
explanation: When none other than ministers were present, Vibheeshana spoke these meaningful words to the distinguished Ravana, decidedly wishing for welfare.

shloka_text: प्रसाद्यभ्रातरंजेष्ठंसान्त्वेनोपस्थितक्रमः । देशकालार्थसंवादिदृष्टलोकपरावरः ।।6.10.13।।
explanation: Vibheeshana who knew the good and bad of the world and knew to advice in consonance with place and time said to his elder brother in an appeasing manner, propitiating him observing the customary tradition.

shloka_text: यदाप्रभृतिवैदेहीसम्प्रास्तेमांपुरींतव । तदाप्रभृतिदृश्यन्तेनिमित्तान्यशुभानिनः ।।6.10.14।।
explanation: "Since Vaidehi has come to this city, inauspicious happenings are seen by us."

shloka_text: सस्फुलिङ्गस्सधूमार्चिस्सधूमकलुषोदयः । मन्त्रसङ्घहुतोऽप्यग्निर्नसम्यगभिवर्थते ।।6.10.15।।
explanation: "Even from the fire of fire sacrifices, fire particles polluted with smoke are rising and the fire is not burning with brilliance."

shloka_text: अग्निष्ठेष्वग्निशलासुतथाब्रह्मस्थालीषुच । सरीसृपाणिदृश्यन्तेहन्येषुचपिपीलिकाः ।।6.10.16।।
explanation: "In the cooking fire, in places of fire sacrifice, so also at places where offerings are made into fire, serpents are seen. Ants are seen in the Havis."

shloka_text: गवांसयांसिस्कन्नानिविमदावीरकुञ्जराः । दीनमश्वाःप्रहेषन्तेनचग्रासाभिनन्दिनः ।।6.10.17।।
explanation: "The udder of cows is dried up, the proud elephants have lost their ichor, the horses are pathetic and neighing. They are not even interested in fodder."

shloka_text: खरोष्ट्राश्वतराराजभनभिन्नरोमास्स्रवन्तिच । नस्वभावेऽवतिष्ठन्तिविधानैरपिचिन्तिताः ।।6.10.18।।
explanation: "O King the donkeys and camels have shed their body hair and are crying. Even though they are treated for it in different ways they are not getting to be in normal natural form."

shloka_text: वायसाःसङ्घशःक्रूराव्याहरन्तिसमन्ततः । समवेताश्चदृश्यन्तेविमानाग्रेषुसङ्घशः ।।6.10.19।।
explanation: Wild crows are seen in flocks all over the top of aerial chariot sounding harsh gathered in groups.

shloka_text: गृध्राश्चपरिलीयन्तेपुरीमुपरिपिण्डिताः । उपपन्नाश्चस्नध्येद्वेव्याहऱ्नत्यशिवंशिवाः ।।6.10.20।।
explanation: "Even the eagles are collecting together and standing over the houses of the capital repeatedly in both the auspicious times of morning and evening and making inauspicious sounds."

shloka_text: क्रव्यादानांमृगाणांचपुरीद्वारेषुसङ्घशः । श्रूयन्तेविपुलाघोषास्सविस्फूर्जितनिस्स्वनाः ।।6.10.21।।
explanation: At the entrance of the capital are heard thunderous sounds of carnivorous animals collected together sounding like thunder.

shloka_text: तदेवंप्रस्तुतेकार्येप्रायश्चित्तमिदंक्षमम् । रोचतेयदिवैदेहीराघवायप्रदीयताम् ।।6.10.22।।
explanation: "Therefore, the task (of burning Lanka) has commenced. I have thought of this appropriate atonement. Restore Vaidehi to Rama."

shloka_text: इदंचयदिवामोहाल्लोभाद्वाव्याहृतंमया । तत्रापिचमहाराज नदोषंकर्तुमर्हसि ।।6.10.23।।
explanation: "O great king You may know that I am not telling like this out of my delusion or greed. You ought not to find fault with me."

shloka_text: अयंहिदोषस्सर्वस्यजनस्यास्योपलक्ष्यते । रक्षसांराक्षसीनांचपुरस्यान्तःपुरस्यच ।।6.10.24।।
explanation: All of us, the Rakshasas and Rakshasa women of the capital, even those in the harem, and all the common people are aware of this offence.

shloka_text: श्रावणेचास्यमन्त्रस्यनिवृत्तास्सर्वमन्त्रिणः । अवश्यंचमयावाच्यंयद्दृष्टमपिवाश्रुतम् ।।6.10.25।। सम्विधाययथान्यायंतद्भवान् कर्तुमर्हति ।
explanation: All your ministers have abstained from telling you out of fear of you. I must necessarily tell you (as brother) this which is seen and heard. You may determine that which is justifiable by determining the propriety. It is proper for me to submit to you.

shloka_text: इतिस्ममन्त्रिणांमध्येभ्राताभ्रातरमूचिवान् । रावणंराक्षसांश्रेष्ठंपथ्यमेतद्विभीषणः ।।6.11.26।।
explanation: Brother Vibheeshana thus tendered advice to Ravana, the eminent king of Rakshasas in the presence of his ministers.

shloka_text: हितंमहार्थंमृदुहेतुसंहितंव्यतीतकालायतिसम्प्रतिक्षमम् । निशम्यतद्वाक्यमुपस्थितज्वरःप्रसङ्गवानुत्तरमेतदब्रवीत् ।।6.10.27।।
explanation: Foregoing the beneficial, meaningful, and gentle words of counsel of significance in the past, present and future also (given by Vibheeshana), Ravana seized with anger replied in this manner.

shloka_text: भयंनपश्यामिकुतश्चिदप्यहंनराघवःप्राप्स्यतिजातुमैथिलीम् । सुरैस्सहेन्द्रैरपिसङ्गरेकथंममाग्रतस्स्थास्यतिलक्ष्मणाग्रजः ।।6.10.28।।
explanation: "I do not perceive fear from anyone. Rama will not be able to get Mythili at any time. How can the elder brother of Lakshmana withstand me even if Indra and Devatas come (to his help) in battle"

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वासुरसैन्यनाशनोमहाबलस्संयतिचण्डविक्रमः । दशाननोभ्रातरमाप्तवादिनंविसर्जयामासतदाविभीषणम् ।।6.10.29।।
explanation: Then mighty tenheaded Ravana of formidable valour, a destroyer of Devatas' army in war, sent away Vibheeshana who had spoken words of good advice in that manner. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेवामलीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेदशमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the tenth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सबभूवकृशोराजामैथिलीकाममोहितः । असन्मानाच्चसुहृदांपापंपापेनकर्मणा ।।6.11.1।।
explanation: Infatuated with passion towards Mythili, disregarded by his dear ones on account of sinful actions, sinner Ravana became weak.

shloka_text: अतीतसमयेकालेतस्मिन्वैयुधिरावणः । अमात्यैश्चसुहृद्भिश्चप्राप्तकालममन्यत ।।6.11.2।।
explanation: Because of the lapse of time, Ravana considered it imminent to consult with his ministers and friends about war.

shloka_text: सहेमजालविततंमणिविद्रुमभूषितम् । उपगम्यविनीताश्वमारुरोहमहारथम् ।।6.11.3।।
explanation: Ravana, having reached, ascended the magnificent chariot that was overlaid with golden latticework, decked with gems and corals, and yoked to trained horses.

shloka_text: तमास्थायरथश्रेष्ठंमहामेघसमस्वनम् । प्रययौरक्षसांश्रेष्ठोदशग्रीवस्सभांप्रति ।।6.11.4।।
explanation: The tenheaded Ravana, eminent one among Rakshasas climbed up that best of chariots that was making noise like the roaring sound of a huge cloud and went to assembly.

shloka_text: असिचर्मधरायोधास्सर्वायुधधरास्ततः । राक्षसाराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपुरस्तात्सम्प्रतस्थिरे ।।6.11.5।।
explanation: Then soldiers wielding swords and different kinds of weapons stood in front of the Lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: नानाविकृतवेषाश्चनानाभूषणभूषिताः । पार्श्वतस्पृष्ठतश्चैनंपरिवार्यययुस्तत:।। 6.11.6।।
explanation: Further (Rakshasas) adorned in different kinds of uncouth attire, wearing different kinds of ornaments went by his side and also at the back.

shloka_text: रथैश्चातिरथाश्शीघ्रंमत्तैश्चवरवारणैः । अनूत्पेतुर्दशग्रीवमाक्रीडद्भिश्चवाजिभिः ।।6.11.7।।
explanation: (Some Rakshasa) Charioteers riding on chariots, some on proud elephants and some on horses sporting away followed the tenheaded Ravana.

shloka_text: गदापरिघहस्ताश्चशक्तितोमरपाणयः । परश्वथधराश्चान्येतथाऽन्येशूलपाणयः ।।6.11.8।।
explanation: Some holding maces and iron bars, some holding strong iron clubs in hand, and some others holding battle axes, tridents and other weapons went.

shloka_text: ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणांसञ्जज्ञेनिस्स्वनोमहान् । तुमुलश्शङ्खशब्दश्चसभांगच्छतिरावणे ।।6.11.9।।
explanation: Then as Ravana entered the assembly thousands of band instruments sounded aloud. Conchs broke forth producing tumultuous noise.

shloka_text: सनेमिघोषेणमहान्सहसाऽभिनिनादयन् । राजमार्गंश्रियाजुष्टंप्रतिपेदेमहारथः ।।6.11.10।।
explanation: As the rattling sounds of the great chariot echoed in all directions, he entered the bright pleasing royal path all at once.

shloka_text: विमलंचातपत्राणांप्रगृहीतमशोभत । पाण्डुरंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपूर्णस्ताराधिपोयथा ।।6.11.11।।
explanation: The pure white canopy of Ravana held by the Rakshasas spread like lines shone like the Lord of stars (the full moon).

shloka_text: हेममञ्जरिगर्भेचशुद्धस्फटिकविग्रहे । चामरव्यजनेतस्यरेजतुस्सव्यदक्षिणे ।।6.11.12।।
explanation: A pair of fans with pure crystal like handles with a golden bouquet in the middle glowed.

shloka_text: तेकृताञ्जलयस्सर्वेरथस्थंपृथिवीस्थिताः । राक्षसाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंशिरोभिस्तंववन्दिरे ।।6.11.13।।
explanation: Standing on the ground, all the Rakshasas bowing their heads down and with folded palms offered their salutations to the foremost of the Rakshasas seated in the chariot.

shloka_text: राक्षसैस्त्सूयमानस्सञ्जयाशीर्भिररिन्दमः । आससादमहातेजास्सभांविरचितांतदा ।।6.11.14।।
explanation: Then as the conqueror of foes, an exceptionally splendid one, Ravana was praised by the Rakshasas saying, "Victory to you, Prosperity to you", Ravana entered the wellbuilt royal court.

shloka_text: सुवर्णरजतास्तीर्णांविशुद्धस्फटिकान्तराम् । विराजमानोवपुषारुक्मपट्टोत्तरच्छदाम् ।।6.11.15।। तांपिशाचशतै: षङ्भिरभिगुप्तांसदाप्रभाम् । प्रविवेशमहातेजास्सुकृतांविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.11.16।।
explanation: Exceptionally splendid one, (Ravana) embodied with glowing body entered the royal court constructed by Vishwakarma, with pillars of gold and silver. Inside of the court was pure like crystal and carpeted with shining golden silk. It was very beautiful and ever shining and guarded by six hundred devils.

shloka_text: सुवर्णरजतास्तीर्णांविशुद्धस्फटिकान्तराम् । विराजमानोवपुषारुक्मपट्टोत्तरच्छदाम् ।।6.11.15।। तांपिशाचशतै: षङ्भिरभिगुप्तांसदाप्रभाम् । प्रविवेशमहातेजास्सुकृतांविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.11.16।।
explanation: Exceptionally splendid one, (Ravana) embodied with glowing body entered the royal court constructed by Vishwakarma, with pillars of gold and silver. Inside of the court was pure like crystal and carpeted with shining golden silk. It was very beautiful and ever shining and guarded by six hundred devils.

shloka_text: तस्यांसवैडूर्यमयंप्रियकाजिनसम्वृतम् । महत्सोपाश्रयंभेजेरावणःपरमासनम् ।।6.11.17।।
explanation: Ravana sat on a huge excellent seat encrusted with Vydurya gems and covered with deer skin and which had a pillow.

shloka_text: तत: शशासेश्वरवद्दूतान्लघुपराक्रमान् । समानयतमेक्षिप्रमिहैतान्राक्षसानिति ।। कृत्यमस्तिमहज्जानेकर्तव्यमितिशत्रुभिः ।।6.11.18।।
explanation: Then that Lord like Ravana said "We have to do a great task against the enemies now. It has to be performed." He commanded quick footed messengers to get the Rakshasas to him at once.

shloka_text: राक्षसास्तद्वचश्श्रुत्वालङ्कायांपरिचक्रमुः ।।6.11.19।। अनुगेहमवस्थायविहारशयनेषुच । उद्यानेषुचरक्षांसिचोदयन्तोह्यभीतवत् ।।6.11.20।।
explanation: Those Rakshasas having heard the words spoken by Ravana went to places of recreation, bedrooms and gardens and went round without fear into every house directing the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: राक्षसास्तद्वचश्श्रुत्वालङ्कायांपरिचक्रमुः ।।6.11.19।। अनुगेहमवस्थायविहारशयनेषुच । उद्यानेषुचरक्षांसिचोदयन्तोह्यभीतवत् ।।6.11.20।।
explanation: Those Rakshasas having heard the words spoken by Ravana went to places of recreation, bedrooms and gardens and went round without fear into every house directing the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तेरथान् रुचिरानेकेदृप्तानेकेपृथग्घयान् । नागानेकेऽधिरुरुहुर्जग्मुश्चैकेपदातयः ।।6.11.21।।
explanation: Of those (Rakshasas) some went on exquisite chariots, some on proud sturdy horses some ascended elephants and some by foot.

shloka_text: सापुरीपरमाकीर्णारथकुञ्जरवाजिभिः । सम्पतद्भिर्विरुरुचेगरुत्मद्भिरिवाम्बरम् ।।6.11.22।।
explanation: With chariots, elephants and horses advancing in groups the prosperous capital was shining resembling the flocks of birds in the sky.

shloka_text: तेवाहनाव्यवस्थाप्ययानानिविविधानिच । सभांपद्भिःप्रविविशुस्सिंहागिरिगुहामिव ।।6.11.23।।
explanation: Parking those vehicles of several kinds at the entrance they entered the royal court by foot like the lions entering the cave of a mountain.

shloka_text: राज्ञःपादौगृहीत्वातुराज्ञातेप्रतिपूजिताः । पीठेष्वन्येबृसीष्वन्येभूमौकेचिदुपाविशन् ।।6.11.24।।
explanation: They held the feet of the king and on offering salutations to the king took their seat. While some took golden seats, some sat on a kusa grass mat, and some took a se at on the floor.
