shloka_text: यःपुरागोमतीतीरेरम्यंपर्येतिपर्वतम् । नाम्नासङ्कोचनोनामनानानगयुतोगिरिः ।।6.26.27।। तत्रराज्यंप्रशास्त्येषकुमुदोनामयूथपः । योऽसौशतसहस्राणिसहस्रंपरिकर्षति ।।6.26.28।। यस्यवालाबहुव्यामादीर्घलाङ्गूलमाश्रिता । ताम्रापीतास्सीताश्श्वेताःप्रकीर्णाघोरदर्शना ।।6.26.29।। अदीनोरोषणश्चण्डस्सङ्ग्राममभिकाङ् क्षति । एषोऽप्याशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।।6.26.30।।
explanation: "He who was residing on the banks of Gomathi earlier, which was delightful with a range of mountain peaks extending far, was ruling this kingdom from the mountain Sankochana. He is Kumuda by name. He drags his troops delightfully the ones with hairy long tails, some of coppery red colour, some yellow and some with white tails. Such a Vanara called Kumuda is dragging hundred thousand Vanaras, some fastened and some scattered. He is one who has no pity and is frightening to look at. Single handed he is aspiring to crush Lanka with its army in war."

shloka_text: यःपुरागोमतीतीरेरम्यंपर्येतिपर्वतम् । नाम्नासङ्कोचनोनामनानानगयुतोगिरिः ।।6.26.27।। तत्रराज्यंप्रशास्त्येषकुमुदोनामयूथपः । योऽसौशतसहस्राणिसहस्रंपरिकर्षति ।।6.26.28।। यस्यवालाबहुव्यामादीर्घलाङ्गूलमाश्रिता । ताम्रापीतास्सीताश्श्वेताःप्रकीर्णाघोरदर्शना ।।6.26.29।। अदीनोरोषणश्चण्डस्सङ्ग्राममभिकाङ् क्षति । एषोऽप्याशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।।6.26.30।।

Such a Vanara called Kumuda is dragging hundred thousand Vanaras, some fastened and some scattered. He is one who has no pity and is frightening to look at. Single handed he is aspiring to crush Lanka with its army in war."

shloka_text: यस्त्वेषसिंहसङ्काशःकपिलोदीर्घलोचनः । निभृतःप्रेक्षतेलङ्कांदिधक्षन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.26.31।। विन्ध्यंकृष्णगिरिंसह्यंपर्वतंचसुदर्शनम् । राजन्सततमध्यास्तेरम्भोनामयूथपः ।।6.26.32।। शतंशतसहास्राणांत्रिंशच्चहरिपुङ्गवाः । यमेतेवानराश्शूराश्चण्डाश्चण्डपराक्रमाः ।।6.26.33।। परिवार्यानुगच्छन्तिलङ्कांमर्दितुमोजसा ।
explanation: "O king! He who is like a lion, of tawny colour with long hair, who is steady, who is looking at Lanka as though he is going to burn with his eyes, he who is followed by thirty hundred thousand Vanara warriors of dreadful form and terrific valour are marching to crush Lanka, is called Rambha the leader of the troop. He was always ruling over Vindhya, Krishnagiri and Sudarsanam mountains."

shloka_text: यस्तुकर्णौविवृणुतेजृम्बतेचपुनःपुनः । नचसंविजतेमृत्योर्नचयुद्धाद्विधावति ।।6.26.34।। प्रकम्पतेचरोषेणतिर्यक्चपुनरीक्षते । पश्यन् लाङ्गूलमपिचक्ष्वेळतेचमहाबलः ।।6.26.35।। महाजवोवीतभयोरम्यंसाल्वेयपर्वतम् । राजन्सततमध्यास्तेशरभोनामयूथपः ।।6.26.36।।
explanation: "Oh! king of Rakshasas! He who has made his ears stiff, yawning again and again, who is not afraid of death, who will not go back from war, who is looking obliquely and seeing his tail reacting in anger violently and roaring like a lion is a very strong leader called Sarabha. He is a very fast one, a leader of troops, ever in delight. He lives in Salveya mountain."

shloka_text: एतस्यबलिनस्सर्वेविहारानामयूथपाः । राजन् शतसहस्राणिचत्वारिंशस्तथैवच ।।6.26.37।।
explanation: "O King! Under him are forty lakhs of strong warriors known as Viharas."

shloka_text: यस्तुमेघइवाकाशंमहानावृत्यतिष्ठति । मध्येवानरवीराणांसूराणामिववासवः ।।6.26.38।। भेरीणामिवसन्नादोयस्यैषश्रूयतेमहान् । घोषश्शाखामृगेन्द्राणांसङ्ग्राममभिकाङ्क्षिताम् ।।6.26.39।। एषपर्वतमध्यास्तेपारियात्रमनुत्तमम् । युद्धेदुष्प्रसहोनित्यंपनसोनामयूथपः ।।6.26.40।।
explanation: "He who is huge like a cloud covering the sky, roaring like a lion making noise like the beating of the drums, who is eager to wage war, who stands amid Vanaras like Indra in the midst of suras, who is ever difficult to resist in war is known as Panasa is a great warrior. He resides in the Paariyatra mountains."

shloka_text: यस्तुमेघइवाकाशंमहानावृत्यतिष्ठति । मध्येवानरवीराणांसूराणामिववासवः ।।6.26.38।। भेरीणामिवसन्नादोयस्यैषश्रूयतेमहान् । घोषश्शाखामृगेन्द्राणांसङ्ग्राममभिकाङ्क्षिताम् ।।6.26.39।। एषपर्वतमध्यास्तेपारियात्रमनुत्तमम् । युद्धेदुष्प्रसहोनित्यंपनसोनामयूथपः ।।6.26.40।।

shloka_text: एनंशतसहस्राणांशतार्धंपर्युपासते । यूथपायूथपश्रेष्ठंयेषांयूथानिभागशः ।।6.26.41।।
explanation: "Fifty lakhs of best warriors are under him. They are in separate units."

shloka_text: यस्तुभीमांप्रवल्गन्तींचमूंतिष्ठतिशोभयन् । स्थितांतीरेसमुद्रस्यद्वितीयइवसागरः ।।6.26.42।। एषदर्दरसङ्काशोविनतोनामयूथपः । पिबंश्चरतिपर्णासांनदीनामुत्तमांनदीम् ।।6.26.43।। षष्टिश्शतसहस्राणिबलमस्यप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.26.44।।
explanation: "He who is stationed there on the shore like a second sea fluttering the division of army and terrifying is known as Vinata. He is a leader who goes about drinking the waters of the Parnasa, the best among the rivers. He has a sixty hundred thousand army force of Vanaras under him."

shloka_text: यस्तुभीमांप्रवल्गन्तींचमूंतिष्ठतिशोभयन् । स्थितांतीरेसमुद्रस्यद्वितीयइवसागरः ।।6.26.42।। एषदर्दरसङ्काशोविनतोनामयूथपः । पिबंश्चरतिपर्णासांनदीनामुत्तमांनदीम् ।।6.26.43।। षष्टिश्शतसहस्राणिबलमस्यप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.26.44।।

shloka_text: त्वामाह्वयतियुद्धायक्रोधनोनामयूधपः । विक्रान्ताबलवन्तश्चयथायूथानिभागशः ।।6.26.45।।
explanation: "The valiant and powerful troop leaders are a part of units of the army under Vanara called Krodhana. He is challenging you for combat."

shloka_text: यस्तुगैरिकवर्णाभंवपुःपुष्यतिवानरः । अवमत्यसदासर्वान्वानरान्बलदर्पितान् ।।6.26.46।। गवयोनामतेजस्वीत्वांक्रोधादभिवर्तते ।
explanation: "He who is of an orange colour body of hand some form, who nourishes it ever and who is proud of his strength, a glorious one known as Gava ya is coming towards you angrily with disregard for Vanaras."

shloka_text: एनंशतसहस्राणिसप्ततिःपर्युपासते । एषैवाशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।।6.26.47।।
explanation: "He has seventy lakhs under his command. Single handed with army force is aspiring to crush Lanka."

shloka_text: एतेदुष्प्रसहाघोराबलिनःकामरूपिणः । यूथपायूथपश्रेष्ठामेषांयूथानिभागशः ।।6.26.48।।
explanation: "They are difficult to resist, can change their form at will and are strong. These fierce troops, the best of the monkeys, have their units of army force." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषड्विंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तांस्तुतेऽहंप्रवक्ष्यामिप्रेक्षमाणस्ययूथपान् । राघवार्थेपराक्रान्तायेनरक्षन्तिजीवितम् ।।6.27.1।।
explanation: "I will describe the Vanara force, who are not caring for their lives for the cause of Raghava. You may see."

shloka_text: स्निग्धायस्यबहुव्यामावालालाङ्गूलमाश्रिताः । ताम्राःपीतास्सिताश्श्वेताःप्रकीर्णाघोरकर्मणः ।।6.27.2।। प्रगृहीताःप्रकाशन्तेसूर्यस्येवमरीचयः । पृथिव्यांचानुकृष्यन्तेहरोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.3।।
explanation: "One who is of terrific action, whose long tail with plenty of hair of different colours like red, white, yellow with shining ends shining like the scattered rays of the rising sun is holding and dragging on the ground is a leader known as Hara."

shloka_text: स्निग्धायस्यबहुव्यामावालालाङ्गूलमाश्रिताः । ताम्राःपीतास्सिताश्श्वेताःप्रकीर्णाघोरकर्मणः ।।6.27.2।। प्रगृहीताःप्रकाशन्तेसूर्यस्येवमरीचयः । पृथिव्यांचानुकृष्यन्तेहरोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.3।।
explanation: "One who is of terrific action, whose long tail with plenty of hair of different colours like red, white, yellow with shining ends shining like the scattered rays of the rising sun is holding and dragging on the ground is a leader known as Hara."

shloka_text: यंपृष्ठतोऽनुगच्छन्तिशतशोऽथसहस्रशः । द्रुमानुद्यम्यसहसालङ्कारोहणतत्पराः ।।6.27.4।। यूथपाहरिराजस्यकिङ्करास्समुपस्थिताः ।
explanation: "Standing in attention near Sugriva are hundreds and thousands of warriors holding huge trees aspiring to climb Lanka and controlling the Vanaras at the back prominently and following."

shloka_text: नीलानिवमहामेघांस्तिष्ठतोयांस्तुपश्यसि ।।6.27.5।। असिताञ्जनसङ्काशान् युद्धेसत्यपराक्रमान् । असङ् ख्येयाननिर्देश्यान्परंपारमिवोदधेः ।।6.27.6।। पर्वतेषुचयेकेचिद्विषमेषुनदीषुच । एतेत्वामभिवर्तन्तेराजन्नृक्षास्सुदारुणाः ।।6.27.7।।
explanation: "O King! Standing like dark clouds, black in colour like collyrium, who are of unfailing valour in war, innumerable in numbers, like the small particles of sand on the other bank of ocean, who cannot be counted are moving towards you. They are from mountains, riverbanks, and difficult locations. Those highly ferocious Bears are advancing towards you."

shloka_text: नीलानिवमहामेघांस्तिष्ठतोयांस्तुपश्यसि ।।6.27.5।। असिताञ्जनसङ्काशान् युद्धेसत्यपराक्रमान् । असङ् ख्येयाननिर्देश्यान्परंपारमिवोदधेः ।।6.27.6।। पर्वतेषुचयेकेचिद्विषमेषुनदीषुच । एतेत्वामभिवर्तन्तेराजन्नृक्षास्सुदारुणाः ।।6.27.7।।

shloka_text: एषांमध्येस्थितोराजन्भीमाक्षोभीमदर्शनः । पर्जन्यइवजीमूतैस्समन्तात्परिवारितः ।।6.27.8।। ऋक्षवन्तंगिरिश्रेष्ठमध्यास्तेनर्मदांपिबन् । सर्वऋक्षाणामधिपतिर्धूम्रोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.9।।
explanation: "O king! In the midst of these (Vanaras) stands one with frightening eyes and fearful looks, just like Parjanya (RainGod) is surrounded by clouds, is the Lord of all these Bears called Dhumra. He dwells at the great Rkshavana mountain drinking Narmada's (river) water."

shloka_text: एषांमध्येस्थितोराजन्भीमाक्षोभीमदर्शनः । पर्जन्यइवजीमूतैस्समन्तात्परिवारितः ।।6.27.8।। ऋक्षवन्तंगिरिश्रेष्ठमध्यास्तेनर्मदांपिबन् । सर्वऋक्षाणामधिपतिर्धूम्रोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.9।।

shloka_text: यवीयानस्यतुभ्रातापश्यैनंपर्वतोपमम् । भ्रात्रासमानोरूपेणविशिष्टस्तुपराक्रमैः ।।6.27.10।। सएषजाम्बवान्नाममहायूथपयूथपः । प्रक्रान्तोगुरुवर्तीचसम्प्रहारेष्वमर्षण ।।6.27.11।।
explanation: "See this one like a mountain, he is the brother of Dhumra. Even though he is similar to his brother in body form and his valour is great. As such he is superior among leaders. He is called Jambavan, one of valourous deeds, devoted to elders and intolerant in killing."

shloka_text: यवीयानस्यतुभ्रातापश्यैनंपर्वतोपमम् । भ्रात्रासमानोरूपेणविशिष्टस्तुपराक्रमैः ।।6.27.10।। सएषजाम्बवान्नाममहायूथपयूथपः । प्रक्रान्तोगुरुवर्तीचसम्प्रहारेष्वमर्षण ।।6.27.11।।

shloka_text: एतेनसाह्यंसुमहत्कृतंशक्रस्यधीमता । देवासुरेजाम्बवतालब्धाश्चबहवोवराः ।।6.27.12।।
explanation: "His assistance was given to Indra in the war between Devas and demons and in turn he obtained many boons."

shloka_text: आरुह्यपर्वताग्रेभ्योमहाभ्रविपुला: शिलाः । मुञ्चन्तिविपुलाकारानमृत्योरुद्विजन्तिच ।।6.27.13।। राक्षसानांचसदृशाःपिशाचानांचरोमशाः । एतस्यसैन्याबहवोविचरन्त्यग्नितेजसः ।।6.27.14।।
explanation: Appearing with hairybody glowing like fire like the Rakshasas and demons, many of them in huge form are climbing mountain peaks without caring for death and go about throwing rocks.

shloka_text: आरुह्यपर्वताग्रेभ्योमहाभ्रविपुला: शिलाः । मुञ्चन्तिविपुलाकारानमृत्योरुद्विजन्तिच ।।6.27.13।। राक्षसानांचसदृशाःपिशाचानांचरोमशाः । एतस्यसैन्याबहवोविचरन्त्यग्नितेजसः ।।6.27.14।।
explanation: Appearing with hairybody glowing like fire like the Rakshasas and demons, many of them in huge form are climbing mountain peaks without caring for death and go about throwing rocks.

shloka_text: यंत्वेनमभिसम्रब्धंप्लवमानमिवस्थितम् । प्रेक्षन्तेवानरास्सर्वेस्थितायूथपयूथपम् ।।6.27.15।। एषराजन् सहस्राक्षंपर्युपास्तेहरीश्वरः । बलेनबलसम्पन्नोदम्भोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.16।।
explanation: "O king! This Lord of monkeys, whom whether he is jumping like monkeys or standing is the leader of the leaders, whom the monkeys are looking at standing is called Dhamba, a mighty powerful, fearsome leader and Lord of monkeys. He is surrounded by a strong army like the thousand eyed Indra."

shloka_text: यंत्वेनमभिसम्रब्धंप्लवमानमिवस्थितम् । प्रेक्षन्तेवानरास्सर्वेस्थितायूथपयूथपम् ।।6.27.15।। एषराजन् सहस्राक्षंपर्युपास्तेहरीश्वरः । बलेनबलसम्पन्नोदम्भोनामैषयूथपः ।।6.27.16।।
explanation: "O king! This Lord of monkeys, whom whether he is jumping like monkeys or standing is the leader of the leaders, whom the monkeys are looking at standing is called Dhamba, a mighty powerful, fearsome leader and Lord of monkeys. He is surrounded by a strong army like the thousand eyed Indra."

shloka_text: यःस्थितंयोजनेशैलंगच्छन्पार्श्वेनसेवते । ऊर्ध्वंतथैवकायेनगतःप्राप्नोतियोजनम् ।।6.27.17।। यस्मान्नपरमंरूपंचतुष्पादेषुविद्यते । श्रुतस्संन्नादनोनामवानराणांपितामहाः ।।6.27.18।। येनयुद्धंपुरादत्तंरणेशक्रस्यधीमता । पराजयश्चनप्राप्तस्सोऽयंयूथपयूथपः ।।6.27.19।।
explanation: "He who stands at one yojana touches a mountain with his flanks, so also gets up and reaches a yojana height with his body, is Sannadana. He is the grandfather of Vanaras. There is no one who has a bigger body size than him among the four legged ones. He had fought war with Indra and is well known for not losing in the battle."

shloka_text: यःस्थितंयोजनेशैलंगच्छन्पार्श्वेनसेवते । ऊर्ध्वंतथैवकायेनगतःप्राप्नोतियोजनम् ।।6.27.17।। यस्मान्नपरमंरूपंचतुष्पादेषुविद्यते । श्रुतस्संन्नादनोनामवानराणांपितामहाः ।।6.27.18।। येनयुद्धंपुरादत्तंरणेशक्रस्यधीमता । पराजयश्चनप्राप्तस्सोऽयंयूथपयूथपः ।।6.27.19।।

shloka_text: यस्यविक्रममाणस्यशक्रस्येवपराक्रमः । एषगन्धर्वकन्यायामुत्पन्नःकृष्णवर्त्मनः ।।6.27.20।। तदादेवासुरेयुद्धेसाह्यार्थंत्रिदिवौकसाम्
explanation: "His valour is equal to that of Indra. He is born to Gandharva, a maiden of the god of fire. He was created for the sake of assisting gods in the war between gods and demons."

shloka_text: यस्यवैश्रवणोराजाजम्बूमुपनिषेवते ।।6.27.21।। योराजापर्वतेन्द्राणांबहुकिन्नरसेविनाम् । विहारसुखदोनित्यंभ्रातुस्तेराक्षसाधिप ।।6.27.22।। तत्रैषवसतिश्रीमान्बलवान्वानरर्षभः । युद्धेष्वकत्थनोनित्यंक्रोधनोनामयूथपः ।।6.27.23।।
explanation: "O King of Rakshasas! This Vanara who is exceptional among Vanaras, a commander of troops by name Krathana, who is not boastful in wars, lives on Kailas, the king of mountains which is frequented by many Kinnaras, on which your brother king Kubera son of Vysravana stays under Jambu tree and strolls for his pleasure."

shloka_text: यस्यवैश्रवणोराजाजम्बूमुपनिषेवते ।।6.27.21।। योराजापर्वतेन्द्राणांबहुकिन्नरसेविनाम् । विहारसुखदोनित्यंभ्रातुस्तेराक्षसाधिप ।।6.27.22।। तत्रैषवसतिश्रीमान्बलवान्वानरर्षभः । युद्धेष्वकत्थनोनित्यंक्रोधनोनामयूथपः ।।6.27.23।।

shloka_text: वृतःकोटिसहस्रेणहरीणांसमुपस्थितः । एषैवाशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।।6.27.24।।
explanation: "He is surrounded with thousand crores of his Vanara force and with his own force he intends to crush Lanka."

shloka_text: योगङ्गामनुपर्येतित्रासयन्गजयूथपान् । हस्तिनांवानराणांचपूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् ।।6.27.25।। एषयूथपतिर्नेतागच्छन् गिरिगुहाशयः । गजान्योधयतेवन्यान्गिरींश्चैवमहीरुहान् ।।6.27.26।।
explanation: "There is one who roams around Ganga, frightening herds of elephants, remembering the earlier enmity between elephants and Vanaras. This leader of commanders goes about mountain caves, trees and mountains waging war with elephants."

shloka_text: योगङ्गामनुपर्येतित्रासयन्गजयूथपान् । हस्तिनांवानराणांचपूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् ।।6.27.25।। एषयूथपतिर्नेतागच्छन् गिरिगुहाशयः । गजान्योधयतेवन्यान्गिरींश्चैवमहीरुहान् ।।6.27.26।।
explanation: "There is one who roams around Ganga, frightening herds of elephants, remembering the earlier enmity between elephants and Vanaras. This leader of commanders goes about mountain caves, trees and mountains waging war with elephants."

shloka_text: हरीणांवाहिनीमुख्योनदींहैमवतीमनु । उशीरबीजमाश्रित्यपर्वतंमन्दरोपमम् ।।6.27.27।। रमतेवानरश्रेष्ठोदिविशक्रइवस्वयम् ।
explanation: "The chief of the army of monkeys and the excellent one among Vanaras revels on the mountain Usirabeejam like the mountain Mandara on the bank of river Hymavathi just as Indra in heaven."

shloka_text: एनंशतसहस्राणांसहस्रमनुवर्तते । वीर्यविक्रमदृप्तानांनर्दतांबलशालिनाम् ।।6.27.28।।
explanation: "Thousand lakhs of mighty strong Vanaras who are proud of their valour and prowess roaring like lions follow him."

shloka_text: सएषनेताचैतेषांवानराणांमहात्मनाम् । सएषदुर्धरोराजन्प्रमाथीनामयूथपः ।।6.27.29।।
explanation: "He alone is the leader of the great Vanaras, O king. He is called Pramathi, a commander and a difficult one to resist."

shloka_text: वातेनेवोद्धतंमेघंयमेनमनुपश्यसि । अनीकमभिसंरब्धंवानराणांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.27.30।। उद्दूतमरुणाभासंपवनेनसमन्ततः । विवर्तमानंबहुधायत्रैतद्बहुळंरजः ।।6.27.31।।
explanation: "You see him (Pramathi) who resembles a cloud risen up by the wind you may also see the reddish brown dust particles lifted up by excessive whirling of the wind all over and also the furious Vanara army moving swiftly."

shloka_text: वातेनेवोद्धतंमेघंयमेनमनुपश्यसि । अनीकमभिसंरब्धंवानराणांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.27.30।। उद्दूतमरुणाभासंपवनेनसमन्ततः । विवर्तमानंबहुधायत्रैतद्बहुळंरजः ।।6.27.31।।
explanation: "You see him (Pramathi) who resembles a cloud risen up by the wind you may also see the reddish brown dust particles lifted up by excessive whirling of the wind all over and also the furious Vanara army moving swiftly."

shloka_text: एतेऽसितमुखाघोरागोलाङ्गूलामहाबलाः । शतंशतहस्राणिदृष्ट्वावैसेतुबन्धनम् ।।6.27.32।। गोलाङ्गूलंमहावेगंगवाक्षंनामयूधपम् । परिवार्याभिवर्तन्तेलङ्कांमर्दितुमोजसा ।।6.27.33।।
explanation: "These hundred and hundred thousand black monkeys with a tail like that of a cow called Golangulas, endowed with black coloured face, fearsome and with extraordinary strength, watching the bridge constructed, surround Gavaksha the leader, who himself is a Golangula and of great speed. They intend to demolish Lanka with their vigour."

shloka_text: एतेऽसितमुखाघोरागोलाङ्गूलामहाबलाः । शतंशतहस्राणिदृष्ट्वावैसेतुबन्धनम् ।।6.27.32।। गोलाङ्गूलंमहावेगंगवाक्षंनामयूधपम् । परिवार्याभिवर्तन्तेलङ्कांमर्दितुमोजसा ।।6.27.33।।
explanation: "These hundred and hundred thousand black monkeys with a tail like that of a cow called Golangulas, endowed with black coloured face, fearsome and with extraordinary strength, watching the bridge constructed, surround Gavaksha the leader, who himself is a Golangula and of great speed. shloka_text: भ्रमराचरितायत्रसर्वकालफलद्रुमाः ।।6.27.34।। यंसूर्यस्तुल्यपर्णाभमनुपर्येतिपर्वतम् । यस्यभासासदाभान्तितद्वर्णामृगपक्षिणः ।।6.27.35।। यस्यप्रस्थंमहात्मानोनत्यजन्तिमहर्षयः । सर्वकालफलावृक्षास्सदाफलसमन्विताः ।।6.27.36।। मधूनिचमहार्हाणियस्मिन्पर्वतसत्तमे । तत्रैवरमतेराजन्रम्येकाञ्चनपर्वते ।।6.27.37।। मुख्योवानरमुख्यानांकेसरीनामयूथपः ।
explanation: "O king! Where the trees give fruit in all seasons which is inhabited by honeybees, whose leaves shine similar to that of Sunshine, where birds animals and all ever shining in golden colour of the Sun, where sages and great souls reside without leaving where trees always yield tasty fruits and have valuable honey in such a delightful golden mountain Vanara leader named Kesari, the chief of all chief Vanaras revels."

shloka_text: षष्टिर्गिरिसहस्राणांरम्याःकाञ्चनपर्वता ।।6.27.38।। तेषांमध्येगिरिवरस्त्वमिवानघरक्षसाम् । तत्रैतेकपिलाश्श्वेतास्ताम्रास्यामधुपिङ्गलाः ।।6.27.39।। निवसन्त्युत्तमगिरौतीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रानखायुधाः । सिंहाइवचतुर्दंष्ट्राव्याघ्राइवदुरासदाः ।।6.27.40।। सर्वेवैश्वानरसमाज्वलिताशीविषोपमाः । सुदीर्घाञ्चितलाङ्गूलामत्तमातङ्गसन्निभाः ।।6.27.41।। महापर्वतसङ्काशामहाजीमूतनिस्स्वनाः । वृत्तपिङ्गलरक्ताक्षाभीमाभीमगतिस्वराः ।।6.27.42।। मर्दयन्तीवतेसर्वेतस्थुर्लङकासमीक्ष्यते ।
explanation: "O sinless king! there are sixty thousand golden mountains. In the midst of them is this golden mountain just as you are in the midst of the Rakshasas. On the last mountain the Vanaras with brown coloured face, white face, coppery red face and yellow face like honey with sharp teeth like lions, who have nails as weapons, four toothed ones like lions, fearsome ones like tiger, dangerous to approach, all of them like serpents with flaming venomous tongues, with long uplifted tails, like huge elephants in rut in mountain size, roaring like lions, thundering clouds, with round brownish red eyed ones, fearful while walking and causing appalling uproar all of them dwell on the last mountain. They are watching to demolish your Lanka as they look at it."

shloka_text: एषचैषामधिपतिर्मध्येतिष्ठतिवीर्यवान् ।।6.27.43।। जयार्थीनित्यमादित्यमुपतिष्ठतिबुद्धिमान् । नाम्नापृथिव्यांविख्यातोराजन् शतबलीतियः ।।6.27.44।। एषैवाशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।
explanation: "O king! He who is known as Satabali, is a famous one on the earth, is a valiant hero, a leader. He stands in the middle aspiring for victory ever worshipping Sun. He alone with his army is intending to demolish Lanka."

shloka_text: एषचैषामधिपतिर्मध्येतिष्ठतिवीर्यवान् ।।6.27.43।। जयार्थीनित्यमादित्यमुपतिष्ठतिबुद्धिमान् । नाम्नापृथिव्यांविख्यातोराजन् शतबलीतियः ।।6.27.44।। एषैवाशंसतेलङ्कांस्वेनानीकेनमर्दितुम् ।
explanation: "O king! He who is known as Satabali, is a famous one on the earth, is a valiant hero, a leader. He stands in the middle aspiring for victory ever worshipping Sun. He alone with his army is intending to demolish Lanka."

shloka_text: विक्रान्तोबलवान् शूरःपौरुषेस्वेव्यवस्थितः । रामप्रियार्थंप्राणानांदयांनकुरुतेहरिः ।।6.27.45।।
explanation: "He is indomitable, strong and heroic. He will not give up his virility. For the pleasure of Rama, he will not feel pity for his life (he will give up his life)."

shloka_text: गजोगवाक्षोगवयोनलोनीलश्चवानरः । एकैकएवयोधानांकोटीभिर्दशभिर्वृतः ।।6.27.46।।
explanation: "Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Nila each of these Vanara leaders have ten crores of army under them."

shloka_text: तथाऽऽन्येवानरश्रेष्ठाविन्ध्यपर्वतवासिनः । नशक्यन्तेबहुत्वात्तुसङ् ख्यातुंलघुविक्रमाः ।।6.27.47।।
explanation: "So also, those best of Vanaras of many kinds residing in Vindhya mountain of great valour in large numbers is impossible to count."

shloka_text: सर्वेमहाराजमहाप्रभावास्सर्वेमहाशैलनिकाशकायाः । सर्वेसमर्थापृथिवींक्षणेनकर्तुंप्रविध्वस्तविकीर्णशैलाम् ।।6.27.48।।
explanation: "O, Monarch! All of them are highly prominent, their stature equal to high hills and all of them are capable of levelling the earth by uprooting and razing its mountains to the ground in a moment." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेसप्तविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty seventh sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: साराणस्यवचश्श्रुत्वारावणंराक्षसाधिपम् । बलमादिश्यतत्सर्वंशुकोवाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।।6.28.1।।
explanation: Then Ravana the king of Rakshasas having heard Saarana's words and described the strength (of Vanaras) Suka spoke these words.

shloka_text: स्थितान्पश्यसियानेतान्मत्तानिवमहाद्विपान् । न्यग्रोधानिवगाङ्गेयान् सालान् हैमवतानिव ।।6.28.2।। एतेदुष्प्रसहाराजन्बलिनःकामरूपिणः । दैत्यदानवसङ्काशायुद्धेदेवपराक्रमाः ।।6.28.3।।
explanation: "O King! like a banyan tree on the island, like Sala trees on the Himalayan Mountain these people are stationed. You may see them marching. They are strong to encounter, can change form at their free will. They look like gods and Danavas in war and have the valour of gods."

shloka_text: स्थितान्पश्यसियानेतान्मत्तानिवमहाद्विपान् । न्यग्रोधानिवगाङ्गेयान् सालान् हैमवतानिव ।।6.28.2।। एतेदुष्प्रसहाराजन्बलिनःकामरूपिणः । दैत्यदानवसङ्काशायुद्धेदेवपराक्रमाः ।।6.28.3।।

shloka_text: एषांकोटिसहस्राणिनवपञ्चचसप्तच । तथाशङ्खुसहस्राणितथाबृन्दशतानिच ।।6.28.4।।
explanation: "These Vanaras are nine, five and seven thousand crores in number. They are in many thousands of Sankhas and Vrindas."

shloka_text: एतेसुग्रीवसचिवाःकिष्किन्धानिलयास्सदा । हरयोदेवगन्धर्वैरुत्पन्नाःकामरूपिणः ।।6.28.5।।
explanation: "These are allies of Sugriva ever residing at Kishkinda. They are born to celestial gods and Gandharvas and can change their form at their will."

shloka_text: यौतौपश्यसितिष्ठन्तौकुमारौदेवरूपिणौ । मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौताभ्यांनास्तिसमोयुधि ।।6.28.6।।
explanation: "Do you see two of them standing there? They are young and have the form of gods. They are Mainda and Dwivida. Both of them are similar in war and none equal them in war."

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणासममज्ञातावमृतप्राशिनापुभौ । आशंसेतेयुथालङ्कामेतौमर्दितुमोजसा ।।6.28.7।।
explanation: "They drank the nectar of immortality with the permission of Brahma. These leaders are aspiring to destroy Lanka by their prowess."

shloka_text: यंतुपश्यसितिष्टन्तंप्रभिन्नमिवकुञ्जरम् । योबलात् क्षोभयेत् क्रुद्धस्समुद्रमपिवानरः ।।6.28.8।। एषोऽभिगन्तालङ्कायावैदेह्यास्तवचप्रभो: । एनंपश्यपुरादृष्टंवानरंपुनरागतम् ।।6.28.9।।
explanation: "O Lord! You may see the one standing there like an elephant who can churn up the sea when he is angry. He has come to Lanka earlier, seen Sita and gone back. You may see that he has come again."

shloka_text: यंतुपश्यसितिष्टन्तंप्रभिन्नमिवकुञ्जरम् । योबलात् क्षोभयेत् क्रुद्धस्समुद्रमपिवानरः ।।6.28.8।। एषोऽभिगन्तालङ्कायावैदेह्यास्तवचप्रभो: । एनंपश्यपुरादृष्टंवानरंपुनरागतम् ।।6.28.9।।
explanation: "O Lord! You may see the one standing there like an elephant who can churn up the sea when he is angry. He has come to Lanka earlier, seen Sita and gone back. You may see that he has come again."

shloka_text: ज्येष्ठःकेसरिणःपुत्त्रोवातात्मजइतिश्रुतः । हनूमानितिविख्यातोलङ्घितोयेनसागरः ।।6.28.10।।
explanation: "He is the eldest son born of Kesari and the son of WindGod and is popularly known as Hanuman. He leapt over the sea and came."

shloka_text: कामरूपीहरिश्रेष्टोबलरूपसमन्वितः । अनिवार्यगतिश्चैवयथासततगःप्रभुः ।।6.28.11।।
explanation: "He is a jewel among Vanaras. He can change his form at his will. He is endowed with physical strength and charm. Being existent everywhere like windgod his cause cannot be prevented like that of wind god."

shloka_text: उद्यन्तभास्करंदृष्टवाबालःकिलपिपासितः । त्रियोजनसहस्रंतुअध्वानमवतीर्यहि ।।6.28.12।। आदित्यमाहरिष्यामिनमेक्षुत्प्रतियास्यति । इतिसञ्चिन्त्यमनसापुरैषबलदर्पितः ।।6.28.13।।
explanation: When he was a child, on seeing the rising Sun, he travelled three thousand yojanas and said, "I will eat up the Sun otherwise I will not be appeased', being proud of his strength."

shloka_text: उद्यन्तभास्करंदृष्टवाबालःकिलपिपासितः । त्रियोजनसहस्रंतुअध्वानमवतीर्यहि ।।6.28.12।। आदित्यमाहरिष्यामिनमेक्षुत्प्रतियास्यति । इतिसञ्चिन्त्यमनसापुरैषबलदर्पितः ।।6.28.13।।
explanation: When he was a child, on seeing the rising Sun, he travelled three thousand yojanas and said, "I will eat up the Sun otherwise I will not be appeased', being proud of his strength."

shloka_text: अनाधृष्यतमंदेवमपिदेवर्षिदानवैः । अनासाघैवपतितोभास्करोदयनेगिरौ ।।6.28.14।।
explanation: "Unassailable even for gods, sages and Danavas to reach the Sun god, he fell down near the eastern part."

shloka_text: पतितस्यकपेरस्यहनुरेकाशिलातले । किञ्चिद्भिन्नादृढहनोर्हनूमानेषतेनवै ।।6.28.15।।
explanation: "By falling on the mountain one of the jaws of the monkey got broken. This is the reason that he is known as Hanuman."

shloka_text: सत्यमागमयोगेनममैषविदितोहरिः । नास्यशक्यंबलंरूपंप्रभावोवाऽपिभाषितम् ।।6.28.16।।
explanation: "I came to know about him through one of my contacts. His strength, his appearance and glory are indescribable."

shloka_text: एषआशंसतेलङ्कामेकोमर्दितुमोजसा । येवजाज्वल्यतेऽपौवैधूमकेतुस्तवाद्यवै ।।6.28.17।। लङ्कायांनिहितश्चापिकथंविस्मरसेकपिम् ।
explanation: "This monkey is intending to demolish this Lanka single handed. How can you forget about (the task of) setting his tail on fire entrusted by you to Dhoomakethu?"

shloka_text: यश्चैषोऽनन्तरश्शूरश्श्यामःपद्मनिभेक्षणः । इक्ष्वाकूणामतिरथोलोकेविख्यातपौरुष ।।6.28.18।। यस्मिन्नचलतेधर्मोयोधर्मंनातिवर्तते । योब्राह्ममस्त्रंवेदांश्चवेदवेदविदांवरः ।।6.28.19।। योभिन्द्याद्गगनंबाणैःपर्वतांश्चापिदारयेत् । यस्यमृत्योरिवक्रोधश्शक्रस्येवपराक्रमः ।।6.28.20।। यस्यभार्याजनस्थानात्सीताचापिहृतात्वया । सएषरामस्त्वांयोद्धुंराजन्समभिवर्तते ।।6.28.21।।
explanation: "O king! the king who is not distant from him, a dark complexioned, one with lotus eyes who never transgresses his righteousness, who is a great charioteer of Ikshvaku race who knows use of Vedas, who is choicest, who knows the weapons presided over by Brahma whose arrows can pierce through the sky and even mountains whose anger is like anger of death, whose valour is like that of Indra whose consort has been borne away from Janasthana is Rama. He is advancing towards you to wage war with you."

shloka_text: यस्यैषदक्षिणेपार्श्वेशुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभः । विशालवक्षास्ताम्राक्षोनीलकुञ्जितमूर्धजः ।।6.28.22।। एषोऽस्यलक्ष्मणोनामभ्राताप्राणसमःप्रियः । नयेयुद्धेचकुशलस्सर्वशस्त्रभृतंवरः ।।6.28.23।।
explanation: "To his right is his brother known as Lakshmana whose body radiates like gold, he has broad chest, red eyes, dark curly hair. He is as dear as his life to Rama. He is skilled in moral science and warfare. He is the foremost and the best among wielders of weapons."

shloka_text: यस्यैषदक्षिणेपार्श्वेशुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभः । विशालवक्षास्ताम्राक्षोनीलकुञ्जितमूर्धजः ।।6.28.22।। एषोऽस्यलक्ष्मणोनामभ्राताप्राणसमःप्रियः । नयेयुद्धेचकुशलस्सर्वशस्त्रभृतंवरः ।।6.28.23।।

shloka_text: अमर्षीदुर्जयोजेताविक्रान्तोबुद्धिमान् बली । रामस्यदक्षिणोबाहुर्नित्यंप्राणोबहिश्चरः ।।6.28.24।।
explanation: "He is one who does not forgive (Rama's enemies), difficult to win, indomitable, victorious, strong and wise one. He is the right hand of Rama and external breath of his life."

shloka_text: नह्येषराघवस्यार्थेजीवितंपरिरक्षति । एषैवाशंसतेयुद्धेनिहन्तुंसर्वराक्षसान् ।।6.28.25।।
explanation: "For the cause of Rama, he will spare his life. He too is intent upon destroying all Rakshasas."

shloka_text: यस्तुसव्यमसौपक्षंरामस्याश्रित्यतिष्ठति । रक्षोगणपरिक्षिप्तोराजाह्येषविभीषणः ।।6.28.26।।
explanation: "The one who is near Rama's left who sought Rama's refuge and stands surrounded by Rakshasas and protected is the king Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: श्रीमताराजराजेनलङ्कायामभिषेचितः । त्वामेवप्रतिसंरब्दोयुद्धायैषोऽभिवर्तते ।।6.28.27।।
explanation: "He is a prosperous king of the kings of Lanka. He has been consecrated by Rama, filled with anger he is advancing to wage war with you."

shloka_text: यंतुपस्यसितिष्ठन्तंमध्येगिरिमिवाचलम् । सर्वशाखामृगेन्द्राणांभर्तारममितौजसम् ।।6.28.28।। तेजयशसाबुद् ध्याज्ञानेनाभिजनेनच । यःकपीनतिबभ्राजहिमवानिवपर्वतान् ।।6.28.29।। किष्किन्धांयस्समध्यास्तेगुहांसगहनद्रुमाम् । दुर्गांपर्वतदुर्गस्तांप्रधानैस्सहयूथपैः ।।6.28.30।। यस्यैषाकाञ्चनीमालाशोभितेशतपुष्करा । कान्तादेवमनुष्याणांयस्यांलक्ष्मीप्रतिष्ठिता ।।6.28.31।। एतांचमालांतारांचकपिराज्यंचशाश्वतम् । सुग्रीवोवालिनंहत्वारामेणप्रतिपादितः ।।6.28.32।।
explanation: "The one whom you see standing in the midst is the king of all chiefs of the Vanara army, a highly glorious one, steady like a mountain. like Himalayas that outshines all mountains, he surpasses all in fame, in intellect, in wisdom and in lineage. That monkey chief resides in the mountain cave fort with thickly grown trees around in the middle of Kishkinda, which is difficult to access, and is surrounded by his army chiefs. See the golden chain on him shining away with hundred lotuses in which stands Lakshmi installed which is difficult even for gods and human beings to covet. In the same way as the golden chain, even his beloved Tara and kingdom of the monkeys was permanently bestowed upon him by Rama after slaying Vali."

explanation: "It is said by wise men that hundred thousand crores multiplied by hundred thousand crores as Sankha."

explanation: A lakh of Sanku is known as Maha Sanku. A lakh of Maha Shanka is spoken as Vrinda. A lakh of Vrindas is spoken as Maha Brinda. A lakh of Maha Vrindas is known as Padma. One lakh Padmas is known as Maha Padma and a lakh of Maha Padmas is known as Kharva. A lakh of Kharvas is known as Maha Kharva and a lakh of Maha Kharvas is known as a Samudra. A lakh of Samudras is known as an Ogha. A lakh of Oghas is popularly known as Maha Ogha.

shloka_text: इमांमहाराजसमीक्ष्यवाहिनीमुपस्थितांप्रज्वलितग्रहोपमाम् । ततःप्रयत्नःपरमोविधीयतांयथाजयस्स्यान्नपरैःपराजयः ।।6.28.44।।
explanation: "O Great King! Observing the ocean of army close by their appearing cruel like a blazing planet, make supreme efforts to be victorious and not to be defeated in the hands of the enemy." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेअष्टाविंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the twenty eighth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: शुकेनतुसमाख्यातान्दृष्ट्वासहरियूथपान् । समीपस्थंचरामस्यभ्रातरंस्वंविभीषणम् ।।6.29.1।। लक्ष्मणंचमहावीर्यंभुजंरामस्यदक्षिणं । सर्ववानरराजंचसुग्रीवंभीमविक्रमम् ।।6.29.2।। अङ्गदंचापिबलिनंवज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजम् । हनूमन्तंचविक्रान्तंजाम्बवन्तंचदुर्जयम् ।।6.29.3।। सुषेणंकुमुदंनीलंनलंचप्लवगर्षभम् । गजंगवाक्षंशरभंमैन्दंचद्विविदंतथा ।।6.29.4।। किञ्चिदाविग्नहृदयोजातक्रोधश्चरावणः । भर्त्सयामासतौवीरौकथान्तेशुकसारणौ ।।6.29.5।।
explanation: There after Ravana having heard the words spoken by Suka about the army of Vanara heroes, seeing Lakshmana of extraordinary valour, the right shoulder of Rama standing close by Rama his own brother Vibheeshana close by  the king of Vanaras, Sugriva of fierce valour and Angada the son of Vali (the son of Indra who wields thunderbolt)  and valiant Hanuman Jambavan who is difficult to conquer Sushena, Nila, Kumuda, bull among the leaping animals Nala likewise Gaja, Gavaksha, Sarabha, Mainda and Dwivida got a little broken hearted and mixed with fury started to rebuke both the heroes Suka and Saarana.

shloka_text: शुकेनतुसमाख्यातान्दृष्ट्वासहरियूथपान् । समीपस्थंचरामस्यभ्रातरंस्वंविभीषणम् ।।6.29.1।। लक्ष्मणंचमहावीर्यंभुजंरामस्यदक्षिणं । सर्ववानरराजंचसुग्रीवंभीमविक्रमम् ।।6.29.2।। अङ्गदंचापिबलिनंवज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजम् । हनूमन्तंचविक्रान्तंजाम्बवन्तंचदुर्जयम् ।।6.29.3।। सुषेणंकुमुदंनीलंनलंचप्लवगर्षभम् । गजंगवाक्षंशरभंमैन्दंचद्विविदंतथा ।।6.29.4।। किञ्चिदाविग्नहृदयोजातक्रोधश्चरावणः । भर्त्सयामासतौवीरौकथान्तेशुकसारणौ ।।6.29.5।।

shloka_text: अधोमुखौतौप्रणतावब्रवीच्छुकसारणौ । रोषगद्गदयावाचासंरब्धंपरुषंवचः ।।6.29.6।।
explanation: (That Ravana) with his throat choked with anger spoke indignantly and harshly to both Suka and Saarana who stood with their heads bent down in supplication.

shloka_text: नतावत्सदृशंनामसचिवैरुपजीविभिः । विप्रियंनृपतेर्वक्तुंनिग्रहेप्रग्रहेप्रभोः ।।6.29.7।।
explanation: "It is not proper for those ministers dependent on a capable ruler who has the power to check and hold forth, to speak that which is unpleasant."

shloka_text: रिपूणांप्रतिकूलानांयुद्धार्थमभिवर्तताम् । उभाभ्यांसदृशंनामवक्तुमप्रस्तवेस्तवम् ।।6.29.8।।
explanation: "Is it appropriate for both of you to praise the enemy this way before war?"

shloka_text: आचार्यागुरवोवृद्धावृथावांपर्युपासिताः । सारंयद्राजशास्त्राणामनुजीव्यंनगृह्यते ।।6.29.9।।
explanation: "You have not grasped that which is the essence of political wisdom in the sastras in spite of waiting upon elders, teachers and parents which was in vain."

shloka_text: गृहीतोवानविज्ञातोभारोऽज्ञानस्यवाह्यते । ईदृशै: सचिवैर्युक्तोमूर्खैर्दिष्ट्यधराम्यहम् ।।6.29.10।।
explanation: "Even if you have grasped you have not understood the meaning or out of intensity of your ignorance. Or else I am bearing foolish ones like you who are not fit to be ministers. Out of good luck I am ruling this sovereignty."

shloka_text: किंनुमृत्योर्भयंनास्तिवक्तुंमांपरुषंवचः । यस्यमेशासतोजिह्वाप्रयच्छतिशुभाशुभम् ।।6.29.11।।
explanation: "Did you not have fear of death when you spoke such harsh words to me, who can by mere order make good or evil to you?"

shloka_text: अप्येवदहनंस्पृष्टवावनेतिष्ठन्तिपादपाः । राजदोषपरामृष्टास्तिष्ठन्तेनापराधिनः ।।6.29.12।।
explanation: "Trees may remain unscathed even on touching forest fire, but those who are punishable do not remain unpunished on account of the king and are treated harshly."

shloka_text: हन्यामहंत्विमौपापौशत्रुपक्षप्रशंसकौ । यदिपूर्वोपकारैस्तुनक्रोधोमृदुतांव्रजेत् ।।6.29.13।।
explanation: "I would have slayed these two sinners who praise the enemy side, if my anger had not softened and remembered their earlier services."

shloka_text: अपध्वंसतगच्छध्वंसन्निकर्षाद्इतोमम । नहिवांहन्तुमिच्छामिस्मराम्युपकृतानिवाम् ।।6.29.14।। हतावेवकृतघ्नौतौमयिस्नेहपराङ्मुखौ ।
explanation: "You get away from here, disappear from here. On the contrary since I remember your earlier actions performed by you, I do not wish to kill you. Indeed, both of you are devoid of love and are ungrateful. You stand killed (already)."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तौतुसव्रीळौतावुभौशुकसारणौ । रावणंजयशब्देनप्रतिनन्द्याभिनिस्सृतौ ।।6.29.15।।
explanation: Ravana, having spoken that way, both Suka and Saarana felt shy and withdrew from speaking words of praise of Ravana saying, 'Let you be victorious'.

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्सदशग्रीव: समीपस्थंमहोदरम् । उपस्तापयमेशीघ्रंचारान्नीतिविशारदान् ।।6.29.16।।
explanation: Ravana, the tenheaded one, then said to Mahodara who was standing nearby swiftly bring spies who are experts in policy to me.

shloka_text: महोदरस्तथोक्तस्तुशीघ्रमाज्ञापयच्चरान् ।।6.29.17।। ततश्चारास्संत्वरिताःप्राप्ताःपार्थिवशासनात् । उपस्थिताःप्राञ्जलयोवर्धयित्वाजयशिषाः ।।6.29.18।।
explanation: (Ravana) Having said so, Mahodara ordered the spies to approach the king quickly. On reaching they greeted the king with folded hand s promoting h i m to' be victorious' and stood.

shloka_text: महोदरस्तथोक्तस्तुशीघ्रमाज्ञापयच्चरान् ।।6.29.17।। ततश्चारास्संत्वरिताःप्राप्ताःपार्थिवशासनात् । उपस्थिताःप्राञ्जलयोवर्धयित्वाजयशिषाः ।।6.29.18।।
explanation: (Ravana) Having said so, Mahodara ordered the spies to approach the king quickly. On reaching they greeted the king with folded hand s promoting h i m to' be victorious' and stood.

shloka_text: तानब्रवीत्ततोवाक्यंरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । चारान्प्रत्यायितान् शूरान्भक्तान्विगतसाध्वसान् ।।6.29.19।।
explanation: There upon the Lord of Rakshasas, spoke these words to those spies who are dependable ones, warriors devoid of fear of enemies.

shloka_text: इतोगच्छतरामस्यव्यवसायंपरीक्षथ । मन्त्रिष्वभ्यन्तरायेऽस्यप्रीत्यातेनसमागताः ।।6.29.20।।
explanation: "From here you go and reach there you may observe perceptions of Rama and of others close to him, his ministers and those who have reached there in affection to him."

shloka_text: कथंस्वपितिजागर्तिकिमन्यच्चकरिष्यति । विज्ञायनिपुणंसर्वमागन्तव्यमशेषतः ।।6.29.21।।
explanation: "You may see how he goes to sleep, how he wakes up etc., what he does, everything. You may come after knowing everything."

shloka_text: चारेणविदितश्शत्रुःपण्डितैर्वसुधाधिपैः । युद्धेस्वल्पेनयत्नेनसमासाद्यनिरस्यते ।।6.29.22।।
explanation: "Wise kings of the land, having known about enemies from the spies destroy enemies in war with little effort."

shloka_text: चारास्तुतेतथेत्युक्त्वाप्रहृष्टाराक्षसेश्वरम् । शार्दूलमग्रतःकृत्वाततश्चक्रुःप्रदक्षिणम् ।।6.29.23।।
explanation: The spies then gladly uttered the words 'be it so', went round the king in reverence and departed with Saardula leading in front.

shloka_text: ततस्तेतंमहात्मानंचाराराक्षससत्तमम् । कृत्वाप्रदक्षिणंजग्मुर्यत्ररामस्सलक्ष्मणः ।।6.29.24।।
explanation: Then the spies circumambulated the great Rakshasa king and having done so went to the place where Rama and Lakshmana were stationed.

shloka_text: तेसुवेलस्यशैलस्यसमीपेरामलक्ष्मणौ । प्रच्छन्नाददृशुर्गत्वाससुग्रीवविभीषणौ ।।6.29.25।।
explanation: Reaching the Suvela mountain in disguise, they saw Rama and Lakshmana along with Sugriva and Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: प्रेक्षमाणाश्चमूंतांतुबभूवुर्भयविक्लबाः । तेतुधर्मात्मनादृष्टाराक्षसेन्द्रेणराक्षसा ।।6.29.26।।
explanation: Those Rakshasas were bewildered with fear on looking at the army. Righteous Vibheeshana recognized them on seeing them.

shloka_text: विभीषणेनतत्रस्थानिगृहीतायदृच्छया । शार्दूलोग्राहितस्त्वेकःपापोऽयमितिराक्षसः ।।6.29.27।।
explanation: By chance Vibheeshana seized Saardula, the evil Rakshasa who was moving in that army.

shloka_text: मोचितस्सोऽपिरामेणवध्यमानःप्लवङ्गमैः । अनृशंस्येनरामेणमोचिताराक्षसाःपरे ।।6.29.28।।
explanation: As the monkeys attempted to kill him (Saardula), compassionate Rama released him and also the other Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वानरैरर्दितास्तेतुविक्रान्तैर्लघुविक्रमैः । पुनर्लङ्कामनुप्राप्ताश्वसन्तोनष्टचेतसः ।।6.29.29।।
explanation: Harassed by the valorous and swift Vanaras, those Rakshasas lost their senses and returned to Lanka gasping and panting.

shloka_text: ततस्तमक्षोभ्यबलंलङ्काधिपतयेचराः । सुवेलेराघवंशैलेनिविष्टंप्रत्यवेदयन् ।।6.30.1।।
explanation: Thereafter, the spies reported to the king of Lanka that Raghava had camped with an unshakable army at the Suvela mountain.

shloka_text: चाराणांरावणश्श्रुत्वाप्राप्तंरामंमहाबलम् । जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किञ्चिच्छार्दूलंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.30.2।।
explanation: On hearing from the spies that Rama has camped with a great army, Ravana got a little panicky and said these words to Saardula.

shloka_text: अयथावच्चतेवर्णोदीनश्चासिनिशाचर । नासिकच्चिदमित्राणांक्रुद्धानांवशमागतः ।।6.30.3।।
explanation: "O Forest ranger! Your face is not as it should be and also pitiable. Hope the angry enemies have not done anything to you."

shloka_text: इतितेनानुशिष्टस्तुवाचंमन्दमुदीरयत् । तदाराक्षसशार्दूलंशार्दूलोभयविह्वलः ।।6.30.4।।
explanation: And there after questioned by him (Ravana) Saardula revealed these words overwhelmed by fear, in faint tone to the tiger among Rakshasas.

shloka_text: नतेचारयितुंशक्याराजन्वानरपुङ्गवाः । विक्रान्ताबलवन्तश्चराघवेणचरक्षिताः ।।6.30.5।।
explanation: "O King! the Vanara heroes are valiant and highly powerful. They are also protected by Rama. It is not possible to spy on them."

shloka_text: नापिसम्भाषितुंशक्यास्सम्प्रश्नोऽत्रनलभ्यते । सर्वतोरक्ष्यतेपन्थावानरैःपर्वतोपमै ।।6.30.6।।
explanation: "It is not possible to converse with them or to question and or to examine, since they are guarded all over by mountains like Vanaras."

shloka_text: प्रविष्टमात्रेज्ञातोऽहंबलेतस्मिन्नचारिते । बलाद्गृहीतोरक्षोभिर्बहुधाऽस्मिविचालितः ।।6.30.7।।
explanation: "No sooner I entered their army, I was detected. I was forcibly seized by their guards and rolled on the ground."

shloka_text: जानुभिर्मुष्टिभिर्दन्तेस्तलैश्चाभिहतोभृशम् । परिणीतोऽस्मिहरिभिर्बलवद्भिरमर्षणैः ।।6.30.8।।
explanation: "The monkeys had beaten me with fists, bitten my palms with teeth, beaten me intensely and paraded me in the army indignantly."

shloka_text: परिणीयचसर्वत्रनीतोऽहंरामसंसदम् । रुधिरादिग्धसर्वाङ्गोविह्वलश्चलितेन्द्रियः ।।6.30.9।।
explanation: "With all my limbs wet with bleeding, control over senses lost, after parading, I was led to the assembly of Rama."

shloka_text: हरिभिर्वध्यमानश्चयाचमानःकृताञ्जलिः । राघवेणपरित्रातोजीवामीतियदृच्छया ।।6.30.10।।
explanation: "While smitten by the monkeys, offering salutation with folded hands, and pleading for protection from Raghava, luckily, I am alive."

shloka_text: एषशैलैश्शिलाभिश्चपूरयित्वामहार्णवम् । द्वारमाश्रित्यलङ्कायारामस्तिष्ठतिसायुधः ।।6.30.11।।
explanation: "Having filled the great ocean with rocks and stones in that way, taking position at the entrance of Lanka Rama stands equipped with arms."

shloka_text: गरुडव्यूहमास्थायसर्वतोहरिभिर्वृतः । मांविसृज्यमहातेजालङ्कामेवाभिवर्तते ।।6.30.12।।
explanation: "O glorious King! After releasing me, Rama is advancing into Lanka surrounded by mountains like a monkey army in the form of Garuda."

shloka_text: पुराप्राकारमायातिक्षिप्रमेकतरंकुरु । सीतांवास्मैप्रयच्छाशुयुद्धंवाप्रदीयताम् ।।6.30.13।।
explanation: "Before Rama reaches the boundary, the wall, do one thing quickly. Either give away Sita or set out to give a good war."

shloka_text: मनसातंतदाप्रेक्ष्यतच्छ्रुत्वाराक्षसाधिपः । शार्दूलंसुमहद्वाक्यमथोवाचसरावणः ।।6.30.14।।
explanation: "Having heard what has been said by Saardula, Rakshasa king reviewed in his mind and made a good statement before Saardula."

shloka_text: यदिमांप्रतियुध्येरन्देवगन्धर्वदानवाः । नैवसीतांप्रदास्यामिसर्वलोकभयादपि ।।6.30.15।।
explanation: "Even if Devas, Gandharvas and Danavas come to wage war with me and even if I have threats from all worlds, I will not give away Sita."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वामहातेजारावणःपुनरब्रवीत् । चरिताभवतासेनाकेऽत्रशूराःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.30.16।।
explanation: Glorious Ravana having spoken like that, again said (to Saardula), "You moved about in the army (camp) there. Tell me who among the monkeys are warriors?"

shloka_text: कीदृशा: किंप्रभा: सौम्यवानरायेदुरासदाः । कस्यपुत्राश्चपौत्राश्चतत्त्वमाख्याहिराक्षस:।। 6.30.17।।
explanation: "Gentle Saardula! Of those who are difficult to encounter, what is their description? Who are the powerful ones among them? Whose sons and grandsons, are they? You may speak."

shloka_text: तथात्रप्रतिपत्स्यामिज्ञात्वातेषांबलाबलम् । अवश्यंबलसङ् ख्यानंकर्तव्यंयुद्धमिच्छताम् ।।6.30.18।।
explanation: "Likewise knowing their strengths and weaknesses from you I wish to know what to do. It is essential to know their numbers and strength before the war."

shloka_text: अथैवमुक्तश्शार्दूलोरावणेनोत्तमश्चरः । इदंवचनमारेभेवक्तुंरावणसन्निधौ ।।6.30.19।।
explanation: "When Ravana had spoken that way, good spy Saardula proceeded to tell these words in the presence of Ravana."

shloka_text: अथर्क्षरजसःपुत्रोयुधिराजासुदुर्जयः । गद्गदस्याथपुत्त्रोऽत्रजाम्बवानितिविश्रुतः ।।6.30.20।।
explanation: "Certainly, king Sugriva, the son of Rksharaja's, is difficult to be conquered in battle. Here is the son of Gadgada, famously called as Jambavan."

shloka_text: गद्गदस्यैवपुत्त्रोऽन्योगुरुपुत्र: शतक्रतोः । कदनंयस्यपुत्रेणकृतमेकेनरक्षसाम् ।।6.30.21।।
explanation: Another son of Gadgada is Dhumra. One who killed many Rakshasas is Hanuman, the son of Kesari, who is the son of Brhaspati.

shloka_text: सुषेणश्चापिधर्मात्मापुत्रोधर्मस्यवीर्यवान् । सौम्यस्सोमात्मजश्चात्रराजन् दधिमुखःकपिः ।।6.30.22।।
explanation: "O king! Here is a heroic and righteous Sushena, the son of the Lord of death (Yamadharma). Here is Dadhimukha son of noble moon."

shloka_text: सुमुखोदुर्मुखश्चात्रवेगदर्शीचवानरः । मृत्युर्वानररूपेणनूनंसृष्टस्स्वयम्भुवा ।।6.30.23।।
explanation: "Vanaras Sumukha, Durmukha and Vegadarsi are surely created by Brahma in the Vanara form of DeathGod."

shloka_text: पुत्त्रोहुतवहस्याथनीलस्सेनापतिस्स्वयम् । अनिलस्यचपुत्त्रोऽत्रहनूमानितिविश्रुतः ।।6.30.24।।
explanation: "The firegod's son indeed is the army chief known as Nila, and here is windgod's son widely known as Hanuman."

shloka_text: नप्ताशक्रस्यदुर्धर्षोबलवानङ्गदोयुवा । मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौबलिनावश्विसम्भवौ ।।6.30.25।। पुत्त्रावैवस्वतस्यात्रपञ्चकालान्तकोपमाः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.30.26।। दशवानरकोट्यश्चशूराणांयुद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम् । श्रीमतांदेवपुत्त्राणांशेषंनाख्यातुमुत्सहे ।।6.30.27।।
explanation: "The indomitable and powerful young Angada is the grandson of Indra, the strong Mainda and Dwivida are both the twin sons of Ashwini Devas, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamadana are the five sons of Yama, the god of death. There are ten crores of heroic and prosperous Vanaras desiring to wage war who are the sons of gods. It is not possible to speak of the remaining ones", said Saardula to Ravana."

shloka_text: नप्ताशक्रस्यदुर्धर्षोबलवानङ्गदोयुवा । मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौबलिनावश्विसम्भवौ ।।6.30.25।। पुत्त्रावैवस्वतस्यात्रपञ्चकालान्तकोपमाः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.30.26।। दशवानरकोट्यश्चशूराणांयुद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम् । श्रीमतांदेवपुत्त्राणांशेषंनाख्यातुमुत्सहे ।।6.30.27।।
explanation: "The indomitable and powerful young Angada is the grandson of Indra, the strong Mainda and Dwivida are both the twin sons of Ashwini Devas, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamadana are the five sons of Yama, the god of death. There are ten crores of heroic and prosperous Vanaras desiring to wage war who are the sons of gods. It is not possible to speak of the remaining ones", said Saardula to Ravana."

shloka_text: नप्ताशक्रस्यदुर्धर्षोबलवानङ्गदोयुवा । मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौबलिनावश्विसम्भवौ ।।6.30.25।। पुत्त्रावैवस्वतस्यात्रपञ्चकालान्तकोपमाः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.30.26।। दशवानरकोट्यश्चशूराणांयुद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम् । श्रीमतांदेवपुत्त्राणांशेषंनाख्यातुमुत्सहे ।।6.30.27।।
explanation: "The indomitable and powerful young Angada is the grandson of Indra, the strong Mainda and Dwivida are both the twin sons of Ashwini Devas, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamadana are the five sons of Yama, the god of death. There are ten crores of heroic and prosperous Vanaras desiring to wage war who are the sons of gods. It is not possible to speak of the remaining ones", said Saardula to Ravana."

shloka_text: पुत्त्रोदशरथस्यैषसिंहसंहनोयुवा । दूषणोनिहतोयेनखरश्चत्रिशिरास्तथा ।।6.30.28।।
explanation: "That young one whose build is like a lion is Dasaratha's son who slayed Dushana, even Khara, like wise Trisira."

shloka_text: नास्तिरामस्यसदृशोविक्रमेभुविकश्चन । विराधोनिहतोयेनकबन्धश्चान्तकोपमः ।।6.30.29।।
explanation: "Viradha and even Kabhanda who was like the Lord of death were killed by Rama. Perhaps there is none equal to Rama in valour in this world."

shloka_text: वक्तुंनशक्तोरामस्यनरःकश्चिद्गुणान् क्षितौ । जनस्थानगतायेनयावन्तोराक्षसाहताः ।।6.30.30।।
explanation: "It is not even possible to recount the virtues of Rama who killed all the Rakshasas approaching Janasthana."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्चात्रधर्मात्मामातङ्गानामिवर्षभः । यस्यबाणपथंप्राप्यनजीवेदपिवासवः ।।6.30.31।।
explanation: "Here is righteous Lakshmana, who is like a bull (foremost) resembling a proud elephant. Even Indra will not be alive with in the range of his arrows when he strikes."

shloka_text: श्वेतोज्योतिर्मुखश्चात्रभास्करस्यात्मसम्भवौ । वरुणस्यचपुत्त्रोऽन्योःहेमकूटःप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.30.32।। विश्वकर्मसुतोवीरोनलःप्लवगसत्तमः । विक्रान्तोबलवानत्रवसुपुत्रस्सदुर्धरः ।।6.30.33।।
explanation: "Here are Swetha and Jyothirmukha sons of Sun god Hemakuta another son of Varuna Nala the foremost among the monkey heroes is the valiant son of Vishwakarma and Durdhara of swift action, the son of Vasu."

shloka_text: श्वेतोज्योतिर्मुखश्चात्रभास्करस्यात्मसम्भवौ । वरुणस्यचपुत्त्रोऽन्योःहेमकूटःप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.30.32।। विश्वकर्मसुतोवीरोनलःप्लवगसत्तमः । विक्रान्तोबलवानत्रवसुपुत्रस्सदुर्धरः ।।6.30.33।।
explanation: "Here are Swetha and Jyothirmukha sons of Sun god Hemakuta another son of Varuna Nala the foremost among the monkey heroes is the valiant son of Vishwakarma and Durdhara of swift action, the son of Vasu."

shloka_text: राक्षसानांवरिष्ठश्चतवभ्रातावीभीषणः । प्रतिगृह्यपुरींलङ्कांराघवस्यहितेरतः ।।6.30.34।।
explanation: "Here is your brother Vibheeshana the jewel among Rakshasas, who remains as a wellwisher of Rama and has received the city of Lanka (to whom Rama has offered Lanka)."

shloka_text: इतिसर्वंसमाख्यातंतवेदंवानरंबलम् । सुवेलेऽधिष्ठितंशैलेशेषकार्येभवान्गतिः ।।6.30.35।।
explanation: "I have described to you everything about the Vanara strength stationed on Suvela mountain. You may decide the rest of the task to be done." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेत्रिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirtieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततस्तमक्षोभ्यबलंलङ्काधिपतयेचराः । सुवेलेराघवंशैलेनिविष्टंप्रत्यवेदयन् ।।6.31.1।।
explanation: There upon the spies described the unshakeable army of Raghava staying at Suvela mountain, to the king of Lanka.

shloka_text: चाराणांरावणश्श्रुत्वाप्राप्तंरामंमहाबलम् । जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किञ्चित्सचिवानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.31.2।।
explanation: Having heard from the spies that Rama has come with mighty force, Ravana got perturbed and said to the ministers.

shloka_text: मन्त्रिणश्शीघ्रमायान्तुसर्वेवैसुसमाहिताः । अयंनोमन्त्रकालोहिसम्प्रप्ताइतिराक्षसाः ।।6.31.3।।
explanation: "The time has come for us to call for all the rakshasas and ministers immediately and assemble (said Ravana)."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वामन्त्रिणोऽभ्यागमन् द्रुतम् । ततस्समन्त्रयामासराक्षसैस्सचिवैस्सह ।।6.31.4।।
explanation: Having been ordered (by Ravana) that way, the ministers along with Rakshasas instantly reached and he started to think with them.

shloka_text: मन्त्रयित्वासदुर्धर्षःक्षमंयत्समनन्तरम् । विसर्जयित्वासचिवान्प्रविवेशस्वमालयम् ।।6.31.5।।
explanation: Thereafter, thinking about what is appropriate to do, unassailable Ravana dispensed his ministers and entered his own residence.

shloka_text: ततोराक्षसमाहूयविद्युज्जिह्वंमहाबलम् । मायाविदंमहामायःप्राविशद्यत्रमैथिली ।।6.31.6।।
explanation: Then Ravana of extraordinary skills sent for Vidyujihvam, a learned one in conjuring tricks and went from there to Mythili.

shloka_text: विद्युज्जिह्वंचमायाज्ञमब्रवीद्राक्षसाधिपः । मोहयिष्यावहेसीतांमाययाजनकात्मजाम् ।।6.31.7।।
explanation: Rakshasa king Ravana said to Vidyujihvam who knew conjuring tricks, "We will cheat Sita, daughter of Janaka by a trick."

shloka_text: शिरोमायामयंगृह्यराघवस्यनिशाचर: । त्वंमांसमुतिष्ठस्वमहच्चसशरंधनुः ।।6.31.8।।
explanation: "O Night ranger! You make an illusory head of Raghava and come and stand at me holding an arrow with great bow."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्याहविद्युज्जिह्वोनिशाचरः । दर्शयामासतांमायांसुप्रयुक्तांसरावणे ।।6.31.9।। तस्यतुष्टोऽभवद्राजाप्रददौचविभूषणम् ।
explanation: When the Rakshasa king had spoken that way to Vidyujihvam, he said, "Be it so." Pleased with the dexterous production of Vidyujihvam, Ravana presented to him a beautiful ornament.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिकायांतुसीतादर्शनलालसः । वैरृतानामधिपतिस्संविवेशमहाबलः ।।6.31.10।।
explanation: Eager to have a look at Sita, the mighty king of Rakshasas entered Asoka grove.

shloka_text: ततोदीनामदैन्यार्हांददर्शधनदानुजः ।।6.31.11।। अधोमुखींशोकपरामुपविष्टांमहीतले । भर्तारमेवध्यायन्तीमशोकवविकांगताम् ।।6.31.12।।
explanation: Thereafter, the younger brother of Kubera (Ravana) saw sad Sita, who did not deserve that piteous condition, who had been reduced to sorrowful state, seated on the ground in Asoka grove, with her head bent down filled with sorrow contemplating on her husband alone.

shloka_text: ततोदीनामदैन्यार्हांददर्शधनदानुजः ।।6.31.11।। अधोमुखींशोकपरामुपविष्टांमहीतले । भर्तारमेवध्यायन्तीमशोकवविकांगताम् ।।6.31.12।।
explanation: Thereafter, the younger brother of Kubera (Ravana) saw sad Sita, who did not deserve that piteous condition, who had been reduced to sorrowful state, seated on the ground in Asoka grove, with her head bent down filled with sorrow contemplating on her husband alone.

shloka_text: उपास्यमानांघोराभीराक्षसीभिरितस्ततः । उपसृत्यततस्सीतांप्रहर्षंनामकीर्तयन् ।।6.31.13।। इदंचवचनंधृष्टमुवाचजनकात्मजाम् ।
explanation: While she was guarded by dreadful Rakshasa women surrounding her closely, Ravana went near her happily and saw her. He addressed Sita praising her.

shloka_text: सान्त्व्यमानामयाभद्रेयमुपाश्रित्यवल्गसे । खरहन्तासतेभर्ताराघवस्समरेहतः ।।6.31.14।।
explanation: "O Auspicious one! However, much I have requested you, you did not care for me seeking your husband. Raghava, who killed Khara, has been killed in war."

shloka_text: छिन्नंतेसर्वतोमूलंदर्पस्तेनिहतोमया । व्यसनेनात्मनस्सीते ममभार्याभविष्यसि ।।6.31.15।।
explanation: "O Sita! All your roots have been crushed by me. Give up your vanity. By your own accord, you become my wife."

shloka_text: विसृजेमांमतिंमूढे: किंमृतेनकरिष्यसि । भवस्वभद्रे: भार्याणांसर्वेसामीश्वरीमम ।।6.31.16।।
explanation: "O Foolish one! Give up these thoughts from your mind. What will you do with your deceased husband? O auspicious one! You are the queen of all my wives."

shloka_text: अल्पपुण्ये: निवृत्तार्थे: मूढे: पण्डितमानिनि: । शृणुभर्तृवधंसीते: घोरंवृत्रवधंयथा ।।6.31.17।।
explanation: "O woman of less merit! You are one who has given up all worldly actions. Stupid one! You pretend as if you know everything. O Sita! Hear about your husband 's death like that of Vrthasura."

shloka_text: समायातस्समुद्रान्तंमांहन्तुंकिलराघवः । वानरेन्द्रप्रणीतेनबलेनमहतावृतः ।।6.31.18।।
explanation: "Raghava led by the huge army force of the Vanara king has arrived on the seashore."

shloka_text: सन्निविष्टस्समुद्रस्यपीड्यतीरमथोत्तरम् । बलेनमहतारामोव्रजत्यस्तंदिवाकरे ।।6.31.19।।
explanation: And when the Sun moved towards the west, Rama encamped on the northern shore of the sea with a huge army to strike.

shloka_text: अथाध्वनिपरिश्रान्तमर्धरात्रेस्थितंबलम् । सुखसुप्तंसमासाद्यचारित्रंप्रथमंचरैः ।।6.31.20।।
explanation: After having walked all the way they slept well and when they were sleeping at midnight, we found out all about them by sending prime spies.

shloka_text: तत्प्रहस्तप्रणीतेनबलेनमहतामम । बलमस्यहतंरात्रौयत्ररामस्सलक्ष्मणः ।।6.31.21।।
explanation: "There in that camp Lakshmana and Rama are killed by my powerful army led by Prahastha at night."

shloka_text: पट्टसान्परिघांश्चक्रान्दण्डान्महायशान् । बाणजालानिशूलानिभास्वरान्कूटमुद्गरान् ।।6.31.22।। यष्टीश्चतोमरान् शक्तीश्चक्राणिमुसलानिच । उद्यम्योद्यम्यरक्षोभिर्वानरेषुनिपातितां ।।6.31.23।।
explanation: Again, and again lifting spears, iron bars, javelins, huge staffs, sparkling maces, shining iron mallets and clubs, lances and strong Musalas, the Rakshasas hurled at Vanaras.

shloka_text: पट्टसान्परिघांश्चक्रान्दण्डान्महायशान् । बाणजालानिशूलानिभास्वरान्कूटमुद्गरान् ।।6.31.22।। यष्टीश्चतोमरान् शक्तीश्चक्राणिमुसलानिच । उद्यम्योद्यम्यरक्षोभिर्वानरेषुनिपातितां ।।6.31.23।।
explanation: Again, and again lifting spears, iron bars, javelins, huge staffs, sparkling maces, shining iron mallets and clubs, lances and strong Musalas, the Rakshasas hurled at Vanaras.

shloka_text: अथसुप्तस्यरामस्यप्रहस्तेनप्रमाथिना । असक्तंकृतहस्तेनशिरश्छिन्नंमहासिना ।।6.31.24।।
explanation: "There after the head of Rama, who was sleeping, was severed by Prahastha, skilled at striking, with a big sword without any feeling of attachment."

shloka_text: विभीषणस्समुत्पत्यनिगृहीतोयदृच्छया । दिशःप्रव्राजितस्सर्वैस्सर्लक्ष्मणःप्लवगैस्सहा ।।6.31.25।।
explanation: "When Vibheeshana rose up he was caught by chance. Lakshmana and Vanaras fled in all directions."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवोग्रीनयासीतेभग्नयाप्लवगाधिपः । निरस्तहनुकश्शेतेहनुमान्राक्षसैर्हतः ।।6.31.26।।
explanation: "O Sita! Vanara Lord Sugriva with his neck broken, Hanuman with chin broken were killed by Rakshasas and are lying down fallen on the ground."

shloka_text: जाम्बवानथजानुभ्यामुत्पतन्निहतोयुधि । पट्टसैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नोनिकृत्तःपादपोयथा ।।6.31.27।।
explanation: And while Jambavan was rising on his knees, he was struck by many iron bars in comb at and had fallen down like a tree.

shloka_text: मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौनिहतौवानरर्षभौ ।।6.31.28।। निश्श्वसन्तौरुदन्तौचरुधिरेणसमुक्षितौ । असिनाव्यायतौछिन्नौमध्येह्यरिनिषूदनौ ।।6.31.29।।
explanation: "Mainda and Dwivida of huge bodies, who are slayers of enemies, the bulls among Vanaras are breathing hard, and bathed in blood roaring, having been cutin the middle of their body."

shloka_text: मैन्दश्चद्विविदश्चोभौनिहतौवानरर्षभौ ।।6.31.28।। निश्श्वसन्तौरुदन्तौचरुधिरेणसमुक्षितौ । असिनाव्यायतौछिन्नौमध्येह्यरिनिषूदनौ ।।6.31.29।।
explanation: "Mainda and Dwivida of huge bodies, who are slayers of enemies, the bulls among Vanaras are breathing hard, and bathed in blood roaring, having been cutin the middle of their body."

shloka_text: अनुतिष्ठतिमेदिन्यांपनसःपनसोयथा ।।6.31.30।। नाराचैर्बहुभिश्चिन्नश्शेतेदर्यांदरीमुखः । कुमुदस्तुमहातेजानिष्कूजन्सायकै: कृतः ।।6.31.31।।
explanation: "Panasa is lying down on earth like jackfruit. Darimukha is lying down shattered by many arrows. Brilliant Kumuda too is torn off and silently lying down."

shloka_text: अनुतिष्ठतिमेदिन्यांपनसःपनसोयथा ।।6.31.30।। नाराचैर्बहुभिश्चिन्नश्शेतेदर्यांदरीमुखः । कुमुदस्तुमहातेजानिष्कूजन्सायकै: कृतः ।।6.31.31।।
explanation: "Panasa is lying down on earth like jackfruit. Darimukha is lying down shattered by many arrows. Brilliant Kumuda too is torn off and silently lying down."

shloka_text: अङ्गदोबहुभिश्छिन्नश्शरैरासाद्यराक्षसैः । पतितोरुधिरोद्गारीक्षितौनिपतिताङ्गदः ।।6.31.32।।
explanation: "By the many arrows of Rakshasas reaching towards Angada, he lies down chopped up and destroyed, with his armlets dropped down throwing up blood."

shloka_text: हरयोमथितानागैरथजातैस्तथापरे । शयितामृदिताश्चाश्वैर्यायुवेगैरिवाम्बुदाः ।।6.31.33।।
explanation: "There, some of the sleeping Vanaras were crushed by elephants, so also, just as by the speed of wind the clouds are crushed the Vanaras are crushed to death."

shloka_text: प्रहृताश्चपरेत्रस्ताहस्यमानाजघन्यतः । अभिद्रुतास्तुरक्षोभिस्सिंहैरिवमहाद्विपाः ।।6.31.34।।
explanation: "Some were followed behind as they were speeding like lions and mighty elephants afflicted and frightened, struck by Rakshasas."

shloka_text: सागरेपतिताःकेचित्केचिग्दगनमाश्रिताः । ऋक्षावृक्षानुपारूढावानरींवृत्तिमाश्रिताः ।।6.31.35।।
explanation: "While a few Vanaras dived into the sea, some took refuge in the sky. Resorting to their natural way the Bears climbed the trees."

shloka_text: सागरस्यचतीरेषुशैलेषुचवनेषुच । पिङ्गलास्तेविरूपाक्षैर्बहुभिर्बहवोहताः ।।6.31.36।।
explanation: "Many fierceeyed Rakshasas killed several Vanaras on the shore of the ocean, in the mountains and woods."

shloka_text: एवंतवहतोभर्ताससैन्योममसेनया । क्षतजार्द्रंरजोध्वस्तमिदंचस्याहृतंशिरः ।।6.31.37।।
explanation: "In that way the army of your husband has been killed by Rakshasa army and his decayed head drenched in blood covered with dust has been brought."

shloka_text: ततःपरमदुर्धर्षोरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । सीतायामुपशन्त्यांराक्षसीमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.31.38।।
explanation: Then Ravana, the highly unassailable king of Rakshasas spoke these words to the hearing of Sita.

shloka_text: राक्षसंक्रूरकर्माणंविद्युज्जिह्वंत्वमानय । येनतद्राघवशिरस्सङ्ग्रामात्स्वयमाहृतम् ।।6.31.39।।
explanation: "Bring that Rakshasa, Vidyujihvam of cruel deeds who brought Rama's head from the battlefield."

shloka_text: विद्युज्जिह्वस्ततोगृह्यशिरस्तत्सशरासनम् । प्रणामंशिरसाकृत्वारावणस्याग्रतस्थितः ।।6.31.40।।
explanation: Then holding the head along with the bow, Vidyujihvam bowed his head down in salutation and stood in front of Ravana.

shloka_text: तमब्रवीत्ततोराजारावणोराक्षसंस्थितम् । विद्युज्जिह्वंमहाजिह्वंसमीपपरिवर्तिनम् ।।6.31.41।।
explanation: Then the king, Ravana spoke to Vidyujihvam, the Rakshasa with extended tongue, who stood close by.

shloka_text: अग्रतःकुरुसीतायाश्शीघ्रंदाशरधेशशिरः । अवस्थांपश्चिमांभर्तुःकृपणासाधुपश्यतु ।।6.31.42।।
explanation: At once place the head of Dasaratha's son before that piteous woman. Let her see the ultimate status attained by her husband at the end (said Ravana).

shloka_text: एवमुक्तंतुतद्रक्षशशिरस्तत्प्रियदर्शनम् । उपनिक्षिप्यसीतायाःक्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत ।।6.31.43।।
explanation: Having spoken immediately placed the head of Rama that was pleasing to see, by the side of Sita and went away.

shloka_text: रावणश्चापिचिक्षेपभस्वरंकार्मुकंमहत् । त्रिषुलोकेषुविख्यातंसीतामिदमुवाचह ।।6.31.44।।
explanation: Thus addressed Ravana casting down the bright great bow that is famous in the three worlds.

shloka_text: इदंतुतवरामस्यकार्मुकंज्यासमायुतम् । इहप्रहस्तेनानीतंहत्वातंनिशिमानुषम् ।।6.31.45।।
explanation: "Prahastha has brought this bow duly tied with the string after killing human Rama in the night."

shloka_text: सासीतातच्छिरोदृष्टवातच्चकार्मुकमुत्तमम् । सुग्रीवप्रतिसंपर्गमाख्यातंचहनूमता ।।6.32.1।। नयनेमुखवर्णंचभर्तुस्तत्सदृशंमुखम् । केशान् केशान्तदेशंचतंचचूडामणिंशुभम् ।।6.32.2।। एतैस्सर्वेरभिज्ञानैरभिज्ञायसुदुःखिता । निजगर्हेचकैकेयींक्रोशन्तीकुररीयथा ।।6.32.3।।
explanation: On seeing the esteemed Rama's head and bow, remembering the description made by Hanuman about the friendship with Sugriva thinking of the eyes, complexion of the face, the hair, and curls of her husband at the end Sita recognized the auspicious Chudamani. Identifying all those marks to be like Rama's she felt very sad and cried like a deer and abused Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: सासीतातच्छिरोदृष्टवातच्चकार्मुकमुत्तमम् । सुग्रीवप्रतिसंपर्गमाख्यातंचहनूमता ।।6.32.1।। नयनेमुखवर्णंचभर्तुस्तत्सदृशंमुखम् । केशान् केशान्तदेशंचतंचचूडामणिंशुभम् ।।6.32.2।। एतैस्सर्वेरभिज्ञानैरभिज्ञायसुदुःखिता । निजगर्हेचकैकेयींक्रोशन्तीकुररीयथा ।।6.32.3।।
explanation: On seeing the esteemed Rama's head and bow, remembering the description made by Hanuman about the friendship with Sugriva thinking of the eyes, complexion of the face, the hair, and curls of her husband at the end Sita recognized the auspicious Chudamani. Identifying all those marks to be like Rama's she felt very sad and cried like a deer and abused Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: सासीतातच्छिरोदृष्टवातच्चकार्मुकमुत्तमम् । सुग्रीवप्रतिसंपर्गमाख्यातंचहनूमता ।।6.32.1।। नयनेमुखवर्णंचभर्तुस्तत्सदृशंमुखम् । केशान् केशान्तदेशंचतंचचूडामणिंशुभम् ।।6.32.2।। एतैस्सर्वेरभिज्ञानैरभिज्ञायसुदुःखिता । निजगर्हेचकैकेयींक्रोशन्तीकुररीयथा ।।6.32.3।।
explanation: On seeing the esteemed Rama's head and bow, remembering the description made by Hanuman about the friendship with Sugriva thinking of the eyes, complexion of the face, the hair, and curls of her husband at the end Sita recognized the auspicious Chudamani. Identifying all those marks to be like Rama's she felt very sad and cried like a deer and abused Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: सकामाभवकैकेयीहतोऽयंकुलनन्दनः । कुलमुत्सादितंसर्वंत्वयाकलहशीलया ।।6.32.4।।
explanation: "O Kaikeyi! Your desire is fulfilled with the killing of the delight of the race. You, who are given to creating quarrel have ruined the race."

shloka_text: आर्येणकिंतेकैकेयी कृतंरामेणविप्रियम् । यन्मयाचीरवसनस्त्वयाप्रस्थापितोवनम् ।।6.32.5।।
explanation: "Kaikeyi, you have given bark robes to prince Rama and sent him to the forest with me. What harm has he done for you? Thinking of this again and again Sita cried."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुवैदेहीवेपमानातपस्विनी । जगामजगतींबालाछिन्नातुकदळीयथा ।।6.32.6।।
explanation: That miserable young, Vaidehi, having said so, fell on the ground trembling like a cut off banana plant.

shloka_text: सामुहूर्तात्समाश्वास्यप्रतिलभ्यचचेतनाम् । तच्छिरस्समुपाघ्रायविललासायतेक्षणा ।।6.32.7।।
explanation: Broadeyed Sita, regaining her consciousness after a while, sat close to the head of Rama and lamented.

shloka_text: हाहताऽस्मिमहाबाहो वीरव्रतमनुव्रत । इमांतेपश्चिमावस्थांगताऽस्मिविधवाकृता ।।6.32.8।।
explanation: "O mightyarmed one! Alas you are killed while following heroic vow. I live to see you in the last state of your life, widowed. I am done."

shloka_text: प्रथमंमरणंनार्याभर्तुर्वैगुण्यमुच्यते । सुवृत्त: स्साधुवृत्तायास्सम्वृत्तस्त्वंममाग्रतः ।।6.32.9।।
explanation: "O Rama, you are faithful to your vows, a noble one! It is said that because of a woman's faults, the husband will die. It is not even so as you died in front of a virtuous woman of good conduct."

shloka_text: दुःखाद्दुःखंप्रपन्नायामग्नायाश्शोकसागरे । योहिमामुद्यतनिस्त्रातुंसोऽपित्वंविनिपातितः ।।6.32.10।।
explanation: "I am in grief and filled with an ocean of sorrow. You who have come to save me and are also killed."

shloka_text: साश्वश्रूर्ममकौसल्यात्वयापुत्रेणराघव: । वत्सेनेवयथाधेनुर्विवत्सावत्सलाकृता ।।6.32.11।।
explanation: "O Raghava! Even my motherinlaw Kausalya is separated from her dear son just as cow is separated from calf."

shloka_text: आद्दिष्टंदीर्घमायुस्तेयैरचिन्त्यपराक्रम । अनृतंवचनंतेषामल्पायुरपिराघव ।।6.32.12।।
explanation: "O Raghava of incomprehensible valour! the words predicted by astrologers that your life is long is falsified. Your life has been short."

shloka_text: अथवानश्यतिप्रज्ञाप्राज्ञस्यापिसतस्तव । पचत्येनंयथाकालोभूतानांप्रभवोऽह्ययम् ।।6.32.13।।
explanation: "Or else, even the wisdom of a learned one is diffused and lost perhaps! the effect of time which is the cause of all living beings has caused this."

shloka_text: अदृष्टंमृत्युमापन्नःकस्मात्त्वंनयशास्त्रवित् । व्यसनानामुपायज्ञःकुशलोह्यसिवर्जने ।।6.32.14।।
explanation: "You are the knower of all sastras, and capable of warding off all calamities. How did death have a chance to meet you and overtake?"

shloka_text: तथात्वंसम्परिष्वज्यरौद्रयाऽतिनृशंसया । काळरात्य्राममाच्छिद्यहृतःकमललोचन:।। 6.32.15।।
explanation: "O lotuseyed Rama! After you have lost contact with me, the most horrible cruel night has killed you cutting you off from me."

shloka_text: उपशेषेमहाबाहो: मांविहायतपस्विनीम् । प्रियामिवसमालशिष्यपृथिवींपुरुषर्षभ ।।6.32.16।।
explanation: "O mightyarmed one! A bull among men and a noble one, you are embracing the earth as though it is your beloved and sleeping leaving me in the sky."

shloka_text: अर्चितंसततंयत्तद्गन्धमाल्यैर्मयातव । इदंतेमप्रतियंवीरधनुःकाञ्चानभूषणम् ।।6.32.17।।
explanation: "O Hero! This bow that was decorated with gold was always worshipped with sandal and flowers diligently by you and me with utmost devotion."

shloka_text: पित्रादशरथेनत्वंश्वशुरेणममानघ: । सर्वैश्चपितृभिस्सार्थंनूनंस्वर्गेसमागतः ।।6.32.18।।
explanation: "O Sinless one! Surely you have reached heaven where your father, my fatherinlaw Dasaratha and your grandfathers have reached."

shloka_text: दिविनक्षत्रभूतस्त्वंमहात्कर्मकृतप्रियम् । पुण्यंराजर्षिवंशंत्वमात्मनस्समुपेक्षसे ।।6.32.19।।
explanation: "In heaven, you will be seeing luminaries of the sky who are dear, who have done great deeds and earned merit and the royal sages of your own race."

shloka_text: किंमांनप्रेक्षसेराजन् किंमांनप्रतिभाषसे । बालांबाल्येनसम्प्राप्तांभार्यांमांसहचारिणीम् ।।6.32.20।।
explanation: "O King! I have come to you while I was young. I am your companion and wife also. Why are you not seeing me? Why are you not talking to me?"

shloka_text: संश्रुतंगृह्णतापाणिंचरिष्यामीतियत्त्वया । स्मरतन्ममकाकुत्स्थनयमामपिदुःखिताम् ।।6.32.21।।
explanation: "O Kakutstha! while you held my hand (at the time of marriage) you promised that you will be with me and likewise promised to take me, a (wretched one) with you to the other world. Remembering that I am sad."

shloka_text: कस्मान्मामपहायत्वंगतोगतिमतांवर । अस्माल्लोकादमुंलोकंत्यक्त्वामामपिदुःखिताम् ।।6.32.22।।
explanation: "O Jewel among those who attained good state! Why have you gone abandoning me dear? To which world have you gone from here? I am pained by your deserting me."

shloka_text: कल्याणैरुचितंयत्तत्परिष्वक्तंमयैवतु । क्रव्यादैस्तच्छरीरंतेमानंविपरिकृष्यते ।।6.32.23।।
explanation: "This body which used to be decorated by me with auspicious items, with great respect is dragged by cruel animals."

shloka_text: अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः । अग्निहोत्रेणसंस्कारंकेनत्वंनतुलप्स्यसे ।।6.32.24।।
explanation: "Why are you, who performed all kinds of sacrificial rituals of fire with all offerings deserve sanctification without doing fire sacrifice?"

shloka_text: प्रव्रज्यामुपपन्नानांत्रयाणामेकमागतम् । परिप्रक्ष्यतिकौसल्यालक्ष्मणंशोकलालसा ।।6.32.25।।
explanation: "Seeing only Lakshmana returning, of the three exiled, Kausalya will be immersed in grief (will ask)."

shloka_text: सतस्याःपरिपृच्छन्त्यावधंमित्रबलस्यते । तवचाख्यास्यतेनूनंनिशायांराक्षसैर्वधम् ।।6.32.26।।
explanation: "When she questions, he may tell that you and your army were killed by the army of friends at night."

shloka_text: सात्वांसुप्तंहतंश्रुत्वामांचरक्षोगृहंगताम् । हृदयेनविदीर्णेननभविष्यतिराघव ।।6.32.27।।
explanation: "Raghava! Hearing that you were killed while asleep and I was taken to the home of Rakshasas, Kausalya will not be able to survive with a broken heart."

shloka_text: ममहेतोरनार्यायाह्यनर्हःपार्थिवात्म: । रामस्सागरमुततीर्यसत्त्ववान् गोष्पदेहतः ।।6.32.28।।
explanation: "On account of an undeserving one, Rama, the son of the emperor, a valiant one who does not deserve to be killed, after having crossed the ocean is killed by a footprint of a cow(easily)."

shloka_text: अहंदाशरथेनोढामोहात्स्वकुलपांसनी । आर्यपुत्रस्यरामस्यभार्यामृत्युरजायत ।।6.32.29।।
explanation: "In ignorance as an obloquy of his race, the noble son of Dasaratha married me. For such Rama's wife turned out to be his death."

shloka_text: नूनमन्यांमयाजातिंवारितंदानमुत्तमम् । याहमद्येहशोचामिभार्यासर्वतिथेरपि ।।6.32.30।।
explanation: "Undoubtedly I may have obstructed a supreme offering (such as offering a girl in marriage) in some other (previous) life. So now I am pained even though I am the wife of one who is kind to all."

shloka_text: साधुपातयमांक्षिप्रंरामस्योपरिरावण । समानयपतिंपन्त्याकुरुकल्याणमुत्तमम् ।।6.32.31।।
explanation: "O Ravana! You may quickly join me with my husband as it will be highly auspicious for the wife to join the husband."

shloka_text: शिरसामेशिरश्चास्यकायंकायेनयोजय । रावणानुगमिष्यामिगतिंभर्तुर्महात्मनः ।।6.32.32।।
explanation: "O Ravana! Join my head with his and my body with his body. I will follow him in the same way."

shloka_text: इतिसदुःखसन्तप्ताविललापायतेक्षणा । भर्तुश्शिरोधनुस्तत्रसमीक्ष्यचपुनःपुनः ।।6.32.33।।
explanation: Burning in sorrow, the broad eyed Sita gazing at the head of her husband and the bow again and again lamented.

shloka_text: एवंलालप्यमानायांसीतायांतत्रराक्षसः । अभिचक्रामभर्तारमनीकस्थःकृताञ्जलिः ।।6.32.34।।
explanation: While Sita was wailing in that manner, as said earlier, the Rakshasa guarding her approached the king and offered salutations with both hands.

shloka_text: विजयस्वार्यपुत्रेतिसोऽभिवाद्यप्रसाद्यच । न्यवेदयदनुप्राप्तंप्रहस्तंवाहिनीपतिम् ।।6.32.35।।
explanation: The Rakshasa (guard) greeted the king saying, "Let you be victorious!" and announced reverentially, "Prahastha, the army chief has arrived."

shloka_text: अमात्यैस्सहितस्सर्वैःप्रहस्तस्समुपस्थितः । तेनदर्शनकामेनवयंप्रस्थापिताःप्रभो ।।6.32.36।।
explanation: "O Lord! Accompanied by all ministers Prahastha is waiting and sends me desiring to see you."

shloka_text: नूनमस्तिमहाराज राजभावात्क्षमान्वितं । किञ्चिदात्ययिकंकार्यंतेषांत्वंदर्शनंकुरु ।।6.32.37।।
explanation: "O great king, endowed with forgiveness and royalty! there is a little urgent work. Undoubtedly, they are waiting to see you please."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वादशग्रीवोराक्षसप्रतिवेदितम् । अशोकन्विकांत्यक्त्वामन्त्रिणांदर्शनंययौ ।।6.32.38।।
explanation: On hearing the submission of the rakshasa, the tenheaded king left the Asoka grove to see the ministers.

shloka_text: सतुसर्वंसमर्थ्यैवमन्त्रिभिःकृत्यमात्मनः । सभांप्रविश्यविदधेविदित्वारामविक्रमम् ।।6.32.39।।
explanation: Having known all about Rama's prowess, Ravana and ministers entered the assembly to think carefully about the task to be carried out and how to do it.

shloka_text: अन्तर्थानंतुतच्छीर्षंतच्चकार्मुकमुत्तमम् । जगामरावणस्यैवनिर्याणसमनन्तरम् ।।6.32.40।।
explanation: As soon as Ravana departed, that head and the excellent bow vanished from there.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रस्तुतैस्सार्धंमन्त्रिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः । समर्थयामासतदारामकार्यविनिश्चयम् ।।6.32.41।।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas and the ministers of terrific valour then thought about the course of action to be taken against Rama and decided.

shloka_text: अविदूरस्थितान्सर्वान्बलाध्यक्षाहनितैषिणः । अब्रवीत्कालसदृशोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.32.42।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king who resembled the god of death spoke to the heads of army force and wellwishers who stood close by.

shloka_text: शीघ्रंभेरीनिनादेनस्फुटंकोणाहतेनमे । समानयध्वंसैन्यानिवक्तव्यंचनकारणम् ।।6.32.43।।
explanation: "Break forth by beating the drums with powerful drumsticks calling the army to assemble without telling the reason."

shloka_text: ततस्तथेतिप्रतिगृह्यतद्वचोबलाधिपास्तेमहदात्मनोबलम् । समानयंश्चैवसमागमंचतेन्यवेदयन्भर्तरियुद्धकाङ्क्षिणि ।।6.32.44।।
explanation: Then the attendants collected the great powerful army saying, 'so be it', to Ravana who was desirous of war. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्दकाण्डेद्वात्रिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सीतांतुमोहितांदृष्टवासरमानामराक्षसी । आससादाथवैदेहींप्रियांप्रणयिनींसखी ।।6.33.1।।
explanation: Then seeing Sita in distraught, a Rakshasi by name Saarana who was very dear and friendly with Vaidehi approached her.

shloka_text: मोहितांराक्षसेन्द्रेणसीतांपरमदुःखिताम् । आश्वासयामासतदासरमामृदुभाषिणी ।।6.33.2।।
explanation: Then Saarana of sweet expression, comforted Sita who was put off and was extremely sorrowful because of the Rakshasa king.

shloka_text: साहितत्रकृतामित्रंसीतयारक्ष्यमाणया । रक्षन्तीरावणादिष्टासानुक्रोशादृढव्रता ।।6.33.3।।
explanation: Most compassionate Saarana, determined to protect was friendly with Sita while she was ordered for protecting her by Ravana.

shloka_text: साददर्शसखीसीतांसरमानष्टचेतनाम् । उपावृत्त्योत्थितांध्वस्तांबडबामिवपांसुलाम् ।।6.33.4।।
explanation: Saarana saw her friend Sita, who had lost consciousness, fully covered by dust by rolling on the dirty ground like a female horse.

shloka_text: तांसमाश्वासयामाससखीस्नेहेनसुव्रता । समाश्वसिहिवैदेही माभूत्तेमवसोव्यथा ।।6.33.5।।
explanation: Saarana consoled Vaidehi of noble vows in a friendly way and encouraged her to recover saying, "Let there be no pain at heart."

shloka_text: उक्तायद्रावणेनत्वंप्रत्युक्तश्चस्वयंत्वया । सखीस्नेहेनतभदीरुमयासर्वंप्रतिश्रुतम् ।।6.33.6।। लीनयागहनेशून्येभयमुत्सृज्यरावणात् । तवहेतोर्विशालाक्षी नहिमेजीवितंप्रियम् ।।6.33.7।।
explanation: "O Broadeyed friend! You are constantly under fear (timid). Give up fear of Ravana, I have overheard all that you have spoken to Ravana and his reply by hiding in a secret place out of my affection, without caring for my life."

shloka_text: उक्तायद्रावणेनत्वंप्रत्युक्तश्चस्वयंत्वया । सखीस्नेहेनतभदीरुमयासर्वंप्रतिश्रुतम् ।।6.33.6।। लीनयागहनेशून्येभयमुत्सृज्यरावणात् । तवहेतोर्विशालाक्षी नहिमेजीवितंप्रियम् ।।6.33.7।।
explanation: "O Broadeyed friend! You are constantly under fear (timid). Give up fear of Ravana, I have overheard all that you have spoken to Ravana and his reply by hiding in a secret place out of my affection, without caring for my life."

shloka_text: ससम्भ्रान्तश्चनिष्क्रान्तोयत्कृतेराक्षसाधिपः । तच्चमेविदितंसर्वमभिनिष्क्रम्यमैथिलि:।। 6.33.8।।
explanation: "O Mythili! I know all about why the king of Rakshasas returned back agitated."

shloka_text: नशक्यंसौप्तिकंकर्तुंरामस्यविदितात्मनः । वधश्चपुरुषव्याघ्रेतस्मिन्नैवोपपद्यते ।।6.33.9।।
explanation: "Rama is a knower of his Self. It is not possible to kill him while he is asleep. Nay death is not possible for he is a tiger among men."

shloka_text: नत्वेववानराहन्तुंशक्याःपादपयोधिपः । सुरादेवर्षभेणेवरामेणहिसुरक्षिताः ।।6.33.10।।
explanation: "Vanaras are fighting with trees and are not capable of being killed. Just as the gods are protected by their Lord Indra, Vanaras are protected by Rama. It is not feasible to kill them."

shloka_text: दीर्घवृत्तभुज्शीमान्महोरस्कःप्रतापवान् । धन्वीसंहननोपेतोधर्मात्माभुविविश्रुतः ।।6.33.11।। विक्रान्तोरक्षितानित्यमात्मनश्चपरस्यच । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राकुशलीनयशास्त्रवित् ।।6.33.12।। हन्तापरबलौघनामचिन्त्यबलपौरुषः । नहतोराघवश्रशीमान्सीते: शत्रुनिबर्हणः ।।6.33.13।।
explanation: "O Sita! One who is endowed with long rounded arms and broad chest, a valorous one, a glorious wielder of bow and powerful Rama along with his brother Lakshmana, is always a protector of himself and all surrounding him. He is a knower of sastras of propriety. Raghava is majestic with inconceivable courage and a destroyer of foes. He will not be killed."

shloka_text: दीर्घवृत्तभुज्शीमान्महोरस्कःप्रतापवान् । धन्वीसंहननोपेतोधर्मात्माभुविविश्रुतः ।।6.33.11।। विक्रान्तोरक्षितानित्यमात्मनश्चपरस्यच । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राकुशलीनयशास्त्रवित् ।।6.33.12।। हन्तापरबलौघनामचिन्त्यबलपौरुषः । नहतोराघवश्रशीमान्सीते: शत्रुनिबर्हणः ।।6.33.13।।
explanation: "O Sita! One who is endowed with long rounded arms and broad chest, a valorous one, a glorious wielder of bow and powerful Rama along with his brother Lakshmana, is always a protector of himself and all surrounding him. He is a knower of sastras of propriety. Raghava is majestic with inconceivable courage and a destroyer of foes. He will not be killed."

shloka_text: दीर्घवृत्तभुज्शीमान्महोरस्कःप्रतापवान् । धन्वीसंहननोपेतोधर्मात्माभुविविश्रुतः ।।6.33.11।। विक्रान्तोरक्षितानित्यमात्मनश्चपरस्यच । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राकुशलीनयशास्त्रवित् ।।6.33.12।। हन्तापरबलौघनामचिन्त्यबलपौरुषः । नहतोराघवश्रशीमान्सीते: शत्रुनिबर्हणः ।।6.33.13।।
explanation: "O Sita! One who is endowed with long rounded arms and broad chest, a valorous one, a glorious wielder of bow and powerful Rama along with his brother Lakshmana, is always a protector of himself and all surrounding him. He is a knower of sastras of propriety. Raghava is majestic with inconceivable courage and a destroyer of foes. He will not be killed."

shloka_text: अयुक्तबुद्धिकृत्येनसर्वभूतविरोधिना । इहप्रमुक्तारौद्रेणमायामायाविदात्वयि ।।6.33.14।।
explanation: "On account of his perverse thought and being inimical to all beings Ravana a tricker has attempted a trick at you in anger."

shloka_text: शोकस्तेविगतस्सर्वःकल्याणंत्वामुपस्थितम् । ध्रुवंत्वांभजतेलक्ष्मीःप्रियंतेप्रीतिकरंशृणुः ।।6.33.15।।
explanation: "Your sorrow has gone. All auspiciousness awaits you. Surely you will attain good fortune (Lakshmi). You listen to my happy and pleasant news."

shloka_text: उत्तीर्यसागरंरामस्सहवानरसेनया । सन्निविष्टःसमुद्रस्यतीरमासाद्यदक्षिणम् ।।6.33.16।।
explanation: "Rama accompanied by Vanara army has crossed the ocean and reached the southern shore of the ocean."

shloka_text: दृष्टोमेपरिपूर्णार्थःकाकुत्स्थस्सहलक्ष्मणः । सहितैस्सागरान्तस्थैर्बलैस्तिष्ठतिरक्षितः ।।6.33.17।।
explanation: "Rama, a fully accomplished soul accompanied by Lakshmana together with army stands protected by the army and is stationed on the seashore."

shloka_text: अनेनप्रेषितायेचराक्षसालघुविक्रमाः । राघवस्तीर्णइत्येवप्रवृत्तिस्तैरिहाहृता ।।6.33.18।।
explanation: "These swift footed Rakshasas sent by the king brought the news of Rama crossing the sea."

shloka_text: सतांश्रुत्वाविशालाक्षी: प्रवृत्तिंराक्षसाधिपः । एषमन्त्रयतेसर्वैस्सचिवैस्सहरावणः ।।6.33.19।।
explanation: "O Broadeyed Sita! On hearing the news (of Rama crossing) Rakshasa king is holding consultation with ministers about what to do."
