shloka_text: इतिब्रुवाणासरमाराक्षसीसीतयासह । सर्वोद्योगेनसैन्यानांशब्दंशुश्रावभैरवम् ।।6.33.20।।
explanation: While Saarana was speaking to Sita, frightening sounds of the army making all kinds of attempts were heard.

shloka_text: दण्डनिर्घातवादिन्याश्रुत्वाभेर्यामहास्वनम् । उवाचसरमासीतामिदंमधुरभाषिणी ।।6.33.21।।
explanation: On hearing the loud sounds of army maces, rods, and drums, Saarana looked at Sita and spoke these sweet words.

shloka_text: सन्नाहजननीह्येषाभैरवाभीरु: भेरिका । भेरीनादंचगम्भीरंशृणुतोयदनिःस्वनम् ।।6.33.22।।
explanation: "O Timid Sita! Listen to the deep penetrating sounds of drums like the rumbling of rain clouds signifying the preparations of the army."

shloka_text: कल्प्यन्तेमत्तमातङ्गायुज्यन्तेरथवाजिन । हृष्यन्तेतुरगारूढाःप्रासहस्तस्सहस्रशः ।।6.33.23।।
explanation: "Elephants in rut are being decorated, charioteers are getting ready for war in thousands and discharging darts from hands and laughing loudly."

shloka_text: तत्रतत्रचसन्नद्धास्सपततनिपदातयः । अपूर्यन्तेराजमार्गास्सैन्यैरद्भुतदर्शनैः ।।6.33.24।। वेगवभदिन्नदभदिश्चतोयौघैरिवसागरः ।
explanation: "See the weird appearance of footsoldiers collected here and therein groups prepared to go. The royal path is filled with choking sounds of the troops moving fast, like an ocean filled with streams of water. It is strange."

shloka_text: शस्त्राणांचप्रसन्नानांचर्मणांवर्मणांतथा ।।6.33.25।। रथवाजिगजानांचभूषितानांचराक्षसाम् । संभ्रमोराक्षसामेषहृषितानांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.33.26।। प्रभांविसृजतांपश्यनानावर्णांसमुत्थिताम् । वनंनिर्धहतोघर्मेयथारूपंविभावसोः ।।6.33.27।।
explanation: "Look at the sheen of weapons, the leather shields, spreading forth different pleasing colours, the brightness of which resembles the burning of forest fire arisen and spread in summer. And here are chariots, horses and elephants decked with ornaments following Ravana, as well as the powerful Rakshasa army full of joy."

shloka_text: शस्त्राणांचप्रसन्नानांचर्मणांवर्मणांतथा ।।6.33.25।। रथवाजिगजानांचभूषितानांचराक्षसाम् । संभ्रमोराक्षसामेषहृषितानांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.33.26।। प्रभांविसृजतांपश्यनानावर्णांसमुत्थिताम् । वनंनिर्धहतोघर्मेयथारूपंविभावसोः ।।6.33.27।।
explanation: "Look at the sheen of weapons, the leather shields, spreading forth different pleasing colours, the brightness of which resembles the burning of forest fire arisen and spread in summer. And here are chariots, horses and elephants decked with ornaments following Ravana, as well as the powerful Rakshasa army full of joy."

shloka_text: शस्त्राणांचप्रसन्नानांचर्मणांवर्मणांतथा ।।6.33.25।। रथवाजिगजानांचभूषितानांचराक्षसाम् । संभ्रमोराक्षसामेषहृषितानांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.33.26।। प्रभांविसृजतांपश्यनानावर्णांसमुत्थिताम् । वनंनिर्धहतोघर्मेयथारूपंविभावसोः ।।6.33.27।।
explanation: "Look at the sheen of weapons, the leather shields, spreading forth different pleasing colours, the brightness of which resembles the burning of forest fire arisen and spread in summer. And here are chariots, horses and elephants decked with ornaments following Ravana, as well as the powerful Rakshasa army full of joy."

shloka_text: घण्टानांशृणुनिर्घोषंरथानांशृणुनिःस्वनम् । हयानांहेषमाणानांशृणुतूर्यध्वनिंयथा ।।6.33.28।। उद्यतायुधहस्तानांराक्षसेन्द्रानुयायिनाम् । सम्भ्रमोरक्षसामेषतुमुलोरोमहर्षणः ।।6.33.29।।
explanation: "Listen to the bustle of noise of the Rakshasas lifting the weapons, ringing of the bells (of elephants), and rattling of chariots, and neighing of horses. Listen to the flourish of the trumpets. The happy Rakshasas are making tumultuous noise causing horripilation."

shloka_text: घण्टानांशृणुनिर्घोषंरथानांशृणुनिःस्वनम् । हयानांहेषमाणानांशृणुतूर्यध्वनिंयथा ।।6.33.28।। उद्यतायुधहस्तानांराक्षसेन्द्रानुयायिनाम् । सम्भ्रमोरक्षसामेषतुमुलोरोमहर्षणः ।।6.33.29।।
explanation: "Listen to the bustle of noise of the Rakshasas lifting the weapons, ringing of the bells (of elephants), and rattling of chariots, and neighing of horses. Listen to the flourish of the trumpets. The happy Rakshasas are making tumultuous noise causing horripilation."

shloka_text: श्रीस्त्वांभजतिशोकघ्नीरक्षसांभयमागतम् । रामःकमलपत्राक्षोदैत्यानामिववासवः ।।6.33.30।। निर्जित्यजितक्रोधस्त्वामचिन्तपराक्रमः । रावणंसमरेहत्वाभर्तात्वाऽधिगमिष्यति ।।6.33.31।।
explanation: "Your fire of anger will be gone. Your husband, the lotuspetal eyed Rama whose prowess is inconceivable like that of Indra who vanquished Daityas will come and kill Ravana and win you back."

shloka_text: श्रीस्त्वांभजतिशोकघ्नीरक्षसांभयमागतम् । रामःकमलपत्राक्षोदैत्यानामिववासवः ।।6.33.30।। निर्जित्यजितक्रोधस्त्वामचिन्तपराक्रमः । रावणंसमरेहत्वाभर्तात्वाऽधिगमिष्यति ।।6.33.31।।
explanation: "Your fire of anger will be gone. Your husband, the lotuspetal eyed Rama whose prowess is inconceivable like that of Indra who vanquished Daityas will come and kill Ravana and win you back."

shloka_text: विक्रमिष्यतिरक्षस्सुभर्तातेसहलक्ष्मणः । यथाशत्रुषुशत्रुघ्नोविष्णुनासहवासवः ।।6.33.32।।
explanation: "Your husband accompanied by Lakshmana will exhibit his valour against Rakshasas just as Indra did against enemies accompanied by Vishnu (descended as his younger brother)."

shloka_text: हिरामस्यक्षिप्रमङ्कागतांसतीम् । अहंद्रक्ष्यामिसिद्धार्धांत्वांशत्रौविनिपातिते ।।6.33.33।।
explanation: "When the enemy is killed, and your objective is accomplished, I shall behold you mounted on the lap of Rama."

shloka_text: अश्रूण्यानन्दजानित्वंवर्तयिष्यसिशोभने । समागम्यपरिष्वज्यतस्योरसिमहोरसः ।।6.33.34।।
explanation: "Virtuous Sita! Hugged by your broad chested Rama, you will shed tears of joy on his bosom."

shloka_text: अचिरान्मोक्ष्यतेसीते देवितेजघनंगताम् । धृतामेताम्बहून्मासान्वेणींरामोमहाबलः ।।6.33.35।।
explanation: "O Sita! God like lady! Mighty Rama will soon release your single plait hanging up to hind part for many months before."

shloka_text: तस्यदृष्टवामुखंदेवी पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम् । मोक्ष्यसेशोकजंवारिनिर्मोकमिवपन्नगी ।।6.33.36।।
explanation: "God like Lady! Beholding the face of Sri Rama whose face is like a just risen full moon, you will cast off tears of sorrow just as a female snake sets its slough free."

shloka_text: रावणंसमरेहत्वानचिराद्धेवी: मैथिली: । त्वयासमग्रःप्रिययासुखार्होलप्स्यतेसुखम् ।।6.33.37।।
explanation: "O divine Mythili! Killing Ravana in war before long, your beloved who deserves to be happy will be happy in the company of his beloved."

shloka_text: समागतात्वंवीर्येणमोदिष्यसिमहात्मना । सुवर्षेणसमायुक्तायथासस्येनमेदिनी ।।6.33.38।।
explanation: "Just as the earth becomes green with crops blessed with good monsoon, so also you will become joyful by seeing the great soul Rama's heroism."

shloka_text: अथतांजातन्तापांतेनवाक्येनमोहिताम् । सरमाह्लादयामासमहींघौरीमिवाम्भसा ।।6.34.1।।
explanation: Thus, Sita's agony was put off by Saarana's consoling words and Sita was glad just as the parched earth was delighted with shower of rain.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्याहितंसख्याश्चिकीर्षन्तीसखीवचः । उवाचकालेकालज्ञास्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी ।।6.34.2।।
explanation: Then Saarana who knew the right time to do so, wishing the welfare of her dear friend Sita and desirous of doing anything for her smiled before she started speaking.

shloka_text: उत्सहेयमहंगत्वात्वद्वाक्यमसितेक्षणे: । निवेद्यकुशलंरामेप्रतिच्छन्नानिवर्तितुम् ।।6.34.3।।
explanation: "Darkeyed Sita! I am eager to go (to Rama's presence) and communicate your welfare and message. I can return back hidden (from Ravana's view)."

shloka_text: नहिमेक्रममाणायानिरालम्बेविहायसि । समर्थोगतिमन्वेतुंपवनोगरुडोऽपिवा ।।6.34.4।।
explanation: "While I fly through the sky without any support, either the wind god or even Garuda will not be capable of following my movement."

shloka_text: एवंब्रुवाणांतांसीतासरमांपुनरब्रवीत् । मधुरंश्लक्क्षणयावाचापूर्वशोकाभिपन्नया ।।6.34.5।।
explanation: When Saarana was telling Sita in that way, Sita's face which was earlier filled with tears became pleasant and she spoke again.

shloka_text: समर्थागगनंगन्तुमपिवात्वंरसातलम् । अवगच्छाम्यकर्तव्यंकर्तव्यंतेमदन्तरे ।।6.34.6।।
explanation: "You are capable of flying through the sky or even going to the underworld. For my sake you will do what cannot be done also and that it is your bounden duty, is also known to me."

shloka_text: मत्प्रियंयदिकर्तव्यंयदिबुद्धि: स्थिरातव । ज्ञातुमिच्छामितंगत्वाकिंकरोतीतिरावणः ।।6.34.7।।
explanation: "In my opinion, your duty for me is to go and find out what Ravana is doing now, if you are firmly resolved."

shloka_text: सहिमायाबलःक्रूरोरावणश्शत्रुरावणः । मांमोहयतिदुष्टात्मापीतामात्रेववारुणी ।।6.34.8।।
explanation: "Ravana has the power of conjuring tricks, makes enemies cry. He is cruel, evil minded and deluding me as though he has drunk liquor."

shloka_text: तर्जापयतिमांनित्यंभर्त्सापयतिचासकृत् । राक्षसीभिस्सुघूराभिर्यामांरक्षन्तिनित्यशः ।।6.34.9।।
explanation: "He, that Ravana makes even the frightful Rakshasa care takers threaten me and reproach me repeatedly every day."

shloka_text: उद्विग्नाशङ्किताचास्मिनस्वस्थंचमनोमम । तद्भयाच्चाहमुद्विग्नाअशोकवनिकांगता ।।6.34.10।।
explanation: "I am perturbed and doubtful (of my life). My mind is not at ease. Even though I am in Ashoka Grove I am disturbed."

shloka_text: यदिनामकथातस्यनिश्चितंवापियद्भवेत् । निवेदयेथास्सर्वंतत्परोमेस्यादमनुग्रहः ।।6.34.11।।
explanation: "Indeed, please tell me certainly in toot, whatever decision that enemy takes and everything. Be kind to me and tell."

shloka_text: सात्वेवंब्रुवतींसीतांसरमावल्गुभाषिणी । उवाचवदनंतस्यास्स्पृशन्तीबाष्पविक्लबम् ।।6.34.12।।
explanation: Saarana who speaks sweetly, kept wiping Sita's face covered with tears gently and replied in this manner.

shloka_text: एषतेयद्यभिप्रायस्तदागच्छामिजानकी: । गृह्यशत्रोरभिप्रायमुपावृत्तांचपश्यमाम् ।।6.34.13।।
explanation: "Janaki! If you think so, I shall go to Ravana secretly and find out his intention and return back."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाततोगत्वासमीपंतस्यरक्षसः । शुश्रावकथितंतस्यरावणस्यसमन्त्रिणः ।।6.34.14।।
explanation: Having said so to Sita, she (Saarana) moved closer (to Ravana) and heard Ravana's conversation with his ministers.

shloka_text: साश्रुत्वानिश्चयंतस्यनिश्चयज्ञादुरात्मनः । पुनरेवागमत्क्षिप्रमशोकवनिकांशुभाम् ।।6.34.15।।
explanation: Having heard and known the intention of evilminded Ravana, she (Saarana) quickly reached the beautiful Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: साप्रविष्टाततस्तत्रददर्शजनकात्मजाम् । प्रतीक्षमाणांस्वामेवभ्रष्टपद्मामिवश्रियम् ।।6.34.16।।
explanation: On entering the Ashoka grove, she saw the daughter of Janaka eagerly waiting for her every moment, looking like Lord Vishnu's wife Lakshmi, who lost her lotus seat.

shloka_text: तांतुसीतापुनःप्राप्तांसरमांवल्गुभाषिणीम् । परिष्वज्यचसुस्निग्धंददौचस्वयमासनम् ।।6.34.17।।
explanation: On seeing the kind Saarana returning, Sita was very glad. She embraced her and offered a seat herself.

shloka_text: इहासीनासुखंसर्वमाख्याहिममतत्त्वतः । क्रूरस्यनिश्चयंतस्यरावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।।6.34.18।।
explanation: "Seated here happily reveals to me truly that cruel and evil minded Ravana's intention."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तातुसरमासीतयावेपमानया । कथितंसर्वमाचष्टेरावणस्यसमन्त्रिणः ।।6.33.19।।
explanation: To the trembling Sita, Saarana narrated totally all the discussion Ravana had with the ministers.

shloka_text: जनन्याराक्षसेन्द्रोवैत्वन्मोक्षार्थंबृहद्वचः । अविद्धेनचवैदेहिमन्त्रिवृद्धेनबोधितः ।।6.33.20।।
explanation: "O Vaidehi! Ravana's mother Kaikasi and the aged minister Aviddha advised the Lord of Rakshasas to release you."

shloka_text: दीयतामभिसत्कृत्यमनुजेन्द्रायमैथिली । निदर्शनंतेपर्याप्तंजनस्थानेयदद्भुतम् ।।6.34.21।।
explanation: "Let Mythili be given back to the ruler of the people (Rama) offering good hospitality. The (killing of fourteen thousand Rakshasas) amazing performance at Janasthana by Rama should serve as sufficient proof to you (of the consequences)."

shloka_text: लङ्घनंचसमुद्रस्यदर्शनंचहनूमतः । वधंचरक्षसांयुद्धेकःकुर्यान्मानुषोभुवि ।।6.34.22।।
explanation: "Crossing the ocean, reaching Lanka, seeing Sita and killing Rakshasas in comb at was done by Hanuman. Which man can do this on earth?"

shloka_text: एवंसमन्त्रिवृद्धैश्चाविद्धेनबहुभाषितः । नत्वामुत्पनिहतेमोक्तुमर्थमर्थपरोयथा ।।6.34.23।।
explanation: "Even though his mother and aged minister counselled Ravana, he is like a miser holding on treasure not inclined to set you free."

shloka_text: नोत्सहत्यमृतोमोक्तुंयुद्धेत्वामितिमैथिली: । सामात्यस्यनृशंसस्यनिश्चयोह्येषवर्तते ।।6.34.24।।
explanation: "O Mythili! Ravana is not interested in liberating you unless he goes to the other world in combat. (It can't happen when he is alive) This is certain. There is no doubt about this."

shloka_text: तदेषासुस्थिराबुद्धिर्मृत्युलोभादुपस्थिता । भयान्नशक्तस्त्वांमोक्तुमनिरस्तस्संयुगे ।।6.34.25।। रक्षसानांचसर्वेषामात्मनश्चवधेनहि ।
explanation: "This thought has come to him only to cause him death. Because of impending death, he is very steady in his mind. This Ravana will not be able to liberate you before his death and of the Rakshasas."

shloka_text: निहत्यरावणंसङ् ख्येसर्वथानिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.34.26।। प्रतिनेष्यतिरामस्त्वामयोध्यामसितेक्षणे: ।
explanation: "Rama will kill Ravana in war with his sharp arrows and take you back to Ayodhya, O darkeyed lady!"

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेशब्दोभेरीशङ्खसमाकुलः ।।6.34.27।। श्रुतोवानरसैन्यानांकम्पयन् धरणीतलम् ।
explanation: In the meantime (while Saarana was telling Sita) the sounds of drums and conchs combined with the clamour of Vanara troops was heard and it was as though the surface of the earth was shaking.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुतद्वानरसैन्यशब्दंलङ्कागताराक्षसराजभृत्याः । नष्टौजसोदैन्यरीतचेष्टाःश्रेयोनपश्यन्तिनृपस्यदोषैः ।।6.34.28।।
explanation: On hearing the sounds of Vanara troops, the Rakshasas present in Lanka became dull, overcome by depression, thinking that because of Ravana's mistakes they could not see any good prospects for them. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचतुस्त्रिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेनशङ्खविमिश्रेणभेरीशब्देनराघवः । उपयातिमहाबाहूरामःपरपुरञ्जयः ।।6.35.1।।
explanation: The mighty armed Rama, the conqueror of enemy cities, Raghava marched forth with the noise of the blowing of conches and the sounds of drums.

shloka_text: तंनिनादंनिशम्याथरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । मुहूर्तंध्यानमास्थायसचिवानभ्युदैक्षत ।।6.35.2।।
explanation: Ravana, the Lord of Rakshasas, looked at his ministers on hearing the sounds and reflecting for a moment.

shloka_text: अथतान्सचिवांस्तत्रसर्वानाभाष्यरावणः । सभांसन्नादयन् सर्वामित्युवाचमहाबलः ।।6.35.3।। जगत्सन्तापन्क्रूरोगर्हयन्राक्षसेश्वरः ।
explanation: Thereafter the mighty Lord of Rakshasas, a cruel one, a scourge of the world addressed the assembly of his ministers and spoke abusing them.

shloka_text: तरणंसागरस्यापिविक्रमंबलसञ्जियम् ।।6.35.4।। यदुक्तवन्तोरामस्यभवन्तस्तन्मयाश्रुतम् ।
explanation: "You have told me about the valour of Hanuman the messenger of Rama and his prowess in crossing the ocean which I heard just now."

shloka_text: भवतश्चाप्यहंवेमदियुद्धेसत्यपराक्रमान् ।।6.35.5।। तूषिकानीक्षतोऽन्योन्यंविदित्वारामविक्रमम् ।
explanation: "Even though you are truly valorous in war, on knowing Rama's prowess, you are standing mute looking at each other. I know that."

shloka_text: ततस्तुसुमहाप्राज्ञोमाल्यवान्नामराक्षसः ।।6.35.6।। रावणस्यवचश्श्रुत्वामातुःपैतामहोऽब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Then, Malyavan the maternal grandfather of Ravana, a very wise Rakshasa indeed said this on hearing Ravana's statement.

shloka_text: विद्यास्वभिविनीतोयोराजाराजन्नयानुगः ।।6.35.7।। सशास्तिचिरमैश्वर्यमरींश्चकुरुतेवशे ।
explanation: "O king! Whoever is well versed in all the fourteen sciences and is a follower of justice, he alone wins over enemies and rules the kingdom for long."

shloka_text: सन्दधानोहिकालेनविगृह्णंश्चारिभिस्सह ।।6.35.8।। स्वपक्षवर्थनंकुर्वन्महदैश्वर्यमश्नुते ।
explanation: "Continuing to act in that way in course of time a king who encounters his enemies and expands his own side, enjoys great sovereignty."

shloka_text: हीयमानेनकर्तव्योराज्ञासन्धिस्समेवच ।।6.35.9।। नशत्रुमवमन्येतज्यायान्कुर्वीतविग्रहम् ।
explanation: "When a king is losing strength, he should join hand s with the enemy who is equal to him. He should not disrespect the enemy but quit his hostility and join him (if the enemy is more powerful)."

shloka_text: तन्मह्यंरोचतेसन्धिस्सहरामेणरावण ।।6.35.10।। यदर्थमभियुक्ता: स्मसीतातस्मैप्रदीयताम् ।
explanation: "O Ravana! Joining with that Rama is agreeable to me. Let that Sita for whose sake you have been attacked be restored to him."

shloka_text: यस्यदेवर्षयस्सर्वेगन्धर्वाश्चजयैषिणः ।।6.35.11।। विरोथंमागमस्तेनसन्धिस्तेतेनरोचताम् ।
explanation: All the celestial sages and Gandharvas are wishing him victory. Therefore, do not have enmity. Making an alliance with him is desirable for you.

shloka_text: असृजद्भगवान्पक्षौद्वावेनहिपितामहः ।।6.35.12।। सुराणामसुराणांचधर्माधर्मौतदाश्रयौ ।
explanation: "The divine Brahma, the grandfather of the universe created two orders, deities and devils. They took the refuge of virtues and vices respectively."

shloka_text: धर्मोहिश्रूयतेपक्षीह्यमराणांमहात्मनाम् ।।6.35.13।। अधर्मोरक्षसांपक्षोह्यसुराणांचराक्षस ।
explanation: "The great souls were towards righteousness and Rakshasas took the side of unrighteousness."

shloka_text: धर्मोवैग्रसतेऽधर्मंततःकृतमभूद्युगम् ।।6.35.14।। अधर्मोग्रसतेधर्मंततस्तिष्यःप्रवर्तते ।
explanation: "When moral merit destroys unrighteousness, it is called Krtayuga. So also, when virtue gets eclipsed by unrighteousness, it is called Kaliyuga."

shloka_text: तत्त्वयाचरयालोकान्धर्मोपिविनिहतोमहान् ।।6.35.15।। अधर्मःप्रगृहीतश्चतेनास्मद्बलिनःपरे ।
explanation: "While you were ranging in all the worlds, you gave up righteousness and embraced unrighteousness. Therefore, the enemy who is righteous is stronger than you."

shloka_text: सप्रमादावदिवृद्धस्तेऽधर्मोहिग्रसतेहिनः ।।6.35.16।। विवर्थयतिपक्षंचसुराणांसुरभावनः ।
explanation: "You are nourishing unrighteousness mistakenly. Therefore, it is going to swallow us. It has become the cause for the divine celestial side to become powerful."

shloka_text: विषयेषुप्रसक्तेनयत्किञ्चित्कारणात्वया ।।6.35.17।। ऋषीणामग्नकल्पानामुद्वेगोजनितोमहान् ।
explanation: "Being engaged in matters of sense pleasures you have created great agitation(disturbance) in the minds of the seers (engaged in penance) who resemble gods of burning fire."

shloka_text: तेषांप्रभावोदुर्धर्षःप्रदीप्तइवपावकः ।।6.35.18।। तपसाभावितात्मानोधर्मस्यानुग्रहेरताः । मुख्यर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येतेनित्यंतैस्सैर्द्विजातयः ।।6.35.19।। जुह्वत्यनगींश्चविधिवद्वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते । अभिभूयचरक्षांसिब्रह्मघोषानुदैरयन् ।।6.35.20।। दिशोऽपिविद्रुतास्सर्वेस्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे ।
explanation: "Their power is difficult to overcome as they are pure souls and blazing like fire by their austerity. They follow virtues faithfully intending to acquire merit like brahmanas. They are standing firmly curbing their senses doing sacrifices offering oblations into sacrificial fires following tradition. Having subdued the Rakshasas, they are continuing to recite Vedas and on hearing Vedas the Rakshasas are running away in different directions like the rain cloud is scattered in the hot season."

shloka_text: तेषांप्रभावोदुर्धर्षःप्रदीप्तइवपावकः ।।6.35.18।। तपसाभावितात्मानोधर्मस्यानुग्रहेरताः । मुख्यर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येतेनित्यंतैस्सैर्द्विजातयः ।।6.35.19।। जुह्वत्यनगींश्चविधिवद्वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते । अभिभूयचरक्षांसिब्रह्मघोषानुदैरयन् ।।6.35.20।। दिशोऽपिविद्रुतास्सर्वेस्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे ।
explanation: "Their power is difficult to overcome as they are pure souls and blazing like fire by their austerity. They follow virtues faithfully intending to acquire merit like brahmanas. They are standing firmly curbing their senses doing sacrifices offering oblations into sacrificial fires following tradition. Having subdued the Rakshasas, they are continuing to recite Vedas and on hearing Vedas the Rakshasas are running away in different directions like the rain cloud is scattered in the hot season."

shloka_text: तेषांप्रभावोदुर्धर्षःप्रदीप्तइवपावकः ।।6.35.18।। तपसाभावितात्मानोधर्मस्यानुग्रहेरताः । मुख्यर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येतेनित्यंतैस्सैर्द्विजातयः ।।6.35.19।। जुह्वत्यनगींश्चविधिवद्वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते । अभिभूयचरक्षांसिब्रह्मघोषानुदैरयन् ।।6.35.20।। दिशोऽपिविद्रुतास्सर्वेस्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे ।
explanation: "Their power is difficult to overcome as they are pure souls and blazing like fire by their austerity. They follow virtues faithfully intending to acquire merit like brahmanas. They are standing firmly curbing their senses doing sacrifices offering oblations into sacrificial fires following tradition. Having subdued the Rakshasas, they are continuing to recite Vedas and on hearing Vedas the Rakshasas are running away in different directions like the rain cloud is scattered in the hot season."

shloka_text: ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामग्निहोत्रासमुत्थितः ।।6.35.21।। अदत्तेरक्षसांतेजोधूमोव्याप्यदिशोदश ।
explanation: "By the spread of smoke in different directions from the sacrificial fires from the oblations offered by the seers the brilliance of the Rakshasas is taken away."

shloka_text: तेषुतेषुचदेशेषुपुण्येष्वेवदृढव्रतैः ।।6.35.22।। चर्यमाणंतपस्तीव्रंसन्तापयतिराक्षसान् ।
explanation: "The intense austerities performed by the sages in different regions determined firmly are tormenting the Rakshasas."

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षेभ्योगृहीतश्चवरस्त्वया ।।6.35.23।। मनुषावानराऋक्षागोलाङ्गूलामहाबलाः । बलवन्तइहागम्यगर्जन्तीदृढविक्रमाः ।।6.35.24।।
explanation: "You have secured boons of immunity against death at the hand s of strong and mighty and powerful valour, like gods, Danavas, Yakshas and human beings. The Vanaras, Bears and monkeys with dark faces are coming here now thundering."

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षेभ्योगृहीतश्चवरस्त्वया ।।6.35.23।। मनुषावानराऋक्षागोलाङ्गूलामहाबलाः । बलवन्तइहागम्यगर्जन्तीदृढविक्रमाः ।।6.35.24।।
explanation: "You have secured boons of immunity against death at the hand s of strong and mighty and powerful valour, like gods, Danavas, Yakshas and human beings. The Vanaras, Bears and monkeys with dark faces are coming here now thundering."

shloka_text: उत्पातान्विविधान्दृष्टवाघोरन्बहुविधांस्तथा । विनाशमनुपश्यामिसर्वेषांरक्षसामहम् ।।6.35.25।।
explanation: "Beholding different dreadful ones rising up in various directions, I foresee destruction of all Rakshasas."

shloka_text: खराभिस्न्तिताघोरामेघाःप्रतिभयङ्कराः । शोणितेनाभिवर्षन्तिलङ्कामुष्णेनसर्वतः ।।6.35.26।।
explanation: "Formidable clouds are emitting hot and most frightening thunder drenched by rain of blood all over Lanka."

shloka_text: रुदतांवाहनानांचप्रपवन्त्यौस्रबिन्दवः । ध्वजाध्वस्ताविवर्णाश्चनप्रभान्तियथापुरम् ।।6.35.27।।
explanation: "With tear drops falling from the eyes of weeping horses and elephants (carrying army) they are discoloured by dust and are not shining like before."

shloka_text: व्याळागोमायवोगृध्रावाश्यन्तिचसुभैरवम् । प्रविश्यलङ्कामनिशंसमवायांश्चकुर्वते ।।6.35.28।।
explanation: "Wicked jackals and vultures are entering deep into Lanka and gathering. They are crying most frightfully."

shloka_text: काळिकाःपाण्डुरैर्दन्तै: प्रहसन्त्यग्रतःस्थिताः । स्त्रियस्स्वप्नेषुमुष्ण्नत्योगृहाणिप्रतिभाष्यच ।।6.35.29।।
explanation: "Women of dark colour like coal with yellow teeth are speaking unpleasant things standing before us in dreams laughing heartily."

shloka_text: गृहाणांबलिकर्माणिश्वानःपर्युपभुञ्जते । खरागोषुप्रजायन्तेमूषकानकुलैस्सह ।।6.35.30।।
explanation: "In the houses, food offerings made for gods are eaten by dogs, donkeys are procreating cows and rats of mongoose."

shloka_text: मार्जाराद्वीपिभिस्सार्थंसूकराश्शुनकैस्सह । किन्नराराक्षसैश्चापिसमीयुर्मानुषैस्सह ।।6.35.31।।
explanation: "Cats are having the company of (mating) Leopards, pigs are mating with dogs, Kinneras with Rakshasas as well as human beings also."

shloka_text: पाण्डुरारक्तपादाश्चविहङ्गाःकालचोदिताः । राक्षसानांविनाशायकपोताविचरन्तिच ।।6.35.32।।
explanation: "The white and redfooted doves are moving about impelled by time spirit boding destruction of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: वीचीकूचीतिवाश्य्नत्यश्शारिकावेश्मसुस्थिताः । पतन्तिग्रथिताश्चापिनिर्जिताःकलहैषिणः ।।6.35.33।।
explanation: "Minas living in households grappling with bellicose birds in delight are falling down dead."

shloka_text: पक्षिणश्चमृगास्सर्वेप्रत्यादित्यंरुदन्तिच । कराळोविकटोमुण्डःपुरुषःकष्णपिङ्गळः ।।6.35.34।। कालोगृहाणिसर्वेषांकालेकालेऽन्ववेक्षते । एतान्यन्यानिदुष्टानिनिमित्तान्युत्पतन्तिच ।।6.35.35।।
explanation: All birds and animals are making hostile noise. Time is always coming in a dreadful and monstrous blackish form with a shaved head, morning, and evening. Considering all these sinister portents are making an appearance at all households.

shloka_text: पक्षिणश्चमृगास्सर्वेप्रत्यादित्यंरुदन्तिच । कराळोविकटोमुण्डःपुरुषःकष्णपिङ्गळः ।।6.35.34।। कालोगृहाणिसर्वेषांकालेकालेऽन्ववेक्षते । एतान्यन्यानिदुष्टानिनिमित्तान्युत्पतन्तिच ।।6.35.35।।
explanation: All birds and animals are making hostile noise. Time is always coming in a dreadful and monstrous blackish form with a shaved head, morning, and evening. Considering all these sinister portents are making an appearance at all households.

shloka_text: विष्णुंमन्यामहेरामंमानुषंरूपमास्थितम् । नहिमानुषमात्रोऽसौराघवोदृढविक्रमः ।।6.35.36।। येनबद्धःसमुद्रेचसेतुःसपरमाद्भुतः । कुरुष्वनरराजेनसधनिंरामेणरावण ।।6.35.37।। ज्ञात्वावधार्यकर्माणिक्रियतामायतिक्षमम् ।
explanation: Rama is Lord Vishnu in human form endowed with fortitude and prowess. One who has constructed an amazing bridge on the ocean is not just a human being. O Ravana! Align with the ruler of men, Sri Rama. After careful thinking and determining correctly, do what is good.

shloka_text: विष्णुंमन्यामहेरामंमानुषंरूपमास्थितम् । नहिमानुषमात्रोऽसौराघवोदृढविक्रमः ।।6.35.36।। येनबद्धःसमुद्रेचसेतुःसपरमाद्भुतः । कुरुष्वनरराजेनसधनिंरामेणरावण ।।6.35.37।। ज्ञात्वावधार्यकर्माणिक्रियतामायतिक्षमम् ।
explanation: Rama is Lord Vishnu in human form endowed with fortitude and prowess. One who has constructed an amazing bridge on the ocean is not just a human being. O Ravana! Align with the ruler of men, Sri Rama. After careful thinking and determining correctly, do what is good.

shloka_text: तत्तुमाल्यवतोवाक्यंहितमुक्तंदशाननः । नमर्षयतिदुष्टात्माकालस्यवशमागतः ।।6.36.1।।
explanation: The tenheaded Ravana, having fallen under the sway of death could not tolerate Malyavatha's words of advice.

shloka_text: नबद् ध्वाभ्रुकुटींवक्त्रेक्रोधस्यवशमागतः । अमर्षात्परिवृत्ताक्षोमाल्यवन्तमथाब्रवीत् ।।6.36.2।।
explanation: Then Ravana who had come under the influence of anger, knitting the brows of his face rolling his eyes said to Malyavan.

shloka_text: हितबुध्यायदहितंवचःपरुषमुच्यते । परपक्षंप्रनिश्यैवनैतच्च्रोत्रगतंमम ।।6.36.3।।
explanation: "Harsh and not wellmeaning words have been uttered by you taking the enemy's side. I will not listen to what you said earlier."

shloka_text: मानुषंकृपणंराममेकंशाखामृगाश्रयम् । समर्थंमन्यसेकेनत्यक्तंपित्रावनालयम् ।।6.36.4।।
explanation: "For what reason do you say that a wretched human being, alone, forsaken by a father who has taken asylum in the forest, who is taking the help of vanaras is capable?"

shloka_text: रक्षसामीश्वरंमांचदेवानांचभयङ्करम् । हीनंमांमन्यसेकेनह्यहीनंसर्वविक्रमैः ।।6.36.5।।
explanation: "The Lord of Rakshasas is a terror to all including the Devas and am endowed with all kinds of prowess and efficiency. Why do you think I am deficient?"

shloka_text: वीरद्वेषेणवाशङ्केपक्षपातेनवारिपोः । त्वयाहंपरुषाण्युक्तःपरप्रोत्साहनेनवा ।।6.36.6।।
explanation: "I suspect that out of hatred towards me, you are speaking such harsh words to a hero encouraged by the enemy."

shloka_text: प्रभवन्तंपदस्थंहिपरुषंकोऽभिभाषते । पण्डितश्शास्त्रतत्त्वज्ञोविनाप्रोत्साहनाद्रिपोः ।।6.36.7।।
explanation: "Which person who has learned the truth of sastras will address such harsh words to one in power without instigation?"

shloka_text: आनीयचवनासतीतांपद्महीनामिवश्रियम् । किमर्थंप्रतिदास्यामिराघवस्यभयादहम् ।।6.36.8।।
explanation: "Sita who is like Lakshmi without the lotus has been brought from the forest. Why would I return her for the fear of Rama?"

shloka_text: वृतंवानरकोटीभिस्ससुग्रीवंसलक्ष्मणम् । पश्यकैश्चिदहोभिस्त्वंराघवंनिहतंमया ।।6.36.9।।
explanation: "Indeed, in a short while crores of Vanaras, Sugriva and also Lakshmana and Raghava will be killed by me. Oh!"

shloka_text: द्वन्द्वेयस्यनतिष्ठन्तिदैवतान्यपिसंयुगे । सकस्माद्रावणोयुद्धेभयमाहारयिष्यति ।।6.36.10।।
explanation: As even gods will not with stand Ravana in war, of whom Ravana will be afraid of in a duel.

shloka_text: द्विधाभज्येयमप्येवंननमेयंतुकस्यचित् । एषमेसहजोदोषस्स्वभावोदुरतिक्रमः ।।6.36.11।।
explanation: "I would break my head into two also but not bend my head to anyone. It is my weakness. It is hard to overcome nature."

shloka_text: यदितावत्समुद्रेतुसेतुर्बद्धोयदृच्छया । रामेणविस्मयःकोऽत्रयेवमेभयमागतम् ।।6.36.12।।
explanation: "Rama has constructed a bridge by chance and because of that you are fearing what wonder is there in it?"

shloka_text: सतुतीर्त्वार्णवंरामस्सहवानरसेनया । प्रतिजानामितेसत्यंनजीवन्प्रतियास्यति ।।6.36.13।।
explanation: "Rama having crossed the sea with his Vanara army will not go back with life. It is true."

shloka_text: एवंब्रुवाणंसंरब्धंरुष्टंविज्ञायरावणम् । व्रीळितोमाल्यवान्वाक्यंनोत्तरंप्रत्यपद्यत ।।6.36.14।।
explanation: When Ravana was abashed and speaking in that way realizing that he is angry, Malyavan did not reply feeling shy.

shloka_text: जयाशिषाचराजानंवर्धयित्वायथोचितम् । माल्यवानभ्यनुज्ञातोजगामस्वंनिवेशनम् ।।6.36.15।।
explanation: Malyavan offered blessings to the king for success in accordance with tradition left to his house.

shloka_text: रावणस्तुसहामात्योमन्त्रयित्वाविमृश्यच । लङ्कायामतुलांगुप्तिंकारयामासराक्षसः ।।6.36.16।।
explanation: Ravana then held discussions with his companions and ministers and made unequalled arrangements for (safety of) Lanka.

shloka_text: व्यादिदेशसपूर्वस्यांप्रहस्तंद्वारिराक्षसम् । दक्षिणस्यांमहावीर्यौमहापार्श्वमहादरौ ।।6.36.17।। पश्चिमायामथोद्वारिपुत्रमिन्द्रजितंतदा । व्यादिदेशमयामायंबहूभीराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतम् ।।6.36.18।।
explanation: Ravana posted Prahastha surrounded by many Rakshasas at the east gate, and the Rakshasas of great prowess, Mahaparsva and Mahodara at the southern gate, and like that Mahamaya and Indrajith, his own son at the western gate.

shloka_text: व्यादिदेशसपूर्वस्यांप्रहस्तंद्वारिराक्षसम् । दक्षिणस्यांमहावीर्यौमहापार्श्वमहादरौ ।।6.36.17।। पश्चिमायामथोद्वारिपुत्रमिन्द्रजितंतदा । व्यादिदेशमयामायंबहूभीराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतम् ।।6.36.18।।
explanation: Ravana posted Prahastha surrounded by many Rakshasas at the east gate, and the Rakshasas of great prowess, Mahaparsva and Mahodara at the southern gate, and like that Mahamaya and Indrajith, his own son at the western gate.

shloka_text: उतरस्यांपुरद्वारिव्यादिश्यशुकसारणौ । स्वयंचात्रगमिष्यामिमन्त्रिणस्तानुवाचह ।।6.36.19।।
explanation: Ravana posted Suka and Sarana at the north gate of Lanka and himself reached there and told the ministers that he would be there.

shloka_text: राक्षसांतुविरूपाक्षंमहावीर्यपराक्रमम् । मध्यमेऽस्थापयद्गुल्मेबहुभिस्सहराक्षसैः ।।6.36.20।।
explanation: In the middle of the city, he placed Virupaksha, a Rakshasa endowed with extraordinary strength and many more Rakshasas.

shloka_text: एवंविधानंलङ्कायांकृत्वाराक्षसपुङ्गवः । कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानंमन्यतेकालचोदितः ।।6.36.21।।
explanation: The best of Rakshasas under the sway of destiny, having been ordered in that way in Lanka, Ravana felt as though he had accomplished the task.

shloka_text: विसर्जयामासततस्समन्त्रिणोविधानमाज्ञाप्यपुरस्यपुष्कलम् । जयाशिषामन्त्रिगणेनपूजितोविवेशचाऽन्तःपुरमृद्धिमन्महत् ।।6.36.22।।
explanation: There after making arrangements adequately for the protection of Lanka, taking leave of ministers who offered blessings for his prosperity and uttered words of benediction for his success Ravana entered the inner chambers of the palace. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषटित्रंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: नरवानरराजौतौसतुवायुसुतःकपिः । जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्चराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।।6.37.1।। अङ्गदोवालिपुत्रश्चसौमित्रिश्शरभःकपिः । सुषेणस्सहदायादोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.37.2।। गजोगवाक्षःकुमुदोनलोऽथपनसस्तथा । अमित्रविषयंप्राप्तास्समवेतास्समर्धयन् ।।6.37.3।।
explanation: Sugriva the king of men and monkeys, Hanuman the son of wind god, Jambavan the king of Bears, Vibheeshana, Vali's son Angada, Sarabha, accompanied by his kin Sushena, Mainda, Dwivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Kumuda, the wise Nala and Panasa arrived at the enemy city and collected together thought like this.

shloka_text: नरवानरराजौतौसतुवायुसुतःकपिः । जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्चराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।।6.37.1।। अङ्गदोवालिपुत्रश्चसौमित्रिश्शरभःकपिः । सुषेणस्सहदायादोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.37.2।। गजोगवाक्षःकुमुदोनलोऽथपनसस्तथा । अमित्रविषयंप्राप्तास्समवेतास्समर्धयन् ।।6.37.3।।
explanation: Sugriva the king of men and monkeys, Hanuman the son of wind god, Jambavan the king of Bears, Vibheeshana, Vali's son Angada, Sarabha, accompanied by his kin Sushena, Mainda, Dwivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Kumuda, the wise Nala and Panasa arrived at the enemy city and collected together thought like this.

shloka_text: नरवानरराजौतौसतुवायुसुतःकपिः । जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्चराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।।6.37.1।। अङ्गदोवालिपुत्रश्चसौमित्रिश्शरभःकपिः । सुषेणस्सहदायादोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.37.2।। गजोगवाक्षःकुमुदोनलोऽथपनसस्तथा । अमित्रविषयंप्राप्तास्समवेतास्समर्धयन् ।।6.37.3।।
explanation: Sugriva the king of men and monkeys, Hanuman the son of wind god, Jambavan the king of Bears, Vibheeshana, Vali's son Angada, Sarabha, accompanied by his kin Sushena, Mainda, Dwivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Kumuda, the wise Nala and Panasa arrived at the enemy city and collected together thought like this.

shloka_text: इयंसालक्षयतेलङ्कापुरीरावणपालिता । सासुरोरगगन्धर्वैरमरैरपिदुर्जया ।।6.37.4।।
explanation: "This Lanka city ruled by Ravana is seen. It appears that this city is unconquerable to Devas, demons and Gandharvas also by the immortals."

shloka_text: कार्यसिद्धिंपुरस्कृत्यमन्द्रयध्वंविनिर्णये । नित्यंसन्निहितोह्यत्ररावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.37.5।।
explanation: "Rakshasa king Ravana is ever present here. Prepare yourself to achieve success in the mission and determine your duty."

shloka_text: तथातेषुब्रुवाणेषुरावणावरजोऽब्रवीत् । वाक्यमग्राम्यपदवत्पुष्कलार्धंविभीषणः ।।6.37.6।।
explanation: While they were speaking like that to one another, Ravana's brother Vibheeshana spoke courteously, words full of meaning.

shloka_text: अनलश्शरभश्चैवसम्पातिःप्रघसस्तथा । गत्वालङ्कांममामात्याःपुरींपुनरिहागताः ।।6.37.7।।
explanation: "My ministers Anala, Sarabha, Sampathi and also Praghasa went to Lanka and saw it and returned."

shloka_text: भूत्वाशकुनयस्सर्वेप्रविष्टाश्चरिपोर्भलम् । विधानंविहितंयच्चतद्धृष्टवासमुपस्थिताः ।।6.37.8।।
explanation: All of them assumed the form of birds and went deep into Lanka, saw the enemy strength and arrangements made by the enemy and turned up.

shloka_text: संविधानंयथाहुस्तेरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । राम तद्ब्रुवतस्सर्वंयथात्त्वेनमेशृणु ।।6.37.9।।
explanation: "Rama! Alas, they told me everything of the way evil minded Ravana's army is organized as it is. Listen to me."

shloka_text: पूर्वंप्रहस्तस्सबलोद्वारमासाद्यतिष्ठति । दक्षिणंचमहावीर्यौमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.37.10।।
explanation: "Powerful Prahasta stands at east gate with army, Mahaparsva and Mahodara of great valour are at the south gate."

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्पश्चिमंद्वारंराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतः । पट्टसासिधनुष्मद्भिश्शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः ।।6.37.11।। नानाप्रहरणैश्शूरैरावृतोरावणात्मजः ।
explanation: "Ravana's own son, Indrajith stands at the west gate surrounded by numerous Rakshasas collected together wielding sharp swords, bows, spears, arrows and darts and many kinds of weapons."

shloka_text: राक्षसानांसहस्रैस्तुबहुभिश्शस्त्रपाणिभिः ।।6.37.12।। युक्तःपरमसंविग्नोराक्षर्भहुभिर्वृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारंरावणस्स्वयमास्थितः ।।6.37.13।।
explanation: "Ravana himself stands at the north gate of Lanka, highly agitated surrounded by many thousands of Rakshasas wielding weapons."

shloka_text: राक्षसानांसहस्रैस्तुबहुभिश्शस्त्रपाणिभिः ।।6.37.12।। युक्तःपरमसंविग्नोराक्षर्भहुभिर्वृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारंरावणस्स्वयमास्थितः ।।6.37.13।।
explanation: "Ravana himself stands at the north gate of Lanka, highly agitated surrounded by many thousands of Rakshasas wielding weapons."

shloka_text: विरूपाक्षस्तुमहताशूलखडगधनुष्मता । बलेनराक्षसैस्सार्थंमध्यमंगुल्ममास्थितः ।।6.37.14।।
explanation: "Virupaksha stands in the middle of Lanka wielding spears, swords, bows and arrows accompanied by mighty army."

shloka_text: एतानेवंविधान्गुल्मान् लङ्कायांसमुदीक्ष्यते । मामकामन्त्रिणस्सर्वेपुनशशीघ्रमिहागताः ।।6.37.15।।
explanation: All our ministers immediately returned back after keenly observing the city of Lanka in this way.

shloka_text: गजानांचसाहस्रंचरथानामयुतंपुरे । हयानामयुतेद्वेचसाग्राकोटीचरक्षसाम् ।।6.37.16।। विक्रान्ताबलवन्तश्चसंयुगेष्वाततायिनः । इष्टाराक्षसराजस्यनित्यमेतेनिशाचराः ।।6.37.17।।
explanation: "Elephant army of ten thousand, similarly ten thousand charioteers, horse riders in twenty thousand, more than a crore foot soldiers, mighty strong and valiant warriors, night ranger's beloved to Ravana, the king of Rakshasas were staying close and serving."

shloka_text: गजानांचसाहस्रंचरथानामयुतंपुरे । हयानामयुतेद्वेचसाग्राकोटीचरक्षसाम् ।।6.37.16।। विक्रान्ताबलवन्तश्चसंयुगेष्वाततायिनः । इष्टाराक्षसराजस्यनित्यमेतेनिशाचराः ।।6.37.17।।
explanation: "Elephant army of ten thousand, similarly ten thousand charioteers, horse riders in twenty thousand, more than a crore foot soldiers, mighty strong and valiant warriors, night ranger's beloved to Ravana, the king of Rakshasas were staying close and serving."

shloka_text: एकैकस्यात्रयुद्धार्थेराक्षसस्यविशाम्पते । परीवारस्सहस्राणांसहस्रमुपतिष्ठते ।।6.37.18।।
explanation: "O! Lord of men! For the sake of assisting one Rakshasa in war ten lakhs of Rakshasas are staying at his service."

shloka_text: एतांप्रवृत्तिंलङ्कायांमन्त्रिप्रोक्तांविभीषणः । एवमुक्त्वामहाबाहूराक्षसांस्तानदर्शयत् ।।6.37.19।।
explanation: Mighty armed Vibheeshana revealed to Rama all the information that was told to him by ministers.

shloka_text: लङ्कायांसचिवैस्सर्वंरामायप्रत्यवेदयत् । रामंकमलपत्राक्षमिदमुत्तरमब्रवीत् ।।6.37.20।। रावणावरजःश्रीमान् रामप्रियचिकीर्षया ।
explanation: Again, Vibheeshana, the prosperous brother of Ravana, spoke to Rama everything about Lanka made known to him by the ministers. Vibheeshana looking at the lotus petal eyed Rama, intending to please Rama, spoke.

shloka_text: कुबेरंतुयदाराम रावणःप्रत्ययुध्यत ।।6.37.21।। षष्टिश्शतसहस्राणितदानिर्यान्तिरक्षसाः । राक्रमेणवीर्येणतेजसासत्त्वगौरवात् ।।6.37.22।। सदृशाय्येऽत्रदर्पेणरावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।
explanation: "Rama! Earlier when Ravana launched an offensive battle against Kubera, sixty thousand Rakshasas who were equal to him in valour, brilliance, courage, and with respect sallied forth the proud, the evil minded Ravana."

shloka_text: कुबेरंतुयदाराम रावणःप्रत्ययुध्यत ।।6.37.21।। षष्टिश्शतसहस्राणितदानिर्यान्तिरक्षसाः । राक्रमेणवीर्येणतेजसासत्त्वगौरवात् ।।6.37.22।। सदृशाय्येऽत्रदर्पेणरावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।
explanation: "Rama! Earlier when Ravana launched an offensive battle against Kubera, sixty thousand Rakshasas who were equal to him in valour, brilliance, courage, and with respect sallied forth the proud, the evil minded Ravana."

shloka_text: अत्रमन्युर्नकर्तव्योरोषयेत्वांनभीषये ।।6.37.23।। समर्थोह्यसिवीर्येणसुराणामपिनिग्रहे ।
explanation: "Here, in this case do not be angry. I am telling out of my duty and not out of indignation or to cause anger or fear in you. You are capable of resisting even Devatas."

shloka_text: तद्भवांश्चतुरङ्गेणबलेनमहातावृतः ।।6.37.24।। व्यूह्येदंवानरानीकंनिर्मथिष्यतिरावणम् ।
explanation: "You also have these Vanara armies surrounded by four kinds of army, elephants, chariots, cavalry and foot soldiers."

shloka_text: रावणावरजेवाक्यमेवंब्रुवतिराघवः ।।6.37.25।। शत्रूणांप्रतिघातार्थमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: When Ravana's younger brother spoke in that way Raghava instructed the army to attack the enemy.

shloka_text: पूर्वद्वारेतुलङ्कायानीलोवानरपुङ्गवः ।।6.37.26।। प्रहस्तप्रतियोद्धास्याद्वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।
explanation: "Let the Vanara leader Neela along with Vanaras stay at the east gate of Lanka and give fight to Prahasta."

shloka_text: अङ्गदोवालिपुत्रस्तुबलेनमहतावृतः ।।6.37.27।। दक्षिणेबाधतांद्वारेमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।
explanation: "Let Vali's son the mighty and powerful Angada along with army crush Mahaparsva and Mahodara at the south gate."

shloka_text: हनुमान्पश्चिमद्वारंनिपीड्यपवनात्मजः ।।6.37.28।। प्रविशत्वप्रमेयात्माबहुभिःकपिभिर्वृतः ।
explanation: "Let Hanuman, the wind god's son of unimaginable prowess, enter the west gate along with numerous Vanaras and press against the enemy."

shloka_text: दैत्यदावनसङ्घानामृषीणांचमहात्मनाम् ।।6.37.29।। विप्रकारप्रियःक्षुद्रोवरदानबलान्वितः । परिक्रमतियःसर्वान्लोकान्सन्तापयन्प्रजाः ।।6.37.30।। तस्याहंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यस्वयमेववधेधृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारमहंसौमित्रिणासह ।।6.37.31।। निपीड्याभिप्रवेक्ष्यामिसबलोयत्ररावणः ।
explanation: "That Ravana who is harming Daityas and Danavas, and great souls following wicked practices and armed by the boons is oppressing all people wandering all over. I, with Lakshmana, have determined to persecute and kill him and force my entry to the north gate."

shloka_text: दैत्यदावनसङ्घानामृषीणांचमहात्मनाम् ।।6.37.29।। विप्रकारप्रियःक्षुद्रोवरदानबलान्वितः । परिक्रमतियःसर्वान्लोकान्सन्तापयन्प्रजाः ।।6.37.30।। तस्याहंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यस्वयमेववधेधृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारमहंसौमित्रिणासह ।।6.37.31।। निपीड्याभिप्रवेक्ष्यामिसबलोयत्ररावणः ।
explanation: "That Ravana who is harming Daityas and Danavas, and great souls following wicked practices and armed by the boons is oppressing all people wandering all over. I, with Lakshmana, have determined to persecute and kill him and force my entry to the north gate."

shloka_text: दैत्यदावनसङ्घानामृषीणांचमहात्मनाम् ।।6.37.29।। विप्रकारप्रियःक्षुद्रोवरदानबलान्वितः । परिक्रमतियःसर्वान्लोकान्सन्तापयन्प्रजाः ।।6.37.30।। तस्याहंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यस्वयमेववधेधृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारमहंसौमित्रिणासह ।।6.37.31।। निपीड्याभिप्रवेक्ष्यामिसबलोयत्ररावणः ।
explanation: "That Ravana who is harming Daityas and Danavas, and great souls following wicked practices and armed by the boons is oppressing all people wandering all over. I, with Lakshmana, have determined to persecute and kill him and force my entry to the north gate."

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्रश्चबलवानृक्षराजश्चवीर्यवान् ।।6.37.32।। राक्षसेन्द्रानुजश्चैवगुलोभवतुमध्यम: ।
explanation: "Mighty strong Sugriva, valorous Jambavan, the ruler of Vanaras and Vibheeshana, brother of Ravana will remain at the middle of Lanka and fight."

shloka_text: नचैवमानुषंरूपंकार्यंहरिभिराहवे ।।6.37.33।। एषाभवतुसंङञान् युद्धेऽस्मिन् वानरेबले ।
explanation: "In the battle like this at present Vanaras should not be in the semblance of humans. Let this be our sign."

shloka_text: वानराएवनश्चिह्नंस्वजनेऽस्मिन् भविष्यति ।।6.37.34।। वयंतुमानुषेणैवसप्तयोत्प्यामहेपरान् । अहमेषममभ्रात्रालक्ष्मणेनमहौजसौ ।।6.37.35।। आत्मनापञ्चमश्चायंसखाममविभीषणः ।
explanation: "To know our own people the Vanaras are the sign of recognition Chivalrous Lakshmana, my brother, similarly five of us and our friend Vibheeshana, these seven people alone will wage war in human form."

shloka_text: वानराएवनश्चिह्नंस्वजनेऽस्मिन् भविष्यति ।।6.37.34।। वयंतुमानुषेणैवसप्तयोत्प्यामहेपरान् । अहमेषममभ्रात्रालक्ष्मणेनमहौजसौ ।।6.37.35।। आत्मनापञ्चमश्चायंसखाममविभीषणः ।
explanation: "To know our own people the Vanaras are the sign of recognition Chivalrous Lakshmana, my brother, similarly five of us and our friend Vibheeshana, these seven people alone will wage war in human form."

shloka_text: सरामःकृत्यसिध्यर्थएवमुक्त्वाविभीषणम् ।।6.37.36।। सुवेलारोहणेबुद्धिश्चकारमतिमान्मतिम् । रमणीयतरंदृष्टवासुवेलस्यगिरेस्तटम् ।।6.37.37।।
explanation: Wise Rama having spoken like that to Vibheeshana for accomplishing the task, looking at the beauty of Suvela mountain slopes, climbed up and went.

shloka_text: सरामःकृत्यसिध्यर्थएवमुक्त्वाविभीषणम् ।।6.37.36।। सुवेलारोहणेबुद्धिश्चकारमतिमान्मतिम् । रमणीयतरंदृष्टवासुवेलस्यगिरेस्तटम् ।।6.37.37।।
explanation: Wise Rama having spoken like that to Vibheeshana for accomplishing the task, looking at the beauty of Suvela mountain slopes, climbed up and went.

shloka_text: सतुकृत्वासुवेलस्यमतिमारोहणंप्रति । लक्ष्मणानुगतोरामःसुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.38.1।। विभीषणंचधर्मज्ञमनुरक्तंनिशाचरम् । मन्त्रज्ञंचविधिज्ञंचश्लक्क्ष्णयापरयागिरा ।।6.38.2।।
explanation: Rama, the well wisher of Lakshmana climbing up the Suvela mountain thought in his mind and thus spoke to Sugriva and the righteous, affectionate Vibheeshana, a counsellor, knower of right action and facts of Lanka, and a respectable enemy.

shloka_text: सतुकृत्वासुवेलस्यमतिमारोहणंप्रति । लक्ष्मणानुगतोरामःसुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.38.1।। विभीषणंचधर्मज्ञमनुरक्तंनिशाचरम् । मन्त्रज्ञंचविधिज्ञंचश्लक्क्ष्णयापरयागिरा ।।6.38.2।।
explanation: Rama, the well wisher of Lakshmana climbing up the Suvela mountain thought in his mind and thus spoke to Sugriva and the righteous, affectionate Vibheeshana, a counsellor, knower of right action and facts of Lanka, and a respectable enemy.

shloka_text: सुवेलंसाधुशैलेन्द्रमिमंधातुशतैश्चितम् । अध्यारोहामहेसर्वेवत्स्यामोऽत्रनिशामिमाम् ।।6.38.3।।
explanation: "We shall all climb up this Suvela mountain captivating with hundreds of minerals and remain there tonight."

shloka_text: लङ्कांचालोकयिष्यामोनिलयंतस्यरक्षसः । येनमेमरणान्तायहृताभार्यादुरात्मना ।।6.38.4।। येनधर्मोनविज्ञातोनतद्वृत्तंनकुलंतथा । राक्षस्यानीचयाबुद् ध्यायेनतद्गर्हितंकृतम् ।।6.38.5।।
explanation: "We shall see Lanka the abode of Rakshasa by whom, who is evil minded as he is to face death, has stolen my consort not knowing, who turned away from righteous duty not knowing the race with lowly Rakshasa mentality, who is immoral."

shloka_text: लङ्कांचालोकयिष्यामोनिलयंतस्यरक्षसः । येनमेमरणान्तायहृताभार्यादुरात्मना ।।6.38.4।। येनधर्मोनविज्ञातोनतद्वृत्तंनकुलंतथा । राक्षस्यानीचयाबुद् ध्यायेनतद्गर्हितंकृतम् ।।6.38.5।।
explanation: "We shall see Lanka the abode of Rakshasa by whom, who is evil minded as he is to face death, has stolen my consort not knowing, who turned away from righteous duty not knowing the race with lowly Rakshasa mentality, who is immoral."

shloka_text: तस्मिन्मेवर्ततेरोषःकीर्तितेराक्षसाधमे । यस्यापराधाननीचस्यवधंद्रक्ष्यामिरक्षसाम् ।।6.38.6।।
explanation: "My wrath is aroused by the mention of the name of lowly Rakshasa. Because of his mistakes all Rakshasas are to be exterminated now."

shloka_text: एकोहिकुरुतेपापंकालपाशवशंगतः । नीचेनात्मापचारेणकुलंतेनविनश्यति ।।6.38.7।।
explanation: "Only one has done that sin and fallen into the noose of death. Because of one Rakshasa's mistake the race will perish."

shloka_text: एवंसम्मन्त्रयन्नेवसक्रोधोरावणंप्रति । रामःसुवेलमासाद्यचित्रसानुमुपारुहत् ।।6.38.8।।
explanation: Talking about Ravana in that manner, Rama climbed the captivating slopes of Suvela to rest there.

shloka_text: पृष्ठतोलक्ष्मणश्चैवमन्वगच्छत्समाहितः । सशरंचापमुद्यम्यसुमहद्विक्रमेरतः ।।6.38.9।। अन्वारोहत्सुग्रीवस्सामात्यस्सविभीषणः ।
explanation: Heroic and alert Lakshmana also holding his great bow, followed. His ministers and Vibheeshana and Sugriva also followed him up.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.38.10।। गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः । पनसःकुमुदश्चैवहरोरम्भश्चयूथपः ।।6.38.11।। जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चऋषभश्चमहामतिः । दुर्मुखश्चमहातेजास्तथाशतवलिःकपिः ।।6.38.12।। एतेचान्येचबहवोवानराशशीघ्रगामिनः । तेवायुवेगप्रवणास्तंगिरिगिरिचारिणः ।।6.38.13।। अध्यारोहन्तशतशस्सुवेलंयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Hanuman, Angada, Neela, Mainda, Dwivida, Gandhamadana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara. Rambhu, Jambhavan, Sushena, intelligent Rshaba, highly energetic Durmukha and Satavali and similarly swift footed Vanaras, mountain rangers and those who can move at wind speed, all of them in hundreds ascended the Suvela mountain following Rama.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.38.10।। गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः । पनसःकुमुदश्चैवहरोरम्भश्चयूथपः ।।6.38.11।। जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चऋषभश्चमहामतिः । दुर्मुखश्चमहातेजास्तथाशतवलिःकपिः ।।6.38.12।। एतेचान्येचबहवोवानराशशीघ्रगामिनः । तेवायुवेगप्रवणास्तंगिरिगिरिचारिणः ।।6.38.13।। अध्यारोहन्तशतशस्सुवेलंयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Hanuman, Angada, Neela, Mainda, Dwivida, Gandhamadana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara. Rambhu, Jambhavan, Sushena, intelligent Rshaba, highly energetic Durmukha and Satavali and similarly swift footed Vanaras, mountain rangers and those who can move at wind speed, all of them in hundreds ascended the Suvela mountain following Rama.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.38.10।। गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः । पनसःकुमुदश्चैवहरोरम्भश्चयूथपः ।।6.38.11।। जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चऋषभश्चमहामतिः । दुर्मुखश्चमहातेजास्तथाशतवलिःकपिः ।।6.38.12।। एतेचान्येचबहवोवानराशशीघ्रगामिनः । तेवायुवेगप्रवणास्तंगिरिगिरिचारिणः ।।6.38.13।। अध्यारोहन्तशतशस्सुवेलंयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Hanuman, Angada, Neela, Mainda, Dwivida, Gandhamadana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara. Rambhu, Jambhavan, Sushena, intelligent Rshaba, highly energetic Durmukha and Satavali and similarly swift footed Vanaras, mountain rangers and those who can move at wind speed, all of them in hundreds ascended the Suvela mountain following Rama.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलोमैन्दोद्विविदएवच ।।6.38.10।। गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः । पनसःकुमुदश्चैवहरोरम्भश्चयूथपः ।।6.38.11।। जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चऋषभश्चमहामतिः । दुर्मुखश्चमहातेजास्तथाशतवलिःकपिः ।।6.38.12।। एतेचान्येचबहवोवानराशशीघ्रगामिनः । तेवायुवेगप्रवणास्तंगिरिगिरिचारिणः ।।6.38.13।। अध्यारोहन्तशतशस्सुवेलंयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Hanuman, Angada, Neela, Mainda, Dwivida, Gandhamadana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara. Rambhu, Jambhavan, Sushena, intelligent Rshaba, highly energetic Durmukha and Satavali and similarly swift footed Vanaras, mountain rangers and those who can move at wind speed, all of them in hundreds ascended the Suvela mountain following Rama.

shloka_text: तेत्वदीर्घेणकालेनगिरिमारुह्यसर्वतः ।।6.38.14।। ददृशुशशिखरेतस्यविषक्तामिवखेपुरीम् ।
explanation: All of them in no time ascended the mountain peak and saw the city of Lanka which was as if clinging closely to the sky and hanging.

shloka_text: तांशुभांप्रवरद्वारांप्राकारपरिशोभिताम् ।।6.38.15।। लङ्कांराक्षससम्पूर्णांददृशुर्हरियूथपाः ।
explanation: The vanara heroes witnessed beautiful gateways, captivating boundaries of auspicious Lanka filled all over with rakshasas.

shloka_text: प्राकारवरसंस्थैश्चतथानीलैश्चराक्षसैः ।।6.38.16।। ददृशुस्तेहरिश्रेष्ठाःप्राकारमपरंकृतम् ।
explanation: The best of vanaras saw dark coloured rakshasas who stood like another boundary in a row.

shloka_text: तेदृष्टवावानराःसर्वेराक्षसान् युद्धकाङ् क्षिणः ।।6.38.17।। मुमुचुर्विविधान्नादांतत्ररामस्यपश्यतः ।
explanation: All the vanaras saw the rakshasas eager for war, and as Rama stood looking at them many kinds of clamours were heard.

shloka_text: ततोऽस्तमगमत्पूर्यःसन्ध्ययाप्रतिरञ्जितः ।।6.38.18।। पूर्णचन्द्रप्रदीप्ताचक्षपासमभिवर्तते ।
explanation: Thereafter the Sun had set in, and twilight reddened. Full moon started shining as night had set in.

shloka_text: ततस्सरामोहरिवाहिनीपतिर्विभीषणेनप्रतिनन्द्यसत्कृतः । सलक्ष्मणोयूथपयूथसम्वृतस्सुवेलपृष्ठेन्यवसद्यथासुखम् ।।6.38.19।।
explanation: Thereafter, Rama, the leader of Vanara troops happily rested on Suvela peak after Vibheeshana and Lakshmana duly offered their prayers. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेअष्टात्रिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty eighth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तांरात्रिमुषितास्तत्रसुवेलेहरिपुङ्गवाः । लङ्कायांददृशुर्वीरावनान्युपवनानिच ।।6.39.1।।
explanation: The heroic leader of the monkeys kept awake that night on the Suvela and saw forests and gardens there in Lanka.

shloka_text: समसौम्यानिरम्याणिविशालान्यायतानिच । दृष्टिरम्याणितेदृष्टवाबभूवुर्जातविस्मयाः ।।6.39.2।।
explanation: They were amazed to see the even terrain, beautiful and expansive, long, and continuous sanctuary lovely to look at being a feast to the eyes.

shloka_text: चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागसालतालसमाकुला । तमालवनसञ्छन्नानागमालासमावृता ।।6.39.3।। हिन्तालैरर्जुनैर्नीपैस्सप्तपर्णैश्चपुष्पितैः । तिलकैःकर्णिकारैश्चपाटलैश्चसमन्ततः ।।6.39.4।। शुशुभेपुष्पिताग्रैश्चलतापरिगतैर्द्रुमैः । लङ्काबहुविधैर्दिव्यैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती ।।6.39.5।। विचित्रकुसुमोपेतैरक्तकोमलपल्लवैः । शाद्वलैश्चतथानीपैश्चित्राभिर्वनराजिभिः ।।6.39.6।।
explanation: Thickly covered with trees like Champaka, Asoka, Punnaga, Sala, Tala, Samala and Tamala trees concealing the woods, surrounded with Nagamala trees all over  and Hintala, Arjuna and Neepa in full bloom, Saptaparni, Tilaka, Karnakara and Patala trees with crests laden with flowers, intertwined with creepers and wonderful variety of flowers trees with tender red leaves as if clothe d in red, flowers of diverse kind and similarly colourful Neela and Sadala as king of forest, it was shining like Amaravathi, capital of Indra.

shloka_text: गन्धाढ्यान्यभिरम्याणिपुष्पाणिचफलानिच । धारयन्त्यगमास्तत्रभूषणानीवमानवाः ।।6.39.7।।
explanation: Having reached there where trees bore fragrance, very beautiful flowers and fruits seemed as though humans were wearing ornaments.

shloka_text: तच्चैत्ररथसङ्काशंमनोज्ञंनन्दनोपमम् । वनंसर्वरर्तुकंरम्यंशुशुभेषटपदायुतम् ।।6.39.8।।
explanation: Appearing like the chaitra chariot of Kubera, Nandana garden of Indra, green in all seasons filled with bees, the garden was a wonderful delight.

shloka_text: नत्यूहकोयष्टिमकैर्नृत्यमानैश्चबर्हिभि । रुतंपरभृतानांचशुश्रुवुर्वन्निर्झरे ।।6.39.9।।
explanation: The Vanaras heard the singing of cuckoos, dancing of peacocks, crying of gallinules, lapwings and herons from the gardens abounding in cascades.

shloka_text: नित्यमत्तविहङ्गानिभ्रमराचरितानिच । कोकिलाकुलषण्डानिविहगाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.10।। भृङ्गराजाभिगीतानिभ्रमरैस्सेवितानिच । कोणालकविघुष्टानिसारसाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.11।। विविशुस्तेततस्तानिवनान्युपवनानिच । हृष्टाःप्रमुदितावीराहरयःकामरूपिणः ।।6.39.12।।
explanation: There after the rejoiced heroic Vanaras who can change their form at will happily entered the woods and gardens inhabited by birds in heat full of emotion, trees covered with cuckoos, and wandering bees, rendered noisy by birds, resounded with the singing of large black bees and bees going around clinging to trees, mingled with sounds of various birds and noise of cries of cranes.

shloka_text: नित्यमत्तविहङ्गानिभ्रमराचरितानिच । कोकिलाकुलषण्डानिविहगाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.10।। भृङ्गराजाभिगीतानिभ्रमरैस्सेवितानिच । कोणालकविघुष्टानिसारसाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.11।। विविशुस्तेततस्तानिवनान्युपवनानिच । हृष्टाःप्रमुदितावीराहरयःकामरूपिणः ।।6.39.12।।

shloka_text: नित्यमत्तविहङ्गानिभ्रमराचरितानिच । कोकिलाकुलषण्डानिविहगाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.10।। भृङ्गराजाभिगीतानिभ्रमरैस्सेवितानिच । कोणालकविघुष्टानिसारसाभिरुतानिच ।।6.39.11।। विविशुस्तेततस्तानिवनान्युपवनानिच । हृष्टाःप्रमुदितावीराहरयःकामरूपिणः ।।6.39.12।।

shloka_text: तेषांप्रविशतांतत्रवानराणांमहौजसाम् । पुष्पसंसर्गसुरभिर्ववौघ्राणसुखोऽनिलः ।।6.39.13।।
explanation: Then the Vanaras of extraordinary energy, were enjoying the breeze redolent with the fragrance of flowers as they were entering, and the wind blew.

shloka_text: अन्येतुहरिवीराणांयूथान्निष्क्रम्ययूथपाः । सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातालङ्कांजग्मुःपताकिनीम् ।।6.39.14।।
explanation: Some other monkey heroes permitted by Sugriva went to Lanka decorated with flags.

shloka_text: वित्रासयन्तोविहगांस्त्रासयन्तोमृगद्विपान् । कम्पयन्तश्चतांलङ्कांनादैस्तेनदतांवराः ।।6.39.15।।
explanation: Other monkeys capable of roaring went into Lanka, spreading out terrifying the birds, dispiriting the deer and elephants by noise.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तस्तेमहावेगामहींचरणपीडिताम् । रजश्चसहसैवोर्थ्वंजगामचरणोत्थितम् ।।6.39.16।।
explanation: Those Vanaras endowed with speed went trampling down on the ground with force, the dust under their feet rose to the sky in a fraction of a second.

shloka_text: ऋक्षास्सिंहावराहाश्चमहिषावारणामृगाः । तेनशब्देनवित्रस्ताजग्मुर्भीतादिशोदश ।।6.39.17।।
explanation: Alarmed by that sound the Bears, lions, pigs, elephants, buffaloes were frightened and went in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: शिखरंतत्त्रिकूटस्यप्रांशुचैकंदिविस्पृशम् । समन्तात्पुष्पसंञ्छन्नंमहारजतसन्निभम् ।।6.39.18।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णंविमलंचारुदर्शनम् । श्लक्ष्णंश्रीमन्महच्छैवदुष्प्रापंशकुनैरपि ।।6.39.19।। मनसाऽपिदुरारोहंकिंपुनःकर्मणाजनैः ।
explanation: Trikuta peak was fully covered with flowers, sparkled with gold, spread over a hundred yojanas, beautiful to look at, splendid and smooth. It is difficult even for birds to reach, for sages even in thought and difficult to access by any physical action. It is praiseworthy as if touching the sky alone.

shloka_text: शिखरंतत्त्रिकूटस्यप्रांशुचैकंदिविस्पृशम् । समन्तात्पुष्पसंञ्छन्नंमहारजतसन्निभम् ।।6.39.18।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णंविमलंचारुदर्शनम् । श्लक्ष्णंश्रीमन्महच्छैवदुष्प्रापंशकुनैरपि ।।6.39.19।। मनसाऽपिदुरारोहंकिंपुनःकर्मणाजनैः ।
explanation: Trikuta peak was fully covered with flowers, sparkled with gold, spread over a hundred yojanas, beautiful to look at, splendid and smooth. It is difficult even for birds to reach, for sages even in thought and difficult to access by any physical action. It is praiseworthy as if touching the sky alone.

shloka_text: निविष्टातत्रशिखरेलङ्कारावणपालिता ।।6.39.20।। शतयोजनविस्तीर्णात्रिंशद्योजनमायता ।
explanation: Lanka ruled by Ravana was a hundred yojanas in breadth and thirty yojanas in length was seen.

shloka_text: सापुरीगोपुरैरुच्चैःपाण्डुराम्बुदसन्निभैः । काञ्चनेनचशालेनराजतेनचशोभते ।।6.39.21।।
explanation: The city of Lanka looked charming with tall towers resembling white cluster of clouds fortified with gold and silver.

shloka_text: प्रासादैश्चविमानैश्चलङ्कापरमभूषिता । घनैरिवाऽतपापायेमध्यमंवैष्णवंपदम् ।।6.39.22।।
explanation: The tall buildings decorated beautifully resembled air planes and were shining like heavy rainy clouds exposed to the sun. The building in the centre resembled the abode of Vishnu.

shloka_text: यस्यांस्तम्भसहस्रेणप्रासादस्समलङ्कृतः । कैलासशिखराकारोदृश्यतेखमिवोललिखन् ।।6.39.23।। चैत्यस्सराक्षसेन्द्रस्यबभूवपुरभूषणम् । शतेनरक्षसांनित्यंयस्समग्रेणरक्ष्यते ।।6.39.24।।
explanation: In that city, which was always protected fully by a hundred Rakshasas, there was a palace with thousand pillars, which looked like peak of mount Kailas, and was as though it was scraping the sky and it as like an ornament of Lanka, the city of Rakshasa's Lord.

shloka_text: यस्यांस्तम्भसहस्रेणप्रासादस्समलङ्कृतः । कैलासशिखराकारोदृश्यतेखमिवोललिखन् ।।6.39.23।। चैत्यस्सराक्षसेन्द्रस्यबभूवपुरभूषणम् । शतेनरक्षसांनित्यंयस्समग्रेणरक्ष्यते ।।6.39.24।।
explanation: In that city, which was always protected fully by a hundred Rakshasas, there was a palace with thousand pillars, which looked like peak of mount Kailas, and was as though it was scraping the sky and it as like an ornament of Lanka, the city of Rakshasa's Lord.

shloka_text: मनोज्ञांकाननवतींपर्वतैरुपशोभिताम् । नानाधातुविचित्रैश्चउद्यानैरुपशोभिताम् ।।6.39.25।। नानाविहङ्गासङ्घुष्टांनानामृगनिषेविताम् । नानाकुसुमसञ्छन्नांनानाराक्षससेविताम् ।।6.39.26।। तांसमृद्धांसमृद्धार्धांलक्ष्मीनान्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । रावणस्यपुरींरामोददर्शसहवानरैः ।।6.39.27।।
explanation: Prosperous Rama, brother of Lakshmana along with Vanaras saw different kinds of forests, mountains filled with different kinds of minerals, delightful gardens endowed with different varieties of flowers, charming birds singing happily, frequented by a variety of deer, attended by Rakshasas. The city was blooming with prosperity.

shloka_text: मनोज्ञांकाननवतींपर्वतैरुपशोभिताम् । नानाधातुविचित्रैश्चउद्यानैरुपशोभिताम् ।।6.39.25।। नानाविहङ्गासङ्घुष्टांनानामृगनिषेविताम् । नानाकुसुमसञ्छन्नांनानाराक्षससेविताम् ।।6.39.26।। तांसमृद्धांसमृद्धार्धांलक्ष्मीनान्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । रावणस्यपुरींरामोददर्शसहवानरैः ।।6.39.27।।
explanation: Prosperous Rama, brother of Lakshmana along with Vanaras saw different kinds of forests, mountains filled with different kinds of minerals, delightful gardens endowed with different varieties of flowers, charming birds singing happily, frequented by a variety of deer, attended by Rakshasas. The city was blooming with prosperity.

shloka_text: मनोज्ञांकाननवतींपर्वतैरुपशोभिताम् । नानाधातुविचित्रैश्चउद्यानैरुपशोभिताम् ।।6.39.25।। नानाविहङ्गासङ्घुष्टांनानामृगनिषेविताम् । नानाकुसुमसञ्छन्नांनानाराक्षससेविताम् ।।6.39.26।। तांसमृद्धांसमृद्धार्धांलक्ष्मीनान्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । रावणस्यपुरींरामोददर्शसहवानरैः ।।6.39.27।।
explanation: Prosperous Rama, brother of Lakshmana along with Vanaras saw different kinds of forests, mountains filled with different kinds of minerals, delightful gardens endowed with different varieties of flowers, charming birds singing happily, frequented by a variety of deer, attended by Rakshasas. The city was blooming with prosperity.

shloka_text: तांमहागृहसम्बाधांदृष्टवालक्ष्मणपूर्वजः । नगरीममरप्रख्योविस्मयंप्राप्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.39.28।।
explanation: Valiant brother of Lakshmana wondered seeing the city filled with great palaces, distinct like Lord Indra's city.

shloka_text: तांरत्नपूर्णांबहुसंविधानांप्रासादमालाभिरलङ्कृतांच । पुरींमहायन्त्रकवाटमुख्यांददर्शरामोमहताबलेन ।।6.39.29।।
explanation: Accompanied by huge Vanara army, Rama saw in the city of Lanka rows of buildingspalaces, adorned with gems, gates fitted with huge machines for war and large army of Ravana. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकोनचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the thirty ninth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोरामस्सुवेलाग्रंयोजनद्वयमण्डलम् । अरुरोहससुग्रीवोहरियूधपसम्वृतः ।।6.40.1।।
explanation: Rama accompanied by Vanara troop and Sugriva, ascended the peak of Suvela mountain spread over yojanas.

shloka_text: स्थित्वामुहूर्तंतत्रैवदिशोदशविलोकयन् । त्रिकूटशिखरेरम्येनिर्मितांविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.40.2।। ददर्शलङ्कांसुन्यस्तांरम्यकाननशोभिताम् ।
explanation: Remaining there for a short while, Rama observed the view of Lanka in all directions. He saw Lanka built on the charming peak of Trikuta strongly by Vishwakarma, endowed with delightful groves.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।
explanation: From there Rama saw on the peak of the tower the Rakshasa king, who is difficult to approach. He was fanned by white whisks on both sides, graced with triumphal parasol, decorated his body with red sandal paste, adorned in redcoloured ornaments, resembling dark clouds, attired in red like the hare's blood, embroidered with golden thread, with scars on his chest caused by indentations made by the tusks of Airavata the elephant of Indra, looked like a mass of cloud covered by sunshine at dusk.

shloka_text: तस्यांगोपुरशृङ्गस्थंराक्षसेन्द्रंदुरासदम् ।।6.40.3।। श्वेतचामरपर्यन्तंविजयच्छत्रशोभितम् । रक्तचन्दनसंलिप्तंरत्नाभरणभूषितम् ।।6.40.4।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंहेमसञ्छादिताम्बरम् । ऐरावतविषाणाग्रैरुत्कृष्टकिणवक्षसम् ।।6.40.5।। शशलोहितरागेणसंवीतंरक्तवाससा । सन्ध्यातपेनसंवीतंमेघराशिमिवाम्बरे ।।6.40.6।।

shloka_text: पश्यतांवानरेन्द्राणांराघवस्यापिपश्यतः । दर्शनाद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्यसुग्रीवस्सहसोत्थितः ।।6.40.7।।
explanation: Looking at the sight of Raghava seeing Rakshasa king, Sugriva the king of Vanaras got up instantly rashly.

shloka_text: क्रोधवेगेनसंयुक्तस्सत्त्वेनचबलेनच । अचलाग्रादथोत्थायपुप्लुवेगोपुरस्थले ।।6.40.8।।
explanation: Provoked by anger, courageous and strong Sugriva rose up impelled by impetuosity and flew to the peak of the tower.

shloka_text: स्थित्वामुहूर्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यनिर्भयेनान्तरात्मना । तृणीकृत्यचतद्रक्षस्सोऽब्रवीत्परुषंवचः ।।6.40.9।।
explanation: For a moment he stood looking at the ogre fearlessly in his mind and treating him like straw spoke harsh words.

shloka_text: लोकनाथस्यरामस्यसखादासोऽस्मिराक्षस । नमयामोक्ष्यसेऽद्यत्वंपार्थिवेन्द्रस्यतेजसा ।।6.40.10।।
explanation: "O Rakshasa! I am a friend and servant of the king of kings, ruler of the world. By his power I will not leave you!", Sugriva said.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वासहसोत्पत्यपुप्लुवेतस्यचोपरि । आकृष्यमुकुटंचित्रंपातयित्वाऽपतद्भुवि ।।6.40.11।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, Sugriva got up speedily and flew to the top of the tower (here Ravana was located) held the diadem and pushed it on the ground.

shloka_text: समीक्ष्यतूर्णमायान्तमबभाषेनिशाचरः । सुग्रीवस्त्वपरोक्षम् मेहीनग्रीवोभविष्यसि ।।6.40.12।।
explanation: Observing Sugriva coming towards him, Ravana said, "When you were not seen by me you had a neck. I will make you neckless."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वोत्थायतंक्षिप्रंबाहुभ्यामाक्षिपत्तले । कन्तुवत्तंसमुत्थायबाहुभ्यामाक्षिपद्धरि ।।6.40.13।।
explanation: Telling like that that Ravana got up and threw Sugriva by his hand s to the ground. Then Sugriva getting up like a ball fallen pushed Ravana down.

shloka_text: परस्परंस्वेदविदग्धगात्रौपरस्परंशोणितदिग्धदेहौ । परस्परंलशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौपरस्परंशाल्मलिकिंशुकौयधा ।।6.40.14।। मुष्टिप्रहारैश्चतलप्रहारैररत्निघातैश्चकराग्रघातैः । तौचक्रतुर्युद्धमसह्यरूपंमहाबलौराक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ ।।6.40.15।।
explanation: Sugriva and Ravana, their bodies sweating all over, bodies coloured red with blood looking like red silk cotton trees, their bodies clinging together interlocked with each other stood motionless. They were fighting with their fists, palms and blows of forearms, hurting each other with nails and carrying out unbearable forms of war.

shloka_text: परस्परंस्वेदविदग्धगात्रौपरस्परंशोणितदिग्धदेहौ । परस्परंलशिष्टनिरुद्धचेष्टौपरस्परंशाल्मलिकिंशुकौयधा ।।6.40.14।। मुष्टिप्रहारैश्चतलप्रहारैररत्निघातैश्चकराग्रघातैः । तौचक्रतुर्युद्धमसह्यरूपंमहाबलौराक्षसवानरेन्द्रौ ।।6.40.15।।
explanation: Sugriva and Ravana, their bodies sweating all over, bodies coloured red with blood looking like red silk cotton trees, their bodies clinging together interlocked with each other stood motionless. They were fighting with their fists, palms and blows of forearms, hurting each other with nails and carrying out unbearable forms of war.

shloka_text: कृत्वानियुद्धंभृशमुग्रवेगौकालंचिर, गोपुरवेदिमध्ये । उत्क्षिप्यचोत्क्षिप्यविनम्यदेहौपादक्रमाद्गोपुरवेदिलग्नौ ।।6.40.16।।
explanation: Violently fighting like that aggressively for long, throwing each other down repeatedly, bending and moving their feet in a direction, stood on the fl at area of the peak in the middle portion.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यमाविध्यवेदिलग्नौतौपेततुस्सालनिखातमध्ये । उत्पेततुर्भूतलमस्पृशन्तौस्थित्वामुहूर्तंत्वभिनिश्श्वसन्तौ ।।6.40.17।।
explanation: Squeezing their bodies of each other they dropped down between the boundary of the peak and the moat. They were gasping heavily for a moment and clung their body to each other jumping.

shloka_text: आलिङ् ग्यचालिङ् ग्यचबाहुयोक्स्रैस्संयोजयामासतुराहवेतौ । सम्रम्भशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौसंचेरतुस्सम्प्रतियुद्धमार्गैः ।।6.40.18।।
explanation: Both pressing their bosom to each other, clung to each other, and fastened themselves in embrace in the comb at having received similar training in war and both endowed with might. At this time, they went on in comb at using several war methods.

shloka_text: शार्दूरसिंहाविवजातदर्पौगजेन्द्रपोताविवसम्प्रयुक्तौ । संहत्यचापीड्यचतावुरोभ्यांनिपेततुर्वैयुगपद्धरण्याम् ।।6.40.19।।
explanation: Both of them resembled a tiger and lion affected by pride, connecting to each other through their shoulders like Lordly elephants, hitting and hurting one another holding one another fell down at once simultaneously.

shloka_text: उद्यम्यचान्योन्यमधिक्षिपन्तौसञ्चक्रमातेबहुयुद्धमार्गे: । व्यायामशिक्षाबलसम्प्रयुक्तौक्लमंनतौजग्मतुराशुवीरौ ।।6.40.20।।
explanation: Both of them were holding one another, snubbing each other gradually following many kinds of combat. As both the heroes were well trained in wrestling and fighting, they did not feel tiresome.

shloka_text: बाहूत्तमैर्वारणवारणाभैर्निवारयन्तौवरवारणाभौ । चिरेणकालेनतुसम्प्रयुक्तौसञ्चेरतुर्मण्डलमार्गमाशु ।।6.40.21।।
explanation: Both Ravana and Sugriva endowed with mighty arms, were resisting each other, and keeping away one another engaging in comb at for a long time. They kept on moving, going around each other swiftly.

shloka_text: तौपरस्परमासाद्ययत्तावन्योन्यसूदने । मार्जाराविवभक्ष्यार्थेऽवितस्थातेमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.40.22।।
explanation: Both of them intent on destroying each other were approaching one another and now and then growling like cats for the sake of food.

shloka_text: मण्डलानिविचित्राणिस्थानानिविविधानिच । मूत्रकाणिचित्राणिगतप्रत्यागतानिच ।।6.40.23।। तिरच्शीनगतान्येवतथावक्रगतानिच । परिमोक्षंप्रहाराणांवर्जनंपरिधावनम् ।।6.40.24।। अभिद्रवणमाप्लावमावस्थानंसविग्रहम् । परावृत्तमपावृत्तमपद्रुतमवप्लुतम् ।।6.40.25।। उपन्यस्तपमन्यस्तंयुद्धमार्गविशारदौ । तौसञ्चेचेरतुरन्योन्यंवानरेन्द्रश्चरावणः ।।6.40.26।।
explanation: Both Vanara king and Ravana being learned in war craft, went around in circles like ox's urine, stood in different wonderful postures, moved forward and backward horizontally and obliquely to evade movements, hitting, and delivering each other, standing steadily motionless, striking, jumping, assaulting each other coming forward and going away, going backwards jumping from behind, holding hands and folding to resist exhibiting their skill in combat.

shloka_text: मण्डलानिविचित्राणिस्थानानिविविधानिच । मूत्रकाणिचित्राणिगतप्रत्यागतानिच ।।6.40.23।। तिरच्शीनगतान्येवतथावक्रगतानिच । परिमोक्षंप्रहाराणांवर्जनंपरिधावनम् ।।6.40.24।। अभिद्रवणमाप्लावमावस्थानंसविग्रहम् । परावृत्तमपावृत्तमपद्रुतमवप्लुतम् ।।6.40.25।। उपन्यस्तपमन्यस्तंयुद्धमार्गविशारदौ । तौसञ्चेचेरतुरन्योन्यंवानरेन्द्रश्चरावणः ।।6.40.26।।
