shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरक्षोमायाबलमथात्मनः । आरब्धुमुपसंपेदेज्ञात्वातंवानराधिपः ।।6.40.27।। उत्पपाततदाकाशंजितकाशीजितक्लमः । रावणःस्थितएवात्रहरिराजेववञ्चितः ।।6.40.28।।
explanation: In the meantime, Ravana thought of exhibiting his superiority by jugglery and jumped to the sky. Knowing that Sugriva, the untiring Vanara king assumed the air of victor and rose up to the sky. Baffled Ravana stood thinking Sugriva would come there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरक्षोमायाबलमथात्मनः । आरब्धुमुपसंपेदेज्ञात्वातंवानराधिपः ।।6.40.27।। उत्पपाततदाकाशंजितकाशीजितक्लमः । रावणःस्थितएवात्रहरिराजेववञ्चितः ।।6.40.28।।
explanation: In the meantime, Ravana thought of exhibiting his superiority by jugglery and jumped to the sky. Knowing that Sugriva, the untiring Vanara king assumed the air of victor and rose up to the sky. Baffled Ravana stood thinking Sugriva would come there.

shloka_text: अथहरिवरनाथःप्राप्यसङ्ग्रामकीर्तिंनिशिचरपतिमाजौयोजयित्वाश्रमेण । गगनमतिविशालंलङ्घयित्वार्कसूनुर्हरिगणमध्येरामपार्श्वंजगाम ।।6.40.29।।
explanation: Then Sugriva, the Sun god's son, the Lord of Vanara chiefs, who had won fame of winning in battles, victorious exhausting Ravana in comb at flying the extensive sky reached Rama who was amid Vanara army.

shloka_text: इतिससवितृसूनुस्तत्रतत्कर्मकृत्वापवनगतिरनीकंप्राविशत्ससम्प्रहृष्टः । रघुवरनृपसूनोद्वर्धयन्युद्धहर्षंतरुमृगगणमुख्यैःपूज्यमानोहरीन्द्रः ।।6.40.30।।
explanation: Sugriva the son of the Sun god, having completed the feat, rejoiced by increasing the joy of foremost of Raghus. Then he who is adored by the monkey chiefs entered the army of Vanaras. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fortieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथतस्मिन्निमित्तानिदृष्टवालक्ष्मणपूर्वजः । सुग्रीवंसम्परिष्वज्यतथावचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.1।।
explanation: Rama, brother of Lakshmana, seeing the signs of war, embraced Sugriva and spoke these words.

shloka_text: असन्त्ऱ्यमयासार्थंतदिदंसाहसंकृतम् । एवंसाहसुक्तानिनकुर्वन्तिजनेश्वराः ।।6.41.2।।
explanation: "You have done this courageous feat without consulting me. Rulers do not do such actions."

shloka_text: संशयेस्थाप्यमांचेदंबलंचसविभीषणम् । कष्टंकृतमिदंवीर साहसंसाहसप्रिय ।।6.41.3।।
explanation: "O hero, who is fond of daring actions! To me, to the army and Vibheeshana you created a great doubt by this bold action of yours."

shloka_text: इदानींमाकृथावीर एवंविधमचिन्तितम् । त्वयिकिञ्चित्समापन्नेकिंकार्यंसीतयामम ।।6.41.4।। भरतेनमहाबाहो लक्ष्मणेनयवीयसा । शत्रुघ्नेनचशत्रुघ्नस्वशरीरेणवापुन:।। 6.41.5।।
explanation: "O broad shouldered hero, tamer of foes! Do not do this kind of action. Even if you were harmed a bit, O destroyer of foes, of what use is it to me or even to Sita, Bharata, Satrughna or to Lakshmana or even to my body?"

shloka_text: इदानींमाकृथावीर एवंविधमचिन्तितम् । त्वयिकिञ्चित्समापन्नेकिंकार्यंसीतयामम ।।6.41.4।। भरतेनमहाबाहो लक्ष्मणेनयवीयसा । शत्रुघ्नेनचशत्रुघ्नस्वशरीरेणवापुन:।। 6.41.5।।
explanation: "O broad shouldered hero, tamer of foes! Do not do this kind of action. Even if you were harmed a bit, O destroyer of foes, of what use is it to me or even to Sita, Bharata, Satrughna or to Lakshmana or even to my body?"

shloka_text: त्वयिचानागतेपूर्वमितिमेनिश्चितामतिः । जानतश्चापितेवीर्यंमहेन्द्रवरुणोसम ।।6.41.6।। हत्वाऽहंरावणंयुद्धेसपुत्रबलवाहनम् । अभिषिच्यचलङ्कायांविभीषणमथापिच ।।6.41.7।। भरतेराज्यमावेश्यत्यक्ष्येदेहंमहाबल ।
explanation: "Mighty Sugriva! You resemble Indra and Varuna in might. Your valour is known to me. I have decided in my mind to kill the sons of Ravana and his relatives in battle, coronate Vibheeshana in Lanka, and hand over the kingdom to Bharata and give up my body."

shloka_text: त्वयिचानागतेपूर्वमितिमेनिश्चितामतिः । जानतश्चापितेवीर्यंमहेन्द्रवरुणोसम ।।6.41.6।। हत्वाऽहंरावणंयुद्धेसपुत्रबलवाहनम् । अभिषिच्यचलङ्कायांविभीषणमथापिच ।।6.41.7।। भरतेराज्यमावेश्यत्यक्ष्येदेहंमहाबल ।
explanation: "Mighty Sugriva! You resemble Indra and Varuna in might. Your valour is known to me. I have decided in my mind to kill the sons of Ravana and his relatives in battle, coronate Vibheeshana in Lanka, and hand over the kingdom to Bharata and give up my body."

shloka_text: तमेवंवादिनंरामंसुग्रीवःप्रत्यभाषत ।।6.41.8।। तवभार्यापहर्तारंदृष्टवाराघव रावणम् । मर्षयामिकथंवीरजानपौरुषमात्मनः ।।6.41.9।।
explanation: To Rama who was speaking in that manner, Sugriva replied, "Heroic Rama! Seeing that Ravana, who has borne away your consort, and knowing my own strength, how can I tolerate?"

shloka_text: तमेवंवादिनंरामंसुग्रीवःप्रत्यभाषत ।।6.41.8।। तवभार्यापहर्तारंदृष्टवाराघव रावणम् । मर्षयामिकथंवीरजानपौरुषमात्मनः ।।6.41.9।।
explanation: To Rama who was speaking in that manner, Sugriva replied, "Heroic Rama! Seeing that Ravana, who has borne away your consort, and knowing my own strength, how can I tolerate?"

shloka_text: इत्येवंवादिनंवीरमभिनन्द्यचराघवः । लक्ष्मणंलक्षीसम्पन्नमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.10।।
explanation: Raghava heard the hero Sugriva, applauding him and spoke these words to Lakshmana, who was endowed with prosperity.

shloka_text: परिगृह्योदकंशीतंवनानिफलवन्तिच । बलौघंसंविभज्येमंव्यूह्यतिष्ठेमलक्ष्मण ।।6.41.11।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! We should occupy a region with cool water and good fruits and plan to divide the army and be ready."

shloka_text: लोकक्षयकरंभीमंभयंपश्याम्युपस्थितम् । निबर्हणंप्रवीराणामृक्षवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.41.12।।
explanation: "I foresee the terrific destruction of eminent heroes among Bears, monkeys and Rakshasas. I see the danger approaching."

shloka_text: वाताश्चहिपरुषांवान्तिकम्पतेचवसुन्धरा । पर्वताग्राणिवेपन्तेपतन्तिधरणीधराः ।।6.41.13।।
explanation: "The winds are blowing severely, the earth is quaking in, the mountain peaks are shaking, and the elephants bearing the earth (in the four corners) are falling."

shloka_text: मेघाःक्रवादसङ्काशाःपरुषाःपरुषस्वनाः । क्रूराःक्रूरंप्रवर्षन्तिमिश्रंशोणितबिन्दुभिः ।।6.41.14।।
explanation: "The fierce clouds resembling wild birds are making terrible harsh sounds and rain mixed with drops of blood is showering."

shloka_text: रक्तचन्दनसङ्काशासन्ध्यापरमदारुणा । ज्वलच्चनिपतत्येतदादित्यादग्निमण्डलम् ।।6.41.15।।
explanation: "The twilight appears like red sander trees, the burning fire falling from the sun is like a mass of fire and frightening."

shloka_text: आदित्यमभिवाश्यन्तिजनयन्तोमहद्भयम् । दीनादीनस्वराःघोरानप्रशस्तामृगद्विजाः ।।6.41.16।।
explanation: "The desperate inauspicious sounds of ominous beasts crying pitifully facing the sun are causing great fear."

shloka_text: रजन्यामप्रकाशश्चसन्तापयतिचन्द्रमाः । कृष्णरक्तांशुपर्यन्तोयथालोकस्यसंक्ष्ये ।।6.41.17।।
explanation: "Like at the time of universal dissolution, the moon is not radiant, being surrounded by black and red halo at night and is tormenting."

shloka_text: ह्रस्वोरूक्षोऽप्रशस्तश्चपरिवेषस्सुलोहितः । आदित्यमण्डलेनीलंलक्ष्मलक्ष्मण दृश्यते ।।6.41.18।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! Short dark spot observed in the Sun 's orbit is inauspicious. moon is surrounded by copper colour and dreary."

shloka_text: दृश्यन्तेनयथावच्छनक्षत्राण्यभिवर्तते । युगान्तमिवलोकस्यपश्यलक्ष्मण शंसति ।।6.41.19।।
explanation: "Just as the spots on the moon, the stars are also dirty and not visible. It forebodes the end of the universe Lakshmana!"

shloka_text: काकाश्येनास्तथागृध्रानीचैःपरिपतन्तिच । शिवाश्चाप्यशिवावाचःप्रवदन्तिमहास्वनाः ।।6.41.20।।
explanation: "The crows, hawks and also vultures are joining lowly animals like jackals and making loud noises which is inauspicious and not good."

shloka_text: क्षिप्रमद्यदुराधर्षांलङ्कांरावणपालिताम् । अभियामजवेनैवसर्वतोहरिभिर्वृताः ।।6.41.21।।
explanation: Let us swiftly attack today the impregnable Lanka, protected by Ravana, with great speed, surrounded on all sides by monkeys.

shloka_text: शैलैःशूलैश्चखडगैश्चविमुक्स्सैःकपिराक्षसैः । भविष्यत्यावृताभूमिर्मांसशोणितकर्दमा ।।6.41.22।।
explanation: "The land will remain covered by rocks, tridents, swords hurled by the Vanaras and Rakshasas and with flesh and blood."

shloka_text: इत्येवंतुवदवनीर्वोलक्ष्मणंलक्ष्मणाग्रजः । तस्मादवातरच्छीघ्रंपर्वताग्रान्महाबलः ।।6.41.23।।
explanation: Mighty hero Rama, (the elder brother of Lakshmana) said to Lakshmana in this manner (as described earlier) and descended from the peak of the mountain without delay.

shloka_text: अवतीर्यचधर्मात्मातस्माच्छैलात्सराघवः । परैःपरमदुर्धर्षंददर्शबलमात्मनः ।।6.41.24।।
explanation: Climbing down the mountain, the righteous Rama reviewed in his mind the strength of his army and the enemy which is difficult to assail.

shloka_text: सन्नह्यतुससुग्रीवःकपिराजबलंमहत् । कालज्ञोराघवःकालेसंयुगायाभ्यचोदयत् ।।6.41.25।।
explanation: Raghava, who is knowledgeable of when to do what, motivated the army of Vanaras and Sugriva and ordered.

shloka_text: ततःकालेमहाबाहुर्बलेनमहतावृतः । प्रस्थितःपुरतोधवनीलङ्कामभिमुखःपुरीम् ।।6.41.26।।
explanation: Surrounded by a large army in front, the broad shouldered Rama proceeded towards Lanka.

shloka_text: तंविभीषणसुग्रीवौहनूमाञ्जाम्बवान्नळ । ऋक्षराजस्तथानीलोलक्ष्मणश्चान्वयुस्तदा ।।6.41.27।।
explanation: Then Vibheeshana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, Nala, Neela in the same way Lakshmana followed.

shloka_text: ततःपशचात्सुमहतीपृतनर् क्षवनौकसाम् । प्रच्छाद्यमहतींभूमिमनुयातिस्मराघवम् ।।6.41.28।।
explanation: Then the bears, monkeys, covering all over the land went behind Rama.

shloka_text: शैलशृङ्गाणिशतशःप्रवृद्धांश्चमहीरुहान् । जगृहुःकुञ्जरप्रख्यावानराःपरवारणाः ।।6.41.29।।
explanation: The monkeys who were of the size of elephants capable of warding off the enemy, bore huge grown up trees in their hands and went.

shloka_text: तौत्वदीर्घेणकालेनभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । रावणस्यपुरींलङ्कामसेदतुररिन्दमौ ।।6.41.30।।
explanation: In a short while the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, tamers of foes reached the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: पताकामालिनींरम्यामुद्यानवनशोभिताम् । चित्रवप्रासुदुष्प्रापमुच्चैःप्राकारतोरणाम् ।।6.41.31।। तांसुरैरपिदुर्धर्षांरामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः । यथानिदेशंसम्पीड्यन्यविशन्तवनौकसः ।।6.41.32।।
explanation: Commanded by Rama's words the Vanaras remaining in their positions as ordained, entered the wonderful Lanka, which was decorated with flags, embellished with gardens. The defensive walls and arches of the boundary of Lanka were difficult to access even for Devatas.

shloka_text: पताकामालिनींरम्यामुद्यानवनशोभिताम् । चित्रवप्रासुदुष्प्रापमुच्चैःप्राकारतोरणाम् ।।6.41.31।। तांसुरैरपिदुर्धर्षांरामवाक्यप्रचोदिताः । यथानिदेशंसम्पीड्यन्यविशन्तवनौकसः ।।6.41.32।।
explanation: Commanded by Rama's words the Vanaras remaining in their positions as ordained, entered the wonderful Lanka, which was decorated with flags, embellished with gardens. The defensive walls and arches of the boundary of Lanka were difficult to access even for Devatas.

shloka_text: लङ्कायास्तूत्तरंद्वारंशैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् । रामःसहानुजोधन्वीजुगोपचरुरोधच ।।6.41.33।।
explanation: Accompanied by his brother Lakshmana, Rama, armed with bow, blocked the northern gate of Lanka which was like a lofty mountain peak and protected.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: लङ्कामुपनिविष्टस्तुरामोदशरथात्मजः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोवीरःपुरींरावणपालिताम् ।।6.41.34।। उत्तरद्वारमासाद्ययत्रतिष्ठतिरावणः । नान्योरामाद्धितद् द्वारंसमर्थःपरिरक्षितुम् ।।6.41.35।। सायुथैराक्षसैर्भीमैरभिगुप्तंसमन्ततः । लघूनांत्रासजननंपाताळमिवदानवैः ।।6.41.36।।
explanation: (Dasaratha's son) Rama who had Lakshmana as follower reached the northern gate protected by Ravana. Just as the ocean is guarded by Varuna, it was guarded by terrific Rakshasas, who were secretly hiding all over like the Rakshasas in the subterranean region with small amounts of numerous armours for protection. It was not possible for anyone other than Rama to enter.

shloka_text: विन्यस्तानिचयोधानांबहूनिविविधानिच । ददर्शाऽयुधजालानितत्रैवकवचानिच ।।6.41.37।।
explanation: Rama Saw there, numerous weapons of every kind so also shields for the combatants of war.

shloka_text: पूर्वंतुद्वारमासाद्यनीलोहरिचमूपतिः । अतिष्ठत्सहमैन्देनद्विविदेनचवीर्यवान् ।।6.41.38।।
explanation: Neela the commanderinchief of the army of monkeys, a valiant one, also Dwivida, and Mainda reached the east gate and remained there.

shloka_text: अङ्गदोदक्षिणद्वारंजग्राहसुमहाबलः । ऋषभेणगवाक्षेणगजेनगवयेनच ।।6.41.39।।
explanation: Angada endowed with great prowess along with Rshaba, Gavaksha, Gaja, and Gavaya reached the south gate.

shloka_text: हनुमान् पश्चिमद्वारंररक्षबलवान्कपिः । प्रमाथिप्रषुभ्यांचवीरैरन्यैश्चसङ्गतः ।।6.41.40।।
explanation: Mighty monkey Hanuman united with heroes Pramati and Praghasa and others protected the west gate.

shloka_text: मध्यमेचस्वयंगुल्मेसुग्रीवस्समतिष्ठत । सहसर्वैर्हरिश्रेष्ठैस्सुपर्णश्वसनोपमैः ।।6.41.41।।
explanation: Sugriva chief of all army and best of the monkey army who was equal to Garuda of beautiful wings, endowed with wind speed remained in the middle (of north and west) post.

shloka_text: वानराणांतुषटित्रंशत्कोट्यःप्रख्यातयूथपाः । निपीड्योपनिविष्टाश्चसुग्रीवोयत्रवानरः ।।6.41.42।।
explanation: Renowned generals of the Vanara army and thirtysix crores of Vanaras stood there camping.

shloka_text: शासनेनतुरामस्यलक्ष्मणस्सविभीषणः । द्वारेद्वारेहरीणांतुकोटिंकोटिंन्यवेशयेत् ।।6.41.43।।
explanation: By the command of Rama, Vibheeshana accompanied by Lakshmana posted crores and crores of Vanaras there.

shloka_text: पश्चिमेनतुरामस्यसुषेणःसहजाम्बवान् ।।6.41.44।। आदूरान्मध्यमेगुल्मेतस्थौबहुबलानुगः ।
explanation: Sushena along with Jambavan and a large army of Vanaras were posted in the centre not far from Rama at the west by Rama's order.

shloka_text: तेतुवानरशार्धूलाःशार्दूलाइवदंष्ट्रिणः ।।6.41.45।। गृहीत्वाद्रुमशैलाग्रान्हृष्टायुद्धायतस्थिरे ।
explanation: Vanaras who resembled tigers, endowed with sharp teeth joyfully stood there holding trees and peaks of mountain waiting to combat.

shloka_text: सर्वेविकृतलाङ्गूलास्सर्वेदंष्ट्रानखायुधा:।। 6.41.46।। सर्वेविकृतचित्राङ्गास्सर्वेचविकृताननाः ।
explanation: All had their tails lifted unusually, had their nails and teeth sharp as weapons, some had unnatural face, and all of them had distorted eyes (as in fury).

shloka_text: दशनागबलाःकेचित्केचिद्धशगुणोत्तराः ।।6.41.47।। केचिन्नागसहस्रस्यबभूवुस्तुल्यविक्रमाः ।
explanation: A few of them were having the strength of ten elephants, some had ten times more than others, and a few were endowed with great strength equal to thousand elephants.

shloka_text: सन्तिचौघबलाःकेचित्केचिच्छतगुणोत्तराः ।।6.41.48।। अप्रमेयबलाश्चान्येतत्रासन्हरियूथपाः
explanation: Few monkeys had strength of an ogha, some had a hundred times more, and the monkey commanders possessed immeasurable strength.

shloka_text: अद्भुतश्चविचित्रश्चतेषामासीत्समागमः ।।6.41.49।। तत्रवानरसैन्यानांशलभानामिवोद्यमः ।
explanation: There it seemed as if a flight of locusts had gathered, with monkey army gathered there. It was amazing and astonishing.

shloka_text: प्रतिपूर्णमिवाकाशंसञ्छन्नेवचमेदिनी ।।6.41.50।। लङ्कापुमनिविष्टैश्चसम्पतद्भिश्चवानरैः ।
explanation: Vanaras settled in such a way all around Lanka completely covering the land with those already at Lanka.

shloka_text: शतंशतसहस्राणांपृथगृक्षवनौकसाम् ।।6.41.51।। लङ्काद्वाराङयुपाजग्मुरन्येयोद्धुंसमन्ततः ।
explanation: A hundred thousand bars and monkeys and several others already gathered at the gates of Lanka to fight proceeded.

shloka_text: आवृतस्सगिरिस्सर्वैस्सैस्समन्तात् प्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.41.52।। अयुतानांसहस्रंचपुरींतामभ्यवर्तत ।
explanation: All over the mountain the monkeys surrounded the boundary wall of Lanka city to collect information.

shloka_text: वानरैर्बलवद्भिश्चबभूवद्रुमपाणिभिः ।।6.41.53।। सम्वृतासर्वतोलङ्कादुष्प्रवेशाऽपिवायुना ।
explanation: Mighty Vanaras holding uprooted trees occupied everywhere and it seemed difficult for even wind to enter Lanka.

shloka_text: राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुःसहसाऽभिनिपीडिताः ।।6.41.54।। वानरैर्मेघसङ्काशैश्शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः ।
explanation: Caught by Vanaras like clouds and equalled Indra in valour gave way to wonder for the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: महान् शब्दोऽभवत्तत्रबलौघस्याभिवर्ततः ।।6.41.55।। सागरस्येवभिन्नस्ययथास्यात्सलिलस्वनः ।
explanation: Thereafter with the divisions of the Vanara army moving like the ocean on the mountain peak, appeared like the roaring sound of water in the ocean moving out of boundary.

shloka_text: तेनशब्देनमहतासप्राकारासतोरणा ।।6.41.56।। लङ्काप्रचलितासर्वासशैलवनकानना ।
explanation: By the great sound the boundary, the archways and the mountains and forests shook violently.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणगुप्तासासुग्रीवेणचवाहिनी ।।6.41.57।। बभूवदुर्धर्षतरासर्वैरपिसुरासुरैः ।
explanation: Protected by Rama and Lakshmana and Sugriva that an army of monkeys became difficult to assail even for Rakshasas and Devatas.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।
explanation: Deliberating on the action to be taken to kill the Rakshasas, Raghava himself called the army and gathered them and the ministers all of them again and again discussed and took the decision. Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।
explanation: Deliberating on the action to be taken to kill the Rakshasas, Raghava himself called the army and gathered them and the ministers all of them again and again discussed and took the decision. Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: राघवःसन्निवेश्यैवंस्वसैन्यंरक्षसांवधे ।।6.41.58।। सम्मन्त्ऱ्यमन्त्रिभिस्सार्थंनिश्चित्यचपुनःपुनः । आनन्तर्यमभिप्रेप्सुःक्रमयोगार्थतत्त्ववित् ।।6.41.59।। विभीषणस्यानुमतेराजधर्ममनुस्मरन् । अङ्गदंवालितनयंसमाहूयेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.41.60।।
explanation: Deliberating on the action to be taken to kill the Rakshasas, Raghava himself called the army and gathered them and the ministers all of them again and again discussed and took the decision. Later recalling the king's duty with Vibheeshana, summoned Vali's son Angada and spoke these words.

shloka_text: गत्वासौम्य दशग्रीवंब्रूहिमद्वचनात्कपे । लङ्घयित्वापुरींलङ्कांभयंत्यक्त्वागतव्यधः ।।6.41.61।। भ्रष्टश्रीक गतैश्वर्य मुमूर्षो नष्टचेतनः ।
explanation: "O noble Hanuman crossing over Lanka without fear, giving up the difficulties experienced earlier we reached. Admonish the tenheaded king who has lost senses, his past fortune and sovereignty."

shloka_text: ऋषीणांदेवतानांचगन्धर्वाप्सरसांतथा ।।6.41.62।। नागानामथयक्षाणांराज्ञांचरजनीचर । यच्चपापंकृतंमोहादवलिप्तेनराक्षस ।।6.41.63।। नूनंतेविगतोदर्पःस्वयम्भुवरदानजः । तस्यपापस्यसम्प्राप्ताव्युष्टिरद्यदुरसदा ।।6.41.64।।
explanation: "O night ranger! the time has come for punishment for the sins committed by you to the sages, Devatas, so also to Gandharvas, celestial beauties, Nagas, Yakshas and the kings because of your delusion in conceit. Surely your pride about the boons begotten from the selfborn creator will be gone, said Rama.

shloka_text: ऋषीणांदेवतानांचगन्धर्वाप्सरसांतथा ।।6.41.62।। नागानामथयक्षाणांराज्ञांचरजनीचर । यच्चपापंकृतंमोहादवलिप्तेनराक्षस ।।6.41.63।। नूनंतेविगतोदर्पःस्वयम्भुवरदानजः । तस्यपापस्यसम्प्राप्ताव्युष्टिरद्यदुरसदा ।।6.41.64।।
explanation: "O night ranger! the time has come for punishment for the sins committed by you to the sages, Devatas, so also to Gandharvas, celestial beauties, Nagas, Yakshas and the kings because of your delusion in conceit. Surely your pride about the boons begotten from the selfborn creator will be gone, said Rama.

shloka_text: ऋषीणांदेवतानांचगन्धर्वाप्सरसांतथा ।।6.41.62।। नागानामथयक्षाणांराज्ञांचरजनीचर । यच्चपापंकृतंमोहादवलिप्तेनराक्षस ।।6.41.63।। नूनंतेविगतोदर्पःस्वयम्भुवरदानजः । तस्यपापस्यसम्प्राप्ताव्युष्टिरद्यदुरसदा ।।6.41.64।।
explanation: "O night ranger! the time has come for punishment for the sins committed by you to the sages, Devatas, so also to Gandharvas, celestial beauties, Nagas, Yakshas and the kings because of your delusion in conceit. Surely your pride about the boons begotten from the selfborn creator will be gone, said Rama.

shloka_text: तस्यदण्डधरस्तेऽहंदाराहरकर्शितः । दण्डंधारयमाणस्तुलङ्काद्वारेव्यवस्थितः ।।6.41.65।।
explanation: "You, who have abducted my wife, I will punish you with a rod of punishment. I am your chastiser, O king of Lanka I have taken position."

shloka_text: पदवींदेवतानांचमहर्षीणांचराक्षस । राजर्षीणांचसर्वेषांगमिष्यसिमयाहतः ।।6.41.66।।
explanation: "O Rakshasa! Even Devatas, sages and even royal sages have also lost their lives, killed by me."

shloka_text: बलेनयेनवैसीतांमाययाराक्षसाधम । यामतिक्रामयित्वात्वंहृतवांस्तद्विदर्शय ।।6.41.67।।
explanation: "O lowly Rakshasa! By deceiving me you took away Sita. Display that strength now."

shloka_text: अराक्षसमिमंलोकंकर्तास्मिनिशितैःशरैः । नचेच्छरणमभ्येषितामादायतुमैथिलीम् ।।6.41.68।।
explanation: "If you do not seek my protection I will devoid this world of Rakshasas with my sharp arrows."

shloka_text: धर्मात्माराक्षसश्रेष्ठःसम्प्राप्तोऽयंविभीषणः । लङ्कैश्वर्यंधृवंश्रीमानयंप्राप्नोत्यकण्डकम् ।।6.41.69।।
explanation: "This Vibheeshana, the best of Rakshasas will be glorious and fortunate undoubtedly having got the kingdom of Lanka."

shloka_text: नहिराज्यमधर्मेणभोक्तुंक्षणमपित्वया । शक्यंमूर्खसहायेनपापेनाविदितात्मना ।।6.41.70।।
explanation: "One who is not aware of himself, an unrighteous sinner ruling with foolish mates cannot enjoy the kingdom even for a moment."

shloka_text: युध्यस्ववाधृतिंकृत्वाशौर्यमालम्ब्यराक्षस । मच्छरैस्त्वंरणेशान्तस्ततःशान्तोभविष्यसि ।।6.41.71।।
explanation: "O Rakshasa! You are resorting to fortitude and valour and embracing gallantry in war. By my arrows you will obtain peace (in death)."

shloka_text: यद्वाविशसिलोकांस्त्रीन्पक्षीभूतोमनोजवः । ममचक्षुष्पथंप्राप्यनजीवन्प्रतियास्यसि ।।6.41.72।।
explanation: "O Ravana! You have no control over your mind, and if you come in the range of my eyesight and enter the three worlds also you will not go alive again."

shloka_text: ब्रवीमित्वांहितंवाक्यंक्रियतामौर्ध्वदैहिकम् । सुदृष्टाक्रियतांलङ्काजीवितंतेमयिस्थितम् ।।6.41.73।।
explanation: Having addressed it in well meaning words, Rama said 'I will do you obsequies as no one will be left in Lanka to do your last rites'.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तःसतुतारेयोरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । जगामाकाशामाविश्यमूर्तिमानिवहव्यवाट् ।।6.41.74।।
explanation: Rama having spoken that way, Tara's son, Angada, who was like fire god, who was unwearied in action flew to the sky.

shloka_text: सोऽतिपत्यमुहूर्तेनश्रीमान्रावणमन्दिरम् । ददर्शासीनमव्यग्रंरावणंसचिवैःसह ।।6.41.75।।
explanation: Angada landed on Ravana's palace in a moment and saw the tiger like prosperous Ravana seated with his ministers.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्य I विदूरेणनिपत्यसहरिपुङ्गवः । दीप्ताग्निसदृशस्तस्थावङ्गदःकनकाङ्गदः ।।6.41.76।।
explanation: Thereafter, the leader of the monkeys, Angada adorned with golden armlets stood like a blazing fire at a distance.

shloka_text: तद्रामवचनंसर्वमन्यूनाधिकमुत्तमम् । सामात्यंश्रावयामासनिवेद्यात्मानमात्मना ।।6.41.77।।
explanation: "I made known the words of Rama completely without adding or deleting. You may listen."

shloka_text: दूतोऽहंकोशलेन्द्रस्यरामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोनामयदितेश्रोत्रमागतः ।।6.41.78।।
explanation: "I am the son of Vali,by name Angada,an envoy of Rama ,the king of Kosala of unwearied action. You may know that I have landed"

shloka_text: अहत्वांराघवोरामःकौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । निष्पत्यप्रतियुध्यस्वनृशंस पुरुषोभव ।।6.41.79।।
explanation: "Raghava, the enhancer of the happiness of Kausalya speaks to you. Ruthless Rakshasa! Sallying forth, get ready for combat."

shloka_text: हन्तास्मित्वांसहामात्यंसपुत्रज्ञातिबान्धवम् । निरुद्विग्नास्त्रयोलोकाभविष्यन्तिहतेत्वयि ।।6.41.80।।
explanation: "You and your son's relatives and followers being killed (by me) the three worlds will be rid of fear of you."

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षाणांगन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् । शत्रुमद्योद्धरिष्यामित्वामृषीणांचकण्टकम् ।।6.41.81।।
explanation: "You are an enemy of the gods, Danavas and Yakshas, Gandharvas and Nagas and being a thorn in the neck of sages, I will uproot you from here."

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यचैश्वर्यंभविष्यतिहतेत्वयि । नचेत्सत्कृत्यवैदेहींप्रणिपत्यप्रदास्यसि ।।6.41.82।।
explanation: "Unless you return back Vaidehi respectfully, bowing down to me you will be killed and Vibheeshana will get the fortune."

shloka_text: इत्येवंपरुषंवाक्यंब्रुवाणेहरिपुङ्गवे । अमर्षवशमापन्नोनिशाचरगणेश्वरः ।।6.41.83।।
explanation: The leader of the monkeys having spoken in that manner, Ravana the ruler of night rangers was overtaken by fury.

shloka_text: ततस्सरोषताम्राक्षश्शशापसचिवांन्नोस्तदा । गृह्यतामेषदुर्मेधावध्यतामितिचासकृत् ।।6.41.84।।
explanation: Thereafter, Ravana who was shaken by fury repeatedly commanded his ministers and said 'Let this evil minded monkey be seized and killed'.

shloka_text: रावणस्यवच्शुत्वादीप्ताग्निसमतेजसा । जगृहुस्तंततोघोराश्चत्वारोरजनीचराः ।।6.41.85।।
explanation: Thereafter, having heard the words of Ravana, the four Rakshasas seized Angada blazing in brilliance like fire.

shloka_text: ग्राहयामासतारेयस्स्वयमात्मनमात्मवान् । बलंदर्शयितुंवीरोयातुधानगणेतदा ।।6.41.86।।
explanation: Then Angada, the son of Tara, on his own wanting to exhibit his strength in the presence of the Rakshasa army allowed himself to be caught.

shloka_text: सतान्बाहुद्वयासक्तानादायपतगानिव । प्रासादंशैलसङ्कामुत्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा ।।6.41.87।।
explanation: Then Angada holding the Rakshasas by his arms came down like birds on the roof of the palace which stood like a mountain.

shloka_text: तेन्तरिक्षाद्विनिर्धूतास्तस्यवेगेनराक्षसाः । भूमौनिपतिताःसर्वेराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपश्यतः ।।6.41.88।।
explanation: Crushed by that speed of Angada coming down as if from the sky all the Rakshasas fell down on the ground while the Rakshasa king looked on.

shloka_text: ततःप्रासादशिखरंशैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम् । ददर्शराक्षसेन्द्रस्यवालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.41.89।।
explanation: Then as the courageous Vali's son landed on the high peak of the palace which resembled a mountain peak, Ravana stood looking.

shloka_text: तत्पफालपदाक्रान्तंदशग्रीवस्यपश्यतः । पुराहिमवतश्शृङ्गंवज्रिणेवविदारितम् ।।6.41.90।।
explanation: As Ravana was looking, Angada trampling his feet gave way to the palace just as Himalayan peak broke to hit Indra.

shloka_text: भङ् क्त्वाप्रासादशिखरंनामविश्राव्यचात्मनः । विनद्यसुमहानादमुत्पपातविहायसम् ।।6.41.91।।
explanation: Hitting on the peak of the palace, Angada declaring his own name emitting loud sound rose up to the sky.

shloka_text: व्यथयन्राक्षसान्सर्वान्हर्षयंश्चापिवानरान् । सवानराणांमध्येतुरामपार्श्वमुपागतः ।।6.41.92।।
explanation: Angada caused pain to the Rakshasas and delighted the monkeys and returned to the midst of Vanaras near Rama.

shloka_text: रावणस्तुपरंचक्रेक्रोधंप्रासादधर्षणात् । विनाशंचात्मनःपश्यन्निश्श्वासपरमोऽभवत् ।।6.41.93।।
explanation: Ravana exhibiting extreme anger at the shattering of his palace and seeing his destruction started sighing heavily.

shloka_text: रामस्तुबहुभिर्हृष्टर्निनदद्भिःप्लवङ्गमैः । वृतोरिपुवधाकाङ्क्षीयुद्धायैवाभ्यवर्तत ।।6.41.94।।
explanation: Delighted by the roaring sound of many monkeys Rama awaited surrounded by groups of monkeys desirous of starting war.

shloka_text: सुषेणस्तुमहावीर्योगिरिकूटोपमोहरिः । बहुभिःसम्वृतस्तत्रवानरैःकामरूपिभिः ।।6.41.95।।
explanation: Sushena of great prowess, who resembled a mountain in form stood there surrounded by many Vanaras who could change their form at their will.

shloka_text: सचतुर्द्वाराणिसर्वाणिसुग्रीववचनात्कपिः । पर्यक्रामतदुर्धर्षोनक्षत्राणीवचन्द्रमाः ।।6.41.96।।
explanation: Sushena, a monkey who is difficult to encounter, went around all the four gates just like the moon goes around stars by the order of Sugriva.

shloka_text: तेषामक्षौहिणिशतंसमवेक्ष्यवनौकसाम् । लङ्कामुपनिविष्टानांसागरंचानिवर्तताम् ।।6.41.97।। राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुस्त्रासंजग्मुस्तथापरे । अपरेसमरोध्धर्षाद्धर्षमेवप्रपेदिरे ।।6.41.98।।
explanation: Seeing the large army of a hundred Akshauhinis of monkeys staying near Lanka spreading beyond the sea waiting for war the Rakshasas were wonder struck, some feared, some were alarmed to witness the jubilant Vanaras who exhibited joy alone.

shloka_text: तेषामक्षौहिणिशतंसमवेक्ष्यवनौकसाम् । लङ्कामुपनिविष्टानांसागरंचानिवर्तताम् ।।6.41.97।। राक्षसाविस्मयंजग्मुस्त्रासंजग्मुस्तथापरे । अपरेसमरोध्धर्षाद्धर्षमेवप्रपेदिरे ।।6.41.98।।
explanation: Seeing the large army of a hundred Akshauhinis of monkeys staying near Lanka spreading beyond the sea waiting for war the Rakshasas were wonder struck, some feared, some were alarmed to witness the jubilant Vanaras who exhibited joy alone.

shloka_text: कृत्स्नंहिकपिभिर्व्याप्तंप्राकारपरिखान्तरम् । ददृशूराक्षसादीनाःप्राकारंनानरीकृतम् ।।6.41.99।। हाहाकारंप्रकुर्वन्तिराक्षसाभयमोहिताः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas were desperate to see the spread of monkeys over the entire area from the boundary to moat of Lanka. The way the space between was filled with Vanaras seemed as though the Vanaras converted into boundaries. Rakshasas were seen making a loud noise.

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्तत्रगत्वारावणमन्दिरम् । न्यवेदयन्पुरींरुद्धांरामेणसहवानरैः ।।6.42.1।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas proceeding to Ravana's abode informed that Rama along with the vanaras have occupied the whole of Lanka.

shloka_text: रुद्धांतुनगरींश्रुत्वाजातक्रोधोनिशाचरः । विधानंद्विगुणंश्रुत्वाप्रासादंसोऽध्यरोहत ।।6.42.2।।
explanation: On knowing that Lanka is occupied, the night ranger Ravana, became very furious and doubled the forces of Lanka for the protection and went to the top of Lanka palace.

shloka_text: सददर्शावृतांलङ्कांसशैलवनकाननाम् । असङ्ख्येयैर्हरिगणैःसर्वतोयुद्धकाङ्क्षिभिः ।।6.42.3।।
explanation: He observed a countless number of Vanara troops spread all over Lanka, mountains, and forests.

shloka_text: सदृष्ट्वावानरैःसर्वांवसुधांकवलीकृताम् । कथंक्षपयितव्याःस्युरितिचिन्तापरोऽभवत् ।।6.42.4।।
explanation: Seeing the Vanaras occupying the entire earth, Ravana thought of destroying and started thinking.

shloka_text: सचिन्तयित्वासुचिरंधैर्यमालम्ब्यरावणः । राघवंहरियूथांश्चददर्शायतलोचनः ।।6.42.5।।
explanation: Ravana, thinking over for long, picking up courage, saw Rama's Vanaras with thoughtful eyes.

shloka_text: राघवःसहसैन्येनमुदितोनामपुप्लुवे । लङ्कांददर्शगुप्तांवैसर्वतोराक्षसैर्वृताम् ।।6.42.6।।
explanation: Raghava accompanied by the army happily went near and witnessed Lanka filled with Rakshasas all over.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वादाशरथिर्लङ्कांचित्रध्वजपताकिनीम् । जगामसहसासीतांदूयमानेनचेतसा ।।6.42.7।।
explanation: The son of Dasaratha saw Lanka decorated with flags and posts and thinking of Sita he became very worried.

shloka_text: अत्रसामृगशावाक्षीमत्कृतेजनकात्मजा । पीड्यतेशोकसन्तप्ताकृशास्थण्डिलशायिनी ।।6.42.8।।
explanation: "Here (Lanka) is the daughter of Janaka, immersed in sorrow because of me, tormented and emaciated without food and struggling."

shloka_text: पीड्यमानांसधर्मात्मावैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन् । क्षिप्रमाज्ञापयामासवानरान्द्विषतांवधे ।।6.42.9।।
explanation: Thinking of Vaidehi again and again, who is pained, Rama ordered the Vanaras to kill the enemies immediately.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तेतुवचनेरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । संघर्षमाणाःप्लवगाःसिम्हनादैरनादयन् ।।6.42.10।।
explanation: Ordered in that way by Rama, who does not cause sorrow, the monkeys roared like lions getting ready for war on hearing Rama's words.

shloka_text: शिखरैर्विकिरामैनांलङ्कांमुष्टिभिरेववा । इतिस्मदधिरेसर्वेमनांसिहरियूथपाः ।।6.42.11।।
explanation: The monkey troops thought of crushing Lanka with their fists and mountain peaks.

shloka_text: उद्यम्यगिरिशृङ्गाणिशिखराणिमहान्तिच । तरूंश्चोत्पाट्यविविधांस्तिष्ठन्तिहरियूथपाः ।।6.42.12।।
explanation: Holding the mountain peaks, huge trees of many kinds, the Vanara leaders stood ready to fight.

shloka_text: प्रेक्षतोराक्षसेन्द्रस्यतान्यनीकानिभागशः । राघवप्रियकामार्थंलङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा ।।6.42.13।।
explanation: To make Rama happy, all the Vanara army divided into groups and started ascending the boundary (of Lanka) walls the king of Rakshasas was witnessing.

shloka_text: तेताम्रवक्त्राहेमाभारामार्थेत्यक्तजीविताः । लङ्कामेवाभ्यवर्तन्तसालतालशिलायुधाः ।।6.42.14।।
explanation: Vanaras of copper colour faces and golden coloured ones, dedicating their lives for the sake of Rama holding Sala trees and rocks went towards Lanka.

shloka_text: तेद्रुमैःपर्वताग्रैश्चमुष्टिभिश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । प्राकाराग्राण्यरण्यानिममन्थुस्तोरणानिच ।।6.42.15।।
explanation: With the means of mountain peaks, as well as their fists, the Vanaras scaled the boundary walls and gateways of the city.

shloka_text: पारिखाःपूरयन्तिस्मप्रसन्नसलिलायुताः । पांसुभिःपर्वताग्रैश्चतृणैःकाष्ठैश्चवानराः ।।6.42.16 ।।
explanation: The Vanaras started filling the moats with soil, pure water, logs of wood, grass, and mountain peaks.

shloka_text: ततःसहस्रयूथाश्चकोटीयूथाश्चवानराः । कोटीशतयुताश्चान्येलङ्कामारुरुहुस्तदा ।।6.42.17।।
explanation: Then the Vanaras in thousands and crores ascended Lanka.

shloka_text: काञ्चनानिप्रमृद्नन्तस्तोरणानिप्लवङ्गमाः । कैलासशिखराभानिगोपुराणिप्रमथ्यच ।।6.42.18।।
explanation: The Vanaras started breaking the golden gateways and crushing them which were like peaks of Kailasa mountain.

shloka_text: आप्लवन्तःप्लवन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । लङ्कांतामभिधावन्तिमहावारणसंनिभाः ।।6.42.19।।
explanation: Jumping here and there like huge elephants, the Vanaras roaring like lions went into Lanka.

shloka_text: जयत्यतिबलोरामोलक्ष्मणश्चमहाबलः । राजाजयतिसुग्रीवोराघवेणाभिपालितः ।।6.42.20।।
explanation: "Victorious is Sri Rama, who is exceedingly strong and Lakshmana who is endowed with supreme strength. Victorious is Sugriva the king of Vanaras who is protected by Raghava on all sides."

shloka_text: इत्येवंघोषयन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । अभ्यधावन्तलङ्कायाःप्राकारंकामरूपिणः ।।6.42.21।।
explanation: Shouting in that manner, the monkeys who could change their form at their will started roaring and rushed towards the defensive walls.

shloka_text: वीरबाहुःसुबाहुश्चनलश्चवनगोचरः । निपीड्योपनिविष्टास्तेप्राकारंहरियूथपाः । एतस्मिन्नन्तरेचक्रुःस्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् ।।6.42.22 ।।
explanation: Veerabahu, Subahu, Nala and the foremost of the Vanara leaders storming the boundary walls in the meantime went inside and stationed at the northeast gate.

shloka_text: पूर्वद्वारंतुकुमुदःकोटीभिर्दशभिर्वृतः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौहरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः ।।6.42.23।।
explanation: Kumuda, surrounded by ten crores of mighty monkeys, who appeared like conquerors, stationed at the east gate.

shloka_text: साहाय्यार्थंतुतस्यैवनिविष्टःप्रघसोहरिः । पनसश्चमहाबाहुर्वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।।6.42.24।।
explanation: Praghasa the broad shouldered Vanara, was surrounded by Panasa for assisting him who encamped surrounded by many.

shloka_text: दक्षिणंद्वारमागम्यवीरःशतबलिःकपिः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौविंशत्याकोटिभिर्वृतः ।।6.42.25।।
explanation: Valiant Satabali with twenty crores of monkeys stood besieging the south gate.

shloka_text: सुषेणःपश्चिमद्वारंगतस्तारापिताहरिः । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौषष्टिकोटिभिरावृतः ।।6.42.26।।
explanation: Sushena, father of Tara, (Vali's wife) the mighty, stood with sixty crores of monkeys at the western gate.

shloka_text: उत्तरंद्वारमासाद्यरामःसौमित्रिणासह । आवृत्यबलवांस्तस्थौसुग्रीवश्चहरीश्वरः ।।6.42.27।।
explanation: Reaching the north gate, Sri Rama along with Saumithri, blockading the gate stood Sugriva the Lord of monkeys.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलोमहाकायोगवाक्षोभीमदर्शनः । वृतःकोट्यामहावीर्यस्तस्थौरामस्यपार्श्वतः ।।6.42.28।।
explanation: Gavaksha of gigantic body and fierce appearance, along with one crore of Golangula species of monkeys endowed with extraordinary virility stood by the side of Sri Rama.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाणांभीमवेगानांधूम्रःशत्रुनिबर्हणः । वृतःकोट्यामहावीर्यस्तस्थौरामस्यपार्श्वतः ।।6.42.29।।
explanation: Accompanied by a crore of Bears of redoubtable fury, Dhumra (brother of Jambavan), an exterminator of foes endowed with extraordinary valour stood by Rama's side.

shloka_text: सन्नद्धस्तुमहावीर्योगदापाणिर्विभीषणः । वृतोयस्तैस्तुसचिवैस्तस्थौतत्रमहाबलः ।।6.42.30।।
explanation: Vibheeshana with defensive clamour, of extraordinary virility accompanied by his mighty ministers, stood there with his mace in hand.

shloka_text: गजोगवाक्षोगवयःशरभोगन्धमादनः । समन्तात्परिधावन्तोररक्षुर्हरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.42.31।।
explanation: Gaja, Gavaksha, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana stood protecting the monkey troops wandering all over.

shloka_text: ततःकोपपरीतात्मारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । निर्याणंसर्वसैन्यानांद्रुतमाज्ञापयत्तदा ।।6.42.32।।
explanation: Thereafter Ravana, the Lord of Rakshasas overcome by fury ordered all his forces to advance.

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वाततोवाक्यंरावणस्यमुखोद्गतम् । सहसाभीमनिर्घोषमुद्घुष्टंरजनीचरैः ।।6.42.33।।
explanation: Hearing the command issued from Ravana's mouth, immediately a terrific roar was raised by the night rangers.

shloka_text: ततःप्रचोदिताभेर्यश्चन्द्रपाण्डरपुष्कराः । हेमकोणाहताभीमाराक्षसानांसमन्ततः ।।6.42.34।।
explanation: Then shone the white discs like the moon beaten by the Rakshasas with gold sticks making terrific sound.

shloka_text: विनेदुश्चमहाघोषाःशङ्खाःशतसहस्रशः । राक्षसानांसुघोराणांमुखमारुतपूरिताः ।।6.42.35।।
explanation: With hundred thousand Rakshasas blowing sonorous conchs, with the wind from their mouths, terrific noise arose.

shloka_text: तेबभुःशुभनीलाङ्गाःसशङ्खारजनीचराः । विद्युन्मण्डलसन्नद्धाःसबलाकाइवाम्बुदाः ।।6.42.36।।
explanation: The night rangers with their brilliant dark limbs, with conchs, were like dark clouds provided with armour with flashes of lightning and accompanied by herons.

shloka_text: निष्पतन्तिततःसैन्याहृष्टारावणचोदिताः । समयेपूर्यमाणस्यवेगाइवमहोदधेः ।।6.42.37।।
explanation: Urged by Ravana, the army then joyfully rushed forth swiftly like a great ocean at the time of universal destruction.

shloka_text: ततोवानरसैन्येनमुक्तोनादःसमन्ततः । मलयःपूरितोयेनससानुप्रस्थकन्दरः ।।6.42.38।।
explanation: Thereafter the Vanara army emitted a sound that filled all sides of Malaya Mountain, its major and minor caves.

shloka_text: शङ्खदुन्दुभिसंघुष्टःसिम्हनादस्तरस्विनाम् । पृथिवींचान्तरिक्षंचसागरंचैवनादयन् ।।6.42.39।।
explanation: By the blast of conchs and roll of drums, and roar of lions of Vanara and Rakshasa forces it resounded all over the earth, sky and up to the ocean.

shloka_text: गजानांबृंहितैःसार्धंहयानांहेषितैरपि । रथानांनेमिघोषैश्चरक्षसाम्वदनस्वनः ।।6.42.40 ।।
explanation: The trumpeting of the elephants, the neighing of horses, the clatter of the wheels of the chariots and the shout of Rakshasas resounded in the air.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेघोरःसङ्ग्रामःसमवर्तत । रक्षसांवानराणांचयथादेवासुरेपुरा ।।6.42.41।।
explanation: In the meantime, dreadful conflict arose all over between Rakshasas and Vanaras, which was like the conflict between Devas and asuras earlier.

shloka_text: तेगदाभिःप्रदीप्ताभिःशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः । निजघ्नुर्वानरान्घोराःकथयन्तःस्वविक्रमान् ।।6.42.42।।
explanation: Vowing their own prowess, the Rakshasas began to strike the Vanaras with maces, flaming javelins, tridents, and pikes fiercely.

shloka_text: राजाजयतिसुग्रीवइतिशब्दोमहानभूत् । राजन्जयजयेत्युक्त्वास्वस्वनामकथान्ततः ।।6.42.43।।
explanation: "May the vanara king,triumphant Sugriva be victorious", thus sounded the cry of vanaras in the battlefield.

shloka_text: तथावृक्षैर्महाकायाःपर्वताग्रैश्चवानराः । निजघ्नुस्तानिरक्षांसिनखैर्दन्तैश्चवेगिताः ।।6.42.44।।
explanation: Vanaras in the same manner attacked the Rakshasas, with trees and mountains, swiftly and with their nails and teeth.

shloka_text: राक्षसास्त्वपरेभीमाःप्राकारस्थामहीगतान् । भिन्दिपालैश्चखड्गैश्चशूलैश्चैवव्यदारयन् ।।6.42.45।।
explanation: Standing on the walls, the redoubtable Rakshasas, pierced the Vanaras with swords, dreadful Bhindipalas.

shloka_text: वानराश्चापिसङ्क्रुद्धाःप्राकारस्थान्महीगताः । राक्षसान्पातयामासुःसमाप्लुत्यप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.42.46।।
explanation: The vanaras jumping up dragged the Rakshasas stationed on the boundary wall down to the ground.

shloka_text: ससम्प्रहारस्तुमुलोमांसशोणितकर्दमः । रक्षसांवानराणांचसम्बभूवाद्भुतोपमाः।।6.42.47।।
explanation: The conflict that happened between the Rakshasas and Vanaras was amazing and intense and left a mire of flesh and blood. ।। इत्यार्षेश्रीमद्वाल्मीकिरामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेद्विचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: युध्यतांतुततस्तेषांवानराणांमहात्मनाम् । रक्षसांसम्बभूवाथबलकोपस्सुदारुणः ।।6.43.1।।
explanation: Thereafter the gigantic army of Vanaras were fighting with exceedingly terrific Rakshasas and the anguished Rakshasas could not tolerate the sight.

shloka_text: तेहयैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्ध्वश्चाग्निशिखोपमैः । रथैश्चादित्यसङ्काशैःकवचैश्चमनोरमैः ।।6.43.2।। निर्ययूराक्षसव्याघ्रानादयन्तोदिशोदश । राक्षसाभीमकर्माणोरावणस्यजयैषिणः ।।6.43.3।।
explanation: Wishing victory for Ravana, the tiger among ogres, the Rakshasas of terrific deeds sallied forth accompanied by horses with golden trappings and seizing posts, which were like flames of fire shining like the sun's rays on the chariots and delightful shields, roaring resounding in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: तेहयैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्ध्वश्चाग्निशिखोपमैः । रथैश्चादित्यसङ्काशैःकवचैश्चमनोरमैः ।।6.43.2।। निर्ययूराक्षसव्याघ्रानादयन्तोदिशोदश । राक्षसाभीमकर्माणोरावणस्यजयैषिणः ।।6.43.3।।
explanation: Wishing victory for Ravana, the tiger among ogres, the Rakshasas of terrific deeds sallied forth accompanied by horses with golden trappings and seizing posts, which were like flames of fire shining like the sun's rays on the chariots and delightful shields, roaring resounding in all the ten directions.

shloka_text: वानराणामपिचमूर्बृहतीजयमिच्छताम् । अभ्यधावततांसेनांरक्षसांकामरूपिणम् ।।6.43.4।।
explanation: Wishing triumph even the powerful army of powerful Vanaras of terrific deeds went ahead to fight with Rakshasas.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेतेषामन्योन्यमभिधावताम् । रक्षसांवानराणांचद्वन्द्वयुद्धमवर्तत ।।6.43.5।।
explanation: At that time the Vanaras and Rakshasas facing each other started a dual fight.

shloka_text: अङ्गदेन्द्रजित्सार्धंवालिपुत्रेणराक्षसः । आयुध्यतमहातेजास्त्ऱ्यम्बकेणयथाऽन्तकः ।।6.43.6।।
explanation: Indrajith, an exceedingly brilliant Rakshasa, contended with Angada, son of Vali just like Lord Siva with and haka, the Lord of death.

shloka_text: प्रजङ्घेनचसम्पातिर्नित्यंदुर्मर्षणोरणे । जम्बुमालिनमारब्धोहनुमानपिवानरः ।।6.43.7।।
explanation: Sampathi , who is invariably difficult to encounter in war fought with Prajangha, and Hanuman started with Jambumali.

shloka_text: संगतस्तुमहाक्रोधोराक्षसोरावणानुजः । समरेतीक्ष्णवेगेनमित्रघ्नेनविभीषणः ।।6.43.8।।
explanation: Highly furious Rakshasa, Vibheeshana, brother of Ravana fought with Rakshasa, Mitraghna.

shloka_text: तपनेनगजस्सार्धंराक्षसेनमहाबलः । निकुम्भेनमहातेजानीलोऽपिसमयुध्यत ।।6.43.9।।
explanation: Gaja of great strength fought with Rakshasa Tapa, and highly energetic Neela fought with Nikumbha.

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्रस्तुसुग्रीवःप्रघसेनसमागतः । सङ्गतःसमरेश्रीमान्विरूपाक्षेणलक्ष्मणः ।।6.43.10।।
explanation: Sugriva the Lord of Vanaras fought with Praghana and prosperous Lakshmana fought with Virupaksha.

shloka_text: अग्निकेतुश्चसुदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चराक्षसः । सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चरामेणसहसङ्गताः ।।6.43.11।।
explanation: Agnikethu, a Rakshasa who is difficult to win over, Rasmikethu, Suptaghna and Yajnakepu waged war with Rama.

shloka_text: वज्रमुष्टिस्तुमैन्देनद्विविदेनाशनिप्रभः । राक्षसाभ्यांसुघोराभ्यांकपिमुख्यौसमागतौ ।।6.43.12।।
explanation: Vajramushti with Mainda and Asaniprabhu with Dwivida, the chief of monkeys, fought with the two Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वीरःप्रतपनोघोरोराक्षसोरणदुर्धरः । समरेतीक्ष्णवेगेननळेनसमयुध्यत ।।6.43.13।।
explanation: Heroic and dreadful Pratapana, who is indomitable in the battle, fought with Nala endowed with high speed.

shloka_text: धर्मस्यपुत्रोबलवान्सुषेणइतिविश्रुतः । सविद्युन्मालिनासार्धमयुध्यतमहाकपिः ।।6.43.14।। वानराश्चापरेभीमाराक्षसैरपरैस्सह । द्वन्द्वंसमीयुस्सहसायुद्धायबहुभिस्सह ।।6.43.15।।
explanation: Mighty Sushena, the righteous son fought with well known Vidyunmali. And fierce monkeys and Rakshasas fought in dual war with each other.

shloka_text: धर्मस्यपुत्रोबलवान्सुषेणइतिविश्रुतः । सविद्युन्मालिनासार्धमयुध्यतमहाकपिः ।।6.43.14।। वानराश्चापरेभीमाराक्षसैरपरैस्सह । द्वन्द्वंसमीयुस्सहसायुद्धायबहुभिस्सह ।।6.43.15।।
explanation: Mighty Sushena, the righteous son fought with well known Vidyunmali. And fierce monkeys and Rakshasas fought in dual war with each other.

shloka_text: तत्रासीत्सुमहद्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । रक्षसांवानराणांचवीराणांजयमिच्छताम् ।।6.43.16।।
explanation: Fierce war which made hair stand on end happened there, with the heroic Rakshasas and Vanaras longing for victory.

shloka_text: हरिराक्षसदेहेभ्यःप्रभूताःकेशशाद्वलाः । शरीरसङ्घाटावहाःप्रसुस्रुश्शोणितापगाः ।।6.43.17।।
explanation: In that war, the streams of blood that flowed from the bodies of Vanaras and Rakshasas were strewn like weeds in the form of hair, bearing logs of wood in the form of dead bodies.

shloka_text: अजघानेन्द्रजित्क्रुद्धोवज्रेणेवशतक्रतुः । अङ्गदंगदयावीरंशत्रुसैन्यविदारणम् ।।6.43.18।।
explanation: Enraged, Indrajith struck Angada with his mace, the destroyer of hostile forces which was like Indra who had done a hundred sacrifices, would strike with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तस्यकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गंरथंसाश्वंससारथिम् । जघानसमरेश्रीमानङ्गदोवेगवान्कपिः ।।6.43.19।।
explanation: With the same mace (snatched from the Rakshasa) Angada swiftly struck Indrajit hand destroyed the horse, chariot, and charioteer.

shloka_text: सम्पातिस्तुत्रिभिर्भाणैःप्रजङ्घेनसमाहतः । निजघानश्वकर्णेनप्रजङ्घंरणमूर्धनि ।।6.43.20।।
explanation: While Prajangha injured Sampathi with three arrows, in turn Sampathi killed him with Aswakarna tree in the midst of war.

shloka_text: जम्बुमालीरथस्थस्तुरथशक्त्यामहाबलः । बिबेदसमरेक्रुद्धोहनूमन्तंस्तनान्तरे ।।6.43.21।।
explanation: Jambumali of extraordinary might mounting on the chariot in the battle pierced Hanuman in his chest.

shloka_text: तस्यतंरथमास्थायहनूमान् मारुतात्मजः । प्रममाथतलेनाशुसहतेनैवरक्षसा ।।6.43.22।।
explanation: Hanuman the son of wind god, getting on to the chariot quickly destroyed that Rakshasa Jambumali with his palm.

shloka_text: नदन् प्रतपनोघोरोनलंसोप्यन्वधावत । नलःप्रतपनस्याशुपातयामासचक्षुषी ।।6.43.23।।
explanation: Dreadful Pratapan roared and jumped over Nala. Nala in turn gouged out the eyes of Pratapan.

shloka_text: भिन्नगात्रश्शरैस्तीक्ष्णैःक्षिप्रहस्तेनरक्षसा । ग्रसन्तमिवसैन्यानिप्रघसंवानराधिपः ।।6.43.24।। सुग्रीवस्सप्तपर्णेननिर्भिभेदजघानच ।
explanation: Sugriva, the Vanara leader, taking hold of Sapataparni tree hit Pratapan who had his mouth open as if to swallow the army and killed him.

shloka_text: अग्निकेतुश्चदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चराक्षसः ।।6.43.25।। सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चरामंनिर्भिभिदुश्शरैः ।
explanation: Even Agnikethu who is difficult to attack, Rakshasas Rasmikethu, also Mitarghna and Yajakopa mangled Sri Rama with arrows.

shloka_text: तेषांचतुर्णांरामस्तुशिरांसिनिशितैश्शरैः । क्रुद्धश्चतुर्भिश्चिच्छेदघोरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.43.26।।
explanation: Raged Rama with his sharp arrows which were like flames of fire destroyed all the four Rakshasas by cutting their heads.

shloka_text: वज्रमुष्टिस्तुमैन्देनमुष्टिनानिहतोरणे । पपातसरथस्साश्वःपुराट्टइवभूतले ।।6.43.27।।
explanation: Even Vajramushti fell on the ground struck with the fist by Mainda and the chariot and charioteer fell like the fort.

shloka_text: निकुम्बस्तुरणेनीलंनीलाञ्जनचयप्रभम् । निर्बिभेदशरैस्तीक्ष्णैःकरैर्मेघमिवांशुमान् ।।6.43.28।।
explanation: Just as the Sun 's rays pierced through clouds Nikumbha was shattered and fell like a mass of collyrium in the battlefield.

shloka_text: पुनश्शरशतेनाथक्षिप्रहस्तोनिशाचरः । बिभेदसमरेनीलंनिकुम्भःप्रजहासच ।।6.43.29।।
explanation: Nikumbha, the night ranger who was endowed with speed in shooting arrows again shot with a thousand arrows and laughed heartily.

shloka_text: तस्यैवरथचक्रेणनीलोविष्णुरिवाहवे । शिरश्चिच्छेदसमरेनिकुम्भस्यचसारथेः ।।6.43.30।।
explanation: Like Lord Vishnu, Nila took the wheels of the chariot of Nikumbha and shattered the charioteer into pieces.

shloka_text: वज्राशनिसमस्पर्शोद्विविदोऽप्यशनिप्रभम् । जघानगिरिशृङ्गेणमिषतांसर्वरक्षसाम् ।।6.43.31।।
explanation: Dwivida whose body was like a thunderbolt to feel, moved about on the mountain peak as Rakshasas were watching.

shloka_text: द्विदिधंवानरेन्द्रंतुनगयोधिनमाहवे । शरैरशनिसङ्काशैस्सविव्याधाशनिप्रभः ।।6.43.32।।
explanation: Asaniprabha shot arrows resembling lightning at Dwivida the Vanara Lord who was fighting with trees.

shloka_text: सशरैरभिविद्धाङ्गोद्विविदःक्रोधमूर्छितः । सालेनसरथंसाश्वंनिजघानाशनिप्रभम् ।।6.43.33।।
explanation: Dwivida whose limbs have been injured being enraged took Sala tree and killed Asaniprabha and the charioteer as well as the horses.

shloka_text: विद्युन्मालीरथस्थस्तुशरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । सुषेणंताडयामासननादचमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.43.34।।
explanation: Vidyunmali mounting the chariot started releasing arrows covered with gold at Sushena and roared.

shloka_text: तंरथस्थमथोदृष्टवासुषेणोवानरोत्तमः । गिरिशृङ्गेणमहतारथमाशुन्यपातयत् ।।6.43.35।।
explanation: Nay, Sushena, the leader of Vanaras, saw himself down and Jambumali on top in the chariot. He crushed him with a big mountain peak.

shloka_text: लाघवेनतुसंयुक्तोविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । अपक्रम्यरथात्तूर्णंगदापाणिःक्षितौस्थितः ।।6.43.36।।
explanation: Vidyunmali seeing Sushena, the monkey leader got a huge rock, and hit him on his chest with the mace.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधसमाविष्टःसुषेणोहरिपुङ्गवः । शिलांसुमहतींगृह्यनिशाचरमभिद्रवत् ।।6.43.37।।
explanation: Thereafter overtaken by anger, the monkey leader Sushena seized the huge rock from the Rakshasa and dropped it.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंगदयाविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । वक्षस्यभिजघानाशुसुषेणंहरिपुङ्गवः ।।6.43.38।।
explanation: Then Vidyunmali, seeing the leader of monkeys getting the huge rock, hit him on the chest with the mace.

shloka_text: गदाप्रहारंतंघोरमच्नित्यप्लवगोत्तमः । तांशिलांपातयामासतस्योरसिमहामृधे ।।6.43.39।।
explanation: The great monkey leader Sushena, not caring for the mace, dropped the rock on Vidyunmali's chest.

shloka_text: शिलाप्रहारभिहतोविद्युन्मालीनिशाचरः । निष्पिष्टहृदयोभूमौगतासुर्निपपातह ।।6.43.40।।
explanation: Vidyunmali, the Rakshasa hit by the huge rock, was ceased of life.

shloka_text: एवंतैर्वानरैश्शूरैश्शूरास्तेरजनीचराः । द्वन्द्वेविमृदितास्तत्रदैत्याइवदिवौकसैः ।।6.43.41।।
explanation: In that manner the Rakshasa warriors and the Vanara warriors fought the duel wonderfully and like the way Devatas killed the Demons, the Rakshasas were killed.

shloka_text: भग्नैखडगैर्गदाभिश्चशक्तितोमरपट्टसै: । अपविद्धैश्चाभिन्नैश्चरथैस्साङ्ग्रामिकैर्हयैः ।।6.43.42।। निहतैःकुञ्जरैर्मत्स्सैस्तथावानरराक्षसैः । चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्चभग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः ।।6.43.43।। बभूवायोधनंघोरंगोमायुगणसेवितम् ।
explanation: The battlefield was dreadful and, frequented by jackals with spears, javelins, maces, and swords, strewn all over, similarly with broken chariots, horses, elephants, and monkeys fit for war. Broken wheels and axles of chariots were found all over.

shloka_text: भग्नैखडगैर्गदाभिश्चशक्तितोमरपट्टसै: । अपविद्धैश्चाभिन्नैश्चरथैस्साङ्ग्रामिकैर्हयैः ।।6.43.42।। निहतैःकुञ्जरैर्मत्स्सैस्तथावानरराक्षसैः । चक्राक्षयुगदण्डैश्चभग्नैर्धरणिसंश्रितैः ।।6.43.43।। बभूवायोधनंघोरंगोमायुगणसेवितम् ।
explanation: The battlefield was dreadful and, frequented by jackals with spears, javelins, maces, and swords, strewn all over, similarly with broken chariots, horses, elephants, and monkeys fit for war. Broken wheels and axles of chariots were found all over.

shloka_text: कबन्धानिसमुत्पेतुर्दिक्षुवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.43.44।। विमर्देतुमुलेतस्मिन्देवासुररणोपमे ।
explanation: It was like the war between Devatas and demons, with the trunks of the bodies of Vanaras and Rakshasas rubbing together lying scattered in all directions.

shloka_text: विदार्यमाणाहरिपुङ्गवैस्तदानिशाचराश्शोणितदिग्धगात्राः । पुनःसुयुद्धंतरसासमास्थितादिवाकरस्यास्तमयाभिकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.43.45।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas killed by Vanara leaders, their bodies full of blood were looking for sunset and again picking up strength began to battle. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेत्रिचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty third sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: युध्यतामेनतेषांतुतदावानरराक्षसाम् । रविरस्तंगतोरात्रिःप्रवृत्ताप्राणहारिणी ।।6.44.1।।
explanation: Thus, as the Vanaras and Rakshasas were battling, the Sun began to set, which is not favourable to the life of Vanaras.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यंबद्धवैराणांघोराणांजयमिच्छताम् । सम्प्रवृत्तंनिशायुद्धंतदावानररक्षसाम् ।।6.44.2।।
explanation: Then Vanaras and dreadful Rakshasas being strongly inimical to each other started the night battle wishing victory.

shloka_text: राक्षसोऽसीतिहरयोहरिश्चाऽसीतिराक्षसाः । अन्योन्यंसमरेजघ्नुस्तस्मिंस्तमसिदारुणे ।।6.44.3।।
explanation: In the fierce darkness that prevailed, monkeys hit monkeys thinking to be Rakshasas and Rakshasas hit Rakshasas thinking to be Vanaras (not knowing in darkness) hit each other.

shloka_text: जहिदारयचैहीतिकथंविद्रवसीतिच । एवंसुतुमुलश्शब्दस्तस्मिंस्तमसिशुश्रुवे ।।6.44.4।। कालाःकाञ्चनसन्नाहास्तस्मिंस्तमसिराक्षसाः । सम्प्रदृश्यन्तशैलेन्द्रादीप्तौषधिवनाइव ।।6.44.5।।
explanation: "Strike", "Tear", "Why are you running away?" were the kind of tumultuous echo heard in the darkness of the night. In that darkness the dark complexioned Vanaras and Rakshasas covered with golden armour in the night seemed like shining herbs of the forest in the mountain.

shloka_text: जहिदारयचैहीतिकथंविद्रवसीतिच । एवंसुतुमुलश्शब्दस्तस्मिंस्तमसिशुश्रुवे ।।6.44.4।। कालाःकाञ्चनसन्नाहास्तस्मिंस्तमसिराक्षसाः । सम्प्रदृश्यन्तशैलेन्द्रादीप्तौषधिवनाइव ।।6.44.5।।
explanation: "Strike", "Tear", "Why are you running away?" were the kind of tumultuous echo heard in the darkness of the night. In that darkness the dark complexioned Vanaras and Rakshasas covered with golden armour in the night seemed like shining herbs of the forest in the mountain.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तमसिदुष्पारेराक्षसाःक्रोधमूर्छिताः । परिपेतुर्महावेगाभक्षयन्तःप्लवङ्गमान् ।।6.44.6।।
explanation: In that pitch darkness, which was difficult even to move, the Rakshasas overcome by anger and lost senses were wandering devouring the monkeys.

shloka_text: तेहयान् काञ्चनापीडान् ध्वजांश्चाशीविषोपमान् । आप्लुत्यदशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भीमकोपाव्यदारयन् ।।6.44.7।। वानराबलिनोयुद्धेऽक्षोभयन् राक्षसींचमूम् ।
explanation: The mighty strong Vanaras, terribly angry at the Rakshasas sprang up to the sky, and tore with their sharp teeth, the horses of Rakshasas decked with golden ornaments pervading like fire in the battle.

shloka_text: कुञ्जरान् कुञ्जरारोहान् पताकाध्वजिनोरथान् ।।6.44.8।। कर्षुश्चददंशुश्चदशनैःक्रोधमूर्छिताः ।
explanation: Having lost senses in fury they dragged the elephants, those mounted upon them, and the chariots decorated with posts and flags and tore them with their teeth.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्चापिरामश्चशरैराशीविषोपमैः ।।6.44.9।। दृश्यादृश्यानिरक्षांसिप्रवराणिनिजघ्नतुः ।
explanation: Then Rama as well as Lakshmana with their venomous snakelike arrows killed both visible and invisible principal Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तुरङ्गखुरविध्वस्तंरथनेमिसमुत्थितम् ।।6.44.10।। रुरोधकर्णनेत्राणियुध्यतांधरणीरजः ।
explanation: Then the dust rose from the ground pulverised the horses' hooves and crushed by the chariot wheels, filling the ears and eyes of those in war.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतथाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेरोमहर्षणे ।।6.44.11।। रुधिरोधामहाघोरानद्यस्तत्रप्रसुस्रुवुः ।
explanation: In that way as the war was going on, and rivers of blood flowing with the terrific noise it made hair stand on end.

shloka_text: ततोभेरीमृदङ्गानांपणवानांचनिस्स्वनः ।।6.44.12।। शङ्खवेणुस्वनोन्मिश्रस्सम्भूवाद्भुतोपमः ।
explanation: There arose wonderful sounds of musical instruments, the sounds of kettle drums, wooden drums, mixed with conchs and flutes.

shloka_text: हतानांस्तनमानानांराक्षसानांचनिःस्वनः ।।6.44.13।। शस्तानांवानराणांचसम्बभूवातिदारुणः ।
explanation: There from the battlefield arose the roaring sounds of wounded and appeased Rakshasas and Vanaras.

shloka_text: हतैर्वानरवीरैश्चशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः ।।6.44.14।। निहतैःपर्वताकारैराक्षसैःकामरूपिभिः । शस्त्रपुष्पोपहाराचतत्रासीद्युद्धमेदिनी ।।6.44.15।। दुर् ज्ञेयादुर्निवेशाचशोणितास्रावकर्दमा ।
explanation: There with warriors of Vanaras wounded by javelins, tridents and axes, and the Rakshasas of mountain size who could change their form at will, the battlefield was muddy, and wet with blood flowing and difficult to reach.

shloka_text: हतैर्वानरवीरैश्चशक्तिशूलपरश्वधैः ।।6.44.14।। निहतैःपर्वताकारैराक्षसैःकामरूपिभिः । शस्त्रपुष्पोपहाराचतत्रासीद्युद्धमेदिनी ।।6.44.15।। दुर् ज्ञेयादुर्निवेशाचशोणितास्रावकर्दमा ।
explanation: There with warriors of Vanaras wounded by javelins, tridents and axes, and the Rakshasas of mountain size who could change their form at will, the battlefield was muddy, and wet with blood flowing and difficult to reach.

shloka_text: साबभूवनिशाघोराहरिराक्षसहारिणी ।।6.44.16।। कालरात्रीवभूतानांसर्वेषांदुरतिक्रमा ।
explanation: Like the dreadful night for all beings, difficult to spend, as if it were a dissolution, destructive to Vanaras and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्तत्रतस्मिंस्तमसिदारुणे ।।6.44.17।। राममेवाभ्यवर्तन्तसम्हृष्टाश्शरवृष्टिभिः ।
explanation: Thereafter in that exceedingly fearsome dark night in the battlefield highly delighted Rakshasas assailed Rama with a rain of arrows.

shloka_text: तेषामापततांशब्दःक्रुद्धानामपिगर्जताम् ।।6.44.18।। उद्वर्तइवसत्त्व, नांसमुद्राणांप्रशुश्रुवे ।
explanation: The thundering noise of the angry Rakshasas rushing towards Rama was like the seven seas rising to flow into the ocean.

shloka_text: तेषांरामश्शरैःषडिभःषडजघाननिशाचरान् ।।6.44.19।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेणशितैरग्निशिखोपमैः । यमशत्रुश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.44.20।। वज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाकायस्तौचोभौशुकसारणौ । तेतुरामेणबाणौघैस्सर्वेमर्मसुताडिताः ।।6.44.21।। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्रसावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ।
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

shloka_text: तेषांरामश्शरैःषडिभःषडजघाननिशाचरान् ।।6.44.19।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेणशितैरग्निशिखोपमैः । यमशत्रुश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.44.20।। वज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाकायस्तौचोभौशुकसारणौ । तेतुरामेणबाणौघैस्सर्वेमर्मसुताडिताः ।।6.44.21।। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्रसावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ।
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

shloka_text: तेषांरामश्शरैःषडिभःषडजघाननिशाचरान् ।।6.44.19।। निमेषान्तरमात्रेणशितैरग्निशिखोपमैः । यमशत्रुश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.44.20।। वज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाकायस्तौचोभौशुकसारणौ । तेतुरामेणबाणौघैस्सर्वेमर्मसुताडिताः ।।6.44.21।। युद्धादपसृतास्तत्रसावशेषायुषोऽभवन् ।
explanation: On Rama striking with the six best of shafts like flames in a time of twinkling of eyelids, the six Rakshasas, Yamasatru, Mahaparva, Mahodara, Mahakaya, and Vajradamshtra found it difficult to overcome. Along with the two Suka, Saranas all of them were struck by Rama's fire like arrows in their vital parts and escaped with leftover life.

shloka_text: तत्रकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.44.22।। दिशश्चकारविमलाःप्रदिशश्चमहारथः ।
explanation: Mighty Rama with his shafts that were like flames of fire, decorated with gold, brightened in all directions.

shloka_text: येत्वन्येराक्षसाभीमारामस्याभिमुखेस्थिताः ।।6.44.23।। तेऽपिनष्टाःसमासाद्यपतङ्गाइवपावकम् ।
explanation: Those fierce Rakshasas who stood in front of Rama were destroyed like fireflies fallen in fire.

shloka_text: सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्विशिखैस्सपतद्भिस्सहस्रशः ।।6.44.24।। बभूवरजनीचित्राखद्योतैरिवशारदी ।
explanation: By the rain of thousands of golden feathered arrows, the night appeared as if illumined by fireflies and like a wonderful autumnal night.

shloka_text: राक्षसानांचनिनदैर्हरीणांचापिनिस्स्वनैः ।।6.44.25।। साबभूवनिशाघोराभूयोघोरतरातदा ।
explanation: The night which was fierce appeared more dreadful with the loud noise of Rakshasas and Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेनशब्देनमहताप्रवृद्धेनसमन्ततः ।।6.44.26।। त्रिकूटःकन्दराकीर्णःप्रव्याहरदिवाचलः ।
explanation: Resounding with the sound rising all over the caves of Trikuta mountain echoed and it looked as if the mountain was responding to someone's call.

shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलामहाकायास्तमसातुल्यवर्चसः ।।6.44.27।। सम्परिष्वज्यबाहुभ्यांभक्षयन्रजनीचरान् ।
explanation: The dark complexioned Rakshasas of gigantic body, who were highly energetic were held tightly by the monkeys with black faces and long tails and allowed them to be devoured.

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्तुरणेशत्रूननिहन्तुंसमुपस्थितः ।।6.44.28।। रावणिंनिजघानाशुसारथिंचहयानपि ।
explanation: Angada who was determined to kill the enemies, in no time wounded Ravana's charioteer and also the horses.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतदाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेभृशदारुणे ।।6.44.29।। इन्द्रजित्तुरथंत्यक्त्वाहताश्वोहतसारथिः । अङ्गदेनमहामायस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।।6.44.30।।
explanation: As the violent war was going on, the great cheat, Indrajith disappeared from there as Angada had already killed his horses and charioteer.

shloka_text: वर्तमानेतदाघोरेसङ्ग्रामेभृशदारुणे ।।6.44.29।। इन्द्रजित्तुरथंत्यक्त्वाहताश्वोहतसारथिः । अङ्गदेनमहामायस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।।6.44.30।।
explanation: As the violent war was going on, the great cheat, Indrajith disappeared from there as Angada had already killed his horses and charioteer.

shloka_text: तत्कर्मवालिपुत्रस्यसर्वेदेवास्सहर्षिभिः । तुष्टुवुःपूजनार्हस्यतौचोभौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.44.31।।
explanation: Angada who was worthy of worship, was praised by even the sages, all deities and both Rama and Lakshmana for his action.

shloka_text: प्रभावंसर्वभूतानिविदुरिन्द्रजितोयुधि । तेनतेतंमहात्मानंतुष्टाःदृष्टवाप्रधर्षितम् ।।6.44.32।।
explanation: All beings present in war were aware of Indrajith's deeds. Therefore, they were gratified to see him defeated.

shloka_text: ततःप्रहृष्टाःकपयस्ससुग्रीवविभीषणाः । साधुसाध्वितिनेदुश्चदृष्टवाशत्रुंप्रधर्षितम् ।।6.44.33।।
explanation: Thereafter, Sugriva, Vibheeshana and all monkeys gratified with Angada's deed cried out saying "Excellent, Well done".

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुतदातेननिर्जितोभीमकर्मणा । संयुगेवालिपुत्रेणक्रोधंचक्रेसुदारुणम् ।।6.44.34।।
explanation: Then Indrajith of terrible deeds defeated by Angada in the comb at became terribly angry.

shloka_text: सोऽन्तर्धानगतःपापोरावणीरणकर्कशः । अदृश्योनिशितान्बाणान्मुमोचाशनिवर्चसः ।।6.44.35।।
explanation: That sinful son of Ravana, who is capable of encountering rising up remained invisible and shot sharp arrows.

shloka_text: सरामंलक्ष्मणंचैवघोरैर्नागमयैश्शरैः । बिभेदसमरेक्रुद्धःसर्वगात्रेषुराक्षसः ।।6.44.36।।
explanation: The angry Rakshasa (remaining invisible) pierced arrows full of serpents all over the body of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: माययासम्वृतस्तत्रमोहयन्राघवौयुधि । अदृश्यस्सर्वभूतानांकूटयोधीनिशाचरः ।।6.44.37।। बबन्धशरबन्धेनभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: The Rakshasa waging war in invisible form with all beings by his supernatural powers fought with both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana and bound them in a network of arrows.

shloka_text: तेनतौपुरुषव्याघ्रौक्रुद्धेनाशीविषैश्शरैः ।।6.44.38।। सहसानिहतौवीरौतदाप्रैक्षन्तवानराः ।
explanation: Then the Vanaras beheld the two brothers, tigers among men bound forcibly by the angry Rakshasas like venomous monkeys.

shloka_text: प्रकाशरूपस्तुतदानशक्तस्तौबाधितुंराक्षसराजपुत्रः । मायांप्रयोक्तुंसमुपाजगामबबन्धतौराजसुतौदुरात्मा ।।6.44.39।।
explanation: Then the evil minded Rakshasa king's son, being incapable of getting bound in visible form, by remaining invisible, bound them deceitfully. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचतुश्चत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सतस्यगतिमन्विच्छन्राजपुत्रःप्रतापवान् । दिदेशातिबलोरामोदशवानरयूथपान् ।।6.45.1।।
explanation: Rama, the son of the king, a powerful and strong warrior, ordered ten Vanaras to know the whereabouts (of Indrajith).

shloka_text: द्वौसुषेणस्यदायादौनीलंचप्लवगर्षपम् । अङ्गदंवालिपुत्रंचशरभंचतरस्विनम् ।।6.45.2।। विनतंजाम्बवन्तंचसानुप्रस्थंमहाबलम् । ऋषभंचर्षभस्कन्थमादिदेशपरन्तपः ।।6.45.3।।
explanation: Rama, the scorcher of enemies, ordered the two sons of Sushena, the best of Vanaras Neela, Jambavantha, Angada, as well as courageous Sarabha, Vinatha, and Hanumantha and Sanuprastha endowed with extraordinary might, also Rshaba and Rshaba Skanda.

shloka_text: द्वौसुषेणस्यदायादौनीलंचप्लवगर्षपम् । अङ्गदंवालिपुत्रंचशरभंचतरस्विनम् ।।6.45.2।। विनतंजाम्बवन्तंचसानुप्रस्थंमहाबलम् । ऋषभंचर्षभस्कन्थमादिदेशपरन्तपः ।।6.45.3।।
explanation: Rama, the scorcher of enemies, ordered the two sons of Sushena, the best of Vanaras Neela, Jambavantha, Angada, as well as courageous Sarabha, Vinatha, and Hanumantha and Sanuprastha endowed with extraordinary might, also Rshaba and Rshaba Skanda.

shloka_text: तेसम्प्रहृष्टाहरयोभीमानुद्यम्यपादपान् । आकाशंविविशुस्सर्वेमार्गमाणादिशोदशः ।।6.45.4।।
explanation: All those monkeys, exceedingly rejoiced, held huge trees, and went in ten directions searching and sprang to the sky.

shloka_text: तेषांवेगवतांवेगमिषुभिर्वेगवत्तरैः । अस्त्रवित्परमास्तैरैस्तुवारयामासरावणिः ।।6.45.5।।
explanation: Ravana's son being skilled in the use of weapons and an expert in mystic powers, he prohibited the speed of the Vanaras with his swift arrows.

shloka_text: तंभीममार्गमाणादिशोदशःवेगाहरयोनाराचैःक्षतविग्रहाः । अन्धकारेनददृशुर्मेघैस्सूर्यमिवावृतम् ।।6.45.6।।
explanation: The Vanaras were mangled with iron arrows, however endowed with high speed they could not make out Indrajith in utter darkness just as the sun covered by clouds.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोरेवसर्वदेहभिदश्शरान् । भृशमावेशयामासरावणिस्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.45.7।।
explanation: Indrajith who is ever victorious, pierced repeatedly arrows all over the body of Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: निरन्तरशीरीरौतुतावुभौरामलक्ष्मणौ । क्रुद्धेनेन्द्रजितावीरौपन्नगैश्शरतांगतैः ।।6.45.8।।
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana were pierced by furious Indrajith with serpents like arrows furious.

shloka_text: तयोःक्षतजमार्गेणसुस्रावरुधिरंबहु । तावुभौचप्रकाशेतेपुष्पिताविवकिंशुकौ ।।6.45.9।।
explanation: Both Rama and Lakshmana bleeding excessively, wounded profusely, looked bright and red like Kimsuka trees with flowers.

shloka_text: ततःपर्यन्तरक्ताक्षोभिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः । रावणिर्भ्रातरौवाक्यमन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.45.10।।
explanation: Then Ravana's son with the corner of his eyes turned red in anger looking like a huge collyrium, vanished from there and spoke these words to the two brothers, Rama, and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: युध्यमानमनालक्षयंशक्रोऽपित्रिदशेश्वरः । द्रष्टुमासादितुंवापिनशक्तःकिंपुनर्युवाम् ।।6.45.11।।
explanation: Indrajith who had fire like eyes, said," even the ruler of gods cannot discern while I am fighting war, why speak about you? It is not possible."

shloka_text: प्रावृताविषुजालेनराघवौकङ्कपत्रिणा । एषरोषपरीतात्मानयामियमसादनम् ।।6.45.12।।
explanation: "Raghava brothers! You are enmeshed with plumes of arrows all over the body. My anger will not go waste. I will send you to the abode of Yama, the Lord of death."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुधर्मज्ञौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । निर्बिभेदशितैर्बाणैःप्रजहर्षननादच ।।6.45.13।।
explanation: Indrajith having spoken to the righteous brothers Rama and Lakshmana in that way, began to pain them with arrows and stood rejoiced roaring aloud.

shloka_text: भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामोविष्फार्यविपुलंधनुः । भूयोभूयश्शरान्घोरान् विससर्जमहामृथे ।।6.45.14।।
explanation: Indrajith who was like a mass of crushed black hill, mounting the huge bow released terrific arrows again and again in that great conflict.

shloka_text: ततोमर्मसुमर्मज्ञोमज्जयननिशितान् शरान् । रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वीरोननदाचमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.45.15।।
explanation: There after that warrior went on digging sharp arrows into the vital parts of Rama and Lakshmana again and again and kept roaring.

shloka_text: बद्धौतुशरशब्देनतावुभौरणमूर्धनि । निमेषान्तरमात्रेणनशेकतुदीक्षितुम् ।।6.45.16।।
explanation: In a fraction of a second, both Rama and Lakshmana facing the battle were bound by arrows and did not have energy to retaliate.

shloka_text: ततोविभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरशल्याचितावुभौ । ध्वजाविवमहेन्द्रस्यरज्जुमुक्तौप्रकम्पितौ ।।6.45.17।। तौसम्प्रचलितौवीरौमर्मभेदेनकर्शितौ । निपेततुर्महेष्वासौजगत्यांजगतीपती ।।6.45.18।।
explanation: Pierced all over their bodies with the heads of arrows, the gallant princes freed themselves from the cords by shaking violently like the banners of Indra. Pained by the hurting of the vital parts of both the princes, the Lords of the world fell.

shloka_text: ततोविभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरशल्याचितावुभौ । ध्वजाविवमहेन्द्रस्यरज्जुमुक्तौप्रकम्पितौ ।।6.45.17।। तौसम्प्रचलितौवीरौमर्मभेदेनकर्शितौ । निपेततुर्महेष्वासौजगत्यांजगतीपती ।।6.45.18।।
explanation: Pierced all over their bodies with the heads of arrows, the gallant princes freed themselves from the cords by shaking violently like the banners of Indra. Pained by the hurting of the vital parts of both the princes, the Lords of the world fell.

shloka_text: तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ । शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गैवार्तौपरमपीडितौ ।।6.45.19।।
explanation: The princes were lying on the warrior's bed in the battlefield, their limbs fully covered with arrows, in a highly distressed state.

shloka_text: नह्यविद्धंतयोर्गात्रेबभूवाङ्गुळमन्तरम् । नानिर्भिन्नंनचास्तब्दमाकराग्रादजिह्मगैः ।।6.45.20।।
explanation: Not an inch of space on their bodies remained without being pierced. Not even a part of the body was left unshaken, unhurt, or wounded.

shloka_text: तौतुक्रूरेणनिहतौरक्षसाकामरूपिणा । असृक्सुस्रुवतुस्तीव्रंजलंप्रस्रवणाविव ।।6.45.21।।
explanation: Wounded by the cruel Rakshasas capable of changing form at their will, blood flowed from their body copiously like water from spring bringing out their vital life breaths.

shloka_text: पपातप्रथमंरामोविद्धोमर्मसुमार्गणैः । क्रोधादिन्द्रजितायेनपुराशक्रोविनिर्जितः ।।6.45.22।।
explanation: Rama fell first pierced by arrows in his vital parts released in anger by Indrajith, by whom Indra was utterly defeated.

shloka_text: रुक्मपुङ्खैःप्रसन्नाग्रैरधोगतिभिराशुगैः । नाराचैरर्धनाराचैर्भल्लैरञ्जलिकैरपि ।।6.45.23।। विव्याधवत्सदन्तैश्चसिंहदंष्ट्रैःक्षुरैस्तथा ।
explanation: Indrajith pierced Rama with arrows coated with gold and gold tipped arrows, which had even and circular heads, with halfmoon arrows, with axe like heads, heads like joined palms, heads resembling teeth of calf and lion teeth arrows as well as razor sharp arrows which descended quickly unobstructed like dust.

shloka_text: सवीरशयनेशिश्येविज्यमादायकार्मुकम् ।।6.45.24।। भिन्नमुष्टिपरीणाहंत्रिणतंरुक्मभूषितम् ।
explanation: Rama lay relaxed on the hero's bed quitting his goldplated bow strung and bent at both ends, and the middle.

shloka_text: बाणपातान्तरेरामंपतितंपुरुषर्षभम् ।।6.45.25।। सतत्रलक्ष्मणोदृष्टवानिराशोजीवितेऽभवत् ।
explanation: Lakshmana remained beholding the best of men fallen at an arrow's throw disappointed at his life.

shloka_text: रामंकमलपत्राक्षंशरबन्धपरिक्षतम् ।।6.45.26।। शुशोचभ्रातरंदृष्टवापतितंधरणीतले ।
explanation: Lakshmana grieved seeing his elder brother Rama pierced by arrows, pained, and fallen on the ground.

shloka_text: हरयश्चापितंदृष्टवासन्तापंपरमंगताः ।।6.45.27।। शोकार्ताश्चुक्रशुर्घोरमश्रुपूरितलोचनाः ।
explanation: Even the monkeys' eyes were filled with tears, very much stricken with grief seeing Rama fallen and shrieked.

shloka_text: बद्धौतुवीरौपतितौशयानौतेवानरास्सम्परिवार्यतस्थुः । समागतावायुसुतप्रमुख्याविषादमार्ताःपरमंचजग्मुः ।।6.45.28।।
explanation: Hanuman's army of Vanaras collected together stood surrounding fallen princes lying on the ground, despondent and extremely sorrowful. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेपञ्चचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty fifth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोद्यांपृथिवींचैववीक्षमाणावनौकसः । ददृशुःसन्ततौबाणैर्भ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.46.1।।
explanation: Thereafter looking at the sky and the ground for Rama and Lakshmana, the Vanara leaders saw the two brothers, lying on the ground hurt by arrows.

shloka_text: वृष्टवेवोपरतेदेवेकृतकर्मणिराक्षसे । आजगामाथतंदेशंससुग्रीवोविभीषणः ।।6.46.2।।
explanation: Indrajith retired after completing the task, like a cloud that retires after raining. Then came Vibheeshana and Sugriva to that location.

shloka_text: नीलद्विविदमैन्दाश्चसुषेणःकुमुदाङ्गदा: । तूर्णंहनुमतासार्धमन्वशोचन्तराघवौ ।।6.46.3।।
explanation: Neela, Dwivida, Mainda, Sushena, Kumuda, Angada accompanied by Hanuman grieved intensely on looking at the Raghavas.

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।
explanation: Unable to move, with feeble breath, drenched in blood and the body covered all over with arrows, lying on a bed of arrows, stunned, with reduced prowess, sighing like serpents, the heroes, Rama, and Lakshmana, who were like golden posts became dull. Rama and Lakshmana were lying on a heroic bed, arrows stuck to the bodies. Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras kept seeing both the scions and wept surrounding them.

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।

Rama and Lakshmana were lying on a heroic bed, arrows stuck to the bodies. Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras kept seeing both the scions and wept surrounding them.

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।

shloka_text: अचेष्टौमन्दनिश्श्वासौशोणितौघपरिप्लुतौ । शरजालाचितौस्तब्दौशयानौशरतल्पयोः ।।6.46.4।। निःश्वसन्तौयथासर्पौनिश्चेष्टौमन्दविक्रमौ । रुधिरस्राद्विग्धाङ्गौतापनीयाविवध्वजौ ।।6.46.5।। तौवीरशयनेवीरौशयानौमन्दचेष्टितौ । यूथपैस्तै: परिवृतौबाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः ।।6.46.6।। राघवौपतितौदृष्टवाशरजालसमावृतौ । बभूवुर्वेर्व्यथितास्सर्वेवानरास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.46.7।।

Rama and Lakshmana were lying on a heroic bed, arrows stuck to the bodies. Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras kept seeing both the scions and wept surrounding them.

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षंनिरीक्षन्तोदिशस्सर्वाश्चवानराः । नचैनंमाययाछन्नंददृशूरावणिःरणे ।।6.46.8।।
explanation: Though the Vanaras searched all over the battlefield and in all directions of the sky, they could not see Indrajith of mystical powers.

shloka_text: तंतुमायाप्रतिच्छन्नंमाययैवविभीषणः । वीक्षमाणोददर्शाथभ्रातुःपुत्रमवस्थितम् ।।6.46.9।।
explanation: Vibheeshana started looking with occult powers for his brother's son endowed with occult power following occult means and found Indrajith.

shloka_text: तमप्रतिकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे । ददर्शान्तर्हितंवीरंवरदानाद्विभीषणः ।।6.46.10।। तेजसायशसाचैवविक्रमेणचसम्युतम् ।
explanation: Brilliant and glorious Vibheeshana, capable of difficult deeds, incomparable at work, and in fight, unrivalled in battle, saw the hidden hero Indrajith by virtue of a boon (from Brahma).

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्त्वात्मनःकर्मतौशयानौसमीक्ष्यच ।।6.46.11।। उवाचपरमप्रीतोहर्षयन् सर्वनैरृतान् ।
explanation: Reviewing the scions lying on bed by his action, Indrajith caused extreme joy to all Rakshasas and spoke.

shloka_text: दूषणस्यचहन्तारौखरस्यचमहाबलौ ।।6.46.12।। सादितौमामकैर्बाणैर्भ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: "The two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, who slayed Dushana and Khara have been struck."

shloka_text: नेमौमोक्षयितुंशक्यावेतस्मादिषुबन्धनात् ।।6.46.13।। सर्वैरपिसमागम्यसर्षिसङ्घैस्सुरासुरैः ।
explanation: "Even if all the sages, Devatas and Rakshasas collected together come, they cannot get liberated from this bondage of arrows."

shloka_text: यत्कृतेचिन्तयानस्यशोकार्तस्यपितुर्मम ।।6.46.14।। अस्पृष्टवाशयनंगात्रैस्त्रियामायातिशर्वरी । त्स्नेयंयत्कृतेलङ्कानदीवर्षास्विवाकुला ।।6.46.15।। सोऽयंमूलहरोऽनर्थःसर्वेषांनिहतोमया ।
explanation: "On whose account my father was in grief and spent all night and passed the three parts of the night (without sleep) and why he was unable to sleep was not understood clearly. By his (Rama's) action this Lanka is agitated like a river during the rainy season. He, who is the root cause of this calamity, has been got rid of by me," thought Indrajith.

shloka_text: यत्कृतेचिन्तयानस्यशोकार्तस्यपितुर्मम ।।6.46.14।। अस्पृष्टवाशयनंगात्रैस्त्रियामायातिशर्वरी । त्स्नेयंयत्कृतेलङ्कानदीवर्षास्विवाकुला ।।6.46.15।। सोऽयंमूलहरोऽनर्थःसर्वेषांनिहतोमया ।
explanation: "On whose account my father was in grief and spent all night and passed the three parts of the night (without sleep) and why he was unable to sleep was not understood clearly. By his (Rama's) action this Lanka is agitated like a river during the rainy season. He, who is the root cause of this calamity, has been got rid of by me," thought Indrajith.

shloka_text: रामस्यलक्ष्मणस्यैवसर्वेषांचवनौकसाम् । विक्रमानिष्फलाःसर्वेयथाशरदितोयदाः ।।6.46.16।।
explanation: "Rama, and Lakshmana and even all valiant Vanaras have been got rid of just like clouds of autumn are wasted."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुतान् सर्वान्राक्षसान्परिपार्श्वतः ।।6.46.17।। यूथपानपितान्सर्वांस्ताडयामासरावणिः ।
explanation: Indrajith, having spoken in that way to all Rakshasas, began to strike all the Vanara leaders looking at him.

shloka_text: नीलंनवभिराहत्यमैन्दंचद्विविदंतथा ।।6.46.18।। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरमित्रघ्नस्ततापप्रवरेषुभिः ।
explanation: The slayer of enemies, Indrajith attacked Neela with nine shafts, so also Mainda and Dwivida with three separate sharpedged shafts.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तंमहेष्वासोविद् ध्वाबाणेनवक्षसि ।।6.46.19।। हनूमतोवेगवतोविससर्जशरान्दश ।
explanation: Indrajith endowed with great bow pierced Jambavan in his chest, and released ten arrows at Hanuman, endowed with speed in war.

shloka_text: गवाक्षंशरभंचैवद्वावप्यमिततेजसौ ।।6.46.20।। द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यांमहावेगोविव्याधयुधिरावणिः ।
explanation: Indrajith endowed with speed in war, attacked highly energetic Gavaksha and Sarabha with two arrows each.
