shloka_text: गोलाङ्गूलेश्वरंचैववालिपुत्रमथाङ्गदम् ।।6.46.21।। विव्याधबहुभिर्बाणैस्त्वरमाणोऽथरावणिः ।
explanation: Thereafter Indrajith attacked the ruler of Golangulas, and Vali's son Angada with many arrows.

shloka_text: तान्वानरवरान्भित्त्वाशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.46.22।। ननादबलवांस्तत्रमहासत्त्वस्सरावणिः ।
explanation: Mighty son of Ravana, then attacked the best of monkeys with arrows which were like flames of fire.

shloka_text: तानर्धयित्वाबाणौघैस्त्रासयित्वाचवानरान् ।।6.46.23।। प्रजहासमहाबाहुर्वचनंचेदमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Indrajith hurt the Vanaras with hails of arrows terrifying them. Then the mighty armed son of Ravana laughed and spoke these words.

shloka_text: शरशब्देनघोरेणमयाबद्धौचमूमुखे ।।6.46.24।। सहितौभ्रातरवेतौनिशामयतराक्षसाः ।
explanation: "O Rakshasas! Look at these two brothers together bound by my fierce arrows in front of you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्तुतेसर्वेराक्षसाःकूटयोधिनः ।।6.46.25।। परंविस्मयामाजग्मुःकर्मणातेनहर्षिताः ।
explanation: Indrajith having spoken in that way to the Rakshasas, all of them were highly amazed by the action of Indrajith and went laughing.

shloka_text: विनेदुश्चमहानादान् सर्वेतेजलदोपमाः ।।6.46.26।। हतोरामइतिज्ञात्वारावणिंसमपूजयन् ।
explanation: The Rakshasas thundering like rain clouds, roaring aloud thinking 'Rama is killed' by Ravana's son offered prayers.

shloka_text: निष्पन्दौतुतदादृष्टवाभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.46.27।। वसुधायांनिरुच्छवासौहतावित्यन्वमन्यत ।
explanation: Thereafter having seen the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana not responding or breathing, lying on the ground, he thought they were dead.

shloka_text: हर्षेणतुसमाविष्टइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.46.28।। प्रविवेशपुरींलङ्कांहर्षयन् सर्वनैर्वृतान् ।
explanation: Indrajith, who is victorious in battles, feeling happy and creating happiness to all Rakshasas collected there entered the city of Lanka.

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्टवाशरीरेसायकैश्चिते ।।6.46.29।। सर्वाणिचाङ्गोपाङ्गानिसुग्रीवंभयमाविशत् ।
explanation: Sugriva was overtaken by fear on seeing Rama and Lakshmana riddled with arrows from head to foot all over the body

shloka_text: पर्यवस्थापयात्मानमनाथंमांचवानर ।।6.46.33।। सत्यधर्माभिरक्तानांनास्तिमृत्युकृतंभयम् ।
explanation: "O Vanara! We are helpless, be confident, for those following righteousness and truthfulness there is no fear of death."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाततस्तस्यजलक्लन्नेनपाणिना ।।6.46.34।। सुग्रीवस्यशुभेनेत्रेप्रममार्जविभीषणः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana, having spoken in that manner, there after dipped his hand in water and wiped the beautiful eyes of Sugriva to brighten.

shloka_text: ततस्सलिलमादायविद्ययापरिजप्यच ।।6.46.35।। सुग्रीवनेत्रेधर्मात्मासममार्जविभीषणः ।
explanation: Thereafter the dutiful Vibheeshana taking water as per tradition consecrated chanting sacred text and wiped Sugriva's eyes.

shloka_text: विमृज्यवदनंतस्यकपिराजस्यधीमतः ।।6.46.36।। अब्रवीत्कालसम्प्राप्तसम्भ्रान्तमिदंवचः ।
explanation: Wise Vibheeshana having wiped Sugriva's face clean in accordance with time addressed with opportune words.

shloka_text: नकालःकपिराजेन्द्रवैक्लब्यमवलम्बितुम् ।।6.46.37।। अतिस्नेहोऽप्यकालेऽस्मिन्मरणायोपकल्पते ।
explanation: "O king of monkeys! This is not the time for faint heartedness. Extreme attachment at this time will lead us to death."

shloka_text: तस्मादुत्सृज्यवैक्लब्यंसर्वकार्यविनाशनम् ।।6.46.38।। हितंरामपुरोगणांसैन्यानानुचिन्त्यताम् ।
explanation: "Therefore, give up faintheartedness as all actions will be destroyed by that. Following Rama's leadership, think of the army's welfare."

shloka_text: अथवारक्ष्यतांरामोयावत्संज्ञाविपर्ययः ।।6.46.39।। लब्धसंज्ञौहिकाकुत्स्थौभयंनौव्यपनेष्यतः ।
explanation: "Or else till they become conscious, protect the Kakuthsa princes. When they become conscious, they can get rid of our fear."

shloka_text: नैतत्किञ्चनरामस्यनचरामोमुमूर्षति ।।6.46.40।। नह्येनंहास्यतेलक्ष्मीद्दुर्लभायागतायुषाम् ।
explanation: "Therefore, Rama has no fear of death, even a little. Whatever splendour is lost, prosperity will not leave him."

shloka_text: तस्मादाश्वासयात्मानंबलंचाश्वासयस्वकम् ।।6.46.41।। यावत्कार्याणिसर्वाणिपुनःसंस्थापयाम्यहम् ।
explanation: "Therefore, restoring breath let us reassure the army again till all actions are carried out by restoring their confidence."

shloka_text: एतेहिफुल्लनयनास्त्रासादागतसाध्वसाः ।।6.46.42।। कर्णेकर्णेप्रकथिताहरयोहरिसत्तम ।
explanation: "O Monkey leader! these monkeys whose eyes have become big (are dilated) with fear are talking ear to ear (about Rama)."

shloka_text: मांतुदृष्टवाप्रधावन्तमनीकंसम्प्रहर्षितुम् ।।6.46.43।। त्यजस्तुहरयस्त्रासंभुक्तपूर्वामिवस्रजम् ।
explanation: "Let the army forces of monkeys be happy seeing me moving, getting rid of the inherent fear in them just as they discard a garland of flowers enjoyed by them earlier."

shloka_text: समाश्वास्यतुसुग्रीवंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.46.44।। विद्रुतंवानरानीकंतत्समाश्वासयत्पुनः ।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, Vibheeshana having assured Sugriva, knowing the Vanara army he reassured them.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुमहामायःसर्वसैन्यसमावृतः ।।6.46.45।। विवेशनगरींलङ्कांपितरंचाभ्युपागमत् ।
explanation: Great Indrajith surrounded by all army entered the city of Lanka and approached his father.

shloka_text: तत्ररावणमासाद्यअभिवाद्यकृताञ्जलिः ।।6.46.46।। आचचक्षेप्रियंपित्रेनिहतौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: Having reached Ravana, Indrajith greeted him with folded palms and broke the pleasant news, "Rama and Lakshmana are killed."

shloka_text: उत्पपातततोहृष्टःपुत्रंचपरिषस्वजे ।।6.46.47।। रावणोरक्षसांमध्येश्रुत्वाशत्रूनिपातितौ ।
explanation: In the midst of Rakshasas, Ravana hearing the news of his enemies being killed, rejoiced, and got up from his couch and embraced his son.

shloka_text: उपाघ्रायचतंमूद् र्नेनंपप्रच्छप्रीतमानसः ।।6.46.48।। पृच्छतेचयथावृत्तंपित्रेतस्मैसर्वंन्यवेदयत् । यथातौशरबन्धेननिश्चेष्टौनिष्प्रभौकृतौ ।।6.46.49।।
explanation: Delighted Ravana kissed his son on the forehead and enquired of him of the details. Indrajith presented details saying that both Rama and Lakshmana were stunned in the network of arrows, and lost splendour.

shloka_text: उपाघ्रायचतंमूद् र्नेनंपप्रच्छप्रीतमानसः ।।6.46.48।। पृच्छतेचयथावृत्तंपित्रेतस्मैसर्वंन्यवेदयत् । यथातौशरबन्धेननिश्चेष्टौनिष्प्रभौकृतौ ।।6.46.49।।
explanation: Delighted Ravana kissed his son on the forehead and enquired of him of the details. Indrajith presented details saying that both Rama and Lakshmana were stunned in the network of arrows, and lost splendour.

shloka_text: सहर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्माश्रुत्वावचस्तस्यमहारथस्य । जहौज्वरंदाशरथेःसमुत्थितंप्रहृष्यवाचाऽभिननन्दपुत्रम् ।।6.46.50।।
explanation: Hearing the words of the great chariot warrior, Ravana was filled with excessive joy at heart. His fear and agony of Dasaratha's son having gone on hearing the words of his son, Ravana greeted him. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषटचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रतिप्रविष्टेलङ्कायांकृतार्थेरावणात्मजे । राघवंपरिवार्यार्तुरक्षुर्वानरर्षभाः ।।6.47.1।।
explanation: After accomplishing the task Ravana's son entered Lanka while the bull among monkeys guarded Raghava staying around.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: हनुमानङ्गदोनीलःसुषेणःकुमुदोनलः । गजोगवाक्षोगवयश्शरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.47.2।। जाम्बवानृषभःसुन्दोरम्भःशतवलिःपृथुः । व्यूढानीकाश्चयत्ताश्चद्रुमानादायसर्वतः ।।6.47.3।। वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वंचवानराः । तृणेष्वपिचचेष्टत्सुराक्षसाइतिमेनिरे ।।6.47.4।।
explanation: Having arranged the army in place, Hanuman, Angada, Nila, Kumuda, Nala, Gava, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Sanuprastha, Jambavan, Rshaba, Rambha, Satavali, Pruthu, who are always alert were holding trees and looking above, on either side and in all directions and guarded Rama. Whenever there was movement of even a blade of grass, they thought that it might be Rakshasa.

shloka_text: रावणश्चापिसम्हृष्टोविसृज्येन्द्रजितंसुतम् । अजुहावततस्सीताक्षिणीराक्षसीस्तदा ।।6.47.5।।
explanation: Ravana was also content to send away his son Indrajith and calls for the Rakshasa woman, caretaker of Sita.

shloka_text: राक्षस्यस्त्रिजटाचैवशासनात्समुपस्थिताः । ताउवाचततोहृष्टोराक्षसीराक्षसाधमः ।।6.47.6।।
explanation: The rakshasi and also Trijata came and waited there by the order. Lowly Rakshasa, Ravana, full of joy addressed rakshasi.

shloka_text: हताविन्द्रजिताख्यातवैदेह्यारामलक्ष्मणौ । पुष्पकंतत्समारोप्यदर्शयध्वंहतौरणे ।।6.47.7।।
explanation: "Rama and Lakshmana are killed by Indrajith in war. Take Vaidehi in the aerial car and show her."

shloka_text: यदाश्रयादवष्टब्धामामुपतिष्ठति । सोऽस्याभर्तासहभ्रात्रानिहतोरणमूर्धनि ।।6.47.8।।
explanation: "That husband with whose support she was proud and not yielding to me is unconscious along with his brother who have been killed," said Ravana.

shloka_text: निर्विशङ्कानिरुद्विग्नानिरपेक्षाचमैथिली । मामुपस्थास्यतेसीतासर्वाभरणभूषिता ।।6.47.9।।
explanation: "Mythili, rid of sorrow and free from perturbation, giving up hope (of Rama) can wait upon me adorned with all kinds of jewels."

shloka_text: अद्यकालवशंप्राप्तंरणेरामंसलक्ष्मणम् । अवेक्ष्यविनिवृत्तासाचान्यांगतिमपश्यती ।।6.47.10।। निरपेक्षाविशालाक्षीमामुपस्थास्यतेस्वयम् ।
explanation: Ravana thought that the broad eyed Sita coming to conclusion in course of time that Rama has gone along with Lakshmana, rid of hope, with no other haven, will seek him on her own accord.

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वारावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।।6.47.11।। राक्षस्यस्तास्तथेत्युक्त्वाजग्मुर्वैयत्रपुष्पकम् ।
explanation: The evil minded Rakshasas listening to Ravana's words went to the aerial car.

shloka_text: ततःपुष्पकमादायराक्षस्योरावणाज्ञया ।।6.47.12।। अशोकवनिकास्थांतांमैथिलींसमुपानयन् ।
explanation: Thereafter, by Ravana's order the Rakshasas went with the aerial car to Mythili in the Ashoka Garden.

shloka_text: तामादायतुराक्षस्योभर्तृशोकपराजिताम् ।।6.47.13।। सीतामारोपयामासुर्विमानंपुष्पकंतदा ।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas took the aerial car near Sita who was overcome by her husband's grief.

shloka_text: ततःपुष्पकमारोप्यसीतांत्रिजटयासह ।।6.47.14।। जग्मुर्दर्शयितुंतस्यैराक्षस्योरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: Thereafter the Rakshasas along with Trijata went to Sita and made her ascend Pushpaka to see Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: रावणोऽकारयल्लङ्कांपताकाध्वजमालिनीम् ।।6.47.15।। प्राघोषयतहृष्टश्चलङ्कायांराक्षसेश्वरः । राघवोलक्ष्मणश्चैवहताविन्द्रजितारणे ।।6.47.16।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas rejoiced and went to Lanka decorated with flags and posts proclaiming that Rama and Lakshmana were killed by Indrajith in war.

shloka_text: रावणोऽकारयल्लङ्कांपताकाध्वजमालिनीम् ।।6.47.15।। प्राघोषयतहृष्टश्चलङ्कायांराक्षसेश्वरः । राघवोलक्ष्मणश्चैवहताविन्द्रजितारणे ।।6.47.16।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas rejoiced and went to Lanka decorated with flags and posts proclaiming that Rama and Lakshmana were killed by Indrajith in war.

shloka_text: विमानेनापिगत्वातुसीतात्रिजटयासह । ददर्शवानराणांतुसर्वंसैन्यंनिपातितम् ।।6.47.17।।
explanation: Sita and Trijata flying on the Pushpaka saw all the fallen Vanara army.

shloka_text: प्रहृष्टमनसश्चापिददर्शपिशिताशनान् । वानरांश्चातिदुःखार्तान्रामलक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः ।।6.47.18।।
explanation: Sita beheld extremely happy Rakshasas, and grief stricken Vanaras, in great agony near Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ततस्सीताददर्शोभौशयानौशरतल्पगौ । लक्ष्मणंचापिरामंचविसंज्ञौशरपीडितौ ।।6.47.19।। विध्वस्तकवचौवीरौविप्रविद्धशरासनौ । सायकैचशिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरस्तम्बमयौक्षितौ ।।6.47.20।।
explanation: Thereafter Sita beheld both Rama and Lakshmana lying on the bed of arrows, unconscious, struck by arrows, with shields of darts, arrows with feathers, all limbs wounded with shattered armour, bows and reeds.

shloka_text: ततस्सीताददर्शोभौशयानौशरतल्पगौ । लक्ष्मणंचापिरामंचविसंज्ञौशरपीडितौ ।।6.47.19।। विध्वस्तकवचौवीरौविप्रविद्धशरासनौ । सायकैचशिन्नसर्वाङ्गौशरस्तम्बमयौक्षितौ ।।6.47.20।।
explanation: Thereafter Sita beheld both Rama and Lakshmana lying on the bed of arrows, unconscious, struck by arrows, with shields of darts, arrows with feathers, all limbs wounded with shattered armour, bows and reeds.

shloka_text: तौदृष्टवाभ्रातरौतत्रप्रवीरौपुरुषर्षभौ । शयानौपुण्डरीकाक्षौकुमाराविवपावकी ।।6.47.21।। शरतल्पगतौवीरौतथाभूतानरर्षभौ । दुःखार्ताकरुणंसीतासुभृशंविललापह ।।6.47.22।।
explanation: Seeing the gallant bulls among men, the two brothers with big eyes, the two heroes like sons of fire god lying on the bed of arrows in such a state, Sita was filled with intense sorrow and pity burst into tears being affected extremely.

shloka_text: तौदृष्टवाभ्रातरौतत्रप्रवीरौपुरुषर्षभौ । शयानौपुण्डरीकाक्षौकुमाराविवपावकी ।।6.47.21।। शरतल्पगतौवीरौतथाभूतानरर्षभौ । दुःखार्ताकरुणंसीतासुभृशंविललापह ।।6.47.22।।
explanation: Seeing the gallant bulls among men, the two brothers with big eyes, the two heroes like sons of fire god lying on the bed of arrows in such a state, Sita was filled with intense sorrow and pity burst into tears being affected extremely.

shloka_text: भर्तारमनवद्याङ्गीलक्ष्मणंचासितेक्षणा । प्रेक्ष्यपांसुषुचेष्टन्तौरुरोदजनकात्मजा ।।6.47.23।।
explanation: Janaka's daughter of beautiful limbs and dark eyes, seeing her husband and Lakshmana, both powerful ones rolling, roared aloud.

shloka_text: भर्तारंनिहतंदृष्टवालक्ष्मणंचमहाबलम् । विललापभृशंसीताकरुणंशोककर्शिता ।।6.48.1।।
explanation: On seeing her husband killed and also mighty Lakshmana, Sita became emotional in intense sorrow and cried piteously.

shloka_text: ऊचुर्लक्षणिकायेमांपुत्रिण्यविधवेतिच । तेऽद्यसर्वेहतेरामेज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः ।।6.48.2।।
explanation: "Whoever was capable of predicting the future have said that I will be the mother of sons and not become a widow. Now if Rama is dead, they become liars."

shloka_text: यज्वनोमहिषींयेमामूचुःपत्नींचसत्त्रिणः । तेऽद्यसर्वेहतेरामेज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः ।।6.48.3।।
explanation: "Whoever conducted sacrificial ceremonies and are knowledgeable of sastras have told me that I would be consort. They are all liars now as Rama is killed."

shloka_text: ऊचुस्संश्रवणेयेमांद्विजाःकार्तान्तिकाश्शुभाम् । तेऽद्यसर्वेहतेरामेज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः ।।6.48.4।।
explanation: "The astrologers, brahmins who have promised me to be auspicious and all the wise who have spoken are liars if Rama is killed."

shloka_text: वीरपार्थिवपत्नीत्वांयेविदुर्भर्तृपूजिताम् । तेऽद्यसर्वेहतेरामेज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः ।।6.48.5।।
explanation: "Whoever has told me that I will be the wife of a man of great prowess, worshipped by husband, and all wise men are liars if Rama is killed."

shloka_text: इमानिखलुपद्मानिपादयोर्यैःकुलस्त्रियः । अधिराज्येऽभिषिच्यन्तेनरेन्द्रैःपतिभिःसह ।।6.48.6।।
explanation: "Those virtuous lotus marks that a woman has on their feet to become crowned queen of a kingdom are seen in my feet."

shloka_text: वैधव्यंयान्तियैर्नार्योऽलक्षणैर्भाग्यदुर्लभाः । नात्मनन्तानिपश्यामिपश्यन्तीहतलक्षणा ।।6.48.7।।
explanation: "Those inauspicious signs found in unlucky and widowed women are difficult to find in me. I do not see any such signs in me."

shloka_text: सत्यनामानिपद्मानिस्त्रीणामुक्तानिलक्षणैः । तान्यद्यनिहतेरामेवितथानिभवन्तिमे ।।6.48.8।।
explanation: "Characteristic marks of lotuses, unfailing in their effect (truthful) predicted are all false if Rama is killed."

shloka_text: केशास्सूक्ष्मास्समानीलाभ्रुवौचासंहतेमम । वृत्तेचारोमकेजङ्घेदन्ताश्चाविरळामम ।।6.48.9।।
explanation: "My hair is fine and dark, my eyebrows are uniform and not joined, my shanks are round devoid of hair, and my teeth are closely set."

shloka_text: शङ्खेनेत्रेकरौपादौगुल्फावूरूचमेचितौ । अनुवृत्तनखास्स्निग्धास्समाश्चाङ्गुलयोमम ।।6.48.10।।
explanation: "My temporal bones, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, thighs are even, and my fingers are fleshy and round with nails proportioned and bright."

shloka_text: स्तनौचाविरळौमामकौमग्नचूचुकौ । मग्नाचोत्सङ्गिनीनाभःपार्श्वोरस्कंचमेचितम् ।।6.48.11।।
explanation: "My breasts are well formed and developed, the nipples are depressed and joined, the navel is deep, and the surrounding part is fleshy."

shloka_text: ममवर्णोमणिनिभोमृदून्यङ्गरुहाणिच । प्रतिष्ठितांद्वादशभिर्मामूचुश्शुभलक्षणाम् ।।6.48.12।।
explanation: "My complexion is like the shine of a gem. My hair on the skin is soft. When I touch the ground with my ten fingers and toes, it is said to leave auspicious marks."

shloka_text: समग्रयवमच्छ्रिद्रपाणिपादंचवर्णवत् । मन्दस्मितेत्येवचमांकन्यालाक्षणिनोद्विजाः ।।6.48.13।।
explanation: "My palms and feet placed together have no space which are auspicious marks and brahmins have said that my gentle smile is also a mark of auspiciousness."

shloka_text: आधिराज्येऽभिषेकोमेब्राह्मणैःपतिनासह । कृतान्तकुशलैरुक्तंतत्सर्वंवितथीकृतम् ।।6.48.14।।
explanation: "The prediction of astrologers that I will be consecrated with my husband and all that is falsified."

shloka_text: शोधयित्वाजनस्थानंप्रवृततिमुपलभ्यच । तीर्त्वासागरमक्षोभ्यंभ्रातरौगोष्पदेहतौ ।।6.48.15।।
explanation: "Having gained Janasthana and crossing the ocean which is impossible knowing about my whereabouts and getting me is impossible since the brothers have been killed by the maya of Indrajith whose footprints are like a cow's hoof."

shloka_text: ननुवारुणमाग्नेयमैन्द्रंवायव्यमेवच । अस्त्रंब्रह्मशिरश्चैवप्रत्यपद्यताम् ।।6.48.16।।
explanation: "Raghavas knew to use Varuna's weapons, fire god's weapons, Indra's also, even wind god's and Brahma's weapons. Why have they not used?"

shloka_text: अदृश्यमानेनरणेमाययावासवोपमौ । ममनाथावनाथायानिहतौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.48.17।।
explanation: "Indrajith remaining invisible in war by conjuring could kill my husband who is equal to Indra in valour. Rama and Lakshmana! I am orphaned now."

shloka_text: नहिदृष्टिपथंप्राप्यराघवस्यरणेरिपुः । जीवन्प्रन्तिवर्तेतयद्यपिस्यान्मनोजवः ।।6.48.18।।
explanation: "Even if the enemy is endowed with speed of thought, if he comes in the range of Rama's sight, he will not go alive."

shloka_text: नकलस्यातिभारोऽस्तिकृतान्तश्चसुदुर्जयः । यत्ररामःसहभ्रात्राशेतेयुधिनिपातितः ।।6.48.19।।
explanation: "Rama along with Lakshmana has fallen in the battlefield. Time spirit is too heavy and capable of doing anything, so difficult to conquer."

shloka_text: नशोचामितथारामंलक्ष्मणंचमहारथम् । वात्मानंजननींचापियथाश्वश्रूंतपस्विनीम् ।।6.48.20।।
explanation: "When I think of Rama or even great warrior Lakshmana, or my mother or myself I am not so sad as when I think of my motherinlaw who is an observer of austerity."

shloka_text: सातुचिन्तयतेनित्यंसमाप्तव्रतमागतम् । कदाद्रक्ष्यामिसीतांचलक्ष्मणंचसराघवम् ।।6.48.21।।
explanation: "She will also be worried and wait for Rama who has completed his vow (for fourteen years) and Lakshmana and Sita to come."

shloka_text: परिदेवयमानांतांराक्षसीत्रिजटाब्रवीत् । माविषादंकृथादेवी भर्ताऽयंतवजीवति ।।6.48.22।।
explanation: Looking at Sita, worried, Trijata said 'Devi, do not despair. Your husband is alive'.

shloka_text: कारणानिचवक्ष्यामिमहान्तिसदृशानिच । यथेमौजीवतोदेवीभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.48.23।।
explanation: "O Devi! Rama and Lakshmana are alive. I see great reasons for this."

shloka_text: नहिकोपपरीतानिहर्षपर्युत्सुकानिच । भवन्तियुधियोधानांमुखानिनिहतेपतौ ।।6.48.24।।
explanation: "If a husband ceases life in war, their face will not have an angry look or happy appearance."

shloka_text: इदंविमानंवैदेही पुष्पकंनामनामतः । दिव्यंत्वांदारयन्नैवंयद्येतौगतजीवितौ ।।6.48.25।।
explanation: "Vaidehi! Indeed, this aerial car called Pushpaka which is an auspicious one would not have brought you if they are ceased of life."

shloka_text: हतवीरप्रधानाहिगतोत्साहानिरुद्यमा । सेनाभ्रमतिसङ् ख्येषुहतकर्णेवनौर्जले ।।6.48.26।।
explanation: "The army chief killed, the interest of the troop lost, Pushpaka will move about without making an effort like the ship which lost the helmsman."

shloka_text: इयंपुनरसम्भ्रान्तानिरुद्विग्नातरस्विनी । सेनारक्षतिकाकुत्स्थौमयाप्रीत्यानिवेदितौ ।।6.48.27।।
explanation: "O Lady, given to austerities! These monkeys are guarding Kakuthsa as proclaimed by me lovingly. Do not be confused. They are safe."

shloka_text: सात्वंभवसुविस्रब्धाअनुमानैस्सुखोदयैः । अहतौपश्यकाकुत्स्थौस्नेहादेतद्ब्र्रवीमिते ।।6.48.28।।
explanation: "This army is not doubting, not perturbed also, that they are killed. They are guarding the Kakutsthas lovingly. I am telling you."

shloka_text: अनृतंनोक्तपूर्वंमेनचवक्ष्येकदाचन । चारित्रसुखशीलत्वात् प्रविष्टाअसिमनःमम ।।6.48.29।।
explanation: "I have not uttered untruth earlier nor shall I do now. Indeed, you have found entry into my mind being a woman of good disposition."

shloka_text: नेमौशक्यारणेजेतुंसेन्द्रैरपिसुरासुरैः । तादृशंदर्शनंदृष्टवामयाचावेदितंतव ।।6.48.30।।
explanation: "These two are not capable of being won in war even by gods or demons. On observation of the indications by me I am making you realize."

shloka_text: इदंचसुमहचचित्रंशरैःपश्यस्वमैथिलि । निस्संज्ञावप्युभावेतौनैवलक्ष्मीर्विमुञ्चति ।।6.48.31।।
explanation: "O Mythili! Even though both of them have fallen and unconscious under arrows their body splendour has not diminished. You may see."

shloka_text: प्रायेणगतसत्त्वानांपुरुषाणांगतायुषाम् । दृश्यमानेषुवक्त्रेषुपरंभवतिवैकृतम् ।।6.48.32।।
explanation: "Normally when we see men who have ceased life and stopped breathing their features are unappealing."

shloka_text: त्यजशोकंचमोहंचदुःखंचजनकात्मजे । रामलक्ष्मणयोरर्थेनाद्यशक्यमजीवितुम् ।।6.48.33।।
explanation: "O Janaka's daughter! You give up grief and delusion about Rama and Lakshmana. They are alive, no doubt."

shloka_text: शुत्वातुवचनंतस्याःसीतासुरसुतोपमा । कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेमामेवमस्त्वितिमैथिलि ।।6.48.34।।
explanation: Sita who was like deity, on hearing the words of consolation, spoken by Trijata, greeted Trijata with palms together.

shloka_text: विमानंपुष्पकंतत्तुसन्निवर्त्यमनोजवम् । दीनात्रिजटयासीतालङ्कामेवप्रवेशिता ।।6.48.35।।
explanation: Then Trijata took Sita in the Pushpaka chariot endowed with the speed of mind and entered Lanka.

shloka_text: ततस्त्रिजटयासार्थंपुष्पकादवरुह्यसा । अशोकवनिकामेवराक्षसीभिःप्रवेशिता ।।6.48.36।।
explanation: Thereafter Sita along with Trijata went to Pushpaka. Making Sita to get down, rakshasi also entered Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: प्रविश्यसीताबहुवृक्षषण्डांतांराक्षसेन्द्रस्यविहारभूमिम् । सम्प्रेक्ष्यसञ्चिन्त्यचराजपुत्रौपरंविषादंसमुपाजगाम ।।6.48.37।।
explanation: Having entered the Rakshasa's pleasure garden which had many trees, Sita gave way to intense sorrow having keenly observed the king's sons. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेअष्टचत्वारिंशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty eighth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: घोरेणशरबन्धेनबद्धौदशरथात्मजौ । निःश्वसन्तौयथानागौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ ।।6.49.1।। सर्वेतेवानरश्रेष्ठास्ससुग्रीवामहाबलाः । परिवार्यमहात्मानौतस्थुश्शोकपरिप्लुताः ।।6.49.2।।
explanation: Sugriva, the very powerful one and all the best of Vanaras stood immersed in sorrow surrounding the great sons of Dasaratha, who were lying on the ground bound by a network of arrows like serpents, sighing, bodies covered with blood.

shloka_text: घोरेणशरबन्धेनबद्धौदशरथात्मजौ । निःश्वसन्तौयथानागौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ ।।6.49.1।। सर्वेतेवानरश्रेष्ठास्ससुग्रीवामहाबलाः । परिवार्यमहात्मानौतस्थुश्शोकपरिप्लुताः ।।6.49.2।।
explanation: Sugriva, the very powerful one and all the best of Vanaras stood immersed in sorrow surrounding the great sons of Dasaratha, who were lying on the ground bound by a network of arrows like serpents, sighing, bodies covered with blood.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरामःप्रत्यबुध्यतवीर्यवान् । स्थिरत्वात्सत्त्वयोगाच्चशरैस्सन्दानितोऽपिसन् ।।6.49.3।।
explanation: In the meantime, Rama, although bound, being a man of fortitude established in spiritual discipline, returned to consciousness.

shloka_text: ततोदृष्टवासरुधिरंनिषण्णंगाढमर्पितम् । भ्रातरंदीनवदनंपर्यदेवयदातुरः ।।6.49.4।।
explanation: There after seeing the piteous countenance of his brother, bound, and injured, Rama lamented.

shloka_text: किंनुमेसीतयाकार्यंकिंकार्यंजीवितेनवा । शयानंयोऽद्यपश्यामिभ्रातरंयुधिनिर्जितम् ।।6.49.5।।
explanation: "Of what purpose is my life when I behold my brother lying lifeless in war? What do I have with Sita? Or even with my life?"

shloka_text: शक्यासीतासमानारीमर्त्यलोकेविचिन्वता । नलक्ष्मणसमोभ्रातासचिवस्साम्पपरायिकः ।।6.49.6।।
explanation: "In a mortal world I can look for a woman like Sita but not possible to find a helpful and capable brother."

shloka_text: परित्यक्षाम्यहंप्राणान्वानराणांतुपश्याताम् । यदिपञ्चत्वमापन्नस्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ।।6.49.7।।
explanation: "If Sumithra's dear son gets merged with the five elements, I will give up my life as the Vanaras are beholding."

shloka_text: किंनुवक्ष्यामिकौसल्यांमातरंकिंनुकैकयीम् । कथमम्बांसुमित्रांचपुत्रदर्शनलालसाम् ।।6.49.8।।
explanation: "What can I say to mother Kausalya, Kaikeyi and mother Sumithra waiting to see her son?"

shloka_text: विवत्सांवेपमानांचक्रोशन्तींकुररीमिव । कथमाश्वासयिष्यामियदियास्यामितंविना ।।6.49.9।।
explanation: "If I go to Ayodhya without him, how can I console Sumithra crying aloud like a female osprey?"

shloka_text: कथंवक्ष्यामिशत्रुघ्नंभरतंचयशस्विनम् । मयासहवनंयातोविनातेनापुनमागतः ।।6.49.10।।
explanation: "How can I return bereft of Lakshmana who went with me to the forest? What can I tell Satrughna, also the Bharata of great fame?"

shloka_text: उपालम्बंनशक्ष्यामिसोढुंबतसुमित्रया । इहैवदेहंत्यक्ष्यामिनहिजीवितुमुत्सहे ।।6.49.11।।
explanation: "If Sumithra asks me, I can't endure. I cannot bear it. I shall give up my body, my life here itself."

shloka_text: धिङ्मांदुष्कृतकर्माणमनार्यंमत्कृतेह्यसौ । लक्ष्मणःपतितश्शेतेशरतल्पेगतासुवत् ।।6.49.12।।
explanation: "What a pity! Me of sinful deeds and not a noble one, because of whose action Lakshmana's life having departed and lying on the bed of arrows."

shloka_text: त्वंनित्यंसुविषण्णंमामाश्वासयसिलक्ष्मण । गतासुर्नाद्यशक्तोऽसिमामार्तमभिभाषितुम् ।।6.49.13।।
explanation: "You were always comforting me when I was sad. Now however much I am grieved, ceased of life you cannot comfort me."

shloka_text: येनाद्यबहवोयुद्धेनिहताराक्षसाविनिपातिताः । तस्यामेवाद्यशूरस्त्वंशेषेविनिहतःपरैः ।।6.49.14।।
explanation: "You, who have struck down many Rakshasas in war, are lying unconscious on the same ground struck by arrows."

shloka_text: शयानःशरतल्पेऽस्मिन् सशोणितपरिप्लुतः । शरजालैचशितोभासिभास्करोऽस्तमिवव्रजन् ।।6.49.15।।
explanation: "Lying on the bed of arrows in the network of arrows, blood flowing out from the body he remains shining like the setting sun."

shloka_text: बाणाभिहतमर्मत्वान्नशक्नोत्यभिभाषितुम् । रुजाचाब्रुवतोऽप्यस्यदृष्टिरागेणसूच्यते ।।6.49.16।।
explanation: "Struck in the vital parts by the arrows, it is not possible for you to speak, but your anguish is indicated in your looks."

shloka_text: यथैवमांवनंयान्तमनुयातोमहाद्युतिः । अहमप्यनुयास्यामितथैवैनंयमक्ष्यम् ।।6.49.17।।
explanation: "This Lakshmana glowing in brightness, travelled with me following me in the forest. In the same way I shall follow him to the abode of death."

shloka_text: इष्टबन्धुजनोनित्यंमांचनित्यमनुव्रतः । इमामद्यगतोऽवस्थांममानार्यस्यदुर्नयैः ।।6.49.18।।
explanation: "He who was liked by relatives, was following ignoble me ever devoutly has reached this state."

shloka_text: सुरुष्टेनापिवीरेणलक्ष्मणेननसंस्मरे । परुषंविप्रियंवापिश्रावितंनकदाचन ।।6.49.19।।
explanation: "Indeed, heroic Lakshmana never uttered an unpalatable word. I do not remember him speaking harsh words even when he was deeply provoked."

shloka_text: विससर्जैकवेगेनपञ्चबाणशतानियः । इष्वस्त्रष्वधिकस्तस्मात्कार्तवीर्याच्चलक्ष्मणः ।।6.49.20।।
explanation: "He who, in one go released five hundred arrows (with two hand s) is therefore superior to Kartaveerya (with thousand hands) releasing the same arrows."

shloka_text: अस्स्रैरस्त्राणियोहन्याच्छक्रस्यापिमहात्मनः । सोऽयमुर्व्यांहतश्शेतेमहार्हशयनोचितः ।।6.49.21।।
explanation: "He, who could destroy Indra's arrows also deserves to be on Indra's bed, is lying on the ground, killed."

shloka_text: तच्चमिथ्याप्रलप्तंमांप्रधक्ष्यतिनसंशयः । यन्मयानकृतोराजाराक्षसानांविभीषणः ।।6.49.22।।
explanation: "I have not made Vibheeshana as the king of Rakshasas. Because of that untruth utterance they want to consume me, no doubt."

shloka_text: अस्मिन्मुहूर्तेसुग्रीव प्रतियातुमितोऽर्हसि । मत्वाहीनंराजन् रावणोऽभिद्रवेद्बली ।।6.49.23।।
explanation: "Sugriva! You return back from here now. Strong Ravana will chase you because of my not being here."

shloka_text: अङ्गदंतुपुरस्कत्यससैन्यस्सपरिच्छदम् । सागरंतरसुग्रीव नीलेनचनलेनच ।।6.49.24।।
explanation: "Sugriva! Return back from here along with the army keeping Angada in front, even Neela and Nala. Cross the ocean."

shloka_text: कृतंहनुमताकार्यंयदन्यैर्दुष्करंरणे । ऋक्षराजेनतुष्यामिगोलाङ्गूलाधिपेनच ।।6.49.25।।
explanation: "O King of Bears! King of Golangulas! Difficult action has been done by you and others in war. I am pleased with Hanumantha's action."

shloka_text: अङ्गदेनकृतंकर्ममैन्देनद्विविदेनच । युद्धंकेसरिणासङ् ख्येघोरंसम्पातिनाकृतम् ।।6.49.26।।
explanation: "Formidable war was done by Angada, Mainda, Dwivida, and by all the Vanaras, Kesari and Sampathi."

shloka_text: गवयेनगवाक्षेणशरभेणगजेनच । अन्यैश्चहरिभिर्युद्धंमदर्थेत्यक्तजीवितैः ।।6.49.27।।
explanation: "Gava, Gavaksha, Sarabha and others even Vanaras have done war sacrificing their lives for me."

shloka_text: नचातिक्रमितुंशक्यंदैवंसुग्रीव मानुषैः । यत्तुशक्यंवयस्येनसुहृदाचपरन्तप ।।6.49.28।। कृतंसुग्रीव तत्सर्वंभवताधर्मभीरुणा ।
explanation: "Sugriva! It is not possible for human beings to overcome God (destiny). O scorcher of enemies! Sugriva, my best friend, you have all done righteously that which is not possible."

shloka_text: मित्रकार्यंकृतमिदंभवद्भिर्वानरर्षभाः ।।6.49.29।। अनुज्ञातामयासर्वेयथेष्टंगन्तुमर्हथ ।
explanation: "O Bulls among Vanaras! All of you should go permitted by me. You have done friend's work. You may go where you wish to go. I permit said Rama."

shloka_text: शुश्रुवुस्तस्यतेसर्वेवानराःपरिदेवनम् ।।6.49.30।। वर्तयाञ्चक्रूरश्रूणिनेत्रैःकृष्णेतरेक्षणाः ।
explanation: All the Vanaras started shedding tears from their tawny eyes on listening to the lamentation of Rama.

shloka_text: ततस्सर्वाण्यनीकानिस्थापयित्वाविभीषणः ।।6.49.31।। आजगामगदापाणिस्त्वरितंयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Thereafter, Vibheeshana, settling all the army, hastened to reach Raghava with a mace.

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवात्वरितंयान्तंनीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् ।।6.49.32।। वानरादुद्रुवुस्सर्वेमन्यमानास्तुरावणिम् ।
explanation: Seeing Vibheeshana resembling a dark mountain, thinking him to be Indrajith, all the Vanaras ran from there. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकोनपञ्चाशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the forty ninth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथोवाचमहातेजाहरिराजोमहाबलः । किमियंव्यथितासेनामूढवातेवनौर्जले ।।6.50.1।।
explanation: Extremely brilliant and mighty Sugriva looking at the army of Vanaras said, "Why are you worried like a boat tossed by wind in water?"

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वावालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत् । नत्वंपश्यसिरामंचलक्ष्मणंचमहारथम् ।।6.50.2।। शरजालचितौवीरावुभौदशरथात्मजौ । शरतल्पेमहात्मानौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ ।।6.50.3।।
explanation: On hearing Sugriva's question, Angada the son of Vali said, "Did you not see Dasaratha's sons Rama and chariot warrior Lakshmana, the great souls lying on a bed of arrows bathed in blood?"

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वावालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत् । नत्वंपश्यसिरामंचलक्ष्मणंचमहारथम् ।।6.50.2।। शरजालचितौवीरावुभौदशरथात्मजौ । शरतल्पेमहात्मानौशयानौरुधिरोक्षितौ ।।6.50.3।।
explanation: On hearing Sugriva's question, Angada the son of Vali said, "Did you not see Dasaratha's sons Rama and chariot warrior Lakshmana, the great souls lying on a bed of arrows bathed in blood?"

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वानरेन्द्रस्सुग्रीवःपुत्रमङ्गदम् । नानिमित्तमिदंमन्येभवितव्यंभयेनतु ।।6.50.4।।
explanation: Then Vanara king Sugriva looking at Angada said, "I do not think that the Vanaras running like this is not without any cause. Maybe out of fear of some reason ahead."

shloka_text: विषण्णवदनाह्येतेत्यक्तप्रहरणादिशः । प्रपलायन्तिहरयस्त्रासादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः ।।6.50.5।।
explanation: "Here, the distressed Vanaras with sad faces, their eyes downcast, are fleeing in all directions abandoning their arms."

shloka_text: अन्योन्यस्यनलज्जन्तेनिरीक्षन्तिपृष्ठतः । विप्रकर्षन्तिचान्योन्यंपतितंलङ्घयन्तिच ।।6.50.6।।
explanation: "Without waiting to look back at others, not shy to see one another, the Vanaras are distancing themselves from those fallen and are seen fleeing."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेवीरोगदापाणिर्विभीषणः । सुग्रीवंवर्धयामासराघवंचनिरैक्षत ।।6.50.7।।
explanation: In the meantime, heroic Vibheeshana holding mace came to Sugriva and Rama and cheered with victory.

shloka_text: विभीषणंचसुग्रीवोदृष्टवावानरभीषणम् । ऋक्षराजंमहात्मानंसमीपस्थमुवाचह ।।6.50.8।।
explanation: Beholding Vibheeshana, the Vanaras fled, said Sugriva to the great Jambavan who stood near him.

shloka_text: विभीषणोऽयंसम्प्राप्तोयंदृष्टवावानरर्षभाः । विद्रवन्तिपरितत्रसरावणात्मजशङ्कया ।।6.50.9।।
explanation: "Vibheeshana has come here. Beholding him the foremost of the Vanaras fleeing suspecting him to be the son of Ravana."

shloka_text: शीघ्रमेतान् सुसन्त्रस्तान्बहुधाविप्रधावितान् । पर्यवस्थापयाख्याहिविभीषणमुपस्थितम् ।।6.50.10।।
explanation: "Call them back who are running in different directions quickly. Tell them Vibheeshana has come here."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तुजाम्बवानृक्षपार्थिवः । वानरान्सान्त्वयामाससन्निरुध्यप्रधानतः ।।6.50.11।।
explanation: Sugriva having spoken in that way, the king of Bears, Jambavan restored the confidence of Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेनिवृत्ताःपुनःसर्वेवानरास्त्यक्तसम्भ्रमाः । ऋक्षराजवचश्श्रुत्वातंचदृष्टवाविभीषणम् ।।6.50.12।।
explanation: Having heard Jambavan, all the Vanaras finally shed their fear and returned to see Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तुरामस्यदृष्टवागात्रंशरैश्चितम् । लक्ष्मणस्यचधर्मात्माबभूवव्यथितस्तदा ।।6.50.13।।
explanation: On seeing the body of Rama and Lakshmana fully covered by arrows, Vibheeshana also became piteous and sad.

shloka_text: जलक्लिन्नेनहस्तेनतयोर्नेत्रेप्रमृज्यच । शोकसम्पीडितमनारुरोदविललापच ।।6.50.14।।
explanation: Vibheeshana, wetting his hands with water cleaned the eyes of Rama and Lakshmana. Tormented with pain he cried aloud.

shloka_text: इमौतौसत्त्वसम्पन्नौविक्रान्तौप्रियसम्युगौ । इमामवस्थांगमितौराक्षसैःकूटयोधिभिः ।।6.50.15।।
explanation: "Both the princess, who are endowed with good nature, and power are fond of combat. The Rakshasas have reduced them to this state by their deceitful ways."

shloka_text: भ्रातुःपुत्रेणमेतेनदुष्पुत्रेणदुरात्मना । राक्षस्याजिह्मयाबुध्याचालितावृजुविक्रमौ ।।6.50.16।।
explanation: "The princess who were guileless in their prowess were cheated by my evil minded and stupid son of my brother by his crooked thinking and cheating."

shloka_text: शरैरिमावलंविद्धौरुधिरेणसमुक्षितौ । वसुधायामिमौसुप्तौदृश्येतेशल्यकाविव ।।6.50.17।।
explanation: "Pierced with arrows, fully covered with blood, the bodies of the two princes appear like porcupines sleeping on the ground."

shloka_text: ययोर्वीर्यमुपाश्रित्यप्रतिष्ठाकाङ्क्षितामया । तावुभौदेहनाशायप्रसुप्तौपुरुषर्षभौ ।।6.50.18।।
explanation: "These two bulls among men of great valour and fame whose refuge was sought by me are lying asleep wounded all over and limbs broken."

shloka_text: जीवन्नद्यविपन्नोऽस्मिनष्टराज्यमनोरथः । प्राप्तप्रतिज्ञश्चरिपुःसकामोरावणःकृतः ।।6.50.19।।
explanation: "Having lost my life ambition for the kingdom, frustrated I am. My enemy Ravana, having succeeded in his vow, did this deed."

shloka_text: एवंविलपमानंतंपरिष्वज्यविभीषणम् । सुग्रीवःसत्त्वसम्पन्नोहरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम् ।।6.50.20।।
explanation: To Vibheeshana who was lamenting in that way, Sugriva, who was endowed with good qualities embraced him and spoke.

shloka_text: राज्यंप्राप्स्यसिधर्मज्ञ लङ्कायांनात्रसंशयः । रावणस्सहपुत्रेणस्वकामंनेहलप्स्यते ।।6.50.21।।
explanation: "O righteous one! there is no doubt that you will attain the kingdom of Lanka. Ravana and his sons will not attain what they desire."

shloka_text: नरुजापीडितावेतावुभौराघवलक्ष्मणौ । त्यक्त्वामोहंवधिष्येतेसगणंरावणंरणे ।।6.50.22।।
explanation: "Both these heroes Raghava and Lakshmana wounded and pained having shaken off from their unconscious state will kill Ravana and his army in war."

shloka_text: तमेवंसान्त्वयित्वातुसमाश्वास्यचराक्षसम् । सुषेणंश्वशुरंपार्श्वेसुग्रीवस्तमुवाचह ।।6.50.23।।
explanation: Thus, consoling and pacifying, the Rakshasa, Vibheeshana in that manner, Sugriva turned to his uncle Sushena and spoke.

shloka_text: सहशूरैर्हरिगणैर्लब्धसंज्ञावरिन्दमौ । गच्छत्वंभ्रातरंगृह्यकिष्किन्धांरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.50.24।।
explanation: "On regaining consciousness, take the brothers Rama and Lakshmana, the tamers of enemies to Kishkinda accompanied by the heroic monkey army."

shloka_text: अहंतुरावणंहत्वासपुत्रंसहबान्धवम् । मैथिलीमानयिष्यामिशक्रोनष्टामिवश्रियम् ।।6.50.25।।
explanation: "On killing Ravana and his sons along with his kin, I will on my part also bring Mythili just as Indra recovered his prosperity."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैतद्वानरेन्द्रस्यसुषेणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् । दैवासुरंमहद्युद्धमनुभूतंसुदारुणम् ।।6.50.26।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Vanara Lord, Sushena spoke about the fierce and great war that he had experienced between Devas and asuras.

shloka_text: तदास्मदानवाशरसम्स्पर्शकोविदाः । निजघ्नुश्शस्त्रविदुषश्चादयन्तोमुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.50.27।।
explanation: "Then the Rakshasas adept in using arms went about agitating concealing themselves, attacking Devatas who were learned in using arms."

shloka_text: तानार्तान्नष्टसंज्ञांश्चगतासूंश्चबृहस्पतिः । विद्याभिर्मन्त्रयुक्ताभिरोषधीभिश्चिकित्सति ।।6.50.28।।
explanation: "Brhaspati, the priest restored the wounded and lifeless, unconscious by means of reciting mantras, prayers and treatment by herbs."

shloka_text: तान्यौषधान्यानयितुंक्षीरोदंयान्तुसागरम् । जवेनवानराःशीघ्रंसम्पातिपनसादयः ।।6.50.29।।
explanation: "Let Sampati and Panasa go quickly to the milky ocean in a swift phase to get those medicines."

shloka_text: हरयस्तुविजानन्तिपार्वतीस्तामहौषधीः । सञ्जीवकरणींदिव्यांविशल्यांदेवनिर्मिताम् ।।6.50.30।।
explanation: "Those monkeys only know the supreme medicine available in the mountains. They have to get Sanjeevakarani and Visalyakarani known to Brahma."

shloka_text: चन्द्रश्चनामद्रोणश्चक्षीरोदेसागरोत्तमे । अमृतंयत्रमथितंतत्रतेपरमौषधी ।।6.50.31।।
explanation: "There, where the milky ocean, the foremost of oceans, was churned, two mountains have risen by the name Chandra and Drona. The supreme herbs of medicine are present there."

shloka_text: तौतत्रविहितेदेवैःपर्वतौमहोदधौ । अयंवायुसुतोराजन् हनूमांस्तत्रगच्छतु ।।6.50.32।।
explanation: "Both the mountains are well known. Deities have kept the herbal medicine there. Let the son of wind god, Hanuman proceed."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेवायुर्मेगांश्चापिसविद्युतः । पर्यस्यसागरेतोयंकम्पयननिवमेदिनीम् ।।6.50.33।।
explanation: In the mean while winds blew, clouds also rose up, water in the ocean was scattered about by the wind and lightning appeared in the sky.

shloka_text: महतापक्षवातेनसर्ववदीपमहाद्रुमाः । निपेतुर्भग्नविटपाःसलिलेलवणाम्भसि ।।6.50.34।।
explanation: All the huge trees of the island were broken by the flutter of the wings (of Garuda) and fell into the salt water of the ocean.

shloka_text: अभवन् पन्नगास्त्रस्ताभोगिनस्तत्रवासिनः । शीघ्रंसर्वाणियादांसिजग्मुश्चलवणार्णवम् ।।6.50.35।।
explanation: All the serpents and sea monsters inhabiting there terrified at Garuda went quickly into the salty waters of the ocean.

shloka_text: ततोमुहूर्तार्गरुडंवैनतेयंमहाबलम् । वानराददृशुःसर्वेज्वलन्तमिवपावकम् ।।6.50.36।।
explanation: Then all the Vanaras perceived Garuda endowed with mighty prowess, the son of Vinatha blazing like fire.

shloka_text: तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्यनागास्तेसम्प्रदुद्रुवुः । यैस्तौसत्पुरुषौबद्धौशरभूतैर्महाबलौ ।।6.50.37।।
explanation: Seeing the noble Rama and Lakshmana bound by the serpents in the form of arrows (released by Indrajith), the serpents fled.

shloka_text: ततस्सुपर्णःकाकुत्स्थौस्पृष्टवाप्रत्यभिनदनितः । विममर्शचपाणिभ्यांमुखेचन्द्रसमप्रभे ।।6.50.38।।
explanation: Thereafter Garuda paying his respects to the noble Rama and Lakshmana, touching their feet, wiped their face which shone like the moon.

shloka_text: वैनतेयेनसम्स्पृष्टास्तयोःसम्रुरुहुर्व्रणाः । सुवर्णेचतनूस्निग्धेतयोराशुबभूवतुः ।।6.50.39।।
explanation: Caressed by Garuda, both their bodies were cleared of wounds instantly shone like gold and turned bright.

shloka_text: तेजोवीर्यंबलंचौजउत्साहश्चमहागुणाः । प्रदर्शनंचबुद्धिश्चस्मृतिश्चद्विगुणंतयोः ।।6.50.40।।
explanation: Their brilliance, prowess, daring courage, intelligence, memory, and great qualities got manifested many folds.

shloka_text: तावुत्थाप्यमहातेजागरुडोवासवोपमौ । उभौतौसस्वजेहृष्टोरामश्चैनमुवाचह ।।6.50.41।।
explanation: Raising up both the princes who were extraordinarily brilliant and equalled Indra, Garuda embraced Rama joyfully and thus spoke.

shloka_text: भवत्प्रसादाद् व्यसनंरावणिप्रभवंमहत् । आवामिहव्यतिक्रान्तौपूर्ववद् बलिनौकृतौ ।।6.50.42।।
explanation: "By your kindness, we have overcome this calamity caused by Ravana's son and regained our strength as before."

shloka_text: यथातातंदशरथंयथाऽजंचपितामहम् । तथाभवन्तमासाद्यहृदयंमेप्रसीदति ।।6.50.43।।
explanation: "For me to meet you is like meeting my father Dasaratha and grandfather, Aja. My heart rejoices."

shloka_text: कोभवान्रूपसम्पन्नोदिव्यस्रगनुलेपनः । वसानोविरजेवस्त्रदिव्याभरणभूषितः ।।6.50.44।।
explanation: "Who are you, richly endowed with charming appearance, smeared with unguents adored in dust free garments, wearing beautiful ornaments?"

shloka_text: तमुवाचमहातेजावैनतेयोमहाबलः । पतत्त्रिराजःप्रीतात्माहर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणः ।।6.50.45।।
explanation: To Rama whose eyes were filled with joyful tears, Vinatha, the king of birds, full of brightness and strength said.

shloka_text: अहंसखातेकाकुत्स्थ प्रियःप्राणोबहिश्चरः । गरुत्मानिहसम्प्राप्तोयुवयोःसाह्यकारणात् ।।6.50.46।।
explanation: "O Kakuthsa! I am Garuthman, your dear friend and your outer breath. I reached here to help you."

shloka_text: असुरावामहावीर्यावानरावामहाबलाः । सुराश्चापिसगन्ध्वर्वाःपुरस्कृत्यशतक्रतुम् ।।6.50.47।। नेमंमोक्षयितुंशक्ताश्शरबन्धंसुदारुणम् । मायाबलादिन्द्रजितानिर्मितंक्रूरकर्मणा ।।6.50.48।।
explanation: "For the demons endowed with great strength and of mighty valour or for Gandharvas, or Vanaras or for even Devatas, or Indra who has done a hundred sacrifices, it is not possible to get relieved from bondage of the arrows of Indrajith of cruel deeds carried out by tricks."

shloka_text: असुरावामहावीर्यावानरावामहाबलाः । सुराश्चापिसगन्ध्वर्वाःपुरस्कृत्यशतक्रतुम् ।।6.50.47।। नेमंमोक्षयितुंशक्ताश्शरबन्धंसुदारुणम् । मायाबलादिन्द्रजितानिर्मितंक्रूरकर्मणा ।।6.50.48।।
explanation: "For the demons endowed with great strength and of mighty valour or for Gandharvas, or Vanaras or for even Devatas, or Indra who has done a hundred sacrifices, it is not possible to get relieved from bondage of the arrows of Indrajith of cruel deeds carried out by tricks."

shloka_text: एतेनागाःकाद्रवेयास्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्राविषोल्बणाः । रक्षोमायाप्रभावेणशराभूत्वास्त्वदाश्रिताः ।।6.50.49।।
explanation: "These arrows are serpents born of Kadra Devata. They have sharp fangs and are highly poisonous. By the tricks of Rakshasa, it has turned into arrows and reached you."

shloka_text: सभाग्यश्चासिधर्मज्ञ राम सत्यपराक्रम । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्रासमरेरिपुघातिना ।।6.50.50।।
explanation: "You are lucky and also Lakshmana your brother, destroyer of foes in war. Rama your strength is truth, and you are righteous."

shloka_text: इमंश्रुत्वातुवृत्तान्तंत्वरमाणोऽहमागतः । सहसायुवयोःस्नेहात्सखित्वमनुपालयन् ।।6.50.51।।
explanation: "Having heard the information about both of you bound by serpents, out of my friendship and affection and in obedience to you I hastened and reached here."

shloka_text: मोक्षितौचमहाघोरादस्मात्सायकबन्धनात् । अप्रमादश्चकर्तव्योयुवाभ्यांनित्यमेवच ।।6.50.52।।
explanation: "Considering it as my duty to relieve you both from the frightful bondage of snakes I reached. Do not be inattentive and guileless."

shloka_text: प्रकृत्याराक्षसाःसर्वेसङ्ग्रामेकूटयोधिनः । शूराणांशुद्धभावानांभवतामरार्जवंबलम् ।।6.50.53।।
explanation: "Rakshasas by nature use tricks in war. For noble people with good nature guilelessness is strength."

shloka_text: तन्नविश्वसनीयंवोराक्षसानांरणाजिरे । एतेनैवोपमानेननित्यंजिह्माहिराक्षसाः ।।6.50.54।।
explanation: "Being so you should not trust Rakshasas. By this experience you know that Rakshasas are crooked."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातदारामंसुपर्णस्सुमहाबलः । परिष्वज्यचसुहृत्स्निग्धमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे ।।6.50.55।।
explanation: Having said so, Suparna endowed with mighty strength embraced Rama most affectionately and took leave of him.

shloka_text: सखे राघव धर्मज्ञ रिपूणामपिवत्सल । अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामिगमिष्यामियथामतम् ।।6.50.56।।
explanation: "My dear friend! I wish to take leave of you. Truly you are knower of what is right, and you are dear even to an enemy."

shloka_text: नचकौतूहलंकार्यंसखित्वंप्रतिराघव । कृतकर्मारणेवीर सखित्वंप्रतिवेत्स्यसि ।।6.50.57।।
explanation: "Heroic Rama! No question about your curiosity about our friendship now. After winning the war you will recognize."

shloka_text: बालवृद्धावशेषांतुकृत्वालङ्कांशरोर्मिभिः । रावणंचरिपुंहत्वासीतांत्वंसमुलप्स्यते ।।6.50.58।।
explanation: "Lanka will be left with youngsters and the aged with your arrows. The enemy Ravana killed, you will recover Sita."

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वावचनंसुपर्णश्शीघ्रविक्रमः । रामंचविरुजंकृत्वामध्येतेषांवनौकसाम् ।।6.5.59।। प्रदक्षिणंततःकृत्वापरिष्वज्यचवीर्यवान् । जगामाकाशमाविश्यसुपर्णःपवनोयथा ।।6.50.60।।
explanation: Having spoken to Rama in that manner, Suparna endowed with wind speed in flight embraced Rama and went around him as a mark of reverence and soared into the sky.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वावचनंसुपर्णश्शीघ्रविक्रमः । रामंचविरुजंकृत्वामध्येतेषांवनौकसाम् ।।6.5.59।। प्रदक्षिणंततःकृत्वापरिष्वज्यचवीर्यवान् । जगामाकाशमाविश्यसुपर्णःपवनोयथा ।।6.50.60।।
explanation: Having spoken to Rama in that manner, Suparna endowed with wind speed in flight embraced Rama and went around him as a mark of reverence and soared into the sky.

shloka_text: विरुजौराघवौदृष्टवाततोवानरयूथपाः । सिंहनादांस्तदानेदुर्लङ्गूलंन्दुधुवुस्तदा ।।6.50.61।।
explanation: Thereafter the Vanara troops, seeing the Raghavas freed from anguish, roared like a lion, and lashed their tails.

shloka_text: ततोभेरीस्समाजघ्नुर्मृदङ्गांश्चाप्यनादयन् । दध्मुश्शङ्खान्सम्प्रहृष्टाःक्षेवलन्त्यपियथापुरम् ।।6.50.62।।
explanation: Then the Vanaras played drums and even mridangams, blew conches and started jumping and leaping as before.

shloka_text: आस्फोट्याःस्पोट्यविक्रान्ताःवानराःनगयोधिनः । द्रुमानुत्पट्यविविधांस्तस्थुश्शतसहस्रशः ।।6.50.63।।
explanation: The Vanaras who can fight with trees, uprooted several trees expressing their capacity distinctly and breaking them, and cracking their fingers. Making loud noise in hundreds and thousands stood there.

shloka_text: विसृजन्तोमहानादांस्त्रासयन्तोनिशाचरान् । लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुर्युद्धकामाःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.50.64।।
explanation: Making a lot of noise, the Vanaras reached the gates of Lanka frightening night rangers and desiring to wage war.

shloka_text: तेषांसुखीमस्तुमुलोनिनादोबभूवशाखामृगयूथपानाम् । क्षयेनिदाघस्ययथाघनानांनादस्सुभीमोनदतांनिशीथे ।।6.50.65।।
explanation: Thundering sounds resembling heavy clouds making terrific sounds arose, as if universal destruction was taking place at midnight. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेपञ्चाशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fiftieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेषांसुतुमुलंशब्दंवानराणांतरस्विनाम् । नर्दतांराक्षसैस्सार्धंतदाशुश्रावरावणः ।।6.51.1।।
explanation: Then Ravana and all the Rakshasas heard the increasing and highly tumultuous sound made by the courageous Vanaras.

shloka_text: स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषंश्रुत्वासनिनदंभृशम् । सचिवानांततस्तेषांमध्येवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.51.2।।
explanation: Thereafter, hearing the loud and deep sounds of roaring and seeing his (Ravana's) ministers in the midst, he spoke as follows.

shloka_text: यथाऽसौसम्प्रहृष्टानांवानराणांसमुत्थितः । बहूनांसुमहान्नादोमेघनामिवगर्जिताम् ।।6.51.3।। व्यक्तंसुमहतीप्रीतिरेतेषांनात्रसंशयः । तथाहिविपुलैर्नादैश्चुक्षुभेवरुणालयः ।।6.51.4।।
explanation: "Many Vanaras have collected together and roared making loud noises just as thunder rumbling clouds. By that there is no doubt that they are very happy. For that reason, even the wide ocean is agitated."

shloka_text: यथाऽसौसम्प्रहृष्टानांवानराणांसमुत्थितः । बहूनांसुमहान्नादोमेघनामिवगर्जिताम् ।।6.51.3।। व्यक्तंसुमहतीप्रीतिरेतेषांनात्रसंशयः । तथाहिविपुलैर्नादैश्चुक्षुभेवरुणालयः ।।6.51.4।।
explanation: "Many Vanaras have collected together and roared making loud noises just as thunder rumbling clouds. By that there is no doubt that they are very happy. For that reason, even the wide ocean is agitated."

shloka_text: तौतुबद्धौशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । अयंचसुमहान्नादशङ्कांजनयतीवमे ।।6.51.5।।
explanation: "The two brothers Rama and Lakshmana are bound by sharp arrows. By the loud noise that I hear I doubt in my mind!"

shloka_text: एतत्तुवचनंचोक्त्वामन्त्रिणोराक्षसेश्वरः । उवाचनैरृतांस्तत्रसमीपपरिवर्तिनः ।।6.51.6।।
explanation: Having spoken like that to the ministers, the Lord of Rakshasas said to the Rakshasas who stood waiting close by.

shloka_text: ज्ञायतांतूर्णमेतेषांसर्वेषांचवनचारिणाम् । शोककालेसमुत्पन्नहर्षकारणमुत्थितम् ।।6.51.7।।
explanation: "For what reason are the Vanaras (rangers of woods) rejoicing that way in the time of grief? It may be found out speedily."

shloka_text: तथोक्तास्तेनसम्भ्रान्ताःप्राकारमधिरुह्यच । ददृशुःपालितांसेनांसुग्रीवेणमहात्मना ।।6.51.8।। तौचमुक्तौसुघोरेणशरबन्धेनराघवौ । समुत्थितौमहाभागौविषेदुःप्रेक्ष्यराक्षसाः ।।6.51.9।।
explanation: Ravana having said so, the bewildered Rakshasas scaling the boundary wall beheld the army protected by great Sugriva and the prosperous Raghavas relieved from arrows and happy, he became worried.

shloka_text: तथोक्तास्तेनसम्भ्रान्ताःप्राकारमधिरुह्यच । ददृशुःपालितांसेनांसुग्रीवेणमहात्मना ।।6.51.8।। तौचमुक्तौसुघोरेणशरबन्धेनराघवौ । समुत्थितौमहाभागौविषेदुःप्रेक्ष्यराक्षसाः ।।6.51.9।।
explanation: Ravana having said so, the bewildered Rakshasas scaling the boundary wall beheld the army protected by great Sugriva and the prosperous Raghavas relieved from arrows and happy, he became worried.

shloka_text: सन्त्रस्तहृदयाःसर्वेप्राकारात् वरुह्यते । विषण्णवदनाघोराराक्षसेन्द्रमुपस्थिता ।।6.51.10।।
explanation: All the dreadful Rakshasas getting down the boundary wall with pale faces, sad countenance reached the Lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तदप्रियंदीनमुखारावणस्यनिशाचराः । कृत्स्नंनिवेदयामासुर्यथावद्वाक्यकोविदाः ।।6.51.11।।
explanation: Rakshasas who were well versed in talking, desperately conveyed the unpleasantness as it is to Ravana.

shloka_text: यौताविन्द्रजितायुद्धेभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । निबद्धौशरबन्धेननिष्प्रकम्पभुजौकृतौ ।।6.51.12।। विमुक्तौशरबन्धेनदृश्येतेतौरणाजिरे । पाशानिवगजौछित्वागजेन्द्रसमविक्रमौ ।।6.51.13।।
explanation: "The two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, who are like powerful elephants have been set free from the bondage of arrows of Indrajith in the battlefield. Their shoulders are relieved and are like elephants snapped off the rope binding them."

shloka_text: यौताविन्द्रजितायुद्धेभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । निबद्धौशरबन्धेननिष्प्रकम्पभुजौकृतौ ।।6.51.12।। विमुक्तौशरबन्धेनदृश्येतेतौरणाजिरे । पाशानिवगजौछित्वागजेन्द्रसमविक्रमौ ।।6.51.13।।
explanation: "The two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, who are like powerful elephants have been set free from the bondage of arrows of Indrajith in the battlefield. Their shoulders are relieved and are like elephants snapped off the rope binding them."

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वावचनंतेषांराक्षसेन्द्रोमहाबलः । चिन्तारोषसमाक्रान्तोविषण्णवदनोऽभवत् ।।6.51.14।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king endowed with mighty prowess became pale in face, worried and enraged on hearing the words of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्भद्धौशरैराशीविषोपमैः । अमोघैस्सूर्यसङ्काशैःप्रमथ्येन्द्रजितायुधि ।।6.51.15।। तदस्त्रबन्धमासाद्ययदिमुक्तौरिपूमम । संशयस्थमिदंसर्वमनुपश्याम्यहंबलम् ।।6.51.16।।
explanation: "My enemies who are bound by the formidable and unfailing, sharp, poisonous and bright arrows like the sun of Indrajith blessed with boons, are liberated from the bondage! I doubt if my army is in danger!"

shloka_text: घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्भद्धौशरैराशीविषोपमैः । अमोघैस्सूर्यसङ्काशैःप्रमथ्येन्द्रजितायुधि ।।6.51.15।। तदस्त्रबन्धमासाद्ययदिमुक्तौरिपूमम । संशयस्थमिदंसर्वमनुपश्याम्यहंबलम् ।।6.51.16।।
explanation: "My enemies who are bound by the formidable and unfailing, sharp, poisonous and bright arrows like the sun of Indrajith blessed with boons, are liberated from the bondage! I doubt if my army is in danger!"

shloka_text: निष्फलाःखलुसम्वृत्ताश्शराःवासुकितेजसः । अदत्तंयैस्तुसङ्ग्रामेरिपूणांजीवितंमम ।।6.51.17।।
explanation: "My arrows which are equal in brilliance to Vasuki by which my enemies' life was taken away has become in fructuous now."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुसङ्क्रुद्धोनिश्श्वसन्नुरगोयथा । अब्रवीद्रक्षसांमध्येधूम्राक्षंनामराक्षसम् ।।6.51.18।।
explanation: Having said so, hissing Ravana called Dhumraksha to the midst.

shloka_text: बलेनमहतायुक्तोराक्षसैर्भीमविक्रमः । त्वंवधायाभिनिर्याहिरामस्यसहवानरैः ।।6.51.19।।
explanation: "Dhumraksha of fierce prowess, you along with a huge Rakshasa army go just now to destroy Rama along with able Vanaras."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुधूम्राक्षोराक्षसेन्द्रेणधीमता । कृत्वाप्रणामंसम्हृष्टोनिर्जगामनृपालयत् ।।6.51.20।।
explanation: Commanded by the Intelligent king of Rakshasas in that manner, Dhumraksha offered prayers and went from there joyfully.

shloka_text: अभिनिष्क्रम्यतदद्वारंबलाध्यक्षमुवाचह । त्वरयस्वबलंतूर्णंकिंचिरेणयुयुत्सतः ।।6.51.21।।
explanation: There after Dhumraksha went from the gateway and said to the CommanderinChief of the army" Get ready immediately and start quickly. Why delay?"

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षवचनंश्रुत्वाबलाध्यक्षोबलानुगः । बलमुद्योजयामासरावणस्याज्ञयाद्रुतम् ।।6.51.22।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Dhumraksha, the CommanderinChief of the large army, he got ready quickly by the order of Ravana.

shloka_text: तेबद्धघण्टाबलिनोघोररूपानिशाचराः । विगर्जमानास्सम्हृष्टाधूम्राक्षंपर्यवारयन् ।।6.51.23।।
explanation: Mighty army bound with girdles of bells to their waist, of fierce form roaring surrounded Dhumraksha joyfully.

shloka_text: विविधायुधहस्ताश्चशूलमुद्गरपाणयः । गदाभिःपट्टसैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैर्भृशम् ।।6.51.24।। परिघैर्भिण्डिवालैश्चभल्लैप्रासै: परश्वथै: । निर्ययूराक्षसादिभ्योनर्धन्तोजलदायथा ।।6.51.25।।
explanation: The dreadful Rakshasas set out roaring like rain clouds armed with different kinds of weapons, like tridents, darts, maces, spears, iron bars, rods, even clubs, spears and slings, arrows in thousands.

shloka_text: विविधायुधहस्ताश्चशूलमुद्गरपाणयः । गदाभिःपट्टसैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैर्भृशम् ।।6.51.24।। परिघैर्भिण्डिवालैश्चभल्लैप्रासै: परश्वथै: । निर्ययूराक्षसादिभ्योनर्धन्तोजलदायथा ।।6.51.25।।
explanation: The dreadful Rakshasas set out roaring like rain clouds armed with different kinds of weapons, like tridents, darts, maces, spears, iron bars, rods, even clubs, spears and slings, arrows in thousands.

shloka_text: रथैःकवचिनस्त्वन्येध्वजैश्चसमलङ्कृतैः । सुवर्णजालविहितैःखरैश्चविविधाननैः ।।6.51.26।। हयैःपरमशीघ्रैश्चगजैश्चैवमदोत्कटैः । निर्ययुर्नैरृतव्याघ्राव्याघ्राइवदुरासदाः ।।6.51.27।।
explanation: And others collected together holding shields, fearless like tigers, frightful in appearance, mounted on fast horses, chariots yoked to donkeys of different kinds covered with gold mesh, on maddened elephants Set out.

shloka_text: रथैःकवचिनस्त्वन्येध्वजैश्चसमलङ्कृतैः । सुवर्णजालविहितैःखरैश्चविविधाननैः ।।6.51.26।। हयैःपरमशीघ्रैश्चगजैश्चैवमदोत्कटैः । निर्ययुर्नैरृतव्याघ्राव्याघ्राइवदुरासदाः ।।6.51.27।।
explanation: And others collected together holding shields, fearless like tigers, frightful in appearance, mounted on fast horses, chariots yoked to donkeys of different kinds covered with gold mesh, on maddened elephants Set out.

shloka_text: वृकसिंहमुखैर्युक्तंखरैःकनकभूषणै: । आरुरोहरथंदिव्यंधूम्राक्षःखरनिस्स्वनः ।।6.51.28।।
explanation: Dhumraksha of frightful tone mounted on a chariot adorned with gold yoked to donkeys with lion and bear like faces.

shloka_text: सनिर्यातोमहावीर्योधूम्राक्षोराक्षसैर्वृतः । प्रहसन्पश्चिमद्वारंहनुमान्यत्रयूथपः ।।6.51.29।।
explanation: Heroic Rakshasa, Dhumraksha surrounded by rakshasas set forth laughing to the west gate where Hanuman stood.

shloka_text: रथप्रवरमास्थायखरयुक्तंखरस्वनम् । प्रयान्तंतुमहाघोरंराक्षसंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.51.30।। अन्तरिक्षगताःघोराशकुनाःप्रत्यषेधयन् ।
explanation: While the Rakshasa was mounted on the chariot and going braying like a donkey, a fearful bird going in the sky stood before his chariot.

shloka_text: रथशीर्षेमहान्भीमोगृध्रश्चनिपपातह ।।6.51.31।। ध्वजाग्रेग्रथिताश्चैवनिपेतुःकुणपाशनाः ।
explanation: A foul smelling frightening vulture (that feeds on the dead body) descended on top of the chariot and fell down.

shloka_text: रुधिरार्द्रोमहान् श्वेतःकबन्धःपतितोभुवि ।।6.51.32।। विस्वरंचोत्सृजन्नादंधूम्राक्षस्यसमीपतः । ववर्षरुधिरंदेवस्सञ्चचालचमेदिनी ।।6.51.33।।
explanation: A trunk of a white bird drenched in blood sounding discordant fell near by Dhumraksha. It appeared like a rain god shedding blood on the ground.

shloka_text: रुधिरार्द्रोमहान् श्वेतःकबन्धःपतितोभुवि ।।6.51.32।। विस्वरंचोत्सृजन्नादंधूम्राक्षस्यसमीपतः । ववर्षरुधिरंदेवस्सञ्चचालचमेदिनी ।।6.51.33।।
explanation: A trunk of a white bird drenched in blood sounding discordant fell near by Dhumraksha. It appeared like a rain god shedding blood on the ground.

shloka_text: प्रतिलोमंवनौवायुर्निर्घातसमनिस्वनः । तिमिरौघवृतास्तत्रदिशश्चनचकाशिरे ।।6.51.34।।
explanation: Thunder like roar was heard. Wind blew adversely. Darkness pervaded, and directions could not be seen.

shloka_text: सतूत्पातांस्तदादृष्टवाराक्षसानांभयावहान् । प्रादुर्भूतान्सुघोरांश्चधूम्राक्षोव्यथितोऽभवत् ।।6.51.35।। मुमुहूराक्षसाःसर्वेधूम्राक्षस्यपुरस्सराः ।
explanation: Then Rakshasa feared seeing the dreadful manifestation and got worried. All the Rakshasas walking in front of Dhumraksha lost consciousness.

shloka_text: ततःसुभीमोबहुभिर्निशाचरैर्वृतोऽभिनिष्क्रम्यरणोत्सुकोबली । ददर्शतांराघवबाहुपालितांमहौघकल्पांबहुवानरींचमूम् ।।6.51.36।।
explanation: Thereafter many strong and powerful Rakshasas surrounding Dhumraksha, who was enthusiastic about war, beheld many Vanaras protected by Raghava like at universal dissolution. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकपञ्चाशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fifty first sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षंप्रेक्ष्यनिर्यान्तंराक्षसंभीमविक्रमम् । विनेदुर्वानरास्सर्वेप्रहृष्टायुद्धकाङ् क्षिणः ।।6.52.1।।
explanation: Seeing Dhumraksha of terrible prowess returning, the vanaras made loud noises out of joy and desire to wage war.

shloka_text: तेषांसुतुमुलंयुद्धंसञ्जज्ञेकपिरक्षसाम् । अन्योन्यंपादपैर्घोरंनिघ्नतांशूलमुद्गरैः ।।6.52.2।।
explanation: Tumultuous war took place between Vanaras and Rakshasas, striking one another, monkeys with terrible trees and Rakshasas with tridents and clubs.

shloka_text: राक्षसैर्वानराघोराविनिकृत्तस्समन्ततः । वानरैराक्षसाश्चापिद्रुमैर्भूमिसमीकृताः ।।6.52.3।।
explanation: Fierce Rakshasas mowed down the Vanaras all over and even the Vanaras pulled down Rakshasas to the ground with trees.

shloka_text: राक्षसास्त्वभिसङ्क्रुद्धावानरान्निशितैश्शरैः । विव्यथुर्घोरसङ्काशैःकङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः ।।6.52.4।।
explanation: Highly enraged Rakshasas on their part fixed the Vanaras with sharp dreadful arrows with itching feathers.

shloka_text: तेगदाभिश्चभीमाभिःपट्टसै: कूटमुद्गरैः । घोरैश्चपरिघैश्चित्रैस्त्रिशूलैश्चापिसंश्रितैः ।।6.52.5।। विदार्यमाणारक्षोभिर्वानरास्तेमहाबलाः । अमर्षाज्जनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुःकर्माण्यभीतवत् ।।6.52.6।।
explanation: The Vanaras although strong were wielding maces, spikes, tridents, terrific iron bars and multitude of weapons of many kinds to crush the Rakshasas. They were endowed with prowess, knowledgeable of weapons and doing their duty without fear and with great enthusiasm.

shloka_text: तेगदाभिश्चभीमाभिःपट्टसै: कूटमुद्गरैः । घोरैश्चपरिघैश्चित्रैस्त्रिशूलैश्चापिसंश्रितैः ।।6.52.5।। विदार्यमाणारक्षोभिर्वानरास्तेमहाबलाः । अमर्षाज्जनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुःकर्माण्यभीतवत् ।।6.52.6।।
explanation: The Vanaras although strong were wielding maces, spikes, tridents, terrific iron bars and multitude of weapons of many kinds to crush the Rakshasas. They were endowed with prowess, knowledgeable of weapons and doing their duty without fear and with great enthusiasm.

shloka_text: शरनिर्भिन्नगात्रास्तेशूलनिर्भिन्नदेहिनः । जगृहुस्तेद्रुमांस्तत्रशिलाश्चहरियूथपाः ।।6.52.7।।
explanation: Vanaras 's bodies split in their necks by the terrible tridents, took up trees and rocks to fight.

shloka_text: तेभीमवेगाहरयोनर्दमानास्ततस्ततः । ममन्थूराक्षसान्वीरान्नामानिचबभाषिरे ।।6.52.8।।
explanation: The monkeys endowed with terrific speed, proceeding from there roaring, proclaiming their names crushed the Rakshasa heroes.

shloka_text: तद्भभूवाद्भुतंघोरंयुद्धंवानररक्षसाम् । शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्चबहुभिश्चैवपादपैः ।।6.52.9।।
explanation: Wonderful fight took place between Vanaras and Rakshasas who held trees and rocks of several kinds.

shloka_text: राक्षसामथिताःकेचिद्वानरैर्जितकाशिभिः । ववमूरुधिरंकेचिन्मुखैरुधिरभोजनाः ।।6.52.10।।
explanation: Vanaras who had conquered fear crushed Rakshasas into lumps of flesh indeed the Rakshasas threw out blood from their mouths.

shloka_text: पार्श्वेषुदारिताःकेचित्केचिद्राशीकृताद्रुमैः । शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताःकेचित्केचिद्धन्तैर्विदारिताः ।।6.52.11।।
explanation: Some tore by the sides of the body, some crushed by the trees, some powdered by the rocks, and some were torn into pieces with teeth.

shloka_text: ध्वजैर्विमथितैर्भग्नैःखङ्गैश्चविनिपातितैः । रथैर्विध्वंसितैश्चापिपतितैःरजनीचरैः ।।6.52.12।।
explanation: Indeed, the night rangers were killed, their flags were broken. They were crushed, their swords were destroyed with chariots fallen.

shloka_text: गजेन्द्रैःपर्वताकारैःपर्वताग्रैर्वनौकसाम् । मथितैर्वाजिभिःकीर्णंसारोहैर्वसुधातलम् ।।6.52.13।।
explanation: By the Vanaras hurling from the mountains, the crushed elephants were like mountains and the horses with riders crushed covered the ground all over.

shloka_text: वानरैर्भीमविक्रान्स्सैराप्लुत्याऽप्लुत्यवेगितैः । राक्षसाःकरजैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मुखेषुविनिर्तिताः ।।6.52.14।।
explanation: The Vanaras with their terrific valour jumping up wounded the Rakshasas in their face with their sharp nails.

shloka_text: विषण्णवदनाभूयोविप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः । मूढाश्शोणितगन्धेननिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.52.15।।
explanation: Some others with pale faces and dishevelled hair lost senses due to rolling in blood dropped on the ground.

shloka_text: अन्येतुपरमसङ्कृक्रुद्धाराक्षसाभीमनिश्वना: । तलैरेवाभिधावन्तिवज्रस्पर्शसमैर्हरीन् ।।6.52.16।।
explanation: Other Rakshasas of terrific valour, extremely enraged, hit the monkeys with their palms which were hard as diamond to touch.

shloka_text: वानरैरापतन्तस्तेवेगितावेगवत्तरैः । मुष्टिभिश्चरणैर्दन्स्सैःपादपैश्चावपोथिता ।।6.52.17।।
explanation: Endowed with speed, the Vanaras also fell on the Rakshasas at greater speed, knocking them down with fists, feet, teeth and even trees.

shloka_text: सैन्यंतुविद्रुतंदृष्टवाधूम्राक्षोराक्षसर्षभः । रोषेणकदनंचक्रेवानराणांयुयुत्सताम् ।।6.52.18।।
explanation: Dhumraksha, the bull among the Rakshasas seeing the army distressed and running away, being eager to fight began to cause havoc to the Vanaras.

shloka_text: प्तासैःप्रमथिताःकेचिद्वानराश्शोणितस्रवाः । मुद्गरैराहताःकेचित्पातिताधरणीतले ।।6.52.19।।
explanation: Few Vanaras mutilated by barbed darts, some struck with mallets, blood oozing dropped down.

shloka_text: परिघैर्मथिताःकेचिद्भिण्डिवालैर्विदारिताः । पट्टसैराहता: केचिद्विह्वलन्तोगतासवः ।।6.52.20।।
explanation: Some were pound by iron bars, some were torn up, some split and some pierced and cut ceased in life.

shloka_text: केचिद्विनिहताश्शूलैरुधिरार्द्रावनौकसः । केचिद्विद्रावितानष्टाःसङ्क्रुद्धैराक्षसैर्युधि ।।6.52.21।।
explanation: In the battlefield some Vanaras, attacked by Rakshasas, were floating on the ground in blood, dead.

shloka_text: विभिन्नहृदयाःकेचिदेकपार्श्वेनदारिताः । विदारितास्त्रिशूलैश्चकेचिदान्स्रैर्विनिःसृताः ।।6.52.22।।
explanation: Some with their hearts open and broken, beaten on side laid detached of their inner parts.

shloka_text: तत्सुभीमंमहायुद्धंहरिराक्षससङ्कुलम् । प्रबभौशब्दबहुलंशिलापादपसङ्कुलम् ।।6.52.23।।
explanation: The monkeys and Rakshasa groups took part in a fierce fight with rocks and trees abounding loud noise.

shloka_text: धनुर्ज्यातन्त्रिमधुरंहिक्कातालसमन्वितम् । मन्धस्न्तितसङ्गीतंतद्युद्धगान्धर्वमाबभौ ।।6.52.24।।
explanation: It seemed like music in the form of twang of bow strings, neighing of horses like the sound of wooden cymbals, vocal music in the form of trumpeting of elephants, that battle seemed like symphony.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षस्तुधनुष्पाणिर्वानरान्रणमूर्धनि । हसन्विद्रावयामासदिशस्तुशरवृष्टिभिः ।।6.52.25।।
explanation: Dhumraksha with his bow in hand, showering arrows, laughing in battlefront dispersed the Vanaras in directions.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षेणार्दितंसैन्यंव्यथितंप्रेक्ष्यमारुतिः । अभ्यवर्ततसङ्क्रुद्धःप्रगृह्यविपुलांशिलाम् ।।6.52.26।।
explanation: Beholding the perturbed army, Hanuman seized a huge rock and turned towards Dhumraksha.

shloka_text: क्रोधाद् द्विद्द्विगुणताम्राक्षःपितृस्तुल्यपराक्रमः । शिलांतांपातयामासधूम्राक्षस्यरथंप्रति ।।6.52.27।।
explanation: Endowed with mighty valour equal to his father, an angry Hanuman hurled the rock at the chariot of Dhumraksha.

shloka_text: आपततनींशिलांदृष्टवागदामुद्यम्यसम्भ्रमात् । रथादाप्लुत्यवेगेनवसुधायांव्यतिष्ठत ।।6.52.28।।
explanation: Beholding the rock descending upon him, Dhumraksha rushed instantly on the ground from the chariot and stood.

shloka_text: साप्रमथ्यरथंतस्यनिपपातशिलाभुवि । सचक्रकूबरसाश्वंसध्वजंसशरासनम् ।।6.52.29।।
explanation: That rock fell on the chariot and got crushed along with its wheel and axle and with arrows.

shloka_text: सभङ् क्त्वातुरथंतस्यहनुमान् मारुतात्मजः । रक्षसांकदनंचक्रेसस्कन्धविटपैर्द्रुमैः ।।6.52.30।।
explanation: Hanuman the son of WindGod in that way started destroying the chariot and the Rakshasa with tree trunks and stems.

shloka_text: विभिन्नशिरसोभूत्वाराक्षसाश्शोणितोक्षिता: । द्रुमैःप्रमथिताश्चान्येनिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.52.31।।
explanation: Some Rakshasas hit by trees with their heads broken, shedding blood fell on the ground.

shloka_text: विद्राव्यराक्षसंसैन्यंहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । गिरिशशिखरमादायधूम्राक्षमभिदुद्रुवे ।।6.52.32।।
explanation: Hanuman the son of WindGod, after chasing the army of Rakshasas reaching the top of the mountain, jumped on Dhumraksha.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंधूम्राक्षोगदामुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । विनर्दमानःसहसाहनूमन्तमभिद्रवत् ।।6.52.33।।
explanation: Lifting his mace on seeing Hanuman, heroic and brave Dhumraksha darted on Hanuman, roaring like a lion.

shloka_text: तस्यक्रुद्धस्यरोषेणगदांतांबहुकण्टकाम् । पातयामासधूम्राक्षोमस्तकेऽथहनूमतः ।।6.52.34।।
explanation: And then lifting his mace fixed with many nails, Dhumraksha enraged lighted on Hanuman.

shloka_text: ताडितःसतयातत्रगदयाभीमरूपया । सकपिर्मारुतबलस्तंप्रहारमचिन्तयन् ।।6.52.35।। धूम्राक्षस्यशिरोमध्येगिरिशृङ्गमपातयत् ।
explanation: That fierce mace fell on Hanuman's head. Hanuman who was equal to wind god without caring for the hit dropped the peak of the mountain on the centre of Dhumraksha's head.

shloka_text: सविस्फारितसर्वाङ्गोगिरिशृङ्गेणताडितः । पपातसहसाभूमौविकीर्णइवपर्वतः ।।6.52.36।।
explanation: By the falling of the peak of the mountain on Dhumraksha, all his limbs broken to pieces and crushed fell on the ground like a mountain.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षंनिहतंदृष्टवाहतशेषानिशाचराः ।।6.52.37।। त्रस्ताःप्रविविशुर्लङ्कांवध्यमानाःप्लवङ्गमैः ।
explanation: Those Rakshasas who survived the onslaught, seeing Dhumraksha killed, reentered Lanka out of fear of being killed by Vanaras.

shloka_text: सतुपवनसुतोनिहत्यशत्रून्क्षतजवहरिस्सरितश्चसन्निकीर्य । रिपुवधजनितश्रमोमहात्मामुदमगमत्कपिभिःसुपूज्यमानः ।।6.52.38।।
explanation: The son of wind god, the great soul, having killed the enemy in the battlefield and making the river of blood to flow, was exhausted by killing enemies. The monkeys started worshipping him in joy. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेद्विपञ्चाशस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fifty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षंनिहतंश्रुत्वारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । क्रोधेनमहताऽविष्टोनिश्श्वसन्नुरगोयथा ।।6.53.1।। दीर्घमुष्णंविनिश्श्वस्यक्रोधेनकलुषीकृतः । अब्रवीद्राक्षसंक्रूरंवज्रदंष्ट्रंमहाबलम् ।।6.53.2।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas was overcome with anger on hearing about Dhumraksha's death. He was hissing like a serpent, heaving a deep burning sigh, for having done a dirty task. He spoke to cruel Vajradamshtra of mighty prowess.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षंनिहतंश्रुत्वारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । क्रोधेनमहताऽविष्टोनिश्श्वसन्नुरगोयथा ।।6.53.1।। दीर्घमुष्णंविनिश्श्वस्यक्रोधेनकलुषीकृतः । अब्रवीद्राक्षसंक्रूरंवज्रदंष्ट्रंमहाबलम् ।।6.53.2।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas was overcome with anger on hearing about Dhumraksha's death. He was hissing like a serpent, heaving a deep burning sigh, for having done a dirty task. He spoke to cruel Vajradamshtra of mighty prowess.

shloka_text: गच्छत्वंवीर निर्याहिराक्षसैःपरिवारितः । जहिदाशरथिंरामंसुग्रीवंवानरैःसह ।।6.53.3।।
explanation: "O Hero, proceed, accompanied by Rakshasa companions and kill Dasaratha's Rama and Sugriva along with Vanaras."

shloka_text: तथेत्युक्त्वाद्रुततरंमायावीराक्षसेश्वरम् । निर्जगामबलैस्सार्दंबहुभिःपरिवारितः ।।6.53.4।। नागैरश्वैःखरैरुष्ट्रैःसंयुक्तस्सुसमाहितः । पताकाध्वजचित्रैश्चरथैश्चसमलङ्कृतः ।।6.53.5।।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, being a deceit, having spoken in that way, many generals of the army went accompanied by elephants, horses, camels, and donkeys with chariots decorated with banners and pennons, and diadems collected together.

shloka_text: तथेत्युक्त्वाद्रुततरंमायावीराक्षसेश्वरम् । निर्जगामबलैस्सार्दंबहुभिःपरिवारितः ।।6.53.4।। नागैरश्वैःखरैरुष्ट्रैःसंयुक्तस्सुसमाहितः । पताकाध्वजचित्रैश्चरथैश्चसमलङ्कृतः ।।6.53.5।।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, being a deceit, having spoken in that way, many generals of the army went accompanied by elephants, horses, camels, and donkeys with chariots decorated with banners and pennons, and diadems collected together.

shloka_text: ततोविचित्रकेयूरमुकुटैश्चविभूषितः । तनुत्राणिचसमावृत्यसधनुर्निर्ययौद्रुतम् ।।6.53.6।।
explanation: Thereafter adorned with wonderful crowns studded with keyura gems, wearing a co at covering the body with bow in hand went alert.

shloka_text: पताकालङ्कृतंदीप्तंतप्तकाञ्चनभूषितम् । रथंप्रदक्षिणंकृत्वासमारोहच्चमूपतिः ।।6.53.7।।
explanation: The general went ascending the chariot shining with well polished shining gold, decked with flags after going around clockwise.

shloka_text: यष्टिभिस्तोमरैचशित्रैश्शूलैश्चमुसलैरपि । भिण्डिपालैश्चपाशैश्चशक्तिभिःपट्टसैरपि ।।6.53.8।। खडगैश्चक्रैर्गदाभिश्चनिशितैश्चपरश्वधैः । पदातयश्चनिर्यान्तिविविधाःशस्त्रपाणयः ।।6.53.9।।
explanation: Armed with swords, many foot soldiers carrying poles, strange clubs, tridents, iron bars, slings and roped to throw spears and spears with sharp edges, swords, battle axes, javelins, and maces, departed.

shloka_text: यष्टिभिस्तोमरैचशित्रैश्शूलैश्चमुसलैरपि । भिण्डिपालैश्चपाशैश्चशक्तिभिःपट्टसैरपि ।।6.53.8।। खडगैश्चक्रैर्गदाभिश्चनिशितैश्चपरश्वधैः । पदातयश्चनिर्यान्तिविविधाःशस्त्रपाणयः ।।6.53.9।।
explanation: Armed with swords, many foot soldiers carrying poles, strange clubs, tridents, iron bars, slings and roped to throw spears and spears with sharp edges, swords, battle axes, javelins, and maces, departed.

shloka_text: विचित्रवाससस्सर्वेदीप्ताराक्षसपुङ्गवाः । गजामदोत्कटाश्शूराश्चलन्तइवपर्वताः ।।6.53.10।।
explanation: All the Rakshasa leaders decorated with lovely raiment, glowing, the heroes moved like mountains. They seemed like elephants intoxicated with ichor.

shloka_text: तेयुद्धकुशलैरूढास्तोमराङ्कुशपाणिभिः । अन्येलक्षणसंयुक्ताश्शूरारूढामहाबलाः ।।6.53.11।।
explanation: Carrying tridents, clubs, and goads eager for war the Rakshasas mounted on mahouts and horses of noble characteristics, warriors with extraordinary might departed.

shloka_text: तद्राक्षसबलंसर्वंविप्रस्थितमशोभत । प्रावृटकालेयथामेघानर्दमानास्सविद्युतः ।।6.53.12।। निस्सृतादक्षिणद्वारादङ्गदोयत्रयूथपः ।
explanation: Then the entire Rakshasa army determined with a purpose roaring like clouds of the rainy season it looked splendid and crossed over the southern gate where Angada was stationed.

shloka_text: तेषांनिष्क्रममाणानामशुभंसमजायत ।।6.53.13।। आकाशाद्विघनात्तीव्रादुल्काश्चाभ्यन्यपतंस्तदा । वमन्त्यःपावकज्वालाशशिवाघोरंववाशिरे ।।6.53.14।।
explanation: As they were leaving evil portents appeared. Dreadful jackals, dazzling fire from the sky and meteors falling appeared.

shloka_text: तेषांनिष्क्रममाणानामशुभंसमजायत ।।6.53.13।। आकाशाद्विघनात्तीव्रादुल्काश्चाभ्यन्यपतंस्तदा । वमन्त्यःपावकज्वालाशशिवाघोरंववाशिरे ।।6.53.14।।
explanation: As they were leaving evil portents appeared. Dreadful jackals, dazzling fire from the sky and meteors falling appeared.

shloka_text: व्याहरन्तमृगाघोरारक्षसांनिधनंतदा । समापतन्तोयोधास्तुप्रास्खलन् स्तत्रदारुणम् ।।6.53.15।।
explanation: Then the fierce animals indicated the death of Rakshasas, who were going deluded with war and fell down.

shloka_text: एतानौत्पातिकान् दृष्टवावज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाबलः । धैर्यमालम्भ्यतेजस्वीनिर्जगामरणोत्सुकः ।।6.53.16।।
explanation: Mighty Vajradamshtra who was energetic, picking up courage seeing the portents that came up, sallied forth eager for war.

shloka_text: तांस्तुनिष्क्रमतोदृष्टवावानराजितकाशिनः । प्रणेदुस्सुमहानादान्पूरयांश्चदिशोदश ।।6.53.17।।
explanation: Vanaras who assumed victory, seeing the Rakshasas coming out stretching filled all the ten directions with loud noise.

shloka_text: ततःप्रवृत्तंतुमुलंहरीणांराक्षसैस्सह । घोराणांभीमरूपाणामन्योन्यवथकाङ् क्षिणाम् ।।6.53.18।।
explanation: Then dreadful encounters of fierce form took place between Vanaras and Rakshasas each one trying to kill another.

shloka_text: निष्पतन्तोमहोत्साहोभिन्नदेहशिरोधराः । रुधिरोक्षितसर्वाङ्गान्यपतन्थरणीतले ।।6.53.19।।
explanation: Proceeding Further, very eager to fight they fell on the ground with their bodies broken, heads severed, and all limbs bathed in blood.

shloka_text: केचिदन्योन्यमासाद्यशूराःपरिघपाणयः । चिक्षिपुर्विविधंशस्त्रंसमरेष्न्विवर्तिनः ।।6.53.20।।
explanation: Heroes in war whose hand s were like iron clubs, who never turned back in war, indeed flung weapons of many kinds on one another.

shloka_text: द्रुमाणांचशिलानांचशस्त्राणांचापिनिस्स्वनः ।।6.53.21।। श्रूयतेसुमहांस्तत्रघोरोहृदयभेदसः ।
explanation: There, a very loud fearful noise was heard which pierced the hearts in the battlefield, that was produced by the striking of weapons with trees and rocks.

shloka_text: रथनेमिस्वनस्तत्रधनुषश्चापिनिस्वसत् ।।6.53.22।। शङ्खभेरीमृदङ्गानांबभूवतुमुलःस्वनः ।
explanation: Then came out tumultuous sounds of clutter of chariots, bows, conches, kettle drums and tom toms.

shloka_text: केचिदस्त्राणिसन्सृज्यबाहुयुद्धमकुर्वत । तलैश्चचरणैश्चापिमुष्टिभिश्चद्रुमैरपि ।।6.53.23।। जानुभिश्चहताःकेचिद्भिन्नदेहाश्चराक्षसाः । शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताःकेचिद्वानरैर्युद्धदुर्मदैः ।।6.53.24।।
explanation: Indeed, abandoning the weapons, the Vanaras fought with their palms, fists, feet, trees, and knees and smashed the Rakshasas crushing their bodies like rocks.

shloka_text: केचिदस्त्राणिसन्सृज्यबाहुयुद्धमकुर्वत । तलैश्चचरणैश्चापिमुष्टिभिश्चद्रुमैरपि ।।6.53.23।। जानुभिश्चहताःकेचिद्भिन्नदेहाश्चराक्षसाः । शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताःकेचिद्वानरैर्युद्धदुर्मदैः ।।6.53.24।।
explanation: Indeed, abandoning the weapons, the Vanaras fought with their palms, fists, feet, trees, and knees and smashed the Rakshasas crushing their bodies like rocks.

shloka_text: वज्रदंष्ट्रोभृशंबाणै: रणेवित्रासयन्हरीन् । चचारलोकसंहारेपाशहस्तइवान्तकः ।।6.53.25।।
explanation: Vajradamshtra went about in the battle striking Vanaras just like death goes with a noose for destruction of the world.

shloka_text: बलवन्तोऽस्त्रविदुषोनानाप्रहरणारणे । जघ्नुर्वानरसैन्यानिराक्षसाःक्रोधमूर्छिताः ।।6.53.26।।
explanation: Mighty Vajradamshtra, who was endowed with the skill of using every kind of weapon, deluded with anger, went after the Vanara army.

shloka_text: निघ्नतोराक्षसान्दृष्टवासर्वान्वालिसुतोरणे । क्रोधेनवदिगुणाविष्टःसंवर्तकइवानलः ।।6.53.27।।
explanation: Seeing the Vanaras being destroyed, Vali's son, Angada with redoubled anger, like fire at the time of universal destruction, started to exterminate Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तान् राक्षसगणान्सर्वान्वृक्षमुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । अङ्गदःक्रोधताम्राक्षःसिंहःक्षुद्रमृगानिव ।।6.53.28।। कारकदनंघोरंशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः ।।6.53.29।।
explanation: Heroic Angada, equal to Indra in prowess, enraged, eyes turned red in anger, seizing a tree made a fierce fight with Rakshasa army like a lion with small animals.

shloka_text: तान् राक्षसगणान्सर्वान्वृक्षमुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । अङ्गदःक्रोधताम्राक्षःसिंहःक्षुद्रमृगानिव ।।6.53.28।। कारकदनंघोरंशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः ।।6.53.29।।
explanation: Heroic Angada, equal to Indra in prowess, enraged, eyes turned red in anger, seizing a tree made a fierce fight with Rakshasa army like a lion with small animals.

shloka_text: अङ्गदाभिहतास्तत्रराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः । विभिन्नशिरसःपेतुर्विकृताइवपादपाः ।।6.53.30।।
explanation: There, struck by Angada of fearful valour, the Rakshasas fell like trees smashed and heads broken.

shloka_text: रथैरश्वैर्ध्वजैश्चित्रैश्शरैर्हरिरक्षसाम् । रुधिरेणसञ्छन्नाभूमिर्भयकरातदा ।।6.53.31।।
explanation: Then the wonderful chariots, flags, horses, Vanaras and Rakshasas bodies bathed in blood fell on the ground looked fearful.

shloka_text: हारकेयूरवस्स्रैश्चशत्रैश्चसमलङ्कृता । भूमिर्भातिरणेतत्रशारदीवयथानिशा ।।6.53.32।।
explanation: The battlefield with strewn armlets, necklaces and clothes, weapons looked like autumnal night decorated all over.

shloka_text: बलस्यचविघातेनअङ्गदस्यजयेनच । राक्षसःक्रोधमाविष्टोवज्रदंष्ट्रोमहाबलः ।।6.54.1।।
explanation: Vajradamshtra, the mighty Rakshasa became enraged with the destruction of his army and victory of Angada.

shloka_text: विष्पार्यचधनुर्घोरंशक्राशनिसमस्वनम् । वानराणामनीकानिप्राकिरच्छरवृष्टिभिः ।।6.54.2।।
explanation: Stretching his terrific bow which had the splendour of Indra's bow he (Vajradamshtra) showered shafts at the army troops of Vanaras and assailed them.

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्चापिमुख्यास्तेरथेषुसमवस्थिताः । नानाप्रहरणाश्शूराःप्रायुध्यन्तस्तदारणे ।।6.54.3।।
