shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजारावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । कपेलाघवयुक्तोऽसिमाययापरयाऽनया ।।6.59.86।।
explanation: Ravana endowed with extraordinary energy said, "Oh monkey, you are unfair, very tricky and further deceptive."

shloka_text: जीवितंखलुरक्षस्वयदिशक्तोऽपिवानर । तानितान्यात्मरूपाणिसृजसित्वमनेकशः ।।6.59.87।।
explanation: "Oh monkey! You are taking different forms and doing different deeds. If you have the ability, save your life."

shloka_text: तथापित्वांमयामुक्तस्सायोकोऽस्त्रप्रयोजितः । जीवितंपरिरक्षन्तंजीविताद्भ्रंशयिष्यति ।।6.59.88।।
explanation: "The arrow released by me now is charged with a missile and will destroy your life. You have been protecting (changing your forms) your life."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वामहाबाहूरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । सन्धायबाणमस्त्रणचमूपतिमताडयत् ।।6.59.89।।
explanation: Speaking like that, Ravana, the king of Rakshasas chanting the mantras and fixing the arrow struck the commander in chief (Neela) of the Vanara army.

shloka_text: सोऽस्त्रयुक्तेनबाणेननीलोवक्षसिताडितः । निर्धह्यमानस्सहसानिपपातमहीतले ।।6.59.90।।
explanation: Struck by the arrow propelled by the missile (of Ravana) on the chest, Neela fell on the ground.

shloka_text: पितृमहात्म्यसंयोगात्मनश्चापितेजसा । जानुभ्यानुपतद्भूमौनतुप्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत ।।6.59.91।।
explanation: By virtue of his father's greatness and his own power, his life did not cease but he fell on the ground.

shloka_text: विसंज्ञंवानरंदृष्टवादशग्रीवोरणोत्सुकः । रथेनाम्बुदनादेनसौमित्रिमभिदुद्रुवे ।।6.59.92।।
explanation: Finding the vanara unconscious the ten headed Ravana who was eager to fight went towards Saumithri in the chariot making sounds that resembled the sound of rattling of clouds.

shloka_text: आसाद्यरणमध्येतंवारयित्वास्थितोज्वलन् । धनुर्विष्फारयामासकम्पयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.59.93।।
explanation: In the midst of the battlefield stood Ravana, intercepting with his glowing bow making loud sounds as though shaking the earth.

shloka_text: तमाहसौमित्रिरदीनसत्त्वोविष्फारयन्तंधनुरप्रमेयम् । अभ्येहिमामद्यनिशाचरेन्द्रनवानरांस्त्वप्रतियोद्धुमर्हः ।।6.59.94।।
explanation: Saumithri who was not depressed in spirit (by Ravana's attack) addressing Ravana who was stretching his bow said "Oh! Lord of night rangers, Be aware. You ought not to fight with vanaras."

shloka_text: सतस्यवाक्यंप्रतिपूर्णघोषंज्याशब्दमुग्रंचनिशम्यराजा । आसाद्यसौमित्रिमवस्थितंतंकोपान्वितोवाचमुवाचरक्षः ।।6.59.95।।
explanation: Hearing the challenging statement of the king of Rakshasas and hearing the vibrating sound, Saumithri standing close by spoke these wrathful words.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्यासिमेराघव दृष्टिमार्गंप्राप्तोऽन्तगामीविपरीतबुद्धिः । अस्मिन् क्षणेयास्यसिमृत्युदेशंसम्पाद्यमानोममबाणजालैः ।।6.59.96।।
explanation: "Oh Raghava! You have come under the path of my sight. You are going to meet your end. You who are perverted in mind, struck by a stream of my arrows will reach the abode of death this very moment."

shloka_text: तमाहसौमित्रिरविस्मयानोगर्जन्तमुद्वृत्तसिताग्रदंष्ट्रम् । राजन्नगर्जन्तिमहाप्रभावाविकत्थसेपापकृतांवरिष्ठ ।।6.59.97।।
explanation: Saumithri, not surprised at the screaming of Ravana with his projected teeth, said, "You are great in sinful action. People of great valour do not display such bluster. Do not shout like that."

shloka_text: जानामिवीर्यंतवराक्षसेन्द्रबलंप्रतापंचपराक्रमंच । अवस्थितोऽहंशरचापपाणिरागच्छकिंमोघविकत्थनेन ।।6.59.98।।
explanation: "Your valour, heroism, strength and prowess are known to me. I stand firmly with bow and arrow come on. What is the use of bragging"

shloka_text: सएवमुक्तःकुपितस्ससर्जरक्षोथिपस्सप्तशरान् सुपुङ्खान् । तान्लक्ष्मणःकाञ्चनचित्रिपुङ्खैश्चिच्छेदबाणैर्निशिताग्रधारैः ।।6.59.99।।
explanation: Lakshmana, having spoken in that manner, the Lord of Rakshasas released seven arrows with beautiful plumes. Lakshmana tore them into pieces with sharp pointed and sharpheaded arrows with gold shafts.

shloka_text: तान् प्रेक्षमाणस्सहसानिकृत्तानिकृत्तभोगानिवपन्नगेन्द्रान् । लङ्केश्वरःक्रोधवशंजगामससर्जचान्यान्निशितान्पृषत्कान् ।।6.59.100।।
explanation: Seeing the arrows cut down with force broken pieces like coils of serpents, the Lord of Lanka overtaken by anger let go another sharp arrow.

shloka_text: सबाणवर्षंतुववर्षतीव्रंरामानुजःकार्मुकसम्प्रयुक्तम् । क्षुरार्धचन्द्रोत्तमकर्णिभल्लैःशरांश्चचिच्छेदनचुक्षुभेच ।।6.59.101।।
explanation: The brother of Rama stretched his bow into a circle and showered rain of piercing arrows. He tore the arrows of his enemy with his arrows Kshura, Ardhachandra, karni and Balan without nay, perturbance.

shloka_text: सबाणजालान्यथतानितानिमोघानिपश्यंस्त्रिदशारिराजः । विसिस्मियेलक्ष्मणलाघवेनपुनश्चबाणान्निशितान्मुमोच ।।6.59.102।।
explanation: Ravana, the enemy of gods seeing all his streams of arrows ineffective, was astonished at Lakshmana's skill, and let go sharp arrows again and again.

shloka_text: सलक्ष्मणश्चापिशरान् शिताग्रान्महेन्द्रतुल्योऽशनितुल्यवेगान् । सन्धायचापेज्वलनप्रकाशान् ससर्जरक्षोधिपतेर्वधाय ।।6.59.103।।
explanation: Lakshmana also, who is comparable to Mahendra, fitting his bow and arrows that shone like fire released sharp and pointed arrows to put an end to Rakshasa king.

shloka_text: सतान् प्रचिच्छेदहिराक्षसेन्द्रःछित्वाचतन्लक्ष्मणमाजघान । शरेणकालाग्निसमप्रभेणस्वयम्भुदत्तेनललाटदेशे ।।6.59.104।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king broke into pieces those arrows of Lakshmana and struck him on the forehead with the arrow gifted to him by Brahma, that was bright like the fire at the time of universal destruction.

shloka_text: सलक्ष्मणोरावणसायकार्तश्चचालचापंशिधिलंप्रगृह्य । पुनश्चसंज्ञांप्रतिलभ्यकृच्छ्राच्चिच्छेदचापंत्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रो ।।6.59.105।।
explanation: Lakshmana hurt by Ravana's dart, shaken up, seizing the bow feebly with great difficulty regaining consciousness tore the bow of the enemy of Indra into pieces in return.

shloka_text: निकृत्तचापंत्रिभिराजघानबाणैस्तदादाशरथिश्शिताग्रैः । ससायकार्तोविचचालराजाकृच्छ्राच्छसंज्ञांपुनराससाद ।।6.59.106।।
explanation: Then Lakshmana son of Dasaratha, struck the bow of the king into pieces with three sharp and pointed arrows. The king swooned and recovered with great difficulty.

shloka_text: सकृत्तचापःशरताडितश्चमेदार्द्रगात्रोरुधिरावसिक्तः । जग्राहशक्तिंस्वयमुग्रशक्तिस्स्वयम्भुदत्तांयुधिदेवशत्रुः ।।6.59.107।।
explanation: Hurt by the arrows, bow cut, bathed in blood, limbs splattered with fat, Ravana the enemy of gods, himself being endowed with formidable energy gifted by the Self born creator seized javelin on the battlefield.

shloka_text: सतांसधूमानलसन्निकाशांवित्रासनींसंयतिवानराणाम् । चिक्षेपशक्तिंतरसाज्वलन्तींसौमित्रयेराक्षसराष्ट्रनाथः ।।6.59.108।।
explanation: The Lord of the world of Rakshasas instantly flung javelin, emitting fire without smoke, on Saumithri, which created fear among Vanaras.

shloka_text: तामापतन्तींभरतानुजोऽस्त्रैर्जघानबाणैश्चहुताग्निकल्पैः । तथापिसातस्यविवेशशक्तिर्भुजान्तरंदाशरथेर्विशालम् ।।6.59.109।।
explanation: Lakshmana, the brother of Bharata struck the fierce weapon coming towards him like flames of fire fuelled by ghee, even then it struck him on his broad chest.

shloka_text: सशक्तिमान् शक्तिसमाहतःसन् प्रजज्वालमुहुःरघुप्रवीरः । तंविह्वलन्तंसहसाभ्युपेत्यजग्राहराजातरसाभुजाभ्याम् ।।6.59.110।।
explanation: Lakshmana the eminent hero of Raghu's was badly hurt by the javelin and was burning in pain. King Ravana caught him who was losing consciousness, violently and held him by his shoulders.

shloka_text: हिमवान् मन्दरोमेरुस्तैलोक्यंवासहामरैः । शक्यंभुजाभ्यामुद्धर्तुंनसङ् ख्येभरतानुजः ।।6.59.111।।
explanation: It may be possible to lift Himalayas, Mandara, Meru mountains or even the Devatas of the three worlds but not possible to lift Lakshmana by shoulders.

shloka_text: शक्त्याब्राह्म्याहिसौमित्रिस्ताडितास्तुस्तनान्तरे । विष्णोरचिन्यन्त्यंस्वंभागमात्मानंप्रत्यनुस्मरत् ।।6.59.112।।
explanation: Even though Saumithri was wounded in the chest and the power of Brahma entered (into his chest) he recalled himself as an inconceivable form of Vishnu.

shloka_text: ततोदानवदर्पघ्नंसौमित्रिंदेवकण्टकः । तंपीडयित्वाबाहुभ्यांनप्रभुर्लङ्घनेऽभवत् ।।6.59.113।।
explanation: Thereafter, Ravana the enemy of Devatas was not capable of lifting Lakshmana's shoulders. Lakshmana could crush the pride of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: अथवायुसुतःक्रुद्धोरावणंसमभिद्रवत् । आजघानोरसिक्रुद्धोवज्रकल्पेनमुष्टिना ।।6.59.114।।
explanation: Then the son of the wind god, enraged, came towards Ravana. Full of anger, he struck him with his thunderbolt like fist on the chest of Ravana.

shloka_text: तेनमुष्टिप्रहारेणरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । जानुभ्यामपतद्भूमौचचालचपपातच ।।6.59.115।।
explanation: By the blow of Hanuman's fist, Ravana the Lord of Rakshasas was shaken and fell on the ground on his knees.

shloka_text: अस्यैश्चनेत्रैश्श्रवणैःपपातरुधिरंबहु । विघूर्णमानोनिश्चेष्टोरथोपस्थउपाविशत् ।।6.59.116।।
explanation: Much blood flowed from his(Ravana's) mouth, ears, and eyes. Rolling in the hind part of the chariot he became still and sank.

shloka_text: विसंज्ञोमूर्च्छ्रितश्चासीन्नचस्थानंसमालभत् । विसंज्ञंरावणंदृष्टवासमरेभीमविक्रमम् ।।6.59.117।। ऋषयोवानराश्चैवनेदुर्देवास्सवासवाः ।
explanation: Ravana of fierce valour having lost senses and waking up from unconscious state, perturbed, did not know where he was. Seeing this the sages, even Vanaras, the demons as well as Devatas shouted in joy.

shloka_text: हनूमानपितेजस्वीलक्ष्मणंरावणार्धितम् ।।6.59.118।। आनयद्राघवाभ्याशंबाहुभ्यांपरिगृह्यतम् ।
explanation: Brilliant Hanuman holding Lakshmana wounded by Ravana in both shoulders brought him to Rama.

shloka_text: वायुसूनोःसुहृत्त्वेनभक्त्यापरमयाचसः ।।6.59.119।। शत्रूणामप्रकम्प्योऽपिलघुत्वमगमत्कपेः ।
explanation: Lakshmana though unshakeable for enemies, became light for the son of wind god by his friendship and high devotion.

shloka_text: तंसमुत्सृज्यसाशक्तिःसौमित्रिंयुधिदुर्जयम् ।।6.59.120।। रावणस्यरथेतस्मिन् स्थानंपुनरुपागता ।
explanation: That power returned back to Ravana's chariot to its position, leaving Lakshmana, who was difficult to vanquish.

shloka_text: आश्वस्तश्चनिशल्यश्चलक्ष्मणश्शत्रुसूदनः ।।6.59.121।। विष्णोर्भागममीमांस्यमात्मानंप्रत्यनुस्मरन् ।
explanation: Lakshmana who could destroy foes, recovering from unconsciousness, relieved of wounds again remembered himself to be part of Vishnu of immeasurable power.

shloka_text: रावणोऽपिमहातेजाःप्राप्यसंज्ञांमहाहवे ।।6.59.122।। आददेनिशितान् बाणान् जग्राहचमहद्धमः ।
explanation: Ravana of mighty prowess waking up from consciousness took over his sharp arrows and the great bow also.

shloka_text: निपातितमहावीरांद्रवन्तींवानरींचमूम् ।।6.59.123।। राघवस्तुरणेदृष्टवारावणंसमभिद्रवत् ।
explanation: Raghava also assailed Ravana seeing the fallen Vanara heroes struck in the combat.

shloka_text: अथैवमुपसङ्गम्यहनूमान्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.59.124।। ममपृष्ठंसमारुह्यराक्षसंशास्तुमर्हसि । विष्णुर्यथागरुत्मन्तंबलवन्तंसमाहितः ।।6.59.125।।
explanation: And then Hanuman submitted to Rama, "Just as Lord Vishnu mounted on mighty Garuda, you should also be mounted on my back and subdue Ravana."

shloka_text: अथैवमुपसङ्गम्यहनूमान्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.59.124।। ममपृष्ठंसमारुह्यराक्षसंशास्तुमर्हसि । विष्णुर्यथागरुत्मन्तंबलवन्तंसमाहितः ।।6.59.125।।
explanation: And then Hanuman submitted to Rama, "Just as Lord Vishnu mounted on mighty Garuda, you should also be mounted on my back and subdue Ravana."

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वाराघवोवाक्यंवायुपुत्रेणभाषितम् । आरुरोहमहाशूरंबलवन्तंमहाकपिम् ।।6.59.126।। रथस्थंरावणंसङ् ख्येददर्शमनुजाधिपः ।
explanation: On hearing the sub mission of Hanuman, Sri Rama, the Lord of humans climbed on the great monkey and saw Ravana on the chariot.

shloka_text: तमालोक्यमहातेजाःप्रदुद्रावसराघवः ।।6.59.127।। वैरोचनिवक्रुद्धोविष्णुरभ्युद्यतायुधः ।
explanation: Beholding Ravana, highly energetic Rama wielding his bow went furiously towards him just as Lord Vishnu went with his discuss against Virochana.

shloka_text: ज्याशब्दमकरोत्तीव्रंवज्रनिष्पेषनिस्वनम् ।।6.59.128।। गिरागम्भीरयारामोराक्षसेन्द्रमुवाचह ।
explanation: Rama created a sound like a clap of thunder ringing intensely, a majestic one and spoke in a deep voice to the king.

shloka_text: तिष्ठतिष्ठममत्वंहिकृत्वाविप्रियमीदृशम् ।।6.59.129।। क्वनुराक्षसशार्दूल गतोमोक्षमवाप्स्यसि ।
explanation: "Oh! Tiger among Rakshasas, forbear, forbear. Having done such an offence to me, where are you going for deliverance"

shloka_text: यदीन्द्रवैवस्वतभास्करान्वास्वयम्भुवैश्वानरशंकरान्वा । गमिष्यसित्वंदशवादिशोवातथापिमेनाद्यगतोविमोक्ष्यसे ।।6.59.130।।
explanation: "If you go to Indra or Yama or Sun God or the selfborn Brahma or fire God or Shankara or the ten directions like that, and if you run in front of me you cannot escape."

shloka_text: यश्चैवशक्त्याभिहतस्त्वयाऽद्यइच्छन्विषादंसहसाभ्युपेत्य । सएषरक्षोगणराजमृत्युःसपुत्रपौत्रस्यतवाद्ययुद्धे ।।6.59.131।।
explanation: "Oh! king of Rakshasa troop! He, who was struck without support now, even if he were to come now in front, you with your sons and grandsons will be struck to death by him."

shloka_text: एतेनचात्यद्भुतदर्शनानिशरैर्जवस्थानकृतालयानि । चतुर्धशान्यात्तवरायुधानिरक्षःसहस्राणिनिषूदितानि ।।6.59.132।।
explanation: "By me, who is your adversary, fourteen thousand Rakshasas of fierce forms, who had taken abode at Janasthana and used choicest weapons were exterminated."

shloka_text: राघवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाराक्षसेन्द्रोमहाबलः । वायुपुत्रंमहावेगंवहन्तंराघवंरणे ।।6.59.133।। रोषेणमहताविष्टःपूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् । आजघानशरैर्दीप्स्सैःकालानलशिखोपमैः ।।6.59.134।।
explanation: On hearing Raghava's words, the mighty strong king of Rakshasas seized with violent anger, recalling earlier enmity, struck with blazing arrows like tongues of fire at the time of universal destruction while Hanuman bore Rama.

shloka_text: राघवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाराक्षसेन्द्रोमहाबलः । वायुपुत्रंमहावेगंवहन्तंराघवंरणे ।।6.59.133।। रोषेणमहताविष्टःपूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् । आजघानशरैर्दीप्स्सैःकालानलशिखोपमैः ।।6.59.134।।
explanation: On hearing Raghava's words, the mighty strong king of Rakshasas seized with violent anger, recalling earlier enmity, struck with blazing arrows like tongues of fire at the time of universal destruction while Hanuman bore Rama.

shloka_text: राक्षसेनाहवेतस्यताडितस्यापिसायकैः । स्वभावतेजोयुक्तस्यभूयस्तेजोऽभ्यवर्धत ।।6.59.135।।
explanation: Even though Hanuman was hurt by the arrows discharged by the Rakshasa king, being endowed with energy by nature, his energy went on increasing.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजारावणेनकृतव्रणम् । दृष्टवाप्लवगशार्दूलंक्रोधस्यवशमेयिवान् ।।6.59.136।।
explanation: Seeing the wounds caused by Ravana to Hanuman, the tiger among monkeys, possibly Rama was seized with anger.

shloka_text: तस्याभिसङ्क्रम्यरथंसचक्रंसाश्वध्वजच्छत्रमहापताकम् । ससारथिंसाशनिशूलखडगंरामःप्रचिच्छेदशरैस्सुपुङ्खैः ।।6.59.137।।
explanation: Advancing towards him, (Ravana), Rama tore into pieces his chariot, wheels, horses, standard and canopy including the charioteer and the darts and swords.

shloka_text: अथेन्द्रशत्रुंतरसाजघानबाणेनवज्राशनिसन्निभेन । भुजान्तरेव्यूढसुजातरूपेवज्रेणमेरुंभगवानिवेन्द्रः ।।6.59.138।।
explanation: Then with a shining thunderbolt like arrows Rama struck with the weapon of Indra into the fine chest in between the shoulders just as Indra would strike the Meru Mountain with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: योवज्रपातशनिसन्निपातान्नचक्षुभेनापिचचालराजा । सरामबाणाभिहतोभृशार्तश्चचालचापंचमुमोचवीरः ।।6.59.139।।
explanation: He, that heroic king, who was not disturbed hurt by thunderbolt of lightning, was agonized when struck by Rama's arrow and let his bow fall.

shloka_text: तंविह्वलन्तंप्रसमीक्ष्यरामस्समाददेदीप्तमथार्थचन्द्रम् । तेनार्कवर्णंसहसाकिरीटंचिच्छेदरक्षोधिपतेर्महात्मा ।।6.59.140।।
explanation: Seeing Ravana swooning, great soul Rama took up a crescent shaped arrow and hastily broke his crown into pieces which were shining bright red like the Sun.

shloka_text: तंनिर्विषाशीविषसन्निकाशंशान्तार्चिषंसूर्यमिवाप्रकाशम् । गतश्रियंकृत्तकिरीटकूटमुवाचरामोयुधिराक्षसेन्द्रम् ।।6.59.141।।
explanation: Rama said to the king of Rakshasas, who was like a serpent rid of poison without (head) crown, without splendour like the Sun without brightness, his glory lost with the crown broken in the combat.

shloka_text: कृतंत्वयाकर्ममहत्सुभीमंहतप्रवीरश्चकृतस्त्वयाऽहम् । तस्मात्परिश्रान्तइतिव्यवस्यन्नत्वांशरैर्मृत्युवशंनयामि ।।6.59.142।।
explanation: A great task of killing mighty heroes has been accomplished by you. Therefore, you are exhausted. I declare that I will not send you to death.

shloka_text: गच्छानुजानामिरणार्धितस्त्वंप्रविश्यरात्रिंचरराजलङ्काम् । आश्वस्यनिर्याहिरथीचधन्वीतदाबलंप्रेक्ष्यसिमेरथस्थः ।।6.59.143।।
explanation: "King of night rangers! I know you are agonized after the war. Go to Lanka and rest and reenter, mounted on your chariot with bow. You will witness my strength."

shloka_text: सएवमुक्तोहतदर्पहर्षोनिकृत्तचापश्चहताश्वसूतः । शरार्दितःकृत्तमहाकिरीटोविवेशलङ्कांसहसास्मराजा ।।6.59.144।।
explanation: Rama having spoken in that way (consoling), the king with his vanity and pride crushed, bow broken into pieces, horses and charioteer killed, wounded by arrows, crown broken entered Lanka hastily.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टेरजनीचरेन्द्रेमहाबलेदाववदेवशत्रौ । हरीन् विशल्यान् सहलक्ष्मणेनचकाररामःपरमाहवाग्रे ।।6.59.145।।
explanation: After the king of prowlers, the enemy of Danavas and Devas entered Lanka, Rama and Lakshmana also drew out the arrows from monkeys in the forefront of the battlefield and went.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रभन्नेत्रिदशेन्द्रशतौसुरासुराभूतगणादिशश्च । ससागरास्सर्षिमहोरगाश्चतथैवभूम्यम्बुचराश्चप्रहृष्टाः ।।6.59.146।।
explanation: The enemy of Indra having been routed, the suras and asuras, the guardians of the four quarters, including the sea, the large serpents, and sages so also the creatures of land and water were joyful. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेएकोनषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the fifty ninth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: सप्रविश्यपुरींलङ्कांरामबाणभयार्धितः । भग्नदर्पस्तदाराजाबभूवव्यथितेन्द्रियः ।।6.60.1।।
explanation: Then the king of Lanka after entering the city of Lanka, felt humiliated by Rama's arrow, vanity crushed and had lost control over his senses.

shloka_text: मातङ्गइवसिंहेनगरुडेनेवपन्नगः । अभिभूतोऽभवद्राजाराघवेणमहात्मना ।।6.60.2।।
explanation: Overcome by humiliation from the high souled Rama, Ravana remained like an elephant rejected by a lion and a serpent rejected by Garuda.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मदण्डप्रतीकानांविद्युत्सदृशवर्चसाम् । स्मरन्राघवबाणानांविव्यथेराक्षसेश्वरः ।।6.60.3।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas remained disquieted recalling the arrows of Rama which emitted light like lightning, resembling Brahmadanda.

shloka_text: नकाञ्चनमयंदिव्यमाश्रित्यपरमासनम् । विप्रेक्षमाणोरक्षांसिरावणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.60.4।।
explanation: Ravana seated on the wonderful golden magnificent throne gazing at Rakshasas spoke these words.

shloka_text: सर्वंतत्खलुमेमोघंयत्तप्तंपरमंतपः । यत्समानोमहेन्द्रेणमानुषेणास्मिर्जितः ।।6.60.5।।
explanation: " All the penance which I have done, and the asceticism practised by me equal to Mahendra has become purposeless and defeated."

shloka_text: इदंतद्ब्रह्मणोघोरंवाक्यंमामभ्युपस्थितम् । मानुषेभ्योविजानीहिभयंत्वमितितत्तथा ।।6.60.6।।
explanation: The dreadful words of Brahma spoken to me" know that danger from humans is coming to be true.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः । अवध्यत्वंमयाप्राप्तंमानुषेभ्योनयाचितम् ।।6.60.7।।
explanation: "I sought protection from Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Rakshasas and serpents but not asked for protection from humans."

shloka_text: विदितंमानुषंमन्येरामंदशरथात्मजम् । इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातेनअनरण्येनयत्पुरा ।।6.60.8।। उत्पत्स्यतेहिमद्वंशेपुरुषोराक्षसाधनु । यस्त्वांसपुत्रंसामात्यंसबलंसाश्वसारथिम् ।।6.60.9।। निहनिष्यतिसङ्ग्रामेत्वांकुलाधम दुर्मते ।
explanation: "I think that Dasaratha's son Rama, a human being is about whom king Anaranya born in Ikshvaku race, who cursed me earlier saying, 'In my race will be born a man who will kill you in war, with your sons, your horses, charioteers, all army, O evil minded lowest of Rakshasas, and the vilest of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: विदितंमानुषंमन्येरामंदशरथात्मजम् । इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातेनअनरण्येनयत्पुरा ।।6.60.8।। उत्पत्स्यतेहिमद्वंशेपुरुषोराक्षसाधनु । यस्त्वांसपुत्रंसामात्यंसबलंसाश्वसारथिम् ।।6.60.9।। निहनिष्यतिसङ्ग्रामेत्वांकुलाधम दुर्मते ।
explanation: "I think that Dasaratha's son Rama, a human being is about whom king Anaranya born in Ikshvaku race, who cursed me earlier saying, 'In my race will be born a man who will kill you in war, with your sons, your horses, charioteers, all army, O evil minded lowest of Rakshasas, and the vilest of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: शप्तोऽहंवेदवत्याचयदासाधर्षितापुरा ।।6.60.10।। सेयंसीतामहाभागाजाताजनकनन्दिनी ।
explanation: "In the past, I violated Vedavathi and got cursed by her. The same Woman born as Sita, the daughter of Janaka, is a highly blessed one."

shloka_text: उमानन्दीश्वरश्चापिरम्भावरुणकन्यका ।।6.60.11।। यथोक्तास्तन्मयाप्राप्तंनमिथ्याऋषिभाषितम्
explanation: "Uma, Nandeeswara, Rambha and daughter of Varuna have cursed me like that and the prediction of those endowed with vision has been attained by me."

shloka_text: एतदेवाभ्युपागम्ययत्नंकर्तुमहार्हथ ।।6.60.12।। राक्षसाश्चापितिष्ठन्तुचर्यागोपुरमूर्थसु ।
explanation: "Knowing all this, make effort doing what ought to be done and let the Rakshasas strive to succeed positioned on top of the gates."

shloka_text: सचाप्रतिमगाम्भीर्योदेवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.60.13।। ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतस्तुकुम्भकर्णोविबोध्यताम् ।
explanation: "Let Kumbhakarna of unparalleled profundity, capable of crushing Devas and Danavas, who is in slumber owing to the curse of Brahma be awakened."

shloka_text: सपराजितमात्मानंप्रहस्तंचनिषूदितम् ।।6.60.14।। ज्ञात्वारक्षोबलंभीममादिदेशमहाबलः ।
explanation: "Let him be instructed that Prahastha endowed with mighty prowess has been defeated and killed."

shloka_text: द्वारेषुयत्नःक्रियतांप्राकारश्चाधिरुह्यताम् ।।6.60.15।। निद्रावशसमाविष्टःकुम्भकर्णोविबोद्यताम् ।
explanation: "Let the Rakshasas climb up the defensive walls and attempt to guard. Also let Kumbhakarna be aroused from sleep."

shloka_text: सुखंस्वपितिनिश्चिन्तःकालोपहतचेतनः ।।6.60.16।। नवषट् सप्तचाष्टौचमासान् स्वपितिराक्षसः ।
explanation: "The Rakshasa, Kumbhakarna, lost consciousness is slumbering at ease and has been sleeping for six to nine months happily."

shloka_text: मन्त्रयित्वाप्रसुप्तोऽयमितस्तुनवमेऽहनि ।।6.60.17।। तंतुबोधयतक्षिप्रंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।
explanation: "Deliberating like this with me, Kumbhakarna is sleeping for the ninth day from now. He may be quickly informed (aroused)."

shloka_text: सतुसङ् ख्येमहाबाहुःककुदस्सर्वरक्षसाम् ।।6.60.18।। वानरान् राजपुत्रौचक्षिप्रमेवहनिष्यति
explanation: "Endowed with broad shoulders, he is the foremost of Rakshasas. He will crush many Vanaras immediately and the two princes (Rama and Lakshmana)."

shloka_text: एषःकेतुःपरंसङ् ख्येमुख्योवैसर्वरक्षसाम् ।।6.60.19।। कुम्भकर्णःसदाशेतेमूढोग्राम्यसुखेरतः ।
explanation: "He, (Kumbhakarna) is the foremost chief among all Rakshasas enumerated. In that way he is distinguished. But he is insensate, remains addicted always to indecent delight in the form of sleep."

shloka_text: रामेणहिनिरस्तस्यसङ्ग्रामेऽस्मिन् सुदारुणे ।।6.60.20।। भविष्यतिनमेशोकःकुम्भकर्णेविबोधिते ।
explanation: " After Kumbhakarna is fully aroused, my sorrow impelled in this terrible comb at with Rama will not be there."

shloka_text: किंकरिष्याम्यहंतेनशक्रतुल्यबलेनहि ।।6.60.21।। ईदृशेव्यसनेघोरेयोनसाह्यायकल्पते ।
explanation: "What can I do if he does not assist me in such a dreadful comb at because of his weakness, even though he is equal to Indra in strength"

shloka_text: तेतुतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराक्षसेन्द्रस्यराक्षसाः ।।6.60.22।। जग्मुःपरमसम्भ्रान्ताःकुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम् ।
explanation: On listening to the Rakshasa king's words, the Rakshasas went to the abode of Kumbhakarna highly puzzled.

shloka_text: तांप्रविश्यमहाद्वारंसर्वतोयोजनायताम् ।।6.60.23।। कुम्भकर्णगुहांरम्यांसर्वगन्धप्रवाहिनीम् । कुम्भकर्णस्यनिःश्वासादवधूतामहाबलाः ।।6.60.24।। प्रतिष्ठमानाःकृच्छ्रेणयत्नात्प्रविविशुर्गुहाम् ।
explanation: The Rakshasas entered the beautiful residence of Kumbhakarna which was one yojana on all sides with huge gates, taking fragrant garlands and foods (to wake up Kumbhakarna) from where they were pushed out by the breath of Kumbhakarna. The Rakshasas endowed with mighty strength pushed their way into the residence of Kumbhakarna and entered.

shloka_text: तांप्रविश्यमहाद्वारंसर्वतोयोजनायताम् ।।6.60.23।। कुम्भकर्णगुहांरम्यांसर्वगन्धप्रवाहिनीम् । कुम्भकर्णस्यनिःश्वासादवधूतामहाबलाः ।।6.60.24।। प्रतिष्ठमानाःकृच्छ्रेणयत्नात्प्रविविशुर्गुहाम् ।
explanation: The Rakshasas entered the beautiful residence of Kumbhakarna which was one yojana on all sides with huge gates, taking fragrant garlands and foods (to wake up Kumbhakarna) from where they were pushed out by the breath of Kumbhakarna. The Rakshasas endowed with mighty strength pushed their way into the residence of Kumbhakarna and entered.

shloka_text: तांप्रविश्यगुहांरम्यांशुभांकाञ्चनकुट्टिमाम् ।।6.60.25।। ददृशुर्नैरृतव्याघ्रंशयानंभीमविदर्शनम् ।
explanation: The tigers among Rakshasas entered the residence paved with gold and precious stones, a delightful one and saw sleeping Kumbhakarna of great prowess.

shloka_text: तेतुतंविकृतंसुप्तंविकीर्णमिवपर्वतम् ।।6.60.26।। कुम्भकर्णंमहानिद्रंसहिताःप्रत्यबोधयन् ।
explanation: Those Rakshasas collected together started to awaken Kumbhakarna, who was like a scattered mountain in dead sleep.

shloka_text: ऊर्ध्वरोमाञ्चिततनुंश्वसन्तमिवपन्नगम् । भ्रामयन्तम् न्विश्श्वसैःशयानम् भीमविदर्शमम् ।।6.60.27।। भीमनासापुटंतंतुपातालोविपुलाननम् । शयनेन्यस्तसर्वाङ्गंमेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम् ।।6.60.28।। काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाङ्गंकिरीटिनमरिन्दमम् । ददृशुर्नैरृतव्याघ्रंकुम्भकर्णमरिन्दमम् ।।6.60.29।।
explanation: The Rakshasas saw Kumbhakarna, destroyer of enemies, the tiger of the southwest, tamer of foes, with his body fully covered with bristling hair, breathing heavily like a serpent with horrible nostrils, turning back with facemouth as vast as underworld all limbs stretched out, emitting smell of fat and blood, arms adorned with gold bracelets, wearing a crown, and sleeping.

shloka_text: ऊर्ध्वरोमाञ्चिततनुंश्वसन्तमिवपन्नगम् । भ्रामयन्तम् न्विश्श्वसैःशयानम् भीमविदर्शमम् ।।6.60.27।। भीमनासापुटंतंतुपातालोविपुलाननम् । शयनेन्यस्तसर्वाङ्गंमेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम् ।।6.60.28।। काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाङ्गंकिरीटिनमरिन्दमम् । ददृशुर्नैरृतव्याघ्रंकुम्भकर्णमरिन्दमम् ।।6.60.29।।
explanation: The Rakshasas saw Kumbhakarna, destroyer of enemies, the tiger of the southwest, tamer of foes, with his body fully covered with bristling hair, breathing heavily like a serpent with horrible nostrils, turning back with facemouth as vast as underworld all limbs stretched out, emitting smell of fat and blood, arms adorned with gold bracelets, wearing a crown, and sleeping.

shloka_text: ऊर्ध्वरोमाञ्चिततनुंश्वसन्तमिवपन्नगम् । भ्रामयन्तम् न्विश्श्वसैःशयानम् भीमविदर्शमम् ।।6.60.27।। भीमनासापुटंतंतुपातालोविपुलाननम् । शयनेन्यस्तसर्वाङ्गंमेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम् ।।6.60.28।। काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाङ्गंकिरीटिनमरिन्दमम् । ददृशुर्नैरृतव्याघ्रंकुम्भकर्णमरिन्दमम् ।।6.60.29।।
explanation: The Rakshasas saw Kumbhakarna, destroyer of enemies, the tiger of the southwest, tamer of foes, with his body fully covered with bristling hair, breathing heavily like a serpent with horrible nostrils, turning back with facemouth as vast as underworld all limbs stretched out, emitting smell of fat and blood, arms adorned with gold bracelets, wearing a crown, and sleeping.

shloka_text: ततश्चक्रुर्महात्मानंकुम्भकर्णाग्रतस्तदाचाग्रतः ।।6.60.30।। मांसानांमेरुसङ्काशंराशिंपरमतर्पणम् ।
explanation: Thereafter the Rakshasas placed a heap of me at the size of Meru Mountain to please him immensely.

shloka_text: मृगाणांमहिषाणांचवराहाणांचसञ्चयान् ।।6.60.31।। चक्रुर्नैरृतशार्दूलाराशिमन्नस्यचाद्भुतम् ।
explanation: The tigers of the south west Rakshasas piled up a mass of marvellous food like the me at of buffaloes, swine, and antelopes.

shloka_text: ततश्शोणितकुम्भांश्चमद्यानिविविधानिच ।।6.60.32।। पुरस्तात्कुम्भकर्णस्यचक्रुस्त्रिदशशत्रवः ।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas placed thirty three kinds of meat, pails of blood, and a variety of wines in front of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: लिलिपुश्चपरार्ध्येनचन्दनेनपरन्तपम् ।।6.60.33।। दिव्यैराश्वासयामामासुर्माल्यैर्गन्धैस्सुगन्धिभिः ।
explanation: Again, they daubed Kumbhakarna with highly fragrant sandal paste to take in fragrance, with wonderful garlands and perfumes.

shloka_text: धूपंसुगन्धांश्चससृजुस्तुष्टवुश्चपरन्ततम् ।।6.60.34।। जलदाइवचानेदुर्यातुधानास्ततस्ततः ।
explanation: They also burnt incense, sandal to send forth fragrance to gratify Kumbhakarna and thundered like clouds here and there.

shloka_text: शङ्खांनापूरयामासुश्शशाङ्कसदृशप्रभान् ।।6.60.35।। तुमुलंयुगपच्छापिविनेदुश्चाप्यमर्षिताः ।
explanation: They blew moon size conches shining brightly. Intolerant Rakshasas raised loud noise simultaneously.

shloka_text: नेदुरास्फोटयामासुश्चिक्षिपुस्तेनिशाचराः ।।6.60.36।। कुम्भकर्णविबोधार्थंचक्रुस्तेविपुलंस्वनम् ।
explanation: Those night rangers drawing the limbs of Kumbhakarna pushed his arms, clapping loudly to awaken him making a sound.

shloka_text: सशङ्खभेरीपणवप्रणादमास्फोटितक्षेवळितसिंहनादम् । दिशोद्रवन्तस्त्रिदिवंकीरन्तःश्रुत्वाविहंगाःसहसानिपेतुः ।।6.60.37।।
explanation: On hearing the conchs, and of the clapping of arms, and thundering like a lion, the birds playing in the sky got scattered and fell.

shloka_text: यदाभृशंतैर्निनदैर्महात्मानकुम्बकर्णोबुबुधेप्रसुप्तः । ततोमुसुण्ठीर्मुसलानिसर्वेरक्षोगणास्तेजगृहुर्गदाश्च ।।6.60.38।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna sleeping like that, could not be awakened. Angry Rakshasas roared and hit him with mallets and maces.

shloka_text: तंशैलशृङ्गैर्मुसलैर्गदाभिर्वृक्षैस्तरैर्मुद्गरमुष्टिभिश्च । सुखप्रसुप्तंभुविकुम्भकर्णंरक्षांस्युदग्राणितदानिजघ्नुः ।।6.60.39।।
explanation: Then the excited Rakshasas could not wake up Kumbhakarna happily sleeping on the ground in spite of hitting with rocks and trees and their fists.

shloka_text: तस्यनिःश्वासवातेनकुम्भकर्णस्यरक्षसः । राक्षसाबलवन्तोऽपिस्थातुनाशक्नुवन्पुरः ।।6.60.40।।
explanation: Unable to bear the force of the breathing out of Kumbhakarna, the Rakshasas could not stand.

shloka_text: ततःपरिहितागाढंराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः । मृदङ्गपणवान् भेरीश्शङ्खकुम्भगणांस्तथा ।।6.60.41।।
explanation: The Rakshasas of terrible valour resorted to abandoned drums and tom toms that way and pails of clay.

shloka_text: दशराक्षससाहस्रंयुगपत्पर्यवारयन् । नीलाञ्जनचयाकारंतेतुतंप्रत्यबोधयन् ।।6.60.42।। अभिघ्नन्तोनदन्तश्चनैवसंविविदेतुसः ।
explanation: Ten thousand Rakshasas surrounded him all at once like a mass of antimony striking him and even made a loud noise. But he never responded.

shloka_text: यदाचैनंनशेकुस्तेप्रतिबोधयितुंतदा ।।6.60.43।। ततोगुरुतरंयत्नंदारुणंसमुपाक्रमन् ।
explanation: They called him again and again, but he never got up. Then they made a difficult and dreadful effort approaching him.

shloka_text: आश्वानुष्ट्रान् खरन्नागान् जघ्नुर्दण्डकशाङ्कुशैः ।।6.60.44।। भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गांश्चसर्वप्राणैरवादयन् ।
explanation: They urged horses, elephants, camels, and donkeys to pounce on him, whipping with staff, whips, and goads.

shloka_text: निजघ्नुश्चास्यगात्राणिमहाकाष्ठकङ्करैः ।।6.60.45।। मुद्गरैर्मुसलैश्चापिसर्वप्राणसमुद्यतैः ।
explanation: The city of Lanka including the woods was filled with that noise. They pushed him with mallets with all their strength, but he did not wake up.

shloka_text: तेननादेवमहतालङ्कासमभिपूरिता ।।6.60.46।। सपर्वतवनासर्वासोऽपिनैवप्रबुध्यते ।
explanation: All Lanka and mountains were filled by the great noise made by the Rakshasas. Even then Kumbhakarna did not wake up.

shloka_text: ततस्सहस्रंभेरीणांयुगसत्समहन्यत ।।6.60.47।। मृष्टकाञ्चनकोणानामासक्तानांसमन्ततः ।
explanation: Then was collected a thousand drums and beaten with polished gold sticks on all sides continuously.

shloka_text: एवमप्यन्तिद्रिस्तुयदानैवप्रबुध्यत ।।6.60.48।। शापस्यवशमापन्नस्ततःक्रुद्धानिशाचराः ।
explanation: Wrapped in sleep like that because of the spell of the curse, he had not wakened. The Rakshasas got enraged.

shloka_text: महाक्रोधसमाविष्टास्सर्वेभीमपराक्रमाः ।।6.60.49।। तद्रक्षोबोधयिष्यन्तश्चक्रुरन्येपराक्रमम् ।
explanation: All the Rakshasas endowed with mighty prowess became enraged and others started to arouse with all their strength.

shloka_text: अन्येभेरीस्समाजघ्नुरन्येचक्रुर्महास्वनम् ।।6.60.50।। केशानन्येप्रलुलुपुःकर्णावन्येदशन्तिच ।
explanation: While some were beating the drums, some shouted at the pitch of their voice, some started pulling his hair and some bit his ears.

shloka_text: उदकुम्बशतान्यन्येसमसिञ्चन्तकर्णयोः ।।6.60.51।। नकुम्भकर्णःपस्पन्देमहानिद्रावशंगतः ।
explanation: Some poured hundreds of pails of water into ears, distressed that he did not wake up under the spell of deep sleep.

shloka_text: अन्येचबलिनस्तस्यकूटमुद्गरपाणयः ।।6.60.52।। मूर्ध्निवक्षसिगात्रेषुपातन् कूटमुद्गरान् ।
explanation: Some had their nails fixed with mallets, letting their mallets fall on the forehead, on the chest and throw at of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: रज्जुबन्धनबद्धाभिश्शतघ्नीभिश्चसर्वशः ।।6.60.53।। वध्यमानोमहाकायोनप्राबुध्यतराक्षसः ।
explanation: Some struck with sataghni (mace) all over his huge body fastened with cords.

shloka_text: वारणानांसहस्रंचशरीरेऽस्यप्रधावितम् ।।6.60.54।। कुम्बकर्णस्तदाबुद् ध्वास्पर्शंपरमबुध्यत ।
explanation: A thousand elephants were made to walk over his body. Then Kumbhakarna felt the touch but did not understand.

shloka_text: सपात्यमानैर्गिरिशृङ्गवृक्षैरचिन्तयंस्तान्विपुलान् प्रहारान् । निद्राक्ष्यात् क्षुद्भयपीडितश्चविजृम्भमाणस्सहसोत्पपाप ।।6.60.55।।
explanation: Tormented by hunger and hit by mountain peaks and huge trees he sprang up suddenly descended and awakened.

shloka_text: सनागभोगाचलशृङ्गकल्पौविक्षिप्यबाहूगिरशृङ्गसारौ । निवृत्यवक्त्रंवडवामुखाभंनिशाचरोऽसौविकृतंजजृम्भे ।।6.60.56।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, devoid of any beauty threw out his limbs which were like the coils of cobra and as hard as mountain tops, his mouth was unnatural like a submarine fire as he yawned.

shloka_text: तस्यजाजृम्भमाणस्यवक्त्रंपातालसन्निभम् । ददृशेमेरुशृङ्गाग्रेदिवाकरइवोदितः ।।6.60.57।।
explanation: As he yawned his mouth resembling the underworld, it was like the Sun rose over the top of Mount Meru.

shloka_text: सजृम्भमाणोऽतिबलःप्रद्धोनिशाचरः । निःश्वासश्चास्यसञ्जज्ञेपर्वतादिवमारुतः ।।6.60.58।।
explanation: As the mighty night ranger awakened and yawned continuously his breath was like wind blowing from the mountain.

shloka_text: रूपमुत्तिष्ठतस्तस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यतद्बभौ । तपान्तेसबलाकस्यमेघस्येवविवर्षतः ।।6.60.59।।
explanation: As Kumbhakarna woke up he appeared like the time spirit at the time of dissolution of the universe like a rainy cloud at twilight as if seeking to consume all beings.

shloka_text: तस्यदीप्ताग्निसदृशेविद्युत्सदृशवर्चसी । ददृशातेमहानेत्रेदीप्ताविवमहाग्रहौ ।।6.60.60।।
explanation: His huge eyes were like blazing fire dazzling like lightning glowing like two huge planets.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वदर्शयन् सर्वान्भक्ष्यांश्चविविधान् बहून् । वराहान्महिषांश्चैवबभक्षसमहाबलः ।।6.60.61।।
explanation: Thereafter having seen several kinds of food items of hogs, buffaloes he ate them.

shloka_text: आददुन्भुक्षितोमांसंशोणितंतृषितःपिबन् । मेदःकुम्भांश्चमद्यांश्चपपौशक्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.60.62।।
explanation: After eating the meat and feeling thirsty, the enemy of Indra drank blood, pails of fat and wine.

shloka_text: ततस्तृप्तइतिज्ञात्वासमुत्पेतुर्निशाचराः । शिरोभिश्चप्रणम्यैनंसर्वतःपर्यवारयन् ।।6.60.63।।
explanation: There upon the night rangers realizing that he got up, came before him, and greeted him with heads bent down.

shloka_text: निद्राविशदनेत्रस्तुकलुषीकृतलोचनः । चारयन् सर्वतोदृष्टिंतान् ददर्शनिशाचरान् ।।6.60.64।।
explanation: With sleepy eyes casting his glance at the night rangers looked at all of them.

shloka_text: ससर्वान् सान्त्वयामासनैरृतान् नैरृतर्षभः । बोधनाद्विस्मितश्चापिराक्षसानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.60.65।।
explanation: He, the bull among the south west region, astonished at his awakening, soothed, and spoke to all the Rakshasas in this way.

shloka_text: किमर्थमहमादृत्यभवद्भिःप्रतिबोधितः । कच्छित्सुकुशलंराज्ञोभयंवानेषनकिम् ।।6.60.66।।
explanation: "What have you done to wake me Hope King is fine and has no fear of danger"

shloka_text: अथवाध्रुवमन्येभ्योभयंपरमुपस्थितम् । यदर्थमेवत्वरितैर्भवद्भिःप्रतिबोधितः ।।6.60.67।।
explanation: "Is there any fear of some enemies Is it because of that you have woken me up Let me know."

shloka_text: अद्यराक्षसराजस्यभयमुत्पाटयाम्यहम् । दारयिष्येमहेन्द्रंवाशातयिष्येतथानलम् ।।6.60.68।।
explanation: "I will devour Rakshasa king's fear. I will eradicate even Mahendra (mountain) or alleviate fire."

shloka_text: नह्यल्पकारणेसुप्तंबोधयिष्यतिमांगुरुः । तदाख्यातार्थतत्त्वेनमत्प्रबोधनकारणम् ।।6.60.69।।
explanation: "For a small reason he will not awaken me. Tell me the reason truly for waking me."

shloka_text: एवंब्रुवाणंसम्रब्धंकुम्भकर्णमरिन्दमम् । यूपाक्षःसचिवोराज्ञःकृताञ्जलिरभाषत ।।6.60.70।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, tamer of enemies having spoken in that way in anger, Yupaksha, a minister joined palms and replied to him.

shloka_text: ननोदेवकृतंकिञ्चिद्भयमस्तिकदाचन । मानुषान्नोभयंराजंस्तुमुलंसम्प्रबाधते ।।6.60.71।।
explanation: "O King! there is no danger from Devas. Only a small destruction done by a human is pressing and causing pain."

shloka_text: नदैत्यदानवेभ्योवाभयमस्तिहितादृशम् । यादृशंमानुषंराजन् भयमस्मानुपस्थितम् ।।6.60.72।।
explanation: "O King! This kind of fear from humans has not arisen for us either from Daityas or Danavas."

shloka_text: वानरैःपर्वताकारैर्लङ्केयंपरिवारिता । सीताहरणसन्तप्ताद्रामान्नस्तुमुलंभयम् ।।6.60.73।।
explanation: This Lanka is seized by a mountain like army of Vanaras. By the abduction of Sita, there is little fear from Rama.

shloka_text: एकेनवानरेणेयंपूर्वंदग्धामहापुरी । कुमारोनिहतश्चाक्षस्सानुयात्रःसकुञ्जरः ।।6.60.74।।
explanation: "Earlier this great city was burnt by a single Vanara who killed Prince Aksha, and his elephants and followers."

shloka_text: स्वयंरक्षोधिपश्चापिपौलस्त्योदेवकण्टकः । मृतेतिसंयुगेमुक्तोरामेणादित्यतेजसा ।।6.60.75।।
explanation: "Rakshasa king, scion of sage Paulastya, an enemy of Devatas, was let off from death by Rama who has the splendour of Sun."

shloka_text: यन्नदेवैःकृतोराजानापिदैत्यैर्नदानवैः । कृतःसइहरामेणविमुक्तःप्राणसंशयात् ।।6.60.76।।
explanation: "The king could escape from the verge of death and such an act was never done by Daityas or Danavas earlier in the encounter."

shloka_text: सयूपाक्ष्वचश्श्रुत्वाभ्रातुर्युधिपराभवम् । कुम्भकर्णोविवृत्ताक्षोयूपाक्षमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.60.77।।
explanation: On hearing the words of Yupaksha, regarding the insult of his brother Kumbhakarna said this rolling his eyes.

shloka_text: सर्वमद्यैवयूपाक्षहरिसैन्यंसलक्ष्मणम् । राघवंचरणेजित्वाततोद्रक्ष्यामिरावणम् ।।6.60.78।।
explanation: "I will conquer now the Vanara army along with Lakshmana and Raghava in war and see Ravana."

shloka_text: राक्षसांस्तर्पयिष्यामिहरीणांमांसशोणितैः । रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापिस्वयंपास्यामिशोणितम् ।।6.60.79।।
explanation: "I will satisfy the Rakshasas with the flesh and blood of Rama and Lakshmana. You will see."

shloka_text: तत्तस्यवाक्यंब्रुवतोनिशम्यसगर्वितंरोषविवृद्धदोषम् । महोदरोनैरृतयोधमुख्यःकृताञ्जलिर्वाक्यमिदंबभाषे ।।6.60.80।।
explanation: Hearing the words of the reply of Kumbhakarna, filled with arrogance and pride, Mahodara, chief of the army, submitted with folded hands and said.

shloka_text: रावणस्यवचःश्रुत्वागुणदोषौविमृश्यच । पश्चादपिमहाबाहो शत्रून्युधिविजेष्यसि ।।6.60.81।।
explanation: "O Mighty Armed One! You hear from Ravana the advantages and disadvantages and thereafter assess the enemy to conquer."

shloka_text: महोदरवचश्श्रुत्वाराक्षसैःपरिवारितः । कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजास्सम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.60.82।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna of extraordinary energy, mighty strong, on hearing Mahodara went in surrounded by Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सुप्तमुत्थाप्यभीमाक्षंभीमरूपपराक्रमम् । राक्षसास्त्वरिताजुग्मर्दशग्रीन्विवेशनम् ।।6.60.83।।
explanation: After rousing up Kumbhakarna of frightful eyes and fierce strength from sleep the Rakshasas quickly went to the abode of the ten headed king.

shloka_text: ततोगत्वादशग्रीवमासीनंपरमासने । ऊचुर्बद्धाञ्जलिपुटास्सर्वएवनिशाचराः ।।6.60.84।।
explanation: All those night rangers, approaching the tenheaded king seated on an excellent se at greeted with folded hands and said.

shloka_text: प्रबुद्धोऽयंकुम्भकर्णभ्रातातेराक्षसेश्वर । कथंतत्रैवनिर्यातुद्रक्ष्यसेतमिहागतम् ।।6.60.85।।
explanation: "O Rakshasa Lord! Your brother Kumbhakarna has come here. Greetings to you. Tell us what to do."

shloka_text: रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्धृष्टोराक्षसांस्तानुपस्थितान् । द्रष्टुमेनमिहेच्छामियथान्यायंचपूज्यताम् ।।6.60.86।।
explanation: Ravana on his part said this to the Rakshasas feeling cheerful. "Honour him as propriety demands. I wish to see him."

shloka_text: तथेत्युक्त्वातुतेसर्वेपुनरागम्यराक्षसाः । कुम्भकर्णमिदंवाक्यमूचूरावणचोदिताः ।।6.60.87।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas taking leave from Ravana said this again approaching Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: द्रष्टुंत्वांकांक्षतेराजासर्वराक्षसपुङ्गवः । गमनेक्रियतांबुद्धिर्भ्रातरंसम्प्रहर्षयः ।।6.60.88।।
explanation: All the Rakshasa leaders said to Kumbhakarna," the king desires to see you. Start. Make up your mind. Be pleased to depart to your brother."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्तुदुर्धर्षोभ्रातुराज्ञायशासनम् । तथेत्युक्त्वामहावीर्यश्शयनादुत्पपातह ।।6.60.89।।
explanation: Formidable and courageous Kumbhakarna also got up from sleep saying 'yes' and rose up.

shloka_text: प्रक्षाळ्यवदनंहृष्टस्स्नातःपरमभूषितः । पिपासुस्त्वरयामासपानंबलसमीरणम् ।।6.60.90।।
explanation: Joyful Kumbhakarna, washed his face, had a bath and being thirsty ordered a drink that can increase his strength.

shloka_text: ततस्तेत्वरितास्तत्रराक्षसारावणाज्ञया । मद्यकुम्भांश्चविविधान् क्षिप्रमेवोपहारयन् ।।6.60.91।।
explanation: By the order of Ravana hurriedly they got several kinds of wine in pots.

shloka_text: पीत्वाघटसहस्रेद्वेगमनायोपचक्रमे । ईषत्समुत्कटोमत्तस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः ।।6.60.92।।
explanation: (Kumbhakarna) Having drunk two thousand pots of wine, slightly excited and inebriated and replenished with strength and energy was ready to depart.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णोबभौहृष्टःकालान्तकयमोपमः । भ्रातुस्सभवनंगच्छन्रक्षोबलसमन्वितः ।।6.60.93।। कुम्भकर्णःपदन्यासैरकम्पयतमेन्दिीम् ।
explanation: Kumbhakarna surrounded by Rakshasas going to his brother's abode happily looked like the Lord of death bent on destroying the creation. He took strides which shook the earth.

shloka_text: सराजमार्गंवपुषाप्रकाशयन् सहस्ररश्मिर्धरणीमिवांशुभिः । जगामतत्राञ्जलिमालयावृतश्शतक्रतुर्गेहमिवस्वयम्भुवः ।।6.60.94।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna went like the thousand rayed Sun illuminating the earth by his splendour brightening the royal path, greeted by a circle of Rakshasas joining palms like Indra who has done a hundred sacrifices went to the abode of selfborn Brahma.

shloka_text: तंराजमार्गस्थममित्रघातिनंवनौकसस्तेसहसाबहिस्स्थिताः । दृष्टवाऽप्रमेयंगिरिशृङ्गकल्पंवितत्रसुस्तेहरियूथपालाः ।।6.60.95।।
explanation: And then the Vanaras and the leaders of the Vanara army who were present looked at the immeasurably tall form of Kumbhakarna walking through the royal path and got alarmed.

shloka_text: केचिच्छरण्यंशरणंस्मरामंव्रजन्तिकेचिद् व्यथिताःपतन्ति । केचिद्धशस्मव्यथिताःपतन्तिकेचिद्भयार्ताभुविशेरतेस्म ।।6.60.96।।
explanation: Indeed, some took refuge from Rama who could give shelter, some fell down in panic, some went in all directions in panic, and some out of fear lay down on the ground.

shloka_text: तमद्रिशृङ्गप्रतिमंकिरीटिनंस्पृशन्तमादित्यमिवाऽत्मतेजसा । वनौकसःप्रेक्ष्यविवृद्धमद्भुतं 3 भयार्धितादुद्रुविरेततस्ततः ।।6.60.97।।
explanation: Oppressed with fear the Vanaras ran here and there seeing the form of Kumbhakarna that was like the peak of a mountain as if touching the selfluminous Sun, crowned and wonderful, grown in size. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixtieth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजाधनुरादायवीर्यवान् । किरीटिनंमहाकायंकुम्भकर्णंददर्श ह ।।6.61.1।।
explanation: On taking up a bow Rama saw Kumbhakarna of extraordinary energy, prodigious, and of large body, adorned with a crown.

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंपर्वताकारदर्शनम् । क्रममाणमिवाकाशंपुरानारायणंप्रभुम् ।।6.61.2।।
explanation: That foremost of Rakshasas was like a mountain in appearance, it was like Lord Narayana taking steps to the sky earlier.

shloka_text: सतोयाम्बुदसङ्काशंकाञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम् । दृष्टवापुनःप्रदुद्रवावानराणांमहाचमूः ।।6.61.3।।
explanation: Seeing the Rakshasa who was like a rainy cloud with water, decked with gold ornaments, the commander in chief of Vanaras ran.

shloka_text: विद्रुतांवाहिनींदृष्टवावर्धमानं च राक्षसम् । सविस्मयमिदंरामोविभीषणमुवाच ह ।।6.61.4।।
explanation: Seeing the army scared away and the army of Rakshasas growing in size, Rama was astonished and thus spoke to Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: कोऽसौपर्वतसङ्काशःकिरीटीहरिलोचनः । लङ्कायांदृश्यतेवीरःसविद्युदिवतोयदः ।।6.61.5।।
explanation: "Who is that hero resembling a mountain, a crowned one with tawny eyes, looking like a rainy cloud driven by lightning? He is seen in Lanka."

shloka_text: पृथिव्यांकेतुभूतोऽसौमहानेकोऽत्रदृश्यते । यंदृष्टवावानरास्सर्वेविद्रवन्तिततस्ततः ।।6.61.6।।
explanation: "He is seen here like a lone comet on earth. Seeing him the Vanaras are fleeing hither and thither."

shloka_text: आचक्षवसुमहान् कोऽसौरक्षोवायदिवाऽसुरः । न मयैवंविधंभूतंदृष्टपूर्वंकदाचन ।।6.61.7।।
explanation: "Who is he, that gigantic Rakshasa? Is he a demon or perhaps a colossus? No such being was seen by me earlier."

shloka_text: संपृष्टोराजपुत्रेणरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । विभीषणोमहाप्राज्ञःकाकुत्थ्समिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.61.8।।
explanation: Asked by the prince Rama, of unwearied action, highly intelligent Vibheeshana spoke.

shloka_text: येनवैवस्वतोयुद्धेवासवश्चपराजितः । सैषविश्रवसःपुत्रःकुम्भकर्णःप्रतापवान् ।।6.61.9।। अस्यप्रमाणसदृशोराक्षसाऽन्यो न विद्यते ।
explanation: "Vyvasvatha (Lord of death) as well as Vasava (Indra) were defeated by him in war. He is Kumbhakarna, the son of sage Visrava, a stupendous one and there is no other Rakshasa who equals him in size."

shloka_text: एतेनदेवायुधिदानवाश्चयक्षाभुजङ्गाःपिशिताशनाश्च । गन्धर्वविद्याधरकिन्नरैश्चसहस्रशोराघवसम्प्रभग्नाः ।।6.61.10।।
explanation: "O Raghava! In war Devas, Danavas, Yakshas, Nagas, ogres, Gandharvas, Vidydharas, Kinneras in thousands were defeated by him."

shloka_text: शूलपाणिंविरूपाक्षंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । हन्तुं न शेकुस्त्रिदशाःकालोऽयमितिमोहिताः ।।6.61.11।।
explanation: "This Kumbhakarna with pike in hand and fierce eyes, is mighty strong. All the Devatas could not kill him, deluded that he is death personified."

shloka_text: प्रकृत्याह्येषतेजस्वीकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । अन्येषांराक्षसेन्द्राणांवरदानकृतंबलम् ।।6.61.12।।
explanation: "Kumbhakarna is by nature (by birth) energetic and mighty. The strength of other Rakshasas is on account of their boons received by them."

shloka_text: एतेनजातमात्रेणक्षुधार्तेनमहात्मना । भक्षितानिसहस्राणिसत्त्वानांसुबहून्यपि ।।6.61.13।।
explanation: " As soon as he was born, he was hungry and this great soul being strong consumed thousands of created beings."

shloka_text: तेषुसंभक्षयमाणेषुप्रजाभयनिपीडिताः । यान्तिस्मशरणंशक्रंतमप्यर्थंन्यवेदयन् ।।6.61.14।।
explanation: "In that way when Kumbhakarna was devouring, out of fear all people sought the refuge of Indra and represented."

shloka_text: सकुन्भकर्णंकुपितोमहेन्द्रोजघानवज्रेणशितेनवज्री । सशक्रवज्राभिहतोमहात्माचचालकोपाच्चभृशंननाद ।।6.61.15।।
explanation: "Mahendra who was armed with thunderbolt got enraged and hurt Kumbhakarna with thunderbolt. He reeled and roared with the strike."

shloka_text: तस्यनानद्यमानस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यरक्षसः । श्रुत्वानिनादंवित्रस्ताःभूमिभूयोवितत्रसे ।।6.61.16।।
explanation: "People were already afraid of Kumbhakarna, and after hearing the lion roar of this Rakshasa they were even more scared."

shloka_text: तत्रकोपान्महेन्द्रस्यकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । विकृष्यैरावताद्धन्तंजघानोरसिवासवम् ।।6.61.17।।
explanation: "Then mighty Kumbhakarna, who was enraged, pulled out the tusk of Airavatham and struck at the chest of Indra."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णप्रहारार्तोविजज्वाल स वासवः । ततोविषेदुस्सहसादेवाब्रह्मर्षिदानवाः ।।6.61.18।। प्रजाभिस्सहशक्रश्चययौस्थानंस्वयम्भुवः ।
explanation: "Hit by Kumbhakarna Indra felt tormented. The Devatas, Brahmarshis and Danavas became despondent. Accompanied by created beings they complained to Brahma."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्यदौरात्म्यंशशंसुस्तेप्रजापतेः ।।6.61.19।। प्रजानांभक्षणंचापिधर्षणं च दिवौकसाम् । आश्रमध्वंसनंचापिपरस्त्रीहरणंभृशम् ।।6.61.20।।
explanation: "They reported to Brahma about Kumbhakarna's ruthless deeds, devouring created beings, insulting, harsh and also destroying the abodes of sages violently and abducting others' wives."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्यदौरात्म्यंशशंसुस्तेप्रजापतेः ।।6.61.19।। प्रजानांभक्षणंचापिधर्षणं च दिवौकसाम् । आश्रमध्वंसनंचापिपरस्त्रीहरणंभृशम् ।।6.61.20।।
explanation: "They reported to Brahma about Kumbhakarna's ruthless deeds, devouring created beings, insulting, harsh and also destroying the abodes of sages violently and abducting others' wives."

shloka_text: एवंप्रजायदित्वेषभक्षयिष्यतिनित्यशः । अचिरेणैवकालेनशून्योलोकोभविष्यति ।।6.61.21।।
explanation: "If he consumes created beings every day like that, in the course of time the world will be devoid of beings."

shloka_text: वासवस्यवचश्श्रुत्वासर्वलोकपितामहः । रक्षांस्यावाहयामासकुम्भकर्णंददर्श ह ।।6.61.22।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Indra, Brahma conjured the Rakshasas and saw Kumbhakarna with them.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णंसमीक्ष्यैववितत्रासप्रजापतिः । दृष्टवाविश्वास्यचैवैनंस्वयम्भूरिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.61.23।।
explanation: "Beholding Kumbhakarna, Brahma was alarmed and spoke to him to restore the confidence of Kumbhakarna."

shloka_text: ध्रुवंलोकविनाशायपौलस्त्येनासिनिर्मितः । तस्मात्त्वमद्यप्रभृतिमृतकल्पःशयिष्यसे ।।6.61.24।।
explanation: "Surely you are begotten by Paulastya for the destruction of the universe. Therefore, remain sleeping like a dead one from today, ' said Brahma and cursed him."

shloka_text: ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतोऽथनिपपाताग्रतःप्रभोः । ततःपरमसम्भ्रान्तोरावणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.61.25।।
explanation: "Thereafter, by the curse of Lord Brahma, Kumbhakarna fell in front. Highly agitated at this Ravana spoke these words to Brahma."

shloka_text: विवृद्धःकाञ्चनोवृक्षःफलकालेनिकृत्यते । न नप्तारंस्वकंन्यायंशप्तुमेवंप्रजापते ।।6.61.26।।
explanation: "Oh Brahma! Cutting a golden tree at the stage of fruiting is not fair. It is not proper for you to curse your great grandson in that way."

shloka_text: न मिथ्यावचनश्चत्वंस्वप्स्यत्येष न संशयः । कालस्तुक्रियतामस्यशयनेजागरेतथा ।।6.61.27।।
explanation: "Your words will not become untrue, no doubt. Sleep, he must but waking time may be fixed."

shloka_text: रावणस्यवचश्श्रुत्वास्वयम्भूरिदमब्रवीत् । शयिताह्येषषण्मासानेकाहंजागरिष्यति ।।6.61.28।।
explanation: On hearing Ravana's words, Brahma said" He will sleep for six months and stay awake for a day."

shloka_text: एकेनाह्नात्वसौवीरश्चरन् भूमिंबुभुक्षितः । व्यात्तास्योभक्षयेल्लोकान् सङ्कृद्धइवपावकः ।।6.61.29।।
explanation: "This hero will open his mouth wide and move about and alone he will consume the world like the swollen fire."

shloka_text: सोऽसौव्यसमापन्नःकुम्भकर्णमबोधयत् । त्वत्पराक्रमभीतश्चराजासम्प्रतिरावणः ।।6.61.30।।
explanation: "Overtaken by worry, the king out of fear of your prowess just awakened sleeping Kumbhakarna."

shloka_text: स एषनिर्गतोवीरःशिबिराद्भीमविक्रमः । वानरान्भृशसङ्कृद्धोभक्षयन्परिधावति ।।6.61.31।।
explanation: "This heroic Kumbhakarna has come out of his residence extremely angry and going to and from to consume all Vanaras."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णंसमीक्ष्यैवहरयोऽद्यप्रविद्रुतुः । कथमेनंरणेक्रुद्धंवारयिष्यन्तिवानराः ।।6.61.32।।
explanation: "On merely seeing Kumbhakarna, the monkeys are running away. How will they check him who is enraged in war?"

shloka_text: उच्यन्तांवानराःसर्वेयन्त्रमेतत्समुच्छ्रितम् । इतिविज्ञायहरयोभविष्यन्तीहनिर्भयाः ।।6.61.33।।
explanation: "Let all the Vanaras be told, that this one standing high is a machine then the Vanaras will not be scared of victory."

shloka_text: विभीषणवचश्श्रुत्वाहेतुमत्सुमुखेरितम् । उवाचराघवोवाक्यंनीलंसेनापतिंतदा ।।6.61.34।।
explanation: Hearing the words of Vibheeshana, which was reasonable and, in their favour, Raghava said this to Nila, the commander in chief of the army.

shloka_text: गच्छसैन्यानिसर्वाणिव्यूह्यतिष्ठस्वपावके । द्वाराण्यादायलङ्कायाश्चर्याश्चाप्यथसङ्क्रमान् ।।6.61.35।।
explanation: "Pavaka, go and organize all the army and get together to occupy all the gates, highways, bridges in Lanka."

shloka_text: शैलशृङ्गाणिवृक्षांश्चशिलाश्चाप्युपसंहर । तिष्ठन्तुसायुधास्सर्वेसायुधाश्शैलपाणयः ।।6.61.36।।
explanation: "Be ready staying on mountain tops, trees, rocks armed with weapons and rocks in hand."

shloka_text: राघवेणसमादिष्टोनीलोहरिचमूपतिः । शशासवानरानीकंयथावत्कपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.61.37।।
explanation: As instructed by Raghava, the monkey leader Nila, elephant among the monkeys, ordered the monkey troops as instructed.

shloka_text: ततोगवाक्षश्शरभोहनूमानङ्गदस्तथा । शैलशृङ्गाणिशैलाभागृहीत्वाद्वारमभ्ययुः ।।6.61.38।।
explanation: Then taking mountains, Gavaksha, Sarabha, Hanuman, Angada who looked like mountains themselves marched to the gate.

shloka_text: रामवाक्यमुपश्रुत्य हरयो जितकाशिनः । पादपैरर्दयवनीरावानराःपरवाहिनीम् ।।6.61.39।।
explanation: The monkeys desiring to be triumphant, took trees and began to strike at the enemies on hearing Rama's control.

shloka_text: ततोहरीणांतदनीकमुग्रंरराजशैलोद्यतदीप्तहस्तम् । गिरेःसमीपानुगतंयथैवहन्महाम्भोधरजालमुग्रम् ।।6.61.40।।
explanation: Then Vanaras taking trees and mountains in their shining hand s marching close to each other seemed like a huge mass of terrible clouds hanging close to a mountain. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty first sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स तुराक्षसशार्दूलोनिद्रामदसमाकुलः । राजमार्गंश्रियाजुष्टंययौविपुलविक्रमः ।।6.62.1।।
explanation: He (Kumbhakaran), who was endowed with indomitable prowess, a tiger among Rakshasas, was sleepy and inebriated, marched along the splendid royal path.

shloka_text: राक्षसानांसहस्रैश्चवृतःपरमदुर्जयः । गृहेभ्यःपुष्पवर्षेणकीर्यमाणस्तदाययौ ।।6.62.2।।
explanation: Then, Kumbhakarna, who is very difficult to win over, walked violently surrounded by Rakshasas, covered with showers of flowers from houses.

shloka_text: स हेमजालविततंभानुभास्वरदर्शनम् । ददर्शविपुलंरम्यंराक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम् ।।6.62.3।।
explanation: He saw the vast abode of the king of Rakshasas, with lattice work of gold and looking bright like the morning Sun

shloka_text: स तत्तदासूर्यइवाभ्रजालंप्रविश्यरक्षोधिपतेर्निवेशम् । ददर्शदूरेऽग्रजमासनस्थंस्वयम्भुवंशक्रवासनस्थम् ।।6.62.4।।
explanation: He saw entering the abode of Lord of Rakshasas like the Sun penetrating into a mass of clouds, from a distance his elder brother seated on the throne just like Indra saw the SelfBorn Brahma on the throne.

shloka_text: भ्रातुस्सभवनंगच्छन्रक्षोगणसमन्विम् । कुम्भकर्णःपदन्यासैरकम्पयतमेदिनीम् ।।6.62.5।।
explanation: While Kumbhakarna accompanied by troops of Rakshasas, was taking strides to his brother's abode, even the earth was shaken.

shloka_text: सोऽभिगम्यगृहंभ्रातुःकक्ष्यामभिविगाह्य च । ददर्शोद्विगन्नमासीनंविमानेपुष्पकेगुरुम् ।।6.62.6।।
explanation: Having gone to his brother's residence, stepping into the enclosure, he saw his brother seated in a perturbed state.

shloka_text: अथदृष्टवादशग्रीवःकुम्भकर्णमुपस्थितम् । तूर्णमुत्थायसंहृष्टःसन्निकर्षमुपानयत् ।।6.62.7।।
explanation: The ten headed Ravana seeing Kumbhakarna, was delighted and got up quickly and made him come close to him.

shloka_text: अथासीनस्यपर्यङ्केकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । भ्रातुर्ववन्देचरणौकिंकृत्यमितिचाब्रवीत् ।।6.62.8।।
explanation: Getting up from his seat, Kumbhakarna endowed with extraordinary might bowed down and clasped his brother's feet and asked him, what task he had to do?

shloka_text: उत्पत्यचैनंमुदितोरावणःपरिषस्वजे । स भ्रात्रासम्परिष्वक्तोयथावच्छाभिनन्दितः ।।6.62.9।। कुम्भकर्णश्शुभंदिव्यंप्रतिपेदेवरासनम् ।
explanation: Getting up from his seat Ravana embraced and greeted Kumbhakarna. So also, he duly rejoiced and occupied the seat.

shloka_text: स तदासनमाश्रित्यकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.62.10।। संरक्तनयनःक्रोधाद्रावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Mighty Kumbhakarna, duly took the seat. Enraged Ravana with blood shot eyes spoke these words.

shloka_text: किमर्थमहमादृत्यत्वयाराजन्विबोधितः ।।6.62.11।। शंसकस्माद्भयंतेऽत्रकोऽद्यप्रेतोभविष्यति ।
explanation: "O King! For what purpose have I been awakened by you? Whom are you fearing? I wish to know who is to be ceased in life?"

shloka_text: भ्रातरंरावणःक्रुद्धंकुम्भकर्णमवस्थितम् ।।6.62.12।। ईषत्तुपरिवृत्ताभ्यांनेत्राभ्यांवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, was overcome with anger, and asked his brother Ravana, who was seated and rolling his eyes in anger.

shloka_text: अद्यतेसुमहान्कालश्शयानस्यमहाबल ।।6.62.13।। सुखितस्त्वं न जानीषेममरामकृतंभयम् ।
explanation: "Oh! Kumbhakarna of extraordinary prowess! You were asleep for long happily. You do not know that I am afraid of Rama."

shloka_text: एषदाशरथीरामःसुग्रीवसहितोबली ।।6.62.14।। समुद्रंसबलस्तीर्त्वामूलंनःपरिकृन्तति ।
explanation: "Rama, the son of Dasaratha accompanied by Sugriva, crossed the ocean with an army that was cutting our roots."

shloka_text: हन्तपश्यस्वलङ्कायावनान्युपवनानि च ।।6.62.15।। सेतुनासुखमागम्यवानरैकार्णवीकृतम् ।
explanation: " Alas! You see how the Vanaras, arriving at Lanka, crossing the bridge have done away with groves and gardens."

shloka_text: येराक्षसामुख्यतमाहतास्तेवानरैर्युधि ।।6.62.16।। वानराणांक्षयंयुद्धे न पश्यामिकदाचन । नचापिवानरायुद्धेजितपूर्वाःकदाचन ।।6.62.17।।
explanation: "Of the Rakshasas, the chiefs have been killed in war by Vanaras. But I did not see even one Vanara to have been killed in war. Vanaras have not failed to succeed in war."

shloka_text: येराक्षसामुख्यतमाहतास्तेवानरैर्युधि ।।6.62.16।। वानराणांक्षयंयुद्धे न पश्यामिकदाचन । नचापिवानरायुद्धेजितपूर्वाःकदाचन ।।6.62.17।।
explanation: "Of the Rakshasas, the chiefs have been killed in war by Vanaras. But I did not see even one Vanara to have been killed in war. Vanaras have not failed to succeed in war."

shloka_text: तदेतद्भयमुत्पन्नंत्रायस्वेमांमहबल । नाशयत्वमिमानद्यतदर्थंबोधितोभवान् ।।6.62.18।।
explanation: "Mighty strong I am, but such is the fear that has been created in me from them. You have been awakened, to destroy them. Reported Ravana."

shloka_text: सर्वक्षपितकोशं च स त्वमभ्यवपद्यमाम् । त्रायस्वेमांपुरींलङ्कांबालवृद्धावशेषिताम् ।।6.62.19।।
explanation: " All resources of mine are exhausted. These children and aged are only left in Lanka city, knowing that you will save the city of Lanka."

shloka_text: भ्रातुरर्थेमहाबाहो कुरुकर्मसुदुष्करम् । मयैवंनोक्तपूर्वोहिकश्चिद्भ्रातः परन्तप ।।6.62.20।।
explanation: "O broad shouldered brother! Do this task which is difficult for others. O Scourge of enemies! I have not asked you before for such a task."

shloka_text: त्वय्यस्तिममस्नेहःपरासम्भावना च मे । दैवासुरेषुयुद्धेषुबहुशोराक्षसर्षभ ।।6.62.21।। त्वयादेवाःप्रतिव्यूह्यनिर्जिताश्चासुरायुधि ।
explanation: "O Bull among Rakshasas! Being my brother, do this for me. I always have affection for you. Considering that you have encountered war with Devas and Asuras and won both Devas and Asuras, do this help."

shloka_text: तदेतत्सर्वमातिष्ठवीर्यंभीमपराक्रम ।।6.62.22।। न हितेसर्वभूतेषुदृश्यतेसदृशोबली ।
explanation: "O Brother of fierce valour! Get up. I have not seen anyone stronger than you among all beings."

shloka_text: कुरुष्वमेप्रियहितमेतदुत्तमंयथाप्रियंप्रियरणबान्धवप्रिय । स्वतेजसाविधमसपत्नवाहिनींशरद्घनंपवनइवोद्यतोमहान् ।।6.62.23।।
explanation: "You are a lover of wars. You are a lover of relations. You are always my dear well wisher. O self glorious one! Do this task of throwing out the torrent army just like wind throws rainy clouds." ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty second sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्यराक्षसराजस्यनिशम्यपरिदेवितम् । कुम्भकर्णोबभाषेदंवचनंप्रजहास च ।।6.63.1।।
explanation: Hearing the lament of the Rakshasa king, Kumbhakarna replied laughing.

shloka_text: दृष्टोदोषोहियोऽस्माभिःपुरामन्त्रन्वििर्णये । हितेष्वनभियुक्तेनसोऽयमासादितस्त्वया ।।6.63.2।।
explanation: "While we were discussing earlier and taking decisions, that disaster foreseen by me has reaped for having not trusted the well wishers."

shloka_text: शीघ्रंखल्वभ्युपेतंत्वांफलंपापस्यकर्मणः । निरयेष्वेवपतनंयथादुष्कृतकर्मणः ।।6.63.3।।
explanation: "Those who do sinful deeds fall unobstructed so also the fruit of your sinful action has come upon you."

shloka_text: प्रथमंवैमहाराजकृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम् । केवलंवीर्यदर्पेणनानुबन्धोविचिन्तितः ।।6.63.4।।
explanation: "O king! All this action was not thought of at the beginning, nor the consequences of action weighed in the pride of your prowess."

shloka_text: यःपश्चातूर्वकार्याणिकुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः । पूर्वंचोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेदनयानया ।।6.63.5।।
explanation: "Confident of prosperity, he who defers action earlier, he does not know what is right and wrong later on."

shloka_text: देशकालविहीनानिकर्माणिविपरीतवत् । क्रियमाणानिदुष्यन्तिहवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव ।।6.63.6।।
explanation: " Actions performed without regard for time and place will be disastrous like the oblations offered into fire without consecration, gets wasted."

shloka_text: त्रयाणांपञ्चधायोगंकर्मणांयःप्रपश्यति । सचिवैस्समयंकृत्वा स सभ्येवर्ततेपथि ।।6.63.7।।
explanation: He who thinks with ministers and considers the five aspects of threefold duties and moves in the right path performs (Five aspects of action are the method of initiating action, material to be worked upon, time and place of action, provision against mischance and the chances of success). Threefold duties with reference to enemies are Sama, Daana, and Bedha."

shloka_text: यथागमं च योराजासमयंविचिकीर्षति । बुध्यतेसचिवान्बध्यासुहृदश्चानुपश्यति ।।6.63.8।।
explanation: "The king who does his duty in time in accordance with justice and thinking intelligently with his ministers, understands rightly."

shloka_text: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च सर्वान्वारक्षसांपते । भजतेपुरुषःकालेत्रीणिद्वन्द्वानिवापुनः ।।6.63.9।।
explanation: "O Rakshasa king! A man should pursue his duty or worldly gain or sensual pleasures all the three combined or at least any two in time (the scriptures lay down that duty should be pursued in the morning, wealth in the afternoon and sensual pleasures at night)."

shloka_text: त्रिषुचैतेषुयच्छ्रेष्ठंश्रुत्वातन्नावबुध्यते । राजावाराजमात्रोवाव्यर्थंतस्यबहुश्रुतम् ।।6.63.10।।
explanation: " A sovereign king or a king hearing these three does not recognize the best of the three is in vain even though he heard many."

shloka_text: उपप्रदानंसान्त्वं च भेदंकाले च विक्रमम् । योगं च रक्षसांश्रेष्ठतावुभौ च नयानयौ ।।6.63.11।। कालेधर्मार्थकामान्यस्सम्मन्त्ऱ्यसचिवैःसह । निषेवेतात्मवान्लोके न स व्यसनमाप्नुयात् ।।6.63.12।।
explanation: "You are the foremost of the Rakshasas! After discussing with ministers, a king either by gifting or conciliation or dissension or resorting to all of them at the appropriate time takes resort to pursue virtue, wealth, or sensual pleasures at the right time, never meets with sorrow."

shloka_text: उपप्रदानंसान्त्वं च भेदंकाले च विक्रमम् । योगं च रक्षसांश्रेष्ठतावुभौ च नयानयौ ।।6.63.11।। कालेधर्मार्थकामान्यस्सम्मन्त्ऱ्यसचिवैःसह । निषेवेतात्मवान्लोके न स व्यसनमाप्नुयात् ।।6.63.12।।
explanation: "You are the foremost of the Rakshasas! After discussing with ministers, a king either by gifting or conciliation or dissension or resorting to all of them at the appropriate time takes resort to pursue virtue, wealth, or sensual pleasures at the right time, never meets with sorrow."

shloka_text: हितानुबन्धमालोच्यकार्यात्कार्यमिहात्मनः । राजासहार्थतत्त्वज्ञैस्सचिवैर्बुस्सहिजीवति ।।6.63.13।।
explanation: "That king who knows the reality of things and makes decisions in consultation with his ministers, who make their living with their intelligence will live happily."

shloka_text: अनभिज्ञायशास्त्रार्थान् पुरुषाःपशुबुद्धयः । प्रागल्भ्याद्वक्तुमिच्छन्तिमन्त्रेष्वभ्यन्तरीकृताः ।।6.63.14।।
explanation: "People whose intelligence level is no better than animals, who have been included to express their views, who do not know the meaning of shastras express their views out of impudence."

shloka_text: अशास्त्रविदुषांतेषां न कार्यमभिहितंवचः । अर्थशास्त्रानभिज्ञानांविपुलांश्रियमिच्छताम् ।।6.63.15।।
explanation: "Those who have no knowledge of shastras are ignorant of the science of wealth and desire huge wealth. Their advice ought not to be followed."

shloka_text: अहितं च हिताकारंधार्ष्ट्याज्जल्पन्तियेनराः । अवेक्ष्यमन्त्रबाह्यास्तेकर्तव्याःकृत्यदूषणा:।। 6.63.16।।
explanation: "Those who tender advice, which is unwholesome but in wholesome grab, out of their impudence should be kept away from discussion examining early as they mar the purpose."

shloka_text: विनाशयन्तोभर्तारंसहिताश्शत्रुभिर्बुधैः । विपरीतानिकृत्यानिकारयन्तीहमन्त्रिणः ।।6.63.17।।
explanation: "Some ministers in order to ruin the king, collide with enemies and make the king take wrong actions."

shloka_text: तान्भर्तामित्रसङ्काशानमित्रान्मन्त्रनिर्णये । व्यवहारेणजानीयात्सचिवानुपसम्हितान् ।।6.63.18।।
explanation: " A ruler should know those ministers bribed by the enemy, who have become close to the enemy and appear as friends. Those ministers must be known through their behaviour in the deliberations."

shloka_text: चपलस्येहकृत्यानिसहसानुप्रधावतः । छिद्रमन्येप्रपद्यन्तेक्रौञ्चस्य ख मिवद्विजाः ।।6.63.19।।
explanation: "Enemies find out the weakness of the king who is unsteady and rush after the actions forcibly without thinking like brahmins just as birds find the holes in Krauncha mountain and elaborate to others."

shloka_text: योहिशत्रुमवज्ञायनात्मानमभिरक्षति । अवाप्नोतिहिसोऽनर्थान् स्थानाच्चव्यवरोप्यते ।।6.63.20।।
explanation: "He who knowing fully the actions of the enemy does not protect himself he attains reverses and is also dragged down from position."

shloka_text: यदुक्तमिहतेपूर्वंक्रियतामनुजेन च । तदेवनोहितंवाक्यंयदिच्छसि च तत्कुरु ।।6.63.21।।
explanation: "The advice given to you in the past by your brother alone is good. That is good for you. Or you may do what you wish."

shloka_text: तत्तुश्रुत्वादशग्रीवःकुम्भकर्णस्यभाषितम् । भ्रुकुटिंचैवसञ्चक्रेक्रुद्धश्चैनमभाषत ।।6.63.22।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna having spoken that way, the ten headed Ravana frowned, shaking his eyebrows in anger and spoke this way.

shloka_text: मान्योगुरुवारिचार्यःकिमांत्वमनुशाससि । किमेवंवाक्छ्रमंकृत्वाकालेयुक्तंविधीयताम् ।।6.63.23।।
explanation: "Why do you, who are worthy of respect, instruct me like a father or teacher? These words express your cleverness in speaking. It is time to do what is appropriate now. Follow what is to be done."

shloka_text: विभ्रमाच्चित्तमोहाद्वाबलवीर्याश्रयेणवा । नाभिपन्नमिदानींयद्व्यर्थातस्यपुनःकथाः ।।6.63.24।।
explanation: "Due to delusion, or lack of understanding or due to pride of my strength I did something. To talk of it now again is futile."

shloka_text: अस्मिन्कालेतुयद्युक्तंतदिदानींविधीयताम् । गतंतुनानुशोचन्तिगतंतुगतमेवहि ।।6.63.25।।
explanation: "You may speak of only what is proper to do now. Do not think of the past as it is gone."

shloka_text: ममापनयजंदोषंविक्रमेणसमीकुरु । यदिखल्वस्तिमेस्नेहोविक्रमंवाऽवगच्छसि ।।6.63.26।। यदिवकार्यंमेतत्तेहृदिकार्यतमंमतम् ।
explanation: "If at all there is any affection in you for me now, you recognize your strengths and think what action is justified in your heart. You may nullify the evil that sprung from my heart."

shloka_text: स सुहृद्योविपन्नार्थंदीनमभ्यवपद्यते ।।6.63.27।। स बन्धुर्योऽपनीतेषुसाहाय्यायोपकल्पते ।
explanation: " A friend is one who helps when one's fortune is lost and is desperate. Deviating from morals the one who is prepared to help is a relation."

shloka_text: तमथैवंब्रुवाणंतुवचनंधीरदारुणम् ।।6.63.28।। रुष्टोऽयमितिविज्ञायशनैश्श्लक्षणमुवाच ह ।
explanation: Thereafter knowing that Ravana is agitated and arguing in a grave and harsh manner, Kumbhakarna, spoke slowly in a gentle tone.

shloka_text: अतीवहिसमालक्ष्यभ्रातरंक्षुभितेन्द्रियम् ।।6.63.29।। कुम्भकर्णश्शनैर्वाक्यंबभाषेपरिसान्त्वयन् ।
explanation: Sensing that Ravana is disturbed very much, Kumbhakarna taking hold of the brother and consoling him slowly said these words.

shloka_text: शृणुराजन्नवहितोममवाक्यमरिन्दम ।।6.63.30।। अलंराक्षसराजेन्द्र सन्तापमुपपद्यते । रोषं च सम्परित्यज्यस्वस्थोभवितुमर्हसि ।।6.63.31।।
explanation: "Listen to my words, Rakshasa king! You are a scourge of enemies. Put aside this sorrow. Give up the agony also. Be normal. You ought to be your normal self again."

shloka_text: शृणुराजन्नवहितोममवाक्यमरिन्दम ।।6.63.30।। अलंराक्षसराजेन्द्र सन्तापमुपपद्यते । रोषं च सम्परित्यज्यस्वस्थोभवितुमर्हसि ।।6.63.31।।
explanation: "Listen to my words, Rakshasa king! You are a scourge of enemies. Put aside this sorrow. Give up the agony also. Be normal. You ought to be your normal self again."

shloka_text: नैतन्मनसिकर्तव्यंमयिजीवतिपार्थिव । तमहंनाशयिष्यामियत्कृतेपरितप्यते ।।6.63.32।।
explanation: "While I am (my body is) with life you need not entertain despondency. I will exterminate him, by whose account you are agitated."

shloka_text: अवश्यंतुहितंवाच्यंसर्वावस्थांतवमया । बन्धुभावादभिहितंभ्रातृस्नेहाच्छपार्थिव ।।6.63.33।।
explanation: "O king! I will give you good advice in all circumstances being a relation. Salutary advice has been given to you out of brotherly affection."

shloka_text: सदृशंयत्तुकालेऽस्मिन् कर्तुंस्निग्धेनबन्धुना । शत्रूणांकदनंपश्यक्रियमाणंमयारणे ।।6.63.34।।
explanation: " At this time, you will see a relation doing that which is right out of affection. All enemies will be destroyed."

shloka_text: अद्यपश्यमहाबाहो मयासमरमूर्धनि । हतेरामेसहभ्रात्राद्रवन्तींहरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.63.35।।
explanation: "O mighty armed King! You see Rama along with his brother being killed by me and Vanaras fleeing away from the forefront of war."

shloka_text: अद्यरामस्यतद्दृष्टवामयानीतंरणाच्छिरः । सुखीभवमहाबाहो सीताभवतुदुःखिता ।।6.63.36।।
explanation: "Be happy today, O Mighty armed brother! I will bring Rama's head from the battlefield. Sita will be sad. You will see."

shloka_text: अद्यरामस्यपश्यन्तुनिधनंसुमहत्प्रियम् । लङ्कायांराक्षसाःसर्वेयेतेनिहतबान्धवाः ।।6.63.37।।
explanation: " All the Rakshasas in Lanka whose relations have been killed will witness Rama's death which will be very welcome."

shloka_text: अद्यशोकपरीतानांस्वबन्धुवधकारणात् । शत्रोर्युधिविनाशेनकरोम्यस्रप्रमार्जनम् ।।6.63.38।।
explanation: Now I will wipe the tears of Rakshasas who lost their kin and are bewailing their loss.

shloka_text: अद्यपर्वतसङ्काशंससूर्यमिवतोयदम् । विकीर्णंपश्यसमरेसुग्रीवंप्लवगोत्तम ।।6.63.39।।
explanation: "Now you will see Sugriva the foremost of monkeys in mountain shape, resembling mountains bathed in blood like evening Sun illumined like the cloud."

shloka_text: कथं च राक्षसैरेभिर्मया च परिरक्षितः । जिघांसुभिर्दाशरथिं वध्यसे त्वमिहानघ ।।6.63.40।।
explanation: "O Sinless Ravana! As I am going to kill this son of Dasaratha whom Rakshasas are intending to kill, how can Rama kill you now?"

shloka_text: मांनिहत्यकिलत्वांहिनिहनिष्यतिराघवः । नाहमात्मनिसन्तापंगच्छेयंराक्षसाधिप ।।6.63.41।।
explanation: "Rakshasa king! Raghava will kill you only after killing me. Never give way for distress."

shloka_text: कामंवतिदानीमपिमांव्यादिशत्वंपरन्तप । न परःप्रेषणीयस्तेयुद्धायातुलविक्रम ।।6.63.42।।
explanation: "Command me to wage war at this moment, O Scorcher of enemies. There is no one better than me to be sought for O hero endowed with extraordinary strength."

shloka_text: अहमुत्सादयिष्यामिशत्रूंस्तवमहाबल: । यदिशक्रोयदियमोयदिपावकमारुतौ ।।6.63.43।। तानहंयोधयिष्यामिकुबेरवरुणावपि ।
explanation: "I shall exterminate your enemies, however mighty they may be. I can contend with Indra or fire god or Yama or wind god, Kubera or even Varuna."

shloka_text: गिरिमात्रशरीरस्यशितशूलधरस्यमे ।।6.63.44।। नर्दतस्तीक्षणदंष्ट्रस्यबिभीयाच्चपुरन्दरः ।
explanation: "Even Indra with a body as big as a mountain, with pointed teeth like a spike, with sharp teeth will fear me and run if I roar.

shloka_text: अथवात्यक्तशस्त्रस्यमृद्नतस्तरसारिपून् ।।6.63.45।। न मेप्रतिमुखेस्थातुंकश्चित् शक्तोजिजीविषुः ।
explanation: "Or else giving up weapons and swords using my arms indeed I can crush, and no one can stand in front of me."

shloka_text: नैवशक्त्या न गदयानासिनानिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.63.46।। हस्ताभ्यामेवसम्रब्दोहनिष्याम्यपिवज्रिणम् ।
explanation: "I shall not fight with javelin or mace or sword or sharp arrows. Enraged, alone I can strike down even Indra."

shloka_text: यदिमेमुष्टिवेगं स राघवोऽद्यसहिष्यते ।।6.63.47।। ततःपाश्यन्तिबाणौघारुधिरंराघवस्यतु ।
explanation: "Now if that Raghava can withstand the force of my fists, you will see volleys of Rama's arrows will drink my blood."

shloka_text: चिन्तयाबाध्यसेराजन्किमर्थंमयितिष्ठति ।।6.63.48।। सोऽहंशत्रुविनाशाय तव निर्यातुमुद्यतः ।
explanation: "O King! while I am here for what reason do you worry and have anxiety? I will go now and decidedly destroy your enemy."

shloka_text: मुञ्चरामाद्भयंराज न्हनिष्यामीहसम्युगे ।।6.63.49।। राघवंलक्ष्मणंचैवसुग्रीवं च महाबलम् । हनूमन्तं च रक्षोघ्नंलङ्कायेनप्रदीपिता ।।6.63.50।।
explanation: "O King! Give up the fear, as both Rama and Lakshmana will be made short of work in the battlefield, as also mighty Sugriva and dispose of Hanuman, the destroyer of many Rakshasas and who set fire to Lanka."

shloka_text: मुञ्चरामाद्भयंराज न्हनिष्यामीहसम्युगे ।।6.63.49।। राघवंलक्ष्मणंचैवसुग्रीवं च महाबलम् । हनूमन्तं च रक्षोघ्नंलङ्कायेनप्रदीपिता ।।6.63.50।।
explanation: "O King! Give up the fear, as both Rama and Lakshmana will be made short of work in the battlefield, as also mighty Sugriva and dispose of Hanuman, the destroyer of many Rakshasas and who set fire to Lanka."

shloka_text: हरींश्चापिहनियिष्यामिसंयुगेसमवास्थिवान् । असाधारणमिच्छामिनदातुंमहद्यशः ।।6.63.51।।
explanation: "I will remain steady in the battlefield and devour monkeys also. I wish to confer an unusual and great glory on you."

shloka_text: तदिचेन्द्राद्भयं राजन्यदि चापिस्वयम्भुवः । ततोऽहंनाशयिष्यामिनैशंतमइवांशुमान् ।।6.63.52।। अपिदेवाश्शयिष्यन्तेक्रुद्धेमयिमहीतले ।
explanation: "Even if there is fear of Indra and Brahma that haunts you, I shall destroy them away like the sun dispels darkness. Devas will fall flat on earth when I am enraged."

shloka_text: यमं च शमयिष्यामिभक्षयिष्यामिपावकम् ।।6.63.53।। आदित्यंपातयिष्यामिसनक्षत्रंमहीतले ।
explanation: "I shall quell Lord Yama also, devour fire god, make the Sun including stars fall on earth."

shloka_text: शतक्रतुंवधिष्यामिपास्यामिवरुणालयम् ।।6.63.54।। पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामिदारयिष्यामिमेदिनीम् ।
explanation: "I shall kill Indra who has done a hundred sacrifices, drink up the ocean the abode of Varuna, crush the mountains totally, and break the earth."

shloka_text: दीर्घकालंप्रसुप्तस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यविक्रमम् ।।6.63.55।। अद्यपश्यन्तुभूतानिभक्ष्यमाणानिसर्वशः । नन्विदंत्रिदिवंसर्वमाहारस्य न पूर्यते ।।6.63.56।।
explanation: " All beings all over will be eaten now. For a long time Kumbhakarna was sleeping. Now you will see that the food of all the three worlds, earth, heaven and intermediate region will not be enough to fill my stomach."

shloka_text: दीर्घकालंप्रसुप्तस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यविक्रमम् ।।6.63.55।। अद्यपश्यन्तुभूतानिभक्ष्यमाणानिसर्वशः । नन्विदंत्रिदिवंसर्वमाहारस्य न पूर्यते ।।6.63.56।।
explanation: " All beings all over will be eaten now. For a long time Kumbhakarna was sleeping. Now you will see that the food of all the three worlds, earth, heaven and intermediate region will not be enough to fill my stomach."

shloka_text: वधेनतेदाशरथेःसुखार्हंसुखंसमाहर्तुमहंव्रजामि । निहत्यरामंसहलक्ष्मणेनखादामिन्हरियूथमुख्यान् ।।6.63.57।।
explanation: "Through the destruction of Rama, I will bring happiness to you who are worthy of happiness. I will collect Rama along with Lakshmana and all the Vanara leaders and devour all."

shloka_text: तदुक्तमतिकायस्यबलिनोबाहुशालिनः । कुम्भकर्णस्यवचनंश्रुत्वोवाचमहोदरः ।।6.64.1।।
explanation: Hearing the words of mighty Kumbhakarna, of massive body and round arms Mahodara said.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णकुलेजातोधृष्टःप्राकृतदर्शनः । अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषिकृत्यंसर्वत्रवेदितुम् ।।6.64.2।।
explanation: "Kumbhakarna! Although you are born of noble race, you are insolent, seeing your low intellect in all aspects you have no knowledge of what should be done or not to be done."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णकुलेजातोधृष्टःप्राकृतदर्शनः । अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषिकृत्यंसर्वत्रवेदितुम् ।।6.64.2।।
explanation: "Kumbhakarna! Although you are born of noble race, you are insolent, seeing your low intellect in all aspects you have no knowledge of what should be done or not to be done."

shloka_text: स्थानंवृद्धिं च हानि च देशकालविभागवित् । आत्मनश्चपरेषां च बुध्यतेराक्षसर्षभः ।।6.64.4।।
explanation: "Ravana, a bull among Rakshasas is conversant with rules of time and place and knows his own enemies, his progress and decline also."

shloka_text: यत्तुशक्यंबलवताकर्तुंप्राकृतबुद्धिना । अनुपासितवृद्धेनकःकुर्यात्तादृशंनरः ।।6.64.5।।
explanation: " A strong person of unsophisticated intellect, who is progressive, a knower of everything will do such a task which is not possible to do?"

shloka_text: यांस्तुधर्मार्थकामांस्त्वंब्रवीषिपृथगाश्रयान् । अवबोद्धुंस्वभावेतान्नहिलक्षणमस्तितान् ।।6.64.6।।
explanation: "The virtues, worldly gain and sensuous pleasures give results separately as you said. They are incompatible with what you said and that it is its nature you said. what is the proof?"

shloka_text: कर्मचैवहिसर्वेषांकारणानांप्रयोजकम् । श्रेयःपापीयसांचात्रफलंभवतिकर्मणाम् ।।6.64.7।।
explanation: " Actions alone are the means of happiness. Being so how can sinful actions accrue good results?"

shloka_text: निश्श्रेयसफलावेवधर्मार्थावितरावपि । अधर्मानर्थयोःप्राप्तिःफलं च प्रत्यवायिकम् ।।6.64.8।।
explanation: " All virtues and worldly pleasures and even otherwise give only benefit. But if done with disinterest and unrighteousness it can give a result which is other than prosperity."

shloka_text: ऐहलौकिकपारक्यंकर्मपुम्भिर्निषेव्यते । कर्माण्यपितुकल्यानिलभतेकाममास्थितः ।।6.64.9।।
explanation: " All beings reap the fruit of their actions in this world as well as in other worlds. He, who remains to be pleasure seeking, devoted to actions will receive blessings and attain pleasures in this life only (not here after)."

shloka_text: तत्रक्लुप्तमिदंराज्ञाहृदिकार्यंमतं च नः । शत्रौहिसाहसंयत्स्यात्किमिवात्रापनीयते ।।6.64.10।।
explanation: " At that time the king intended in his heart (to abduct Sita), and we approved his action, and it was done. What is wrong in doing such a courageous action against an enemy?"

shloka_text: एकस्यैवाभियानेतुहेतुर्यःकथितस्त्वया । तत्राप्यनुपपन्नंतेवक्ष्यामियदसाधु च ।।6.64.11।।
explanation: "You have set out alone (for war) and the reason adduced by you is ill conceived and improper. I shall tell you."

shloka_text: येनपूर्वंजनस्थानेबहवोऽतिबलाहताः । राक्षसाराघवंतंत्वंकथमेकोजयिष्यसि ।।6.64.12।।
explanation: "How is it possible for you single handed to win Raghava of exceeding might, who killed many Rakshasas in the past at Janasthana?"

shloka_text: येपुरानिर्जितास्तेनजनस्थानेमहौजसः । राक्षसांस्तान्पुरेसर्वान्भीतानद्यापिपश्यसि ।।6.64.13।।
explanation: "Look! Those highly energetic Rakshasas, who were won by Rama at Janasthana are scared of him even now."

shloka_text: तंसिंहमिवसङ्क्रुद्धंरामंदशरथात्मजम् । सर्पंसुप्तमिवबुद्ध्यप्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि ।।6.64.14।।
explanation: "Do you desire to awaken Rama, who is like an enraged lion knowingly, who is like a sleeping snake?"

shloka_text: ज्वलन्तंतेजसानित्यंक्रोधेन च दुरासदम् । कस्तंमृत्युमिवासह्यमासादयितुमर्हति ।।6.64.15।।
explanation: "Who can dare to approach Rama, who is difficult to encounter, unbearable and burning in anger like the spirit of death."

shloka_text: संशयस्थमिदंसर्वंशत्रोःप्रतिसमासने । एकस्यगमनंतत्र न हिमेरोचतेभृशम् ।।6.64.16।।
explanation: "Face to face with the enemy this total army will be in danger. You're going alone is certainly not desirable."

shloka_text: हीनार्थस्तुसमृद्धार्थंकोरिपुंप्राकृतंयथा । निश्चित्यजीवितत्यागेवशमानेतुमिच्छति ।।6.64.17।।
explanation: "How can a weak person desire to go to the enemy who is rich in resources, determined to sacrifice his life several times and submit himself?"
