shloka_text: यस्यनास्तिमनुष्येषुसदृशोराक्षसोत्तम । कथमाशंससेयोद्धुंतुल्येनेन्द्रविवस्वतोः ।।6.64.18।।
explanation: "O Best of Rakshasas! How would you enter into combat with one who is great among all human beings and while even Indra and Sun God are not equal to him in war?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुसम्रब्दःकुम्भकर्णंमहोदरः । उवाचरक्षसांमध्येरावणंलोकरावणम् ।।6.64.19।।
explanation: Mahodara having spoken to agitated Kumbhakarna in the midst of Rakshasas in this way, submitted to Ravana, who makes people cry.

shloka_text: लब्ध्वापुनस्त्वंवैदेहींकिमर्थंसम्प्रजल्पसि । यदीच्छसितदासीतावशगातेभविष्यति ।।6.64.20।।
explanation: "Having got Vaidehi, why are you talking like that? Sita will submit to you if you desire."

shloka_text: दृष्टःकश्चदुपायोमेसीतोपस्थानकारकः । रुचितश्चेत्स्वयाबुध्याराक्षसेन्द्र तंशृणु ।।6.64.21।।
explanation: "O King of Rakshasas! A means of bringing her round is known to me. Listen, think over with your intellect."

shloka_text: अहंद्विजिह्वस्सम्ह्रादीकुम्भकर्णोवितर्दनः । पञ्चरामवधायैतेनिर्यान्त्वित्यवघोषय ।।6.64.22।।
explanation: "You pronounce that I, Dwijihva, Samhradri, Kumbhakarna and Vitardana, five of us will go forth to kill Rama."

shloka_text: ततोगत्वावयंयुद्धंदास्यामस्तस्ययत्नतः । जेष्यामोयदितेशत्रून्नोपायैःकृत्यमस्तिनः ।।6.64.23।।
explanation: "Thereafter, proceeding forth we shall try to win your enemy. If we win, there will be no purpose for you to do any action."

shloka_text: अथजीवतिनश्शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसम्युगाः । ततस्तदभिपत्स्यामोमनसायत्समीक्षितम् ।।6.64.24।।
explanation: "If our enemy survives in combat, we too will survive and review as we planned and see."

shloka_text: वयंयुद्धादिहेष्यामोरुधिरेणसमुक्षिताः । विदार्यस्वतनुंबाणैरामनामाङ्कितैश्शितैः ।।6.64.25।।
explanation: "Bathed in blood, wounded by the arrows marked with Rama's name, bodies torn cruelly we will come here from war."

shloka_text: भक्षितोराघवोऽस्माभिर्लक्ष्मणश्चेतिवादिनः । तवपादौग्रहीष्यामस्त्वंनःकामंप्रपूरय ।।6.64.26।।
explanation: "We too will hold your feet saying 'Rama and Lakshmana have been devoured by us'. Then you will grant our desires."

shloka_text: ततोऽवघोषयपुरेगजस्कन्धेनपार्थिव । हतोरामस्सहभ्रात्राससैन्यइतिसर्वतः ।।6.64.27।।
explanation: "Thereafter mounted on elephant backs all over the city will make a rakshasa pronounce that Rama accompanied by his brother are killed."

shloka_text: प्रीतोनामततोभूत्वाभृत्यानांत्वमरिन्दम । भोगांश्चपरिवारांश्चकामांश्चवसुदापय ।।6.64.28।।
explanation: "O tamer of enemies! In the name of expression of happiness, thereafter gift items of enjoyment to the attendants, and companions and granting wealth as per their desire.

shloka_text: ततोमाल्यानिवासांसिवीराणामनुलेपनम् । पेयं च बहुयोधेभ्यस्स्वयं च मुदितःपिब ।।6.64.29।।
explanation: "Thereafter give your warriors, garlands, cosmetics and many drinks and drink yourself happily."

shloka_text: ततोऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूतेकौलीनेसर्वतोगते । भक्षितस्ससुहृद्रामोराक्षसैरितिविश्रुते ।।6.64.30।। प्रविश्याश्वास्यचापित्वंसीतांरहसिसान्त्वय । धनधान्यैश्चकामैश्चरत्नैश्चानांप्रलोभय ।।6.64.31।।
explanation: Thereafter, when the scandal that Rama and Lakshmana with all his friends have been devoured is widely spread everywhere, approaching Sita privately, restoring confidence and consoling her, tempt her with offering wealth, grain and gems and conciliate.

shloka_text: ततोऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूतेकौलीनेसर्वतोगते । भक्षितस्ससुहृद्रामोराक्षसैरितिविश्रुते ।।6.64.30।। प्रविश्याश्वास्यचापित्वंसीतांरहसिसान्त्वय । धनधान्यैश्चकामैश्चरत्नैश्चानांप्रलोभय ।।6.64.31।।
explanation: Thereafter, when the scandal that Rama and Lakshmana with all his friends have been devoured is widely spread everywhere, approaching Sita privately, restoring confidence and consoling her, tempt her with offering wealth, grain and gems and conciliate.

shloka_text: अनयोपधयाराजन् भयशोकानुबन्धया । अकामात्वद्वशंसीतानष्टनाथाभविष्यति ।।6.64.32।।
explanation: "O King! By conjuring her like this, helpless Sita overtaken by fear and sorrow having lost her husband will submit to you in spite of no desire to you."

shloka_text: ञ्जनीयम्हिभर्तारंविनष्टमवगम्यसा । नैराश्यात् स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्चत्वद्वशंप्रतिपत्स्यते ।।6.64.33।।
explanation: "Her charming husband ceased to live and thinking of no alternate, being a fickle woman, will accept your dependence."

shloka_text: सापुरासुखसम्वृद्धासुखार्हादुःखकर्शिता । त्वय्यधीनंसुखंज्ञात्वासर्वथोगमिष्यति ।।6.64.34।।
explanation: "That Sita having grown up in much comfort, deserved felicity. Tormented with grief, desperate, depending on you alone for happiness, will submit to you completely."

shloka_text: एतत्सुनीतंममदर्शनेनरामंहिदृष्टवैभवेदनर्धः । इहैवतेसेत्स्यतिमोत्सुकोभूर्महानयुद्धेनसुखस्यलाभः ।।6.64.35।।
explanation: "To me this is the best course. As soon as you see Rama, do not be eager for war. It is meaningless. Great gain will accrue to you from here."

shloka_text: अदृष्टसैन्योह्यनवाप्तसंशयोरिपूनयुद्धेनजयन् जनाधिप । यशश्चपुण्यं च महन्महीपतेश्रशियं च कीर्तिं च चिरं ।।6.64.36।।
explanation: "O Lord of the people! If a king conquers his enemy without any loss of army, without facing any dangerand without war, such a mighty ruler of the earth will indeed earn fame and merit and attain prosperity." ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेचतुष्षष्टितमस्सर्गः।। This is the end of the sixty fourth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स तथोक्तस्तुनिर्भर्त्स्यकुम्भकर्णोमहोदरम् । अब्रवीद्राक्षसश्रेष्ठंभ्रातरंरावणंततः ।।6.65.1।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna having heard Mahodara, warned him not to speak that way and spoke to Ravana, the foremost of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सोऽहंतवभयंघोरंवधात्तस्यदुरात्मनः । रामस्याद्यप्रमार्जामिनिर्वैरोहिसुखीभव ।।6.65.2।।
explanation: "You know me. I will get rid of your enmity killing the cruel minded Rama. Be fearless and happy now."

shloka_text: गर्जन्ति न वृथाशूरानिर्जलाइवतोयदाः । पश्यसम्पद्यमानंतुगर्जितंयुधिकर्मणा ।।6.65.3।।
explanation: "Warriors will not roar wastefully like waterless clouds. You will see me roaring after having completed the action."

shloka_text: न मर्षयन्तिचात्मानंसम्भावयतिनात्मना । अदर्शयित्वाशूरास्तुकर्मकुर्वन्तिदुष्करम् ।।6.65.4।।
explanation: "Warriors do not tolerate even when glorified. They never praise themselves. They accomplish difficult deeds without displaying them."

shloka_text: विक्लबानामबुद्धीनांराज्ञापण्डितमानिनाम् । श्रृण्वतासदितमिदंत्वाद्विधानांमहोदर ।।6.65.5।।
explanation: "O Mahodara! Your words of appeal will be accepted as cowardly, devoid of intellect and to those who do not know anything, it looks as if you know."

shloka_text: युद्धेकापुरुषैर्नित्यंभवद्भिःप्रियवादिभि: । राजानमनुगच्छद्भिःसर्वंकृत्यमोद्धिसादितम् ।।6.65.6।।
explanation: "You, who always fear in combat, are talking pleasingly to the king , going after him happily brought the matter to this state."

shloka_text: राजशेषाकृतालङ्काक्षीणःकोशोबलंहतम् । राजानमिममासाद्यसुहृचचिह्नममित्रकम् ।।6.65.7।।
explanation: "The king is left alone in Lanka, which is divested of its wealth, and treasury reduced, and the army destroyed by unfriendly people pretending as good friends around him."

shloka_text: एषनिर्याम्यहंयुद्धमुद्यतश्शत्रुनिर्जये । दुर्नयंभवतामद्यसमीकर्तुंमिहाहवे ।।6.65.8।।
explanation: "I am setting out in this manner to the battlefield, to overpower the enemies in the battle in order to redeem the mistakes done by all of you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तवतोवाक्यंकुम्भकर्णस्यधीमतः । प्रत्युवाचततोवाक्यंप्रहसन्राक्षसाधिपः ।।6.65.9।।
explanation: Wise Kumbhakarna having spoken in that way, the Rakshasa king, Ravana laughed and replied in this way.

shloka_text: महोदरोऽयंरामात्तुपरित्रस्तो न संशयः । न हिरोचयतेतात युद्धंयुद्धविशारद ।।6.65.10।।
explanation: "O dear! You are an expert in war! This Mahodara is terrified at Rama. He is not desiring war. There is no doubt."

shloka_text: कश्चिन्मेत्वत्समोनास्तिसौहृदेनबलेन च । गच्छशत्रुवधायत्वंकुम्भकर्णजयाय च ।।6.65.11।।
explanation: "O Kumbhakarna! There is none who is equal to you in might and friendliness at heart towards me. You go and be victorious by killing the enemies."

shloka_text: तस्मात्तुशत्रुनाशार्थंभवान्सम्बोधितोमया । अयंहिकालस्सुहृदांराक्षसानामरिन्दम ।।6.65.12।।
explanation: "You are difficult to encounter. You have awakened for the sake of putting an end to the enemy. It is a momentous period for the Rakshasas, O tamer of enemies."

shloka_text: तद्गच्छशूलमादायपाशहस्तइवान्तकः । वानरान्राजपुत्रौ च भक्ष्यादित्यतेजसा ।।6.65.13।।
explanation: "Therefore, taking up trident holding the noose in hand like the God of Death proceed to devour the monkeys as well as the two princes shining like the Sun."

shloka_text: समालोक्यतुतेरूपंविद्रविष्यन्तिवानराः । रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापिहृदयेप्रस्फुटिष्यतः ।।6.65.14।।
explanation: "Seeing your form, the Vanaras will run away, Rama and Lakshmana's heart will break."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वामहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । पुनर्जातमिवात्मानंमेनेराक्षसपुङ्गवः ।।6.65.15।।
explanation: The highly energetic king of Rakshasas having spoken like that to mighty Kumbhakarna, felt as if he had taken birth again.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णबलाभिज्ञोजानंस्तस्यपराक्रमम् । बभूवमुदितोराजाशशाङ्कइवनिर्मलः ।।6.65.16।।
explanation: The king who knew the valour and mighty strength of Kumbhakarna remained happy like the moon.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तःसम्हृष्टोनिर्जगाममहाबलः । राज्ञस्तुवचनंश्रुत्वाकुम्भकर्णस्समुद्यत:।। 6.65.17।।
explanation: The king having spoken these words, mighty Kumbhakarna, pleased with the king's words set forth to fight.

shloka_text: आददेनिशितंशूलंवेगाच्छत्रुनिबर्हणम् । सर्वकालायसंदीप्तंतप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम् ।।6.65.18।।
explanation: The destroyer of enemies, hurriedly seized a whetted flaming iron dart, embellished with polished gold.

shloka_text: इन्द्राशनिसमंभीमंवज्रप्रतिमगौरवम् । देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् ।।6.65.19 ।। रक्तमाल्यंमहाधामंस्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम् । आदायनिशितंशूलंशत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम् ।।6.65.20।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजारावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: The dart was like Indra's thunderbolt in form and was equal to thunderbolt, capable of destroying Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas and Pannagas, was like rising fire shining like the face of an enemy. It was sharp, wreathed in garlands of red colour and emitting flame. Kumbhakarna wielding the dart said.

shloka_text: इन्द्राशनिसमंभीमंवज्रप्रतिमगौरवम् । देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् ।।6.65.19 ।। रक्तमाल्यंमहाधामंस्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम् । आदायनिशितंशूलंशत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम् ।।6.65.20।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजारावणंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: The dart was like Indra's thunderbolt in form and was equal to thunderbolt, capable of destroying Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas and Pannagas, was like rising fire shining like the face of an enemy. It was sharp, wreathed in garlands of red colour and emitting flame. Kumbhakarna wielding the dart said.

shloka_text: गमिष्याम्यहमेकाकीतिष्ठत्विहबलंमम ।।6.65.21।। अद्यतान् क्षुभितान् क्रुद्धोभक्षयिष्यामिवानरान् ।
explanation: Enraged and angry Kumbhakarna said, "I will proceed now. Let my army remain here. I will consume them on keys today."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णवचश्श्रुत्वारावणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.65.22।। सैन्यैःपरिवृतोगच्छशूलमुद्गतपाणिभिः ।
explanation: Hearing Kumbhakarna's words Ravana said," Go with trident, sword and iron bar in hand surrounded by the army."

shloka_text: वानराहिमहात्मानश्शीघ्रास्सव्यवसायिनः ।।6.65.23।। एकाकिनंप्रमत्तंवानयेयुद्धशनैःक्ष्यम् ।
explanation: "The Vanaras are gigantic, endowed with speed and determination. They will destroy with their teeth when you are not alert and alone."

shloka_text: तस्मात्परमदुर्धर्षै: सैन्यैःपरिवृतोव्रज ।।6.65.24।। रक्षसामहितंसर्वंशत्रुपक्षंनिषूदय ।
explanation: "Therefore, go surrounded by the army. They are extremely difficult to encounter. They are like thunderbolts. Destroy them who are on the enemy side and not favourable to Rakshasas."

shloka_text: अथासनात्समुत्पत्यस्रजं मणिकृतान्तराम् ।।6.65.25।। आबबन्धमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णस्यरावणः ।
explanation: And then the brilliant Ravana got up from his seat, garlanded Kumbhakarna with garland s of flowers encrusted with gems.

shloka_text: अङ्गदान्यङ्गुलीवेष्टान्वराण्याभरणानि च ।।6.65.26।। हारं च श्शिसङ्काशमाबबन्दमहात्मनः ।
explanation: Then Ravana placed armlets, rings, exquisite ornaments, garland s of pearls like moonlight on Kumbhakarna's neck.

shloka_text: दिव्यानि च सुगन्धीनिमाल्यदामानिरावणः ।।6.65.27।। श्रोत्रिचासञ्जयामासश्रीमतीचास्यकुण्डले ।
explanation: Ravana then placed his crown, wonderful fragrant garlands and rich suspended earrings on Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: काञ्चनाङ्गदकेयूरोनिष्काभरणभूषितः ।।6.65.28।। कुम्भकर्णोबृहत्कर्णस्सुहुतोऽग्निरिवाबभौ ।
explanation: Adorned with armlets studded with gems and golden ornaments on his distinguished large ears, Kumbhakarna shone like fire.

shloka_text: श्रोणीसूत्रेणमहतामेचकेनव्यराजत ।।6.65.29।। अमृतोत्पादनेनद्धोभुजङ्गेनेवमन्दरः ।
explanation: Adorned with a huge dark girdle, Kumbhakarna seemed like a bright jewel like Mount Mandara used for churning nectar of immortality fastened by Vasuki.

shloka_text: स काञ्चनंभारसहंनिवातंविद्युत्प्रभंदीप्तमिवात्मभासा । आबध्यमानःकवचंरराजसन्ध्याभ्रसम्वीतराजः ।।6.65.30।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna decked in heavy golden shield (impenetrable by any weapon) and difficult to break, seemed like the lightning with self effulgence, glowing like fire, shone like the evening twilight around the mountain peak.

shloka_text: सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गश्शूलपाणिस्सराक्षसः । त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहोनारायणइवाबभौ ।।6.65.31।। भ्रातरंसम्परिष्वज्यकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् । प्रणम्यशिरसातस्मैसम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.65.32।।
explanation: Decked with ornaments on all his limbs, with pike in hand, the Rakshasa was like Narayana ready to take three strides to cover the universe. Endowed with great strength, embraced his brother, went round in reverence bowing down his head and sallied forth.

shloka_text: सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गश्शूलपाणिस्सराक्षसः । त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहोनारायणइवाबभौ ।।6.65.31।। भ्रातरंसम्परिष्वज्यकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् । प्रणम्यशिरसातस्मैसम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.65.32।।
explanation: Decked with ornaments on all his limbs, with pike in hand, the Rakshasa was like Narayana ready to take three strides to cover the universe. Endowed with great strength, embraced his brother, went round in reverence bowing down his head and sallied forth.

shloka_text: निष्पतन्तंमहाकायंमहानादंमहाबलम् । तमाशीर्भिःप्रशस्ताभिःप्रेषयामासरावणः ।।6.65.33।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, of huge body, of loud voice and highly capable having been dismissed by Ravana, went with the great army after benediction and started observing.

shloka_text: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैस्सैन्यैश्चापिवरायुथैः । तंगजैश्चतुरङ्गैश्चस्यन्दनैश्चाम्बुदस्वनैः ।।6.65.34।। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं रथिनो रथिनां वरम् ।
explanation: Many great warriors seated on the best of chariots, with best of weapons amidst noise of conchs and drums, elephants, horses also and thunder like chariot warriors, started to proceed.

shloka_text: सर्पैरुष्ट्रैःखरैरश्वैस्सिम्हद्विपमृगद्विजैः । अनुजग्मुश्चतंघोरंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.65.35।।
explanation: On dreadful and mighty serpents, camels, donkeys, horses, lions, antelopes, and birds also the Rakshasas accompanied Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: स पुष्पवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणोधृतातपत्रःशितशूलपाणिः । मदोत्कटःशोणितगन्धमत्तोविनिर्ययौदावनदेवशत्रुः ।।6.65.36।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, the enemy of Devas and Danavas determined and eager showered with a rain of flowers, head covered with parasol, excited with drink, wielding sharpened tridents in hand and smeared with blood red fragrant sandal paste, sallied forth in that state.

shloka_text: पदातयश्चबहवोमहानादामहाबलाः । अन्वयूराक्षसाभीमाभीमाक्षाश्शस्त्रपाणयः ।।6.65.37।।
explanation: Rakshasas of loud voice, great prowess, and fearful with frightening eyes, lifted the many weapons in hand and followed on foot.

shloka_text: रक्ताक्षास्सुमहाकायानीलाञ्चनचयोपमाः । शूलानुद्यम्यखडगांश्चनिशितांश्चपरश्वधान् ।।6.65.38।। बहुव्यामांश्चपरिघान्गदाश्चमुसलानि च । तालस्कन्धांश्चविपुलान्क्षेपणीयान्दुरासदान् ।।6.65.39।।
explanation: Rakshasas with blood red eyes, of huge body size, dark blue in colour, holding tridents, sharpened whetted axes and weapons of many kinds, iron bars and maces, clubs, mallets and palmyra trees, the evil minded vast army set out.

shloka_text: रक्ताक्षास्सुमहाकायानीलाञ्चनचयोपमाः । शूलानुद्यम्यखडगांश्चनिशितांश्चपरश्वधान् ।।6.65.38।। बहुव्यामांश्चपरिघान्गदाश्चमुसलानि च । तालस्कन्धांश्चविपुलान्क्षेपणीयान्दुरासदान् ।।6.65.39।।
explanation: Rakshasas with blood red eyes, of huge body size, dark blue in colour, holding tridents, sharpened whetted axes and weapons of many kinds, iron bars and maces, clubs, mallets and palmyra trees, the evil minded vast army set out.

shloka_text: अथान्यद्वपुरादायदारुणंरोमहर्षणम् । निष्पपातमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.65.40।। धनुःशतपरीणाहः स षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः । रौद्रःशकटचक्राक्षोमहापर्वतसन्निभः ।।6.65.41।।
explanation: Assuming another fearful form, Kumbhakarna who was highly energetic, endowed with mighty strength and frightful in form, which was a hundred bows in breadth and six hundred bows in height, with eyes like wheels of chariot, enraged, seemed like a huge mountain.

shloka_text: अथान्यद्वपुरादायदारुणंरोमहर्षणम् । निष्पपातमहातेजाःकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.65.40।। धनुःशतपरीणाहः स षट्छत्रसमुच्छ्रितः । रौद्रःशकटचक्राक्षोमहापर्वतसन्निभः ।।6.65.41।।
explanation: Assuming another fearful form, Kumbhakarna who was highly energetic, endowed with mighty strength and frightful in form, which was a hundred bows in breadth and six hundred bows in height, with eyes like wheels of chariot, enraged, seemed like a huge mountain.

shloka_text: सन्निपत्य च रक्षांसिदग्धशैलोपमामहान् । कुम्भकर्णोमहावक्त्रःप्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत् ।।6.65.42।।
explanation: Thus spoke, Kumbhakarna who resembled a charred mountain, with wide mouth, reaching near the Rakshasas, laughing.

shloka_text: अद्यवानरमुख्यानांतानियूथानिभागश । निर्दहिष्यामिसङ्ख्रुद्धश्शलाभानिवपावकः ।।6.65.43।।
explanation: Thereafter, furious Kumbhakarna said "Now I will consume all the battalions of Vanaras just as moths are consumed by fire."

shloka_text: नापराध्यन्तिमेकामंवानरा: वनचारिणः । जातिरस्मद्विधानांसापुरोद्यानविभूषणम् ।।6.65.44।।
explanation: "These forest rangers have never desired to do any harm to me. This clan serve as ornaments of our gardens."

shloka_text: पुररोधस्यमूलंतुराघवस्सहलक्ष्मणः । हतेतस्मिन् हतंसर्वंतंवधिष्यामिसंयुगे ।।6.65.45।।
explanation: "The root cause of besieging Lanka is Rama and Lakshmana. I will kill them in combat."

shloka_text: एवंतस्यब्रुवाणस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यराक्षसाः । नादंचक्रुर्महाघोरंकम्पयन्तइवार्णवम् ।।6.65.46।।
explanation: When Kumbhakarna had spoken that way the Rakshasas made noise that was like the sound of an agitated ocean.

shloka_text: तस्यनिष्पततस्तूर्णंकुम्भकर्णस्यधीमतः । बभूवुर्घोररूपाणिनिमित्तानिसमन्ततः ।।6.65.47।।
explanation: As wise Kumbhakarna was proceeding swiftly , dreadful portents appeared.

shloka_text: उल्काशनियुतामेघाबभूवुर्गर्धभारुणाः । ससागरवनाचैववसुधासमकम्पत ।।6.65.48।।
explanation: The clouds appeared in the colour of donkey and there was thunder and lightning. The oceans, forests and earth seemed as though shaken.

shloka_text: घोररूपाश्शिवानेदुस्सज्वालकबलैर्मुखैः । मण्डलान्यपसव्यानिबबन्धुश्चविहङ्गमाः ।।6.65.49।।
explanation: She jackals were seen with flaming morsels throwing from their mouths. Birds wheeled in a circular way and settled.

shloka_text: निष्पपात च गृध्रोमालेवाऽस्यपथिगच्छतः । प्रास्फुरन्नयनंचास्यसव्योबाहुश्चकम्पत ।।6.65.50।।
explanation: On the way as he was going an eagle alighted on his pike. His eyes twitched and left shoulder throbbed.

shloka_text: निष्पपाततदाचोल्काज्वलन्तीभीमनिश्श्वना । आदित्योनिष्प्रभश्चासीन्नप्रवाति च ऽनिलः ।।6.65.51।।
explanation: Then a burning meteor fell from the sky making a terrible sound. The sun lost his glow and the wind lost its delight।।

shloka_text: अचिन्तयन्महोत्पातानुदितान्रोमहर्षणान् । निर्ययौकुम्भकर्णस्तुकृतान्तबलचोदितः ।।6.65.52।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna went unmindful of the portents which made hair stand on end propelled by the force of destiny.

shloka_text: न लङ्घयित्वाप्राकारंपद्भ्यांपर्वतसन्निभः । ददर्शाभ्रघनप्रख्यंवानरानीकमद्भुतम् ।।6.65.53।।
explanation: He who resembled a mountain in form, leapt the boundary wall on foot like a cloud and witnessed the amazing Vanara troops.

shloka_text: तेदृष्टवाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंवानराःपर्वतोपमम् । वायुनुन्नाइवघनाययुस्सर्वादिशस्तदा ।।6.65.54।।
explanation: On seeing the mountain like form of the foremost of the Rakshasas. the vanaras dispersed in all directions like clouds swept by the wind.

shloka_text: तद्वानरानीकमतिप्रचण्डंदिशोद्रवद्भिन्नमवाभ्रजालम् । स कुम्भकर्णस्समवेक्ष्यहर्षान्ननादभूयोघनवद्घनाभः ।।6.65.55।।
explanation: Heavy cloud like Kumbhakarna, a notorious one, perceiving the Vanara troops scattered like clouds in all directions emitted roar, laughing aloud.

shloka_text: तेतस्यघोरंनिनदंनिशम्ययथानिनादंदिविवारिदस्य । पेतुर्धरण्यांबहवःप्लवङ्गानिकृत्तमूलाइवशालवृक्षाः ।।6.65.56।।
explanation: Hearing the dreadful roar of Kumbhakarna, that resembled the rumbling of clouds, many Vanaras fell on the ground like severed Sala trees.

shloka_text: विपुलपरिघवान् स कुम्भकर्णोरिपुनिधनायविनिस्पृतोत्मा । कपिषणभयमाददत्सुभीमंप्रभुरिवदण्डवान्युगान्ते ।।6.65.57।।
explanation: Armed with a huge iron bar, Kumbhakarna stood for destroying the enemies like the great time spirit, deadly God of Death waits at the end of the universe along with Kinkaras, like a king. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेपञ्चाषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty fifth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: स लङ्घयित्वाप्राकारंगिरिकूटोपमोमहान् । निर्ययौनगरात्तूर्णंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.66.1।।
explanation: Mighty Kumbhakarna, a gigantic one, resembling a mountain peak, having swiftly crossed over the boundary of the city roared.

shloka_text: ननाद च महानादंसमुद्रमभिनादयन् । विजयन्निवनिर्घातन्विधमन्निवपर्वतान् ।।6.66.2।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna roared making loud noises as if proclaiming victory, like the breaking of mountains and reverberating of ocean.

shloka_text: तमवध्यंमघवतायमेनवरुणेनवा । प्रेक्ष्यभीमाक्षमायान्तंवानराविप्रदुद्रुवुः ।।6.66.3।।
explanation: Observing that rakshasa with frightening eyes, who could not be killed by Indra or Yama or even by Varuna coming towards them the vanaras ran in fear.

shloka_text: तांस्तुविप्रद्रुतान् दृष्टवाराजपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत् । नलंनीलंगवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम् ।।6.66.4।।
explanation: Seeing the Vanaras running in fear, Angada spoke to Nala, Nila, Gavaksha, Mahabala and Kumuda.

shloka_text: आत्मानमत्रविस्मृत्यवीर्याण्यभिजनानि च । क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःप्राकृताहरयोयथा ।।6.66.5।।
explanation: "Forgetting yourself, that you are warriors, not knowing by nature, being Vanaras where are you going?"

shloka_text: साधुसौम्या निवर्तध्वंकिप्राणान्परिरक्षथ । नालंयुद्धायवैरक्षोमहतीयंबिभीषका ।।6.66.6।।
explanation: "O good Vanaras! You are modest. Return. Why are you protecting your life? This Rakshasa is not capable of facing war. He can create only fear."

shloka_text: महतीमुथतितामेनांराक्षसानांबिभीषिकाम् । विक्रमाद्विधमिष्यामोनिवर्तध्वंप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.66.7।।
explanation: "O Vanaras! We will dispel this huge rakshasa, a nightmare with our power. Come back."

shloka_text: कृच्छ्रेणतुसमाश्वस्यसङ्गम्य च ततस्ततः । वृक्षाद्रिहस्ताहरयस्सम्प्रतस्थूरणाजिरम् ।।6.66.8।।
explanation: Overcoming fear, the Vanaras getting together from here and there holding trees by hand, proceeded to the battlefield.

shloka_text: तेनिवृत्यतुसङ्कृद्धाःकुम्भकर्णंवनौकसः । निर्जघ्नुःपरमक्रुद्धास्समदाइवकुञ्जराः ।।6.66.9।।
explanation: Those forest rangers who were extremely enraged turned back to hit, determined like the elephants in rut went to vanquish Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्चशिलाभिश्चमहाबलः । पादपैःपुष्पिताग्रैश्चहन्यमानो न कम्पते ।।6.66.10।।
explanation: Though Kumbhakarna was hit with lofty mountain peaks and trees with blossoms at crests, he was not shaken.

shloka_text: तस्यगात्रेषुपतिताभिद्यन्तेशतशश्शिलाः । पादपाःपुष्पिताग्राश्चभग्नाःपेतुर्महीतले ।।6.66.11।।
explanation: Fallen on his limbs many rocks got broken, even the treetops with blossoms were broken and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: सोऽपिसैन्यानिसङ्क्रुद्धोवानराणांमहौजसाम् । ममन्थपरमायत्तोवनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः ।।6.66.12।।
explanation: Enraged Kumbhakarna began to destroy Vanaras endowed with extraordinary vigour, just as great forest fire burns the forest.

shloka_text: लोहितार्द्रास्तुबहवश्शेरतेवानरर्षभाः । निरस्तांपतिताभूमौताम्रपुष्पाइवद्रुमाः ।।6.66.13।।
explanation: Many bulls among the Vanaras lay on the ground like trees with red flowers on top tossed and fallen on the ground.

shloka_text: लङ्घयन्तःप्रधावन्तोवानरानावलोकयन् । केचित्समुद्रेपतिताःकेचिद्गगनमास्थिताः ।।6.66.14।।
explanation: The Vanaras leapt without looking back. Indeed, some dropped into the ocean, and some flew into space.

shloka_text: वध्यमानास्तुतेवीराराक्षसेन च लीलया । सागरंयेनतेतीर्णाःपथातेनदुद्रुवुः ।।6.66.15।।
explanation: Struck by Rakshasa, the Vanaras ran in the same path crossing the ocean (by which they came).

shloka_text: तेस्थलानितदानिम्नंविवर्णमानाभयात् । ऋक्षावृक्षान् समारूढाःकेचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः ।।6.66.16।।
explanation: Out of fear the vanaras rushed to plains with pale countenance, some climbed up mountains and bears climbed up trees.

shloka_text: ममज्जुरर्णवेकेचिद्गुहाःकेचित्समाश्रिताः । निपेतुःकेचिदपरेकेचिन्नैवावतस्थिरे ।।6.66.17।। केचिद्भूमौनिपतिताःकेचित्सुप्तामृताइव ।
explanation: Some drowned in the ocean, some entered into the caves, some others not knowing what to do sat down and others fell on the ground and some slept as if dead.

shloka_text: तान्समीक्ष्याङ्गदोभग्नान्वानरानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.66.18।। अवतिष्ठतयुध्यामोनिवर्तध्वंप्लवङ्गमाः ।
explanation: Seeing the monkeys routed, Angada spoke, 'Stay, return back. We will fight'

shloka_text: भग्नानांवो न पश्यामिपरिगम्यमहीमिमाम् ।।6.66.19।। स्थानंसर्वेनिवर्तध्वंकिंप्राणान् परिरक्षथ ।
explanation: "I do not see any refuge for you even if you go round the globe. All of you return back. Why do you preserve life?"

shloka_text: निरायुधानांद्रवतामसङ्गगतिपौरुषाः ।।6.66.20।। दाराह्युपहसिष्यन्ति स वैघातस्तुजीवताम् ।
explanation: "Monkeys! Your valour can't be challenged. If you run away for life abandoning weapons even your wives will ridicule you. That is more than death."

shloka_text: कुलेषुजातास्सर्वेस्मविस्तीर्णेषुमहत्सु च ।।6.66.21।। क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःहरयःप्राकृतायथा । अनार्याःखलुयद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वावीर्यंप्रधावत ।।6.66.22।।
explanation: "You are born in noble families, and are widely spread. As such why are you running away like ordinary monkeys as if terrified giving up your valour. It is not worthy of you."

shloka_text: कुलेषुजातास्सर्वेस्मविस्तीर्णेषुमहत्सु च ।।6.66.21।। क्वगच्छतभयत्रस्ताःहरयःप्राकृतायथा । अनार्याःखलुयद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वावीर्यंप्रधावत ।।6.66.22।।
explanation: "You are born in noble families, and are widely spread. As such why are you running away like ordinary monkeys as if terrified giving up your valour. It is not worthy of you."

shloka_text: विकत्थनानिवोयानि तदावैजनसंसदि । तानिवःक्वनुयातानिसोदग्राणिम हितानि च ।।6.66.23।।
explanation: "Earlier in the assembly of people you made vigorous statements and acclaimed yourselves highly with selfpraise. Where has it gone?"

shloka_text: भीरुप्रवादाश्श्रूयन्तेयस्तुजीवतिधिक्कृतः । मार्गस्सत्पुरुषैर्जष्टःसेव्यतांत्यज्यतांभयम् ।।6.66.24।।
explanation: "He who is defeated lives, but people will say he is timid. Resorting to the path of good people and serving them gives up fear."

shloka_text: शयामहेऽनिहताःपृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः । दुष्प्रापंब्रह्मलोकंवाप्राप्नुयामोयुधिसूदिता ।।6.66.25।।
explanation: "If we are killed in war, fallen dead on the ground and our life span is reduced, we will attain the realm of Brahma which is difficult to attain."

shloka_text: सम्प्राप्नुयामःकीर्तिंवानिहत्वाशत्रुमाहवे । जीवितंवीरलोकस्यमोक्ष्यामोवसुवानराः ।।6.66.26।।
explanation: "By killing the enemy, we will attain fame. Or else we will attain the world of Brahma, liberated."

shloka_text: न कुम्भकर्णःकाकुत्स्थंदृष्टवाजीवन् गमिष्यति । दीप्यमानमिवासाद्यपतङ्गोज्वलनंयथा ।।6.66.27।।
explanation: "Just as flies reaching the blazing fire can't escape, so also Kumbhakarna can't escape with life after facing Kakuthsa."

shloka_text: लायनेनचोद्धिष्टाःप्राणान् रक्षामहेवयम् । एकेनबहवोभग्नायशोनाशंगमिष्यति ।।6.66.28।।
explanation: "Even though we are distinguished, if we preserve our life by running away for life, destroyed by one, our glory will come to an end."

shloka_text: एवंब्रुवाणंतंशूरमङ्गदंकनकाङ्गदम् । द्रवमाणास्ततोवाक्यमूचुःशूरुविगर्हितम् ।।6.66.29।।
explanation: While the heroic Angada, adorned with gold armlets, was speaking in that manner to the fleeing vanara heroes, condemned by the hero the vanaras replied as follows.

shloka_text: कृतंनःकदनंघोरंकुम्भकर्णेनरक्षसा । न स्थानकालोगच्छामोदयितंजीवितंहिनः ।।6.66.30।।
explanation: "Kumbhakarna, the Rakshasa has done havoc to us. This is not the moment to stay. Our life is dear to us."

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वावचनंसर्वेतेभेजिरेदिशः । भीमंभीमाक्षमायान्तंदृष्टवावानरयूथपाः ।।6.66.31।।
explanation: All the Vanara troops having replied that way, seeing Kumbhakarna of frightful eyes coming towards them, scattered in all directions.

shloka_text: द्रवमाणस्तुतेवीराअङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः । सान्त्वैश्चैहनुमानैश्चततस्सर्वेनिवर्तिताः ।।6.66.32।।
explanation: Though the heroic monkeys were running away, Angada by his good words and examples turned them to return from wherever they were.

shloka_text: प्रहर्षमुपनीताश्चवालिपुत्रेणधीमता । आज्ञाप्रतीक्षास्तस्थुश्चसर्वेवानरयूथपाः ।।6.66.33।।
explanation: All the Vanara troops having heard Angada, son of Vali happily restored awaiting his command.

shloka_text: ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाःकुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः । द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्यास्त्वरिततराभिमुखंरणं ।।6.66.34।।
explanation: Rshaba, Sarabha, Mainda and Nila, Kumuda, Susena, Rambha, and Tara headed by Dwiviida, Panasa and Hanuman marched ahead swiftly to the battlefield. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty sixth sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic, the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तेनिवृत्तामहाकायाश्श्रुत्वाङ्गदवचस्तदा । नैष्ठिकींबुद्धिमास्थायसर्वेसङ्ग्रामकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.67.1।।
explanation: Having heard Angada's words, the Vanaras of gigantic body firmly decided to wage war and returned back.

shloka_text: समुदीरितवीर्यास्तेसमारोपितविक्रमाः । पर्यवस्थापितावाक्यैरङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः ।।6.67.2।। प्रयाताश्चगताहर्षंमरणेकृतश्चयाः । चक्रुस्सुतुमुलंयुद्धंवानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः ।।6.67.3।।
explanation: The Vanara leaders, having been reminded of their valour in battle by Angada gladly returned with a resolve to stake their life and carried on the battle.

shloka_text: समुदीरितवीर्यास्तेसमारोपितविक्रमाः । पर्यवस्थापितावाक्यैरङ्गदेनवलीमुखाः ।।6.67.2।। प्रयाताश्चगताहर्षंमरणेकृतश्चयाः । चक्रुस्सुतुमुलंयुद्धंवानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः ।।6.67.3।।
explanation: The Vanara leaders, having been reminded of their valour in battle by Angada gladly returned with a resolve to stake their life and carried on the battle.

shloka_text: अथवृक्षान्महाकायास्सानूनिसुमहान्ति च । वानरास्तूर्णमुद्यम्यकुम्भकर्णमभिद्रुताः ।।6.67.4।।
explanation: Thereafter the Vanaras of huge body wielding huge trees and mountain peaks quickly rushed towards Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्सङ्कृद्धोगदामुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । अर्थयन्समहाकायस्समन्ताद् व्यक्षिपद्रिपून् ।।6.67.5।।
explanation: Valiant Kumbhakarna, a gigantic one, highly enraged lifted mace and crescent shaped arrow struck the enemies on all sides.

shloka_text: शतानिसप्तचाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः । प्रकीर्णाःशेरतेभूमौकुम्भकर्णेनपोधिताः ।।6.67.6।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna held seven or eight or even hundred, thousand vanaras and threw them on the ground like serpents thrown by Garuda.

shloka_text: षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्रतिंशस्तथैव च । परिक्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यांखादन्विपरिधावति ।।6.67.7।। भक्ष्यन् भृशसङ्क्रुद्धोगरुडःपन्नगानिव ।
explanation: Kumbhakarna became extremely angry, and caught hold of sixteen, eight, ten vanaras in the same way ninetynine and thirty and many more Vanaras and devoured them and went about like Garuda after having eaten the serpents.

shloka_text: कृच्छ्रेणचसमाश्वस्ताःसङ्गम्यचततस्ततः ।।6.67.8।। वृक्षाद्रिहस्ताहरयस्तस्थुस्सङ्ग्राममूर्थनि ।
explanation: The Vanaras collected from here and there, having restored confidence in themselves with great difficulty, held trees and mountains and stood in the forefront of the battle.

shloka_text: ततःपर्वतमुत्पाट्यद्विविदःप्लवगर्षभः ।।6.67.9।। दुद्रावगिरिशृङ्गाभंविलम्बइवतोयदः ।
explanation: Thereafter Dwivida, a bull among the Vanaras lifted a mountain and went towards Kumbhakarna who resembled a threatening cloud.

shloka_text: तंसमुत्पत्यचिक्षेपकुम्भकर्णायवानरः ।।6.67.10।। तमप्राप्यमहाकायंतस्यसैन्येऽपतत्तधा ।
explanation: Vanara (Dwivida) going near Kumbhakarna struck him with the mountain. He missed the target and it fell on his army.

shloka_text: ममर्दाश्वान्गजांश्चापिरथांश्चापिनगोत्तमः ।।6.67.11।। तानिचान्यानिरक्षांसिएवंचान्यगदिरेःशिरः ।
explanation: The huge mountain peak crushed the horses, elephants and chariots and Rakshasa charioteers also.

shloka_text: तच्चैलवेगाभिहतंहताश्वंहतसारथि ।।6.67.12।। रक्षसांरुधिरक्लिन्नंबभूवायोधनंमहत् ।
explanation: The battlefield on which the Rakshasas and horses were crushed, charioteers were killed by the speed of the mountain remained wet with blood.

shloka_text: रथिनोवानरेन्द्राणांशरैःकालान्तकोपमैः ।।6.67.13।। शिरांसिनर्दतांजह्रुस्सहसाभीमनिस्स्वना ।
explanation: The Rakshasa charioteers severed the roaring Vanara leaders forcibly with their arrows emitting frightening sounds. They were like the Lord of Death at universal dissolution.

shloka_text: वानराश्चमहात्मानस्समुत्पाट्यमहाद्रुमान् ।।6.67.14।। रथावश्वान्गजानुष्ट्रान्राक्षसानभ्यसूदयन् ।
explanation: Great monkeys, uprooting huge trees, began to destroy chariots, horses, camels, and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: हनुमान् शैलशृङ्गाणिशिलाश्चविविधान् द्रुमान् ।।6.67.15।। ववर्षकुम्भकर्णस्यशिरस्यम्बरमास्थितः ।
explanation: Stationed in the sky Hanuman rained mountain peaks, rocks, and huge trees of several kinds on the head of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: तानिपर्वतशृङ्गाणिशूलेन स बिभेद ह ।।6.67.16।। बभञ्जवृक्षवर्षं च कुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः ।
explanation: Mighty Kumbhakarna split off the rocks, mountain peaks and the trees breaking them.

shloka_text: ततोहरीणांतदनीकमुग्रंदुद्रावशूलंनिशितंप्रगृह्य । तस्थौ स तस्यापततःपुरस्तान्महीधराग्रंहनुमान् प्रगृह्य ।।6.67.17।।
explanation: Thereafter Kumbhakarna holding a sharp pike rushed towards Hanuman who uprooted a mountain peak and obstructed him placing it before him.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णंकुपितोजघानवेगेनशैलोत्तमभीमकायम् । स चक्षुभेतेनतदाभिभूतोमेदार्द्रगात्रोरुधिरावसिक्तः ।।6.67.18।।
explanation: Enraged Hanuman struck Kumbhakarna endowed with a rock like frightening body. Overpowered by that blow Kumbhakarna was upset and bespattered with fat and got bathed in blood.

shloka_text: स शूलमासाद्यतटित्प्रकाशंगिरिर्यथाप्रज्वलिताग्रशृङ्गम् । बाह्वन्तरेमारुतिमाजघानगुहोऽचलंक्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्त्या ।।6.67.19।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna ,who was like a mountain blazing like fire, pierced at Maruti's chest with his pike shining like lightning just as Guha struck at Krauncha mountain.

shloka_text: शूलनिर्भिन्नमहाभुजान्तरःप्रविह्वलःशोणितमुद्वमन् मुखात् । ननादभीमंहनुमान् महाहवेयुगान्तमेघस्न्तितस्वनोपमम् ।।6.67.20।।
explanation: The great son of windgod, pierced with pike in the chest, ejected blood from his mouth, and roared in a frightening manner which was like thunder rumbling at the time of dissolution of the universe.

shloka_text: ततोविनेदुःसहसाप्रहृष्टारक्षोगणास्तंव्यथितंसमीक्ष्य । प्लवङ्गमास्तुव्यथिताभयर्ताःप्रदुद्रुवुःसंयतिकुम्भकर्णात् ।।6.67.21।।
explanation: Rakshasa's army collected together rejoiced to see Hanuman agonized. Vanaras were frightened and fled in fear of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: ततस्तुनीलोबलवान् पर्यवस्थापयन्बलम् । प्रविचिक्षेपशैलाग्रंकुम्भकर्णायधीमते ।।6.67.22।।
explanation: The mighty and wise Neela flung a peak of a mountain on Kumbhakarna and restored the confidence of the army.

shloka_text: तदापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यमुष्टिनाभिजघान ह । मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतंतच्छैलाग्रंव्यशीर्यत ।।6.67.23।। सविस्फुलिंगंसज्वालनिपपातमहेतले ।
explanation: (Kumbhakarna) observing the mountain peak coming towards him pierced it with his fist. Struck by the fist, the peak broke and sparks of fire came out shining brightly and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: ऋषभश्शरभोनीलोगवाक्षोगन्धमादनः ।।6.67.24।। पञ्चवानरशार्दूलाःकुम्बुकर्णमुपाद्रवन् ।
explanation: Rshaba, Sarabha, Neela, Gavaksha and Gandhamadana, these five tigers among Vanaras attacked Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: शैलैर्ववृक्षैस्तलैःपादैर्मुष्टिभिश्चमहाबलाः ।।6.67.25।। कुम्भकर्णंमहाकायंसर्वतोऽभिप्रदुद्रुवुः ।
explanation: Those Vanaras of exceptional strength attacked gigantic Kumbhakarna on all sides by rocks, trees and by their fists, hands and feet also.

shloka_text: स्पर्शानिवप्रहारांस्तान्वेद्वयानो न विव्यथे ।।6.67.26।। ऋषभंतुमहावेगंबाहुभ्यांपरिषस्वजे ।
explanation: Their attacks were like soft touches to Kumbhakarna, and no pain was experienced by him, and he encircled Rshaba by the shoulders with great impetuosity.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णभुजाभ्यांतुपीडितोवानरर्षभः ।।6.67.27।। निपपातर्षभोभीमःप्रमुखाद्वान्तशोणितः ।
explanation: Rshaba, the bull among Vanaras, of frightful appearance pressed by Kumbhakarna's shoulders, started bleeding from his teeth and fell down.

shloka_text: मुष्टिनाशरभंहत्वाजानुनानीलमाहवे ।।6.67.28।। आजघानगवाक्षंतुलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा । पादेनाभ्यहनत्कृद्धस्तरसागन्धमादनम् ।।6.67.29।।
explanation: Angry Kumbhakarna (enemy of Indra) hit Sarabha with his fist, Neela with his knees hurt Gavaksha and slapped him with his palms. Gandhamadana was kicked with force.

shloka_text: मुष्टिनाशरभंहत्वाजानुनानीलमाहवे ।।6.67.28।। आजघानगवाक्षंतुलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा । पादेनाभ्यहनत्कृद्धस्तरसागन्धमादनम् ।।6.67.29।।
explanation: Angry Kumbhakarna (enemy of Indra) hit Sarabha with his fist, Neela with his knees hurt Gavaksha and slapped him with his palms. Gandhamadana was kicked with force.

shloka_text: दत्तप्रहारव्यथितामुमुहुश्शोणितोक्षिताः । निपेतुस्तेतुमेदिन्यांनिकृत्ताइवकिंशुकाः ।।6.67.30।।
explanation: Hurt by the blows of Kumbhakarna, their eyes bathed in blood, the Vanaras fainted and fell on the ground like cut down Kimsuka trees.

shloka_text: तेषुवानरमुख्येषुपातितेषुमहात्मसु । वानराणांसहस्राणिकुम्बकर्णंप्रदद्रुवुः ।।6.67.31।।
explanation: Being great leaders and the important among them fallen, the Vanaras went in thousands towards Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: तंशैलमिवशैलाभाःसर्वेतुप्लवगर्षभाः । समारुह्यसमुत्पत्यददंशुश्चमहाबलाः ।।6.67.32।।
explanation: The bulls among Vanaras themselves looking like mountains endowed with great strength climbed up Kumbhakarna and bit him.

shloka_text: तंनखैर्धशनैश्चापिमुष्टिभिर्बाहुभिस्तथा । कुम्भकर्णंमहाबाहहुंतेजघ्नुःप्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.67.33।।
explanation: The bulls among Vanaras hurt Kumbhakarna, endowed with strong shoulders, by scratching with nails, biting with teeth and hitting him with arms and fists.

shloka_text: स वानरसहस्त्रैरजितः पर्वतोपमैः । रराजराक्षसव्याघ्रोगिरिरात्मरुहैरिव ।।6.67.34।।
explanation: The tiger among Rakshasas covered with thousands of Rakshasas was resembling a mountain with trees grown on itself.

shloka_text: बाहुभ्यांवानरान्सर्वान्प्रगृह्य स महाबलः । भक्ष्यामाससङ्क्रुद्धोगरुडःपन्नगानिव ।।6.67.35।।
explanation: Holding the Vanaras, the mighty Kumbhakarna started devouring all Vanaras just as Garuda does with serpents.

shloka_text: प्रक्षिप्ताःकुम्बकर्णेनवक्त्रेपातालसन्निभे । नासापुटाभ्यांनिर्जग्मुःकर्णाभ्यांचैववानराः ।।6.67.36।।
explanation: As Kumbhakarna thrust Vanaras into his mouth, the Vanaras came out through his nostrils and also through his ears.

shloka_text: भक्ष्यन्भृशसङ्क्रुद्धो हरीन् पर्वतसन्निभः । बभञ्जवानरान् सर्वान् सङ्क्रुद्धोराक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.67.37।।
explanation: The foremost of the Rakshasas, who resembled a mountain became enraged and mutilated the Vanaras.

shloka_text: मांसशोणितसंक्लेदाकुर्वन् भूमिं स राक्षसः । चचारहरिनैन्येषुकालानगिरिवमूर्छितः ।।6.67.38।।
explanation: That terrible Rakshasa swooning and wetting the ground with flesh and blood ranged through the army of Vanaras like fire at the time of dissolution of the universe.

shloka_text: वज्रहस्तोयथाशक्रःपाशहस्तइवान्तकः । शूलहस्तोबभौयुद्धेकुम्बकर्णोमहाबलः ।।6.67.39।।
explanation: Holding pike in hand, mighty Kumbhakarna was shining in the battlefield like Indra holding thunderbolt, and like Lord of Death holding the noose.

shloka_text: यथाशुष्काण्यरण्यानिग्रीष्मेदहतिपावकः । तथावानरसैन्यानिकुम्बकर्णोविनिर्दहत् ।।6.67.40।।
explanation: Just as fire god consumes dried forest in summer, Kumbhakarna was consuming the Vanara army.

shloka_text: ततस्तेवध्यमानास्तुहतयूथाविनायकाः । वानराभयसंविग्नाविनेदुर्विस्वरंभृशैः ।।6.67.41।।
explanation: Then with the army killed, the Vanaras moved without any leader making unnatural sounds out of fear and anger.

shloka_text: अनेकशोवध्यमानाःकुम्भकर्णेनवानराः । राघवंशरणंजग्मुर्व्यथिताःभिन्नचेतसः ।।6.67.42।।
explanation: Destroyed by Kumbhakarna in many ways, the Vanaras were heartbroken and sought the refuge of Raghava.

shloka_text: प्रभग्नान् वानरान् दृष्टवावज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजः । अभ्यधावतवेगेनकुम्भकर्णंमहाहवे ।।6.67.43।।
explanation: The son of Vali who sprung from Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt seeing the Vanaras routed, rushed towards Kumbhakarna to assault.

shloka_text: शैलशृङ्गंमहद्गृह्यविनदंश्चमुहुर्मुहुः । त्रासयन्राक्षसान्सर्वान् कुम्भकर्णपदानुगान् ।।6.67.44।। चिक्षेपशैलशिखरंकुम्भकर्णस्यमूर्धनि ।
explanation: Angada taking a huge peak of a mountain roaring again and again following Kumbhakarna frightening the Rakshasas flung the mountain top on the forehead of Kumbhakarna and crushed him.

shloka_text: स तेनाभिहतोमूर्ध्निशैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.67.45।। कुम्भकर्णःप्रजज्वालक्रोधेनमहतातदा । सोऽभ्यधावतवेगेनवालिपुत्रममर्षणम् ।।6.67.46।।
explanation: Hit on the forehead by Angada, Kumbhakarna, burning with fury rushed. The intolerant Rakshasa then rushed to Vali's son with force.

shloka_text: स तेनाभिहतोमूर्ध्निशैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.67.45।। कुम्भकर्णःप्रजज्वालक्रोधेनमहतातदा । सोऽभ्यधावतवेगेनवालिपुत्रममर्षणम् ।।6.67.46।।
explanation: Hit on the forehead by Angada, Kumbhakarna, burning with fury rushed. The intolerant Rakshasa then rushed to Vali's son with force.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णोमहानादस्त्रासयन् सर्ववानरान् । शूलंससर्जवैरोषादङ्गदेतुमहाबलः ।।6.67.47।।
explanation: Mighty Kumbhakarna agitated, making loud noise and frightening all the Vanaras hurled his pike on Angada.

shloka_text: त मापतन्तंबुद्ध्वातुयुद्धमार्गविशारदः । लाघवान्मोचयामाबलवान् वानरर्षभः ।।6.67.48।।
explanation: Angada who was knowledgeable of warfare, endowed with prowess, a bull among Vanaras, stopped the pike approaching him with agility and escaped.

shloka_text: उत्पत्यचैनंतरसातलेनोरस्यताडयत् । स तेनाभिहतःकोपात्प्रमुमोहाचलोपमः ।।6.67.49।।
explanation: Jumping up that way, Angada slapped him with his palm on the chest in anger. By that the mountain like Kumbhakarna became unconscious.

shloka_text: स लब्दसंज्ञोबलवान्मुष्टिमावर्त्यराक्षसः । अपहास्तेनचिक्षेपविसंज्ञः स पपात ह ।।6.67.50।।
explanation: The mighty Rakshasa regained his consciousness and, doubling his fist hit Angada with the back of his hand and Angada fell, lost senses.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूलेविसंज्ञेपतितेभुवि । तच्छूलंसमुपादायसुग्रीवमभिदुद्रुवे ।।6.67.51।।
explanation: When the tiger among the monkeys fell unconscious on ground, Kumbhakarna rushed towards Sugriva taking out the pike.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । उत्पपाततदावीरस्सुग्रीवोवानराधिपः ।।6.67.52।।
explanation: Valiant Sugriva, seeing the mighty Kumbhakarna coming towards him jumped (in excitement).

shloka_text: स पर्वताग्रमुत्क्षिप्यसमाविध्यमहाबलः । अभिदुद्राववेगेनकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.67.53।।
explanation: Sugriva, of great prowess lifting a mountain peak, whirled it round and round and darted towards Kumbhakarna swiftly.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्यकुम्भकर्णःप्लवङ्गमम् । तस्थौविवृतसर्वाङ्गोवानरेन्द्रस्यसम्मुखः ।।6.67.54।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, looking at the monkey Lord advancing towards him, stood in front of all limbs braced.

shloka_text: कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गंभक्ष्यन्तंप्लवङ्गमान् । कुम्भकर्णंस्थितंदृष्टवासुग्रीवोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.67.55।।
explanation: Sugriva spoke these words seeing Kumbhakarna who stood smeared with the blood of Vanaras and eating monkeys.

shloka_text: कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गंभक्ष्यन्तंप्लवङ्गमान् । कुम्भकर्णंस्थितंदृष्टवासुग्रीवोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.67.55।।
explanation: Sugriva spoke these words seeing Kumbhakarna who stood smeared with the blood of Vanaras and eating monkeys.

shloka_text: त्वजतद्वानरानीकंप्राकृतैःकिंकरिष्यसि । सहस्वैकंनिपातंमेपर्वतस्यास्यराक्षस ।।6.67.57।।
explanation: "Give up with Vanaras, who are monkeys by nature. Bear this one mountain's blow of mine."

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यंहरिराजस्यसत्त्वधैर्यसमन्वितम् । श्रुत्वाराक्षसशार्दूलःकुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद्वचः ।।6.67.58।।
explanation: Hearing the king of Vanara's words of courage and strength, the tiger among Rakshasas, Kumbhakarna spoke these words.

shloka_text: प्रजापतेस्तुपौत्रस्त्वंतथैवरक्षरजस्सुतः । श्रुतपौरुषसम्पन्नःकस्माद्गर्जसिवानर ।।6.67.59।।
explanation: "O Vanara! You are the grandson of creator Brahma and son of Rksharaja, endowed with fortitude and so roaring like this."

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णस्यवचोनिशम्यव्याविध्यशैलंसहसामुमोच । तेनाजघानोरसिकुम्भकर्णंशैलेनवज्राशनिसन्निभेन ।।6.67.60।।
explanation: On hearing Kumbhakarna's words, Sugriva forcibly discharged a mountain resembling a thunderbolt on the chest of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: तच्छैलशृङ्गंसहसाविकीर्णंभुजान्तरेतस्यतदाविशाले । ततोनिषेदुःसहसाप्लवङ्गारक्षोगणाश्चापिमुदाविनेदुः ।।6.67.61।।
explanation: Then the mountain peak dropped on the chest broke into pieces. Thereafter the monkeys were despaired, and Rakshasas roared in joy.

shloka_text: स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतश्चुकोपननादरोषाच्चविवृत्यवक्त्रम् । व्याविध्यशूलं च तटित्प्रकाशंचिक्षेपहर्यृक्षिपतेर्वधाय ।।6.67.62।।
explanation: Struck with mountain peaks, the Rakshasa became furious, and his pride was hurt. He opened his mouth widely making loud noises, his pike glowing like lightning, turned the pike into circles and hurled at Sugriva to put an end to him.

shloka_text: तत्कुम्भकर्णस्यभुजप्रविद्धंशूलंशितंकाञ्चनदामजुष्टम् । क्षिप्रंसमुत्पत्यनिगृह्यदोर्भ्यांबभञ्जवेगेनसुतोऽनिलस्य ।।6.67.63।।
explanation: Hanuman the son of windgod instantly seized Kumbhakarna with his arms, whose shaft was covered by chains and broke with both hands quickly.

shloka_text: कृतंभारसहस्रस्यशूलंकालायसंमहत् । बभञ्जजानुमारोप्यतदाहृष्टःप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.67.64।।
explanation: Then a rejoiced monkey, resting the thousand bharas iron pike on his knee broke it.

shloka_text: शूलंभग्नंहनुमतादृष्टवावानरवाहिनी । हृष्टाननादबहुशस्सर्वतश्चापिदुद्रुवे ।।6.67.65।।
explanation: Seeing the pike broken by Hanuman, the army of Vanaras rejoiced and roared repeatedly all over and rushed.

shloka_text: बभूवथपरित्रस्तोराक्षसोविमुखोऽभवत् । सिंहनादं च तेचक्रुःप्रहृष्टावनगोचराः ।।6.67.66।। मारुतिंपूजयाञ्चक्रुर्दृष्टवाशूलंतथागतम् ।
explanation: Rakshasa was dismayed and mellowed. The forest rangers rejoiced and roared like lions going round. Seeing the broken pike Vanaras applauded Hanuman.

shloka_text: स तत्तथाभग्नमवेक्ष्यशूलंचुकोपरक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा । उत्पाट्यलङ्कामलयात्सशृङ्गंजघानसुग्रीवमुपेत्यतेन ।।6.67.67।।
explanation: That great soul, the Lord of Rakshasas seeing the pike broken in that way, was highly enraged. Taking Malaya Mountain from Lanka, he struck Sugriva who was approaching him.

shloka_text: स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतोविसंज्ञःपपातभूमौयुधिवानरेन्द्रः । तंप्रेक्ष्यभूमौपतितंविसंज्ञनेदुःप्रहृष्टास्त्वथयातुधानाः ।।6.67.68।।
explanation: Struck by the piece of mountain the Vanara king became unconscious and dropped on the battlefield. Seeing that the Rakshasas were happy and naturally roared with a feeling of triumph.

shloka_text: मभ्युपेत्याद्भुतघोरवीर्यं स कुम्भकर्णोयुधिवानरेन्द्रम् । जहारसुग्रीवमभिप्रगृह्ययथानिलोमेघमतिप्रचण्डः ।।6.67.69।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna approaching the Vanara Lord Sugriva endowed with wonderful and dreadful prowess, went like wind carrying clouds taking him.

shloka_text: स तंमहामेघनिकाशरूपमुत्पाट्यगच्छन्युधिकुम्भकर्णः । रराजमेरुप्रतिमानरूपोमेरुर्यथाभ्युछ्रचितघोरशृङ्गः ।।6.67.70।।
explanation: In the battlefield, the form of Kumbhakarna which resembled a huge cloud was distinguished in appearance like the lofty peak of mountain Meru.

shloka_text: ततस्तमादायजगामवीरस्संस्तूयमानोयुधिराक्षसेन्द्रैः । शृण्वन्निनादंत्रिदिवालयानांप्लवङ्गराजग्रहविस्मितानाम् ।।6.67.71।।
explanation: Thereafter the heroic Rakshasa king having held Sugriva in the battle went, duly praised (by Rakshasas), hearing the roaring sounds of gods in heaven wondering at Sugriva's capture.

shloka_text: ततस्तमादायतदा स मेनेहरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः । अस्मिन् हतेसर्वमिदंहतंस्यात्सराघवंसैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः ।।6.67.72।।
explanation: Then Kumbhakarna, an enemy of Indra, who was equal to Indra in heroism seizing Sugriva, the Indra of monkeys, who is equal to Indra, thought, 'If Sugriva is killed it is like killing all the army including Rama.'

shloka_text: विद्रुतांवाहिनींदृष्टवावानराणामितस्ततः । कुम्भकर्णेनसुग्रीवंगृहीतंचापिवानरम् ।।6.67.73।। हनुमांश्चिन्तयामासमतिमान् मारुतात्मजः ।
explanation: Seeing the army running away here and there and Sugriva being captured by Kumbhakarna, wise Hanuman, the son of Maruti started thinking.

shloka_text: एवंगृहीतेसुग्रीवेकिंकर्तव्यंमयाभवेत् ।।6.67.74।। यद्वैन्यायंमयाकर्तुंतत्करिष्यामिसर्वधा । भूत्वापर्वतसङ्काशोनाशयिष्यामिराक्षसम् ।।6.67.75।।
explanation: 'Sugriva has been caught. What is my duty now? I will do what is just. I will destroy that Rakshasa who is in the form of a mountain', thought Maruti.

shloka_text: एवंगृहीतेसुग्रीवेकिंकर्तव्यंमयाभवेत् ।।6.67.74।। यद्वैन्यायंमयाकर्तुंतत्करिष्यामिसर्वधा । भूत्वापर्वतसङ्काशोनाशयिष्यामिराक्षसम् ।।6.67.75।।
explanation: 'Sugriva has been caught. What is my duty now? I will do what is just. I will destroy that Rakshasa who is in the form of a mountain', thought Maruti.

shloka_text: मयाहतेसंयतिकुम्भकर्णेमहाबलेमुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे । विमोचितेवानरपार्थिवे च भवन्तुहृष्टाःप्लवगास्समस्ताः ।।6.67.76।।
explanation: 'Mighty Kumbhakarna shattered by my fist in a duel, and the king of Vanaras delivered, all the monkeys will be rejoiced.'

shloka_text: अथवास्वयमप्येषमोक्षंप्राप्स्यतिपार्थिव । गृहीतोऽयंयदिभवेत्रिदशैस्सासुरोरगैः ।।6.67.77।।
explanation: 'Or else this Sugriva alone can get liberated by fighting by himself with gods, demons and Nagas also, even if he is captured'.

shloka_text: मन्ये न तावदात्मानंबुध्यतेवानराधिपः । शैलप्रहाराभिहतःकुम्भकर्णेनसंयुगे ।।6.67.78।।
explanation: "I think that Sugriva, hit by Kumbhakarna with a mountain, has lost senses and is not able to know."

shloka_text: अयंमुहूर्तात्सुग्रीवोलब्दसंज्ञोमहाहवे । आत्मनोवानराणां च यत्पथ्यंतत्करिष्यति ।।6.67.79।।
explanation: Sugriva will soon regain consciousness and do what is good for Vanaras.

shloka_text: मयातुमोक्षितस्यास्यसुग्रीवस्यमहात्मनः । अप्रीतिश्चभवेत्कष्टाकीर्तिनाशश्चशाश्वतः ।।6.67.80।।
explanation: "If Sugriva is released by me, he will not be happy forever. His fame will be lost."

shloka_text: तस्मान्मुहूर्तंकाङ्क्षिष्येविक्रमंपार्थिवस्यतु । भिन्नं च वानरानीकंतावदाश्वासयाम्यहम् ।।6.67.81।।
explanation: "Therefore, I will see the exhibition of his prowess for a while. Thereafter I shall reinforce the scattered army of Vanaras."

shloka_text: इत्येवंचिन्तयित्वातुहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । भूयःसंस्तम्भयामासवानराणांमहाचमूम् ।।6.67.82।।
explanation: Hanuman, the son of Maruti thinking in this way said to the Vanara army and brought determination.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णोऽथविवेशलङ्कांस्पुरन्तमादायमहाकपिंतम् । विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैःपुष्पाग्य्रवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणः ।।6.67.83 ।
explanation: Then Kumbhakarna taking the great Vanara who started to shake by then, entered Lanka through the roads of lofty mansions from where Rakshasas hailed showering flowers.

shloka_text: लाजगन्धोदवर्षैस्तुसिच्यमानश्सनैश्शनैः । राजवीथ्यास्तुशीतत्वात्संज्ञांप्रापमहाबलः ।।6.67.84।।
explanation: Exceptionally strong Sugriva with parched grain and fragrant water showered on him in the royal path, being cool, regained consciousness.

shloka_text: ततस्ससंज्ञामुपलभ्यकृच्छ्राद्बलीयसस्तस्यभुजान्तरस्थः । अवेक्षमाणःपुरसाजमार्गंविचिन्तयामासमुहुर्महात्मा ।।6.67.85।।
explanation: (Sugriva) being strong and painfully gained senses, from the arms of the great Rakshasa, started looking at the royal path of the city. He was bewildered and started pondering this way.

shloka_text: एवंगृहीतेनकथंनुनामशक्यंमयासम्प्रतिकर्तुमद्य । तथाकरिष्यामियथाहरीणांभविष्यतीष्टं च हितं च कार्यम् ।।6.67.86।।
explanation: 'Caught in this way, how can I do (take action)? I will do what is possible, pleasing, and good to Vanaras now.'

shloka_text: ततःकराग्रैःसहसासमेत्यराजाहरीणाममरेन्द्रशत्रुम् । खरैश्चकर्णौदशनैश्चनासांददंशपार्श्वेषु च कुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.87।।
explanation: There after the king of Vanaras decided to act and tore off the ears of the enemy ruler of gods (Kumbhakarna) with his sharp nails, bit off the nose with his teeth, and sides of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णोहृतकर्णनासोविदारितस्तेनरदैर्नखैश्च । रोषाभिभूतःक्षतजार्द्रगात्रःसुग्रीवमाविध्यपिपेषभूमौ ।।6.67.88।।
explanation: Deprived of ears and nose by Sugriva, splitting with nails and teeth, Kumbhakarna was highly furious and pinning down Sugriva pounded him against the ground, limbs bespattered.

shloka_text: स भूतलेभीमबलाभिपिष्टस्सुरारिभिस्स्सैरभिहन्यमानः । जगामखंवेगवदभ्युपेत्यपुनश्चरामेणसमाजगाम ।।6.67.89।।
explanation: Dropped on the ground by Kumbhakarna of dreadful strength, pressed against the ground surface, Sugriva bounced to the sky to get reunited with Rama.

shloka_text: कर्णनासाविहीनस्तुकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । रराजशोणितैःसिक्तोगिरिःप्रस्रवणैरिव ।।6.67.90।।
explanation: Great hero Kumbhakarna, devoid of ears and nose drenched in blood shone like a mountain in springs.

shloka_text: शोणितार्द्रोमहाकायोराक्षसोभीमविक्रमः । युद्धायाभिमुखोभीमोमनश्चक्रेनिशाचरः ।।6.67.91।। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यःसस्नध्यइवतोयदः । अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारीशुशुभेरावणानुजीः ।।6.67.92।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna of terrific valour and gigantic body, drenched in blood, dark in colour like a mountain of collyrium, resembling evening cloud, the night ranger went towards the battlefield.

shloka_text: शोणितार्द्रोमहाकायोराक्षसोभीमविक्रमः । युद्धायाभिमुखोभीमोमनश्चक्रेनिशाचरः ।।6.67.91।। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यःसस्नध्यइवतोयदः । अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारीशुशुभेरावणानुजीः ।।6.67.92।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna of terrific valour and gigantic body, drenched in blood, dark in colour like a mountain of collyrium, resembling evening cloud, the night ranger went towards the battlefield.

shloka_text: गतेतुतस्मिन् सुरराजशत्रुःक्रोधात्प्रदुद्रावरणायभूयः । अनायुधोऽस्मीतिविचिन्त्यरौद्रोघोरंतदामुद्गरमाससाद ।।6.67.93।।
explanation: Himself (Sugriva) gone, the enemy of the Lord of gods rushed again retreating, "I am ferocious, without weapon." Then seizing an iron mallet, Sugriva went reflecting.

shloka_text: ततस्सपुर्यास्ससहसामहात्मानिष्क्रम्यतद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम् । बभक्षरक्षोयुधिकुम्भकर्णःप्रजायुगान्तानगिरिवप्रवृद्धः ।।6.67.94।।
explanation: The great Kumbhakarna then departing instantly entered into Vanara army consumed them as fire at dissolution consumed people.

shloka_text: बुभुक्षितःशोणइतमांसगृध्नुःप्रविव्यतद्वानरसैन्यमुग्रम् । चखादरक्षांसिहरीन् पिशाचान् ऋक्षांश्चमोहाद्युधिकुम्भकर्णः । यथैवमृत्युर्हरतेयुगान्ते स भक्ष्यामासहरींश्चमुख्यान् ।।6.67.95।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna started seizing principal monkeys in the same way as death at the end of universe. Being famished for flesh and blood he entered the Vanara army in delusion and consumed not only Vanaras but Rakshasas, demons and bears also.

shloka_text: एकंद्वौत्रीन् बहून् क्रुद्धोवानरान्सहराक्षसैः । समादायैकहस्तेनप्रचिक्षेपत्वरन्मुखे ।।6.67.96।।
explanation: Taking one, two, three, and many Vanaras along with Rakshasas hastily with one hand he was gulping them.

shloka_text: सम्प्रस्रवंस्तदामेदश्शोणिते च महाबलः । वध्यमानोनगेन्द्राग्रैर्भक्ष्यामासवानरान् ।।6.67.97।।
explanation: Then the mighty Kumbhakarna while being struck by peaks of mountains, he was feasting on Vanaras fat and blood oozing out from his mouth.

shloka_text: तेभक्ष्यमाणाहरयोरामंजुग्मुस्तदागतिम् । कुम्भकर्णोभृशंक्रुद्धःकपीन् खादन् प्रधावति ।।6.67.98।।
explanation: Being devoured by Kumbhakarna, the Vanaras went for refuge to Rama. Enraged Kumbhakarna followed the Vanaras behind.

shloka_text: शतानिसप्तचाष्टौ च विंशत्रतिंशत्तथैव च । सम्परिष्वज्यबाहुभ्यांखादवनिपरिधावति ।।6.67.99।।
explanation: Stretching his arms on all sides picking hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred and two hundred and three hundred, he ran devouring the vanaras.

shloka_text: मेदोवसाशोणितदिग्धगात्रःकरायवसक्तग्रथितान्त्रमालः । ववर्षशूलानिसतीक्षणदंष्ट्रःकालोयुगान्तस्थइववृद्धः ।।6.67.100।।
explanation: His limbs smeared with fat and blood, with wreaths of entrails hanging on his ears, with sharp teeth, grown in his body to huge size, rained darts like the spirit of death at the end of the world.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् कालेसुमित्रायाःपुत्रःपरबलार्दनः । चकारलक्ष्मणःक्रुद्धोयुद्धंपरपुरञ्जयः ।।6.67.101।।
explanation: At that time, Sumitra's son, Lakshmana, winner of enemy forces, conqueror of forts, enraged went to fight.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णस्यशरान् शरीरेसप्तवीर्यवान् । निचखादाददेचान्यावनिससर्ज च लक्ष्मणः ।।6.67.102।।
explanation: Valiant Lakshmana pierced seven arrows on Kumbhakarna's body and discharged many arrows on him.

shloka_text: पीड्यमानस्तदस्त्रंतुविशेषंतत्सराक्षसः । ततश्चुकोपबलवान्सुमित्रानन्दवर्दनः ।।6.67.103।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna having been tormented, put an end to the dart (of Lakshmana). Mighty Lakshmana there upon flew into a rage.

shloka_text: अथास्यकवचंशुभ्रंजाम्भूनदमयंशुभम् । प्रच्छादयामासशरैस्सन्ध्याभ्रमिवमारुतः ।।6.67.104।।
explanation: Then he covered Kumbhakarna's glittering golden shield with arrows just as the evening wind covered the cloud.

shloka_text: नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यश्शरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । अपीड्यमानश्शुशुभेमेघैस्सूर्यइवांशुमान् ।।6.67.105।।
explanation: Adorned with golden ornaments (Kumbhakarna), covered with darts without being tormented he looked like a dark mountain shining like sun rays covered by clouds.

shloka_text: ततस्सराक्षसोभीमस्सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनम् । सावज्ञमेवप्रोवाचवाक्यंमेघौघनिस्स्वनः ।।6.67.106।।
explanation: Thereupon the Rakshasa sounding like the rumblings of clouds disdainfully spoke these words to Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra.

shloka_text: अन्तकस्याप्यकष्टेन युधि जेतारमाहवे । युध्यतामामभीतेनख्यापितावीरतात्वया ।।6.67.107।।
explanation: "You have exhibited your valour without fear in battle, challenging me who has conquered even Lord of Death without difficulty in battle."

shloka_text: प्रगृहीतायुधस्येहमृत्योरिवमहामृधे । तिष्ठन्नप्रग्रतःपूज्यःकिमुयुद्धप्रदायकः ।।6.67.108।।
explanation: "He who is ready to face me, a rival of Lord of Death in conflict, with weapons in hand in great battle is worthy of honour to me."

shloka_text: ऐरावतंबलेनसमारूढोवृतःसर्वामरैःप्रभुः । नैवशक्रोऽपिसमरेस्थितपूर्वःकदाचन ।।6.67.109।।
explanation: "Indra mounted on the elephant, Airavata surrounded by all Devatas, indeed never stood before me in conflict."

shloka_text: अद्यत्वयाहम्सौमित्रेबालेनापि , नापिपराक्रमैः । तोषितोगन्तुमिच्छामित्यामनुज्ञाप्यराघवम् ।।6.67.110।।
explanation: "Now I am gratified with your valour, though young. Taking leave of you, I wish to go to Raghava."

shloka_text: यत्तुवीर्यबलोत्साहैस्तोषितोऽहंरणेत्वया । राममेवैकमिच्छामिहन्तुंयस्मिन् हतेहतम् ।।6.67.111।।
explanation: "I am gratified by your valour, strength and enthusiasm which has been exhibited by you in the battle. However, I wish to kill Rama alone."

shloka_text: रामेमयात्रनिहतेयेऽन्येस्थास्यन्तिसंयुगे । तानहंयोधयिष्यामिस्वबलेनप्रमाथिना ।।6.67.112।।
explanation: "When Rama has been put to an end by me in conflict, whoever remains can be struck down by my army."

shloka_text: इत्युक्तवाक्यंतद्रक्षःप्रोवाचस्तुतिसंहितम् । मृधेघोरतरंवाक्यंसौमित्रिःप्रहसन्निव ।।6.67.113।।
explanation: When that Rakshasa made such boastful and dreadful statements in the battlefield, laughing heartily, Saumitri replied as follows.

shloka_text: यस्त्वंशक्रादिभिर्वरैरसह्यःप्राप्यपौरुषम् । तत्सत्यंनान्यथावीरदृष्टस्तेऽद्यपराक्रमः ।।6.67.114।। एषदाशरथीरामस्तिष्ठत्यद्रिरिवाचलः ।
explanation: "O Hero! that heroism you have acquired is irresistible even by Indra is true. Now your prowess has been witnessed. Rama stands here, immovable like a mountain."

shloka_text: इतिश्रुत्वाह्यनादृत्यलक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः ।।6.67.115।। अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । राममेवाभिदुद्रावकम्पयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.67.116।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna of mighty strength, the night ranger hearing Lakshmana, rather disregarding his words, overlooking him went alone towards Rama as if shaking the earth.

shloka_text: इतिश्रुत्वाह्यनादृत्यलक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः ।।6.67.115।। अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिंकुम्भकर्णोमहाबलः । राममेवाभिदुद्रावकम्पयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.67.116।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna of mighty strength, the night ranger hearing Lakshmana, rather disregarding his words, overlooking him went alone towards Rama as if shaking the earth.

shloka_text: अथदाशरथींरामोरौद्रमस्त्रंप्रयोजयन् । कुम्भकर्णस्यहृदयेससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।।6.67.117।।
explanation: Sri Rama, son of Dasaratha, now released a sharp arrow presided over by Rudra and fixed into the chest of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: तस्यरामेणविद्धस्यसहसाभिप्रधावतः । अङ्गालमिश्राःक्रुद्धस्यमुखान्निश्चेरुरर्चिषः ।।6.67.118।।
explanation: As Rama hit in anger, at once fire mixed with flames shot forth from Kumbhakarna's mouth.

shloka_text: रामास्त्रविद्धोघोरंवैनदन्राक्षसपुङ्गवः । अभ्यधावतसङ्कृद्धोहरीन् निद्रावयन् रणे ।।6.67.119।।
explanation: Pierced by Rama's missiles, the foremost of the Rakshasas, Kumbhakarna was very angry and rushed towards him dispersing all the vanaras in the battle.

shloka_text: तस्योरसिनिमग्नास्तेशराबर्हिणवाससः । हस्ताच्छास्यपरिभ्रष्टागदाचोर्व्यांपपात ह ।।6.67.120।।
explanation: Adorned by peacock's plumes, those arrows slipped into his breast, he lost senses, his mace naturally dropped down from his hand.

shloka_text: आयुधानि च सर्वाणिविप्राकीर्यन्तभूतले । स निरायुधमात्मानंयदामेनेमहाबलः ।।6.67.121।। मुष्टिभ्यां च चरणाभ्यां च चकारकदनंमहत् ।
explanation: All his weapons scattered on the ground, the mighty Kumbhakarna deprived of weapons thought for himself and created havoc with his feet and fists.

shloka_text: स बाणैरतिविद्धाङ्गःक्षतजेनसमुक्षितः ।।6.67.122।। रुधिरंपरिसुस्रावगिरिःप्रस्रवणंयथा ।
explanation: Pierced by arrows excessively all over his limbs, bathing in blood flowing from the injury was like a mountain with a spring.

shloka_text: स तीव्रेण च कोपेनरुधिरेण च मूर्छितः ।।6.67.123।। वानरान्राक्षसानृक्षान्खादन्विपरिधावति ।
explanation: Kumbhakarna in violent anger, blood flowing from the injury, went about devouring Vanaras, Rakshasas and bears.

shloka_text: अथशृङ्गंसमाविध्यभीमंभीमपराक्रमः । चिक्षेपराममुद्धिश्यबलवानन्तकोपमः ।।6.67.124।।
explanation: Thereupon, Kumbhakarna endowed with terrific valour like God of Death hurled towards Rama a mountain peak whirling it round which split.

shloka_text: अप्राप्तमन्तरारामःसप्तभिस्तमजिह्मगैः । चिच्छेदगिरिशृङ्गंतंपुनःसन्धायकार्मुकम् ।।6.67.125।।
explanation: Rama once again taking the bow, split the peak of the mountain with seven unfailing arrows on its way even before it reached the target.

shloka_text: ततस्तुरामोधर्मात्मातस्यशृङ्गंमहत्तदा ।।6.67.126।। शरैःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्चिच्छेदपुरुषर्षभः ।
explanation: The righteous Rama, a bull among men, taking his arrows adorned with gold split the peak of the mountain.

shloka_text: तन्मेरुशिखराकारंद्योतमानमिवश्रिया ।।6.67.127।। द्वेशतेवानराणां च पतमानमपातयत् ।
explanation: While falling down, Kumbhakarna was like Mount Meru, shining by his splendour was falling down and knocking down two hundred monkeys.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् काले स धर्मात्मालक्ष्मणोराममब्रवीत् ।।6.67.128।। कुम्भकर्णवधेयुक्तोयोगान् परिमृशन्बहून् ।
explanation: At that time, righteous Lakshmana who was attentively deliberating on many plans to kill Kumbhakarna, said to Rama.

shloka_text: नैवायंवानरान्राजन्नविजानातिराक्षसान् ।।6.67.129।। मत्तश्शोणितगन्धे न स्वान् परांश्चैवखादति ।
explanation: "This king intoxicated with the smell of blood is not knowing his own people and foes and devouring both Vanaras and Rakshasas."

shloka_text: साध्वेनमधिरोहस्तुसर्वतोवानरर्षभाः ।।6.67.130।। यूथपाश्चयथामुख्यास्तिष्ठन्त्वस ।
explanation: Let the bulls among Vanaras climb upon him and the foremost of Vanaras and the troops stand all over.

shloka_text: अप्ययंदुर्मतिःकालेगुरुभारप्रपीडितः ।।6.67.131।। प्रपतन्राक्षसोभूमौनान्यान्हन्यात्ल्पवङ्गमान् ।
explanation: Distressed by heavy weight unable to get up evil minded Rakshasa fallen on the ground will not destroy monkeys.

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराजपुत्रस्यधीमतः ।।6.67.132।। तेसमारुरुहुर्हृष्टाःकुम्भकर्णंप्लवङ्गमाः ।
explanation: Having heard the words of the wise Prince, the monkeys collected climbed on Kumbhakarna happily.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्तुसङ्कृद्धस्समारूढःप्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.67.133।। व्यधूनयत्तान्वेगेनदुष्टहस्तीवहस्तिपान् ।
explanation: Enraged Kumbhakarna shook off the monkeys climbed on his body like a harsh elephant shakes off its rider.

shloka_text: तान् न्दृष्टवानिर्धुतान्रामोदुष्टोऽयमितिराक्षसः ।।6.67.134।। समुत्पपातवेगेनधनुरुत्तममाददे ।
explanation: Seeing the Vanaras shaken, Rama went towards the Rakshasa instantly and took out his best bow.

shloka_text: क्रोधरक्तेक्षणोवीरोनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.67.135।। राघवोराक्षसंरोषाभिदुद्राववेगितः । यूथपान्हर्षयन्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णभयार्दितान् ।।6.67.136।।
explanation: Raghava's eyes turned red with anger, went quickly in anger as monkeys and troop leaders oppressed by Kumbhakarna were rejoiced.

shloka_text: क्रोधरक्तेक्षणोवीरोनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.67.135।। राघवोराक्षसंरोषाभिदुद्राववेगितः । यूथपान्हर्षयन्सर्वान्कुम्भकर्णभयार्दितान् ।।6.67.136।।
explanation: Raghava's eyes turned red with anger, went quickly in anger as monkeys and troop leaders oppressed by Kumbhakarna were rejoiced.

shloka_text: स चापमादायभुजङ्गकल्पंधृढज्यमुग्रंतपनीयचित्रम् । हरीन् समाश्वास्यसमुत्पपातरामोनिबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः ।।6.67.137।।
explanation: Rama, taking a formidable bow which resembled a great serpent, with a quiver full of excellent arrows shining in gold that looked beautiful, went forward restoring the confidence of the monkeys.

shloka_text: स वानरगणैस्तैस्तुवृतःपरमदुर्जयः । लक्ष्मणानुचरोरामस्सम्प्रतस्थेमहाबलः ।।6.67.138।।
explanation: Mighty Rama, who is extremely difficult to win over, went with full conviction followed by Lakshmana and surrounded by vanara troops.

shloka_text: स ददर्शमहात्मानंकिरीटिनमरिन्दमम् । शोणितावृतरक्ताक्षंकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् ।।6.67.139।।
explanation: Great Rama, endowed with extraordinary might, saw Kumbhakarna, the tamer of enemies covered with blood and having red eyes.

shloka_text: सर्वान् समभिधावन्तंयथारुष्टंदिशागजम् । मार्गमाणंहरीन्कक्रुद्धंराक्षसैःपरिवारितम् ।।6.67.140।।
explanation: Surrounded by Rakshasas, he was searching for Vanaras, like an elephant, guarding a quarter, searches.

shloka_text: व्निध्यमन्दरसङ्काशंकाञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम् । स्रवन्तंरुधिरंवक्त्राद्वर्षामेघमिवोथतितम् ।।6.67.141।।
explanation: (Kumbhakarna) Adorned with gold armlets, blood flowing from his mouth was like a rain cloud showering from Vindhya or Mandara mountain.

shloka_text: जिह्वयापरिलिह्यन्तंसृक्किणीशोणितेक्षणम् । मृद्नन्तंवानरानीकंकालान्तकयमोपमम् ।। 6.67.142।।
explanation: With blood red eyes, licking the corner of his mouth with his tongue, crushing Vanara army, he looked like God of Death at dissolution.

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवाराक्षसश्रेष्ठंप्रदीप्तानलवर्चसम् । विस्फारयामासतदाकार्मुकंपुरुषर्षभः ।।6.67.143।।
explanation: Seeing the foremost of Rakshasas, shining like fire, Rama, the bull among men stretched his bow.

shloka_text: स तस्यचापनिर्घोषात्कुपितोराक्षसर्षभः । अमृष्यमाणस्तंघोषमभिदुद्रावराघवम् ।।6.67.144।।
explanation: Enraged by the loud sound of the twang of the bow, the bull among Rakshasas unable to bear rushed towards Raghava.

shloka_text: ततस्तुवातोद्धतमेघकल्पंभुजङ्गराजोत्तमभोगबाहुम् । तमापतन्तंधरणीराभमुवाचरामोकुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.145।।
explanation: Thereafter Rama spoke to Kumbhakarna, whose hands were like Vasuki's body, coming towards him to attack on the battlefield like a cloud chased by wind.

shloka_text: आगच्छरक्षोधिपमाविषादमवस्थितोऽहंप्रगृहीतचापः । अवेहिमांराक्षसवंशनाशनंयस्त्वंमुहूर्ताद्भविता ।।6.67.146।।
explanation: "O king of Rakshasas! Come. Do not be despondent. I stand with my bow. In a moment I will destroy you. Look, the Rakshasa clan will be put to an end."

shloka_text: रामोऽयमितिविज्ञायजहासविकृतस्वनम् । अभ्यधावतसङ्ककृद्धोहरीवनिद्रावयन्रणे ।।6.67.147।।
explanation: Knowing that this is Rama, Kumbhakarna laughed in an unnatural manner making a sound and ran after scattering the monkeys in great rage.

shloka_text: पातयन्निवसर्वेषांहृदयनिवनौकसाम् । प्रहस्यविकृतंभीमंसमेघस्न्तितोपमम् ।।6.67.148।। कुम्भकर्णोमहातेजाराघवंवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Highly energetic Kumbhakarna laughing in hideous ways making sounds like rumblings of clouds breaking the hearts of forest rangers spoke these words.

shloka_text: नाहंविराधोविज्ञेयो न कबन्दःखरो न च । न वाली न च मारीचःकुम्भकर्णःसमागतः ।।6.67.149।।
explanation: "I am not Viradha, not Vijeya, not Kabhanda, not also Vali or Maricha. I am Kumbhakarna and have come."

shloka_text: पश्यमेमुद्गरंभीमंसर्वकालायसंमहत् । अनेननिर्जितादेवादानवाश्चपुरामया ।।6.67.150।।
explanation: "See my terrible club made of wrought iron. By this I have won earlier Devatas and Danavas."

shloka_text: विकर्णवासइतिमांनावज्ञातुंत्वमर्हसि । स्वल्पाऽपिहि न मेपीडार्णनासाविनाशनात् ।।6.67.151।।
explanation: "Do not think I have been deprived of ears and nose and look with contempt. I do not have little pain."

shloka_text: दर्शयेक्ष्वाकुशार्दूलवीर्यंगात्रेषुमेलघु । ततस्त्वांभक्षयिष्यामिदृष्टपौरुषविक्रमम् ।।6.67.152।।
explanation: "O Tiger of the Ikshvaku clan! Exhibit your manliness, prowess, and valour on me. I will eat you up later."

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णस्यवचोनिशम्यरामस्सुपुङ्खान् विससर्जन् । तैराहतोवज्रसमवेगैर्नचुक्षुभे न व्यथतेसुरारिः ।।6.67.153।।
explanation: On hearing Kumbhakarna's words Rama was bewildered. He discharged plumed arrows at a speed of thunderbolt. Struck by the arrows the enemy of Devatas was not shaken or agonized.

shloka_text: यैस्सायकैस्सालवरानिकृत्तावालीहतोवानरपुङ्गवश्च । तेकुम्भकर्णस्यतदाशरीरंवज्रोपमं न व्यधयांप्रचक्रुः ।।6.67.154।।
explanation: Those arrows which had cut down the Sala trees and the Vanara leader, Vali, which were like thunderbolts, did not affect Kumbhakarna's body.

shloka_text: स वारिधाराइवसायकास्तान् पिबन् शरीरेणमहेन्द्रशत्रुः । जघानरामस्यशरप्रवेगंव्याविध्यतंमुग्रवेगम् ।।6.67.155।।
explanation: The enemy of Lord Indra drank the arrows through his body and hurled his club at great speed whirling it round and round arrested the arrows of Rama.

shloka_text: ततस्तुरक्षःक्षतजावलिप्तंवित्रासनंदेवमहचमूनाम् । व्याविध्यतंमुद्गरमुग्रवेगंनिद्रावयामासचमूंम् ।।6.67.156।।
explanation: Then Kumbhakarna with his club covered with blood and frightening even the celestials scattered the monkeys.

shloka_text: वायव्यमादायततोमहास्त्रंरामःप्रचिक्षेपनिशाचराय । समुद्गरंतेनजघानबाहुं स कृत्तबाहुस्तुमुलंनाद ।।6.67.157।।
explanation: Thereupon taking up the weapon of Wind God, Rama discharged on the night ranger and severed his right arm with the mace. His arm torn off, Kumbhakarna made uproarious noise.

shloka_text: स तस्यबाहुर्गिरिशृङ्गकल्पःसमुद्गरोराघवबाणकृत्तः । पपाततस्मिन् हरिराजसैन्येजघानतांवानरवाहिनीं ।।6.17.158।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna's arm severed by Rama's arrow was like a mountain peak. It fell on Vanara army too and killed the monkey king's army.

shloka_text: तेवानराभग्नहतावशेषाःपर्यन्तमाश्रित्यतदाविषण्णाः । प्रपीडिताङ्गाददृशुस्सुघोरंनरेन्द्ररक्षोधिपन्निपातम् ।।6.67.159।।
explanation: Then the remaining Vanaras who escaped killing and mutilation went close feeling desperate and witnessed the comb at between Rama and Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णोऽस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहुर्महासिकृत्ताग्रइवाचलेन्द्रः । उत्पाटयामासकरेणवृक्षंततोऽभिदुद्रावरणेनरेन्द्रम् ।।6.67.160।।
explanation: One arm cut off, Kumbhakarna deprived of limb looked like a mountain with peak cut off. Thereafter he seized a palmyra tree and went towards Rama.

shloka_text: स तस्यबाहुंसहतालवृक्षंसमुद्यतंपन्नगभोगकल्पम् । इन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेनजघानरामोबाणेनजाम्भूनदचित्रितेन ।।6.67.161।।
explanation: Then Rama yoking his bow with an arrow charged with Indra's mantra and decked with gold severed Kumbhakarna's arm which was like coils of serpent and held the palmyra tree.

shloka_text: स कुम्भकर्णस्यभुजोनिकृत्तःपपातभूमौगिरिसन्निकाशः । विवेष्टमानोनिजाघनवृक्षान् शैलान्शिलावानरराक्षसांश्च ।।6.67.162।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna who resembled a mountain, his arm severed turning round and round fell on trees, mountains, Vanaras and Rakshasas crushing them.

shloka_text: तंछिन्नबाहुंसमवेक्ष्यरामःसमापतन्तंसहसानदन्तम् । द्वावर्धचन्द्रौनिशितौप्रगृह्यचिच्छेदपादौयुधिराक्षसस्य ।।6.67.163।।
explanation: Perceiving Kumbhakarna with broken arms rushing towards him, Rama at once took a sharp moon shaped arrow and split his feet.

shloka_text: तौतस्यपादौप्रदिशोदिशश्चगिरेर्गुहाश्चैवमहार्णवं च । लङ्कां च सेनांकपिराक्षसानांविनादयन्तौविनिपेततुश्च ।।6.67.164।।
explanation: Both the feet falling on ground made a resounding noise that filled all over the four quarters, all directions, nay all mountains and caves of Trikuta and also Lanka.

shloka_text: निकृत्तबाहुद्विनिकृत्तपादोविदार्यवक्त्रंबडबामुखाभम् । दुद्रावरामंसहसाभिगर्जन् राहुर्यथाचन्द्रमिवान्तऽरिक्षे ।।6.67.165।।
explanation: Arms broken, feet cut off, dilating his mouth like fire, shouting aloud like Rahu entering moon in the sky he rushed to Rama speedily.

shloka_text: अपूरयत्तस्यमुखंशिताग्रैरामश्शरैर्हेमपिनद्धपुङ्खैः । स पूर्णवक्त्रो न शशाकवक्तुंचुकूजकृच्छ्रेणमुमूर्छचापि ।।6.67.166।।
explanation: Rama filled the mouth of Kumbhakarna with his sharp and pointed gold encrusted arrows. Unable to speak the Rakshasa moaned and fainted.

shloka_text: अथाददेसूर्यमरीचिकल्पं स ब्रह्मदण्डान्तककाकलकल्पम् । अरिष्टमैन्द्रंनिशितंसुपुङ्खंरामश्शरंमारुततुल्यवेगम् ।।6.67.167।।
explanation: Then Rama took up the effulgent sun beam like arrow with feathers and the destructive rod of Brahma and the Time spirit that was fatal to enemies that was fast as wind speed and charged with Indra's mantra.

shloka_text: तंवज्रजाम्भूनदचारुपुङ्खंप्रदीप्तसूर्यज्वलनप्रकाशम् । महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यवेगंरामःप्रचिक्षेपनिशाचराय ।।6.67.168।।
explanation: Rama crushed the night ranger to pieces with his arrow encrusted with diamonds and gold, glowing like the Sun 's rays and fire which resembled Indra's thunderbolt, in speed.

shloka_text: स सायकोराघवबाहुचोदितोदिशस्स्वभासादशसम्प्रकाशयन् । विधूमवैश्वानरभीमदर्शनोजगामशक्राशनिवीर्यविक्रमः ।।6.67.169।।
explanation: Discharged from Rama's arm, the terrific weapon went just as the Lord of god's weapon, which was like Indra's thunderbolt burning like fire, shining by its brilliance and went in all directions and cut the head of Vritasura.

shloka_text: स तन्महापर्वतकूटसन्निभंविवृत्तदंष्ट्रंचलचारुकुण्डलम् । चकर्तरक्षोधिपतेश्शिरस्तदायथैववृत्रस्यपुरापुरन्दरः ।।6.67.170।।
explanation: The arrow (of Rama) severed the head of Rakshasa king whose body was like a lofty mountain peak, whose teeth were large and protruded, hanging earrings shaking, just as Indra severed the head of Vritasura earlier.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णशिरोभातिकुण्डलालङ्कृतंमहत् । आदित्येऽभ्युदितेरात्रौमध्यस्थइवचन्द्रमाः ।।6.67.171।।
explanation: The huge head of Kumbhakarna adorned with earrings was like the moon rising between the stars in the heaven at night presided by Aditi, the mother of twin gods.

shloka_text: तद्रामबाणाभिहतंपपातरक्षःशिरःपर्वतसन्निकाशम् । बभञ्जचर्यागृहगोपुराणिप्राकारमुच्चंतमपातयच्च ।।6.67.172।।
explanation: Killed by Rama's arrow, that head of the Rakshasa, which was like a mountain had demolished the walls and houses and peaks of buildings.

shloka_text: तच्चातिकायंहिमहत्प्रकाशंरक्षस्तदातोयनिधौपपात । ग्राहान्परान् मीनवरान्भुजङ्गान् ममर्दभूमिच तदाविवेश ।।6.67.173।।
explanation: The shining huge body of Rakshasa fell into the ocean crushing the other beings in the ocean like alligators, fishes and serpents that entered into the earth.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्हतेब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौमहाबलेसंयतिकुम्भकर्णे । चचालभूर्भूमिधराश्चसर्वेहर्षाच्चदेवास्तुमुलंविनेदुः ।।6.67.174।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, the enemy of Brahmans and Devatas, having been killed, the Earth, all mountains, Devatas highly rejoiced.

shloka_text: ततस्तुदेवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाःसुराश्चभूतानिसुपर्णगुह्यकाः । सयक्षगन्धर्वगणानभोगताःप्रहर्षितारामपराक्रमेण ।।6.67.175।।
explanation: Thereafter the celestial sages and other sages, serpents, Devatas and all beings including eagles and Guhyakas (airborne animals), Yakshas and Gandharvas rejoiced very much at Rama's valour.

shloka_text: ततस्तुतेतस्यवधेनभूरिणामनस्विनोनैरृतराजबान्धवाः । विनेदुरुच्चैर्व्यथितारघूत्तमंहरिंसमीक्ष्यैवयथासुरार्धिताः ।।6.67.176।।
explanation: Thereupon, the courageous kinsfolk of Ravana, resolute in mind, pained by the death of Kumbhakarna, feared the foremost of Raghus, just as elephants feared seeing the Lord of Devatas, and emitted loud cries.

shloka_text: स देवलोकस्यतमोनिहत्यसूर्योयथाराहुमुखाद्विमुक्तः । तथाव्यभासीद्धरिसैन्यमध्येनिहत्यरामोयुधिकुम्भकर्णम् ।।6.67.177।।
explanation: Having killed Kumbhakarna, in the combat, Rama shone brilliantly just as Sun liberated from Rahu's mouth, after dispersing the darkness of the abode of Devatas.

shloka_text: प्रहर्षमीयुर्भवश्चवानराःप्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमैरिवाननैः । अपूजयन् राघवमिष्टभागिनंहतेरिसौभीमबलेदुरासदम् ।।6.67.178।।
explanation: Many Vanaras, with their faces resembling full blown lotuses joyfully laughed and worshipped Rama for getting rid of an enemy of terrific strength.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णंहतंदृष्टवाराघवेणमहात्मना । राक्षसाराक्षसेन्द्रायरावणायन्यवेदयन् ।।6.68.1।।
explanation: Seeing Kumbhakarna slain by the glorious Raghava, the Rakshasas informed Ravana, the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: राजन् स कालसङ्काशस्संयुक्तःकालकर्मणा । विद्राव्यवानरींसेनांभक्षयित्वा च वानरान् ।।6.68.2।।
explanation: "O King! Kumbhakarna, who was equal to the God of Death, devoured and won over the Vanaras, scattered the army, has joined death as a consequence of time (fate)."

shloka_text: प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
explanation: "Your brother Kumbhakarna showed his might for a short time. But by virtue of Rama's energy and arrows, his mountainlike body was reduced to a trunk of dreadful appearance. Bleeding excessively, he was like a mass submerged in an ocean of blood. like a tree caught in forest fire he was blocking the gate of Lanka in ugly form with a head, nose and ears chopped off."

shloka_text: प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
explanation: "Your brother Kumbhakarna showed his might for a short time. But by virtue of Rama's energy and arrows, his mountainlike body was reduced to a trunk of dreadful appearance. Bleeding excessively, he was like a mass submerged in an ocean of blood. like a tree caught in forest fire he was blocking the gate of Lanka in ugly form with a head, nose and ears chopped off."

shloka_text: प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तंतुप्रशान्तोरामतेजसा । कायेनार्थप्रविष्टेनसमुद्रंभीमदर्शनम् ।।6.68.3।। निकृत्तकण्ठोरुभुजोविक्षरन्रुधिरंबहु । रुद्ध्वाद्वारंशरीरेणलङ्कायाःपर्वतोपमः ।।6.68.4।। कुम्भकर्णस्तवभ्राताकाकुत्स्थशरपीडितः । लगण्डभूतोविकृतोदावदग्धइवद्रुमः ।।6.68.5।।
explanation: "Your brother Kumbhakarna showed his might for a short time. But by virtue of Rama's energy and arrows, his mountainlike body was reduced to a trunk of dreadful appearance. Bleeding excessively, he was like a mass submerged in an ocean of blood. like a tree caught in forest fire he was blocking the gate of Lanka in ugly form with a head, nose and ears chopped off."
