shloka_text: तंश्रुत्वाविनिहतंसङ्ख्येकुम्भकर्णंमहाबलम् । रावणश्शोकसन्तप्तोमुमोह च पपात च ।।6.68.6।।
explanation: Hearing that Kumbhakarna of great strength was slain, Ravana immersed in grief became deluded and fell.

shloka_text: पितृव्यंनिहतंश्रुत्वादेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चरुरुदुश्शोकपीडिताः ।।6.68.7।।
explanation: Hearing about uncle's destruction, the sons of Ravana, Devanthaka, Naranthaka, Trisira and Atikaya, roared aloud afflicted by grief.

shloka_text: भ्रातरंनिहतंश्रुत्वारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । महोदरमहापार्श्वौशोकाक्रान्तौबभूवतुः ।।6.68.8।।
explanation: Ravana's brothers, Mahodara and Mahaparsva were overtaken by sorrow on hearing about the unwearied action of Rama and slaying of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: ततःकृच्छ्रात्समासाद्यसंज्ञांराक्षसपुङ्गवः । कुम्भकर्णवधाद्दीनोविललापकुलेन्द्रियः ।।6.68.9।।
explanation: Thereafter the foremost of the Rakshasas regained consciousness with great difficulty and awakened to the situation of Kumbhakarna's destruction, wailed disturbed in mind.

shloka_text: हावीर रिपुदर्पघ्न कुम्भकर्ण महाबल । त्वंमांविहायवैदैवाद्यातोऽसियमसादनम् ।।6.68.10।।
explanation: "Ha! Hero! Kumbhakarna! You, who crushed the pride of the enemy, endowed with great prowess have deserted me and gone to the abode of death, actually by divine will."

shloka_text: ममशल्यमनुद्धृत्यबान्धवानांमहाबल । शत्रुसैन्यंप्रताप्यैकस्त्वंमांसन्त्यज्यगच्छसि ।।6.68.11।।
explanation: "O Kumbhakarna of extraordinary might! You have tormented the enemy army singlehanded with valour. You are going alone leaving me and the kinsfolk."

shloka_text: इदानींखल्वहंनास्मियस्यमेदक्षिणोभुजः । पतितोयंसमाश्रित्य न बिभेमिसुरासुरान् ।।6.68.12।।
explanation: "I who depended on you like my right arm did not fear Devatas or Danavas and I am destroyed now."

shloka_text: कथमेवंविधोवीरोदेवदानवदर्पहा । कालाग्निरुद्राप्रतिमोरणेराघवेणवैहतः ।।6.68.13।।
explanation: "You, who crushed the pride of Devas and Danavas are equal to timespirit and death at dissolution and being a hero, how did you die in the hands of Raghava?"

shloka_text: यस्यतेवज्रनिष्पेषो न कुर्वाद्व्यसनंसदा । स कथंरामबाणार्तंप्रसुप्तोऽसिमहीतले ।।6.68.14।।
explanation: "You are never affected by the strike of thunderbolt. How are you sleeping on the ground hit by Rama's arrows?"

shloka_text: एतेदेवगणास्सार्थमृषिभिर्गगनेस्थिताः । निहतंत्वांरणेदृष्टवानिनदन्तिप्रहर्षिताः ।।6.68.15।।
explanation: "These Devatas and all sages are standing in the sky, seeing the battle and laughing aloud seeing your destruction."

shloka_text: ध्रुवमद्यैवसंहृष्टालब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः । आरोक्ष्यन्तीहदुर्गाणिलङ्काद्वाराणिसर्वशः ।।6.68.16।।
explanation: "Having found an opportunity, all the Vanaras, highly rejoiced, on this very day, will surely climb over the gates of forts of Lanka determined."

shloka_text: राज्येननास्तिमेकार्यंकिंकरिष्यामिसीतया । कुम्भकर्णविहीनस्यजीवितेनास्तिमेमतिः ।।6.68.17।।
explanation: "I have no purpose with the kingdom. What will I do with Sita? I have lost my life and mind with Kumbhakarna's death."

shloka_text: यद्यहंभ्रातृहन्तारं न हन्मियुधिराघवम् । ननुमेमरणंश्रेयो न चेदंव्यर्थजीवितम् ।।6.68.18।।
explanation: "If I do not kill Raghava who killed my brother in battle it is a waste of my life." Thus, thought Ravana.

shloka_text: अद्यैवतंगमिष्यामिदेशंयत्रानुजोमम । न हिभ्रातृ़न् समुत्सृज्यक्षणंजीवितमुत्सहे ।।6.68.19।।
explanation: "This very day, this very minute I shall reach the region where my brother died, I have no interest in life."

shloka_text: देवाहिमांहसिष्यन्तिदृष्टवापूर्वापकारिणम् । कथमिन्द्रंजयिष्यामिकुम्भकर्ण हतेत्वयि ।।6.68.20।।
explanation: "Devatas who were harmed by me earlier will laugh at me now that Kumbhakarna is slain. How will I win Indra?"

shloka_text: तदिदंमामनुप्राप्तंविभीषणवचश्शुभम् । यदज्ञानान्मयातस्य न गृहीतंमहात्मनः ।।6.68.21।।
explanation: "This calamity that has come upon me was because I have not taken such auspicious advice rendered by the great soul Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: विभीषणवचोयावत्कुम्भकर्णप्रहस्तयोः । विनाशोऽयंसमुत्पन्नोमांव्रीडयतिदारुणः ।।6.68.22।।
explanation: "Thus, loss of both Kumbhakarna and Prahastha is dreadful. It is because of not following the words of advice of Vibheeshana totally. It hurts me."

shloka_text: तस्यायंकर्मणःप्राप्तोविपाकोममशोकदः । यन्मयाधार्मिकश्शमान् स निरस्तोविभीषणः ।।6.68.23।।
explanation: "Righteous and prosperous Vibheeshana has been expelled by me earlier. By that action, I have obtained this grief."

shloka_text: एवंविलपमानस्यरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । श्रुत्वाशोकाभितप्तस्यत्रिशिरावाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.69.1।।
explanation: Hearing the lamentations of the evilminded Ravana, Trisira spoke to him.

shloka_text: एवमेवमहावीर्योहतोनस्तातमध्यमः । न तुसत्पुरुषाराजन्विलपन्तियथाभवान् ।।6.69.2।।
explanation: "There is no doubt that Kumbhakarna, who is your middle father and uncle, was also endowed with great prowess. He has been killed. O King! Good men like you do not wail."

shloka_text: नूनंत्रिभुवनस्यापिपर्याप्तस्त्वमसिप्रभो । स कस्मात्प्राकृतइवशोचस्यात्मानमीदृशम् ।।6.69.3।।
explanation: "O King! You are a conqueror of the three worlds. Why do you wail like a common man?"

shloka_text: ब्रह्मदत्ताऽस्तितेशक्तिःकवचस्सायकोधनुः । सहस्रखरसंयुक्तोरथोमेघस्वनोमहान् ।।6.69.4।।
explanation: "You are bestowed by Brahma with a javelin, a shield and an arrow and a chariot yoked by a thousand donkeys making rumbling sounds like a cloud."

shloka_text: त्वयाऽसकृद्विशस्त्रेणविशस्तादेवदानवाः । स सर्वायुधसम्पन्नोराघवंशास्तुमर्हसि ।।6.69.5।।
explanation: "Devas and Danavas have been won over by you, deprived of weapons also. Now endowed with all weapons you will be able to win Raghava."

shloka_text: कामंतिष्ठमहाराजनिर्गमिष्याम्यहंरणम् । उद्धरिष्यामितेशत्रूंन्गरुडःपन्नगानिव ।।6.69.6।।
explanation: "O King! Stay on. I will move forth to the battlefield and uproot your enemy like Garuda uprooted serpents."

shloka_text: शम्बरोदेवराजेननरकोविष्णुवायथा । तथाऽद्यशयितारामोमयायुधिनिपातितः ।।6.69.7।।
explanation: "Just as Lord of Devas by Sambara, and Vishnu by Naraka, in the same way Rama will also be destroyed struck by me."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वात्रिशिरसोवाक्यंरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । पुनर्जातमिवात्मानंमन्यतेकालचोदितः ।।6.69.8।।
explanation: Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, hearing Trisira's words thought that impelled by destiny that he was reborn.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वात्रिशिरसोवाक्यंदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । अतिकायश्चतेजस्वीबभूवुर्युद्धहर्षिताः ।।6.69.9।।
explanation: Hearing Trisira's words both Devanthaka and Naranthaka and glorious Atikaya became enthusiastic for combat.

shloka_text: ततोऽहमहमित्येवगर्जन्तोनैरृतर्षभाः । रावणस्यसुतावीराश्शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः ।।6.69.10।।
explanation: Then Ravana's sons, the heroes, and bulls among ogres, equal to Indra in valour, roared saying, "I will start", "I will lead."

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षगतास्सर्वेसर्वेमायाविशारदाः । सर्वेत्रिदशदर्पघ्नास्सर्वे च रणदुर्जयाः ।।6.69.11।।
explanation: All (sons of Ravana) are capable of coursing through the sky, experts in conjuring tricks, capable of crushing the pride of Devatas and all, are fierce in fighting.

shloka_text: सर्वेसुबलसम्पन्नास्सर्वेविस्तीर्णकीर्तयः । सर्वेसमरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्तेस्मपराजिताः ।।6.69.12।। देवैरपिसगन्धर्वैस्सकिन्नरमहोरगैः ।
explanation: All sons of Ravana possessed stupendous strength, all were very famous, and never got defeated in war be it Gandharvas, Kinnaras or even gods will get vanquished by them.

shloka_text: सर्वेस्त्रविदुषोवीरास्सर्वेयुद्धविशारदाः ।।6.69.13।। सर्वेप्रसवरविज्ञानास्सर्वेलब्धवरास्तथा ।
explanation: All were experts in the use of weapons, all were heroes and skilled in warfare, knowledgeable in scriptures, so also all were blessed with boons.

shloka_text: सतैस्तथाभास्करतुल्यवर्चसैःपुस्त्रैर्वृतश्शत्रुबलप्रमार्दनैः । रराजराजामघवान्यथामरै ।र्वृतोमहादानवदर्पनाशनैः ।।6.69.14।।
explanation: Surrounded by his sons, who matched Sun in brilliance and capable of crushing the pride of foes, great in destroying immortals, Ravana shone like Lord gods.

shloka_text: स पुत्रान् सम्परिष्वज्यभूषयित्वा च भूषणैः । आशीर्भिश्चप्रशस्ताभिःप्रेषयामाससम्युगे ।।6.69.15।।
explanation: Ravana embraced his sons, decked them with ornaments and jewels and enriched them and offered benediction and sent to encounter.

shloka_text: युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौचापिरावणः । रक्षणार्थंकुमाराणांप्रेषयामाससंयुगे ।।6.69.16।।
explanation: Ravana sent his two brothers Yuddhonmatta and Matta for the protection of his sons for defence in combat.

shloka_text: तेऽभिवाद्यमहात्मानंरावणंरिपुरावणम् । कृत्वाप्रदक्षिणंचैवमहाकायाःप्रतस्थिरे ।।6.69.17।।
explanation: Those heroes greeting gigantic Ravana, went around him clockwise (as per tradition) and departed.

shloka_text: सर्वौषधीभिर्गन्धैश्चसमालभ्यमहाबलाः । निर्जग्मुर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठाषडेतेयुद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.69.18।।
explanation: The six leaders endowed with great strength, anointing themselves with fragrance, which can ward off injury went to fight.

shloka_text: त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ । महोदरमहापार्श्वौनिर्जग्मुःकालचोदिताः ।।6.69.19।।
explanation: Trisira, also Atikaya, Devanthaka, Naranthaka, Mahodara and Mahaparsva impelled by destiny went.

shloka_text: ततस्सुदर्शनंनागंनीलजीमूतसन्निभम् । ऐरावतकुलेजातमारुरोहमहोदरः ।।6.69.20।।
explanation: Thereafter Mahodara mounted on an elephant born of Airavata (Indra 's elephant) family, by name Sudarsana went.

shloka_text: सर्वायुधसमायुक्तंतूणीभिश्चस्वलङ्कृतम् । रराजगजमास्थायसवितेवास्तमूर्धनि ।।6.69.21।।
explanation: Ready with all kinds of weapons, quivers as well mounted on elephants shone like the setting Sun in the west.

shloka_text: हयोत्तमसमायुक्तंसर्वायुधसमाकुलम् । आरुरोहरथश्रेष्ठंत्रिशिरारावणात्मजः ।।6.69.22।।
explanation: Ravana's brother, Trisira went mounted on a chariot yoked to the best of horses with all kinds of weapons.

shloka_text: त्रिशिरारथमास्थायविरराजधनुर्धरः । सविद्युदुल्कश्शैलाग्रेस्सेन्द्रइवाम्बुदः ।।6.69.23।।
explanation: Wielding a bow and sitting like a leader in the chariot Trisira shone as if attended by lightning, meteors, light, and rainbows.

shloka_text: त्रिभिःकिरीटैश्शुशुभेत्रिशिरास्सरथोत्तमे । हिमवानिशैलेन्द्रस्त्रिभिःकाञ्चनपर्वतैः ।।6.69.24।।
explanation: Trisira seated in the best of chariots, with his three heads adorned with crowns shone like the golden mountain, Himalayas with its three peaks.

shloka_text: अतिकायोऽपितितेजस्वीराक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्तदा । आरुरोहरथश्रेष्ठंश्रेष्ठस्सर्वधनुष्मताम् ।।6.69.25।।
explanation: Then Atikaya the very bright son of Rakshasa king, foremost of all archers mounted on the best of chariots.

shloka_text: सुचक्राक्षंसुसंयुक्तंस्वनुकर्षंसुकूबरम् । तूणीबाणासनैर्दीप्तंप्रासासिपरिघाकुलम् ।।6.69.26।।
explanation: The chariot (of Atikaya) had excellent wheels, well fitted with strong axles, stout poles, equipped with quivers and bows, with best of spears, bars, and swords.

shloka_text: सकाञ्चनविचित्रेणमकुटेनविराजता । भूषणैश्चबभौमेरुःप्रभाभिरिवभासयन् ।।6.69.27।।
explanation: His wonderful coronet encrusted with gold was shining, sparkling, and looked splendid like the Meru Mountain.

shloka_text: स रराजरथेतस्मिन् राजसूनुर्महाबलः । वृतोनैरृतशार्दूलैर्वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः ।।6.69.28।।
explanation: The tiger among ogres (Atikaya) surrounded by the great army of ogres, the prince was shining in the chariot like Indra, the king of gods and wielder of thunderbolt.

shloka_text: हयमुच्चैश्श्रवःप्रख्यंश्वेतंकनकभूषणम् । मनोजवंमहाकायमारुरोहनरान्तकः ।।6.69.29।।
explanation: Naranthaka, mounted on Uchaisrava, the white horse, decked in gold, was swift as thought in speed.

shloka_text: गृहीत्वाप्रासमुल्काभंविरराजनरान्तकः । शक्तिमादायतेजस्वीगुहशशिखिगतोयथा ।।6.69.30।।
explanation: Naranthaka seizing a barbed missile like a burning spear, looked like son of Lord Siva wielding javelin in hand.

shloka_text: देवान्ककस्समादायपरिघंवज्रभूषणम् । परिगृह्यगिरिंदोर्भ्यांवपुर्विष्णोर्विडम्बयन् ।।6.69.31।।
explanation: Devanthaka, holding a bar encrusted with diamonds in both hands, seemed like Vishnu in disguise with a mountain (to churn the milky ocean).

shloka_text: महापार्श्वोमहाकायोगदामादायवीर्यवान् । विरराजगदापाणिःकुबेरइवसंयुगे ।।6.69.32।।
explanation: Mahaparsva holding an ace in hand in the war shone like Kubera.

shloka_text: तेप्रतस्थुर्महात्मानोऽमरावत्यास्सुराइव । तान् गजैश्चतुरङ्गैश्चरथैश्चाम्बुन्दिस्स्वनैः ।।6.69.33।। अनूत्पेतुर्महात्मानोराक्षसाःप्रवरायुधाः ।
explanation: Those great souls followed by elephants, horses, Rakshasas with superb weapons sounding like the rumbling of rainy clouds went like gods of Amaravati.

shloka_text: तेविरेजुर्महात्मानःकुमारास्सूर्यवर्चसः ।।6.69.34।। किरीटिनश्रशियाजुष्टाग्रहादीप्ताइवाम्बरे ।
explanation: The great princes were wearing crowns resplendent like the Sun and glowing like planets in the sky.

shloka_text: प्रगृहीताबभौतेषांशस्त्राणामावळिस्सिता ।।6.69.35।। शारदाभ्रप्रतीकाशाहंसावळिरिवाम्बरे ।
explanation: The princes, grasping the white weapons shone like flocks of white cranes in the dark autumnal clouds in the sky.

shloka_text: मरणंवापिनिश्चित्यशत्रूणांवापराजयम् ।।6.69.36।। इतिकृत्वामतिंवीरानिर्जग्मुस्संयुगार्थिनः ।
explanation: Those heroes determined to defeat the enemy even if it meant death and went thinking for the combat.

shloka_text: जगर्जुश्चप्रणेदुश्चचिक्षिपुश्चापिसायकान् ।।6.69.37।। जगृहुश्चमहात्मानोनिर्वातायुद्धदुर्मदाः ।
explanation: The great Rakshasas who were fierce in combat went roaring shouting loudly and discharging arrows.

shloka_text: क्ष्वेळिडितास्फोटिनिनदैश्चचाल च वसुन्दरा ।।6.69.38।। रक्षसांसिंहनादैश्चसंस्फोटेवतदाम्बरम् ।
explanation: By the sound of their clapping of arms and their lion roar it was as though the sky was breaking and the earth was shaking.

shloka_text: अभिनिष्क्रम्यमुदिताराक्षसेन्द्रामहाबलाः ।।6.69.39।। ददृशुर्वानरानीकंसमुद्यतशिलानगम् ।
explanation: Departing from there the Rakshasa army saw Vanara army ready with many rocks.

shloka_text: हरयोपिमहात्मानोददृशुर्नेरृतम् ।।6.69.40।। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंसमुद्यतमहायुधम् ।।6.69.41।। दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैस्सर्वतोनैरृतैर्वृतम् ।
explanation: The huge monkeys also saw groups of elephants, horses and chariots and heard hundreds of bells of the chariots and Rakshasas all over like groups of dark clouds with huge weapons glowing like fire and Sun surrounded by Rakshasa army.

shloka_text: हरयोपिमहात्मानोददृशुर्नेरृतम् ।।6.69.40।। हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । नीलजीमूतसङ्काशंसमुद्यतमहायुधम् ।।6.69.41।। दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैस्सर्वतोनैरृतैर्वृतम् ।
explanation: The huge monkeys also saw groups of elephants, horses and chariots and heard hundreds of bells of the chariots and Rakshasas all over like groups of dark clouds with huge weapons glowing like fire and Sun surrounded by Rakshasa army.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्टवाबलमायान्तंलब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.42।। समुद्यतमहाशैलास्सम्प्रणेदुर्महाबला । अमृष्यमाणारक्षांसिप्रतिनर्दन्तवानराः ।।6.69.43।।
explanation: Seeing the Rakshasa army approaching, the monkeys found an opportunity to attack them and collected huge mountains, deadly strong trees in great joy unable to tolerate roared in return.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्टवाबलमायान्तंलब्धलक्षाःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.42।। समुद्यतमहाशैलास्सम्प्रणेदुर्महाबला । अमृष्यमाणारक्षांसिप्रतिनर्दन्तवानराः ।।6.69.43।।
explanation: Seeing the Rakshasa army approaching, the monkeys found an opportunity to attack them and collected huge mountains, deadly strong trees in great joy unable to tolerate roared in return.

shloka_text: ततस्समुद्घुष्टरवंनिशम्य।रक्षोगणावानरयूथपानाम् । अमृष्यमाणाःपरहर्षमुग्रं।महाबलाःभीमतरंविनेदुः ।।6.69.44।।
explanation: There upon the Vanara leaders, endowed with extraordinary prowess, beholding the joy of Rakshasa troops, unable to bear roared dreadfully.

shloka_text: तेराक्षसबलंघोरंप्रविश्यहरियूथपाः । विचेरुरुद्यतैश्शैलैर्नगाश्शिखरिणोयथा ।।6.69.45।।
explanation: Those monkey leaders entering dreadful Rakshasa army uplifted rocks and mountains with trees and shone.

shloka_text: केचिदाकाशमाविश्यकेचिदुर्व्यांप्लवङ्गमाः । रक्षस्सैन्येषुसङ्कृद्धाःश्चेरुर्द्रुमशिलायुधाः ।।6.69.46।।
explanation: Some monkeys springing into the sky, while some staying on earth, with trees, rocks as weapons, enraged, ranged the Rakshasa army.

shloka_text: द्रुमांश्चविपुलस्कन्थान् गृह्यवानरपुङ्गवाः । तद्युद्धमभवद्घोरंरक्षोवानरसङ्कुलम् ।।6.69.47।।
explanation: Vanara leaders seizing huge branches of trees fought a frightening war with Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तेपादपशिलाश्शैलैश्चक्रुर्वृष्टिमनूपमाम् । बाणौघैर्वार्यमाणाश्चहरयोभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.69.48।।
explanation: The Vanaras of dreadful valour and unparalleled might waged with trees, rock and mountain when obstructed by the Rakshasas।।

shloka_text: सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्चरणेराक्षसवानराः । शिलाभिश्चूर्णयामासुर्यातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.69.49।।
explanation: The Rakshasas and Vanaras enthusiastic in the battlefield roared like lion. The Vanaras pounded the Rakshasas with rocks.

shloka_text: नर्जघ्नुस्संयुगेक्रुद्धाःकवचाभरणावृतान् । केचिद्रथगतावनीरान्गजवाजिगतानपि ।।6.69.50।।
explanation: In the combat, the enraged Vanaras killed Rakshasas decked with shields and ornaments. Some killed the ones mounted on chariots, elephants, and horses.

shloka_text: निर्जघ्नुस्सहसाऽप्लुत्ययातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः । शैलशृङ्गाचिताङ्गाश्चमुष्टिभिर्वान्तलोचनाः ।।6.69.51।। चेरुःपेतुश्चनेदुश्चतत्रराक्षसपुङ्गवाः ।
explanation: The Rakshasa leaders, hit by the blows of Vanaras, fell down on the mountain peaks, trembling with their eyes protruded by the blows of fists.

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्चशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिदुःकपिकुञ्जरान् ।।6.69.52।। शूलमुद्गरखडगैश्चजघ्नुःप्रासैश्चशक्तिभिः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas also pierced with arrows the foremost of the monkeys and struck with tridents swords and lances.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यंपातयामासुःपरस्परजयैषिणः ।।6.69.53।। रिपुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गास्तत्रवानरराक्षसाः
explanation: Their limbs stained with the blood of foes, both Vanaras and Rakshasas eager to conquer one another started striking one another.

shloka_text: ततश्शैलैश्चखडगैश्चविसृष्टैर्हरिराक्षसैः ।।6.69.54।। मुहूर्तेनावृताभूमिरभवच्छोणिताप्लुता ।
explanation: Then in a short while the battlefield was covered with blood and rocks and swords used by the monkeys and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: विकीर्णैःपर्वताकारैरक्षोभिररिमर्दनैः ।।6.69.55।। आसीद्वसुमतीपूर्णातदायुद्धमदान्वितैः ।
explanation: There, the battlefield was filled with mountain like forms of Rakshasas drunk with the pride of warfare, lying scattered all over.

shloka_text: आक्षिप्ताःक्षिप्यमाणाश्चभग्नशूलाश्चवानरैः ।।6.69.56।। पुनरङ्गैस्तदाचक्रुरासन्नायुद्धमद्भुतम् ।
explanation: Vanaras, were lifting and dropping the scattered Rakshasas, breaking the tridents and a wonderful war went on using their limbs.

shloka_text: वानरान्वानरैरेवजघ्नुस्तेनैरृतर्षभाः ।।6.69.57।। राक्षसान्राक्षसैरेवजघ्नुस्तेवानराअपि ।
explanation: The bull among Rakshasas struck at Vanaras with other Vanaras and the monkeys struck Rakshasas with other Rakshasas.

shloka_text: आक्षिप्य च शिलास्तेषांनिजघ्नाराक्षसाहरीन् ।।6.69.58।। तेषांचाछचिद्यशस्त्राणिजघ्नूरक्षांसिवानराः ।
explanation: The monkeys struck at the Rakshasas taking the weapons left over and tearing the weapons of the Rakshasas and the Vanaras also struck the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: निजघ्नुश्शैलशूलार्स्सैर्भिभिदुश्चपरस्परम् ।।6.69.59।। सिंहनादान्विनेदुश्चरणेराक्षसावानराः ।
explanation: In the battlefield both Vanaras and Rakshasas struck at one another with their head, rocks and swords and emitted lion roar.

shloka_text: छिन्नवर्णतनुत्राणाराक्षसावानरैर्हताः ।।6.69.60।। रुधिरंप्रसृतास्तत्ररससारमिवद्रुमाः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas killed by Vanaras, their shields and weapons broken, blood flowed from their limbs just as sap exudes from broken trees.

shloka_text: रथेन च रथंचापिवारणेनैववारणम् ।।6.69.61।। हयेन च हयंकेचिन्निजघ्नुर्वानरारणे ।
explanation: In the battlefield a chariot with another chariot, an elephant with another elephant, a horse with another horse struck one another.

shloka_text: क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्द्रैश्चभल्लैश्चनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.69.62।। राक्षसावानरेन्द्राणांबिभिदुःपादपान् शिलाः ।
explanation: Rakshasas shattered the Vanara leaders with horseshoe shaped, halfmoon shaped, spear shaped sharp arrows, as well as trees and rocks.

shloka_text: विकीर्णैपर्वताग्रैश्चद्रुमैछशिनैश्चसंयुगे ।।6.69.63।। हतैश्चकपिरक्षोभिर्दुर्गमावसुधाऽभवत् ।
explanation: The battlefield, covered with broken trees and mountains, fallen vanaras and rakshasas, seemed difficult to tread on ground.

shloka_text: तेवानरागर्वितहृष्टचेष्टास्सङ्ग्राममासाद्यभयंविम । युद्धंस्मसर्वेसहराक्षसैस्सैयुधाश्चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः ।।6.69.64।।
explanation: Those Vanaras leaving behind fear, reaching the war field, rejoicing with pride, not at all depressed, carried out war with Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रवृत्तेतुमुलेविमर्देप्रहृष्यमाणेषुवलीमुखेषु । निपात्यमानेषु च राक्षसेषुमहर्षयोदेवगणाश्चनेदुः ।।6.69.65।।
explanation: As the conflict progressed and tumultuous fighting was on, Vanaras were feeling exultant and seeing Rakshasas struck down the ascetics and Devatas made loud noises in joy.

shloka_text: ततोहयंमारुततुल्यवेगमारुह्यशक्तिंनिशितांप्रगृह्य । नरान्तकोवानरराजसैन्यंमहार्णवंमीनइवाविवेश ।।6.69.66।।
explanation: Then Naranthaka, mounted on horseback went at wind speed taking hold of javelin and entered Vanara army just as fish entered the ocean.

shloka_text: स वानरान् सप्तशतानिवीरःप्रासेनदीप्तेनन्वििर्बिभेद । एकःक्षणेनेन्द्ररिपुर्महात्माजघानसैन्यंहरिपुङ्गवानाम् ।।6.69.67।।
explanation: Great hero (Naranthaka) single handed persistently destroyed seven hundred Vanaras with his glowing spear. In that way the enemy of Indra shattered Vanara army and monkey leaders.

shloka_text: ददृशुश्चमहात्मानंहयपृष्ठेप्रतिष्ठितम् । चरन्तंहरिसैन्येषुविद्याधरमहर्षयः ।।6.69.68।।
explanation: Vidhyadhara, the great sage, witnessed Naranthaka moving seated on the horseback firmly.

shloka_text: स तस्यददृशेमार्गोमांसशोणितकर्दमः । पतितैःपर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः ।।6.69.69।।
explanation: On the way he saw flesh and blood fallen like a heap of a mountain covered fully with Vanaras.

shloka_text: यावद्विक्रमितुंबुधदिंचक्रुःप्लवगपुङ्गवाः । तावदेतानतिक्रम्यनिर्बिभेदनरान्तकः ।।6.69.70।।
explanation: Naranthaka went past the Vanara leaders all over even before they attempted, he destroyed them.

shloka_text: ददाहहरिसैन्यानिवनानीवविभावसुः । यावदुत्पाटयामासुर्वृक्षान्शैलान्वनौकसः ।।6.69.71।। तावत्प्रासहताःपेतुर्वज्रकृत्ताइवाचलाः ।
explanation: Uplifting his lance in the battle, Naranthaka consumed the Vanara troops as fire would burn up forests even before the Vanaras uprooted trees and rocks. many Vanaras fell like mountains hit by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: ज्वलन्तम्प्रासमुद्यम्यसङ्ग्रामान्तेनरान्तकः ।।6.69.72।। दिक्षुसर्वासुबलवान् विचचारनरान्तकः । प्रमृद्नन्सर्वतोयुद्धेप्रावृटकालेयथानिलः ।।6.69.73।।
explanation: Mighty Naranthaka, the destroyer of humans, ranged over all sides in all directions in the battlefield, like the wind in the rainy season, taking a burning spear and crushing everything.

shloka_text: ज्वलन्तम्प्रासमुद्यम्यसङ्ग्रामान्तेनरान्तकः ।।6.69.72।। दिक्षुसर्वासुबलवान् विचचारनरान्तकः । प्रमृद्नन्सर्वतोयुद्धेप्रावृटकालेयथानिलः ।।6.69.73।।
explanation: Mighty Naranthaka, the destroyer of humans, ranged over all sides in all directions in the battlefield, like the wind in the rainy season, taking a burning spear and crushing everything.

shloka_text: न शेकुर्भाषितुंवीरा न स्थातुंस्पन्दितुंभयात् । उत्पतन्तंस्थितंयान्तंसर्वान्विव्याधवीर्यवान् ।।6.69.74।।
explanation: The gallant monkeys got terrified and could not flee, nor stand, nor move. The audacious Naranthaka marching ahead pierced the Vanaras either marching or jumping or stationary.

shloka_text: एकेनानन्तकल्पेनप्रासेनादित्यतेजसा । भग्नानिहरिसैन्यानिनिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.69.75।।
explanation: With lance that looked like death and the spear glowing like the Sun, Naranthaka routed the Vanaras, who fell down.

shloka_text: वज्रनिष्पेषदृशंप्रासस्याभिनिपातनम् । न शेकुर्वानरास्सोढुंतेविनेदुर्महास्वनम् ।।6.69.76।।
explanation: Unable to bear the very severe impact of the strike of the spear which was like the strike of thunderbolt the Vanaras cried making loud noise.

shloka_text: पततांहरिवीराणांरूपाणिप्रचकाशिरे । वज्रभिन्नाग्रकूटानांशैलानांपततामिव ।।6.69.77।।
explanation: The forms of the monkey heroes fallen down unconscious shone like mountain peaks struck by the thunderbolt and fallen.

shloka_text: येतुपूर्वंमहात्मानःकुम्भकर्णेनपातिताः । तेस्वस्थावानरश्रेष्ठास्सुग्रीवमुपतस्थिरे ।।6.69.78।।
explanation: The Vanaras who were struck by Kumbhakarna and fallen unconscious, came and stood before Sugriva.

shloka_text: विप्रेक्षमाणस्सुग्रीवोददर्शहरिवाहिनीम् । नरान्तकभयत्रस्तांविद्रवन्तीमितस्ततः ।।6.69.79।।
explanation: Sugriva looked around all over the monkey troops running here and there out of fear of Naranthaka.

shloka_text: विद्रुतांवाहिनींदृष्टवा स ददर्शनरान्तकम् । गृहीतप्रासमायान्तंहयपृष्ठेप्रतिष्ठितम् ।।6.69.80।।
explanation: (Sugriva) saw the Vanaras troops running and Naranthaka seated on horseback advancing with a spear.

shloka_text: अथोवाचमहातेजास्सुग्रीवोवानराधिपः । कुमारमङ्गदंवीरंशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम् ।।6.69.81।।
explanation: Sugriva, the Lord of Vanaras seeing (Naranthaka advancing) spoke to his son Angada who resembled Indra in valour.

shloka_text: गच्छत्वंराक्षसंवीरोयोऽसौतुरगमास्थितः । क्षोभयन्तहरिबलंक्षिप्रंप्राणैर्वियोजय ।।6.69.82।।
explanation: "Oh! March ahead and immediately release the life of the Rakshasa seated on horseback terrifying the Vanara army."

shloka_text: स भर्तुर्वचनंश्रुत्वानिष्पपाताङ्गदतः । अनीकान्मेघसङ्काशादंशुमानिववीर्यवान् ।।6.69.83।।
explanation: On hearing the king's words, Angada went just as the sun rays comes out of a cluster of clouds.

shloka_text: शैलसङ्घातसङ्काशोहरीणामुत्तमोऽङ्गदः । रराजाङ्गदसन्नद्धस्सधातुरिवपर्वतः ।।6.69.84।।
explanation: Angada, the best of the Vanaras, adorned with arm lets resembled masses of rocks and shone like a mountain with metal streaks.

shloka_text: निरायुधोमहातेजाःकेवलंनखदंष्ट्रवान् । नरान्तकमभिक्रम्यवालिपुत्रोऽब्रवीद्वचः ।।6.69.85।।
explanation: Brilliant Angada, unarmed only with nails and teeth (to fight) advanced towards Naranthaka and spoke these words.

shloka_text: तिष्ठकिंप्राकृतैरेभिर्हरिभिस्त्वंकरिष्यसि । अस्मिन्वज्रसमस्पर्शंप्रासंक्षिपममोरसि ।।6.69.86।।
explanation: "Stop! What can you do with these common monkeys? Throw your spear at me, which equals thunderbolt."

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाप्रचुक्रोधनरान्तकः । सन्दश्यदशनैरोष्ठंन्वििश्श्वस्यभुजङ्गवत् ।।6.69.87।। अभिगम्याङ्गदंक्रुद्धोवालिपुत्रंनरान्तकः । प्रासंसमाविध्यतदाङ्गदायसमुज्ज्वलन्तंसहसोत्ससर्ज । स वालिपुत्रोरसिवज्रकल्पेबभूवभग्नोन्यपतच्चभूमौ ।।6.69.88।।
explanation: Hearing Angada's words Naranthaka flew into a rage. Biting his lips with teeth, hissing like a serpent Naranthaka stood before Angada. He hurled his spear glowing like fire on Angada's chest violently. It struck Angada and shattered, went round, and fell.

shloka_text: अङ्गदस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाप्रचुक्रोधनरान्तकः । सन्दश्यदशनैरोष्ठंन्वििश्श्वस्यभुजङ्गवत् ।।6.69.87।। अभिगम्याङ्गदंक्रुद्धोवालिपुत्रंनरान्तकः । प्रासंसमाविध्यतदाङ्गदायसमुज्ज्वलन्तंसहसोत्ससर्ज । स वालिपुत्रोरसिवज्रकल्पेबभूवभग्नोन्यपतच्चभूमौ ।।6.69.88।।
explanation: Hearing Angada's words Naranthaka flew into a rage. Biting his lips with teeth, hissing like a serpent Naranthaka stood before Angada. He hurled his spear glowing like fire on Angada's chest violently. It struck Angada and shattered, went round, and fell.

shloka_text: तंप्रासमालोक्यतदाविभग्नंसुपर्णकृत्तोरगभोगकल्पम् । तलंसमुद्यम्य स वालिपुत्रस्तुरङ्गमतस्यजघानमूर्ध्नि ।।6.69.89।।
explanation: Then Vali's son beholding the broken and shattered spear fallen like the coils of serpent, raised his palm and struck at the head of Naranthaka's horse.

shloka_text: निमग्नतालुस्फ्सुटिताक्षितारोनिष्क्रान्तजिह्वोऽचलसन्निकाशः । स तस्यवाजीनिपपातभूमौतलप्रहारेणविशीर्णमूर्धा ।।6.69.90।।
explanation: His horse, which closely resembled a mountain, fell on the ground, its head broken, cheeks drawn in, eyeballs broken, tongue got ejected by the stroke of the palm of Angada.

shloka_text: नरान्तकःक्रोधवशंजगामहतंतुरङ्गंपतितंनिरीक्ष्य । स मुष्टिमुद्यम्यमहाप्रभावोजघानशीर्षेयुधि वालिपुत्रम् ।।6.69.91।।
explanation: Observing the horse fallen, Naranthaka, endowed with great power, overcome by anger raised his fist and struck at the head of Vali's son.

shloka_text: अथाङ्गदोमुष्टिविशीर्णमूर्धासुस्रावतीव्रंरुधिरंभृशोष्णम् । मुहुर्विजज्वालमुमोहचापिसंज्ञांसमासाद्यविसिष्मिये च ।।6.69.92।।
explanation: Angada's head smashed by the blow of the fist of Naranthaka, hot blood flowed rapidly for a while. Recovering from delusion, gaining consciousness he wondered at the strength of Naranthaka.

shloka_text: अथाङ्गदोमृत्युसमानवेगंसंवर्त्यमुष्टिंगिरिशृङ्गकल्पम् । निपातयामासतदामहात्मानरान्तकस्योरसिवालिपुत्रः ।।6.69.93।।
explanation: Angada clenching his fist, whose vehemence was equal to vehemence of death coming down from the top of the mountain peak, brought down Naranthaka.

shloka_text: स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नवक्षाज्वालावमन्शोणितदिग्धगात्रः । नरान्तकोभूमितलेपपातयथाऽचलोवज्रनिपातभग्नः ।।6.69.94।।
explanation: Naranthaka's chest having been split by a blow on his chest, vomiting flaming blood from his throat was as if shattered by the stroke of lightning fell down like a mountain.

shloka_text: अथान्तरिक्षेत्रिदशोत्तमानांवनौकसांचैवमहाप्रणादः । बभूवतस्मिन्निहतेऽग्य्रवीर्येनरान्तकेवालिसुतेनसंख्ये ।।6.69.95।।
explanation: Naranthaka, the foremost of the heroes, having been killed in combat, the Devatas and gods of the three worlds experienced great joy.

shloka_text: नरान्तकंहतंदृष्टवाचुक्रुशुर्नैरृतर्षभाः । देवान्तकस्त्रिमूर्धा च पौलस्त्यश्चमहोदरः ।।6.70.1।।
explanation: Seeing the bulls among Rakshasas Naranthaka, Devanthaka, Trisira and Mahodara a scion of Paulastya and Mahodara, killed the Rakshasas cried aloud.

shloka_text: आरूढोमेघसङ्काशंवारणेन्द्रंमहोदरः । वालिपुत्रंमहावीर्यमभिदुद्राववीर्यवान् ।।6.70.2।।
explanation: Mahodara who closely resembled a cloud, mounted on the best of elephants chased brave and courageous son of Vali.

shloka_text: भ्रारातृव्यसनसन्तप्तस्तदादेवान्तकोबली । आदायपरिघंदीप्तमङ्गदंसमभिद्रवत् ।।6.70.3।।
explanation: Then, powerful Devanthaka who was immersed in grief of his brother, taking hold of a glowing iron bar rushed forward towards Angada.

shloka_text: रथमादित्यसङ्काशंयुक्तंपरमवाजिभिः । आस्थायत्रिशिरावीरोवालिपुत्रमथाभ्ययात् ।।6.70.4।।
explanation: Then Trisira, seated on the chariot, effulgent as the Sun, yoked to the best horse marched towards Angada.

shloka_text: स त्रिभिर्देवदर्पघ्नेर्नेरृतीन्द्रेरभिद्रुतः । वृक्षमुत्पाटयामासमहाविटपमङ्गदः ।।6.70.5।।
explanation: Angada observed that all the three chiefs of Rakshasas, who were capable of crushing the pride of gods marching towards him and uprooted a huge tree.

shloka_text: देवान्तकायतंवीरच्शिक्षेपसहसाङ्गदः । महावृक्षंमहाशाखंशक्रोदीप्तमिवाशनिम् ।।6.70.6।।
explanation: Just as Indra took a flaming thunderbolt, Angada, the hero took hold of huge branches of trees and hurled at Devanthaka with force.

shloka_text: त्रिशिरास्तंप्रचिच्छेदशरैराशीविषोपमैः । स वृक्षंकृत्तमालोक्यउत्पपाततदाङ्गदः ।।6.70.7।।
explanation: Trisira split the trees with the arrows which were like venomous serpents. Observing Angada's action he flew up.

shloka_text: स ववर्षततोवृक्षान् शैलाश्चकपिकुञ्जरः । तान् प्रचिच्छेदसङ्कृद्धस्त्रिशिरानिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.8।।
explanation: Then the leader of the monkeys, rained trees and rocks. Angry Trisira attacked all of them with sharp arrows.

shloka_text: परिघाग्रेणतान् वृक्षान्बभञ्ज च महोदरः । त्रिशिराश्चाङ्गदंवीरमभिदुद्रावसायकैः ।।6.70.9।।
explanation: Mahodara shattered those trees with the iron clubs. Trisira attacked brave Angada with arrows.

shloka_text: गजेनसमभिद्रुत्यवालिपुत्रंमहोदरः । जघानोरसिसङ्कृद्धस्तोमरैर्वज्रसन्निभैः ।।6.70.10।।
explanation: Mahodara chased the elephant on to Angada in anger and attacked him on his chest with his iron clubs.

shloka_text: देवान्तकश्चसङ्कृद्धःपरिघेणतदाङ्गदम् । उपगम्याभिहत्याशुव्यपचक्रामवेगवान् ।।6.70.11।।
explanation: Then infuriated Devanthaka quickly came over Angada directly and attacked him with his iron club and retreated.

shloka_text: सत्रिभिर्नैरृतश्रेष्ठैर्युगतपत्समभिद्रुतः । न विव्यथेमहातेजावालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.70.12।।
explanation: Eminent and highly energetic son of Vali did not feel perturbed when three of the foremost Rakshasas attacked him together.

shloka_text: स वेगवान्महावेगंकृत्वापरमदुर्जयः । तलेनभृशमुत्पत्यजघानास्यमहागजम् ।।6.70.13।।
explanation: Angada, who was endowed with high speed, and exceedingly difficult to encounter, jumped up the huge elephant of Mahodara attacked him.

shloka_text: तस्यतेनप्रहारेणनागराजस्यसंयुगे । पेततुर्लोचनेतस्यविननाद स वारणः ।।6.70.14।।
explanation: By that blow of Angada, that king of elephant's eyes dropped, and it cried.

shloka_text: विषाणंचास्यसःनिष्कृष्यवालिपुत्रोमहाबलः । देवान्तकमभिप्लुत्यताडयामाससंयुगे ।।6.70.15।।
explanation: Mighty son of Vali removed the tusk of the elephant and hit Devanthaka with it by jumping over him in the battlefield.

shloka_text: स विह्वलस्तुतेजस्वीवातोद्धूतइवद्रुमः । लक्षारससवर्णं च सुस्रावरुधिरंमहत् ।।6.70.16।।
explanation: That astonishing Rakshasa shaken like a tree, thrown by the wind, shed huge amounts of blood which was of the colour of lacquer.

shloka_text: अथाश्वस्यमहातेजाःकृच्छ्राद्देवान्तकोबली । आविध्यपरिघंवेगादाजघानतदाङ्गदम् ।।6.70.17।।
explanation: Thereafter the terribly strong Devanthaka taking iron spike quickly pierced Angada.

shloka_text: परिघाभिहतश्चापिवानरेन्द्रात्मजस्तदा । जानुभ्यांपतितोबूमौपुनरेवोत्पपात ह ।।6.70.18।।
explanation: Then, hurt by the club the son of Vanara king fell down on his knees once again and got up.

shloka_text: तमुत्पतन्तंत्रिशिरास्त्रिभिर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः । घोरैर्हरिपतेःपुत्रेंललाटेऽभिजघान ह ।।6.70.19।।
explanation: While Angada was getting up, Trisira again hit him on the forehead with three straight going arrows.

shloka_text: ततोऽङ्गदंपरिक्षिप्तंत्रिभिर्नैरृतपुङ्गवैः । हनूमानपिविज्ञायनीलश्चापिप्रतस्थतुः ।।6.70.20।।
explanation: Then finding Angada surrounded by the three Rakshasa leaders, Hanuman as well as Neela set out.

shloka_text: तश्चिक्षेपशैलाग्रंनीलस्त्रिशिरसेतदा । तद्रावणसुतोधीमाबनिभेदनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.21।।
explanation: Thereafter Neela hit Trisira with the peak of the mountain and Ravana's son broke the mountain into pieces with arrows.

shloka_text: तद्बाणशतनिर्भिन्नंविदारितशिलातलम् । सविस्फुलिंगंसज्वालंनिपपातगिरेशशिरः ।।6.70.22।।
explanation: Hit by hundreds of arrows, the mountain peak broke into pieces of stones like sparks and flames fell from it.

shloka_text: ततोजृम्भितमालोक्यहर्षाद्वेवान्तकस्तदा । परिघेणाभिदुद्रावमारुतात्मजमाहवे ।।6.70.23।।
explanation: Mighty Devanthaka, observing (Trisira's action), was happy on the battlefield, and went with his club to assault Hanuman.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तमुत्प्लुत्यहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । आजघानतदामूर्ध्निवज्रकल्पेनमुष्टिना ।।6.70.24।।
explanation: Then the son of wind god, Hanuman observing Devanthaka coming towards him, got up and hit him on the forehead with his thunderbolt like fist.

shloka_text: शिरसिप्रहरवनीरस्तदावायुसुतोबली । नादेनाकम्पयच्चैवराक्षसान् स महाकपिः ।।6.70.25।।
explanation: When the heroic and strong son of the wind god hit on the head of Devanthaka, the Rakshasas trembled by the sound of the great monkey 's blow.

shloka_text: मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नमूर्धानिर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिव्वाः । देवान्तकोराक्षसराजसूनुर्गतासुरुत्व्यांसहसापपात ।।6.70.26।।
explanation: Devanthaka's skull was shattered by the blow, and his teeth, eyes and tongue were forced out, the son of Rakshasa king fell dead on the ground.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्हतेराक्षसयोधमुख्येमहाबलेसंयतिदेवशत्रौ । क्रुद्धस्त्रिमूर्धानिशिताग्रमुग्रंववर्षनीलोरसिबाणवर्षम् ।।6.70.27।।
explanation: Devanthaka, the foremost of Rakshasa warriors, an enemy of gods, endowed with great strength, having been killed in the conflict, Trisira became angry and rained arrows on Neela's chest.

shloka_text: महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धःकुञ्जरंपर्वतोपमम् । भूयस्समधिरुह्याशुमन्दरंरमशिमानिव ।।6.70.28।। ततोबाणमयंवर्षंनीलस्योरस्यपातयत् । गिरौवर्षंतडिच्चक्रचापवानिवतोयदः ।।6.70.29।।
explanation: Mahodara got enraged, mounted on an elephant just as the Sun went over Mandara mountain and went for war. Then Mahodara wielding bow rained arrows, just as rainy clouds with lightning and rainbows showers rain, on the mountain like chest of Neela.

shloka_text: महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धःकुञ्जरंपर्वतोपमम् । भूयस्समधिरुह्याशुमन्दरंरमशिमानिव ।।6.70.28।। ततोबाणमयंवर्षंनीलस्योरस्यपातयत् । गिरौवर्षंतडिच्चक्रचापवानिवतोयदः ।।6.70.29।।
explanation: Mahodara got enraged, mounted on an elephant just as the Sun went over Mandara mountain and went for war. Then Mahodara wielding bow rained arrows, just as rainy clouds with lightning and rainbows showers rain, on the mountain like chest of Neela.

shloka_text: ततश्शरौघेरभिवर्ष्यमाणोविभिन्नगात्रःकपिसैन्यपालः । नीलोबभूवाथविसृष्टगात्रोविष्टम्भितस्तेनमहाबलेन ।।6.70.30।।
explanation: Neela's body wetted by arrows all over, the limbs pierced with arrows, the monkey leader remained powerless and could not move in spite of being extraordinarily strong.

shloka_text: ततस्तुनीलःप्रतिलभ्यसंज्ञांशैलंसमुत्पाट्यसवृक्षषंण्डम् । ततस्समुत्पत्यभृशोग्रवेशोमहादरंतेनजघानमूर्ध्नि ।।6.70.31।।
explanation: Thereafter Neela also regained his senses and uprooting a mountain filled with trees went over Mahodara at high speed and attacked him on the forehead.

shloka_text: तत: स्सशैलेद्रनिपातभग्नोमहोदरस्तेनमहाद्विपेन । विपोथितोभूमितलेगतासुःपपातवज्राभिहतोयथाद्रिः ।।6.70.32।।
explanation: Then smashed by the impact of the mountain, along with his elephant Mahodara's body fell to the ground. Released from life, he fell like a mountain struck with lightning.

shloka_text: पितृव्यंनिहतंदृष्टवात्रिशिराश्चापमाददे । हनूमन्तं च सङ्कृद्धोविव्याथनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.70.33।।
explanation: Trisira got enraged seeing his uncle killed, seized his bow and with a sharp arrow pierced Hanuman.

shloka_text: स वायुसुनूःकुपितश्चिक्षेपशिखरंगिरेः । त्रिशिरास्तच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभेदबहुधाबली ।।6.70.34।।
explanation: The son of the wind god in anger hurled a top of the mountain on mighty Trisira, who split the mountain into several pieces with an arrow.

shloka_text: तद्व्यर्थंशिखरंदृष्टवाद्रुमवर्षंमहाकपिः । विससर्जरणेतस्मिन्रावणस्यसुतंप्रति ।।6.70.35।।
explanation: Then seeing that the top of the mountain hurled was ineffective in that battle over Ravana's son, Hanuman discharged rain of trees.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तमाकाशेद्रुमवर्षंप्रतापवान् । त्रिशिरानिशितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद च ननाद च ।।6.70.36।।
explanation: Stupendous Trisira tore with his whetted arrows the rain of trees through the sky and roared.

shloka_text: हनूमानुतोप्लुत्यहयंस्त्रीशिरसस्तदा । विददारनखैःक्रुद्धोनागेन्द्रंमृगराडिव ।।6.70.37।।
explanation: Then Hanuman also jumped up in anger and tore the horse off Trisira just as the lion would tear the lordly elephant with nails.

shloka_text: अथशक्तिंसमादायकाळरात्रिमिवान्तकः । चिक्षेपानिलपुत्रायत्रिशिरारावणात्मजः ।।6.70.38।।
explanation: In the same manner, Trisira, the son of Ravana sprung up and seized a javelin, just as God of death in dark night and hurled at the son of wind god and shattered.

shloka_text: दिवःक्षिप्तामिवोल्कांतांशक्तिंक्षिप्तामसङ्गताम् । गृहीत्वाहरिशार्दूलोबभञ्ज च ननाद च ।।6.70.39।।
explanation: Hanuman, the best of monkeys, snapped the javelin flung by Trisira on him, which came down unobstructed like a meteor from heaven and the monkeys roared.

shloka_text: तांदृष्टवाघोरसङ्काशांशक्तिंभग्नांहनूमता । प्रहृष्टावानरगणाविनेदुर्जलदाइव ।।6.70.40।।
explanation: Seeing the dreadful form of shattered javelin, all Vanaras rejoiced and thundered like rain clouds.

shloka_text: तःखडगंसमुद्यम्यत्रिशिराराक्षसोत्तमः । निजघानतदाव्यूढेवायुपुत्रस्यवक्षसि ।।6.70.41।।
explanation: Trisira, the foremost of Rakshasas then lifted his sword, placed it on the chest of Hanuman and dug into it.

shloka_text: खडगप्रहाराभिहतोहनुमान्मारुतात्मजः । आजघानतिशिरसंतलेनोरसिवीर्यवान् ।। 6.70.42।।
explanation: Heroic Hanuman hit by Trisira, attacked him with his palm on the chest.

shloka_text: सतलाभिहतस्तेनस्रस्तहस्तायुधोभुवि । निपपातमहातेजास्त्रिशिरास्त्यक्तचेतनः ।।6.70.43।।
explanation: Trisira, a highly energetic one, hit by Hanuman with his palm, dropped the weapon from his hand, lost his senses and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: स तस्यपततःखङ्गंतमाच्छिद्यमहाकपिः । ननादगिरिसङ्काशस्त्रासयन् सर्वनैरृता ।।6.70.44।।
explanation: Taking the sword from Trisira, as he was falling, the great Vanara who resembled a mountain roared, creating terror in all, surrounded there.

shloka_text: अमृष्यमाणस्तंघोषमुत्पपातनिशाचरः । उत्पत्य च हनूमन्तंताडयामासमुष्टिना ।।6.70.45।।
explanation: Unable to bear that roar, that Rakshasa got up jumping and struck Hanuman with his fist.

shloka_text: तेनमुष्टिप्रहोरेणसञ्चुकोपमहाकपिः । कुपितश्चनिजग्राहकिरीटेराक्षसर्षभम् ।।6.70.46।।
explanation: The great monkey hit by the fist (of Trisira) became furious and in anger he got hold of Trisira's head with crown.

shloka_text: स तस्यशीर्षाण्यसिनाशितेनकिरीटजुष्टानिसकुण्डलानि । क्रुद्धःप्रचिच्छेदसुतोऽनिलस्यत्वष्टुस्सुतस्येवशिरांसिशक्रः ।।6.70.47।।
explanation: Enraged wind god's son, cut off the three heads of Trisira adorned with earrings just as Indra cut off the heads of Vishwarupa, son of Twashta.

shloka_text: तान्यायताक्षाण्यगसन्निभानिप्रदीप्तवैश्वानरलोचनानि । पेतुशिरांसीन्द्ररिपोःर्धरण्यांज्योतींषिमुक्तानियथार्कमार्गात् ।।6.70.48।।
explanation: The heads of Trisira, an enemy of Indra, resembling mountains with incongruous eyes glowing like Vyshvanara's eyes, fell into wilderness like stars fallen from the path of Sun.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् न्हतेदेवरिपौत्रिशीर्षेहनूमताशक्रपराक्रमेण । नेदुःप्लवंगाःप्रचचालभूमीरक्षांस्यथोदुद्रुविरेसमन्तात् ।।6.70.49।।
explanation: Trisira, the enemy of gods, endowed with the prowess of Indra got killed by Hanuman. The earth shook, the monkeys roared and the Rakshasas from all sides took to their heels.

shloka_text: हतंत्रिशिरसंदृष्टवातथैवचमहोदरं । हतौप्रेक्षयदुराधर्षौदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।6.70.50।। चुकोपपरमामर्षीमत्तोराक्षसपुङ्गवः ।
explanation: Witnessing Trisira killed, earlier Mahodara also, Devanthaka and Naranthaka who are difficult to encounter killed, monkeys roared in joy seeing that Matta became very angry.

shloka_text: जग्राहार्चिष्मतींघोरांगदांसर्वायसींशुभां ।।6.70.51।। हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तांमांसशोणितफेनिलाम् । विराजमानांवपुषांशत्रुशोणितरंजिताम् ।।6.70.52।। तेजसासंप्रदीप्ताग्रांरक्तमाल्यविभूषिताम् । ऐरावतमहापद्मसार्वभौमभयावहाम् ।।6.70.53।।
explanation: Mahaparsva seized hold of a good venerable, allpowerful mace plated with gold, smeared with flesh and blood, shining with lustre, shining red with enemy's blood, an effulgent one whose head has been glowing decorated with red flower garlands that brought terror to Airavatam, Mahapadma, and Sarvabhuama, the three elephants guarding the three of the four quarters.

shloka_text: जग्राहार्चिष्मतींघोरांगदांसर्वायसींशुभां ।।6.70.51।। हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तांमांसशोणितफेनिलाम् । विराजमानांवपुषांशत्रुशोणितरंजिताम् ।।6.70.52।। तेजसासंप्रदीप्ताग्रांरक्तमाल्यविभूषिताम् । ऐरावतमहापद्मसार्वभौमभयावहाम् ।।6.70.53।।
explanation: Mahaparsva seized hold of a good venerable, allpowerful mace plated with gold, smeared with flesh and blood, shining with lustre, shining red with enemy's blood, an effulgent one whose head has been glowing decorated with red flower garlands that brought terror to Airavatam, Mahapadma, and Sarvabhuama, the three elephants guarding the three of the four quarters.

shloka_text: जग्राहार्चिष्मतींघोरांगदांसर्वायसींशुभां ।।6.70.51।। हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तांमांसशोणितफेनिलाम् । विराजमानांवपुषांशत्रुशोणितरंजिताम् ।।6.70.52।। तेजसासंप्रदीप्ताग्रांरक्तमाल्यविभूषिताम् । ऐरावतमहापद्मसार्वभौमभयावहाम् ।।6.70.53।।
explanation: Mahaparsva seized hold of a good venerable, allpowerful mace plated with gold, smeared with flesh and blood, shining with lustre, shining red with enemy's blood, an effulgent one whose head has been glowing decorated with red flower garlands that brought terror to Airavatam, Mahapadma, and Sarvabhuama, the three elephants guarding the three of the four quarters.

shloka_text: गदामादायसङ्कृद्धोमत्तोराक्षसपुङ्गवः । हरीन् समभिदुद्रावयुगान्तानगिरिवज्वलन् ।।6.70.54।।
explanation: Matta, the Rakshasa leader became very furious and took hold of the mace glowing like fire, at the time of dissolution of the universe and scattered the monkeys.

shloka_text: अथर्षभस्समुत्पत्यवानरोरावणानुजम् । मत्तानीकमुपागम्यतस्थौतस्याग्रतोबली ।।6.70.55।।
explanation: Rshaba, the bull among Vanaras endowed with prowess, springing up came and stood in front of Mahaparsva.

shloka_text: तंपुरस्तात् स्थितंदृष्टवावानरंपर्वतोपमम् । आजघानोरसिक्रुद्धोगदयावज्रकल्पया ।।6.70.56।।
explanation: Again, seeing Rshaba standing in front like a mountain, enraged Mahaparsva hit him on the chest with the mace that was like a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: स तयाऽभिहतस्तेनगदयावानरर्षभः । भिन्नवक्षास्समाधूतस्सुस्रावरुधिरंबहु ।।6.70.57।।
explanation: Hit in that way by the mace, Rshaba, bull of Vanaras, with chest broken, blood flowed excessively.

shloka_text: स संज्ञांप्राप्यसुचिरादृषभोवानरर्षभः । क्रुद्धोविस्फुरमाणौष्ठोमहापार्श्वमुदैक्षत ।।6.70.58।।
explanation: Regaining consciousness after a long time the monkey chief, Rshaba, was angry, his lips quivering as he was, ran to Mahaparsva.

shloka_text: स वेगवान् वेगवदभ्युपेत्यतंराक्षसंवानरवीरमुख्यः । सम्वर्त्यमुष्टिंसहसाजघानबाह्वन्तरेशैलनिकाशरूपः ।।6.70.59।।
explanation: The chief of the Vanaras, whose form was like a mountain, endowed with speed, got up quickly, duly, and forcibly hit the Rakshasa (Mahaparsva) in the space between his arms.

shloka_text: स कृत्तमूलस्सहसेववृक्षःक्षितौपपातक्षतजोक्षिताङ्गः । तांचास्यघोरांयमदण्डकल्पांगदांप्रगृह्याशुतदाननाद ।।6.70.60।।
explanation: Like a tree whose roots have been severed, the Rakshasa fell on the ground. Then seizing forcibly, the dreadful mace that resembled the rod of Lord of death he roared.

shloka_text: मुहूर्तमासीत्सगतासुकल्पःप्रत्यागतात्मासहसासुरारिः । उत्पत्यसन्ध्याभ्रसमानवर्णस्तंवारिराजात्मजमाजघान ।।6.70.61।।
explanation: For a short while, Mahaparsva, the enemy of gods remained as if life had gone off up and struck the son of waters (Rshaba).

shloka_text: स मूर्भितोभूमितलेपपातमुहूर्तमुत्पत्यपुनस्ससंज्ञः । तामेवतस्याद्रिवराद्रिकल्पांगदांसमाविध्यजघानसङ्ख्ये ।।6.70.62।।
explanation: The monkey was unconscious for a while having fallen on the ground. Regaining senses, overcoming, took up the mace which looked like the rock of a foremost mountain and struck him (Mahaparsva) on the battlefield.

shloka_text: सातस्यरौद्रासमुपेत्यदेहंरौद्रस्यदेवाध्वरविप्रशत्रोः । बिभेदवक्षःक्षतजं च भूरिसुस्रावधात्वम्भइवाद्रिराजः ।।6.70.63।।
explanation: He (Rshaba) reached the body of the ferocious enemy of gods and brahmins. He split his chest with his mace and the timid Rakshasa shed blood just as Himalaya Mountain discharges water.

shloka_text: अभिदुद्राववेगेनगदांतस्यमहात्मनः । गृहीत्वातांगदांभीमामाविध्य च पुनःपुनः ।।6.70.64।। मत्तानीकंमहात्मानंजघानरणमूर्धनि ।
explanation: The great Rakshasa Mahaparsva went towards the mace held by Rshaba, the great soul. Taking hold of the mace, Rshaba struck the Rakshasa again and again and pierced him in the forefront of the battlefield.

shloka_text: स स्वयागदयाभग्नोविदीर्णदशनेक्षणः ।।6.70.65।। निपपातततोमत्तोवज्राहतइवाचलः ।
explanation: Shattered by his own mace, Matta (Mahaparsva), whose eyes had been crushed, had fallen like a mountain struck by lightning.

shloka_text: विदीर्णनयनेभूमौगतसत्त्वेगतायुषि ।।6.70.66।। पतितेराक्षसेतस्मिन् विद्रुतंराक्षसंबलम् ।
explanation: Strength gone, life ceased, eyes crushed, his own Rakshasas fallen on the ground, the Rakshasa army fled.

shloka_text: स्वबलंव्यथितंदृष्टवातुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । भ्रातृ़ंश्चनिहतान् दृष्टवाशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान् ।।6.71.1।। पितृव्यौचापिसनृदृश्यसमरेसन्निघादितौ । युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौराक्षसर्षभौ ।।6.71.2।। चुकोप च महातेजाब्रह्मदत्तवरोयुधि । अतिकायोऽद्रिसङ्काशोदेवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.71.3।।
explanation: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.

shloka_text: स्वबलंव्यथितंदृष्टवातुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । भ्रातृ़ंश्चनिहतान् दृष्टवाशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान् ।।6.71.1।। पितृव्यौचापिसनृदृश्यसमरेसन्निघादितौ । युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौराक्षसर्षभौ ।।6.71.2।। चुकोप च महातेजाब्रह्मदत्तवरोयुधि । अतिकायोऽद्रिसङ्काशोदेवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.71.3।।
explanation: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.

shloka_text: स्वबलंव्यथितंदृष्टवातुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । भ्रातृ़ंश्चनिहतान् दृष्टवाशक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान् ।।6.71.1।। पितृव्यौचापिसनृदृश्यसमरेसन्निघादितौ । युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौराक्षसर्षभौ ।।6.71.2।। चुकोप च महातेजाब्रह्मदत्तवरोयुधि । अतिकायोऽद्रिसङ्काशोदेवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.71.3।।
explanation: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.

shloka_text: स भास्करसहस्रस्यसङ्घातमिवभास्वरम् । रथमास्थायशक्रारिरभिदुद्राववानरान् ।।6.71.4।।
explanation: Adorned with a crown, Ravana glowing like a thousand suns collected together mounted the chariot and darted towards Vanaras.

shloka_text: स विस्फार्यमहाचापंकिरीटीमृष्टकुण्डलः । नामविश्रावयामासननाद च महास्वनम् ।।6.71.5।।
explanation: Adorned with crown, and polished earrings, twanging his bow, proclaimed his name and roared sounding aloud.

shloka_text: तेनसिंहप्रणादेननामविश्रावणेन च । ज्याशब्देन च भीमेनत्रासयामासवानरान् ।।6.71.6।।
explanation: By that lionroar, and proclamation of his name (by the sound of the twang) frightening the Vanaras he struck terror.

shloka_text: तेदृष्टवादेहमाहात्म्यंकुम्भकर्णोऽयमुथतितः । भयार्तावानरास्सर्वेसंश्रयन्तेपरस्परम् ।।6.71.7।।
explanation: Those Vanaras seeing the huge body thought, "This is Kumbhakarna, who has got up and come'. Out of fear, they sought the help of one another.

shloka_text: तेतस्यरूपमालोक्ययथाविष्टोस्त्रिविक्रमे । भयाद्वानरयूधास्तेविद्रवन्तिततस्ततः ।।6.71.8।।
explanation: The Vanara troops, observing his form resembling the Trivikram form assumed by Vishnu, the monkey troops fled here and there in panic.

shloka_text: तेऽतिकायंसमासाद्यवानरामूढचेतसः । शरण्यंशरणंजग्मुर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजमाहवे ।।6.71.9।।
explanation: The Vanaras were deluded on reaching the huge body and went to Sri Rama to seek refuge.

shloka_text: तोऽतिकायंकाकुत्स्थोरथस्थंपर्वतोपमम् । ददर्शधवनिनंदूराद्गर्जन्तंकालमेघवत् ।।6.71.10।।
explanation: Then Kakutstha saw from a distance form of huge body looking like a mountain, wielding bow, rumbling like a cloud at universal destruction.

shloka_text: स तंदृष्टवामहात्मानंराघवस्तुविसिस्मिये । वानरान् सान्त्वयित्वा च विभीषणमुवाच ह ।।6.71.11।।
explanation: Raghava the great, seeing the form of a huge body, was amazed, reassured by the Vanaras, and spoke to Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: कोऽसौपर्वतसङ्काशोधनुष्मान्हरिलोचनः । युक्तेहयसहस्रेणविशालेस्यन्दनेस्थितः ।।6.71.12।।
explanation: "Who is he, the yelloweyed, resembling a mountain, seated in the broad chariot drawn by a thousand horses?"

shloka_text: य एषनिशितैश्शूलैस्सुतीक्णैःप्रासमुद्गरैः । अर्चिष्मद्भिर्वृतोभातिभूतैरिवमहेश्वरः ।।6.71.13।।
explanation: "Who is he in the midst, with sharp tridents and shining spears, like Maheswara surrounded by beings?"

shloka_text: कालजिह्वाप्रकाशाभिर्यएषोऽतिविराजते । आवृतोरथशक्तीभिर्विद्युद्भिरिवतोयदः ।।6.71.14।।
explanation: "Who is he, gleaming like the tongues of time spirit (Kala spirit), with flashes of javelins, encircled with lightning and looking like a cloud shining very bright?"

shloka_text: धनूंषिचास्यसज्जानिहेमपृष्ठानिसर्वशः । शोभयन्तिरथश्रेष्ठंशक्रचापमिवाम्बरम् ।।6.71.15।।
explanation: "His bows decorated with gold on the back, are like a rainbow in the sky on all sides and makes the chariot excellent."

shloka_text: क एषरक्षश्शार्दूलोरणभूमिविराजयन् । अभ्येतिरथिनांश्रेष्ठोरथेनादित्यतेजसा ।।6.71.16।। ध्वजशृङ्गप्रतिष्ठेनराहुणाभिविराजते । सूर्यरमशिनिभैर्बाणैर्दिशो दश विराजयन् ।।6.71.17।।
explanation: "The tiger among the Rakshasas seated in the chariot is the foremost car warrior. He is illuminating the battlefield like the brightness of the Sun, resplendent like Sun 's rays. By his arrows he is illuminating the ten directions. The Rahu emblem on top of the pole of the chariot is very splendid."

shloka_text: क एषरक्षश्शार्दूलोरणभूमिविराजयन् । अभ्येतिरथिनांश्रेष्ठोरथेनादित्यतेजसा ।।6.71.16।। ध्वजशृङ्गप्रतिष्ठेनराहुणाभिविराजते । सूर्यरमशिनिभैर्बाणैर्दिशो दश विराजयन् ।।6.71.17।।
explanation: "The tiger among the Rakshasas seated in the chariot is the foremost car warrior. He is illuminating the battlefield like the brightness of the Sun, resplendent like Sun 's rays. By his arrows he is illuminating the ten directions. The Rahu emblem on top of the pole of the chariot is very splendid."

shloka_text: त्रिणतंमेघसन्नादंहेमपृष्ठमलङ्कृतम् । शतक्रतुधनुःप्रख्यंधनुश्चास्यविराजते ।।6.71.18।।
explanation: "His bow with three curves, covered with gold, decorated, is close to a thundering cloud, casting its splendour."

shloka_text: स ध्वजस्सपताकश्चसानुकर्षोमहारथः । चतुस्सादिसमायुक्तोमेघस्तनितानि ।।6.71.19।।
explanation: "His chariot with standard, flag and axletree is a great one driven by four charioteers emitting sound like the rumblings of clouds."

shloka_text: विंशतिर्दशचाष्टौ च तूण्योऽस्यरथमास्थिताः । कार्मुकानि च भीमानिज्याश्चकाञ्चनपिङ्गळाः ।।6.71.20।।
explanation: "This chariot has twenty quivers, ten frightening bows, and eight bow strings of golden colour lay arranged in the chariot."

shloka_text: द्वौ च खडगौरथगतौपार्श्वस्थौपार्श्वशोभितौ । चतुर्हस्तत्सरुयुतौव्यक्तहस्तदशायतौ ।।6.71.21।।
explanation: "It has two swords off our cubits and ten cubits long swords provided with hilts hanging on its sides as decoration."

shloka_text: रक्तगण्ठगुणोधीरोमहापर्वतसन्निभः । कालःकालमहावक्त्रोमेघस्थइवभास्करः ।।6.71.22।।
explanation: "Wearing red garland s round the neck, brave, like a mountain in form, dark with large mouth, like death, like sun veiled by clouds he seems."

shloka_text: काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाभ्यांभूजाभ्यामेषशोभते । शृङ्गाभ्यामिवतुङ्गाभ्यांहिमवान् पर्वतोत्तमः ।।6.71.23।।
explanation: "By adorning armlets, his both arms are like high peaks of Himalaya mountain shining away."

shloka_text: कुण्डलाभ्यांतुयस्यैतद्भतध्भातिशुभेक्ष । पुनर्वस्वन्तरगतंपूर्णंभिंबमिवैंदवम् ।।6.71.24।।
explanation: "He who shines like the full moon between two Punarvasu stars, his auspicious eyes and countenance shines with both earrings."

shloka_text: आचक्ष्वमेमहाबाहोत्वमेनंराक्षसोत्तमम् । यंदृष्टवावानरास्सर्वेभयार्ताविद्रुतादिशः ।।6.71.25।।
explanation: "Oh! Vibheeshana, a mighty armed one! Show me that foremost of Rakshasas, whom all Vanaras feared and fled in all directions."

shloka_text: स पृष्टोराजपुत्रेणरामेणामिततेजसा । आचचक्षेमहातेजारघवायविभीषणः ।।6.71.26।।
explanation: Interrogated by the highly brilliant prince Raghava, energetic Vibheeshana revealed.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवोमहातेजाराजावैश्रवणानुजः । भीमकर्मामहोत्साहोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.71.27।।
explanation: "The tenheaded and highly brilliant king Ravana, who is the brother of Vysravana, is of terrible deeds and highly exploitative."

shloka_text: तस्यासीद्वीर्यवान्पुत्रोरावणप्रतिमोरणे । वृद्धसेवीश्रुतिधरस्सर्वास्त्रविदुषांवरः ।।6.71.28।।
explanation: "To him was born a blessed son, valiant one, compeer of Ravana, who served elders, learned and well versed in sastras."

shloka_text: अश्वपृष्ठेरथेनागेखडगेधनुषिकर्षणे । भेदेसान्त्वे च दाने च नयेमन्त्रे च सम्मतः ।।6.71.29।।
explanation: "He is best in riding on horseback, on elephant back and in the use of sword and bow. He is capable of sowing dissension, making peace, giving charity and statecraft."

shloka_text: यस्यबाहूसमाश्रित्यलङ्कावसतिनिर्भया । तनयंधान्यमालिन्याअतिकायमिमंविदुः ।।6.71.30।।
explanation: "He is known as Atikaya, son of Dhanyamalini. Lanka remains fearless on his shoulders, you may know."

shloka_text: एतेनाराधितोब्रह्मोतपसाभावितात्मना । अस्त्राणिचाप्यवाप्तानिरिपवश्चपराजिताः ।।6.71.31।।
explanation: "By penance on supreme self he propitiated Brahma, who blessed him with mystic missiles by way of boons by which his enemies were subdued."

shloka_text: सुरासुरैरवध्यत्वंदत्तमस्मैस्वयम्भुवा । एतच्चकवचंदिव्यंरधश्चैषोऽरभास्वरः ।।6.71.32।।
explanation: "Exemption from death from gods and demons was given to him and all this wonderful shield and chariot as bright as the sun."

shloka_text: एतेनशतशोदेवादानवाश्चपराजिताः । रक्षितानि च रक्षांसियक्षाश्चापिनिषूदिताः ।।6.71.33।।
explanation: "By this (boon) hundreds of Devatas and demons were defeated by him, Yakshas were killed, nay Rakshasas were protected."

shloka_text: वज्रंविष्टम्भितंयेनबाणैरिन्द्रस्यधीमतः । पाशस्सलिलराजस्यरणेप्रतिहतस्तथा ।।6.71.34।। एषोऽतिकायोबलवान्राक्षसानामथर्षभः । रावणस्यतोधीमान्देवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.71.35।।
explanation: "Here is strong Atikaya, a wise son of Ravana, bull among Rakshasas, who is a subduer of the pride of Devas and Danavas, by whom thunderbolt of Indra was obstructed firmly in battle and likewise the noose of Varuna was repelled in war."

shloka_text: वज्रंविष्टम्भितंयेनबाणैरिन्द्रस्यधीमतः । पाशस्सलिलराजस्यरणेप्रतिहतस्तथा ।।6.71.34।। एषोऽतिकायोबलवान्राक्षसानामथर्षभः । रावणस्यतोधीमान्देवदानवदर्पहा ।।6.71.35।।
explanation: "Here is strong Atikaya, a wise son of Ravana, bull among Rakshasas, who is a subduer of the pride of Devas and Danavas, by whom thunderbolt of Indra was obstructed firmly in battle and likewise the noose of Varuna was repelled in war."

shloka_text: तदस्मिन्क्रियतांयत्नःक्षिप्रंपुरुषपुंगव । पुरावानरसैन्यानिक्ष्यंनयतिसायकैः ।।6.71.36।।
explanation: "Oh, best of men! Quickly make efforts to put an end to him before he puts down Vanara army."

shloka_text: ततोतिकायोबलवान्प्रविश्यहरिवाहिनीम् । विष्फारयामासधनुर्ननाद च पुनःपुनः ।।6.71.37।।
explanation: Thereafter, mighty Atikaya entered the monkey army, twanged his bow again and again and made a loud noise.

shloka_text: तंभीमवपुषंदृष्टवारथस्थंरथिनांवरम् । अभिपेतुर्महात्मानोयेप्रधानावनौकसः ।।6.71.38।।
explanation: Observing the dreadful enemy seated on the chariot, the foremost of the great Vanaras rushed towards him.

shloka_text: कुमुदोद्विविदोमैन्दोनीलश्शरभएव च । पादपैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्चयुगपत्समभिद्रवन् ।।6.71.39।।
explanation: Kumuda, Dwivida, Mainda, Neela, even Sarabha, all at once assailed him with trees and mountain peaks.

shloka_text: तेषांवृक्षांश्चशैलांश्चशरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । अतिकायोमहातेजाश्चिच्छेदास्त्रविदांवरः ।।6.71.40।।
explanation: Atikaya, endowed with extraordinary energy, efficient in the use of weapons, shattered the trees and rocks hurled by the Vanaras with his arrows adorned with gold.

shloka_text: तांश्चैवसर्वान् स हरीन् शरैस्सर्वायसैर्बली । विव्याथाभिमुखस्सङ्ख्येभीमकायोनिशाचर ।।6.71.41।।
explanation: The powerful night ranger of terrible form, pierced all monkeys who were facing him in the battlefield with iron arrows.

shloka_text: तेऽर्दितांबाणवर्षेणभिन्नगात्राःप्लवङ्गमाः । न शेकुरतिकायस्यप्रतिकर्तुंमहारणे ।।6.71.42।।
explanation: The monkeys were hard pressed by Atikaya's hail of arrows. Their limbs broke and were unable to resist.

shloka_text: तत् त्सैन्यंहरिवीराणांत्रासयामासराक्षसः । मृगयूथमिवक्रुद्धोहरिर्यौवनदर्पितः ।।6.71.43।।
explanation: Just as a young lion with youthful pride would strike a group of deer, the enraged Rakshasa struck the army of monkey heroes.

shloka_text: सराक्षसेन्द्रोहरिसैन्यमध्येनायुध्यमानंनिजघानकञ्चित् । उपेत्यरामंसधम: कलापी स गर्वितंवाक्यमिदंबभाषे ।।6.71.44।।
explanation: The Rakshasa lord, wielding a weapon in the midst of the monkey army, indeed did not strike any, but armed with bow and quiver went with pride towards Rama and spoke.

shloka_text: रथेस्थितोहंशरचापपाणिर्नप्राकृतंकञ्चनयोधयामि । यस्यास्तिकश्चिद्व्यवसाययुक्तोददातुमेक्षिप्रमिहाद्ययुद्धम् ।।6.71.45।।
explanation: "I am with a bow and arrow seated in the chariot. Indeed, I am not strong in fighting with common warriors. Whoever is interested to fight now can come speedily to fight with me."

shloka_text: तत्तस्यवाक्यंब्रुवतोनिशम्यचुकोपसौमित्रिरमित्रहन्ता । अमृष्यमाणश्चसमुत्पपातजग्राहचापं च ततस्स्मयित्वा ।।6.71.46।।
explanation: On hearing Atikaya, Saumithri the destroyer of enemies, became angry, not enduring and not able to tolerate went towards him taking a sword.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धस्सौमित्रिरुत्पत्यतूणादाक्षिप्यसायकम् । पुरस्तादतिकायस्यविचकर्षमहद्धनुः ।।6.71.47।।
explanation: Furious Saumithri, springing up, took up his arrow from the quiver, stretching to full length before he discharged the arrow.

shloka_text: पूरयन् स महींशैलानाकाशंसागरंदिशः । ज्याशब्दोलक्ष्मणस्योग्रस्त्रासयन् रजनीचरान् ।।6.71.48।।
explanation: The twang of Lakshmana filled the mountains, earth, ocean, and all directions striking terrible fear in the night ranger.

shloka_text: सौमित्रेश्चापनिर्घोषंश्रुत्वाप्रतिभयंतदा । विसिष्मियेमहातेजाराक्षसेन्द्रात्मजोबली ।।6.71.49।।
explanation: Then the extraordinarily energetic and powerful son of Rakshasa king was in turn frightened at the sound of Saumithri's bow and was astonished.

shloka_text: अथातिकायःकुपितोदृष्टवालक्ष्मणमुत्थितम् । आदायनिशितंबाणमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.71.50।।
explanation: Seeing Atikaya, furious Lakshmana sprang up and took a sharp shaft and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: बालस्त्वमसिसौमित्रेविक्रमेष्वविचक्षणः । गच्छकिंकालसदृशंमांयोधयतुमिच्छसि ।।6.71.51।।
explanation: "O Saumithri! You are valiant but young, not able to discriminate. I am equal to the Lord of death. Why do you desire to comb at with me?"

shloka_text: न हिमद्बाहुसृष्टानामस्त्राणाहिमवानपि । सोढुमुत्सहतेवेगमन्तरिक्षमथोमही ।।6.71.52।।
explanation: The shafts discharged from my arm can't be borne, by the Himalayas, even the atmosphere between the sky and earth can't bear the force.

shloka_text: सुखप्रसुप्तंकालाग्निंविबोधयितुमिच्छसि । न्यस्यचापंनिवर्तस्वमाप्राणान् जहिमद्गतः ।।6.71.53।।
explanation: "Why do you want to arouse the fire of dissolution sleeping comfortably? Return, casting away your bow, without confronting. Go away."

shloka_text: अथवात्वंप्रतिष्टब्धो न निवर्तितुमिच्छसि । तिष्ठप्राणान् परित्यज्यगमिष्यसियमक्ष्यम् ।।6.71.54।।
explanation: "Or else if you want to oppose and not return, give up your life and proceed to Yama's abode."

shloka_text: पश्यमेनिशितान्बाणानरिदर्पनिषूदनान् । ईश्वरायुधसङ्काशांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणान् ।।6.71.55।।
explanation: "See my sharp shafts capable of reducing enemy's pride like Ishwara's trident, ornamented with polished gold."

shloka_text: एषतेसर्पसंकाशोबाणःपास्यतिशोणितम् । मृगराजइवक्रुद्धोनागराजस्यशोणितम् ।।6.71.56।। इत्येवमुक्त्वासंक्रुद्धश्शरंधनुषिसंदधे ।
explanation: "These arrows are like serpents and can drink your blood just as an angry lion drinks the blood of elephants. Therefore, I tell you", said Atikaya to Lakshmana."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातिकायस्यवचस्सरोषंसगर्वितंसम्यतिराजपुत्रः । स सञ्चुकोपातिबलोमनस्वीरुवाचवाक्यं च ततोमहार्थम् ।।6.71.57।।
explanation: Prince Atikaya, having spoken as said before, fitted his bow in wrath. Hearing the proud statement of Atikaya, the highminded Lakshmana, endowed with strength, enraged, and spoke these words of great meaning.

shloka_text: न वाक्यमात्रेणभवान् प्रधानो न कत्थनात्सत्पुरुषाभवन्ति । मयिस्थितेधन्विनिबाणपाणौनिदर्शयस्वात्मबलंदुरात्मन् ।।6.71.58।।
explanation: "You are evil minded. By mere statement you people can't become good chiefs. I stand armed with a bow and arrow. Prove your strength."

shloka_text: कर्मणासूचयात्मानं न विकत्थितुमर्हसि । पौरुषेणतुयोयुक्तस्सतुशूरइतिस्मृतः ।।6.71.59।।
explanation: "Reveal yourself by action not by indication. You do not deserve it. He who is with prowess is a right hero."

shloka_text: सर्वायुधसमायुक्तोधन्वीत्वंरथमास्थितः । शरैर्वायदिवाप्यस्त्रैर्दर्शयस्वपराक्रमम् ।।6.71.60।।
explanation: "You are seated in the chariot with all kinds of weapons collected. By that alone you do not become capable. Show your capacity."

shloka_text: ततश्शिरस्तेनिशितैःपातयिष्याम्यहंशरैः । मारुतःकालसम्पक्वंवृन्तात्ताळफलंयथा ।।6.71.61।।
explanation: "Then I will strike down his head with sharp arrows and throw him just as ripened palm fruit drops in the process of time."

shloka_text: अद्यतेमामकाबाणास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः । पास्यन्तिरुधिरंगात्राद्बाणशल्यान्तरोत्थितम् ।।6.71.62।।
explanation: "Now, you will drink the blood ejected from your neck by the holes made with my pointed arrows decked with polished gold."

shloka_text: बालोऽयमितिविज्ञाय न मावज्ञातुमर्हसि । बालोवायदिवावृद्धोमृत्युंजानीहिसंयुगे ।।6.71.63।। बालेनविष्णुनालोकास्त्रयःक्रान्तास्त्रिविक्रमैः ।
explanation: "You should not underestimate me thinking I am young or old to win. You do not know that I am spirit of death in battle. Did not Vishnu as young Trivikrama win the three worlds going by three strides?"

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाहेतुमत्परमार्थवत् ।।6.71.64।। अतिकायःप्रचुक्रोधबाणंचोत्तममाददे ।
explanation: On hearing the words of Lakshmana, which was reasonable and full of truth, Atikaya became furious and took up the best of arrows.

shloka_text: ततोविद्याधराभूतादेवादैत्यामहर्षयः ।।6.71.65।। गुह्यकाश्चमहात्मानस्तद्युद्धंद्रष्टुमागमन् ।
explanation: Then vidhyadharas, demons, devatas, daityas, sages and great guhyakas arrived at the battlefield to witness.

shloka_text: तोऽतिकायःकुपितश्चापमारोप्यसायकम् ।।6.71.66।। लक्ष्मणायप्रचिक्षेपसङ्क्षिपन्निवचाम्बरम् ।
explanation: Then enraged Atikaya, fixing his arrow to the bow as if discharging it in the sky directed at Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंनिशितंशरमाशीविषोपमम् ।।6.71.67।। अर्धचन्द्रेणचिच्छेदलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।
explanation: Lakshmana, the heroic destroyer of enemies, shattered the venomous serpent like arrow with his sharp half moon shaped arrow.

shloka_text: तंनिकृत्तंशरंदृष्टवाकृत्तभोगमिवोरगम् ।।6.71.68।। अतिकायोभृशंक्रुद्धःपञ्चबाणान् समाददे ।
explanation: Seeing the arrow torn asunder like a serpent, Atikaya was offended and became very angry and fitted five arrows to his bow.

shloka_text: तान्शरान् सम्प्रचिक्षेपलक्ष्मणायनिशाचरः ।।6.71.69।। तानप्राप्तान् शरैस्तीक्ष्णैश्चिच्छेदभरतानुजः ।
explanation: The night ranger set loose those arrows at Lakshmana, Bharata's brother. Lakshmana shattered them even before it reached him.

shloka_text: सतान् छित्त्वाशितैर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.71.70।। आददेनिशितंबाणंज्वलन्तमिवतेजसा ।
explanation: Lakshmana, the heroic destroyer of foes, having split those arrows, seized a shaft which was a bright and sharp flaming arrow.

shloka_text: तमादायधनुश्श्रेष्ठेयोजयामासलक्ष्मणः ।।6.71.71।। विचकर्ष च वेगेनविससर्ज च वीर्यवान् ।
explanation: Valiant Lakshmana, foremost of the wielders of bow stretching his bow till the ear, quickly discharged the arrow.

shloka_text: पूर्णायतविसृषेनशरेणनतपर्वणा ।।6.71.72।। ललाटेराक्षसश्रेष्ठमाजघान स वीर्यवान् ।
explanation: The heroic Lakshmana fully stretching the arrow bending to curvature struck Atikaya, the foremost of Rakshasas on his forehead.

shloka_text: सललाटेशरोमग्नस्तस्यभीमस्यरक्षसः ।।6.71.73।। ददृशेशोणितेनाक्तःपन्नगेन्द्रइवाचले ।
explanation: That arrow stuck on the forehead of the terrific Rakshasa looked like a serpent on a mountain.

shloka_text: राक्षसःप्रचकम्पे च लक्ष्मणेषुप्रपीडितः ।।6.71.74।। रुद्रबाणहतंघोरंयथात्रिपुरगोपुरम् ।
explanation: Now tormented by Lakshmana's arrow the Rakshasa was shaken dreadfully like the gate of Tripura (the city built of gold, silver, and iron in heaven, in space and earth by Maya and burnt by Rudra).

shloka_text: चिन्तयामासचाश्वास्यविमृश्य च महाबलः ।।6.71.75।। साधुबाणनिपातेनश्लाघनीयोऽसिमेरिपुः ।
explanation: Recovering from the hurt and reflecting, the Rakshasa contemplated the course of action, and said 'By releasing the arrow on me you are an enemy worthy of praise."

shloka_text: विधायैवंविनम्यास्यंनियम्य च भुजावुभौ ।।6.71.76।। स रथोपस्थमास्थायरथेनप्रचचार ह ।
explanation: Having spoken that way bending his face setting both shoulders right, he settled at the rear end of the chariot started to move from the chariot.

shloka_text: कंत्रीन्पञ्चसप्तेतिसायन्राक्षसर्षभः ।।6.71.77।। आददेसन्दधेचापिविचकर्षोत्ससर्ज च ।
explanation: The bull among the Rakshasas taking, one, three, five and seven arrows, fixing them to the bow stretching released.

shloka_text: तेबाणाःकालसङ्काशाराक्षसेन्द्रधुनुश्च्युताः ।।6.71.78।। हेमपुङ्खारविप्रख्याश्चक्रुर्दीप्तमिवाम्बरम् ।
explanation: The gold feathered arrows released from the rakshasas's bow, were like death arrows which shone in the sky as if the sky was glowing.

shloka_text: तस्तान्राक्षसोत्सृष्टान्शरौघान्राघवानुजः ।।6.71.79।। असम्ब्रान्तःप्रचिच्छेदनिशितैर्बहुभिश्शरैः ।
explanation: Raghava's brother remained unconfounded and then he shattered the volley of many sharp arrows released by the Rakshasa.

shloka_text: तान् शरान्युधिसम्प्रेक्ष्यनिकृत्तान्रावणात्मजः ।।6.71.80।। चुकोपत्रिदशेन्द्रारिर्जग्राहनिशितंशरम् ।
explanation: Ravana's son, an enemy of Indra, observing that all arrows have been ineffective, took up another sharp arrow.

shloka_text: ससन्धायमहातेजास्तंबाणंसहसोत्सृजत् ।।6.71.81।। तेनस्सौमित्रिमायान्तमाजघानस्तनान्तरे ।
explanation: Highly energetic Atikaya, fixing another arrow released it between the breasts of Saumithri and pierced.

shloka_text: अतिकायेनसौमित्रिस्ताडितोयुधिवक्षसि ।।6.71.82।। सुस्रावरुधिरंतीव्रंमदंमत्तइवद्विपः ।
explanation: In the battle, Saumithri was hurt in the chest by Atikaya's arrow and blood flowed like the ichor from elephant in rut.

shloka_text: सचकारतदात्मानंविशल्यंसहसाविभुः ।।6.71.83।। जग्राह च शरंतीक्ष्णमस्त्रेणापिचसन्दधे ।
explanation: He (Lakshmana) being glorious and noble himself seized hold of the pointed arrow stuck in his body and removed it with a mystic spell.

shloka_text: आग्नेयेनतदाऽस्त्रेणयोजयामाससायकम् ।।6.71.84।। स जज्वालतदाबाणोधनुष्यस्यमहात्मनः ।
explanation: Then Lakshmana by concentration of his mind fixed on fire god which presided over the arrow, that great selffixed in his bow glowed.

shloka_text: अतिकायोतितेजस्वीसौरमस्त्रंसमादधे ।।6.71.85।। तेनबाणंभुजङ्गाभंहेमपुङ्खमयोजयत् ।
explanation: Highly energetic Atikaya took a serpentlike arrow with gold feathers and charged it by the concentration of his mind on the power of Sun god.

shloka_text: तदस्त्रंज्वलितंघोरंलक्ष्मणश्शरमाहितम् ।।6.71.86।। अतिकायायचिक्षेपकालदण्डमिवान्तकः ।
explanation: Lakshmana placed that fierce, glowing missile looking like the staff of God of death on Atikaya.

shloka_text: आग्नेयेनाभिसंयुक्तंदृष्टवाबाणंनिशाचरः ।।6.71.87।। उत्ससर्जतदाबाणंदीप्तंसूर्यास्त्रयोजितम् ।
explanation: The night ranger, seeing the missile charged with fire god coming towards him, released the glowing arrow charged with the power of Sun god.

shloka_text: तावुभावम्बरेबाणावन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः ।।6.71.88।। तेजसासंप्रदीप्ताग्रौक्रुद्धाविवभुजंगमौ ।
explanation: Both the arrows effulgent, flaming with fire, were like angry serpents in the sky striking one another violently.

shloka_text: तावन्योन्यंविनिर्दह्यपेततुर्धरणीतले ।।6.71.89।। निरर्चिषौभस्मकृतौ न भ्राजेतेशरोत्तमौ । तावुभौदीप्यमानौस्म न भ्राजेतेमहीतले ।।6.71.90।।
explanation: Those two burning one another and themselves burning had fallen on the earth surface with no fire. Those two best of arrows though glowing, having fallen on earth did not shine as they ceased to emit flames and had been reduced to ashes.

shloka_text: तावन्योन्यंविनिर्दह्यपेततुर्धरणीतले ।।6.71.89।। निरर्चिषौभस्मकृतौ न भ्राजेतेशरोत्तमौ । तावुभौदीप्यमानौस्म न भ्राजेतेमहीतले ।।6.71.90।।
explanation: Those two burning one another and themselves burning had fallen on the earth surface with no fire. Those two best of arrows though glowing, having fallen on earth did not shine as they ceased to emit flames and had been reduced to ashes.

shloka_text: ततोऽतिकायस्सङ्कृद्धस्त्वस्त्रमैषीकमुत्सृजत् । तत्प्रचिच्छेदसौमित्रिरस्त्रमैन्द्रेणवीर्यवान् ।।6.71.91।।
explanation: Then Atikaya seized with anger discharged Ishikam presided over by Twashta (the architect of gods). Saumithri then split the arrow with one presided by Indra and split Ishikam.

shloka_text: ऐषीकंनिहतंदृष्टवारुषितोरावणात्मजः । याम्येनार्स्तेणसङ्कृद्धोयोजयामाससायकम् ।।6.71.92।।
explanation: Annoyed by his arrow Ishikam being struck, Atikaya, son of Ravana charged Lakshmana's arrow with an arrow presided over by Yama.

shloka_text: ततस्तदस्त्रंचिक्षेपलक्ष्मणायनिशाचरः । वायव्येनतदस्त्रेणनिजघान स लक्ष्मणः ।।6.71.93।।
explanation: Then the night ranger shattered the arrow of Lakshmana and in turn released an arrow presided by Vayu.

shloka_text: अथैनंशरधाराभिर्धाराभिरिवतोयदः । अभ्यवर्षत्सुसङ्कृद्धोलक्ष्मणोरावणात्मजम् ।।6.71.94।।
explanation: And then enraged Lakshmana covered with water like a rainy cloud would shower with torrents.

shloka_text: तेऽतिकायंसमासाद्यकवचेवज्रभूषिते । भग्नाग्रशल्यास्सहसापेतुर्बाणामहीतले ।।6.71.95।।
explanation: On those arrows touching Atikaya's diamond like body, the pointed arrows shattered the coat covering the body and the broken coat of nails had fallen down.

shloka_text: तान्मोघानभिसम्प्रेक्ष्यलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा । अभ्यवर्षन्महेषूणांसहस्रेणमहायशाः ।।6.71.96।।
explanation: Lakshmana of great fame, subduer of enemy looking at the arrows becoming useless mighty hero released thousand arrows.

shloka_text: स वृष्यमाणोबाणौघैरतिकायोमहाबलः । अवध्यकवचस्सङ्ख्येराक्षसोनैवविव्यथे ।।6.71.97।।
explanation: Though covered with arrows showered on him, mighty Rakshasa Atikaya had an impenetrable shield in the battlefield and could not feel the torment.

shloka_text: शरंचाशीविषाकारंलक्ष्मणायव्यपासृजत् । स तेनविद्धस्सौमित्रिर्मर्मदेशेशरेण ह ।।6.71.98।। मुहूर्तमात्रंनिस्संज्ञोह्यभवच्छत्रुतापनः ।
explanation: Atikaya released an arrow resembling a poisonous serpent at Lakshmana. Pierced in vital part Saumithri, the tormentor of the enemy lost consciousness for a while.

shloka_text: ततःस्संज्ञामुपालभ्यचतुर्भिस्सायकोत्तमैः ।।6.71.99।। निजघानहयान्सङ्ख्येसारथिं च महाबलः । ध्वजस्योन्मथनंकृत्वाशरवर्षैररिन्दमः ।।6.71.100।।
explanation: Then mighty subduer of enemies, regaining senses, getting up destroyed the chariot pole with rain of arrows. Taking up four best arrows he struck down the chariot, charioteer, and the horses.

shloka_text: ततःस्संज्ञामुपालभ्यचतुर्भिस्सायकोत्तमैः ।।6.71.99।। निजघानहयान्सङ्ख्येसारथिं च महाबलः । ध्वजस्योन्मथनंकृत्वाशरवर्षैररिन्दमः ।।6.71.100।।
explanation: Then mighty subduer of enemies, regaining senses, getting up destroyed the chariot pole with rain of arrows. Taking up four best arrows he struck down the chariot, charioteer, and the horses.

shloka_text: असम्भ्रान्तस्ससौमित्रिस्तान्शरानभिलक्षितान् । मुमोचलक्ष्मणोबाणान्वधार्थंतस्यरक्षसः ।।6.71.101।।
explanation: Saumithri, son of Sumithra, was not able to inflict injury on that Rakshasa with those arrows, though desiring to kill him.

shloka_text: न शशाकरुजंकर्तुंयुधितस्यनरोत्तमः । अथैनमभ्युपागम्यवायुर्वाक्यमुवाच ह ।।6.71.102।।
explanation: Wind god (Vayu) having come to the best of men, Lakshmana, spoke to him that in battle it is not possible to injure him or kill him.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मदत्तवरोह्येषअवध्यकवचावृतः । ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेणभ्निथ्येनमेषवध्योहिनान्यथा ।।6.71.103।। अवध्यएषह्यन्येषामस्त्राणांकवचीबली ।
explanation: By the boon given by Brahma his body is covered with armour which can't be broken. By Brahma's weapon only you can strike to kill him because of his armour and might. By any other weapon it is not possible to kill him.

shloka_text: ततस्तुवायोर्वचनंनिशम्यसौमित्रिरिन्द्रप्रतिमानवीर्यः । समाददेबाणममोघवेगंतद्ब्राह्ममस्त्रंसहसानियोज्य ।।6.71.104।।
explanation: Then Saumithri who is equal to Indra hearing wind god's words invoked Brahma's weapon into service. While he was charging into his arrows and fixing the arrow went at terrific speed.

shloka_text: नियुज्यमानेसौमित्रिणाबाणवरेशिताग्रे । दिशश्चचन्द्रर्कमहाग्रहाश्चनभश्चतत्रासचचालचोर्वी ।।6.71.105।।
explanation: As Saumithri charged the sharp pointed foremost arrow, the directions, moon, Sun and other planets and the sky, earth, and all space shook.

shloka_text: तंब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेणनियुज्यचापेशरंसुपुङ्खंयमदूतकल्पम् । सौमित्रिरिन्द्रारिसुतस्यतस्यससर्जबाणंयुधिवज्रकल्पम् ।।6.71.106।।
explanation: Golden feathered arrow, which resembled thunderbolt, was released on Atikaya, enemy of Indra for whom it was like a messenger of death. It was charged with Brahma's mystic by Saumithri and released on fixing it.

shloka_text: तंलक्ष्मणोत्सृष्टममोघवेगंसमापतन्तंज्यलनप्रकाशम् । सुपर्णवज्रोत्तमचित्रपुङ्खंतदाऽतिकायस्समरेददर्श ।।6.71.107।।
explanation: Atikaya saw the arrow of Lakshmana coming at a speed, which possessed the velocity of the wind, fixed with feathers resembling the wings of Garuda in the battle.

shloka_text: तंप्रेक्षमाणस्सहसाऽतिकायोजघानबाणैर्निशितैरनेकैः । स सायकस्तस्यसुपर्णवेगस्तदातिकायस्यजगामपार्श्वम् ।।6.71.108।।
explanation: As Atikaya was looking at the arrow, Lakshmana struck many arrows forcibly with sharp arrows possessing the speed of Garuda. The arrows reached towards Atikaya.

shloka_text: तमागतंप्रेक्ष्यतदातिकायोबाणंप्रदीप्तान्तककालकल्पम् । जघानक्त्यृष्टिगदाकुठारैशूलैर्हुलैश्चाप्यविपन्नचेता ।।6.71.109।।
explanation: Perceiving the glowing arrow coming, like the spirit of death, Atikaya struck it with unceasing effort with javelins, spears, maces, axes, tridents and even arrows.

shloka_text: तान्यायुधान्यद्भुतविग्रहाणिमोघानिकृत्वा स शरोऽग्निदीप्तः । प्रगृह्यतस्यैवकिरीटजुष्टम् ततोऽतिकायस्यशिरोजहार ।।6.71.110।।
explanation: This great arrow of Lakshmana glowing like fire rendered the weapons in wonderful shapes released by Atikaya unsuccessful and severed the head of Atikaya decked with a crown.

shloka_text: तछचिरस्सशिरस्त्राणंलक्ष्मणेषुप्रपीडितम् । पपातसहसाभूमौशृङ्गंहिमवतोयथा ।।6.71.111।।
explanation: Struck by Lakshmana's arrow, the crowned head of Atikaya fell on the ground like Himalaya peak.

shloka_text: तंभूमौनिपतितंदृष्टवाविक्षिप्तभूषणम् बभूवुर्व्यथितास्सर्वेहतशेषानिशाचराः ।।6.71.112।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas who escaped from killing, felt distressed seeing the king and his ornaments scattered on the ground.

shloka_text: तेविषण्णमुखादीनाःप्रहारजनितश्रमाः । विनेदुरुच्चैर्बहवस्सहसाविस्वरैस्स्वरैः ।।6.71.113।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas with desperate looks, their pride hurt, became very sad and burst into discordant tones roared aloud.

shloka_text: ततस्तेत्वरितंयातानिरपेक्षानिशाचराः । पुरीमभिमुखाभीताद्रवन्तोनायकेहते ।।6.71.114।।
explanation: With Leader killed, the night rangers were afraid. Listless they ran quickly towards Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रहर्षयुक्ताबहवस्तुवानराःप्रबुद्दपद्मप्रतिमाननास्तदा । अपूजयन्लक्ष्मणविष्टभागिनंहतेरिपौभीमबलेदुरासदे ।।6.71.115।।
explanation: Enemy who was difficult to approach and of terrible might being killed, the Vanaras were extremely delighted. Their faces looked like lotuses in bloom. Filled with joy they worshipped Lakshmana.

shloka_text: अतिकायंहतंश्रुत्वालक्ष्मणेनमहौजसा । उद्वेगमगमद्राजावचनंचेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.72.1।।
explanation: On hearing that Atikaya was killed by highly energetic Lakshmana, the king was overtaken by emotion and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षःपरमामर्षीधन्वीशस्त्रभृतांवरः । अकम्पनःप्रहस्तश्चकुम्भुकर्णस्तथैव च ।।6.72.2।। एतेमहाबलावीराराक्षसायुद्धकाङ्क्षिणः । जेतारःपरसैन्यानांपरैर्नित्यापराजिताः ।।6.72.3।। निहतास्तेमहावीर्यारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । राक्षसास्सुमहाकायानानाशस्त्रविशारदाः ।।6.72.4।। अन्ये च बहवश्शूरामहात्मानोनिपातिताः ।
explanation: "Dhumraksha, a highly intolerant one, Akampana, the foremost of the Rakshasas and skilled in the use of bow and arms, in the same way Prahastha, Kumbhakarna of stupendous valour and heroes among Rakshasas desiring for combat, who have never been defeated and conquerors of hostile armies, have been killed. Great heroes of huge body, skilled in the use of many weapons and other warriors have been killed by Rama."

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षःपरमामर्षीधन्वीशस्त्रभृतांवरः । अकम्पनःप्रहस्तश्चकुम्भुकर्णस्तथैव च ।।6.72.2।। एतेमहाबलावीराराक्षसायुद्धकाङ्क्षिणः । जेतारःपरसैन्यानांपरैर्नित्यापराजिताः ।।6.72.3।। निहतास्तेमहावीर्यारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । राक्षसास्सुमहाकायानानाशस्त्रविशारदाः ।।6.72.4।। अन्ये च बहवश्शूरामहात्मानोनिपातिताः ।
