Great heroes of huge body, skilled in the use of many weapons and other warriors have been killed by Rama."

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षःपरमामर्षीधन्वीशस्त्रभृतांवरः । अकम्पनःप्रहस्तश्चकुम्भुकर्णस्तथैव च ।।6.72.2।। एतेमहाबलावीराराक्षसायुद्धकाङ्क्षिणः । जेतारःपरसैन्यानांपरैर्नित्यापराजिताः ।।6.72.3।। निहतास्तेमहावीर्यारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । राक्षसास्सुमहाकायानानाशस्त्रविशारदाः ।।6.72.4।। अन्ये च बहवश्शूरामहात्मानोनिपातिताः ।

Great heroes of huge body, skilled in the use of many weapons and other warriors have been killed by Rama."

shloka_text: प्रख्यातबलवीर्येणपुत्रेणेन्द्रजितामम ।।6.72.5।। यौहितौभ्रातरौतदावीरौबद्धौदत्तवरैश्शरैः ।
explanation: "Both the famous brothers, Rama and Lakshmana were bound with arrows by my heroic son Indrajith who is conferred with boons and whose strength is well known.

shloka_text: यन्नशक्यंसुरैस्सर्वैरसुरैर्वामहाबलैः ।।6.72.6।। मोक्तुंतद्बन्धनंघोरंयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरैः । तन्नजानेप्रभावैर्वामाययामोहनेनवा ।।6.72.7।। शरबन्धाद्विमुक्तौतौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: "That formidable bond which could not be undone by Devatas, mighty Demons, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras got released by both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana by their powers and conjuring tricks which are not known to me."

shloka_text: यन्नशक्यंसुरैस्सर्वैरसुरैर्वामहाबलैः ।।6.72.6।। मोक्तुंतद्बन्धनंघोरंयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरैः । तन्नजानेप्रभावैर्वामाययामोहनेनवा ।।6.72.7।। शरबन्धाद्विमुक्तौतौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।
explanation: "That formidable bond which could not be undone by Devatas, mighty Demons, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras got released by both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana by their powers and conjuring tricks which are not known to me."

shloka_text: येयोधानिर्गताश्शूराराक्षसाममशासनात् ।।6.72.8।। तेसर्वेनिहतायुद्धेवानरैस्सुमहाबलैः ।
explanation: " All those heroes who have gone by my order for combat, have been killed in the battle by mighty Vanaras."

shloka_text: तम्नपश्याम्यहंयुद्धेयोऽद्यरामंसलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.72.9।। शासयेत्सबलंवीरंससुग्रीवविभीषणम् ।
explanation: "I do not see any warrior who will be able to wage with that Lakshmana, or his army, or with Sugriva, Vibheeshana or with Rama to put an end to them."

shloka_text: अहोसुबलवान् रामोमहदस्त्रबलं च वै ।।6.72.10।। यस्यविक्रममासाद्यराक्षसानिधनंगताः ।
explanation: "Rama's valour is great the strength of his missiles is great, and his valour is formidable. Rakshasas can't stand his range."

shloka_text: अप्रमत्सैश्चसर्वत्रगुप्सैरक्ष्यापुरीवतियम् ।।6.72.11।। अशोकवनिकायांचयत्रसीताऽभिरक्ष्यते ।
explanation: "This city and even the Ashoka grove where Sita is kept secretly to be guarded by being vigilant on all sides."

shloka_text: निष्क्रामोवाप्रवेशोवाज्ञातव्यस्सर्वदैवनः ।।6.72.12।। यत्रयत्रभवेद्गुल्मस्तत्रतत्रपुनःपुनः ।
explanation: "Wherever the troops are posted here and there be it exit, or entrance should be checked again and again and not to go out."

shloka_text: सर्वतश्चापितिष्ठध्वंस्स्वै: परिवृताबलैः ।।6.72.13।। द्रष्टव्यं च पदंतेषांवानराणांनिशाचराः ।
explanation: "Surrounded by the army on all sides, whoever it may be, keep watching the movement of Vanaras."

shloka_text: प्रदोषेवार्धरात्रेवाप्रत्यूषेवापिसर्वत ।।6.72.14।। नावज्ञातेषुकर्तव्यावानरेषुकदाचन । द्विषतांबलमुद्युक्तमापतकतिंस्थितंसदा ।।6.72.15।।
explanation: " At all times, whether it is evening or midnight or early morning, Vanaras movements are to be watched by the army without indifference. Indeed, the army should be active or inactive, standing, advancing constantly and staying wherever they are."

shloka_text: प्रदोषेवार्धरात्रेवाप्रत्यूषेवापिसर्वत ।।6.72.14।। नावज्ञातेषुकर्तव्यावानरेषुकदाचन । द्विषतांबलमुद्युक्तमापतकतिंस्थितंसदा ।।6.72.15।।
explanation: " At all times, whether it is evening or midnight or early morning, Vanaras movements are to be watched by the army without indifference. Indeed, the army should be active or inactive, standing, advancing constantly and staying wherever they are."

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्सर्वेश्रुत्वालङ्काधिपस्यतत् । वचनंसर्वमातिष्ठन् यथावत्तुमहाबलाः ।।6.72.16।।
explanation: On hearing the words of the king of Lanka all Rakshasas and the great army got up.

shloka_text: स तान् सर्वान् हिसन्दिश्यरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । मन्युशल्यंवहन् दीनःप्रविवेशस्वमालयम् ।।6.72.17।।
explanation: Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, enjoined the Rakshasas and himself bearing the thorn of wrath, entered the abode desperately.

shloka_text: ततोहतान्राक्षसपुङ्गवांस्तान् देवान्तकादित्रिशिरोतिकायान् । रक्षोगणास्तत्रहतावशिष्टास्तेरावणायत्वरिताश्शशंसुः ।।6.73.1।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas who survived the killings, hurriedly reported to the Rakshasa king, Ravana about the killing of Devanthaka, Trisira and Atikaya.

shloka_text: ततोहतांस्तान् सहसानिशम्यराजामुमोहपरिप्लुताक्षः । पुत्रक्षयंभ्रातृवधं च घोरंविचिन्त्यराजाविपुलंप्रदध्यौ ।।6.73.2।।
explanation: There upon the king, getting to know suddenly about the dreadful killing of his son and brother lost his senses. His eyes were filled with tears, and he was thinking seriously.

shloka_text: ततस्तुराजानमुदीक्ष्यदीनंशोकार्णवेसम्परिपुप्लुवानम् । रथर्षभोराक्षसराजसूनुस्तमिन्द्रजिद्वाक्यमिदंबभाषे ।।6.73.3।।
explanation: Thereafter, seeing the desperate Rakshasa king immersed in a sea of sorrow, Indrajith, son of Ravana, foremost of the chariot riders, submitted as follows.

shloka_text: न तात मोहंपरिगन्तुमर्हसियत्रेन्द्रजिजजीवतिराक्षसेन्द्र । नेन्द्रारिबाणाभिहतोहिकश्चित्प्राणान् समर्थस्समरेऽभिपातुम् ।।6.73.4।।
explanation: "Dear king of Rakshasas! Do not give way to despair when Indrajith is alive. Indeed, struck by Indrajith's arrows in battle it is not possible for anyone to be with life."

shloka_text: पश्याद्यरामंसहलक्ष्मणेनमद्बाणनिर्भिन्नविकीर्णदेहम् । गतायुषंभूमितलेशयानंशितैश्शरैराचितसर्वगात्रम् ।।6.73.5।।
explanation: "Now you will see Rama along with Lakshmana also, their body torn into pieces along with their army their life ceased, lying on the ground pierced with arrows all over the limbs."

shloka_text: इमांप्रतिज्ञांशृणुशक्रशत्रोःसुनिश्चितांपौरुषदैवयुक्ताम् । अद्यैवरामंसहलक्ष्मणेनसन्तर्पयिष्यामिशरैरमोघैः ।।6.73.6।।
explanation: "Listen to this vow of Indra's enemy, which is fully determined and combined with manliness and divinity. I shall put an end to Rama and Lakshmana with my wonderful arrows."

shloka_text: अद्येन्द्रवैवस्वतविष्णुमित्रसाध्याश्चवैश्वानरचन्द्रसूर्याः । द्रक्ष्यन्तुमेविक्रममप्रमेयंविष्णोरिवोग्रंबलियज्ञवाटे ।।6.73.7।।
explanation: "Today, Indra, Vishnu, Mitra, Sadhyas, Vysvanara, moon and Sun will witness my immeasurable prowess as they witnessed the terrible prowess of Vishnu at the fire sacrifice of Bali."

shloka_text: स एवमुक्त्वात्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रुरापृच्छयराजानमदीनसत्त्वः । समारुरोहानितुल्यवेगंरथंखरश्रेष्ठसमाधियुक्तम् ।।6.73.8।।
explanation: (Indrajith) having spoken in that manner, taking leave of the king, the enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods), ascended the chariot swift as wind in speed, drawn by the best of donkeys.

shloka_text: तमास्थायमहातेजारथंहरिरथोपमम् । जगामसहसातत्रयत्रयुद्धमरिन्दमः ।।6.73.9।।
explanation: Highly energetic he (Indrajith) was, a tamer of enemies, seated in the chariot that was like Indra's, quickly went to the battlefield from there.

shloka_text: तंप्रस्थितंमहात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः । सम्हर्षमाणाबहनोधनुष्प्रवरपाणयः ।।6.73.10।। गजस्कन्धगताःकेचित्केचित्प्रवरवाजिभिः । व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोरोष्ट्रैश्चभुजङ्गमैः ।।6.73.11।। वराहैश्श्वापदैस्सिंहैर्जम्बुकैःपर्वतोपमैः । काकहंसमयूरैश्चराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.73.12।। प्रासमुद्गरनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वथगदाधराः । भुशुण्डिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधा ।।6.73.13।।
explanation: Many Rakshasas of terrific valour, endowed with extraordinary strength, happily, wielding excellent bows, taking barbed missiles, hammers, whetted axes, maces, Bhusandi mallets, Ayasthis, Sataghnis, and Parighas, making noise, went following great Indrajith. Some went on the back of elephants and horses, tigers as large as mountains, scorpions, cats, donkeys, and camels. As well as on serpents, lions, tigers, and jackals.

shloka_text: तंप्रस्थितंमहात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः । सम्हर्षमाणाबहनोधनुष्प्रवरपाणयः ।।6.73.10।। गजस्कन्धगताःकेचित्केचित्प्रवरवाजिभिः । व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोरोष्ट्रैश्चभुजङ्गमैः ।।6.73.11।। वराहैश्श्वापदैस्सिंहैर्जम्बुकैःपर्वतोपमैः । काकहंसमयूरैश्चराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.73.12।। प्रासमुद्गरनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वथगदाधराः । भुशुण्डिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधा ।।6.73.13।।

shloka_text: तंप्रस्थितंमहात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः । सम्हर्षमाणाबहनोधनुष्प्रवरपाणयः ।।6.73.10।। गजस्कन्धगताःकेचित्केचित्प्रवरवाजिभिः । व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोरोष्ट्रैश्चभुजङ्गमैः ।।6.73.11।। वराहैश्श्वापदैस्सिंहैर्जम्बुकैःपर्वतोपमैः । काकहंसमयूरैश्चराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.73.12।। प्रासमुद्गरनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वथगदाधराः । भुशुण्डिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधा ।।6.73.13।।

shloka_text: तंप्रस्थितंमहात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः । सम्हर्षमाणाबहनोधनुष्प्रवरपाणयः ।।6.73.10।। गजस्कन्धगताःकेचित्केचित्प्रवरवाजिभिः । व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोरोष्ट्रैश्चभुजङ्गमैः ।।6.73.11।। वराहैश्श्वापदैस्सिंहैर्जम्बुकैःपर्वतोपमैः । काकहंसमयूरैश्चराक्षसाभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.73.12।। प्रासमुद्गरनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वथगदाधराः । भुशुण्डिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधा ।।6.73.13।।
explanation: Many Rakshasas of terrific valour, endowed with extraordinary strength, happily, wielding excellent bows, taking barbed missiles, hammers, whetted axes, maces, Bhusandi mallets, Ayasthis, Sataghnis, and Parighas, making noise, went following great Indrajith. Some went on the back of elephants and horses, tigers as large as mountains, scorpions, cats, donkeys, and camels. As well as on serpents, lions, tigers, and jackals.

shloka_text: स शङ्खनिनदैःपूर्णैर्भेरीणांचापिनिस्स्वनैः । जगामत्रिदशेन्द्रास्तूयमानोनिशाचरैः ।।6.73.14।।
explanation: The Rakshasas went on praising the enemy of Indra, Indrajith, making noise, blowing conchs in full blast, beating drums.

shloka_text: स शङ्खशशिवर्णेनछत्रेणरिपुसूदनः । रराजप्रतिपूर्णेननभश्चन्द्रमसायथा ।।6.73.15।।
explanation: He, the destroyer of foes went with white parasols like a full moon shine in the sky.

shloka_text: अवीज्यतततोवीरोहैमैर्हेमविभूषितैः । चारुचामरमुख्यैश्चमुख्यस्सर्वधनुष्मताम् ।।6.73.16।।
explanation: Thereafter the chief hero went decked with golden ornaments, fanned by archers holding whisks with gold handles.

shloka_text: स तुदृष्टवाविनिर्यान्तंबलेनमहातावृतम् । राक्षसाधिपतिश्रशीमान् रावणःपुत्रमब्रवीत् ।।6.73.17।।
explanation: Ravana, the prosperous king of Rakshasas, seeing his son sallying forth surrounded by huge army spoke.

shloka_text: त्वमप्रतिरथःपुत्रत्वयावैवासवोजितः । किम्पुनर्मानुषंधृष्यंनिहनिष्यसिराघवम् ।।6.73.18।। तथोक्तोराक्षसेन्द्रेणप्रत्यगृह्णान्महाशिषः ।
explanation: "Son! there is no adversary who can fight with you sitting in a chariot. Indra has been won by you. What to say about mortals like Rama who can be assailed by you."Rakshasa king having spoken that way, Indrajith accepted the blessings and departed.

shloka_text: तस्त्विन्द्रजितालङ्कासूर्यप्रतिमतेजसा ।।6.73.19।। रराजाप्रतिवीर्येणद्यौरिवार्केणभास्वता ।
explanation: Then Lanka shone like the Sun in the sky with Indrajith who was effulgent like the Sun and matchless in valour shone.

shloka_text: सम्प्राप्यमहातेजायुद्धभूमिमरिन्दमः ।।6.73.20।। स्थापयामासरक्षांसिरथंप्रतिसमन्ततः ।
explanation: Upon reaching the battlefield, he, the tamer of foes, highly energetic Indrajith, ranged the Rakshasas around the chariot.

shloka_text: ततस्तुहुतभोक्तारंहुतभुक्सदृशप्रभः ।।6.73.21।। जुहावराक्षसश्रेष्ठोमन्त्रवद्विधिवत्तदा ।
explanation: Then the foremost of Rakshasas, who was like fire god in brilliance worshipped fire god with chanting of mantras as per tradition.

shloka_text: सहविर्लाजसंस्कारैर्माल्यगन्धपुरस्कृतैः ।।6.73.22।। जुहुवेपावकंतत्रराक्षनेन्द्रःप्रतापवान् ।
explanation: The heroic Rakshasa king worshipped according to tradition with flowers and fragrance followed by parched grain and fire god.

shloka_text: शस्त्राणिशरपत्राणिसमिधोऽथविभीतकाः ।।6.73.23।। लोहितानि च वासांसिस्रुवंकार्ष्णायसंतथा ।
explanation: In that fire sacrifice, weapons were leaves, bibika sticks were fuel, red pieces of cloth were used, and in the same way the ladle for sacrifice was made of iron.

shloka_text: सतत्राग्निंसमास्तीर्यशरपत्रैस्सतोमरैः ।।6.73.24।। छागस्यकृष्णवर्णस्यगळंजग्राहजीवतः ।
explanation: There he strewed into the fire, lances as leaves, dark coloured live go at clasped by its neck and consigned.

shloka_text: सकृदेवसमिद्धस्यविधूमस्यमहार्चिषः ।।6.73.25।। बभूवुस्तानिलिङ्गानिविजयंयान्यदर्शयन् ।
explanation: From the fire set ablaze by the of fearing of fire sticks into it was free from smoke burst into flames indicating victory.

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणः ।।6.72.26।। हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राहपावकस्स्वयमास्थितः ।
explanation: The fire god himself, decked in polished gold ornaments turned round and accepted the offerings.

shloka_text: सोऽस्त्रमाहारयामासब्राह्ममिन्द्ररिपुस्तदा ।।6.73.27।। धनुश्चात्मरथंचैवसर्वंतत्राभ्यमन्त्रयत् ।
explanation: He, with whom weapons are adept invoked weapon presided over by Brahma and charged his own chariot with it.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नाहूयमानेस्त्रेहूयमाने च पावके ।।6.73.28।। सार्धंग्रहेन्दुनक्षत्रैर्वितत्रासनभस्थ्सलम् ।
explanation: While the missile was being invoked and fire sacrifice was done, all planets, moon, Sun, and Stars in the sky shook in fear.

shloka_text: स पावकंपावकदीप्ततेजाहुत्वामहेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभावः । स चापबाणासिरथाश्वसूतःखेऽन्तर्दधेऽत्मानमचिन्त्यरूपः ।।6.73.29।।
explanation: Flaming like fire god, endowed with the prowess of Indra, possessing inconceivable form, Indrajith with his bow, arrows and chariot disappeared into the sky.

shloka_text: ततोहयरथाकीर्णंपताकाध्वजशोभितम् । निर्ययौराक्षसबलंनर्दमानंययुत्सया ।।6.73.30।।
explanation: Then, the Rakshasa army filled with horses and chariots, graced with pennants and flags, desiring to fight went roaring aloud.

shloka_text: तेशरैर्बहुभिश्चित्रैस्तीक्ष्णवेगैरलङ्कृतैः । तोमरैरङ्कुशैश्चापिवानरान् जघ्नुराहवे ।।6.73.31।।
explanation: They began to strike Vanaras, with many wonderfully decorated, sharp and swift arrows, lances, and tridents.

shloka_text: रावणिस्तुततस्सङ्कृद्धस्तान्निरीक्ष्यनिशाचरान् । हृष्टाभवन्तोयुध्यन्तुवानराणांजिघांसया ।।6.73.32।।
explanation: Thereafter enraged Ravana's son looking at the Rakshasas said, "Be happy and kill the Vanaras in fight."

shloka_text: ततस्तेराक्षसास्सर्वेनर्धन्तोजयकाङ्क्षिणः । अभ्यवर्षंस्ततोघोरान्वानरान् शरवृष्टिभिः ।।6.73.33।।
explanation: Thereafter the Rakshasas roaring and longing for victory rained arrows in a terrific manner at the Vanaras.

shloka_text: स तुनालीकनाराचैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि । रक्षोभिस्सम्वृतस्सङ्ख्येवानरान् विचकर्त ह ।।6.73.34।।
explanation: Indrajith, remaining concealed and surrounded by Rakshasas, destroyed the Vanaras with nalikas, steel arrows and maces.

shloka_text: तेवध्यमानास्समरेवानराःपादपायुधाः । अभ्यवर्षन्तसहसारावणिंशैलपादपैः ।।6.73.35।।
explanation: Struck in the battle by Indrajith, the Vanaras rained heavily armed with trees and rocks.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुतदाक्रुद्धोमहातेजामहाबलः । वानराणांशरीराणिव्यधमद्रावणात्मजः ।।6.73.36।।
explanation: Mighty and energetic son of Ravana, Indrajith became angry and began to attack the Vanaras.

shloka_text: शरेणैकेन च हरीन्नवपञ्च च सप्त च । बिभेदसमरेक्रुद्धोराक्षसान् संप्रहर्षयन् ।।6.73.37।।
explanation: Filled with anger, Indrajith alone with nine, five, seven arrows tore the Vanaras into pieces.

shloka_text: स शरैस्सूर्यसङ्काशैश्शातकुम्भविभूषितैः । वानरान् समरेवीरःप्रममाथसुदुर्जयः ।।6.73.38।।
explanation: Hero Indrajith, who is difficult to conquer in battle, killed the Vanaras with sun like arrows decorated with gold.

shloka_text: तेभिन्नगात्रास्समरेवानराश्शरपीडिताः । पेतुर्मथितसङ्कल्पास्सुरैरिवमहासुराः ।।6.73.39।।
explanation: Pierced by arrows in the battle, those Vanaras with their necks broken, giving up hopes of winning, frustrated, fell like the demons oppressed by great gods.

shloka_text: तंतपन्तमिवादित्यंघोरैर्बाणगभस्तिभिः । अभ्यधावन्तसङ्कृद्धास्सम्युगेवानरर्षभाः ।।6.73.40।।
explanation: Then the bulls among Vanaras rushed in the battlefield towards Indrajith whose arrows were dreadful and blazing like the Sun 's rays.

shloka_text: ततस्तुवानरास्सर्वेभिन्नदेहाविचेतसः । व्यथिताविद्रवन्तिस्मरुधिरेणसमुक्षिताः ।।6.73.41।।
explanation: Then Vanaras with their bodies broken, courage and consciousness lost, blood flowed from mutilated bodies.

shloka_text: रामस्यार्थेपराक्रम्यवानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः । नर्दन्तस्तेऽभिवृत्तास्तुसमरेसशिलायुधाः ।।6.73.42।।
explanation: Vanaras, armed with rocks in the battle, roaring and not turning back, stood for the cause, giving up their life.

shloka_text: तेद्रुमैःपर्वताग्रैश्चशिलाभिश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । अभ्यवर्षन्तसमरेरावणिंपर्यवस्थिताः ।।6.73.43।।
explanation: The Vanaras retreated back to the battle and rained on Ravana's son, trees, mountains and rocks.

shloka_text: तद्रुमाणांशिलानां च वर्षंप्राणहरंमहत् । व्यपोहतमहातेजारावणिस्समितिंजयः ।।6.73.44।।
explanation: Energetic Indrajith, who is ever victorious in battle dispersed the deadly rain of rocks and trees capable of taking out life.

shloka_text: ततःपावकसङ्काशैश्शरैराशीविषोपमैः । वानराणामनीकानिबिभेदसमरेप्रभुः ।।6.73.45।।
explanation: Then the Lord of Rakshasas dispersed the complete army of Vanaras with arrows burning like fire and resembling venomous serpents.

shloka_text: अष्टादशशरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्सविदद्वागन्धमादनम् । विव्याथनवभिश्चैवनलंदूरादवस्थितम् ।।6.73.46।।
explanation: He shattered Gandhamadana with eighteen very sharp arrows and Nala standing at far with nine arrows.

shloka_text: सप्तभिस्तुमहावीर्योमैन्दंमर्मविदारणैः । पञ्चभिर्विशिखैश्चैवगजंविव्याथसंयुगे ।।6.73.47।।
explanation: Indrajith, the eminent hero, hurt Mainda in private parts and even afflicted Gaja with five spades in the battle.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तंतुदशभिर्नीलंत्रिंशद्भिरेव च । सुग्रीवमृषभंचैवसोऽङ्गदंद्विविधंतथा ।।6.73.48।। घोरैर्दत्तवरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्निष्प्राणानकरोत्तदा ।
explanation: Then he struck Jambavan with ten, Neela with thirty, and Sugriva, Rshaba and Angada. In the same way Dwivida with sharp and terrific arrows that were bestowed upon him as boons and made them lose consciousness.

shloka_text: अन्यानपितदामुख्यान्वानरान् बहुभिश्शरैः ।।6.73.49।। अर्दयामाससङ्कृद्धःकालानगिरिवमूर्छितः ।
explanation: Highly enraged like the fire at the time of universal destruction, he tormented many chiefs of Vanaras and others.

shloka_text: सशरैस्सूर्यसङ्काशैस्सुमुक्सैशशीघ्रगामिभिः ।।6.73.50।। वानराणामनीकानिनिर्ममन्थमहारणे ।
explanation: He, with his swift moving arrows, bright like the Sun , stretching to the ear hurt many vanaras in that great war.

shloka_text: आकुलांवानरींसेनांशरजालेनमोहिताम् ।।6.73.51।। हृष्टस्सपरयाप्रीत्याददर्शक्षतजोक्षिताम् ।
explanation: Seeing the vast Vanara army deluded by the net of arrows, Indrajith was very happy.

shloka_text: वानरेवमहातेजाराक्षसेन्द्रात्मजोबली ।।6.73.52।। संसृज्यबाणवर्षं च शस्त्रवर्षं च दारुणम् । ममर्दवानरानीकमिन्द्रजित्त्वरितोबली ।।6.73.53।।
explanation: Highly energetic, mighty, and swift Indrajith raining sharp arrows and weapons quickly Devastated the Vanara army.

shloka_text: वानरेवमहातेजाराक्षसेन्द्रात्मजोबली ।।6.73.52।। संसृज्यबाणवर्षं च शस्त्रवर्षं च दारुणम् । ममर्दवानरानीकमिन्द्रजित्त्वरितोबली ।।6.73.53।।
explanation: Highly energetic, mighty, and swift Indrajith raining sharp arrows and weapons quickly Devastated the Vanara army.

shloka_text: स्वसैन्यमुत्सृज्यसमेत्यतूर्णंमहारणेवानरवाहिनीषु । अदृश्यमानश्शरजालमुग्रंववर्षनीलाम्बुधरोयथाम्बु ।।6.73.54।।
explanation: Leaving from his own army space, moving swiftly, remaining concealed in the blue sky like a rain cloud, Indrajith rained a net of arrows.

shloka_text: तेशक्रजिद्बाणविशीर्णदेहामायाहताविस्वरमुन्नदन्तः । रणेनिपेतुर्हरयोऽद्रिकल्पायथेन्द्रवज्राभिहतानगेन्द्राः ।।6.73.55।।
explanation: In the battle, the Vanaras who were like mountains, became victims of cheating, and were struck by Indrajith's thunderbolt like arrows. Their bodies were broken and shrieking in discordant tones they fell like mountains.

shloka_text: तेकेवलंसन्ददृशुशशिताग्रान्बाणान्रणेवानरवाहिनीषु । मायानिगूढंतुसुरेन्द्रशत्रुं न चावृतंराक्षसमभ्यपश्यन् ।।6.73.56।।
explanation: The Vanara troops saw only the sharp pointed arrows covering them. They could not see the enemy of Indra being concealed by magical power.

shloka_text: ततस्सरक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मासर्वादिशोबाणगणैशशिताग्रैः । प्रच्छादयामासरविप्रकाशैर्विपादयामास च वानरेन्द्रान् ।।6.73.57।।
explanation: Thereafter the mighty Lord of Rakshasas despatched volley of sharp tipped arrows bright like the Sun, at Vanara leaders on all sides and eradicated.

shloka_text: स शूलनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वधानिव्याविध्यदीप्तानलसन्निभानि । सविस्फुलिङ्गोज्ज्वलपावकानिववर्षतीव्रंप्लवगेन्द्रसैन्ये ।।6.73.58।।
explanation: He rained a violent shower of tridents, swords and axes burning like sacrificial fire shedding flames with fire sparks on the Vanara army.

shloka_text: ततोज्वलनसङ्काशैश्शरैर्वानरयूथपाः । ताडिताश्शक्रजिद्बाणैःप्रफुल्लाइवकिंशुकाः ।।6.73.59।।
explanation: Struck by Indrajith's arrows, the (bodies of) Vanara troops were glowing like Kimsuka trees (red in colour) bearing flowers.

shloka_text: तेन्योन्यमभिसर्पन्तोनिनदन्तश्चविस्वरम् । राक्षसेन्द्रास्त्रनिर्भिन्नानिपेतुर्वानरर्षभाः ।।6.73.60।।
explanation: Hit by the Rakshasa king, the bulls among Vanaras gliding towards one another roared in discordant tones and fell down.

shloka_text: उदीक्षमाणागगनंकेचिन्नेत्रेषुताडिताः । शरैर्विविशुरन्योन्यंपेतुश्चजगतीतले ।।6.73.61।।
explanation: Some Vanaras looking up to the sky eyes pierced with arrows held one another and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदंगन्धमादनम् । जाम्बवन्तंसुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च ।।6.73.62।। मैन्दं च द्विविदंनीलंगवाक्षंगजगोमुभौ । केसरिंहरिलोमानंविद्युद्धंष्ट्रं च वानरम् ।।6.73.63।। सूर्याननंज्योतिमुखंतथादधिमुखंहरिम् । पावकाक्षनळंचैवकुमुदंचैववानरम् ।।6.73.64।। प्रसैश्शूलैश्शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसम्हितैः । विव्याधहरिशार्दूलान् सर्वांस्तान्राक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.73.65।।
explanation: Indrajith, the foremost of the Rakshasas, with lances, tridents, sharp arrows charged with mantras pierced at all the tigers among Vanaras --Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, Gandhamadanam, Jambavantha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Mainda, Dwivida, Neela, Gavaksha, Vidyuuhamshtra, and monkeys Suryanana, Jyothimukha, Dadhimukha, Pavaksha, and also Nala, Kumuda.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदंगन्धमादनम् । जाम्बवन्तंसुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च ।।6.73.62।। मैन्दं च द्विविदंनीलंगवाक्षंगजगोमुभौ । केसरिंहरिलोमानंविद्युद्धंष्ट्रं च वानरम् ।।6.73.63।। सूर्याननंज्योतिमुखंतथादधिमुखंहरिम् । पावकाक्षनळंचैवकुमुदंचैववानरम् ।।6.73.64।। प्रसैश्शूलैश्शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसम्हितैः । विव्याधहरिशार्दूलान् सर्वांस्तान्राक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.73.65।।
explanation: Indrajith, the foremost of the Rakshasas, with lances, tridents, sharp arrows charged with mantras pierced at all the tigers among Vanaras --Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, Gandhamadanam, Jambavantha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Mainda, Dwivida, Neela, Gavaksha, Vidyuuhamshtra, and monkeys Suryanana, Jyothimukha, Dadhimukha, Pavaksha, and also Nala, Kumuda.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदंगन्धमादनम् । जाम्बवन्तंसुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च ।।6.73.62।। मैन्दं च द्विविदंनीलंगवाक्षंगजगोमुभौ । केसरिंहरिलोमानंविद्युद्धंष्ट्रं च वानरम् ।।6.73.63।। सूर्याननंज्योतिमुखंतथादधिमुखंहरिम् । पावकाक्षनळंचैवकुमुदंचैववानरम् ।।6.73.64।। प्रसैश्शूलैश्शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसम्हितैः । विव्याधहरिशार्दूलान् सर्वांस्तान्राक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.73.65।।
explanation: Indrajith, the foremost of the Rakshasas, with lances, tridents, sharp arrows charged with mantras pierced at all the tigers among Vanaras --Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, Gandhamadanam, Jambavantha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Mainda, Dwivida, Neela, Gavaksha, Vidyuuhamshtra, and monkeys Suryanana, Jyothimukha, Dadhimukha, Pavaksha, and also Nala, Kumuda.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदंगन्धमादनम् । जाम्बवन्तंसुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च ।।6.73.62।। मैन्दं च द्विविदंनीलंगवाक्षंगजगोमुभौ । केसरिंहरिलोमानंविद्युद्धंष्ट्रं च वानरम् ।।6.73.63।। सूर्याननंज्योतिमुखंतथादधिमुखंहरिम् । पावकाक्षनळंचैवकुमुदंचैववानरम् ।।6.73.64।। प्रसैश्शूलैश्शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसम्हितैः । विव्याधहरिशार्दूलान् सर्वांस्तान्राक्षसोत्तमः ।।6.73.65।।
explanation: Indrajith, the foremost of the Rakshasas, with lances, tridents, sharp arrows charged with mantras pierced at all the tigers among Vanaras --Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, Gandhamadanam, Jambavantha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Mainda, Dwivida, Neela, Gavaksha, Vidyuuhamshtra, and monkeys Suryanana, Jyothimukha, Dadhimukha, Pavaksha, and also Nala, Kumuda.

shloka_text: स वैगदाभिर्हरियूथमुख्यान्निर्भिद्यबाणैस्तपनीयवङ्खैः । ववर्षरामंशरवृष्टिजालैस्सलक्ष्मणंभास्कररमशिकल्पैः ।।6.73.66।।
explanation: Having hurt the Vanara leaders with maces and arrows shining like gold, he rained volley of arrows shining like sun rays on Lakshmana and Rama.

shloka_text: स बाणवर्षैरभिवृष्यमाणोधारानिपातानिवतानच्नित्य । समीक्षमाणःपरमाद्भुतश्रीरामतदालक्ष्मणमित्युवाच ।।6.73.67।।
explanation: Most wonderful and prosperous Rama, looking at the rain of arrows continuing to shower, not minding it as if they are rain of water drops, spoke this to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: असौपुनर्लक्ष्मणराक्षसेन्द्रोब्रह्मास्त्रमाश्रित्यसुरेन्द्रशत्रुः । निपातयित्वाहरिसैन्यमुग्रमस्मान्शरैरर्दयतिप्रसक्तः ।।6.73.68।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! Rakshasa king, an enemy of Indra afflicted the Vanaras with the Brahmastram secured by him. Using that power, he is tormenting us with sharp arrows."

shloka_text: स्वयम्भुवादत्तवरोमहात्मा । समाहितोन्तर्हितभीमकायः । कथंनुशक्योयुधिनष्टदेहोनिहन्तुमद्येन्द्रजिदुद्यतास्त्रः ।।6.73.69।।
explanation: "How can it be possible now to destroy that great Indrajith who is conferred with boons of invincibility by the creator Brahma, who is steadfast and is concealed in dreadful form with weapons uplifted?"

shloka_text: मन्येस्वयम्भुर्भगवानच्नित्योयस्यैतदस्त्रंप्रभवश्चयोऽस्य । बाणावपातास्त्वमिहाद्यधीमन्मयासहाव्यग्रमनास्सहस्व ।।6.73.70।।
explanation: "This weapon of him (Indrajith) is that of the glorious creator and is presided by Him. By that reason he is inconceivable. O! Wise Lakshmana, remain calm and undisturbed at this hail of arrows."

shloka_text: प्रच्छादयत्येषहिराक्षसेन्द्रस्सर्वाधिशस्सायकवृष्टिजालैः । एतच्चसर्वंपतिताग्य्रशूरं न भ्राजतेवानरराजसैन्यम्।। 6.73.71।।
explanation: "This Rakshasa king is covered thickly with volley of arrows on all sides. Able warriors of Vanaras are falling and not happy."

shloka_text: आवांतुदृष्टवापतितौविसंज्ञौनिवृत्तयुद्दौगतरोषहर्षे । ध्रुवंप्रवेक्ष्यत्यमरारिवासमसौसमादायरणाग्रलक्ष्मीम् ।।6.73.72।।
explanation: "This Indrajith is desisting from comb at on seeing us. As the Vanaras have lost pride and happiness and fallen into unconscious state, he would surely think that he has attained prosperity after victory in war and surely enter Lanka, the abode of enemies of god."

shloka_text: ततस्तुताविन्द्रजिदस्त्रजालैर्भभूवतुस्तत्रतथाविशस्तौ । स चापितौतत्रविदर्शयित्वाननादहर्षाद्युधिराक्षसेन्द्रः ।।6.73.73।।
explanation: Seeing the two princes severed and fallen down struck by the net of arrows of Indrajith, he roared happily in the battle.

shloka_text: सतत्तदावानरसैन्यमेवंरामं च सङ्ख्येसहलक्ष्मणेन । विषादयित्वासहसाविवेशपुरींदशग्रीवभुजाभिगुप्ताम् ।।6.73.74।। सन्स्तूयमानस्सतुयातुधानैः । पत्रे च सर्वंहृषितोऽभ्युवाच ।।6.73.75।।
explanation: Thereafter Vanara army withdrew from the battle along with Rama and Lakshmana. Indrajith for his part moved to the abode protected by Ravana's arms, while being praised. He at once entered the city happily and related everything to the father. ।। इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेत्रिसप्ततितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the Seventy third sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by Sage Valmiki.

shloka_text: तयोस्तदासादितयोरणाग्रेमुमोहसैन्यंहरिपुङ्गवानाम् । सुग्रीवनीलाङ्गदजाम्बवन्तो न चापिकिञ्चित्प्रतिपेदिरेते ।।6.74.1।।
explanation: The two brothers (Rama and Lakshmana) become unconscious in the forefront of the battle the monkey leaders lose senses. Sugriva, Neela, Angada and Jambavantha did not know What to do.

shloka_text: ततोविषण्णंसमवेक्ष्यसैन्यंविभीषणोबुद्धिमतांवरिष्ठः । उवाचशाखमृगराजवीरानाश्वासयन्नप्रतिमैर्वचोभिः ।।6.74.2।।
explanation: Thereafter, foremost among the wise, Vibheeshana observing the despondency of the monkey leaders spoke to them reassuring in incomparable words.

shloka_text: माभैष्टनास्त्यत्रविषादकालोयदार्यपुत्त्रौविवशौविषण्णौ । स्वयम्भुवोवाक्यमथोद्वहन्तौयत्सादिताविन्द्रजिदस्त्रजालैः ।।6.74.3।।
explanation: "O Noble men! Do not fear. Rama and Lakshmana are afflicted by Indrajith's volley of arrows and have lost senses. They are despondent to honour the statement of the creator not otherwise."

shloka_text: तस्मैतुदत्तंपरमास्त्रमेतत्स्वयम्भुवाब्राह्मममोघवेगम् । तन्मानयन्तौयुधिराजपुत्रौनिपातितौकोऽत्रविषादकालः ।।6.74.4।।
explanation: To him (Indrajith), the creator has conferred this weapon of Brahma endowed with terrific speed. To respect the missile both the princes have fallen. Why do you grieve?

shloka_text: ब्राह्ममस्त्रंततोधीमान्मानयित्वातुमारुतिः । विभीषणवचश्श्रुत्वाहनूमांस्तमथाब्रवीत् ।।6.74.5।।
explanation: Thereafter, hearing Vibheeshana's words, wise Hanuman spoke this with respect to the missile of Brahma.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्निहतेसैन्येवानराणांतरस्विनाम् । योयोधारयतेप्राणांस्तंतमाश्वासयाव ।।6.74.6।।
explanation: "Whoever is strong among Vanaras, have been struck and are alive breathing among the Vanaras. Let us restore their confidence."

shloka_text: तावुभौयुगपवदीरौहनूमद्राक्षसोत्तमौ । उल्काहस्तौतदारात्रौरणशीर्षेविचेरतुः ।।6.74.7।।
explanation: The two heroes, Hanuman and Vibheeshana, and the foremost of Rakshasas with torch in hand searched for the left over Vanaras in the battlefield.

shloka_text: भिन्नलाङ्गूलहस्तोरुपादाङ्गुळशिरोधरैः । स्रवद्भिःक्षतजंगात्रैःप्रस्रवद्भिस्ततस्ततः ।।6.74.8।। पतितैःपर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसङ्कुलाम् । शस्सैश्चपतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशातेवसुन्धराम् ।।6.74.9।।
explanation: Two of them saw the ground covered with Vanaras of mountainlike forms, who had fallen with tails cut off, some with broken thighs, broken legs and fingers, necks severed, letting off blood, discharging urine and glowing weapons lying on the ground.

shloka_text: भिन्नलाङ्गूलहस्तोरुपादाङ्गुळशिरोधरैः । स्रवद्भिःक्षतजंगात्रैःप्रस्रवद्भिस्ततस्ततः ।।6.74.8।। पतितैःपर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसङ्कुलाम् । शस्सैश्चपतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशातेवसुन्धराम् ।।6.74.9।।
explanation: Two of them saw the ground covered with Vanaras of mountainlike forms, who had fallen with tails cut off, some with broken thighs, broken legs and fingers, necks severed, letting off blood, discharging urine and glowing weapons lying on the ground.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवमङ्गदंनीलंशरभंगन्धमादनम् । गवाक्षं च सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमाहुकम् ।।6.74.10।। मैन्दंनळंज्योतिमुखंद्विविदंपनसंतथा । विभीषणोहनूमांश्चददृशातेहतान् रणे ।।6.74.11।।
explanation: Vibheeshana and Hanuman saw in the battlefield Sugriva, Angada, Neela, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Gavaksha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Ahuka, Mainda, Nala, Jyothimukha, Dwivida and Panasa struck down.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवमङ्गदंनीलंशरभंगन्धमादनम् । गवाक्षं च सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमाहुकम् ।।6.74.10।। मैन्दंनळंज्योतिमुखंद्विविदंपनसंतथा । विभीषणोहनूमांश्चददृशातेहतान् रणे ।।6.74.11।।
explanation: Vibheeshana and Hanuman saw in the battlefield Sugriva, Angada, Neela, Sarabha, Gandhamadana, Gavaksha, Sushena, Vegadarsi, Ahuka, Mainda, Nala, Jyothimukha, Dwivida and Panasa struck down.

shloka_text: सप्तषष्टिर्हताःकोट्योवानराणांतरस्विनाम् । अह्नःपञ्चमशेषेणवल्लभेनस्वयम्भुवः ।।6.74.12।।
explanation: By the creator's missile Indrajith struck down sixtyseven crores of strong Vanaras between the fifth and last part of the day.

shloka_text: सागरौघनिभंभीमंदृष्टवाबाणार्दितंबलम् । मार्गतेजाम्बवन्तंस्मिहनूमान् सविभीषणः ।।6.74.13।।
explanation: Vibheeshana and Hanuman seeing the ocean of Vanara army and the glowing arrows on them, looked for Jambavantha.

shloka_text: स्वभावजरयायुक्तंवृद्धंशरशतैश्चितम् । प्रजापतिसुतंवीरंशाम्यन्तमिवपावकम् ।।6.74.14।। दृष्टवातमुपसङ्ग्रम्यपौलस्त्योवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Paulastya (Vibheeshana of Paulastya clan), seeing the son of Prajapathi (Jambavan), who by nature was wise and aged, afflicted by hundreds of arrows, like a cooling fire sacrifice, went close by and spoke these words.

shloka_text: च्चिदार्यशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नप्राणाध्वंसितास्तव ।।6.74.15।। विभीषणवचश्श्रुत्वाजाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गवः । कृच्छ्रादभ्युग्दिरन्वाक्यमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.74.16।।
explanation: "O Noble Jambavan! Indeed, your life has not been afflicted with these sharp arrows." Hearing this, Jambavan uttered these words with difficulty."

shloka_text: च्चिदार्यशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नप्राणाध्वंसितास्तव ।।6.74.15।। विभीषणवचश्श्रुत्वाजाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गवः । कृच्छ्रादभ्युग्दिरन्वाक्यमिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.74.16।।
explanation: "O Noble Jambavan! Indeed, your life has not been afflicted with these sharp arrows." Hearing this, Jambavan uttered these words with difficulty."

shloka_text: नैरृतेन्द्रमहावीर्यस्वरेणत्वाऽभिलक्ष्ये । पीड्यमानशशितैर्बाणैर्नत्वापश्यामिचक्षुषा ।।6.74.17।।
explanation: "Great hero, Vibheeshana! I recognise you by your voice. Pierced with sharp arrows I am not able to see you."

shloka_text: अञ्जनासुप्रजायेनमातरिश्वा च नैरृत । हनुमान् वानरश्रेष्ठःप्राणान् धारयतेक्वचित् ।।6.74.18।।
explanation: Vibheeshana (Rakshasa)! Indeed, Hanuman, the foremost of Vanaras, by whose birth, Anjana and Supraja are blessed as parents, are they alive?

shloka_text: श्रुत्वाजाम्बवतोवाक्यमुवाचेदंविभीषणः । आर्यपुत्रावतिक्रम्यकस्मात्पृच्छसिमारुतिम् ।।6.74.19।।
explanation: After hearing Jambavantha, Vibheeshana said "Noble son, why are you enquiring about Hanuman?"

shloka_text: नैवराजनिसुग्रीवेनाङ्गदेनापिराघवे । आर्यसन्दर्शितस्स्नेहोयथावायुसुतेपरः ।।6.74.20।।
explanation: "Noble one! You are showing affection to Hanuman but not to King Sugriva, or Angada or even Raghava?"

shloka_text: विभीषणवचश्श्रुत्वाजाम्बवान्वाक्यमब्रवीत् । शृणुनैरृतशार्दूलयस्मात् पृच्छामिमारुतिम् ।।6.74.21।।
explanation: On hearing Vibheeshana, the tiger among Rakshasas, Jambavan replied, "Listen why I enquired about Maruthi."

shloka_text: तस्मिन्जीवतिवीरेतुहतमप्यहतंबलम् । हनूमत्युज्झितप्राणेजीवन्तोऽपिवयम् हृता ।।6.74.22।।
explanation: If this hero Hanuman is alive, even if the army is destroyed and if we are alive, it is like dead only.

shloka_text: धरतेमारुतिस्तातमारुतप्रतिमोयदि । वैश्वानरसमोवीर्वेजीविताशाततोभवेत् ।।6.74.23।।
explanation: "Dear! If Hanuman who is equal to wind god, resembles Vyshvanara (God of fire) is breathing, then we can hope to live (for life)."

shloka_text: ततोवृद्धमुपागम्यनियमेनाभ्यवादयत् । गृह्यजाम्बवतःपादौहनूमान्मारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.24।।
explanation: Thereafter, Hanuman the son of the wind god coming close to the aged Jambavan clasped his feet in accordance with tradition and greeted him.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वाहनुमतोवाक्यंतदाऽपिव्यथितेन्द्रियः । पुनर्जातमिवात्मानंमन्यतेप्लवगोत्तमः ।।6.74.25।।
explanation: Then again, Jambavan whose senses were affected, on hearing the statement of Hanuman, the foremost of Vanaras, felt as though he was born again.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजाहनूमन्तं स जाम्बवान् । आगच्छहरिशार्दूल वानरांस्त्रातुमर्हसि ।।6.74.26।।
explanation: Then brilliant Jambavan spoke to Hanuman, the tiger among Vanaras, on reaching him. "You ought to protect the Vanaras."

shloka_text: नान्योवक्रमपर्याप्तस्त्वमेषांपरमस्सखा । त्वत्पराक्रमकालोऽयंनान्यंपश्यामिकथञ्चन ।।6.74.27।।
explanation: "You are fully endowed with prowess and great friend of monkeys in that way. It is time for you to show your talent. Indeed, I do not see anyone else."

shloka_text: ऋक्ष्वानरवीराणामनीकानिप्रहर्षय । शल्यौकुरुचाप्येतासादितौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.74.28।।
explanation: For the Bears and Vanaras, create excessive happiness. For Rama and Lakshmana who are unconscious, make them comfortable.

shloka_text: गत्वापरममध्वानमुपर्युपरिसागरम् । हिमवन्तंनगश्रेष्ठंहनुमन्गन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.74.29।।
explanation: "Hanuman, you ought to go very far over the sea to the Himalayas, the highest mountain."

shloka_text: ततःकाञ्चनमत्युच्चमृषभंपर्वतोत्तमम् । कैलासशिखरंचापिद्रक्ष्यस्यरिनिषूदन ।।6.74.30।।
explanation: "O Destroyer of enemies! there on top you will see the foremost of the mountain Rshaba and on the peak of Kailasa."

shloka_text: तयोशशिखरयोर्मध्येप्रदीप्तमतुलप्रभम् । सर्यौषधियुतंवीर द्रक्ष्यस्यौषधिपर्यतम् ।।6.74.31।।
explanation: "Heroic Hanuman! In the middle of those two mountains, you will see a highly splendid mountain covered with all kinds of medicinal herbs."

shloka_text: तस्यवानरशार्दूल चतस्रो मूधि सम्भवाः । द्रक्ष्यस्योषधयोदीप्तादीपय्नत्योदिशोदश ।।6.74.32।।
explanation: "O Tiger among monkeys! You will see on the summit four medicinal herbs growing there illuminating the ten directions."

shloka_text: मृतसञ्जीवनींचैवविशल्यकरणीमपि । सुवर्णकरणींचैवसन्धानकरणींतथा ।।6.74.33।।
explanation: "Mrtasanjivani, Visalyakarani, Suvarnakarani, Sandhani, all these herbs are grown there."

shloka_text: तास्सर्वाहनुमन्गृह्वक्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि । आश्वासयहरीन् प्राणैर्योज्यगन्धवहात्मज ।।6.74.34।।
explanation: "Hanuman, taking the four herbs you, the son of wind god ought to return immediately with the speed of wind, to unite the life of the monkeys and reassure."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वाजाम्बवतोवाक्यंहनूमान् हरिपुङ्गवः । आपूर्यतबलोद्धर्षैस्तोयवेगैरिवार्णवः ।।6.74.35।।
explanation: "Hearing the instruction of Jambavantha, the son of the wind god, infused with wind speed as the ocean, heaves with the force of wind increasing his strength fully."

shloka_text: पर्वततटाग्रस्थःपीडयन् पर्वतोत्तमम् । हनूमान्दृश्यतेवीरोद्वितीयइवपर्वतः ।।6.74.36।।
explanation: Standing on the summit of the foremost of the mountains, hero Hanuman pressing his feet seemed like a second mountain

shloka_text: हरिपादविनिर्भग्नोनिषसाद स पर्वतः । न शशाकतदात्मानंसोढुंभृशनिपीडितः ।।6.74.37।।
explanation: Trodden by the feet of Hanuman that mountain pressed forcibly by himself could not bear his strength.

shloka_text: तस्यपेतुर्नगाभूमौहरिवेगाच्चजज्वलुः । शृङ्गाणि च व्यशीर्यन्तपीडितस्यहनूमता ।।6.74.38।।
explanation: Oppressed by the speed of Hanuman, the mountain fell to the ground and by the impetuosity of his speed the mountain got shattered.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् सम्पीड्यमानेतुभग्नद्रुमशिलातले । न शेकुर्वानरास्स्थातुंघूर्णमानेनगोत्तमे ।।6.74.39।।
explanation: As the foremost of the mountain got oppressed it crushed the trees and rocks on it and Vanaras were unable to stand on it.

shloka_text: साघूर्णितमहाद्वाराप्रभग्नगृहगोपुरा । लङ्कात्रासाकुलारात्रौप्रवृत्तेवाभवत्तदा ।।6.74.40।।
explanation: Then the mighty gates of Lanka shaking, homes shattered, stricken with fear that night it seemed Lanka was dancing.

shloka_text: पृथिवीधरसङ्काशोनिपीड्यधरणीधरम् । पृथिवींक्षोभयामाससार्णवांमारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.41।।
explanation: Son of the wind god, who was like a mountain supported by earth, pressing hard caused the earth with its ocean to shake.

shloka_text: आरुरोहतदातस्माद्धरिर्मलयपर्वतम् । मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशंनानाप्रस्रवणाकुलम् ।।6.74.42।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णंविकासिकमलोत्पलम् । सेवितंदेवगन्धर्वैष्षष्टियोजनमुच्छ्रितम् ।।6.74.43।। विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णंबहुकन्दरशोभितम् ।।6.74.44।। सर्वानाकुलयंस्तत्रयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरान् । हनुमान् मेघसङ्काशोववृधेमारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.45।।
explanation: From that mountain the monkey sprang to Malaya Mountain which was like Meru and Mandara mountains. It was set with various springs, covered with various trees and creepers, abounded with lotuses, frequented by Devas, Gandharvas. It was sixty yojanas high and visited by Vidhyadharas, celestial nymphs, and sages, filled with various species of deer and numerous caves. Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras were living there. There the son of the wind god grew in size like a cloud.

shloka_text: आरुरोहतदातस्माद्धरिर्मलयपर्वतम् । मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशंनानाप्रस्रवणाकुलम् ।।6.74.42।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णंविकासिकमलोत्पलम् । सेवितंदेवगन्धर्वैष्षष्टियोजनमुच्छ्रितम् ।।6.74.43।। विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णंबहुकन्दरशोभितम् ।।6.74.44।। सर्वानाकुलयंस्तत्रयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरान् । हनुमान् मेघसङ्काशोववृधेमारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.45।।
explanation: From that mountain the monkey sprang to Malaya Mountain which was like Meru and Mandara mountains. It was set with various springs, covered with various trees and creepers, abounded with lotuses, frequented by Devas, Gandharvas. It was sixty yojanas high and visited by Vidhyadharas, celestial nymphs, and sages, filled with various species of deer and numerous caves. Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras were living there. There the son of the wind god grew in size like a cloud.

shloka_text: आरुरोहतदातस्माद्धरिर्मलयपर्वतम् । मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशंनानाप्रस्रवणाकुलम् ।।6.74.42।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णंविकासिकमलोत्पलम् । सेवितंदेवगन्धर्वैष्षष्टियोजनमुच्छ्रितम् ।।6.74.43।। विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णंबहुकन्दरशोभितम् ।।6.74.44।। सर्वानाकुलयंस्तत्रयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरान् । हनुमान् मेघसङ्काशोववृधेमारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.45।।
explanation: From that mountain the monkey sprang to Malaya Mountain which was like Meru and Mandara mountains. It was set with various springs, covered with various trees and creepers, abounded with lotuses, frequented by Devas, Gandharvas. It was sixty yojanas high and visited by Vidhyadharas, celestial nymphs, and sages, filled with various species of deer and numerous caves. Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras were living there. There the son of the wind god grew in size like a cloud.

shloka_text: आरुरोहतदातस्माद्धरिर्मलयपर्वतम् । मेरुमन्दरसङ्काशंनानाप्रस्रवणाकुलम् ।।6.74.42।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णंविकासिकमलोत्पलम् । सेवितंदेवगन्धर्वैष्षष्टियोजनमुच्छ्रितम् ।।6.74.43।। विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णंबहुकन्दरशोभितम् ।।6.74.44।। सर्वानाकुलयंस्तत्रयक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरान् । हनुमान् मेघसङ्काशोववृधेमारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.45।।
explanation: From that mountain the monkey sprang to Malaya Mountain which was like Meru and Mandara mountains. It was set with various springs, covered with various trees and creepers, abounded with lotuses, frequented by Devas, Gandharvas. It was sixty yojanas high and visited by Vidhyadharas, celestial nymphs, and sages, filled with various species of deer and numerous caves. Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras were living there. There the son of the wind god grew in size like a cloud.

shloka_text: पद्भ्यांतुशैलमापीड्यबडबामुखवन्मुखम् । विवृत्योग्रंननादोच्चैस्त्रासयन्निवराक्षसान् ।।6.74.46।।
explanation: Pressing the mountain hard by his feet, opening his largemouth wide, he roared like Rakshasas to make Rakshasas fearful.

shloka_text: तस्यनानद्यमानस्यश्रुत्वानिनदमद्भुतम् । लङ्कास्थाराक्षसास्सर्वे न शेकुस्स्पन्दितुंभयात् ।।6.74.47।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas in Lanka hearing the loud roar of Hanuman were afraid and could not stir from there.

shloka_text: नमस्कृत्वाऽथरामायमारुतिर्भीमविक्रमः । राघवार्थेपरंकर्मसमीहतपरन्तपः ।।6.74.48।।
explanation: Maruti, scorcher of enemies, endowed with terrific valour offered prayers to Sri Rama and made up his mind to embark on the stupendous task for Raghava.

shloka_text: स पुच्छमुद्यम्यभुजङ्गकल्पंविनम्यपृष्ठंश्रवणेनिकुञ्च्य । विवृत्यवक्त्रंबडबामुखाभमापुफ्लुवेव्योमनिचण्डवेगः ।।6.74.49।।
explanation: Raising his tail which resembled a serpent, bending his back, and ears, opening his mouth wide expounded Hanuman sprang up at terrific speed.

shloka_text: सवृक्षषण्डांस्तरसाजहारशैलान् शिलाःप्राकृतवानरांश्च । बाहूरुवेगोद्धतसम्प्रणुन्नास्तेक्षीणवेगास्सलिलेनिपेतुः ।।6.74.50।।
explanation: By the speed of his arms and thighs clusters of branches of trees, mountains, rocks, and common monkeys were attracted, and with reduction of speed along the way the rocks fell.

shloka_text: तौप्रसार्योरगभोगकल्पौभुजौभुजङ्गारिनिकाशवीर्यः । जगाममेरुंनगराजमग्य्रंदिशःप्रकर्षन्निववायुसूनुः ।।6.74.51।।
explanation: Stretching his arms which resembled coils of serpents, whose valour equalled Garuda, enemy of serpents, as if attracting all the directions went to the summit of the foremost mountain which equalled Meru mountain.

shloka_text: स सागरंघूर्णितवीचिमालंतथाभृशंभ्रामितसर्वसत्त्वम् । समीक्षमाणस्सहसाजगामचक्रंयथाविष्णुकराग्रमुक्तम् ।।6.74.52।।
explanation: Observing the ocean whose waves were made to revolve round (by his speed), exceedingly, whose creatures were made to whirl round violently (by the wind force generated by his speed), he went forth like the wheel loosened from Vishnu's hand.

shloka_text: स पर्वतान्वृक्षगवान् सरांसिनदीस्तटाकानिपुरोत्तमानि । स्फीतान् जनान्तानपिसम्प्रवीक्ष्यजगामवेगापतितृतुल्यवेगः ।।6.74.53।।
explanation: Watching the mountains, trees, birds, rivers, tanks, the best of cities, all of them and prosperous people, he went at his father's speed.

shloka_text: आदित्यपथमाश्रित्यजगाम स गतक्लमः । हनूमांस्त्वरितोवीरःपितृतुल्यपराक्रमः ।।6.74.54।।
explanation: Hanuman who was equal to his father in prowess, went unwearied, hurriedly in the path of the Sun.

shloka_text: जवेनमहतायुक्तोमारुतिर्मारुतोयथा । जगामहरिशार्दूलोदिशश्शब्देनपूरयन् ।।6.74.55।।
explanation: Maruthi, the tiger among monkeys went like the wind possessing great speed filling sound in all directions.

shloka_text: स्म्मरन्जाम्बवतोवाक्यंमारुतिर्वातरंहसा । ददर्शसहसागत्वाहिमवन्तंमहाकपिः ।।6.74.56।।
explanation: Going at wind speed, the great monkey Maruthi, remembering Jambavantha's words, reached and sighted the Himalayas.

shloka_text: नानाप्रस्रवणोपेतंनानाकन्दरनिर्घरम् । श्वेताभ्रचयसङ्काशैशशिखरैश्चारुदर्शनैः ।।6.74.57।। शोभितंविविधैर्वृक्षैरगमत्पर्वतोत्तमम् ।
explanation: He reached the foremost of mountains, which was adorned with different kinds of springs, many caves and cascades and graced with trees. The peaks were like masses of white autumn clouds graced with splendour and beautiful to look at.

shloka_text: स तंसमासाद्यमहानगेन्द्रमतिप्रवृद्धोत्तमघोरशृङ्गम् । ददर्शपुण्यानिमहाश्रमाणिसुरर्षिसंघोत्तमसेवितानि ।।6.74.58।।
explanation: Reaching there he saw the tall and terrifying peaks of the Lord of mountains frequented by Devatas and sages, meritorious hermitages.

shloka_text: स ब्रह्मकोशंरजतालयं च शक्रालयंरुद्रशरप्रमोक्षम् । हयाननंब्रह्मशिरश्चदीप्तंददर्शवैवस्वतकिङ्करांश्च ।।6.74.59।।
explanation: He saw the seat of Brahma, the abode of Rajathanabha, the abode of Indra, the location from which Rudra discharged an arrow (at Tripura), the abode of Lord Hayagriva, and glowing abode of the deity presiding over Brahmastra and Vyvasvatah's attendants.

shloka_text: वज्रालयंवैश्रवणालयं च सूर्यप्रभंसूर्यनिबन्धनंच । a. ब्रह्मासनंशङ्करकार्मुकं च ददर्शनाभिं च वसुन्धरायाः ।।6.74.60।।
explanation: He saw Vajralayam (where Brahma gave Indra the thunderbolt), the abode of Kubera shining like the Sun, the spot where the Sun was bound, Brahma's abode and the abode of the bow of Lord Siva, and the earth navel.

shloka_text: कैलासमग्य्रंहिमवच्छिलां च तथर्षभंकाञ्चनशैलमग्य्रम् । सन्दीप्तसर्वौषधिसन्प्रदीप्तंददर्शसर्वौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रम् ।।6.74.61।।
explanation: He saw Kailas, the rocks of Himalayas, that way on the Rshaba the foremost Lord Siva, the golden mountain, and the great mountain on which grew, glowing medicinal herbs.

shloka_text: स तंसमीक्ष्यानलरश्मिदीप्तंविसिष्मियेवासवदूतसूनुः । आवृत्यतंचौषधिपर्वतेन्द्रंतत्रौषधीनांविचयंचकार ।।6.74.62।।
explanation: Observing the herbs blazing like fire, he was astonished at the herbs on the mountain and went round thinking of the names of herbs (asked by Jambavan).

shloka_text: सयोजनसहस्राणिसमतीत्यमहाकपिः । दिव्यौषधिधरंशैलंव्यचरन्मारुतात्मजः ।।6.74.63।।
explanation: The great monkey, son of the wind god, having traversed a thousand yojanas began to range the wonderful herbs and went about searching.

shloka_text: महौषध्यस्ततस्सर्वास्तस्मिन् पर्वतसत्तमे । विज्ञायार्थिनमायान्तंततोजग्मुरदर्शनम् ।।6.74.64।।
explanation: Perceiving a seeker coming for them, the herbs all over the wonderful mountain disappeared.

shloka_text: स तामहात्माहनुमानपश्यंश्चुकोपकोपाच्चभृशंननाद । अमृष्यमाणोऽनगिनिकाशचक्षुर्महीधरेन्द्रंतमुवाचवाक्यम् ।।6.74.65।।
explanation: The great soul Hanuman was not able to see, those herbs, became angry and his eyes were burning like fire in anger. He jumped up and roared and said to the lordly mountain.

shloka_text: कीमेतदेवंसुविनिश्चितंतेयद्राघवेनासिकृतानुकम्प । पश्याद्यमद्बाहुबलाभिभूतोविकीर्णमात्मानमथोनगेन्द्र ।।6.74.66।।
explanation: "O King of mountains! You are not showing compassion to Raghava. Is it your determination to be like this? Overcome by my shoulder strength I shall crush you now. You may see."

shloka_text: स तस्यशृङ्गंसनगंसनागंसकाञ्चनंधातुसहस्रजुष्टम् । विकीर्णकूटंज्वलिताग्रसानुंप्रगृह्यवेगात्सहसोन्ममाथ ।।6.74.67।।
explanation: Seizing hold of the peaks vehemently, its trees, elephants, gold mines withthousands of minerals he crushed the projections and set fire and burnt and uprooted swiftly.

shloka_text: सतसमुत्पाट्यखमुत्पपातवित्रास्यलोकान् ससुरासुरेन्द्रान् । संस्तूयमानःखचरैरनेकैर्जगामवेगाद्गरुडोग्रवेगः ।।6.74.68।।
explanation: Striking terror among Devatas and demons and leaders inhabiting the world, uprooting the mountain he hurried at Garuda's speed into the sky praised by aerial creatures.

shloka_text: स भास्कराध्वानमनुप्रपन्नस्तंभास्कराभंशिखरंप्रगृह्य । बभौतदाभास्करसन्निकाशोरवेस्समीपेप्रतिभास्कराभः ।।6.74.69।।
explanation: Resembling the Sun closely, radiant like the Sun he was taking the top of the mountain, betaking himself in the vicinity of the Sun he was like another Sun.

shloka_text: स तेनशैलेनभृशंरराजशैलोपमोगन्धवहात्मजस्तु । सहस्रधारेणसपावकेनचक्रेणखेविष्णुरिवार्पितेन ।।6.74.70।।
explanation: He, the son of the wind god sitting upon the crag, was delightful like Vishnu with a flaming wheel shining.

shloka_text: तंवानराःप्रेक्ष्यविनेदुरुच्चैस्सतानपिप्रेक्ष्यमुदाननाद । तेषांसमुध्घुष्टरवंनिशम्यलङ्कालयाभीमतरंविनेदुः ।।6.74.71।।
explanation: Observing him high the Vanaras became joyful, and he also saw them. Hearing their loud noise becoming aware of the Rakshasas of Lanka also roared in terrible fear.

shloka_text: ततोमहात्मानिपपाततस्मिन् शैलोत्तमेवानरसैन्यमथ्ये । हर्युत्तमेभ्यशशिरसाऽभिवाद्यविभीषणंतत्र स सस्वजे च ।।6.74.72।।
explanation: The great Hanuman along with the mountain descended in the midst of the Vanara army, and greeted the army head bent down and embraced Vibheeshana standing there.

shloka_text: तावप्युभौमानुषराजपुत्रौतंगन्धमाघ्रायमहौषधीनाम् । बभूवतुस्तत्रतदाविशल्यावुत्तस्थुरन्ये च हरिप्रवीराः ।।6.74.73।।
explanation: The two sons of the ruler of men inhaling the fragrance of the herbs became free from wounds. Other Vanara heroes also got restored.

shloka_text: सर्वेविशल्याविरुजाःक्षणेनहरिप्रवीराश्चहताश्चयेस्युः । गन्धेनतासांप्रवरौषधीनांसुप्तानिशान्तेष्विवसम्प्रबुद्धाः ।।6.74.74।।
explanation: All those Vanara warriors killed were restored with life instantly by the fragrance. Those who were asleep also got up when they became fully awake.

shloka_text: दाप्रभृतिलङ्कायांयुध्यन्तेहरिराक्षसाः । तदाप्रभृतिमानार्थमाज्ञयारावणस्य च ।।6.74.75।। येहन्यन्तेरणेतत्रराक्षसाःकपिकुञ्जरैः । हताहतास्तुक्षिप्यन्तेसर्वएवतुसागरे ।।6.74.76।।
explanation: From the beginning of the war in Lanka till the end without exception, all the Rakshasas were killed in war by the Vanara leaders then and there were thrown into the ocean by Ravana's instruction, not to have means of proof.

shloka_text: दाप्रभृतिलङ्कायांयुध्यन्तेहरिराक्षसाः । तदाप्रभृतिमानार्थमाज्ञयारावणस्य च ।।6.74.75।। येहन्यन्तेरणेतत्रराक्षसाःकपिकुञ्जरैः । हताहतास्तुक्षिप्यन्तेसर्वएवतुसागरे ।।6.74.76।।
explanation: From the beginning of the war in Lanka till the end without exception, all the Rakshasas were killed in war by the Vanara leaders then and there were thrown into the ocean by Ravana's instruction, not to have means of proof.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजास्सुग्रीवोवानराधिपः । अर्थ्यंविज्ञापयंश्चापिहनूमन्तमिदंवचः ।।6.75.1।।
explanation: Sugriva, the king of Vanaras called Hanuman to make him know the task ahead and said these words.

shloka_text: यतोहतःकुम्भकर्णःकुमाराश्चनिषूदिताः । नेदानीमुपनिर्हारंरावणोदातुमर्हति ।।6.75.2।।
explanation: " As Kumbhakarna is killed and his sons are destroyed, Ravana may not putup defence again. I think."

shloka_text: येयेमहाबलास्सन्तिलघवश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । लङ्कामभ्युतन्त्याशुगृह्योल्काःप्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.75.3।। हरयोहरिसङ्काशाःप्रदग्धुंरावणालयम् ।
explanation: "Of the bulls among vanaras, endowed with prowess, whoever is quick, able and foremost, let them go to Lanka, the abode of Ravana."

shloka_text: तोस्तंगतआदित्येरौद्रेतस्मिन्निशामुखे ।।6.75.4।। लङ्कामभिमुखास्सोल्काजग्मुस्तेप्लवगर्षभाः ।
explanation: Thereafter the bulls among Vanaras turned their faces towards Lanka and went holding torches in hand, after the Sun set as the frightening night started.

shloka_text: उल्काहस्सैर्हरिगणैस्सर्वतस्समभिद्रुताः ।।6.75.5।। आरक्षस्थाविरूपाक्षास्सहसाविप्रदद्रुवुः ।
explanation: Vanara troops went all over with torches and chased by them, the Rakshasas at the gates ran instantly.

shloka_text: गोपुराट्टप्रतोलीषुचर्यासुविविधासु च ।।6.75.6।। प्रासादेषु च सम्हृष्टास्ससृजुस्तेहुताशनम् ।
explanation: Rejoiced Vanaras set fire to the towering gates, attics, different streets as well as mansions to send away Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तेषांगृहसहस्राणिददाहहुतभुक्तदा ।।6.75.7।। प्रासादाःपर्वताकाराःपतन्तिधरणीतले ।
explanation: Then thousands of their houses were burnt by fire (consumer of offerings), and mountain like mansions collapsed to the ground.

shloka_text: अगुरुर्दह्यतेतत्रवरं च हरिचन्दनम् ।।6.75.8।। मौक्तिकामणयस्स्निग्धावज्रंचापिप्रवालकम् ।
explanation: There, in Lanka, incense and the best of sandalwood was burnt. Nay even glossy pearls, gems and diamonds were also burnt.

shloka_text: क्षौमं च दह्यतेतत्रकौशेयंचापिशोभनं ।।6.75.9।। आविकंविविधंचौर्णंकाञ्चनंभाण्डमायुधम् ।
explanation: Their white linen and beautiful silks were burnt. Nay, even several blankets of wool, chests and weapons were also burnt.

shloka_text: नानाविकृतसंस्थानंवाजिभाण्डपरिच्छदौ ।।6.75.10।। गजग्रैवेयकक्ष्याश्चरथभाण्डाश्चसम्स्कृताः ।
explanation: Different kinds of peculiar kinds of ornaments used to decorate horses, ornaments worn round the neck and girths of elephants, and polished chariot decorations.

shloka_text: नुत्राणि च योधानांहस्त्यश्वानां व चर्म च ।।6.75.11।। खडगाधनूंषिज्वाबाणास्तोमराङ्कुशशक्तयः ।
explanation: Leather armour of the warriors, shields of horses, excellent bow strings, swords, arrows, goads, lances, and javelins.

shloka_text: रोमजंवालजंचर्मव्याघ्रजंचण्डजंबहु ।।6.75.12।। मुक्तामणिविचित्रांश्चप्रासादांश्चसमन्ततः । विविधानस्त्रसंयोगानग्निर्दहतितत्रवै ।।6.75.13।।
explanation: With fire all over, rugs made of hair of animals, whisks made of fur of animals, tiger skins, musk, wonderful pearls, and gems in laid dwellings of many kinds, and clusters of war weapons were burnt.

shloka_text: रोमजंवालजंचर्मव्याघ्रजंचण्डजंबहु ।।6.75.12।। मुक्तामणिविचित्रांश्चप्रासादांश्चसमन्ततः । विविधानस्त्रसंयोगानग्निर्दहतितत्रवै ।।6.75.13।।

explanation: The fire consumed many kinds of wonderful homes of Rakshasas, with loved ones on the best beds, their armour made of gold Rakshasas decked with garland s and best of attire their eyes inebriated with intoxication, shaking while walking slowly, holding their loved ones, seized with anger against enemies, holding mace and tridents in hand, eating, drinking and sleeping on the best beds, fast asleep some out of fear taking their sons going quickly and all of them dwelling there in hundreds and thousands were burning again and again.

shloka_text: सारवन्तिमहार्हाणिगम्भीरगुणवन्ति च । हेमचन्द्रार्धचन्द्राणिचन्द्रशालोनतानि च ।।6.75.19।। तत्रचित्रगवाक्षाणिसाधिष्ठानानिसर्वशः । मणिविद्रुमचित्राणिस्पृशन्तीवदिवाकरम् ।।6.75.20।। क्रौञ्चबर्हिबवीणानांभूषणानां च निस्स्वनैः । नादितान्यचलाभानिवेश्मान्यग्निर्ददाह स ।।6.75.21।।
explanation: The fire consumed the houses which were strong and impenetrable, with many enclosures, magnificent ones, constructed in gold in the shape of a half moon and full moon, windows endowed with wonderful pictures. All over the rooms were high on top, decorated with gems, and as if touching the Sun. It was rendered noisy with notes of herons and peacocks, playing of Veena, and jingling of ornaments like the vibration of sounds. The dwellings which looked like mountains were consumed by fire.

shloka_text: सारवन्तिमहार्हाणिगम्भीरगुणवन्ति च । हेमचन्द्रार्धचन्द्राणिचन्द्रशालोनतानि च ।।6.75.19।। तत्रचित्रगवाक्षाणिसाधिष्ठानानिसर्वशः । मणिविद्रुमचित्राणिस्पृशन्तीवदिवाकरम् ।।6.75.20।। क्रौञ्चबर्हिबवीणानांभूषणानां च निस्स्वनैः । नादितान्यचलाभानिवेश्मान्यग्निर्ददाह स ।।6.75.21।।

explanation: The fire consumed the houses which were strong and impenetrable, with many enclosures, magnificent ones, constructed in gold in the shape of a half moon and full moon, windows endowed with wonderful pictures. All over the rooms were high on top, decorated with gems, and as if touching the Sun. It was rendered noisy with notes of herons and peacocks, playing of Veena, and jingling of ornaments like the vibration of sounds. The dwellings which looked like mountains were consumed by fire.

shloka_text: ज्वलनेनपरीतानितोरणानिचकाशिरे । विद्युद्भिरिवनद्धानिमेघजालानिघर्मगे ।।6.75.22।।
explanation: The archways covered with a touch of fire shone like lightning in summer, girt round like clusters of clouds.

shloka_text: ज्वलनेनपरीतानिनिपेतुर्भवनान्वथ । वज्रिवज्रहतानीवशिखराणिमहागिरेः ।।6.75.23।।
explanation: The mansions burnt by fire fell down like a huge mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: विमानेषुप्रसुस्ताश्चदह्यमानावराङ्गनाः । त्यक्ताभरणसर्वाङ्गाहाहेत्युच्चैर्विचुक्रुशुः ।।6.75.24।।
explanation: The lovely women sleeping in burnt mansion tops screamed loudly in desperation saying 'Alas! Oh Oh!' and removing their ornaments.

shloka_text: तत्रचाग्निपरीतानिनिपेतुर्भवनान्यपि । वज्रिवज्रहतानीवशिखराणिमहागिरेः ।।6.75.25।।
explanation: Like peaks of mountains struck by thunderbolt the mansions also fell, caught in fire.

shloka_text: तानिनिर्दह्यमानानिदूरतःप्रचकाशिरे । हिमवच्छिखराणीवदीप्तौषदिवनानिच ।।6.75.26।।
explanation: As the mansions were burning, they shone like the peaks of Himalayas glowing at a distance.

shloka_text: हर्म्याग्रैर्दह्यमानैश्चज्वालाप्रज्वलितैरपि । रात्रौसादृश्यतेलङ्कापुष्पितैरिवकिंशुकैः ।।6.75.27।।
explanation: While the tops of dwellings were burning, flames were blazing, and Lanka seemed adorned with Kimsuka blossoms.

shloka_text: हस्त्यध्यक्षैर्गजैर्मुक्तेर्मुक्सैश्चैवतुरङ्गमैः । बभूवलङ्कालोकान्तेभ्रान्तग्राहइवार्णवः ।।6.75.28।।
explanation: In Lanka with the elephants set free, horses set free by the guards, it was like an agitated ocean at the end of the world cycle.

shloka_text: अश्वंमुक्तंगजोदृष्टवाक्वचिद्भीतोऽपसर्पति । भीतोभीतंगजंदृष्टवाक्वचिदश्वोनिवर्तते ।।6.75.29।।
explanation: Some horses that were released, went in different directions afraid of elephants. Some elephants seeing horses ran away in fear.

shloka_text: लङ्कायांदह्यमानायांशुशुभे स महार्णवः । छायासंसक्तसलिलोलोहितोदइवार्णवः ।।6.75.30।।
explanation: While Lanka was burning its image reflected in the ocean made the ocean look like an ocean of red waters.

shloka_text: साबभूवमुहूर्तेनहरिभिर्दीपितापुरी । लोकस्यास्यक्ष्येघोरेप्रदीप्तेववसुन्दरा ।।6.75.31।।
explanation: Set fire by the monkeys, in a short while, the city was like a land flaming out of dreadful destruction in the world.

shloka_text: नारीजनस्यधूमेनव्याप्तस्योच्चैर्विनेदुषः । स्वनोज्वलनतप्तस्यशुश्रुवेशतयोजनम् ।।6.75.32।।
explanation: By the smoke that spread, scorched by the fire, the clamour of the women folk at the top of their voice was heard at a hundred yojanas.

shloka_text: प्रदग्धकायानपरान् राक्षसान्निर्गतान् बहिः । सहसाभ्युत्पतन्तिस्महरयोऽथयुयुत्सवः ।।6.75.33।।
explanation: And thereafter the monkeys who were eager to fight assailed the Rakshasas who came out suddenly unable to bear the burning of the bodies.

shloka_text: उद्घुष्टंवानराणां च राक्षसानां च निस्स्वनः । दिशोदशसमुद्रं च पृथिवींचान्वनादयत् ।।6.75.34।।
explanation: The clamour of the monkeys and the sighing of the Rakshasas resounded in all the ten directions including the ocean as well as the earth.

shloka_text: विशल्यौतुमहात्मानौतावुभौरामलक्ष्मणौ । असम्भ्रान्तौजगृहतुस्तदोभौधनुषीवरे ।।6.75.35।।
explanation: The two great souls, Rama, and Lakshmana, both relieved of pain seized hold of excellent and wellknown bows.

shloka_text: ततोविस्फारयानस्यरामस्यधनुरुत्तमम् । बभूवतुमुलश्शब्दोराक्षसानांभयावहः ।।6.75.36।।
explanation: Then Rama drew the best of bow, that created fear among the Rakshasas by its tumultuous sound.

shloka_text: अशोभततदारामोधनुर्विष्फारयन् महत् । भगवानिवसङ्कृद्धोभवोवेदमयंधनुः ।।6.75.37।।
explanation: Then, great Rama stretching his bow in great fury shone as though the divine Lord Siva was stretching his bow with imprints of Vedas.

shloka_text: उद्घुष्टंवानराणां च राक्षसानां च निस्स्वनम् । ज्याशब्दस्तावुभौशब्दावतिरामस्यशुश्रुवे ।।6.75.38।।
explanation: That sound of the twang of Rama's bow could be heard very high over and above the sounds of the Vanaras and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वानरोद्घुष्टघोषश्चराक्षसानां च निस्स्वनः । ज्याशब्दश्चापिरामस्यत्रयंव्याप्यदिशोदश ।।6.75.39।।
explanation: The sound of Rama's bow twang, the clamour of the Vanaras as well as the wailing of Rakshasas, all the three could be heard in all ten directions.

shloka_text: तस्यकार्मुकमुक्सैश्चशरैस्तत्पुरगोपुरम् । कैलासशृङ्गप्रतिमंविशीर्णमपतद्भुवि ।।6.75.40।।
explanation: The entrance gate of Lanka, which was like Kailasa, crumbled and fell by the shaft released from the bow of Rama.

shloka_text: ततोरामशरान् दृष्टवाविमानेषुगृहेषु च । सन्नाहोराक्षसेन्द्राणांतुमुलस्समपद्यत ।।6.75.41।।
explanation: Seeing Rama's arrows on the highrise mansions and houses, the Rakshasa leaders started preparing for comb at out of fear.

shloka_text: तेषांसन्नह्यमानानांसिंहनादं च कुर्वताम् । शर्वरीराक्षसेन्द्राणांरौद्रीवसमपद्यत ।।6.75.42।।
explanation: As the Rakshasa leaders were preparing (for attack) and emitting leonine roar, night came upon like the night of Rudra (night of final dissolution).

shloka_text: आदिष्टावानरेन्द्रास्तेसुग्रीवेणमहात्मना । आसन्नद्वारमासाद्ययुध्यध्वंप्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.75.43।। यश्चवोवितथंकुर्वात्तत्रतत्रव्यवस्थितः । स हन्तव्योहिसंफ्लुत्यराजशासनदूषकः ।।6.75.44।।
explanation: Sugriva the great king of Vanaras commanded all the bulls among Vanaras, to encounter after reaching the gate of Lanka. "He who is staying wherever they are does not obey the king's command will be killed for being guilty of flouting the command", ordered Sugriva to the Vanaras.

shloka_text: आदिष्टावानरेन्द्रास्तेसुग्रीवेणमहात्मना । आसन्नद्वारमासाद्ययुध्यध्वंप्लवगर्षभाः ।।6.75.43।। यश्चवोवितथंकुर्वात्तत्रतत्रव्यवस्थितः । स हन्तव्योहिसंफ्लुत्यराजशासनदूषकः ।।6.75.44।।
explanation: Sugriva the great king of Vanaras commanded all the bulls among Vanaras, to encounter after reaching the gate of Lanka. "He who is staying wherever they are does not obey the king's command will be killed for being guilty of flouting the command", ordered Sugriva to the Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेषुवानरमुखेषुदीप्तोल्कोज्ज्वलपाणिषु । स्थितेषुद्वारमासाद्यरावणंमन्युराविशत् ।।6.75.45।।
explanation: Holding burning torches in hand the Vanara chiefs reached and standing at the gate, saw that Ravana was overtaken by anger.

shloka_text: तस्यजृम्भितविक्षेपाद्व्यामिश्रावैदिशोदश । रूपवानिवरुद्रस्यमन्युर्गात्रेष्वदृश्यत ।।6.75.46।।
explanation: The ten directions were disturbed violently by his yawning and his wrath was perceptible like Rudra' s form in his limbs by his wrath.

shloka_text: स निकुम्भं च कुम्भं च कुम्भकर्णात्मजावुभौ । प्रेषयामाससङ्कृद्धोराक्षससैर्बहुभिस्सह ।।6.75.47।।
explanation: Seized with anger, he sent for Kumbha and Nikumbha, both the sons of Kumbhakarna and many Rakshasas.

shloka_text: यूपाक्षश्शोणिताक्षश्चप्रजङ्घःकम्पनस्तथा । निर्ययुःकौम्भकर्णिभ्यांसहरावणशासनात् ।।6.75.48।।
explanation: Yupaksha, Sonithaksha, Prajangha, Kampana set out with both the sons of Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: शशासचैवतान् सर्वान्राक्षसान् सुमहाबलान् । राक्षसागच्छताद्यैवसिंहनादं च नादयन् ।।6.75.49।।
explanation: Roaring like a lion, he ordered all the Rakshasas of extraordinary strength to proceed instantly.

shloka_text: ततस्तुचोदितास्तेनराक्षसाज्वलितायुधाः । लङ्कायानिर्ययुर्वीराःप्रणदन्तःपुनःपुनः ।।6.75.50।।
explanation: Ordered by him again and again, the Rakshasa warriors went from Lanka with glowing weapons offering salutations to him.

shloka_text: रक्षसांभूषणस्थाभिर्भाभिस्स्वाभिश्चसर्वशः । चक्रुस्तेसप्रभंव्योमहरयश्चाग्निभिस्सह ।।6.75.51।।
explanation: The Rakshasas by the effulgence of ornaments and by themselves illumined all over the sky like monkeys did with torches.

shloka_text: तत्रताराधिपस्याभाताराणां च तथैव च । तयोराभरणासा च बलयोर्द्यामभासयन् ।।6.75.52।।
explanation: There the radiance of the moon and stars and the splendour of their ornaments brightened the sky.

shloka_text: चन्द्राभाभूषणाभा च गृहाणांसागरःपुनः । हरिराक्षससैन्यानिभ्राजयामाससर्वतः ।।6.75.53।।
explanation: The moon light and the splendour of the ornaments, also the light of shining ocean and dwellings lit up the Vanara and Rakshasa armies.

shloka_text: तत्रचोर्ध्वंप्रदीप्तानांगृहाणांसागरःपुनः । भाभिस्संसक्तसलिलश्चलोर्मिश्शुशुभेऽधिकम् ।।6.75.54।।
explanation: There the waves of the ocean shone brightly getting united with the fire of half burnt houses.

shloka_text: पताकाध्वजसंसक्तमुत्तमासिपरश्वधम् । भीमाश्वरथमातङ्गंनानापततिसमाकुलम् ।।6.75.55।। दीप्तशूलगदाखडगप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम् । तद्राक्षसबलंघोरभीमंविक्रमपौरुषम् ।।6.75.56।। ददृशेज्वलितप्रासंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । हेमजालाचितभुजंव्यावेष्टितपरश्वथम् ।।6.75.57।। व्याघूर्णितमहाशस्त्रंबाणसंसक्तकार्मुकम् । गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसम्मोदितमहानिलम् ।।6.75.58।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa army appeared terrific, fixed with flags and poles, equipped with best of axes, horses yoked to formidable chariots and elephants different kinds of foot soldiers, distinguished by wielding shining tridents, maces, swords spears and lances warriors of frightening valour and prowess holding shining barbed missiles hundreds of tiny bells tied to the chariots and elephants making noise  warriors endowed with arms decorated with gold, with axes and weapons to pierce arrows fixed to the bows, with an abundance of fragrance.

shloka_text: पताकाध्वजसंसक्तमुत्तमासिपरश्वधम् । भीमाश्वरथमातङ्गंनानापततिसमाकुलम् ।।6.75.55।। दीप्तशूलगदाखडगप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम् । तद्राक्षसबलंघोरभीमंविक्रमपौरुषम् ।।6.75.56।। ददृशेज्वलितप्रासंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । हेमजालाचितभुजंव्यावेष्टितपरश्वथम् ।।6.75.57।। व्याघूर्णितमहाशस्त्रंबाणसंसक्तकार्मुकम् । गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसम्मोदितमहानिलम् ।।6.75.58।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa army appeared terrific, fixed with flags and poles, equipped with best of axes, horses yoked to formidable chariots and elephants different kinds of foot soldiers, distinguished by wielding shining tridents, maces, swords spears and lances warriors of frightening valour and prowess holding shining barbed missiles hundreds of tiny bells tied to the chariots and elephants making noise  warriors endowed with arms decorated with gold, with axes and weapons to pierce arrows fixed to the bows, with an abundance of fragrance.

shloka_text: पताकाध्वजसंसक्तमुत्तमासिपरश्वधम् । भीमाश्वरथमातङ्गंनानापततिसमाकुलम् ।।6.75.55।। दीप्तशूलगदाखडगप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम् । तद्राक्षसबलंघोरभीमंविक्रमपौरुषम् ।।6.75.56।। ददृशेज्वलितप्रासंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । हेमजालाचितभुजंव्यावेष्टितपरश्वथम् ।।6.75.57।। व्याघूर्णितमहाशस्त्रंबाणसंसक्तकार्मुकम् । गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसम्मोदितमहानिलम् ।।6.75.58।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa army appeared terrific, fixed with flags and poles, equipped with best of axes, horses yoked to formidable chariots and elephants different kinds of foot soldiers, distinguished by wielding shining tridents, maces, swords spears and lances warriors of frightening valour and prowess holding shining barbed missiles hundreds of tiny bells tied to the chariots and elephants making noise  warriors endowed with arms decorated with gold, with axes and weapons to pierce arrows fixed to the bows, with an abundance of fragrance.

shloka_text: पताकाध्वजसंसक्तमुत्तमासिपरश्वधम् । भीमाश्वरथमातङ्गंनानापततिसमाकुलम् ।।6.75.55।। दीप्तशूलगदाखडगप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम् । तद्राक्षसबलंघोरभीमंविक्रमपौरुषम् ।।6.75.56।। ददृशेज्वलितप्रासंकिङ्किणीशतनादितम् । हेमजालाचितभुजंव्यावेष्टितपरश्वथम् ।।6.75.57।। व्याघूर्णितमहाशस्त्रंबाणसंसक्तकार्मुकम् । गन्धमाल्यमधूत्सेकसम्मोदितमहानिलम् ।।6.75.58।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa army appeared terrific, fixed with flags and poles, equipped with best of axes, horses yoked to formidable chariots and elephants different kinds of foot soldiers, distinguished by wielding shining tridents, maces, swords spears and lances warriors of frightening valour and prowess holding shining barbed missiles hundreds of tiny bells tied to the chariots and elephants making noise  warriors endowed with arms decorated with gold, with axes and weapons to pierce arrows fixed to the bows, with an abundance of fragrance.

shloka_text: घोरंशूरजनाकीर्णंमहाम्बुदरनिस्स्वनम् । तद्दृष्टवाबलमायातंराक्षसानांसुदारुणं ।।6.75.59।। सञ्चचालप्लवङ्गानांबलमुच्चैर्ननाद च ।
explanation: Crowded with fierce warriors coming like thundering rainy clouds, the Rakshasas, and the monkey troops coming forward made loud noises with an elevated tone.

shloka_text: जवेनाफ्लुत्य च पुनस्तद्बलंरक्षसांमहत् ।।6.75.60।। अभ्ययात्प्रत्यरिबलंपतङ्गाइवपावकम् ।
explanation: The great army of Rakshasas rushed towards the hostile army just as moths flew up towards flame.

shloka_text: तेषांभुजपरामर्शव्यामृष्टपरिघाशनि ।।6.75.61।। राक्षसानांबलंश्रेष्ठंभूयस्तरमशोभत ।
explanation: Their Clubs and Asanis brandished by rubbing with their arms, the great army of Rakshasas appeared very bright.

shloka_text: तत्रोन्मत्ताइवोत्पेतुर्हरयोऽथयुयुत्सवः ।।6.75.62।। तरुशैलैरभिघ्नन्तोमुष्टिभिश्चनिशाचरान् ।
explanation: Thereafter the monkeys eager to fight with night rangers rose as if gone mad striking the night rangers with trees and rocks.

shloka_text: तथैवापततांतेषांकपीनामसिभिशशितैः ।।6.75.63।। शिरांसिसहसाजह्रूराक्षसाभीमदर्शना ।
explanation: When the Rakshasas showed up in that manner, the monkeys approaching them cut off their heads instantly with sharp swords.

shloka_text: दशनैर्हतकर्णाश्चमुष्टिनिष्कीर्णमस्तकाः ।।6.75.64।। शिलाप्रहारभग्नाङ्गाविचेरुस्तत्रराक्षसाः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas with ears bitten off by the teeth of the monkeys, skulls smashed with fists, and limbs broken with blows of rocks they moved about.

shloka_text: तथैवाप्यपरेतेषांकपीनामभिलक्षिता ।।6.75.65।। प्रवीरानभितोजघ्नुर्घोररूपानिशाचराः ।
explanation: In the aforesaid manner the Vanaras struck more night rangers of terrific appearance, great heroes in front of them with sharp swords.

shloka_text: घ्नन्तमन्यंजघानान्यःपातयन्तमपातयत् ।।6.75.66।। गर्हमाणंजगर्हेऽन्योदशन्तमपरोऽदशत् ।
explanation: One struck another, who was striking the other. One threw down another who was throwing the other. One abused another reproaching contemptuously, and one bit his rival biting the other.

shloka_text: देहीत्यन्योददात्यन्योददामीत्यपरःपुनः ।।6.75.67।। किंक्लेशयसितिष्ठेतितत्रान्योन्यंबभाषिरे ।
explanation: There they conversed this way with one another 'One said hit me and another one offered to hit,', again another intervened and said, 'Why are you crying?' meaning I offer resistance, one said 'Why are you suffering like this?'.

shloka_text: विप्रलम्भितवस्त्रं च विमुक्तकवचायुधम् ।।6.75.68।। समुद्यतमहाप्रासंयष्टिशूलासिसङ्कुलम् । प्रावर्ततमहारौद्रंयुद्धंवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.75.69।।
explanation: Highly enraged Vanaras and Rakshasas fought with them, raiment slipping, shields and weapons dodged, huge lances lifted to fight. They used fists, tridents, spears, and swords.

shloka_text: विप्रलम्भितवस्त्रं च विमुक्तकवचायुधम् ।।6.75.68।। समुद्यतमहाप्रासंयष्टिशूलासिसङ्कुलम् । प्रावर्ततमहारौद्रंयुद्धंवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.75.69।।
explanation: Highly enraged Vanaras and Rakshasas fought with them, raiment slipping, shields and weapons dodged, huge lances lifted to fight. They used fists, tridents, spears, and swords.

shloka_text: वानरान्दशसप्तेतिराक्षसाजघ्नुराहवे । राक्षसान्दशसप्तेतिवानराश्चाभ्यपातयन् ।।6.75.70।।
explanation: In that fight the Rakshasas killed the Vanaras at the rate of ten to seven and the Vanaras struck down Rakshasas at the rate of ten to seven.

shloka_text: प्रवृत्तेसङ्कुलेतस्मिन् घोरेवीरजनक्ष्ये । अङ्गदःकम्पनंवीरमाससादरणोत्सुकः ।।6.76.1।।
explanation: While the fierce fight brought destruction of heroes in the ongoing combat, Angada eager to fight, assailed gallant Kampana.

shloka_text: आहूयसोङ्गदंकोपात्ताडयामासवेगितः । गदयाकम्पनःपूर्वं स चचालभृशाहतः ।।6.76.2।।
explanation: Kampana struck Angada challenging himin anticipation. He swiftly hurled a mace in anger and hurt him grievously and Angada reeled.

shloka_text: स संज्ञांप्राप्यतेजस्वीचिक्षेपशिखरंगिरेः । अर्दितस्तत्प्रहारेणकम्पनःपतितोभुवि ।।6.76.3।।
explanation: Rejuvenated Angada, after gaining consciousness acquired a mountain peak and shattered Kampana with a blow. wounded Kampana fell down.

shloka_text: ततस्तुकम्पनंदृष्टवाशोणिताक्षोहतंरणे । रथेनाभ्यपतत् क्षिप्रंतत्राङ्गदमभीतवत् ।।6.76.4।।
explanation: Then seeing Kampana killed, Sonitaksha, a fearless hero, quickly reached Angada by chariot.

shloka_text: सोङ्गदंनिशितैर्बाणैस्तदाविव्याधवेगितः । शरीरदारणैस्तीक्ष्णैःकालाग्निसमविग्रहैः ।।6.76.5।। क्षुरक्षुरप्रैर्नाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैश्शिलीमुखैः । कर्णिशल्यविपाठैश्चबहुभिश्चशितैश्शरैः ।।6.76.6।।
explanation: He (Sonitaksha) swiftly pierced with pointed shafts resembling fire raging at the time of dissolution and struck Angada with arrows known by names, Ksura, Ksurapra, Naracha, Vatsadanta, Silimukha, Karni, Salya, vipada and many sharp arrows.

shloka_text: सोङ्गदंनिशितैर्बाणैस्तदाविव्याधवेगितः । शरीरदारणैस्तीक्ष्णैःकालाग्निसमविग्रहैः ।।6.76.5।। क्षुरक्षुरप्रैर्नाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैश्शिलीमुखैः । कर्णिशल्यविपाठैश्चबहुभिश्चशितैश्शरैः ।।6.76.6।।
explanation: He (Sonitaksha) swiftly pierced with pointed shafts resembling fire raging at the time of dissolution and struck Angada with arrows known by names, Ksura, Ksurapra, Naracha, Vatsadanta, Silimukha, Karni, Salya, vipada and many sharp arrows.

shloka_text: अङ्गदःप्रतिविद्धाङ्गोवालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् । धनुरग्य्रंरथंबाणान्ममर्दतरसाबली ।।6.76.7।।
explanation: Courageous son of Vali, the mighty Angada encountered with vigour and crumbled the formidable bow (of Sonitaksha), his chariot and arrows.

shloka_text: शोणिताक्षस्ततःक्षिप्रमसिचर्मसमाददे । उत्पपातदिवंक्रुद्धोवेगवानविचारयन् ।।6.76.8।।
explanation: Thereupon enraged Sonitaksha, quickly sprang up to the sky at high speed with sword and shield.

shloka_text: तंक्षिप्रतरमाफ्लुत्यपरामृश्याङ्गदोबली । करेणतस्यतंखङ्गंसमाच्छिद्यननाद च ।।6.76.9।।
explanation: Mighty Angada springing up at a higher speed grasped his (Sonitaksha) hand and irritated him with a sword making loud noise.

shloka_text: तस्यांसफलकेखडगंनिजघानततोऽङ्गदः । यज्ञोपवीतवच्चैनंचिच्छेदकपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.76.10।।
explanation: Then Angada pierced his sword on the fl at surface of his shoulder diagonally and cut him with his sword.

shloka_text: तंप्रगृह्यमहाखडगंविनद्य च पुनःपुनः । वालिपुत्रोऽभिदुद्रावरणशीर्षेपरानरीन् ।।6.76.11।।
explanation: Vali's son, seizing that great sword again and again, roaring to finally terminate the remaining Rakshasas, went forward.

shloka_text: आयसींतुगदांप्रगृह्य स वीरःकनकाङ्गदः । शोणिताक्षस्समाविध्यतमेवानुपपात ह ।।6.76.12।।
explanation: Sonitha adorned with golden armlets taking hold of iron mace rushed behind Angada.

shloka_text: प्रजङ्घसहितोवीरोयूपाक्षस्तुततोबली । रथेनाभिययौक्रुद्दोवालिपुत्रंमहाबलम् ।।6.76.13।।
explanation: Then mighty Yupaksha, and Prajaghna for his part in fury assailed mighty Angada's chariot.

shloka_text: तयोर्मध्येकपिश्रेष्ठश्शोणिताक्षप्रजङ्घयोः । विशाखयोर्मध्यगतःपूर्णचन्द्रइवाभवत् ।।6.76.14।।
explanation: Angada, the foremost of Vanaras, coming between both Sonitaksha and Prajaghna shone like a full moon between the Visakha stars.

shloka_text: अङ्गदंपरिरक्षन्तौमैन्दोद्विविदएव च । तस्यतस्थतुरभ्याशेपरस्परदिदृक्ष्या ।।6.76.15।।
explanation: Both Mainda and Dwivida (maternal uncles of Angada) took position for the protection of one another facing the enemy.

shloka_text: भिपेतुर्महाकायाःप्रतियत्तामहाबलाः । राक्षसावानरान् रोषादसिचर्मगदाधराः ।।6.76.16।।
explanation: Rakshasas wielding swords and mace, endowed with stupendous strength and of huge body agitated and assailed Vanaras.

shloka_text: त्रयाणांवानरेन्द्राणांत्रिभीराक्षसपुङ्गवैः । संसक्तानांमहद्युद्धमभवद्रोमहर्षणम् ।।6.76.17।।
explanation: A momentous war took place between the three Rakshasas (Prajaghna, Yupaksha and Sonitaksha) and Vanara chiefs (Angada, Dwivida and Mainda) that caused horripilation.

shloka_text: तेतुवृक्षान् समादायसम्प्रचिपुराहवे । खडगेनप्रतिचिच्छेदतान् प्रजङ्घोमहाबलः ।।6.76.18।।
explanation: In the comb at the Vanaras seizing hold of trees hurled violently and mighty Prajaghna with his sword shattered them

shloka_text: रथानश्वान् द्रुमैश्शैलैस्तेप्रचिक्षिपुराहवे । शरौघैःप्रतिचिच्छेदतान्यूपाक्षोनिशाचरः ।।6.76.19।।
explanation: In that war the Vanaras hurled trees, rocks on chariots and horses and Yupaksha encountered them and tore them.

shloka_text: सृष्टाव्निविदमैन्दाभ्यांद्रुमानुत्पाट्यवीर्यवान् । बभञ्जगदयामध्येशोणिताक्षःप्रतापवान् ।।6.76.20।।
explanation: Heroic and courageous Sonitaksha tore the trees hurled by Dwivida and Mainda in midway by his mace and crushed them.

shloka_text: उद्यम्यविपुलंखडगंपरमर्मनिकृन्तनम् । प्रजङ्घोवालिपुत्रायअभिदुद्राववेगितः ।।6.76.21।।
explanation: Prajaghna taking up a huge sword went forward swiftly and assailed Angada.

shloka_text: तमभ्याशगतंदृष्टवावानरेन्द्रोमहाबलः । आजघानाश्वकर्णेनद्रुमेणातिबलस्तदा ।।6.76.22।।
explanation: Then Vanara leader Angada who was endowed with extraordinary strength, seeing Prajaghna of stupendous power coming forward, hit him with Aswakarna tree.

shloka_text: बाहुंचास्यसनिस्त्रिंशमाजघान स मुष्टिना । वालिपुत्रस्यघातेन स पपातक्षितावसिः ।।6.76.23।।
explanation: Angada hit the shoulder of Prajaghna which held the sword, with his fist. By that blow the sword got broken and dropped down

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवापतितंभूमौखङ्गमुलसन्निभम् । मुष्टिंसम्वर्तयामासवज्रकल्पंमहाबलः ।।6.76.24।।
explanation: Seeing the pestle shaped sword fallen on the ground, mighty Prajaghna clenched his fist, which was as hard as the thunderbolt.

shloka_text: स ललाटेमहावीर्यमङ्गदंवानरर्षभम् । आजघानमहातेजास्समुहूर्तंचचाल ह ।।6.76.25।।
explanation: Sonitaksha of extraordinary energy hit at the forehead of highly valiant Angada. For a while Angada was unable to move.

shloka_text: स संज्ञांप्राप्यतेजस्वीवालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् । प्रजङ्घस्यशिरःकायातखङ्गेनपातयत्क्षितौ ।।6.76.26।।
explanation: Son of Vali, who was full of vigour, on regaining consciousness hit Prajaghna on the head and trunk and made him fall down.

shloka_text: स यूपाक्षोऽश्रुपूर्णाक्षःपितृव्येनिहतेरणे । अवरुह्यरथात्क्षिप्रंक्षीणेषुखङ्गमाददे ।।6.76.27।।
explanation: Instantly alighting from the chariot, Yupaksha seeing the uncle exhausted and hurt, eyes filled with tears, he wielded the sword.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंसम्प्रेक्ष्ययूपाक्षंद्विविदस्त्वरन् । आजघानोरसिक्रुद्धोजग्राह च बलाद्बली ।।6.76.28।।
explanation: Observing Yupakasha fallen and rushing quickly, furious Dwivida struck him in the bosom with force and caught him

shloka_text: गृहीतंभ्रातरंदृष्टवाशोणिताक्षोमहाबलः । आजघानगदाग्रेणवक्षसिद्विविदंततः ।।6.76.29।।
explanation: Then seeing the brother caught, mighty Sonitaksha struck Dwivida in the bosom by a mace.

shloka_text: स गदाभिहतस्तेनसञ्चचालमहाबलः । उद्यता च पुनस्तस्यजहारद्विविदोगदाम् ।।6.76.30।।
explanation: Dwivida, though mighty reeled and could not move when struck by Sonitaksha. He got up and again and snatched the mace from Sonithaksha.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नन्तरेमैन्दोवीरोवानरयूथपः । यूपाक्षंताडयामासतलेनोरसिवीर्यवान् ।।6.76.31।।
explanation: In the meantime, valiant Vanara leader Mainda arrived and struck with his palm on the chest of Yupaksha.

shloka_text: तौशोणिताक्ष्यूपाक्षौप्लवङ्गाभ्यांतरस्विनौ । चक्रतुस्समरेतीव्रमाकर्षोत्पाटनंभृशम् ।।6.76.32।।
explanation: In that fight, courageous Sonitaksha and Yupaksha contested with the two monkeys pulling one another violently and throwing intensely.

shloka_text: द्विविदश्शोणिताक्षंतुविददारनखैर्मुखै । निष्पिपेष च वेगेनक्षितावाविध्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.76.33।।
explanation: Valiant Dwivida, for his part, tore Sonitaksha on his face with his nails, and quickening his pace threw him on the surface of the ground and bruised him.

shloka_text: पाक्षमभिसङ्कृद्धो मैन्दो वानरयूथपः । पीडयामासबाहुभ्यांसपपातहतःक्षितौ ।।6.76.34।।
explanation: Vanara leader, Mainda on his part, angrily pierced Yupaksha many times who fell on the ground dead.

shloka_text: हतप्रवीराव्यथिताराक्षसेन्द्रचमूस्तदा । जगामाभिमुखीसातुकुम्भकर्णसुतोयतः ।।6.76.35।।
explanation: Then many heroes died, Rakshasa king's army was distressed and went towards where Kumbhakarna's son was fighting.
