shloka_text: आपततनीं च वेगेनकुम्भस्तांसान्त्वयच्चमूम् । अथोत्कष्टंमहावीर्यैर्लब्धलक्ष्यैःप्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.76.36।। निपातितमहावीरांदृष्टवारक्षश्चमूंततः । कुम्भःप्रचक्रेतेजस्वीरणेकर्मसुदुष्करम् ।।6.76.37।।
explanation: Kumbha quickly restored the confidence of the troops. Then energetic Kumbha seeing the eminent heroes of Rakshasa army struck down, he found a favourable opportunity and drew up an excellent strategy and performed an extremely difficult deed in the battlefield.

shloka_text: आपततनीं च वेगेनकुम्भस्तांसान्त्वयच्चमूम् । अथोत्कष्टंमहावीर्यैर्लब्धलक्ष्यैःप्लवङ्गमैः ।।6.76.36।। निपातितमहावीरांदृष्टवारक्षश्चमूंततः । कुम्भःप्रचक्रेतेजस्वीरणेकर्मसुदुष्करम् ।।6.76.37।।
explanation: Kumbha quickly restored the confidence of the troops. Then energetic Kumbha seeing the eminent heroes of Rakshasa army struck down, he found a favourable opportunity and drew up an excellent strategy and performed an extremely difficult deed in the battlefield.

shloka_text: स धनुर्धन्विनांश्रेष्ठःप्रगृह्यसुसमाहितः । मुमोचाशीविषप्रख्यान्शरान्देहविदारणान् ।।6.76.38।।
explanation: He (Kumbha), the foremost wielder of bow, taking up the bow, remaining fully composed released arrows that resembled poisonous serpents capable of tearing the flesh.

shloka_text: तस्यतच्छुशुभेभूयस्सशरंधनुरुत्तमम् । विद्युदैरावतार्चिष्मद्िद्वतीयेन्द्रधनुर्यथा ।।6.76.39।।
explanation: Those best arrows fixed to the bow were shining like the cloud with flashes of lightning, and like a second bow of Indra.

shloka_text: आकर्णाकृष्टमुक्तेनजघानद्विविदंतदा । तेनहाटकपुङ्खेनपत्रतिणापत्त्रवाससा ।।6.76.40।।
explanation: Then he struck Dwivida with a golden shafted arrow that was loosened to kill by stretching the bow till the ear and released.

shloka_text: सहसाभिहतस्तेनविप्रमुक्तपदस्स्फुरन् । निपपाताद्रिकूटाभोविह्वलन् प्लवगोत्तमः ।।6.76.41।।
explanation: Struck all of a sudden, the foremost Vanara (Dwivida) alarmed, fell with legs, outstretched, trembling.

shloka_text: मन्दस्तुभ्रातरंभग्नंदृष्टवातत्रमहाहवे । लभिदुद्राववेगेनप्रगृह्यमहतींशिलाम् ।।6.76.42।।
explanation: Seeing the brother shattered in the great combat, Mainda on his part seizing a huge rock rushed swiftly.

shloka_text: तांशिलांतुप्रचिक्षेपराक्षसायमहाबलः । बिभेदतांशिलांकुम्भःप्रसन्नैःपञ्चभिश्शरैः ।।6.76.43।।
explanation: The mighty Vanara (Mainda) for his part hurled the rock to crush the Rakshasa. Kumbha attacked him with five sharp arrows and rock got broken.

shloka_text: सन्धायचान्यंसुमुखंशरमाशीविषोपमम् । आजघानमहातेजावक्षसिद्विविदाग्रजम् ।।6.76.44।।
explanation: Haughty Kumbha, fixed a charming arrow resembling a venomous serpent and struck at Dwivida's brother.

shloka_text: स तुतेनप्रहारेणमैन्दोवानरयूथपः । मर्मण्यभिहतस्तेनपपा त भुविमूर्छितः ।।6.76.45।।
explanation: That blow hit the Vanara leader in his private parts, and Mainda lost consciousness and fell down.

shloka_text: अङ्गदोमातुलौदृष्टवापथितौतुमहाबलौ । अभिदुद्राववेगेनकुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम् ।।6.76.46।।
explanation: Seeing the two maternal uncles fallen, Angada, who was endowed with great strength, attacked Kumbha, wielding a bow.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंविव्याधकुम्भःपञ्चभिरायसैः । त्रिभिश्चान्यैश्शितैर्बाणैर्मातङ्गमिवतोमरैः ।।6.76.47।।
explanation: Kumbha seeing Angada advancing towards him, with five steel arrows and three shafts pierced him just as an elephant is pierced with lances.

shloka_text: सोऽङ्गदंविविधैभिर्बाणैःकुम्भोविव्याथवीर्यवान् । अकुण्ठधारैर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णैःकनकभूषणैः ।।6.76.48।।
explanation: Kumbha, a valiant hero pierced Angada continuously with several sharp and pointed arrows decked with gold.

shloka_text: अङ्गदःप्रतिविद्धाङ्गोवालिपुत्रो न कम्पते । शिलापादपवर्षाणितस्यमूर्ध्निववर्ष ह ।।6.76.49।।
explanation: Vali's son was not shaken by the strike, showered rain of rocks and trees on his (Kumbha) forehead.

shloka_text: स प्रचिच्छेदतान् सर्वान् बिभेद च पुनश्शिलाः । कुम्भकर्णात्मजश्रशीमान् वालिपुत्त्रसमीरितान् ।।6.76.50।।
explanation: Prosperous Kumbhakarna's son also shattered the rocks hurled on him, breaking them.

shloka_text: आपतन्तं च ससम्प्रेक्ष्यकुम्भोवानरयूथपम् । भ्रुवोर्विव्याथबाणाभ्यामुल्काभ्यामिवकुञ्जरम् ।।6.76.51।।
explanation: Kumbha observing the Vanara leader coming towards him attacked him with fire sticks and pierced his eyebrows.

shloka_text: तस्यसुस्रावरुधिरंपिहितेचास्यलोचने । अङ्गदःपाणिनानेत्रेपिधायरुधिरोक्षिते ।।6.76.52।। सालमासन्नमेकेनपरिजग्राहपाणिवा ।
explanation: Blood flowed from his injured eyes and his eyes got veiled by blood. Covering his eyes with one hand he took hold of a Sal tree nearby.

shloka_text: सम्पीड्यरसिचास्कन्धम् करेणाभिनिवेश्य च ।।6.76.53।। किञ्चिदभ्यवनम्यैनमुन्ममाथयथागजः ।
explanation: Compressing the trunk of the tree on the chest with one hand and bending forward a little its branches with another hand, he (Angada) tore Kumbha in that way in the great fight like an elephant.

shloka_text: तमिन्द्रकेतुप्रतिमंवृक्षंमन्दरसन्निभम् ।।6.76.54।। समुत्सृजन्तंवेगेनपश्यतांसर्वरक्षसाम् ।
explanation: All the Rakshasas seeing the tall tree, which was like Mandara mountain, resembling Indra's banner hurriedly was about to let loose.

shloka_text: सबिभेदशितैर्बाणैस्सप्तभिःकायभेदनैः ।।6.76.55।। अङ्गदोविव्यधेऽभीक्षणंससादचमुमोह च ।
explanation: Kumbha shattered Angada with seven sharp arrows capable of tearing the body. Angada, pained by that screamed and lost his senses.

shloka_text: अङ्गदंव्यथितंदृष्टवासीदन्तमिवसागरम् ।।6.76.56।। दुरासदंहरिश्रेष्ठंरामायन्येन्यवेदयन् ।
explanation: Seeing the foremost Vanara, Angada who was difficult to encounter fell and like sinking into the ocean of despondency, the foremost Vanaras submitted to Rama.

shloka_text: रामस्तुव्यथितंश्रुत्वावालिपुत्त्रंरणाजरे ।।6.76.57।। व्यादिदेशहरिश्रेष्ठान्जाम्बवत्प्रमुखांस्ततः ।
explanation: On hearing that Angada was tormented in the battlefield and pained he ordered Jambavan and the best of monkey leaders to help him.

shloka_text: तेतुवानरशार्दूलाश्श्रुत्वारामस्यशासनम् ।।6.76.58।। अभिपेतुस्सुसङ्कृद्धाःकुम्भमुद्यतकार्मुकम् ।
explanation: On hearing Rama's command, the enraged Vanara tigers took up bows to attack Kumbha.

shloka_text: ततोद्रुमशिलाहस्ताःकोपसंरक्तलोचनाः ।।6.76.59।। रिरक्षिषन्तोऽभ्यपतन्नङ्गदंवानरर्षभाः ।
explanation: Bulls among Vanaras then took trees, and rocks in hand, with their eyes red in anger started for the protection of Angada.

shloka_text: जाम्बवांश्चसुषेणश्चवेगदर्शी च वानरः ।।6.76.60।। कुम्भकर्णात्मजंवीरंक्रुद्धास्समभिदुद्रुवुः ।
explanation: Jambavan, Sushena, Vegadarsi and other heroic Vanaras, full of anger also rushed to assail Kumbhakarna's son.

shloka_text: समीक्ष्यापततस्तांस्तुवानरेन्द्रान् महाबलान् ।।6.76.61।। आववारशरौघेणनगेनेवजलाशयम् ।
explanation: Perceiving that great army of Vanara leaders are advancing, Kumbha obstructed them with a volley of arrows just like a mountain obstructing the path of torrent.

shloka_text: तस्यबाणपथंप्राप्य न शेकुरतिवर्तितुम् ।।6.76.62।। वानरेन्द्रामहात्मानोवेलामिवमहादधिः ।
explanation: The Vanara leaders could not bear the range of arrows of Kumbhaka, just as a tide can't overstep the shore of an ocean.

shloka_text: तांस्तुदृष्टवाहरिगणान् शरवृष्टिभिरर्दितान् ।।6.76.63।। अङ्गदंपृष्ठतःकृत्वाभ्रातृजंप्लवगेश्वरः । भिदुद्राववेगेनसुग्रीवःकुम्भमाहवे ।।6.76.64।। शैलसानुचरंनागंवेगवानिवकेसरी ।
explanation: Seeing the Vanara army pained by the rain of arrows, Sugriva, the Lord of Vanaras having Angada in his rear, swiftly rushed and assailed Kumbhakarna's son just like a lion roaming in the mountains attacks elephants.

shloka_text: तांस्तुदृष्टवाहरिगणान् शरवृष्टिभिरर्दितान् ।।6.76.63।। अङ्गदंपृष्ठतःकृत्वाभ्रातृजंप्लवगेश्वरः । भिदुद्राववेगेनसुग्रीवःकुम्भमाहवे ।।6.76.64।। शैलसानुचरंनागंवेगवानिवकेसरी ।
explanation: Seeing the Vanara army pained by the rain of arrows, Sugriva, the Lord of Vanaras having Angada in his rear, swiftly rushed and assailed Kumbhakarna's son just like a lion roaming in the mountains attacks elephants.

shloka_text: उत्पाट्य च महाशैलनश्वकर्णान्दवान्बहून् ।।6.76.65।। अन्यांश्चविविधान्ववृक्षाचिक्षेपचिमहाबलः ।
explanation: Mighty strong he was, uprooting Aswakarna and many other several kinds of trees he hurled at them (Rakshasas).

shloka_text: तांछादयन्तीमाकाशंवृक्षवृष्टिंदुरासदाम् ।।6.76.66।। कुम्भकर्णात्मजश्शीघ्रंचिच्छेदनिशितैश्शरैः ।
explanation: Frenzied Kumbhakarna's son was torn under the shower of trees that covered space with sharp arrows which was difficult to approach.

shloka_text: अभिलक्षेणतीव्रेणकुम्भेननिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.76.67।। अचितास्तेद्रुमारेजुर्यथाघोराषतघ्नयः ।
explanation: The sharp arrows aimed at the target by Kumbha covered the trees and they shone like dreadful Sataghnis.

shloka_text: द्रुमवर्षंतुसञ्छिन्नंदृष्टवाकुम्भोनवीर्यवान् ।।6.76.68।। वानराधिपति: शीमान्महासत्त्वो न विव्यथे ।
explanation: Valiant hero, the prosperous and noble Sugriva, the chief of Vanaras did not get distressed when tormented with rain of trees.

shloka_text: निर्भिद्यमानस्सहसासहमानश्चतान् शरान् ।।6.76.69।। कुम्भस्यधनुराक्षिप्यबभञ्जेन्द्रधनुष्प्रभम् ।
explanation: He snatched the bow of Kumbha forcibly which was like Indra's rainbow, pulled it and broke, while tolerating the pain of the arrows.

shloka_text: अवफ्लुत्यततश्शीघ्रंकृत्वाकर्मसुदुष्करम् ।।6.76.70।। अब्रवीत्कुपितःकुम्भंभग्नशृङ्गमिवद्विपम् ।
explanation: Then Sugriva leapt into the chariot, which was a difficult deed to perform, saw Kumbha who was like an elephant and whose tusks were broken and spoke.

shloka_text: निकुम्भाग्रजवीर्यंतेबाणवेगवदद्भुतम् ।।6.76.71।। सन्नतिश्चप्रभावश्चतववारावणस्यवा ।
explanation: "Oh, elder brother of Nikumbha! Your valour, speed of your arrows, compliance, and glory is wonderful like that of Ravana's."

shloka_text: प्रह्लादबलिवृत्रघ्नकुभेरवरुणोपम ।।6.76.72।। एकस्त्वमनुजातोऽसिपितरंबलवृत्ततः ।
explanation: "You are equal to Prahlada, Bali, Indra, Kubera and Varuna in might. You alone have taken over like your father."

shloka_text: त्वामेवैकंमहाबाहुंचापहस्तमरिन्दमम् ।।6.76.73।। त्रिदशानातिवर्तन्तेजितेन्द्रियमिवाधयः । विक्रमस्वमहाबुद्धे कर्माणिममपश्यतः ।।6.76.74।।
explanation: "Oh! mightyarmed, Kumbha! wielding pike in hand, you are a tamer of enemies, you alone are the one that gods are not able to overcome, a pre eminent one who has gained over senses, highly intelligent, exhibiting your prowess and deeds before me."

shloka_text: त्वामेवैकंमहाबाहुंचापहस्तमरिन्दमम् ।।6.76.73।। त्रिदशानातिवर्तन्तेजितेन्द्रियमिवाधयः । विक्रमस्वमहाबुद्धे कर्माणिममपश्यतः ।।6.76.74।।
explanation: "Oh! mightyarmed, Kumbha! wielding pike in hand, you are a tamer of enemies, you alone are the one that gods are not able to overcome, a pre eminent one who has gained over senses, highly intelligent, exhibiting your prowess and deeds before me."

shloka_text: वरदानापतितृव्यस्तेसहतेदेवदानवान् । कुम्भकर्णस्तुवीर्येणसहते च सुरासुरान् ।।6.76.75।।
explanation: "Your uncle Ravana is able to withstand the Devas and Danavas by virtue of the boons and Kumbhakarna was able to with stand gods and demons by virtue of his courage."

shloka_text: ततःकुम्भस्तुसुग्रीवंबाहुभ्यांजगृहेतदा । गजाविवाहितमदौनिश्श्वसन्तौमुहुर्मुहु 76.81।। अन्योन्यगात्रग्रथितौकर्षन्तावितरेतरम् । सधूमांमुखतोज्वालांविसृजन्तौपरिश्रमात् ।।6.76.82।।
explanation: Thereafter Kumbha held Sugriva's shoulders. They were like two intoxicated elephants holding one another's limbs and rubbing each other and breathing heavily. In exertion they let out from their face fire mixed with smoke.

shloka_text: महाविमर्दंसमरेमयासहतवाद्भुतम् । अद्यभूतानिपश्यन्तुशक्रशम्बरयोरिव ।।6.76.77।।
explanation: "Just as the wonderful conflict between Indra and Sambara let the beings witness the mighty comb at between me and you."

shloka_text: कृतमप्रतिमंकर्मदर्शितंचास्त्रकौशलम् । पातिताहरिवीराश्चत्वयावैभीमविक्रमाः ।।6.76.78।।
explanation: "By an unequal deed done by you in the efficiency in the use of weapons has been exhibited. The monkey heroes of terrific valour have been made to fall."

shloka_text: उपालम्भभयाच्चापिनासिवीरमयाहतः । कृतकर्मपरिश्रान्तोविश्रान्तःपश्यमेबलम् ।।6.76.79।।
explanation: "O Stalwart! You have not been finished by me for the fear of reproaching. You are exhausted by your deeds and resting. Having rested, witness my strength now."

shloka_text: तेनसुग्रीववाक्येनसावमानेनमानितः । अग्नेराज्याहुतस्येवतेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत ।।6.76.80।।
explanation: Sugriva's words of flattering royalty captivated Kumbha's fire of energy, which doubled like fire fed with ghee.

shloka_text: तेनसुग्रीववाक्येनसावमानेनमानितः । अग्नेराज्याहुतस्येवतेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत ।।6.76.80।।
explanation: Sugriva's words of flattering royalty captivated Kumbha's fire of energy, which doubled like fire fed with ghee.

shloka_text: तेनसुग्रीववाक्येनसावमानेनमानितः । अग्नेराज्याहुतस्येवतेजस्तस्याभ्यवर्धत ।।6.76.80।।
explanation: Sugriva's words of flattering royalty captivated Kumbha's fire of energy, which doubled like fire fed with ghee.

shloka_text: तयोःपादाभिघाताच्चनिमग्नाचाभवन्महि । व्याघूर्णिततरङ्गश्चचुक्षुभेवरुणालयः ।।6.76.83।।
explanation: Then by the trampling of their feet the earth sank down, the abode of Varuna (ocean) was agitated with rolling waves.

shloka_text: ततःकुम्भंसमुत्क्षिप्यसुग्रीवोलवणाम्भसि । पातयामासवेगेनदर्शयन्नुदधेस्तलम् ।।6.76.84।।
explanation: Then Sugriva lifted Kumbha and threw him into the ocean quickly, to show him the bottom.

shloka_text: ततःकुम्भनिपातेनजलराशिस्समुत्थितः । व्निध्यमन्दरसङ्काशोविससर्पसमन्ततः ।।6.76.85।।
explanation: By Kumbha falling into the ocean, it got swollen to the form of Vindhya and Mandara mountain and water flowed all over.

shloka_text: ततःकुम्भस्समुत्पत्यसुग्रीवमभिपद्य च । आजघानोरसिक्रुद्धोवज्रवेगेनमुष्टिना ।।6.76.86।।
explanation: Then Kumbha hit Sugriva in anger with his fist at the speed of a thunderbolt on his chest.

shloka_text: तस्यचचर्मच पुस्फोटबहुसुस्रावशोणितम् । स च मुष्टिर्महावेगःप्रतिजघ्नेऽस्थिमण्डले ।।6.76.87।।
explanation: The armour of Sugriva slit open, and blood flowed at high speed and excessively. The first hit of Kumbha hit the skeletal framework of Sugriva in return.

shloka_text: त्दावेगेनतत्रासीत्तेजःप्रज्वलितंमहत् । वज्रनिष्पेषसञ्जाताज्वालामेरोर्यथागिरेः ।।6.76.88।।
explanation: Then by the speed of the hit on Sugriva's chest by Kumbha's fist a flame burst forth like the flame of Meru Mountain.

shloka_text: स तत्राभिहतस्तेनसुग्रीवोवानरर्षभः । मुष्टिंसम्वर्तयामासवज्रकल्पंमहाबलः ।।6.76.89।।
explanation: Then mighty Sugriva, the bull among Vanaras, hit by the fist, clenched his fist adamantly.

shloka_text: अर्चिस्सहस्रविकचरविमण्डलसप्रभम् । स मुष्टिंपातयामासकुम्भस्योरसिवीर्यवान् ।।6.76.90।।
explanation: Sugriva, the champion pressed his first which shone like the Sun encircled with rays on the chest of Kumbha.

shloka_text: स तुतेनप्रहारेणविह्वलोभृशताडितः । निपपाततदाकुम्भोगतार्चिरिवपावकः ।।6.76.91।।
explanation: By the blow of Sugriva, that Kumbha was pained severely and overcome by fear he fell like fire which has lost its glow.

shloka_text: मुष्टिनाभिहतस्तेननिपपाताशुराक्षसः । लोहिताङ्गइवाकाशाददीप्तरमशिर्यदृच्छया ।।6.76.92।।
explanation: Struck by the fist of Sugriva, the Rakshasa fell just as the glowing planet endowed with brightness accidentally fell from the sky.

shloka_text: कुम्भस्यपततोरूपंभग्नस्योरसिमुष्टीना । बभौरुद्राभिपन्नस्ययथारूपंगवांपतेः ।।6.76.93।।
explanation: Struck in the chest by Sugriva's fist, Kumbha fell down and shone like the Sun god over powered by Rudra।।

shloka_text: निकुम्भोभ्रातरंदृष्टवासुग्रीवेणनिपातितम् । प्रदहन्निवकोपेनवानरेन्द्रमवैक्षत ।।6.77.1।।
explanation: Seeing his brother struck down by Sugriva, Nikumbha gazed at him as if to burn him in wrath.

shloka_text: ततस्स्रग्दामसन्नद्धंदत्तपञ्चाङ्गुलंशुभम् । आददेपरिघंवीरोमहेन्द्रशिखरोपमम् ।।6.77.2।।
explanation: Then the hero Nikumbha, girded with flowers measuring five digits in breadth, took an auspicious club like the peak of Mahendra mountain.

shloka_text: हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तंवज्रविद्रुमभूषितम् । यमदण्डोपमंभीमंरक्षसांभयनाशनम् ।।6.77.3।।
explanation: It was decked with a gold band, encrusted with diamonds and corals, in the form of Yama's rod, a fierce one which dispelled fear.

shloka_text: तमाविध्यमहातेजाश्शक्रध्वजसमंतदा । निननादविवृत्तास्योनिकुम्भोभीमविक्रमः ।।6.77.4।।
explanation: The club was highly splendorous and of terrific strength with the banner of Indra and Nikumbha took that club roared opening his mouth wide and pierced it with force.

shloka_text: उरोगतेननिष्केणभुजस्थैरङ्गदैरपि । कुण्डलाभ्यां च चित्राभ्यांमालया च विचित्रया ।।6.77.5।। निकुम्भोभूषणैर्भातितेनस्मपरिघेण च । यथेन्द्रधनुषामेघस्सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान् ।।6.77.6।।
explanation: Nikumbha was shining with ornaments on his chest, golden armlets on arms, wonderful earrings and wonderful garland s holding clubs in hand, with bow like Indra's and roaring like lightning and thunder in the clouds.

shloka_text: उरोगतेननिष्केणभुजस्थैरङ्गदैरपि । कुण्डलाभ्यां च चित्राभ्यांमालया च विचित्रया ।।6.77.5।। निकुम्भोभूषणैर्भातितेनस्मपरिघेण च । यथेन्द्रधनुषामेघस्सविद्युत्स्तनयित्नुमान् ।।6.77.6।।
explanation: Nikumbha was shining with ornaments on his chest, golden armlets on arms, wonderful earrings and wonderful garland s holding clubs in hand, with bow like Indra's and roaring like lightning and thunder in the clouds.

shloka_text: परिघाग्रेणपुष्पोटवातग्रथनिर्महात्मनः । प्रजज्वालसघोषश्चविधूमइवपावकः ।।6.77.7।।
explanation: By Nikumbha whirling around the club and the conjunction of the seven winds coming in contact with the club in his hand crashed in space and glowed like a smokeless fire burst forth.

shloka_text: नगर्याविटपावत्यागन्धर्वभवनोत्तमैः । सतारग्रहनक्षत्रंसचन्द्रंसमहाग्रहम् ।।6.77.8।। निकुम्भपरिघाघूर्णंभ्रमतीवनभस्थ्सलम् ।
explanation: The heaven with the city of Vitapavati, including the excellent abodes of Gandharvas, the hosts of stars and mansions, the lunar abodes along with other planet abodes revolved round as though it was caused by the spinning of Nikumbha's club.

shloka_text: दुरासदश्चसञ्जज्ञेपरिघाभरणप्रभः ।।6.77.9।। कपीनांसनिकुम्भाग्निर्युगान्ताग्निरिवोत्थितः ।
explanation: The glow of the club, the ornaments, and the fire of Nikumbha that burst forth was like the fire at the time of dissolution of the universe. It was formidable for the Vanaras to reflect on.

shloka_text: राक्षसावानराश्चापि न शेकुस्स्पन्दितुंभयात् ।।6.77.10।। हनूमांस्तुविवृत्योरस्तस्थौतस्याग्रतोबली ।
explanation: The Rakshasas and even Vanaras were not able to move out of fear. Only mighty Hanuman stood there showing his chest.

shloka_text: परिघोपमबाहुस्तुपरिघंभास्करप्रभम् ।।6.77.11।। बलीबलवतस्तस्यपातयामासवक्षसि ।
explanation: The Rakshasa, whose arms were like iron bars and shining like the Sun brought it down on the breast of mighty Hanuman.

shloka_text: स्थिरेतस्योरसिव्यूढेपरिघश्शतधाकृतः ।।6.77.12।। विकीर्यमाणस्सहसाउल्काशतमिवाम्बरे ।
explanation: As soon as the iron club touched the broad chest (of Hanuman), it split into a hundred splinters, in the sky and crumbled.

shloka_text: स तुतेनप्रहारेणविचचालमहाकपिः ।।6.77.13।। परिघेणसमाधूतोयथाभूमिचलेऽचलः ।
explanation: The great Vanara did not move and remained steady like a mountain in an earthquake with the iron club touching him.

shloka_text: तथाभिहतस्तेनहनुमान् प्लवगोत्तमः ।।6.77.14।। मुष्टिंसम्वर्तयामासबलेनातिमहाबलः ।
explanation: Struck by the Rakshasa, Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys of extraordinary strength clenched his fist violently.

shloka_text: तमुद्यम्यमहातेजानिकुम्भोरसिवीर्यवान् ।।6.77.15।। अभिचिक्षेपवेगेनवेगवान् वायुविक्रमः ।
explanation: Highly energetic champion endowed with speed, close to wind god in valour raising his fist instantly crushed Nikumbha on the chest.

shloka_text: ततःपुस्फोटचर्मास्यप्रसुस्राव च शोणितम् ।।6.77.16।। मुष्टिनातेनसञ्जज्ञेमेघेविद्युदिवोत्थिता ।
explanation: Then Nikumbha's skin split, and blood started flowing, which appeared as though lightning had risen in the cloud.

shloka_text: सःतुतेनप्रहारेणनिकुम्भोविचचाल ह ।।6.77.17।। स्वस्थश्चापिनिजग्राहहनूमन्तंमहाबलम् ।
explanation: By that blow, Nikumbha was not moved. Recovering from that he caught hold of Hanuman of extraordinary strength.

shloka_text: चुक्रुशुस्तदासङ्ख्येभीमंलङ्कानिवासिनः ।।6.77.18।। निकुम्भेनोद्यतंदृष्टवाहनूमन्तंमहाबलम् ।
explanation: Then seeing Hanuman endowed with might, lifted by Nikumbha in the battlefield the residents of Lanka roared terribly.

shloka_text: तदाह्रियमाणोऽपिकुम्भकर्णात्मजेन ह ।।6.77.19।। आजघानानिलसुतोवज्रकल्पेनमुष्टिना ।
explanation: Even while being carried by Rakshasa also, the son of the wind god hit Kumbhakarna's son with his hard adamant fist.

shloka_text: आत्मानंमोक्षयित्वाथक्षितावभ्यवपद्यत ।।6.77.20।। हनूमानुन्ममाथाशुनिकुम्भंमारुतात्मजः ।
explanation: Hanuman, the son of wind god getting himself released from Nikumbha, springing up standing on the ground tormented Nikumbha.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्यपरमायत्तोनिकुम्भंनिष्पिपेष ह ।।6.77.21।। उत्पत्यचास्यवेगेनपपातोरसिवीर्यवान् ।
explanation: Throwing down Nikumbha with great effort, Hanuman endowed with speed sprang up and fell on his chest.

shloka_text: परिगृह्य च बाहुभ्यांपरिवृत्यशिरोधराम् ।।6.77.22।। उत्पाटयामानशिरोभैरवंनदतोमहत् ।
explanation: Taking hold of the neck with both arms and twisting it round Hanuman broke off the neck of Nikumbha while he was crying terribly.

shloka_text: अथनिनदतिसादितेनिकुम्भेपवनसुतेनरणेबभूवयुद्धम् । दशरथसुतराक्षसेन्द्रसून्वोर्भृशतरमागतरोषयोस्सुभीमम् ।।6.77.23।।
explanation: And thereafter as Nikumbha killed by windgod's son was crying aloud in the battlefield, a violent and fierce war took place between the highly disturbed son of Dasharatha and Rakshasa Makara.

shloka_text: निकुम्भंनिहतंश्रुत्वाकुम्भं च विनिपातितम् । रावणःपरमामर्षीप्रजज्वालानलोयथा ।।6.78.1।।
explanation: On hearing that Nikumbha and Kumbha had been killed, Ravana was very furious and burning in anger.

shloka_text: नैरृतःक्रोधशोकाभ्यांद्वाभ्यांतुपरिमूर्छितः । खरपुत्रंविशालाक्षंमकराक्षमचोदयत् ।।6.78.2।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king was overtaken by both anger and sorrow, bewildered excessively sent for broadeyed Makara, the son of Khara.

shloka_text: गच्छपुत्रऽमयाऽजाज्ञप्तोबलेनाभिसमवनितः । राघवंलक्ष्मणंचैवजहितांश्चवनौकसः ।।6.78.3।।
explanation: "Son! commanded by me, you go accompanied by arm and kill the Vanaras, Raghava and Lakshmana aslo,

shloka_text: रावणस्यवचश्श्रुत्वाशूरमानीखरात्मजः । बाढमित्यब्रवीद्धृष्टोमकराक्षोनिशाचरम् ।।6.78.4।।
explanation: Rejoicing to hear the words of Ravana, proclaiming himself to be a hero, Maka raksha, the son of Khara said 'good'.

shloka_text: सोऽभिवाद्यदशग्रीवंकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् । निर्जगामगृहाच्छुभ्राद्रावणस्याज्ञयाबली ।।6.78.5।।
explanation: Greeting the tenheaded Rakshasa and going round him according to tradition, the mighty warrior went out from the abode early morning by the command of Ravana.

shloka_text: समीपस्थंबलाध्यक्षंखरपुत्रोऽब्रवीदिदम् । रथश्चानीयतांशीघ्रंसैन्यंत्वानीयतांत्वरात् ।।6.78.6।।
explanation: Khara's son spoke to the commanderinchief of the army standing nearby 'Let the chariot be brought quickly and the army proceed'.

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाबलाध्यक्षोनिशाचरः । स्यन्दनं च बलंचैवसमीपंप्रत्यपादयत् ।6.78.7।।
explanation: Upon hearing those words, the commanderinchief of the Rakshasas responded and placed the army near him.

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणंरथंकृत्वाआरुरोहनिशाचरः । सूतंसञ्चोदयामासशीघ्रंमेरथमावह ।।6.78.8।।
explanation: After having gone round the chariot he (Makara) ascended and said to the charioteer, 'let the chariot be driven quickly'.

shloka_text: अथतान्राक्षसान्सर्वान्मकराक्षोऽब्रवीदिदम् । यूयंसर्वेप्रयुध्यध्वंपुरस्तान्ममराक्षसाः ।।6.78.9।।
explanation: Thereafter, Maka raksha spoke to all Rakshasas, 'All of you be ahead of me and fight violently'.

shloka_text: अहंराक्षसराजेनरावणेनमहात्मना । आज्ञप्तःसमरेहन्तुंतावुभौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.78.10।।
explanation: "I will kill both Rama and Lakshmana in the battle, by the order of Ravana, the king of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: अद्यरामंवधिष्यामिलक्ष्मणं च निशाचराः । शाखामृगं च सुग्रीवंवानरांश्चशरोत्तमैः ।।6.78.11।।
explanation: "Now I shall put an end to Rama and Lakshmana, Sugriva and the Vanaras with the best of arrows."

shloka_text: अद्यशूलनिपातैश्चवानराणांमहाचमूम् । प्रदहिष्यामिसम्प्राप्तांशुष्केन्धनमिवानलः ।।6.78.12।।
explanation: "Going there now, I will terminate the great Vanara army with these pikes just as drywood is burnt by fire."

shloka_text: मकराक्षस्यतच्छ्रुत्वावचनंतेनिशाचराः । सर्वेनानायुधोपेताबलवन्तःसमाहिताः ।।6.78.13।।
explanation: On hearing Maka raksha's words all the mighty Rakshasas came with different kinds of weapons.

shloka_text: तेकामरूपिणस्सरेदंष्ट्रिणःपिङ्गलेक्षणा । मातङ्गाइवनर्दन्तोध्वस्तकेशाभयावहाः ।।6.78.14।। परिवार्यमहाकायामहाकायंखरात्मजम् । अभिजघ्नुस्ततोहृष्टाश्चालयन्तोवसुन्धराम् ।।6.78.15।।
explanation: Those who could change their form at will, cruel, with protruding teeth, yellow eyes, dishevelled hair, of frightful appearance, huge like elephants surrounding the son of Khara went joyously forward shaking the earth.

shloka_text: तेकामरूपिणस्सरेदंष्ट्रिणःपिङ्गलेक्षणा । मातङ्गाइवनर्दन्तोध्वस्तकेशाभयावहाः ।।6.78.14।। परिवार्यमहाकायामहाकायंखरात्मजम् । अभिजघ्नुस्ततोहृष्टाश्चालयन्तोवसुन्धराम् ।।6.78.15।।
explanation: Those who could change their form at will, cruel, with protruding teeth, yellow eyes, dishevelled hair, of frightful appearance, huge like elephants surrounding the son of Khara went joyously forward shaking the earth.

shloka_text: शङ्खभेरीसहस्राणामाहतानांसमन्ततः । क्ष्येळितास्फोटितानां च तत्रशब्दोमहानभूत् ।।6.78.16।।
explanation: There was a beating of drums, blowing of thousands of conchs, clapping of arms and great sound was heard.

shloka_text: प्रभ्रष्टोऽथकरात्तस्यप्रतोदस्सारथेस्तदा । पपातसहसादैवाद्ध्वजस्तस्यतुरक्षसः ।।6.78.17।।
explanation: There, the long whip dropped from the charioteer's hand and the Rakshasa's standard had fallen suddenly by divine will.

shloka_text: तस्यतेरथसंयुक्ताहयाविक्रमवर्जिताः । चरणैराकुलैर्गत्वादीनाःसास्रमुखाययुः ।।6.78.18।।
explanation: His horses yoked to the chariot went giving up their valour, faltering feet, desperate and shedding tears.

shloka_text: प्रवातिपवनस्तस्मिन् सपांसुःखरदारुणः । निर्याणेतस्यरौद्रस्यमकराक्षस्यदुर्मतेः ।।6.78.19।।
explanation: At the departure of evil minded and angry Maka raksha, dreadful and violent wind blew carrying with crumbling dust.

shloka_text: तानिदृष्टवानिमित्तानिराक्षसावीर्यवत्तमाः । अचिन्त्यनिर्गतास्सर्वेयत्रतौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.78.20।।
explanation: Seeing those portents incidentally and not taking into account those Rakshasas went where Rama and Lakshmana were.

shloka_text: निर्गतंमकराक्षंतेदृष्टवावानरपुङ्गवाः । आप्लुत्यसहसासर्वेयोद्धुकामाव्यवस्थिताः ।।6.79.1।।
explanation: On seeing Maka raksha all the Vanara chiefs returned, jumped, and stood ready enthusiastically to fight.

shloka_text: ततःप्रवृत्तंसुमहत्तद्युद्धंरोमहर्षणम् । निशाचरैःप्लवङ्गानांदेवानांदानवैरिव ।।6.79.2।।
explanation: Then ensued a battle between Rakshasas and Vanaras whichcaused horripilation, just like the battle between Devas and Danavas.

shloka_text: वृक्षशूलनिपातैश्चशिलापरिघपातनैः । अन्योन्यंमर्दयन्तिस्मतदाकपिनिशाचराः ।।6.79.3।।
explanation: Then monkeys as well as Rakshasas fought hurling trees and pikes and bringing down rocks and clubs physically hurting each other.

shloka_text: शक्तिखडगगदाकुन्तैस्तोमरैश्चनिशाचराः । पट्टसैर्भिण्ढिपालैश्चबाणपातैःसमन्ततः ।।6.79.4।। पाशमुद्गरदण्डैश्चनिखातैश्चापरेस्तथा । कदनंकपिसिंहानांचक्रुस्तेरजनीचराः ।।6.79.5।।
explanation: Those prowlers, then ight rangers discharging javelins, swords, maces, spears, lances, small swords, bhindi Palas, shafts, nooses, mallets and staff and other weapons on the lions among the monkeys, caused destruction.

shloka_text: शक्तिखडगगदाकुन्तैस्तोमरैश्चनिशाचराः । पट्टसैर्भिण्ढिपालैश्चबाणपातैःसमन्ततः ।।6.79.4।। पाशमुद्गरदण्डैश्चनिखातैश्चापरेस्तथा । कदनंकपिसिंहानांचक्रुस्तेरजनीचराः ।।6.79.5।।
explanation: Those prowlers, then ight rangers discharging javelins, swords, maces, spears, lances, small swords, bhindi Palas, shafts, nooses, mallets and staff and other weapons on the lions among the monkeys, caused destruction.

shloka_text: बाणौघैरर्दिताश्चापिखरपुत्रेणवानराः । सम्भ्रान्तमनसस्सर्वेदुद्रुवुर्भयपीडिताः ।।6.79.6।।
explanation: Vanaras perturbed terribly by the volley of arrows of Khara's son were stricken with fear and ran.

shloka_text: तान्दृष्टवाराक्षसास्सर्वेद्रवमाणान्वलीमुखान् । नेदुस्तेसिम्हवद्दृष्टाराक्षसाजितकाशिनः ।।6.79.7।।
explanation: The monkeys saw all the arrogant Rakshasas roaring like lions and running as though triumphed.

shloka_text: विद्रवत्सुतदातेषुवानरेषुसमन्ततः । रामस्तान्वारमायासशरवर्षेणराक्षसान् ।।6.79.8।।
explanation: Thereafter, seeing the Vanaras running all over, Rama stopped the Rakshasas by rain of arrows.

shloka_text: रितान्राक्षसान्दृष्टवामकराक्षोनिशाचरः । क्रोधानलसमाविष्टोवचनंचेदमब्रवीत् ।।6.79.9।।
explanation: Seeing the intercepted Rakshasas, the night ranger Maka raksha was overtaken by fire of anger spoke these words.

shloka_text: तिष्ठराम मयासार्धंद्वन्द्वयुद्धंददामिते । त्याजयिष्यामितेप्राणान् धनुर्मुक्सैशशितैश्शरैः ।।6.79.10।।
explanation: "Rama Stop. Duel will take place with me. I will give you sharpened arrows from my bow and relieve you of your life."

shloka_text: यत्तदादण्डकारण्येपितरंहतवान्मम । तदग्रतःस्वकर्मस्थंदृष्टवारोषोऽभिवर्धते ।।6.79.11।।
explanation: "Then in Dandakaranya my father was killed. Now for the samereason you are in front of me. Seeing you my anger is increasing."

shloka_text: दह्यन्तेधृशमङ्गानिदुरात्मन्ममराघव । यन्मयासि न दृष्टस्त्वंतस्मिन् कालेमहावने ।।6.79.12।।
explanation: "O Evil minded Raghava! at that time, I did not see you in D and aka forest. My limbs are burning in anger."

shloka_text: दिष्ट्यासिदर्शनंराम ममत्वंप्राप्तवानिह । काङ्क्षितोऽसिक्षुधार्तस्यसिंहस्येवेतरोमृगः ।।6.79.13।।
explanation: "Rama! To my good fortune it became possible for me to see you here. Just as a hungry lion waits for an animal, I am waiting for you."

shloka_text: अद्यमद्बाणवेगेनप्रेतराडिवषयंगतः । येत्वयानिहताःशूराःसहतैश्चसमेष्यसि ।।6.79.14।।
explanation: "Now by the speed of my arrow I will send you totherealm of Yama and there you will be along with the demons killed by you."

shloka_text: बहुनात्रकिमुक्तेनशृणुराम वचोमम । पश्यन्तुसकलालोकास्त्वा, मांचैवरणाजिरे ।।6.79.15।।
explanation: "Rama, why talk so much? Listen to my words. Let people in all worldssee you and me in the battlefield."

shloka_text: अस्त्रैर्वागदयावापिबाहुभ्यांवामहाहवे । अभ्यस्तंयेनवाराम तेनैवयुधिवर्तताम् ।।6.79.16।।
explanation: "By weapons, or by mace or else with hand s or any other weapon or with your military practice, you fight, he said to Rama."

shloka_text: मकराक्ष्वचश्श्रुत्वारामोदशरथात्मजः । अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्वाक्यमुत्तरोत्तरवादिनम् ।।6.79.17।।
explanation: Laughing at the words of Maka raksha who was speaking again and again Rama said.

shloka_text: कत्थसेकिंवृथारक्षो बहून्यसदृशानिते । न रणेशक्यतेजेतुंविनायुद्धेनवाग्भलात् ।।6.79.18।।
explanation: "Rakshasa! Why so much of wasteful talk about What you can't accomplish? Victory is not possible on the battlefield with your force of speech"

shloka_text: चतुर्दशसहस्राणिरक्षसांत्वत्पिता च यः । त्रिशिरादूषणश्चापिदण्डकेनिहतामया ।।6.79.19।।
explanation: "In Dandaka, fourteen thousand Rakshasas, your father, Trisira, and also Dooshana were killed by me alone."

shloka_text: स्वाशितास्तवमांसेनगृध्रगोमायुवायसाः । भविष्यन्त्यद्यवैपाप तीक्ष्णतुण्डनखाङ्कुराः ।।6.79.20।।
explanation: "O Sinner! Today vultures, jackals and crows with sharp beaks and goads like claws will also be satiated with your flesh."

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तुमकराक्षोमहाबलः । बाणौघानमुचत्तस्मैराघवायरणाजिरे ।।6.79.21।।
explanation: Spoken in that manner by Raghava in the battlefield, Maka raksha, endowed with extraordinary strength, released a volley of arrows on Rama.

shloka_text: तान्शरान् शरवर्षेणरामश्चिच्छेदनैकधा । निपेतुर्भुवितेछिन्नारुक्मपुङ्खास्सहस्रशः ।।6.79.22।।
explanation: Rama rained volley of arrows on the Rakshasa and shattered those golden feathered arrows which fell on the ground into thousands of pieces.

shloka_text: तद्युद्धमभवत्तत्रसमेत्यान्योन्यमोजसा । खरराक्षसपुत्रस्यसूनोर्धशरथस्य च ।।6.79.23।।
explanation: On meeting one another between Khara's son and Dasharatha's son a fierce comb at happened.

shloka_text: जीमूतयोरिवाकाशेशब्दोज्यातलयोस्तदा । धनुर्मुक्तःस्वनोत्कृष्टश्श्रूयते च रणाजिरे ।।6.79.24।।
explanation: Then the sound released by the friction of the bowstring and the hand (of the two heroes) filled the sky like thunder of clouds.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वाःकिन्नराश्चमहोरगाः । अन्तरिक्षगतास्सर्वेद्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम् ।।6.79.25।।
explanation: Devas, Danavas, Ghand arvas, Kinnaras and huge serpents all of them stood in space to look at the wonderful evil deed.

shloka_text: विद्धमन्योन्यगात्रेषुद्विगुणंवर्धतेपरम् । कृतप्रतिकृतान्योन्यंकुरुतांतौरणाजिरे ।।6.79.26।।
explanation: Even though they were piercing one another with limbs, their strength remained doubled in the battlefield. Each of them was countering the other and inflicting and hitting each other.

shloka_text: राममुक्तांस्तुबाणौघान् राक्षसस्त्वच्छिनद्रणे । रक्षोमुक्तांस्तुरामोवैनैकथाप्राच्छिनच्छरैः ।।6.79.27।।
explanation: In the comb at Rakshasa split the arrows released by Rama and Rakshasa shattered the arrows released by Rama.

shloka_text: बाणौघैर्विततास्सर्वादिशश्चप्रदिशस्तथा । सञ्छन्नावसुधाचैवसमन्तान्नप्रकाशते ।।6.79.28।।
explanation: All quarters were covered by the arrows in that manner all over and even the intermediate point, the earth could not be seen.

shloka_text: तःक्रुद्धोमहाबाहुर्धनुच्शिच्छेदरक्षसः । अष्टाभिरथनाराचैस्सूतंविव्याधराघवः ।।6.79.29।।
explanation: Then broad shouldered Raghava was enraged and split the bow with eight steel arrows and the charioteer also.

shloka_text: भित्त्वारथंशरैरामोहत्वाआश्वानपातयत् । विरथोवसुधास्थश्चमकराक्षोनिशाचरः ।।6.79.30।।
explanation: Rama broke the chariot, killed the horses, and laid down the night ranger Maka raksha. Deprived of the chariot he stood on the ground.

shloka_text: तत्तिष्ठद्वसुधांरक्षश्शूलंजग्राहपाणिना । त्रासनंसर्वभूतानांयुगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम् ।।6.79.31।।
explanation: Standing on the ground that Rakshasa who created fear among all beings shone like fire at the time of dissolution of the universe, seized his pike in hand.

shloka_text: दुरवापम् महच्छूलंरुद्रदत्तंभयङ्करम् । जाज्वल्यमानमाकाशेसंहारास्त्रमिवापरम् ।।6.79.32।। यंदृष्टवादेवताःसर्वाभयार्ताविद्रुतादिशः ।
explanation: Seeing that pike, which was glowing like flame, by which the quarters were glowing brightly in the sky like the flame, which had been given by Rudra, which caused fear like another weapon of destruction, all gods fled in panic in all directions.

shloka_text: विभ्राम्यतुमहच्छूलंप्रज्वलन्तन्निशाचरः ।।6.79.33।। स क्रोधाप्राहिणोत्तस्मैराघवायमहात्मने ।
explanation: The night ranger whirling round and round the glowing pike furiously hurled at Raghava in that conflict.

shloka_text: तमापतन्तंज्वलितंखरपुत्रकराच्च्युतम् ।।6.79.34।। बाणैत्रिभिराकाशेशूलंचिच्छेदराघवः ।
explanation: Raghava split with his three arrows the burning pike released from the hand of Khara's son while it was still flying in the sky.

shloka_text: सच्छन्नोनैकथाशूलोदिव्यहाटकमण्डितः ।।6.79.35।। व्यशीर्यतमहोल्केवरामबाणार्दितोभुवि ।
explanation: That pike, which was decorated with gold, broke into pieces, and fell down like fire sticks by the many supreme arrows of Rama.

shloka_text: च्छूलंनिहतंदृष्टवारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.79.36।। साधुसावधितिभूतानिव्याहरन्तिनभोगताः ।
explanation: Seeing the unwearied action of Raghava in destroying the pike, the beings in the sky praised him saying," well done, well done."

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवानिहतंशूलंमकराक्षोनिशाचरः ।।6.79.37।। मुष्टिमुद्यम्यकाकुत्स्थंतिष्ठतिष्ठेतिचाब्रवीत् ।
explanation: The night ranger Makaraksha seeing his pike destroyed lifting up his fist said this to Kakuthsa, "Wait, wait."

shloka_text: सःतंदृष्टवाऽपतन्तंवैप्रहस्यरघुनन्दनः ।।6.79.38।। पावकास्त्रंततोरामस्सन्दधेतुशरासने ।
explanation: Then Rama the beloved of Raghus, laughing at Maka raksha, fixed missile presided by fire god.

shloka_text: तेनास्त्रणहतंरक्षःकाकुत्थ्सेनतदारणे ।।6.79.39।। सञ्चिन्नहृदयंतत्रपपात च ममार च ।
explanation: Then struck in the battlefield by that missile of Kakuthsa, the Rakshasa fell down with his heart split open and died.

shloka_text: दृष्टवातेराक्षसास्सर्वेमकराक्षस्यपातनम् ।।6.79.40।। लङ्कामेवप्रधावन्तरामबाणभयार्दिताः ।
explanation: Seeing Maka raksha fall, those Rakshasas became scared of Rama's arrow and ran straight to Lanka.

shloka_text: मकराक्षंहतंश्रुत्वारावणस्समितिञ्जयः । रोषेणमहताविष्टोदन्ताङ्कटकटाय्य च ।।6.80.1।। कोपितश्चतदातत्रकिंकार्यमितिचिन्तयन् । आदिदेशाथसङ्क्रुद्धोरणायेजितंसुतम् ।।6.80.2।।
explanation: Ravana, who was always victorious in warhearing that Maka raksha had been killed, became highly enraged and grinding his teeth in anger was engrossed in thinking. He commanded his son Indrajith to go to battle.

shloka_text: मकराक्षंहतंश्रुत्वारावणस्समितिञ्जयः । रोषेणमहताविष्टोदन्ताङ्कटकटाय्य च ।।6.80.1।। कोपितश्चतदातत्रकिंकार्यमितिचिन्तयन् । आदिदेशाथसङ्क्रुद्धोरणायेजितंसुतम् ।।6.80.2।।
explanation: Ravana, who was always victorious in warhearing that Maka raksha had been killed, became highly enraged and grinding his teeth in anger was engrossed in thinking. He commanded his son Indrajith to go to battle.

shloka_text: जहिवीर महावीर्यौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । अदृश्योदृश्यमानोवासर्वथात्वंबलाधिकः ।।6.80.3।।
explanation: "Oh, Valiant son! You destroy the two heroic brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, by being visible or invisible as you are always superior to them."

shloka_text: त्वमप्रतिमकर्माणमिन्द्रंजयसिसंयुगे । किंपुनर्मानुषौदृष्टवा न वधिष्यसिसंयुगे ।।6.80.4।।
explanation: "You have won the battle with Indra of incomparable deeds. Why not kill men, onseeing them in combat?"

shloka_text: तथोक्तोराक्षसेन्द्रेणप्रतिगृह्यपितुर्वचः । यज्ञभूमौ स विधिवत् पावकंजुहवेन्द्रजित् ।।6.80.5।।
explanation: Hearing the words spoken by the Lord of Rakshasas, Indrajith respecting the command poured oblations in the fireas per tradition before proceeding.

shloka_text: जुह्वतश्चापितत्राग्निंरक्तोष्णीषधरास्त्रिरियः । आजग्मुस्तत्रसम्भ्रान्ताराक्षस्योयत्ररावणिः ।।6.80.6।।
explanation: Thereafter, as he went to the place of fire sacrifice, Rakshasa women brought red coloured head dresses to wear (for the priests).

shloka_text: शस्त्राणिशरपत्राणिसमिधोऽथविभीतकाः । लोहितानि च वासांहिस्रुवंकार्ष्णायसंतथा ।।6.80.7।।
explanation: Then, in that fire sacrifice, weapons as grass, wooden pieces as sticks for offering into fire, redcoloured clothes for the priests to wear, and so also iron containers as ladles to offer in fire were used.

shloka_text: सर्वतोऽग्निंसमास्तीर्यशरपत्रैस्सतोमरैः । छागस्यसर्वकृष्णस्यगळंजग्राहजीवतः ।।6.80.8।।
explanation: Weapons were spread on all sides of the fire sacrifice like grass. A darkcoloured live goat's neck was consigned for offering into fire.

shloka_text: सकृदेवसमिद्धस्यविधूमस्यमहार्चिषः । बभूवुस्तानिलिङ्गानिविजयंदर्शयन्ति च ।।6.80.9।।
explanation: By that action of fire sacrifice, the mighty flames and the smoke that appeared from the mighty smokeless fire signifying victory appeared.

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तहाटकसन्निभः । हविस्तत्प्रतिजग्राहपावकस्स्वयमुत्थितः ।।6.80.10।।
explanation: The flames of fire going round the fire by itself which closely resembled refined gold, received the offerings into fire.

shloka_text: हुत्वाग्निंतर्पयित्वाथदेवदानवराक्षसान् । आरुरोहरथश्रेष्ठमन्तर्थानगतंशुभम् ।।6.80.11।।
explanation: Having offered fire that way, and gratified Devas, Danavas and Rakshasas, he (Indrajith) ascended the best of chariots and disappeared.

shloka_text: स वाजिभिश्चतुर्भिस्तुबाणैश्चनिशितैर्युतः । आरोपितमहाचापश्शुशुभेस्यन्दनोत्तमः ।।6.80.12।।
explanation: Drawn by horses, fitted with sharp mighty bows, the chariot was shining exquisitely and looked charming.

shloka_text: जाज्वल्यमानोवपुषातपनीयपरिच्छदः । मृगैश्चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रैश्च स रथस्समलङ्कृतः ।।6.80.13।।
explanation: The chariot was glittering incarnated with gold covered with images offull moon, crescent moon inscriptions and decorated with images of antelopes.

shloka_text: जाम्बूनदमहाकम्बुर्दीप्तपावकसन्निभः । बभूवेन्द्रजितःकेतुर्वैदूर्यसमलङ्कृतः ।।6.80.14।।
explanation: Like flaming fire in appearance, the chariot was provided with rings of gold, the standard of the chariot was adorned with gems of Vydurya.

shloka_text: तेनचादित्यकल्पेनब्रह्मास्त्रण च पालितः । स बभूवदुराधर्षोरावणिस्सुमहाबलः ।।6.80.15।।
explanation: Protected by the weapon of Brahma, effulgent as the orbit of the Sun, the son of Ravana was endowed with mighty prowess and was difficult to gain over.

shloka_text: सोऽभिनिर्यायनगरादिन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । हत्वाग्निंराक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.80.16।।
explanation: Indrajith who had acquired the power of being victorious in the wars departed, after uttering ritualistic verses which are known to Rakshasas only and making an offering into fire disappeared and bragged as follows.

shloka_text: अद्यहत्वारणेयौतौमिथ्याप्रव्रजितौवने । जयंपित्रेप्रदास्यामिरावणायरणार्जितम् ।।6.80.17।।
explanation: "Having put an end to war, and the two princes who are in exile in the forest in vain, I will present the victory earned to my father now."

shloka_text: अद्यनिर्वानरमुर्वींहत्वारामंसलक्ष्मणम् । करिष्येपरमांप्रीतिमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत ।।6.80.18।।
explanation: 'Making the earth devoid of monkeys, killing Rama and Lakshmana, I will provide supreme joy to my father now', saying so he became invisible.

shloka_text: आपपातथसङ्कृद्धोदशग्रीवेणचोदितः । तीक्षणकार्मुकनाराचैस्तीक्षणस्त्विन्द्ररिपूरणे ।।6.80.19।।
explanation: Directed by the ten headed Ravana, enemy of Indra, equipped with sharp bows Indrajith rushed furiously.

shloka_text: स ददर्शमहावीर्यौनागौत्रिशिरसानिव । सृजन्ताविषुजालानिवीरौवानरमध्यगौ ।।6.80.20।।
explanation: That great hero saw Rama and Lakshmana like three serpents in the midst of Vanaras raining network of arrows.

shloka_text: इमौतावितिसञ्चिन्त्यसज्जंकृत्वा च कार्मुकम् । सन्ततानेषुधाराभिःपर्जन्यइववृष्टिमान् ।।6.80.21।।
explanation: Recognising the two princes, stringing his bow, and fastening, affixing he showered a continuous flow of arrows like rain from rain clouds and covered them.

shloka_text: तुवैहायसंप्राप्यसरथोरामलक्ष्मणौ । आचक्षुर्विषयेतिष्ठवनिव्याधनिशितैश्शरैः ।।6.80.22।।
explanation: Riding in the aerial car, Indrajith remaining out of sight released pointed arrows from the sky and tormented Rama and Lakshmana standing in the battlefield.

shloka_text: तौतस्यशरवेगेनपरीतौरामलक्ष्मणौ । धनुषीसशरेकृत्वादिव्यमस्त्रंप्रचक्रतुः ।।6.80.23।।
explanation: Covered by the speed of the arrows released on them, both Rama and Lakshmana wielding their bows and arrows discharged wonderful arrows and exhibited their power.

shloka_text: प्रच्छादयन्तौगगनंशरजालैर्महाबलौ । तमस्त्रःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्नैवपस्पृशतुश्शरैः ।।6.80.24।।
explanation: Though the mighty Rama and Lakshmana were covering the sky with their arrows resembling the sun they could not touch Indrajith.

shloka_text: स हिधूमान्धकारं च चक्रेप्रच्चादयन्नभः । दिशश्चान्तर्दधेश्रीमान्नीहारतमसावृताः ।।6.80.25।।
explanation: The glorious Indrajith obscured the sky by making it dark through smoke and fog and made the surrounding directions invisible.

shloka_text: नैवज्यातलनिर्घोषा न च नेमिखुरस्वनः । शुश्रुवेचरतस्तस्य न च रूपंप्रकाशते ।।6.80.26।।
explanation: While Indrajith was moving, neither the sounds produced by palms or of the wheels or the hoof s were heard and the form was also not visible.,

shloka_text: घनान्धकारेतिमिरेशरावर्षमिवाद्भुतम् । स ववर्षमहाबाहुर्नाराचशरवृष्टिभिः ।।6.80.27।।
explanation: The mighty armed Indrajith showered rocks and hails of steel arrows in that pitch darkness like the darkness of clouds.

shloka_text: स रामंसूर्यसङ्काशैश्शरैर्धत्तवरोर्भृशम् । विव्याधसमरेक्रुद्धःसर्वगात्रेषुरावणिः ।।6.80.28।।
explanation: In that conflict, the enraged son of Ravana, pierced all over Rama's limbs, with arrows bestowed to him, which were as effulgent as the Sun.

shloka_text: तौहन्यमानौनाराचैर्धाराभिरिवपर्वतौ । हेमपुङ्खान्नरव्याघ्रौतिग्मान्मुमुचतुःशरान् ।।6.80.29।।
explanation: The tigers among humans, Rama, and Lakshmana, like two mountains hit by steel arrows, released sharp pointedgold shafted steel arrows and tormented (Indrajith).

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षेसमासाद्यरावणिंकङ्कपत्रिणः । निकृत्यपतगाभूमौसेतुस्तेशोणितोक्षिताः ।।6.80.30।।
explanation: The arrows fixed with swords like wings, reaching Ravana's son in the sky pierced him and he fell down soaked in blood.

shloka_text: अतिमात्रंशरौघेणपीड्यमानौनरोत्तमौ । तानिषून्पततोभल्लैरनेकैर्विचकर्ततुः ।।6.80.31।।
explanation: Brightened by the mass of arrows on their body, the best of men, Rama and Lakshmana began to tear the numerous arrows called Bhallas.

shloka_text: यतोहिददृशातेतौशरान् निपतितान्शितान् । ततस्तुतौदाशरथीससृजातेऽस्त्रमुत्तमम् ।।6.80.32।।
explanation: Both the sons of Dasharatha, directed their best weapons in the direction from where arrows were falling on two of them.

shloka_text: रावणिस्तुदिशस्सर्वारथेनातिरथोऽपतत् । विव्याधतौदाशरथीलघ्वस्त्रनिशितैःशरैः ।।6.80.33।।
explanation: The son of Ravana who was a superior chariot warrior and swift in discharging arrows coursed through all directions and pierced arrows at Rama and Lakshmana from the aerial car.

shloka_text: तेनातिविद्धौतौवीरौरुक्मपुङ्खैःसुसम्हतैः । बभूवतुर्धाशरथीपुष्पितामिवकिंशुकौ ।।6.80.34।।
explanation: Both the sons of Dasharatha looked like fully blossomed Kimsuka trees (blood flowing from the body) pierced by wellmade gold shafted arrows.

shloka_text: नास्यवेगगतिंकचशिन्न च रूपंधनुश्शरान् । न चान्यद्विदितंकिञ्चित्सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसम्प्लवे ।।6.80.35।।
explanation: When the clouds are cast thickly, except the position of the Sun, nothing is visible. So also, with a swift movement of Indrajith, neither his form nor his bow and arrows were visible.

shloka_text: तेनविद्धाश्चहरयोनिहताश्चगतासवः । बभूवुःशतशस्तत्रपतिताधरणीतले ।।6.80.36।।
explanation: Then, monkeys struck and killed, lifelessin hundreds fell on the ground.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्तुततस्सुङ्क्रृद्धोभ्रातरंवाक्यमब्रवीत् । ब्राह्ममस्त्रंप्रयोक्ष्यामिवधार्थंसर्वरक्षसाम् ।।6.80.37।।
explanation: Then Lakshmana also, enraged, spoke to his brother, saying," I will kill all the Rakshasas using the weapon of Brahma."

shloka_text: तमुवाचततोरामोलक्ष्मणंशुभलक्षणम् । नैकस्यहेतोरक्षांसिपृथिव्यांहन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.80.38।।
explanation: To Lakshmana, gifted with auspicious signs, Rama said" for the sake of killing one Rakshasa, you are not to kill all the Rakshasas on the earth."

shloka_text: अयुध्यमानंप्रच्छन्नंप्राञ्जलिंशरणागतम् । पलायमानंमत्तंवा न हन्तुंत्वमिहार्हसि ।।6.80.39।।
explanation: "You should not kill anyone who is not waging war, not fighting and hidden, one with folded palms surrendered, one who runs away from war and not alert in war"

shloka_text: अस्यैवतुवधेयत्नंकरिष्यावोमहाभुज । आदेक्ष्यावोमहावेगावस्त्रानाशीविषोपमान् ।।6.80.40।।
explanation: "O mighty armed Lakshmana! I will make an effort to kill Indrajith by commanding weapons like venomous serpents endowed with high speed."

shloka_text: तमेनंमायिनंक्षुद्रमन्तर्हितरथंबलात् । राक्षसंनिहनिष्यन्तिदृष्टवावानरयूथपाः ।।6.80.41।।
explanation: " A conjurer, mean, and invisible Indrajith with the chariot, if seen, in any way the Vanara troops will forcibly kill him with their strength."

shloka_text: यद्येषभूमिंविशतेदिवंवारसातलंवापिनभस्स्थलंवा । एवंनिगूढोऽममास्त्रदग्धःपतिष्यतेभूमितलेगतासुः ।।6.80.42।।
explanation: "If he enters into earth, heaven or the underground world or the subterranean world or remains hidden, my weapon will consume him, and he will fall on earth."

shloka_text: विज्ञायतुमनस्तस्यराघवस्यमहात्मनः । स निवृत्याहवात्तस्मात् प्रविवेशपुरींततः ।।6.81.1।।
explanation: Knowing the highsouled Raghava's mind, Indrajith departed from there and entered the city.

shloka_text: सोऽनुस्मृत्यवधंतेषांराक्षसानांतरस्विनाम् । क्रोधताम्रेक्षणश्शूरोनिर्जगामाहाद्युति: ।।6.81.2।।
explanation: Recollecting those Rakshasas killed, the heroic, mighty and courageous Indrajith's eyes were red in anger.

shloka_text: स पश्चिमेवद्वारेणनिर्ययौराक्षसैर्वृतः । इन्द्रजित्सुमहावीर्यःपौलस्त्योदेवकण्टकः ।।6.81.3।।
explanation: Paulastya (one of the nine mind born sons of Brahma, a scion of sage Paulastya), stupendous hero, a tormentor of Devatas, Indrajith, surrounded by Rakshasas came out through the western gate.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुततोदृष्टवाभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । रणायाभ्युद्यतौवीरौमायांप्रादुष्करोत्तदा ।।6.81.4।।
explanation: Indrajith, also witnessing the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana prepared for war, exhibited his trickery.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्तुरथेस्थाप्यसीतांमायामयींतदा । बलेनमहतावृत्यतस्यावधमरोचयत् ।।6.81.5।।
explanation: Indrajith, also through a trick, wanted to make illusory Sita and place her in the chariot surrounded by Rakshasas and thought of killing her.

shloka_text: मोहनार्थंतुसर्वेषांबुद्धिंकृत्वासुदुर्मतिः । हन्तुंसीतांव्यवसितोवानराभिमुखोययौ ।।6.81.6।।
explanation: Evil minded Indrajith, made up his mind to hoodwink every one who decided to kill Sita and went towards the Vanaras.

shloka_text: तम्दृष्टवात्वभिनिर्यान्तंसर्वेतेकाननौकसः । उत्पेतुरभिसङ्क्रुद्धाश्शिलाहस्तायुयुत्सवः ।।6.81.7।।
explanation: All the forest animals perceiving Indrajithadvancing became angry and with rocks in hand faced him with enthusiasm.

shloka_text: हनूमान् पुरतस्तेषांजगामकपिकुञ्जरः । प्रगृह्यसुमहच्छृङ्गंपर्वतस्यदुरासदम् ।।6.81.8।।
explanation: Hanuman, the elephant among monkeys, taking hold of a huge mountain peak that was difficult to reach marched forward and went.

shloka_text: स ददर्शहतानन्दांसीतामिन्द्रजितोरथे । एकवेणीधरांदीनामुपवासकृशाननाम् ।।6.81.9।। परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजांराघवप्रियाम् । रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैस्सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम् ।।6.81.10।।
explanation: Hanuman beheld in the chariot of Indrajith, cheerless Sita with one braid, with no desire to live, emaciated by fasting, wearing a single cloth, body not anointed, covered with dust and dirt all over the body, who was dear to Raghava.

shloka_text: स ददर्शहतानन्दांसीतामिन्द्रजितोरथे । एकवेणीधरांदीनामुपवासकृशाननाम् ।।6.81.9।। परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजांराघवप्रियाम् । रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैस्सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम् ।।6.81.10।।
explanation: Hanuman beheld in the chariot of Indrajith, cheerless Sita with one braid, with no desire to live, emaciated by fasting, wearing a single cloth, body not anointed, covered with dust and dirt all over the body, who was dear to Raghava.

shloka_text: तांनिरीक्ष्यमुहूर्तंतुमैथिलीत्यध्यवस्यतु । बभूवाचिरदृष्टाहितेनसाजनकात्मजा ।।6.81.11।।
explanation: He looked at her for a moment and recognised her as Janaka's daughter since he had seen her not long before.

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तांतुशोकार्तांनिरानन्दांतपस्विनीम् । दृष्टवारथोस्थितांदृष्ट्वाराक्षसेन्द्रसुतश्रिताम् ।।6.81.12।। कंसमर्थितमस्येतिचिन्तयन्समहाकपिः । सहतैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावतरावणिम् ।।6.81.13।।
explanation: Great Vanara, Hanuman, gazing at miserable, joyless, ascetic woman seated in the chariot, worried, why she is in the chariot. He spoke to the best of Vanara leaders and rushed towards the son of Ravana with them.

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तांतुशोकार्तांनिरानन्दांतपस्विनीम् । दृष्टवारथोस्थितांदृष्ट्वाराक्षसेन्द्रसुतश्रिताम् ।।6.81.12।। कंसमर्थितमस्येतिचिन्तयन्समहाकपिः । सहतैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावतरावणिम् ।।6.81.13।।
explanation: Great Vanara, Hanuman, gazing at miserable, joyless, ascetic woman seated in the chariot, worried, why she is in the chariot. He spoke to the best of Vanara leaders and rushed towards the son of Ravana with them.

shloka_text: तद्वानरबलंदृष्टवारावणिःक्रोधमूर्छितः । कृत्वाविकोशंनिस्त्रिंशंमूर्ध्निसीतामकर्षयत् ।।6.81.14।।
explanation: Indrajith saw the Vanara army coming towards him, deluded with anger, unsheathed the sword and touched Sita's forehead.

shloka_text: तांस्त्रियंपश्यतांतेषांताडयामासरावणि: । क्रोशन्तींरामरामेतिमाययायोजितांरथे ।।6.81.15।।
explanation: As they were looking at Sita on the chariot trickishly constructed, and she was crying saying, 'O Rama, O Rama', he stood and hit her.

shloka_text: गृहीतमूर्धजांदृष्टवाहनुमान् दैन्यमागतः । शोकजंवारिनेत्राभ्यामुत्सृजन्मारुतात्मजः ।।6.81.16।।
explanation: Seeing Indrajith holding Sita's head, Maruti's son, was immersed in grief, and shed tears of sorrow from his eyes.

shloka_text: तांदृष्टवाचारुसर्वाङ्गींरामस्यमहिषींप्रियाम् । अब्रवीत्पुरुषंवाक्यंक्रोधाद्रक्षोधिपात्मजम् ।।6.81.17।।
explanation: Looking at Rama's dear wife, of lovely limbs, Hanuman rebuked Indrajith in anger and spoke harsh words.

shloka_text: दुरात्मन्नात्मनाशायकेशपक्षेपरामृशः । ब्रह्मर्षीणांकुलेजातोराक्षसींयोनिमाश्रितः ।।6.81.18।।
explanation: "O evil minded Indrajith! You are born as Rakshasa in the clan of seers of vedic mantras and sought the womb of Rakshasa woman. It is for your own self destruction you seized her hair.

shloka_text: धिक्त्वांपापसमाचारंयस्यतेमतिरिदृशी । नृशंसानार्य दुर्वृत्त क्षुद्र पापपराक्रम ।।6.81.19।। अनार्यस्येदृशंकर्मघृणातेनास्तिनिर्घृण ।
explanation: "You are ignoble, mean, of sinful prowess, not merciful. You have resolved to take such a sinful action which is not worthy of you. You have no compassion to act in this manner."

shloka_text: च्युतागृहाच्चराज्याच्चरामहस्ताच्चमैथिली ।।6.81.20।। किंतवैषापराद्धाहियदेनांहन्तुमिच्छसि ।
explanation: "This Mythili is sent away from home, from the kingdom, and also distanced from Rama's protection. You are unkind and hitting in this way. What harm has she done?"

shloka_text: सीतांहत्वातु न चिरंजीविष्यसिकथञ्चन ।।6.81.21।। वधार्हकर्मणानेनममहस्तगतोह्यसि ।
explanation: "Indeed, you will not live long after killing Sita. You deserve to be killed for your actions, that is why you have come into my hands."

shloka_text: येच स्त्रीघातिनांलोकालोकवध्यैषुकुसतिताः ।।6.81.22।। इहजीवितमुत्सृज्यप्रेत्यतान्प्रतिपत्स्यसे ।
explanation: "You deserve to be killed by the world here. Giving up your life, you will be thrown out and descend to the world with those who killed women have gone, after your death."

shloka_text: तिब्रुवाणोहनुमान् सायुधैर्हरिभिर्वृतः ।।6.81.23।। अभ्यदावत् ससुङ्कृद्धोराक्षसेन्द्रसुतंप्रति ।
explanation: Hanuman was highly enraged and speaking like got prepared for war and went surrounded by the monkeys towards Indrajith, the son of Rakshasa king.

shloka_text: पतन्तंमहावीर्यंतदनीकंवनौकसाम् ।।6.81.24।। रक्षसांभीमकोपानामनीकंतुन्यवारयत् ।
explanation: Rakshasa army troops of mighty prowess, terribly angry, were advancing towards wood dwellers (Vanara troops) and were intercepted by the Vanara troops.

shloka_text: सःतांबाणसहस्रेणविक्षोभ्यहरिवाहिनीम् ।।6.81.25।। हनूमन्तंहरिश्रेष्ठमिन्द्रजित् प्रत्युवाच ह ।
explanation: Indrajith shattered the army of monkeys with a thousand arrows. Hanuman the foremost Vanara replied to them as follows.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्त्वं च रामश्चयन्निमित्तमिहागताः ।।6.81.26।। तांवधिष्यामिवैदेहीमद्यैवतवपश्यतः ।
explanation: "I will kill your Vaidehi today as you keep seeing her for whose sake Sugriva, you and Rama also came here," said Indrajith.

shloka_text: इमांहत्वाततोरामंलक्ष्मणंत्वां च वानर ।।6.81.27।। सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामितंचानार्यंविभीषणम् ।
explanation: "O Vanara! This day, having killed her, I will kill Rama, Lakshmana, and you, also Sugriva and that ignoble Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: न हन्तव्याःस्त्रियश्चेतियद् ब्रवीषिप्लवङ्गम ।।6.81.28।। पीडाकरममित्राणांयत्स्यात्कर्तव्यमेवतत् ।
explanation: "O Hanuman! You said women should not be killed. But whoever causes trouble to the enemy, action should be taken, said Indrajith."

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वारुदतींसीतांमयामयीं च ताम् ।।6.81.29।। शितधारेणखङ्गेननिजघानेन्द्रजित्स्वयम् ।
explanation: Indrajith having spoken like that killed that crying illusory Sita with a sharpedged sword.

shloka_text: यज्ञोपवीतमार्गेणभिन्नातेनतपस्विनी ।।6.81.30।। सापृथिव्यांपृथुश्रोणीपपातप्रियदर्शना ।
explanation: Split diagonally, the ascetic woman with charming hips and pleasing countenance sank into the ground.

shloka_text: त्तामिन्द्रजित् स्त्रियंहत्वाहनूमन्तमुवाच ह ।।6.81.31।। मयारामस्यपश्येमांकोपेन च । एषाविशस्तावैदेहीनिष्फलोवःपरिश्रमः ।।6.81.32।।
explanation: Indrajith killed that woman and said to Hanuman" see this Vaidehi, Rama's wife, cut up by my sword. Your exertion is useless now."

shloka_text: त्तामिन्द्रजित् स्त्रियंहत्वाहनूमन्तमुवाच ह ।।6.81.31।। मयारामस्यपश्येमांकोपेन च । एषाविशस्तावैदेहीनिष्फलोवःपरिश्रमः ।।6.81.32।।
explanation: Indrajith killed that woman and said to Hanuman" see this Vaidehi, Rama's wife, cut up by my sword. Your exertion is useless now."

shloka_text: ततःखडगेनमहताहत्वातामिन्द्रजित् स्वयम् । हृष्टस्सरथमास्थायननाद च महास्वनम् ।।6.81.33।।
explanation: Indrajith himself with his long sword killed her, then rejoiced, he ascended the chariot and roared in a loud tone.

shloka_text: वानराश्शुश्रुवुश्शब्दमदूरेप्रत्यवस्थिताः । व्यादितास्यस्यनदतस्तद्दुर्गंसंश्रितस्यतु ।।6.81.34।।
explanation: The sound of his roar was heard by the Vanaras waiting for war standing not far from there, which was difficult for Indrajith to access.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुभीमनिर्ह्रादंशक्राशनिसमस्वनम् । वीक्षमाणादिशस्सर्वादुद्रुवुर्वानरर्षभा: ।।6.82.1।।
explanation: The bulls among Vanaras heard the roar which was like thunder and looking at Indrajith fled in all directions.

shloka_text: तानुवाचततःसर्वान्हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः । विषण्णवदनान्दीनांस्त्रस्तान्विद्रवतःपृथक् ।।6.82.2।।
explanation: Thereafter, Maruti's son, Hanuman said to all Vanaras who were looking sad, piteous, feeling singly out of fear, and running away.

shloka_text: कस्माद्विषण्णवदनाविद्रवध्वंप्लवङ्गमाः । त्यक्तयुद्धसमुत्साहाश्शूरत्वंक्वनुवोगतम् ।।6.82.3।।
explanation: "O monkeys! Why have you lost enthusiasm to fight, looking sad and running away? Where has your valour gone?"

shloka_text: पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजध्वंमामग्रतोयन्तमाहवे । शूरैरनिजनोपेतैरयुक्तंहिनिवर्तितुम् ।।6.82.4।।
explanation: "Return and come in front, close to me and follow me. It is not proper for you to win wars and be praised."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्सुसङ्क्रुद्धावायुपुत्रेणधीमता । शैलशृङ्गान् द्रुमांश्चवजगृहुर्हृष्टमानसाः ।।6.82.5।।
explanation: Wise son of wind god having spoken in that way, delighted in mind the Vanaras seized peaks of mountains and also trees in great fury.

shloka_text: अभिपेतुश्चगर्जन्तोराक्षसान्वानरर्षभाः । परिवार्यहनूमन्तमन्वयुश्चमहाहवे ।।6.82.6।।
explanation: Surrounding Hanuman, the Vanara leaders followed him for a great fight.

shloka_text: स तैर्वानरमुख्यैश्चहनुमान्सर्वतोवृतः । हुताशनइवार्चिष्मानदहच्छत्रुवाहिनीम् ।।6.82.7।।
explanation: Hanuman went surrounded by Vanara leaders who resembled flaming fire and began to consume the enemy troops like flaming fire.

shloka_text: स राक्षसानांकदनंचकारसुमहाकपिः । वृतोवानरसैन्येनकालान्तकयोमोपमः ।।6.82.8।।
explanation: The Vanara army surrounded that great monkey, Hanuman, who was like Yama, the god of death and caused havoc to Rakshasas.

shloka_text: स तुकोपेनचाविष्टःशोकेन च महाकपिः । हनूमान्रावणिरथेमहतींपातयच्छिलाम् ।।6.82.9।।
explanation: Hanuman, overtaken by anger, filled with great sorrow hurled a huge rock at the chariot of Ravana's son.

shloka_text: तामापतन्तींदृष्टवैवरथस्सारथिनातदा । विधेयाश्वसमायुक्तोविदूरमपवाहितः ।।6.82.10।।
explanation: Then seeing that rock coming towards the chariot yoked to obedient horses, the chariot rider drove it to a long distance.

shloka_text: तमिन्द्रजितमप्राप्यरथस्थंसहसारथिम् । विवेशधरणींभित्त्वासाशिलाव्यर्थमुद्यता ।।6.82.11।।
explanation: That rock hurled by Hanuman failed to reach the chariot in which Indrajith was seated and also the charioteer. It cleaved the earth and entered.

shloka_text: पतितायांशिलायांतुव्यथितारक्षसांचमूः । निपतन्त्या च शिलयाराक्षसामथिताभृशम् ।।6.82.12।।
explanation: As the rock fell on the battlefield the Rakshasa troops got alarmed and were violently crushed to death.

shloka_text: तमभ्यधावन् शतशोनदन्तःकाननौकसः । तेद्रुमांश्चमहाकायागिरिशृङ्गाणिचोद्यताः ।।6.82.13।।
explanation: Those gigantic forest dwellers in hundreds seizing trees and rocks lifted and fought making loud noise.

shloka_text: क्षिपनीन्द्रजितंसङ्ख्येवानराभीमविक्रमाः । वृक्षशैलमहावर्षंविसृजन्तःप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.82.14।। शत्रूणांकदनंचक्रुर्नेदुश्चविविधैस्स्वनैः ।
explanation: Courageous Vanaras, innumerable in number began to rain trees and rocks throwing on the enemies. The Rakshasas number rolled on the battlefield shouting in numerous tones.

shloka_text: वानरैसैर्महाभीमैर्घोररूपानिशाचराः ।।6.82.15।। वीर्यादभिहतावृक्षैर्व्यचेष्टन्तरणक्षितौ ।
explanation: Night rangers of dreadful appearance beaten up with trees by most fierce Vanaras, fell on the battlefield and struck one another.

shloka_text: स्वसैन्यमभिवीक्ष्याथवानरार्दितमिन्द्रजित् ।।6.82.16।। प्रगृहीतायुधःक्रुद्धःपरानभिमुखोययौ ।
explanation: Indrajith, looking at his own army tormented by the Vanaras, was enraged, and went towards the enemies' seizing weapons.

shloka_text: सःशरौघानवसृजन्स्वसैन्येनाभिसम्वृतः ।।6.82.17।। जघानकपिशार्दूलान्सुबहून्दृष्टविक्रमः ।
explanation: Indrajith of unyielding valour, combining with his own army let go numerous arrows on the tigers of Vanaras and struck them.

shloka_text: शूलैःरशनिभिःखङ्गै: पट्टसै: कूटमुद्गरैः ।।6.82.18।। तेचाप्यनुचरास्तस्यवानरान्जघ्नुराहवे ।
explanation: In the battle, followers of Indrajith struck the Vanaras with tridents, asanis, swords, sharp edged spears, and kutamudgaras.

shloka_text: स्कन्धविटपैश्शालैश्शिलाभिश्चमहाबलः ।।6.82.19।। हनूमान्कदनंचक्रेरक्षसांभीमकर्मणाम् ।
explanation: Hanuman, who was endowed with great strength, killed Rakshasas capable of terrific tasks with trees having large trunks and branches and stones also.

shloka_text: सनिवार्यपरानीकमब्रवीत्तान्वनौकसः ।।6.82.20।। हनूमान् सन्निवर्तध्वं न नस्साध्यमिदंबलम् ।
explanation: Hanuman made the enemy army retreat, and spoke to his own army," No use of defeating this army for us as our mission is not winning the army."

shloka_text: त्यक्त्वाप्राणान्विवेष्टन्तोरामप्रियचिकीर्षवः ।।6.82.21।। यन्निमित्तंहियुध्यामोहतासाजनकात्मजा ।
explanation: "To please Rama, we are giving up life. Let us make Rama know that the daughter of Janaka for whose sake we are fighting this war and giving up life has been killed."

shloka_text: इममर्थंहिविज्ञाप्यरामंसुग्रीवमेव च ।।6.82.22।। तौयत्प्रतिविधास्येतेतत्करिष्यामहेवयम् ।
explanation: "On telling this fact (that Indrajith has killed Sita) to Rama and Sugriva and knowing their reply we will do what is to be done."

shloka_text: त्युक्त्वावानरश्रेष्ठोवारयन्सर्ववानरान् ।।6.82.23।। शनैश्शनैरसन्त्रस्तस्सबलस्सन्यवर्तत ।
explanation: The foremost of the Vanaras, kept back all the Vanaras after speaking that way to the army and slowly and slowly retreated.

shloka_text: ततःप्रेक्ष्यहनूमन्तंव्रजन्तंयत्रराघवः ।।6.82.24।। स होतुकामोदुष्टात्मागतश्चैत्यंनिकुम्भिलाम् ।
explanation: Thereafter, observing Hanuman going to Raghava, the evil minded Indrajith went to Nikumbhilam desiring to offer oblations at the sanctuary.

shloka_text: निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठायपावकंजुहवेन्द्रजित् ।।6.82.25।। यज्ञभूम्यांततोगत्वापावकस्तेनरक्षसा । हूयमानःप्रजज्वालमांसशोणितभुक्तदा ।।6.82.26।।
explanation: Indrajith reaching Nikumbhilam, the sacrificial ground, poured oblation of blood into the sacrificial fire for Devatas and the fire blazed.

shloka_text: निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठायपावकंजुहवेन्द्रजित् ।।6.82.25।। यज्ञभूम्यांततोगत्वापावकस्तेनरक्षसा । हूयमानःप्रजज्वालमांसशोणितभुक्तदा ।।6.82.26।।
explanation: Indrajith reaching Nikumbhilam, the sacrificial ground, poured oblation of blood into the sacrificial fire for Devatas and the fire blazed.

shloka_text: सोऽर्चिःपिनद्धोददृशेहोमशोणिततर्पितः । सन्ध्यागतइवादित्यःसुतीव्रोऽग्नि: समुत्थितः ।।6.82.27।।
explanation: The flame had swollen up with the offering of blood as oblation and risen. It was very bright and wrapped in the flames the fire resembled the sun.

shloka_text: राघवश्चापिविपुलंतंराक्षसवनौकसाम् । श्रुत्वासङ्ग्रामनिर्घोषंजाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह ।।6.83.1।।
explanation: Hearing the great noise of war between Rakshasas and Vanaras, Rama said to Jambavantha.

shloka_text: सौम्यनूनंहनुमताकृतंकर्मसुदुष्करम् । श्रूयते च यथाभीमस्सुमहावायुधस्वनः ।।6.83.2।।
explanation: "O gentle Jambavan! The terrifying sound of weapons is heard. Surely Hanuman has done a difficult task."

shloka_text: तद्गच्छकुरुसाहाय्यंस्वबलेनाभिसम्वृतः । क्षिप्रमक्षपतेतस्यकपिश्रेष्ठस्ययुध्यतः ।।6.83.3।।
explanation: "O King of Bears! Accompanied by your army, go to the battlefield and help the best of monkeys."

shloka_text: ऋक्षराक्षस्तथोक्तस्तुस्वेनानीकेनसम्वृतः । आगच्छत्पश्चिमद्वारंहनूमान्यत्रवानरः ।।6.83.4।।
explanation: Rama having spoken thus, King of Bears surrounded by Vanaras went to Hanuman at the western gate.

shloka_text: अथायान्तंहनूमन्तंददर्शर्क्षपतिपथि । वानरैःकृतसङ्ग्रामैश्श्वसद्भिरभिसम्वृतम् ।।6.83.5।।
explanation: Then the Lord of Bears saw Hanuman accompanied by Vanaras who fought in war coming sighing.

shloka_text: दृष्टापथिहनूमांश्चतदृक्षबलमुद्यतम् । नीलमेघनिभंभीमंसन्निवार्यन्यवर्तत ।।6.83.6।।
explanation: Hanuman seeing the terrific army of Bears marching like a dark cloud asked them to return and he also returned with them.

shloka_text: स तेनसहसैन्येनसन्निकर्षंमहायशाः । शीघ्रमागम्यरामायदुःखितोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।।6.83.7।।
explanation: Hanuman of great fame accompanied by army quickly came to Rama and submitted as follows.

shloka_text: समरेयुध्यमानानामस्माकंप्रेक्षतांपुरः । जघानरुदतींसीतामिन्द्रजिद्रावणात्मजः ।।6.83.8।।
explanation: "Ravana's son, Indrajith struck Sita, who was crying in front of us looking at us while we were fighting in war."

shloka_text: उद्भ्रान्तचित्तस्तांदृष्टवाविषण्णोऽहमरिन्दमः । तदहंभवतोवृतंविज्ञापयितुमागतः ।।6.83.9।।
explanation: "O Tamer of enemies! Seeing her (Sita) bewildered in mind, worried, I have come to inform you accompanied by Vanaras."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराघवश्शोकमूर्चितः । निपपाततदाभूमौछिन्नमूलंइवद्रुमः ।।6.83.10।।
explanation: On hearing, Hanuman's words Raghava became deluded in sorrow and fell on the ground like a tree cut at the root.

shloka_text: तंभूमौदेवसङ्काशंपतितंदृश्यराघवम् । अभिपेतुस्समुत्पत्यसर्वतःकपिसत्तमाः ।।6.83.11।।
explanation: Seeing Raghava who is equal to god fallen on the ground, and the best of monkeys lifting him, the Vanaras from all over came jumping.

shloka_text: आसिञ्चन् सलिलैश्चैनंपद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिभिः । प्रदहन्तमानासाद्यंसहसाग्निमिवोद्यतम् ।।6.83.12।।
explanation: Reaching Rama, who was like a burning fire that has risen up and suddenly fallen, the Vanaras sprinkled water with fragrance of lotuses and lilies on Rama just as sprinkling water on an inextinguishable fire that has flared up suddenly.

shloka_text: तंलक्ष्मणोऽथबाहुभ्यांपरिष्वज्यसुदुःखितः । उवाचराममस्वस्थंवाक्यंहेत्वर्थसम्युतम् ।।6.83.13।।
explanation: Then, Lakshmana who was very worried held the arms of Rama who was unwell and spoke these meaningful words.

shloka_text: शुभेवर्त्मनितिष्ठन्तंत्वामार्यविजितेन्द्रियम् । अनर्थेभ्यो न शक्नोतित्रातुंधर्मोनिरर्थकः ।।6.83.14।।
explanation: "O Noble Rama! If You, who have gained over senses and sticking to a virtuous path are not protected, from this calamity by righteousness, then righteousness is useless."

shloka_text: भूतानांस्थावाराणां च जङ्गमानां च दर्शनम् । यथास्ति न तथाधर्मस्तेननास्तीतिमेमतिः ।।6.83.15।।
explanation: " As animate and inanimate beings are seen experiencing joy at present, righteousness is not the cause of joy, I think so."

shloka_text: यथैवस्थावरंव्यक्तंजङ्गमं न तथाविधम् । नायमर्थस्तथायुक्तस्त्वद्विधो न विपद्यते ।।6.83.16।।
explanation: "Just as inanimate beings which are seen happy and animate are also seen in the same manner, in which case that righteousness alone prospers is not there (for a person like you would not suffer). Knowing this you should not suffer."

shloka_text: यद्यधर्मोभवेद्भूतोरावणोनरकंव्रजेत् । भवांश्चधर्मसम्युक्तोनैवंव्यसनमाप्नुयात् ।।6.83.17।।
explanation: "If there is unrighteousness, Ravana should be in hell. You who are endowed with righteousness should not have agony."

shloka_text: तस्य च व्यसनाभावाद्व्यसनंचागतेत्वयि । धर्मोभवत्यधर्मश्चपरस्परविरोधिनौ ।।6.83.18।।
explanation: " As Ravana has no sorrow and you have experienced agony the contraries of each other have changed the roles of righteousness and unrighteousness."

shloka_text: धर्मेणोपलभेद्धर्ममधर्मंचाप्यधर्मतः । यद्यधर्मेणयुज्येयुर्येष्वधर्मःप्रतिष्ठितः ।।6.83.19।। यदिधर्मेणवियुज्येरन्नधर्मरुचयोजनाः । धर्मेणचरतांधर्मंचैषांधर्मफलंभवेत् ।।6.83.20।।
explanation: "The righteous attains the benefit through righteous means, and the unrighteous suffer by unrighteous means. If unrighteousness is rooted in the unrighteous and are pleased with unrighteousness they will be deprived of the result of righteousness. It is not otherwise."

shloka_text: धर्मेणोपलभेद्धर्ममधर्मंचाप्यधर्मतः । यद्यधर्मेणयुज्येयुर्येष्वधर्मःप्रतिष्ठितः ।।6.83.19।। यदिधर्मेणवियुज्येरन्नधर्मरुचयोजनाः । धर्मेणचरतांधर्मंचैषांधर्मफलंभवेत् ।।6.83.20।।
explanation: "The righteous attains the benefit through righteous means, and the unrighteous suffer by unrighteous means. If unrighteousness is rooted in the unrighteous and are pleased with unrighteousness they will be deprived of the result of righteousness. It is not otherwise."

shloka_text: यस्मादर्थाविवर्धन्तेयेष्वधर्मःप्रतिष्ठितः । क्लिश्यन्तेधर्मशीलाश्चतस्मादेतौनिरर्थकौ ।।6.83.21।।
explanation: "Since those rooted in unrighteous develop and are wealthy, and those who follow dharma suffer both these are meaningless."

shloka_text: वध्यन्तेपापकर्माणोयद्यधर्मेणराघव । वधकर्महतोऽधर्मः स हतःकिंवधिष्यति ।।6.83.22।।
explanation: "Righteousness and unrighteousness are forms of actions, sinful or not sinful. If sinful action is unrighteous, those who have done sinful actions should suffer. Since sinful action is momentary, and as soon as the action is over unrighteousness is also gone. That being so how can unrighteousness cause pain to anyone?"

shloka_text: अथवाविहितेनायंहन्यतेहन्तिवापरम् । विधिरालिप्यतेतेन न स पापेनकर्मणा ।।6.83.23।।
explanation: "Or else if a man is destroyed by killing another, destiny which is engendered by the sinful action suffers and not the doer of sinful action."

shloka_text: अदृष्टप्रतिकारेणत्वव्यक्तेनासतासता । कथंशक्यंपरंप्राप्तुंधर्मेणारिविकर्षण ।।6.83.24।।
explanation: "O Crusher of enemies! How does righteousness get encountered? It is not seen. How to know whether it is real or unreal? Is it possible to know that the best result is attained by righteousness."

shloka_text: यदिसत्स्यात्सतांमुख्यनासत्स्यत्तवकिञ्चन । त्वयायदीदृशंप्राप्तंतस्मात्सन्नोपपद्यते ।।6.83.25।।
explanation: "O foremost among the victorious! To you, who are a jewel no evil should accrue. Since such difficulty has been faced by you, the fact that good actions result in good destiny is not true."

shloka_text: अथवादुर्बलःक्लीबोबलंधर्मोऽनुवर्तते । दुर्बलोहृतमर्यादो न सेव्यइतिमेमतिः ।।6.83.26।।
explanation: "Or else dharma becomes feeble, ineffective, submits to might, then it is better not to follow such dharma which is feeble, I think."

shloka_text: बलस्ययदिचेद्धर्मोगुणभूतःपराक्रमे । धर्ममुत्सृज्यवर्तस्वयथाधर्मेतथाबले ।।6.83.27।।
explanation: "Giving up predominance of virtue, seek courage and submit to might for succeeding in action. Seek might just as you have sought dharma earlier for success."

shloka_text: अथचेत्सत्यवचनंधर्म: किलपरन्तप । अनृतस्त्वय्यकरुणःकिं न बद्धस्त्वयापिता ।।6.83.28।।
explanation: "O scorcher of enemies! If you consider speaking the truth is dharma, why did you not bind your father (who promised to give the kingdom) and was not compassionate (spoke untruth later)."

shloka_text: यदिधर्मोभवेद्भूतअधर्मोवापरन्तप । न स्महत्वामुनिंवज्रीकुर्यादिज्यांशतक्रतुः ।।6.83.29।।
explanation: "Indra killed an ascetic (Viswarupa) and did fire sacrifice. If dharma alone is his duty, he could have done hundreds of fire sacrifices and not have killed the ascetic. If adharma is duty he would have killed the ascetic and not done fire sacrifice."

shloka_text: अधर्मसंश्रितोधर्मोविनाशयतिराघव । सर्वमेतद्यथाकामंकाकुत्स्थकुरुतेनरः ।।6.83.30।।
explanation: "Kakuthsa Rama! Kings followed dharma and adharma both according to context. Whether following dharma or adharma destruction is happening. Therefore, humans keep doing both as per their desire."

shloka_text: ममचेदंमतंतातधरोऽयमितिराघव । धर्ममूलंत्वयाछिन्नंराज्यमुत्सृजतातदा ।।6.83.31।।
explanation: "Dear Raghava! In my opinion also depending on desire and context, following dharma or adharma is proper. You have severed the roots of dharma by giving up the kingdom."

shloka_text: अर्थेभ्योहिप्रवृद्धेभ्यःसम्वृत्तेभ्यस्ततस्ततः । क्रियाःसर्वाःप्रवर्तन्तेपर्वतेभ्यःइवापगाः ।।6.83.32।।
explanation: "Prosperity is augmented gradually and developed by all means just as rivers flow from mountains, all undertakings follow conducive to success."

shloka_text: अर्थेनहिविमुक्तस्यपुरुषस्याल्पचेतसः । विच्छिद्यन्तेक्रियास्सर्वाग्रीष्मेकुसरितोयथा ।।6.83.33।।
explanation: "Just like streams dry up in summer, if one who is of meagre intelligence and forsakes wealth, all his actions will be interrupted."

shloka_text: सोऽयमर्थंपरित्यज्यसुखकामःसुखैधितः । पापमारभतेकर्तुंतदादोषःप्रवर्तते ।।6.83.34।।
explanation: "If one who has been happy seeks happiness on renouncing wealth then proceeds to perform sinful actions it is a mistake."

shloka_text: यस्यार्थास्तस्यमित्राणियस्यार्थास्यस्यबान्धवाः । यस्यार्थास्सपुमान्लोकेयस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः ।।6.83.35।।
explanation: "Friends gather round him in whom riches abide. Relations stand by him who has wealth. He is considered manly in whom wealth abides, and he is learned who has wealth."

shloka_text: यस्यार्थास्स च विक्रान्तोयस्यार्थास्स च बुद्धिमान् । यस्यार्थास्समहाभागोयस्यार्थास्समहागुणः ।।6.83.36।।
explanation: He is gallant to whom wealth has flown, he is intelligent in whom wealth abides, he is glorious in whom wealth exists and he is superior in great virtues in whom wealth found receptacle.

shloka_text: अर्थस्यैतेपरित्यागेदोषाःप्रव्याहृतामया । राज्यमुत्सृजतावीरयेनबुद्धिस्त्वयाकृता ।।6.83.37।।
explanation: 'If you give up wealth the evils will follow you', said I. Now you left the kingdom. The basis on which you made such a resolve is not known to me.

shloka_text: यस्यार्थाःधर्मकामार्थास्तस्यसर्वंप्रदक्षिणम् । अधनेनार्थकामेननार्थश्शक्योविचिन्वता ।।6.83.38।।
explanation: For one who has wealth all his actions of dharma would give pleasure and favourable. One who has no wealth and is worrying about it can't attain it.

shloka_text: हर्षःकामश्चदर्पश्चधर्मःक्रोधश्शमोदमः । अर्थादेतानिसर्वाणिप्रवर्तन्तेनराधिप ।।6.83.39।।
explanation: "O Rama! Desire, delight, pride, virtue, anger, forgiveness, fortitude all these are effective through wealth."

shloka_text: येषांनश्यत्ययंलोकश्चरतांधर्मचारिणाम् । तेऽर्थास्त्वयि न दृश्यन्तेदुर्दिनेषुयथाग्रहाः ।।6.83.40।।
explanation: "Even if there is wealth if one renunciates wealth and follows dharma in this world they perish like planets on cloudy days."

shloka_text: त्वयिप्रव्रजितेवीरगुरोश्चवचनेस्थिते । रक्षसापहृताभार्याप्राणैःप्रियतरातव ।।6.83.41।।
explanation: "O heroic Rama! You have been faithful to the promise to your father and left home following dharma (giving up wealth), and your dear wife who is your life has been abducted by Rakshasa."

shloka_text: तदद्यविपुलंवीरदुःखमिन्द्रजिताकृतम् । कर्मणाव्यपनेष्यामितस्मादुत्तिष्ठराघव ।।6.83.42।।
explanation: "Get up, heroic Raghava! I will get rid of the agony caused to you by Indrajith, by the action."

shloka_text: उत्थिष्ठनरशार्दूलदीर्घबाहोधृतव्रत । किमात्मानंमहात्मानंमात्मानं न बुध्यसे ।।6.83.43।।
explanation: "O tiger among men! O broad shouldered endowed with fortitude! Why do you not know yourself that you are a great soul and doer of action?"

shloka_text: राममाश्वासयानेतुलक्ष्मणेभ्रातृवत्सले । निक्षिप्यगुल्मान् स्वस्थानेतत्रागच्छद्विभीषणः ।।6.84.1 ।।
explanation: As Lakshmana was comforting his affectionate brother, Vibheeshana came to Rama assigning the troops to reach their respective places.

shloka_text: नानाप्रहरणैर्वीरैश्चतुर्भिस्सचिवैर्वृत: । नीलाञ्जनचयाकारैर्मातङ्गैरिवयूथप ।।6.84.2।।
explanation: Accompanied by the four ministers surrounded by four ministers resembling leaders of elephants, who looked dark like collyrium, Vibheeshana came to highsouled Rama. He witnessed Vanaras whose eyes were filled with tears.

shloka_text: राघवं च महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् । ददर्शमोहमापन्नंलक्ष्मणस्याङ्गमाश्रितम् ।।6.84.3।।
explanation: He (Vibheeshana) saw the great soul, the delight of the Ikshvaku race deluded, distressed, and lying on the lap of Lakshmana.

shloka_text: राघवं च महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् । ददर्शमोहमापन्नंलक्ष्मणस्याङ्गमाश्रितम् ।।6.84.3।।
explanation: He (Vibheeshana) saw the great soul, the delight of the Ikshvaku race deluded, distressed, and lying on the lap of Lakshmana.

shloka_text: व्रीडितंशोकसन्तप्तंदृष्टवारामंविभीषणः । अन्तर्धुःखएनदीनात्माकिमेतदितिसोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.84.5।।
explanation: Vibheeshana was pained to see Rama immersed in grief, depressed in spirit, and asked for What is all this grief for?

shloka_text: विभीषणमुखंदृष्टवासुग्रीवंतांश्चवानरान् । लक्ष्मणोवाचमन्दार्थमिदंबाष्पपरिप्लुतः ।।6.84.6।।
explanation: Lakshmana looking at Sugriva's face and also at the Vanaras, his eyes bathed in tears spoke in a dull tone.

shloka_text: हताइन्द्रजितासीताइतिश्रुत्वैवराघवः । हनूमद्वचनात्सौम्यततोमोहमुपागतः ।।6.84.7।।
explanation: "O Noble one! On hearing Hanuman that Sita is killed by Indrajith, Rama is deluded', said Lakshmana to Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: कथयन्तंतुसौमित्रिंसन्निवार्यविभीषणः । पुष्कलार्थमिदंवाक्यंविसंज्ञंराममब्रवीत् ।।6.84.8।।
explanation: Vibheeshana spoke these meaningful words to Rama, who was unconscious, restraining Saumithri from speaking.

shloka_text: मनुजेन्द्रार्थरूपेणयदुक्ततुहनूमता । तदयुक्तमहंमन्येसागरस्येवशोषणम् ।।6.84.9।।
explanation: "I think that what has been spoken by Hanuman as truth (that Sita has been killed) is like drying up an ocean."

shloka_text: अभिप्रायंतुजानामिरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । सीतांप्रतिमहाबाहो न च घातंकरिष्यति ।।6.84.10।।
explanation: "O mighty armed Rama! with reference to Sita, you do not know Ravana's opinion. He will never kill Sita."

shloka_text: त्तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराघवश्शोककर्शितः । नोपधारयतेव्यक्तंयदुक्तंतेनरक्षसा ।।6.85.1।।
explanation: Immersed in grief, Raghava could not make out the words spoken by Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: ततोधैर्यमवष्टभ्यरामःपरपुरञ्जयः । विभीषणमुपासीनमुवाचकपिसन्निधौ ।।6.85.2।।
explanation: Then Rama, who can win over enemies, picked up courage, said to Vibheeshana seated near him in front of Vanaras.

shloka_text: नैरृताधिपतेवाक्यंयदुक्तंतेविभीषण । भूयस्तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामिब्रूहियत्तेविवक्षितम् ।।6.85.3।।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas, Vibheeshana! I wish to hear the words spoken by you. You may repeat that which you wanted to convey. I wish to hear."

shloka_text: राघवस्यवचःश्रुत्वावाक्यंवाक्यविशारद. । यत्तत्पुनरिदंवाक्यंबभाषे स विभीषणः ।।6.85.4।।
explanation: Vibheeshana, who was skilled in expression, spoke again as follows on hearing Raghava's words.

shloka_text: यथाज्ञप्तंमहाबाहोत्वयागुल्मनिवेशनम् । तत्तथाऽनुष्ठितंवीरत्वद्वाक्यसमनन्तरम् ।।6.85.5।।
explanation: " After your command the army has been divided and placed at respective places as you said."

shloka_text: तान्यनीकानिसर्वाणिविभग्नानिसमन्ततः । विन्यस्तायूथपाश्चैवयथान्यायंविभागशः ।।6.85.6।।
explanation: All the army forces have been collected, divided, and assigned to respective places separately.

shloka_text: भूयस्तुममविज्ञाप्यंतच्छ्रुणुष्वमहायश: । त्वय्यकारणसन्तप्तेसन्तप्तहृदयावयम् ।।6.85.7।।
explanation: "O great Lord! Hear me, which is yet to be submitted by me to you. You are afflicted without cause and pained at heart."

shloka_text: त्यजराजन्निमंशोकंमिथ्यासन्तापमागतम् । तदियंत्यज्यतांचिन्ताशत्रुहर्षविवर्धिनी ।।6.85.8।।
explanation: "O king! Give up this false agony which has set in. It enhances the joy of the enemy. Give up this anxiety."

shloka_text: उद्यमःक्रियतांवीरहर्षःसमुपसेव्यताम् । प्राप्तव्यायदितेसीताहन्तव्याश्चनिशाचराः ।।6.85.9।।
explanation: "Let efforts be made to recover Sita. Let enthusiasm be restored to recover Sita. Rakshasas will be exterminated."

shloka_text: रघुनन्दनवक्ष्यामिश्रूयतांमेहितंवचः । साध्वयंयातुसौमित्रिर्बलेनमहतावृतः ।।6.85.10।। निकुम्भिलायांसम्प्राप्यहन्तुंरावणिमाहवे । धनुर्मण्डलनिर्मुक्तैराशीविषविषोपमैः ।।6.85.11।।
explanation: "Delight of Raghus! You may listen to my words of advice. Let Saumithri march ahead to Nikumbhilam accompanied by the great army. On reaching, let Lakshmana who is capable of killing Indrajith discharge venomous serpents like deadly poisonous arrows from his bow in circular form and kill Rakshasas."

shloka_text: रघुनन्दनवक्ष्यामिश्रूयतांमेहितंवचः । साध्वयंयातुसौमित्रिर्बलेनमहतावृतः ।।6.85.10।। निकुम्भिलायांसम्प्राप्यहन्तुंरावणिमाहवे । धनुर्मण्डलनिर्मुक्तैराशीविषविषोपमैः ।।6.85.11।।
