shloka_text: प्रहस्तोनिहतोवीरोनिकुम्भश्चमहाबल. । कुम्भकर्णश्चकुम्भश्चधूम्राक्षश्चनिशाचरः ।।6.90.10।। जम्बुमालीमहामालीतीक्ष्णवेगोऽशनिप्रभः । सुप्तघ्नोयज्ञकोपश्चवज्रदंष्ट्रश्चराक्षसः ।।6.90.11।। सम्ह्रादीविकटोऽरिघ्नस्तपनोदमएव च । प्रघासःप्रघसश्चैवप्रजङ्घोजङ्घएव च ।।6.90.12।। अग्निकेतुश्चदुर्धर्षोरश्मिकेतुश्चवीर्यवान् । विद्युज्जिह्वाद्विजिह्वश्चसूर्यशत्रुश्चराक्षसः ।।6.90.13।। अकम्पनःसुपार्श्वश्चचक्रमाली च राक्षसः । कम्पनस्सत्त्ववन्तौतौदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।6.90.14।।
explanation: "The heroic Prahastha, Nikumbha also and Kumbhakarna of mighty prowess, Kumbha also, night ranger Dum raksha, Jambumali, Mahamali, Teekshanavega, Asanibhra, Suptanga, Yagnakopa, Vajradamshtra, Rakshasas Simhadri, Arigna, Vikata, Tapana, Dama also, Praghaasa, Praghasa, Prajaghna, and Jaghan also, Durdarsha, Agniketha, heroes Rasmikethu, Vidyajihva, Dwijihwa, Suryasatru, and Rakshasas Akampana, Suparswa, Chakramali, and Rakshasas Kampana, and energetic Devanthaka and Naranthaka have been killed by you."

shloka_text: एतान्निहत्यातिबलान्बहून्राक्षससत्तमान् । बाहुभ्यांसागरंतीर्त्वालङ्घ्यतांगोष्पदं लघु ।6.90.15।।
explanation: "You have made short of many exceedingly mighty leaders of Rakshasas and swum the ocean. You cross this hoof mark of a cow without delay."

shloka_text: एतावदेवशेषंवोजेतव्यमिहवानराः । हतास्सर्वेसमागम्यराक्षसाबलदर्पिताः ।।6.90.16।।
explanation: "O Vanaras! Left over Rakshasas only to be conquered now. Rakshasas, who were proud of their might have been killed on meeting you."

shloka_text: अयुक्तंनिधनंकर्तुंपुत्रस्यजनितुर्मम । घृणामपास्यरामार्थेनिहन्यांभ्रातुरात्मजम् ।।6.90.17।।
explanation: "For the sake of Rama, I will strike my brother's son. Being a father, taking pity, I am helpless as it is not proper for me to take the life of my son."

shloka_text: हन्तुकामस्यमेबाष्पंचक्षुश्चैवनिरुध्यति । तमेवैषमहाबाहुर्लक्ष्मणश्शमयिष्यति ।।6.90.18।। वानराघ्नतसम्भूयभृत्यानस्यसमीपगान् ।
explanation: "I wish to kill him, tears are clouding my eyes. Mighty armed Lakshmana will kill him. Vanaras collected together are coming near him and can destroy his attendants."

shloka_text: इतितेनातियशसाराक्षसेनाभिचोदिताः ।।6.90.19।। वानरेन्द्राजहृषिरेलाङ्गूलानि च विव्यधुः ।
explanation: Incited by the encouraging words of Vibheeshana (Rakshasa), Vanara chiefs rejoiced and went shaking their tails.

shloka_text: ततस्तुकपिशार्दूलाःश्रवेन्तःश्चपुनःपुनः ।।6.90.20।। मुमुचुर्विविधान्नादान्मेघान् दृष्टवेवबर्हिणः ।
explanation: Then the tigers among monkeys again and again roaring in seeing the clouds made several kinds of sounds like peacocks.

shloka_text: जाम्बवानपितैःसर्वैःसयूथ्यैरभिसम्वृतः ।।6.90.21।। तेऽश्मभिस्ताडयामासुर्नखैर्धन्स्सैश्चराक्षसान् ।
explanation: All the troops surrounded by Jambavan too, pierced the Rakshasas with their nails and teeth.

shloka_text: निघ्नन्तमृक्षाधिपतिंराक्षसास्तेमहाबलाः ।।6.90.22।। परिवव्रुर्भयंत्यक्त्वातमनेकविधायुथाः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas who were endowed with mighty strength giving up fear, armed with different kinds of weapons surrounded Jambavan, the Lord of Bears.

shloka_text: शरैःपरशुभिस्तीक्ष्णैःपट्टिशैर्यष्टितोमरैः ।।6.90.23।। जाम्बवन्तंमृधेजघ्नुर्निघ्नन्तंराक्षसींचमूम् ।
explanation: The Rakshasas then assailed Jambvan who was destroying the Rakshasa army with axes, pointed arrows, iron bars and sharpedged spears.

shloka_text: स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलःसञ्जज्ञेकपिरक्षसाम् ।।6.90.24।। देवासुराणांक्रुद्धानांयथाभीमोमहास्वनः ।
explanation: Fearful and vehement battle took place between enraged Vanaras and Rakshasas making loud clamours like the battle (in the past) between Devas and asuras.

shloka_text: हनुमानपिसङ्क्रुद्धःसानुमुत्पाट्यपर्वतात् ।।6.90.25।। स लक्ष्मणंस्वयंपृष्ठादवरोप्यमहामनाः । रक्षसांकदनंचक्रेसमासाद्यसहस्रशः ।।6.90.26।।
explanation: Great selfHanuman too became furious and dismounting Lakshmana from his back uprooted a sala tree from a mountain and went on exterminating thousands of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: हनुमानपिसङ्क्रुद्धःसानुमुत्पाट्यपर्वतात् ।।6.90.25।। स लक्ष्मणंस्वयंपृष्ठादवरोप्यमहामनाः । रक्षसांकदनंचक्रेसमासाद्यसहस्रशः ।।6.90.26।।
explanation: Great selfHanuman too became furious and dismounting Lakshmana from his back uprooted a sala tree from a mountain and went on exterminating thousands of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: स दत्त्वातुमुलंयुद्धंपितृव्यस्येन्द्रजत् बली । लक्ष्मणंपरवीरघ्नःपुनरेवाभ्यधावत ।।6.90.27।।
explanation: Mighty Indrajith who can give tough fight to enemies gave a violent fight to his father's brother and again rushed towards Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तौप्रयुद्दौतदावीरौमृधेलक्ष्मणराक्षसौ । शरौघानभिवर्षन्तौजघ्नतुस्तौपरस्परम् ।।6.90.28।।
explanation: In that battle the two heroes, Lakshmana and Indrajith rained streams of arrows on each other and engaged themselves in the battle.

shloka_text: अभीक्षणमन्तर्धदतुश्शरजालैर्महाबलौ । चन्द्रादित्याविवोष्णान्तेयथामेघैस्तरस्विनौ ।।6.90.29।।
explanation: Both the mighty and energetic heroes, covered each other with arrows just as after summer the moon and Sun are veiled frequently by clouds.

shloka_text: न ह्यादानं न सन्धानंधनुषोवापरिग्रहः । न विप्रमोक्षोबाणानां न विकर्षो न विग्रहः ।।6.90.30।। न मुष्टिप्रतिसन्धानं न लक्ष्यप्रतिपादनम् । अदृश्यततयोस्तत्रयुध्यतोःपाणिलाघवात् ।।6.90.31।।
explanation: While both were fighting, due to the quickness of their hand movement, it could not be perceived whether they were taking out arrows from the quiver, drawing the string, or seizing arrows, or aiming to shoot or not. Whether they were drawing or stretching the bow or not or fixing with their fist or hitting the target or not, was not clear.

shloka_text: न ह्यादानं न सन्धानंधनुषोवापरिग्रहः । न विप्रमोक्षोबाणानां न विकर्षो न विग्रहः ।।6.90.30।। न मुष्टिप्रतिसन्धानं न लक्ष्यप्रतिपादनम् । अदृश्यततयोस्तत्रयुध्यतोःपाणिलाघवात् ।।6.90.31।।
explanation: While both were fighting, due to the quickness of their hand movement, it could not be perceived whether they were taking out arrows from the quiver, drawing the string, or seizing arrows, or aiming to shoot or not. Whether they were drawing or stretching the bow or not or fixing with their fist or hitting the target or not, was not clear.

shloka_text: चापवेगप्रयुक्स्सैश्चबाणजालैःसमन्ततः । अन्तरिकेऽभिसम्पन्ने न रूपाणिचकाशिरे ।।6.90.32।।
explanation: As they were discharging arrows from the bow swiftly, the arrows formed a net covering all over the sky and no object could be visible.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणोरावणिंप्राप्यरावणिश्चापिलक्ष्मणम् । अव्यवस्थाभवत्युग्राताभ्यामन्योन्यविग्रहे ।।6.90.33।।
explanation: As Lakshmana was meeting Indrajith and Indrajith was reaching out to Lakshmana, confusion prevailed about who was hitting whom?

shloka_text: ताभामुभाभ्यांतरसाप्रसृष्टैर्विशिखैःशितैः । निरन्तरमिवाकाशंबभूवतमसावृतम् ।।6.90.34।।
explanation: while both of them one over the other swiftly extended and loosened the whetted arrows continuously, the sky, shrouded with arrows, became dark.

shloka_text: तैःपतभदिश्चबहुभिस्तयोःशरशतैःशितैः । दिशश्चप्रदिशश्चैवबभूवुःशरसङ्कुलाः ।।6.90.35।।
explanation: Many hundreds of pointed arrows falling in all directions and intermediate points spread all over.

shloka_text: तमसापिहितंसर्वमासीत्प्रतिभयंमहत् । अस्तंगतेसहस्रांशेसम्वृतेतमसा च वै ।।6.90.36।। रुधिरौघामहानद्यःप्रावर्तन्तसहस्रशः ।
explanation: As the sun sank down, darkness enveloped, everything was dark and dreadful in appearance. Streams of blood of thousands flowed.

shloka_text: क्रव्यादादारुणावाग्भिश्चिक्षिपुर्भीमनिःस्वनान् ।।6.90.37।। न तदानींवनौवायुर्न च जज्वालपावकः ।
explanation: Carnivorous animals cried frightfully with their tongues. Wind did not blow, the fire did not glow.

shloka_text: स्व्स्त्वस्तुलोकेभ्यइतिजजल्पुस्तेमहर्षयः ।।6.90.38।। सम्पेतुश्चात्रसन्तप्तागन्धर्वाःसहचारणैः ।
explanation: Sages murmured saying" may this world be well." Gandharvas, Charanas (who came to see the battle) went distressed.

shloka_text: अथराक्षससिंहस्यकृष्णान् कनकभूषणान् ।।6.90.39।। शरैश्चतुर्भिःसौमित्रिद्विव्याधचतुरोहयान् ।
explanation: Then Saumithri pierced with four shafts all the four black horses decked in gold, of the lion of Rakshasas (Indrajith) and finished them

shloka_text: ततोऽपरेणभल्लेनपीतेननिशितेन च ।।6.90.40।। सम्पूर्णायतमुक्तेनसुपत्रेणसुवर्चसा । महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनसूतस्यविचरिष्यतः ।।6.90.41।। स तेनबाणाशनिनातलशब्दानुवादिना । लाघवाद्राघवःश्रीमान् शिरःकायादपाहरत् ।।6.90.42।।
explanation: Then glorious Raghava with pointed bhalla furnished with beautiful plumes, splendid, deadly as Indra's thunderbolt, released and as it resounded the hit of the sword and severed the head from the body of the charioteer, who was driving in circles.

shloka_text: ततोऽपरेणभल्लेनपीतेननिशितेन च ।।6.90.40।। सम्पूर्णायतमुक्तेनसुपत्रेणसुवर्चसा । महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनसूतस्यविचरिष्यतः ।।6.90.41।। स तेनबाणाशनिनातलशब्दानुवादिना । लाघवाद्राघवःश्रीमान् शिरःकायादपाहरत् ।।6.90.42।।
explanation: Then glorious Raghava with pointed bhalla furnished with beautiful plumes, splendid, deadly as Indra's thunderbolt, released and as it resounded the hit of the sword and severed the head from the body of the charioteer, who was driving in circles.

shloka_text: ततोऽपरेणभल्लेनपीतेननिशितेन च ।।6.90.40।। सम्पूर्णायतमुक्तेनसुपत्रेणसुवर्चसा । महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनसूतस्यविचरिष्यतः ।।6.90.41।। स तेनबाणाशनिनातलशब्दानुवादिना । लाघवाद्राघवःश्रीमान् शिरःकायादपाहरत् ।।6.90.42।।
explanation: Then glorious Raghava with pointed bhalla furnished with beautiful plumes, splendid, deadly as Indra's thunderbolt, released and as it resounded the hit of the sword and severed the head from the body of the charioteer, who was driving in circles.

shloka_text: स यन्तरिमहातेजाहतेमन्दोदरीसुतः । स्वयंसारथ्यमकरोत्सुनश्चधनुरस्प ृशत् ।।6.90.43।।
explanation: When the charioteer got killed, the brilliant son of Mandodari, played the role of charioteer and wielded the bow again.

shloka_text: तदद्भुतमभूत्तत्रसामर्थ्यंपश्यतांयुधि । हयेषुव्यग्रहस्तं त विव्याधनिशितैःशरैः ।।6.90.44।। धनुष्यथपुनर्व्यग्रेहयेषुमुमुचेशरान् ।
explanation: While Indrajith was engaged with the horses in one hand and battling, his capacity was a wonder to the onlookers. Lakshmana again attacked him loosening pointed arrows at him while Indrajith was busy with his bow.

shloka_text: छिद्रेषुतेषुबाणौघैर्विचरन्तमभीतवत् ।।6.90.45।। अर्धयामाससमरेसौमित्रिःशीघ्रकृत्तमः ।
explanation: While Indrajith was moving undaunted being hurt, Lakshmana who acts with extreme alacrity and fearless easily pierced Indrajith with arrows.

shloka_text: निहतंसारथिंदृष्टवासमरेरावणात्मजः ।।6.90.46।। प्रजहौसमरोद्धर्षंविषण्णः स बभूव ह ।
explanation: Seeing the charioteer killed, Ravana's son was despondent and lost enthusiasm to fight (said people).

shloka_text: विषण्णवदनंदृष्टवाराक्षसंहरियूथपाः ।।6.90.47।। ततःपरमसम्हृष्टालक्ष्मणंचाभ्यपूजयन् ।
explanation: The Vanara leaders were joyful upon seeing the worried face of the Rakshasa and acclaimed Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ततःप्रमाथीरभसःशरभोगन्धमादनः ।।6.90.48।। अमृष्यमाणाश्चत्वारश्चक्रुर्वेगंहरीश्वराः ।
explanation: Then the four monkey leaders, Pramati, Rabahasa, Sarabha, and Gandamadhana exhibited their intolerance and went quickly.

shloka_text: तेचास्यहयमुख्येषुतूर्णमुत्पत्यवानराः ।।6.90.49।। चतुर्षुसुमहावीर्यानिपेतुर्भीमविक्रमाः ।
explanation: The four Vanaras of remarkable valour and of terrific courage getting up immediately fell on the best of the horses (of Indrajith).

shloka_text: तेषामधिष्ठितानांतैर्वानरैःपर्वतोपमैः ।।6.90.50।। मुखेभ्योरुधिरंरक्तंहयानांसमवर्तत ।
explanation: Those Vanaras of huge mountain forms getting on top of those horses (of Indrajith),

shloka_text: तेहयामथिताभग्नाव्यसवोधरणींगताः ।।6.90.51।। तेनिहत्यहयांस्तस्यप्रमथ्य च महारथम् । पुनरुत्पत्यवेगेनतस्थुर्लक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः ।।6.90.52।।
explanation: The horses were mutilated, broken, and sunk into the earth and killed. Again, bounding the great chariot, they got up quickly and stood nearby Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तेहयामथिताभग्नाव्यसवोधरणींगताः ।।6.90.51।। तेनिहत्यहयांस्तस्यप्रमथ्य च महारथम् । पुनरुत्पत्यवेगेनतस्थुर्लक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः ।।6.90.52।।
explanation: The horses were mutilated, broken, and sunk into the earth and killed. Again, bounding the great chariot, they got up quickly and stood nearby Lakshmana.

shloka_text: स हताश्वादवप्लुत्यरथान्मथितसारथिः । शरवर्षेणसौमित्रिमभ्यधावतरावणिः ।।6.90.53।।
explanation: Charioteer dead, horses killed that Indrajith leapt down and assailed Lakshmana by raining arrows.

shloka_text: स हताश्वोमहातेजाभूमौतिष्ठन्निशाचरः । इन्द्रजित्परमक्रुद्धस्सजज्वालतेजसा ।।6.91.1।।
explanation: The nightranger, effulgent Indrajith standing on the ground very angry, with horses lost, was flaming with energy.

shloka_text: तौधवनिनौजिघांसन्तवन्योन्यमिषुभिर्भृशम् । विजयेनाभिनिष्क्रान्तौवनेगजवृषाविव ।।6.91.2।।
explanation: Exceedingly wanting to kill one another, wielding bows, both sallied forth like Lordly elephants in the forest, to succeed.

shloka_text: निबर्हयन्तश्चान्योन्यंतेराक्ष्वनौकसः । भर्तारं न जहुर्युद्धेसम्पतन्तस्ततस्ततः ।।6.91.3।।
explanation: Moving all over, both Rakshasas and Vanaras killing one another in the battle did not leave their master.

shloka_text: ततस्तान् राक्षसान् सर्वान् हर्षयन् रावणात्मजः । स्तुवानोहर्षमाणश्चइदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.91.4।।
explanation: Then Ravana's son, praising all the Rakshasas making them happy, spoke these words.

shloka_text: तमसाबहुलेनेमास्सम्सक्तांसर्वतोदिशः । नेहविज्ञायतेस्वोवापरोवारक्षसोत्तमाः ।।6.91.5।।
explanation: " As all directions are spread with darkness now it is not possible to know who one's own is or others at this time."

shloka_text: धृष्टंभवन्तोयुध्यन्तुहरीणांमोहनायवै । अहंतुरथमास्थायआगमिष्यामिसंयुगे ।।6.91.6।।
explanation: "You delude the sight of Vanaras in battle. I will come to the battle taking the chariot."

shloka_text: तथाभवन्तःकुर्वन्तुयथेमेहिवनौकसः । न युध्येयुर्दुरात्मानःप्रविष्टेनगरंमयि ।।6.91.7।।
explanation: "While I enter the city you must see that these wicked minded Vanaras do not prevent me from going."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वारावणसुतोवञ्चयित्वावनौकसः । प्रविवेशपुरींलङ्कांरथहेतोरमित्रहा ।।6.91.8।।
explanation: Ravana's son, a slayer of his enemies, having spoken to Vanaras in that way, in deceiving manner entered Lanka to get the chariot.

shloka_text: स रथंभूषयित्वाथरुचिरंहेमभूषितम् । प्रासासिशरसंयुक्तंयुक्तंपरमवाजिभिः ।।6.91.9।। अधिष्ठितंहयज्ञेनसूतेनाप्तोपदेशिना । आरुरोहमहातेजारावणिःसमतिञ्जियः ।।6.91.10।।
explanation: Ravana's son ascended a decorated chariot yoked to horses, directed by a charioteer who could tender good advice and a knower of the nature of horses. It was a beautiful chariot decked with darts and swords adorned with gold which Ravana's son of extraordinarily bright, who has won enemies, ascended.

shloka_text: स रथंभूषयित्वाथरुचिरंहेमभूषितम् । प्रासासिशरसंयुक्तंयुक्तंपरमवाजिभिः ।।6.91.9।। अधिष्ठितंहयज्ञेनसूतेनाप्तोपदेशिना । आरुरोहमहातेजारावणिःसमतिञ्जियः ।।6.91.10।।
explanation: Ravana's son ascended a decorated chariot yoked to horses, directed by a charioteer who could tender good advice and a knower of the nature of horses. It was a beautiful chariot decked with darts and swords adorned with gold which Ravana's son of extraordinarily bright, who has won enemies, ascended.

shloka_text: स राक्षसगणैर्मुख्यैर्वृतोमन्दोदरीसुतः । निर्ययौनगरावदीरःकृतान्तबलचोदितः ।।6.91.11।।
explanation: Heroic son of Mandodari, impelled by the force of destiny, departed from the city surrounded by Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सोऽभिनिष्क्रम्यनगरादिन्द्रजित्परवीरहा । अभ्ययाज्ञवनैरश्वैर्लक्ष्मणंसविभीषणम् ।।6.91.12।।
explanation: Heroic in the act of destruction of enemies, Indarjith having started from the city in his chariot drawn by swift horses assailed Vibheeshana and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ततोरथस्थमालोक्यसौमत्रीरावणात्मजम् । वानराश्चमहावीर्याराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।।6.91.13।। विस्मयंपरमंजग्मुर्लाघवात्तस्यधीमतः ।
explanation: Seeing Indrajith seated in the chariot, great hero Lakshmana as well as the Vanaras and Vibheeshana wondered how easily he went and returned.

shloka_text: रावणिश्चापिसङ्क्रुद्धोरणेवानरयूथपान् ।।6.91.14।। पातयामासबाणौघैःशतशोऽथसहस्रशः ।
explanation: Indrajith, highly enraged, struck Vanara leaders with a volley of hundreds and thousands of arrows.

shloka_text: मण्डलीकृतधनूरावणिःसमतिञ्जयः ।।6.91.15।। हरीनभ्यहनत्कृद्धःपरंलाघवमास्थितः ।
explanation: Indrajith, a winner of combat, became highly furious and stretched his bow showing his skill easily struck at Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेवध्यमानाहरयोनाराचैर्भीमविक्रमैः ।।6.91.16।। सौमित्रिंशरणंप्राप्ताःप्रजापतिमिवप्रजाः ।
explanation: (The Vanaras), though endowed with prowess and of terrific courage, struck by the Rakshasa, they sought refuge of Lakshmana, their Lord, just as people seek the refuge of their Lord, the creator.

shloka_text: ततःसमरकोपेनज्वलितोरघुनन्दनः ।।6.91.17।। चिच्छेदकार्मुकंतस्यदर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम् ।
explanation: There, in the battlefield the delight of Raghus glowing with anger shattered the Rakshasas showing the skill of his hand s.

shloka_text: सोन्यऽत्कार्मुकम् मादायसज्जंचक्रेत्वरन्निव ।।6.91.18।। तदप्यस्यत्रिभिर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणोनिरकृन्तत ।
explanation: Indrajith seizing another bow hastily targeted at Lakshmana and Lakshmana split them with three arrows.

shloka_text: अथैवंछिन्नधन्वानमाशीविषविषोपमैः ।।6.91.19।। विव्याधोरसिसौमित्रीरावणिंपञ्चभिःशरैः ।
explanation: Then Saumithri pierced with five arrows into the chest of Indrajith like a venomous serpent and split the bow.

shloka_text: तेतस्यकायंनिर्भिद्यमहाकार्मुकनिस्सृताः ।।6.91.20।। निपेतुर्धरणींबाणारक्ताइवमहोरगाः ।
explanation: Those arrows released from the great bow of Lakshmana, entered the body of Indrajithand fell on the ground like a huge red serpent.

shloka_text: भिन्नवर्मारुधिरंवमन्वक्त्रेणरावणिः ।।6.91.21।। जग्राहकार्मुकश्रेष्ठंदृढज्यंबलवत्तरम् ।
explanation: Bow split, ejecting blood from mouth, Indrajith took his strong best of bows which had a stout string.

shloka_text: सःलक्ष्मणंसमुद्धिश्यपरंलाघवमाश्रितः ।।6.91.22।। ववर्षशरवर्षाणिवर्षाणीवपुरन्दरः ।
explanation: Indrajith, aiming at Lakshmana, let loose rain of arrows easily like rain.

shloka_text: मुक्तमिन्द्रजितातत्तुशरवर्षमरिन्दमः ।।6.91.23।। अवारयदसम्भ्रान्तोलक्ष्मणःसुदुरासदम् ।
explanation: Lakshmana, the tamer of enemies, without reacting intercepted the shower of arrows released by Indrajith which was difficult to resist.

shloka_text: संदर्शयामासतदारावणिंरघुनन्दनः ।।6.91.24।। असम्ब्रान्तोमहातेजेस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
explanation: Highly energetic Lakshmana, a delight of Raghus, unperturbed, demonstrated to Indrajith, which was a wonder indeed.

shloka_text: तस्तान् राक्षसान् सर्वांस्त्रिभिरेकैकमाहवे ।।6.91.25।। अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धश्शीघ्रास्त्रंसम्प्रदर्शयन् । राक्षसेन्द्रसुतंचापिबाणौघैस्समताडयत् ।।6.91.26।।
explanation: Then extremely angry Lakshmana pierced all the Rakshasas quickly, each one with three arrows and struck them and even the son of Rakshasa king, exhibiting his skills.

shloka_text: तस्तान् राक्षसान् सर्वांस्त्रिभिरेकैकमाहवे ।।6.91.25।। अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धश्शीघ्रास्त्रंसम्प्रदर्शयन् । राक्षसेन्द्रसुतंचापिबाणौघैस्समताडयत् ।।6.91.26।।
explanation: Then extremely angry Lakshmana pierced all the Rakshasas quickly, each one with three arrows and struck them and even the son of Rakshasa king, exhibiting his skills.

shloka_text: सोऽतिविद्धोबलवताशत्रुणाशत्रुघातिना । असक्तंप्रेषयामासलक्ष्मणायबहून् शरान् ।।6.91.27।।
explanation: Indrajith, who was grievously wounded by his hostile enemy, Lakshmana, the destroyer of hostile enemies, continuously discharged arrows at him.

shloka_text: तानप्राप्तान् शितैर्भाणैश्चिच्छेदपरवीरहा । सारथेरस्य च रणेरथिवोरघुसत्तमः ।।6.91.28।। शिरोजहारधर्मात्माभल्लेनानतपर्वणा ।
explanation: Heroic enemy, the righteous Lakshmana, tore the head of the carwarrior as well as the charioteer in the battle with bhala (spear), even before Indrajith discharged pointed arrows at him.

shloka_text: सूतास्तेहयास्तत्ररथमूहुरविक्लबाः ।।6.91.29।। मण्डलान्यभिधावन्तस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ।
explanation: There, though there was no charioteer, the horses went round in circles and as they went forward it was wonderful.

shloka_text: अमर्षवशमापन्नःसौमित्रिर्दृढविक्रमः ।।6.91.30।। प्रत्यविद्ध्यद्धयांस्तस्यशरैर्वित्रासयन् रणे ।
explanation: Saumithri of untiring valour, overcome with fury in the battle, struck the horses to scare them and destroyed them.

shloka_text: अमर्षमाणस्तत्कर्मरावणस्यसुतोबली ।।6.91.31।। विव्याथदशभिर्बाणैस्सौमित्रिंतममर्षणम् ।
explanation: Indrajith, unable to tolerate the action of Saumithri, was angry and struck him with ten arrows.

shloka_text: तेतस्यवज्रप्रतिमाःशरास्सर्पविषोपमाः ।।6.91.32।। विलयंजग्मुरागत्यकवचंकाञ्चनप्रभम् ।
explanation: His arrows, which resembled thunderbolts and were like venomous serpents, touching Lakshmana's shield shining like gold, broken, and fallen

shloka_text: अभ्येद्यकवचंमत्वालक्ष्मणंरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.33।। ललाटेलक्ष्मणंबाणैस्सुपुङ्खैस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित् । अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धःशीघ्रमस्त्रंप्रदर्शयन् ।।6.91.34।।
explanation: Ravana's son, knowing that it is not possible to break the shield of Lakshmana, quickly showed his weapon with three arrows with plumes and gems and struck him on the forehead.

shloka_text: अभ्येद्यकवचंमत्वालक्ष्मणंरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.33।। ललाटेलक्ष्मणंबाणैस्सुपुङ्खैस्त्रिभिरिन्द्रजित् । अविध्यत्परमक्रुद्धःशीघ्रमस्त्रंप्रदर्शयन् ।।6.91.34।।
explanation: Ravana's son, knowing that it is not possible to break the shield of Lakshmana, quickly showed his weapon with three arrows with plumes and gems and struck him on the forehead.

shloka_text: तैःपृषत्कैर्ललाटस्थैश्शुशुभेरघुनन्दनः । रणाग्रेसमरश्लाघीत्रिशृङ्गइवपर्वतः ।।6.91.35।।
explanation: Lakshmana, the delight of Raghus, who loved to fight, looked charming in the battlefield with three arrows stuck on his forehead looking like three mountain peaks.

shloka_text: स तथाह्यर्दितोबाणैराक्षसेनतदामृधे । तमाशुप्रतिविव्याधलक्ष्मणःपञ्चभिःशरैः ।।6.91.36।। विकृष्वेन्द्रजितोयुद्धेवदनेशुभकुण्डले ।
explanation: Then in the battle, pierced by Rakshasa in that manner, Laksmana immediately stretched his bow and struck with five arrows on the face of Indrajith, who was adorned with auspicious earrings.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौवीरौमहाबलशरासनौ ।।6.91.37।। अन्योन्यंजघ्नतुर्बाणैर्विशिखैर्मीविक्रमौ ।
explanation: Both heroes of extraordinary might and equipped with huge arms, endowed with terrific valour, Lakshmana and Indrajith struck one another with sharp arrows.

shloka_text: ततःशोणितदिग्धाङ्गौलक्ष्मणेन्दजितावुभौ ।।6.91.38।। रणेतौराजतुर्वीरौपुष्पिताविवकिंशुकौ ।
explanation: Then smeared with blood the two, Lakshmana and Indrajit, shone like fully blossomed Kimsuka in battle.

shloka_text: तौपरस्परमभ्येत्यसर्वगात्रेषुधवनिनौ ।।6.91.39।। घोरैर्विव्यधतुर्भाणैःकृतभावावुभौजये ।
explanation: Both wishing for victory, set to tear each other, pierced dreadful arrows on one another all over the limbs, opposing.

shloka_text: ततःसमरकोपेनसम्वृतोरावणात्मजः ।।6.91.40।। विभीषणंत्रिभिर्बाणैर्विव्याथवदनेशुभे ।
explanation: Then Ravana's son in his charming countenance, filled with wrath because of conflict, struck at Vibheeshana with three arrows.

shloka_text: अयोमुखैस्त्रिभिर्विद्ध्वाराक्षसेन्द्रंविभीषणम् ।।6.91.41।। एकैकेनाभिविव्याथतान्सर्वान् हरियूथपान् ।
explanation: Having struck Vibheeshana with three arrows, he struck again all the Vanara leaders with one arrow each.

shloka_text: तस्मैदृढतरंक्रुद्धोजघानगदयाहयान् ।।6.91.42।। विभीषणोमहातेजारावणेस्सदुरात्मनः ।
explanation: Brilliant Vibheeshana struck evil minded Indrajith, his horses and elephants with his mace.

shloka_text: पहताश्वादवाप्लुत्यरथान्निहतसारथे: ।।6.91.43।। रथशक्तिंमहातेजाःपितृव्यायमुमोच ह ।
explanation: Highly energetic Indrajith, leaping down from the chariot, horses destroyed, now hurled a javelin at his uncle in the chariot.

shloka_text: तामापततनींसम्प्रेक्ष्यसुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः ।।6.91.44।। चिच्छेदनिशितैर्बाणैर्धशथापातयद्भुवि ।
explanation: Observing the javelin coming towards him, Lakshmana, the delight of Raghus and enhancer of Sumithra's joy, split it into ten pieces, which had fallen on the ground.

shloka_text: तस्मैदृढतनुःक्रुद्धोहताश्वायविभीषणः ।।6.91.45।। वज्रस्पर्शसमान् पञ्चससर्जोरसिसायकान् ।
explanation: Vibheeshana of strong body, pierced five arrows like thunderbolt in impact into the chest of Indrajith.

shloka_text: तेतस्यकायंभित्वातुरुक्मपुङ्खानिमित्तगाः ।।6.91.46।। बभूवुर्लोहितादिग्धारक्ताइवमहोरगाः ।
explanation: The arrows with red feathers of Vibheeshana having penetrated the body of Indrajith, piercing into the body they became red coloured seemed like a red serpent.

shloka_text: सःपितृव्यस्यसङ्क्रुद्धःइन्द्रजिच्छरमाददे ।।6.91.47।। उत्तमंरक्षसांमध्येयमदत्तंमहाबलम् ।
explanation: Indrajith, angry with his uncle, staying in the midst of Rakshasas, seized a mighty strong best arrow gifted by Yama.

shloka_text: तंसमीक्ष्यमहातेजामहेषुंतेनसंहितम् ।।6.91.48।। लक्ष्मणोऽप्याददेबाणमद्यभदीमपराक्रमः ।
explanation: Extraordinarily brilliant and of terrific valour, Lakshmana, perceiving the mighty shaft yoked by him (by Indrajith), he took up another arrow.

shloka_text: कुबेरेणस्वयंस्वप्नेयद्दत्तममितात्मना ।।6.91.49।। दुर्जयंदुर्विषह्यं च सेन्द्रैरपिसुरासुरैः ।
explanation: That arrow was gifted to Lakshmana in dream by Kubera, the god of wealth and even Suras or Asuras cannot resist it and is difficult to win.

shloka_text: तयोस्तुधनुषीश्रेष्ठेबाहुभिःपरिघोपमैः ।।6.91.50।। विकृष्यमाणेबलवत् क्रौञ्चविवचुकूजतुः ।
explanation: Excellent bows of the two made noise like Krauncha birds while being drawn with great strength by the two, whose arms resembled iron bars.

shloka_text: ताभ्यांतुधनुषिश्रेष्ठेसंसितौसायकोत्तमौ ।।6.91.51।। विकृष्यमाणेवीराभ्यांभृशंजज्वलतुःश्रिया ।
explanation: The two best bows of both the heroes together, being powerful, shone with splendour when drawn with bowstring.

shloka_text: तौभासयन्तावाकाशंधनुर्भ्यांविशिखौच्युतौ ।।6.91.52।। मुखेनमुखमाहत्यसन्निपेततुरोजसा ।
explanation: Those arrows released from the bows lit the sky when their heads collided with each other and glowed by rubbing against each other.

shloka_text: सन्निपातस्तयोश्चासीच्छरयोर्घोररूपयोः ।।6.91.53।। सधूमविस्फुलिङ्गश्चतज्जोऽनगिर्दारुणोऽभवत् ।
explanation: By the impact of the two arrows brought together, a formidable form of fire frightening with smoke and sparks was created.

shloka_text: तौमहाग्रहसङ्काशावन्योन्यंसन्निपत्य च ।।6.91.54।। सङ्ग्रामेशतधायातौमेदिन्यांचैवपेततुः ।
explanation: In the battle both of them touching each other in conflict like the major planets flew into a hundred pieces and fell on earth.

shloka_text: शरौप्रतिहतौदृष्टवातावुभौरणमूर्धनि ।।6.91.55।। व्रीडितौजातरोषौ च लक्ष्मणेन्द्रजितौतदा ।
explanation: Then both Lakshmana and Indrajith in the face of the battle seeing their arrows in nought with each other were abashed and got agitated.

shloka_text: सुसंरर्ब्धस्तुसौमित्रिरस्त्रंवारुमाददे ।।6.91.56।। रौद्रंमहेन्द्रजिद्युद्धेऽप्यसृजद्युद्धनिष्ठितः ।
explanation: Enraged Saumithri, seizing the weapon of Varuna, skilled in warfare loosened on Indrajith (Mahendra's enemy), which was presided over by Rudra.

shloka_text: तेनतद्विहतंशस्त्रंवारुणंपरमाद्भुतम् ।।6.91.57।। ततःक्रुद्धोमहातेजाइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । आग्नेयंसन्दधेदीप्तं स लोकंसङ्क्षिपन्निव ।।6.91.58।।
explanation: Then the very wonderful weapon of Varuna was made ineffective by the highly energetic Indrajith's who used glowing fire missiles as if to destroy the whole world.

shloka_text: तेनतद्विहतंशस्त्रंवारुणंपरमाद्भुतम् ।।6.91.57।। ततःक्रुद्धोमहातेजाइन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । आग्नेयंसन्दधेदीप्तं स लोकंसङ्क्षिपन्निव ।।6.91.58।।
explanation: Then the very wonderful weapon of Varuna was made ineffective by the highly energetic Indrajith's who used glowing fire missiles as if to destroy the whole world.

shloka_text: सौरेणास्त्रणतवदीरोलक्ष्मणःपर्यवारयत् । अस्त्रंनिवारितंदृष्टवारावणिःक्रोथमूर्छितः ।।6.91.59।। आददेनिशितंबाणमासुरंशत्रुदारुणम् ।
explanation: Then Lakshmana used a Sun missile and repelled (Indrajith's fire missile). Seeing his missile obstructed, Indrajith deluded with anger used a sharp Asura missile capable of destroying the enemy.

shloka_text: तस्माच्चापाद्विनिष्पेतुर्भास्वराःकूटमुद्गराः ।।6.91.60।। शूलानि च मुशुण्ड्यश्चगदाःखङ्गा: परश्वथा: ।
explanation: By the Sun missile, the Kutamudgaras, tridents, Bhusundas, swords and axes issued forth from Indrajith's bow.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्टवालक्ष्मणःसङ्ख्येघोरमस्त्रंसुदारुणम् ।।6.91.61।। अवार्यंसर्वभूतानांसर्वशस्त्रविदारणम् । महेश्वरेणद्युतिमांस्तदस्त्रंप्रत्यवारयत् ।।6.91.62।।
explanation: Effulgent Lakshmana, seeing the terrible Asura missile and deliberating that it is capable of destroying all human beings and difficult to repel, used a Maheswara missile to divert.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्टवालक्ष्मणःसङ्ख्येघोरमस्त्रंसुदारुणम् ।।6.91.61।। अवार्यंसर्वभूतानांसर्वशस्त्रविदारणम् । महेश्वरेणद्युतिमांस्तदस्त्रंप्रत्यवारयत् ।।6.91.62।।
explanation: Effulgent Lakshmana, seeing the terrible Asura missile and deliberating that it is capable of destroying all human beings and difficult to repel, used a Maheswara missile to divert.

shloka_text: तयोःसमुतुलंयुद्धंसम्बभूवारोमहर्षणम् । गगनस्थानिभूतानिलक्ष्मणंपर्यवारयन् ।।6.91.63।।
explanation: The war between both was wonderful and horripulating. Beings from the sky saw Lakshmana diverting the Asura missile.

shloka_text: भैरवाभिरुतेभीमेयुद्धेवानरक्षसाम् । भूतैर्बहुभिराकाशंविस्मितैरावृतंबभौ ।।6.91.64।।
explanation: As the frightful war between Vanaras and Rakshasas went on, many beings surrounded in the sky were astonished and looked charming.

shloka_text: ऋषयःपितरोदेवागन्धर्वगरुडोरगाः । शतक्रतुंपुरस्कृत्यररक्षुर्लक्ष्मणंरणे ।।6.91.65।।
explanation: The Rsis, Devatas, manes, Gandharvas, Garudas, serpents and Indra who had performed hundred sacrifices, protected Lakshmana in war.

shloka_text: अथान्यंमार्गणश्रेष्ठंसन्दधेराघवानुजः । हुताशनसमस्पर्शंरावणात्मजदारणम् ।।6.91.66।।
explanation: And thereafter, Raghava's brother fitted another excellent arrow which had the impact of the touch of fire capable of tearing Indrajith.

shloka_text: सुपत्रमनुवृत्ताङ्गंसुपर्वाणंसुसंस्थितम् । सुवर्णविकृतंवीरश्शरीरान्तकरंशरम् ।।6.91.67।। दुरावारंदुर्विषहंराक्षसानांभयावहम् । आशीविषविषप्रख्यंदेवसङ्घैःसमर्चितम् ।।6.91.68।।
explanation: The arrow with lovely feathers, consisting of beautiful parts, skilfully done, well jointed, decked with gold, was not only difficult to put off but also difficult to bear, was capable of destroying enemies, frightful, resembling venomous serpents, and worshipped by gods.

shloka_text: सुपत्रमनुवृत्ताङ्गंसुपर्वाणंसुसंस्थितम् । सुवर्णविकृतंवीरश्शरीरान्तकरंशरम् ।।6.91.67।। दुरावारंदुर्विषहंराक्षसानांभयावहम् । आशीविषविषप्रख्यंदेवसङ्घैःसमर्चितम् ।।6.91.68।।
explanation: The arrow with lovely feathers, consisting of beautiful parts, skilfully done, well jointed, decked with gold, was not only difficult to put off but also difficult to bear, was capable of destroying enemies, frightful, resembling venomous serpents, and worshipped by gods.

shloka_text: येनशक्रोमहातेजादानवानजत्प्रभुः । पुरादेवासुरेयुद्धेवीर्यवान् हरिवाहनः ।।6.91.69।।
explanation: In the past at the war between Devas and Asuras, a mighty and energetic valiant Lord of Devas who had green horses conquered Danavas (with the same sword).

shloka_text: तदैन्द्रमस्त्रंसौमित्रिःसम्युगेष्वपराजितम् । शरश्रेष्ठंधनु: श्रेष्ठेविकर्षन्निदमिब्रवीत् ।।6.91.70।। लक्ष्मीवान् लक्ष्मणोवाक्यमर्थसाधकमात्मनः ।
explanation: Son of Saumithri, that prosperous Lakshmana, drawing Indra's missile, the foremost one, and also the best of arrows, which has never been defeated, spoke these words set to achieve the purpose.

shloka_text: धर्मात्मासत्यसन्धश्चरामोदाशरथिर्यति ।।6.91.71।। पौरुषेचाप्रतिद्वन्द्वःशरैनंजसिरावणिम् ।
explanation: "If Dasharatha's son, Sri Rama is righteous, truthful, of unrivalled valour and true to his promise this arrow will kill Indrajith."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वाबाणमाकर्णंविकृष्यतमजिह्मगम् ।।6.91.72।। लक्ष्मणःसमरेवीरःससर्जेन्द्रजितंप्रति ।
explanation: Having spoken that way, Lakshmana, heroic in battle, bending the bow, stretching the arrow till the ear released on Indrajith.

shloka_text: ऐन्द्रास्त्रेणसमायुज्यलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.91.73।। ततशिरःसशिरस्त्राणंश्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । प्रमथ्येन्द्रजितःकायात्पातयामासभूतले ।।6.91.74।।
explanation: Prosperous Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies, aiming at Indrajith's head shining with earrings belonging to the head severed from the body, it fell on ground.

shloka_text: ऐन्द्रास्त्रेणसमायुज्यलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.91.73।। ततशिरःसशिरस्त्राणंश्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । प्रमथ्येन्द्रजितःकायात्पातयामासभूतले ।।6.91.74।।
explanation: Prosperous Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies, aiming at Indrajith's head shining with earrings belonging to the head severed from the body, it fell on ground.

shloka_text: तद्राक्षसतनूजस्यभिन्नस्कन्धंशिरोमहत् । तपनीयनिभंभूमौददृशेरुधिरोक्षितम् ।।6.91.75।।
explanation: Trunk broken off, the huge head of Indrajith bathed in blood was seen on the earth shining like gold.

shloka_text: हतः स निपपाताथधरण्यांरावणात्मजः । कवचीसशिरस्त्राणोविद्धस्थशरासनः ।।6.91.76।।
explanation: Thereafter Indrajith with his shield, and helmet of the head broken was thrown on earth killed.

shloka_text: चुक्रुशुस्तेततःसर्वेवानराःसविभीषणाः । हृष्यन्तोनिहतेतस्मिन् देवावृत्रवधेयथा ।।6.91.77।।
explanation: Then Vibheeshana and all the Vanaras rejoiced just as Devas, when Vrtasura was killed.

shloka_text: अथान्तरिक्षेभूतानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम् । जज्ञेऽथजयसन्नादोगन्धर्वाप्सरसामपि ।।6.91.78।।
explanation: Then shouts of victory aroused from the heavens from the created beings of heaven, Rsis also, Gandharvas and Apsaras.

shloka_text: पतितंतमभिज्ञायराक्षसीसामहाचमूः । वध्यमानादिशोभेजेहरिभिर्जितकाशिभिः ।।6.91.79।।
explanation: Great army of Rakshasas even though desired to win seeing (Indrajith dead), Vanaras started attacking them. Unable to bear Rakshasas screamed.

shloka_text: वानरैर्वध्यमानास्तेशस्त्रानुत्सृज्यराक्षसाः । लङ्कामभिमुखास्सस्रुर्भ्रष्टसंज्ञाःप्रधाविताः ।।6.91.80।।
explanation: Those Rakshasas being killed by Vanaras, went running to Lanka leaving their weapons, with senses lost.

shloka_text: दुद्रुवुर्भहुधाभीताराक्षसाश्शतशोदिशः । त्यक्त्वाप्रहरणान्सर्वेपट्टसासिपरश्वधान् ।।6.91.81।।
explanation: All Rakshasas feared and panic stricken fled in hundreds, in groups in all directions leaving their sharpedged spears, swords, and axes.

shloka_text: केचिल्लङ्कांपरित्रस्ताःविष्टावानरार्दिताः । समुद्रेपतिताःकेचित्केचित्पर्वतमाश्रिताः ।।6.91.82।।
explanation: Pained by Vanaras, some fearful entered Lanka, few had fallen in the ocean and some sought refuge in the mountain.

shloka_text: हतमिन्द्रजितंदृष्टवाशयानं च रणक्षितौ । राक्षसानांसहस्रेषु न कश्चित्प्रत्यदृश्यत ।।6.91.83।।
explanation: Indrajith was lying, having fallen on the ground, and not even one of the thousands of Rakshasas was present there to see.

shloka_text: यथास्तङ्गतआदित्येनावतिष्ठन्तिरश्मयः । तथातस्मिन्निपतितेराक्षसास्तेगतादिशः ।।6.91.84।।
explanation: Just as Sun rays go away as soon as the Sun sets in the evening, the Rakshasas also went in all directions seeing Indrajith fallen.

shloka_text: शान्तरश्मिरिवादित्योनिर्वाणइवपावकः । बभूव स महाबाहुर्व्यपास्तगतजीवितः ।।6.91.85।।
explanation: Shorn of life, the broad shouldered Indrajith remained on the ground like the Sun whose rays have become cool, after death.

shloka_text: प्रशान्तपीडाबहुलोविनष्टारिःप्रहर्षवान् । बभूवलोकःपतितेराक्षसेन्द्रसुतोतदा ।।6.91.86।।
explanation: Then many were at peace and rejoiced in the world, being relieved, when Ravana's son dropped dead.

shloka_text: हर्षं च शक्रोभगवान् सहसर्वैर्महर्षिभिः । जगामनिहतेतस्मिन्राक्षसेपापकर्मणि ।।6.91.87।।
explanation: Glorious Rakshasa of sinful deeds having been killed, all including great sages and Indra felt rejoiced.

shloka_text: आकाशेचापिदेवानांशुश्रुवेदुन्दुभिस्वनः । नृत्यद्भिरप्सरोभिश्चगन्धर्वैश्चमहात्मभिः ।।6.91.88।।
explanation: In heaven also, sounds of drums of Gandharvas, great souls and dance of Apsaras were heard.

shloka_text: ववर्षुःपुष्पवर्षाणितदद्भुतमिवाभवत् । प्रशशंसुर्हतेतस्मिन्राक्षसेक्रूरकर्मणि ।।6.91.89।।
explanation: With cruel minded Rakshasa killed, celebrities showered rain of flowers praising the wonderful deed.

shloka_text: शुद्धाआपोनभश्चैवजहृषुर्देवदानवाः । आजग्मुःपतितेतस्मिन्सर्वलोकभयावहे ।।6.91.90।।
explanation: As the terror of all worlds had fallen and the water from the sky became pure, Devas and Danavas rejoiced and came there.

shloka_text: ऊचुश्चसहितास्तुष्टादेवगन्धर्वदानवाः । विज्वराश्शान्तकलुषाब्राह्मणाविचरन्त्विति ।।6.91.91।।
explanation: Devas, Danavas and Ghandharvas arrived there and said, "Let the Brahmins be without anxiety and move about without fear."

shloka_text: ततोऽभ्यनन्दन्सम्हृष्टास्समरेहरियूथपाः । तमप्रतिबलंदृष्टवाहतंनैरृतपुङ्गवम् ।।6.91.92।।
explanation: When, the best of Rakshasa, a leader of extraordinary prowess was killed, the Vanara army seeing Lakshmana felt happy and greeted him.

shloka_text: विभीषणोहनूमांश्चजाम्बवांश्चर्क्षयूथपः । विजयेनाभिनन्दन्तसुष्टुवुश्चापिलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.91.93।।
explanation: Vibheeshana and Hanuman, leader of Bears Jambavan praised Lakshmana and greeted him for his victory.

shloka_text: क्ष्वेळन्तश्चप्लवन्तश्चगर्जन्तश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । लब्दलक्षारघुसुतंपरिवार्योपतस्थिरे ।।6.91.94।।
explanation: Having accomplished their goal, monkeys roaring, playing, surrounded Lakshmana, and stood.

shloka_text: लाङ्गूलानिप्रविध्यन्तस्स्फोटयन्तश्चवानराः । लक्ष्मणोजयतीत्येवंवाक्यंविश्रावयंस्तदा ।।6.91.95।।
explanation: Then Vanaras wagging their tails and lashing them announced slogans saying," Lakshmana is winning."

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं च समालशिष्यहरयोहृष्टमानसाः । चक्रुरुच्चावगुणाराघवाश्रयसजा: कथा: ।।6.91.96।।
explanation: The monkeys feeling very happy embraced one another singing in praise of Lakshmana saying" Lakshmana has won"and stories related to Lakshmana

shloka_text: रुधिरक्लिन्नगात्रस्तुलक्ष्मणःशुभलक्षणः । बभूवहृष्टस्तंहत्वाशक्रजेतारमाहवे ।।6.92.1।।
explanation: Body having auspicious marks, smeared with blood, Lakshmana experienced the joy of having won Indra in battle.

shloka_text: ततःसजाम्बवन्तंचहनूमन्तंचवीर्यवान् । संनिपत्यमहातेजास्तांश्चसर्वान्वनौकसः ।।6.92.2।। आजगामततःशीघ्रंयत्रसुग्रीवराघवौ । विभीषणमवष्टभ्यहनूमन्तंचलक्ष्मणः ।।6.92.3।।
explanation: Then Valiant and mighty Lakshmana called Jambavantha, Hanumantha, all the Vanaras, following Vibheeshana and Hanuman quickly reached Sugriva and Raghava.

shloka_text: ततःसजाम्बवन्तंचहनूमन्तंचवीर्यवान् । संनिपत्यमहातेजास्तांश्चसर्वान्वनौकसः ।।6.92.2।। आजगामततःशीघ्रंयत्रसुग्रीवराघवौ । विभीषणमवष्टभ्यहनूमन्तंचलक्ष्मणः ।।6.92.3।।
explanation: Then Valiant and mighty Lakshmana called Jambavantha, Hanumantha, all the Vanaras, following Vibheeshana and Hanuman quickly reached Sugriva and Raghava.

shloka_text: ततोराममभिक्रम्यसौमित्रिरभिवाद्य च । तस्थौभ्रातृसमीपस्थःशक्रस्येन्द्रानुजोयथा ।।6.92.4।।
explanation: Thereafter Saumithri went close to Rama and offered prayers, like Indra's brother Upendra and stood close to his brother.

shloka_text: निष्टनन्निवचागत्यराघवायमहात्मने । आचचक्षेतदावीरोघोरमिन्द्रजितोवधम् ।।6.92.5।।
explanation: Then heroic Lakshmana coming close to the great selfRaghava, in shaking tone (being tired) reported" Indrajith is killed."

shloka_text: रावणेस्तुशिरश्छिन्नंलक्ष्मणेनमहात्मना । न्यवेदयतरामायतदाहृष्टोविभीषणः ।।6.92.6।।
explanation: Then Vibheeshana gladly informed Rama that Ravana's son's head had been severed by great Lakshmana.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैवतुमहावीर्योलक्षणनेन्द्रजिद्वधम् । प्रहर्षमतुलंलेभेवाक्यंचेदमुवाच ह ।।6.92.7।।
explanation: As soon as Lakshmana said that Indrajith was killed, Rama was very glad and immediately spoke as follows.

shloka_text: साधुलक्ष्मणतुष्टोऽस्मिकर्मचासुकरंकृतम् । रावणेर्हिविनाशेनजितमुत्यपधारय ।।6.92.8।।
explanation: "Well done, Lakshmana! I am glad. A difficult deed has been done. By the fall of Indrajith success has been achieved."

shloka_text: स तंशिरस्युपाघ्रायलक्ष्मणंकीर्तिवर्धनम् । लज्जमानंबलात्स्नेहादङ्गमारोप्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.92.9।। उपवेश्यतमुत्सङ्गेपरिष्वज्यावपीडितम् । भ्रातरंलक्ष्मणंस्निग्धंपुनःपुनरुदैक्षत ।।6.92.10।।
explanation: Bending the head of Lakshmana, a valiant one and enhancer of glory, who was shy of praising him, Rama lovingly, forcibly drawing him onto his lap and making him sit on examined again and again the wounded body and looked at him.

shloka_text: स तंशिरस्युपाघ्रायलक्ष्मणंकीर्तिवर्धनम् । लज्जमानंबलात्स्नेहादङ्गमारोप्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.92.9।। उपवेश्यतमुत्सङ्गेपरिष्वज्यावपीडितम् । भ्रातरंलक्ष्मणंस्निग्धंपुनःपुनरुदैक्षत ।।6.92.10।।
explanation: Bending the head of Lakshmana, a valiant one and enhancer of glory, who was shy of praising him, Rama lovingly, forcibly drawing him onto his lap and making him sit on examined again and again the wounded body and looked at him.

shloka_text: शल्यसंपीडितंशस्तंनिःश्वसन्तंतुंलक्ष्मणम् । रामस्तुदुःखसन्तप्तंतंतुनिःश्वासपीडितम् ।।6.92.11।। मूर्ध्निचैनमुपाघ्रायभूयःसंस्पृश्य च त्वरन् । उवाचलक्ष्मणंवाक्यमाश्वास्यपुरुषर्षभः ।।6.92.12।।
explanation: Lakshmana, a bull among men, body tormented by arrows, immersed in pain, breathing heavily. Rama stroking him, restoring his confidence, quickly spoke as follows.

shloka_text: शल्यसंपीडितंशस्तंनिःश्वसन्तंतुंलक्ष्मणम् । रामस्तुदुःखसन्तप्तंतंतुनिःश्वासपीडितम् ।।6.92.11।। मूर्ध्निचैनमुपाघ्रायभूयःसंस्पृश्य च त्वरन् । उवाचलक्ष्मणंवाक्यमाश्वास्यपुरुषर्षभः ।।6.92.12।।
explanation: Lakshmana, a bull among men, body tormented by arrows, immersed in pain, breathing heavily. Rama stroking him, restoring his confidence, quickly spoke as follows.

shloka_text: कृतंपरमकळ्याणंकर्मदुष्करकर्मणा । अद्यमन्येहतेपुत्रेरावणंनिहतंयुधि ।।6.92.13।।
explanation: "You have done an extremely beneficial task which is difficult for others to do. I think Ravana is killed in the battle with your action of killing Indrajith."

shloka_text: अद्याहंविजयीशत्रौहतेतस्मिन् दुरात्मनि । रावणस्यनृशंसस्यदिष्ट्यावीरत्वयारणे ।।6.92.14।। छिन्नोहिदक्षिणोबाहुः स हितस्यव्यपाश्रयः । विभीषणहनूमद्भ्यांकृतंकर्ममहद्रणे ।।6.92.15।।
explanation: 'Ravana was depending on Indrajith indeed. Now by that a great action of severing his right hand in comb at by Vibheeshana and Hanuman, I consider victorious.'

shloka_text: अद्याहंविजयीशत्रौहतेतस्मिन् दुरात्मनि । रावणस्यनृशंसस्यदिष्ट्यावीरत्वयारणे ।।6.92.14।। छिन्नोहिदक्षिणोबाहुः स हितस्यव्यपाश्रयः । विभीषणहनूमद्भ्यांकृतंकर्ममहद्रणे ।।6.92.15।।
explanation: 'Ravana was depending on Indrajith indeed. Now by that a great action of severing his right hand in comb at by Vibheeshana and Hanuman, I consider victorious.'

shloka_text: अहोरात्रैस्त्रिभिर्वीरःकथञ्चितवन्दिपातितः । विरमित्रःकृतोऽस्म्यद्यनिर्यास्यतिहिरावणः ।।6.92.16।। बलव्यूहेनमहताश्रुत्वापुत्त्रंनिपातितम् ।
explanation: 'Hero! In three days and nights indeed, you have made short of Indrajith. Hearing that Ravana's son has been made short of, Ravana will come now with large army troops.'

shloka_text: तंपुत्रवधसन्तप्तंनिर्यान्तंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.92.17।। बलेनावृत्यमहतानिहनिष्यामिदुर्जयम् ।
explanation: 'On hearing of his son's death, the Rakshasa Lord will come forth with a huge army. Turning towards him I will put an end to him.'

shloka_text: त्वयालक्ष्मणनाथेनसीता च पृथिवी च मे ।।6.92.18।। न दुष्प्रापाहतेतस्मिन् शक्रजेतरिचाहवे ।
explanation: Lakshmana, with you as my protector and Indra's enemy killed, neither Sita nor earth will be difficult to get back.

shloka_text: सतंभ्रातरमाश्वास्यपरिष्वज्य च राघवः ।।6.92.19।। रामःसुषेणंमुदितस्समाभाष्येदमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Rama, the celebrated scion of Raghu dynasty, restored the confidence of Lakshmana and embraced him happily. He invited Sushena and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: सशल्योऽयंमहाप्राज्ञस्सौमित्रिर्मित्रवत्सलः ।।6.92.20।। यथाभवतिसुस्वस्थस्तथात्वंसमुपाचर ।
explanation: "O very wise Sushena! Treat Saumithri in such a way that this Lakshmana, loved by friends pained by the arrows pierced, will be relieved."

shloka_text: विशल्यःक्रियतांक्षिप्रंसौमित्रिस्सविभीषणः ।।6.92.21।। ऋक्ष्वानरसैन्यानांशूराणांद्रुमयोधिनाम् । येचाप्यन्येऽत्रयुध्यन्तिसशल्याव्रणिनस्तथा ।।6.92.22।। तेऽपिसर्वेप्रयत्नेनक्रियन्तांसुखिनस्तथा ।
explanation: "Let Vibheeshana and Saumithri be treated quickly. Let all the army of Bears and others who fought with trees, and the heroes be treated. Let all others who fought in the battlefield and wounded be also healed by your effort and make them happy."

shloka_text: विशल्यःक्रियतांक्षिप्रंसौमित्रिस्सविभीषणः ।।6.92.21।। ऋक्ष्वानरसैन्यानांशूराणांद्रुमयोधिनाम् । येचाप्यन्येऽत्रयुध्यन्तिसशल्याव्रणिनस्तथा ।।6.92.22।। तेऽपिसर्वेप्रयत्नेनक्रियन्तांसुखिनस्तथा ।
explanation: "Let Vibheeshana and Saumithri be treated quickly. Let all the army of Bears and others who fought with trees, and the heroes be treated. Let all others who fought in the battlefield and wounded be also healed by your effort and make them happy."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणमहात्माहरियूथपः ।।6.92.23।। लक्ष्मणायदरौनस्तस्सुषेणःपरमौषधम् ।
explanation: Spoken by Rama in that manner, the great Vanara leader, Sushena gave supreme medicine to Lakshman through his nose.

shloka_text: स तस्यगन्धमाघ्रायविशल्यस्समपद्यत ।।6.92.24।। तदानिर्वेदनश्चैवसंरूढव्रणएव च ।
explanation: He then inhaled the fragrance and got freed from arrows, the pain of wounds and restored to normal state.

shloka_text: विभीषणमुखानां च सुहृदांराघवाज्नाया ।।6.92.25।। सर्ववानरमुख्यानांचिकित्सामकरोत्तदा ।
explanation: Then by Rama's order Vibheeshana and other friends and all Vanara leaders were healed.

shloka_text: ततःप्रकृतिमापन्नोहृतशल्योगतव्यथ: ।।6.92.26।। सौमित्रिर्मुदितस्तत्र क्षणेन विगतज्वरः ।
explanation: Then Saumithri, freed from arrows, relieved from pain, anguish gone in a moment, and naturally restored, was happy.

shloka_text: तदैवरामःप्लवगाधिपस्तथाविभीषणश्चर्क्षपतिश्चजाम्बवान् । आवेक्ष्यसौमित्रिमरोगमुथतितंमुदाससैन्यास्सुचिरंजहर्षिरे ।।6.92.27।।
explanation: At that time, Rama, also the monkey leader, and Vibheeshana, Jambavan with their army seeing Lakshmana getting up, free from wounds were full of joy.

shloka_text: ततःपौलस्त्यसचिवा्श्रुत्वाचेन्द्रजितोवधम् । आचचक्षुरभिज्ञायदशग्रीवायसव्यथा: ।।6.93.1।।
explanation: Then, having known about the distressing fall of Indrajith, the ministers of Ravana reported to the tenheaded Ravana.

shloka_text: युद्धेहतोमहाराजलक्ष्मणेनतवात्मजः । विभीषणसहायेनमिषतांनोमहाद्युतिः ।।6.93.2।।
explanation: "O King! Your glorious son was killed by Lakshmana with the assistance of Vibheeshana, as we were witnessing."

shloka_text: शूरंशूरेणसम्गम्यसम्युगेष्वपराजितः । लक्ष्मणेनहतश्शूरःपुत्रस्तेमहेन्द्रजित् ।।6.93.3।। गतस्सपरमान्लोकान्शरैस्सन्ताप्यलक्ष्मणम् ।
explanation: "Your son who has never been defeated in war, who won Indra, the ruler of gods, after fighting and fighting was killed by Lakshmana's arrows. He has ascended to the higher world."

shloka_text: स तंप्रतिभयंश्रुत्वावधंपुत्रस्यदारुणम् ।।6.93.4।। घोरमिन्द्रजितःसङ्ख्येकश्मलंप्राविशन्महत् ।
explanation: On hearing about the enumeration of his son Indrajith's dreadful, frightening and ghastly end, Ravana gave way to swoon.

shloka_text: उपलभ्यचिरात्संज्ञां राजाराक्षसपुङ्गव ।।6.93.5।। पुत्रशोकाकुलोदीनोविललापाकुलेन्द्रियः ।
explanation: Coming to senses after a long time, the Rakshasa king Ravana, dejected with sorrow of his son's death, lost senses, lamented.

shloka_text: हाराक्षसचमूमुख्यममवत्समहाबल ।।6.93.6।। जित्वेन्द्रंकथमद्यत्वंलक्ष्मणस्यवशंगतः ।
explanation: 'My son who was a chief of the Rakshasa army, a mighty one, who has won even Indra, how has he become a victim of Lakshmana'?

shloka_text: ननुत्वमिषुभिःक्रुद्धोभिन्द्याःकालान्तकावपि ।।6.93.7।। मन्दरस्यापिशृङ्गाणिकिंपुनर्लक्ष्मणंयुधि ।
explanation: 'When angry, you could pierce with arrows even the time spirit or peak of Mandara mountain, why to speak of Lakshmana again'?

shloka_text: अद्यवैनस्वतोराजाभूयोबहुमतोमम ।।6.93.8।। येनाद्यत्वंमहाबाहो संयुक्तःकालधर्मणा ।
explanation: 'O mighty armed! Today by virtue of time you have joined Yama and become esteemed King'.

shloka_text: एषपन्थाःसुयोधानांसर्वामरगणेष्वपि ।।6.93.9।। यःकृतेहन्यतेभर्तुस्सपुमान्स्वर्गमृच्छति ।
explanation: 'Killed in war for the cause of the king and treading the path of noble warriors, one attains the heaven. Even for a human it is desirable'.

shloka_text: अद्यदेवगणास्सर्वेलोकपालामहर्षयः ।।6.93.10।। हतमिन्द्रजितंदृष्टवासुखंस्वप्स्यन्तिनिर्भयाः ।
explanation: 'Today, seeing Indrajith killed, Devatas in heaven, guardians of the worlds, great sages would be fearless and be happy and comfortable'.

shloka_text: अद्यलोकास्त्रय: कृत्स्नापृथिवी च सकानना ।।6.93.11।। एकेनेन्द्रजिताहीनाशून्येवप्रतिभातिमे ।
explanation: Today without Indrajith alone the three worlds (earth, heaven, and underworld) including forests are desolate, dark, and lustreless to me.

shloka_text: अद्यनैरृतकन्यानांश्रोष्याम्यन्तःपुरेरवम् ।।6.93.12।। करेणुसङ्घस्ययथानिनादंगिरिगह्वरे ।
explanation: 'Today in the gynaecium we will hear the cries of Rakshasa maidens like the roaring of elephants in the cave'.

shloka_text: यौवराज्यं च लङ्कां च रक्षांसि च परन्तप ।।6.93.13।। मातरंमां च भार्याश्चक्वगतोऽसिविहायनः ।
explanation: 'O Scourge of enemies! You have left giving up prince regent, Rakshasas, from Lanka, your mother, me, and your wife also. And went. Why'?

shloka_text: ममनामत्वयावीरगतस्ययमसादनम् ।।6.93.14।। प्रेतकार्याणिकार्याणिविपरीतेहिवर्तसे ।
explanation: 'O hero! My obsequies should have been done by you. It is peculiar that I have to perform'.

shloka_text: स त्वंजीवतिसुग्रीवेलक्ष्मणेन च राघवे ।।6.93.15।। ममशल्यमनुद्धृत्यक्वगतोऽसिविहायनः ।
explanation: 'While Sugriva is living, Lakshmana and Raghava also, deserting me, you have gone. Where have you gone'?

shloka_text: एवमादिविलापार्तंरावणंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.93.16।। आविवेशमहान् कोपःपुत्रव्यसनसम्भवः ।
explanation: Distressed Ravana was lamenting in this way on account of his son deserting, as anger had taken over him.

shloka_text: प्रकृत्याकोपनंह्येनंपुत्रस्यपुनराधयः ।।6.93.17।। दीप्तंसन्दीपयामासुर्घर्मेऽर्कमिवरश्मयः ।
explanation: By nature, he is angry. Now with the loss of his son, he was glowing like the Sun that shines brighter by the rays in summer.

shloka_text: ललाटेभ्रुकुटीभिश्चसङ्गताभिर्व्यरोचत ।।6.93.18।। युगान्तेसहनक्रैस्तुमहोर्मिभिरिवोदधिः ।
explanation: Ravana's eyebrows contracted on his forehead, he shone like the waves in the great ocean with crocodiles at the time of dissolution of the universe.

shloka_text: कोपाद्विजृम्भमाणस्यवक्त्राद्व्यक्तमिवज्वलन् ।।6.93.19।। उत्पपातसधूमानगिर्वृत्रस्यवदनादिव ।
explanation: As Ravana yawned in anger, fire with smoke burst forth from his mouth like Vrtra'.

shloka_text: स पुत्रवधसन्तप्तश्शूरःक्रोधवशंगतः ।।6.93.20।। समीक्ष्यरावणोबुद्ध्यावैदेह्यारोचयद्वधम् ।
explanation: Pondering over the death of his asura son, Ravana was overtaken by fury, and reviwed thinking about the destruction of Vaidehi.

shloka_text: तस्यप्रकृत्यारक्ते च रक्तेक्रोथानगिनापि च ।।6.93.21।। रावणस्यमहाघोरेदीप्तेनेत्रेबभूवतुः ।
explanation: By nature, Ravana's eyes are red, through the fire of anger it was even more red glowing and very dreadful.

shloka_text: घोरंप्रकृत्यारूपंतत्तस्यक्रोधाग्निमूर्छितम् ।।6.93.22।। बभूवरूपंक्रुद्धस्यरुद्रस्येवदुरासदम् ।
explanation: His eyes are naturally dreadful, deluded with fire of anger his form was like Rudra's and threatening.

shloka_text: तस्यक्रुद्धस्यनेत्राभ्यांप्रापतन्नाश्रृबिन्दवः ।।6.93.23।। दीपाभ्यामिवदीप्ताभ्यांसार्चिषस्स्नेहबिन्दवः ।
explanation: Just as drops of oil drop from flaming lamps, tears dropped from his enraged flaming eyes.

shloka_text: दन्तावनिदशतस्तस्यश्रूयतेदशनस्वनः ।।6.93.24।। यन्त्रस्यावेष्ट्यमाणस्य महतो दानवैरिव ।
explanation: When he was biting on his teeth (enraged), the sound from his teeth resembled the sound of a grinder revolved round by Danavas.

shloka_text: कालानगिरिवसङ्क्रुद्धोयांयांदिशमवैक्षत ।।6.93.25।। तस्यांतस्यांभयत्रस्ताराक्षसास्सन्विलियलिरे ।
explanation: Fearing Ravana who was enraged like the time of universal destruction, the Rakshasashid themselves in the very quarter he was looking.

shloka_text: तमन्तकमिवक्रुद्धंचराचरचिखादिषुम् ।।6.93.26।। वीक्षमाणंदिशस्सर्वाराक्षसानोपचक्रमुः ।
explanation: The Rakshasas could not go near Ravana who was moving in anger in all directions like the moving and unmoving creations move when chased by the god of death.

shloka_text: ततःपरमसङ्क्रुद्धोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.93.27।। अब्रवीद्रक्षसांमध्येसंस्तम्भयिषुराहवे ।
explanation: To provoke Rakshasas for battle, an angry Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, spoke as follows.

shloka_text: मयावर्षसहस्राणिचरित्वापरमंतपः ।।6.93.28।। तेषुतेष्ववकाशेषुस्वयम्भूःपरितोषितः ।
explanation: 'I have done penance for thousands of years several times and am a pleased selfborn creator'.

shloka_text: तस्यैवतपसोव्युष्ट्याप्रसादाच्छस्वयम्भुवः ।।6.93.29।। नासुरेभ्यो न देवेभ्योभयंममकदाचन ।
explanation: 'By the power of the penancedone by me once, creator Brahma has given me reward, pleased with my penance. I have no fear of Asuras or Devas'.

shloka_text: कवचंब्रह्मदत्तंमेयदादित्यसमप्रभम् ।।6.93.30।। देवासुरविमर्धेषु न भिन्नंवज्रमुष्टिभिः ।
explanation: 'I was given a shield by Brahma, effulgent like the Sun which the Devas or Danavas could not break with their thunderbolt fists'.

shloka_text: तेनमामद्यसम्युक्तंरथस्थमिहसम्युगे ।।6.93.31।। प्रतीयात्कोऽद्यमामाजौसाक्षादपिपुरन्दरः ।
explanation: 'Today if I, with that shield mounted the chariot go for battle, who can dare to withstand me openly? Even Indra can't'.

shloka_text: त्तदातिप्रसन्नेनसशरंकार्मुकंमहत् ।।6.93.32।। देवासुरविमर्धेषुममदत्तंस्वयम्भुवा । अद्यतूर्यशतैर्भीमंधनुरुत्थाप्यतांमम ।।6.93.33।। रामलक्ष्मणयोरेववधायपरमाहवे ।
explanation: 'Let that supreme bow and the great arrows bestowed to me, by Brahma the creator who was pleased, when I fought in battle between Devas and Asuras, be brought to destroy Rama and Lakshmana today accompanied by hundreds of trumpets.'

shloka_text: त्तदातिप्रसन्नेनसशरंकार्मुकंमहत् ।।6.93.32।। देवासुरविमर्धेषुममदत्तंस्वयम्भुवा । अद्यतूर्यशतैर्भीमंधनुरुत्थाप्यतांमम ।।6.93.33।। रामलक्ष्मणयोरेववधायपरमाहवे ।
explanation: 'Let that supreme bow and the great arrows bestowed to me, by Brahma the creator who was pleased, when I fought in battle between Devas and Asuras, be brought to destroy Rama and Lakshmana today accompanied by hundreds of trumpets.'

shloka_text: स पुत्रवधसन्तप्तःक्रूरःक्रोधवशंगतः ।।6.93.34।। समीक्ष्यरावणोबुद्ध्यासीतांहन्तुंव्यवस्यत ।
explanation: Feeling very sad about the death of his son, cruel Ravana overpowered by anger went thinking to destroy Sita.

shloka_text: प्रत्यवेक्ष्यताम्राक्षस्सुघोरोघोरदर्शनः ।।6.93.35।। दीनोदीनस्वरान्सर्वांस्तानुवाचनिशाचरान् ।
explanation: Redeyed Ravana, looking dreadful with a frightening face, desperate, spoke in a low voice to all Rakshasas as follows.

shloka_text: माययाममवत्सेनवञ्चनार्थंवनौकसाम् ।।6.93.36।। किञ्चिदेवहतंतत्रसीतेयमितिदर्शितम् ।
explanation: 'My son showed the Vanaras there something which had been killed there to hoodwink as Sita."

shloka_text: तदिदंतथ्यमेवाहंकरिष्येप्रियमात्मनः ।।6.93.37।। वैदेहींनाशयिष्यामिक्षत्रबन्धुमनुव्रताम् । इत्येवमुक्त्वासचिवान्खङ्गमाशुपरामृशत् ।।6.93.38।।
explanation: "I myself will rejoice now in the same way (as Indarjith had done for cheating) making it true. I will destroy that lowly kshatriya, Rama's very dear Vaidehi". Having spoken like that to the ministers he took up the sword."

shloka_text: तदिदंतथ्यमेवाहंकरिष्येप्रियमात्मनः ।।6.93.37।। वैदेहींनाशयिष्यामिक्षत्रबन्धुमनुव्रताम् । इत्येवमुक्त्वासचिवान्खङ्गमाशुपरामृशत् ।।6.93.38।।
explanation: "I myself will rejoice now in the same way (as Indarjith had done for cheating) making it true. I will destroy that lowly kshatriya, Rama's very dear Vaidehi". Having spoken like that to the ministers he took up the sword."

shloka_text: उत्प्लुत्यगुणसम्पन्नंविमलाम्बरवर्चसम् । निष्पपात स वेगेनसभार्यःसचिवैर्वृतः ।।6.93.39।। रावणःपुत्रशोकेनभृशमाकुलचेतनः । सङ्क्रुद्धःखडगमादायसहसायत्रमैथिली ।।6.93.40।।
explanation: In a totally confused state on account of the death of his son, he went to Mythili taking the excellent sword, which was shining resembling pure sky, feeling enraged, accompanied by his wife, and surrounded by the ministers.

shloka_text: उत्प्लुत्यगुणसम्पन्नंविमलाम्बरवर्चसम् । निष्पपात स वेगेनसभार्यःसचिवैर्वृतः ।।6.93.39।। रावणःपुत्रशोकेनभृशमाकुलचेतनः । सङ्क्रुद्धःखडगमादायसहसायत्रमैथिली ।।6.93.40।।
explanation: In a totally confused state on account of the death of his son, he went to Mythili taking the excellent sword, which was shining resembling pure sky, feeling enraged, accompanied by his wife, and surrounded by the ministers.

shloka_text: व्रजन्तंराक्षसंप्रेक्ष्यसिंहनादंविचक्रुशुः । ऊचुश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्ग्यसङ्क्रुद्धंप्रेक्ष्यराक्षसम् ।।6.93.41।।
explanation: ( As Ravana marched) the Rakshasas in the abode roared like a lion seeing enraged Ravana and embraced each other (thinking of Ravana's victory) and spoke to one another.

shloka_text: अद्यैनंतावुभौदृष्टवाभ्रातरौप्रव्यधिष्यतः । लोकपालाहिचत्वारःक्रुद्धेनानेनतर्जिताः ।।6.93.42।। बहवःशत्रवश्चान्येसम्युगेष्वभिपातिताः ।
explanation: "Seeing Ravana, the two brothers will tremble. By Ravana's fury all the four rulers of the world (Indra, Yama, Varuna, Kubera), would have disappeared. He has struck down many other enemies in wars."

shloka_text: त्रिषुलोकेषुरत्नानिभुङक्तेचाहृत्यरावणः ।।6.93.43।। विक्रमे च बलेचैवनास्त्यस्यसदृशोभुवि ।
explanation: "Ravana has collected gems from the three worlds as tax. There is none equal to him in might and prowess in this world."

shloka_text: तेषांसञ्जल्पमानामशोकवनिकांगताम् ।।6.93.44।। अभिदुद्राववैदेहींरावणःक्रोधमूर्छितः ।
explanation: As the Rakshasas were talking in that manner, Ravana, deluded with anger, went fast to Vaidehi in Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: वार्यमाणःसुसङ्क्रुद्धःसुहृद्भिर्हितबुद्धिभिः ।।6.93.45।। अभ्यधावतसङ्क्रुद्धःखेग्रहोरोहिणीमिव ।
explanation: Highly enraged Ravana, darted just as planet Mars rushed to Rohini in the sky, even while his wellwishers were obstructing.

shloka_text: मैथिलीरक्ष्यमाणातुराक्षसीरनिन्दिता ।।6.93.46।। ददर्शराक्षसंक्रुद्धंनिस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम् । तंनिशाम्यसविस्त्रिंशंव्यथिताजनकात्मजा ।।6.93.47।। निवार्यमाणंबहुशःसुहृद्भिरनिवर्तिनम् ।
explanation: While irreproachable Mythili was being guarded by rakshasi women, she saw him bearing an excellent sword and crossing. When he was repeatedly stopped by friends and obstructed, he was not receding and reaching Janaka's daughter.

shloka_text: मैथिलीरक्ष्यमाणातुराक्षसीरनिन्दिता ।।6.93.46।। ददर्शराक्षसंक्रुद्धंनिस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम् । तंनिशाम्यसविस्त्रिंशंव्यथिताजनकात्मजा ।।6.93.47।। निवार्यमाणंबहुशःसुहृद्भिरनिवर्तिनम् ।
explanation: While irreproachable Mythili was being guarded by rakshasi women, she saw him bearing an excellent sword and crossing. When he was repeatedly stopped by friends and obstructed, he was not receding and reaching Janaka's daughter.

shloka_text: सीतादुःखसमाविष्टाविलपन्तीदमब्रवीत् ।।6.93.48।। यथायंमामभिक्रुद्धःसमभिद्रवतिस्वयम् । वधिष्यतिसनाथांमामनाथामिवदुर्मतिः ।।6.93.49।।
explanation: Thus spoke Sita filled with sorrow crying," This evil minded angry one is coming to me to kill me as though I am an orphan even though I have a protector."

shloka_text: सीतादुःखसमाविष्टाविलपन्तीदमब्रवीत् ।।6.93.48।। यथायंमामभिक्रुद्धःसमभिद्रवतिस्वयम् । वधिष्यतिसनाथांमामनाथामिवदुर्मतिः ।।6.93.49।।
explanation: Thus spoke Sita filled with sorrow crying," This evil minded angry one is coming to me to kill me as though I am an orphan even though I have a protector."

shloka_text: बहुशश्चोदयामासभर्तारंमामनुव्रताम् । भार्याभवरमस्वेतिप्रत्याख्यातोध्रुवंमया ।।6.93.50।। सोऽयंमामनुपस्थानेव्यक्तंनैराश्यमागतः । क्रोधमोहसमाविष्टोनिहन्तुंमांसमुद्यतः ।।6.93.51।।
explanation: 'I who am devoted to my husband and this Ravana wanted me to revel with him. He has been entreated by me several times. Surely, he, having been rejected by me is dejected, filled with anger and infatuation, intends to kill me, is evident'.

shloka_text: बहुशश्चोदयामासभर्तारंमामनुव्रताम् । भार्याभवरमस्वेतिप्रत्याख्यातोध्रुवंमया ।।6.93.50।। सोऽयंमामनुपस्थानेव्यक्तंनैराश्यमागतः । क्रोधमोहसमाविष्टोनिहन्तुंमांसमुद्यतः ।।6.93.51।।
explanation: 'I who am devoted to my husband and this Ravana wanted me to revel with him. He has been entreated by me several times. Surely, he, having been rejected by me is dejected, filled with anger and infatuation, intends to kill me, is evident'.

shloka_text: अथवातौनरव्याघ्रौभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । मन्निमित्तमनार्येणसमरेऽद्यनिपातितौ ।।6.93.52।।
explanation: 'Or else, have the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana fallen to unworthy Ravana on my account'?

shloka_text: भैरवोहिमहान्नादोराक्षसानांश्रुतोमया । बहूनामिहहृष्टानांतथाविक्रोशतांप्रियम् ।।6.93.53।।
explanation: Many Rakshasas rejoiced, calling out their loved ones loudly, making huge noise, were heard.

shloka_text: अहोधिङ्मन्निमित्तोऽयंविनाशोराजपुत्रयोः । अथवापुत्रशोकेनअहत्यारामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.93.54।। विधमिष्यतिमांरौद्रोराक्षसःपापनिश्चयः ।
explanation: Wow! Has the destruction of the two brothers brought about on account of the grief of the death of his son or on my account? Not able to kill Rama and Lakshmana, has this fierce Rakshasa who does not hesitate, resolved to kill me?

shloka_text: हनूमतस्तुतद्वाक्यं न कृतंक्षुद्रयामया ।।6.93.55।। यद्यहंतस्यपृष्ठेवतदायासमनिर्जिता । नाद्यैवमनुशोचेयंभर्तुरङ्कगतासती ।।6.93.56।।
explanation: 'I am a foolish woman. I did not follow Hanuman's advice and had I left mounted on his back, no doubt I would be on my husband 's lap. I did not think in this way'.

shloka_text: हनूमतस्तुतद्वाक्यं न कृतंक्षुद्रयामया ।।6.93.55।। यद्यहंतस्यपृष्ठेवतदायासमनिर्जिता । नाद्यैवमनुशोचेयंभर्तुरङ्कगतासती ।।6.93.56।।
explanation: 'I am a foolish woman. I did not follow Hanuman's advice and had I left mounted on his back, no doubt I would be on my husband 's lap. I did not think in this way'.

shloka_text: मन्येतुहृदयंतस्याःकौसल्यायाःफलिष्यति । एकपुत्रायदापुत्रंविनष्टंश्रोष्यतेयुधि ।।6.93.57।।
explanation: 'Kausalya will think her only son has been killed in the battle. I think her heart would break'.

shloka_text: साहिजन्म च बाल्यं च यौवनं च महात्मनः । धर्मकार्याणिरूपं च रुदतीसंस्मरिष्यति ।।6.93.58।।
explanation: 'She will be crying and keep remembering his birth, childhood, youth, and his rightful actions, and his charm'.

shloka_text: निराशानिहतेपुत्रेदत्त्वाश्राद्धमचेतना । अग्निमावेक्ष्यतेनूनमापोवापिप्रवेक्ष्यति ।।6.93.59।।
explanation: 'Son killed, Kausalya will be disappointed, lost sentience will be offering obsequies, surely and enter fire or water and drown'.

shloka_text: धिगस्तुकुब्जामसतींमन्थरांपापनिश्चयाम् । यन्निमित्तमिमंशोकंकौसल्याप्रतिपत्स्यते ।।6.93.60।।
explanation: 'Because of the sinful resolve of hunch back Mandara, this grief has come to Kausalya surely. Let her be burnt'.

shloka_text: इत्येवंमैथिलींदृष्टवाविलपन्तींतपस्विनीम् । रोहिणीमिवचन्द्रेणविनाग्रहवशंगताम् ।।6.93.61।। एतस्मिन्नन्तरेतस्यअमात्यःशीलवान् शुचिः । सुपार्श्वोनाममेधावीरावणंरक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.93.62।। निवार्यमाणःसचिवैरिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Seeing Mythili in this manner grieving, just as Rohini fell under the sway of the Mars planet in the absence of the moon, being away from her husband, Suparsva, an upright minister of Ravana who was pure and wise spoke these words of advice to the Lord of Rakshasas in spite of other ministers trying to stop him.

shloka_text: इत्येवंमैथिलींदृष्टवाविलपन्तींतपस्विनीम् । रोहिणीमिवचन्द्रेणविनाग्रहवशंगताम् ।।6.93.61।। एतस्मिन्नन्तरेतस्यअमात्यःशीलवान् शुचिः । सुपार्श्वोनाममेधावीरावणंरक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.93.62।। निवार्यमाणःसचिवैरिदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Seeing Mythili in this manner grieving, just as Rohini fell under the sway of the Mars planet in the absence of the moon, being away from her husband, Suparsva, an upright minister of Ravana who was pure and wise spoke these words of advice to the Lord of Rakshasas in spite of other ministers trying to stop him.

shloka_text: कथंनामदशग्रीव साक्षद्वैश्रवणानुज ।।6.93.63।। हन्तुमिच्छसिवैदेहींक्रोधाद्धर्ममपास्य च ।
explanation: "You being the direct brother of Kubera (one of the guardians of the world), ten head Lord desires to seek Vaidehi in fury and kill her casting righteousness?"

shloka_text: वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातःस्वकर्मनिरतस्तथा ।।6.93.64।। स्त्रियःकस्माद्वधंवीरमन्यसेराक्षसेश्वर ।
explanation: "O Hero! Lord of Rakshasas! You made a vow of celibacy essential for Vedic study, so also engaged in your obligatory duties. Do you think of killing a woman?"

shloka_text: मैथिलींरूपसम्पन्नांप्रत्यवेक्षस्वपार्थिव ।।6.93.65।। तस्मिन्नेवसहास्माभिराहेवक्रोधमुत्सृज ।
explanation: "O King! Mythili is endowed with charm. Your anger may be exhibited on Rama in battle (not Sita)'."

shloka_text: अभ्युत्थानंत्वमद्यैवकृष्णपक्षचतुर्धशीम् ।।6.93.66।। कृत्वानिर्याह्यमावास्यांविजयायबलैर्वृतः ।
explanation: "Today being the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, start on the next day that is the fifteenth dark day surrounded by the army and win."

shloka_text: शूरःधीमान् रथीखडगीरथप्रवमास्थितः ।।6.93.67।। हत्वादाशरथिंरामंभवान् प्राप्स्यसिमैथिलीम् ।
explanation: "Shrewd carwarrior, you are wise. Seated in the foremost chariot with your sword, kill Dasharatha's son and attain Sita."

shloka_text: स प्रविश्यसभांराजादीनःपरमदुःखितः । निषपादासनेमुख्येसिंहःक्रुद्धइवश्वसन् ।।6.94.1।।
explanation: Ravana, the king entered the council, angry like a lion, looking piteous, very sad and sat on the seat.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च स तान्सर्वान् बलमुख्यान् महाबलः । रावणःप्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंपुत्रव्यसनकर्शितः ।।6.94.2।।
explanation: Ravana, endowed with mighty prowess, shrunken on account of his son, greeting all the army chiefs with folded hands spoke as follows.

shloka_text: सर्वेभवन्तस्सर्वेणहस्त्यश्वेनसमावृताः । निर्यान्तुरथसङ्घैश्चपादातैश्चोपशोभिताः ।।6.94.3।।
explanation: All of you, accompanied by all your elephants and horses, set forth, splendidly equipped with throngs of chariots and foot-soldiers.

shloka_text: एकंरामंपरिक्षिप्यसमरेहन्तुमर्हथ । वर्षन्तश्शरवर्षाणिप्रावृट् कालइवाम्बुदाः ।।6.94.4।।
explanation: Surrounding the single Rama in battle, you should kill him, showering down volleys of arrows like clouds in the rainy season.

shloka_text: अथवाहंशरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भिन्नगात्रंमहाहवे । भवद्भिःश्वोनिहन्तास्मिरामंलोकस्यपश्यतः ।।6.94.5।।
explanation: "I shall kill him with huge sharp arrows as the world looks at Rama, once his limbs are struck by you."

shloka_text: इत्येतद्वाक्यमादायरक्षसेन्द्रस्यराक्षसाः । निर्ययुस्तेरथैःशीघ्रैर्नानानीकैश्चसंयुताः ।।6.94.6।।
explanation: On Rakshasa king speaking like that, all the diverse battalions together departed swiftly on chariots.

shloka_text: परिघान् पट्टसांश्चैवशरखङ्गपरश्वधान् । शरीरान्तकरान् सर्वेचिक्षिपुर्वानरान् प्रति ।।6.94.7।। वानराश्चद्रुमान्शैलान्राक्षसान्प्रतिचिक्षिपुः ।
explanation: All the Rakshasas threw at the Vanaras iron bars, clubs, axes, swords, and arrows, which were capable of destroying the life. Vanaras also attacked Rakshasas with trees and rocks.

shloka_text: स सङ्ग्रामोमहाभीमस्सूर्यस्यदयनंप्रति ।।6.94.8।। रक्षसांवानराणां च तुमुलस्समपद्यत ।
explanation: By the time of sunrise, the most terrific war started between Vanaras and Rakshasas, which became tumultuous.

shloka_text: तेगदाभिश्चचित्राभिःप्रासैःखडगैःपरश्वधैः ।।6.94.9।। अन्योन्यंसमरेजघ्नुस्तदावानरराक्षसाः ।
explanation: The Vanaras and Rakshasas attacked one another with wonderful maces, darts, swords, and axes in war.

shloka_text: एवंप्रवृत्तेसङ्ग्रामेह्यद्भुतंसुमहद्रजः ।।6.94.10।। रक्षसांवानराणां च शान्तंशोणितविस्रवैः ।
explanation: As the war was in progress, wonderful dust had risen which subsided by the flow of blood of Vanaras and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: मातङ्गरथकूलाश्चवाजिमत्सास्यध्वजद्रुमाः ।।6.94.11।। शरीरसङ्घाटवहाःप्रसस्रुःशोणितापगाः ।
explanation: There with rivers of blood flowing, elephants and chariots were like banks, horses were like fish, staff of chariots like trees and dead bodies as logs of wood seemed.

shloka_text: ततस्तेवानराःसर्वेशोणितौघपरिप्लुताः ।।6.94.12।। ध्वजवर्मरथानश्वान्नानाप्रहरणानि च । आप्लुत्याप्लुत्यसमरेवानरेन्द्राबभञ्चिरे ।।6.94.13।।
explanation: Leaping and jumping the Vanaras and also the leaders of Vanaras bathed in blood broke all kinds of weapons, staff of chariots and the horses.

shloka_text: ततस्तेवानराःसर्वेशोणितौघपरिप्लुताः ।।6.94.12।। ध्वजवर्मरथानश्वान्नानाप्रहरणानि च । आप्लुत्याप्लुत्यसमरेवानरेन्द्राबभञ्चिरे ।।6.94.13।।
explanation: Leaping and jumping the Vanaras and also the leaders of Vanaras bathed in blood broke all kinds of weapons, staff of chariots and the horses.

shloka_text: केशान् कर्णललाटं च नासिकाश्चप्लवङ्गमाः । रक्षसांदशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नखैश्चापिव्यकर्तयन् ।।6.94.14।।
explanation: The monkeys with their sharp teeth and nails tore off the hair, ears, noses, and forehead of the Rakshasas,

shloka_text: एकैकंराक्षसंसङ्ख्येशतंवानरपुङ्गवाः । अभ्यधावन्तफलिनंवृक्षंशकुनयोयथा ।।6.94.15।।
explanation: Just as trees laden with fruits are attacked by birds, each one of the Rakshasas was attacked by hundreds of Vanaras.

shloka_text: तदागदाभिर्गुर्वीभिःप्रासैःखडगैःपरश्वधैः । निर्जघ्नुर्वानरान्घोरान्राक्षसाःपर्वतोपमाः ।।6.94.16।।
explanation: Then the mountainlike forms of Rakshasas attacked the Vanaras with heavy maces, darts, swords, and axes in frightening ways.

shloka_text: राक्षसैर्वध्यमानानांवानराणांमहाचमूः । शरण्यंशरणंयातारामंदशरथात्मजम् ।।6.94.17।।
explanation: The Vanaras being struck by Rakshasas sought the protection of Rama, the son of Dasharatha.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजाधनुरादायवीर्यवान् । प्रविश्यराक्षसंसैन्यंशरवर्षंववर्ष ह ।।6.94.18।।
explanation: Then, the highly energetic and valiant Rama, taking up the bow showered rain of arrows on Rakshasa army.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टंतुतदारामंमेघास्सूर्यमिवाम्बरे । नाथिजग्मुर्महाघोरानिर्दहन्तंशराग्निना ।।6.94.19।।
explanation: Then Rama entered the army with fire like arrows which were consuming the Rakshasas like the clouds in the sky which can't approach the scorching Sun.

shloka_text: कृतान्येवसुघोराणिरामेणरजनीचराः । ददृशुस्ते न वैरामंकर्माण्यसुकराणिते ।।6.94.20।।
explanation: The night rangers were able to see Rama's terrible action which was difficult for others only after he had performed not otherwise (as they could not see his quick movement).

shloka_text: चालयन्तंमहासैन्यंविधमन्तंमहारथान् । ददृशुस्ते न वैरामंवातंवनगतंयथा ।।6.94.21।।
explanation: They could not see Rama while he was moving and breaking huge chariots as one would not be able to see the trees in the forest when the wind blew fast.

shloka_text: छिन्नंभिन्नंशरैर्दग्धंप्रभन्नंशस्त्रपीडितम् । बलंरामेणददृशुर्नरामंशीघ्रकारिणम् ।।6.94.22।।
explanation: They saw the army shattered, broken into pieces, tormented with darts by Rama but could not make out Rama who was very fast in action.

shloka_text: प्रहरन्तंशरीरेषु न तेपश्यन्तिराघवम् । इन्द्रियार्थेषुतिष्ठन्तंभूतात्मानमिवप्रजाः ।।6.94.23।।
explanation: Just as created beings experience their senses and do not perceive their soul, the army experienced the hitting of Raghava by their senses but were not able to perceive him who was hitting them.

shloka_text: एषहन्तिगजानीकमेषहन्तिमहारथान् । एषहन्तिशरैस्तीक्ष्णैःपदातीस्वाजिभिःसह ।।6.94.24।। इतितेराक्षसास्सर्वेरामस्यसदृशान्रणे । अन्योन्यंकुपिताजघ्नुस्सादृश्याद्राघवस्यते ।।6.94.25।।
explanation: 'Rama is here killing elephants', 'Here is Rama destroying chariot warriors', 'Rama is killing horses, foot soldiers with sharp arrows', saying like that, the Rakshasas were striking one another in the battle. Being there where Rama was, they were mistaking one another for Rama there because of the socalled resemblance and attacking one another.

shloka_text: एषहन्तिगजानीकमेषहन्तिमहारथान् । एषहन्तिशरैस्तीक्ष्णैःपदातीस्वाजिभिःसह ।।6.94.24।। इतितेराक्षसास्सर्वेरामस्यसदृशान्रणे । अन्योन्यंकुपिताजघ्नुस्सादृश्याद्राघवस्यते ।।6.94.25।।
explanation: 'Rama is here killing elephants', 'Here is Rama destroying chariot warriors', 'Rama is killing horses, foot soldiers with sharp arrows', saying like that, the Rakshasas were striking one another in the battle. Being there where Rama was, they were mistaking one another for Rama there because of the socalled resemblance and attacking one another.

shloka_text: न तेददृशिरेरामंदहन्तमपिवाहिनीम् । मोहिताःपरमास्त्रणगान्धर्वेणमहात्मना ।।6.94.26।।
explanation: The Rakshasas got confused by the supreme missile presided over by Gandharvas, released by Rama, which was burning their army, and were not able to see.

shloka_text: तेतुरामसहस्राणिरणेपश्यन्तिराक्षसाः । पुनःपश्यन्तिकाकुत्स्थमेकमेवमहाहवे ।।6.94.27।।
explanation: In the battle those Rakshasas could see a thousand Ramas at one place and again one Rama alone at another place

shloka_text: भ्रमन्तीकाञ्चनींकोटिंकार्मुकस्यमहात्मनः । अलातचक्रप्रतिमांददृशुस्ते न राघवम् ।।6.94.28।।
explanation: While Rama was going around in circles with his bow, the Rakshasas were confused, and saw the golden ends of the bow to be like a burning fire stick circling and could not see Rama.

shloka_text: शरीरनाभिसत्त्वार्चिश्शरारंनेमिकार्मुकम् । ज्याघोषतलनिर्घोषंतेजोबुधदिगुणप्रभम् ।।6.94.29।। दिव्यास्त्रगुणपर्यन्तंनिघ्नन्तंयुधिराक्षसान् । ददृशूरामचक्रंतत्कालचक्रमिवप्रजाः ।।6.94.30।।
explanation: People saw Rama in the form of wheel exterminating the Rakshasas on the battlefield, which had the body of Sri Rama as its navel, his strength as its glow, the arrows as spokes, his bow as belly, the twangling of the bowstring as its sound, his virtues and effulgence as the power of his mystic missiles in war. Rama was seen as a wheel of time spirit by the people.

shloka_text: शरीरनाभिसत्त्वार्चिश्शरारंनेमिकार्मुकम् । ज्याघोषतलनिर्घोषंतेजोबुधदिगुणप्रभम् ।।6.94.29।। दिव्यास्त्रगुणपर्यन्तंनिघ्नन्तंयुधिराक्षसान् । ददृशूरामचक्रंतत्कालचक्रमिवप्रजाः ।।6.94.30।।
explanation: People saw Rama in the form of wheel exterminating the Rakshasas on the battlefield, which had the body of Sri Rama as its navel, his strength as its glow, the arrows as spokes, his bow as belly, the twangling of the bowstring as its sound, his virtues and effulgence as the power of his mystic missiles in war. Rama was seen as a wheel of time spirit by the people.

shloka_text: अनीकंदशसाहस्रंरथानांवातरम्हसाम् । अष्टादशसहस्राणिकुञ्जराणांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.94.31।। चतुर्दशसहस्राणिसारोहाणां च वाजिनाम् । पूर्णेशतसहस्रेद्वेराक्षसानांपदातिनाम् ।।6.94.32।। दिवसस्याष्टभागेनशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः । हतात्यान्येकेनरामेणरक्षसांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.94.33।।
explanation: In the eighth part of the day, in the battlefield, an army of Rakshasas who were capable of changing their forms at will, constituting a myriad of chariots with wind speed, eighteen thousand fleetfooted elephants, fourteen thousand horses with riders, two lakh Rakshasas fighting on foot exterminated by Rama singlehanded with his arrows that resembled tongues of fire.

shloka_text: अनीकंदशसाहस्रंरथानांवातरम्हसाम् । अष्टादशसहस्राणिकुञ्जराणांतरस्विनाम् ।।6.94.31।। चतुर्दशसहस्राणिसारोहाणां च वाजिनाम् । पूर्णेशतसहस्रेद्वेराक्षसानांपदातिनाम् ।।6.94.32।। दिवसस्याष्टभागेनशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः । हतात्यान्येकेनरामेणरक्षसांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.94.33।।
explanation: In the eighth part of the day, in the battlefield, an army of Rakshasas who were capable of changing their forms at will, constituting a myriad of chariots with wind speed, eighteen thousand fleetfooted elephants, fourteen thousand horses with riders, two lakh Rakshasas fighting on foot exterminated by Rama singlehanded with his arrows that resembled tongues of fire.

shloka_text: तेहताश्वाहतरथाश्शान्ताविमथितध्वजाः । अभिपेतुःपुरींलङ्कांहतशेषानिशाचराः ।।6.94.34।।
explanation: Rakshasas dead, chariots destroyed, staff of chariots broken, remaining Rakshasas returned to Lanka.

shloka_text: हतैर्गजपदात्यश्वैस्तद्बभूवरणाजिरम् । अक्रीडभूमिःक्रुद्धस्यरुद्रस्येवमहात्मनः ।।6.94.35।।
explanation: With the elephants, horses, and foot soldiers killed, the battlefield was like the ground where mighty Rudra sported in anger.

shloka_text: ततोदेवास्कसगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः । साधुसावधितिरामस्यतत्कर्मसमपूजयन् ।।6.94.36।।
explanation: Then, the Gandharvas, Devas, and Siddhas were very happy and praised Sri Rama saying, 'well done, well done' and offered prayers.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्छतदारामःसुग्रीवंप्रत्यनन्तरम् । विभीषणं च धर्मात्माहनूमन्तं च वानरम् ।।6.94.37।। जाम्बवन्तंहरिश्रेष्ठंमैन्दंद्विविदमेव च । एतदस्त्रबलंदिव्यंममवात्ऱ्यम्बकस्यवा ।।6.94.38।।
explanation: Then righteous Sri Rama said to nearby Sugriva, Vibheeshana, Hanuman, Jambavan and leaders of Vanaras like Mainda, Dwivida, that the power of these arrows are in him and Lord Siva only.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्छतदारामःसुग्रीवंप्रत्यनन्तरम् । विभीषणं च धर्मात्माहनूमन्तं च वानरम् ।।6.94.37।। जाम्बवन्तंहरिश्रेष्ठंमैन्दंद्विविदमेव च । एतदस्त्रबलंदिव्यंममवात्ऱ्यम्बकस्यवा ।।6.94.38।।
explanation: Then righteous Sri Rama said to nearby Sugriva, Vibheeshana, Hanuman, Jambavan and leaders of Vanaras like Mainda, Dwivida, that the power of these arrows are in him and Lord Siva only.

shloka_text: तानितानिसहस्राणिसारोहाणां च वाजिनाम् । रथानांत्वग्निवर्णानांसध्वजानांसहस्रशः ।।6.95.1।। राक्षसानांसहस्राणिगदापरिघयोधिनाम् । काञ्चनध्वजचित्राणांशूराणांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.95.2।। निहतानिशरैर्दीस्तीक्ष्णैस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणैः । रावणेनप्रयुक्तानिरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.95.3।।
explanation: "Rama who can work without getting tired put an end to thousands of Rakshasa warriors with his sharp glowing arrows decked with gold. Thousands of warriors sent by king Ravana, mounted on chariots, yoked to horses, of the colour of fire, thousands of warriors who could wage with iron bars, decked in gold, mounted on colourful chariots of golden colour pictures and Rakshasas who can change their form at will, were destroyed by Sri Rama."

shloka_text: तानितानिसहस्राणिसारोहाणां च वाजिनाम् । रथानांत्वग्निवर्णानांसध्वजानांसहस्रशः ।।6.95.1।। राक्षसानांसहस्राणिगदापरिघयोधिनाम् । काञ्चनध्वजचित्राणांशूराणांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.95.2।। निहतानिशरैर्दीस्तीक्ष्णैस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणैः । रावणेनप्रयुक्तानिरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.95.3।।
explanation: "Rama who can work without getting tired put an end to thousands of Rakshasa warriors with his sharp glowing arrows decked with gold. Thousands of warriors sent by king Ravana, mounted on chariots, yoked to horses, of the colour of fire, thousands of warriors who could wage with iron bars, decked in gold, mounted on colourful chariots of golden colour pictures and Rakshasas who can change their form at will, were destroyed by Sri Rama."

shloka_text: तानितानिसहस्राणिसारोहाणां च वाजिनाम् । रथानांत्वग्निवर्णानांसध्वजानांसहस्रशः ।।6.95.1।। राक्षसानांसहस्राणिगदापरिघयोधिनाम् । काञ्चनध्वजचित्राणांशूराणांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.95.2।। निहतानिशरैर्दीस्तीक्ष्णैस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणैः । रावणेनप्रयुक्तानिरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.95.3।।
explanation: "Rama who can work without getting tired put an end to thousands of Rakshasa warriors with his sharp glowing arrows decked with gold. Thousands of warriors sent by king Ravana, mounted on chariots, yoked to horses, of the colour of fire, thousands of warriors who could wage with iron bars, decked in gold, mounted on colourful chariots of golden colour pictures and Rakshasas who can change their form at will, were destroyed by Sri Rama."

shloka_text: दृष्टवाश्रुत्वा च सम्भ्रान्ताहतशेषानिशाचराः । राक्षसीश्चसमागम्यदीनाश्चिन्तापरिप्लुताः ।।6.95.4।। विधवाहतपुत्राश्चक्रोशन्त्योहतबान्दवाः । राक्षस्यःसहसङ्गम्यदुःखार्ताःपर्यदेवयन् ।।6.95.5।।
explanation: "On seeing and hearing of the others left over, the night rangers felt bewildered and piteous with agony coming together, moving in groups, those who lost husband, son, kin and protectors along with associates crying, stricken with grief."

shloka_text: दृष्टवाश्रुत्वा च सम्भ्रान्ताहतशेषानिशाचराः । राक्षसीश्चसमागम्यदीनाश्चिन्तापरिप्लुताः ।।6.95.4।। विधवाहतपुत्राश्चक्रोशन्त्योहतबान्दवाः । राक्षस्यःसहसङ्गम्यदुःखार्ताःपर्यदेवयन् ।।6.95.5।।
explanation: "On seeing and hearing of the others left over, the night rangers felt bewildered and piteous with agony coming together, moving in groups, those who lost husband, son, kin and protectors along with associates crying, stricken with grief."

shloka_text: कथंशूर्पणखावृद्धाकरालानिर्णतोदरी । आससादवनेरामंकन्दर्पमिवरूपिणम् ।।6.95.6।।
explanation: "How did that old, dreadful and hideous Surpanakha approach Rama, whose form is charming like the god of love, in the forest?"

shloka_text: सुकुमारंमहासत्त्वंसर्वभूतहितेरतम् । तंदृष्टवालोकनिन्द्यासाहीनरूपाप्रकामिता ।।6.95.7।।
explanation: "That woman of ugly appearance deserves to be killed. How is it that she was stung with love with that delicate Rama, a well wisher of all beings?"

shloka_text: कथंसर्वगुणैर्हीनागुणवन्तंमहौजसम् । सुमुखंदुर्मुखीरामंकामयामासराक्षसी ।।6.95.8।।
explanation: "How did that rakshasi of terrible appearance dare to love that virtuous Rama?"

shloka_text: जनस्यास्याल्पभाग्यत्वाद्वलिनीश्वेतमूर्धजा । अकार्यमपहास्यं च सर्वलोकविगर्हितम् ।।6.95.9।। राक्षसानांविनाशायदूषणस्यखरस्य च । चकाराप्रतिरूपासाराघवस्यप्रधर्षणम् ।।6.95.10।।
