explanation: "Because of our bad luck and to the destruction of her own people, Khara and Dooshana, that old lady, with wrinkled face, grey haired (Surpanakha) Rakshasa woman tried to go and attack Raghava, a misdeed which was ridiculed and condemned by the whole world?"

shloka_text: जनस्यास्याल्पभाग्यत्वाद्वलिनीश्वेतमूर्धजा । अकार्यमपहास्यं च सर्वलोकविगर्हितम् ।।6.95.9।। राक्षसानांविनाशायदूषणस्यखरस्य च । चकाराप्रतिरूपासाराघवस्यप्रधर्षणम् ।।6.95.10।।
explanation: "Because of our bad luck and to the destruction of her own people, Khara and Dooshana, that old lady, with wrinkled face, grey haired (Surpanakha) Rakshasa woman tried to go and attack Raghava, a misdeed which was ridiculed and condemned by the whole world?"

shloka_text: तन्निमित्तमिदंवैरंरावणेनकृतंमहत् । वधायसीतासासीतादशग्रीवेणरक्षसा ।।6.95.11।।
explanation: "For that reason of Surpanakha, this enmity has been conceived by Ravana and Sita was borne away by the ten headed Rakshasa."

shloka_text: न च सीतांदशग्रीवःप्राप्नोतिजनकात्मजाम् । बद्धंबलवतावैरमक्षयंराघवेण च ।।6.95.12।।
explanation: "Hope the ten headed Ravana will not touch Sita forcibly, by which undying enmity has been contracted already."

shloka_text: वैदेहींप्रार्थयानंतंविराधंप्रेक्षयराक्षसम् । हतमेकेनरामेणपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.13।।
explanation: "On perceiving that Viradha solicitous of Vaidehi, the Rakshasa was killed by Rama with one arrow. That is sufficient proof (of Rama's valour)."

shloka_text: चतुर्धशसहस्राणिरक्षसांभीमकर्मणाम् । निहतानिजनस्थानेशरैरग्निशिखोपमैः ।।6.95.14।।
explanation: " At Janasthana fourteen thousand Rakshasas have been destroyed with his arrows like peaks of fire."

shloka_text: खरश्चनिहतःसङ्ख्येदूषणस्त्रिशिरास्तथा । शरैरादितसङ्काशैःपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.15।।
explanation: "Khara was killed in that combat with sunlike arrows, so also Dooshana and Trisira. That example is sufficient proof."

shloka_text: हतोयोजनबाहुश्चकबन्दोरुदिराशनः । क्रोधान्नादंनदन् सोऽथपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.16।।
explanation: "Kabhanda who lived on blood came roaring, enraged, whose arms were eight meters long was also killed and that is a sufficient example."

shloka_text: जघानबलिनंरामस्सहस्रनयनात्मजम् । वालिनंमेरुसङ्काशंपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.17।।
explanation: "Mighty Rama killed the son of thousand eyed Indra, Vali, who resembled mountain Meru. That example is sufficient proof."

shloka_text: ऋष्यमूकेवसंश्चैवदीनोभग्नमनोरथः । सुग्रीवःप्रापितोराज्यंपर्याप्तंतन्निदर्शनम् ।।6.95.18।।
explanation: "Sugriva, who was living on Rishyamukha, dejected and disconsolate was restored with his kingdom. That is sufficient."

shloka_text: धर्मार्थसहितंवाक्यंसर्वेषांरक्षसांहितम् । युक्तंविभीषणेनोक्तंमोहत्तस्य न रोचते ।।6.95.19।।
explanation: "Good advice given by Vibheeshana in accordance with righteousness was not liked by him in delusion."

shloka_text: विभीषणवचःकुर्याद्यदिस्मधनदानुजः । श्मशानभूतादुःखार्तानेयंलङ्काभविष्यति ।।6.95.20।।
explanation: "Had Ravana, the younger brother of Kubera followed the advice of Vibheeshana, this Lanka would not have been stricken with grief and turned into a crematorium."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णंहतंश्रुत्वाराघवेणमहाबलम् । अतिकायं च दुर्मर्षंलक्ष्मणेनहतंतदा ।।6.95.21।। प्रियंचेन्द्रजितंपुत्रंरावणोनावबुध्यते ।
explanation: "Kumbhakarna of extraordinary strength having been killed by Raghava, and even on hearing that Atikaya who is difficult to disregard, and Indrajith, dear son killed by Lakshmana also, Ravana has not realised."

shloka_text: ममपुत्रोममभ्राताममभर्तारणेहतः ।।6.95.22।। इत्येषश्रूयतेशब्दोराक्षसीनांकुलेकुले ।
explanation: "My son is killed, my brother is killed, my husband is killed," was the sound heard from every family.

shloka_text: रथश्चाश्वाश्चनागाश्चहताःशतसहस्रशः ।।6.95.23।। रणेरामेणशूरेणहताश्चापिपदातयः ।
explanation: "Horses, elephants, warriors, even foot soldiers were killed, chariots were destroyed, and hundreds and thousands struck down in war by Rama."

shloka_text: रुद्रोवायदिवाविष्णुर्महेन्द्रोवाशतक्रतुः ।।6.95.24।। हन्तिनोरामरूपेणयदिवास्वयमन्तकः ।
explanation: "Is it Rudra, or Lord Vishnu, or Indra, who has done hundred sacrifices in the past or is it that the god of death itself has taken the form of Rama and killed him?"

shloka_text: हतप्रवीरारामेणनिराशाजीवितेवयम् ।।6.95.25।। अपश्य्नत्योभयस्यान्तमनाथाविलपामहे ।
explanation: "Eminent heroes killed by Rama, hopes of life lost, not able to see the end of fear, we are like orphans weeping."

shloka_text: रामहस्ताद्धशग्रीवश्शूरोदत्तमहावरः ।।6.95.26।। इदंभयंमहाघोरंसमुत्पन्नं न बुध्यते ।
explanation: "Graced with the boon of arrows the tenheaded Ravana has not realised the appalling danger to him from Rama."

shloka_text: तं न देवा न गन्धर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः ।।6.95.27।। उपसृष्टंपरित्रातुंशक्तारामेणसम्युगे ।
explanation: "Neither gods nor Gandharvas, not even fiends will be able to protect, struck by Rama in war."

shloka_text: त्पताश्चापिदृश्यन्तेरावणस्यरणेरणे ।।6.95.28।। कथयन्तिहिरामेणरावणस्यनिबर्हणम् ।
explanation: "In every war evil portents are noticed rising up, of Rama destroying Ravana. How much more to say?"

shloka_text: पितामहेनप्रीतेनदेवदानवराक्षसैः ।।6.95.29।। रावणस्याभयंदत्तंमनुष्येभ्यो न याचितम् ।
explanation: "Brahma has lovingly provided protection to Ravana from Devas, Danavas and Rakshasas. He did not seek protection from humans."

shloka_text: तदिदंमानुषंमन्येप्राप्तंनिःसंशयंभयम् ।।6.95.30।। जीवितान्तकंघोरंरक्षसांरावणस्य च ।
explanation: "Fearlessness of death from human beings attained by Ravana in this way was no doubt terrific to Rakshasas and Ravana."

shloka_text: पीड्यमानास्तुबलिनावरदानेनरक्षसा ।।6.95.31।। दीप्स्सैस्तपोभिर्विबुधाःपितामहमपूजयन् ।
explanation: "Tormented by the oppression of Ravana, on account of the boon (given to him by the creator) and intensity of his austerities, the learned worshipped Brahma."

shloka_text: देवतानांहितार्थायमहात्मावैपितामहः ।।6.95.32।। उवाचदेवताःसर्वाइदंतुष्टोमहद्वचः ।
explanation: "Gratified by the worship of Devatas, wishing them good, Brahma spoke these words."

shloka_text: अद्यप्रभृतिलोकांस्त्रीन् सर्वेदानवराक्षसाः ।।6.95.33।। भयेनप्रावृतानित्यंविचरिष्यन्तिशाश्वतम् ।
explanation: "From now ,all Danavas and Rakshasas will range the three worlds every day permanently in fear."

shloka_text: दैवतैस्तुसमागम्यसर्वैश्चेन्द्रपुरोगमैः ।।6.95.34।। वृषध्वजस्त्रिपुरहामहादेवःप्रसादितः ।
explanation: "Getting together all the Devatas marched towards Indra and propitiated Lord MahaDeva, destroyer of Tripura, who Bears the sign of bull on his abode."

shloka_text: प्रसन्नस्तुमहादेवोदेवानेतद्वचोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.95.35।। उत्पत्स्यतिहितार्थंवोनारीरक्षःक्षयावहा ।
explanation: MahaDeva was pleased by the Devatas and spoke these words for their benefit," a woman will be born for the destruction of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: एषादेवैःप्रयुक्तातुक्षुद्यथादानवान् पुरा ।।6.95.36।। भक्षयिष्यतिनःसीताराक्षसघ्नीसरावणान् ।
explanation: "Just as hunger consumed Danavas earlier, this woman, instigated (by Devatas) will consume all Rakshasas and Ravana."

shloka_text: रावणस्यापनीतेनदुर्विनीतस्यदुर्मतेः ।।6.95.37।। अयंनिष्टानकोघोरंशोकेनसमभिप्लुतः ।
explanation: "Because of the misconduct of the evilminded Ravana's immoral action, terrific destruction attended by grief stares at us."

shloka_text: तंन पश्यामहेलोकेयोनःशरणदोभवेत् ।।6.95.38।। राघवेणोपसृष्टानां कालेनेव युगक्षये ।
explanation: "Threatened like this by Raghava, we cannot perceive anyone in this world who can protect us now. Just as beings are threatened by the time spirit at the end of the destruction of this world, we are threatened."

shloka_text: नास्तिनःशरणंकश्चिद्भयेमहतितिष्ठताम् ।।6.95.39।। दावाग्निवेष्टितानांहिकरेणूनांयथावने ।
explanation: "Indeed, there is no protection for us here to stay, as we are like the female elephants in the forest covered by huge wildfire."

shloka_text: प्राप्तकालंकृतंतेनपौलस्त्येनमहात्मना ।।6.95.40।। यतएवंभयंदृष्टंतमेवशरणंगतः ।
explanation: "Great Vibheeshana of the Paulastya race, perceiving opportune time, has sought refuge out of fear."

shloka_text: आर्तानांराक्षसीनांतुलङ्कायांवैकुलेकुले । रावणःकरुणंशब्दंशुश्रावपरिदेवितम् ।।6.96.1।।
explanation: Ravana heard from every house in Lanka sounds of piteous cries and pathetic sounds of the afflicted.

shloka_text: स तुदीर्घंविनिःश्वस्यमुहूर्तंध्यानमास्थितः । बभूवपरमक्रुद्धोरावणोभीमदर्शनः ।।6.96.2।।
explanation: Ravana remained silent for long, thought for a moment and assumed a terrific angry form.

shloka_text: सन्दश्यदशनैरोष्ठंक्रोधसम्रक्तलोचनः । राक्षसैरपिदुर्दर्शःकालाग्निरिवमूर्छितः ।।6.96.3।।
explanation: Biting his teeth, eyes turned red in wrath, Ravana was perplexed. He was difficult to look at even for the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: उवाच च समीपस्थान्राक्षसान्राक्षसेश्वरः । क्रोधाव्यक्तकथस्तत्रनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.96.4।। महोदरंमहापार्श्वंविरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम् । शीघ्रंवदतसैन्यानिनिर्यातेतिममाज्ञया ।।6.96.5।।
explanation: Thus spoke the Lord of Rakshasas indistinctly in anger with his eyes burning as though it would consume them (Rakshasas). He commanded Mahodara, Mahaparsva and Virupaksha who stood nearby saying" quickly instruct the army to go."

shloka_text: उवाच च समीपस्थान्राक्षसान्राक्षसेश्वरः । क्रोधाव्यक्तकथस्तत्रनिर्दहन्निवचक्षुषा ।।6.96.4।। महोदरंमहापार्श्वंविरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम् । शीघ्रंवदतसैन्यानिनिर्यातेतिममाज्ञया ।।6.96.5।।
explanation: Thus spoke the Lord of Rakshasas indistinctly in anger with his eyes burning as though it would consume them (Rakshasas). He commanded Mahodara, Mahaparsva and Virupaksha who stood nearby saying" quickly instruct the army to go."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराक्षसास्तेभयार्दिताः । चोदयामासुरव्यग्रान्राक्षसांस्तान्नृपाज्ञया ।।6.96.6।।
explanation: On hearing the words of the king's order, the Rakshasas stricken with fear, unagitated, started thinking.

shloka_text: तेतुसर्वेतथेत्युक्त्वाराक्षसाभीमदर्शनाः । कृतस्वस्त्वयनाःसर्वेतेरणाभिमुखाययुः ।।6.96.7।।
explanation: All the Rakshasas with frightful looks saying 'Be it so', having prepared themselves with armor went towards the battlefield.

shloka_text: प्रतिपूज्ययथान्यायंरावणंतेमहारथाः । तस्थुःप्राञ्जलयःसर्वेभर्तुर्विजयकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.96.8।।
explanation: All the great chariot warrior spraying to Ravana with folded palms stood desiring success.

shloka_text: अथोवाचप्रहस्यैतान्रावणःक्रोधमूर्छितः । महोदरमहापार्श्वौविरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम् ।।6.96.9।।
explanation: Then Ravana who was deluded with anger, laughing aloud spoke to Mahodara, Mahaparsva and Virupaksha.

shloka_text: अद्यबाणैर्धनुर्मुक्स्सैर्युगान्तादित्यसन्निभैः । राघवंलक्ष्मणंचैवनेष्यामियमसादनम् ।।6.96.10।।
explanation: Loosening the shafts from the bow, Ravana resembling the Sun at the time of dissolution of the universe said," I shall dispatch Raghava and Lakshmana to the abode of the Lord of death."

shloka_text: खरस्यकुम्भकर्णस्यप्रहसेन्द्रजितोस्तथा । करिष्यामिप्रतीकारमद्यशत्रुवधादहम् ।।6.96.11।।
explanation: "Today by the killing the enemy I will take my revenge and also of Khara, Kumbhakarna, Prahastha and Indrajith."

shloka_text: नैवान्तरिक्षं न दिशो न नद्यौर्नापिसागराः । प्रकाशत्वंगमिष्यन्तिमद्बाणजलदावृताः ।।6.96.12।।
explanation: "By my arrows covering the sky like clouds there will be no effulgence both in space and in the quarters and not even in the ocean."

shloka_text: अद्यवानरमुख्यानांतानियूथानिभागशः । धनुषाशरजालेनवधिष्यामिपतत्रिणा ।।6.96.13।।
explanation: "Today by the network of plumed arrows released from my bow I shall kill the troops of Vanara leaders' part by part."

shloka_text: अद्यवानरसैन्यानिरथेनपवनौजसा । धनुस्समुद्रादुद्भूतैर्मथिष्यामिशरोर्मिभिः ।।6.96.14।।
explanation: "Seated on the chariot I shall knock out the Vanara army by the waves in the form of arrows released from the ocean of my bow."

shloka_text: व्याकोशपद्मवक्त्राणिपद्मकेसरवर्चसाम् । अद्ययूथतटाकानिगजवत्प्रमथाम्यहम् ।।6.96.15।।
explanation: "Like an elephant now I shall torment the ponds in the form of battalions of Vanaras shining like the filaments of lotuses, with their faces resembling open lotuses."

shloka_text: सशरैरद्यवदनैस्सङ्ख्येवानरयूथपाः । मण्डयिष्यन्तिवसुधांसनालैरिवपङ्कजैः ।।6.96.16।।
explanation: "Now with the arrows fixed on their faces the Vanara battalions spread on the earth will adorn the earth like lotuses spread on earth."

shloka_text: अद्ययूथप्रचण्डानांहरीणांद्रुमयोधिनाम् । मुक्तेनैकेषुणायुद्धेभेत्स्यामि च शतंशतम् ।।6.96.17।।
explanation: "Today in the combat each one of the arrows released by me will pierce through one hundred monkeys vehemently fighting with trees"

shloka_text: हतोभर्ताहतोभ्रातायासां च चतनयोहतः । वधेनाद्यरिपोस्तासांकरोम्यश्रुप्रमार्जनम् ।।6.96.18।।
explanation: "Today through the destruction of the enemy I will wipe the tears of the one whose son has been killed, whose brother has been killed."

shloka_text: अद्यमद्भाणनिर्भिन्नैःप्रकीर्णैर्गतचेतनैः । करोमिवानरैर्युद्धेयत्नावेक्ष्यतलांमहीम् ।।6.96.19।।
explanation: "Today, in the combat, my arrows will split open the Vanaras and ceased of life, they will be covering the earth. It will be possible to see the ground only with effort."

shloka_text: अद्यगोमयवोगृध्राश्चये च मांसाशिनोऽपरे । सर्वांस्तांस्तर्पयिष्यामिशत्रुमांसैश्शरार्दितैः ।।6.96.20।।
explanation: "Today I shall provide for whatever animals, eagles or flesheating animals the flesh of enemies killed by my arrows."

shloka_text: कल्प्यतांमेरथंशीघ्रंक्षिप्रमानीयतांधनुः । अनुप्रयान्तुमांयुद्धेयेऽत्रशिष्टानिशाचराः ।।6.96.21।।
explanation: "Let my chariot and bow be ready and brought here. Let the night rangers who survived follow me."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वामहापार्श्वोऽब्रवीद्वचः । बलाध्यक्षान् स्थिथांस्तत्रबलंसंत्वर्यतामिति ।।6.96.22।।
explanation: On hearing the speech of Ravana, Mahaparsva enjoined the mighty leaders of the army standing there and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: बलाध्यक्षास्तुसम्रब्दाराक्षसांस्तान् गृहेगृहे । चोदयन्तःपरिययुर्लङ्कांलघुपराक्रमाः ।।6.96.23।।
explanation: "Let the army leaders of mighty valour go hurriedly to search in every house in Lanka for Rakshasas."

shloka_text: ततोमुहूर्तान्निष्पेतूराक्षसाभीमदर्शनाः । नदन्तोभीमवदनानानाप्रहरणैर्भुजैः ।।6.96.24।। असिभिःपट्टसै: शूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैर्हलैः । शक्तिभिस्तीक्ष्णधाराभिर्महद्भि: कूटमुद्गरैः ।।6.96.25।। यष्टिभिर्विमलैश्चक्रैर्निशितैश्चपरश्वथै: । भिन्दिपालैःशतघ्नीभिरन्यैश्चापिवरायुधैः ।।6.96.26।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas of terrific looks, and frightening faces holding on shoulders roaring departed with swords, spears, tridents, maces, iron bars, halas, sharp pointed javelins, huge Kutamudgaras, staffs and several discusses, sharp Bhindipalas, Sataghnis and many kinds of excellent weapons.

shloka_text: ततोमुहूर्तान्निष्पेतूराक्षसाभीमदर्शनाः । नदन्तोभीमवदनानानाप्रहरणैर्भुजैः ।।6.96.24।। असिभिःपट्टसै: शूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैर्हलैः । शक्तिभिस्तीक्ष्णधाराभिर्महद्भि: कूटमुद्गरैः ।।6.96.25।। यष्टिभिर्विमलैश्चक्रैर्निशितैश्चपरश्वथै: । भिन्दिपालैःशतघ्नीभिरन्यैश्चापिवरायुधैः ।।6.96.26।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas of terrific looks, and frightening faces holding on shoulders roaring departed with swords, spears, tridents, maces, iron bars, halas, sharp pointed javelins, huge Kutamudgaras, staffs and several discusses, sharp Bhindipalas, Sataghnis and many kinds of excellent weapons.

shloka_text: ततोमुहूर्तान्निष्पेतूराक्षसाभीमदर्शनाः । नदन्तोभीमवदनानानाप्रहरणैर्भुजैः ।।6.96.24।। असिभिःपट्टसै: शूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैर्हलैः । शक्तिभिस्तीक्ष्णधाराभिर्महद्भि: कूटमुद्गरैः ।।6.96.25।। यष्टिभिर्विमलैश्चक्रैर्निशितैश्चपरश्वथै: । भिन्दिपालैःशतघ्नीभिरन्यैश्चापिवरायुधैः ।।6.96.26।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas of terrific looks, and frightening faces holding on shoulders roaring departed with swords, spears, tridents, maces, iron bars, halas, sharp pointed javelins, huge Kutamudgaras, staffs and several discusses, sharp Bhindipalas, Sataghnis and many kinds of excellent weapons.

shloka_text: अथानयद्बलाध्यक्षस्सत्वरोरावणाज्ञया । द्रुतंसूतसमायुक्तंयुक्ताष्टतुरगंरथम् । आरुरोहतदाभीमोदीप्यमानंस्वतेजसा ।।6.96.27।।
explanation: Then by Ravana's command. the chief of the army with chariot rider brought the chariot yoked to eight horses quickly. Then dreadful and selfeffulgent glowing Ravana ascended the chariot."

shloka_text: ततःप्रयातस्सहसाराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतः ।।6.96.28।। रावणःसत्त्वगाम्भीर्याद्दारयन्निवमेदिनीम् ।
explanation: Then Ravana surrounded by many Rakshasas set out swiftly rending the earth with all his might and majesty.

shloka_text: रावणेनाभ्यनुज्ञातौमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ । विरूपाक्षश्चदुर्धर्षोरथानारुरुहुस्तदा ।।6.96.29।।
explanation: Duly permitted by Ravana, Mahaparsva and Mahodara who are difficult to overpower and also Virupaksha ascended their chariots.

shloka_text: तेतुहृष्टाविवर्धन्तोभिन्दन्तइवमेदिनीम् । नादंघोरंविमुञ्चन्तोनिर्ययुर्जयकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.96.30।।
explanation: Happy leaders, roaring exultantly, as if breaking the earth, emerged, turning round, desiring victory and sallied forth.

shloka_text: ततोयुद्धायतेजस्वीरक्षोगणबलैर्वृतः । निर्ययावुद्यतधनुःकालान्तकयमोपमः ।।6.96.31।।
explanation: Then Ravana surrounded by the army of Rakshasas lifted his bow, like the Lord Yama at the time of dissolution of the universe, went for the battle glowing.

shloka_text: ततःप्रजविताश्वेनरथेन स महारथः । द्वारेणनिर्ययौतेनयत्रतौरामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.96.32।।
explanation: Then from the mighty chariot yoked to exceedingly swift horses, the mighty charioteer made his exit from the entrance and saw Rama and Lakshmana there.

shloka_text: ततोनष्टप्रभःसूर्योदिशश्चतिमिरावृताः । द्विजाश्चनेदुर्घोराश्चसञ्चचाल च मेदिनी ।।6.96.33।।
explanation: Then the Sun lost his radiance, and the four directions were enveloped by gloom, the birds made fearful noise and the earth shook.

shloka_text: ववर्षरुधिरंदेवश्चस्खलुश्चतुरङ्गमाः । ध्वजाग्रेन्यपतद्गृध्रोविनेदुश्चाशिवाःशिवाः ।।6.96.34।।
explanation: Devas rained blood, horses stumbled, eagles settled on top of the post and jackals howled in a frightening way.

shloka_text: नयनंचास्फुरद्वामंवामोबाहुरकम्पत । विवर्णवदनश्साकतिंचिदभ्रश्यतस्वनः ।।6.96.35।।
explanation: His left eye twitched, left arm quivered, face turned pale and indeed his tone became hoarse.

shloka_text: ततोनिष्पततोयुद्धेदशग्रीवस्यरक्षसः । रणेनिधनशंसीनिरूपाण्येतानिजज्ञिरे ।।6.96.36।।
explanation: Thereafter as Ravana set forth for the battle, all the following forms predicting his death appeared.

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षात्पपातोल्कानिराघतसमनिर्घास्वना । विनेदुरशिवागृध्रावायसैरभिमिश्रिताः ।।6.96.37।।
explanation: A meteor had fallen from the sky resembling thunder, coupled with inauspicious eagle cries.

shloka_text: एतानचिन्तयन्घोरानुत्पातान्समवस्थितान् । निर्ययौरावणोमोहाद्वधार्थंकालचोदितः ।।6.96.38।।
explanation: Impelled by the time spirit, Ravana set forth without thinking of the terrific portents that had appeared in delusion for his destruction.

shloka_text: तेषांतुरथघोषेणराक्षसानांमहात्मनाम् । वानराणामपिचमूर्युद्धायैवाभ्यवर्तत ।।6.96.39।।
explanation: The Vanaras stood facing the great sound of Rakshasa troops, on hearing the sounds of chariots for the sake of battle.

shloka_text: तेषांतुतुमुलंयुद्धंबभूवकपिरक्षसाम् । अन्योन्यमाह्वयानानांक्रुद्धानांजयमिच्छताम् ।।6.96.40।।
explanation: Intense battle took place between the angry Vanaras and Rakshasas challenging one another desiring victory.

shloka_text: ततःक्रुद्धोदशग्रीवश्शरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । वानराणामनीकेषुचकारकदनंमहत् ।।6.96.41।।
explanation: There the tenheaded Ravana using arrows adorned with gold plumes struck Vanaras and a great war took place.

shloka_text: विकृत्तशिरसःकेचिद्रावणेनवलीमुखाः । केचिद्विच्छिन्नहृदयाःकेचिच्छ्रोत्रविवर्जिताः ।।6.96.42।।
explanation: Some Vanaras ' heads were deformed, some were pierced in their hearts, and some had their ears cut off.

shloka_text: निरुच्छवासाहताःकेचित्केचित्पार्श्वेषुदारिताः । केचिद्विभिन्नशिरसःकेचिच्चक्षुर्विनाकृताः ।।6.96.43।।
explanation: A few were made lifeless, some had their flanks split, some had their heads smashed and few were deprived of their eyes.

shloka_text: तथातैःकृत्तगात्रैस्तुदशग्रीवेणमार्गणैः । बभूववसुधातत्रप्रकीर्णाहरिभिस्तदा ।।6.97.1।।
explanation: That time the battlefield was strewn with bodies of Vanaras whose limbs had been severed by the arrows of Ravana.

shloka_text: रावणस्याप्रसह्यंतंशरसम्पातमेकतः । न शेकुस्सहितुंदीप्तंपतङ्गाज्वलनंयथा ।।6.97.2।।
explanation: Just as moths cannot bear the blazing fire, the Vanaras could not bear the glowing hail of Ravana's arrows even for an instant.

shloka_text: तेऽर्दितानिशितैर्बाणैःक्रोशन्तोविप्रदुद्रुवुः । पावकार्चिस्समाविष्टादह्यमानायथागजाः ।।6.97.3।।
explanation: Tormented by sharp arrows, the scorched Vanaras fled screaming like elephants enveloped in flames.

shloka_text: प्लवङ्गनामनीकानिमहाभ्राणीवमारुतः । सययौसमरेतस्मिन्विधमन्रावणश्शरैः ।।6.97.4।।
explanation: At that time, driven by Ravana's arrows, the Vanaras fled from the battlefield just like huge clouds are dissipated by wind.

shloka_text: कदनंतरसाकृत्वाराक्षसेन्ध्रोवनौकसाम् । आससादततोत्वरितंयुद्धेराघवंस्तदा ।।6.97.5।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king, having destroyed the forest rangers, thereafter, went to Raghava hurriedly.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्तान्कपीन्दृष्टवाभग्नान्विद्रावितान्रणे । गुल्मेसुषेणंनिक्षिप्यचक्रेयुद्धेऽद्भुतंमनः ।।6.97.6।।
explanation: Seeing the defeated and broken monkeys, Sugriva assigned Sushena for their protection and went to the battle making others wonder at his wonderful action.

shloka_text: आत्मनस्सदृशंवीरस्सतंनिक्षिप्यवानरम् । सुग्रीवोऽऽभिमुखश्शत्रुंप्रतस्थेपादपायुधः ।।6.97.7।।
explanation: Sugriva, being a hero himself, uprooting a tree as a weapon, went towards the enemy after having assigned Sushena the responsibility of protection of Vanaras.

shloka_text: पार्श्वतःपृष्ठतश्चास्यसर्वेयूथाधिपास्स्वयम् । अनुजह्रुर्महाशैलान् विविधांश्चमहाद्रुमान् ।।6.97.8।।
explanation: All the leaders of the army themselves seizing hold of huge mountains and trees of several kinds followed his side.

shloka_text: सनदन्युधिसुग्रीवस्स्वरेणमहतामहान् । पातयन्विविधांश्चान्यान्ञ्जगामोत्तमराक्षसान् ।।6.97.9।।
explanation: Great Sugriva roaring at high pitch in war destroyed several other Rakshasas and went towards the best of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ममन्थ च महाकायान्राक्षसान्वानरेश्वरः । युगान्तसमयेवायुःप्रवृद्धानगमानिव ।।6.97.10।।
explanation: The Vanara Lord of gigantic body, moving like the wind, tortuously destroyed the Rakshasas like a huge wind destroying the universe.

shloka_text: राक्षसानामनीकेषुशैलवर्षंववर्ष ह । अश्मवर्षंयथामेघःपक्षिसङ्घेषुकानने ।।6.97.11।।
explanation: Just as clouds shower hail stones on flocks of birds in the forest, Sugriva rained showers of rocks on the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: कपिराजविमुक्तैस्तैश्शैलवर्षैस्तुराक्षसाः । विकीर्णशिरसःपेतुर्निकृत्ताइवपर्वताः ।।6.97.12।।
explanation: Hit by the rocks rained by the Vanara king, the Rakshasas with heads broken and body mutilated had fallen like mountains.

shloka_text: अथसंक्षीयमाणेषुराक्षसेषुसमन्ततः । सुग्रीवेणप्रभग्नेषुपतत्सुनिनदत्सु च ।।6.97.13।। विरूपाक्षस्स्वकंनामधन्वीविश्राव्यराक्षसः । रथादाप्लुत्यदुर्धर्षोगजस्कन्धमुपारुहत् ।।6.97.14।।
explanation: And thereafter, all the Rakshasas shattered by Sugriva, tormented, fallen on the ground were shouting. Seeing that Virupaksha, himself, who is difficult to encounter, holding his bow, announcing his name, jumped from the chariot onto an elephant in a rut.

shloka_text: अथसंक्षीयमाणेषुराक्षसेषुसमन्ततः । सुग्रीवेणप्रभग्नेषुपतत्सुनिनदत्सु च ।।6.97.13।। विरूपाक्षस्स्वकंनामधन्वीविश्राव्यराक्षसः । रथादाप्लुत्यदुर्धर्षोगजस्कन्धमुपारुहत् ।।6.97.14।।
explanation: And thereafter, all the Rakshasas shattered by Sugriva, tormented, fallen on the ground were shouting. Seeing that Virupaksha, himself, who is difficult to encounter, holding his bow, announcing his name, jumped from the chariot onto an elephant in a rut.

shloka_text: स तंद्विरदमारुह्यविरूपाक्षोमहारथः । वनर्दभनीमनिर्ह्रादंवानरानभ्यधावत ।।6.97.15।।
explanation: That great charioteer Virupaksha ascended the elephant, frightening like a lion, and rushed towards Vanaras roaring.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवे स शरान्घोरान्विससर्जचमूमुखे । स्थापयामासचोद्विग्नान्राक्षसान् सम्प्रहर्षयन् ।।6.97.16।।
explanation: Releasing arrows at the army of Vanaras and Sugriva, he (Virupaksha) pierced arrows and relieved the Rakshasas of fear and made them happy.

shloka_text: सतुविद्धश्शितैर्बाणैःकपीन्द्रस्तेनरक्षसा । चुक्रोध स महाक्रोधोवधेचास्यमनोदधे ।।6.97.17।।
explanation: The king of Vanaras, pained by the shafts of Rakshasa, roared, and became very furious. He set in his mind to kill the Rakshasa.

shloka_text: ततःपादपमुद्धृत्यशूरस्सम्प्रधनोहरिः । अभिपत्यजघानास्यप्रमुखेतुमहागजम् ।।6.97.18।।
explanation: Then springing up, the valiant Vanara uprooting a tree struck the face of the Rakshasa seated on the great elephant.

shloka_text: स तुप्रहाराभिहतस्सुग्रीवेणमहागजः । अपासर्पद्धनुर्मात्रंनिषसादननाद च ।।6.97.19।।
explanation: Overwhelmed by the blow of Sugriva, that great elephant retreated four cubits, distressed, and roared.

shloka_text: गजात्तुमथितात्तूर्णमपक्रम्य स वीर्यवान् । राक्षसोऽऽभिमुखश्शत्रुंप्रत्युद्गम्यततःकपिम् ।।6.97.20।। आर्षभंचर्मखडगं च प्रगृह्यलघुविक्रमः । भर्त्सयन्निवसुग्रीवमाससादव्यवस्थितम् ।।6.97.21।।
explanation: That valiant Rakshasa hero jumped down quickly from the wounded elephant, seizing hold of a shield made of bull's hide and a sword, advancing towards the enemy who stood firmly, and facing him, as if threatening him.

shloka_text: गजात्तुमथितात्तूर्णमपक्रम्य स वीर्यवान् । राक्षसोऽऽभिमुखश्शत्रुंप्रत्युद्गम्यततःकपिम् ।।6.97.20।। आर्षभंचर्मखडगं च प्रगृह्यलघुविक्रमः । भर्त्सयन्निवसुग्रीवमाससादव्यवस्थितम् ।।6.97.21।।
explanation: That valiant Rakshasa hero jumped down quickly from the wounded elephant, seizing hold of a shield made of bull's hide and a sword, advancing towards the enemy who stood firmly, and facing him, as if threatening him.

shloka_text: स हितस्याभिसङ्कृद्धःप्रगृह्यविपुलांशिलाम् । विरूपाक्षायचिक्षेपसुग्रीवोजलदोपमाम् ।।6.97.22।।
explanation: Holding a huge rock which was like a mass of clouds, Sugriva, who was very angry, hurled at Virupaksha.

shloka_text: स तांशिलामापतन्तींदृष्टवाराक्षसपुङ्गवः । अपक्रम्यसुविक्रान्तःखडगेनप्राहरत्तदा ।।6.97.23।।
explanation: Then that exceedingly powerful Rakshasa leader, seeing the rock falling, struck it with a sword, jumping.

shloka_text: तेनखडगप्रहारेणरक्षसाबलिनाहतः । मुहूर्तमभवद्वीरोविसंज्ञइववानरः ।।6.97.24।।
explanation: Struck by the mighty Rakshasa with a sword, the Vanara leader, a heroic one, got wounded, and became unconscious for a while.

shloka_text: स तदा स हसोत्पत्यराक्षसस्यमहाहवे । मुष्टिंसन्वर्त्यवेगेनपातयामासवक्षसि ।।6.97.25।।
explanation: Then in that great war, Sugriva getting up at once whirling his fist, hit (Virupaksha) him on the chest.

shloka_text: मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतोविरूपाक्षोनिशाचरः । तेनखडगेनसङ्कृद्दस्सुग्रीवस्यचमूमुखे ।।6.97.26।। कवचंपातयामासपद्भ्यामभिहतोऽऽपतत् ।
explanation: Hit by the fist, Virupaksha became very angry and tore the armor of Sugriva by his sword in the forefront of the army. Wounded severely, Sugriva fell on his feet.

shloka_text: स समुत्थायपतितःकपिस्तस्यव्यसर्जयत् । तलप्रहारमशनेस्समानंभीमनिस्स्वनम् ।।6.97.27।।
explanation: Dropped down by him (Virupaksha), Sugriva, got up, and gave the Rakshasa a slap with his palm which was equal to thunderbolt that produced a terrific sound like crash.

shloka_text: तलप्रहारंतद्रक्षस्सुग्रीवेणसमुद्यतम् । नैपुण्यान्मोचयित्वैनंमुष्टिनोरस्यताडयत् ।।6.97.28।।
explanation: Virupaksha, escaping the slap of Sugriva with great skill, hit him (Sugriva) on the chest with his fist.

shloka_text: तस्सुसङ्कृद्धतरःसुग्रीवोवानरेश्वरः ।।6.97.29।। मोक्षितंचात्मनोदृष्टवाप्रहारंतेनरक्षसा ।
explanation: Then Sugriva, the king of the forest, grew angry and hit the Rakshasa on the forehead.

shloka_text: ददर्शान्तरंतस्यविरूपाक्षस्यवानरः ।।6.97.30।। ततोन्यपातयत्क्रोधाच्छङ्खदेशेमहात्तलम् ।
explanation: The Vanara, seeing the blow given by Virupaksha, enraged Sugriva hit him with another palm on the temporal bone by which he fell.

shloka_text: महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनतलेनाभिहतःक्षितौ ।।6.97.31।। पपातरुधिरक्लिन्नश्शोणितंसमुद्यमन् । स्रोतोभ्यस्तुविरूपाक्षोजलंप्रस्रवणादिव ।।6.97.32।।
explanation: Hurt by the palm which resembled Indra's weapon, blood started flowing from Virupaksha's body just like water flowed from waterfalls. Bathed in blood, vomiting blood, Virupaksha fell on the ground.

shloka_text: महेन्द्राशनिकल्पेनतलेनाभिहतःक्षितौ ।।6.97.31।। पपातरुधिरक्लिन्नश्शोणितंसमुद्यमन् । स्रोतोभ्यस्तुविरूपाक्षोजलंप्रस्रवणादिव ।।6.97.32।।
explanation: Hurt by the palm which resembled Indra's weapon, blood started flowing from Virupaksha's body just like water flowed from waterfalls. Bathed in blood, vomiting blood, Virupaksha fell on the ground.

shloka_text: विवृत्तनयनंक्रोधात्सफेनंरुधिराप्लुतम् । ददृशुस्तेविरूपाक्षंविरूपाक्षतरंकृतम् ।।6.97.33।।
explanation: The Vanaras witnessed Virupaksha who had misshapen eyes, turning his eyeballs in anger, foaming blood flowing from nostrils.

shloka_text: स्फुरन्तंपरिवर्तन्तंपार्श्वेनरुधिरोक्षितम् । करुणं च विनर्दन्तंददृशुःकपयोरिपुम् ।।6.97.34।।
explanation: Virupaksha rolled, by changing sides bathed in blood, causing sorrow and compassion to Vanaras who witnessed.

shloka_text: तथातुतौसंम्यतिसम्प्रयुक्तौ । तरस्विनौवानरराक्षसानाम् ।।6.97.35।।
explanation: Thus, both close to each other, both redoubtable armies, of Vanaras and Rakshasas, both powerful and terrific, both mighty, roared as if the great ocean had burst.

shloka_text: हन्यमानेबलेतूर्णमन्योन्यंतेमहामृथे । सरसीवमहाघर्मेसोपक्षीणेबभूवतुः ।।6.98.1।।
explanation: In the major conflict, each one destroying the other army, it seemed like the midsummer lakes totally lost its water.

shloka_text: स्वबलस्यविघातेनविरूपाक्ष्वधेन च । बभूवद्विगुणंक्रुद्धोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.98.2।।
explanation: The Lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, became doubly angry by the destruction of his army and fall of Virupaksha.

shloka_text: प्रक्षीणंतुबलंदृष्टवावध्यमानंवलीमुखैः । बभूवास्यव्यथायुद्धेप्रेक्ष्यदैवविपर्ययम् ।।6.98.3।।
explanation: Rakshasa's army was killed by Vanaras and drastically reduced. Seeing the adversary of God's grace, Ravana was agonized on witnessing it.

shloka_text: उवाच च समीपस्थंमहोदरमरिन्दमम् । अस्मिन्कालेमहाबाहोजयाशात्वयिमेस्थिता ।।6.98.4।।
explanation: And then Ravana spoke to Mahodara who was close by, one who is difficult to encounter, saying " At this time the hope for my victory is centered in you."

shloka_text: जहिशत्रुचमूंवीरदर्शयाद्यपराक्रमम् । भर्तृपिण्डस्यकालोऽऽयंनिर्देष्टुंसाधुयुध्यताम् ।।6.98.5।।
explanation: "O heroic Mahodara! Today, exhibit your valour by destroying the enemy army. Having received my subsistence, this is the time to repay. Fight well in war."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वाराक्षसेन्द्रोमहोदरः । प्रविवेशारिसेनांतांपतङ्गइवपावकम् ।।6.98.6।।
explanation: Having spoken like that by the king of Rakshasas, Mahodara entered the army of the enemy like a moth enters fire.

shloka_text: ततस्सकदनंचक्रेवानराणांमहाबलः । भर्तृवाक्येनतेजस्वीस्वेनवीर्येणचोदितः ।।6.98.7।।
explanation: Thereafter, the mighty and brilliant Mahodara, in obedience to the word of the king, inspired by his own valour, went to fight with Vanaras.

shloka_text: वानराश्चमहासत्त्वाःप्रगृह्वःविपुलाशशिलाः । प्रविश्यारिबलंभीमंजघ्नुस्तेरजनीचरान् ।।6.98.8।।
explanation: The mighty Vanaras also seizing huge rocks entered into the frightening enemy army of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: महोदरस्तुसङ्कृद्धश्शरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः । चिच्छेदपाणिपादोरुन्वानराणांमहाहवे ।।6.98.9।।
explanation: In that great war, enraged Mahodara with arrows decked in gold shattered the Vanaras by attacking on hands, legs, and thighs.

shloka_text: ततस्तेवानरास्सर्वेराक्षसैरर्दिताभृशम् । दिशोदशद्रुताःकेचित्केचित्सुग्रीवमाश्रिताः ।।6.98.10।।
explanation: Thereafter, unable to bear the pain, those Vanaras hit by Rakshasas, went in ten directions and some went to Sugriva for refuge.

shloka_text: प्रभग्नांसमरेदृष्टवावानराणांमहाचमूम् । अभिदुद्रावसुग्रीवोमहोदरमनन्तरम् ।।6.98.11।।
explanation: Seeing the great army of Vanaras defeated in the conflict, Sugriva rushed towards Mahodara.

shloka_text: प्रगृह्यविपुलांघोरांमहीधरसमांशिलाम् । चिक्षेप स महातेजास्तद्वधायहरीश्वरः ।।6.98.12।।
explanation: Endowed with great energy, Sugriva, the monkey Lord, seizing a huge mountain like dreadful rock, hurled to kill Mahodara.

shloka_text: तामापततनींसहसाशिलांदृष्टवामहोदरः । असम्भ्रान्तस्ततोबाणैर्निर्बिभेददुरासदाम् ।।6.98.13।।
explanation: Then seeing the formidable rock coming towards him, he was not bewildered and immediately struck and broke it with his arrows.

shloka_text: रक्षसातेनबाणौघैर्निकृत्तासासहस्रधा । निपपातशिलाभूमौगृध्रचक्रमिवाकुलम् ।।6.98.14।।
explanation: That rock, struck by Mahodara fell on the ground shattered and broken into a thousand pieces.

shloka_text: तांतुभिन्नांशिलांदृष्टवासुग्रीवःक्रोधमूर्छितः । सालमुत्पाट्यचिक्षेपराक्षसेरणमूर्थनि ।।6.98.15।।
explanation: Seeing the fragmented rock, Sugriva was deluded with anger, and tearing up a sala tree, he shattered on the Rakshasa (Mahodara) in the battlefield.

shloka_text: शरैश्चविददारैनंशूरःपरपुरञ्जयः । स ददर्शततःक्रुद्धःपरिघंपतितंभुवि ।।6.98.16।।
explanation: Mahodara, a scourge of enemy forces, who lacerated Sugriva in that manner, angry, made the tree fall on the ground.

shloka_text: आविध्यतु स तंदीप्तंपरिघंतस्यदर्शयन् । परिघाग्रेणवेगेनजघानास्यहयोत्तमान् ।6.98.17।।
explanation: Sugriva, picking up that glowing iron bar, exhibiting its top, whirling it around, struck the best of horses of Mahodara.

shloka_text: तस्माद्धतहयावदीरःसोऽऽवप्लुत्यमहारथात् । गदांजग्राहसंक्रुद्धोराक्षसोऽऽथमहोदरः ।।6.98.18।।
explanation: Then the hero, Mahodara, his horses destroyed, jumped from the great chariot, and took hold of a mace.

shloka_text: गदापरिघहस्तौतौयुधिवीरौसमीयतुः । नर्दन्तौगोवृषप्रख्यौघनाविवसविद्युतौ ।।6.98.19।।
explanation: Both the heroes, Mahodara and Sugriva like two bulls holding mace and iron bar respectively, like clouds charged with lightning came roaring in the battlefield.

shloka_text: ततःक्रुद्धोगदांतस्यैचिक्षेपरजनीचरः । ज्वलतनींभास्कराभासांसुग्रीवायमहोदरः ।।6.98.20।।
explanation: Then provoked by anger, the night ranger, Mahodara flung his mace at Sugriva which shone like the Sun.

shloka_text: गदांतांसुमहाघोरामापततनींमहाबलः । सुग्रीवोरोषताम्राक्षस्समुद्यम्यमहाहवे ।।6.98.21।। आजघानगदांतस्यपरिघेणहरीश्वर । पपात स गदोद्भिन्नःपरिघस्तस्यभूतले ।।6.98.22।।
explanation: In that terrible conflict, seeing the mace broken and falling, mighty Sugriva, whose eyes turned red in anger, lifted up his iron bar, struck at the mace of the Rakshasa. The mace fell on the ground and broke into pieces.

shloka_text: गदांतांसुमहाघोरामापततनींमहाबलः । सुग्रीवोरोषताम्राक्षस्समुद्यम्यमहाहवे ।।6.98.21।। आजघानगदांतस्यपरिघेणहरीश्वर । पपात स गदोद्भिन्नःपरिघस्तस्यभूतले ।।6.98.22।।
explanation: In that terrible conflict, seeing the mace broken and falling, mighty Sugriva, whose eyes turned red in anger, lifted up his iron bar, struck at the mace of the Rakshasa. The mace fell on the ground and broke into pieces.

shloka_text: ततोजग्राहतेजस्वीसुग्रीवोवसुधातलात् । आयसंमुसलंघोरंसर्वतोहेमभूषितम् ।।6.98.23।।
explanation: Then, energetic Sugriva picked from the ground a frightening steel club encrusted with gold on all sides.

shloka_text: स तमुद्यम्यचिक्षेपसोऽऽप्यन्यांव्याक्षिपद्गदाम् । भिन्नावन्योन्यमासाद्यपेततुद्दरणीतले ।।6.98.24।।
explanation: Sugriva took up the steel club and hurled at Mahodara who took another mace and hit back. Both collided with each other and shattered they fell down on the surface of the earth.

shloka_text: ततोग्नप्रहरणौमुष्टिभ्यांतौसमीयतुः । तेजोबलसमाविष्टौदीप्ताविवहुताशनौ ।।6.98.25।।
explanation: Thereafter, both of them fully endowed with strength, with their weapons broken, who resembled glowing fires, fought with their fists.

shloka_text: जघ्नतुस्तौतदान्योन्यंवेदतुश्चपुनःपुनः । तलैश्चान्योन्यमहत्यपेततुश्चमहीतले ।।6.98.26।।
explanation: Then both of them again and again striking each other slapping with palms fell down and rolled on the ground.

shloka_text: उत्पेततुस्ततस्तूर्णंजघ्नतुश्चपरस्परम् । भुजैश्चिक्षिपतुर्वीरावन्योन्यमपराजितौ ।।6.98.27।।
explanation: Then quickly getting up striking one another, both the heroes who have never been defeated, pushed each other by their arms.

shloka_text: जग्मतुस्तौश्रमंवीरौबाहुयुधेपरंतपौ । अजहारतदाखडगमदूरपरिवर्तिनम् ।।6.98.28।। राक्षसश्चर्मणासार्धंमहावेगोमहोदरः ।
explanation: Both being scourge of their enemies, both heroes wrestling were exhausted with fighting. Then the Rakshasa picked up a sword lying not far from there along with a shield.

shloka_text: थैव च महाखडगंचर्मणापतितंसह ।।6.98.29।। जग्राहवानरश्रेष्ठस्सुग्रीवोवेगवत्तरः।।
explanation: Likewise, Sugriva endowed with speed, a champion of Vanaras, took up a huge sword fallen down with a shield.

shloka_text: तौतुरोषपरीताङ्गौनर्दन्तावभ्यधावताम् ।।6.98.30।। उद्यतासीरणेहृष्टावुभौशस्त्रविशारदौ ।
explanation: Then the two, whose limbs ceased, who were knowledgeable in the use of weapons, furious, sprang forward in the battle, both with joy, roaring to destroy one another.

shloka_text: दक्षिणंमण्डलंचोभौसुतूर्णंसम्परीयतुः ।।6.98.31।। अन्योन्यमभिसङ्कृद्धौ जये प्रणिहितावुभौ ।
explanation: Enraged at one another, intent to win, both stretched forth at great speed, going from left to right in circles and encountered each other.

shloka_text: तुशूरोमहावेगोवीर्यश्लाघीमहोदरः ।।6.98.32।। महाचर्मणितंखडगंपातयामासदुर्मतिः ।
explanation: Mahodara, a warrior, evil minded one, endowed with great speed, hurled the sword on the shield of Sugriva.

shloka_text: लग्नमुत्कर्षतःखडगंखडगेनकपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.98.33।। जहारसशिरस्त्राणंकुण्डलोपहितंशिरः ।
explanation: While Mahodara was extracting the sword stuck to the head, Sugriva, the elephant of the monkeys, severed the head of Mahodara which was decked with earrings and helmet.

shloka_text: निकृत्तशिरसस्तस्यपतितस्यमहीतले ।।6.98.34।। तद्बलंराक्षसेन्द्रस्यदृष्टवातत्र न तिष्टते ।
explanation: Mahodara's head severed and fell on the ground. Seeing that Rakshasa king's army ran from there.

shloka_text: हत्वांतंवानरैस्सार्धंननादमुदितोहरिः ।।6.98.35।। चुक्रोध च दशग्रीवोबभौहृष्टश्चराघवः ।
explanation: Sugriva, the monkey leader having killed Mahodara, the Vanaras shouted in joy. The ten headed Ravana became enraged. Raghava was glad.

shloka_text: विषण्णवदनास्सर्वेराक्षसादीनचेतसः ।।6.98.36।। विद्रवन्तिततस्सर्वेभयवित्रस्तचेतसः ।
explanation: All the Rakshasas became dull and piteous with sad faces. Out of fear they ran.

shloka_text: महोदरंतंन्वििपात्यभूमौमहागिरेःकीर्णमिवैकदेशम् । सूर्यात्मजस्तत्ररराजलक्ष्म्यसूर्यस्स्वतेजोभिरिवाप्रधृष्यः ।।6.98.37।।
explanation: Just as a part of a huge mountain thrown down, an unassailable Mahodara, fallen on the ground, shone there like Lakshmi, just as the Sun shines by his own radiance.

shloka_text: महोदरेतुनिहतेमहापार्श्वोमहाबलः । सुग्रीवेणसमीक्ष्याथक्रोधात्सम्ररक्तलोचनः ।।6.99.1।। अङ्गदस्यचमूंभीमांक्षोभयामाससायकैः ।
explanation: Gazing at Mahodara killed by Sugriva, mighty Mahaparsva's eyes turned red in anger. He created a commotion in the army of Angada.

shloka_text: सवानराणांमुख्यानामुत्तमाङ्गानिसर्वशः ।।6.99.2।। पातयामानकायेभ्यःफलंवृन्तादिवानिलः ।
explanation: That leader (Mahaparsva) severed the heads of Vanara leaders from their body just as wind drops fruits from stalks.

shloka_text: केषांचिदिषुभिर्बाहुन् स्कन्धांश्छिच्छेदराक्षसः च ।।6.99.3।। वानराणांसुङ्कृद्ध: पार्श्वंकेषांव्यदारयत् ।
explanation: Then with his arrows, that Rakshasa (Mahaparsva) shattered the arms of some, shoulders of some, sides, and ribs of some Vanaras.

shloka_text: तेऽर्दिताबाणवर्षेणमहापार्श्वेनवानराः ।।6.99.4।। विषादविमुखाःसर्वेबभूवुर्गतचेतसः ।
explanation: By the rain of arrows of Mahaparsva, the Vanaras were dejected and wore a sad look on their face and lost senses.

shloka_text: निरीक्ष्यबलमुद्विग्नमङ्गदोराक्षसार्दितम् ।।6.99.5।। वेगंचक्रेमहावेगमहाबाहुस्समुद्रइवपर्वणि ।
explanation: Observing the army oppressed by the Rakshasa leader, Angada, endowed with broad shoulders, exhibited his might speedily like the ocean on full moon days.

shloka_text: आयसंपरिघंगृह्यसूर्यरमशिसमप्रभम् ।।6.99.6।। समरेवानरश्रेष्ठोमहापार्श्वेन्यपातयत् ।
explanation: The foremost of the Vanaras (Angada), taking an iron bar flung on Mahaparsva in the battlefield.

shloka_text: स तुतेनप्रहारेणमहापार्श्वोविचेतनः ।।6.99.7।। ससूतस्स्यन्दनात्तस्माद्विसंज्ञश्चापतद्भुवि ।
explanation: By that hit, Mahaparsva became unconscious and fell on the ground, senseless, from the chariot along with the charioteer.

shloka_text: स ऋक्षराजस्तेजस्वीनीलाञ्जनचयोपमः ।।6.99.8।। निष्पत्यसुमहावीर्यस्स्वाद्व्यूहन्मेघसन्निभात् । प्रगृह्यगिरिशृङ्गाभांक्रुद्धस्सविपुलांशिलाम् ।।6.99.9।। अश्वाञ्जघानतरसाबभञ्जतम् स्यन्दनं च तम् ।
explanation: Jambavantha, the mighty king of Bears, rushed from his army that looked like a dark cloud. The great hero with his army resembling a heap of black mountain, in his fury seized a huge rock resembling a mountain peak, crushed the chariot and struck the horses.

shloka_text: स ऋक्षराजस्तेजस्वीनीलाञ्जनचयोपमः ।।6.99.8।। निष्पत्यसुमहावीर्यस्स्वाद्व्यूहन्मेघसन्निभात् । प्रगृह्यगिरिशृङ्गाभांक्रुद्धस्सविपुलांशिलाम् ।।6.99.9।। अश्वाञ्जघानतरसाबभञ्जतम् स्यन्दनं च तम् ।
explanation: Jambavantha, the mighty king of Bears, rushed from his army that looked like a dark cloud. The great hero with his army resembling a heap of black mountain, in his fury seized a huge rock resembling a mountain peak, crushed the chariot and struck the horses.

shloka_text: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसंज्ञस्तुमहापार्श्वोमहाबलः ।।6.99.10।। अङ्गदंबहुभिर्बाणैर्भूयस्तंप्रत्यविध्यत ।
explanation: In a short while, regaining consciousness, mighty Mahaparsva struck Angada again with many shafts.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तंत्रिभिर्बाणैराजघानस्तनान्तरे ।।6.99.11।। ऋक्षराजंगवाक्षं च जघानबहुभिश्शरैः ।
explanation: Mahaparsva pierced three shafts into the chest of Jambavantha and attacked Gavaksha with many arrows.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तंगवाक्षं च स दृष्टवाशरपीडितौ ।।6.99.12।। जग्राहपरिघंघोरमङ्गदःक्रोधमूर्छितः ।
explanation: Seeing Gavaksha and Jambavantha afflicted by shafts, deluded with anger, Angada took hold of a dreadful iron bar.

shloka_text: तस्याङ्गदःप्रकुपितोराक्षसस्यतमायसम् ।।6.99.13।। दूरस्थितस्यपरिघंरविरश्मिसमप्रभम् । द्वावाभ्यांभुजाभ्यांसङ्गृह्यभ्रामयित्वा च वेगवान् ।।6.99.14।। महापार्श्वस्यचिक्षेपवधार्थंवालिनस्सुतः ।
explanation: Vali's son Angada got enraged, seized an iron bar which shone like the radiant sun's rays and stood at a distance to kill Mahaparsva. Angada whirling the iron bar round and round hurled it around and thrown at Mahaparsva.

shloka_text: तस्याङ्गदःप्रकुपितोराक्षसस्यतमायसम् ।।6.99.13।। दूरस्थितस्यपरिघंरविरश्मिसमप्रभम् । द्वावाभ्यांभुजाभ्यांसङ्गृह्यभ्रामयित्वा च वेगवान् ।।6.99.14।। महापार्श्वस्यचिक्षेपवधार्थंवालिनस्सुतः ।
explanation: Vali's son Angada got enraged, seized an iron bar which shone like the radiant sun's rays and stood at a distance to kill Mahaparsva. Angada whirling the iron bar round and round hurled it around and thrown at Mahaparsva.

shloka_text: स तुक्षिप्तोबलवतापरिघन्तस्यरक्षसः ।।6.99.15।। धनुश्चसशरंहस्ताछचिरस्त्रांचाप्यपातयत् ।
explanation: That iron bar hurled by Angada hit the forehead of the Rakshasa.

shloka_text: तंसमासाद्यवेगेनवालिपुत्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.99.16।। तलेनाभ्यहनत्क्रुद्धः कर्णमूले सकुण्डले ।
explanation: Courageous son of Vali, enraged, with all speed, slapped the Rakshasa's ear adorned with shining earrings, with his palm.

shloka_text: स तुक्रुद्धोमहावेगोमहापार्श्वोमहाद्युति ।।6.99.17।। करेणैकेनजग्राहसुमहान्तंपरश्वथम् ।
explanation: Angry Mahaparsva, who was endowed with speed and shining brightly, took hold of an extraordinary battle axe in one hand.

shloka_text: तंम्तैलधौतंविमलंशैलसारमयंदृढम् ।।6.99.18।। राक्षसःपरमक्रुद्धोवालिपुत्रेन्यपातयत् ।
explanation: Extremely enraged Rakshasa, hurled at Vali's son that axe that was cleansed with oil, the clean strong axe that was like feet of a mountain.

shloka_text: तेनवामांसफलकेभृशंप्रत्यवपादितम् ।।6.99.19।। अङ्गदोमोक्ष्यामाससरोषस्सपरश्वधम् ।
explanation: Angada, full of fury, escaped Mahaparsva's aim to strike his left shoulder blade in violence.

shloka_text: सवीरोवज्रसङ्काशमङ्गदोमुष्टिमात्मनः ।।6.99.20।। संवर्तयत्सुसङ्कृद्धःपितृतुल्यपराक्रमः ।
explanation: Angada, who was equal to his father in his prowess, was highly furious and himself clenched his fist which resembled thunderbolt.

shloka_text: राक्षसस्यस्तनाभ्याशेमर्मज्ञोहृदयंप्रति ।।6.99.21।। इन्द्राशनिमस्पर्शं स मुष्टिंविन्यपातयत् ।
explanation: Angada who knew the vital parts, pierced into the middle of the breasts of the Rakshasa into the heart by his fist which was equal to Indra's thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तेनतस्यनिपातेनराक्षसस्यमहामृधे ।।6.99.22।। पफालहृदयंचास्य स पपातहतोभुवि ।
explanation: In that great conflict, struck by the fist, the Rakshasa (Mahaparsva's) heart broke and killed and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: स्मिन्निपतितेभूमौतत्सैन्यंसम्प्रचुक्षुभे ।।6.99.23।। अभवच्चमहान्क्रोधस्समरेरावणस्यतु ।
explanation: Mahaparsva having fallen down in the battle, the army was bewildered, and Ravana was overcome with anger.

shloka_text: वानराणांश्चहृष्टानांसिंहनादःसुपुष्कलः ।।6.99.24।। स्पोटयन्निवशब्देनलङ्कांसाट्टालगोपुराम् । महेन्द्रेणेवदेवानांनादस्समभवन्महान् ।।6.99.25।।
explanation: Highly rejoiced Vanaras roared in high pitch sound. The tall attics and gates of Lanka vibrated with sound. Even the gods, accompanied by Indra, made great sounds.

shloka_text: वानराणांश्चहृष्टानांसिंहनादःसुपुष्कलः ।।6.99.24।। स्पोटयन्निवशब्देनलङ्कांसाट्टालगोपुराम् । महेन्द्रेणेवदेवानांनादस्समभवन्महान् ।।6.99.25।।
explanation: Highly rejoiced Vanaras roared in high pitch sound. The tall attics and gates of Lanka vibrated with sound. Even the gods, accompanied by Indra, made great sounds.

shloka_text: महोदरमहापार्श्वौहतौदृष्टवातुराक्ष । तस्मिंश्चनिहतेवीरेविरूपाक्षेमहाबले ।।6.100.1।। आविवेशमहान् क्रोधोरावणंतुमहामृधे । सूतं सञ्चोदयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ।।6.100.2।।
explanation: On seeing Mahodara and Mahaparsva killed in the great war, Virupaksha of extraordinary might also killed, Ravana was highly infuriated and addressed the charioteer in the following words.

shloka_text: महोदरमहापार्श्वौहतौदृष्टवातुराक्ष । तस्मिंश्चनिहतेवीरेविरूपाक्षेमहाबले ।।6.100.1।। आविवेशमहान् क्रोधोरावणंतुमहामृधे । सूतं सञ्चोदयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ।।6.100.2।।
explanation: On seeing Mahodara and Mahaparsva killed in the great war, Virupaksha of extraordinary might also killed, Ravana was highly infuriated and addressed the charioteer in the following words.

shloka_text: निहतानाममात्यानांरुद्धस्यनगरस्य च । दुःखमेवापनेष्यामि हत्या तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ।।6.100.3।।
explanation: "On killing both Rama and Lakshmana, I will relieve the sorrow of ministers killed and of Lanka from suffering.

shloka_text: रामवृक्षंरणेहमनिसीतापुष्पफलप्रदम् । प्रशाखायस्यसुग्रीवोजाम्बवान्कुमुदोनलः ।।6.100.4।। दिविदश्चैवमैन्दश्चअङ्गदोगन्दमादनः । हनुमांश्चसुषेणव्चसर्वे च हरियूथपाः ।।6.100.5।।
explanation: That tree in the shape of Rama for which Sugriva, Jambavan, Kumuda, Dwivida, Mainda, Angada, Gandhamadana and Hanuman are the principal branches, that tree which will yield flowers and fruit in the shape of Sita will be cut down in the battle.

shloka_text: रामवृक्षंरणेहमनिसीतापुष्पफलप्रदम् । प्रशाखायस्यसुग्रीवोजाम्बवान्कुमुदोनलः ।।6.100.4।। दिविदश्चैवमैन्दश्चअङ्गदोगन्दमादनः । हनुमांश्चसुषेणव्चसर्वे च हरियूथपाः ।।6.100.5।।
explanation: That tree in the shape of Rama for which Sugriva, Jambavan, Kumuda, Dwivida, Mainda, Angada, Gandhamadana and Hanuman are the principal branches, that tree which will yield flowers and fruit in the shape of Sita will be cut down in the battle.

shloka_text: स दिशोदशघोषेणरथस्यातिरथोमहान् । नादयन् प्रययौतूर्णंराघवंचाभ्यधावत ।।6.100.6।।
explanation: Ravana, the great charioteer, who could surpass many rushed quickly towards Raghava, by the chariot making great noise reverberating in all directions.

shloka_text: पूरितातेनशब्देनसनदीगिरिकानना । सञ्चचाल मही सर्वा त्रस्तसिंहमृगद्विजा ।।6.100.7।।
explanation: By that sound, the rivers, mountains, and forests including the earth, filled with the boars, lions and other beasts were shaken.

shloka_text: तामसंसुमहाघोरंचकारास्त्रंसुदारुणम् । निर्ददाहकपीन् सर्वांस्तेप्रपेतुःसमन्ततः ।।6.100.8।।
explanation: He released an exceedingly formidable weapon called Taamasa which consumed all the monkeys all over and had fallen.

shloka_text: उत्पपातरजोभूमौतैर्भग्नैःसम्प्रधावितैः । न हितत्सहितुंशेकुर्भ्रह्मणानिर्मितंस्वयम् ।।6.100.9।।
explanation: As the Taamasa missile had been built and bestowed by Brahma, the monkeys were unable to bear and by their running dust had risen.

shloka_text: तान्यनीकान्यनेकानि रावणस्य शरोत्तमैः । दृष्टवाभग्नानि शतशो राघवः पर्यवस्थितः ।।6.100.10।।
explanation: Ravana's shafts had burnt many hundreds of Vanaras in war and seeing that Rama took a firm stand.

shloka_text: ततोराक्षसशार्दूलोविद्राव्यहरिवाहिनीम् । स ददर्शततोरामंतिष्ठन्तमपराजितम् ।।6.100.11।। लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राविष्णुनावासवंयथा । अलिखन्तमिवाकाशमवष्टभ्यमहद्धनुः ।।6.100.12।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षंदीर्घबाहुमरिन्दमम् ।
explanation: Thereafter, the tiger among Rakshasas having routed the Vanaras from there, saw the lotus petaleyed Rama, endowed with long arms, an unconquered one, the tamer of enemies, standing with his brother Lakshmana like Lord Vishnu with Indra, holding a huge bow that was scraping the sky.

shloka_text: ततोराक्षसशार्दूलोविद्राव्यहरिवाहिनीम् । स ददर्शततोरामंतिष्ठन्तमपराजितम् ।।6.100.11।। लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राविष्णुनावासवंयथा । अलिखन्तमिवाकाशमवष्टभ्यमहद्धनुः ।।6.100.12।। पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षंदीर्घबाहुमरिन्दमम् ।
explanation: Thereafter, the tiger among Rakshasas having routed the Vanaras from there, saw the lotus petaleyed Rama, endowed with long arms, an unconquered one, the tamer of enemies, standing with his brother Lakshmana like Lord Vishnu with Indra, holding a huge bow that was scraping the sky.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजाःसौमित्रिसहितोबली ।।6.100.13।। वानरांश्चरणेभग्नानापतन्तं च रावणम् । समीक्ष्यराघवोहृष्टोमध्येजग्राहकार्मुकम् ।।6.100.14।।
explanation: Then the highly brilliant, mighty Raghava along with Saumithri, witnessing the Vanaras routed in war and Ravana coming towards him. joyful Rama took hold of his bow and held in the midst.

shloka_text: ततोरामोमहातेजाःसौमित्रिसहितोबली ।।6.100.13।। वानरांश्चरणेभग्नानापतन्तं च रावणम् । समीक्ष्यराघवोहृष्टोमध्येजग्राहकार्मुकम् ।।6.100.14।।
explanation: Then the highly brilliant, mighty Raghava along with Saumithri, witnessing the Vanaras routed in war and Ravana coming towards him. joyful Rama took hold of his bow and held in the midst.

shloka_text: विस्फारयितुमारेभेततः स धनुरुत्तमम् । महावेगंमहानादंनिर्भन्दन्निवमेदिनीम् ।।6.100.15।।
explanation: Then he began to stretch his best bow endowed with an impelling force, sounding as if breaking the earth.

shloka_text: रावणस्य च बाणौघैरामविस्फारितेन च । शब्देनराक्षसास्तेन पेतुश्च शतशस्तदा ।।6.100.16।।
explanation: Then by Ravana's shafts and Sri Rama's stretching of the bow and sound of twang, Rakshasas fell in hundreds.

shloka_text: तयोःशरपथंप्राप्यरावणोराजपुत्रयोः । स बभौ च यथाराहुःसमीपशशिसूर्ययोः ।।6.100.17।।
explanation: That way when the two princes came near the range of Ravana's arrows, it was like the Sun and the moon near planet Rahu.

shloka_text: तमिच्छन् प्रधमम् योद्धुंलक्ष्मणोनिशितैःशरैः । मुमोचधनुरायम्यशरानग्निशिखोपमान् ।।6.100.18।।
explanation: Lakshmana desiring to fight first stretched his bow and took out his sharp arrows which were like peaks of fire and released.

shloka_text: तान्मुक्तमात्रानाकाशे लक्ष्मणेन धनुष्मता । बाणान् बाणैर्महातेजा रावणः प्रत्यवारयत् ।।6.100.19।।
explanation: As soon as the excellent archer, Lakshmana released his arrows, effulgent Ravana intercepted the arrows in the sky.

shloka_text: एकमेकेनबाणेनत्रिभिस्त्रीन् दशभिर्दश । लक्ष्मणस्य प्रचिच्छेद दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम् ।।6.100.20।।
explanation: Exhibiting his skill by hand, he split the arrows of Lakshmana with only one arrow, three with three and ten with ten.

shloka_text: अभ्यतिक्रम्यसौमित्रिंरावणःसमितिञ्जयः । आससादरणेरामंस्थितंशैलमिवापरम् ।।6.100.21।।
explanation: Ravana, who won many battles, overlooking Lakshmana went towards Rama standing like a rock in the battle.

shloka_text: स राघवंसमासाद्यक्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः । व्यसृजच्छरवर्षाणिरावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।।6.100.22।।
explanation: Ravana the king of Rakshasas coming near Raghava with angry looks in his eyes, showered rain of arrows at Rama.

shloka_text: शराधारास्ततोरामोरावणस्यधनुश्च्युताः । दृष्टवैवापतिताःशीघ्रंभल्लान् जग्राहसत्वरम् ।।6.100.23।।
explanation: Then Rama immediately seized hold of bhallas and released swiftly seeing Ravana's volley of arrows flowing.

shloka_text: तान् शरौघांस्ततोभल्लैस्तीक्ष्णैश्चिच्छेदराघवः । दीप्यमानान् महाघोरान्क्रुद्धानाशीविषानिव ।।6.100.24।।
explanation: Thereafter, Raghava with glowing terrific arrows, which were like poisonous serpents split the sharp streams of arrows.

shloka_text: राघवोरावणंतूर्णंरावणोराघवंतथा । अन्योन्यंविविधैस्तीक्ष्णैःशरवर्षैर्ववर्षतुः ।।6.100.25।।
explanation: Thus, Raghava on Ravana and Ravana on Raghava, in that manner sharp arrows showered on one another.

shloka_text: चेरतुश्चचिरंचित्रंमण्डलंसव्यदक्षिणम् । बाणवेगात्समुत्क्षिप्तावन्योन्यमपराजितौ ।।6.100.26।।
explanation: Each of them pushing one another by the speed of the arrows, went round in circles and created wonderful rounds.

shloka_text: तयोर्भूतानिवित्रेसुर्युगपत्सम्प्रयुध्यतोः । रौद्रयोःसायकमुचोर्यमान्तकनिकाशयोः ।।6.100.27।।
explanation: Just as created beings fight at the end of the dissolution of the universe, like God of death and God of retribution, both were fighting discharging arrows which was frightening to all beings.

shloka_text: सततंविविधैर्बाणैर्बभूवगगनंतदा । घनैरिवातपापायेविद्युन्मालाससमाकुलैः ।।6.100.28।।
explanation: Then the sky overcast with arrows of different kinds seemed like clouds with flashes of lightning.

shloka_text: गवाक्षितमिवाकाशंबभूवशरवृष्टिभिः । महावेगैस्सुतीक्ष्णैग्रैर्गृध्रपत्रैःसुवाजितैः ।।6.100.29।।
explanation: By the speed of the arrows with sharp heads, with plumes of eagles, the shower of extremely pointed arrows covering the sky made it dark and seemed like windows in the sky.

shloka_text: शरान्धकारमाकाशंचक्रतुःप्रथमंतदा । गतेऽस्तं तपने चापि महामेघाविवोथतितौ ।।6.100.30।।
explanation: Then the sky covered with darkness of arrows was like two huge clouds rising even though the Sun had set.

shloka_text: तयोरभून्महद्युद्धमन्योन्यवथकाङ्क्षिणोः । अनासाद्यमच्नित्यं च वृत्रवासवयोरिव ।।6.100.31।।
explanation: Each of them desiring to end the other, fought a terrific battle like Vrtra and Indra earlier, a great fight unimaginable for others.

shloka_text: उभौहिपरमेष्वासावुभौयुद्धविशारदौ । उभावस्त्रविदां मुख्यावुभौ युद्धेविचेरतुः ।।6.100.32।।
explanation: Both Rama and Ravana were armed with excellent bows, both highly skilled in war, both adept in the use of missiles, both were foremost in fighting and were unmoved.

shloka_text: उभौहियेनव्रजतस्तेनतेनशरोर्मयः । ऊर्मयोवायुनाविद्धा जग्मुः सागरयोरिव ।।6.100.33।।
explanation: Whichever course they took, by those streams of arrows were seen like waves in two oceans stirred up by the wind.

shloka_text: ततःसंसक्तहस्तस्तुरावणोलोकरावणः । नराचमालांरामस्यललाटेप्रत्यमुञ्चत ।।6.100.34।।
explanation: Then Ravana, who made the people cry, whose hands were engaged in the fight, discharged a row of steel arrows into Rama's forehead.

shloka_text: रौद्रचापप्रयुक्तांतांनीलोत्पलदलप्रभाम् । शिरसाधारयद्रामो न व्यथमभ्यपद्यत ।।6.100.35।।
explanation: Rama, into whose forehead Ravana had stuck arrows, felt them like blue lotuses released from his bow, and did not experience any pain.

shloka_text: अथमन्त्रानभिजपन्रौद्रमस्तमुदीरयन् । शरान् भूयःसमादाय रामः क्रोधसमन्वितः ।।6.100.36।। मुमोच च महातेजाश्चापमायम्यवीर्यवान् ।
explanation: Then valiant and bright Rama, enraged, chanting the mantras of missiles presided over by Rudra (God of destruction) taking many more arrows, stretching the bow, and fixing discharged arrows.

shloka_text: तेमहामेघसङ्काशेकवचेपतिताःशराः ।।6.100.37।। अवध्येराक्षसेन्द्रस्य न व्यथांजनयंस्तदा ।
explanation: Fallen on the impenetrable shield of Ravana, those arrows did not inflict any pain.

shloka_text: पुनरेवाधतंरामोरथस्थंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.100.38।। ललाटेपरमास्त्रणसर्वास्त्रकुशलोऽभिनत् ।
explanation: Again Rama, who was skilled in the use of all weapons, pierced that king of Rakshasas seated in the chariot with an excellent missile on the forehead.

shloka_text: तेभित्त्वाबाणरूपाणिपञ्चशीर्षाइवोरगाः ।।6.100.39।। श्वसन्तोविविशुर्भूमिंरावणप्रतिकूलिताः ।
explanation: The five headed serpent like arrows released by Rama penetrated and having been repelled by Ravana they entered the earth hissing.

shloka_text: निहत्यराघवस्यास्त्रंरावणःक्रोधमूर्छितः ।।6.100.40।। असुरंसुमहाघोरमन्यदस्त्रं चकारसः ।
explanation: Making Rama's missile void, Ravana manifested another missile presided over by demon and released.

shloka_text: सिंहव्याघ्रमुखांश्चापिकङ्ककाकमुखानपि ।।6.100.41।। गृध्रश्येनमुखांश्चापिशृगाववदनांस्तथा । ईहामृगमुखांश्चापिव्यादितास्यान् भयावहान् ।।6.100.42।। पञ्चास्यान् लेलिहानांश्चससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।
explanation: Arrows having lion and tiger face, buzzards and red geese face, eagles and falcons faced, in the same way arrows with jackals' face, wolves' face, terrible with mouth wide open five headed serpent like fearful sharp arrows were released by Ravana.

shloka_text: सिंहव्याघ्रमुखांश्चापिकङ्ककाकमुखानपि ।।6.100.41।। गृध्रश्येनमुखांश्चापिशृगाववदनांस्तथा । ईहामृगमुखांश्चापिव्यादितास्यान् भयावहान् ।।6.100.42।। पञ्चास्यान् लेलिहानांश्चससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।
explanation: Arrows having lion and tiger face, buzzards and red geese face, eagles and falcons faced, in the same way arrows with jackals' face, wolves' face, terrible with mouth wide open five headed serpent like fearful sharp arrows were released by Ravana.

shloka_text: शरान् खरमुखांश्चान्यान्वराहमुखसंश्रितान् ।।6.100.43।। श्वानकुक्कुटवक्त्रांश्चमकराशीविषाननान् । एतांश्चान्यांश्चमायावीससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।।6.100.44।। रामंप्रतिमहातेजाःक्रुद्धस्सर्पइवश्वसन् ।
explanation: Deceitful and energetic Ravana provoked by anger, let loose more arrows of boar faced, dog faced, cocks faced, and alligators and serpents faced hissing like serpents and other such arrows against Rama.

shloka_text: शरान् खरमुखांश्चान्यान्वराहमुखसंश्रितान् ।।6.100.43।। श्वानकुक्कुटवक्त्रांश्चमकराशीविषाननान् । एतांश्चान्यांश्चमायावीससर्जनिशितान् शरान् ।।6.100.44।। रामंप्रतिमहातेजाःक्रुद्धस्सर्पइवश्वसन् ।
explanation: Deceitful and energetic Ravana provoked by anger, let loose more arrows of boar faced, dog faced, cocks faced, and alligators and serpents faced hissing like serpents and other such arrows against Rama.

shloka_text: असुरेणसमाविष्टंसोऽस्त्रणरघुपुङ्गवः ।।6.100.45।। ससर्जास्त्रं महोत्साहः पावकः पावकोपमः ।
explanation: In that way facing the demonic missiles, the leader of Raghus, overwhelmed, very enthusiastic, released missiles presided over by God of fire.

shloka_text: अग्निदीप्तमुखान्बाणांस्तत्रसूर्यमुखानपि ।।6.100.46।। चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रवक्रांश्चधूमकेतुमुखानपि । ग्रहनक्षत्रवर्णांश्चमहोल्कामुखसंस्थितान् ।।6.100.47।। विद्युजजिह्वोपमांश्चापिससर्ज विविधान् शरान् ।
explanation: There Rama produced missiles glowing like fire, like Sun 's face, like moon's face, crescent moon face, face like Dhumakethu, missiles like planets, and star faced, with fire sticks like face resembling flashes and lightning and several others and let loose.

shloka_text: अग्निदीप्तमुखान्बाणांस्तत्रसूर्यमुखानपि ।।6.100.46।। चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रवक्रांश्चधूमकेतुमुखानपि । ग्रहनक्षत्रवर्णांश्चमहोल्कामुखसंस्थितान् ।।6.100.47।। विद्युजजिह्वोपमांश्चापिससर्ज विविधान् शरान् ।
explanation: There Rama produced missiles glowing like fire, like Sun 's face, like moon's face, crescent moon face, face like Dhumakethu, missiles like planets, and star faced, with fire sticks like face resembling flashes and lightning and several others and let loose.

shloka_text: तेरावणशराघोराराघवास्त्रसमाहताः ।।6.100.48।। विलयं जग्मुराकाशे जग्मुश्चैव सहस्रशः ।
explanation: Struck by Raghava's missiles, the terrific missiles of Ravana melted in the air and split into thousands of pieces.

shloka_text: तदस्त्रंनिहतंदृष्टवारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.100.49।। हृष्टानेदुस्ततःसर्वेकपयःकामरूपिणः । सुग्रीवप्रमुखावीराःसम्परिक्षिप्यराघवम् ।।6.100.50।।
explanation: Sugriva and other leaders, heroes who can change form at their will and all monkeys rejoiced.

shloka_text: तदस्त्रंनिहतंदृष्टवारामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।।6.100.49।। हृष्टानेदुस्ततःसर्वेकपयःकामरूपिणः । सुग्रीवप्रमुखावीराःसम्परिक्षिप्यराघवम् ।।6.100.50।।
explanation: Sugriva and other leaders, heroes who can change form at their will and all monkeys rejoiced.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रतिहतेऽस्त्रेतुरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । क्रोधं च द्विगुणंचक्रेक्रोधाच्चास्त्रमनन्तरम् ।।6.101.1।।
explanation: Missile being counteracted, Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, doubled the army later in anger.

shloka_text: मयेनविहितंरौद्रमन्यदस्त्रंमहाद्युतिः । उत्सृष्टुंरावणोभीमंराघवायप्रचक्रमे ।।6.101.2।।
explanation: Highly effulgent Ravana used another terrific missile, presided over by Rudra, produced by Maya.

shloka_text: ततःशूलानिनिश्चेरुर्गदाश्चमुसलानि च । कार्मुकाद्दीप्यमानानिवज्रसाराणिसर्वशः ।।6.101.3।।
explanation: Then from his bow issued forth all over flaming tridents, maces, and iron bars like thunderbolt.

shloka_text: मुद्गराःकूटपाशाश्चदीप्ताश्चाशनयस्तथा । निष्पेतुर्विविधास्तीक्ष्णावाताइवयुगक्षये ।।6.101.4।।
explanation: Several kinds of sharp multitudes of weapons and flaming thunderbolts issued forth like gales at the time of universal destruction.

shloka_text: तदस्त्रंराघव्श्रीमानुत्तमास्त्रविदांवरः । जघानपरमास्त्रणगान्धर्वेणमहाद्युतिः ।।6.101.5।।
explanation: Glorious Raghava, who is the best of those proficient in the use of missiles endowed with great splendour, neutralized that missile (of Ravana) with the missile presided over by Gandharvas.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रतिहतेऽतुराघवेणमहात्मना । रावणःक्रोधाताम्राक्षस्सौरमस्त्रमुदैरयत् ।।6.101.6।।
explanation: When the missile of Ravana was turned void by the great selfRaghava, Ravana's eyes turned red in anger, and he used a missile presided over by the Sun God.

shloka_text: ततश्चक्राणिनिष्पेतुर्भास्वराणिमहान्ति च । कार्मुकाद्भीमवेगस्यदशग्रीवस्यधीमतः ।।6.101.7।।
explanation: Thereafter, brilliant discus of the Sun God, issued forth from wise Ravana's bow at a terrific speed.

shloka_text: तैरासीद्गगनंदीप्तंसन्ततद्भिःरितस्ततः । पतद्भिश्चदिशोदीप्ताश्चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहैरिव ।।6.101.8।।
explanation: As they landed together from the sky glowing like Sun, moon, and the planets, it illuminated the quarters.

shloka_text: तानिचिच्छेदबाणौघैश्चक्राणितु स राघवः । आयुधानि च चित्राणिरावणस्यचमूमुखे ।।6.101.9।।
explanation: Raghava with his shafts shattered the discuses and the weapons of Ravana in the forefront of his army.

shloka_text: तदस्त्रंतुहतंदृष्टवारावणोराक्षसाधिपः । विव्याथदशभिर्बाणैरामंसर्वेषुमर्मसु ।।6.101.10।।
explanation: Rakshasa king, frustrated on seeing the missiles, pierced Rama in his private parts with shafts.

shloka_text: स विद्धोदशभिर्बाणैर्महाकार्मुकनिस्सृतैः । रावणेनमहातेजा न प्राकम्पतराघवः ।।6.101.11।।
explanation: Even though pierced by Ravana with ten arrows, Rama, endowed with high energy, was not shaken.

shloka_text: ततोविव्याथगात्रेषुसर्वेषुसमितिञ्जयः । राघवस्तुसुसङ्क्रुद्धोरावणंबहुभिश्शरैः ।।6.101.12।।
explanation: Then, Raghava, who had won many battles, became highly furious, piercing Ravana in all his limbs with many arrows.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेक्रुद्धोराघवस्यानुजोबली । लक्ष्मणःसायकान्सप्तजग्राहपरवीरहा ।।6.101.13।।
explanation: In the meantime, enraged Lakshmana, the brother of Rama, a mighty warrior, seized hold of seven shafts.

shloka_text: तै: स्सायकैर्महावेगैरावणस्यमहाद्युति । ध्वजंमनुष्यशीर्षंतुतस्यचिच्छेदनैकधा ।।6.101.14।।
explanation: Lakshmana, who was endowed with extraordinary splendour, for his part, with his shafts which had great force, shattered the device of man's head on the flag post of Ravana.

shloka_text: सारदथेश्चापिबाणेनशिरोज्वलितकुण्डलम् । जहारलक्ष्मणःश्रीमान्नैरृतस्यमहाबलः ।।6.101.15।।
explanation: Celebrated, mighty Lakshmana struck with his arrows, that hit the head of the charioteer of night ranger, which was glittering with earrings.

shloka_text: तस्यबाणैश्चचिच्छेदधनुर्गजकरोपमम् । लक्ष्मणोराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपञ्चभिर्निशितैस्तदा ।।6.101.16।।
explanation: Then Lakshmana split with five sharpened arrows the bow of Rakshasa king that resembled elephant's trunk.

shloka_text: नीलमेघनिभांश्चास्यसदश्वान् पर्वतोपमान् । जघानाप्लुत्यगदयारावणस्यविभीषणः ।।6.101.17।।
explanation: Vibheeshana struck with his formidable mace the horses of Ravana which were like dark clouds and huge like mountains.

shloka_text: हताश्वात्त्तुस्वोवेगादवप्लुत्यमहारथात् । कोपमाहारत्तीव्रंभ्रातरंप्रतिरावणः ।।6.101.18।।
explanation: With the horses of his chariot dead, Ravana descended from the huge chariot and exhibited violent rage against his brother.

shloka_text: ततश्शक्तिंमहाशक्तिर्दीप्तार्दीप्ताशनीमिव । विभीषणस्यचिक्षेपराक्षसेन्द्रःप्रतापवान् ।।6.101.19।।
explanation: Then, endowed with extraordinary energy, the powerful leader of Rakshasas hurled a flaming thunderbolt like javelin at Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: अप्राप्तामेवतांबाणैस्त्रिभिश्चिच्छेदलक्ष्मणः । अथोदतिष्ठत्सन्नादोवानराणांमहारणे ।।6.101.20।।
explanation: Lakshmana shattered the javelin with three shafts even before it reached him (Vibheeshana). Then the Vanaras raised loud cheer in that huge conflict.

shloka_text: स पपातत्रिधाछिन्नाशक्तिःकाञ्चनमालिनी । सविस्फुलिङ्गाज्वलितामहोल्केवदिवश्च्युता ।।6.101.21।।
explanation: The javelin, which was covered with gold, broke into three parts, and fell down like a huge meteor emitting fire sparks from the heavens.

shloka_text: ततःसम्भाविततरांकालेनापिदुरासदाम् । जग्राहविपुलांशक्तिंदीप्यमानांस्वतेजसा ।।6.101.22।।
explanation: Then, Ravana seized hold of a huge javelin shining with its own splendour, a formidable one even for the god of death.

shloka_text: सावेगिताबलवतारावणेनदुरात्मना । जज्वालसुमहातेजादीप्ताशनिसमप्रभा ।।6.101.23।।
explanation: That javelin was endowed with speed, resembling thunderbolt in splendour, whirled round by the mighty and evilminded Ravana, shone.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेवीरोलक्ष्मणस्तंविभीषणम् । प्राणसंशयमापन्नंतूर्णमभ्यवपद्यत ।।6.101.24।।
explanation: In the meantime, seeing Vibheeshana's life in danger, heroic Lakshmana reached him and stood obstructing (the javelin).

shloka_text: तंविमोक्षयितुंवीरश्चापमायम्यलक्ष्मणः । रावणंशक्तिहस्तंवैशरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ।।6.101.25।।
explanation: Heroic Lakshmana stretched his bow and showered volley of arrows and covered Ravana who held javelin in hand.

shloka_text: कीर्यमाणश्शरौघेणविसृष्टेनमहात्मना । न प्रहर्तुंमनश्चक्रेविमुखीकृतविक्रमः ।।6.101.26।।
explanation: Covered by the stream of shafts discharged by the great self, Lakshmana, Ravana could not shake his hand and was not inclined in his mind to strike (Vibheeshana).

shloka_text: मोक्षितंभ्रातरंदृष्टवालक्ष्मणेन स रावणः । लक्ष्मणाभिमुखस्तिष्ठन्निदंवचनमब्रवीत् ।।6.101.27।।
explanation: Thus spoke Ravana seeing Lakshmana who stood facing him, who rescued his brother (Vibheeshana).

shloka_text: मोक्षितस्तेबलश्लाघिन्यस्मादेवंविभीषणः । विमुच्यराक्षसंशक्तिस्त्वयीयंविनिपात्यते ।।6.101.28।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! You are proud of your might of rescuing Vibheeshana. Now this javelin released from me will strike at you."

shloka_text: एषातेहृदयंभित्त्वाशक्तिर्लोहितलक्षणा । मद्भाहुपरिघोत्सृष्टाप्राणानादाययास्यति ।।6.101.29।।
explanation: "This javelin released by my bludgeonlike arm will pierce your heart and take away your life."

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तातांशक्तिमष्टघण्टांमहास्वनाम् । मयेनमायाविहिताममोघंशत्रुघातिनीम् ।।6.101.30।। लक्ष्मणायसमुद्धिश्यज्वलन्तीमिवतेजसा । रावणःपरमक्रुद्धश्चिक्षेप च ननाद च ।।6.101.31।।
explanation: Enraged Ravana, having spoken in this manner, hurled the javelin adorned with eight bells making loud noise, designed magically by Maya, a stupendous one capable of destroying any enemy, which was glowing with shine, aiming at Lakshmana, and roared aloud.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तातांशक्तिमष्टघण्टांमहास्वनाम् । मयेनमायाविहिताममोघंशत्रुघातिनीम् ।।6.101.30।। लक्ष्मणायसमुद्धिश्यज्वलन्तीमिवतेजसा । रावणःपरमक्रुद्धश्चिक्षेप च ननाद च ।।6.101.31।।
explanation: Enraged Ravana, having spoken in this manner, hurled the javelin adorned with eight bells making loud noise, designed magically by Maya, a stupendous one capable of destroying any enemy, which was glowing with shine, aiming at Lakshmana, and roared aloud.

shloka_text: साक्षिप्ताभीमवेगेनवज्राशनिसमस्वना । शक्तिरभ्यपतद्वेगाल्लक्ष्मणंरणमूर्धनि ।।6.101.32।।
explanation: Hurled at terrific speed, that javelin, which was equal to thunderbolt, speedily went towards Lakshmana in the forefront of war.

shloka_text: तामनुव्याहरच्छक्तिमापतन्तीं स राघवः । स्वस्त्यस्तुलक्ष्मणआयेतिमोघाभवहतोद्यमा ।।6.101.33।।
explanation: Seeing the javelin coming towards Lakshmana, Raghava said 'May Lakshmana be auspicious. May he be well. May your attempt to kill Lakshmana be ineffective and wasted'.

shloka_text: रावणेनरणेशक्तिःक्रुद्धेनाशीविषोपमाः । मुक्ताशूरस्यभीतस्यलक्ष्मणस्यममज्जसा ।।6.101.34।।
explanation: Released by Ravana in anger, that javelin, which was like poison of venomous serpent, pierced into the chest of Lakshmana who stood fearless.

shloka_text: न्यपतत्सामहावेगालक्ष्मणस्यमहोरसि । जिह्वेवोरगराजस्यदीप्यमानामहाद्युतिः ।।6.101.35।।
explanation: Glowing like the tongue of Vasuki, the king of serpents, flaming, त्त्जवेलिन descended at high speed on the chest of Lakshmana.

shloka_text: ततोरावणवेगेनसुदूरमवगाढया । शक्त्याविभिन्नहृदयःपपातभुविलक्ष्मणः ।।6.101.36।।
explanation: Thereafter, Lakshmana fell on the ground, pierced by the javelin, deep into the heart from far with great force by Ravana.

shloka_text: तदवस्थंसमीपस्थोलक्ष्मणंप्रेक्ष्यराघवः । भ्रातृस्नेहान्महातेजाविषण्णहृदयोऽभवत् ।।6.101.37।।
explanation: Watching Lakshmana in that situation, most courageous Raghava, out of brotherly affection felt despondent at heart.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तमिवध्यात्वाबाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणः । बभूवसम्रब्धतरोयुगान्तइवपावकः ।।6.101.38।।
explanation: He (Raghava) stood confused for a short while as it was, his eyes filled with tears like fire at the end of the universe.

shloka_text: न विषादस्यकालोऽयमितिसञ्चिन्त्यराघवः । चक्रेसुतुमुलंयुद्धंरावणस्यवधेधृतः ।।6.101.39।। सर्वयत्नेनमहतालक्ष्मणंपरिवीक्ष्य च ।
explanation: Realizing that this is not the time to be disconsolate, observing Lakshmana's efforts, Raghava resolved to destroy Ravana and started a fierce struggle.

shloka_text: सददर्शततोरामःशक्त्याभिन्नंमहाहवे ।।6.101.40।। लक्ष्मणंरुधिरादिग्धंसपन्नगमिवाचलम् ।
explanation: Rama beheld Lakshmana pierced with javelin in the great war bathed in blood and resembling a mountain with a snake penetrated into it.

shloka_text: तामपिप्रहितांशक्तिंरावणेनबलीयसा ।।6.101.41।। यत्नतस्तेहरिश्रेष्ठा न शेकुरवमर्दितुम् । अर्दिताश्चैवबाणौघैस्तेक्षिप्रहस्तेनरक्षसा ।।6.101.42 ।
explanation: It was not feasible for the best of Vanaras to pull out the javelin (from Lakshmana's body) discharged with great strength from Ravana's hand, despite great efforts.

shloka_text: तामपिप्रहितांशक्तिंरावणेनबलीयसा ।।6.101.41।। यत्नतस्तेहरिश्रेष्ठा न शेकुरवमर्दितुम् । अर्दिताश्चैवबाणौघैस्तेक्षिप्रहस्तेनरक्षसा ।।6.101.42 ।
explanation: It was not feasible for the best of Vanaras to pull out the javelin (from Lakshmana's body) discharged with great strength from Ravana's hand, despite great efforts.

shloka_text: सौमित्रिंसाविनिर्भिद्यप्रविष्टाधरणीतलम् । तांकराभ्यांपरामृश्यरामःशक्तिंभयावहाम् ।।6.101.43।। बभञ्जसमरेक्रुद्धोबलवान्विचकर्ष च ।
explanation: It pierced through Lakshmana's body and entered into the earth. Mighty Rama held the terrific javelin with both hands bent it and removed in the course of struggle.

shloka_text: तस्यनिष्कर्षतःशक्तिंरावणेनबलीयसा ।।6.101.44।। शराःसर्वेषुगात्रेषुपातितामर्मभेदिनः ।
explanation: While Rama was pulling out the javelin, mighty and courageous Ravana struck him in his private parts and all over the body with arrows.

shloka_text: अचिन्तयित्वातान्बाणान्समालशिष्य च लक्ष्मणम् ।।6.101.45।। अब्रवीच्चहनूमन्तंसुग्रीवं च महाकपिम् ।
explanation: Not minding the arrows struck, Rama embraced Lakshmana and spoke to Hanumantha and the great Vanara Sugriva.

shloka_text: क्ष्मणंपरिवार्यैवतिष्ठध्वंवानरोत्तमाः ।।6.101.46।। पराक्रमस्यकालोऽयंसम्प्राप्तोमेचिरेप्सितः । पापात्मायंदशग्रीवोवध्यतांपापनिश्चयः ।।6.101.47।। काङ्क्षितस्स्तोककस्येवघर्मान्तेमेघदर्शनम् ।
explanation: "O foremost of Vanaras! Take care of Lakshmana by surrounding him. Just as clouds appeared before the chataka bird waiting for long, time has come to exhibit my valour which was awaited for long. Now I will destroy the ten headed Ravana of sinful resolve rightfully in a short while from now."

shloka_text: शक्त्याविनिहतंदृष्टवारावणेनबलीयसा । लक्ष्मणंसमरेशूरंरूधिरौघपरिप्लुतम् ।।6.102.1।। स दत्त्वातुमुलंयुद्धंरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । विसृजन्नेवबाणौघान् सुषेणमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.102.2।।
explanation: Seeing Lakshmana struck by exceedingly mighty, evil minded Ravana's javelin and soaked in blood Rama giving intense fight by discharging arrows also spoke as follows to Sushena.

shloka_text: शक्त्याविनिहतंदृष्टवारावणेनबलीयसा । लक्ष्मणंसमरेशूरंरूधिरौघपरिप्लुतम् ।।6.102.1।। स दत्त्वातुमुलंयुद्धंरावणस्यदुरात्मनः । विसृजन्नेवबाणौघान् सुषेणमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.102.2।।
explanation: Seeing Lakshmana struck by exceedingly mighty, evil minded Ravana's javelin and soaked in blood Rama giving intense fight by discharging arrows also spoke as follows to Sushena.

shloka_text: एषरावणवीर्येणलक्ष्मणःपतितोभुविः । सर्पवच्चेष्टतेवीरोभूमौशोकमुदिरीयन् ।।6.102.3।।
explanation: 'Heroic Lakshmana struck by Ravana, fell on the ground and writhing like a snake and rolling made me sad'.

shloka_text: शोणितार्द्रमिमंवीरंप्राणैःप्रियतरंमम । पश्यतोममकाशक्तिर्योद्धुंपर्याकुलात्मनः ।।6.102.4।।
explanation: ' As I see Lakshmana, who is more than my life, and loving soaked in blood, my mind is agitated. How can I have the energy to fight?'

shloka_text: अ यं स समरश्लाघीभ्रातामेशुभलक्षणः । यदिपञ्चत्वमापन्नःप्राणैर्मेकिंसुखेनवा ।।6.102.5।।
explanation: 'Lakshmana, my brother, is praised for his efficiency in war, is endowed with auspicious marks. If he is met with death, what use is my happiness and life for me?'

shloka_text: लज्जतीवहिवीर्यंभ्रश्यतीवकराद्धनुः । सायकाव्यवसीदन्तिदृष्टिर्भाष्पवशंगता ।।6.102.6।।
explanation: 'My heroism is shy, my bow slips from my hand, arrows are dropping, my vision is blurred with tears with my brother gone.'

shloka_text: अवसीदन्तिगात्राणिस्वप्नयानेनृणामिव । चिन्तामेवर्ततेतीव्रामुमूर्षापि च जायते ।।6.102.7।।
explanation: 'Seeing Lakshmana in this state, just as in dream, my limbs are retrieving while walking, being on the point of death intense sorrow is growing and the desire to live is gone.'

shloka_text: भ्रातरंनिहतंदृष्टवारावणेनदुरात्मना । विष्टनन्तंतुदुःखार्तंमर्मण्यभिहतंभृशम् ।।6.102.8।।
explanation: Seeing the brother struck in vital parts and wounded by the evilminded Ravana, Rama was filled with grief and breathing heavily.

shloka_text: राघवोभ्रातरंदृष्टवाप्रियंप्राणंबहिश्चरम् । दुःखेनमहताविष्टोध्यानशोकपरायणः ।।6.102.9।।
explanation: Beholding his dear brother, who is his life outside him overcome by anxiety, Rama lost senses and gave himself to great sorrow.

shloka_text: परंविषादमापन्नोविललापाकुलेन्द्रियः । भ्रातरंनिहतंदृष्टवालक्ष्मणंरणपांसुषु ।।6.102.10।।
explanation: Seeing the wounded brother Lakshmana in the battlefield, the very sad Rama lost control over his senses and grieved.

shloka_text: विजयोऽपिहिमेशूर न प्रियायोपकल्पते । अचक्षुर्विषयश्चन्द्रःकांप्रीतिंजनयिष्यति ।।6.102.11।।
explanation: 'O Hero! Even victory for me will not give joy. What pleasure will one have if he desires to see the moon when he has lost vision?'

shloka_text: किंमेयुद्धेनकिंप्राणैर्युद्धकार्यं न विद्यते । यत्रायंनिहतश्शेतेरणमूर्धनिलक्ष्मणः ।।6.102.12।।
explanation: 'What purpose is there to fight in battle or in life with Lakshmana lying in the forefront struck in the battlefield?'

shloka_text: यथैवमांवनंयान्तमनुयातिमहाद्युतिः । अहमप्युपयास्यामितथैवैनंयमक्षयम् ।।6.102.13।।
explanation: 'Lakshmana who is endowed with splendour followed me to the forest. In the same way I will follow him to the god of death.'

shloka_text: इष्टबन्धुजनोनित्यंमां स नित्यमनुव्रतः । इमामवस्थांगमितोराक्षसैःकूटयोधिभिः ।।6.102.14।।
explanation: 'Lakshmana, who loved the kin and was devoted to me, has been led to pass by the Rakshasas.'

shloka_text: देशेदेशेकलत्राणिदेशेदेशे च बान्दवाः । तंतुदेशं न पश्यामियत्रभ्रातासहोदरः ।।6.102.15।।
explanation: 'Wives can be found everywhere, relatives can be found everywhere but biological sibling brothers are not found in any place.'

shloka_text: इत्येवंविलपन्तंतंशोकविह्वलितेद्रनियम् । विवेष्टमानंकरुणमच्छवसन्तंपुनःपुनः ।।6.102.16।। राममाश्वासयनवीरसुषेनोवाक्यमब्रवीत
explanation: Grieving in this manner, lost control over senses, and discrimination, Rama was sighing again and again and was pitiable. Sushena, the hero consoling Rama spoke these words.

shloka_text: किनुराज्येनदुर्धर्षलक्ष्मणेनविनामम । कथंवक्ष्याम्यहंत्वम्बांसुमित्रांपुत्रवत्सलाम् ।।6.102.17।।
explanation: 'Without Lakshmana who is difficult to win, what use is kingdom to me? What can I tell mother Sumithra who is the lover of her son?'

shloka_text: न मृथोयंमहाबाहो लक्ष्मणोलक्षमिवर्धन: । न चास्यविक्रतंवक्त्रानापिशस्वासं न निष्प्रभं ।।6.102.18।।
explanation: O Broad shouldered Rama! Enhancer of prosperity, Lakshmana is not dead. His face has not changed, and he has not lost splendour.

shloka_text: सुप्रभंसुप्रसन्नं च मुखमस्यनिरीक्ष्यताम् ।।6.102.19।। पद्मपत्रतलौहस्तौसुप्रसन्ने च लोचने ।
explanation: 'His face is radiant and pleasing to see. His palms are like red lotuses and his eyes are so pleasant'.

shloka_text: ऐ वं न विद्यतेरूपंगतासूनांविशम्पते ।।6.102.20।। माविषादंमृकृथावीरसप्राणोऽयमरिन्दम ।
explanation: "O hero! Those who cease to live will not have such appearance and signs. He who is a tamer of foes is alive. I tell you, do not grieve."

shloka_text: आ ख्यासतितुप्रसुप्तस्यस्रस्तगात्रस्यभूतले ।।6.102.21।। सोच्छवासंहृदयंवीरकम्पमानंमुहुर्मुहुः ।
explanation: "From the movement of his limbs and throbbing of his heart again and again it is known that he is alive."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वामहाप्राज्ञःसुषेणोराघवंवचः ।।6.102.22।। समीपस्थमुवाचेदंहनूमन्तंमहाकपिम् ।
explanation: Very wise Sushena, having spoken like that to Raghava, spoke to the great Vanara, Hanuman nearby.

shloka_text: सौम्य शीघ्रमितोगत्वाशैलमौषधिपर्वतम् ।।6.102.23।। पूर्वंतुकथितोयोऽसौवीर जाम्बवताशुभ: । दक्षिणेशिखरेजातामोषधिमानय ।।6.102.24।। सवर्णकरणींनाम्नासावर्ण्यकरणींतथा । सञ्जीवकरणींवीरसन्धानीं च महौषधीम् ।।6.102.25।। सञ्जीवनार्धंवीरस्यलक्ष्मणस्यमहात्मनः ।
explanation: "O gentle Hanumantha! Going to that mountain of herbs about which Jambavan had earlier spoken to you, get the herbs from the southern peak of that great mountain. To make Lakshmana the great soul alive quickly go and get Savarankarani, Sarvakarani so also Sanjeevakarani and Sandhanakarani and come."

shloka_text: सौम्य शीघ्रमितोगत्वाशैलमौषधिपर्वतम् ।।6.102.23।। पूर्वंतुकथितोयोऽसौवीर जाम्बवताशुभ: । दक्षिणेशिखरेजातामोषधिमानय ।।6.102.24।। सवर्णकरणींनाम्नासावर्ण्यकरणींतथा । सञ्जीवकरणींवीरसन्धानीं च महौषधीम् ।।6.102.25।। सञ्जीवनार्धंवीरस्यलक्ष्मणस्यमहात्मनः ।
explanation: "O gentle Hanumantha! Going to that mountain of herbs about which Jambavan had earlier spoken to you, get the herbs from the southern peak of that great mountain. To make Lakshmana the great soul alive quickly go and get Savarankarani, Sarvakarani so also Sanjeevakarani and Sandhanakarani and come."

shloka_text: सौम्य शीघ्रमितोगत्वाशैलमौषधिपर्वतम् ।।6.102.23।। पूर्वंतुकथितोयोऽसौवीर जाम्बवताशुभ: । दक्षिणेशिखरेजातामोषधिमानय ।।6.102.24।। सवर्णकरणींनाम्नासावर्ण्यकरणींतथा । सञ्जीवकरणींवीरसन्धानीं च महौषधीम् ।।6.102.25।। सञ्जीवनार्धंवीरस्यलक्ष्मणस्यमहात्मनः ।
explanation: "O gentle Hanumantha! Going to that mountain of herbs about which Jambavan had earlier spoken to you, get the herbs from the southern peak of that great mountain. To make Lakshmana the great soul alive quickly go and get Savarankarani, Sarvakarani so also Sanjeevakarani and Sandhanakarani and come."

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तोहनुमान्गत्वाचौषथिपर्वतम् ।।6.102.26।। चिन्तामभ्यगमछ्रचीमानजानं स्ता महौषधीः ।
explanation: Sushena having said so, glorious Hanuman set out to the mountain of herbs. Not able to recognise the herbs he thought over.

shloka_text: तस्यबुद्धि: समुत्पन्नामारुतेरमितौजसः ।।6.102.27।। इदमेवगमिष्यामिगृहीत्वाशिखरंगिरेः ।
explanation: Highly brilliant Hanuman used his intellect and thought to seize the peak of the mountain on which herbs had sprung.
