shloka_text: अस्मिंस्तुशिखरेजातामोषधिंतांसुखावहाम् ।।6.102.28।। प्रतर्केणावगच्छामिसुषेणोह्यवमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: By reasoning it is known that the herb which is good for him is grown in this peak, for Sushena said so.

shloka_text: अगृह्ययदिगच्छामिविशल्यकरणीमहम् ।।6.102.29।। कालात्ययेनदोषःस्याद्वैक्लब्यं च महद्भवेत् ।
explanation: 'If I go without taking Visalakarani, through the passage of time huge mistakes will happen and perplexity will arise'.

shloka_text: इतिसञ्चिन्त्यहनूमान्गत्वाक्षिप्रंमहाबलः ।।6.102.30।। आसाद्यपर्वतश्रेष्ठंप्रक्रम्यगिरेश्शिरः । फुल्लनानातरुगणंसमुत्पाट्यमहाबलः ।।6.102.31।। गृहीत्वाहरिशार्दूलोहस्ताभ्यांसमतोलयत् ।
explanation: Hanuman, the mighty among the Vanaras, thinking so quickly reached the foremost of the mountains, seized the mountain with both hands by shaking it thrice, uprooted the plants with flowers in bloom and balanced it with his hands.

shloka_text: इतिसञ्चिन्त्यहनूमान्गत्वाक्षिप्रंमहाबलः ।।6.102.30।। आसाद्यपर्वतश्रेष्ठंप्रक्रम्यगिरेश्शिरः । फुल्लनानातरुगणंसमुत्पाट्यमहाबलः ।।6.102.31।। गृहीत्वाहरिशार्दूलोहस्ताभ्यांसमतोलयत् ।
explanation: Hanuman, the mighty among the Vanaras, thinking so quickly reached the foremost of the mountains, seized the mountain with both hands by shaking it thrice, uprooted the plants with flowers in bloom and balanced it with his hands.

shloka_text: सनीलमिवजीमूतंतोयपूर्णंनभस्तलात् ।।6.102.32।। उत्पपातगृहीत्वातुहनूमान् शिखरंगिरेः ।
explanation: Like a dark cloud filled with water carried by wind, Hanuman held the mountain peak and went in the air from the surface of the earth.

shloka_text: समागम्यमहावेगःसंन्यस्यशिखरंगिरेः ।।6.102.33।। विश्रम्यकिञ्चिद्धनुमान्सुषेणमिदमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Hanuman came at high speed with the mountain and letting it down and resting for a while spoke as follows.

shloka_text: ओषधीर्नावगच्छामिताअहंहरिपुङ्गव ।।6.102.34।। तदिदंशिखरंकृत्स्नंगिरेस्तस्याहृतंमया ।
explanation: "O leader of the Vanaras! I did not know those herbs. So, the mountain peak was brought here by me."

shloka_text: एवंकथयमानंतुप्रशस्यपवनात्मजम् ।।6.102.35।। सुषेणोवानरश्रेष्ठोजग्राहोत्पाट्यचौषधीः ।
explanation: The son of wind god, having revealed it like that, Sushena the leader of the Vanaras uprooted the herb and took out.

shloka_text: विस्मितास्तुबभूवुस्तेसर्वेवानरपुङ्गवाः ।।6.102.36।। दृष्टवाहनूमतःकर्मसुरैरपिसुदुष्करम् ।
explanation: It is a difficult task even for Suras. Seeing Hanuman doing it all the Vanara leaders were amazed.

shloka_text: ततःसङ्क्षोदयित्वातामोषधिंवानरोत्तमः ।।6.102.37।। लक्ष्मणस्यददौनस्तस्सुषेणस्सुमहाद्युतिः ।
explanation: Thereafter, Sushena the foremost of the Vanaras, a brilliant one crushed the herbs and dropped the extract into Lakshmana's nose.

shloka_text: विशल्यस्ससमाघ्रायलक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा ।।6.102.38।। विशल्योविरुजश्शीघ्रमुदतिष्ठन्महीतलात् ।
explanation: The destroyer of enemies, Lakshmana, who was pained by the javelin stuck in his body, on inhaling the herb, was devoid of javelin and rid of pain. He got up from the ground.

shloka_text: तमुत्थितंतुहरयोभूतलात्प्रेक्ष्यलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.102.39।। साधुसावधितिसुप्रीतालक्ष्मणंप्रत्यपूजयन् ।
explanation: Seeing Lakshmana rise up from the surface of the ground, the Vanaras said Well done and offered prayers very affectionately.

shloka_text: एह्येहीत्यब्रवीद्रामोलक्ष्मणंपरवीरहा ।।6.102.40।। सस्वजेस्नेहगाढं च बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणः ।
explanation: Rama the destroyer of enemies seeing Lakshmana saying, 'come come', eyes filled with tears of joy affectionately embraced him and spoke.

shloka_text: ब्रवीच्छपरिष्वज्यसौमित्रिंराघवस्तदा ।।6.102.41।। दिष्ट्यात्वांवीरपश्यामिमरणात्पुनरागतम् ।
explanation: Embracing Saumithri, Rama spoke 'luckily you have recovered from death again and I am able to see you'.

shloka_text: न हिमेजीवितेनार्थस्सीतयाविजयनेवा ।।6.102.42।। कोहिमेवदतेनार्धस्त्वयिपञ्चत्वमागते ।
explanation: 'Lakshmana! If you had not come out of death, what use is life to me? What is the use of Sita? What is the meaning of life' said Rama?

shloka_text: इत्येवंवदतस्तस्यराघवस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.102.43।। भिन्नश्शिथिलयावाचालक्ष्मणोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: When Raghava had spoken in that manner, Lakshmana spoke, pained by the irresolute talk (of Rama).

shloka_text: तांप्रतिज्ञांप्रतिज्ञायपुरासत्यपराक्रम ।।6.102.44।। लघुःकश्चिदिवासत्त्वोनैवंवक्तुमिहार्हसि ।
explanation: "You who are of truthful valour having made a vow, now speaking in this way, like a lowly person is not appropriate."

shloka_text: न हिप्रतिज्ञांकुर्वन्तिवितथांसत्यवादिनः ।।6.102.45।। लक्षणंहिमहत्त्वस्यप्रतिज्ञापरिपालनम् ।
explanation: 'Those who speak truth never fail their vows futile for fulfilment of the vows is a mark of greatness for them'.

shloka_text: नैराश्यमुपगन्तुं च नालंतेमत्कृतेऽनघ ।।6.102.46।। वधेनरावणस्याद्यप्रतिज्ञामनुपालय ।
explanation: "O Sinless Rama! To be in despair on my account is not fair. Destroy Ravana and redeem your vow."

shloka_text: नजीवन्यास्यतेशत्रुस्तवबाणपथंगतः ।।6.102.47।। नर्दतस्तीक्षणदंष्ट्रस्यसिंहस्येवमहागजः ।
explanation: " A victim of your arrow can not be alive just as an elephant fallen into the clutch of a roaring lion with sharp teeth is not possible to live."

shloka_text: अहंतुवधमिच्छामिशीघ्रमस्यदुरात्मनः ।।6.102.48।। यावदस्तं न यात्येषकृतकर्मादिवाकरः ।
explanation: "I wish to see the destruction of this evil minded one quickly before the sun completes the day and sets."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनतुतद्वाक्यमुक्तंश्रुत्वा स राघवः । सन्दधेपरवीरघ्नोधनुरादायवीर्यवान् ।।6.103.1।।
explanation: Courageous Raghava, the destroyer of enemies on hearing the words spoken by Lakshmana took up his bow and fixed it.

shloka_text: रावणायशरानघोरान्विससर्जचमूमुखे । अधान्यंरथमास्थायरावणोराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.103.2।। अभ्यधावतकाकुत्स्थंस्वर्भानुरिवभास्करम् ।
explanation: Rama discharged dreadful shafts at Ravana's army in the forefront. Ravana ascended another chariot and went towards Rama, just as the planet Rahu moved towards the Sun.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवोरधस्थस्तुरामंवज्रोपमैश्शरैः ।।6.103.3।। आजघानमहाशैलंधाराभिरिवतोयदः ।
explanation: Seated in the chariot, the ten headed Ravana showered thunderbolt like shafts just as rain cloud showers on a huge mountain and struck.

shloka_text: दीप्तपावकसङ्काशैःशरैःकाञ्चनभूषणैः ।।6.103.4।। अभ्यवर्षद्रणरामोदशग्रीवंसमाहितः ।
explanation: Sri Rama steadily covered Ravana, the ten headed Rakshasa with shining shafts covered with gold glowing like fire in the battle.

shloka_text: भूमौस्थितस्यरामस्यरथस्थस्य च रक्षसः ।।6.103.5।। न समंयुद्धमित्याहुर्देवगन्धर्वकिन्नराः ।
explanation: Rama standing on the earth and Ravana seated on the chariot and waging war is not fair, declared Devas, Gandharvas and Kinneras.

shloka_text: ततोदेववरर्श्रीमान् श्रुत्वातेषांवचोऽमृतम् ।।6.103.6।। आहूयमातलिंशक्रोवचनंचेदमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: The foremost of Devas, the glorious Indra, on hearing their sweet words called his charioteer Matali and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: रथेनममभूमिष्ठंशीघ्रंयाहिरघूत्तमम् ।।6.103.7।। आहूयभूतलंयातःकुरुदेवहितंमहत् ।
explanation: "Proceed quickly in my chariot to the foremost of the Raghus on the earth, where Sri Rama stands and call him to sit in the chariot as per the words of Devas."

shloka_text: इत्युक्तोदेवराजेनमातलिर्देवसारथिः ।।6.103.8।। प्रणम्यशिरसादेवंततोवचनमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Lord of Devas having spoken that way, the charioteer of Devas offering salutations to Devas in obedience spoke these words.

shloka_text: शीघ्रंयास्यामिदेवेन्द्रसारथ्यं च करोम्यहम् ।।6.103.9।। ततोहयैश्चसम्योज्यहरितैःस्यन्दनोत्तमम् ।
explanation: "O Devendra, I will do the duty of charioteer duly to the Lord of gods with green horses proceeding quickly", said the charioteer."

shloka_text: ततःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गःकिङ्किणीशतभूषितः ।।6.103.10।। तरुणादित्यसङ्काशोवैदूर्यमयकूबरः । सदश्वैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्युक्तश्श्वेतप्रकीर्णकैः ।।6.103.11।। हरिभिःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्हेमजालविभूषितैः । रुक्मवेणुध्वज्श्रीमन्देवराजरथोवरः ।।6.103.12।। देवराजेनन्दिष्टोरथमारुह्यमातलिः । अभ्यवर्ततकाकुत्स्थमवतीर्यत्रिवष्टपात् ।।6.103.13।।
explanation: Thereafter, Matali brought the glorious chariot of Lord of Devas. It was decked with charming gold wheels, body fitted with hundreds of gold bells that shone like the early morning sun, decked with gold on top, green horses with white whisks shining like the Sun, decked with golden net, the horses yoked to staff, and the flag fitted on golden bamboo staff. Descending from the chariot, like from heaven, Matali went towards Kakuthsa.

shloka_text: ततःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गःकिङ्किणीशतभूषितः ।।6.103.10।। तरुणादित्यसङ्काशोवैदूर्यमयकूबरः । सदश्वैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्युक्तश्श्वेतप्रकीर्णकैः ।।6.103.11।। हरिभिःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्हेमजालविभूषितैः । रुक्मवेणुध्वज्श्रीमन्देवराजरथोवरः ।।6.103.12।। देवराजेनन्दिष्टोरथमारुह्यमातलिः । अभ्यवर्ततकाकुत्स्थमवतीर्यत्रिवष्टपात् ।।6.103.13।।
explanation: Thereafter, Matali brought the glorious chariot of Lord of Devas. It was decked with charming gold wheels, body fitted with hundreds of gold bells that shone like the early morning sun, decked with gold on top, green horses with white whisks shining like the Sun, decked with golden net, the horses yoked to staff, and the flag fitted on golden bamboo staff. Descending from the chariot, like from heaven, Matali went towards Kakuthsa.

shloka_text: ततःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गःकिङ्किणीशतभूषितः ।।6.103.10।। तरुणादित्यसङ्काशोवैदूर्यमयकूबरः । सदश्वैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्युक्तश्श्वेतप्रकीर्णकैः ।।6.103.11।। हरिभिःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्हेमजालविभूषितैः । रुक्मवेणुध्वज्श्रीमन्देवराजरथोवरः ।।6.103.12।। देवराजेनन्दिष्टोरथमारुह्यमातलिः । अभ्यवर्ततकाकुत्स्थमवतीर्यत्रिवष्टपात् ।।6.103.13।।
explanation: Thereafter, Matali brought the glorious chariot of Lord of Devas. It was decked with charming gold wheels, body fitted with hundreds of gold bells that shone like the early morning sun, decked with gold on top, green horses with white whisks shining like the Sun, decked with golden net, the horses yoked to staff, and the flag fitted on golden bamboo staff. Descending from the chariot, like from heaven, Matali went towards Kakuthsa.

shloka_text: ततःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गःकिङ्किणीशतभूषितः ।।6.103.10।। तरुणादित्यसङ्काशोवैदूर्यमयकूबरः । सदश्वैःकाञ्चनापीडैर्युक्तश्श्वेतप्रकीर्णकैः ।।6.103.11।। हरिभिःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्हेमजालविभूषितैः । रुक्मवेणुध्वज्श्रीमन्देवराजरथोवरः ।।6.103.12।। देवराजेनन्दिष्टोरथमारुह्यमातलिः । अभ्यवर्ततकाकुत्स्थमवतीर्यत्रिवष्टपात् ।।6.103.13।।
explanation: Thereafter, Matali brought the glorious chariot of Lord of Devas. It was decked with charming gold wheels, body fitted with hundreds of gold bells that shone like the early morning sun, decked with gold on top, green horses with white whisks shining like the Sun, decked with golden net, the horses yoked to staff, and the flag fitted on golden bamboo staff. Descending from the chariot, like from heaven, Matali went towards Kakuthsa.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्चतदारामंसप्रतोदोरथेस्थितः । प्राञ्जलिर्मातलिर्वाक्यंसहस्राक्षस्यसारथिः ।।6.103.14।।
explanation: Then the thousand eyed charioteer, holding the whip in hand, from the chariot, offered salutations with folded palms to Sri Rama and spoke these words.

shloka_text: सहस्राक्षेणकाकुत्थ्सरथोऽयंविजयायते । दत्तस्तवमहासत्त्वश्रीमन् शत्रुनिबर्हण ।।6.103.15।।
explanation: "To you, Kakuthsa, who are endowed with great prowess, destroyer of enemies, this chariot has been sent by Indra for your victory."

shloka_text: इदमैन्द्रंमहच्चापंकवचंचानगिसन्निभम् । शराश्चादित्यसङ्काशाःशक्तिश्चविमलाशिवा ।।6.103.16।।
explanation: "Here is Indra's mighty bow, armour shining like fire, shafts resembling the Sun and stainless auspicious javelin."

shloka_text: आरुह्येमंरथंवीरराक्षसंजहिरावणम् । मयासारथिनाराजन् महेन्द्रइवदानवान् ।।6.103.17।।
explanation: "O heroic king! With me as charioteer, mounting this chariot, kill the Rakshasa Ravana as Mahendra killed the demons."

shloka_text: इत्युक्तःसम्परिक्रम्यरथंतमभिवाद्य च । आरुरोहतदारामोलोकान् लक्ष्मविराजयन् ।।6.103.18।।
explanation: Speaking like that, Matali went round Sri Rama, and went round the chariot clockwise saluting him. Sri Rama then ascended the chariot, illuminating his splendour to the world.

shloka_text: तद्भभूवाद्भुतंयुद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । रामस्य च महाबाहोरावणस्य च रक्षसः ।।6.103.19।।
explanation: Then a wonderful, severe thrilling fight took place between Sri Rama and Ravana.

shloka_text: स गान्धर्वेणगान्धर्वंदैवंदैवेनराघवः । अस्त्रंराक्षसराजस्यजघानपरमास्त्रवित् ।।6.103.20।।
explanation: Raghava who was highly skilled in the use of supreme weapons destroyed that missile presided over by Gandharvas and gods, released by Ravana.

shloka_text: अस्त्रंतुपरमंघोरंराक्षसंराक्षसाधिपः । ससर्जपरमक्रुद्धःपुनरेवनिशाचरः ।।6.103.21।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king, the night ranger, became highly furious and once again discharged the most terrific missile presided over by Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तेरावणधनुर्मुक्ताःशराःकाञ्चनभूषणाः । अभ्यवर्तन्तकाकुत्स्थंसर्पाभूत्वामहाविषाः ।।6.103.22।।
explanation: The shafts released from Ravana's bow were covered with gold and highly venomous like serpents reached near Kakuthsa.

shloka_text: तेदीप्तवदनादीप्तंसमन्तोज्वलनंमुखैः । राममेवाभ्यवर्तन्तव्यादितास्याभयानकाः ।।6.103.23।।
explanation: Those shafts with wide flaming mouths, vomiting fire, glowing, frightening, and striking went over to Rama.

shloka_text: तैर्वासुकिसमस्पर्शैर्दीप्तभोगैर्महाविषैः । दिशश्चसन्ततास्सर्वाप्रदिशश्चसमावृताः ।।6.103.24।।
explanation: Flaming coils like the Vasuki, covering all quarters with poison, enveloped all over.

shloka_text: तान् दृष्टवापन्नगान् रामःसमापततआहवे । अस्त्रंगारुत्मतंघोरंप्रादुश्चक्रेभयावहम् ।।6.103.25।।
explanation: Seeing the dreadful reptiles approaching, Rama discharged the missile presided over by Garuda.

shloka_text: तेराघवधनुर्मुक्तारुक्मपुङ्खाःशिखिप्रभाः । सुपर्णाःकाञ्चनाभूत्वाविचेरुःसर्पशत्रवः ।।6.103.26।।
explanation: By the missile discharged by Raghava those reptiles and snakes turned into golden feathered eagles and by the shine of the feathers, the reptiles flew.

shloka_text: तेतान्सर्वान् जघ्नुस्सर्परूपान्महाजवान् । सुपर्णरूपारामस्यविशिखाःकामरूपिणः ।।6.103.27।।
explanation: Those shafts of Rama in the form of eagles which could change their form at will, destroyed the serpent forms and they flew at great speed.

shloka_text: अस्त्रेप्रतिहतेक्रुद्धोरावणोराक्षसाधिपः । अभ्यवर्षत्तदारामंघोराभिःशरवृष्टिभिः ।।6.103.28।।
explanation: King of Rakshasas knocked back, became enraged and covered Rama with a terrific shower of shafts.

shloka_text: ततश्शरसहस्रेणराममक्लिष्टकारिणम् । अर्दयित्वाशरौघेणमातलिम्प्रत्यविध्यत ।।6.103.29।।
explanation: Thereafter having showered a thousand shafts on Rama, of unwearied action, Ravana pierced Matali with shafts.

shloka_text: चिच्छेदकेतुमुद्धिश्यशरेणैकेनरावणः । पातयित्वारथोपस्थेरथात्केतुं च काञ्चनम् ।।6.103.30।। ऐन्द्रानपिजघानाश्वान्शरजालेनरावणः ।
explanation: Ravana attacked the flag post of the chariot with one arrow and felled it down. Then he released a network of arrows on Indra's horses and struck them.

shloka_text: तदृष्ट्वासुमहातत्कर्मरावणस्यदुरात्मना: । विषेदुर्देवगन्धर्वाचारणादानवैस्सह ।।6.103.31।। राममार्तंतदादृष्टवासिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः । व्यथितावानरेन्द्राश्चबभूवुस्सविभीषणाः ।।6.103.32।। रामचन्द्रमसंदृष्टवाग्रस्तंरावणराहुणा ।
explanation: On seeing Sri Rama afflicted by the action of evilminded Ravana, the Devas, Gandharvas, Charanas, Danavas also, Siddhas and foremost rishis were despondent. Seeing the moon like Sri Rama eclipsed by planet Rahu in the form of Ravana, the Vanara leaders and Vibheeshana became worried.

shloka_text: तदृष्ट्वासुमहातत्कर्मरावणस्यदुरात्मना: । विषेदुर्देवगन्धर्वाचारणादानवैस्सह ।।6.103.31।। राममार्तंतदादृष्टवासिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः । व्यथितावानरेन्द्राश्चबभूवुस्सविभीषणाः ।।6.103.32।। रामचन्द्रमसंदृष्टवाग्रस्तंरावणराहुणा ।
explanation: On seeing Sri Rama afflicted by the action of evilminded Ravana, the Devas, Gandharvas, Charanas, Danavas also, Siddhas and foremost rishis were despondent. Seeing the moon like Sri Rama eclipsed by planet Rahu in the form of Ravana, the Vanara leaders and Vibheeshana became worried.

shloka_text: प्राजात्यं च नक्षत्रंरोहिणींकशशिनःप्रियाम् ।।6.103.33।। समाक्रम्यबुधस्तस्थौप्रजानामशुभावहः ।
explanation: When the planet Budha comes closer to the Rohini planet presided over by the Lord of creation, people predict bad luck.

shloka_text: सधूमपरिवृत्तोर्मिःप्रज्वलन्निवसागरः ।।6.103.34।। उत्पपाततदाक्रुद्धस्स्पृशन्निवदिवाकरम् ।
explanation: The waves of the ocean were, as if in fury, waves covered with mist turning around as though to touch the radiant sun rose high.

shloka_text: शस्त्रवर्णस्सुपरुषोमन्दरश्मिद्दिवाकरः ।।6.103.35।। अदृश्यतकबन्धाङ्कःसंसक्तोधूमकेतुना ।
explanation: The Sun seemed without radiance like the colour of weapon (grey), in the form of Kabhanda (headless trunk), combined with Dhumakethu.

shloka_text: कोसलानां च नक्षत्रंव्यक्तमिन्द्राग्निदैवतम् ।।6.103.36।। आक्रम्याङ्गारकस्तस्थौविशाखामपिचाम्बरे ।
explanation: In the sky, the planet Mars too stood in constellation with Visakha star presided over by gods Indra and Agni in heaven, which was propitious for the kosala kings.

shloka_text: दशास्योविंशतिभुजःप्रगृहीतशरासनः ।।6.103.37।। अदृशास्यःदशग्रीवःमैनाकःपर्वतःइव
explanation: Ravana with ten heads and twenty arms seizing his bow appeared like the Mynaka mountain.

shloka_text: निरस्यमानोरामस्तुदशग्रीवेणरक्षसा ।।6.103.38।। नाशक्नोदभिसन्धातुंसायकान्रणमूर्धनि ।
explanation: While Ravana with ten heads and arms was ready in the forefront of the battle, Sri Rama had no possibility to fix his arrows.

shloka_text: तस्यक्रुद्धस्यवदनंदृष्टवारामस्यधीमतः ।।6.104.1।। सर्वभूतानिवित्रेसुःप्राकम्पत च मेदिनी ।
explanation: Seeing enraged wise Rama's countenance, all beings on earth were shaken in fear.

shloka_text: सिंहशार्दूलान्शैलस्सञ्चचालचलद्द्रुमः । बभूवचापिक्षुभितःसमुद्रःसरिताम्पतिः ।।6.104.2।।
explanation: The mountains that were abode of lions and tigers with trees shook and the ocean, the king of rivers, was seen agitated.

shloka_text: खराश्चखरनिर्घोषागगनेपरुषाघनाः । औत्पातिकानिनर्दन्तस्समन्तात्परिचक्रमुः ।।6.104.3।।
explanation: Dreadful and portentous clouds went in circles all over sky looking like donkeys emitting harsh sounds.

shloka_text: रामंदृष्टवासुसङ्क्रुद्धमुत्पातांश्चैवसुदारुणान् । वित्रेसुस्सर्वभूतानिरावणस्याभवद्भयम् ।।6.104.4।।
explanation: Rama became highly furious, most dreadful sounds were rising up and all beings were frightened. Ravana was also afraid.

shloka_text: विमानस्थास्तदादेवागन्धर्वाश्चमहोरगाः । ऋषिदावनदैत्याश्चगरुत्मन्तश्चखेचराः ।।6.104.5।। ददृशुस्तेतदायुद्धंलोकसम्वर्तसंस्थितम् । नानाप्रहरणैर्भीमैश्शूरयोस्सम्प्रयुध्यतोः ।।6.104.6।।
explanation: Then from the aerial chariots, Devas, Gandharvas, great Nagas, sages, devils, giants, birds, and eagles watched the duel war that went on between the heroes clashing with different kinds of frightening weapons like at the dissolution of the world.

shloka_text: विमानस्थास्तदादेवागन्धर्वाश्चमहोरगाः । ऋषिदावनदैत्याश्चगरुत्मन्तश्चखेचराः ।।6.104.5।। ददृशुस्तेतदायुद्धंलोकसम्वर्तसंस्थितम् । नानाप्रहरणैर्भीमैश्शूरयोस्सम्प्रयुध्यतोः ।।6.104.6।।
explanation: Then from the aerial chariots, Devas, Gandharvas, great Nagas, sages, devils, giants, birds, and eagles watched the duel war that went on between the heroes clashing with different kinds of frightening weapons like at the dissolution of the world.

shloka_text: ऊचुस्सुरासुरास्सर्वेतदाविग्रहमागताः । प्रेक्षमाणामहर्युद्धंवाक्यंभक्त्याप्रहृष्टवत् ।।6.104.7।।
explanation: Then watching the great war, all the Suras, Asuras, lost control and overcome with happiness spoke these words with devotion.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवंजयेत्याहुरसुराःसमवस्थिताः । देवाराममवोचंस्तेत्वंजयेतिपुनःपुनः ।।6.104.8।।
explanation: Firmly established the Asuras uttered 'Victory to the Ten headed Ravana', and Devas for their part pronounced 'Rama be victorious' again and again.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेक्रोधाद्राघवस्य स रावणः । प्रहर्तुकामोदुष्टात्मास्पृशन् प्रहरणंमहत् ।।6.104.9।। वज्रसारंमहानादंसर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम् । शैलशृङ्गनिभैःकूटैश्चित्तदृष्टिभयावहम् ।।6.104.10।। सधूममिवतीक्ष्णाग्रंयुगान्ताग्निचमोपमम् । अतिरौद्रमनासाद्यंकालेनापिदुरासदम् ।।6.104.11।। त्रासनंसर्वभूतानांदारणंभेदनंतथा । प्रदीप्तमिवरोषेणशूलंजग्राहरावणः ।।6.104.12।।
explanation: In the meantime, the evil self Ravana who is called so, as he makes others cry, in intense anger making loud noise, stroking an unassailable weapon which was like the thunderbolt, capable of killing all enemies, a spike which closely resembled mountain peaks, dreadful even to think, like a mass of smoke, sharp and pointed, blazing like at the dissolution of the universe, very frightening, difficult to hand le, like the god of death, a terror for all beings, frightening, tearing, splitting, glowing like trident seized hold of to attack Rama.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेक्रोधाद्राघवस्य स रावणः । प्रहर्तुकामोदुष्टात्मास्पृशन् प्रहरणंमहत् ।।6.104.9।। वज्रसारंमहानादंसर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम् । शैलशृङ्गनिभैःकूटैश्चित्तदृष्टिभयावहम् ।।6.104.10।। सधूममिवतीक्ष्णाग्रंयुगान्ताग्निचमोपमम् । अतिरौद्रमनासाद्यंकालेनापिदुरासदम् ।।6.104.11।। त्रासनंसर्वभूतानांदारणंभेदनंतथा । प्रदीप्तमिवरोषेणशूलंजग्राहरावणः ।।6.104.12।।
explanation: In the meantime, the evil self Ravana who is called so, as he makes others cry, in intense anger making loud noise, stroking an unassailable weapon which was like the thunderbolt, capable of killing all enemies, a spike which closely resembled mountain peaks, dreadful even to think, like a mass of smoke, sharp and pointed, blazing like at the dissolution of the universe, very frightening, difficult to hand le, like the god of death, a terror for all beings, frightening, tearing, splitting, glowing like trident seized hold of to attack Rama.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेक्रोधाद्राघवस्य स रावणः । प्रहर्तुकामोदुष्टात्मास्पृशन् प्रहरणंमहत् ।।6.104.9।। वज्रसारंमहानादंसर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम् । शैलशृङ्गनिभैःकूटैश्चित्तदृष्टिभयावहम् ।।6.104.10।। सधूममिवतीक्ष्णाग्रंयुगान्ताग्निचमोपमम् । अतिरौद्रमनासाद्यंकालेनापिदुरासदम् ।।6.104.11।। त्रासनंसर्वभूतानांदारणंभेदनंतथा । प्रदीप्तमिवरोषेणशूलंजग्राहरावणः ।।6.104.12।।
explanation: In the meantime, the evil self Ravana who is called so, as he makes others cry, in intense anger making loud noise, stroking an unassailable weapon which was like the thunderbolt, capable of killing all enemies, a spike which closely resembled mountain peaks, dreadful even to think, like a mass of smoke, sharp and pointed, blazing like at the dissolution of the universe, very frightening, difficult to hand le, like the god of death, a terror for all beings, frightening, tearing, splitting, glowing like trident seized hold of to attack Rama.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेक्रोधाद्राघवस्य स रावणः । प्रहर्तुकामोदुष्टात्मास्पृशन् प्रहरणंमहत् ।।6.104.9।। वज्रसारंमहानादंसर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणम् । शैलशृङ्गनिभैःकूटैश्चित्तदृष्टिभयावहम् ।।6.104.10।। सधूममिवतीक्ष्णाग्रंयुगान्ताग्निचमोपमम् । अतिरौद्रमनासाद्यंकालेनापिदुरासदम् ।।6.104.11।। त्रासनंसर्वभूतानांदारणंभेदनंतथा । प्रदीप्तमिवरोषेणशूलंजग्राहरावणः ।।6.104.12।।
explanation: In the meantime, the evil self Ravana who is called so, as he makes others cry, in intense anger making loud noise, stroking an unassailable weapon which was like the thunderbolt, capable of killing all enemies, a spike which closely resembled mountain peaks, dreadful even to think, like a mass of smoke, sharp and pointed, blazing like at the dissolution of the universe, very frightening, difficult to hand le, like the god of death, a terror for all beings, frightening, tearing, splitting, glowing like trident seized hold of to attack Rama.

shloka_text: तच्छूलंपरमक्रुद्धोमध्येजग्राहवीर्यवान् । अनेकैःसमरेश्शूरैराक्षसैःपरिवारितः ।।6.104.13।।
explanation: In the battlefield surrounded by Rakshasa heroes, enraged valiant Ravana took up the trident holding it in the middle.

shloka_text: समुद्यम्यमहाकायोननादयुधिभैरवम् । संरक्तनयनोरोषात्स्वसैन्यमभिहर्षयन् ।।6.104.14।।
explanation: Gigantic Ravana, eyes turned red in anger, raising the trident made formidable noise to make his army extremely joyful in the battlefield.

shloka_text: पृथिवींचान्तरिक्षं च दिशश्चप्रदिशस्तथा । प्राकम्पयत्तदाशब्दोराक्षसेन्द्रस्यदारुणः ।।6.104.15।।
explanation: By the horrible sound made by the Rakshasa king, the earth, even the heavens, similarly the quarters and corners trembled.

shloka_text: अतिनादस्य्यदानेनतेनतस्यदुरात्मनः । सर्वभूतानिवित्रेसुस्सागरश्चप्रचुक्षुभे ।।6.104.16।।
explanation: By the loud roar of the evilminded Ravana's sound, all living beings feared and even the ocean was set to tremble.

shloka_text: स गृहीत्वामहावीर्यश्शूलंतद्रावणोमहत् । विनद्यसुमहानादंरामंपरुषमब्रवीत् ।।6.104.17।।
explanation: Ravana who was endowed with extraordinary valour, taking hold of the trident, addressed Rama harshly in a loud tone.

shloka_text: शूलोऽयंवज्रसारस्तेरामरोषान्मयोद्यतः । तवभ्रातृसहायस्यसम्यक् प्राणान् हरिष्यति ।।6.104.18।।
explanation: "O Rama! This thunderbolt like trident taken up by me now will take away your life along with your brother's."

shloka_text: रक्षसामद्यशूराणांनिहतानांचमूमुखे । त्वांनिहत्यरणश्लाघीकरोमितरसासमम् ।।6.104.19।।
explanation: "I, who commend warfare, will quickly kill you today in the forefront of the army and join you with Rakshasa heroes who were killed."

shloka_text: तिष्ठेदानींनिहमनित्वामेषशूलेनराघव । एवमुक्त्वा स चिक्षेपतच्छूलंराक्षसाधिपः ।।6.104.20।।
explanation: "O Raghava! Stay there. Right now, I will kill you with this trident." Having spoken that way, Ravana hurled the trident.

shloka_text: तद्रावणकरान्मुक्तंविद्युन्मालासमावृतम् । अष्टघण्टंमहानादंवियद्गतमशोभत ।।6.104.21।।
explanation: The trident discharged from Ravana's hand, made circles of lightning, and covered the atmosphere with its glow and shine along with eight bells making loud sounds.

shloka_text: तच्छूलंराघवोदृष्टवाज्वलन्तंघोरदर्शनम् । ससर्जविशिखान्रामश्चापमायम्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.104.22।।
explanation: Valiant Raghava, seeing the glowing trident that was horrible to look at, loosed a number of arrows at it.

shloka_text: आपतन्तंशरौघेणवारयामासराघवः । उत्पतन्तंयुगान्तानगिंजलौघैरिववासवः ।।6.104.23।।
explanation: Raghava intercepted the trident, just as the fire was obstructed by the flow of water, at the time of universal dissolution, and obstructed.

shloka_text: निर्ददाह स तान्बाणान्रामकार्मुकनिःसृतान् । रावणस्यमहान् शूलःपतङ्गानिवपावकः ।।6.104.24।।
explanation: The arrows released from Rama's bow fell on the great trident of Ravana and burnt like moths falling in fire.

shloka_text: तान्दृष्टवाभस्मसाद्भूतान्शूलसम्स्पर्शचूर्णितान् । सायकानन्तरिक्षस्थान् राघवःक्रोधमाहरत् ।।6.104.25।।
explanation: Rama was overcome with fury on seeing his arrows being crushed to powder in the sky on touching the trident and reduced to ashes.

shloka_text: स तांमातलिनानीतांशक्तिंवासवसम्मताम् । जग्राहपरमक्रुद्धोराघवोरघुनन्दनः ।।6.104.26।।
explanation: Raghava, the enhancer of the joy of Raghus, lifted up the javelin brought by Matali, esteemed by Indra.

shloka_text: सातोलिताबलवताशक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना । नभःप्रज्वालयामासयुगान्तोल्केवसप्रभा ।।6.104.27।।
explanation: When mighty Rama lifted up that javelin, it rendered sonorous sounds of bells and lit up the sky like a meteor at the end of the universal dissolution.

shloka_text: साक्षिप्ताराक्षसेन्द्रस्यतस्मिन्कूलेपपात ह । भिन्नःशक्त्यामहान् शूलोनिपपातहतद्युतिः ।।6.104.28।।
explanation: With the hurling of the javelin by Rama at the great trident of Ravana and on (the javelin) touching the trident, it was broken, lost its splendour and fell down.

shloka_text: निर्भिभेदततोबाणैर्हयानस्यमहाजवान् । रामस्त्रीक्ष्णैर्महावेगैर्भाणवद्भिरजिह्मगैः ।।6.104.29।।
explanation: Rama then released arrows endowed with great speed, shower of multitude of arrows straight into the horses of Ravana and shattered them.

shloka_text: निर्बिभेदोरपितदारावणंनिशितैश्शरैः । राघवःपरमायत्तोललाटेपत्रतिभिस्त्रिभिः ।।6.104.30।।
explanation: Raghava pierced into the chest of Ravana sharp arrows and with great effort three sharp arrows on the forehead.

shloka_text: स शरैर्भिन्नसर्वाङ्गोगात्रप्रसृतशोणितः । राक्षसेन्द्रस्समूहस्थःफुल्लाशोकइवाबभौ ।।6.104.31।।
explanation: Pierced all over the limbs with arrows, blood flowing from the limbs, he (Rakshasa king) appeared like an Ashoka tree in the gathering.

shloka_text: स तेनतुतदाक्रोधात्काकुत्स्थेनार्दितोरणे । रावणस्समरश्लाघिमहाक्रोधामुपागमत् ।।6.105.1।।
explanation: Ravana, who was proud of his skill in warfare, became very angry when he was pained by Kakuthsa's arrows.

shloka_text: स दीप्तनयनोरोषाच्चापमायाम्यवीर्यवान् । अभ्यर्दयत्सुसङ्कृद्धोराघवंपरमाहवे ।।6.105.2।। बाणधारसहस्रैस्तैस्सतोयदइवाम्बरात् । राघवंरावणोबाणैस्तटकमिवपूरयन् ।।6.105.3।।
explanation: Valiant hero, Ravana, with his eyes flaming in anger, raising his bow, rained arrows at Sri Rama. He continued to rain thousands of arrows just as rain filled the tank, his arrows covered Raghava.

shloka_text: स दीप्तनयनोरोषाच्चापमायाम्यवीर्यवान् । अभ्यर्दयत्सुसङ्कृद्धोराघवंपरमाहवे ।।6.105.2।। बाणधारसहस्रैस्तैस्सतोयदइवाम्बरात् । राघवंरावणोबाणैस्तटकमिवपूरयन् ।।6.105.3।।
explanation: Valiant hero, Ravana, with his eyes flaming in anger, raising his bow, rained arrows at Sri Rama. He continued to rain thousands of arrows just as rain filled the tank, his arrows covered Raghava.

shloka_text: पूरितःशरजालेनधनुर्मुक्तेनसम्युगे । महागिरिरिवाकम्प्यःकाकुत्स्थो न प्रकम्पते ।।6.105.4।।
explanation: Sri Rama did not get agitated, and stood like a huge mountain, even though the network of arrows released from the bow of Ravana covered him in the conflict.

shloka_text: स शरैश्शरजालानिवारयन् समरेस्थितः । गभस्तीनिवसूर्यस्यप्रतिजग्राहवीर्यवान् ।।6.105.5।।
explanation: Valiant Sri Rama stood intercepting them when streams of arrows covered him, and tolerated them like the rays of the Sun.

shloka_text: ततश्शरसहस्राणिक्षिप्रहस्तोनिशाचरः । निजघानोरसिक्रुद्धोराघवस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.105.6।।
explanation: Thereafter the quickhanded angry night ranger struck into the chest of Raghava thousands of arrows.

shloka_text: स शोणितसमादिग्धस्समरेलक्ष्मणाग्रजः । दृष्टःफुल्लइवारण्येसुमहान् किंशुकद्रुमः ।।6.105.7।।
explanation: In that conflict Lakshmana's elder brother looked like a huge Kimsuka tree in bloom in the forest body being covered with blood all over.

shloka_text: शराभिघातसम्रब्दःसोऽभिजग्राहसायकान् । काकुत्स्थ: सुमहातेजायुगान्तादित्यतेजसः ।।6.105.8।।
explanation: Endowed with extraordinary energy, Kakuthsa, angered by the impact of arrows resembled the Sun at the end of universal dissolution, took up arrows.

shloka_text: ततोऽन्योन्यंसुसम्रब्धौतावुभौरामरावणौ । शरान्धकारेसमरेनोपलक्ष्यतांतदा ।।6.105.9।।
explanation: Then with both Rama and Ravana speedily releasing (hail of) arrows on one another, the battlefield was darkened by arrows, and they were not able to see each other.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधसमाविष्टोरामोदशरथात्मजः । उवाचरावणंवीरःप्रहस्यपरुषंवचः ।।6.105.10।।
explanation: Then Rama, the heroic son of Dasharatha, overcome by anger, laughing at Ravana, spoke these words.

shloka_text: ममभार्याजनस्थानादज्ञानाद्राक्षसाधम । हृतातेविवशायस्मात्तस्मात्त्वंनासिवीर्यवान् ।।6.105.11।।
explanation: "Lowly Rakshasa! My wife was abducted by you ignorantly when she was helpless. Therefore, you are not valiant."

shloka_text: मयाविरहितांदीनांवर्तमानांमहावने । वैदेहींप्रसभंहृत्वाशूरोऽहमितिमन्यसे ।।6.105.12।।
explanation: "Having abducted Vaidehi living in the forest by force, when she was desperate and separated from me, do you think that you are a hero?

shloka_text: स्त्रीषुशूरविनाथासुपरदाराभिमर्शक । कृत्वाकापुरुषंकर्मशूरोऽहमितिमन्यसे ।।6.105.13।।
explanation: "Timid fellow! You having laid hands on another woman think you are a hero? You, who have done such an action, think that you are a hero?"

shloka_text: भिन्नमर्यादनिर्लज्ज चारित्रेष्वनवस्थित । दर्पान्मृत्युमुपादायशूरोऽहमितिमन्यसे ।।6.105.14।।
explanation: "O shameless one! You have transgressed morality and traditional practice. You are dissolute and by your pride seeking death. You think that you are a hero!"

shloka_text: शूरेणधनदभ्रात्राबलैःसमुदितेन च । श्लाघनीयंमहत्कर्मयशस्यं च कृतंत्वया ।।6.105.15।।
explanation: "By laudable great action performed by you (of abducting Sita and your penance) you have attained fame. You are a heroic brother of Kubera, rich in might."

shloka_text: उत्सेकानाभिपन्नस्यगर्हितस्याहितस्य च । कर्मणःप्राप्नुहीदानांतस्याद्यसुमहत्फलम् ।।6.105.16।।
explanation: "You will attain the great result of your hurtful action, overpowered by pride and vanity today."

shloka_text: शूरोऽहमितिचात्मानमवगच्छसिदुर्मते । नैवलज्जास्तितेसीतांचौरवद्वृपकर्षतः ।।6.105.17।।
explanation: "O Evil minded fellow! You boast yourself as a hero, while you abducted Sita like a thief. Shame did not stand in your way."

shloka_text: यदिमत्सन्निधौसीताधर्षितास्यात्त्वयाबलात् । भ्रातरंतुखरंपश्येस्तदामत्सायकैर्हतः ।।6.105.18।।
explanation: "If Sita had been seen by me forcibly taken by you in my presence, then you would have been killed by my arrows and seen your brother Khara."

shloka_text: दिष्ट्यासिममदुष्टात्मश्चक्षुर्विषयमागतः । अद्यत्वांसायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नयामियमसादनम् ।।6.105.19।।
explanation: "O selfish Ravana! Today you have come in my sight by good fortune. I shall send you to the abode of Yama with my arrows."

shloka_text: अद्यतेमच्छरैश्चिन्नंशिरोज्वलितकुण्डलम् । क्रव्यादाव्यपकर्षन्तुविकीर्णंरणपांसुषु ।।6.105.20।।
explanation: "Now, let your head severed by my shafts lying in dust in the battlefield with the shining earrings be dragged by the carnivorous animals."

shloka_text: निपत्योरसिगृध्रास्तेक्षितौक्षिप्तस्यरावण । पिबन्तुरुधिरंतर्षाद्बाणशल्यान्तरोत्थितम् ।।6.105.21।।
explanation: "Ravana! After your body is caused to destroy and scattered on the ground, let the vultures drink the blood oozing from your chest pierced by the heads of my arrows."

shloka_text: अद्यमद्बाणभिन्नस्यगतासोःपतितस्यते । कर्षन्त्वन्त्राणिपतगागरुत्मन्तइवोरगान् ।।6.105.22।।
explanation: "Let the birds tear your intestines as eagles would tear off snakes, now when your body is split and fallen, split by my arrows and ceased of life."

shloka_text: इत्येवं स वदन्वीरोरामश्शत्रुनिबर्हणः । राक्षसेन्द्रंसमीपस्थंशरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ।।6.105.23।।
explanation: Speaking in this way to Ravana who was nearby, Rama the exterminator of enemies rained showers of arrows and covered.

shloka_text: बभूवद्विगुणंवीर्यंबलंहर्षश्चसंयुगे । रामस्यास्त्रबलंचैवशत्रोर्निधनकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.105.24।।
explanation: The strength, valiance, enthusiasm, and the strength of missiles of Rama, who was desirous of the destruction of the enemy, doubled.

shloka_text: प्रादुर्भभूवुरस्त्राणिसर्वाणिविदितात्मनः । प्रहर्षाच्चमहातेजाश्शीघ्रहस्ततरोऽभवत् ।।6.105.25।।
explanation: All missiles appeared before Rama because of his richness in selfknowledge. In his excessive energy and joy the prince became more skillful with his hands.

shloka_text: शुभान्येतानिचिह्नानिविज्ञायात्मगतानिसः । भूयएवार्दयद्रामोरावणंराक्षसान्तकृत् ।।6.105.26।।
explanation: Rama, who can put an end to Rakshasas, knower of his own self having experienced auspicious signs, began to strike at Ravana more vehemently.

shloka_text: हरीणांचाश्मनिकरैश्शरवर्षाच्चराघवात् । हन्यमानोदशग्रीवोविघूर्णहृदयोऽभवत् ।।6.105.27।।
explanation: By the stones thrown by the Vanaras and rain of shafts from Raghava, the ten headed Ravana was pained and was bewildered.

shloka_text: यदा च शस्त्रंनारेभे न चकर्षशरासनम् । नास्यप्रत्यकरोवदीर्यंविक्लबेनान्तरात्मना ।।6.105.28।।
explanation: Being confused mentally, Ravana did not start his arrows, nor stretch his bow, nor was able to use missiles and was not able to oppose Rama's valour.

shloka_text: क्षिप्ताःश्चाशुशरास्तेनशस्त्राणिविविधानि च । मरणार्थायवर्तन्तेमृत्युकालोऽभ्यवर्तत ।।6.105.29।।
explanation: Ravana's arrows of several kinds being destroyed, perceiving that his death is objective Rama's missiles, and that the time of death appeared, he was unable to act.

shloka_text: सूतस्तुरथनेतास्यतदवस्थंनिरीक्ष्यतम् । शनैर्युद्धासम्भ्रान्तोरथंतस्यापवाहयत् ।।6.105.30।।
explanation: Observing his (Ravana's) condition, the charioteer quietly, slowly withdrew his chariot from the battlefield.

shloka_text: सतुमोहात्सुसङ्क्रुद्धःकृतान्तबलचोदितः । क्रोधसंरक्तनयनोरावणंसूतमब्रवीत् ।।6.106.1।।
explanation: Enraged out of delusion, by force of destiny, Ravana's eyes turned red in anger and spoke to his charioteer.

shloka_text: हीनवीर्यमिवाशक्तंपौरुषेणविवर्जितम् । भीरुंलघुमिवासत्त्वंविहीनमिवतेजसा ।।6.106.2।। विमुक्तमिवमायाभिरस्त्रैरिवबहिष्कृतम् । मामवज्ञायदुर्बुद्धेस्वयाबुद्ध्याविचेष्टसे ।।6.106.3।।
explanation: "You dullard! Disdaining me as not capable, lacking manliness, powerless, deficient in valour, timid, incapable, petty, devoid of energy, not knowing conjuring tricks, abandoned weapons, driven out, you act not knowing me in your own way foolishly using your discretion."

shloka_text: हीनवीर्यमिवाशक्तंपौरुषेणविवर्जितम् । भीरुंलघुमिवासत्त्वंविहीनमिवतेजसा ।।6.106.2।। विमुक्तमिवमायाभिरस्त्रैरिवबहिष्कृतम् । मामवज्ञायदुर्बुद्धेस्वयाबुद्ध्याविचेष्टसे ।।6.106.3।।
explanation: "You dullard! Disdaining me as not capable, lacking manliness, powerless, deficient in valour, timid, incapable, petty, devoid of energy, not knowing conjuring tricks, abandoned weapons, driven out, you act not knowing me in your own way foolishly using your discretion."

shloka_text: किमर्थंमामवज्ञायमच्छन्दमनवेक्ष्य च । त्वयाशत्रुसमक्षंमेरथोऽयमपवाहितः ।।6.106.4।।
explanation: Not knowing my opinion, for what reason have you removed my chariot in the presence of my enemy, belittling me?

shloka_text: त्वयाद्यहिममानार्य चिरकालसमार्जितम् । यशोवीर्यं च तेजश्चप्रत्ययश्चविनाशितः ।।6.106.5।।
explanation: "O evil minded one! My fame, glory, valiance and bravery earned over a long period has been wiped out by you."

shloka_text: प्रख्यातवीर्यस्यरञ्जनीयस्यविक्रमैः । पश्यतोयुद्धलुब्धोऽहंकृतंकापुरुषस्त्वया ।।6.106.6।।
explanation: "While my adversary's valour is widely known, you brought me back like a timid one, while I love war, while I am to be praised in the presence of my enemy."

shloka_text: यस्त्वंरथमिदंमोहान्नचेद्वहसिदुर्मते । सत्योऽप्रतितर्कोमेपरेणत्वमुपस्कृतः ।।6.106.7।।
explanation: "O Evil minded one! If out of delusion you are not willing to drive, truly you are influenced by the enemy."

shloka_text: न हितद्विद्यतेकर्मसुहृदोहितकाङ्क्षिणः । रिपूणांसदृशंत्वेतद्यतत्त्वयैतदनुष्ठितम् ।।6.106.8।।
explanation: What has been done by you is not befitting, this is What an enemy should have done. Being good at heart you have done What is good for enemy.

shloka_text: निवर्तयरथंशीघ्रंयावन्नापैतिमेरिपुः । यदिवाध्युषितोऽसित्वंस्मर्यतेयदिमेगुणः ।।6.106.9।।
explanation: "If you remember that you lived long with me and know my virtues, quickly turn back the chariot before my adversary with draws.

shloka_text: एवंपुरुषमुक्तस्तुहितबुद्धिबुद्धिना । अब्रवीद्रावणंसूतोहितंसानुनयंवचः ।।6.106.10।।
explanation: When the insensitive Ravana spoke harshly in that manner, to the charioteer who was wishing his benefit, he spoke in friendly language to Ravana.

shloka_text: न भीतोऽस्मि न मूढोऽस्मिनोपजप्तोऽस्मिशत्रुभिः । न प्रमत्तो न निःस्नेहोविस्मृता न च सत्क्रिया ।।6.106.11।।
explanation: "I was not fearing, nor foolish, not won by the enemy, not negligent also, not lacking friendliness and not forgetting good deeds done by you."

shloka_text: मयातुहितकामेवयशश्चपरिरक्षता । स्नेहप्रसन्नमनसाहितमित्यप्रियंकृतम् ।।6.106.12।।
explanation: Wishing your welfare, for your fame and to protect you with a friendly and pleasant feeling I did that which is good for you. You are unpleasant about this action.

shloka_text: नास्मिन्नर्थेमहाराज त्वंमांप्रियहितेरतम् । कश्चिल्लघुरिवानार्योदोषतोगन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.106.13।।
explanation: "O King! I who wish your welfare ought not to be blamed like an unworthy and pettyminded person by mistake."

shloka_text: श्रूयतांप्रतिदास्यामियन्निमित्तंमयारथः । नदीवेगइवामंभोभिेसंयुगेविनिवर्तितः ।।6.106.14।।
explanation: "O yes! I will answer you. Please listen. like the river entering the ocean speedily is diverted, I have taken back the chariot from the battle.

shloka_text: श्रमंतवावगच्छामिमहतारणकर्मणा । न हितेवीर्यसौमुख्यंप्रकर्षंवोपधारये ।।6.106.15।।
explanation: "Great Ravana! After the strenuous task in the battle, there was no exhibition of your valour, and I did not cognize any superiority in your action."

shloka_text: रथोद्वहनखिन्नाश्चभग्नामेरथवाजिनः । दीनाघर्मपरिश्रान्तागावोवर्षहताइव ।।6.106.16।।
explanation: "The horses of my chariot were exhausted by dragging, broken down, worn out by the hot sun, and desperate like cows lashed by rain."

shloka_text: निमित्तानि च भूयिष्ठंयानिप्रादुर्भवन्तिनः । तेषुतेष्वभिपन्नेषुलक्ष्याम्यप्रदक्षिणम् ।।6.106.17।।
explanation: "Those portents manifesting again and again, that I am seeing, all of them are in the reverse direction (meaning not proptitious)."

shloka_text: देशकालौ च विज्ञेयौलक्षणानीङ्गितानि च । दैन्यंहर्षश्चखेदश्चरथिनश्चबलाबलम् ।।6.106.18।।
explanation: "Propitious and unpropitious, time and place, good and evil signs and omens, depression and liveliness of the warrior as well as strength and weakness of the one in the chariot must be ascertained."

shloka_text: स्थलनिम्नानिभूमेश्चसमानिविषमाणि च । युद्धकालश्चविज्ञेयःपरस्यान्तरदर्शनम् ।।6.106.19।।
explanation: "The earths' ups and downs, evenness and ruggedness, difficult locations, the right time and place for war should be known in advance and the inner weakness of the enemy also to be known."

shloka_text: उपयानापयाने च स्थानंप्रत्यपसर्पणम् । सर्वमेतद्रथस्थेनज्ञेयंरथकुटुम्भिना ।।6.106.20।।
explanation: "To hold the chariot or advance, to go near the (enemy) or retreat, to return back or advance, everything should be known to the charioteer."

shloka_text: तवविश्रामहेतोस्तुतथैषांरथवाजिनाम् । रौद्रंवर्जयताखेदंक्षमंकृतमिदंमया ।।6.106.21।।
explanation: "The reason for retreating in this way is to give you rest and relieve the horses from the terrible feat and fatigue. I deserve to be excused for this action."

shloka_text: स्वेच्छयान मयावीररथोऽयमपवाहितः । भर्तृस्नेहपरीतेनमयेदंयत्कृतंप्रभो ।।6.106.22।।
explanation: "Heroic Lord! I have not brought back this chariot independently (without thinking). I have acted in friendliness to the master (to give rest) not otherwise."

shloka_text: आज्ञापययथातत्त्वंवक्ष्यस्यरिनिषूदन । तत्करिष्याम्यहंवीरगतानृण्येनचेतसा ।।6.106.23।।
explanation: "O Tamer of enemies! Order now and in that way, I shall carry out your order in accordance with you wholeheartedly."

shloka_text: सन्तुष्टस्तेनवाक्येनरावणस्तस्यसारथेः । प्रशस्यैनंबहुविधंयुद्धलुब्धोऽब्रवीदिदम् ।।6.106.24।।
explanation: Ravana was fully satisfied with the words of the charioteer. He praised the charioteer in many ways and spoke like this desiring to wage war.

shloka_text: रथंशीघ्रमिदंसूतराघवाभिमुखंनय । नाहत्वासमरेशत्रून्निवर्तिष्यतिरावणः ।।6.106.25।।
explanation: "Quickly drive the chariot towards Raghava. As a policy, Ravana would never turn back on the battlefield without putting an end to the enemy."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वाततस्तुष्टोरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः । ददौतस्यशुभंह्येकंहस्ताभरणमुत्तमम् ।।6.106.26।। श्रुत्वारावणवाक्यानिसारथिस्सन्यवर्तत ।
explanation: Fully satisfied with Charioteer's words, Ravana bestowed him with an excellent auspicious ornament of the hand. On hearing Ravana's words, the charioteer advanced the chariot.

shloka_text: ततोयुद्धपरिश्रान्तंसमरेचिन्तयास्थितम् । रावणंचाग्रतोदृष्टवायुद्धायसमुपस्थितम् ।।6.107.1।। दैवतैश्चसमागम्यद्रष्टुमभ्यागतोरणम् । उपागम्याब्रवीद्राममगस्त्योभगवान् ऋषिः ।।6.107.2।।
explanation: Then seeing Sri Rama standing and thinking of the war, duly prepared, Rishi Agastya came with Devatas to witness the war with Ravana and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: ततोयुद्धपरिश्रान्तंसमरेचिन्तयास्थितम् । रावणंचाग्रतोदृष्टवायुद्धायसमुपस्थितम् ।।6.107.1।। दैवतैश्चसमागम्यद्रष्टुमभ्यागतोरणम् । उपागम्याब्रवीद्राममगस्त्योभगवान् ऋषिः ।।6.107.2।।
explanation: Then seeing Sri Rama standing and thinking of the war, duly prepared, Rishi Agastya came with Devatas to witness the war with Ravana and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: राम राम महाबाहो शृणुगुह्यंसनातनम् । येनसर्वानरीस्वत्ससमरेविजयिष्यसे ।।6.107.3।।
explanation: "O mighty armed Sri Rama! Dear, hear this eternal secret (mantra) which will enable you to win all the enemies in war."

shloka_text: आदित्यहृदयंपुण्यंसर्वशत्रुविनाशनम् । जयावहंजपेन्नित्यमक्षय्यंपरमंशिवम् ।।6.107.4।। सर्वमङ्गलमङ्गल्यंसर्वपापप्रणाशनम् । चिन्ताशोकप्रशमनमायुर्वर्धनमुत्तमम् ।।6.107.5।।
explanation: "Rama! Listen to this sacred mantra, 'Aditya Hridayam' which can bring victory, which is eternal, very auspicious, and supremely blessed and prolongs life of all by means of which you will destroy all enemies, root out sins, remove anxiety and always bring victory.

shloka_text: आदित्यहृदयंपुण्यंसर्वशत्रुविनाशनम् । जयावहंजपेन्नित्यमक्षय्यंपरमंशिवम् ।।6.107.4।। सर्वमङ्गलमङ्गल्यंसर्वपापप्रणाशनम् । चिन्ताशोकप्रशमनमायुर्वर्धनमुत्तमम् ।।6.107.5।।
explanation: "Rama! Listen to this sacred mantra, 'Aditya Hridayam' which can bring victory, which is eternal, very auspicious, and supremely blessed and prolongs life of all by means of which you will destroy all enemies, root out sins, remove anxiety and always bring victory.

shloka_text: रस्मीमन्तंसमुद्यन्तंदेवासुरनमस्कृतम् । पूजयस्वविवस्त्वन्तंभास्करंभुवनेश्वरम् ।।6.107.6।।
explanation: "You worship the Sun God, crowned with rays rising up at the horizon, greeted by all gods and demons, who brings light to all and who is the embodiment of all gods."

shloka_text: सर्वदेवात्मकोह्येषतेजस्वीरस्मीभावनः । एषदेवासुरगणान्लोकान्पातिगभस्तिभिः ।।6.107.7।।
explanation: "He is the self in all, glorious, he sustains by his rays of light, the gods, suras and the whole world. He is the Lord of all.

shloka_text: एषब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्चशिवःस्कन्धःप्रजापतिः । महेन्द्रोधनदःकालोयमःसोमोह्यपांपतिः ।।6.107.8।।
explanation: "In the same way, he is the body of Brahma the creator, he is Vishnu also, Shiva also, S Kanda, Prajapati, Mahendra, Kubera, time spirit, Yama, Soma, and Varuna also.

shloka_text: पितरोवसवस्साध्याअश्विनौमरुतोमनुः । वायुर्वह्निःप्रजाःप्राणऋतुकर्ताप्रभाकरः ।।6.107.9।।
explanation: "He is the god of manes, Vasava, Sadhayas, Aswins, Marutha, Manu, wind god, fire god, life of all beings and god of all seasons.

shloka_text: आदित्यःसवितासूर्यःखगःपूषागभस्तिमान् । सुवर्णसदृशोभानुर्हिरण्यरेतादिवाकरः ।।6.107.10।।
explanation: "You are the son of Aditi, the sungod, creator Savitha, the courser in the heavens, the sustainer, the possessor of golden rays, Bhanu, shining with golden rays, the Sun god.

shloka_text: हरिदश्वस्सहस्रार्चिस्सप्तसप्तिर्मरीचिमान् । तिमिरोन्मथनश्शम्भुस्त्वष्टामार्तण्डकोऽंशुमान् ।।6.107.11।।
explanation: "You are the possessor of seven green horses, having a thousand rays, having horse Sapta, destroyer of darkness, mitigator of the suffering of all devotees, giver of happiness, destroyer of all names and forms, the infuser of life in the cosmic egg and having the allpervading rays.

shloka_text: हिरण्यगर्भश्शिशिरस्तपनोभास्करोरविः । अग्निगर्भोऽदितेःपुत्रःशङ्घश्शिशिरनाशनः ।।6.107.12।।
explanation: "You have the golden cosmic egg in the womb, you are cool, you are the purifier, the ruler of all, bringer of day, who Bears the fire of dissolution in the womb. You are the son of Aditi, blissful personified and destroyer of cold.

shloka_text: व्योमनाथस्तमोभेदीऋग्यजुस्सामपारगः । घनवृष्टिरपांमित्रोविन्ध्यवीथीप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.107.13।।
explanation: "You are the Lord of the sky, dispeller of darkness, the master of the three VedasRig, Yajur and Sama, the sender of rain, the friend of water and the courser of the path of Vindhya swiftly.

shloka_text: आतपीमण्डलेमृत्युःपिङ्गलस्सर्वतापनः । कविर्विश्वोमहातेजारक्तस्सर्वभवोद्भव: ।।6.107.14।।
explanation: "You are the possessor of heat, adorned with a circle of rays. You are killer of all enemies, tawny destroyer of all, omniscient, lover of all devotees and source of all evolutes.

shloka_text: नक्षत्रग्रहताराणामधिपोविश्वभावनः । तेजसामपितेजस्वीद्वादशात्मन्नमोऽस्तुते ।।6.107.15।।
explanation: "You are the Lord of all stars and planets. You are the creator of all, resplendent among the splendid, the twelve faces of twelve months. Hail to you.

shloka_text: नमःपूर्वायगिरयेपश्चिमायाद्रयेनमः । ज्योतिर्गणानांपतयेदिनाधिपतयेनमः ।।6.107.16।।
explanation: "Hail to you, rising on the east mountain, setting in the west. Hail to the Lord of all luminaries.

shloka_text: जयायजयभद्रायहर्यश्वायनमोनमः । नमोनमस्सहस्रांशोआदित्यायनमोनमः ।।6.107.17।।
explanation: "Namaskar, Namaskar to the giver of victory, joy born of victory, god having green horses. Hail to you Aditya.

shloka_text: नमउग्रायवीरायसारङ्गायनमोनमः । नमःपद्मप्रबोधायमार्ताण्डायनमोऽस्तुते ।।6.107.18।।
explanation: "Hail to you of terrible form, of valiant one, denoted by the syllable 'AUM'. Namaskar to the awakener of lotuses. Namaskar to the fierce one.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मेशानाच्युतेशायसूर्यायादित्यवर्चसे । भास्वतेसर्वभक्षायरौद्रायवपुषेनमः ।।6.107.19।।
explanation: "Namskar to you, the ruler of Brahma, Siva and Vishnu, to you the Sun god, the spiritual dwelling light in solar orbit, the consumer of all appearing in the form of Rudra.

shloka_text: तमोघ्नायहिमघ्नायशत्रुघ्नायामितात्मने । कृतघ्नघ्नायदेवायज्योतिषांपतयेनमः ।।6.107.20।।
explanation: "You are the dispeller of darkness, dispeller of cold, dispeller of enemies, your extent is immeasurable. You are the destroyer of the ungrateful, the ruler of lights, the Lord of all and namaskar to you.

shloka_text: तप्तचामीकराभायहरयेविश्मकर्मणे । नमस्तमोभिनिघ्नायरुचयेलोकसाक्षिणे।।1.107.21।।
explanation: "Namaskar to one possessing the lustre of pure gold, dispeller of darkness, architect of the universe, splendor incarnate in the form of fire in all, witnessor of all actions in the world.

shloka_text: नाशयत्येषवैभूतंतदेवसृजतिप्रभुः । पायत्येषतपत्येषवर्षत्येष गभस्तिभिः ।1.107.22।।
explanation: "Being a creator and destroyer of the world, this Sun god alone radiates, creates thirst by heat and rains to relieve.

shloka_text: एषसुप्तेषुजागर्तिभूतेषुपरिनिष्ठितः । एषचैवाग्निहोत्रं च फलंचैवाग्निहोत्रिणाम् ।।6.107.23।।
explanation: "He alone pervades the created beings and remains awake in sleep. He alone is the fire sacrifice as well as the fruits obtained from fire sacrifice.

shloka_text: वेदश्चक्रतवश्चैवक्रतूनांफलमेव च । यानिकृत्यानिलोकेषुसर्वेषुपरमप्रभुः ।।6.107.24।।
explanation: "He is all vedas, as well as all the sacrifices as also the fruits of all sacrifices. He is the supreme controller of all actions in all worlds.

shloka_text: एनमापत्सुकृच्छ्रेषुकान्तारेषुभयेषु च । कीर्तयन्पुरुषःकश्चिनावसीदतिराघव ।।6.107.25।।
explanation: "O Raghava! Anyone praying to him will surely not experience grief in straits, in difficulties, in the woods and in times of fear.

shloka_text: पूजयस्वैनमेकाग्रोदेवदेवंजगत्पतिम् । एतत्त्रिगुणितंजप्त्वायुद्धेषुविजयिष्यसि ।।6.107.26।।
explanation: "Worship the Lord of the universe, the Lord of Lords. Worship him alone with concentration of mind, three times of the day by chanting his name. You will attain victory in war."

shloka_text: अस्मिन् क्षणेमहाबाहोरावणंत्वंवधिष्यसि । एवमुक्त्वाततोऽगस्त्योजगाम स यथागतम् ।।6.107.27।।
explanation: Agastya having spoken in that way to the mighty armed Rama to worship the Sun God and assuring him that the very moment he will be able to kill Ravana, left in the same way.

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वामहातेजानष्टशोकोऽभवत्तदा । धारयामाससुप्रीतोराघवःप्रयतात्मवान् ।।6.107.28।।
explanation: Then Rama endowed with extra ordinary energy having heard Agastya, was very delighted and stopped worry. He remembered Aditya and chanted in his mind.

shloka_text: आदित्यंप्रेक्ष्यजप्त्वातुपरंहर्षमवाप्तवान् । त्रिराचम्यशुचिर्भूत्वाधनुरादायवीर्यवान् ।।6.107.29।। रावणंप्रेक्ष्यहृष्टात्मायुद्धार्थंसमुपागमत् । सर्वयत्नेनमहतावधेतस्यधृतोऽभवत् ।।6.107.30।।
explanation: Sipping water three times and looking at Aditya, the valiant Rama getting purified, with devotion chanted the supreme with delight. Then he took up his bow, fixing his eyes at Ravana, and advanced for war with an allout effort determined to destroy Ravana.

shloka_text: आदित्यंप्रेक्ष्यजप्त्वातुपरंहर्षमवाप्तवान् । त्रिराचम्यशुचिर्भूत्वाधनुरादायवीर्यवान् ।।6.107.29।। रावणंप्रेक्ष्यहृष्टात्मायुद्धार्थंसमुपागमत् । सर्वयत्नेनमहतावधेतस्यधृतोऽभवत् ।।6.107.30।।
explanation: Sipping water three times and looking at Aditya, the valiant Rama getting purified, with devotion chanted the supreme with delight. Then he took up his bow, fixing his eyes at Ravana, and advanced for war with an allout effort determined to destroy Ravana.

shloka_text: स रथंसारथिःहृष्टंपरसैन्यप्रधर्षणम् । गन्धर्वनगराकारंसमुच्छ्रितपाताकिनम् ।।6.108.1।। युक्तंपरमसम्पन्नैर्वजिभिर्हेममालिभिः । युद्धोपकरणैःपूर्णंपताकाध्वजमालिनीम् ।।6.108.2।। ग्रसन्तमिवचाकाशंनादयन्तंवसुन्धराम् । प्रणाशंपरनैन्यानांस्वनैन्यस्यप्रहर्षणम् ।।6.108.3।। रावणस्यरथंक्षिप्रंचोदयामाससारथिः ।
explanation: Delighted charioteer drove the chariot of Ravana with speed. It was of the shape of the abode of Gandharvas, capable of destroying enemy's army. It had rows of excellent flags, richly endowed, like the best piece of artwork. It was fixed with flag posts in rows touching the sky and filling space. It was yoked to excellent horses adorned with gold chains and equipped with implements for war. The earth was resounding as it was driven as if to crush the enemy's army and its own army was happy.

shloka_text: स रथंसारथिःहृष्टंपरसैन्यप्रधर्षणम् । गन्धर्वनगराकारंसमुच्छ्रितपाताकिनम् ।।6.108.1।। युक्तंपरमसम्पन्नैर्वजिभिर्हेममालिभिः । युद्धोपकरणैःपूर्णंपताकाध्वजमालिनीम् ।।6.108.2।। ग्रसन्तमिवचाकाशंनादयन्तंवसुन्धराम् । प्रणाशंपरनैन्यानांस्वनैन्यस्यप्रहर्षणम् ।।6.108.3।। रावणस्यरथंक्षिप्रंचोदयामाससारथिः ।
explanation: Delighted charioteer drove the chariot of Ravana with speed. It was of the shape of the abode of Gandharvas, capable of destroying enemy's army. It had rows of excellent flags, richly endowed, like the best piece of artwork. It was fixed with flag posts in rows touching the sky and filling space. It was yoked to excellent horses adorned with gold chains and equipped with implements for war. The earth was resounding as it was driven as if to crush the enemy's army and its own army was happy.

shloka_text: स रथंसारथिःहृष्टंपरसैन्यप्रधर्षणम् । गन्धर्वनगराकारंसमुच्छ्रितपाताकिनम् ।।6.108.1।। युक्तंपरमसम्पन्नैर्वजिभिर्हेममालिभिः । युद्धोपकरणैःपूर्णंपताकाध्वजमालिनीम् ।।6.108.2।। ग्रसन्तमिवचाकाशंनादयन्तंवसुन्धराम् । प्रणाशंपरनैन्यानांस्वनैन्यस्यप्रहर्षणम् ।।6.108.3।। रावणस्यरथंक्षिप्रंचोदयामाससारथिः ।
explanation: Delighted charioteer drove the chariot of Ravana with speed. It was of the shape of the abode of Gandharvas, capable of destroying enemy's army. It had rows of excellent flags, richly endowed, like the best piece of artwork. It was fixed with flag posts in rows touching the sky and filling space. It was yoked to excellent horses adorned with gold chains and equipped with implements for war. The earth was resounding as it was driven as if to crush the enemy's army and its own army was happy.

shloka_text: समापतन्तंसहसास्वनवन्तंमहाध्वजम् ।।6.108.4।। रथंराक्षसराजस्यनरराजोददर्श ह । कृष्णवाजिसमायुक्तंयुक्तंरौद्रेणवर्चसा ।।6.108.5।। दीप्यमानमिवाकाशेविमानंसूर्यवर्चसं । तडित्पताकागहनंदर्शितेन्द्रायुधप्रभम् ।।6.108.6।।
explanation: The chariot bells fixed to the huge flag post were making sounds, yoked to dark horses, and was shining with splendor with rage. It was glowing like a bright sun in the sky displaying its splendor, like the aerial chariot. It looked like a cloud holding water, releasing water of arrows from Rakshasa king's bow. The king of humans saw this chariot.

shloka_text: समापतन्तंसहसास्वनवन्तंमहाध्वजम् ।।6.108.4।। रथंराक्षसराजस्यनरराजोददर्श ह । कृष्णवाजिसमायुक्तंयुक्तंरौद्रेणवर्चसा ।।6.108.5।। दीप्यमानमिवाकाशेविमानंसूर्यवर्चसं । तडित्पताकागहनंदर्शितेन्द्रायुधप्रभम् ।।6.108.6।।
explanation: The chariot bells fixed to the huge flag post were making sounds, yoked to dark horses, and was shining with splendor with rage. It was glowing like a bright sun in the sky displaying its splendor, like the aerial chariot. It looked like a cloud holding water, releasing water of arrows from Rakshasa king's bow. The king of humans saw this chariot.

shloka_text: समापतन्तंसहसास्वनवन्तंमहाध्वजम् ।।6.108.4।। रथंराक्षसराजस्यनरराजोददर्श ह । कृष्णवाजिसमायुक्तंयुक्तंरौद्रेणवर्चसा ।।6.108.5।। दीप्यमानमिवाकाशेविमानंसूर्यवर्चसं । तडित्पताकागहनंदर्शितेन्द्रायुधप्रभम् ।।6.108.6।।
explanation: The chariot bells fixed to the huge flag post were making sounds, yoked to dark horses, and was shining with splendor with rage. It was glowing like a bright sun in the sky displaying its splendor, like the aerial chariot. It looked like a cloud holding water, releasing water of arrows from Rakshasa king's bow. The king of humans saw this chariot.

shloka_text: शराधाराविमुञ्चन्तंधारासारमिवाम्बुदम् । तंदृष्टवामेघसङ्काशमापतन्तंरथंरिपोः ।।6.108.7।। गिरेर्वज्राभिमृष्टस्यदीर्यतस्सदृशस्वनम् । विस्पारयन्वैवेगेनबालचन्द्रानतंधनुः ।।6.108.8।। उवाचसारथिंरामंसहस्राक्षस्यमातलिम् ।
explanation: The flow of arrows (from Ravana) released from the chariot were seen by Rama like the flow of water from rain clouds. Seeing that, Sri Rama made terrific sounds by stretching his bow to crescent shape, and it was as if a mountain struck by thunderbolt had broken and resounding and seeing Matali, charioteer of Indra, Sri Rama spoke as follows.

shloka_text: शराधाराविमुञ्चन्तंधारासारमिवाम्बुदम् । तंदृष्टवामेघसङ्काशमापतन्तंरथंरिपोः ।।6.108.7।। गिरेर्वज्राभिमृष्टस्यदीर्यतस्सदृशस्वनम् । विस्पारयन्वैवेगेनबालचन्द्रानतंधनुः ।।6.108.8।। उवाचसारथिंरामंसहस्राक्षस्यमातलिम् ।
explanation: The flow of arrows (from Ravana) released from the chariot were seen by Rama like the flow of water from rain clouds. Seeing that, Sri Rama made terrific sounds by stretching his bow to crescent shape, and it was as if a mountain struck by thunderbolt had broken and resounding and seeing Matali, charioteer of Indra, Sri Rama spoke as follows.

shloka_text: मातलेपश्यसम्रद्धमापतन्तंरथंरिपोः ।।6.108.9।। यथापसव्यंपततावेगेनमहतापुनः । समरेहन्तुमात्मानंतथानेनकृतामतिः ।।6.108.10।।
explanation: "Matali! the enemy's chariot is darting forward hurriedly. See him coming in the reverse direction with great speed once again. It strikes my mind that he is surely causing his fall."

shloka_text: मातलेपश्यसम्रद्धमापतन्तंरथंरिपोः ।।6.108.9।। यथापसव्यंपततावेगेनमहतापुनः । समरेहन्तुमात्मानंतथानेनकृतामतिः ।।6.108.10।।
explanation: "Matali! the enemy's chariot is darting forward hurriedly. See him coming in the reverse direction with great speed once again. It strikes my mind that he is surely causing his fall."

shloka_text: तदप्रमादमातिष्ठन्प्रत्युद्गच्छरथंरिपोः । विध्वंसयितुमिच्छामिवायुर्मेघमिवोत्थितम् ।।6.108.11।।
explanation: "Being alert, you drive the chariot towards Ravana, just as wind drives the cloud in the sky, as I wish to destroy him."

shloka_text: अविक्लबमसम्भ्रान्तमव्यग्रहृदयेक्षणम् । रमशिसञ्चारनियंप्रचोदयरथंद्रुतम् ।।6.108.12।।
explanation: "Drive the chariot swiftly without confusion, without any agitation, with steady heart and vision, controlling the movement of reins and determination.

shloka_text: कामं न त्वंसमाधेयःपुरन्दररथोचितः । युयुत्सुरहमेकाग्रःस्मारयेत्वां न शिक्ष्ये ।।6.108.13।।
explanation: "You are a driver of great Indra's chariot. You are not required to be told. Wishing to fight with rapt attention, I will remind you now and then not instruct you", said Rama to Matali."

shloka_text: परितुष्टः स रामस्यतेनवाक्येनमातलिः । प्रचोदयामासरथंसुरसारथिरुत्तमः ।।6.108.14।।
explanation: Matali, the best charioteer of the Devatas, was highly delighted at Rama's words and started driving.

shloka_text: अपसव्यंततःकुर्वन् रावणस्यमहारथम् । चक्रसम्भूतरसारावणंव्यवदूनयन् ।।6.108.15।।
explanation: Then Matali made the chariot turn round and by the dust rising from the rolling wheels of the chariot, Ravana was shaken.

shloka_text: ततःक्रुद्धोदशग्रीवस्ताम्रविस्फारितेक्षणः । रथप्रतिमुखंरामंसायकैरवधूनयत् ।।6.108.16।।
explanation: Then furious Ravana, the ten headed Rakshasa, whose eyes turned coppery in anger, struck Rama with arrows.

shloka_text: धर्षणामर्षितोरामोधैर्यंरोषेणलम्भयन् । जग्राहसुमहावेगमैन्द्रंयुधिशरासनम् ।।6.108.17।।
explanation: Rama who was provoked by the assault and army was perturbed. He took up Indra's bow of extraordinary impulse and of high speed like sunbeams.

shloka_text: शरांश्चसुमहावेगान्सूर्यरश्मिसमप्रभान् । तदुपोढुंमहद्युद्धमन्योन्यवधकाङ्क्षिणोः ।।6.108.18।। परस्पराभिमुखयोर्दृप्तयोरिवसिंहयोः ।
explanation: The arrows endowed with very high speed, glowing in radiance like the sun's radiance, holding the arrows, each one desirous of killing the other stood facing each other, came near, and started fighting like lions in the great war.

shloka_text: ततोदेवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः ।।6.108.19।। समीयुर्द्वैरथंद्रष्टुंरावणक्षयकाङ्क्षिणः ।
explanation: Thereafter, the Gandharvas, Devas, Siddhas and sages longing for the end of Ravana came there to witness the duel.

shloka_text: वर्षरुधिरंदेवोरावणस्यरधोपरि ।।6.108.20।। वातामण्डलिनस्त्रीव्राह्यपसव्यंप्रचक्रमुः ।
explanation: Devas rained blood on Ravana's chariot, wind blew in circles intensely from left to right.

shloka_text: महत् गृध्रकुलंचास्यभ्रममाणंनभस्तले ।।6.108.21।। येनयेनरथोयातितेनतेनप्रधावति
explanation: In the sky, a huge flock of eagles hovering on the chariot of Ravana went following the chariot wherever it went.

shloka_text: सन्ध्ययाचावृतालङ्काजपापुष्पनिकाशया ।।6.108.22।। दृश्यतेसम्प्रदीप्तेवदिवसेऽपिवसुन्धरा ।
explanation: Lanka seemed glowing in red colour like at dusk, and as though the earth was burning, shrouded with Japa flowers, even though it was daytime.

shloka_text: सनिर्घातामहोल्काश्चसम्प्रपेतुर्महास्वनाः ।।6.108.23।। विषादयंस्तेरक्षांसिरावणस्यतदाहिताः ।
explanation: Meteors and huge fire dropped there indicating Ravana's end. Seeing them, Rakshasas were sad.

shloka_text: सनिर्घातामहोल्काश्चसम्प्रपेतुर्महास्वनाः ।।6.108.23।। विषादयंस्तेरक्षांसिरावणस्यतदाहिताः ।
explanation: Meteors and huge fire dropped there indicating Ravana's end. Seeing them, Rakshasas were sad.

shloka_text: रावणश्चयतस्तत्रप्रचचालवसुन्धरा ।।6.108.25।। रक्षसां च प्रहरतांगृहीताइवबाहवः ।
explanation: Wherever Ravana went, the earth shook. Many Rakshasas felt their hands clasped.

shloka_text: ताम्राःपीतास्सिताश्वेताःपतितास्सूर्यरश्मयः ।।6.108.26।। दृश्यन्तेरावणस्याग्रेपर्वतस्येवधातवः ।
explanation: The rays of the Sun fell in front of Ravana, in red, yellow, white, and dark like minerals on the mountain.

shloka_text: गृध्रैरनुगताश्चास्यवमन्त्योज्वलनंमुखैः ।।6.108.27।। प्रणेदुर्मुखमीक्षन्त्यःसम्रद्धमशिवंशिवाः ।
explanation: The vultures followed by shejackals vomited, burning fire from their mouths indicating inauspiciousness and screamed.

shloka_text: प्रतिकूलंववेवायूरणेपांसून् समुकतिरन् ।।6.108.28।। तस्यराक्षसराजस्यकुर्वन्दृष्टिविलोपनम् ।
explanation: The unfavourable wind that blew in war, clouded the sight of Rakshasa king.

shloka_text: निपेतुरिन्द्राशनयस्सैन्येचाप्यसमन्ततः ।।6.108.29।। दुर्विषह्यस्वनाघोरंविनाजलधरोदयम् ।
explanation: Without clouds, terrific thunderbolts of Indra (rain) dropped on his (Ravana's) army all over causing unbearable sound.

shloka_text: दिशश्चप्रदिशस्सर्वाबभूवुस्तिमिरावृताः ।।6.108.30।। पांसुवर्षेणमहतादुर्दर्शं च नभोऽभवत् ।
explanation: All directions and intermediate points were enveloped by darkness by the shower of dust and the huge sky was obscure.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्त: कलहंघोरंशारिकास्तद्रथंप्रति ।।6.108.31।। निपेतुश्शतशस्तत्रदारुणादारुणारुताः ।
explanation: Hundreds of minas making frightening sounds, fighting in terrific manner emitting dreadful cries had fallen on the chariot there.

shloka_text: जघनेभ्यःस्फुलिङ्गांश्चनेत्रेभ्योऽश्रूणिसन्ततम् ।।6.108.32।। मुमुचुस्तस्यतुरगास्तुल्यमग्नि च वारि च ।
explanation: His (Ravana's) horses were letting out fire sparks from their hips, tears, water, and fire from their eyes at a time, continuously.

shloka_text: एवंप्रकाराबहवस्समुत्पाताभयापहाः ।।6.108.33।। रावणस्यविनाशायदारुणाःसम्प्रजज्ञिरे ।
explanation: In that manner, many frightful and dreadful objects falling indicated destruction of Ravana.

shloka_text: रामस्यापिनिमित्तानिसौम्यानि च शिवानि च ।।6.108.34।। बभूवुर्जयशंसीनिप्रादुर्भूतानिसर्वशः ।
explanation: On all sides appeared indications of signs of victory for Rama, displaying beings delightful and auspicious.

shloka_text: निमित्तानि च सौम्यानिराघवःस्वजयायवै ।।6.108.35।। दृष्टवापरमसम्हृष्टोहतंमेने च रावणम् ।
explanation: Sri Rama was very delighted over the appearance of good signs of his own victory and thought 'Ravana is destroyed by me'.

shloka_text: ततःप्रवृत्तंसुक्रूरंरामरावणयोस्तदा । सुमहदद्वैरथंयुद्धंसर्वलोकभयावहम् ।।6.109.1।।
explanation: Then there ensued a fierce duel between Rama and Ravana that was fearsome to the whole world.

shloka_text: ततोराक्षससैन्यं च हरीणां च महद्बलम् । प्रगृहीतप्रहरणंनिश्चेष्टंसमवर्तत ।।6.109.2।।
explanation: Then, both Rakshasa army and huge Vanara army, stood motionless holding their weapons ready.

shloka_text: सम्प्रयुद्धेतुतौदृष्टवाबलवन्नरराक्षसौ । व्याक्षिप्तहदृयास्सर्वेपरंविस्मयमागताः ।।6.109.3।।
explanation: Then, when the mighty human and the Rakshasa were both engaged in the battle, distracted at heart, all experienced supreme wonderment.

shloka_text: नाप्रहरणैर्व्यग्रैर्भुजैर्विस्मितबुद्धयः । तस्थुःप्रेक्षय च सर्वेतेनाभिजग्मुःपरस्परम् ।।6.109.4।।
explanation: All the army on both sides lifted their hands up, holding different kinds of implements, and were amazed looking at them and did not attack one another.

shloka_text: रक्षसांरावणंचापिवानराणां च राघवम् । पश्यतांविस्मिताक्षाणांसैन्यंचित्रमिवाबभौ ।।6.109.5।।
explanation: The army of Rakshasas was looking at Ravana and the Vanaras were looking at Raghava with astonishment as though it was a wonderful picture.

shloka_text: तौतुतत्रनिमित्तानिदृष्टवाराघवरावणौ । कृतबुद्धीस्थिरामर्षौयुयुधातेह्यभीतवत् ।।6.109.6।।
explanation: Both Ravana and Rama, seeing their portents, firmly resolved in mind with indignation, fought fearlessly.

shloka_text: जेतव्यमितिकाकुत्स्थोमर्तव्यमितिरावणः । धृतौस्ववीर्यसर्वस्वंयुद्धेऽदर्शयतांतदा ।।6.109.7।।
explanation: Kakuthsa Rama, sure of his victory and Ravana thinking surely of his death, exhibited their prowess totally in the battle, with determination.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधाद्धशग्रीवश्शरान्सन्धायवीर्यवान् । मुमोचध्वजमुद्धिस्यराघवस्यरथेस्थितम् ।।6.109.8।।
explanation: Thereafter, valiant ten headed Ravana, fixing arrows released them in anger aiming at the flag post of Rama's chariot.

shloka_text: तेशरास्तमनासाद्यपुरन्दररथध्वजम् । रथशक्तिंपरामृश्यनिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.109.9।।
explanation: Those arrows, without reaching the post on Indra's chariot, touching the chariot fell on ground.

shloka_text: ततोरामोऽपिसङ्क्रुद्धश्चपमाकृष्यवीर्यवान् । कृतप्रतिकृतंकर्तुंमनसस्सम्प्रचक्रमे ।।6.109.10।।
explanation: Valiant Rama too stretching his bow in anger and thinking of returning back blow to Ravana and started compliance.

shloka_text: रावणध्वजमुद्दिस्यमुमोचनिशितंशरम् । महासर्पमिवासह्यंज्वलन्तंस्वेनतेजसा ।।6.109.11।।
explanation: Rama, intolerant like a snake, targeting Ravana's post, released a sharp bright glowing arrow.

shloka_text: रामश्चिक्षेपतेजस्वीकेतुमुद्धिश्यसायकम् । जगाम स महींछित्त्वादशग्रीवध्वजंशरः ।।6.109.12।।
explanation: Glorious Rama aiming at the flag post of Ravana, released an arrow that tore the post and went into the ground.

shloka_text: स निकृत्तोऽपतद्भूमौरावणस्यन्दनध्वजः । ध्वजस्योन्मथनंदृष्टवारावणस्समहाबलः ।।6.109.13।। सम्प्रदीप्तोऽभवत्क्रोधादमर्षात्प्रहसन्निव । स रोषवशमापन्नश्शरवर्षंववर्ष ह ।।6.109.14।।
explanation: Ravana's flag post fell down, struck by Rama. Mighty Ravana, observing his post being struck, became intolerant, and burning in anger, laughing, rained showers of arrows at Rama out of fury.

shloka_text: स निकृत्तोऽपतद्भूमौरावणस्यन्दनध्वजः । ध्वजस्योन्मथनंदृष्टवारावणस्समहाबलः ।।6.109.13।। सम्प्रदीप्तोऽभवत्क्रोधादमर्षात्प्रहसन्निव । स रोषवशमापन्नश्शरवर्षंववर्ष ह ।।6.109.14।।
explanation: Ravana's flag post fell down, struck by Rama. Mighty Ravana, observing his post being struck, became intolerant, and burning in anger, laughing, rained showers of arrows at Rama out of fury.

shloka_text: रामस्यतुरगान्दीप्तै: शरैर्विव्याथरावणः । तेदिव्याहरयस्तत्रनास्खलन्नापिबभ्रमुः ।।6.109.15।। बभूवुःस्वस्थहृदयाःपद्मनालैरिवाहताः ।
explanation: Ravana with his burning arrows pierced Rama's horses. Those horses were wonderful as they did not stagger or reel as if hurt by lotus stalks and remained complacent.

shloka_text: तेषामसम्भ्रमंदृष्टवावाजिनांरावणस्तदा ।।6.109.16।। भूयएवसुसङ्क्रुद्धश्शरवर्षंमुमोच ह ।
explanation: Ravana perceived that the horses were just unperturbed by his arrows, became enraged and showered arrows excessively.

shloka_text: गदाश्चपरिघांश्चैवचक्राणिमुसलानि च ।।6.109.17।। गिरिशृङ्गाणिवृक्षांश्चतथाशूलपरश्वधान् ।
explanation: Ravana used maces, iron bars, discuses, clubs, mountain peaks, trees and also tridents and axes.

shloka_text: मायाविहितमेतत्तुशस्त्रवर्षमपातयत् ।।6.109.18।। सहस्रशस्तदाबाणानश्रान्तहृदयोद्यमः ।
explanation: Unwearied at heart, Ravana let loose rain of arrows created by magic in thousands.

shloka_text: तुमुलंत्रासजननंभीमंभीमप्रतिस्वनम् ।।6.109.19।। तद्वर्षमभवद्युद्धेनैकशस्त्रमयंमहत् ।
explanation: In that war, noisy, alarming, fearful loud noise of weapons of different kinds, in huge numbers, descended.

shloka_text: राघवरथंसमन्ताद्वानरेबले ।।6.109.20।। सायकैरन्तरिक्षं च चकारसुनिरन्तरम् ।
explanation: Obstructed by Raghava's chariot on all sides, the arrows covered the Vanara army and up to the sky.

shloka_text: मुमोच ह दशग्रीवोनिःसङ्गेनान्तरात्मना ।।6.109.21।। व्यायच्छमानंतंदृष्टवासत्वरमरावणंरणे । प्रहसन्निवकाकुत्स्थसन्दधेनिशितान्शरान् ।।6.109.22।। स मुमो च ततोबाणान्शतशोऽथसहस्रशः ।
explanation: Seeing the ten headed Ravana releasing arrows with enthusiasm, not thinking of anything in his mind, quickly Kakuthsa laughed at them, fixed pointed arrows, and released hundreds and thousands.

shloka_text: मुमोच ह दशग्रीवोनिःसङ्गेनान्तरात्मना ।।6.109.21।। व्यायच्छमानंतंदृष्टवासत्वरमरावणंरणे । प्रहसन्निवकाकुत्स्थसन्दधेनिशितान्शरान् ।।6.109.22।। स मुमो च ततोबाणान्शतशोऽथसहस्रशः ।
explanation: Seeing the ten headed Ravana releasing arrows with enthusiasm, not thinking of anything in his mind, quickly Kakuthsa laughed at them, fixed pointed arrows, and released hundreds and thousands.

shloka_text: तान् दृष्टवारावणश्चक्रेस्वशरैःखंनिरन्तरम् ।।6.109.23।। ततस्थाभ्यांप्रमुक्तेनशरवर्षेणभास्वता । शरबद्धमिवाभातिद्वितीयंभास्वदम्भरम् ।।6.109.24।।
explanation: Seeing the arrows in the sky released by Rama, even Ravana released arrows up to the sky. With the arrows released by both of them, the space became resplendent and by the network of arrows covering it seemed like another sky.

shloka_text: तान् दृष्टवारावणश्चक्रेस्वशरैःखंनिरन्तरम् ।।6.109.23।। ततस्थाभ्यांप्रमुक्तेनशरवर्षेणभास्वता । शरबद्धमिवाभातिद्वितीयंभास्वदम्भरम् ।।6.109.24।।
explanation: Seeing the arrows in the sky released by Rama, even Ravana released arrows up to the sky. With the arrows released by both of them, the space became resplendent and by the network of arrows covering it seemed like another sky.

shloka_text: नानिमित्तोऽभवद्भाणोनानिर्भेत्ता न निष्फलः । अन्योन्यमभिसम्हत्यनिपेतुर्धरणीतले ।।6.109.25।। तथाविसृजतोर्भाणान् रामरावणयोर्मृथे ।
explanation: The arrows released by both Rama and Ravana were without result. None failed to reach the target. None failed to complete the target. The arrows were colliding with one another and fell on the ground.

shloka_text: प्रायुध्येतामविच्छिन्नमस्यन्तौसव्यदक्षिणम् ।।6.109.26।। चक्रतुश्चशरैर्घोरैर्निरुच्छवासमिवाम्बरम् ।
explanation: Discharging from right and left, the two heroes without break vehemently released dreadful arrows that covered the sky and left no breathing space between them.

shloka_text: रावणस्यहयान्रामोहयान्रामस्यरावणः ।।6.109.27।। जघ्नतुस्तौतदान्योन्यंकृतानुकृतकारिणौ ।
explanation: Ravana struck Rama's horses and Rama struck Ravana's horses blow to blow at that time.

shloka_text: एवंतुतौसुसङ्क्रुद्धौचक्रतुर्युद्धमुत्तमम् ।।6.109.28।। मुहूर्तमभवद्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् ।
explanation: Both became furious in that way and the best duel took place for a moment that was fierce and horipulating.

shloka_text: तौतथायुध्यमानौतुसमरेरामरावणौ । ददृशुस्सर्वभूतानिविस्मितेनान्तरात्मना ।।6.110.1।।
explanation: As Rama and Ravana were thus fighting in war, all beings watched with astonishment in mind.

shloka_text: अर्धयन्तौतुसमरेतयोस्तौस्यन्दनोत्तमौ । परस्परमभिक्रुद्धौपरस्परमभिद्रुतौ ।।6.110.2।।
explanation: Both of them were moving quickly seeking to gain one another, very furiously persevering.

shloka_text: परस्परवधेयुक्तौघोररूपौबभूवतुः । मण्डलानि च वीधीश्चगतप्रत्यागतानि च ।।6.110.3।। दर्शयन्तौबहुविधांसूतसामर्थ्यजांगतिम् ।
explanation: Both striking one another diligently, going in circles moving forward and backward displaying feats, went on.

shloka_text: अर्धयन्रावणंरामोराघवंचापिरावणः ।।6.110.4।। गतिवेगंसमापन्नौप्रतिवेगप्रवर्तने ।
explanation: Ravana hurting Rama and vice versa displaying quickness in retaliation and speed of arrows, the fight happened.

shloka_text: क्षिपतोश्शरजालानितयोस्तौस्यन्दनोत्तमौ ।।6.110.5।। चेरतुस्सम्युगमहीं सासारौ जलदाविव ।
explanation: The network of arrows released by both of them from the chariots were like water streams from two clouds in the battlefield

shloka_text: दर्शयित्वातदातौतुगतिंबहुविधांरणे ।।6.110.6।। परस्परस्याभिमुखौपुनरेव च तस्थतुः ।
explanation: Then those two, having seen many movements, once again stood facing each other in the battlefield.

shloka_text: धुरंधुरेणरथयोर्वक्त्रंवक्त्रेणवाजिनाम् ।।6.110.7।। पताकाश्चपताकाभिस्समीयुस्स्थितयोस्तदा ।
explanation: The two chariots stood facing each other on the battlefield once more, the axle of one chariot facing the axle of another chariot, the flag of one with another flag, the standard with another standard, the face of one horse with the face of another horse stood and it seemed as though they were together.

shloka_text: रावणस्यततोरामोधनुर्मुस्तैश्शितैश्शरैः ।।6.110.8।। चतुर्भिश्चतुरोदीप्तान्हयान्प्रत्यपसर्पयत् ।
explanation: Thereupon, Rama, stretching the bow, released four sharp glowing arrows at Ravana's four horses and drove them back.

shloka_text: सक्रोधवशमापन्नोहयानामपसर्पणे ।।6.110.9।। मुमोचनिशितान्बाणान्राघवायदशाननः ।
explanation: Fallen prey to anger for retreating the horses, the ten headed Ravana released pointed arrows on Raghava.

shloka_text: सोतिविद्धोबलवतादशग्रीवेणराघवः ।।6.110.10।। जगाम न विकारं च न चापिव्यथितोऽभवत् ।
explanation: Raghava, though wounded by the mighty Ravana's arrows, did notexperience suffering or agitation, nor disquiet.

shloka_text: चिक्षेप च पुनर्भाणान्वज्रपातसमस्वनान् ।।6.110.11।। सारथिंवज्रहस्तस्यसमुद्दिश्यदशाननः ।
explanation: The ten headed Ravana with his thunderbolt like hands hurled arrows and struck the charioteer of Rama, making sounds like thunder.

shloka_text: मातलेस्तुमहावेगाश्शरीरेपतिताश्शराः ।।6.110.12।। न सूक्ष्ममपिसम्मोहंव्यथांवाप्रददुर्युधि ।
explanation: Even though the arrows fell on Matali's body at great speed, he did not feel perturbed or experience even slight suffering.

shloka_text: तयाधर्षणयाक्रुद्धोमातलेर्नतथात्मनः ।।6.110.13।। चकारशरजालेनराघवोविमुखंरिपुम् ।
explanation: Rama was furious for tormenting Matali like that, but not for hurting him and in fury discharged a network of arrows on him (Ravana) and diverted him.

shloka_text: विंशतिंत्रिंशतिंषष्टिंशतशोऽथसहस्रशः ।।6.110.14।। मुमोचराघवोवीरस्सायकान्स्यन्दनेरिपोः ।
explanation: Heroic Raghava thereafter, let loose shafts in twenties, thirties, sixties, hundreds, and thousands at Ravana's chest.

shloka_text: रावणोऽपिततःक्रुद्धोरथस्थराक्षसेश्वरः ।।6.110.15।। गदामुसलवर्षेणरामंप्रत्यर्दयद्रणे ।
explanation: Enraged Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, also in return, retaliated with maces and mallets.

shloka_text: तत्प्रवृतंपुनर्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् ।।6.110.16।। गदानांमुसलानां च परिघाणांचनिस्स्वनैः । शराणांपुङ्खवातैश्चक्षुभितास्सप्तसागराः ।।6.110.17।।
explanation: Once again ensued a tumultuous war fought with maces, mallets, and iron bars, caused hair to stand and the resound of the speed of weapons caused agitation in the seven seas.

shloka_text: तत्प्रवृतंपुनर्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् ।।6.110.16।। गदानांमुसलानां च परिघाणांचनिस्स्वनैः । शराणांपुङ्खवातैश्चक्षुभितास्सप्तसागराः ।।6.110.17।।
explanation: Once again ensued a tumultuous war fought with maces, mallets, and iron bars, caused hair to stand and the resound of the speed of weapons caused agitation in the seven seas.

shloka_text: क्षुब्दानांसागराणां च पातालतलवासिनः । व्यथितादानवाःसर्वेपन्नगाश्चसहस्रशः ।।6.110.18।।
explanation: By the agitation and sounds in the seas, all the Danavas and snakes in thousands inhabiting the seas got distressed.

shloka_text: चकम्पेमेदिनीकृत्स्नासशैलवनकानना । भास्करोनिष्प्रभश्चासीन्नवनौचापिमारुतः ।।6.110.19।।
explanation: The entire globe with its mountains, gardens and forests shook, the Sun lost his radiance, even the wind did not blow.

shloka_text: ततोदेवास्सगन्धर्वास्सिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः । चिन्तामापेदिरेसर्वेसकिन्नरमहोरगाः ।।6.110.20।।
explanation: Thereafter, the Gandharvas, Devas, Siddhas, great sages, Kinneras and huge serpents all of them became anxious.

shloka_text: स्वस्तिगोब्राह्मणेभ्योऽस्तुलोकास्तिष्ठन्तुशाश्वताः । जयतांराघयसङ्ख्येरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.110.21।। एवंजपन्तोऽपश्यंस्तेदेवास्सर्षिगणास्तदा । रामरावणयोर्युद्धंसुघोरंरोमहर्षणम् ।।6.110.22।।
explanation: "May the hosts of sages, Devas, cows and brahmanas be auspicious. May all the worlds endure forever. May Rama conquer Ravana, the Rakshasa king," chanting in that manner all witnessed the terrific war between Rama and Ravana that caused hair to stand.

shloka_text: स्वस्तिगोब्राह्मणेभ्योऽस्तुलोकास्तिष्ठन्तुशाश्वताः । जयतांराघयसङ्ख्येरावणंराक्षसेश्वरम् ।।6.110.21।। एवंजपन्तोऽपश्यंस्तेदेवास्सर्षिगणास्तदा । रामरावणयोर्युद्धंसुघोरंरोमहर्षणम् ।।6.110.22।।
explanation: "May the hosts of sages, Devas, cows and brahmanas be auspicious. May all the worlds endure forever. May Rama conquer Ravana, the Rakshasa king," chanting in that manner all witnessed the terrific war between Rama and Ravana that caused hair to stand.

shloka_text: गन्धर्वाप्सरसांसङ्घादृष्टवायुद्धमनूपमम् । गगनंगगनाकारंसागरस्सागरोपमः ।।6.110.23।। रामरावणयोर्युद्धंरामरावणयोरिव । एवंब्रुवन्तोददृशुस्तद्युद्धंरामरावणम् ।।6.110.24।।
explanation: Gandharvas and Apsaras watching the combination of Rama and Ravana fighting an unimaginable war said that sky is its own analogue for sky, sea is its own analogue to sea, in the same way is the struggle between Rama and Ravana is unique like Rama and Ravana's struggle and looked at the combat.

shloka_text: गन्धर्वाप्सरसांसङ्घादृष्टवायुद्धमनूपमम् । गगनंगगनाकारंसागरस्सागरोपमः ।।6.110.23।। रामरावणयोर्युद्धंरामरावणयोरिव । एवंब्रुवन्तोददृशुस्तद्युद्धंरामरावणम् ।।6.110.24।।
explanation: Gandharvas and Apsaras watching the combination of Rama and Ravana fighting an unimaginable war said that sky is its own analogue for sky, sea is its own analogue to sea, in the same way is the struggle between Rama and Ravana is unique like Rama and Ravana's struggle and looked at the combat.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधान्महाबासूरघूणांकीर्तिवर्धनः । सन्धायधनुषारामश्शरमाशीविषोपमम् ।।6.110.25।। रावणस्यशिरोऽच्छिन्दच्छ्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । तछचिरःपतितंभूमौदृष्टंइलोकैस्त्रिभिस्तदा ।।6.110.26।।
explanation: Then the mighty armed Raghava, enhancer of glory, in wrath like a venomous snake, fitting the bow with arrows cut off the head of Ravana graced with shining earrings. Then the three worlds witnessed the head cut off and fallen on the earth surface.

shloka_text: ततःक्रोधान्महाबासूरघूणांकीर्तिवर्धनः । सन्धायधनुषारामश्शरमाशीविषोपमम् ।।6.110.25।। रावणस्यशिरोऽच्छिन्दच्छ्रीमज्ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । तछचिरःपतितंभूमौदृष्टंइलोकैस्त्रिभिस्तदा ।।6.110.26।।
explanation: Then the mighty armed Raghava, enhancer of glory, in wrath like a venomous snake, fitting the bow with arrows cut off the head of Ravana graced with shining earrings. Then the three worlds witnessed the head cut off and fallen on the earth surface.

shloka_text: तस्यैवसदृशंचान्यद्रावणस्योत्थितंशिरः । तत्क्षिप्तंक्षिप्रहस्तेनरामेणक्षिप्रकारिणा ।।6.110.27।।
explanation: A similar looking head arose on Ravana's head. Rama, endowed with a quick hand, cut off by his hand the other head.

shloka_text: द्वितीयंरावणशिरश्छिन्नंसम्यतिसायकैः । छिन्नमात्रं च तच्चीर्षंपुनरेवप्रदृश्यते ।।6.110.28।।
explanation: Before cutting that second head of Ravana again another head appeared.

shloka_text: तदप्यशनिसङ्काशैश्छिन्नंरामस्यसायकैः । एवमेवशतंछिन्नंशिरसांतुल्यवर्चसाम् ।।6.110.29।।
explanation: Rama cut off the afore said head with Indra's thunderbolt like arrows. In that way equally charming a hundred heads were struck off.
