shloka_text: न चैवरावणस्यान्तोदृश्यतेजीवितक्षये । ततस्सर्वास्त्रविद्वीरःकौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः ।।6.110.30।। मार्गणैर्बहुभिर्युक्तश्चिन्तयामासराघवः ।
explanation: Rama, knower of all shastras, valiant, enhancer of Kausalya's joy, well versed in the use of weapons, was not able to see the end of Ravana's life. He started thinking.

shloka_text: मारीचोनिहतोयैस्तुखरोयैस्तुसदूषणः ।।6.110.31।। क्रौञ्चावनेविराधस्तुकबन्धोदण्डकेवने । यैस्सालागिरयोभग्नावाली च क्षुभितोऽम्बुधिः ।।6.110.32।। त इमेसायकास्सर्वेयुद्धेप्रात्ययिकामम किनुतत्कारणंयेनरावणेमन्दतेजसः ।।6.110.33।।
explanation: 'Earlier, by my arrows, Maricha was killed, Dushana and Khara were killed, Kabhanda was killed in Krauncha forest, Virada was killed in Dandaka forest. By which arrows Sala trees were cut off, mountain was broken, ocean was agitated, and Vali was killed, are wasted with Ravana, who is less brilliant in war. What is the reason?'

shloka_text: मारीचोनिहतोयैस्तुखरोयैस्तुसदूषणः ।।6.110.31।। क्रौञ्चावनेविराधस्तुकबन्धोदण्डकेवने । यैस्सालागिरयोभग्नावाली च क्षुभितोऽम्बुधिः ।।6.110.32।। त इमेसायकास्सर्वेयुद्धेप्रात्ययिकामम किनुतत्कारणंयेनरावणेमन्दतेजसः ।।6.110.33।।
explanation: 'Earlier, by my arrows, Maricha was killed, Dushana and Khara were killed, Kabhanda was killed in Krauncha forest, Virada was killed in Dandaka forest. By which arrows Sala trees were cut off, mountain was broken, ocean was agitated, and Vali was killed, are wasted with Ravana, who is less brilliant in war. What is the reason?'

shloka_text: मारीचोनिहतोयैस्तुखरोयैस्तुसदूषणः ।।6.110.31।। क्रौञ्चावनेविराधस्तुकबन्धोदण्डकेवने । यैस्सालागिरयोभग्नावाली च क्षुभितोऽम्बुधिः ।।6.110.32।। त इमेसायकास्सर्वेयुद्धेप्रात्ययिकामम किनुतत्कारणंयेनरावणेमन्दतेजसः ।।6.110.33।।
explanation: 'Earlier, by my arrows, Maricha was killed, Dushana and Khara were killed, Kabhanda was killed in Krauncha forest, Virada was killed in Dandaka forest. By which arrows Sala trees were cut off, mountain was broken, ocean was agitated, and Vali was killed, are wasted with Ravana, who is less brilliant in war. What is the reason?'

shloka_text: इतिचिन्तापरश्चासीदप्रमत्तश्चसम्युगे । ववर्षशरवर्षाणीराघवोरावणोरसि ।।6.110.34।।
explanation: Even though Raghava was thinking so, yet remaining alert in the duel, rained arrows on Ravana's chest.

shloka_text: रावणोऽपिततःक्रुद्धोरथस्थोराक्षसेश्वरः । गदामुसलवर्षेणरामंप्रत्यर्दयद्रणे ।।6.110.35।।
explanation: Valiant enemy of Raghava also seated in the chariot, rained three hundred, sixties, hundreds, and thousands of arrows.

shloka_text: तत्प्रवृत्तंमहद्युद्धंतुमुलंरोमहर्षणम् । अन्तरिक्षे च भूमौ च पुनश्चगिरिमूर्धनि ।।6.110.36।।
explanation: Great war commenced in the sky, as well as on the earth, and on top of mountain again, which was horipulating,

shloka_text: देवदानवयक्षाणांपिशाचोरगरक्षसाम् । पश्यतांतन्महायुद्धंसप्तरात्रमवर्तत ।।6.110.37।।
explanation: The Devas, Danavas, Yakshasas also the fiends Demon, Nagas and Rakshasas watched the great war that continued for seven days and nights.

shloka_text: नैव रात्रिं न दिवसंमुहूर्तं न च क्षणम् । रामरावणयोर्युद्धंविराममुपगच्छति ।।6.110.38।।
explanation: The fight between Rama and Ravana continued all day and night, without stopping for a moment.

shloka_text: अथसंस्मारयामासमातलिराघवंतदा । अजानन्निवकिंवीरत्वमेनमनुवर्तसे ।।6.111.1।।
explanation: Matali reminded Rama in this way," O heroic Rama, why are you doing this way, as if you do not know?"

shloka_text: विसृजास्मैवधायत्वमस्त्रंपैतामहंप्रभो । विनाशकालःकथितोःयःसुरैःसोऽद्यवर्तते ।।6.111.2।।
explanation: "O king! As spoken by Suras, the destruction of Ravana has come now. Use the missile of the creator Brahma."

shloka_text: ततःसंस्मारितोरामस्तेनवाक्येनमातलेः । जग्राह स शरंदीप्तंनिःश्वसन्तमिवोरगम् ।।6.111.3।। यंतस्मैप्रथमंप्रादादगस्त्योभगवानृषिः । ब्रह्मदत्तंमहाबाणममोघंयुधिवीर्यवान् ।।6.111.4।।
explanation: Suggested and reminded by Matali, valiant Sri Rama seized hold of the wonderful glowing arrow, bestowed by Brahma, and given by the divine to sage Agastya first. Breathing heavily, like a serpent, Rama seized the arrow.

shloka_text: ततःसंस्मारितोरामस्तेनवाक्येनमातलेः । जग्राह स शरंदीप्तंनिःश्वसन्तमिवोरगम् ।।6.111.3।। यंतस्मैप्रथमंप्रादादगस्त्योभगवानृषिः । ब्रह्मदत्तंमहाबाणममोघंयुधिवीर्यवान् ।।6.111.4।।
explanation: Suggested and reminded by Matali, valiant Sri Rama seized hold of the wonderful glowing arrow, bestowed by Brahma, and given by the divine to sage Agastya first. Breathing heavily, like a serpent, Rama seized the arrow.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणानिर्मितंपूर्वमिन्द्रार्थममितौजसा । दत्तंसुरपतेःपूर्वंत्रिलोकजयकाङ्क्षिणः ।।6.111.5।।
explanation: Earlier, this powerful arrow was created for Indra's sake by Brahma and was bestowed to Indra, the king of gods, who was desirous of conquering the three worlds.

shloka_text: यस्यवाजेषुपवनःफलेपावकभास्करौ । शरीरमाकाशमयंगौरवेमेरुमन्दरौ ।।6.111.6।।
explanation: The wind god presided over its feathers, the fire god and the Sun god presided over its head, its energy was presided over by Meru and Mandara mountains and its weight by the sky.

shloka_text: जाज्वल्यमानंवपुषासुपुङ्खंहेमभूषितम् । तेजसासर्वभूतानांकृतंभास्करवर्चसम् ।।6.111.7।।
explanation: Its form was shining with feathers, decked with gold, splendid with all elements and brilliant like the sun.

shloka_text: सधूममिवकालानगिंदीप्तमाशीविषोपमम् । नरनागाश्ववृद्धानांभेदनंक्षिप्रकारिणम् ।।6.111.8।।
explanation: Like fire at the time of dissolution of the universe, burning like venomous serpent, capable of splitting hosts of enemy, men, elephants, and horses and quick in action.

shloka_text: द्वाराणांपरिघाणां च गिरीणांचापिभेदनम् । नानारुधिरदिग्धाङ्गंमेदोदिग्धंसुदारुणम् ।।6.111.9।।
explanation: Capable of splitting gateways, iron bars, even mountains, smeared with blood and brain marrow of various Asuras, of dreadful appearance.

shloka_text: वज्रसारंमहानादंनानासमितिदारणम् । सर्ववित्रासनंभीमंश्वसन्तमिवपन्नगम् ।।6.111.10।।
explanation: Strong as thunderbolt, loud sounding, dispersing every deceitful kind of army, frightening to all kinds of beings, hissing like a serpent.

shloka_text: कङ्कगृध्रबकानां च गोमायुगणरक्षसाम् । नित्यंभक्षप्रदंयुद्धेयमरूपंभयापहम् ।।6.111.11।।
explanation: In war, it provides food for buzzards, vultures, and herons, and also jackals and Rakshasas, causing terror in the form of Yama (God of death).

shloka_text: नन्दनंवानरेन्द्राणांरक्षसामवसादनम् । वाजितंविविधैर्वाजैश्चारुचित्रैर्गरुत्मतः ।।6.111.12।।
explanation: Provides delight for Vanara chiefs, causes destruction of Rakshasas, provides picturesque plumes of eagles to arrows.

shloka_text: तमुत्तमेषुंलोकानामिक्ष्वाकुभयनाशनम् । द्विषतांकीर्तिहरणंप्रहर्षकरमात्मनः ।।6.111.13।। अभिम्नत्यततोरामस्तंमहेषुंमहाबलः । वेदप्रोक्तेनविधिनासन्दधेकार्मुकेबली ।।6.111.14।।
explanation: The great arrow, was a dispeller of fear of enemies to Ikshvaku kings, which takes away the glory of enemies, delighting to oneself, chanting vedas as per tradition, charging with mystic power, mighty strong Rama fitted to the bow.

shloka_text: तमुत्तमेषुंलोकानामिक्ष्वाकुभयनाशनम् । द्विषतांकीर्तिहरणंप्रहर्षकरमात्मनः ।।6.111.13।। अभिम्नत्यततोरामस्तंमहेषुंमहाबलः । वेदप्रोक्तेनविधिनासन्दधेकार्मुकेबली ।।6.111.14।।
explanation: The great arrow, was a dispeller of fear of enemies to Ikshvaku kings, which takes away the glory of enemies, delighting to oneself, chanting vedas as per tradition, charging with mystic power, mighty strong Rama fitted to the bow.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् सधनीयमानेतुराघवेणशरोत्तमे । सर्वभूतानिसन्त्रेसुश्चचाल च वसुन्धरा ।।6.111.15।।
explanation: As Raghava started fixing his excellent arrow, all beings got terrified and the earth shook.

shloka_text: स रावणायसङ्रुद्धोभृशमायम्यकार्मुकम् । चिक्षेपपरमायत्तःशरंमर्मविदारणम् ।।6.111.16।।
explanation: Rama, provoked by anger, stretched the bow to full length, very well prepared, released the arrow on Ravana, which was capable of tearing into the vital parts.

shloka_text: स वज्रइवदुर्धर्षोवज्रिबाहुविसर्जितः । कृतान्तइवचावार्योन्यपतद्रावणोरसि ।।6.111.17।।
explanation: Like the thunderbolt hurled by the arm of Indra, difficult to obstruct, capable of bringing life to an end, that arrow released by Rama penetrated into Ravana's chest.

shloka_text: स विसृष्टोमहावेगश्शरीरान्तकरश्शरः । चिच्छेदहृदयंतस्यरावणस्यदुरात्मनः ।।6.111.18।।
explanation: Loosed at high velocity, that arrow capable of putting an end to the body, split as under the heart of evilminded Ravana

shloka_text: रुधिराक्तस्सवेगेनशरीरान्तकरःशरः । रावणस्यहरन्प्राणान्विवेशधरणीतलम् ।।6.111.19।।
explanation: That arrow which was capable of putting an end to the body took out Ravana's life and smeared with blood, it entered the earth.

shloka_text: स शरोरावणंहत्वारुधिरार्द्रीकृतच्छविः । कृतकर्मानिभृतवत्स्वतूणींपुनराविशत् ।।6.111.20।।
explanation: That arrow of Rama, on killing Ravana, soaked in blood, having accomplished the task quietly reentered its quiver.

shloka_text: तस्यहस्ताद्धतस्याशुकार्मुकं च ससायकम् । निपपातसहप्राणैर्भ्रश्यमानस्यजीवितात् ।।6.111.21।।
explanation: Thus, when Ravana was killed and lost his life, the bow and arrow in his hand also fell along with his life breath.

shloka_text: गतासुर्भीमवेगस्तुनैरृतेन्द्रोमहाद्युतिः । पपातस्यन्दनाद्भूमौवृत्रोवज्रहतोयथा ।।6.111.22।।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, who possessed terrific speed and courage, having lost life, fell on earth like Vrttra struck down by thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तंदृष्टवापतितंभूमौहतशेषानिशाचराः । हतनाधाभयत्रस्तास्सर्वतस्सम्प्रदुद्रुवुः ।।6.111.23।।
explanation: Seeing their Lord killed and fallen on the ground, the leftover night rangers fled all over in fear.

shloka_text: सर्वतश्चाभिपेतुस्तान्वानराद्रुमयोधिनः । दशग्रीववधंदृष्टवावानराजितकाशिनः ।।6.111.24।।
explanation: Seeing Ravana killed, the Vanaras holding trees went roaming on all sides, feeling triumphant.

shloka_text: अर्दितावानरैर्भ्रष्टालङ्कामभ्यपतन् भयात् । हताश्रयात्वात्करुणैर्भाष्पप्रस्रवणैर्मुखैः ।।6.111.25।।
explanation: The Rakshasas hurt by the Vanaras, lost battle and their king killed, were piteous and went towards Lanka in fear, eyes filled with tears.

shloka_text: ततोविनेदुःसम्हृष्टावानराःजितकाशिनः । वदन्तोराघवजयंरावणस्य ज तद्वधम् ।।6.111.26।।
explanation: Then the Vanaras, feeling triumphant, got highly excited over Rama's victory and the death of Ravana, and shouted aloud in joy.

shloka_text: अथान्तरिक्षेव्यनदत्सौम्यस्त्रिदशदुन्धुभिः । दिव्यगन्धशहस्तत्रमारुतस्सुसुकोववौ ।।6.111.27।।
explanation: And then thirty drums of gods sounded in the sky. Divine fragrant pleasant breeze blew.

shloka_text: निपपातान्तरिक्षाच्चपुष्पवृष्टिस्तदाभुवि । किरन्तीराघवरथंदुरवापामनोहरा ।।6.111.28।।
explanation: Then from heaven, a very pleasing shower of flowers, difficult to know from where, fell on Raghava's chariot covering it and dropped on the ground.

shloka_text: राघवस्तवसंयुक्तागगने च विशुश्रुवे । साधुसाध्वितिवागग्य्रादेवतानांमहात्मनाम् ।।6.111.29।।
explanation: The gods too praised Sri Rama, the great soul saying, 'Well done, Well done', from the heaven, which was distinctly heard.

shloka_text: अविवेशमहान् हर्षोदेवानांचारणैःसह । रावणेनिहतेरौद्रेसर्वलोकभयङ्करे ।।6.111.30।।
explanation: When Ravana, a terror of all worlds was killed, the Charanas and Devas were filled with great joy.

shloka_text: ततःसकामंसुग्रीवमङ्गदं च विभीषणम् । चकारराघवःप्रीतोहत्वाराक्षसपुङ्गवम् ।।6.111.31।।
explanation: The foremost of the Rakshasas killed, Raghava was pleased and having fulfilled the desire of Sugriva, Angada, Vibheeshana, he made them happy.

shloka_text: ततःप्रजग्मुःप्रशमंमरुद्गणादिशःप्रसेदुर्विमलंनभोऽभवत् । महीचकम्पे न च मारुतोववौस्थिरप्रभश्चाप्यभवद्दिवाकरः ।।6.111.32।।
explanation: Then the host of gods attained tranquil, quarters brightened, sky became clear, earth no longer shook, wind blew and even the Sun became steady and radiant.

shloka_text: ततस्तुसुग्रीवविभीषणाङ्गदाःसुहृद्विशिष्टास्सहलक्ष्मणास्तदा । समेत्यहृष्टाविजयेनराघवंरणेऽभिरामंविधिनाभ्यपूजयन् ।।6.111.33।।
explanation: Then all of them (hosts of gods) coming together, accompanied by Lakshmana, Sugriva, Vibheeshana, and Angada along with other friends, happy about the victory in the battle offered prayers to charming Sri Rama in accordance with tradition.

shloka_text: भ्रातरंनिहतंदृष्टवाशयानंनिर्जितंरणे । शोकवेगपरीतात्माविललापविभीषणः ।।6.112.1।।
explanation: Vibheeshana, seeing his brother killed and lying in the battlefield, lamented immersed in sorrow.

shloka_text: वीर विक्रान्त विख्यात प्रवीण नयकोविद । महार्हाशयनोपेतकिंशेषेनिहतोभुवि ।।6.112.2।।
explanation: "O valiant, powerful and renowned king! You who were skilled in all fields and in polity, accustomed to a sumptuous bed, why are you lying on ground?"

shloka_text: विक्षिप्यदीर्घौनिश्चेष्टौभुजावङ्गभूषितौ । मुकुटेनापवृत्तेनभास्कराकारवर्चसा ।।6.112.3।।
explanation: "Decked with armlets, motionless are your arms, broken, knocked down with the crown, radiant like the Sun."

shloka_text: दंवीरसम्प्राप्तंयन्मयापूर्वमीरितम् । काममोहपरीतस्ययत्तन्नरुचितंतव ।।6.112.4।।
explanation: "Hero! That which was predicted by me earlier, which did not find your favour due to your infatuation, has come true."

shloka_text: यन्नदर्पात्प्रहस्तोवानेन्द्रजिन्नापरेजनाः । न कुम्बकर्णोऽतिरथोनातिकायोनरान्तकः ।।6.112.5।। न स्वयंत्वममन्येथास्तस्योदर्कोऽयमागतः ।
explanation: "Either Prahastha or Indrajith or other Rakshasas, or even Kumbhakarna, an exceeding car warrior, nor Atikaya or Naranthaka or you also did not care for my counsel. Its consequence has come now."

shloka_text: गतस्सेतुस्सुनीतीनांगतोधर्मस्यविग्रहः ।।6.112.6।। गतस्सत्त्वस्यसङ्क्षेपःप्रस्तावानांगतिर्गता । आदित्यःपतितोभूमौमग्नस्तमसिचन्द्रमाः ।।6.112.7।। चित्रभानुःप्रशान्तार्चिर्व्यवसायोनिरुद्यमः । अस्मिन्निपतितेवीरे भूमौशस्त्रभृतांवरे ।।6.112.8।।
explanation: " As this hero, the wielder of weapons has fallen down on ground, the prudent one who was at boundary, disappeared he who was the form of righteousness, departed he who was a repository of might, thrown down and out of sight he, who was praiseworthy for all, lost position. With the hero falling down, it seems the Sun has fallen down, the moon plunged into darkness, fire became extinct, and the enthusiasm of people wasted."

shloka_text: गतस्सेतुस्सुनीतीनांगतोधर्मस्यविग्रहः ।।6.112.6।। गतस्सत्त्वस्यसङ्क्षेपःप्रस्तावानांगतिर्गता । आदित्यःपतितोभूमौमग्नस्तमसिचन्द्रमाः ।।6.112.7।। चित्रभानुःप्रशान्तार्चिर्व्यवसायोनिरुद्यमः । अस्मिन्निपतितेवीरे भूमौशस्त्रभृतांवरे ।।6.112.8।।
explanation: " As this hero, the wielder of weapons has fallen down on ground, the prudent one who was at boundary, disappeared he who was the form of righteousness, departed he who was a repository of might, thrown down and out of sight he, who was praiseworthy for all, lost position. With the hero falling down, it seems the Sun has fallen down, the moon plunged into darkness, fire became extinct, and the enthusiasm of people wasted."

shloka_text: गतस्सेतुस्सुनीतीनांगतोधर्मस्यविग्रहः ।।6.112.6।। गतस्सत्त्वस्यसङ्क्षेपःप्रस्तावानांगतिर्गता । आदित्यःपतितोभूमौमग्नस्तमसिचन्द्रमाः ।।6.112.7।। चित्रभानुःप्रशान्तार्चिर्व्यवसायोनिरुद्यमः । अस्मिन्निपतितेवीरे भूमौशस्त्रभृतांवरे ।।6.112.8।।
explanation: " As this hero, the wielder of weapons has fallen down on ground, the prudent one who was at boundary, disappeared he who was the form of righteousness, departed he who was a repository of might, thrown down and out of sight he, who was praiseworthy for all, lost position. With the hero falling down, it seems the Sun has fallen down, the moon plunged into darkness, fire became extinct, and the enthusiasm of people wasted."

shloka_text: किंशेषमिहलोकस्यगतसत्त्वस्यसम्प्रति । रणेराक्षसशार्दूलेप्रसुप्तइवपांसुषु ।।6.112.9।।
explanation: "With the tiger among the Rakshasas fallen asleep like this in the dust in the battlefield, strength of the people departed. What is left in this world?"

shloka_text: धृतिप्रवालःप्रसह्याग्य्रपुष्पस्तपोबलश्शौर्यनिबद्धमूलः । रणेमहान्राक्षसराजवृक्षःसम्मर्दितोराघवमारुतेन ।।6.112.10।।
explanation: "The great tree in the form of Rakshasa king, with its firmness as leaves, stubbornness as its blossom, austerity as strength, valour as strong roots, was crushed by the tempest of Raghava in the battlefield."

shloka_text: तेजोविषाणःकुलवंशवंशःकोपप्रसादापरगात्रहस्तः । इक्ष्वाकुसिंहावगृहीतदेहःसुप्तःक्षितौरावणगन्धहस्ती ।।6.112.11।।
explanation: "Ravana's prowess as tusks, father and grand fathers' race as back of the body, wrath as lower body and graciousness as proboscis, overthrown by a lion in the shape of Ikshvaku race having killed him he is lying asleep thrown down."

shloka_text: पराक्रमोत्साहविजृम्भितार्चिर्निःश्वासधूमस्स्वबलप्रतापः । प्रतापवान्सम्यतिराक्षसाग्निर्विर्वापितोरामपयोधरेण ।।6.112.12।।
explanation: "The prowess and exceeding energy of Ravana as flames, his sighs as smoke, his own strength as heat, endowed with might, that fire of Rakshasa has been extinguished by the rainy cloud in the shape of Rama in the battlefield."

shloka_text: सिंहरक्षलाङ्गूलककुद्विषाणःपराभिजिद्गन्धनगन्धहस्ती । रक्षोवृषश्चापलकर्णचक्षुःक्षितीश्वरव्याघ्रहतोऽवसन्नः ।।6.112.13।।
explanation: "Rakshasas who followed as tails, humps and horns, Ravana the conquerors of enemies, like elephants in pride, animality as ears and eyes, the bull in the form of Rakshasa Ravana was killed by Rama, the master of earth in the form of tiger."

shloka_text: वदन्तंहेतुमद्वाक्यंपरिदृष्टार्थनिश्चयम् । रामःशोकसमाविष्टमित्युवाचविभीषणम् ।।6.112.14।।
explanation: Thus spoke Rama to Vibheeshana, who was overcome with sorrow and speaking with reason, his determined opinion.

shloka_text: नायंविनष्टोनिश्चेष्टस्समरेचण्डविक्रमः । अत्युन्नतमहोत्साहःपतितोऽयमशङ्कितः ।।6.112.15।।
explanation: "This Ravana is not destroyed without power in war. He is of terrible prowess, of extraordinary enthusiasm and fought without any fear and fallen."

shloka_text: नैवंविनष्टाःशोच्यन्तेक्षत्रधर्मव्यवस्थिताः । वृधदिमाशंसमानायेनिपतन्तिरणाजिरे ।।6.112.16।।
explanation: "Those kings who follow duty steadfast, desiring advancement, fearless in the battlefield, who die in that way should not be mourned."

shloka_text: येनसेन्द्रास्त्रयोलोकास्त्रासितायुधिधीमता । तस्मिन्कालसमायुक्ते न कालःपरिशोचितुम् ।।6.112.17।।
explanation: "He who is wise, and the three worlds fear him, including Indra, the Lord of gods, when brought under the sway of death according to timespirit, should not be mourned."

shloka_text: नैकान्तविजयोयुद्धेभूतपूर्वःकदाचन । परैराहन्यतेवीरःपरान्वाहन्तिसंयुगे ।।6.112.18।।
explanation: "Not only that, in war, he will only will be victorious is not true now or before. Hero may kill the enemy or will be killed by the enemy."

shloka_text: इयंहिपूर्वैस्सन्दिष्टागतिःक्षत्रियसम्मता । क्षत्रियोनिहतंसङ्ख्ये न शोच्यइतिनिश्चयः ।।6.112.19।।
explanation: "This course has been practised in the past by ancient kings for those killed in war. Warrior killed in war is not to be mourned', is true."

shloka_text: तदेवंनिश्चयंदृष्टवातत्त्वमास्थायविज्वरः । यदिहानन्तरंकार्यंकल्प्यंतदनुचिन्तय ।।6.112.20।।
explanation: In principle, in that way, decide the action, freed from grief, considering what action is required."

shloka_text: मुक्तवाक्यंविक्रान्तंराजपुत्रंविभीषणः । उवाचशोकसन्तप्तोभ्रातुर्हितमनन्तरम् ।।6.112.21।।
explanation: Having spoken that way by the valiant prince to Vibheeshana, who was immersed in grief, spoke to Rama for the good of his brother.

shloka_text: योऽयंविमर्देष्वविभग्नपूर्वःसुरैस्समस्थेरपिवासवेन । भवन्तमासाद्यरणेविभग्नोवेलामिवासाद्ययथासमुद्रः ।।6.112.22।।
explanation: "He who has not been defeated in battle by even gods or Indra combined together in a trial of strength has been routed by you like the flow of the ocean divides on reaching the shore."

shloka_text: अनेनदत्तानिवनीपकेषुभुक्ताश्चभोगानिभृताश्चभृत्याः । धनानिमित्रेषुसमर्पितानिवैराण्यमित्रेषुनिपातितानि ।।6.112.23।।
explanation: "He bestowed gifts to mendicants, nurtured dependents, filled his friends with wealth, and held grudges against enemies and destroyed them."

shloka_text: एषोहिताग्निश्च:महातपाश्चवेदान्तगःकर्मसुचाग्य्रशूरः । एतस्ययत्प्रेतगतस्यकृत्यंतत्कर्तुमिच्छामितवप्रसादात् ।।6.112.24।।
explanation: "He maintained sacrificial fire and practised austerities. He mastered vedas and was even doing rituals. To the foremost brother's departed soul, I desire your permission to do the rituals."

shloka_text: रावणंनिहतंदृष्टवाराघवेणमहात्मना । अन्तःपुराद्विनिष्पेतूराक्षस्यश्शोककर्शिताः ।।6.113.1।।
explanation: On seeing Ravana killed by the great soul Raghava, the Rakshasas from the gynaeceum stricken with grief rushed out.

shloka_text: वार्यमाणास्सुबहुशोवेष्टन्त्यःक्षितिपांसुषु । विमुक्तकेश्यश्शोकार्तागावोवत्सहतायथा ।।6.113.2।।
explanation: Numerous women, though obstructed, were rolling in dust, with dishevelled hair and crying like cows which had lost their calves.

shloka_text: उत्तरेणविनिष्क्रम्यद्वारेणसहराक्षसैः । प्रविश्यायोधनंघोरंविचिन्वन्त्वोहतंपतिम् ।।6.113.3।। आर्यपुत्रेतिवादिन्योहानाथेति च सर्वशः । परिपेतुःकबन्धाङ्कांमहींशोणितकर्दमाम् ।।6.113.4।।
explanation: The Rakshasa women along with Rakshasas came out of the north gate and entered the battlefield screaming 'O son', 'O husband' and crying, seeing the trunks soaked in blood and mud on the ground and went about all over.

shloka_text: उत्तरेणविनिष्क्रम्यद्वारेणसहराक्षसैः । प्रविश्यायोधनंघोरंविचिन्वन्त्वोहतंपतिम् ।।6.113.3।। आर्यपुत्रेतिवादिन्योहानाथेति च सर्वशः । परिपेतुःकबन्धाङ्कांमहींशोणितकर्दमाम् ।।6.113.4।।
explanation: The Rakshasa women along with Rakshasas came out of the north gate and entered the battlefield screaming 'O son', 'O husband' and crying, seeing the trunks soaked in blood and mud on the ground and went about all over.

shloka_text: ताबाष्पपरिपूर्णाक्ष्योभर्तृशोकपराजिताः । करेण्वइवनर्द्नत्योविनेदुर्हतयूथपाः ।।6.113.5।।
explanation: Bellowing like female elephants that had lost their husbands, the women roared eyes filled with tears on account of grief for their husbands.

shloka_text: ददृशुस्तामहाकायंमहावीर्यंमहाद्युतिम् । रावणंनिहतम्भूमौनीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् ।।6.113.6।।
explanation: They looked at the gigantic body of Ravana of extraordinary valour, full of splendor, killed and lying like a heap of dark mountain on the ground.

shloka_text: ताःपतिंसहसादृष्टवाशयानंरणपांसुषु । निपेतुस्तस्यगात्रेषुछिन्नावनलताइव ।।6.113.7।।
explanation: In the battlefield they saw their husband lying, and precipitately fell on his limbs like broken creepers in a garden.

shloka_text: बहुमानात्परिष्वज्यकाचिदेवंरुरोद ह । चरणौकाचिदालम्ब्यकाचित्कण्ठेऽवलम्ब्य च ।।6.113.8।।
explanation: Indeed, out of respect some embraced him and roared aloud, some held his feet and wept, some held his neck and started weeping.

shloka_text: उत्क्षिप्य च भुजौकाचिद्भूमौसुपरिवर्तते । हतस्यवदनंदृष्टवाकाचिन्मोहमुपागमत् ।।6.113.9।।
explanation: Some lifting their arms threw themselves on ground, some rolled, some beholding the dead Ravana's face became deluded.

shloka_text: काचिदङ्केशिरःकृत्वारुरोदमुखमीक्षती । स्नापयन्तीमुखंबाष्पैस्तुषारैरिवपङ्कजम् ।।6.113.10।।
explanation: One held his head on her lap, and one held his face and looking at it shed tears, like nature covers lotus with dew and roared.

shloka_text: एवमार्ताःपतिंदृष्टवारावणंनिहतंभुवि । चुक्रुशुर्भहुधाशोकाद्भूयस्ताःपर्यदेवयन् ।।6.113.11।।
explanation: Afflicted on beholding their husband Ravana, killed, and lying on the ground, the Rakshasa women again and again cried exceedingly in many ways overcome with grief.

shloka_text: येनमित्रासितःशक्रोयेनवित्रासितोयमः । येनवैश्रवणोराजापुष्पकेणवियोजितः ।।6.113.12।। गन्धर्वाणामृषीणां च सुराणां च महात्मनाम् । भयंयेनरणेदत्तंसोऽयंशेतेरणेहतः ।।6.113.13।।
explanation: "By whom Indra feared, by whom Yama feared, at whom king Visrava feared, by whom Pushpaka was deprived to Kubera in war, by whom Gandharvas and ascetics were afraid of, by whom high souled Suras were afraid of lies in the battlefield asleep."

shloka_text: येनमित्रासितःशक्रोयेनवित्रासितोयमः । येनवैश्रवणोराजापुष्पकेणवियोजितः ।।6.113.12।। गन्धर्वाणामृषीणां च सुराणां च महात्मनाम् । भयंयेनरणेदत्तंसोऽयंशेतेरणेहतः ।।6.113.13।।
explanation: "By whom Indra feared, by whom Yama feared, at whom king Visrava feared, by whom Pushpaka was deprived to Kubera in war, by whom Gandharvas and ascetics were afraid of, by whom high souled Suras were afraid of lies in the battlefield asleep."

shloka_text: असुरेभ्यःसुरेभ्योवापन्नगेभ्योऽपिवातथा । भयंयो न विजानातितस्येदंमानुषाद् भयम् ।।6.113.14।।
explanation: "He, who did not know fear from Asuras or Uragas, experienced fear from a mortal."

shloka_text: अवध्योदेवतानांयस्तथादानवराक्षसाम् । हतःसोऽयंरणेशेतेमानुषेणपदातिना ।।6.113.15।।
explanation: "He, whom Devatas, Danavas and Rakshasas could not kill, lies asleep, killed by a mortal who came by walk."

shloka_text: यो न शक्यस्सुरैर्हन्तुं न यक्षैर्नासुरैस्तथा । सोऽयंकश्चिदिवासत्त्वोमृत्युंमर्त्येनलम्भितः ।।6.113.16।।
explanation: "He, who could not be killed by Suras, Asuras or Yakshas, such a hero lies like a weak person devoid of strength, killed by a mortal, is resting."

shloka_text: एवंवदन्त्योरुरुदुस्तस्यतादुःखिताःस्त्रियः । भूयएव च दुःखार्ताविलेपुश्चपुनःपुनः ।।6.113.17।।
explanation: Those women grieving in that way roared aloud, lamenting again and again cried, afflicted by sorrow.

shloka_text: अशृण्वतातुसुहृदांसततंहितवादिनाम् । मरणायहृतासीताराक्षसाश्चनिपातिताः ।।6.113.18।। एतास्सममिदानींतेवयमात्मा च पातितः ।
explanation: "You did not listen to the good advice of your dear and good at heart. You brought Sita and destroyed yourself and all of us at a time."

shloka_text: ब्रुवाणोऽपिहितंवाक्यमिष्टोभ्राताविभीषणः ।।6.113.19।। धृष्टंपरुषितोमोहत्त्वयात्मवथकाङ्क्षिणा ।
explanation: "Even though good advice was given by your dear brother Vibheeshana, in your delusion evidently you sought your own destruction."

shloka_text: दिनिर्यातितातेस्वासतीतारामायमैथिली ।।6.113.20।। ननस्स्याद्व्यसनंघोरमिदंमूलहरंमहत् ।
explanation: "If Sita, princess of Mithila had been returned by you, this great destruction of the very root and calamity with you and for us would not have happened."

shloka_text: वृत्तकामोभवेद्भ्रातारामोमित्रकुलंभवेत् ।।6.113.21।। वयंचाध्विवाःसर्वाःसकमा न च शत्रवः ।
explanation: "If your brother's desire had been fulfilled Rama would have turned to be our friend. We would not have been widows. Our enemy's desire would not have been fulfilled."

shloka_text: त्वयापुनर्नृशंशंसेनसीतांसंरुन्धताबलात् ।।6.113.22।। राक्षसावयमात्मा च त्रयंतुल्यंनिपातितम् ।
explanation: "With evil intention you kept Sita under detention. These Rakshasas and you and us all the three are together destroyed."

shloka_text: न कामकारःकामंवातवराक्षसपुङ्गव । दैवंचेष्टयतेसर्वंहतंदैवेनहन्यते ।।6.113.23।।
explanation: "O Foremost of Rakshasas! You have acted according to your desire alone is not sufficient as divine will make you do everything. He is killed whom destiny kills."

shloka_text: वानराणांविनाशोऽयंराक्षसानां च तेरणे । तवचैवमहाबाहो दैवयोगादुपागतः ।।6.113.24।।
explanation: "O mighty armed Ravana! For Vanaras, Rakshasas and you too, this destruction in this war has come by divine grace."

shloka_text: नैवार्थेन न कामेनविक्रमेण न चाज्ञया । शक्यादैवगतिर्लोकेनिवर्तयितुमुद्यता ।।6.113.25।।
explanation: "In the world, to change the divine course of action, it is not possible with wealth, or will or by prowess or king's orders."

shloka_text: तासांविलपमानानांतदाराक्षसयोषिताम् । ज्येष्ठापत्नीप्रियाजीनाभर्तारंसमुदैक्षत ।।6.114.1।।
explanation: Then from among the wives lamenting, the first wife, dear to Ravana gazed at her husband lamenting piteously.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवंहतंदृष्टवारामेणाचिन्त्यकर्मणा । पतिंमण्डोदरीतत्रकृपणापर्यदेवयत् ।।6.114.2।।
explanation: Looking at her husband Ravana killed by Rama of inconceivable exploits, Mandodari piteously lamented there.

shloka_text: ननुनाममहाबाहोतववैश्रवणानुज । क्रुद्धस्यप्रमुखेस्थातुंत्रस्यत्यपिपुरन्दरः ।।6.114.3।।
explanation: "O mighty armed Ravana! O, brother of Visrava! When in anger even Purandara was afraid to stand before you, it is well known."

shloka_text: ऋषयश्चमहान्तोऽपिगन्धर्वाश्चयशस्विनः । ननुनामतवोद्वेगाच्चारणाश्चदिशोगताः ।।6.114.4।।
explanation: "For fear of you, even great seers, illustrious Gandharvas, Charanas also went in all directions, is well known."

shloka_text: स त्वंमानुषमात्रेणरामेणयुधिनिर्जितः । न व्यपत्रपसेराजन् किमिदंराक्षसेश्वर ।।6.114.5।।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas! Just by Rama, a mortal, you have been killed in war. Are you not shy of it?"

shloka_text: कथंत्रैलोक्यमाक्रम्यश्रियावीर्येणचान्वितम् । अविषह्यंजघानत्वांमानुषोवनगोचरः ।।6.114.6।।
explanation: "Winning the three worlds by your valour, you are glorious, irresistible and beyond reach. How did the wanderer in the forest strike you?"

shloka_text: मानुषाणामविषयेचरतःकामरूपिणः । विनाशस्तवरामेणसम्युगेनोपपद्यते ।।6.114.7।।
explanation: "You lived in an inaccessible place and are capable of assuming any form at will. It is not believable how you have been destroyed by Rama."

shloka_text: न चैतत्कर्मरामस्यश्रद्धधामिचमूमुखे । सर्वतस्समुपेतस्यतवतेनाभिमर्षणम् ।।6.114.8।।
explanation: "You are always well equipped with the army, so such action (killing you) is not possible for Rama."

shloka_text: यदैव च जनस्थानेराक्षसैर्भहुनिर्ववृतः । खरस्तवहतोभ्रातातदैवासौ न मानुषः ।।6.114.9।।
explanation: " At Janasthana your brother Khara, who was surrounded by many Rakshasas, was killed by a mortal in the same manner."

shloka_text: यदैवनगरींलङ्कांदुष्प्रवेशांसुरैरपि । प्रविष्टोहनुमान्वीर्यात्तदैवव्यथितावयम् ।।6.114.10।।
explanation: "To Lanka, which is inaccessible to anyone, Hanuman entered by increasing his valour. Knowing this we worried (that Rama may not be mere mortal)."

shloka_text: यदैववानरैर्घोरैर्बद्धस्सेतुर्महार्णवे । तदैवहृदयेनाहंशङ्केरामममानुषम् ।।6.114.11।।
explanation: "When these terrific Vanaras constructed a bridge over the great ocean, I doubted in my mind at that time itself that Rama is not a mortal."

shloka_text: अथवारामरूपेणकृतान्तस्स्वयमागतः । मायांतवविनाशायविधायाप्रतितर्किताम् ।।6.114.12।।
explanation: "Or else, the god of death would have come in the form of Rama for your destruction, having right knowledge and taking an inconceivable recourse.

shloka_text: अथवावासवेनत्वंधर्षितोऽपिमहाबल । वासवस्यतुकाशक्तिस्त्वांद्रष्टुमपिसंयुगे ।।6.114.13।।
explanation: "Or else O king of extraordinary might! Indra would have come to overthrow you in the form of Rama. Indra has no energy even to look at you in the battlefield."

shloka_text: व्यक्तमेषमहायोगीपरमात्मासनातनः । अनादिमध्यनिधनोमहतंपरमोमहान् ।।6.114.14।। तमसःपरमोधाताशङ्खचक्रगदाधरः । श्रीवत्सवक्षानित्यश्रीरजय्यश्शाश्वतोध्रुवः ।।6.114.15।। मानुषंरूपमास्थायविष्णुस्सत्यपराक्रमः । सर्वैःपरिवृतोदेवैर्वानरत्वमुपागतैः ।।6.114.16।। सर्वलोकेश्वर्श्रीमान्लोकानांहितकाम्यया । सराक्षसरपरीवारंहतवांस्त्वांमहाद्युतिः ।।6.114.17।।
explanation: "It is evident that this Rama is a great yogi, eternal, who has no beginning, middle or end. He is supreme, greater than great and stands beyond darkness, a sustainer. He holds conch, discus, and mace in hand. He has symbols of Srivatsa on his chest. He is ever rich, invincible, everlasting, steady supreme soul and of truthful valour. He is prosperous, a mass of brilliance, Lord Vishnu and the Lord of all worlds, a wellwisher of all. He has come in mortal form, in the form of Vanaras also, and by all gods. He vanquished you along with Rakshasas is evident."

shloka_text: व्यक्तमेषमहायोगीपरमात्मासनातनः । अनादिमध्यनिधनोमहतंपरमोमहान् ।।6.114.14।। तमसःपरमोधाताशङ्खचक्रगदाधरः । श्रीवत्सवक्षानित्यश्रीरजय्यश्शाश्वतोध्रुवः ।।6.114.15।। मानुषंरूपमास्थायविष्णुस्सत्यपराक्रमः । सर्वैःपरिवृतोदेवैर्वानरत्वमुपागतैः ।।6.114.16।। सर्वलोकेश्वर्श्रीमान्लोकानांहितकाम्यया । सराक्षसरपरीवारंहतवांस्त्वांमहाद्युतिः ।।6.114.17।।

shloka_text: इन्द्रियाणिपुराजित्वाजितंत्रिभुवनंत्वया । स्मरद्भिरिवतद्वैरमिन्द्रियैरेवनिर्जितः ।।6.114.18।।
explanation: "In the past by winning your senses you gained the three worlds. Now it seems as though the senses have recollected and taken their grudge. You have lost control over your senses, thereby you are killed by your enemy."

shloka_text: यदैवहिजनस्थानेराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतः । खरस्तुनिहतोभ्रातातदारामो न मानुषः ।।6.114.19।। यदैवनगरींलङ्कांदुष्प्रवेशांसुरैरपि । प्रविष्टोहनुमान्वीर्यात्तदैवव्यथितावयम् ।।6.114.20।।
explanation: " At Janasthana when your brother Khara was surrounded by many Rakshasas also he got killed by a mortal. So also, when Hanuman entered the city of Lanka, which is difficult to enter even for gods, I got perturbed."

shloka_text: यदैवहिजनस्थानेराक्षसैर्भहुभिर्वृतः । खरस्तुनिहतोभ्रातातदारामो न मानुषः ।।6.114.19।। यदैवनगरींलङ्कांदुष्प्रवेशांसुरैरपि । प्रविष्टोहनुमान्वीर्यात्तदैवव्यथितावयम् ।।6.114.20।।
explanation: " At Janasthana when your brother Khara was surrounded by many Rakshasas also he got killed by a mortal. So also, when Hanuman entered the city of Lanka, which is difficult to enter even for gods, I got perturbed."

shloka_text: क्रियतामविरोधश्चराघवेणेतियन्मया । उच्यमानं न गृह्णासितस्येयंव्युष्टिरागता ।।6.114.21।।
explanation: "You were advised by me not to have any hostile action with Rama. You had not listened to me. This is the result of that action."

shloka_text: अकस्माच्छाभिकामोऽसिसीतांराक्षसपुङ्गवः । ऐश्वर्यस्यविनाशायदेहस्यस्वजनस्य च ।।6.114.22।।
explanation: "O Foremost of Rakshasas! To the destruction of your wealth, life and your own people you suddenly developed passion for Sita."

shloka_text: अरुन्धत्याविशिष्टांतांरोहिण्याश्चापिदुर्मते । सीतांधर्षयतामान्यांत्वयाह्यसदृशंकृतम् ।।6.114.23।।
explanation: "O evil minded king! Sita is to be respected even more than Arundathi or Rohini. Your arrogant action to her is unworthy."

shloka_text: वसुधायाहिवसुधांश्रियःश्रींभर्तृवत्सलाम् । सीतांसर्वानवद्याङ्गीमरण्येविजनेशुभाम् ।।6.114.24।। आनयित्वातुतांदीनांछद्मनात्मस्वदूषण । अप्राप्यतंचैवकामंमैथिलीसङ्गमेकृतम् ।।6.114.25।। पतिव्रतायास्तपसानूनंदग्धोऽसिमेप्रभो ।
explanation: "O king! You dishonoured your wives and me. Sita, who is tolerant as the goddess of earth, prosperous, goddess of fortune, who is fond of her husband, charming in all respects, living alone in the forest, an auspicious one, desperate, was brought in disguise by you. Before you cherished your desire to be in union with Mythili, surely you got burnt by her austerity."

shloka_text: वसुधायाहिवसुधांश्रियःश्रींभर्तृवत्सलाम् । सीतांसर्वानवद्याङ्गीमरण्येविजनेशुभाम् ।।6.114.24।। आनयित्वातुतांदीनांछद्मनात्मस्वदूषण । अप्राप्यतंचैवकामंमैथिलीसङ्गमेकृतम् ।।6.114.25।। पतिव्रतायास्तपसानूनंदग्धोऽसिमेप्रभो ।
explanation: "O king! You dishonoured your wives and me. Sita, who is tolerant as the goddess of earth, prosperous, goddess of fortune, who is fond of her husband, charming in all respects, living alone in the forest, an auspicious one, desperate, was brought in disguise by you. Before you cherished your desire to be in union with Mythili, surely you got burnt by her austerity."

shloka_text: तदैवयन्नदग्धगद्धस्त्वंधर्षयंस्तनुममध्यमाम् । देवाभिभ्यतेतेसर्वेसेन्द्राःसानाग्नीपुरोगमाः ।।6.114.26।।
explanation: "When you touched Sita of slender waist, at that time itself you were not burnt. All gods including Indra headed by fire god are approaching you with hostile intention."

shloka_text: अवश्यमेवलभतेफलंपापस्यकर्मणः । घोरंपर्यागतेकालेकर्तानास्त्यत्रसंशयः ।।6.114.27।।
explanation: "When time comes surely one who does sinful action will reap the result. There is no doubt that the doer of a terrible action will be destroyed."

shloka_text: न कुलेन न रूपेण न दाक्षिण्येनमैथिली । मयाधिकावातुल्यावातत्त्वंमोहान्नबुध्यसे ।।6.114.28।।
explanation: "Mythili by race is not superior to me even a little, not in civility. Out of infatuation you did not perceive this."

shloka_text: सर्वदासर्वभूतानांनास्तिमुत्युरलक्षणः । तवतावदयंमृत्युर्मैथिलीकृतलक्षणः ।।6.114.29।।
explanation: "Death does not happen without reason for any being. To you this happened because of getting Mythili."

shloka_text: सीतानिमित्तजोमृत्युस्त्वयादूरादुपाहृतः । मैथिलीसहरामेणविशोकाविहरिष्यति ।।6.114.30।।
explanation: "On account of abducting Sita, you invited death from a distance. Devoid of sorrow, Sita will sport with Rama."

shloka_text: अल्पपुण्यात्वहंघोरेपतिताशोकसागरे । कैलासेमन्दरेमेरौतथाचैत्ररथेवने ।।6.114.31।। देवोद्यानेषुसर्वेषुविहृत्यसहितात्वया । विमानेनानुरूपेणयायाम्यतुलयाश्रिया ।।6.114.32।। पश्यन्तिविविधान्देशांस्तांस्तांश्चित्रस्रगम्बरा । भ्रम्शिताकामभोगेभ्यःसास्मिवीरवधात्तव ।।6.114.33।। सैवान्येवास्मिसम्वृत्ताधिग्राज्ञांचञ्चलाःश्रियः ।
explanation: "O Hero! Whose stock of merit was less, that you have tumbled down into an ocean of grief. I, having sported with you, clad in picturesque robes and the like, by the aerial car Chaitra ratha on mount Kailasa, Mount Meru and Mandara as well as in divine gardens all over, and various lands with matchless splendour, have been deprived of sensual pleasures because of your falling down. What a pity I am surrounded by ordinary women changed into another woman with fleeting fortunes!"

shloka_text: अल्पपुण्यात्वहंघोरेपतिताशोकसागरे । कैलासेमन्दरेमेरौतथाचैत्ररथेवने ।।6.114.31।। देवोद्यानेषुसर्वेषुविहृत्यसहितात्वया । विमानेनानुरूपेणयायाम्यतुलयाश्रिया ।।6.114.32।। पश्यन्तिविविधान्देशांस्तांस्तांश्चित्रस्रगम्बरा । भ्रम्शिताकामभोगेभ्यःसास्मिवीरवधात्तव ।।6.114.33।। सैवान्येवास्मिसम्वृत्ताधिग्राज्ञांचञ्चलाःश्रियः ।

I, having sported with you, clad in picturesque robes and the like, by the aerial car Chaitra ratha on mount Kailasa, Mount Meru and Mandara as well as in divine gardens all over, and various lands with matchless splendour, have been deprived of sensual pleasures because of your falling down. What a pity I am surrounded by ordinary women changed into another woman with fleeting fortunes!"

shloka_text: हाराजन् सुकुमारंतेसुभ्रुसुत्वक्समुन्नसम् ।।6.114.34।। कान्तिश्रीद्युतिभिस्तुल्यमिन्दुपद्मदिवाकरैः । किरीटकूटोज्ज्वलितंताम्रास्यंदीप्तकुण्डलम् ।।6.114.35।। मदव्याकुललोलाक्षंभूत्वायत्पानभूमिषु । विविधस्रग्धरंचारुवल्गुस्मितकथंशुभम् ।।6.114.36।। तदेवाद्यतवैवंहिवक्त्रं न भ्राजतेप्रभो । रामसायकनिर्भिन्नंरक्तंरुधिरविस्रवैः ।।6.114.37।। वीशीर्णमेदोमस्तिष्कंरूक्षस्यन्दनरेणुभिः ।
explanation: "Oh King, My Lord! Your shiny eyes with delicate eyebrows, which used to be shiny and delicate your prominent nose brilliant skin resembling moon in pleasantness, lotus in beauty, and Sun in radiance your illuminating crown, your shining crown with gems like the peaks of mountains your coppery lips, glowing earrings, rolling eyes were pleasing earlier in the drinking parlours through inebriety, and your auspicious mouth having been indulged in pleasing talk. Today you are pierced by Rama's arrow and shattered with blood flowing, marrow of brain scattered, soiled by dust, dirtied and without any shine."

shloka_text: हापश्चिमामेसम्प्राप्तादशावैधव्यदायिनी ।।6.114.38।। यामयासीन्नसुम्बद्धाकदाचिदपिमन्दया ।
explanation: "Ha! You are dead. I am widowed. I am foolish as I never thought that this stage will come."

shloka_text: पतादानवराजोमेभर्तामेराक्षसेश्वरः ।।6.114.39।। पुत्रोमेशक्रनिर्जेताइत्यहंगर्विताभृशम् ।
explanation: "My father is a king of Danavas, my husband is a Lord of Rakshasas, and my son has won over Indra, the Lord of gods, thus I was excessively proud."

shloka_text: दृप्तामर्दनाःशूराःप्रख्यातबलपौरुषाः ।।6.114.40।। अकुतश्चिद्भयानाथाममेत्यासीन्मतिर्दृढा ।
explanation: "Those who are capable of protecting me are warriors, as they are capable of crushing the enemies and renowned for their pride of their strength. They had no fear from any quarter. I had this conviction in my mind."

shloka_text: तेषामेवंप्रभावाणांयुष्माकंराक्षसर्षभाः ।।6.114.41।। कथंभयमसम्बुद्धंमानुषादिदमागतम् ।
explanation: "O Bull among Rakshasas! You are such a famous king. This fear from a human is unknown. How did it come?"

shloka_text: स्निग्धेन्द्रनीलनीलंतुप्रांशुशैलोपमंमहत् ।।6.114.42।। केयूराङ्गदवैडूर्यमुक्ताहारस्रगुज्ज्वलम् । कान्तंविहारेष्वधिकंदीप्तांसङ्ग्रामभूमिषु ।।6.114.43।। भात्याभरणभाभिर्यद्विद्युद्भिरिवतोयदः । तदेवाद्यशरीरंतेतीक्ष्णैर्नैकशरैश्चितम् ।।6.114.44।। पुनर्दुर्लभसम्पर्शंपरिष्वक्तुं न शक्यते । श्वाविधःशलकैर्यद्वद्भाणैर्लग्नैर्निरन्तरम् ।।6.114.45।। स्वर्पितैर्मर्मसुभृशंसञ्छिन्नस्नायुबन्धनम् । क्षितौनिपतितंराजन् श्यामंवैरुधिरच्छवि ।।6.114.46।। वज्रप्रहाराभिहतोविकीर्णइवपर्वतः ।
explanation: "O king! Your body which is gigantic like a mountain, dark like a sapphire adorned with Keyuras, Angadas, necklaces of cat's eye gems and pearls, which were charming when in the battlefield, and shone brightly on your body with the lustre of your jewels like a rainy cloud with flashes of lightning. It is fixed with numerous arrows cut into pieces by darts and difficult to touch. Since the darts are inserted deep into your vital parts, it is not possible to perform ablution. It is dark, soaked in blood, broken, and crushed like a mountain hit by thunderbolt. Alas, it is not possible to embrace."

shloka_text: हास्वप्नस्सत्यमेवेदंत्वंरामेणकथंहतः ।।6.114.47।। त्वंमृत्योरपिमृत्युस्स्याःकथंमृत्युवशंगत:
explanation: "Ha! Could it be a dream? Is it true? How could you be killed by Rama? You who can kill death also, how did you fall prey to death?"

shloka_text: त्रैलोक्यवसुभोक्तारंत्रैलोक्योद्वेगदंमहत् ।।6.114.48।। जेतारंलोकपालानांक्षेप्तारांशङ्करस्य च ।
explanation: "You are the enjoyer of the treasures of the three worlds, you are the great annoyer of the three worlds and conqueror of the world, and you are the one who lifted up Lord Shanakara's seat."

shloka_text: दृप्तानांनिग्रहीतारमाविष्कृतपराक्रमम् ।।6.114.49।। लोकक्षोभयितारं च नादैर्भूतविराविणम् ।
explanation: "You are a subduer of the arrogant, who manifested prowess, who tormented the world, who made the world cry with insolent words."

shloka_text: ओजसादृप्तवाक्यानांवक्तारंरिपुसन्निधौ ।।6.114.50।। स्वयूथभृत्यगोप्तारंहन्तारंभीमकर्मणाम् ।
explanation: "He, who commanded uttering harsh words in the presence of the enemy, who protected his own brand, who killed those indulged in terrible deeds.

shloka_text: हन्तारंदानवेन्द्राणांयक्षाणां च सहस्रशः ।।6.114.51।। निवातकवचानां च सङ्ग्रहीतारमाहवे ।
explanation: "He who killed thousands of chiefs of Danavas, Yakshas, and subdued Nivatakavachas in combat"

shloka_text: नैकयज्ञविलोप्तारंत्रातारंस्वजनस्य च ।।6.114.52।। धर्मव्यवस्थाभेत्तारंमायास्रष्टारमाहवे ।
explanation: "He, who obstructed performance of sacrificial rituals, protected his own people, who violated code of conduct in comb at by using conjuring tricks"

shloka_text: देवासुरनृकन्यानामाहर्तारंततस्ततः ।।6.114.53।। शत्रुस्त्रीशोकदातारं नेतारं स्वजनस्य च ।
explanation: "Brought by force virgin girls of Devas, suras and human beings from here and there forcibly and caused the enemy women to mourn"

shloka_text: लङ्काद्वीपस्यगोप्तारंकर्तारंभीमकर्मणाम् ।।6.114.54।। अस्माकंकामभोगानांदातारंरथिनांवरम् ।
explanation: "In the island of Lanka, he provided for his own sexual pleasures in a concealing manner. He was the foremost among those providers of sensual pleasures."

shloka_text: एवंप्रभावंभर्तारंदृष्टवारामेणपातितम् ।।6.114.55।। स्थिरास्मियादेहमिमंधारयामिहतप्रिया ।
explanation: "Such a husband of mine endowed with this kind of influence, killed by Rama, is lying here. Beholding the lover gone, I am holding this body and standing here."

shloka_text: शयनेषुमहार्हेषुशयित्वाराक्षसेश्वर ।।6.114.56।। इहकर्मात्प्रसुप्तोऽसिधरण्यांरेणुगुण्ठितः ।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas! Having slept on the best of beds, you are now lying here on the hard ground, body covered with dust. Where are you sleeping?"

shloka_text: यदातेतनयश्शस्तोलक्ष्मणेनेन्द्रजिद्युधि ।।6.114.57।। तदात्वभिहतातीव्रमद्यत्वस्मिनिपातिता ।
explanation: "When my son Indrajith was killed by Lakshmana I was in intense grief. Now you have fallen."

shloka_text: साहंबन्धुजनैर्हीनाहीनानाथेन च त्वया ।।6.114.58।। विहीनाकामभोगैश्चशोचिष्येशाश्वतीस्समाः ।
explanation: "Disconnected with relatives, forsaken by you also, deprived of sensual pleasures, I shall grieve permanently."

shloka_text: प्रपन्नोदीर्घमध्वानंराजन्नद्यसुदुर्गमम् ।।6.114.59।। नयमामपिदुःखार्तां न वर्तिष्येत्वयाविना ।
explanation: "O king! Today, take me on your journey which is very difficult. Stricken with sorrow I cannot live without you."

shloka_text: कस्मात्त्वंमांविहायेहकृपणांगन्तुमिच्छसि ।।6.114.60।। दीनांविलपतींमन्दांकिंवामांनाभिभाषसे ।
explanation: "You are leaving me, a desperate one, stricken, crying. Why are you desiring to go? Why are you not replying to me?"

shloka_text: दृष्टवा न खल्वभिक्रुद्धोमामिहानवकुण्ठिताम् ।।6.114.61।। निर्गतांनगरद्वारात्पद्भ्यामेवागतांप्रभो ।
explanation: "Lord! How is it that you are not angry seeing me coming forth walking through the city gate?"

shloka_text: पश्येष्टदारदारांस्तेभ्रष्टलज्जावकुण्ठितान् ।।6.114.62।। बहिर्निष्पतितान्सर्वान्कथंदृष्टवा न कुप्यसि ।
explanation: "O lover of wives! Your wives have come out leaving their veils from their abode to see you. See them, and how is it that you are not angry?"

shloka_text: अयंक्रीडासहायस्तेऽनाथेलालप्यतेजनः ।।6.114.63।। न चैवमाश्वासयसिकिंवा न बहुमन्यसे ।
explanation: "These people who were with you are always sporting my Lord. Why do you not call them, why are you not consoling them, or inviting them?"

shloka_text: याःस्त्वयाविधवाराजन्कृतानैकाःकुलस्त्रियः ।।6.114.64।। पतिव्रताधर्मरतागुरुशुश्रूषणेरताः । ताभिश्शोकाभितप्ताभिश्शप्तःपरवशंगतः ।।6.114.65।। त्वयाविप्रकृताभिर्यत्तदाशप्तंतदागतम् ।
explanation: "King! Chaste women of noble lineage being righteous, serving the elders have been widowed by you. Because of their curse, you have fallen under the sway of your enemy and because of that, this has come to you."

shloka_text: याःस्त्वयाविधवाराजन्कृतानैकाःकुलस्त्रियः ।।6.114.64।। पतिव्रताधर्मरतागुरुशुश्रूषणेरताः । ताभिश्शोकाभितप्ताभिश्शप्तःपरवशंगतः ।।6.114.65।। त्वयाविप्रकृताभिर्यत्तदाशप्तंतदागतम् ।
explanation: "King! Chaste women of noble lineage being righteous, serving the elders have been widowed by you. Because of their curse, you have fallen under the sway of your enemy and because of that, this has come to you."

shloka_text: प्रवादस्सत्यएवायंत्वांप्रतिप्रायशोनृप ।।6.114.66।। प्रतिव्रतानांनाकस्मात्सपत्नत्यश्रूणिभूतले ।
explanation: "King! 'The tears of noble women should not fall on the earth's surface' is a popular saying. This calamity is truly a result to you in return."

shloka_text: कथं च नामतेराजन् लोकानाक्रम्यतेजसा ।।6.114.67।। नारीचौर्यमिदंक्षुद्रंकृतंशौण्डीर्यमानिना ।
explanation: "King! You have invaded the world by your brilliance and were proud of your heroism. How did you do this mean act of abducting a woman?"

shloka_text: अपनीयाश्रमाद्रामंयन्मृगच्छद्मनात्वया ।।6.114.68।। आनीतारामपनतीसातत्तेकातर्यलक्षणम् ।
explanation: "By your cowardly action of creating an illusory deer, you have brought Rama's consort from the hermitage."

shloka_text: कातर्यं न च तेयुद्धेकदाचित्संस्मराम्यहम् ।।6.114.69।। तत्तुभाग्यविपर्यासान्नूनंतेपक्वलक्षणम् ।
explanation: "Indeed, I do not remember you being cowardly in war. The timidness that appeared in you is a sign of the adverseness of fate, for your destruction."

shloka_text: अतीतानागतार्थज्ञोवर्तमानविचक्षणः ।।6.114.70।। मैथिलीमाहृतांदृष्टवाध्यात्वानिःश्वस्यचायतम् । सत्यवाक्यमहाबाहो देवरोमेयदब्रवीत् ।।6.114.71।। अयंराक्षसमुख्यानांविनाशःपर्युपस्थितः । कामक्रोधसमुत्थेनव्यसनेनप्रसङ्गिना ।।6.114.72।।
explanation: "Mighty armed King! Your brother, who is a knower of matters relating to future, present and past, a truthful one, after your getting Mythili, thought for a while and sighing spoke this. 'The destruction of Rakshasa chiefs is now sure to happen', has come true.' The desire for sensual pleasures and anger has resulted in your death and resulting in this calamity."

shloka_text: अतीतानागतार्थज्ञोवर्तमानविचक्षणः ।।6.114.70।। मैथिलीमाहृतांदृष्टवाध्यात्वानिःश्वस्यचायतम् । सत्यवाक्यमहाबाहो देवरोमेयदब्रवीत् ।।6.114.71।। अयंराक्षसमुख्यानांविनाशःपर्युपस्थितः । कामक्रोधसमुत्थेनव्यसनेनप्रसङ्गिना ।।6.114.72।।
explanation: "Mighty armed King! Your brother, who is a knower of matters relating to future, present and past, a truthful one, after your getting Mythili, thought for a while and sighing spoke this. 'The destruction of Rakshasa chiefs is now sure to happen', has come true.' The desire for sensual pleasures and anger has resulted in your death and resulting in this calamity."

shloka_text: अतीतानागतार्थज्ञोवर्तमानविचक्षणः ।।6.114.70।। मैथिलीमाहृतांदृष्टवाध्यात्वानिःश्वस्यचायतम् । सत्यवाक्यमहाबाहो देवरोमेयदब्रवीत् ।।6.114.71।। अयंराक्षसमुख्यानांविनाशःपर्युपस्थितः । कामक्रोधसमुत्थेनव्यसनेनप्रसङ्गिना ।।6.114.72।।
explanation: "Mighty armed King! Your brother, who is a knower of matters relating to future, present and past, a truthful one, after your getting Mythili, thought for a while and sighing spoke this. 'The destruction of Rakshasa chiefs is now sure to happen', has come true.' The desire for sensual pleasures and anger has resulted in your death and resulting in this calamity."

shloka_text: निर्वृत्तस्त्वत्कृतेऽनर्थःसोऽयंमूलहरोमहान् । त्वयाकृतमिदंसर्वमनाधंराक्षसंकुलम् ।।6.114.73।।
explanation: "By this major disaster of yours, the very root has been destroyed. With the extermination of the Rakshasas, the entire Rakshasa clan is orphaned now by your action."

shloka_text: हित्वंशोचितव्योमेप्रख्यातबलपौरुषः । स्त्रीस्वभावात्तुमेबुद्धिःकारुण्येपरिवर्तते ।।6.114.74।।
explanation: "You are famous for your strength and courage. I do not need to wail for you. Being a woman, by nature I am compassionate, and my mind is moving towards sorrow."

shloka_text: सुकृतंदुष्कृतं च त्वंगृहीत्वास्वांगतिंगतः । आत्मानमनुशोचामित्वद्विनाशेनदुःखिताम् ।।6.114.75।।
explanation: "You have taken away the good and evil deeds done by your death. I'm thinking of myself and wailing."

shloka_text: सुहृदांहितकामानां न श्रुतंवचनंत्वया । भ्रात्रूणांचैवकार्त्न्सनहितमुक्तंदशानन ।।6.114.76।।
explanation: "O Ten headed king! You did not heed the good words of advice given by your friends. You did not totally heed the good words spoken by your brothers."

shloka_text: हेत्वर्थयुक्तंविधिवच्छ्रेयस्करमदारुणम् । विभीषणेनाभिहितं न कृतंहेतुमत्त्वया ।।6.114.77।।
explanation: "You have not listened to the meaningful, agreeable and reasonable advice given according to tradition by Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: मारीचकुम्भकर्णाभ्यांवाक्यंममपितुस्तथा । न श्रुतंवीर्यमत्तेनतस्येदंफलमीदृशम् ।।6.114.78।।
explanation: "You did not take the advice of both Maricha and Kumbhakarna. You have also not taken the advice of my father because of the pride of your valour. This kind of result is the consequence of that."

shloka_text: नीलजीमूतसङ्काश पीताम्बरशुभाङ्गद । स्वगात्राणिविनिक्षिप्यकिंशेषेरुधिराप्लुतः ।।6.114.79।।
explanation: "Resembling a dark cloud clad in yellow silk, why are you lying like this with limbs thrown down and body covered with blood?"

shloka_text: प्रसुप्तइवशोकार्तांकिंमां न प्रतिभाषसे । महावीर्यस्यदक्षस्यसम्युगेष्वपलायिनः ।।6.114.80।। यातुधानस्यदौहित्रींकिंमां न प्रतिभाषसे ।
explanation: "You are sleeping like this while I am stricken with grief. Why are you not replying to me? I am the granddaughter of Malyavantha, a great hero who fought with Daksha. Why are you disowning me and not answering me?"

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठकिंशेषेनवेपरिभवेकृते ।।6.114.81।। अद्यवैनिर्भयालङ्कांप्रविष्टांसूर्यरश्मयः ।
explanation: "Get up, Rise up. When you are insulted why are you lying down? Because you are lying down, even the radiance of the Sun has entered Lanka without fear."

shloka_text: येनसूदयसेशत्रून् समरेसूर्यवर्चसा ।।6.114.82।। वज्रंवज्रधरस्येवसोऽयंतेसततार्चितः । रणेबहुप्रहरणोहेमजापरिष्कृतः ।।6.114.83।। परिघोव्यवकीर्णस्तेबाणैश्चिन्नैःसहस्रधा ।
explanation: "The iron bar of yours which is effulgent like the Sun and closely resembles the thunderbolt of Indra, with which you have terminated your enemies in the combat, which is regularly worshipped by you, which is adorned with a network of gold, is broken into thousand pieces and lies scattered."

shloka_text: येनसूदयसेशत्रून् समरेसूर्यवर्चसा ।।6.114.82।। वज्रंवज्रधरस्येवसोऽयंतेसततार्चितः । रणेबहुप्रहरणोहेमजापरिष्कृतः ।।6.114.83।। परिघोव्यवकीर्णस्तेबाणैश्चिन्नैःसहस्रधा ।
explanation: "The iron bar of yours which is effulgent like the Sun and closely resembles the thunderbolt of Indra, with which you have terminated your enemies in the combat, which is regularly worshipped by you, which is adorned with a network of gold, is broken into thousand pieces and lies scattered."

shloka_text: अप्रियामिवोपसंगृह्यकिंशेषेरणमेदिनीम् ।।6.114.84।। अप्रियामिवकस्माच्छमांनेच्छस्यभिभाषितुम् ।
explanation: "You are lying in the battlefield embracing it as if it is a loved one. Why are you not willing to answer me?"

shloka_text: धिगस्तुहृदयंयस्याममेदं न सहस्रधा ।।6.114.85।। त्वयिपञ्चत्वमापन्नेफलतेशोकपीडितम् ।
explanation: "You have returned to the five elements. This heart of mine distressed with grief is not breaking into a thousand pieces."

shloka_text: इत्येवंविलपन्तिसाबाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा ।।6.114.86।। स्नेहोपस्कन्नहृदया तदा मोहामुपागमत् ।
explanation: Wailing in this way, eyes filled with tears, heart filled with extreme love, (Mandodari) she was in delusion.

shloka_text: कश्मलाभिहतासन्नाबभौसारावणोरसि ।।6.114.87।। स्नध्यानुरक्तेजलदेदीप्ताविद्युदिवोज्ज्वला ।
explanation: In a state of unconsciousness, when Mandodari, fell on Ravana's chest, shrunk in agony, she was like a flash of lightning glowing in a rainy cloud reddened by the blow of twilight.

shloka_text: तथागतंसमुत्थाप्यसपत्नयस्तांभृशातुराः ।।6.114.88।। पर्यवस्थापयामासूरुदन्त्योरुदतींभृशम् ।
explanation: The cowives who had come there weeping aloud and distressed, lifted up roaring Mandodari quickly.

shloka_text: न तेसुविदितादेविलोकानांस्थितिरध्रुवा ।।6.114.89।। दशाविभागपर्यायेराज्ञांवैचञ्चलाःश्रियः ।
explanation: "Devi! Not that you do not know that when fortune changes in the world, dynasty changes. Fortune is not steady."

shloka_text: इत्येवमुच्यमानासासशब्दंप्ररुरोद ह ।।6.114.90।। स्नापयन्तीतदास्रेणस्तनौवक्रंसुनिर्मलम् ।
explanation: While Mandodari was being counselled by the co wives like this, she was weeping, shedding tears on her breast as well as bathing her face. She once again wept making a loud sound.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरेरामोविभीषणमुवाच ह ।।6.114.91।। संस्कारःक्रियतांभ्रातुःस्त्रीगणःपरिसान्त्व्यताम् ।
explanation: Thereafter, Rama spoke to Vibheeshana like this." Let the obsequies be carried out and all the women comforted."

shloka_text: तमुवाचततोधीमान् विभीषणइदंवचः ।।6.114.92।। विमृश्यबुद्ध्याधर्मज्ञोधर्मार्थसहितंहितम् ।
explanation: Then  the wise and righteous Vibheeshana thinking made a wholesome and righteous submission in the following words.

shloka_text: त्यक्तधर्मव्रतंशूरंनृशंसमनृतंतथा ।।6.114.93।। नाहमर्होऽस्मिसंस्कर्तुंपरदाराभिमर्शिनम् ।
explanation: "This Ravana had given up righteous conduct, was cruel, merciless, untrue, and had laid hands on others' wives. I do not deserve to perform obsequies to him.

shloka_text: भ्रातृरूपःहिमेशत्रुरेषसर्वाहितेरतः ।।6.114.94।। रावणोनार्हतेपूजांपूज्योऽपिगुरुगौरवात् ।
explanation: "This Ravana remained doing harm to all and does not deserve the respect of his elder brother, or prayers. He is an enemy in the form of brother. He does not deserve to be worshipped.

shloka_text: नृशंसइतिमांराम वक्ष्यन्तिमनुजाभुवि ।।6.114.95।। श्रुत्वातस्यागुणान्सर्वेवक्ष्यन्तिसुकृतंपुनः ।
explanation: "If I am not performing obsequies to my elder brother, the people in this world will call me ruthless. Again, on hearing his blemishes they will say that it is good not to do it for him."

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वापरमप्रीतोरामोधर्मभृतांवरः ।।6.114.96।। विभीषणमुवाचेदंवाक्यज्ञंवाक्यकोविदः ।
explanation: On hearing Vibheeshana's words, Rama, who is good at expression, very affectionately, upholding virtues, spoke as follows to Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: तवापिमेप्रियंकार्यंत्वत्प्रभावान्मयाजितम् ।।6.114.97।। अवश्यंतुक्षमंवाच्योमयात्वांराक्षसेश्वर ।
explanation: "O Lord of Rakshasas! You are dear to me. It is by your strength I could be victorious. I have to do some kind deed for you.

shloka_text: अधर्मानृतसंयुक्तःकामंत्वेषनिशाचरः ।।6.114.98।। तेजस्वीबलवान् शूरःसङ्ग्रामेषु च नित्यशः ।
explanation: "This nightranger is full of unrighteousness and untrue. But he was a strong, energetic hero in combat."

shloka_text: शतक्रतुमुखैर्वीरैःश्रूयते न पराजितः ।।6.114.99।। महात्माबलसम्पन्नोरावणोलोकरावणः ।
explanation: "Though he is richly endowed with prowess, he is a tyranny to the world, who has performed a hundred sacrifices (like Indra) and never got defeated, I heard."

shloka_text: मरणानान्तिवैराणिनिर्वृत्तंनःप्रयोजनम् ।।6.114.100।। क्रियतामस्यसंस्कारोममाप्येषयथातव ।
explanation: "There is no hostility after death for heroes. Let us perform his obsequies. I am also like that in this regard.

shloka_text: त्वत्सत्सकाशाद्धशग्रीवस्संस्कारंविधिपूर्वकम् ।।6.114.101।। क्षिप्रमर्हतिधर्मेणत्वंयशोभाग्भविष्यसि ।
explanation: "Ten headed Ravana being so (knower of righteousness), he deserves your performance of his last rites as per tradition and righteously You will attain fame by doing this deed."

shloka_text: राघवस्यवच्श्रुत्वात्वरमाणोविभीषण: ।।6.114.102।। संस्कारयितुमारेभेभ्रातरंरावणंहतम् ।
explanation: On hearing Raghava's words, Vibheeshana hastened to perform the last rites of his brother Ravana who had been killed.

shloka_text: सप्रविश्यपुरींलङ्कांराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.114.103।। रावणस्याअग्निहोत्रंतुनिर्यापयतिसत्वरम् ।
explanation: Vibheeshana entered the city of Lanka and carried out fire sacrifice quickly for Ravana, the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: शकटान् दारुरूपाणिअग्नीनवैयाजकांस्तथा ।।6.114.104।। तथाचन्दनकाष्ठानिकाष्ठानिविविधानि च । अगरूणिसुगधनीनिगन्धांश्चसुरभींस्तथा ।।6.114.105।। मणिमुक्ताप्रवाळानिनिर्यापयतिराक्षसः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana arranged to get excellent carts, fires maintained by Ravana, priests, so also sandalwood, and many kinds of wood, fragrant perfumes, sandals, sweet smelling odours, gems, pearls, and corals and proceeded with obsequies.

shloka_text: शकटान् दारुरूपाणिअग्नीनवैयाजकांस्तथा ।।6.114.104।। तथाचन्दनकाष्ठानिकाष्ठानिविविधानि च । अगरूणिसुगधनीनिगन्धांश्चसुरभींस्तथा ।।6.114.105।। मणिमुक्ताप्रवाळानिनिर्यापयतिराक्षसः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana arranged to get excellent carts, fires maintained by Ravana, priests, so also sandalwood, and many kinds of wood, fragrant perfumes, sandals, sweet smelling odours, gems, pearls, and corals and proceeded with obsequies.

shloka_text: आजगाममुहूर्तेनराक्षसैःपरिवारितः ।।6.114.106।। ततोमाल्यवतासार्थंक्रियामेवचकारसः ।
explanation: Surrounded by Rakshasas, in a short time he returned with Malyavan (Maternal uncle of Ravana) and Vibheeshana initiated the task.

shloka_text: सौवर्णींशिबिकांदिव्यामारोप्यक्षौमवासनम् ।।6.114.107।। रावणंराक्षसाधीशमश्रुपूर्यमुखाद्विजाः । तूर्यघोषैश्चविविधैस्स्तुवद्भिश्चाभिनन्दितम् ।।6.114.108।। प्ताकाभिश्चचित्राभिस्सुमनोभिश्चचित्रिताम् । उत्क्षिप्यशिबिकांतांतुविभीषणपुरोगमाः ।।6.114.109।। दक्षिणाभिमुखास्सर्वेगृह्यकाष्ठानिभेजिरे ।
explanation: As the dead body of Ravana was lifted up for final beatitude, panegyrists hailed him with blasts of several musical instruments and praised him with their faces bathed in tears. The golden cart was decorated with beautiful, picturesque, wonderful pictures and flags. Logs of wood were placed on the body and consecrated by sprinkling fragrant water. With Vibheeshana in the forefront, faces turned to the southern side, all proceeded.

shloka_text: सौवर्णींशिबिकांदिव्यामारोप्यक्षौमवासनम् ।।6.114.107।। रावणंराक्षसाधीशमश्रुपूर्यमुखाद्विजाः । तूर्यघोषैश्चविविधैस्स्तुवद्भिश्चाभिनन्दितम् ।।6.114.108।। प्ताकाभिश्चचित्राभिस्सुमनोभिश्चचित्रिताम् । उत्क्षिप्यशिबिकांतांतुविभीषणपुरोगमाः ।।6.114.109।। दक्षिणाभिमुखास्सर्वेगृह्यकाष्ठानिभेजिरे ।

shloka_text: अग्नयोदीप्यमानास्तेतदाध्वर्युसमीरिताः ।।6.114.110।। शरणाभिगताःसर्वेपुरस्तात्तस्यतेययुः ।
explanation: Then Advarya lighted the fires that started glowing up. All the ogres paid their respects seeking refuge and followed.

shloka_text: अन्तःपुराणिसर्वाणिरुदमानानिसत्वरम् ।।6.114.111।। पृष्ठतोऽनुययुस्तानिप्लवमानानिसर्वतः ।
explanation: All the women from the gynaeceum weeping aloud from all sides hastened at quick paces and followed sobbing.

shloka_text: रावणंप्रयतेदेशेस्थाप्यतेभृशदुःखिताः ।।6.114.112।। चितांचन्दनकाष्ठैश्चपद्मकोशीसंवृताम् । ब्राह्म्यासम्वर्तयामासूराङ्कवास्तरणावृताम् ।।6.114.113।। वर्ततेवेदविहितोराज्ञोवैपश्चिमःक्रतुः ।
explanation: As they advanced forth with Ravana's body, they placed it in a consecrated place. All were highly afflicted with grief. Logs of sandal wood, blocks of Padmaka wood and finally fragrant root of Usira plant, and Brahmya grass were placed on the body. It was covered with the skin of antelope. The last rites of the king were carried out with vedic rites.

shloka_text: रावणंप्रयतेदेशेस्थाप्यतेभृशदुःखिताः ।।6.114.112।। चितांचन्दनकाष्ठैश्चपद्मकोशीसंवृताम् । ब्राह्म्यासम्वर्तयामासूराङ्कवास्तरणावृताम् ।।6.114.113।। वर्ततेवेदविहितोराज्ञोवैपश्चिमःक्रतुः ।
explanation: As they advanced forth with Ravana's body, they placed it in a consecrated place. All were highly afflicted with grief. Logs of sandal wood, blocks of Padmaka wood and finally fragrant root of Usira plant, and Brahmya grass were placed on the body. It was covered with the skin of antelope. shloka_text: प्रचक्रुःराक्षसेन्द्रस्यपितृमेधमनुक्रमम् ।।6.114.114।। वेदिं च दक्षिणप्राच्यांयथास्थानं च पावकम् ।
explanation: Then proceeding in sequence constructing an altar in the southeast and placing sacrificial fire in a proper place, they duly performed in honour of the ruler of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: पृषदाज्येनसम्पूर्णंस्रुवंसर्वेप्रचिक्षिपुः ।।6.114.115।। पादयोश्शकटंप्रादुरन्तरूर्वोरुलूखलंतदा ।
explanation: Then they poured a ladle full of ghee mixed with curd on his shoulders and placed a cart on his feet and a wooden mortar on his thighs.

shloka_text: दारुपात्राणिसर्वाणिआरणिंचोत्तारारणिम् ।।6.114.116।। दत्त्वातुमुसलंचान्यथास्थानंविचक्षणा: ।
explanation: The learned having placed everything including wooden vessels, wooden ladle to kindle fire, wooden pestle, spoon, and all other requirements at the right place.

shloka_text: शास्त्रादृष्टेनविधिनामहर्षिविहितेन च ।।6.114.117।। तत्रमेध्यंपशुंहत्वाराक्षसेन्द्रस्यराक्षसाः । परिस्तरणिकांराज्ञोघृताक्तांसमवेशयन् ।।6.114.118।।
explanation: Thereafter according to tradition laid down in sastras by great Rsis, the ogres killed a cow and spread a sheet, daubed it with ghee and spread it on the body of the king of Rakshasa.

shloka_text: शास्त्रादृष्टेनविधिनामहर्षिविहितेन च ।।6.114.117।। तत्रमेध्यंपशुंहत्वाराक्षसेन्द्रस्यराक्षसाः । परिस्तरणिकांराज्ञोघृताक्तांसमवेशयन् ।।6.114.118।।
explanation: Thereafter according to tradition laid down in sastras by great Rsis, the ogres killed a cow and spread a sheet, daubed it with ghee and spread it on the body of the king of Rakshasa.

shloka_text: गन्धैर्माल्यैरलङ्कृत्यरावणंदीनमानसाः ।।6.114.119।। विभीषणसहायास्तेवस्त्रैश्चविविधैरपि । लाजैरश्चावकिरन्तिस्मबाष्पपूर्णमुखास्तदा ।।6.114.120।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas along with Vibheeshana desperately, eyes dimmed with tears, covered Ravana with several clothes and decorated with garland s and sandal. They sprinkled parched grain.

shloka_text: गन्धैर्माल्यैरलङ्कृत्यरावणंदीनमानसाः ।।6.114.119।। विभीषणसहायास्तेवस्त्रैश्चविविधैरपि । लाजैरश्चावकिरन्तिस्मबाष्पपूर्णमुखास्तदा ।।6.114.120।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasas along with Vibheeshana desperately, eyes dimmed with tears, covered Ravana with several clothes and decorated with garland s and sandal. They sprinkled parched grain.

shloka_text: ददौ च पावकंतस्यविधियुक्तंविभीषणः । स्नात्वाचैवार्द्रवस्त्रेणतिलान्दूर्वाभिमिश्रितान् ।।6.114.121।। उदकेन च सम्मिश्रान्प्रदायविधिपूर्वकम् । प्रदायचोदकंतस्मैमूर्ध्नाचैनंनमस्य च ।।6.114.122।। ताःस्त्रियोऽनुनयामाससान्तमुक्त्वापुनःपुनः । गम्यतामितितास्सर्वाविविशुर्नगरीतदा ।।6.114.123।।
explanation: In accordance with tradition, Vibheeshana set fire. He bathed himself and with wet clothes offered in a wet cloth, holding kusa grass a mixture of sesame seeds and water to Ravana. He prostrated to Ravana and offered his prayers with folded palms. Then he comforted the wives of Ravana and all of them to return to Lanka.

shloka_text: ददौ च पावकंतस्यविधियुक्तंविभीषणः । स्नात्वाचैवार्द्रवस्त्रेणतिलान्दूर्वाभिमिश्रितान् ।।6.114.121।। उदकेन च सम्मिश्रान्प्रदायविधिपूर्वकम् । प्रदायचोदकंतस्मैमूर्ध्नाचैनंनमस्य च ।।6.114.122।। ताःस्त्रियोऽनुनयामाससान्तमुक्त्वापुनःपुनः । गम्यतामितितास्सर्वाविविशुर्नगरीतदा ।।6.114.123।।

He prostrated to Ravana and offered his prayers with folded palms. Then he comforted the wives of Ravana and all of them to return to Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टासुसर्वासुराक्षसीषुविभीषणः । रामपार्श्वमुपागम्यतदातिष्ठद्विनीतवत् ।।6.114.124।।
explanation: After the women entering the city, Vibheeshana came towards Rama and stood in a submissive manner.

shloka_text: रामोऽपिसहसैन्येनससुग्रीवस्सलक्ष्मणः । हर्षंलेभेरिपुंहत्वायथावृत्रंशतक्रतु: ।।6.114.125।।
explanation: Enemy killed, Rama also accompanied by Sugriva, Lakshmana, and army experienced joy, like Indra (who performed a hundred sacrifices) after killing Vrta.

shloka_text: तेरावणवधंदृष्टवादेवगन्धर्वदानवाः । जग्मुस्स्वैस्वैर्विमानैस्तेकथयन्तश्शुभाःकथाः ।।6.115.1।।
explanation: In the meantime, Devas, Gandharvas, Danavas speaking to each other an auspicious story of Ravana's destruction went in their respective aerial cars.

shloka_text: रावणस्यवधंघोरंराघवस्यपराक्रमम् । सुयुद्धंवानराणां च सुग्रीवस्य च मन्त्रितम् ।।6.115.2।। अनुरागं च वीर्यं च सौमित्रेर्लक्ष्मणस्य च । पतिव्रतात्वंसीतायाहनूमतिपराक्रमम् ।।6.115.3।। कथयन्तोमहाभागाजग्मुर्हष्टायथागतम् ।
explanation: Speaking about the highly respected Raghava's prowess, the end of dreadful Ravana, the good fighting of Vanaras, counsel of Sugriva, valour of Hanuman, love of Lakshmana, fidelity of Sita, all rejoiced and returned as they had come.

shloka_text: रावणस्यवधंघोरंराघवस्यपराक्रमम् । सुयुद्धंवानराणां च सुग्रीवस्य च मन्त्रितम् ।।6.115.2।। अनुरागं च वीर्यं च सौमित्रेर्लक्ष्मणस्य च । पतिव्रतात्वंसीतायाहनूमतिपराक्रमम् ।।6.115.3।। कथयन्तोमहाभागाजग्मुर्हष्टायथागतम् ।
explanation: Speaking about the highly respected Raghava's prowess, the end of dreadful Ravana, the good fighting of Vanaras, counsel of Sugriva, valour of Hanuman, love of Lakshmana, fidelity of Sita, all rejoiced and returned as they had come.

shloka_text: राघवस्तुरथंदिव्यमिन्द्रदत्तंशिखिप्रभम् ।।6.115.4।। अनुज्ञायमहाभागोर्मातलिंप्रत्यपूजयत् ।
explanation: Bidding farewell to Matali joyously, honourable Raghava returned the aerial chariot bestowed to him by Indra.

shloka_text: राघवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातोमातलिश्शक्रसारथिः ।।6.115.5।। दिव्यंतंरथमास्थायदिवमेवारूरोहसह ।
explanation: Matali, charioteer of Indra too taking Raghava's permission went to heaven in that wonderful chariot.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तुदिवमारूढेसुसारथिसन्तमे ।।6.115.6।। राघवःपरमप्रीतस्सुग्रीवंपरिषस्वजे ।
explanation: "On Matali ascending to heaven, Raghava very dearly embraced Sugriva for his help in his victory."

shloka_text: परिष्वज्य च सुग्रीवंलक्ष्मणेनाभिवादितः ।।6.115.7।। पूज्यमानोहरिगणैराजगामबलालयम् ।
explanation: On embracing Sugriva, greeted by Lakshmana, and worshipped by the army of Vanaras, Rama returned to the camp.

shloka_text: अथोवाच स काकुत्स्थस्समीपपरिवर्तिनम् ।।6.115.8।। सौमित्रिंसत्त्वसम्पन्नंलक्ष्मणंशुभलक्षणम् ।
explanation: And then, Kakuthsa spoke to Saumithri, of auspicious nature and endowed richly with prowess, who stood close by.

shloka_text: भीषणमिमंसौम्य लङ्कायामभिषेचय ।।6.115.9।। अनुरक्तं च भक्तं च तथापूर्वोपकारिणम् ।
explanation: "Gentle Lakshmana! Vibheeshana is friendly to me and devoted. He has done me good work in the past. Consecrate him in Lanka."

shloka_text: एषमेपरमःकामोयदिमंरावणानुजम् ।।6.115.10।। लङ्कायांसौम्य पश्येमभिषिक्तंविभीषणम् ।
explanation: "O gentle Lakshmana! I desire to see this Vibheeshana, Ravana's brother, consecrated at Lanka"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुसौमित्रीराघवेणमहात्मना ।।6.115.11।। तथेत्युक्त्वासुसम्हृष्टःसौवर्णंघटमाददे ।
explanation: Great selfRaghava having spoken like that, Saumithri, very happily arranged to get a golden vessel.

shloka_text: तम्घटंवानरेन्द्राणांहस्तेदत्त्वामनोजवान् ।।6.115.12।। व्यादिदेशमहासत्त्व: समुद्रसलिलंतदा ।
explanation: Commanded like that, Lakshmana, endowed with mighty prowess placed that vessel in the hands of Vanara chief, who was endowed with the speed of the mind, to get water from the ocean.

shloka_text: अतिशीघ्रंततोगत्वावानरास्तेमनोजवाः ।।6.115.13।। आगतास्तुजलंगृह्यसमुद्राद्वानरोत्तमाः ।
explanation: Then the foremost of the Vanaras, endowed with the speed of mind, with all speed went and got water from the ocean.

shloka_text: ततःस्त्वेकंघटंगृह्यसम्स्थाप्यपरमासने ।।6.115.14।। घटेनतेनसौमित्रिरभ्यषिञ्चद्विभीषणम् । लङ्कायांरक्षसांमध्येराजानंरामशासनात् ।।6.115.15।। विधिनामन्त्रदृष्टेनसुहृद्गणसमावृतः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana was made to sit on an excellent seat, surrounded by hosts of friends and dear ones. Thereafter, in the midst of Rakshasas chanting sacred verses in accordance with scriptures, Saumithri took a vessel of water and duly consecrated Vibhishana with the water in the vessel as commanded by Rama, in Lanka.

shloka_text: ततःस्त्वेकंघटंगृह्यसम्स्थाप्यपरमासने ।।6.115.14।। घटेनतेनसौमित्रिरभ्यषिञ्चद्विभीषणम् । लङ्कायांरक्षसांमध्येराजानंरामशासनात् ।।6.115.15।। विधिनामन्त्रदृष्टेनसुहृद्गणसमावृतः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana was made to sit on an excellent seat, surrounded by hosts of friends and dear ones. Thereafter, in the midst of Rakshasas chanting sacred verses in accordance with scriptures, Saumithri took a vessel of water and duly consecrated Vibhishana with the water in the vessel as commanded by Rama, in Lanka.

shloka_text: अभ्यषिञ्चंस्तदासर्वेराक्षसावानरास्तथा ।।6.115.16।। प्रहर्षमतुलंगत्वातुष्टुवूराममवे ह ।
explanation: Thereafter all the Rakshasas and Vanaras also consecrated with extreme joy and paid tribute to Rama alone.

shloka_text: तस्यामात्याजहृषिरेभक्तायेचास्यराक्षसाः ।।6.115.17।। दृष्टवाभिषिक्तंलङ्कायांराक्षसेन्द्रंविभीषणम् ।
explanation: Seeing Vibheeshana consecrated and becoming a king of Lanka, all his ministers and devotees felt rejoiced.

shloka_text: राघवःपरमांप्रीतिंजगामसहलक्ष्मणः ।।6.115.18।। स तद्राज्यंमहत्प्राप्यरामदत्तंविभीषणः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana felt extreme felicity for attaining the kingdom given by great Rama with Lakshmana.

shloka_text: प्रकृतयस्सान्त्वयित्वा च ततोराममुपागमत् ।।6.115.19।। दध्यक्षतान्मोदकांश्चलाजास्सुमनसस्तथा । आजह्रुरथसन्तुष्टाःपौरास्तस्मैनिशाचराः ।।6.115.20।।
explanation: Consoling the subjects of the kingdom with good words, Vibheeshana sought Rama's presence. The people were very happy and brought curds, yellow rice grains (rice mixed with turmeric), flowers and sweets and parched grain and offered.

shloka_text: प्रकृतयस्सान्त्वयित्वा च ततोराममुपागमत् ।।6.115.19।। दध्यक्षतान्मोदकांश्चलाजास्सुमनसस्तथा । आजह्रुरथसन्तुष्टाःपौरास्तस्मैनिशाचराः ।।6.115.20।।
explanation: Consoling the subjects of the kingdom with good words, Vibheeshana sought Rama's presence. The people were very happy and brought curds, yellow rice grains (rice mixed with turmeric), flowers and sweets and parched grain and offered.

shloka_text: सःतान् गृहीत्वादुर्धर्षोराघवायन्यवेदयत् ।।6.115.21।। माङ्गल्यंमङ्गलंसर्वंलक्ष्मणाय च वीर्यवान् ।
explanation: Valiant Vibheeshana, who is difficult to encounter, presented the benign offerings and auspicious ones received by him to Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: कृतकार्यंसमृद्धार्थंदृष्टवारामोविभीषणम् ।।6.115.22।। प्रतिजग्राहतत्सर्वंतस्यैवप्रियकाम्यया ।
explanation: Rama having accomplished the task, thoughtfully pleased did not desire for the offerings, accepted them to please Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: ततःशैलोपमंवीरंप्राञ्जलिंप्रणतंस्थितम् ।।6.115.23।। उवाचेदंवचोरामोहनूमन्तंप्लवङ्गमम् ।
explanation: Then Rama, seeing a heroic mountain like Hanuman, who stood there in supplicant mood greeting him with joined palms, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अनुज्ञाप्यमहाराजमिमंसौम्य विभीषणम् ।।6.115.24।। प्रविश्यनगरींलङ्कांकौशलंब्रूहिमैथिलीम् ।
explanation: "O Gentle Hanuman! Taking the permission of the great king Vibheeshana, entering the city of Lanka, enquire the wellbeing of Mythili."

shloka_text: वैदेह्यैमांकुशलिनंसुग्रीवं च सलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.115.25।। आचक्ष्ववदतांश्रेष्ठरावणं च हतंरणे ।
explanation: "Convey to Vaidehi that me and Lakshman and also Sugriva are doing well, and that Ravana has been killed, O Best among the eloquent."

shloka_text: इतिप्रतिसमादिष्टोहनूमान्मारुतात्मजः । प्रविवेशपुरींलङ्कांपूज्यमानोनिशाचरैः ।।6.116.1।।
explanation: Having been commanded, Hanuman offered prayers to Vibheeshana and entered Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य चपुरींलङ्कांपूज्यमानोनिशाचारै: । ततस्तेनाभ्युनुज्ञातोहनुमान्वृक्षवाटिकाम् ।।6.116.2।। सम्प्रविश्ययथान्यायंसीतायाद्विितोहरिः । ददर्शमृजयाहीनांसातङ्कांरोहिणीमिव ।।6.116.3।। वृक्षमूलेनिरानन्दांराक्षसीभिःपरीवृताम् । निभृतःप्रणतःप्रह्वस्सोऽभिगम्याभिवाद्य च ।।6.116.4।।
explanation: The monkey, having sought the permission of Vibheeshana, entered Lanka city. Duly entering the Asoka grove, he attracted the attention of Sita, who was weak with no bath, cheerless, seated at the root of the tree, like Rohini star. After reaching the grove, he greeted Sita with folded palms and stood motionless.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य चपुरींलङ्कांपूज्यमानोनिशाचारै: । ततस्तेनाभ्युनुज्ञातोहनुमान्वृक्षवाटिकाम् ।।6.116.2।। सम्प्रविश्ययथान्यायंसीतायाद्विितोहरिः । ददर्शमृजयाहीनांसातङ्कांरोहिणीमिव ।।6.116.3।। वृक्षमूलेनिरानन्दांराक्षसीभिःपरीवृताम् । निभृतःप्रणतःप्रह्वस्सोऽभिगम्याभिवाद्य च ।।6.116.4।।
explanation: The monkey, having sought the permission of Vibheeshana, entered Lanka city. Duly entering the Asoka grove, he attracted the attention of Sita, who was weak with no bath, cheerless, seated at the root of the tree, like Rohini star. After reaching the grove, he greeted Sita with folded palms and stood motionless.

shloka_text: प्रविश्य चपुरींलङ्कांपूज्यमानोनिशाचारै: । ततस्तेनाभ्युनुज्ञातोहनुमान्वृक्षवाटिकाम् ।।6.116.2।। सम्प्रविश्ययथान्यायंसीतायाद्विितोहरिः । ददर्शमृजयाहीनांसातङ्कांरोहिणीमिव ।।6.116.3।। वृक्षमूलेनिरानन्दांराक्षसीभिःपरीवृताम् । निभृतःप्रणतःप्रह्वस्सोऽभिगम्याभिवाद्य च ।।6.116.4।।
explanation: The monkey, having sought the permission of Vibheeshana, entered Lanka city. Duly entering the Asoka grove, he attracted the attention of Sita, who was weak with no bath, cheerless, seated at the root of the tree, like Rohini star. After reaching the grove, he greeted Sita with folded palms and stood motionless.

shloka_text: दृष्टवासमागतंदेवीहनूमन्तंमहाबलम् । तूष्णीमास्ततदादृष्टवास्मृत्वासृष्टाभवत्तदा ।।6.116.5।।
explanation: Seeing the mighty Hanuman, who arrived quietly, she was quiet. Then she saw him and experienced joy on recognizing him

shloka_text: सौम्यंतस्यामुखंदृष्टवाहनुमान्प्लवगोत्तमः । रामस्यवचनंसर्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे ।।6.116.6।।
explanation: Gentle Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, seeing her started to communicate every word of Rama.

shloka_text: वैदेही कुशलीरामस्सहसुग्रीवलक्ष्मणः । वभीषणसहायश्चहरीणांसहितोबलैः ।।6.116.7।।
explanation: Hanuman said" O Vaidehi! Sri Rama accompanied by Sugriva and Lakshmana, with the help of Vibheeshana, is doing well."

shloka_text: कुशलंचाहसिद्धार्थोहतशत्रुरिमत्रजित् । विभीषणसहायेनरामेणहरिभिस्सह ।।6.116.8।। निहतोरावणोदेविलक्ष्मणेन च वीर्यवान् ।
explanation: "Noble lady! Sri Rama killed Ravana and won the enemy. He accomplished the purpose with the help of Vibheeshana, the valiant Lakshmana and the monkeys also so to speak. He inquired of your wellbeing."

shloka_text: प्रियमाख्यामितेदेविभूयश्चत्वांसभाजये ।।6.116.9।। तवप्रभावाद्धर्मजेमहान् रामेणसंयुगे । लब्धोऽयंविजयस्सीतेस्वस्थाभवगतज्वरा ।।6.116.10।।
explanation: "O noble lady! I am communicating delightful news to you. O Sita, a respectable lady and knowledgeable one, the victory is attained in the combat by the great soul Rama, by virtue of your strength and devotion."

shloka_text: प्रियमाख्यामितेदेविभूयश्चत्वांसभाजये ।।6.116.9।। तवप्रभावाद्धर्मजेमहान् रामेणसंयुगे । लब्धोऽयंविजयस्सीतेस्वस्थाभवगतज्वरा ।।6.116.10।।
explanation: "O noble lady! I am communicating delightful news to you. O Sita, a respectable lady and knowledgeable one, the victory is attained in the combat by the great soul Rama, by virtue of your strength and devotion."

shloka_text: रावणश्चहतश्शत्रुर्लङ्कचैववशीकृता । मयाह्यलब्न्दिद्रेणधृतेनतवनिर्जये ।।6.116.11।। प्रतिज्ञैषाविनिस्तीर्णाबद्ध्वासेतुंमहोदधौ ।
explanation: 'Ravana has been killed, Lanka is under our side vanquished completely. Without any sleep, with forbearance, building an extensive bridge on the great ocean, the vow has been redeemed', is Rama's message to you, said Hanuman.

shloka_text: सम्भ्रमश्च न कर्तव्योवर्तन्त्यारावणालये ।।6.116.12।। विभीषणविधेयंहिलङ्कैश्वर्यमिदंकृतम् ।
explanation: "This Lanka is under Vibheeshana, Lord of Lanka. There is no need for perturbation thinking that you are in Ravana's abode."

shloka_text: तदाश्वसिहिविस्रब्धंस्वगृहेपरिवर्तसे ।।6.116.13।। अयंचाभ्येतिसम्हृष्टस्त्वद्धर्शनसमुत्सुकः ।
explanation: "You be at ease, as you are living in your own abode", said Hanuman consoling Sita. 'Vibheeshana, who is very happy, is eager and favouring to see you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तासमुत्पत्यसीताशशिनिभानना ।।6.116.14।। प्रहर्षेणावरुद्धासाव्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।
explanation: Hanuman having spoken in that way, Sita got up in excessive joy and could not speak naturally.

shloka_text: ततोऽब्रवीद्धरिवरःसीतामप्रतिजल्पतीम् ।।6.116.15।। किंत्वंचिन्तयसेदेविकिं च मांनाभिभाषसे ।
explanation: Then seeing Sita not answering him, the monkey chief asked her" Why are you not replying. What are you thinking?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्ताहनुमतासीताधर्मपथेस्थिता ।।6.116.16।। अब्रवीत्परमप्रीताबाष्पगद्गदयागिरा ।
explanation: When Hanuman spoke in that way virtuous Sita was overwhelmed with joy and spoke with a voice choked with tears.

shloka_text: प्रियमेतदुपश्रुत्यभर्तुर्विजयसंश्रयम् ।।6.116.17।। प्रहर्षवशमापन्नानिर्वाक्यास्मिक्षणान्तरम् ।
explanation: "No doubt that my husband is victorious is very delightful. Hearing this, I am overcome with delight and am unable to speak for a moment."

shloka_text: न हिपश्यामिसदृशंचिन्तयन्तीप्लवङ्गमा ।।6.116.18।। मप्रतियाब्यानकस्येहदातुंप्रत्यभिनन्दनम् ।
explanation: "Hanuman! However, I think to give you a befitting gift for this happy news. I am not able to see any."

shloka_text: नहिपश्यामिततसौम्यपृथिव्यामपिवानर ।।6.116.19।। सदृशंयत्प्रियाख्यानेतवदत्त्वाभवेत्सुखम् ।
explanation: "I am not able to see on this earth, a gift befitting the value of your message, which can be given to you to make you happy."

shloka_text: हिरण्यंवासुवर्णंवारत्नानिविविधानिच ।।6.116.20।। राज्यंवात्रिषुलोकेषुनैतदर्हतिभाषितम् ।
explanation: "Neither gold or silver or gems, not even kingdom or the three worlds are equal to what you have spoken now."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुवैदेह्याप्रत्युवाचप्लवङ्गमः ।।6.116.21।। प्रगृहीताञ्जलिर्हर्षासतीतायाःप्रमुखेस्थितः ।
explanation: Spoken in that way by Vaidehi, Hanuman stood with folded palms in front of Sita and replied in delight.

shloka_text: भर्तुःप्रियहितेयुक्तेभर्तुर्विजयकाङ्क्षिण: ।।6.116.22।। स्निग्धमेवंविधंवाक्यंत्वमेवार्हस्यनिन्दिते ।
explanation: "You alone can speak such affectionate words in this manner wishing victory and welfare of your dear husband. You are irreproachable."

shloka_text: तवैतद्वचनंसौम्येसारवत् स्निग्धमेव च ।।6.116.23।। रत्नौघाद्विविधाच्चापिदेवराज्याद्विशिष्यते ।
explanation: "O gentle one! Your meaningful words full of affection are more valuable than clusters of gems or Indra, the Lord of gods."

shloka_text: अर्थतश्चमयाप्राप्तादेवरज्यादयोगुणाः ।।6.116.24।। हतशत्रुंविजयिनंरामंपश्यामिसुस्थितम् ।
explanation: "Now that the enemy is killed, Rama is happy, which means as if I have attained the rulership of gods."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वामैथिलीजनकात्मजा ।।6.116.25।। ततःशुभतरंवाक्यमुवाचपवनात्मजम् ।
explanation: Hearing the words of Mythili, daughter of Janaka, Hanuman spoke these auspicious words.

shloka_text: अतिलक्षणसम्पन्नंमाधुर्यगुणभूषितम् ।।6.116.26।। बुद्ध्याह्यष्टाङ्गयायुक्तंत्वमेवार्हसिभाषितुम् ।
explanation: Continuing to pay tribute to Hanuman's words, Sita said" Your language and expression are always richly endowed with virtuous qualities, sweet and valuable, combined with eight excellences. (Eight excellences areKeenness to hear discourses, readiness to hear discourses, receptivity, retentive power, reasoning for a proposition, against a proposition, faculty of comprehension, realization of truth)."

shloka_text: श्लाघनीयोऽनिलस्यत्वंसुतःपरमधार्मिकः ।।6.116.27।। बलंशौर्यंश्रुतंसत्त्वंविक्रमोदाक्ष्यमुत्तमम् । तेजःक्षमाधृतिस्स्थैर्यंविनीतत्वं न संशयः ।।6.116.28।। एतेचान्ये च बहवोगुणास्त्वय्येवशोभनाः ।
