explanation: "You are a praiseworthy son of wind god. In strength, righteousness, valour, vigour, prowess, skill, you are excellent. You are energetic, endowed with tolerance, forbearance, firmness, brilliance, and humility. You alone have many more qualities, no doubt."

shloka_text: श्लाघनीयोऽनिलस्यत्वंसुतःपरमधार्मिकः ।।6.116.27।। बलंशौर्यंश्रुतंसत्त्वंविक्रमोदाक्ष्यमुत्तमम् । तेजःक्षमाधृतिस्स्थैर्यंविनीतत्वं न संशयः ।।6.116.28।। एतेचान्ये च बहवोगुणास्त्वय्येवशोभनाः ।
explanation: "You are a praiseworthy son of wind god. In strength, righteousness, valour, vigour, prowess, skill, you are excellent. You are energetic, endowed with tolerance, forbearance, firmness, brilliance, and humility. You alone have many more qualities, no doubt."

shloka_text: अथोवाचपुनस्सीतामसम्भ्रान्तोविनीतवत् ।।6.116.29।। प्रगृहीताञ्चलिर्हर्षात्सीतायाःप्रमुखेस्थितः ।
explanation: Now with folded palms offering prayers to Sita, Hanuman stood without perturbation, with all humility and again spoke to Sita.

shloka_text: इमास्तुखलुराक्षस्योयदित्वमनुमन्यसे ।।6.116.30।। हन्तुमिच्छामितास्सर्वायाभिस्त्वंतर्जितापुरा ।
explanation: "I desire to kill all those Rakshasas who in the past have intimidated you indeed and whoever threatened you."

shloka_text: क्लिश्यन्तीम् पतिदेवांत्वामशोकवनिकांगताम् ।।6.116.31।। घोररूपसमाचाराःक्रूराःक्रूरतरेक्षणाः । इहश्रुतामयादेवि राक्षस्योविकृताननाः ।।6.116.32।। असकृत्परुषैर्वाक्यैर्वद्नत्योरावणाज्ञया ।
explanation: "O Devi! You, who were so devoted to your husband, were tormented in Asoka grove earlier. These cruel Rakshasas of hideous conduct, of fierce and distorted forms with terrible eyes addressing you in harsh words by Ravana's order, were heard by me."

shloka_text: क्लिश्यन्तीम् पतिदेवांत्वामशोकवनिकांगताम् ।।6.116.31।। घोररूपसमाचाराःक्रूराःक्रूरतरेक्षणाः । इहश्रुतामयादेवि राक्षस्योविकृताननाः ।।6.116.32।। असकृत्परुषैर्वाक्यैर्वद्नत्योरावणाज्ञया ।
explanation: "O Devi! You, who were so devoted to your husband, were tormented in Asoka grove earlier. These cruel Rakshasas of hideous conduct, of fierce and distorted forms with terrible eyes addressing you in harsh words by Ravana's order, were heard by me."

shloka_text: विकृताविकृताकाराःक्रूराःक्रूरकचेक्षणाः ।।6.116.33।। इच्छामिविविधैराघतैर्हन्तुमेतास्सुदारुणाः । राक्षस्योदारुणकथावरमेतत्प्रयच्छमे ।।6.116.34।।
explanation: "I wish to kill by all kinds of strokes, these cruel distorted forms of Rakshasas having terrible hair and fierce eyes and not to mention their violence. Permit me."

shloka_text: विकृताविकृताकाराःक्रूराःक्रूरकचेक्षणाः ।।6.116.33।। इच्छामिविविधैराघतैर्हन्तुमेतास्सुदारुणाः । राक्षस्योदारुणकथावरमेतत्प्रयच्छमे ।।6.116.34।।
explanation: "I wish to kill by all kinds of strokes, these cruel distorted forms of Rakshasas having terrible hair and fierce eyes and not to mention their violence. Permit me."

shloka_text: मुष्टिभिःपर्षिणघातैश्चविशालैश्चैवबाहुभिः । जङ्घाजानुप्रहारैश्चदन्तानांचैवपीडनैः ।।6.116.35।। भक्षणैःकर्णनासानांकेशानांलुञ्चनैस्तथा । भृशंशुष्कमुखैश्चैवदारणैर्लङ्घनैर्हतैः ।।6.116.36।। विभिन्नशङ्कुग्रीवांशपार्श्वकैश्चकलेवरैः । निपात्यहन्तुमिच्छामितवविप्रियकारिणीः ।।6.116.37।।
explanation: "These Rakshasas who have wronged, who are of dreadful appearance, I wish to hit them with fists, with feet spreading long arms, strike with blows of shanks and knees, with teeth, and torment by pulling their ears and nose. Their hair will be torn off violently, their faces will be made dry, they will be tossed up, torn with different sharp conches. Their broken bodies, heads, necks, and trunks will be thrown down and killed. Grant this boon to me."

shloka_text: मुष्टिभिःपर्षिणघातैश्चविशालैश्चैवबाहुभिः । जङ्घाजानुप्रहारैश्चदन्तानांचैवपीडनैः ।।6.116.35।। भक्षणैःकर्णनासानांकेशानांलुञ्चनैस्तथा । भृशंशुष्कमुखैश्चैवदारणैर्लङ्घनैर्हतैः ।।6.116.36।। विभिन्नशङ्कुग्रीवांशपार्श्वकैश्चकलेवरैः । निपात्यहन्तुमिच्छामितवविप्रियकारिणीः ।।6.116.37।।
explanation: "These Rakshasas who have wronged, who are of dreadful appearance, I wish to hit them with fists, with feet spreading long arms, strike with blows of shanks and knees, with teeth, and torment by pulling their ears and nose. Their hair will be torn off violently, their faces will be made dry, they will be tossed up, torn with different sharp conches. Their broken bodies, heads, necks, and trunks will be thrown down and killed. Grant this boon to me."

shloka_text: मुष्टिभिःपर्षिणघातैश्चविशालैश्चैवबाहुभिः । जङ्घाजानुप्रहारैश्चदन्तानांचैवपीडनैः ।।6.116.35।। भक्षणैःकर्णनासानांकेशानांलुञ्चनैस्तथा । भृशंशुष्कमुखैश्चैवदारणैर्लङ्घनैर्हतैः ।।6.116.36।। विभिन्नशङ्कुग्रीवांशपार्श्वकैश्चकलेवरैः । निपात्यहन्तुमिच्छामितवविप्रियकारिणीः ।।6.116.37।।
explanation: "These Rakshasas who have wronged, who are of dreadful appearance, I wish to hit them with fists, with feet spreading long arms, strike with blows of shanks and knees, with teeth, and torment by pulling their ears and nose. Their hair will be torn off violently, their faces will be made dry, they will be tossed up, torn with different sharp conches. Their broken bodies, heads, necks, and trunks will be thrown down and killed. Grant this boon to me."

shloka_text: एवंप्रहारैर्बहुभिःसंप्प्रहार्ययशस्विनि । घातयेतीव्ररूपाभिर्याभिस्त्वंतर्जितापुरा ।।6.116.38।।
explanation: "O Illustrious lady! I would like to kill the terrible forms of ogres who threatened you, in that way, I will be at and strike in many ways and destroy them", said Hanuman to Sita.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तासाहनुमताकृपणादीनवत्सला । हनूमन्तमुवाचेदंचिन्तयित्वाविमृश्य च ।।6.116.39।।
explanation: Hanuman having spoken like that, Sita who was fond of the desperate, thus spoke to Hanuman thinking for a while.

shloka_text: राजसंश्रयवश्यानांकुर्वतीनांपराज्ञया । विधेयानां च दासीनांकःकुप्यद्वानरोत्तम ।।6.116.40।।
explanation: "Foremost of Vanaras! Who will be angry? Being under the command of the king and being obedient maids, they did so according to king's order.

shloka_text: भाग्यवैषम्यदोषेणपुरस्ताद्धुष्कृतेन च । मयैतत्प्राप्यसर्वंस्वकृतंह्युपभुज्यते ।।6.116.41।।
explanation: Due to the flaw of adverse fortune and past misdeeds, all this, having been obtained by me, is indeed being experienced as the consequence of my own actions.

shloka_text: मैवंवदमहाबाहो दैवेह्येषापरागतिः । प्राप्तव्यंतुदशायोगान्मयैतदितिनिश्चितम् ।।6.116.42।। दासीनांरावणस्याहंमर्षयामीहदुर्बला ।
explanation: "Mighty Armed Hanuman! Do not speak in this manner. It was my fate which was supreme. Because of my predetermined circumstances I reaped such a result. I am feeblehearted and condone the maids surely."

shloka_text: आज्ञप्ताराक्षसेनेहराक्षस्यस्तर्जयन्तिमाम् ।।6.116.43।। हतेतस्मिन्नकुर्वन्तितर्जनंमारुतात्मज ।
explanation: "By Ravana's order they threatened me so. Now with his death, they will not be threatening me."

shloka_text: अयंव्याघ्रसमीपेतुपुराणोधर्मसंहितः ।।6.116.44।। ऋक्षेणगीतःश्लोकोऽस्तितंनिबोधप्लवङ्गम ।
explanation: "O Monkey! In olden days a bear had uttered a verse which conforms to righteousness. I shall tell you now."

shloka_text: न पर: पापमादत्तेपरेषांपापकर्मणाम् ।।6.116.45।। समयोरक्षितव्यस्तुसप्तश्चारित्रभूषणाः ।
explanation: Another does not acquire the sin of others who commit evil deeds. But the vow must be protected, which are the seven ornaments of character.

shloka_text: पापानांवाशुभानांवावधार्हाणांप्लवङ्गम ।।6.116.46।। कार्यंकरुण्यमार्येण न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति ।
explanation: "Sinners or noble men, having done a wrong deed and deserve death. Also noble, will show compassion and not commit harm."

shloka_text: लोकहिंसाविहाराणांरक्षसांकामरूपिणाम् ।।6.116.47।। कुर्वतामपिपापानिनैवकार्यमशोभनम् ।
explanation: "Rakshasas by nature are cruel in their deeds and can assume any form according to their will. No sinful actions to be done even if they do sinful actions."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुहनुमान् सीतयावाक्यकोविदः ।।6.116.48।। प्रत्युवाचततस्सीतांरामपत्नीयशश्विनीम् ।
explanation: Sita, having spoken that way to Hanuman, he, who was capable of good expression, replied as follows to Rama's consort, who was irreproachable.

shloka_text: युक्तारामस्यभवतीधर्मपत्नीयशश्विनी ।।6.116.49।। प्रतिसन्दिशमांदेवि गमिष्येयत्रराघवः ।
explanation: "Devi! you are the righteous wife of Rama and earned fame. Give me the right message to Rama in return. I will go."

shloka_text: एवमुक्ताहनुमतावैदेहिजनकात्मजा ।।6.116.50।। साब्रवीद्ध्रष्टुमिच्छामिभर्तारंवानरोत्तम ।
explanation: Hanuman, having spoken that way to Vaidehi, daughter of Janaka, she said" I desire to see my husband."

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनंश्रुत्वाहनुमान्पवनात्मजः ।।6.116.51।। हर्षयन्मैथिलींवाक्यमुवाचेदंमहामतिः ।
explanation: On hearing Mythili, wise Hanuman spoke these words to her bringing joy to her.

shloka_text: पूर्णचन्द्राननंरामंद्रक्ष्यस्यार्येसलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.116.52।। स्थिरमित्रंहतामित्रंशचीवत्रिदशेश्वरम् ।
explanation: "Now you will see Sri Rama whose countenance resembles the moon, with Lakshmana, with friends who are alive, with friends whose enemies are gone, just as Sachi, the consort of Indra, the Lord of gods saw."

shloka_text: तामेवमुक्त्वाराजन्तींसीतांसाक्षादिवश्रियम् ।।6.116.53।। आजगाममहावेगोहनूमान्यत्रराघवः ।
explanation: Hanuman reached Raghava with extraordinary speed assuring Sita, who shone like Lakshmi, goddess of prosperity, and had spoken like that.

shloka_text: स उवाचमहाप्रामस्सोऽभिवाद्यप्लवङ्गमः । रामंवचनमर्थज्ञोवरंसर्वधनुष्मताम् ।।6.117.1।।
explanation: Highly learned Hanuman greeted and spoke meaningfully to Rama, the foremost among the wielders of bow.

shloka_text: यन्निमित्तोऽयमारम्बःकर्मणांयःफलोदयः । तांदेवींशोकसन्तप्तांद्रष्टुमर्हसिमैथिलीम् ।।6.117.2।।
explanation: "You ought to see that noble lady Mythili, who was immersed in grief, for whose sake these actions were started and has borne fruit."

shloka_text: साहिशोकसमाविष्टाबाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा । मैथिलीविजयंश्रुत्वाद्रष्टुंत्वामभिकाङ्क्षति ।।6.117.3।।
explanation: "Mythili who is overcome with grief on hearing your victory, was filled with tears in her eyes and desired to see you."

shloka_text: पूर्वकात्प्रत्ययाच्चाहमुक्तोविश्वस्तयातया । भर्तारंद्रष्टुमिच्छामिकृतार्थंसहलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.117.4।।
explanation: "In an earlier occasion having known me and trusting me expressed that she desires to see Rama with Lakshmana after victory and with gratitude."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोहनुमतारामोधर्मभृतांवरः । आगच्छत्सहसाध्यानमीषद्भाष्पपरिप्लुतः ।।6.117.5।।
explanation: When Hanuman had spoken like that, Rama, the upholder of righteousness, shed tears slightly and suddenly became thoughtful.

shloka_text: दीर्घमुष्णंविनिःश्वस्यजगतीमवलोकयन् । उवाचमेघसङ्काशंविभीषणमुपस्थितम् ।।6.117.6।।
explanation: Drawing a long hot breath, looking at the ground, he spoke to Vibheeshana, who was like a cloud standing there.

shloka_text: दिव्याङ्गरागांवैदेहींदिव्याभरणभूषिताम् । इहसीतांशिरःस्नातामुपस्थापयमाचिरम् ।।6.117.7।।
explanation: Bring Vaidehi (Sita) here without delay, adorned with divine unguents and divine ornaments, having taken a ceremonial head-bath.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणत्वरमाणोविभीषणः । प्रविश्यान्तःपुरंसीतांस्त्रीभिस्स्वाभिरोचदयत् ।।6.117.8।।
explanation: When Rama had spoken in that manner, Vibheeeshana for his part hastened to the Gynaeceum and assigned through the women to convey to Sita.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतांमहाभागांदृष्टवोवाचविभीषणः । मूर्ध्निबद्धाञ्जलिश्रीमान्विनीतोराक्षसेश्वरः ।।6.117.9।।
explanation: Then Vibheeshana, the prosperous Lord of the Rakshasas seeing Sita greeted her with palms joined together lifted it over his head (as a sign of respect).

shloka_text: दिव्याङ्गरागावैदेहीदिव्याभरणभूषिता । यानमारोहभद्रंतेभर्तात्वांद्रष्टुमिच्छति ।।6.117.10।।
explanation: "Vaidehi! Anointed with a wonderful fragrance, decked with beautiful ornaments, auspicious and ascending the palanquin, your husband desires to see you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तातुवैदेहीप्रत्युवाचविभीषणम् । अस्नात्वाद्रष्टुमिच्छामिभर्तारंराक्षसेश्वर ।।6.117.11।।
explanation: Vibheeshana, having spoken that way, Vaidehi said to the Lord of Rakshasas that she would like to see him without having a bath.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनंश्रुत्वाप्रत्युवाचविभीषणः । यथाहरामोभहर्तातेतत्तथाकर्तुमार्हसिमार्हसि ।।6.117.12।।
explanation: Hearing Sita's words Vibheeshana replied saying," You will and ought to do what your husband Rama has said."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वामैथिलीपतिदेवता । भर्तृभक्त्यावृतासाध्वीतथेतिप्रत्यभाषत ।।6.117.13।।
explanation: Noble Mythili (on hearing Vibheeshana), who looked upon her husband as God, said in reply, 'Alright'.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतांशिरःस्नातांसंयुक्तांप्रतिकर्मणा । महार्हाभरणोपेतांमहार्हाम्बरधारिणीम् ।।6.117.14।। आरोप्यशिबिकांदीप्तांपरार्घ्याम्बरसम्वृताम् । राक्षसैर्भहुभिर्गुप्तामाजहारविभीषणः ।।6.117.15।।
explanation: Thereafter Vibheeshana, making Sita to ascend the palanquin, covered with valuable clothes and guarded by numerous Rakshasas after she adorned herself in the best of ornaments and put on glowing wonderful clothes brought to Rama.

shloka_text: ततस्सीतांशिरःस्नातांसंयुक्तांप्रतिकर्मणा । महार्हाभरणोपेतांमहार्हाम्बरधारिणीम् ।।6.117.14।। आरोप्यशिबिकांदीप्तांपरार्घ्याम्बरसम्वृताम् । राक्षसैर्भहुभिर्गुप्तामाजहारविभीषणः ।।6.117.15।।
explanation: Thereafter Vibheeshana, making Sita to ascend the palanquin, covered with valuable clothes and guarded by numerous Rakshasas after she adorned herself in the best of ornaments and put on glowing wonderful clothes brought to Rama.

shloka_text: सोऽभिगम्यमहात्मानंज्ञातावपिध्यानमास्थितम् । प्रणतश्चप्रहृष्टश्चप्राप्तांसीतांन्यवेदयत् ।।6.117.16।।
explanation: Knowing that Sita reached also, great Rama was seen in a meditative mood absorbed in thought. Vibheeshana announced saying, 'Sita has been brought' and greeted with folded palms, full of joy.

shloka_text: तामागतामुपश्रुत्यरक्षोगृहचिरोषिताम् । हर्षोदैन्यंच रोषश्चत्रयंराघवमाविशत् ।।6.117.17।।
explanation: On hearing that Sita had arrived, who stayed in Rakshasa's abode for long, Raghava had experienced joy, indignation, and anger, all the three at the same time.

shloka_text: ततःपार्श्वगतंदृष्टवासविमर्शंविचारयन् । विभीषणमिदंवाक्यमहृष्टोराघवोऽब्रवीत् ।।6.117.18।।
explanation: Raghava, analysed with in him, distressed and thinking deeply, seeing Vibheeshana close by, spoke these words.

shloka_text: राक्षसाधिपतेसौम्यनित्यंमद्विजयेरत । वैदेहीसंनिकर्षंमेशीघ्रंसमुपगच्छतु ।।6.117.19।।
explanation: "O gentle Vibheeshana, let Sita who sought my victory always be quickly brought near me."

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाराघवस्यविभीषणः । तूर्णमुत्सारणंतत्रकारयामासधर्मवित् ।।6.117.20।।
explanation: On hearing Raghava's words, faithful Vibheeshana instantly assigned people to disperse from there.

shloka_text: कञ्चुकोष्णीषिणस्तत्रवेत्रजर्जरपाणयः । उत्सारयन्तस्तान्योधान्समन्तात् परिचक्रमुः ।।6.117.21।।
explanation: Then those who were wearing coats and turbans, holding staffs in hand, warriors started moving and dispersed.

shloka_text: ऋक्षाणांवानराणां च राक्षसानां च सर्वशः । वृन्दान्युत्सार्यमाणानिदूरमुत्तस्थुरन्ततः ।।6.117.22।।
explanation: The hordes of Bears, Vanaras and Rakshasas moving about all over there were driven away to a distance from the vicinity.

shloka_text: तेषामुत्सार्यमाणानांनिःस्वनःसुमहानभूत् । वायुनोद्धूयामानस्यसागरस्येवनिःस्वनः ।।6.117.23।।
explanation: The great sound heard there was like the uproar of an ocean lashed by a storm.

shloka_text: उत्सार्यमाणान् दृष्टवाथजगत्यांजातसम्भ्रमान् । दाक्षिण्यात्तदमर्षाच्चवारयामासराघवः ।।6.117.24।।
explanation: Seeing them excited to know and dispersing, Raghava stopped them out of kindness.

shloka_text: संरम्बश्चाब्रवीद्रामश्चक्षुषाप्रदहन्निव । विभीषणंमहाप्राज्ञंसोपालम्बमिदंवचः ।।6.117.25।।
explanation: Exhibiting anger with his gaze at the uproar, Rama addressed the highly intelligent Vibheeshana resenting their action.

shloka_text: किमर्थंमामनादृत्यक्लिश्यतेऽयंत्वयाजनः । निवर्तयैनमुद्योगंजनोऽयंस्वजनोमम ।।6.117.26।।
explanation: "Why are these people being troubled without disregard for me? Stop this excitement. They are my own people."

shloka_text: न गृहाणि न वस्त्राणि न प्राकारास्तिरस्क्रिया । नेदृशाराजसत्कारावृत्तमावरणंस्त्रियाः ।।6.117.27।।
explanation: "For women it is not the house, boundary wall or clothes or protective wall or screen of cloth or even this kind of royal treatment or surrounding, is the protection."

shloka_text: व्यसनेषु न कृच्छ्रेषु न युद्धेषुस्वयंवरे । न क्रतौनोविवाहेवादर्शनंदूष्यतेस्त्रियाः ।।6.117.28।।
explanation: "The appearance of a woman in public is not condemned in times of difficulty, in straits, in conflicts, in the selection of a husband, or in sacrificial ceremonies or marriage ceremonies."

shloka_text: सैषाविपद्गताचैवकृच्छ्रेव च महतिस्थिता । दर्शनेनास्तिदोषोऽस्यामत्समीपेविशेषतः ।।6.117.29।।
explanation: "Sita is in distress and in a highly miserable situation. Her appearance is no fault especially in my presence."

shloka_text: विसृज्यशिबिकांतस्मात्पद्भ्यामेवोपसर्पतु । समीपेममवैदेहींपश्यन्त्वेतेवनौकसः ।।6.117.30।।
explanation: "Therefore, leaving the palanquin let Vaidehi walk on foot only towards me with the help of these Vanaras."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणसविमर्शोविभीषणम् । रामस्योपानयसतीतांसन्निकर्षंविनीतवत् ।।6.117.31।।
explanation: Rama having spoken clearly in that way, Vibheeshana reverently conducted Sita to Rama.

shloka_text: ततोलक्ष्मणसुग्रीवौहनूमांश्चप्लवङ्गमः । निशम्यवाक्यंरामस्यबभूवुर्व्यथिताभृशम् ।।6.117.32।।
explanation: There upon Lakshmana, Sugriva, and Vanara Hanuman, astonished at Rama's statement, became highly distressed.

shloka_text: कलत्रनिरपेक्ष्षैश्चइङ्गितैरस्यदारुणैः । अप्रीतमिवसीतायांतर्कयन्तिस्मराघवम् ।।6.117.33।।
explanation: Seeing Rama having no regard towards Sita, and his harsh gestures, Lakshmana and Sugriva discussed if Rama was displeased with Sita?

shloka_text: लज्जयात्ववलीयन्तीस्वेषुगात्रेषुमैथिली । विभीषणेनानुगताभर्तारंसाभ्यवर्तत ।।6.117.34।।
explanation: Mythili, also adopting modesty, shrinking into her own limbs, approached her husband followed by Vibheeshana.

shloka_text: विस्मयाच्छप्रहर्षाच्चस्नेहाच्चपतिदेवता । उदैक्षतमुखंभर्तुःसौम्यंसौम्यतरानना ।।6.117.35।।
explanation: Sita, a gentle lady, who considered her husband as God only wondered with a mixed feeling of joy and affection and looked at the gentle face of Rama.

shloka_text: तांतुपाश्वस्थितांप्रह्वांरामस्सम्प्रेक्ष्यमैथिलीम् । हृदयान्तर्गतंक्रोधव्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।।6.118.1।।
explanation: Observing Mythili who stood near him, Rama started to give expression to what was in his heart.

shloka_text: एषासिनिर्जिताभद्रेशत्रुंजित्वारणाजिरे । पौरुषाद्यदनुष्ठेयंमयैतदुपपादितम् ।।6.118.2।।
explanation: "O Auspicious Sita! You are won by destruction of the enemy in the battlefield. What was worth doing has been done with all my effort."

shloka_text: गतोऽस्म्यन्तममर्षस्यधर्षणासम्प्रमार्जिता । अवमानश्चशत्रुश्चयुगपन्निहतौमया ।।6.118.3।।
explanation: "I have put an end to the indignity that I lost. I gained reward for the insult. The indignity offered by the enemy has been wiped out all at once."

shloka_text: अद्यमेपौरुषंदृष्टमद्यमेसफल्श्रमः । अद्यतीर्णप्रतिज्ञोऽत्वाप्रभवाम्यद्यचात्मनः ।।6.118.4।।
explanation: "Now you see the result of my effort. I am successful and fulfilled my vow. Today I am independent."

shloka_text: यात्वंविरहितानीताचलचित्तेनरक्षसा । दैवसम्पादितोदोषोमानुषेणमयाजितः ।।6.118.5।।
explanation: "When you were alone you were abducted by the fickle minded Rakshasa. The fault of destiny has been won by me, a mortal by the will of god।।"

shloka_text: सम्प्राप्तमवमानंयस्तेजसा न प्रमार्जति । कस्तस्यपुरुषार्थोमहताप्यल्पचेतसः ।।6.118.6।।
explanation: "What is the purpose of might however great he might be, if he is petty minded and does not wipe off the insult?"

shloka_text: लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्यलङ्कायाश्चापिमर्धनम् । सफलंतस्य च श्लाघ्यमद्यकर्महनूमतः ।।6.118.7।।
explanation: "Hanuman's leaping across the ocean and devastating action of Lanka has yielded results now."

shloka_text: युद्धेविक्रमतश्चैवहितंमन्त्रयतस्तथा । सुग्रीवस्यससैन्यस्यसफलोऽद्यपरिश्रमः ।।6.118.8।।
explanation: "The prowess of Sugriva and also his army, his good advice and efforts in combat have become successful."

shloka_text: विभीषणस्य च तथासफलोऽद्यपरिश्रमः । विगुणंभ्रातरंत्यक्त्वायोमांस्वयमुपस्थितः ।।6.118.9।।
explanation: "In the same way even Vibheeshana's hard work leaving his brother devoid of good qualities and coming to me on his own has given success."

shloka_text: इत्येवंवदत्श्रुत्वासीतारामस्यतद्वचः । मृगीवोत्फुल्लनयनाबभूवाश्रुपरिप्लुता ।।6.118.10।।
explanation: Sita's broad eyes which were like that of female deer were filled with tears on hearing the words of Rama.

shloka_text: पश्यतस्तांतुरामस्यसमीपेहृदयप्रियाम् । जनवादभयाद्राज्ञोबभूवहृदयंद्विधा ।।6.118.11।।
explanation: Rama was already hurt and on seeing Sita who was dear to his heart nearby, he was burning with the fear of public opinion.

shloka_text: सीतामुत्पलपत्राक्षींनीलकुञ्चितमूर्थजाम् । अवदद्वैवरारोहंमध्येवानररक्षसाम् ।।6.118.12।।
explanation: In the midst of Vanaras and Rakshasas, Rama spoke with great discomfort to Sita whose eyes were like lotus petals and hair was dark and curly and whose limbs were beautiful.

shloka_text: यत्कर्तव्यंमनुष्येणधर्षणांप्रतिमार्जता । तत्कृतंरावणंहत्वामयेदंमानकाङ्क्षिणा ।।6.118.13।।
explanation: "That which my mind desired as a duty of a human being, to get rid of the insult has been done by killing Ravana."

shloka_text: निर्जिताजीवलोकस्यतपसाभावितात्मना । अगस्त्येनदुराधर्षामुनिनादक्षिणेवधिक् ।।6.118.14।।
explanation: "Though the southern quarter is difficult to assail for the world of mortals, Agastya, a realized sage, has won by the power of his austerity. In the same way I have won you."

shloka_text: विदितश्चास्तुभत्रंतेयोऽयंरणपरिश्रमः । सुतीर्णःसुहृदांवीर्यान्नत्वदर्थंमयाकृतः ।।6.118.15।। रक्षतातुमयावृत्तपमवादं च सर्वतः । प्रख्यातस्यात्मवंशस्यव्यङ्ग्यं च परिमार्जता ।।6.118.16।।
explanation: "Sita! This effort in carrying out with the assistance of valiant friends is not done for your sake. Let it be known to you. I have done this to protect good conduct and my illustrious race from scandal and rid of obloquy from all sides."

shloka_text: विदितश्चास्तुभत्रंतेयोऽयंरणपरिश्रमः । सुतीर्णःसुहृदांवीर्यान्नत्वदर्थंमयाकृतः ।।6.118.15।। रक्षतातुमयावृत्तपमवादं च सर्वतः । प्रख्यातस्यात्मवंशस्यव्यङ्ग्यं च परिमार्जता ।।6.118.16।।
explanation: "Sita! This effort in carrying out with the assistance of valiant friends is not done for your sake. Let it be known to you. I have done this to protect good conduct and my illustrious race from scandal and rid of obloquy from all sides."

shloka_text: प्राप्तचारित्रसन्देहाममप्रतिमुखेस्थिता । दीपोनेत्रातुरस्येवप्रतिकूलासिमेदृढम् ।।6.118.17।।
explanation: "In the event of doubtful conduct also you are standing firmly like a glowing lamp for me suffering from sore eyes and disagreeable to me."

shloka_text: तद्गच्छत्वानुजानेऽद्ययथेष्टंजनकात्मजे । एतादशदिशोभद्रेकार्यमस्ति न मेत्वया ।।6.118.18।।
explanation: "O Janaka's daughter! therefore now you are permitted to go wherever to any quarter. Let you be auspicious. I have no work with you."

shloka_text: कःपुमांस्तुकुलेजातस्स्त्रयंपरगृहाषिताम् । तेजस्वीपुनरादद्यात्सुहृल्लेख्येनचेतसा ।।6.118.19।।
explanation: "Which eminent man born in a good race will again consciously accept a wife who lived in another's home?"

shloka_text: रावणाङ्कपरिक्लिष्टांदृष्टांदुष्टेनचक्षुषा । कथंत्वापुनरादद्यांकुलंव्यपदिशन् महत् ।।6.118.20।।
explanation: "You are thrown out of the arms of Ravana. You have been seen by him with lustful eyes, have been seen by all with evil eyes. How can one born in a great race accept you again?"

shloka_text: तदर्थंनिर्जितामेत्वंयशःप्रत्याहृतंमया । नास्तिमेत्यय्यभिष्वङ्गोयथेष्टंगम्यतामितः ।।6.118.21।।
explanation: "The reason for winning you back is to get rid of the insult. Now I have no interest in you. You may go to the place of your choice."

shloka_text: तदद्यव्याहृतंभद्रेमयैतत् कृतबुधदिना । लक्ष्मणेनाथभरतेकुरुबुधदिंयथासुखम् ।।6.118.22।।
explanation: " Auspicious one! This utterance has been thought over well today. You may go wherever you find happiness, either to Lakshmana or else to Bharata. Think well and do."

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नेवाथसुग्रीवेराक्षसेवाविभीषणे । निवेशयमनस्सीतेयथावासुखमात्मनः ।।6.118.23।।
explanation: "Sita! You can go to Shatrughna or else Sugriva or even Rakshasa Vibheeshana, wherever you feel like to live."

shloka_text: न हित्वांरावणोदृष्टवादिव्यरूपांमनोरमाम् । मर्षयेतचिरंसीतेस्वगृहेपर्यवस्थिताम् ।।6.118.24।।
explanation: "Sita! You are endowed with beauty and having you in his own house for so long and seeing you, how Ravana could have resisted or detained you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तातुवैदेहिपरुषंरोमहर्षणम् । राघवेणसरोषेणश्रुत्वाप्रव्यथिताऽभवत् ।।6.119.1।।
explanation: Vaidehi heard the harsh horripilating words spoken by Rama in anger and was very much afflicted.

shloka_text: सातदश्रुतपूर्वंहिजनेमहतिमैथिली । श्रुत्वाभर्तृर्वचोरूक्षंलज्जयावनताभवत् ।।6.119.2।।
explanation: Then Mythili hearing her husband 's harsh words, in the presence of a large number of people, stayed bent with shyness.

shloka_text: प्रविशन्तीवगात्राणिस्वानिसाजनकात्मजा । वाक्षरैस्स्सैःसशल्येवभृशमाश्रूण्यवर्तयत् ।।6.119.3।।
explanation: As if pierced by those arrowlike words, Janaka's daughter shed tears excessively, shrinking into her own limbs.

shloka_text: ततोबाष्पपरिक्लिन्नंप्रमार्जन्तीस्वमाननम् । शनैर्गद्गदयावाचाभर्तारमिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.119.4।।
explanation: Thereafter, wiping her face clean from flowing tears she spoke slowly in a choked voice in broken words to her husband.

shloka_text: किंमामसदृशंवाक्यमीदृशंश्रोत्रदारुणम् । रूक्षंश्रावयसेवीर प्राकृतःप्राकृतमिव ।।6.119.5।।
explanation: "Hero! Why are you addressing me in such harsh unkind words in a rude manner, in a harsh tone like a common man?"

shloka_text: न तथास्मिमहाबाहो यथामामवगच्छसि । प्रत्ययंगच्छमेस्वेनचारित्रेणैवतेशपे ।।6.119.6।।
explanation: "O Mighty armed! I am not as you think of me, so also show me a proof of it in my past. I swear on my past."

shloka_text: पृथकस्त्रीणांप्रचारेणजातिंत्वंपरिशङ्कसे । परित्यजैनांशङ्कांतुयदितेऽहंपरीक्षिता ।।6.119.7।।
explanation: "You give up judging all womankind by the path followed by vulgar women. You give up these doubts if you have examined."

shloka_text: यदहंगात्रसम्पर्शंगतास्मिविशवाप्रभो । कामकारो न मेतत्रदैवंतत्रापराध्यति ।।6.119.8।।
explanation: "O Lord! I was helpless when Ravana contacted my limbs in the past. I was not acting according to my will. My fate is to be blamed and not me."

shloka_text: मदधीनंतुयत्तन्मेहृदयंत्वयिवर्तते । पराधीनेषुगात्रेषुकिंकरिष्याम्यनीश्वरी ।।6.119.9।।
explanation: "That mind which is under my control is my heart and it abides in you. What can I do about my limbs when I am at others' mercy?"

shloka_text: सहसम्वृद्धभावेनसंसर्गेण च मानद । यदितेऽहं न विज्ञाताहतातेनास्मिशाश्वतम् ।।6.119.10।।
explanation: "Honourable Rama! If I am not understood by you despite our growing up together with love and in spite of our intimate relationship, I am done forever."

shloka_text: प्रेषितस्तेमहावीरोहनुमानवलोककः । लङ्कास्थाहंत्वयाराजन्किंतदा न विसर्जिता ।।6.119.11।।
explanation: "King! When the great hero Hanuman was sent by you to find me in Lanka, why did you not leave me then."

shloka_text: प्रत्यक्षंवानरस्यास्यतद्वाक्यसमनन्तरम् । त्वयासन्त्यक्तयावीरत्यक्तंस्याजजीवितंमया ।।6.119.12।।
explanation: "O hero! Had you given me up immediately on receiving your message from Vanara I would have given up my life in the presence of Hanuman there itself."

shloka_text: न वृथातेश्रमोऽयंस्यात्संशयेन्यस्यजीवितम् । सुहृज्जनपरिक्लेशो न चायंविपुलस्तव ।।6.119.13।।
explanation: "O Life! If you had a doubt this exertion to you is wasteful. This fruitless hard work was perhaps not required on your part nor your friends."

shloka_text: त्वयातुनृपशार्दूलदोषमेवानुवर्तता । लघुनेवमनुष्येणस्त्रीत्वमेवपुरस्कृतम् ।।6.119.14।।
explanation: "O tiger among kings! You also gave up yourself to anger like a weak man and adopted womanliness"

shloka_text: अपदेशेनजनकादुत्पततिर्वसुथातलात् । ममवृत्तं च वृत्तज्ञबहुते न पुरस्कृतम् ।।6.119.15।।
explanation: My origin from the surface of the earth, under the guise of Janaka, and my conduct, O knower of events, has not been greatly esteemed.

shloka_text: न प्रमाणीकृतंपाणिर्भाल्येममनिपीडितः । ममभक्तिश्चशीलं च सर्वंतेपृष्ठतःकृतम् ।।6.119.16।।
explanation: "When in my young age you held my hand as a mark of acceptance (in our marriage), has it not been considered by you? Has my devotion, character and chastity not been taken into account?"

shloka_text: इतिब्रुवन्तीरुदतीबाष्पगद्गगभाषिणी । उवाचलक्ष्मणंसीतादीनंध्यानपरायणम् ।।6.119.17।।
explanation: Thus speaking, and weeping with tears, with choked throat, Sita was absorbed in her mind and piteous. She spoke to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: चितांमेकुरुसौमित्रेव्यवनस्यास्यभेषजम् । मिध्यापवादोपहतानाहंजीवितुमुत्सहे ।।6.119.18।।
explanation: "Saumithri! Cure for this sorrow is only pyre. Arrange for pyre as I do not desire to live with false reproaches."

shloka_text: अप्रीतेनगुणैर्भर्त्रात्यक्तायाजनसंसदि । याक्षमामेगतिर्गन्तुंप्रवेक्ष्येहव्यवाहनम् ।।6.119.19।।
explanation: "When my husband is not pleased with my virtues, renounces me in the gathering of people, I have only that path for me, that is, entering fire and offering myself as oblation."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुवैदेह्यालक्ष्मणःपरवीरहा । अमर्षवशमापन्नोराघवंसमुदैक्षत ।।6.119.20।।
explanation: Spoken in that manner by Vaidehi, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies, overcome with indignation looked at Raghava.

shloka_text: स विज्ञायततश्छन्दंरामस्याकारसूचितम् । चितांचकारसौमित्रिर्मतेरामस्यवीर्यवान् ।।6.119.21।।
explanation: Understanding Rama's indication from his looks, Saumithri started to prepare the earth for pyre.

shloka_text: नहिरामंतदाकश्चित्कालान्तकयमोपमम् । अनुनेतुमथोवक्तुंद्रष्टुंवाप्यशकत्सुहृत् ।।6.119.22।।
explanation: Indeed, no friend or dear could see or speak or make a request or pacify Rama. at that time.

shloka_text: अधोमुखंस्थितंरामंततःकृत्वाप्रदक्षिणम् । उपावर्ततवैदेहीदीप्यमानंहुताशनम् ।।6.119.23।।
explanation: Thereafter, Vaidehi, walking clockwise near Rama went round him in accordance with tradition and approached the pyre.

shloka_text: प्रणम्यदैवतेभ्यश्चब्राह्मणेभ्यश्चमैथिली । बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाचेदमुवाचानगिसमीपतः ।।6.119.24।।
explanation: Mythili greeted the gods and brahmanas with joined palms and went near fire and again joined her palms in greeting and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: यथामेहृदयंनित्यंनापसर्पतिराघवात् । तथालोकस्यसाक्षीमांसर्वतःपातुपावकः ।।6.119.25।।
explanation: "If it is true that my heart has never slid from Raghava at all, may the fire god protect me always and so also the world witness."

shloka_text: यथामांशुद्धचरितांदुष्टांजानातिराघवः । तथालोकस्यसाक्षीमांसर्वतःपातुपावकः ।।6.119.26।।
explanation: "If in Rama's view, I am of impeccable conduct and so also if what he is seeing is not known to be true, let the world witness and fire god protect me."

shloka_text: कर्मणामनसावाचायथानातिचराम्यहम् । राघवंसर्वधर्मज्ञंतथामांपातुपावकः ।।6.119.27।।
explanation: 'If I have ever acted or been unfaithful at heart or in speech and did not follow a righteous path with Rama, who is a knower of all virtues, let the fire god protect me."

shloka_text: आदित्योभगवान्वायुर्धिशश्चन्द्रस्तथैव च । अहश्चापितथासन्ध्येरात्रिश्चपृथिवीतथआ ।।6.119.28।। यथान्येऽपिविजानन्तितथाचारित्रसंयुताम् ।
explanation: "O gods! Supreme Aditya, wind god, god of the four quarters, and also by moon, and gods presiding during day, night, twilight and so also earth, know me as a woman of good character, let the fire god protect me that way."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वातुवैदेहीपरिक्रम्यहुताशनम् । विवेशज्वलनंदीप्तंनिःशङ्केनान्तरात्मना ।।6.119.29।।
explanation: Having spoken in that way, Vaidehi went round fire fearlessly, absorbed with in herself and entered the flaming and burning fire.

shloka_text: नश्चसुमहांस्तत्रबालवृद्धसमाकुलः ।।6.119.30।। ददर्शमैथिलींदीप्तांप्रविशन्तींहुताशनम् ।
explanation: Young and old assembled there, and the gathering of people witnessed Mythili entering the flaming and burning fire.

shloka_text: सातप्तनवहेमाभातप्तकाञ्चनभूषणा ।।6.119.31।। पपातज्वलनंदीप्तंसर्वलोकस्यसन्निधौ ।
explanation: Like freshly polished gold, like shining gold ornament, in the presence of the whole world she fell into flaming and glowing fire.

shloka_text: ददृशुस्तांविशालाक्षींपतन्तींहव्यवाहनम् ।।6.119.32।। सीतांसर्वाणिरूपाणिरुक्मवेदिनिभांतदा ।
explanation: All created beings and forms witnessed large eyed Sita descending on the golden altar, into the fire like goddess of fortune descending on her vehicle.

shloka_text: ददृशुस्तांमहाभागांप्रविशन्तींहुताशनम् ।।6.119.33।। सीतांकृत्स्नास्त्रयोलोकाःपुण्यामाज्याहुतीमिव ।
explanation: All the three worlds witnessed noble dark Sita entering the fire, like ghee offered to fire.

shloka_text: प्रचुक्रुशुःस्त्रियःसर्वास्तांदृष्टवाहव्यवाहवे ।।6.119.34।। पतन्तींसंस्कृतांमन्रन्स्सैर्वसोर्दारामिवाध्वरे ।
explanation: All the women who stood there fled, screaming on seeing Sita falling into fire, like the flow of ghee poured continuously into sacrificial fire reciting sacred verses by priests.

shloka_text: ददृशुस्तांत्रयोलोकादेवगन्धर्वदानवाः ।।6.119.35।। शस्तांपतन्तींनिरयेत्रिविवाद्धेवतामिव ।
explanation: All the Devas, Gandharvas and Danavas of the three worlds who witnessed her falling, extolled her as if goddess was falling from heaven into hell.

shloka_text: ततोहिदुर्मनाराम्श्रुत्वैवंवदतांगिरः । दध्यौमुहूर्तंधर्मात्माबाष्पव्याकुललोचनः ।।6.120.1।।
explanation: Then righteous Rama, hearing the wailing of the people, whose eyes were dimmed with tears, remained for a moment.

shloka_text: ततोवैश्रवणोराजायमश्चपितृभिःसह । सहस्राक्षश्चदेवेशोवरुणश्चजलेश्वरः ।।6.120.2।। षडर्धनयन्श्रीमान्महादेवोवृषध्वजः । कर्तासर्वस्यलोकस्यब्रह्माब्रह्मविदांवरः ।।6.120.3।। एतेसर्वेसमागम्यविमानैस्सूर्यसन्निभैः । आगम्यनगरींलङ्कामभिजग्मुश्चराघवम् ।।6.120.4।।
explanation: Then king Kubera, son of Vysravana, Yama, with Devas, Indra of thousand eyes, Varuna, the god of waters, glorious six eyed MahaDeva, who has bull on his banner, the creator of all the worlds, foremost of creators, Brahma, all of them reached Lanka city and went towards Raghava.

shloka_text: ततोवैश्रवणोराजायमश्चपितृभिःसह । सहस्राक्षश्चदेवेशोवरुणश्चजलेश्वरः ।।6.120.2।। षडर्धनयन्श्रीमान्महादेवोवृषध्वजः । कर्तासर्वस्यलोकस्यब्रह्माब्रह्मविदांवरः ।।6.120.3।। एतेसर्वेसमागम्यविमानैस्सूर्यसन्निभैः । आगम्यनगरींलङ्कामभिजग्मुश्चराघवम् ।।6.120.4।।
explanation: Then king Kubera, son of Vysravana, Yama, with Devas, Indra of thousand eyes, Varuna, the god of waters, glorious six eyed MahaDeva, who has bull on his banner, the creator of all the worlds, foremost of creators, Brahma, all of them reached Lanka city and went towards Raghava.

shloka_text: ततोवैश्रवणोराजायमश्चपितृभिःसह । सहस्राक्षश्चदेवेशोवरुणश्चजलेश्वरः ।।6.120.2।। षडर्धनयन्श्रीमान्महादेवोवृषध्वजः । कर्तासर्वस्यलोकस्यब्रह्माब्रह्मविदांवरः ।।6.120.3।। एतेसर्वेसमागम्यविमानैस्सूर्यसन्निभैः । आगम्यनगरींलङ्कामभिजग्मुश्चराघवम् ।।6.120.4।।
explanation: Then king Kubera, son of Vysravana, Yama, with Devas, Indra of thousand eyes, Varuna, the god of waters, glorious six eyed MahaDeva, who has bull on his banner, the creator of all the worlds, foremost of creators, Brahma, all of them reached Lanka city and went towards Raghava.

shloka_text: ततःसहस्ताभरणान्प्रगृह्यविपुलान्भुजान् । अब्रुवंस्त्रिदशश्रेष्ठाराघवंप्राञ्जलिंस्थितम् ।।6.120.5।।
explanation: Then foremost of gods adorned with ornaments in hands lifted up their long shoulders and greeted Raghava with joined palms and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: कर्तासर्वस्यलोकस्यश्रेष्ठोज्ञानवतांप्रभुः । उपेक्षसेकथंसीतांपतन्तींहव्यवाहने ।।6.120.6।। कथंदेवगणश्रेष्ठमात्मानंनावबुद्ध्यसे ।
explanation: "You are the creator of the entire world, knowledgeable and the foremost Lord of the host of gods. How did you keep watching Sita falling into fire'?

shloka_text: ऋतधामावसुःपूर्वंवसूनां च प्रजापतिः ।।6.120.7।। त्रयाणामपिलोकानामादिकर्तास्वयंप्रभुः ।
explanation: " Among the Vasus, you are the Rtadhama and the creator of the three worlds and the first creator and selfconstituted ruler."

shloka_text: रुद्राणामष्टमोरुद्रस्साध्यानामपिपञ्चमः ।।6.120.8।। अश्विनौचापिकर्णौतेसूर्यचन्द्रामसौदृशौ ।
explanation: "You are the eighth among the Rudras, fifth among the Sadhyas, two Aswins are your ears, and the sun and moon are your eyes."

shloka_text: अन्तेचादौ च लोकानांदृश्यसे च परन्तप ।।6.120.9।। उपेक्षसे च वैदेहींमानुषःप्राकृतोयथा ।
explanation: "O Tormentor of enemies! You are at the beginning and at the end of the world. You are looking like a common man would look at Sita, when she was falling into pyre."

shloka_text: इत्युक्तोलोकपालैस्तैस्स्वामीलोकस्यराघवः ।।6.120.10।। अब्रवीत्त्रिदशश्रेष्ठान्रामधर्मभृतांवरः ।
explanation: Rama the upholder of dharma and foremost and supreme god spoke after the ruler of the world had spoken to him.

shloka_text: आत्मानंमानुषंमन्येरामंदशरथात्मजम् ।।6.120.11।। सोऽहंयस्ययतश्चाहंभगववंस्तद्भ्रवीतुमे ।
explanation: "I am Dasharatha's son, a human and thinking to be Rama. Tell me O divine creator, from where and whence I am here."

shloka_text: इतिब्रुवाणंकाकुत्स्थंब्रह्माब्रह्मविदांवरः ।।6.120.12।। अब्रवीच्छ्रुणुमेवाक्यंसत्यंसत्यपराक्रम ।
explanation: To Kakuthsa who spoke that way, creator Brahma replied, "O Lord of truthful prowess, listen to my true submission."

shloka_text: भवान्नारायणोदेवःश्रीमांश्चक्रायुधःप्रभुः ।।6.120.13।। एकशृङ्गोवराहस्त्वंभूतभव्यसपत्नजित् ।
explanation: "You are the divine self, glorious Narayana himself, wielder of discus. You are having a single tusk and a divine boar, knower of past and present."

shloka_text: अक्षरंब्रह्मसत्यं च मध्येचान्ते च राघव ।।6.120.14।। लोकानांत्वंपरोधर्मोविष्वक्सेनश्चतुर्भुजः ।
explanation: "You are the imperishable Brahma in the midst or end, abiding in truth. You are dharma, all pervading four shouldered Vishnu in the world."

shloka_text: शार्ङ्गधन्वाहृषीकेशःपुरुषःपुरुषोत्तमः ।।6.120.15।। अजितःखङ्गदृग्विष्णुःकृष्णश्चैवमहाबलः ।
explanation: "You are the wielder of Sarang bow, subduer of enemies, a supreme person, never faced defeat, wielder of sword, Vishnu, Krishna also and mighty."

shloka_text: सेनानीर्ग्रामणीश्चत्वंत्वंबुद्धिस्त्वंक्षमादमः ।।6.120.16।। प्रभवश्चाप्ययश्चत्वमुपेन्द्रोमधुसूदनः ।
explanation: "You are the Karthikeya, the commander of army, village headman. You are the intellect, forbearance. You are the origin and end also. You are Vamana and destroyer of demon Madhu."

shloka_text: इन्द्रकर्मामहेन्द्रस्त्वंपद्मनाभोरणान्तकृत् ।।6.120.17।। शरण्यंशरणं च त्वामाहुर्दिव्यामहर्षयः ।
explanation: "You are spoken of as the creator of Indra, Mahendra himself, Padmanabha, who puts an end to combat. You are a wonderful great sage and refuge of seekers."

shloka_text: सहस्रशृङ्गोवेदात्माशरशीर्षोमहर्षभः ।।6.120.18।। त्वंत्रयाणांहिलोकानामादिकर्तास्वयम्प्रभुः । सिद्धानामपिसाध्यानामाश्रयश्चासिपूर्वजः ।।6.120.19।।
explanation: "You are the self of Vedas with its thousand branches and hundred divisions. You are the beginning of the three worlds and end. You are the selfshining. You are the Siddha among the achievers and their refuge as well as their protector."

shloka_text: सहस्रशृङ्गोवेदात्माशरशीर्षोमहर्षभः ।।6.120.18।। त्वंत्रयाणांहिलोकानामादिकर्तास्वयम्प्रभुः । सिद्धानामपिसाध्यानामाश्रयश्चासिपूर्वजः ।।6.120.19।।
explanation: "You are the self of Vedas with its thousand branches and hundred divisions. You are the beginning of the three worlds and end. You are the selfshining. You are the Siddha among the achievers and their refuge as well as their protector."

shloka_text: त्वम्यज्ञस्त्वंवषटकारस्त्वमोङ्कारःपरात्परः ।।6.120.20।। प्रभवंनिधनंवातेनोविदुःकोभवानिति ।
explanation: "You are the form of sacrifice ritual you are worshipped by Vasat. You are the syllable OM. Only the highest of the higher know you. You are without a beginning or end. Who you are is not known to Vedas also?"

shloka_text: दृश्यसेसर्वभूतेषुगोषु च ब्राह्मणेषु च ।।6.120.21।। दिक्षुसर्वासुगगनेपर्वतेषुनदीषु च ।
explanation: "You are seen in cows and brahmanas. You exist in all quarters, in the sky, mountains and rivers."

shloka_text: सहस्रचरण्श्रीमान् शतशीर्षस्सहस्रदृक् ।।6.120.22।। त्वंधारयसिभूतानिपृथिवीं च सपर्वताम् ।
explanation: "You are endowed with thousand feet, glorious, with hundred heads and hundred eyes, you sustain all beings, mountains and earth."

shloka_text: अन्तेपृथिव्याःसलिलेदृश्यसेत्वंमहोरगः ।।6.120.23।। त्रीन्लोकान्धारयन् राम देवगन्धर्वदानवान् ।
explanation: "Rama, at the dissolution of the earth you are seen to live on water and sustain a huge serpent. You are supporting the three worlds, the Devas, Gandharvas and Danavas."

shloka_text: अहंतेहृदयंरामजिह्वादेवीसरस्वती ।।6.120.24।। देवारोमाणिगात्रेषुब्रह्मणानिर्मिताःप्रभो ।
explanation: "Rama, all gods constitute your heart, Devi Saraswathi is your tongue, the gods created by Brahma are the hair on your limbs."

shloka_text: निमेषस्तेस्मृतारात्रिरुन्मेषोदिवसस्तथा ।।6.120.25।। संस्कारास्त्वभवन्वेदानैतदस्तित्वयाविना ।
explanation: "When you close your eyelids, it becomes night and when you open it becomes day. Your perfection in action are the Vedas. Without you, there is nothing."

shloka_text: जगत्सर्वंशरीरंतेस्थैर्यंतेवसुथातलम् ।।6.120.26।। अग्निःकोपःप्रसादस्तेसोम्श्रीवत्सलक्षणः ।
explanation: "The total world represents your body, your firmness represents the earth, your anger is fire, your grace is nobility, a sign of Srivatsa."

shloka_text: त्वयालोकास्त्रयःक्रान्ताःपुरास्वैर्विक्रमैस्त्रिभिः ।।6.120.27।। महेन्ध्रश्चकृतोराजाबलिंबद्ध्वासुदारुणम् ।
explanation: "Before you took the form of Trivikrama, and took three strides, occupied the three worlds and bound the dreadful king Bali you made Mahendra as king of heaven."

shloka_text: सीतालक्ष्मीर्भवान् विष्णुर्देवःकृष्णःप्रजापतिः ।।6.120.28।। वधार्थंरावणस्येहप्रविष्टोमानुषींतनुम् ।
explanation: "Sita is goddess Lakshmi while you are Vishnu. You are Krishna. You are the Lord of created beings. In order to put an end to Ravana, you entered the mortal body on earth."

shloka_text: तदिदंनस्त्वयाकार्यंकृतंधर्मभृतांवर ।।6.120.29।। निहतोरावणोरामप्रहृष्टोदिवमाक्रम ।
explanation: "Rama you are the supreme and upholder of dharma. The purpose for which you are born has been accomplished. Ravana is killed. You return to your abode happily."

shloka_text: अमोघंदेववीर्यंते न तेमोघाःपराक्रमाः ।।6.120.30।। अमोघंदर्शनंरामअमोघस्तवसंस्तवः ।
explanation: "O God! Your valour is wonderful, your prowess never goes in vain. Your sight is a blessing, and your praise is unfailing and not gone in vain."

shloka_text: अमोघास्तेभविष्यन्तिभक्तिमन्तोनराभुवि ।।6.120.31।। येत्वांदेवंध्रुवंभक्ताःपुराणंपुरुषोत्तमम् । प्राप्नुवन्तिसदाकामनिहलोकेपरत्र च ।।6.120.32।।
explanation: "Those mortals who are devoted to you, the supreme god, will be very successful. You are eternal, supreme being. Your devotees in this world and other world will always attain the desired results."

shloka_text: अमोघास्तेभविष्यन्तिभक्तिमन्तोनराभुवि ।।6.120.31।। येत्वांदेवंध्रुवंभक्ताःपुराणंपुरुषोत्तमम् । प्राप्नुवन्तिसदाकामनिहलोकेपरत्र च ।।6.120.32।।
explanation: "Those mortals who are devoted to you, the supreme god, will be very successful. You are eternal, supreme being. Your devotees in this world and other world will always attain the desired results."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वाशुभंवाक्यंपितामहसमीरितम् । अङ्केनादायवैदेहिमुत्पपातविभावसुः ।।6.121.1।।
explanation: On hearing creator Brahma's address to Rama, fire god emerged picking auspicious Vaidehi in his arms.

shloka_text: नविधूयाथचितांतांतुवैदेहींहव्यवाहनः । उत्तस्थौमूर्तिमानाशुगृहीत्वाजनकात्मजाम् ।।6.121.2।।
explanation: Then the fire god taking human form emerged from the fire immediately,with Janaka's daughter shaking off the fire sticks.

shloka_text: तरुणादित्यसङ्काशंतप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाम् । रक्ताम्बरधरांबालांसीलकुञ्चितमूर्थजाम् ।।6.121.3।। अक्लिष्टमाल्याभरणांतथारूपामनिन्दिताम् । ददौरामायवैदेहीमङ्केकृत्वाविभावसुः ।।6.121.4।।
explanation: Radiating like the rising sun, adorned with polished gold ornaments, wearing red coloured clothes, with beautiful black hair, wearing fresh flowers, being in the same young form as before, blameless Vaidehi was held in the arms of the fire god and presented to Rama.

shloka_text: तरुणादित्यसङ्काशंतप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाम् । रक्ताम्बरधरांबालांसीलकुञ्चितमूर्थजाम् ।।6.121.3।। अक्लिष्टमाल्याभरणांतथारूपामनिन्दिताम् । ददौरामायवैदेहीमङ्केकृत्वाविभावसुः ।।6.121.4।।
explanation: Radiating like the rising sun, adorned with polished gold ornaments, wearing red coloured clothes, with beautiful black hair, wearing fresh flowers, being in the same young form as before, blameless Vaidehi was held in the arms of the fire god and presented to Rama.

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तुतदारामंसाक्षीलोकस्यपावकः । एषातेराम वैदेहीपापमस्यां न विद्यते ।।6.121.5।।
explanation: Then the fire god who is a witness in the world, spoke to Rama," Here is your wife Vaidehi and she does not know any sin."

shloka_text: नैववाचा न मनसानैवबुद्ध्या न चक्षुषा । सुवृत्तावृत्तशौण्डीरन त्वामत्यचरच्छुभा ।।6.121.6।।
explanation: "Sita is of good conduct and auspicious. To you who are endowed with valour, she is faithful by speech, by intention of thought and intellect and even by glance."

shloka_text: रावणेनापनीतैषावीर्योसतिक्तेनरक्षसा । त्वयाविरहितादीनाविवशानिर्जनाद्वनात् ।।6.121.7।।
explanation: "When she was lonely, piteous, having no control, Rakshasa Ravana, who was proud of his valour abducted her from the forest when no one was there."

shloka_text: रुद्धाचान्तःपुरेगुप्तात्वच्छित्तात्वत्परायणा । रक्षिताराक्षसीभिश्चघोराभिर्घोरबुद्धिभिः ।।6.121.8।।
explanation: "She was separated from you yet fully absorbed in you. She was kept in the gynaeceum secretly and guarded by frightful and ruthless Rakshasa women."

shloka_text: प्रलोभ्यमानाविविधंभर्त्स्यमाना च मैथिली । नाचिन्तयततद्रक्षस्त्वद्गतेनान्तरात्मना ।।6.121.9।।
explanation: " Although Mythili was tempted, threatened also, she had set her mind on you only and not thought of that Rakshasa."

shloka_text: विशुद्धभावांनिष्पापांप्रतिगृह्णीष्वमैथिलीम् । न किञ्चिरभिधातव्याअहमाज्ञापयामिते ।।6.121.10।।
explanation: "Mythili is of untainted mind and a sinless one. Take her back without any reply, I am ordering you."

shloka_text: ततःप्रीतिमानारामःश्रुत्यैवंवदतांवरः । दध्यौमुहूर्तंधर्मात्माबाष्पव्याकुललोचनः ।।6.121.11।।
explanation: Then the supremely righteous Rama, who is good at speaking rejoiced at heart, his eyes filled with tears, thought for a moment.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोमहातेजाधृतिमान्दृढविक्रमः । उवाचत्रिदशश्रेष्ठंरामोधर्मभृतांवरः ।।6.121.12।।
explanation: Rama who is endowed with valour and firmness, and an upholder of dharma, a supreme person said to Brahma.

shloka_text: अवश्यंत्रिषुलोकेषु न सीतापापमर्हति । दीर्घकालोषिताहीयंरावणान्तःपुरेशुभा ।।6.121.13।।
explanation: "That Sita is auspicious and has surely not done any sin is known to three worlds. But she lived long in the gynaeceum of Ravana."

shloka_text: बालिशोखलुकामात्मारामोदशरथात्मजः । इतिवक्ष्यन्तिमांसन्तोजानकीमविशोध्यहि ।।6.121.14।।
explanation: "The people will surely say that mighty Dasharatha's son, Rama being lusty at heart has accepted Janaki without testing."

shloka_text: अनन्यहृदयांभक्तांमच्चित्तपरिवर्तिनीम् । अहमप्यवगच्छामिमैथिलींजनकात्मजाम् ।।6.121.15।।
explanation: "I also know that Mythili is ever coming around me with undivided love and is devoted to me."

shloka_text: इमामपिविशालाक्षींरक्षितांस्वेनतेजसा । रावणोनातिवर्तेतवेलामिवमहोदधिः ।।6.121.16।।
explanation: "Naturally she is selfeffulgent and can protect herself. Will Ravana be able to violate broad eyed Janakijust as the great ocean can't cross the bounds."

shloka_text: प्रत्ययार्थंतुलोकानांत्रयाणांसत्यसंश्रयः । उपेक्षेचापिवैदेहींप्रविशन्तींहुताशनम् ।।6.121.17।।
explanation: " As I am a follower of truth only, to convince the three worlds I was disregarding Vaidehi entering fire."

shloka_text: न हिशक्तःसुदुष्टात्मामनसापिहिमैथिलीम् । प्रधर्षयितुमप्राप्यांदीप्तामग्निशिखामिव ।।6.121.18।।
explanation: "It could not be possible for the evil minded Rakshasa to access or lay thoughts on Mythili who was glowing like flames of fire."

shloka_text: नेयमर्हतिचैश्वर्यंरावणान्तःपुरेशुभा । अनन्याहिमयासीताभास्करेणप्रभायथा ।।6.121.19।।
explanation: " Auspicious Sita would not have cared for the fortunes in the gynaeceum of Ravana. She is just like the radiance of the sun attached to the sun, attached to me and none other."

shloka_text: विशुद्धात्रिषुलोकेषुमैथिलीजनकात्मजा । न विहातुंमयाशक्याकीर्तिरात्ववतायथा ।।6.121.20।।
explanation: "Mythili is unsullied in the three worlds. Renouncing her is not feasible just as fame and as she is like my own self."

shloka_text: अवश्यं च मयाकार्यंसर्वेषांवोवचोहितम् । स्निग्धानांलोकनाधानामेवं च वदतांहितम् ।।6.121.21।।
explanation: "You are worship worthy of the world and loving people advising me in this way. Your words of good advice are good to all and for me. I will certainly follow."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वाशुभंवाक्यंराघवेणानुभाषितम् । ततश्शुभतरंवाक्यंव्याजहारमहेश्वरः ।।6.122.1।।
explanation: On hearing the sweet reply of Raghava, Lord Maheswara delivered an auspicious message.

shloka_text: पुष्कराक्ष महाबाहो महावक्ष परन्तप । दिष्ट्याकृतमिदंकर्मत्वयाधर्मभृतांवर ।।6.122.2।।
explanation: "O Lotuseyed, mighty armed, broadchested, a subduer of enemies, by good luck you have performed this action."

shloka_text: दिष्ट्यासर्वस्यलोकस्यप्रवृद्धंदारुणंतमः । अपावृत्तंत्वयासङ्ख्येरामरावणजंभयम् ।।6.122.3।।
explanation: "The dread of Ravana in all the worlds which caused gloom and fear has been fortunately removed by you in the war."

shloka_text: आश्वास्यभरतंदीनंकौसल्यां च यशस्विनीम् । कैकेयीं च सुमित्रां च दृष्टवालक्ष्मणमातरम् ।।6.122.4।। प्राप्यराज्यमयोध्यायांनन्दयित्वासुहृज्जनम् । इक्ष्वाकूणांकुलेवंशंस्थापयित्वामहाबल ।।6.122.5।। इष्टवातुरगमेधेनप्राप्यचानुत्तमंयशः । ब्राह्मणेभ्योधनंदत्त्वात्रिदिवंगन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.122.6।।
explanation: "Comforting piteous Bharata, illustrious Kausalya and Kaikeyi too, seeing Lakshmana's mother Sumithra, and attaining sovereignty, make relatives happy. Establishing Ikshvaku race, conducting horse sacrifice and satisfying the Lord attain highest renown by giving wealth in charity to brahmins. You, who are endowed with mighty prowess, deserve to go to heaven", said Lord Maheswara.

shloka_text: आश्वास्यभरतंदीनंकौसल्यां च यशस्विनीम् । कैकेयीं च सुमित्रां च दृष्टवालक्ष्मणमातरम् ।।6.122.4।। प्राप्यराज्यमयोध्यायांनन्दयित्वासुहृज्जनम् । इक्ष्वाकूणांकुलेवंशंस्थापयित्वामहाबल ।।6.122.5।। इष्टवातुरगमेधेनप्राप्यचानुत्तमंयशः । ब्राह्मणेभ्योधनंदत्त्वात्रिदिवंगन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.122.6।।
explanation: "Comforting piteous Bharata, illustrious Kausalya and Kaikeyi too, seeing Lakshmana's mother Sumithra, and attaining sovereignty, make relatives happy. Establishing Ikshvaku race, conducting horse sacrifice and satisfying the Lord attain highest renown by giving wealth in charity to brahmins. You, who are endowed with mighty prowess, deserve to go to heaven", said Lord Maheswara.

shloka_text: आश्वास्यभरतंदीनंकौसल्यां च यशस्विनीम् । कैकेयीं च सुमित्रां च दृष्टवालक्ष्मणमातरम् ।।6.122.4।। प्राप्यराज्यमयोध्यायांनन्दयित्वासुहृज्जनम् । इक्ष्वाकूणांकुलेवंशंस्थापयित्वामहाबल ।।6.122.5।। इष्टवातुरगमेधेनप्राप्यचानुत्तमंयशः । ब्राह्मणेभ्योधनंदत्त्वात्रिदिवंगन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.122.6।।
explanation: "Comforting piteous Bharata, illustrious Kausalya and Kaikeyi too, seeing Lakshmana's mother Sumithra, and attaining sovereignty, make relatives happy. Establishing Ikshvaku race, conducting horse sacrifice and satisfying the Lord attain highest renown by giving wealth in charity to brahmins. You, who are endowed with mighty prowess, deserve to go to heaven", said Lord Maheswara.

shloka_text: एषराजादशरथोविमानस्थःपितातव । काकुत्स्थमानुषेलोकेगुरुस्तवमहायशाः ।।6.122.7।।
explanation: "O Kakuthsa! Here is your father, teacher in the mortal world, king Dasharatha seated in the aerial car."

shloka_text: इन्द्रलोकंगतःश्रीमांस्त्वयापुत्रेणतारितः । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्रात्वमेममभिवादय ।।6.122.8।।
explanation: "Liberated by you, his son, the glorious emperor has reached Indra's world. You with your brother Lakshmana offer your salutations to him."

shloka_text: महदेववच्श्रुत्वाराघवःसहलक्ष्मणः । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राददर्शपितरंप्रभुः ।।6.122.9।।
explanation: Raghava along with Lakshmana offered salutations to his father seated on top of the aerial chariot after listening to Lord MahaDeva.

shloka_text: दीप्यमानंस्वयालक्ष्मविरजोऽम्भरधारिणम् । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राददर्शपितरंप्रभुः ।।6.122.10।।
explanation: Raghava with his younger brother Lakshmana saw his father who was effulgent, blazing and adorned in white clothes.

shloka_text: हर्षेणमहताविष्टोविमनस्थोमहीपतिः । प्राणैःप्रियतरंदृष्टवापुत्रंदशरथस्तदा ।।6.122.11।। आरोप्याङ्केमहबाहुर्वरासनगतःप्रभुः । बाहुभ्यांसम्परिष्वज्यततोवाक्यंसमाददे ।।6.122.12।।
explanation: Then Dasaratha, the ruler of the world, seated in an elevated seat in the aerial car, seeing his son who was dearer than life to him, extremely rejoiced and made Raghava sit on his lap, embraced him, and started speaking as follows.

shloka_text: हर्षेणमहताविष्टोविमनस्थोमहीपतिः । प्राणैःप्रियतरंदृष्टवापुत्रंदशरथस्तदा ।।6.122.11।। आरोप्याङ्केमहबाहुर्वरासनगतःप्रभुः । बाहुभ्यांसम्परिष्वज्यततोवाक्यंसमाददे ।।6.122.12।।
explanation: Then Dasaratha, the ruler of the world, seated in an elevated seat in the aerial car, seeing his son who was dearer than life to him, extremely rejoiced and made Raghava sit on his lap, embraced him, and started speaking as follows.

shloka_text: न मेस्वर्गोबहुमतस्सम्मानश्चसुरर्षभैः । त्वयारामविहीनस्यसत्यंप्रतिशृणोमिते ।।6.122.13।।
explanation: "Rama separated from you, even the suras and sages honouring me in heaven does not give me happiness. It is true and I promise."

shloka_text: अद्यत्वांनिहतामित्रंदृष्टवासम्पूर्णमानसम् । निस्तीर्णवनवासं च प्रीतिरासीत्परामम ।।6.122.14।।
explanation: "Today the enemies are killed, and you have completed the exile. I am fully satisfied and experiencing joyfulness on seeing you."

shloka_text: कैकेय्यायानिचोक्तानिवाक्यानिवदतांवर । तवप्रव्राजनार्थानिस्थितानिहृदयेमम ।।6.122.15।।
explanation: "Those utterances of Kaikeyi with a motive to send you on exile are still hurting my heart, O Best among speakers!"

shloka_text: त्वांतुदृष्टवाकुशलिनंपरिष्वज्यसलक्ष्मणम् । अद्यदुःखाद्विमुक्तोऽस्मिनीहारादिवभास्करः ।।6.122.16।।
explanation: "Seeing you with Lakshmana and embracing you makes me happy freed from grief just as the sun freed from mist."

shloka_text: तारितोऽहंत्वयापुत्र सुपुत्रेणमहात्मना । अष्टावक्रेणधर्मात्माकहोलोब्राह्मणोयथा ।।6.122.17।।
explanation: "Son! I am liberated by you today, my great son, just as Kahola who was set on righteousness was liberated by Ashtavakra."

shloka_text: इदानीं च विजानामियथासौम्य सुरेश्वरैः । वधार्थंरावणस्येहविहितंपुरुषोत्तम ।।6.122.18।।
explanation: "O gentle son! I did not know that the ruler of gods had sent you for the destruction of Ravana, O excellent one."

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थाखलुकौसल्यायात्वांराम गृहंगतम् । वनान्निवृत्तंसंहृष्टाद्रक्ष्यतेशत्रुसूदनम् ।।6.122.19।।
explanation: "Rama! Kausalya will see you, as an accomplished one, as a destroyer of enemies, on returning home from the forest and will be highly rejoiced."

shloka_text: सिद्धार्थाःखलुतेराम नरायेत्वांपुरींगतम् । राज्येचावाभिषिक्तं च द्रक्ष्यन्तेवसुधाधिपम् ।।6.122.20।।
explanation: "On reaching the city and consecrated in the kingdom as ruler of the world, people will see you as an accomplished person."

shloka_text: अनुरक्तेनबलिनाशुचिनाधर्मचारिणा । इच्छेयंत्वामहंद्रष्टुंभरतेनसमागतम् ।।6.122.21।।
explanation: "I desire to see you reunited with mighty Bharata who is pure and follower of dharma."

shloka_text: चतुर्दशसमास्सौम्यवनेनिर्यातितास्त्वया । वसतासीतयासार्धंलक्ष्मणेन च धीमता ।।6.122.22।।
explanation: "O Gentle Rama! Fourteen years have been spent in the forest with Sita and Lakshmana after my departure from life."

shloka_text: निवृत्तवनवासोऽसिप्रतिज्ञापूरितात्वया । रावणं च रणेहत्वादेवताःपरितोषिताः ।।6.122.23।।
explanation: "The period of your exile has been completed, my promise has been fulfilled in the battlefield and the gods have also gratified you."

shloka_text: कृतंकर्मयशश्श्लाघ्यंप्राप्तंतेशत्रुसूदन । भ्रातृभिःसहराज्यस्थोदीर्घमायुरवाप्नुहि ।।6.122.24।।
explanation: O destroyer of enemies, the praiseworthy deed and fame have been attained by you. May you attain a long life, established in the kingdom with your brothers.

shloka_text: इतिब्रुवाणंराजानंरामःप्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् । कुरुप्रसादंधर्मज्ञकैकेय्याभरतस्य च ।।6.122.25।।
explanation: Dasaratha having spoken to Rama, offered salutations with joined palms and said," You are righteous. Be gracious to Bharata and Kaikeyi also."

shloka_text: सपुत्रांत्वांत्यजामीतियदुक्ताकेकयीत्वया । स शापःकेकयींघोरस्सपुत्रां न स्पृशेत्प्रभो ।।6.122.26।।
explanation: "O Lord! You had spoken in such a way saying 'I disown a good son and Kaikeyi' and cursed. May that dreadful curse not touch your son and Kaikeyi," said Rama.

shloka_text: तथेति स महाराजोराममुक्त्वाकृताञ्जलिम् । लक्ष्मणं च परिष्वज्यपुनर्वाक्यमुवाच ह ।।6.122.27।।
explanation: The king (Dasharatha) saying 'so be it' and embracing Lakshmana again and saluting Rama spoke to Lakshmana as follows.

shloka_text: रामंशुश्रूषताभक्त्यावैदेह्यासहसीतया । कृतमममहाप्रीतिःप्राप्तंधर्मफलं च ते ।।6.122.28।।
explanation: "You have served with devotion to Rama and Sita and made me very happy. By this task you have earned the merit of righteousness."

shloka_text: धर्मंप्राप्स्यसिधर्मज्ञ यशश्चविपुलंभुवि । रामेप्रसन्नेस्वर्गं च महिमानंतथोत्तमाम् ।।6.122.29।।
explanation: "O knower of dharma! If Rama is pleased, extensive fame as well as heaven and supreme glory will be attained on this earth."

shloka_text: रामंशुश्रूषभद्रंतेसुमित्रानन्दवर्धन । रामस्सर्वस्यलोकस्यसुभेष्वभिरतःसदा ।।6.122.30।।
explanation: "O Lakshmana, the enhancer of Sumithra's joy, 'Be auspicious. Rama will always remain good in the service of the three worlds."

shloka_text: एतेसेन्द्रास्त्रयोलोकास्सिद्धाश्चपरमर्षयः । अभिगम्यमहात्मानमर्चन्तिपुरुषोत्तमम् ।।6.122.31।।
explanation: "This Indra and also Siddhas, supreme sages who are great souls pay respects to Rama and worship him."

shloka_text: एतत्तदुक्तमव्यक्तमक्षरंब्रह्मनिर्मितम् । देवानांहृदयंसौम्य गुह्यंरामःपरन्तप ।।6.122.32।।
explanation: "O Gentle! Rama, the tormentor of enemies is the unmanifest and imperishable secret, is Brahma alone. This is created by Brahma. It is the secret in the heart of gods."

shloka_text: अवाप्तंधर्मचरणंयशश्चविपुलंत्वया । एनंशुश्रूषताभक्त्यावैदेह्यासहसीतया ।।6.122.33।।
explanation: "Videha's Sita, you have also earned fame by serving Rama with devotion and following the righteous path."

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वालक्ष्मणंराजास्नुषांबद्धाञ्जलिंस्थिताम् । पुत्रीत्याभाष्यमधुरंशनैरेनामुवाच ह ।।6.122.34।।
explanation: Having spoken like that to Lakshmana, looking at the daughter in law standing there with folded palms, Dasaratha addressed her saying," Daughter", gently and sweetly and said.

shloka_text: कर्तव्यो न तुवैदेहीमन्युस्त्यागमिमंप्रति । रामेणेत्वद्विशुध्यर्थंकृतमेतद्धितैषिणा ।।6.122.35।।
explanation: "In the event of Rama abandoning you, resentment should not be shown in this way. It is your duty to endure. Rama himself has done this to prove your purity."

shloka_text: सुदुष्करमिदंपुत्रितवचारित्रलक्षणम् । कृतंयत्तेऽन्यनारीणांयशोह्यभिभविष्यति ।।6.122.36।।
explanation: "Daughter! that which you have done is a sign of your character. It is highly difficult to do. You will overshadow the future of other women."

shloka_text: न त्वंकामंसमाधेयाभर्तृशुश्रूषणंप्रति । अवश्यंतुमयावाच्यमेषतेदैवतंपरम् ।।6.122.37।।
explanation: "You need not be told about the service to your husband. Nevertheless, I am giving instruction. This Rama is supreme god for you."

shloka_text: इतिप्रतिसमादिश्यपुत्रौसीतां च राघवः । इन्द्रलोकंविमानेनययौदशरथोज्वलन् ।।6.122.38।।
explanation: Having admonished the two glowing sons, and Sita, Dasaratha went by aerial car to the world of Indra.

shloka_text: प्रतिप्रयातेकाकुत्स्थेमहेन्द्रःपाकशासनः । अब्रवीत्परमप्रीतोराघवंप्राञ्जलिंस्थितम् ।।6.123.1।।
explanation: Mahendra, the tamer of demon Paka, spoke very affectionately to Rama, who stood with joined palms before Dasharatha who had returned.

shloka_text: अमोघंदर्शनंराम तवास्माकंनरर्षभ । प्रीतियुक्ताःस्मतेनत्वंब्रूहियन्मनसेप्सितम् ।।6.123.2।।
explanation: "O Rama, a bull among men! Your sight was amazing, and we are happy. Please tell us the desire in your mind?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोमहेन्द्रेणप्रसन्नेनमहात्मना । सुप्रसन्नमनाहृष्टोवचनंप्राहराघवः ।।6.123.3।।
explanation: Gratified by Mahendra's words, Raghava was very happy and pleased, submitting to him as follows.

shloka_text: यदिप्रीतिस्समुत्पन्नामयितेविबुधेश्वर । वक्ष्यामिकुरुमेसत्यंवचनंवदतांवर ।।6.123.4।।
explanation: "O Lord of gods, you are one who is good at expression. If happiness has risen in, you please make my words true."

shloka_text: ममहेतोःपराक्रान्तायेगतायमसादनम् । तेसर्वेजीवितंप्राप्यसमुततिष्ठन्तुवानराः ।।6.123.5।।
explanation: "The Vanaras have fought for my cause and reached the abode of Yama. Make them rise up and get them back to life."

shloka_text: मत्कृतेविप्रयुक्तायेपुत्रैर्दारैश्चवानराः । तान्प्रीतमनसःसर्वान्द्रष्टुमिच्छामिमानद ।।6.123.6।।
explanation: "O honourable Indra! I wish to see all those Vanaras who are separated forever from their sons, and wives for my cause, delighted."

shloka_text: विक्रान्ताश्चापिशूराश्च न मृत्युंगणयन्ति च । कृतयत्नाविपन्नाश्चजीवयैनान् पुरन्दर ।।6.123.7।।
explanation: "They were valiant and courageous and did not care for life. They did their utmost, died and fell into adversity. Purandara! Get all of them back to life."

shloka_text: मत्प्रियेष्वभिरक्ताश्च न मृत्युंगणयन्तिये । त्वत्प्रसादात्समेयुस्तेवरमेतमहंवृणे ।।6.123.8।।
explanation: "They were fond of doing and not counted death. I seek your grace to give a boon to relieve all of them from death."

shloka_text: नीरुजोनिर्व्रणांश्चैवसम्पन्नबलपौरुषान् । गोलाङ्गूलांस्तथैवर्क्षांन्द्रष्टुमिच्छामिमानद ।।6.123.9।।
explanation: "Bestower of honour! I wish to see the longtailed Vanaras, and Bears rid of pain and death, enriched with strength and courage."

shloka_text: अकालेचापिपुष्पाणिमूलानि च फलानि च । नद्यश्चविमलास्तत्रतिष्ठेयुर्यत्रवानराः ।।6.123.10।।
explanation: "Let the location where Vanaras lived, have flowers, roots, fruits even though out of season and rivers with pure water."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुवचनंतस्यराघवस्यमहात्मनः । महेन्द्रःप्रत्युवाचेदंवचनंप्रीतिसंयुतम् ।।6.123.11।।
explanation: Hearing high souled Raghava's words, Mahendra in turn replied as follows.

shloka_text: महानयंवरस्तातयस्त्वयोक्तोरघूत्तम । वदिर्मयानोक्तपूर्वं च तस्मादेतद्भविष्यति ।।6.123.12।।
explanation: "Dear Rama! that which has been sought by you is great. Nothing has been revised by me in the past. Therefore, everything asked by you will be granted by this boon."

shloka_text: समुत्तिष्ठन्तुतेसर्वेहतायेयुधिराक्षसैः । ऋक्षाश्चसहगोपुच्छैर्निकृत्ताननबाहवः ।।6.123.13।।
explanation: "Let those long tailed Vanaras and Bears killed by Rakshasas, whose heads and arms had been severed, duly rise to life."

shloka_text: नीरुजोनिर्व्रणाश्चैवसम्पन्नबलपौरुषाः । समुत्थास्यन्तिहरयस्सुप्तानिद्राक्ष्येयथा ।।6.123.14।।
explanation: The monkeys duly healed, so also from death, enriched with strength and power rose up like rising from sleep.

shloka_text: सुहृद्भिर्बान्धवैश्चैवज्ञातिभिःस्वजनेन च । सर्वएवसमेष्यन्तिसम्युक्ताःपरयामुदा ।।6.123.15।।
explanation: "Let all in that way happily get reunited and highly rejoiced, with relatives, own clan and own people get united."

shloka_text: अकालेपुष्पशबलाःफलवन्तश्चपादपाः । भविष्यन्तिमहेष्वास नद्यश्चसलिलायुताः ।।6.123.16।।
explanation: The trees will be with blossoms and fruits even though it is unseasonal. The rivers will remain with waters.

shloka_text: सव्रणैःप्रथमंगात्रैरिदानींनिर्व्रणैस्समैः । ततस्समुत्थितास्सर्वेसुप्त्वेवहरियूथपाः ।।6.123.17।। बभूवुर्वानरास्सर्वेकिंन्वेतदितिविस्मिताः ।
explanation: All the army of Vanaras healed from the wounds, who were earlier covered with wounds and all the dead monkeys together rose up like getting up from sleep. They were amazed and started saying 'What happened'!

shloka_text: काकुत्स्थंपरिपूर्णार्थंदृष्टवासर्वेसुरोत्तमाः ।।6.123.18।। अब्रुवन्परमप्रीतास्स्तुत्वारामंसलक्ष्मणम् ।
explanation: Seeing all of them fully accomplished, the best of Suras very affectionately praised Rama and Lakshmana and spoke.

shloka_text: गच्छायोध्यामितोराजन्विसर्जय च वानरान् ।।6.123.19।। मैथिलींसान्त्वयस्वैनामनुरक्तांयशस्विनीम् ।
explanation: "King, return from here to Ayodhya leaving the monkeys. Reassure Mythili, who is very dear to you and an illustrious one."

shloka_text: भ्रारातरंभरतंपश्यत्वच्छोकाद्व्रतचारिणम् ।।6.123.20।। शत्रुघ्नं च महात्मानंमात्रूःसर्वाःपरन्तप । अभिषेचयचात्मानंपौरान्गत्वाप्रहर्षय ।।6.123.21।।
explanation: "Subduer of enemies! See your brothers, great souls Bharata and Satrughna devoted to you who are in grief due to your separation, see your mothers. Get consecrated. People will rejoice.

shloka_text: भ्रारातरंभरतंपश्यत्वच्छोकाद्व्रतचारिणम् ।।6.123.20।। शत्रुघ्नं च महात्मानंमात्रूःसर्वाःपरन्तप । अभिषेचयचात्मानंपौरान्गत्वाप्रहर्षय ।।6.123.21।।
explanation: "Subduer of enemies! See your brothers, great souls Bharata and Satrughna devoted to you who are in grief due to your separation, see your mothers. Get consecrated. People will rejoice.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वासहस्राक्षोरामंसौमित्रिणासह । विमानैःसूर्यसङ्काशैर्ययौहृष्टःसुरैःसह ।।6.123.22।।
explanation: The thousand eyed Indra, having spoken in that way to Rama and Saumithri, delighted, they returned to heaven in an aerial car with Suras.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य च काकुत्स्थ: सर्वांस्तांस्त्रिदशोत्तमान् । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्रावासमाज्ञापयत्तदा ।।6.123.23।।
explanation: Then greeting all the jewels among gods present there, accompanied by brother Lakshmana, Kakuthsa Rama ordered all Vanaras to go home and rest.

shloka_text: तांरात्रिमुषितंरामंसुखोत्थिमरिन्दमम् । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंजयंपृष्टवाविभीषणः ।।6.124.1।।
explanation: Rising in the morning after comfortable rest that night, Vibheeshana saw Rama the subduer of enemies, offered salutations and asked him of the victory and spoke.

shloka_text: स्नानानिचाङ्गरागाणिवस्त्राण्याभरणानि च । चन्दनानि च दिव्यानिमाल्यानिविविधानि च ।।6.124.2।। अलङ्कारविदश्चेमानार्यःपद्मनिभेक्षणाः । उपस्थितास्त्वांविधवत्स्नापयिष्यन्तिराघव ।।6.124.3।।
explanation: These lotus petal eyed women well versed in decoration are at your service. They are willing to assist you in bath. There are cosmetics for anointing your body, and clothes as well as ornaments, sandal paste etc. for you. There are garlands of several types here.

shloka_text: स्नानानिचाङ्गरागाणिवस्त्राण्याभरणानि च । चन्दनानि च दिव्यानिमाल्यानिविविधानि च ।।6.124.2।। अलङ्कारविदश्चेमानार्यःपद्मनिभेक्षणाः । उपस्थितास्त्वांविधवत्स्नापयिष्यन्तिराघव ।।6.124.3।।
explanation: These lotus petal eyed women well versed in decoration are at your service. They are willing to assist you in bath. There are cosmetics for anointing your body, and clothes as well as ornaments, sandal paste etc. for you. There are garlands of several types here.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुकाकुत्स्थ: प्रत्युवाचविभीषणम् । हरीन्सुग्रीवमुख्यांस्त्वंस्नानेनोपनिमन्त्रय ।।6.124.4।।
explanation: When Vibheeshana had spoken like that, Kakuthsa Rama replied 'you and monkeys headed by Sugriva bathe and come.'

shloka_text: स तुताम्यतिधर्मात्माममहेतोस्सुखोचितः । सुकुमारोमहाबाहोकुमार: सत्यसंश्रयः ।।6.124.5।।
explanation: "Mighty armed Bharata, righteous, giving up comforts of delicate body, resorting to truth is distressed for my cause."

shloka_text: तंविनाकैकयीपुत्रंभरतंधर्मचारिणम् । न मेस्नानंबहुमतंवस्त्राण्याभरणानि च ।।6.124.6।।
explanation: "When the virtuous Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, is not here, why do I need bath, why so many clothes and ornaments?"

shloka_text: एतत्पश्ययथाक्षिप्रंप्रतिगच्छामतांपुरीम् । अयोध्यांगच्छतोह्येषपन्थाःपरमदुर्गमः ।।6.124.7।।
explanation: " As it is very difficult to return to that city, think of the path to depart."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुकाकुत्स्थंप्रत्युवाचविभीषणः । अह्नात्वांप्रापयिष्यामितांपुरींपार्थिवात्मज ।।6.124.8।।
explanation: When Rama had spoken in the aforesaid manner, Vibheeshana replied" O son of the ruler of the earth! I will make you reach Ayodhya in a day."

shloka_text: पुष्पकंनामभद्रंतेविमानंसूर्यसन्निभम् । ममभ्रातुःकुबेरस्यरावणेनबलीयसा ।।6.124.9।। हृतंनिर्जित्यसङ्ग्रामेकामगंदिव्यमुत्तमम् । त्वदर्थंपालितंचेदंतिष्ठत्यतुलविक्रम ।।6.124.10।।
explanation: " An aerial car called Pushpaka, a wonderful one, which closely resembles the sun, which goes according to the will of the rider has been retained with me. It was earned by Ravana from my brother Kubera in a combat. Be auspicious. O Rama, of unequal prowess, this is retained for your cause."

shloka_text: पुष्पकंनामभद्रंतेविमानंसूर्यसन्निभम् । ममभ्रातुःकुबेरस्यरावणेनबलीयसा ।।6.124.9।। हृतंनिर्जित्यसङ्ग्रामेकामगंदिव्यमुत्तमम् । त्वदर्थंपालितंचेदंतिष्ठत्यतुलविक्रम ।।6.124.10।।
explanation: " An aerial car called Pushpaka, a wonderful one, which closely resembles the sun, which goes according to the will of the rider has been retained with me. It was earned by Ravana from my brother Kubera in a combat. Be auspicious. O Rama, of unequal prowess, this is retained for your cause."

shloka_text: तदिदंमेघसङ्काशंविमानमिहतिष्ठति । तेनयास्यसियानेनत्वमयोध्यांगतज्वरः ।।6.124.11।।
explanation: "This aerial car which waits here which resembles a cloud, will take you to Ayodhya. Be fearless."

shloka_text: अहंतेयुद्यनुग्राह्योयदिस्मरसिमेगुणान् । वसतावदिहप्राज्ञ यद्यस्तिमयिसौहृदम् ।।6.124.12।।
explanation: "O Wise Rama! If you permit me, and think kindly of me and remember me, and if you have affection for me stay here for a while."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्रावैदेह्याभार्ययासह । अर्चितस्सर्वकामैस्त्वंततोराम गमिष्यसि ।।6.124.13।।
explanation: "Rama, if all your requirements are met and you are satisfied, then you can start with your brother Lakshmana and wife Vaidehi."

shloka_text: प्रीतियुक्तस्यविहितांससैन्यःससुहृद्गणः । सक्रतियांराममेतावद्गृहेणत्वंमयोद्यताम् ।।6.124.14।।
explanation: "Rama, you should accept this hospitality from me at this one occasion, which has been arranged with affection to the army and host of friends."

shloka_text: प्रणयाद्भहुमानाच्चसौहार्देन च राघव । प्रसादायामिप्रेष्योऽहं न खल्वाज्ञापयामिते ।।6.124.15।।
explanation: "I request you out of my high esteem towards you and friendliness. I am your servant and not commanding you to do so."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्ततोरामःप्रत्युवाचविभीषणम् । रक्षसांवानराणां च सर्वेषामेवशृण्वताम् ।।6.124.16।।
explanation: On hearing Vibheeshana spoken in the aforesaid manner, Rama replied to the hearing of Rakshasas, Vanaras and all of them there.

shloka_text: पूजितोऽस्मित्वयावीर साचिव्येनपरन्तप । सर्वात्मना च चेष्टाभिःसौहार्देनपरेण च ।।6.124.17।।
explanation: "O tormentor of enemies! Hero, I am honoured by your friendship, by your efforts, and good heartedness of all of you."

shloka_text: न खल्वेतन्नकुर्यांतेवचनंराक्षसेश्वर । तंतुमेभ्रातरंद्रष्टुंभरतंत्वरतेमनः ।।6.124.18।।
explanation: "Ruler of Rakshasas! Not accepting your request will surely not happen. (but) my mind is hastening to see my brother Bharata."

shloka_text: मांनिवर्तयितुंयोऽसौचित्रकूटमुपागतः । शिरसायाचतोयस्यवचनं न कृतंमया ।।6.124.19।। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं च यशस्विनीम् । गुहं च सुहृदंचैवपौरान्जनपदैस्सह ।।6.124.20।।
explanation: "He came to Chitrakuta and on reaching bent down obediently, begged me by his words to return which I did not do. Kausalya, Sumithra and Kaikeyi and Guha also requested and the request of the citizens has been turned down.

shloka_text: मांनिवर्तयितुंयोऽसौचित्रकूटमुपागतः । शिरसायाचतोयस्यवचनं न कृतंमया ।।6.124.19।। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं च यशस्विनीम् । गुहं च सुहृदंचैवपौरान्जनपदैस्सह ।।6.124.20।।

shloka_text: अनुजानीहमांसौम्य पूजितोऽस्मिविभीषण । मन्युर्नखलुकर्तव्यःसखेत्वांचानुमानये ।।6.124.21।।
explanation: Noble Vibheeshana! Please permit me to go. I am honoured by you, my friend. Do not be angry or feel sorry. Let me do my duty."

shloka_text: उपस्थापयमेशीघ्रंविमानंराक्षसेश्वर । कृतकार्यस्यमेवासःकथंस्यादिहसम्मतः ।।6.124.22।।
explanation: "O Ruler of Rakshasas, send for my aerial car. My task has been completed here. How can I continue to stay here?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः । विमानसूर्यसङ्काशमाजुहावत्वरान्वितः ।।6.124.23।। ततःकाञ्चनचित्राङ्गंवैदूर्यमणिवेदिकम् । कूटागारैःपरिक्षिप्तंसर्वतोरजतप्रभम् ।।6.124.24।। पाण्डुराभिःपताकाभिर्ध्वजैश्चसमलङ्कृतम् । शोभितंकाञ्चनैर्हर्म्यैर्हेमपद्मविभूषितैः ।।6.124.25।। प्रकीर्णंकिङ्किणीजालैर्मुक्तामणिगवाक्षकम् । घण्टाजालैःपरिक्षिप्तंसर्वतोमधुरस्वनम् ।।6.124.26।। यन्मेरुशिखराकारंनिर्मितंविश्वकर्मणा । बृहभिर्भूषितंहर्म्यैर्मुक्तारजतशोभितैः ।।6.124.27।। तलैस्स्फटिकचित्राङ्गैदूर्यैश्चवरासनैः । महार्हास्तरणोपेतैरुपपन्नंमहाधनैः ।।6.124.28।।
explanation: Rama having spoken that way, Vibheeshana the king of Rakshasas, hurriedly ordered for the aerial car. The aerial car Pushpaka's parts were decorated with golden pictures, its altars were made of cat's eye gems, its squares were fixed with pillars and shone like silver. It was surrounded on all sides with yellow pennons. It had posts and flags all over, decorated with golden lotuses. The mansions in Pushpak had networks scattered with eyeholes set with pearls like windows. It had rows of bells, surrounded on all sides which had sweet sound. The Pushpak constructed by Viswakarma was huge like mountain Meru's peak and decorated with silver and pearls. Its pavements were fixed with crystals and encrusted with cat's eye gems. The seats were excellent and had rich coverings.
