shloka_text: उपस्थितमनाधृष्यंतद्विमानंमनोजवम् । निवेदयित्वारामायतस्थौतत्रविभीषणः ।।6.124.29।।
explanation: The Pushpak which could not be assailed was endowed with mind speed. Vibheeshana presented it to Rama and stood.

shloka_text: उपस्थितंतुतंकृत्वापुष्पकंपुष्पभूषितम् । अविदूरेस्थितोराममित्युवाचविभीषणः ।।6.125.1।।
explanation: Offering to Sri Rama the Pushpak decorated with flowers to sit, Vibheeshana stood at a distance and spoke.

shloka_text: स तुबद्धाञ्जलि: प्रह्वोविनीतोराक्षसेश्वरः । अब्रवीत्त्वरयोपेतःकिंकरोमीतिराघवम् ।।6.125.2।।
explanation: The Rakshasa king humbly offered salutation to Raghava with joined palms, quickly approached, and said, 'What is to be done'?

shloka_text: तमब्रवीन्महातेजालक्ष्मणस्योपशृण्वतः । विमृश्यराघवोवाक्यमिदंस्नेहपुरस्कृतम् ।।6.125.3।।
explanation: Highly brilliant Raghava was thinking and spoke in a friendly manner while Lakshmana was listening closely.

shloka_text: कृतप्रयत्नकर्माणःसर्वएववनेचराः । रत्नैरर्थैश्चविविधैस्सम्पूज्यन्तांविभीषण ।।6.125.4।।
explanation: "Let all the forest rangers (without exception) who made effort and fought be duly honoured with valuables and several luxuries."

shloka_text: सहामीभिस्त्वयालङ्कानिर्जिताराक्षसेश्वर । हृष्टैःप्राणभयंत्यक्त्वासङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिभिः ।।6.125.5।।
explanation: "This Lanka could be won with the help of these heroes who never turned back and fought in comb at without fear of life, O Lord of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: त इमेकृतकर्माणस्सर्वएववनौकसः । धनरत्नप्रदानेनकर्मैषांसफलंकुरु ।।6.125.6।।
explanation: "These forest rangers, all of them have struggled and accomplished success. Reward them with wealth and gems."

shloka_text: एवंसम्मानिताश्चेतेमानार्हमानदात्वया । भविष्यन्तिकृतज्ञेननिर्वृताहरियूथपाः ।।6.125.7।।
explanation: "These helpless monkey troops will be content with gratitude when rewarded, O respectable Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: त्यागिनंसङ्ग्रहीतारंसानुक्रोशंजितेन्द्रियम् । सर्वेततःअवगच्छन्तिसम्बोधयामिते ।।6.125.8।।
explanation: "If you do so you will be called as charitable and kind, not seizing wealth and as one who has gained over senses. That is why I am telling you for so long."

shloka_text: हीनंरतिगुणैस्सर्वैरभिहन्तारमाहवे । सेनात्यजतिसम्विग्नानृपतिंतंनरेश्वरा ।।6.125.9।।
explanation: "O Ruler of men, all the army will desert a king who is devoid of virtues, lowly and who is a destructor in the battlefield."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणवानरांस्तान्विभीषणः । रत्नार्थसंविभागेनसर्वानेवाभ्यपूजयत् ।।6.125.10।।
explanation: Vibheeshana honoured the Vanaras with gems and valuables, after Rama had spoken like that.

shloka_text: ततस्तान्पूजितान्दृष्टवारत्नार्थैर्हरियूथपान् । आरुरोहतदारामस्तद्विमानमनुत्तमम् ।।6.125.11।।
explanation: Then on seeing the monkey troops being honoured with excellent gemsRama ascended the aerial car.

shloka_text: ﻿अङ्केनादायवैदेहींलज्जमानांयशस्विनीम् । लक्ष्मणेनसहभ्रात्राविक्रान्तेवधनुष्मता ।।6.125.12।।
explanation: ﻿ Illustrious Vaidehi was abashed while she was taken in his(Hanuman’s) arms to Pushpalata while the valiant archers Lakshmana and his brother were there .

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्सविमानस्थःपूजयन्सर्वावानरान् । सुग्रीवं च महावीर्यंकाकुत्स्थसविभीषणम् ।।6.125.13।।
explanation: After duly honouring all the Vanaras, to Vibheeshana and highly courageous Sugriva, Kakuthsa spoke as follows.

shloka_text: मित्रकार्यंकृतमिदंभवद्भिद्वानरर्षभाः । अनुज्ञातामयासर्वेयथेष्टंप्रतिगच्छत ।।6.125.14।।
explanation: "Bull among Vanaras! Since this work of the friend has been accomplished, you too have my permission to go where you will."

shloka_text: यत्तुकार्यंवयस्येनस्निग्धेन च हितेन च । कृतंसुग्रीवतत्सर्वंभवताधर्मभीरुणा ।।6.125.15।। किष्किन्धांप्रतियाह्यावुस्वसैन्येनाभिसम्वृतः ।
explanation: All that has to be done by an affectionate friend in advanced age has been done, for the fear of unrighteousness. Now you may advance with your army to Kishkinda.

shloka_text: स्वराज्येवसलङ्कायांमयादत्तेविभीषण ।।6.125.16।। न त्वांधर्षयितुंशक्तास्सेन्द्राअपिदिवौकसः ।
explanation: "Vibheeshana, I would like to see you living like Indra bestowed with your own kingdom in Lanka. It will not be possible for even gods to attack you."

shloka_text: योध्यांप्रतियास्यामिराजधानींपितुर्मम ।।6.125.17।। अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामिसर्वानामन्त्रयामिवः ।
explanation: "I shall proceed to my father's capital, Ayodhya. You may permit me. Be auspicious. I take leave of you."

shloka_text: वमुक्तास्तुरामेणहरीन्द्राहरयस्तथा ।।6.125.18।। ऊचुःप्राञ्जलयस्सर्वेराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।
explanation: After Rama had spoken that way Sugriva, Vibheeshana, monkeys and Rakshasas saluted Rama and said as follows.

shloka_text: अयोध्यांगन्तुमिच्छामःसर्वन्नयतुनोभवान् ।।6.125.19।। मुद्युक्ताविचरिष्यामोवनान्युपननानि च ।
explanation: We wish to proceed with you to Ayodhya, and many wishes to go with you and range the forests and groves without anxiety.

shloka_text: दृष्टवात्वामभिषेकार्ध्रंकौसल्यामभिवाद्य च ।।6.125.20।। अचिरादगमिष्यामःस्वगृहान्नृपसत्तम ।
explanation: "O Jewel among kings! We will see you being consecrated and see Kausalya, greet her and return back to our own house."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्सधर्मात्मावानरैस्सविभीषणैः ।।6.125.21।। अब्रवीद्वानरान्रामस्ससुग्रीवविभीषणान् ।
explanation: Vibheeshana and Vanaras had spoken in that way, Rama replied to Sugriva, Vibheeshana and Vanaras as follows.

shloka_text: प्रिययतरंलब्दंयदहंससुहृज्जनः ।।6.125.22।। सर्वैर्भवद्भिःसहितःप्रीतिंलप्स्येपुरींगतः ।
explanation: "If I with my dear and near and together with you go to Ayodhya, that will give more happiness with Sita coming and with all of you."

shloka_text: क्षिप्रम् सुग्रीवविमानंवानरैस्सह ।।6.125.23।। त्वमप्यारोहसामात्योराक्षसेन्द्रविभीषण ।
explanation: Sugriva and the Vanaras, quickly ascended the aerial car. Vibheeshana, the king of Rakshasas and ministers all of them ascended.

shloka_text: ततः स पुष्पकंदिव्यंसुग्रीवस्सहवानरैः ।।6.125.24।। आरुरोहमुदायुक्तःसामात्यश्चविभीषणः ।
explanation: Then Sugriva with Vanaras happily joined the wonderful Pushpaka, Vibheeshana and his ministers also ascended.

shloka_text: तेष्वारूढेषुसर्वेषुकौबेरंपरमासनम् ।।6.125.25।। राघवणाभ्यनुज्ञातमुत्पपातविहायसम् ।
explanation: All the Vanaras and others having got into Kubera's Pushpaka with Rama's permission, it flew into the sky.

shloka_text: गतेनविमानेनहंसयुक्तेनभास्वता ।।6.125.26।। प्रहृष्टश्चप्रतीतश्चबभौरामःकुबेरवत् ।
explanation: Delighted and thrilled, Rama was flying in the sky in Pushpaka and with shining swans, he shone like Kubera.

shloka_text: अनुज्ञातंतुरामेणतद्विमानमनुत्तमम् । हंसयुक्तंमहानादमुत्पपातविहायसम् ।।6.126.1।।
explanation: Swan shaped Pushpak, unsurpassed in appearance like swan, making great sound started to fly with the permission of Rama.

shloka_text: पातयित्वाततश्चक्षुस्सर्वतोरघुनन्दनः । अब्रवीन्मैथिलींसीतांरामश्शशिनिभाननाम् ।।6.126.2।।
explanation: Then Rama, the enhancer of the joy of Raghu race casting his gaze at the moon like face of Sita spoke.

shloka_text: कैलासशिखराकारेत्रिकूटशिखरेस्थिताम् । लङ्कामीक्षस्ववैदेहीनिर्मितांविश्वकर्मणा ।।6.126.3।।
explanation: "Vaidehi, you may see the peak of Trikuta which stands on Lanka in the shape of the peak of Kailasa, constructed by Viswakarma."

shloka_text: एतदायोधनंपश्यमांसशोणितकर्दमम् । हरीणांराक्षसानां च सीते विशसनंमहत् ।।6.126.4।।
explanation: "Sita, see the mire of flesh and blood of the carnage of many monkeys and Rakshasas on the battlefield."

shloka_text: अत्रदत्तवरश्शेतेप्रमाथीराक्षसेश्वरः । तवहेतोर्विशालाक्षीनिहतोरावणोमया ।।6.126.5।।
explanation: "Broad eyed Sita, there lies Ravana, the Rakshasa king, who by virtue of boon tortured people, destroyed by me on your account."

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णोऽऽत्रनिहतःप्रहस्तश्चनिशाचरः । धूम्राक्षश्चात्रनिहतोवानरेणहनूमता ।।6.126.6।।
explanation: "There lies Kumbhakarna, the night ranger killed by me, Prahastha killed by Vanaras, DhumRaksha killed by Hanuman."

shloka_text: विद्युन्मालीहतश्चात्रसुषेणेनमहात्मना । लक्ष्मणेनेन्द्राजिच्चात्ररावणिर्निहितोरणे ।।6.126.7।।
explanation: "There lies Vidyunmali killed by great Sushena and Ravana's son Indrajith killed by Lakshmana in the battlefield."

shloka_text: अङ्गदेनात्रनिहतोविकटोनामराक्षसः । विरूपाक्षश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.126.8।। अकम्पनश्चनिहतोबलिनोऽऽन्ये च राक्षसाः । त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।6.126.9।।
explanation: "There is the Rakshasa by name Vikata killed by Angada, and Virupaksha (killed by Sugriva), Mahaparsva (killed by Rshaba), Mahodara (killed by Neela), Akampana and other Rakshasas, like Trisira killed by the mighty Hanuman and Atikaya by Lakshmana and Devanthaka (by Hanuman), and Naranthaka (by Angada)."

shloka_text: अङ्गदेनात्रनिहतोविकटोनामराक्षसः । विरूपाक्षश्चदुर्धर्षोमहापार्श्वमहोदरौ ।।6.126.8।। अकम्पनश्चनिहतोबलिनोऽऽन्ये च राक्षसाः । त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्चदेवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।6.126.9।।
explanation: "There is the Rakshasa by name Vikata killed by Angada, and Virupaksha (killed by Sugriva), Mahaparsva (killed by Rshaba), Mahodara (killed by Neela), Akampana and other Rakshasas, like Trisira killed by the mighty Hanuman and Atikaya by Lakshmana and Devanthaka (by Hanuman), and Naranthaka (by Angada)."

shloka_text: युद्धोन्मत्तश्चमत्तश्चराक्षसप्रवरावुभौ । निकुम्भश्चैवकुम्भश्चकुम्भकर्णात्मजौबली ।।6.126.10।। वज्रदंष्ट्रश्चदंष्ट्रश्चबहवोराक्षसाहताः । मकराक्षश्चदुर्धर्षोमयायुधिनिपातितः ।।6.126.11।।
explanation: "Yuddhonmatta and Matta both Rakshasa chiefs, and also Nikumbha and Kumbha, sons of Kumbhakarna (killed by Hanuman and Sugriva), and Vajradamshtra and Damshtra (killed by Angada), and Maha raksha who was difficult to encounter was killed by me in the combat."

shloka_text: युद्धोन्मत्तश्चमत्तश्चराक्षसप्रवरावुभौ । निकुम्भश्चैवकुम्भश्चकुम्भकर्णात्मजौबली ।।6.126.10।। वज्रदंष्ट्रश्चदंष्ट्रश्चबहवोराक्षसाहताः । मकराक्षश्चदुर्धर्षोमयायुधिनिपातितः ।।6.126.11।।
explanation: "Yuddhonmatta and Matta both Rakshasa chiefs, and also Nikumbha and Kumbha, sons of Kumbhakarna (killed by Hanuman and Sugriva), and Vajradamshtra and Damshtra (killed by Angada), and Maha raksha who was difficult to encounter was killed by me in the combat."

shloka_text: अकम्पनश्चनिहतःशोणिताक्षश्चवीर्यवान् । यूपाक्षश्चप्रजङ्घश्चनिहतौतुमहाहवे ।।6.126.12।।
explanation: " Akampana and also Sonithaksha got killed (by Dwivida), Yupaksha and Prajaghna (by Mainda and Angada)."

shloka_text: विद्युज्जिह्वोऽऽत्रनिहतोराक्षसोभीमदर्शनः । यज्ञशत्रुश्चनिहतःसुप्तघ्नश्चमहाबलः ।।6.126.13।। सूर्यशत्रुश्चनिहतोब्रह्मशत्रुस्तथापरः ।
explanation: "There is Vidyujihva of dreadful appearance killed, Yajnasatru killed, and the mighty Suptaghna. Similarly Suryasatru and another Rakshasa Brahmasatru were killed. in the shape of the peak of Kailasa."

shloka_text: अत्रमन्दोदरीनामभार्यातंपर्यदेवयत् ।।6.126.14।। सपत्नीनांसहस्रेणसाग्रेणपरिवारिता ।
explanation: "Mandodari wife of Ravana, with a thousand cowives is on the seashore surrounded by associates."

shloka_text: तत्तुदृश्यतेतीर्थंसमुद्रस्यवरानने ।।6.126.15।। यत्रसागरमुत्तीर्यतांरात्रिमुषितावयम् ।
explanation: "Charming lady! You see the seashore there, where we crossed the sea that night and slept on the shore."

shloka_text: एषसेतुर्मयाबद्धस्सागरेसलिलार्णवे ।।6.126.16।। तवहेतोर्विशालाक्षिनलसेतुःसुदुष्करः ।
explanation: "Broad eyed lady! Here is the bridge built on the salty ocean by Nala, which was difficult to construct."

shloka_text: पश्यसागरमक्षोभ्यंवैदेहिवरुणालयम् ।।6.126.17।। अपारमभिगर्जन्तंशङ्खशुक्तिसमाकुलम् ।
explanation: "Vaidehi! See the abode of Varuna, impenetrable and immeasurable roaring aloud filled with conches and oystershells."

shloka_text: हिरण्यनाभंशैलेन्द्रंकाञ्चनंपश्यमैथिलि ।।6.126.18।। विश्रमार्थंहनुमतोभित्त्वासागरमुत्थितम् ।
explanation: "Mythili! See the mountain which has golden caves and has risen cleaving the ocean in order to give place for Hanuman to rest while crossing the ocean."

shloka_text: एततत्कुक्षौसमुद्रस्यस्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् ।।6.126.19।। अत्रपूर्वंमहादेवःप्रसादमकरोत्प्रभुः ।
explanation: "Here is a cavern where all these troops were stationed before crossing the ocean. At this place Lord MahaDeva bestowed his grace on me (before construction of the bridge)."

shloka_text: एतत्तुदृश्यतेतीर्थंसागरस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.126.20।। सेतुबन्दइतिख्यातंत्रैलोक्येन च पूजितम् । एतत्पवित्रंपरमंमहापातकनाशनम् ।।6.126.21।। अत्रराक्षसराजोऽऽयमाजगामविभीषणः ।
explanation: "See in the middle of the ocean a very popular spot which is worshipped by the three worlds. It is supremely sacred known by the name Sethubandha. It is capable of removing all sins. It is here that the Rakshasa king Vibhishana came to meet me."

shloka_text: एतत्तुदृश्यतेतीर्थंसागरस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.126.20।। सेतुबन्दइतिख्यातंत्रैलोक्येन च पूजितम् । एतत्पवित्रंपरमंमहापातकनाशनम् ।।6.126.21।। अत्रराक्षसराजोऽऽयमाजगामविभीषणः ।
explanation: "See in the middle of the ocean a very popular spot which is worshipped by the three worlds. It is supremely sacred known by the name Sethubandha. It is capable of removing all sins. It is here that the Rakshasa king Vibhishana came to meet me."

shloka_text: एषासादृश्यतेसीतेकिष्किन्धाचित्रकानना ।।6.126.22।। सुग्रीवस्यपुरीरम्यायत्रवालीमयाहतः ।
explanation: "Sita! You are seeing the capital of Sugriva, beautiful Kishkinda with lovely woods. Vali was killed here by me."

shloka_text: अथदृष्टवापुरींसीताकिष्किन्धांवालिपालिताम् ।।6.126.23।। अब्रवीत्पश्रितंवाक्यंरामंप्रणतसाध्वसा ।
explanation: Sita, seeing the beautiful Kishkinda city ruled by Vali, gazing at Rama timidly and through love spoke to him.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवप्रियभार्याभिस्ताराप्रमुखतोनृप ।।6.126.24।। अन्येषांवानरेन्द्राणांस्त्रीभिःपरिवृताह्यहम् । गन्तुमिच्छेसहायोध्यांराजधानींत्वयासह ।।6.126.25।।
explanation: "O King! I wish to go to the capital city Ayodhya with you, Tara and other consorts of Sugriva, and other women, surrounded by Vanara chiefs."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवप्रियभार्याभिस्ताराप्रमुखतोनृप ।।6.126.24।। अन्येषांवानरेन्द्राणांस्त्रीभिःपरिवृताह्यहम् । गन्तुमिच्छेसहायोध्यांराजधानींत्वयासह ।।6.126.25।।
explanation: "O King! I wish to go to the capital city Ayodhya with you, Tara and other consorts of Sugriva, and other women, surrounded by Vanara chiefs."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोऽऽथवैदेह्याराघवःप्रत्युवाचताम् । एवमस्त्वितिकिष्किन्धांप्राप्यसंस्थाप्यराघवः ।।6.126.26।। विमानंप्रेक्ष्यसुग्रीवंवाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।
explanation: Vaidehi having spoken like that, Raghava replied her saying 'So be it' and Raghava stopped Pushpaka at Kishkinda, looked at Sugriva and spoke as follows.

shloka_text: ब्रूहिवानरशूर्दूल सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान् ।।6.126.27।। स्त्रीभिःपरिवृताःसर्वेह्ययोध्यांयान्तुसीतया ।
explanation: "Sugriva, the tiger among Vanaras! Let all Vanara chiefs and all women too collected, proceed to Ayodhya. Sita desires you to go."

shloka_text: तथात्वमपिसर्वाभिस्स्त्ीभिस्सहमहाबल ।।6.126.28।। अभित्वरस्वसुग्रीव गच्छामःप्लवगाधिप ।
explanation: Sugriva the head of the monkeys said" all of you including women also have to go quickly."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुसुग्रीवोरामेणामिततेजसा ।।6.126.29।। वानराधिपतिश्रीमांस्स्सैश्चसर्वैस्समावृतः । प्रविश्यान्तःपुरंशीघ्रंतारामुवदीक्ष्यसोऽऽब्रवीत् ।।6.126.30।।
explanation: When Rama of immeasurable energy had spoken in the aforesaid manner, Sugriva, the prosperous leader of Vanaras, surrounded by the monkeys entered the gynaeceum and looking at Tara said.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुसुग्रीवोरामेणामिततेजसा ।।6.126.29।। वानराधिपतिश्रीमांस्स्सैश्चसर्वैस्समावृतः । प्रविश्यान्तःपुरंशीघ्रंतारामुवदीक्ष्यसोऽऽब्रवीत् ।।6.126.30।।
explanation: When Rama of immeasurable energy had spoken in the aforesaid manner, Sugriva, the prosperous leader of Vanaras, surrounded by the monkeys entered the gynaeceum and looking at Tara said.

shloka_text: प्रिये त्वंसहनाराभिर्वानराणांमहात्मनाम् । राघवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातामैथिलीप्रियकाम्यया ।।6.126.31।।
explanation: "Dear, you have been duly permitted by the great soul Raghava to go to Ayodhya with Vanaras and also women to gratify Mythili."

shloka_text: त्वरत्वमभिगच्छामोगृह्यवानरयोषितः । अयोध्यांदर्शयिष्यामःसर्वादशरथस्त्रियः ।।6.126.32।।
explanation: "You hasten the wives of the monkeys. Taking all of them we shall depart to Ayodhya and shall see the consorts of Dasharatha."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्य व चःश्रुत्वातारासर्वाङ्गशोभना । आहूयचाब्रवीत्सर्वावानराणांतुयोषितः ।।6.126.33।।
explanation: On hearing Sugriva's words, Tara of beautiful limbs spoke, summoning all women.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातागन्तुंसर्वैश्चवानरैः । ममचापिप्रियंकार्यमयोध्यादर्वनेन च ।।6.126.34।।
explanation: Sugriva has permitted all the Vanaras to go with wives and look at Ayodhya." Dear, some kindly act will be done for us also."

shloka_text: प्रवेशंचैवरामस्यपौरजानपदैस्सह । विभूतिंचैवसर्वासांस्त्रीणांदशरथस्य च ।।6.126.35।।
explanation: "We shall see with all the citizens, Rama's entry into Ayodhya, Dasharatha's women and the glory of Ayodhya, everything."

shloka_text: तारयाचाभ्यनुज्ञातास्सर्वावानरयोषितः । नेपथ्यविधिपूर्वंतुकृत्वाचापिप्रदक्षिणम् ।।6.126.36।। अध्यारोहन्विमानंतत्सीतादर्शनकाङ्क्षया ।
explanation: Duly permitted, all Vanaras wives and Tara also decorated themselves according to tradition, went around the Pushpaka and looked forward to seeing Sita.

shloka_text: ताभिःसहोत्थितंशीघ्रंविमानंप्रेक्ष्यराघवः ।।6.126.37।। ऋष्यमूकसमीपेतुवैदेहींपुनरब्रवीत् ।
explanation: After Rama and all others ascended and Pushpaka rose up speedily over the Rshyamuka, gazing at Rshyamuka, Rama spoke toVaidehi.

shloka_text: दृश्यतेऽऽसौमहान्सीते सविद्युदिवतोयदः ।।6.126.38।। ऋष्यमूकोगिरिवरःकाञ्चनैर्धातुभिर्वृतः ।
explanation: "Sita! Rshyamuka is seen covered with streaks of gold minerals, glowing like clouds with lightning."

shloka_text: त्राहंवानरेन्द्रेणसुग्रीवेणसमागतः ।।6.126.39।। समयश्चकृतःसीतेवधार्थंवालिनोमया ।
explanation: "Here is the place I met the Vanara king Sugriva and made an agreement to put an end to Vali."

shloka_text: एषासादृश्यतेपम्पानलिनीचित्रकानना ।।6.126.40 ।। त्वयाविहीनोयत्राहंविललापसुदुःखितः ।
explanation: "Here is seen lovely woods and Pampa waters. I lamented here, separated from you."

shloka_text: अस्यास्तीरेमयादृष्टाशबरीधर्मचारिणी ।।6.126.41।। अत्रयोजनबाहुश्चकबन्धोनिहतोमया ।
explanation: "On its bank (Pampa) I saw Sabari, who was following the righteous path. Kabhanda, of eight miles long arms, was killed by me."

shloka_text: दृश्यतेऽऽसौजनस्थानेश्रीमान्सीते वनस्पतिः ।।6.126.42।। जटायुश्चमहातेजास्तवहेतोर्विलासिनि । रावणेनहतोयत्रपक्षिणांप्रवरोबली ।।6.126.43।।
explanation: "Sita, here is Janasthana, where a mighty tree is seen. Oh sportive lady! There the exceptionally strong and highly energetic vulture Jatayu got killed by Ravana on account of you."

shloka_text: दृश्यतेऽऽसौजनस्थानेश्रीमान्सीते वनस्पतिः ।।6.126.42।। जटायुश्चमहातेजास्तवहेतोर्विलासिनि । रावणेनहतोयत्रपक्षिणांप्रवरोबली ।।6.126.43।।
explanation: "Sita, here is Janasthana, where a mighty tree is seen. Oh sportive lady! There the exceptionally strong and highly energetic vulture Jatayu got killed by Ravana on account of you."

shloka_text: खरश्चनिहतोयत्रदूषणश्चनिपातितः । त्रिशिराश्चमहावीर्योमयाबाणैरजिह्मगैः ।।6.126.44।। एतत्तदाश्रममदमस्माकंवरवर्णिनि । पर्णशालातथाचित्रादृश्यतेशुभदर्शने ।।6.126.45।। यत्रत्वंराक्षसेन्द्रेणरावणेनहृताबलात् ।
explanation: "O excellent lady! Here is the location where Khara was killed by my straight going arrows and Dushana had fallen. Here is our hermitage covered with leaves, a well known site. It is from here that Ravana had borne you away forcibly."

shloka_text: खरश्चनिहतोयत्रदूषणश्चनिपातितः । त्रिशिराश्चमहावीर्योमयाबाणैरजिह्मगैः ।।6.126.44।। एतत्तदाश्रममदमस्माकंवरवर्णिनि । पर्णशालातथाचित्रादृश्यतेशुभदर्शने ।।6.126.45।। यत्रत्वंराक्षसेन्द्रेणरावणेनहृताबलात् ।
explanation: "O excellent lady! Here is the location where Khara was killed by my straight going arrows and Dushana had fallen. Here is our hermitage covered with leaves, a well known site. It is from here that Ravana had borne you away forcibly."

shloka_text: एषागोदावरीरम्याप्रसन्नसलिलाशुभा ।।6.126.46।। अगस्त्यस्याश्रमश्चैव दृश्यते कदलीवृतः ।
explanation: "Here is an auspicious, beautiful Godavari with pure water. Here is also seen the hermitage of Agastya surrounded by banana plants."

shloka_text: दीप्तशैवाश्रमोह्येषसुतीक्षणस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.126.47।। वैदेहिदृश्यतेचैवशरभङ्गाश्रमोमहान् । उपयातःसहस्राक्षोयत्रशक्रःपुरन्दरः ।।6.126.48।।
explanation: "See the glowing hermitage of the great sage Sutikshna. Vaidehi, see Sarabhanga's hermitage here, where the thousand eyed Indra, the destroyer of citadels (Purandara) had come."

shloka_text: दीप्तशैवाश्रमोह्येषसुतीक्षणस्यमहात्मनः ।।6.126.47।। वैदेहिदृश्यतेचैवशरभङ्गाश्रमोमहान् । उपयातःसहस्राक्षोयत्रशक्रःपुरन्दरः ।।6.126.48।।
explanation: "See the glowing hermitage of the great sage Sutikshna. Vaidehi, see Sarabhanga's hermitage here, where the thousand eyed Indra, the destroyer of citadels (Purandara) had come."

shloka_text: एतेहितापसावासादृश्यन्तेतनुमध्यमे । अत्रिःकुलपतिर्यत्रसूर्यवैश्वानरोपमः ।।6.126.49।।
explanation: "There are seen the abodes of ascetics. Here was seen by you hermitage of Atri (whose wife Anasuya you had seen) glowing like sun and fire."

shloka_text: अस्मिन् देशेमहाकायोविराधोनिहतोमया । अत्रसीते त्वयादृष्टवातापसीधर्मचारिणी ।।6.126.50।।
explanation: "In these countries was a Rakshasa, called Viradha of gigantic size who was killed by me. There is an ascetic woman Anasuya practicing virtues whom you saw."

shloka_text: असौसुतनुशैलेन्द्रत्रकूटःप्रकाशते । अत्रमांकैकयीपुत्रप्रसादयितुमागतः ।।6.126.51।।
explanation: "O Charming lady! See the best of the mountains Chitrakuta shining there. Kaikeyi's son had come here to request me to accept the kingdom."

shloka_text: एषासायमुनारम्यादृश्यतेचित्रकानना । भरद्वाजाश्रमःश्रीमान्दृश्यतेचैषमैथिलि ।।6.126.52।।
explanation: "Mythili! See the wonderful woods bordering beautiful Yamuna. Glorious hermitage of Bharadwaja is seen there."

shloka_text: इयं च दृश्यतेगङ्गापुण्यात्रिपथगानदी । नानाद्विजगणाकीर्णासम्प्रपुष्पितकानना ।।6.126.53।।
explanation: "There is a sacred river Ganga where several kinds of birds frequent and are filled with trees full of blossoms."

shloka_text: शृङ्गिबेरपुरंचैतद्गुहोयत्रसखामम । एषासादृश्यतेसीतेसरयूर्यूपमालिनी ।।6.126.54।। नानातरुशताकीर्णासम्प्रपुष्पितकानना ।
explanation: "See this Sringaberipura. Their lives my friend Guha. Sita, several kinds of trees full of blossoms are seen on the bank of Sarayu. See the rows of sacrificial posts."

shloka_text: एषासादृश्यतेसीतेराजधानीपितुर्मम ।।6.126.55।। अयोध्यांकुरुवैदेहिप्रणामंपुनरागता ।
explanation: Sita! My father's capital Ayodhya is seen. We have come here. Offer your salutations."

shloka_text: ततस्तेवानरास्सर्वेराक्षसास्सविभीषणाः ।।6.126.56।। उत्पत्योत्पत्यसम्हृष्टास्तांपुरींददृशुस्तदा ।
explanation: Then all the Vanaras, Vibheeshana too and Rakshasas got up and saw the delightful city.

shloka_text: पूर्णेचतुर्दशेवर्षेपञ्चम्यांलक्ष्मणाग्रजः । भरद्वाजाश्रमंप्राप्यववन्देनियतोमुनिम् ।।6.127.1।।
explanation: After the fourteenth year of exile, on the fifth day of the bright half of lunar month Sri Rama and Lakshmana reached Bharadwaja's hermitage. They bent their heads down (as a mark of respect) and offered salutations.

shloka_text: सोऽपृच्छदभिवाद्यैनंभरद्वाजंतपोधनम् । शृणोषिकच्चिद्भगवन्सुभिक्षानायमंपुरे ।।6.127.2।। कच्चित्सयुक्तोभरतोजीवन्त्यपि च मातरः ।
explanation: Rama and Lakshmana having greeted sage Bharadwaja who had asceticism as his wealth, enquired, saying, "Have you heard that crops have been good, Bharata is active, and mothers are doing well in Ayodhya?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तुरामेणभरद्वाजोमहामुनिः ।।6.127.3।। प्रत्युवाचरघुश्रेष्ठंस्मितपूर्वंप्रहृष्टवत् ।
explanation: When Rama had spoken that way to the great sage, Bharadwaja was delighted and with a smiling look replied.

shloka_text: पङ्कदिग्धस्तुभरतोजटिलस्त्वांप्रतीक्षते ।।6.127.4।। पादुकतेपुरस्कृत्यसर्वं च कुशलंगृहे ।
explanation: "Bharata is without attention to his body, wearing matted locks, placing your wooden sandals in front expecting you in the house. All is well at Ayodhya."

shloka_text: त्वांपुराचीरवसनंप्रविशन्तंमहावनम् ।।6.127.5।। स्त्रीतृतीयंच्युतंराज्याद्धर्मकामं च केवलम् । पदातिंत्यक्तसर्वस्वंपितुर्वचनकारिणम् ।।6.127.6।। सर्वभोगैःपरित्यक्तंस्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम् । दृष्टातुकरुणापूर्वंममासीत्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.127.7।। कैकेयीवचनेयुक्तंवन्यमूलफलाशिनम् ।
explanation: "Rama! You, who are victorious in winning enemies, have earlier on account of father's words, intent on following father's words, accepting Kaikeyi's words, went with Lakshmana and Sita, clad in bark clothes, giving up kingdom and all possessions, like heaven set out on foot and entered huge forest, living on roots and fruits of the forest. Seeing you, compassion arose in me."

shloka_text: त्वांपुराचीरवसनंप्रविशन्तंमहावनम् ।।6.127.5।। स्त्रीतृतीयंच्युतंराज्याद्धर्मकामं च केवलम् । पदातिंत्यक्तसर्वस्वंपितुर्वचनकारिणम् ।।6.127.6।। सर्वभोगैःपरित्यक्तंस्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम् । दृष्टातुकरुणापूर्वंममासीत्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.127.7।। कैकेयीवचनेयुक्तंवन्यमूलफलाशिनम् ।
explanation: "Rama! You, who are victorious in winning enemies, have earlier on account of father's words, intent on following father's words, accepting Kaikeyi's words, went with Lakshmana and Sita, clad in bark clothes, giving up kingdom and all possessions, like heaven set out on foot and entered huge forest, living on roots and fruits of the forest. Seeing you, compassion arose in me."

shloka_text: त्वांपुराचीरवसनंप्रविशन्तंमहावनम् ।।6.127.5।। स्त्रीतृतीयंच्युतंराज्याद्धर्मकामं च केवलम् । पदातिंत्यक्तसर्वस्वंपितुर्वचनकारिणम् ।।6.127.6।। सर्वभोगैःपरित्यक्तंस्वर्गच्युतमिवामरम् । दृष्टातुकरुणापूर्वंममासीत्समितिञ्जयः ।।6.127.7।। कैकेयीवचनेयुक्तंवन्यमूलफलाशिनम् ।
explanation: "Rama! You, who are victorious in winning enemies, have earlier on account of father's words, intent on following father's words, accepting Kaikeyi's words, went with Lakshmana and Sita, clad in bark clothes, giving up kingdom and all possessions, like heaven set out on foot and entered huge forest, living on roots and fruits of the forest. Seeing you, compassion arose in me."

shloka_text: साम्प्रतंतुसमृद्धार्थंसमित्रगणबान्धवम् ।।6.127.8।। समीक्ष्यविजितारिं च समाभूप्रतीतिरुत्तमा ।
explanation: "I am happy to see you coming to me, who have completed the task and won the enemies and after successful completion, you are meeting relatives and friends."

shloka_text: सर्वं च सुखदुःखंतेविदितंममराघव । यत्त्वयाविपुलंप्राप्तंजनस्थान्नवधादिकम् ।।6.127.9।।
explanation: "Raghava, while you were sojourning at Janasthana, you experienced joy and sorrow abundantly all that is known to me."

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणार्थेनियुक्तस्यरक्षतःसर्वतापसान् । रावणेनहृताभार्याबभूवेयमनिता ।।6.127.10।।
explanation: "This irreproachable wife of yours was abducted by Ravana while you were engaged with the protection of all ascetics and entrusted with the care of brahmanas."

shloka_text: मारीचदर्शनंचैवसीतोन्मधनमेव च । कबन्धदर्शनंचैवसम्पाभिगमनंतथा ।।6.127.11।। सुग्रीवेण च तेसख्यंयथावालीहतस्त्वया । मार्गणंचैववैदेह्याःकर्मवातात्मजस्य च ।।6.127.12।। विदितायां च सीतायांनलसेतुर्यथाकृतः । यथाचादीपितालङ्काप्रहृष्टैर्हरियूथपैः ।।6.127.13।। सपुत्रबान्दवामात्यःसबलःसहावाहनः । यथा च निहतःसंख्येरावणोबलदर्पितः ।।6.127.14।। यथा च निहतेतस्मिन् रावणेदेवकण्टके । समागमश्चत्रिदशैर्यथादत्तश्चतेवरः ।।6.127.15।। सर्वंममैतद्विदितंतपसाधर्मवत्सल । सम्पतन्ति च मेशिष्याःप्रवृत्ताख्याःपुरीमितः ।।6.127.16।।
explanation: "O, you are a lover of rightful duty, seeing Maricha, searching Sita, appearance of Kabhanda, your going to Pampa, making friendship with Sugriva, killing of Vali, searching for Vaidehi, finding of Sita by the son of wind god, and his action, setting fire to Lanka, finding of Nalasethu, construction of bridge, delighted Vanaras, destruction of sons, relatives and vehicles of Ravana's army, killing of Ravana who was a thorn in the eyes of god, coming of Brahma and gods, bestowing a boon and all that is known to me by the power of my penance. My disciples in Ayodhya communicated to me."

shloka_text: मारीचदर्शनंचैवसीतोन्मधनमेव च । कबन्धदर्शनंचैवसम्पाभिगमनंतथा ।।6.127.11।। सुग्रीवेण च तेसख्यंयथावालीहतस्त्वया । मार्गणंचैववैदेह्याःकर्मवातात्मजस्य च ।।6.127.12।। विदितायां च सीतायांनलसेतुर्यथाकृतः । यथाचादीपितालङ्काप्रहृष्टैर्हरियूथपैः ।।6.127.13।। सपुत्रबान्दवामात्यःसबलःसहावाहनः । यथा च निहतःसंख्येरावणोबलदर्पितः ।।6.127.14।। यथा च निहतेतस्मिन् रावणेदेवकण्टके । समागमश्चत्रिदशैर्यथादत्तश्चतेवरः ।।6.127.15।। सर्वंममैतद्विदितंतपसाधर्मवत्सल । सम्पतन्ति च मेशिष्याःप्रवृत्ताख्याःपुरीमितः ।।6.127.16।।

shloka_text: अहमप्यद्यतेदद्मिवरंशस्त्रभृतांवर । अर्घ्यंप्रतिगृहाणेदमयोध्यांश्वोगमिष्यसि ।।6.127.17।।
explanation: "Jewel among the wielders of weapons! Now you take this water, and I shall bestow a boon to you. After taking my blessings you proceed to Ayodhya."

shloka_text: तस्यतच्छिरसावाक्यंप्रतिगृह्यनृपात्मजः । बाढमित्येवसम्हृष्टःश्रीमान्वरमयाचत ।।6.127.18।।
explanation: Glorious son of emperor obeying the words of Bharadwaja bending his head in reverence requested for that boon.

shloka_text: अकालफलिनोवृक्षास्सर्वेचापिमधुस्रवाः । फलान्यमृतगन्धीनिबहूनिविविधानि च ।।6.127.19।। भवन्तुमार्गेभगवन्नयोध्यांप्रतिगच्छतः ।
explanation: "O divine sage! Let all the trees bear fruits out of season of several kinds of many sweet and juicy, tasting nectar appear on our way as we proceed to Ayodhya."

shloka_text: तथेति च प्रतिज्ञातेवचनात्समनन्तरम् ।।6.127.20।। अभवन्पादपास्तत्रस्वर्गपादपसन्निभाः ।
explanation: When Bharadwaja promised saying, 'Be it so' and the trees on all sides grew like heavenly trees.

shloka_text: पुष्फलाःफलिनश्चासवनिपुष्पाःपुष्पशालिनः ।।6.127.21।। शुष्कास्समग्रपत्रास्तेनगाश्चैवमधुस्रवाः । सर्वतोयोजनास्त्रिस्रोगच्छतामभवंस्तदा ।।6.127.22।।
explanation: "Then while we were proceeding for three yojanas on all sides the trees that did not have fruits started bearing fruits, trees that did not have blossoms started having blossoms and the trees that dried up developed leaves and began to shed honey."

shloka_text: अयोध्यांतुसमालोक्यचिन्तयामासराघवः । प्रियकामःप्रियंरामस्ततस्त्वरितविक्रमः ।।6.128.1।।
explanation: There upon Raghava who was quick in exhibiting his prowess started thinking with his friends looking at Ayodhya (from Pushpaka).

shloka_text: चिन्तयित्वाततोदृष्टिंवानरेषुन्यपातयत् । उवाचधीमांस्तेजस्वीहनूमन्तंप्लवङ्गमम् ।।6.128.2।।
explanation: Then wise and energetic Rama, thinking, casting his attention on the Vanaras, spoke to Hanuman.

shloka_text: अयोध्यांत्वरितोगत्वाशीघ्रंप्लवगसत्तम । जानीहिकछचित्कुशलीजनोनृपतिमन्दिरे ।।6.128.3।।
explanation: "Chief of monkeys! Going quickly to the king's mansion in Ayodhya try to find out about the wellbeing of the people."

shloka_text: शृङ्गबेरिपुरंप्राप्यगुहंगहनगोचरम् । निषादाधिपतिंब्रूहिकुशलंवचनान्मम ।।6.128.4।।
explanation: "Go to Sringaberipuram which is seen from the sky, meet Guha the leader of Nishadas and tell him of my inquiry and wellbeing."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुमांकुशलिनमरोगंविगतज्वरम् । भविष्यतिगुहःप्रीतस्सममात्मसमस्सखा ।।6.128.5।।
explanation: "He will be very happy to hear that I am in good health free from anxiety. He is equal to me and my friend."

shloka_text: अयोध्यायाश्चतेमार्गंप्रवृत्तिंभरतस्य च । निवेदयिष्यतिप्रीतोनिषादाधिपतिर्गुहः ।।6.128.6।।
explanation: "Dear Guha, the king of Nishadas will tell you the way to Ayodhya and Bharata's nature."

shloka_text: भरतस्तुत्वयावाच्यःकुशलंवचनान्मम । सिद्धार्थंशंसमांतस्मैसभार्यंसहलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.128.7।।
explanation: "Please tell Bharata my words of inquiry of his wellbeing and that having accomplished my purpose I returned with my wife and Lakshmana."

shloka_text: हरणंचापिवैदेह्यारावणेनबलीयसा । सुग्रीवेण च सम्वादंवालिनश्चवधंरणे ।।6.128.8।।
explanation: "O powerful Hanuman! you may tell him of the abduction of Vaidehi by Ravana, my friendship with Sugriva and killing of Vali in combat."

shloka_text: मैथिल्यन्वेषणंचैवयथाचाधिगतात्वया । लङ्घयित्वामहातोयमापगापतिमव्ययम् ।।6.128.9।।
explanation: "You may tell him of the search for Mythili by you, crossing the vast never decreasing stretch of water, leaping across and finding Sita."

shloka_text: उपयानंसमुद्रस्यसागरस्य च दर्शनम् । यथा च कारितस्सेतूरावणश्चयथाहतः ।।6.128.10।।
explanation: " Also, about my going near ocean and his (Ocean god) appearance before me, construction of the bridge killing of Ravana."

shloka_text: वरदानंमहेन्द्रेणब्रह्मणावरुणेन च । महादेवप्रसादाच्छपित्राममसमागमम् ।।6.128.11।।
explanation: " About Mahendra accompanied by Brahma and Varuna bestowing boon and by the grace of Mahadeva and meeting my father."

shloka_text: उपयातं च मांसौम्य भरतायनिवेदय । सहराक्षसराजेनहरीणामीश्वरेण च ।।6.128.12।।
explanation: "Gentle Hanuman! tell him about my coming with Sugriva the king of Vanaras, and king of Rakshasas, Vibheeshana."

shloka_text: जित्वाशत्रुगणान्रामःप्राप्यचानुत्तमंयशः । उपायानंसमृद्धार्थस्सहमित्रैर्महाबलैः ।।6.128.13।।
explanation: "Tell him that Rama , after conquering hosts of enemies, attaining unsurpassed fame, accomplished his purpose, has returned with mighty friends."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वायमाकारंभजतेभरतस्ततः । स च तेवेदितव्यःस्यात्सर्वंयच्छापिमांप्रति ।।6.128.14।।
explanation: "Listening to Bharata, and seeing his form, expression on hearing this news and knowing his intent, checking all this you may return to me."

shloka_text: ज्ञेयाःसर्वे च वृत्तान्ताःभरतस्येङ्गितानि च । तत्त्वेनमुखवर्णेनदृष्ट्याव्याभाषितेन च ।।6.128.15।।
explanation: " All the information, everything to be known by his facial colour, expression, by his speech, his intention to be ascertained truly."

shloka_text: सर्वकालसमृद्धंहिहस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलम् । पितृपैतामहंराज्यंकस्यनावर्तयेन्मनः ।।6.128.16।।
explanation: "Whose mind will not be tempted at the abundance of elephants and horses of father's and grandfather's kingdom?"

shloka_text: सङ्गत्याभरत्श्रीमान् राज्येनार्थीस्वयंभवेत् । प्रशास्तुवसुधांसर्वामखिलांरघुनन्दनः ।।6.128.17।।
explanation: "If the glorious Bharata who is an enhancer of the joy of Raghus having enjoyed the kingdom for long himself, let him rule all the entire earth it is laudable."

shloka_text: तस्यबुद्धिं च विज्ञायव्यवसायं च वानर । यावन्नदूरंयाताःस्मक्षिप्रमागन्तुमर्हसि ।।6.128.18।।
explanation: "Hanuman, making an effort to know his mind you ought to come quickly before we go too far a distance."

shloka_text: इतिप्रतिसमादिष्टोहनूमान्मारुतात्मजः । मानुषःधारयनृपमयोध्यांत्वरितोययौ ।।6.128.19।।
explanation: Commanded like that Hanuman went speedily taking human form to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: अतोत्पपातवेगेनहनूमान्मारुतात्मजः । गरुत्मानिववेगेनजिघृक्षन्पन्नगोत्तमम् ।।6.128.20।।
explanation: Then Hanuman rose up just like Garuda who goes at great speed to vanquish the best of serpents.

shloka_text: लङ्घयित्वापितृपथंविहगेन्द्रालयंशुभम् । गङ्गायमुनयोर्भीमंसमतीत्यसमागमम् ।।6.128.21।। शृङ्गबेरपुरंप्राप्यगुहमासाद्यवीर्यवान् । स वाचाशुभयाहृष्टोहनुमानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.128.22।।
explanation: Valiant Hanuman, flying through the course of the birds, through the auspicious path of the wind god, leaping across Ganga and Yamuna, reached Sringaberipuram, saw Guha, rejoiced and thus spoke charming words.

shloka_text: लङ्घयित्वापितृपथंविहगेन्द्रालयंशुभम् । गङ्गायमुनयोर्भीमंसमतीत्यसमागमम् ।।6.128.21।। शृङ्गबेरपुरंप्राप्यगुहमासाद्यवीर्यवान् । स वाचाशुभयाहृष्टोहनुमानिदमब्रवीत् ।।6.128.22।।
explanation: Valiant Hanuman, flying through the course of the birds, through the auspicious path of the wind god, leaping across Ganga and Yamuna, reached Sringaberipuram, saw Guha, rejoiced and thus spoke charming words.

shloka_text: सखातुतवकाकुत्स्थोरामस्सत्यपराक्रमः । ससीतस्सहसौमित्रिस्सत्वांकुशलमब्रवीत् ।।6.128.23।।
explanation: "Your friend Rama, truly valiant one, with his wife Sita, with Lakshmana conveys his welfare to you."

shloka_text: पञ्चमीमद्यरजनीमुषित्वावचनान्मुनेः । भरद्वाजाभ्यनुज्ञातंद्रक्ष्यस्यद्यैवराघवम् ।।6.128.24।।
explanation: "Tomorrow that is the fifth lunar day, after spending the night at sage Bharadwaja's hermitage Raghava will see you."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वामहातेजास्सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः । उत्पपातमहावेगाद्वेगवान्विचारयन् ।।6.128.25।।
explanation: Highly energetic Hanuman, was thrilled, overcome with happiness (that he was able to communicate to Guha) and unmindful of the fatigue, being endowed with speed and swift movement, went up.

shloka_text: सोऽपश्यद्रामतीर्थं च नदींवालुकिनींतथा । वरूथींगोमतींचैवभीमंशालवनंतथा ।।6.128.26।। प्रजाश्चबहुसाहस्रीःस्फीतान्जनपदानपि ।
explanation: He saw waters associated with Parasurama, and rivers Valukini, Varuthini, and Gomathi so also fearful woods of Sala trees and thousands of people, numerous kingdoms on the way.

shloka_text: सःगत्वादूरमध्वानंत्वरितःकपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.128.27।। आससादद्रुमान् फुल्लान्नन्दिग्रामसमीपगान् । स्त्रीभिस्सपुत्रैर्वृद्धैश्चरममाणैःस्वलङ्कृतैः । सुराधिपस्योपवनेयथाचैत्ररथेद्रुमान् ।।6.128.28।।
explanation: Speeding on the journey for long distance Hanuman, the elephant among the monkeys saw women, their sons, grand sons and the old, well decorated, sporting in the gardens which were like the gardens of Indra and the gardens of Chaitraratha of Kubera with trees and close to Nandigrama, he saw trees full of blossoms.

shloka_text: सःगत्वादूरमध्वानंत्वरितःकपिकुञ्जरः ।।6.128.27।। आससादद्रुमान् फुल्लान्नन्दिग्रामसमीपगान् । स्त्रीभिस्सपुत्रैर्वृद्धैश्चरममाणैःस्वलङ्कृतैः । सुराधिपस्योपवनेयथाचैत्ररथेद्रुमान् ।।6.128.28।।

shloka_text: क्रोशमात्रेत्वयोध्यायाचशीरकृष्णाजिनम्बरम् ।।6.128.29।। ददर्शभरतंदीनंकृशमाश्रमवासिनम् । जटिलंमलदिग्धाङ्गंभ्रातृव्यसनकर्शितम् ।।6.128.30 । फलमूलाशिनंदान्तंतापसंधर्मचारिणम् । समुन्नतजटाभारंवल्कलाजिनवाससम् ।।6.128.31।। नियतंभावितात्मानंब्रह्मर्षिसमतेजसम् । पादुकेतेपुरस्कृत्यप्रशासन्तंवसुन्धराम् ।।6.128.32 । चातुर्वर्णस्यलोकस्यत्रातारंमहतोभयात् । उपस्थितममात्यैश्चशुचिभिश्चपुरोहितैः ।।6.128.33।। बलमुख्यैश्चयुक्तैश्चकाषायाम्बरदारिभिः ।
explanation: ' At a distance of two miles from Ayodhya, Hanuman saw Bharata living in a hermitage wearing black skin of antelope, emaciated, piteous, not clean, without any cleaning of the body, affected by the separation from brother living on fruits and roots, subdued practicing austerities, following righteous practices disciplined, soul purified by meditation, like Brahmarshi in brilliance, placing your sandals on ground ruling the earth, all the four divisions free from fear on all sides, protecting the upright, ministers, priests, united with chiefs of army stood there' (reported Hanuman).

shloka_text: क्रोशमात्रेत्वयोध्यायाचशीरकृष्णाजिनम्बरम् ।।6.128.29।। ददर्शभरतंदीनंकृशमाश्रमवासिनम् । जटिलंमलदिग्धाङ्गंभ्रातृव्यसनकर्शितम् ।।6.128.30 । फलमूलाशिनंदान्तंतापसंधर्मचारिणम् । समुन्नतजटाभारंवल्कलाजिनवाससम् ।।6.128.31।। नियतंभावितात्मानंब्रह्मर्षिसमतेजसम् । पादुकेतेपुरस्कृत्यप्रशासन्तंवसुन्धराम् ।।6.128.32 । चातुर्वर्णस्यलोकस्यत्रातारंमहतोभयात् । उपस्थितममात्यैश्चशुचिभिश्चपुरोहितैः ।।6.128.33।। बलमुख्यैश्चयुक्तैश्चकाषायाम्बरदारिभिः ।

shloka_text: नहितेराजपुत्रंतंचीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरम् ।।6.128.34।। परिभोक्तुंव्यवस्यन्तिपौरावैधर्मवत्सलाः ।
explanation: The citizens (of Ayodhya) who were lovers of virtues did not enjoy any luxuries, not inclined for pleasures as the prince himself was wearing bark of trees and skin of antelope.

shloka_text: तम्धर्ममिवधर्मज्ञंदेहवन्तमिवापरम् ।।6.128.35।। उवाचप्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यंहनूमान्मारुतात्मजः ।
explanation: Maruti's son Hanuman offered salutations to Bharata who was seen like a supreme body of dharma itself as if he was another form of dharma.

shloka_text: वसन्तंदण्डकारण्येयंत्वंचीरजटाधरम् ।।6.128.36।। अनुशोचसिकाकुत्स्थं स त्वांकौशलमब्रवीत् ।
explanation: "That Kakuthsa for whom you are worrying and living as he was at Dandaka forest with bark tree fabric, and matted hair sent me to tell you about his welfare."

shloka_text: प्रियमाख्यामितेदेवशोकंत्यजसुदारुणम् ।।6.128.37।। अस्मिन्मुहूर्तेभ्रात्रात्वंरामेणसहसङ्गतः ।
explanation: "O God! I will tell you some pleasant news. Give up that terrible grief. You will be reunited with your brother this moment."

shloka_text: निहत्यरावणंरामःप्रतिलभ्य च मैथिलीम् ।।6.128.38।। उपयातिसमृद्धार्थःसहमित्रैर्महाबलैः ।
explanation: "Rama killed Ravana and recovered Mythili. He, having accomplished the purpose, is coming with his mighty friends."

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणश्चमहातेजावैदेही च यशस्विनी ।।6.128.39।। सीतासमग्रारामेणमहेन्द्रेणशचीयथा ।
explanation: "Lakshmana who is endowed with extraordinary energy, and illustrious Sita accompanied by Rama will be coming as Sachi with Mahendra."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोहनुमताभरतःकैकयीसुतः ।।6.128.40।। पपातसहसाहृष्टोहर्षान्मोहमुपागमत् ।
explanation: Hanuman having said that, the son of Kaikeyi was delighted and instantly fell on ground and lost senses by extreme joy.

shloka_text: ततोमुहूर्तादुत्थायप्रत्याश्वस्य च राघवः ।।6.128.41।। हनूमन्तमुवाचेदंभरतःप्रियवादिनम् ।
explanation: Bharata got up in a moment and saw Hanuman, who is sweet in speech said this.

shloka_text: अशोकजैःप्रीतिमयैःकपिमालिङ्ग्यसम्भ्रमात् ।।6.128.42।। सिषेचभरतःश्रीमान्विपुलैरश्रुबिन्धुभिः ।
explanation: Glorious Bharata was overwhelmed with joy and embraced Hanuman and copious tears of joy born of joy.

shloka_text: देवोवामानुषोवात्वमनुक्रोशादिहागतः ।।6.128.43।। प्रियाख्यानस्यतेसौम्यददामिब्रुवतःप्रियम् । गवांशतसहस्रं च ग्रामाणां च शतंपरम् ।।6.128.44।। सकुण्डलाश्शुभाचाराभार्याःकन्यास्तुषोडश । हेमवर्णास्सुनासोरूश्शशिसौम्याननाःस्त्रियः ।।6.128.45।। सर्वाभरणसम्पन्नास्सम्पन्नाःकुलजातिभिः ।
explanation: "O Gentle Hanuman! You have come here with great compassion. Are you God or a human being? For the sweet tidings brought by you to me, I will bestow a hundred thousand cows, hundred best villages, sixteen virgin women of good conduct as wives with earrings, with shapely noses, full moon like face, golden complexioned, decked with ornaments and rich women."

shloka_text: देवोवामानुषोवात्वमनुक्रोशादिहागतः ।।6.128.43।। प्रियाख्यानस्यतेसौम्यददामिब्रुवतःप्रियम् । गवांशतसहस्रं च ग्रामाणां च शतंपरम् ।।6.128.44।। सकुण्डलाश्शुभाचाराभार्याःकन्यास्तुषोडश । हेमवर्णास्सुनासोरूश्शशिसौम्याननाःस्त्रियः ।।6.128.45।। सर्वाभरणसम्पन्नास्सम्पन्नाःकुलजातिभिः ।
explanation: "O Gentle Hanuman! You have come here with great compassion. Are you God or a human being? For the sweet tidings brought by you to me, I will bestow a hundred thousand cows, hundred best villages, sixteen virgin women of good conduct as wives with earrings, with shapely noses, full moon like face, golden complexioned, decked with ornaments and rich women."

shloka_text: देवोवामानुषोवात्वमनुक्रोशादिहागतः ।।6.128.43।। प्रियाख्यानस्यतेसौम्यददामिब्रुवतःप्रियम् । गवांशतसहस्रं च ग्रामाणां च शतंपरम् ।।6.128.44।। सकुण्डलाश्शुभाचाराभार्याःकन्यास्तुषोडश । हेमवर्णास्सुनासोरूश्शशिसौम्याननाःस्त्रियः ।।6.128.45।। सर्वाभरणसम्पन्नास्सम्पन्नाःकुलजातिभिः ।

For the sweet tidings brought by you to me, I will bestow a hundred thousand cows, hundred best villages, sixteen virgin women of good conduct as wives with earrings, with shapely noses, full moon like face, golden complexioned, decked with ornaments and rich women."

shloka_text: बहूनिनामवर्षाणिगतस्यसुमहद्वनम् । शृणोम्यहंप्रीतिकरंममनाथस्यकीर्तनम् ।।6.129.1।।
explanation: "I am hearing the good news of my Lord returning from the forest, who was living in the great forest for many years."

shloka_text: कल्याणीबतगाथेयंलौकिकीप्रतिभातिमे । एतिजीवन्तमानन्दोनरंवर्षशतादपि ।।6.129.2।।
explanation: The saying that "If a human being lives (long), for a hundred years, he will experience joy" is true and auspicious.

shloka_text: राघवस्यहरीणां च कथमासीत्समागमः । कस्मिन् देशेकिमाश्रित्यतत्त्वमाख्याहिपृच्छतः ।।6.129.3।।
explanation: "How did the alliance of monkeys happen with Rama? Where and why? I am asking you. Tell me truly."

shloka_text: स पृष्टोराजपुत्रेणबृश्यांसमुपवेशितः । आचचक्षेततस्सर्वंरामस्यचरितंवने ।।6.129.4।।
explanation: Prince Bharata seated comfortably on kusa grass asked Hanuman for all the history that happened in the forest, wishing to hear from him.

shloka_text: यथाप्रव्राजितोरामोमातुर्दत्तौवरौतव । यथापुत्रशोकेनराजादशरथोमृतः ।।6.129.5।। यथादूतैस्त्वमानीतस्तूर्णंराजगृहात्प्रभो । त्वयायोध्यांप्रविष्टेनयथाराज्यं न चेप्सितम् ।।6.129.6।। चित्रकूटगिरिंगत्वाराज्येनामित्रकर्शनः । निमन्त्रितस्त्वयाभ्राताधर्ममाचरतासताम् ।।6.129.7।। स्थितेनराज्ञोवचनेयथाराज्यंविसर्जितम् । आर्यस्यमादुकेगृह्ययथासिपुनरागतः।।य6.129.8।। सर्वमेतन्महाबाहोयथावद्विदितंतव । त्वयिप्रतिप्रयातेतुयद्वृत्तंतन्निबोधमे ।।6.129.9।।
explanation: "O Lord, mighty armed Bharata! the boons bestowed on your mother, how Sri Rama went on exile, how king Dasharatha died out of grief of son, envoys bringing you to Ayodhya, entering the kingdom, your unwillingness to accept the sovereignty, going to Chitrakuta mountain, seeking your brother noble Rama, a scourge of enemies to accept the kingdom, renouncing the kingdom by Rama, taking his sandals, and again returning here, all this is known to you."

shloka_text: अपयातेत्वयितदासमुद्भ्रान्तमृगद्विजम् । परिध्युIनमिवात्यर्थंतद्वनंसमपद्यत ।।6.129.10।।
explanation: "When you had gone away the beasts and birds scared of your army got agitated and had a doleful appearance."

shloka_text: तदथस्तिमृदितंघोरंसिंहव्याघ्रमृगाकुलम् । प्रविवेशाथविजनं स महद्दण्डकावनम् ।।6.129.11।।
explanation: "Then he entered into dreadful Dandaka forest that was devoid of people which was crowded with lions, tigers, and deer, and trampled by the elephants."

shloka_text: तेषांपुरस्ताद्भलवान् गच्छतांगहनेवने । विनदन् सुमहानादंविराधःप्रत्यदृश्यत ।।6.129.12।।
explanation: As they proceeded through the dense forest, the powerful Viradha appeared before them, roaring a mighty sound.

shloka_text: तमुत्क्षिप्यमहानादमूर्ध्वबाहुमधोमुखम् । निखातेप्रक्षिपन्तिस्मवदन्तमिवकुञ्जरम् ।।6.129.13।।
explanation: "That Viradha uplifted his arms and bent his head low screamed like an elephant. The three dug up a pit and threw him into it."

shloka_text: तत्कृत्वादुष्करंकर्मभ्रातरौरामलक्ष्मणौ । सायाह्नेशरभङ्गस्यरम्यमाश्रममीयतुः ।।6.129.14।।
explanation: "Both the brothers Rama and Lakshmana encountered Viradha who was difficult to attack and having completed their task, reached the beautiful hermitage of Sarabhanga in the evening."

shloka_text: शरभङ्गेदिवंप्राप्तेरामस्सत्यपराक्रमः । अभिवाद्यमुनीन्सर्वान्जनस्थानमुपागमत् ।।6.129.15।।
explanation: When Sharabhanga had attained heaven, Rama, of true valor, having saluted all the sages, approached Janasthana.

shloka_text: ततःपश्चाच्छूर्पणखानामरामपार्शमुपागता । ततोरामेणसन्दिष्टोलक्ष्मणस्सहसोत्थितः ।।6.129.16।। प्रगृह्यखङ्गंचिच्छेदकर्णनासेमहाबलः ।
explanation: "Later came an ogre called Surpanakha close by Rama. Rama indicated to mighty Lakshmana, who got up quickly and cut off her ears and nose with a sword."

shloka_text: चतुर्दशसहस्राणिजनस्तान्निवासिनाम् ।।6.129.17।। हतानिवसतातत्रराघवेणमहात्मना ।
explanation: "While the great soul Rama lived at Janasthana, he killed fourteen thousand ogres".

shloka_text: एकेनसहसङ्गम्यरामेणरणमूर्धनि ।।6.129.18।। अह्नश्चतुर्थभागेननिःशेषाराक्षसाःकृताः ।
explanation: "Rama alone in a day finished fourteen thousand Rakshasas standing alone in the forefront of the combat".

shloka_text: मबलामहावीर्यास्तपसोविघ्नकारिणः ।।6.129.19।। निहताराघवेणाजौदण्डकारण्यवासिनः ।
explanation: "Mighty strong heroic ogres obstructing the penance of sages living in Dandakaranya were killed by Raghava in the combat."

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्चविनिष्पिष्टाःखरश्चनिहतोरणे ।।6.129.20।। दूषणंचाग्रतोहत्वात्रिशिरास्तदनन्तम् ।
explanation: "In the battle Rama terminated Khara and killed his elder brother Dushana and also Trisira thereafter."

shloka_text: तस्तेनार्दिताबालारावणंसमुपागता ।।6.129.21।। रावणानुचरोघोरोमारीचोनामराक्षसः । लोभयामासवैदेहींभूत्वारत्नमयोमृगः ।।6.129.22।।
explanation: "Then Surpanakha afflicted by Rama returned to Ravana and informed. Ravana sent dreadful Rakshasa by name Maricha, who assumed the form of deer with precious stones (on body) created a desire for it in Vaidehi."

shloka_text: तस्तेनार्दिताबालारावणंसमुपागता ।।6.129.21।। रावणानुचरोघोरोमारीचोनामराक्षसः । लोभयामासवैदेहींभूत्वारत्नमयोमृगः ।।6.129.22।।
explanation: "Then Surpanakha afflicted by Rama returned to Ravana and informed. Ravana sent dreadful Rakshasa by name Maricha, who assumed the form of deer with precious stones (on body) created a desire for it in Vaidehi."

shloka_text: साराममब्रवीदृष्टवावैदेसीगृह्यतामिति । अयंमनोहरःकान्तआश्रमोनोभविष्यति ।।6.129.23।।
explanation: "Seeing that deer Vaidehi spoke to Rama to capture it as she desired and that it was beautiful and will make the hermitage bright."

shloka_text: ततोरामोधनुष्पाणिर्मृगंतमनुधावति । स तंजघानधावन्तंशरेणानतपर्वणा ।।6.129.24।।
explanation: "Rama, wielder of bow, chased the deer and followed it chasing and attacked with his arrow."

shloka_text: अथसौम्य दशग्रीवोमृगंयातेतुराघवे । लक्ष्मणेचापिनिष्क्रान्तेप्रविवेशाश्रमंतदा ।।6.129.25।।
explanation: "When gentle Raghava went after the deer and Lakshmana also went from there, the ten headed Ravana entered the hermitage."

shloka_text: जग्राहतरसासीतांग्रहःखेरोहिणीमिव । त्रातुकामंततोयुद्धेहत्वागृध्रंजटायुषम् ।।6.129.26।। प्रगृह्यसहसासीतांजगामाशु स राक्षसः ।
explanation: He forcefully seized Sita, like a planet seizing Rohini in the sky, after having killed the vulture Jatayu in battle, who desired to protect her. Having forcefully seized Sita, that demon swiftly departed.

shloka_text: तस्त्वद्भुतसङ्काशास्स्थिताःपर्वतमूर्धनि ।।6.129.27।। सीतांगृहीत्वागच्छन्तंवानराःपर्वतोपमाः । ददृशुर्मिस्मिताकारारावणंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.129.28।।
explanation: "Standing on the mountain top, the Vanaras who were like mountains in size watched the wonderful feat of the king of Rakshasas of wonderful form taking Sita."

shloka_text: तस्त्वद्भुतसङ्काशास्स्थिताःपर्वतमूर्धनि ।।6.129.27।। सीतांगृहीत्वागच्छन्तंवानराःपर्वतोपमाः । ददृशुर्मिस्मिताकारारावणंराक्षसाधिपम् ।।6.129.28।।
explanation: "Standing on the mountain top, the Vanaras who were like mountains in size watched the wonderful feat of the king of Rakshasas of wonderful form taking Sita."

shloka_text: ततशीघ्रतरंगत्वातद्विमानंमनोजवम् । आरुह्यसहवैदेह्यापुष्पकं स महाबलः ।।6.129.29।। प्रविवेशतदालङ्कांरावणोराक्षसेश्वरः ।
explanation: "Then the king of Rakshasas, mighty Ravana ascended with Vaidehi into the Pushpaka, an aerial car that went swiftly at the speed of the mind and entered Lanka."

shloka_text: तांसुवर्णपरिष्कारेशुभेमहतिवेश्मनि ।।6.129.30।। प्रवेश्यमैथिलींवाक्यैस्सान्त्वयामासरावणः ।
explanation: "Ravana kept Mythili in an auspicious huge mansion with golden walls and consoled her with good words."

shloka_text: तृणवद्भाषितंतस्यतं च नैरृतपुङ्गवम् ।।6.129.31।। अचिन्तयन्तीवैदेहीह्यशोकवनिकांगता ।
explanation: "Vaidehi did not care to talk to the chief of Rakshasas. She ignored him like a straw and stayed in the Ashoka grove."

shloka_text: न्यवर्तततदारामोमृगंहत्वातदावने ।।6.129.32।। निवर्तमानःकाकुत्स्थोदृष्टवागृध्रं स विव्यथे । गृध्रंहतंतदादृष्टवारामःप्रियतरंपितुः ।।6.129.33।।
explanation: "Rama returned after killing the deer. On his return Kakuthsa saw in the forest, the vulture, who was dearer than his own father, killed."

shloka_text: न्यवर्तततदारामोमृगंहत्वातदावने ।।6.129.32।। निवर्तमानःकाकुत्स्थोदृष्टवागृध्रं स विव्यथे । गृध्रंहतंतदादृष्टवारामःप्रियतरंपितुः ।।6.129.33।।
explanation: "Rama returned after killing the deer. On his return Kakuthsa saw in the forest, the vulture, who was dearer than his own father, killed."

shloka_text: मार्गमाणस्तुवैदेहींराघवंसहलक्ष्मणः । गोदावरीमन्वचरद्वनोद्धेशांश्चपुष्पितान् ।।6.129.34।।
explanation: "Rama with Lakshmana went about searching, ranging along the banks of Godavari among the blossomed woods."

shloka_text: आसेदतुर्महारण्येकबन्धंनामराक्षसम् । ततःकबन्दवचनाद्रामस्सत्यपराक्रमः ।।6.129.35।। ऋष्यमूकगिरिंगत्वासुग्रीवेणसमागतः ।
explanation: "While going in the huge forest the valiant and truthful Rama saw a Rakshasa by the name Kabhanda. According to Kabhanda's words of advice they went to Rshyamuka mountain and met Sugriva."

shloka_text: तयोस्समागमःपूर्वंप्रीत्यहार्दोव्यजायत ।।6.129.36।। भ्रात्रानिरस्तःक्रुद्धेनसुग्रीवोवालिनापुरा । इतरेतरसंवादात्प्रगाढःप्रणयस्तयोः ।।6.129.37।।
explanation: "Even before they met, they had a happy feeling at heart towards each other. Earlier Sugriva was banished by his enraged brother (Vali). On mutual talk and discussion, they both developed deep friendship."

shloka_text: तयोस्समागमःपूर्वंप्रीत्यहार्दोव्यजायत ।।6.129.36।। भ्रात्रानिरस्तःक्रुद्धेनसुग्रीवोवालिनापुरा । इतरेतरसंवादात्प्रगाढःप्रणयस्तयोः ।।6.129.37।।
explanation: "Even before they met, they had a happy feeling at heart towards each other. Earlier Sugriva was banished by his enraged brother (Vali). On mutual talk and discussion, they both developed deep friendship."

shloka_text: रामस्स्वबाहुवीर्येणस्वराज्यंप्रत्यपादयत् । वालिनंसमरेहत्वामहाकायंमहाबलम् ।।6.129.38।।
explanation: "Rama of mighty arms killed Vali of gigantic body and mighty prowess and restored Sugriva's own kingdom to him."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवस्स्थापितोराज्येसहितस्सर्ववानरैः । रामायप्रतिजानीतेराजपुत्य्रास्तुमार्गणम् ।।6.129.39।।
explanation: "Sugriva attained the kingdom and established. He promised to search with all Vanaras and promised to find Sita."

shloka_text: अदिष्टावानरेन्द्रेणसुग्रीवेणमहात्मना । दशकोट्यःप्लवङ्गानांसर्वाःप्रस्थापिताःदिशः ।।6.129.40।।
explanation: "Vanara Lord Sugriva ordered the monkeys to go to all countries and all directions and dispatched them to find Sita."

shloka_text: तेषांनोविप्रनष्टानांविन्ध्येपर्वतसत्तमो । भृशंशोकानितप्तानांमहान्कालो त्यवर्तत ।।6.129.41।।
explanation: "Monkeys that went to the foremost of mountains Vindhya lost their way and a lot of time and returned with intense grief."

shloka_text: भ्रातातुगृध्रराजस्यसम्पातिर्नामवीर्यवान् । समाख्यातिस्मवसतींसीतांरावणमन्दिरे ।।6.129.42।।
explanation: "Vulture king's brother called Sampathi told the Vanaras positively that Sita is dwelling in Ravana's mansion."

shloka_text: सोहंदुःखपरीतानांदुःखंतद् ज्ञातीनांनुदन् । आत्मवीर्यंसमास्थाययोजनानांशतंप्लुतः ।।6.129.43।।
explanation: "To dispel the grief of the Vanaras and relieve them, I resorted to my valour and leapt a hundred yojanas."

shloka_text: तत्राहमेकामद्राक्षमशोकवनिकांगताम् । कौशेयवस्त्रांमलिनांनिरनन्दांदृढव्रताम् ।।6.129.44।।
explanation: "There at Ashoka Grove, I saw her wearing unclean silk clothes, dirty in body, devoid of happiness, determined and staying alone."

shloka_text: तयासमेत्यविधिवत् पृष्टवासर्वमनिन्दिताम् । अभिज्ञानंमयादत्तंरामनामाङ्गुलीयकम् ।।6.129.45।।
explanation: "Met that irreproachable lady like that and duly enquired everything, delighted Mythili gave me a ring with Rama's name as a token to be given to Sri Rama."

shloka_text: अभिज्ञानंमणिंलब्द्वाचरितार्धो हमागतः । मया च पुनरागम्यरामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः ।।6.129.46।। अभिज्ञानंमयादत्तमर्चिष्मान् स महामणिः ।
explanation: "Knowing that the most difficult task has been accomplished, again I returned and gave the valuable jewel to Rama."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातांमैथिलींरामस्त्वाशशंसे च जीवितम् ।।6.129.47।। जीवितान्तमनुप्राप्तःपीत्वामृतमिवातुरः ।
explanation: "Just as an ailing man at the end of life regains hope on drinking nectar, Sri Rama also gains hope on hearing about Mythili."

shloka_text: उद्योजयिष्यन्नुद्योगंदध्रेकामंवधेमनः ।।6.129.48।। जिघांसुरिवलोकान्तेसर्वान्लोकान्विभावसुः ।
explanation: "Rama made war efforts to win the war for the destruction of Lanka just as fire burns at the dissolution of the worlds and to conquer Ravana."

shloka_text: ततस्समुद्रमासाद्यनलंसेतुमकारयत् ।।6.129.49।। अतरत्कपिवीराणां वाहिनी तेन सेतुना ।
explanation: "Then Nala constructed the bridge, and the monkey heroes crossed the bridge."

shloka_text: प्रहस्तम्वधीन्नीलःकुम्भकर्णंतुराघवः ।।6.129.50।। लक्ष्मणोरावणसुतंस्वयंरामस्तुरावणम् ।
explanation: "Prahastha was killed by Nila. Rama killed Kumbhakarna. Lakshmana killed Indrajith, the son of Ravana."

shloka_text: सशक्रेणसमागम्ययमेनवरुणेन च ।।6.129.51।। महेश्वरस्वयंभूभ्यां तथा दशरथेन च । तैश्चदत्तवर्श्रीमानृषिभिश्चसमागतैः ।।6.129.52।। सुरर्षिभिश्चकाकुत्स्थोवरान्लेभेपरन्तपः ।
explanation: "Then to the glorious Kakuthsa, the tormentor of enemies, Indra, Yama, and Varuna bestowed boons, so also Maheswara and Brahma, Dasharatha also reached and bestowed boons on Rama. Ascetics and suras also conferred boons."

shloka_text: सशक्रेणसमागम्ययमेनवरुणेन च ।।6.129.51।। महेश्वरस्वयंभूभ्यां तथा दशरथेन च । तैश्चदत्तवर्श्रीमानृषिभिश्चसमागतैः ।।6.129.52।। सुरर्षिभिश्चकाकुत्स्थोवरान्लेभेपरन्तपः ।
explanation: "Then to the glorious Kakuthsa, the tormentor of enemies, Indra, Yama, and Varuna bestowed boons, so also Maheswara and Brahma, Dasharatha also reached and bestowed boons on Rama. Ascetics and suras also conferred boons."

shloka_text: सतुदत्तवरःप्रीत्यावानरैश्चसमागतः ।।6.129.53।। पुष्पकेनविमानेनकिष्किनष्धामभ्युपागमत् ।
explanation: "Having received boons, Rama with the Vanaras collected together reached Kishkinda by Pushpaka aerial car."

shloka_text: तंगङ्गांपुनारासाद्यवसन्तंमुनिसन्निधौ ।।6.129.54।। अविघ्नंपुष्ययोगेनश्वोरामंद्रष्टुमर्हसि ।
explanation: "He reached the bank of Ganga and is staying at the hermitage of sage. Tomorrow at the time when Pushya star is in union with the moon you will be able to see Rama without any obstruction."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वातुपरमानन्दंभरतस्सत्यविक्रमः । हृष्टमाज्ञापयामासशत्रुघ्नंपरवीरहा ।।6.130.1।।
explanation: Hearing the delightful news, Bharata of truthful prowess, the destroyer of enemies, was very happy and ordered Shatrughna.

shloka_text: दैवतानि च सर्वाणिचैत्यानिनगरस्य च । सुगन्धमाल्यैर्यादित्रैरर्चन्तु शुचयो नराः ।।6.130.2।।
explanation: "Let all gods in the temples of the capital be worshiped by people purifying themselves, duly adorned with fragrance and garlands."

shloka_text: सूतास्स्तुतिपुराणज्ञास्सर्वेवैतालिकास्तथा । सर्वेवादित्रकुशलागणिकाश्चैवसङ्घशः ।।6.130.3।। राजदारास्तथामात्यास्सैन्यास्सेनाङ्गनागणाः । ब्राह्मणाश्चसराजन्याश्रेणिमुख्यास्तथागणाः ।।6.130.4।। अभिनिर्यान्तुरामस्यद्रष्टुंशशिनिभंमुखम् ।
explanation: "Let the bards well versed in singing praises, charioteers, all courtesans, in groups, artists who can play musical instruments, similarly ministers, army men, traders, service providers, Kshatriyas, brahmins so also top people, troops proceed to see the moon like face of Rama."

shloka_text: सूतास्स्तुतिपुराणज्ञास्सर्वेवैतालिकास्तथा । सर्वेवादित्रकुशलागणिकाश्चैवसङ्घशः ।।6.130.3।। राजदारास्तथामात्यास्सैन्यास्सेनाङ्गनागणाः । ब्राह्मणाश्चसराजन्याश्रेणिमुख्यास्तथागणाः ।।6.130.4।। अभिनिर्यान्तुरामस्यद्रष्टुंशशिनिभंमुखम् ।
explanation: "Let the bards well versed in singing praises, charioteers, all courtesans, in groups, artists who can play musical instruments, similarly ministers, army men, traders, service providers, Kshatriyas, brahmins so also top people, troops proceed to see the moon like face of Rama."

shloka_text: भरतस्यवच्श्रुत्वाशत्रुघ्नःपरवीरहा ।।6.130.5।। विष्टीरनेकसाहस्रीश्चोदयामानभागशः ।
explanation: Shatrughna, a destroyer of enemies, hearing the words of Bharata, ordered for many divisions of labour and the courageous ones to come.

shloka_text: समीकुरुतनिम्नानिविषमानिसमानि च ।।6.130.6।। स्थानानितुनिरस्यन्तांनन्दिग्रामादितःपरम् ।
explanation: From here (Nandigrama to Ayodhya) low lying areas are to be made even and uneven areas to be levelled.

shloka_text: सिञ्चस्तुपृथिवींकृत्स्नांहिवशीतेववारिणा ।।6.130.7।। ततोऽभ्यवकिरन्त्वन्येलाजैःपुष्पैश्चसर्वतः ।
explanation: Let the ground be sprinkled with cold water and then parched grain and flowers to be sprinkled.

shloka_text: सुमुच्छ्रितपताकास्तुरथ्याःपुरवरोत्तमेः ।।6.130.8।। शोभयन्तु च वेश्मानिसूर्यस्योदयनंप्रति ।
explanation: Let the streets of the foremost of the best cities (Ayodhya), be decorated with flags till the sun rises and houses be decorated.

shloka_text: स्रग्दाममुक्तपुष्पैश्चसुगन्धै: पञ्चवर्णकैः ।।6.130.9।। राजमार्गमसम्बाधंकिरन्तुशतशोनराः ।
explanation: Let hundreds of people decorate with fragrant garlands of five colours closely tied and decorate the royal paths.

shloka_text: तस्तच्छासनंश्रुत्वाशत्रुघ्नस्यमुदान्विताः ।।6.130.10।। धृष्टिर्जयन्तोविजयस्सिद्धार्थश्चार्थसाधकः । अशोकोमन्त्रपालश्चसुमन्त्रश्चापिनिर्ययुः ।।6.130.11।।
explanation: On hearing Shatrughna's command, all the eight ministers, Dhristi, Jayanta, Vijaya, Siddhartha, Arthasadhaka, Ashoka, and Mantrapala issued forth with great joy.

shloka_text: तस्तच्छासनंश्रुत्वाशत्रुघ्नस्यमुदान्विताः ।।6.130.10।। धृष्टिर्जयन्तोविजयस्सिद्धार्थश्चार्थसाधकः । अशोकोमन्त्रपालश्चसुमन्त्रश्चापिनिर्ययुः ।।6.130.11।।
explanation: On hearing Shatrughna's command, all the eight ministers, Dhristi, Jayanta, Vijaya, Siddhartha, Arthasadhaka, Ashoka, and Mantrapala issued forth with great joy.

shloka_text: मत्तैर्नागसहस्रैश्चसध्वजैस्सुविभूषितैः । अपरेहेमकक्षाभिस्सगजाभिःकरेणुभिः ।।6.130.12।। निर्ययुस्तुररथैश्चसुमहारथाः ।
explanation: Seated on top of thousands of well decorated elephants in rut, and on the best of horses, people went (to receive Rama). Female elephants had golden girths on their waist. Best charioteers on best chariots proceeded.

shloka_text: शक्त्यृष्टिपाशहस्तानांसध्वजानांपताकिनाम् ।।6.130.13।। तुरगाणांसहस्रैश्चमुख्यैर्मुख्यतरान्वितैः । पदातीनांसहस्रैश्चवीराःपरिवृताययुः ।।6.130.14।।
explanation: Chiefs on horses, champions in thousands went surrounded by thousands of foot soldiers carrying javelins, spears, and nooses.

shloka_text: शक्त्यृष्टिपाशहस्तानांसध्वजानांपताकिनाम् ।।6.130.13।। तुरगाणांसहस्रैश्चमुख्यैर्मुख्यतरान्वितैः । पदातीनांसहस्रैश्चवीराःपरिवृताययुः ।।6.130.14।।
explanation: Chiefs on horses, champions in thousands went surrounded by thousands of foot soldiers carrying javelins, spears, and nooses.

shloka_text: ततोयानान्युपारूढास्सर्वादशरथस्त्रियः । कौसल्यांप्रमुखेकृत्वासुमित्रांचापिनिर्ययुः ।।6.130.15।। कैकेय्यासहिताःसर्वानन्दिग्राममुपागमन् ।
explanation: Then all the consorts of Dasharatha, keeping Kausalya and Sumitra in front, seated in palanquin accompanied by Kaikeyi, started from Nandigram.

shloka_text: द्विजातिमुख्यैर्धर्मात्माश्रेणीमुख्यैस्सनैगमैः ।।6.130.16।। माल्यमोदकहस्तैश्चमन्त्रिभिर्भरतोवृतः । शङ्खभेरीनिनादैश्चवन्दिभिश्चाभिवनन्दितः ।।6.130.17।। आर्यपादौगृहीत्वातौशिरसाधर्मकोविदः । पाण्डुरंछत्रमादायशुक्लमाल्योपशोभितम् ।।6.130.18।। शुक्ले च वालव्यजनेराजार्हेहेमभूषिते । उपवासकृशोदीनश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरः ।।6.130.19।। भ्रातुरागमनंश्रुत्वातत्पूर्वंहर्षमागतः । प्रत्युद्ययौतदारामंमहात्मासचिवैस्सह ।।6.130.20।।
explanation: Then the foremost of brahmins, leaders with garlands and Modaka sweets in hand, surrounded by ministers went with righteous Bharata, accompanied by bards praising, accompanied by sounds of blowing conches and drums and greeting. Bharata was emaciated due to fastings, was desperate, wearing bark fabric and skin of antelope. The great soul Bharata, knower of righteous responsibilities, greeting, experienced great joy, on hearing about the returning of the brother. Decorated with white garlands, he carried Rama's sandals on his head. His friends accompanied him and took with him a yellow umbrella adorned with gold, worthy of kings and white whisks. Bharata went to receive Sri Rama.
