Decorated with white garlands, he carried Rama's sandals on his head. His friends accompanied him and took with him a yellow umbrella adorned with gold, worthy of kings and white whisks. Bharata went to receive Sri Rama.

shloka_text: द्विजातिमुख्यैर्धर्मात्माश्रेणीमुख्यैस्सनैगमैः ।।6.130.16।। माल्यमोदकहस्तैश्चमन्त्रिभिर्भरतोवृतः । शङ्खभेरीनिनादैश्चवन्दिभिश्चाभिवनन्दितः ।।6.130.17।। आर्यपादौगृहीत्वातौशिरसाधर्मकोविदः । पाण्डुरंछत्रमादायशुक्लमाल्योपशोभितम् ।।6.130.18।। शुक्ले च वालव्यजनेराजार्हेहेमभूषिते । उपवासकृशोदीनश्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरः ।।6.130.19।। भ्रातुरागमनंश्रुत्वातत्पूर्वंहर्षमागतः । प्रत्युद्ययौतदारामंमहात्मासचिवैस्सह ।।6.130.20।।
explanation: Then the foremost of brahmins, leaders with garlands and Modaka sweets in hand, surrounded by ministers went with righteous Bharata, accompanied by bards praising, accompanied by sounds of blowing conches and drums and greeting. Bharata was emaciated due to fastings, was desperate, wearing bark fabric and skin of antelope. The great soul Bharata, knower of righteous responsibilities, greeting, experienced great joy, on hearing about the returning of the brother. Decorated with white garlands, he carried Rama's sandals on his head. His friends accompanied him and took with him a yellow umbrella adorned with gold, worthy of kings and white whisks. Bharata went to receive Sri Rama.

shloka_text: अश्वानांखुरशब्दैश्चरथनेमिस्वनेन च । शङ्खदुन्दुभिनादेनसञ्चचालेवमेदिनी ।।6.130.21।।
explanation: The earth shook by the sounds of hooves of the horses, sounds of conches and drums, and the rattling of the chariot wheels.

shloka_text: कृत्स्नंतुनगरंतत्तुनन्दिग्राममुपागमत् । समीक्ष्यभरतोवाक्यमुवाचपवनात्मजम् ।।6.130.22।।
explanation: Reviewing the arrangements, Bharata spoke these words to wind god's son, Hanuman.

shloka_text: कच्चिन्नखलुकापेयीसेव्यतेचकचित्तता । न हिपश्यामिकाकुत्स्थंराममार्यंपरन्तपम् ।।6.130.23।।
explanation: "O monkey! Indeed, you monkey being fickle minded, hope you have not resorted to your nature. I am not seeing noble Rama, the tormentor of enemies."

shloka_text: अथैवमुक्तेवचनेहनूमानिदमब्रवीत् । अर्थ्यंविज्ञापयन्नेवभरतंसत्यविक्रमम् ।।6.130.24।।
explanation: And then Bharata having spoken that way, Hanuman understood the meaning of his words and spoke thus.

shloka_text: सदाफलान्कुसुमितान्वृक्षान् प्राप्यमधुस्रवान् । भरद्वाजप्रसादेनमत्तभ्रमरनादितान् ।।6.130.25।। तस्यचैषवरोदत्तोवासवेनपरन्तप । ससैन्यस्यतवातिथ्यंकृतंसर्वगुणान्वितम् ।।6.130.26।। निस्स्वन्श्रूयतेभीमःप्रहृष्टानांवनौकसाम् । मन्येवानरसेनासानदींतरतिगोमतीम् ।।6.130.27।।
explanation: "By the grace of Bharadwaja, all the trees have fruits shedding sweet juice, and in bloom, the Vanaras are very delighted. The forest rangers are making terrific sounds. The tormentor of enemies, endowed with all virtues, by virtue of the boon given by Indra extended hospitality to the Vanara army. I think they are crossing the river Gomathi now."

shloka_text: सदाफलान्कुसुमितान्वृक्षान् प्राप्यमधुस्रवान् । भरद्वाजप्रसादेनमत्तभ्रमरनादितान् ।।6.130.25।। तस्यचैषवरोदत्तोवासवेनपरन्तप । ससैन्यस्यतवातिथ्यंकृतंसर्वगुणान्वितम् ।।6.130.26।। निस्स्वन्श्रूयतेभीमःप्रहृष्टानांवनौकसाम् । मन्येवानरसेनासानदींतरतिगोमतीम् ।।6.130.27।।
explanation: "By the grace of Bharadwaja, all the trees have fruits shedding sweet juice, and in bloom, the Vanaras are very delighted. The forest rangers are making terrific sounds. The tormentor of enemies, endowed with all virtues, by virtue of the boon given by Indra extended hospitality to the Vanara army. I think they are crossing the river Gomathi now."

shloka_text: सदाफलान्कुसुमितान्वृक्षान् प्राप्यमधुस्रवान् । भरद्वाजप्रसादेनमत्तभ्रमरनादितान् ।।6.130.25।। तस्यचैषवरोदत्तोवासवेनपरन्तप । ससैन्यस्यतवातिथ्यंकृतंसर्वगुणान्वितम् ।।6.130.26।। निस्स्वन्श्रूयतेभीमःप्रहृष्टानांवनौकसाम् । मन्येवानरसेनासानदींतरतिगोमतीम् ।।6.130.27।।
explanation: "By the grace of Bharadwaja, all the trees have fruits shedding sweet juice, and in bloom, the Vanaras are very delighted. The forest rangers are making terrific sounds. The tormentor of enemies, endowed with all virtues, by virtue of the boon given by Indra extended hospitality to the Vanara army. I think they are crossing the river Gomathi now."

shloka_text: रजोवर्षंसमुद्भूतंपश्यसालवनंप्रति । मन्येसालवनंरम्यंलोपयन्तिप्लवङ्गमाः ।।6.130.28।।
explanation: "See the rain of dust started at Sala Forest. Vanaras are shaking the beautiful Sala grove, I think."

shloka_text: तदेतद्दृश्यतेदूराद्विमानंचन्द्रसन्निभम् । विमानंपुष्पकंदिव्यंमनसाब्रह्मनिर्मितम् ।।6.130.29।।
explanation: Pushpaka is seen at a distance, resembling the moon. This wonderful Pushpaka has been created through Brahma's mind.

shloka_text: रावणंबान्धवैःसार्थंहत्वालब्धंमहात्मना । तरुणादित्यसङ्काशंविमानंरामवाहनम् ।।6.130.30।। धनदस्यप्रसादेनदिव्यमेतन्मनोजवम् ।
explanation: "Rama's vehicle is amazing, and he got it by killing Ravana and his relatives. It shines brightly like the rising sun, and it speeds at the thought of mind. Kubera got this aerial car by Brahma's grace."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन् भ्रातरौवीरौवैदेह्यासहराघवौ ।।6.130.31।। सुग्रीवश्चमहातेजाराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।
explanation: "Heroic Raghava brothers are there with Vaidehi, that highly energetic Sugriva and Rakshasa Vibheeshana also."

shloka_text: एतोहर्षसमुद्भूतोनिःस्वनोदिवमस्पृशत् ।।6.130.32।। स्त्रीबालयुववृद्धानांरामोऽयमितिकीर्तिते ।
explanation: Then when "Sri Rama is here" was uttered a fantastic expression of joy of the women, young, youth and aged was heard, which reached the heaven.

shloka_text: रथकुञ्जरवाजिभ्यस्तेऽवतीर्यमहींगताः ।।6.130.33।। ददृशुस्तंविमानस्थंनरास्सोममिवाम्बरे ।
explanation: Those people on the chariots, elephants and horses got down and saw them on the moon like Pushpaka.

shloka_text: प्राज्ञलिर्भरतोभूत्वाप्रसृष्टोराघवोन्मुखः ।।6.130.34।। स्वागतेनयथार्हेणततोराममपूजयत् ।
explanation: Highly rejoiced, Bharata offered salutations standing as he ought to within himself and worshiped Sri Rama from a distance.

shloka_text: मनसाब्रह्मणासृष्टेविमानेभरताग्रजः ।।6.130.35।। रराजपृथुदीर्घाक्षोवज्रपाणिरिवापरः ।
explanation: Sri Rama, elder brother of Bharata shone in the aerial car created by Brahma like another Indra.

shloka_text: ततोविमानाग्रगतंभरतोभ्रातरंतदा ।।6.130.36।। ववन्देप्रणतोरामंमेरुस्थमिवभास्करम् ।
explanation: Then Bharata offered salutations with joined palms to Sri Rama seated in the peak of Pushpaka like saluting Sun from the mountain Meru.

shloka_text: ततोरामाभ्यनुज्ञातंतद्विमानमनुत्तमम् ।।6.130.37।। हंसयुक्तंमहावेगंनिपपातमहीतले ।
explanation: Then that excellent Pushpaka which had pictures of swans on it came down to the ground with Rama's permission.

shloka_text: आपितोविमानंतद्भरतस्सत्यविक्रमः ।।6.130.38।। राममासाद्यमुदितःपुनरेवाभ्यवादयत् ।
explanation: Bharata of unfailing valour duly permitted to ascend Pushpaka by Sri Rama, reached Rama and once again offered salutations to Rama.

shloka_text: तंसमुत्थाप्यकाकुत्स्थश्चिरस्याक्षिरथंगतम् ।।6.130.39।। अङ्केभरतमारोप्यमुदितःपरिषस्वजे ।
explanation: Kakuthsa Rama happily lifting up Bharata, who came into his sight after long, on to his thigh embraced him.

shloka_text: ततोलक्ष्मणमासाद्यवैदेहीं च परन्तपः ।।6.130.40।। अथाभ्यवादयप्रतीतोभरतोनामचाब्रवीत् ।
explanation: Then the tormentor of enemies, Bharata approached Lakshmana and then greeted Vaidehi and announced his name.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवंकेकयीपुत्रोजाम्बवन्तमथाङ्गदम् ।।6.130.41।। मैन्दं च द्विविदंनीलमृषभंपरिषस्वजे ।
explanation: Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi thereafter embraced Sugriva, Jambavantha, Angada, Mainda, Dwivivida, Nila and Rshaba.

shloka_text: सुषेणं च नलंचैवगवाक्षंगन्धमादनम् ।।6.130.42।। शरभंपनसंचैवपरितःपरिषस्वजे ।
explanation: He embraced Sushena, Nala, Gavaksha, Gandhamadana, Sarabha, Panasa who were around.

shloka_text: तेकृत्वामानुषंरूपंवानराःकामरूपिणः ।।6.130.43।। कुशलंपर्यपृच्छंस्तेप्रहृष्टाभरतंतदा ।
explanation: Then he inquired about the welfare of those Vanaras who can take any form at will, who were in human form and was delighted.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रस्सुग्रीवंवानरर्षभम् ।।6.130.44।। परिष्वज्यमहातेजाभरतोधर्मिणांवरः ।
explanation: And thereafter highly brilliant, foremost among the righteous, prince Bharata embraced Sugriva, the bull among Vanaras and spoke.

shloka_text: त्वम्स्माकंचतुर्णांवैभ्रातासुग्रीवपञ्चमः ।।6.130.45।। सौहार्दाज्जायतेमित्रमपकारोऽरिलक्षणम् ।
explanation: "Sugriva, you are the fifth brother to four of us and should have been born like that" said Bharata. One who helps becomes friend and maleficence is a sign of an enemy.

shloka_text: विभीषणं च भरतःसान्त्ववाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।।6.130.46।। दिष्ट्यात्वयासहायेनकृतंकर्मसुदुष्करम् ।
explanation: And then Bharata spoke this good word. "Luckily with your help, the very difficult task was done."

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्चतदाराममभिवाद्यसलक्ष्मणम् ।।6.130.47।। सीतायाश्चरणौवीरोविनयादभ्यवादयत् ।
explanation: Then hero Shatrughna and Lakshmana also greeted Rama and then worshipped Sita also.

shloka_text: रामोमातरमासाद्यविवर्णांशोककर्शिताम् ।।6.130.48।। जग्राहप्रणतःपादौमनोमातुःप्रहर्षयन् ।
explanation: Rama reached his mother who was pale and emaciated in grief and offered salutations clasping her feet in obedience and was delighted in his mind.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्यसुमित्रां च कैकेयीं च यशस्विनीम् ।।6.130.49।। स मात्रूश्चततस्सर्वापुरोहितमुपागमत् ।
explanation: Then he greeted Sumitra, and illustrious Kaikeyi also and then all the mothers and the priests who had come.

shloka_text: स्वागतंतेमहाबाहोकौसल्यानन्दवर्धना ।।6.130.50।। इतिप्राञ्जलयःसर्वेनागराराममब्रुवन् ।
explanation: "Welcome to you mighty armed Rama, enhancer of Kausalya's joy" saying so citizens of the city spoke with folded hand s greeting Rama.

shloka_text: तान्यञ्जलिसहस्राणिप्रगृहीतानिनागरैः ।।6.130.51।। व्याकोचानीवपद्मानिददर्शभरताग्रजः ।
explanation: The citizens in thousands greeting Rama, elder brother of Bharata lifting up their hand s with folded palms seemed like lotus buds.

shloka_text: पादुकेतेतुरामस्यगृहीत्वाभरतस्स्वयम् ।।6.130.52।। चरणाभ्यांनरेन्द्रस्ययोजयामासधर्मवित् ।
explanation: Taking the sandals given to Bharata, the knower of dharma put on the sandals on Rama's feet by himself.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्चतदारामंभरतः स कृताञ्जलिः ।।6.130.53।। एतत्तेसकलंराज्यंन्यासंनिर्यातितंमया ।
explanation: Bharata then greeted Rama with folded palms, spoke saying, "this kingdom and everything held in trust by me is returned to you."

shloka_text: अद्यजन्मकृतार्थंमेसम्वृत्तश्चमनोरथः ।।6.130.54।। यत्त्वांपश्यामिराजानमयोध्यांपुनरागतम् ।
explanation: Today my life is fulfilled, my wish is completed. I am seeing you returned to Ayodhya again as king of this kingdom.

shloka_text: अवेक्षतांभवान्शोकंकोष्ठागारंगृहंबलम् ।।6.130.55।। भवतस्तेजसासर्वंकृतंदशगुणंमया ।
explanation: You may review your treasury, granary, palaces, army. Everything has increased tenfold by me by virtue of your brilliance.

shloka_text: तथाब्रुवाणंभरतंदृष्टवातंभ्रातृवत्सलम् ।।6.130.56।। मुमुचुर्वानराबाष्पंराक्षसश्चविभीषणः ।
explanation: Seeing Bharata, the lover of his brother, who spoke like that, the Vanaras, Rakshasas, and Vibheeshana shed tears.

shloka_text: ततःप्रहर्षाद्भरतमङ्गमारोप्यराघवः ।।6.130.57।। ययौतेनविमानेनससैन्योभरताश्रमम् ।
explanation: Then rejoiced Raghava took Bharata on his lap and flew to Bharata's hermitage with the army.

shloka_text: भरताश्रममासाद्यससैन्योराघवस्तदा ।।6.130.58।। अवतीर्यविमानाग्रादवतस्थेमहीतले ।
explanation: Raghava alighted from the top of the Pushpaka on reaching the hermitage of Bharata and stood on ground.

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तुतदारामस्तद्विमानमनुत्तमम् ।।6.130.59।। वहवैश्रवणंदेवमनुजानामिगम्यताम् ।
explanation: Then Rama told Pushpaka that he was permitted to go to God Vysravana.

shloka_text: ततोरामाभ्यनुज्ञातंतद्विमानमनुत्तमम् ।।6.130.60।। उत्तरांदिशमुद्दिश्यजगामधनदालयम् ।
explanation: That aerial car duly permitted by Rama rose up to go to Kubera and set out in the northern direction and flew.

shloka_text: विमानंपुष्पकंदिव्यंसम्गृहीतंतुरक्षसा ।।6.130.61।। अगमद्धनदंवेगाद्रामवाक्यप्रचोदितम् ।
explanation: That wonderful Pushpaka received from Rakshasa impelled by Rama's order speedily went to Kubera.

shloka_text: शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधायकैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनः । बभाषेभरतोज्येष्ठंरामंसत्यपराक्रमम् ।।6.131.1।।
explanation: Bharata, the enhancer of Kaikeyi's joy, of unfailing valour, with folded palms on head submitted to his elder brother.

shloka_text: पूजितामामिकामातादत्तंराज्यमिदंमम । तद्ददामिपुनस्तुभ्यंयथात्वमददामम ।।6.131.2।।
explanation: "This kingdom was bestowed on me and my mother. I return it back to you now again."

shloka_text: धुरमेकाकिनान्यस्तांवृषभेणबलीयसा । किशोरवद्गुरुंभारं न वोढुमहमुत्सहे ।।6.131.3।।
explanation: "I am not able to bear the heavy burden transferred to me any more like a young ox can't bear like a bull.

shloka_text: वारिवेगेनमहताभिन्नस्सेतुरिवक्षरन् । दुर्बन्धनमिदंमन्येराज्यच्छ्रिदमसम्वृतम् ।।6.131.4।।
explanation: "If the kingdom containing vulnerable points is not protected on all sides, it can't stand, just as a strong rush of water can be prevented from breach only by constructing a dam.

shloka_text: गतिंखरइवाश्वस्यहंसस्येव च वायसः । नान्वेतुमुत्सहेराम तवमार्गमरिन्दम ।।6.131.5।।
explanation: "O Rama! Donkey can't run like horse crow can't run like swan. I am not able to bear the burden of kingdom like you, O tormentor of enemies."

shloka_text: यथाचारोपितोवृक्षोजातश्चार्न्न्तिवेशने । महांश्चसुदुरारोहोमहास्कन्दःप्रशाखवान् ।।6.131.6।। शीर्येतपुष्पितोभूत्वा न फलानिप्रदर्शयन् । तस्यनानुभवेदर्थंयस्यहेतोस्सरोपितः ।।6.131.7।। एषोपमामहाबाहोत्वमर्थंवेत्तुमर्हसि । यद्यस्मान्मनुजेन्द्रत्वंभर्ताभृत्यान्नशाधिहि ।।6.131.8।।
explanation: "If for example you have planted a tree in your own house, it becomes huge and difficult to climb in spite of a large trunk, many branches and after flowering does not yield fruits and is withered, the person who planted will not enjoy the fruit. In that way O mighty armed Rama, you are the ruler of the people, if you would not take care of us, your dependants, I solicit you ought to understand what I mean.

shloka_text: यथाचारोपितोवृक्षोजातश्चार्न्न्तिवेशने । महांश्चसुदुरारोहोमहास्कन्दःप्रशाखवान् ।।6.131.6।। शीर्येतपुष्पितोभूत्वा न फलानिप्रदर्शयन् । तस्यनानुभवेदर्थंयस्यहेतोस्सरोपितः ।।6.131.7।। एषोपमामहाबाहोत्वमर्थंवेत्तुमर्हसि । यद्यस्मान्मनुजेन्द्रत्वंभर्ताभृत्यान्नशाधिहि ।।6.131.8।।
explanation: "If for example you have planted a tree in your own house, it becomes huge and difficult to climb in spite of a large trunk, many branches and after flowering does not yield fruits and is withered, the person who planted will not enjoy the fruit. In that way O mighty armed Rama, you are the ruler of the people, if you would not take care of us, your dependants, I solicit you ought to understand what I mean.

shloka_text: यथाचारोपितोवृक्षोजातश्चार्न्न्तिवेशने । महांश्चसुदुरारोहोमहास्कन्दःप्रशाखवान् ।।6.131.6।। शीर्येतपुष्पितोभूत्वा न फलानिप्रदर्शयन् । तस्यनानुभवेदर्थंयस्यहेतोस्सरोपितः ।।6.131.7।। एषोपमामहाबाहोत्वमर्थंवेत्तुमर्हसि । यद्यस्मान्मनुजेन्द्रत्वंभर्ताभृत्यान्नशाधिहि ।।6.131.8।।
explanation: "If for example you have planted a tree in your own house, it becomes huge and difficult to climb in spite of a large trunk, many branches and after flowering does not yield fruits and is withered, the person who planted will not enjoy the fruit. In that way O mighty armed Rama, you are the ruler of the people, if you would not take care of us, your dependants, I solicit you ought to understand what I mean.

shloka_text: जगदद्याभिषिक्तंत्वामनुपश्यतुराघव । प्रतपन्तमिवादित्यंमध्याह्नेदीप्ततेजसम् ।।6.131.9।।
explanation: "Raghava, let you be consecrated in the afternoon and the world will see you dazzling in brilliance like the sun today."

shloka_text: तूर्यसङ्घान्तिर्घोषैःकाञ्चीनूपुरनिःस्वनैः । मधुरैर्गीतशब्दैश्चप्रतिबुध्यस्वशेष्व च ।।6.131.10।।
explanation: May you wake up to the sounds of musical instruments and the tinkling of ornaments worn around the waist and anklets and sweet sounds of singing.

shloka_text: यावदावर्ततेचक्रंयावती च वसुन्धरा । तावत्त्वमिहलोकस्यस्वामित्वमनुवर्तय ।।6.131.11।।
explanation: As long as the stellar sphere goes round, and as long as the earth revolves around that long you enjoy the rulership of the world."

shloka_text: भरतस्यवच्श्रुत्वारामःपरपुरञ्जयः । तथेतिप्रतिजग्राहनिषसादासनेशुभे ।।6.131.12।।
explanation: Hearing Bharata's words, the conqueror of enemies, Rama said 'Be it so'. Then Bharata took the auspicious seat.

shloka_text: ततश्शत्रुघ्नवचनान्निपुणाःश्मश्रुवर्धनाः । सुखहस्ताःसुशीघ्राश्चराघवंपर्यवारयन् ।।6.131.13।।
explanation: Then at the command of Shatrughna's words, experts with hand work (barbers) who had soft skills quickly surrounded Raghava.

shloka_text: पूर्वंतुभरतेस्नातेलक्ष्मणे च महाबले । सुग्रीवेवानरेन्द्रे च राक्षसेन्द्रेविभीषणे ।।6.131.14।। विशोधितजटस्स्नातश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः । महार्हवसनोपेतस्तस्थौतत्रश्रियाज्वलन् ।।6.131.15।।
explanation: Bharata had his bath first, and mighty Lakshmana, Sugriva the monkey king, and Vibheeshana the Rakshasa king followed him. Sri Rama removed the matted hair, had bath, adorned with colourful garlands, and daubed with sandal paste and clothed in exquisite robes stood glowing and shining.

shloka_text: पूर्वंतुभरतेस्नातेलक्ष्मणे च महाबले । सुग्रीवेवानरेन्द्रे च राक्षसेन्द्रेविभीषणे ।।6.131.14।। विशोधितजटस्स्नातश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः । महार्हवसनोपेतस्तस्थौतत्रश्रियाज्वलन् ।।6.131.15।।
explanation: Bharata had his bath first, and mighty Lakshmana, Sugriva the monkey king, and Vibheeshana the Rakshasa king followed him. Sri Rama removed the matted hair, had bath, adorned with colourful garlands, and daubed with sandal paste and clothed in exquisite robes stood glowing and shining.

shloka_text: प्रतिकर्म च रामस्यकारयामासवीर्यवान । लक्ष्मणस्य च लक्ष्मीवानिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्धनः ।।6.131.16।।
explanation: Then valiant and prosperous, Shatrughna, who is an enhancer of the glory of Ikshvaku race decorated Sri Rama and Lakshmana (duly with ornaments).

shloka_text: प्रतिकर्मचसीतायास्सर्वादशरथस्त्रियः । आत्मनैवतदाचक्रुर्मनस्विन्योमनोहरम् ।।6.131.17।।
explanation: Then all the nobleminded Dasharatha's wives themselves decorated Sita beautifully.

shloka_text: ततोवानरपत्नीनांसर्वासामेवशोभनम् । चकारयत्नात्कौसल्याप्रहृष्टापुत्रवत्सला ।।6.131.18।।
explanation: The very delighted Kausalya, lover of her sons started making effort to decorate the wives of all Vanaras in a splendid manner.

shloka_text: तत: श्शत्रुघ्नवचनात्सुमन्त्रोनामसारथिः । योजयित्वाभिचक्रामरथंसर्वाङ्गशोभनम् ।।6.131.19।।
explanation: Then Sumantra the charioteer, commanded by Shatrughna came there with all parts of the chariot decorated and yoked.

shloka_text: अर्कमण्डलसङ्काशंदिव्यंदृष्टवारथंस्थितम् । आरुरोहमहाबाहूरामःपरपुरंञ्जयः ।।6.131.20।।
explanation: Seeing the wonderful chariot like the radiance of the planet sun, mighty armed Rama the conqueror of hostile enemies ascended.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवोहनुमांश्चैवमहेन्द्रसदृशद्युती । स्नातौदिव्यनिभैर्वस्त्रैर्जग्मतुश्शुभकुण्डलौ ।।6.131.21।।
explanation: Sugriva and Hanuman having bathed wore sparkling earrings, clothed in heavenly robes vied with Mahendra in splendour, started.

shloka_text: सर्वाभरणजुष्टाश्चयुयुस्तश्शुभकुण्डलाः । सुग्रीवपत्नयःसीता च द्रष्टुंनगरमुत्सुकाः ।।6.131.22।।
explanation: Sugriva's wife and Sita decked with all kinds of ornaments and earrings, enthused to see the city, started.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायांतुसचिवाराज्ञोदशरथस्य च । पुरोहितंपुरस्कृत्यमन्त्रयामासुरर्थवत् ।।6.131.23।।
explanation: At Ayodhya also, king Dasharatha's ministers, priests started to Vasishta and thought of the required arrangements.

shloka_text: अशोकोविजयश्चैवसिद्धार्थश्चसमाहिताः । मन्त्रयन्रामवृध्यर्थंबुध्यर्थंनगरस्य च ।।6.131.24।।
explanation: Ashoka, Vijaya, Siddhartha, collected together and started consulting with each other for the growth of Rama and the City.

shloka_text: सर्वमेवाभिषेकार्थंजयार्हस्यमहात्मनः । कर्तुमर्हथरामस्ययद्यन्मङ्गलपूर्वकम् ।।6.131.25।।
explanation: For the success of the great soul Rama's consecration, whatever was auspicious, all that ought to be done as he deserves.

shloka_text: इतितेमन्त्रिणस्सर्वेसन्दिश्य च पुरोहितम् । नगरान्निर्ययुस्तूर्णंरामदर्शनबुद्धयः ।।6.131.26।।
explanation: All those ministers, priests thus communicating with each other, speedily set forth to have a glance at Sri Rama.

shloka_text: हरियुक्तंसहस्राक्षोरथमिन्द्रइवानघः । प्रययौरथमास्थायरामोनगरमुत्तमम् ।।6.131.27।।
explanation: Like the thousand eyed Indra seated in the excellent chariot yoked to green horses, the sinless Rama departed to the city.

shloka_text: जग्राहभरतोरमशीन्शत्रुघ्नश्चत्रमाददे । लक्ष्मणोव्यजनंतस्यमूर्ध्निसम्पर्यवीजयत् ।।6.131.28।। श्वेतं च वालव्यजनंजगृहेपरितस्स्थितः । अपरंचन्द्रसङ्काशंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.131.29।।
explanation: Bharata held the reins, Shatrughna took hold of the parasol, Lakshmana standing in front held the fan, and the Rakshasa king Vibheeshana held a white whisk which was like a moon for driving the air.

shloka_text: जग्राहभरतोरमशीन्शत्रुघ्नश्चत्रमाददे । लक्ष्मणोव्यजनंतस्यमूर्ध्निसम्पर्यवीजयत् ।।6.131.28।। श्वेतं च वालव्यजनंजगृहेपरितस्स्थितः । अपरंचन्द्रसङ्काशंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.131.29।।
explanation: Bharata held the reins, Shatrughna took hold of the parasol, Lakshmana standing in front held the fan, and the Rakshasa king Vibheeshana held a white whisk which was like a moon for driving the air.

shloka_text: ऋषिसङ्घैस्तदाकाशेदेवैश्चसमरुद्गणैः । स्तूयमास्यरामस्यशुश्रुवमधुरध्वनिः ।।6.131.30।।
explanation: Then the host of sages, Rudras and gods from the heaven started praising Rama with sweet sounding chanting.

shloka_text: ततःशत्रुञ्जयंनामकुञ्जरंपर्वतोपमम् । आरुरोहमहातेजास्सुग्रीवःप्लवगर्षभः ।।6.131.31।।
explanation: Then resplendent Sugriva, the bull among Vanaras, ascended the mountain like elephant by the name Satrumjaya.

shloka_text: नवनागसहस्राणिययुरास्थायवानराः । मानुषंविग्रहंकृत्वासर्वाभरणभूषिताः ।।6.131.32।।
explanation: Assuming human semblance, the Vanaras adorned with ornaments ascended nine thousand elephants and departed.

shloka_text: शङ्खशब्दप्रणादैश्चदुन्दुभीनां च निस्स्वनैः । प्रययौपुरुषव्याघ्रस्तांपुरींहर्म्यमालिनीम् ।।6.131.33।।
explanation: Sri Rama the tiger among men went accompanied by sounds of blasts of conches and shouts and roll of drums along the rows of mansions in the city.

shloka_text: ददृशुस्तेसमायान्तंराघवंसपुरस्सरम् । विराजमानंवपुषारथेनातिरथंतदा ।।6.131.34।।
explanation: Then they saw all those who had gone to Ayodhya coming in advance in accordance with tradition, to receive Rama, the great car warrior, who was shining brightly advancing by the chariot.

shloka_text: तेवर्थयित्वाकाकुत्स्थंरामेणप्रतिनन्दिताः । अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानंभ्रातृभिःपरिवारितम् ।।6.131.35।।
explanation: They were blessing Sri Rama in turn and Rama responded to them very happily. Surrounded by brothers and all followed Rama the great soul.

shloka_text: अमात्यैर्ब्राह्मणैश्चैवतथाप्रकृतिभिर्ववृतः । श्रियाविरुरुचेरामोनक्षत्ररिवचन्द्रमाः ।।6.131.36।।
explanation: Surrounded by ministers, brahmins and common people, glorious Rama shone brightly like the moon surrounded by stars.

shloka_text: स पुरोगामिभिस्तूर्यैस्तालस्वस्तिकपाणिभिः । प्रव्याहरद्भिर्मुदितैर्मङ्गलानिवृतोययौ ।।6.131.37।।
explanation: He went forward surrounded by bands, trumpets, wooden cymbals and swastikas and very happily singing auspicious festive songs.

shloka_text: अक्षतंजातरूपं च गावःकन्यास्सहद्विजाः । नरामोदकहस्ताश्चरामस्यपुरतोययुः ।।6.131.38।।
explanation: Taking yellow rice (rice smeared with turmeric) appearing like gold, cows, virgin women, brahmins with Modakas in hand went before Rama.

shloka_text: सख्यं च रामस्सुग्रीवेप्रभावंचानिलात्मजे । वानराणां च तत्कर्मह्याचचक्षेऽऽथमन्त्रिणाम् ।।6.131.39।।
explanation: Rama narrated about his friendship with Sugriva and the distinct performance of Hanuman and Vanaras to the ministers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा च विस्मयंजग्मुरयोध्यापुरवासिनः । वानराणां च ततकर्मराक्षसानां च तद्बलम् ।।6.131.40।।
explanation: Hearing about the action of Vanaras and the strength of Rakshasas, the citizens of Ayodhya were astonished.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्यसम्योगमाचचक्षेऽथमन्त्रिणाम् । द्युतिमानेतदाख्यायरामोवानरसम्युतः ।।6.131.41।। हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णमयोध्यांप्रविवेशसः ।
explanation: Sri Rama narrated about Vibheeshana's friendship to the ministers. Splendorous Rama then entered Ayodhya filled with very happy people accompanied by Vanaras.

shloka_text: ततोह्यभ्युच्छ्रयन्पौराःपताकाश्चगृहेगृहे ।।6.131.42।। ऐक्ष्वाकुध्युषितंरम्यमाससादपितुर्गृहम् ।
explanation: The citizens of Ayodhya held the flags up in every house. Thereupon Rama reached the beautiful home of his father, the abode of the Ikshvaku dynasty.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रोभरतंधर्मिणांवरम् ।।6.131.43।। अर्धोपहितयावाचामधुरंरघुनन्दनः । पितुर्भवनमासाद्यप्रविश्य च महात्मनः ।।6.131.44।। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीमभिवाद्य च ।
explanation: And thereafter prince Rama, the joy of Raghus, the great soul reached father's mansion and then to Kausalya's and to Sumitra, to Kaikeyi and greeted them. He then spoke meaningful words to virtuous Bharata in a sweet tone.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्राजपुत्रोभरतंधर्मिणांवरम् ।।6.131.43।। अर्धोपहितयावाचामधुरंरघुनन्दनः । पितुर्भवनमासाद्यप्रविश्य च महात्मनः ।।6.131.44।। कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीमभिवाद्य च ।
explanation: And thereafter prince Rama, the joy of Raghus, the great soul reached father's mansion and then to Kausalya's and to Sumitra, to Kaikeyi and greeted them. He then spoke meaningful words to virtuous Bharata in a sweet tone.

shloka_text: यच्छमद्भवनंश्रेष्ठंसाशोकवनिकंमहत् ।।6.131.45।। मुक्तावैदूर्यसङ्कीर्णंसुग्रीवायनिवेदय ।
explanation: Let the splendid, excellent mansion attached to Ashoka grove, encrusted with cat's eye gems and pearls be placed at the disposal of Sugriva.

shloka_text: तस्यतद्वचनंश्रुत्वाभरतस्सत्यविक्रमः ।।6.131.46।। हस्तेगृहीत्वासुग्रीवंप्रविवेशतमालयम् ।
explanation: Then that upright Bharata hearing the words of Rama taking the hand of Sugriva led him to that temple like abode.

shloka_text: तत: स्स्सैलप्रदीपांश्चपर्यङ्कास्तरणानि च ।।6.131.47।। गृहीत्वाविविशुःक्षिप्रंशत्रुघ्नेप्रचोदिताः ।
explanation: Then as commanded by Shatrughna, people taking glowing oil lamps and coverlets for the couches quickly entered the palace.

shloka_text: उवाच च महातेजास्सुग्रीवंराघवानुजः ।।6.131.48।। अभिषेकायरामस्यदूतानाज्ञापयप्रभो ।
explanation: Highly brilliant Sugriva said to Bharata, "Let envoys be sent for the consecration of Rama."

shloka_text: सौवर्णान्वानरेन्द्राणांचतुर्णांचतुरोघटान् ।।6.131.49।। ददौक्षिप्रंससुग्रीवस्सर्वरत्नविभूषितान् ।
explanation: Sugriva instantly gave four golden pots decorated well to the four Vanara leaders.

shloka_text: यथाप्रत्यूषसमयेचतुर्णांसागराम्बसाम् ।।6.131.50।। पूर्णघटैःप्रतीक्षध्वंतथाकुरुतवानराः ।
explanation: Sugriva gave four pots to the four of the Vanaras to get them filled with the water of the four oceans and get them by early morning and said to await for him.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तामहात्मानोवानरावारणोपमाः ।।6.131.51।। उत्पेतुर्गगनंशीघ्रंगरुडाइवशीघ्रगाः ।
explanation: Having spoken like that by Sugriva, the Vanaras of mountainlike forms fled like Garuda into the sky quickly.

shloka_text: जाम्बवांश्चहनूमांश्चवेगदर्शी च वानरः ।।6.131.52।। ऋषभश्चैवकलशान्जलपूर्णानथानयन् । नदीशतानांपञ्चानांजलंकुम्भैरुपाहरन् ।।6.131.53।। पूर्वात्समुद्रात्कलशंजलपूर्णमथानयत् । सुषेणस्सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् ।।6.131.54।।
explanation: Jambavan, Hanuman, Vegadarsa and Rshaba brought pots of water from the seas. Another five hundred monkeys brought five hundred pots from five hundred rivers of the country. Jambavan richly endowed with courage brought in a pot encrusted with all kinds of gems. Sushena brought water from the eastern sea.

shloka_text: जाम्बवांश्चहनूमांश्चवेगदर्शी च वानरः ।।6.131.52।। ऋषभश्चैवकलशान्जलपूर्णानथानयन् । नदीशतानांपञ्चानांजलंकुम्भैरुपाहरन् ।।6.131.53।। पूर्वात्समुद्रात्कलशंजलपूर्णमथानयत् । सुषेणस्सत्त्वसम्पन्नस्सर्वरत्नविभूषितम् ।।6.131.54।।
explanation: Jambavan, Hanuman, Vegadarsa and Rshaba brought pots of water from the seas. Another five hundred monkeys brought five hundred pots from five hundred rivers of the country. shloka_text: ऋषभोदक्षिणात्तूर्णंसमुद्राज्जलमानयत् । रक्तचन्दनशाखाभिस्सम्वृतंकाञ्चनंघटम् ।।6.131.55।।
explanation: Rshaba quickly brought water from the southern sea in a golden pot covered with sandal paste.

shloka_text: गवयःपश्चिमात्तोयमाजहारमहार्णवात् । रत्नकुम्भेनमहताशीतंमारुतविक्रमः ।।6.131.56।।
explanation: Gavaya, an expert like WindGod brought cold water from the abode of Varuna in the west, in a pot encrusted with gems.

shloka_text: उत्तराच्चजलंशीघ्रंगरुडानिलविक्रमः । आजहार स धर्मात्मानलःसर्वगुणान्वितः ।।6.131.57।।
explanation: Nala who vied with Garuda in speed, a righteous one, endowed with all virtues quickly brought water from the north.

shloka_text: ततस्तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरानीतंप्रेक्ष्यतज्जलम् । अभिषेकायरामस्यशत्रुघ्नस्सचिवैस्सह ।।6.131.58।। पुरोहितायश्रेष्ठायसुहृद्भ्यश्चन्यवेदयत् ।
explanation: Then seeing the water brought by the monkeys for Rama's consecration Shatrugna along with ministers placed them at the disposal of the supreme priest along with friends.

shloka_text: ततस्सप्रयतोवृद्धोवसिष्ठोब्राह्मणैःसह ।।6.131.59।। रामंरत्नमयेपीठेससीतंसन्नयवेशयत् ।
explanation: Then accompanied by brahmins, sage Vasishta, active though aged, asked Sita and Sri Rama to occupy the plank made with full of precious stones.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठोवामदेवश्चजाबालिरथकाश्यपः ।।6.131.60।। कात्यायनोसुयज्ञश्चगौतमोविजयस्तथा । अभ्यषिञ्चन्नरव्याघ्रंप्रसन्नेनसुगन्धिना ।।6.131.61।। सलिलेनसहस्राक्षंवसवोवासवंयथा ।
explanation: Eight sages, Vasishta, Vama Deva, Jabali, Kasyapa, Katyayana, Suyajna, Gautama and Vijaya consecrated Sri Rama, the tiger among men, with pure fragrant waters as the Vasus consecrated the thousand eyed Indra.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठोवामदेवश्चजाबालिरथकाश्यपः ।।6.131.60।। कात्यायनोसुयज्ञश्चगौतमोविजयस्तथा । अभ्यषिञ्चन्नरव्याघ्रंप्रसन्नेनसुगन्धिना ।।6.131.61।। सलिलेनसहस्राक्षंवसवोवासवंयथा ।
explanation: Eight sages, Vasishta, Vama Deva, Jabali, Kasyapa, Katyayana, Suyajna, Gautama and Vijaya consecrated Sri Rama, the tiger among men, with pure fragrant waters as the Vasus consecrated the thousand eyed Indra.

shloka_text: ऋग्भिर्भ्राह्मणैःपूर्वंकन्याभिर्मन्त्रिभिस्तथा ।।6.131.62।। योथौश्चैवाभ्यषिञ्चंस्तेसम्प्रहृष्टास्सनैगमैः । सर्वौषधीनसैश्चापिदैवतैर्नभसिस्थितैः ।।6.131.63।। चतुर्भिर्लोकपालैश्चसर्वैर्देवैश्चसङ्गतैः ।
explanation: First by priests, followed by brahmins, virgin women, so also ministers, merchants, warriors consecrated. Those who stood in the sky, the gods, the rulers of the four quarters, and all gods consecrated by sprinkling water containing medicinal herbs. All were very delighted.

shloka_text: ऋग्भिर्भ्राह्मणैःपूर्वंकन्याभिर्मन्त्रिभिस्तथा ।।6.131.62।। योथौश्चैवाभ्यषिञ्चंस्तेसम्प्रहृष्टास्सनैगमैः । सर्वौषधीनसैश्चापिदैवतैर्नभसिस्थितैः ।।6.131.63।। चतुर्भिर्लोकपालैश्चसर्वैर्देवैश्चसङ्गतैः ।
explanation: First by priests, followed by brahmins, virgin women, so also ministers, merchants, warriors consecrated. Those who stood in the sky, the gods, the rulers of the four quarters, and all gods consecrated by sprinkling water containing medicinal herbs. All were very delighted.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणानिर्मितंपूर्वंकिरीटंरत्नशोभितम् ।।6.131.64।। अभिषिक्तःपुरायेवमनुस्तंदीप्ततेजसम् । तस्यान्ववायेराजानःक्रमाद्येनाभिषेचिताः ।।6.131.65।। सभायांहेमक्लुप्तायांशोभितायांमहाधनैः । रत्नैर्नानाविधैश्चवचित्रितायांसुशोभनैः ।।6.131.66।। नानारत्नमयेपीठेकल्पयित्वायथाविधि । किरीटेनततःपश्चाद्वसिष्ठेनमहात्मना ।।6.131.67।। ऋत्विगिमभगिर्भूषणैश्चैवसमयोक्ष्यतराघवः ।
explanation: In the past, Manu was consecrated with a crown encrusted with gems crafted by Brahma and it was adorned at consecration by successive kings. After the consecration, Rama was dazzling seated on a throne made of several kinds of gems as per tradition. The council hall was also made of gold with charming pictures and looked splendid. The great soul Raghava was crowned and adorned with ornaments by Vasishta and the priests.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणानिर्मितंपूर्वंकिरीटंरत्नशोभितम् ।।6.131.64।। अभिषिक्तःपुरायेवमनुस्तंदीप्ततेजसम् । तस्यान्ववायेराजानःक्रमाद्येनाभिषेचिताः ।।6.131.65।। सभायांहेमक्लुप्तायांशोभितायांमहाधनैः । रत्नैर्नानाविधैश्चवचित्रितायांसुशोभनैः ।।6.131.66।। नानारत्नमयेपीठेकल्पयित्वायथाविधि । किरीटेनततःपश्चाद्वसिष्ठेनमहात्मना ।।6.131.67।। ऋत्विगिमभगिर्भूषणैश्चैवसमयोक्ष्यतराघवः ।
