shloka_text: छत्रंतस्य च जग्राहशत्रघ्नःपाण्डुरंशुभम् ।।6.131.68।। श्वेतं च वालव्यजनंसुग्रीवोवानरेश्वरः । अपरंचन्द्रसङ्काशंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.131.69।।
explanation: Shatrughna held white auspicious parasol, Sugriva the Vanara Lord held a white whisk, Vibheeshana the Lord of Rakshasas held a white whisk shining like the moon.

shloka_text: छत्रंतस्य च जग्राहशत्रघ्नःपाण्डुरंशुभम् ।।6.131.68।। श्वेतं च वालव्यजनंसुग्रीवोवानरेश्वरः । अपरंचन्द्रसङ्काशंराक्षसेन्द्रोविभीषणः ।।6.131.69।।
explanation: Shatrughna held white auspicious parasol, Sugriva the Vanara Lord held a white whisk, Vibheeshana the Lord of Rakshasas held a white whisk shining like the moon.

shloka_text: मालांज्वलन्तींवपुषाकाञ्चनींशतपुष्कराम् । राघवायददौवायुर्वासवेनप्रचोदितः ।।6.131.70।।
explanation: The WindGod prompted by deity Indra presented a dazzling golden garland of hundred flowers to Raghava.

shloka_text: सर्वरत्नसमायुक्तंमणिभिश्चविभूषितम् । मुक्ताहारंनरेन्द्रायददौशक्रप्रचोदितः ।।6.131.71।।
explanation: Urged by Indra the wind god gave a dazzling pearls chain intercepted by several kinds of gems and precious stones to the ruler of the world.

shloka_text: प्रजगुर्धेवगन्धर्वाननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः । अभिषेकेतदर्हस्यतदारामस्यधीमतः ।।6.131.72।।
explanation: The Gandharvas from among the gods sang and Apsara groups danced for Rama's consecration.

shloka_text: भूमिःसस्यवतीचैवफलवन्तश्चपादपाः । गन्धवन्ति च पुष्पाणिबभूवूराघवोत्सवे ।।6.131.73।।
explanation: At the time of celebration of Rama's coronation, earth became green with crops, trees bore fruits and filled with flowers which spread fragrance.

shloka_text: सहस्रशतमश्वानांधेनूनां च गवांतथा । ददौशतवृषान्पूर्वंद्विजेभ्योमनुजर्षभः ।।6.131.74।।
explanation: Sri Rama, the bull among men gave first, a hundred thousand cows with just born calves to hundred thousand brahmins.

shloka_text: त्रिंशत्कोटीर्हिरण्यस्यब्राह्मणेभ्योददौपुनः । नानाभरणवस्त्राणिमहार्हाणि च राघवः ।।6.131.75।।
explanation: Raghava again gave brahmins thirty crores of golden coins and different kinds of ornaments and clothes.

shloka_text: अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशांकाञ्चनींमणिविग्रहाम् । सुग्रीवायस्रजंदिव्यांप्रायच्छन्मनुजाधिपः ।।6.131.76।।
explanation: Sri Rama gave a wonderful golden garland with a stretch of gems tied to it which was dazzling like the sun's rays to Sugriva.

shloka_text: वैदूर्यमयचित्रे च मणिरत्नविभूषिते । वालिपुत्रायधृतिमानङ्गदायाङ्गदेददौ ।।6.131.77।।
explanation: Very lovingly Rama gave Angada the son of Vali, wonderful armlets encrusted with cat's eye stones and precious gems.

shloka_text: मणिप्रवरजुष्टंतुमुक्ताहारमनुत्तमम् । सीतायैप्रददौरामश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभम् ।।6.131.78।। अरजेवाससीदिव्येशुभान्याभरणानि च । अवेक्षमाणावैदेहीप्रददौवायुसूनवे ।।6.131.79।।
explanation: Rama gave Sita an unsurpassed pearl chain (given to him by the wind god) encrusted with the best of gems and corals wonderfully shining like moonbeams. And Sita looking at Rama presented that immaculate wonderful pearl chain, and splendid clothes with some ornaments to Hanuman.

shloka_text: मणिप्रवरजुष्टंतुमुक्ताहारमनुत्तमम् । सीतायैप्रददौरामश्चन्द्ररश्मिसमप्रभम् ।।6.131.78।। अरजेवाससीदिव्येशुभान्याभरणानि च । अवेक्षमाणावैदेहीप्रददौवायुसूनवे ।।6.131.79।।
explanation: Rama gave Sita an unsurpassed pearl chain (given to him by the wind god) encrusted with the best of gems and corals wonderfully shining like moonbeams. And Sita looking at Rama presented that immaculate wonderful pearl chain, and splendid clothes with some ornaments to Hanuman.

shloka_text: अवमुच्यात्मनःकण्ठाद्दारंजनकनन्दिनी । अवैक्षतहरीन्सर्वान्भर्तारं च मुहुर्मुहुः ।।6.131.80।।
explanation: Removing the pearl chain from her neck, Janaki looked at all the monkeys as well as her husband again and again.

shloka_text: तामिङ्गितज्ञस्सम्प्रेक्ष्य बभाषे जनकात्मजाम् । प्रदेहिसुभगेहारंयस्यतुष्टासिभामिनि ।।6.131.81।। तेजोधृतिर्यशोदाक्ष्यंसामर्थ्यंविनयोनयः । पौरुषंविक्रमोबुद्धिर्यस्मिन्नेतानिसर्वदा ।।6.131.82।।
explanation: Seeing Janaki looking at him, Rama who could read her mind, and said" Lovely Sita, Beautiful young lady, give the pearl chain to one with whom you are pleased." Sita you may give the chain to one in whom you always found to have brilliance, determination, fame, dexterity, capacity, modesty, prudence, virility, prowess, and intelligence always.

shloka_text: तामिङ्गितज्ञस्सम्प्रेक्ष्य बभाषे जनकात्मजाम् । प्रदेहिसुभगेहारंयस्यतुष्टासिभामिनि ।।6.131.81।। तेजोधृतिर्यशोदाक्ष्यंसामर्थ्यंविनयोनयः । पौरुषंविक्रमोबुद्धिर्यस्मिन्नेतानिसर्वदा ।।6.131.82।।
explanation: Seeing Janaki looking at him, Rama who could read her mind, and said" Lovely Sita, Beautiful young lady, give the pearl chain to one with whom you are pleased." Sita you may give the chain to one in whom you always found to have brilliance, determination, fame, dexterity, capacity, modesty, prudence, virility, prowess, and intelligence always.

shloka_text: ददौसावायुपुत्रायतंहारमसितेक्षणा । हनूमांस्तेनहारेणशुशुभेवानरर्षभः ।।6.131.83।। चन्रांशुचयगौरेणश्वेताभ्रेणयथाचलः ।
explanation: Blackeyed Sita, gave that chain to Hanuman, the bull among Vanaras who shone like a mountain behind white silver like cloud.

shloka_text: तोद्विविदमैन्धाभ्यांनीलाय च परन्तपः सर्वेवानरवृद्धाश्चयेचान्येवानरोत्तमाः ।।6.131.84।। वासोभिर्भूषणैश्चैवयथार्हंप्रतिपूजिताः । सर्वान्कामगुणावनीक्ष्यप्रददौवसुधाधिपः।।। 6.131.85।।
explanation: Then Sri Rama, the tormentor of enemies, the ruler of the earth looking at Mainda, Dwivida and Neela presented articles according to their desires. For the aged among the Vanaras and the foremost Vanaras, he gave ornaments and garments duly as much as they deserved and worshipped.

shloka_text: तोद्विविदमैन्धाभ्यांनीलाय च परन्तपः सर्वेवानरवृद्धाश्चयेचान्येवानरोत्तमाः ।।6.131.84।। वासोभिर्भूषणैश्चैवयथार्हंप्रतिपूजिताः । सर्वान्कामगुणावनीक्ष्यप्रददौवसुधाधिपः।।। 6.131.85।।
explanation: Then Sri Rama, the tormentor of enemies, the ruler of the earth looking at Mainda, Dwivida and Neela presented articles according to their desires. For the aged among the Vanaras and the foremost Vanaras, he gave ornaments and garments duly as much as they deserved and worshipped.

shloka_text: विभीषणोऽथसुग्रीवोहनुमान्जाम्बवांस्तथा ।।6.131.86।। सर्वेवानरमुख्याश्चरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । यथार्हंपूजिताःसर्वेकामैरत्नैश्चपुष्कलैः ।।6.131.87।। प्रहृष्टमानसःसर्वेजग्मुरेवयथागतम् ।
explanation: And thereafter Vibheeshana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, all Vanara chiefs of unwearied action having received gifts, abundant gems, and desired objects as they deserved from Rama. They worshipped Rama and very delighted at heart went to their respective places.

shloka_text: विभीषणोऽथसुग्रीवोहनुमान्जाम्बवांस्तथा ।।6.131.86।। सर्वेवानरमुख्याश्चरामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । यथार्हंपूजिताःसर्वेकामैरत्नैश्चपुष्कलैः ।।6.131.87।। प्रहृष्टमानसःसर्वेजग्मुरेवयथागतम् ।
explanation: And thereafter Vibheeshana, Sugriva, Hanuman, Jambavan, all Vanara chiefs of unwearied action having received gifts, abundant gems, and desired objects as they deserved from Rama. They worshipped Rama and very delighted at heart went to their respective places.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वासर्वेमहात्मानस्ततस्तेवानरर्षभाः ।।6.131.88।। विसृष्टाःपार्थिवेन्द्रेणकिष्किन्धांसमुपागमन् ।
explanation: All the high souled bulls among Vanaras, lauded by the ruler of the earth departed to Kishkinda after seeing the great celebration.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवोवानरश्रेष्ठो दृष्टवारामभिषेचनम् ।।6.131.89।। पूजितश्चैवरामेयकिष्किन्धांप्राविशत्पुरीम् ।
explanation: Sugriva, the foremost of the Vanaras having seen Rama's coronation and been honoured, entered Kishkinda.

shloka_text: विभीषणोऽपिधर्मात्मासहतैर्नैरृतर्षभैः ।।6.131.90।। लब्ध्वाकुलधनंराजालङ्कांप्रायान् महायशाः ।
explanation: Vibheeshana, the bull of Rakshasas, of great fame and a righteous king, having received family fortune departed to Lanka.

shloka_text: सराज्यमखिलंशासन्निहतारिर्महायशाः ।।6.131.91।। राघवःपरमोदारश्शशासपरयामुदा ।
explanation: Highly renowned and generous Raghava, putting an end to enemies ruled the entire kingdom with great joy. He said to Lakshmana who was a lover of duty and knower of dharma.

shloka_text: उवाचलक्ष्मणंरामोधर्मज्ञंधर्मवत्सलः ।।6.131.92।। आतिष्ठधर्मज्ञ मयासहेमांगांपूर्वराजाध्युषितांबलेन । तुल्यंमयात्वंपितृभिर्धृतायातांयौवराज्येधुरमुद्वहस्व ।।6.131.93।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! You are a knower of dharma and a lover of dharma. Prior to my consecration, this kingdom was ruled by former kings, fathers, and forefathers also with the help of the army. You bear the burden equally with me by being installed as Prince Regent", said Rama.

shloka_text: उवाचलक्ष्मणंरामोधर्मज्ञंधर्मवत्सलः ।।6.131.92।। आतिष्ठधर्मज्ञ मयासहेमांगांपूर्वराजाध्युषितांबलेन । तुल्यंमयात्वंपितृभिर्धृतायातांयौवराज्येधुरमुद्वहस्व ।।6.131.93।।
explanation: "Lakshmana! You are a knower of dharma and a lover of dharma. Prior to my consecration, this kingdom was ruled by former kings, fathers, and forefathers also with the help of the army. You bear the burden equally with me by being installed as Prince Regent", said Rama.

shloka_text: सर्वात्मनापर्यनुनीयमानोयदा न सौमित्रिरुपैतियोगम् । नियुज्यमानोऽपि च यौवराज्येततोऽभ्यषिञ्चद्भरतंमहात्मा ।।6.131.94।।
explanation: When Saumithri was compelled repeatedly to accept the position of Prince Regent by the high soul great Rama, he had not accepted. Rama consecrated Bharata as Prince Regent.

shloka_text: पौण्डरीकाश्वमेधाभ्यांवाजपेयेनचासकृत् । अन्यैश्चविविधैर्यज्ञैरयजत्पार्थिवात्मजः ।।6.131.95।।
explanation: Rama, the son of Dasharatha, had performed many a time Pundarika, Aswamedha, Vajapeya and several other yajnas and propitiated gods.

shloka_text: राज्यंदशसहस्राणिप्राप्यवर्षाणिराघवः । शताश्वमेधानाजह्रेसदश्वान् भूरिदक्षिणान् ।।6.131.96।।
explanation: Raghava in the ten thousand years of his rule performed hundred horse sacrifices with excellent horses and gave donations liberally.

shloka_text: आजानुलम्बिबाहुस्समहावक्षाःप्रतापवान् । लक्ष्मणानुचरोरामःशशासपृथिवीमिमाम् ।।6.131.97।।
explanation: Sri Rama whose arms reached unto knees, endowed with broadchest and stupendous glory, ruled this earth with Lakshmana as his follower.

shloka_text: राघवश्चापिधर्मात्माप्राप्यराज्यमनुत्तमम् । ईजेबहुविधैर्यज्ञैससुतभ्रातृबान्धवः ।।6.131.98।।
explanation: Righteous Rama also, having inherited the kingdom, conducted several sacrifices with brothers, friends and relatives.

shloka_text: स पर्यदेवन्विधवा न च व्यालकृतंभयम् । न व्याधिजंभयंचासीद्रामेराज्यंप्रशासति ।।6.131.99।।
explanation: While Rama was ruling there was no lamentation of widows (over their loss), fear of cruel animals, or fear of disease.

shloka_text: निर्दस्युरभवल्लोकोनानर्थंकश्चिदस्पृशत् । न च स्मवृद्धाबालानांप्रेतकार्याणिकुर्वते ।।6.131.100।।
explanation: There were no thieves, indeed there was no loss, aged did not perform obsequies (no deaths in the young population) for the young and no harm to people.

shloka_text: सर्वंमुदितमेवासीत्सर्वोधर्मपरोऽभवत् । राममेवानुपश्यन्तोनाभ्यहिंसन् परस्परम् ।।6.131.101।।
explanation: All were happy, and followed the righteous path, looking at Rama alone and no one hit another.

shloka_text: आसन्वर्षसहस्राणितथापुत्रसहस्रिणः । निरामयाविशोकाश्चरामेराज्यंप्रशासति ।।6.131.102।।
explanation: While Rama was ruling for thousands of years, people were blessed with thousands of sons and lived free from trouble and sorrow.

shloka_text: रामोरामोराम: इतिप्रजानामभवन्कथाः । रामभूतंजगदभूद्रामेराज्यंप्रशासति ।।6.131.103।।
explanation: While Rama was ruling the kingdom, everything was Rama, Rama, and Rama. People spoke stories of Rama and the world was resonating with Rama.

shloka_text: नित्यपुष्पानित्यफलान्तरवस्तत्रनिर्व्रणाः । कामवर्षी च पर्जन्यस्सुखस्पर्शश्चमारुतः ।।6.131.104।।
explanation: The trees were always in bloom, and always bore fruits. Clouds sent rain when desired. People lived with delightful feelings.

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणाःक्षत्रियावैश्याश्शूद्रालोभविवर्जिताः । स्वकर्मसुप्रवर्तन्तेतुष्टास्स्वैरेवकर्मभिः ।।6.131.105।। आसन्प्रजाधर्मपरारामेशासतिनानृताः ।
explanation: While Rama ruled brahmins, kshatriyas, vaisyas and sudras were free from avarice, were engaged in their own avocations and delighted. People remained righteous, pious, and never told lies.

shloka_text: सर्वेलक्षणसम्पन्नास्सर्वेधर्मपरायणाः ।।6.131.106।। दशवर्षसहस्राणिदशवर्षशतानि च भ्रातृभि: सहितःश्रीमानरामोराज्यमकारयत् ।
explanation: All were endowed with signs of good culture, given to righteous behaviour. Rama ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years with brothers.

shloka_text: धन्यंयशस्यमायुष्यंराज्ञां च वियावहम् ।।6.131.107।। आदिकाव्यमिदंचार्षंपुरावाल्मीकिनाकृतम् । पठेध्यःशृणुयाल्लोकेनरःपापात्प्रमुच्यते ।।6.131.108।।
explanation: He who reads, listens to this first epic, a noble text composed by Valmiki will be blessed, attain fame, enjoy long life and victory in this world and will be rid of sins.

shloka_text: धन्यंयशस्यमायुष्यंराज्ञां च वियावहम् ।।6.131.107।। आदिकाव्यमिदंचार्षंपुरावाल्मीकिनाकृतम् । पठेध्यःशृणुयाल्लोकेनरःपापात्प्रमुच्यते ।।6.131.108।।
explanation: He who reads, listens to this first epic, a noble text composed by Valmiki will be blessed, attain fame, enjoy long life and victory in this world and will be rid of sins.

shloka_text: पुत्रकामश्चपुत्रान्वैधनकामोधनानि च । लभतेमनुजोलोकेश्रुत्वारामाभिषेचनम् ।।6.131.109।। महींविजयतेराजारिपूंश्चाप्यधितिष्ठति ।
explanation: On hearing about Rama's consecration, in this world, one who is seeking sons will get sons, one who is desirous of wealth will attain wealth, kings will overcome enemies and conquer earth.

shloka_text: राघवेणयथामातासुमित्रालक्ष्मणेन च ।।6.131.110।। भरतेन च कैकेयीजीवपुत्रास्तथास्त्रियः । भविष्यन्तिसदानन्दाःपुत्रपौत्रसमन्विताः ।।6.131.111।।
explanation: Women listening to Ramayana will have Kausalya's Rama, Sumitra's Lakshmana, Kaikeyi's Bharata as living sons and will be always happy and blessed with sons and grandsons.

shloka_text: राघवेणयथामातासुमित्रालक्ष्मणेन च ।।6.131.110।। भरतेन च कैकेयीजीवपुत्रास्तथास्त्रियः । भविष्यन्तिसदानन्दाःपुत्रपौत्रसमन्विताः ।।6.131.111।।
explanation: Women listening to Ramayana will have Kausalya's Rama, Sumitra's Lakshmana, Kaikeyi's Bharata as living sons and will be always happy and blessed with sons and grandsons.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वारामायणमिदंदीर्घमायुश्चविन्दति । रामस्यविजयंचैवसर्वमक्लिष्टकर्मणः ।।6.131.112।।
explanation: He who listens to Ramayana, the story of Rama of unwearied action will be victorious and blessed with long life.

shloka_text: शृणोति य इदंकाव्यंपुरावाल्मीकिनाकृतम् । श्रद्धधानोजितक्रोधोदुर्गाण्यतितरत्यसौ ।।6.131.113।।
explanation: He who listens with devotion, this epic composed by sage Valmiki in the past, will conquer anger and overcome difficulties.

shloka_text: समागम्यप्रवासान्तेरमन्तेसहबान्धवैः । शृण्वन्ति य इदंकाव्यंपुरावाल्मीकिनाकृतम् ।।6.131.114।।
explanation: Whoever listens to this epic written in the past by sage Valmiki will be united with relations and rejoice with them.

shloka_text: तेप्रार्थितान्वरान्सर्वान्प्राप्नुवन्तीहराघवात् । श्रवणेनसुरास्सर्वेप्रीयन्तेसम्प्रशृण्वताम् ।।6.131.115।।
explanation: Those who listen well to Ramayana will obtain all boons here in this world and all gods will be pleased.

shloka_text: विनायकाश्चशाम्यन्तिगृहेतिष्ठन्तियस्यवै । विजयेतमहींराजाप्रवासीस्वस्तिमान्भवेत् ।।6.131.116।।
explanation: The god who removes obstacles will be staying in peace in the house where Ramayana is there. The kings listening to Ramayana will conquer the world and those gone out of home will return back safe.

shloka_text: स्त्रियोरजस्वला्श्रुत्वापुत्रान्सूयुरनुत्तमान् । पूजयंश्चपठंश्चैवमितिहासंपुरातनम् ।।6.131.117।। सर्वपापैःप्रमुच्येतदीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ।
explanation: Women listening to Ramayana prior to pregnancy will deliver sons. This ancient epic if worshipped or read, one will get rid of all sins and attain long life.

shloka_text: प्रणम्यशिरसानित्यंश्रोतव्यंक्षत्रियैर्द्विजात् ।।6.131.118।। ऐश्वर्यंपुत्रलाभाश्चभविष्यति न संशयः । रामायणमिदंकृत्स्नंशृण्वतःपठतस्सदा ।।6.131.119।।
explanation: A kshatriya should always offer salutations with his head bent down before listening to Ramayana from a brahmin. Such a kshatriya will obtain kingship and also beget sons in future. There is no doubt.

shloka_text: प्रणम्यशिरसानित्यंश्रोतव्यंक्षत्रियैर्द्विजात् ।।6.131.118।। ऐश्वर्यंपुत्रलाभाश्चभविष्यति न संशयः । रामायणमिदंकृत्स्नंशृण्वतःपठतस्सदा ।।6.131.119।।
explanation: A kshatriya should always offer salutations with his head bent down before listening to Ramayana from a brahmin. Such a kshatriya will obtain kingship and also beget sons in future. There is no doubt.

shloka_text: प्रीयतेसततंरामस्सहिविष्णुस्सनातनः । आदिदेवोमहाबाहुर्हरिन्नारायणःप्रभुः ।।6.131.120।। साक्षाद्रामोरघुश्रेष्ठश्शेषोलक्ष्मणउच्यते ।
explanation: Rama is said to be ever pleased with him who listens or reads the Ramayana daily. Foremost of Raghus, the mighty armed Rama is eternal Lord Vishnu himself. He is Hari, the ruler Narayana and Lakshmana is Sesha.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तमाख्यानंभद्रमस्तुवः ।।6.131.121।। प्रव्याहरतविस्रब्धंबलंविष्णोःप्रवर्थताम् ।
explanation: This way Ramayana is the ancient narration. Read it daily with trust and devotion. You be auspicious and let the strength of Vishnu grow in you.

shloka_text: देवाश्चसर्वेतुष्यन्तिग्रहणाच्छ्रवणात्तथा ।।6.131.122।। रामायणस्यश्रवणेतुष्यन्तिपितस्सदा ।
explanation: By grasping and listening to Ramayana, all gods will be delighted, ancestors will be pleased.

shloka_text: भक्त्यारामस्ययेचेमांसंसितामृषिणाकृताम् ।।6.131.123।। येलिखन्ती ह च नरास्तेषांवासस्त्रिविष्टपे ।
explanation: Residence in heaven is assured for those who transcribe this Ramayana with devotion and full of meaning, composed by the great sage.

shloka_text: कुटुम्बवृद्धिंधनधान्यवृद्धिंस्त्रियश्चमुख्यास्सुखमुत्तमं च । श्रुत्वाशुभंकाव्यमिदंमहार्थंप्राप्नोतिसर्वांभुविचार्थसिद्धम् ।।6.131.124।।
explanation: Listening to this great auspicious epic will result in the growth of the family, excellent women, augmentation of wealth and grains and comfort on the earth and accomplishment of one's objectives.

shloka_text: प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य राक्षसानां वधे कृते । आजग्मुर्ऋषयः सर्वे राघवं प्रतिनन्दितुम् ।। 7.1.1 ।।
explanation: After Rama had obtained his kingdom and the destruction of the Rakshasas was accomplished, all the sages came to Raghava to congratulate him.

shloka_text: कौशिको ऽथ यवक्रीतो गार्ग्यो गालव एव च । कण्वो मेधातिथेः पुत्रः पूर्वस्यां दिशि ये श्रिताः ।। 7.1.2 ।।
explanation: Kaushika, then Yavakrita, Gargya, and Galava, and Kanva, the son of Medhatithi, who resided in the eastern direction.

shloka_text: स्वस्त्यात्रेयो ऽथ भगवान्नमुचिः प्रमुचिस्तथा । आजग्मुस्ते सहागस्त्या ये श्रिता दक्षिणां दिशम् ।। 7.1.3 ।।
explanation: Then, Svasti, Atreya, and the revered Namuci and Pramuci, along with Agastya, who had resorted to the southern direction, arrived.

shloka_text: नृषद्गुः कवषो धौम्यो रौद्रेयश्च महानृषिः । ते ऽप्याजग्मुः सशिष्या वै ये श्रिताः पश्चिमां दिशम् ।। 7.1.4 ।।
explanation: Nṛṣadgu, Kavaṣa, Dhaumya, and Raudreya, the great sages, who resided in the western direction, also came with their disciples.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठः कश्यपो ऽथात्रिर्विश्वामित्रः सगौतमः । जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजस्ते ऽपि सप्तर्षयस्तथा ।। 7.1.5 ।।
explanation: Vashistha, Kashyapa, Atri, Vishwamitra, Gautama, Jamadagni, and Bharadvaja – these are the seven sages.

shloka_text: उदीच्यां दिशि सप्तैते नित्यमेव निवासिनः ।। 7.1.6 ।।
explanation: These seven are always residents in the northern direction.

shloka_text: सम्प्राप्य ते महात्मानो राघवस्य निवेशनम् । विष्टिताः प्रतिहारार्थं हुताशनसमप्रभाः । वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषो नानाशास्त्रविशारदाः ।। 7.1.7 ।।
explanation: Having reached the abode of Rama, those great-souled ones, radiant like fire, learned in the Vedas and Vedangas, and skilled in various sciences, were stationed for guarding the entrance.

shloka_text: द्वाःस्थं प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः । निवेद्यतां दाशरथेर्ऋषीनस्मान्समागतान् ।। 7.1.8 ।।
explanation: The righteous Agastya, the foremost among sages, said to the doorkeeper: "Inform Dasharatha's son that we, the sages, have arrived."

shloka_text: प्रतीहारस्ततस्तूर्णमगस्त्यवचनाद्द्रुतम् । समीपं राघवस्याशु प्रविवेश महात्मनः ।। 7.1.9 ।।
explanation: Then, the doorkeeper, quickly and swiftly, by the command of Agastya, immediately entered the presence of the great-souled Raghava.

shloka_text: नयेङ्गितज्ञः सद्वृत्तो दक्षो धैर्यसमन्वितः । स रामं दृश्य सहसा पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभम् ।। 7.1.10 ।।
explanation: Skilled in policy and gestures, of good conduct, efficient, and endowed with courage, he, having suddenly seen Rama, who was resplendent like the full moon.

shloka_text: अगस्त्यं कथयामास सम्प्राप्तमृषिभिः सह ।। 7.1.11 ।।
explanation: He told Agastya, who had arrived with the sages.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा प्राप्तान्मुनींस्तांस्तु बालसूर्यसमप्रभान् । प्रत्युवाच ततो द्वास्स्थं प्रवेशय यथासुखम् ।। 7.1.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard that those sages, radiant like the morning sun, had arrived, he then replied to the doorkeeper, "Let them enter comfortably."

shloka_text: तान् सम्प्राप्तान् मुनीन् दृष्ट्वा प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः । पाद्यार्घ्यादिभिरानर्च गां निवेद्य च सादरम् ।। 7.1.13 ।।
explanation: Seeing those sages arrive, he rose up with folded hands, and respectfully offering a cow, he worshipped them with water for their feet, offerings, and so on.

shloka_text: रामो ऽभिवाद्य प्रयत आसनान्यादिदेश ह । तेषु काञ्चनचित्रेषु महत्सु च वरेषु च ।। 7.1.14 ।।
explanation: Having greeted them, Rama reverently offered seats, which were grand, excellent, and adorned with gold.

shloka_text: कुशान्तर्धानदत्तेषु मृगचर्मयुतेषु च । यथार्हमुपविष्टास्ते आसनेष्वृषिपुङ्गवाः ।। 7.1.15 ।।
explanation: The chief sages sat down appropriately on the seats, which were provided with kusha grass placed within and covered with deer skins.

shloka_text: रामेण कुशलं पृष्टाः सशिष्याः सपुरोगमाः । महर्षयो वेदविदो रामं वचनमब्रुवन् ।। 7.1.16 ।।
explanation: When asked about their well-being by Rama, the great sages, accompanied by their disciples and elders, and learned in the Vedas, spoke to Rama.

shloka_text: कुशलं नो महाबाहो सर्वत्र रघुनन्दन । त्वां तु दिष्ट्या कुशलिनं पश्यामो हतशात्रवम् ।। 7.1.17 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, O scion of Raghu, we are well in all respects. But we are fortunate to see you safe, with your enemies slain.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राजन्रावणो लोकरावणः । न हि भारः स ते राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान् ।। 7.1.18 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, O King, Ravana, the tormentor of the worlds, has been slain by you. Indeed, that Ravana, with his sons and grandsons, was no burden to you, O Rama.

shloka_text: सधनुस्त्वं हि लोकांस्त्रीन्विजयेथा न संशयः । दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राम रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।। 7.1.19 ।।
explanation: Indeed, with your bow, you would conquer the three worlds, there is no doubt. Fortunately, O Rama, Ravana, the lord of Rākṣasas, has been slain by you.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या विजयिनं त्वाद्य पश्यामः सह सीतया । लक्ष्मणेन च धर्मात्मन्भ्रात्रा त्वद्धितकारिणा ।। 7.1.20 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, O righteous one, today we see you, victorious, with Sita and with your well-wishing brother Lakshmana.

shloka_text: मातृभिर्भ्रातृसहितं पश्यामो ऽद्य वयं नृप । दिष्ट्या प्रहस्तो विकटो विरूपाक्षो महोदरः । अकम्पनश्च दुर्धर्षो निहतास्ते निशाचराः ।। 7.1.21 ।।
explanation: O King, today we see ourselves with mothers and brothers. Fortunately, Prahasta, Vikata, Virupaksha, Mahodara, Akampana, and Durgharsha – those night-roaming demons – have been slain.

shloka_text: यस्य प्रमाणाद्विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते । दिष्ट्या ते समरे राम कुम्भकर्णो निपातितः ।। 7.1.22 ।।
explanation: There is no greater measure than his in this world. Fortunately, O Rama, Kumbhakarna has been slain by you in battle.

shloka_text: त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ । दिष्ट्या ते निहता राम महावीर्या निशाचराः ।। 7.1.23 ।।
explanation: Trishira, Atikaya, Devantaka, and Narantaka – those exceedingly mighty night-wanderers, O Rama, have fortunately been slain.

shloka_text: कुम्भश्चैव निकुम्भश्च राक्षसौ भीमदर्शनौ । दिष्ट्या तौ निहतौ राम कुम्भकर्णसुतौ मृधे ।। 7.1.24 ।।
explanation: O Rama, fortunately, Kumbha and Nikumbha, the two formidable-looking Rakshasas, the sons of Kumbhakarna, were slain in battle.

shloka_text: युद्धोन्मत्तश्च मत्तश्च कालान्तकयमोपमौ । यज्ञकोपश्च बलवान्धूम्राक्षो नाम राक्षसः ।। 7.1.25 ।।
explanation: Mad with war and intoxicated, like Kala the destroyer and Yama, and wrathful towards sacrifices, was the powerful demon named Dhumraksha.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तः कदनं घोरमेते शस्त्रास्त्रपारगाः । अन्तकप्रतिमैर्बाणैर्दिष्ट्या विनिहतास्त्वया ।। 7.1.26 ।।
explanation: These experts in weapons and missiles, who were causing dreadful slaughter, have fortunately been slain by you with arrows resembling Yama.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रेण द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतः । देवतानामवध्येन विजयं प्राप्तवानसि ।। 7.1.27 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, you engaged in a duel with the king of Rākṣasas, who was unslayable by the gods, and you have achieved victory.

shloka_text: सङ्ख्ये तस्य न किञ्चित्तु रावणस्य पराभवः । द्वन्द्वयुद्धमनुप्राप्तो दिष्ट्या ते रावणिर्हतः ।। 7.1.28 ।।
explanation: Indeed, in battle, there was no defeat for Ravana. Fortunately, Ravani was killed by you in single combat.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या तस्य महाबाहो कालस्येवाभिधावतः । मुक्तः सुररिपोर्वीर प्राप्तश्च विजयस्त्वया ।। 7.1.29 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, O mighty-armed one, you have been freed from that enemy of the gods who was rushing like Time itself. And victory has been achieved by you, O hero.

shloka_text: अभिनन्दाम ते सर्वे संश्रुत्येन्द्रजितो वधम् । सो ऽवध्यः सर्वभूतानां महामायाधरो युधि ।। 7.1.30 ।।
explanation: All of us congratulate you, having heard of the slaying of Indrajit. He was invincible to all beings, a master of great illusion in battle.

shloka_text: विस्मयस्त्वेष चास्माकं तच्छ्रुत्वेन्द्रजितं हतम् ।। 7.1.31 ।।
explanation: And this is our astonishment, having heard that Indrajit was slain.

shloka_text: एते चान्ये च बहवो राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः । दिष्ट्या त्वया हता वीरा रघूणां कुलवर्द्धन ।। 7.1.32 ।।
explanation: These and many other Rakshasas, who could assume any form at will, have fortunately been slain by you, O hero, O enhancer of the Raghu lineage.

shloka_text: दत्त्वा पुण्यामिमां वीर सौम्यामभयदक्षिणाम् ।। दिष्ट्या वर्धसि काकुत्स्थ जयेनामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.1.33 ।।
explanation: O hero, having given this sacred, gentle gift of fearlessness, fortunately, you prosper with victory, O Kakutstha, O destroyer of enemies.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु तेषां वचनमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम् । विस्मयं परमं गत्वा रामः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् ।। 7.1.34 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of those pure-souled sages, Rama, filled with great wonder, spoke with folded hands.

shloka_text: भगवन्तः कुम्भकर्णं रावणं च निशाचरम् । अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यौ किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.35 ।।
explanation: O revered ones, having overcome Kumbhakarna and Ravana, the night-roaming demon, why do you, of great valor, praise Ravani?

shloka_text: महोदरं प्रहस्तं च विरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम् । मत्तोन्मत्तौ च दुर्धर्षौ देवान्तकनरान्तकौ ।।
explanation: Mahodara, Prahasta, and the demon Virupaksha, and the formidable Matta and Unmatta, Devantaka and Narantaka.

shloka_text: अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान् किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.36 ।।
explanation: Why do you praise Ravani, having disregarded the greatly powerful ones?

shloka_text: अतिकायं त्रिशिरसं धूम्राक्षं च निशाचरम् । अतिक्रम्य महावीर्यान्किं प्रशंसथ रावणिम् ।। 7.1.37 ।।
explanation: Having overcome the greatly powerful night-wanderers Atikaya, Trishiras, and Dhumraksha, why do you praise Ravani?

shloka_text: कीदृशो वै प्रभावो ऽस्य किं बलं कः पराक्रमः । केन वा कारणेनैष रावणादतिरिच्यते ।। 7.1.38 ।।
explanation: What kind of power is his? What is his strength? What is his prowess? And for what reason does he surpass Rāvaṇa?

shloka_text: शक्यं यदि मया श्रोतुं न खल्वाज्ञापयामि वः । यदि गुह्यं न चेद्वक्तुं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम् ।। 7.1.39 ।।
explanation: If it is possible for me to hear, I am certainly not commanding you. If it is not a secret to be told, I wish to hear it; please tell.

shloka_text: शक्रो ऽपि विजितस्तेन कथं लब्धवरश्च सः । कथं च बलवानन्पुत्रो न पिता तस्य रावणः ।। 7.1.40 ।।
explanation: Even Indra was conquered by him, and how did he obtain boons? And how is this son so powerful? Is Ravana not his father?

shloka_text: कथं पितुश्चाभ्यधिको महाहवे शक्रस्य जेता हि कथं स राक्षसः । वराश्च लब्धाः कथयस्व मे ऽद्य तत्पृच्छतश्चास्य मुनीन्द्र सर्वम् ।। 7.1.41 ।।
explanation: How was that demon superior to his father? How indeed was he the conqueror of Indra in a great battle? And how were boons obtained by him? O chief of sages, tell me all of that today, as I am asking you.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः ।। 1 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the first chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः । कुम्भयोनिर्मिहातेजा राममेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of the great-souled Raghava, Kumbhayoni, the greatly effulgent one, spoke this to Rama.

shloka_text: शृणु राम कथावृत्तं तस्य तेजोबलं महत् । जघान शत्रून्येनासौ न च वध्यः स शत्रुभिः ।। 7.2.2 ।।
explanation: Listen, Rama, to the account of his great might and strength, by which he slew enemies, and he himself was not to be slain by enemies.

shloka_text: तावत्ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव । वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते ।। 7.2.3 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, I will now tell you about this lineage and birth of Ravana, and also the boons granted to him.

shloka_text: पुरा कृतयुगे राम प्रजापतिसुतः प्रभुः । पुलस्त्यो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षादिव पितामहः ।। 7.2.4 ।।
explanation: O Rama, formerly in the Krita Yuga, there was a powerful Brahmarshi named Pulastya, the son of Prajapati, who was like the grandfather (Brahma) himself.

shloka_text: नानुकीर्त्या गुणास्तस्य धर्मतः शीलतस्तथा । प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः ।। 7.2.5 ।।
explanation: His qualities are not to be described by righteousness and character. Indeed, it is possible to call him 'son of Prajapati' by name.

shloka_text: प्रजापतिसुतत्वेन देवानां वल्लभो हि सः । हृष्टः सर्वस्य लोकस्य गुणैः शुभ्रैर्महामतिः ।। 7.2.6 ।।
explanation: Indeed, being the son of Prajapati, he was beloved by the gods. He was great-minded and delighted by the pure qualities of all people.

shloka_text: स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः । तृणविन्द्वाश्रमं गत्वा न्यवसन्मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.2.7 ।।
explanation: But that excellent sage, for the sake of religious matters, went to the hermitage of Tṛṇabindu on the side of the great mountain Meru and resided there.

shloka_text: तपस्तेपे स धर्मात्मा स्वाध्यायनियतेन्द्रियः । गत्वाश्रमपदं तस्य विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.8 ।।
explanation: That righteous-souled one, whose senses were controlled by self-study, performed penance. Maidens, having gone to his hermitage, create obstacles for him.

shloka_text: देवपन्नगकन्याश्च राजर्षितनयाश्च याः । क्रीडन्त्यो ऽप्सरसश्चैव तं देशमुपपेदिरे ।। 7.2.9 ।।
explanation: The daughters of gods and serpents, and those who were daughters of royal sages, and the Apsaras, playing, arrived at that place.

shloka_text: सर्वर्तुषृपभोग्यत्वाद्रम्यत्वात्काननस्य च । नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः ।। 7.2.10 ।।
explanation: Because of the forest's enjoyability in all seasons and its beauty, the maidens constantly go to that place and play.

shloka_text: देशस्य रमणीयत्वात्पुलस्त्यो यत्र स द्विजः । गायन्त्यो वादयन्त्यश्च लासयन्त्यस्तथैव च । मुनेस्तपस्विनस्तस्य विघ्नं चक्रुरनिन्दिताः ।। 7.2.11 ।।
explanation: Due to the beauty of the place, where that brahmin Pulastya was, blameless women, singing, playing instruments, and dancing, caused a hindrance to that ascetic sage.

shloka_text: अथ क्रुद्धो महातेजा व्याजहार महामुनिः । या मे दर्शनमागच्छेत्सा गर्भं धारयिष्यति ।। 7.2.12 ।।
explanation: Then the greatly effulgent, enraged great sage declared: "Whoever comes into my sight, she will conceive a child."

shloka_text: तास्तु सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्य वाक्यं महात्मनः । ब्रह्मशापभयाद्भीतास्तं देशं नोपचक्रमुः ।। 7.2.13 ।।
explanation: But all of them, having heard the words of that great-souled one, and being frightened by the fear of a Brahmana's curse, did not approach that place.

shloka_text: तृणबिन्दोस्तु राजर्षेस्तनया न शृणोति तत् ।। 7.2.14 ।।
explanation: But the daughter of the royal sage Tṛṇabindu does not hear that.

shloka_text: गत्वाश्रमपदं तत्र विचचार सुनिर्भया । न सापश्यत्स्थिता तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् ।। 7.2.15 ।।
explanation: Having gone to the hermitage, she wandered there very fearlessly. She did not see any friend present there, nor any who had arrived.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्काले महातेजाः प्राजापत्यो महानृषिः । स्वाध्यायमकरोत्तत्र तपसा भावितः स्वयम् ।। 7.2.16 ।।
explanation: At that time, the greatly effulgent great sage, a descendant of Prajapati, himself purified by penance, performed self-study there.

shloka_text: सा तु वेदश्रुतिं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा वै तपसो निधिम् । अभवत्पाण्डुदेहा सा सुव्यञ्जितशरीरजा ।। 7.2.17 ।।
explanation: She, however, having heard the sacred sound and having seen the treasure of penance, became pale-bodied, and her bodily signs became clearly manifest.

shloka_text: वभूव च समुद्विग्ना दृष्ट्वा तद्दोषमात्मनः । इदं मे किन्त्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वा ऽ ऽश्रमे स्थिता ।। 7.2.18 ।।
explanation: And she became greatly distressed, having seen her own fault. Realizing, "What is this that has happened to me?", she went to her father's hermitage and stayed there.

shloka_text: तां तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतां तृणविन्दुरथाब्रवीत् । किं त्वमेतत्त्वसदृशं धारयस्यात्मनो वपुः ।। 7.2.19 ।।
explanation: Seeing her in that state, Trinavindu then said: "Why do you bear this body of yours, which is so unbefitting you?"

shloka_text: सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योवाच तपोधनम् । न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम् ।। 7.2.20 ।।
explanation: Distressed, the maiden, having folded her hands, said to the ascetic: "O father, I do not know the reason why my appearance is like this."

shloka_text: किं तु पूर्वं गतास्म्येका महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं दिव्यमन्वेष्टुं स्वसखीजनम् ।। 7.2.21 ।।
explanation: But formerly, I went alone to the divine hermitage of the great sage Pulastya, the self-realized one, to search for my female companions.

shloka_text: न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम् । रूपस्य तु विपर्यासं दृष्ट्वा त्रासादिहागता ।। 7.2.22 ।।
explanation: I did not see any female friend who had come there. But having seen a distortion of form, I came here out of fear.

shloka_text: तृणबिन्दुस्तु राजर्षिस्तपसा द्योतितप्रभः । ध्यानं विवेश तच्चापि ह्यपश्यदृषिकर्मजम् ।। 7.2.23 ।।
explanation: The royal sage Tṛṇabindu, whose splendor was illuminated by his penance, entered into meditation. And he also saw that which was born of the sage's action.

shloka_text: स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः । गृहीत्वा तनयां गत्वा पुलस्त्यमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.2.24 ।।
explanation: But he, having understood that curse of the great sage of purified soul, took his daughter, went to Pulastya, and spoke thus.

shloka_text: भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम् । भिक्षां प्रतिगृहाणेमां महर्षे स्वयमुद्यताम् ।। 7.2.25 ।।
explanation: O Lord, O great sage, please accept this daughter of mine, adorned by her own virtues, as this offering, which she herself has presented.

shloka_text: तपश्चरणयुक्तस्य श्रम्यमाणेन्द्रियस्य ते । शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.2.26 ।।
explanation: She will always be devoted to serving you, whose senses are fatigued by the practice of penance; there is no doubt.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षिं धार्मिकं तदा । जिघृक्षुरब्रवीत्कन्यां बाढमित्येव स द्विजः ।। 7.2.27 ।।
explanation: Then, that brahmin, desiring to take the maiden, said 'Very well' to that righteous royal sage who was speaking those words.

shloka_text: दत्त्वा स तु यथान्यायं स्वमाश्रमपदं गतः । सापि तत्रावसत्कन्या तोषयन्ती पतिं गुणैः ।। 7.2.28 ।।
explanation: He, having duly performed [the necessary rites], returned to his hermitage. The maiden also lived there, pleasing her husband with her virtues.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तु शीलवृत्ताभ्यां तुतोष मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.2.29 ।।
explanation: The foremost among sages was pleased by her character and conduct. That greatly effulgent one, being pleased, then spoke these words.

shloka_text: परितुष्टो ऽस्मि सुश्रोणि गुणानां सम्पदा भृशम् । तस्माद्देवि ददाम्यद्य पुत्रमात्मसमं तव ।। 7.2.30 ।।
explanation: O beautiful-hipped one, I am exceedingly pleased by the abundance of your virtues. Therefore, O goddess, today I give you a son equal to myself.

shloka_text: उभयोर्वंशकर्तारं पौलस्त्य इति विश्रुतम् । यस्मात्तु विश्रुतो वेदस्त्वयैषो ऽध्ययतो मम ।। 7.2.31 ।।
explanation: Renowned as Pulastya, the progenitor of both lineages, from whom this Veda became known to me as I studied it from you.

shloka_text: तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः । एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ।। 7.2.32 ।।
explanation: Therefore, he will be named Vishrava, without doubt. Thus addressed, that goddess, with a delighted inner self,

shloka_text: अचिरेणैव कालेनासूत विश्रवसं सुतम् । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं यशोधर्मसमन्वितम् ।। 7.2.33 ।।
explanation: In a short time, she gave birth to a son, Vishravas, who was renowned in the three worlds and endowed with fame and righteousness.

shloka_text: श्रुतिमान्समदर्शी च व्रताचाररतस्तथा । पितेव तपसा युक्तो ह्यभवद्विश्रवा मुनिः ।। 7.2.34 ।।
explanation: Sage Vishrava was learned, impartial, and devoted to vows and observances; indeed, like a father, he was endowed with asceticism.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः ।। 2 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: अथ पुत्रः पुलस्त्यस्य विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । अचिरेणैव कालेन पितेव तपसि स्थितः ।। 7.3.1 ।।
explanation: Then, Vishrava, the son of Pulastya, the foremost among sages, in a short time, became established in penance, just like his father.

shloka_text: सत्यवाञ्छीलवाञ्छान्तः स्वाध्यायनिरतः शुचिः । सर्वभोगेष्वसंसक्तो नित्यं धर्मपरायणः ।। 7.3.2 ।।
explanation: Truthful, virtuous, peaceful, devoted to self-study, pure, unattached to all enjoyments, and always intent on righteousness.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा तस्य तु तद्वृत्तं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः । ददौ विश्रवसे भार्यां स्वसुतां देववर्णिनीम् ।। 7.3.3 ।।
explanation: Having known his conduct, the great sage Bharadvaja gave his own daughter, Devavarṇinī, as a wife to Vishravas.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु धर्मेण भरद्वाजसुतां तदा । प्रजान्वेक्षिकया बुद्ध्या श्रेयो ह्यस्य विचिन्तयन् ।। 7.3.4 ।।
explanation: Having then righteously accepted Bharadvaja's daughter, and indeed, with an intellect focused on the welfare of his subjects, contemplating his well-being.

shloka_text: मुदा परमया युक्तो विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । स तस्यां वीर्यसम्पन्नमपत्यं परमाद्भुतम् ।। 7.3.5 ।।
explanation: Vishrava, the foremost among sages, filled with supreme joy, begot in her an exceedingly wonderful offspring endowed with great prowess.

shloka_text: जनयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्युतम् । तस्मिञ्जाते तु संहृष्टः सम्बभूव पितामहः ।। 7.3.6 ।।
explanation: The knower of Dharma begot one endowed with all divine qualities. When he was born, the Grandfather became greatly delighted.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा श्रेयस्करीं बुद्धिं धनाध्यक्षो भविष्यति । नाम तस्याकरोत्प्रीतः सार्धं देवर्षिभिस्तदा ।। 7.3.7 ।।
explanation: Having seen his auspicious intellect, he will become the lord of wealth. Then, pleased, he gave him a name along with the divine sages.

shloka_text: यस्माद्विश्रवसो ऽपत्यं सादृश्याद्विश्रवा इव । तस्माद्वैश्रवणो नाम भविष्यत्वेष विश्रुतः ।। 7.3.8 ।।
explanation: Because he is the offspring of Vishravas, and like Vishravas due to resemblance, therefore he will be renowned by the name Vaishravana.

shloka_text: स तु वैश्रवणस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा । अवर्धताहुतिहुतो महातेजा यथानलः ।। 7.3.9 ।।
explanation: But that Vaishravana, who was then in the hermitage, grew in great splendor like a fire fed with oblations.

shloka_text: तस्याश्रमपदस्थस्य बुद्धिर्जज्ञे महात्मनः । चरिष्ये परमं धर्मं धर्मो हि परमा गतिः ।। 7.3.10 ।।
explanation: While he was staying in the hermitage, a thought arose in the mind of that great soul: 'I shall practice the supreme dharma, for dharma is indeed the supreme refuge.'

shloka_text: स तु वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्तप्त्वा महावने । यन्त्रितो नियमैरुग्रैश्चकार सुमहत्तपः ।। 7.3.11 ।।
explanation: But he, having performed penance for thousands of years in the great forest, restrained by severe rules, undertook a very great austerity.

shloka_text: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रान्ते तं तं विधिमकल्पयत् । जलाशी मारुताहारो निराहारस्तथैव च ।। 7.3.12 ।।
explanation: At the end of a full thousand years, he adopted each of those practices: subsisting on water, subsisting on air, and similarly, fasting.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि जग्मुस्तान्येकवर्षवत् । अथ प्रीतो महातेजाः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह ।। 7.3.13 ।।
explanation: Thus, thousands of years passed like a single year. Then, the greatly effulgent one, pleased, along with Indra and the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: गत्वा तस्याश्रमपदं ब्रह्मेदं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । परितुष्टो ऽस्मि ते वत्स कर्मणानेन सुव्रत । वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते वरार्हस्त्वं महामते ।। 7.3.14 ।।
explanation: Having gone to his hermitage, Brahma spoke these words: "I am very pleased with you, my child, O virtuous one, by this deed. Choose a boon; may good be to you. You are worthy of a boon, O great-minded one."

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः पितामहमुपस्थितम् । भगवँल्लोकपालत्वमिच्छेयं वित्तरक्षणम् ।। 7.3.15 ।।
explanation: Then Vaiśravaṇa spoke to the grandfather who was present: "O Lord, I desire the guardianship of the world and the protection of wealth."

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणं परितुष्टेन चेतसा । ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धं बाढमित्येव हृष्टवत् ।। 7.3.16 ।।
explanation: Then Brahmā, along with the hosts of gods, with a very pleased mind, joyfully said to Vaiśravaṇa, "Very well!"

shloka_text: अहं वै लोकपालानां चतुर्थं स्रष्टुमुद्यतः ।। 7.3.17 ।।
explanation: I am indeed ready to create the fourth world-protector.

shloka_text: यमेन्द्रवरुणानां च पदं यत्तव चेप्सितम् । तद्गच्छ त्वं हि धर्मज्ञ निधीशत्वमवाप्नुहि । शक्राम्बुपयमानां च चतुर्थस्त्वं भविष्यसि ।। 7.3.18 ।।
explanation: O knower of Dharma, you shall attain that desired position of Yama, Indra, and Varuna, and become the lord of treasures. You will be the fourth among Indra, Varuna, and Yama.

shloka_text: एतच्च पुष्पकं नाम विमानं सूर्यसन्निभम् । प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यानार्थं त्रिदशैः समतां व्रज ।। 7.3.19 ।।
explanation: And accept this aerial vehicle named Pushpaka, which is like the sun, for your journey. Attain equality with the gods.

shloka_text: स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामः सर्व एव यथागतम् । कृतकृत्या वयं तात दत्त्वा तव वरद्वयम् ।। 7.3.20 ।।
explanation: May you fare well. We shall all depart as we arrived. Our purpose is fulfilled, dear one, having granted you two boons.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा स गतो ब्रह्मा स्वस्थानं त्रिदशैः सह ।। 7.3.21 ।।
explanation: Having said this, Brahma went to his own abode with the gods.

shloka_text: गतेषु ब्रह्मपूर्वेषु देवेष्वथ नभस्थलम् । वने स पितरं प्राह प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतात्मवान् । निवासनं न मे देवो विदधे स प्रजापतिः ।। 7.3.22 ।।
explanation: When Brahma and the other gods had departed to the sky, he, self-controlled and with folded hands, said to his father in the forest: "That Lord of Creation, the god, did not provide a dwelling place for me."

shloka_text: भगवँल्लब्धवानस्मि वरमिष्टं पितामहात् । तं पश्य भगवन्कञ्चिन्निवासं साधु मे प्रभो ।। 7.3.23 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I have obtained a desired boon from the Grandfather. O Lord, O Master, please find some suitable dwelling for me.

shloka_text: न च पीडा भवेद्यत्र प्राणिनो यस्य कस्यचित् । एवमुक्तस्तु पुत्रेण विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.3.24 ।।
explanation: And where no suffering should befall any living being whatsoever. Vishrava, the foremost among sages, was thus addressed by his son.

shloka_text: वचनं प्राह धर्मज्ञः श्रूयतामिति सत्तमः । दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः ।। 7.3.25 ।।
explanation: The righteous one, the most excellent, spoke these words: "Listen! On the shore of the southern ocean is a mountain named Trikuta."

shloka_text: तस्याग्रे तु विशाला सा महेन्द्रस्य पुरी यथा । लङ्का नाम पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ।। 7.3.26 ।।
explanation: In front of it was that vast and beautiful city named Lanka, built by Vishwakarma, like the city of Mahendra.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां निवासार्थं यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती । तत्र त्वं वस भद्रं ते लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः ।। 7.3.27 ।।
explanation: Just as Amaravati is for the residence of Indra, so too is Lanka for the residence of the Rākṣasas. You reside there in Lanka. May good fortune be to you; there is no doubt about this.

shloka_text: हेमप्राकारपरिघा यन्त्रशस्त्रसमावृता । रमणीया पुरी सा हि रुक्मवैडूर्यतोरणा ।। 7.3.28 ।।
explanation: That city was indeed beautiful, with golden ramparts and moats, equipped with machines and weapons, and its gateways were of gold and lapis lazuli.

shloka_text: राक्षसैः सा परित्यक्ता पुरा विष्णुभयार्दितैः । शून्या रक्षोगणैः सर्वै रसातलतलं गतैः ।। 7.3.29 ।।
explanation: She was abandoned by the Rākṣasas, who were formerly tormented by fear of Vishnu. She was empty, as all the hosts of Rākṣasas had gone to the lowest level of Rasātala.

shloka_text: शून्या सम्प्रति लङ्का सा प्रभुस्तस्या न विद्यते । स त्वं तत्र निवासाय गच्छ पुत्र यथासुखम् ।। 7.3.30 ।।
explanation: That Lanka is now empty, and its lord is no more. Therefore, son, you go there to dwell comfortably.

shloka_text: निर्दोषस्तत्र ते वासो न बाधास्तत्र कस्यचित् । एतच्छुत्वा स धर्मात्मा धर्मिष्ठं वचनं पितुः ।। 7.3.31 ।।
explanation: Your dwelling there will be faultless, and there will be no harm to anyone there. Having heard this most righteous word of his father, that righteous soul...

shloka_text: निवासयामास तदा लङ्कां पर्वतमूर्धनि । नैर्ऋतानां सहस्रैस्तु हृष्टैः प्रमुदुतैः सह ।। 7.3.32 ।।
explanation: Then he established Lanka on the mountain-top, along with thousands of joyful and greatly pleased Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: अचिरेणैव कालेन सम्पूर्णा तस्य शासनात् ।। 7.3.33 ।।
explanation: In a very short time, it was completed by his command.

shloka_text: स तु तत्रावसत्प्रीतो धर्मात्मा नैर्ऋतर्षभः । समुद्रपरिघायां तु लङ्कायां विश्रवात्मजः ।। 7.3.34 ।।
explanation: But he, the righteous-souled chief of the Rākṣasas, the son of Viśravas, lived there contentedly in Laṅkā, which was surrounded by the ocean.

shloka_text: काले काले तु धर्मात्मा पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः । अभ्यागच्छद्विनीतात्मा पितरं मातरं च हि ।। 7.3.35 ।।
explanation: From time to time, the righteous and humble Kubera, the lord of wealth, would indeed come to his father and mother by means of the Pushpaka.

shloka_text: स देवगन्धर्वगणैरभिष्टुतस्तथाप्सरोनृत्यविभूषितालयः । गभस्तिभिः सूर्य इवावभासयन्पितुः समीपं प्रययौ स वित्तपः ।। 7.3.36 ।।
explanation: That lord of wealth, praised by hosts of gods and gandharvas, and whose abode was adorned by the dances of Apsaras, approached his father, illuminating (the surroundings) like the sun with its rays.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः ।। 3 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the third canto.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वागस्त्येरितं वाक्यं रामो विस्मयमागतः । कथमासीत्तु लङ्कायां सम्भवो रक्षसां पुरा ।। 7.4.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, Rama was filled with wonder. How then did the Rākṣasas originate in Lanka in ancient times?

shloka_text: ततः शिरः कम्पयित्वा त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम् । तमगस्त्यं मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानो ऽभ्यभाषत ।। 7.4.2 ।।
explanation: Then, shaking his head, and repeatedly looking at Agastya, whose form was like the Tretā fire, he spoke with a smile.

shloka_text: भगवन्पूर्वमप्येषा लङ्कासीत्पिशिताशिनाम् । श्रुत्वेदं भगवद्वाक्यं जातो मे विस्मयः परः ।। 7.4.3 ।।
explanation: O Lord, even previously this Lanka belonged to the flesh-eaters. Having heard these words of yours, great astonishment has arisen in me.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्यवंशादुद्भूता राक्षसा इति नः श्रुतम् । इदानीमन्यतश्चापि सम्भवः कीर्तितस्त्वया ।। 7.4.4 ।।
explanation: We have heard that Rākṣasas originated from the lineage of Pulastya. And now, an origin from another source has also been described by you.

shloka_text: रावणात्कुम्भकर्णाच्च प्रहस्ताद्विकटादपि । रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः ।। 7.4.5 ।।
explanation: Are they indeed more powerful than Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Prahasta, Vikata, and Ravana's sons?

shloka_text: क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किन्नामा च बलोत्कटः । अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः कथम् ।। 7.4.6 ।।
explanation: Who was their ancestor, O Brahmana, and what was his name, the mighty one? And having committed what offense, how were they driven away by Vishnu?

shloka_text: एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ । कुतूहलमिदं मह्यं नुद भानुर्यथा तमः ।। 7.4.7 ।।
explanation: O sinless one, please tell me all this in detail. Dispel this great curiosity of mine, just as the sun dispels darkness.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संस्कारालङ्कृतं शुभम् । ईषद्विस्मयमानस्तमगस्त्यः प्राह राघवम् ।। 7.4.8 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's auspicious words, adorned with refinement, Agastya, slightly amazed, spoke to Rama.

shloka_text: प्रजापतिः पुरा सृष्ट्वा ह्यपः सलिलसम्भवः । तासां गोपायने सत्त्वानसृजत्पद्मसम्भवः ।। 7.4.9 ।।
explanation: Prajapati, the water-born, having formerly created the waters, the lotus-born one, created beings for their protection.

shloka_text: ते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वकर्तारं विनीतवदुपस्थिताः । किं कुर्म इति भाषन्तः क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः ।। 7.4.10 ।।
explanation: Those beings, tormented by hunger, thirst, and fear, approached the creator of beings respectfully, saying, 'What shall we do?'

shloka_text: प्रजापतिस्तु तान्याह सत्वानि प्रहसन्निव । आभाष्य वाचा यत्नेन रक्षध्वमिति मानदः ।। 7.4.11 ।।
explanation: Prajapati, the giver of honor, then said to those beings, as if smiling, having addressed them with words, "Protect diligently!"

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च तत्रान्ये जक्षाम इति चापरे । भुक्षिताभुक्षितैरुक्तस्ततस्तानाह भूतकृत् ।। 7.4.12 ।।
explanation: And there, some others said, 'Let us protect!' And others said, 'Let us eat!' Then, addressed by the hungry and the non-hungry, the Creator of beings spoke to them.

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः । जक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं यक्षा एव भवन्तु वः ।। 7.4.13 ।।
explanation: And by whom it was said, "Let us protect," let them be Rākṣasas for you. And by whom it was said, "Let us eat," let them indeed be Yakṣas for you.

shloka_text: तत्र हेतिः प्रहेतिश्च भ्रातरौ राक्षसाधिपौ । मधुकैटभसङ्काशौ बभूवतुररिन्दमौ ।। 7.4.14 ।।
explanation: There, Heti and Praheti, two brothers and lords of Rākṣasas, were like Madhu and Kaiṭabha, the vanquishers of enemies.

shloka_text: प्रहेतिर्धार्मिकस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा । हेतिर्दारक्रियार्थे तु परं यत्नमथाकरोत् ।। 7.4.15 ।।
explanation: Praheti, the righteous one, was then in the hermitage there. Heti, however, then made a great effort for the purpose of marriage.

shloka_text: स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम भयावहाम् । उदावहदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव महामतिः ।। 7.4.16 ।।
explanation: He, the one of immeasurable spirit and great intellect, himself married the formidable maiden named Bhaya, who was the sister of Kala.

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः । पुत्रं पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केश इति श्रुतम् ।। 7.4.17 ।।
explanation: Heti, the foremost among Rakshasas and the best among those with sons, begot in her a son known as Vidyutkesha.

shloka_text: विद्युत्केशो हेतिपुत्रः स दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः । व्यवर्धत महातेजास्तोयमध्य इवाम्बुदः ।। 7.4.18 ।।
explanation: Vidyutkesha, the son of Heti, of great splendor and shining like the blazing sun, grew like a cloud in the midst of water.

shloka_text: स यदा यौवनं भद्रमनुप्राप्तो निशाचरः । ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता ।। 7.4.19 ।।
explanation: When that night-wanderer attained auspicious youth, his father then resolved to perform his marriage.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां सो ऽथ सन्ध्यातुल्यां प्रभावतः । वरयामास पुत्रार्थं हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः ।। 7.4.20 ।।
explanation: Then, Heti, the foremost among Rakshasas, sought Sandhya's daughter, who was equal to Sandhya in power, as a bride for a son.

shloka_text: अवश्यमेव दातव्या परस्मै सेति सन्ध्यया । चिन्तयित्वा सुता दत्ता विद्युत्केशाय राघव ।। 7.4.21 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, Sandhya, having thought, 'She must certainly be given to another,' gave the daughter to Vidyutkesha.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां लब्ध्वा विद्युत्केशो निशाचरः । रमते स्म तया सार्धं पौलोम्या मघवानिव ।। 7.4.22 ।।
explanation: Having obtained the daughter of Sandhya, the night-wanderer Vidyutkesha enjoyed with her, just as Maghavan (Indra) enjoys with Paulomi.

shloka_text: केनचित्त्वथ कालेन राम सालकटङ्कटा । विद्युत्केशाद्गर्भमाप घनराजिरिवार्णवात् ।। 7.4.23 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, O Rama, Salakaṭaṅkaṭā conceived from Vidyutkeśa, just as a mass of clouds obtains (its origin) from the ocean.

shloka_text: ततः सा राक्षसी गर्भं घनगर्भसमप्रभम् । प्रसूता मन्दरं गत्वा गङ्गा गर्भमिवाग्निजम् ।। 7.4.24 ।।
explanation: Then, that ogress, having gone to Mandara mountain, gave birth to an offspring resplendent like a thundercloud, just as Ganga gave birth to the fire-born offspring.

shloka_text: समुत्सृज्य तु सा गर्भं विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी । रेमे तु सार्धं पतिना विस्मृत्य सुतमात्मजम् ।। 7.4.25 ।।
explanation: Having abandoned the child, she, desirous of union with Vidyutkesha, indeed enjoyed with her husband, forgetting her own son.

shloka_text: उत्सृष्टस्तु तदा गर्भो घनशब्दसमस्वनः । तयोत्सृष्टः स तु शिशुः शरदर्कसमद्युतिः । निधायास्ये स्वयं मुष्टिं रुरोद शनकैस्तदा ।। 7.4.26 ।।
explanation: Then the fetus was released with a sound like a thundercloud. That child, released by her, shone with the brilliance of the autumn sun. Placing his own fist in his mouth, he then cried softly.

shloka_text: ततो वृषभमास्थाय पार्वत्या सहितः शिवः । वायुमार्गेण गच्छन्वै शुश्राव रुदितस्वनम् ।। 7.4.27 ।।
explanation: Then Shiva, accompanied by Parvati, having mounted a bull, while going through the air, heard the sound of weeping.

shloka_text: अपश्यदुमया सार्धं रुदन्तं राक्षसात्मजम् । कारुण्यभावात्पार्वत्या भवस्त्रिपुरसूदनः ।। 7.4.28 ।।
explanation: Bhava, the destroyer of Tripura, saw the demon's son crying along with Uma, due to Parvati's feeling of compassion.

shloka_text: तं राक्षसात्मजं चक्रे मातुरेव वयःसमम् । अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवो ऽक्षरो ऽव्ययः ।। 7.4.29 ।।
explanation: The imperishable and immutable Mahadeva made that son of the demon equal in age to his mother, and also made him immortal.

shloka_text: पुरमाकाशगं प्रादात्पार्वत्याः प्रियकाम्यया । उमयापि वरो दत्तो राक्षसानां नृपात्मज ।। 7.4.30 ।।
explanation: He gave a sky-going city to Parvati, desiring to please her. O son of the king, a boon was also given by Uma to the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: सद्योपलब्धिर्गर्भस्य प्रसूतिः सद्य एव च । सद्य एव वयःप्राप्तिर्मातुरेव वयस्समम् ।। 7.4.31 ।।
explanation: Immediate conception of the embryo, and immediate birth. Immediate attainment of age, equal to the mother's age.

shloka_text: ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः । चचार सर्वत्र महान्महामतिः खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरन्दरो यथा ।। 7.4.32 ।।
explanation: Then Sukesha, proud of the boon, having obtained the splendor of the Lord from Hara, the great one of great intellect, roamed everywhere, just as Purandara (Indra) having reached the celestial city.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः ।। 4 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the fourth chapter.

shloka_text: सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम् । ग्रामणीर्नाम गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुसमप्रभः ।। 7.5.1 ।।
explanation: Having seen Sukeśa, the righteous Rakshasa who had obtained boons, a Gandharva named Gramaṇī, whose splendor was equal to Viśvāvasu.

shloka_text: तस्य देववती नाम द्वितीया श्रीरिवात्मजा । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता रूपयौवनशालिनी । तां सुकेशाय धर्मेण ददौ रक्षःश्रियं यथा ।। 7.5.2 ।।
explanation: His second daughter, named Devavati, was like Shri herself. She was renowned in the three worlds, endowed with beauty and youth. He gave her to Sukesha righteously, as if she were the glory of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम् । आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः ।। 7.5.3 ।।
explanation: Having obtained that dear husband, whose power was established by a boon, Devavati was pleased, just as a poor person is pleased upon obtaining wealth.

shloka_text: स तया सह संयुक्तो रराज रजनीचरः । अञ्जनादभिनिष्क्रान्तः करेण्वेव महागजः ।। 7.5.4 ।।
explanation: He, the night-wanderer, united with her, shone splendidly, like a great elephant emerging from Anjana mountain accompanied by a female elephant.

shloka_text: देववत्यां सुकेशस्तु जनयामास राघव ।। 7.5.5 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, Sukesha begot (a son) in Devavati.

shloka_text: त्रीन् पुत्रान् जनयामास त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहान् । माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम् । त्रींस्त्रिनेत्रसमान्पुत्रान्राक्षसान्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.5.6 ।।
explanation: । माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम् । त्रींस्त्रिनेत्रसमान्पुत्रान्राक्षसान्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.5.6

shloka_text: त्रयो लोका इवाव्यग्राः स्थितास्त्रय इवाग्नयः । त्रयो मन्त्रा इवात्युग्रास्त्रयो घोरा इवामयाः ।। 7.5.7 ।।
explanation: They stood undisturbed like the three worlds, like the three fires; like three extremely potent mantras, like three dreadful diseases.

shloka_text: त्रयः सुकेशस्य सुतास्त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः । विवृद्धिमगमंस्तत्र व्याधयोपेक्षिता इव ।। 7.5.8 ।।
explanation: The three sons of Sukesha, whose splendor was like that of the three sacred fires, grew there, like neglected diseases.

shloka_text: वरप्राप्तिं पितुस्ते तु ज्ञात्वेश्वरतपोबलात् । तपस्तप्तुं गता मेरुं भ्रातरः कृतनिश्चयाः ।। 7.5.9 ।।
explanation: Knowing of your father's attainment of a boon through the power of the Lord's penance, the brothers, having made a firm resolve, went to Meru to perform austerities.

shloka_text: प्रगृह्य नियमान्घोरान्राक्षसा नृपसत्तम । विचेरुस्ते तपो घोरं सर्वभूतभयावहम् ।। 7.5.10 ।।
explanation: O best among kings, the Rākṣasas, having undertaken terrible vows, performed dreadful penance, terrifying all creatures.

shloka_text: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैस्तपोभिरतिदुष्करैः । सन्तापयन्तस्त्रील्लोँकान्सदेवासुरमानुषान् ।। 7.5.11 ।।
explanation: By exceedingly difficult austerities, endowed with truth, straightforwardness, and tranquility, they tormented the three worlds, including gods, demons, and humans.

shloka_text: ततो विभुश्चतुर्वक्त्रो विमानवरमास्थितः । सुकेशपुत्रानामन्त्र्य वरदो ऽस्मीत्यभाषत ।। 7.5.12 ।।
explanation: Then the powerful four-faced one, having ascended the excellent aerial chariot, called the sons of Sukesha and said, "I am a giver of boons."

shloka_text: ब्रह्माणं वरदं ज्ञात्वा सेन्द्रैर्देवगणैर्वृतम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव द्रुमाः ।। 7.5.13 ।।
explanation: Having perceived Brahma, the bestower of boons, surrounded by the hosts of gods led by Indra, all of them, with folded hands, spoke, trembling like trees.

shloka_text: तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम् । अजेयाः शत्रुहन्तारस्तथैव चिरजीविनः ।। 7.5.14 ।।
explanation: O God, worshipped by penance, if you grant us a boon, (let us be) unconquerable, destroyers of enemies, and long-lived.

shloka_text: प्रभविष्ण्वो भवामेति परस्परमनुव्रताः ।। 7.5.15 ।।
explanation: "Let us be powerful," thus they were mutually devoted to each other.

shloka_text: एवं भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा सुकेशतनयान्विभुः । स ययौ ब्रह्मलोकाय ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणवत्सलः ।। 7.5.16 ।।
explanation: Having said to the sons of Sukesha, "Thus it shall be," that powerful Brahma, benevolent to Brahmins, went to Brahmaloka.

shloka_text: वरं लब्ध्वा तु ते सर्वे राम रात्रिञ्चरास्तदा । सुरासुरान्प्रबाधन्ते वरदानसुनिर्भयाः ।। 7.5.17 ।।
explanation: O Rama, having obtained the boon, all those night-wanderers then harassed the gods and asuras, being utterly fearless due to the gift of the boon.

shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमानास्त्रिदशाः सर्षिसङ्घाः सचारणाः । त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति निरयस्था यथा नराः ।। 7.5.18 ।।
explanation: Being slain by them, the gods, along with the hosts of sages and Charanas, do not find a protector, just like men dwelling in hell.

shloka_text: अथ ते विश्वकर्माणं शिल्पिनां वरमव्ययम् । ऊचुः समेत्य संहृष्टा राक्षसा रघुसत्तम ।। 7.5.19 ।।
explanation: Then, O best of Raghu, the Rākṣasas, having assembled and being greatly delighted, spoke to Vishwakarma, the imperishable best of artisans.

shloka_text: ओजस्तेजोबलवतां महतामात्मतेजसा । गृहकर्ता भवानेव देवानां हृदयेप्सितम् ।। 7.5.20 ।।
explanation: You, who are great, vigorous, brilliant, and strong, are indeed the creator of the abode, desired by the hearts of the gods, through your own splendor.

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि तावत्त्वं गृहं कुरु महामते । हिमवन्तमपाश्रित्य मेरुमन्दरमेव वा । महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं गृहं नः क्रियतां महत् ।। 7.5.21 ।।
explanation: O great-minded one, you should also make a house for us now. Relying on Himavat or even Meru and Mandara, let a grand house, resembling the abode of Maheśvara, be built for us.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मा ततस्तेषां राक्षसानां महाभुजः । निवासं कथयामास शक्रस्येवामरावतीम् ।। 7.5.22 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Vishwakarma described to those Rākṣasas a dwelling place like Amaravati, the city of Shakra.

shloka_text: दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः । सुवेल इति चाप्यन्यो द्वितीयस्तत्र सत्तमाः ।। 7.5.23 ।।
explanation: On the shore of the southern ocean, there is a mountain named Trikuta. And there, O best among men, is also another, a second one, named Suvela.

shloka_text: शिखरे तस्य शैलस्य मध्यमे ऽम्बुदसन्निभे । शकुनैरपि दुष्प्रापे टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि ।। 7.5.24 ।।
explanation: On the central peak of that mountain, resembling a cloud, inaccessible even to birds, and carved on all four sides with a chisel.

shloka_text: त्रिंशद्योजनक्स्तीर्णा शतयोजनमायता । स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता हेमतोरणसंवृता ।। 7.5.25 ।।
explanation: Thirty yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, surrounded by golden walls and adorned with golden archways.

shloka_text: मया लङ्केति नगरी शक्राज्ञप्तेन निर्मिता । तस्यां वसत दुर्धर्षा यूयं राक्षसपुङ्गवाः ।। 7.5.26 ।।
explanation: The city named Lanka was built by me at the command of Shakra. O unconquerable ones, O foremost among Rākṣasas, you all dwell in it.

shloka_text: अमरावतीं समासाद्य सेन्द्रा इव दिवौकसः । लङ्कादुर्गं समासाद्य राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृताः ।। 7.5.27 ।।
explanation: Having reached Amaravati, like the gods with Indra, (they) having reached the fortress of Lanka, were surrounded by many Rakshasas.

shloka_text: भविष्यथ दुराधर्षाः शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनाः ।। 7.5.28 ।।
explanation: You will be invincible to enemies, O destroyers of foes.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मवचः श्रुत्वा ततस्ते राक्षसोत्तमाः । सहस्रानुचरा भूत्वा गत्वा तामवसन्पुरीम् ।। 7.5.29 ।।
explanation: Having heard Viśvakarmā's words, those foremost Rākṣasas, accompanied by thousands of followers, then went and resided in that city.

shloka_text: दृढप्राकारपरिखां हैमैर्गृहशतैर्वृताम् । लङ्कामवाप्य ते हृष्टा न्यवसन्रजनीचराः ।। 7.5.30 ।।
explanation: Having reached Lanka, fortified with strong walls and moats, and surrounded by hundreds of golden houses, those night-wanderers, delighted, resided there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथाकामं च राघव । नर्मदा नाम गन्धर्वी बभूव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.5.31 ।।
explanation: At this very time, O Raghava, O Raghunandana, a Gandharva woman named Narmada came into being as she desired.

shloka_text: तस्याः कान्यात्रयं ह्यासीत् धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति । ज्येष्ठक्रमेण सा तेषां राक्षसानामराक्षसी ।। 7.5.32 ।।
explanation: She indeed had three daughters, whose splendor was equal to intellect, prosperity, and fame. By seniority, she herself was not a Rākṣasī among those Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: कन्यास्ताः प्रददौ हृष्टा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः । त्रयाणां राक्षसेन्द्राणां तिस्रो गन्धर्वकन्यकाः ।। 7.5.33 ।।
explanation: Joyfully, he gave away those three Gandharva maidens, whose faces resembled the full moon, to the three chiefs of Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: दत्ता मात्रा महाभागा नक्षत्रे भगदैवते । कुतदारास्तु ते राम सुकेशतनयास्तदा ।। 7.5.34 ।।
explanation: The greatly blessed mother gave (them in marriage) in the constellation ruled by Bhaga. And then, O Rama, those sons of Sukesha were married.

shloka_text: चिक्रीडुः सह भार्याभिरप्सरोभिरिवामराः । ततो माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.35 ।।
explanation: They played with their wives like gods with Apsaras. Then, Malyavat's wife, named Sundari, who was beautiful.

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत् । वज्रमुष्टिर्विरूपाक्षोदुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः ।। 7.5.36 ।।
explanation: Know the offspring he begot upon her: Vajramushti, Virupaksha, and Durmukha, the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च मत्तोन्मत्तौ तथैव च । अनला चाभवत्कन्या सुन्दर्यां राम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.37 ।।
explanation: O Rama, Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, and similarly Matta and Unmatta, and Anala, a beautiful daughter, were born from Sundari.

shloka_text: सुमालिनो ऽपि भार्यासीत्पूर्णचद्रनिभानना । नाम्ना केतुमती राम प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयसी ।। 7.5.38 ।।
explanation: O Rama, Sumali also had a wife whose face resembled the full moon, named Ketumati, who was dearer even than life.

shloka_text: सुमाली जनयामास यदपत्यं निशाचरः । केतुमत्यां महाराज तन्निबोधानुपूर्वशः ।। 7.5.39 ।।
explanation: O great king, know in due order the offspring that Sumali, the night-wanderer, begot in Ketumati.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तो ऽकम्पनश्चैव विकटः कालकार्मुखः । धूम्राक्षश्चैव दण्डश्च सुपार्श्वश्च महाबलः ।। 7.5.40 ।।
explanation: Prahasta, Akampana, Vikata, Kālakārmukha, Dhūmrākṣa, Daṇḍa, and the mighty Supārśva.

shloka_text: संह्रादिः प्रघसश्चैव भासकर्णश्च राक्षसः । राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिता ।। कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
explanation: Samhradi, Praghāsa, and the Rākṣasa Bhāskarṇa; Raka, Pushpotkata, and Kaikasi, the pure-smiling one; and Kumbhinasi – these are known as the offspring of Sumali.

shloka_text: कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
explanation: Kumbhīnasī and these are known as the offspring of Sumali.

shloka_text: मालेस्तु वसुधा नाम गन्धर्वी रूपशालिनी । भार्यासीत्पद्मपत्राक्षी स्वक्षी यक्षीवरोपमा ।। 7.5.42 ।।
explanation: Māli had a wife named Vasudha, a beautiful Gandharva woman, lotus-petal-eyed, beautiful-eyed, and resembling the best of Yakshis.

shloka_text: सुमालेरनुजस्तस्यां जनयामास यत् प्रभो । अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तु मया त्वं शृणु राघव ।। 7.5.43 ।।
explanation: O Lord, O Raghava, listen to me as I tell you about the offspring that Sumali's younger brother begot in her.

shloka_text: अनिलश्चानलश्चैव हरः सम्पातिरेव च । एते विभीषणामात्या मालेयास्तु निशाचरः ।। 7.5.44 ।।
explanation: Anila, Anala, Hara, and Sampati – these are Vibhishana's ministers. Maleya, however, is a night-wanderer.

shloka_text: ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुङ्गवास्त्रयो निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृताः । सुरान्सहेन्द्रानृषिनागयक्षान्बबाधिरे तान्बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः ।। 7.5.45 ।।
explanation: Then, those three chief Rakshasas, accompanied by other night-wanderers and hundreds of their sons, very proud of their great strength, tormented the gods including Indra, sages, Nagas, and Yakshas.

shloka_text: जगद्भ्रमन्तो ऽनिलवद्दुरासदा रणेषु मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः । वरप्रदानादतिगर्विता भृशं क्रतुक्रियाणां प्रशमङ्कराः सदा ।। 7.5.46 ।।
explanation: Roaming the world like the wind, formidable in battles, their might like death, exceedingly proud due to the granting of boons, they always cause the cessation of sacrificial rites.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः ।। 5 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (composed by a Rishi), the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the fifth chapter.

shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमाना देवाश्च ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः । भयार्ताः शरणं जग्मुर्देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ।। 7.6.1 ।।
explanation: Tormented by them, the gods and the ascetics, distressed by fear, sought refuge in Maheśvara, the God of gods.

shloka_text: जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारमजमव्यक्तरूपिणम् । आधारं सर्वलोकानामाराध्यं परमं गुरुम् ।। 7.6.2 ।।
explanation: The creator and destroyer of the world, the unborn, whose form is unmanifest, the support of all worlds, the adorable, the supreme preceptor.

shloka_text: ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारिं त्रिलोचनम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा भयगद्गदभाषिणः ।। 7.6.3 ।।
explanation: They, the gods, having approached Kāmāri, Tripurāri, the three-eyed one, spoke with folded hands, their voices choked with fear.

shloka_text: सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः । प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधनैः ।। 7.6.4 ।।
explanation: O Lord, O Ruler of creatures, all creatures are being tormented by the sons of Sukesha, who are arrogant due to the boon from Brahma, with their hostile oppressions.

shloka_text: शरण्यान्यशरण्यानि ह्याश्रमाणि कृतानि नः । स्वर्गाच्च देवान्प्रच्याव्य स्वर्गे क्रीडन्ति देववत् ।। 7.6.5 ।।
explanation: Indeed, our hermitages have been made (into) places of refuge and non-refuge for us; and having dislodged the gods from heaven, they sport in heaven like gods.

shloka_text: अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम् । अहं यमश्च वरुणश्चन्द्रो ऽहं रविरप्यहम् ।। 7.6.6 ।।
explanation: I am Vishnu, I am Rudra, I am Brahma, I am the king of gods. I am Yama and Varuna, I am Chandra, and I am also Ravi.

shloka_text: इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः । बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । तन्नो देव भयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि ।। 7.6.7 ।।
explanation: Thus, Mali, Sumali, and Malyavan, these Rakshasas, who are zealous for battle, along with their leaders, torment us. Therefore, O God, you ought to grant protection to us who are terrified.

shloka_text: अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि वै देवकण्टकान् ।। 7.6.8 ।।
explanation: Assuming an inauspicious form, indeed destroy the enemies of the gods.

shloka_text: धन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः । इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः । सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्षः प्राह देवगणान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.9 ।।
explanation: They bear the excitement of battle, and those who are their leaders. Thus addressed by all the gods, Kapardi, Nīlalohita, the Lord, having regard for Sukeśa, spoke to the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि मयावध्या हि ते सुराः । किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.10 ।।
explanation: I will not kill them, for those gods are inviolable by me. But I will give a mantra which will indeed kill them.

shloka_text: एतमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः ।। 7.6.11 ।।
explanation: O great sages, making this very endeavor your foremost aim, go to Vishnu for refuge. That Lord will destroy them.

shloka_text: ततस्तु जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम् । विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः ।। 7.6.12 ।।
explanation: Then, having acclaimed Maheśvara with shouts of victory, they, tormented by the fear of night-roaming demons, approached Vishnu.

shloka_text: शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च । ऊचुः सम्भ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ।। 7.6.13 ।।
explanation: Having bowed down and greatly honored the god bearing the conch and discus, they spoke bewildered words to the sons of Sukesha.

shloka_text: सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः । आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहृतानि नः ।। 7.6.14 ।।
explanation: O god, our abodes have been seized by the three sons of Sukesha, who resemble the three sacred fires, after they overpowered us by means of a boon.

shloka_text: लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता । तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः ।। 7.6.15 ।।
explanation: The city named Lanka is an impregnable fortress, situated on the peak of Trikuta. The night-wanderers residing there torment all of us.

shloka_text: स त्वमस्मद्धितार्थाय जहि तान्मधुसूदन । शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.6.16 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Madhusudana, for our welfare, destroy them. We have come to you for refuge; be our protector, O Lord of the gods.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान्निवेदय यमाय वै । भयेष्वभयदो ऽस्माकं नान्यो ऽस्ति भवता विना ।। 7.6.17 ।।
explanation: Present to Yama those whose lotus-like faces are severed by the discus. Indeed, for us, there is no other giver of fearlessness in dangers except you.

shloka_text: राक्षसान्समरे दुष्टान्सानुबन्धान्मदोद्धतान् । नुदं त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः ।। 7.6.18 ।।
explanation: O God, you dispel our fear, just as the sun dispels mist, [by driving away] the wicked, arrogant demons along with their followers in battle.

shloka_text: इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः । अभयं भयदो ऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह ।। 7.6.19 ।।
explanation: Thus, addressed by the gods, Janardana, the God of gods, having granted fearlessness (protection) and being a terror to his enemies, then spoke to the gods.

shloka_text: सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम् । तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान् ।। 7.6.20 ।।
explanation: I know the demon Sukeśa, who was emboldened by a boon from Ishana. And I know his sons, among whom Mālyavān is the eldest.

shloka_text: तानहं समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान्राक्षसाधमान् । निहनिष्यामि सङ्क्रुद्धः सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.21 ।।
explanation: I, greatly enraged, will slay those vilest Rākṣasas who have transgressed all limits. O gods, be free from anxiety.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । यथावासं ययुर्हृष्टाः प्रशंसन्तो जनार्दनम् ।। 7.6.22 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the powerful Vishnu, all those gods, delighted, went to their respective abodes, praising Janardana.

shloka_text: विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवांस्तु निशाचरः । श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.23 ।।
explanation: But Malyavan, the Rakshasa, having heard of the gods' great endeavor, spoke these words to those two heroic brothers.

shloka_text: अमरा ऋषयश्चैव सङ्गम्य किल शकरम् । अस्मद्वधं परीप्सन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ।। 7.6.24 ।।

shloka_text: सुकेशतनया देव वरदानबलोद्धताः । बाधन्ते ऽस्मान्समुद्दृप्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे ।। 7.6.25 ।।
explanation: O Lord, the sons of Sukesha, arrogant due to the power of boons, exceedingly proud and of terrible form, trouble us at every step.

shloka_text: राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते । स्वेषु सद्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम् ।। 7.6.26 ।।
explanation: O Prajapati, we are oppressed by demons. We are unable to reside in our own homes due to fear of those wicked ones.

shloka_text: तदस्माकं हितार्थाय जहि तांश्च त्रिलोचन । राक्षसान्हुङ्कृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर ।। 7.6.27 ।।
explanation: Therefore, for our welfare, O Three-eyed one, kill those Rākṣasas. Burn them with a mere roar, O best among incinerators.

shloka_text: इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः । शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.6.28 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the gods, the slayer of Andhaka, upon hearing, shaking his head and hand, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे । मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति ।। 7.6.29 ।।
explanation: Those sons of Sukesa are unkillable by me in battle, O gods. But I will give you a mantra which will indeed kill them.

shloka_text: यो ऽसौ चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः । हरिर्नारायणः श्रीमान् शरणं तं प्रपद्यथ ।। 7.6.30 ।।
explanation: Take refuge in him, Janardana, Hari, Narayana, the glorious one, who holds the discus and mace in his hands and is clad in yellow garments.

shloka_text: हरादवाप्य ते मन्त्रं कामारिमभिवाद्य च । नारायणालयं प्राप्य तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन् ।। 7.6.31 ।।
explanation: Having obtained the mantra from Hara, and having saluted Kamari, they reached the abode of Narayana and reported everything to Him.

shloka_text: ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः । सुरारींस्तान्हनिष्यामि सुरा भवत विज्वराः ।। 7.6.32 ।।
explanation: Then, Narayana spoke to the gods, led by Indra: "I will slay those enemies of the gods. O gods, be free from distress."

shloka_text: देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ । प्रतिज्ञातो वधो ऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम् ।। 7.6.33 ।।
explanation: O best of Rākṣasas, Hari has promised the terrified gods our destruction. Let what is suitable here be considered.

shloka_text: हिरण्यकशिपोर्मृत्युरन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम् । नमुचिः कालनेमिश्च संह्रादो वीरसत्तमः ।। 7.6.34 ।।
explanation: The death of Hiranyakashipu and other enemies of the gods: Namuchi, Kalanemi, and Samhrada, the most excellent warrior.

shloka_text: राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालो ऽथ धार्मिकः । यमलार्जुनौ च हार्दिक्यः शुम्भश्चैव निशुम्भकः ।। 7.6.35 ।।
explanation: Karna, the very deceitful, and Lokapala, and also the righteous; Yama and Arjuna, and Kritavarma, and also Shumbha and Nishumbha.

shloka_text: असुरा दानवाश्चैव सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः । सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते ऽपराजिताः ।। 7.6.36 ।।
explanation: Asuras and Danavas, who are indeed powerful and and mighty, all of them, having entered battle, are not heard of as undefeated.

shloka_text: सर्वैः क्रतुशतैरिष्टं सर्वे मायाविदस्तथा । सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वे शत्रुभयङ्कराः ।। 7.6.37 ।।
explanation: All had performed hundreds of sacrifices, all were experts in illusion, all were skilled in all weapons, and all were terrifying to their enemies.

shloka_text: नारायणेन निहताः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु सर्वेषां क्षमं कर्तुमिहार्हथ ।। 7.6.38 ।।
explanation: Hundreds and thousands were slain by Narayana. Therefore, knowing this, you all should do what is proper for everyone here.

shloka_text: ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः । ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं भगांशाविव वासवम् ।। 7.6.39 ।।
explanation: Then Sumali and Mali, having heard Malyavan's words, spoke to their elder brother, just as Bhaga and Amsha (spoke) to Vasava.

shloka_text: स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं चाप्यैश्वर्यं परिपालितम् । आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं सुधर्मः प्रापितः पथि ।। 7.6.40 ।।
explanation: Well-studied, given, and sacrificed; prosperity was also protected. A healthy life was obtained, and good dharma was attained on the path.

shloka_text: देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रैः समवगाह्य च । जिता द्विषो ह्यप्रतिमास्तन्नो मृत्युकृतं भयम् ।। 7.6.41 ।।
explanation: Having plunged into the unshakeable divine ocean with weapons, and indeed having conquered the unequalled enemies, therefore there is no fear of death for us.

shloka_text: नारायणश्च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा । अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा ।। 7.6.42 ।।
explanation: Narayana, Rudra, Shakra, and even Yama, all always fear to stand in our presence.

shloka_text: विष्णोर्देवस्य नास्त्येव कारणं राक्षसेश्वर । देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः ।। 7.6.43 ।।
explanation: O Lord of Rakshasas, there is no inherent cause for the god Vishnu. It is indeed due to the fault of the gods themselves that Vishnu's mind has become agitated.

shloka_text: तस्मादद्य समुद्युक्ताः सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः । देवानेव जिघांसाम एभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः ।। 7.6.44 ।।
explanation: Therefore, today, being well-prepared and accompanied by all armies, we shall indeed kill the gods, from whom this fault has arisen.

shloka_text: एवं सम्मन्त्र्य बलिनः सर्वे सैन्यसमावृताः । उद्योगं घोषयित्वा तु सर्वे नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः ।। युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धा जम्भवृत्रबला इव ।। 7.6.45 ।।
explanation: Thus, having deliberated, all the powerful and foremost Rākṣasas, surrounded by their armies, and having declared their resolve, set out for battle, enraged, like the forces of Jamba and Vṛtra.

shloka_text: इति ते राम सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः । युद्धाय निर्ययुः सर्वे महाकाया महाबलाः ।। 7.6.46 ।।
explanation: Thus, O Rama, having deliberated, all those Rākṣasas, huge-bodied and mighty, set out for battle with full preparation.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैर्वारणैश्चैव हयैश्च गिरिसन्निभैः । खरैर्गोभी रथोष्ट्रैश्च शिंशुमारैर्भुजङ्गमैः ।। 7.6.47 ।।
explanation: By chariots, by elephants, and also by mountain-like horses, by donkeys, by cows, and by chariots and camels, by porpoises, and by serpents.

shloka_text: मकरैः कच्छपैर्मीनैर्विहङ्गैर्गरुडोपमैः । सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्वराहैश्च सृमरैश्चमरैरपि ।। 7.6.48 ।।
explanation: By crocodiles, by tortoises, by fish, by birds resembling Garuḍa, by lions, by tigers, and by boars, and also by sṛmaras and chamaras.

shloka_text: त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । प्रयाता देवलोकाय योद्धुं दैवतशत्रवः ।। 7.6.49 ।।
explanation: All the Rākṣasas, arrogant with power and enemies of the gods, having abandoned Lanka, departed for the world of the gods to fight.
