shloka_text: लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ । भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः ।। 7.6.50 ।।
explanation: Having seen the destruction of Lanka, all the beings dwelling in Lanka became completely fearful and disheartened.

shloka_text: रथोत्तमैरुह्यमानाः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.51 ।।
explanation: Being carried by excellent chariots, by hundreds and by thousands.

shloka_text: प्रयाता राक्षसास्तूर्णं देवलोकं प्रयत्नतः । रक्षसामेव मार्गेण दैवतान्यपचक्रमुः ।। 7.6.52 ।।
explanation: The Rākṣasas quickly departed to the world of the gods with effort. The gods retreated by the very path of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: भौमाश्चैवान्तरिक्षाश्च कालाज्ञप्ता भयावहाः । उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावाय समुत्थिताः ।। 7.6.53 ।।
explanation: Earthly and atmospheric portents, dreadful and ordained by time, have arisen for the destruction of the Rākṣasa lords.

shloka_text: अस्थीनि मेघा ववृषुरुष्णं शोणितमेव च । वेलां समुद्राश्चोत्क्रान्ताश्चेलुश्चाप्यथ भूधराः ।। 7.6.54 ।।
explanation: Clouds rained bones and hot blood. Oceans transgressed their shores, and mountains also trembled.

shloka_text: अट्टहासान्विमुञ्चन्तो घननादसमस्वनाः । वाश्यन्त्यश्च शिवास्तत्र दारुणं घोरदर्शनाः ।। 7.6.55 ।।
explanation: The jackals there, emitting loud roars, with voices like the thunder of clouds, and howling, were terribly dreadful to behold.

shloka_text: सम्पतन्त्यथ भूतानि दृश्यन्ते च यथाक्रमम् । गृध्रचक्रं महच्चात्र ज्वलनोद्गारिभिर्मुखैः ।। 7.6.56 ।।
explanation: Then creatures gather and are seen in succession. And here, a great flock of vultures with mouths spewing fire.

shloka_text: राक्षसानामुपरि खे भ्रमते ऽलातचक्रवत् । कपोता रक्तपादाश्च शारिका विद्रुता ययुः ।। काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडाला वै द्विपादयः ।। 7.6.57 ।।
explanation: Above the Rākṣasas, it revolves in the sky like a firebrand wheel. Pigeons with red feet and mynah birds fled and departed. Crows caw right there, and cats indeed are two-footed.

shloka_text: उत्पातांस्ताननादृत्य राक्षसा बलगर्विताः । यान्त्येव न निवर्त्तन्ते मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः ।। 7.6.58 ।।
explanation: Disregarding those omens, the Rākṣasas, arrogant with their strength, proceed and do not return, bound by the noose of death.

shloka_text: माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलाः । आसन्पुरःसरास्तेषां क्रतूनामिव पावकाः ।। 7.6.59 ।।
explanation: Malyavan, Sumali, and Mali, who were exceedingly powerful, were at the forefront of them, like the fires of sacrifices.

shloka_text: माल्यवन्तं च ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् । निशाचरा ह्याश्रयन्ति धातारमिव देवताः ।। 7.6.60 ।।
explanation: And all those night-wanderers indeed take refuge in Malyavan, like the immovable Malyavan mountain, just as the gods take refuge in Dhata.

shloka_text: तद्बलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम् । जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ मालिवशे स्थितम् ।। 7.6.61 ।।
explanation: That army of the Rākṣasa lords, resounding like the thunder of great clouds, being under the command of Māli, went to the world of the gods, desiring victory.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः । देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य चक्रे युद्धे तदा मनः ।। 7.6.62 ।।
explanation: Lord Nārāyaṇa, having heard from the messenger of the gods about that mobilization of the Rākṣasas, then set his mind on battle.

shloka_text: स सज्जायुधतूणीरो वैनतेयोपरि स्थितः । आसज्ज्य कवचं दिव्यं सहस्रार्कसमद्युति ।। 7.6.63 ।।
explanation: He, with weapons and quivers ready, stood upon Vainateya, having donned his divine armor, which shone with the brilliance of a thousand suns.

shloka_text: आबध्य शरसम्पूर्णे इषुधी विमले तदा । श्रोणिसूत्रं च खड्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः ।। शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् ।। 7.6.64 ।।
explanation: Then, the lotus-eyed one, having fastened the two bright quivers full of arrows, the waist-cord, and the bright sword, (also prepared) the excellent weapons named conch, discus, mace, Śārṅga bow

shloka_text: सुपर्णं गिरिसङ्काशं वैनतेयमथास्थितः । राक्षसानामभावाय ययौ तूर्णतरं प्रभुः ।। 7.6.65 ।।
explanation: Then the mighty lord, having mounted Vainateya (Garuda) who was like a mountain and had beautiful wings, went very swiftly for the annihilation of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपृष्ठे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः । काञ्चनस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.6.66 ।।
explanation: Dark-complexioned Hari, clad in yellow garments, shone on Suparna's back, like a lightning-laden cloud on the peak of a golden mountain.

shloka_text: स सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च गन्धर्वयक्षैरुपगीयमानः । समाससादासुरसैन्यशत्रूंश्चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः ।। 7.6.67 ।।
explanation: He, being glorified by Siddhas, divine sages, great serpents, Gandharvas, and Yakshas, approached the enemies of the Asura army, bearing the discus, sword, Sharnga bow, and conch in his hands.

shloka_text: सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् । चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं चलोपलं नील इवाचलेन्द्रः ।। 7.6.68 ।।
explanation: That army of the king of Rakshasas, whose flanks were driven by a wind like that from Garuda's wings, with fluttering banners and scattered weapons, trembled like the great mountain Nila with its rocks shaking.

shloka_text: ततः शरैः शोणितमांसरूषितैर्युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः । निशाचराः सम्परिवार्य माधवं वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः ।। 7.6.69 ।।
explanation: Then, the night-wanderers, having completely surrounded Madhava, pierced him by thousands with excellent weapons and arrows, which were stained with blood and flesh and whose forms were like the fire of the dissolution of the world.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः ।। 6 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the sixth chapter.

shloka_text: नारायणगिरिं ते तु गर्जन्तो राक्षसाम्बुदाः । ववर्षुः शरवर्षेण वर्षेणेवाद्रिमम्बुदाः ।। 7.7.1 ।।
explanation: Those roaring rakshasa-clouds rained upon Mount Narayana with a shower of arrows, just as clouds rain upon a mountain with rain.

shloka_text: श्यामावदातस्तैर्विष्णुर्नीलैर्नक्तञ्चरोत्तमैः । वृतो ऽञ्जनगिरीवासीत् वर्षमाणैः पयोधरैः ।। 7.7.2 ।।
explanation: Vishnu, dark-complexioned, surrounded by those blue, best of night-wanderers, was like the Anjana mountain surrounded by raining clouds.

shloka_text: शलभा इव केदारं मशका इव पर्वतम् । यथामृतघटं दंशा मकरा इव चार्णवम् ।। 7.7.3 ।।
explanation: Locusts like a field, mosquitoes like a mountain, as flies (attack) a pot of nectar, and crocodiles like the ocean.

shloka_text: तथा रक्षोधनुर्मुक्ता वज्रानिलमनोजवाः । हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोका इव विपर्यये ।। 7.7.4 ।।
explanation: Thus, the arrows released from the demon's bow, swift as a thunderbolt, wind, and thought, entered Hari, just as worlds dissolve at the time of cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: स्यन्दनैः स्यन्दनगता गजैश्च गजपृष्ठगाः । अश्वारोहास्तथाश्वैश्च पादाताश्चाम्बरे स्थिताः ।। 7.7.5 ।।
explanation: Chariot-riders with chariots, and elephant-riders with elephants, and similarly horse-riders with horses, and foot-soldiers stood in the sky.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रा गिरिनिभाः शरैः शक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः । निरुछ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायामा इव द्विजम् ।। 7.7.6 ।।
explanation: The mountain-like chiefs of Rākṣasas, with arrows, spears, lances, and javelins, made the monkey breathless, just as breath control (prāṇāyāma) makes a brahmin breathless.

shloka_text: निशाचरैस्ताड्यमानो मीनैरिव महोदधिः । शार्ङ्गमायम्य दुर्धर्षो राक्षसेभ्यो ऽसृजच्छरान् ।। 7.7.7 ।।
explanation: Even as he was being struck by the night-wanderers, like the great ocean by fish, the formidable one, having drawn the Sharnga bow, released arrows at the demons.

shloka_text: शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैर्वज्रवक्त्रैर्मनोजवैः । चिच्छेद विष्णुर्निशितैः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.8 ।।
explanation: Vishnu cut them down by hundreds and then by thousands with sharp arrows, shot with full draw, having adamantine points and swift as thought.

shloka_text: विद्राव्य शरवर्षेण वर्षा वायुरिवोत्थितम् । पाञ्चजन्यं महाशङ्खं प्रदध्मौ पुरुषोत्तमः ।। 7.7.9 ।।
explanation: Having dispersed (the enemy) with a shower of arrows, just as wind disperses rising rain, Purushottama blew his great conch, Panchajanya.

shloka_text: सो ऽम्बुजो हरिणा ध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट् । ररास भीमनिर्हादस्त्रैलोक्यं व्यथयन्निव ।। 7.7.10 ।।
explanation: That conch, the king of conches, blown by Hari with all His might, roared with a terrible sound, as if agitating the three worlds.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवः सो ऽथ त्रासयामास राक्षसान् । मृगराज इवारण्ये समदानिव कुञ्जरान् ।। 7.7.11 ।।
explanation: Then, that sound of the conch-king terrified the Rākṣasas, just as a lion in the forest frightens rutting elephants.

shloka_text: न शेकुरश्वाः संस्थातुं विमदाः कुञ्जराभवन् । स्यन्दनेभ्यश्च्युता वीराः शङ्खरावितदुर्बलाः ।। 7.7.12 ।।
explanation: The horses could not stand still, the elephants lost their rut, and heroes, weakened by the sound of conches, fell from their chariots.

shloka_text: शार्ङ्गचापविनिर्मुक्ता वज्रतुल्याननाः शराः । विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम् ।। 7.7.13 ।।
explanation: The arrows, released from the Śārṅga bow, with points like thunderbolts, having torn apart those Rākṣasas, with their well-feathered shafts, entered the earth.

shloka_text: भिद्यमानाः शरैः सङ्ख्ये नारायणकरच्युतैः । निपेतू राक्षसा भूमौ शैला वज्रहता इव ।। 7.7.14 ।।
explanation: The Rakshasas, being pierced in battle by arrows released from Narayana's hands, fell to the ground like mountains struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: व्रणानि परगात्रेभ्यो विष्णुचक्रकृतानि वै । असृक्क्षरन्ति धाराभिः स्वर्णधारा इवाचलाः ।। 7.7.15 ।।
explanation: The wounds made by Vishnu's discus on the bodies of the enemies indeed stream blood in torrents, like golden streams from mountains.

shloka_text: शङ्खराजरवश्चापि शार्ङ्गचापरस्वस्तथा । राक्षसानां रवांश्चापि ग्रसते वैष्णवो रवः ।। 7.7.16 ।।
explanation: And the sound of the great conch, and the sound of the Sharnga bow, and also the sounds of the Rakshasas, the Vaishnava sound overwhelms them.

shloka_text: तेषां शिरोधरान्धूताञ्छरध्वजधनूंषि च । रथान्पताकास्तूणीरांश्चिच्छेद स हरिः शरैः ।। 7.7.17 ।।
explanation: He, Hari, with his arrows, cut off their shaken necks, and their arrows, banners, bows, chariots, pennants, and quivers.

shloka_text: सूर्यादिव करा घोरा ऊर्मयः सागरादिव । पर्वतादिव नागेन्द्रा धारौघा इव चाम्बुदात् ।। 7.7.18 ।।
explanation: Terrible rays like from the sun, waves like from the ocean, lordly elephants like from the mountain, and torrents of water like from the cloud.

shloka_text: तथा शार्ङ्गविनिर्मुक्ताः शरा नारायणेरिताः । निर्धावन्तीषवस्तूर्णं शतशोथ सहस्रशः ।। 7.7.19 ।।
explanation: Similarly, arrows released from the Sharnga, propelled by Narayana, rush forth swiftly by hundreds and by thousands.

shloka_text: शरभेण यथा सिंहाः सिंहेन द्विरदा यथा । द्विरदेन यथा व्याघ्रा व्याघ्रेण द्वीपिनो यथा ।। 7.7.20 ।।
explanation: Just as lions [are overcome] by a Sharabha, just as elephants [are overcome] by a lion, just as tigers [are overcome] by an elephant, just as leopards [are overcome] by a tiger.

shloka_text: द्वीपिनेव यथा श्वानः शुना मार्जारका यथा । मार्जारेण यथा सर्पाः सर्पेण च यथा ऽ ऽखवः ।। 7.7.21 ।।
explanation: Just as a leopard preys upon dogs, just as a dog preys upon cats, just as a cat preys upon snakes, and just as a snake preys upon mice.

shloka_text: तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । द्रवन्ति द्राविताश्चन्ये शायिताश्च महीतले ।। 7.7.22 ।।
explanation: Thus, all those demons, by the mighty Vishnu, flee; and others are driven away and laid low on the ground.

shloka_text: राक्षसानां सहस्राणि निहत्य मधुसूदनः । वारिजं पूरयामास तोयदं सुरराडिव ।। 7.7.23 ।।
explanation: Having killed thousands of Rākṣasas, Madhusūdana blew his conch, just as the king of gods (Indra) makes a cloud thunder.

shloka_text: नारायणशरत्रस्तं शङ्खनादसुविह्वलम् । ययौ लङ्कामभिमुखं प्रभग्नं राक्षसं बलम् ।। 7.7.24 ।।
explanation: The routed Rakshasa army, terrified by Narayana's arrows and greatly bewildered by the sound of the conch, went towards Lanka.

shloka_text: प्रभग्ने राक्षसबले नारायणशराहते । सुमाली शरवर्षेण निववार रणे हरिम् ।। 7.7.25 ।।
explanation: When the demon army was shattered, struck by Narayana's arrows, Sumali obstructed Hari in battle with a rain of arrows.

shloka_text: स तु तं छादयामास नीहार इव भास्करम् । राक्षसाः सत्त्वसम्पन्नाः पुनर्धैर्यं समादधुः ।। 7.7.26 ।।
explanation: He covered him, just as mist obscures the sun. The Rākṣasas, full of valor, again regained their courage.

shloka_text: अथ सो ऽभ्यपतद्रोषाद्राक्षसो बलदर्पितः । महानादं प्रकुर्वाणो राक्षसाञ्जीवयन्निव ।। 7.7.27 ।।
explanation: Then, that Rakshasa, arrogant with strength, angrily rushed forward, making a great roar, as if enlivening the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: उत्क्षिप्य लम्बाभरणं धुन्वन्करमिव द्विपः । ररास राक्षसो हर्षात्सतडित्तोयदो यथा ।। 7.7.28 ।।
explanation: Lifting up his long ornaments, shaking them like an elephant shakes its trunk, the demon roared with joy, like a thundercloud accompanied by lightning.

shloka_text: सुमालेर्नर्दतस्तस्य शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् । चिच्छेद यन्तुरश्वाश्च भ्रान्तास्तस्य तु रक्षसः ।। 7.7.29 ।।
explanation: He cut off the head of that roaring Sumali, adorned with shining earrings. And the charioteer's horses of that demon became bewildered.

shloka_text: तैरश्वैर्भ्राम्यते भ्रान्तैः सुमाली राक्षसेश्वरः । इन्द्रियाश्वैः परिभ्रान्तैर्धृतिहीनो यथा नरः ।। 7.7.30 ।।
explanation: Sumali, the lord of Rakshasas, is made to wander by those bewildered horses, just as a man devoid of fortitude is completely led astray by his bewildered sense-horses.

shloka_text: ततो विष्णुं महाबाहुं प्रपतन्तं रणाजिरे । हृते सुमालेरश्वैश्च रथे विष्णुरथं प्रति ।। 7.7.31 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Vishnu, falling in the battlefield, rushed towards his own chariot when it was carried off by Sumali's horses.

shloka_text: माली चाभ्यद्रवद्युक्तः प्रगृह्य सशरं धनुः । मालेर्धनुश्च्युता बाणाः कार्तस्वरविभूषिताः । विविशुर्हरिमासाद्य क्रौञ्चं पत्ररथा इव ।। 7.7.32 ।।
explanation: And Mali, prepared, rushed forth, holding a bow with arrows. Arrows, adorned with gold, shot from Mali's bow, struck and pierced Hari, like feathered arrows piercing the Krauncha mountain.

shloka_text: अर्द्यमानः शरैः सो ऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः । चुक्षुभे न रणे विष्णुर्जितेन्द्रिय इवाधिभिः ।। 7.7.33 ।।
explanation: Then, though tormented by thousands of arrows released by Mali, Vishnu was not disturbed in battle, just like one who has conquered his senses is not disturbed by mental afflictions.

shloka_text: अथ मौर्वीस्वनं कृत्वा भगवान्भूतभावनः । मालिनं प्रति बाणौघान्ससर्जारिनिषूदनः ।। 7.7.34 ।।
explanation: Then, having twanged his bowstring, the divine Lord, the creator of beings, the destroyer of enemies, discharged a multitude of arrows towards Malina.

shloka_text: ते मालिदेहमासाद्य वज्रविद्युत्प्रभाः शराः । पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव सुधारसम् ।। 7.7.35 ।।
explanation: Those arrows, brilliant like thunderbolts and lightning, having reached Māli's body, drank his blood like serpents drink nectar.

shloka_text: मालिनं विमुखं कृत्वा शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः । मालिमौलिं ध्वजं चापं वाजिनश्चाप्यपातयत् ।। 7.7.36 ।।
explanation: Having defeated Mālin, the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace struck down Mālin's crown, banner, bow, and also his horses.

shloka_text: विरथस्तु गदां गृह्य माली नक्तञ्चरोत्तमः । आपुप्लुवे गदापाणिर्गिर्यग्रादिव केसरी ।। 7.7.37 ।।
explanation: But Mali, the foremost of the night-wanderers, being chariotless, seized his mace. Mace in hand, he leaped up like a lion from a mountain peak.

shloka_text: गदया गरुडेशानमीशानमिव चान्तकः । ललाटदेशे ऽभ्यहनद्वज्रेणेन्द्रो यथा ऽचलम् ।। 7.7.38 ।।
explanation: With a mace, he struck the lord of eagles on the forehead, just as Antaka (Yama) would strike Ishana (Shiva), and as Indra strikes a mountain with his thunderbolt.

shloka_text: गदयाभिहतस्तेन मालिना गरुडो भृशम् । रणात्पराङ्मुखं देवं कृतवान्वेदनातुरः ।। 7.7.39 ।।
explanation: Severely struck by Mālin with his mace, Garuḍa, distressed by pain, made the god turn away from the battle.

shloka_text: पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै । उदतिष्ठन्महाञ्छब्दो रक्षसामभिनर्दताम् ।। 7.7.40 ।।
explanation: When the god (Vishnu), mounted on Garuda, was made to turn away by Mālī, a great roar arose from the exultant Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: रक्षसां रवतां रावं श्रुत्वा हरिहयानुजः ।। 7.7.41 ।।
explanation: Having heard the roar of the roaring Rākṣasas, the younger brother of Indra.

shloka_text: तिर्यगास्थाय सङ्क्रुद्धः पक्षीशे भगवान्हरिः । पराङ्मुखो ऽप्युत्ससर्ज मालेश्चक्रं जिघांसया ।। 7.7.42 ।।
explanation: Lord Hari, intensely angry, while on the lord of birds, turned sideways and, even though his back was turned, hurled his discus at Māli with the intention to kill.

shloka_text: तत्सूर्यमण्डलाभासं स्वभासा भासयन्नभः । कालचक्रनिभं चक्रं मालेः शीर्षमपातयत् ।। 7.7.43 ।।
explanation: That discus, brilliant like the sun's orb, illuminating the sky with its own radiance, and resembling the wheel of time, severed Mali's head.

shloka_text: तच्छिरो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रोत्कृत्तं बिभीषणम् । पपात रुधिरोद्गारि पुरा राहुशिरो यथा ।। 7.7.44 ।।
explanation: That terrifying head of the king of Rākṣasas, severed by the discus, fell, gushing blood, just as Rāhu's head did formerly.

shloka_text: ततः सुरैः संसहृष्टैः सर्वप्राणसमीरितः । सिंहनादरवोन्मुक्तः साधु देवेतिवादिभिः ।। 7.7.45 ।।
explanation: Then, by the greatly delighted gods, who were exclaiming 'Excellent, O God!', a lion-like roar was released, uttered with all their might.

shloka_text: मालिनं निहतं दृष्ट्वा सुमाली माल्यवानपि । सबलौ शोकसन्तप्तौ लङ्कामेव प्रधावितौ ।। 7.7.46 ।।
explanation: Seeing Malina killed, Sumali and Malyavan, both with their forces and afflicted with sorrow, ran towards Lanka.

shloka_text: गरुडस्तु समाश्वस्तः सन्निवृत्य यथा पुरा । राक्षसान्द्रावयामास पक्षवातेन कोपितः ।। 7.7.47 ।।
explanation: Garuḍa, having been comforted, returned as before. Enraged, he drove away the Rākṣasas with the wind from his wings.

shloka_text: चक्रकृत्तास्यकमला गदासञ्चूर्णितोरसः । लाङ्गलग्लपितग्रीवा मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकाः ।। 7.7.48 ।।
explanation: Their lotus-like faces severed by discuses, their chests crushed by maces, their necks destroyed by ploughs, and their heads shattered by pestles.

shloka_text: केचिच्चैवासिना छिन्नास्तथान्ये शरपीडिताः । निपेतुरम्बरात्तूर्णं राक्षसाः सागराम्भसि ।। 7.7.49 ।।
explanation: Some were cut down by swords, and others, wounded by arrows, the Rākṣasas swiftly fell from the sky into the ocean's waters.

shloka_text: नारायणो बाणवराशनीभिर्विदारयामास धनुर्विमुक्तैः । नक्तञ्चरान्मुक्तविधूतकेशान्यथा ऽशनीभिः सतडिन्महाभ्राः ।। 7.7.50 ।।
explanation: Narayana tore apart the night-wanderers, whose hair was loose and dishevelled, with excellent arrows released from his bow, which were like thunderbolts, just as great clouds with lightning are torn apart by thunderbolts.

shloka_text: भिन्नातपत्रं पतमानमस्त्रं शरैरपध्वस्तविनीतवेषम् । विनिस्सृतान्त्रं भयलोलनेत्रं बलं तदुन्मत्ततरं बभूव ।। 7.7.51 ।।
explanation: The army, with broken parasols, falling weapons, disciplined attire destroyed by arrows, with protruding intestines, and eyes rolling in fear, became even more frenzied.

shloka_text: सिंहार्दितानामिव कुञ्जराणां निशाचराणां सह कुञ्जराणाम् । रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम् ।। 7.7.52 ।।
explanation: Like elephants tormented by lions, the roars and movements of the night-wanderers along with their elephants, who were being crushed by the ancient lion, occurred simultaneously.

shloka_text: ते वार्यमाणा हरिबाणजालैः सबाणजालानि समुत्सृजन्तः । धावन्ति नक्तञ्चरकालमेघा वायुप्रभिन्ना इव कालमेघाः ।। 7.7.53 ।।
explanation: They, being repelled by the multitude of Hari's arrows, and themselves discharging their own multitudes of arrows, the night-roaming demons flee like dark clouds scattered by the wind.

shloka_text: चक्रपहारैर्विनिकृत्तशीर्षाः सञ्चूर्णिताङ्गाश्च गदाप्रहारैः । अभिप्रहारैर्द्विविधा विभिन्नाः पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः ।। 7.7.54 ।।
explanation: Their heads severed by blows of discus, and their limbs crushed by blows of mace, split into two by various blows, the chief Rakshasas fall like mountains.

shloka_text: विलम्बमानैर्मणिहारकुण्डलैर्निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः । निपात्यमानैर्ददृशे निरन्तरं निपात्यमानैरिव नीलपर्वतैः ।। 7.7.55 ।।
explanation: The night-wanderers, resembling dark clouds, with their dangling jewel necklaces and earrings, were continuously seen being struck down, as if dark mountains were being felled.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः ।। 7 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the seventh chapter.

shloka_text: हन्यमाने बले तस्मिन्पद्मनाभेन पृष्ठतः । माल्वान्सन्निवृत्तो ऽथ वेलामेत्य इवार्णवः ।। 7.8.1 ।।
explanation: When that army was being struck down from behind by Padmanabha, Mālva then retreated, like the ocean reaching the shore.

shloka_text: संरक्तनयनः कोपाच्चलन्मौलिर्निशाचरः । पद्मनाभमिदं प्राह वचनं पुरुषोत्तमम् ।। 7.8.2 ।।
explanation: The demon, with bloodshot eyes from anger and a trembling head, spoke these words to Padmanābha, Puruṣottama.

shloka_text: नारायण न जानीषे क्षात्रधर्मं पुरातनम् । अयुद्धमनसो भीतानस्मान्हंसि यथेतरः ।। 7.8.3 ।।
explanation: O Narayana, you do not know the ancient duty of a Kshatriya. You kill us, who are fearful and disinclined to fight, just like any other person.

shloka_text: पराङ्मुखवधं पापं यः करोत्यसुरेतरः । स हन्ता न गतः स्वर्गं लभते पुण्यकर्मणाम् ।। 7.8.4 ।।
explanation: He who, being a non-demon, commits the sin of killing one who has turned their back, that killer does not attain the heaven of those who perform meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: युद्धश्रद्धा ऽथवा ते ऽस्ति शङ्खचक्रगदाधर । 4अहं स्थितो ऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत्तव ।। 7.8.5 ।।
explanation: O holder of conch, discus, and mace, or if you have a desire for battle, I am standing here. Show me your strength.

shloka_text: माल्यवन्तं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् । उवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं तं देवराजानुजो बली ।। 7.8.6 ।।
explanation: Having seen Malyavan standing like an immovable mountain, the mighty younger brother of the king of gods spoke to that king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मया ऽभयम् । राक्षसोत्सादनं दत्तं तदेतदनुपाल्यते ।। 7.8.7 ।।
explanation: Indeed, by me, protection was granted to the gods who were terrified by you, and the destruction of the Rakshasas was also granted. That (promise) is now being fulfilled.

shloka_text: प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया । सो ऽहं वो निहनिष्यामि रसातलगतानपि ।। 7.8.8 ।।
explanation: Indeed, I must always do what is dear to the gods, even at the cost of my life. Therefore, I will kill you, even if you have gone to Rasatala.

shloka_text: देवदेवं ब्रुवाणं तं रक्ताम्बुरुहलोचनम् । शक्त्या बिभेद सङ्क्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रो भुजान्तरे ।। 7.8.9 ।।
explanation: The greatly enraged king of Rākṣasas pierced him, who was speaking (as) the God of gods and had red-lotus eyes, with a spear in the chest.

shloka_text: माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना । हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतह्रदा ।। 7.8.10 ।।
explanation: The spear, released from Malyavan's arm, making a bell-like sound, shone on Hari's chest, like lightning in a cloud.

shloka_text: ततस्तामेव चोत्कृष्य शक्तिं शक्तिधरप्रियः । माल्यवन्तं समुद्दिश्य चिक्षेपाम्बुरुहेक्षणः ।। 7.8.11 ।।
explanation: Then, the lotus-eyed one, beloved of the wielder of the spear, having lifted up that very spear, aimed at Malyavan and threw it.

shloka_text: स्कन्दोत्सृष्टेव सा शक्तिर्गोविन्दकरनिस्सृता । काङ्क्षन्ती राक्षसं प्रायान्माहेन्द्रीवाञ्जनाचलम् ।। 7.8.12 ।।
explanation: That power, having emerged from Govinda's hand, as if hurled by Skanda, went towards the demon, desiring it, like Indra's lightning bolt towards Añjana mountain.

shloka_text: सा तस्योरसि विस्तीर्णे हारभारा ऽवभासिते । अपतद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्य गिरिकूट इवाशनिः ।। 7.8.13 ।।
explanation: She fell upon the broad chest of the lord of Rākṣasas, which was resplendent with many necklaces, like a thunderbolt upon a mountain peak.

shloka_text: तया भिन्नतनुत्राणः प्राविशद्विपुलं तमः । माल्यवान्पुनराश्वस्तस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः ।। 7.8.14 ।।
explanation: His armor shattered by her, Malyavan entered a vast darkness; but having recovered, he stood like an immovable mountain.

shloka_text: ततः कार्ष्णायसं शूलं कण्टकैर्बहुभिर्वतम् । प्रगृह्याभ्यहनद्देवं स्तनयोरन्तरे दृढम् ।। 7.8.15 ।।
explanation: Then, having seized an iron spear furnished with many spikes, he struck the god firmly in between the breasts.

shloka_text: तथैव रणरक्तस्तु मुष्टिना वासवानुजम् । ताडयित्वा धनुर्मात्रमपक्रान्तो निशाचरः ।। 7.8.16 ।।
explanation: And similarly, the demon, eager for battle, having struck the younger brother of Vasava with his fist, retreated a bow's length.

shloka_text: ततो ऽम्बरे महाञ्छब्दः साधुसाध्विति चोदितः । आहत्य राक्षसो विष्णुं गरुडं चाप्यताडयत् ।। 7.8.17 ।।
explanation: Then, a great sound of "Excellent! Excellent!" was raised in the sky. The demon, having struck Vishnu, also struck Garuda.

shloka_text: वैनतेयस्ततः क्रुद्धः पक्षवातेन राक्षसम् । व्यपोहद्बलवान्वायुः शुष्कपर्णचयं यथा ।। 7.8.18 ।।
explanation: Then, the enraged Vainateya, by the wind of his wings, blew away the demon, just as a powerful wind scatters a heap of dry leaves.

shloka_text: द्विजेन्द्रपक्षवातेन द्रावितं दृश्य पूर्वजम् । सुमाली स्वबलैः सार्धं लङ्कामभिमुखो ययौ ।। 7.8.19 ।।
explanation: Having seen his elder brother routed by the wind from the wings of the king of birds, Sumali, along with his own forces, went towards Lanka.

shloka_text: पक्षवातबलोद्धूतो माल्यवानपि राक्षसः । स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः ।। 7.8.20 ।।
explanation: Malyavan, the Rakshasa, also, having been tossed by the force of the wind from the wings, gathered his own army and went to Lanka, covered with shame.

shloka_text: एवं ते राक्षसा तेन हरिणा कमलेक्षण । बहुशः संयुगे भग्ना हतप्रवरनायकाः ।। 7.8.21 ।।
explanation: Thus, O lotus-eyed one, those demons were repeatedly routed in battle by that Hari, their chief leaders slain.

shloka_text: अशक्नुवन्तस्ते विष्णुं प्रतियोद्धुं भयार्दिताः । त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः ।। 7.8.22 ।।
explanation: Unable to fight against Vishnu, and afflicted by fear, they abandoned Lanka and went to reside in Patala with their wives.

shloka_text: सुमालिनं समासाद्य राक्षसं रघुसत्तम । स्थिताः प्रख्यातवीर्यास्ते वंशे सालकटङ्कटे ।। 7.8.23 ।।
explanation: O best of the Raghus, having approached the demon Sumalin, they, of renowned valor, resided in the Salakatankata lineage.

shloka_text: ये त्वया निहतास्ते तु पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः । सुमाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः ।।
explanation: Indeed, those Rakshasas named Paulastyas who were slain by you were Sumali, Malyavan, Mali, and those who were their leaders.

shloka_text: सर्वे तेभ्यो महाभागा रावणाद्बलवत्तराः ।। 7.8.24 ।।
explanation: All of them, the great-souled ones, were more powerful than Ravana.

shloka_text: न चान्यो राक्षसान्हन्ता सुरारीन्देवकण्टकान् । ऋते नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ।। 7.8.25 ।।
explanation: And there is no other slayer of the Rakshasas, who are enemies and tormentors of the gods, except Lord Narayana, the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace.

shloka_text: भवान्नारायणो देवश्चतुर्बाहुः सनातनः । राक्षसान्हन्तुमुत्पन्नो ह्यजेयः प्रभुरव्ययः ।। 7.8.26 ।।
explanation: You are the God Narayana, four-armed and eternal. You have indeed manifested to kill the Rakshasas, an unconquerable, imperishable Lord.

shloka_text: नष्टधर्मव्यवस्थाता काले काले प्रजाकरः । उत्पद्यते दस्युवधे शरणागतवत्सलः ।। 7.8.27 ।।
explanation: The restorer of the lost order of righteousness, the protector of the people, appears from time to time for the destruction of the wicked, affectionate towards those who seek refuge.

shloka_text: एषा मया तव नराधिप राक्षसानामुत्पत्तिरद्य कथिता सकला यथावत् । भूयो निबोध रघुसत्तम रावणस्य जन्मप्रभावमतुलं ससुतस्य सर्वम् ।। 7.8.28 ।।
explanation: O king, I have today narrated to you the entire origin of the Rākṣasas, just as it happened. Now, O best of the Raghu dynasty, listen further to the complete and unparalleled account of Rāvaṇa's birth and might, along with that of his sons.

shloka_text: चिरात्सुमाली व्यचरद्रसातलं स राक्षसो विष्णुभयार्दितस्तदा । पुत्रैश्च पौत्रैश्च समन्वितो बली ततस्तु लङ्कामवसद्धनेश्वरः ।। 7.8.29 ।।
explanation: That powerful demon Sumali, tormented by fear of Vishnu, then went to Rasatala for a long time, accompanied by his sons and grandsons. Thereafter, the lord of wealth resided in Lanka.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टमः सर्गः ।। 8 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by the sage Valmiki, this is the eighth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य सुमाली नाम राक्षसः । रसातलान्मर्त्यलोकं सर्वं वै विचचार ह ।। 7.9.1 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, a demon named Sumali wandered throughout the entire mortal world from Rasatala.

shloka_text: नीलजीमूतसङ्काशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः । कन्यां दुहितरं गृह्य विना पद्ममिव श्रियम् ।। 7.9.2 ।।
explanation: Resembling a blue cloud, with glowing golden earrings, he took his daughter, the maiden, who was like Shri without her lotus.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा विचरन्वै महीतलम् । तदापश्यत्स गच्छन्तं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरम् ।। 7.9.3 ।।
explanation: Then, that king of Rakshasas, while wandering on the earth, saw the lord of wealth going by the Pushpaka.

shloka_text: गच्छन्तं पितरं द्रष्टुं पुलस्त्यतनयं विभुम् । तं दृष्ट्वा ऽमरसङ्काशं स्वच्छन्दं तपनोपमम् ।। 7.9.4 ।।
explanation: Going to see his father, the mighty son of Pulastya. Having seen him, who was god-like, moving freely, and resembling the sun.

shloka_text: रसातलं प्रविष्टः सन्मर्त्यलोकात्सविस्मयः । इत्येवं चिन्तयामास राक्षसानां महामतिः ।। 7.9.5 ।।
explanation: Having entered Rasatala from the mortal world, astonished, the great-minded one of the Rakshasas thus thought.

shloka_text: किं कृतं श्रेय इत्येवं वर्धेमहि कथं वयम् । अथाब्रवीत्सुतां रक्षः कैकसीं नाम नामतः ।। 7.9.6 ।।
explanation: What good deed should be done, and how may we thus prosper? Then the Rakshasa spoke to his daughter, Kaikasi by name.

shloka_text: पुत्रि प्रदानकालो ऽयं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते । प्रत्याख्यानाच्च भीतैस्त्वं न वरैः प्रतिगृह्यसे ।। 7.9.7 ।।
explanation: O daughter, this is the time for giving (you in marriage); your youth is passing away. And you are not accepted by suitors, who are afraid of rejection.

shloka_text: त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः । त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके । कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम् ।। 7.9.8 ।।
explanation: For your sake, all of us, whose minds are fixed on righteousness, are constrained. Indeed, O daughter, you are endowed with all virtues, as if Lakshmi herself incarnate. Truly, fatherhood of a daughter is a sorrow for all who desire honor.

shloka_text: न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति कन्यके ।। 7.9.9 ।।
explanation: And it is not known, O maiden, who would marry the girl.

shloka_text: त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके । मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते । कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति ।। 7.9.10 ।।
explanation: You are indeed endowed with all virtues, like Lakshmi herself, O daughter. A maiden always keeps three families – her mother's family, her father's family, and the family to which she is given – in a state of uncertainty.

shloka_text: सा त्वं मुनिवरं श्रेष्ठं प्रजापतिकुलोद्भवम् । भज विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम् ।। 7.9.11 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O daughter, you yourself choose Vishravas, the best and most excellent of sages, born in the lineage of Prajapati, the descendant of Pulastya.

shloka_text: ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः । तेजसा भास्करसमो यादृशो ऽयं धनेश्वरः ।। 7.9.12 ।।
explanation: O daughter, your sons will undoubtedly be of such a kind. They will be equal to the sun in splendor, just like this Dhaneshvara.

shloka_text: सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्यका पितृगौरवात् । तत्रोपागम्य सा तस्थौ विश्रवा यत्र तप्यते ।। 7.9.13 ।।
explanation: But that maiden, having heard his words, out of reverence for her father, approached and stood there where Vishrava was performing penance.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम पुलस्त्यतनयो द्विजः । अग्निहोत्रमुपातिष्ठच्चतुर्थ इव पावकः ।। 7.9.14 ।।
explanation: O Rama, in the meantime, the son of Pulastya, a brahmin, performed the Agnihotra, like a fourth fire.

shloka_text: अविचिन्त्य तु तां वेलां दारुणां पितृगौरवात् । उपसृत्याग्रतस्तस्य चरणाधोमुखी स्थिता । विलिखन्ती मुहुर्भूमिमङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण भामिनी ।। 7.9.15 ।।
explanation: But, without considering that dreadful moment, out of respect for her father, the beautiful lady approached and stood before him, her face cast down towards his feet, repeatedly scratching the ground with the tip of her big toe.

shloka_text: स तु तां वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । अब्रवीत्परमोदारो दीप्यमानां स्वतेजसा ।। 7.9.16 ।।
explanation: But he, the exceedingly noble one, having seen her, with beautiful hips and a face like the full moon, shining with her own splendor, spoke.

shloka_text: भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता । किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने ।। 7.9.17 ।।
explanation: O good lady, whose daughter are you? Or from where have you come here? What is your purpose, or for what reason? Tell me truly, O beautiful one.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या कृताञ्जलिरथाब्रवीत् । आत्मप्रभावेण मुने ज्ञातुमर्हसि मे मतम् ।। 7.9.18 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, that maiden, with folded hands, then spoke: "O sage, by your own spiritual power, you ought to know my intention."

shloka_text: किं तु मां विद्धि ब्रह्मर्षे शासनात्पितुरागताम् । कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.9.19 ।।
explanation: But know me, O Brahmarshi, as one who has come by the command of my father. My name is Kaikasi. You ought to know the rest.

shloka_text: स तु गत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह । विज्ञातं ते मया भद्रे कारणं यन्मनोगतम् ।। 7.9.20 ।।
explanation: He, the sage, having gone into meditation, spoke these words: "O good lady, the reason that is in your mind has been understood by me."

shloka_text: सुताभिलाषो मत्तस्ते मत्तमातङ्गगामिनि । दारुणायां तु वेलायां यस्मात्त्वं मामुपस्थिता ।। 7.9.21 ।।
explanation: O you who walk like an intoxicated elephant, your desire for a son is from me, because you have approached me at this dreadful time.

shloka_text: शृणु तस्मात्सुतान्भद्रे यादृशाञ्जनयिष्यसि । दारुणान्दारुणाकारान्दारुणाभिजनप्रियान् ।। 7.9.22 ।।
explanation: Therefore, listen, O auspicious one, to the kind of sons you will bear: terrible, of fierce appearance, and fond of cruel people.

shloka_text: प्रसविष्यसि सुश्रोणि राक्षसान्क्रूरकर्मणः । सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रणिपत्याब्रवीद्वचः ।। 7.9.23 ।।
explanation: O beautiful-hipped one, you will give birth to Rākṣasas of cruel deeds. But she, having heard those words, prostrated and spoke.

shloka_text: भगवन्नीदृशान्पुत्रांस्त्वत्तो ऽहं ब्रह्मवादिनः । नेच्छामि सुदुराचारान्प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.9.24 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I do not desire such sons from you, who, though speakers of Brahman, are extremely ill-behaved. Please grant your favor.

shloka_text: कन्यया त्वेवमुक्तस्तु विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । उवाच कैकसीं भूयः पूर्णेन्दुरिव रोहिणीम् ।। 7.9.25 ।।
explanation: When thus addressed by the maiden, Vishrava, the foremost of sages, spoke again to Kaikasi, just as the full moon speaks to Rohini.

shloka_text: पश्चिमो यस्तव सुतो भविष्यति शुभानने । मम वंशानुरूपः स धर्मात्मा च भविष्यति ।। 7.9.26 ।।
explanation: O beautiful-faced one, your youngest son will be suitable to my lineage and will be righteous.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या राम कालेन केनचित् । जनयामास बीभत्सं रक्षोरूपं सुदारुणम् ।। 7.9.27 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, that maiden, O Rama, after some time, gave birth to a hideous, very terrible demon-form.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवं महादंष्ट्रं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् । ताम्रोष्ठं विंशतिभुजं महास्यं दीप्तमूर्धजम् ।। 7.9.28 ।।
explanation: Ten-headed, with great fangs, resembling a heap of dark collyrium, with copper-colored lips, twenty-armed, with a large mouth, and blazing hair.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्जाते तु तत्काले सज्वालकवलाः शिवाः । क्रव्यादाश्चापसव्यानि मण्डलानि प्रचक्रमुः ।। 7.9.29 ।।
explanation: Upon his birth, at that very time, jackals with flaming mouths and other flesh-eaters moved in inauspicious circles.

shloka_text: ववर्ष रुधिरं देवो मेघाश्च खरनिःस्वनाः । प्रबभौ न च सूर्यो वै महोल्काश्चापतन्भुवि ।। 7.9.30 ।।
explanation: The sky rained blood, and the clouds roared loudly. The sun did not shine, and great meteors fell on the earth.

shloka_text: चकम्पे जगती चैव ववुर्वाताः सुदारुणाः । अक्षोभ्यः क्षुभितश्चैव समुद्रः सरितां पतिः ।। 7.9.31 ।।
explanation: The earth trembled, and exceedingly fierce winds blew. The ocean, the lord of rivers, though normally unagitated, became agitated.

shloka_text: अथ नामाकरोत्तस्य पितामहसमः पिता । दशग्रीवः प्रसूतो ऽयं दशग्रीवो भविष्यति ।। 7.9.32 ।।
explanation: Then his father, who was like his grandfather, named him, saying, "This one born is Daśagrīva; he will be Daśagrīva."

shloka_text: तस्य त्वनन्तरं जातः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः । प्रमाणाद्यस्य विपुलं प्रमाणं नेह विद्यते ।। 7.9.33 ।।
explanation: And immediately after him was born Kumbhakarna, the greatly powerful, whose immense size has no equal measure in this world.

shloka_text: ततः शूर्पणखा नाम सञ्जज्ञे विकृतानना । विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा कैकस्याः पश्चिमः सुतः ।। 7.9.34 ।।
explanation: Then, Shurpanakha, of deformed face, was born. And Vibhishana, the righteous-souled, was the last son of Kaikasi.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्जाते महासत्त्वे पुष्पवर्षं पपात ह ।। 7.9.35 ।।
explanation: When that great being was born, a shower of flowers fell.

shloka_text: नभःस्थाने दुन्दुभयो देवानां प्राणदंस्तदा । वाक्यं चैवान्तरिक्षे च साधु साध्विति तत्तदा ।। 7.9.36 ।।
explanation: Then, in the sky, the drums of the gods sounded. And a voice in the atmosphere then said, "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: तौ तु तत्र महारण्ये ववृधाते महौजसौ । कुम्भकर्णदशग्रीवौ लोकोद्वेगकरौ तदा ।। 7.9.37 ।।
explanation: Indeed, those two, Kumbhakarna and Dashagriva, of great might, grew up there in the great forest, causing agitation to the world at that time.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णः प्रमत्तस्तु महर्षीन्धर्मवत्सलान् । त्रैलोक्यं भक्षयन्नित्यासन्तुष्टो विचचार ह ।। 7.9.38 ।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, reckless and perpetually discontented, wandered, devouring the great sages devoted to righteousness and the three worlds.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मे व्यवस्थितः । स्वाध्यायनियताहार उवास विजितेन्द्रियः ।। 7.9.39 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, the righteous-souled, ever established in dharma, lived with his senses subdued, disciplined in self-study and regulated in his diet.

shloka_text: अथ वैश्रवणो देवस्तत्र कालेन केनचित् । आगतः पितरं द्रष्टुं पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः ।। 7.9.40 ।।
explanation: Then, the god Vaiśravaṇa, the lord of wealth, arrived there after some time, by means of the Puṣpaka (chariot), to see his father.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा कैकसी तत्र ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । आगम्य राक्षसी तत्र दशग्रीवमुवाच ह ।। 7.9.41 ।।
explanation: Seeing him there, shining as if with splendor, Kaikasi, the Rakshasi, came there and spoke to Dashagriva.

shloka_text: पुत्र वैश्रवणं पश्य भ्रातरं तेजसा वृतम् । भ्रातृभावे समे चापि पश्यात्मानं त्वमीदृशम् ।। 7.9.42 ।।
explanation: Son, behold Vaiśravaṇa, your brother, enveloped in splendor. And though the brotherly bond is equal, behold yourself in such a state.

shloka_text: दशग्रीव तथा यत्नं कुरुष्वामितविक्रम । यथा त्वमसि मे पुत्र भव र्वैश्रवणोपमः ।। 7.9.43 ।।
explanation: O Daśagrīva, O one of immeasurable valor, make such an effort that you, my son, become like Vaiśravaṇa.

shloka_text: मातुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् । अमर्षमतुलं लेभे प्रतिज्ञां चाकरोत्तदा ।। 7.9.44 ।।
explanation: Having heard that word of his mother, the mighty Dashagriva felt unequalled indignation and then made a vow.

shloka_text: सत्यं ते प्रतिजानामि भ्रातृतुल्यो ऽधिको ऽपि वा । भविष्याम्योजसा चैव सन्तापं त्यज हृद्गतम् ।। 7.9.45 ।।
explanation: I truly promise you, I shall be equal to a brother, or even superior, by my might. And indeed, abandon the sorrow residing in your heart.

shloka_text: ततस्तेनैव कोपेन दशग्रीवः सहानुजः । चिकीर्षुर्दुष्करं कर्म तपसे धृतमानसः ।। 7.9.46 ।।
explanation: Then, with that very anger, Daśagrīva, accompanied by his brother, with his mind set on penance, desired to perform a difficult deed.

shloka_text: प्राप्स्यामि तपसा काममिति कृत्वा ऽध्यवस्य च । आगच्छदात्मसिद्ध्यर्थं गोकर्णस्याश्रमं शुभम् ।। 7.9.47 ।।
explanation: Having resolved, "I will achieve my desire through penance," he came to the auspicious hermitage of Gokarna for the fulfillment of his own purpose.

shloka_text: स राक्षसस्तत्र सहानुजस्तदा तपश्चकारातुलमुग्रविक्रमः । अतोषयच्चापि पितामहं विभुं ददौ स तुष्टश्च वराञ्जयावहान् ।। 7.9.48 ।।
explanation: That demon, of fierce prowess, then performed immense penance there along with his younger brother. He also pleased the powerful grandfather (Brahma). And Brahma, being pleased, bestowed boons that bring victory.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः ।। 9 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered Rāmāyaṇa, the glorious original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the ninth chapter.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीन्मुनिं रामः कथं ते भ्रातरो वने । कीदृशं तु तदा ब्रह्मंस्तपस्तेपुर्महाबलाः ।। 7.10.1 ।।
explanation: Then Rama said to the sage, "How were your brothers in the forest? What kind of penance did those mighty ones perform then, O Brahmana?"

shloka_text: अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र रामं सुप्रीतमानसम् । तांस्तान्धर्मविधींस्तत्र भ्रातरस्ते समाविशन् ।। 7.10.2 ।।
explanation: Agastya then spoke there to Rama, whose mind was greatly pleased. Your brothers there engaged in those various religious duties.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्ततो यत्तो नित्यं धर्मपथे स्थितः । तताप ग्रीष्मकाले तु पञ्चाग्नीन्परितः स्थितः ।। 7.10.3 ।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, then, ever diligent and established on the path of righteousness, performed severe austerities in the summer season, standing surrounded by five fires.

shloka_text: मेघाम्बुसिक्तो वर्षासु वीरासनमसेवत । नित्यं च शिशिरे काले जलमध्यप्रतिश्रयः ।। 7.10.4 ।।
explanation: During the rainy season, drenched by cloud-water, he practiced the Vīrāsana posture. And always during the cold season, he took refuge in the midst of water.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तस्यातिचक्रमुः । धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य सत्पथे निष्ठितस्य च ।। 7.10.5 ।।
explanation: Thus, ten thousand years passed for him, who was striving in righteousness and steadfast in the good path.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा नित्यं धर्मपरः शुचिः । पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि पादेनैकेन तस्थिवान् ।। 7.10.6 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, the righteous-souled, always devoted to dharma and pure, stood on one foot for five thousand years.

shloka_text: समाप्ते नियमे तस्य ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः । पपात पुष्पवर्षं च क्षुभिताश्चापि देवताः ।। 7.10.7 ।।
explanation: Upon the completion of his vow, groups of Apsaras danced. And a shower of flowers fell, and the gods were also moved.

shloka_text: पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यं चैवान्ववर्तत । तस्थौ चोर्ध्वशिरोबाहुः स्वाध्यायधृतमानसः ।। 7.10.8 ।।
explanation: For five thousand years, he followed the Sun. He stood with his head and arms raised upwards, his mind fixed on spiritual study.

shloka_text: एवं विभीषणस्यापि स्वर्गस्थस्येव नन्दने । दशवर्षसहस्राणि गतानि नियतात्मनः ।। 7.10.9 ।।
explanation: Thus, for the self-controlled Vibhishana, ten thousand years passed as if he were in the Nandana garden of heaven.

shloka_text: दशवर्षसहस्रं तु निराहारो दशाननः । पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शिरश्चाग्नौ जुहाव सः ।। 7.10.10 ।।
explanation: Ravana fasted for ten thousand years. At the completion of a thousand years, he offered his head into the fire.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि नव तस्यातिचक्रमुः । शिरांसि नव चाप्यस्य प्रविष्टानि हुताशनम् ।। 7.10.11 ।।
explanation: Thus, nine thousand years passed for him, and his nine heads also entered the fire.

shloka_text: अथ वर्षसहस्रे तु दशमे दशमं शिरः । छेत्तुकामे दशग्रीवे प्राप्तस्तत्र पितामहः ।। 7.10.12 ।।
explanation: Then, in the tenth thousandth year, when Daśagrīva was desirous of cutting his tenth head, Pitāmaha arrived there.

shloka_text: पितामहस्तु सुप्रीतः सार्धं देवैरुपस्थितः । तव तावद्दशग्रीव प्रीतो ऽस्मीत्यभ्यभाषत ।। 7.10.13 ।।
explanation: The Grandfather (Brahma), greatly pleased, appeared along with the gods. He addressed (him), saying, "O Daśagrīva, I am indeed pleased with you."

shloka_text: शीघ्रं वरय धर्मज्ञ वरो यस्ते ऽभिकाङ्क्षितः । कं ते कामं करोम्यद्य न वृथा ते परिश्रमः ।। 7.10.14 ।।
explanation: O knower of Dharma, quickly choose the boon that you desire. What wish shall I fulfill for you today? Your effort is not in vain.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीदृशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा ।। 7.10.15 ।।
explanation: Then Daśagrīva, with a greatly delighted inner self, having bowed his head to the deity, spoke with a voice choked with joy.

shloka_text: भगवन्प्राणिनां नित्यं नान्यत्र मरणाद्भयम् । नास्ति मृत्युसमः शत्रुरमरत्वमहं वृणे ।। 7.10.16 ।।
explanation: O Lord, for living beings, there is always fear only from death. There is no enemy like death. I desire immortality.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा दशग्रीवमुवाच ह । नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं ते वरमन्यं वृणीष्व मे ।। 7.10.17 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Brahma then spoke to Daśagrīva: "Complete immortality is not for you. Ask for another boon from me."

shloka_text: एवमुक्ते तदा राम ब्रह्मणा लोककर्तृणा । दशग्रीव उवाचेदं कृताञ्जलिरथाग्रतः ।। 7.10.18 ।।
explanation: When Brahma, the creator of the worlds, had thus spoken, then Dashagriva, with folded hands, spoke this before him.

shloka_text: सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम् । अवध्यो ऽहं प्रजाध्यक्ष देवतानां च शाश्वत ।। 7.10.19 ।।
explanation: O Lord of creatures, O Eternal one, I am invulnerable to Suparnas, Nagas, Yakshas, Daityas, Danavas, Rakshasas, and gods.

shloka_text: नहि चिन्ता ममान्येषु प्राणिष्वमरपूजित । तृणभूता हि ते मन्ये प्राणिनो मानुषादयः ।। 7.10.20 ।।
explanation: I have no concern for other creatures, O worshipped by immortals. Indeed, I consider those creatures, humans and others, to be like grass.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा । उवाच वचनं देवः सह देवैः पितामहः ।। 7.10.21 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the Rākṣasa Daśagrīva, the righteous god, the Grandfather (Brahmā), then spoke words along with the gods.

shloka_text: भविष्यत्येवमेतत्ते वचो राक्षसपुङ्गव । एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं पितामहः ।। 7.10.22 ।।
explanation: This word of yours, O best among Rākṣasas, will indeed be so. Having thus spoken to that Rāma, Daśagrīva, the Grandfather (Brahma)...

shloka_text: शृणु चापि वरो भूयः प्रीतस्येह शुभो मम । हुतानि यानि शीर्षाणि पूर्वमग्नौ त्वयानघ ।। 7.10.23 ।।
explanation: Listen, O sinless one, to another auspicious boon from me, who is pleased here. Those heads which were formerly offered by you in the fire.

shloka_text: पुनस्तानि भविष्यन्ति तथैव तव राक्षस । वितरामीह ते सौम्य वरं चान्यं दुरासदम् ।। 7.10.24 ।।
explanation: Again those will be yours in the same way, O demon. And I grant you here, O gentle one, another formidable boon.

shloka_text: छन्दतस्तव रूपं च मनसा यद्यथेप्सितम् । भविष्यति न सन्देहो मद्वरात्तवराक्षस ।। 7.10.25 ।।
explanation: Whatever form you desire in your mind, that will be yours according to your will. There is no doubt, O Rakshasa, by my boon.

shloka_text: एवं पितामहोक्तस्य दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः । अग्नौ हुतानि शीर्षाणि पुनस्तान्युत्थितानि वै ।। 7.10.26 ।।
explanation: Thus, the heads of the demon Daśagrīva, offered into the fire as spoken by the grandfather, indeed rose again.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तं राम दशग्रीवं पितामहः । विभीषणमथोवाच वाक्यं लोकपितामहः ।। 7.10.27 ।।
explanation: O Rama, the Grandfather, having thus spoken to Dashagriva, the Grandfather of the worlds then spoke a word to Vibhishana.

shloka_text: विभीषण त्वया वत्स धर्मसंहितबुद्धिना । परितुष्टो ऽस्मि धर्मात्मन्वरं वरय सुव्रत ।। 7.10.28 ।।
explanation: O Vibhishana, dear child, whose intellect is imbued with righteousness, O righteous soul, I am greatly pleased. O virtuous one, ask for a boon.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तु धर्मात्मा वचनं प्राह साञ्जलिः । वृतः सर्वगुणैर्नित्यं चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिर्यथा ।। 7.10.29 ।।
explanation: The righteous-souled Vibhishana, with folded hands, spoke words, always endowed with all virtues, just as the moon (is endowed) with its rays.

shloka_text: भगवन्कृतकृत्यो ऽहं यन्मे लोकगुरुः स्वयम् । प्रीतेन यदि दातव्यो वरो मे शृणु सुव्रत ।। 7.10.30 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I am fulfilled, for the preceptor of the world himself (is present for me). If, being pleased, a boon is to be granted to me, O virtuous one, listen.

shloka_text: परमापद्गतस्यापि धर्मे मम मतिर्भवेत् । अशिक्षितं च ब्रह्मास्त्रं भगवन्प्रतिभातु मे ।। 7.10.31 ।।
explanation: May my mind be fixed on righteousness, even when I am in the greatest calamity. And, O Lord, may the untaught Brahmastra manifest to me.

shloka_text: या या मे जायते बुद्धिर्येषु येष्वाश्रमेषु च । सा सा भवतु धर्मिष्ठा तं तु धर्मं च पालये ।। 7.10.32 ।।
explanation: Whatever thought arises in me, in whichever stage of life, may that be most righteous, and may I uphold that very dharma.

shloka_text: एष मे परमोदार वरः परमको मतः । नहि धर्माभिरक्तानां लोके किञ्चन दुर्लभम् ।। 7.10.33 ।।
explanation: This is considered by me as the most generous and supreme boon. Indeed, for those devoted to righteousness, nothing is unattainable in this world.

shloka_text: पुनः प्रजापतिः प्रीतो विभीषणमुवाच ह । धर्मिष्ठस्त्वं यथा वत्स तथा चैतद्भविष्यति ।। 7.10.34 ।।
explanation: Again, Prajapati, pleased, said to Vibhishana: "O dear child, just as you are most righteous, so shall this be."

shloka_text: यस्माद्राक्षसयोनौ ते जातस्यामित्रनाशन । नाधर्मे जायते बुद्धिरमरत्वं ददामि ते ।। 7.10.35 ।।
explanation: Because, O destroyer of enemies, though born in the lineage of a Rākṣasa, your mind does not incline towards unrighteousness, I grant you immortality.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा कुम्भकर्णाय वरं दातुमुपस्थितम् । प्रजापतिं सुराः सर्वे वाक्यं प्राञ्जलयो ऽब्रुवन् ।। 7.10.36 ।।
explanation: Having said this, all the gods, with folded hands, spoke to Prajapati, who was present to grant a boon to Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: न तावत्कुम्भकर्णाय प्रदातव्यो वरस्त्वया । जानीषे हि यथा लोकांस्त्रासयत्येष दुर्मतिः ।। 7.10.37 ।।
explanation: Therefore, a boon should not be granted by you to Kumbhakarna. For you know how this wicked one terrorizes the people.

shloka_text: नन्दने ऽप्सरसः सप्त महेन्द्रानुचरा दश । अनेन भक्षिता ब्रह्मन्नृषयो मानुषास्तथा ।। 7.10.38 ।।
explanation: O Brahman, by him, seven Apsaras, ten attendants of Mahendra, and also sages and humans were devoured in Nandana.

shloka_text: अलब्धवरपूर्वेण यत्कृतं राक्षसेन तु । तदेष वरलब्धः स्याद्भक्षयेद्भुवनत्रयम् ।। 7.10.39 ।।
explanation: Whatever was done by the demon who had not previously obtained a boon, this one, having obtained a boon, would surely devour the three worlds.

shloka_text: वरव्याजेन मोहो ऽस्मै दीयताममितप्रभ । लोकानां स्वस्ति चैवं स्याद्भवेदस्य च सन्नतिः ।। 7.10.40 ।।
explanation: O immeasurable splendor, let delusion be given to him under the guise of a boon. And thus there would be welfare for the worlds, and for him there would be humility.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्मा ऽचिन्तयत् पद्मसम्भवः । चिन्तिता चोपतस्थे ऽस्य पार्श्वं देवी सरस्वती ।। 7.10.41 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the gods, Brahma, the lotus-born, pondered. And as he pondered, the goddess Saraswati, having been thought of, appeared by his side.

shloka_text: प्राञ्जलिः सा तु पार्श्वस्था प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वती । इयमस्म्यागता देव किं कार्यं करवाण्यहम् ।। 7.10.42 ।।
explanation: Sarasvati, standing nearby with folded hands, then spoke these words: "O Deva, I have arrived. What work shall I do?"

shloka_text: प्रजापतिस्तुं तां प्राप्तां प्राह वाक्यं सरस्वतीम् । वाणि त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भव या देवतेप्सिता ।। 7.10.43 ।।
explanation: Prajapati, having approached her, spoke these words to Saraswati: "O Vani, you shall become the desired deity of the king of Rakshasas."

shloka_text: तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत् । कुम्भकर्ण महाबाहो वरं वरय यो मतः ।। 7.10.44 ।।
explanation: Having said 'So be it,' she entered. Then Prajapati spoke: 'O Kumbhakarna, O mighty-armed one, choose the boon that you desire.'

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वचनमब्रवीत् । स्वप्तुं वर्षाण्यनेकानि देवदेव ममेप्सितम् ।। 7.10.45 ।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, having heard those words, said: "O God of gods, I desire to sleep for many years."

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रायाद्ब्रह्मा सुरैः समम् । देवी सरस्वती चैव राक्षसं तं जहौ पुनः ।। 7.10.46 ।।
explanation: Having said to him, "So be it," Brahma departed along with the gods. And indeed, the goddess Saraswati again abandoned that demon.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मणा सह देवेषु गतेषु च नभःस्थलम् । विमुक्तो ऽसौ सरस्वत्या स्वां सञ्ज्ञां च ततो गतः ।। 7.10.47 ।।
explanation: When Brahma and the gods had gone to the sky, he was released by Sarasvati and then regained his own consciousness.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुष्टात्मा चिन्तयामास दुःखितः । ईदृशं किमिदं वाक्यं ममाद्य वदनाच्च्युतम् ।। 7.10.48 ।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, the wicked-minded, distressed, pondered: "What kind of words are these that have escaped my mouth today?"

shloka_text: अहं व्यामोहितो देवैरिति मन्ये तदा ऽ ऽगतैः । एवं लब्धवराः सर्वे भ्रातरो दीप्ततेजसः । श्लेष्मातकवनं गत्वा तत्र ते न्यवसन्सुखम् ।। 7.10.49 ।।
explanation: I believe that I was then deluded by the gods who had arrived. Thus, all the brothers, having obtained boons and possessing blazing splendor, went to the Shleshmātaka forest and resided there happily.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः ।। 10 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, composed by the sage, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the tenth chapter.

shloka_text: सुमाली वरलब्धांस्तु ज्ञात्वा चैतान्निशाचरान् । उदतिष्ठद्भयं त्यक्त्वा सानुगः स रसातलात् ।। 7.11.1 ।।
explanation: Sumali, having known that these night-wanderers had obtained boons, abandoned fear and rose up from Rasatala with his followers.

shloka_text: मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च विरूपाक्षो महोदरः । उदतिष्ठन्सुसंरब्धाः सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.11.2 ।।
explanation: Maricha, Prahasta, Virupaksha, and Mahodara, the greatly enraged ministers of that Rakshasa, stood up.

shloka_text: सुमाली सचिवैः सार्धं वृतो राक्षसपुङ्गवैः । अभिगम्य दशग्रीवं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.11.3 ।।
explanation: Sumali, accompanied by his ministers and surrounded by chief Rākṣasas, approached Dashagriva, embraced him, and spoke thus.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या ते वत्स सम्प्राप्तश्चिन्तितो ऽयं मनोरथः । यस्त्वं त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठाल्लब्धवान्वरमुत्तमम् ।। 7.11.4 ।।
explanation: Fortunately for you, O child, this desired wish has been fulfilled, as you have obtained an excellent boon from the best of the three worlds.

shloka_text: यत्कृते च वयं लङ्कां त्यकत्वा याता रसातलम् । तद्गतं नो महाबाहो महद्विष्णुकृतं भयम् ।। 7.11.5 ।।
explanation: And for whose sake we abandoned Lanka and went to Rasatala, that great fear caused by Vishnu has now departed from us, O mighty-armed one.

shloka_text: असकृत्तद्भयाद्भीताः परित्यज्य स्वमालयम् । विद्रुताः सहिताः सर्वे प्रविष्टाः स्म रसातलम् ।। 7.11.6 ।।
explanation: Frightened by that fear repeatedly, all of them together abandoned their own abode, fled, and entered Rasatala.

shloka_text: अस्मदीया च लङ्केयं नगरी राक्षसोचिता । निवेशिता तव भ्रात्रा धनाध्यक्षेण धीमता ।। 7.11.7 ।।
explanation: And this city of Lanka, which is ours and suitable for Rakshasas, was established by your intelligent brother, the lord of wealth.

shloka_text: यदि नामात्र शक्यं स्यात्साम्ना दानेन वानघ । तरसा वा महाबाहो प्रत्यानेतुं कृतं भवेत् ।। 7.11.8 ।।
explanation: O sinless one, O mighty-armed one, if it were not possible here to bring back by conciliation, or by gifts, or by force, then it would have been accomplished.

shloka_text: त्वं तु लङ्केश्वरस्तात भविष्यसि न संशयः । त्वया राक्षसवंशो ऽयं निमग्नो ऽपि समुद्धृतः । सर्वेषां नः प्रभुश्चैव भविष्यसि महाबल ।। 7.11.9 ।।
explanation: You, my dear, will certainly be the Lord of Lanka, there is no doubt. By you, this Rākṣasa lineage, even though fallen, has been uplifted. And you will indeed be the lord of all of us, O mighty one.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवो मातामहमुपस्थितम् । वित्तेशो गुरुरस्माकं नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम् ।। 7.11.10 ।।
explanation: Then Dashagriva spoke to his maternal grandfather who was present: "Kubera is our preceptor; you should not speak such words."

shloka_text: साम्नापि राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रत्याख्यातो गरीयसा । किञ्चिन्नाह तदा रक्षो ज्ञात्वा तस्य चकीर्षितम् ।। 7.11.11 ।।
explanation: Even though he offered conciliation, he was rejected by the mighty lord of Rakshasas. Then, knowing his intention, the Rakshasa said nothing.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य वसन्तं रावणं ततः । उक्तवन्तं तथा वाक्यं दशग्रीवं निशाचरः ।। 7.11.12 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, a night-wanderer spoke a statement to Ravana, Dashagriva, who was residing there and had spoken thus.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तः प्रश्रितं वाक्यमिदमाह स कारणम् ।। 7.11.13 ।।
explanation: Prahasta spoke this humble statement with reason.

shloka_text: दशग्रीव महाबाहो नार्हस्त्वं वक्तुमीदृशम् । सौभ्रात्रं नास्ति शूराणां शृणु चेदं वचो मम ।। 7.11.14 ।।
explanation: O Daśagrīva, O mighty-armed one, you ought not to speak such things. There is no brotherhood among heroes. And listen to this word of mine.

shloka_text: अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव भगिन्यौ सहिते हि ते । भार्ये परमरूपिण्यौ कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः ।। 7.11.15 ।।
explanation: Aditi and Diti were indeed sisters, and they were the exceedingly beautiful wives of Prajapati Kashyapa.

shloka_text: अदितिर्जनयामास देवांस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरान् । दितिस्त्वजनयत्पुत्रान्कश्यपस्यात्मसम्भवान् ।। 7.11.16 ।।
explanation: Aditi gave birth to the gods, the lords of the three worlds. Diti, however, gave birth to sons, born of Kashyapa.

shloka_text: दैत्यानां किल धर्मज्ञ पुरीयं सवनार्णवा । सपर्वता मही वीर ते ऽभवन्प्रभविष्णवः ।। 7.11.17 ।।
explanation: O knower of Dharma, O hero, this city, along with the earth, its forests, oceans, and mountains, indeed belonged to the Daityas. They became powerful.

shloka_text: निहत्य तांस्तु समरे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । देवानां वशमानीतं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम् ।। 7.11.18 ।।
explanation: Having killed them in battle, the mighty Vishnu brought this imperishable three worlds under the control of the gods.

shloka_text: नैतदेको भवानेव करिष्यति विपर्ययम् । सुरासुरैराचरितं तत्कुरुष्व वचो मम ।। 7.11.19 ।।
explanation: You alone will not cause this misfortune. What has been done by gods and asuras, that you should do; follow my command.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना । चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं वै बाढमित्येव सो ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.11.20 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Dashagriva, with his inner self greatly delighted, having pondered for a moment, he indeed said, "Certainly!"

shloka_text: स तु तेनैव हर्षेण तस्मिन्नहनि वीर्यवान् । वनं गतो दशग्रीवः सह तैः क्षणदाचरैः ।। 7.11.21 ।।
explanation: But that powerful Daśagrīva, filled with that very joy, went to the forest on that day along with those night-wanderers.

shloka_text: त्रिकूटस्थः स तु तदा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । प्रेषयामास दौत्येन प्रहस्तं वाक्यकोविदम् ।। 7.11.22 ।।
explanation: Then, Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, residing on Trikuta, sent Prahasta, who was skilled in speech, as an envoy.

shloka_text: प्रहस्त शीघ्रं गच्छ त्वं ब्रूहि नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवम् । वचसा मम वित्तेशं सामपूर्वमिदं वचः ।। 7.11.23 ।।
explanation: O Prahasta, you go quickly. Tell the chief of the Rākṣasas, the lord of wealth, these conciliatory words of mine.

shloka_text: इयं लङ्का पुरी राजन्राक्षसानां महात्मनाम् । त्वया निवेशिता सौम्य नैतद्युक्तं तवानघ ।। 7.11.24 ।।
explanation: O King, this city of Lanka, established by you for the mighty Rākṣasas, O gentle one, this is not proper for you, O sinless one.

shloka_text: तद्भवान्यदि नो ह्यद्य दद्यादतुलविक्रम । कृता भवेन्मम प्रीतिर्धुर्मश्चैवानुपालितः ।। 7.11.25 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O unequalled in valor, if you would grant it to us today, my satisfaction would be accomplished, and duty would certainly be fulfilled.

shloka_text: स तु गत्वा पुरीं लङ्कां धनदेन सुरक्षिताम् । अब्रवीत्परमोदारं वित्तपालमिदं वचः ।। 7.11.26 ।।
explanation: But he, having gone to the city of Lanka, well-protected by Kubera, spoke these words to the most noble treasurer.

shloka_text: प्रेषितो ऽहं तव भ्रात्रा दशग्रीवेण सुव्रत । त्वत्समीपं महाबाहो सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वर ।। 7.11.27 ।।
explanation: I was sent by your brother Dashagriva, O virtuous one, to your presence, O mighty-armed one, O best among all wielders of weapons.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रूयतां महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद । वचनं मम वित्तेश यद्ब्रवीति दशाननः ।। 7.11.28 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O greatly wise one, O expert in all scriptures, O lord of wealth, listen to my words, what Daśānana speaks.

shloka_text: इयं किल पुरी रम्या सुमालिप्रमुखैः पुरा । भुक्तपूर्वा विशालाक्ष राक्षसैर्भीमविक्रमैः ।। 7.11.29 ।।
explanation: Indeed, this beautiful city, O wide-eyed one, was formerly enjoyed by the Rākṣasas of terrible valor, led by Sumali and others.

shloka_text: तेन विज्ञाप्यते सो ऽयं साम्प्रतं विश्रवात्मज । तदेषा दीयतां तात याचतस्तस्य सामतः ।। 7.11.30 ।।
explanation: O son of Vishrava, he is now being informed by him. Therefore, O dear one, let this (Sita) be given to him who is requesting her by peaceful means.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तादभिसंश्रुत्य देवो वैश्रवणो वचः । प्रत्युवाच प्रहस्तं तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः ।। 7.11.31 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words from Prahasta, the god Vaishravana, an expert in speech, replied to Prahasta with these words.

shloka_text: दत्ता ममेयं पित्रा तु लङ्का शून्या निशाचरैः । निवासिते च मे यक्षैर्दानमानादिभिर्गुणैः ।। 7.11.32 ।।
explanation: This Lanka, devoid of night-wanderers, was given to me by my father, and it was settled by me with Yakṣas through qualities such as giving gifts and showing respect.

shloka_text: ब्रूहि गच्छ दशग्रीवं पुरं राज्यं च यन्मम । तवाप्येतन्महाबाहो भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमकण्टकम् ।। 7.11.33 ।।
explanation: Tell Daśagrīva: "Go! My city and kingdom, these are also yours, O mighty-armed one. Enjoy a kingdom free from obstacles."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा धनाध्यक्षो जगाम पितुरन्तिकम् ।। 7.11.34 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken, the lord of wealth went to his father.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य गुरुं प्राह रावणस्य यदीप्सितम् । एष तात दशग्रीवो दूतं प्रेषितवान्मम ।। 7.11.35 ।।
explanation: Having saluted his preceptor, he spoke what Ravana desired: "O father, this Dashagriva has sent a messenger to me."

shloka_text: दीयतां नगरी लङ्का पूर्वं रक्षोगणोषिता । मयात्र यदनुष्ठेयं तन्ममाचक्ष्व सुव्रत ।। 7.11.36 ।।
explanation: Let the city of Lanka, formerly inhabited by hosts of Rākṣasas, be given. O virtuous one, tell me what is to be done by me here.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मर्षिस्त्वेवमुक्तो ऽसौ विश्रवा मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्राञ्जलिं धनदं प्राह शृणु पुत्र वचो मम ।। 7.11.37 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, that Brahmarshi Vishrava, the foremost among sages, said to Dhanada, who stood with folded hands, "Listen, O son, to my words."

shloka_text: दशग्रीवो महाबाहुरुक्तवान्मम सन्निधौ । मया निर्भर्त्सितश्चासीद्बहुशोक्तः सुदुर्मतिः ।। 7.11.38 ।।
explanation: The mighty-armed Daśagrīva spoke in my presence. That evil-minded one was rebuked by me and spoken to repeatedly.

shloka_text: स क्रोधेन मया चोक्तो ध्वंसते च पुनः पुनः । श्रेयो ऽभियुक्तं धर्म्यं च शृणु पुत्र वचो मम ।। 7.11.39 ।।
explanation: He, addressed by me in anger, is repeatedly destroyed. Listen, son, to my words, which are beneficial, proper, and righteous.

shloka_text: वरप्रदानसम्मूढो मान्या ऽमान्यान् स दुर्मतिः । न वेत्ति मम शापाच्च प्रकृतिं दारुणां गतः ।। 7.11.40 ।।
explanation: That evil-minded one, deluded by the granting of boons, does not distinguish between the respectable and the unrespectable, and due to my curse, he has attained a terrible nature.

shloka_text: तस्माद्गच्छ महाबाहो कैलासं धरणीधरम् । निवेशय निवासार्थं त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां सहानुगः ।। 7.11.41 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, go to Kailasa, the mountain, and establish your residence there, abandoning Lanka along with your followers.

shloka_text: तत्र मन्दाकिनी रम्या नदीनामुत्तमा नदी । काञ्चनैः सूर्यसङ्काशैः पङ्कजैः संवृतोदका ।। 7.11.42 ।।
explanation: There, the beautiful Mandakini, the best of rivers, has its waters covered with golden lotuses shining like the sun.

shloka_text: कुमुदैरुत्पलैश्चैव तथा ऽन्यैश्च सुगन्धिभिः ।। 7.11.43 ।।
explanation: With water lilies, lotuses, and other fragrant ones.

shloka_text: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः साप्सरोरगकिंनराः । विहारशीलाः सततं रमन्ते सर्वदा ऽ ऽश्रिताः ।। 7.11.44 ।।
explanation: There, the gods, along with Gandharvas, Apsaras, Uragas, and Kinnaras, who are fond of recreation, constantly and always delight themselves, residing there.

shloka_text: न हि क्षमं तवानेन वैरं धनद रक्षसा । जानीषे हि यथा ऽनेन लब्धः परमको वरः ।। 7.11.45 ।।
explanation: Indeed, it is not proper for you, O Kubera, to have enmity with this demon. For you surely know how a supreme boon was obtained by him.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो गृहीत्वा ऽ ऽशु तद्वचः पितृगौरवात् । सदारपुत्रः सामान्यः सवाहनधनो गतः ।। 7.11.46 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, having quickly accepted that word out of respect for his father, he departed with his wife, son, vehicles, and wealth.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तो ऽथ दशग्रीवं गत्वा वचनमब्रवीत् । प्रहृष्टात्मा महात्मानं सहामात्यं सहानुजम् ।। 7.11.47 ।।
explanation: Then Prahasta, with a joyful heart, went to the great-souled Daśagrīva, who was accompanied by his ministers and younger brother, and spoke words.

shloka_text: शून्या सा नगरी लङ्का त्यक्त्त्वैनां धनदो गतः । प्रविश्य तां सहास्माभिः स्वधर्मं प्रतिपालय ।। 7.11.48 ।।
explanation: That city Lanka is empty; Kubera has abandoned it and departed. Enter it with us and uphold your own dharma.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रहस्तेन महाबलः । विवेश नगरीं लङ्कां भ्रातृभिः सबलानुगैः ।। 7.11.49 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Prahasta, the mighty Dashagriva entered the city of Lanka with his brothers and his army and followers.

shloka_text: धनदेन परित्यक्तां सुविभक्तमहापथाम् । आरुरोह स देवारिः स्वर्गं देवाधिपो यथा ।। 7.11.50 ।।
explanation: He, the enemy of the gods, ascended to heaven, which was abandoned by Kubera and had well-divided great paths, just like the lord of the gods.

shloka_text: स चाभिषिक्तः क्षणदाचरैस्तदा निवेशयामास पुरीं दशाननः । निकामपूर्णा च बभूव सा पुरी निशाचरैर्नीलबलाहकोपमैः ।। 7.11.51 ।।
explanation: And Dashanana, having been consecrated by the night-wanderers, then established the city. And that city became completely filled with night-wanderers resembling dark clouds.

shloka_text: धनेश्वरस्त्वथ पितृवाक्यगौरवान्न्यवेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम् । स्वलङ्कृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां पुरन्दरस्वेव तदा ऽमरावतीम् ।। 7.11.52 ।।
explanation: Then, Dhaneshvara, out of reverence for his father's command, established a city on the pure, moon-bright mountain. It was adorned with splendid mansions, just like Purandara's Amaravati at that time.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः ।। 11 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred epic, the glorious Ramayana, the original poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the eleventh chapter.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽभिषिक्तस्तु भ्रातृभ्यां सहितस्तदा । ततः प्रदानं राक्षस्या भगिन्याः समचिन्तयत् ।। 7.12.1 ।।
explanation: Then, the king of the Rākṣasas, having been consecrated and accompanied by his two brothers, considered the marriage of his Rākṣasī sister.

shloka_text: स्वसारं कालकेयाय दानवेन्द्राय राक्षसीम् । ददौ शूर्पणखां नाम विद्युज्जिह्वाय नामतः ।। 7.12.2 ।।
explanation: He gave his sister, the demoness named Shurpanakha, to Vidyujjihva, a Kālakeya and lord of Danavas.

shloka_text: अथ दत्त्वा स्वयं रक्षो मृगयामटते स्म तत् । तत्रापश्यत्ततो राम मयं नाम दितेः सुतम् ।। 7.12.3 ।।
explanation: Then, having engaged himself, the demon roamed for hunting. Thereupon, O Rama, he saw Maya, the son of Diti.

shloka_text: कन्यासहायं तं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । अपृच्छत्को भवानेको निर्मनुष्यमृगे वने । अनया मृगशावाक्ष्या किमर्थं सह तिष्ठसि ।। 7.12.4 ।।
explanation: Seeing him with a maiden as companion, Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, asked, "Who are you, alone in this forest devoid of humans and animals? Why do you stay with this fawn-eyed one?"

shloka_text: मयस्तथाब्रवीद्राम पृच्छन्तं तं निशाचरम् । श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये यथावृत्तमिदं मम ।। 7.12.5 ।।
explanation: O Rama, Maya then spoke to that night-wanderer who was questioning: "Listen, I will narrate everything that has happened to me."

shloka_text: हेमा नामाप्सरास्तात श्रुतपूर्वा यदि त्वया । दैवतैर्मम सा दत्ता पौलोमीव शतक्रतोः ।। 7.12.6 ।।
explanation: O dear one, if you have heard of the Apsara named Hema, she was given to me by the gods, just as Paulomi was given to Indra.

shloka_text: तस्यां सक्तमनास्तात पञ्चवर्षशतान्यहम् । सा च दैवतकार्येण त्रयोदश समा गताः ।। 7.12.7 ।।
explanation: Dear son, my mind was attached to her for five hundred years. And she, for a divine purpose, was gone for thirteen years.

shloka_text: वर्षं चतुर्दशं चैव ततो हेममयं पुरम् । वज्रवैडूर्यचित्रं च मायया निर्मितं मया ।। 7.12.8 ।।
explanation: And then, in the fourteenth year, a golden city, adorned with diamonds and lapis lazuli, was created by me through illusion.

shloka_text: तत्राहमवसं दीनस्तया हीनः सुदुःखितः ।। 7.12.9 ।।
explanation: There I lived, miserable, bereft of her, greatly distressed.

shloka_text: तस्मात्पुराद्दुहितरं गृहीत्वा वनमागतः । इयं ममात्मजा राजंस्तस्याः कुक्षौ विवर्धिता ।। 7.12.10 ।।
explanation: Having taken my daughter from that city, I came to the forest. This is my daughter, O King, who grew in her womb.

shloka_text: भर्तारमनया सार्धमस्याः प्राप्तो ऽस्मि मार्गितुम् । कन्यापितृत्वं दुःखं हि सर्वेषां मानकाङ्क्षिणाम् ।। 7.12.11 ।।
explanation: I have come with her to seek a husband for her. Indeed, fatherhood of a daughter is a sorrow for all who desire honor.

shloka_text: कन्या हि द्वे कुले नित्यं संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति । पुत्रद्वयं ममाप्यस्यां भार्यायां सम्बभूव ह ।। 7.12.12 ।।
explanation: A daughter indeed always keeps two families in doubt. And indeed, two sons were born to me from this wife.

shloka_text: मायावी प्रथमस्तात दुन्दुभिस्तदनन्तरः । एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः ।। 7.12.13 ।।
explanation: The illusionist was the first, O dear one, and Dundubhi was next. Thus, all has been told to you truthfully, as you asked.

shloka_text: त्वामिदानीं कथं तात जानीयां को भवानिति । एवमुक्तस्तु तद्रक्षो विनीतमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.12.14 ।।
explanation: How, dear one, may I now know who you are? Thus addressed, that Rākṣasa humbly spoke this.

shloka_text: अहं पौलस्त्यतनयो दशग्रीवश्च नामतः । मुनेर्विश्रवसो यस्तु तृतीयो ब्रह्मणो ऽभवत् ।। 7.12.15 ।।
explanation: I am Dashagriva by name, the son of Pulastya. And he (Pulastya) was the sage Vishravas, who was the third from Brahma.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तदा राम राक्षसेन्द्रेण दानवः । महर्षेस्तनयं ज्ञात्वा मयो हर्षमुपागतः । दातुं दुहितरं तस्मै रोचयामास यत्र वै ।। 7.12.16 ।।
explanation: O Rama, when the Danava Maya was thus addressed by the lord of Rakshasas, knowing him to be the son of the great sage, he became delighted. He then indeed desired to give his daughter to him.

shloka_text: करेण तु करं तस्या ग्राहयित्वा मयस्तदा । प्रहसन्प्राह दैत्येन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रमिदं वचः ।। 7.12.17 ।।
explanation: Then Maya, taking her hand in his, laughing, the lord of the Daityas spoke these words to the lord of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: इयं ममात्मजा राजन्हेमया ऽप्सरसा धृता । कन्या मन्दोदरी नाम पत्न्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ।। 7.12.18 ।।
explanation: O King, this is my daughter, named Mandodari, who was brought up by the Apsara Hema. Let her be accepted as a wife.

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव तं राम दशग्रीवो ऽभ्यभाषत । प्रज्चाल्य तत्र चैवाग्निमकरोत्पाणिसङ्ग्रहम् ।। 7.12.19 ।।
explanation: "Yes, indeed," Dashagriva spoke to him. And having kindled fire there, he performed the taking of the hand (marriage ritual).

shloka_text: स हि तस्य मयो राम शापाभिज्ञस्तपोधनात् । विदित्वा तेन सा दत्ता तस्य पैतामहं कुलम् ।। 7.12.20 ।।
explanation: For Maya, O Rama, having learned of the curse concerning him from the ascetic, gave her to him, recognizing his paternal lineage.

shloka_text: अमोघां तस्य शक्तिं च प्रददौ परमाद्भुताम् । परेण तपसा लब्धां जघ्निवाँल्लक्ष्मणं यया ।। 7.12.21 ।।
explanation: And he gave him an unfailing and exceedingly wonderful power, obtained by great penance, by which Lakshmana was killed.

shloka_text: एवं सीकृतदारो वै लङ्काया ईश्वरः प्रभुः । गत्वा तु नगरीं भार्ये भ्रातृभ्यां समुपाहरत् ।। 7.12.22 ।।
explanation: Thus, the mighty lord, the ruler of Lanka, having taken Sita as his wife, indeed went to his city and presented his wives to his brothers.

shloka_text: वैरोचनस्य दौहित्रीं वज्रज्वालेति नामतः । तां भार्यां कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः समकल्पयत् ।। 7.12.23 ।।
explanation: Ravana arranged Vajrajvala, the granddaughter of Vairochana, to be Kumbhakarna's wife.

shloka_text: गन्धर्वराजस्य सुतां शैलूषस्य महात्मनः । सरमां नाम धर्मज्ञां लेभे भार्यां विभीषणः ।। 7.12.24 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana took as his wife Sarama, the righteous daughter of the great-souled Gandharva king Shailusha.

shloka_text: तीरे तु सरसो वै तु सञ्जज्ञे मानसस्य हि । सरस्तदा मानसं तु ववृधे जलदागमे ।। 7.12.25 ।।
explanation: On the bank of the Manasa lake, it indeed originated. Then the Manasa lake indeed grew at the arrival of the clouds.

shloka_text: मात्रा तु तस्याः कन्यायाः स्नेहेनाक्रन्दितं वचः । सरो मा वर्धयस्वेति ततः सा सरमा ऽभवत् ।। 7.12.26 ।।
explanation: Her mother, out of affection for her daughter, cried out the words: 'O lake, do not grow!' From that, she became Sarama.

shloka_text: एवं ते कृतदारा वै रेमिरे तत्र राक्षसाः । स्वां स्वां भार्यामुपागम्य गन्धर्वा इव नन्दने ।। 7.12.27 ।।
explanation: Thus, those Rākṣasas, having taken wives, indeed enjoyed themselves there, each approaching his own wife, like Gandharvas in Nandana.

shloka_text: ततो मन्दोदरी पुत्रं मेघनादमजीजनत् । स एष इन्द्रजिन्नाम युष्माभिरभिधीयते ।। 7.12.28 ।।
explanation: Then Mandodari gave birth to a son, Meghanada. He is the one whom you call Indrajit.

shloka_text: जातमात्रेण हि पुरा तेन रावणसूनुना । रुदता सुमहान्मुक्तो नादो जलधरोपमः ।। 7.12.29 ।।
explanation: Indeed, formerly, as soon as he was born, that son of Ravana, while crying, emitted a mighty roar, resembling a thundercloud.

shloka_text: जडीकृता च सा लङ्का तस्य नादेन राघव । पिता तस्याकरोन्नाम मेघनाद इति स्वयम् ।। 7.12.30 ।।
explanation: And that Lanka was stunned by his roar, O Raghava. His father himself gave him the name Meghanada.

shloka_text: सो ऽवर्धत तदा राम रावणान्तःपुरे शुभे । रक्ष्यमाणो वरस्त्रीभिश्छन्नः काष्ठैरिवानलः ।। 7.12.31 ।।
explanation: Then he grew, O Rama, in Ravana's beautiful inner palace, protected by noble women, like fire concealed by logs.

shloka_text: मातापित्रोर्महाहर्षं जनयन्रावणात्मजः ।। 7.12.32 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa's son, causing great joy to his mother and father.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः ।। 12 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तत्र कालेन केनचित् । निद्रा समभवत्तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी ।। 7.13.1 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, an intense, embodied sleep, sent forth by the Lord of the worlds, manifested there for Kumbhakarna.

shloka_text: ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णो ऽब्रवीद्वचः । निद्रा मां बाधते राजन्कारयस्व ममालयम् ।। 7.13.2 ।।
explanation: Then Kumbhakarna spoke to his seated brother: "O King, sleep afflicts me. Have my dwelling constructed."

shloka_text: विनियुक्तास्ततो राज्ञा शिल्पिनो विश्वकर्मवत् । विस्तीर्णं योजनं शुभ्रं ततो द्विगुणमायतम् ।। 7.13.3 ।।
explanation: Then, the artisans, appointed by the king, like Vishwakarma, [made it] a yojana wide, splendid, and twice as long.

shloka_text: दर्शनीयं निराबाधं कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रिरे । स्फाटिकैः काञ्चनैश्चित्रैः स्तम्भैः सर्वत्र शोभितम् ।। 7.13.4 ।।
explanation: They built for Kumbhakarna a beautiful and unobstructed (abode), splendid everywhere with variegated pillars of crystal and gold.

shloka_text: वैडूर्यकृतसोपानं किङ्किणीजालकं तथा । दान्ततोरणविन्यस्तं वज्रस्फटिकवेदिकम् ।। 7.13.5 ।।
explanation: With steps made of lapis lazuli, and a network of tinkling bells, adorned with ivory archways, and having platforms of diamond and crystal.

shloka_text: मनोहरं सर्वसुखं कारयामास राक्षसः । सर्वत्र सुखदं नित्यं मेरोः पुण्यां गुहामिव ।। 7.13.6 ।।
explanation: The demon caused to be made a charming place, full of all comforts, which was always delightful everywhere, like a sacred cave of Mount Meru.

shloka_text: तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः । बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो न प्रबुद्ध्यते ।। 7.13.7 ।।
explanation: There, the mighty Kumbhakarna, overcome by sleep, does not awaken, having slept for many thousands of years.

shloka_text: निद्राभिभूते तु तदा कुम्भकर्णे दशाननः । देवर्षियक्षगन्धर्वान्सञ्जघ्ने हि निरङ्कुशः ।। 7.13.8 ।।
explanation: When Kumbhakarna was then overcome by sleep, the unrestrained Dashanana indeed slew the Devas, Rishis, Yakshas, and Gandharvas.

shloka_text: उद्यानानि च चित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च । तानि गत्वा सुसङक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः ।। 7.13.9 ।।
explanation: And the beautiful gardens, including Nandan and others, Daśānana, extremely enraged, went to them and destroyed them.

shloka_text: नदीं गज इव क्रीडन्वृक्षान्वायुरिव क्षिपन् । नगान्व्रज्र इवोत्सृष्टो विध्वंसयति राक्षसः ।। 7.13.10 ।।
explanation: The demon destroys, sporting like an elephant in a river, felling trees like the wind, and shattering mountains like a hurled thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तथावृत्तं तु विज्ञाय दशग्रीवं धनेश्वरः । कुलानुरूपं धर्मज्ञो वृत्तं संस्मृत्य चात्मनः ।। 7.13.11 ।।
explanation: Having understood such conduct of Daśagrīva, and remembering his own conduct befitting his lineage, the lord of wealth, Kubera, a knower of dharma,

shloka_text: सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्रवणस्तदा । लङ्कां सम्प्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम् ।। 7.13.12 ।।
explanation: Then Vaishravana, to demonstrate fraternal affection, sent a messenger to Lanka, indeed for the welfare of Dashagriva.

shloka_text: स गत्वा नगरीं लङ्कामाससाद विभीषणम् । मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति ।। 7.13.13 ।।
explanation: Having gone to the city of Lanka, he met Vibhishana. He was honored by him with due respect and questioned about his arrival.

shloka_text: पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनां च बिभीषणः । सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम् ।। 7.13.14 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, having inquired about the welfare of the king and his kinsmen, presented himself to Dashanana, who was seated in the assembly.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । जयेति वाचा सम्पूज्य तूष्णीं समभिवर्तत ।। 7.13.15 ।।
explanation: He, having seen the king there, shining with his own splendor, and having honored him with the words 'Victory!', approached silently.

shloka_text: तं तत्रोत्तमपर्यङ्के वरास्तरणशोभिते । उपविष्टं दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.13.16 ।।
explanation: To him, Daśagrīva, seated there on an excellent couch adorned with splendid coverings, a messenger then spoke words.

shloka_text: राजन्वदामि ते सर्वं भ्राता तव यदब्रवीत् । उभयोः सदृशं वीर वृत्तस्य च कुलस्य च ।। 7.13.17 ।।
explanation: O King, I will tell you everything that your brother said. O hero, it is befitting of the character and lineage of both.

shloka_text: साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत्कृतश्चारित्रसङ्ग्रहः । साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते ।। 7.13.18 ।।
explanation: Good, this much is sufficient; good character has been acquired. Well, let a firm stand in righteousness be established, if it is possible.

shloka_text: दृष्टं मे नन्दनं भग्नमृषयो निहताः श्रुताः । देवतानां समुद्योगस्त्वत्तो राजन्मम श्रुतः ।। 7.13.19 ।।
explanation: I have seen Nandana destroyed. I have heard that the sages were slain. O King, I have heard from you about the mobilization of the gods.

shloka_text: निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वया ऽहं राक्षसाधिप । अपराद्धा हि बाल्याच्च रमणीयाः स्वबान्धवाः ।। 7.13.20 ।।
explanation: O king of Rākṣasas, I have been repeatedly rejected by you. For indeed, one's own relatives, even if they have erred due to childishness, should be cherished.
