shloka_text: अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम् । रौद्रं व्रत्तं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः ।। 7.13.21 ।।
explanation: But I went to the peak of the Himalayas to practice Dharma, having undertaken a severe vow, disciplined and with my senses controlled.

shloka_text: तत्र देवो मया दृष्टः सह देव्या मया प्रभुः । सव्यं चक्षुर्मया दैवात्तत्र देव्यां निपातितम् ।। 7.13.22 ।।
explanation: There, I saw the god, the Lord, with the goddess. Accidentally, my left eye fell upon the goddess there.

shloka_text: का न्वियं स्यादिति शुभा न खल्वन्येन हेतुना । रूपं ह्यनुपमं कृत्वा रुद्राणी तत्र तिष्ठति ।। 7.13.23 ।।
explanation: Who indeed could this auspicious one be? It is certainly not for any other reason, for Rudrani stands there, having assumed an incomparable form.

shloka_text: देव्या दिव्यप्रभावेण दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम् । रेणुध्वस्तमिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गुलत्वमुपागतम् ।। 7.13.24 ।।
explanation: My left eye, burnt by the divine power of the goddess, has become tawny, like a light obscured by dust.

shloka_text: ततो ऽहमन्यद्विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम् । तूष्णीं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ समाधारं महाव्रतम् ।। 7.13.25 ।।
explanation: Then I, having gone to another vast side of that mountain, silently observed a great vow for eight hundred years.

shloka_text: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः । प्रीतः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः ।। 7.13.26 ।।
explanation: Upon the completion of that observance, there the Lord, the god Maheśvara, pleased with a delighted mind, spoke this word.

shloka_text: पैङ्गल्यं यदवाप्तं हि देव्या रूपनिरीक्षणात् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसा नेन सुव्रत ।। 7.13.27 ।।
explanation: The paleness which was indeed acquired from gazing upon the form of the goddess – I am pleased with this penance of yours, O knower of Dharma, O virtuous one.

shloka_text: मया चैतद्व्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप । तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चरेव्रतमीदृशम् ।। 7.13.28 ।।
explanation: This vow has been observed by me, and indeed by you, O lord of wealth. There is no third person who would perform such a vow.

shloka_text: व्रतं सुनिश्चयं ह्येतन्मया ह्युत्पादितं पुरा । तत्सखित्वं मया सौम्य रोचयस्व धनेश्वर ।। 7.13.29 ।।
explanation: This very firm vow was indeed established by me long ago. Therefore, O gentle lord of wealth, please accept friendship with me.

shloka_text: तपसा निर्जितश्चैव सखा भव ममानघ । देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेण यच्च सव्यं तवेक्षणम् ।। 7.13.30 ।।
explanation: O sinless one, having been conquered by my penance, become my friend. And your left eye was burnt by the power of the Goddess.

shloka_text: एकाक्षिपिङ्गलेत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम् । एवं तेन सखित्वं च प्राप्यानुज्ञां च शङ्करात् ।। 7.13.31 ।।
explanation: The name 'Ekakshipingala' will remain eternal. Thus, having obtained friendship from him and permission from Shankara.

shloka_text: आगत्य च श्रुतो ऽयं मे तव पापविनिश्चयः ।। 7.13.32 ।।
explanation: And having come, I heard this wicked resolve of yours.

shloka_text: तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगान्निवर्त कुलदूषणात् । चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसङ्घैः सुरैस्तव ।। 7.13.33 ।।
explanation: Therefore, desist from that unrighteous association, which is a disgrace to your family. For indeed, the means of your destruction are being considered by the gods along with the assemblies of sages.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः क्रुद्धसंरक्तलोचनः । हस्तौ दन्तांश्च सम्पीड्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.13.34 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Daśagrīva, with angry, bloodshot eyes, clenched his hands and teeth and spoke this word.

shloka_text: विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यस्य प्रभाषसे । नैतत्त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि चोदितः ।। 7.13.35 ।।
explanation: O messenger, the words you speak have been understood by me. This is not you, nor is it he (who sent you), but rather it is by the brother by whom you were commanded.

shloka_text: हितं नैष ममैतद्धि ब्रवीति धनरक्षकः । महेश्वरसखित्वं तु मूढ श्रावयते किल ।। 7.13.36 ।।
explanation: This guardian of wealth does not speak what is beneficial for me; rather, O fool, he merely boasts of his friendship with Maheśvara.

shloka_text: न चेदं क्षमणीयं मे यदेतद्भाषितं त्वया । यदेतावन्मया कालं दूत तस्य तु मर्षितम् ।। 7.13.37 ।।
explanation: What you have spoken is not pardonable by me. O messenger, that I have tolerated it for so long is already much.

shloka_text: न हन्तव्यो गुरुर्ज्येष्ठो मया ऽयमिति मन्यते । तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः ।। 7.13.38 ।।
explanation: He considers, 'This venerable elder should not be killed by me.' But now, having heard my words, this resolve has been made.

shloka_text: त्रीँल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः ।। 7.13.39 ।।
explanation: Relying on the strength of my arms, I will conquer even the three worlds.

shloka_text: एतन्मुहूर्तमेवाहं तस्यैकस्य तु वै कृते । चतुरो लोकपालांस्तान्नयिष्यामि यमक्षयम् ।। 7.13.40 ।।
explanation: In this very moment, for the sake of that one, I will indeed lead those four world-protectors to Yama's abode.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खड्गेन जघ्निवान् । ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम् ।। 7.13.41 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, the lord of Lanka struck the messenger with a sword. He gave him to the wicked Rākṣasas to devour.

shloka_text: एवं कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः । त्रैलोक्यविजयाकाङ्क्षी ययौ यत्र धनेश्वरः ।। 7.13.42 ।।
explanation: Thus, having performed auspicious rites, Ravana, desirous of conquering the three worlds, mounted his chariot and went to where the lord of wealth was.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः ।। 13 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by a sage.

shloka_text: ततस्तु सचिवैः सार्धं षड्भिर्नित्यं बलोद्धतैः । महोदरप्रहस्ताभ्यां मारीचशुकसारणैः ।। 7.14.1 ।।
explanation: Then, along with six constantly powerful ministers: Mahodara, Prahasta, Maricha, Shuka, and Sarana.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगृध्नुना । वृतः संप्रययौ श्रीमान्क्रोधाल्लोकान्दहन्निव ।। 7.14.2 ।।
explanation: And the glorious Dhūmraksha, the brave one, always eager for battle, set out, surrounded (by his forces), as if burning the worlds with anger.

shloka_text: पुराणि स नदीः शैलान्वनान्युपवनानि च । अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमागमत् ।। 7.14.3 ।।
explanation: He, having crossed cities, rivers, mountains, forests, and groves, reached Mount Kailasa in a moment.

shloka_text: सन्निविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन्राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु । युद्धे ऽत्यर्थकृतोत्साहं दुरात्मानं समन्त्रिणम् ।। 7.14.4 ।।
explanation: Having learned that the evil-minded lord of Rakshasas, exceedingly enthusiastic for battle, was stationed on that mountain with his ministers.

shloka_text: यक्षा न शेकुः संस्थातुं प्रमुखे तस्य रक्षसः । राज्ञो भ्रातेति विज्ञाय गता यत्र धनेश्वरः ।। 7.14.5 ।।
explanation: The Yakshas were unable to stand before that Rakshasa. Realizing, "He is the king's brother," they went to where the lord of wealth (Kubera) was.

shloka_text: ते गत्वा सर्वमाचख्युर्भ्रातुस्तस्य चिकीर्षितम् । अनुज्ञाता ययुर्हष्टा युद्धाय धनदेन ते ।। 7.14.6 ।।
explanation: They went and reported all of his brother's intentions. Permitted by Kubera, they joyfully went for battle.

shloka_text: ततो बलानां सङ्क्षोभो व्यवर्धत महोदधेः । तस्य नैर्ऋतराजस्य शैलं सञ्चालयन्निव ।। 7.14.7 ।।
explanation: Then the agitation of the forces increased like that of a great ocean, as if shaking the mountain of that king of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवद्यक्षराक्षससङ्कुलम् । व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवा राक्षसस्य ते ।। 7.14.8 ।।
explanation: Then a battle, tumultuous with Yakshas and Rakshasas, took place. And those ministers of the Rakshasa became distressed there.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । हर्षनादान्बहून्कृत्वा स क्रोधादभ्यधावत ।। 7.14.9 ।।
explanation: Having seen such an army, Daśagrīva, the night-wanderer, uttered many shouts of joy and then rushed forth with anger.

shloka_text: ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमाः । तेषां सहस्रमेकैकं यक्षाणां समयोधयन् ।। 7.14.10 ।।
explanation: And those ministers of the king of Rakshasas, who were of terrible prowess, each one of them fought a thousand Yakshas.

shloka_text: ततो गदाभिर्मुसलैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः । हन्यमानो दशग्रीवस्तत्सैन्यं समगाहत ।। 7.14.11 ।।
explanation: Then, Dashagriva, though being struck by maces, clubs, swords, spears, and javelins, plunged into that army.

shloka_text: स निरुच्छ्वासवत्तत्र वध्यमानो दशाननः । वर्षद्भिरिव जीमूतैर्धाराभिरवरुध्यत ।। 7.14.12 ।।
explanation: He, Dashanana, being struck there as if breathless, was overwhelmed by torrents, as if by clouds raining down streams.

shloka_text: न चकार व्यथां चैव यक्षशस्त्रैः समाहतः । महीधर इवाम्भोदैर्धाराशतसमुक्षितः ।। 7.14.13 ।।
explanation: He did not feel any pain, even when struck by the weapons of the Yakshas, just like a mountain is showered by hundreds of streams from clouds.

shloka_text: स दुरात्मा समुद्यम्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम् । प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन्यक्षान्यमक्षयम् ।। 7.14.14 ।।
explanation: That wicked soul, having raised his mace resembling the staff of Death, then entered the army, sending the Yakshas to destruction.

shloka_text: स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्केन्धनमिवाकुलम् । वातेनाग्निरिवायत्तो यक्षसैन्यं ददाह तत् ।। 7.14.15 ।।
explanation: He, like fire propelled by wind, burned that Yaksha army, which was vast like a thicket and dense like dry fuel.

shloka_text: तैस्तु तत्र महामात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः । अल्पावशेषास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः ।। 7.14.16 ।।
explanation: By those great ministers there, Mahodara, Shuka, and others, those Yakshas were made few in number, like clouds by winds.

shloka_text: केचित्समाहता भग्नाः पतिताः समरक्षितौ । ओष्ठांश्च दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैरदशन्कुपिता रणे ।। 7.14.17 ।।
explanation: Some, struck down and broken, fell on the battlefield. Enraged in battle, they bit their lips with sharp teeth.

shloka_text: श्रान्ताश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्ग्य भ्रष्टशस्त्रा रणाजिरे । सीदन्ति च तदा यक्षाः कूला इव जलेन ह ।। 7.14.18 ।।
explanation: Exhausted, and embracing each other, with their weapons lost on the battlefield, the Yakshas then collapsed, like river banks by water.

shloka_text: हतानां गच्छतां स्वर्गं युध्यतां पृथिवीतले । प्रेक्षतामृषिसङ्घानां न बभूवान्तरं दिवि ।। 7.14.19 ।।
explanation: There was no space in the sky for the slain going to heaven, for those fighting on the surface of the earth, and for the hosts of sages watching.

shloka_text: भग्नांस्तु तान्समालक्ष्य यक्षेन्द्रांस्तु महाबलान् । धनाध्यक्षो महाबाहुः प्रेषयामास यक्षकान् ।। 7.14.20 ।।
explanation: Seeing those mighty chief Yakshas defeated, the mighty-armed lord of wealth sent (other) Yakshas.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः । प्रेषितो न्यपतद्यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः ।। 7.14.21 ।।
explanation: O Rama, at this moment, a Yaksha named Samyodhakantaka, who had been sent with a vast army and vehicles, arrived.

shloka_text: तेन चक्रेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव रणे हतः । पतितो भूतले शैलात्क्षीणपुण्य इव ग्रहः ।। 7.14.22 ।।
explanation: By that discus, Maricha was slain in battle, just as if by Vishnu. He fell to the ground, like a planet whose merit is exhausted falls from a mountain.

shloka_text: ससञ्ज्ञस्तु मुहूर्तेन स विश्रम्य निशाचरः । तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे ।। 7.14.23 ।।
explanation: Having regained consciousness in a moment, and having rested, the night-wanderer fought that Yaksha. And he (the Yaksha), being defeated, fled.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं वैडूर्यरजसोक्षितम् । मर्यादां प्रतिहाराणां तोरणान्तरमाविशत् ।। 7.14.24 ।।
explanation: Then, he/it entered the interior of the archway, which was adorned with gold, sprinkled with lapis lazuli dust, and served as the boundary for the doorkeepers.

shloka_text: तं तु राजन्दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम् । सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत् ।। 7.14.25 ।।
explanation: O King, that Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, as he was entering, was stopped by the gatekeeper known as Suryabhanu.

shloka_text: स वार्यमाणो यक्षेण प्रविवेश निशाचरः । यदा तु वारितो राम न व्यतिष्ठत्स राक्षसः ।। 7.14.26 ।।
explanation: Though obstructed by the Yaksha, that night-wanderer entered. But when he was stopped, O Rama, that demon did not desist.

shloka_text: ततस्तोरणमुत्पाट्य तेन यक्षेण ताडितः । रुधिरं प्रस्रवन्भाति शैलो धातुस्रवैरिव ।। 7.14.27 ।।
explanation: Then, having uprooted the gateway, struck by that Yaksha, he, gushing blood, shone like a mountain with streams of minerals.

shloka_text: स शैलशिखराभेण तोरणेन समाहतः । जगाम न क्षतिं वीरो वरदानात्स्वयम्भुवः ।। 7.14.28 ।।
explanation: The hero, struck by the archway resembling a mountain peak, did not suffer harm due to the boon of Svayambhu.

shloka_text: तेनैव तोरणेनाथ यक्षस्तेनाभिताडितः । नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्मीकृततनुस्तदा ।। 7.14.29 ।।
explanation: Then, the Yaksha, struck by that very archway, was not seen, his body having been reduced to ashes at that time.

shloka_text: ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा रक्षःपराक्रमम् । ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः । त्यक्तप्रहरणाः श्रान्ता विवर्णवदनास्तदा ।। 7.14.30 ।।
explanation: Then, all of them fled, having witnessed the prowess of the Rākṣasa. Then, afflicted by fear, they entered rivers and caves, having abandoned their weapons, weary, and with pale faces.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः ।। 14 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana by Valmiki, the original epic, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the fourteenth chapter.

shloka_text: ततस्ताँल्लक्ष्य वित्रस्तान्यक्षेन्द्रांश्च सहस्रशः । धनाध्यक्षो महायक्षं माणिचारमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.15.1 ।।
explanation: Then, observing those thousands of terrified chief Yakshas, the lord of wealth then spoke to the great Yaksha Manichara.

shloka_text: रावणं जहि यक्षेन्द्र दुर्वृत्तं पापचेतसम् । शरणं भव वीराणां यक्षाणां युद्धशालिनाम् ।। 7.15.2 ।।
explanation: O king of Yakshas, kill Ravana, the wicked and evil-minded one. Be a refuge for the heroes, for the Yakshas valiant in battle.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो महाबाहुर्माणिभद्रः सुदुर्जयः । वृतो यक्षसहस्रैस्तु चतुर्भिः समयोधयत् ।। 7.15.3 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed, unconquerable Manibhadra, surrounded by four thousand Yakshas, fought.

shloka_text: ते गदामुसलप्रासैः शक्तितोमरमुद्गरैः । अभिघ्नन्तस्तदा यक्षा राक्षसान्समुपाद्रवन् ।। 7.15.4 ।।
explanation: Then the Yakshas, striking with maces, pestles, spears, lances, javelins, and hammers, attacked the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: कुर्वन्तस्तुमुलं युद्धं चरन्तः श्येनवल्लघु । बाढं प्रयच्छन्नेच्छामि दीयतामिति भाषिणः ।। 7.15.5 ।।
explanation: Waging a tumultuous battle, moving swiftly like hawks, they were speakers of the words, "I do not wish to give anything, let it be given!"

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः । दृष्ट्वा तत्तुमुलं युद्धं परं विस्मयमागमन् ।। 7.15.6 ।।
explanation: Then the gods, along with the Gandharvas, and the sages, the expounders of the Vedas, seeing that tumultuous battle, were greatly astonished.

shloka_text: यक्षाणां तु प्रहस्तेन सहस्रं निहतं रणे । महोदरेण चानिन्द्यं सहस्रमपरं हतम् ।। 7.15.7 ।।
explanation: However, a thousand of the Yakshas were slain in battle by Prahasta. And another blameless thousand were slain by Mahodara.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धेन च तदा राजन्मारीचेन युयुत्सुना । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण द्वे सहस्रे निपातिते ।। 7.15.8 ।।
explanation: And then, O King, by the enraged Maricha, who was eager to fight, two thousand were struck down in just the blink of an eye.

shloka_text: क्व च यक्षार्जवं युद्धं क्व च मायाबलाश्रयम् । रक्षसां पुरुषव्याघ्र तेन ते ऽभ्यधिका युधि ।। 7.15.9 ।।
explanation: O tiger among men, how can the straightforwardness of the Yakshas in battle compare with the Rakshasas' reliance on illusion and strength? Therefore, they are superior in battle.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षेण समागम्य माणिभद्रो महारणे । मुसलेनोरसि क्रोधात्तडितो न च कम्पितः ।। 7.15.10 ।।
explanation: Having met Dhūmrākṣa in the great battle, Māṇibhadra was struck on the chest with a mace out of anger, yet he did not tremble.

shloka_text: ततो गदां समाविध्य माणिभद्रेण राक्षसः । धूम्राक्षस्ताडितो मूर्ध्नि विह्वलः स पपात ह ।। 7.15.11 ।।
explanation: Then, Maṇibhadra, having whirled his mace, struck the demon Dhūmrākṣa on the head. He fell, bewildered.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षं ताडितं दृष्ट्वा पतितं शोणितोक्षितम् । अभ्यधावत सङ्ग्रामे माणिभद्रं दशाननः ।। 7.15.12 ।।
explanation: Having seen Dhūmrākṣa struck, fallen, and drenched in blood, Daśānana rushed towards Māṇibhadra in battle.

shloka_text: तं क्रुद्धमभिधावन्तं माणिभद्रो दशाननम् । शक्तिभिस्ताडयामास तिसृभिर्यक्षपुङ्गवः ।। 7.15.13 ।।
explanation: Maṇibhadra, the foremost among Yakṣas, struck Daśānana, who was enraged and rushing forward, with three spears.

shloka_text: ताडितो माणिभद्रस्य मुकुटे प्राहरद्रणे । तस्य तेन प्रहारेम मुकुटं पार्श्वमागतम् ।। 7.15.14 ।।
explanation: Having been struck, he struck Maṇibhadra's crown in battle. By that blow, his crown was dislodged to the side.

shloka_text: ततः संयुध्यमानेन विष्टब्धो न व्यकम्पत । तदाप्रभृति यक्षो ऽसौ पार्श्वमौलिरिति स्मृतः । सन्नादः सुमहान्राजंस्तस्मिन्शैले ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.15.15 ।।
explanation: Then, though held firm by the one fighting, he did not tremble. From that time onwards, that Yaksha was known as Pārśvamauli. A very great roar, O King, resounded on that mountain.

shloka_text: ततो दूरात्प्रददृशे धनाध्यक्षो गदाधरः । शुक्रप्रौष्ठपदाभ्यां च पद्मशङ्खसमावृतः ।। 7.15.16 ।।
explanation: Then, from a distance, the lord of wealth, bearing a mace, was seen, surrounded by Shukra, Praushthapada, Padma, and Shankha.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरं सङ्ख्ये शापाद्विभ्रष्टगौरवम् । उवाच वचनं धीमान्युक्तं पैतामहे कुले ।। 7.15.17 ।।
explanation: The wise one, having seen his brother in battle, whose glory was diminished by a curse, spoke words befitting the ancestral lineage.

shloka_text: यन्मया वार्यमाणस्त्वं नावगच्छसि दुर्मते । पश्चादस्य फलं प्राप्य ज्ञास्यसे निरयं गतः ।। 7.15.18 ।।
explanation: O evil-minded one, because you do not understand what I am preventing, you will know later, having obtained the consequence of this and gone to hell.

shloka_text: यो हि मोहाद्विषं पीत्वा नावगच्छति दुर्मतिः । स तस्य परिणामान्ते जानीते कर्मणः फलम् ।। 7.15.19 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the foolish-minded person who, having drunk poison out of delusion, does not understand, he knows the fruit of that action at the end of its consequence.

shloka_text: देवता नाभिनन्दन्ति धर्मयुक्तेन केनचित् । येन त्वमीदृशं भावं नीतस्सन्नावबुद्ध्यसे ।। 7.15.20 ।।
explanation: The gods do not approve of you by any righteous means, because of which, having been brought to such a state, you do not understand.

shloka_text: मातरं पितरं यो हि आचार्यं चावमन्यते । स पश्यति फलं तस्य प्रेतराजवशं गतः ।। 7.15.21 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he who disrespects his mother, father, and teacher, experiences the consequence of that, having fallen under the sway of the Lord of the Dead.

shloka_text: अध्रुवे हि शरीरे यो न करोति तपोर्जनम् । स पश्चात्तप्यते मूढो मृतो दृष्ट्वा ऽ ऽत्मनो गतिम् ।। 7.15.22 ।।
explanation: He who does not accumulate merit in this impermanent body, that fool repents afterwards, having died and seen his own destiny.

shloka_text: धर्माद्राज्यं धनं सौख्यमधर्माद्दुःखमेव च । तस्माद्धर्मं सुखार्थाय कुर्यात्पापं विसर्जयेत् ।। 7.15.23 ।।
explanation: From righteousness come kingdom, wealth, and happiness; and from unrighteousness comes only sorrow. Therefore, for the sake of happiness, one should practice righteousness and abandon sin.

shloka_text: पापस्य हि फलं दुःखं तद्भोक्तव्यमिहात्मना । तस्मादात्मापघातार्थं मूढः पापं करिष्यति ।। 7.15.24 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the fruit of sin is sorrow, and that must be experienced by oneself in this world. Therefore, a fool will commit sin for the sake of self-destruction.

shloka_text: कस्य चिन्न हि दुर्बुद्धेश्छन्दतो जायते मतिः । देवं चेष्टयते सर्वं हतो दैवेन हन्यते । यादृशं कुरुते कर्म तादृशं फलमश्नुते ।। 7.15.25 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the intellect of a foolish person does not arise by their own will. Destiny causes everything to act; one struck by destiny is destroyed. Whatever action one performs, such a fruit one obtains.

shloka_text: बुद्धिरूपं फलं पुत्राञ्छौर्यं धीरत्वमेव च । प्राप्नुवन्ति नरा लोके निर्जितं पुण्यकर्मभिः ।। 7.15.26 ।।
explanation: People in the world obtain intelligence, beauty, sons, valor, and indeed steadfastness, all acquired through meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: एवं निरयगामी त्वं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी । न त्वां समभिभाषिष्ये ऽसद्वृत्तेष्वेव निर्णयः ।। 7.15.27 ।।
explanation: Since your mind is of this kind, you are destined for hell. I will not speak to you, for the judgment is only for those of wicked conduct.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्ततस्तेन तस्यामात्याः समाहताः । मारीचप्रमुखाः सर्वे विमुखा विप्रदुद्रुवुः ।। 7.15.28 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by him, his summoned ministers, all led by Maricha, turned away and fled.

shloka_text: ततस्तेन दशग्रीवो यक्षेन्द्रेण महात्मना । गदयाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि न च स्थानात्प्रकम्पितः ।। 7.15.29 ।।
explanation: Then, Daśagrīva was struck on the head with a mace by that great-souled Yakṣendra, yet he was not shaken from his place.

shloka_text: ततस्तौ राम निघ्नन्तौ तदान्योन्यं महामृधे । न विह्वलौ न च श्रान्तौ बभूवतुरमर्षणौ ।। 7.15.30 ।।
explanation: Then, O Rama, those two, striking each other in that great battle, became neither distressed nor weary, but remained unyielding.

shloka_text: आग्नेयमस्त्रं तस्मै स मुमोच धनदस्तदा । राक्षसेन्द्रो वारुणेन तदस्त्रं प्रत्यवारयत् ।। 7.15.31 ।।
explanation: Then Dhanada released the Agneya weapon at him. The lord of Rakshasas countered that weapon with a Varuna weapon.

shloka_text: ततो मायां प्रविष्टो ऽसौ राक्षसीं राक्षसेश्वरः । रूपाणां शतसाहस्रं विनाशाय चकार च ।। 7.15.32 ।।
explanation: Then, that lord of Rākṣasas, having entered into a demonic illusion, created a hundred thousand forms for destruction.

shloka_text: व्याघ्रो वराहो जीमूतः पर्वतः सागरो द्रुमः । यक्षो दैत्यस्वरूपी च सो ऽदृश्यत दशाननः ।। 7.15.33 ।।
explanation: Daśānana appeared as a tiger, a boar, a cloud, a mountain, an ocean, a tree, a Yaksha, and a Daitya in form.

shloka_text: बहूनि च करोति स्म दृश्यन्ते न त्वसौ ततः । प्रतिगृह्य ततो राम महदस्त्रं दशाननः ।। 7.15.34 ।।
explanation: He performed many deeds, but they were not seen from that point. Then, O Rama, Daśānana, having received a great weapon,

shloka_text: जघान मूर्ध्नि धनदं व्याविद्ध्य महतीं गदाम् । एवं स तेनाभिहतो विह्वलः शोणितोक्षितः ।। 7.15.35 ।।
explanation: Having whirled a mighty mace, he struck Dhanada on the head. Thus struck by him, he was bewildered and drenched in blood.

shloka_text: कृत्तमूल इवाशोको निपपात धनाधिपः ।। 7.15.36 ।।
explanation: The lord of wealth fell down like an Ashoka tree whose roots had been cut.

shloka_text: ततः पद्मादिभिस्तत्र निधिभिः स तदा वृतः । धनदोच्छ्वासितस्तैस्तु वनमानीय नन्दनम् ।। 7.15.37 ।।
explanation: Then, at that time, he was surrounded there by the treasures like Padma and others. Having been revived by them, Dhanada (Kubera) brought Nandana to the forest.

shloka_text: निर्जित्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्तं धनदं हृष्टमानसः । पुष्पकं तस्य जग्राह विमानं जयलक्षणम् ।। 7.15.38 ।।
explanation: Having conquered Dhanada, the king of Rakshasas, with a joyful mind, seized his Pushpaka aerial chariot, a symbol of victory.

shloka_text: काञ्चनस्तम्भसंवीतं वैडूर्यमणितोरणम् । मुक्ताजालप्रतिच्छन्नं सर्वकामफलद्रुमम् ।। 7.15.39 ।।
explanation: Adorned with golden pillars, with archways of vaidurya gems, covered with networks of pearls, a tree that grants all desires.

shloka_text: मनोजवं कामगमं कामरूपं विहङ्गमम् । मणिकाञ्चनसोपानं तप्तकाञ्चनवेदिकम् ।। 7.15.40 ।।
explanation: Swift as the mind, moving at will, assuming any desired form, flying; with steps of jewels and gold, and platforms of refined gold.

shloka_text: देवोपवाह्यमक्षय्यं सदादृष्टिमनःसुखम् । बह्वाश्चर्यं भक्तिचित्रं ब्रह्मणा परिनिर्मितम् ।। 7.15.41 ।।
explanation: A divine vehicle, imperishable, always pleasing to the sight and mind, full of many wonders, wonderfully adorned, perfectly fashioned by Brahmā.

shloka_text: निर्मितं सर्वकामैस्तु मनोहरमनुत्तमम् । न तु शीतं न चोष्णं च सर्वर्तुसुखदं शुभम् ।। 7.15.42 ।।
explanation: Created to fulfill all desires, charming and unsurpassed. It is neither cold nor hot, providing comfort in all seasons, and is auspicious.

shloka_text: स तं राजा समारुह्य कामगं वीर्यनिर्जितम् । जितं त्रिभुवनं मेने दर्पोत्सेकात्सुदुर्मतिः ।। 7.15.43 ।।
explanation: That king, having mounted that (vehicle/creature) moving at will, which was conquered by his valor, considered the three worlds to be conquered, due to his excessive pride, being very evil-minded.

shloka_text: जित्वा वैश्रवणं देवं कैलासात्समवातरत् ।। 7.15.44 ।।
explanation: Having conquered the god Vaiśravaṇa, he descended from Kailasa.

shloka_text: स्वतेजसा विपुलमवाप्य तं जयं प्रतापवान्विमलकिरीटहारवान् । रराज वै परमविमानमास्थितो निशाचरः सदसि गतो यथानलः ।। 7.15.45 ।।
explanation: Having achieved that great victory by his own prowess, the powerful night-prowler, adorned with a spotless crown and necklaces, shone brilliantly, seated in a magnificent aerial chariot, like fire entering an assembly.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः ।। 15 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred and glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the fifteenth canto in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: स जित्वा धनदं राम भ्रातरं राक्षसाधिपः । महासेनप्रसूतिं तद्ययौ शरवणं महत् ।। 7.16.1 ।।
explanation: O Rama, that king of Rakshasas, having conquered his brother Dhanada, then went to the great Sharavana, the birthplace of Mahasena.

shloka_text: अथापश्यदृशग्रीवो रौक्मं शरवणं महत् । गभस्तिजालसंवीतं द्वितीयमिव भास्करम् ।। 7.16.2 ।।
explanation: Then Daśagrīva saw a great golden thicket of arrows, enveloped in a network of rays, like a second sun.

shloka_text: स पर्वतं समारुह्य कञ्चिद्रम्यवनान्तरम् । अपश्यत् पुष्पकं तत्र रामविष्टम्भितं तदा ।। 7.16.3 ।।
explanation: Having climbed a certain mountain with a beautiful forest, he then saw the Pushpaka there, halted by Rama.

shloka_text: विष्टब्धं पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा ह्यगमं कामागं कृतम् । अचिन्तयद्राक्षसेन्द्रः सचिवैस्तैः समावृतः ।। 7.16.4 ।।
explanation: Having seen the Pushpaka, which was capable of moving at will, stopped and rendered motionless, the king of Rakshasas, surrounded by those ministers, pondered.

shloka_text: किन्निमित्तं चेच्छया मे नेदं गच्छति पुष्पकम् । पर्वतस्योपरिष्ठस्य कर्मेदं कस्यचिद्भवेत् ।। 7.16.5 ।।
explanation: For what reason does this Pushpaka not move according to my will? This must be the deed of someone on top of the mountain.

shloka_text: ततो ऽब्रवीत्तदा राम मारीचो बुद्धिकोविदः । नेदं निष्कारणं राजन्पुष्पकं यन्न गच्छति ।। 7.16.6 ।।
explanation: Then Maricha, the wise one, spoke to Rama at that time: "O King, it is not without reason that this Pushpaka does not go."

shloka_text: अथवा पुष्पकमिदं धनदान्नान्यवाहनम् । अतो निष्पन्दमभवद्धनाध्यक्षविनाकृतम् ।। 7.16.7 ।।
explanation: Or, this Pushpaka, no longer the vehicle of Dhanada, became motionless, being separated from the lord of wealth.

shloka_text: इति वाक्यान्तरे तस्य करालः कृष्णपिङ्गलः । वामनो विकटो मुण्डी नन्दी प्रह्वभुजो बली ।। 7.16.8 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the midst of his speech, Karala, Krishnapingala, Vamana, Vikata, Mundi, Nandi, Prahvabhuja (the one with bowed arms), and Bali (the strong one).

shloka_text: ततः पार्श्वमुपागम्य भवस्यानुचरो ऽब्रवीत् । नन्दीश्वरो वचश्चेदं राक्षसेन्द्रमशङ्कितः ।। 7.16.9 ।।
explanation: Then, Nandiśvara, the attendant of Bhava, having approached his side, fearlessly spoke this word to the king of Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: निवर्तस्व दशग्रीव शैले क्रीडति शङ्करः । सुपर्णनागयक्षाणां देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् ।। 7.16.10 ।।
explanation: Turn back, O Daśagrīva! Shankara plays on the mountain, (a place) of Suparṇas, Nāgas, Yakṣas, Devas, Gandharvas, and Rakṣasas.

shloka_text: सर्वेषामेव भूतानामगम्यः पर्वतः कृतः । इति नन्दिवचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधात्कम्पितकुण्डलः ।। 7.16.11 ।।
explanation: Having heard these words of Nandi, "The mountain has been made inaccessible to all beings," (he was) with earrings trembling from anger.

shloka_text: रोषात्तु ताम्रनयनः पुष्पकादवरुह्य सः । को ऽयं शङ्कर इत्युक्त्वा शैलमूलमुपागतः ।। 7.16.12 ।।
explanation: Red-eyed from anger, he descended from the Pushpaka, and saying, "Who is this Shankara?", approached the base of the mountain.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यन्नन्दिनं तत्र देवस्यादूरतः स्थितम् । दीप्तं शूलमवष्टभ्य द्वितीयमिव शङ्करम् ।। 7.16.13 ।।
explanation: He saw Nandin there, standing near the god, holding a blazing trident, as if he were a second Shankara.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा वानरमुखमवज्ञाय स राक्षसः । प्रहासं मुमुचे तत्र सतोय इव तोयदः ।। 7.16.14 ।।
explanation: Seeing that monkey-faced one, the demon, scorning him, burst into a loud laugh there, like a water-filled cloud.

shloka_text: तं क्रुद्धो भगवान्नन्दी शङ्करस्यापरा तनुः । अब्रवीत्तत्र तद्रक्षो दशाननमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.16.15 ।।
explanation: Enraged, Lord Nandi, another form of Shankara, spoke to that demon Ravana who was present there.

shloka_text: यस्माद्वानररूपं मामवज्ञाय दशानन । अशनीपातसङ्काशमपहासं प्रमुक्तवान् ।। 7.16.16 ।।
explanation: Because, O Daśānana, having scorned me in the form of a monkey, you let out a derisive laugh like the strike of a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तस्मान्मद्रूपसम्पन्ना मद्वीर्यसमतेजसः । उत्पत्स्यन्ति वधार्थं हि कुलस्य तव वानराः ।। 7.16.17 ।।
explanation: Therefore, monkeys endowed with my form and possessing might and splendor equal to mine will indeed be born for the destruction of your lineage.

shloka_text: नखदंष्ट्रायुधाः क्रूरा मनःसम्पातरंहसः । युद्धोन्मत्ता बलोद्रिक्ताः शैला इव विसर्पिणः ।। 7.16.18 ।।
explanation: Cruel, armed with claws and fangs, swift as the flight of the mind, maddened by battle, overflowing with strength, advancing like mountains.

shloka_text: ते तव प्रबलं दर्पमुत्सेधं च पृथग्विधम् । व्यपनेष्यन्ति सम्भूय सहामात्यसुतस्य च ।। 7.16.19 ।।
explanation: They, having assembled, will remove your strong pride and diverse haughtiness, along with your ministers and sons.

shloka_text: किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं हन्तुं त्वां हे निशाचर । न हन्तव्यो हतस्त्वं हि पूर्वमेव स्वकर्मभिः ।। 7.16.20 ।।
explanation: But now, O night-wanderer, how can I kill you? You are not to be killed, for you have already been slain by your own deeds.

shloka_text: इत्युदीरितवाक्ये तु देवे तस्मिन्महात्मनि । देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता ।। 7.16.21 ।।
explanation: When those words were thus spoken by that great-souled god, divine drums sounded, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky.

shloka_text: अचिन्तयित्वा स तदा नन्दिवाक्यं महाबलः । पर्वतं तु समासाद्य वाक्यमाह दशाननः ।। 7.16.22 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty Daśānana, without considering Nandi's words, approached the mountain and spoke.

shloka_text: पुष्पकस्य गतिश्छिन्ना यत्कृते मम गच्छतः । तमिमं शैलमुन्मूलं करोमि तव गोपते ।। 7.16.23 ।।
explanation: The movement of Pushpaka, by which I was going, has been obstructed. This mountain, I will uproot it for you, O Gopati.

shloka_text: केन प्रभावेण भवो नित्यं क्रीडति राजवत् । विज्ञातव्यं न जानीते भयस्थानमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.16.24 ।।
explanation: By what power does Bhava always play like a king? He does not know the imminent danger that should be known.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा ततो राम भुजान्विक्षिप्य पर्वते । तोलयामास तं शीघ्रं स शैलं समकम्पत ।। 7.16.25 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, O Rama, then, spreading his arms on the mountain, he quickly began to lift it. That mountain trembled.

shloka_text: चालनात्पर्वतस्यैव गणा देवस्य कम्पिताः । चचाल पार्वती चापि तदा ऽ ऽश्लिष्टा महेश्वरम् ।। 7.16.26 ।।
explanation: From the shaking of the mountain itself, the gaṇas of the god trembled. Parvati also trembled then, clinging to Maheśvara.

shloka_text: ततो राम महादवो देवानां प्रवरो हरः । पादाङ्गुष्ठेन तं शैलं पीडयामास लीलया ।। 7.16.27 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, the great god, the foremost among the gods, Hara, playfully pressed that mountain with the big toe of his foot.

shloka_text: पीडितास्तु ततस्तस्य शैलस्याधोगता भुजाः । विस्मिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवास्तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.16.28 ।।
explanation: Then his arms, crushed, went beneath the mountain. And the ministers of that Rākṣasa became astonished there.

shloka_text: रक्षसा तेन रोषाच्च भुजानां पीडनात्तदा । मुक्तो विरावः सहसा त्रैलोक्यं येन कम्पितम् ।। 7.16.29 ।।
explanation: Then, by that Rakshasa, due to anger and the crushing of his arms, a sudden roar was let out, by which the three worlds were shaken.

shloka_text: मेनिरे वज्रनिष्पेषं तस्यामात्या युगक्षये । तदा वर्त्मस्थचलिता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः ।। 7.16.30 ।।
explanation: His ministers considered it a thunderbolt's strike at the dissolution of the age. Then the gods, led by Indra, were moved from their path.

shloka_text: समुद्राश्चापि सङ्क्षुब्धाश्चलिताश्चापि पर्वताः । यक्षा विद्याधराः सिद्धाः किमेतदिति चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.16.31 ।।
explanation: The oceans were agitated, and the mountains also moved. Yakshas, Vidyadharas, and Siddhas said, "What is this?"

shloka_text: अथ ते मन्त्रिणस्तस्य विक्रोशन्तमथाब्रुवन् । तोषयस्व महादेवं नीलकण्ठमुमापतिम् ।। 7.16.32 ।।
explanation: Then those ministers said to him who was crying out, "Propitiate Mahadeva, Nilakantha, the husband of Uma."

shloka_text: तमृते शरणं नान्यं पश्यामो ऽत्र दशानन । स्तुतिभिः प्रणतो भूत्वा तमेव शरणं व्रज ।। 7.16.33 ।।
explanation: O Daśānana, we see no other refuge here except for him. Having prostrated with praises, take refuge in him alone.

shloka_text: कृपालुः शङ्करस्तुष्टः प्रसादं ते विधास्यति । एवमुक्तस्तदामात्यैस्तुष्टाव वृषभध्वजम् ।। 7.16.34 ।।
explanation: The compassionate Shankara, being pleased, will bestow his grace upon you. Thus addressed by the ministers, he then praised the Bull-bannered one (Shiva).

shloka_text: सामभिर्विविधैः स्तोत्रैः प्रणम्य स दशाननः । संवत्सरसहस्रं तु रुदतो रक्षसो गतम् ।। 7.16.35 ।।
explanation: That Daśānana, having bowed down with various hymns and praises, a thousand years passed for the weeping demon.

shloka_text: ततः प्रीतो महादेवः शैलाग्रे विष्ठितः प्रभुः । मुक्त्वा चास्य भुजान्राम प्राह वाक्यं दशाननम् ।। 7.16.36 ।।
explanation: Then, the pleased Lord Mahadeva, situated on the mountain peak, having released his arms, O Rama, spoke words to Dashanana.

shloka_text: प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव वीर्यस्य शौण्डार्याच्च दशानन । शैलाक्रान्तेन यो मुक्तस्त्वया रावः सुदारुणः ।। 7.16.37 ।।
explanation: O Daśānana, I am pleased with your valor and heroism, and with that exceedingly terrible roar which was uttered by you when crushed by the mountain.

shloka_text: यस्माल्लोकत्रयं चैतद्रावितं भयमागतम् । तस्मात्त्वं रावणो नाम नाम्ना राजन्भविष्यसि ।। 7.16.38 ।।
explanation: Because of this, these three worlds have been made to flee and fear has come. Therefore, O King, you shall be known by the name Rāvaṇa.

shloka_text: देवता मानुषा यक्षा ये चान्ये जगतीतले । एवं त्वामभिधास्यन्ति रावणं लोकरावणम् ।। 7.16.39 ।।
explanation: Gods, humans, Yakshas, and any others on the earth will thus call you Ravana, the tormentor of the worlds.

shloka_text: गच्छ पौलस्त्य विस्रब्धं पथा येन त्वमिच्छसि । मया चैवाभ्यनुज्ञातो राक्षसाधिप गम्यताम् ।। 7.16.40 ।।
explanation: Go, O Paulastya, confidently by the path you desire. O king of Rakshasas, you are indeed permitted by me; depart.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशः शम्भुना स्वयमब्रवीत् । प्रीतो यदि महादेव वरं मे देहि याचतः ।। 7.16.41 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Shambhu himself, the lord of Lanka spoke: "If you are pleased, O Mahadeva, grant a boon to me who asks."

shloka_text: अवध्यत्वं मया प्राप्तं देवगन्धर्वदानवैः । राक्षसैर्गुह्यकैर्नागैर्ये चान्ये बलवत्तराः ।। 7.16.42 ।।
explanation: I have obtained invincibility from gods, gandharvas, danavas, rakshasas, guhyakas, nagas, and any others who are more powerful.

shloka_text: मानुषान्न गणे देव स्वल्पास्ते मम सम्मताः । दीर्घमायुश्च मे प्राप्तं ब्रह्मणस्त्रिपुरान्तक ।। 7.16.43 ।।
explanation: O god, I do not count humans; they are considered insignificant by me. And a long life has been obtained by me from Brahma, O Destroyer of Tripura.

shloka_text: वाञ्छितं चायुषः शेषं शस्त्रं त्वं च प्रयच्छ मे । एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन रावणेन स शङ्करः ।। 7.16.44 ।।
explanation: Grant me the desired remainder of my life and a weapon. Thus addressed by Ravana, then Shankara...

shloka_text: ददौ खड्गं महादीप्तं चन्द्रहासमिति श्रुतम् । आयुषश्चावशेषं च स्थित्वा भूतपतिस्तदा ।। 7.16.45 ।।
explanation: Then the lord of beings, having stood, gave the greatly radiant sword known as Chandrahāsa, and the remainder of life.

shloka_text: दत्त्वोवाच ततः शम्भुर्नावज्ञेयमिदं त्वया । अवज्ञातं यदि हि ते मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ।। 7.16.46 ।।
explanation: Having given, Shiva then said: "This should not be disregarded by you. For if it is disregarded by you, it will undoubtedly come back to me."

shloka_text: एवं महेश्वरेणैव कृतनामा स रावणः । अभिवाद्य महादेवमारुरोहाथ पुष्पकम् ।। 7.16.47 ।।
explanation: Thus, Ravana, having been named by Maheśvara himself, saluted Mahadeva and then ascended the Pushpaka.

shloka_text: ततो महीतले राम पर्यक्रामत रावणः । क्षत्ऺित्रयान्सुमहावीर्यान्बाधमान इतस्ततः ।। 7.16.48 ।।
explanation: Then, O Rama, Ravana roamed on the earth, harassing the exceedingly mighty Kshatriyas here and there.

shloka_text: केचित्तेजस्विनः शूराः क्षत्ऺित्रया युद्धदुर्मदाः । तच्छासनमकुर्वन्तो विनेशुः सपरिच्छदाः ।। 7.16.49 ।।
explanation: Some spirited and brave Kshatriyas, fierce in battle, not obeying his command, perished along with their retinue.

shloka_text: अपरे दुर्जयं रक्षो जानन्तः प्राज्ञसम्मताः । जिताः स्म इत्यभाषन्त राक्षसं बलदर्पितम् ।। 7.16.50 ।।
explanation: Others, esteemed by the wise, knowing the invincible Rakshasa, said to the demon, arrogant with strength, "We are defeated."

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः ।। 16 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the sixteenth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: अथ राजन्महाबाहुर्विचरन्स महीतले । हिमवद्वनमासाद्य परिचक्राम रावणः ।। 7.17.1 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed King Ravana, wandering on the surface of the earth, reached the forest of the Himalayas and roamed about.

shloka_text: तत्रापश्यत्स वै कन्यां कृष्णाजिनजटाधराम् । आर्षेण विधिना युक्तां दीप्यन्तीं देवतामिव ।। 7.17.2 ।।
explanation: There he saw a maiden, wearing a black deer skin and matted hair, observing ascetic rites, shining like a goddess.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां कन्यां तां सुमहाव्रताम् । काममोहपरीतात्मा पप्रच्छ प्रहसन्निव ।। 7.17.3 ।।
explanation: Having seen that beautiful and highly virtuous maiden, he, his mind overwhelmed by infatuation, asked with a smile.

shloka_text: किमिदं वर्तसे भद्रे विरुद्धं यौवनस्य ते । नहि युक्ता तवैतस्य रूपस्यैव प्रतिक्रिया ।। 7.17.4 ।।
explanation: O good lady, why are you behaving in this manner, which is contrary to your youth? Indeed, such an action is not suitable for your beauty.

shloka_text: रूपं ते ऽनुपमं भीरु कामोन्मादकरं नृणाम् । न युक्तं तपसि स्थातुं निर्गतो ह्येष निर्णयः ।। 7.17.5 ।।
explanation: O timid one, your incomparable form, which incites lustful madness in men, is not suitable for you to remain in penance. Indeed, this is the conclusion.

shloka_text: कस्यासि किमिदं भद्रे कश्च भर्ता वरानने । येन सम्भुज्यसे भीरु स नरः पुण्यभाग्भुवि ।। 7.17.6 ।।
explanation: Whose are you, O gentle lady? What is this? And who is your husband, O beautiful-faced one? That man by whom you are enjoyed, O timid one, is indeed fortunate on earth.

shloka_text: पृच्छतः शंस मे सर्वं कस्य हेतोः परिश्रमः । एवमुक्ता तु सा कन्या रावणेन यशस्विनी ।। 7.17.7 ।।
explanation: Tell me everything, to me who asks, for what reason is this exertion. Thus addressed by Ravana, that glorious maiden...

shloka_text: कुशध्वजो मम पिता ब्रह्मर्षिरमितप्रभः । बृहस्पतिसुतः श्रीमान्बुद्ध्या तुल्यो बृहस्पतेः ।। 7.17.8 ।।
explanation: My father, Kushadhvaja, is a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor. He is the glorious son of Brihaspati, equal to Brihaspati in intellect.

shloka_text: तस्याहं कुर्वतो नित्यं वेदाभ्यासं महात्मनः । सम्भूय वाङ्मयी कन्या नाम्ना वेदवती स्मृता ।। 7.17.9 ।।
explanation: To that great soul, who was constantly engaged in Vedic study, I was born as a daughter, a manifestation of speech, known by the name Vedavati.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः । ते ऽपि गत्वा हि पितरं वरणं रोचयन्ति मे ।। 7.17.10 ।।
explanation: Then the gods, along with the Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pannagas, they too, having gone to the father, approve of my selection.

shloka_text: न च मां स पिता तेभ्यो दत्तवान्राक्षसर्षभ । कारणं तद्वदिष्यामि निशाचर निशामय ।। 7.17.11 ।।
explanation: And that father did not give me to them, O best of Rākṣasas. I will tell you that reason, O night-wanderer, listen.

shloka_text: पितुस्तु मम जामाता विष्णुः किल सुरेश्वरः । अभिप्रेतस्त्रिलोकेशस्तस्मान्नान्यस्य मे पिता ।। 7.17.12 ।।
explanation: Vishnu, the lord of the gods, is indeed my father's son-in-law. He is the beloved lord of the three worlds; therefore, my father has no other.

shloka_text: दातुमिच्छति तस्मै तु तच्छ्रुत्वा बलदर्पितः । दम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितो ऽभवत् ।। 7.17.13 ।।
explanation: But having heard that he wished to give it to him, Dambhu, the king of the Daityas, proud of his strength, then became angry.
My father, sleeping at night, was killed by that wicked one.

shloka_text: ततो मे जननी दीना तच्छरीरं पितुर्मम । परिष्वज्य महाभागा प्रविष्टा हव्यवाहनम् ।। 7.17.15 ।।
explanation: Then my distressed mother, the illustrious one, embracing that body of my father, entered the fire.

shloka_text: ततो मनोरथं सत्यं पितुर्नारायणं प्रति । करोमीति तमेवाहं हृदयेन समुद्वहे ।। 7.17.16 ।।
explanation: Therefore, I shall fulfill my father's true desire concerning Narayana; that very desire I bear in my heart.

shloka_text: इति प्रतिज्ञामारुह्य चरामि विपुलं तपः । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं मया राक्षसपुङ्गव ।। 7.17.17 ।।
explanation: Thus, having undertaken this vow, I perform great penance. All this has been told by me to you, O best of Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: नारायणो मम पतिर्न त्वन्यः पुरुषोत्तमात् । आश्रये नियमं घोरं नारायणपरीप्सया । विज्ञातस्त्वं हि मे राजन्गच्छ पौलस्त्यनन्दन ।। 7.17.18 ।।
explanation: Narayana is my husband, not any other than Purushottama. I undertake a severe vow with the desire to obtain Narayana. You are indeed known to me, O King. Go, O delight of Pulastya.

shloka_text: जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते ।। 7.17.19 ।।
explanation: I know through penance everything that exists in the three worlds.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीद्रावणो भूयस्तां कन्यां सुमहाव्रताम् । अवरुह्य विमानाग्रात्कन्दर्पशरपीडितः ।। 7.17.20 ।।
explanation: Ravana, tormented by the arrows of Kama, descended from the top of his aerial chariot and spoke again to that highly virtuous maiden.

shloka_text: अवलिप्ता ऽसि सुश्रोणि यस्यास्ते मतिरीदृशी । वृद्धानां मृगशावाक्षि भ्राजते पुण्यसञ्चयः ।। 7.17.21 ।।
explanation: You are arrogant, O beautiful-hipped one, whose mind is of this kind. The accumulation of merit of the elders shines, O fawn-eyed one.

shloka_text: त्वं सर्वंगुणसम्पन्ना नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशम् । त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी भीरु यौवनं ते निवर्तते ।। 7.17.22 ।।
explanation: You, endowed with all virtues, should not speak like this. O most beautiful in the three worlds, O timid one, your youth is passing away.

shloka_text: अहं लङ्कापतिर्भद्रे दशग्रीव इति श्रुतः । तस्य मे भव भार्या त्वं भुङ्क्ष्व भोगान्यथासुखम् ।। 7.17.23 ।।
explanation: O gentle lady, I am known as Dashagriva, the lord of Lanka. Become my wife and enjoy pleasures as you please.

shloka_text: कश्च तावदसौ यं त्वं विष्णुरित्यभिभाषसे । वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च ।।
explanation: Who then is he whom you call Vishnu, by his valor, by his penance, by his enjoyment, and by his strength?

shloka_text: न मया स समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसे ऽङ्गने ।। 7.17.24 ।।
explanation: O good lady, O woman, he whom you desire is not equal to me.

shloka_text: इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु वेदवत्यथ सा ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.17.25 ।।
explanation: When he had thus spoken, Vedavati then said.

shloka_text: वै भोगेन च बलेन च ।। मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम् । त्रैलोक्याधिपति विष्णुं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् । त्वदृते राक्षसेन्द्रान्यः को ऽवमन्येत बुद्धिमान् ।। 7.17.26 ।।
explanation: Indeed, with enjoyment and with strength. That maiden said to the night-wanderer, "Never so! O king of demons, who else, being wise, would disrespect Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds, revered by all people, except for you?"

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तया तत्र वेदवत्या निशाचरः । मूर्धजेषु तदा कन्यां कराग्रेण परामृशत् ।। 7.17.27 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Vedavati there, the night-wanderer then seized the maiden by her hair with the tip of his hand.

shloka_text: ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन सा ऽच्छिनत् । असिर्भूत्वा करस्तस्याः केशांश्छिन्नांस्तदा ऽकरोत् ।। 7.17.28 ।।
explanation: Then Vedavati, enraged, cut off her hair with her hand. Her hand, having become a sword, then severed those hairs.

shloka_text: सा ज्वलन्तीव रोषेण दहन्तीव निशाचरम् । उवाचाग्निं समाधाय मरणाय कृतत्वरा ।। 7.17.29 ।।
explanation: She, blazing with anger as if burning up the demon, spoke, having prepared the fire, resolved for death.

shloka_text: धर्षितायास्त्वयानार्य न मे जीवितमिष्यते । रक्षस्तस्मात्प्रवेक्ष्यामि पश्यतस्ते हुताशनम् ।। 7.17.30 ।।
explanation: O ignoble one, I do not desire to live, having been violated by you. Therefore, O demon, I will enter the fire while you are watching.

shloka_text: यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहं त्वया पापात्मना वने । तस्मात्तव वधार्थं हि समुत्पत्स्ये ह्यहं पुनः ।। 7.17.31 ।।
explanation: Since I was indeed molested by you, the sinful one, in the forest, therefore, I shall indeed be born again for your death.

shloka_text: न हि शक्यं स्त्रिया हन्तुं पुरुषः पापनिश्चः । शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत् ।। 7.17.32 ।।
explanation: A man with wicked resolve cannot be killed by a woman. And if a curse were cast by me upon you, there would be a loss of my ascetic power.

shloka_text: यदि त्वस्ति मया किञ्चित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा । तस्मात्त्वयोनिजा साध्वी भवेयं धर्मिणः सुता ।। 7.17.33 ।।
explanation: If any good deed has been done by me, or any gift given, or any offering made, then may I become a virtuous daughter, not born from a womb, to a righteous man.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा प्रविष्टा सा ज्वलितं जातवेदसम् । पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः ।। 7.17.34 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, she entered the blazing fire. And from the sky, a divine shower of flowers fell all around.

shloka_text: पुनरेव समुद्भूता पद्मे पद्मसमप्रभा । तस्मादपि पुनः प्राप्ता पूर्ववत्तेन रक्षसा ।। 7.17.35 ।।
explanation: Once again, she, radiant like a lotus, emerged in a lotus. Even from there, she was again seized by that demon, just as before.

shloka_text: कन्यां कमलगर्भाभां प्रगृह्य स्वगृहं ययौ । प्रगृह्य रावणस्त्वेतां दर्शयामास मन्त्रिणे ।। 7.17.36 ।।
explanation: Having seized the girl, radiant like the inside of a lotus, he went to his own house. Ravana, having seized her, showed her to his minister.

shloka_text: लक्षणज्ञो निरीक्ष्यैव रावणं चैवमब्रवीत् । गृहस्थैषां हि सुश्रोणी त्वद्वधायैव दृश्यते ।। 7.17.37 ।।
explanation: The expert in characteristics, having observed Ravana, spoke thus: "Indeed, this beautiful-hipped woman dwelling among these (people) is seen to be for your destruction alone."

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ऽर्णवे राम तां प्रचिक्षेप रावणः । सा चैव क्षितिमासाद्य यज्ञायतनमध्यगा ।। 7.17.38 ।।
explanation: Having heard this, O Rama, Ravana cast her into the ocean. And she, reaching the earth, went into the midst of a sacrificial ground.

shloka_text: राज्ञो हलमुखोत्कृष्टा पुनरप्युत्थिता सती । सैषा जनकराजस्य प्रसूता तनया प्रभो । तव भार्या महाबाहो विष्णुस्त्वं हि सनातनः ।। 7.17.39 ।।
explanation: She, extracted by the ploughshare from the king, having risen again, is the daughter born to King Janaka, O Lord. She is your wife, O mighty-armed one, for you are indeed the eternal Vishnu.

shloka_text: पूर्वं क्रोधाहितः शत्रुर्यया ऽसौ निहतस्तथा । उपाश्रयित्वा शैलभस्तव वीर्यममानुषम् ।। 7.17.40 ।।
explanation: O Śailabha, previously, the enemy born of anger was slain by her, who thus resorted to your superhuman prowess.

shloka_text: एवमेषा महाभागा मर्त्येषूत्पत्स्यते पुनः । क्षेत्रे हलमुखोत्कृष्टे वेद्यामग्निशिखोपमा ।। 7.17.41 ।।
explanation: Thus, this greatly fortunate one will be born again among mortals, in a field ploughed by the tip of a plough, resembling a flame of fire on an altar.

shloka_text: एषा वेदवती नाम पूर्वमासीत्कृते युगे । त्रेतायुगमनुप्राप्य वधार्थं तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.17.42 ।।
explanation: This one, named Vedavati, was formerly in the Krita Yuga. Upon the arrival of the Treta Yuga, she was for the purpose of killing that demon.

shloka_text: उत्पन्ना मैथिलकुले जनकस्य महात्मनः । सीतोत्पन्ना तु सीतेति मानुषैः पुनरुच्यते ।। 7.17.43 ।।
explanation: Born in the family of the great-souled Janaka, she who was born from the furrow is indeed called Sita by humans.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः ।। 17 ।।
explanation: Here ends the seventeenth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic by Valmiki.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः । पुष्पकं तु समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् ।। 7.18.1 ।।
explanation: When Vedavati entered the fire, that Ravana, having ascended the Pushpaka, roamed the earth.

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः । उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु रावणः ।। 7.18.2 ।।
explanation: Then Ravana, having reached Uśīrabīja, saw King Marutta performing a sacrifice with the deities.

shloka_text: संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षाद्भ्राता बृहस्पतेः । याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्देवगणैर्वृतः ।। 7.18.3 ।।
explanation: The Brahmarshi named Samvarta, the direct brother of Brihaspati, a knower of Dharma, officiated at a sacrifice, surrounded by all the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद्रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम् । तिर्यग्योनिं समाविष्टास्तस्य दर्शनभीरवः ।। 7.18.4 ।।
explanation: But the gods, having seen that demon, who was unconquerable by virtue of the boon, and fearing his sight, entered into animal forms.

shloka_text: इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः । कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसश्च वरुणो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.5 ।।
explanation: Indra became a peacock, and Dharma-rāja a crow. The lord of wealth became a chameleon, and Varuna became a swan.

shloka_text: अन्येष्वपि गतेष्वेवं देवेष्वरिनिषूदन । रावणः प्राविशद्यज्ञं सारमेय इवाशुचिः ।। 7.18.6 ।।
explanation: O destroyer of enemies, when the gods had thus departed, Ravana entered the sacrifice like an unclean dog.

shloka_text: तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा वद ।। 7.18.7 ।।
explanation: Approaching that king, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, said, "Either give battle, or declare, 'I am defeated.'"

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम् । अपहासं ततो मुक्त्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.8 ।।
explanation: Then King Marutta asked him, "Who are you?" Thereupon, Ravana, bursting into scornful laughter, spoke.

shloka_text: अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव पार्थिव । धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम् ।। 7.18.9 ।।
explanation: O King, I am pleased by your lack of curiosity, you who do not recognize me, Ravana, the younger brother of Dhanada.

shloka_text: त्रिषु लोकेषु को ऽन्यो ऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम् । भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम् । ततो मरुत्तः स नृपस्तं रावणमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.10 ।।
explanation: Who in the three worlds does not know my strength, by which I conquered my brother and seized this aerial chariot? Then King Marutta spoke to that Ravana.

shloka_text: धन्यः खलु भवान्येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः । न त्वया सदृशः श्लाध्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ।। 7.18.11 ।।
explanation: Fortunate indeed are you, who conquered your elder brother in battle. There is no one praiseworthy like you in the three worlds.

shloka_text: नाधर्मसहितं श्लाध्यं तल्लोकं प्रतिसंहितम् । कर्म दौरात्म्यकं कृत्वा श्लाघ्यसे भ्रातृनिर्जयात् ।। 7.18.12 ।।
explanation: That which is accompanied by unrighteousness is not praiseworthy in the world. Having performed a wicked deed, you boast by conquering your brothers.

shloka_text: क त्वं प्राक्केवलं धर्मं चरित्वा लब्धवान्वरम् । श्रूतपूर्वं हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम् ।। 7.18.13 ।।
explanation: Who are you, who, having practiced only righteousness previously, obtained a boon? For I have never heard before such things as you yourself speak.

shloka_text: तिष्ठेदानीं न मे जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि दुर्मते । अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम् ।। 7.18.14 ।।
explanation: Stop now, O evil-minded one! You will not return alive from me. Today, I shall send you to the abode of Yama with sharp arrows.

shloka_text: ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च नराधिपः । रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत् ।। 7.18.15 ।।
explanation: Then, taking his bow and arrows, the king, enraged, set out for battle. Samvarta blocked the path.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीत्स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः । श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं सम्प्रहारो न ते क्षमः ।। 7.18.16 ।।
explanation: That great sage spoke affectionately to Marutta: 'If my words are to be heeded, then battle is not advisable for you.'

shloka_text: माहेश्वरमिदं सत्रमसमाप्तं कुलं दहेत् ।। 7.18.17 ।।
explanation: This Maheśvara sacrifice, if left incomplete, would destroy the family.

shloka_text: दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः । संशयश्च जये नित्यं राक्षसश्च सुदुर्जयः ।। 7.18.18 ।।
explanation: How can there be war for one who is consecrated? How can there be anger in one who is consecrated? And there is always doubt about victory, and the demon is very difficult to conquer.

shloka_text: स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः । विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.19 ।।
explanation: King Marutta, having desisted at the guru's command, laid aside his bow with arrows, became calm, and prepared for the sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः । रावणो जयतीत्युच्चैर्हर्षान्नादं विमुक्तवान् ।। 7.18.20 ।।
explanation: Then, considering him defeated, Shuka proclaimed, "Ravana is victorious!" and loudly uttered a cry of joy.

shloka_text: तान्भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान्महर्षीन्यज्ञमागतान् । वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः सम्प्रययौ महीम् ।। 7.18.21 ।।
explanation: Having devoured those great sages who were present there, having come for the sacrifice, and being fully satisfied with their blood, he again went to the earth.

shloka_text: रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः । ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.18.22 ।।
explanation: When Ravana had departed, the gods, along with Indra and the celestial beings, then, having returned to their own forms, spoke to those creatures.

shloka_text: हर्षात्तदाब्रवीदिन्द्रो मयूरं नीलबर्हिणम् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजङ्गाद्धि न ते भयम् ।। 7.18.23 ।।
explanation: Then, Indra, with joy, said to the blue-plumed peacock: "I am pleased with you, O knower of dharma. Indeed, you shall have no fear from serpents."

shloka_text: इदं नेत्रसहस्रं तु यत्त्वद्बर्हे भविष्यति । वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणाम् । एवमिन्द्रो वरं प्रादान्मयूरस्य सुरेश्वरः ।। 7.18.24 ।।
explanation: These thousand eyes that will be on your tail-feathers, when I rain, you will experience joy, a sign of affection. Thus, Indra, the lord of gods, gave this boon to the peacock.

shloka_text: नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप । सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वे ऽपि बर्हिणः ।। 7.18.25 ।।
explanation: O king, it is said that formerly, the feathers of peacocks were blue. All peacocks, having obtained a boon from the lord of gods, became (so).

shloka_text: धर्मराजो ऽब्रवीद्राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं स्थितम् । पक्षिंस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य वचनं शृणु ।। 7.18.26 ।।
explanation: Dharmaraja said to Rama, (addressing) the crow situated in the eastern shed: "O bird, I am very pleased with you. Listen to the words of one who is pleased."

shloka_text: यथान्ये विविधै रोगै; पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया । ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः ।। 7.18.27 ।।
explanation: As other living beings are tormented by various diseases by me, they will not be able to affect them when I am pleased, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान्मम विहङ्गम । यावत्त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद्भविष्यसि ।। 7.18.28 ।।
explanation: There is no fear of death for you, O bird, by my boon. You will exist as long as men do not kill you.

shloka_text: एते मद्विषयस्था वै मानवाः क्षुद्भयार्दिताः । त्वयि भुक्ते तु तृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः ।। 7.18.29 ।।
explanation: These people in my domain, indeed, afflicted by the fear of hunger, will become satisfied along with their kinsmen when you are fed.

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविहारिणम् । श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं वचः पत्ररथेश्वर ।। 7.18.30 ।।
explanation: Varuna then spoke to the swan, sporting in the waters of the Ganga: "O lord of birds, listen to these affectionate words."

shloka_text: वर्णो मनोहरः सौम्यश्चन्द्रमण्डलसन्निभः । भविष्यति तवोदग्रः शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः ।। 7.18.31 ।।
explanation: Your complexion will be charming, gentle, resembling the disc of the moon, excellent, and radiant like pure foam.

shloka_text: मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि । प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम् ।। 7.18.32 ।।
explanation: By attaining my body, you will always be beloved. And you will obtain unequalled joy; this is my token of affection.

shloka_text: हंसानां हि पुरा राम नीलवर्णः सपाण्डुरः । पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः ।। 7.18.33 ।।
explanation: O Rama, formerly, the swans were indeed blue-colored with a pale hue. Their wings were tipped with blue, and their bellies were as pure as the tips of fresh grass.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः कृकलासं गिरौ स्थितम् । हैरण्यं सम्प्रयच्छामि वर्णं प्रीतस्तवाप्यहम् ।। 7.18.34 ।।
explanation: Then Vaiśravaṇa spoke to the chameleon situated on the mountain: "I am pleased with you, and I bestow upon you a golden color."

shloka_text: सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम् । एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति ।। 7.18.35 ।।
explanation: And your head will always be imperishable and opulent. This golden color will be yours by my favor.

shloka_text: एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन्यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः । निवृत्ताः सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः ।। 7.18.36 ।।
explanation: Thus, having given boons to them at that festival of sacrifice, the gods, along with the king, departed and returned to their own abodes.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टादशः सर्गः ।। 18 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the eighteenth chapter.

shloka_text: अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः । नगराणि नरेन्द्राणां युद्धकाङ्क्षी दशाननः ।। 7.19.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having conquered Marutta, that lord of Rakshasas, Dashanana, desirous of battle, proceeded to the cities of kings.

shloka_text: समासाद्य तु राजेन्द्रान्महेन्द्रवरुणोपमान् । अब्रवीद्राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु युद्धं मे दीयतामिति ।। 7.19.2 ।।
explanation: Having approached the kings, who were comparable to Mahendra and Varuna, the lord of Rākṣasas said, "Let battle be given to me."

shloka_text: निर्जिताः स्मेति वा ब्रूत एष मे हि सुनिश्चयः । अन्यथा कुर्वतामेवं मोक्षो नैवोपपद्यते ।। 7.19.3 ।।
explanation: Or say, 'We are conquered.' This is indeed my firm conviction. Otherwise, for those who act differently, liberation is certainly not possible.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वभीरवः प्राज्ञाः पार्थिवा धर्मनिश्चयाः । मन्त्रयित्वा ततो ऽन्योन्यं राजानः सुमहाबलाः । निर्जिताः स्मेत्यभाषन्त ज्ञात्वा वरबलं रिपोः ।। 7.19.4 ।।
explanation: Then, the fearless, wise kings, resolute in righteousness, the very mighty kings, having consulted among themselves, and having understood the enemy's superior strength, said, "We are defeated."

shloka_text: दुष्यन्तः सुरथो गाधिर्गयो राजा पुरूरवाः । एते सर्वे ऽब्रुवंस्तात निर्जिताः स्मेति पार्थिवाः ।। 7.19.5 ।।
explanation: Dushyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, King Gaya, and Pururavas – all these kings said, "O dear one, we have been defeated."

shloka_text: अथायोध्यां समासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.19.6 ।।
explanation: Then, having reached Ayodhya, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सुगुप्तामनरण्येन शक्रेणेवामरावतीम् । स तं पुरुषशार्दूलं पुरन्दरसमं बले ।। 7.19.7 ।।
explanation: Well-protected by Anaraṇya, like Amaravati by Indra. He, that tiger among men, equal to Purandara in strength.

shloka_text: प्राह राजानमासाद्य युद्धं देहीति रावणः । निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा ब्रूहि त्वमेवं मम शासनम् ।। 7.19.8 ।।
explanation: Having approached the king, Ravana said, 'Either give battle, or say, "I am defeated!" This is my command to you.'

shloka_text: अयोध्याधिपतिस्तस्य श्रुत्वा पापात्मनो वचः । अनरण्यस्तु सङ्क्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.19.9 ।।
explanation: The king of Ayodhya, Anaranya, having heard the words of that wicked soul, became greatly enraged and then spoke to the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: दीयते द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ते राक्षसाधिपते मया । सन्तिष्ठ क्षिप्रमायत्तो भव चैवं भवाम्यहम् ।। 7.19.10 ।।
explanation: O king of Rākṣasas, I offer you a duel. Prepare yourself quickly, and I too shall be ready.

shloka_text: अथ पूर्वं श्रुतार्थेन निर्जितं सुमहद्बलम् । निष्क्रामत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्य बलं रक्षोवधोद्यतम् ।। 7.19.11 ।।
explanation: Now, that very great army of the king, previously defeated, was marching forth, intent on killing the Rākṣasas, by the purpose that had been heard.

shloka_text: नागानां दशसाहस्रं वाजिनां नियुतं तथा । रथानां बहुसाहस्रं पत्तीनां च नरोत्तम ।। 7.19.12 ।।
explanation: Ten thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses, many thousands of chariots, and foot soldiers, O best among men.

shloka_text: महीं सञ्छाद्य निष्क्रान्तं सपदातिरथं रणे । ततः प्रवृत्तं सुमहद्युद्धं युद्धविशारद ।। 7.19.13 ।।
explanation: Having covered the earth, with infantry and chariots having emerged for battle, then a very great battle ensued, O expert in warfare.

shloka_text: अनरण्यस्य नृपते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चाद्भुतम् । तद्रावणबलं प्राप्य बलं तस्य महीपतेः ।। 7.19.14 ।।
explanation: Of King Anaranya and of the formidable lord of Rakshasas. Having encountered that army of Ravana, the strength of that king...

shloka_text: प्राणश्यत तदा सर्वं हव्यं हुतमिवानले । युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं कृत्वा विक्रममुत्तमम् ।। 7.19.15 ।।
explanation: Then all perished, like an oblation poured into the fire, having fought for a very long time and having displayed supreme valor.

shloka_text: प्रज्वलन्तं तमासाद्य क्षिप्रमेवावशेषितम् । प्राविशत्सङ्कुलं तत्र शलभा इव पावकम् । नश्यति स्म बलं तत्र हव्यं हुतमिवानले ।। 7.19.16 ।।
explanation: Approaching that blazing one, they were quickly consumed. The multitude entered there like moths into a fire. The army there was destroyed like an oblation offered into the fire.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्तन्नरेन्द्रस्तु नश्यमानं महाबलम् । महार्णवं समासाद्य वनापगशतं यथा ।। 7.19.17 ।।
explanation: That king saw that mighty army perishing, just as hundreds of forest rivers disappear upon reaching the great ocean.

shloka_text: ततः शक्रधनुःप्रख्यं धनुर्विस्फारयन्स्वयम् । आससाद नरेन्द्रस्तं रावणं क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.19.18 ।।
explanation: Then, the king, overcome with rage, himself drawing his bow resembling Indra's bow, approached that Ravana.

shloka_text: अनरण्येन ते ऽमात्या मारीचशुकसारणाः । प्रहस्तसहिता भग्ना व्यद्रवन्त मृगा इव ।। 7.19.19 ।।
explanation: By Anaranya, your ministers Maricha, Shuka, and Sarana, along with Prahasta, were defeated and fled like deer.

shloka_text: ततो बाणशतान्यष्टौ पातयामास मूर्धनि । तस्य राक्षसराजस्य इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनः ।। 7.19.20 ।।
explanation: Then, the delight of the Ikshvaku lineage showered eight hundred arrows on the head of that king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित् । वारिधारा इवाभ्रेभ्यः पतन्त्यो गिरिमूर्धनि ।। 7.19.21 ।।
explanation: His arrows, as they fell, caused no wound anywhere, just like streams of water falling from clouds onto a mountain peak.

shloka_text: ततो राक्षसराजेन क्रुद्धेन नृपतिस्तदा । तलेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि स रथान्निपपात ह ।। 7.19.22 ।।
explanation: Then, the enraged king of Rakshasas struck the king on the head with his palm, and he fell from the chariot.

shloka_text: स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलाङ्गः प्रवेपितः । वज्रदग्ध इवारण्ये सालो निपतितो यथा ।। 7.19.23 ।।
explanation: That king fell to the ground, his limbs trembling and greatly shaking, like a Sala tree struck by a thunderbolt and fallen in the forest.

shloka_text: तं प्रहस्याब्रवीद्द्रक्ष इक्ष्वाकुं पृथिवीपतिम् । किमिदानीं फलं प्राप्तं त्वया मां प्रति युद्ध्यता ।। 7.19.24 ।।
explanation: Laughing, the demon said to Ikshvaku, the king: "What fruit have you gained now by fighting against me?"

shloka_text: त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यान्नराधिप । शङ्के प्रसक्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम ।। 7.19.25 ।।
explanation: O king, there is no one in the three worlds who can challenge me. I suspect you are engrossed in pleasures and do not hear of my strength.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं ब्रुवतो राजा मन्दासुर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् । किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः ।। 7.19.26 ।।
explanation: To him speaking thus, the king, whose life was ebbing, said: "What can be done here? For time is indeed insurmountable."

shloka_text: नह्यहं निर्जितो रक्षस्त्वया चात्मप्रशंसिना । कालेनैव विपन्नो ऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान् ।। 7.19.27 ।।
explanation: O self-praising demon, I was not conquered by you. I am ruined by time alone, but you have become the instrument for me.

shloka_text: किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं प्राणपरिक्षये । नह्यहं विमुखी रक्षो युध्यमानस्त्वया हतः ।। 7.19.28 ।।
explanation: But what can I do now, with my life at an end? For I, fighting, was not killed by you, O Rakshasa, while turning my back.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकुपरिभावित्वाद्वचो वक्ष्यामि राक्षस । यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः ।। यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक्तदा सत्यं वचो ऽस्तु मे ।। 7.19.29 ।।
explanation: O demon, because of being honored by Ikshvaku, I will speak a word. If charity has been given, if oblations have been offered, if my penance has been well-performed, if the subjects have been properly protected, then let

shloka_text: उत्पत्स्यते कुले ह्यस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । रामो दाशरथिर्नाम यस्ते प्राणान्हरिष्यति ।। 7.19.30 ।।
explanation: In this lineage of the great-souled Ikshvakus, Rama, the son of Dasharatha, will be born, who will take your lives.

shloka_text: ततो जलधरोदग्रस्ताडितो देवदुन्दुभिः । तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता ।। 7.19.31 ।।
explanation: Then, the divine drum was struck with the intensity of a thundercloud. And when that curse was uttered, a shower of flowers fell from the sky.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम् । स्वर्गते च नृपे तस्मिन्राक्षसः सो ऽपसर्पत ।। 7.19.32 ।।
explanation: Then that king, O best of kings, went to the abode of heaven. And when that king had gone to heaven, that demon retreated.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः ।। 19 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by a sage.

shloka_text: ततो वित्रासयन्मर्त्यान्पृथिव्यां राक्षसाधिपः । आससाद घने तस्मिन्नारदं मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।। 7.20.1 ।।
explanation: Then, the lord of Rākṣasas, terrifying mortals on earth, met Nārada, the foremost among sages, in that dense place.

shloka_text: तस्याभिवादनं कृत्वा दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । अब्रवीत्कुशलं पृष्ट्वा हेतुमागमनस्य च ।। 7.20.2 ।।
explanation: Having offered salutations to him, Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, after inquiring about his welfare, then spoke of the reason for his arrival.

shloka_text: नारदस्तु महातेजा देवर्षिरमितप्रभः । अब्रवीन्मेघपृष्ठस्थो रावणं पुष्पके स्थितम् ।। 7.20.3 ।।
explanation: The greatly lustrous divine sage Nārada, of immeasurable splendor, situated on the back of a cloud, spoke to Rāvaṇa, who was in the Puṣpaka chariot.

shloka_text: राक्षसाधिपते सौम्य तिष्ठ विश्रवसः सुत । प्रीतो ऽस्म्यभिजनोपेतविक्रमैरूर्जितैस्तव ।। 7.20.4 ।।
explanation: O king of Rākṣasas, O gentle one, O son of Viśravas, stop! I am pleased by your mighty valor, which is accompanied by noble birth.

shloka_text: विष्णुना दैत्यघातैश्च गन्धर्वोरगधर्षणैः । त्वया समं विमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः ।। 7.20.5 ।।
explanation: He was greatly pleased by Vishnu, by the slaying of demons, by the subjugation of Gandharvas and Uragas, and by the conflicts with you.

shloka_text: किंचिद्वक्ष्यामि तावत्ते श्रोतव्यं श्रोष्यसे यदि । श्रुत्वा चानन्तरं कार्यं त्वया राक्षससत्तम । तन्मे निगदतस्तात समाधिं श्रवणे कुरु ।। 7.20.6 ।।
explanation: I will tell you something first, if you are willing to listen to what should be heard. And having heard it, O best among Rākṣasas, it must then be done by you. Therefore, O dear one, as I speak, apply your full attention to listening.

shloka_text: किमयं वध्यते तात त्वया ऽवध्येन दैवतैः । हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः ।। 7.20.7 ।। ्तम ।
explanation: Why is this one being killed by you, O father, who are not to be killed even by the gods? Indeed, this world is as good as dead when it has fallen under the sway of death.

shloka_text: देवदानवदैत्यानां यक्षगन्धर्वरक्षसाम् । अवध्येन त्वया लोकः क्लेष्टुं युक्तो न मानुषः ।। 7.20.8 ।।
explanation: It is not proper for you, who are unslayable by Devas, Danavas, Daityas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Rakshasas, to torment mankind.

shloka_text: नित्यं श्रेयसि सम्मूढं महद्भिर्व्यसनैर्वृतम् । हन्यात्कस्तादृशं लोकं जराव्याधिशतैर्युतम् ।। 7.20.9 ।।
explanation: Who would kill such a person, who is always bewildered about what is good, surrounded by great calamities, and afflicted by hundreds of old age and diseases?

shloka_text: तैस्तैरनिष्टोपगमैरजस्रं यत्र कुत्र कः । मतिमान्मानुषे लोके युद्धेन प्रणयी भवेत् ।। 7.20.10 ।।
explanation: Given the constant arrival of various misfortunes, what intelligent person in the human world, wherever he may be, would constantly be fond of war?

shloka_text: क्षीयमाणं दैवहतं श्रुत्पिपासाजरादिभिः । विषादशोकसम्मूढं लोकं त्वं क्षपयस्व मा ।। 7.20.11 ।।
explanation: Do not destroy this world, which is wasting away, struck by fate, afflicted by hunger, thirst, old age, and the like, and bewildered by dejection and sorrow.

shloka_text: पश्य तावन्महाबाहो राक्षसेश्वर मानुषम् । मूढमेवं विचित्रार्थं यस्य न ज्ञायते गतिः ।। 7.20.12 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed lord of Rākṣasas, just behold this human, so foolish and of strange purpose, whose course is not understood.

shloka_text: क्वचिद्वादित्रनृत्यादि सेव्यते मुदितैर्जनैः । रुद्यते चापरैरार्तैर्धाराश्रुनयनाननैः ।। 7.20.13 ।।
explanation: In some places, joyful people enjoy music, dance, and the like. And elsewhere, others, distressed, with faces and eyes streaming with tears, are weeping.

shloka_text: मातापितृसुतस्नेहैर्भार्याबन्धुमनोरमैः । मोहितो ऽयं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते ।। 7.20.14 ।।
explanation: This person, deluded by the affections for mother, father, and son, and by charming wife and relatives, is ruined and does not comprehend his own suffering.

shloka_text: अलमेनं परिक्लिश्य लोकं मोहनिराकृतम् । जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः ।। 7.20.15 ।।
explanation: Enough of tormenting this world, which is overcome by delusion. O gentle one, the mortal world has indeed been conquered by you, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: अवश्यमेभिः सर्वैश्च गन्तव्यं यमसादनम् । तन्निगृह्णीष्व पौलस्त्य यमं परपुरञ्जय ।। 7.20.16 ।।
explanation: Certainly, all these must go to the abode of Yama. Therefore, O son of Pulastya, O conqueror of enemy cities, subdue Yama.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्जिते जितं सर्वं भवत्येव न संशयः । एवमुक्तस्तु लङ्केशो दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । अब्रवीन्नारदं तत्र सम्प्रहस्याभिवाद्य च ।। 7.20.17 ।।
explanation: When he is conquered, everything is certainly conquered, without a doubt. Thus spoken to, the lord of Lanka, shining with his own splendor, laughed heartily, saluted Narada, and spoke to him there.

shloka_text: महर्षे देवगन्धर्वविहार समरप्रिय । अहं समुद्यतो गन्तुं विजयार्थं रसातलम् ।। 7.20.18 ।।
explanation: O great sage, who delights among gods and gandharvas, and is fond of battle! I am prepared to go to Rasatala for victory.

shloka_text: ततो लोकत्रयं जित्वा स्थाप्य नागान्सुरान्वशे । समुद्रममृतार्थं च मथिष्यामि रसालयम् ।। 7.20.19 ।।
explanation: Then, having conquered the three worlds and brought the Nagas and Suras under control, I will churn the ocean, the abode of waters, for nectar.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीदृशग्रीवं नारदो भगवानृषिः । क्व खल्विदानीं मार्गेण त्वया ह्यन्येन गम्यते ।। 7.20.20 ।।
explanation: Then the revered sage Nārada spoke to Daśagrīva: "Indeed, by which path are you going now, or by another?"

shloka_text: अयं खलु सुदुर्गम्यः प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति । मार्गो गच्छति दुर्धर्षो यमस्यामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.20.21 ।।
explanation: This path, indeed, is very difficult to traverse, leading to the city of the King of Ghosts. It is formidable, O destroyer of enemies, this path of Yama.

shloka_text: स तु शारदमेघाभं हासं मुक्त्वा दशाननः । उवाच कृतमित्येव वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.20.22 ।।
explanation: But Daśānana, letting out a laugh like an autumn cloud, merely said, 'It is done,' and then spoke these words.

shloka_text: तस्मादेवमहं ब्रह्मन् वैवस्वतवधोद्यतः । गच्छामि दक्षिणामाशां यत्र सूर्यात्मजो नृपः ।। 7.20.23 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Brahmana, I, intent on slaying Vaivasvata, go to the southern direction where the king, the son of Surya, resides.

shloka_text: मया हि भगवन्क्रोधात्प्रतिज्ञातं रणार्थिना । अवजेष्यामि चतुरो लोकपालानिति प्रभो ।। 7.20.24 ।।
explanation: Indeed, O Lord, by me, desiring battle, it has been vowed out of anger: 'I will conquer the four Lokapalas,' O Master.

shloka_text: तदिह प्रस्थितो ऽहं वै प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति । प्राणिसङ्क्लेशकर्तारं योजयिष्यामि मृत्युना ।। 7.20.25 ।।
explanation: Therefore, I am now proceeding to the city of the King of the Dead. I will deliver the tormentor of living beings to death.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवो मुनिं तमभिवाद्य च । प्रययौ दक्षिणामाशां प्रविष्टः सह मन्त्रिभिः ।। 7.20.26 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken, Dashagriva, after saluting that sage, departed towards the southern direction, accompanied by his ministers.

shloka_text: नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः । चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः ।। 7.20.27 ।।
explanation: Narada, the greatly effulgent chief among Brahmins, remained absorbed in meditation for a moment. He then pondered, like a smokeless fire.

shloka_text: येन लोकास्त्रयः सेन्द्राः क्लिश्यन्ते सचराचराः । क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मेण स कालो जेष्यते कथम् ।। 7.20.28 ।।
explanation: By which (Time), the three worlds, along with Indra and all moving and non-moving beings, are afflicted. When life is exhausted, how can that Time be conquered by righteousness?

shloka_text: स्वदत्तकृतसाक्षी यो द्वितीय इव पावकः । लब्धसञ्ज्ञा विजेष्यन्ते लोका यस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.20.29 ।।
explanation: He who is a witness to his own deeds, like a second fire; the people of that great soul, having gained understanding, will be victorious.

shloka_text: यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः । तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽसौ स्वयमेव गमिष्यति ।। 7.20.30 ।।
explanation: From whom the three worlds constantly flee, terrified, how will this king of Rākṣasas himself go to him?

shloka_text: यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा । त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं विजयिष्यते ।। 7.20.31 ।।
explanation: He who is the ordainer and the sustainer, and of both good and evil deeds; by whom the three worlds have been conquered, how will one conquer him?

shloka_text: अपरं किन्तु कृत्वायं विधानं संविधास्यति । कौतूहलसमुत्पन्नो यास्यामि यमसादनम् ।। 7.20.32 ।।
explanation: But what else will he do, having made this arrangement? Filled with curiosity, I will go to Yama's abode.

shloka_text: विमर्दं द्रष्टुमनयोर्यमराक्षसयोः स्वयम् ।। 7.20.33 ।।
explanation: To personally witness the conflict between these two, Yama and the Rākṣasa.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः ।। 20 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the twentieth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by the sage.

shloka_text: एवं सञ्चिन्त्य विप्रेन्दो जगाम लघुविक्रमः । आख्यातुं तद्यथावृत्तं यमस्य सदनं प्रति ।। 7.21.1 ।।
explanation: Having thus pondered, the chief of Brahmins went with swift steps towards Yama's abode to narrate what had transpired.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्स यमं तत्र देवमग्निपुरस्कृतम् । विधानमुपतिष्ठन्तं प्राणिनो यस्य यादृशम् ।। 7.21.2 ।।
explanation: He saw there Yama, the god, with Agni leading, executing the ordinance for living beings, whatever it might be for each.

shloka_text: स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम् । अब्रवीत्सुखमासीनमर्घ्यमावेद्य धर्मतः ।। 7.21.3 ।।
explanation: Yama, having seen the great sage Narada arrived there, and having offered arghya according to dharma, spoke to him as he was comfortably seated.

shloka_text: कच्चित्क्षेमं तु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति । किमागमनकृत्यं ते देवगन्धर्वसेवित ।। 7.21.4 ।।
explanation: O divine sage, I hope all is well? I hope dharma is not perishing? What is the purpose of your arrival, O you who are served by gods and Gandharvas?

shloka_text: अब्रवीत्तु तदा वाक्यं नारदो भगवानृषिः । श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि विधानं च विधीयताम् ।। 7.21.5 ।।
explanation: Then the divine sage Narada spoke this word: "Listen, I will explain, and let the procedure be carried out."

shloka_text: एष नाम्नो दशग्रीवः पितृराज निशाचरः । उपयाति वशं नेतुं विक्रमैस्त्वां सुदुर्जयम् ।। 7.21.6 ।।
explanation: This one, Daśagrīva by name, the king of the night-prowlers, approaches to bring you, the unconquerable one, under his control by his valor.

shloka_text: एतेन कारणेनाहं त्वरितो ह्यागतः प्रभो । दण्डप्रहरणस्याद्य तव किं नु भविष्यति ।। 7.21.7 ।।
explanation: Because of this reason, I have indeed come quickly, O Lord. What will be your fate today concerning the blow of the staff?

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दुरादंशुमन्तमिवोदितम् । ददृशुर्दीप्तमायान्तं विमानं तस्य रक्षसः ।। 7.21.8 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, from afar, they saw that Rakshasa's radiant aerial chariot approaching, shining like the risen sun.

shloka_text: तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः । कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.21.9 ।।
explanation: The mighty one, having illuminated that entire region with the splendor of that Pushpaka, approached near.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्स महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवस्ततस्ततः । प्राणिनः सुकृतं कर्म भुञ्जानांश्चैव दुष्कृतम् ।। 7.21.10 ।।
explanation: He, that mighty-armed Daśagrīva, saw everywhere living beings experiencing the results of their good deeds and also their evil deeds.

shloka_text: अपश्यत्सैनिकांश्चास्य यमस्यानुचरैः सह । यमस्य पुरुषैरुग्रैर्घोररूपैर्भयानकैः ।। 7.21.11 ।।
explanation: He saw his soldiers along with Yama's attendants, and with Yama's fierce, dreadful-looking, terrifying messengers.

shloka_text: ददर्श वध्यमानांश्च क्लिश्यमानांश्च देहिनः । क्रोशतश्च महानादं तीव्रनिष्टनतत्परान् ।। 7.21.12 ।।
explanation: He saw living beings being killed and tormented, and those crying out with a great sound, intensely engaged in lamentation.

shloka_text: कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणांश्च सारमेयैश्च दारुणैः ।। 7.21.13 ।।
explanation: and being eaten by worms and by fierce dogs.

shloka_text: क्षोत्रायासकरा वाचो वदतश्च भयावहाः । सन्तार्यमाणान्वैतरणीं बहुशः शोणितोदकाम् ।। 7.21.14 ।।
explanation: Words that are painful to the ears and fearful for the speaker, (cause them) to be repeatedly ferried across the Vaitarani river, whose waters are blood.

shloka_text: वालुकासु च तप्तासु तप्यमानान्मुहूर्मुहुः । असिपत्रवने चैव भिद्यमानानधार्मिकान् ।। 7.21.15 ।।
explanation: And in the hot sands, the unrighteous are tormented again and again; and indeed, in the forest of sword-leaves, they are being cut.

shloka_text: रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि । पानीयं याचमानांश्च तृषितान्क्षुधितानपि ।। 7.21.16 ।।
explanation: In Raurava, in the river of caustic water, and indeed on the razor-sharp streams, those who are thirsty and hungry, begging for water.

shloka_text: शवभूतान्कृशान्दीनान्विवर्णान्मुक्तमूर्धजान् । मलपङ्कधरान्दीनान्रूक्षांश्च परिधावतः ।। 7.21.17 ।।
explanation: Like corpses, emaciated, miserable, discolored, with disheveled hair, covered in dirt and mud, wretched, and running around unkempt.

shloka_text: ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः । कांश्चिच्च गृहमुख्येषु गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः । प्रमोदमानानद्राक्षीद्रावणः सुकृतैः स्वकैः ।। 7.21.18 ।।
