explanation: Ravana saw on the path hundreds and then thousands (of people). He also saw some in the principal houses, rejoicing with the sounds of singing and musical instruments, due to their own good deeds.

shloka_text: गौरसं गोप्रदातारो ह्यन्नं चैवान्नदायिनः । गृहांश्च गृहदातारः स्वकर्मफलमश्नतः ।। 7.21.19 ।।
explanation: Givers of milk and dairy products, givers of cows, and indeed givers of food, and givers of houses, enjoy the fruit of their own actions.

shloka_text: सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताभिः प्रमदाभिरलङ्कृतान् ।। 7.21.20 ।।
explanation: Adorned by women with gold, jewels, and pearls.

shloka_text: धार्मिकानपरांस्तत्र दीप्यमानान्स्वतेजसा । ददर्श सुमहाबाहू रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.21 ।।
explanation: There, the mighty-armed Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, saw other righteous ones, shining with their own splendor.

shloka_text: ततस्तान्भिद्यमानांश्च कर्मभिर्दुष्कृतैः स्वकैः । रावणो मोचयामास विक्रमेण बलाद्बली ।। 7.21.22 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty Ravana, by his valor and force, released them who were being tormented by their own wicked deeds.

shloka_text: प्राणिनो मोचितास्तेन दशग्रीवेण रक्षसा । सुखमापुर्मुहूर्तं ते ह्यतर्कितमचिन्तितम् ।। 7.21.23 ।।
explanation: The living beings, released by that demon Daśagrīva, attained happiness for a moment, which was indeed unexpected and unthought of.

shloka_text: प्रेतेषु मुच्यमानेषु राक्षसेन महीयसा । प्रेतगोपाः सुसङ्क्रुद्धा राक्षसेन्द्रमभिद्रवन् ।। 7.21.24 ।।
explanation: As the dead were being released by the mighty Rākṣasa, the guardians of the dead, greatly enraged, rushed towards the king of Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वदिग्भ्यः समुत्थितः । धर्मराजस्य योधानां शूराणां सम्प्रधावताम् ।। 7.21.25 ।।
explanation: Then a tumultuous sound arose from all directions, from the brave warriors of Dharmaraja as they rushed forth.

shloka_text: ते प्रासैः परिघैः शूलैर्मुसलैः शक्तितोमरैः । पुष्पकं समवर्षन्त शूराः शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.26 ।।
explanation: Hundreds of thousands of heroes showered the Pushpaka with spears, iron clubs, lances, maces, shaktis, and tomaras.

shloka_text: तस्यासनानि प्रासादान्वेदिकास्तोरणानि च । पुष्पकस्य बभञ्जुस्ते शीघ्रं मधुकरा इव ।। 7.21.27 ।।
explanation: They quickly shattered the seats, grand chambers, platforms, and archways of the Pushpaka, like bees.

shloka_text: देवनिष्ठानभूतं तद्विमानं पुष्पकं मृधे । भज्यमानं तथैवासीदक्षयं ब्रह्मतेजसा ।। 7.21.28 ।।
explanation: That Pushpaka aerial chariot, which was the abode of the gods, though being shattered in battle, remained indestructible due to the power of Brahman.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्या सुमहत्यासीत्तस्य सेना महात्मनः । शूराणामग्रयातऽणां सहस्राणि शतानि च ।। 7.21.29 ।।
explanation: The army of that great-souled one was innumerable and very great, comprising hundreds of thousands of foremost heroes.

shloka_text: ततो वृक्षैश्च शैलैश्च प्रासादानां शतैस्तथा । ततस्ते सचिवास्तस्य यथाकामं यथाबलम् । अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः ।। 7.21.30 ।।
explanation: Then, with trees, and with rocks, and also with hundreds of palaces, those great heroic ministers of his, and King Daśānana, fought according to their desire and strength.

shloka_text: ते तु शोणितदिग्धाङ्गाः सर्वशस्त्रसमाहताः । अमात्या राक्षसेन्द्रस्य चक्रुरायोधनं महत् ।। 7.21.31 ।।
explanation: But those ministers of the king of Rakshasas, with their bodies smeared with blood and wounded by all weapons, waged a great battle.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं ते महाभागा जघ्नुः प्रहरणैर्भृशम् । यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः ।। 7.21.32 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, those greatly glorious ministers of Yama and Ravana struck each other severely with weapons.

shloka_text: अमात्यांस्तांस्तु सन्त्यज्य यमयोधा महाबलाः । तमेव चाभ्यधावन्त शूलवर्षैर्दशाननम् ।। 7.21.33 ।।
explanation: And the mighty warriors of Yama, abandoning those ministers, rushed towards him, Daśānana, with showers of spears.

shloka_text: ततः शोणितदिग्धाङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः । फुल्लाशोक इवाभाति पुष्पके राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.21.34 ।।
explanation: Then, the king of Rākṣasas, his body smeared with blood and shattered by blows, appeared in the Puṣpaka like a blooming Aśoka tree.

shloka_text: स तु शूलगदापासाञ्छक्तितोमरसायकान् । मुसलानि शिलावृक्षान्मुमोचास्त्रबलाद्बली ।। 7.21.35 ।।
explanation: But that mighty one, with the power of his weapons, hurled spears, maces, nooses, javelins, iron clubs, arrows, pestles, stones, and trees.

shloka_text: तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम् । यमसैन्येषु तद्वर्षं पपात धरणीतले ।। 7.21.36 ।।
explanation: That exceedingly terrible shower of trees, stones, and weapons fell upon Yama's armies on the ground.

shloka_text: तांस्तु सर्वान्विनिर्भिद्य तदस्त्रमपहत्य च । जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसं घोरमेकं शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.21.37 ।।
explanation: Having shattered all of them and repelled that weapon, they, in hundreds of thousands, killed that one terrible demon.

shloka_text: परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मोघोत्करा इव । भिन्दिपालैश्च शूलैश्च निरुच्छ्वासमपोथयन् ।। 7.21.38 ।।
explanation: And all of them, surrounding him like a mountain (is assailed by) futile attacks, struck him breathless with spears and javelins.

shloka_text: विमुक्तकवचः क्रुद्धः सिक्तः शोणितविस्रवैः । ततः स पुष्पकं त्यक्त्वा पृथिव्यामवतिष्ठत ।। 7.21.39 ।।
explanation: His armor discarded, enraged, drenched in streams of blood, he then abandoned the Pushpaka and stood upon the earth.

shloka_text: ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्तत । लब्धसञ्ज्ञो मुहूर्तेन क्रुद्धस्तस्थौ यथान्तकः ।। 7.21.40 ।।
explanation: Then he, the archer, and his voice advanced in battle. Having regained consciousness in a moment, he stood enraged like Death.

shloka_text: ततः पाशुपतं दिव्यमस्त्रं सन्धाय कार्मुके । तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं विचकर्ष स ।। 7.21.41 ।।
explanation: Then, having fixed the divine Pāśupata weapon on his bow, and saying to them, 'Stop! Stop!', he drew that bow.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ चापमिन्द्रारिराहवे । मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शङ्करो यथा ।। 7.21.42 ।।
explanation: Then, that enemy of Indra, enraged, having drawn his bow up to his ear in battle, released that arrow, just as Shankara did at Tripura.

shloka_text: तस्य रूपं शरस्यासीत्विधूमज्वालमण्डलम् । वनं दहिष्यतो घर्मे दावाग्नेरिव मूर्च्छतः ।। 7.21.43 ।।
explanation: The form of his arrow was a mass of smokeless flames, like a forest fire raging in summer, about to consume the forest.

shloka_text: ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे । मुक्तो गुल्मान्द्रुमांश्चापि भस्म कृत्वा प्रधावति ।। 7.21.44 ।।
explanation: That fiery arrow, accompanied by flesh-eaters in battle, when released, reduces shrubs and trees to ashes and rushes forth.

shloka_text: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु । रणे तस्मिन्निपतिता दावदग्धा नगा इव ।। 7.21.45 ।।
explanation: His armies, consumed by his might, fell in that battle like trees burnt by a forest fire.

shloka_text: ततस्तु सिचवैः सार्धं राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः । ननाद सुमहानादं कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम् ।। 7.21.46 ।।
explanation: Then, with his companions, the demon of terrible prowess roared a very great roar, as if shaking the earth.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः ।। 21 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the first epic poem by the glorious Valmiki, this is the twenty-first chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: स तस्य तु महानादं श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतः प्रभुः । शत्रुं विजयिनं मेने स्वबलस्य च सङ्क्षयम् ।। 7.22.1 ।।
explanation: Upon hearing his great roar, Lord Vaivasvata considered the enemy victorious and his own army annihilated.

shloka_text: स हि योधान्हतान्मत्वा क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः । अब्रवीत्त्वरितं सूतं रथो ऽयमुपनीयताम् ।। 7.22.2 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he, thinking the warriors slain, with eyes reddened by anger, quickly said to the charioteer, "Let this chariot be brought forth."

shloka_text: तस्य सूतस्तदा दिव्यमुपस्थाप्य महारथम् । स्थितः स च महातेजा ह्यध्यारोहत तं रथम् । प्राशमुद्गरहस्तश्च मृत्युस्तस्याग्रतः स्थितः ।। 7.22.3 ।।
explanation: His charioteer then brought forth the divine great chariot, and that greatly effulgent one mounted that chariot. Death, with a spear and a mace in hand, stood before him.

shloka_text: येन सङ्क्षिप्यते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यमिदमव्ययम् । कालदण्डस्तु पार्श्वस्थो मूर्तिमानस्य चाभवत् । यमप्रहरणं दिव्यं तेजसा ज्वलदग्निमत् ।। 7.22.4 ।।
explanation: By whom all these imperishable three worlds are brought to an end. The staff of Time, personified, stood by his side, a divine weapon of Yama, blazing with splendor and fire.

shloka_text: तस्य पार्श्वेषु निच्छिद्राः कालपाशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।। 7.22.5 ।।
explanation: On his sides, unbroken nooses of time were fixed.

shloka_text: पावकस्पर्शसङ्काशः स्थितो मूर्तश्च मुद्गरः ।। 7.22.6 ।।
explanation: A mace, whose touch was like fire, stood embodied.

shloka_text: ततो लोकत्रयं क्षुब्धमकम्पन्त दिवौकसः । कालं दृष्ट्वा तथा क्रुद्धं सर्वलोकभयावहम् ।। 7.22.7 ।।
explanation: Then the three worlds were agitated, and the gods trembled, having seen Time thus enraged, terrifying to all worlds.

shloka_text: ततः प्रचोदयन्सूतस्तानश्वान्रुचिरप्रभान् । प्रययौ भीमसन्नादो यत्र रक्षःपतिः स्थितः ।। 7.22.8 ।।
explanation: Then, the charioteer, driving those splendid-looking horses, proceeded with a terrible roar to where the lord of the Rākṣasas was situated.

shloka_text: मुहूर्तेन यमं ते तु हया हरिहयोपमाः । प्रापयन्मनसस्तुल्या यत्र तत्प्रस्तुतं रणम् ।। 7.22.9 ।।
explanation: In a moment, those horses, swift as thought and like the horses of Indra, brought death to the commenced battle.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तथैव विकृतं रथं मृत्युसमन्वितम् । सचिवा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सहसा विप्रदुद्रुवुः ।। 7.22.10 ।।
explanation: Seeing the chariot thus disfigured and accompanied by death, the ministers of the king of the Rākṣasas suddenly fled.

shloka_text: लघुसत्त्वतया ते हि नष्टसञ्ज्ञा भयार्दिताः । नेह योद्धुं समर्थाः स्म इत्युक्त्वा प्रययुर्दिशः ।। 7.22.11 ।।
explanation: Indeed, being of weak spirit, they, bewildered and tormented by fear, said, 'We are not able to fight here,' and fled in all directions.

shloka_text: स तु तं तादृशं दृष्ट्वा रथं लोकभयावहम् । नाक्षुभ्यत दशग्रीवो न चापि भयमाविशत् ।। 7.22.12 ।।
explanation: But Dashagriva, having seen that chariot, which was so terrifying to the world, neither became agitated nor did fear enter him.

shloka_text: स तु रावणमासाद्य व्यसृजच्छक्तितोमरान् । यमो मर्माणि सङ्क्रुद्धो रावणस्योपकृन्तत ।। 7.22.13 ।।
explanation: He, having approached Ravana, discharged shaktis and tomaras. Yama, greatly enraged, pierced Ravana's vital parts.

shloka_text: रावणस्तु ततः स्वस्थः शरवर्षं मुमोच ह । तस्मिन्वैवस्वतरथे तोयवर्षमिवाम्बुदः ।। 7.22.14 ।।
explanation: Then Rāvaṇa, having recovered, released a shower of arrows, like a cloud raining water on that chariot of Vaivasvata.

shloka_text: ततो महाशक्तिशरैः पात्यमानैर्महोरसि (पात्यमानो) । नाशक्नोत्प्रतिकर्तुं स राक्षसः शल्यपीडितः ।। 7.22.15 ।।
explanation: Then, as arrows of great power struck his mighty chest, that demon, tormented by the shafts, was unable to retaliate.

shloka_text: एवं नानाप्रहरणैर्यमेनामित्रकर्षिणा । सप्तरात्रं कृतः सङ्ख्ये विसञ्ज्ञो विमुखो रिपुः ।। 7.22.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, with various weapons, by the destroyer of enemies, the foe was rendered unconscious and turned away in battle for seven nights.

shloka_text: तदासीत्तुमुलं युद्धं यमराक्षसयोर्द्वयोः । जयमाकाङ्क्षतोर्वीर समरेष्वनिवर्तिनोः ।। 7.22.17 ।।
explanation: Then there was a tumultuous battle between Yama and the Rākṣasa, the two heroes, both desiring victory and unyielding in battles.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः । प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य समेतास्तद्रणाजिरम् ।। 7.22.18 ।।
explanation: Then the gods, along with Gandharvas, Siddhas, and great sages, with Prajapati at their head, assembled at that battlefield.

shloka_text: संवर्त इव लोकानां क्रुध्यतोरभवत्तदा । राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य प्रेतानामीश्वरस्य च ।। 7.22.19 ।।
explanation: Then, when the chief of the Rākṣasas and the lord of the Pretas became enraged, it was like the dissolution of the worlds.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽपि विस्फार्य चापमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम् । निरन्तरमिवाकाशं कुर्वन्बाणांस्ततो ऽसृजत् ।। 7.22.20 ।।
explanation: The lord of the Rākṣasas also, having drawn his bow which shone like Indra's thunderbolt, then discharged arrows, as if making the sky continuous.

shloka_text: मृत्युं चतुर्भिर्विशिखैः सूतं सप्तभिरार्दयत् । यमं शतसहस्रेण शीघ्रं मर्मस्वताडयत् ।। 7.22.21 ।।
explanation: He wounded Death with four arrows and the charioteer with seven. He quickly struck Yama in his vital spots with a hundred thousand (arrows).

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धस्य वदनाद्यमस्य समजायत । ज्वालामाली सनिःश्वासः सधूमः कोपपावकः ।। 7.22.22 ।।
explanation: Then, from the face of the enraged Yama, arose the fire of wrath, wreathed in flames, accompanied by breath and smoke.

shloka_text: तदाश्चर्यमथो दृष्ट्वा देवदानवसन्निधौ । प्रहर्षितौ सुसंरब्धौ मृत्युकालौ बभूवतुः ।। 7.22.23 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen that wonder in the presence of gods and demons, Death and Time became greatly delighted and highly agitated.

shloka_text: ततो मृत्युः क्रुद्धतरो वैवस्वतमभाषत । मुञ्च मां समरे यावद्धन्मीमं पापराक्षसम् । नैषा रक्षो भवेदद्य मर्यादा हि निसर्गतः ।। 7.22.24 ।।
explanation: Then Death, extremely enraged, spoke to Vaivasvata (Yama): "Release me in battle so that I may kill this sinful demon. This protection (or limit) should not exist today, for it is against the natural order."

shloka_text: हिरण्यकशिपुः श्रीमान्नमुचिः शम्बरस्तथा । विसन्धिर्धूमकेतुश्च बलिर्वैरोचनो ऽपि च ।। 7.22.25 ।।
explanation: The glorious Hiranyakashipu, Namuchi, Shambara, Visandhi, Dhumaketu, and Bali, the son of Virochana.

shloka_text: दम्भुर्दैत्यमहाराजो वृत्रो बाणस्तथैव च । राजर्षयः शास्त्रविदो गन्धर्वाः समहोरगाः ।। 7.22.26 ।।
explanation: Dambhu, the great king of Daityas, Vritra, and Bana, and similarly, royal sages who know the scriptures, Gandharvas, and great serpents.

shloka_text: ऋषयः पन्नगा दैत्या यक्षाश्चाप्यप्सरोगणाः । युगान्तपरिवर्ते च पृथिवी समहार्णवा ।। 7.22.27 ।।
explanation: Sages, serpents, Daityas, and also Yakshas and groups of Apsaras, and the Earth with its great oceans, at the change of the yuga's end.

shloka_text: क्षयं नीता महाराज सपर्वतसरिद्द्रुमा । एते चान्ये च बहवो बलवन्तो दुरासदाः ।। 7.22.28 ।।
explanation: O great king, along with mountains, rivers, and trees, these and many other powerful, formidable ones have been brought to destruction.

shloka_text: विनिपन्ना मया दृष्टाः किमुतायं निशाचरः ।। 7.22.29 ।।
explanation: Many have been seen by me fallen; what then of this night-wanderer?

shloka_text: मुञ्चं मां साधु धर्मज्ञ यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम् । नहि कश्चिन्मया दृष्टो बलवानपि जीवति ।। 7.22.30 ।।
explanation: Release me, O righteous one, until I kill him. For no one, however powerful, whom I have seen, survives.

shloka_text: बलं मम न खल्वेतन्मर्यादैषा निसर्गतः । स दृष्टो न मया कालं मुहुर्तमापि जीवति ।। 7.22.31 ।।
explanation: This is not my strength, but a natural law. He whom I have seen does not live even for a moment.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मराजः प्रतापवान् । अब्रवीत्तत्र तं मुत्युं त्वं तिष्ठैनं निहन्म्यहम् ।। 7.22.32 ।।
explanation: Having heard such words from him, the mighty Dharma-rāja said there to that Death, "You stand still, I will kill him."

shloka_text: ततः संरक्तनयनः क्रुद्धो वैवस्वतः प्रभुः । कालदण्डममोघं तु तोलयामास पाणिना ।। 7.22.33 ।।
explanation: Then, the enraged Lord Vaivasvata, with blood-red eyes, weighed his infallible Rod of Time in his hand.

shloka_text: यस्य पार्श्वेषु निखिला कालपाशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । पावकाशनिसङ्काशो मुद्गरो मूर्तिमान्स्थितः ।। 7.22.34 ।।
explanation: On whose sides all the nooses of time are fixed. An embodied mace, resembling fire and lightning, stands.

shloka_text: दर्शनादेव यः प्राणान्प्राणिनामपकर्षति । किं पुनः स्पृश्यमानस्य पात्यमानस्य वा पुनः ।। 7.22.35 ।।
explanation: He who takes away the lives of creatures merely by his sight, how much more so for one who is being touched or struck down?

shloka_text: स ज्वालापरिवारस्तु निर्दहन्निव राक्षसम् । तेन स्पृष्टो बलवता महाप्रहरणो ऽस्फुरत् ।। 7.22.36 ।।
explanation: That great weapon, surrounded by flames and as if burning the demon completely, flashed when struck by the powerful one.

shloka_text: ततो विदुद्रुवुः सर्वे तस्मात्रस्ता रणाजिरे । सुराश्च क्षुभिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा दण्डोद्यतं यमम् ।। 7.22.37 ।।
explanation: Then all, terrified, fled from him in the battlefield. And all the gods were agitated upon seeing Yama with his staff uplifted.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रहर्तुकामे तु यमे दण्डेन रावणम् । यमं पितामहः साक्षाद्दर्शयित्वेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.22.38 ।।
explanation: When Yama was about to strike Ravana with his mace, the Grandfather (Brahma) himself appeared before Yama and spoke thus.

shloka_text: वैवस्वत महाबाहो न खल्वमितविक्रम । न हन्तव्यस्त्वया तेन दण्डेनैव निशाचरः ।। 7.22.39 ।।
explanation: O Vaivasvata, O mighty-armed one, O one of immeasurable valor, indeed, that night-wanderer should not be slain by you with that very rod.

shloka_text: वरः खलु मयैतस्मै दत्तस्त्रिदशपुङ्गव । स त्वया नानृतः कार्यो यन्मया व्याहृतं वचः ।। 7.22.40 ।।
explanation: O best among the gods, a boon was indeed given by me to him. That word which I have spoken should not be made false by you.

shloka_text: यो हि मामनृतं कुर्याद्देवो वा मानुषो ऽपि वा । त्रैलोक्यमनृतं तेन कृतं स्यान्नात्र संशयः ।। 7.22.41 ।।
explanation: Whoever, be it a god or a human, would make me false, by him the three worlds would be made false; there is no doubt in this.

shloka_text: क्रुद्धेन विप्रमुक्तो ऽयं निर्विशेषं प्रियाप्रिये । प्रजाः संहरते रौद्रो लोकत्रयभयावहः ।। 7.22.42 ।।
explanation: Released by the enraged one, this terrible being indiscriminately destroys creatures, making no distinction between the dear and the not-dear, and causes fear to the three worlds.

shloka_text: अमोघो ह्येष सर्वेषां प्राणिनाममितप्रभः । कालदण्डो मया सृष्टः पूर्वं मृत्युपुरस्कृतः ।। 7.22.43 ।।
explanation: Indeed, this unfailing rod of Time, of immeasurable power, led by Death, was created by me long ago for all living beings.

shloka_text: तन्न खल्वेष ते सौम्य पात्यो रावणमूर्धनि । नह्यस्मिन्पतिते कश्चिन्मुहूर्तमपि जीवति ।। 7.22.44 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O gentle one, this (arrow) of yours should certainly not be dropped on Ravana's head. For if it falls, no one will live even for a moment.

shloka_text: यदि ह्यन्मिन्निपतिते न म्रियेतैष राक्षसः । म्रियते वा दशग्रीवस्तदाप्युभयतो ऽनृतम् ।। 7.22.45 ।।
explanation: If indeed this demon does not die when struck down, or if Dashagriva dies, then in both cases, it is a falsehood.

shloka_text: तन्निवर्तय लङ्केशं द्दण्डमेतं समुद्यतम् । सत्यं च मां कुरुष्वाद्य लोकांस्त्वं यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.22.46 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Lord of Lanka, avert this raised punishment. And make my words true today, if you care for the worlds.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मात्मा प्रत्युवाच यमस्तदा । एष व्यावर्तितो दण्डः प्रभविष्णुर्हि नो भवान् ।। 7.22.47 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, the righteous Yama then replied: "This punishment has been averted, for you are indeed our master."

shloka_text: किं न्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं रणगतेन हि । न मया यद्ययं शक्यो हन्तुं वरपुरस्कृतः ।। 7.22.48 ।।
explanation: What indeed can be done by me now, who has entered the battle, if this one, protected by boons, cannot be killed by me?

shloka_text: एष तस्मात्प्रणश्यामि दर्शनादस्य रक्षसः । इत्युक्त्वा सरथः साश्वस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।। 7.22.49 ।।
explanation: "I will disappear from the sight of this demon." Having said this, he, along with his chariot and horses, vanished right there.

shloka_text: दशग्रीवस्तु तं जित्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः । आरुह्य पुष्पकं भूयो निष्क्रान्तो यमसादनात् ।। 7.22.50 ।।
explanation: Dashagriva, having conquered him and having proclaimed his own name, again ascended the Pushpaka and departed from Yama's abode.

shloka_text: स तु वैवस्वतो देवैः सह ब्रह्मपुरोगमैः । जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टो नारदश्च महामुनिः ।। 7.22.51 ।।
explanation: And that Vaivasvata, delighted, went to heaven with the gods headed by Brahma, and the great sage Narada also went.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः ।। 22 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the twenty-second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: ततो जित्वा दशग्रीवो यमं त्रिदशपुङ्गवम् । रावणस्तु रणश्लाघी स्वसहायान्ददर्श ह ।। 7.23.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having conquered Yama, the chief among the gods, Ravana, who gloried in battle, indeed saw his companions.

shloka_text: ततो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम् । रावणं राक्षसा दृष्ट्वा ह्यष्टवत् समुपागमन् ।। 7.23.2 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen Ravana, whose body was soaked in blood and shattered by blows, the Rakshasas approached him as if lost.

shloka_text: जयेन वर्धयित्वा च मारीचप्रमुखास्ततः । पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु ।। 7.23.3 ।।
explanation: And having celebrated the victory, then all of them, led by Maricha, comforted by Ravana, boarded the Pushpaka.

shloka_text: ततो रसातलं गच्छन् प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम् । दैत्योरगगणाध्युष्टं वरुणेन सुरक्षितम् ।। 7.23.4 ।।
explanation: Then, going to Rasatala, he entered the abode of waters, inhabited by hosts of Daityas and Uragas, and well-protected by Varuna.

shloka_text: स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम् । कृत्वा नागान्वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम् ।। 7.23.5 ।।
explanation: He, however, having gone to Bhogavati, the city protected by Vasuki, and having brought the Nagas under his control, joyfully went to the gem-studded city.

shloka_text: निवातकवचास्तत्र दैत्या लब्धवरा वसन् । राक्षसान्तान्समागम्य युद्धाय समुपाह्वयत् ।। 7.23.6 ।।
explanation: The Nivātakavaca Daityas, who had obtained boons, resided there. Having approached the Rākṣasas for their destruction, they challenged them to battle.

shloka_text: ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः । नानाप्रहरणास्तत्र प्रहृष्टा युद्धदुर्मदाः ।। 7.23.7 ।।
explanation: All those Daityas, exceedingly valorous and mighty, armed with various weapons, were delighted there and irresistible in battle.

shloka_text: शूलैस्त्रिशूलैः कुलिशैः पट्टिशासिपरश्वधैः । अन्योन्यं बिभिदुः क्रुद्धा राक्षसा दानवास्तथा ।। 7.23.8 ।।
explanation: With spears, tridents, thunderbolts, paṭṭiśas, swords, and axes, the enraged Rākṣasas and Dānavas pierced each other.

shloka_text: तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः । न चान्यतरयोस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयो ऽपि वा ।। 7.23.9 ।।
explanation: While they were fighting, more than a year passed. And there was neither victory nor destruction for either of them.

shloka_text: ततः पितामहस्तत्र त्रैलोक्यगतिरव्ययः । आजगाम द्रुतं देवो विमानवरमास्थितः ।। 7.23.10 ।।
explanation: Then, the imperishable Grandfather, the divine one who moves through the three worlds, swiftly arrived there, seated in the best of aerial chariots.

shloka_text: निवातकवचानां तु निवार्य रणकर्म तत् । वृद्धः पितामहो वाक्यमुवाच विदितार्थवत् ।। 7.23.11 ।।
explanation: The aged grandfather, having stopped that warfare of the Nivātakavacas, spoke a meaningful word.

shloka_text: नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः । न भवन्तः क्षयं नेतुमपि सामरदानवैः ।। 7.23.12 ।।
explanation: Indeed, this Ravana cannot be conquered in battle by gods and asuras. Nor can you be led to destruction even by gods and Danavas.

shloka_text: राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते । अविभक्ताश्च सर्वार्थाः सुहृदां नात्र संशयः ।। 7.23.13 ।।
explanation: The friendship of the Rakshasa with you is pleasing. And all interests of friends are undivided; there is no doubt about this.

shloka_text: ततो ऽग्निसाक्षिकं सख्यं कृतवांस्तत्र रावणः । निवातकवचैः सार्धं प्रीतिमानभवत्तदा ।। 7.23.14 ।।
explanation: Then, Ravana, with fire as witness, established friendship there with the Nivātakavacas and became pleased at that time.

shloka_text: अर्थतस्तैर्यथान्यायं संवत्सरमथोषितः । स्वपुरान्निर्विशेषं च प्रियं प्राप्तो दशाननः ।। 7.23.15 ।।
explanation: Then, having resided for a year, Daśānana, treated by them according to their means and propriety, obtained pleasure as if he were in his own city.

shloka_text: ततोपधार्य मायानां शतमेकं समाप्तवान् । सलिलेन्द्रपुरान्वेषी भ्रमति स्म रसातलम् ।। 7.23.16 ।।
explanation: Then, having perceived a hundred illusions, he exhausted them. Seeking the city of the lord of waters, he wandered in Rasatala.

shloka_text: ततो ऽश्मनगरं नाम कालकेयैरधिष्ठितम् । गत्वा तु कालकेयांश्च हत्वा तत्र बलोत्कटान् ।। 7.23.17 ।।
explanation: Then, having gone to the city named Ashmanagara, which was occupied by the Kalakeyas, and having killed the mighty Kalakeyas there.

shloka_text: शूर्पणख्याश्च भर्तारमसिना प्राच्छिनत्तदा । श्यालं च बलवन्तं च विद्युज्जिह्वं बलोत्कटम् । जिह्वया संलिहन्तं च राक्षसं समरे तथा ।। 7.23.18 ।।
explanation: He then cut off Shurpanakha's husband, the powerful brother-in-law Vidyujjihva, who was exceedingly strong and a Rakshasa licking with his tongue in battle, with a sword.

shloka_text: तं विजित्य मुहूर्तेन जघ्ने दैत्यांश्चतुःशतम् ।। 7.23.19 ।।
explanation: Having conquered him, he killed four hundred Daityas in a moment.

shloka_text: ततः पाण्डुरमेघाभं कैलासमिव भास्वरम् । वरुणस्यालयं दिव्यमपश्यद्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.23.20 ।।
explanation: Then the lord of Rakshasas saw the divine abode of Varuna, radiant like Kailasa and resembling white clouds.

shloka_text: क्षरन्तीं च पयस्तत्र सुरभिं गामवस्थिताम् । यस्याः पयोभिनिष्यन्दात्क्षीरोदो नाम सागरः ।। 7.23.21 ।।
explanation: And there was the divine cow Surabhi, situated and exuding milk, from the abundant flow of whose milk is the ocean named Kṣīroda.

shloka_text: ददर्श रावणस्तत्र गोवृषेन्द्रवरारणिम् । यस्माच्चन्द्रः प्रभवति शीतरश्मिर्निशाकरः ।। 7.23.22 ।।
explanation: Ravana saw there the excellent source of the best of cows and bulls, from which the cool-rayed moon, the maker of night, originates.

shloka_text: यं समाश्रित्य जीवन्ति फेनपाः परमर्षयः । अमृतं यत्र चोत्पन्नं स्वधा च स्वधभोजिनाम् ।। 7.23.23 ।।
explanation: Whom the great sages, the foam-drinkers, rely upon for their life, and where nectar was produced, and Svadhā for the ancestors.

shloka_text: यां ब्रुवन्ति नरा लोके सुरभिं नाम नामतः । प्रदक्षिणं तु तां कृत्वा रावणः परमाद्भुताम् ।। 7.23.24 ।।
explanation: Whom men in the world call by the name Surabhi, Ravana, having indeed circumambulated that exceedingly wonderful one.

shloka_text: प्रविवेश महाघोरं गुप्तं बहुविधैर्बलैः । ततो धाराशताकीर्णं शारदाभ्रनिभं तदा । नित्यप्रहृष्टं ददृशे वरुणस्य गृहोत्तमम् ।। 7.23.25 ।।
explanation: He entered a very formidable, secret place, protected by various kinds of forces. Then, he saw Varuna's excellent abode, which was pervaded by hundreds of streams, resembled an autumn cloud, and was eternally joyful.

shloka_text: ततो हत्वा बलाध्यक्षान्समरे तैश्च ताडितः । अब्रवीच्च ततो योधान्राजा शीघ्रं निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.23.26 ।।
explanation: Then, having killed the commanders of the army in battle, and being struck by them, he then said to the warriors, "Let the king be quickly informed."

shloka_text: युद्धार्थी रावणः प्राप्तस्तस्य युद्धं प्रदीयताम् । वद वा न भयं ते ऽस्ति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति साञ्जलिः ।। 7.23.27 ।।
explanation: Ravana, desirous of battle, has arrived; let battle be given to him. Or, with folded hands, let him say, "You have no fear," or "I am conquered."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धा वरुणस्य महात्मनः । पुत्राः पौत्राश्च निष्क्रामन्गौश्च पुष्कर एव च ।। 7.23.28 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the angry sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuna, and Gau and Pushkara also, came out.

shloka_text: ते तु वीर्यगुणोपेता बलैः परिवृताः स्वकैः । युङ्क्त्वा रथान्कामगमानुद्यद्भास्वरवर्चसः ।। 7.23.29 ।।
explanation: But they, endowed with valor and virtues, surrounded by their own forces, having yoked chariots that moved at will, shone with rising, brilliant splendor.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवद्दारुणं रोमहर्षणम् । सलिलेन्द्रस्य पुत्राणां रावणस्य च धीमतः ।। 7.23.30 ।।
explanation: Then a fierce, hair-raising battle took place between the sons of the lord of waters and the intelligent Ravana.

shloka_text: अमात्यैश्च महावीर्यैर्दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः । वारुणं तद्बलं कृत्स्नं क्षणेन विनिपातितम् ।। 7.23.31 ।।
explanation: And by the greatly valorous ministers of the demon Daśagrīva, that entire army of Varuṇa was annihilated in an instant.

shloka_text: समीक्ष्य स्वबलं सङ्ख्ये वरुणस्य सुतास्तदा । अर्दिताः शरजालेन निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः ।। 7.23.32 ।।
explanation: Having assessed their own strength in battle, Varuna's sons, then afflicted by a shower of arrows, retreated from the act of fighting.

shloka_text: महीतलगतास्ते तु रावणं दृश्य पुष्पके । आकाशमाशु विविशुः स्यन्दनैः शीघ्रगामिभिः ।। 7.23.33 ।।
explanation: But those who were on the earth, having seen Ravana in the Pushpaka, swiftly entered the sky with their fast-moving chariots.

shloka_text: महादासीत्ततस्तेषां तुल्यं स्थानमवाप्य तत् । आकाशयुद्धं तुमुलं देवदानवयोरिव ।। 7.23.34 ।।
explanation: Then, having obtained that equal position, a great and tumultuous sky-battle ensued among them, like that of the Devas and Danavas.

shloka_text: ततस्ते रावणं युद्धे शरैः पावकसन्निभैः । विमुखीकृत्य सन्तुष्टा विनेदुर्विविधान्रवान् ।। 7.23.35 ।।
explanation: Then, having repulsed Ravana in battle with fire-like arrows, they, satisfied, uttered various roars.

shloka_text: ततो महोदरः क्रुद्धो राजानं दृश्य धर्षितम् । त्यक्त्वा मृत्युभयं वीरो युद्धकाङ्क्षी व्यलोकयत् ।। 7.23.36 ।।
explanation: Then Mahodara, enraged, seeing the king attacked, the hero, abandoning the fear of death and desirous of battle, looked around.

shloka_text: तेन ते दारुणा युद्धे कामगाः पवनोपमाः । महोदरेण गदया हता वै प्रययुः क्षितिम् ।। 7.23.37 ।।
explanation: By him, in that fierce battle, those swift-moving, wind-like (beings) were struck by Mahodara with a mace and indeed fell to the ground.

shloka_text: तेषां वरुणपुत्राणां हत्वा योधान्हयाञ्छतान् । मुमोचाशु महानादं विरथान्प्रेक्ष्य तान्स्थितान् ।। 7.23.38 ।।
explanation: Having killed the warriors and hundreds of horses belonging to those sons of Varuna, and seeing them standing dismounted from their chariots, he quickly let out a great roar.

shloka_text: ते तु तेषां रथाः साश्वाः सह सारथिभिर्हतैः । महोदरेण निहताः पतिताः पृथिवीतले ।। 7.23.39 ।।
explanation: But their chariots, with their horses and along with their slain charioteers, were struck down by Mahodara and fell to the ground.

shloka_text: ते तु त्यक्त्वा रथान्पुत्रा वरुणस्य महात्मनः । आकाशे विष्ठिताः शूराः स्वप्रभावान्न विव्यथुः ।। 7.23.40 ।।
explanation: But those heroic sons of the great-souled Varuna, having abandoned their chariots, stood in the sky and were not distressed by their own power.

shloka_text: धनूंषि कृत्वा सज्जानि विनिर्भिद्य महोदरम् । रावणं समरे क्रुद्धाः सहिताः समभिद्रवन् ।। 7.23.41 ।।
explanation: Having readied their bows, and having defeated Mahodara, they, enraged and united, rushed towards Ravana in battle.

shloka_text: सायकैश्चापविभ्रष्टैर्वज्रकल्पैः सुदारुणैः । दारयन्ति स्म सङ्क्रुद्धा मेघा इव महागिरिम् ।। 7.23.42 ।।
explanation: Enraged, they tore apart (the enemy) with arrows, released from bows, resembling thunderbolts, and extremely fierce, just as clouds (tear apart) a great mountain.

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः कालाग्निरिव निर्गतः । शरवर्षैर्महाघोरैस्तेषां मर्मस्वताडयत् ।। 7.23.43 ।।
explanation: Then, enraged, Dashagriva, having emerged like the fire of destruction, struck their vital spots with dreadful showers of arrows.

shloka_text: ततस्तेनैव सहसा सीदन्ति स्म पदातयः । मुसलानि विचित्राणि ततो भल्लशतानि च ।। 7.23.44 ।।
explanation: Then, by that very (force), the foot soldiers suddenly collapsed. Various maces and then hundreds of spears (were seen/used).

shloka_text: पट्टिशांश्चैव शक्तीश्च शतघ्नीस्तोमरांस्तथा । पातयामास दुर्धर्षस्तेषामुपरि विष्ठितः ।। 7.23.45 ।।
explanation: The formidable one, positioned above them, hurled down spears, shaktis, śataghnīs, and tomaras upon them.

shloka_text: अपविद्धास्तु ते वीरा विनिष्पेतुः पदातयः । महापङ्कमिवासाद्य कुञ्जराष्षष्टिहायनाः ।। 7.23.46 ।।
explanation: Those brave foot soldiers, being repulsed, fled, just as sixty-year-old elephants would, having encountered a deep mire.

shloka_text: सीदमानान्सुतान्दृष्ट्वा विह्वलान्सुमहौजसः । ननाद रावणो हर्षान्महानम्बुधरो यथा ।। 7.23.47 ।।
explanation: Seeing his sons, though of great might, disheartened and bewildered, Ravana roared with joy, like a great cloud.

shloka_text: ततो रक्षो महानादान्मुक्त्वा हन्ति स्म वारुणान् । नानाप्रहरणोपेतैर्धारापातैरिवाम्बुदः ।। 7.23.48 ।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa, having let out great roars, killed the Varunas, just as a cloud (pours down) with torrents of rain resembling various weapons.

shloka_text: ततस्ते विमुखाः सर्वे पतिता धरणीतले । रणात्स्वपुरुषैः शीघ्रं गृहाण्येव प्रवेशिताः ।। 7.23.49 ।।
explanation: Then all of them, defeated, fell to the ground. They were swiftly brought into their homes from the battlefield by their own men.

shloka_text: तानब्रवीत्ततो रक्षो वरुणाय निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.23.50 ।।
explanation: Then the Rakshasa said to them, "Let it be reported to Varuna."

shloka_text: रावणं त्वब्रवीन्मन्त्री प्रहस्तो (प्रहसो) नाम वारुणः । गतः खलु महाराजो ब्रह्मलोकं जलेश्वरः ।। 7.23.51 ।।
explanation: Then the minister named Prahastha, son of Varuna, spoke to Ravana: "Indeed, the great king, the lord of waters, has gone to the world of Brahma."

shloka_text: गान्धर्वं वरुणः श्रोतुं यं त्वमाह्वयसे युधि । तत्किं तव वृथा वीर परिश्रम्य गते नृपे । ये तु सन्निहिता वीराः कुमारास्ते पराजिताः ।। 7.23.52 ।।
explanation: Whom you challenge in battle, that Gandharva, for Varuna to hear (of it), what is the use of your effort, O hero, when the king has departed? And those heroes, the princes who were present, they have been defeated

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः । हर्षान्नादं विमुञ्चन्वै निष्क्रान्तो वरुणालयात् ।। 7.23.53 ।।
explanation: The king of Rakshasas, having heard that and having proclaimed his own name, indeed letting out a joyful roar, emerged from the abode of Varuna.

shloka_text: आगतस्तु पथा येन तेनैव विनिवृत्य सः । लङ्कामभिमुखो रक्षो नभस्तलगतो ययौ ।। 7.23.54 ।।
explanation: But having returned by the very path by which he had come, that demon, facing Lanka, went through the sky.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः ।। 23 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered Ramayana, the original epic by Valmiki, this is the twenty-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: निवर्तमानः संहृष्टो रावणस्सुदुरात्मवान् । जह्रे पथि नरेन्द्रर्षिदेवगन्धर्वकन्यकाः ।। 7.24.1 ।।
explanation: Returning, greatly delighted, Rāvaṇa, the extremely wicked one, abducted on the way the maidens of kings, sages, gods, and gandharvas.

shloka_text: दर्शनीयां हि रक्षः स कन्यां स्त्रीं वापि पश्यति । हत्वा बन्धुजनं तस्या विमाने तां रुरोध ह ।। 7.24.2 ।।
explanation: Indeed, that Rakshasa sees a beautiful maiden or a woman. Having killed her relatives, he imprisoned her in his aerial car.

shloka_text: एवं पन्नगकन्याश्च राक्षसासुरमानुषीः । यक्षदानवकन्याश्च विमाने सो ऽध्यरोपयत् ।। 7.24.3 ।।
explanation: Thus, he placed the daughters of serpents, Rākṣasas, Asuras, humans, Yakṣas, and Dānavas in the aerial chariot.

shloka_text: ताश्च सर्वाः समं दुःखान्मुमुचुर्बाष्पजं जलम् । तुल्यमग्न्यर्चिषां तत्र शोकाग्निभयसम्भवम् ।। 7.24.4 ।।
explanation: And all of them equally shed tears from sorrow. There, those tears were like the flames of fire, born from the fire of grief and fear.

shloka_text: ताभिः सर्वानवद्याभिर्नदीभिरिव सागरः । आपूरितं विमानं तद्भयशोकाशिवाश्रुभिः ।। 7.24.5 ।।
explanation: That aerial car was filled by those tears of fear, sorrow, and inauspiciousness, just as the ocean is filled by all blameless rivers.

shloka_text: नागगन्धर्वकन्याश्च महर्षितनयाश्च याः । दैत्यदानवकन्याश्च विमाने शतशो ऽरुदन् ।। 7.24.6 ।।
explanation: Nāga and Gandharva maidens, and daughters of great sages, and also the daughters of Daityas and Dānavas, wept by hundreds in the aerial car.

shloka_text: दीर्घकेश्यः सुचार्वङ्ग्यः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः । पीनस्तन्यस्तथा वज्रवेदिमध्यसमप्रभाः ।। 7.24.7 ।।
explanation: Long-haired, with very beautiful limbs, faces like the full moon, full-breasted, and with waists as slender and perfect as the middle of a diamond altar.

shloka_text: रथकूबरसङ्काशैः श्रोणिदेशैर्मनोहराः । स्त्रियः सुराङ्गनाप्रख्या निष्टप्तकनकप्रभाः ।। 7.24.8 ।।
explanation: The women, charming with their hip regions resembling the chariot's pole, were like celestial nymphs, possessing the radiance of refined gold.

shloka_text: शोकदुःखभयत्रस्ता विह्वलाश्च सुमध्यमाः । तासां निश्वासवातेन सर्वतः सम्प्रदीपितम् ।। 7.24.9 ।।
explanation: The beautiful women, terrified by sorrow, suffering, and fear, and overwhelmed, by the wind of their sighs, everything was thoroughly kindled everywhere.

shloka_text: अग्निहोत्रमिवाभाति सन्निरुद्धाग्निपुष्पकम् । दशग्रीववशं प्राप्तास्तास्तु शोकाकुलाः स्त्रियः ।। 7.24.10 ।।
explanation: They appeared like an Agnihotra with its fire confined within the Pushpaka, those women, having fallen under the control of Dashagriva, were distressed with sorrow.

shloka_text: दीनवक्रेक्षणाः श्यामा मृग्यः सिंहवशा इव । काचिच्चिन्तयती तत्र किं नु मां भक्षयिष्यति ।। 7.24.11 ।।
explanation: The dark-complexioned women, with pitiable, distressed gazes, were like does under the sway of a lion. One of them was thinking, "Will he indeed devour me?"

shloka_text: काचिद्दध्यौ सुदुःखार्ता अपि मां मारयेदयम् । इति मातृपितऽन्स्मृत्वा भर्तऽन्भ्रातऽंस्तथैव च । दुःखशोकसमाविष्टा विलेपुः सहिताः स्त्रियः ।। 7.24.12 ।।
explanation: Some deeply distressed woman thought, "Perhaps this one might kill me." Remembering their mothers, fathers, husbands, and brothers, the women, overwhelmed by sorrow and grief, lamented together.

shloka_text: कथं नु खलु मे पुत्रो भविष्यति मया विना । कथं माता कथं भ्राता निमग्नाः शोकसागरे ।। 7.24.13 ।। ।
explanation: How indeed will my son fare without me? How will mother, how will brother be plunged into the ocean of sorrow?

shloka_text: हा कथं नु करिष्यामि भर्तुस्तस्मादहं विना । मृत्यो प्रसादयामि त्वां नय मां दुःखभागिनीम् ।। 7.24.14 ।।
explanation: Alas! How shall I manage without that husband? O Death, I implore you, take me, the one afflicted with sorrow.

shloka_text: किन्नु तद्दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम् ।। 7.24.15 ।।
explanation: What indeed was that evil deed done in a previous birth?

shloka_text: एवं स्म दुःखिताः सर्वाः पतिताः शोकसागरे । न खल्विदानीं पश्यामो दुःखस्यास्यान्तमात्मनः ।। 7.24.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, all were distressed, fallen into an ocean of grief. Indeed, we do not now see an end to this sorrow for ourselves.

shloka_text: अहो धिङ्मानुषं लोकं नास्ति खल्वधमः परः । यद्दुर्बला बलवता भर्तारो रावणेन नः ।। 7.24.17 ।।
explanation: Oh, shame on the human world! There is indeed no greater degradation, that our weak husbands are (helpless) against the mighty Ravana.

shloka_text: सूर्येणोदयता काले नक्षत्राणीव नाशिताः । अहो सुबलवद्रक्षो वधोपायेषु युज्यते ।। 7.24.18 ।।
explanation: Like stars are made to disappear by the rising sun at dawn, (so were they destroyed). Oh, the very powerful demon applies himself to means of destruction.

shloka_text: अहो दुर्वृत्तमास्थाय नात्मानं वैजुगुप्सते । सर्वथा सदृशस्तावद्विक्रमो ऽस्य दुरात्मनः ।। 7.24.19 ।।
explanation: Oh! Having resorted to evil conduct, he certainly does not feel ashamed of himself. Indeed, the prowess of this wicked one is completely befitting.

shloka_text: इदं त्वसदृशं कर्म परदाराभिमर्शनम् । यस्मादेष परक्यासु रमते राक्षसाधमः ।। 7.24.20 ।।
explanation: This act, the molestation of another's wife, is indeed unseemly, because this vilest of demons delights in others' wives.

shloka_text: तस्माद्वै स्त्रीकृतेनैव प्राप्स्यते दुर्मतिर्वधम् । सतीभिर्वरनारीभिरेवं वाक्ये ऽभ्युदीरिते ।। 7.24.21 ।।
explanation: Therefore, the evil-minded one will certainly meet death only on account of a woman, when such a statement was uttered by chaste and excellent women.

shloka_text: नेदुर्दुन्दुभयः खस्थाः पुष्पवृष्टिः पपात च । शप्तः स्त्रीभिः स तु समं हतौजा इव निष्प्रभः ।। 7.24.22 ।।
explanation: The drums in the sky resounded, and a shower of flowers fell. But he, cursed by the women, became devoid of luster, as if his power had been destroyed.

shloka_text: पतिव्रताभिः साध्वीभिर्बभूव विमना इव । एवं विलपितं तासां शृण्वन्राक्षसपुङ्गवः । प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां पूज्यमानो निशाचरैः ।। 7.24.23 ।।
explanation: He became disheartened, as if by the chaste and virtuous wives. Hearing their lamentation thus, the foremost of Rakshasas entered the city of Lanka, being honored by the night-wanderers.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे घोरा राक्षसी कामरूपिणी । सहसा पतिता भूमौ भगिनी रावणस्य सा ।। 7.24.24 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, that terrible, shape-shifting demoness, Ravana's sister, suddenly fell to the ground.

shloka_text: तां स्वसारं समुत्थाप्य रावणः परिसान्त्वयन् । अब्रवीत्किमिदं भद्रे वक्तुकामा ऽसि मे द्रुतम् ।। 7.24.25 ।।
explanation: Having raised up his sister and comforting her, Ravana said, "O good lady, what is it that you wish to tell me quickly?"

shloka_text: सा बाष्पपरिरुद्धाक्षी रक्ताक्षी वाक्यमब्रवीत् । कृता ऽस्मि विधवा राजंस्त्वया बलवता बलात् ।। 7.24.26 ।।
explanation: Her eyes obstructed by tears and red, she spoke these words: "O King, I have been forcibly made a widow by you, the powerful one."

shloka_text: एते राजंस्त्वया वीरा दैत्या विनिहता रणे । कालकेया इति ख्याताः सहस्राणि चतुर्दश ।। 7.24.27 ।।
explanation: O King, these brave Daityas, known as the Kalakeyas, fourteen thousand in number, were slain by you in battle.

shloka_text: प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयान्मे तत्र भर्ता महाबलः ।। 7.24.28 ।।
explanation: My mighty husband is dearer to me than even my life.

shloka_text: सो ऽपि त्वया हतस्तात रिपुणा भ्रातृगृध्नुना । त्वया ऽस्मि निहता राजन्स्वयमेव हि बन्धुना ।। 7.24.29 ।।
explanation: He also was killed by you, O dear one, by an enemy greedy for a brother. I am killed by you, O King, indeed by yourself, a kinsman.

shloka_text: राजन्वैधव्यशब्दं च भोक्ष्यामि त्वत्कृते ह्यहम् । ननु नाम त्वया रक्ष्यो जामाता समरेष्वपि । स त्वया निहतो युद्धे स्वयमेव न लज्जसे ।। 7.24.30 ।।
explanation: O King, I shall indeed suffer widowhood because of you. Surely, your son-in-law ought to be protected by you, even in battles. He was killed by you in battle, by yourself. Are you not ashamed?

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवो भगिन्या क्रोशमानया । अब्रवीत्सान्त्वयित्वा तां सामपूर्वमिदं वचः ।। 7.24.31 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by his wailing sister, Daśagrīva, having consoled her, spoke these gentle words.

shloka_text: अलं वत्से रुदित्वा ते न भेतव्यं च सर्वशः । दानमानप्रसादैस्त्वां तोषयिष्यामि यत्नतः ।। 7.24.32 ।।
explanation: Enough of your crying, dear child. You have nothing to fear at all. I will diligently satisfy you with gifts, honors, and favors.

shloka_text: युद्धप्रमत्तो व्याक्षिप्तो जयाकाङ्क्षी क्षिपञ्छरान् । नावगच्छामि युद्धेषु स्वान्परान्वाप्यहं शुभे ।। 7.24.33 ।।
explanation: Intoxicated by battle, agitated, desiring victory, and shooting arrows, I do not discern my own people or others in battles, O auspicious one.

shloka_text: जामातरं न जाने स्म प्रहरन्युद्धदुर्मदः । तेनासौ निहतः सङ्ख्ये मया भर्ता तव स्वसः ।। 7.24.34 ।।
explanation: I, battle-mad and striking, did not know he was my son-in-law. Therefore, O sister, that very husband of yours was killed by me in battle.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्काले तु यत्प्राप्तं तत्करिष्यामि ते हितम् । भ्रातुरैश्वर्ययुक्तस्य खरस्य वस पार्श्वतः ।। 7.24.35 ।।
explanation: At this time, I will do for your good whatever is appropriate. Dwell by the side of your brother Khara, who is endowed with power.

shloka_text: चतुर्दशानां भ्राता ते सहस्राणां भविष्यति । प्रभुः प्रयाणे दाने च राक्षसानां महाबलः ।। 7.24.36 ।।
explanation: Your brother will be the lord of fourteen thousand Rākṣasas, very powerful in battle and in giving.

shloka_text: तत्र मातृष्वसेयस्ते भ्राता ऽयं वै खरः प्रभुः । भविष्यति तवादेशं सदा कुर्वन्निशाचरः ।। 7.24.37 ।।
explanation: There, this brother of yours, Khara, your maternal cousin, a powerful demon, will always be carrying out your commands.

shloka_text: शीघ्रं गच्छत्वयं वीरो दण्डकान्परिरक्षितुम् । दूषणो ऽस्य बलाध्यक्षो भविष्यति महाबलः ।। 7.24.38 ।।
explanation: Let this hero quickly go to protect Daṇḍaka. Dūṣaṇa, the mighty, will be his army commander.

shloka_text: तत्र ते वचनं शूरः करिष्यति सदा खरः । रक्षसां कामरूपाणां प्रभुरेष भविष्यति ।। 7.24.39 ।।
explanation: There, the brave Khara will always carry out your command. He will be the lord of the Rākṣasas who can assume any form at will.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दशग्रीवः सैन्यमस्यादिदेश ह । चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां वीर्यशालिनाम् ।। 7.24.40 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken, Dashagriva commanded his army of fourteen thousand valorous Rakshasas.

shloka_text: स तैः परिवृतस्सर्वै राक्षसैर्घोरदर्शनैः । आगच्छत खरः शीघ्रं दण्डकानकुतोभयः ।। 7.24.41 ।।
explanation: He, Khara, surrounded by all those demons of dreadful appearance, quickly came to Dandaka, fearless.

shloka_text: स तत्र कारयामास राज्यं निहतकण्टकम् । सा च शूर्पणखा तत्र न्यवसद्दण्डकावने ।। 7.24.42 ।।
explanation: He established a kingdom there, free from enemies. And Shurpanakha resided there in the Dandaka forest.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः ।। 24 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: स तु दत्त्वा दशग्रीवो वनं घोरं स्वरस्य तत् । भगिनीं च समाश्वास्य हृष्टः स्वस्थतरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.25.1 ।।
explanation: But Dashagriva, having given that dreadful forest for himself, and having consoled his sister, became delighted and more at ease.

shloka_text: ततो निकुम्भिला नाम लङ्कोपवनमुत्तमम् । तद्राक्षसेन्द्रो बलवान्प्रविवेश सहानुगः ।। 7.25.2 ।।
explanation: Then, that powerful lord of Rakshasas, accompanied by his followers, entered Nikumbhila by name, the excellent grove of Lanka.

shloka_text: ततो यूपशताकीर्णं सौम्यचैत्योपशोभितम् । ददर्श विष्ठितं यज्ञं श्रिया सम्प्रज्वलन्निव ।। 7.25.3 ।।
explanation: Then he saw the sacrifice, which was arranged, crowded with hundreds of sacrificial posts, adorned with beautiful altars, and shining as if ablaze with splendor.

shloka_text: ततः कृष्णाजिनधरं कमण्डलुशिखाध्वजम् । ददर्श स्वसुतं तत्र मेघनादं भयावहम् ।। 7.25.4 ।।
explanation: Then he saw his own son Meghanada there, terrifying, wearing a black deer skin, and bearing a water-pot and a topknot as his emblem.

shloka_text: तं समासाद्य लङ्केशः परिष्वज्वाथ बाहुभिः । अब्रवीत्किमिदं वत्स वर्तसे ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः ।। 7.25.5 ।।
explanation: Having approached him, the lord of Lanka then embraced him with his arms and said, 'What is this, dear child, in which you find yourself? Tell me truthfully.'

shloka_text: उशना त्वब्रवीत्तत्र यज्ञसम्पत्समृद्धये । रावणं राक्षसश्रेष्ठं द्विजश्रेष्ठो महातपाः ।। 7.25.6 ।।
explanation: Uśanas, the best among Brahmins and a great ascetic, indeed spoke there to Ravana, the foremost of the Rakshasas, for the flourishing of the sacrificial prosperity.

shloka_text: अहमाख्यामि ते राजञ्छ्रूयतां सर्वमेव तत् । यज्ञास्ते सप्त पुत्रेण प्राप्तास्सुबहुविस्तराः ।। 7.25.7 ।।
explanation: I will tell you, O King, listen to all of that. Those seven very extensive sacrifices were performed by the son.

shloka_text: अग्निष्टोमो ऽश्वमेधश्च यज्ञो बहुसुवर्णकः । राजसूयस्तथा यज्ञो गोमेधो वैष्ववस्तथा ।। 7.25.8 ।।
explanation: Agnishtoma, and Ashwamedha, and the Bahusuvarṇaka sacrifice; similarly, the Rajasuya sacrifice, the Gomedha, and the Vaishvava.

shloka_text: माहेश्वरे प्रवृत्ते तु यज्ञे पुम्भिः सुदुर्लभे । वरांस्ते लब्धवान्पुत्रः साक्षात्पशुपतेरिह ।। 7.25.9 ।।
explanation: When the Maheśvara sacrifice, which is very difficult for men to perform, was underway, your son obtained boons directly from Paśupati here.

shloka_text: कामगं स्यन्दनं दिव्यमन्तरिक्षचरं ध्रुवम् । मायां च तामसीं नाम यया सम्पद्यते तमः ।। 7.25.10 ।।
explanation: A divine chariot moving at will, traversing the sky, steadfast, and the illusion named Tamasi, by which darkness is produced.

shloka_text: एतया किल सङ्ग्रामे मायया राक्षसेश्वर । प्रयुक्तया गतिः शक्या नहि ज्ञातुं सुरासुरैः ।। 7.25.11 ।।
explanation: O lord of Rākṣasas, indeed, when this illusion is employed in battle, its movement cannot be known by gods and asuras.

shloka_text: अक्षयाविषुधी बाणैश्चापं चापि सुदुर्जयम् । अस्त्रं च बलवद्राजञ्छत्रुविध्वंसनं रणे ।। 7.25.12 ।।
explanation: Two inexhaustible quivers with arrows, and an invincible bow, and a powerful weapon, O King, which is a destroyer of enemies in battle.

shloka_text: एतान्सर्वान्वरांल्लब्ध्वा पुत्रस्ते ऽयं दशानन । अद्य यज्ञसमाप्तौ च त्वां दिदृक्षुस्स्थितो ह्यहम् ।। 7.25.13 ।।
explanation: O Daśānana, this son of yours, having obtained all these boons, and I have indeed come here today, at the completion of the sacrifice, desiring to see you.

shloka_text: ततो ऽब्रवीदृशग्रीवो न शोभनमिदं कृतम् । पूजिताः शत्रवो यस्माद्द्रव्यैरिन्द्रपुरोगमाः ।। 7.25.14 ।।
explanation: Then Daśagrīva said, "This was not done well, because the enemies, led by Indra, were honored with wealth."

shloka_text: एहीदानीं कृतं विद्धि सुकृतं तन्न संशयः । आगच्छ सौम्य गच्छामः स्वमेव भवनं प्रति ।। 7.25.15 ।।
explanation: Come now, know that a good deed has been done; there is no doubt about it. Come, O gentle one, let us go to our own home.

shloka_text: ततो गत्वा दशग्रीवः सपुत्रः सविभीषणः । स्त्रियो ऽवतारयामास सर्वास्ता बाष्पगद्गदाः ।। 7.25.16 ।।
explanation: Then, having gone, Dashagriva, with his son and Vibhishana, disembarked all those women, who were choked with tears.

shloka_text: लक्षिण्यो रत्नभूताश्च देवदानवरक्षसाम् । तस्य तासु मतिं ज्ञात्वा धर्मत्मा वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.25.17 ।।
explanation: Auspicious and like jewels among the gods, Danavas, and Rakshasas, the righteous one, having understood his intention concerning them, spoke.

shloka_text: ईदृशैस्त्वं समाचारैर्यशोर्थकुलनाशनैः । धर्षणं ज्ञातिनां ज्ञात्वा स्वमतेन विचेष्टसे ।। 7.25.18 ।।
explanation: By such conduct, which destroys fame, wealth, and family, you, knowing the oppression of your kinsmen, act according to your own will.

shloka_text: ज्ञातींस्तान्धर्षयित्वेमास्त्वया ऽ ऽनीता वराङ्गनाः । त्वामतिक्रम्य मधुना राजन्कुम्भीनसी हृता ।। 7.25.19 ।।
explanation: Having overpowered those kinsmen, these beautiful women were brought by you. O King, Madhu, having disregarded you, abducted Kumbhinasi.

shloka_text: रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं नावगच्छामि किं त्विदम् । को ऽयं यस्तु त्वया ऽ ऽख्यातो मधुरित्येव नामतः ।। 7.25.20 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa, however, said: "I do not understand what this is. Who is this person named Madhu, whom you have mentioned?"

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तु सङ्क्रुद्धो भ्रातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । श्रूयतामस्य पापस्य कर्मणः फलमागतम् ।। 7.25.21 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, greatly enraged, spoke these words to his brother: "Listen, the fruit of this sinful deed has arrived."

shloka_text: मातामहस्य यो भ्राता ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सुमालिनः । माल्यवानिति विख्यातो वृद्धः प्राज्ञो निशाचरः ।। 7.25.22 ।।
explanation: The brother of the maternal grandfather, who was the elder brother of Sumali, was renowned as Malyavan, an old, wise night-wanderer.

shloka_text: पिता ज्येष्ठो जनन्या नो ह्यस्माकं चार्यको ऽभवत् । तस्य कुम्भीनसी नाम दुहितुर्दुहिता ऽभवत् ।। 7.25.23 ।।
explanation: Our mother's elder father was our grandfather. His granddaughter was named Kumbhinasi.

shloka_text: मातृष्वसुरथास्माकं सा च कन्या ऽनलोद्भवा । भवत्यस्माकमेवैषा भ्रातृणां धर्मतः स्वसा ।। 7.25.24 ।।
explanation: And she, the daughter of our maternal aunt, born from fire, indeed becomes our sister by dharma, for us brothers.

shloka_text: सा हृता, मधुना राजन्राक्षसेन बलीयसा । यज्ञप्रवृत्ते पुत्रे तु मयि चान्तर्जलोषिते ।। 7.25.25 ।।
explanation: She was abducted, O King, by the powerful Rakshasa Madhu, while my son was engaged in a sacrifice and I was dwelling submerged in water.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णे महाराज निद्रामनुभवत्यथ । निहत्य राक्षसश्रेष्ठानमात्यानिह सम्मतान् ।। 7.25.26 ।।
explanation: O great king, when Kumbhakarna was experiencing sleep, then, having killed the esteemed ministers, the best of the Rākṣasas, here..."

shloka_text: धर्षयित्वा हृता सा तु सुप्ताप्यन्तःपुरे तव । श्रुत्वा ऽपि तन्महाराज क्षान्तमेव हतो न सः ।। 7.25.27 ।।
explanation: Having assaulted her, she was abducted, even while sleeping in your inner chambers. Even after hearing that, O great king, it was forgiven; he was not killed.

shloka_text: यस्मादवश्यं दातव्या कन्या भर्त्रे हि भ्रातृभिः । तदेतत्कर्मणो ह्यस्य फलं पापस्य दुर्मते ।। 7.25.28 ।।
explanation: Since a maiden must certainly be given to her husband by her brothers, therefore this is indeed the fruit of this sinful deed, O evil-minded one!

shloka_text: अस्मिन्नेवाभिसम्प्राप्तं लोके विदितमस्तु ते । विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रः स रावणः । दौरात्म्येनात्मनोद्धूतस्तप्ताम्भ इव सागरः ।। 7.25.29 ।।
explanation: Let it be known to you that this has indeed come to pass in this world. Having heard Vibhishana's words, that Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, was agitated by his own wickedness, like the ocean by heated water.

shloka_text: ततो ऽब्रवीदृशग्रीवः क्रुद्धः संरक्तलोचनः । कल्प्यतां मे रथः शीघ्रं शूराः सज्जीभवन्तु नः ।। 7.25.30 ।।
explanation: Then Dashagriva, enraged and with blood-red eyes, said: "Let my chariot be prepared quickly, and let our warriors be ready."

shloka_text: भ्राता मे कुम्भकर्णश्च ये च मुख्या निशाचराः । वाहनान्यधिरोहन्तु नानाप्रहरणायुधाः ।। 7.25.31 ।।
explanation: My brother Kumbhakarna and those who are the chief night-wanderers, armed with various weapons, should mount their vehicles.

shloka_text: अद्य तं समरे हत्वा मधुं रावणनिर्भयम् । सुरलोकं गमिष्यामि युद्धकाङ्क्षी सुहृद्वृतः ।। 7.25.32 ।।
explanation: Today, having killed that Madhu, who is unafraid of Ravana, in battle, I shall go to the world of gods, desirous of war, surrounded by my friends.

shloka_text: अक्षौहिणीसहस्राणि चत्वार्यग्र्याणि रक्षसाम् । नानाप्रहरणान्याशु निर्ययुर्युद्धकाङ्क्षिणाम् ।। 7.25.33 ।।
explanation: Four thousand excellent Akshauhinis of the Rakshasas, eager for battle, swiftly marched out with various weapons.

shloka_text: इन्द्रजित्त्वग्रतः (अग्रतः) सैन्यात्सैनिकान्परिगृह्य च । जगाम रावणो मध्ये कुम्भकर्णश्च पृष्ठतः ।। 7.25.34 ।।
explanation: Indrajit, leading the soldiers from the front of the army, and Ravana went in the middle, and Kumbhakarna at the back.

shloka_text: विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा लङ्कायां धर्मामाचरत् । शोषाः सर्वे महाभागा ययुर्मधुपुरं प्रति ।। 7.25.35 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, the righteous soul, practiced dharma in Lanka. All the remaining illustrious ones went to Madhupura.

shloka_text: खरैरुष्ट्रैर्हयैर्दीप्तैः शिंशुमारैर्महोरगैः । राक्षसाः प्रययुः सर्वे कृत्वा ऽ ऽकाशं निरन्तरम् ।। 7.25.36 ।।
explanation: All the Rākṣasas proceeded, filling the sky completely, with donkeys, camels, fierce horses, aquatic monsters, and great serpents.

shloka_text: दैत्याश्च शतशस्तत्र कृतवैराश्च दैवतैः । रावणं प्रेक्ष्य गच्छन्तमन्वगच्छन्हि पृष्ठतः ।। 7.25.37 ।।
explanation: And hundreds of Daityas there, who were hostile to the gods, seeing Ravana departing, indeed followed him from behind.

shloka_text: स तु गत्वा मधुपुरं प्रविश्य च दशाननः । न ददर्श मधुं तत्र भगिनीं तत्र दृष्टवान् ।। 7.25.38 ।।
explanation: Dashanana, having gone to Madhupura and entered, did not see Madhu there, but saw his sister.

shloka_text: सा च प्रह्वाञ्जलिर्भूत्वा शिरसा चरणौ गता ।। 7.25.39 ।।
explanation: And she, having become humble with folded hands, bowed her head to his feet.

shloka_text: तस्य राक्षसराजस्य त्रस्ता कुम्भीनसी तदा । तां समुत्थापयामास न भेतव्यमिति ब्रुवन् ।। 7.25.40 ।।
explanation: Then, Kumbhīnasi, who was frightened by that king of Rākṣasas, he made her rise up, saying, "Do not be afraid."

shloka_text: रावणो राक्षसश्रेष्ठः किं चापि करवाणि ते । साब्रवीद्यदि मे राजन्प्रसन्नस्त्वं महाभुज । भर्तारं न ममेहाद्य हन्तुर्महसि मानद ।। 7.25.41 ।।
explanation: Ravana, the best of Rakshasas, (asked) "What else can I do for you?" She said, "If you are pleased with me, O King, O mighty-armed one, O giver of honor, you should not kill my husband here today."

shloka_text: न हीदृशं भयं किञ्चित्कुलस्त्रीणामिहोच्यते । भयानामपि सर्वेषां वैधव्यं व्यसनं महत् ।। 7.25.42 ।।
explanation: Indeed, no such fear is spoken of for noble women in this world. Among all fears, widowhood is a great calamity.

shloka_text: सत्यवाग्भव राजेन्द्र मामवेक्षस्व याचतीम् । त्वयाप्युक्तं महाराज न भेतव्यमिति स्वयम् ।। 7.25.43 ।।
explanation: Be truthful, O King of kings, and look upon me who is pleading. You yourself, O Great King, had said, 'There is no need to fear.'

shloka_text: रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्धृष्टः स्वसारं तत्र संस्थिताम् । क्व चासौ तव भर्ता वै मम शीघ्रं निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.25.44 ।।
explanation: But Ravana, emboldened, said to his sister who was standing there, "Where is that husband of yours? Let him be quickly reported to me."

shloka_text: सह तेन गमिष्यामि सुरलोकं जयावहे । तव कारुण्यसौहार्दान्निवृत्तो ऽस्मि मधोर्वधात् ।। 7.25.45 ।।
explanation: I will go with him to the world of gods, bringing victory. Due to your compassion and friendship, I have refrained from killing Madhu.

shloka_text: इत्युक्ता सा समुत्थाप्य प्रसुप्तं तं निशाचरम् । अब्रवीत्सम्प्रहृष्टेव राक्षसी सा पतिं वचः ।। 7.25.46 ।।
explanation: Thus spoken to, that demoness, having awakened her sleeping husband, the night-wanderer, spoke words to him as if greatly delighted.

shloka_text: एष प्राप्तो दशग्रीवो मम भ्राता महाबलः । सुरलोकजयाकाङ्क्षी साहाय्ये त्वां वृणोति च ।। 7.25.47 ।।
explanation: Here has arrived Daśagrīva, my mighty brother. Desiring to conquer the world of gods, he requests your assistance.

shloka_text: तदस्य त्वं सहायार्थं सबन्धुर्गच्छ राक्षस । स्निग्धस्य भजमानस्य युक्तमर्थाय कल्पितुम् ।। 7.25.48 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Rakshasa, you go with your kinsmen to help him. It is proper to accomplish the purpose for one who is affectionate and devoted.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा तथेत्याह मधुर्वचः ।। 7.25.49 ।।
explanation: Having heard her words, Madhu spoke, saying, 'So be it.'"

shloka_text: ददर्श राक्षसश्रेष्ठं यथान्यायमुपेत्य सः । पूजयमास धर्मेण रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ।। 7.25.50 ।।
explanation: He, having approached properly, saw Ravana, the best of Rakshasas and the lord of Rakshasas, and worshipped him righteously.

shloka_text: प्राप्य पूजां दशग्रीवो मधुवेश्मानि वीर्यवान् । तत्र चैकां निशामुष्य गमनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.25.51 ।।
explanation: The powerful Daśagrīva, having received honor in Madhu's abode, and having stayed there for one night, began to depart.

shloka_text: ततः कैलासमासाद्य शैलं वैश्रवणालयम् । राक्षसेन्द्रो महेन्द्राभः सेनामुपनिवेशयत् ।। 7.25.52 ।।
explanation: Then, the king of Rākṣasas, mighty as Mahendra, having reached the Kailasa mountain, the abode of Vaiśravaṇa, encamped his army.

shloka_text: स तु तत्र दशग्रीवः सह सैन्येन वीर्यवान् । अस्तं प्राप्ते दिनकरे निवासं समरोचयत् ।। 7.26.1 ।।
explanation: The powerful Daśagrīva, along with his army, chose to encamp there when the sun had set.

shloka_text: उदिते विमले चन्द्रे तुल्यपर्वतवर्चसि । प्रसुप्तं सुमहत्सैन्यं नानाप्रहरणायुधम् ।। 7.26.2 ।।
explanation: When the spotless moon, shining with mountain-like splendor, had risen, the huge army, armed with various weapons, was fast asleep.

shloka_text: रावणस्तु महावीर्यो निषण्णः शैलमूर्धनि । स ददर्श गुणांस्तत्र चन्द्रपादपशोभितान् ।। 7.26.3 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa, of great valor, seated on the mountain peak. He saw there the beautiful features, adorned with trees shining like the moon.

shloka_text: कर्णिकारवनैर्दीप्तैः कदम्बगहनैस्तथा । पद्मिनीभिश्च फुल्लाभिर्मन्दाकिन्या जलैरपि ।। 7.26.4 ।।
explanation: By resplendent groves of Karnikara trees, and by dense thickets of Kadamba trees, and by blooming lotus ponds, and also by the waters of the Mandakini.

shloka_text: चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागमन्दारतरुभिस्तथा । चूतपाटललोध्रैश्च प्रियङ्ग्वर्जुनकेतकैः । तगरैर्नारिकैलैश्च प्रियालपनसैस्तथा ।। 7.26.5 ।।
explanation: And with Champak, Ashoka, Punnaga, and Mandara trees; with Mango, Patala, Lodhra, Priyangu, Arjuna, and Ketaka; and with Tagara, Coconut, Priyala, and Jackfruit trees.

shloka_text: आरग्वधैस्तमालैश्च प्रियालवकुलैरपि । एतैरन्यैश्च तरुभिरुद्भासितवनान्तरे । किन्नरा मदनेनार्ता रक्ता मधुरकण्ठिनः ।। 7.26.6 ।।
explanation: In the forest interior, made radiant by Aragvadha, Tamala, Priyala, Bakula, and other trees, the sweet-voiced Kinnaras were impassioned and afflicted by love.

shloka_text: समं सम्प्रजगुर्यत्र मनस्तुष्टिविवर्धनम् ।। 7.26.7 ।।
explanation: Where they sang in unison, increasing the mind's satisfaction.

shloka_text: भिरुद्भासितवनान्तरे । विद्याधरा मदक्षीबा मदरक्तान्तलोचनाः । योषिद्भिः सह सङ्क्रान्ताश्चिक्रीडुर्जहृषुश्च वै ।। 7.26.8 ।।
explanation: In the brightly illuminated forest interior, Vidyadharas, intoxicated with passion, their eyes red at the corners from intoxication, gathered with women, played and indeed rejoiced.

shloka_text: घण्टानामिव सन्नादः शुश्रुवे मधुरस्वरः । अप्सरोगणसङ्घानां गायतां धनदालये ।। 7.26.9 ।।
explanation: A sweet sound, like the ringing of bells, was heard in the abode of Kubera, from the groups of Apsaras singing.

shloka_text: पुष्पवर्षाणि मुञ्चन्तो नगाः पवनताडिताः । शैलं तं वासयन्तीव मधुमाधवगन्धिनः ।। 7.26.10 ।।
explanation: The trees, swayed by the wind, showering rains of flowers, as if perfumed that mountain with the fragrance of spring.

shloka_text: मधुपुष्परजःपृक्तं गन्धमादाय पुष्कलम् । प्रववौ वर्धयन्कामं रावणस्य सुखो ऽनिलः ।। 7.26.11 ।।
explanation: A pleasant wind, carrying an abundant fragrance mixed with the pollen of honeyed flowers, blew, increasing Ravana's desire.

shloka_text: गेयात्पुष्पसमृद्ध्या च शैत्याद्वायोर्गिरेर्गुणात् । प्रवृत्तायां रजन्यां च चन्द्रस्योदयनेन च ।। 7.26.12 ।।
explanation: From singing, and by the abundance of flowers, and from the coolness of the wind, and from the excellence of the mountain, and when the night had begun, and by the rising of the moon.

shloka_text: रावणस्तु महावीर्यः कामस्य वशमागतः । विनिःश्वस्य विनिःश्वस्य शशिनं समवैक्षत ।। 7.26.13 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa, the greatly valorous one, having come under the sway of desire, repeatedly sighed and gazed at the moon.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र दिव्याभरणभूषिता । सर्वाप्सरोवरा रम्भा दिव्यपुष्पविभूषिता ।। 7.26.14 ।।
explanation: Meanwhile, there, Rambha, the foremost of all Apsaras, adorned with divine ornaments and divine flowers.

shloka_text: दिव्यचन्दनलिप्ताङ्गी मन्दारकृतमूर्धजा । दिव्योत्सवकृतारम्भा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानना ।। 7.26.15 ।।
explanation: Her body smeared with divine sandalwood, her hair adorned with Mandara flowers, having commenced a divine celebration, her face resembling the full moon.

shloka_text: चक्षुर्मनोहरं पीनं मेखलादामभूषितम् । समुद्वहन्ती जघनं रतिप्राभृतमुत्तमम् ।। 7.26.16 ।।
explanation: Bearing her hips, which were captivating to the eyes, plump, adorned with a girdle-chain, and an excellent offering for love.

shloka_text: कृतैर्विशेषकैरार्द्रैः षडर्तुकुसुमोद्भवैः ।। 7.26.17 ।।
explanation: With fresh decorative marks made from flowers of the six seasons.

shloka_text: बभावन्यतमेव श्रीकान्तिद्युतिमतिह्रियाम् । नीलं सतोयमेघाभं वस्त्रं समवकुण्ठिता ।। 7.26.18 ।।
explanation: She shone as one of the foremost among those possessing beauty, radiance, brilliance, intelligence, and modesty, enveloped in a blue garment resembling a water-laden cloud.

shloka_text: यस्या वक्त्रं शशिनिभं भ्रुवौ चापनिभे शुभे । ऊरू करिकराकारौ करौ पल्लवकोमलौ । सैन्यमध्येन गच्छन्ती रावणेनोपवीक्षिता ।। 7.26.19 ।।
explanation: Whose face was like the moon, whose beautiful eyebrows were like bows, whose thighs resembled elephant trunks, and whose hands were soft as new leaves, she, while passing through the midst of the army, was observed by Ravana.

shloka_text: तां समुत्थाय गच्छन्तीं कामबाणवशं गतः । करे गृहीत्वा लज्जन्तीं स्मयमानो ऽभ्यभाषत ।। 7.26.20 ।।
explanation: Overcome by the arrows of desire, he rose up and, seizing her hand as she was going and blushing, he spoke to her with a smile.

shloka_text: क्व गच्छसि वरारोहे कां सिद्धिं भजसे स्वयम् । कस्याभ्युदयकालो ऽयं यस्त्वां समुपभोक्ष्यते ।। 7.26.21 ।।
explanation: O lady with beautiful hips, where are you going? What accomplishment do you seek for yourself? Whose time of prosperity is this, that he will enjoy you?

shloka_text: त्वदाननरसस्याद्य पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिनः । सुधामृतरसस्येव को ऽद्य तृप्तिं गमिष्यति ।। 7.26.22 ।।
explanation: Who today will attain satisfaction from the nectar of your face, fragrant like a lotus and a water-lily, and like the nectar of ambrosia?

shloka_text: स्वर्णकुम्भनिभौ पीनौ शुभौ भीरु निरन्तरौ । कस्योरस्थलसंस्पर्शं दास्यतस्ते कुचाविमौ ।। 7.26.23 ।।
explanation: O timid one, these two plump, beautiful breasts of yours, resembling golden pitchers and close together, to whose chest will they grant their touch?

shloka_text: सुवर्णचक्रप्रतिमं स्वर्णदामचितं पृथु । अध्यारोहति कस्ते ऽद्य जघनं स्वर्गरूपिणम् ।। 7.26.24 ।।
explanation: Who today will ascend your broad, heaven-like hips, which are like a golden wheel and adorned with golden chains?

shloka_text: मद्विशिष्टः पुमान्को ऽद्य शक्रो विष्णुरथाश्विनौ । मामतीत्य हि यं च त्वं यासि भीरु न शोभनम् ।। 7.26.25 ।।
explanation: Who is the man superior to me today? Is it Indra, Vishnu, or the Ashvins? Indeed, O timid one, it is not proper that you go to him, bypassing me.

shloka_text: विश्रम त्वं पृथुश्रोणि शिलातलमिदं शुभम् ।। 7.26.26 ।।
explanation: O broad-hipped one, rest on this auspicious stone surface.

shloka_text: त्रैलोक्ये यः प्रभुश्चैव मदन्यो नैव विद्यते ।। 7.26.27 ।।
explanation: He who is the lord in the three worlds, and indeed, no other exists besides me.

shloka_text: तदेवं प्राञ्जलिः प्रह्वो याचते त्वां दशाननः । भर्तुर्भर्ता विधाता च त्रैलोक्यस्य भजस्व माम् ।। 7.26.28 ।।
explanation: Thus, Daśānana, with folded hands and bowed, begs you: "You are the master of masters and the creator of the three worlds. Serve me!"

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता ऽब्रवीद्रम्भा वेपमाना कृताञ्जलिः । प्रसीद नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशं त्वं हि मे गुरुः ।। 7.26.29 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Rambha, trembling and with folded hands, said: "Be gracious! You ought not to speak such a thing, for you are indeed my guru."

shloka_text: अन्येभ्यो हि त्वया रक्ष्या प्राप्नुयां धर्षणं यदि । तद्धर्मतः स्नुषा ते ऽहं तत्त्वमेव ब्रवीमि ते ।। 7.26.30 ।।
explanation: Indeed, I must be protected by you from others, should I suffer molestation. Therefore, by dharma, I am your daughter-in-law; I tell you the truth itself.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्दशग्रीवश्चरणाधोमुखीं स्थिताम् । रोमहर्षमनुप्राप्तां दृष्टमात्रेण तां तदा ।। 7.26.31 ।।
explanation: Then Dashagriva spoke to her, who was standing with her face bowed down towards her feet, having experienced horripilation merely upon seeing him then.

shloka_text: सुतस्य यदि मे भार्या ततस्त्वं हि स्नुषा भवेः । बाढमित्येव सा रम्भा प्राह रावणमुत्तरम् ।। 7.26.32 ।।
explanation: If you were the wife of my son, then you would indeed be my daughter-in-law. Rambha then replied to Ravana, "Very well."

shloka_text: धर्मतस्ते सुतस्याहं भार्या राक्षसपुङ्गव । पुत्रः प्रियतरः प्राणैर्भ्रातुर्वैश्रवणस्य ते । विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु नलकूबर इत्ययम् ।। 7.26.33 ।।
explanation: O best of Rakshasas, I am lawfully the wife of your son. This Nalakubara, the son of your brother Vaishravana, is dearer than life and renowned in the three worlds.

shloka_text: धर्मतो यो भवेद्विप्रः क्षत्रियो वीर्यतो भवेत् । क्रोधाद्यश्च भवेदग्निः क्षान्त्या च वसुधासमः ।। 7.26.34 ।।
explanation: He who is a Brahmana by righteousness, a Kshatriya by valor; and becomes like fire by anger, and like the earth by forbearance.

shloka_text: तस्यास्मि कृतसङ्केता लोकपालसुतस्य वै । तमुद्दिश्य तु मे सर्वं विभूषणमिदं कृतम् ।। 7.26.35 ।।
explanation: I am committed to him, the son of the Lokapala. Indeed, all these ornaments of mine have been made for his sake.

shloka_text: तथा तस्य हि नान्यस्य भावो मां प्रति तिष्ठति ।। 7.26.36 ।।
explanation: Thus, indeed, his feeling towards me does not exist for anyone else.

shloka_text: तेन सत्येन मां राजन्मोक्तुमर्हस्यरिन्दम ।। 7.26.37 ।।
explanation: O King, O vanquisher of foes, by that truth, you ought to release me.

shloka_text: स हि तिष्ठति धर्मात्मा मां प्रतीक्ष्य समुत्सुकः । तत्र विघ्नं सुतस्येह कर्तुं नार्हसि मुञ्च माम् ।। 7.26.38 ।।
explanation: Indeed, that righteous soul waits for me, very eager. You should not create an obstacle for the son in this matter. Release me.

shloka_text: सद्भिराचरितं मार्गं गच्छ राक्षसुपुङ्गव । माननीयो मम त्वं हि पालनीया तथा ऽस्मि ते ।। 7.26.39 ।।
explanation: Follow the path trodden by the virtuous, O best among Rākṣasas. You are indeed worthy of my respect, and I am to be protected by you.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रत्युवाच विनीतवत् । स्नुषा ऽस्मि यदवोचस्त्वमेकपत्नीष्वयं क्रमः । देवलोकस्थितिरियं सुराणां शाश्वती मता ।। 7.26.40 ।।
explanation: Thus spoken, Dashagriva replied humbly: "I am your daughter-in-law, as you said. This is the custom among chaste wives. This is considered the eternal custom of the gods in the divine realm."

shloka_text: पतिरप्सरसां नास्ति न चैकस्त्रीपरिग्रहः ।। 7.26.41 ।।
explanation: Apsaras have no husband, nor is there the custom of being taken as a single wife.

shloka_text: अस्मि यदवोचस्त्वमेकपत्नीष्वयं क्रमः । एवमुक्त्वा स तां रक्षो निवेश्य च शिलातले । कामभोगाभिसंसक्तो मैथुनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.26.42 ।।
explanation: "I am aware of what you said: 'This is the custom among chaste wives.' " Having thus spoken, that demon, having seated her on the rock surface, deeply engrossed in sensual pleasures, proceeded for sexual intercourse.

shloka_text: सा विमुक्ता ततो रम्भा भ्रष्टमाल्यविभूषणा । गजेन्द्राक्रीडमथिता नदीवाकुलतां गता ।। 7.26.43 ।।
explanation: Then Rambha, released, with her garlands and ornaments dishevelled, became agitated like a river churned by the sport of a great elephant.

shloka_text: लुलिताकुलकेशान्ता करवेपितपल्लवा । पवनेनावधूतेव लता कुसुमशालिनी ।। 7.26.44 ।।
explanation: Her hair dishevelled and agitated, her hands trembling like quivering sprouts, she was like a flower-laden creeper shaken by the wind.

shloka_text: सा वेपमाना लज्जन्ती भीता करकृताञ्जलिः । नलकूबरमासाद्य पादयोर्निपपात ह ।। 7.26.45 ।।
explanation: She, trembling, ashamed, and frightened, with folded hands, approached Nalakūbara and fell at his feet.

shloka_text: तदवस्थां च तां दृष्ट्वा महात्मा नलकूबरः । अब्रवीत्किमिदं भद्रे पादयोः पतिता ऽसि मे ।। 7.26.46 ।।
explanation: And seeing her in that state, the great Nalakūbara said, "What is this, O good lady, that you have fallen at my feet?"

shloka_text: सा वै निःश्वसमाना तु वेपमाना कृताञ्जलिः । तस्मै सर्वं यथातत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.26.47 ।।
explanation: She, indeed, sighing and trembling, with folded hands, began to narrate everything to him as it truly was.

shloka_text: एष देव दशग्रीवः प्राप्तो गन्तुं त्रिविष्टपम् । तेन सैन्यसहायेन निशेयं परिणामिता ।। 7.26.48 ।।
explanation: O god, this Dashagriva has come to go to heaven. With the help of his army, he has brought this night to an end.

shloka_text: आयन्ती तेन दृष्टा ऽस्मि त्वत्सकाशमरिन्दम । गृहीता तेन पृष्टा ऽस्मि कस्य त्वमिति रक्षसा ।। 7.26.49 ।।
explanation: O destroyer of enemies, I was seen by him as I was coming to your presence. I was seized by him, and the demon asked me, "Whose are you?"

shloka_text: मया तु सर्वं यत्सत्यं तस्मै सर्वं निवेदितम् । काममोहाभिभूतात्मा नाश्रौषीत्तद्वचो मम ।। 7.26.50 ।।
explanation: I indeed told him all the truth, everything. But his mind, overpowered by lust and delusion, did not listen to my words.

shloka_text: याच्यमानो मया देव स्नुषा ते ऽहमिति प्रभो । तत्सर्वं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा बलात्तेनास्मि धर्षिता ।। 7.26.51 ।।
explanation: O god, O lord, though I implored him, saying, 'I am your daughter-in-law,' he disregarded all that and violated me by force.

shloka_text: एवं त्वमपराधं मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत । न हि तुल्यं बलं सौम्य स्त्रियाश्च पुरुषस्य च ।। 7.26.52 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O virtuous one, you should forgive my offense. For, O gentle one, the strength of a woman and a man is certainly not equal.

shloka_text: एतछुत्वा तु सङ्क्रुद्धस्तदा वैश्रवणात्मजः । धर्षणां तां परां श्रुत्वा ध्यानं सम्प्रविवेश ह ।। 7.26.53 ।।
explanation: Having heard this, then Vaiśravaṇa's son, greatly enraged upon hearing of that extreme outrage, entered into deep thought.

shloka_text: तस्य तत्कर्म विज्ञाय तदा वैश्रवणात्मजः । मुहूर्तात्क्रोधताम्राक्षस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना ।। 7.26.54 ।।
explanation: Having understood his deed, then the son of Vaishravana, in an instant, with eyes red with anger, took water in his hand.

shloka_text: गृहीत्वा सलिलं सर्वमुपस्पृश्य यथाविधि । उत्ससर्ज यथा शापं राक्षसेन्द्राय दारुणम् ।। 7.26.55 ।।
explanation: Having taken all the water and performed the ritual ablution, he uttered a terrible curse upon the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: अकामा तेन यस्मात्त्वं बलाद्भद्रे प्रधर्षिता । तस्मात्स युवतीमन्यां नाकामामुपयास्यति ।। 7.26.56 ।।
explanation: Because you, O good lady, were forcibly violated by him against your will, therefore he will not approach another young woman against her will.

shloka_text: यदा ह्यकामां कामार्तो धर्षयिष्यति योषितम् । मूर्धा तु सप्तधा तस्य शकलीभविता तदा ।। 7.26.57 ।।
explanation: When a man, afflicted by lust, violates an unwilling woman, then his head will be shattered into seven pieces.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नुदाहृते शापे ज्वलिताग्निसमप्रभे । देवदुन्दुभयो नेदुः पुष्पवृष्टिश्च खाच्च्युता । पितामहमुखाश्चैव सर्वे देवाः प्रहर्षिताः ।। 7.26.58 ।।
explanation: When that curse, shining like a blazing fire, was uttered, divine drums sounded, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky. All the gods, led by Brahma, were greatly delighted.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा लोकगतिं सर्वां तस्य मृत्युं च रक्षसः । ऋषयः पितरश्चैव प्रीतिमापुरनुत्तमाम् ।। 7.26.59 ।।
explanation: Having known all the ways of the world, and the death of that demon, the sages and the ancestors attained unsurpassed joy.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु स दशग्रीवस्तं शापं रोमहर्षणम् । नारीषु मैथुने भावं नाकामास्वभ्यरोचयत् ।। 7.26.60 ।।
explanation: Upon hearing that terrifying curse, Daśagrīva did not desire sexual union with unwilling women.

shloka_text: तेन नीताः स्त्रियः प्रीतिमापुः सर्वाः पतिव्रताः । नलकूबरनिर्मुक्तं शापं श्रुत्वा मनःप्रियम् ।। 7.26.61 ।।
explanation: All the chaste wives, led by him, attained joy, having heard the curse from which Nalakūbara was freed, which was pleasing to their hearts.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षड्वविंशः सर्गः ।। 26 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the twenty-sixth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: कैलासं लङ्घयित्वाथ दशग्रीवः स रावणः । आससाद महातेजा इन्द्रलोकं निशाचरः ।। 7.27.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having crossed Kailasa, that Dashagriva Ravana, the greatly powerful night-wanderer, reached Indraloka.

shloka_text: तस्य राक्षससैन्यस्य समन्तादुपयास्यतः । देवलोकं ययौ शब्दो मथ्यमानार्णवोपमः ।। 7.27.2 ।।
explanation: The sound of that demon army, advancing from all sides, reached the world of gods, like the churning ocean.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु रावणं प्राप्तमिन्द्रश्चलित आसनात् । अब्रवीत्तत्र तान् देवान् सर्वानेव समागतान् ।। 7.27.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard that Ravana had arrived, Indra moved from his seat. He then spoke to all the gods who had assembled there.

shloka_text: आदित्यान्सवसून्रुद्रान्विश्वान्साध्यान्मरुद्गणान् । सज्जीभवत युद्धार्थं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः ।। 7.27.4 ।।
explanation: Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Vishvas, Sadhyas, and hosts of Maruts, prepare yourselves for battle against the wicked Ravana.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तास्तु शक्रेण देवाः शक्रसमा युधि । सन्नह्य सुमहासत्त्वा युद्धश्रद्धासमन्विताः ।। 7.27.5 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Shakra, the gods, who were equal to Shakra in battle, of great valor, and filled with eagerness for war, armed themselves.

shloka_text: स तु दीनः परित्रस्तो महेन्द्रो रावणं प्रति । विष्णोः समीपमागत्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.27.6 ।।
explanation: But he, Mahendra, distressed and greatly frightened by Ravana, approached Vishnu and spoke these words.

shloka_text: विष्णो कथं करिष्यामि महावीर्यपराक्रमः । असौ हि बलवद्रक्षो युद्धार्थमभिवर्तते ।। 7.27.7 ।।
explanation: O Vishnu, how shall I proceed? This powerful demon, possessing great might and valor, is indeed approaching for battle.

shloka_text: वरप्रदानाद्बलवान्न खल्वन्येन हेतुना । तत्तु सत्यवचः कार्यं यदुक्तं पद्मयोनिना ।। 7.27.8 ।।
explanation: He is powerful due to the boon, certainly not by any other reason. But that truthful word which was spoken by the lotus-born (Brahma) must be fulfilled.

shloka_text: तद्यथा नमुचिर्वृत्रो बलिर्नरकशम्बरौ । त्वद्बलं समवष्टभ्य मया दग्धास्तथा कुरु ।। 7.27.9 ।।
explanation: Just as Namuchi, Vritra, Bali, Naraka, and Shambara were destroyed by me, relying on your strength, so do likewise.

shloka_text: नह्यन्यो देवदेवेश त्वामृते मधुसूदन । गतिः परायणं नास्ति त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे ।। 7.27.10 ।।
explanation: O Lord of Lords, O Madhusudana, without you, there is indeed no other refuge or ultimate resort in the three worlds, including all animate and inanimate beings.

shloka_text: त्वं हि नारायणः श्रीमान्पद्मनाभः सनातनः । त्वयेमे स्थापिता लोकाः शक्रश्चाहं सुरेश्वरः ।। 7.27.11 ।।
explanation: You are indeed Narayana, the glorious, Padmanabha, the eternal. By you were these worlds established, and I, Shakra, the lord of gods.

shloka_text: त्वया सृष्टमिदं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् । त्वामेव भगवन्सर्वे प्रविशन्ति युगक्षये ।। 7.27.12 ।।
explanation: This entire three worlds, with its moving and non-moving beings, was created by you. O Lord, all enter you alone at the end of an age.

shloka_text: तदाचक्ष्व यथा तत्त्वं देवदेव मम स्वयम् । अपि चक्रसहायस्त्वं योत्स्यसे रावणं प्रभो ।। 7.27.13 ।।
explanation: O God of gods, O Lord, tell me the truth yourself: will you fight Ravana, even aided by the discus?

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः स शक्रेण देवो नारायणः प्रभुः । अब्रवीन्न परित्रासः कर्तव्यः श्रूयतां च मे ।। 7.27.14 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Shakra, the lord god Narayana said, "Do not be afraid, and listen to me."

shloka_text: न तावदेष दुष्टात्मा शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः । हन्तुं चापि समासाद्य वरदानेन दुर्जयः ।। 7.27.15 ।।
explanation: This wicked soul cannot be conquered by gods and asuras. And even if approached, he is invincible due to the boon, making him impossible to kill.

shloka_text: सर्वथा तु महत्कर्म करिष्यति बलोत्कटः । राक्षसः पुत्रसहितो दृष्टमेतन्निसर्गतः ।। 7.27.16 ।।
explanation: Certainly, the exceedingly powerful Rakshasa, along with his son, will perform a great deed. This is naturally observed.

shloka_text: यत्तु मां त्वमभाषिष्ठ युद्ध्यस्वेति सुरेश्वर । नाहं तं प्रतियोत्स्यामि रावणं राक्षसं युधि ।। 7.27.17 ।।
explanation: But as for what you, O lord of gods, told me, 'Fight!', I will not fight against that demon Ravana in battle.

shloka_text: नाहत्वा समरे शत्रुं विष्णुः प्रतिनिवर्तते । दुर्लभश्चैव कामो ऽद्य वरगुप्ताद्धि रावणात् ।। 7.27.18 ।।
explanation: Vishnu does not return from battle without slaying the enemy. And indeed, the desired object is difficult to obtain now, as Ravana is protected by a boon.

shloka_text: प्रतिजाने च देवेन्द्र त्वत्समीपे शतक्रतो । भविता ऽस्मि यथा ऽस्याहं रक्षसो मृत्युकारणम् ।। 7.27.19 ।।
explanation: And I vow, O Devendra, O Shatakratu, in your presence, that I shall become the cause of death for this Rakshasa.

shloka_text: अहमेव निहन्ता ऽस्मि रावणं सपुरःसरम् । देवता नन्दयिष्यामि ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम् । एतत्ते कथितं तत्त्वं देवराज शचीपते ।। 7.27.20 ।।
explanation: I myself will slay Ravana along with his followers. I will gladden the gods, knowing that the time has come. This truth has been revealed to you, O King of Gods, husband of Sachi.

shloka_text: युद्ध्यस्व विगतत्रासः सर्वैः सार्धं महाबल ।। 7.27.21 ।।
explanation: O mighty one, fight fearlessly with all.

shloka_text: यामि ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम् । ततो रुद्राः सहादित्या वसवो मरुतो ऽश्वनौ । सन्नद्धा निर्ययुस्तूर्णं राक्षसानभितः पुरात् ।। 7.27.22 ।।
explanation: I go, having known that the time has arrived. Then the Rudras with the Adityas, the Vasus, the Maruts, and the Ashvins, equipped, quickly went out from the city towards the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे नादः शुश्रुवे रजनीक्षये । तस्य रावणसैन्यस्य प्रयुद्धस्य समन्ततः ।। 7.27.23 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, at the end of the night, a sound was heard from Ravana's army, which was fighting all around.

shloka_text: ते प्रयुद्धा महावीर्या ह्यन्योन्यमभिवीक्ष्य वै । सङ्ग्राममेवाभिमुखा ह्यभवर्तन्त हृष्टवत् ।। 7.27.24 ।।
explanation: They, the greatly valorous and battle-ready ones, having looked at each other, indeed advanced towards the battle joyfully.
