shloka_text: ततो दैवतसैन्यनां सङ्क्षोभः समजायत । तदक्षयं महासैन्यं दृष्ट्वा समरमूर्धनि ।। 7.27.25 ।।
explanation: Then, seeing that indestructible great army at the forefront of the battle, a commotion arose among the armies of the gods.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवेद्देवदानवरक्षसाम् । घोरं तुमुलनिर्ह्रादं नानाप्रहरणोद्यतम् ।। 7.27.26 ।।
explanation: Then a terrible battle arose among the gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, with tumultuous roars and various weapons uplifted.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरा राक्षसा घोरदर्शनाः । युद्धार्थं समवर्तन्त सचिवा रावणस्य ते ।। 7.27.27 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, those brave demons, Ravana's ministers, dreadful to behold, assembled for battle.

shloka_text: मारीचश्च प्रहस्तश्च महापार्श्वमहोदरौ । अकम्पनो निकुम्भश्च शुकः सारण एव च ।। 7.27.28 ।।
explanation: Maricha, Prahasta, Mahaparshva, Mahodara, Akampana, Nikumbha, Shuka, and Sarana.

shloka_text: संह्लादो धूमकेतुश्च महादंष्ट्रो घटोदरः । जम्बुमाली महाह्रादो विरूपाक्षश्च राक्षसः ।। 7.27.29 ।।
explanation: Saṃhlāda, Dhūmaketu, Mahādaṃṣṭra, Ghaṭodara, Jambumālī, Mahāhrāda, and Virūpākṣa, the Rākṣasa.

shloka_text: सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च दुर्मुखो दूषणः खरः । त्रिशिराः करवीराक्षः सूर्यशत्रुश्च राक्षसः ।। 7.27.30 ।।
explanation: Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, Durmukha, Dushana, Khara, Trishira, Karaviraksha, and Suryashatru were Rakshasas.

shloka_text: महाकायो ऽतिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ । एतैः सर्वैः परिवृतो महावीर्यो महाबलः ।। 7.27.31 ।।
explanation: Mahakaya and Atikaya, Devantaka and Narantaka. Surrounded by all these, (he was) of great valor and great strength.

shloka_text: रावणस्यार्यकः सैन्यं सुमाली प्रविवेश ह । स दैवतगणान्सर्वान्नानाप्रहरणैः शितैः । व्यध्वंसयत्सुसङ्क्रुद्धो वायुर्जलधरानिव ।। 7.27.32 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa's grandfather Sumali entered the army. He, extremely enraged, destroyed all the hosts of gods with various sharp weapons, just as the wind scatters clouds.

shloka_text: तद्दैवतबलं राम हन्यमानं निशाचरैः । प्रणुन्नं सर्वतो दिग्भ्यः सिंहनुन्ना मृगा इव ।। 7.27.33 ।।
explanation: O Rama, that army of gods, being struck by the night-wanderers, was scattered from all directions, like deer driven by lions.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरो वसूनामष्टमो वसुः । सावित्र इति विख्यातः प्रविवेश रणाजिरम् ।। 7.27.34 ।।
explanation: Meanwhile, the brave eighth Vasu among the Vasus, renowned as Savitra, entered the battlefield.

shloka_text: तथा ऽ ऽदित्यौ महावीर्यौ त्वष्टा पूषा च दंशितौ । निंर्भयौ सह सैन्येन तदा प्राविशतां रणे ।। 7.27.35 ।।
explanation: And so, the two Adityas of great valor, Tvashta and Pushan, armored and fearless, then entered the battle with their army.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवत्सुराणां सह राक्षसैः । क्रुद्धानां रक्षसां कीर्तिं समरेष्वनिवर्तिनाम् ।। 7.27.36 ।।
explanation: Then a battle occurred between the gods and the Rākṣasas, who were enraged and famous for never retreating in battles.

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विबुधान्समरे स्थितान् । नानाप्रहरणैर्घोरैर्जघ्नुः शतसहस्रशः ।। 7.27.37 ।।
explanation: Then all those Rakshasas struck the gods standing in battle, with various terrible weapons, hundreds of thousands of times.

shloka_text: देवाश्च राक्षसान्घोरान्महाबलपराक्रमान् । समरे विमलैः शस्त्रैरुपनिन्युर्यमक्षयम् ।। 7.27.38 ।।
explanation: And the gods, in battle, with their bright weapons, brought the terrible Rākṣasas, who were of great strength and valor, to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम सुमाली नाम राक्षसः । नानाप्रहरणैः क्रुद्धस्तत्सैन्यं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.27.39 ।।
explanation: O Rama, at that moment, the demon named Sumali, enraged, attacked that army with various weapons.

shloka_text: स दैवतबलं सर्वं नानाप्रहणैः शितैः । व्यध्वंसयत सङ्क्रुद्धो वायुर्जलधरं यथा ।। 7.27.40 ।।
explanation: Greatly enraged, he destroyed the entire army of the gods with sharp, various weapons, just as the wind scatters a cloud.

shloka_text: ते महाबाणवर्षैश्च शूलप्रासैः सुदारुणैः । हन्यमानाः सुराः सर्वे न व्यतिष्ठन्त संहताः ।। 7.27.41 ।।
explanation: All those gods, being struck by very terrible showers of great arrows and by spears and javelins, could not stand firm united.

shloka_text: ततो विद्राव्यमाणेषु दैवतेषु सुमालिना । वसूनामष्टमः क्रुद्धः सावित्रो वै व्यवस्थितः ।। 7.27.42 ।।
explanation: Then, when the gods were being put to flight by Sumali, the eighth of the Vasus, Savitra, enraged, stood firm.

shloka_text: संवृतः स्वैरथानीकैः प्रहरन्तं निशाचरम् । विक्रमेण महातेजा वारयामास संयुगे ।। 7.27.43 ।।
explanation: The mighty one, surrounded by his own chariot armies, in battle, by his prowess, warded off the attacking demon.

shloka_text: ततस्तयोर्महायुद्धमभवद्रोमहर्षणम् ।। 7.27.44 ।।
explanation: Then a great and hair-raising battle occurred between those two.

shloka_text: सुमालिनो वसोश्चैव समरेष्वनिवर्तिनोः । ततस्तस्य महाबाणैर्वसुना सुमहात्मना । निहतः पन्नगरथः क्षणेन विनिपातितः ।। 7.27.45 ।।
explanation: Sumalin and Vasu were both unyielding in battles. Then, the very great-souled Vasu, with his mighty arrows, struck down Sumalin's serpent-chariot, felling it in an instant.

shloka_text: हत्वा तु संयुगे तस्य रथं बाणशतैश्चितम् । गदां तस्य वधार्थाय वसुर्जग्राह पाणिना ।। 7.27.46 ।।
explanation: Having destroyed his chariot, which was pierced by hundreds of arrows, in battle, Vasu then grasped a mace with his hand to kill him.

shloka_text: ततः प्रगृह्य दीप्ताग्रां कालदण्डोपमां गदाम् । तां मूर्ध्नि पातयामास सावित्रो वै सुमालिनः ।। 7.27.47 ।।
explanation: Then, having seized the mace with a blazing tip, resembling the staff of Yama, Savitri's son indeed struck it on Sumalin's head.

shloka_text: सा तस्योपरि चोल्काभा पतन्तीव बभौ गदा । इन्द्रप्रमुक्ता गर्जन्ती गिराविव महाशनिः ।। 7.27.48 ।।
explanation: That mace, falling upon him, shone like a meteor, and like a great thunderbolt released by Indra, roaring upon a mountain.

shloka_text: तस्य नैवास्थि न शिरो न मांसं ददृशे तदा । गदया भस्मतां नीतं निहतस्य रणाजिरे ।। 7.27.49 ।।
explanation: Neither his bone, nor head, nor flesh was seen then. The slain one had been reduced to ashes by the mace on the battlefield.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं सङ्ख्ये राक्षसास्ते समन्ततः । व्यद्रवन्सहिताः सर्वे क्रोशमानाः परस्परम् । विद्राव्यमाणा वसुना राक्षसा नावतस्थिरे ।। 7.27.50 ।।
explanation: Seeing him killed in battle, all those Rakshasas from all sides fled together, crying out to each other. Being driven away by Vasu, the Rakshasas did not stand their ground.

shloka_text: सुमालिनं हतं दृष्ट्वा वसुना भस्मसात्कृतम् । स्वसैन्यं विद्रुतं चापि लक्षयित्वा ऽर्दितं सुरैः ।। 7.28.1 ।।
explanation: Having seen Sumalin killed and reduced to ashes by Vasu, and having also observed his own army scattered and tormented by the gods,

shloka_text: ततः स बलवान्क्रुद्धो रावणस्य सुतस्तदा । निवर्त्य राक्षसान्सर्वान्मेघनादो व्यवस्थितः ।। 7.28.2 ।।
explanation: Then, that mighty son of Ravana, Meghanada, enraged, having dismissed all the Rakshasas, took his stand.

shloka_text: सुरथेनाग्निवर्णेन कामगेन महारथः । अभिदुद्राव सेनां तां वनान्यग्निरिव ज्वलन् ।। 7.28.3 ।।
explanation: The great charioteer, Agnivarna, with his excellent chariot that moved at will, rushed towards that army, blazing like fire consuming forests.

shloka_text: ततः प्रविशतस्तस्य विविधायुधधारिणः । विदुद्रुवुर्दिशः सर्वा दर्शनादेव देवताः ।। 7.28.4 ।।
explanation: Then, as he, bearing various weapons, entered, all the deities fled in all directions merely at his sight.

shloka_text: न बभूव तदा कश्चिद्युयुत्सोरस्य सम्मुखे । सर्वानाविद्ध्य वित्रस्तांस्ततः शक्रो ऽब्रवीत्सुरान् ।। 7.28.5 ।।
explanation: Then, no one was able to stand before him, who was eager to fight. Having struck all and made them terrified, Shakra then spoke to the gods.

shloka_text: न भेतव्यं न गन्तव्यं निवर्तध्वं रणे सुराः । एष गच्छति पुत्रो मे युद्धार्थमपराजितः ।। 7.28.6 ।।
explanation: O gods, do not fear, do not retreat; return to the battle. My unconquered son goes forth for battle.

shloka_text: ततः शक्रसुतो देवो जयन्त इति विश्रुतः । रथेनाद्भुतकल्पेन सङ्ग्रामे सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.28.7 ।।
explanation: Then, the divine son of Indra, renowned as Jayanta, advanced into the battle with a wonderfully designed chariot.

shloka_text: ततस्ते त्रिदशाः सर्वे परिवार्य शचीसुतम् । रावणस्य सुतं युद्धे समासाद्य प्रजघ्निरे ।। 7.28.8 ।।
explanation:
ुतम" be a compound? No, it's clearly "शचीसुतम्".

shloka_text: तेषां युद्धं समभवत्सदृशं देवरक्षसाम् । महेन्द्रस्य च पुत्रस्य राक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्य च ।। 7.28.9 ।।
explanation: Their battle, similar to that of gods and demons, took place between Mahendra's son and the son of the king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ततो मातलिपुत्रे तु गोमुखे राक्षसात्मजः । सारथौ पातयामास शरान्कनकभूषणान् ।। 7.28.10 ।।
explanation: Then, the son of the Rākṣasa shot gold-ornamented arrows at Gomukha, the charioteer, Matali's son.

shloka_text: शचीसुतश्चापि तथा जयन्तस्तस्य सारथिम् । तं चापि रावणिः क्रुद्धः समन्तात्प्रत्यविध्यत ।। 7.28.11 ।।
explanation: And similarly, Jayanta, the son of Sachi, and his charioteer – him too, Ravani, enraged, pierced from all sides.

shloka_text: स हि क्रोधसमाविष्टो बली विस्फारितेक्षणः । रावणिः शक्रतनयं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ।। 7.28.12 ।।
explanation: Indeed, that powerful son of Ravana, overcome by rage and with wide-open eyes, assailed the son of Indra with showers of arrows.

shloka_text: ततो नानाप्रहरणाञ्छितधारान्सहस्रशः । पातयामास सङ्क्रुद्धः सुरसैन्येषु रावणिः ।। 7.28.13 ।।
explanation: Then, greatly enraged, Ravani hurled thousands of sharp-edged, various weapons upon the armies of the gods.

shloka_text: शतघ्नीमुसलप्रासगदाखड्गपरश्वधान् । महान्ति गिरिशृङ्गाणि पातयामास रावणिः ।। 7.28.14 ।।
explanation: Ravani hurled down śataghnīs, pestles, spears, maces, swords, axes, and great mountain peaks.

shloka_text: ततः प्रव्यथिता लोकाः सञ्जज्ञे च तमो ऽभवत् । तस्य रावणपुत्रस्य शत्रुसैन्यानि निघ्नतः ।। 7.28.15 ।।
explanation: Then the people were greatly distressed, and darkness arose, as Ravana's son was destroying the enemy armies.

shloka_text: ततस्तद्दैवतबलं समन्तात्तं शचीसुतम् । बहुप्रकारमस्वस्थमभवच्छरपीडितम् ।। 7.28.16 ।।
explanation: Then, that divine army, tormented by arrows all around that son of Shachi, became greatly distressed in many ways.

shloka_text: नाभ्यजानन्त चान्योन्यं रक्षो वा देवता ऽथवा । तत्र तत्र विपर्यस्तं समन्तात्परिधावति ।। 7.28.17 ।।
explanation: They did not recognize each other, whether a demon or a deity. Confused, they ran about here and there, all around.

shloka_text: देवा देवान्निजघ्नुस्ते राक्षसान्राक्षसास्तथा । सम्मूढास्तमसाच्छन्ना व्यद्रवन्नपरे तथा ।। 7.28.18 ।।
explanation: Gods killed gods, and demons likewise killed demons. Bewildered and enveloped in darkness, others fled.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः पुलोमा नाम वीर्यवान् । दैत्येन्द्रस्तेन सङ्गृह्य शचीपुत्रो ऽपवाहितः ।। 7.28.19 ।।
explanation: At that moment, the brave and powerful lord of Daityas named Puloma, having seized Shachi's son, carried him away.

shloka_text: सङ्गृह्य तं तु दौहित्रं प्रविष्टः सागरं तदा । आर्यकः स हि तस्यासीत्पुलोमा येन सा शची ।। 7.28.20 ।।
explanation: Having taken that grandson, he then entered the ocean. Indeed, he was his grandfather, Puloma, whose daughter was Shachi.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा प्रणाशं तु तदा जयन्तस्याथ देवताः । अप्रहृष्टास्ततः सर्वा व्यथिताः सम्प्रदुद्रुवुः ।। 7.28.21 ।।
explanation: Then, having learned of Jayanta's demise, all the gods, dejected and distressed, fled.

shloka_text: रावणिस्त्वथ सङ्क्रुद्धो बलैः परिवृतः स्वकैः । अभ्यधावत देवांस्तान्मुमोच च महास्वनम् ।। 7.28.22 ।।
explanation: Then, the son of Ravana, greatly enraged, surrounded by his own forces, rushed towards those gods and let out a great roar.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा प्रणाशं पुत्रस्य दैवतेषु च विद्रुतम् । मातलिं चाह देवेशो रथः समुपनीयताम् ।। 7.28.23 ।।
explanation: Having seen the destruction of his son and the flight of the gods, the lord of the gods said to Matali, "Let the chariot be brought forth."

shloka_text: स तु दिव्यो महाभीमः सज्ज एव महारथः । उपस्थितो मातलिना वाह्यमानो महाजवः ।। 7.28.24 ।।
explanation: But that divine, exceedingly formidable, and fully equipped great chariot, of great speed, driven by Matali, appeared.

shloka_text: ततो मेघा रथे तस्मिंस्तडित्त्वन्तो महाबलाः । अग्रतो वायुचपला नेदुः परमनिःस्वनाः ।। 7.28.25 ।।
explanation: Then, mighty clouds, possessing lightning, swift as the wind, roared with a very loud sound in front of that chariot.

shloka_text: नानावाद्यानि वाद्यन्त गन्धर्वाश्च समाहिताः । ननृतुश्चाप्सरःसङ्घा निर्याते त्रिदशेश्वरे ।। 7.28.26 ।।
explanation: Various musical instruments were played, and the Gandharvas, absorbed, and groups of Apsaras danced, when the lord of the gods came forth.

shloka_text: रुद्रैर्वसुभिरादित्यैस्साध्यैश्च समरुद्गणैः । वृतो नानाप्रहरणैर्निर्ययौ त्रिदशाधिपः ।। 7.28.27 ।।
explanation: The lord of the gods, surrounded by the Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, Sadhyas, and the hosts of Maruts, and bearing various weapons, went forth.

shloka_text: निर्गच्छतस्तु शक्रस्य परुषं पवनो ववौ । भास्करो निष्प्रभश्चासीन्महोल्काश्च प्रपेदिरे ।। 7.28.28 ।।
explanation: As Shakra was departing, the wind blew harshly. The sun lost its brilliance, and great meteors fell down.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शूरो दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् । आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा ।। 7.28.29 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the brave and mighty Dashagriva mounted the divine chariot built by Vishwakarma.

shloka_text: पन्नगैः सुमहाकार्यैर्वेष्टितं रोमहर्षणैः । तेषां निःश्वासवातेन प्रदीप्तमिव संयुगे ।। 7.28.30 ।।
explanation: Surrounded by terrifying serpents of immense size, it was as if ablaze in battle from the wind of their breath.

shloka_text: दैत्यैर्निशाचरैश्चैव स रथः परिवारितः । समराभिमुखो दैत्यो महेन्द्रं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.28.31 ।।
explanation: That chariot was surrounded by demons and night-wanderers. The demon, facing battle, advanced towards Mahendra.

shloka_text: पुत्रं तं वारयित्वा तु स्वयमेव व्यवस्थितः । सो ऽपि युद्धाद्विनिष्क्रम्य रावणिः समुपाविशत् ।। 7.28.32 ।।
explanation: Having restrained that son, he himself took his stand. Ravana's son also, having departed from the battle, sat down.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं प्रवृत्तं तु सुराणां राक्षसैः सह । शस्त्राणि वर्षतां घोरं मेघानामिव संयुगे ।। 7.28.33 ।।
explanation: Then a terrible battle commenced between the gods and the Rākṣasas, as they rained down weapons fiercely, like clouds in combat.

shloka_text: कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुष्टात्मा नानाप्रहरणोद्यतः । नाज्ञायत तदा युद्धे सह केनाप्ययुध्यत ।। 7.28.34 ।।
explanation: But the wicked-souled Kumbhakarna, ready with various weapons, was not recognized in battle then, nor was it known with whom he was fighting.

shloka_text: दन्तैः भुजाभ्यां पद्मां च शक्तितोमरसायकैः । येन केनैव संरब्धस्ताडयामास वै सुरान् ।। 7.28.35 ।।
explanation: Enraged by whatever means, he struck the gods with his teeth, two arms, the lotus, and with spears, javelins, and arrows.

shloka_text: ततो रुद्रैर्महाघोरैः सङ्गम्याथ निशाचरः । प्रयुद्धस्तैश्च सङ्ग्रामे क्षतः शस्त्रैर्निरन्तरम् ।। 7.28.36 ।।
explanation: Then, having encountered the very terrible Rudras, the night-wanderer was fought by them in battle and continuously wounded by weapons.

shloka_text: बभौ शस्त्राचिततनुः कुम्भकर्णः क्षरन्नसृक् । विद्युत्स्तनितनिर्घोषो धारवानिव तोयदः ।। 7.28.37 ।।
explanation: Kumbhakarna, his body covered with weapons and oozing blood, shone like a rain-bearing cloud, whose roar was like lightning and thunder.

shloka_text: ततस्तद्राक्षसं सैन्यं प्रयुद्धं समरुद्गणैः । रणे विद्रावितं सर्वं नानाप्रहरणैः शितैः ।। 7.28.38 ।।
explanation: Then that Rākṣasa army, having fought with the hosts of Maruts, was completely routed in battle by their sharp, various weapons.

shloka_text: केचिद्विनिहताः कृत्ताश्चेष्टन्ति स्म महीतले । वाहनेष्ववसक्ताश्च स्थिता एवापरे रणे ।। 7.28.39 ।।
explanation: Some, struck down and cut, struggled on the ground. And others remained stuck on their vehicles, right there in the battle.

shloka_text: रथान्नागान्खरानुष्ट्रान्पन्नगांस्तुरगान् रणे । शिंशुमारान्वराहांश्च पिशाचवदनान्तथा ।। 7.28.40 ।।
explanation: Chariots, elephants, donkeys, camels, serpents, horses in battle, porpoises, and boars, and also those with demon-like faces.

shloka_text: तान्समालिङ्ग्य बाहुभ्यां विष्टब्धाः केचिदुच्छ्रुताः । देवैस्तु शस्त्रसम्भिन्ना मम्रिरे च निशाचराः ।। 7.28.41 ।।
explanation: Embracing them with their arms, some were held fast and lifted high. And the night-rovers, pierced by the weapons of the gods, died.

shloka_text: चित्रकर्म इवाभाति स तेषां रणसम्प्लवः । निहतानां प्रमत्तानां राक्षसानां महीतले ।। 7.28.42 ।।
explanation: That scene of battle, with the slain and heedless Rākṣasas on the ground, appeared like a painting.

shloka_text: शोणितोदकनिष्पन्दकङ्कगृध्रसमाकुला । प्रवृत्ता संयुगमुखे शस्त्रग्राहवती नदी ।। 7.28.43 ।।
explanation: A river, whose current was blood-water, crowded with herons and vultures, and having weapons as its crocodiles, began to flow on the battlefield.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धो दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् । निरीक्ष्य तद्बलं कृत्स्नं दैवतैर्विनिपातितम् ।। 7.28.44 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the mighty Dashagriva, enraged, having seen his entire army destroyed by the gods.

shloka_text: स तं प्रति विगाह्याशु प्रवृद्धं सैन्यसागरम् । त्रिदशान्समरे निघ्नञ्छक्रमेवाभ्यवर्तत ।। 7.28.45 ।।
explanation: He, quickly penetrating that vast ocean of an army, and slaying the gods in battle, indeed advanced towards Indra.

shloka_text: आगाच्छक्रो महच्चापं विस्फार्य सुमहास्वनम् । यस्य विस्फारघोषेण स्तनन्ति स्म दिशो दश ।। 7.28.46 ।।
explanation: Indra came, stretching his great bow with a tremendous sound, by the twang of which the ten directions roared.

shloka_text: तद्विकृष्य महच्चापमिन्द्रो रावणमूर्धनि । निपातयामास शरान्पावकादित्यवर्चसः ।। 7.28.47 ।।
explanation: Having drawn that great bow, Indra showered arrows, brilliant as fire and the sun, upon Ravana's head.

shloka_text: तथैव च महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवो व्यवस्थितः । शक्रं कार्मुकविभ्रष्टैः शरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ।। 7.28.48 ।।
explanation: And similarly, the mighty-armed Dashagriva, standing firm, assailed Indra with showers of arrows released from his bow.

shloka_text: प्रयुध्यतोरथ तयोर्बाणवर्षैः समन्ततः । न ज्ञायते तदा किञ्चित्सर्वं हि तमसा वृतम् ।। 7.28.49 ।।
explanation: Then, as those two fought, with showers of arrows from all sides, nothing was discernible at that time, for everything was enveloped in darkness.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टाविंशः सर्गः ।। 28 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem by the glorious Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the twenty-eighth chapter.

shloka_text: ततस्तमसि सञ्जाते सर्वे ते देवराक्षसाः । अयुद्ध्यन्त बलोन्मत्ताः सूदयन्तः परस्परम् ।। 7.29.1 ।।
explanation: Then, when darkness had set in, all those gods and demons, maddened by their strength, fought, destroying each other.

shloka_text: ततस्तु देवसैन्येन राक्षसानां बृहद्बलम् । दशांशं स्थापितं युद्धे शेषं नीतं यमक्षयम् ।। 7.29.2 ।।
explanation: Then, by the army of gods, only a tenth part of the great army of Rākṣasas remained in the battle; the rest was led to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तु तामसे युद्धे सर्वे ते देवराक्षसाः । अन्योन्यं नाभ्यजानन्त युध्यमानाः परस्परम् ।। 7.29.3 ।।
explanation: In that very dark battle, all those gods and demons, fighting amongst themselves, did not recognize each other.

shloka_text: इन्द्रश्च रावणश्चैव रावणिश्च महाबलः । तस्मिंस्तमोजालवृते मोहमीयुर्न ते त्रयः ।। 7.29.4 ।।
explanation: Indra, Ravana, and the mighty Ravani – those three were not bewildered when it was enveloped in a net of darkness.

shloka_text: स तु दृष्ट्वा बलं सर्वं रावणो निहतं क्षणात् । क्रोधमभ्यगमत्तीव्रं महानादं च मुक्तवान् ।। 7.29.5 ।।
explanation: But Ravana, having seen his entire army destroyed in an instant, became intensely angry and let out a great roar.

shloka_text: क्रोधात्सूतं च दुर्धर्षः स्यन्दनस्थमुवाच ह । परसैन्यस्य मध्येन यावदन्तो नयस्व माम् ।। 7.29.6 ।।
explanation: The formidable one, angrily, said to the charioteer in the chariot: "Lead me through the middle of the enemy army until the very end."

shloka_text: अद्यैतान् त्रिदशान्सर्वान्विक्रमैः समरे स्वयम् । नानाशस्त्रैर्महाघोरैर्नयामि यमसादनम् ।। 7.29.7 ।।
explanation: Today, I myself, with terrible and various weapons, will send all these gods to the abode of Yama in battle by my prowess.

shloka_text: अहमिन्द्रं वधिष्यामि धनदं वरुणं यमम् । त्रिदशान्विनिहत्याथ स्वयं स्थास्याम्यथोपरि । विषादो न च कर्तव्यः शीघ्रं वाहय मे रथम् ।। 7.29.8 ।।
explanation: I will kill Indra, Dhanada, Varuna, and Yama. Having completely slain the gods, I myself will then stand supreme. Despondency should not be felt. Quickly drive my chariot.

shloka_text: द्विः खलु त्वां ब्रवीम्यद्य यावदन्तो नयस्व माम् ।। 7.29.9 ।।
explanation: Indeed, I tell you twice today, lead me to the end.

shloka_text: अयं स नन्दनोद्देशो यत्र वर्तामहे वयम् । नय मामद्य तत्र त्वमुदयो यत्र पर्वतः ।। 7.29.10 ।।
explanation: This is the Nandan region where we are. Lead me today to where Mount Udaya is.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा तुरगान्स मनोजवान् । आदिदेशाथ शत्रणां मध्येनैव च सारथिः ।। 7.29.11 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, the charioteer then directed the mind-swift horses right through the midst of the enemies.

shloka_text: तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा शक्रो देवेश्वरस्तदा । रथस्थः समरस्थस्तान्देवान्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.29.12 ।।
explanation: Then, Shakra, the lord of the gods, having understood his resolve, standing in his chariot in the battle, spoke these words to those gods.

shloka_text: सुराः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यत्तावन्मम रोचते । जीवन्नेव दशग्रीवः साधु रक्षो निगृह्यताम् ।। 7.29.13 ।।
explanation: O gods, listen to my words, which I deem good. Let the demon Daśagrīva be properly seized while he is still alive.

shloka_text: एष ह्यतिबलः सैन्यै रथेन पवनौजसा । गमिष्यति प्रवृद्धोर्मिः समुद्र इव पर्वणि ।। 7.29.14 ।।
explanation: He, indeed, exceedingly powerful, with his armies and by a chariot swift as the wind, will proceed like the ocean with surging waves on a full moon day.

shloka_text: नह्येष हन्तुं शक्यो ऽद्य वरदानात्सुनिर्भयः । तद्ग्रहीष्यामहे रक्षो यत्ता भवत संयुगे ।। 7.29.15 ।।
explanation: This one cannot be killed today, as he is utterly fearless due to the boon. Therefore, we shall capture this demon; be prepared in battle.

shloka_text: यथा बलौ निरुद्धे च त्रैलोक्यं भुज्यते मया । एवमेतस्य पापस्य निरोधो मम रोचते ।। 7.29.16 ।।
explanation: Just as I enjoy the three worlds after Bali was restrained, similarly, the suppression of this sin is pleasing to me.

shloka_text: ततो ऽन्यं देशमास्थाय शक्रः सन्त्यज्य रावणम् । अयुध्यत महाराज राक्षसांस्त्रासयन्रणे ।। 7.29.17 ।।
explanation: Then, having taken another position, Indra, abandoning Ravana, fought, O great king, terrifying the Rākṣasas in battle.

shloka_text: उत्तरेण दशग्रीवः प्रविवेशानिवर्तकः । दक्षिणेन तु पार्श्वेन प्रविवेश शतक्रतुः ।। 7.29.18 ।।
explanation: Daśagrīva, irresistible, entered from the north. And Śatakratu entered from the southern side.

shloka_text: ततः स योजनशतं प्रविष्टो राक्षसाधिपः । देवतानां बलं सर्वं शरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ।। 7.29.19 ।।
explanation: Then, having advanced a hundred yojanas, that lord of Rākṣasas overwhelmed the entire army of the gods with showers of arrows.

shloka_text: ततः शक्रो निरीक्ष्याथ प्रनष्टं तु स्वकं बलम् । न्यवर्तयदसम्भ्रान्तः समावृत्य दशाननम् ।। 7.29.20 ।।
explanation: Then Indra, having seen his own army routed, undismayed, turned back and confronted Ravana.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे नादो मुक्तो दानवराक्षसैः । हा हताः स्म इति ग्रस्तं दृष्ट्वा शक्रेण रावणम् ।। 7.29.21 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the Danavas and Rakshasas, seeing Ravana seized by Shakra, let out a cry, "Alas, we are slain!"

shloka_text: ततो रथं समास्थाय रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । तत्सैन्यमतिसङ्क्रुद्धः प्रविवेश सुदारुणम् ।। 7.29.22 ।।
explanation: Then, Ravani, overcome with rage and exceedingly enraged, having mounted his chariot, entered that very terrible army.

shloka_text: तां प्रविश्य महामायां प्राप्तां गोपतिना पुरा । प्रविवेश सुसंरब्धस्तत्सैन्यं समभिद्रवत् ।। 7.29.23 ।।
explanation: Having entered that great illusion, which was formerly obtained by Gopati, he, greatly enraged, entered that army and attacked it.

shloka_text: स सर्वा देवतास्त्यक्त्वा शक्रमेवाभ्यधावत । महेन्द्रश्च महातेजा नापश्यच्च सुतं रिपोः ।। 7.29.24 ।।
explanation: Abandoning all deities, he indeed ran towards Shakra. And the greatly effulgent Mahendra did not see the enemy's son.

shloka_text: विमुक्तकवचस्तत्र वध्यमानो ऽपि रावणिः । त्रिदशैः सुमहावीर्यैर्न चकार च किञ्चन ।। 7.29.25 ।।
explanation: There, Ravana's son, with his armor removed, even though being struck by the exceedingly mighty gods, could do nothing at all.

shloka_text: स मातलिं समायान्तं ताडयित्वा शरोत्तमैः । महेन्द्रं बाणवर्षेण भूय एवाभ्यवाकिरत् ।। 7.29.26 ।।
explanation: He, having struck the approaching Matali with excellent arrows, showered Mahendra again with a rain of arrows.

shloka_text: ततस्त्यक्त्वा रथं शक्रो विससर्ज च सारथिम् । ऐरावतं समारुह्य मृगयामास रावणिम् ।। 7.29.27 ।।
explanation: Then Shakra, having abandoned his chariot and dismissed his charioteer, mounted Airavata and searched for Ravani.

shloka_text: स तत्र मायाबलवानदृश्यो ऽथान्तरिक्षगः । इन्द्रं मायापरिक्षिप्तं कृत्वा स प्राद्रवच्छरैः ।। 7.29.28 ।।
explanation: He, powerful with illusion, invisible and moving in the sky, then, having enveloped Indra with illusion, attacked him with arrows.

shloka_text: स तं यदा परिश्रान्तमिन्द्रं जज्ञे ऽथ रावणिः । तदैनं मायया बद्ध्वा स्वसैन्यमभितो ऽनयत् ।। 7.29.29 ।।
explanation: When the son of Ravana perceived Indra to be exhausted, he then bound him with illusion and led him towards his own army.

shloka_text: तं तु दृष्ट्वा बलात्तेन नीयमानं महारणात् । महेन्द्रममराः सर्वे किं नु स्यादित्यचिन्तयन् ।। 7.29.30 ।।
explanation: But having seen him, Mahendra, being carried away by force from the great battle by him, all the gods thought, 'What indeed will happen?'

shloka_text: दृश्यते न स मायावी शक्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । विद्यावानपि येनेन्द्रो मायया नीयते बलात् ।। 7.29.31 ।।
explanation: That illusionist, Indrajit, the conqueror of Indra and victor in battle, is not seen, by whom even Indra, though possessing knowledge, is forcibly led away by illusion.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे क्रुद्धाः सर्वे सुरगणास्तदा । रावणं विमुखीकृत्य शरवर्षैरवाकिरन् ।। 7.29.32 ।।
explanation: At that moment, all the enraged hosts of gods, having made Ravana turn away, assailed him with showers of arrows.

shloka_text: रावणस्तु समासाद्य आदित्यांश्च वसूंस्तदा । न शशाक स सङ्ग्रामे योद्धुं शत्रुभिरर्दितः ।। 7.29.33 ।।
explanation: But Rāvaṇa, having encountered the Adityas and the Vasus at that time, was unable to fight in battle, being harassed by his enemies.

shloka_text: स तं दृष्ट्वा परिम्लानं प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतम् । रावणिः पितरं युद्धे दर्शनस्थो ऽब्रवीदिदम् ।। 7.29.34 ।।
explanation: Having seen his father, greatly exhausted and mangled by blows in battle, Ravana's son, standing in sight, spoke this.

shloka_text: आगच्छ तात गच्छामो रणकर्म निवर्तताम् । जितं नो विदितं ते ऽस्तु स्वस्थो भव गतज्वरः ।। 7.29.35 ।।
explanation: Come, dear one, let us go; let the work of battle cease. Our victory is known to you. Be well, free from anxiety.

shloka_text: अयं हि सुरसैन्यस्य त्रैलोक्यस्य च यः प्रभुः । स गृहीतो दैवबलाद्भग्नदर्पाः सुराः कृताः ।। 7.29.36 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he who is the lord of the army of gods and of the three worlds, has been captured by the power of destiny, and the gods have been rendered broken in pride.

shloka_text: यथेष्टं भुङ्क्ष्व लोकांस्त्रीन्निगृह्यारातिमोजसा । वृथा किं ते श्रमेणेह युद्धमद्य तु निष्फलम् ।। 7.29.37 ।।
explanation: Enjoy the three worlds as you wish, having subdued the enemy with your might. Why this vain effort of yours here? For today's battle is indeed fruitless.

shloka_text: ततस्ते दैवतगणा निवृत्ता रणकर्मणः । तच्छ्रुत्वा रावणेर्वाक्यं स्वस्थचेताः बभूव ह ।। 7.29.38 ।।
explanation: Then those hosts of gods withdrew from the act of battle. Having heard that statement of Ravana's son, their minds became composed.

shloka_text: अथ स रणविगतज्वरः प्रभुर्विजयमवाप्य निशाचराधिपः । स्वभवनमभितो जगाम हृष्टः स्वसुतमवाप्य च वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.29.39 ।।
explanation: Then, that lord of the night-wanderers, whose battle-fever had subsided, having achieved victory, went joyfully towards his own abode. And having met his son, he spoke words.

shloka_text: अतिबलसदृशैः पराक्रमैस्तैर्मम कुलमानविवर्धनं कृतम् । यदयमतुल्यबलस्त्वयाद्य वै त्रिदशपतिस्त्रिदशाश्च निर्जिताः ।। 7.29.40 ।।
explanation: By those immensely powerful valorous deeds, the honor of my family has been increased, because today you, of unequalled might, have indeed conquered the lord of the gods and the gods themselves.

shloka_text: नय रथमधिरोप्य वासवं नगरमितो व्रज सेनया वृतस्त्वम् । अहमपि तव गच्छतो द्रुतं सह सचिवैरनुयामि पृष्ठतः ।। 7.29.41 ।।
explanation: Place Vasava on the chariot and lead him. You, surrounded by the army, proceed from here to the city. I too will swiftly follow behind you as you go, along with the ministers.

shloka_text: अथ स बलवृतः सवाहनस्त्रिदशपतिं परिगृह्य रावणिः । स्वभवनमभिगम्य वीर्यवान्कृतसमरान्विससर्ज राक्षसान् ।। 7.29.42 ।।
explanation: Then, that powerful Ravani, surrounded by his army and with his vehicles, having captured the lord of the gods, went to his own abode and dismissed the Rakshasas who had fought the battle.

shloka_text: जिते महेन्द्रे ऽतिबले रावणस्य सुतेन वै । प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य ययुर्लङ्कां सुरास्तदा ।। 7.30.1 ।।
explanation: When the exceedingly powerful Mahendra was conquered by Ravana's son, then the gods, led by Prajapati, went to Lanka.

shloka_text: तत्र रावणमासाद्य पुत्रभ्रातृभिरावृतम् । अब्रवीद्गगने तिष्ठन्सामपूर्वं प्रजापतिः ।। 7.30.2 ।।
explanation: Then, having approached Ravana, who was surrounded by his sons and brothers, Prajapati, standing in the sky, spoke gently.

shloka_text: वत्स रावण तुष्टो ऽस्मि पुत्रस्य तव संयुगे । अहो ऽस्य विक्रमौदार्यं तव तुल्यो ऽधिको ऽपि वा ।। 7.30.3 ।।
explanation: Son Ravana, I am pleased with your son in battle. Oh, his valor and magnanimity are equal to yours, or even greater.

shloka_text: जितं हि भवता सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं स्वेन तेजसा । कृता प्रतिज्ञा सफला प्रीतो ऽस्मि स्वसुतेन वै ।। 7.30.4 ।।
explanation: Indeed, all the three worlds have been conquered by you with your own might. The vow has been fulfilled, and I am truly pleased with my own son.

shloka_text: अयं च पुत्रो ऽतिबलस्तव रावण वीर्यवान् । जगतीन्द्रजिदित्येव परिख्यातो भविष्यति ।। 7.30.5 ।।
explanation: And this exceedingly strong and mighty son of yours, O Ravana, will be renowned in the world as Indrajit.

shloka_text: बलवान्दुर्जयश्चैव भविष्यत्येव राक्षसः । यं समाश्रित्य ते राजन्स्थापितास्त्रिदशा वशे ।। 7.30.6 ।।
explanation: That demon will certainly be powerful and unconquerable. It is by relying on him, O King, that the gods were brought under control.

shloka_text: तन्मुच्यतां महाबाहो महेन्द्रः पाकशासनः । किञ्चास्य मोक्षणार्थाय प्रयच्छन्तु दिवौकसः ।। 7.30.7 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, let Mahendra, the chastiser of Paka, be released. And for his liberation, let the gods give.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा इन्द्रजित्समितिञ्जयः । अमरत्वमहं देव वृणे यद्येष मुच्यते ।। 7.30.8 ।।
explanation: Then spoke the greatly effulgent Indrajit, the conqueror in battle: "O god, I ask for immortality, if it is granted."

shloka_text: चतुष्पदां खेचराणामन्येषां वा महौजसाम् । वृक्षगुल्मक्षुपलतातृणोपलमहीभृताम् ।। 7.30.9 ।।
explanation: Of quadrupeds, of sky-dwellers, or of other mighty beings; of trees, bushes, shrubs, creepers, grasses, stones, and mountains.

shloka_text: सर्वे ऽपि जन्तवो ऽन्योन्यं भेतव्ये सति बिभ्यति । अतो ऽत्र लोके सर्वेषां सर्वस्माच्च भवेद्भयम् ।। 7.30.10 ।।
explanation: All creatures, when there is cause for fear, fear each other. Therefore, in this world, all should fear everything.

shloka_text: ततो ऽब्रवीन्महातेजा मेघनादं प्रजापतिः । नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं हि कस्यचित्प्राणिनो भुवि । चतुष्पदः पक्षिणश्च भूतानां वा महौजसाम् ।। 7.30.11 ।।
explanation: Then Prajapati, the greatly effulgent one, spoke to Meghanada: "Indeed, complete immortality does not exist for any living being on earth, neither for quadrupeds, nor for birds, nor for any beings, even those of great power."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा पितामहेनोक्तमिन्द्रजित्प्रभुणाव्ययम् ।। 7.30.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard what was spoken by the grandfather, Indrajit, the imperishable lord.

shloka_text: ्वं हि कस्यचित्प्राणिनो भुवि । अथाब्रवीत्स तत्रस्थं मेघनादो महाबलः । श्रूयतां वा भवेत्सिद्धिः शतक्रतुविमोक्षणे ।। 7.30.13 ।।
explanation: You are indeed a creature on earth. Then the mighty Meghanada, who was present there, spoke: "Listen, or there may be success in freeing Shakra."

shloka_text: ममेष्टं नित्यशो हर्व्यैर्मन्त्रैः सम्पूज्य पावकम् । सङ्ग्राममवतर्त्तुं च शत्रुनिर्जयकाङ्क्षिणः ।। 7.30.14 ।।
explanation: It is my constant wish to enter battle, desiring victory over foes, after having worshipped the fire with oblations and mantras.

shloka_text: अश्वयुक्तो रथो मह्यमुत्तिष्ठेत्तु विभावसोः । तत्स्थस्यामरता स्यान्मे एष मे निश्चयो वरः ।। 7.30.15 ।।
explanation: May a horse-drawn chariot rise for me from the sun. Immortality would be mine, standing in it. This is my excellent firm resolve.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्यद्यसमाप्ते च जप्यहोमे विभावसौ । युध्येयं देव सङ्ग्रामे तदा मे स्याद्विनाशनम् ।। 7.30.16 ।।
explanation: O Deva, if that japa and homa in the fire were incomplete, and I were to fight in battle, then my destruction would occur."

shloka_text: सर्वो हि तपसा देव वृणोत्यमरतां पुमान् । विक्रमेण मया त्वेतदमरत्वं प्रवर्तितम् ।। 7.30.17 ।।
explanation: Indeed, O god, every man obtains immortality through penance. But this immortality has been brought about by me through valor.

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति तं चाह वाक्यं देवः पितामहः । मुक्तश्चेन्द्रजिता शक्रो गताश्च त्रिदिवं सुराः ।। 7.30.18 ।।
explanation: "So be it," the divine Grandfather (Brahma) said these words to him. And Shakra (Indra) was released by Indrajit, and the gods went to heaven.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम दीनो भ्रष्टाम्बरद्युतिः । इन्द्रश्चिन्तापरीतात्मा ध्यानतत्परतां गतः ।। 7.30.19 ।।
explanation: O Rama, in the meantime, Indra, distressed, with his celestial radiance diminished, and his mind enveloped by anxiety, became absorbed in meditation.

shloka_text: तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं प्राह देवः प्रजापतिः । शतक्रतो किमु पुरा करोति स्म सुदुष्कृतम् ।। 7.30.20 ।।
explanation: Seeing him in that state, the god Prajapati said, "O Shatakratu, what great evil deed did you commit previously?"

shloka_text: अमरेन्द्र मया बह्व्यः प्रजाः सृष्टास्तथा प्रभो । एकवर्णाः समाभाषा एकरूपाश्च सर्वशः ।। 7.30.21 ।।
explanation: O Lord of Immortals, O Lord, by me many creatures were created, all of one color, speaking the same language, and uniform in every respect.

shloka_text: तासां नास्ति विशेषो हि दर्शने लक्षणे ऽपि वा । ततो ऽहमेकाग्रमनास्ताः प्रजाः परिचिन्तयम् ।। 7.30.22 ।।
explanation: Indeed, there is no distinction among them, either in appearance or in characteristics. Therefore, I, with a concentrated mind, contemplated those beings.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं तासां विशेषार्थं स्त्रियमेकां विनिर्ममे । यद्यत्प्रजानां प्रत्यङ्गं विशिष्टं तत्तदुद्धृतम् ।। 7.30.23 ।।
explanation: So I, for their special purpose, created one woman. Whatever excellent part there was in each limb of the creatures, that was extracted.

shloka_text: ततो मया रूपगुणैरहल्या स्त्री विनिर्मिता । हलं नामेह वैरूपं हल्यं तत्प्रभवं भवेत् ।। 7.30.24 ।।
explanation: Then by me, Ahalya, a woman endowed with beauty and qualities, was created. Here, the word 'Hala' means 'ugliness' (or 'absence of beauty'), and 'Halya' would be that which originates from it.

shloka_text: यस्मान्न विद्यते हल्यं तेनाहल्येति विश्रुता । अहल्येति मया शक्र तस्या नाम प्रवर्तितम् ।। 7.30.25 ।।
explanation: Because there is no blemish, she is renowned as Ahalya. O Shakra, I gave her the name Ahalya.

shloka_text: निर्मितायां च देवेन्द्र तस्यां नार्यां सुरर्षभ । भविष्यतीति कस्यैषा मम चिन्ता ततो ऽभवत् ।। 7.30.26 ।।
explanation: O Lord of Devas, O best among gods, when that woman was created, then this concern arose in me: 'Whose will she be?'

shloka_text: त्वं तु शक्र तदा नारीं जानीषे मनसा प्रभो । स्थानाधिकतया पत्नी ममैषेति पुरन्दर ।। 7.30.27 ।।
explanation: But you, O Shakra, O Lord, then in your mind, due to your superior position, considered that woman, 'This one is my wife,' O Purandara.

shloka_text: सा मया न्यासभूता तु गौतमस्य महात्मनः । न्यस्ता बहूनि वर्षाणि तेन निर्यातिता च ह ।। 7.30.28 ।।
explanation: She, as a deposit, was entrusted by me to the great-souled Gautama. And for many years, she was indeed returned by him.

shloka_text: ततस्तस्य परिज्ञाय महास्थैर्यं महामुनेः । ज्ञात्वा तपसि सिद्धिं च पत्न्यर्थं स्पर्शिता तदा ।। 7.30.29 ।।
explanation: Then, having understood the great steadfastness of that great sage, and having known his success in penance, she was then offered for a wife.

shloka_text: सङ्क्रुद्धस्त्वं हि धर्मात्मन् गत्वा तस्याश्रमं मुनेः । दृष्टवांश्च तदा तां स्त्रीं दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव ।। 7.30.30 ।।
explanation: O righteous soul, you, having become enraged, indeed went to that sage's hermitage. And then you saw that woman, radiant like a flame of fire.

shloka_text: सा त्वया धर्षिता शक्र कामार्तेन समन्युना । दृष्टस्त्वं च तदा तेन ह्याश्रमे परमर्षिणा ।। 7.30.31 ।।
explanation: She was violated by you, O Shakra, who were overcome by lust and anger. And you were then seen by that great sage in the hermitage.

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धेन तेना ऽसि शप्तः परमतेजसा । गतो ऽसि येन देवेन्द्र दशाभागविपर्ययम् ।। 7.30.32 ।।
explanation: Then, by that greatly powerful and enraged one, you were cursed, O king of gods, because of which you experienced a reversal of a tenth part.

shloka_text: यस्मान्मे धर्षिता पत्नी त्वया वासव निर्भयम् । तस्मात्त्वं समरे राजञ्छत्रुहस्तं गमिष्यसि ।। 7.30.33 ।।
explanation: Because my wife was fearlessly violated by you, O Vasava, therefore, O King, you will fall into the hands of the enemy in battle.

shloka_text: अयं तु भावो दुर्बुद्धे यस्त्वयेह प्रवर्तितः । मानुषेष्वपि लोकेषु भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.30.34 ।।
explanation: O evil-minded one, this very act which has been instigated by you here, will certainly come to pass even among human beings, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: तत्रार्धं तस्य यः कर्ता त्वय्यर्धं निपतिष्यति । न च ते स्थावरं स्थानं भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.30.35 ।।
explanation: Half of that which the doer commits, half will fall upon you. And there will be no permanent abode for you, without a doubt.

shloka_text: यश्च यश्च सुरेन्द्रः स्याद्ध्रुवः स न भविष्यति । एष शापो मया मुक्त इत्यसौ त्वां तदा ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.30.36 ।।
explanation: Whosoever becomes the lord of the gods, he shall not be permanent. This curse has been uttered by me," thus he said to you then.

shloka_text: तां तु भार्यां स निर्भर्त्स्य सो ऽब्रवीत्सुमहातपाः । दुर्विनीते विनिध्वंस ममाश्रमसमीपतः ।। 7.30.37 ।।
explanation: Having rebuked that wife, he, the great ascetic, said: "O ill-behaved one, disappear from near my hermitage!"

shloka_text: रूपयौवनसम्पन्ना यस्मात्त्वमनवस्थिता । तस्माद्रूपवती लोके न त्वमेका भविष्यति ।। 7.30.38 ।।
explanation: Since you, endowed with beauty and youth, are unsteady, therefore you will not be the only beautiful woman in the world.

shloka_text: रूपं च ते प्रजाः सर्वा गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः । यत्तदेकं समाश्रित्य विभ्रमो ऽयमुपस्थितः ।। 7.30.39 ।।
explanation: And all creatures will undoubtedly attain your form. This delusion has arisen by resorting to that one.

shloka_text: तदाप्रभृति भूयिष्ठं प्रजा रूपसमन्विताः । सा तं प्रसादयामास महर्षिं गौतमं तदा ।। 7.30.40 ।।
explanation: From that time onwards, most people were endowed with beauty. Then she appeased that great sage Gautama.

shloka_text: अज्ञानाद्धर्षिता विप्र त्वद्रूपेण दिवौकसा । न कामकाराद्विप्रर्षे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.30.41 ।।
explanation: O Brahmana, the gods were gladdened by your form due to ignorance. O Sage among Brahmanas, you should grant favor, not considering it an intentional act (on their part).

shloka_text: अहल्यया त्वेवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच स गौतमः । उत्पत्स्यति महातेजा इक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः ।। 7.30.42 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Ahalya, Gautama replied: 'A greatly effulgent, great warrior of the Ikshvakus will be born.'

shloka_text: रामो नाम श्रुतो लोके वनं चाप्युपयास्यति । ब्राह्मणार्थे महाबाहुर्विष्णुर्मानुषविग्रहः । तं द्रक्ष्यसि यदा भद्रे ततः पूता भविष्यसि ।। 7.30.43 ।।
explanation: Rama, renowned by name in the world, will also come to the forest. He is the mighty-armed Vishnu in human form, for the sake of Brahmins. When you see him, O auspicious one, then you will become purified.

shloka_text: स हि पावयितुं शक्तस्त्वया यद्दुष्कृतं कृतम् । तस्यातिथ्यं च कृत्वा वै मत्समीपं गमिष्यसि ।। 7.30.44 ।।
explanation: He is indeed capable of purifying whatever sin has been committed by you. And having offered him hospitality, you will come to my presence.

shloka_text: वत्स्यसि त्वं मया सार्धं तदा हि वरवर्णिनि । एवमुक्त्वा स विप्रर्षिराजगाम स्वमाश्रमम् ।। 7.30.45 ।।
explanation: O beautiful lady, you will indeed live with me then. Having said this, that Brahmarshi returned to his own hermitage.

shloka_text: तपश्चाचार सुमहत्सा पत्नी ब्रह्मवादिनः । शापोत्सर्गाद्धि तस्येदं मुनेः सर्वमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.30.46 ।।
explanation: And she, the wife of the knower of Brahman, performed very great penance. Indeed, all this has come to pass for that sage from the utterance of his curse.

shloka_text: तत्स्मर त्वं महाबाहो दुष्कृतं यत्त्वया कृतम् । तेन त्वं ग्रहणं शत्रोर्यातो नान्येन वासव ।। 7.30.47 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, remember that misdeed which was committed by you. By that alone, you have been captured by the enemy, O Vasava, and not by anything else.

shloka_text: शीघ्रं वै यज यज्ञं त्वं वैष्णवं सुसमाहितः । पावितस्तेन यज्ञेन यास्यसे त्रिदिवं ततः ।। 7.30.48 ।।
explanation: You, being well-concentrated, quickly perform the Vaishnava sacrifice. Purified by that sacrifice, you will then go to heaven.

shloka_text: पुत्रश्च तव देवेन्द्र न विनष्टो महारणे । नीतः सन्निहितश्चैव आर्यकेण महोदधौ ।। 7.30.49 ।।
explanation: O Devendra, your son was not destroyed in the great battle. He was taken and kept hidden by Aryaka in the great ocean.

shloka_text: एतच्छ्रुत्वा महेन्द्रस्तु यज्ञमिष्ट्वा च वैष्णवम् । पुनस्त्रिदिवमाक्रामदन्वशासच्च देवराट् ।। 7.30.50 ।।
explanation: Having heard this, Mahendra, having performed a Vaishnava sacrifice, again ascended to heaven, and the king of gods ruled.

shloka_text: एतदिन्द्रजितो नाम बलं यत्कीर्तितं मया । निर्जितस्तेन देवेन्द्रः प्राणिनो ऽन्ये तु किं पुनः ।। 7.30.51 ।।
explanation: This is the power of Indrajit, which I have described. By him, Devendra was conquered; what then of other living beings?

shloka_text: आश्चर्यमिति रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्चाब्रवीत्तदा । अगस्त्यवचनं श्रुत्वा वानरा राक्षसास्तदा ।। 7.30.52 ।।
explanation: Having heard Agastya's words, Rama and Lakshmana then exclaimed, "Amazing!" The monkeys and demons were also present at that time.

shloka_text: विभीषणस्तु रामस्य पार्श्वस्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । आश्चर्यं स्मारितो ऽस्म्यद्य यत्तद्दृष्टं पुरातनम् ।। 7.30.53 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, standing by Rama's side, spoke these words: "Today I am reminded of that ancient wonder which was seen."

shloka_text: अगस्त्यं त्वब्रवीद्रामः सत्यमेतच्छ्रुतं च मे ।। 7.30.54 ।।
explanation: Rama said to Agastya: "This is true, and I have heard it."

shloka_text: एवं राम समुद्भूतो रावणो लोककण्टकः । सपुत्रो येन सङ्ग्रामे जितः शक्रः सुरेश्वरः ।। 7.30.55 ।।
explanation: Thus, O Rama, was born Ravana, the tormentor of the world, by whom, along with his son, Indra, the lord of the gods, was conquered in battle.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 30 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the thirtieth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: ततो रामो महातेजा विस्मयात्पुनरेव हि । उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यमगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम् ।। 7.31.1 ।।
explanation: Then, the greatly effulgent Rama, filled with wonder, again reverently spoke these words to Agastya, the foremost among sages.

shloka_text: भगवन्राक्षसः क्रूरो यदाप्रभृति मेदिनीम् । पर्यटत्किं तदा लोकाः शून्या आसन्द्विजोत्तम ।। 7.31.2 ।।
explanation: O Lord, O best of Brahmins, when that cruel demon began to roam the earth, were the worlds then empty?

shloka_text: राजा वा राजमात्रो वा किं तदा नात्र कश्चन । धर्षणं यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः ।। 7.31.3 ।।
explanation: Was there no king, or royal minister, or anyone at all there then, where Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, was not subjected to humiliation?

shloka_text: उताहो हतवीर्यास्ते बभूवुः पृथिवीक्षितः । बहिष्कृता वरास्त्रैश्च बहवो निर्जिता नृपाः ।। 7.31.4 ।।
explanation: Or perhaps those kings of the earth became devoid of valor. And many kings were defeated and expelled by excellent weapons.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ह्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः । उवाच रामं प्रहसन्पितामह इवेश्वरम् ।। 7.31.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of Rama, the divine sage Agastya, smiling, spoke to Rama, just as Brahma (the Grandfather) would speak to the Lord.

shloka_text: इत्येवं बाधमानस्तु पार्थिवान्पार्थिवर्षभ । चचार रावणो राम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते ।। 7.31.6 ।।
explanation: Thus, harassing the kings, O best of kings, Ravana roamed the earth, O Rama, O lord of the earth.

shloka_text: ततो माहिष्मतीं नाम पुरीं स्वर्गपुरीप्रभाम् । सम्प्राप्तो यत्र सान्निध्यं सदासीद्वसुरेतसः ।। 7.31.7 ।।
explanation: Then he arrived at the city named Mahishmati, which shone with the splendor of a heavenly city, and where the presence of Vasu-retas was always manifest.

shloka_text: तुल्य आसीन्नृपस्तस्य प्रभावाद्वसुरेतसः । अर्जुनो नाम यत्राग्निः शरकुण्डेशयः सदा ।। 7.31.8 ।।
explanation: His king, named Arjuna, was equal in might to Vasu-retas, in whom Agni always resided, dwelling in his quiver of arrows.

shloka_text: तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ हैहयाधिपतिर्बली । अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः ।। 7.31.9 ।।
explanation: On that very day, the mighty lord of the Haihayas, Arjuna, the ruler, went to the Narmada to sport with his women.

shloka_text: तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ रावणस्तत्र आगतः । रावणो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तस्यामात्यानपृच्छत ।। 7.31.10 ।।
explanation: On that very day, Ravana arrived there. Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, then asked his ministers.

shloka_text: क्वार्जुनो नृपतिः शीघ्रं सम्यगाख्यातुमर्हथ । रावणो ऽहमनुप्राप्तो युद्धेप्सुर्नृवरेण ह । ममागमनमप्यग्रे युष्माभिः सन्निवेद्यताम् ।। 7.31.11 ।।
explanation: Where is King Arjuna? You must tell me quickly and accurately. I am Ravana, I have arrived, desirous of battle with that foremost of men. My arrival should also be announced to him by you.

shloka_text: इत्येवं रावणेनोक्तास्ते ऽमात्याः सुविपश्चितः । अब्रुवन्राक्षसपतिमसान्निध्यं महीपतेः ।। 7.31.12 ।।
explanation: Thus, addressed by Ravana, those very wise ministers spoke to the lord of Rakshasas about the absence of the king.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा विश्रवसः पुत्रः पौराणामर्जुनं गतम् । अपसृत्यागतो विन्ध्यं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् ।। 7.31.13 ।।
explanation: Having heard that Arjuna had gone to the citizens, the son of Vishravas retreated and came to the Vindhya mountain, which resembled the Himalayas.

shloka_text: स तमभ्रमिवाविष्टमुद्भ्रन्तमिव मेदिनीम् । अपश्यद्रावणो विन्ध्यमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम् ।। 7.31.14 ।।
explanation: Ravana saw him, the Vindhya, as if pervading the clouds, as if making the earth reel, and as if scratching the sky.

shloka_text: सहस्रशिखरोपेतं सिंहाध्युषितकन्दरम् । प्रपातपतितैस्तोयैः साट्टहासमिवाम्बुधिम् ।। 7.31.15 ।।
explanation: Endowed with a thousand peaks, its caves inhabited by lions, and with waters falling from its cascades, it was like an ocean with a mighty roar.

shloka_text: देवदानवगन्धर्वैः साप्सरोगणकिन्नरैः । स्वस्त्रीभिः क्रीडमानैश्च स्वर्गभूतं महोच्छ्रयम् ।। 7.31.16 ।।
explanation: By gods, demons, and gandharvas, along with groups of apsaras and kinnaras, sporting with their own wives, it became a heaven, exceedingly grand.

shloka_text: नदीभिः स्यन्दमानाभिः स्फटिकप्रतिमं जलम् । फणाभिश्चलजिह्वाभिरनन्तमिव विष्ठितम् ।। 7.31.17 ।।
explanation: The crystal-like water, flowing from the rivers, was spread out as if it were Ananta with his hoods and flickering tongues.

shloka_text: उत्क्रामन्तं दरीवन्तं हिमवत्सन्निभं गिरिम् । पश्यमानस्ततो विन्ध्यं रावणो नर्मदां ययौ ।। 7.31.18 ।।
explanation: Then Ravana, seeing the Vindhya mountain, which was towering, full of caves, and resembled the Himalayas, went to the Narmada.

shloka_text: चलोपलजलां पुण्यां पश्चिमोदधिगामिनीम् ।। 7.31.19 ।।
explanation: Whose water flows over moving stones, sacred, and flowing towards the western ocean.

shloka_text: महिषैः सृमरैः सिंहैः शार्दूलर्क्षगजोत्तमैः । उष्णाभितप्तैस्तृषितैः सङ्क्षोभितजलाशयाम् ।। 7.31.20 ।।
explanation: A water body agitated by buffaloes, sṛmaras, lions, mighty tigers, bears, and elephants, who were tormented by heat and thirsty.

shloka_text: चक्रवाकैः सकारण्डैः सहंसजलकुक्कुटैः । सारसैश्च सदा मत्तैः सुकूजद्भिः समावृताम् ।। 7.31.21 ।।
explanation: Surrounded by chakravaka birds, along with karanda ducks, swans, and water-hens, and by cranes, always joyful and sweetly cooing.

shloka_text: फुल्लद्रुमकृतोत्तंसां चक्रवाकयुगस्तनीम् । विस्तीर्णपुलिनश्रोणीं हंसावलिसुमेखलाम् ।। 7.31.22 ।।
explanation: Adorned with blooming trees as a head-ornament, having a pair of ruddy geese as her breasts, with wide sandbanks as her hips, and a beautiful girdle of rows of swans.

shloka_text: पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गीं जलफेनामलांशुकाम् । जलावगाहसंस्पर्शां फुल्लोत्पलशुभेक्षणाम् । पुष्पकादवरुह्याशु नर्मदां सरितां वराम् ।। 7.31.23 ।।
explanation: Whose body was smeared with flower pollen, whose spotless garment was like water foam, whose body had the touch of water immersion, whose beautiful eyes were like blooming lotuses, having quickly descended from the Pushpaka to the Narmada, the best of rivers.

shloka_text: इष्टामिव वरां नारीमवगाह्य दशाननः । स तस्याः पुलिने रम्ये नानामुनिनिषेविते ।। 7.31.24 ।।
explanation: Dashanana, having plunged into (the water) as if it were a desired excellent woman, he (was) on its beautiful sandbank, frequented by various sages.

shloka_text: उपोपविष्टैः सचिवैः सार्धं राक्षसपुङ्गवः । प्रख्याय नर्मदां सो ऽथ गङ्गेयमिति रावणः ।। 7.31.25 ।।
explanation: Then Rāvaṇa, the foremost of Rākṣasas, along with his ministers who were seated nearby, declared the Narmada to be the Ganga.

shloka_text: नर्मदादर्शजं हर्षमाप्तवान् राक्षसाधिपः । उवाच सचिवांस्तत्र सलीलं शुकसारणौ ।। 7.31.26 ।।
explanation: The lord of the Rakshasas, having experienced joy from seeing the Narmada, then playfully spoke to his ministers, Shuka and Sarana, there.

shloka_text: एष रश्मिसहस्रेण जगत्कृत्वैव काञ्चनम् । तीक्ष्णतापकरः सूर्यो नभसो ऽर्धं समाश्रितः ।। 7.31.27 ।।
explanation: This Sun, having made the world golden with its thousand rays, and causing intense heat, has occupied half of the sky.

shloka_text: मामासीनं विदित्वैव चन्द्रायति दिवाकरः ।। 7.31.28 ।।
explanation: The sun, just by knowing me to be seated, becomes like the moon.

shloka_text: नर्मदाजलशीतश्च सुगन्धिः श्रमनाशनः । मद्भयादनिलो ऽप्यत्र वात्येष सुसमाहितः ।। 7.31.29 ।।
explanation: The wind, cool from the waters of Narmada, fragrant, and dispelling fatigue, blows here very calmly, even out of fear of me.

shloka_text: इयं वापि सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा नर्मदा नर्मवर्धिनी । नक्रमीनविहङ्गोर्मिः सभयेवाङ्गना स्थिता ।। 7.31.30 ।।
explanation: And this best of rivers, the Narmada, which enhances delight, with its crocodiles, fish, birds, and waves, stands like a timid woman.

shloka_text: तद्भवन्तः क्षताः शस्त्रैर्नृपैरिन्द्रसमैर्युधि । चन्दनस्य रसेनेव रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः ।। 7.31.31 ।।
explanation: Therefore, you, wounded by weapons by kings equal to Indra in battle, are drenched in blood as if with sandalwood paste.

shloka_text: ते यूयमवगाहध्वं नर्मदां शर्मदां शुभाम् । महापद्ममुखा मत्ता गङ्गामिव गहागजाः । अस्यां स्नात्वा महानद्यां पाप्मानं विप्रमोक्ष्यथ ।। 7.31.32 ।।
explanation: You all should immerse yourselves in the Narmada, the auspicious giver of joy, just as mighty, rutting elephants, led by Mahapadma, plunge into the Ganga. Having bathed in this great river, you will be freed from sin.

shloka_text: अहमप्यद्य पुलिने शरदिन्दुसमप्रभे । पुष्पोपहारं शनकैः करिष्यामि कपर्दिनः ।। 7.31.33 ।।
explanation: I too, today, on the sandbank radiant like the autumn moon, will gently make an offering of flowers to Kapardin.

shloka_text: रावणेनैवमुक्तास्तु प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः । समहोदरधूम्राक्षा नर्मदां विजगाहिरे ।। 7.31.34 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Ravana, Prahasta, Shuka, Sarana, along with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, went to the Narmada.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द्रगजैस्तैस्तु क्षोभिता नर्मदा नदी । वामनाञ्जनपद्माद्यैर्गङ्गा इव महागजैः ।। 7.31.35 ।।
explanation: The Narmada river was agitated by those elephants of theha Rakshasa lords, just as the Ganga (river) is agitated by great elephants like Vamana, Anjana, Padma, and others.

shloka_text: ततस्ते राक्षसाः स्नात्वा नर्मदायां महाबलाः । उत्तीर्य पुष्पाण्याजह्रुर्बल्यर्थं रावणस्य तु ।। 7.31.36 ।।
explanation: Then those mighty Rākṣasas, having bathed in the Narmada and come out, brought flowers for Ravana's offering.

shloka_text: नर्मदापुलिने हृद्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे । राक्षसैस्तु मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः ।। 7.31.37 ।।
explanation: On the delightful bank of the Narmada, shining like a white cloud, a mountain made of flowers was quickly created by the Rākṣasas in a moment.

shloka_text: पुष्पेषूपहृतेष्वेवं रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । अवतीर्णो नदीं स्नातुं गङ्गामिव महागजः ।। 7.31.38 ।।
explanation: When flowers had thus been offered, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, descended into the river to bathe, like a great elephant into the Ganga.

shloka_text: तत्र स्नात्वा च विधिवज्जप्त्वा जप्यमनुत्तमम् । नर्मदासलिलात्तस्मादुत्ततार स रावणः ।। 7.31.39 ।।
explanation: Having bathed there properly and having recited the excellent mantra, that Ravana emerged from the waters of the Narmada.

shloka_text: ततः क्लिन्नाम्बरं त्यक्त्वा शुक्लवस्त्रसमावृतम् । रावणं प्राञ्जलिं यान्तमन्वयुः सर्वराक्षसाः ।। 7.31.40 ।।
explanation: Then, having discarded his wet clothes and adorned in white garments, all the Rakshasas followed Ravana as he proceeded with folded hands.

shloka_text: तद्गतीवशमापन्ना मूर्तिमन्त इवाचलाः । यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते ।। 7.31.41 ।।
explanation:
मापन्ना - Having come under the sway of his movement (Ravana's).
मूर्तिमन्त इवाचलाः - Like embodied mountains (referring to the carriers).
यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रा

shloka_text: वालुकावेदिमध्ये तु तल्लिङ्गं स्थाप्य रावणः । अर्चयामास गन्धैश्च पुष्पैश्चामृतगन्धिभिः ।। 7.31.42 ।।
explanation: Ravana, having placed that Linga in the middle of a sand altar, worshipped it with fragrances and with flowers fragrant like nectar.

shloka_text: ततः सतामार्तिहरं परं वरं वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम् । समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ प्रसार्य हस्तान्प्रणनर्त चाग्रतः ।। 7.31.43 ।।
explanation: Then, having worshipped that supreme bestower of boons, the remover of the suffering of the good, who is adorned with moonbeams, that demon sang and danced before him, extending his hands.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 31 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (composed by a sage), the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the thirty-first chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: नर्मदापुलिने यत्र राक्षसेन्द्रः सुदारुणः । पुष्पोपहारं कुरुते तस्माद्देशाददूरतः ।। 7.32.1 ।।
explanation: Not far from that place, on the bank of the Narmada, where the extremely fierce king of Rakshasas performs an offering of flowers.

shloka_text: अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो माहिष्मत्याः पतिः प्रभुः । क्रीडते सह नारीभिर्नर्मदातोयमाश्रितः ।। 7.32.2 ।।
explanation: Arjuna, the best of the victorious, the lord and master of Mahishmati, plays with women, dwelling by the waters of the Narmada.

shloka_text: तासां मध्यगतो राजा रराज च तदार्जुनः । करेणूनां सहस्रस्य मध्यस्थ इव कुञ्जरः ।। 7.32.3 ।।
explanation: And that King Arjuna, situated in their midst, shone, like an elephant in the midst of a thousand female elephants.

shloka_text: जिज्ञासुः स तु बाहूनां सहस्रस्योत्तमं बलम् । रुरोध नर्मदावेगं बाहुभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।। 7.32.4 ।।
explanation: Desirous of knowing the supreme strength of his thousand arms, he, surrounded by his many arms, obstructed the current of the Narmada.

shloka_text: कार्तवीर्यभुजासक्तं तज्जलं प्राप्य निर्मलम् । कूलोपहारं कुर्वाणं प्रतिस्रोतः प्रधावति ।। 7.32.5 ।।
explanation: That pure water, having been held by Kartavirya's arms, rushes upstream, eroding the banks.

shloka_text: समीननक्रमकरः सपुष्पकुशसंस्तरः । स नर्मदाम्भसो वेगः प्रावृट्काल इवाबभौ ।। 7.32.6 ।।
explanation: That current of the Narmada's water, teeming with fish, crocodiles, and makaras, and adorned with a spread of flowers and kusha grass, appeared like the rainy season.

shloka_text: स वेगः कार्तवीर्येण सम्प्रेषित इवाम्भसः । पुष्पोपहारं सकलं रावणस्य जहार ह ।। 7.32.7 ।।
explanation: That current, as if sent by Kartavirya from the water, indeed carried away all of Ravana's flower offering.

shloka_text: रावणो ऽर्धसमाप्तं तमुत्सृज्य नियमं तदा । नर्मदां पश्यते कान्तां प्रतिकूलां यथा प्रियाम् ।। 7.32.8 ।।
explanation: Then Ravana, having abandoned that half-completed vow, saw the beautiful Narmada, which was adverse like a beloved woman.

shloka_text: पश्चिमेन तु तं दृष्ट्वा सागरोद्गारसन्निभम् । वर्धन्तमम्भसो वेगं पूर्वामाशां प्रविश्य तु ।। 7.32.9 ।।
explanation: But seeing from the west that increasing surge of water, resembling an ocean's outpouring, it entered the eastern direction.

shloka_text: ततो ऽनुभ्रान्तशकुनां स्वभावोपरमे स्थिताम् । निर्विकाराङ्गनाभासामपश्यद्रावणो नदीम् ।। 7.32.10 ।।
explanation: Then Ravana saw the river, where birds were flying around, which was still, its natural state having ceased, and which resembled an unperturbed woman.

shloka_text: सव्येतरकराङ्गुल्या सशब्दं च दशाननः । वेगप्रभावमन्वेष्टुं सो ऽदिशच्छुकसारणौ ।। 7.32.11 ।।
explanation: Daśānana, with the finger of his right hand and making a sound, ordered Śuka and Sāraṇa to investigate the speed and power.

shloka_text: तौ तु रावणसन्दिष्टौ भ्रातरौ शुकसारणौ । व्योमान्तरगतौ वीरौ प्रस्थितौ पश्चिमामुखौ ।। 7.32.12 ।।
explanation: Those two valiant brothers, Shuka and Sarana, sent by Ravana, having ascended into the sky, departed westward.

shloka_text: अर्धयोजनमात्रं तु गत्वा तौ रजनीचरौ । पश्येतां पुरुषं तोये क्रीडन्तं सहयोषितम् ।। 7.32.13 ।।
explanation: Having gone just half a yojana, those two night-wanderers saw a man playing in the water accompanied by a woman.

shloka_text: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशं तोयव्याकुलमूर्धजम् । मदरक्तान्तनयनं मदव्याकुलतेजसम् ।। 7.32.14 ।।
explanation: Resembling a large Sal tree, with hair dishevelled by water, with the corners of the eyes red from intoxication, and with splendor agitated by intoxication.

shloka_text: नदीं बाहुसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमरिमर्दनम् । गिरिं पादसहस्रेण रुन्धन्तमिव मेदिनीम् ।। 7.32.15 ।।
explanation: Obstructing a river with a thousand arms, the destroyer of enemies, as if obstructing the earth with a thousand feet like a mountain.

shloka_text: बालानां वरनारीणां सहस्रेण समावृतम् । समदानां करेणूनां सहस्रेणेव कुञ्जरम् ।। 7.32.16 ।।
explanation: Surrounded by a thousand young and beautiful women, like an elephant by a thousand female elephants in rut.

shloka_text: तमद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसौ शुकसारणौ । सन्निवृत्तावुपागम्य रावणं तमथोचतुः ।। 7.32.17 ।।
explanation: Having seen that most extraordinary one, the two Rakshasas, Shuka and Sarana, returned and, approaching Ravana, then spoke to him.

shloka_text: बृहत्सालप्रतीकाशः को ऽप्यसौ राक्षसेश्वर । नर्मदां रोधवद्रुद्ध्वा क्रीडापयति योषितः ।। 7.32.18 ।।
explanation: O king of Rākṣasas, who is this one, resembling a great Sala tree, who, having obstructed the Narmada like a dam, makes women sport?

shloka_text: तेन बाहुसहस्रेण सन्निरुद्धजला नदी । सागरोद्गारसङ्काशानुद्गारान्सृजते मुहुः ।। 7.32.19 ।।
explanation: By his thousand arms, the river, its waters completely obstructed, repeatedly emits surges resembling the eruptions of the ocean.

shloka_text: इत्येवं भाषमाणौ तौ निशाम्य शुकसारणौ । रावणो ऽर्जुन इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ युद्धलालसः ।। 7.32.20 ।।
explanation: Having heard Shuka and Saraṇa speaking thus, Rāvaṇa, exclaiming "Arjuna!", proceeded, eager for battle.

shloka_text: अर्जुनाभिमुखे तस्मिन्रावणे राक्षसाधिपे । चण्डः प्रवाति पवनः सनादः सुरजास्तथा ।। 7.32.21 ।।
explanation: When that Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, was facing Arjuna, a fierce wind blew, roaring, and the gods (were also present/reacting).

shloka_text: सकृदेव कृतो रावः सरक्तः प्रेषितो घनैः । महोदरमहापार्श्वधूम्राक्षशुकसारणैः ।। 7.32.22 ।।
explanation: A bloody roar was made just once, sent forth by the mighty Mahodara, Mahaparshva, Dhumraksha, Shuka, and Sarana.

shloka_text: संवृतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तत्रागाद्यत्र चार्जुनः । अदीर्घेणैव कालेन स तदा राक्षसो बली । तं नर्मदाह्रदं भीममाजगामाञ्जनप्रभः ।। 7.32.23 ।।
explanation: Surrounded, the king of Rakshasas came to where Arjuna was. Soon thereafter, that powerful Rakshasa, dark as collyrium, arrived at that formidable Narmada pool.

shloka_text: स तत्र स्त्रीपरिवृतं वाशिताभिरिव द्विपम् । नरेन्द्रं पश्यते राजा राक्षसानां तदार्जुनम् ।। 7.32.24 ।।
explanation: The king of Rākṣasas sees there King Arjuna, surrounded by women, like an elephant by female elephants.

shloka_text: स रोषाद्रक्तनयनो राक्षसेन्द्रो बलोद्धतः ।। 7.32.25 ।।
explanation: He, the king of Rākṣasas, arrogant with power, his eyes red with anger.

shloka_text: इत्येवमर्जुनामात्यनाह गम्भीरया गिरा । अमात्याः क्षिप्रमाख्यात हैहयस्य नृपस्य वै ।। 7.32.26 ।।
explanation: Thus, Arjuna said to his ministers with a deep voice: "O ministers, quickly inform the Haihaya king."

shloka_text: युद्धार्थी समनुप्राप्तो रावणो नाम राक्षसः । रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणो ऽथार्जुनस्य ते । उत्तस्थुः सायुधास्त्राश्च रावणं वाक्यमब्रुवन् ।। 7.32.27 ।।
explanation: The demon named Ravana, desirous of battle, arrived. Having heard Ravana's words, those ministers of Arjuna then rose up with their weapons and missiles, and spoke to Ravana.

shloka_text: युद्धस्य कालो विज्ञेयः साधु भोः साधु रावण ।। 7.32.28 ।।
explanation: The time for war should be understood. Well done, O Ravana, well done!

shloka_text: चः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणो ऽथार्जुनस्य ते । यः क्षीबं स्त्रीवृतं चैव योद्धुमुत्सहते नृपम् । स्त्रीसमक्षं कथं यत्तद्योद्धुमुत्सहसे ऽर्जुनम् । वाशितामध्यगं मत्तं शार्दूल इव कुञ्जरम् ।। 7.32.29 ।।
explanation: And having heard, the ministers then (said) to Arjuna: "How can you, Arjuna, desire to fight a king who is intoxicated and surrounded by women, in the presence of women, like an elephant among roaring lionesses?"

shloka_text: क्षमस्वाद्य दशग्रीव चोष्यतां रजनी त्वया । युद्धे श्रद्धा च यद्यस्ति श्वस्तात समरे ऽर्जुनम् ।। 7.32.30 ।।
explanation: Forgive me today, O Daśagrīva. Let the night be spent by you. And if there is a desire for battle, then tomorrow, dear one, (you may fight) Arjuna in battle.

shloka_text: यद्यद्यास्ति मतिर्योद्धुं युद्धतृष्णासमावृता । निहत्यास्मांस्ततो युद्धमर्जुनेनोपयास्यसि ।। 7.32.31 ।।
explanation: Whatever intention you have to fight, being enveloped by the thirst for battle, only after killing us will you then engage in battle with Arjuna.

shloka_text: ततस्ते रावणामात्यैरमात्याः पार्थिवस्य तु । सूदिताश्चापि ते युद्धे भक्षिताश्च बुभुक्षितैः ।। 7.32.32 ।।
explanation: Then, those ministers of the king were killed by Ravana's ministers in battle, and they were also devoured by the hungry ones.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दो नर्मदातीर आबभौ । अर्जुनस्यानुयातऽणां रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणाम् ।। 7.32.33 ।।
explanation: Then a tumultuous sound arose on the bank of the Narmada, from Arjuna's followers and Ravana's ministers.

shloka_text: इषुभिस्तोमरैः शूलैस्त्रिशूलैर्वज्रकर्षणैः । सरावणानर्दयन्तः समन्तात्समभिद्रुताः ।। 7.32.34 ।।
explanation: Rushing from all sides, they tormented Ravana and his followers with arrows, lances, spears, tridents, and thunderbolt-like weapons.

shloka_text: हैहयाधिपयोधानां वेग आसीत्सुदारुणः । सनक्रमीनमकरसमुद्रस्येव निःस्वनः ।। 7.32.35 ।।
explanation: The impetus of the warriors of the Haihaya king was exceedingly fierce, like the roar of an ocean teeming with crocodiles, fish, and sea-monsters.

shloka_text: रावणस्य तु ते ऽमात्याः प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः । कार्तवीर्यबलं क्रुद्धा निर्दहन्ति स्म तेजसा ।। 7.32.36 ।।
explanation: But those ministers of Ravana, Prahasta, Shuka, and Sarana, enraged, were burning down Kartavirya's army with their might.

shloka_text: अर्जुनाय तु तत्कर्म रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः । क्रीडमानाय कथितं पुरुषैर्द्वाररक्षिभिः ।। 7.32.37 ।।
explanation: And that deed of Ravana, accompanied by his ministers, was told to Arjuna, who was playing, by the doorkeepers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा न भेतव्यमिति स्त्रीजनं तं ततो ऽर्जुनः । उत्ततार जलात्तस्माद्गङ्गातोयादिवाञ्जनः ।। 7.32.38 ।।
explanation: Having heard from those women, "There is no need to fear," Arjuna then rose from that water, just as Añjana would emerge from the waters of the Ganga.

shloka_text: क्रोधदूषितनेत्रस्तु स ततो ऽर्जुनपावकः । प्रजज्वाल महाघोरो युगान्त इव पावकः ।। 7.32.39 ।।
explanation: Then, he, with eyes reddened by anger, Arjuna, like a fire, blazed forth, exceedingly terrible, like the fire at the end of an age.

shloka_text: स तूर्णतरमादाय वरहेमाङ्गदो गदाम् । अभिदुद्राव रक्षांसि तमांसीव दिवाकरः ।। 7.32.40 ।।
explanation: Wearing excellent golden armlets, he swiftly took his mace and attacked the Rākṣasas, just as the sun dispels darkness.

shloka_text: बाहुविक्षेपकरणां समुद्यम्य महागदाम् । गारुडं वेगमास्थाय चापपातैव सो ऽर्जुनः ।। 7.32.41 ।।
explanation: Having raised his great mace, which caused arms to be flung about, and having adopted the speed of Garuda, that Arjuna indeed rushed down.

shloka_text: तस्य मार्गं समारुद्ध्य विन्ध्यो ऽर्कस्येव पर्वतः । स्थितो विन्ध्य इवाकम्प्यः प्रहस्तो मुसलायुधः ।। 7.32.42 ।।
explanation: Prahasta, armed with a mace, blocked his path. He stood like the Vindhya mountain obstructing the sun, as unshakable as the Vindhya.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्य मुसलं घोरं लोहबद्धं महोद्धतः । प्रहस्तः प्रेषयन्क्रुद्धो ररास च यथाम्बुदः ।। 7.32.43 ।।
explanation: Then, the greatly agitated Prahasta, enraged, hurled a terrible, iron-bound mace at him and roared like a cloud.

shloka_text: तस्याग्रे मुसलस्याग्निरशोकापीडसन्निभः । प्रहस्तकरमुक्तस्य बभूव प्रदहन्निव ।। 7.32.44 ।।
explanation: Before him, the fire of the mace, released from Prahasta's hand, appeared resembling a cluster of Ashoka flowers, as if burning.

shloka_text: अथायान्तं तु मुसलं कार्तवीर्यस्तदार्जुनः । निपुणं वञ्चयामास सगदो ऽगदविक्रमः ।। 7.32.45 ।।
explanation: Then, Kartavirya Arjuna, wielding his mace and of unimpeded valor, skillfully dodged the approaching mace.

shloka_text: ततस्तमभिदुद्राव प्रहस्तं हैहयाधिपः । भ्रामयानो गदां गुर्वीं पञ्चबाहुशतोच्छ्रयाम् ।। 7.32.46 ।।
explanation: Then the Haihaya king rushed towards Prahasta, whirling his heavy mace, which was five hundred arms in height.

shloka_text: तथा हतो ऽतिवेगेन प्रहस्तो गदया तदा । निपपात स्थितः शैलो वज्रिवज्रहतो यथा ।। 7.32.47 ।।
explanation: Thus, Prahasta, struck with great force by a mace at that time, fell down like a standing mountain struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तं पतितं दृष्ट्वा मारीचशुकसारणाः । समहोदरधूम्राक्षा ह्यपसृष्टा रणाजिरात् ।। 7.32.48 ।।
explanation: Having seen Prahasta fallen, Maricha, Shuka, Sarana, along with Mahodara and Dhumraksha, retreated from the battlefield.

shloka_text: अपक्रान्तेष्वमात्येषु प्रहस्ते वै निपातिते । रावणो ऽभ्यद्रवत्तूर्णमर्जुनं नृपसत्तमम् ।। 7.32.49 ।।
explanation: When his ministers had fled and Prahasta was struck down, Ravana quickly rushed towards Arjuna, the best of kings.

shloka_text: सहस्रबाहोस्तद्युद्धं विंशद्बाहोश्च दारुणम् । नृपराक्षसयोस्तत्र चारब्धं रोमहर्षणम् ।। 7.32.50 ।।
explanation: There commenced that terrible and hair-raising battle between the thousand-armed one and the twenty-armed one, between the king and the demon.

shloka_text: सागराविव संरब्धौ चलन्मूलाविवाचलौ । तेजोयुक्ताविवादित्यौ प्रदहन्ताविवानलौ ।। 7.32.51 ।।
explanation: Like two enraged oceans, like two mountains whose roots are shaking, like two suns endowed with splendor, like two fires burning intensely.

shloka_text: बलोद्धतौ यथा नागौ वाशितार्थे यथा वृषौ । मेघाविव विनर्दन्तौ सिंहाविव बलोत्कटौ ।। 7.32.52 ।।
explanation: Like two elephants arrogant with strength, like two bulls for the sake of a female, roaring like two clouds, like two exceedingly strong lions.

shloka_text: रुद्रकालाविव क्रुद्धौ तदा तौ राक्षसार्जुनौ । परस्परं गदाभ्यां तौ ताडयामासतुर्भृशम् ।। 7.32.53 ।।
explanation: Then, those two, the Rakshasa and Arjuna, enraged like Rudra and Kala, struck each other fiercely with maces.

shloka_text: वज्रप्रहारानचला यथा घोरान्विषेहिरे । गदाप्रहारांस्तौ तत्र सेहाते नरराक्षसौ ।। 7.32.54 ।।
explanation: Just as mountains endured terrible thunderbolt strikes, so did the man and the demon endure mace strikes there.

shloka_text: यथा ऽ शनिरवेभ्यस्तु जायते ऽथ प्रतिश्रुतिः । तथा तयोर्गदापोथैर्दिशः सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुताः ।। 7.32.55 ।।
explanation: Just as an echo arises from the sounds of thunderbolts, so too, by the blows of their maces, all directions reverberated.

shloka_text: अर्जुनस्य गदा सा तु पात्यमाना ऽहितोरसि । काञ्चनाभं नभश्चक्रे विद्युत्सौदामिनी यथा ।। 7.32.56 ।।
explanation: That mace of Arjuna, as it fell upon the enemy's chest, made the sky golden-hued, like a flash of lightning.

shloka_text: तथैव रावणेनापि पात्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः । अर्जुनोरसि निर्भाति गदोल्केव महागिरौ ।। 7.32.57 ।।
explanation: Similarly, being struck repeatedly by Ravana, it shone on Arjuna's chest like a mace-meteor on a great mountain.

shloka_text: नार्जुनः खेदमायाति न राक्षसगणेश्वरः । इदमासीत्तयोर्युद्धं यथा पूर्वं बलीन्द्रयोः ।। 7.32.58 ।।
explanation: Arjuna did not experience weariness, nor did the lord of the Rakshasa hosts. Their battle was like that of Bali and Indra in the past.

shloka_text: शृङ्गैरिव वृषायुध्यन्दन्ताग्रैरिव कुञ्जरौ । परस्परं तौ निघ्नन्तौ नरराक्षससत्तमौ ।। 7.32.59 ।।
explanation: Like bulls fighting with their horns, and like two elephants with the tips of their tusks, those two, the best among men and demons, struck each other.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्जुनेन क्रुद्धेन सर्वप्राणेन सा गदा । स्तनयोरन्तरे मुक्ता रावणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.32.60 ।।
explanation: Then, the enraged Arjuna, with all his might, hurled that mace at Ravana's great chest, between his breasts.

shloka_text: वरदानकृतत्राणे सा गदा रावणोरसि । दुर्बलेव यथावेगं द्विधाभूत्वा ऽपतत्क्षितौ ।। 7.32.61 ।।
explanation: That mace, upon Ravana's chest, which was protected by a boon, fell to the ground, splitting into two, as if weak, despite its full force.

shloka_text: स त्वर्जुनप्रमुक्तेन गदापातेन रावणः । अपासर्पद्धनुर्मात्रं निषसाद च निष्टनन् ।। 7.32.62 ।।
explanation: But Ravana, by the mace-blow released by Arjuna, recoiled a bow's length and sat down, groaning.

shloka_text: स विह्वलं तदालक्ष्य दशग्रीवं ततो ऽर्जुनः । सहसोत्पत्य जग्राह गरुत्मानिव पन्नगम् ।। 7.32.63 ।।
explanation: Seeing Dashagriva bewildered, Arjuna then suddenly sprang up and seized him, just as Garuda seizes a serpent.

shloka_text: स तु बाहुसहस्रेण बलाद्गृह्य दशाननम् । बबन्ध बलवान्राजा बलिं नारायणो यथा ।। 7.32.64 ।।
explanation: But that powerful king, with his thousand arms, forcibly seizing Dashanana, bound him, just as Narayana bound Bali.

shloka_text: बध्यमाने दशग्रीवे सिद्धचारणदेवताः । साध्वीतिवादिनः पुष्पैः किरन्त्यर्जुनमूर्धनि ।। 7.32.65 ।।
explanation: As Daśagrīva was being bound, the Siddhas, Chāraṇas, and Devas, exclaiming "Excellent!", showered flowers upon Arjuna's head.

shloka_text: व्याघ्रो मृगमिवादाय मृगराडिव दन्तिनम् । ननाद हैहयो राजा हर्षादम्बुदवन्मुहुः ।। 7.32.66 ।।
explanation: Like a tiger seizing a deer, or a lion an elephant, the Haihaya king roared repeatedly with joy, like a cloud.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तस्तु समाश्वस्तो दृष्ट्वा बद्धं दशाननम् । सह तै राक्षसैः क्रुद्धश्चाभिदुद्राव पार्थिवम् ।। 7.32.67 ।।
explanation: Prahasta, however, emboldened upon seeing Daśānana bound, became enraged and, along with those Rākṣasas, rushed towards the king.

shloka_text: नक्तञ्चराणां वेगस्तु तेषामापततां बभौ । उद्भूत आतपापाये पयोदानामिवाम्बुधौ ।। 7.32.68 ।।
explanation: The rush of those night-wanderers as they descended appeared, like the clouds arising in the ocean at the end of the hot season.

shloka_text: मुञ्च मुञ्चेति भाषन्तस्तिष्ठतिष्ठेति चासकृत् । मुसलानि सशूलानि सोत्ससर्ज तदार्जुने ।। 7.32.69 ।।
explanation: Saying 'Release! Release!' and 'Stop! Stop!' repeatedly, he then hurled maces along with spears at Arjuna.

shloka_text: अप्राप्तान्येव तान्याशु असम्भ्रान्तस्तदार्जुनः । आयुधान्यमरारीणां जग्राहारिनिषूदनः ।। 7.32.70 ।।
explanation: Then Arjuna, the destroyer of enemies, quickly and without agitation, seized those very weapons of the enemies of the gods, even before they had reached their target.

shloka_text: ततस्तैरेव रक्षांसि दुर्धरैः प्रवरायुधैः । भित्त्वा विद्रावयामास वायुरम्बुधरानिव ।। 7.32.71 ।।
explanation: Then, with those very formidable excellent weapons, they pierced the demons and put them to flight, just as the wind disperses clouds.

shloka_text: राक्षसांस्त्रासयित्वा तु कार्तवीर्यो ऽर्जुनस्तदा । रावणं गृह्य नगरं प्रविवेश सुहृद्वृतः ।। 7.32.72 ।।
explanation: Then Kārtavīrya Arjuna, having terrified the Rākṣasas and captured Rāvaṇa, entered the city, surrounded by his friends.

shloka_text: स कीर्यमाणः कुसुमाक्षतोत्करैर्द्विजैः सपौरैः पुरुहूतसन्निभः । तदा ऽर्जुनः सम्प्रविवेश तां पुरीं बलिं निगृह्येव सहस्रलोचनः ।। 7.32.73 ।।
explanation: He, Arjuna, resembling Puruhūta, being showered with heaps of flowers and unbroken rice by the Brahmins and citizens, then entered that city, just as the thousand-eyed one (Indra) would after subduing Bali.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 32 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the first epic poem by the glorious Valmiki, this is the thirty-second chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: रावणग्रहणं तत्तु वायुग्रहणसन्निभम् । ततः पुलस्त्यः शुश्राव कथितं दिवि दैवतैः ।। 7.33.1 ।।
explanation: Rāvaṇa's capture was indeed like the capture of wind. Then, Pulastya heard it spoken by the gods in heaven.

shloka_text: ततः पुत्रकृतस्नेहात्कम्प्यमानो महाधृतिः । माहिष्मतीपतिं द्रष्टुमाजगाम महानृषिः ।। 7.33.2 ।।
explanation: Then, the great sage, though of great fortitude, trembling due to affection for his son, came to see the lord of Mahiṣmatī.

shloka_text: स वायुमार्गमास्थाय वायुतुल्यगतिर्द्विजः । पुरीं माहिष्मतीं प्राप्तो मनःसम्पातविक्रमः ।। 7.33.3 ।।
explanation: That Brahmana, having taken the aerial path, possessing speed like the wind and prowess like the swiftness of thought, arrived at the city of Mahishmati.

shloka_text: सो ऽमरावतिसङ्काशां हृष्टपुष्टजनाकुलाम् । प्रविवेश पुरीं ब्रह्मा इन्द्रस्येवामरावतीम् ।। 7.33.4 ।।
explanation: He entered the city, which resembled Amaravati and was crowded with happy and well-fed people, just as Brahma enters Indra's Amaravati.

shloka_text: पादचारमिवादित्यं निष्पतन्तं सुदुर्दशम् । ततस्ते प्रत्यभिज्ञाय अर्जुनाय निवेदयन् ।। 7.33.5 ।।
explanation: Then they, having recognized the sun, which was emerging like a foot-traveler and was very difficult to behold, reported to Arjuna.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्य इति विज्ञाय वचनाद्धैहयाधिपः । शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय प्रत्युद्गच्छत्तपस्विनम् ।। 7.33.6 ।।
explanation: The Haihaya king, having known him to be Pulastya from the words (spoken), placed his folded hands on his head and went forward to meet the ascetic.

shloka_text: पुरोहितो ऽस्य गृह्यार्घ्यं मधुपर्कं तथैव च । पुरस्तात्प्रययौ राज्ञः शक्रस्येव बृहस्पतिः ।। 7.33.7 ।।
explanation: His priest, taking the arghya and madhuparka, went ahead of the king, just as Brihaspati precedes Indra.

shloka_text: ततस्तमृषिमायान्तमुद्यन्तमिव भास्करम् । अर्जुनो दृश्य सम्भ्रान्तो ववन्देन्द्र इवेश्वरम् ।। 7.33.8 ।।
explanation: Then, Arjuna, seeing that sage approaching like the rising sun, was overwhelmed and bowed down, just as Indra bows to the Lord.

shloka_text: स तस्य मधुपर्कं गां पाद्यमर्घ्यं निवेद्य च । पुलस्त्यमाह राजेन्द्रो हर्षगद्गदया गिरा ।। 7.33.9 ।।
explanation: Having offered him Madhuparka, a cow, water for the feet, and Arghya, the great king spoke to Pulastya with a voice choked with joy.

shloka_text: अद्यैवममरावत्या तुल्या माहिष्मती कृता । अद्याहं तु द्विजेन्द्र त्वां यस्मात्पश्यामि दुर्दशम् ।। 7.33.10 ।।
explanation: Today, Maheshmati has thus been made equal to Amravati. But today, O best among Brahmins, because I see you in a pitiable state.

shloka_text: अद्य मे कुशलं देव अद्य मे कुशलं व्रतम् । अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः । यस्माद्देवगणैर्वन्द्यौ वन्दे ऽहं चरणौ तव ।। 7.33.11 ।।
explanation: Today, O God, is my good fortune; today my vow is auspicious. Today my life is fruitful; today my penance is fruitful. Because I bow to your feet, which are revered by the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: इदं राज्यमिमे पुत्रा इमे दारा इमे वयम् । ब्रह्मन्किं कुर्मि किं कार्यमाज्ञापयतु नो भवान् ।। 7.33.12 ।।
explanation: This kingdom, these sons, these wives, and we ourselves – O Brahmana, what should we do? What is the task? Please command us.

shloka_text: तं धर्मे ऽग्निषु पुत्रेषु शिवं पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम् । पुलस्त्योवाच राजानं हैहयानां तथा ऽर्जुनम् ।। 7.33.13 ।।
explanation: Having asked that king, the ruler of the earth, about his welfare concerning dharma, the sacred fires, and his sons, Pulastya then spoke to Arjuna, the king of the Haihayas.

shloka_text: नरेन्द्राम्बुजपत्राक्ष पूर्णचन्द्रनिभानन । अतुलं ते बलं येन दशग्रीवस्त्वया जितः ।। 7.33.14 ।।
explanation: O King, whose eyes are like lotus petals, whose face resembles the full moon, your strength is unequalled, by which Dashagriva was conquered by you.

shloka_text: भयाद्यस्योपतिष्ठेतां निष्पन्दौ सागरानिलौ । सो ऽयं मृधे त्वया बद्धः पौत्रो मे रणदुर्जयः ।। 7.33.15 ।।
explanation: From whose fear the ocean and the wind become motionless, that very grandson of mine, unconquerable in battle, has been bound by you in combat.

shloka_text: पुत्रकस्य यशः पीतं नाम विश्रावितं त्वया । मद्वाक्याद्याच्यमानो ऽद्य मुञ्च वत्सं दशाननम् ।। 7.33.16 ।।
explanation: You have eclipsed your son's glory and made his name known. Being implored by my words today, release the child, Dashanana.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्याज्ञां प्रगृह्योचे न किञ्चन वचो ऽर्जुनः । मुमोच वै पार्थिवेन्द्रो राक्षसेन्द्रं प्रहृष्टवत् ।। 7.33.17 ।।
explanation: Having received Pulastya's command, Arjuna did not utter any word. Indeed, the great king released the king of Rakshasas with great delight.

shloka_text: स तं प्रमुच्य त्रिदशारिमर्जुनः प्रपूज्य दिव्याभरणस्रगम्बरैः । अहिंसकं सख्यमुपेत्य साग्निकं प्रणम्य तं ब्रह्मसुतं गृहं ययौ ।। 7.33.18 ।।
explanation: Arjuna, having released that enemy of the gods, and having honored him with divine ornaments, garlands, and garments, having entered into a non-violent friendship sworn before fire, and having bowed down to that son of Brahma, went home.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्येनापि सन्त्यक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान् । परिष्वक्तः कृतातिथ्यो लज्जमानो विनिर्जितः ।। 7.33.19 ।।
explanation: The mighty king of Rākṣasas, even though abandoned by Pulastya, was embraced, received hospitality, yet felt ashamed and was defeated.

shloka_text: पितामहसुतश्चापि पुलस्त्यो मुनिपुङ्गवः । मोचयित्वा दशग्रीवं ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ह ।। 7.33.20 ।।
explanation: And Pulastya, the son of Brahma, the foremost among sages, having released Daśagrīva, went to Brahmaloka.

shloka_text: एवं स रावणः प्राप्तः कार्तवीर्यात्प्रधर्षणम् । पुलस्त्यवचनाच्चापि पुनर्मुक्तो महाबलः ।। 7.33.21 ।।
explanation: Thus, that mighty Ravana, having suffered defeat at the hands of Kartavirya, was again released by the words of Pulastya.

shloka_text: एवं बलिभ्यो बलिनः सन्ति राघवनन्दन । नावज्ञा हि परे कार्या य इच्छेत् प्रियमात्मनः ।। 7.33.22 ।।
explanation: Thus, O delight of Raghu, there are those who are stronger than the strong. Indeed, one who desires one's own good should not show disrespect towards others.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा पिशिताशनानां सहस्रबाहोरुपलभ्य मैत्रीम् । पुनर्नृपाणां कदनं चकार चचार सर्वां पृथिवीं च दर्पात् ।। 7.33.23 ।।
explanation: Then that king, having obtained the friendship of Sahasrabahu and of the flesh-eaters, again caused the destruction of kings and roamed over the entire earth with pride.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 33 ।।
