explanation: Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: अर्जुनेन विमुक्तस्तु रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । चचार पृथिवीं सर्वामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः ।। 7.34.1 ।।
explanation: Ravana, the lord of the Rakshasas, having been released by Arjuna, thus wandered the entire earth undiscouraged.

shloka_text: राक्षसं वा मनुष्यं वा शृणुते ऽयं बलाधिकम् । रावणस्तं समासाद्य युद्धे ह्वयति दर्पितः ।। 7.34.2 ।।
explanation: Whenever this arrogant Rāvaṇa hears of a demon or a human who is superior in strength, he approaches him and challenges him in battle.

shloka_text: ततः कदाचित्किष्किन्धां नगरीं वालिपालिताम् । गत्वा ह्वयति युद्धाय वालिनं हेममालिनम् ।। 7.34.3 ।।
explanation: Then, one day, having gone to the city of Kishkindha, ruled by Vali, he challenged Vali, who wore a golden garland, for battle.

shloka_text: ततस्तु वानरामात्यस्तारस्तारापिता प्रभुः । उवाच वानरो वाक्यं युद्धप्रेप्सुमुपागतम् ।। 7.34.4 ।।
explanation: Then, the powerful monkey minister Tara, whose father is the star, spoke a word to the monkey who had approached, eager for battle.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द गतो वाली यस्ते प्रतिबलो भवेत् । को ऽन्यः प्रमुखतः स्थातुं तव शक्तः प्लवङ्गमः ।। 7.34.5 ।।
explanation: O King of Rākṣasas, Vali, who was your equal opponent, is gone. What other monkey is capable of standing before you?

shloka_text: चतुर्भ्यो ऽपि समुद्रेभ्यः सन्ध्यामन्वास्य रावण । इमं मुहूर्तमायाति वाली तिष्ठ मुहूर्तकम् ।। 7.34.6 ।।
explanation: O Ravana, having performed his twilight worship from all four oceans, Vali is coming this very moment. Wait for a moment.

shloka_text: एतानस्थिचयान्पश्य य एते शङ्खपाण्डुराः । युद्धार्थिनामिमे राजन्वानराधिपतेजसा ।। 7.34.7 ।।
explanation: Behold these heaps of bones, which are white as conches. O King, these belong to those who desired battle, [vanquished] by the might of the lord of monkeys.

shloka_text: यद्वा ऽमृतरसः पीतस्त्वया रावण राक्षस । तदा वालिनमासाद्य तदन्तं तव जीवितम् ।। 7.34.8 ।।
explanation: Even if the nectar of immortality was drunk by you, O demon Ravana, then upon encountering Valin, that would have been the end of your life.

shloka_text: पश्येदानीं जगच्चित्रमिमं विश्रवसः सुत । इदं मुहूर्तं तिष्ठस्व दुर्लभं ते भविष्यति ।। 7.34.9 ।।
explanation: O son of Vishravas, behold now this spectacle of the world. Stay for this moment; it will be rare for you.

shloka_text: अथवा त्वरसे मर्तुं गच्छ दक्षिणसागरम् । वालिनं द्रक्ष्यसे तत्र भूमिस्थमिव पावकम् ।। 7.34.10 ।।
explanation: Or, if you hasten to die, go to the southern ocean. There you will see Valin, like a fire on the ground.

shloka_text: स तु तारं विनिर्भर्त्स्य रावणो लोकरावणः । पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य प्रययौ दक्षिणार्णवम् ।। 7.34.11 ।।
explanation: He, that Rāvaṇa, the tormentor of the worlds, having severely rebuked Tāra, ascended that Pushpaka and went to the southern ocean.

shloka_text: तत्र हेमगिरिप्रख्यं तरुणार्कनिभाननम् । रावणो वालिनं दृष्ट्वा सन्ध्योपासनतत्परम् ।। 7.34.12 ।।
explanation: There, Ravana saw Vali, who resembled a golden mountain, whose face was like the rising sun, and who was intent on performing his evening prayers.

shloka_text: पुष्पकादवरुह्याथ रावणो ऽञ्जनसन्निभः । ग्रहीतुं वालिनं तूर्णं निःशब्दपदमाव्रजत् ।। 7.34.13 ।।
explanation: Then Ravana, dark like collyrium, having descended from the Pushpaka, quickly approached with silent steps to seize Vali.

shloka_text: यदृच्छया तदा दृष्टो वालिनापि स रावणः । पापाभिप्रायवान् दृष्ट्वा चकार न तु सम्भ्रमम् ।। 7.34.14 ।।
explanation: Then, Ravana was seen by Vali by chance. But Ravana, being of evil intent, did not show any alarm upon seeing (Vali).

shloka_text: शशमालक्ष्य सिंहो वा पन्नगं गरुडो यथा । न चिन्तयति तं वाली रावणं पापनिश्चयम् ।। 7.34.15 ।।
explanation: Just as a lion does not consider a rabbit, or Garuda a snake, so too Vali does not give a thought to that Ravana, who is resolute in evil.

shloka_text: जिघृक्षमाणमायान्तं रावणं पापचेतसम् । कक्षावलम्बिनं कृत्वा गमिष्ये त्रीन्महार्णवान् ।। 7.34.16 ।।
explanation: Having made the evil-minded Ravana, who was approaching to seize me, hang from my armpit, I will go through the three great oceans.

shloka_text: द्रक्ष्यन्त्यरिं ममाङ्कस्थं स्रंसदूरुकराम्बरम् । लम्बमानं दशग्रीवं गरुडस्येव पन्नगम् ।। 7.34.17 ।।
explanation: They will see the enemy Daśagrīva on my lap, with his thighs, hands, and garments slipping, hanging down like a serpent in the grasp of Garuda.

shloka_text: इत्येवं मतिमास्थाय वाली कर्णमुपाश्रितः । जपन्वै नैगमान्मन्त्रांस्तस्थौ पर्वतराडिव ।। 7.34.18 ।।
explanation: Thus having adopted this resolve, Vali, having taken a secluded position, chanting the Vedic mantras, stood like a king of mountains.

shloka_text: तावन्योन्यं जिघृक्षन्तौ हरिराक्षसपार्थिवौ । प्रयत्नवन्तौ तत्कर्म ईहतुर्बलदर्पितौ ।। 7.34.19 ।।
explanation: Those two, the monkey and the Rakshasa king, desiring to seize each other, proud of their strength, strove with great effort in that deed.

shloka_text: हस्तग्राहं तु तं मत्वा पादशब्देन रावणम् । पराङ्मुखो ऽपि जग्राह वाली सर्पमिवाण्डजः ।। 7.34.20 ।।
explanation: Vali, recognizing Ravana by the sound of his footsteps as one who could be caught by hand, seized him even while facing away, just as a bird catches a snake.

shloka_text: ग्रहीतुकामं तं गृह्य रक्षसामीश्वरं हरिः । खमुत्पपात वेगेन कृत्वा कक्षावलम्बिनम् ।। 7.34.21 ।।
explanation: Hari, having seized that lord of Rakshasas who was desirous of seizing, and having made him hang from his armpit, swiftly flew up into the sky.

shloka_text: तं चापीडयमानं तु वितुदन्तं नखैर्मुहुः । जहार रावणं वाली पवनस्तोयदं यथा ।। 7.34.22 ।।
explanation: Vali carried away Ravana, who, though being crushed, was repeatedly scratching him with his nails, just as the wind carries a cloud.

shloka_text: अथ ते राक्षसामात्या ह्रियमाणं दशाननम् । मुमोक्षयिषवो वालिं रवमाणा अभिद्रुताः ।। 7.34.23 ।।
explanation: Then those demon ministers, desiring to free Daśānana who was being carried away, rushed towards Vāli, roaring.

shloka_text: अन्वीयमानस्तैर्वाली भ्राजते ऽम्बरमध्यगः । अन्वीयमानो मेघौघैरम्बरस्थ इवांशुमान् ।। 7.34.24 ।।
explanation: Vali, being followed by them, shone in the middle of the sky, like the sun in the sky accompanied by masses of clouds.

shloka_text: ते ऽशक्नुवन्तः सम्प्राप्तुं वालिनं राक्षसोत्तमाः । तस्य बाहूरुवेगेन परिश्रान्ता व्यवस्थिताः ।। 7.34.25 ।।
explanation: The foremost Rākṣasas, being unable to catch Valin, became exhausted by the speed of his arms and thighs and stood still.

shloka_text: वालिमार्गादपाक्रामन्पर्वतेन्द्रो हि गच्छतः । किं पुनर्जीवितप्रेप्सुर्बिभ्रद्वै मांसशोणितम् ।। 7.34.26 ।।
explanation: Indeed, even the lord of mountains retreated from Vali's path as he went. How much more so should one, desiring to live and bearing flesh and blood, do the same?

shloka_text: अपक्षिगणसम्पातान्वानरेन्द्रो महाजवः । क्रमशः सागरान्सर्वान्सन्ध्याकालमवन्दत ।। 7.34.27 ।।
explanation: The very swift king of monkeys, where the flights of bird flocks had ceased, successively worshipped all the oceans at twilight.

shloka_text: सभाज्यमानो भूतैस्तु खैचरैः खैचरोत्तमः । पश्चिमं सागरं वाली ह्याजगाम सरावणः ।। 7.34.28 ।।
explanation: Vali, the best among sky-dwellers, being honored by sky-dwelling beings, indeed arrived at the western ocean along with Ravana.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्सन्ध्यामुपासित्वा स्नात्वा जप्त्वा च वानरः । उत्तरं सागरं प्रायाद्वहमानो दशाननम् ।। 7.34.29 ।।
explanation: Having performed the twilight worship there, having bathed and chanted, the monkey proceeded to the northern ocean, carrying Daśānana.

shloka_text: बहुयोजनसाहस्रं वहमानो महाहरिः । वायुवच्च मनोवच्च जगाम सह शत्रुणा ।। 7.34.30 ।।
explanation: The great Hari, carrying the enemy, traveled for many thousands of yojanas, moving like the wind and like the mind.

shloka_text: उत्तरे सागरे सन्ध्यामुपासित्वा दशाननम् । वहमानो ऽगमद्वाली पूर्वं वै स महोदधिम् ।। 7.34.31 ।।
explanation: Having performed his twilight worship in the northern ocean, Vali, carrying Dashanana, went to the great eastern ocean.

shloka_text: तत्रापि सन्ध्यामन्वास्य वासविः सहरीश्वरः । किष्किन्धामभितो गृह्य रावणं पुनरागमत् ।। 7.34.32 ।।
explanation: Even there, having performed the evening rites, Vasavi (Rama), along with the lord of monkeys, having secured the area around Kishkindha, returned to Ravana.

shloka_text: चतुर्ष्वपि समुद्रेषु सन्ध्यामन्वास्य वानरः । रावणोद्वहनश्रान्तः किष्किन्धोपवने ऽपतत् ।। 7.34.33 ।।
explanation: The monkey, having performed the evening prayer in all four oceans, tired from carrying Ravana, landed in the grove of Kishkindha.

shloka_text: रावणं तु मुमोचाथ स्वकक्षात्कपिसत्तमः । कुतस्त्वमिति चोवाच प्रहसन्रावणं मुहुः ।। 7.34.34 ।।
explanation: Then the best of monkeys released Ravana from his armpit. And laughing repeatedly, he asked Ravana, "Where are you from?"

shloka_text: विस्मयं तु महद्गत्वा श्रमलोलनिरीक्षणः । राक्षसेन्द्रो हरीन्द्रं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.34.35 ।।
explanation: Having experienced great astonishment, and with his gaze unsteady from fatigue, the lord of Rākṣasas spoke these words to that lord of monkeys.

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्र महेन्द्राभ राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽस्मि रावणः । युद्धेप्सुरिह सम्प्राप्तः स चाद्यासादितस्त्वया ।। 7.34.36 ।।
explanation: O king of monkeys, O one resembling Mahendra, I am Ravana, the king of Rakshasas. Desiring battle, I have arrived here, and today you have found me.

shloka_text: अहो बलमहो वीर्यमहो गाम्भीर्यमेव च । येनाहं पशुवद्गृह्य भ्रामितश्चतुरो ऽर्णवान् ।। 7.34.37 ।।
explanation: Oh, the strength! Oh, the valor! And oh, the profundity! By which I was seized like an animal and made to wander through the four oceans.

shloka_text: एवमश्रान्तवद्वीर शीघ्रमेव महार्णवान् । मां चैवोद्वहमानस्तु को ऽन्यो वीरः क्रमिष्यति ।। 7.34.38 ।।
explanation: Thus, O hero, who else will swiftly traverse the great oceans, tirelessly carrying me?

shloka_text: त्रयाणामेव भूतानां गतिरेषा प्लवङ्गम । मनोनिलसुपर्णानां तव चात्र न संशयः ।। 7.34.39 ।।
explanation: O monkey, this speed belongs to only three beings: the mind, the wind, and Suparna (Garuda), and to you. There is no doubt in this.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं दृष्टबलस्तुभ्यमिच्छामि हरिपुङ्गव । त्वया सह चिरं सख्यं सुस्निग्धं पावकाग्रतः ।। 7.34.40 ।।
explanation: Therefore, I, having seen your strength, O best of monkeys, desire a very affectionate, long-lasting friendship with you in front of the fire.

shloka_text: दाराः पुत्राः पुरं राष्ट्रं भोगाच्छादनभोजनम् । सर्वमेवाविभक्तं नौ भविष्यति हरीश्वर ।। 7.34.41 ।।
explanation: Wives, sons, city, kingdom, enjoyments, clothing, and food – all of this will indeed be undivided for us, O Lord of Hari.

shloka_text: ततः प्रज्वालयित्वाग्निं तावुभौ हरीराक्षसौ । भ्रातृत्वमुपसम्पन्नौ परिष्वज्य परस्परम् ।। 7.34.42 ।।
explanation: Then, having kindled the fire, those two, the monkey and the demon, having attained brotherhood, embraced each other.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं लम्बितकरौ ततस्तौ हरिराक्षसौ । किष्किन्धां विशतुर्हृष्टौ सिंहौ गिरिगुहामिव ।। 7.34.43 ।।
explanation: Then, holding each other's hands, those two, the monkey and the demon, joyfully entered Kishkindha, like two lions entering a mountain cave.

shloka_text: स तत्र मासमुषितः सुग्रीव इव रावणः । अमात्यैरागतैर्नीतस्त्रैलोक्योत्सादनार्थिभिः ।। 7.34.44 ।।
explanation: He, Ravana, having resided there for a month, like Sugriva, was led by his arriving ministers who desired the destruction of the three worlds.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तं वालिना रावणः प्रभो । धर्षितश्च कृतश्चापि भ्राता पावकसन्निधौ ।। 7.34.45 ।।
explanation: O Lord, thus this ancient event occurred: Ravana was humiliated by Vali and also made his brother in the presence of fire.

shloka_text: बलमप्रतिमं राम वालिनो ऽभवदुत्तमम् । सो ऽपि त्वया विनिर्दग्धः शलभो वह्निना यथा ।। 7.34.46 ।।
explanation: O Rama, Vali's strength was unequalled and supreme. Yet, even he was completely consumed by you, just as a moth by fire.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 34 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Sri Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the thirty-fourth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: अपृच्छत तदा रामो दक्षिणाशाश्रमं मुनिम् । प्राञ्जलिर्विनयोपेत इदमाह वचो ऽर्थवत् ।। 7.35.1 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, respectfully, with folded hands, asked the sage of the southern hermitage, speaking these meaningful words.

shloka_text: अतुलं बलमेतद्वै वालिनो रावणस्य च । न त्वेताभ्यां हनुमता समं त्विति मतिर्मम ।। 7.35.2 ।।
explanation: This indeed is the incomparable strength of Vali and Ravana. But, in my opinion, these two are not equal to Hanuman.

shloka_text: शौर्यं दाक्ष्यं बलं धैर्यं प्राज्ञता नयसाधनम् । विक्रमश्च प्रभावश्च हनूमति कृतालयाः ।। 7.35.3 ।।
explanation: Valor, skill, strength, fortitude, wisdom, political acumen, prowess, and influence have made their abode in Hanumān.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वैव सागरं वीक्ष्य सीदन्तीं कपिवाहिनीम् । समाश्वास्य महाबाहुर्योजनानां शतं प्लुतः ।। 7.35.4 ।।
explanation: Having seen the ocean and observing the monkey army despairing, the mighty-armed one, having consoled them, leaped a hundred yojanas.

shloka_text: धर्षयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां रावणान्तःपुरं तदा । दृष्ट्वा सम्भाषिता चापि सीता ह्याश्वासिता तथा ।। 7.35.5 ।।
explanation: Having ravaged the city of Lanka and Ravana's inner palace, Sita was then seen, spoken to, and also comforted.

shloka_text: सेनाग्रगा मन्त्रिसुताः किङ्करा रावणात्मजः । एते हनुमता तत्र ह्येकेन वितिपातिताः ।। 7.35.6 ।।
explanation: The army leaders, the ministers' sons, the attendants, and Ravana's son – all these were struck down there by Hanuman, by him alone.

shloka_text: भूयो बन्धाद्विमुक्तेन भाषयित्वा दशाननम् । लङ्का भस्मीकृता येन पावकेनेव मेदिनी ।। 7.35.7 ।।
explanation: Again, by him who was released from bondage, after having spoken to Ravana, Lanka was reduced to ashes by him, just as the earth is by fire.

shloka_text: न कालस्य न शक्रस्य न विष्णोर्वित्तपस्य च । कर्माणि तानि श्रूयन्ते यानि युद्धे हनूमतः ।। 7.35.8 ।।
explanation: Such deeds as Hanuman performed in battle are not heard of (as performed) by Kala, nor by Shakra, nor by Vishnu, nor by Kubera.

shloka_text: एतस्य बाहुवीर्येण लङ्का सीता च लक्ष्मणः । प्राप्ता मया जयश्चैव राज्यं मित्राणि बान्धवाः ।। 7.35.9 ।।
explanation: By the might of his arms, Lanka, Sita, and Lakshmana were regained by me, and indeed, victory, the kingdom, friends, and kinsmen.

shloka_text: हनूमान्यदि मे नः स्याद्वानराधिपतेः सखा । प्रवृत्तिमपि को वेत्तुं जानक्याः शक्तिमान्भवेत् ।। 7.35.10 ।।
explanation: If Hanuman, the friend of the lord of monkeys, were not with us, who would be capable of knowing even the news of Janaki?

shloka_text: किमर्थं वाल्यनेनैव सुग्रीवप्रियकाम्यया । तदा वैरे समुत्पन्ने न दग्धो वीरुधो यथा ।। 7.35.11 ।।
explanation: Why was this very Vali not burnt like a creeper when enmity arose then, for the sake of pleasing Sugriva?

shloka_text: नहि वेदितवान्मन्ये हनूमानात्मनो बलम् । यद्दृष्टवाञ्जीवितेष्टं क्लिश्यन्तं वानराधिपम् ।। 7.35.12 ।।
explanation: I do not think Hanuman knew his own strength, because he saw the lord of monkeys, dear as life, suffering.

shloka_text: एतन्मे भगवन्सर्वं हनूमति महामतौ । विस्तरेण यथातत्त्वं कथयामरपूजित ।। 7.35.13 ।।
explanation: O Lord, O worshipped by the gods, tell me all this about the great-minded Hanuman, in detail and truthfully.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुयुक्तमृषिस्तदा । हनूमतः समक्षं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.35.14 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard Rama's well-reasoned words, the sage spoke these words to him in Hanuman's presence.

shloka_text: सत्यमेतद्रघुश्रेष्ठ यद्ब्रवीषि हनूमतः । न बले विद्यते तुल्यो न गतौ न मतौ परः ।। 7.35.15 ।।
explanation: O best of Raghu's lineage, what you say about Hanuman is true. No one is equal to him in strength, nor in speed, nor is anyone superior in intellect.

shloka_text: अमोघशापैः शप्तस्तु दत्तो ऽस्य मुनिभिः पुरा । न वेत्ता हि बलं येन बली सन्निरिमर्दनः ।। 7.35.16 ।।
explanation:
्य मुनिभिः पुरा ।
By unfailing curses, he was indeed cursed by the sages long ago.
न वेत्ता हि बलं येन बली सन्निरिमर्दनः ।।
Indeed, he does not know the strength

shloka_text: बाल्ये ऽप्येतेन यत्कर्म कृतं राम महाबल । तन्न वर्णयितुं शक्यमिति बालतया ऽ ऽस्यते ।। 7.35.17 ।।
explanation: O Rama, O mighty-armed one, whatever deeds were done by him even in childhood, that cannot be described; therefore, it is left unsaid due to his childhood.

shloka_text: यदि वा ऽस्ति त्वभिप्रायस्तच्छ्रोतुं तव राघव । समाधाय मतिं राम निशामय वदाम्यहम् ।। 7.35.18 ।।
explanation: If you have the intention to hear that, O Raghava, then concentrating your mind, O Rama, listen, I will speak.

shloka_text: सूर्यदत्तवरस्वर्णः सुमेरुर्नाम पर्वतः । यत्र राज्यं प्रशास्त्यस्य केसरी नाम वै पिता ।। 7.35.19 ।।
explanation: Sumeru is a mountain, golden, having received a boon from the Sun, where his father, named Kesari, rules.

shloka_text: तस्य भार्या बभूवैषा ह्यञ्जनेति परिश्रुता । जनयामास तस्यां वै वायुरात्मजमुत्तमम् ।। 7.35.20 ।।
explanation: His wife was the renowned Anjana. In her, Vayu indeed begot an excellent son.

shloka_text: शालिशूकनिभाभासं प्रासूतामुं तदा ऽञ्जना । फलान्याहर्तुकामा वै निष्क्रान्ता गहनेचरा ।। 7.35.21 ।।
explanation: Then Anjana gave birth to him, radiant like the awn of rice. Desirous of gathering fruits, she had gone out into the dense forest.

shloka_text: एष मातुर्वियोगाच्च क्षुधया च भृशार्दितः । रुरोद शिशुरत्यर्थं शिशुः शरवणे यथा ।। 7.35.22 ।।
explanation: This child, greatly afflicted by separation from his mother and by hunger, cried excessively, like the child in Sharavana.

shloka_text: तदोद्यन्तं विवस्वन्तं जपापुष्पोत्करोपमम् । ददर्श फललोभाच्च ह्युत्पपात रविं प्रति ।। 7.35.23 ।।
explanation: Then he saw the rising sun, resembling a heap of hibiscus flowers. And out of greed for fruit, he flew up towards the sun.

shloka_text: बालार्काभिमुखो बालो बालार्क इव मूर्तिमान् । ग्रहीतुकामो बालार्कं प्लवते ऽम्बरमध्यगः ।। 7.35.24 ।।
explanation: The child, facing the rising sun, himself like an embodied rising sun, desirous of seizing the rising sun, leaps into the middle of the sky.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्प्लवमाने तु शिशुभावे हनूमति । देवदानवयक्षाणां विस्मयः सुमहानभूत् ।। 7.35.25 ।।
explanation: When this Hanumān was flying in his childhood, a very great wonder arose among the Devas, Dānavas, and Yakṣas.

shloka_text: नाप्येवं वेगवान्वायुर्गरुडो वा मनस्तथा । यथा ऽयं वायुपुत्रस्तु क्रमते ऽम्बरमुत्तमम् ।। 7.35.26 ।।
explanation: Neither the wind, nor Garuda, nor the mind is as swift as this son of Vayu traverses the excellent sky.

shloka_text: यदि तावच्छिशोरस्य त्वीदृशो गतिविक्रमः । यौवनं बलमासाद्य कथं वेगो भविष्यति ।। 7.35.27 ।।
explanation: If such is the speed and might of this child, how great will his speed be when he attains youth and strength?

shloka_text: तमनुप्लवते वायुः प्लवन्तं पुत्रमात्मनः । सूर्यदाहभयाद्रक्षंस्तुषारचयशीतलः ।। 7.35.28 ।।
explanation: The wind, cool with a mass of snow, follows his own son who is flying, protecting him from the fear of being burnt by the sun.

shloka_text: बहुयोजनसाहस्रं क्रमत्येष गतोम्बरम् । पितुर्बलाच्च बाल्याच्च भास्कराभ्याशमागतः ।। 7.35.29 ।।
explanation: He traverses many thousands of yojanas, having reached the sky. By his father's strength and his childishness, he came near the sun.

shloka_text: शिशुरेष त्वदोषज्ञ इति मत्वा दिवाकरः । कार्यं चात्र समायत्तमित्येवं न ददाह सः ।। 7.35.30 ।।
explanation: Thinking, "This child is innocent," and "The task here is dependent (on him)," the Sun did not burn him.

shloka_text: यमेव दिवसं ह्येष ग्रहीतुं भास्करं प्लुतः । तमेव दिवसं राहुर्जिघृक्षति दिवाकरम् ।। 7.35.31 ।।
explanation: On the very day that this one (Hanuman) leapt to seize the sun, on that very day Rahu desires to seize the sun.

shloka_text: अनेन स परामृष्टो राम सूर्यरथोपरि । अपक्रान्तस्ततस्त्रस्तो राहुश्चन्द्रार्कमर्दनः ।। 7.35.32 ।।
explanation: O Rama, by him, Rahu, the oppressor of the moon and sun, was seized upon the sun's chariot, and then, terrified, he fled from there.

shloka_text: स इन्द्रभवनं गत्वा सरोषः सिंहिकासुतः । अब्रवीद्भ्रुकुटिं कृत्वा देवं देवगणैर्वृतम् ।। 7.35.33 ।।
explanation: The son of Simhika, enraged, having gone to Indra's abode, spoke with a frown to the god (Indra) who was surrounded by hosts of gods.

shloka_text: बुभुक्षापनयं दत्त्वा चन्द्रार्कौ मम वासव । किमिदं तत्त्वया दत्तमन्यस्य बलवृत्रहन् ।। 7.35.34 ।।
explanation: O Vasava, having given the moon and the sun for the appeasement of my hunger, what is this that has been given by you to another, O slayer of Bala and Vritra?

shloka_text: अद्याहं पर्वकाले तु जिघृक्षुः सूर्यमागतः । अथान्यो राहुरासाद्य जग्राह सहसा रविम् ।। 7.35.35 ।।
explanation: Today, at the time of the eclipse, I arrived, desiring to seize the sun. But then another, Rahu, having approached, suddenly seized the sun.

shloka_text: स राहोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा वासवः सम्भ्रमान्वितः । उत्पपातासनं हित्वा चोद्वहन्काञ्चनीं स्रजम् ।। 7.35.36 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rahu's words, Vasava, filled with agitation, rose up, abandoning his seat and bearing his golden garland.

shloka_text: ततः कैलासकूटाभं चतुर्दन्तं मदस्रवम् । शृङ्गारधारिणं प्रांशुं स्वर्णघण्टाट्टहासिनम् ।। 7.35.37 ।।
explanation: Then, resembling the peak of Kailasa, with four tusks, exuding ichor, bearing adornments, tall, and whose golden bells resounded like loud laughter.

shloka_text: इन्द्रः करीन्द्रमारुह्य राहुं कृत्वा पुरःसरम् । प्रायाद्यत्राभवत्सूर्यः सहानेन हनूमता ।। 7.35.38 ।।
explanation: Indra, having mounted the lord of elephants and making Rahu his vanguard, went to where the Sun was, accompanied by Hanuman.

shloka_text: अथातिरभसेनागाद्राहुरुत्सृज्य वासवम् । अनेन च स वै दृष्टः प्रधावञ्छैलकूटवत् ।। 7.35.39 ।।
explanation: Then Rahu, having abandoned Vasava, went with great speed. And he was indeed seen by him, running like a mountain peak.

shloka_text: ततः सूर्यं समुत्सृज्य राहुं फलमवेक्ष्य च । उत्पपात पुनर्व्योम ग्रहीतुं सिंहिकासुतम् ।। 7.35.40 ।।
explanation: Then, having abandoned the sun and having perceived Rahu as a fruit, he flew up into the sky again to seize the son of Simhika.

shloka_text: उत्सृज्यार्कमिमं राम प्रधावन्तं प्लवङ्गमम् । अवेक्ष्यैवं परावृत्त्य मुखशेषः पराङ्मुखः ।। 7.35.41 ।।
explanation: O Rama, having abandoned this sun, and having seen this monkey rushing forth, Rahu, with only his face remaining, turned away.

shloka_text: इन्द्रमाशंसमानस्तु त्रातारं सिंहिकासुतः । इन्द्र इन्द्रेति संत्रासान्मुहुर्महुरभाषत ।। 7.35.42 ।।
explanation: Simhika's son, appealing to Indra as his protector, repeatedly cried out 'Indra! Indra!' in terror.

shloka_text: राहोर्विक्रोशमानस्य प्रागेवालक्षितं स्वरम् । श्रुत्वेन्द्रोवाच मा भैषीरहमेनं निषूदये ।। 7.35.43 ।।
explanation: Having heard the previously unperceived sound of Rahu crying out, Indra said, "Do not fear. I will kill him."

shloka_text: ऐरावतं ततो दृष्ट्वा महत्तदिदमित्यपि । फलं मत्वा हस्तिराजमभिदुद्राव मारुतिः ।। 7.35.44 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen Airavata, and thinking, "This is a great fruit," Maruti rushed towards the king of elephants.

shloka_text: तथास्य धावतो रूपमैरावतजिघृक्षया । मुहूर्तमभवद्घोरमिन्द्राग्न्योरिव भास्वरम् ।। 7.35.45 ।।
explanation: Thus, his form, as he ran with the desire to seize Airavata, became terrible and radiant for a moment, like that of Indra and Agni.

shloka_text: एवमाधावमानं तु नातिक्रुद्धः शचीपतिः । हस्तान्तादतिमुक्तेन कुलिशेनाभ्यताडयत् ।। 7.35.46 ।।
explanation: As he was thus rushing, the lord of Sachi, not excessively angry, struck him with the thunderbolt released from his hand.

shloka_text: ततो गिरौ पपातैष इन्द्रवज्राभिताडितः । पतमानस्य चैतस्य वामो हनुरभज्यत ।। 7.35.47 ।।
explanation: Then, struck by Indra's thunderbolt, he fell upon the mountain. And as he was falling, his left jaw was broken.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तु पतिते बाले वज्रताडनविह्वले । चुक्रोधेन्द्राय पवनः प्रजानामहिताय सः ।। 7.35.48 ।।
explanation: When that child, distressed by the blow of the thunderbolt, had fallen, Pavan became angry at Indra, for the harm of the creatures.

shloka_text: प्रचारं स तु सङ्गृह्य प्रजास्वन्तर्गतः प्रभुः । गुहां प्रविष्टः स्वसुतं शिशुमादाय मारुतः ।। 7.35.49 ।।
explanation: But that lord Marut, having gathered intelligence among the people, went inside. Taking his infant son, he entered a cave.

shloka_text: विण्मूत्राशयमावृत्य प्रजानां परमार्तिकृत् । रुरोध सर्वभूतानि यथा वर्षाणि वासवः ।। 7.35.50 ।।
explanation: Covering the receptacles of feces and urine, causing great distress to creatures, it obstructed all beings, just as Vasava (Indra) obstructs the rains.

shloka_text: वायुप्रकोपाद्भूतानि निरुच्छ्वासानि सर्वतः । सन्धिभिर्भिद्यमानैश्च काष्ठभूतानि जज्ञिरे ।। 7.35.51 ।।
explanation: Due to the fury of the wind, beings everywhere became breathless. And with their joints being broken, they turned into wood.

shloka_text: निःस्वाध्यायवषट्कारं निष्क्रियं धर्मवर्जितम् । वायुप्रकोपात्ऺत्रैलोक्यं निरयस्थमिवाभवत् ।। 7.35.52 ।।
explanation: Without Vedic study and sacrificial offerings, inactive, and devoid of righteousness, the three worlds, due to the fury of the wind, became as if they were in hell.

shloka_text: ततः प्रजाः सगन्धर्वाः सदेवासुरमानुषाः । प्रजापतिं समाधावन्दुःखिताश्च सुखेच्छया ।। 7.35.53 ।।
explanation: Then, the creatures, along with Gandharvas, Devas, Asuras, and humans, being distressed and desiring happiness, rushed to Prajapati.

shloka_text: ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा महोदरनिभोदराः । त्वया नु भगवन्सृष्टाः प्रजानाथ चतुर्विधाः ।। 7.35.54 ।।
explanation: The gods, with folded hands, whose bellies resembled large pots, said: "O Lord, O Lord of creatures, indeed, the four types of beings were created by you."

shloka_text: त्वया दत्तो ऽयमस्माकमायुषः पवनः पतिः । सो ऽस्मान्प्राणेश्वरो भूत्वा कस्मादेषो ऽद्य सत्तम ।। 7.35.55 ।।
explanation: This breath, the lord of our life, was given to us by you. Having become the master of our life, why is this one today, O best among the good?

shloka_text: रुरोध दुःखं जनयन्नन्तःपुर इव स्त्रियः । तस्मात्त्वां शरणं प्राप्ता वायुनोहता वयम् ।। 7.35.56 ।।
explanation: He confined (us), causing sorrow, like women in the inner chambers. Therefore, we, afflicted by the wind, have sought refuge in you.

shloka_text: एतत्प्रजानां श्रुत्वा तु प्रजानाथः प्रजापतिः । कारणादिति चोक्त्वासौ प्रजाः पुनरभाषत ।। 7.35.57 ।।
explanation: Having heard this from the subjects, Prajapati, the lord of the subjects, then said, "This is the reason," and spoke to the subjects again.

shloka_text: यस्मिंश्च कारणे वायुश्चुक्रोध च रुरोध च । प्रजाः शृणुध्वं तत्सर्वं श्रोतव्यं चात्मनः क्षमम् ।। 7.35.58 ।।
explanation: And for what reason Vayu became angry and obstructed, O people, listen to all that, which is worthy of hearing and beneficial for yourselves.

shloka_text: पुत्रस्तस्यामरेशेन इन्द्रेणाद्य निपातितः । राहोर्वचनमास्थाय ततः स कुपितो ऽनिलः ।। 7.35.59 ।।
explanation: His son was killed today by Indra, the lord of the immortals. Having followed Rahu's words, Vayu then became enraged.

shloka_text: अशरीरः शरीरेषु वायुश्चरति पालयन् । शरीरं हि विना वायुं समतां याति दारुभिः ।। 7.35.60 ।।
explanation: The bodiless Vayu moves within bodies, sustaining them. For a body without Vayu surely attains the state of logs.

shloka_text: वायुः प्राणः सुखं वायुर्वायुः सर्वमिदं जगत् । वायुना सम्परित्यक्तं न सुखं विन्दते जगत् ।। 7.35.61 ।।
explanation: Vayu is life-breath, Vayu is happiness, Vayu is this entire world. The world, abandoned by Vayu, does not find happiness.

shloka_text: अद्यैव च परित्यक्तं वायुना जगदायुषा । अद्यैव ते निरुच्छ्वासाः काष्ठकुड्योपमाः स्थिताः ।। 7.35.62 ।।
explanation: And just today, they have been abandoned by the breath, the life of the world. Just today, they are breathless, remaining like wooden walls.

shloka_text: तद्यामस्तत्र यत्रास्ते मारुतो रुक्प्रदो हि नः । मा विनाशं गमिष्याम अप्रसाद्यादितेः सुताः ।। 7.35.63 ।।
explanation: Therefore, let us go there where Maruta, who indeed causes us suffering, resides. Lest we perish without propitiating the sons of Aditi.

shloka_text: ततः प्रजाभिः सहितः प्रजापतिः सदेवगन्धर्वभुजङ्गगुह्यकैः । जगाम तत्रास्यति यत्र मारुतः सुतं सुरेन्द्राभिहतं प्रगृह्य सः ।। 7.35.64 ।।
explanation: Then Prajapati, accompanied by the creatures, along with the gods, Gandharvas, serpents, and Guhyakas, went to that place where Maruta, having taken his son struck by the lord of gods, was casting him down

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्कवैश्वानरकाञ्चनप्रभं सुतं तदोत्सङ्गगतं सदागतेः । चतुर्मुखो वीक्ष्य कृपामथाकरोत्सदेवगन्धर्वर्षियक्षराक्षसैः ।। 7.35.65 ।।
explanation: Then, the four-faced one, having seen the son of Vayu, who was then seated on his lap and shone with the splendor of the sun, fire, and gold, then showed compassion, along with the gods, gandharvas, sages, yakshas, and rakshasas.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पंचत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 35 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, ends the thirty-fifth chapter.

shloka_text: ततः पितामहं दृष्ट्वा वायुः पुत्रवधार्दितः । शिशुकं तं समादाय उत्तस्थौ धातुरग्रतः ।। 7.36.1 ।।
explanation: Then, Vayu, afflicted by the death of his son, having seen the grandfather, picked up that child and rose before the Creator.

shloka_text: चलकुण्डलमौलिस्रक्तपनीयविभूषणः । पादयोर्न्यपतद्वायुस्तिस्रोपस्थाय वेधसे ।। 7.36.2 ।।
explanation: Vayu, having approached Brahma, who was adorned with swaying earrings, a crown, a garland, and golden ornaments, fell down at his feet.

shloka_text: तं तु वेदविदा तेन लम्बाभरणशोभिना । वायुमुत्थाप्य हस्तेन शिशुं तं परिमृष्टवान् ।। 7.36.3 ।।
explanation: But that knower of the Vedas, adorned with long ornaments, having raised the vital breath with his hand, stroked that child.

shloka_text: स्पृष्टमात्रस्ततः सो ऽथ सलीलं पद्मयोनिना । जलसिक्तं यथा सस्यं पुनर्जीवितमाप्तवान् ।। 7.36.4 ।।
explanation: Then, as soon as he was playfully touched by the lotus-born (Brahma), he regained life, just like a plant that has been watered.

shloka_text: प्राणवन्तमिमं दृष्ट्वा प्राणो गन्धवहो मुदा । चचार सर्वभूतेषु सन्निरुद्धं यथा पुरा ।। 7.36.5 ।।
explanation: Having seen this living being, Prana, the carrier of fragrance, joyfully moved among all creatures, just as it was formerly restrained.

shloka_text: मरुद्रोधाद्विनिर्मुक्तास्ताः प्रजा मुदिता ऽभवन् । शीतदाहविनिर्मुक्ताः पद्मिन्य इव साम्बुजाः ।। 7.36.6 ।।
explanation: Those people, freed from the obstruction of the wind, became joyful, just like lotus plants with their blossoms, freed from the extremes of cold and heat.

shloka_text: ततस्त्रियुग्मस्त्रिककुत्ऺित्रधामा त्रिदशार्चितः । उवाच देवता ब्रह्मा मारुतप्रियकाम्यया ।। 7.36.7 ।।
explanation: Then Brahma, who is associated with the three ages, who has three prominent aspects, who presides over the three realms, and who is worshipped by the gods, spoke to the deities, desiring to please Maruta.

shloka_text: भो महेन्द्रेशवरुणप्रजेश्वरधनेश्वराः । जानतामपि वः सर्वं वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां हितम् ।। 7.36.8 ।।
explanation: O Mahendra, Ishvara, Varuna, Prajeshvara, and Dhaneshvara! Even though you know everything, I will tell you what is beneficial; listen to it.

shloka_text: अनेन शिशुना कार्यं कर्तव्यं वो भविष्यति । तद्वदध्वं वरान्सर्वे मारुतस्यास्य तुष्टये ।। 7.36.9 ।।
explanation: A task will be accomplished for you by this child. Therefore, all of you, declare boons for the satisfaction of this Maruta.

shloka_text: ततः सहस्रनयनः प्रीतियुक्तः शुभाननः । कुशेशयमयीं मालामुत्क्षिप्येदं वचो ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.36.10 ।।
explanation: Then, the thousand-eyed one, filled with joy, with an auspicious face, lifting up a lotus garland, spoke these words.

shloka_text: मत्करोत्सृष्टवज्रेण हनुरस्य यथा हतः । नाम्ना वै कपिशार्दूलो भविता हनुमानिति ।। 7.36.11 ।।
explanation: Just as his jaw was struck by the thunderbolt released from my hand, so indeed, the foremost among monkeys will be known by the name Hanuman.

shloka_text: अहमस्य प्रदास्यामि परमं वरमद्भुतम् । इतः प्रभृति वज्रस्य ममावध्यो भविष्यति ।। 7.36.12 ।।
explanation: I will grant him a supreme and wonderful boon. From this moment onwards, he will be invulnerable to the thunderbolt and to me.

shloka_text: मार्तण्डस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र भगवांस्तिमिरापहः । तेजसो ऽस्य मदीयस्य ददामि शतिकां कलाम् ।। 7.36.13 ।।
explanation: Then the venerable Mārtaṇḍa, the dispeller of darkness, spoke there: "I give a hundredth part of my own splendor to him."

shloka_text: यदा तु शास्त्राण्यध्येतुं शक्तिरस्य भविष्यति । तदास्य शास्त्रं दास्यामि येन वाग्ग्मी भविष्यति ।। 7.36.14 ।।
explanation: When he will have the ability to study the scriptures, then I will give him the scripture by which he will become eloquent.

shloka_text: नचास्य भविता कश्चित्सदृशः शास्त्रदर्शने । वरुणश्च वरं प्रादान्नास्य मृत्युर्भविष्यति । वर्षायुतशतेनापि मत्पाशादुदकादपि ।। 7.36.15 ।।
explanation: And there will be no one equal to him in the knowledge of scriptures. And Varuna gave a boon: "Death will not befall him, even for a million years, nor from my noose, nor from water."

shloka_text: यमो दण्डादवध्यत्वमरोगत्वं च नित्यशः । वरं ददामि सन्तुष्ट अविषादं च संयुगे ।। 7.36.16 ।।
explanation: Pleased, I grant this boon: invulnerability to Yama's mace, perpetual freedom from disease, and freedom from dejection in battle.

shloka_text: गदेयं मामिका नैनं संयुगेषु वधिष्यति । इत्येवं वरदः प्राह तदा ह्येकाक्षिपिङ्गलः ।। 7.36.17 ।।
explanation: This mace of mine will not kill him in battles. Thus, the boon-giver, the one-eyed tawny (deity), then said.

shloka_text: मत्तो मदायुधानां च न वध्यो ऽयं भविष्यति । इत्येवं शङ्करेणापि दत्तो ऽस्य परमो वरः ।। 7.36.18 ।।
explanation: He will not be slain by me or by my weapons. Thus, even by Shankara, this supreme boon was granted to him.

shloka_text: सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्यो ऽयं भविष्यति । दीर्घायुश्च महात्मा च इति ब्रह्माब्रवीद्वचः ।। 7.36.19 ।।
explanation: He will be invincible to all divine curses, long-lived, and a great soul. Thus spoke Brahma.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मा च दृष्ट्वैनं बालसूर्योपमं शिशुम् । शिल्पिनां प्रवरः प्रादाद्वरमस्य महामतिः ।। 7.36.20 ।।
explanation: And Vishwakarma, the great-minded and foremost among artisans, having seen this child resembling the rising sun, bestowed a boon upon him.

shloka_text: मत्कृतानि च शस्त्राणि यानि दिव्यानि संयुगे । तैरवध्यत्वमापन्नश्चिरजीवी भविष्यति ।। 7.36.21 ।।
explanation: And by those divine weapons made by me, which are used in combat, he will attain invincibility and become long-lived.

shloka_text: ततः सुराणां तु वरैर्दृष्ट्वा ह्येनमलङ्कृतम् । चतुर्मुखस्तुष्टमना वायुमाह जगद्गुरुः ।। 7.36.22 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen him adorned by the excellent gifts of the gods, the four-faced one, the preceptor of the world, with a pleased mind, spoke to Vayu.

shloka_text: अमित्राणां भयकरो मित्राणामभयङ्करः । अजेयो भविता पुत्रस्तव मारुत मारुतिः ।। 7.36.23 ।।
explanation: O Maruta, your son Maruti will be a terror to enemies, a giver of fearlessness to friends, and unconquerable.

shloka_text: कामरूपः कामचारी कामगः प्लवतां वरः । भवत्यव्याहतगतिः कीर्तिमांश्च भविष्यति ।। 7.36.24 ।।
explanation: Assuming any form at will, moving at will, going anywhere at will, the best among the swift, he will have unobstructed movement and will be glorious.

shloka_text: रावणोत्सादनार्थानि रामप्रियकरणि च । रोमहर्षकराण्येष कर्ता कर्माणि संयुगे ।। 7.36.25 ।।
explanation: He will perform deeds in battle that are for the destruction of Ravana, pleasing to Rama, and hair-raising.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तमामन्त्र्य मारुतं त्वमरैः सह । यथागतं ययुः सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमाः ।। 7.36.26 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken, and having addressed her and Maruta along with the gods, all of them, led by the Grandfather (Brahma), departed as they had come.

shloka_text: सो ऽपि गन्धवहः पुत्रं प्रगृह्य गृहमानयत् । अञ्जनायास्तमाचख्यौ वरदत्तं विनिर्गतः ।। 7.36.27 ।।
explanation: He, the wind god, having taken the son, brought him home. He announced him to Anjana as one born from a boon.

shloka_text: प्राप्य राम वरानेष वरदानसमन्वितः । बलेनात्मनि संस्थेन सो ऽपूर्यत यथा ऽर्णवः ।। 7.36.28 ।।
explanation: O Rama, this one, having obtained boons and being endowed with the granting of boons, was filled with the strength residing within himself, just like the ocean.

shloka_text: तरसा पूर्यमाणो ऽपि तदा वानरपुङ्गवः । आश्रमेषु महर्षीणामपराध्यति निर्भयः ।। 7.36.29 ।।
explanation: Even though filled with might at that time, the monkey chief, fearless, commits offenses in the hermitages of the great sages.

shloka_text: स्रुग्भाण्डान्यग्निहोत्रं च वल्कलाजिनसञ्चयान् । भग्नविच्छिन्नविध्वस्तान्संशान्तानां करोत्ययम् ।। 7.36.30 ।।
explanation: This one makes the sacrificial ladles and vessels, the sacred fire, and the collections of bark garments and deer skins of those who have become peaceful, broken, torn, and destroyed.

shloka_text: एवंविधानि कर्माणि प्रावर्तत महाबलः । सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्यः शम्भुना कृतः ।। 7.36.31 ।।
explanation: The mighty one performed such deeds; he was made invulnerable by Shambhu to all curses of Brahmins.

shloka_text: जानन्त ऋषयस्तं वै सहन्ते तस्य शक्तितः ।। 7.36.32 ।।
explanation: The sages, knowing him, indeed endure (it) by his power.

shloka_text: यथा केसरिणा त्वेष वायुना सो ऽञ्जनासुतः । प्रतिषिद्धो ऽपि मर्यादां लङ्घयत्येव वानरः ।। 7.36.33 ।।
explanation: Just as this monkey, the son of Anjana, even though restrained by Kesari and Vayu, certainly transgresses the boundary.

shloka_text: ततो महर्षयः क्रुद्धा भृग्वङ्गिरसवंशजाः । शेपुरेनं रघुश्रेष्ठ नातिक्रुद्धातिमन्यवः ।। 7.36.34 ।।
explanation: Then, O best of the Raghus, the great sages, descendants of Bhrigu and Angiras, though not excessively angry, but greatly indignant, cursed him.

shloka_text: बाधसे यत्समाश्रित्य बलमस्मान्प्लवङ्गम । तद्दीर्घकालं वेत्तासि नास्माकं शापमोहितः । यदा ते स्मार्यते कीर्तिस्तदा ते वर्धते बलम् ।। 7.36.35 ।।
explanation: O monkey, because you torment us relying on your strength, you will know (the effect of this) for a long time, being deluded by our curse. When your prowess is remembered, then your strength increases.

shloka_text: ततस्स हृततेजौजा महर्षिवचनौजसा । एषोश्रमाणि तान्येव मृदुभावं गतो ऽचरत् ।। 7.36.36 ।।
explanation: Then he, whose brilliance and power were diminished by the power of the great sage's words, having become gentle, wandered in those very hermitages.

shloka_text: अथर्क्षरजसो नाम वालिसुग्रीवयोः पिता । सर्ववानरराजा ऽ ऽसीत्तेजसा भास्करप्रभः ।। 7.36.37 ।।
explanation: Then, Riksharajas by name, the father of Vali and Sugriva, was the king of all monkeys, shining with the splendor of the sun.

shloka_text: स तु राज्यं चिरं कृत्वा वानराणां हरीश्वरः । स च ऋक्षरजा नाम कालधर्मेण सङ्गतः ।। 7.36.38 ।।
explanation: That lord of monkeys, having ruled the kingdom of the monkeys for a long time, and he, named Riksharaja, succumbed to the law of time.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नस्तमिते चाथ मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रकोविदैः । पित्र्ये पदे कृतो वाली सुग्रीवो वालिनः पदे ।। 7.36.39 ।।
explanation: And when he had passed away, then by the ministers skilled in counsel, Vali was placed on the paternal throne, and Sugriva in Vali's position.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेण समं त्वस्य अद्वैधं छिद्रवर्जितम् । आबाल्यं सख्यमभवदनिलस्याग्निना यथा ।। 7.36.40 ।।
explanation: His friendship with Sugriva was undivided and flawless from childhood, just like the friendship of wind with fire.

shloka_text: एष शापवशादेव न वेद बलमात्मनः । वालिसुग्रीवयोर्वैरं यदा राम समुत्थितम् ।। 7.36.41 ।।
explanation: He, by the power of a curse, does not know his own strength. O Rama, when the enmity between Vali and Sugriva arose.

shloka_text: न ह्येष राम सुग्रीवो भ्राम्यमाणो ऽपि वालिना ।। 7.36.42 ।।
explanation: Indeed, O Rama, this Sugriva, even though being whirled around by Vali...

shloka_text: देव जानाति न ह्येष बलमात्मनि मारुतिः । ऋषिशापाहृतबलस्तदैष कपिसत्तमः ।। 7.36.43 ।।
explanation: O divine one, this son of Marut (Hanuman) indeed does not know the strength within himself. This best of monkeys was then deprived of his strength by a sage's curse.

shloka_text: सिंहः कुञ्जररुद्धो वा आस्थितः सहितो रणे ।। 7.36.44 ।।
explanation: A lion, either obstructed by an elephant, or standing united in battle.

shloka_text: पराक्रमोत्साहमतिप्रतापसौशील्यमाधुर्यनयानयैश्च । गाम्भीर्यचातुर्यसुवीर्यधैर्यैर्हनूमतः को ऽभ्यधिको ऽस्ति लोके ।। 7.36.45 ।।
explanation: Who in the world is superior to Hanuman in valor, enthusiasm, intelligence, majesty, good conduct, sweetness, skill in policy and strategy, profundity, cleverness, great prowess, and fortitude?

shloka_text: असौ पुनर्व्याकरणं ग्रहीष्यन्सूर्योन्मुखः प्रष्टुमना कपीन्द्रः । उद्यद्गिरेरस्तगिरिं जगाम ग्रन्थं महद्धारयनप्रमेयः ।। 7.36.46 ।।
explanation: This immeasurable lord of monkeys, again intending to learn grammar, facing the sun and desirous of asking, went from the rising mountain to the setting mountain, bearing the great treatise.

shloka_text: ससूत्रवृत्त्यर्थपदं महार्थं ससङ्ग्रहं साद्ध्यति वै कपीन्द्रः । नह्यस्य कश्चित्सदृशो ऽस्ति शास्त्रे वैशारदे च्छन्दगतौ तथैव ।। 7.36.47 ।।
explanation: The chief of monkeys indeed expounds [speech] with aphorisms, commentaries, profound meanings, and precise words, all presented concisely. There is certainly no one equal to him in scriptural knowledge, in expertise, and similarly in the understanding of prosody.

shloka_text: सर्वासु विद्यासु तपोविधाने प्रस्पर्धते ऽयो हि गुरुं सुराणाम् । सो ऽयं नवव्याकरणार्थवेत्ता ब्रह्मा भविष्यत्यपि ते प्रसादात् ।। 7.36.48 ।।
explanation: In all sciences and in the practice of austerities, this one indeed rivals the preceptor of the gods. This very one, a knower of the meaning of the nine grammars, will even become Brahma by your grace.

shloka_text: प्रवीविवक्षोरिव सागरस्य लोकान्दिधक्षोरिव पावकस्ययुगक्षये ह्येव यथान्तकस्य हनूमतः स्थास्यति कः पुरस्तात् ।। 7.36.49 ।।
explanation: Who will stand before Hanuman, who is like the ocean wishing to swallow completely, like fire wishing to burn the worlds, and indeed like Antaka (the god of death) at the end of a cosmic age?

shloka_text: एषेव चान्ये च महाकपीन्द्राः सुग्रीवमैन्दद्विविदाः सनीलाः । सतारतारेयनलाः सरम्भास्त्वत्कारणाद्राम सुरैर्हि सृष्टाः ।। 7.36.50 ।।
explanation: These and other great monkey chiefs—Sugriva, Mainda, Dvivida, Nila, Tara, Tareya, Nala, and Rambha—O Rama, were indeed created by the gods for your sake.

shloka_text: तदेत्कथितं सर्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि । हनूमतो बालभावे कर्मैतत्कथितं मया ।। 7.36.51 ।।
explanation: All this that you asked me has been told. This deed of Hanuman in his childhood has been narrated by me.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा ऽगस्त्यस्य कथितं रामः सौमित्रिरेव च । विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्वानरा राक्षसैः सह ।। 7.36.52 ।।
explanation: Having heard what Agastya had narrated, Rama and Lakshmana, along with the monkeys and rakshasas, experienced great wonder.

shloka_text: अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीद्रामं सर्वमेतछ्रुतं त्वया । दृष्टः सम्भाषितश्चासि राम गच्छामहे वयम् ।। 7.36.53 ।।
explanation: Agastya said to Rama: "You have heard all this. You have been seen and spoken to, O Rama. We are departing."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैतद्राघवो वाक्यमगस्त्यस्योग्रतेजसः । प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतश्चापि महर्षिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.36.54 ।।
explanation: Having heard these words of Agastya, the one of fierce splendor, Rama, with folded hands and bowing down, spoke this to the great sage.

shloka_text: अद्य मे देवता हृष्टाः पितरः प्रपितामहाः । युष्माकं दर्शनादेव नित्यं तुष्टाः सबान्धवाः ।। 7.36.55 ।।
explanation: Today my deities are pleased. My ancestors, great-grandfathers, and all my kinsmen are always satisfied merely by your sight.

shloka_text: विज्ञाप्यं तु ममैतद्धि यद्वदाम्यागतस्पृहः । तद्भवद्भिर्मम कृते कर्तव्यमनुकम्पया ।। 7.36.56 ।।
explanation: This indeed is my request, which I speak with longing. Therefore, that should be done by you for my sake, out of compassion.

shloka_text: पौरजानपदान्स्थाप्य स्वकार्येष्वहमागतः । क्रतूनेव करिष्यामि प्रभावाद्भवतां सताम् ।। 7.36.57 ।।
explanation: Having settled the citizens and country folk in their respective duties, I have come. I shall indeed perform sacrifices by the power of you, the virtuous.

shloka_text: सदस्या मम यज्ञेषु भवन्तो नित्यमेव तत् । भविष्यथ महावीर्या ममानुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः ।। 7.36.58 ।।
explanation: You, the participants in my sacrifices, will always indeed be very powerful, desiring my favor.

shloka_text: अहं युष्मान्समाश्रित्य तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् । अनुग्रहीतः पितृभिर्भविष्यामि सुनिर्वृतः ।। 7.36.59 ।।
explanation: By relying on you, whose sins have been purified by penance, I shall be blessed by my ancestors and become greatly content.

shloka_text: तदागन्तव्यमनिशं भवद्भिरिह सङ्गतैः । अगस्त्याद्यास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषयः संशितव्रताः ।। 7.36.60 ।।
explanation: Then you, assembled here, should constantly come. But Agastya and other sages of firm vows, having heard that...

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रयातुमुपचक्रमुः ।। 7.36.61 ।।
explanation: Having said to him, "So be it," they began to depart.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा गताः सर्वे ऋषयस्ते यथागतम् । राघवश्च तमेवार्थं चिन्तयामास विस्मितः ।। 7.36.62 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, all those sages departed the way they had come. And Rama, astonished, pondered over that very matter.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्तं भास्करे याते विसृज्य नृपवानरान् । सन्ध्यामुपास्य विधिवत्तदा नरवरोत्तमः । प्रवृत्तायां रजन्यां तु सो ऽन्तःपुरचरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.36.63 ।।
explanation: Then, when the sun had set, having dismissed the king and the monkeys, and having duly performed the evening prayer, that best among men, as night began, entered the inner apartments.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 36 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु काकुत्स्थे धर्मेण विदितात्मनि । व्यतीता या निशा पूर्वा पौराणां हर्षवर्धिनी ।। 7.37.1 ।।
explanation: When Kakutstha, the self-realized one, was consecrated according to dharma, the previous night, which had increased the joy of the citizens, passed.

shloka_text: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां प्रातर्नृपतिबोधकाः । वन्दिनः समुपातिष्ठन्सौम्या नृपतिवेश्मनि ।। 7.37.2 ।।
explanation: When that night had dawned, in the morning, the gentle bards, who awaken the king, assembled in the king's palace.

shloka_text: ते रक्तकण्ठिनः सर्वे किन्नरा इव शिक्षिताः । तुष्टुवुर्नपतिं वीरं यथावत् सम्प्रहर्षिणः ।। 7.37.3 ।।
explanation: All of them, with melodious voices, trained like Kinnaras, greatly delighted, praised the heroic king appropriately.

shloka_text: वीर सौम्य प्रबुध्यस्व कौसल्याप्रीतिवर्धन । जगद्धि सर्वं स्वपिति त्वयि सुप्ते नराधिप ।। 7.37.4 ।।
explanation: O Hero, O Gentle one, awaken, O augmenter of Kausalya's joy. For indeed, the entire world sleeps when you, O King, are asleep.

shloka_text: विक्रमस्ते यथा विष्णो रूपं चैवाश्विनोरिव । बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यः प्रजापतिसमो ह्यसि ।। 7.37.5 ।।
explanation: Your valor is like Vishnu's, and your form is indeed like that of the Ashvins. You are equal to Brihaspati in intellect, and you are certainly like Prajapati.

shloka_text: क्षमा ते पृथिवीतुल्या तेजसा भास्करोपमः । वेगस्ते वायुना तुल्यो गाम्भीर्यमुदधेरिव ।। 7.37.6 ।।
explanation: Your patience is like the earth, your splendor is like the sun. Your speed is equal to the wind, and your profundity is like that of the ocean.

shloka_text: अप्रकम्प्यो यता स्थाणुश्चन्द्रे सौम्यत्वमीदृशम् । नेदृशाः पार्थिवाः पूर्वं भवितारो नराधिप ।। 7.37.7 ।।
explanation: Unshakable like a pillar, such gentleness as in the moon. Not such kings were there before, nor will there be, O king.

shloka_text: यथा त्वमतिदुर्धर्षो धर्मनित्यः प्रजाहितः । न त्वां जहाति कीर्तिश्च लक्ष्मीश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.37.8 ।।
explanation: As you are extremely formidable, ever-righteous, and devoted to the welfare of the people, fame and prosperity will not abandon you, O best among men.

shloka_text: श्रीश्च धर्मश्च काकुत्स्थ त्वयि नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितौ । एताश्चान्याश्च मधुरा वन्दिभिः परिकीर्तिताः ।। 7.37.9 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, Śrī (prosperity/glory) and Dharma (righteousness) are always established in you. These and other sweet words are proclaimed by the bards.

shloka_text: सूताश्च संस्तवैर्दिव्यैर्बोधयन्ति स्म राघवम् । स्तुतिभिः स्तूयमानाभिः प्रत्यबुध्यत राघवः ।। 7.37.10 ।।
explanation: And the bards, with divine praises, awakened Rama. Rama awoke to the praises being sung.

shloka_text: स तद्विहाय शयनं पाण्डराच्छादनास्तृतम् । उत्तस्थौ नागशयनाद्धरिर्नारायणो यथा ।। 7.37.11 ।।
explanation: He, abandoning that bed spread with white coverings, rose up, just as Hari Narayana rises from his serpent-bed.

shloka_text: तमुत्थितं महात्मानं प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो नराः । सलिलं भाजनैः शुभ्रैरुपतस्थुः सहस्रशः ।। 7.37.12 ।।
explanation: Thousands of men, humble and with folded hands, approached that great soul who had risen, offering water in pure vessels.

shloka_text: कृतोदकशुचिर्भूत्वा काले हुतहुताशनः । देवागारं जगामाशु पुण्यमिक्ष्वाकुसेवितम् ।। 7.37.13 ।।
explanation: Having purified himself with water and having offered oblations into the fire at the proper time, he quickly went to the sacred temple, which was frequented by the Ikshvakus.

shloka_text: तत्र देवान्पितऽन्विप्रानर्चयित्वा यथाविधि । बाह्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम जनैर्वृतः ।। 7.37.14 ।।
explanation: Then, having worshipped the gods, ancestors, and Brahmins according to the prescribed rites, Rama, surrounded by people, departed to the outer chamber.

shloka_text: उपतस्थुर्महात्मानो मन्त्रिणः सपुरोहिताः । वसिष्ठप्रमुखाः सर्वे दीप्यमाना इवाग्नयः ।। 7.37.15 ।।
explanation: All the great-souled ministers, accompanied by their priests and headed by Vasishtha, approached, shining like fires.

shloka_text: क्षत्रियाश्च महात्मानो नानाजनपदेश्वराः । रामस्योपाविशन्पार्श्वे शक्रस्येव यथा ऽमराः ।। 7.37.16 ।।
explanation: And great-souled Kshatriyas, lords of various countries, sat by Rama's side, just as the gods sit by Indra.

shloka_text: भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चात्र शत्रुघ्नश्च महायशाः । उपासाञ्चक्रिरे हृष्टा वेदास्त्रय इवाध्वरम् ।। 7.37.17 ।।
explanation: Bharata, Lakshmana, and the greatly renowned Shatrughna, delighted, attended, just as the three Vedas attend a sacrifice.

shloka_text: याताः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा किङ्करा मुदिताननाः । मुदिता नाम पार्श्वस्था बहवः समुपाविशन् ।। 7.37.18 ।।
explanation: The servants, with folded hands and joyful faces, went. Many joyful ones nearby sat down.

shloka_text: वानराश्च महावीर्या विंशतिः कामरूपिणः । सुग्रीवप्रमुखा राममुपासन्ते महौजसः ।। 7.37.19 ।।
explanation: And twenty greatly valorous monkeys, who can assume any form at will, led by Sugriva, and possessing great might, attend upon Rama.

shloka_text: विभीषणश्च रक्षोभिश्चतुर्भिः परिवारितः । उपासते महात्मानं धनेशमिव गुह्यकाः ।। 7.37.20 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, surrounded by four Rakshasas, attends upon the great soul, just as the Guhyakas attend upon Kubera, the lord of wealth.

shloka_text: तथा निगमवृद्धाश्च कुलीना ये च मानवाः । शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः ।। 7.37.21 ।।
explanation: And similarly, the wise elders of the city and those noble men, having bowed their heads, attend upon the king.

shloka_text: तथा परिवृतो राजा श्रीमद्भिर्ऋषिभिर्वृतः । राजभिश्च महावीर्यैर्वानरैश्च सराक्षसैः ।। 7.37.22 ।।
explanation: Thus, the king was surrounded by glorious sages, by mighty kings, and by monkeys along with rakshasas.

shloka_text: यथा देवेश्वरो नित्यमृषिभिः समुपास्यते । अधिकस्तेन रूपेण सहस्राक्षाद्विरोचते ।। 7.37.23 ।।
explanation: Just as the lord of gods is always worshipped by sages, he shines more splendidly than the thousand-eyed one by that form.

shloka_text: तेषां समुपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः । कथ्यन्ते धर्मसंयुक्ताः पुराणज्ञैर्महात्मभिः ।। 7.37.24 ।।
explanation: To them, as they sat assembled, various very sweet stories, imbued with righteousness, are narrated by great souls who are experts in the Puranas.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 37 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Rāmāyaṇa, the first epic composed by Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमास्ते महाबाहुरहन्यहनि राघवः । प्रशासत्सर्वकार्याणि पौरजानपदेषु च ।। 7.38.1 ।।
explanation: Thus, the mighty-armed Rama remained day after day, administering all affairs for the citizens and the people of the countryside.

shloka_text: ततः कतिपयाहःसु वैदेहं मिथिलाधिपम् । राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.38.2 ।।
explanation: Then, after a few days, Rama, with folded hands, spoke this word to Vaideha, the king of Mithila.

shloka_text: भवान्हि गतिरव्यग्रा भवता पालिता वयम् । भवतस्तेजसोग्रेण रावणो निहतो मया ।। 7.38.3 ।।
explanation: You are indeed the unwavering refuge. We have been protected by you. By your fierce might, Ravana was killed by me.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकूणां च सर्वेषां मैथिलानां च सर्वशः । अतुलाः प्रीतयो राजन्सम्बन्धकपुरोगमाः ।। 7.38.4 ।।
explanation: O King, the incomparable affections of all the Ikshvakus and all the Maithilas were entirely based on their kinship.

shloka_text: तद्भवान्स्वपुरं यातु रत्नान्यादाय पार्थिव । भरतश्च सहायार्थं पृष्ठतस्ते ऽनुयास्यति ।। 7.38.5 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O King, you should go to your own city, taking the jewels. And Bharata will follow behind you for assistance.

shloka_text: स तथेति नृपः कृत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि भवतो राजन्दर्शनेन नयेन च ।। 7.38.6 ।।
explanation: The king, having said "So be it," spoke to Raghava: "O King, I am pleased by your sight and by your wisdom."

shloka_text: यान्येतानि तु रत्नानि मदर्थं सञ्चितानि वै । दुहित्रे तानि वै राजन्सर्वाण्येव ददामि च ।। 7.38.7 ।।
explanation: O King, these very jewels that have been collected for my sake, I give all of them to my daughter.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थं जनको हृष्टमानसः । प्रययौ मिथिलां श्रीमांस्तमनुज्ञाय राघवम् ।। 7.38.8 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Kakutstha, the glorious Janaka, with a joyful mind, having taken leave of Raghava, departed for Mithila.

shloka_text: ततः प्रयाते जनके केकयं मातुलं प्रभुः । राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.38.9 ।।
explanation: Then, when Janaka had departed for Kekaya, the maternal uncle's land, Lord Raghava, having folded his hands, spoke this word.

shloka_text: इदं राज्यमहं चैव भरतश्च सलक्ष्मणः । आयत्तास्त्वं हि नो राजन्गतिश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.38.10 ।।
explanation: This kingdom, I, and Bharata with Lakshmana, are dependent on you. Indeed, O King, you are our refuge, O best among men.

shloka_text: राजा हि वृद्धः सन्तापं त्वदर्थमुपयास्यति । तस्माद्गमनमद्यैव रोचते तव पार्थिव ।। 7.38.11 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the aged King will experience sorrow on your account. Therefore, O King, your departure today itself is agreeable to you.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनानुयात्रेण पृष्ठतो ऽनुगमिष्यते । धनमादाय विपुलं रत्नानि विविधानि च ।। 7.38.12 ।।
explanation: He will be followed from behind by Lakshmana, his attendant, carrying abundant wealth and various jewels.

shloka_text: युधाजित्तु तथेत्याह गमनं प्रति राघवम् । रत्नानि च धनं चैव त्वय्येवाक्षय्यमस्त्विति ।। 7.38.13 ।।
explanation: Yudhājit said to Rāghava concerning his departure, 'So be it. May jewels and wealth be inexhaustible for you.'

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणं स राजानं कृत्वा केकयवर्धनः । रामेण हि कृतः पूर्वमभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम् ।। 7.38.14 ।।
explanation:
हि कृतः पूर्वम् अभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम्" - Indeed, previously, circumambulation was performed by Rama after saluting.

This structure suggests that Bharata performed circumambulation to the king. And then it adds a detail about

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन सहायेन प्रयातः केकयेश्वरः । हते ऽसुरे यथा वृत्रे विष्णुना सह वासवः ।। 7.38.15 ।।
explanation: The lord of Kekaya proceeded with Lakṣmaṇa as his helper, just as Vāsava (Indra) did with Vishnu when the demon Vṛtra was slain.

shloka_text: तं विसृज्य ततो रामो वयस्यमकुतोभयम् । प्रतर्दनं काशिपतिं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.38.16 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, having dismissed that fearless friend, embraced Pratardana, the lord of Kashi, and spoke thus.

shloka_text: दर्शिता भवता प्रीतिर्दर्शितं सौहृदं परम् । उद्योगश्च कृतो राजन्भरतेन त्वया सह ।। 7.38.17 ।।
explanation: Affection has been shown by you, and supreme friendship displayed. And effort has been made, O King, by Bharata along with you.

shloka_text: तद्भवानद्य काशेय पुरीं वाराणसीं व्रज । रमणीयां त्वया गुप्तां सुप्रकाशां सुतोरणाम् ।। 7.38.18 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Kaśeya, you go today to the city of Varanasi, which is delightful, protected by you, well-illuminated, and adorned with beautiful gateways.

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वा चोत्थाय काकुत्स्थः परमासनात् । पर्यष्वजत धर्मात्मा निरन्तरमुरोगतम् ।। 7.38.19 ।।
explanation: Having said this much, and having risen from his excellent seat, the righteous Kakutstha embraced tightly the one who had come to his chest.

shloka_text: विसर्जयामास तदा कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः । राघवेणाभ्यनुज्ञातः काशीशो ऽप्यकुतोभयः । वाराणसीं ययौ तूर्णं राघवेण विसर्जितः ।। 7.38.20 ।।
explanation: Then, the one who increased Kaushalya's joy (Rama) sent him away. The king of Kashi, fearless, having been permitted and dismissed by Raghava, quickly went to Varanasi.

shloka_text: विसृज्य तं काशिपतिं त्रिशतं पृथिवीपतीन् । प्रहसन्राघवो वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम् ।। 7.38.21 ।।
explanation: Having dismissed the lord of Kashi and three hundred kings, Rama, smiling, spoke sweet words.

shloka_text: भवतां प्रीतिरव्यग्रा तेजसा परिरक्षिता । धर्मश्च नियतो नित्यं सत्यं च भवतां सदा ।। 7.38.22 ।।
explanation: May your unwavering affection be protected by splendor. And may your righteousness always be constant, and truth always be with you.

shloka_text: युष्माकं चानुभावेन तेजसा च महात्मनाम् । हतो दुरात्मा दुर्बुद्धी रावणो राक्षसाधमः ।। 7.38.23 ।।
explanation: By your power and by the might of the great souls, the evil-minded, wicked-minded Ravana, the vilest of demons, has been slain.

shloka_text: हेतुमात्रमहं तत्र भवतां तेजसा हतः । रावणः सगणो युद्धे सपुत्रामात्यबान्धवः ।। 7.38.24 ।।
explanation: I was merely an instrument there; by your power, Ravana was slain in battle, along with his retinue, sons, ministers, and kinsmen.

shloka_text: भवन्तश्च समानीता भरतेन महात्मना । श्रुत्वा जनकराजस्य काननात्तनयां हृताम् ।। 7.38.25 ।।
explanation: And you were brought together by the great-souled Bharata, having heard that the daughter of King Janaka was abducted from the forest.

shloka_text: उद्युक्तानां च सर्वेषां पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम् । कालो व्यतीतः सुमहान्गमनं रोचयाम्यतः ।। 7.38.26 ।।
explanation: A very long time has passed for all the great-souled kings who were ready. Therefore, I desire to depart.

shloka_text: प्रत्यूचुस्तं च राजानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । दिष्ट्यां त्वं विजयी राम स्वराज्ये ऽपि प्रतिष्ठितः ।। 7.38.27 ।।
explanation: And the kings, filled with great joy, replied to him: "Fortunately, O Rama, you are victorious and re-established in your own kingdom."

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या प्रत्याहृता सीता दिष्ट्या शत्रुः पराजितः । एष नः परमः काम एषा नः पीतिरुत्तमा ।। 7.38.28 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, Sita has been brought back, fortunately, the enemy has been defeated. This is our greatest desire, this is our supreme joy.

shloka_text: यत्त्वां विजयिनं राम पश्यामो हतशात्रवम् ।। 7.38.29 ।।
explanation: That we see you, O Rama, victorious, with your enemies slain.

shloka_text: एतत्त्वय्युपपन्नं च यदस्मांस्त्वं प्रशंससे । प्रशंसार्ह न जानीमः प्रशंसां वक्तुमीदृशीम् ।। 7.38.30 ।।
explanation: It is indeed fitting for you that you praise us. O worthy of praise, we do not know how to speak such praise.

shloka_text: आपृच्छामो गमिष्यामो हृदिस्थो नः सदा भवान् । वर्तामहे महाबाहो प्रीत्यात्र महता वृताः । भवेच्च ते महाराज प्रीतिरस्मासु नित्यदा ।। 7.38.31 ।।
explanation: We bid farewell, we shall depart. You will always be in our hearts. O mighty-armed one, we have lived here, surrounded by great affection. And may your love for us, O great king, be eternal.

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव राजानो हर्षेण परमान्विताः । उचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे राघवं गमनोत्सुकाः ।। 7.38.32 ।।
explanation: All the kings, overwhelmed with supreme joy, with folded hands, and eager for departure, said to Rama: 'Indeed!'

shloka_text: पूजिताश्चैव रामेण जग्मुर्देशान्स्वकान्स्वकान् ।। 7.38.33 ।।
explanation: And having been honored by Rama, they went to their own respective countries.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 38 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the thirty-eighth chapter.

shloka_text: ते प्रयाता महात्मानः पार्थिवास्ते प्रहृष्टवत् । गजवाजिसहस्रौघैः कम्पयन्तो वसुन्धराम् ।। 7.39.1 ।।
explanation: Those great-souled kings departed joyfully, shaking the earth with thousands of elephants and horses.

shloka_text: अक्षौहिण्यो हि तत्रासन्राघवार्थे समुद्यताः । भरतस्याज्ञया ऽनेकाः प्रहृष्टा बलवाहनाः ।। 7.39.2 ।।
explanation: Indeed, many Akṣauhiṇīs were present there, prepared for the sake of Raghava, by the command of Bharata, joyful with their forces and mounts.

shloka_text: ऊचुस्ते च महीपाला बलदर्पसमन्विताः । न रामरावणं युद्धे पश्यामः पुरतः स्थितम् ।। 7.39.3 ।।
explanation: And those kings, filled with the pride of strength, said: "We do not see Rama and Ravana standing before us in battle."

shloka_text: भरतेन वयं पश्चात्समानीता निरर्थकम् । हता हि राक्षसाः क्षिप्रं पार्थिवैः स्युर्न संशयः ।। 7.39.4 ।।
explanation: We were brought by Bharata later, in vain. The Rākṣasas would certainly have been quickly killed by kings, without a doubt.

shloka_text: रामस्य बाहुवीर्येण रक्षिता लक्ष्मणस्य च । सुखं पारेसमुद्रस्य युध्येम विगतज्वराः ।। 7.39.5 ।।
explanation: Protected by the valor of Rama and Lakshmana, we would fight happily beyond the ocean, free from anxiety.

shloka_text: एताश्चान्याश्च राजानः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः । कथयन्तः स्वराज्यानि जग्मुर्हर्षसमन्विताः ।। 7.39.6 ।।
explanation: There, these and other kings, narrating thousands of stories, went to their own kingdoms, filled with joy.

shloka_text: स्वानि राज्यानि मुख्यानि ऋद्धानि मुदितानि च । समृद्धधनधान्यानि पूर्णानि वसुमन्ति च ।। 7.39.7 ।।
explanation: Their own principal kingdoms, prosperous and joyful, rich in wealth and grain, complete and full of treasures.

shloka_text: यथापुराणि ते गत्वा रत्नानि विविधान्यथ । रामस्य प्रियकामार्थमुपहारान् नृपा ददुः ।। 7.39.8 ।।
explanation: As before, the kings, having gone, gave various jewels and offerings for the sake of Rama's pleasure.

shloka_text: अश्वान्यानानि रत्नानि हस्तिनश्च मदोत्कटान् । चन्दनानि च मुख्यानि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.39.9 ।।
explanation: Horses, vehicles, jewels, and intoxicated elephants, and excellent sandalwoods, and divine ornaments.

shloka_text: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालांस्तु दास्यो रूपसमन्विताः । अजाविकांश्च विविधान् रथांस्तु विविधान्ददुः ।। 7.39.10 ।।
explanation: Maidservants endowed with beauty gave jewels, pearls, and corals, and various goats and sheep, and various chariots.

shloka_text: भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलाः । आदाय तानि रत्नानि स्वां पुरीं पुनरागताः ।। 7.39.11 ।।
explanation: Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, the mighty ones, having taken those jewels, returned to their own city.

shloka_text: आगम्य च पुरीं रम्यामयोध्यां पुरुषर्षभाः । तानि रत्नानि चित्राणि रामाय समुपाहरन् ।। 7.39.12 ।।
explanation: And having arrived at the beautiful city of Ayodhya, those foremost among men presented those various jewels to Rama.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य च तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिसमन्वितः । सुग्रीवाय ददौ राज्ञे महात्मा कृतकर्मणे ।। 7.39.13 ।।
explanation: And having received all that, Rama, filled with joy, the great-souled one, gave it to King Sugriva, who had accomplished the task.

shloka_text: बिभीषणाय च ददौ तथान्येभ्यो ऽपि राघवः । राक्षसेभ्यः कपिभ्यश्च यैर्वृतो जयमाप्तवान् ।। 7.39.14 ।।
explanation: Rama gave to Vibhishana, and similarly to other Rakshasas and monkeys, by whom surrounded he had obtained victory.

shloka_text: ते सर्वे रामदत्तानि रत्नानि कपिराक्षसाः । शिरोभिर्धारयामासुर्बाहुभिश्च महाबलाः ।। 7.39.15 ।।
explanation: All those mighty monkeys and rakshasas wore the jewels given by Rama on their heads and arms.

shloka_text: हनूमन्तं च नृपतिरिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः । अङ्गदं च महाबाहुमङ्कमारोप्य वीर्यवान् ।। 7.39.16 ।।
explanation: The valiant king of the Ikshvakus, a great charioteer, having placed Hanumana and the mighty-armed Angada on his lap.

shloka_text: रामः कमलपत्राक्षः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् । अङ्गदस्ते सुपुत्रो ऽयं मन्त्री चाप्यनिलात्मजः ।। 7.39.17 ।।
explanation: Rama, the lotus-petal-eyed, said this to Sugriva: "This Angada is your excellent son, and the son of Anila (Hanuman) is also a minister."

shloka_text: सुग्रीवमन्त्रिते युक्तौ मम चापि हिते रतौ । अर्हतो विविधां पूजां त्वत्कृते वै हरीश्वर ।। 7.39.18 ।।
explanation: O Lord of monkeys, the two who are engaged in Sugriva's counsel and also devoted to my welfare, they indeed deserve various honors for your sake.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा व्यवमुच्याङ्गाद्भूषणानि महायशाः । स बबन्ध महार्हाणि तदाङ्गदहनूमतोः ।। 7.39.19 ।।
explanation: Having said this, the greatly renowned one removed the ornaments from his body and then fastened those very valuable ones on Angada and Hanuman.

shloka_text: आभाष्य च महावीर्यान्राघवो यूथपर्षभान् । नीलं नलं केसरिणं कुमुदं गन्धमादनम् ।। 7.39.20 ।।
explanation: And Rama, having addressed the very mighty chiefs of the troops—Nila, Nala, Kesarin, Kumuda, and Gandhamadana.

shloka_text: सुषेणं पनसं वीरं मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च । जाम्बवन्तं गवाक्षं च विनतं धूम्रमेव च ।। 7.39.21 ।।
explanation: Suṣeṇa, Panasa, the brave one, Mainda, and Dvivida, Jāmbavanta, and Gavākṣa, Vinata, and Dhūmra.

shloka_text: वलीमुखं प्रजङ्घं च सन्नादं च महाबलम् । दरीमुखं दधिमुखमिन्द्रजानुं च यूथपम् ।। 7.39.22 ।।
explanation: Valimukha, Prajangha, and Sannada, and Mahabala, Darimukha, Dadhimukha, and Indrajanu, and Yuthapa.

shloka_text: मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा नेत्राभ्यामापिबन्निव । सुहृदो मे भवन्तश्च शरीरं भ्रातरस्तथा ।। 7.39.23 ।।
explanation: With sweet and gentle speech, as if drinking in with his eyes, you are my friends, my very body, and my brothers.

shloka_text: युष्माभिरुद्धृतश्चाहं व्यसनात्काननौकसः । धन्यो राजा च सुग्रीवो भवद्भिः सुहृदां वरैः ।। 7.39.24 ।।
explanation: By you, I, the forest dweller, have been rescued from distress. And King Sugriva is blessed by you, the best of friends.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा ददौ तेभ्यो भूषणानि यथार्हतः । वज्राणि च महार्हाणि सस्वजे च नरर्षभः ।। 7.39.25 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken, the best among men gave them ornaments as was fitting, and very valuable diamonds, and embraced them.

shloka_text: ते पिबन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः । मांसानि च सुमृष्टानि मूलानि च फलानि च ।। 7.39.26 ।।
explanation: They, tawny like honey, were drinking fragrant sweet drinks, and delicious meats, roots, and fruits.

shloka_text: एवं तेषां निवसतां मासः साग्रो ययौ तदा । मुहूर्तमिव ते सर्वे रामभक्त्या च मेनिरे ।। 7.39.27 ।।
explanation: Thus, as they resided there, more than a month passed. Yet, all of them, due to their devotion to Rama, felt it like a mere moment.

shloka_text: रामो ऽपि रेमे तैः सार्धं वानरैः कामरूपिभिः । राक्षसैश्च महावीर्यैर्ऋक्षैश्चैव महाबलैः ।। 7.39.28 ।।
explanation: Rama also sported with them, with the shape-shifting monkeys, and with the greatly valorous Rakshasas, and also with the immensely powerful bears.

shloka_text: एवं तेषां ययौ मासो द्वितीयः शिशिरः सुखम् । वानराणां प्रहृष्टानां राक्षसानां च सर्वशः ।। 7.39.29 ।।
explanation: Thus, for all those delighted monkeys and Rākṣasas, the second cool month passed pleasantly.

shloka_text: इक्ष्वाकुनगरे रम्ये परां प्रीतिमुपासताम् । रामस्य प्रीतिकरणैः कालस्तेषां सुखं ययौ ।। 7.39.30 ।।
explanation: In the beautiful city of Ikshvaku, for those who experienced supreme joy, their time passed happily due to the pleasing actions of Rama.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 39 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the thirty-ninth chapter.

shloka_text: तथा स्म तेषां वसतामृक्षवानररक्षसाम् । राघवस्तु महातेजाः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.40.1 ।।
explanation: Thus, while those bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas were dwelling there, the greatly effulgent Rama spoke this to Sugriva.

shloka_text: गम्यतां सौम्य किष्किन्धां दुराधर्षां सुरासुरैः । पालयस्व सहामात्यो राज्यं निहतकण्टकम् ।। 7.40.2 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, go to Kishkindha, which is impregnable even to gods and demons. Rule the kingdom, along with your ministers, with all enemies destroyed.

shloka_text: अङ्गदं च महाबाहो प्रीत्या परमया युतः । पश्य त्वं हनुमन्तं च नलं च सुमहाबलम् ।। 7.40.3 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, you, full of supreme affection, behold Angada, and Hanuman, and Nala of immense strength.

shloka_text: सुषेणं श्वशुरं वीरं तारं च बलिनां वरम् । कुमुदं चैव दुर्धर्षं नीलं चैव महाबलम् ।। 7.40.4 ।।
explanation: Suṣeṇa, the heroic father-in-law, and Tāra, the best among the strong, and also Kumuda, the unconquerable, and also Nīla, the very mighty.

shloka_text: वीरं शतवलिं चैव मैन्दं द्विविदमेव च । गजं गवाक्षं गवयं शरभं च महाबलम् । पश्य प्रीतिसमायुक्तो गन्धमादनमेव च ।। 7.40.5 ।।
explanation: See the valiant Vīra, and Śatavali, and Mainda, and Dvivida, and Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, and the mighty Śarabha, and also Gandhamādana, filled with joy.

shloka_text: ऋषभं च सुविक्रान्तं जाम्बवन्तं महाबलम् । ये चेमे सुमहात्मानो मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।। 7.40.6 ।।
explanation: And Rishabha, the very mighty, and Jambavan, the greatly powerful, and these other great-souled ones who have sacrificed their lives for my sake.

shloka_text: पश्य त्वं प्रीतिसंयुक्तो मा चैषां विप्रियं कृथाः ।। 7.40.7 ।।
explanation: Look with affection, and do not cause them any displeasure.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवमाश्लिष्य च पुनः पुनः । विभीषणमुवाचाथ रामो मधुरया गिरा ।। 7.40.8 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken and repeatedly embraced Sugriva, Rama then addressed Vibhishana with sweet words.

shloka_text: लङ्कां प्रशाधि धर्मेण धर्मज्ञस्त्वं मतो मम । पुरस्य राक्षसानां च स्वभ्रातुस्सम्मतो ह्यसि ।। 7.40.9 ।।
explanation: Rule Lanka righteously, for I consider you a knower of dharma. You are indeed agreeable to the city, to the Rākṣasas, and to your own brother.

shloka_text: मा च बुद्धिमधर्मे त्वं कुर्या राजन्कथञ्चन । बुद्धिमन्तो हि राजानो ध्रुवमश्नन्ति मेदिनीम् ।। 7.40.10 ।।
explanation: O King, never ever incline your mind towards unrighteousness. For intelligent kings surely possess the earth.

shloka_text: अहं च नित्यशो राजन्सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया । स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः ।। 7.40.11 ।।
explanation: O King, you should always remember me along with Sugriva with great affection. Go now, free from distress.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः । साधुसाध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः ।। 7.40.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's speech, the bears, monkeys, and Rākṣasas repeatedly praised Kakutstha, saying, "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: तव बुद्धिर्महाबाहो वीर्यमद्भुतमेव च । माधुर्यं परमं राम स्वयम्भोरिव नित्यदा ।। 7.40.13 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, your intellect and amazing valor, and supreme sweetness, O Rama, are always like Svayambhu's.

shloka_text: तेषामेवं ब्रुवाणानां वानराणां च राक्षसाम् । हनूमान्प्रवणः भूत्वा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.40.14 ।।
explanation: While the monkeys and Rākṣasas were speaking thus, Hanumān, becoming humble, spoke a word to Rāghava.

shloka_text: स्नेहो मे परमो राजंस्त्वयि तिष्ठतु नित्यदा । भक्तिश्च नियता वीर भावो नान्यत्र गच्छतु ।। 7.40.15 ।।
explanation: O King, may my supreme affection always abide in you. And O hero, may my devotion be constant, and my sentiment not go elsewhere.

shloka_text: वायद्रामकथा वीर चरिष्यति महीतले । तावच्छरीरे वत्स्यन्ति प्राणा मम न संशयः ।। 7.40.16 ।।
explanation: O hero, as long as the story of Rama will prevail on the earth, so long will my life breaths dwell in my body, without doubt.

shloka_text: यच्चैतच्चरितं दिव्यं कथा ते रघुनन्दन । तन्मयाप्सरसो नाम श्रावयेयुर्नरर्षभ ।। 7.40.17 ।।
explanation: And this divine story, your narrative, O delight of the Raghus, that indeed the Apsaras should hear from me, O best among men.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वाहं ततो वीर तव चर्यामृतं प्रभो । उत्कण्ठां तां हरिष्यामि मेघलेखामिवानिलः ।। 7.40.18 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, O valiant one, O Lord, I shall then dispel that longing by means of the nectar of your deeds, just as the wind disperses a line of clouds.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणं रामस्तु हनूमन्तं वरासनात् । उत्थाय सस्वजे स्नेहाद्वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.40.19 ।।
explanation: Thus speaking, Rama, rising from his excellent seat, embraced Hanumana with affection and spoke these words.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्कपिश्रेष्ठ भविता नात्र संशयः । चरिष्यति कथा यावदेषा लोके च मामिका । तावत्ते भविता कीर्तिः शरीरे ऽप्यसवस्तथा ।। 7.40.20 ।।
explanation: This will indeed happen, O best of monkeys, there is no no doubt about it. As long as this story of mine circulates in the world, so long will your fame endure, and your life-breaths in your body.

shloka_text: लोका हि यावत्स्थास्यन्ति तावत्स्थास्यति मे कथा ।। 7.40.21 ।।
explanation: For as long as the worlds exist, so long will my story endure.

shloka_text: लोके च मामिका । एकैकस्योपकारस्य प्राणान्दास्यामि ते कपे । नरः प्रत्युपकाराणामापस्त्वायाति पात्रताम् ।। 7.40.22 ।।
explanation: And mine in the world. For each and every favor, I will give my lives to you, O monkey. A man in distress attains worthiness for counter-favors.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्य हारं चन्द्राभं मुच्य कण्ठात्स राघवः । वैडूर्यतरलं कण्ठे बबन्ध च हनूमतः ।। 7.40.23 ।।
explanation: Then, Rama, having taken off from his (own) neck the moon-like necklace, which had a cat's eye gem as its centerpiece, fastened it on Hanuman's neck.

shloka_text: तेनोरसि निबद्धेन हारेण महता कपिः । रराज हेमशैलेन्द्रश्चन्द्रेणाक्रान्तमस्तकः ।। 7.40.24 ।।
explanation: With that magnificent necklace fastened on his chest, the monkey shone like a great golden mountain whose peak is adorned by the moon.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतदुत्थायोत्थाय वानराः । प्रणम्य शिरसा पादौ निर्जग्मुस्ते महाबलाः ।। 7.40.25 ।।
explanation: Having heard this from Rama, those mighty monkeys, repeatedly rising and bowing their heads at his feet, departed.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवः स च रामेण निरन्तरमुरोगतः । विभीषणश्च धर्मात्मा सर्वे ते बाष्पविक्लवाः ।। 7.40.26 ।।
explanation: Sugriva, who was constantly embraced by Rama, and the righteous Vibhishana—all of them were overcome with tears.

shloka_text: सर्वे च ते बाष्पकलाः साश्रुनेत्रा विचेतसः । सम्मूढा इव दुःखेन त्यजन्तो राघवं तदा ।। 7.40.27 ।।
explanation: And all of them, with tears in their eyes, distraught, as if stupefied by sorrow, were then abandoning Rama.

shloka_text: कृतप्रसादास्तेनैवं राघवेण महात्मना । जग्मुः स्वं स्वं गृहं सर्वे देही देहमिव त्यजन् ।। 7.40.28 ।।
explanation: Having thus been favored by the great-souled Raghava, all of them went to their respective homes, just as an embodied soul abandons its body.

shloka_text: ततस्तु ते राक्षसऋक्षवानराः प्रणम्य रामं रघुवंशवर्धनम् । वियोगजाश्रुप्रतिपूर्णलोचनाः प्रतिप्रयातास्तु यथा निवासिनः ।। 7.40.29 ।।
explanation: Then, those Rakshasas, bears, and monkeys, having bowed down to Rama, the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty, their eyes filled with tears born of separation, returned to their respective dwellings.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 40 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the glorious first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the fortieth chapter.

shloka_text: विसृज्य च महाबाहुर्ऋक्षवानरराक्षसान् । भ्रातृभिः सहितो रामः प्रमुमोद सुखं सुखी ।। 7.41.1 ।।
explanation: And the mighty-armed Rama, having dismissed the bears, monkeys, and rakshasas, rejoiced happily with his brothers.

shloka_text: अथापराह्णसमये भ्रातृभिः सह राघवः । शुश्राव मधुरां वाणीमन्तरिक्षात् प्रभाषिताम् ।। 7.41.2 ।।
explanation: Then, in the afternoon, Rama, along with his brothers, heard a sweet voice spoken from the sky.

shloka_text: सौम्य राम निरीक्षस्व सौम्येन वदनेन माम् । कुबेरभवनात्प्राप्तं विद्धि मां पुष्पकं प्रभो ।। 7.41.3 ।।
explanation: O gentle Rama, look at me with a gentle face. O Lord, know me to be the Pushpaka, arrived from Kubera's abode.

shloka_text: तव शासनमाज्ञाय गतो ऽस्मि भवनं प्रति । उपस्थातुं नरश्रेष्ठ स च मां प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.41.4 ।।
explanation: Having understood your command, I went to the house to attend, O best among men, and he spoke to me.

shloka_text: निर्जितस्त्वं नरेन्द्रेण राघवेण महात्मना । निहत्य युधि दुर्धर्षं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम् ।। 7.41.5 ।।
explanation: You were conquered by the great-souled king Rama, who, in battle, killed the formidable Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: ममापि परमा प्रीतर्हते तस्मिन्दुरात्मनि । रावणे सगणे चैव सपुत्रे सहबान्धवे ।। 7.41.6 ।।
explanation: My supreme joy will also be upon the killing of that evil-minded Ravana, along with his retinue, his sons, and his kinsmen.

shloka_text: स त्वं रामेण लङ्कायां निर्जितः परमात्मना । वह सौम्य तमेव त्वमहमाज्ञापयामि ते ।। 7.41.7 ।।
explanation: You, who were conquered by Rama, the Supreme Soul, in Lanka, O gentle one, carry him alone. I command you.

shloka_text: परमो ह्येष मे कामो यत्त्वं राघवनन्दनम् । वहेर्लोकस्य संयानं गच्छस्व विगतज्वरः ।। 7.41.8 ।।
explanation: This is indeed my greatest desire, that you carry the son of Raghu for the world's passage. Go, free from anxiety.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं शासनमाज्ञाय धनदस्य महात्मनः । त्वत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तो निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीक्ष माम् ।। 7.41.9 ।।
explanation: Therefore, I, having understood the command of the great-souled Kubera, have arrived in your presence. Await me without apprehension.

shloka_text: अदृष्यः सर्वभूतानां सर्वेषां धनदाज्ञया । चराम्यहं प्रभावेण तवाज्ञां परिपालयन् ।। 7.41.10 ।।
explanation: Invisible to all beings, by the command of Dhanada, I wander by my power, fulfilling your command.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तदा रामः पुष्पकेण महाबलः । उवाच पुष्पकं दृष्ट्वा विमानं पुनरागतम् ।। 7.41.11 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Pushpaka, the mighty Rama then, seeing the Pushpaka aerial chariot returned, spoke to Pushpaka.

shloka_text: यद्येवं स्वागतं ते ऽस्तु विमानवर पुष्पक । आनुकूल्याद्धनेशस्य वृत्तदोषो न नो भवेत् ।। 7.41.12 ।।
explanation: If this is so, welcome to you, O excellent Pushpaka aerial chariot. Due to the favor of the lord of wealth, no fault will occur to us.

shloka_text: लाजैश्चैव तथा पुष्पैर्धूपैश्चैव सुगन्धिभिः । पूजयित्वा महाबाहू राघवः पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.13 ।।
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Rama worshipped the Pushpaka with parched grains, flowers, and fragrant incense.

shloka_text: गम्यतामिति चोवाच आगच्छ त्वं स्मरे यदा । सिद्धानां च गतौ सौम्य मा विषादेन योजय । प्रतिघातश्च ते मा भूद्यथेष्टं गच्छतो दिशः ।। 7.41.14 ।।
explanation: And he said, 'Go! Come when you remember. O gentle one, do not let sorrow afflict you on the path of the perfected ones. And may there be no obstruction for you as you go in any direction you desire.'

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति रामेण पूजयित्वा विसर्जितम् । अभिप्रेतां दिशं तस्मात्प्रायात्तत्पुष्पकं तदा ।। 7.41.15 ।।
explanation: Having been honored and dismissed by Rama with the words "So be it," that Pushpaka then departed from there towards its desired direction.

shloka_text: एवमन्तर्हिते तस्मिन्पुष्पके सुकृतात्मनि । भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.41.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, when that blessed Pushpaka had vanished, Bharata, with folded hands, spoke words to Raghunandana.

shloka_text: विविधात्मनि दृश्यन्ते त्वयि वीर प्रशासति । अमानुषाणां सत्त्वानां व्याहृतानि मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.41.17 ।।
explanation: O hero, while you are ruling, the utterances of non-human beings are repeatedly manifested in your diverse self.

shloka_text: अनामयश्च सत्वानां साग्रो मासो गतो ह्ययम् । जीर्णानामपि सत्त्वानां मृत्युर्नायाति राघव ।। 7.41.18 ।।
explanation: This full month has passed, and beings are free from illness. Even for old creatures, death does not come, O Raghava.

shloka_text: अरोगप्रसवा नार्यो वपुष्मन्तो हि मानवाः । हर्षश्चाभ्यधिको राजञ्जनस्य पुरवासिनः ।। 7.41.19 ।।
explanation: Women give birth without illness, and indeed, people are robust. And there is abundant joy, O King, among the city dwellers.

shloka_text: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः पातयन्नमृतं पयः । वाताश्चापि प्रवान्त्येते स्पर्शयुक्ताः सुखाः शिवाः ।। 7.41.20 ।।
explanation: At the proper time, the cloud rains, dropping nectar-like water. And these winds blow, pleasant to the touch, comfortable, and auspicious.

shloka_text: ईदृशो ऽनश्वरो राजा भवेदिति नरेश्वरः । कथयन्ति पुरे राजन्पौरजानपदास्तथा ।। 7.41.21 ।।
explanation: O King, O Lord of men, the citizens and the people of the countryside in the city say, "Such an imperishable king should be."
