shloka_text: एता वाचः सुमधुरा भरतेन समीरिताः । श्रुत्वा रामो मुदा युक्तो बभूव नृपसत्तमः ।। 7.41.22 ।।
explanation: Having heard these exceedingly sweet words spoken by Bharata, Rama, the foremost of kings, became filled with joy.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 41 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the forty-first chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: स विसृज्य ततो रामः पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम् । प्रविवेश महाबाहुरशोकवनिकां तदा ।। 7.42.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having dismissed the Pushpaka chariot adorned with gold, the mighty-armed Rama entered the Ashoka grove.

shloka_text: चन्दनागुरुचूतैश्च तुङ्गकालेयकैरपि । देवदारुवनैश्चापि समन्तादुपशोभिताम् ।। 7.42.2 ।।
explanation: Adorned all around with sandalwood, agarwood, and mango trees, and also with tall Kāleyaka trees, and with forests of Deodar.

shloka_text: चम्पकाशोकपुन्नागमधूकपनसासनैः । शोभितां पारिजातैश्च विधूमज्वलनप्रभैः ।। 7.42.3 ।।
explanation: Adorned with Champaka, Ashoka, Punnaga, Madhuka, Jackfruit, and Asana trees, and with Parijata trees whose brilliance was like smokeless flames.

shloka_text: लोध्रनीपार्जुनैर्नागैः सप्तपर्णातिमुक्तकैः । मन्दारकदलीगुल्मलताजालसमावृताम् ।। 7.42.4 ।।
explanation: Covered with Lodhra, Kadamba, Arjuna, Nāga, Saptaparṇa, and Atimuktaka trees, and enveloped by thickets of Mandāra and Kadalī plants, and networks of creepers.

shloka_text: प्रियङ्गुभिः कदम्बैश्च तथा च वकुलैरपि । जम्बूभिर्दाडिमैश्चैव कोविदारैश्च शोभिताम् ।। 7.42.5 ।।
explanation: Adorned with Priyangu, and with Kadamba, and also with Bakula, with Jambu, and also with Pomegranate, and also with Kovidara.

shloka_text: सर्वदा कुसुमै रम्यैः फलवद्भिर्मनोरमैः । दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतैस्तरुणाङ्कुरपल्लवैः ।। 7.42.6 ।।
explanation: Always with beautiful flowers, delightful and fruit-bearing, endowed with divine fragrance and taste, and with young sprouts and tender leaves.

shloka_text: तथैव तरुभिर्दिव्यैः शिल्पिभिः परिकल्पितैः । चारुपल्लवपुष्पाढ्यैर्मत्तभ्रमरसङ्कुलैः ।। 7.42.7 ।।
explanation: Similarly, with divine trees, fashioned by artisans, rich with beautiful sprouts and flowers, and swarming with intoxicated bees.

shloka_text: कोकिलैर्भृङ्गराजैश्च नानावर्णैश्च पक्षिभिः । शोभितां शतशश्चित्रां चूतवृक्षावतंसकैः ।। 7.42.8 ।।
explanation: Adorned by hundreds of cuckoos, king-bees, and various-colored birds, and variegated with mango trees as its ornaments.

shloka_text: शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः । नीलाञ्जननिभाश्चान्ये भान्ति तत्रत्यपादपाः ।। 7.42.9 ।।
explanation: The trees there shine, some resembling pure gold, some like flames of fire, and others like blue collyrium.

shloka_text: सुरभीणि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि विविधानि च । दीर्घिका विविधाकाराः पूर्णाः परमवारिणा ।। 7.42.10 ।।
explanation: Fragrant flowers and various garlands, and long ponds of various shapes, full of excellent water.

shloka_text: माणिक्यकृतसोपानाः स्फाटिकान्तरकुट्टिमाः । फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवनाश्चक्रवाकोपशोभिताः ।। 7.42.11 ।।
explanation: With steps made of rubies, inner floors paved with crystal, and adorned with groves of blooming lotuses and water-lilies, graced by Chakravaka birds.

shloka_text: दात्यूहशुकसङ्घुष्टा हंससारसनादिताः । तरुभिः पुष्पवद्भिश्च तीरजैरुपशोभिताः ।। 7.42.12 ।।
explanation: Resounding with water-cocks and parrots, filled with the calls of swans and cranes, and adorned by flowering trees growing on its banks.

shloka_text: प्राकारैर्विविधाकारैः शोभिताश्च शिलातलैः । तत्रैव च वनोद्देशे वैडूर्यमणिसन्निभैः ।। 7.42.13 ।।
explanation: Adorned by walls of various forms and by stone surfaces resembling lapis lazuli gems; and in that very forest region.

shloka_text: शाद्वलैः परमोपेतां पुष्पितद्रुमकाननाम् । तत्र सङ्घर्षजातानां वृक्षाणां पुष्पशालिनाम् ।। 7.42.14 ।।
explanation: Supremely endowed with green meadows and forests of flowering trees. There, the trees, grown densely together, were resplendent with flowers.

shloka_text: प्रस्तराः पुष्पशबला नभस्तारागणैरिव । नन्दनं हि यथेन्द्रस्य ब्राह्मं चैत्ररथं यथा ।। 7.42.15 ।।
explanation: The rocks were variegated with flowers, like the sky with its multitude of stars. Indeed, it was like Indra's Nandana garden, and like Brahma's Chaitraratha.

shloka_text: तथाभूतं हि रामस्य काननं सन्निवेशनम् । बह्वासनगृहोपेतां लतागृहसमावृताम् ।। 7.42.16 ।।
explanation: Indeed, such was Rama's forest dwelling, equipped with many seating areas and rooms, and surrounded by creeper-bowers.

shloka_text: अशोकवनिकां स्फीतां प्रविश्य रघुनन्दनः । आसने च शुभाकारे पुष्पप्रकरभूषिते ।। 7.42.17 ।।
explanation: Having entered the extensive Ashoka grove, the delight of the Raghus (Rama) [sat] on an auspicious-looking seat adorned with a multitude of flowers.

shloka_text: कुशास्तरणसंस्तीर्णे रामः सन्निषसाद ह । सीतामादायं हस्तेन मधुमैरेयकं शुचि ।। 7.42.18 ।।
explanation: Rama sat down on the Kusa-grass mat. Taking Sita by the hand, he partook of pure Maireyaka wine.

shloka_text: पाययामास काकुत्स्थः शचीमिव पुरन्दरः । मांसानि च समृष्टानि फलानि विविधानि च ।। 7.42.19 ।।
explanation: Kakutstha served well-prepared meats and various fruits, just as Purandara (Indra) served Shachi.

shloka_text: रामस्याभ्यवहारार्थं किङ्करास्तूर्णमाहरन्उ । उपानृत्यंश्च राजानं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः ।। 7.42.20 ।।
explanation: For Rama's meal, servants quickly brought food. And those skilled in dance and song danced before the king.

shloka_text: बालाश्च रूपवत्यश्च स्त्रियः पानवशानुगाः । मनोभिरामा रामास्ता रामो रमयतां वरः ।। 7.42.21 ।।
explanation: Young and beautiful women, women fond of drink, those charming women—Rama, the best among those who delight, enjoyed with them.

shloka_text: उपानृत्यन्त काकुत्स्थं नृत्यगीतविशारदाः । मनोभिरामा रामास्ता रामो रमयतां वरः ।। 7.42.22 ।।
explanation: Those women, skilled in dance and song, charming to the mind, danced before Kakutstha. Rama was the best among those who give delight.

shloka_text: रमयामास धर्मात्मा नित्यं परमभूषितः । स तया सीतया सार्धमासीनो विरराज ह ।। 7.42.23 ।।
explanation: The righteous soul, always supremely adorned, constantly enjoyed himself. He, seated with Sita, shone splendidly.

shloka_text: अरुन्धत्या सहासीनो वसिष्ठ इव तेजसा । एवं रामो मुदा युक्तः सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम् ।। 7.42.24 ।।
explanation: Like Vasistha, seated with Arundhati, radiant with splendor, so too Rama, filled with joy, was with Sita, who resembled a divine maiden.

shloka_text: रमयामास वैदेहीमहन्यहनि देववत्त । था तयोर्विहरतोः सीताराघवयोश्चिरम् ।। 7.42.25 ।।
explanation: He delighted Vaidehi day after day, like a god. Thus, Sita and Raghava sported for a long time.

shloka_text: अत्यक्रामच्छुभः कालः शैशिरो भोगदः सदा । प्राप्तयोर्विविधान्भोगानतीतः शिशिरागमः ।। 7.42.26 ।।
explanation: The auspicious winter season, always providing enjoyment, passed. After they had obtained various pleasures, the winter season came to an end.

shloka_text: पूर्वाह्णे धर्मकार्याणि कृत्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित् । शेषं दिवसभागार्धमन्तःपुरगतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.42.27 ।।
explanation: The knower of dharma, having performed his righteous duties righteously in the forenoon, spent the remaining half of the day in the inner chambers.

shloka_text: सीतापि देवकार्याणि कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकानि वै । श्वश्रूणामकरोत्पूजां सर्वासामविशेषतः ।। 7.42.28 ।।
explanation: Sita, having performed her morning divine duties, also offered reverence to all her mothers-in-law without discrimination.

shloka_text: अभ्यगच्छत्ततो रामं विचित्राभरणाम्बरा । त्रिविष्टपे सहस्राक्षमुपविष्टं यथा शची ।। 7.42.29 ।।
explanation: Then, adorned with various ornaments and garments, she approached Rama, just as Sachi approaches the thousand-eyed (Indra) seated in heaven.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः पत्नीं कल्याणेन समन्विताम् । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.42.30 ।।
explanation: Having seen his wife, who was endowed with auspiciousness, Rama felt unequalled joy and exclaimed, 'Excellent! Excellent!'

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम् । अपत्यलाभो वैदेहि त्वयि मे समुपस्थितः ।। 7.42.31 ।।
explanation: And he said to Sita, the beautiful-hipped one, who resembled a daughter of a god: 'O Vaidehi, the acquisition of offspring has come to me through you.'

shloka_text: किमिच्छसि वरारोहे कामः किं क्रियतां तव । स्मितं कृत्वा तु वैदेही रामं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.42.32 ।।
explanation: "What do you desire, O lady with beautiful hips? What wish shall be fulfilled for you?" Having smiled, Vaidehi then spoke these words to Rama.

shloka_text: तपोवनानि पुण्यानि द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघव । गङ्गातीरोपविष्टानामृषीणामुग्रतेजसाम् ।। 7.42.33 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, I wish to see the sacred hermitages of the sages of fierce splendor who are seated on the banks of the Ganga.

shloka_text: फलमूलाशिनां देव पादमूलेषु वर्तितुम् । एष मे परमः कामो यन्मूलफलभोजिनाम् ।। 7.42.34 ।।
explanation: O god, to dwell at the feet of those who subsist on fruits and roots, this is my greatest desire, that I may be among those who subsist on roots and fruits.

shloka_text: अप्येकरात्रं काकुत्स्थ निवसेयं तपोवने । तथेति च प्रतिज्ञातं रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । विस्रब्धा भव वैदेहि श्वो गमिष्यस्यसंशयम् ।। 7.42.35 ।।
explanation: "O Kakutstha, I would stay in the hermitage even for one night." And "So be it," was promised by Rama, the unwearied doer. "Be confident, O Vaidehi, you will certainly go tomorrow."

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम् । मध्यकक्षान्तरं रामो निर्जगाम सुहृद्वृतः ।। 7.42.36 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Maithili, Janaka's daughter, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, departed to the inner apartment, surrounded by friends.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 42 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, ends the forty-second chapter.

shloka_text: तत्रोपविष्टं राजानमुपासन्ते विचक्षणाः । कथानां बहुरूपाणां हास्यकाराः समन्ततः ।। 7.43.1 ।।
explanation: Wise men attend the king seated there. All around him are jesters who tell varied stories.

shloka_text: विजयो मधुमत्तश्च काश्यपो मङ्गलः कुटः । सुराजः कालियो भद्रो दन्तवक्रः सुमागधः ।। 7.43.2 ।।
explanation: Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kashyapa, Mangala, Kuta, Suraja, Kaliya, Bhadra, Dantavakra, and Sumagadha.

shloka_text: एते कथा बहुविधाः परिहाससमन्विताः । कथयन्ति स्म संहृष्टा राघवस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.43.3 ।।
explanation: Delighted, they narrated these various stories, full of humor, about the great-souled Rama.

shloka_text: ततः कथायां कस्याञ्चिद्राघवः समभाषत । काः कथा नगरे भद्र वर्तन्ते विषयेषु च ।। 7.43.4 ।।
explanation: Then, in the course of some conversation, Rama spoke: "O good one, what news is current in the city and in the regions?"

shloka_text: मामाश्रितानि कान्याहुः पौरजानपदा जनाः । किं च सीतां समाश्रित्य भरतं किं च लक्ष्मणम् ।। 7.43.5 ।।
explanation: What do the citizens and country people say concerning me? And what do they say concerning Sita, Bharata, and Lakshmana?

shloka_text: किं नु शत्रुघ्नमुद्दिश्य कैकयीं किं नु मातरम् । वक्तव्यतां च राजानो वरे राज्ये व्रजन्ति च ।। 7.43.6 ।।
explanation: Is it regarding Shatrughna, or is it regarding mother Kaikeyi, that the kings incur reproach concerning the boon and the kingdom?

shloka_text: एवमुक्ते तु रामेण भद्रः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् । स्थिताः कथा शुभाः राजन्वर्तन्ते पुरवासिनाम् ।। 7.43.7 ।।
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Bhadra, with folded hands, said: "O King, auspicious talks are current among the city dwellers."

shloka_text: अमुं तु विजयं सौम्य दशग्रीववधार्जितम् । भूयिष्ठं स्वपुरे पौरैः कथ्यन्ते पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.43.8 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, O best among men, this victory, however, obtained by the slaying of Daśagrīva, is being widely spoken of by the citizens in their own city.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु भद्रेण राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । कथयस्व यथातत्त्वं सर्वं निरवशेषतः ।। 7.43.9 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Bhadra, Rama spoke these words: "Relate everything as it truly is, completely without omission."

shloka_text: शुभाशुभानि वाक्यानि यान्याहुः पुरवासिनः । श्रुत्वेदानीं शुभं कुर्यां नकुर्यामशुभानि च ।। 7.43.10 ।।
explanation: Having heard now the auspicious and inauspicious words spoken by the city dwellers, I should do good and not do inauspicious deeds.

shloka_text: कथयस्व च विस्रब्धो निर्भयं विगतज्वरः । कथयन्ति यथा पौराः पापा जनपदेषु च ।। 7.43.11 ।।
explanation: Tell me confidently, fearlessly, and free from anxiety, just as citizens and wicked people speak in the countries.

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भद्रः सुरुचिरं वचः । प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुं प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः ।। 7.43.12 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Bhadra, with folded hands and great composure, replied with very pleasing words to the mighty-armed one.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्यथा पौराः कथयन्ति शुभाशुभम् । चत्वरापणरथ्यासु वनेषूपवनेषु च ।। 7.43.13 ।।
explanation: Listen, O King, to what the citizens say, both good and bad, in the squares, markets, streets, forests, and gardens.

shloka_text: दुष्करं कृतवान्रामः समुद्रे सेतुबन्धनम् । अश्रुतं पूर्वकैः कैश्चिद्देवैरपि सदानवैः ।। 7.43.14 ।।
explanation: Rama accomplished the extraordinary feat of building a bridge in the ocean, a deed unheard of by any of the ancients, even by the gods and the Danavas.

shloka_text: रावणश्च दुराधर्षो हतः सबलवाहनः । वानराश्च वशं नीता ऋक्षाश्च सह राक्षसैः ।। 7.43.15 ।।
explanation: And the invincible Rāvaṇa was killed along with his army and mounts. And the monkeys and bears, along with the Rākṣasas, were brought under control.

shloka_text: हत्वा च रावणं सङ्ख्ये सीतामाहृत्य राघवः । अमर्षं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा स्ववेश्म पुनरानयत् ।। 7.43.16 ।।
explanation: Having killed Ravana in battle, Rama, bringing back Sita, set aside his anger and brought her back to his own home.

shloka_text: कीदृशं हृदये तस्य सीतासम्भोगजं सुखम् । अङ्कमारोप्य तु पुरा रावणेन बलाद्धृताम् ।। 7.43.17 ।।
explanation: What kind of pleasure was in his heart, born from the enjoyment of Sita, whom Ravana had previously forcibly abducted after placing her on his lap?

shloka_text: लङ्कामपि पुरा नीतामशोकवनिकां गताम् । रक्षसां वशमापन्नां कथं रामो न कुत्सते ।। 7.43.18 ।।
explanation: How does Rama not blame her, who was formerly taken to Lanka, went to the Ashoka grove, and fell into the power of the Rakshasas?

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि दारेषु सहनीयं भविष्यति । यथा हि कुरुते राजा प्रजा तमनुवर्तते ।। 7.43.19 ।।
explanation: Even for us, it will have to be endured concerning our wives. For as the king acts, the subjects follow him.

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधा वाचो वदन्ति पुरवासिनः । नगरेषु च सर्वेषु राजञ्जनपदेषु च ।। 7.43.20 ।।
explanation: Thus, the city dwellers speak many kinds of words in all cities and districts, O King.

shloka_text: तस्यैवं भाषितं श्रुत्वा राघवः परमार्तवत् । उवाच सुहृदः सर्वान्कथमेतद्ब्रवीथ माम् ।। 7.43.21 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, Rama, greatly distressed, said to all his friends, "How do you say this to me?"

shloka_text: सर्वे तु शिरसा भूमावभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च । प्रत्यूचू राघवं दीनमेवमेतन्न संशयः ।। 7.43.22 ।।
explanation: All of them, having saluted and prostrated with their heads on the ground, replied to the distressed Rama: "This is indeed so, there is no doubt."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु वाक्यं काकुत्स्थः सर्वेषां समुदीरितम् । विसर्जयामास तदा वयस्याञ्छत्रुसूदनः ।। 7.43.23 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by all, Kakutstha, the destroyer of enemies, then dismissed his friends.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 43 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the forty-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: विसृज्य तु सुहृद्वर्गं बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य राघवः । समीपे द्वाःस्थमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.1 ।।
explanation: Having dismissed his friends, and having determined with his intellect, Rama spoke these words to the doorkeeper sitting nearby.

shloka_text: शीघ्रमानय सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम् । भरतं च महाभागं शत्रुघ्नमपराजितम् ।। 7.44.2 ।।
explanation: Quickly bring Saumitri, Lakshmana of auspicious marks, and Bharata, the greatly fortunate, and Shatrughna, the unconquered.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । लक्ष्मणस्य गृहं गत्वा प्रविवेशानिवारितः ।। 7.44.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, the doorkeeper, with folded hands on his head, went to Lakshmana's house and entered unhindered.

shloka_text: उवाच सुमहात्मानं वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः । द्रष्टुमिच्छति राजा त्वां गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम् ।। 7.44.4 ।।
explanation: With folded hands, having praised the very great soul, he said: "The king wishes to see you. Go there without delay."

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव सौमित्रिः श्रुत्वा राघवशासनम् । प्राद्रवद्रथमारुह्य राघवस्य निवेशनम् ।। 7.44.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's command, Lakshmana, saying "Very well," mounted a chariot and hastened to Rama's dwelling.

shloka_text: प्रयान्तं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा द्वाःस्थो भरतमन्तिकात् । उवाच भरतं तत्र वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.6 ।।
explanation: Having seen Lakshmana departing, the doorkeeper, from near Bharata, greeted Bharata there with folded hands and spoke.

shloka_text: विनयावनतो भूत्वा राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति । भरतस्तु वचःश्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थाद्रामसमीरितम् ।। 7.44.7 ।।
explanation: The king, having become humble, wishes to see you. But Bharata, having heard the words spoken by Rama from the doorkeeper,

shloka_text: उत्पपातासनात्तूर्णं पद्भ्यामेव ययौ बली । दृष्ट्वा प्रयान्तं भरतं त्वरमाणः कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.8 ।।
explanation: Upon seeing Bharata departing, the strong one, hurrying with folded hands, quickly sprang up from his seat and went on foot.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नभवनं गत्वा ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह । एह्यागच्छ रघुश्रेष्ठ राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति ।। 7.44.9 ।।
explanation: Having gone to Shatrughna's house, he then spoke these words: "Come here, O best of the Raghus, the king wishes to see you."

shloka_text: गतो हि लक्ष्मणः पूर्वं भरतश्च महायशाः । श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य शत्रुघ्नः परमासनात् ।। 7.44.10 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana had indeed gone before, and the greatly renowned Bharata. But having heard his words, Shatrughna from his excellent seat...

shloka_text: शिरसा धरणीं प्राप्य प्रययौ यत्र राघवः । द्वाःस्थस्त्वागम्य रामाय सर्वानेव कृताञ्जलिः । निवेदयामास तदा भ्रातऽन्स्वान्समुपस्थितान् ।। 7.44.11 ।।
explanation: Having touched the ground with his head, he went to where Rama was. The doorkeeper, having approached Rama, then, with folded hands, reported about all his own brothers who had arrived.

shloka_text: कुमारानागताञ्छ्रुत्वा चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना द्वाःस्थं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard that the princes had arrived, his senses agitated by worry, with a downcast face and a distressed mind, he spoke to the doorkeeper.

shloka_text: प्रवेशय कुमारांस्त्वं मत्समीपं त्वरान्वितः । एतेषु जीवितं मह्यमेते प्राणाः प्रिया मम ।। 7.44.13 ।।
explanation: Bring the princes to me quickly. My life is in them; they are my beloved vital breaths.

shloka_text: आज्ञप्तास्तु नरेन्द्रेण कुमाराः शक्रतेजसः । प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा विविशुस्ते समाहिताः ।। 7.44.14 ।।
explanation: Commanded by the king, the princes, who possessed the prowess of Indra, became humble, and with folded hands, they entered attentively.

shloka_text: ते तु दृष्ट्वा मुखं तस्य सग्रहं शशिनं यथा । सन्ध्यागतमिवादित्यं प्रभया परिवर्जितम् ।। 7.44.15 ।।
explanation: But they, having seen his face, which was like the moon seized by an eclipse, or like the sun at twilight, devoid of its splendor.

shloka_text: बाष्पपूर्णे च नयने दृष्ट्वा रामस्य धीमतः । हतशोभं यथा पद्मं मुखं वीक्ष्य च तस्य ते ।। 7.44.16 ।।
explanation: And having seen the tear-filled eyes of the wise Rama, and having observed his face, which was devoid of beauty like a lotus.

shloka_text: ततो ऽभिवाद्य त्वरिताः पादौ रामस्य मूर्धभिः । तस्थुः समाहिताः सर्वे रामस्त्वश्रूण्यवर्तयत् ।। 7.44.17 ।।
explanation: Then, having quickly saluted Rama's feet with their heads, all of them stood composed. Rama, however, shed tears.

shloka_text: तान्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यामुत्थाप्य च महाबलः । आसनेष्वासतेत्युक्त्वा ततो वाक्यं जगाद ह ।। 7.44.18 ।।
explanation: The mighty one, having embraced them with his two arms and lifted them up, then, saying 'Please sit on the seats,' spoke a word.

shloka_text: भवन्तो मम सर्वस्वं भवन्तो जीवितं मम । भवद्भिश्च कृतं राज्यं पालयामि नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.19 ।।
explanation: You are my everything, you are my life. I rule the kingdom that was established by you, O kings.

shloka_text: भवन्तः कृतशास्त्रार्था बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठिताः । सम्भूय च मदर्थो ऽयमन्वेष्टव्यो नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.20 ।।
explanation: You are learned in the scriptures and accomplished in intellect. O kings, this purpose of mine should be sought out by you, having assembled together.

shloka_text: तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे अवधानपरायणाः । उद्विग्नमनसः सर्वे किं नु राजाभिधास्यति ।। 7.44.21 ।।
explanation: As Kakutstha spoke thus, all of them, attentive and with agitated minds, wondered what the king would say.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 44 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the forty-fourth chapter.

shloka_text: तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीनचेतसाम् । उवाच वाक्यं काकुत्स्थो मुखेन परिशुष्यता ।। 7.45.1 ।।
explanation: To all of them, who were seated and dejected, Kakutstha spoke a word, his face parched.

shloka_text: सर्वे शृणुत भद्रं वो मा कुरुध्वं मनो ऽन्यथा । पौराणां मम सीतायां यादृशी वर्तते कथा ।। 7.45.2 ।।
explanation: All of you listen, may good fortune be upon you. Do not let your minds be otherwise. (This is) the kind of talk that exists among the citizens concerning my Sita.

shloka_text: पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च । वर्तते मयि बीभत्सा सा मे मर्माणि कृन्तति ।। 7.45.3 ।।
explanation: A very great scandal from the citizens and also from the people of the country exists. A disgust concerning me is present; that cuts my vital parts.

shloka_text: अहं किल कुले जात इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । सीता ऽपि सत्कुले जाता जनकानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.45.4 ।।
explanation: I was indeed born in the family of the great-souled Ikshvakus. Sita also was born in the noble family of the great-souled Janakas.

shloka_text: जानासि त्वं यथा सौम्य दण्डके विजने वने । रावणेन हृता सीता स च विध्वंसितो मया ।। 7.45.5 ।।
explanation: You know, O gentle one, how in the desolate Daṇḍaka forest, Sītā was abducted by Rāvaṇa, and he was destroyed by me.

shloka_text: तत्र मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना जनकस्य सुतां प्रति । अत्रोषितामिमां सीतामानयेयं कथं पुरीम् ।। 7.45.6 ।।
explanation: Then, a thought arose in my mind concerning Janaka's daughter. How should I bring this Sita, who has resided here, to the city?

shloka_text: प्रत्ययार्थं ततः सीता विवेश ज्वलनं तदा । प्रत्यक्षं तव सौमित्रे देवानां हव्यवाहनः । अपापां मैथिलीमाह वायुश्चाकाशगोचरः ।। 7.45.7 ।।
explanation: Then, for the sake of proof, Sita entered the fire at that time. In your presence, O Saumitri, and before the gods, Agni declared Maithili to be sinless, and so did Vayu, who moves in the sky.

shloka_text: चन्द्रादित्यौ च शंसेते सुराणां सन्निधौ पुरा । ऋषीणां चैव सर्वेषामपापां जनकात्मजाम् ।। 7.45.8 ।।
explanation: Formerly, the Moon and the Sun declared, in the presence of the gods and all the sages, Janaka's daughter to be sinless.

shloka_text: एवं शुद्धसमाचारा देवगन्धर्वसन्निधौ । लङ्काद्वीपे महेन्द्रेण मम हस्ते निवेशिता ।। 7.45.9 ।।
explanation: Thus, she of pure conduct was entrusted into my hand by Mahendra on the island of Lanka, in the presence of gods and gandharvas.

shloka_text: अन्तरात्मा च मे वेत्ति सीतां शुद्धां यशस्विनीम् । ततो गृहीत्वा वैदेहीमयोध्यामहमागतः ।। 7.45.10 ।।
explanation: And my inner self knows Sita to be pure and glorious. Therefore, having brought Vaidehi, I came to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: अयं तु मे महान्वादः शोकश्च हृदि वर्तते । पौरापवादः सुमहांस्तथा जनपदस्य च ।। 7.45.11 ।।
explanation: This great accusation, however, is upon me, and sorrow dwells in my heart. And a very great scandal from the citizens, as well as from the people of the land.

shloka_text: अकीर्तिर्यस्य गीयेत लोके भूतस्य कस्यचित् । पतत्येवाधमाँल्लोकान्यावच्छब्दः प्रकीर्त्यते ।। 7.45.12 ।।
explanation: If the ill-fame of any person is sung in the world, that person certainly falls to the lower worlds as long as that word (of infamy) is proclaimed.

shloka_text: अकीर्तिर्निन्द्यते देवैः कीर्तिर्लोकेषु पूज्यते । कीर्त्यर्थं तु समारम्भः सर्वेषां सुमहात्मनाम् ।। 7.45.13 ।।
explanation: Disrepute is condemned by the gods; fame is honored among people. Indeed, the undertakings of all great souls are for the sake of fame.

shloka_text: अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां युष्मान्वा पुरुषर्षभाः । अपवादभयाद्भीतः किं पुनर्जनकात्मजाम् ।। 7.45.14 ।।
explanation: O best among men, even I, fearful of public criticism, would abandon my life or even you. What then of Janaka's daughter?

shloka_text: तस्माद्भवन्तः पश्यन्तु पतितं शोकसागरे । नहि पश्याम्यहं भूतं किञ्चिद्दुःखमतो ऽधिकम् ।। 7.45.15 ।।
explanation: Therefore, you should behold me fallen into the ocean of sorrow. Indeed, I do not perceive any suffering greater than this.

shloka_text: श्वस्त्वं प्रभाते सौमित्रे सुमन्त्राधिष्ठितं रथम् । आरुह्य सीतामारोप्य विषयान्ते समुत्सृज ।। 7.45.16 ।।
explanation: Tomorrow morning, O son of Sumitra, you, having mounted the chariot driven by Sumantra, and having placed Sita upon it, abandon her at the end of the kingdom.

shloka_text: गङ्गायास्तु परे पारे वाल्मीकेस्तु महात्मनः । आश्रमो दिव्यसङ्काशस्तमसातीरमाश्रितः ।। 7.45.17 ।।
explanation: On the far bank of the Ganga, belonging to the great sage Valmiki, is a hermitage, divine in appearance, situated on the bank of the Tamasa.

shloka_text: तत्रैनां विजने देशे विसृज्य रघुनन्दन । शीघ्रमागच्छ भद्रं ते कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.45.18 ।।
explanation: O Raghunandana, having abandoned her there in a secluded place, come back quickly. May good fortune be to you. Obey my command.

shloka_text: न चास्मिन् प्रतिवक्तव्यः सीतां प्रति कथञ्चन । तस्मात्त्वं गच्छ सौमित्रे नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।। 7.45.19 ।।
explanation: And he should not be contradicted regarding Sita in any way. Therefore, you go, O son of Sumitra; no deliberation is to be made here.

shloka_text: अप्रीतिर्हि परा मह्यं त्वयेतत्प्रतिवारिते । शापिता हि मया यूयं भुजाभ्यां जीवितेन च ।। 7.45.20 ।।
explanation: For indeed, great displeasure will be mine if this is prevented by you, as I have made you swear by your arms and by your life.

shloka_text: ये मां वाक्यान्तरे ब्रूयुरनुनेतुं कथञ्चन । अहिता नाम ते नित्यं मदभीष्टविघातनात् ।। 7.45.21 ।।
explanation: Those who would speak to me with other words, somehow to persuade me, they are indeed always my enemies, because they obstruct my cherished desire.

shloka_text: मानयन्तु भवन्तो मां यदि मच्छासने स्थिताः । इतो ऽद्य नीयतां सीता कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.45.22 ।।
explanation: If you abide by my command, then honor me. Let Sita be taken from here today. Obey my word.

shloka_text: पूर्वमुक्तो ऽहमनया गङ्गातीरे ऽहमाश्रमान् । पश्येयमिति तस्याश्च कामः संवर्त्यतामयम् ।। 7.45.23 ।।
explanation: She had previously told me, "I wish to see hermitages on the bank of the Ganga." Let this desire of hers be fulfilled.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थो बाष्पेण पिहिताननः । प्रविवेश स धर्मात्मा भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः ।। 7.45.24 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, Kakutstha, his face veiled by tears, that righteous soul, entered, accompanied by his brothers.

shloka_text: शोकसंलग्नहृदयो निशश्वास यथा द्विपः ।। 7.45.25 ।।
explanation: With a heart engrossed in sorrow, he sighed like an elephant.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 45 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the forty-fifth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: ततो रजन्यां व्युष्टायां लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । सुमन्त्रमब्रवीद्वाक्यं मुखेन परिशुष्यता ।। 7.46.1 ।।
explanation: Then, when the night had dawned, Lakshmana, with a sorrowful mind, spoke a word to Sumantra, his face parched.

shloka_text: सारथे तुरगाञ्छीघ्रं योजयस्व रथोत्तमे । स्वास्तीर्णं राजभवनात्सीतायाश्चासनं कुरु ।। 7.46.2 ।।
explanation: O charioteer, quickly harness the horses to the excellent chariot. And prepare a well-cushioned seat for Sita from the royal palace.

shloka_text: सीता हि राजवचनादाश्रमं पुण्यकर्मणाम् । मया नेया महर्षीणां श्रीघ्रमानीयतां रथः ।। 7.46.3 ।।
explanation: Indeed, by the king's command, Sita is to be taken by me to the hermitage of the great sages who perform meritorious deeds. Let the chariot be brought quickly.

shloka_text: सुमन्त्रस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा युक्तं परमवाजिभिः । रथं सुरुचिरप्रख्यं स्वास्तीर्णं सुखशय्यया ।। 7.46.4 ।।
explanation: Sumantra, having said "so be it," yoked the chariot, which was harnessed with excellent horses, splendidly radiant, and well-furnished with a comfortable bed.

shloka_text: आनीयोवाच सौमित्रिं मित्राणां मानवर्धनम् । रथो ऽयं समनुप्राप्तो यत्कार्यं क्रियतां प्रभो ।। 7.46.5 ।।
explanation: He brought and said to Saumitri, the enhancer of the honor of friends: "This chariot has arrived. O Lord, let whatever needs to be done, be done."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुमन्त्रेण राजवेश्मनि लक्ष्मणः । प्रविश्य सीतामासाद्य व्याजहार नरर्षभः ।। 7.46.6 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Sumantra, Lakshmana, the foremost of men, having entered the royal palace and approached Sita, spoke.

shloka_text: त्वया किलैष नृपतिर्वरं वै याचितः प्रभुः । नृपेण च प्रतिज्ञातमाज्ञप्तश्चाश्रमं प्रति ।। 7.46.7 ।।
explanation: Indeed, this king, the lord, was asked for a boon by you. And it was promised by the king, and he was commanded to the hermitage.

shloka_text: गङ्गीतीरे मया देवि ऋषीणामाश्रमाञ्छुभान् । शीघ्रं गत्वा तु वैदेहि शासनात्पार्थिवस्य नः । अरण्ये मुनिभिर्जुष्टे अपनेया भविष्यसि ।। 7.46.8 ।।
explanation: O Devi, O Vaidehi, by me, by the command of our king, having quickly gone to the auspicious hermitages of the sages on the bank of the Ganga, you will be abandoned in the forest frequented by sages.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे गमनं चाप्यरोचयत् ।। 7.46.9 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the magnanimous Lakshmana, Vaidehi attained incomparable joy and also desired the journey.

shloka_text: वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च । गृहीत्वा तानि वैदेही गमनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.46.10 ।।
explanation: And taking those costly garments and various jewels, Vaidehi began to depart.

shloka_text: इमानि मुनिपत्नीनां दास्याम्याभरणान्हम् । वस्त्राणि च महार्हाणि धनानि विविधानि च ।। 7.46.11 ।।
explanation: I will give these ornaments to the wives of the sages, and precious clothes, and various riches.

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा रथमारोप्य मैथिलीम् । प्रययौ शीघ्रतुरगै रामस्याज्ञामनुस्मरन् ।। 7.46.12 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, having said "so be it," and having placed Maithili upon the chariot, departed with swift horses, remembering Rama's command.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च तदा सीता लक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मिवर्धनम् । अशुभानि बहून्येव पश्यामि रघुनन्दन ।। 7.46.13 ।।
explanation: And then Sita spoke to Lakshmana, the enhancer of prosperity: "O scion of Raghu, I see many inauspicious omens."

shloka_text: नयनं मे स्फुरत्यद्य गात्रोत्कम्पश्च जायते । हृदयं चैव सौमित्रे अस्वस्थमिव लक्षये ।। 7.46.14 ।।
explanation: My eye is twitching today, and a trembling of my limbs is occurring. And indeed, O Saumitri, I perceive my heart as if it is uneasy.

shloka_text: औत्सुक्यं परमं चापि अधृतिश्च परा मम । शून्यामेव च पश्यामि पृथिवीं पृथुलोचन ।। 7.46.15 ।।
explanation: My longing is supreme, and my restlessness is extreme. I see the earth as utterly desolate, O wide-eyed one.

shloka_text: अपि स्वस्ति भवेत्तस्य भ्रातुस्ते भ्रातृवत्सल । श्वश्रूणां चैव मे वीर सर्वासामविशेषतः ।। 7.46.16 ।।
explanation: O brother-loving one, may there be well-being for your brother, and indeed, O hero, for all my mothers-in-law, especially.

shloka_text: पुरे जनपदे चैव कुशलं प्राणिनामपि । इत्यञ्जलिकृता सीता देवता अभ्ययाचत ।। 7.46.17 ।।
explanation: Sita, with folded hands, thus prayed to the deities for the well-being of all living beings in the city and in the countryside.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणो ऽर्थं ततः श्रुत्वा शिरसा वन्द्य मैथिलीम् । शिवमित्यब्रवीद्धृष्टो हृदयेन विशुष्यता ।। 7.46.18 ।।
explanation: Then Lakshmana, having heard the matter, bowed his head to Maithili and, though his heart was parched, he delightedly said, "Auspicious!"

shloka_text: ततो वासमुपागम्य गोमतीतीर आश्रमे । प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय सौमित्रिः सूतमब्रवीत् ।। 7.46.19 ।।
explanation: Then, having spent the night in a hermitage on the bank of the Gomati, Saumitri, having risen again in the morning, spoke to the charioteer.

shloka_text: योजयस्व रथं शीघ्रमद्य भागीरथीजलम् । शिरसा धारयिष्यामि त्र्यम्बकः पर्वते यथा ।। 7.46.20 ।।
explanation: Harness the chariot quickly today. I will bear the water of the Bhagirathi on my head, just as Tryambaka (Shiva) [bears it] on the mountain.

shloka_text: सो ऽश्वान् रज्वाथ चतुरो रथे युङ्क्त्वा मनोजवान् । आरोहस्वेति वैदेहीं सूतः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् ।। 7.46.21 ।।
explanation: Then, the charioteer, having yoked the four mind-swift horses to the chariot with reins, said to Vaidehi with folded hands, "Please ascend."

shloka_text: सा तु सूतस्य वचनादारुरोह रथोत्तमम् । सीता सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सुमन्त्रेण च धीमता ।। 7.46.22 ।।
explanation: Sita, at the charioteer's command, ascended the excellent chariot, along with Lakshmana and the wise Sumantra.

shloka_text: आससाद विशालाक्षी गङ्गां पापविनाशिनीम् । अथार्धदिवसं गत्वा भागीरथ्या जलाशयम् ।। 7.46.23 ।।
explanation: The wide-eyed one reached the sin-destroying Ganga, the waters of the Bhagirathi, after traveling for half a day.

shloka_text: निरीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणो दीनः प्ररुरोद महास्वनः ।। 7.46.24 ।।
explanation: Having seen, distressed Lakshmana wept with a great sound.

shloka_text: सीता तु परमायत्ता दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमातुरम् । उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञा किमिदं रुद्यते त्वया ।। 7.46.25 ।।
explanation: Sita, greatly distressed, having seen Lakshmana afflicted, the knower of dharma, spoke these words: "What is this being wept by you?"

shloka_text: जाह्नवीतीरमासाद्य चिराभिलषितं मम । हर्षकाले किमर्थं मां विषादयसि लक्ष्मण ।। 7.46.26 ।।
explanation: Having reached the bank of the Jahnavi, which was long desired by me, why do you make me sad, Lakshmana, at this time of joy?

shloka_text: नित्यं त्वं रामपार्श्वेषु वर्तसे पुरुषर्षभ । कच्चिद्विनाकृतस्तेन द्विरात्रं शोकमागतः ।। 7.46.27 ।।
explanation: You are always by Rama's side, O best among men. Have you perhaps been overcome with sorrow, separated from him for two nights?

shloka_text: ममापि दयितो रामो जीवितादपि लक्ष्मण । न चाहमेवं शोचामि मैवं त्वं बालिशो भव ।। 7.46.28 ।।
explanation: Rama is dearer to me than life itself, O Lakshmana. Yet I do not grieve in this manner. Do not be so foolish.

shloka_text: तारयस्व च मां गङ्गां दर्शयस्व च तापसान् । ततो मुनिभ्यो दास्यामि वांसास्याभरणानि च ।। 7.46.29 ।।
explanation: Please ferry me across the Ganga and show me the ascetics. Then I will give clothes and ornaments to the sages.

shloka_text: ततः कृत्वा महर्षीणां यथार्हमभिवादनम् । तत्र चैकां निशामुष्य यास्यामस्तां पुरीं पुनः ।। 7.46.30 ।।
explanation: Then, having offered due salutations to the great sages, and having stayed there for one night, we shall go to that city again.

shloka_text: ममापि पद्मपत्राक्षं सिंहोरस्कं कृशोदरम् । त्वरते हि मनो द्रष्टुं रामं रमयतां वरम् ।। 7.46.31 ।।
explanation: Indeed, my mind also yearns to see Rama, who has eyes like lotus petals, a lion-like chest, and a slender waist, the best among those who delight.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रमृज्य नयने शुभे । नाविकानाह्वयामास लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा ।। 7.46.32 ।।
explanation: Having heard her words, Lakshmana, the slayer of enemy heroes, wiped his beautiful eyes and summoned the boatmen.

shloka_text: इयं च सज्जा नौश्चेति दाशाः प्राञ्जलयो ऽब्रुवन् ।। 7.46.33 ।।
explanation: "This boat is ready," the boatmen said with folded hands.

shloka_text: तितीर्षुर्लक्ष्मणो गङ्गां शुभां नावमुपारुहत् । गङ्गां सन्तारयामास लक्ष्मणस्तां समाहितः ।। 7.46.34 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, desiring to cross the Ganga, boarded an auspicious boat. Lakshmana, being attentive, ferried her across the Ganga.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 46 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (sage-composed), glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the forty-sixth chapter.

shloka_text: अथ नावं सुविस्तीर्णां नैषादीं राघवानुजः । आरुरोह समायुक्तां पूर्वमारोप्य मैथिलीम् ।। 7.47.1 ।।
explanation: Then, Rama's younger brother, having first placed Maithili, boarded the very spacious and well-equipped boat of the Niṣāda.

shloka_text: सुमन्त्रं चैव सरथं स्थीयतामिति लक्ष्मणः । उवाच शोकसन्तप्तः प्रयाहीति च नाविकम् ।। 7.47.2 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, distressed by sorrow, said to Sumantra, "Stay with the chariot," and to the boatman, "Depart."

shloka_text: ततस्तीरमुपागम्य भागीरथ्याः स लक्ष्मणः । उवाच मैथिलीं वाक्यं प्राञ्जलिर्बाष्पसम्प्लुतः ।। 7.47.3 ।।
explanation: Then, having reached the bank of the Bhagirathi, Lakshmana, with folded hands and overwhelmed with tears, spoke to Maithili.

shloka_text: हृद्गतं मे महच्छल्यं यस्मादार्येण धीमता । अस्मिन्निमित्ते वैदेहि लोकस्य वचनीकृतः ।। 7.47.4 ।।
explanation: A great thorn has entered my heart, O Vaidehi, because of which I, the wise one, have been made an object of public reproach in this matter.

shloka_text: श्रेयो हि मरणं मे ऽद्य मृत्युर्वा यत्परं भवेत् । न चास्मिन्नीदृशे कार्ये नियोज्यो लोकनिन्दिते ।। 7.47.5 ।।
explanation: Indeed, death is preferable for me today, or whatever ultimate death may come. And I should not be engaged in such a task as this, which is condemned by people.

shloka_text: प्रसीद च न मे पापं कर्तुमर्हसि शोभने । इत्यञ्जलिकृतो भूमौ निपपात स लक्ष्मणः ।। 7.47.6 ।।
explanation: Be pleased, O beautiful one, and you should not commit a wrong against me. Saying this, Lakshmana, with folded hands, fell down on the ground.

shloka_text: रुदन्तं प्राञ्जलिं दृष्ट्वा काङ्क्षन्तं मृत्युमात्मनः । मैथिली भृशसंविग्ना लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.47.7 ।।
explanation: Seeing him crying, with folded hands, and desiring his own death, Maithili, greatly distressed, spoke these words to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: किमिदं नावगच्छामि ब्रूहि तत्त्वेन लक्ष्मण । पश्यामि त्वां न च स्वस्थमपि क्षेमं महीपतेः ।। 7.47.8 ।।
explanation: What is this? I do not understand. Tell me the truth, Lakshmana. I see you are not well, and is the king also well?

shloka_text: शापितो ऽसि नरेन्द्रेण यत्त्वं सन्तापमागतः । तद्ब्रूयाः सन्निधौ मह्यमहमाज्ञापयामि ते ।। 7.47.9 ।।
explanation: You have been cursed by the king, and you have fallen into distress. Tell me that in my presence. I command you.

shloka_text: वैदेह्या चोद्यमानस्तु लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । अवाङ्मुखो बाष्पकलं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.47.10 ।।
explanation: Being urged by Vaidehi, Lakshmana, with a distressed mind, his face downcast, spoke these words with a voice choked by tears.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा परिषदो मध्ये ह्यपवादं सुदारुणम् । पुरे जनपदे चैव त्वत्कृते जनकात्मजे । रामः सन्तप्तहृदयो मा निवेद्य गृहं गतः ।। 7.47.11 ।।
explanation: Having heard the very terrible slander in the midst of the assembly, in the city and in the countryside, on your account, O daughter of Janaka, Rama, with a tormented heart, went home without revealing it.

shloka_text: न तानि वचनीयानि मया देवि तवाग्रतः । यानि राज्ञा हृदि न्यस्तान्यमर्षात्पृष्ठतः कृतः ।। 7.47.12 ।।
explanation:

"अमर्षात् पृष्ठतः कृतः" - (something) was made

shloka_text: सा त्वं त्यक्ता नृपतिना निर्दोषा मम सन्निधौ । पौरापवादभीतेन ग्राह्यं देवि न ते ऽन्यथा ।। 7.47.13 ।।
explanation: You, though abandoned by the king, blameless in my presence, due to his fear of public criticism, O Devi, must be accepted; there is no other way for you.

shloka_text: आश्रमान्तेषु च मया त्यक्तव्या त्वं भविष्यसि । राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तवेदं किल दौर्हृदम् ।। 7.47.14 ।।
explanation: And you will be abandoned by me at the edge of the hermitages. This is indeed your longing, having understood the king's command.

shloka_text: तदेतज्जाह्नवीतीरे ब्रह्मर्षीणां तपोवनम् । पुण्यं च रमणीयं च मा विषादं कृथाः शुभे ।। 7.47.15 ।।
explanation: This is the hermitage of the Brahmarishis on the bank of the Jahnavi, both sacred and delightful. Do not grieve, O auspicious one.

shloka_text: राज्ञो दशरथस्येष्टः पितुर्मे मुनिपुङ्गवः । सखा परमको विप्रो वाल्मीकिः सुमहायशाः ।। 7.47.16 ।।
explanation: Valmiki, the greatly illustrious, is the foremost among sages, a very great Brahmin friend, beloved of my father, King Dasharatha.

shloka_text: पादच्छायामुपागम्य सुखमस्य महात्मनः । उपवासपरैकाग्रा वस त्वं जनकात्मजे ।। 7.47.17 ।।
explanation: O daughter of Janaka, having happily sought the protection of this great soul, you should dwell here, solely devoted to fasting and with a single mind.

shloka_text: पतिव्रतात्वमास्थाय रामं कृत्वा सदा हृदि । श्रेयस्ते परमं देवि तथा कृत्वा भविष्यति ।। 7.47.18 ।।
explanation: By adopting the state of a devoted wife and always keeping Rama in your heart, your supreme welfare, O Goddess, will thus be achieved.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 47 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha, the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the forty-seventh chapter.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दारुणं जनकात्मजा । परं विषादमागम्य वैदेही निपपात ह ।। 7.48.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard Lakshmana's harsh words, Janaka's daughter, Vaidehi, overcome with extreme sorrow, fell down.

shloka_text: सा मुहूर्तमिवासञ्ज्ञा बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणा । लक्ष्मणं दीनया वाचा उवाच जनकात्मजा ।। 7.48.2 ।।
explanation: For a moment, as if unconscious, her eyes agitated by tears, Janaka's daughter spoke to Lakshmana with a piteous voice.

shloka_text: मामिकेयं तनुर्नूनं सृष्टा दुःखाय लक्ष्मण । धात्रा यस्यास्तथा मे ऽद्य दुःखमूर्तिः प्रदृश्यते ।। 7.48.3 ।।
explanation: This body of mine, O Lakshmana, was surely created for sorrow by the Creator, as its very form appears to me today as an embodiment of misery.

shloka_text: किं नु पापं कृतं पूर्वं को वा दारैर्वियोजितः । या ऽहं शुद्धसमाचारा त्यक्ता नृपतिना सती ।। 7.48.4 ।।
explanation: What sin was committed previously, or who was separated from his wife, that I, of pure conduct and chaste, have been abandoned by the king?

shloka_text: पुरा ऽहमाश्रमे वासं रामपादानुवर्तिनी । अनुरुध्यापि सौमित्रे दुःखे च परिवर्तिनी ।। 7.48.5 ।।
explanation: Formerly, I resided in the hermitage, following Rama's feet. O son of Sumitra, even though devoted, I was also dwelling in sorrow.

shloka_text: सा कथं ह्याश्रमे सौम्य वत्स्यामि विजनीकृता । आख्यास्यामि च कस्याहं दुःखं दुःखपरायणा ।। 7.48.6 ।।
explanation: How indeed shall I, made desolate, live in the hermitage, O gentle one? And to whom shall I, immersed in sorrow, narrate my sorrow?

shloka_text: किं नु वक्ष्यामि मुनिषु कर्म वा सत्कृतं च किम् । कस्मिंश्चित् कारणे त्यक्ता राघवेण महात्मना ।। 7.48.7 ।।
explanation: What indeed shall I say to the sages, or what meritorious deed have I performed, since I have been abandoned by the great-souled Raghava for some reason?

shloka_text: न खल्वद्यैव सौमित्रे जीवितं जाह्नवीजले । त्यजेयं राजवंशस्तु भर्तुर्मे परिहास्यते ।। 7.48.8 ।।
explanation: O Saumitri, I would certainly not abandon my life in the waters of the Ganga today itself, for then my husband's royal lineage would be ridiculed.

shloka_text: यथाज्ञं कुरु सोमित्रे त्यज मां दुःखभागिनीम् । निदेशे स्थीयतां राज्ञः शृणु चेदं वचो मम ।। 7.48.9 ।।
explanation: Do as commanded, O son of Sumitra. Abandon me, who is destined for sorrow. Abide by the king's command, and listen to this word of mine.

shloka_text: श्वश्रूणामविशेषेण प्राञ्जलिप्रग्रहेण च । शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य चरणौ कुशलं ब्रूहि पार्थिवम् ।। 7.48.10 ।।
explanation: Having bowed down with your head to the feet of the mothers-in-law without distinction, and with folded hands and reverence, tell the king of their well-being.

shloka_text: शिरसा ऽभिनतो ब्रूयाः सर्वासामेव लक्ष्मण । वक्तव्यश्चापि नृपतिर्धर्मेषु सुसमाहितः ।। 7.48.11 ।।
explanation: O Lakshmana, you should speak to all of them, bowing your head humbly. And the king, who is well-attentive to matters of righteousness, should also be addressed.

shloka_text: जानासि च यथा शुद्धा सीता तत्त्वेन राघव । भक्त्या च परया युक्ता हिता च तव नित्यशः ।। 7.48.12 ।।
explanation: And you know, O Raghava, how truly pure Sita is, and that she is endowed with supreme devotion and is always beneficial to you.

shloka_text: अहं त्यक्ता त्वया वीर अयशोभीरुणा जने । यच्च ते वचनीयं स्यादपवादसमुत्थितम् । मया च परिहर्तव्यं त्वं हि मे परमा गतिः ।। 7.48.13 ।।
explanation: I was abandoned by you, O hero, who feared dishonor among people. And whatever blame might arise from calumny against you, that must be avoided by me, for you are indeed my ultimate refuge.

shloka_text: वक्तव्यश्चेति नृपतिर्धमेण सुसमाहितः । यथा भ्रातृषु वर्तेथास्तथा पौरेषु नित्यदा ।। 7.48.14 ।।
explanation: And thus the king, steadfast in righteousness, should be told: "Just as you behave towards your brothers, so should you always behave towards your citizens."

shloka_text: परमो ह्येष धर्मस्ते तस्मात्कीर्तिरनुत्तमा ।। 7.48.15 ।।
explanation: For this is your supreme duty, and from it comes unsurpassed glory.

shloka_text: यत्तु पौरजनो राजन्धर्मेण समवाप्नुयात् । अहं तु नानुशोचामि स्वशरीरं नरर्षभ ।। 7.48.16 ।।
explanation: O King, whatever the citizens may obtain through righteousness, I, O best among men, do not lament for my own body.

shloka_text: यथापवादं पौराणां तथैव रघुनन्दन । पतिर्हि देवता नार्याः पतिर्बन्धुः पतिर्गुरुः ।। 7.48.17 ।।
explanation: According to the accusation of the citizens, so it is, O Raghunandana. For a woman, the husband is indeed the deity, the husband is the kinsman, the husband is the preceptor.

shloka_text: प्राणैरपि प्रियं तस्माद्भर्तुः कार्यं विशेषतः । इति मद्वचनाद्रामो वक्तव्यो मम सङ्ग्रहः । निरीक्ष्य मा ऽद्य गच्छ त्वमृतुकालातिवर्तिनीम् ।। 7.48.18 ।।

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवन्त्यां सीतायां लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य धरणीं व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।। 7.48.19 ।।
explanation: As Sita spoke thus, Lakshmana, with a dejected mind, bowed his head to the ground and could not utter a word.

shloka_text: प्रदक्षिणं च तां कृत्वा रुदन्नेव महास्वनः । ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तामाह किं मां वक्ष्यसि शोभने ।। 7.48.20 ।।
explanation: And having circumambulated her, weeping loudly, he pondered for a moment and said to her, "What will you say to me, O beautiful one?"

shloka_text: दृष्टपूर्वं न ते रूपं पादौ दृष्टौ तवानघे । कथमत्र हि पश्यामि रामेण रहितां वने ।। 7.48.21 ।।
explanation: Your form has not been seen before. Your feet have been seen, O sinless one. How can I see you here in the forest, separated from Rama?

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा तां नमस्कृत्य पुनर्नावमुपारुहत् । आरुह्य च पुनर्नावं नाविकं चाभ्यचोदयत् ।। 7.48.22 ।।
explanation: Having said this, and having saluted her, he again boarded the boat. And having boarded the boat again, he urged the boatman.

shloka_text: स गत्वा चोत्तरं तीरं शोकभारसमन्वितः । सम्मूढ इव दुःखेन रथमध्यारुहद्द्रुतम् ।। 7.48.23 ।।
explanation: He, having gone to the northern bank, overwhelmed by the burden of sorrow, and as if bewildered by grief, quickly mounted the chariot.

shloka_text: मुहुर्मुहुः परावृत्य दृष्ट्वा सीतामनाथवत् । चेष्टन्तीं परतीरस्थां लक्ष्मणः प्रययावथ ।। 7.48.24 ।।
explanation: Repeatedly turning back, Lakshmana saw Sita, helpless and struggling on the opposite bank. Then he departed.

shloka_text: दूरस्थं रथमालोक्य लक्ष्मणं च मुहूर्मुहुः । निरीक्षमाणां तूद्विग्नां सीतां शोकः समाविशत् ।। 7.48.25 ।।
explanation: Seeing the distant chariot, and repeatedly looking at Lakshmana, sorrow overcame Sita, who was distressed.

shloka_text: सा दुःखभारावनता यशस्विनी यशोधना नाथमपश्यती सती । रुरोद सा बर्हिणनादिते वने महास्वनं दुःखपरायणा सती ।। 7.48.26 ।।
explanation: Bowed down by the weight of sorrow, that glorious one, whose wealth was fame, not seeing her lord, she cried loudly in the forest resounding with peacock calls, being overwhelmed by sorrow.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 48 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana composed by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the forty-eighth chapter.

shloka_text: सीतां तु रुदतीं दृष्ट्वा ते तत्र मुनिदारकाः । प्राद्रवन्यत्र भगवानास्ते वाल्मीकिरुग्रधीः ।। 7.49.1 ।।
explanation: Seeing Sita weeping, those young ascetics there ran to where the venerable Valmiki, of keen intellect, was.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य मुनेः पादौ मुनिपुत्रा महर्षये । सर्वं निवेदयामासुस्तस्यास्तु रुदितस्वनम् ।। 7.49.2 ।।
explanation: Having saluted the feet of the sage, the sons of the sage reported everything, including her lamentation, to the great sage.

shloka_text: अदृष्टपूर्वा भगवन्कस्याप्येषा महात्मनः । पत्नी श्रीरिव सम्मोहाद्विरौति विकृतानना ।। 7.49.3 ।।
explanation: O Lord, this wife of some great soul, never seen before, with a distorted face, cries out due to great delusion, like Shri.

shloka_text: भगवन्साधु पश्य त्वं देवतामिव खाच्च्युताम् । नद्यास्तु तीरे भगवन्वरस्त्री कापि दुःखिता ।। 7.49.4 ।।
explanation: O Lord, look carefully, she is like a goddess fallen from the sky. O Lord, on the river bank, there is some distressed beautiful woman.

shloka_text: दृष्टास्माभिः प्ररुदिता दृढं शोकपरायणा । अनर्हा दुःखशोकाभ्यामेकां दीनां ह्यनाथवत् ।। 7.49.5 ।।
explanation: We saw her weeping profusely, deeply immersed in sorrow. Undeserving of such pain and grief, she was alone and miserable, indeed like an orphan.

shloka_text: न ह्येनां मानुषीं विद्मः सत्क्रिया ऽस्याः प्रयुज्यताम् । आश्रमस्याविदूरे च त्वामियं शरणं गता ।। 7.49.6 ।।
explanation: Indeed, we do not know her to be human. Let proper rites be performed for her. And she has come to you for refuge, not far from the hermitage.

shloka_text: त्रातारमिच्छते साध्वी भगवंस्त्रातुमर्हसि । तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य धर्मवित् । तपसा लब्धचक्षुष्मान् प्राद्रवद्यत्र मैथिली ।। 7.49.7 ।।
explanation: The virtuous woman desires a protector, O Lord, you ought to protect. But having heard their words, and having ascertained with his intellect, the knower of dharma, who had obtained sight through penance, rushed to where Maithili was.

shloka_text: तं प्रयान्तमभिप्रेत्य शिष्या ह्येनं महामतिम् । तं तु देशमभि प्रेत्य किञ्चित्पद्भ्यां महामतिः ।। 7.49.8 ।।
explanation: Having perceived that great-minded one going, the disciples indeed (followed) him. But having perceived that place, the great-minded one (proceeded) a little with his feet.

shloka_text: अर्घ्यमादाय रुचिरं जाह्नवीतीरमागमत् । ददर्श राघवस्येष्टां सीतां पत्नीमनाथवत् ।। 7.49.9 ।।
explanation: Taking the beautiful offering, he came to the bank of the Jahnavi. He saw Sita, Raghava's beloved wife, like one without a protector.

shloka_text: तां सीतां शोकभारार्तां वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं ह्लादयन्निव तेजसा ।। 7.49.10 ।।
explanation: To that Sita, afflicted by the burden of sorrow, Valmiki, the foremost among sages, spoke sweet words, as if comforting her with his spiritual power.

shloka_text: स्नुषा दशरथस्य त्वं रामस्य महिषी प्रिया । जनकस्य सुता राज्ञः स्वागतं ते पतिव्रते ।। 7.49.11 ।।
explanation: You are the daughter-in-law of Dasharatha, the beloved queen of Rama. You are the daughter of King Janaka. Welcome to you, O chaste wife.

shloka_text: आयान्ती चासि विज्ञाता मया धर्मसमाधिना । कारणं चैव सर्वं मे हृदयेनोपलक्षितम् ।। 7.49.12 ।।
explanation: You, approaching, have been recognized by me through my righteous contemplation. And indeed, all the reason has been perceived by my heart.

shloka_text: तव चैव महाभागे विदितं मम तत्त्वतः । सर्वं च विदितं मह्यं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते ।। 7.49.13 ।।
explanation: And indeed, O greatly fortunate one, your true nature is known to me. And everything that exists in the three worlds is known to me.

shloka_text: अपापां वेद्मि सीते त्वां तपोलब्धेन चक्षुषा । विस्रब्धा भव वैदेहि साम्प्रतं मयि वर्तसे ।। 7.49.14 ।।
explanation: O Sita, I know you are sinless with the eye obtained through my penance. O Vaidehi, be confident; you are now with me.

shloka_text: आश्रमस्याविदूरे मे तापस्यस्तपसि स्थिताः । तास्त्वां वत्से यथा वत्सं पालयिष्यन्ति नित्यशः ।। 7.49.15 ।।
explanation: Not far from my hermitage, female ascetics devoted to penance reside. O child, they will always protect you as they would a calf.

shloka_text: इदमर्ध्यं प्रतीच्छ त्वं विस्रब्धा विगतज्वरा । यथा स्वगृहमभ्येत्य विषादं चैव मा कृथाः ।। 7.49.16 ।।
explanation: Accept this offering, being confident and free from distress. And when you return to your own home, do not feel any sorrow.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं सीता मुनेः परममद्भुतम् । शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य चरणौ तथेत्याह कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.49.17 ।।
explanation: Upon hearing the sage's most wonderful words, Sita bowed her head at his feet and, with folded hands, said, "So be it."

shloka_text: तं प्रयान्तं मुनिं सीता प्राञ्जलिः पृष्ठतो ऽन्वगात् ।। 7.49.18 ।।
explanation: Sita, with folded hands, followed the departing sage from behind.

shloka_text: तं दृष्ट्वा मुनिमायान्तं वैदेह्या मुनिपत्नयः । उपाजग्मुर्मुदा युक्ता वचनं चेदमब्रुवन् ।। 7.49.19 ।।
explanation: Seeing that sage approaching with Vaidehi, the wives of the sages, filled with joy, came near and spoke these words.

shloka_text: स्वागतं ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ चिरस्यागमनं च ते । अभिवादयामस्त्वां सर्वा उच्यतां कि च कुर्महे ।। 7.49.20 ।।
explanation: Welcome to you, O best among sages! Your arrival is after a long time. We all salute you. Please tell us what we should do.

shloka_text: तासां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिरिदमब्रवीत् । सीतेयं समनुप्राप्ता पत्नी रामस्य धीमतः ।। 7.49.21 ।।
explanation: Having heard their words, Valmiki said this: "This is Sita, the wife of the wise Rama, who has arrived."

shloka_text: स्नुषा दशरथस्यैषा जनकस्य सुता सती । अपापा पतिना त्यक्ता परिपाल्या मया सदा ।। 7.49.22 ।।
explanation: This daughter-in-law of Dasharatha, the daughter of Janaka, is chaste and sinless. Though abandoned by her husband, she must always be protected by me.

shloka_text: इमां भवन्त्यः(?) पश्यन्तु स्नेहेन परमेण हि । गौरवान्मम वाक्याच्च पूज्या वो ऽस्तु विशेषतः ।। 7.49.23 ।।
explanation: May you all look upon her with supreme affection. And may she be especially worthy of your respect, both out of reverence and by my word.

shloka_text: मुहुर्मुहुश्च वैदेहीं प्रणिधाय महायशाः । स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः पुनरायान्महातपाः ।। 7.49.24 ।।
explanation: The greatly renowned, great ascetic, having repeatedly fixed his mind on Vaidehi, returned again to his own hermitage, surrounded by his disciples.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 49 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the forty-ninth chapter.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु मैथिलीं सीतामाश्रमे सम्प्रवेशिताम् । सन्तापमगमद्घोरं लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः ।। 7.50.1 ।।
explanation: Having seen Maithili Sita brought into the hermitage, Lakshmana, with a distressed mind, experienced terrible grief.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च महातेजाः सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रसारथिम् । सीतासन्तापजं दुःखं पश्य रामस्य सारथे ।। 7.50.2 ।।
explanation: And the greatly effulgent one said to Sumantra, the wise charioteer: "O charioteer, behold Rama's sorrow born of Sita's distress."

shloka_text: ततो दुःखतरं किं नु राघवस्य भविष्यति । पत्नीं शुद्धसमाचारां विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम् ।। 7.50.3 ।।
explanation: What indeed will be more sorrowful for Rama than that, having abandoned Janaka's daughter, his wife of pure conduct?

shloka_text: व्यक्तं दैवादहं मन्ये राघवस्य विना भवम् । वैदेह्या सारथे नित्यं दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.50.4 ।।
explanation: O charioteer, I clearly believe that the separation of Rama and Vaidehi is due to destiny. Indeed, destiny is always insurmountable.

shloka_text: यो हि देवान्सगन्धर्वानसुरान्सह राक्षसैः । निहन्याद्राघवः क्रुद्धः स दैवमनुवर्तते ।। 7.50.5 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he who, enraged, would destroy the gods, along with the Gandharvas, Asuras, and Rakshasas, that Raghava follows destiny.

shloka_text: पुरा रामः पितुर्वाक्याद्दण्डके विजने वने । उषित्वा नव वर्षाणि पञ्च चैव महावने ।। 7.50.6 ।।
explanation: Formerly, Rama, by his father's command, having resided in the desolate Dandaka forest for nine years and five years in the great forest.

shloka_text: ततो दुःखतरं भूयः सीताया विप्रवासनम् । पौराणां वचनं श्रुत्वा नृशंसं प्रतिभाति मे ।। 7.50.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the citizens, the banishment of Sita appears to me to be even more painful and cruel than that.

shloka_text: को नु धर्माश्रयः सूत कर्मण्यस्मिन्यशोहरे । मैथिलीं प्रतिसम्प्राप्तः पौरैर्हीनार्थवादिभिः ।। 7.50.8 ।।
explanation: O charioteer, who indeed is the righteous person who, in this reputation-destroying act concerning Maithili, has been approached by citizens speaking words devoid of substance?

shloka_text: एता वाचो बहुविधाः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणभाषिताः । सुमन्त्रः श्रद्धया प्राज्ञो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.50.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard these various words spoken by Lakshmana, the wise Sumantra, with faith, spoke this statement.

shloka_text: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यः सौमित्रे मैथिलीं प्रति । दृष्टमेतत्पुरा विप्रैः पितुस्ते लक्ष्मणाग्रतः ।। 7.50.10 ।।
explanation: O Saumitri, you should not grieve for Maithili. This was seen before by Brahmins in the presence of your father, O Lakshmana.

shloka_text: भविष्यति दृढं रामो दुःखप्रायो ऽपि सौख्यभाक् । प्राप्स्यते च महाबाहुर्विप्रयोगं प्रियैर्ध्रुवम् ।। 7.50.11 ।।
explanation: Rama, though predominantly sorrowful, will certainly partake in happiness. And the mighty-armed one will surely experience separation from his beloved ones.

shloka_text: त्वां चैव मैथिलीं चैव शत्रुघ्नभरतावुभौ । सन्त्यजिष्यति धर्मात्मा कालेन महता महान् ।। 7.50.12 ।।
explanation: The great and righteous one will abandon you, Maithili, and both Shatrughna and Bharata after a long time.

shloka_text: इदं त्वयि न वक्तव्यं सौमित्रे भरते ऽपि वा । राज्ञा वो व्याहृतं वाक्यं दुर्वासा यदुवाच ह ।। 7.50.13 ।।
explanation: This should not be spoken to you, O Saumitri, or even to Bharata. The word which Durvasa spoke was spoken by the king to you all.

shloka_text: महाजनसमीपे च मम चैव नरर्षभ । ऋषिणा व्याहृतं वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्य च सन्निधौ ।। 7.50.14 ।।
explanation: O best among men, a statement was uttered by the sage and indeed by me, in the presence of great people and in the presence of Vasiṣṭha.

shloka_text: ऋषेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा मामाह पुरुषर्षभः । सूत न क्वचिदेवं ते वक्तव्यं जनसन्निधौ ।। 7.50.15 ।।
explanation: Having heard the sage's words, the best among men said to me: "O Sūta, this should never be spoken by you in the presence of people."

shloka_text: तस्याहं लोकपालस्य वाक्यं तत्सुसमाहितः । नैव जात्वनृतं कार्यमिति मे सौम्य दर्शनम् ।। 7.50.16 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, I, being very attentive to that word of the protector of the world, should never utter a falsehood; this is my view.

shloka_text: सर्वथैव न वक्तव्यं मया सौम्य तवाग्रतः । यदि ते श्रवणे श्रद्धा श्रूयतां रघुनन्दन ।। 7.50.17 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, I should absolutely not speak this before you. If you have earnestness in hearing, then listen, O Raghunandana.

shloka_text: यद्यप्यहं नरेन्द्रेण रहस्यं श्रावितः पुरा । तथाप्युदाहरिष्यामि दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.50.18 ।।
explanation: Although I was formerly told a secret by the king, still I will speak it out, for destiny is indeed insurmountable.

shloka_text: येनेदमीदृशं प्राप्तं दुःखं शोकसमन्वितम् । न त्वया भरते वाच्यं शत्रुघ्नस्यापि सन्निधौ ।। 7.50.19 ।।
explanation: You should not tell Bharata about this kind of sorrow, accompanied by grief, which has been experienced, nor even in the presence of Shatrughna.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य गम्भीरार्थपदं महत् । तथ्यं ब्रूहीति सौमित्रिः सूतं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.50.20 ।।
explanation: Having heard his profound and weighty words, Saumitri then spoke to the charioteer, saying, "Speak the truth!"

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 50 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the fiftieth chapter.

shloka_text: तथा सञ्चोदितः सूतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । तद्वाक्यमृषिणा प्रोक्तं व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.51.1 ।।
explanation: Thus urged by the great-souled Lakshmana, the charioteer began to utter that speech spoken by the sage.

shloka_text: पुरा नाम्ना हि दुर्वासा अत्रेः पुत्रो महामुनिः । वसिष्ठस्याश्रमे पुण्ये वार्षिक्यं समुवास ह ।। 7.51.2 ।।
explanation: Formerly, indeed, the great sage Durvasa, son of Atri, resided for the annual retreat in the sacred hermitage of Vasishtha.

shloka_text: तमाश्रमं महातेजाः पिता ते सुमहायशाः । पुरोहितं महात्मानं दिदृक्षुरगमस्त्वयम् ।। 7.51.3 ।।
explanation: Your greatly effulgent and very famous father himself went to that hermitage, desirous of seeing the great-souled priest.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा सूर्यसङ्काशं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । उपविष्टं वसिष्ठस्य सव्यपार्श्वे महामुनिम् ।। 7.51.4 ।।
explanation: He, having seen the great sage, seated on Vasiṣṭha's left side, resembling the sun, as if blazing with splendor.

shloka_text: तौ मुनी तापसश्रेष्ठौ विनीतो ह्यभिवादयत् । स ताभ्यां पूजितो राजा स्वागतेनासनेन च ।।
explanation: The humble king greeted those two excellent ascetic sages. He was honored by them with a welcome and a seat.

shloka_text: पाद्येन फलमूलैश्च उवास मुनिभिः सह ।। 7.51.5 ।।
explanation: He lived with the sages, with fruits, roots, and water for the feet.

shloka_text: तेषां तत्रोपविष्टानां तास्ताः सुमधुराः कथाः । बभूवुः परमर्षीणां मध्यादित्यगते ऽहनि ।। 7.51.6 ।।
explanation: As those great sages sat there, various very sweet stories took place among them when the sun had passed midday.

shloka_text: ततः कथायां कस्याञ्चित्प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः । उवाच तं महात्मानमत्रेः पुत्रं तपोधनम् ।। 7.51.7 ।।
explanation: Then, in a certain discourse, the king, with folded hands and respectfully, spoke to that great-souled son of Atri, the ascetic.

shloka_text: भगवन्किं प्रमाणेन मम वंशो भविष्यति । किमायुश्च हि मे रामः पुत्राश्चान्ये किमायुषः ।। 7.51.8 ।।
explanation: O Lord, for how long will my lineage endure? And indeed, what will be the lifespan of my Rama, and what will be the lifespan of my other sons?

shloka_text: रामस्य च सुता ये स्युस्तेषामायुः कियद्भवेत् । काम्यया भगवन्बूहि वंशस्यास्य गतिं मम ।। 7.51.9 ।।
explanation: And what would be the lifespan of Rama's sons? O Lord, out of my desire, tell me the future of this lineage.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं राज्ञो दशरथस्य च । दुर्वासाः सुमहातेजा व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.51.10 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech spoken by King Dasharatha, Durvasa, of great splendor, began to speak.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्पुरावृत्तं तदा देवासुरे युधि । दैत्याः सुरैर्भर्त्स्यमाना भृगुपत्नीं समाश्रिताः ।। 7.51.11 ।।
explanation: Listen, O King, to an ancient event. At that time, in the war between the Devas and Asuras, the Daityas, being harassed by the Devas, took refuge with Bhṛgu's wife.

shloka_text: तया परिगृहीतांस्तान्दृष्ट्वा क्रुद्धः सुरेश्वरः । चक्रेण शितधारेण भृगुपत्न्याः शिरो ऽहरत् ।। 7.51.13 ।।
explanation: Having seen them protected by her, the enraged lord of the gods, with his sharp-edged discus, severed the head of Bhrigu's wife.

shloka_text: ततस्तां निहतां दृष्ट्वा पत्नीं भृगुकुलोद्वहः । शशाप सहसा क्रुद्धो विष्णुं रिपुकुलार्दनम् ।। 7.51.14 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen his wife slain, the leader of the Bhrigu lineage, enraged, suddenly cursed Vishnu, the destroyer of enemy clans.

shloka_text: यस्मादवध्यां मे पत्नीमवधीः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । तस्मात्त्वं मानुषे लोके जनिष्यसि जनार्दन ।। 7.51.15 ।।
explanation: Because you, maddened by rage, killed my inviolable wife, therefore you, O Janardana, will be born in the human world.

shloka_text: तत्र पत्नीवियोगं त्वं प्राप्स्यसे बहुवार्षिकम् ।। 7.51.16 ।।
explanation: There, you will experience separation from your wife for many years.

shloka_text: शापाभिहतचेतास्स स्वात्मना भावितो ऽभवत् ।। 7.51.17 ।।
explanation: He, whose mind was afflicted by the curse, became absorbed in his own self.

shloka_text: अर्चयामास तं देवं भृगुः शापेन पीडितः । तपसाराधितो देवो ह्यब्रवीद्भक्तवत्सलः । लोकानां संहितार्थं तु तं शापं ग्राह्यमुक्तवान् ।। 7.51.19 ।।
explanation: Bhrigu, afflicted by the curse, worshipped that deity. The god, propitiated by his penance and benevolent to his devotees, then spoke. For the welfare of the worlds, he declared that the curse should be accepted.

shloka_text: इति शप्तो महातेजा भृगुणा पूर्वजन्मनि । इहागतो हि पुत्रत्वं तव पार्थिवसत्तम ।। 7.51.20 ।।
explanation: Thus cursed by Bhrigu in a previous birth, that greatly effulgent one has indeed come here as your son, O best among kings.

shloka_text: राम इत्यभिविख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु मानद । तत्फलं प्राप्स्यते चापि भृगुशापकृतं महत् ।। 7.51.21 ।।
explanation: O giver of honor, Rama, renowned in the three worlds, will also obtain that great consequence brought about by Bhrigu's curse.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायाः पती रामो दीर्घकालं भविष्यति । सुखिनश्च समृद्धाश्च भविष्यन्त्यस्य ये ऽनुगाः ।। 7.51.22 ।।
explanation: Rama will be the lord of Ayodhya for a long time. His followers will be happy and prosperous.

shloka_text: दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च । रामो राज्यमुपासित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति ।। 7.51.23 ।।
explanation: Rama, having ruled the kingdom for eleven thousand years, will go to Brahmaloka.

shloka_text: समृद्धैश्चाश्वमेधैश्च इष्ट्वा परमदुर्जयः । राजवंशांश्च बहुशो बहून्संस्थापयिष्यति ।। 7.51.24 ।।
explanation: The supremely unconquerable one, having performed many prosperous Ashvamedha sacrifices, will establish many royal dynasties repeatedly.

shloka_text: द्वौ पुत्रौ तु भविष्येते सीतायां राघवस्य तु । अन्यत्र न त्वयोध्यायां सत्यमेतन्नसंशयः ।। 7.51.25 ।।
explanation: Two sons will indeed be born to Raghava through Sita, but elsewhere, not in Ayodhya. This is the truth, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: सीतायाश्च ततः पुत्रावभिषेक्ष्यति राघवः ।। 7.51.26 ।।
explanation: And then Rāghava will consecrate Sītā's two sons.

shloka_text: स सर्वमखिलं राज्ञो वंशस्याह गतागतम् । आख्याय सुमहातेजास्तूष्णीमासीन्महामुनिः ।। 7.51.27 ।।
explanation: He, the great sage of immense splendor, having narrated the entire history of the king's lineage, became silent.

shloka_text: तूष्णीम्भूते तदा तस्मिन्राजा दशरथो मुनौ । अभिवाद्य महात्मानौ पुनरायात्पुरोत्तमम् ।। 7.51.28 ।।
explanation: When that sage fell silent, King Dasharatha, having saluted the two great souls, returned again to the best of cities.

shloka_text: एतद्वचो मया तत्र मुनिना व्याहृतं पुरा । श्रुतं हृदि च निक्षिप्तं नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति ।। 7.51.29 ।।
explanation: This word was spoken to me by the sage there long ago. It was heard and deposited in my heart, and it will not be otherwise.

shloka_text: एवं गते न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि राघव । सीतार्थे राघवार्थे वा दृढो भव नरोत्तम ।। 7.51.30 ।।
explanation: Since this has happened, O Raghava, you should not grieve. Be firm, O best among men, for Sita's sake or for your own sake.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु व्याहृतं वाक्यं सूतस्य परमाद्भुतम् । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.51.31 ।।
explanation: Having heard the exceedingly wonderful words spoken by the charioteer, he felt immeasurable joy and said, "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: ततः संवदतोरेवं सूतलक्ष्मणयोः पथि । अस्तमर्के गते वासं केशिन्यां तावथोषतुः ।। 7.51.32 ।।
explanation: Then, as the charioteer and Lakshmana were thus conversing on the way, when the sun had set, they stayed in Keshini.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 51 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the fifty-first chapter.

shloka_text: तत्र तां रजनीमुष्य केशिन्यां रघुनन्दनः । प्रभाते पुनरुत्थाय लक्ष्मणः प्रययौ तदा ।। 7.52.1 ।।
explanation: Having spent that night there in Keśinī, Lakshmana, the scion of Raghu, rose again in the morning and then departed.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते प्रविवेश महारथः । अयोध्यां रत्नसम्पूर्णां हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम् ।। 7.52.2 ।।
explanation: Then, when midday arrived, the great charioteer entered Ayodhya, which was full of jewels and thronged with happy and well-nourished people.

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु परं दैन्यं जगाम सुमहामतिः । रामपादौ समासाद्य वक्ष्यामि किमहं गतः ।। 7.52.3 ।।
explanation: But Saumitri, the very intelligent one, fell into extreme distress. Having approached Rama's feet, what will I say I have done?

shloka_text: तस्यैवं चिन्तयानस्य भवनं शशिसन्निभम् । रामस्य परमोदारं पुरस्तान्समदृश्यत ।। 7.52.4 ।।
explanation: As he was thus contemplating, Rama's exceedingly grand palace, resembling the moon, appeared before him.

shloka_text: राज्ञस्तु भवनद्वारि सो ऽवतीर्य रथोत्तमात् । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमनाः प्रविवेशानिवारितः ।। 7.52.5 ।।
explanation: He, having dismounted from the best chariot at the king's palace gate, with a downcast face and dejected mind, entered unhindered.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा राघवं दीनमासीनं परमासने । नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां ददर्शाग्रजमग्रतः ।। 7.52.6 ।।
explanation: He, with eyes full of tears, saw his elder brother Rama, distressed and seated on a high throne, before him.

shloka_text: जग्राह चरणौ तस्य लक्ष्मणो दीनचेतनः । उवाच दीनया वाचा प्राञ्जलिः सुसमाहितः ।। 7.52.7 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, with a distressed mind, seized his feet. With folded hands and great composure, he spoke in a sorrowful voice.

shloka_text: आर्यस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य विसृज्य जनकात्मजाम् । गङ्गातीरे यथोद्दिष्टे वाल्मीकेराश्रमे शुचौ ।। 7.52.8 ।।
explanation: Honoring the command of the noble one, having left Janaka's daughter at the pure hermitage of Valmiki on the bank of the Ganga, as instructed.

shloka_text: तत्र तां च शुभाचारामाश्रमान्ते यशस्विनीम् । पुनरप्यागतो वीर पादमूलमुपासितुम् ।। 7.52.9 ।।
explanation: O hero, I have come again to that renowned and virtuous lady, who resides near the hermitage, to serve at her feet.

shloka_text: मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र कालस्य गतिरीदृशी । त्वद्विधा न हि शोचन्ति बुद्धिमन्तो मनस्विनः ।। 7.52.10 ।।
explanation: Do not grieve, O best of men, such is the course of time. Indeed, intelligent and high-minded persons like you do not sorrow.

shloka_text: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ।। 7.52.11 ।।
explanation: All accumulations end in depletion, all rises end in falls, all unions end in separation, and life ends in death.

shloka_text: तस्मात्पुत्रेषु दारेषु मित्रेषु च धनेषु च । नातिप्रसङ्गः कर्तव्यो विप्रयोगो हि तैर्ध्रुवम् ।। 7.52.12 ।।
explanation: Therefore, one should not have excessive attachment to sons, wives, friends, and wealth, for separation from them is certain.

shloka_text: शक्तस्त्वमात्मना ऽ ऽत्मानं विनेतुं मनसैव हि । लोकान्सर्वांश्च काकुत्स्थ किं पुनः शोकमात्मनः ।। 7.52.13 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, you are indeed capable of guiding yourself by your own mind, and all the worlds. How much more then your own sorrow?

shloka_text: नेदृशेषु विमुह्यन्ति त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभाः । अपवादः स किल ते पुनरेष्यति राघव ।। 7.52.14 ।।
explanation: O foremost of men, those like you are not bewildered in such matters. That censure will certainly return to you, O Raghava.

shloka_text: यदर्थं मैथिली त्यक्ता अपवादभयान्नृप । सो ऽपवादः पुरे राजन्भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.52.15 ।।
explanation: O King, the very scandal for fear of which Maithili was abandoned, that scandal will undoubtedly arise in the city.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धैर्येण सुसमाहितः । त्यजैनां दुर्बलां बुद्धिं सन्तापं मा कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.52.16 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O best among men, being well-composed with fortitude, abandon this weak mindset and do not give way to sorrow.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः स काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । उवाच परया प्रीत्या सौमित्रिं मित्रवत्सलः ।। 7.52.17 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakshmana, that Kakutstha, who was affectionate towards friends, spoke to Saumitri with great affection.

shloka_text: एवमेतन्नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण । परितोषश्च मे वीर मम कार्यानुशासने ।। 7.52.18 ।।
explanation: It is exactly so, O best among men, just as you say, Lakshmana. And I am satisfied, O hero, with your execution of my command.

shloka_text: निवृत्तिश्चागता सौम्य सन्तापश्च निराकृतः । भवद्वाक्यैः सुरुचिरैरनुनीतो ऽस्मि लक्ष्मण ।। 7.52.19 ।।
explanation: Relief has come, O gentle one, and sorrow has been dispelled. I have been consoled by your very charming words, O Lakshmana.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 52 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the fifty-second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं निशम्य परमाद्भुतम् । सुप्रीतश्चाभवद्रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.53.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that most wonderful speech of Lakshmana, Rama became greatly pleased and spoke these words.

shloka_text: दुर्लभस्त्वीदृशो बन्धुरस्मिन्काले विशेषतः । यादृशस्त्वं महाबुद्धेर्मम सौम्य मनो ऽनुगः ।। 7.53.2 ।।
explanation: Indeed, such a friend as you, O great-minded and gentle one, who is agreeable to my mind, is rare, especially in this time.

shloka_text: यच्च मे हृदये किञ्चिद्वर्तते शुभलक्षण । तन्निशामय च श्रुत्वा कुरुष्व वचनं मम ।। 7.53.3 ।।
explanation: And whatever auspicious thought is present in my heart, pay attention to that, and having heard, carry out my word.

shloka_text: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्यं पौरजनस्य वै । अकुर्वाणस्य सौमित्रे तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति ।। 7.53.4 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, O Saumitri, that the work of the citizens has not been done for four days, indeed, cuts my vital parts.

shloka_text: आहूयन्तां प्रकृतयः पुरोधा मन्त्रिणस्तथा । कार्यार्थिनश्च पुरुषाः स्त्रियश्च पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.53.5 ।।
explanation: Let the officials, the chief priest, and the ministers be summoned. And also men and women who have business, O best among men.

shloka_text: पौरकार्याणि यो राजा न करोति दिने दिने । संवृते नरके घोरे पतितो नात्र संशयः ।। 7.53.6 ।।
explanation: That king who does not perform the duties of the citizens day by day, undoubtedly falls into a dreadful, enclosed hell.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि पुरा राजा नृगो नाम महायशाः । बभूव पृथिवीपालो ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यवाक् शुचिः ।। 7.53.7 ।।
explanation: It is heard that in ancient times there was a king named Nriga, of great renown. He was a ruler of the earth, devoted to Brahmins, truthful, and pure.

shloka_text: स कदाचिद्गवां कोटीः सवत्साः स्वर्णभूषिताः । नृदेवो भूमिदेवेभ्यः पुष्करेषु ददौ नृपः ।। 7.53.8 ।।
explanation: That king, the lord of men, once gave ten million cows, with their calves and adorned with gold, to the Brahmins in Pushkara.

shloka_text: ततः सङ्गाद्गता धेनुः सवत्सा स्पर्शिता ऽनघ । ब्राह्मणस्याहिताग्नेश्च दरिद्रस्योञ्छवर्तिनः ।। 7.53.9 ।।
explanation: Then, O sinless one, a cow with its calf was offered, due to attachment, to a Brahmin who maintains the sacred fires, and who is poor and lives by gleaning.

shloka_text: स नष्टां गां क्षुधार्तो वै अन्विषंस्तत्र तत्र च । नापश्यत्सर्वराज्येषु संवत्सरगणान्बहून् ।। 7.53.10 ।।
explanation: He, hungry, searching here and there for the lost cow, did not see it in any kingdom for many years.

shloka_text: ततः कनखलं गत्वा जीर्णवत्सां निरामयाम् । ददर्श गां स्वकां धेनुं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने ।। 7.53.11 ।।
explanation: Then, having gone to Kanakhala, he saw his own healthy milch cow, whose calf was grown, in the dwelling of a Brahmin.

shloka_text: अथ तां नामधेयेन स्वकेनोवाच स द्विजः । आगच्छ शबलेत्येवं सा तु शुश्राव गौः स्वरम् ।। 7.53.12 ।।
explanation: Then that Brahmin addressed her by her own name, saying, 'Come, Shabala!' And the cow heard his voice.

shloka_text: तस्य तं स्वरमाज्ञाय क्षुधार्तस्य द्विजस्य वै । अन्वगात्पृष्ठतः सा गौर्गच्छन्तं पावकोपमम् ।। 7.53.13 ।।
explanation: Having recognized the sound of that hungry Brahmin, that cow indeed followed behind him as he walked, radiant like fire.

shloka_text: यो ऽपि पालयते विप्रः सो ऽपि गामन्वगाद्द्रुतम् । गत्वा तमृषिमाचष्ट मम गौरिति सत्वरम् ।। 7.53.14 ।।
explanation: Even the Brahmin who was protecting (her), he too quickly followed the cow. Having gone, he swiftly told that sage, "This is my cow."

shloka_text: स्पर्शिता राजसिंहेन मम दत्ता नृगेण ह । तयोर्ब्राह्मणयोर्वादो महानासीद्विपश्चितोः ।। 7.53.15 ।।
explanation: It was touched by the great king, and given to me by Nriga, indeed. A great dispute arose between those two learned Brahmins.

shloka_text: विवदन्तौ ततो ऽन्योन्यं दातारमभिजग्मतुः । तौ राजभवनद्वारि न प्राप्तौ नृगशासनम् ।। 7.53.16 ।।
explanation: Then, disputing with each other, they both approached the giver. Those two did not obtain Nṛga's judgment at the gate of the royal palace.

shloka_text: अहोरात्राण्यनेकानि वसन्तौ क्रोधमीयतुः । ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ तावुभौ द्विजसत्तमौ ।। क्रुद्धौ परमसम्प्राप्तौ वाक्यं घोराभिसंहितम् ।। 7.53.17 ।।
explanation: For many days and nights, as they dwelt, they both became angry. And those two great-souled ones, the best among the twice-born, having become extremely enraged, spoke a dreadful statement.

shloka_text: अर्थिनां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं यस्मात्त्वं नैषि दर्शनम् । अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां कृकलासो भविष्यसि ।। 7.53.18 ।।
explanation: Since you do not show yourself for the accomplishment of the tasks of those who seek, you will become a chameleon, invisible to all beings.

shloka_text: बहुवर्षसहस्राणि बहुवर्षशतानि च । श्वभ्रे ऽस्मिन् कृकलासो वै दीर्घकालं वसिष्यसि ।। 7.53.19 ।।
explanation: For many thousands and many hundreds of years, O chameleon, you will indeed dwell for a long time in this pit.

shloka_text: उत्पत्स्यते हि लोके ऽस्मिन्यदूनां कीर्तिवर्धनः । वासुदेव इति ख्यातो विष्णुः पुरुषविग्रहः ।। 7.53.20 ।।
explanation: Indeed, in this world, Vishnu, known as Vasudeva, the enhancer of the Yadus' glory, will be born in a human form.

shloka_text: स ते मोक्षयिता राजंस्तस्माच्छापाद्भविष्यसि । कृता च तेन कालेन निष्कृतिस्ते भविष्यति ।। 7.53.21 ।।
explanation: O King, he will liberate you from that curse. And your expiation will be accomplished by him in due time.

shloka_text: भारावतरणार्थं हि नरनारायणावुभौ । उत्पत्स्येते महावीर्यौ कलौ युग उपस्थिते ।। 7.53.22 ।।
explanation: Indeed, for the purpose of relieving the burden, both Nara and Narayana, of great valor, will be born when the Kali Yuga arrives.

shloka_text: एवं तौ शापमुत्सृज्य ब्राह्मणौ विगतज्वरौ । तां गां हि दुर्बलां वृद्धां ददतुर्ब्राह्मणाय वै ।। 7.53.23 ।।
explanation: Thus, those two Brahmins, having released the curse and being free from distress, indeed gave that weak and old cow to a Brahmin.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुङ्क्ते सुदारुणम् ।। 7.53.24 ।।
explanation: Thus that king experiences that very terrible curse.

shloka_text: कार्यार्थिनां विमर्दो हि राज्ञां दोषाय कल्पते । तच्छीघ्रं दर्शनं मह्यमभिवर्तन्तु कार्यिणः ।। 7.53.25 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the delay of those seeking their purpose leads to harm for kings. Therefore, let the petitioners quickly come to me for an audience.

shloka_text: सुकृतस्य हि कार्यस्य फलं नापैति पार्थिवः । तस्माद्गच्छ प्रतीक्षस्व सौमित्रे कार्यवाञ्जनः ।। 7.53.26 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the fruit of a well-done action does not perish, O King. Therefore, go and wait, O son of Sumitra, for the person who has business.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 53 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the fifty-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परमार्थवित् । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.54.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Lakshmana, the knower of the ultimate truth, spoke with folded hands to Raghava, who was radiant with splendor.

shloka_text: अल्पापराधे काकुत्स्थ द्विजाभ्यां शाप ईदृशः । महान्नृगस्य राजर्षेर्यमदण्ड इवापरः ।। 7.54.2 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, for a minor offense, such a curse from the two Brahmins is like another great punishment from Yama for the royal sage Nṛga.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु पापसंयुक्तमात्मानं पुरषर्षभ । किमुवाच नृगो राजा द्विजौ क्रोधसमन्वितौ ।। 7.54.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard himself described as sinful, O best among men, what did King Nṛga say to the two enraged Brahmins?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । शृणु सौम्य यथा पूर्वं स राजा शापविक्षतः ।। 7.54.4 ।।
