explanation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Rama spoke again: "Listen, O gentle one, how that king was formerly afflicted by a curse."

shloka_text: अथाध्वनि गतौ विप्रौ विज्ञाय स नृगस्तदा । आहूय मन्त्रिणः सर्वान्नैगमान्सपुरोधसः ।। 7.54.5 ।।
explanation: Then, having learned that the two Brahmins had departed on their way, King Nṛga then summoned all his ministers, citizens, and priests.

shloka_text: तानुवाच नृगो राजा सर्वाश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा । दुःखेन सुसमाविष्टः श्रूयतां मे समाहितैः ।। 7.54.6 ।।
explanation: King Nṛga, deeply afflicted with sorrow, said to them and all the subjects, "Let my words be heard by those who are attentive."

shloka_text: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव मम दत्त्वा महद्भयम् । गतौ त्रिभुवनं भद्रौ वायुभूतावनिन्दितौ ।। 7.54.7 ।।
explanation: Narada and Parvata, having caused me great fear, went to the three worlds, those auspicious and blameless ones, having become like wind.

shloka_text: कुमारो ऽयं वसुर्नाम स देवो ऽद्याभिषिच्यताम् । श्वभ्रं च यत्सुखस्पर्शं क्रियतां शिल्पिभिर्मम । यत्राहं सङ्क्षयिष्यामि शापं ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् ।। 7.54.8 ।।
explanation: Let this prince, named Vasu, that god, be consecrated today. And let a pit, pleasant to touch, be made for me by artisans, where I shall exhaust the curse issued by the Brahmin.

shloka_text: वर्षघ्नमेकं श्वभ्रं तु हिमघ्नमपरं तथा । ग्रीष्मघ्नं तु सुखस्पर्शमेकं कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः ।। 7.54.9 ।।
explanation: Let the artisans construct one cave that repels rain, another that repels cold, and one that repels heat and is pleasant to the touch.

shloka_text: फलवन्तश्च ये वृक्षाः पुष्पवत्यश्च या लताः । विरोप्यन्तां बहुविधाश्छायावन्तश्च गुल्मिनः ।। 7.54.10 ।।
explanation: Let fruit-bearing trees, flowering creepers, and various kinds of shade-giving shrubs be planted.

shloka_text: क्रियतां रमणीयं च श्वभ्राणां सर्वतोदिशम् । सुखमत्र वसिष्यामि यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः ।। 7.54.11 ।।
explanation: Let the caves be made beautiful and pleasant all around. I shall dwell here happily until the change of time.

shloka_text: पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि क्रियतां तेषु नित्यशः । परिवार्य यथा मे स्युरध्यर्धं योजनं तथा ।। 7.54.12 ।।
explanation: And fragrant flowers should always be placed there, surrounding [the area], so that they may extend for me over one and a half yojanas.

shloka_text: एवं कृत्वा विधानं स सन्दिदेश वसं तदा । धर्मनित्यः प्रजाः पुत्र क्षत्रधर्मेण पालय ।। 7.54.13 ।।
explanation: Thus, having made this arrangement, he then instructed (him), saying: "O son, ever devoted to righteousness, protect the subjects according to the duty of a Kshatriya."

shloka_text: प्रत्यक्षं ते यथा शापो द्विजाभ्यां मयि पातितः । नरश्रेष्ठ सरोषाभ्यामपराधे ऽपि तादृशे ।। 7.54.14 ।।
explanation: O best among men, you directly witnessed how a curse was inflicted upon me by the two angry Brahmins, even for such a fault.

shloka_text: मा कृथास्तनुसन्तापं मत्कृते ऽपि नरर्षभ । कृतान्तः कुशलः पुत्र येनास्मि व्यसनीकृतः ।। 7.54.15 ।।
explanation: O best among men, do not cause yourself sorrow even for my sake. O son, Destiny is powerful, by whom I have been made miserable.

shloka_text: प्राप्तव्यान्येव प्राप्नोति गन्तव्यान्येव गच्छति । लब्धव्यान्येव लभते दुःखानि च सुखानि च ।। 7.54.16 ।।
explanation: One obtains only what is destined to be obtained. One goes only where one is destined to go. One receives only what is destined to be received, be it sorrows or joys.

shloka_text: पूर्वे जात्यन्तरे वत्स मा विषादं कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.54.17 ।।
explanation: O child, do not despair about a previous birth.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा नृपस्तत्र सुतं राजा महायशाः । श्वभ्रं जगाम सुकृतं वासाय पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.54.18 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to his son, the king, that best among men, of great renown, went to the well-prepared subterranean dwelling for residence.

shloka_text: एवं प्रविश्यैव नृपस्तदानीं श्वभ्रं महारत्नविभूषितं तत् । सम्पादयामास तदा महात्मा शापं द्विजाभ्यां हि रुषा विमुक्तम् ।। 7.54.19 ।।
explanation: Thus, having just entered that pit adorned with great jewels, the great-souled king then caused to be fulfilled the curse that had indeed been pronounced with anger by the two Brahmins.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 54 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana by Valmiki, the first epic poem, the Rishi's work, is the fifty-fourth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरो ऽभिहितो मया । यद्यस्ति श्रवणे श्रद्धा शृणुष्वेहापरां कथाम् ।। 7.55.1 ।।
explanation: I have narrated to you this detailed account of Nṛga's curse. If you have an interest in listening, then listen to another story here.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण सौमित्रिः पुनरब्रवीत् । तृप्तिराश्चर्यभूतानां कथानां नास्ति मे नृप ।। 7.55.2 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Saumitri again spoke: 'O King, I have no satisfaction from wonderful stories.'

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राम इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । कथां परमधर्मिष्ठां व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.3 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Rama, the scion of Ikshvaku, began to narrate a most righteous tale.

shloka_text: आसीद्राजा निमिर्नाम इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः ।। 7.55.4 ।।
explanation: Among the great-souled Ikshvakus, there was a king named Nimi. He was the twelfth son, firmly established in valor and righteousness.

shloka_text: स राजा वीर्यसम्पन्नः पुरं देवपुरोपमम् । निवेशयामास तदा अभ्याशे गौतमस्य तु ।। 7.55.5 ।।
explanation: That king, endowed with valor, then founded a city resembling a divine city, near Gautama.

shloka_text: पुरस्य सुकृतं नाम वैजयन्तमिति श्रुतम् । निवेशं यत्र राजर्षिर्निमिश्चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.55.6 ।।
explanation: The city named Sukrita, renowned as Vaijayanta, where the greatly illustrious royal sage Nimi established his abode.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य सुमहापुरम् । यजेयं दीर्घसत्रेण पितुः प्रह्लादयन्मनः ।। 7.55.7 ।।
explanation: An idea arose in him: 'Having established a very great city, I should perform a prolonged sacrifice, delighting my father's mind.'

shloka_text: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम् । वसिष्ठं वरयामास पूर्वं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमम् ।। 7.55.8 ।।
explanation: Then, having addressed his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he chose Vasishtha, the foremost among the Brahmarshis.

shloka_text: अनन्तरं स राजर्षिर्निमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोधनम् ।। 7.55.9 ।।
explanation: Afterwards, that royal sage Nimi, the son of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and also Bhrigu, the ascetic.

shloka_text: तमुवाच वसिष्ठस्तु निमिं राजर्षिसत्तमम् । वृतो ऽहं पूर्वमिन्द्रेण अन्तरं प्रतिपालय ।। 7.55.10 ।।
explanation: Vasishtha said to him, Nimi, the best among royal sages: "I have been chosen by Indra previously. Wait for an interval."

shloka_text: अनन्तरं महाविप्रो गौतमः प्रत्यपूरयत् । वसिष्ठो ऽपि महातेजा इन्द्रयज्ञमथाकरोत् ।। 7.55.11 ।।
explanation: Afterwards, the great Brahmin Gautama completed. And the greatly effulgent Vasistha also then performed the Indra-sacrifice.

shloka_text: निमिस्तु राजा विप्रांस्तान्समानीय नराधिपः । अयजद्धिमवत्पार्श्वे स्वपुरस्य समीपतः । पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि राजा दीक्षामुपागमत् ।। 7.55.12 ।।
explanation: King Nimi, the lord of men, having gathered those Brahmins, performed a sacrifice near his own city, by the side of the Himalayas. The king undertook the vow for five thousand years.

shloka_text: इन्द्रयज्ञावसाने तु वसिष्ठो भगवनृषिः । सकाशमागतो राज्ञो हौत्रं कर्तुमनिन्दितः ।। 7.55.13 ।।
explanation: At the conclusion of the Indra-sacrifice, the revered sage Vasiṣṭha, who was blameless, came to the king to perform the priestly duties.

shloka_text: तदन्तरमथापश्यद्गौतमेनाभिपूरितम् । कोपेन महताविष्टो वसिष्ठो ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।। 7.55.14 ।।
explanation: Thereafter, he saw Vasishtha, the son of Brahma, overcome by great anger, (the place/situation) having been filled/pervaded by Gautama.

shloka_text: स राज्ञो दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी मुहूर्तं समुपाविशत् । तस्मिन्नहनि राजर्षिर्निद्रया ऽपहृतो भृशम् ।। 7.55.15 ।।
explanation: He, desirous of seeing the king, sat down for a moment. On that day, the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.

shloka_text: ततो मन्युर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रादुरासीन्महात्मनः । अदर्शनेन राजर्षेर्व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.55.16 ।।
explanation: Then, anger arose in the great-souled Vasishtha. Due to the non-appearance of the royal sage, he began to speak.

shloka_text: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव । चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्तव भविष्यति ।। 7.55.17 ।।
explanation: Since you have chosen another, disregarding me, O king, your body will be devoid of consciousness.

shloka_text: ततः प्रबुद्धो राजर्षिः श्रुत्वा शापमुदाहृतम् । ब्रह्मयोनिमथोवाच संरम्भात् क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।। 7.55.18 ।।
explanation: Then the awakened royal sage, having heard the uttered curse, spoke to the Brahmayoni, overcome with agitation and maddened by anger.

shloka_text: अजानतः शयानस्य क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः । मुक्तवान्मयि शापाग्निं यमदण्डमिवापरम् ।। 7.55.19 ।।
explanation: Enraged by anger, he hurled upon me, who was unaware and sleeping, the fire of a curse, like another rod of Yama.

shloka_text: तस्मात्तवापि ब्रह्मर्षे चेतनेन विना कृतः । देहः सुरुचिरप्रख्यो भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.55.20 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, your body, even without consciousness, will become exceedingly beautiful in appearance, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: इति रोषवशादुभौ तदानीमन्योन्यं शपितौ नृपद्विजेन्द्रौ । सहसैव बभूवतुर्विदेहौ तत्तुल्याधिगतप्रभाववन्तौ ।। 7.55.21 ।।
explanation: Thus, at that time, both the king and the chief of brahmins, having mutually cursed each other out of anger, suddenly became bodiless, each having acquired power equal to the other's.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.56.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Lakshmana, the slayer of enemy heroes, with folded hands, spoke words to Raghava, who possessed blazing splendor.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्य कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ । पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मतुर्देवसम्मतौ ।। 7.56.2 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, how did those two, the brahmin and the king, whose bodies had been cast off, attain union with a body again, being approved by the gods?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु रामश्चेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजा लक्ष्मणं पुरुषर्षभः ।। 7.56.3 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Rama, the descendant of Ikshvaku, the greatly effulgent one, the best among men, replied to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: तौ परस्परशापेन देहावुत्सृज्य धार्मिकौ । अभूतां नृपविप्रर्षी वायुभूतौ तपोधनौ ।। 7.56.4 ।।
explanation: Those two righteous ones, the king and the brahmin sage, ascetics, having abandoned their bodies by a mutual curse, became wind-formed.

shloka_text: अशरीरः शरीरस्य कृते ऽन्यस्य महामुनिः । वसिष्ठः सुमहातेजा जगाम पितुरन्तिकम् ।। 7.56.5 ।।
explanation: The great sage Vasishtha, of immense splendor, though disembodied, went to his father's presence for the sake of another body.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ देवदेवस्य धर्मवित् । पितामहमथोवाच वायुभूत इदं वचः ।। 7.56.6 ।।
explanation: Then, he, the knower of Dharma, having saluted the feet of the god of gods, having become ethereal, spoke this word to the Grandfather.

shloka_text: भगवन्निमिशापेन विदेहत्वमुपागमम् । लोकनाथ महादेव अण्डजो ऽपि त्वमब्जजः ।। 7.56.7 ।।
explanation: O Lord, by Nimi's curse, I attained the state of being bodiless. O Lord of the worlds, O Great God, you are both born from an egg and born from a lotus.

shloka_text: सर्वेषां देहहीनानां महद्दुःखं भविष्यति । लुप्यन्ते सर्वकार्यणि हीनदेहस्य वै प्रभो । देहस्यान्यस्य सद्भावे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.56.8 ।।
explanation: Great suffering will befall all those without bodies. All actions of the body-less are indeed obstructed, O Lord. If another body exists, please show your grace.

shloka_text: तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूरमितप्रभः । मित्रावरुणजं तेज प्रविश त्वं महायशः ।। 7.56.9 ।।
explanation: Then Brahma, the self-born, of immeasurable splendor, said to him: "O greatly renowned one, enter the energy born of Mitra and Varuna."

shloka_text: अयोनिजस्त्वं भविता तत्रापि द्विजसत्तम । धर्मेण महता युक्तः पुनरेष्यसि मे वशम् ।। 7.56.10 ।।
explanation: You will be unoriginated even there, O best among the twice-born. Endowed with great righteousness, you will again come under my control.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन चाभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम् । कृत्वा पितामहं तूर्णं प्रययौ वरुणालयम् ।। 7.56.11 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the god, and having saluted and circumambulated the Grandfather, he quickly went to Varuna's abode.

shloka_text: तमेव कालं मित्रो ऽपि वरुणत्वमकारयत् । क्षीरोदेन सहोपेतः पूज्यमानः सुरोत्तमैः ।। 7.56.12 ।।
explanation: At that very time, Mitra also assumed the state of Varuna, having arrived with the Milk Ocean, being worshipped by the best of the gods.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु उर्वशी परमाप्सराः । यदृच्छया तमुद्देशमाययौ सखिभिर्वृता ।। 7.56.13 ।।
explanation: At this very time, Urvashi, the foremost Apsara, arrived at that spot by chance, accompanied by her companions.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां क्रीडन्तीं वरुणालये । आविशत्परमो हर्षो वरुणं चोर्वशीकृते ।। 7.56.14 ।।
explanation: Having seen her, endowed with beauty, playing in Varuna's abode, supreme joy overcame Varuna because of Urvashi.

shloka_text: स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । वरुणो वरयामास मैथुनायाप्सरोवराम् ।। 7.56.15 ।।
explanation: Varuna wooed her, the best of Apsaras, who had eyes like lotus petals and a face like the full moon, for sexual union.

shloka_text: प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता । मित्रेणाहं वृता साक्षात्पूर्वमेव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.56.16 ।।
explanation: Then she, standing with folded hands, replied to Varuna: "O Lord of gods, I was indeed chosen by Mitra himself beforehand."

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं कन्दर्पशरपीडितः । इदं तेजः समुत्स्रक्ष्ये कुम्भे ऽस्मिन्देवनिर्मिते ।। 7.56.17 ।।
explanation: Varuna, tormented by the arrows of Kama, then spoke: "I shall discharge this semen into this pot made by the gods."

shloka_text: एवमुत्सृज्य सुश्रोणि त्वय्यहं वरवर्णिनि । कृतकामो भविष्यामि यदि नेच्छसि सङ्गमम् ।। 7.56.18 ।।
explanation: Thus, O beautiful-hipped one, O lady of excellent complexion, I shall consider my desire fulfilled by giving you up, if you do not wish for union.

shloka_text: तस्य तल्लोकपालस्य वरुणस्य सुभाषितम् । उर्वशी परमप्रीता श्रुत्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.56.19 ।।
explanation: Having heard those well-spoken words of Varuna, the guardian of the world, Urvashi, greatly delighted, spoke.

shloka_text: काममेतद्भवत्वेवं हृदयं मे त्वयि स्थितम् । भावश्चाप्यधिकस्तुभ्यं देहो मित्रस्य तु प्रभो ।। 7.56.20 ।।
explanation: Let this indeed be so, my heart is fixed on you. And my devotion to you is also greater, but this body, O Lord, belongs to a friend.

shloka_text: उर्वश्या एवमुक्तस्तु रेतस्तन्महदद्भुतम् । ज्वलदग्निशिखाप्रख्यं तस्मिन्कुम्भे ह्यपासृजत् ।। 7.56.21 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Urvashi, he indeed discharged that great and wondrous semen, resembling a blazing flame of fire, into that pot.

shloka_text: उर्वशी त्वगमत्तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता । तां तु मित्रः सुसङ्क्रम्य उर्वशीमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.56.22 ।।
explanation: Urvashi went to that place where Mitra was the deity. Then Mitra, approaching Urvashi, said this to her.

shloka_text: मया निमन्त्रिता पूर्वं कस्मात्त्वमवसर्जिता । पतिमन्यं वृतवती तस्मात्त्वं दुष्टचारिणी ।। 7.56.23 ।।
explanation: Why were you, previously invited by me, abandoned? Because you chose another husband, therefore you are an unchaste woman.

shloka_text: अनेन दुष्कृतेन त्वं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता । मनुष्यलोकमास्थाय कञ्चित्कालं निवत्स्यसि ।। 7.56.24 ।।
explanation: By this misdeed, you, defiled by my anger, will reside in the human world for some time.

shloka_text: बुधस्य पुत्रो राजर्षिः काशीराजः पुरूरवाः । तमद्य गच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति ।। 7.56.25 ।।
explanation: O foolish one, go today to Pururavas, the royal sage, the son of Budha, the King of Kashi. He will be your husband.

shloka_text: ततः सा शापदोषेण पुरूरवसमभ्यगात् । प्रतियाते पुरूरवं बुधस्यात्मजमौरसम् ।। 7.56.26 ।।
explanation: Then she, due to the effect of a curse, approached Pururavas, the legitimate son of Budha, upon his return.

shloka_text: तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः । नहुषो यस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवेन्द्रसमद्युतिः ।। 7.56.27 ।।
explanation: Then, from him was born the glorious and mighty son, Ayu. His son, Nahusha, was indeed as radiant as Indra.

shloka_text: वज्रमुत्सृज्य वृत्राय भ्रान्ते ऽथ त्रिदिवेश्वरे । शतं वर्षसहस्राणि येनेन्द्रत्वं प्रशासितम् ।। 7.56.28 ।।
explanation: When the lord of heaven (Indra), having hurled the thunderbolt at Vritra, became bewildered, by whom Indraship was ruled for a hundred thousand years.

shloka_text: सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमिं तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा । बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च ।। 7.56.29 ।।
explanation: Then, Urvashi, with her beautiful teeth, lovely eyes, and graceful eyebrows, went to the earth due to that curse. She resided there for many years, and upon the expiry of the curse, she returned to Indra's abode.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 56 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the fifty-sixth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तां श्रुत्वा दिव्यसङ्काशां कथामद्भुतदर्शनाम् । लक्ष्मणः परमप्रीतो राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.57.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that divine-like and wondrous story, Lakshmana, greatly pleased, spoke to Raghava.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्थ कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ । पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मुर्देवसम्मतौ ।। 7.57.2 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, how did those two, the Brahmin and the king, whose bodies had been cast off, again attain union with a body, being approved by the gods?

shloka_text: तस्य तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः । तां कथां कथयामास वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.57.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, Rama, of true valor, narrated that story to the great-souled Vasistha.

shloka_text: यस्तु कुम्भो रघुश्रेष्ठ तेजःपूर्णो महात्मनोः । तस्मिंस्तेजोमयौ विप्रौ सम्भूतावृषिसत्तमौ ।। 7.57.4 ।।
explanation: O best of the Raghus, that pot, which was full of the splendor of the two great souls, in it were born two radiant Brahmins, the best of sages.

shloka_text: पूर्वं समभवत्तत्र ह्यगस्त्यो भगवानृषिः । नाहं सुतस्तवेत्युक्त्वा मित्रं तस्मादपाक्रमत् ।। 7.57.5 ।।
explanation: Formerly, the revered sage Agastya was born there. Having said, "I am not your son," he departed from Mitra.

shloka_text: तद्धि तेजस्तु मित्रस्य उर्वस्याः पूर्वमाहितम् । तस्मिन्समभवत्कुम्भे तत्तेजो यत्र वारुणम् ।। 7.57.6 ।।
explanation: That very brilliance of Mitra, indeed, previously deposited due to Urvashi, was born in that pot, where also was the brilliance of Varuna.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य मित्रावरुणसम्भवः । वसिष्ठस्तेजसा युक्तो जज्ञे इक्ष्वाकुदैवतम् ।। 7.57.7 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, Vasishtha, born of Mitra and Varuna, endowed with splendor, was born as the preceptor of the Ikshvakus.

shloka_text: तमिक्ष्वाकुर्महातेजा जातमात्रमनिन्दितम् । वव्रे पुरोधसं सौम्य वंशस्यास्य भवाय नः ।। 7.57.8 ।।
explanation: The greatly effulgent Ikshvaku chose that blameless and gentle one, immediately after his birth, as the family priest for the prosperity of our lineage.

shloka_text: एवं त्वपूर्वदेहस्य वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः । कथितो निर्गमः सौम्य निमेः शृणु यथा ऽभवत् ।। 7.57.9 ।।
explanation: Thus, indeed, the origin of the great-souled Vasishtha, who had an unprecedented body, has been narrated. O gentle one, listen now to how it happened for Nimi.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा विदेहं राजानमृषयः सर्व एव ते । तं च ते योजयामासुर्यागदीक्षां मनीषिणः ।। 7.57.10 ।।
explanation: All those sages, the wise ones, having seen King Videha, initiated him into the sacrificial vow.

shloka_text: तं च देहं नरेन्द्रस्य रक्षन्ति स्म द्विजोत्तमाः । गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च वस्त्रैश्च पौरभृत्यसमन्विताः ।। 7.57.11 ।।
explanation: And that body of the king was protected by the best of the twice-born, accompanied by citizens and servants, with fragrances, garlands, and garments.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु भृगुस्तत्रेदमब्रवीत् । आनयिष्यामि ते चेतस्तुष्टो ऽस्मि तव पार्थिव ।। 7.57.12 ।।
explanation: Then, when the sacrifice was concluded, Bhrigu said there: "I shall make your mind content, O King, for I am pleased with you."

shloka_text: सुप्रीताश्च सुराः सर्वे निमेश्चेतस्तथाब्रुवन् । वरं वरय राजर्षे क्व ते चेतो निरूप्यताम् ।। 7.57.13 ।।
explanation: And all the very pleased gods, with a clear mind, thus spoke: "O royal sage, choose a boon; let your mind be revealed (as to what you desire)."

shloka_text: एवमुक्तः सुरैः सर्वैर्निमेश्चेतस्तदाब्रवीत् । नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वसेयं सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.57.14 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by all the gods, Nimi's mind then spoke: "O best of gods, may I dwell in the eyes of all beings."

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव विबुधा निमेश्चेतस्तदा ऽब्रुवन् । नेत्रेषु सर्वभूतानां वायुभूतश्चरिष्यसि ।। 7.57.15 ।।
explanation: Then the gods said to Nimi, "So be it. You will wander in the eyes of all beings as air."

shloka_text: त्वत्कृते च निमिष्यन्ति चक्षूंषि पृथिवीपते । वायुभूतेन चरता विश्रमार्थं मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.57.16 ।।
explanation: O lord of the earth, for your sake, eyes will close repeatedly for rest, as one moves about having become wind.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु विबुधाः सर्वे जग्मुर्यथागतम् । ऋषयो ऽपि महात्मानो निमेर्देहं समाहरन् ।। 7.57.17 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, all the gods departed as they had arrived. The great-souled sages also gathered Nimi's body.

shloka_text: अरणिं तत्र निक्षिप्य मथनं चक्रुरोजसा । मन्त्रहोमैर्महात्मानः पुत्रहेतोर्निमेस्तदा ।। 7.57.18 ।।
explanation: Then, the great souls, for the sake of Nimi's son, having placed the fire-drill wood there, performed the churning with vigor, accompanied by mantra-offerings.

shloka_text: अरण्यां मथ्यामानायां प्रादुर्भूतो महातपाः । मथनान्मिथिरित्याहुर्जननाज्जनको ऽभवत् । यस्माद्विदेहात्सम्भूतो वैदेहस्तु ततः स्मृतः ।। 7.57.19 ।।
explanation: When the Arani was being churned, the great ascetic appeared. From the churning, he was called Mithir; from his birth, he became Janaka. Because he was born from Videha, he is therefore remembered as Vaideha.

shloka_text: एवं विदेहराजश्च जनकः पूर्वको ऽभवत् । मिथिर्नाम महातेजास्तेनायं मैथिलो ऽभवत् ।। 7.57.20 ।।
explanation: Thus, Janaka, the king of Videha, was the first (ancestor). He was named Mithi, the greatly effulgent one. By him, this (lineage/region) became Maithila.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 57 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the fifty-seventh chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा ।। 7.58.1 ।।
explanation: When Rama spoke thus, Lakshmana, the slayer of enemy heroes, replied to the great-souled one, who was blazing as if with splendor.

shloka_text: महदद्भुतमाश्चर्यं विदेहस्य पुरातनम् । निर्वृत्तं राजशार्दूल वसिष्ठस्य निमेस्सह ।। 7.58.2 ।।
explanation: O tiger among kings, a great, wonderful, and ancient marvel concerning Videha, along with Vasishtha and Nimi, has occurred.

shloka_text: निमिस्तु क्षत्रियः शूरो विशेषेण च दीक्षितः । न क्षमां कृतवान्राजा वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.58.3 ।।
explanation: But King Nimi, a brave Kshatriya, and especially consecrated, did not show forbearance towards the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु तेनायं श्रीमान् क्षत्रियपुङ्गवः । उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् ।। 7.58.4 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by him, this glorious foremost among Kshatriyas spoke words to Lakshmana, who was proficient in all scriptures.

shloka_text: रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठो भ्रातरं दीप्ततेजसम् । न सर्वत्र क्षमा वीर पुरुषेषु प्रदृश्यते ।। 7.58.5 ।।
explanation: Rama, the best among those who delight, (said) to his brother of blazing splendor: "O hero, forgiveness is not always seen among men everywhere."

shloka_text: सौमित्रे दुःसहो रोषो यथा क्षान्तो ययातिना । सत्त्वानुगं पुरस्कृत्य तन्निबोध समाहितः ।। 7.58.6 ।।
explanation: O Saumitri, listen carefully to how Yayati endured unbearable anger, having prioritized virtue.

shloka_text: नहुषस्य सुतो राजा ययातिः पौरवर्धनः । तस्य भार्याद्वयं सौम्य रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि ।। 7.58.7 ।।
explanation: King Yayati, son of Nahusha, the promoter of his people, had two wives, O gentle one, whose beauty was unequalled on earth.

shloka_text: एका तु तस्य राजर्षेर्नाहुषस्य पुरस्कृता । शर्मिष्ठा नाम दैतेयी दुहिता वृषपर्वणः ।। 7.58.8 ।।
explanation: One of his, that royal sage, the descendant of Nahusha, was Sharmishtha by name, a Daitya woman, daughter of Vrishaparvan, who was honored.

shloka_text: अन्या तूशनसः पत्नी ययातेः पुरुषर्षभ । न तु सा दयिता राज्ञो देवयानी सुमध्यमा ।। 7.58.9 ।।
explanation: O best among men, another wife of Yayāti was not that slender-waisted Devayani, the beloved of the king, who was the daughter of Uśanas.

shloka_text: तयोः पुत्रौ तु सम्भूतौ रूपवन्तौ समाहितौ । शर्मिष्ठा ऽजनयत्पूरुं देवयानी यदुं तदा ।। 7.58.10 ।।
explanation: Two handsome and well-disposed sons were born to them. Sharmishtha gave birth to Puru, and Devayani then gave birth to Yadu.

shloka_text: पूरुस्तु दयितो राज्ञो गुणैर्मातृकृतेन च । ततो दुःखसमाविष्टो यदुर्मातरमब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.11 ।।
explanation: Pūru, however, was dear to the king because of his virtues and what he had done for his mother. Then, overcome with sorrow, Yadu spoke to his mother.

shloka_text: भार्गवस्य कुले जाता देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । सहसे हृद्गतं दुःखमवमानं च दुःसहम् ।। 7.58.12 ।।
explanation: Born in the lineage of Bhrigu, of the god whose deeds are unblemished, you endure the sorrow residing in your heart and unbearable humiliation.

shloka_text: आवां च सहितौ देवि प्रविशाव हुताशनम् । राजा तु रमतां सार्धं दैत्यपुत्र्या बहुक्षपाः ।। 7.58.13 ।।
explanation: O Goddess, let us two together enter the fire. But let the king enjoy with the daughter of the Daitya for many nights.

shloka_text: यदि वा सहनीयं ते मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि । क्षम त्वं न क्षमिष्ये ऽहं मरिष्यामि न संशयः ।। 7.58.14 ।।
explanation: If it is bearable for you, you ought to permit me. You may forgive, but I will not forgive; I will die, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: पुत्रस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा परमार्तस्य रोदतः । देवयानी तु सङ्क्रुद्धा सस्मार पितरं तदा ।। 7.58.15 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of her extremely distressed and weeping son, Devayani, greatly enraged, then remembered her father.

shloka_text: इङ्गितं तदभिज्ञाय दुहितुर्भार्गवस्तदा । आगतस्त्वरितं तत्र देवयानी तु यत्र सा ।। 7.58.16 ।।
explanation: Then, having understood that hint of his daughter, Bhargava quickly came to where Devayani was.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा चाप्रकृतिस्थां तामप्रहृष्टामचेतनाम् । पिता दुहितरं वाक्यं किमेतदिति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.17 ।।
explanation: And having seen her disturbed, unhappy, and bewildered, the father said to his daughter, "What is this?"

shloka_text: पृच्छन्तमसकृत्तं वै भार्गवं दीप्ततेजसम् । देवयानी तु सङ्क्रुद्धा पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.58.18 ।।
explanation: Devayani, greatly enraged, spoke a word to her father, the brilliant Bhargava, who was repeatedly questioning.

shloka_text: अहमग्निं विषं तीक्ष्णमपो वा मुनिसत्तम । भक्षयिष्ये प्रवेक्ष्यामि न तु शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम् ।। 7.58.19 ।।
explanation: O best of sages, I will consume fire, potent poison, or water, or I will enter (them), but I will not be able to live.

shloka_text: न मां त्वमवजानीषे दुःखितामवमानिताम् । वृक्षस्यावज्ञया ब्रह्मंश्छिद्यन्ते वृक्षजीविनः ।। 7.58.20 ।।
explanation: Do not disregard me, who am distressed and humiliated. O Brahman, by disrespecting a tree, those who live on it are destroyed.

shloka_text: अवज्ञया च राजर्षिः परिभूय च भार्गव । मय्यवज्ञां प्रयुङ्क्ते हि न च मां बहु मन्यते ।। 7.58.21 ।।
explanation: O Bhargava, the royal sage, both with disrespect and having insulted (me), indeed shows contempt towards me and does not hold me in high esteem.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कोपेनाभिपरिप्लुतः । व्याहर्तुमुपचक्राम भार्गवो नहुषात्मजम् ।। 7.58.22 ।।
explanation: Having heard her words, Bhargava, overwhelmed by anger, began to speak to Nahusha's son.

shloka_text: यस्मान्मामवजानीषे नाहुष त्वं दुरात्मवान् । जरया परया जीर्णः शैथिल्यमुपयास्यसि ।। 7.58.23 ।।
explanation: Because you disrespect me, O wicked-minded Nahusha, you will become extremely feeble, worn out by severe old age.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा दुहितरं समाश्वास्य च भार्गवः । पुनर्जगाम ब्रह्मर्षिर्भवनं स्वं महायशाः ।। 7.58.24 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to his daughter and consoled her, the greatly renowned Brahmarshi Bhargava returned to his own abode.

shloka_text: स एवमुक्त्वा द्विजपुङ्गवाग्र्यः सुतां समाश्वास्य च देवयानीम् । पुनर्ययौ सूर्यसमानतेजा दत्त्वा च शापं नहुषात्मजाय ।। 7.58.25 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken and having consoled his daughter Devayani, he, the foremost among excellent Brahmins, whose splendor was like the sun, then departed, having also given a curse to the son of Nahusha.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 58 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the glorious original epic poem by Valmiki, is the fifty-eighth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तूशनसं क्रुद्धं तदा ऽ ऽर्तो नहुषात्मजः । जरां परमिकां प्राप्य यदुं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.59.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard the enraged Uśanas, the distressed son of Nahuṣa, having attained extreme old age, spoke to Yadu.

shloka_text: यदो त्वमसि धर्मज्ञो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम् । जरां परमिकां पुत्र भोगै रंस्ये महायशः ।। 7.59.2 ।।
explanation: Since you are righteous, O son, let this extreme old age be accepted for my sake. O greatly renowned one, I will enjoy pleasures.

shloka_text: न तावत्कृतकृत्यो ऽस्मि विषयेषु नरर्षभ । अनुभूय तदा कामं ततः प्राप्स्याम्यहं जराम् ।। 7.59.3 ।।
explanation: O best among men, I am not yet satisfied with worldly pleasures. Having then experienced enjoyment, I shall thereafter attain old age.

shloka_text: यदुस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच नरर्षभम् । पुत्रस्ते दयितः पूरुः प्रतिगृह्णातु वै जराम् ।। 7.59.4 ।।
explanation: Yadu, having heard that speech, replied to the best of men: "Let your beloved son Puru indeed accept old age."

shloka_text: बहिष्कृतो ऽहमर्थेषु सन्निकर्षाच्च पार्थिव । प्रतिगृह्णातु वै राजन्क सहाश्नाति भोजनम् ।। 7.59.5 ।।
explanation: I am excluded from affairs and from proximity, O King. Indeed, O King, who would accept (me)? Who would eat food together with me?

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत् । इयं जरा महाबाहो मदर्थं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ।। 7.59.6 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, the king then said to Puru, 'O mighty-armed one, let this old age be accepted for my sake.'

shloka_text: नाहुषेणैवमुक्तस्तु पूरुः प्राञ्जलिरब्रवीत् । धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि शासने ऽस्मि तव स्थितः ।। 7.59.7 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Nahusha, Puru, with folded hands, spoke: "I am blessed, I am favored; I abide by your command."

shloka_text: पूरोर्वचनमाज्ञाय नाहुषः परया मुदा । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे जरां सङ्क्रामयच्च ताम् ।। 7.59.8 ।।
explanation: Having accepted Puru's word, Nahusha's son obtained unequalled joy with supreme delight and transferred that old age.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा तरुणः प्राप्य यज्ञान्सहस्रशः । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि पालयामास मेदिनीम् ।। 7.59.9 ।।
explanation: Then that young king, having performed thousands of sacrifices, ruled the earth for many thousands of years.

shloka_text: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राजा पूरुमथाब्रवीत् । आनयस्व जरां पुत्र न्यासं निर्यातयस्व मे ।। 7.59.10 ।।
explanation: Then, after a long time, the king spoke to Puru: "O son, bring back old age, return the deposit to me."

shloka_text: न्यासभूता मया पुत्र त्वयि सङ्क्रामिता जरा । तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि तां जरां मा व्यथां कृथाः ।। 7.59.11 ।।
explanation: O son, the old age that I transferred to you as a deposit, I will therefore take back that old age. Do not be distressed.

shloka_text: प्रीतश्चास्मि महाबाहो शासनस्य प्रतिग्रहात् । त्वां चाहमभिषेक्ष्यामि प्रीतियुक्तो नराधिपम् ।। 7.59.12 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, I am pleased by the acceptance of the command. And I, being delighted, shall anoint you as king.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा सुतं पूरुं ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः । देवयानीसुतं क्रुद्धो राजा वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.59.13 ।।
explanation: Yayati, the son of Nahusha, having thus spoken to his son Puru, then, enraged, the king spoke words to Devayani's son.

shloka_text: राक्षसस्त्वं मया जातः पुत्ररूपो दुरासदः । प्रतिहंसि ममाज्ञां यत् प्रजार्थे विफलो भव ।। 7.59.14 ।।
explanation: You are a formidable demon, born by me in the form of a son. Since you defy my command, be fruitless regarding progeny.

shloka_text: पितरं गुरुभूतं मां यस्मात्त्वमवमन्यसे । राक्षसान्यातुधानांस्त्वं जनयिष्यसि दारुणान् ।। 7.59.15 ।।
explanation: Since you disrespect me, your father and venerable one, you will give birth to terrible Rākṣasas and Yātudhānas.

shloka_text: न तु सोमकुलोत्पन्ने वंशे स्थास्यति दुर्मतेः । वंशो ऽपि भवतस्तुल्यो दुर्विनीतो भविष्यति ।। 7.59.16 ।।
explanation: But the lineage of the wicked one, born in the Soma dynasty, will not endure. Your lineage also will become ill-behaved, just like you.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिः पूरुं राज्यविवर्धनम् । अभिषेकेण सम्पूज्य आश्रमं प्रविवेश ह ।। 7.59.17 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Puru, the enhancer of the kingdom, the royal sage, having honored him with consecration, entered the hermitage.

shloka_text: ततः कालेन महता दिष्टान्तमुपजग्मिवान् । त्रिदिवं सङ्गतो राजा ययातिर्नहुषात्मजः ।। 7.59.18 ।।
explanation: Then, after a long time, King Yayati, the son of Nahusha, met his end and went to heaven.

shloka_text: पूरुश्चकार तद्राज्यं धर्मेण महता वृतः । प्रतिष्ठाने पुरवरे काशिराज्ये महायशाः ।। 7.59.19 ।।
explanation: The greatly renowned Pūru ruled that kingdom with great righteousness, in Pratiṣṭhāna, the excellent city, in the kingdom of Kashi.

shloka_text: यदुस्तु जनयामास यातुधानान्सहस्रशः । पुरे क्रौञ्चवने दुर्गे राजवंशबहिष्कृतः ।। 7.59.20 ।।
explanation: But Yadu, having been expelled from the royal lineage, begot thousands of Rakshasas in the stronghold of Kraunchavana.

shloka_text: एष तूशनसा मुक्तः शापोत्सर्गो ययातिना । धारितः क्षत्रधर्मेण यन्निमिश्च न चक्षमे ।। 7.59.21 ।।
explanation: This curse, uttered by Uśanas, was indeed endured by Yayati in accordance with the Kshatriya dharma, which Nimi also could not tolerate.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं दर्शनं सर्वकारिणाम् । अनुवर्तामहे सौम्य दोषो न स्याद्यथा नृगे ।। 7.59.22 ।।
explanation: All this understanding of all agents has been explained to you. O gentle one, we shall act so that no fault may occur, just as it did to Nṛga.

shloka_text: इति कथयति रामे चन्द्रतुल्यानने च प्रविरलतरतारं व्योम जज्ञे तदानीम् । अरुणकिरणरक्ता दिग्बभौ चैव पूर्वा कुसुमरसविमुक्तं वस्त्रमाकुण्ठितेव ।। 7.59.23 ।।
explanation: As Rama, whose face was like the moon, spoke thus, the sky at that time became sparsely starred. And the eastern direction shone, reddened by the rays of dawn, like a garment unfurled, fresh from flower-dye.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 59 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by the sage.

shloka_text: तयोः संवदतोरेवं रामलक्ष्मणयोस्तदा । वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च घर्मदा ।। 7.60.1 ।।
explanation: As Rama and Lakshmana were thus conversing, a spring night arrived, neither cold nor hot.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतपौर्वाह्णिकक्रियः । अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थो दर्शनं पौरकार्यवित् ।। 7.60.2 ।।
explanation: Then, in the clear morning, Kakutstha, having performed his morning rituals and being knowledgeable about the citizens' affairs, went to grant an audience.

shloka_text: ततः सुमन्त्रस्त्वागम्य राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । एते प्रतिहता राजन्द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति तापसाः ।। 7.60.3 ।।
explanation: Then Sumantra, having approached Rama, spoke these words: 'O King, these ascetics are standing at the door, having been stopped.'

shloka_text: भार्गवच्यवनं चैव पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः । दर्शनं ते महाराज्ञश्चोदयन्ति कृतत्वराः । प्रीयमाणा नरव्याघ्र यमुनातीरवासिनः ।। 7.60.4 ।।
explanation: And having honored Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, the great sages, residents of the Yamuna bank, being pleased, O tiger among men, quickly urged for an audience with the great king.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित् । प्रवेश्यन्तां महाभागा भार्गवप्रमुखा द्विजाः ।। 7.60.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, Rama, the knower of righteousness, said: "Let the venerable Brahmins, led by Bhargava, be admitted."

shloka_text: राज्ञस्त्वाज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । प्रवेशयामास तदा तापसान्सुदुरासदान् ।। 7.60.6 ।।
explanation: Then, the doorkeeper, honoring the king's command, with folded hands placed on his head, admitted the very formidable ascetics.

shloka_text: शतं समधिकं तत्र दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । प्रविष्टं राजभवनं तापसानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.60.7 ।।
explanation: There, more than a hundred great-souled ascetics, radiant with their own splendor, entered the royal palace.

shloka_text: ते द्विजाः पूर्णकलशैः सर्वतीर्थाम्बुसत्कृतैः । गृहीत्वा फलमूलं च रामस्याभ्याहरन्बहु ।। 7.60.8 ।।
explanation: Those Brahmins, with full pitchers consecrated with water from all sacred fords, brought many fruits and roots for Rama.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तु तत्सर्वं रामः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः । तीर्थोदकानि सर्वाणि फलानि विविधानि च ।। 7.60.9 ।।
explanation: Rama, filled with joy, accepted all those sacred waters and various fruits.

shloka_text: उवाच च महाबाहुः सर्वानेव महामुनीन् । इमान्यासनमुख्यानि यथार्हमुपविश्यताम् ।। 7.60.10 ।।
explanation: And the mighty-armed one said to all the great sages: "Please be seated suitably on these excellent seats."

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः । बृसीषु रुचिराख्यासु निषेदुः काञ्चनीषु ते ।। 7.60.11 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, all the great sages sat down on the beautiful golden seats.

shloka_text: उपविष्टानृषींस्तत्र दृष्ट्वा परपुरञ्जयः । प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा राघवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.60.12 ।।
explanation: Having seen the sages seated there, Rama, the conqueror of enemy cities, reverently folded his hands and spoke these words.

shloka_text: किमागमनकार्यं वः किं करोमि समाहितः । आज्ञाप्यो ऽहं महर्षीणां सर्वकामकरः सुखम् ।। 7.60.13 ।।
explanation: What is the purpose of your coming? What shall I do, being attentive? I am at the command of the great sages, a fulfiller of all desires with ease.

shloka_text: इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम् । सर्वमेतद्द्विदार्थं मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि वः ।। 7.60.14 ।।
explanation: This entire kingdom and my life, which is dear to my heart, all this is for Dvivida's sake. This truth I tell to you.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा साधुकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां यमुनातीरवासिनाम् ।। 7.60.15 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, a great applause arose from the sages of severe austerities who dwelt on the banks of the Yamuna.

shloka_text: ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः ।। 7.60.16 ।।
explanation: And those great souls, filled with great joy, said: 'This is fitting for you alone on earth, O best of men, and for no one else.'

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवा राजन्नतिक्रान्ता महाबलाः । कार्यस्य गौरवं मत्वा प्रतिज्ञां नाभ्यरोचयन् ।। 7.60.17 ।।
explanation: O King, many mighty kings of the past, having considered the gravity of the task, did not approve of the vow.

shloka_text: त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम् । ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो महाभयात्ऺत्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि ।। 7.60.18 ।।
explanation: You, moreover, made this vow out of respect for Brahmins, indeed without considering the reason. Therefore, you will surely fulfill it; there is no doubt in this. You ought to protect the sages from great fear.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 60 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the glorious first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the sixtieth chapter.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवद्भिर्ऋषिभिः काकुत्स्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । किं कार्यं ब्रूत मुनयो भयं तावदपैतु वः ।। 7.61.1 ।।
explanation: When the sages spoke thus, Kakutstha said: "What is the task? Tell me, O sages. Let your fear depart for now."

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे भार्गवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । भयानां शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर ।। 7.61.2 ।।
explanation: When Kakutstha spoke thus, Bhargava said: "O King, listen to that which is the root cause of the fears and of the country."

shloka_text: पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन्दैतेयः सुमहाबलः । लोलापुत्रो ऽभवज्ज्येष्ठो मधुर्नाम महासुरः ।। 7.61.3 ।।
explanation: O King, formerly, in the Krita Yuga, there was a Daitya of very great strength, the eldest son of Lola, named Madhu, a great Asura.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः । सुरैश्च परमोदारैः प्रीतिस्तस्यातुला ऽभवत् ।। 7.61.4 ।।
explanation: He was devoted to Brahmins, a protector, and resolute in wisdom. And his unequalled affection was with the most noble gods.

shloka_text: स मधुर्वीर्यसम्पन्नो धर्मे च सुसमाहितः । बहुवर्षसहस्राणि रुद्रप्रीत्या ऽकरोत्तपः ।। 7.61.5 ।।
explanation: That Madhu, endowed with valor and well-established in righteousness, performed penance for many thousands of years to please Rudra.

shloka_text: रुद्रः प्रीतो ऽभवत्तस्मै वरं दातुं ययौ च सः । बहुमानाच्च रुद्रेण दत्तस्तस्याद्भुतो वरः ।। 7.61.6 ।।
explanation: Rudra became pleased with him, and he went to grant a boon. And Rudra, out of great esteem, gave him a wonderful boon.

shloka_text: शूलं शूलाद्विनिष्कृष्य महावीर्यं महाप्रभम् । ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह ।। 7.61.7 ।।
explanation: Having drawn out the spear of great power and great splendor from its source, the great-souled one, greatly pleased, gave it and spoke these words.

shloka_text: त्वयायमतुलो धर्मो मत्प्रसादकरः कृतः । प्रीत्या परमया युक्तो ददाम्यायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.61.8 ।।
explanation: This unequalled righteous deed, which pleases me, has been performed by you. Filled with supreme affection, I give you an excellent weapon.

shloka_text: यावत्सुरैश्च विप्रैश्च न विरुध्येर्महासुर । तावच्छूलं तवेदं स्यादन्यथा नाशमेप्यति ।। 7.61.9 ।।
explanation: O great demon, as long as you do not oppose the gods and the brahmins, this spear shall be yours. Otherwise, it will be destroyed.

shloka_text: यश्च त्वामभियुञ्जीत युद्धाय विगतज्वरः । तं शूलो भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम् ।। 7.61.10 ।।
explanation: And whoever, fearless, challenges you for battle, that spear, having reduced him to ashes, will return to your hand again.

shloka_text: एवं रुद्राद्वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः । प्रणिपत्य महादेवं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.61.11 ।।
explanation: Thus, having obtained a boon from Rudra, the great demon, bowing down to Mahadeva, spoke these words again.

shloka_text: भगवन्मम वंशस्य शूलमेतदनुत्तमम् । भवेत्तु सततं देव सुराणामीश्वरो ह्यसि ।। 7.61.12 ।।
explanation: O Lord, may this unsurpassed torment always be for my lineage, O God, for you are indeed the lord of the gods.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजा नैतदेवं भविष्यति ।। 7.61.13 ।।
explanation: The greatly effulgent god Shiva, the lord of all beings, replied to Madhu who was speaking: "This will not happen thus."

shloka_text: मा भूत्ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा । भवतः पुत्रमेकं तु शूलमेतद्भजिष्यते ।। 7.61.14 ।।
explanation: May your auspicious words, spoken by my grace, not be fruitless. But this spear will indeed befall one of your sons.

shloka_text: यावत्करस्थः शूलो ऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते । अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां शूलहस्तो भविष्यति ।। 7.61.15 ।।
explanation: As long as this spear is in your son's hand, he will be invulnerable to all beings, being the one with the spear in hand.

shloka_text: एवं मधुर्वरं लब्ध्वा देवात्सुमहदद्भुतम् । भवनं सो ऽसुरश्रेष्ठः कारयामास सुप्रभम् ।। 7.61.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, Madhu, having obtained a very great and wonderful boon from the god, that chief of Asuras caused a very splendid palace to be built.

shloka_text: तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसीति या । विश्वावसोरपत्यं सा ह्यनलायां महाप्रभा ।। 7.61.17 ।।
explanation: His highly fortunate and beloved wife, who was named Kumbhinasi, she was the daughter of Vishvavasu, born from Anala, and of great splendor.

shloka_text: तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः । बाल्यात्प्रभृति दुष्टात्मा पापान्येव समाचरत् ।। 7.61.18 ।।
explanation: Her son, named Lavana, was exceedingly powerful and terrible. From childhood onwards, that evil-minded one committed only sins.

shloka_text: तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः । मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किञ्चिदब्रवीत् ।। 7.61.19 ।।
explanation: Seeing that ill-behaved son, Madhu, filled with anger, became sorrowful and did not say anything to him.

shloka_text: स विहाय त्विमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम् । शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ।। 7.61.20 ।।
explanation: He, having abandoned this world, entered the abode of Varuna. Having placed his trident in the ocean, he offered a boon to him.

shloka_text: स प्रभावेण शूलस्य दौरात्म्येनात्मनस्तथा । सन्तापयति लोकांस्त्रीन्विशेषेण च तापसान् ।। 7.61.21 ।।
explanation: By the power of the trident and by his own wickedness, he torments the three worlds, especially the ascetics.

shloka_text: एवंप्रभावो लवणः शूलं चैव तथाविधम् । श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः ।। 7.61.22 ।।
explanation: Having heard the truth about Lavana's power and his trident of that nature, O Kakutstha, you are indeed our supreme refuge.

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवा राम भयार्तैर्ऋषिभिः पुरा । अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे ।। 7.61.23 ।।
explanation: O Rama, O hero, in the past, many kings were implored for protection by the sages afflicted with fear, but we do not find a protector.

shloka_text: ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम् । त्रातारं विद्महे तात नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम् । तत्परित्रातुमिच्छामो लवणाद्भयपीडितान् ।। 7.61.24 ।।
explanation: Having heard that Ravana, along with his army and vehicles, has been slain, O dear one, we know no other king on earth as a protector. Therefore, we wish to protect those afflicted by fear from Lavana.

shloka_text: इति राम निवेदितं तु ते भयजं कारणमुत्थितं च यत् । विनिवारयितुं भवान्क्षमः कुरु तं काममहीनविक्रम ।। 7.61.25 ।।
explanation: O Rama, this has been reported to you, and whatever cause has arisen from fear, you are capable of preventing it. O one of undiminished valor, accomplish that task.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 61 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered and glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the sixty-first chapter.

shloka_text: तथोक्ते तानृषीन्रामः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिः । किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते ।। 7.62.1 ।।
explanation: When thus addressed, Rama, with folded hands, replied to those sages: 'What is Lavana's diet? What is his conduct? And where does he reside?'

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते । ततो निवेदयामासुर्लवणो ववृधे यथा ।। 7.62.2 ।।
explanation: Having heard Raghava's words, all those sages then informed him how Lavana had grown.

shloka_text: आहारः सर्वसत्त्वानि विशेषेण च तापसाः । आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा ।। 7.62.3 ।।
explanation: Their food is all beings, especially ascetics. Their conduct is always fierce, and their dwelling is in Madhuvana.

shloka_text: हत्वा बहुसहस्राणि सिंहव्याघ्रमृगद्विपान् । मानुषांश्चैव कुरुते नित्यमाहारमाह्निकम् ।। 7.62.4 ।।
explanation: Having killed many thousands of lions, tigers, deer, and elephants, and also humans, he constantly makes them his daily food.

shloka_text: ततो ऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः । संहारे समनुप्राप्ते व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः ।। 7.62.5 ।।
explanation: Then, that mighty one devours the beings within, like Antaka (the god of death) with a gaping mouth when the time of dissolution has arrived.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यमुवाच स महामुनीन् । घातयिष्यामि तद्रक्षो ह्यपगच्छतु वो भयम् ।। 7.62.6 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, Rama said to the great sages: "I will slay that demon; let your fear depart."

shloka_text: प्रतिज्ञाय तथा तेषां मुनीनामुग्रतेजसाम् । स भ्रातऽन्सहितान्सर्वानुवाच रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.7 ।।
explanation: Having thus promised to those sages of fierce ascetic power, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, spoke to all his brothers who were assembled.

shloka_text: को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम् । भरतस्य महाबाहोः शत्रुघ्नस्य च धीमतः ।। 7.62.8 ।।
explanation: Who is the brave one to kill Lavana? To whom among the mighty-armed Bharata and the intelligent Shatrughna should that task be assigned?

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु भरतो वाक्यमब्रवीत् । अहमेनं वधिष्यामि ममांशः स विधीयताम् ।। 7.62.9 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Raghava, Bharata spoke these words: "I will kill him; let that be my share."

shloka_text: भरतस्य वचः श्रुत्वा धैर्यशौर्यसमन्वितम् । लक्ष्मणावरजस्तस्थौ हित्वा सौवर्णमासनम् ।। 7.62.10 ।।
explanation: Having heard Bharata's words, which were imbued with courage and valor, Lakṣmaṇa's younger brother (Shatrughna) stood up, abandoning his golden seat.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं प्रणिपत्य नराधिपम् । कृतकर्मा महाबाहुर्मध्यमो रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.62.11 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna, having bowed down to the king, spoke these words: "The mighty-armed scion of Raghu, the middle one, has accomplished his task."

shloka_text: आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता । सन्तापं हृदये कृत्वा आर्यस्यागमनं प्रति ।। 7.62.12 ।।
explanation: Indeed, formerly, Ayodhya, desolate (without the noble one), was protected by the noble one, who, having placed sorrow in his heart, awaited the noble one's arrival.

shloka_text: दुःखानि च बहूनीह ह्यनुभूतानि पार्थिव । शयानो दुःखशय्यासु नन्दिग्रामे ऽवसत्पुरा ।। 7.62.13 ।।
explanation: O King, many sorrows were indeed experienced here. He formerly lived in Nandigrama, lying on beds of sorrow.

shloka_text: फलमूलाशनो भूत्वा जटी चीरधरस्तथा । अनुभूयेदृशं दुःखमेष राघवनन्दनः । प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात् ।। 7.62.14 ।।
explanation: Having become an eater of fruits and roots, with matted hair and wearing bark garments, this son of Raghu, having experienced such sorrow, should not, O King, suffer further distress while I am present as his servant.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति शत्रुघ्ने राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम् ।। 7.62.15 ।।
explanation: When Shatrughna spoke thus, Rama spoke again: "So be it, O Kakutstha. Let my command be carried out."

shloka_text: राज्ये त्वामभिषेक्ष्यामि मधोस्तु नगरे शुभे । निवेशय महाबाहो भरतं यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.16 ।।
explanation: I will consecrate you in the kingdom, in the auspicious city of Madhu. O mighty-armed one, establish Bharata, if you deem it proper.

shloka_text: शूरस्त्वं कृतविद्यश्च समर्थश्च निवेशने ।। 7.62.17 ।।
explanation: You are brave, learned, and capable in the household.

shloka_text: यो हि शत्रुं समुत्पाट्य पार्थिवस्य पुनः क्षये । न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति ।। 7.62.18 ।।
explanation: He who, having uprooted an enemy, does not establish a king there again in the absence of a ruler, he indeed goes to hell.

shloka_text: स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम् । राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे ।। 7.62.19 ।।
explanation: You, therefore, having slain Lavana, the son of Madhu, who is of evil resolve, rule the kingdom righteously, if you heed my word.

shloka_text: उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम । बालेन पूर्वजस्याज्ञा कर्तव्या नात्र संशयः ।। 7.62.20 ।।
explanation: And no answer should be spoken by you, O hero, interrupting my words. A child must obey the command of an elder; there is no doubt about this.

shloka_text: अभिषेकं च काकुत्स्थ प्रतीच्छस्व मयोद्यतम् । वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्विप्रैर्विधिमन्त्रपुरस्कृतम् ।। 7.62.21 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, please accept this coronation prepared by me, which is performed with rituals and mantras by Brahmins headed by Vasishtha.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 62।।
explanation: Thus ends the sixty-second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem composed by Valmiki, a sacred text by a Rishi.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण परां व्रीडामुपागमत् । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह ।। 7.63.1 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Shatrughna, endowed with valor, felt great shame and spoke very slowly.

shloka_text: अधर्मं विद्म काकुत्स्थ ह्यस्मिन्नर्थे नरेश्वर । कथं तिष्ठत्सु ज्येष्ठेषु कनीयानभिषिच्यते ।। 7.63.2 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, O lord of men, we know this to be unrighteousness in this matter. How can the younger one be consecrated while the elders are present?

shloka_text: अवश्यं करणीयं च शासनं पुरुषर्षभ । तव चैव महाभाग शासनं दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.63.3 ।।
explanation: O best among men, your command must certainly be carried out. And indeed, O illustrious one, your command is inviolable.

shloka_text: त्वत्तो मया श्रुतं वीर श्रुतिभ्यश्च मया श्रुतम् । नोत्तरं हि मया वाच्यं मध्यमे प्रतिजानति ।। 7.63.4 ।।
explanation: O hero, I have heard from you, and I have heard from the scriptures. Indeed, I should not speak a reply when the mediator makes a declaration.

shloka_text: व्याहृतं दुर्वचो घोरं हन्तास्मि लवणं मृधे । तस्यैवं मे दुरुक्तस्य दुर्गतिः पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.63.5 ।।
explanation: Terrible, harsh words have been spoken: 'I will kill Lavana in battle.' For me, who has spoken such ill, there will be misfortune, O best among men.

shloka_text: उत्तरं नहि वक्तव्यं ज्येष्ठेनाभिहिते पुनः । अधर्मसहितं चैव परलोकविवर्जितम् ।। 7.63.6 ।।
explanation: A reply should not be given again when an elder has spoken, especially if it is unrighteous and not conducive to the afterlife.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं द्वितीयं काकुत्स्थ न वक्ष्यामि तवोत्तरम् । मा द्वितीयेन दण्डो वै निपतेन्मयि मानद ।। 7.63.7 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Kakutstha, I will not give you a second answer. Lest, O giver of honor, a second punishment indeed fall upon me.

shloka_text: कामकारो ह्यहं राजंस्तवास्मि पुरुषर्षभ । अधर्मं जहि काकुत्स्थ मत्कृते रघुनन्दन ।। 7.63.8 ।।
explanation: O King, O best among men, I am indeed at your disposal. O Kakutstha, O delight of the Raghus, abandon unrighteousness for my sake.

shloka_text: एवमुक्ते तु शूरेण शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । उवाच रामः संहृष्टो भरतं लक्ष्मणं तथा ।। 7.63.9 ।।
explanation: When thus spoken by the brave and great-souled Shatrughna, Rama, greatly delighted, spoke to Bharata and Lakshmana.

shloka_text: सम्भारानभिषेकस्य आनयध्वं समाहिताः । अद्यैव पुरुषव्याघ्रमभिषेक्ष्यामि राघवम् ।। 7.63.10 ।।
explanation: Bring the preparations for the coronation, attentively. Today itself I shall coronate Rama, the tiger among men.

shloka_text: पुरोहितं च काकुत्स्थं नैगमानृत्विजस्तथा । मन्त्रिणश्चैव तान्सर्वानानयध्वं ममाज्ञया ।। 7.63.11 ।।
explanation: Bring the royal priest, and Kakutstha, and the citizens, and the sacrificial priests, and the ministers – all of them – by my command.

shloka_text: राज्ञः शासनमाज्ञाय तथा ऽकुर्वन्महारथाः । अभिषेकसमारम्भं पुरस्कृत्य पुरोधसम् । प्रविष्टा राजभवनं राजानो ब्राह्मणास्तथा ।। 7.63.12 ।।
explanation: Having understood the king's command, the great charioteers acted accordingly. Kings and Brahmins, with the chief priest leading the commencement of the anointing, entered the royal palace.

shloka_text: तथो ऽभिषेको ववृधे शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । सम्प्रहर्षकरः श्रीमान्राघवस्य पुरस्य च ।। 7.63.13 ।।
explanation: Thus, the glorious anointing of the great-souled Shatrughna flourished, causing great joy to Rama and the city.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्तस्तु शत्रुघ्नो बभौ चादित्यसन्निभः । अभिषिक्तः पुरा स्कन्दः सेन्द्रैरिव मरुद्गणैः ।। 7.63.14 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna, having been consecrated, shone like the sun, just as Skanda was consecrated formerly by the hosts of Maruts along with Indra.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्ते तु शत्रुघ्ने रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा । पौराः प्रमुदिताश्चासन्ब्राह्मणाश्च बहुश्रुताः ।। 7.63.15 ।।
explanation: When Shatrughna was consecrated by Rama, the one of unblemished deeds, the citizens were greatly delighted, and so were the very learned Brahmins.

shloka_text: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च मङ्गलं केकयी तथा । चक्रुस्ता राजभवने याश्चान्या राजयोषितः ।। 7.63.16 ।।
explanation: Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi, and also other royal women, performed auspicious rites in the royal palace.

shloka_text: ऋषयश्च महात्मानो यमुनातीरवासिनः । हतं लवणमाशंसुः शत्रुघ्नस्याभिषेचनात् ।। 7.63.17 ।।
explanation: The great-souled Rishis dwelling on the banks of the Yamuna hoped for Lavana's death upon Shatrughna's anointing.

shloka_text: ततो ऽभिषिक्तं शत्रुघ्नमङ्कमारोप्य राघवः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं तेजस्तस्याभिपूरयन् ।। 7.63.18 ।।
explanation: Then, Rama, having placed the consecrated Shatrughna on his lap, spoke sweet words, augmenting his splendor.

shloka_text: अयं शरस्त्वमोघस्ते दिव्यः परपुरञ्जयः । अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्ता ऽसि रघुनन्दन ।। 7.63.19 ।।
explanation: This arrow of yours is indeed unfailing, divine, and a conqueror of enemy cities. With this, O gentle one, O scion of Raghu, you shall slay Lavana.

shloka_text: सृष्टः शरो ऽयं काकुत्स्थ यदा शेते महार्णवे ।। 7.63.20 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, when this arrow, once discharged, lies in the great ocean.

shloka_text: स्वयम्भूरजितो देवो यन्नापश्यन्सुरासुराः । अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां तेनायं तु शरोत्तमः ।। 7.63.21 ।।
explanation: Which (arrow) Svayambhu, the unconquered god, did not see, nor did the gods and demons. Invisible to all beings, therefore, this is indeed the best of arrows.

shloka_text: सृष्टः क्रोधाभिभूतेन विनाशार्थं दुरात्मनोः । मधुकैटभयोर्वीर विघाते वर्तमानयोः । स्रष्टुकामेन लोकांस्त्रींस्तौ चानेन हतौ युधि ।। 7.63.22 ।।
explanation: O hero, (he) was created by one overwhelmed by anger for the destruction of the two wicked Madhu and Kaitabha, who were obstructing (the creation). And those two were killed in battle by him who desired to create the three worlds

shloka_text: तौ हत्वा जनभोगार्थं कैटभं तु मधुं तथा । अनेन शरमुख्येन ततो लोकांश्चकार सः ।। 7.63.23 ।।
explanation: Having killed those two, Kaitabha and Madhu, for the enjoyment of people, he then created the worlds with this chief arrow.

shloka_text: नायं मया शरः पूर्वं रावणस्य वधार्थिना । मुक्तः शत्रुघ्न भूतानां महांस्त्रासो भवेदिति ।। 7.63.24 ।।
explanation: O Shatrughna, this arrow was not released by me before, even when I sought to kill Ravana, thinking that it would cause great terror to all beings.

shloka_text: यच्च तस्य महच्छूलं त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना । दत्तं शत्रुविनाशाय मधोरायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.63.25 ।।
explanation: And that great trident of his, an excellent weapon of Madhu, was given by the great-souled Tryambaka for the destruction of enemies.

shloka_text: स तं निक्षिप्य भवने पूज्यमान पुनः पुनः । दिशः सर्वाः समासाद्य प्राप्नोत्याहारमुत्तमम् ।। 7.63.26 ।।
explanation: He, being worshipped again and again, having placed him in the house, having reached all directions, obtains excellent food.

shloka_text: यदा तु युद्धमाकाङ्क्षन् कश्चिदेनं समाह्वयेत् । तदा शूलं गहीत्वा तं भस्म रक्षः करोति हि ।। 7.63.27 ।।
explanation: However, when someone, desiring battle, challenges him, then the Rākṣasa, taking a spear, certainly turns him into ashes.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमायुधविनाकृतम् । अप्रविष्टं पुरं पूर्वं द्वारि तिष्ठ धृतायुधः ।। 7.63.28 ।।
explanation: You, O tiger among men, stand at the gate, weapon in hand, (facing) him who is weaponless and has not yet entered the city.

shloka_text: अप्रविष्टं च भवनं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभ । आह्वयेथा महाबाहो ततो हन्तासि राक्षसम् ।। 7.63.29 ।।
explanation: O best among men, O mighty-armed one, challenge him for battle without entering his dwelling. Then you will kill the demon.

shloka_text: अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु अवध्यः स भविष्यति । यदि त्वेवं कृते वीर विनाशमुपयास्यति ।। 7.63.30 ।।
explanation: If it is done otherwise, he will become unslayable. But if it is done thus, O hero, he will meet destruction.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शूलस्य च विपर्ययः । श्रीमतः शितिकण्ठस्य कृत्यं हि दुरतिक्रमम् ।। 7.63.31 ।।
explanation: All this has been narrated to you, and the transformation of the trident. For the deed of the glorious blue-throated one is indeed irresistible.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 63 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the sixty-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the revered Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा च काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः । पुनरेवापरं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.64.1 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Kakutstha and repeatedly praised him, Raghunandana then spoke another word.

shloka_text: इमान्यश्वसहस्राणि चत्वारि पुरुषर्षभ । रथानां द्वे सहस्रे च गजानां शतमुत्तमम् ।। 7.64.2 ।।
explanation: O best among men, these are four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, and a hundred excellent elephants.

shloka_text: अन्तरा पणवीथ्यश्च नानापण्योपशोभिताः । अनुगच्छन्तु काकुत्स्थं तथैव नटनर्तकाः ।। 7.64.3 ।।
explanation: Let the market streets, adorned with various goods, and likewise, the actors and dancers, follow Kakutstha.

shloka_text: हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य नियुतं पुरुषर्षभ । आदाय गच्छ शत्रुघ्न पर्याप्तधनवाहनः ।। 7.64.4 ।।
explanation: O best among men, O Shatrughna, having taken a million [units] of gold, go, [you will be] sufficiently endowed with wealth and conveyances.

shloka_text: बलं च सुभृतं वीर हृष्टपुष्टमनुद्धतम् । सम्भाषासम्प्रदानेन रञ्जयस्व नगेत्तम ।। 7.64.5 ।।
explanation: O hero, O best among mountains, please your well-maintained, cheerful, strong, and disciplined army with kind words and gifts.

shloka_text: न ह्यर्थास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः । सुप्रीतो भृत्यवर्गश्च यत्र तिष्ठसि राघव ।। 7.64.6 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, where you reside, indeed, wealth does not remain, nor wives, nor relatives, but the group of servants is very pleased.

shloka_text: ततो हृष्टजनाकीर्णां प्रस्थाप्य महतीं चमूम् । एक एव धनुष्पाणिर्गच्छ त्वं मधुनो वनम् ।। 7.64.7 ।।
explanation: Then, having dispatched a great army filled with joyful people, you alone, bow in hand, go to the forest of Madhu.

shloka_text: यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम् । लवणस्तु मधोः पुत्रस्तथा गच्छेरशङ्कितम् ।। 7.64.8 ।।
explanation: You should go unhesitatingly, so that Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, does not recognize you as one going and desiring battle.

shloka_text: न तस्य मूत्युरन्यो ऽस्ति कश्चिद्धि पुरुषर्षभ । दर्शनं यो ऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि ।। 7.64.9 ।।
explanation: O best among men, indeed, there is no other death for him. Whoever comes into his sight, he is certainly to be killed by Lavaṇa.

shloka_text: स हि ग्रीष्मो ऽपयाते तु वर्षारात्र उपागते । हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य सहि कालो ऽस्य दुर्मतेः ।। 7.64.10 ।।
explanation: When summer has indeed departed and the rainy season has arrived, you should kill Lavaṇa, O gentle one. That indeed is the time for this wicked one.

shloka_text: महर्षींस्तु पुरत्कृत्य प्रयान्तु तव सौनिकाः । यथा ग्रीष्मावशेषेण तरेयुर्जाह्नवीजलम् ।। 7.64.11 ।।
explanation: Let your soldiers proceed, with the great sages leading, so that they may cross the waters of the Jahnavi (Ganga) as one would at the end of summer.

shloka_text: तत्र स्थाप्य बलं सर्वं नदीतीरे समाहितः । अग्रतो धनुषा सार्धं गच्छ त्वं लघुविक्रमः ।। 7.64.12 ।।
explanation: Having stationed your entire army there on the river bank, you, being attentive and swift in valor, go forth with your bow.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण शत्रुघ्नस्तान्महाबलान् । सेनामुख्यान्समानीय ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.64.13 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Rama, Shatrughna, having assembled those mighty army chiefs, then spoke.

shloka_text: एते वो गणिता वासा यत्र तत्र निवत्स्यथ । स्थातव्यं चाविरोधेन यथा बाधा न कस्यचित् ।। 7.64.14 ।।
explanation: These are your allotted dwellings; you shall reside wherever. And you must remain without conflict, so that no one is troubled.

shloka_text: तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य प्रस्थाप्य च महद्बलम् । कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत् ।। 7.64.15 ।।
explanation: Thus, having commanded them and dispatched a great army, he then greeted Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi.

shloka_text: रामं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य शिरसा ऽभिप्रणम्य च । रामेण चाभ्यनुज्ञातः शत्रुघ्नः शत्रुतापनः ।। 7.64.16 ।।
explanation: Having circumambulated Rama and bowed down with his head, and having been permitted by Rama, Shatrughna, the tormentor of foes...

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव प्रणिपत्य कृताञ्जलिः । पुरोहितं वसिष्ठं च शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान् । प्रदक्षिणमथो कृत्वा निर्जगाम महाबलः ।। 7.64.17 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna, the self-controlled and mighty one, bowed down with folded hands to Lakshmana, Bharata, and the priest Vasishtha. Then, having circumambulated them, he departed.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य सेनामथ सो ऽग्रतस्तदा गजेन्द्रवाजिप्रवरौघसङ्कुलाम् । उपास मासं तु नरेन्द्रपार्श्वतस्त्वथ प्रयातो रघुवंशवर्धनः ।। 7.64.18 ।।
explanation: Then, having sent forth that army, teeming with multitudes of excellent elephants and horses, ahead, the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty stayed for a month beside the king, and then departed.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 64 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the sixty-fourth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the revered and original epic, Valmiki's Ramayana.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य च बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि । एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितं तदा ।। 7.65.1 ।।
explanation: And having dispatched all the army, and having stayed on the path for only a month, Shatrughna alone then departed with great speed.

shloka_text: द्विरात्रमन्तरे शूर उष्य राघवनन्दनः । वाल्मीकेराश्रमं पुण्यमगच्छद्वासमुत्तमम् ।। 7.65.2 ।।
explanation: Having stayed for two nights, the heroic son of Raghu went to the excellent and sacred hermitage of Valmiki for his dwelling.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाल्मीकिं मुनिसत्तमम् । कृताञ्जलिरथो भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.65.3 ।।
explanation: Having saluted the great-souled Valmiki, the best among sages, he then, with folded hands, spoke these words.

shloka_text: भगवन्वस्तुमिच्छामि गुरोः कृत्यादिहागतः । श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीचीं वारुणीं दिशम् ।। 7.65.4 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I wish to stay here, having come from a task for my guru. Tomorrow morning, I will go to the western direction.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुङ्गवः । प्रत्युवाच महात्मानं स्वागतं ते महायशः ।। 7.65.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard Shatrughna's words, the foremost among sages, smiling, replied to the great-souled one, "Welcome to you, O greatly renowned one!"

shloka_text: स्वमाश्रममिदं सौम्य राघवाणां कुलस्य हि । आसनं पाद्यमर्ध्यं च निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ मे ।। 7.65.6 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, this hermitage is my own, and indeed it is for the family of the Raghus. Accept from me, without hesitation, a seat, water for your feet, and an offering.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य तदा पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम् । भक्षयामास काकुत्स्थस्तृप्तिं च परमां गतः ।। 7.65.7 ।।
explanation: Then, having accepted the worship and the food consisting of fruits and roots, Kakutstha ate and attained supreme satisfaction.

shloka_text: स भुक्त्वा फलमूलं च महर्षिं तमुवाच ह । इयं यज्ञविभूतिस्ते कस्याश्रमसमीपतः ।। 7.65.8 ।।
explanation: Having eaten fruits and roots, he said to that great sage: "This sacrificial splendor of yours, near whose hermitage is it?"

shloka_text: तत्तस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा वाल्मीकिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् । शत्रुघ्न शृणु यस्येदं बभूवायतनं पुरा ।। 7.65.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, Valmiki spoke: "O Shatrughna, listen, whose abode this was formerly."

shloka_text: युष्माकं पूर्वको राजा सौदासस्तस्य भूपतेः । पुत्रो वीरसहो नाम वीर्यवानतिधार्मिकः ।। 7.65.10 ।।
explanation: Your former king was Saudasa. That king's son was named Virasaha, who was valorous and extremely righteous.

shloka_text: स बाल एव सौदासो मृगयामुपचक्रमे । चञ्चूर्यमाणं ददृशे स शूरो राक्षसद्वयम् ।। 7.65.11 ।।
explanation: Saudasa, even as a child, began hunting. He, the brave one, saw two demons roaming about.

shloka_text: शार्दूलरूपिणौ घोरौ मृगान्बहुसहस्रशः । भक्षमाणावसन्तुष्टौ पर्याप्तिं नैव जग्मतुः ।। 7.65.12 ।।
explanation: The two terrible ones, in the form of tigers, devouring thousands upon thousands of deer, were unsatisfied and never attained sufficiency.

shloka_text: स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मृगं च वनं कृतम् । क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो जघानैकं महेषुणा ।। 7.65.13 ।।
explanation: But he, having seen those two demons and the forest made devoid of animals, filled with great anger, killed one with a mighty arrow.

shloka_text: विनिपात्य तमेकं तु सौदासः पुरुषर्षभः । विज्वरो विगतामार्षो हतं रक्षो ह्युदैक्षत ।। 7.65.14 ।।
explanation: Having struck down that one, Saudasa, the foremost of men, free from anxiety and his anger gone, looked at the slain Rakshasa.

shloka_text: निरीक्षमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा सहायं तस्य रक्षसः । सन्तापमकरोद्घोरं सौदासं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.65.15 ।।
explanation: Having seen him, the helper of that Rākṣasa, observing, he caused great sorrow to Saudāsa and said this.

shloka_text: यस्मादनपराधं त्वं सहायं मम जघ्निवान् । तस्मात्तवापि पापिष्ठ प्रदास्यामि प्रतिक्रियाम् ।। 7.65.16 ।।
explanation: Since you have killed my innocent companion, therefore, O most sinful one, I will inflict retribution upon you as well.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तद्राक्षस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । कालपर्याययोगेन राजा मित्रसहो ऽभवत् ।। 7.65.17 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, that demon disappeared right there. By the passage of time, the king became Mitrasaha.

shloka_text: राजापि यजते यज्ञमस्याश्रमसमीपतः । अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं तं वसिष्ठो ऽभ्यपालयत् ।। 7.65.18 ।।
explanation: The king also performs a great Ashwamedha sacrifice near his hermitage. Vasishtha supervised it.

shloka_text: तत्र यज्ञो महानासीद्बहुवर्षगणायुतः । समृद्धः परया लक्ष्म्या देवयज्ञसमो ऽभवत् ।। 7.65.19 ।।
explanation: A great sacrifice took place there, lasting for many years. It was endowed with supreme splendor and became equal to a sacrifice of the gods.

shloka_text: अथावसाने यज्ञस्य पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् । वसिष्ठरूपी राजानमिति होवाच राक्षसः ।। 7.65.20 ।।
explanation: Then, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, remembering his former enmity, the demon, disguised as Vasishtha, spoke thus to the king.

shloka_text: अस्य यज्ञस्य जातो ऽन्तः सामिषं भोजनं मम । दीयतामिह शीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।। 7.65.21 ।।
explanation: This sacrifice has ended. My meat meal should be given here quickly; no deliberation is to be made.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं रक्षसा ब्रह्मरूपिणा । भक्ष्यसंस्कारकुशलमुवाच पृथिवीपतिः ।। 7.65.22 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech spoken by the Rākṣasa who had assumed the form of a Brāhmaṇa, the king spoke to the one skilled in preparing food.

shloka_text: हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम् । तथा कुरुष्व शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद्यथा गुरुः ।। 7.65.23 ।।
explanation: Make the food quickly, so that it is wholesome, with meat, and delicious, and the guru may be pleased.

shloka_text: शासनात्पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य सूदः सम्भ्रान्तमानसः । स राक्षसः पुनस्तत्र सूदवेषमथाकरोत् ।। 7.65.24 ।।
explanation: At the command of the king, the cook became bewildered. That demon then again assumed the disguise of a cook there.

shloka_text: स मानुषमथो मांसं पार्थिवाय न्यवेदयत् । इदं स्वादु हविष्यं च सामिषं चान्नमाहृतम् ।। 7.65.25 ।।
explanation: He then offered human flesh to the king. This delicious, pure, and meaty food has been brought.

shloka_text: स भोजनं वसिष्ठाय पत्न्या सार्धमुपाहरत् । मदयन्त्या नरव्याघ्र सामिषं रक्षसा हृतम् ।। 7.65.26 ।।
explanation: He offered food to Vasiṣṭha along with his wife Madayantī, O tiger among men, but the meaty food was stolen by a Rākṣasa.

shloka_text: ज्ञात्वा तदामिषं विप्रो मानुषं भाजनं गतम् । क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो व्याहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.65.27 ।।
explanation: The Brahmin, having known that that human meat had been placed in the dish, overcome by great anger, began to speak.

shloka_text: यस्मात्त्वं भोजनं राजन्ममैतद्दातुमिच्छसि । तस्माद्भोजनमेतत्ते भविष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.65.28 ।।
explanation: Since you, O King, wish to give this food to me, therefore this food will be yours, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: ततः क्रुद्धस्तु सौदासस्तोयं जग्राह पाणिना । वसिष्ठं शप्तुमारेभे भार्या चैनमवारयत् ।। 7.65.29 ।।
explanation: Then, enraged, Saudasa took water in his hand and began to curse Vasistha, and his wife restrained him.

shloka_text: राजन्प्रभुर्यतो ऽस्माकं वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः । प्रतिशप्तुं न शक्तस्त्वं देवतुल्यं पुरोधसम् ।। 7.65.30 ।।
explanation: O King, since our lord is the divine sage Vasiṣṭha, you are not able to curse back a priest who is equal to a god.

shloka_text: ततः क्रोधमयं तोयं तेजोबलसमन्वितम् । व्यसर्जयत धर्मात्मा ततः पादौ सिषेच च ।। 7.65.31 ।।
explanation: Then, the righteous one released water full of anger, endowed with splendor and strength. And then he sprinkled his feet.

shloka_text: तेनास्य राज्ञस्तौ पादौ तदा कल्माषतां गतौ । तदाप्रभृति राजा ऽसौ सौदासः सुमहायशाः । कल्माषपादः संवृत्तः ख्यातश्चैव तथा नृपः ।। 7.65.32 ।।
explanation: By that, the two feet of this king then became spotted. From that time onwards, that very illustrious King Saudasa became known as Kalmashapada, the king.

shloka_text: स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः । पुनर्वसिष्ठं प्रोवाच यदुक्तं ब्रह्मरूपिणा ।। 7.65.33 ।।
explanation: That king, along with his wife, having bowed down repeatedly, spoke again to Vasiṣṭha what had been said by the Brahma-like one.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य रक्षसा विकृतं च तत् । पुनः प्रोवाच राजानं वसिष्ठः पुरुषर्षभम् ।। 7.65.34 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, and that which was spoiled by the Rakshasa concerning the king, Vasishtha again spoke to the king, the best among men.

shloka_text: मया रोषपरीतेन यदिदं व्याहृतं वचः । नैतच्छक्यं वृथा कर्तुं प्रदास्यामि च ते वरम् ।। 7.65.35 ।।
explanation: This word, which was uttered by me, overcome by anger, cannot be made futile. And I will grant you a boon.

shloka_text: कालो द्वादश वर्षाणि शापस्यान्तो भविष्यति । मत्प्रासादाच्च राजेन्द्र व्यतीतं न स्मरिष्यसि ।। 7.65.36 ।।
explanation: The curse will end in twelve years. And by my grace, O great king, you will not remember the past.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुज्यारिसूदनः । प्रतिलेभे पुना राज्यं प्रजाश्चैवान्वपालयत् ।। 7.65.37 ।।
explanation: Thus, that king, the destroyer of enemies, having undergone that curse, again regained his kingdom and protected his subjects.

shloka_text: तस्य कल्माषपादस्य यज्ञस्यायतनं शुभम् । आश्रमस्य समीपे ऽस्य यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव ।। 7.65.38 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, you ask me about that auspicious sacrificial altar of Kalmashapada, which is near his hermitage.

shloka_text: तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम् । विवेश पर्णशालायां महर्षिमभिवाद्य च ।। 7.65.39 ।।
explanation: Having heard that extremely dreadful tale of that king, and having greeted the great sage, he entered the leaf-hut.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 65 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the sixty-fifth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: यामेव रात्रिं शत्रुघ्नः पर्णशालामुपाविशत् । तामेव रात्रिं सीतापि प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् ।। 7.66.1 ।।
explanation: The very night Shatrughna entered the leaf-hut, that very night Sita also gave birth to two sons.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धरात्रसमये बालका मुनिदारकाः । वाल्मीकेः प्रियमाचख्युः सीतायाः प्रसवं शुभम् ।। 7.66.2 ।।
explanation: Then, at midnight, the boys, the sons of the sages, announced the pleasing news of Sita's auspicious delivery to Valmiki.

shloka_text: भगवन्रामपत्नी सा प्रसूता दारकद्वयम् । ततो रक्षां महातेजः कुरु भूतविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.3 ।।
explanation: O Lord, Rama's wife has given birth to two sons. Therefore, O greatly effulgent one, provide protection that destroys evil spirits.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः समुपागमत् । बालचन्द्रप्रतीकाशौ देवपुत्रौ महौजसौ ।। 7.66.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard their words, the great sage approached the two divine sons, who resembled the young moon and were of great might.

shloka_text: जगाम तत्र हृष्टात्मा ददर्श च कुमारकौ । भूतघ्नीं चाकरोत्ताभ्यां रक्षां रक्षोविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.5 ।।
explanation: With a joyful heart, he went there and saw the two boys. And he performed for them a protection that destroys spirits and demons.

shloka_text: कुशमुष्टिमुपादाय लवं चैव तु स द्विजः । वाल्मीकिः प्रददौ ताभ्यां रक्षां भूतविनाशिनीम् ।। 7.66.6 ।।
explanation: Having taken a handful of Kusha grass, that Brahmana Valmiki gave to them both protection that destroys evil spirits.

shloka_text: यस्तयोः पूर्वजो जातः स कुशैर्मन्त्रसत्कृतैः । निर्मार्जनीयस्तु तदा कुश इत्यस्य नाम तत् ।। 7.66.7 ।।
explanation: He who was born as the elder of the two, he was to be purified then with Kuśa grass consecrated by mantras. Therefore, his name was Kuśa.

shloka_text: यश्चावरो भवेत्ताभ्यां लवेन स समाहितः । निर्मार्जनीयो वृद्धाभिर्लव इत्येव नामतः ।। 7.66.8 ।।
explanation: And whoever is inferior to them, he is to be purified by a 'lava'. He should be cleansed by old women, by the very name 'lava'.

shloka_text: एवं कुशलवौ नाम्ना तावुभौ यमजातकौ । मत्कृताभ्यां च नामभ्यां ख्यातियुक्तौ भविष्यतः ।। 7.66.9 ।।
explanation: Thus, those two, born as twins, named Kuśa and Lava, will become renowned by the names bestowed by me.

shloka_text: तां रक्षां जगृहुस्ताश्च मुनिहस्तात्समाहिताः । अकुर्वंश्च ततो रक्षां तयोर्विगतकल्मषाः ।। 7.66.10 ।।
explanation: And they, attentively, received that protection from the hand of the sage. Then, pure, they performed protection for the two of them.

shloka_text: तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्जन्म नाम च । सङ्कीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ ।। 7.66.11 ।।
explanation: And thus, the birth and naming ceremonies, and the chanting of Rama's name, were being performed by the elderly women, along with the auspicious births of Sita's two sons.

shloka_text: अर्धरात्रे तु शत्रुघ्नः शुश्राव सुमहत्प्रियम् । पर्णशालां ततो गत्वा मातर्दिष्ट्येति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.66.12 ।।
explanation: At midnight, Shatrughna heard very great good news. Then, having gone to the hermitage, he said, "O Mother, fortunately!"

shloka_text: तथा तस्य प्रहृष्टस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । व्यतीता वार्षिकी रात्रिः श्रावणी लघुविक्रमः ।। 7.66.13 ।।
explanation: Thus, for that delighted, great-souled Shatrughna, the rainy night of Shravana passed swiftly.

shloka_text: प्रभाते सुमहावीर्यः कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकीं क्रियाम् । मुनिं प्राञ्जलिरामन्त्र्य ययौ पश्चान्मुखः पुनः ।। 7.66.14 ।।
explanation: In the morning, the very mighty one, having performed his forenoon duties, and having respectfully taken leave of the sage with folded hands, then departed again, facing west.

shloka_text: स गत्वा यमुनातीरं सप्तरात्रोषितः पथि । ऋषीणां पुण्यकीर्तीनामाश्रमे वासमभ्ययात् ।। 7.66.15 ।।
explanation: He, having gone to the bank of the Yamuna, and having stayed for seven nights on the way, took up residence in the hermitage of the sages of sacred renown.

shloka_text: स तत्र मुनिभिः सार्धं भार्गवप्रमुखैर्नृपः । कथाभिरभिरूपाभिर्वासं चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.66.16 ।।
explanation: The greatly renowned king, along with the sages, chief among whom was Bhargava, made his stay there, engaging in charming stories.

shloka_text: स काञ्चनाद्यैर्मुनिभिः समेतो रघुप्रवीरो रजनीं तदानीम् । कथाप्रकारैर्बहुभिर्महात्मा विरामयामास नरेन्द्रसूनुः ।। 7.66.17 ।।
explanation: Then, that great-souled son of the king, the chief of the Raghu dynasty, accompanied by sages like Kañcana and others, spent the night with many kinds of stories.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 66 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the sixty-sixth chapter.

shloka_text: अथ रात्र्यां प्रवृत्तायां शत्रुघ्नो भृगुनन्दनम् । पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथा बलम् ।। 7.67.1 ।।
explanation: Then, when night had begun, Shatrughna asked the Brahmin Chyavana, son of Bhrigu, about Lavana's strength.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन्के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः । अनेन शूलमुख्येन द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागताः ।। 7.67.2 ।।
