explanation: O Brahman, what is the power of this spear, and who were those previously destroyed by this excellent spear, having engaged in a duel?

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजाश्च्यवनो रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.67.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of the great-souled Shatrughna, the greatly effulgent Chyavana replied to Raghunandana.

shloka_text: असङ्ख्येयानि कर्माणि यान्यस्य रघुनन्दन । इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवे यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणष्व मे ।। 7.67.4 ।।
explanation: O Raghunandana, listen to me about his innumerable deeds and whatever transpired concerning him, who was born in the Ikshvaku lineage.

shloka_text: अयोध्यायां पुरा राजा युवनाश्वसुतो बली । मान्धातेति स विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ।। 7.67.5 ।।
explanation: Formerly, in Ayodhya, there was a mighty king, the son of Yuvanashva. He was renowned as Mandhata, valorous in the three worlds.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां शासने पृथिवीपतिः । सुरलोकमितो जेतुमुद्योगमकरोन्नृपः ।। 7.67.6 ।।
explanation: The king, the lord of the earth, having brought the entire earth under his rule, then made an effort from this world to conquer the world of the gods.

shloka_text: इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्रं सुराणां च महात्मनाम् । मान्धातरि कृतोद्योगे देवलोकजिगीषया ।। 7.67.7 ।।
explanation: And a severe fear arose in Indra and the great-souled gods when Mandhata made an effort with the desire to conquer the world of the gods.

shloka_text: अर्धासनेन शक्रस्य राज्यार्धेन च पार्थिवः । वन्द्यमानः सुरगणैः प्रतिज्ञामध्यरोहत ।। 7.67.8 ।।
explanation: The king, sharing half of Shakra's seat and half of his kingdom, and being worshipped by the hosts of gods, undertook a vow.

shloka_text: तस्य पापमभिप्रायं विदित्वा पाकशासनः । सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वाक्यमुवाच युवनाश्वजम् ।। 7.67.9 ।।
explanation: Knowing his sinful intention, Indra spoke these conciliatory words to the son of Yuvanashva.

shloka_text: राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत्पुरुषर्षभ । अकृत्वा पृथिवीं वश्यां देवराज्यमिहेच्छसि ।। 7.67.10 ।।
explanation: You are a king in the human world, O best among men. You desire the kingdom of the gods here, without first having brought the earth under your control.

shloka_text: यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे । देवराज्यं कुरुष्वेह सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.67.11 ।।
explanation: If, O hero, the entire earth is completely under your control, then establish here the kingdom of the gods, along with your servants, army, and conveyances.

shloka_text: इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मान्धाता वाक्यमब्रवीत् । क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले ।। 7.67.12 ।।
explanation: To Indra, who was speaking thus, Mandhata said: "O Shakra, where on the earth is my rule obstructed?"

shloka_text: तमुवाच सहस्राक्षो लवणो नाम राक्षसः । मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न ते ऽ ऽज्ञां कुरुते ऽनघ ।। 7.67.13 ।।
explanation: Sahasraksha said to him: "O sinless one, the demon named Lavana, son of Madhu, does not obey your command in Madhuvana."

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रियं घोरं सहस्राक्षेण भाषितम् । व्रीडितो ऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।। 7.67.14 ।।
explanation: Having heard those terrible and unpleasant words spoken by Sahasraksha, the king, ashamed and with a downcast face, was unable to reply.

shloka_text: आमन्त्र्य तु सहस्राक्षं ह्रिया किञ्चिदवाङ्मुखः । पुनरेवागमच्छ्रीमानिमं लोकं नरेश्वरः ।। 7.67.15 ।।
explanation: Having bid farewell to Sahasraksha, the glorious lord of men, with his face somewhat downcast out of shame, returned to this world again.

shloka_text: स कृत्वा हृदये ऽमर्षं सभृत्यबलवाहनः । आजगाम मधोः पुत्रं वशे कर्तुमरिन्दमः ।। 7.67.16 ।।
explanation: Having conceived anger in his heart, that subduer of enemies, accompanied by his servants, army, and vehicles, came to subdue Madhu's son.

shloka_text: स काङ्क्षमाणो लवणं युद्धाय पुरुषर्षभः । दूतं सम्प्रेषयामास सकाशं लवणस्य हि ।। 7.67.17 ।।
explanation: That best among men, desiring battle with Lavaṇa, indeed sent a messenger to Lavaṇa.

shloka_text: स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम् । वदन्तमेवं तं दूतं भक्षयामास राक्षसः ।। 7.67.18 ।।
explanation: Having gone, he spoke many offensive words to the son of Madhu. The demon devoured that messenger as he was speaking thus.

shloka_text: चिरायमाणे दूते तु राजा क्रोधसमन्वितः । अर्दयामास तद्रक्षः शरवृष्ट्या समन्ततः ।। 7.67.19 ।।
explanation: When the messenger delayed, the king, filled with anger, tormented that demon with a shower of arrows from all sides.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य तद्रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना । वधाय सानुबन्धस्य मुमोचायुधमुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.20 ।।
explanation: Then, that demon, laughing, grasped a spear with his hand. For the destruction of him and his followers, he hurled that excellent weapon.

shloka_text: तच्छूलं दीप्यमानं तु सभृत्यबलवाहनम् । भस्मीकृत्वा नृपं भूयो लवणस्यागमत्करम् ।। 7.67.21 ।।
explanation: That blazing trident, having incinerated the king along with his servants, army, and vehicles, then returned to Lavaṇa's hand.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा सुमहान्हतः सबलवाहनः । शूलस्य तु बलं सौम्य अप्रमेयमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.67.22 ।।
explanation: Thus, that very great king was slain along with his army and vehicles. But the power of the spear, O gentle one, is immeasurable and unsurpassed.

shloka_text: श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः । अगृहीतायुधं क्षिप्रं ध्रुवो हि विजयस्तव ।। 7.67.23 ।।
explanation: Tomorrow morning, you will kill Lavana, there is no doubt. Your victory is certainly swift over him who has not taken up arms.

shloka_text: लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्यात्कृते कर्मणि च त्वया । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं लवणस्य दुरात्मनः ।। 7.67.24 ।।
explanation: And may there be welfare for the worlds through the action performed by you. All this has been explained to you concerning the wicked Lavana.

shloka_text: शूलस्य च बलं घोरमप्रमेयं नरर्षभ । विनाशश्चैव मान्धातुर्यत्तेनाभूच्च पार्थिव ।। 7.67.25 ।।
explanation: O best among men, O king, the terrible and immeasurable power of the spear, and indeed the destruction of Mandhatu, which occurred by it.

shloka_text: त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन्वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे । शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र ।। 7.67.26 ।।
explanation: O great-souled one, tomorrow morning you will kill Lavana; there is no doubt in my mind about this. O king, your victory will be certain, as he has gone out without his spear for the sake of prey.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 67 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sage-composed glorious Ramayana, the original epic by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the sixty-seventh chapter.

shloka_text: कथां कथयतां तेषां जयं चाकाङ्क्षतां शुभम् । व्यतीता रजनी शीघ्रं शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.68.1 ।।
explanation: As they narrated stories and wished for auspicious victory, the night quickly passed for the great-souled Shatrughna.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभाते विमले तस्मिन्काले स राक्षसः । निर्गतस्तु पुराद्धीरो भक्ष्याहारप्रचोदितः ।। 7.68.2 ।।
explanation: Then, in that clear morning, that brave Rakshasa, impelled by the desire for food, came out from the city.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः शत्रुघ्नो यमुनां नदीम् । तीर्त्वा मधुपुरद्वारि धनुष्पाणिरतिष्ठत ।। 7.68.3 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the brave Shatrughna, having crossed the Yamuna river, stood at the gate of Madhupura with a bow in hand.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते क्रूरकर्मा स राक्षसः । आगच्छद्बहुसाहस्रं प्राणिनां भारमुद्वहन् ।। 7.68.4 ।।
explanation: Then, when midday arrived, that cruel-deeded demon came, carrying a load of many thousands of living beings.

shloka_text: ततो ददर्श शत्रुघ्नं स्थितं द्वारि धृतायुधम् । तमुवाच ततो रक्षः किमनेन करिष्यसि ।। 7.68.5 ।।
explanation: Then (the demon) saw Shatrughna, armed, standing at the door. Then the demon said to him, "What will you do with this?"

shloka_text: ईदृशानां सहस्राणि सायुधानां नराधम । भक्षितानि मया रोषात्कालमाकाङ्क्षसे नु किम् ।। 7.68.6 ।।
explanation: O vilest of men, thousands of such armed beings have been devoured by me in my wrath. Why then do you seek your death?

shloka_text: आहारश्चास्य सम्पूर्णो ममायं पुरुषाधम । स्वयं प्रविष्टो ऽद्य मुखं कथमासाद्य दुर्मते ।। 7.68.7 ।।
explanation: O vilest of men, this complete food of mine, this very one, how did you, O evil-minded one, enter my mouth yourself today, having approached it?

shloka_text: तस्यैवं भाषमाणस्य हसतश्च मुहुर्मुहुः । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो रोषादश्रूण्यवासृजत् ।। 7.68.8 ।।
explanation: As he spoke thus and laughed again and again, Shatrughna, full of prowess, shed tears from anger.

shloka_text: तस्य रोषाभिभूतस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । तेजोमया मरीच्यस्तु सर्वगात्रैर्विनिष्पतन् ।। 7.68.9 ।।
explanation: From that great-souled Shatrughna, who was overcome by rage, radiant rays were shooting forth from all his limbs.

shloka_text: उवाच च सुसङ्क्रुद्धः शत्रुघ्नस्तं निशाचरम् । योद्धुमिच्छामि दुर्बुद्धे द्वन्द्वयुद्धं त्वया सह ।। 7.68.10 ।।
explanation: And Shatrughna, extremely enraged, said to that night-wanderer: "O evil-minded one, I wish to fight a duel with you."

shloka_text: पुत्रो दशरथस्याहं भ्राता रामस्य धीमतः । शत्रुघ्नो नित्यशत्रुघ्नो वधाकाङ्क्षी तवागतः ।। 7.68.11 ।।
explanation: I am the son of Dasharatha, the brother of the wise Rama. I am Shatrughna, the eternal slayer of enemies, and I have come desirous of your death.

shloka_text: तस्य मे युद्धकामस्य द्वन्द्वयुद्धं प्रदीयताम् । शत्रुस्त्वं सर्वभूतानां न मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि ।। 7.68.12 ।।
explanation: Grant me, who desires battle, a duel. You are the enemy of all beings; you will not escape alive from me.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु राक्षसः प्रहसन्निव । प्रत्युवाच नरश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो ऽसि दुर्मते ।। 7.68.13 ।।
explanation: As he spoke thus, the demon, as if laughing, replied to the best of men, "Fortunately, you have arrived, O evil-minded one!"

shloka_text: मम मातृष्वसुर्भ्राता रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । हतो रामेण दुर्बुद्धे स्त्रीहेतोः पुरुषाधम ।। 7.68.14 ।।
explanation: My mother's sister's brother, Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, was killed by Rama, O evil-minded one, O lowest of men, for the sake of a woman.

shloka_text: तच्च सर्वं मया क्षान्तं रावणस्य कुलक्षयम् । अवज्ञां पुरतः कृत्वा मया यूयं विशेषतः ।। 7.68.15 ।।
explanation: And all that, the destruction of Ravana's lineage, was forgiven by me. Having disregarded the disrespect, you were especially (treated thus) by me.

shloka_text: निहताश्च हि मे सर्वे परिभूतास्तृणं यथा । भूताश्चैव भविष्याश्च यूयं च पुरुषाधमाः ।। 7.68.16 ।।
explanation: Indeed, all of them were slain by me, treated with contempt like grass. Both those who have been and those who will be, and you, O vilest of men.

shloka_text: तस्य ते युद्धकामस्य युद्धं दास्यामि दुर्मते । तिष्ठं त्वं च मुहूर्तं तु यावदायुधमानये । ईप्सितं यादृशं तुभ्यं सज्जये यावदायुधम् ।। 7.68.17 ।।
explanation: O evil-minded one, I will give battle to you who desires battle. You wait for a moment until I bring my weapon. I will prepare the weapon as you desire.

shloka_text: तमुवाचाशु शत्रुघ्नः क्व मे जीवन्गमिष्यसि । शत्रुर्यदृच्छया दृष्टो न मोक्तव्यः कृतात्मना ।। 7.68.18 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna quickly said to him, "Where will you go alive from me? An enemy encountered by chance should not be released by a resolute person."

shloka_text: यो हि विक्लवया बुद्ध्या प्रसरं शत्रवे ददौ । स हतो मन्दबुद्धित्वाद्यथा कापुरुषस्तथा ।। 7.68.19 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he who, with a bewildered mind, gave an advantage to the enemy, he is destroyed due to his foolishness, just like a coward.

shloka_text: तस्मात्सुदृष्टं कुरु जीवलोकं शरैः शितैस्त्वां विविधैर्नयामि । यमस्य गेहाभिमुखं हि पापं रिपुं त्रिलोकस्य च राघवस्य ।। 7.68.20 ।।
explanation: Therefore, take a good look at the world of living beings. For with various sharp arrows, I shall indeed lead you, the sinful enemy of the three worlds and of Raghava, towards Yama's abode.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 68 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the sixty-eighth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । क्रोधामाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of the great-souled Shatrughna, he felt intense anger and said, "Stop! Stop!"

shloka_text: पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च । लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत् ।। 7.69.2 ।।
explanation: Rubbing his hands together and gnashing his teeth, Lavaṇa repeatedly challenged the tiger among the Raghus.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम् । शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.3 ।।
explanation: To him, Lavana, who was speaking such words and was of dreadful appearance, Shatrughna, the slayer of the enemies of the gods, spoke these words.

shloka_text: न शत्रुघ्नस्तथा जातो यथा ऽन्ये निर्जितास्त्वया । तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम् ।। 7.69.4 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna is not like others whom you have conquered. Therefore, today, struck by arrows, you go to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: ऋषयो ऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे । पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम् ।। 7.69.5 ।।
explanation: O evil-souled one, let even the sages, the learned Brahmins, see you slain by me in battle today, just as the gods saw Ravana.

shloka_text: त्वयि मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे पतिते ऽद्य निशाचर । पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति ।। 7.69.6 ।।
explanation: O night-wanderer, when you fall today, consumed by my arrows, there will indeed be peace in the city and in the kingdom.

shloka_text: अद्य मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः । प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः ।। 7.69.7 ।।
explanation: Today, an arrow released from my arm, with a thunderbolt-like tip, will enter your heart, just as a sunbeam enters a lotus.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत् ।। 7.69.8 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, Lavana, overwhelmed with anger, hurled a great tree at Shatrughna's chest, and he (Shatrughna) cut it into a hundred pieces.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु । पादपान्सुबहून्गृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद्बली ।। 7.69.9 ।।
explanation: Seeing that action futile, the powerful demon, once again, taking many trees, hurled them at Shatrughna.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून् । त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः ।। 7.69.10 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna, too, mighty, cut down many falling trees, each one with three or four arrows with firm shafts.

shloka_text: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद्राक्षसोरसि । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः ।। 7.69.11 ।।
explanation: Then, Shatrughna, endowed with great prowess, discharged a shower of arrows upon the demon's chest. But that demon was not wounded.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान् । शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै ।। 7.69.12 ।।
explanation: Then, the powerful Lavana, laughing, lifted a tree and struck the hero on the head. With his limbs slackened, he fainted.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणां देवसङ्घानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा ।। 7.69.13 ।।
explanation: Upon the fall of that hero, a great cry of lamentation arose among the sages, the hosts of gods, and the Gandharvas and Apsaras.

shloka_text: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम् । रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम् ।। 7.69.14 ।।
explanation: Even though the demon (Lavana) was killed by Shatrughna and lay fallen on the ground, having disregarded him, the demon (Shatrughna) did not enter his own abode, even though he had found an opportunity.

shloka_text: नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम् । ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान्भक्षान्समुदावहत् ।। 7.69.15 ।।
explanation: Seeing him fallen on the ground, he did not even take up the spear. Then, knowing him to be killed, he carried away those foods.

shloka_text: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः । शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः सम्प्रपूजितः ।। 7.69.16 ।।
explanation: In a moment, having regained consciousness, Shatrughna again stood, armed, at the city gate, greatly honored by the sages.

shloka_text: ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम् । ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश ।। 7.69.17 ।।
explanation: Then he took that excellent, divine, infallible arrow, blazing with terrible splendor and filling the ten directions.

shloka_text: वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् । नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम् ।। 7.69.18 ।।
explanation: Having a thunderbolt-like face, thunderbolt-swift, resembling Mount Meru and Mount Mandara. Revered in all festivals, unconquered in battles.

shloka_text: असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्रिणम् । दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारणम् ।। 7.69.19 ।।
explanation: Whose body is smeared with blood and sandalwood, with beautiful wings, the bird, the destroyer of the chief of Danavas, the chief of mountains, and the Asuras.

shloka_text: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते । दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन् ।। 7.69.20 ।।
explanation: Seeing him, blazing like the fire of destruction at the end of an age, all beings were filled with great terror.

shloka_text: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम् । जगद्धि सर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.69.21 ।।
explanation: Indeed, the entire world, along with gods, demons, gandharvas, sages, and hosts of apsaras, being distressed, approached the Grandfather (Brahma).

shloka_text: उवाच देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम् । देवानां भयसंमोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.22 ।।
explanation: He spoke to the God of gods, the bestower of boons, the great-grandfather, concerning the fear and delusion of the gods and the destruction of the worlds.

shloka_text: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह । देवानां भयसम्मोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.23 ।।
explanation: O great-grandfather, never before has such a thing been seen or heard – the fear and delusion of the gods concerning the destruction of the worlds.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः । भयकारणमाचष्ट लोकानामभयङ्करः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.69.24 ।।
explanation: Having heard their words, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, the dispeller of fear for the worlds, explained the cause of fear. He spoke sweet words: "Listen, O all deities!"

shloka_text: वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नधारितः । तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.69.25 ।।
explanation: The arrow wielded by Shatrughna for the slaying of Lavana in battle – by its brilliance, all of us, O best of gods, are bewildered.

shloka_text: एष पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः । शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम् ।। 7.69.26 ।।
explanation: This, O child, is the eternal, radiant arrow of the ancient god, the creator of the worlds, by which fear has indeed come.

shloka_text: एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः । सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः ।। 7.69.27 ।।
explanation: This great arrow was indeed created by that great soul for the destruction of those two demons, Kaitabha and Madhu.

shloka_text: एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम् । एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.69.28 ।।
explanation: Only one knows Vishnu's effulgent arrow. This alone is the primeval form of that great-souled Vishnu.

shloka_text: इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना । रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम् ।। 7.69.29 ।।
explanation: Go from here, behold Lavana, the foremost of Rakshasas, being slain by the great-souled and heroic younger brother of Rama.

shloka_text: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः । आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ ।। 7.69.30 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of that God of gods, the gods arrived where both Shatrughna and Lavana were fighting.

shloka_text: तं शरं दिव्यसङ्काशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम् ।। 7.69.31 ।।
explanation: All beings saw that arrow, divine in appearance, held by Shatrughna's hand, like the rising fire of the cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: अकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः । सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लक्षणं पुनः ।। 7.69.32 ।।
explanation: Having seen the sky covered by the gods, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, indeed, let out a mighty lion's roar and saw Lakshmana again.

shloka_text: आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः ।। 7.69.33 ।।
explanation: And Lavana, summoned again by that great-souled Shatrughna, filled with rage, stood ready for battle.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ तद्धनुर्धन्विनां वरः । तं मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.69.34 ।।
explanation: Then, he, the best among archers, having drawn that bow up to his ear, released that great arrow into Lavana's broad chest.

shloka_text: उरस्तस्य विदार्याशु प्रविवेश रसातलम् ।। 7.69.35 ।।
explanation: Quickly tearing open his chest, it entered Rasatala.

shloka_text: गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः । पुनरेवागमत्तूर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् ।। 7.69.36 ।।
explanation: The divine arrow, worshipped by the gods, having gone to Rasatala, quickly returned again to the delight of the Ikshvaku family.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः । पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः ।। 7.69.37 ।।
explanation: That demon Lavana, pierced by Shatrughna's arrows, suddenly fell to the ground, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तच्च शूलं महत्तेन हते लवणराक्षसे । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात् ।। 7.69.38 ।।
explanation: And that great trident, when the demon Lavana was slain by him, went under the control of Rudra while all the gods were watching.

shloka_text: एकेषुपातेन भृशं निपात्य लोकत्रयस्यापि रघुप्रवीरः । विनिर्बभावुत्तमचापबाणस्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः ।। 7.69.39 ।।
explanation: The great hero of the Raghu dynasty, having completely struck down (the enemy) with a single arrow-shot, (an act as if felling) even the three worlds, shone forth with his excellent bow and arrow, just like the thousand-rayed sun dispelling darkness.

shloka_text: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः । दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्तस्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः ।। 7.69.40 ।।
explanation: Then indeed, the gods, sages, and serpents, and all the Apsaras worshipped. Fortunately, victory was attained by Dasharatha's son, and having abandoned fear, he became peaceful like a serpent.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 69 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered Ramayana, the glorious original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the sixty-ninth chapter.

shloka_text: हते तु लवणे देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः । ऊचुः सुमधुरां वाणीं शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम् ।। 7.70.1 ।।
explanation: When Lavana was killed, the gods, with Indra and Agni at their forefront, spoke very sweet words to Shatrughna, the tormentor of enemies.

shloka_text: दिष्ट्या ते विजयो वत्स दिष्ट्या लवणराक्षसः । हतः पुरुषशार्दूल वरं वरय सुव्रत ।। 7.70.2 ।।
explanation: Fortunately, O dear one, you are victorious! Fortunately, the demon Lavana has been slain, O tiger among men! O virtuous one, ask for a boon.

shloka_text: वरदास्तु महाबाहो सर्व एव समागताः । विजयाकाङ्क्षिणस्तुभ्यममोघं दर्शनं हि नः ।। 7.70.3 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, all who have assembled are indeed givers of boons. Our sight is certainly fruitful for you who desire victory.

shloka_text: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा शूरो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । प्रत्युवाच महाबाहुः शत्रुघ्नः प्रयतात्मवान् ।। 7.70.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the gods, the brave, mighty-armed, and self-controlled Shatrughna, with folded hands on his head, replied.

shloka_text: इयं मधुपुरी रस्या मधुरा देवनिर्मिता । निवेशं प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रमेष मे ऽस्तु वरः परः ।। 7.70.5 ।।
explanation: This delightful and sweet Madhupuri, built by the gods, may it quickly obtain a settlement. Let this be my supreme boon.

shloka_text: तं देवाः प्रीतमनसो बाढमित्येव राघवम् । भविष्यति पुरी रम्या शूरसेना न संशयः ।। 7.70.6 ।।
explanation: The gods, with delighted minds, said to Raghava, "So be it. A beautiful city named Surasena will certainly come into existence, there is no doubt."

shloka_text: ते तथोक्त्वा महात्मानो दिवमारुरुहुस्तदा । शत्रुघ्नो ऽपि महातेजास्तां सेनां समुपानयत् ।। 7.70.7 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones then ascended to heaven. The greatly effulgent Shatrughna also led that army.

shloka_text: सा सेना शीघ्रमागच्छच्छ्रुत्वा शत्रुघ्नशासनम् । निवेशनं च शत्रुघ्नः श्रावणेन समारभत् ।। 7.70.8 ।।
explanation: That army quickly arrived, having heard Shatrughna's command. And Shatrughna commenced the establishment (of the city) in the month of Shravana.

shloka_text: सा पुरा दिव्यसङ्काशा वर्षे द्वादशमे शुभे । निविष्टा शूरसेनानां विषयश्चाकुतोभयः ।। 7.70.9 ।।
explanation: She, of divine splendor, was formerly established in the auspicious twelfth year. And the territory of the Shurasenas was free from all fear.

shloka_text: क्षेत्राणि सस्ययुक्तानि काले वर्षति वासवः । अरोगवीरपुरुषा शत्रुघ्नभुजपालिता ।। 7.70.10 ।।
explanation: The fields are abundant with crops, Vasava (Indra) rains at the proper time. The men are healthy and brave, protected by the arms of Shatrughna.

shloka_text: अर्धचन्द्रप्रतीकाशा यमुनातीरशोभिता । शोभिता गृहमुख्यैश्च चत्वरापणवीथिकैः । चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्ता नानावाणिज्यशोभिता ।। 7.70.11 ।।
explanation: Resembling a half-moon, adorned on the bank of the Yamuna, beautiful with prominent houses, squares, shops, and streets, endowed with the four social classes, and adorned with various trades.

shloka_text: यच्च तेन पुरा शुभ्रं लवणेन कृतं महत् । तच्छोभयति शत्रुघ्नो नानावर्णोपशोभिताम् ।। 7.70.12 ।।
explanation: And that great and splendid (city/structure) which was formerly made by Lavana, Shatrughna now beautifies it, making it resplendent with various colors.

shloka_text: आरामैश्च विहारैश्च शोभमानं समन्ततः । शोभितां शोभनीयैश्च तथा ऽन्यैर्दैवमानुषैः ।। 7.70.13 ।।
explanation: Adorned on all sides by gardens and pleasure-grounds, and made beautiful by other divine and human elements.

shloka_text: तां पुरीं दिव्यसङ्काशां नानापण्योपशोभिताम् । नानादेशागतैश्चापि वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम् ।। 7.70.14 ।।
explanation: That city, resembling heaven, was adorned with various merchandise and beautified by merchants who had come from diverse lands.

shloka_text: तां समृद्धां समृद्धार्थः शत्रुघ्नो भरतानुजः । निरीक्ष्य परमप्रीतः परं हर्षमुपागमत् ।। 7.70.15 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, whose purpose was fulfilled, having seen that prosperous one, became greatly pleased and attained supreme joy.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य मधुरां पुरीम् । रामपादौ निरीक्षे ऽहं वर्षे द्वादश आगते ।। 7.70.16 ।।
explanation: A thought arose in him: 'Having established the city of Mathura, I shall behold Rama's feet when the twelfth year arrives.'

shloka_text: ततः स ताममरपुरोपमां पुरीं निवेश्य वै विविधजनाभिसंवृताम् । नराधिपो रघुपतिपाददर्शने दधे मतिं रघुकुलवंशवर्धनः ।। 7.70.17 ।।
explanation: Then, that king, the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty, having established that city, which was like a city of gods and bustling with diverse people, set his mind on seeing the feet of Ragupati.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 70 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the seventieth chapter.

shloka_text: ततो द्वादशमे वर्षे शत्रघ्नो रामपालिताम् । अयोध्यां चकमे गन्तुमल्पभृत्यबलानुगः ।। 7.71.1 ।।
explanation: Then, in the twelfth year, Shatrughna, accompanied by a small retinue and army, desired to go to Ayodhya, which was protected by Rama.

shloka_text: ततो मन्त्रिपुरोगांश्च बलमुख्यान्निवर्त्य च । जगाम हयमुख्यैश्च रथानां च शतेन सः ।। 7.71.2 ।।
explanation: Then, having dismissed the chief ministers and the army commanders, he went with excellent horses and a hundred chariots.

shloka_text: स गत्वा गणितान्वासान्सप्ताष्टौ रघुनन्दनः । वाल्मीक्याश्रममागत्य वासं चक्रे महायशाः ।। 7.71.3 ।।
explanation: Having traveled for seven or eight specified days, the greatly renowned Raghunandana arrived at Valmiki's hermitage and resided there.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ वाल्मीकेः पुरुषर्षभः । पाद्यमर्ध्यं तथातिथ्यं जग्राह मुनिहस्ततः ।। 7.71.4 ।।
explanation: Then, that best among men, having saluted Valmiki's feet, accepted the water for washing feet, the respectful offering, and the hospitality from the hands of the sage.

shloka_text: बहुरूपाः सुमधुराः कथास्तत्र सहस्रशः । कथयामास स मुनिः शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने ।। 7.71.5 ।।
explanation: There, that sage narrated thousands of diverse and very sweet stories to the great-souled Shatrughna.

shloka_text: उवाच च मुनिर्वाक्यं लवणस्य वधाश्रितम् । सुदुष्करं कृतं कर्म लवणं निघ्नता त्वया ।। 7.71.6 ।।
explanation: And the sage spoke words concerning the slaying of Lavana: "A very difficult deed has been accomplished by you by killing Lavana."

shloka_text: बहवः पार्थिवाः सौम्य हताः सबलवाहनाः । लवणेन महाबाहो युध्यमाना महाबलाः ।। 7.71.7 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, O mighty-armed one, many mighty kings, along with their armies and mounts, were slain by Lavana while fighting.

shloka_text: स त्वया निहतः पापो लीलया पुरुषर्षभ । जगतश्च भयं तत्र प्रशान्तं तव तेजसा ।। 7.71.8 ।।
explanation: That sinful one was slain by you with ease, O best among men. And the fear of the world was then pacified by your might.

shloka_text: रावणस्य वधो घोरो यत्नेन महता कृतः । इदं तु सुमहत्कर्म त्वया कृतमयत्नतः ।। 7.71.9 ।।
explanation: The terrible slaying of Ravana was accomplished with great effort. But this very great deed was done by you effortlessly.

shloka_text: प्रीतिश्चास्मिन्परा जाता देवानां लवणे हते । भूतानां चैव सर्वेषां जगतश्च प्रियं कृतम् ।। 7.71.10 ।।
explanation: And supreme joy arose for the gods when Lavana was slain. And indeed, the welfare of all beings and of the world was accomplished.

shloka_text: तच्च युद्धं मया दृष्टं यथावत्पुरुषर्षभ । सभायां वासवस्याथ उपविष्टेन राघव ।। 7.71.11 ।।
explanation: O best among men, O Raghava, that battle was seen by me exactly as it happened, while I was seated in the assembly of Vasava.

shloka_text: ममापि परमा प्रीतिर्हृदि शत्रुघ्न वर्तते । उपाघ्रास्यामि ते मूर्ध्नि स्नेहस्यैषा परा गतिः ।। 7.71.12 ।।
explanation: O Shatrughna, supreme affection also resides in my heart. I will kiss your head; this is the highest expression of love.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा मूर्ध्नि शत्रुघ्नमुपाघ्राय महामुनिः । आतिथ्यमकरोत्तस्य ये च तस्य पदानुगाः ।। 7.71.13 ।।
explanation: Having said this, the great sage, having smelled Shatrughna on the head, offered hospitality to him and to those who were his followers.

shloka_text: स भुक्तवान्नरश्रेष्ठो गीतमाधुर्यमुत्तमम् । शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले यथाकृमम् ।। 7.71.14 ।।
explanation: That best of men, having eaten, heard the excellent sweet song, the story of Rama, at that time, in due order.

shloka_text: तन्त्रीलयसमायुक्तं त्रिस्थानकरणान्वितम् । संस्कृतं लक्षणोपेतं समतालसमन्वितम् । शुश्राव रामचरितं तस्मिन्काले पुरा कृतम् ।। 7.71.15 ।।
explanation: He heard the story of Rama, composed long ago, accompanied by the melody of stringed instruments, performed in the three registers, in refined language, endowed with all the proper characteristics, and perfectly synchronized with rhythm.

shloka_text: तान्यक्षराणि सत्यानि यथावृत्तानि पूर्वशः । श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलो विसञ्ज्ञो बाष्पलोचनः ।। 7.71.16 ।।
explanation: Having heard those truthful words, which had happened exactly as described previously, the foremost among men became stunned, with tearful eyes.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तमिवासञ्ज्ञो विनिःश्वस्य मुहुर्मुहुः । तस्मिन् गीते यथावृत्तं वर्तमानमिवाशृणोत् ।। 7.71.17 ।।
explanation: He, as if unconscious for a moment, sighing repeatedly, heard in that song the past events as if they were happening in the present.

shloka_text: पदानुगाश्च ये राज्ञस्तां श्रुत्वा गीतिसम्पदम् । अवाङ्मुखाश्च दीनाश्च ह्याश्चर्यमिति चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.71.18 ।।
explanation: And the king's followers, having heard that excellent song, with downcast faces and dejected, exclaimed, "This is indeed a wonder!"

shloka_text: परस्परं च ये तत्र सैनिकाः सम्बभाषिरे । किमिदं क्व च वर्तामः किमेतत्स्वप्नदर्शनम् ।। 7.71.19 ।।
explanation: And the soldiers there spoke to each other: "What is this? And where are we? Is this a dream vision?"

shloka_text: अर्थो यो नः पुरा दृष्टस्तमाश्रमपदे पुनः । शृणुमः किमिदं स्वप्नो गीतबन्धं श्रियो भवेत् ।। 7.71.20 ।।
explanation: That matter which we saw before, we hear it again in the hermitage. What is this? Is it a dream? May it be a song of fortune.

shloka_text: विस्मयं ते परं गत्वा शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रुवन् । साधु पृच्छ नरश्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिं मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।। 7.71.21 ।।
explanation: They, having been greatly astonished, said this to Shatrughna: "O best among men, properly ask Valmiki, the foremost among sages."

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीत्सर्वान्कौतूहलसमन्वितान् । सैनिका न क्षमो ऽस्माकं परिप्रष्टुमिहेदृशः ।। 7.71.22 ।।
explanation: Shatrughna then said to all who were filled with curiosity: "It is not proper for our soldiers to question such things here."

shloka_text: आश्चर्याणि बहूनीह भवन्त्यस्याश्रमे मुनेः । न तु कौतूहलाद्युक्तमन्वेष्टुं तं महामुनिम् ।। 7.71.23 ।।
explanation: Many wonders occur here in the hermitage of this sage. But it is not proper to investigate that great sage out of curiosity.

shloka_text: एवं तद्वाक्यमुक्त्वा च सैनिकान्रघुनन्दनः । अभिवाद्य महर्षिं तं स्वं निवेशं ययौ तदा ।। 7.71.24 ।।
explanation:
ान्'? It's 'सैनिकान्'.

If 'सैनिकान्' is the object of 'उक्त्वा', then it would be "having spoken those words to the soldiers".

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकसप्ततिमः सर्गः ।। 71 ।।
explanation: Here ends the seventy-first chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Rāmāyaṇa, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तं शयानं नरव्याघ्रं निद्रा नाभ्यागमत्तदा । चिन्तयन्तमनेकार्थं रामगीतमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.72.1 ।।
explanation: Then, sleep did not come to that tiger among men as he lay there, contemplating the unsurpassed story of Rama, which had many meanings.

shloka_text: तस्य शब्दं सुमधुरं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम् । श्रुत्वा रात्रिर्जगामाशु शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.72.2 ।।
explanation: Having heard his exceedingly sweet sound, accompanied by the rhythm of stringed instruments, the night of the great-souled Shatrughna swiftly passed.

shloka_text: तस्यां निशायां व्युष्टायां कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकं क्रमम् । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शत्रुघ्नो मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।। 7.72.3 ।।
explanation: When that night had dawned, having performed his morning duties, Shatrughna, with folded hands, spoke words to the chief of sages.

shloka_text: भगवन्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि राघवं रघुनन्दनम् । त्वया ऽनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि सहैभिः संशितव्रतैः ।। 7.72.4 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I wish to see Rama, the delight of the Raghus. I desire to be permitted by you, along with these (sages) of firm vows.

shloka_text: इत्येवंवादिनं तं तु शत्रुघ्नं शत्रुतापनम् । वाल्मीकिः सम्परिष्वज्य विससर्ज च राघवम् ।। 7.72.5 ।।
explanation: Having embraced Shatrughna, the tormentor of enemies, who had spoken thus, Valmiki then sent away the descendant of Raghu.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं रथमारुह्य सुप्रभम् । अयोध्यामगमत्तूर्णं राघवोत्सुकदर्शनः ।। 7.72.6 ।।
explanation: He, having saluted the best of sages, and having mounted the splendid chariot, went quickly to Ayodhya, eager to see Rama.

shloka_text: स प्रविष्टः पुरीं रम्यां श्रीमानिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्यत्र रामो महाद्युतिः ।। 7.72.7 ।।
explanation: He, the glorious son of Ikshvaku, the mighty-armed one, having entered the beautiful city, entered where the greatly radiant Rama was.

shloka_text: स रामं मन्त्रिमध्यस्थं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननम् । पश्यन्नमरमध्यस्थं सहस्रनयनं यथा ।। 7.72.8 ।।
explanation: He, seeing Rama, who was seated amidst his ministers and whose face resembled the full moon, was like seeing the thousand-eyed Indra seated amidst the gods.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् ।। 7.72.9 ।।
explanation: He, having saluted the great-souled one, who was blazing with splendor, spoke words with folded hands to Rama, whose prowess was true.

shloka_text: यदाज्ञप्तं महाराज सर्वं तत्कृतवानहम् । हतः स लवणः पापः पुरी चास्य निवेशिता ।। 7.72.10 ।।
explanation: O great king, I have accomplished all that was commanded. That sinful Lavana has been killed, and his city has been established.

shloka_text: द्वादशैते गता वर्षास्त्वां विना रघुनन्दन । नोत्सहेयमहं वस्तुं त्वया विरहितो नृप ।। 7.72.11 ।।
explanation: These twelve years have passed without you, O Raghunandana. I cannot bear to live separated from you, O King.

shloka_text: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम । मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम् ।। 7.72.12 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, O one of immeasurable valor, grant me your favor. Like a motherless calf, I shall not stay away for long.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणं शत्रुघ्नं परिष्वज्येदमब्रवीत् । मा विषादं कृथाः शूर नैतत्क्षत्रियचेष्टितम् ।। 7.72.13 ।।
explanation: Embracing Shatrughna, who was speaking thus, he said this: "O brave one, do not grieve! This is not the conduct of a Kshatriya."

shloka_text: नावसीदन्ति राजानो विप्रवासेषु राघव । प्रजा नः परिपाल्या हि क्षत्रधर्मेण राघव ।। 7.72.14 ।।
explanation: Kings do not become distressed in foreign lands, O Raghava. For our subjects must indeed be protected by the duty of a Kshatriya, O Raghava.

shloka_text: काले काले तु मां वीर अयोध्यामवलोकितुम् । आगच्छ त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गन्तासि च पुरं तव ।। 7.72.15 ।।
explanation: O hero, O best among men, you must come to Ayodhya from time to time to see me, and you will return to your city.

shloka_text: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः । अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम् ।। 7.72.16 ।।
explanation: You are very dear to me, even more than life, there is no doubt. And the protection of the kingdom must certainly be carried out.

shloka_text: तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रमिहावस । ऊर्ध्वं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.72.17 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O Kakutstha, you stay here for seven nights. Afterwards, you will go to Mathura with your servants, army, and vehicles.

shloka_text: रामस्यैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तं मनोगतम् । शत्रुघ्नो दीनया वाचा बाढमित्येव चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.72.18 ।।
explanation: Having heard these righteous and heartfelt words of Rama, Shatrughna, with a humble voice, simply said, "Yes, indeed."

shloka_text: सप्तरात्रं च काकुत्स्थो राघवस्य यथाज्ञया । उष्य तत्र महेष्वासो गमनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.72.19 ।।
explanation: And Kakutstha, the great archer, having stayed there for seven nights according to Raghava's command, prepared to depart.

shloka_text: आमन्त्र्य तु महात्मानं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् । भरतं लक्ष्मणं चैव महारथमुपारुहत् ।। 7.72.20 ।।
explanation: Having taken leave of the great-souled Rama, whose valor is true, and Bharata and Lakshmana, he then ascended a great chariot.

shloka_text: दूरमाभ्यामनुगतो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना । भरतेन च शत्रुघ्नो जगामाशु पुरं ततः ।। 7.72.21 ।।
explanation: Then, Shatrughna, accompanied a long distance by the great-souled Lakshmana and Bharata, quickly went to the city.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 72 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the seventy-second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by a sage.

shloka_text: प्रस्थाप्य तु स शत्रुघ्नं भ्रातृभ्यां सह राघवः । प्रमुमोद सुखी राज्यं धर्मेण परिपालयन् ।। 7.73.1 ।।
explanation: Having dispatched Shatrughna, Rama, accompanied by his two brothers, ruled the kingdom righteously and was happy, greatly rejoicing.

shloka_text: ततः कतिपयाहःसु वृद्धो जानपदो द्विजः । मृतं बालमुपादाय राजद्वारमुपागमत् ।। 7.73.2 ।।
explanation: Then, in a few days, an old country brahmin, taking a dead child, approached the royal gate.

shloka_text: रुदन्बहुविधा वाचः स्नेहदुःखसमन्विताः । असकृत्पुत्र पुत्रेति वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.73.3 ।।
explanation: Weeping, he spoke many kinds of words, filled with love and sorrow, repeatedly uttering the phrase, 'O son! O son!'

shloka_text: किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम् । यदहं पुत्रमेकं त्वां पश्यामि निधनं गतम् ।। 7.73.4 ।।
explanation: What evil deed did I commit in a previous life, that I see you, my only son, dead?

shloka_text: अप्राप्तयौवनं बालं पञ्चवर्षसहस्रकम् । अकाले कालमापन्नं मम दुःखाय पुत्रक ।। 7.73.5 ।।
explanation: O son, my child, who had not attained youth, though five thousand years old, met an untimely death, to my sorrow.

shloka_text: अल्पैरहोभिर्निधनं गमिष्यामि न संशयः । अहं च जननी चैव तव शोकेन पुत्रक ।। 7.73.6 ।।
explanation: In a few days, I will surely die. Both I and your mother, O son, will perish from your grief.

shloka_text: न स्मराम्यनृतं ह्युक्तं न च हिंसां स्मराम्यहम् । सर्वेषां प्राणिनां पापं कृतं नैव स्मराम्यहम् ।। 7.73.7 ।।
explanation: I do not remember ever having spoken an untruth, nor do I remember any act of violence. I certainly do not remember having committed any sin against any living being.

shloka_text: केनाद्य दुष्कृतेनायं बाल एव ममात्मजः । अकृत्वा पितृकार्याणि गतो वैवस्वतक्षयम् ।। 7.73.8 ।।
explanation: By what misdeed today has this son of mine, a mere child, gone to the abode of Yama without performing the ancestral duties?

shloka_text: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं मे श्रुतं वा घोरदर्शनम् । मृत्युरप्राप्तकालानां रामस्य विषये यथा ।। 7.73.9 ।।
explanation: I have never before seen or heard of such a terrible sight, like the death of those whose time has not yet come, in Rama's kingdom.

shloka_text: रामस्य दुष्कृतं किञ्चिन्महदस्ति न संशयः । यथा हि विषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युरागतः ।। 7.73.10 ।।
explanation: There is no doubt that Rama has committed some great misdeed, just as death has come upon the children of the subjects.

shloka_text: नह्यन्यविषयस्थानां बालानां मृत्युतो भयम् । त्वं राजञ्जीवयस्वैनं बालं मृत्युवशं गतम् ।। 7.73.11 ।।
explanation: Indeed, children in other lands have no fear of death. O King, you revive this child who has fallen under the sway of death.

shloka_text: राजद्वारि मरिष्यामि पत्न्या सार्धमनाथवत् । ब्रह्महत्यां ततो राम समुपेत्य सुखी भव ।। 7.73.12 ।।
explanation: I will die at the king's gate with my wife, like an orphan. Then, O Rama, having incurred the sin of killing a Brahmin, be happy.

shloka_text: भ्रातृभिः सहितो राजन्दीर्घमायुरवाप्स्यसि । उषिताः स्म सुखं राज्ये तवास्मिन्सुमहाबल ।। 7.73.13 ।।
explanation: O King, accompanied by your brothers, you will obtain a long life. O greatly mighty one, we have resided happily in this your kingdom.

shloka_text: इदं तु पतितं तस्मात्तव राम वशे स्थिताः । कालस्य वशमापन्नाः स्वल्पं हि नहि नः सुखम् ।। 7.73.14 ।।
explanation: O Rama, this has indeed fallen from that. We are situated under your control, having fallen under the sway of time. Indeed, there is not even a little happiness for us.

shloka_text: सम्प्रत्यनाथो विषय इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम् । रामं नाथमिहासाद्य बालान्तकरणं ध्रुवम् ।। 7.73.15 ।।
explanation: Now, the kingdom of the great-souled Ikshvakus, being without a lord, having obtained Rama as its lord here, will certainly be the destroyer of children.

shloka_text: राजदोषैर्विपद्यन्ते प्रजा ह्यविधिपालिताः । असद्वृत्ते तु नृपतावकाले म्रियते जनः ।। 7.73.16 ।।
explanation: Subjects, when ill-governed, perish due to the king's faults. But when the king is of bad conduct, people die untimely.

shloka_text: यद्वा पुरेष्वयुक्तानि जना जनपदेषु च । कुर्वते न च रक्षा ऽस्ति तदा कालकृतं भयम् ।। 7.73.17 ।।
explanation: Or when people commit improper acts in cities and in the countryside, and there is no protection, then there is fear caused by time.

shloka_text: सुव्यक्तं राजदोषो हि भविष्यति न संशयः । पुरे जनपदे चापि ततो बालवधो ह्ययम् ।। 7.73.18 ।।
explanation: It will very clearly be the king's fault, there is no doubt. And in the city and the countryside, this killing of children is indeed due to that.

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधैर्वाक्यैरुपरुध्य मुहुर्मुहुः । राजानं दुःखसन्तप्तः सुतं तमुपगूहते ।। 7.73.19 ।।
explanation: Thus, repeatedly importuning the king with various words, he, distressed by sorrow, embraces that son.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 73 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the seventy-third chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: तथा तु करुणं तस्य द्विजस्य परिदेवनम् । शुश्राव राघवः सर्वं दुःखशोकसमन्वितम् ।। 7.74.1 ।।
explanation: Thus, Rama heard all the piteous lamentation of that Brahmin, filled with sorrow and grief.

shloka_text: स दुःखेन च सन्तप्तो मन्त्रिणस्तानुपाह्वयत् । वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च भ्रातरौ सह नैगमान् ।। 7.74.2 ।।
explanation: He, tormented by sorrow, summoned those ministers, and Vasishtha, Vamadeva, the two brothers, along with the citizens.

shloka_text: ततो द्विजा वसिष्ठेन सार्धमष्टौ प्रवेशिताः । राजानं देवसङ्काशं वर्धस्वेति ततो ऽब्रुवन् ।। 7.74.3 ।।
explanation: Then, eight Brahmins, along with Vasiṣṭha, were introduced to the king, who resembled a god. Then they said, "May you prosper!"

shloka_text: मार्कण्डेयो ऽथ मौद्गल्यो वामदेवश्च काश्यपः । कात्यायनो ऽथ जाबालिर्गौतमो नारदस्तथा । एते द्विजर्षभाः सर्वे आसनेषूपवेशिताः ।। 7.74.4 ।।
explanation: Markandeya, and Mudgalya, Vamadeva, and Kashyapa, Katyayana, and Jabali, Gautama, and Narada – all these eminent Brahmins were seated on seats.

shloka_text: महर्षीन्समनुप्राप्तानभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः । मन्त्रिणो नैगमांश्चैव यथार्हमनुकूलतः ।। 7.74.5 ।।
explanation: Having greeted the great sages who had arrived, with folded hands, and also the ministers and citizens, appropriately and respectfully.

shloka_text: तेषां समुपविष्टानां सर्वेषां दीप्ततेजसाम् । राघवः सर्वमाचष्टे द्विजो ऽयमुपरोधते ।। 7.74.6 ।।
explanation: To all of them, who were seated and possessed of blazing splendor, Rama explained everything: "This Brahmin is causing trouble."

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राज्ञो दीनस्य नारदः । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमृषीणां सन्निधौ नृपम् ।। 7.74.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of the distressed king, Narada, in the presence of the sages, replied to the king with auspicious words.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्यथाकाले प्राप्तो बालस्य सङ्क्षयः । श्रुत्वा कर्तव्यतां राजन्कुरुष्वरघुनन्दन ।। 7.74.8 ।।
explanation: Listen, O King, how the child's demise occurred in due time. Having heard what is to be done, O King, perform it, O Raghunandana.

shloka_text: पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्ब्राह्मणा वै तपस्विनः । अब्राह्मणस्तदा राजन्न तपस्वी कथञ्चन ।। 7.74.9 ।।
explanation: Formerly, in the Krita Yuga, O King, Brahmins were indeed ascetics. At that time, O King, a non-Brahmin was never an ascetic.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्युगे प्रज्वलिते ब्रह्मभूते त्वनावृते । अमृत्यवस्तदा सर्वे जज्ञिरे दीर्घदर्शिनः ।। 7.74.10 ।।
explanation: In that blazing, divine, and unobstructed age, all the immortal and far-seeing ones were born.

shloka_text: ततस्त्रेतायुगं नाम मानवानां वपुष्मताम् । क्षत्रियास्तत्र जायन्ते पूर्णेन तपसा ऽन्विताः ।। 7.74.11 ।।
explanation: Then came the age named Treta Yuga, for embodied humans. In that age, Kshatriyas are born, endowed with complete austerity.

shloka_text: वीर्येण तपसा चैव ते ऽधिकाः पूर्वजन्मनि । मानवा ये महात्मानस्त्वत्र त्रेतायुगे युगे ।। 7.74.12 ।।
explanation: By valor and by penance, they were superior in previous births, those great-souled humans who are here in the Treta Yuga, in this age.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मक्षत्रं च तत्सर्वं यत्पूर्वमपरं च यत् । युगयोरुभयोरासीत्समवीर्यसमन्वितम् ।। 7.74.13 ।।
explanation: The entire Brahma-Kshatra, both what was earlier and what was later, was endowed with equal prowess in both ages.

shloka_text: अपश्यंस्तु न ते सर्वे विशेषमधिकं ततः । स्थापनं चक्रिरे तत्र चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य सम्मतम् ।। 7.74.14 ।।
explanation: Even though all of them did not perceive any greater distinction than that, they established there the agreed-upon system of four varnas.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्युगे प्रज्वलिते धर्मभूते ह्यनावृते । अधर्मः पादमेकं तु पातयत्पृथिवीतले ।। 7.74.15 ।।
explanation: In that age, when Dharma was fully manifest and unobstructed, unrighteousness indeed placed one foot on the earth.

shloka_text: अधर्मेण हि संयुक्तस्तेजो मन्दं भविष्यति ।। 7.74.16 ।।
explanation: For, indeed, when associated with unrighteousness, one's splendor will become dim.

shloka_text: आमिषं यच्च पूर्वेषां राजसं च मलं भृशम् । अनृतं नाम तद्भूतं पादेन पृथिवीतले ।। 7.74.17 ।।
explanation: And that which is the temptation of the ancients, and a very great Rajasic impurity, that being named Untruth, has taken a foothold on the surface of the earth.

shloka_text: अनृतं पातयित्वा तु पादमेकमधर्मतः । ततः प्रादुष्कृतं पूर्वमायुषः परिनिष्ठितम् ।। 7.74.18 ।।
explanation: Indeed, having uttered one falsehood unrighteously, then the former part of life is revealed as concluded.

shloka_text: पतिते त्वनृते तस्मिन्नधर्मे च महीतले । शुभान्येवाचरँल्लोकः सत्यधर्मपरायणः ।। 7.74.19 ।।
explanation: When that untruth and unrighteousness had fallen upon the earth, the people, devoted to truth and righteousness, performed only auspicious deeds.

shloka_text: त्रेतायुगे च वर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाश्च ये । तपो ऽतप्यन्त ते सर्वे शुश्रूषामपरे जनाः ।। 7.74.20 ।।
explanation: In the Treta Yuga, those Brahmins and Kshatriyas who existed, all of them performed penance. Other people rendered service.

shloka_text: स धर्मः परमस्तेषां वैश्यशूद्रं समागमत् । पूजां च सर्ववर्णानां शूद्राश्चक्रुर्विशेषतः ।। 7.74.21 ।।
explanation: That supreme dharma came to be associated with the Vaisyas and Shudras. And the Shudras especially performed worship of all castes.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तेषामधर्मे चानृते च ह । ततः पूर्वे भृशं ह्रासमगमन्नृपसत्तम ।। 7.74.22 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, due to their unrighteousness and untruth, the former ones greatly declined, O best of kings.

shloka_text: ततः पादमधर्मस्स द्वितीयमवतारयत् । ततो द्वापरसञ्ज्ञा ऽस्य युगस्य समजायत ।। 7.74.23 ।।
explanation: Then Adharma manifested its second quarter. Thereafter, this age came to be known as Dvapara.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्द्वापरसञ्ज्ञे तु वर्तमाने युगक्षये । अधर्मश्चानृतं चैव ववृधे पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.74.24 ।।
explanation: O best among men, in that Dvapara Yuga, which was then ongoing at the decline of the age, unrighteousness and untruth indeed increased.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्द्वापरसङ्ख्याते तपो वैश्यान्समाविशत् । त्रिभ्यो युगेभ्यस्त्रीन्वर्णान्क्रमाद्वै तप आविशत् ।। 7.74.25 ।।
explanation: In that Dvapara age, austerity entered the Vaishyas. Indeed, austerity entered the three varnas sequentially from the three ages.

shloka_text: त्रिभ्यो युगेभ्यस्त्रीन्वर्णान्धर्मश्च परिनिष्ठितः । न शुद्धो लभते धर्मं युगतस्तु नरर्षभ । हीनवर्णो नृपश्रेष्ठ तप्यते सुमहत्तपः ।। 7.74.26 ।।
explanation: Dharma is established for the three varnas throughout the three yugas. A Shudra does not obtain Dharma, O best among men, due to the age. A person of lower varna, O best of kings, performs very great penance.

shloka_text: भविष्यच्छूद्रयोन्यां वै तपश्चर्या कलौ युगे । अधर्मः परमो राजन्द्वापरे शूद्रजन्मनः ।। 7.74.27 ।।
explanation: O King, for those who will be born as Shudras in the Kali Yuga, the practice of asceticism is indeed the greatest unrighteousness, just as it was for one born as a Shudra in the Dvapara Yuga.

shloka_text: स वै विषयपर्यन्ते तव राजन्महातपाः । अद्य तप्यति दुर्बुद्धिस्तेन बालवधो ह्ययम् ।। 7.74.28 ।।
explanation: O King, that evil-minded great ascetic is indeed performing penance today at the border of your kingdom. Therefore, this is the killing of children.

shloka_text: यो ह्यधर्ममकार्यं वा विषये पार्थिवस्य तु । करोति चाश्रीमूलं तत्पुरे वा दुर्मतिर्नरः । क्षिप्रं च नरकं याति स च राजा न संशयः ।। 7.74.29 ।।
explanation: That evil-minded person who commits unrighteousness or an improper act, which is the source of misfortune, in the king's realm or in that city, quickly goes to hell, and that king too, without doubt.

shloka_text: अधीतस्य च तप्तस्य कर्मणः सुकृतस्य च । षष्ठं भजति भागं तु प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् ।। 7.74.30 ।।
explanation: Protecting the subjects righteously, one obtains the sixth share of the merit from study, penance, and good deeds.

shloka_text: षङ्भागस्य न भोक्ता ऽसौ रक्षते न प्रजाः कथम् ।। 7.74.31 ।।
explanation: How can he, who does not protect the subjects, be the enjoyer of the sixth part?

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल मार्गस्व विषयं स्वकम् । दुष्कृतं यत्र पश्येथास्तत्र यत्नं समाचर ।। 7.74.32 ।।
explanation: O best of men, you should investigate your own domain. Where you perceive wrongdoing, there make an effort.

shloka_text: एवं चेद्धर्मवृद्धिश्च नृणां चायुर्विवर्धनम् । भविष्यति नरश्रेष्ठ बालस्यास्य च जीवितम् ।। 7.74.33 ।।
explanation: If this is so, O best among men, there will be an increase in righteousness and the longevity of people, and also the life of this child will be preserved.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 74 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred text composed by a sage, the glorious Ramayana, composed by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the seventy-fourth chapter.

shloka_text: नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा ऽमृतमयं तदा । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे लक्ष्मणं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.75.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard that nectar-like speech of Narada, he obtained unequalled joy and spoke this to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: गच्छ सौम्य द्विजश्रेष्ठं समाश्वासय सुव्रतम् । बालस्य तु शरीरं तत्तैलद्रोण्यां निधापय ।। 7.75.2 ।।
explanation: Go, O gentle one, console the virtuous best of Brahmins. And place that child's body in the oil-tub.

shloka_text: गन्धैश्च परमोदारैस्तैलैश्चापि सुगन्धिभिः । यथा न क्षीयते बालस्तथा सौम्य विधीयताम् ।। 7.75.3 ।।
explanation: And with very excellent fragrances, and also with fragrant oils, O gentle one, let it be done so that the child does not waste away.

shloka_text: यथा शरीरो बालस्य गुप्तः सन् शिष्टकर्मणः । विपत्तिः परिभेदो वा न भवेच्च तथा कुरु ।। 7.75.4 ।।
explanation: Just as the body of a child, being protected by proper action, should not suffer calamity or injury, so should you act.

shloka_text: एवमादिश्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम् । मनसा पुष्पकं दध्यावागच्छेति महायशाः ।। 7.75.5 ।।
explanation: Thus having commanded Lakshmana of auspicious marks, the greatly renowned Kakutstha mentally thought, "Let the Pushpaka come!"

shloka_text: इङ्गितं स तु विज्ञाय पुष्पको हेमभूषितः । आजगाम मुहूर्तेन समीपे राघवस्य वै ।। 7.75.6 ।।
explanation: And that gold-adorned Pushpaka, having understood the hint, indeed came in a moment near Rama.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीत्प्रणतो भूत्वा अयमस्मि नराधिप । वश्यस्तव महाबाहो किङ्करः समुपस्थितः ।। 7.75.7 ।।
explanation: He, having bowed down, said: 'O King, O mighty-armed one, I am present here as your obedient servant.'

shloka_text: भाषितं रुचिरं श्रुत्वा पुष्पकस्य नराधिपः । अभिवाद्य महर्षींस्तान् विमानं सो ऽध्यरोहत ।। 7.75.8 ।।
explanation: Having heard Pushpaka's delightful speech, the king, after saluting those great sages, ascended the aerial chariot.

shloka_text: धनुर्गृहीत्वा तूणी च खड्गं च रुचिरप्रभम् । निक्षिप्य नगरे वीरौ सौमित्रिभरतावुभौ ।। 7.75.9 ।।
explanation: Having left the bow, the quiver, and the splendidly shining sword in the city, both the heroes Saumitri and Bharata,

shloka_text: प्रायात्प्रतीचीं हरितं विचिन्वंश्च ततस्ततः । उत्तरामगमच्छ्रीमान्दिशं हिमवता वृताम् ।। 7.75.10 ।।
explanation: He went to the western quarter, searching here and there. The glorious one then proceeded to the northern quarter, which was enveloped by the Himalayas.

shloka_text: अपश्यमानस्तत्रापि स्वल्पमप्यथ दुष्कृतम् । पूर्वामपि दिशं सर्वामथो ऽपश्यन्नराधिपः ।। 7.75.11 ।।
explanation: Not finding even a slight wrong there, the king then did not see the entire eastern direction.

shloka_text: प्रविशुद्धसमाचारामादर्शतलनिर्मलाम् । पुष्पकस्थो महाबाहुस्तदापश्यन्नराधिपः ।। 7.75.12 ।।
explanation: Then the mighty-armed king, seated in the Pushpaka, beheld her, whose conduct was perfectly pure and who was as clear as a mirror's surface.

shloka_text: दक्षिणां दिशमाक्रामत्ततो राजर्षिनन्दनः । शैवलस्योत्तरे पार्श्वे ददर्श सुमहत्सरः ।। 7.75.13 ।।
explanation: Then the son of the royal sage proceeded towards the southern direction. On the northern side of Shaivala, he saw a very large lake.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्सरसि तप्यन्तं तापसं सुमहत्तपः । ददर्श राघवः श्रीमाँल्लम्बमानमधोमुखम् ।। 7.75.14 ।।
explanation: The glorious Rama saw an ascetic in that lake, performing a very great penance, hanging head downwards.

shloka_text: राघवस्तमुपागम्य तप्यन्तं तप उत्तमम् । उवाच स तदा वाक्यं धन्यस्त्वमसि सुव्रत ।। 7.75.15 ।।
explanation: Rama, having approached him who was performing excellent penance, then spoke these words: "O virtuous one, you are blessed."

shloka_text: कस्यां योन्यां तपोवृद्ध वर्तसे दृढविक्रम । कौतूहलात्त्वां पृच्छामि रामो दाशरथिर्ह्यहम् ।। 7.75.16 ।।
explanation: O one aged in penance, O mighty one, in what species are you born? I ask you out of curiosity, for I am Rama, the son of Dasaratha.

shloka_text: को ऽर्थो मनीषितस्तुभ्यं स्वर्गलाभः परो ऽथवा । वराश्रयो यदर्थं त्वं तपस्यसि सुदुष्करम् । यमाश्रित्य तपस्तप्तं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तापस ।। 7.75.17 ।।
explanation: What is your desired object? Is it the attainment of heaven, or something else supreme? For what boon are you performing such extremely arduous penance? O ascetic, I wish to hear for whom this penance has been undertaken.

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणो वा ऽसि भद्रं ते क्षत्रियो वा ऽसि दुर्जयः । वैश्यस्तृतीयवर्णो वा शूद्रो वा सत्यवाग्भव ।। 7.75.18 ।।
explanation: Whether you are a Brahmin, may good fortune be yours; or a Kshatriya, unconquerable; or a Vaishya, the third class; or a Shudra, be truthful.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तः स नराधिपेन ह्यवाक्छिरा दाशरथाय तस्मै । उवाच जातिं नृपपुङ्गवाय यत्कारणे चैव तपःप्रयत्नः ।। 7.75.19 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the king, he, with his head bowed down, spoke to that son of Dasharatha, the best of kings, about his origin and the reason for his ascetic endeavor.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 75 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred epic Śrīmad Rāmāyaṇa, the original poem by Vālmīki, in the glorious Uttarakāṇḍa, is the seventy-fifth chapter.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । अवाक्छिरास्तथाभूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.76.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of Rama, the one of unblemished deeds, he, with his head bowed down, spoke this statement.

shloka_text: शूद्रयोन्यां प्रसूतो ऽस्मि शम्बूको नाम नामतः । देवत्वं पार्थये राम सशरीरो महायशः ।। 7.76.2 ।।
explanation: I am born from a Shudra womb, my name is Shambuka. O greatly renowned Rama, I seek divinity with this body.

shloka_text: न मिथ्या ऽहं वदे राम देवलोकजिगीषया । शूद्रं मां विद्धि काकुत्स्थ तप उग्रं समास्थितम् ।। 7.76.3 ।।
explanation: O Rama, I do not speak falsely with the desire to conquer the world of the gods. O Kakutstha, know me to be a Shudra who has undertaken severe penance.

shloka_text: भाषतस्तस्य शूद्रस्य खड्गं सुरुचिरप्रभम् । निष्कृष्य कोशाद्विमलं शिरश्चिच्छेद राघवः ।। 7.76.4 ।।
explanation: As that Shudra spoke, Rama, drawing out from the sheath his spotless, very radiant sword, cut off his head.

shloka_text: तस्मिञ्छूद्रे हते देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः । साधु साध्विति काकुत्स्थं प्रशशंसुर्मुहुर्मुहुः ।। 7.76.5 ।।
explanation: Upon the killing of that Shudra, the gods, with Indra and Agni at their forefront, repeatedly praised Kakutstha, saying, "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: पुष्पवृष्टिर्महत्यासीद्दिव्यानां सुसुगन्धिनाम् । पुष्पाणां वायुमुक्तानां सर्वतः प्रपपात ह ।। 7.76.6 ।।
explanation: A great shower of divine, very fragrant flowers occurred. Wind-blown flowers fell everywhere from all sides.

shloka_text: सुप्रीताश्चाब्रुवन्रामं देवाः सत्यपराक्रमम् । सुरकार्यमिदं सौम्य सुकृतं ते महामते ।। 7.76.7 ।।
explanation: And the well-pleased gods spoke to Rama, whose valor is true: "This divine task, O gentle one, has been well accomplished by you, O great-minded one."

shloka_text: गृहाण च वरं सौम्य यत्त्वमिच्छस्यरिन्दम । स्वर्गभाङ्नहि शूद्रो ऽयं त्वत्कृते रघुनन्दन ।। 7.76.8 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, O subduer of enemies, accept the boon that you desire. This Shudra is certainly not a partaker of heaven for your sake, O delight of the Raghus.

shloka_text: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा राघवः सुसमाहितः । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं सहस्राक्षं पुरन्दरम् ।। 7.76.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the gods, Rama, being very composed, spoke with folded hands to the thousand-eyed Purandara.

shloka_text: यदि देवाः प्रसन्ना मे द्विजपुत्रः स जीवतु । दिशन्तु वरमेतं मे इप्सितं परमं मम ।। 7.76.10 ।।
explanation: If the gods are pleased with me, may that brahmin's son live. May they grant me this boon, my supreme desire.

shloka_text: ममापचाराद्यातो ऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्यैकपुत्रकः । अप्राप्तकालः कालेन नीतो वैवस्वतक्षयम् ।। 7.76.11 ।।
explanation: Due to my offense, that only son of the Brahmin, whose time had not yet come, was taken by Time to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: तं जीवयथ भद्रं वो नानृतं कर्तुमर्हथ । द्विजस्य संश्रुतो ऽर्थो मे जीवयिष्यामि ते सुतम् ।। 7.76.12 ।।
explanation: Revive him, may good fortune be to you. You should not commit falsehood. I have promised the Brahmin's request; I will revive your son.

shloka_text: राघवस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा विबुधसत्तमाः । प्रत्युचू राघवं प्रीता देवाः प्रीतिसमन्वितम् ।। 7.76.13 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of Rama, the best among the gods, delighted and filled with joy, replied to Rama.

shloka_text: निर्वृतो भव काकुत्स्थ सो ऽस्मिन्नहनि बालकः । जीवितं प्राप्तवान्भूयः समेतश्चापि बन्धुभिः ।। 7.76.14 ।।
explanation: Be comforted, O Kakutstha. On this very day, the boy has regained his life and has been reunited with his kinsmen.

shloka_text: यस्मिन्मुहूर्ते काकुत्स्थ शूद्रो ऽयं विनिपातितः । तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते बालो ऽसौ जीवेन समयुज्यत ।। 7.76.15 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, at the moment this Shudra was struck down, at that very moment that child was reunited with life.

shloka_text: स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते साधु याम नरर्षभ । अगस्त्यस्याश्रमपदं द्रष्टुमिच्छाम राघव ।। 7.76.16 ।।
explanation: May you attain well-being, good fortune be to you. O best among men, let us go. O Raghava, we wish to see Agastya's hermitage.

shloka_text: तस्य दीक्षा समाप्ता हि ब्रह्मर्षेः सुमहाद्युतेः । द्वादशं हि गतं वर्षं जलशय्यां समासतः ।। 7.76.17 ।।
explanation: The initiation of that greatly effulgent Brahmarshi was completed. Indeed, the twelfth year of his water-penance had entirely passed.

shloka_text: काकुत्स्थ तद्गमिष्यामो मुनिं समभिनन्दितुम् । त्वं चाप्यागच्छ भद्रं ते द्रष्टुं तमृषिसत्तमम् ।। 7.76.18 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, we shall therefore go to greet the sage. And you too come, may good befall you, to see that best of sages.

shloka_text: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय देवानां रघुनन्दनः । आरुरोह विमानं तं पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम् ।। 7.76.19 ।।
explanation: Having promised the gods, 'So be it,' Rama, the delight of the Raghus, ascended that Pushpaka aerial chariot, adorned with gold.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः प्रयातास्ते विमानैर्बहुविस्तरैः । रामो ऽप्यनुजगामाशु कुम्भयोनेस्तपोवनम् ।। 7.76.20 ।।
explanation: Then those gods departed by their vast aerial chariots. Rama also quickly went to the hermitage of Agastya.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु देवान्सम्प्राप्तानगस्त्यस्तपसां निधिः । अर्चयामास धर्मात्मा सर्वांस्तानविशेषतः ।। 7.76.21 ।।
explanation: Having seen the gods who had arrived, Agastya, the righteous-souled and a treasure of austerities, worshipped all of them without distinction.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य ततः पूजां सम्पूज्य च महामुनिम् । जग्मुस्ते त्रिदशा हृष्टा नाकपृष्ठं सहानुगैः ।। 7.76.22 ।।
explanation: Then, having accepted the worship and having honored the great sage, those delighted gods, along with their followers, went to heaven.

shloka_text: गतेषु तेषु काकुत्स्थः पुष्पकादवरुह्य च । ततो ऽभिवादयामास ह्यगस्त्यमृषिसत्तमम् ।। 7.76.23 ।।
explanation: When they had departed, Kakutstha, having descended from the Pushpaka, then paid his respects to Agastya, the foremost among sages.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । आतिथ्यं परमं प्राप्य निषसाद नराधिपः ।। 7.76.24 ।।
explanation: Having saluted the great soul, who was blazing with splendor, the king received supreme hospitality and then sat down.

shloka_text: तमुवाच महातेजाः कुम्भयोनिर्महातपाः । स्वागतं ते नरश्रेष्ठ दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो ऽसि राघव ।। 7.76.25 ।।
explanation: The greatly effulgent Agastya, the great ascetic, said to him: "Welcome to you, O best among men, O Raghava, by good fortune you have arrived."

shloka_text: त्वं मे बहुमतो राम गुणैर्बहुभिरुत्तमैः । अतिथिः पूजनीयश्च मम नित्यं हृदि स्थितः ।। 7.76.26 ।।
explanation: O Rama, you are highly esteemed by me for your many excellent qualities. You are a guest worthy of worship, and you always dwell in my heart.

shloka_text: सुरा हि कथयन्ति त्वामागतं शूद्रघातिनम् । ब्राह्मणस्य तु धर्मेण त्वया जीवापितः सुतः ।। 7.76.27 ।।
explanation: The gods indeed declare that you have come as a killer of a Shudra. But by the dharma of a Brahmana, a son was brought back to life by you.

shloka_text: उष्यतां चेह रजनी सकाशे मम राघव । प्रभाते पुष्पकेण त्वं गन्ता ऽसि पुरमेव हि ।। 7.76.28 ।।
explanation: Let the night be spent here in my presence, O Raghava. In the morning, you will indeed go to the city by the Pushpaka.

shloka_text: त्वं हि नारायणः श्रीमांस्त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । त्वं प्रभुः सर्वदेवानां पुरुषस्त्वं सनातनः ।। 7.76.29 ।।
explanation: You are indeed the glorious Narayana; in you everything is established. You are the lord of all gods; you are the eternal Purusha.

shloka_text: इदं चाभरणं सौम्य निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा । दिव्यं दिव्येन वपुषा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । प्रतिगृह्णीष्व काकुत्स्थ मत्प्रियं कुरु राघव ।। 7.76.30 ।।
explanation: And this ornament, O gentle one, created by Vishwakarma, is divine, shining with divine splendor and its own brilliance. Please accept it, O Kakutstha, and do this favor for me, O Raghava.

shloka_text: दत्तस्य हि पुनर्दाने सुमहत्फलमुच्यते । भरणे हि भवान् शक्तः सेन्द्राणां मरुतामपि ।। 7.76.31 ।।
explanation: Indeed, a very great reward is declared for returning what has been given. For you are capable of sustaining even the Maruts along with Indra.

shloka_text: त्वं हि शक्तस्तारयितुं सेन्द्रानपि दिवौकसः । तस्मात्प्रदास्ये विधिवत्तत्प्रतीच्छ नराधिप ।। 7.76.32 ।।
explanation: Indeed, you are capable of saving even the gods, including Indra. Therefore, I shall properly bestow it; O king, accept that.

shloka_text: दिव्यमाभरणं चित्रं प्रदीप्तमिव भास्करम् ।। 7.76.33 ।।
explanation: A divine and wonderful ornament, radiant like the sun.

shloka_text: अथोवाच महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः । रामो मतिमतां श्रेष्ठः क्षत्रधर्ममनुस्मरन् ।। 7.76.34 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, the great charioteer of the Ikshvakus, the best among the intelligent, remembering the duty of a Kshatriya, spoke to the great-souled one.

shloka_text: प्रतिग्रहो ऽयं भगवन्ब्राह्मणस्याविगर्हितः । गृह्णीयां क्षत्रियो ऽहं वै कथं ब्राह्मणपुङ्गव ।। 7.76.35 ।।
explanation: O revered one, this acceptance is blameless for a Brahmana. I am a Kshatriya, O best among Brahmanas, how can I accept it?

shloka_text: ब्राह्मणेन विशेषेण दत्तं तद्वक्तुमर्हसि । एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण प्रत्युवाच महानृषिः ।। 7.76.36 ।।
explanation: You ought to tell that which was given, especially by a Brahmin. Thus spoken by Rama, the great sage replied.

shloka_text: आसन्कृतयुगे राम ब्रह्मभूते पुरायुगे । अपार्थिवाः प्रजाः सर्वाः सुराणां तु शतक्रतुः ।। 7.76.37 ।।
explanation: O Rama, in the Krita Yuga, in the ancient age when Brahma was, all beings were non-earthly, and Indra was the lord of the gods.

shloka_text: ताः प्रजा देवदेवेशं राजार्थं समुपाद्रवन् । सुराणां स्थापितो राजा त्वया देव शतक्रतुः ।। 7.76.38 ।।
explanation: Those subjects approached the Lord of gods for a king. O God, by you, Indra was appointed as the king of the gods.

shloka_text: प्रयच्छ नो हि लोकेश पार्थिवं नरपुङ्गवम् । यस्मै पूजां प्रयुञ्जाना धूतपापाश्चरेमहि । न वसामो विना राज्ञा एष नो निश्चयः परः ।। 7.76.39 ।।
explanation: O Lord of the world, indeed grant us an earthly ruler, a chief among men, to whom, offering worship, we may live with our sins washed away. We do not dwell without a king; this is our supreme resolve.

shloka_text: प्रजानां वचनं श्रुत्वा निश्चयित्वा ऽर्थमुत्तमम् ।। 7.76.40 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the subjects, and having decided upon the best course of action.

shloka_text: ततो ब्रह्मा सुरश्रेष्ठो लोकपालान्सवासवान् । समाहूयाब्रवीत्सर्वांस्तेजोभागान्प्रयच्छत ।। 7.76.41 ।।
explanation: Then Brahma, the best among gods, having summoned all the guardians of the worlds along with Vasava, said to them: "Give your portions of splendor."

shloka_text: ततो ददुर्लोकपालाः सर्वे भागान्स्वतेजसः । अक्षुपच्च ततो ब्रह्मा यतो जातः क्षुपो नृपः ।। 7.76.42 ।।
explanation: Then all the Lokapalas gave portions of their own splendor. And then Brahma became agitated, from whom King Kṣupa was born.

shloka_text: तं ब्रह्मा लोकपालानां सहांशैः समयोजयत् । ततो ददौ नृपं तासां प्रजानामीश्वरं क्षुपम् ।। 7.76.43 ।।
explanation: Brahma endowed him with the portions of the Lokapalas. Then he appointed Kṣupa as the king, the lord of those subjects.

shloka_text: तत्रैन्द्रेण च भागेन महीमाज्ञापयन्नृपः । वारुणेन तु भागेन वपुः पुष्यति पार्थिवः ।। 7.76.44 ।।
explanation: The king, by the Indric aspect, commands the earth; but by the Varunic aspect, the king nourishes his body.

shloka_text: कौबेरेण तु भागेन वित्तमासां ददौ तदा । यस्तु याम्यो ऽभवद्भागस्तेन शास्ति स्म स प्रजाः ।। 7.76.45 ।।
explanation: He then gave wealth to them from the northern region. And with the southern region, he ruled the people.

shloka_text: तत्रैन्द्रेण नरश्रेष्ठ भागेन रघुनन्दन । प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भद्रं ते तारणार्थं मम प्रभो ।। 7.76.46 ।।
explanation: O best among men, O delight of the Raghus, O Lord, accept that share from Indra for my deliverance. May good fortune be to you.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋषेः परमधार्मिकम् । तद्रामः प्रतिजग्राह मुनेराभरणं वरम् ।। 7.76.47 ।।
explanation: Having heard that highly righteous speech of the sage, Rama accepted that excellent ornament from the sage.

shloka_text: प्रतिगृह्य ततो रामस्तदाभरणमुत्तमम् । आगमं तस्य दीप्तस्य प्रष्टुमेवोपचक्रमे ।। 7.76.48 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, having accepted that excellent ornament, began to inquire about the origin of that radiant one.

shloka_text: अत्यद्भुतमिदं दिव्यं वपुषा युक्तमुत्तमम् । कथं वा भगवता प्राप्तं कुतो वा केन वा हृतम् ।। 7.76.49 ।।
explanation: This exceedingly wonderful, divine, and supreme form, how was it obtained by the Lord? Or from where, or by whom was it taken away?

shloka_text: कुतूहलितया ब्रह्मन्पृच्छामि त्वां महायशः । आश्चर्याणां बहूनां हि निधिः परमको भवान् ।। 7.76.50 ।।
explanation: O Brahman, O greatly renowned one, I ask you out of curiosity. For you are indeed the supreme repository of many wonders.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् । शृणु राम यथावृत्तं पुरा त्रेतायुगे युगे ।। 7.76.51 ।।
explanation: When Kakutstha spoke thus, the sage then said these words: "Listen, O Rama, to what happened formerly in the Treta Yuga."

shloka_text: रमणीयप्रदेशे ऽस्मिन् वने यद्दृष्टवानहम् । आश्चर्यं मे महाबाहो दानमाश्रित्य केवलम् ।। 7.76.52 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, what I saw in this beautiful forest region is a wonder to me, solely concerning charity.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 76 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (work) of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic by Valmiki, this is the seventy-sixth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: पुरा त्रेतायुगे राम बभूव बहुविस्तरम् । समन्ताद्योजनशतं विमृगं पक्षिवर्जितम् ।। 7.77.1 ।।
explanation: Formerly, O Rama, in the Treta Yuga, it was very extensive. For a hundred yojanas all around, it was devoid of animals and birds.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्निर्मानुषे ऽरण्ये कुर्वाणस्तप उत्तमम् । अहमाक्रमितुं सौम्य तदरण्यमुपागमम् ।। 7.77.2 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, I approached that uninhabited forest, where excellent penance was being performed, in order to attack it.

shloka_text: तस्य रूपमरण्यस्य निर्देष्टुं न शशाक ह । फलमूलैः सुखास्वादैर्बहुरूपैश्च पादपैः ।। 7.77.3 ।।
explanation: Indeed, one could not describe the beauty of that forest, with its delicious fruits and roots, and trees of many forms.

shloka_text: तस्यारण्यस्य मध्ये तु सरो योजनमायतम् । हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम् ।। 7.77.4 ।।
explanation: In the middle of that forest, there was a lake a yojana in length, filled with swans and karandavas, and adorned with chakravakas.

shloka_text: पद्मोत्पलसमाकीर्णं समतिक्रान्तशैवलम् । तदाश्चर्यमिवात्यर्थं सुखास्वादमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.77.5 ।।
explanation: Filled with lotuses and water-lilies, free from moss, it was exceedingly wonderful, an unsurpassed delight.

shloka_text: अरजस्कं तथा ऽक्षोभ्यं श्रीमत्पक्षिगणायुतम् । समीपे तस्य सरसो महदद्भुतमाश्रमम् ।। 7.77.6 ।।
explanation: Near that lake, a great and wonderful hermitage, dustless and undisturbed, glorious and filled with flocks of birds.

shloka_text: पुराणं पुण्यमत्यर्थं तपस्विजनवर्जितम् । तत्राहमवसं रात्रिं नैदाघीं पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.77.7 ।।
explanation: An ancient, exceedingly sacred place, yet devoid of ascetics, there I dwelt for a summer night, O best among men.

shloka_text: प्रभाते काल्यमुत्थाय सरस्तदुपचक्रमे । अथापश्यं शवं तत्र सुपुष्टमजरं क्वचित् ।। 7.77.8 ।।
explanation: Having risen early in the morning, I approached that lake. Then, there, I saw somewhere a very robust, undecaying corpse.

shloka_text: पङ्किभेदेन पुष्टाङ्गं समाश्रितसरोवरम् । तिष्ठन्तं परया लक्ष्म्या तस्मिंस्तोयाशये नृप ।। 7.77.9 ।।
explanation: O King, in that water reservoir, standing with supreme splendor, its body nourished by breaking through the mud, having taken refuge in the lake.

shloka_text: तमर्थं चिन्तयानो ऽहं मुहूर्तं तत्र राघव । उषितो ऽस्मि सरस्तीरे किन्न्विदं स्यादिति प्रभो ।। 7.77.10 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, O Lord, pondering that matter, I stayed there for a moment on the bank of the lake, wondering, 'What could this be?'

shloka_text: अथापश्यं मुहूर्तेन दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् । विमानं परमोदारं हंसयुक्तं मनोजवम् ।। 7.77.11 ।।
explanation: Then, in a moment, I saw a divine aerial chariot of wondrous appearance, exceedingly grand, yoked with swans, and swift as thought.

shloka_text: अत्यर्थं स्वर्गिणं त विमाने रघुनन्दन । उपास्ते ऽप्सरसां वीर सहस्रं दिव्यभूषणम् ।। 7.77.12 ।।
explanation: O Raghunandana, O hero, a thousand divinely adorned Apsaras exceedingly attend upon that celestial being in the celestial chariot.

shloka_text: गायन्ति दिव्यगेयानि वादयन्ति तथा ऽपराः । क्ष्वेलयन्ति तथा चान्या नृत्यन्ति च तथा ऽपराः ।। 7.77.13 ।।
explanation: They sing divine songs, and others play instruments. And some others make playful sounds, and still others dance.

shloka_text: अपराश्चन्द्ररश्म्याभैर्हेमदण्डैश्च चामरैः । दोधूयुर्वदनं तस्य पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम् ।। 7.77.14 ।।
explanation: And others fanned his lotus-like eyed face with whisks having golden handles and the luster of moonbeams.

shloka_text: ततः सिंहासनं त्यक्त्वा मेरुकूटमिवांशुमान् । पश्यतो मे तदा राम विमानादवरुह्य च । तं शवं भक्षयामास स स्वर्गी रघुनन्दन ।। 7.77.15 ।।
explanation: Then, O Rama, O scion of Raghu, that heavenly being, having abandoned his throne like the sun (leaving) Mount Meru, and having descended from the aerial chariot, then ate that corpse while I was watching.

shloka_text: तथा भुक्त्वा यथाकामं मांसं बहु सुपीवरम् । अवतीर्य सरः स्वर्गी संस्प्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.77.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, having eaten much very fat meat to his heart's content, the celestial being descended into the lake and began to bathe.

shloka_text: उपस्पृश्य यथान्यायं स स्वर्गी रघुपुङ्गव । आरोढुमुपचक्राम विमानवरमुत्तमम् ।। 7.77.17 ।।
explanation: Having duly performed the ablution, he, the best of the Raghus, who was now celestial, began to ascend the excellent, supreme aerial chariot.

shloka_text: तमहं देवसङ्काशमारोहन्तमुदीक्ष्य वै । अथाहमब्रुवं वाक्यं स्वर्गिणं पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.77.18 ।।
explanation: Having seen him, who was like a god, ascending, I then spoke these words to that heavenly being, O best among men.

shloka_text: को भवान्देवसङ्काश आहारश्च विगर्हितः । त्वयेदं भुज्यते सौम्य किमर्थं वक्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.77.19 ।।
explanation: Who are you, O god-like one? And this food is reprehensible. Why are you eating this, O gentle one? You ought to tell.

shloka_text: कस्य स्यादीदृशो भाव आहारो देवसम्मतः । आश्चर्यं वर्तते सौम्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ।। 7.77.20 ।।
explanation: Whose could be such a disposition and food agreeable to the gods? O gentle one, it is a wonder, I wish to hear it in detail.

shloka_text: नाहमौपयिकं मन्ये तव भक्ष्यमिदं शवम् ।। 7.77.21 ।।
explanation: I do not consider this corpse suitable as your food.

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्तः स नरेन्द्र नाकी कौतूहलात्सूनृतया गिरा च । श्रुत्वा च वाक्यं मम सर्वमेतत्सर्वं तथा चाकथयन्ममेति ।। 7.77.22 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed, that celestial king, out of curiosity and with pleasant speech, having heard all this speech of mine, narrated all of it to me.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 77 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Rāmāyaṇa, the sacred text of the sages, the original epic by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the seventy-seventh chapter.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं वाक्यं मम राम शुभाक्षरम् । प्राञ्जलिः प्रत्युवाचेदं स स्वर्गी रघुनन्दन ।। 7.78.1 ।।
explanation: O Rama, having heard my auspicious words, that celestial being, O Raghunandana, replied thus with folded hands.

shloka_text: शृणु ब्रह्मन्पुरा वृत्तं ममैतत्सुखदुःखयोः । अनतिक्रमणीयं हि यथा पृच्छसि मां द्विज ।। 7.78.2 ।।
explanation: Listen, O Brahmana, to this past account of my joys and sorrows. For it is indeed inevitable, as you ask me, O twice-born.

shloka_text: पुरा वैदर्भको राजा पिता मम महायशाः । सुदेव इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ।। 7.78.3 ।।
explanation: Formerly, my greatly renowned father, the king of Vidarbha, was known as Sudeva, valiant and famous in the three worlds.

shloka_text: तस्य पुत्रद्वयं ब्रह्मन्द्वाभ्यां स्त्रीभ्यामजायत । अहं श्वेत इति ख्यातो यवीयान्सुरथो ऽभवत् ।। 7.78.4 ।।
explanation: O Brahmana, he had two sons born from two wives. I am known as Shveta, and the younger one was Suratha.

shloka_text: ततः पितरि स्वर्याते पौरा मामभ्यषेचयन् । तत्राहं कृतवान्राज्यं धर्म्यं च सुसमाहितः ।। 7.78.5 ।।
explanation: Then, when my father had ascended to heaven, the citizens crowned me. There I ruled the kingdom righteously and with great diligence.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि समतीतानि सुव्रत । राज्यं कारयतो ब्रह्मन्प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः ।। 7.78.6 ।।
explanation: Thus, thousands of years passed, O virtuous one, O Brahmana, while he was ruling the kingdom and protecting the subjects righteously.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं निमित्ते कस्मिंश्चिद्विज्ञातायुर्द्विजोत्तम । कालधर्मं हृदि न्यस्य ततो वनमुपागमम् ।। 7.78.7 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O best of Brahmins, having ascertained my lifespan through some sign, and having resolved the law of time (death) in my heart, I then went to the forest.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं वनमिदं दुर्गं मृगपक्षिविवर्जितम् । तपश्चर्तुं प्रविष्टो ऽस्मि समीपे सरसः शुभे ।। 7.78.8 ।।
explanation: I have entered this formidable forest, devoid of deer and birds, to perform penance near a beautiful lake.

shloka_text: भ्रातरं सुरथं राज्ये ह्यभिषिच्य महीपतिम् । इदं सरः समासाद्य तपस्तप्तं मया चिरम् ।। 7.78.9 ।।
explanation: Having consecrated my brother Suratha as king in the kingdom, I have performed penance for a long time, having reached this lake.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं वर्षसहस्राणि तपस्त्रीणि महावने । तप्त्वा सुदुष्करं प्राप्तो ब्रह्मलोकमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.78.10 ।।
explanation: I, having performed three extremely difficult penances for thousands of years in the great forest, have attained the supreme abode of Brahma.

shloka_text: तस्य मे स्वर्गभूतस्य क्षुत्पिपासे द्विजोत्तम । बाधेते परमोदार ततो ऽहं व्यथितेन्द्रियः । गत्वा त्रिभुवनश्रेष्ठं पितामहमुवाच ह ।। 7.78.11 ।।
explanation: O best of Brahmins, O most generous one, hunger and thirst afflict me, who have attained heaven. Therefore, with distressed senses, I went and spoke to the Grandfather (Brahma), the best of the three worlds.

shloka_text: भगवन्ब्रह्मलोको ऽयं क्षुत्पिपासाविवर्जितः । कस्यायं कर्मणः पाकः क्षुत्पिपासानुगो ह्यहम् ।। 7.78.12 ।।
explanation: O Lord, this world of Brahma is free from hunger and thirst. What is the fruit of the action by which I am indeed afflicted by hunger and thirst?

shloka_text: आहारः कश्च मे देव तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ।। 7.78.13 ।।
explanation: O god, and what is my food? Tell me that, O grandfather.
