shloka_text: पितामहस्तु मामाह तवाहारः सुदेवज । स्वादूनि स्वानि मांसानि तानि भक्षय नित्यशः ।। 7.78.14 ।।
explanation: The Grandfather said to me, "O well-born one, your food is your own delicious flesh. Eat it always."

shloka_text: स्वशरीरं त्वया पुष्टं कुर्वता तप उत्तमम् । अनुप्तं रोहते श्वेत न कदाचिन्महामते ।। 7.78.15 ।।
explanation: O Śveta, O great-minded one, while you perform excellent penance, your own body is nourished. An unsown seed never sprouts.

shloka_text: तृप्तिर्न ते ऽस्ति सूक्ष्मा ऽपि वने सत्वनिषेविते । पुरा तु भिक्षमाणाय भिक्षा वै यतये नृप । न हि दत्ता त्वयेन्द्राभ यस्मादतिथये ऽपि वै ।। 7.78.16 ।।
explanation: You have no satisfaction, not even a little, in this forest frequented by creatures. O King, O Indra-like one, because formerly you did not give alms to an ascetic who was begging, nor indeed did you give anything even to a guest.

shloka_text: दत्तं न ते ऽस्ति सूक्ष्मो ऽपि तप एव निषेवसे । तेन स्वर्गगतो वत्स बाध्यसे क्षुत्पिपासया ।। 7.78.17 ।।
explanation: You have not given even a small amount in charity; you only practiced penance. Therefore, having gone to heaven, dear child, you are tormented by hunger and thirst.

shloka_text: स त्वं सुपुष्टमाहारैः स्वशरीरमनुत्तमम् । भक्षयित्वामृतरसं तेन तृप्तिर्भविष्यति ।। 7.78.18 ।।
explanation: Therefore, having nourished your own excellent body well with foods, and having consumed the nectar, you will achieve satisfaction thereby.

shloka_text: यदा तु तद्वनं श्वेत अगस्त्यः सुमहानृषिः । आगमिष्यति दुर्धर्षस्तदा कृच्छ्राद्विमोक्ष्यते ।। 7.78.19 ।।
explanation: However, O Śveta, when that formidable great sage Agastya will come to that forest, then you will be freed from distress.

shloka_text: स हि तारयितुं सौम्य शक्तः सुरगणानपि । किं पुनस्त्वां महाबाहो क्षुत्पिपासावशं गतम् ।। 7.78.20 ।।
explanation: Indeed, O gentle one, he is capable of saving even the hosts of gods; much less you, O mighty-armed one, who have fallen under the sway of hunger and thirst.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं भगवतः श्रुत्वा देवदेवस्य निश्चयम् । आहारं गर्हितं स्वशरीरं द्विजोत्तम ।। 7.78.21 ।।
explanation: So I, having heard the resolve of the God of gods, O best of the twice-born, considered my own body as reprehensible food.

shloka_text: बहून्वर्षगणान्ब्रह्मन्भुज्यमानमिदं मया । क्षयं नाभ्येति ब्रह्मर्षे तृप्तिश्चापि ममोत्तमा ।। 7.78.22 ।।
explanation: O Brahman, O Brahmarshi, this, though enjoyed by me for many years, does not diminish, and my satisfaction is also supreme.

shloka_text: तस्य मे कृच्छ्रभूतस्य कृच्छ्रादस्माद्विमोचय । अन्येषां न गतिर्ह्यत्र कुम्भयोनिमृते द्विजम् ।। 7.78.23 ।।
explanation: Release me, who has fallen into such distress, from this difficulty. For others, there is no recourse here, O Brahmana, except for the sage born from a pot.

shloka_text: इदमाभरणं सौम्य तारणार्थं द्विजोत्तम । प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भद्रं ते प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.78.24 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, O best among the twice-born, please accept this ornament for the purpose of deliverance. May good be to you. You ought to grant this favor.

shloka_text: इदं तावत्सुवर्णं च धनं वस्त्राणि च द्विज । भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च ब्रह्मर्षे ददात्याभरणानि च ।। 7.78.25 ।।
explanation: O Brahmana, O Brahmarshi, this (person/thing) gives, first of all, gold, wealth, clothes, food, drink, and ornaments.

shloka_text: सर्वान्कामान्प्रयच्छामि भोगांश्च मुनिपुङ्गव । तारणे भगवन्मह्यं प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.78.26 ।।
explanation: O best among sages, I grant all desires and enjoyments. O Lord, you ought to show favor to me for my deliverance.

shloka_text: तस्याहं स्वर्गिणो वाक्यं श्रुत्वा दुःखसमन्वितम् । तारणायोपजग्राह तदाभरणमुत्तमम् ।। 7.78.27 ।।
explanation: Having heard the sorrowful words of that departed one, I accepted that excellent ornament for his deliverance.

shloka_text: मया प्रतिगृहीते तु तस्मिन्नाभरणे शुभे । मानुषः पूर्वको देहो राजर्षेर्विननाश ह ।। 7.78.28 ।।
explanation: When that auspicious ornament was accepted by me, the former human body of the royal sage indeed perished.

shloka_text: प्रनष्टे तु शरीरे ऽसौ राजर्षिः परया मुदा । तृप्तः प्रमुदितो राजा जगाम त्रिदिवं सुखम् ।। 7.78.29 ।।
explanation: Upon the destruction of his body, that royal sage, the king, satisfied and greatly delighted, went to heaven with supreme joy and happiness.

shloka_text: तेनेदं शक्रतुल्येन दिव्यमाभरणं मम । तस्मिन्निमित्ते काकुत्स्थ दत्तमद्भुतदर्शनम् ।। 7.78.30 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, this divine ornament of mine, of wonderful appearance, was given by him, who is equal to Indra, on that occasion.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 78 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the seventy-eighth chapter.

shloka_text: तदद्भुततमं वाक्यं श्रुत्वागस्त्यस्य राघवः । गौरवाद्विस्मयाच्चैव पुनः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.79.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that most wonderful speech of Agastya, Rama, out of reverence and astonishment, began to ask again.

shloka_text: भगवंस्तद्वनं घोरं तपस्तप्यति यत्र सः । श्वेतो वैदर्भको राजा कथं स्यादमृगद्विजम् ।। 7.79.2 ।।
explanation: O Lord, how could that dreadful forest, where King Shveta of Vidarbha performs penance, be without deer and birds?

shloka_text: तद्वनं स कथ राजा शून्यं मनुजवर्जितम् । तपश्चर्तुं प्रविष्टः स श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ।। 7.79.3 ।।
explanation: How did that king enter that forest, empty and devoid of humans, to perform penance? I truly wish to hear that.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम् । वाक्यं परमतेजस्वी वक्तुमेवोपचक्रमे ।। 7.79.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, which were full of curiosity, the greatly effulgent one began to speak.

shloka_text: पुरा कृतयुगे राम मनुर्दण्डधरः प्रभुः । तस्य पुत्रो महानासीदिक्ष्वाकुः कुलनन्दनः ।। 7.79.5 ।।
explanation: O Rama, formerly, in the Krita Yuga, Manu was a powerful ruler. His great son was Ikshvaku, the delight of his family.

shloka_text: तं पुत्रं पूर्वंकं राज्ये निक्षिप्य भुवि दुर्जयम् । पृथिव्यां राजवंशानां भव कर्तेत्युवाच ह ।। 7.79.6 ।।
explanation: Having installed that unconquerable first-born son in the kingdom on earth, he said, "Be the founder of royal dynasties on earth."

shloka_text: तथैवेति प्रतिज्ञातं पितुः पुत्रेण राघव । ततः परमसन्तुष्टो मनुः पुत्रमुवाच ह ।। 7.79.7 ।।
explanation: "So be it," thus was promised by the son to the father, O Raghava. Then, exceedingly pleased, Manu spoke to his son.

shloka_text: प्रीतो ऽस्मि परमोदार त्वं कर्ता ऽसि न संशयः । दण्डेन च प्रजा रक्ष मा च दण्डमकारणे ।। 7.79.8 ।।
explanation: I am pleased, O most generous one. You are capable, there is no doubt. And protect the subjects with the rod of justice, but do not use the rod without cause.

shloka_text: अपराधिषु यो दण्डः पात्यते मानवेषु वै । स दण्डो विधिवन्मुक्तः स्वर्गं नयति पार्थिवम् ।। 7.79.9 ।।
explanation: The punishment which is inflicted upon offenders among men, that punishment, when duly administered, leads the king to heaven.

shloka_text: तस्माद्दण्डे महाबाहो यत्नवान्भव पुत्रक । धर्मो हि परमो लोके कुर्वतस्ते भविष्यति ।। 7.79.10 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O mighty-armed son, be diligent in matters of justice. For indeed, supreme righteousness will be yours in the world by doing so.

shloka_text: इति तं बहु सन्दिश्य मनुः पुत्रं समाधिना । जगाम त्रिदिवं हृष्टो ब्रह्मलोकं सनातनम् ।। 7.79.11 ।।
explanation: Thus, having extensively instructed his son with great composure, Manu, joyful, departed to heaven, the eternal world of Brahma.

shloka_text: प्रयाते त्रिदिवं तस्मिन्निक्ष्वाकुरमितप्रभः । जनयिष्ये कथं पुत्रानिति चिन्तापरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.79.12 ।।
explanation: When he had departed to heaven, Ikshvaku, of immeasurable splendor, became absorbed in the thought, 'How shall I beget sons?'

shloka_text: कर्मभिर्बहुरूपैश्च तैस्तैर्मनुसुतस्सुतान् । जनयामास धर्मात्मा शतं देवसुतोपमान् ।। 7.79.13 ।।
explanation: The righteous-souled son of Manu, through various kinds of deeds, begot a hundred sons who resembled sons of gods.

shloka_text: तेषामवरजस्तात सर्वेषां रघुनन्दन । मूढश्चाकृतविद्यश्च न शुश्रूषति पूर्वजान् ।। 7.79.14 ।।
explanation: O dear one, O Raghunandana, the youngest among all of them, who is foolish and uneducated, does not serve his elders.

shloka_text: नाम तस्य च दण्डेति पिता चक्रे ऽल्पमेधसः । अवश्यं दण्डपतनं शरीरे ऽस्य भविष्यति ।। 7.79.15 ।।
explanation: His father named that dull-witted one Daṇḍa. Punishment will certainly befall his body.

shloka_text: अपश्यमानस्तं देशं घोरं पुत्रस्य राघव । विन्ध्यशैवलयोर्मध्ये राज्यं प्रादादरिन्दम ।। 7.79.16 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, O subduer of enemies, not finding that dreadful region for his son, he gave the kingdom in the middle of Vindhya and Śaivala.

shloka_text: स दण्डस्तत्र राजाभूद्रम्ये पर्वतरोधसि । पुरं चाप्रतिमं राम न्यवेशयदनुत्तमम् ।। 7.79.17 ।।
explanation: There, on the beautiful mountain slope, Daṇḍa became king. And, O Rama, he established an unequalled, unsurpassed city.

shloka_text: पुरस्य चाकरोन्नाम मधुमन्तमिति प्रभो । पुरोहितं तूशनसं वरयामास सुव्रतम् ।। 7.79.18 ।।
explanation: And he named the city Madhumanta, O Lord. And he chose Ushanas, the virtuous, as the priest.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा तद्राज्यमकरोत्सपुरोहितः । प्रहृष्टमनुजाकीर्णं देवराजं यथा वृषा ।। 7.79.19 ।।
explanation: Thus, that king, accompanied by his priest, ruled that kingdom, which was filled with joyful people, just as Vṛṣa (Indra) rules the kingdom of the gods.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रः सार्धं च तेनोशनसा तदानीम् । चकार राज्यं सुमहान्महात्मा शक्रो दिवीवोशनसा समेतः ।। 7.79.20 ।।
explanation: Then that very great, great-souled king, the son of the lord of men, at that time ruled the kingdom together with Ushanas, just as Indra in heaven rules accompanied by Ushanas.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 79 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (composed by a Rishi), the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the seventy-ninth chapter.

shloka_text: एतदाख्याय रामाय महर्षिः कुम्भसम्भवः । अस्यामेवापरं वाक्यं कथायामुपचक्रमे ।। 7.80.1 ।।
explanation: Having narrated this to Rama, the great sage Agastya then commenced another statement in this very narrative.

shloka_text: ततः स दण्डः काकुत्स्थ बहुवर्षगणायुतम् । अकरोत्तत्र दान्तात्मा राज्यं निहतकण्टकम् ।। 7.80.2 ।।
explanation: Then, O Kakutstha, that self-controlled Daṇḍa ruled there a kingdom free from enemies for many tens of thousands of years.

shloka_text: अथ काले तु कस्मिंश्चिद्राजा भार्गवमाश्रमम् । रमणीयमुपाक्रामच्चैत्रे मासि मनोरमे ।। 7.80.3 ।।
explanation: Then, at a certain time, the king approached the beautiful hermitage of Bhargava in the delightful month of Chaitra.

shloka_text: तत्र भार्गवकन्यां स रूपेणाप्रतिमां भुवि । विचरन्तीं वनोद्देशे दण्डो ऽपश्यदनुत्तमाम् ।। 7.80.4 ।।
explanation: There, Daṇḍa saw the daughter of Bhargava, unrivaled in beauty on earth, wandering in the forest region, a most excellent woman.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा तां सुदुर्मेधा अनङ्गशरपीडितः । अभिगम्य सुसंविग्नां कन्यां वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.80.5 ।।
explanation: Having seen her, he, being of very foolish mind and tormented by the arrows of Ananga, approached the very agitated girl and spoke words.

shloka_text: कुतस्त्वमसि सुश्रोणि कस्य वा ऽसि सुता शुभे । पीडितो ऽहमनङ्गेन गच्छामि त्वां शुभानने ।। 7.80.6 ।।
explanation: From where are you, O beautiful-hipped one? Or whose daughter are you, O auspicious one? I am tormented by Ananga (the god of love), and I approach you, O beautiful-faced one.

shloka_text: तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य मोहोन्मत्तस्य कामिनः । भार्गवी प्रत्युवाचेदं वचः सानुनयं नृपम् ।। 7.80.7 ।।
explanation: To him, who was thus speaking, maddened by delusion and desire, Bhargavi respectfully spoke these words to the king.

shloka_text: भार्गवस्य सुतां विद्धि देवस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । अरजां नाम राजेन्द्र ज्येष्ठामाश्रमवासिनीम् ।। 7.80.8 ।।
explanation: O best of kings, know her to be Arajā, the eldest daughter of Bhargava, the god of untiring deeds, who dwells in the hermitage.

shloka_text: मा मां स्पृश बलाद्राजन्कन्या पितृवशा ह्यहम् । गुरुः पिता मे राजेन्द्र त्वं च शिष्यो महात्मनः । व्यसनं सुमहत्क्रुद्धः स ते दद्यान्महातपाः ।। 7.80.9 ।।
explanation: Do not touch me by force, O King, for I am a maiden under my father's control. My father is a teacher, O great King, and you are a disciple of that great soul. Enraged, that great ascetic would inflict a very great calamity upon you.

shloka_text: यदि वान्यन्मया कार्यं धर्मदृष्टेन सत्पथा । वरयस्व नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं मे महाद्युतिम् ।। 7.80.10 ।।
explanation: O best among men, if anything else is to be done by me according to the righteous and good path, then ask my greatly effulgent father.

shloka_text: अन्यथा तु फलं तुभ्यं भवेद्घोराभिसंहितम् । क्रोधेन हि पिता मे ऽसौ त्रैलोक्यमपि निर्दहेत् ।। 7.80.11 ।।
explanation: Otherwise, the consequence for you will be terribly dire. For, this father of mine, by his anger, could burn down even the three worlds.

shloka_text: दास्यते चानवद्याङ्ग तव मा याचितः पिता ।। 7.80.12 ।।
explanation: And, O blameless-limbed one, your father, when requested, will give me to you.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणामरजां दण्डः कामवशं गतः । प्रत्युवाच मदोन्मत्तः शिरस्याधाय चाञ्जलिम् ।। 7.80.13 ।।
explanation: To Arajā, who was speaking thus, Daṇḍa, having fallen under the sway of desire, replied, intoxicated with passion, and placing his folded hands on his head.

shloka_text: प्रसादं कुरु सुश्रोणि न कालं क्षेप्तुमर्हसि । त्वत्कृते हि मम प्राणा विदीर्यन्ते वरानने ।। 7.80.14 ।।
explanation: O beautiful-hipped one, be gracious; you should not delay. Indeed, for your sake, O beautiful-faced one, my life is breaking apart.

shloka_text: त्वां प्राप्य मे वधो वा स्याच्छापो वा यदि दारुणः । भक्तं भजस्व मां भीरु भजमानं सुविह्वलम् ।। 7.80.15 ।।
explanation: If, upon obtaining you, my death or a terrible curse were to befall me, O timid one, accept me, your devotee, who is serving you and is greatly distressed.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तु तां कन्यां दोर्भ्यां गृह्य बलाद्बली । विस्फुरन्तीं यथाकामं मैथुनायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.80.16 ।।
explanation: Having said thus, the strong one, seizing that maiden with his arms by force, began intercourse as he desired, while she was struggling.

shloka_text: एतमर्थं महाघोरं दण्डः कृत्वा सुदारुणम् । नगरं प्रययावाशु मधुमन्तमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.80.17 ।।
explanation: Having committed this very terrible and extremely cruel act, Daṇḍa quickly went to the excellent city of Madhumanta.

shloka_text: अरजा ऽपि रुदन्ती सा आश्रमस्याविदूरतः । प्रतीक्षन्ति सुसंत्रस्ता पितरं देवसन्निभम् ।। 7.80.18 ।।
explanation: Arajā, though weeping and greatly terrified, waited not far from the hermitage for her god-like father.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 80 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred, glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the eightieth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: स मुहूर्तादुपश्रुत्य देवर्षिरमितप्रभः । स्वमाश्रमं शिष्यवृतः क्षुधार्तः सन्न्यवर्तत ।। 7.81.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard within a moment, that divine sage of immeasurable splendor, afflicted by hunger and surrounded by disciples, returned to his own hermitage.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यदरजां दीनां रजसा समभिप्लुताम् । ज्योत्स्नामिव ग्रहग्रस्तां प्रत्यूषे न विराजतीम् ।। 7.81.2 ।।
explanation: He saw her, spotless but distressed, completely covered with dust, like moonlight eclipsed by a planet, not shining at dawn.

shloka_text: तस्य रोषः समभवत्क्षुधार्तस्य विशेषतः । निर्दहन्निव लोकांस्त्रीञ्छिष्यांश्चैतदुवाच ह ।। 7.81.3 ।।
explanation: His anger arose, especially as he was afflicted by hunger. As if burning the three worlds, he spoke this to his disciples.

shloka_text: पश्यध्वं विपरीतस्य दण्डस्याविजितात्मनः । विपत्तिं घोरसङ्काशां क्रुद्धामग्निशिखामिव ।। 7.81.4 ।।
explanation: Behold the dreadful calamity, like an enraged flame of fire, of the perverse and uncontrolled ruler.

shloka_text: क्षयो ऽस्य दुर्मतेः प्राप्तः सानुगस्य दुरात्मनः । यः प्रदीप्तां हुताशस्य शिखां वै स्प्रष्टुमिच्छति ।। 7.81.5 ।।
explanation: The destruction of this wicked-souled, evil-minded one, along with his followers, has come, who indeed desires to touch the blazing flame of fire.

shloka_text: यस्मात्स कृतवान्पापमीदृशं घोरसंहितम् । तस्मात्प्राप्स्यति दुर्मेधाः फलं पापस्य कर्मणः ।। 7.81.6 ।।
explanation: Since he has committed such a dreadful sin, therefore that foolish one will obtain the fruit of his evil deed.

shloka_text: सप्तरात्रेण राजासौ सभृत्यबलवाहनः । पापकर्मसमाचारो वधं प्राप्स्यति दुर्मतिः ।। 7.81.7 ।।
explanation: That evil-minded king, who practices sinful deeds, along with his servants, army, and conveyances, will meet his death within seven nights.

shloka_text: समन्ताद्योजनशतं विषयं चास्य दुर्मतेः । धक्ष्यते पांसुवर्षेण महता पाकशासनः ।। 7.81.8 ।।
explanation: Paka-shasana will consume the territory of this evil-minded one, for a hundred yojanas all around, with a great shower of dust.

shloka_text: सर्वसत्वानि यानीह स्थावराणि चराणि च । महता पांसुवर्षेण विलयं सर्वतो ऽगमन् ।। 7.81.9 ।।
explanation: All beings here, both stationary and mobile, met their destruction everywhere due to a great rain of dust.

shloka_text: दण्डस्य विषयो यावत्तावत्सर्वसमुच्छ्रयम् । पांसुवर्षमिवालक्ष्यं सप्तरात्रं भविष्यति ।। 7.81.10 ।।
explanation: As far as the territory of Danda extends, throughout its entire extent, there will be an imperceptible shower of dust for seven nights.

shloka_text: इत्युक्त्वा क्रोधताम्राक्षस्तदाश्रमनिवासिनम् । जनं जनपदान्तेषु स्थीयतामिति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.81.11 ।।
explanation: Having said this, he, with eyes red with anger, told the people residing in that hermitage, "Stay at the borders of the country."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तूशनसो वाक्यं सो ऽ ऽश्रमावसथो जनः । निष्क्रान्तो विषयात्तस्मात्स्थानं चक्रे ऽथ बाह्यतः ।। 7.81.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of Uśanas, those people dwelling in the hermitage departed from that region and then made their abode outside.

shloka_text: स तथोक्त्वा मुनिजनमरजामिदमब्रवीत् । इहैव वस दुर्मेधे आश्रमे सुसमाहिता ।। 7.81.13 ।।
explanation: He, having thus spoken to the sages, said this to Arajā: "O foolish one, stay right here in the hermitage, being well-composed."

shloka_text: इदं योजनपर्यन्तं सरः सुरुचिरप्रभम् । अरजे विज्वरा भुङ्क्ष्व कालश्चात्र प्रतीक्ष्यताम् ।। 7.81.14 ।।
explanation: O sinless one, free from distress, enjoy this lake, which extends for a yojana and possesses a very beautiful splendor. And let time be awaited here.

shloka_text: त्वत्समीपे च ये सत्त्वा वासमेष्यन्ति तां निशाम् । अवध्याः पांसुवर्षेण ते भविष्यन्ति नित्यदा ।। 7.81.15 ।।
explanation: And those beings who will dwell near you for that night, they shall always be invulnerable to the shower of dust.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा नियोगं ब्रह्मर्षेः सा ऽरजा भार्गवी तदा । तथेति पितरं प्राह भार्गवं भृशदुःखिता । इत्युक्त्वा भार्गवो वासमन्यत्र समकारयत् ।। 7.81.16 ।।
explanation: Having heard the Brahmarshi's command, Arajā, the daughter of Bhṛgu, then, greatly distressed, said "So be it" to her father, Bhārgava. Having said this, Bhārgava made his dwelling elsewhere.

shloka_text: तच्च राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य सभृत्यबलवाहनम् । सप्ताहाद्भस्मसाद्भूतं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ।। 7.81.17 ।।
explanation: That kingdom of the king, along with its servants, army, and conveyances, was reduced to ashes within seven days, just as it was declared by the knower of Brahman.

shloka_text: तस्यासौ दण्डविषयो विन्ध्यशैवलयोर्नृप । शप्तो ब्रह्मर्षिणा तेन वैधर्म्ये सहिते कृते ।। 7.81.18 ।।
explanation: O king, that region of his, subject to punishment, between Vindhya and Śaivala, was cursed by that Brahmarshi when unrighteousness was committed.

shloka_text: ततः प्रभृति काकुत्स्थ दण्डकारण्यमुच्यते । तपस्विनः स्थिता ह्यत्र जनस्थानमतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.81.19 ।।
explanation: From then onwards, O Kakutstha, it is called Dandakaranya. Indeed, ascetics resided here, hence it became Janasthana.

shloka_text: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव । सन्ध्यामुपासितुं वीर समयो ह्यतिवर्तते ।। 7.81.20 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, all this that you asked me has been narrated to you. O hero, the time for performing the Sandhya prayer is indeed passing.

shloka_text: एते महर्षयः सर्वे पूर्णकुम्भाः समन्ततः । कृतोदका नरव्याघ्र आदित्यं पर्युपासते ।। 7.81.21 ।।
explanation: O tiger among men, all these great sages, with full water-pots all around, having offered water libations, are worshipping the Sun.

shloka_text: स तैर्ब्राह्मणमभ्यस्तं सहितैर्ब्रह्मवित्तमैः । रविरस्तं गतो राम गच्छोदकमुपस्पृश ।। 7.81.22 ।।
explanation: He, by those Brahmins who had mastered the Veda, accompanied by the best knowers of Brahman. The sun has set, Rama, go and perform your ablutions.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 81 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the eighty-first chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: ऋषेर्वचनमाज्ञाय रामः सन्ध्यामुपासितुम् । उपाक्रमत्सरः पुण्यमप्सरोगणसेवितम् ।। 7.82.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard the sage's words, Rama began to perform his twilight prayers at the sacred lake, frequented by groups of Apsaras.

shloka_text: तत्रोदकमुपस्पृश्य सन्ध्यामन्वास्य पश्चिमाम् । आश्रमं प्राविशद्रामः कुम्भयोनेर्महात्मनः ।। 7.82.2 ।।
explanation: Having performed ablution there and observed the evening twilight worship, Rama entered the hermitage of the great-souled Kumbhayoni.

shloka_text: तस्यागस्त्यो बहुगुणं कन्दमूलं तथौषधिम् । शाल्यादीनि पवित्राणि भोजनार्थमकल्पयत् ।। 7.82.3 ।।
explanation: Agastya prepared for him roots and tubers of many qualities, as well as herbs, and pure rice and other grains for food.

shloka_text: स भुक्तवान्नरश्रेष्ठस्तदन्नममृतोपमम् । प्रीतश्च परितुष्टश्च तां रात्रिं समुपाविशत् ।। 7.82.4 ।।
explanation: The best among men ate that nectar-like food. Pleased and greatly satisfied, he passed that night.

shloka_text: प्रभाते काल्यमुत्थाय कृत्वा ऽ ऽह्निकमरिन्दमः । ऋषिं समुपचक्राम गमनाय रघूत्तमः ।। 7.82.5 ।।
explanation: Having risen early in the morning and performed his daily rituals, the best of the Raghus, the subduer of enemies, approached the sage for departure.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्याब्रवीद्रामो महर्षिं कुम्भसम्भवम् । आपृच्छे स्वां पुरीं गन्तुं मामनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.82.6 ।।
explanation: Having saluted, Rama said to the great sage Agastya, "I seek permission to go to my city; you should allow me."

shloka_text: धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि दर्शनेन महात्मनः । द्रष्टुं चैवागमिष्यामि पावनार्थमिहात्मनः ।। 7.82.7 ।।
explanation: I am blessed, I am graced by the sight of the great soul. I shall certainly come here to see for the purification of my self.

shloka_text: तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् । उवाच परमप्रीतो धर्मनेत्रस्तपोधनः ।। 7.82.8 ।।
explanation: Thus, when Kakutstha spoke words of wondrous sight, the ascetic, whose eye was dharma, spoke, greatly pleased.

shloka_text: अत्यद्भुतमिदं वाक्यं तव राम शुभाक्षरम् । पावनः सर्वभूतानां त्वमेव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.82.9 ।।
explanation: O Rama, this exceedingly wonderful speech of yours, with its auspicious words. O Raghunandana, you alone are the purifier of all beings.

shloka_text: मुहूर्तमपि राम त्वां ये च पश्यन्ति केचन । पाविताः स्वर्गभूताश्च पूज्यास्ते सर्वदैवतैः ।। 7.82.10 ।।
explanation: O Rama, those who see you even for a moment become purified and attain the state of celestial beings, and are revered by all deities.

shloka_text: ये च त्वां घोरचक्षुर्भिः पश्यन्ति प्राणिनो भुवि । हतास्ते यमदण्डेन सद्यो निरयगामिनः ।। 7.82.11 ।।
explanation: And those living beings on earth who look at you with terrible eyes, they are immediately struck by Yama's rod and go to hell.

shloka_text: ईदृशस्त्वं रघुश्रेष्ठ पावनः सर्वदेहिनाम् । भुवि त्वां कथयन्तो ऽपि सिद्धिमेष्यन्ति राघव ।। 7.82.12 ।।
explanation: O best of the Raghus, you are such a purifier of all embodied beings. O Raghava, even those who speak of you on earth will attain perfection.

shloka_text: गच्छ चारिष्टमव्याग्रः पन्थानमकुतोभयम् । प्रशाधि राज्यं धर्मेण गतिर्हि जगतो भवान् ।। 7.82.13 ।।
explanation: Go, undisturbed and safe, on a fearless path. Rule the kingdom righteously, for you are indeed the refuge of the world.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना प्राञ्जलिः प्रग्रहो नृपः । अभ्यवादयत प्राज्ञस्तमृषिं पुण्यशालिनम् ।। 7.82.14 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the sage, the wise king, with folded hands and humility, saluted that meritorious sage.

shloka_text: अभिवाद्य मुनिश्रेष्ठं तांश्च सर्वांस्तपोधनान् । अध्यारोहत्तदव्यग्रः पुष्पकं हेमभूषितम् ।। 7.82.15 ।।
explanation: Having saluted the foremost sage and all those ascetics, he then, without agitation, ascended the gold-adorned Pushpaka.

shloka_text: तं प्रयान्तं मुनिगणा ह्याशीर्वादैः समन्ततः । अपूजयन्महेन्द्राभं सहस्राक्षमिवामराः ।। 7.82.16 ।।
explanation: As he departed, the groups of sages, indeed, honored him from all sides with blessings, just as the gods worship the thousand-eyed Indra, who was like Mahendra.

shloka_text: स्वस्थः स ददृशे रामः पुष्पके हेमभूषिते । शशी मेघसमीपस्थो यथा जलधरागमे ।। 7.82.17 ।।
explanation: Rama, at ease, was seen in the gold-adorned Pushpaka, just as the moon appears near the clouds at the advent of the rainy season.

shloka_text: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते पूज्यमानस्ततस्ततः । अयोध्यां प्राप्य काकुत्स्थो मध्यकक्ष्यामवारुहत् ।। 7.82.18 ।।
explanation: Then, when midday arrived, Kakutstha, being honored from all sides, having reached Ayodhya, dismounted in the middle courtyard.

shloka_text: ततो विसृज्य रुचिरं पुष्पकं कामगामि तत् । विसर्जयित्वा गच्छेति स्वस्ति ते ऽस्त्विति च प्रभुः ।। 7.82.19 ।।
explanation: Then, the lord, having dismissed that beautiful Pushpaka, which moves at will, sent it off saying, "Go! And may there be welfare for you."

shloka_text: कक्षान्तरविनिक्षिप्तं द्वास्स्थं रामो ऽब्रवीद्वचः । लक्ष्मणं भरतं चैव गत्वा तौ लघुविक्रमौ ।। ममागमनमाख्याय शब्दापयत मा चिरम् ।। 7.82.20 ।।
explanation: Rama spoke these words to the doorkeeper stationed within the chamber: "Go and announce my arrival to Lakshmana and Bharata, those swift-footed ones, and summon them without delay."

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे व्द्यशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 82 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the eighty-second chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य रामस्याक्लिष्ट कर्मणः । द्वास्स्थः कुमारावाहूय राघवाय न्यवेदयत् ।। 7.83.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of Rama, the one of unwearied deeds, the doorkeeper, having called the two princes, announced them to Raghava.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः प्राप्तौ प्रियौ भरतलक्ष्मणौ । परिष्वज्य तदा रामो वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.83.2 ।।
explanation: Having seen his beloved Bharata and Lakshmana arrive, Rama then embraced them and spoke these words.

shloka_text: कृतं मया यथा तथ्यं द्विजकार्यमनुत्तमम् । धर्मसेतुमथो भूयः कर्तुमिच्छामि राघवौ ।। 7.83.3 ।।
explanation: I have truthfully performed the unsurpassed duty of a Brahmin. And now, O Raghavas, I wish to further establish the bridge of righteousness.

shloka_text: अक्षय्यश्चाव्ययश्चैव धर्मसेतुर्मतो मम । धर्मप्रसाधकं ह्येतत् सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ।। 7.83.4 ।।
explanation: It is imperishable and immutable, and is considered by me as the bridge of righteousness. For this indeed promotes righteousness and destroys all sins.

shloka_text: युवाभ्यामात्मभूताभ्यां राजसूयमनुत्तमम् । सहितो यष्टुमिच्छामि तत्र धर्मो हि शाश्वतः ।। 7.83.5 ।।
explanation: I wish to perform the unsurpassed Rajasuya sacrifice, accompanied by both of you, who are my very self. For eternal righteousness indeed lies therein.

shloka_text: इष्ट्वा तु राजसूयेन मित्रः शत्रुनिबर्हणः । सुहुतेन सुयज्ञेन वरुणत्वमुपागमत् ।। 7.83.6 ।।
explanation: Having performed the Rajasuya sacrifice, Mitra, the destroyer of enemies, through well-offered oblations and a well-conducted sacrifice, attained the state of Varuna.

shloka_text: सोमश्च राजसूयेन इष्ट्वा धर्मेण धर्मवित् । प्राप्तश्च सर्वलोकेषु कीर्तिस्थानं च शाश्वतम् ।। 7.83.7 ।।
explanation: Soma, the knower of dharma, having righteously performed the Rājasūya sacrifice, obtained an eternal place of fame in all worlds.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्नहनि यच्छ्रेयश्चिन्त्यतां तन्मया सह । हितं चायतियुक्तं च प्रयतौ कर्तुमर्हथः ।। 7.83.8 ।।
explanation: Whatever is beneficial on this day, let it be considered with me. And you two should strive to do what is beneficial and conducive to the future.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवस्यैतद्वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः । भरतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.83.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard these words of Raghava, Bharata, an expert in speech, joined his palms and spoke these words.

shloka_text: त्वयि धर्मः परः साधो त्वयि सर्वा वसुन्धरा । प्रतिष्ठिता महाबाहो यशश्चामितविक्रम ।। 7.83.10 ।।
explanation: O virtuous one, supreme righteousness is in you. O mighty-armed one, the entire earth is established in you, and O one of immeasurable valor, so is fame.

shloka_text: महीपालाश्च सर्वे त्वां प्रजापतिमिवामराः । निरीक्षन्ते महात्मानं लोकानाथं यथा वयम् ।। 7.83.11 ।।
explanation: All the kings look upon you, the great-souled one, the lord of the worlds, just as the gods look upon Prajapati, and just as we do.

shloka_text: पुत्राश्च पितृवद्राजन्पश्यन्ति त्वां महाबल । पृथिव्या गतिभूतो ऽसि प्राणिनामपि राघव ।। 7.83.12 ।।
explanation: O King, O mighty-armed one, your sons see you like a father. You are the refuge of the earth and also of all living beings, O Raghava.

shloka_text: स त्वमेवंविधं यज्ञमाहर्तासि कथं नृप । पृथिव्यां राजवंशानां विनाशो यत्र दृश्यते ।। 7.83.13 ।।
explanation: O King, how will you, being such, perform such a sacrifice, in which the destruction of royal dynasties on earth is seen?

shloka_text: पृथिव्यां ये च पुरुषा राजन्पौरुषमागताः । सर्वेषां भविता तत्र सङ्क्षयः सर्वकोपजः ।। 7.83.14 ।।
explanation: O King, all those men on earth who have attained valor, for all of them there will be destruction born of universal wrath.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल गुणैरतुलविक्रम । पृथिवीं नार्हसे हन्तुं वशे हि तव वर्तते ।। 7.83.15 ।।
explanation: You, O tiger among men, endowed with virtues and unequalled valor, ought not to oppress the earth, for it is indeed under your control.

shloka_text: भरतस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा ऽमृतमयं तदा । प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे रामः सत्यपराक्रमः ।। 7.83.16 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard that nectar-like speech of Bharata, Rama, of true valor, obtained immeasurable joy.

shloka_text: उवाच च शुभं वाक्यं कैकेय्यानन्दवर्धनम् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि परितुष्टो ऽस्मि तवाद्य वचने ऽनघ ।। 7.83.17 ।।
explanation: And he spoke an auspicious word, enhancing Kaikeyi's joy: "O sinless one, I am pleased and completely satisfied by your statement today."

shloka_text: इदं वचनमक्लीबं त्वया धर्मसमाहितम् । व्याहृतं पुरुषव्याघ्र पृथिव्याः परिपालनम् ।। 7.83.18 ।।
explanation: This resolute and righteous statement concerning the protection of the earth has been uttered by you, O tiger among men.

shloka_text: एष्यदस्मदभिप्रायाद्राजसूयात्क्रतूत्तमात् । निवर्तयामि धर्मज्ञ तव सुव्याहृतेन च ।। 7.83.19 ।।
explanation: O knower of Dharma, I will desist from the impending Rajasuya, the best of sacrifices, which was our intention, and (I will do so) by your excellent words.

shloka_text: लोकपीडाकरं कर्म न कर्तव्यं विचक्षणैः । बालानां तु शुभं वाक्यं ग्राह्य लक्ष्मणपूर्वज । तस्माच्छृणोमि ते वाक्यं साधु युक्तं महामते ।। 7.83.20 ।।
explanation: Actions that cause distress to people should not be done by the wise. But good advice from children should be accepted, O elder brother of Lakshmana. Therefore, I listen to your words, which are proper and reasonable, O great-minded one.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्र्यशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 83 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the eighty-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरते च महात्मनि । लक्ष्मणो ऽथ शुभं वाक्यमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.84.1 ।।
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, and the great-souled Bharata (was also present), then Lakshmana spoke auspicious words to Raghunandana.

shloka_text: अश्वमेधो महायज्ञः पावनः सर्वपाप्मनाम् । पावनस्तव दुर्धर्षो रोचतां रघुनन्दन ।। 7.84.2 ।।
explanation: The Ashvamedha is a great sacrifice, a purifier of all sins. May this unconquerable purifier be pleasing to you, O Raghunandana.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि पुरावृत्तं वासवे सुमहात्मनि । ब्रह्महत्यावृतः शक्रो हयमेधेन पावितः ।। 7.84.3 ।।
explanation: Indeed, an ancient story is heard about the great-souled Vasava (Indra). Shakra, afflicted by the sin of Brahman-slaughter, was purified by a horse sacrifice.

shloka_text: पुरा किल महाबाहो देवासुरसमागमे । वृत्रो नाम महानासीद्दैतेयो लोकसम्मतः ।। 7.84.4 ।।
explanation: Formerly, it is said, O mighty-armed one, in the great battle between the Devas and Asuras, there was a powerful Daitya named Vritra, who was respected by the world.

shloka_text: विस्तीर्णो योजनशतमुच्छ्रितस्त्रिगुणं ततः । अनुरागेण लोकांस्त्रीन्स्नेहात्पश्यति सर्वतः ।। 7.84.5 ।।
explanation: It is a hundred yojanas wide and three times that in height. He beholds the three worlds everywhere with affection and love.

shloka_text: धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठितः । शशास पृथिवीं स्फीतां धर्मेण सुसमाहितः ।। 7.84.6 ।।
explanation: Knowledgeable in dharma, grateful, and perfected by intellect, he ruled the prosperous earth righteously with great composure.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रशासति तदा सर्वकामदुघा मही । रसवन्ति प्रभूनानि मूलानि च फलानि च ।। 7.84.7 ।।
explanation: While he was ruling then, the earth yielded all desires, and roots and fruits were juicy and abundant.

shloka_text: अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी सुसम्पन्ना महात्मनः । स राज्यं तादृशं भुङ्क्ते स्फीतमद्भुतदर्शनम् ।। 7.84.8 ।।
explanation: For the great-souled one, the earth yields without cultivation and is very prosperous. He enjoys such a kingdom, flourishing and marvelous to behold.

shloka_text: तस्य बुद्धिः समुप्तन्ना तपः कुर्यामनुत्तमम् । तपो हि परमं श्रेयः सम्मोहमितरत्सुखम् ।। 7.84.9 ।।
explanation: A thought arose in him: 'I should perform unsurpassed penance. For penance is indeed the supreme good; other happiness is mere delusion.'

shloka_text: स निक्षिप्य सुतं ज्येष्ठं पौरेषु मधुरेश्वरम् । तप उग्रं समातिष्ठत्तापयन्सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.84.10 ।।
explanation: Having entrusted his eldest son to the citizens as the lord of Madhura, he undertook severe penance, tormenting all the deities.

shloka_text: तपस्तप्यति वृत्रे तु वासवः परमार्तवत् । विष्णुं समुपसङ्क्रम्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.84.11 ।।
explanation: When Vritra was performing penance, Indra, extremely distressed, approached Vishnu and spoke these words.

shloka_text: तपस्यता महाबाहो लोकाः वृत्रेण निर्जिताः । बलवान्स हि धर्मात्मा नैनं शक्ष्यामि शासितुम् ।। 7.84.12 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, the worlds have been conquered by Vritra through his penance. He is indeed powerful and righteous-souled; I shall not be able to control him.

shloka_text: यद्यसौ तप आतिष्ठेद्भूय एवासुरेश्वर । यावल्लोका धरिष्यन्ति तावदस्य वशानुगाः ।। 7.84.13 ।।
explanation: If he performs penance again, O lord of Asuras, for as long as the worlds endure, they will remain subservient to him.

shloka_text: तं चैनं परमोदारमुपेक्षसि महाबलम् । क्षणं हि न भवेद्वृत्रः क्रुद्धे त्वयि सुरेश्वर ।। 7.84.14 ।।
explanation: And you neglect this exceedingly noble and mighty one. Indeed, Vritra would not exist for a moment if you were angered, O Lord of gods.

shloka_text: यदा हि प्रीतिसंयोगं त्वया विष्णो समागतः । तदाप्रभृति लोकानां नाथत्वमुपलब्धवान् ।। 7.84.15 ।।
explanation: When indeed I attained a loving union with you, O Vishnu, from that time onwards, I obtained the lordship of the worlds.

shloka_text: स त्वं प्रसादं लोकानां कुरुष्व सुसमाहितः । त्वत्कृतेन हि सर्वं स्याप्रशान्तमरुजं जगत् ।। 7.84.16 ।।
explanation: Therefore, you, being well-composed, bestow your grace upon the people. For by your actions, the entire world will indeed become peaceful and free from suffering.

shloka_text: इमे हि सर्वे विष्णो त्वां निरीक्षन्ते दिवौकसः । वृत्रघातेन महता तेषां साह्यं कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.84.17 ।।
explanation: Indeed, all these gods, O Vishnu, are looking to you. Do help them by the great slaying of Vritra.

shloka_text: त्वया हि नित्यशः साह्यं कृतमेषां महात्मनाम् । असह्यमिदमन्येषामगतीनां गतिर्भवान् ।। 7.84.18 ।।
explanation: Indeed, you have always rendered help to these great souls. This is unbearable for others; you are the refuge of the helpless.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 84 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (composed by a Rishi), the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the eighty-fourth chapter.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा शत्रुनिबर्हणः । वृत्रघातमशेषेण कथयेत्याह सुव्रत ।। 7.85.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemies said, "O virtuous one, narrate the slaying of Vritra completely."

shloka_text: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः । भूय एव कथां दिव्यां कथयामास सुव्रतः ।। 7.85.2 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Raghava, Lakshmana, the virtuous one who enhances Sumitra's joy, narrated the divine story once more.

shloka_text: सहस्राक्षवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम् । विष्णुर्देवानुवाचेदं सर्वानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् ।। 7.85.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed (Indra) and of all the gods, Vishnu spoke this to all the gods, led by Indra.

shloka_text: पूर्वं सौहृदबद्धो ऽस्मि वृत्रस्य ह महात्मनः । तेन युष्मत्प्रियार्थं हि नाहं हन्मि महासुरम् ।। 7.85.4 ।।
explanation: Formerly, I was indeed bound by friendship with the great-souled Vritra. Therefore, for your sake, I certainly do not kill the great Asura.

shloka_text: अवश्यं करणीयं च भवतां सुखमुत्तमम् । तस्मादुपायमाख्यास्ये येन वृत्रो निहन्यते ।। 7.85.5 ।।
explanation: And your supreme happiness must certainly be achieved. Therefore, I shall declare the means by which Vritra is slain.

shloka_text: त्रिधाभूतं करिष्यामि ह्यात्मानं सुरसत्तमाः । तेन वृत्रं सहस्राक्षो वधिष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.85.6 ।।
explanation: O best among gods, I will indeed make myself threefold. By that, the thousand-eyed one will kill Vritra, without a doubt.

shloka_text: एकांशो वासवं यातु द्वितीयो वज्रमेव तु । तृतीयो भूतलं शक्रस्तदा वृत्रं वधिष्यति ।। 7.85.7 ।।
explanation: Let one part go to Vasava, the second to the thunderbolt itself. The third to the earth. Then Shakra will slay Vritra.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति देवेशे देवा वाक्यमथाब्रुवन् । एवमेतन्न सन्देहो यथा वदसि दैत्यहन् ।। 7.85.8 ।।
explanation: When the lord of gods spoke thus, the gods then said: "This is indeed so, there is no doubt, just as you say, O slayer of demons."

shloka_text: भद्रं ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामो वृत्रासुरवधैषिणः । भजस्व परमोदार वासवं स्वेन तेजसा ।। 7.85.9 ।।
explanation: May you be well. We shall go, seeking the death of Vritrasura. Resort to the most generous Vasava with your own power.

shloka_text: ततः सर्वे महात्मानः सहस्राक्षपुरोगमाः । तदारण्यमुपाक्रामन्यत्र वृत्रो महासुरः ।। 7.85.10 ।।
explanation: Then all the great souls, led by Sahasraksha, approached that forest where the great demon Vritra was.

shloka_text: ते पश्यंस्तेजसा भूतं तप्यन्तमसुरोत्तमम् । पिबन्तमिव लोकांस्त्रीन्निर्दहन्तमिवाम्बरम् ।। 7.85.11 ।।
explanation: They saw the chief of the Asuras, endowed with splendor and intensely burning, as if drinking up the three worlds and consuming the sky.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वैव चासुरश्रेष्ठं देवास्त्रासमुपागमन् । कथमेनं वधिष्यामः कथं न स्यात्पराजयः ।। 7.85.12 ।।
explanation: And just by seeing the chief of the Asuras, the gods were overcome with fear. How shall we kill him? How can there be no defeat?

shloka_text: तेषां चिन्तयतां तत्र सहस्राक्षः पुरन्दरः । वज्रं प्रगृह्य पाणिभ्यां प्राहिणोद्वृत्रमूर्धनि ।। 7.85.13 ।।
explanation: While they were contemplating there, the thousand-eyed Purandara, grasping the thunderbolt with both hands, hurled it upon Vritra's head.

shloka_text: कालाग्निनेव घोरेण तप्तेनैव महार्चिषा । पतता वृत्रशिरसा जगत्ऺत्रासमुपागमत् ।। 7.85.14 ।।
explanation: The world was filled with terror by the falling head of Vritra, as if by the dreadful Kālāgni, indeed with a greatly burning mighty flame.

shloka_text: असम्भाव्यं वधं तस्य वृत्रस्य विबुधाधिपः । चिन्तयानो जगामाशु लोकस्यान्तं महायशाः ।। 7.85.15 ।।
explanation: The greatly renowned lord of the gods, pondering the impossible slaying of Vritra, quickly went to the end of the world.

shloka_text: तमिन्द्रं ब्रह्महत्या ऽ ऽशु गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति । अपतच्चास्य गात्रेषु तमिन्द्रं दुःखमाविशत् ।। 7.85.16 ।।
explanation: As that Indra went, the sin of Brahman-killing quickly followed him. It fell upon his limbs, and sorrow entered that Indra.

shloka_text: हतारयः प्रनष्टेन्द्रा देवाः साग्निपुरोगमाः । विष्णुं त्रिभुवनेशानं मुहुर्मुहुरपूजयन् ।। 7.85.17 ।।
explanation: The gods, whose enemies were slain, and whose Indra had vanished, led by Agni, repeatedly worshipped Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds.

shloka_text: त्वं गतिः परमेशान पूर्वजो जगतः पिता । रक्षार्थं सर्वभूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान् ।। 7.85.18 ।।
explanation: O Supreme Lord, You are the ultimate refuge, the first-born, the father of the world. For the protection of all beings, You have assumed the state of Vishnu.

shloka_text: हतश्चायं त्वया वृत्रो ब्रह्महत्या च वासवम् । बाधते सुरशार्दूल मोक्षं तस्या विनिर्दिश ।। 7.85.19 ।।
explanation: O best of gods, this Vritra was killed by you (Indra), and the sin of Brahmanicide afflicts Vasava. Prescribe a remedy for that.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां विष्णुरब्रवीत् । मामेव यजतां शक्रः पावयिष्यामि वज्रिणम् ।। 7.85.20 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of the gods, Vishnu said: "Let Shakra worship me alone; I will purify the wielder of the thunderbolt."

shloka_text: पुण्येन हयमेधेन मामिष्ट्वा पाकशासनः । पुनरेष्यति देवानामिन्द्रत्वमकुतोभयम् ।। 7.85.21 ।।
explanation: Having worshipped me with the meritorious Hayamedha sacrifice, Paka-shasana will again attain the fearless Indra-ship of the gods.

shloka_text: एवं सन्दिश्य तां वाणीं देवानाममृतोपमाम् । जगाम विष्णुर्देवेशः स्तूयमानस्त्रिविष्टपम् ।। 7.85.22 ।।
explanation: Having thus conveyed that nectar-like message of the gods, Vishnu, the Lord of the gods, being praised, went to heaven.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 85 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the eighty-fifth chapter.

shloka_text: तदा वृत्रवधं सर्वमखिलेन स लक्ष्मणः । कथयित्वा नरश्रेष्ठः कथाशेषं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.86.1 ।।
explanation: Then, that best among men, Lakshmana, having completely narrated the entire story of the killing of Vritra, proceeded with the rest of the narrative.

shloka_text: ततो हते महावीर्ये वृत्रे देवभयङ्करे । ब्रह्महत्यावृतः शक्रः सञ्ज्ञां लेभे न वृत्रहा ।। 7.86.2 ।।
explanation: Then, when the mighty Vritra, who was terrifying to the gods, had been slain, Indra, the slayer of Vritra, enveloped by the sin of Brahman-slaughter, did not regain consciousness.

shloka_text: सो ऽन्तमाश्रित्य लोकानां नष्टसञ्ज्ञो विचेतनः । कालं तत्रावसत्कञ्चिद्वेष्टमान इवोरगः ।। 7.86.3 ।।
explanation: He, having reached the end of the worlds, lost his senses and became unconscious. He remained there for some time, writhing like a serpent.

shloka_text: अथ नष्टे सहस्राक्षे उद्विग्नमभवज्जगत् । भूमिश्च ध्वस्तसङ्काशा निःस्नेहा शुष्ककानना ।। 7.86.4 ।।
explanation: Then, when Sahasraksha disappeared, the world became agitated. The earth, too, appeared devastated, devoid of moisture, and with parched forests.

shloka_text: निःस्रोतसश्च ते सर्वे तु ह्रदाश्च सरितस्तथा । सङ्क्षोभश्चैव सत्त्वानामनावृष्टिकृतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.86.5 ।।
explanation: And all those lakes and rivers dried up. And there was distress among living beings, caused by the lack of rain.

shloka_text: क्षीयमाणे तु लोके ऽस्मिन्सम्भ्रान्तमनसः सुराः । यदुक्तं विष्णुना पूर्वं तं यज्ञं समुपानयन् ।। 7.86.6 ।।
explanation: As this world was perishing, the gods, with bewildered minds, performed that sacrifice which had been previously declared by Vishnu.

shloka_text: ततः सर्वे सुरगणाः सोपाध्यायाः सहर्षिभिः । तं देशं समुपाजग्मुर्यत्रेन्द्रो भयमोहितः ।। 7.86.7 ।।
explanation: Then all the hosts of gods, with their preceptors and with the sages, approached that place where Indra was bewildered by fear.

shloka_text: ते तु दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षमावृतं ब्रह्महत्यया । तं पुरस्कृत्य देवेशमश्वमेधमुपाक्रमन् ।। 7.86.8 ।।
explanation: But they, having seen the thousand-eyed one afflicted by the sin of Brahman-slaughter, making that lord of gods the chief, commenced the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततो ऽश्वमेधः सुमहान्महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः । ववृधे ब्रह्महत्ययाः पावनार्थं नरेश्वर ।। 7.86.9 ।।
explanation: Then, the very grand Ashwamedha sacrifice of the great-souled Mahendra was performed for purification from the sin of Brahman-killing, O king of men.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनः । अभिगम्याब्रवीद्वाक्यं क्व मे स्थानं विधास्यथ ।। 7.86.10 ।।
explanation: Then, when the sacrifice was completed, the sin of Brahman-killing of the great soul approached and spoke these words: "Where will you assign my place?"

shloka_text: ते तामूचुस्तदा देवास्तुष्टाः प्रीतिसमन्विताः । चतुर्धा विभजात्मानमात्मनैव दुरासदे ।। 7.86.11 ।।
explanation: Then the gods, pleased and filled with affection, said to her: "O formidable one, divide yourself into four parts by yourself."

shloka_text: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनाम् । सन्निधौ स्थानमन्यत्र वरयामास दुर्वसा ।। 7.86.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the great-souled gods, Brahmahatya chose another place, away from their presence.

shloka_text: एकेनांशेन वत्स्यामि पूर्णोदासु नदीषु वै । चतुरो वार्षिकान्मासान्दर्पघ्नी कामवारिणी ।। 7.86.13 ।।
explanation: With one part, I will reside in the full-watered rivers for the four months of the rainy season, subduing pride and restraining desires.

shloka_text: भूम्यामहं सर्वकालमेकेनांशेन सर्वदा । वसिष्यामि न सन्देहः सत्येनैतद्ब्रवीमि वः ।। 7.86.14 ।।
explanation: I shall always reside on the earth with one part of myself, at all times. Without doubt, I speak this to you truthfully.

shloka_text: यो ऽयमंशस्तृतीयो मे स्त्रीषु यौवनशालिषु । त्रिरात्रं दर्पपूर्णासु वशिष्ये दर्पघातिनी ।। 7.86.15 ।।
explanation: This third part of me, among youthful women full of pride, for three nights, I will subdue (them) as a destroyer of pride.

shloka_text: हन्तारो ब्राह्मणान्ये तु मृषापूर्वमदूषकान् । तांश्चतुर्थेन भागेन संश्रयिष्ये सुरर्षभाः ।। 7.86.16 ।।
explanation: O best among gods, those who falsely kill innocent Brahmins, I shall take a fourth part (of their sin).

shloka_text: प्रत्यूचुस्तां ततो देवा यथा वदसि दुर्वसे । तथा भवतु तत्सर्वं साधयस्व यदीप्सितम् ।। 7.86.17 ।।
explanation: Then the gods replied to her: "O Durvasa, as you say, so let all that be. Accomplish whatever you desire."

shloka_text: ततः प्रीत्या ऽन्विता देवाः सहस्राक्षं ववन्दिरे । विज्वरः स च पूतात्मा वासवः समपद्यत ।। 7.86.18 ।।
explanation: Then, the gods, filled with joy, bowed to the thousand-eyed one. And he, Vasava, became free from distress and pure in spirit.

shloka_text: प्रशान्तं च जगत्सर्वं सहस्राक्षे प्रतिष्ठिते । यज्ञं चाद्भुतसङ्काशं तदा शक्रो ऽभ्यपूजयत् ।। 7.86.19 ।।
explanation: And the entire world became peaceful when Sahasraksha was established. And then Shakra worshipped the sacrifice, which was wondrous to behold.

shloka_text: ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रसादो रघुनन्दन । यजस्व सुमहाभाग हयमेधेन पार्थिव ।। 7.86.20 ।।
explanation: Such indeed is the blessing of the Ashwamedha, O Raghunandana. O greatly fortunate king, perform the horse sacrifice.

shloka_text: इति लक्ष्मणवाक्यमुत्तमं नृपतिरतीव मनोहरं महात्मा । परितोषमवाप हृष्टचेता निशमय्येन्द्रसमानविक्रमौजाः ।। 7.86.21 ।।
explanation: Thus, having heard Lakshmana's excellent and exceedingly charming words, the great-souled king, whose valor and might were equal to Indra, became joyful in heart and attained great satisfaction.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षडशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 86 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, this is the eighty-sixth chapter.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः प्रहसन्राघवो वचः ।। 7.87.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that statement spoken by Lakshmana, the greatly effulgent Rama, who was skilled in speech, replied with a smile.

shloka_text: एवमेव नरश्रेष्ठ यथा वदसि लक्ष्मण । वृत्रघातमशेषेण वाजिमेधफलं च यत् ।। 7.87.2 ।।
explanation: Exactly so, O best among men, O Lakshmana, as you say, the complete slaying of Vritra and that which is the fruit of the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: श्रूयते हि पुरा सौम्य कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः । पुत्रो बाह्लीश्वरः श्रीमानिलो नाम महाशयाः ।। 7.87.3 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, it is indeed heard of old that Kardama Prajapati had a son, the illustrious Ila, lord of Bahlika, a great soul.

shloka_text: स राजा पृथिवीं सर्वां वशे कृत्वा सुधार्मिकः । राज्यं चैव नरव्याघ्र पुत्रवत्पर्यपालयत् ।। 7.87.4 ।।
explanation: That very righteous king, a tiger among men, having brought the entire earth under his control, protected the kingdom and its people as if they were his own sons.

shloka_text: सुरैश्च परमोदारैर्दैतेयैश्च महाधनैः । नागराक्षसगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सुमहात्मभिः ।। 7.87.5 ।।
explanation: And by the gods, and by the most generous Daityas who possess great wealth, and by Nagas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, and by the very great-souled Yakshas.

shloka_text: पूज्यते नित्यशः सौम्य भयार्तै रघुनन्दन । अबिभ्यंश्च त्रयो लोकाः सरोषस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.87.6 ।।
explanation: O gentle Raghunandana, he is constantly worshipped by those afflicted by fear. And the three worlds do not fear the angry great soul.

shloka_text: स राजा तादृशो ह्यासीद्धर्मे वीर्ये च निष्ठितः । बुद्ध्या च परमोदारो बाह्लीकेशो महायशाः ।। 7.87.7 ।।
explanation: That king, the lord of Bahlika, was indeed such, firmly established in righteousness and valor. He was exceedingly noble in intellect and greatly renowned.

shloka_text: स प्रचक्रे महाबाहुर्मृगयां रुचिरे वने । चैत्रे मनोरमे मासि सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.87.8 ।।
explanation: The mighty-armed one, accompanied by his servants, army, and conveyances, undertook a hunt in the beautiful forest during the delightful month of Chaitra.

shloka_text: प्रजघ्ने च नृपो ऽरण्ये मृगाञ्छतसहस्रशः । हत्वैव तृप्तिर्नाभूच्च राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.87.9 ।।
explanation: And the king slaughtered hundreds of thousands of animals in the forest. Even after killing, that great-souled king found no satisfaction.

shloka_text: नानामृगाणामयुतं वध्यमानं महात्मना । यत्र जातो माहासेनस्तं देशमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.87.10 ।।
explanation: He approached that region where Mahasena was born, and where ten thousand various animals were being slaughtered by the great soul.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्प्रदेशे देवेश शैलराजसुतां हरः । रमयामास दुर्धर्षः सर्वैरनुचरैः सह ।। 7.87.11 ।।
explanation: In that region, the formidable Hara, the Lord of gods, enjoyed with the daughter of the mountain king, accompanied by all his attendants.

shloka_text: कृत्वा स्त्रीरूपमात्मानमुमेशो गोपतिध्वजः । देव्याः प्रियचिकीर्षुः संस्तस्मिन्पर्वतनिर्झरे ।। 7.87.12 ।।
explanation: Umesha, whose banner bears the bull, desirous of pleasing the Goddess, having assumed a female form, in that mountain stream.

shloka_text: ये तु तत्र वनोद्देशे सत्त्वाः पुरुषवादिनः । वृक्षाः पुरुषनामानस्ते ऽभवन् स्त्रीजनास्तदा ।। 7.87.13 ।।
explanation: And those beings in that forest region who spoke like men, and the trees that bore male names, they all became women at that time.

shloka_text: यच्च किञ्चन तत्सर्वं नारीसञ्ज्ञं बभूव ह । एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजा स इलः कर्दमात्मजः । निघ्नन्मृगसहस्राणि तं देशमुपचक्रमे ।। 7.87.14 ।।
explanation: And whatever existed, all of that became female. Meanwhile, King Ila, the son of Kardama, hunting thousands of deer, approached that region.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा स्त्रीकृतं सर्वं सव्यालमृगपक्षकम् । आत्मनं स्त्रीकृतं चैव सानुगं रघुनन्दन ।। 7.87.15 ।।
explanation: Having seen everything, including snakes, deer, and birds, transformed into females, and himself along with his followers also transformed into females, O scion of Raghu.

shloka_text: तस्य दुःखं महच्चासीद्दृष्ट्वा ऽ ऽत्मानं तथागतम् । उमापतेश्च तत्कर्म ज्ञात्वा त्रासमुपागमत् ।। 7.87.16 ।।
explanation: He experienced great sorrow, having seen himself in that condition. And having understood that deed of Uma's lord, he was struck with terror.

shloka_text: ततो देवं महात्मानं शितिकण्ठं कपर्दिनम् । जगाम शरणं राजा सभृत्यबलवाहनः ।। 7.87.17 ।।
explanation: Then the king, with his servants, army, and vehicles, went for refuge to the great-souled god, the blue-necked one with matted hair.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य वरदः सह देव्या महेश्वरः । प्रजापतिसुतं वाक्यमुवाच वरदः स्वयम् ।। 7.87.18 ।।
explanation: Then, Maheśvara, the bestower of boons, smiling, along with the Goddess, himself spoke a word to the son of Prajāpati.

shloka_text: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ राजर्षे कार्दमेय महाबल । पुरुषत्वमृते सौम्य वरं वरय सुव्रत ।। 7.87.19 ।।
explanation: Arise, arise, O Royal Sage, O son of Kardama, O mighty-armed one! O gentle one, O virtuous one, choose a boon, except for manhood.

shloka_text: ततः स राजा दुःखार्तः प्रत्याख्यातो महात्मना । न च जग्राह स्त्रीभूतो वरमन्यं सुरोत्तमात् ।। 7.87.20 ।।
explanation: Then that king, distressed, having been rejected by the great soul, and having become a woman, did not accept any other boon from the best of gods.

shloka_text: ततः शोकेन महता शैलराजसुतां नृपः । प्रणिपत्य ह्युमां देवीं सर्वेणैवान्तरात्मना ।। 7.87.21 ।।
explanation: Then, the king, with great sorrow, prostrated himself before Uma, the Goddess, the daughter of the king of mountains, with his entire inner self.

shloka_text: ईशे वराणां वरदे लोकानामसि भामिनी । अमोघदर्शने देवी भज सौम्येन चक्षुषा ।। 7.87.22 ।।
explanation: O giver of boons, O beautiful lady, you are the mistress of boons and of the worlds. O Goddess whose sight is unfailing, look upon me with a gentle eye.

shloka_text: हृद्गतं तस्य राजर्षेर्विज्ञाय हरसन्निधौ । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं देवी रुद्रस्य संमता ।। 7.87.23 ।।
explanation: Having understood what was in the heart of that royal sage, in the presence of Hara, the Goddess, beloved of Rudra, spoke an auspicious word.

shloka_text: अर्धस्य देवो वरदो वरार्धस्य तव ह्यहम् । तस्मादर्धं गृहाण त्वं स्त्रीपुंसोर्यावदिच्छसि ।। 7.87.24 ।।
explanation: The god is the giver of boons for half, and I am indeed for your other half of the boon. Therefore, take half, as much as you desire of the male and female (aspects).

shloka_text: तदद्भुततरं श्रुत्वा देव्या वरमनुत्तमम् । सम्प्रहृष्टमना भूत्वा राजा वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.87.25 ।।
explanation: Having heard that most wonderful and excellent boon from the goddess, the king, becoming greatly delighted in mind, then spoke.

shloka_text: यदि देवि प्रसन्ना मे रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि । मासं स्त्रीत्वमुपासित्वा मासं स्यां पुरुषः पुनः ।। 7.87.26 ।।
explanation: If, O goddess, you are pleased with me, who am unparalleled in beauty on earth, then having lived as a woman for a month, may I again be a man for a month.

shloka_text: ईप्सितं तस्य विज्ञाय देवी सुरुचिरानना । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यमेवमेव भविष्यति ।। 7.87.27 ।।
explanation: Having understood his desire, the goddess with the very beautiful face replied with an auspicious statement: "It shall be just so."

shloka_text: राजन्पुरुषभूतस्त्वं स्त्रीभावं न स्मरिष्यसि । स्त्रीभूतश्च परं मासं न स्मरिष्यसि पौरुषम् ।। 7.87.28 ।।
explanation: O King, when you are a man, you will not remember your state as a woman. And when you are a woman, for the next month, you will not remember your manhood.

shloka_text: एवं स राजा पुरुषो मासं भूत्वाथ कार्दमिः । त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी नारी मासमेकमिला ऽभवत् ।। 7.87.29 ।।
explanation: Thus, that king, the son of Kardama, having been a man for a month, then became Ila, a woman beautiful in the three worlds, for one month.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्ताशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 87 ।।
explanation: Thus in the Arsha, the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, the eighty-seventh chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: तां कथामिलसम्बद्धां रामेण समुदीरिताम् । लक्ष्मणो भरतश्चैव श्रुत्वा परमविस्मितौ ।। 7.88.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that story related to Ila, narrated by Rama, Lakshmana and Bharata were greatly astonished.

shloka_text: तौ रामं प्राञ्जली भूत्वा तस्य राज्ञो महात्मनः । विस्तरं तस्य भावस्य तदा पप्रच्छतुः पुनः ।। 7.88.2 ।।
explanation: Then, those two, having folded their hands, asked Rama for the full account of the state of that great-souled king.

shloka_text: कथं स राजा स्त्रीभूतो वर्तयामास दुर्गतिः । पुरुषः स यदा भूतः कां वृत्तिं वर्तयत्यसौ ।। 7.88.3 ।।
explanation: How did that king, having become a woman, live in distress? When he became a man, what kind of life did he lead?

shloka_text: तयोस्तद्भाषितं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितम् । कथयामास काकुत्स्थस्तस्य राज्ञो यथागतम् ।। 7.88.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard their words, which were full of curiosity, Kakutstha narrated to that king what had transpired.

shloka_text: तमेव प्रथमं मासं स्त्रीभूता लोकसुन्दरी । ताभिः परिवृता स्त्रीभिर्ये च पूर्वपदानुगाः ।। 7.88.5 ।।
explanation: In that very first month, having become a woman, a beauty of the world, she was surrounded by those women, and by those who were her former followers.

shloka_text: तत्काननं विगाह्वाशु विजह्रे लोकसुन्दरी । द्रुमगुल्मलताकीर्णं पद्भ्यां पद्मदलेक्षणा ।। 7.88.6 ।।
explanation: The most beautiful woman in the world, whose eyes were like lotus petals, quickly entered that forest, dense with trees, bushes, and creepers, and wandered through it on foot.

shloka_text: वाहनानि च सर्वाणि सा त्यक्त्वा वै समन्ततः । पर्वताभोगविवरे तस्मिन्रेमे इला तदा ।। 7.88.7 ।।
explanation: And she, Ila, having completely abandoned all her vehicles, then sported in that wide mountain hollow.

shloka_text: अथ तस्मिन्वनोद्देशे पर्वतस्याविदूरतः । सरः सुरुचिरप्रख्यं नानापक्षिगणैर्युतम् ।। 7.88.8 ।।
explanation: Then, in that forest region, not far from the mountain, there was a lake of exceedingly charming appearance, filled with various flocks of birds.

shloka_text: ददर्श सा त्विला तस्मिन्बुधं सोमसुतं तदा । ज्वलन्तं स्वेन वपुषा पूर्णसोममिवोदितम् ।। 7.88.9 ।।
explanation: Then, Ila saw Budha, the son of Soma, blazing with his own form, like the full moon risen.

shloka_text: तपन्तं च तपस्तीव्रमम्भोमध्ये दुरासदम् । यशस्करं कामकरं कारुण्ये पर्यवस्थितम् ।। 7.88.10 ।।
explanation: And performing severe penance in the midst of water, which is formidable, bestowing fame, fulfilling desires, and abiding in compassion.

shloka_text: सा तं जलाशयं सर्वं क्षोभयामास विस्मिता । सहगैः पूर्वपुरुषैः स्त्रीभूतै रघुनन्दन ।। 7.88.11 ।।
explanation: Astonished, she agitated that entire lake, along with her companions, the former men who had become women, O Raghunandana.

shloka_text: बुधस्तु तां समीक्ष्यैव कामबाणवशं गतः । नोपलेभे तदा ऽ ऽत्मानं सञ्चचाल तदा ऽ ऽम्भसि ।। 7.88.12 ।।
explanation: But Budha, having just seen her, fell under the sway of Cupid's arrows. He then lost his self-awareness and swayed in the water.

shloka_text: इलां निरीक्षमाणस्तु त्रैलोक्याभ्यधिकां शुभाम् । चिन्तां समभ्यतिक्रामत् का न्वियं देवताधिका ।। 7.88.13 ।।
explanation: Gazing upon Ila, who was more beautiful and radiant than anything in the three worlds, he was seized by the thought, "Who indeed is this superior deity?"

shloka_text: न देवीषु न नागीषु नासुरीष्वप्सरःसु च । दृष्टपूर्वा मया काचिद्रूपेणानेन शोभिता ।। 7.88.14 ।।
explanation: I have never before seen anyone among goddesses, Nāginis, Asuris, or Apsaras, adorned with such beauty.

shloka_text: सदृशीयं मम भवेद्यदि नान्यपरिग्रहः । इति बुद्धिं समास्थाय जलात्कूलमुपागमत् ।। 7.88.15 ।।
explanation: If this one were suitable for me, and not possessed by another, having thus resolved in his mind, he came to the shore from the water.

shloka_text: आश्रमं समुपागम्य ततस्ताः प्रमदोत्तमाः । शब्दापयत धर्मात्मा ताश्चैनं च ववन्दिरे ।। 7.88.16 ।।
explanation: Having arrived at the hermitage, those excellent women were summoned by the righteous one, and they worshipped him.

shloka_text: स ताः पप्रच्छ धर्मात्मा कस्यैषा लोकसुन्दरी । किमर्थमागता चैव सर्वमाख्यात मा चिरम् ।। 7.88.17 ।।
explanation: The righteous one asked them, "Whose is this woman, most beautiful in the world? And why has she come? Tell me everything without delay."

shloka_text: शुभं तु तस्य तद्वाक्यं मधुरं मधुराक्षरम् । श्रुत्वा स्त्रियश्च ताः सर्वा ऊचुर्मधुरया गिरा ।। 7.88.18 ।।
explanation: Having heard his auspicious, sweet, and melodious speech, all those women spoke with a sweet voice.

shloka_text: अस्माकमेषा सुश्रोणी प्रभुत्वे वर्तते सदा । अपतिः काननान्तेषु सहास्माभिश्चरत्यसौ ।। 7.88.19 ।।
explanation: This beautiful-hipped woman is always under our control. She, without a husband, roams with us in the forest regions.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यमव्यक्तपदं तासां स्त्रीणां निशम्य च । विद्यामावर्तनीं पुण्यामावर्तयत स द्विजः ।। 7.88.20 ।।
explanation: Having heard the indistinct words of those women, that Brahmin performed the sacred spell of turning back.

shloka_text: सो ऽर्थं विदित्वा सकलं तस्य राज्ञो यथागतम् । सर्वा एव स्त्रियस्ताश्च बभाषे मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.88.21 ।।
explanation: The foremost among sages, having understood the entire matter of that king as it had come to pass, addressed all those women.

shloka_text: अत्र किम्पुरुषीर्भूत्वा शैलरोधसि वत्स्यथ । आवासस्तु गिरावस्मिञ्छीघ्रमेव विधीयताम् ।। 7.88.22 ।।
explanation: Here, having become Kimpuruṣīs, you shall dwell on the mountain slope. Let a dwelling be quickly arranged on this mountain.

shloka_text: मूलपत्रफलैः सर्वा वर्तयिष्यथ नित्यदा । स्त्रियः किम्पुरुषान्नाम भर्तऽन्समुपलप्स्यथ ।। 7.88.23 ।।
explanation: All of you will always subsist on roots, leaves, and fruits. Women, you will obtain husbands named Kimpurushas.

shloka_text: ताः श्रुत्वा सोमपुत्रस्य वाचं किम्पुरुषीकृताः । उपासाञ्चक्रिरे शैलं वध्वस्ता बहुलास्तदा ।। 7.88.24 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words of the son of Soma, those women, transformed into Kimpuruṣīs, then approached that mountain in great numbers.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 88 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha, the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the eighty-eighth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा किम्पुरुषोत्पत्तिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तदा । आश्चर्यमिति चाब्रूतामुभौ रामं जनेश्वरम् ।। 7.89.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard the origin of the Kimpurushas, Lakshmana and Bharata then both said to Rama, the lord of the people, "How wonderful!"

shloka_text: अथ रामः कथामेतां भूय एव महायशाः । कथयामास धर्मात्मा प्रजापतिसुतस्य वै ।। 7.89.2 ।।
explanation: Then, the greatly renowned and righteous Rama again narrated this story to the son of Prajapati.

shloka_text: सर्वास्ता विद्रुता दृष्ट्वा किन्नरीर्ऋषिसत्तमः । उवाच रूपसम्पन्नां तां स्त्रियं प्रहसन्निव ।। 7.89.3 ।।
explanation: Having seen all those Kinnaris flee, the best of sages, as if laughing, spoke to that beautiful woman.

shloka_text: सोमस्याहं सुदयितः सुतः सुरुचिरानने । भजस्व मां वरारोहे भक्त्या स्निग्धेन चक्षुषा ।। 7.89.4 ।।
explanation: O lady with a very beautiful face, I am the dearly beloved son of Soma. O lady with beautiful hips, worship me with devotion and with loving eyes.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शून्ये स्वजनवर्जिते । इला सुरुचिरप्रख्यं प्रत्युवाच महाग्रहम् ।। 7.89.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words in that desolate place, devoid of her own people, Ila replied to the great celestial being, who was exceedingly beautiful.

shloka_text: अहं कामचरी सौम्य तवास्मि वशवर्तिनी । प्रशाधि मां सोमसुत यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ।। 7.89.6 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, I, who am free to move at will, am now under your control. O son of Soma, command me, and do as you wish.

shloka_text: तस्यास्तदद्भुतप्रख्यं श्रुत्वा हर्षमुपागतः । स वै कामी सह तया रेमे चन्द्रमसः सुतः ।। 7.89.7 ।।
explanation: Upon hearing that wonderful thing from her, he became joyful. Indeed, that desirous son of the moon enjoyed with her.

shloka_text: बुधस्य माधवो मासस्तामिलां रुचिराननाम् । गतो रमयतो ऽत्यर्थं क्षणवत्तस्य कामिनः ।। 7.89.8 ।।
explanation: For Budha, the month of Madhava, as he greatly enjoyed with the lovely-faced Tamila, passed like a moment for that lover.

shloka_text: अथ मासे तु सम्पूर्णे पूर्णेन्दुसदृशाननः । प्रजापतिसुतः श्रीमाञ्छयने प्रत्यबुध्यत ।। 7.89.9 ।।
explanation: Then, when the month was complete, the glorious son of Prajapati, whose face was like the full moon, awoke from his bed.

shloka_text: सो ऽपश्यत्सोमजं तत्र तपन्तं सलिलाशये । ऊर्ध्वबाहुं निरालम्बं तं राजा प्रत्यभाषत ।। 7.89.10 ।।
explanation: He saw the son of Soma there, performing penance in the water, with arms raised upwards, unsupported. The king addressed him.

shloka_text: भगवन्पर्वतं दुर्गं प्रविष्टो ऽस्मि सहानुगः । न च पश्यामि तत्सैन्यं क्व नु ते मामका गताः ।। 7.89.11 ।।
explanation: O Lord, I have entered the difficult mountain stronghold with my followers. But I do not see that army. Where have my people gone?

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा तस्य राजर्षेर्नष्टसञ्ज्ञस्य भाषितम् । प्रत्युवाच शुभं वाक्यं सान्त्वयन्परया गिरा ।। 7.89.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of the royal sage who had lost consciousness, he replied with auspicious words, comforting him with a supreme voice.

shloka_text: अश्मवर्षेण महता भृत्यास्ते विनिपातिताः । त्वं चाश्रमपदे सुप्तो वातवर्षभयार्दितः ।। 7.89.13 ।।
explanation: Your servants were struck down by a great shower of stones. And you were sleeping in the hermitage, afflicted by the fear of wind and rain.

shloka_text: समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते निर्भयो विगतज्वरः । फलमूलाशनो वीर निवसेह यथासुखम् ।। 7.89.14 ।।
explanation: Be comforted, may good fortune be yours. Fearless and free from distress, O hero, subsisting on fruits and roots, dwell here happily.

shloka_text: स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महामतिः । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यक्षयाद् भृशम् ।। 7.89.15 ।।
explanation: That great-minded king, reassured by that speech, then replied, greatly distressed due to the loss of his servants.

shloka_text: त्यक्ष्याम्यहं स्वकं राज्यं नाहं भृत्यैर्विनाकृतः । वर्तयेयं क्षणं ब्रह्मन्समनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.89.16 ।।
explanation: I will abandon my own kingdom. I cannot live even for a moment without my servants. O Brahman, you should grant me permission.

shloka_text: सुतो धर्मपरो ब्रह्मञ्ज्येष्ठो मम महायशाः । शशबिन्दुरिति ख्यातः स मे राज्यं प्रपत्स्यते ।। 7.89.17 ।।
explanation: O Brahmana, my eldest son, the illustrious Shasabindu, who is devoted to righteousness, will inherit my kingdom.

shloka_text: न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं हित्वा भृत्यदारान्सुखान्वितान् । प्रतिवक्तुं महातेजः किञ्चिदप्यशुभं वचः ।। 7.89.18 ।।
explanation: O greatly powerful one, I will certainly not be able to utter any inauspicious word, having abandoned my happy servants and wives.

shloka_text: तथा ब्रुवति राजेन्द्रे बुधः परममद्भुतम् । सान्त्वपूर्वमथोवाच वासस्त इह रोचताम् ।। 7.89.19 ।।
explanation: When the king of kings spoke thus, Budha, greatly astonished, then spoke with soothing words: 'May your dwelling here be pleasing.'

shloka_text: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यः कार्दमेय महाबल । संवत्सरोषितस्येह कारयिष्यामि ते हितम् ।। 7.89.20 ।।
explanation: O son of Kardama, O mighty-armed, you should not grieve. I will bring about your welfare here, after you have resided for a year.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बुधस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः । वासाय विदधे बुद्धिं यदुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ।। 7.89.21 ।।
explanation: Having heard that statement of Budha, whose actions were untroubled, he resolved to dwell there, as had been spoken by the speaker of Brahman.

shloka_text: मासं स स्त्री तदा भूत्वा रमयत्यनिशं शुदा । मासं पुरुषभावेन धर्मबुद्धिं चकार सः ।। 7.89.22 ।।
explanation: For a month, he, having then become a woman, enjoyed constantly and happily. For a month, in the state of a man, he cultivated a righteous mind.

shloka_text: ततः सा नवमे मासि इला सोमसुतात्सुतम् । जनयामास सुश्रोणी पुरूरवसमूर्जितम् ।। 7.89.23 ।।
explanation: Then, in the ninth month, Ila, the beautiful-hipped, gave birth to a mighty son, Pururavas, from the son of Soma.

shloka_text: जातमात्रं तु सुश्रोणी पितुर्हस्ते न्यवेशयत् । बुधस्य समवर्णभमिला पुत्रं महाबलम् ।। 7.89.24 ।।
explanation: As soon as he was born, the beautiful-hipped one placed the mighty son, who was of the same form as Ila, into the hand of Budha, his father.

shloka_text: बुधस्तु पुरुषीभूतं स वै संवत्सरान्तरम् । कथाभी रमयामास धर्मयुक्ताभिरात्मवान् ।। 7.89.25 ।।
explanation: The wise Budha indeed entertained him who had assumed a human form for a year with stories full of righteousness.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोननवतितमः सर्गः ।। 89 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the eighty-ninth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति रामे तु तस्य जन्म तदद्भुतम् । उवाच लक्ष्मणो भूयो भरतश्च महायशाः ।। 7.90.1 ।।
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Lakshmana and the greatly renowned Bharata spoke again about that wonderful birth.

shloka_text: इला सा सोमपुत्रस्य संवत्सरमथोषिता । अकरोत्किं नरश्रेष्ठ तत्त्वं शंसितुमर्हसि ।। 7.90.2 ।।
explanation: Having resided with the son of Soma for a year, what did Ila do then? O best among men, you ought to tell the truth.

shloka_text: तयोस्तद्वाक्यमाधुर्यं निशम्य परिपृच्छतोः । रामः पुनरुवाचेमां प्रजापतिसुते कथाम् ।। 7.90.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard the sweetness of their words, as they questioned him, Rama again spoke this story to the daughters of Prajapati.

shloka_text: पुरुषत्वं गते शूरे बुधः परमबुद्धिमान् । संवर्तं परमोदारमाजुहाव महायशाः ।। 7.90.4 ।।
explanation: When the hero attained manhood, the supremely intelligent and very famous Budha summoned the extremely generous Samvarta.

shloka_text: च्यवनं भृगुपुत्रं च मुनिं चारिष्टनेमिनम् । प्रमोदनं मोदकरं ततो दुर्वाससं मुनिम् ।। 7.90.5 ।।
explanation: Cyavana, the son of Bhrigu, and the sage Ariṣṭanemi, Pramodana, Modakara, and then the sage Durvasas.

shloka_text: एतान्सर्वान्समानीय वाक्यज्ञस्तत्त्वदर्शनः । उवाच सर्वान्सुहृदो धैर्येण सुसमाहितान् ।। 7.90.6 ।।
explanation: Having gathered all these, the one skilled in speech and a seer of truth spoke to all his well-composed friends with fortitude.

shloka_text: अयं राजा महाबाहुः कर्दमस्य इलः सुतः । जानीतैनं यथाभूतं श्रेयो ह्यत्र विधीयताम् ।। 7.90.7 ।।
explanation: This mighty-armed king is Ila, the son of Kardama. Know him as he truly is. Indeed, let what is beneficial be done here.

shloka_text: तेषां संवदतामेव तमाश्रममुपागमत् । कर्दमस्तु महातेजा द्विजैः सह महात्मभिः ।। 7.90.8 ।।
explanation: Even as they were conversing, Kardama, the greatly effulgent one, approached that hermitage along with great-souled Brahmins.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुश्चैव वषट्कारस्तथैव च । ओङ्कारश्च महातेजास्तमाश्रममुपागमत् ।। 7.90.9 ।।
explanation: Pulastya, Kratu, and Vaṣaṭkāra, and similarly the greatly effulgent Oṅkāra, came to that hermitage.

shloka_text: ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसः परस्परसमागमे । हितैषिणो बाल्हिपतेः पृथग्वाक्यान्यथाब्रुवन् ।। 7.90.10 ।।
explanation: All of them, with joyful minds, upon their mutual meeting, being well-wishers of Bahlipati, then spoke various words.

shloka_text: कर्दमस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं सुतार्थं परमं हितम् । द्विजाः शृणुत मद्वाक्यं यच्छ्रेयः पार्थिवस्य हि ।। 7.90.11 ।।
explanation: Kardama then spoke words, supremely beneficial for his son. O Brahmins, listen to my words, which are indeed for the welfare of the king.

shloka_text: नान्यं पश्यामि भैषज्यमन्तरा वृषभध्वजम् । नाश्वमेधात्परो यज्ञः प्रियश्चैव महात्मनः । तस्माद्यजामहे सर्वे पार्थिवार्थे दुरासदम् ।। 7.90.12 ।।
explanation: I see no other remedy apart from Shiva, whose emblem is the bull. There is no sacrifice greater than the Ashwamedha, and it is indeed dear to the great-souled one. Therefore, all of us shall worship the unassailable (deity) for the sake of the king.

shloka_text: कर्दमेनैवमुक्तास्तु सर्व एव द्विजर्षभाः । रोचयन्ति स्म तं यज्ञं रुद्रस्याराधनं प्रति ।। 7.90.13 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Kardama, all the eminent Brahmins approved of that sacrifice for the worship of Rudra.

shloka_text: संवर्तस्य तु राजर्षेः शिष्यः पुरपुरञ्जयः । मरुत्त इति विख्यातस्तं यज्ञं समुपाहरत् ।। 7.90.14 ।।
explanation: Marutta, the renowned disciple of the royal sage Samvarta, who was a conqueror of cities, performed that sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञो महानासीद्बुधाश्रमसमीपतः । रुद्रश्च परमं तोषमाजगाम महायशाः ।। 7.90.15 ।।
explanation: Then a great sacrifice took place near Budha's hermitage. And the greatly renowned Rudra attained supreme satisfaction.

shloka_text: अथ यज्ञे समाप्ते तु प्रीतः परमया मुदा । उमापतिर्द्विजान्सर्वानुवाच इलसन्निधौ ।। 7.90.16 ।।
explanation: Then, when the sacrifice was completed, Umāpati, pleased with supreme joy, spoke to all the Brahmins in the presence of Ila.

shloka_text: प्रीतो ऽस्मि हयमेधेन भक्त्या च द्विजसत्तमाः । अस्य बाह्लिपतेश्चैव किं करोमि प्रियं शुभम् ।। 7.90.17 ।।
explanation: O best of Brahmins, I am pleased by the horse sacrifice and by devotion. What good and pleasing thing shall I do for this lord of Bahlika?

shloka_text: तथा वदति देवेशे द्विजास्ते सुसमाहिताः । प्रसादयन्ति देवेशं यथा स्यात्पुरुषस्त्विला ।। 7.90.18 ।।
explanation: When the Lord of the gods spoke thus, those brahmins, being very attentive, propitiated the Lord of the gods so that Ila might become a man.

shloka_text: ततः प्रीतो महादेवः पुरुषत्वं ददौ पुनः । इलायै सुमहातेजा दत्त्वा चान्तरधीयत ।। 7.90.19 ।।
explanation: Then, the greatly effulgent Mahadeva, being pleased, restored Ila to manhood, and having done so, disappeared.

shloka_text: निवृत्ते हयमेधे च गतश्चादर्शनं हरः । यथागतं द्विजाः सर्वे ह्यगच्छन्दीर्घदर्शिनः ।। 7.90.20 ।।
explanation: And when the horse sacrifice was concluded, Hara also disappeared. All the far-sighted twice-born ones departed just as they had arrived.

shloka_text: राजा तु बाह्लिमुत्सृज्य मध्यदेशे ह्यनुत्तमम् । निवेशयामास पुरं प्रतिष्ठानं यशस्करम् ।। 7.90.21 ।।
explanation: But the king, having abandoned Bāhli, established the unsurpassed and glorious city of Pratiṣṭhāna in the middle country.

shloka_text: शशबिन्दुश्च राजर्षिर्बाह्लिं पुरपुरञ्जयः । प्रतिष्ठाने इलो राजा प्रजापतिसुतो बली ।। 7.90.22 ।।
explanation: And Śaśabindu, the royal sage, Bāhli, Purapurañjaya; King Ila, the mighty son of Prajāpati, was in Pratiṣṭhāna.

shloka_text: स काले प्राप्तवाँल्लोकमिलो ब्राह्ममनुत्तमम् । ऐलः पुरूरवा राजा प्रतिष्ठानमवाप्तवान् ।। 7.90.23 ।।
explanation: Ila, in due course, attained the unsurpassed Brahminic world. King Pururavas, the son of Ila, attained Pratishthana.

shloka_text: ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रभावः पुरुषर्षभौ । स्त्रीभूतः पौरुषं लेभे यच्चान्यदपि दुर्लभम् ।। 7.90.24 ।।
explanation: Such indeed is the power of the Ashwamedha, O best among men. One who had become a woman regained his manhood, and whatever else is difficult to obtain.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः ।। 90 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninetieth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: एतदाख्याय काकुत्स्थो भ्रातृभ्याममितप्रभः । लक्ष्मणं पुनरेवाह धर्मयुक्तमिदं वचः ।। 7.91.1 ।।
explanation: Having narrated this to his two brothers, Kakutstha of immeasurable splendor again spoke these righteous words to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च जाबालिमथ कश्यपम् । द्विजांश्च सर्वप्रवरानश्वमेधपुरस्कृतान् ।। 7.91.2 ।।
explanation: Vasistha, Vamadeva, Jabali, and Kashyapa, and all the foremost Brahmins who were honored at the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: एतान्सर्वान्समानीय मन्त्रयित्वा च लक्ष्मण । हयं लक्षणसम्पन्नं विमोक्ष्यामि समाधिना ।। 7.91.3 ।।
explanation: Having assembled all these and deliberated, O Lakshmana, I shall release the horse endowed with auspicious marks, with due ceremony.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा त्वरितविक्रमः । द्विजान्सर्वान्समाहूय दर्शयामास राघवम् ।। 7.91.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words spoken by Rama, he, swift in action, summoned all the Brahmins and showed them Rama.

shloka_text: ते दृष्ट्वा देवसङ्काशं कृतपादाभिवन्दनम् । राघवं सुदुराधर्षमाशीर्भिः समपूजयन् ।। 7.91.5 ।।
explanation: They, having seen Rama, who was god-like, unassailable, and had performed obeisance at their feet, honored him with blessings.

shloka_text: प्राञ्जलिः स तदा भूत्वा राघवो द्विजसत्तमान् । आचचक्षे ऽश्वमेधस्य ह्यभिप्रायं महायशाः ।। 7.91.6 ।।
explanation: Then, the greatly renowned Rama, with folded hands, explained to the foremost Brahmins his intention regarding the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: ते तु रामस्य तच्छ्रुत्वा नमस्कृत्वा वृषध्वजम् । अश्वमेधं द्विजाः सर्वे पूजयन्ति स्म सर्वशः ।। 7.91.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard that from Rama, and having bowed down to Vrṣadhvaja (Shiva), all the twice-born (Brahmins) honored the Ashwamedha sacrifice in every way.

shloka_text: स तेषां द्विजमुख्यानां वाक्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् । अश्वमेधाश्रितं श्रुत्वा भृशं प्रीतो ऽभवत्तदा ।। 7.91.8 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard the extraordinary statement of those chief Brahmins concerning the Ashwamedha, he became exceedingly pleased.

shloka_text: विज्ञाय कर्म तत्तेषां रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् । प्रेषयस्व द्रुतं दूतान् सुग्रीवाय महात्मने ।। 7.91.9 ।।
explanation: Having understood their action, Rama said to Lakshmana: "Quickly send messengers to the great-souled Sugriva."

shloka_text: यथा महद्भिर्हरिभिर्बहुभिश्च वनौकसाम् । सार्धमागच्छ भद्रं ते ह्यनुभोक्तुं महोत्सवम् ।। 7.91.10 ।।
explanation: Come along with many great monkeys to enjoy the great festival of the forest dwellers. May good fortune be yours.

shloka_text: बिभीषणश्च रक्षोभिः कामगैर्बहुभिर्वृतः । अश्वमेधं महायज्ञमायात्वतुलविक्रमः ।। 7.91.11 ।।
explanation: And Bibhishana, of incomparable valor, surrounded by many Rakshasas who can move at will, should come to the great Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: राजानश्च महाभागा ये मे प्रियचिकीर्षवः । सानुगाः क्षिप्रमायान्तु यज्ञं द्रष्टुमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.91.12 ।।
explanation: And the illustrious kings who wish to please me, let them quickly come with their followers to see this unsurpassed sacrifice.

shloka_text: देशान्तरगता ये च द्विजा धर्मसमाहिताः । आमन्त्रयस्व तान्सर्वानश्वमेधाय लक्ष्मण ।। 7.91.13 ।।
explanation: O Lakshmana, invite all those Brahmins who have gone to other lands and are devoted to righteousness, for the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: ऋषयश्च महाबाहो आहूयन्तां तपोधनाः । देशान्तरगताः सर्वे सदाराश्च द्विजातयः । तथैव तालावचरास्तथैव नटनर्तकाः ।। 7.91.14 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, let the Rishis, whose wealth is austerity, be invited. And all the twice-born ones who have gone to other lands, along with their wives, should also be invited. Likewise, the musicians, and similarly, the actors and dancers.

shloka_text: यज्ञवाटश्च सुमहान्गोमत्या नैमिशे वने । आज्ञाप्यतां महाबाहो तद्धि पुण्यमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.91.15 ।।
explanation: And let a very large sacrificial enclosure be arranged in the Naimisha forest, by the Gomati. O mighty-armed one, that indeed is an unsurpassed meritorious act.

shloka_text: शान्तयश्च महाबाहो प्रवर्त्यन्तां समन्ततः ।। 7.91.16 ।।
explanation: And let rites for peace be performed everywhere, O mighty-armed one.

shloka_text: शतशश्चापि धर्मज्ञाः क्रतुमुख्यमनुत्तमम् । अनुभूय महायज्ञं नैमिशे रघुनन्दन ।। 7.91.17 ।।
explanation: O Raghunandana, hundreds of righteous ones also, having performed the great and unsurpassed principal sacrifice in Naimisha.

shloka_text: तुष्टः पुष्टश्च सर्वो ऽसौ मानितश्च यथाविधि । प्रीतिं यास्यति धर्मज्ञ शीघ्रमामन्त्र्यतां जनः ।। 7.91.18 ।।
explanation: All of them, satisfied, well-nourished, and duly honored, will attain joy, O knower of dharma. Let the people be invited quickly.

shloka_text: शतं वाहसहस्राणां तण्डुलानां वपुष्मताम् । अयुतं तिलमुद्गानां प्रयात्वग्रे महाबल ।। 7.91.19 ।।
explanation: Let one hundred thousand loads of excellent rice, and ten thousand [loads] of sesame and mung beans, go forth, O mighty one.

shloka_text: चणकानां कुलित्थानां माषाणां लवणस्य च । अतो ऽनुरूपं स्नेहं च गन्धं सङ्क्षिप्तमेव च ।। 7.91.20 ।।
explanation: Of chickpeas, horse gram, black gram, and salt. And from these, suitable oil and spices, and that too in a small quantity.
