shloka_text: सुवर्णकोट्यो बहुला हिरण्यस्य शतोत्तराः । अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे समाधिना ।। 7.91.21 ।।
explanation: Let Bharata go forward with resolve, having placed in front numerous millions of gold coins and more than a hundred (units) of gold.

shloka_text: अन्तरा पण्यवीथ्यश्च सर्वे च नटनर्तकाः । सूदा नार्यश्च बहवो नित्यं यौवनशालिनः ।। 7.91.22 ।।
explanation: And within were market streets, and all the actors and dancers, cooks, and many women, always youthful.

shloka_text: भरतेन तु सार्धं ते यान्तु सैन्यानि चाग्रतः । नैगमा बलवृद्धाश्च द्विजाश्च सुसमाहिताः ।। 7.91.23 ।।
explanation: Let those armies go forth along with Bharata, and also the merchants, the strong and the aged, and the Brahmins, well-prepared.

shloka_text: कर्मान्तिकान्वर्धकिनः कोशाध्यक्षांश्च नैगमान् । मम मातऽस्तथा सर्वाः कुमारान्तःपुराणि च ।। 7.91.24 ।।
explanation: Workers, carpenters, treasurers, and merchants; and my mothers, and all the inner apartments of the princes.

shloka_text: काञ्चनीं मम पत्नीं च दीक्षायां ज्ञांश्च कर्मणि । अग्रतो भरतः कृत्वा गच्छत्वग्रे महायशाः ।। 7.91.25 ।।
explanation: Let the greatly renowned Bharata go ahead, having placed my golden wife and the kinsmen in front for the ritual of consecration.

shloka_text: उपकार्या महार्हाश्च पार्थिवानां महौजसाम् । सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महाबलः ।। 7.91.26 ।।
explanation: The mighty best among men commanded valuable provisions and services for the powerful kings and their followers.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 91 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-first chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Valmiki Ramayana, the original epic poem.

shloka_text: तत्सर्वमखिलेनाशु प्रस्थाप्य भरताग्रजः । हयं लक्षणसम्पन्नं कृष्णसारं मुमोच ह ।। 7.92.1 ।।
explanation: Having quickly dispatched all that completely, the elder brother of Bharata released a horse, endowed with auspicious marks and of black antelope color.

shloka_text: ऋत्विग्भिर्लक्ष्मणं सार्धमश्वतन्त्रे नियोज्य च । ततो ऽभ्यगच्छत्काकुत्स्थः सह सैन्येन नैमिशम् ।। 7.92.2 ।।
explanation: Having appointed Lakshmana along with the priests to the task of the horse (sacrifice), Kakutstha then proceeded to Naimisha with his army.

shloka_text: यज्ञवाटं महाबाहुर्दृष्ट्वा परममद्भुतम् । प्रबर्षमतुलं लेभे श्रीमानिति वचो ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.92.3 ।।
explanation: Having seen the exceedingly wonderful sacrificial enclosure, the mighty-armed one received an incomparable shower. Thereupon, the glorious one spoke these words.

shloka_text: नैमिषे वसतस्तस्य सर्व एव नराधिपाः । आनिन्युरुपहारांश्च तान्रामः प्रत्यपूजयत् ।। 7.92.4 ।।
explanation: While he resided in Naimiṣa, all the kings brought him gifts, and Rama honored them in return.

shloka_text: उपकार्या महार्हाश्च पार्थिवानां महात्मनाम् । सानुगानां नरश्रेष्ठो व्यादिदेश महामतिः ।। 7.92.5 ।।
explanation: The great-minded best among men commanded splendid provisions and services for the noble kings and their retinues.

shloka_text: अन्नपानानि वस्त्राणि सानुगानां महात्मनाम् । भरतः सन्ददावाशु शत्रुघ्नसहितस्तदा ।। 7.92.6 ।।
explanation: Then Bharata, accompanied by Shatrughna, quickly gave food, drinks, and clothes to the great souls and their followers.

shloka_text: वानराश्च महात्मानः सुग्रीवसहितास्तदा । विप्राणां प्रणताः सर्वे चक्रिरे परिवेषणम् ।। 7.92.7 ।।
explanation: Then, all the great-souled Vanaras, along with Sugriva, bowed down and served the Brahmins.

shloka_text: बिभीषणश्च रक्षोभिर्बहुभिः स्रग्विभिर्वृतः । ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां पूजां चक्रे महात्मनाम् ।। 7.92.8 ।।
explanation: Bibhishana, surrounded by many Rakshasas adorned with garlands, performed worship of the great-souled Rishis of severe penance.

shloka_text: एवं सुविहितो यज्ञो हयमेधो ऽभ्यवर्तत । लक्ष्मणेनागुप्ता च हयचर्या प्रवर्तत । ईदृशं राजसिंहस्य यज्ञप्रवरमुत्तमम् ।। 7.92.9 ।।
explanation: Thus, the well-arranged Ashvamedha sacrifice was performed. And the horse's wandering proceeded, unguarded by Lakshmana. Such was the best and foremost sacrifice of the lion among kings.

shloka_text: नान्यः शब्दो ऽभवत्तत्र हयमेधे महात्मनः । छन्दतो देहि विस्रब्धो यावत्तुष्यन्ति याचकाः ।। 7.92.10 ।।
explanation: No other word was heard there at the great-souled one's horse sacrifice: "Give as you please, confidently, until the supplicants are satisfied."

shloka_text: तावत्सर्वाणि दत्तानि क्रतुमध्ये महात्मनः । विविधानि च गौडानि खाण्डवानि तथैव च ।। 7.92.11 ।।
explanation: All those various things, from Gauda and Khandava, and likewise, were given to the great soul in the midst of the sacrifice.

shloka_text: न निस्सृतं भतत्योष्ठाद्वचनं यावदर्थिनाम् । तावद्वानररक्षोभिर्दत्तमेवाभ्यदृश्यत ।। 7.92.12 ।।
explanation: Before the words of the petitioners had even issued from their lips, it was seen that the monkeys and Rakshasas had already given what was desired.

shloka_text: न कश्चिन्मलिनस्तत्र दीनो वा ऽप्यथ कृर्शतः । तस्मिन्यज्ञवरे राज्ञो हृष्टपुष्टजनावृते ।। 7.92.13 ।।
explanation: In that excellent sacrifice of the king, which was filled with happy and well-nourished people, there was no one who was dirty, poor, or emaciated.

shloka_text: ये च तत्र महात्मानो मुनयश्चिरजीविनः । नास्मरंस्तादृशं यज्ञं नाप्यासीत् स कदाचन ।। 7.92.14 ।।
explanation: And those great souls and long-lived sages there did not remember such a sacrifice, nor did it ever exist.

shloka_text: यः कृत्यवान्सुवर्णेन सुवर्णं लभते स्म सः । वित्तार्थी लभते वित्तं रत्नार्थी रत्नमेव च ।। 7.92.15 ।।
explanation: He who is engaged with gold obtains gold; one who desires wealth obtains wealth, and one who desires jewels obtains jewels indeed.

shloka_text: रजतानां सुवर्णानामश्मनामथ वाससाम् । अनिशं दीयमानानां राशिः समुपदृश्यते ।। 7.92.16 ।।
explanation: A heap of silver, gold, gems, and garments, constantly being given, is seen.

shloka_text: न शक्रस्य धनेशस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य वा । ईदृशो दृष्टपूर्वो न एवमूचुस्तपोधनाः ।। 7.92.17 ।।
explanation: Such a thing has not been seen before, not even by Indra, Kubera, Yama, or Varuna. Thus spoke the ascetics.

shloka_text: सर्वत्र वानरास्तस्थुः सर्वत्रैव च राक्षसाः । वासोधनान्नमर्थिभ्यः पूर्णहस्ता ददुर्भृशम् ।। 7.92.18 ।।
explanation: Monkeys were present everywhere, and Rākṣasas too were everywhere. With full hands, they generously gave clothes, wealth, and food to the supplicants.

shloka_text: ईदृशो राजसिंहस्य यज्ञः सर्वगुणान्वितः । संवत्सरमथो साग्रं वर्तते न च हीयते ।। 7.92.19 ।।
explanation: Such a sacrifice of the king-lion, endowed with all virtues, continues for more than a year and does not diminish.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्विनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 92 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-second chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: वर्तमाने तथाभूते यज्ञे च परमाद्भुते । सशिष्य आजगामाशु वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.93.1 ।।
explanation: While that exceedingly wonderful sacrifice was thus going on, Valmiki, the foremost among sages, quickly arrived with his disciples.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा दिव्यसङ्काशं यज्ञमद्भुतदर्शनम् । एकान्ते ऋषिवाटानां चकार उटजाञ्छुभान् ।। 7.93.2 ।।
explanation: Having seen the divine-like sacrifice, which was wonderful to behold, he built auspicious huts in a secluded place among the hermitages of the sages.

shloka_text: शकटांश्च बहून्पूर्णान्फलमूलैश्च शोभनान् । वाल्मीकिवाटे रुचिरे स्थापयन्नविदूरतः ।। 7.93.3 ।।
explanation: And many beautiful carts, full of fruits and roots, were placed nearby in the charming hermitage of Valmiki.

shloka_text: आसीत्सुपूजितो राज्ञा मुनिभिश्च महात्मभिः । वाल्मीकिः सुमहातेजा न्यवसत्परमात्मवान् ।। 7.93.4 ।।
explanation: Valmiki, of great splendor and highly spiritual, resided there, greatly honored by the king and by the great-souled sages.

shloka_text: स शिष्यावब्रवीद्धृष्टौ युवां गत्वा समाहितौ । कृत्स्नं रामायणं काव्यं गायेथां परया मुदा ।। 7.93.5 ।।
explanation: He spoke to the two disciples: "You two, confident and attentive, go and sing the entire epic poem Ramayana with great delight."

shloka_text: ऋषिवाटेषु पुण्येषु ब्राह्मणावसथेषु च । रथ्यासु राजमार्गेषु पार्थिवानां गृहेषु च ।। 7.93.6 ।।
explanation: In the sacred hermitages of sages, and in the dwellings of Brahmins, in the streets, on the royal highways, and in the houses of kings.

shloka_text: रामस्य भवनद्वारि यत्र कर्म च कुर्वते । ऋत्विजामग्रतश्चैव तत्र गेयं विशेषतः ।। 7.93.7 ।।
explanation: Where rituals are performed at the door of Rama's palace, and indeed in front of the priests, there it should be sung especially.

shloka_text: इमानि च फलान्यत्र स्वादूनि विविधानि च । जातानि पर्वताग्रेषु चास्वाद्यास्वाद्य गायताम् ।। 7.93.8 ।।
explanation: And here are these delicious and various fruits, grown on the mountain peaks; and having tasted them repeatedly, let them sing.

shloka_text: न यास्यथः श्रमं वत्सौ भक्षयित्वा फलानि वै । मूलानि च सुमृष्टानि नगराद्बहिरास्यथः ।। 7.93.9 ।।
explanation: O sons, you two will not experience fatigue after eating delicious fruits and roots. You two will stay outside the city.

shloka_text: यदि शब्दापयेद्रामः श्रवणाय महीपतिः । ऋषीणामुपविष्टानां ततो गेयं प्रवर्तताम् ।। 7.93.10 ।।
explanation: If King Rama summons (us) to listen, (and) the sages are seated, then let the singing commence.

shloka_text: दिवसे विंशतिः सर्गा गेया मधुरया गिरा । प्रमाणैर्बहुभिस्तत्र यथोद्दिष्टा मया पुरा ।। 7.93.11 ।।
explanation: In a day, twenty cantos should be recited with a sweet voice, with many details, as previously instructed by me.

shloka_text: लोभश्चापि न कर्तव्यः स्वल्पो ऽपि धनकाङ्क्षया । किं धनेनाश्रमस्थानां फलमूलोपजीविना ।। 7.93.12 ।।
explanation: One should not be greedy, even a little, for the sake of wealth. What is the use of wealth for those living in hermitages, who subsist on fruits and roots?

shloka_text: यदि पृच्छेत्स काकुत्स्थो युवां कस्येति दारकौ । आवां वाल्मीकिशिष्यौ स्वो ब्रूतमेवं नराधिपम् ।। 7.93.13 ।।
explanation: If Kakutstha asks, 'Whose boys are you two?' then you two should tell the king thus: 'We are disciples of Valmiki.'

shloka_text: इमास्तन्त्रीः सुमधुराः स्थानं वा ऽपूर्वदर्शनम् । मूर्च्छयित्वा सुमधुरं गायतां विगतज्वरौ ।। 7.93.14 ।।
explanation: Let the two, free from distress, sing very sweetly, having tuned these very sweet strings, or (having seen) this unprecedented sight."

shloka_text: आदिप्रभृति गेयं स्यान्न चावज्ञाय पार्थिवम् । पिता हि सर्वभूतानां राजा भविति धर्मतः ।। 7.93.15 ।।
explanation: From the very beginning, it should be sung, and the king should not be disrespected. For indeed, the king is the father of all beings by dharma.

shloka_text: तद्युवां हृष्टमनसौ श्वः प्रभाते समास्थितौ । गायेथां मधुरं गेयं तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितम् ।। 7.93.16 ।।
explanation: Therefore, you two, with joyful hearts, tomorrow morning, having taken your seats, should sing a sweet song accompanied by string instruments and rhythm.

shloka_text: इति सन्दिश्य बहुशो मुनिः प्राचेतसस्तदा । वाल्मीकिः परमोदारस्तूष्णीमासीन्महायशाः ।। 7.93.17 ।।
explanation: Thus having instructed repeatedly, the greatly renowned sage Valmiki, the most noble son of Pracetas, then became silent.

shloka_text: सन्दिष्टौ मुनिना तेन तावुभौ मैथिलीसुतौ । तथैव करवावेति निर्जग्मतुररिन्दमौ ।। 7.93.18 ।।
explanation: Instructed by that sage, those two sons of Maithili, the destroyers of enemies, departed, saying, "We shall do just so."

shloka_text: तामद्भुतां तौ हृदये कुमारौ निवेश्य वाणीमृषिभाषितां तदा । समुत्सुकौ तौ सममूषतुर्निशां यथा ऽश्विनौ भार्गवनीतिसंहिताम् ।। 7.93.19 ।।
explanation: Then, those two princes, having placed those wonderful words spoken by the sage in their hearts, spent the night eagerly, just as the two Ashvins (would spend the night, having absorbed) the code of conduct taught by Bhargava

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 93 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-third chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: तौ रजन्यां प्रभातायां स्नातौ हुतहुताशनौ । यथोक्तमृषिणा पूर्वं सर्वं तत्रोपगायताम् ।। 7.94.1 ।।
explanation: When the night dawned, those two, having bathed and offered oblations to the fire, recited all that had been previously spoken by the sage.

shloka_text: तां स शुश्राव काकुत्स्थः पूर्वाचार्यविजिर्मिताम् । अपूर्वां पाठ्यजातिं च गेयेन समलङ्कृताम् ।। 7.94.2 ।।
explanation: Kakutstha heard that, composed by ancient teachers, an unprecedented form of recitation, adorned with melody.

shloka_text: प्रमाणैर्बहुभिर्बद्धां तन्त्रीलयसमन्विताम् । बालाभ्यां राघवः श्रुत्वा कौतूहलपरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.94.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard [it], meticulously composed with many standards and accompanied by stringed instruments and rhythm, from the two boys, Rama became filled with curiosity.

shloka_text: अथ कर्मान्तरे राजा समाहूय महामुनीन् । पार्थिवांश्च नरव्याघ्रः पण्डितान्नैगमांस्तथा ।। 7.94.4 ।।
explanation: Then, during another task, the king, that tiger among men, having summoned the great sages, and kings, and learned men, and also the merchants.

shloka_text: पौराणिकाञ्छब्दविदो ये च वृद्धा द्विजातयः । स्वराणां लक्षणज्ञांश्च उत्सुकान्द्विजसत्तमान् ।। 7.94.5 ।।
explanation: Pauranikas, those who know words, and those elderly twice-born, and those who know the characteristics of accents, and the eager best among the twice-born.

shloka_text: लक्षणज्ञांश्च गान्धर्वान्नैगमांश्च विशेषतः । पादाक्षरसमासज्ञांश्छन्दःसु परिनिष्ठितान् ।। 7.94.6 ।।
explanation: And experts in characteristics, and in Gandharva arts, and especially in traditional lore; and those thoroughly proficient in prosody, knowing its feet, syllables, and compounds.

shloka_text: कलामात्राविशेषज्ञाञ्ज्योतिषे च परं गतान् । क्रियाकल्पविदश्चैव तथा कार्यविदो जनान् ।। 7.94.7 ।।
explanation: Experts in even the minutest distinctions, who have attained the highest in astronomy, and indeed those who know the rules of actions, and similarly, experts in practical affairs.

shloka_text: भाषाज्ञानिङ्गितज्ञांश्च नैगमांश्चाप्यशेषतः । हेतूपचारकुशलान् वचने चापि हैतुकान् ।। 7.94.8 ।।
explanation: Knowers of languages and gestures, and all citizens, skilled in reasoning and application, and also logicians in speech.

shloka_text: छन्दोविदः पुराणज्ञान्वैदिकान्द्विजसत्तमान् । चित्रज्ञान्वृत्तसूत्रज्ञान्गीतनृत्यविशारदान् ।। 7.94.9 ।।
explanation: Experts in prosody, knowers of the Puranas, Vedic scholars, the foremost among the twice-born, knowers of painting, those skilled in metrics and aphorisms, and experts in singing and dancing.

shloka_text: शास्त्रज्ञान्नीतिनिपुणान्वेदान्तार्थप्रबोधकान् । एतान्सर्वान्समानीय गातारौ समवेशयत् ।। 7.94.10 ।।
explanation: Having assembled all these who were knowledgeable in the scriptures, skilled in policy, and expounders of the meaning of Vedanta, he seated the two singers.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा मुनिगणाः सर्वे पार्थिवाश्च महौजसः । पिबन्त इव चक्षुर्भ्यां राजानं गायकौ च तौ ।। 7.94.11 ।।
explanation: All the groups of sages and the mighty kings, having seen, were as if drinking with their eyes the king and those two singers.

shloka_text: ऊचुः परस्परं चेदं सर्व एव समन्ततः । उभौ रामस्य सदृशौ बिम्बाद्बिम्बमिवोत्थितौ ।। 7.94.12 ।।
explanation: And all of them, from all sides, said this to each other: "Both are like Rama, as if one image has emerged from another image."

shloka_text: जटिलौ यदि न स्यातां न वल्कलधरौ यदि । विशेषं नाधिगच्छामो गायतो राघवस्य च ।। 7.94.13 ।।
explanation: If they were not with matted hair, and if they were not wearing bark garments, we would not perceive any distinction between the two singers and Rama.

shloka_text: तेषां संवदतामेवं श्रोतऽणां हर्षवर्धनम् । गेयं प्रचक्रतुस्तत्र तावुभौ मुनिदारकौ ।। 7.94.14 ।।
explanation: While they were thus conversing, those two sons of the sage began to sing there, a song that delighted the listeners.

shloka_text: ततः प्रवृत्तं मधुरं गान्धर्वमतिमानुषम् । न च तृप्तिं ययुः सर्वे श्रोतारो गानसम्पदा ।। 7.94.15 ।।
explanation: Then, sweet, superhuman music commenced. All the listeners were not satiated by the richness of the singing.

shloka_text: प्रवृत्तमादितः पूर्वसर्गं नारददर्शितम् । ततः प्रभृति सर्गांश्च यावद्विंशत्यगायताम् ।। 7.94.16 ।।
explanation: The previous creation, which began from the very first and was revealed by Narada, and from then onwards, the chapters up to the twentieth, were narrated.

shloka_text: ततो ऽपराह्णसमये राघवः समभाषत । श्रुत्वा विंशतिसर्गांस्तान्भ्रातरं भ्रातृवत्सलः ।। 7.94.17 ।।
explanation: Then, in the afternoon, Rama, who was affectionate towards his brother, spoke to his brother after hearing those twenty cantos.

shloka_text: अष्टादशसहस्राणि सुवर्णस्य महात्मनोः । प्रयच्छ शीघ्रं काकुत्स्थ यदन्यदभिकाङ्क्षितम् । ददौ शीघ्रं स काकुत्स्थो बालयोर्वै पृथक्पृथक् ।। 7.94.18 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, quickly give eighteen thousand [coins] of gold to the great souls, and whatever else is desired. He, Kakutstha, quickly gave [it] to the two boys, separately.

shloka_text: दीयमानं सुवर्णं तु नागृह्णीतां कुशीलवौ । ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ किमनेनेति विस्मितौ ।। 7.94.19 ।।
explanation: The two bards, however, did not accept the gold being offered. And the two great souls, astonished, said, "What is the use of this?"

shloka_text: वन्येन फलमूलेन निरतौ वनवासिनौ । सुवर्णेन हिरण्येन किं करिष्यावहे वने ।। 7.94.20 ।।
explanation: We, the forest dwellers, subsisting on wild fruits and roots, what shall we do with gold and riches in the forest?

shloka_text: तथा तयोः प्रब्रुवतोः कौतूहलसमन्विताः । श्रोतारश्चैव रामश्च सर्व एव सुविस्मिताः ।। 7.94.21 ।।
explanation: Thus, as those two spoke, all the listeners, filled with curiosity, and Rama himself, were greatly astonished.

shloka_text: तस्य चैवागमं रामः काव्यस्य श्रोतुमुत्सुकः । पप्रच्छ तौ महातेजास्तावुभौ मुनिदारकौ ।। 7.94.22 ।।
explanation: And the greatly effulgent Rama, eager to hear the story of that poem, asked those two sons of the sage.

shloka_text: किम्प्रमाणमिदं काव्यं का प्रतिष्ठा महात्मनः । कर्ता काव्यस्य महतः क्व चासौ मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.94.23 ।।
explanation: What is the authority of this poem? What is the reputation of the great soul? And where is that eminent sage, the author of this great poem?

shloka_text: पृच्छन्तं राघवं वाक्यमूचतुर्मुनिदारकौ ।। 7.94.24 ।।
explanation: The two sons of the sage spoke words to Rama, who was asking.

shloka_text: वाल्मीकिर्भगवान्कर्ता सम्प्राप्तो यज्ञसंविधम् । येनेदं चरितं तुभ्यमशेषं सम्प्रदर्शितम् ।। 7.94.25 ।।
explanation: Valmiki, the divine author, having attained the knowledge of sacrifice, by whom this entire story has been completely revealed to you.

shloka_text: सन्निबद्धं हि श्लोकानां चतुर्विशत्सहस्रकम् । उपाख्यानशतं चैव भार्गवेण तपस्विना ।। 7.94.26 ।।
explanation: Twenty-four thousand verses and a hundred sub-stories were indeed composed by the ascetic Bhargava.

shloka_text: आदिप्रभृति वै राजन्पञ्चसर्गशतानि च । काण्डानि षट् कृतानीह सोत्तराणि महात्मना । कृतानि गुरुणास्माकमृषिणा चरितं तव ।। 7.94.27 ।।
explanation: O King, from the very beginning, five hundred sargas and six *kāṇḍas*, including the Uttara, have been composed here by the great soul. Your story has been composed by our guru, the sage.

shloka_text: प्रतिष्ठा ऽ ऽजीवितं यावत्तावत्सर्वस्य वर्तते ।। 7.94.28 ।।
explanation: As long as life exists, so long does the existence of all continue.

shloka_text: सोत्तराणि महात्मना । यदि बुद्धिः कृता राजञ्छ्रवणाय महारथ । कर्मान्तरे क्षणीभूतस्तच्छृणुष्व सहानुजः ।। 7.94.29 ।।
explanation: O King, O great charioteer, if your mind is made up for listening, having found a moment during a pause in action, then listen to the replies of the great soul, along with your younger brother(s).

shloka_text: बाढमित्यब्रवीद्रामस्तौ चानुज्ञाप्य राघवम् । प्रहृष्टौ जग्मतुः स्थानं यत्रास्ते मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.94.30 ।।
explanation: Rama said, "Yes." And they, having taken leave of Raghava, greatly delighted, went to the place where the foremost of sages resided.

shloka_text: रामो ऽपि मुनिभिः सार्धं पार्थिवैश्च महात्मभिः । श्रुत्वा तद्गीतिमाधुर्यं कर्मशालामुपागमत् ।। 7.94.31 ।।
explanation: Rama also, along with the great-souled sages and kings, having heard the sweetness of their song, went to the performance hall.

shloka_text: शुश्राव तत्ताललयोपपन्नं सर्गान्वितं स स्वरशब्दयुक्तम् । तन्त्रीलयव्यञ्जनयोगयुक्तं कुशीलवाभ्यां परिगीयमानम् ।। 7.94.32 ।।
explanation: He heard that, endowed with rhythm and tempo, accompanied by chapters, filled with musical notes and words, and characterized by the harmony of string instruments and clear articulation, as it was being sung by the two bards.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्नवतितमः सर्गः ।। 94 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the ninety-fourth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: रामो बहून्यहान्येवं तद्गीतं परमं शुभम् । शुश्राव मुनिभिः सार्धं पार्थिवैः सह वानरैः ।। 7.95.1 ।।
explanation: For many days, Rama thus heard that supreme and auspicious song, along with sages, kings, and monkeys.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्गीते तु विज्ञाय सीतापुत्रौ कुशीलवौ । तस्याः परिषदो मध्ये रामो वचनमब्रवीत् । दूताञ्छुद्धसमाचारानाहूयात्ममनीषया ।। 7.95.2 ।।
explanation: Having recognized Kusha and Lava, the sons of Sita, during that song, Rama spoke words in the midst of that assembly, having called messengers of pure conduct by his own will.

shloka_text: मद्वचो ब्रूत गच्छध्वमितो भगवतो ऽन्तिकम् ।। 7.95.3 ।।
explanation: Go from here and speak my words to the Lord.

shloka_text: परिषदो मध्ये रामो वचनमब्रवीत् । यदि शुद्धसमाचारा यदि वा वीतकल्मषा । करोत्विहात्मनः शुद्धिमनुमान्य महामुनिम् ।। 7.95.4 ।।
explanation: Rama spoke words in the midst of the assembly: "If she is of pure conduct, or if she is sinless, let her perform her own purification here, having obtained the permission of the great sage."

shloka_text: छन्दं मुनेश्च विज्ञाय सीतायाश्च मनोगतम् । प्रत्ययं दातुकामायास्ततः शंसत मे लघु ।। 7.95.5 ।।
explanation: Having understood the will of the sage and the intention of Sita, who wishes to provide assurance, therefore tell me quickly.

shloka_text: श्वः प्रभाते तु शपथं मैथिली जनकात्मजा । करोतु परिषन्मध्ये शोधनार्थं ममैव च ।। 7.95.6 ।।
explanation: Tomorrow morning, Maithili, Janaka's daughter, should take an oath in the assembly for my purification.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु ऱागवस्यैतद्वचः परममद्भुतम् । दूताः सम्प्रययुर्बाटं यत्रास्ते मुनिपुङ्गवः ।। 7.95.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard these exceedingly wonderful words of Rama, the messengers proceeded to the hermitage where the foremost of sages dwells.

shloka_text: ते प्रणम्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तममितप्रभम् । ऊचुस्ते रामवाक्यानि मृदूनि मधुराणि च ।। 7.95.8 ।।
explanation: They, having bowed down to the great soul, who was blazing with immeasurable splendor, spoke Rama's words, which were gentle and sweet.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्व्याहृतं श्रुत्वा रामस्य च मनोगतम् । विज्ञाय सुमहातेजा मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.95.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard their words, and having understood what was in Rama's mind, the greatly effulgent sage then spoke.

shloka_text: एवं भवतु भद्रं वो यथा वदति राघवः । तथा करिष्यते सीता दैवतं हि पतिः स्त्रियाः ।। 7.95.10 ।।
explanation: Let it be so, welfare to you. As Rama says, so will Sita do, for indeed, the husband is the deity for a woman.

shloka_text: तथोक्ता मुनिना सर्वे राजदूता महौजसम् । प्रत्येत्य राघवं क्षिप्रं मुनिवाक्यं बभाषिरे ।। 7.95.11 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the sage, all the royal messengers quickly returned to the greatly powerful Rama and narrated the sage's words.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहृष्टः काकुत्स्थः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं महात्मनः । ऋषींस्तत्र समेतांश्च राज्ञश्चैवाभ्यभाषत ।। 7.95.12 ।।
explanation: Then, Kakutstha, greatly pleased after hearing the words of the great soul, addressed the sages assembled there and also the kings.

shloka_text: भगवन्तः सशिष्या वै सानुगाश्च नराधिपाः । पश्यन्तु सीताशपथं यश्चैवान्यो ऽपि काङ्क्षते ।। 7.95.13 ।।
explanation: Let the revered ones with their disciples, and the kings with their attendants, witness Sita's oath, and also anyone else who desires to.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः । सर्वेषामृषिमुख्यानां साधुवादो महानभूत् ।। 7.95.14 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech of the great-souled Rama, a great applause arose from all the chief sages.

shloka_text: राजानश्च महात्मानः प्रशंसन्ति स्म राघवम् । उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ त्वय्येव भुवि नान्यतः ।। 7.95.15 ।।
explanation: Kings and great-souled ones praised Rama. O best among men, it is fitting in you alone on earth, not elsewhere.

shloka_text: एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा श्वोभूत इति राघवः । विसर्जयामास तदा सर्वांस्ताञ्छत्रुसूदनः ।। 7.95.16 ।।
explanation: Having thus made a firm decision, saying, "Let it be tomorrow," then Rama, the destroyer of enemies, dismissed all of them.

shloka_text: इति सम्प्रविचार्य राजसिंहः श्वोभूते शपथस्य निश्चयं वै । विससर्ज मुनीन्नृपांश्च सर्वान्स महात्मा महतो महानुभावः ।। 7.95.17 ।।
explanation: Thus, having thoroughly deliberated on the certainty of the oath for the morrow, that great-souled, illustrious king, a lion among kings, dismissed all the sages and kings.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चनवतितमः सर्ग ।। 95 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Srimad Ramayana, the original epic by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the ninety-fifth chapter.

shloka_text: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां यज्ञवाटगतो नृपः । ऋषीन्सर्वान्महातेजाः शब्दापयति राघवः ।। 7.96.1 ।।
explanation: When that night had dawned, King Rama, of great splendor, having gone to the sacrificial enclosure, summoned all the sages.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठो वामदेवश्च जाबालिरथ काश्यपः । विश्वामित्रो दीर्घतपा दुर्वासाश्च महातपाः ।। 7.96.2 ।।
explanation: Vasistha, Vamadeva, Jabali, and Kashyapa, Vishvamitra, Dirghatapas, and Durvasa, and Mahatapas.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्यो ऽपि तथा शक्तिर्भार्गवश्चैव वामनः । मार्कण्डेयश्च दीर्घायुर्मौद्गल्यश्च महायशाः ।। 7.96.3 ।।
explanation: Pulastya also, and similarly Shakti, and Bhargava, and Vamana, and Markandeya the long-lived, and Maudgalya the greatly renowned.

shloka_text: गर्गश्च च्यवनश्चैव शतानन्दश्च धर्मवित् । भरद्वाजश्च तेजस्वी ह्यग्निपुत्रश्च सुप्रभः ।। 7.96.4 ।।
explanation: Garga, and Cyavana also, and Śatānanda, the knower of dharma; and Bharadvāja, the radiant; and indeed the son of Agni, the very brilliant.

shloka_text: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव गौतमश्च महायशाः । कात्यायनः सुयज्ञश्च ह्यगस्त्यस्तपसां निधिः ।। 7.96.5 ।।
explanation: Narada, Parvata, and Gautama, the greatly renowned; Katyayana, Suyajna, and Agastya, the repository of austerities.

shloka_text: एते चान्ये च बहवो मुनयः संशितव्रताः । कौतूहलसमाविष्टाः सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.96.6 ।।
explanation: These and many other sages of strict vows, all of them filled with curiosity, assembled.

shloka_text: राक्षसाश्च महावीर्या वानराश्च महाबलाः । सर्व एव समाजग्मुर्महात्मानः कुतूहलात् ।। 7.96.7 ।।
explanation: The greatly valorous Rākṣasas and the greatly powerful Vānaras, all of them, the great-souled ones, assembled out of curiosity.

shloka_text: क्षत्रिया ये च शूद्राश्च वैश्याश्चैव सहस्रशः । नानादेशगताश्चैव ब्राह्मणाः संशितव्रताः ।। 7.96.8 ।।
explanation: Kshatriyas, and Shudras, and Vaishyas, indeed by thousands; and also Brahmins of firm vows who had come from various countries.

shloka_text: ज्ञाननिष्ठाः कर्मनिष्ठाः योगनिष्ठास्तथापरे । सीताशपथवीक्षार्थं सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.96.9 ।।
explanation: Those firm in knowledge, those firm in action, and others firm in yoga, all had gathered to witness Sita's oath.

shloka_text: तदा समागतं सर्वमश्मभूतमिवाचलम् । श्रुत्वा मुनिवरस्तूर्णं ससीतः समुपागमत् ।। 7.96.10 ।।
explanation: Then, having heard that all had become like unmoving stone, the great sage quickly came with Sita.

shloka_text: तमृषिं पृष्ठतः सीता त्वन्वगच्छदवाङ्मुखी । कृताञ्जलिर्बाष्पगला कृत्वा रामं मनोगतम् ।। 7.96.11 ।।
explanation: Sita, with downcast face, followed that sage from behind. With folded hands and her throat choked with tears, she kept Rama in her mind.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा श्रुतिमिवायान्तीं ब्रह्माणमनुगामिनीम् । वाल्मीकेः पृष्ठतः सीतां साधुवादो महानभूत् ।। 7.96.12 ।।
explanation: Having seen Sita, coming from behind Valmiki, like a Shruti (Vedic revelation) approaching and following Brahma, a great acclamation arose.

shloka_text: ततो हलहलाशब्दः सर्वेषामेवमाबभौ । दुःखजन्मविशालेन शोकेनाकुलितात्मनाम् ।। 7.96.13 ।।
explanation: Then a tumultuous sound arose from all, whose minds were agitated by the immense sorrow that had come into being.

shloka_text: साधु रामेति केचित्तु साधु सीतेति चापरे । उभावेव च तत्रान्ये प्रेक्षकाः सम्प्रचुक्रुशुः ।। 7.96.14 ।।
explanation: Some indeed shouted, 'Excellent, Rama!', and others, 'Excellent, Sita!'. And still others among the spectators loudly acclaimed, 'Both of them!'

shloka_text: ततो मध्ये जनौघस्य प्रविश्य मुनिपुङ्गवः । सीतासहायो वाल्मीकिरिति होवाच राघवम् ।। 7.96.15 ।।
explanation: Then, having entered the midst of the crowd of people, Valmiki, the foremost among sages, accompanied by Sita, thus spoke to Rama.

shloka_text: इयं दाशरथे सीता सुव्रता धर्मचारिणी । अपवादैः परित्यक्ता ममाश्रमसमीपतः ।। 7.96.16 ।।
explanation: O son of Dasaratha, this Sita, virtuous and devoted to dharma, was abandoned near my hermitage due to public slanders.

shloka_text: लोकापवादभीतस्य तव राम महाव्रत । प्रत्ययं दास्यते सीता तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।। 7.96.17 ।।
explanation: O Rama, O greatly vowed one, for you who are afraid of public scandal, Sita will give proof. You ought to permit that.

shloka_text: इमौ तु जानकीपुत्रावुभौ च यमजातकौ । सुतौ तवैव दुर्धर्षौ सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ।। 7.96.18 ।।
explanation: These two are the sons of Janaki, both born as twins. They are indeed your own unconquerable sons. I speak this truth to you.

shloka_text: प्रचेतसो ऽहं दशमः पुत्रो राघवनन्दन । न स्मराम्यनृतं वाक्यमिमौ तु तव पुत्रकौ ।। 7.96.19 ।।
explanation: I am the tenth son of Pracetas, O delight of Raghu. I do not recall speaking any falsehood; these two are indeed your sons.

shloka_text: बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तपश्चर्या मया कृता । नोपाश्नीयां फलं तस्या दुष्टेयं यदि मैथिली ।। 7.96.20 ।।
explanation: I have performed penance for many thousands of years. I would not partake of its fruit if this Maithili is wicked.

shloka_text: मनसा कर्मणा वाचा भूतपूर्वं न किल्बिषम् । तस्याः फलमुपाश्नीयामपापा मैथिली यदि ।। 7.96.21 ।।
explanation: If Maithili is sinless, and no sin has ever been committed by me in thought, word, or deed, then may I partake of the fruit of that.

shloka_text: अहं पञ्चसु भूतेषु मनष्षष्ठेषु राघव । विचिन्त्य सीतां शुद्धेति जग्राह वननिर्झरे ।। 7.96.22 ।।
explanation: O Raghava, I, who am (composed) of the five elements with the mind as the sixth, having considered Sita as pure, accepted her in the forest stream.

shloka_text: इयं शुद्धसमाचारा अपापा पतिदेवता । लोकापवादभीतस्य प्रत्ययं तव दास्यति ।। 7.96.23 ।।
explanation: This woman, of pure conduct, sinless, and devoted to her husband, will give you proof, as you are afraid of public scandal.

shloka_text: तस्मादियं नरवरात्मज शुद्धभावा दिव्येन दृष्टिविषयेण तदा प्रविष्टा । लोकापवादकलुषीकृतचेतसा या त्यक्ता त्वया प्रियतमा विदिता ऽपि शुद्धा ।। 7.96.24 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O son of the best of men, this pure-hearted one, who then entered the realm of divine vision, was abandoned by you, whose mind was defiled by public slander, even though she was your dearest and known to be

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षण्णवतितमः सर्गः ।। 96 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-sixth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by a sage.

shloka_text: वाल्मीकिनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः प्रत्यभाषत । प्राञ्जलिर्जगतो मध्ये दृष्ट्वा तां वरवर्णिनीम् ।। 7.97.1 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Valmiki, Rama, having seen that beautiful lady amidst the people, replied with folded hands.

shloka_text: एवमेतन्महाभाग यथा वदसि धर्मवित् । प्रत्ययस्तु मम ब्रह्मंस्तव वाक्यैरकल्मषैः ।। 7.97.2 ।।
explanation: O highly esteemed one, O knower of Dharma, this is indeed as you say. My conviction, O Brahmana, is from your faultless words.

shloka_text: प्रत्ययस्तु पुरा वृत्तो वैदेह्याः सुरसन्निधौ । शपथस्तु कृतस्तत्र तेन वेश्म प्रवेशिता । लोकापवादो बलवान्येन त्यक्ता हि मैथिली ।। 7.97.3 ।।
explanation: Her purity was indeed proven before the gods in the past. An oath was taken there, and by him, she was admitted into the home. But the public scandal was powerful, due to which Maithili was indeed abandoned.

shloka_text: सेयं लोकभयाद्ब्रह्मन्नपापेत्यभिजानता । परित्यक्ता मया सीता तद्भावन्क्षन्तुमर्हति ।। 7.97.4 ।।
explanation: O Brahman, though I knew this Sita to be innocent, she was abandoned by me due to fear of the people. Therefore, you ought to forgive (me for) that.

shloka_text: जानामि चेमौ पुत्रौ मे यमजातौ कुशीलवौ । शुद्धायां जगतो मध्ये मैथिल्यां प्रीतिरस्तु मे ।। 7.97.5 ।।
explanation: I know these two sons of mine, Kusha and Lava, born as twins. Let my affection be for Maithili, who is pure in the midst of the world.

shloka_text: अभिप्रायं तु विज्ञाय रामस्य सुरसत्तमाः । सीतायाः शपथे तस्मिन् महेन्द्राद्या महौजसः ।। 7.97.6 ।।
explanation: Having understood Rama's intention regarding that oath of Sita, the best among the gods, led by Mahendra, who were of great power,

shloka_text: पितामहं पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.97.7 ।।
explanation: All of them assembled, with the grandfather at the forefront.

shloka_text: आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा ह्यश्विनौ समरुद्गणाः । गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.97.8 ।।
explanation: The Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ashvins along with the Marut hosts, and the Gandharvas and Apsaras, all of them indeed assembled.

shloka_text: साध्याश्च विश्वेदेवाश्च सर्वे च परमर्षयः । नागाः सुपर्णाः सिद्धाश्च ते सर्वे हृष्टमानसाः । सीताशपथसम्भ्रान्ताः सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.97.9 ।।
explanation: The Sādhyas and the Viśvedevas, and all the great sages; the Nāgas, Suparṇas, and Siddhas – all of them, with joyful minds, were stirred by Sita's oath, and all indeed assembled

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा देवानृषींश्चैव राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । प्रत्ययो मे नरश्रेष्ठा ऋषिवाक्यैरकल्मषैः ।। 7.97.10 ।।
explanation: Having seen the gods and the sages, Rama again spoke: "O best among men, I have conviction through the faultless words of the sages."

shloka_text: शुद्धायां जगतो मध्ये वैदेह्यां प्रीतिरस्तु मे ।। 7.97.11 ।।
explanation: May my affection be for Vaidehi, the pure one in the world.

shloka_text: ततो वायुः शुभः पुण्यो दिव्यगन्धो मनोरमः । तज्जनौघं सुरश्रेष्ठो ह्लादयामास सर्वतः ।। 7.97.12 ।।
explanation: Then, the auspicious, sacred, divinely fragrant, and delightful wind, the best among gods, gladdened that multitude of people from all sides.

shloka_text: तदद्भुतमिवाचिन्त्यं निरैक्षन्त समागताः । मानवाः सर्वराष्ट्रेभ्यः पूर्वं कृतयुगे यथा ।। 7.97.13 ।।
explanation: Humans assembled from all nations beheld that, which was wonderful and inconceivable, just as they did formerly in the Krita Yuga.

shloka_text: सर्वान्समागतान्दृष्ट्वा सीता काषायवासिनी । अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमधोदृष्टिरवाङ्मुखी ।। 7.97.14 ।।
explanation: Having seen all who had assembled, Sita, clad in ochre robes, spoke with folded hands, her eyes downcast and face turned downwards.

shloka_text: यथा ऽहं राघवादन्यं मनसापि न चिन्तये । तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति ।। 7.97.15 ।।
explanation: Just as I do not think of anyone other than Raghava even in my mind, so may Goddess Madhavi grant me an opening.

shloka_text: मनसा कर्मणा वाचा यथा रामं समर्चये । तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति ।। 7.97.16 ।।
explanation: Just as I worship Rama with mind, action, and speech, so may Goddess Madhavi grant me a refuge.

shloka_text: यथैतत्सत्यमुक्तं मे वेद्मि रामात्परं न च । तथा मे माधवी देवी विवरं दातुमर्हति ।। 7.97.17 ।।
explanation: Just as this truth has been spoken by me, and I know no one superior to Rama, so may Goddess Madhavi grant me an opening.

shloka_text: तथा शपन्त्यां वैदेह्यां प्रादुरासीत्तदद्भुतम् । भूतलादुत्थितं दिव्यं सिंहासनमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.97.18 ।।
explanation: Thus, as Vaidehi was cursing, that wonder appeared: a divine, unsurpassed throne, risen from the ground.

shloka_text: ध्रियमाणं शिरोभिस्तु नागैरमितविक्रमैः । दिव्यं दिव्येन वपुषा दिव्यरत्नविभूषितैः ।। 7.97.19 ।।
explanation: Being held by the heads of Nāgas of immeasurable valor, who are adorned with divine jewels, a divine (object/being) with a divine body.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तु धरणी देवी बाहुभ्यां गृह्य मैथिलीम् । स्वागतेनाभिनन्द्यैनामासने चोपवेशयत् ।। 7.97.20 ।।
explanation: Then Goddess Earth, embracing Maithili with her arms, welcomed her and made her sit on a seat.

shloka_text: तामासनगतां दृष्ट्वा प्रविशन्तीं रसातलम् । पुष्पवृष्टिरविच्छिन्ना दिव्या सीतामवाकिरत् ।। 7.97.21 ।।
explanation: Having seen her, seated, entering the netherworld, an uninterrupted divine shower of flowers rained down upon Sita.

shloka_text: साधुकारश्च सुमहान्देवानां सहसोत्थितः । साधु साध्विति वै सीते यस्यास्ते शीलमीदृशम् ।। 7.97.22 ।।
explanation: A great acclamation suddenly arose from the gods, saying, "Excellent! Excellent, O Sita, whose character is of this kind!"

shloka_text: एवं बहुविधा वाचो ह्यन्तरिक्षगताः सुराः । व्याजह्रुर्हृष्टमनसो दृष्ट्वा सीताप्रवेशनम् ।। 7.97.23 ।।
explanation: Thus, the gods dwelling in the sky, with joyful minds, uttered various kinds of words upon seeing Sita's entry.

shloka_text: यज्ञवाटगताश्चापि मुनयः सर्व एव ते । राजानश्च नरव्याघ्रा विस्मयान्नोपरेमिरे ।। 7.97.24 ।।
explanation: All those sages who had come to the sacrificial enclosure, and the kings, the foremost of men, did not cease from their astonishment.

shloka_text: अन्तरिक्षे च भूमौ च सर्वे स्थावरजङ्गमाः । दानवाश्च महाकायाः पाताले पन्नगाधिपाः ।। 7.97.25 ।।
explanation: In the sky and on the earth, all stationary and moving beings, and the gigantic Danavas, and the lords of serpents in Patala.

shloka_text: केचिद्विनेदुः संहृष्टाः केचिद्ध्यानपरायणाः । केचिद्रामं निरीक्षन्ते केचित्सीतामचेतनाः ।। 7.97.26 ।।
explanation: Some roared with great delight, some were absorbed in contemplation. Some gazed at Rama, and some were stupefied at Sita.

shloka_text: सीताप्रवेशनं दृष्ट्वा तेषामासीत्समागमः । तन्मुहूर्तमिवात्यर्थं समं सम्मोहितं जगत् ।। 7.97.27 ।।
explanation: Upon seeing Sita's entry, they gathered. For that moment, as if intensely, the entire world was equally enchanted.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 97 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-seventh chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, composed by the sage.

shloka_text: रसातलं प्रविष्टायां वैदेह्यां सर्ववानराः । चुक्रुशुः साधु साध्वीति मुनयो रामसन्निधौ ।। 7.98.1 ।।
explanation: When Vaidehī entered the netherworld, all the monkeys and sages in the presence of Rama cried out, "Excellent! Excellent!"

shloka_text: दण्डकाष्ठमवष्टभ्य बाष्पव्याकुलितेक्षणः । अवाक्छिरा दीनमना रामो ह्यासीत्सुदुःखितः ।। 7.98.2 ।।
explanation: Leaning on a wooden staff, with eyes agitated by tears, his head bowed down, and his mind dejected, Rama was extremely sorrowful.

shloka_text: स रुदित्वा चिरं कालं बहुशो बाष्पमुत्सृजन् । क्रोधशोकसमाविष्टो रामो वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.3 ।।
explanation: Having cried for a long time, profusely shedding tears, Rama, overwhelmed by anger and sorrow, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अभूतपूर्वं शोकं मे मनः स्प्रष्टुमिवेच्छति । पश्यतो मे यथा नष्टा सीता श्रीरिव रूपिणी ।। 7.98.4 ।।
explanation: My mind desires to experience an unprecedented sorrow, just as Sita, like embodied Shri, was lost before my very eyes.

shloka_text: सा ऽदर्शनं पुरा सीता लङ्कापारे महोदधेः । ततश्चापि मयानीता किं पुनर्वसुधातलात् ।। 7.98.5 ।।
explanation: She, Sita, formerly disappeared beyond Lanka, across the great ocean. And even from there, she was brought by me. What then to say of (bringing her back) from the surface of the earth?

shloka_text: वसुधे देवि भवति सीता निर्यात्यतां मम । दर्शयिष्यामि वा रोषं यथा मामवगच्छसि ।। 7.98.6 ।।
explanation: O Goddess Earth, let Sita be brought forth to me. Otherwise, I will show my wrath, so that you may understand me.

shloka_text: कामं श्वश्रूर्ममैव त्वं त्वत्सकाशाद्धि मैथिली । कर्षता हलहस्तेन जनकेनोद्धृता पुरा ।। 7.98.7 ।।
explanation: Indeed, you are my mother-in-law, for Maithili was found long ago from you by Janaka, who was plowing with a plow in hand.

shloka_text: तस्मान्निर्यात्यतां सीता विवरं वा प्रयच्छ मे । पाताले नाकपृष्ठे वा वसेयं सहितस्तया ।। 7.98.8 ।।
explanation: Therefore, let Sita be released, or give me a refuge. I would dwell with her in Patala or on the surface of heaven.

shloka_text: आनय त्वं हि तां सीतां मत्तो ऽहं मैथिलीकृते । न मे दास्यसि चेत्सीतां यथारूपां महीतले ।। 7.98.9 ।।
explanation: Bring that Sita. I am passionate for Maithili. If you do not give Sita to me, in her true form on earth.

shloka_text: सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां विधमिष्यामि ते स्थितम् । नाशयिष्याम्यहं भूमिं सर्वमापो भवत्विह ।। 7.98.10 ।।
explanation: I will shatter your entire established [world], with its mountains and forests. I will destroy the earth; let everything here become water.

shloka_text: एवं ब्रुवाणे काकुत्स्थे क्रोधशोकसमन्विते । ब्रह्मा सुरगणैः सार्धमुवाच रघुनन्दनम् ।। 7.98.11 ।।
explanation: When Kakutstha, filled with anger and sorrow, was speaking thus, Brahma, along with the hosts of gods, spoke to Raghunandana.

shloka_text: राम राम न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत । स्मर त्वं पूर्वकं भावं मन्त्रं चामित्रकर्शन ।। 7.98.12 ।।
explanation: O Rama, O Rama, O virtuous one, you should not feel sorrow. O destroyer of enemies, remember your former nature and the mantra.

shloka_text: न खलु त्वां महाबाहो स्मारयेयमनुत्तमम् । इमं मुहूर्तं दुर्धर्ष स्मर त्वं जन्म वैष्णवम् ।। 7.98.13 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, I certainly should not remind you, the unsurpassed one. O unconquerable one, remember this moment, your Vaishnava birth.

shloka_text: सीता हि विमला साध्वी तव पूर्वपरायणा । नागलोकं सुखं प्रायात्त्वदाश्रयतपोबलात् ।। 7.98.14 ।।
explanation: Sita, indeed, the pure and virtuous woman, who was always devoted to you, happily went to the Naga world by the power of her penance, strengthened by her reliance on you.

shloka_text: स्वर्गे ते सङ्गमो भूयो भविष्यति न संशयः । अस्यास्तु परिषन्मध्ये यद्ब्रवीमि निबोध तत् ।। 7.98.15 ।।
explanation: Your reunion in heaven will certainly happen again. But in the midst of this assembly, listen to what I tell you.

shloka_text: एतदेव हि काव्यं ते काव्यानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् । सर्वं विस्तरतो राम व्याख्यास्यति न संशयः ।। 7.98.16 ।।
explanation: This very poem, indeed, is heard by you as the best among poems. Rama will explain everything in detail, without a doubt.

shloka_text: जन्मप्रभृति ते वीर सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् । भविष्यदुत्तरं चेह सर्वं वाल्मीकिना कृतम् ।। 7.98.17 ।।
explanation: O hero, from your birth onwards, your experience of happiness and sorrow, and all that is yet to come in this world, has been composed by Valmiki.

shloka_text: आदिकाव्यमिदं राम त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । नह्यन्यो ऽर्हति काव्यानां यशोभाग्राघवादृते ।। 7.98.18 ।।
explanation: O Rama, this primal epic, everything is established in you. No one else, except for Rama, is worthy of the glory of these poems.

shloka_text: श्रुतं ते पूर्वमेतद्धि मया सर्वं सुरैः सह । दिव्यमद्भुतरूपं च सत्यवाक्यमनावृतम् ।। 7.98.19 ।।
explanation: This, all of it, was indeed heard by me previously from you, along with the gods. It was divine, of wondrous form, and a true, unconcealed statement.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धर्मेण सुसमाहितः । शेषं भविष्यं काकुत्स्थ काव्यं रामायणं शृणु ।। 7.98.20 ।।
explanation: Therefore, O tiger among men, O descendant of Kakutstha, being steadfast in righteousness, listen to the remaining future epic, the Ramayana.

shloka_text: उत्तरं नाम काव्यस्य शेषमत्र महायशः । तच्छृणुष्व महातेज ऋषिभिः सार्धमुत्तमम् ।। 7.98.21 ।।
explanation: O greatly renowned one, here is the remaining part of the poem, named 'Uttara'. O greatly effulgent one, listen to that excellent part along with the sages.

shloka_text: न खल्वन्येन काकुत्स्थ श्रोतव्यमिदमुत्तमम् । परमम् ऋषिणा वीर त्वयैव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.98.22 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, this excellent and supreme (narrative) should certainly not be heard by anyone else. O hero, O delight of the Raghus, it should be heard by you alone from the sage.

shloka_text: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः । जगाम त्रिदिवं देवो देवैः सह सबान्धवैः ।। 7.98.23 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus, Brahma, the Lord of the three worlds, the god, went to heaven with the gods and his kinsmen.

shloka_text: ये च तत्र महात्मान ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाता न्यवर्तन्त महौजसः । उत्तरं श्रोतुमनसो भविष्यं यच्च राघवे ।। 7.98.24 ।।
explanation: And those great-souled sages there, who belonged to Brahma's realm, the greatly powerful ones, having been permitted by Brahma, departed, with minds eager to hear the subsequent events and what was to happen in the future concerning Raghava.

shloka_text: ततो रामः शुभां वाणीं देवदेवस्य भाषिताम् । श्रुत्वा परमतेजस्वी वाल्मीकिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.98.25 ।।
explanation: Then, the exceedingly radiant Rama, having heard the auspicious words spoken by the god of gods, spoke this to Valmiki.

shloka_text: भगवन् श्रोतुमनस ऋषयो ब्राह्मलौकिकाः । भविष्यदुत्तरं यन्मे श्वोभूते सम्प्रवर्तताम् ।। 7.98.26 ।।
explanation: O Lord, the divine sages are desirous of hearing. Let my future outcome manifest tomorrow.

shloka_text: एवं विनिश्चयं कृत्वा सम्प्रगृह्य कुशीलवौ । तं जनौघं विसृज्याथ पर्णशालामुपागमत् । तामेव शोचतः सीतां सा व्यतीयाय शर्वरी ।। 7.98.27 ।।
explanation: Having thus made a firm decision, and having taken the two bards (Kusha and Lava), he then dismissed that multitude of people and went to the leaf-hut. That night passed while Sita was lamenting.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 98 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the ninety-eighth chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki.

shloka_text: रजन्यां तु प्रभातायां समानीय महामुनीन् । गीयतामविशङ्काभ्यां रामः पुत्रावुवाच ह ।। 7.99.1 ।।
explanation: When the night dawned, having assembled the great sages, Rama said to his two sons, "Sing it without hesitation."

shloka_text: ततः समुपविष्टेषु ब्रह्मर्षिषु महात्मसु । भविष्यदुत्तरं काव्यं जगतुस्तौ कुशीलवौ ।। 7.99.2 ।।
explanation: Then, when the great-souled Brahmarishis were seated, those two bards sang the subsequent epic describing future events.

shloka_text: प्रविष्टायां तु सीतायां भूतलं सत्यसम्पदा । तस्यावसाने यज्ञस्य रामः परमदुर्मनाः ।। 7.99.3 ।।
explanation: When Sita, by the power of her truthfulness, entered the earth, at the conclusion of that sacrifice, Rama became extremely distressed.

shloka_text: अपश्यमानो वैदेहीं मेने शून्यमिदं जगत् । शोकेन परमायस्तो न शान्तिं मनसा ऽगमत् ।। 7.99.4 ।।
explanation: Unable to find Vaidehi, he considered this world empty. Greatly distressed by sorrow, he did not attain peace of mind.

shloka_text: विसृज्य पार्थिवान्सर्वानृक्षवानरराक्षसान् । जनौघं विप्रमुख्यानां वित्तपूर्वं विसृज्य च ।। 7.99.5 ।।
explanation: Having dismissed all the kings, bears, monkeys, and Rākṣasas, and having sent away the multitude of chief Brahmins after bestowing wealth upon them.

shloka_text: एवं समाप्य यज्ञं तु विधिवत्स तु राघवः । ततो विसृज्य तान्सर्वान्रामो राजीवलोचनः ।। 7.99.6 ।।
explanation: Having thus properly completed the sacrifice according to the rules, that Rama, the descendant of Raghu, the lotus-eyed one, then dismissed all of them.

shloka_text: हृदि कृत्वा तदा सीतामयोध्यां प्रविवेश ह । इष्टयज्ञो नरपतिः पुत्रद्वयसमन्वितः ।। 7.99.7 ।।
explanation: Then, having kept Sita in his heart, the king, who had performed sacrifices, accompanied by his two sons, entered Ayodhya.

shloka_text: न सीतायाः परां भार्यां वव्रे स रघुनन्दनः । यज्ञे यज्ञे च पत्न्यर्थं जानकी काञ्चनी भवत् ।। 7.99.8 ।।
explanation: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, did not choose any wife other than Sita. And in every sacrifice, a golden Janaki was made to serve as his wife.

shloka_text: दशवर्षसहस्राणि वाजिमेघानथाकरोत् । वाजपेयान्दशगुणांस्तथा बहुसुवर्णकान् ।। 7.99.9 ।।
explanation: He then performed horse sacrifices for ten thousand years, and similarly, Vajapeya sacrifices that were tenfold (in number/value), as well as those involving much gold.

shloka_text: अग्निष्टोमातिरात्राभ्यां गोसवैश्च महाधनैः । ईजे क्रतुभिरन्यैश्च स श्रीमानाप्तदक्षिणैः ।। 7.99.10 ।।
explanation: He, the prosperous one, performed Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices, and Gosava sacrifices, and other sacrifices, all of which were rich in wealth and had ample sacrificial fees.

shloka_text: एवं स कालः सुमहान्राज्यस्थस्य महात्मनः । धर्मे प्रयतमानस्य व्यतीयाद्राघवस्य तु ।। 7.99.11 ।।
explanation: Thus, that very long time passed for the great-souled Rama, who was ruling the kingdom and striving in righteousness.

shloka_text: अनुरञ्जन्ति राजानमहन्यहनि राघवम् । ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि स्थिता रामस्य शासने ।। 7.99.12 ।।
explanation: Bears, monkeys, and Rākṣasas, abiding under Rama's command, daily please King Rama.

shloka_text: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः सुभिक्षं विमला दिशः । हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णं पुरं जनपदास्तथा ।। 7.99.13 ।।
explanation: At the proper time, the rain falls; there is good harvest, and the directions are clear. The city and the rural areas are filled with happy and well-nourished people.

shloka_text: नाकाले म्रियते कश्चिन्न व्याधिः प्राणिनां तथा । नानर्थो विद्यते कश्चिद्रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ।। 7.99.14 ।।
explanation: No one dies prematurely, nor do living beings suffer from disease, nor does any misfortune exist, when Rama is ruling the kingdom.

shloka_text: अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य राममाता यशस्विनी । पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृता कालधर्ममुपागमत् ।। 7.99.15 ।।
explanation: Then, after a long time, Rama's illustrious mother, surrounded by sons and grandsons, attained the law of time.

shloka_text: अन्वियाय सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च यशस्विनी । धर्मं कृत्वा बहुविधं त्रिदिवे पर्यवस्थिता ।। 7.99.16 ।।
explanation:
्विनी" modifies both Sumitra and Kaikeyi? "Sumitra and the glorious Kaikeyi". This is common.
"अन्वियाय" (anviyāya) - perfect tense, 3rd singular.
"पर्यव

shloka_text: सर्वाः प्रमुदिताः स्वर्गे राज्ञा दशरथेन च । समागता महाभागाः सर्वधर्मं च लेभिरे ।। 7.99.17 ।।
explanation: All the highly fortunate ones, greatly delighted, having assembled in heaven with King Dasharatha, obtained all merit.

shloka_text: तासां रामो महादानं काले काले प्रयच्छति । मातऽणामविशेषेण ब्राह्मणेषु तपस्विषु ।। 7.99.18 ।।
explanation: Rama gives great charity from time to time, without distinction among the mothers, to the Brahmins and ascetics.

shloka_text: पित्र्याणि ब्रह्मरत्नानि यज्ञान्परमदुस्तरान् । चकार रामो धर्मात्मा पितऽन्देवान्विवर्धयन् ।। 7.99.19 ।।
explanation: The righteous-souled Rama performed ancestral spiritual treasures and extremely difficult sacrifices, honoring the ancestors and the gods.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि बहून्यथ ययुः सुखम् । यज्ञैर्बहुविधं धर्मं वर्धयानस्य सर्वदा ।। 7.99.20 ।।
explanation: Thus, many thousands of years passed happily, as he was always promoting various kinds of righteousness through sacrifices.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनशततमः सर्गः ।। 99 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred epic, the glorious Ramayana, the original poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the ninety-ninth chapter.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य युधाजित्केकयो नृपः । स्वगुरुं प्रेषयामास राघवाय महात्मने । गार्ग्यमङ्गिरसः पुत्रं ब्रह्मर्षिममितप्रभम् ।। 7.100.1 ।।
explanation: After some time, Yudhājit, the king of Kekaya, sent his own preceptor, Gārgya, the son of Angiras, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, to the great-souled Rāghava.

shloka_text: दश चाश्वसहस्राणि प्रीतिदानमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.100.2 ।।
explanation: Ten thousand horses, an unsurpassed gift of affection.

shloka_text: कम्बलानि च रत्नानि चित्रवस्त्रमथोत्तमम् । रामाय प्रददौ राजा शुभान्याभरणानि च ।। 7.100.3 ।।
explanation: The king gave Rama blankets, jewels, excellent colorful clothes, and auspicious ornaments.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु राघवो धीमान्महर्षिं गार्ग्यमागतम् । मातुलस्याश्वपतिनः प्रहितं तन्महाधनम् ।। 7.100.4 ।।
explanation: The intelligent Rama, having heard that the great sage Gargya had arrived, sent by his maternal uncle Ashwapati with that great wealth.

shloka_text: प्रत्युद्गम्य च काकुत्स्थः क्रोशमात्रं सहानुजः । गार्ग्यं सम्पूजयामास यथा शक्रो बृहस्पतिम् ।। 7.100.5 ।।
explanation: Kakutstha, accompanied by his younger brother, went forth a distance of a krosha to meet and honor Gargya, just as Shakra honors Brihaspati.

shloka_text: तथा सम्पूज्य तमृषिं तद्धनं प्रतिगृह्य च । पृष्ट्वा प्रतिपदं सर्वं कुशलं मातुलस्य च । उपविष्टं महाभागं रामः प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.100.6 ।।
explanation: Thus, having honored that sage and accepted that wealth, and having thoroughly inquired about all the welfare of his maternal uncle, Rama began to question the illustrious one who was seated.

shloka_text: किमाह मातुलो वाक्यं यदर्थं भगवानिह । प्राप्तो वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठः साक्षादिव बृहस्पतिः ।। 7.100.7 ।।
explanation: What did the maternal uncle say, for which reason the revered one, the foremost among eloquent speakers, has arrived here, as if Brihaspati himself?

shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा महर्षिः कार्यविस्तरम् । वक्तुमद्भुतसङ्काशं राघवायोपचक्रमे ।। 7.100.8 ।।
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, the great sage began to speak to Raghava about the detailed and wondrous task.

shloka_text: मातुलस्ते महाबाहो वाक्यमाह नरर्षभः । युधाजित्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं श्रूयतां यदि रोचते ।। 7.100.9 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, your maternal uncle Yudhājit, the best among men, spoke a word filled with affection. Let it be heard if it pleases you.

shloka_text: अयं गन्धर्वविषयः फलमूलोपशोभितः । सिन्धोरुभयतः पार्श्वे देशः परमशोभनः ।। 7.100.10 ।।
explanation: This Gandharva territory, adorned with fruits and roots, is an exceedingly beautiful land on both sides of the Sindhu.

shloka_text: तं च रक्षन्ति गन्धर्वाः सायुधा युद्धकोविदाः । शैलूषस्य सुता वीर त्रिकोट्यो वै महाबलाः ।। 7.100.11 ।।
explanation: And him the Gandharvas protect, armed and skilled in battle. O hero, the sons of Shailusha, indeed three crores of mighty ones.

shloka_text: तान्विनिर्जित्य काकुत्स्थ गन्धर्वनगरं शुभम् । निवेशय महाबोहो स्वे पुरे सुसमाहिते ।। 7.100.12 ।।
explanation: O Kakutstha, O mighty-armed one, having completely conquered them, establish that auspicious city of the Gandharvas in your own well-governed territory.

shloka_text: अन्यस्य न गतिस्तत्र देशः परमशोभनः । रोचतां ते महाबाहो नाहं त्वामहितं वदे ।। 7.100.13 ।।
explanation: No one else has access there. The place is exceedingly beautiful. May it be pleasing to you, O mighty-armed one, for I do not speak ill of you.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवः प्रीतो महर्षेर्मातुलस्य च । उवाच बाढमित्येव भरतं चान्ववैक्षत ।। 7.100.14 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, Rama, pleased with the great sage and the maternal uncle, said, "Very well," and looked at Bharata.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीद्राघवः प्रीतः साञ्जलिप्रग्रहो द्विजम् । इमौ कुमारौ तं देशं ब्रह्मर्षे विचरिष्यतः ।। 7.100.15 ।।
explanation: Pleased, Rama, with folded hands and a respectful gesture, said to the Brahmin: "O Brahmarshi, these two boys will wander in that region."

shloka_text: भरतस्यात्मजौ वीरौ तक्षः पुष्कल एव च । मातुलेन सुगुप्तौ तु धर्मेण सुसमाहितौ ।। 7.100.16 ।।
explanation: Bharata's two heroic sons, Taksha and Pushkala, were well-protected by their maternal uncle and well-established in righteousness.

shloka_text: भरतं चाग्रतः कृत्वा कुमारौ सबलानुगौ । निहत्य गन्धर्वसुतान्द्वे पुरे विभजिष्यतः ।। 7.100.17 ।।
explanation: Making Bharata foremost, the two princes, accompanied by their army and followers, having slain the sons of the Gandharvas, will divide the two cities.

shloka_text: निवेश्य ते पुरवरे आत्मजौ सन्निवेश्य च । आगमिष्यति मे भूयः सकाशमतिधार्मिकः ।। 7.100.18 ।।
explanation: Having settled your two sons in that excellent city, and having established them well, the very righteous one will come to my presence again.

shloka_text: ब्रह्मर्षिमेवमुक्त्वा तु भरतं सबलानुगम् । आज्ञापयामास तदा कुमारौ चाभ्यषेचयत् ।। 7.100.19 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Bharata, who was accompanied by his army and followers, the Brahmarshi then issued commands and consecrated the two princes.

shloka_text: नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरस्सुतम् । भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां विनिर्ययौ ।। 7.100.20 ।।
explanation: And with an auspicious constellation, having placed Angiras's son in front, Bharata departed with his army and the two princes.

shloka_text: सा सेना शक्रयुक्तेव नगरान्निर्ययावथ । राघवानुगता दूरं दुराधर्षा सुरैरपि ।। 7.100.21 ।।
explanation: That army, like one accompanied by Indra, then departed from the city. Followed by Raghava for a long distance, it was invincible even by gods.

shloka_text: मांसादानि च सत्त्वानि रक्षांसि सुमहान्ति च । अनुजग्मुर्हि भरतं रुधिरस्य पिपासया ।। 7.100.22 ।।
explanation: Meat-eating creatures and huge Rākṣasas indeed followed Bharata, out of thirst for blood.

shloka_text: भूतग्रामाश्च बहवो मांसभक्षाः सुदारुणाः । गन्धर्वपुत्रमांसानि भोक्तुकामाः सहस्रशः ।। 7.100.23 ।।
explanation: And many hosts of very fierce, flesh-eating beings, by thousands, were desirous of eating the flesh of the Gandharva's son.

shloka_text: सिंहव्याघ्रवराहाणां खेचराणां च पक्षिणाम् । बहूनि वै सहस्राणि सेनाया ययुरग्रतः ।। 7.100.24 ।।
explanation: Many thousands of lions, tigers, boars, flying creatures, and birds went ahead of the army.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धमासमुषिता पथि सेना निरामया । हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा केकयं समुपागमत् ।। 7.100.25 ।।
explanation: The army, having stayed on the path for one and a half months, healthy and filled with cheerful and well-nourished people, arrived at Kekaya.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे शततमः सर्गः ।। 100 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the revered Ramayana, the glorious first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the hundredth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः । युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत् ।। 7.101.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that Bharata, accompanied by Yudhājit and Gārgya, had arrived as commander, the King of Kekaya attained great joy.

shloka_text: स निर्ययौ जनौघेन महता केकयाधिपः । त्वरमाणो ऽभिचक्राम गन्धर्वान्कामरूपिणः ।। 7.101.2 ।।
explanation: The king of Kekaya departed with a great multitude of people. Hurrying swiftly, he attacked the Gandharvas, who could assume any form at will.

shloka_text: भरतश्च युधाजिच्च समेतौ लघुविक्रमैः । गन्धर्वनगरं प्राप्तौ सबलौ सपदानुगौ ।। 7.101.3 ।।
explanation: Bharata and Yudhājit, united with swift warriors, reached the city of the Gandharvas, accompanied by their army and followers.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु भरतं प्राप्तं गन्धर्वास्ते समागताः । योद्धुकामा महावीर्या व्यनदन् वै समन्ततः ।। 7.101.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard that Bharata had arrived, those Gandharvas, mighty and desirous of fighting, gathered and roared from all sides.

shloka_text: ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् । सप्तरात्रं महाभीमं न चान्यतरयोर्जयः ।। 7.101.5 ।।
explanation: Then a tumultuous, hair-raising battle ensued. It was exceedingly dreadful, lasting seven nights, and neither side achieved victory.

shloka_text: खड्गशक्तिधनुर्ग्राहा नद्यः शोणितसंस्रवाः । नृकलेवरवाहिन्यः प्रवृत्ताः सर्वतोदिशम् ।। 7.101.6 ।।
explanation: Rivers, with swords, spears, and bows as their grasping creatures, flowing with streams of blood and carrying human corpses, began to flow in all directions.

shloka_text: ततो रामानुजः क्रुद्धः कालस्यास्त्रं सुदारुणम् । संवर्तं नाम भरतो गन्धर्वेष्वभ्यचोदयत् ।। 7.101.7 ।।
explanation: Then, Bharata, Rama's younger brother, enraged, discharged the exceedingly dreadful weapon of Kala, named Samvarta, upon the Gandharvas.

shloka_text: ते बद्धाः कालपाशेन संवर्तेन विदारिताः । क्षणेनाभिहतास्तेन तिस्रः कोट्यो महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.8 ।।
explanation: They, bound by the noose of Time, were torn apart by the Destroyer. In a moment, three crores of great beings were struck down by him.

shloka_text: तं घातं घोरसङ्काशं न स्मरन्ति दिवौकसः । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण तादृशानां महात्मनाम् ।। 7.101.9 ।।
explanation: The gods do not remember that terrible blow, (which was inflicted) upon such great souls, in the mere interval of a wink.

shloka_text: हतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु भरतः केकयीसुतः । निवेशयामास तदा समृद्धे द्वे पुरोत्तमे ।। 7.101.10 ।।
explanation: After all of them were slain, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, then established two prosperous and excellent cities.

shloka_text: तक्षं तक्षशिलायां तु पुष्कलं पुष्कलावते । गन्धर्वदेशे रुचिरे गान्धारविषये च सः ।। 7.101.11 ।।
explanation: Taksha in Takshashila, and Pushkala in Pushkalavati. And he (placed them) in the beautiful country of the Gandharvas, in the region of Gandhara.

shloka_text: धनरत्नौघसङ्कीर्णे काननैरुपशोभिते । अन्योन्यसङ्घर्षकृते स्पर्धया गुणविस्तरैः ।। 7.101.12 ।।
explanation: Filled with heaps of wealth and jewels, adorned by forests, where mutual conflict is created by rivalry in the display of extensive virtues.

shloka_text: उभे सुरुचिरप्रख्ये व्यवहारैरकिल्बिषैः । उद्यानयानसम्पूर्णे सुविभक्तान्तरापणे ।। 7.101.13 ।।
explanation: Both, renowned for their great beauty, with blameless dealings, full of gardens and conveyances, and having well-arranged inner markets.

shloka_text: उभे पुरवरे रम्ये विस्तरैरुपशोभिते । गृहमुख्यैः सुरुचिरैर्विमानसमवर्णिभिः ।। 7.101.14 ।।
explanation: Both excellent cities, beautiful and adorned with vast expanses, with principal houses that were very charming and described as equal to celestial palaces.

shloka_text: शोभिते शोभनीयैश्च देवायतनविस्तरैः । तालैस्तमालैस्तिलकैर्वकुलैरुपशोभिते ।। 7.101.15 ।।
explanation: Adorned with beautiful and extensive temples, and further beautified by palm, Tamala, Tilaka, and Bakula trees.

shloka_text: निवेश्य पञ्चभिर्वर्षैर्भरतो राघवानुजः । पुनरायान्महाबाहुरयोध्यां केकयीसुतः ।। 7.101.16 ।।
explanation: After establishing (the kingdom/cities) for five years, Bharata, the mighty-armed younger brother of Rama and son of Kaikeyi, returned to Ayodhya.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं साक्षाद्धर्ममिवापरम् । राघवं भरतः श्रीमान्ब्रह्माणमिव वासवः ।। 7.101.17 ।।
explanation: The glorious Bharata, having saluted the great-souled Rama, who was like another Dharma personified, just as Vasava (Indra) salutes Brahma.

shloka_text: शशंस च यथावृत्तं गन्धर्ववधमुत्तमम् । निवेशनं च देशस्य श्रुत्वा प्रीतो ऽस्य राघवः ।। 7.101.18 ।।
explanation: He narrated, as it happened, the excellent killing of the Gandharvas and the establishment of the region. Having heard his account, Rama was pleased.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 101 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha, the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the one hundred and first chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षमापेदे राघवो भ्रातृभिः सह । वाक्यं चाद्भुतसङ्काशं तदा प्रोवाच लक्ष्मणम् ।। 7.102.1 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, Rama, along with his brothers, attained joy, and then he spoke wondrous words to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: इमौ कुमारौ सौमित्रे तव धर्मविशारदौ । अङ्गदश्चन्द्रकेतुश्च राज्यार्थे दृढविक्रमौ ।। 7.102.2 ।।
explanation: O Saumitri, these two princes, Angada and Chandraketu, your experts in dharma, are of firm valor for the sake of the kingdom.

shloka_text: इमौ राज्ये ऽभिषेक्ष्यामि देशः साधु विधीयताम् । रमणीयो ह्यसम्बाधो रमेतां यत्र धन्विनौ ।। 7.102.3 ।।
explanation: I will install these two in the kingdom. Let a suitable region be arranged, for it should be delightful and unobstructed, where the two archers may enjoy themselves.

shloka_text: न राज्ञो यत्र पीडा स्यान्नाश्रमाणां विनाशनम् । स देशो दृश्यतां सौम्य नापराध्यामहे यथा ।। 7.102.4 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, let such a place be found where the king suffers no harm and the hermitages are not destroyed, so that we may not commit any offense.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति रामे तु भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह । अयं कारुपथो देशो रमणीयो निरामयः ।। 7.102.5 ।।
explanation: When Rama had thus spoken, Bharata replied: 'This region, the path of artisans, is delightful and free from ailment.'

shloka_text: निवेश्यतां तत्र पुरमङ्गदस्य महात्मनः । चन्द्रकेतोः सुरुचिरं चन्द्रकान्तं निरामयम् ।। 7.102.6 ।।
explanation: Let a very beautiful, moon-like, and prosperous city be established there for the great-souled Angada and for Chandraketu.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं भरतेनोक्तं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः । तं च कृत्वा वशे देशमङ्गदस्य न्यवेशयत् ।। 7.102.7 ।।
explanation: Rama accepted that statement spoken by Bharata. And having brought that country under control, he established Angada there.

shloka_text: अङ्गदीया पुरी रम्याप्यङ्गदस्य निवेशिता । रमणीया सुगुप्ता च रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।। 7.102.8 ।।
explanation: The city of Angada, Angadiya, was beautiful and established for Angada. It was charming and well-protected by Rama, whose deeds are effortless.

shloka_text: चन्द्रकेतोश्च मल्लस्य मल्लभूम्यां निवेशिता । चन्द्रकान्तेति विख्याता दिव्या स्वर्गपुरी यथा ।। 7.102.9 ।।
explanation: Established in the land of the Mallas by Chandraketu and Malla, it was renowned as Chandrakanta, divine like the city of heaven.

shloka_text: ततो रामः परां प्रीतिं लक्ष्मणो भरतस्तथा । ययुर्युद्धे दुराधर्षा अभिषेकं च चक्रिरे ।। 7.102.10 ।।
explanation: Then Rama, Lakshmana, and Bharata, the unconquerable ones in battle, attained great joy and performed the coronation.

shloka_text: अभिषिच्य कुमारौ स प्रस्थापयति राघवः । अङ्गदं पश्चिमां भूमिं चन्द्रकेतुमुदङ्मुखम् ।। 7.102.11 ।।
explanation: Having consecrated the two princes, Rama dispatched them: Angada to the western land, and Chandraketu to the north.

shloka_text: अङ्गदं चापि सौमित्रिर्लक्ष्मणो ऽनुजगाम ह । चन्द्रकेतोस्तु भरतः पार्ष्णिग्राहो बभूव ह ।। 7.102.12 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, Saumitri, also followed Angada. And Bharata became the rear-guard for Chandraketu.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्त्वङ्गदीयायां संवत्सरमथोषितः । पुत्रे स्थिते दुराधर्षे अयोध्यां पुनरागमत् ।। 7.102.13 ।।
explanation: Lakshmana, having resided in Angadiya for a year, then, after his unconquerable son was established, returned to Ayodhya again.

shloka_text: भरतो ऽपि तथैवोष्य संवत्सरमतो ऽधिकम् । अयोध्यां पुनरागम्य रामपादावुपास्त सः ।। 7.102.14 ।।
explanation: Bharata also, having resided there similarly for more than a year, returned to Ayodhya and worshipped Rama's feet.

shloka_text: उभौ सौमित्रिभरतौ रामपादावनुव्रतौ । कालं गतमपि स्नेहान्न जज्ञाते ऽतिधार्मिकौ ।। 7.102.15 ।।
explanation: Both Saumitri and Bharata, devoted to Rama's feet, being exceedingly righteous, did not perceive the passage of time due to their affection.

shloka_text: एवं वर्षसहस्राणि दश तेषां ययुस्तदा । धर्मे प्रयतमानानां पौरकार्येषु नित्यदा ।। 7.102.16 ।।
explanation: Thus, ten thousand years passed for them, who were always striving in righteousness and in the affairs of the citizens.

shloka_text: विहृत्य कालं परिपूर्णमानसाः श्रिया वृता धर्मपुरे सुसंस्थिताः । त्रयः समिद्धा इव दीप्ततेजसो महाध्वरे साधु हुतास्त्रयो ऽग्नयः ।। 7.102.17 ।।
explanation: Having spent time, with their minds completely satisfied, endowed with prosperity, and well-established in the city of Dharma, the three shone with radiant splendor, like the three fires properly offered into a great sacrifice.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे व्द्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 102 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (work), the glorious Ramayana, composed by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the one hundred and second chapter.

shloka_text: कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य रामे धर्मपरे स्थिते । कालस्तापसरूपेण राजद्वारमुपागमत् ।। 7.103.1 ।।
explanation: Then, after some time, while Rama was devoted to righteousness, Time, in the form of an ascetic, approached the royal gate.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं धृतिमन्तं यशश्विनम् । मां निवेदय रामाय सम्प्राप्तं कार्यगौरवात् ।। 7.103.2 ।।
explanation: He said these words to the steadfast and glorious Lakshmana: "Announce me to Rama, for I have arrived due to the importance of the task."

shloka_text: दूतो ऽस्म्यतिबलस्याहं महर्षेरमितौजसः । रामं दिदृक्षुरायातः कार्येण हि महाबल ।। 7.103.3 ।।
explanation: I am a messenger of the exceedingly powerful great sage of immeasurable might. Indeed, O mighty one, I have come, desiring to see Rama, for a purpose.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिस्त्वरया ऽन्वितः । न्यवेदयत रामाय तापसं तं समागतम् ।। 7.103.4 ।।
explanation: Upon hearing his words, Saumitri, with urgency, informed Rama about the ascetic who had arrived.

shloka_text: जयस्व राम धर्मेण उभौ लोकौ महाद्युते । दूतस्त्वां द्रष्टुमायातस्तपसा भास्करप्रभः ।। 7.103.5 ।।
explanation: O Rama, O greatly effulgent one, conquer both worlds by righteousness. A messenger, radiant like the sun by his penance, has come to see you.

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणेनोक्तं श्रुत्वा राम उवाच ह । प्रवेश्यतां मुनिस्तात महौजास्तस्य वाक्यधृत् ।। 7.103.6 ।।
explanation: Having heard that statement spoken by Lakshmana, Rama said: "Dear one, let that greatly powerful sage, his messenger, be brought in."

shloka_text: सौमित्रिस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रावेशयत तं मुनिम् । ज्वलन्तमेव तेजोभिः प्रदहन्तमिवांशुभिः ।। 7.103.7 ।।
explanation: Saumitri, having said, "So be it," led that sage in, who was blazing with effulgence, as if burning with rays.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिगम्य रघुश्रेष्ठं दीप्यपानं स्वतेजसा । ऋषिर्मधुरया वाचा वर्धस्वेत्याह राघवम् ।। 7.103.8 ।।
explanation: Having approached Rama, the best of the Raghus, who was shining with his own splendor, the sage said to Rama with a sweet voice, "May you prosper!"

shloka_text: तस्मै रामो महातेजाः पूजामर्घ्यपुरोगमाम् । ददौ कुशलमव्यग्रं प्रष्टुमेवोपचक्रमे ।। 7.103.9 ।।
explanation: The greatly effulgent Rama offered him worship, beginning with arghya, and then calmly began to inquire about his welfare.

shloka_text: पृष्टश्च कुशलं तेन रामेण वदतां वरः । आसने काञ्चने दिव्ये निषसाद महायशाः ।। 7.103.10 ।।
explanation: And, having been asked about his welfare by Rama, the best among speakers, the greatly renowned one sat down on the divine golden seat.

shloka_text: तमुवाच ततो रामः स्वागतं ते महामुने । प्रापयास्य च वाक्यानि यतो दूतस्त्वमागतः ।। 7.103.11 ।।
explanation: Then Rama said to him, 'Welcome to you, O great sage. And deliver the words of him from whom you have come as a messenger.'

shloka_text: चोदितो राजसिंहेन मुनिर्वाक्यमभाषत । द्वन्द्वमेतत्प्रवक्तव्यं हितं वै यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.12 ।।
explanation: Urged by the lion among kings, the sage spoke these words: "This duality must be explained, if you indeed desire your welfare."

shloka_text: यः शृणोति निरीक्षेद्वा स वध्यो भविता तव । भवेद्वै मुनिमुख्यस्य वचनं यद्यपेक्षसे ।। 7.103.13 ।।
explanation: He who hears or sees, he shall be slain by you. If you desire it, this will indeed be the word of the chief of sages.

shloka_text: स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् । द्वारि तिष्ठ महाबाहो प्रतिहारं विसर्जय ।। 7.103.14 ।।
explanation: Having assented, saying 'So be it', Rama said to Lakshmana: "O mighty-armed one, stand at the door and dismiss the doorkeeper."

shloka_text: स मे वध्यः खलु भवेत् कथाद्वन्द्वं समीरितम् । ऋषेर्मम च सौमित्रे पश्येद्वा शृणुयाच्च यः ।। 7.103.15 ।।
explanation: Indeed, he would be deserving of death, O Saumitre, who would see or hear the two stories narrated by the sage and me.

shloka_text: ततो निक्षिप्य काकुत्स्थो लक्ष्मणं द्वारि सङ्ग्रहम् । तमुवाच मुने वाक्यं कथयस्वेति राघवः ।। 7.103.16 ।।
explanation: Then Kakutstha, having stationed Lakshmana as a guard at the door, Raghava said to the sage, "O sage, please speak your words."

shloka_text: यत्ते मनीषितं वाक्यं येन वा ऽसि समाहितः । कथयस्वाविशङ्कस्त्वं ममापि हृदि वर्तते ।। 7.103.17 ।।
explanation: Whatever thought you have, or by what you are resolved, speak it without hesitation, for it is also present in my heart.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्र्युत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 103 ।।
explanation: Thus in the sage-composed glorious Ramayana by Valmiki, the original epic poem, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the one hundred and third chapter.

shloka_text: शृणु राजन्महासत्व यदर्थमहमागतः । पितामहेन देवेन प्रेषितो ऽस्मि महाबल ।। 7.104.1 ।।
explanation: Listen, O King, O great being, for what purpose I have come. I have been sent by the divine Grandfather, O mighty one.

shloka_text: तवाहं पूर्वसद्भावे पुत्रः परपुरञ्जय । मायासम्भावितो वीर कालः सर्वसमाहरः ।। 7.104.2 ।।
explanation: O conqueror of enemy cities, O hero, I am your son from a previous existence, manifested by Maya. I am Time, the destroyer of all.

shloka_text: पितामहश्च भगवानाह लोकपतिः प्रभुः । समयस्ते कृतः सौम्य लोकान्सम्परिरक्षितुम् ।। 7.104.3 ।।
explanation: And the divine Pitāmaha, the Lord of the worlds, the powerful lord, said: "O gentle one, a vow has been made by you to fully protect the worlds."

shloka_text: सङ्क्षिप्य हि पुरा लोकान्मायया स्वयमेव हि । महार्णवे शयानो ऽप्सु मां त्वं पूर्वमजीजनः ।। 7.104.4 ।।
explanation: Indeed, having formerly dissolved the worlds by your own māyā, you yourself, lying in the great ocean, in the waters, previously created me.

shloka_text: भोगवन्तं ततो नागमनन्तमुदकेशयम् । मायया जनयित्वा त्वं द्वौ च सत्त्वौ महाबलौ ।। 7.104.5 ।।
explanation: Then, by your illusion, you created Ananta, the hooded serpent lying in the water, and two mighty beings.

shloka_text: मधुं च कैटभं चैव ययोरस्थिचयैर्वृता । इयं पर्वतसम्बाधा मेदिनी चाभवन्मही ।। 7.104.6 ।।
explanation: And this earth, crowded with mountains, became the great land, covered by the heaps of bones of Madhu and Kaitabha.

shloka_text: पद्मे दिव्ये ऽर्कसङ्काशे नाभ्यामुत्पाद्य मामपि । प्राजापत्यं त्वया कर्म मयि सर्वं निवेशितम् ।। 7.104.7 ।।
explanation: In the divine lotus, shining like the sun, having created me also from your navel, all the work of creation was entrusted to me by you.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं सन्न्यस्तभारो हि त्वामुपासे जगत्पतिम् । रक्षां विधत्स्व भूतेषु मम तेजस्करो भवान् ।। 7.104.8 ।।
explanation: Therefore, I, having indeed cast off my burden, resort to you, the Lord of the world. Grant protection to all beings, and may you be the one who enhances my glory.

shloka_text: ततस्त्वमपि दुर्धर्षात्तस्माद्भावात्सनातनात् । रक्षार्थं सर्वभूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान् ।। 7.104.9 ।।
explanation: Then you also, from that unassailable, eternal state, for the protection of all beings, attained the state of Vishnu.

shloka_text: अदित्यां वीर्यवान्पुत्रो भ्रातऽणां वीर्यवर्धनः । समुत्पन्नेषु कृत्येषु तेषां साह्याय कल्पसे ।। 7.104.10 ।।
explanation: You are a mighty son born of Aditi, an enhancer of the valor of your brothers. When tasks arise, you are capable of assisting them.

shloka_text: स त्वं वित्रास्यमानासु प्रजासु जगतां वर । रावणस्य वधाकाङ्क्षी मानुषेषु मनो ऽदधाः ।। 7.104.11 ।।
explanation: O best among the worlds, when the creatures were being terrified, you, desiring the slaying of Ravana, resolved to be among humans.

shloka_text: दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च । कृत्वा वासस्य नियतिं स्वयमेवात्मना पुरा ।। 7.104.12 ।।
explanation: Having fixed the duration of his dwelling for ten thousand years and ten hundred years, by himself, formerly.

shloka_text: स त्वं मनोमयः पुत्रः पूर्णायुर्मानुषेष्विह । कालो ऽयं ते नरश्रेष्ठ समीपमुपवर्तितुम् ।। 7.104.13 ।।
explanation: That you, O best among men, are a mind-born son, destined for a full lifespan among humans here. This is the time for you to come near.

shloka_text: यदि भूयो महाराज प्रजा इच्छस्युपासितुम् । वस वा वीर भद्रं त एवमाह पितामहः ।। 7.104.14 ।।
explanation: O great king, if you again desire to rule the people, then stay, O hero. May good fortune be yours. Thus spoke the Grandfather.

shloka_text: अथ वा विजिगीषा ते सुरलोकाय राघव । सनाथा विष्णुना देवा भवन्तु विगतज्वराः ।। 7.104.15 ।।
explanation: Or else, O Raghava, is your desire for victory for the world of the gods? Let the gods, protected by Vishnu, be free from distress.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा पितामहेनोक्तं वाक्यं कालसमीरितम् । राघवः प्रहसन्वाक्यं सर्वसंहारमब्रवीत् ।। 7.104.16 ।।
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by the grandfather, prompted by time, Rama, laughing, spoke words concerning universal destruction.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा मे देवदेवस्य वाक्यं परममद्भुतम् । प्रीतिर्हि महती जाता तवागमनसम्भवा ।। 7.104.17 ।।
explanation: Having heard my most wonderful words of the God of gods, a great joy has indeed arisen, caused by your arrival.

shloka_text: त्रयाणामपि लोकानां कार्यार्थं मम सम्भवः । भद्रं ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामि यत एवाहमागतः ।। 7.104.18 ।।
explanation: My manifestation is for the purpose of the work of all three worlds. May good fortune be to you. I will go from where I have come.

shloka_text: हद्गतो ह्यसि सम्प्राप्तो न मे तत्र विचारणा । मया हि सर्वकृत्येषु देवानां वशवर्तिनाम् । स्थातव्यं सर्वसंहार यथा ह्याह पितामहः ।। 7.104.19 ।।
explanation: Indeed, you have entered my heart and are fully understood; I have no doubt about that. Indeed, in all my actions, I must, being subservient to the gods, bring about the destruction of all, just as the Grandfather (B

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुरधिकशततमः सर्गः ।। 104 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the first epic poem by Valmiki, this is the one hundred and fourth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: तथा तयोः संवदतोर्दुर्वासा भगवानृषिः । रामस्य दर्शनाकाङ्क्षी राजद्वारमुपागमत् ।। 7.105.1 ।।
explanation: Thus, while those two were conversing, the revered sage Durvasa, desirous of seeing Rama, approached the royal gate.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिगम्य तु सौमित्रिमुवाच ऋषिसत्तमः । रामं दर्शय मे शीघ्रं पुरा मे ऽर्थो ऽतिवर्तते ।। 7.105.2 ।।
explanation: He, the best among sages, having approached Lakshmana, said: "Show Rama to me quickly, before my purpose is lost."

shloka_text: मुनेस्तु भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । अभिवाद्य महात्मानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.105.3 ।।
explanation: Having heard the sage's words, Lakshmana, the slayer of enemy heroes, saluted the great-souled one and spoke these words.

shloka_text: किं कार्यं ब्रूहि भगवन्को वा ऽर्थः किं करोम्यहम् । व्यग्रो हि राघवो ब्रह्मन्मुहूर्तं प्रतिपाल्यताम् ।। 7.105.4 ।।
explanation: What is the task? Tell me, O Lord. What is the purpose? What should I do? Indeed, Raghava is busy, O Brahmana. Please wait for a moment.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषिशार्दूलः क्रोधेन कलुषीकृतः । उवाच लक्ष्मणं वाक्यं निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा ।। 7.105.5 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, the foremost among sages, overwhelmed with anger, spoke to Lakshmana, as if burning him with his eyes.

shloka_text: अस्मिन्क्षणे मां सौमित्रे रामाय प्रतिवेदय । अस्मिन्क्षणे मां सौमित्रे न निवेदयसे यदि ।। 7.105.6 ।।
explanation: O son of Sumitra, inform Rama about me at this moment. If you do not inform Rama about me at this moment, O son of Sumitra.

shloka_text: विषयं त्वां पुरं चैव शपिष्ये राघवं तथा । भरतं चैव सौमित्रे युष्माकं या च सन्ततिः ।। 7.105.7 ।।
explanation: O son of Sumitra, I will curse your territory, you, your city, and also Rama, and also Bharata, and also your progeny.

shloka_text: न हि शक्ष्याम्यहं भूयो मन्युं धारयितुं हृदि । तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसङ्काशं वाक्यं तस्य महात्मनः । चिन्तयामास मनसा तस्य वाक्यस्य निश्चयम् ।। 7.105.8 ।।
explanation: I will not be able to hold anger in my heart any longer. Having heard that formidable speech of that great soul, he pondered with his mind the true meaning of his words.

shloka_text: एकस्य मरणं मे ऽस्तु मा भूत्सर्वविनाशनम् । इति बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य राघवाय न्यवेदयत् ।। 7.105.9 ।।
explanation: Let there be the death of one (person) for me, let there not be the destruction of all. Having thus resolved with his intellect, he reported to Raghava.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रामः कालं विसृज्य च । निस्सृत्य त्वरितं राजा अत्रेः पुत्रं ददर्श ह ।। 7.105.10 ।।
explanation: Having heard Lakshmana's words, and setting aside the delay, King Rama quickly came out and saw the son of Atri.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । किं कार्यमिति काकुत्स्थः कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ।। 7.105.11 ।।
explanation: Kakutstha, having saluted the great soul who was blazing with splendor, spoke with folded hands, 'What is the task?'

shloka_text: तद्वाक्यं राघवेणोक्तं श्रुत्वा मुनिवरः प्रभुम् । प्रत्याह रामं दुर्वासाः श्रूयतां धर्मवत्सल ।। 7.105.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard that speech spoken by Raghava, the best of sages, Durvasa, replied to Lord Rama, "O lover of righteousness, listen!"

shloka_text: अद्य वर्षसहस्रस्य समाप्तिस्तपसो मम । सो ऽहं भोजनमिच्छामि यथासिद्धं तवानघ ।। 7.105.13 ।।
