explanation: Today is the completion of my thousand years of penance. Therefore, I desire food, whatever is ready from you, O sinless one.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं राजा राघवः प्रीतमानसः । भोजनं मुनिमुख्याय यथासिद्धमुपाहरत् ।। 7.105.14 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words, King Rama, with a delighted mind, offered a meal to the chief of sages, as it was prepared.

shloka_text: स तु भुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठस्तदन्नममृतोपमम् । साधु रामेति सम्भाष्य स्वमाश्रममुपागमत् ।। 7.105.15 ।।
explanation: Having eaten that nectar-like food, the best of sages, after saying "Excellent, Rama!", returned to his own hermitage.

shloka_text: तस्मिन् गते मुनिवरे स्वाश्रमं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । संस्मृत्य कालवाक्यानि ततो दुःखमुपागमत् ।। 7.105.16 ।।
explanation: When that excellent sage had gone to his own hermitage, Lakshmana's elder brother (Rama), remembering the words of Kala, was then overcome with sorrow.

shloka_text: दुःखेन च सुसन्तप्तः स्मृत्वा तद्घोरदर्शनम् । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह ।। 7.105.17 ।।
explanation: Greatly tormented by sorrow, and remembering that terrible sight, he was unable to speak, his face downcast and his mind sorrowful.

shloka_text: ततो बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य कालवाक्यानि राघवः । नैतदस्तीति निश्चित्य तूष्णीमासीन्महायशाः ।। 7.105.18 ।।
explanation: Then, having ascertained the words of time with his intellect, the greatly renowned Rama, having determined 'this is not so,' remained silent.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 105 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha (work), the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, the one hundred and fifth chapter.

shloka_text: अवाङ्मुखमथो दीनं दृष्ट्वा सोममिवाप्लुतम् । राघवं लक्ष्मणो वाक्यं हृष्टो मधुरमब्रवीत् ।। 7.106.1 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen Rama, downcast and miserable, as if the moon were immersed (in gloom), Lakshmana, joyful, spoke sweet words.

shloka_text: न संतापं महाबाहो मदर्थं कर्तुमर्हसि । पूर्वनिर्माणबद्धा हि कालस्य गतिरीदृशी ।। 7.106.2 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed, you should not grieve for my sake. For such is the course of time, bound by preordained destiny.

shloka_text: जहि मां सौम्य विस्रब्धं प्रतिज्ञां परिपालय । हीनप्रतिज्ञाः काकुत्स्थ प्रयान्ति नरकं नराः ।। 7.106.3 ।।
explanation: O gentle one, kill me confidently and fulfill your vow. O Kakutstha, men who break their vows go to hell.

shloka_text: यदि प्रीतिर्महाराज यद्यनुग्राह्यता मयि । जहि मां निर्विशङ्कस्त्वं धर्मं वर्धय राघव ।। 7.106.4 ।।
explanation: If there is affection, O great king, if there is favor towards me, then kill me fearlessly, O Raghava, and promote righteousness.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेन तथोक्तस्तु रामः प्रचलितेन्द्रियः । मन्त्रिणः समुपानीय तथैव च पुरोधसम् ।। 7.106.5 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Rama, whose senses were agitated, summoned the ministers and likewise the priest.

shloka_text: अब्रवीच्च तदा वृत्तं तेषां मध्ये स राघवः । दुर्वासोभिगमं चैव प्रतिज्ञां तापसस्य च ।। 7.106.6 ।।
explanation: And then, among them, Rama spoke of what had happened, and also of Durvasa's visit and the ascetic's vow.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणः सर्वे सोपाध्यायाः समासत । वसिष्ठस्तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.106.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard that, all the ministers along with their preceptors assembled. Then Vasistha, the greatly effulgent, spoke this statement.

shloka_text: दृष्टमेतन्महाबाहो क्षयं ते रोमहर्षणम् । लक्ष्मणेन वियोगश्च तव राम महायशः ।। 7.106.8 ।।
explanation: O mighty-armed one, this hair-raising destruction of yours has been seen. And your separation from Lakshmana, O greatly renowned Rama.

shloka_text: त्यजैनं बलवान्कालो मा प्रतिज्ञां वृथा कृताः । विनष्टायां प्रतिज्ञायां धर्मो ऽपि च लयं व्रजेत् ।। 7.106.9 ।।
explanation: Abandon this, for Time is powerful. Let not the promise be made in vain. When a promise is broken, even righteousness will perish.

shloka_text: ततो धर्मे विनष्टे तु त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् । सदेवर्षिगणं सर्वं विनश्येत्तु न संशयः ।। 7.106.10 ।।
explanation: Then, when Dharma is destroyed, the three worlds, along with all animate and inanimate beings, and all groups of gods and sages, would certainly perish, without a doubt.

shloka_text: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल त्रैलोक्यस्याभिपालनात् । लक्ष्मणेन विना चाद्य जगत्स्वस्थं कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.106.11 ।।
explanation: You, O tiger among men, for the protection of the three worlds, and today, without Lakshmana, make the world peaceful.

shloka_text: तेषां तत्समवेतानां वाक्यं धर्मार्थसंहितम् । श्रुत्वा परिषदो मध्ये रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत् ।। 7.106.12 ।।
explanation: Having heard their assembled speech, which was imbued with righteousness and purpose, in the midst of the assembly, Rama spoke to Lakshmana.

shloka_text: विसर्जये त्वां सौमित्रे मा भूद्धर्मविपर्ययः । त्यागो वधो वा विहितः साधूनां तूभयं समम् ।। 7.106.13 ।।
explanation: I must abandon you, O Saumitra, lest there be a transgression of dharma. Abandonment or death is prescribed, and for the virtuous, both are considered equal.

shloka_text: रामेण भाषिते वाक्ये बाष्पव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः । लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितं प्रायात्स्वगृहं न विवेश ह ।। 7.106.14 ।।
explanation: When Rama spoke these words, Lakshmana, with his senses agitated by tears, quickly departed and did not enter his own house.

shloka_text: स गत्वा सरयूतीरमुपस्पृश्य कृताञ्जलिः । निगृह्य सर्वस्रोतांसि निःश्वासं न मुमोच ह ।। 7.106.15 ।।
explanation: He went to the bank of the Sarayu, performed ablution, and with folded hands, he restrained all his vital functions and did not release his breath.

shloka_text: अनिःश्वसन्तं युक्तं तं सशक्राः साप्सरोगणाः । देवाः सर्षिगणाः सर्वे पुष्पैरभ्यकिरंस्तदा ।। 7.106.16 ।।
explanation: Then, all the gods, along with Indra, the groups of Apsaras, and the groups of Rishis, showered him, who was absorbed in meditation and holding his breath, with flowers.

shloka_text: अदृश्यं सर्वमनुजैः सशरीरं महाबलम् । प्रगृह्य लक्ष्मणं शक्रस्त्रिदिवं संविवेश ह ।। 7.106.17 ।।
explanation: Indra, having seized Lakshmana, who was invisible to all humans, mighty, and still in his body, entered heaven.

shloka_text: ततो विष्णोश्चतुर्भागमागतं सुरसत्तमाः । दृष्ट्वा प्रमुदिताः सर्वे ऽपूजयन् समहर्षयः ।। 7.106.18 ।।
explanation: Then, having seen the fourth part of Vishnu arrive, all the best of gods, greatly delighted, worshipped along with the great sages.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षडुत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 106 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the Arsha Ramayana, the glorious first epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the one hundred and sixth chapter.

shloka_text: विसृज्य लक्ष्मणं रामो दुःखशोकसमन्वितः । पुरोधसं मन्त्रिणश्च नैगमांश्चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.107.1 ।।
explanation: Having dismissed Lakshmana, Rama, filled with sorrow and grief, spoke this to the chief priest, the ministers, and the citizens.

shloka_text: अद्य राज्ये ऽभिषेक्ष्यामि भरतं धर्मवत्सलम् । अयोध्यायाः पतिं वीरं ततो यास्याम्यहं वनम् ।। 7.107.2 ।।
explanation: Today I will enthrone Bharata, who is devoted to righteousness, the heroic lord of Ayodhya, in the kingdom. Then I will go to the forest.

shloka_text: प्रवेशयत सम्भारान्माभूत्कालस्य पर्ययः । अद्यैवाहं गमिष्यामि लक्ष्मणेन गतां गतिम् ।। 7.107.3 ।।
explanation: Bring in the preparations, let there be no delay. Today itself I shall go the way Lakshmana has gone.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवेणोक्तं सर्वाः प्रकृतयो भृशम् । मूर्धभिः प्रणता भूमौ गतसत्त्वा इवाभवन् ।। 7.107.4 ।।
explanation: Having heard that spoken by Raghava, all the subjects, greatly, bowed down to the ground with their heads, as if they had lost their spirit.

shloka_text: भरतश्च विसञ्ज्ञो ऽभूच्छ्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम् । राज्यं विगर्हयामास राघवं चेदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.107.5 ।।
explanation: Bharata, having heard Rama's words, became bewildered. He condemned the kingdom and said this to Raghava.

shloka_text: सत्येनाहं शपे राजन्स्वर्गलोके न चैव हि । न कामये यथा राज्यं त्वां विना रघुनन्दन ।। 7.107.6 ।।
explanation: O King, I swear by truth, that I do not desire the kingdom without you, O Raghunandana, nor indeed the heavenly world.

shloka_text: इमौ कुशलवौ राजन्नभिषिञ्च नराधिप । कोसलेषु कुशं वीरमुत्तरेषु तथा लवम् ।। 7.107.7 ।।
explanation: O King, O Lord of men, anoint these two, Kusha and Lava. [Anoint] the brave Kusha in Kosala, and likewise Lava in the northern regions.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नस्य तु गच्छन्तु दूतास्त्वरितविक्रमाः । इदं गमनमस्माकं स्वर्गायाख्यातु मा चिरम् ।। 7.107.8 ।।
explanation: Let swift-acting messengers go to Shatrughna. Let them announce this departure of ours to heaven without delay.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भरतेनोक्तं दृष्ट्वा चापि ह्यधोमुखान् । पौरान्दुःखेन सन्तप्तान्वसिष्ठो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.107.9 ।।
explanation: Having heard what Bharata said, and seeing the citizens with downcast faces, afflicted with sorrow, Vasiṣṭha spoke these words.

shloka_text: वत्स राम इमाः पश्य धरणीं प्रकृतीर्गताः । ज्ञात्वैषामीप्सितं कार्यं मा चैषां विप्रियं कृथाः ।। 7.107.10 ।।
explanation: O dear Rama, behold these subjects of the land. Having known their desires, do not do anything displeasing to them.

shloka_text: वसिष्ठस्य तु वाक्येन उत्थाप्य प्रकृतीजनम् । किं करोमीति काकुत्स्थः सर्वा वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.107.11 ।।
explanation: Indeed, by the words of Vasiṣṭha, having made the citizens stand up, Kakutstha spoke to all, saying, "What shall I do?"

shloka_text: ततः सर्वाः प्रकृतयो रामं वचनमब्रुवन् । गच्छन्तमनुगच्छामो यत्र राम गमिष्यसि ।। 7.107.12 ।।
explanation: Then all the subjects said to Rama, 'We will follow you as you go, O Rama, wherever you go.'

shloka_text: पौरेषु यदि ते प्रीतिर्यदि स्नेहो ह्यनुत्तमः । सपुत्रदाराः काकुत्स्थ समागच्छाम सत्पथम् ।। 7.107.13 ।।
explanation: If your affection for the citizens, if your love is unsurpassed, O Kakutstha, let us, with our sons and wives, come to the righteous path.

shloka_text: तपोवनं वा दुर्गं वा नदीमम्भोनिधिं तथा । वयं ते यदि न त्याज्याः सर्वान्नो नय ईश्वर ।। 7.107.14 ।।
explanation: Whether it is a hermitage, or a fort, or a river, or the ocean. If we are not to be abandoned by you, O Lord, take all of us.

shloka_text: एषा नः परमा प्रीतिरेष नः परमो वरः । हृद्गता नः सदा प्रीतिस्तवानुगमने नृप ।। 7.107.15 ।।
explanation: This is our supreme joy, this is our greatest boon. Our heartfelt affection is always for you, O King, in following you.

shloka_text: पौराणां दृढभक्तिं च बाढमित्येव सो ऽब्रवीत् । स्वकृतान्तं चान्ववेक्ष्य तस्मिन्नहनि राघवः ।। 7.107.16 ।।
explanation: And Rama said, "Indeed!" regarding the firm devotion of the citizens. And on that day, having considered his own destiny,

shloka_text: कोसलेषु कुशं वीरमुत्तरेषु तथा लवम् । अभिषिच्य महात्मानावुभौ रामः कुशीलवौ ।। 7.107.17 ।।
explanation: Rama, having consecrated the heroic Kusha in Kosala and Lava in the northern regions, both great-souled Kusha and Lava.

shloka_text: अभिषिक्तौ सुतावङ्के प्रतिष्ठाप्य पुरे ततः । परिष्वज्य महाबाहुर्मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय चासकृत् ।। 7.107.18 ।।
explanation: Then, in the city, the mighty-armed one, having consecrated his two sons and placed them on his lap, embraced them and repeatedly kissed them on the head.

shloka_text: रथानां तु सहस्राणि नागानामयुतानि च । दशायुतानि चाश्वानामेकैकस्य धनं ददौ ।। 7.107.19 ।।
explanation: He gave thousands of chariots, ten thousands of elephants, and one hundred thousands of horses as wealth to each one.

shloka_text: बहुरत्नौ बहुधनौ हृष्टपुष्टजनावृतौ । स्वे पुरे प्रेषयामास भ्रातरौ तु कुशीलवौ ।। 7.107.20 ।।
explanation: He sent the two brothers, Kuśa and Lava, who were rich in many gems and much wealth, and surrounded by happy and well-nourished people, to their own city.

shloka_text: अभिषिच्य सुतौ वीरौ प्रतिष्ठाप्य पुरे तदा । दूतान्सम्प्रेषयामास शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने ।। 7.107.21 ।।
explanation: Having consecrated his two heroic sons and established them in the city, he then sent messengers to the great-souled Shatrughna.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 107 ।।
explanation: Thus ends the one hundred and seventh chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda of the sacred Ramayana, the original epic composed by Valmiki.

shloka_text: ते दूता रामवाक्येन चोदिता लघुविक्रमाः । प्रजग्मुर्मधुरां शीघ्रं चक्रुर्वासं न चाध्वनि ।। 7.108.1 ।।
explanation: Urged by Rama's words, those swift-footed messengers quickly went to Madhura and made no halt on the way.

shloka_text: ते तु त्रिभिरहोरात्रैः सम्प्राप्य मधुरामथ । शत्रुघ्नाय यथातत्त्वमाचख्युः सर्वमेव तत् ।। 7.108.2 ।।
explanation: They, however, having reached Mathura in three days and nights, then truthfully narrated all of that to Shatrughna.

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणस्य परित्यागं प्रतिज्ञां राघवस्य च । पुत्रयोरभिषेकं च पौरानुगमनं तथा ।। 7.108.3 ।।
explanation: The abandonment of Lakshmana, and Raghava's vow, and the coronation of the two sons, and the following by the citizens.

shloka_text: कुशस्य नगरी रम्या विन्ध्यपर्वतरोधसि । कुशावतीति नाम्ना सा कृता रामेण धीमता । श्रावस्तीति पुरी रम्या श्राविता च लवस्य ह ।। 7.108.4 ।।
explanation: The beautiful city of Kusha, named Kushavati, was established by the wise Rama on the slopes of the Vindhya mountain. And the beautiful city of Shravasti was given to Lava.

shloka_text: अयोध्यां विजनां कृत्वा राघवो भरतस्तथा । स्वर्गस्य गमनोद्योगं कृतवन्तौ महारथौ ।। 7.108.5 ।।
explanation: Having made Ayodhya deserted, Rama and Bharata, the two great charioteers, prepared for their journey to heaven.

shloka_text: एवं सर्वं निवेद्याशु शत्रुघ्नाय महात्मने । विरेमुस्ते ततो दूतास्त्वर राजेति चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.108.6 ।।
explanation: Having thus quickly reported everything to the great-souled Shatrughna, those messengers then ceased and said, "Hasten, O King!"

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसङ्काशं कुलक्षयमुपस्थितम् । प्रकृतीस्तु समानीय काञ्चनं च पुरोधसम् ।। 7.108.7 ।।
explanation: Having heard that dreadful impending destruction of the family, he assembled the ministers and Kancana, the priest.

shloka_text: तेषां सर्वं यथावृत्तमब्रवीद्रघनन्दनः । आत्मनश्च विपर्यासं भविष्यं भ्रातृभिः सह ।। 7.108.8 ।।
explanation: Rama told them everything that had happened, his own misfortune, and the future with his brothers.

shloka_text: ततः पुत्रद्वयं वीरः सो ऽभ्यषिञ्चन्नराधिपः । सुबाहुर्मधुरां लेभे शत्रुघाती च वैदिशम् ।। 7.108.9 ।।
explanation: Then that brave king consecrated his two sons. Subahu obtained Mathura, and Shatrughati obtained Vidisha.

shloka_text: द्विधा कृत्वा तु तां सेनां माधुरीं पुत्रयोर्द्वयोः । धनं च युक्तं कृत्वा वै स्थापयामास पार्थिवः ।। 7.108.10 ।।
explanation: The king, having divided that Madhuri army into two parts for his two sons, and having properly arranged the wealth, entrusted it.

shloka_text: सुबाहुं मधुरायां च वैदेशे शत्रुघातिनम् । ययौ स्थाप्य तदा ऽयोध्यां रथेनैकेन राघवः ।। 7.108.11 ।।
explanation: Having established Subahu in Mathura and Shatrughati in Vaidesha, Rama then went to Ayodhya by a single chariot.

shloka_text: स ददर्श महात्मानं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् । सूक्ष्मक्षौमाम्बरधरं मुनिभिः सार्धमक्षयैः ।। 7.108.12 ।।
explanation: He saw the great soul, blazing like fire, wearing fine silken garments, along with immortal sages.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततो रामं प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतेन्द्रियः । उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञं धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन् ।। 7.108.13 ।।
explanation: Then, he, with folded hands and controlled senses, having saluted Rama, the knower of Dharma, spoke words, contemplating only on righteousness.

shloka_text: कृत्वाभिषेकं सुतयोर्द्वयो राघवनन्दन । तवानुगमने राजन्विद्धि मां कृतनिश्चयम् ।। 7.108.14 ।।
explanation: O son of Raghu, O King, know me to be determined to follow you after performing the coronation of my two sons.

shloka_text: न चान्यदपि वक्तव्यमतो वीर न शासनम् । विलोक्यमानमिच्छामि मद्विधेन विशेषतः ।। 7.108.15 ।।
explanation: And nothing else should be said, O hero. This is not a command. I desire it to be particularly observed by one like me.

shloka_text: तस्य तां बुद्धिमक्लीबां विज्ञाय रघुनन्दनः । बाढमित्येव शत्रुघ्नं रामो वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.108.16 ।।
explanation: Having understood his unwavering resolve, Rama, the scion of Raghu, spoke only this word to Shatrughna: "Very well!"

shloka_text: तस्य वाक्यस्य वाक्यान्ते वानराः कामरूपिणः । ऋक्षराक्षससङ्घाश्च समापेतुरनेकशः ।। 7.108.17 ।।
explanation: At the end of his speech, numerous shape-shifting Vanaras, and hosts of bears and Rakshasas, gathered in great numbers.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवं ते पुरस्कृत्य सर्व एव समागताः । तं रामं द्रष्टुमनसः स्वर्गायाभिमुखं स्थितम् ।। 7.108.18 ।।
explanation: Having made Sugriva their leader, all of them assembled, desirous of seeing that Rama who was standing facing towards heaven.

shloka_text: देवपुत्रा ऋषिसुता गन्धर्वाणां सुतास्तथा । रामक्षयं विदित्वा ते सर्व एव समागताः ।। 7.108.19 ।।
explanation: The sons of gods, the sons of sages, and the sons of Gandharvas, all of them, having learned of Rama's demise, assembled.

shloka_text: ते राममभिवाद्योचुः सर्वे वानरराक्षसाः । तवानुगमने राजन्सम्प्राप्ताः कृतनिश्चयाः ।। 7.108.20 ।।
explanation: All those monkeys and demons, having saluted Rama, said: 'O King, we have come, having made a firm resolve to follow you.'

shloka_text: यदि राम विनास्माभिर्गच्छेस्त्वं पुरुषोत्तम । यमदण्डमिवोद्यम्य त्वया स्म विनिपातिताः ।। 7.108.21 ।।
explanation: If, O Rama, O Purushottama, you go without us, we would be struck down by you as if by Yama's uplifted mace.

shloka_text: तैरेवमुक्तः काकुत्स्थो बाढमित्यब्रवीत् स्मयन् ।। 7.108.22 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by them, Kakutstha, smiling, said, "Very well."

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रामं सुग्रीवो ऽपि महाबलः । प्रणम्य विधिवद्वीरं विज्ञापयितुमुद्यतः ।। 7.108.23 ।।
explanation: In the meantime, the mighty Sugriva, having reverently bowed down to the hero Rama, was ready to make a submission.

shloka_text: अभिषिच्याङ्गदं वीरमागतो ऽस्मि नरेश्वर । तवानुगमने राजन्विद्धि मां कृतनिश्चयम् ।। 7.108.24 ।।
explanation: Having consecrated the heroic Angada, I have come, O lord of men. O king, know me to be resolute in following you.

shloka_text: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो रमयतां वरः । वानरेन्द्रमथोवाचं मैत्रं तस्यानुचिन्तयन् ।। 7.108.25 ।।
explanation: Having heard his words, Rama, the best among those who delight, then spoke to the king of monkeys, contemplating his friendship.

shloka_text: सखे शृणुष्व सुग्रीव न त्वया ऽहं विनाकृतः । गच्छेयं देवलोकं वा परमं वा पदं महत् ।। 7.108.26 ।।
explanation: O friend, listen, Sugriva, I would not go to the world of gods, or to any supreme or great abode, if I were separated from you.

shloka_text: बिभीषणमथोवाच राक्षसेन्द्रं महायशाः । यावत्प्रजा धरिष्यन्ति तावत्त्वं वै बिभीषण । राक्षसेन्द्र महावीर्य लङ्कास्थस्त्वं धरिष्यसि ।। 7.108.27 ।।
explanation: Then the greatly renowned one spoke to Vibhishana, the lord of Rakshasas: "As long as people exist, so long, O Vibhishana, O lord of Rakshasas of great might, you will endure, residing in Lanka."

shloka_text: यावच्चन्द्रश्च सूर्यश्च यावत्तिष्ठति मेदिनी । यावच्च मत्कथा लोके तावद्राज्यं तवास्त्विह ।। 7.108.28 ।।
explanation: As long as the moon and the sun exist, as long as the earth remains, and as long as my story is in the world, so long may your kingdom endure here.

shloka_text: शासितस्त्वं सखित्वेन कार्यं ते मम शासनम् । प्रजाः संरक्ष धर्मेण नोत्तरं वक्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.108.29 ।।
explanation: You are instructed as a friend; my command is to be carried out by you. Protect the subjects righteously; you are not to speak a reply.

shloka_text: किञ्चान्यद्वक्तुमिच्छामि राक्षसेन्द्र महामते ।। 7.108.30 ।।
explanation: Furthermore, I wish to say something else, O great-minded king of Rakshasas.

shloka_text: आराधय जगन्नाथमिक्ष्वाकुकुलदैवतम् । आराधनीयमनिशं सर्वैर्दैवैः सवासवैः ।। 7.108.31 ।।
explanation: Worship Jagannatha, the family deity of the Ikshvaku dynasty, who is constantly worshipped by all gods, along with Indra.

shloka_text: तथेति प्रतिजग्राह रामवाक्यं विभीषणः । राजा राक्षसमुख्यानां राघवाज्ञामनुस्मरन् ।। 7.108.32 ।।
explanation: Vibhishana, the king of the chief Rakshasas, accepted Rama's words, saying "So be it," remembering Raghava's command.

shloka_text: तमेवमुक्त्वा काकुत्स्थो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत् । जीविते कृतबुद्धिस्त्वं मा प्रतिज्ञां विलोपय ।। 7.108.33 ।।
explanation: Having spoken thus to him, Kakutstha then said to Hanuman: "You are determined to live, do not violate your vow."

shloka_text: मत्कथाः प्रचरिष्यन्ति यावल्लोके हरीश्वर । तावद्रमस्व सुप्रीतो मद्वाक्यमनुपालयन् ।। 7.108.34 ।।
explanation: O Lord Hari, as long as my stories circulate in the world, so long, being very pleased, enjoy yourself, following my words.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान्राघवेण महात्मना । वाक्यं विज्ञापयामास परं हर्षमवाप्य च ।। 7.108.35 ।।
explanation: Thus addressed by the great-souled Rama, Hanuman, having attained supreme joy, made a submission.

shloka_text: यावत्तव कथा लोके विचरिष्यति पावनी । तावत्स्थास्यामि मेदिन्यां तवाज्ञामनुपालयन् ।। 7.108.36 ।।
explanation: As long as your purifying story spreads in the world, so long will I remain on earth, obeying your command.

shloka_text: जाम्बवन्तं तथोक्त्वा तु वृद्धं ब्रह्मसुतं तथा । मैन्दं च द्विविदं चैव पञ्च जाम्बवता सह ।
explanation: Having thus spoken to Jambavan, and to the aged son of Brahma, and to Mainda and Dvivida, these five were with Jambavan.

shloka_text: तानेवमुक्त्वा काकुत्स्थः सर्वांस्तानृक्षवानरान् । उवाच बाढं गच्छध्वं मया सार्धं यथेप्सितम् ।। 7.108.38 ।।
explanation: Having thus spoken to them, Kakutstha said to all those bears and monkeys, "Indeed, go with me as you desire."

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टोतरशततमः सर्गः ।। 108 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, ends the one hundred and eighth chapter.

shloka_text: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां पृथुवक्षा महायशाः । रामः कमलपत्राक्षः पुरोधसमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.109.1 ।।
explanation: When the night had dawned, then Rama, the broad-chested, greatly renowned, lotus-petal-eyed, spoke to the chief priest.

shloka_text: अग्निहोत्रं व्रजत्वग्रे दीप्यमानं सह द्विजैः । वाजपेयातपत्रं च शोभमानं महापथे ।। 7.109.2 ।।
explanation: Let the blazing Agnihotra proceed in front with the Brahmins, and the Vajapeya umbrella, splendid on the great path.

shloka_text: ततो वसिष्ठस्तेजस्वी सर्वं निरवशेषतः । चकार विधिवद्धर्मं महाप्रास्थानिकं विधिम् ।। 7.109.3 ।।
explanation: Then, the illustrious Vasiṣṭha performed completely and according to the sacred law, all the rites of the great departure.

shloka_text: ततः सूक्ष्माम्बरधरो ब्रह्ममावर्तयन्परम् । कुशान्गृहीत्वा पाणिभ्यां प्रसज्य प्रययावथ ।। 7.109.4 ।।
explanation: Then, wearing fine clothes, meditating on the Supreme Brahman, and holding Kusha grass with both hands, he proceeded with dedication.

shloka_text: अव्याहरन्क्वचित्किञ्चिन्निश्चेष्टो निःसुखः पथि । निर्जगाम गृहात्तस्माद्दीप्यमान इवांशुमान् ।। 7.109.5 ।।
explanation: Not speaking anything anywhere, motionless, without joy on the path, he departed from that house, shining like the sun.

shloka_text: रामस्य दक्षिणे पार्श्वे सपद्मा श्रीरपाश्रिता । सव्ये तु ह्रीर्महादेवी व्यवसायस्तथाग्रतः ।। 7.109.6 ।।
explanation: On Rama's right side, Shri, bearing a lotus, was present. On his left was the great goddess Hri, and determination stood before him.

shloka_text: शरा नानाविधाश्चापि धनुरायतमुत्तमम् । तथा ऽ ऽयुधानि ते सर्वे ययुः पुरुषविग्रहाः ।। 7.109.7 ।।
explanation: Arrows of various kinds, and also an excellent long bow, and all those weapons, they all assumed human forms.

shloka_text: वेदा ब्राह्मणरूपेण गायत्री सर्वरक्षिणी । ओङ्कारो ऽथ वषट्कारः सर्वे राममनुव्रताः ।। 7.109.8 ।।
explanation: The Vedas in the form of Brahmins, Gayatri the protector of all, Om, and Vaṣaṭkāra – all are devoted to Rama.

shloka_text: ऋषयश्च महात्मानः सर्व एव महीसुराः । अन्वगच्छन्महात्मानं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम् ।। 7.109.9 ।।
explanation: And all the great-souled Rishis, who were indeed Brahmins, followed the great-souled one to the open gate of heaven.

shloka_text: तं यान्तमनुगच्छन्ति ह्यन्तःपुरचराः स्त्रियः । सवृद्धबालदासीकाः सवर्षवरकिङ्कराः ।। 7.109.10 ।।
explanation: As he departed, the women of the inner palace followed him, along with old and young female servants, and eunuchs and male servants.

shloka_text: सान्तःपुरश्च भरतः शत्रुघ्नसहितो ययौ । रामं गतिमुपागम्य साग्निहोत्रमनुव्रतः ।। 7.109.11 ।।
explanation: Bharata, along with his royal women and accompanied by Shatrughna, went, having taken Rama as his refuge, bringing his sacred fire.

shloka_text: ते च सर्वे महात्मानः साग्निहोत्राः समागताः । सपुत्रदाराः काकुत्स्थमनुजग्मुर्महामतिम् ।। 7.109.12 ।।
explanation: And all those great-souled ones, having assembled with their sacred fires, along with their sons and wives, followed the great-minded Kakutstha.

shloka_text: मन्त्रिणो भृत्यवर्गाश्च सपुत्रपशुबान्धवाः । सर्वे सहानुगा राममन्वगच्छन्प्रहृष्टवत् ।। 7.109.13 ।।
explanation: Ministers and servants, along with their sons, cattle, and kinsmen, all with their followers, followed Rama with great delight.

shloka_text: ततः सर्वाः प्रकृतयो हृष्टपुष्टजनावृताः । गच्छन्तमन्वगछंस्तं राघवं गुणरञ्जिताः ।। 7.109.14 ।।
explanation: Then, all the subjects, consisting of happy and prosperous people, and charmed by his virtues, followed Rama as he went.

shloka_text: ततः सस्त्रीपुमांसस्ते सपक्षिपशुवाहनाः । राघवस्यानुगाः सर्वे हृष्टा विगतकल्मषाः ।। 7.109.15 ।।
explanation: Then, all of them, men and women, along with their birds, animals, and vehicles, followers of Raghava, were joyful and free from sin.

shloka_text: स्नाताः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे हृष्टाः पुष्टाश्च वानराः । दृढं किलकिलाशब्दैः सर्वं राममनुव्रतम् ।। 7.109.16 ।।
explanation: All the monkeys, bathed, delighted, joyful, and well-nourished, with loud 'kilakila' sounds, were entirely devoted to Rama.

shloka_text: न तत्र कश्चिद्दीनो वा व्रीडितो वा ऽपि दुःखितः । हृष्टं समुदितं सर्वं बभूव परमाद्भुतम् ।। 7.109.17 ।।
explanation: There, no one was miserable, ashamed, or even sorrowful. Everyone was joyful, prosperous, and exceedingly wonderful.

shloka_text: द्रष्टुकामो ऽथ निर्यान्तं रामं जानपदो जनः । यः प्राप्तः सो ऽपि दृष्ट्वैव स्वर्गायानुगतो मुदा ।। 7.109.18 ।।
explanation: Then, the people of the country, desirous of seeing Rama as he departed, whoever arrived, even he, just by seeing [him], attained heaven with joy.

shloka_text: ऋक्षवानररक्षांसि जनाश्च पुरवासिनः । आगच्छन्परया भक्त्या पृष्ठतः सुसमाहिताः ।। 7.109.19 ।।
explanation: Bears, monkeys, Rākṣasas, and the inhabitants of the city, being very attentive, followed from behind with great devotion.

shloka_text: यानि भूतानि नगरे ऽप्यन्तर्धानगतानि च । राघवं तान्यनुययुः स्वर्गाय समुपस्थितम् ।। 7.109.20 ।।
explanation: All those beings, even those in the city who had become invisible, followed Rama as he proceeded to heaven.

shloka_text: यानि पश्यन्ति काकुत्स्थं स्थावराणि चराणि च । सर्वाणि रामगमने ह्यनुजग्मुर्हि तान्यपि ।। 7.109.21 ।।
explanation: All those, both stationary and moving, who beheld Kakutstha, indeed followed him at Rama's departure.

shloka_text: नोच्छ्वसत्तदयोध्यायां सुसूक्ष्ममपि दृश्यते । तिर्यग्योनिगताश्चापि सर्वे राममनुव्रताः ।। 7.109.22 ।।
explanation: Not even the slightest breath of life was seen in Ayodhya. And even those born in animal wombs were all devoted to Rama.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे नवाधिकशततमः सर्गः ।। 109 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the sacred Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttarakanda, is the one hundred and ninth chapter.

shloka_text: अध्यर्धयोजनं गत्वा नदीं पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम् । सरयूं पुण्यसलिलां ददर्श रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.110.1 ।।
explanation: Having gone one and a half yojanas, Raghunandana saw the river Sarayu, whose sacred waters flowed westward.

shloka_text: तां नदीमाकुलावर्तां सर्वत्रानुसरन्नृपः । आगतः सप्रजो रामस्तं देशं रघुनन्दनः ।। 7.110.2 ।।
explanation: Following that river, turbulent with whirlpools everywhere, King Rama, the scion of Raghu, arrived at that place with his people.

shloka_text: अथ तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते तु ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः । सर्वैः परिवृतो देवैर्ऋषिभिश्च महात्मभिः ।। 7.110.3 ।।
explanation: Then, at that moment, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, was surrounded by all the gods and the great-souled sages.

shloka_text: आययौ यत्र काकुत्स्थः स्वर्गाय समुपस्थितः । विमानशतकोटीभिर्दिव्याभिरभिसंवृतः ।। 7.110.4 ।।
explanation: Where Kakutstha arrived, ready for heaven, surrounded by hundreds of crores of divine aerial cars.

shloka_text: दिव्यतेजोवृतं व्योम ज्योतिर्भूतमनुत्तमम् । स्वयम्प्रभैः स्वतेजोभिः स्वर्गिभिः पुण्यकर्मभिः ।। 7.110.5 ।।
explanation: The sky, enveloped in divine splendor, became unsurpassed light, (shining) with the self-luminous splendors of the celestial beings who had performed meritorious deeds.

shloka_text: पुण्या वाता ववुश्चैव गन्धवन्तः सुखप्रदाः । पपात पुष्पवृष्टिश्च देवैर्मुक्ता महौघवत् ।। 7.110.6 ।।
explanation: Auspicious, fragrant, and comfort-giving winds blew. And a shower of flowers, released by the gods, fell like a mighty torrent.

shloka_text: तस्मिंस्तूर्यशतैः कीर्णे गन्धर्वाप्सरसङ्कुले । सरयूसलिलं रामः पद्भ्यां समुपचक्रमे ।। 7.110.7 ।।
explanation: In that place, filled with hundreds of musical instruments and crowded with Gandharvas and Apsaras, Rama entered the waters of the Sarayu by foot.

shloka_text: ततः पितामहो वाणीमन्तरिक्षादभाषत । आगच्छ विष्णो भद्रं ते दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो ऽसि राघव ।। 7.110.8 ।।
explanation: Then the Grandfather spoke from the sky: "Come, O Vishnu, good fortune be to you! Fortunately, you have arrived, O Raghava."

shloka_text: भ्रातृभिः सह देवाभैः प्रविशस्व स्विकां तनुम् । यामिच्छसि महाबाहो तां तनुं प्रविश स्विकाम् । वैष्णवीं तां महातेजस्तद्वाकाशं सनातनम् ।। 7.110.9 ।।
explanation: With your god-like brothers, enter your own body. O mighty-armed one, whichever body you desire, enter that one of your own. O greatly effulgent one, that Vaishnava form is indeed the eternal sky.

shloka_text: त्वं हि लोकगतिर्देव न त्वां केचित्प्रजानते । ऋते मायां विशालाक्षीं तव पूर्वपरिग्रहाम् । त्वामचिन्त्यं महद्भूतमक्षयं सर्वसङ्ग्रहम् ।। 7.110.10 ।।
explanation: You are indeed the refuge of the world, O Lord. No one truly knows you, except for Maya, the wide-eyed one, your eternal consort. You are inconceivable, the great being, imperishable, and the essence of all.

shloka_text: यामिच्छसि महातेजस्तां तनुं प्रविश स्वयम् ।। 7.110.11 ।। ां
explanation: O greatly powerful one, enter yourself into that body which you desire.

shloka_text: विशालाक्षीं तव पूर्वपरिग्रहाम् । पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा विनिश्चित्य महामतिः । विवेश वैष्णवं तेजः सशरीरः सहानुजः ।। 7.110.12 ।।
explanation: Regarding Visalakshi, your former wife, having heard the words of the grandfather, the great-minded one, having resolved, entered the Vaishnava splendor with his body and with his younger brother.

shloka_text: ततो विष्णुमयं देवं पूजयन्ति स्म देवताः । साध्या मरुद्गणाश्चैव सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः ।। 7.110.13 ।।
explanation: Then the gods, the Sadhyas, and the Marut hosts, along with Indra and with Agni as their leader, worshipped the deity who was Vishnu himself.

shloka_text: ये च दिव्या ऋषिगणा गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्च याः । सुपर्णनागयक्षाश्च दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः ।। 7.110.14 ।।
explanation: And those divine hosts of sages, and those Gandharvas and Apsaras, and Suparnas, Nagas, Yakshas, Daityas, Danavas, and Rakshasas.

shloka_text: सर्वं पुष्टं प्रमुदितं सुसम्पूर्णमनोरथम् । साधु साध्विति तैर्देवैस्त्रिदिवं गतकल्मषम् ।। 7.110.15 ।।
explanation: Everything was prosperous, joyful, and with all desires perfectly fulfilled. 'Excellent! Excellent!' (was exclaimed) by those gods, (and) heaven became free from blemish.

shloka_text: अथ विष्णुर्महातेजाः पितामहमुवाच ह । एषां लोकं जनौघानां दातुमर्हसि सुव्रत ।। 7.110.16 ।।
explanation: Then Vishnu, the greatly effulgent one, spoke to the Grandfather: 'O virtuous one, you should grant a realm to these multitudes of beings.'

shloka_text: इमे हि सर्वे स्नेहान्मामनुयाता यशस्विनः । भक्ता हि भजितव्याश्च त्यक्तात्मानश्च मत्कृते ।। 7.110.17 ।।
explanation: Indeed, all these glorious ones have followed me out of affection. They are truly devoted, worthy of being cherished, and have sacrificed their lives for my sake.

shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा विष्णुवचनं ब्रह्मा लोकगुरुः प्रभुः । लोकान्सान्तानिकान्नाम यास्यन्तीमे समागताः ।। 7.110.18 ।।
explanation: Having heard those words of Vishnu, Brahma, the lord and preceptor of the worlds, (said): 'These who have assembled will go to the worlds named Santanika.'

shloka_text: यच्च तिर्यग्गतं किञ्चित्त्वामेवमनुचिन्तयत् । प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यति भक्त्या वै तत्सन्ताने निवत्स्यति ।। 7.110.19 ।।
explanation: And whatever animal, contemplating you in this manner, will abandon its life with devotion, will be reborn in a (human) lineage.

shloka_text: सर्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्युक्ते ब्रह्मलोकादनन्तरे ।। 7.110.20 ।।
explanation: Endowed with all the qualities of Brahman, immediately next to Brahmaloka.

shloka_text: वानराश्च स्विकां योनिमृक्षाश्चैव तथा ययुः । येभ्यो विनिस्सृताः सर्वे सुरेभ्यः सुरसम्भवाः ।। 7.110.21 ।।
explanation: The monkeys and the bears, similarly, returned to their own origin, from which all of them, born of gods, had emerged from the deities.

shloka_text: तेषु प्रविविशे चैव सुग्रीवः सूर्यमण्डलम् । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां स्वान्पितऽन्प्रतिपेदिरे ।। 7.110.22 ।।
explanation: Among them, Sugriva also entered the solar orb. While all the gods watched, they attained their own fathers.

shloka_text: तथोक्तवति देवेशे गोप्रतारमुपागताः । भेजिरे सरयूं सर्वे हर्षपूर्णाश्रुविक्लवाः ।। 7.110.23 ।।
explanation: When the Lord of the gods had thus spoken, all who had approached Gopratara entered the Sarayu, overwhelmed with tears full of joy.

shloka_text: अवगाह्य जलं यो यः प्राणी ह्यासीत् प्रहृष्टवत् । मानुषं देहमुत्सृज्य विमानं सो ऽध्यरोहत ।। 7.110.24 ।।
explanation: Whichever living being, having entered the water, became joyful, he, abandoning his human body, ascended a celestial chariot.

shloka_text: तिर्यग्योनिगतानां च शतानि सरयूजलम् । सम्प्राप्य त्रिदिवं जग्मुः प्रभासुरवपूंषि च । दिव्या दिव्येन वपुषा देवा दीप्ता इवाभवन् ।। 7.110.25 ।।
explanation: Hundreds of those who had gone into animal wombs, having obtained the water of Sarayu, went to heaven with radiant bodies. Divine, with divine bodies, they became like shining gods.

shloka_text: गत्वा तु सरयूतोयं स्थावराणि चराणि च । प्राप्य तत्तोयविक्लेदं देवलोकमुपागमन् ।। 7.110.26 ।।
explanation: Having gone to the water of Sarayu, and having obtained contact with that water, the immobile and mobile beings attained the world of gods.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नपि समापन्ना ऋक्षवानरराक्षसाः । ते ऽपि स्वर्गं प्रविविशुर्देहान्निक्षिप्य चाम्भसि ।। 7.110.27 ।।
explanation: Even the bears, monkeys, and rakshasas who had fallen there, they also entered heaven, having cast off their bodies in water.

shloka_text: ततः समागतान्सर्वान्स्थाप्य लोकगुरुर्दिवि । जगाम त्रिदशैः सार्धं सदा हृष्टैर्दिवं महत् ।। 7.110.28 ।।
explanation: Then, the preceptor of the world, having established all those who had assembled in heaven, went to his great abode along with the always joyful gods.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे दशाधिकशततमः सर्गः ।। 110 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic poem by Valmiki, this is the one hundred and tenth chapter of the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: एतावदेतदाख्यानं सोत्तरं ब्रह्मपूजितम् । रामायणमिति ख्यातं मुख्यं वाल्मीकीना कृतम् ।। 7.111.1 ।।
explanation: This is the entire narrative, including the Uttara Kanda, revered by Brahma. It is renowned as the Ramayana, the principal work composed by Valmiki.

shloka_text: ततः प्रतिष्ठितो विष्णुः स्वर्गलोके यथा पुरम् । येन व्याप्तमिदं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ।। 7.111.2 ।।
explanation: Then Vishnu was established in the heavenly realm as before, by whom this entire three worlds, with its moving and non-moving beings, is pervaded.

shloka_text: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः । नित्यं शृण्वन्ति सन्तुष्टाः दिव्यं रामायणं दिवि ।। 7.111.3 ।।
explanation: Then, the gods, along with the Gandharvas, Siddhas, and great sages, constantly listen with satisfaction to the divine Ramayana in heaven.

shloka_text: इदमाख्यानमायुष्यं सौभाग्यं पापनाशनम् । रामायणं वेदसमं श्राद्धेषु श्रावयेद्बुधः ।। 7.111.4 ।।
explanation: This narrative, the Ramayana, which promotes longevity, bestows good fortune, and destroys sins, and is equal to the Vedas, a wise person should recite during Shraddha ceremonies.

shloka_text: अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रमधनो लभते धनम् । सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्येत पदमप्यस्य यः पठेत् ।। 7.111.5 ।।
explanation: A childless person obtains a son, a poor person obtains wealth. Whoever reads even a single line of this (text) is freed from all sins.

shloka_text: पापान्यपि च यः कुर्यादहन्यहनि मानवः । पठत्येकमपि श्लोकं पापात्स परिमुच्यते ।। 7.111.6 ।।
explanation: And a human being who commits sins day after day, if he recites even one verse, he is liberated from sin.

shloka_text: वाचकाय च दातव्यं वस्त्रं धेनुं हिरण्यकम् । वाचके परितुष्टे तु तुष्टाः स्युः सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.111.7 ।।
explanation: And to the reciter should be given clothes, a cow, and gold. But when the reciter is fully pleased, all deities become pleased.

shloka_text: एतदाख्यानमायुष्यं पठन्रामायणं नरः । सपुत्रपौत्रो लोके ऽस्मिन्प्रेत्य चेह महीयते ।। 7.111.8 ।।
explanation: A man who reads this auspicious narrative, the Ramayana, is glorified in this world with his sons and grandsons, and also after death.

shloka_text: अयोध्या ऽपि पुरी रम्या शून्या वर्षगणान्बहून् । ऋषभं प्राप्य राजानं निवासमुपयास्यति ।। 7.111.9 ।।
explanation: The beautiful city of Ayodhya, though deserted for many years, will attain habitation upon obtaining King Rishabha.

shloka_text: एतदाख्यानमायुष्यं सभविष्यं सहोत्तरम् । कृतवान्प्रचेतसः पुत्रस्तद्ब्रह्माप्यन्वमन्यत ।। 7.111.10 ।।
explanation: The son of Prachetas composed this narrative, which bestows longevity, along with its future events and its conclusion. Brahma also approved of it.

shloka_text: अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य वाजपेयायुतस्य च । लभते श्रावणादेव सर्गस्यैकस्य मानवः ।। 7.111.11 ।।
explanation: A human being obtains the merit of a thousand Ashvamedha sacrifices and ten thousand Vajapeya sacrifices merely by listening to one chapter.

shloka_text: प्रयागादीनि तीर्थानि गङ्गाद्याः सरितस्तथा । नैमिशादीन्यरण्यानि कुरुक्षेत्रादिकान्यपि । गतानि तेन लोके ऽस्मिन्येन रामायणं श्रुतम् ।। 7.111.12 ।।
explanation: Prayaga and other holy places, Ganga and other rivers, Naimisha and other forests, and Kurukshetra and other places, have been visited in this world by him who has heard the Ramayana.

shloka_text: हेमभारं कुरुक्षेत्रे ग्रस्ते भानौ प्रयच्छति । यश्च रामायणं लोके शृणोति सदृशावुभौ ।। 7.111.13 ।।
explanation: Whoever gives a load of gold in Kurukshetra during a solar eclipse, and whoever listens to the Ramayana in the world, both are equal.

shloka_text: सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमायुक्तः शृणुते राघवीं कथाम् । सर्वपापात्प्रमुच्येत विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ।। 7.111.14 ।।
explanation: One who, endowed with perfect faith, listens to the story of Rama, is liberated from all sins and goes to the world of Vishnu.

shloka_text: आदिकाव्यमिदं त्वार्षं पुरा वाल्मीकिना कृतम् । यः शृणोति सदा भक्त्या स गच्छेद्वैष्णवीं तनुम् ।। 7.111.15 ।।
explanation: This first epic poem, indeed sacred, was composed by Valmiki in ancient times. He who always listens to it with devotion attains a Vaishnava form.

shloka_text: पुत्रदाराश्च वर्धन्ते सम्पदः सन्ततिस्तथा । सत्यमेतद्विदित्वा तु श्रोतव्यं नियतात्मभिः ।। 7.111.16 ।।
explanation: Sons and wives prosper, as do wealth and progeny. Knowing this truth, it should indeed be heard by those with self-controlled minds.

shloka_text: गायत्र्याश्च स्वरूपं तद्रामायणमनुत्तमम् ।। 7.111.17 ।।
explanation: And that unsurpassed Ramayana is the very form of Gayatri.

shloka_text: अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रमधनो लभते धनम् । सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्येत पदमप्यस्य यः पठेत् ।। 7.111.18 ।।
explanation: The childless one obtains a son, the poor one obtains wealth. Whoever reads even a line of this is freed from all sins.

shloka_text: यः पठेच्छृणुयान्नित्यं चरितं राघवस्य ह । भक्त्या निष्कल्मषो भूत्वा दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् ।। 7.111.19 ।।
explanation: Whoever constantly reads or listens to the deeds of Rama with devotion, becoming free from sin, attains a long life.

shloka_text: चिन्तयेद्राघवं नित्यं श्रेयः प्राप्तुं य इच्छति । श्रावयेदिदमाख्यानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो दिने दिने ।। 7.111.20 ।।
explanation: He who desires to attain ultimate good should constantly meditate on Rama. He should daily recite this narrative to Brahmins.

shloka_text: यस्त्विदं रघुनाथस्य चरितं सकलं पठेत् । सो ऽसुक्षये विष्णुलोकं गच्छत्येव न संशयः ।। 7.111.21 ।।
explanation: He who reads this entire story of Raghunatha, he certainly goes to the world of Vishnu at the end of his life, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: पिता पितामहस्तस्य तथैव प्रपितामहः । तत्पिता तत्पिता चैव विष्णुं यान्ति न संशयः ।। 7.111.22 ।।
explanation: His father, his grandfather, and similarly his great-grandfather, his great-great-grandfather, and his great-great-great-grandfather, indeed go to Vishnu, there is no doubt.

shloka_text: चतुर्वर्गप्रदं नित्यं चरितं राघवस्य तु । तस्माद्यत्नवता नित्यं श्रोतव्यं परमं सदा ।। 7.111.23 ।।
explanation: The life story of Rama always bestows the four aims of human existence. Therefore, it should always be diligently listened to, as it is supreme.

shloka_text: शृण्वन्रामायणं भक्त्या यः पादं पदमेव वा । स याति ब्रह्मणः स्थानं ब्रह्मणा पूज्यते सदा ।। 7.111.24 ।।
explanation: He who listens to the Ramayana with devotion, even a quarter of a verse or even a word, he goes to the abode of Brahma and is always worshipped by Brahma.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तमाख्यानं भद्रमस्तु वः । प्रव्याहरत विस्रब्धं बलं विष्णोः प्रवर्धताम् ।। 7.111.25 ।।
explanation: Thus is this ancient narrative; may good fortune be to you. Speak forth confidently; may the strength of Vishnu increase.

shloka_text: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रिकायां संहितायां श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकादशोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 111 ।।
explanation: Thus, in the glorious Ramayana, the original epic composed by the glorious Valmiki, a collection of twenty-four thousand verses, this is the one hundred and eleventh chapter in the glorious Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: ।। इत्युत्तरकाण्डः समाप्तः ।।
explanation: Thus ends the Uttarakanda.

shloka_text: ।। इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्रामायणं सम्पूर्णम् ।।
explanation: Thus, the glorious Ramayana, the original epic by the revered sage Valmiki, is completed.

shloka_text: ।। श्रीसीतारामचन्द्रार्पणमस्तु ।।
explanation: May this be an offering to the glorious Sita-Rama-Chandra.
